That said, I'm sure others might enjoy it more, but for me, if I made it again I'd probably leave out the cocoa powder, and make it LOOK more like an avocado pudding. (Reviewed for Spring PAC 2007)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli and cherry tomato salad

another fresh salad, perfect for summer.

1. steam broccoli until just crisp-tender , about 3 minutes
2. transfer to large bowl and cool
3. add tomatoes
4. place mustard in small bowl
5. gradually whisk in vinegar , then oil
6. mix in oregano
7. add to salad and toss to coat
8. season with salt and pepper
9. can be made 6 hours ahead
10. cover , chill
demonstrations.review: This lovely recipe adds so much to a Sunday afternoon lunch! It brings much needed colour to the plate and leaves you feeling healthy after all the stodge of the potatoes and parsnips! Recommended and will definitely make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach

nan

1. cook spinach about 5 minutes in a heavy enameled pot
2. after squeezing thoroughly to rid of as much water as possible , chop it coarsely and put into enameled saucepan with the softened butter and other seasonings
3. stir over very low heat until butter is almost absorbed
4. add small clove of garlic , crushed in garlic press , 1 / 2 c pine nuts , 1 / 2 c seeded raisins
5. cover and cook over very low heat for about 5 minutes , stirring constantly
6. turn into a hot vegetable dish
7. a cup of chopped , smoked ham may be added if desired
demonstrations.review: This was totally delicious. I didn't add the garlic as I can't have any at the moment, but I loved it. The only thing I will change next time is to roast the pine nuts first. But there'll certainly be a next time!

target.recipe_text:
hamburger noodle casserole

this is really tasty! i love the addition of the sour cream and cream cheese. mmmmmm! prep time approximate. i got this recipe from southern living cookbook that i bought back in the 70's. it did not give number of servings, but i fed a family of 5 with a couple of them having seconds.

1. combine first six ingredients and saute until meat is done
2. add tomato sauce and simmer 20 minutes
3. cook noodles according to pkg
4. directions
5. blend cream cheese and sour cream together
6. add scallions to cream cheese mixture
7. in a slightly greased casserole , place 1 / 3 of the noodles , then 1 / 3 of scallion mixture , then 1 / 3 of the meat sauce
8. continue this two more times
9. top casserole with the shredded cheese and bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes or until thoroughly heated
target.review: I made this last night and we really loved it. This will get a place in my rotating recipe list.  Very good indeed. It was easy to make and came out of the oven smelling so good. I used italian tomato sauce - gave it just the kick it needed for our taste.  Thanks Keen5 for this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger hash browns hotdish

this recipe is from an old cookbook from my mother's home town. very hearty and tasty.

1. butter a 9x13-inch pan
2. cover bottom of pan with hash browns
3. add hamburger , salt pepper and onions
4. sprinkle peas on top
5. mix soup and milk together and pour over peas
6. top with cheese
7. cover with foil and bake at 350f for one hour
8. sprinkle with french fried onions and return to oven for ten more minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a very good recipe. We enjoyed it very much. I think the leftovers were even better. This makes a big casserole, so we got to enjoy it a lot. Next time I will cut in half because we are only two. Thanks for a good recipe I will be making again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tasty apple pork chops   potatoes

very easy and tastes much richer than the cost to prepare. unique flavor and smells so good baking.

1. place pork chops in deep baking dish
2. mix soup , apple juice or cider , onion , thyme , soy sauce and garlic powder and pour over chops
3. bake at 325 degrees fahrenheit for approximately 1 1 / 2 hours or until chops are no longer pink
4. optional: put oiled baking potatoes in the oven with chops , and they will be ready at the same time- dinner is served !
demonstrations.review: This was a great supper. My hubby enjoyed every bite. We thought it was the best pork chop diner we had in a long time.  Thanks for the great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked trout with garlic   mushrooms

nan

1. to cook trout , wash and dry the fish inside and out and coat sides with a little olive oil
2. slice mushrooms and place half in the bottom of a shallow baking dish
3. salt and pepper fish , inside and out , to taste and place in dish on top of mushrooms
4. sprinkle bread crumbs over fish along with the minced parsley , chopped garlic and the green onion
5. if using fresh lemons , squeeze 1 or 2 directly over the entire trout including the inside
6. meanwhile melt butter , add to olive oil and the juice of 2 lemons
7. pour slowly over fish saving about half of the mixture
8. bake for 20-25 minutes at 375 degrees or until they are tender and bread crumbs are light brown
9. fish is done when the meat flakes easily when a fork is inserted into the flesh and lifted up slightly
10. just before the fish are done , saute 1-2 minutes , the remaining mushrooms in the sauce that is left and pour over top after placing trout on a serving plate
11. garnish with a few lemon wedges and a few sprigs of fresh parsley
12. serve this italian trout recipe with rice , or italian pasta , and a vegetable
demonstrations.review: Great way to enjoy trout.  This is restaurant worthy.  Had no green onions, used some yellow onions and it turned out great. The mushrooms & garlic gives it a seafood dish taste. Thanks for the recipe.  I will be making again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
onion cheese bread

a very nice bread, a break from the same ol', same ol'. my guys really love this.

1. cook chopped onion in half of the butter
2. stir together milk and egg
3. add biscuit mix , onion mixture , and 1 / 2 the cheese
4. spread batter in greased 8-inch round pan
5. sprinkle with remaining cheese
6. melt remaining butter , drizzle over mixture
7. bake at 400f degrees about 20 minutes or until toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Delicious bread, so easy to make and looks great too.  Made it exactly as is didn't change a thing. I had forgotten to review and was afraid I could not find it again.  Thank heaven I had copied it on a piece of paper.  It has now found a place in my favorite recipes. Thanks for the great and easy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
so yummy baked potato salad

my deli carries a yummy baked potato salad. i asked them what was in it and they told me. i had some leftover baked potatoes that i needed to use so i tried making it and it was a big hit at my house. it disappeared before i got it to the dinner table...lol !

1. gently stir together all the ingredients in a large bowl using a large spoon , reserving a little cheddar , green onion and bacon for garnish
2. transfer to a serving dish
3. top with reserved shredded cheddar , green onion slices and bacon crumbles for a beautiful presentation
demonstrations.review: This is a fabulous potato salad.  I like that it does not take a lot of time to make.  Made it exactly as posted. This is a keeper for sure.  Thanks Lois.

target.recipe_text:
peach oatmeal muffins

this muffin is simple, flavorful, and moist. using whole wheat pastry flour and oats also make them a fairly healthy start to the day.
if you substitute blueberries for the peaches add a 1/4 tsp of cloves. i like a lot of spice and use the higher amounts given.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix together dry ingredients , stir in oats and peaches
3. mix together eggs , oil and milk , stir into flour and mix gently just until flour is incorporated
4. don't over mix lumpy is ok
5. pour into greased muffin cups - i dislike muffin papers - don't grease if you use them
6. bake 15- 18 minutes until done and muffin springs bake when lightly touched
7. both of these give your muffins a lighter texture while still providing good nutrition
8. if using blueberries use about 1 1 / 2 cups
target.review: Delicious. Used 2 fresh, peeled and chopped peaches and the white whole wheat flour. Next time, I'll add some vanilla with the spices. I also topped them with a sprinkle of Turbinado sugar. YUM!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana wheat waffles

from the better homes and gardens cookbook.  delicious waffles for breakfast (or for any other meal)!

1. combine flour , baking powder , nutmeg , and salt in one bowl
2. in another bow , beat egg yolks slightly
3. beat in milk , bananas , and oil
4. add egg mixture to flour mixture all at once
5. stir just till combined but still slightly lumpy
6. in small bowl , beat egg whites until stiff peaks form
7. gently fold beaten egg whites into flour mixture , leaving a few puffs of egg white
8. do not overmix !
9. pour batter onto pre-heated , lightly greased waffle maker
10. bake waffles according to manufacturer's directions
11. serve hot and fresh
12. i topped mine with butter and syrup , and they were delicious !
demonstrations.review: We loved these! Made half a recipe since we don't have many mouths to feed here. Modifications: Added a splash of lemon juice for brighter flavor and less banana-browning. Used coconut milk beverage because of milk allergies, reduced nutmeg to a shake or two and added cinnamon. I made the recipe for waffles the first time (loved them) and for pancakes. When I made pancakes, I made the above modifications plus added half an apple, finely chopped, and substituted apple sauce for the oil. Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple waffles with cinnamon syrup

i first made these as 

1. sift dry ingredients together
2. set aside
3. combine egg yolks , milk and butter
4. add liquid to dry ingredients and stir to blend
5. fold in stifly beaten egg whites , then chopped apples
6. for syrup: mix together all ingredients except milk
7. bring to a full boil , then cook 2 minutes longer
8. cool 5 minutes
9. stir in milk and serve with apple waffles
demonstrations.review: My rating is just for the cinnamon syrup. It's SO YUMMY! Try it on vanilla ice cream, waffles, apple pie! Oh my!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bottom banana bars

delicious and very moist. even better the second day.

1. in a mixing bowl , cream butter and sugar
2. add egg and vanilla
3. beat until thoroughly combined
4. blend in the bananas
5. combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
6. add to creamed mixture and mix well
7. divide batter in half
8. add cocoa to half
9. spread into a greased 13-in x 9-in pan
10. spoon remaining batter on top and swirl with a knife
11. bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes or until the bars test done
12. cool
demonstrations.review: Really good banana bread in bar-form. Great idea! I cut them into servings, wrapped in plastic wrap and froze for to-go lunches.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
snickerdoodle french toast

this looks yummy (and very sweet!)  found on the web.

1. mix sugar and cinnamon and set aside
2. heat grill or frying pan over medium-high heat
3. in a small bowl , whisk milk , eggs , salt and vanilla
4. pour into a flat dish that is large enough to dip bread slices into
5. dip bread slices in egg mixture and poke with a fork a few times to ensure custard gets all the way through
6. sprinkle one side generously with cinnamon sugar and place this side face down in lightly greased , preheated pan
7. sprinkle the top side of the french toast generously with cinnamon sugar
8. cook until bottom is browned , then flip and cook through until toast is slightly firm and no longer wet
demonstrations.review: This was SO good and SO easy! No syrup needed on these! (I grew up putting cinnamon sugar on French Toast instead, but cooked into it?....Totally yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
double chocolate banana muffins

nan

1. in a large bowl , combine the first six ingredients
2. in a small bowl , combine bananas , oil and egg
3. stir into dry ingredients just until moistened
4. fold in chocolate chips
5. fill greased or paper lined muffin cups three fourths full
6. bake at 350 deg f for 20-25 minutes or until muffins test done
demonstrations.review: These were good, but not great. Next time I'll use dark cocoa powder for a more chocolatey taste. I left out the chocolate chips b/c DH is allergic to dairy, but they really need them! Texture was lovely, just not a lot of flavor.

target.recipe_text:
flax seed whole wheat muffins

i adapted this recipe from runner's world. next time i make this, i might put in additional brown sugar. this recipe makes a not-too-sweet muffin that is nice and light. i added hazelnuts instead of raisins. raisins would have increased the sweetness. these are good with butter.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. spray a standard sized muffin tin with non-stick spray
3. add all the dry ingredients to one bowl , except for the hazelnuts , and mix thoroughly
4. beat the egg substitute or the 2 eggs with the milk and honey and add to the dry ingredients mixing until the dry ingredients are just moistened throughout
5. fold in the hazelnuts
6. fill the muffin cups until they are 3 / 4 full into the greased cups , or use muffin liners to prevent sticking
7. bake for 20-25 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the muffin comes out clean
target.review: Good flavor, but a little dry. I used craisins, which made then very flavorful. I think next time I will add some applesauce (about a half cup) or a mashed banana for moisture.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried catfish with dill tartar sauce

i love catfish and this does hit the spot.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. place breadcrumbs and melted butter in separate shallow dishes
3. cut each fish fillet crosswise in half
4. season fish with salt and pepper
5. dip fish into butter , then into breadcrumbs , coating completely
6. place fish on baking sheet
7. bake fish until crisp , brown and just cooked through , about 12 minutes
8. meanwhile , stir mayonnaise , relish , dill and capers in small bowl to blend
9. season tartar sauce with salt and pepper
10. transfer fish to plates
11. serve fish with tartar sauce
12. recipe can be doubled
demonstrations.review: Excellent! I used an egg instead of the butter to cut the fat even more. The combination of sweet relish and dill made the tartar sauce very tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wild   crazy rice

this recipe is good with grilled chicken or steak. i got this recipe from a news web site here in town and thought it sounded great so i thought i would share it.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a medium-size baking dish , combine rice and seasonings , soups , water chestnuts and mushrooms
3. using one of the opened soup cans , add one additional can of water to the mixture
4. stir until combined
5. cook uncovered for approximately 1 hour or until rice is tender
6. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Good and easy. I made it on top of the stove since  my oven was being used for other things (broiling). It went well with the London Broil and made for a special Valentine's dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bennigan s onion soup

this is the best onion soup recipe i've tasted.  truly gourmet.

1. saute onions in butter and oil until onions are transparent , but not well browned
2. when tender , turn heat to lowest point and sprinkle with flour , stirring vigorously
3. pour into dutch oven and stir in broths
4. heat thoroughly and divide among 8 oven-proof bowls
5. mix equal parts of cheese to smooth paste and spread over bread
6. float a slice ofbread atop each serving
7. place all bowls on oven rack 4" from broiler heat and broil until cheese melts
8. serve at once
9. leftover soup freezes well up to 6 months
demonstrations.review: This is truly a great onion soup! We loved it. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled balsamic london broil

prep time is 5 minutes. the rest is time marinating.

1. put all ingredients , except meat , in a container fitted with a lid
2. cover and shake
3. pour the marinade over the top round steak and cover
4. marinate in the refrigerator for 4 hours or overnight , turning the meat occasionally
5. grill or broil until done as desired
6. slice thinly
demonstrations.review: Excellent marinade. I marinated the steak all day, and it turned out delicious. Broiled it to medium - turned out great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker herb pork roast

oh, the garlic was so good in this roast! we had it for supper that night and then the next day for sandwiches! i did not cook mine as long just depends on your cooker. update: the photo i took on march 09, 2004 makes me think i roasted this in the oven.  if so, i would have roasted it to 145 degrees and let it rest to finish cooking.

1. cut 24 small pockets into roast and insert garlic pieces
2. in a small bowl combine salt , thyme , sage , cloves and lemon rind
3. rub mixture into roast
4. pour 1 / 2 cup water into slow cooker / crock pot then add the roast
5. cook on low for 9- 10 hours
6. use the optional water and cornstarch to make a gravy with the juices
demonstrations.review: I was a little leery of the cloves, but made the recipe according to instructions. It was absolutely delicious! The lemon is very subtle, but a really nice addition. I made gravy from the juices and served it with homemade spaetzle.

target.recipe_text:
slow cooker fondue

from 3-ingredient slow cooker comfort foods cookbook.  it's that time of year here for wine, dip and cozy moments.  stoke the fire and set this with some lovely crusty bread (panera's has some wonderful choices)

1. put the wine in the slow cooker and cook on high for 1 hour
2. dredge the cheese in the flour
3. add the cheese and flour , plus salt and pepper to taste , to the hot wine
4. do not stir !
5. cover and cook for 1 / 2 hour
6. stir until smooth
7. continue to cook for 1 / 2 hour more
8. stir to make sure there are no chunks of unmelted cheese remaining
9. your preference: you can add a fiery cherry brandy just before serving
target.review: I loved making fondue this way.  It was so much easier than on the stove, where I tend to burn the cheese. I served it right out of the crock.  Dipped in bread, broccoli, carrots, shrimp, apple, and pear.  Sprinkled on some nutmeg for added flavor.  Amazing & simple!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red beans and rice  crock pot

this recipe is adapted from www.crock-pot.com.  i estimated the number of servings.

1. soak beans in water to cover overnight , drain , and rinse or in a large pot , cover beans with 3 times their volume of water and bring to a boil
2. boil for 10 minutes
3. remove from heat , cover , and let stand for 1 hour
4. discard water
5. combine all ingredients except rice in crock
6. cover and cook on low for 10 to 12 hours or on high for 5 to 6 hours
7. serve over hot cooked rice
demonstrations.review: The flavor was wonderful.  I made a few changes based on personal preference or because I was out of something.  I added a ham bone and 2 links of cajun sausage cut down the middle.  (I browned the sausage in a pan first).  I did not add salt because of the other additions.  I used vegetable broth instead of beef broth.  I added hot sauce only at the table, rather than to the pot.  Lastly, I did not boil the beans first, but they were plenty soft after cooking on low for 10 hours.  We also would need more rice than this.  I will make more to eat with the leftovers--which I cannot wait to eat!  YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice cooker rice pilaf

my husband loves this rice pilaf. everytime i make rice he requests it. hopefull you'll like it too! it takes a little extra preparation than a rice mix, but i think it's well worth it. you can also use wild rice, instead of white rice, but you'll need to add more liquid and it will take longer to cook.

1. in a small frying pan over medium heat , sautee the onion and garlic until onion is translucent
2. the garlic will cause the onion to scorch a bit , don't worry , it gives it flavor
3. add the rice , sauted onion and garlic , almonds , mushrooms , and chicken broth to a 4 cup capacity or larger rice cooker
4. stir briefly to distribute ingredients
5. set to cook
6. when done , let sit for 10 minutes
7. stir and enjoy !
8. depending on your rice cooker , the bottom may get brown
9. i like it , it gives it some extra zip !
demonstrations.review: I used jasmine rice to make this and we loved it.  It was so easy and yielded so much more flavor than plain rice and way less salt than boxed rice mixes.  I used  extra garlic and a bit of lemon zest.  Next time, I might try brown rice, as I think it would be an even bigger improvement to plain brown rice, but it was great as is.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
harvest time pumpkin dip

just in time for the fall season! this dip is excellent served with thin ginger snaps for a party. looks excellent in a carved out pumpkin as the serving dish!

1. let cream cheese stand at room temperature until softened
2. in a large bowl beat the cream cheese at medium speed of an electric mixer until creamy
3. gradually add the powdered sugar , beating well
4. stir in pumpkin , cinnamon and nutmeg
5. serve immediately with gingersnaps for dipping , or cover and chill
demonstrations.review: We love this!  I made half a batch for our family of three plus one guest as an after school snack.  It was thin, yet lumpy after using the paddle to the stand mixer.  I switched to the wire whisk, which blended it perfectly.  I also added a pinch each of allspice and cloves and served with gingersnaps and hot spiced apple cider.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
penne with vodka

i can't recommend this recipe enough. it is so simple to make and so delicious.

1. cook onion and garlic in butter over moderate heat , stirring , for 5 minutes , or until softened
2. add vodka and cook over moderately-high heat for 4 minutes
3. add puree and cream and cook over moderate heat , stirring , for 5 minutes
4. stir in ham , tabasco and salt to taste
5. cook penne until al dente
6. in a large serving bowl , toss penne with sauce
7. sprinkle parmesan over and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This was very good, but mild.  I would have liked a little more flavor BUT I did sub olive oil for the butter because we ran out.  I added extra Tabasco, but was still looking for a little bit more of some flavor.  Maybe I will add some fresh herbs next time.  The ham taste really stood out, even though it was chopped finely.  Prep was really easy and it looked good enough to serve company.  We made it on a weeknight after a long day at work, but it wasn't too much.  I served with garlic bread and red wine, but it could have used a salad.  With a few very minor changes, I will absolutely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple baked tofu

obtained from my favorite vegetarian website. tofu is healthy and tasty! don't let it scare you away. grill or bake and serve over rice. you can also serve them in stirfrys or salads that call for seasoned tofu. the seasonings are given in very generous amounts so reduce them if you desire a milder taste. considering the amount of salt in the soy sauce, you can completely omit the salt if desired.

1. cube tofu
2. mix all ingredients into a large bowl
3. let marinade in the fridge for about one hour
4. preheat oven to 350
5. place tofu on a cooling rack with a baking pan underneath to catch excess liquid
6. bake for 10 minutes , turn tofu and bake for another 15 minutes , or until the edges start to brown
demonstrations.review: I absolutely loved this.  My family was not as thrilled about the sauce, though they were fine about the tofu and said they even liked it.  So, I will make tofu this way from now on (baked on the cooling rack).  The texture is a bit dryer than usual tofu, which is perfect.  I would make this sauce again, but tone it down a little with some fruit juice and more oil.

target.recipe_text:
one pan chicken and rice

yummy and sophisticated tasting dish that is cooked in and served in only one pan.

1. sprinkle chicken with steak seasoning
2. melt butter in a large thick skillet
3. add chicken and brown for 5 minutes
4. turn
5. add onion , garlic , mushrooms and bay leaf
6. stir vegetables and cook for 5-10 minutes
7. add wine
8. allow to boil and reduce until it is almost all evaporated
9. add rice , tomatoes and water
10. make sure all the rice is in the liquid
11. cover and cook for 20 minutes
target.review:
Everybody loved it.....my 18 y/o says it tastes different than what you would ever expect from chicken (I have to agree with him).  

Very easy to make and totally delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican chicken wrap   chicken fajita   applebee s copycat

here's a south-of-the-border lunch or snack, compliments of *all you* (a new magazine).  use less or more hot sauce depending on how much spice you like!

1. in a small bowl , mix salsa and mayo
2. set aside
3. preheat oven to 350
4. arrange tortillas on two baking sheets
5. sprinkle with cheese
6. bake for five minutes
7. while that's cooking , warm oil in large skillet on medium-high
8. add chicken , sauce and salt and stir-fry until cooked through
9. place tortillas on counter , top with lettuce , chicken , tomatoes
10. roll up , cut in half and serve with the mayo-salsa dip
11. options: black or green olives
12. substitutions: crab or shrimp instead of chicken , romaine lettuce for the iceberg , monterey jack for the cheddar , corn instead of flour tortillas
demonstrations.review: I used precooked breast strips and left out the hot sauce (small children). Family liked it and it was ready in 10 minutes!  Definate winner!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy peezy pizza dough  bread machine pizza dough

this is a really easy way to make a good "yeasty" pizza dough! as well as using this recipe for when i'm making pizza, i also use it for when i'm making a focaccia or a calzone. (the preparation time i have given includes the time it takes to make the dough in the machine and the time it takes for the pizza dough to proof - after removing it from the bread machine, 30 minutes.)

1. some pizza topping ideas
2. caramelised onions and roasted garlic
3. mozzarella cheese , camembert , romano and feta
4. equal parts of basil pesto and olive oil mixed together with parmesan or romano cheese
5. plus some roughly chopped sundried or semi-dried tomatoes , sliced black olives and lots of grated mozzarella cheese , salt and lost of freshly ground black pepper !
6. cranberry jelly , shredded chicken , sliced brie !
7. mozzarella cheese , shredded chicken and sliced avocado !
8. the bread
9. place all the above ingredients in the order i have listed into the bread machine
10. select the dough cycle and press start !
11. when the dough cycle is complete , take the dough out of the machine and place in well greased bowl , and roll the dough around thus 'coating' it in oil
12. cover and leave to rise in a warm place for about 1 / 2 an hour
13. knead the risen dough lightly
14. to shape and bake: roll the dough into a circle
15. place on well greased baking tray or pizza pan
16. then add a topping of your choice and bake at 225'c
demonstrations.review: This was my husbands favorite pizza!  I cooked it at 425 for 5 minutes without toppings and 15 minutes after toppings....better than delivery

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate greek salad

this is the most delicious salad - fresh and wonderful-tasting.  fyi, lettuce can very much be a part of any greek salad - if you want it to.  we like lettuce in my family and i often add it.  it would not be 'authentic' in a horiatiki (village) salad, but who cares?

1. whisk dressing ingredients together until blended
2. season to taste
3. drain onion from ice water and pat dry with paper towels
4. combine all salad ingredients , except cheese , in large bowl
5. toss with dressing
6. sprinkle cheese over and serve
demonstrations.review:
Perfect greek salad....super easy and everyone loves it!

Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate covered strawberries

there is not much to say about this recipe. if you love chocolate and strawberries, try it. :)

1. wash strawberries and pat dry
2. place on paper towels until they reach room temperature
3. melt chocolate chips , corn syrup and butter in a double boiler , stirring occasionally
4. remove from heat and dip each strawberry into chocolate , coating 2 / 3 of strawberry
5. allow excess chocolate to drip off into pan
6. place stem side down on waxed paper covered baking pan or cookie sheet
7. refrigerate until set , about 15-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I was hesistant to add butter to the chocolate.....but WOW is this good.  Sets up nice...firm but it doesn't crumble off.  Thank you Karen!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome high heat holiday turkey

you must try this for your holiday turkey, you will not be disappointed! this is the only way we make turkey, ever! especially since oven space is valuable around the holidays.  why high heat? heat cooks. opening the cavity will allow the heat to cook the bird from the inside as well as the outside. seasoning? why? herbs and spices create a crust on the skin that seals in the flavor and juices, you pick what seasoning. breast side down?  why? the rack keeps the turkey from steaming on the bottom of the pan. 
why metal? it conducts heat better than glass or ceramic. why foil?  high heat can cook too well. loosely covering the top of the turkey will keep it from burning. why liquid? to catch the juices and fat as they drip from the turkey so that they will not burn from the high heat of the oven and stick on the bottom of the pan. you will be able to use this liquid as a base for your gravy. 5 rules for hht:
1) don't salt!!!!!!!! why suck the moisture out?

2)don't let the bird touch the pan! we want to roast, not stew.  when it sits on the bottom of the pan, instead of a rack, or it is squeezed into a too small pan, the hot air is unable to envelop the turkey, causing it to cook in it's own juices

3)don't baste the bird! it will break caramelization, slow down cooking and use up the pan juices

4) don't poke with a fork to turn or check the bird! piercing the meat will allow the flavorful meat juices to escape

5) don't cover the bird with cheesecloth! we don't care what martha says, covering the bird with cheesecloth will prevent browning. it will make a mighty tasting cheesecloth, though, if you are into that kinda thing!



 then spoon the stuffing in. what about stuffing? use chef marc's easy method: using oven mitts, place the turkey, cavity up, into a five-gallon plastic container from chef marc on kgo-am.

1. dry a 16 to 18 lb
2. turkey inside and out with paper towels
3. oil the turkey inside and out with any kind of vegetable oil using your hands
4. cut away any excess skin around the opening of the cavity and wedge a fork inside the cavity to open it further
5. leave the fork in to keep cavity open
6. rub spices , herbs , or just pepper all over the bird with your oily fingers
7. place the turkey , breast side down on a rack in a large metal roasting pan
8. cover the top of the turkey , including legs and wings with greased foil
9. pour -inch of chicken or turkey broth in the bottom of the pan
10. as the turkey cooks , check the liquid every 45 minutes and add more in case it evaporates
11. cook the turkey at 500 to 525 for 2 hours
12. remove foil , stuff the turkey with cooked stuffing and return it to the rack breast side up
13. cook the turkey 30 to 45 minutes longer until an instant-read thermometer stuck deep in the thigh reads 175
14. let the turkey rest at least 20 minutes , this allows the meat to reabsorb its juices
demonstrations.review: Take the plunge and try this method!!  I cannot believe it but this turkey was juicier and more flavorful than the brined turkeys I've been doing for years and sooooo much easier.  I did use "uncle bill's" method of shrinking the skin around the bird with boiling water (cool looking even if it doesn't add anything :0) ).  I rubbed the turkey with herbs, pepper, butter and oil mixed together.  So simple and quick!  Thank you very much for posting!

target.recipe_text:
chicken with bulgur

a tasty middle-eastern style recipe, and one of my favorite ways to fix chicken!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. mix together the salt , cinnamon , allspice , and pepper
3. rub mixture into chicken
4. in a heavy , wide frying pan over medium-high heat , heat the oil
5. add the chicken pieces and cook , turning , until all sides are browned
6. remove the chicken from the pan and set aside
7. discard the pan drippings but do not wipe out the pan
8. melt the butter in the pan you cooked the chicken in
9. add the onion and cook , stirring , until soft
10. add the uncooked bulgur and currants and stir to coat well with butter
11. spread the bulgur mixture in the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking pan
12. place the chicken pieces on top
13. pour the water , then the broth , over the chicken
14. cover the pan tightly with foil and bake in a 375 degree oven for 40 to 45 minutes or until juices run clear and bulgur has absorbed all liquid
15. garnish with sprinkled parsley and mint and serve
target.review: My boyfriend and I prepared this last night and it was wonderful!! Not having allspice I substituted with pumpkin pie spice. Also did not have currants, so used Michigan dried cherries. I used boneless skinless chicken because I was only cooking for two. This is a keeper~!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white ground chicken turkey chili

a really great white chili!

1. heat oil in large pot over medium heat
2. add onions , celery , garlic saute until onions are tender
3. add chicken and cook until no longer pink
4. stir in spices for 1 minute
5. add broth and green chilis
6. bring to a boil
7. reduce heat to low and stir in beans
8. simmer 20-30 minutes
9. serves 6 can substitute ground turkey for the ground chicken
10. this is pretty spicy--reduce the cayenne , if you don't like spicy
demonstrations.review: Although I changed some of the canned ingredients to the ones I had on hand, I and my husband thought this recipe is the best!!! As far as the consistency being like "soup", the fix is, drain the beans before adding.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
light chicken piccata with linguine

this is modified from an old magazine recipe. we've been making this version for years. we prefer the lighter sauce now and often i double the sauce ingredients to make more.

1. place each chicken breast half in a large zip bag , one at a time
2. flatten to 1 / 4 inch thickness using a meat mallet or a rolling pin
3. remove from the bag , set aside and repeat with the remaining chicken breast halves
4. combine flour , salt and pepper
5. dredge chicken in flour mixture
6. heat 1 tsp butter and oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
7. add chicken
8. cook 3 minutes on each side or until golden brown
9. add 3 / 4 cup wine , 2 tbsp lemon juice and capers to pan with chicken , scraping up brown bits and cook 2 minutes
10. remove chicken from pan and keep warm
11. stir in 3 / 4 cup wine , 2 tbsp lemon juice and cook until reduced to about 1 / 2 cup
12. stir in 1 tsp butter
13. return chicken to pan and place 1 / 4 of the chopped parsley on top of each chicken breast half
14. divide the pasta into 4 pasta bowls
15. place a chicken breast half on top of each drizzle about 2 tbsp sauce over each
demonstrations.review: This recipe is wonderful. Not only is the taste superb, but it is easy to prepare.  I chose to served the pasta on a large platter, placing the chicken on top. I then placed lemon wedges around the edges adding the parsley here and there. Next time I will double the sauce. Hmmm Good!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemony salmon patties

enjoy.        

1. combine the first nine ingredients
2. mix well
3. spoon into eight greased muffin cups , using 1 / 4 cup in each
4. bake at 350 for 45 minutes or until browned
5. meanwhile , melt butter in a saucepan
6. stir in the flour to form a smooth paste
7. gradually stir in milk
8. bring to a boil over medium heat , stirring constantly
9. cook for 2 minutes or until thickened
10. remove from the heat
11. stir in lemon juice , salt and cayenne
12. serve over patties
demonstrations.review: Good going Sean, This is a wonderful change in the usual salmon patties.  The baking made it lower cal., and they were so easy to make. Not having muffin pans, I just bake them on a cookie sheet. I love them!!! We drank a Sangiovese Di Toscana (local wine in Italy) and had polenta with the sauce. Windyday, living in Italy

demonstrations.recipe_text:
poached eggs in catsup

surprisingly good.

1. melt butter and catsup in skillet till hot
2. break eggs into catsup mixture separately
3. cover with tight fitting lid and cook on low heat till desired doneness is reached
4. remove with slotted turner and place on buttered toast
5. 2 servings
demonstrations.review: This has to be one of my favorite ways to prepare a quick, great tasting breakfast. It is easy and recommend it highly. Sounds to good to be true, but it is!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yemista  greek stuffed peppers

these peppers stuffed with a seasoned ground pork and rice mix are a greek favourite. you can also use the pork mixture to stuff zucchini and baby eggplants. serve with a green salad and crusty bread.

1. neatly cut the tops off the peppers and set the tops aside
2. remove the membrane and seeds from the peppers and discard
3. heat 4 tablespoons of the oil in a heavy-based saucepan and fry the onion until it begins to colour
4. stir in the rice and ground pork
5. add the herbs , cinnamon , salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste and the tomatoes
6. stir until the rice becomes transparent and the meat loses its redness
7. preheat the oven to 350f
8. use the mixture to loosely fill the empty peppers
9. arrange the filled peppers snugly in a casserole dish
10. put the reserved pepper tops back on the peppers , like lids
11. combine the lemon juice , water and remaining oil and pour into the dish around the peppers
12. bake for about 30 minutes until the peppers are tender and the filling is cooked and hot
demonstrations.review: okay, I did cut the recipe in half, and this may have been the problem. However, the rice was not cooked, the mixture did not fill the four peppers, and the amount of pork was dismal The good news is, I am an experienced cook will take this recipe to new heights!!! The ingredients were lovely, I grow my own mint and others herbs and will use this as a starting point. Thank-you so much for sharing your recipe. THE FLAVOR WAS RIGHT ON !!!!!!

target.recipe_text:
cheddar chicken and peas casserole

another casserole/one dish meal to add to your 'comfort food' collection...serve with a nice tossed salad!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a large skillet , saute the chicken , onion and mushroom in the oil until done
3. in a large bowl , combine the already cooked rotini , green peas , milk , soup , salt , pepper , minced garlic and 1 / 2 of the cheddar cheese
4. add the chicken mixture
5. stir to combine and pour into a greased 3 quart baking dish / pan
6. sprinkle the top with the remaining cheddar cheese
7. bake in the preheated 350f oven for 25 min or until hot and bubbly
target.review: The dish was easy to make and the ingredients sounded good but I did not enjoy the dish.  It did not have much taste.  Maybe it could use more salt.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanish chicken   rice bake

a throw-it-together and pop it in the oven supper. use more chili powder or add hot sauce if you really want to spice it up!
i just want to add:  many people who have tried this recipe have had to cook it longer than i have specified. a hint:  i always use a casserole dish with a heavy tight-fitting lid. i sometimes presoak my rice in cold water for 10 minutes or so.  hope this helps! =)  barb
ps...to freeze : cool, portion and freeze in a ziploc bag.
to reheat: thaw, place in a covered casserole dish and bake until heated through.

1. mix soup , salsa , water , corn , and beans and rice in 2-quart shallow baking dish
2. top with chicken and sprinkle with chili powder
3. cover tightly with casserole lid or foil
4. bake at 375f for 45 minutes or so
5. sprinkle with cheese
demonstrations.review: The dish was not very good.  I will not be making it again.  It may have been better with a really good salsa as I believe that is the most important ingredient.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar bundt cake

my mom passed this recipe along to me. it is easy to make and has been a big hit at home and at the office. i get frequent requests for the recipe. it is very moist and delicious and makes a good breakfast cake as well as a dessert. increase nuts by another 1/3 cup if you like nuts!

1. grease a 10-inch bundt pan well and sprinkle pan with granulated sugar
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
3. combine cake mix , pudding mix , eggs , oil and water in large bowl and beat on medium speed until well mixed , about 4 minutes
4. add brown sugar and pecans and mix to combine well
5. pour batter evenly into prepared bundt pan and bake for 1 hour or until cake tester comes out clean
6. place bundt pan on wire rack and cool 15 minutes
7. invert cake onto rack and slip pan off cake
8. let cool on rack
9. can be stored covered at room temperature
demonstrations.review: Very moist and delicious!  I received many compliments.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oreo balls

my sister's co-worker brought these to a party and they were quite a hit. i don't know where the recipe came from originally.

"bark" is an artificial chocolate or vanilla candy coating/confectioner's coating used to make a treat called almond bark and can be found at most grocery stores near the chocolate chips. 

you can use chocolate chips and white chocolate chips if you don't have almond bark, but i have found that almond bark melts better and is easier to work with.

1. using a blender or hand held mixer , mix oreos and cream cheese together
2. roll into walnut size balls
3. chill for an hour
4. melt approximately 3 / 4 package of white almond bark
5. stick a toothpick in an oreo ball and dip it in the melted white almond bark
6. allow to harden on wax paper
7. takes about 15 minute
8. while waiting , melt about 1 / 4 package of chocolate almond bark
9. when oreo balls are no longer sticky to the touch , decorate with drizzles of chocolate and white almond bark
10. i just use a sandwich bag with a tiny hole cut in one corner to drizzle the almond bark
demonstrations.review: I made these for a shower and everyone raved about them!  They turned out so perfect--looked store bought.  Instead of dipping them in white chocolate, I dipped them in the milk chocolate (because it tasted better) and drizzled with the white chocolate (with a few drops of blue food coloring mixed in) for a baby shower.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese cinnamon crescents

these are so yummy.  would be perfect for breakfast or brunch or anytime!  i just made a batch late this evening.  a parent brought these in for a teacher's luncheon and everyone loved them.

1. roll out one can of crescent rolls in bottom of 9x13 pan
2. i sprayed pan with cooking spray
3. cream together: 2 8oz
4. cream cheese
5. 1 cup sugar
6. 1 teaspoon vanilla
7. spread this mixture over crescent rolls
8. lay second tube of crescent rolls over mixture
9. melt 1 / 2 cup butter , mix in 3 / 4 cup sugar ,
10. 1 teaspoon cinnamon , and pour over top
11. bake at 350 for 30-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good.  I made half a batch and it worked out great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: The pot pie turned out GREAT!  This is the best recipe I have come across in a long time!  I added more potatoes and carrots than called for and I also added frozen peas.  It was soooooo good! This will go in my permanent file.

target.recipe_text:
fruit salad with pudding

i get compliments on this fruit salad wherever i take it. it is super easy to make and a great dish to bring to a potluck or family party. kids love it too. everyone asks "what's in the sauce"? the secret ingredient is the vanilla pudding mix.

1. in a large bowl , combine peaches , pineapples , and vanilla pudding mix
2. this includes the juices from the cans
3. mix well until pudding is dissolved
4. stir in strawberries , banana , blueberries , grapes , and sugar if desired
5. chill
target.review: This is an easy and delicious fruit salad recipe.  I used an assortment of cut-up fruit, not exactly the ones suggested in the recipe.  I did make sure I used two cans of fruit with the juice, however.  The vanilla pudding powder is a great idea to give it a special flavour.  Highly recommend to everyone.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish pub beef stew

start this sunday morning and your ready for kick-off!

1. preheat oven to 300f degrees
2. in a heavy skillet brown the beef in the butter over medium high heat
3. add the soup and water and stir well
4. add the rest of the ingredients and cook for about 5 minutes , stirring once
5. transfer to a cast iron dutch oven or oven proof pot and cook in the oven , covered for 5 hours , stirring occasionally
6. remove from oven , remove bay leaves and serve with irish soda bread and butter
demonstrations.review: Very tasty stew.  I prepared the recipe exactly as stated but, instead of baking in the oven, I used my slow cooker.  The meat was soooo tender, and the combination of vegetables and seasonings were delicious.  The kids loved it too!  Tx for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bev s sauteed yellow squash

this is the way i have been serving summer squash to my family to years. it is so easy and tastes great. i hope you enjoy it too!

1. melt butter in large skillet
2. add onion and cook just till tender
3. add yellow squash and continue cooking over medium heat , stirring until squash begins to soften
4. cover and continue cooking over low heat until nice and tender
5. i add lots of salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: Delicious and easy to prepare.  I really love the onion in it.  Next time I will double up on that.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave brownies in 5 minutes

this is my son's quick fix for a chocolate attack. easy enough for kids to make themselves.

1. cream sugar and butter together
2. add eggs and vanilla , mix well
3. stir flour and cocoa together , then add into egg mixture
4. mix well
5. grease a glass pie pan and then coat with sugar
6. pour brownie mixture into sugared pie pan
7. microwave 4&1 / 2- 5 minutes
8. let sit until cool
9. optional:to sprinkle powder sugar over the top of the brownie
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious!  My 12 y.o. daughter made these on her own.  She knows I'm a Recipezaar fan so searched for a microwave brownie recipe on this site and tried this one.  I wouldn't change a thing.  A+++++

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan   hearty root soup

i have been making this for years and it's the only soup packed with nutrients i've been able to get kids to eat and even ask for a second bowl. each time you make this soup it will be a little different. add more or less of a vegetable and you can mix and match with other vegetables not listed. it freezes well so you can take along to work for lunch weeks later with a nice chunk of bread. enjoy!

1. in a large saucepan add all ingredients and bring to a boil
2. simmer until all vegetables are soft and barley is cooked , about 40 minutes uncovered
3. add additional water if needed
4. when done you can mash a little with the potato masher or eat as is
demonstrations.review: This is so easy, delicious and nutritious!  I didn't have rutabaga or vegetable broth so used sweet potatoes and chicken broth instead.  I didn't have any of the optional ingredients so omitted those also; still, the soup tasted wonderful.  I highly recommend this to everyone - great comfort food!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black eyed pea masala

this is a recipe that i adapted from a recipe my mil made while i was in india. it is fabulous, and is even served for breakfast quite often in her house! (i could eat it for every meal lol)  i donut know the actual name of the chilies they use, but at home i generally use either 2 of the small chiles labeled "hot green chiles" from the market, or i use serranos. the ginger i generally just run over my microplane.

1. drain your peas
2. heat oil / ghee in a medium heavy pot over medium heat and fry chiles , garlic , onion , and ginger for approx 6 minutes
3. add your curry powder / garam masala , turmeric and cumin , and then add the tomatoes
4. cook for approximately 3 minutes until it begins to thicken and add your peas and salt to taste , along with 4 cups of water
5. allow water to boil and then reduce your heat , cover and cook for approximately 2 hours until your peas are done and the sauce is nice and thick
6. after the peas are done , fold in your yogurt and cilantro , and serve
7. this goes well with rice or with chappati / roti
8. garnish with minced cilantro
demonstrations.review: This is outstanding. I took a short cut and used two cans of black-eyed peas, adding them along with the tomatoes and omitting the water. I didn't have green chilies so used bottled (marinated) jalapenos. The recipe turned out wonderfully. It is very spicy/hot and tastes just like the masala I had in the Indian restaurant a few weeks ago. Will definitely make again.

target.recipe_text:
non alcoholic hot buttered rum

wonderful for a chilly evening, after a lovely dinner. sit back and relax!

1. stir together the instant coffee crystals with the boiling water until dissolved
2. stir in the butterscotch topping and rum extract , mix well
3. top with the whipped topping
4. serve immediately
5. enjoy !
target.review: I LOVE this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oranges in red wine   naranjas al vino tinto

so colorful and tasty.  from jose andres.

1. in a medium saucepan , combine all the syrup ingredients and bring to a boil
2. reduce heat to low and simmer until mixture is reduced by one third , about 25 minutes
3. strain the mixture and refrigerate until cooled
4. check the syrup's consistency
5. it should be like honey
6. if too thin , return it to pan and reduce for a few more minutes
7. if too thick , add a little water
8. set aside
9. slice off the tops and bottoms of the oranges
10. then remove all the peel and pith around the oranges
11. slice along the sides of each segment and pull out the segments
12. repeat with lemons
13. spoon the syrup onto a plate and arrange the orange and lemon segments over it
14. sprinkle mint leaves on top
demonstrations.review: Wow!  I used one orange and one lemon, reserving the syrup for a marinade later on in the week.  I actually liked the taste of the lemon with the syrup and a bite of mint.  This really would go with any type of citrus.  Made for RRR, ZWT5.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wine    blue cheese hamburgers  oamc

called different hamburgers by gloria diggs who submitted it to a cookbook.  i cut this out and had it in a folder.  it has an interesting combo of ingredients that you put in a blender and then mix into the meat.  they can be prepared, frozen and cooked when desired.

1. combine all ingredients except the beef , in a blender and mix until liquid
2. pour this over the meat in a bowl and mix until smooth and well blended
3. form into 4-6 patties
4. cook under broiler or in pan or on grill , or you want to freeze the patties for cooking another time
demonstrations.review: I did add breadcrumbs to the recipe as the other poster suggested, and they did stay together better.  However, I wasn't too thrilled with the flavor.  I think it might have been too salty with the blue cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon wrapped shrimp with rosemary and stilton

posted for zwt6: great britain.  stilton cheese is a british blue cheese.  adapted from bon appetit.  the shrimp can be prepared up to 8 hours ahead of time and chilled on the baking sheet.

1. preheat broiler
2. arrange shrimp on baking sheet
3. sprinkle with rosemary , black pepper , and several splashes of vinegar
4. wrap each shrimp in bacon , covering completely
5. secure with toothpick
6. broil shrimp 4 to 5 inches from heat source until shrimp are cooked through and bacon is browned , watching carefully to prevent burning , about 5 minutes per side
7. remove toothpicks
8. transfer shrimp to platter
9. sprinkle hot shrimp with stilton cheese and serve
demonstrations.review: I like the flavors in this!  DH had already made and frozen bacon wrapped shrimp, so it was a chinch to make this from frozen!  Made for ZWT6.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
south of the border quiche  oamc

this came from cooking for 2 magazine, one of my first oamc recipes!!  this makes two pies.  it's also meat-free, if you're a vegan that eats eggs and milk, this will work for you too.  all the stuff i like so i can't wait to try it, since i'm just getting started with oamc.

1. line the unpricked pie crusts with a double thickness of heavy-duty foil
2. bake at 400 degrees for 5 minutes
3. remove foil and bake 5 minutes longer
4. sprinkle the chili powder and cumin over the shells
5. combine the cheeses and divide evenly into the shells
6. in a bowl , whisk the eggs , cream , chilies , olives , onions , cilantro , salt , and pepper
7. pour over the cheese
8. cover and freeze up to three months
9. to prepare a quiche immediately: cover the edges of the crust with foil
10. place on a baking sheet and bake at 400 degrees for 35-40 minutes or until a knife inserted in the middle comes out clean
11. let stand for 10 minutes before cutting
12. serve with salsa and sour cream
13. to prepare the frozen quiche: preheat the oven to 400 degrees
14. remove from the freezer 30 minutes before baking
15. cover the edges of the pie shell loosely with foil and place on a baking sheet
16. bake for 55-60 minutes or until a knife comes out clean when inserted in the center
17. let stand for 10 minutes before baking
demonstrations.review: This is so yummy!  I did everything exactly as the recipe describes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mustard pickled eggs

if you dig pickled eggs, give these a try.  the food coloring is optional..... it just gives a more dramatic deep yellow color.  cook time is chilling time.

1. place the peeled eggs in a non-metal bowl or jar
2. in a saucepan over medium heat , mix together cider vinegar , sugar , onion , mustard powder , garlic powder , salt and food coloring
3. bring just to a simmer
4. pour over the eggs and allow to cool
5. cover and chill for at least 48 hours to allow flavor to develop
demonstrations.review: This is like an inside out deviled egg!  The color was quite bright - I added 4 drops of food coloring in it.  I am, however, going to only be able to eat these at home.  It was quite strong in the lunchroom at work!

target.recipe_text:
north african sweet potato pancakes

these have a very special flavor, go great with my recipe #13577.

1. loosely grate potatoes in food processor and place in mixing bowl
2. season to taste with salt and pepper
3. mix in eggs
4. cover and refrigerate until time to fry
5. in large non-stick skillet , heat enough oil to cover bottom of the pan
6. spoon out the batter into pan , being careful not to crowd
7. cook until crisp and brown on one side , then turn and fry on other side
8. keep finished pancakes warm in oven until all pancakes are fried
9. drain on paper towels
target.review: Delicious - especially straight out of the frying pan! We tried several types of pancakes (onion, carrot, eggplant, etc.) but this won top awards after the onion. And the recipe is so easy to make. I will definitely be making these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cottage cheese roast  vegetarian meatloaf

great vegetarian comfort food! don't be fooled by the ingredients; the flavor is very much like meatloaf. kitchen alchemy at its finest!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease a loaf pan
3. in a large bowl , combine cottage cheese , eggs , vegetable oil , soup mix , walnuts , cereal and onion
4. spoon into prepared pan
5. bake for 60 to 70 minutes
6. let the 'roast' rest for 5 to 10 minutes
7. turn out onto serving platter
demonstrations.review: This recipe is AMAZING! Based on the recommendation of other reviewers, I added about half a cup of tomato sauce to the mixture, but other than that, stuck to the recipe. EVERYONE in my family LOVED it (which is in itself a very rare occasion - usually we only agree on cake and dessert recipes, and even then, not always :-), and of course, no one could figure out what the heck was in it. Luckily, they liked it so much that they continued to eat it even after I told them what a strange blend of ingredients was in there :-) I wonder who thought this recipe up... I've since shared the recipe with all my friends, and plan to make this on a regular basis. BTW, we are FAR from being vegetarians - 'nuff said?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s onion patties latkes

i have been making these for over 20 years, i usually get about 15 patties but it depends on the size of the batter that you drop in the pan, these are better if fried to very brown and crispy, you can make a double recipe, fry them then freeze them on a tray then pop them into freezer bags, then just warm them in the oven to crisp up, they are very addicting and i can tell you i eat half before they even get to the table lol!  if you plan on doubling the recipe then make two separate recipes in two bowls, i have doubled the recipe into one bowl and for some reason they just are not as good ---  if desired you could add in a slightly beaten large egg and reduce the milk by 1/4 cup --- you will *love* these!  also see my
recipe#186700 *and*
recipe#244592

1. chop the onions finely then place into a bowl
2. in another large bowl mix together the flour , sugar , baking powder , seasoning salt , cayenne , garlic powder and a small amount of black pepper
3. mix to combine well
4. add in the milk and whisk until thoroughly combined
5. add in the chopped onions and green onions and mix with a wooden spoon until combined
6. in a large non-stick frypan , heat a small amount of oil to medium-hot , adding in more oil as needed as the patties will absorb too much oil if you add in a large amount of oil at one time
7. drop the batter from a tablespoon into about 1 / 2-inch of hot oil
8. flatten slightly with the spoon or spatula
9. sprinkle with a little salt
10. fry until crispy and brown on both sides
demonstrations.review: Delicious! My family just gobbled them up, and asked for more! (I made another type of latke at the same time - sweet potato - which was also very good, but this won the contest hands down.) Thanks so much for this great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brisket for a beginner

this is our favorite rosh hashana main dish. the smell of this dish cooking is incredible and the meat will fall apart.

1. line roasting pan with aluminum foil and coat with cooking spray
2. place beef in pan
3. mix all ingredients together and pour over beef
4. cover with aluminum foil and bake for 2 1 / 2 to 3 hours at 350 degrees
demonstrations.review: I used tomato sauce with some sugar and spices instead of the ketchup (believe it or not, there's someone in the family who doesn't like ketchup!), and it was DELICIOUS! It was incredibly tender, as promised in the recipe, and everyone loved it. I definitely plan to make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon curd squares

these are to die for. my family goes nuts over them.lol they are from joy of cooking. i put it here so i can find the recipe fast. lol

1. mix 1st three
2. press into an 8" square pan
3. bake at 350 for 20 minutes
4. meanwhile , mix all the rest
5. pour over hot crust
6. bake 25 more minutes
7. chill
8. sprinkle with confex sugar when cold
demonstrations.review: YUM! I had misplaced my own lemon bar recipe, which was very similar to this, so when I found this, I knew I had to try it out. The only change I made was to add more lemon juice (almost doubled the amount), but then again, I didn't put in grated lemon peel. The cake came out fantastic - actually better than my original recipe, although that's hard to believe! One warning to anyone who tries this is that knowing how long to keep this in the oven can be a bit tricky. You don't want to overbake it, but you also don't want the lemon filling to be too liquidy. It's a delicate balance, but spending some time figuring it out is worth the results!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mocha brownies with coffee frosting

i love this recipe because it is easy to mix up, i usually have everything on hand and they taste woooonderful. the frosting is optional.

1. preheat oven to 350f grease a 13x9 inch pan
2. melt shortening and butter over low heat or in the microwave
3. remove from heat and add cocoa , blend well
4. add sugar and mix well
5. dissolve instant coffee in hot water and mix into creamed mixture
6. add eggs one at a time , beat well , by hand , after each addition
7. stir in vanilla , flour , and salt
8. do not over beat !
9. bake 25-30 minutes
10. cool completely before frosting
11. for frosting , cream butter and vanilla
12. add powdered sugar and mix in well on medium speed
13. dissolve instant coffee in milk and add to mixture
14. beat on high until light and fluffy
demonstrations.review: The best! I made this for a family event and it was a HUGE hit. My own family is already asking me to make this again. The only problem is that I am trying to diet, and this cake is WAY to tempting. BTW, an added bonus is that this cake is very easy to make.

target.recipe_text:
super easy general tso chicken

this is not authentic general tso's chicken, but it's a recipe i developed and it tastes quite similar.  it's easy and requires no "odd" ingredients.  you can either batter your chicken before adding to the sauce or just stir-fry your plain chicken, it's up to you.  this makes plenty of sauce- i don't like dry general tso's. after reading several reviews,  i would just like to add that i must use very mild hot sauce, because i am definitely not someone who likes super-hot stuff and several have complained that it's too hot.  i would have to say that it probably varies according to your brand of hot sauce, so be warned!  :-)

1. mix the soy sauce , water , hot sauce , sugar , boullion , and ginger in a saucepan and heat until boiling
2. cut the heat down and simmer while you prepare the chicken
3. take your chicken and cut into bite-size cubes
4. now , at this point you can either use a boxed batter mix to add a coating on it , or you can just stir-fry your plain chicken in a little oil until thoroughly cooked
5. going back to your sauce , use the cornstarch in water to thicken it
6. then add your cooked chicken
7. if you battered your chicken , it's ready to eat
8. if you stir-fried plain chicken , use this time to simmer it awhile and prepare your veggies and rice
9. serve this chicken over the veggies and rice
target.review: EXTREMELY hot!  I used only 5 Tbsp of Tabasco and one whole hot pepper and could not eat it.  My husband loves spicy food, and made it through his serving, but would like it toned down in the future.  It also made quite a bit of sauce, which might have been alright, if it was edible. Too bad, since it smelled and looked SO good!  Definitely easy to make, which I appreciated.  Maybe I'll try again and add the Tabasco a bit at a time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caribbean bar nuts   low carb   no salt added

addictive sweet/hot pecans which are as hot or as mild as you like them, depending upon amount of cayenne used. although they are slightly sweet, they don't stick to your hands. a well-balance blend of flavors that whets your appetite, but are good for diabetics and other persons trying to lower their carbohydrate intake. each tbs. of nuts contains 0.9 grams of carbs, versus double that amount if made with regular sugar. atkins fans take note!

1. it is not the splenda in little packets
2. preheat oven to 325 degrees
3. place pecans in single layer on baking sheet
4. roast 15-17 minutes or until lightly golden brown and slightly crunchy
5. in large bowl , add the dry coating mix
6. set aside
7. about 5 minutes before pecans are done , in a saucepan add all seasoning mix ingredients and bring just to boil
8. it may not seem like enough sauce
9. however , it should be enough to coat the outside of all the nuts
10. immediately add hot nuts and stir continuously until all liquid has been absorbed and no liquid remains on bottom on saucepan
11. this will take about 1-2 minutes
12. pour nuts into dry coating mix bowl and stir to coat nuts
13. pour nuts onto a silpat silicone mat , parchment or waxed paper , separating nuts
14. cool
15. store in air-tight container
16. would keep for weeks , but they won't last that long
17. variation: mix these nuts with craisins , butterscotch chips , and mini-pretzels for a delicious bar mix appetizer
demonstrations.review: Such interesting ingredients, but super yummy!  They certainly are addictive and I couldn't keep my husband and I from snacking on them!  Yes, the coating that you boil is odd and seems like it wouldn't work, but trust BeachGirl, they do.  I made them for a poker party and they were enjoyed by all.  They would make a good Hostess or Christmas gift.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy awesome guacamole

i recently did a taste test of 12 guacamole recipes from zaar. this is the result of mixing the top 2 favorites together.

1. cut avocados in half and take out the seed , scoop out meat with a spoon and place in bowl
2. mash the avocado with a fork
3. add the salsa , mayonnaise , sour cream , salt , pepper , garlic and onion powder
4. mix together well
5. add lemon juice , mix and serve
6. garnish with fresh chives
demonstrations.review: Super Yum!!  I can't claim to have followed the recipe exactly... I just used your ingredients (minus the mayo & onion powder) and it ended up lovely! I mashed 2 avocados, 2 cloves of garlic, 1/4 c. salsa ("Wonderful Salsa' Recipe #9272), 1/3 c. sour cream, ground black pepper, salt, a squirt of lime juice and 3 large fresh chives.  I love that it has chives instead of fresh onions.  Thanks looneytunesfan!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced pear butter

nan

1. combine pears and apple juice in a large dutch oven
2. tie broken cinnamon spices , gingerroot , allspice and cloves in a piece of cheese cloth
3. add to pear mixture
4. bring to a boil
5. cover , reduce heat , and simmer for 45 minutes to 1 hour or until pears are tender
6. drain pears , and discard spice bag
7. mash pears or process in food processor until smooth
8. return pear puree to dutch oven , and add sugar
9. cook , uncovered , over medium heat for 30 to 40 minutes or until mixture thickens , stirring frequently
10. remove from heat , and quickly pour hot pear mixture into hot sterilized jars , leaving 1 / 4-inch headspace
11. wipe jar rims
12. cover at once with metal lids , and screw on bands
13. process in boiling water bath for 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very yummy!  I've made plain pear butter (with orange juice, peel, and nutmeg) and this spiced kind.  The flavor is delicious!  Much more interesting and elegant.  It will make good gifts.  I got a bit over 9 half-pints.  I didn't peel and core my pears, I just removed the stem and blossom end, cooked, and put through a sieve.  I think this gave me more pulp than if you peel and core them.  I also used apple cider instead of the apple juice.  My end product is a medium brown color.  Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
berries and stars

this is the most awesome dessert you could ever make for fourth of july celebrations! you will impress even the most seasoned cooks...and it is quite easy!

1. preheat oven to 400
2. roll one sheet onto baking sheet
3. roll out second sheet and cut 4 1-inch strips from second sheet
4. reserve remaining dough
5. brush edges of pastry on pan with water
6. lay your strips of pastry over edges to form an outer rim
7. trim off any excess dough
8. prick entire bottom of pastry
9. bake 15 minutes or until golden brown
10. center may puff but will flatten
11. cut star shapes from remaining dough with cookie cutter
12. sprinkle with sugar
13. bake separately for 12 minutes
14. zest and juice lemons
15. combine zest , juice and condensed milk
16. fold in one cup cool whip
17. fill pastry with filling top with fruit
18. top with pastry stars
19. decorate with remaining cool whip
demonstrations.review: This was beautiful and tasted great.  Definitely impressive!  Very easy and comes together quickly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco cheesecake

this appetizer proves that cheesecake is not just for dessert. very good and the presentation of this is impressive. enjoy! helpful hint: when cutting or seeding hot peppers, use rubber or plastic gloves to protect your hands and avoid touching your face. prep time includes overnight refrigeration.

1. sprinkle bottom of greased 9-inch springform pan with cornmeal
2. set aside
3. in mixing bowl , beat cream cheese until smooth
4. add the taco seasoning , sour cream and salsa
5. stir in the eggs , pepper jack cheese and chilies
6. fold in olives
7. pour over cornmeal
8. place pan on a baking sheet
9. bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes or until center is almost set
10. cool on a wire rack for about 10 minutes
11. carefully run a knife around edge of pan to loosen
12. cool for 1 hour
13. refrigerate overnight
14. remove sides of pan
15. spread sour cream over top and sides of cheesecake
16. arrange olives , onions , tomatoes and jalapeno slices on top in a circular motion
17. i do tomatoes on the outer edge , then green onion , jalapeno , then scatter black olives randomly , within the circle
18. serve with assorted crackers
demonstrations.review: This was very good!  It looks beautiful and tastes great.  It makes quite a bit, so take it to a large party or pot-luck.  Tortilla chips are a good accompaniment.  I would suggest cutting a wedge or two to get people started.

target.recipe_text:
russian butter cookies for christmas

bite-sized balls that melt in your mouth - fabulous!  these, the chocolate meringues, the lemon-cheese spritz cookies and kathie lee gifford's pecan tarts are truly the only christmas cookies you need to bake - to have the very best...

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. beat well the butter and sugar together
3. blend in the remaining ingredients
4. chill for several hours or overnight
5. shape / roll into 1 inch balls
6. bake at 400f for 10-12 minutes
7. roll at once , while warm , in 1 / 2 cup confectioner's sugar
8. cool and then roll again in confectioner's sugar
9. these are so simple and yet so special
target.review: It doesn't get any better than these. They taste like shortbread and are buttery, sinful goodness.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amaretto apricots with walnuts teriyaki

you can serve this with cocktails or on a dessert tray. they are both sweet and savory. from the new carry-out cuisine. it is hard to stop nibbling on these!

1. line a jelly-roll pan with foil
2. spread the nuts on the foil lined pan
3. combine the remaining ingredients for the walnuts , except the kosher salt , in a saucepan and heat until the sugar is dissolved
4. pour the sauce over the nuts , making sure to coat them well
5. bake at 350 for 15-20 minutes
6. place the toasted nuts on lightly oiled foil and sprinkle with the salt if desired
7. assembly: add the amaretto to the cream cheese and mix well
8. place a teaspoon of the cheese on each apricot and top with a walnut
demonstrations.review: Different, interesting, adventurous on the tongue and popular with party guests.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest chicken rice   veggie casserole

even though i can't eat chicken, this recipe is so ridiculously easy that sometimes i make it for my husband and daughter when i'm tired.  it takes 10 minutes to throw together and has all the important food groups in it!  if you use chicken thighs, its super cheap too.  feel free to sub whatever "cream of..." soup you like, we just happen to like mushrooms.

update: i think people were missing the part of the instructions that called for the 2 soup-can-fulls of water so i'm adding it into the recipe.  this recipe is intentionally on the bland side, making it kid friendly or open to whatever spices and seasonings you prefer!

1. in a baking dish , mix together everything except the chicken
2. place chicken on top
3. sprinkle with additional paprika and pepper if desired
4. bake uncovered at 375 for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I made this last night and it was a big hit! I changed it up just a smidge..I dredged the chicken breasts in seasoned flour and browned them first. I only one can of cream of mushroom and one can of cream of chicken, so I used those. Instead of water I used chicken broth. And instead of frozen veggies I used fresh broccoli florettes (on your suggestion..thank you!) cut up small and fresh sliced mushrooms. This was a fabulous family meal and made my significant other very happy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry cake

this is the cake that most of my family want for their birthday cake. this is a favorite cake of newfounlanders.

1. mix dry ingredients together and set aside
2. cream together butter and sugar , add eggs , vanilla , almond and lemon flavoring and continue to beat
3. add dry ingredients and warm milk a little at a time till well mixed
4. add the glazed cherries
5. bake at 325 for 1 hour or until done
demonstrations.review: What a delicious recipe! I could not find the dried glazed cherries at my local Kroger, so substituted two cups of maraschino cherries (without the liquid). It turned the batter a lovely pink. I frosted it with recipe #122632 and it was the best cake I have ever made. Highly recommend!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sauerkraut meatball appetizers

my friend mary, a diehard packer fan, shared this recipe.  it's perfect for tailgate parties, potlucks, or family gatherings.  you won't recognize the saurkraut at all.  it has a wonderful sweet/sour chunky sauce with just a little kick to it.  there are never any leftovers.

1. mix first four ingredients and shape into 1 inch meatballs
2. place meatballs in a 9 x 13 baking pan
3. pour remaining ingredients in a sauce pan
4. bring to a boil
5. pour sauce over meatballs and bake at 350 f for 1 hour
6. test one meatball to make sure it's done
demonstrations.review: Honestly, this wasn't my favorite, but my guests just raved about it and my kids love it. It made the house smell fantastic in preparation for my holiday party. I did put it in the crock pot rather than doing it in the oven and they turned out wonderful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan pork chops with a crunch

the cheesy crust gives a nice finish to this pork chop casserole. the whole family will love it.

1. melt 2 tbsp butter
2. cook onions until soft
3. stir in red pepper , thyme , salt and pepper and set aside
4. melt remaining butter and brown the chops on both sides until nicely browned
5. in an oven proof dish spread half the onion mixture
6. top with pork chops
7. cover with remaining onion mixture
8. drizzle the chicken stock over casserole
9. bake covered in 400f degrees oven for 40 minutes or until chops are tender , basting one or two times
10. meanwhile mix together
11. bread crumbs , parmesan , mozzarella and 2 tbsp butter
12. sprinkle over the casserole when the chops are done
13. bake for 10 minutes to form a crisp topping and then broil for a minute or two to finish browning
14. serve
demonstrations.review: This had my man groaning with pleasure. Thanks for a fantastic recipe. The only change I made was using 1/2 cup of red wine, 1/2 cup of beef broth instead of the chicken broth. Double thumbs up!

target.recipe_text:
chocolate eclair dessert

who would have thought something so easy could be so delicious!

1. mix together vanilla pudding mix and milk
2. fold in whipped topping
3. line 9 x 13 pan with one layer of graham crackers
4. put half of the pudding mixture over the graham crackers
5. place a second layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
6. put the remaining pudding mixture over the graham crackers
7. place a third layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
8. heat the tub of frosting in the microwave for 30 seconds to soften
9. spread frosting on the top of the last layer of graham crackers
10. cover with plastic wrap and let set a couple hours or overnight in the refrigerator
11. cut in squares
target.review: This is so easy and delicious. The recipe I have calls for 2 cups of milk, so if you are a little short it won't matter. Dark chocolate fudgy frosting is really good to top this with!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple or pear cake

absolutely the most delicious, moist cake ever with a decadent topping. very simple to make, my family just loves this!

1. cake:
2. mix all cake ingredients by hand in order given
3. pour in a greased 9 x 13 inch pan or springform pan
4. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes and remove
5. topping:
6. in saucepan mix all ingredients and bring to a slow boil for 3 minutes
7. pour over cake and return to oven for 4 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was more like bread than cake. I thought it was rather dry. Giving it 3 stars because two people told me they liked it. I threw most of it away. I baked it for 45 minutes as instructed. Smelled heavenly while baking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracker barrel s hash browns casserole   copycat

my parents worked on a cracker barrel training video (which they use to train the chefs) and got this recipe a few years ago. cracker barrel's recipe seems to have changed a bit over these few years but not for the best. this is their recipe though and has become a family favorite. we usually have it now for easter and thanksgiving and its also great for a brunch. happy cooking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix potatoes , onion , celery and mushroom soups , and 1 / 2 of the cheese
3. coat a 9" x 13" baking dish with spray oil
4. spread mixture into dish
5. sprinkle other 1 / 2 of cheese evenly over top
6. dot margarine evenly over the cheese
7. bake at 350f for 45 minutes to 1 hour or until cheese starts to brown at peaks
demonstrations.review: This is very good! I plan to make this again the next time I need to bring a dish to an event. It's great for breakfast, brunch, or as a side item for dinner. Very easy to make! I used a 30 oz. bag of Ore Ida shredded hash browns found in the frozen section of the grocery store, which I partially thawed in the fridge the day before I made the recipe. Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate  butterscotch  pb rice  krispies treats
