born with a rice krispie treat in my hand, you better believe i know my krispies. even if you are not a rice krispie fan, this will become one of your regular "goody" recipes!

1. mix peanut butter , karo syrup , and sugar in a pot , and bring to a slight boil
2. stir until creamy
3. take mixture off the burner , and mix with rice krispies cereal
4. spread mixture in 13 x 9 inch pan
5. melt chocolate and butterscotch chips together in microwave
6. spread melted chips over rice krispie mixture
7. refrigerate until chocolate-butterscotch mixture hardens
8. cut into 2x2-inch squares
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I took these to work, and people are still talking about them weeks later. I followed the recipe exactly. They are sooooo good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious oreo refrigerator cake  no bake

this has remained a long time favorite, i have even made this in the winter months and served it to guests many times, lemon flavor pudding mix is also very good to use in place of the chocolate --- you can make this well in advance, it can also be served as a frozen dessert just remove from freezer about 6 minutes before slicing this is just as delicious frozen!  if you are serving this at a kid's birthday party place mini oreo cookies into the topping of cool whip facing sideways --- i most always double the chocolate pudding mixture, you may also double the cream cheese mixture if desired --- this is very good!

1. crush oreo cookies
2. set 1 / 4 cup aside for topping
3. mix the remaining crushed cookies with the melted butter
4. press into the bottom of a greased 13 x 9-in baking pan
5. in a bowl , beat the cream cheese with the confectioners sugar on medium speed
6. fold in half of the cool whip topping
7. spread over cookie crumb layer
8. refrigerate 1 / 2 hour
9. in the meantime , combine milk with instant pudding mix
10. beat well , until smooth
11. pour over chilled mixture in the pan
12. refrigerate for 1 hour
13. spread remainder of cool whip topping on top of pudding layer
14. sprinkle with remaining reserved cookie crumbs
15. store cake in the refrigerator , covered tightly
demonstrations.review: Very easy and delicious! I followed the recipe exactly as stated. I wasn't sure how fine to crush the Oreos, so I just put them in a plastic baggie and hit them with a hammer until they were in small chunks. They soften the longer you refrigerate this, and I prefer them soft. Next time I make it, I will definitely make it the night before. Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken parmesan

i got this recipe a few years ago and everyone that i have made it for absolutely loves it! it's great with pasta on the side.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. rinse chicken breasts and pat dry
3. combine bread crumbs and 1 / 2 of the parmesan cheese into small bowl
4. mix well
5. dip chicken breasts into egg and coat
6. then , dip into bread crumb and cheese mixture
7. heat oil and fry breaded chicken on both sides for about 5 minutes
8. pour spaghetti sauce into a 13x9 baking dish
9. top with chicken
10. cover with foil
11. bake for 25 minutes
12. pull out and top with mozzarella and remaining parmesan cheese
13. bake uncovered for another 7-10 minutes
14. serve over cooked spaghetti or pasta of your choice
demonstrations.review: Easy and delicious. Great as leftovers.

target.recipe_text:
pan seared cod with basil sauce

this has a fresh pesto-like feel without the nuts, and a lot less fat. any flaky white fish can be used here - i usually have tilapia or whitefish around rather than cod. i had an open bottle of reisling and so i used that in place of the broth.  from cooking light.

1. combine basil , broth , cheese , oil , 1 / 2 tsp salt , and garlic in a small bowl
2. sprinkle fish with 1 / 2 tsp salt and pepper
3. coat a large nonstick pan with cooking spray and heat over medium-high heat
4. saute fish for 5 minutes on each side or until it flakes easily with a fork
5. spoon basil sauce over fish to serve
target.review: Giving five stars for the sauce, really good sauce.  I will try it with tilapia as well.  If I do this with cod again I will probably add garlic powder and flour the fish to pan fry it with olive oil.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken cooked in foil

nan

1. pre-heat oven to 425 degrees f
2. rinse chicken and pat dry with paper towel
3. cut 4 10" squares of heavy-duty foil
4. pour 1 tbsp oil on each sheet of foil- spread to cover foil
5. place chicken on foil squares
6. sprinkle with salt , pepper and garlic powder
7. fold and seal foil
8. place foil packs on cookie sheet
9. bake for 40 minutes
10. serve chicken from foil packets
11. be careful when opening- steam is trapped inside
demonstrations.review: This was a very good healthy dinner.  I put some chopped tomatoes, crushed garlic, and black olives on top of chicken then sealed the foil.  I will probably use more salt next time, just for out tastes. Thank you

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey pecan chicken cutlets

this gives the chicken a nice crunchy bite. you can also cut the cutlets into fingers for a great appetizer.

1. dredge the cutlets in flour , shaking off excess
2. heat two tablespoons margarine in a heavy skillet over medium heat
3. add the cutlets and brown on both sides , about 5-6 minutes
4. stir together the remaining tablespoon margarine , honey and pecans
5. add to the skillet , stir gently
6. cover and simmer gently for 7-8 minutes
7. remove cutlets to a serving platter , pour sauce over and serve
demonstrations.review: This is a must make dish.  We both loved it.  It is so simple yet I would serve this to guests because it is so good.  I did put some fresh pepper on my chicken breasts before flouring.  Came out great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey brine

for a juicier and tastier turkey, brine before cooking! if your turkey or chicken is kosher do not brine since it has already been salted. brining isn't just for poultry but also lean cuts of meat and even fish and shrimp. but you must adjust time to their size. example; a whole trout takes only 20 minutes and the same with shrimp, a whole chicken takes about 4 hours, a cut up chicken about 2hrs. may add honey or maple surup, may replace some of the water with something like apple cider or coffee. let loose your creativity. yes, you have to plan ahead but for little effort the results are worth it!

1. combine 2 quarts of water in a 6 quart pot with salt and sugar , over high heat until dissolved
2. if wanted , add other seasonings at this time
3. let come back to room temperature
4. you will need 2 gallon turkey size oven roasting bags
5. place one roasting bag inside the other , roll down the edges of the bags to help them stay open
6. put bags in a heavy roasting pan that will hold turkey
7. place turkey breast side down , with legs facing you in the inner bag
8. some help from another person at this point would be of help , they can hold the bags open for you as you pour the cooled brine into the cavity and over the turkey
9. gather the inner bag as tightly as possible and secure with a twist tie
10. secure outer bag with twist tie
11. refrigerate in the roasting pan for 12-18 hours
12. remove from bags , rinse very well , pat dry with paper towels
13. it's now ready for your favorite recipe
demonstrations.review: First time I brined, and will be brining from now on.  I pre made the brine one day before the turkey needed to go in, and put the brine in the refridgerator to make sure it was cool enough to put turkey in.  That way I didn't have to wait for it to cool.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breasts cilantro

this chicken stays very moist and tender. has a wonderful mexican flavor.

1. combine lime juice , oil , and honey in shallow dish
2. dip chicken in lime mix
3. coat chicken with tortilla crumbs
4. place in ungreased 11x7 baking dish
5. bake , uncovered at 350 for 25 minutes
6. mix salsa and cilantro
7. pour over chicken
8. sprinkle with cheese
9. bake for 6 minutes more
demonstrations.review: Very good, I will be making again.  I used lemon since I had no lime and put some garlic powder on the chicken. Also, I put some dried cilantro in the tortilla mix.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breasts with roasted red peppers

quick and easy with a rich tasting pan sauce.  from all you magazine - november 2008

1. place each breast between 2 sheets of parchment paper or plastic wrap and pound to an even 1 / 2-inch thickness
2. sprinkle with salt
3. coat with flour , shaking off excess
4. warm 2 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
5. cook chicken until golden brown on both sides and cooked through , about 4 minutes per side
6. transfer to a platter and cover loosely
7. heat remaining 1 tablespoon oil in skillet
8. saute garlic until fragrant , about 30 seconds
9. add peppers and saute 1 minute more
10. add broth , vinegar and sugar
11. bring to a boil , scaping up browned bits from the bottom of the skillet
12. reduce heat and simmer until slightly thickened , about 4 minutes
13. remove from heat
14. stir in butter and parsley until butter melts
15. pour sauce over chicken and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Just made tonight, and it is very very nice.  I did put a little bit of crushed red pepper in the sauce for some heat, along with some butter to thicken a tad.  I also put some garlic powder along with pepper on the chicken before coating in flour. When my DH came home he could smell it outside, and really liked the aroma as well as how it tasted.

target.recipe_text:
vegetarian shepherd s pie

a twist on a fave comfort food

1. cook and mash then whip potatoes
2. with butter and salt and milk until they become light and fluffy
3. saute mushrooms and onions in some butter
4. add salt pepper too taste
5. mix mushrooms and onion with ground round place in bottom of baking dish layer with corn and carrots
6. top with whipped potatoes cook at 350 for about 40mins or until golden top
target.review: sent this to daughter in school..she said it was good and her roomates liked it too

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever chocolate chip cookies

these are our favorite. i usually make 1/2 and freeze the rest for later in the week when we run out.

1. mix flour , soda and salt in a bowl
2. set aside
3. cream together margarine and sugars
4. beat eggs into sugar mixture
5. add vanilla
6. beat until fluffy
7. add the dry ingredients
8. add chocolate chips
9. drop onto ungreased cookie sheet and bake at 350 for 8-10 minutes
10. cookies should be brown around the edges and will finish cooking on the sheet when removed from the oven
demonstrations.review: made with butter .so good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with asparagus and balsamic reduction

my mother made this for a dinner party i loved it so much she gave me the recipe

1. bring water to boil cook pasta
2. mean while
3. place balsamic in a pan cook at med heat untill it reduces to a syrup
4. chopp asparagus in about 1 inch pices place in frying pan with red onion and a bit of the oil and a bit of water cover alow to stream untill asparagus changes dark green and onion is cooked
5. drain pasta
6. top with asparagus and red onion then drizzel balsamic over and top with lots of parm
7. add salt peper to taste
demonstrations.review:
came out good !always looking for more recipes for asparagus 
oh used dry kraft parm

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white cake

this is a very moist and fluffy cake recipe that i got from my sister-in-law. it has never failed me yet. i have used it for different occasions and holidays and its always a big hit.

1. preheat oven to 375f degrees
2. mix butter& sugar until fluffy
3. add eggs& vanilla
4. add flour , little by little
5. add baking powder& salt
6. add milk , little by little until consistency is right
7. pour in a 9x13 or cupcake pan , lightly greased / sprayed& floured
8. bake for 30-33 minutes or until toothpick inserted into middle comes out clean
demonstrations.review: very lovely!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef in red wine mushroom sauce

another of ron kalenuiks creations that was to die for

1. in a large dutch oven or kettle , saut the beef in the butter and oil
2. add the vegetables and continue to cook until tender
3. sprinkle with flour , reduce the heat and cook for 5 minutes
4. add the wine , broth , tomato paste and seasonings
5. simmer for 50 minutes covered
6. serve over noodles
demonstrations.review: oh and i used olive oil not safflower

demonstrations.recipe_text:
double baked potatoes

these are amazing i make them all the time for dinner parties the mushroom and swiss go great together!!!

1. bake potatoes untill soft allow to cool
2. while potatoes cool saute mushrooms in about 2 table spoons of butter for about 4 mins sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. cut tops off potatoes and spoon out insides
4. into bowl
5. mix in butter cottage cheese swiss cheese and mushrooms add some more salt and pepper
6. place potatoe mixture in bag cut off corner and pipe contents back into potatoes shells or skins
7. top with grated parm and chives bake at 350 untill tops are golden brown
demonstrations.review:
so good i used ricotti
cheese instead of cottage cheese made it with chicken dish by blonder as well!!

target.recipe_text:
ex mother in law s pork chops with cream of mushroom

this was the one good memory i have of my first marriage- going to my ex-mother-in-law's and smelling this cooking! of course, i begged for her recipe and have been making it regularly ever since. her son was not a keeper for me, but her pork chops sure were! this recipe may be halved by using 4 pork chops, one can of soup, and two tablespoons of butter with the lawry's seasoning.

1. in skillet with melted butter , sprinkle both sides of pork chops with seasoned salt and seasoned pepper to taste and brown
2. put into 9 x 13 inch glass casserole and spoon mushroom soup and smear all over pork chops
3. cover and seal tightly with heavy aluminum foil and put into pre-heated 350 degree oven for 1 hour
4. remove foil last few minutes
5. serve over rice or noodles
6. yummmmm !
target.review: nice recipe.  I added green pepper rings and white onion rings on top of the porkchops then added the cream of mush soup.  Very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon   tomato presto pasta

one of my favorite pastas--quick and simple but taste great.  i found this from kraft and i make it on nights i'm in  a hurry.

1. cook bacon in skillet 5 minute or until bacon is crisp , stirring occasionally
2. drain skillet , leaving bacon in skillet
3. stir in cherry tomatoes
4. add cream cheese spread , milk and parmesan cheese
5. mix well
6. cook until hot and bubbly , stirring frequently
7. stir in pasta
demonstrations.review: Yum!  real quick too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
guinness burgers

beer - it's not just for drinking any more!

1. preheat oven to 400f degrees
2. combine meat , pepper , tabasco sauce , garlic , chili sauce , dry onion soup mix , and 1 ozs guinness
3. shape into 4 patties
4. bake at 400f until brown , about 10 minutes
5. baste with the remaining guinness
6. continue baking for an additional 10-15 minutes , until well done
7. add your favourite burger garnishes and trimmings
demonstrations.review: 5 for taste 4 because they fell apart.  Made them twice and second time around I cut the beer down to 1/4 cup.  They still tasted awsome and they didn't fall apart.  We grill hamburgs at my home.  these are wonderful and several friends have also enjoyed this recipe.  : )

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome baked pork chops

these chops remain moist and tender, and the sauce is to die for! you probably have all the ingredients in your kitchen to make this! serve these chops over rice!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. rinse pork chops , pat dry , and season with garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste
3. place the beaten eggs in a small bowl
4. dredge the pork chops lightly in flour , dip in the egg , and coat liberally with bread crumbs
5. heat the oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat
6. fry the pork chops 5 minutes per side , or until the breading appears well browned
7. transfer the chops to a 9 x 13 baking dish , and cover with foil
8. bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour
9. while baking , combine the cream of mushroom soup , milk and white wine in a medium bowl
10. after the pork chops have baked for an hour , cover them with the soup mixture
11. replace foil , and bake for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This dish was very good.  I added chicken broth instead of wine, worchestersire sauce, hot sauce and sliced a whole onion and green peppers and put on top.  cooked the sauce the whole time with the pork chops.  will definately make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
capt  phil s crab stuffed mushrooms

captain phil harris of "deadliest catch" made this recipe on the series "after the catch"; i thought they looked interesting. i would suggest garlic and herb cream cheese, aloette or boursin, though you may use what you have handy and suits you. i would think more shredded cheese would be necessary for 40 mushroom caps also. taken from discovery.com.

1. de-stem and scrape out the caps of domestic mushrooms
2. spray with oil
3. bake mushroom caps at 350 degrees for 5-7 minutes to soften
4. prepare the crabmeat stuffing: break up and coarsely chop the crabmeat
5. place in a bowl and blend with cream cheese
6. once thoroughly combined , spoon crab mixture into mushroom caps and sprinkle with shredded cheese
7. broil 6 inches from broiler until melted and lightly browned
8. watch carefully
demonstrations.review: ah ya!  really really good.  I added chopped green onion, 3 Tbl mayo, cut cream cheese down to 6 oz added 1/4 tsp cayanne pepper and 1/4 tsp lawrey seasoning salt and 1 tsp of lemon zest.  And I used the King Crab.  YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: excellent receipe..  I usually make my sauce first and I actually add a cup of pasta sauce to the meatball mixture and mix it in with everything else.  YUM!

target.recipe_text:
chai tea gift mix

what a nice (and easy!) gift to give at the holidays or any time of the year! uses dry ingredients (like powdered instant iced tea mix) that are easily found at the grocery store. i put my mix in a pretty glass container and tie with a ribbon with an instruction card attached. each recipe makes about 4 servings.

1. mix all together and place in pretty airtight container and attach these instructions: for each serving , place 3 to 4 heaping teaspoons mix in a cup
2. fill with 8 ounces very hot water
3. for creamier chai , use half milk and half water
target.review: I added nutmeg in addition to the cinnamon and cloves.  For an even creamier texture I make mine with hot milk.  This comes very close to what I buy at Trader Joes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Good banana-ey bread.  I added 1 cup of walnuts and some cinnamon.  Great flavor and very moist.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hidden valley bacon and cheddar dip

this is always a hit and is simple to make! hope you like ranch!!!!

1. mix ranch dip with sour cream
2. add bacon bits and cheese
3. mix together well
4. serve with your favorite chips
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good.  I cooked bacon for it.  I do not like bacon bits.  I would make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon cheddar bites

a great appetizer to have on hand. great as a side dish for soup too.

1. slice french bread into 1 inch slices
2. combine remaining ingredients and mix well
3. spread 1-2 tablespoons of topping onto each slice of bread
4. lay slices on a cookie sheet and bake at 400 degrees for 5-10 minutes or until topping is bubbling and starting to brown
5. or to make ahead: flash freeze bread on a cookie sheet before baking
6. transfer to large freezer bag and label
7. bake from frozen on a cookie sheet for 10-15 minutes as above
demonstrations.review: WOW!!!  Not one left.  First thing devoured.  Even the unbaked toppping was good as a dip for chips.  Five stars is not enough.  Best post I have eaten.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pistachio ambrosia  2

variation of pistachio ambrosia #22445 posted by barb t 3/14/2002. great summer salad, fluffy and lightly sweet. kids love it. found in a fundraiser cookbook.

1. in large bowl combine cool whip and pudding mix
2. blend well
3. add pineapple , marshmallows and nuts , again blending well
4. chill 2 hours
demonstrations.review: This tasted just like the stuff served at a family restaurant that closed.  It went over well at the gathering I took it to.  It's a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese yeast bread  bread machine

this is a wonderful tasting bread recipe with excellent texture that can also be used to make cinnamon rolls. yum!

1. place the ingredients in the pan in the order as suggested by your bread machine manufacturer
2. process on dough cycle
3. remove from machine , form into a loaf and place in greased 9x5 loaf pan
4. cover and let rise until doubled
5. bake in a 350 oven for approximately 35 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is an exceptionally good bread.  It is kind of dense.  I think if you cut back on the sugar you could use it for sandwiches.  Very easy to make.

target.recipe_text:
easy baked potato wedges

we love these potatoes, they are simple to make and taste great!

1. wash potatoes , cut into wedges
2. place potatoes skin down in a baking dish
3. mix the next 6 ingredients together and brush onto potatoes
4. bake at 350 for 1 hour
target.review: Easy is right!  I used red pepper instead of black.  It added a nice kick.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground beef and cabbage piroshki

nan

1. heat oven to 425 degrees
2. cook and stir ground beef in 10-inch skillet until brown
3. remove beef
4. drain fat from skillet
5. cook cabbage and onion in butter in same skillet over low heat , stirring occasionally , until cabbage is crisp-tender , about 20 minutes
6. reserve 1 tablespoon of the egg
7. stir remaining egg , the beef , cheese , mustard , salt , worcestershire sauce and pepper into cabbage mixture
8. reserve
9. prepare pastry for two crust pie as directed on package , except roll into rectangle , 18 x 12 inches
10. cut into six 6-inch squares
11. place on ungreased baking sheet
12. spoon 1 / 3 cup beef mixture onto each square
13. bring corners to center and pinch together
14. seal edges
15. blend water and reserved egg
16. brush over pastry
17. bake until golden brown , 14 to 16 minutes
18. serve with chili sauce
demonstrations.review: This was good!  I used Dijon mustard instead of yellow.  Also, I'm lazy.  I doubled the batch (and added a little bacon ... yum) and prepared it in a pie pan with top and bottom crust.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious drumsticks

you have to try these drumsticks! they truly are delicious.

1. heat the oven to 425 degrees
2. mix flour , salt , paprika and pepper in a bowl
3. dip chicken drumsticks into margarine
4. roll in flour mixture to coat
5. arrange in an ungreased square pan , 8x8x2 inches
6. bake uncovered until juice of chicken is no longer pink when centers of thickest pieces are cut , about 50 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very Good!  I used olive oil instead of butter, and added 4 T of tobasco to the olive oil.  Turned out great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rib rub that rocks

rub this savoury mixture on to a slab of ribs for your next barbecue!

1. mix em up
2. store in a tightly sealed container
3. fire up the grill !
demonstrations.review: Love it.  I use way less salt, but otherwise, it rocks!!!!  Oh, I frequently use brown sugar too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
freezer apple pie filling   oamc

this is a wonderful apple pie filling that you make in the fall when apples are in abundance.  during the winter months, just pull a package of pie filling from the freezer, defrost, and pour into your favorite pie crust.  this makes enough filling for 4 pies.

1. in a large bowl , toss apples with lemon juice and set aside
2. pour water into a dutch oven over medium heat
3. combine sugar , cornstarch , cinnamon , salt and nutmeg
4. add to water , stir well , and bring to a boil
5. boil for 2 minutes , stirring constantly
6. add apples and return to a boil
7. reduce heat , cover and simmer until apples are tender , about 6 to 8 minutes
8. cool for 30 minutes
9. ladle into 4 freezer containers or gallon freezer bags , leaving 1 / 2 inch headspace
10. cool at room temperature no longer than 1 1 / 2 hours
11. seal and freeze
12. can be stored for up to 12 months
13. you can also make pies right away
demonstrations.review: The recipe was awesome.  I double the apples (and the lemon) becuase I like more apples and less "juice" in my pies.  Very good!  Very easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato  cheese and bacon soup

this is in answer to a question on the threads, it is based on a recipe from the australian womens weekly

1. melt the butter in a large pan , add the bacon and cook until crisp
2. remove the bacon from the pan with a slotted spoon , leaving as much fat as possible
3. add the onion to the same pan and cook for 5 minutes , or until very soft and golden
4. add the paprika and cook for further 30 seconds
5. return the bacon to the pan and add the potato and stock
6. bring to the boil , then reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes or until the potatoes are very soft
7. stir or mash lightly to break up the potato
8. add the cheddar and stir well , until it is melted through
9. season with salt and pepper to taste and serve topped with a sprinkling of chopped chives
demonstrations.review: Excellent Soup!  Since we all like the skins, I just scrubbed the potatoes and then chopped them.  I will be making this again, and again ...

target.recipe_text:
oreo balls

my sister's co-worker brought these to a party and they were quite a hit. i don't know where the recipe came from originally.

"bark" is an artificial chocolate or vanilla candy coating/confectioner's coating used to make a treat called almond bark and can be found at most grocery stores near the chocolate chips. 

you can use chocolate chips and white chocolate chips if you don't have almond bark, but i have found that almond bark melts better and is easier to work with.

1. using a blender or hand held mixer , mix oreos and cream cheese together
2. roll into walnut size balls
3. chill for an hour
4. melt approximately 3 / 4 package of white almond bark
5. stick a toothpick in an oreo ball and dip it in the melted white almond bark
6. allow to harden on wax paper
7. takes about 15 minute
8. while waiting , melt about 1 / 4 package of chocolate almond bark
9. when oreo balls are no longer sticky to the touch , decorate with drizzles of chocolate and white almond bark
10. i just use a sandwich bag with a tiny hole cut in one corner to drizzle the almond bark
target.review: Made these fantastic little treats for our annual Halloween party.  I dipped them in white chocolate, then used the pouches of colored icing to make them look like blood-shot eye balls!  Creepy and yummy, this recipe is a keeper!  I plan to make them for my holiday cookie trays and drizzle red or green icing over the tops.  Just a note, they are extremely rich.  I made them a bit smaller than a golf ball, but will make them much smaller for the holiday trays.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cucumber and garbanzo bean salad

a friend of mine gave me this recipe. i love having this during the summer time.

1. in a medium bowl , combine beans , cucumber , onion , parsley and olives
2. in another bowl or jar combine remaining ingredients , mix well
3. pour over salad and toss
4. serve immediately or chill for up to 24 hours
demonstrations.review: Delicious!!  Whipped this up this morning for dinner tonight and I couldn't stay out of it...taste tested it at least three times....LOL!  I used two cans of beans as I read the ingredient list wrong and already had two cans opened when I realized there should have only been one can, used vidalia onion since I had it on hand already, and as I'm not a fan of green olives, I substituted a small can of sliced black olives.  I feel the changes were minimal, but the result was fantastic!  I'm adding this to my permanent collection and am sure it will be pulled out often for weekends at the lake when we all eat outside together!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick buttermilk cinnamon bread

this quick and easy bread recipe allows you to share a good-looking loaf with a friend. or make five mini loaves for the church bazarr or for freezing.

1. mix flour , baking soda and salt in a large bowl
2. in a small bowl combine oil and sugar
3. add buttermilk and eggs and mix well
4. stir into dry ingredients just until moistened
5. fill 2 greased 8"x4"x2" loaf pans about 1 / 3 full
6. combine cinnamon and remaining 1 cup sugar
7. sprinkle half over the batter
8. top with remaining batter and cinnamon-sugar
9. swirl batter with a knife
10. sprinkle with nuts
11. bake at 350 , 45-55 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean
12. cool in pans for 10 minutes before removing to a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Really good warm out of the oven!  Couple of changes that I made were increasing the salt to 1-1/2 teaspoons and I also added 1 teaspoon of cinnamon to the batter itself, in addition to the cinnamon that was swirled throughout.  I sprayed my loaf pans with Pam and also lined the bottoms with parchment for added ease in removing the loaves.  While they were still hot I drizzled a glaze over the top that consisted of powdered sugar and French Vanilla Coffee-Mate creamer.  Loved the ease of just mixing the batter up by hand really quick and not needing the mixer!  This recipe has been added to my book of keepers!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
better than chicken and dumplings

this dish is baked in a 9x13 casserole, and the dumplings sort of make themselves. it is easy and delicious.
it appeared in a local community paper some time ago.

1. combine the first 6 ingredients and bring to a boil
2. reduce heat to simmer
3. cook until chicken is done
4. remove from broth and cool
5. you will use 2 c of this broth in the preparation !
6. remove from bones if needed
7. saute the vegetables , except peas in a little butter or oil , until soft
8. melt the 1 / 4 cup butter and pour into the 9x13 dish , to grease the bottom
9. cut or tear the chicken into pieces and place on top of the melted butter
10. mix flour and milk
11. pour over chicken
12. mix soup , 2 cups of the broth , the sauteed vegetables and peas
13. pour over the top
14. do not stir !
15. bake at 400 degrees for 30-35 minute or until top is brown
16. to make this realy fast use rotisserie chicken and canned broth !
demonstrations.review: Very good indeed!  I come from a family who has always done the type of dumplings that you roll out and cut.  This was not the same type of thing, but still very good!  DH and DD both immediately said "chicken pot pie?" when I set it in front of them, and that was ok too!  Everyone ate and enjoyed this dish so that makes it a winner around here.  I used a rotisserie chicken from Sam's Club as I decided to try this at the last minute.  I don't keep self rising flour on hand so I used one of the ones listed here on 'Zaar and that worked well too!  Thanks for a great dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
big grandma s best peanut butter cookies

this is my husband's grandmother's recipe that is cherished by the family. they are the best cookie that melts in your mouth. they don't have the normal peanut butter fork crossing...but more of a crackled sugar type cookie... my husband comes from a huge family - and these are one of the cherished recipes!!

1. cream together the sugars , crisco , peanut butter
2. add the eggs and vanilla
3. sift the dry ingredients together and add gradually until blended well
4. roll into tablespoon size balls
5. roll cookie dough balls into sugar
6. place on cookie sheets- do not mash with fork in normal "peanut butter cookie" fashion !
7. bake at 350 oven for 11-13 minutes
demonstrations.review: Loved these cookies!!!  Like a previous reviewer of these cookies I didn't have  butter flavored Crisco on hand so I used half Crisco and half butter.  To portion the cookies I used the medium sized Pampered Chef scoop and got 40 good sized cookies out of it.  For cookie trays during the holidays I'll switch that to the smaller PC scoop that I normally use.  These were a great size for lunches, though!  I baked them for 13 minutes and they were melt-in-your-mouth delicious!  I'll be keeping this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern corn and hominy saute  ww core

i am one of those people who likes hominy, particularly in southwestern soups and stews. came across this side dish in a new weight watchers cookbook and decided that it would soon be making an appearance on my dinner table.

1. remove the frozen corn from the freezer to begin defrosting
2. to prepare the poblano chiles , place them directly over gas flame on your stove
3. allow the skin to char and blister before turning using long tongs
4. once all sides are charred , about five minutes , toss the peppers in a resealable bag and close
5. set aside about ten minutes to allow the heat to steam the chiles
6. once cooled , peel and seed the peppers , and give them rough chop
7. heat the vegetable oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat
8. add the onions and cook for two or three minutes until the onions are tender
9. stir in the garlic , cumin and epazote / oregano and continue to cook another 30 seconds
10. add in the corn and hominy , stirring occasionally , and cook for two minutes
11. stir in the poblanos and salt to taste
12. cook an additional two or three minutes until the everything is heated through
13. remove from heat and mix in the cilantro and lime juice
14. serve with lime wedges
demonstrations.review: Great recipe!  I substituted green bell peppers for the poblanos as I don't like quite as much heat, but it was delicious.  WW flex....3 points per 1 cup serving!

target.recipe_text:
copycat olive garden minestrone soup by todd wilbur

from http://www.topsecretrecipes.com it's finally here! what everyone's been waiting for! just in time for winter, this soup is sure to warm your soul with it's savory flavor and wonderful aroma. i've asked many an olive garden waiter for this recipe, but none gave it to me in detail. one waiter told me the secret ingredient was to add a little red wine to the stock, but i'll leave that up to you to try.

1. heat three tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat in a large soup pot
2. saute onion , celery , garlic , green beans , and zucchini in the oil for 5 minutes or until onions begin to turn translucent
3. add vegetable broth to pot , plus drained tomatoes , beans , carrot , hot water , and spices
4. bring soup to a boil , then reduce heat and allow to simmer for 20 minutes
5. add spinach leaves and pasta and cook for an additional 20 minutes or until desired consistency
6. makes about eight 1 1 / 2 cup servings
target.review: DELICIOUS.  I've made this recipe several times over. It taste like the real thing. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: I loved this.  I used chicken thighs instead and omitted the hot chilli pepper.  Still came out great.  This is so simple & sooooo delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
why i joined zaar carrot cake

on october 2, 2001, i discovered the recipezaar web site. i immediately joined so i could post a request for a recipe i had lost. in less than an hour, i had a reply: this recipe. unfortunately, i never posted it into the database -- until now. my mistake. this cake was the reason i joined, and the friendly response i received was the reason i stayed!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour a 9x13 inch pan
3. mix flour , baking soda , baking powder , salt and cinnamon
4. make a well in the center and add sugar , oil , eggs and vanilla
5. mix with wooden spoon until smooth
6. stir in carrots , coconut , walnuts and pineapple
7. pour into 9x13 inch pan and bake for about 45 minutes
8. don't panic , the centre will sink a little
9. allow to cool
10. when cool , ice the cake
11. you can certainly use your favourite cream cheese frosting to ice this cake , but the one i've included is highly recommended
12. to make the frosting: cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
13. add the icing sugar and beat until creamy
demonstrations.review: This cake was awesome!  One of my new favorite recipes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: This recipe was nice. However, the flavor lacked depth.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
demonstrations.review: I tried this recipe for Thanksgiving. I wanted something a little different than the usual pumpkin pie. It came out beautifully.  Delicious! Everyone polished it off. :) Will make this again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry coffee cake

good for a special occasion breakfast.

1. in a mixing bowl , add the flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
2. stir to mix
3. in a second bowl , add the egg , milk and butter
4. stir to mix
5. add to dry ingredients and stir just until moistened
6. pour mixture into a greased 8-inch square baking dish
7. place strawberries evenly over the top of batter
8. to make the topping: combine the flour and sugar in a bowl
9. with a pastry blender , cut in the butter until consistency of coarse crumbs
10. stir in pecans
11. sprinkle mixture evenly over the strawberries
12. bake at 375 for 30-35 minutes or until wooden pick comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Very delicious and simple to throw together.

target.recipe_text:
new year s oyster stew recipe

this was in taste of home and while the contributor's name wasn't given she said: "my husband is a former member of the air force's thunderbird team, and i developed this recipe after he invited the whole team to our house on short notice for an informal dinner. it was very easy-it was done in 45 minutes, and it turned out to be the best oyster stew i'd ever made!"

1. in a dutch oven , saute leeks in butter for 10 minutes or until tender
2. add the potatoes , water and bouillon
3. cover and simmer 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender
4. cool
5. transfer to a blender
6. cover and process until blended
7. return to the pan
8. stir in the milk , cream , oysters , cayenne , salt and pepper
9. cook on low until heated through
10. garnish with parsley
11. yield: 12 servings
target.review: I found this quite delicious! I had one 7 oz. can of oysters, so I adjusted accordingly. I used the juice from them, to add more flavor to the broth, and I skipped the cayenne. Thanks for posting, it is  a nice change from the usual milk, cream, butter and oysters. Made for Everyday is a Holiday, 2012

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jackie s stroganoff

nan

1. sprinkle meat with salt and pepper and place in the crockpot
2. mix the remaining ingredients , except the flour , butter and sour cream and stir in with the beef
3. cover and cook on low 7 to 8 hours
4. place the crockpot on high and stir in flour and butter which have been blended together
5. stir until thickened
6. turn off the heat and add the sour cream
demonstrations.review: No bad, but needs wok. The only change I made was that I browned the meat in a frying pan first, sauteed the onions and garlic. In my opinion, crock pot meats should be browned first, then put in, much more flavor is developed  that way. The flavor was good, but it needs more thickener than 2 T. of flour. The sauce was very thin. If you like crock pot cooking, give it a try! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
elementary school chili

keen5 posted this in a request thread for school chili.  i asked her to post it to the the site so i could save it to my cookbook because i think it sounds delicious and she was kind enough to let me post it as my first recipe on recipezaar!  thanks, keen5!!

1. brown the ground chuck in skillet and pour off excess grease
2. stir in flour and brown sugar
3. combine tomatoes , tomato paste , and chili beans
4. place all ingredients into a 2 quart cooking pot , adding the onions , chili powder and salt
5. cook over low heat for at least 2 hours
demonstrations.review: I should have gotten a clue from the title! We thought it too sweet, and I did doctor it up a touch with more chili powder and a dash of cumin. I baked  it in the oven in my dutch oven, uncovered,  for four hours as it was quite thin, and we like chili chunky and thick. Still, it would be a great chili for children, they'd gobble it up, I'm sure! Thanks for posting! Made for Fall PAC 2012

demonstrations.recipe_text:
huevos rancheros aussie style

i ate these delicious oven baked eggs in a little cafe very recently while on a few days away. i did my best to recreate them for brunch this morning, and think mine, made with home grown tomatoes and no thoughts about profit, were better! probably nothing like the real thing, but a yummy breakfast, brunch, lunch or dinner dish!

1. preheat oven to 350f or 190c
2. heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion and chorizo until the onion is well softened
3. add the garlic and green pepper , cook a couple of minutes stirring , then add the tomatoes , chilli and brown sugar
4. season to taste with salt and pepper
5. cook for around 20 minutes , until the tomatoes have broken up and cooked down a little , then add the cooked diced potato and lime juice and cook a couple of minutes more
6. spoon into 4 , two cup ramekins or gratin dishes , break 2 eggs into each and top each with about 1 / 4 cup of cheese
7. bake until the eggs are done to your liking starting to check after about 10 minutes
8. serve with the sourdough toast
demonstrations.review: This dish was very good! I only have one cup ramekins, so that is what I used. Also, I had soft chorizo on hand, so the veggies were coated with it, very good! Next time I will omit the sugar, but otherwise, a great breakfast, thanks for posting! Made for Make My recipe Reunion, 2012

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wow that was easy chocolate mousse

i learned this recipe from my husband's grandmother and my kids beg me for it almost every week.

1. combine the milk , sugar , and espresso powder in a small sauce pan
2. heat until the milk is hot but do not to a boiling
3. place the chocolate in a blender and pour in the hot milk and blend for 10 seconds
4. add the egg whites and blend for 1 minute
5. pour into 4 small serving dishes and chill for at least 3 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: This is really yummy! It has great, deep flavor, and was so simple. I got three servings, but that is the perfect amount for us! It didn't have the airy quality I associate with mousse, but still, very good! Thanks for posting! Made for Fall PAC 2012

demonstrations.recipe_text:
danish coffee cream puff muffins

from the joy of muffins - the international muffin cook book. here's what the intro says about this recipe. danish desserts make ample use of cream, sour cream and butter from denmark's thriving dairies. a walk through copenhagen's tivoli gardens is hardly complete without sampling the luxurious creamy danish desserts which inspired this light sour cream muffin with the mocha cream filling. try it with dark scandinavian coffee for a special dessert treat.

1. in a small bowl mix together the cream cheese , instant coffee , powdered sugar and chocolate
2. set aside
3. in a large bowl , mix the flour , baking powder , soda and salt
4. in another bowl , whisk eggs with sour cream , sugar and vanilla
5. make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the egg , sour cream mixture , stirring for 10 seconds
6. dough will be quite thick
7. spoon batter into greased muffin pans to about one-third full
8. then drop a heaping teaspoonful of the cream cheese mixture into the center of each muffin , being sure it doesn't touch the edges of the pan
9. top with the remaining batter , making sure it covers the filling
10. place into preheated oven on center rack and bake until done
11. bake at 375 degrees 18 to 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Yum, these were so good! I used cocoa instead of chopped chocolate. Also, I mixed the wet with the dry ingredients and let sit for 10 mn. so the flour could absorb the liquid. Thanks for posting a real keeper! Made for Name that Ingredient tag game

target.recipe_text:
szechuan chicken

why go out for chinese food when it is this easy? serve with rice or asian noodles. to slice the chicken thin, freeze for 20 minutes or so first or if you are using chicken from the freezer, slice before it is completely thawed.  it isn't as hot as you would expect from "szechuan"--if you want it spicy hot--add more crushed red chilies.

1. with knife held in slanting position , almost parallel to cutting surface , cut each chicken breast half crosswise into 1 / 2-inch thick slices
2. in medium bowl , combine soy sauce , sherry , cornstarch , ginger , sugar , and crushed red pepper
3. add chicken , tossing to coat
4. in wok or large non-stick skillet , heat 1 tablespoon oil over medium-high heat until very hot
5. add green onions and red and green peppers and cook , stirring frequently , until vegetables are tender-crisp , 2 to 3 minutes
6. with slotted spoon transfer vegetables to bowl
7. increase heat to high and add remaining 1 tablespoon oil to skillet
8. heat until very hot
9. add chicken mixture and stir-fry until chicken looses its pink color throughout , 2 to 3 minutes
10. return vegetables to pan
11. heat through
12. to serve , transfer chicken and vegetables to warm platter and sprinkle with peanuts
target.review: My whole family loved this recipe. My six-year-old is asking for it again! I made it exactly as written, but I doubled the whole batch. It was wonderful and easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
n  y  c  irish soda bread

classic irish soda bread

1. in a mixing bowl , combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , brown sugar and teaspoon of salt
2. cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs
3. combine 1 beaten egg , raisins and buttermilk
4. add to mixture above and stir until just moistened
5. on a lightly floured surface , knead gently for 12 strokes
6. on a greased baking sheet , shape the mixture into a 6 inch round loaf and cut a cross in the top
7. brush with the other beaten egg
8. bake at 375f for 35 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: This bread has a wonderful flavor and texture. It is quite easy to make. I added an extra egg and 1/4 cup more flour to adjust for my altitude (7,200 feet). I cooked it on my baking stone, and it was perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican enchilada sauce

i got this recipe from by grmil who was born and raised in mexico city. the secret to its flavor is the cocoa

1. combine all dry ingredients in a small bowl
2. stirring constantly , slowly add enough of the water to make a thin paste
3. pour into pan and add rest of water
4. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until mixture thickens
5. stir in tomato sauce
6. use in your favorite enchilada recipe
7. the amounts on the ingredients are very flexible
8. for instance , if i am feeding my kids who do not like"spicy" , i will halve the chili powder and double the tomato sauce
9. experiment to suit your taste , but don't leave out the cocoa
10. for a quick meal , we will soften a corn tortilla in a bit of hot oil , drag it through the sauce , and lay it flat on a plate
11. cover it with grated cheddar cheese , sprinkle with chopped onions and sliced black olives
12. then cover with another softened sauced tortilla and melt the cheese in the microwave for 1 minute on high
demonstrations.review: This enchilada sauce is so easy to prepare and tastes delicious. I will be using this from now on instead of canned sauce with many additives.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
warm blueberry cobbler

this is a simple recipe,most ingredients we all have around the kitchen.8) (6 ingredients!)

1. heat oven to 375
2. put berries in a 10x6x2 inch baking dish
3. sprinkle with lemon juice
4. mix the sugar , flour , and egg , stirring until resembles coarse meal
5. spread this over the berries
6. drizzle melted butter over berries
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. serve warm with a dallop of whipped cream on side , if you choose
demonstrations.review: I used frozen blueberries,  doubled the recipe and substituted one cup of whole wheat flour for one cup of white. It was delicious and very easy to make. My family could not get enough! I highly recommend this cobbler especially with a large scoop of vanilla icecream.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hummus amongus

there's a large middle eastern population in bayridge brooklyn and amazing restaurants line the avenues...hummus is served with every dish on the menu...it's one of my favorite things in the whole wide world...if you haven't tried it, please do. i think you'll love it!

1. drain beans
2. reserve water
3. in a food processor or blender add beans and all the ingredients
4. process until smooth
5. if mixture is too thick , add some of the reserved liquid from the beans to dilute to a desired consistency
6. serve at room temperature with pita bread , grilled pork , lamb or chicken
demonstrations.review: We love this hummus! I used dried beans (about 1/2 pound) cooked and reserved the cooking liquid for the moisture. We also added more garlic (four cloves total) because we are garlic lovers. Easy to make and very tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bubble up peach cobbler

easy -- the crust rises to the top while baking. always a hit!

1. cream butter and 1 / 2 cup of the white sugar
2. combine flour , baking powder and salt and add to the creamed mixture then add the milk and mix well
3. pour batter into buttered 8x8 baking dish
4. top with peach slices , then pour all of the reserved peach juice over the peaches
5. top with the remaining sugars and cinnamon
6. bake for 45 minutes at 375 degrees
demonstrations.review: I reduced the syrup when making this recipe and still had too much juice! I also adjusted the baking powder for our altitude. It is quite delicious, though a little sweet for us. I will reduce the sugar next time. Very easy to make and tasted wonderful right out of the oven with vanilla icecream.

target.recipe_text:
simple bacon wrapped stuffed chicken breasts

super easy and delicious. 4 ingredients

1. pound 6 boneless skinless chicken breasts until 1 / 4 inch thick
2. season with pepper
3. top each piece with a slice of ham and a slice of muenster cheese
4. wrap them in bundles with 2 strips of bacon for each breast
5. bake in shallow baking dish at 350 degrees for 40-45 minutes
6. garnish with parsley
target.review: This was fantastic.  I did a few different sized chicken breasts and the cheese seemed to have melted out of the smaller ones, but it was still really good.  I cooked it for 45 minutes and then put it under the broiler for 4 minutes to crisp up the bacon.  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground beef stuffed green bell peppers with cheese

we had these not too long ago and we both decided that they needed a little more seasoning. we put a little hot pepper sauce on them and they were much better. i would probably include 2 teaspoons in the meat mix the next time that i make them.

1. cut off the tops of green peppers
2. discard seeds and membranes
3. chop enough of the tops to make 1 / 4 cup , set aside
4. cook the whole green peppers , uncovered in boiling water for about 5 minutes
5. invert to drain well
6. sprinkle insides of the peppers lightly with salt
7. in a skillet cook ground beef , onion and 1 / 4 cup chopped pepper till meat is browned and vegetables are tender
8. drain off excess fat
9. add drained tomatoes , salt , worcestershire , and a dash of pepper
10. in a separate pot put water bring to boil add rice cook until rice is soft
11. if needed add more water
12. add rice to beef mixture
13. stir in cheese
14. stuff peppers with meat mixture
15. place in a 10x6x2 baking dish
16. bake , covered in a 350 degree oven for 30 minutes
17. in the last 5 minutes add any remaining cheese to the top of the peppers
demonstrations.review: This was delicious and easy!  I made several changes due to what I had in my pantry/fridge.  I used 1 lb ground seasoned chicken, 1 small yellow onion, 1/2 cup of green pepper and  added 1/4 cup of fresh parsley and a touch of garlic salt.   For the cheese, I did 1/2 cup mozzarella and half cup of grated parmesan.  I did not have tin foil, so I put 2 inches of water at the bottom of my baking dish.  In the last 5 minutes of cooking, I put 2 tablespoons of sauce over each pepper.  During that 5 min, I put 2 more tablespoons of sauce into an empty bowls and served each pepper on the sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pioneer woman s not your grannys mac   cheese

from pioneer woman's blog. i haven't made this yet but it looks positively scrumptious! please visit her blog for some mouth-watering pictures and recipes.

1. boil pasta until al dente
2. in a large skillet , add olive oil and saute garlic and vegetables over medium heat for a couple of minutes
3. add in canned chilies and stir around , then turn off heat
4. drain pasta and add it to skillet
5. pour on cream , add cheese , then add salt and pepper to taste and stir gently
6. at the end , add 2 tablespoons butter and stir again
7. check seasonings and serve
8. serve with juicy steak , with grilled shrimp , chicken , or on its own
9. itll change your life for the better
demonstrations.review: I used a whole box of elbow macaroni, 1/4 cup of roasted red peppers and eliminated the corn.  I used 2 cups of monterey jack cheese, and 1 1/4 cups of cream.  So good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrot  onion and celery soup by me

a yummy veggie soup. i came up with this after trying another recipe like it on try-foods intl. inc. i just changed it to my liking.

1. slice the carrots fine , mince the onion , slice the celery thin
2. in a big pot saute the onion in butter until softened
3. stir in the carrot , celery and tarragon
4. add broth and wine
5. bring to a boil
6. simmer until done
demonstrations.review: added some fresh parsley and 3/4 cup of alphabet pasta.  Great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot artichoke chicken and brown rice

this recipe is from the welcome home nursing newsletter. this recipe is acceptable for diabetic/"sugar buster" diets.

1. place ingredients , including preferred seasonings , into crock pot early in the morning
2. cook on low / slow heat
3. it's ready to pour over cooked brown rice 8 hours later
demonstrations.review:
I loved this!  I did make some changes.  I added some peas to the mix and used one can of cream of mushroom and also one of cream of chicken.  I served it over campanelle pasta.
I cooked it for 7.5 hours on low and it was perfect.  The chicken was so tender!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuscan white bean   sausage stew

this is a modified recipe from the pampered chef 29 minutes to dinner cookbook. we really enjoyed it.

1. remove casings from sausage
2. place in stockpot with olive oil and cook over medium heat until lightly browned , breaking sausage apart as it cooks
3. add carrots , onion , celery , garlic and italian seasoning to pot , cooking 5-7 minutes or until vegetables start to brown
4. stir tomatoes , tomato paste , arugala , broth and beans into sausage / veggie mixture
5. simmer on medium-low heat 15 to 20 minutes or under vegetables are tender
6. serve with grated fresh parmesan cheese and warm bread
demonstrations.review: Great pretty qucik and easy soup.  I realized last minute that I only had a red onion, no tomato paste, or arugula, and used stewed tomatoes and only one can of white beans.  Even with all these modifications, still fantastic!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot whole chicken

tender, fall-off-the-bone chicken! skip the overnight refrigeration if you are in a hurry. for variety, eliminate the onion and substitute a quartered lemon or two, stuffed into the chicken cavity.  chef shapeweaver had a good suggestion:  use fajita seasoning mix #28011 as another variation.  thanks!  the standard size slow cookers are a bit too small and a whole chicken won't fit.  you'll need a 6-quart slow cooker for this recipe.

1. in a small bowl , combine the spices
2. remove any giblets from chicken and clean chicken
3. rub spice mixture onto the chicken
4. place in resealable plastic bag and refrigerate overnight
5. when ready to cook , put chopped onion in bottom of crock pot
6. add chicken
7. no liquid is needed , the chicken will make its own juices
8. cook on low 4-8 hours
target.review:
This recipe is WILDLY OVER RATED.
It's beyond simple to make but tastes like any garden variety stewed chicken. Nothing to write home about here. Might be a way to cook chicken while you prepare a much more interesting sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish  matter of fact peas   mushy peas

you can also buy these peas canned but they are quite expensive and are so easy to make. these peas are also common in england as pub fare. i love them served with good bangers (sausages) and a green saladwhat we call baking soda in canada is  known elsewhere as bicarbonate of soda.

1. put the peas in a bowl , add baking soda , pour on the boiling water and soak overnight
2. next day drain and barely cover the peas with water , bring to a boil and simmer until tender and soft apprx 15-20 minutes , drain
3. add salt pepper pinch of sugar and the butter , stir and serve
demonstrations.review: Extremely easy but definitely much better with Tabasco for zip !!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple corn casserole

a simple to make, rich side dish--as much a staple at my family gatherings as the paper plates!

1. combine everything but the cheddar cheese
2. pour into greased 8-inch casserole
3. bake at 425 for 45 minutes
4. top with cheddar and bake and additional 5 min or until cheese is melted
5. let stand for 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This cooked up fine with no problems. I REALLY DISLIKED the flavor. I found it unpleasantly sweet (even with the cheddar on top) and the baked corn was gummy. After a piece or two I pulled off the cheddar, ate that, and threw out the rest !!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
momosita s shepherd s pie

i'm dying to make this again next week! this is adapted from a recipe on allrecipes.com. it's my favorite recipe because it has a lot of veggies and a unique twist with the carrot layer below the potatoes. if you are throwing calorie counts to the wind, make this truly decadent and bake it in a butter pie crust (trader joe's is phenomenal!).

1. preheat oven to 375
2. bring a large pot of salted water to a boil
3. add carrots and cook until tender but still firm , about 15 minutes
4. brown ground beef with onions and garlic while carrots are cooking
5. when carrots are finished , drain , mash and set aside
6. add flour to ground beef mixture and mix well
7. add ketchup , wocestershire , stock , and cook to thicken
8. taste and add seasoned salt to desired taste
9. add mixed veggies and simmer until warmed through
10. pour into a 2 quart casserole or deep glass pie dish and top with a layer of mashed carrots , then the mashed potatoes
11. bake at 375 for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: As Gordon Ramsey said when someone served him a so called "Shepherd's Pie" made with beef, " How can you call it shepherd's pie when you make it with beef? I don't know what the hell THIS is ! "

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast  sticky  chicken

beautiful and delicious, this incredibly moist roasted chicken puts kenny roger's roasters, boston market, and other rotisserie style chickens to shame! please don't let the word 

1. blend all spices together and set aside
2. remove neck and giblets from chicken cavity , rinse well inside and out , and pat dry with paper towels
3. rub with spice mixture , both inside and out , then stuff cavity with onions
4. wrap in a resealable"food grade" plastic bag , tie closed , and refrigerate overnight
5. remove from plastic bag and place in a shallow baking pan
6. roast uncovered in a 250 f oven 5 hours
7. if the chicken contains a pop-up thermometer , ignore it
8. this recipe is safe
9. according to the united states department of agriculture food safety and inspection service , a whole chicken should reach an internal temperature of 180 f
10. for more info check out their"thermy" campign web site !
11. baste with drippings every 30 minutes after the first hour
12. let rest for 10 minutes before carving
demonstrations.review: Cooking at 250 and opening the oven door every 30 min to baste probably significantly prolongs the cooking time since heat keeps being lost which is a bigger deal at low temperatures.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
portuguese paella

i love the blend of flavors in this dish.  this is a hearty one dish meal. the secret spice is the saffron.  saffron is expensive, but you must add it or the taste of authentic paella is lost.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. sprinkle chicken with rosemary , 1 / 2 teaspoon salt , and black pepper
3. heat oil in a large oven proof nonstick skillet or paella pan over medium-high heat
4. add chicken
5. cook for 3 minutes on each side or until lightly browned
6. remove chicken from pan
7. cover and keep warm
8. add chourice and cook until lightly browned
9. add onion and bell pepper
10. cook for 7 minutes , stirring constantly
11. add rice , tomato , paprika , saffron and garlic
12. cook for 1 minute stirring constantly
13. return chicken to pan
14. add broth and 1 / 4 teaspoon of salt
15. bring to boil
16. wrap handle of pan with foil , cover pan
17. bake at 400f for 10 minutes
18. stir in shrimp , asparagus , and peas
19. cover and bake an additional 5 minutes or until shrimp are no longer translucent
demonstrations.review: Don't make this without a trial run. Cooked this in the oven an extra 5 min. since the shrimp weren't done. Some of the arborio rice came out overcooked and mushy, while some was undercooked and chalky. Next time I'll make it entirely on the stove so it can be stirred frequently and tested.

target.recipe_text:
george s whole wheat pizza dough

simple whole wheat pizza dough, made using a mixer with a dough hook.

1. combine the yeast and the water , stir until dissolved
2. add the remaining ingredients to a bowl
3. add the yeast mixture and mix using a dough hook
4. knead dough until it forms a nice ball , using extra flour if necessary
5. let rest for at least 1 / 2 hour
6. bake at 450 for 12-15 minutes or until golden brown
target.review: Our family dinner party made pizza's on the grill last night and your pizza crust was a hit!  (the only change I made from the ingredient list was using italian seasonings instead of oregano and thyme seperately).  We doubled the recipe and let it rise a second time after making individual sized pizza dough balls.  I had to refrigerate them since they were prepared in the morning.  Don't know if that made them easier to work with or if it was the wheat flour in your dough, but it was a breeze to shape them compared to the white pizza dough I bought from the store.  (wasn't as elastic-y and kept its shape when we formed them on our floured table.)  We cooked the crust first by brushing each side with olive oil and grilled them over med low heat.  After that we added our toppings and grilled them one last time on low to melt the cheese! Yum!  We ended up with one extra dough ball so we threw that on the grill as an appetizer bread.  After flipping it, we brushed it with butter and garlic salt, and sprinkled it with parmesan cheese.  It was perfect dipping into our homemade pizza sauce!  Thanks for a great recipe that will be used over and over again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked cranberry oatmeal

you can substitute cherries, blueberries or raisins for the dried cranberries.

1. preheat the oven to 350f degrees
2. coat a 9 in square pan with nonstick spray
3. in a large saucepan , bring the milk , brown sugar , margarine , and cinnamon to a boil
4. meanwhile , in a large mixing bowl , mix together the oats , chopped apple , cranberries , and nuts
5. spread evenly into the prepared pan
6. when the milk mixture begins to boil , pour out evenly over the oatmeal mixture
7. bake uncovered for 30-35 minutes , ore until the liquid has been absorbed and the oatmeal is tender
8. cut the mixture into 6 servings , scooping each out into a cereal bowl
9. garnish with a sliced apple and serve with a pitcher of milk
demonstrations.review: This is my favorite recipe for oatmeal in the morning!  It has a great balance of cinnamon, sweetness and crunch from the nuts.  The only change I've done is 2% milk and butter instead of margarine.  Thank you, Tish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
another shrimp scampi

i changed a recipe i got from a cookbook by giuliano hazan. this makes a yummy sauce that is great with crusty bread. when i want to add pasta, i usually double the recipe except for the amount of shrimp.

1. put olive oil and garlic in a large skillet over medium heat and cook slowly to infuse the oil with the garlic , but do not burn garlic
2. add red pepper flakes
3. raise the heat to medium high
4. add shrimp and season with a little salt
5. cook until shrimp is almost done
6. add wine , cook until alcohol is burned off , about 1 minute
7. add the lemon juice and butter to finish
8. garnish with parsley
demonstrations.review: this was really good!  the only thing I did differently was adding a couple dashes of cayenne pepper instead of the pepper flakes and it came out great!  Thank you

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate iced coffee

a treat from southern living........yum!  for zaar world tour purposes, please classify as midatlantic for the hershey syrup.  thanks!

1. bring water and coffee to a boil in a saucepan
2. remove from heat and let stand 10 minutes
3. pour mixture through a fine wire-mesh strainer into a bowl , discarding coffee grounds
4. stir sugar and cinnamon into coffee until sugar dissolves
5. let cool
6. stir in half and half and chocolate syrup
7. chill 2 hours
8. serve over ice
demonstrations.review:
Very good!  We have tried a few different recipes so far, and I like the cinnamon flavor.
Thanks Lori!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey mustard pecan chicken thighs

we love anything honey-mustard. this is great way to prepare chicken thighs. needs to marinate for 2 hours.

1. place chicken thighs in a shallow dish
2. in a small bowl , combine the salt , black pepper , cayenne , and dried thyme
3. sprinkle evenly over the chicken thighs
4. in another bowl , add 1 / 2 cup honey , 1 / 2 cup mustard , and garlic
5. stir to combine
6. pour mixture over the chicken
7. cover and refrigerate for 2 hours
8. take chicken out of marinade and discard marinade
9. dredge chicken in pecans then place chicken on a lightly greased rack in a foil lined broiler pan
10. bake at 375 degrees for 40 minutes or until chicken is done
11. in a small bowl , combine the remaining honey , the remaining mustard , and the curry
12. serve the sauce with the chicken
demonstrations.review: I just made this last nite and it came out great!  My pecan covering started turning a little dark towards the end, but I think it would have been fine if I didn't cook it for the full 40 minutes.  Will definately make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey mustard salad dressing iii

nan

1. mix all ingredients in bowl
2. serve
3. simply add more honey if desired
demonstrations.review: *Y*U*M*!  There's no otherway to say it!  This is so easy to just throw together and use! I had like 2 jars of ranch in the fridge and was wanting something different.  This hit the spot.  I liked how the cayenne gave it a little kick!  I also used Dijon mustard in place of regular mustard.  Thans Tonkcats!

target.recipe_text:
best ever grilled chicken kebabs

this recipe is very simple, very easy, and tastes better than anything you'll find in a restaurant. seriously!

1. place chicken breast pieces in a bowl
2. pour in enough olive oil to completely cover pieces , squeeze the lemon over them , and then add the garlic , oregano , basil , rosemary , salt , and a couple of twists of cracked pepper
3. cover and refrigerate overnight
4. assemble kebabs , and grill until chicken is no longer pink , about 10-15 minutes depending on your grill
5. don't overcook them , though
target.review: Thanks for the great recipe Alex.  We cut the chicken into strips and threaded them on skewers and grilled veggies separately.  We thought this was a dynamite recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker stroganoff

very easy and wonderful stroganoff recipe for the lazy cook!

1. place beef in bottom of cooker and season with salt and pepper to taste
2. add onion , soup , mushrooms , parsley , chives , broth , wine , garlic and worcestershire
3. add to cooker
4. cook on low for 7-8 hours
5. one hour before serving , stir in sour cream
6. i usually don't add this step if adding the egg noodles because they will thicken the sauce
7. if using frozen egg noodles , par boil for 10 minutes and add to sauce
8. cook on low for 1 hr
demonstrations.review: Good flavor; quick and easy to fix. I'll definitely make this again.  Thanks Deb, I'm always looking for slow cooker recipes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tko sangria punch  non alcoholic

this is a great way to cool down after exercising, jogging, or just any time! feel free to use "lite" products, or sugar-free. this is great for guests who do not care to drink, and for children. crystal light comes in a ton of flavors, and the powdered mix is packaged in 6, 1/2 oz. little tubs, so you can make each tub separately, if desired. try all of the flavors!

1. empty drink mix into large pitcher
2. add cranberry juice cocktail , orange juice and lime juice
3. stir until drink mix is completely dissolved
4. stir in club soda and fruit
5. serve over ice cubes in tall glasses
demonstrations.review: What a great punch recipe.  I've made it at least four times this summer and it's only July 3rd.  Everyone really enjoys it.  The flavor is not too sweet and it's very refreshing; I wouldn't change a thing.  It also doubles well and is so quick to put together.  Thanks for sharing, Fluffster!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gentle thanksgiving mushroom gravy

from the farm animal rights movement's "recipes for a gentle thanksgiving." www.gentlethanksgiving.org

1. melt margarine in a saucepan over medium heat
2. saute mushrooms and onions lightly
3. add flour , stirring constantly until frothy
4. while stirring , slowly add vegetable stock to achieve desired consistency
5. add spices
6. bring to a boil , stirring constantly , then turn down heat and let thicken
demonstrations.review: I've made this gravy twice and the flavor is very nice.  It is easy to put together as well.  The second time I added about 1/4 cup diced celery which added even more flavor.  I did find it too salty with the addition of salt because of the salt in the veggie bouillon I used (instead of stock).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin streusel bundt cake

this is a libby's recipe and is it good! really impressive when it is cut and the streusel filling peeks through. great for the holidays.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour a 12 cup bundt pan
3. streusel: combine brown sugar , spices in a small bowl
4. cut in butter until crumbly
5. set aside
6. cake: add flour , cinnamon , salt and baking soda in a medium bowl
7. in a large bowl beat butter and sugar until fluffy
8. add and beat in eggs one at a time
9. add pumpkin , sour cream and vanilla
10. beat well
11. beat in flour mixture
12. spoon half of the batter into the pan
13. sprinkle streursel mixture over batter but don't let it touch the sides of the pan
14. top with remaining batter , making sure batter does touch the sides of the pan
15. bake for 55-60 minutes
16. cool in the pan for 30 minutes
17. turn out onto wire racks in order to cool completely
18. turn out on serving plate
19. drizzle with glaze
demonstrations.review: This was a big hit at our office potluck; lots of compliments.  Next time I will bake the cake for the full 60 minutes.  I see how important it is for the streusel not to touch the sides---it did in one small place and was stuck there.  A little prodding and it came out fine; very pretty.  Thanks Aroostook!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
piquant green beans

one of my favorite ways to have green beans. i could eat the whole pan and forget the rest of dinner! i really could!

1. prepare the green beans for cooking by rinsing and removing
2. steam green beans 15-20 minutes or until tender
3. in a large skillet heat fat or oil and cook onion until caramelized
4. add garlic
5. add green beans to skillet and stir thoroughly
6. in a small bowl mix together vinegar and sugar and pour over beans , stirring well
7. season to taste with salt and pepper
8. mix in bacon crumbles
9. serve
demonstrations.review: My husband and I really enjoyed this side dish.  To cut down a bit on the vinegar flavor I used Rice Vinegar.  I also carmelized the onions as Sue suggested; this made the dish very flavorful with a mild onion taste, so the beans weren't overshadowed.   Thanks Sue L, I'll make this again.

target.recipe_text:
baked caramel french toast

make this casserole the night before and just pop it in the oven for your breakfast or brunch. when turned over and out of pan, a caramel layer will have formed. delicious!

1. boil butter , maple syrup and brown sugar together for 1 minute
2. pour into greased 9 x 13 pan
3. slice french bread and put a layer of slices over the caramel mixture
4. beat rest of ingredients together and pour over the bread
5. refrigerate covered overnight
6. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
7. turn pieces over onto serving platter and caramel will be on top
target.review: Made this for the college girls weekend. Easy to prepare, (after a fun evening),and they all enjoyed it, even the non-breakfast eaters.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
