3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: This was very easy, and I had everything in the pantry. I used a jalapeno, and added crushed red pepper flakes. I let the drummies simmer longer, closer to an hour. The flavor was great,and if you don't want to eat the skin, they peeled off really easily. (but the skin is really tasty).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon rice w  peas   green onions

nan

1. combine 1 3 / 4 cups water , rice , and salt in large saucepan
2. cook until just cooked-- do not overcook
3. fluff with fork
4. cool
5. cook peas in medium saucepan of boiling salted water 1 minute
6. drain
7. rinse under cold water
8. drain
9. heat oil in large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
10. add all but 2 tablespoons green onions
11. saut 30 seconds
12. add rice and saut until heated through , stirring to break pieces , about 4 minutes
13. add peas , lemon juice , parsley , and lemon peel
14. saut 2 minutes to blend flavors
15. garnish with remaining green onions and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: excellent rice variation, very fresh tasting with the lemon and scallions.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled portobello mushroom sandwiches with basil aioli

aioli is a garlic mayonnaise, popular in southern france, and tasty as a spread on sandwiches. this sandwich is hearty, filling, and packed with flavor! you can use minced garlic from the jar where it calls for the garlic in the aioli, but you can definitely tell the difference. i don't have a press, so i just mince the garlic with a knife. this recipe is from "the barbecue! bible" by steven raichlen. it is based on using an outdoor grill, but this is a direct-heat method, so you could also use a grill pan (what i do), and it works great too.

1. make the basil aioli: combine the mayonnaise , garlic , basil , and lemon juice in a small bowl and whisk to mix
2. season with salt and pepper to taste
3. for the sandwiches: cut the stems off the portobello mushrooms flush with the mushroom caps
4. using the
5. combine the olive oil and balsamic vinegar in a small bowl and whisk to mix
6. generously brush the portobello caps and tomato slices with some of the oil and vinegar mixture and season them with salt and pepper
7. set up the grill for direct grilling and preheat to high
8. when ready to cook , place a vegetable grate on the hot grill and preheat the vegetable grate for 5 minutes
9. arrange the portobello caps , rounded side down , and the tomato slices on the hot grate and grill , turning with a spatula , until nicely browned and soft , 3 to 6 minutes per side
10. brush the vegetables once or twice as they cook with the oil and vinegar mixture
11. spread the insides of the rolls or buns with basil aioli
12. add the grilled mushrooms , the tomato slices , and the arugula , and enjoy
demonstrations.review:
Very easy, loved the oil/vinegar combo on the mushrooms.
The basil aioli would be great on a grilled burger or chicken breast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mahogany beef stew

you will not believe the deeply satisfying flavour of this stew. this is our favourite wintry stew dish - comfort food to the max.  the cooking time is more or less accurate, but it really depends on the cut of meat used -  not everyone used chuck, and then, not all chuck is the same!  you really have to poke and prod and taste to get it to where you want it...but that's what cooking is all about, isn't it? ;-)

1. heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in heavy large pot over high heat
2. sprinkle meat with salt and pepper
3. add meat to pot
4. saut until brown on all sides , about 10 minutes
5. push meat to sides of pot
6. reduce heat to medium
7. add 2 tablespoons oil to pot
8. add onions
9. saut until golden brown , about 15 minutes
10. mix meat into onions
11. add 1 cup wine , tomatoes with juices , garlic , herbs , hoisin sauce , and bay leaves
12. bring to boil
13. reduce heat to low , cover pot and simmer 45 minutes , stirring occasionally
14. add carrots and 1 cup wine
15. cover
16. simmer 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
17. uncover , increase heat to high
18. boil until sauce is slightly thickened , stirring occasionally , about 15 minutes longer
19. reduce heat to medium , add cornstarch mixture and simmer until sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 8 minutes
20. discard bay leaves
21. season stew with salt and pepper
22. transfer stew to large bowl
23. sprinkle with parsley and serve
24. excellent with buttered egg noodles
demonstrations.review: Thanks for the suggestions Evelyn. I followed the recipe, but used left over teriyaki marinaded fondue meat. This was easy, and I had all the ingredients on hand. I was tempted to add broth, but didn't. After simmering with the carrots, there was plenty of liquid. I served in a bowl, with bread.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled chicken with coriander cilantro sauce

a simple but delish thai grilled chicken. cook time excludes marinate time.

1. mix the marinade ingredients together , pour over chicken and leave it in the fridge to marinate for at least 30 minutes
2. while chicken is in the fridge , prepare the sauce
3. heat vinegar , sugar in a saucepan over low heat , and stir until dissolved
4. bring to boil and simmer until the sauce thickens , and a syrup forms
5. pour into a bowl
6. preheat grill
7. place chicken about 20cm / 8 inches from the heat , and cook both sides until coloured
8. serve with coriander / cilantro sauce and fragrant rice
demonstrations.review: Excellent flavors! I was looking for a more "exciting" way to prepare chicken breasts. I added a bit more garlic, and was out of white rice, so served it on rice noodles. I used a grill pan, and grilled indoors. I will be making this again!

target.recipe_text:
just like loaded baked potatoes casserole

this is an awesome low-carb version of loaded baked potatoes, and tastes far better than any version of mock potatoes that i have tried. in fact, this dish is soooo good, you will not believe it!  i do not remember where i got this recipe, but it is a fabulous side to any low-carb meal. you will be pleased, i promise! yum! yum!

1. pre-heat oven to 350
2. chop cooked cauliflower into very small pieces
3. mix sour cream , 1 / 2 of the green onions , 1 / 2 of the cheese , 1 / 2 of the bacon , and salt and pepper to taste in medium bowl
4. stir in the cauliflower
5. place in medium baking dish and sprinkle remaining cheese and bacon on top
6. bake for 20 minutes
7. sprinkle the remaining green onions on top just before serving
target.review: I also left out the green onions, but it was still very good. I am always looking for new ways to prepare cauliflower and we'll definitely have this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
boerewors   south african sausage

this is a must on every barbecue whether it be coal, gas or electric!  when i have not been able to get the skins to produce sausages, i have shaped this mixture into patties and have served it in burger form - something my american family and friends have raved over!

1. mix everything very well together
2. stuff casings if used or shape into patties for the best hamburgers in the world !
3. barbecue or pan-fry 4 minutes on each side
demonstrations.review: Wonderful! Reminded me of home :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best blueberry crisp

this is wonderful served warm with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream --- you will love this crisp!

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. prepare an 11 x 7-inch baking dish
3. spread the blueberries in the bottom of the prepared baking pan
4. in a small saucepan over medium heat combine the sugar , cornstarch , water and 2-3 tbsp lemon juice
5. cook and stir until thick and clear , then add in the vanilla
6. pour over , then gently stir in the cooked mixture with the blueberries
7. in a bowl combine the flour with oats , brown sugar and cinnamon
8. add in the melted butter
9. mix until crumbly
10. sprinkle over the top of blueberries
11. bake for 30-35 minutes , or until blueberry mixture bubbles and the topping is brown
12. serve with ice cream-- enjoy !
demonstrations.review: We really liked this. I used frozen blueberries and it turned out great, but I think it would have been even better if I used fresh blueberries.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortilla crusted tilapia

i'm not fond of fish, but even i like this dish.  tilapia is mild, and the spicy crust is very appealing.  i like to make the crumb crust in bulk and freeze in meal sized amounts.  then this becomes a super quick weeknight meal.

1. preheat oven to 375f coat a baking sheet with cooking spray
2. place tortilla pieces , pepper , lime juice , cilantro and spices in blender
3. pulse until the mixture is uniform small crumbs
4. spread on plate
5. beat egg in shallow dish
6. dip each fillet in egg , then in crumbs , patting crumbs to adhere
7. place on baking sheet
8. bake until fish flakes , about 15 minutes depending on thickness of fillets
demonstrations.review: We liked this a lot. I don't really like the taste of cumin, so I used a 1/2 tsp coriander instead. My husband said that it wasn't "spicy" enough and he usually doesn't like anything too spicy. Perhaps I'll double the spices next time, but it was still very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: We liked this recipe, but I also found it a little bland the first time  I tried it. The next time I made it I added salt and black pepper to taste, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, 2 tsp coriander, 2 tsp sweet chili powder and 1/2 a hot chili pepper (we like the heat). I sprinkled half of the additional spices on the chicken and added the rest to the salsa. The extra spices definitely improved the taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate bonbons  brigadeiros    brazil

this from "cuisines of portuguese encounters", in which the author gives recipes she had during travelling thru portugal and its former colonies.  this is a brazilian recipe, named for a famous brazilian air force commander in the 1940's.  he was a chocoholic.  often served at birthday parties and other festivities.  i haven't made it yet.

1. in medium pan , combine milk and cocoa powder
2. cook over low , stirring constantly with a wooden spoon , until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan , about 20 minutes
3. add butter and salt
4. mix thoroughly before removing from heat
5. when mixture is cool , rub hands with butter and shape into 1-inch balls
6. roll in chocolate sprinkles
7. place in mini paper cupcake forms
8. store in fridge until served
demonstrations.review: These are rich, chocolaty and delicious. I made them for my Christmas parcels and they were a hit!

target.recipe_text:
zucchini and rice casserole

this is the first zucchini recipe i ever tasted and it is still my absolute favorite after all of these years. thanks mom for discovering it.

1. cook zucchini in boiling , salted water , 2-3 minutes
2. drain well
3. saute beef , onions , garlic and seasonings until onions are transparent
4. stir in rice and tomato sauce
5. blend cottage cheese and egg in separate bowl
6. arrange 1 / 2 zucchini slices in a buttered casserole
7. spoon meat-rice mixture , then spread with cottage cheese mixture
8. top with remaining zucchini slices
9. sprinkle on cheddar cheese
10. bake at 350 degrees for 20-25 minutes
target.review: Tastes pretty good, but the prep time is really underestimated. Figure the full 50 minutes to get all of the slicing, chopping, browning & cooking done; then yes, about 10 minutes to assemble it. Also, 25 minutes isn't really long enough for baking, given the bulk of it and the fact that you need to be sure that the egg mixture cooks thoroughly. I baked it for 35 minutes, and it could have used 10 more to have the egg mixture really set. As to the ingredient measurements, I assumed that 1 qt. of zucchini was about 4 cups; to balance the amounts of the other ingredients, I wound up using about 5 cups.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy one bowl carrot corn and rice bake

prep time does not include shredding the carrots, please adjust all amounts to taste, you can add in more cheese if desired.

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 2-quart baking dish
3. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients
4. mix well to combine
5. transfer to prepared baking dish
6. bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Definitely simple to make, and I like it after I fiddled a couple of things a bit. The first time I made it, I had used some rather elderly carrots, and they came out tough and chewy; so I tried it again with better carrots, and the result was much better. (although the carrots were still pretty chewy--if you want them soft, probably steam them a little before mixing them into the casserole) I also found from the first time that I wanted more cheesy taste. I had used sharp cheddar rather than Velveeta, but I still upped the amount to 2 c. the second time. I also added 1/4 tsp. of dry mustard, a trick my mother taught me. You don't taste the mustard per se, but it zips up the taste of the cheese. I used milk rather than half-and-half, left out the onions (just don't like them) and definitely no extra salt. The biggest adjustment I had to make was in the cooking time. It was absolutely not done in 45 min. The first time, I used a 2 1/2-qt. pyrex dish; the second time I switched to a 9-in. square aluminum pan, hoping that spreading it out a bit would help it cook faster. Both times it took about 65 min. to get it done in the center.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
auntie barb s moist chocolate cake

my auntie barb always makes the best chocolate cake and it is so moist and delicious. if you are looking for the ultimate chocolate cake, this is the one that you have to make!

1. in a bowl combine the sugar and margarine well and then add the buttermilk , vinegar , vanilla and eggs
2. using a 2 cup measuring cup put the cocoa in and pour the boiling water overtop and mix well
3. add this to the above mixture
4. combine the flour and baking soda and add to the cocoa mixture
5. the batter will be thin
6. pour the batter into a greased and floured 9 x 13 pan
7. bake a 350 for 30-40 minutes or when tooth pick inserted comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Very moist, dense cake, almost like a heavy sponge cake texture. It has a surprisingly chocolatey taste, given the small amount of cocoa powder. I frosted it with No-Cook Chocolate Frosting (recipe#88276) for a nice, rich-tasting double chocolate treat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon cheese bars

these are fabulous for parties or just for snacking. very light but very delicious!

1. mix dry cake mix , 1 egg , and 1 / 3 cup vegetable oil until crumbly
2. reserve 1 cup of the mixture
3. pat remaining mixture in a lightly sprayed 9 by 13 in pan
4. bake 15 minutes at 350 degrees , and let cool
5. in a bowl , beat cheese , sugar , lemon juice , and 1 egg until smooth
6. spread over baked layer
7. sprinkle with reserved crumb mixture
8. bake 15-25 minutes at 350 degrees
9. let cool and cut into bars
demonstrations.review: Pleasant-tasting, but rather bland. To get a real lemony flavor, I'd double the amount of lemon in the cheese mixture, and maybe use a lemon cake mix, rather than yellow. I also thought about making it using the specified amount of lemon and a Betty Crocker chocolate fudge cake mix. It wouldn't exactly be "lemon" cheese bars, but I bet it would be good. Also, I wound up baking it in a 9x9 inch pan, because I couldn't imagine how the cheese mixture could spread over 9x13 inches; even in the 9x9 pan, it was fairly thin. Another time, I think I would double the amounts on the ingredients of the cheese mixture and do everything else as specified, including the pan size. If so, it might be necessary to up the second baking time a little to be sure the cheese mixture got cooked through.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
choctaw pumpkin cake

a native american recipe, this unusual combination of pumpkin & chocolate makes a delicious cake. i never frost it because it doesn't last long enough!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a large mixing bowl , combine flour , sugar , soda , cinnamon and cocoa
3. add pumpkin , oil , eggs , vanilla and blend well
4. pour into greased and floured bundt pan or ring mold and bake 40-50 minutes
5. frost with creamy chocolate frosting if you like
demonstrations.review: I'm posting this as an fyi, rather than as a review, because I made a major change in the recipe. When I read this recipe, I thought it sounded good, but surely the 1 1/2 cups of oil must be a typo. Since it already has one review that doesn't mention changing any ingredients, I guess not. But it's way too much oil for me, especially given the amount of pumpkin and the 4 eggs. When I made it, I used only 3/4 c. of oil, and it was still very moist and good. I may even go to 1/2 cup next time. Also, I don't have a bundt pan, so I used a 9x13 pan and baked it for 30-35 min. Due to careless reading of the ingredient list, I put in 2 Tbsp. of cocoa instead of 1. It was still very good, but the pumpkin was totally overpowered, so next time I'll be more careful--and I don't recommend that particular change.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
audrey s special stew

this is a recipe that i came up with when i was a teenager. we lived in a rural area where you made meals out of what was in the freezer or pantry. this was the results of one of those experiments. my family loves this dish. it is time consuming, but it can also be placed in a slow cooker and left to cook on its own.

1. brown meat in oil
2. drain
3. add remaining ingredients , except potatoes , carrots , celery and cooked rice
4. simmer for 2 hours
5. add vegetables and contine to cook until vegetables are tender
6. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: This made a very tasty stew, although I did make a few changes and would suggest one more. I didn't serve it over rice. It was fine with potatoes, and I can imagine leaving out the potatoes and serving the meat/carrot mixture over rice, but not both potatoes and rice. So one thing I did was cut the water to 1 c., since there would be no rice to absorb it. When it finished cooking, the liquid was awfully thin, so I made a paste of 3 Tbsp. of flour and about 1/2 c. of water, stirred it in and cooked it for a few minutes. It thickened the liquid to a nice gravy consistency. I didn't use the onion or the celery, as I don't like either one-with them you might need a little more water. I don't buy barbeque sauce; I have a recipe I use for the infrequent times I make barbequed beef. If anyone else doesn't want to buy a whole bottle of sauce for 1/4 c., I substituted 1 Tbsp. brown sugar for the 1 tsp. sugar, upped the catsup to 1/2 c. and added 1/2 tsp. basil and 1/4 tsp. chili powder (1/2 tsp. if you like hotter sauce), and the result tasted fine to me. I omitted the salt-not needed with so many already salty flavorings. I was a little leery of the amount of mustard, and next time I will cut that to 1 Tbsp., as I felt it overpowered the taste of the other flavorings. I only cooked the meat for 1 hour before adding the veggies, but wound up having to cook the stew about 40 more minutes to get the pototoes done.

target.recipe_text:
the best apple pie muffins ever

i got this  recipe from a friend.  i make these often and take them to many potlucks, office parties, the cottage, picnics, children's lunch and the list goes on. recipe from the cookbook "just the best."

1. cinnamon could be added to the batter
2. topping: in a small bowl toss together sugar , flour , butter and cinnamon until crumbly
3. set aside
4. muffins: in a large bowl whisk together brown sugar , oil , egg and vanilla until smooth
5. in a separate bowl , sift together flour , soda and salt
6. stir oil mixture into flour mixture alternately with buttermilk
7. fold in apples , mixing just until combined
8. spoon into greased muffin cups filling 3 / 4 full
9. sprinkle topping over evenly
10. bake at 350f for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown and tops spring back
target.review: I LOVED these!  I made them in mini muffin pans and used 1 1/4 cup self rising flour and 1 1/4 cup wheat flour and left our the baking soda.  I also substituded 1/2 cup oil for apple sauce and used 1/4 cup oil instead. They were chewy and moist.  I got many complements!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s crispy potato and green onion pancakes  latkes

this recipe goes back 30 years or more, my family *loves* these! you can make these ahead of time and then freeze, just cool and place on a large baking sheet to freeze, when frozen stack in a freezer container or pop them into a freezer bag, to reheat and re-crisp, defrost the pancakes then place in a 400 degree oven for about 8 minutes turn over then continue baking until crisp, i strongly suggest to double the recipe these will be half gone before they even make it to the table! i like to add in some cayenne pepper and a bit of garlic powder but that is optional --- yield is only estimated you should get between 20-23 pancakes for this recipe, to make things easier use your processor to grate the potatoes, plan ahead the grated potatoes need to soak for a minimum of 8-24 hours or even up to 2 days to remove some of the starch, the longer soaking time the crispier they will be --- serve with sour cream :)

1. grate the potatoes using a the coarse side if the grater or use a food processor
2. place into a large bowl and cover with cold water
3. allow the grated potatoes to soak for at least a minimum of 8 hours or even up to 2 days
4. using your hands firmly squeeze handfuls of the grated potatoes to remove as much liquid as possible , then place in a large mixing bowl
5. add in egg , flour , seasoned salt and pepper
6. mix well with a wooden spoon , then add in the green onions and parsley
7. heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat
8. place a heaping tablespoonful of the potato mixture into the hot skillet and using a fork , flatten slightly
9. sprinkle with more salt if desired
10. place only a few pancakes in the pan , careful not to over crowd
11. cook until golden and crisp on both sides adding in more oil if needed)
12. repeat with remaining potato mixture
13. delicious !
demonstrations.review: As always, Kittencal's recipes are fantastic!  These were great potato pancakes.  Actually followed the recipe this time...not something I do often.  My husband couldn't get enough!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cold veggie pizza

this is perfect for a summer afternoon with some sangria!!!

1. press crescent rolls flat on a cookie sheet
2. bake as directed on package
3. mix together cream cheese , mayo , and ranch dip pack
4. chop up vegetables
5. spread cream cheese mixture on baked crescent rolls
6. put chopped up vegetables evenly over top
7. sprinkle cheese on top of vegetables
8. refridgerate 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I had this recipe and lost it.  It was a perfect match. My co-workers loved it as did my BF. It was gone in no time!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
x ceptionally healthy eggs benedict

don't rate this one as if it were the original version with 30 grams of fat but i do think you'll like it! i love eggs benedict so played around with six different light versions to come up with the best!

1. in a skillet over medium heat , lightly brown canadian bacon or ham in cooking spray
2. remove from skillet and keep warm
3. meanwhile , combine lemon yogurt , dry mustard , salt and cayenne in a small saucepan and whisk gently on low heat until warm and smooth
4. fill a large skillet with 2 inches of water and 1 tablespoon vinegar
5. bring water to a boil and reduce heat to a low temperature where the water is still consistently boiling but very low
6. crack one egg into a small dish and gently pour it into the skillet , doing the same for each additional egg , one by one
7. simmer for 3-5 minutes until desired doneness , spooning hot water over the yolk until slightly opaque
8. in the meantime , toast the english muffin
9. place a toasted muffin half on each plate with a piece of ham on top
10. when the timer rings , carefully remove eggs from the water with a slotted spoon , letting the excess water drain away
11. place on top of ham
12. drizzle sauce over the top
13. garnish with parsley and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Used sour cream, fresh lemon and brown mustard.  It satisfied my craving for Eggs Benedict.  Nice!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon mocha biscotti

delicious italian biscotti recipe that tastes like a cup of fresh cappuccino. great as a christmas gift too. just wrap a biscotto in cellophane and tie with a bow.

1. preheat oven to 325f on convection bake setting
2. combine butter , sugars and espresso or coffee granules in a large bowl and beat with an electric mixer until light and fluffy
3. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
4. add vanilla and mix briefly
5. add flour , baking powder , salt and cinnamon and mix until well blended
6. fold in pecans , chocolate morsels and cinnamon chips
7. line a baking sheet with parchment paper
8. scoop dough out onto paper and form into a large rectangle , -inch thick
9. bake 25 minutes , or until firm
10. remove from oven and cool 10 minutes
11. use a serrated knife to cut the dough into -inch thick slices
12. place on a parchment-lined baking sheet and return to the oven for 8 minutes
13. turn and bake 8 minutes more
14. remove from oven and cool completely on wire racks before storing in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: This is the best biscotti recipe  I have found.  They are wonderful.  I was a little worried that I overbaked them the second time around, as they were pretty dark in color.  I baked them for about 11 minutes on each side.  I may reduce that time when I make them in a few days (since I know they will all be gone before Christmas!) I also used wet hands to form the dough and made two loaves instead of one.  I got 22 biscotti plus the ends. FANTASTIC!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baklava salmon  salmon with honey  butter  walnuts  and mustard

one of my friends deemed this "baklava salmon" and the name stuck. the salmon & mustard go well with the honey, butter, and walnuts. we usually serve this with rice and steamed carrots or broccoli.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. line shallow roasting pan with non-stick aluminum foil , or spray with non-stick pan spray
3. in small bowl , blend butter , mustard , and honey , set aside
4. in another bowl , mix together bread crumbs , nuts , and parsley
5. place salmon fillets on prepared pan , sprinkle with salt and pepper , and brush with honey-mustard mixture
6. sprinkle tops with crumb / nut mixture
7. if any remains , press into sides of salmon
8. bake salmon 12-15 minutes in preheated oven , or until it flakes easily with a fork
9. serve with lime or lemon wedge
demonstrations.review: Wow!  I don't think I have ever had better salmon.  I generally don't like salmon, as it has always been a bit too "fishy" for me.  This recipe balanced out that fishy flavor.  It was FANTASTIC.  I didn't change a thing.

target.recipe_text:
disney s french toast

this stuff is killer good, and if you follow the whole recipe you'll probably have leftovers. not to worry, freezes well. this is not every day eating, but enjoy it when you can.

1. mix all ingredients in a large bowl
2. mix coating in a smaller bowl
3. dip bread into first mixture and fry in vegetable oil on the stove
4. cook 3 minutes on each side
5. when golden brown , remove , pat with paper towel to remove excess oil
6. sprinkle bread with coating
7. to freeze: cool and then store in ziplock freezer bags
8. to reheat: we just put one piece in the microwave at a time for about 30 seconds per side until heated through
target.review: I halved the recipe and it turned out great!  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
5 cheese macaroni and cheese

decadent! everyone raves about this dish. so cheesey and full of flavor. good southern comfort food. wonderful with pork chops or fried chicken. originally i got the base of this recipe from nell carter on some tv show. i had to spice it up a bit.

1. cook 2 cups macaroni noodles in salted boiling water for only about 6 minutes > do not over cook as they will continue to cook in the oven
2. while noodles are cooking: mix eggs , milk , cream cheese , melted butter and spices together in large mixing bowl
3. drain noodles
4. add noodles and all the shredded cheese to egg mixture
5. pour into a greased 9x13 baking pan
6. bake in a 325 degree oven for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Normally, when I have to alter a recipe based off what I have on hand or my preferences I won't rate it; however, I have been searching for a mac and cheese recipe with real flavor for so long that I wouldn't want this one to go unnoticed!!   I followed all directions and quantities with the exception of the types of cheese which is why I feel this is such a great flexible recipe!!  I didn't have any muenster and I don't like swiss cheese so I added additional cheddar, velveeta and a little parmesan to equal the 5 cups cheese required.  The spice quantities are right on....I was tempted to add more seasonings since the recipes I have tried in the past have been bland but I'm glad I stuck to it!!  I also thought the amount of pasta seemed scant for the amount of sauce since it looked like it was drowning so I added an additonal cup of cooked pasta and after tasting see that the amount called for was perfet even though my own results were AWESOME!!  This is a great recipe because not only am I sure it tastes great as is, but I can be the official guinea pig that cheese substituions can be made and it will still be the best tasting mac and cheese I have found!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy chocolate peanut butter pretzel balls

these are absolutely addictive!  sweet and salty with lots of crunch, and very easy to make.  these should probably be stored in the fridge to keep from going soft or you could probably coat in an extra layer of chocolate if you wanted to go through the trouble.

1. in a double boiler or microwave melt the chocolate and peanut butter
2. if microwaving , start with a minute and then add additional time until melted
3. be careful not to burn the chocolate
4. mix in the pretzels and rice cereal until everything is coated and well incorporated
5. drop by the teaspoonful onto a lined cookie sheet and place in the fridge
6. once hardened , you can transfer to a bag or container
7. these are best stored in the fridge
demonstrations.review: These are really good and easy to make!!  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter graham cookies

nan

1. in a large bowl , combine peanut butter , graham cracker crumbs , confectioners' sugar , and corn syrup
2. mix until smooth
3. shape into 1-inch balls
4. place on waxed paper-lined cookie sheets
5. drizzle melted chocolate over balls or roll in colored sprinkles
6. store covered in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: These were very good!  The texture of the graham cracker crumbs with the peanut butter is great!  I halved the recipe without any issues.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chip cookie dough dip

i'm not sure if it taste like chocolate chip cookie dough exactly because of the cream cheese, but it is very good. you can serve this dip with graham crackers, vanilla wafer cookies or pretzels. i love it for when i need a sweet dessert but don't have the time to bake cookies. cook time is cooling time for the butter mixture.

1. in a small saucepan , melt the butter with the brown sugar over medium heat
2. stir continuously , until the brown sugar dissolves
3. remove from heat , whisk in the vanilla and set aside to cool
4. beat the cream cheese and confectioner's sugar for 1 minute
5. slowly beat in the cooled butter mixture and beat again for another minute
6. stir in the chocolate chips and nuts , if using
7. pour into a serving bowl and refrigerate
8. garnish with additional chocolate chips or nuts , if you choose
demonstrations.review: I made this for a tailgate party and it was well received.  The cream cheese gives it almost a chocolate chip cheesecake flavor.  We thought it was best on Vanilla Wafers.  I used fat free cream cheese and reduced fat butter and I don't think it harmed the outcome at all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of red lobster cheddar bay biscuits by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com. the cold butter is the secret. it's not included in other copy cat recipes.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. combine bisquick and cold butter
3. don't combine too thoroughly
4. there should be small chunks of butter about the size of peas
5. add cheddar , milk and 1 / 4 tsp garlic
6. mix by hand until combined , but don't over mix
7. drop 9 equal portions onto greased cookie sheet
8. bake for 15-17 minutes or until tops are light brown
9. melt 2 tbsp butter in a bowl
10. stir in 1 / 2 tsp garlic powder and parsley flakes
11. use a pastry brush to spread garlic butter over tops of biscuits
demonstrations.review: WOW!  These are great and come together in no time!  The only thing I may try next time is to sprinkle some Old Bay seasoning on them, though they are phenomenal as is!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s fluffy omelet

of course you can double this and make it in a large skillet! you can use any favorite cheese you desire, cheddar is good also, i prefer monterey jack for omelets! the trick to a fluffy omelet is the baking powder, so do not omit and don't overcook the eggs! --- also see my recipe#251220

1. in a small bowl whisk together eggs , baking powder , cream , green onions , salt and pepper until frothy
2. heat an 8-inch skillet over medium heat until your hands feel warm when held about 2-inches above the surface
3. add in butter and swirl to coat the bottom of the pan evenly
4. pour the whisked eggs into the skillet
5. let set slightly
6. using a heat-proof spatula , push eggs from edge towards the center
7. tilt pan to let egg fill the spaces
8. repeat until omelet if just set
9. sprinkle the grated cheese down the center of the omelet
10. using the same spatula , gently fold the omelet over the cheese
11. tilt skillet and slide the filled omelet onto a serving plate
target.review: Oh yeah, I just went ahead and memorized this one! In our house we all like different things in our eggs so I always just add whatever's in the fridge, from bacon to broccoli. But I never thought about monterey jack rather than cheddar. That was too good! I hope I can cut this for my daughter down to 2 eggs, 1/16 t. baking powder and 1 T cream, and a smaller pan of course. Thanks for another brilliant recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic bread topped with crab meat and spinach

this i made as an appetizer but you sure can make a meal of it! open faced hot sandwich.
if you can't find old bay there's
dib's old bay seasoning recipe #11791 is posted here on zaar i never made it but it looks good. or you can try mine not old bay but real good.cajun spice rub mix recipe recipe #92066

1. preheat oven to broil
2. place all slices of bread on a cookie sheet in a single layer
3. place under broil to lightly brown one side flip lightly brown other side
4. mix all topping ingredients together gentle
5. top the bread with the topping mixture
6. sprinkle with cheese and drizzle lightly with oil
7. place under broiler a couple minutes till bubbly and lightly browned
demonstrations.review: This was really good! I enjoyed a different way to have crab, but my husband thought it was too fishy for him. He sure did eat his share though! I may split this in 1/2 and make crab for me and chicken for him and use fresh baby spinach. I always have it on hand and this would be a great way to use up the last bit when it starts to wilt. And I have to say that scrumptious photo is what got me to this recipe! Thanks Rita!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: My husband & I both really liked this. The red pepper and season salt were different from how I usually make potato soup and we loved the added flavor. I may try melting the cream cheese before adding it to the soup. Even cut in small little pieces it did not melt in the pot. Oh, and I used peeled & cubed potatoes. We like chunky soups so I would never even try shredded potatoes! I will be making this regularly and may try adding heavy cream when I add the melted cream cheese! Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
restaurant style egg drop soup

i added in a small amount of soy sauce and some cayenne pepper, but that is optional, this is really good! you can double this recipe if desired!

1. reserve 3 / 4 cup broth and pour the remainder into a medium saucepan
2. add in salt , ginger , garlic and chives
3. bring to a rolling boil
4. in a cup or small bowl stir together the remaining broth and cornstarch until smooth
5. set aside
6. in another small bowl whisk the eggs and the egg yolk together until well combined
7. while the soup is boiling drizzle the egg mixture a small amount at a time into the boiling soup
8. once the eggs have all been dropped into the soup , reduce to a light simmer
9. slowly and add in the cornstarch / broth mixture mixing continuously
10. delicious !
demonstrations.review: My first atempt at egg drop soup and it came out really well. I think I may need some more practice 'dropping' the eggs but the taste was really good. I want to learn how to get the eggs to be long flat ribbons like at the restaraunts. Mine were small little specks and a few small chunks as I lost my grip a couple of times while 'drizzling.' For me this was the perfect consistency - I don't like it thick at all. I like more of a broth for egg drop soup. Oh, I too add soy sauce, but just to my bowl. I may come back to this review cuz I'll be practicing this one some more!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the real olive garden alfredo sauce

this recipe was retrieved from olive garden's website.  after browsing hundreds of recipes for that "one" alfredo sauce, i found the one!  i have never liked any other alfredo sauce other then olive garden's - i made this recipe last night with angel hair pasta & roasted chicken

1. heat milk and cream in a heavy bottom saucepan until it begins to simmer
2. turn off heat
3. slowly whip in cheese , then remove from heat
4. place egg yolks in a separate bowl and slowly whip in a portion of the hot milk and cream mixture
5. slowly add egg yolk mixture back into remaining cream mixture
6. place back on very low heat and continually stir until simmering
7. take sauce off heat so it thickens
8. season to taste with salt and black pepper
9. serve over your favorite pasta
demonstrations.review: This was really good, but was not Olive Garden's. Our Olive Garden does not put black pepper in their sauce and they use garlic and it has more of a gritty texture to it. To make it even better, I used about 3/4 cup each of the cheeses, maybe a little more. It gave it a cheesier taste and more of a texture (sort of gritty) like our Olive Garden's. I also used 2-3 cloves of garlic and it turned out ABSOLUTELY, POSITIVELY, TO DIE FOR, GOOD!  The first time I made this I followed the recipe all, but used white pepper. The second time I used the above changes and found that with the garlic it did not need pepper of any kind. This recipe made enough to coat an entire box of angel hair.  I may experiment with freezing super small, more health-concious portions, to use more as a condiment. I will also probably add another 2 cloves of garlic. If you like that gritty texture of Olive Garden's sauce, a real quality, dry cheese is essential. Thank you so much for posting this. It lead me to a fabulous alfredo, which due to health reasons, my family won't be seeing as often as they wish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake cookies  for 1 or 2 people

my mother used to make these when i was a kid.  i still love them as an adult, but don't want to be tempted to eat an entire batch. so i came up with this recipe - perfect when you want just a little something sweet, but not too much.

1. mix sugar , hershey's cocoa and dry milk thoroughly in a small saucepan
2. add water and butter
3. then stir constantly over medium / high heat
4. after butter has completely melted , continue stirring and boil one minute
5. remove from heat
6. stir in peanut butter and then oats
7. drop by the spoonful onto wax paper or dinner plate
8. eat warm or save for later
demonstrations.review: These are the cookies my mom made too! I've tried a few others and have since lost them. I tripled the recipe because there are 3 of us. I used 1" round cookie dough scoop and my batch made 12 cookies. I will be making even twice THAT many next time. These are great! I like only a hint of peanut butter flavor so I will use a little less next time. Thanks for an old time favorite!

target.recipe_text:
yeast pancakes

this recipe is from taste of home/dorothy smith.  the pancakes are golden and thicker than a traditional pancake, and they are really good.  keep in mind, the cooking time doesn't include the time for the yeast to rise.

1. in a mixing bowl , combine the flour , yeast , sugar , and salt
2. add milk , eggs , and butter and beat for 2 minutes
3. cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled
4. pour batter by 1 / 2 cupfuls onto a lightly greased hot griddle
5. turn when bubbles form on top of pancakes
6. cook until second side is golden brown
target.review: OMG these were the BEST pancakes we have ever had! We recently tried the IHOP copy cat recipe and thought it was good until this morning.plan ahead when making so you have time enough to let it rise before you need to make them.I made a 1/2 batch since it was just the two of us.It made 6 large pancakes and that was just right.In cutting the recipe in half I thought it called for 2tbs of sugar and because a reviewer said it wasnt very sweet I just left the sugar at 2tbs(it was supposed to be 2tsp for a full recipe)oops didnt mess it up at all.they looked and tasted like a restaurant style pancake and hubby just loved them.             Thanks AmyZoe :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
farmhouse bed and breakfast apricot scones

pamper guests with a plateful of these (or other) home-baked goodies.  simple to make, nose-twitching scent, and on the table in no time.   serve with bacon or sausages, apricot honey-butter, and coffee or milk.  compliments to reiman's *best of country cooking 2003*

1. preheat oven to 400
2. seasoned baking stone or greased cookie sheet
3. set aside
4. in a bowl , combine dry ingredients
5. cut in butter
6. in a small bowl , combine eggs
7. reserve one tablespoon for glazing
8. set aside
9. in another bowl , combine sour cream , milk and eggs
10. add apricots
11. stir into crumb mixture until dough clings together
12. turn onto lightly floured table , knead 12-15 times
13. divide down into two portions
14. pat one portion into a 6-7 inch disk on the baking sheet
15. combine filling ingredients , sprinkle over first disk in pan to within 1 / 2-inch of edge
16. pat remaining down into matching disk , place over filling , softly pinch edges , but don't worry if they're not sealed
17. glaze top with reserved 1 t
18. egg , sprinkle with additional sugar
19. cut into wedges , leaving in place on pan
20. bake for 15-20 minutes
21. cool slightly , break apart carefully
22. serve warm with honey and apricot jam
23. variation: try dried cranberries for a tangy eye-opening breakfast treat !
demonstrations.review: i wanted so bad to try this recipe this weekend....does it really call for 2 1/2 cups of baking powder? This sound like way too much but i didnt want to waste the time if this was a typo on the recipe......i will check back another time to see if it has been corrected.....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of ihop buttermilk pancakes by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com. these are my favorite pancakes...so light and fluffy.

1. preheat a skillet over medium heat
2. mix all of the ingredients til combined
3. melt a little bit of butter in the pan
4. pour the batter by spoonfuls into the hot pan , forming 5-inch circles
5. when the edges appear to harden , flip the pancakes
6. they should be golden brown
7. cook the pancakes on the other side until they are also golden brown
8. enjoy
demonstrations.review: I doubled the recipe as I love to have leftovers to microwave. I followed the recipe exactly as written with the exception of adding a splash of vanilla and I made my own buttermilk as I didnt have any on hand.Hubby likes thinner pancakes so I decided to give it a try.He loved them and ate way too many, now he is miserably full. Very easy to make and they cook up quickly.Thanks for the wonderful recipe, hubby is very happy :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
incredible soft dinner rolls  abm

made these for our thanksgiving dinner and they are awesome! very light and tasty and the dough is so easy to handle.

1. place all ingredients in bread machine in the order according to manufacturers directions
2. select dough cycle
3. when cycle is complete , remove dough from pan
4. cover and let rest for 10 minutes on lightly floured surface
5. grease a large cookie sheet
6. divide dough into four parts , then cut each part into 5 pieces
7. shape each piece into a ball and place 2" apart on cookie sheet
8. cover and let rise for 30 minutes or until double in size
9. heat oven to 375 and bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until golden brown
10. remove from oven and brush tops with melted butter
11. serve warm or cool on wire rack
12. for rolls with soft sides , place rolls close together on cookie sheet and let rise
demonstrations.review: Awesome rolls, used ABM as I usually do with most of my doughs and they turned out beautiful, I didnt get as many because I guess I made them bigger than the recipe called for but they were all gone nonetheless no matter their size.  Thanks Marie for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
batter for deep frying

this batter is awesome for deep frying anything! onion rings, mushrooms, zucchini spears, fish, chicken, shrimp, etc. it is light and thin so you can actually still taste the food you deep fried. this recipe doesn't seem like it would make a lot, but it's so thin that it really covers a lot of food.

1. in a mixing bowl , combine the flour , cornstarch , baking powder , and salt
2. in a separate mixing bowl , combine 1 / 2 cup plus 1 t
3. water , 1 t
4. beaten egg , and oil
5. add wet ingredients to dry and combine until mixed
6. follow your deep fryer instructions for whatever veggie or meat you're frying
7. this batter is thin and delicious
8. don't worry if it doesn't look like it's thick enough
9. it works great
demonstrations.review: This recipe was the best I have ever used.It didnt get my oil all dirty like most batters do.Light and airy texture.We didnt think it had enough salt but that is easily added.I made 4 batches to do a generous batch of onion rings and catfish nuggets,so make plenty to begin with.try this you will not be sorry!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
just like lambert s  throwed  rolls   copycat

there is a fantastic restaurant in sikeston, mo where they throw the most delicious rolls at you before, during and after your meal. this is a copy cat recipe of those exact rolls. if you get the chance, visit the restaurant. if not, try these rolls anyway. they are so very good!

(the lambert's restaurant is in sikeston, mo.) they have subsequently opened one in ozark, mo and foley, al)

1. combine sugar and yeast in tepid water
2. let stand 5-10 minutes until yeast begins to foam
3. thoroughly mix milk , butter , sugar , egg and salt in large bowl
4. stir in the yeast mixture and 3 1 / 2 cups of flour , adding a bit more if necessary to make a soft , pliable dough
5. turn dough out on floured board and let rest while you clean and butter bowl
6. knead dough gently 4-5 minutes , adding flour if necessary , until dough is smooth and silky
7. return to bowl , cover with plastic wrap , and let rise in warm place until doubled in size
8. butter a 12 cup muffin tin
9. punch down dough
10. pinch off pieces that are about 1 1 / 2 inches in diameter , , and roll into smooth spheres
11. place two such pieces in each prepared muffin cup- it will be a tight fit
12. cover dough loosely with plastic wrap for 45 minutes
13. bake rolls in preheated 350 degree oven for 20-25 minutes , or until light brown
14. serve as soon as they are cool enough to throw
demonstrations.review: I made these today exactly as written except I used my bread machine to make the dough. I didnt think they were as sweet as I would have like them, I will adjust the sugar next time. Also watch them close when baking as I didnt bake them as long as was called for and almost burnt them(I only baked for 15 min and probably should have checked them around 10 min) I will try tio let them rise in the pan more next time as they werent as big as Lamberts rolls, that was my fault for sure, but live and learn. right?  Thanks KC for a great recipe......

target.recipe_text:
spinach garlic soup

this soup turns to a brilliant green color. my kids take leftovers to school for lunch and ask me to often make this easy soup. i have substitued skim milk for the cream with good results

1. in a 5qt dutch oven , bring spinach , broth and carrots to a boil
2. reduce heat
3. simmer 5 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. remove from the heat
5. cool to luke-warm
6. meanwhile , in a skillet , saute onion and garlic in butter until onion is soft , about 5-10 minutes
7. add flour
8. cook and stir over low heat for 3-5 minutes
9. add to spinach mixture
10. puree in small batches in a blender or food processor until finely chopped
11. place in a large saucepan
12. add cream , milk , and pepper , heat through but do not boil
target.review:
First, I have to say that I followed the directions exactly. (I have a terrible habit of "tweaking" recipes.)

Second, I'm not giving this a rating since everyone else who's rated it really liked it. We (4 adults) didn't care for it. We each had a small serving and the rest was thrown out. 

Was this soup supposed to taste slightly fishy? While I was making this, I noticed a fishy scent, and once it was served someone asked if I had used fish stock.

I bought the spinach today specifically for this recipe and the spinach looked fresh. Could it have been the spinach that gave it that flavor?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: I've made this at least a half dozen times in the last year. Everyone loves it. I boil (poach?) the chicken in water with half an onion, bay leaf, salt, pepper and poultry seasoning. I shred the chicken after it's cooked and season it with a bit more salt, pepper, poultry seasoning, garlic and onion powders.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker mediterranean pot roast

this recipe comes from betty crocker easy slow cooked dinners.

1. spray 12 inch skillet with cooking spray
2. heat over medium - high heat
3. cook beef in skillet about 5 minutes , turn once till brown
4. sprinkle with salt , italian seasoning and garlic
5. remove from skillet
6. place beef , seasoned side up in 4-5 quart slow cooker
7. spread tomatoes and olives over roast
8. add broth and onions
9. cover and cook on low 5-6 hours till beef is tender
10. remove beef from slow cooker
11. cover and let stand 15 minutes
12. slice beef
13. serve with beef juice and onions from slow cooker
demonstrations.review:
My family and I love this pot roast. 

I use Kalamata black olives.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review:
Awesome recipe and incredibly easy to make.

I tripled the amount of green onion and doubled everything else. I used Creole seasoning, as that is all I could find.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nuways a k a maid rites

if you're anywhere from the midwest, you will be familiar with these "loose meat" sandwiches. i spent years looking for a recipe that duplicates what i remember eating while growing up. after much experimenting, my sisters and i finally declare this recipe as it. i hope you think so too!  
update:  i spent an afternoon with my mom at the original nuway location down on east douglas in wichita, ks and was able to refine the recipe a bit more after talking to someone who had worked there for years.  i've adjusted the recipe to reflect the information i was given, to be more precise.  i found they cook the meat at a high heat in a cast iron cooker, then hold it at around 200 degrees to serve the lunch crowd.  i was told there is no seasoning in the meat, but that all the flavor is what is on the bun.  i made these again to test that theory, and realized the dill pickles are salty enough that you don't need any extra seasoning. i orginally had counted the "holding" time and realized this actually only takes minutes to cook.   sometimes the best things are ultimately simple!  these are the real deal.

1. pour water into a cast iron pan
2. add l lb
3. ground beef and keep stirring until meat is broken into very small pieces
4. bring to a boil and cook until water is reduced by half
5. ready the buns with frenchs mustard , and a large dill pickle slice , dice an onion and pull out a slice of american cheese
6. dip a 1 / 2 cup strainer into the beef mixture , push the liquid through it with a spoon to the desired "juiciness"
7. fry separately in a cast iron skillet for a few minutes , until the beef is lightly browned
8. salt the meat
9. add the diced onions and cheese
10. put the buns together and cut in two pieces
11. cover the hot sandwich for a couple of minutes to steam the bun and allow the cheese to melt
12. serve immediately with a cold root beer , and blast your way to the past !
demonstrations.review:
I've never eaten a Maid-Rite, so my rating has nothing to do with how much it tastes like one.

I doubled the recipe and, except for adding 2 qts. of chicken broth to the water, followed the recipe exactly.

The meat was more mushy than juicy, and it lacked flavor. 

I knew I was going to rate and review this, so I asked my family to rate this on a scale of 1 to 5. One person gave it a 3 and everyone else gave it a 2 or less.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatloaf burgers

these hearty sandwiches are great for potluck dinners, served on hamburger buns, these burgers get extra flavour when topped with the seasoned tomato sauce. most people love them since they are a fun change from plain burgers and regular meatloaf.

1. place onion and celery in a slow cooker
2. combine beef , and 1 tsp salt and pepper
3. shape into six patties
4. place over onion mixture in slow cooker
5. combine tomato juice , garlic , ketchup , bay leaf , italian seasoning and remaining salt
6. pour over the patties
7. cover
8. cook in slow cooker 7-9 hours until meat is tender
9. discard bay leaf
10. separate patties with spatula if necessary and serve on buns
demonstrations.review:
I make these burgers often. My family and I omit the buns (to cut back on carbs) and eat them as is topped with the sauce. 

I add more salt to both the beef and the sauce, as I find 1&1/2 teaspoons of salt a bit bland for my taste.

target.recipe_text:
island kielbasa

my mother gave this recipe to me and it's a quick and easy recipe to make. take it along to your next pot luck...it's always a favorite

1. slice kielbasa into 1 / 2 inch slices and place in crockpot
2. add ketchup , brown sugar and the can of pineapples
3. stir until thoroughly blended
4. cook on low in crockpot for approximately 4-5 hours
target.review: this was just not something we enjoyed as a family. way too sweet and the saltiness of the keilbasa just didn't mesh well. I paired it with rice like others suggested but it still just didn't do much for us.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome baked pork chops

these chops remain moist and tender, and the sauce is to die for! you probably have all the ingredients in your kitchen to make this! serve these chops over rice!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. rinse pork chops , pat dry , and season with garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste
3. place the beaten eggs in a small bowl
4. dredge the pork chops lightly in flour , dip in the egg , and coat liberally with bread crumbs
5. heat the oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat
6. fry the pork chops 5 minutes per side , or until the breading appears well browned
7. transfer the chops to a 9 x 13 baking dish , and cover with foil
8. bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour
9. while baking , combine the cream of mushroom soup , milk and white wine in a medium bowl
10. after the pork chops have baked for an hour , cover them with the soup mixture
11. replace foil , and bake for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: we didn't really care for this recipe too much. the sauce had a very distinct flavor that we both didn't like.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best twice baked potatoes

family favorite - tried and true - the only recipe we use.

1. microwave the potatoes until done
2. allow to cool a bit
3. slice about a 1" strip of the skin off the top of each potato
4. carefully scoop out the pulp , placing in a large bowl , and leaving potato shells intact
5. mash the potato pulp along with the margarine
6. add milk , sour cream , cheese , salt and pepper
7. combining well
8. spoon the mixture back into the potato shells , piling high
9. top with the crumbled bacon or bacon bits
10. bake at 400 for 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: loved these! so good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern stuffed bell peppers

simple preparation & delicious taste! use a mixture of red, green, yellow & orange peppers for a colourful presentation. recipe #2642 instead of store-bought taco seasoning mix--it makes this dish even better!

1. combine beef , onion , seasoning mix and egg in a large bowl
2. add rice and mix well
3. cut peppers in half lengthwise
4. remove seeds and membrane
5. spread tomatoes on the bottom of an ovenproof 12 x 9 inch baking dish
6. the liquid from the tomatoes will reduce during cooking so if you like lots of sauce , add about a cup of water
7. this also helps make the peppers softer
8. place peppers , cut side up , on top of the tomatoes
9. spoon beef mixture into peppers , mounding as necessary
10. top each pepper with salsa
11. bake in preheated 375f oven for 40-45 minutes or until beef is cooked thoroughly and peppers are soft
12. cover each pepper with cheese and return to oven , under the broiler , until the cheese melts- less than a minute , so watch carefully !
13. serve with sour cream and additional salsa
demonstrations.review: me and my husband absolutely loved this dish! I had never tried stuffed peppers until this recipe and I must say they are amazing. thanks for the recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican egg rolls

yummy!!  this is something a little different and very tasty! next time i'm planning on making a huge batch, frying them and flash freezing them on cookie sheets so my husband and kids can heat them up when they want too, or so i have a ready made appetizer for unexpected guests!!

1. chop the chicken into small dices
2. mix all ingredients together
3. moisten the edges of an eggroll wrap and put approx 2 tablespoons of filling in the middle
4. fold like you would an eggroll
5. make sure the flap is sealed to keep the filling inside
6. heat oil to 350f and cook just until golden browned
7. cut diagonally and serve with guacamole and sour cream
demonstrations.review: my husband didn't mind these but I really couldn't get in to them. the flavor was bland for me and the texture of the mixture inside was something I couldn't get passed.( I have a sensitivity to strange textures:) thanks anyway though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
incredibly delicious cheese garlic bread spread

easy, cheesy, savory spread to transform regular bread into a taste sensation! goes awesome with pasta dishes or beside a fresh salad.

1. microwave margarine in medium glass bowl for about 40 seconds or until its melted
2. mix in all ingredients , using a fork
3. spread the mixture over bread
4. place on baking sheet and bake for about 10 minutes at 450 , until the top is golden brown
5. easy !
demonstrations.review: this was so awesome! i will def be making this over and over!

target.recipe_text:
sticky peachy chicken

i found this on recipes to go, and we love it. it freezes and reheats well, so add it to your oamc cookbooks !

1. preheat oven to 350
2. mix jam , bbq sauce , onion and soy sauce
3. put chicken pieces in baking dish
4. top with sauce
5. cover and bake for 30 minutes , then turn and baste
6. bake another 30 minutes or until done
target.review: This was super easy to prepare and my husband liked it! While it's not the fanciest chicken breast out there, it does the job for a weeknight supper. I had 4 large chicken breasts and had just a little sauce left over.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maryland crab cakes with basil aioli

delicous crab cakes served with a garic dipping sauce. can be made mild or hot and spicy. can be used as a seafood appetizer or a main course. recipe courtesy chef rita carmody (formerly of the red lion hotel)

1. in a large bowl , mix crabmeat , onion , crushed crackers , eggs , mayonnaise and seasonings
2. gently mix everything together and shape into crab cakes
3. saute cakes in a little oil for about five minutes on each side or until golden brown
4. to prepare aioli , place egg yolks , garlic and basil in a blender
5. start the blender and slowly add oil
6. when thoroughly mixed and creamy , add salt and lemon juice and if you want it hot and spicy the option red pepper or cayenne
7. serve the aioli on the side as a dipping sauce
demonstrations.review: The crab cakes turned out very nice. I made them late one afternoon after work before going out for dinner.  DH and I thought they tasted like something you could order in a restaurant! I must have done something wrong with the aioli because it came out way too oily - even for what I think an aioli should be.  I'm not sure what I did wrong, and the crab cakes were great, so 4 stars!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken italiano

this is alva carpenter's recipe from the slim lines column, thursday. enjoy!

1. cook pasta in a large pan of boiling water for 5 minutes or until al dente
2. drain the water
3. do not refresh pasta under cold running water
4. let it stay warm
5. heat a heavy non-stick skillet on medium-high flame
6. pour 1 / 4 of the dressing into it and add the chicken strips
7. saute the chicken in the dressing for 2-3 minutes or until lightly browned
8. add the defrosted vegetables and the remaining dressing
9. cover the skillet
10. simmer for 10 minutes , stirring every 2-3 minutes , or until the vegetables are crisp tender
11. serve over pasta and sprinkle some cheese over pasta if desired
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I have made this before, but I can't recall where I came across the recipe.  It is a light yet filling dish that doesn't require too much work.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best sweet and sour sauce

this came from taste of home's quick cooking and is much better than anything i've created on my own. the sauce is thick and gooy and goes well with so many things.

1. combine all ingredients in a sauce pan
2. cook over medium heat until thick , stirring constantly
3. pour over chicken , meatballs , smoked sausage , veggies , etc
demonstrations.review: Just realized I never reviewed this. I made it in one pan and cooked up some chicken in another, then tossed together with some stir fry veggies from the freezer aisle. Add brown rice, and you have a great meal.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish cream bundt cake

this is a great cake to celebrate st. patrick's day!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. grease and flour a 10 inch bundt pan
3. sprinkle chopped nuts evenly over bottom of pan
4. in a large bowl , combine cake mix and pudding mix
5. mix in eggs , 1 / 4 cup water , 1 / 2 cup oil and 3 / 4 cup irish cream liqueur
6. beat for 5 minutes at high speed
7. pour batter over nuts in pan
8. bake in the preheated oven for 60 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean
9. cool for 10 minutes in the pan , then invert onto the serving dish
10. prick top and sides of cake
11. spoon glaze over top and brush onto sides of cake
12. allow to absorb glaze repeat until all glaze is used up
13. to make the glaze: in a saucepan , combine butter , 1 / 4 cup water and 1 cup sugar
14. bring to a boil and continue boiling for 5 minutes , stirring constantly
15. remove from heat and stir in 1 / 4 cup irish cream
demonstrations.review: Another Sunday dinner, another delicious dessert! My mom recently discovered she is allergic to chocolate so I've been looking for something equally tempting - this is it! I screwed up the glaze and added everything in at once, so I added more Bailey's at the end.  Everyone loved it!  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers stuffed shells

received this from a meeting.  very tasty!  they point value we were told from our meeting leader was 4/serving.  some of the reviews people have recalculated it saying 8.  to be safe, i would refigure it so your comfortable knowing the points.

1. preheat oven 375
2. cook shells until al dente , rinse and set aside
3. mix cheeses , salt , garlic powder , oregano and pepper
4. spread a few spoonfuls of tomato sauce on bottom of 9x13 dish
5. when shells are cool enough to handle , fill each shell with cheese mixture and place in baking dish
6. when all shells are in dish , spoon remaining tomato sauce over shells
7. cover pan and bake for 20 minutes
8. yields about 4 shells per serving
9. servings 6
demonstrations.review: Very tasty!  I agree that the cheese mixture was just the right amount of everything.  I took leftovers for lunch the next day and those were great too!  Everyone in the lounge wanted to know what I was having : )

target.recipe_text:
heather s stir fry sauce

my sil is a newlywed, and she's turning into quite a good cook -- we have even started sharing recipes. this is her stir fry sauce, and i love its basic goodness. you can add ingredients (i'll add a few spoonfuls of black bean sauce sometimes, for example) or change them around (i often use brown sugar instead of white, and sometimes i use rice wine vinegar instead of the white). i keep losing the piece of paper i have this scribbled on, so it's time to bring it to zaar!

1. whisk all ingredients together until smooth
2. add to stir fry just at the end , stirring well into the dish and let sauce come to a bubble
3. let simmer until sauce has thickened , then serve
target.review: This sauce is delicious. I had it with a bag of stir fry veggies over white rice. I used seasoned rice vinegar and also added a tsp. of minced garlic, about a 1/4 tsp. of ground ginger, a 1/2 tsp. of sesame oil and a few pinches of crushed red pepper flakes. It turned out great, just the right thickness, clinging to the veggies so that you get all the flavor. I really did love this and will continue to use it. Thanks so much for sharing your recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar brownies  blondies

an easy & yummy brownie that makes a nice no-chocolate treat! fun to vary the mix-ins - we like to add candy corn! it's a moist slightly cakey brownie that everyone will enjoy!

1. mix all ingredients well
2. bake in 9 inch square pan that you have sprayed well with pam at 350f for 25 to 30 minutes
3. cool before cutting
demonstrations.review: These are definitely outstanding. I used about a  third of a cup of peanut butter instead of nuts, etc. and I only used a fourth cup of margarine, which I didn't melt, but blended with the sugar, PB, and other wet ingredients before adding the dry ingredients. I did bake as directed and they came  out with a wonderful brownie texture. I may try a little more PB next time because I love it, but these were exactly what I was looking for. Thanks, SaraFish for an outstanding recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tofu and broccoli in garlic sauce recipe

i found this easy vegetarian stir-fry from jolinda hackett online.

1. cut tofu into 1 inch cubes
2. in a large skillet , sautee onions and garlic in olive oil until onions turn clear , about 3-5 minutes
3. add the tofu , ginger , cayenne and broccoli to the pan and continue to cook until broccoli is done , another 6-8 minutes
4. in a separate small bowl , mix together the corn starch , soy sauce and water , then add this mixture to the broccoli and tofu
5. cook until sauce thickens , then remove from heat
6. serve over rice or whole grains and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I gave this recipe 4 stars but I did change a few things. I left out the tofu, used more broccoli   1 carrot sliced, decreased ginger to 1/2 tsp., added 1/4 C. of water & 1tsp sesame oil, plus I used 3 Tbsp. of AP flour instead of cornstarch because I was out of cornstarch. I also added 1/8 tsp more garlic and served it over brown rice. It was awesome. The sauce was just the right thickness. The amount of cayenne was perfect for me. I will probably use the tofu next time or increase the broccoli, I used 2  heads of broccoli, but I will make this again. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
halloween party mix

my kids are "freaky" over this.

1. in a large bowl , combine first 3 ingredients
2. in a large saucepan , combine sugar , butter and corn syrup
3. bring to a boil over medium heat
4. boil for 5 minutes
5. remove from the heat
6. stir in vanilla and baking soda
7. pour over pretzel mixture and stir until coated
8. pour into a greased 15x10 inch baking pan
9. bake at 250 degrees for 45 minutes , stirring every 10 minutes
10. break apart while warm
11. cool completely
12. toss with m&m's and candy corn
13. store in airtight container
demonstrations.review: This is great. I took a batch to a Halloween party and it was a hit. I only used a 12 ounce pkg. of candy corn and I doubled the nuts, everything else was the same. I also used Snyders sourdough nibblers for the pretzels. I wanted to be able to pop them into my mouth with the other ingredients to get the complete flavor. It was a little sweeter than I thought it would be but the nuts and pretzels kept it from being too sweet. The flavor reminds me of peanut brittle. It's a keeper. Thanks for the great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot kimchi pickle   quick

so simple so deeelisious!! as a side with any thing. (from canadian living mag.)

1. in a bowl , toss the cucumber with the salt
2. let stand for 15 minutes
3. drain
4. add the vinegar , sugar , sesame oil , garlic , hot pepper flakes and cayenne pepper
5. toss to combine
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: These are really 10 stars, but we are limited. I have had an over abundance of cucumbers in my garden and wasn't sure I could eat another but this recipe changed my mind. I made 2 batches. I ate the first batch immediately. They were so good I didn't even need to let them marinate. Hopefully the second batch will last a little longer so I can share them. Thanks so much for sharing your recipe. I will be using it frequently.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mystery pecan pie

i got this one from the food networks paula deen..i really loved this one..it's easy and delicious. hope you like it too.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. topping: combine all ingredients in a medium bowl
3. set aside
4. filling: in a med bowl , mix cream cheese , sugar , salt , vanilla and egg until combined
5. pour into pie shell top with chopped pecans
6. pour topping over pecans
7. bake for 45 minute serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: I got this same recipe from The Pies and Pastries Cookbook. I have made this pie every Thanksgiving for about 10 years. It is the ultimate pecan pie. It is better than a regular pecan pie because it is not as overwhelmingly sweet.

target.recipe_text:
company pork roast

this is very tasty and have received rave reviews. i serve the liquid from the roast, in a small bowl, to spoon over the meat.

1. place roast , fat side up , in foil lined roasting pan
2. mix remaining ingredients and brush on all sides of roast
3. cover with foil and bake at 325f for 2 1 / 2 hours basting frequently
4. uncover the last 45 minutes to brown roast
target.review: We started to make this and realized that we didn't have any honey in the house and so we used maple syrup. Simply outstanding! I love the fact that it is so easy and that is doesn't require a lot of ingredients. We will definitely be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sage meat loaf

i really like this meat loaf because it's moist and the sage flavor in it makes it really yummy. the topping is not too sweet and adds a nice zip to it. it's also a good way to use up those saltine crackers that linger around. recipe comes from taste of home magazine.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. crush saltine crackers in ziplock bag with mallet or rolling pin until finely crushed
3. combine the first 9 ingredients together in a large bowl and mix well with your hands
4. place and form meat loaf into a greased 9x5 loaf pan
5. bake uncovered for 50 minutes
6. combine sauce ingredients and spread over top of meat loaf
7. bake 15-20 minutes longer , until thermometer reads 160f
8. let meat stand for 10 minutes before slicing
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
I have been looking for a good meat loaf recipe for a loooooooong time. This one is wonderful! I will definitely be making it again (and again). 

I made two changes to the recipe. I added a tsp of dried summer savory (because it's so yummy) and I used bread crumbs instead of saltines (because I didn't have them).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate orange chocolate chip cookies

these cookies are super-packed with intense flavors.

1. heat oven to 350
2. beat 1 cup sugar , butter , 1 tablespoon grated orange peel and the egg in large bowl with electric mixer on medium speed , or mix with spoon
3. stir in flour , cocoa , salt , baking powder and baking soda
4. stir in pecans and chocolate morsels
5. shape dough into 1 1 / 2-inch balls
6. mix 1 / 3 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon grated orange peel
7. roll balls in sugar mixture
8. place about 3 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet
9. flatten to about 1 / 2-inch thickness with bottom of glass
10. bake 9 to 11 minutes or until set
11. cool slightly
12. remove from cookie sheet
13. cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review:
Absolutely wonderful! This is my favourite flavour combination and the cookies did not disappoint! What a pleasure to eat. They were gone in no time at all. 

Note to Mrs. R - I wish I had have read your review before I started baking because I noticed that we had no milk, only after the first batch had come out of the oven! grrrrrr

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry apple crisp

serve this with vanilla ice cream!!

1. combine the blueberries and the apples in a bowl and sprinkle with about 1 tablespoon of the flour
2. toss
3. spoon into 6 custard cups
4. combine the remaining flour and sugar in a bowl
5. cut in margarine until mixture is crumbly and resembles coarse meal
6. add oats , cinnamon and nutmeg
7. sprinkle flour mixture over the fruit
8. bake at 400 degrees for about 30 minutes or until bubbly
9. let stand for 10 minutes
10. serve warm
demonstrations.review:
I made it in a large pan & doubled the topping. I also added just a dash of cloves. 

Mmmmm A perfect autumn comfort food :) Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mojito de mentha

friends of ours made these for us as the prelude to a hot summer evening, and with one drink, this became our favorite new cocktail! very fresh and light and a great way to use the mint from your garden. (from the cookbook, viva la vida by rafael palomino.)

1. tear mint leaves in half and put in cocktail shaker
2. using a pestle or the end of a wooden spoon , mash the leaves until bruised and crushed
3. add all the remaining ingredients except soda
4. cover the shaker and shake briskly
5. pour into a tall glass and top off with sprite or 7-up
6. stir once , garnish with a mint sprig and serve
demonstrations.review:
Thanks for the recipe; we love to make these for guests! 

We tried Mojitos while on vacation in Cuba and fell in love with them. Very refreshing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple sweet scones

this is a simple perfectly delicious recipe my mom used to make for our family. it origioually came from a biscuits and scones recipe book, this one was always my favorite of all the recipes.

1. heat oven to 425f
2. put flour , baking powder and salt into a large bowl
3. stir mix well add butter and cut in with a pastry blender or rub in with your fingers , until the mixture looks like fine crumbs
4. add sugar
5. toss to mix
6. add milk and stir with a wooden spoon until dough forms ,
7. place dough on floured counter and knead gently until the dough comes together in a ball
8. pat or roll into a circle about 1 1 / 2 inches thick
9. cut each circle into 6 or 8 wedges
