10. place wedges on a greased cookie sheet- slightly apart for crisp sides , touching for soft
11. bake about 12 minutes , or until medium brown on top
demonstrations.review: I must have done something wrong because they crumbled were crumbly but still delicious. We serrved them up warm, with raspberry jam, butter and Devonshire cream! Yummm!

target.recipe_text:
tiramisu anacapri

easy to make and delicious!  looks beautiful served in a trifle bowl.

1. combine first 3 ingredients in a large bowl
2. stir well with a whisk
3. cover surface with plastic wrap
4. chill 30 minutes or until firm
5. remove plastic wrap , and add cream cheese
6. beat with a mixer at medium speed until well-blended
7. gently fold in whipped topping
8. combine hot water , kahla , and espresso
9. split ladyfingers in half lengthwise
10. arrange 16 ladyfinger halves , flat sides down , in a trifle bowl or large glass bowl
11. drizzle with 1 / 2 cup kahla mixture
12. spread one-third of pudding mixture evenly over ladyfingers
13. sprinkle with 1 tablespoon cocoa
14. repeat layers , ending with cocoa
15. cover and chill at least 8 hours
target.review: This is a FABULOUS trifle recipe - especially for tiramisu lovers! I first found it on Cooking Light's website and made it with a girlfriend...and it's become a staple ever since! The sweetened condensed milk adds just enough sweetness and the Kahlua gives it the "wow" factor. I use one 6-serving box of vanilla pudding, but I've also tried it with butterscotch and that's yummy too. And in addition to cocoa, add mini-chocolate chips on top of each layer. I've served this at many dinner parties and everyone raves.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweetheart trifle

i love the chocolate/peanut butter taste! i found this in a cooking magazine, it originally called for nestle crunch bars, but i don't care for those, so i decided to use the peanut butter cups. try a different candy bar and find your favorite! i am not positive about the prep time, but it includes chilling.

1. prepare cake mix according to directions , let cool completely
2. in a heavy saucepan , combine chips , 1 / 4 c milk and the whipping cream
3. cook and stir over low heat until chips are melted
4. remove from heat
5. stir in vanilla and cool to room temp
6. place the remaining milk in a mixing bowl
7. beat in the pudding mixes on low speed for 2 minutes
8. to assemble , crumble half the cake into a 4 qt trifle bowl or large bowl
9. layer with 1 / 2 the peanut butter sauce , pudding , whipped topping and then repeat layers
10. at the end , add the crumbled peanut butter cups
11. cool for 3 hours
demonstrations.review: Very rich, but VERY good! If you're a Reese's fan, you'll LOVE this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan cornbread

i took this recipe word-for-word off the about.com website. i haven't tried it, but i figured we needed a vegan cornbread recipe to go along with vegetarian chili :)

1. mix dry ingredients in a bowl
2. mix wet ingredients in another bowl
3. add wet to dry and stir well
4. bake at 375 for about 30 minutes , or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Very good for being so healthy! I used sugar substitue and added a handful of low-fat cheddar cheese - quite tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach mushroom lasagna roll ups with gorgonzola cream sauce

this is a wonderfully flavored dish that my hubby swears is my best dinner yet! served with asparagus topped with some of the sauce is superb.

1. saut mushrooms , chopped onion and garlic in oil over med heat , until mushrooms give off their juice and onion is tender- 7-8 minutes
2. season with salt and pepper
3. add dry chopped spinach to the pan and heat through
4. add ricotta , adjust salt and pepper and heat through
5. remove from burner , but leave in warm skillet
6. heat broth in small sauce pan
7. add gorgonzola into broth , and bring to a bubble
8. stir in cream and thicken about 2 minutes
9. place cooked noodles on work surface
10. place a dollop of spinach mixture on one end of noodles and roll each one up
11. arrange rolled packages , seam side down , in shallow casserole dish
12. pour warm sauce over and top with mozzarella
13. place casserole under broiler to melt mozzarella and slightly brown
demonstrations.review: Made this for a dinner party...alongside eggplant parmesan...and it was fabulous! Great flavor, and not that difficult to prepare. The sauce took a bit longer than stated, but other than that, prep was fairly easy. I also reduced the fat by using part-skim ricotta and fat-free half and half instead of cream. I WILL be making again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
extra moist cornbread with sour cream

this cornbread remains moist and is so good! we really enjoy it with soups or chili.

1. lightly grease a 13"x9" pan
2. preheat your oven to 375 f degrees
3. beat eggs until light , then add the oil and the salt
4. continue to mix this together and add the creamed corn , the sour cream and finally , the muffin mix
5. pour mixture into the prepared pan and place in the oven
6. bake for 35 minutes
7. add extra taste to the recipe using some of the following if you wish: 1 small can diced geen chilies , 1 / 2-3 / 4 cup grated cheese
demonstrations.review: If you like dry, crumbly cornbread, then this is not the recipe for you. It is soooo good though. I made a batch for a chili cook-off at work and everyone kept asking for the recipe. It doesn't need any sugar in my opinion - there's sugar in the Jiffy mix so it already has a touch of sweetness. I added a couple tablespoons of chopped cilantro and a handful of Mexican cheese to the batter. YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian black bean   zucchini risotto

nan

1. in large deep skillet over medium heat , heat oil
2. add rice
3. stir to coat with oil
4. stir in 4 cups water and salt
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat
7. cover and simmer about 15 to 18 minutes , until most of the liquid is absorbed
8. stir black beans , zucchini , salsa , 1 cup cheese and cilantro into rice mixture
9. cover
10. cook about 8 minutes , until zucchini is tender
11. sprinkle with the remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese
12. remove from heat , cover and let stand 4 minutes , until cheese is melted
13. serve with sour cream and green onions
demonstrations.review: Made this for a dinner party and it was raved over! I changed a few things though that I would recommend for better flavor: start out by sauteing some garlic and onion in the olive oil, add 1/2 cup of white wine to the rice before adding more liquid, and use veggie or chicken broth intead of water for more flavor. Otherwise, it's fabulous! For a complete meal, serve with cornbread and a Mexican salad. Yum!

target.recipe_text:
jan s beg for the recipe salad dressing

my fabulous stepmother, jan, has made this salad dressing for years, and everyone she serves it to just loves, loves loves it!  she can't serve this, without almost everyone at the table begging her for the recipe; thus, the name i blessed the recipe 
with! :-)  this is a bit of a sweet dressing, so it goes particularly well in a green salad, with a sliced fruit (like strawberries).  try a salad of mixed greens, feta cheese, sliced strawberries, and walnuts or pecans, as this makes a beautiful and delicious salad!  i have also used it on a number of other types of salads, as well, and it works beautifully with most combinations!  the recipe calls for vegetable oil, only because it keeps better in the fridge (when you make a generous amount to keep on hand all through the week, which i highly recommend), but you can also make it with olive oil, or an oil of your choice.  i use almost no other salad dressing now!  thank you, jan, for a real gem!

1. mix all ingredients in salad dressing bottle , and shake well , until well mixed
2. if using a bowl , add all ingredients , except oil
3. mix with spoon , then whisk in oil
4. keep chilled in fridge
target.review: Oh This is THE KEEPER of dressings! I've made it about 10 times in the last few weeks and it just doesnt last in the fridge! I've added cilantro and basil, extra garlic, part red wine vinegar, part olive oil, even eyeballed it in the making, memorized the recipie and always, it comes out fantastic! Its in my book of favorites now. Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broiled salmon with spicy maple basting sauce

sweet and spicy...great combination for salmon

1. in a small heavy saucepan combine maple syrup , water , gingerroot , garlic , red pepper flakes , and salt and simmer until reduced to about 1 / 2 cup
2. cool basting sauce
3. preheat broiler
4. arrange salmon , skin sides down , on oiled rack of broiler pan and season with salt
5. broil salmon about 4 inches from heat 4 minutes
6. brush salmon with sauce and broil until just cooked through , about 6 minutes more
demonstrations.review: I love this marinade! I use a very similar recipe already and it's a tried and true winner. Mine has a touch of liquid smoke added to bring out the grill flavors. This recipe was acquired after much weedling upon the chef at a VERY fancy restraunt I worked in for many years.  Thank you for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
toasted ravioli

these italian appetizers are crunchy and delicious dipped in a warm marinara sauce. they are very addictive! make a bunch, you'll need to have a lot!

1. cook ravioli in boiling salted water until they float to the top
2. remove from water and drain
3. set aside to cool
4. heat vegetable oil in fryer at least 2" deep to a temperature of 375 degrees
5. dip ravioli in beaten egg , then cover in breadcrumbs
6. fry in batches in hot oil until golden brown , about 5 minutes
7. drain
8. sprinkle hot ravioli with parmesan cheese
9. heat marinara sauce and set aside in serving bowl
10. serve ravioli with dipping sauce
demonstrations.review: Hot damn these are great! Super simple to make - though I am often intimidated by the hot oil (dont have a deep fryer yet) I soldiered through and we were stoked with the outcome! These were gobbled up right away by my guests. I have none for later! Guess its time to heat up some more oil!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled shrimp    mmmmmm

a nice modernized version of the old classic shrimp cocktail. watch 'em disappear!

1. in a 1 gal plastic food bag place shrimp and olive oil , toss to coat , sprinkle enough rub to coat the shrimp
2. the bag should look dark red
3. refrigerate for 1-4 hrs , the longer you wait the hotter they'll be
4. light the grill and while it's heating place shrimp on skewers
5. when coals are very hot , clean the area that the shrimp will be on and rub with a bit of canola oil on a rag
6. immediately place shrimp on greased grill for 2-3 minutes , turn and cook an additional 2-3 minutes
7. remove from skewers and serve hot
8. no dipping sauce required
9. this rub works well on chicken wings too !
demonstrations.review: Super easy and YUMMY! Marinated shrimp about 7 hours (perfect spice!) threaded them on skewers and since the bbq was still frozen under snow, I baked them! They came out perfect, looked spectacular served over greens and though I made 2pnds worth - they are gone!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
charlie s famous chicken salad with grapes

a really great guy i used to work with would make this and bring in to share. we all loved it so much and would beg for more! sounds strange with the grapes, but it's so good! allow time for salad to chill.

1. combine all ingredients
2. chill
3. serve with just about anything- crackers , chips , rolls , bread or bagel
demonstrations.review: Great salad!! I used red grapes cause it needed some color - even though the grapes gave me pause to start I added extra once I tasted the delicious addition they made. Will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
persian chicken breasts

years ago, when i cooked for a caterer, we catered an affair for frank purdue (of chicken fame!) at the boston aquarium. this was what he chose as one of the dishes featuring his chicken. i fell in love with it!

1. cut chicken into 1" cubes
2. marinate chicken in lemon juice for 1 hour
3. peel short , very thin strips of orange zest with a vegetable peeler , about 2 t
4. , set aside
5. peel the oranges , remove as much of the white pith as possible , divide into sections
6. put orange sections , salt , pepper and turmeric in a saucepan
7. saute onions in 1 t
8. butter until browned
9. add orange peel to onions , cook , stirring , about 1-2 minutes
10. add onion mixture to saucepan with orange sections
11. add vinegar and sugar , cook 15 minutes stirring gently so orange sections remain intact
12. remove chicken from marinade , saute in remaining butter until browned
13. to serve: place chicken pieces on plate and spoon orange mixture on top
demonstrations.review: Super quick easy and flavorfully orange receipe. Both myself and the DBF Loved this! He seldom swallows dinner whole while commenting around a biteful "This is really good. Is there more?" Only difference I made was to add the chicken back into the orange/onion saute sauce to impact the flavors a little more. Super great for lunch the next day too.

target.recipe_text:
easy mediterranean pizza

this is a great recipe for a different kind of pizza. it's heavy on the flavors, but you don't feel stuffed after eating it. the recipe was actually born of an experiment performed by myself and a friend on a sunday night. be creative, though... last time i made it, i spread pine nuts over the surface and it was terrific!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. brush pizza shell with olive oil
3. spread pesto sauce thoroughly over the surface of the shell , leaving the edge as a crust
4. top with olives , sundried tomatoes , artichoke hearts , wilted spinach leaves and cover with cheeses
5. place pizza directly on oven rack for 10 minutes , or until cheese is melted from centre to edge
6. allow to cool for 5 minutes before slicing
target.review:
The whole family enjoyed it!
I added the green pepper and romano cheese.Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crisp butter cookies  refrigerator cookies

these are really good! buttery and crispy just like the name suggests!
since these are refrigerator cookies, this is a very handy recipe. 
these can keep in the freezer for up to 6 months.

1. combine the flour , baking soda and salt
2. in a large bowl , cream the butter and sugar
3. beat in the egg
4. gradually blend in the dry ingredients
5. divide the dough in half
6. form each half into a log 1 -inches in diameter
7. wrap in waxed paper and chill for 4 hours
8. preheat oven to 400 degrees
9. lightly grease 2 baking sheets
10. cut the logs into -inch thick slices and place 1-inch apart on the prepared baking sheets
11. bake for 8 to 10 minutes
12. until lightly colored
13. transfer to wire racks to cool
demonstrations.review: Very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh mango bread

i make lots of these during mango season and give away to friends and family. it's great for breakfast or afternoon snack! sometimes i even stick it in the toaster for a different texture.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. combine all of the dry ingredients
3. beat eggs with oil and add to flour mixture
4. add mangos , lemon juice and raisins
5. mix well
6. pour into 2 greased 8x4 loaf pans
7. bake for about 1 hour or until toothpick comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! Thanks for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef rouladen

this recipe, from the dec/jan 1996 issue of taste of home has been a family favorite since the first time i made it. it does require a little effort, but it's worth every minute. i make this on a regular basis, as well as when we have company over. i always serve homemade dinner rolls with it but traditionally it may have been served with potato dumplings. i usually will slice my 8 meat slices in half, lengthwise, to create 16 smaller slices, which are easier to handle.  *note:  most recipes include a dill pickle slice in each roll, and after trying it with pickles my family loves this recipe even more!  i've added the pickle as an optional ingredient.  :)

1. spread mustard on one side of each slice of meat
2. sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. place one strip of bacon , dill pickle slice , and a few onion wedges on each slice of meat
4. roll up and secure with wooden toothpicks
5. put oil in dutch oven or other large pan and brown meat
6. drain
7. add broth and bring to a boil
8. reduce heat and cover and simmer for 1-1 / 2 hours or until meat is tender
9. remove meat and keep warm
10. combine flour and water until smooth and slowly stir into broth
11. bring to a boil , stirring constantly until thickened
12. remove wooden pics from meat and return to gravy
13. heat through
14. sprinkle with parsley if desired
demonstrations.review: YUM!great recipe-Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey chilli chicken

nan

1. dice chicken and coat lightly with flour which has been seasoned with salt
2. fry chicken in batches in hot oil until golden brown or until chicken is cooked through
3. remove from oil , drain on paper towels
4. repeat with remaining chicken
5. pour off excess oil leaving one tablespoon of oil in pan
6. add ginger to pan , saute gently one minute
7. add honey , stir for one minute
8. add combined cornflour , water , chilli sauce , lemon juice and soy sauce
9. stir until sauce boils and thickens
10. add chicken pieces , toss in sauce for three minutes or until chicken is heated through
11. add sliced shallots , cook for a further minute
12. serve with rice or chinese noodles
demonstrations.review: My 14 year old son help me make this he thought it was easy enough for him to make on his own.This is is his new favorite dish,he absoultly loves it. I thought it was very delisious! Thanks for shraring!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian flat green beans with tomatoes and garlic

another reason to celebrate long hot humid days of summer.

this dish is reminiscent of an italian method of cooking green beans with tomatoes for a long time, which was especially good for tenderizing tough, old beans.
from the miami herald.

1. bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat
2. add the green beans and cook for 5 to 7 minutes , until tender
3. drain immediately
4. while the beans are cooking , heat the oil in a medium saut pan or skillet over medium-high heat until the oil shimmers
5. add the garlic slices , distributing them evenly
6. cook for 4 to 5 minutes , until the slices become almost translucent and start to brown on the edges
7. be careful not to let the garlic burn
8. add the diced tomato and salt and pepper to taste , then reduce the heat to medium
9. cook for 2 to 3 minutes , so that the tomato is heated through
10. add the cooked green beans and heat through for 1 to 2 minutes
11. mix well
12. taste and adjust seasoning as needed
13. transfer to a serving dish and top with the basil , if desired
14. serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: YUM! This was a great way to change Green Bean.The only thing I did different was add an extra garlic clove,we love garlic!! Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
chocolate  chocolate  chocolate  bundt cake with chocolate glaze

need i say more...chocolate! decadently rich and moist. add a scoop of vanilla ice cream and you're in heaven.

1. cake: preheat oven to 350
2. grease and flour bundt pan , set aside
3. in large mixing bowl , combine cake mix , pudding mix and chocolate chips
4. in another bowl , combine water , eggs , and vanilla mixing well
5. add egg mixture to dry mixture and mix with spoon until just blended
6. pour into prepared pan
7. bake for 50 to 55 minutes or until cake tests done when wooden pick in center comes out clean
8. cool 15 to 20 minutes before removing cake from pan
9. when completely cool , drizzle cake with chocolate glaze
10. chocolate glaze: combine all ingredients in bowl
11. mix with spoon until smooth
target.review: OMG this cake gets this chubby chocoholic's seal of approval I made this for a very special friends Birthday and was so happy that I did.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream of carrot soup

rich tasting, warm and comforting. i had a recipe i loved for this soup, but the original called for a lot more butter and 2 cups of heavy cream. i didn't really want to save this soup for special occasions only, so i attempted to reduce the fat & calories by reducing the butter and replacing the cream with evaporated milk - i have even tried evaporated skim milk with success (but it is better with whole evaporated milk). if i am serving this to guests, i use the half-n- half, but for just me i like it with the milk. i have never missed the cream in this.

1. in a large stockpot , melt butter and saute onion until soft and tender , about 5 minutes or so
2. add carrots , potatoes , chicken broth , and ginger powder
3. cover and cook on medium heat 30 minutes or until veggies are very tender
4. remove from heat and let cool 15 minutes
5. using a stick blender , puree the soup right in the pot
6. return to heat and add milk , rosemary , salt , and pepper
7. cook over low heat until heated through , maybe 5 minutes or so
demonstrations.review: It was ok I don't like ginger so I added a little curry and it was good I will make it again. I also used half and half cream.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
celery cream soup

imagine the aroma of home made cream of celery soup simmering on the stove. simple, easy and rich in flavor.

1. in a large sauce pan , melt butter , add celery , onions , and garlic
2. cook over medium low heat until soft
3. add flour and cook 1-2 minutes over low heat
4. add chicken broth and bay leaf , bring to a boil reduce heat , cover and simmer 30 minutes
5. remove bay leaf , puree in a blender or processor
6. add cream , lemon juice , hot sauce , salt and pepper
7. reheat and simmer 5 minutes
8. garnish with celery leaves
demonstrations.review: I really liked the soup I made like you said but I think next time I will strain the soup before adding the cream and lemon juice. It was a great flavor but a little to stringy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect perogies casserole

found this in an ad for cheemo perogy. a large bag makes two casseroles, one to freeze.

1. saute butter , onion , and pepper in a skillet for five minutes
2. in a medium casserole dish , combine perogies , onion , pepper and ham
3. mix milk and soup in a separate dish
4. pour over casserole
5. top with shredded cheese
6. bake for 35 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
demonstrations.review: This is my hubby's new fav way to eat perogies. Thank you I can't wait to try the other casseroles that use perogies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
adult popcorn

here's a great, economical snack for those sports fans. it's quick & easy too

1. combine parmesan , salt , cayenne , cumin& thyme
2. this is best done in the processor with the blade , process for 3 minutes so the mix is very fine
3. pop the corn
4. toss with the butter
5. toss with the cheese mix
6. best served now but may be prepared up to 4 hours in advance and served at room temperature
demonstrations.review: The first time I made this I made it twice. the second time I made it I made it three times. I am starting to think that my hubby's friends want to have poker here because they now they will get this popcorn. So good and it literally takes 5 min to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn bread

this is an easy to prepare, mildly-flavored cornbread.  i tried this at a friend's house years ago, and promptly asked for the recipe.  this has been extremely helpful over the years, as we have picky eaters around here who won't touch cornbread that has actual corn in it, but they gobble this one up!  we really like it warm with a bit of butter and honey, or alongside some chili, etc.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. grease well 8 or 9" pan pan
3. combine the flour , cornmeal , sugar , baking powder , and salt and mix well
4. stir in the milk , vegetable oil , and egg
5. mix just until the dough is moistened
6. pour the batter into the pan
7. bake 20-25 minutes , or until golden-brown
demonstrations.review: I like this corn bread it is great for pulled pork dinner I used 1 cup flour and 1 cup corn meal. I also cut the sugar since the meat is a little sweet so I didn't want to over do it.

target.recipe_text:
gates   son s kc bbq sauce

this from the restaurant in kc. i got the recipe when mr gates was on martha stewart.

1. in a small bowl , mix together sugar , salt , celery seed , cumin , red pepper , garlic powder , and chili powder
2. set aside
3. in a large bowl , combine remaining ingredients
4. add dry ingredients , and mix well
5. serve warm or at room temperature
6. sauce can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2 to 3 weeks or in freezer for up to 6 months
target.review: Awesome!  This tastes like the real thing....only better.  Every time I serve it with something off the smoker people ask for  the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome nippy franks  cocktail wieners

excellent combo of sweet and tangy!  everyone will want the recipe and it's easy to boot!

1. combine all ingredients except smokies / cocktail wieners
2. stir wieners into sauce mixture
3. cover and heat 1 hour on low in crockpot
4. remove lid and heat additional hour on low
demonstrations.review: excellent recipe, with or without bourbon.  We use it for brats that we make on the smoker too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory chicken and broccoli casserole

easy to make and great for your family or any gathering.
adapted from all recipes.

1. bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil
2. add pasta and cook for 6 to 8 minutes or until al dente
3. drain
4. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
5. grease a 9x13 inch casserole dish
6. melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat
7. saute onion until tender , about 3 minutes
8. mix in flour
9. gradually stir in chicken broth
10. slowly stir in milk , and cook , stirring , until sauce begins to thicken
11. season with salt and pepper
12. place cooked noodles in the bottom of casserole dish
13. arrange cooked chicken in an even layer over noodles
14. place broccoli over the chicken
15. pour sauce evenly over the broccoli
16. combine cheeses , and sprinkle half over the casserole
17. bake in preheated oven for 20 minutes , or until the cheese melts
18. remove from oven , and sprinkle with remaining cheese
19. allow to set for 5 minutes , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: Great recipe.  Everyone loved it.  Looked like a lot, so "halved" it sort of.  Used Italian blend cheese instead of provolone, and crock pot shredded chicken.  Will certainly make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
back uh the can hawaiian chicken

this is quite yummy.  got this from an albertsons brand chicken broth can and everyone loves it.  very healthy and very easy.  easy meal served over white rice.

1. in a medium bowl in this order , mix together sauce ingredients: cornstarch , vinegar , ketchup , chicken broth , brown sugar , and reserved pineapple juice
2. set aside
3. chop chicken into bite sized pieces , and heat oil in a large skillet over medium high heat
4. add garlic and chicken to hot oil and cook about 5 minutes or until browned
5. add in carrots and cook 2 more minutes
6. pour sauce over chicken and bring to a simmer
7. add in green pepper , pineapple , and return to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes longer , stirring to blend well
8. serve hot over hot fluffy white rice
demonstrations.review: This was EXCELLENT!  Great flavor and very easy.  The whole family loved it.  I wouldn't change a thing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
last minute cheddar chicken and noodles

this one was clipped from the back of the bag of skinner egg noodles. it's good for an easy, one-pan meal the whole family will enjoy. prep time includes chopping the chicken.

1. in 5-quart saucepan over medium heat , heat oil
2. sprinkle chicken with garlic powder
3. cook in oil until no longer pink , about 5 minutes , turning occasionally
4. add broth
5. heat to boiling
6. add uncooked noodles and frozen vegetables , stirring to coat noodles with liquid
7. heat to boiling
8. reduce heat
9. cover
10. simmer 10 minutes or until noodles are tender , stirring every 2 minutes
11. remove from heat , stir in cheese until melted
demonstrations.review: SUPER EASY, and SUPER GOOD.  Followed as directed and used broccolli, kids loved it and so did we.  Easy and quick.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: very tasty, good flavor and kids loved it.  Will certainly make again.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot stuffed cabbage soup

a nice, easy dinner served with buttered rye bread. the wonderful flavor of stuffed cabbage without all the fuss.

1. in a pot , warm the oil over medium heat , and saute beef and onions until onions are soft and beef is browned
2. drain off the fat , and add the tomatoes , bouillon , barley , splenda , paprika , garlic , pepper , and tabasco
3. mix well
4. put the cabbage in the crock pot , and top with meat mixture
5. top with beef broth
6. cover and cook on low for 9 hours
7. stir soup well
8. continue to cook covered on low for another hour
target.review: First, the modifications: I used 1/3 c brown sugar and 1/3 c lemon juice; I used a Napa cabbage and left out the Tabasco. I added a bay leaf and 5-6 stems of dried thyme. I also used only 32oz of broth, because I wanted something a little thicker. It came out DELICIOUS, and a LOT easier than full-blown stuffed cabbage. I loved the barley (instead of the rice) for the flavor and texture. I got... easily 10-12 meals out of it. I remember my grandmother making a mock stuffed cabbage but making little meatballs; I might try doing that next time instead of browning the meat first.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
angel hair pasta w  lemon   chicken

really quick and easy

1. cook pasta according to instructions
2. toss hot pasta with remaining ingredients
3. add salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: I had leftovers of recipe #378371 so I used that. I melted 1/4 c butter and added one garlic clove, grated (could've used two), the zest and juice of one lemon, and not-quite 2 T of parsley. I put the chicken in the steamer basket of my pot to heat while the pasta cooked (which left it a little overcooked, sadly). I added the al dente pasta to the lemon butter and tossed well while I cut up the chicken. I added the chicken and served it up! Quite good, and easy as could be.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new england pork and applesauce

with apples and applesauce plus several other nice but simple ingredients,using a pork loin.from a cookbook of new england recipes.

1. in large dutch oven over med-high heat combine pork , applesauce , cinnamon , nutmeg , and cloves
2. cover tightly and cook 15 minutes , then reduce heat and simmer about 6 hours
3. about 1 1 / 2 hours before serving , add the potatoes , carrots , celery , and onions
4. fifteen minutes before it is done , add the apple slices
demonstrations.review: Very tasty! I reduced the cloves to 1/2 tsp (though it would have been fine at the full amount), grated in about half a nutmeg kernel, and added about 3/4 tsp ground ginger and 1/2 cup dried cranberries. I put it in the crockpot on low for 6 hours, then added the vegetables for another 2 hours, adding the apple in the last 10 minutes. Easy and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon scones

this is a recipe that i saw in my recent toh magazine and posting here for safe keeping.  the author of the recipe stated "i grew up with this very popular bacon scone recipe in scotland. it pairs great with a salad."

1. in a large bowl , combine the first five ingredients
2. cut in butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs
3. in a small bowl , whisk eggs and milk
4. stir into dry ingredients just until moistened
5. fold in the onion , cheese and two-thirds of the bacon
6. transfer dough to a greased baking sheet
7. pat into a 7-1 / 2-in
8. circle
9. cut into eight wedges , but do not separate
10. sprinkle with remaining bacon
11. bake at 400 for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown
12. serve warm
demonstrations.review: These were quite good. I used green onion, as others suggested, and didn't care for the texture. Next time, I will use regular onion or shallot. The bacon needs to be VERY crisp before going into the dough.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hole in the wall

i was taught how to make this by a 9 year old boy (j.r.) who lived in our neighborhood and played with my son.

1. heat non stick skillet
2. tear a circle out of the center of bread
3. spread a very , very thin layer of mayo to both sides of bread
4. place the bread in the skillet
5. add a very small amount of butter in the hole
6. crack the egg into the hole in the bread
7. cook egg till set and bread is browned turn over and brown the other side and egg is done to your desire
8. salt and pepper to taste and enjoy !
9. j
10. r
11. liked to put a little maple syrup on his
12. you can also toast the holes you tear out of the bread in the pan while egg is cooking and serve on the side
demonstrations.review: I've always heard this called "Toad in the Hole."

demonstrations.recipe_text:
walt disney s roast beef hash

in honour of walt disney's 100th birthday, here's another celebrity recipe from my collection.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. saute onion in melted butter until tender but not browned
3. combine sauteed onion with beef , stock and raw potato and put into a buttered 4-cup baking dish
4. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour
5. remove from oven and shape mixture into an oval patty
6. place in a hot buttered skillet
7. saute until lightly browned on both sides
8. meanwhile , in a second skillet , fry the egg
9. top hash with egg and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I will have to try this again, following the directions more closely. I didn't bake it, but just made it in a skillet on the stovetop - and it was VERY wet. I poured off over a cup of liquid once the potatoes were tender, but it never crisped up. It was very tasty (I added a minced garlic clove, a diced green bell pepper and some leftover Brussels sprouts which had been roasted with bacon), but was pretty mushy.

target.recipe_text:
tofu egg salad

i really enjoyed this! it was inspired by a recipe i saw on food 911. careful with the cayenne. (i personally like it a little spicy, but use your own judgment) i also usually only make half of this recipe. (i'm the only one in the house who will actually eat tofu!)

1. i always drain my tofu first
2. i cut it into 1 / 4s , wrap it in paper towels on a cookie sheet , with another one on top , weighted down with some heavy canned goods
3. let sit in refrigerator for 10-20 minutes
4. mash the tofu in a bowl with a wooden spoon
5. mix tofu well with remaining ingredients
6. chill and serve
target.review: This was almost not a five star recipe.  When I first tasted it, I didn't really like it, but I had to run out for errands so I decided to let it sit in the refrigerator and get to trying to fix it later.  I came back later and tasted it again to see what I could do to make it better, but it tasted much better!! I think what happened was the tofu had a little time to absorb the flavors, making themixture much more smooth, instead of a strong sauce around chunks of bland tofu.  So to those of you who are trying it for the first time, I recommend you do the same: let the mixture sit and let the flavors marinade for a while before you taste it.  Oh, and I also added little bits of ham to it.  Thanks a lot! I will be making this often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country white bread or dinner rolls  bread machine

we think this is the best white bread recipe ever! it is a tender bread with a slightly sweet taste. my dinner rolls using this dough are so good, everyone always loves them. it doesn't take to long to make them when the bread maker does most of the work. the cook time is listed for the rolls only because everyone's bread makers cooks at different rates. mine is older and a regular loaf will take 4 hours and 10 minutes. i have found that 15 balls of dough fit perfectly in the 9x13 pan with sides touching after raising the 2nd time but they can be made whatever size you want. i hope you enjoy this great bread as much as we do.

1. in bread machine pan , place all ingredients from flour through yeast in order as recommended by the manufacturer
2. select the basic bread setting
3. check dough after 5 minutes of mixing , if needed add 1-2t of water or flour
4. bake as normal
5. for dinner rolls
6. mix in bread machine but use only the dough option
7. lightly grease a 9 x 13 baking pan
8. when dough is finished shape into 15 uniformly sized balls
9. i always grease my hands with shortening to smooth the dough out and it helps keep the dough from drying out
10. cover and let the rolls rise in a warm , draft free place until risen to the desired size
11. i let them about double in size
12. bake in a 350 oven about 12-15 minutes until golden brown
13. after removing from the oven , brush the tops of the rolls with melted butter
14. take out of pan and let completely cool before storing
demonstrations.review: Delicious and so easy with the bread machine!! I made a little variation.  I cut back on the sugar, added some salt, chopped chives, grated parmesan and garlic, and came out with wonderful, fluffy garlic rolls.  Thanks so much!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
leg of lamb in the crock pot

i love lamb and was happy to have discovered this simple recipe using a crock pot.

1. combine all ingredients in a crock pot
2. cook 8 to 10 hours on low
3. remove roast and let set 20 minutes before carving
4. slice thin
demonstrations.review: My husband and I have been fearful of lamb after a horrible, tough and gamey lamb experience 10 years ago.  Aside from that, we are eager to try new foods and flavors.  I decided to try to cook lamb myself this one time, and I am soooo glad this is the recipe I picked!!  My husband and I ate almost the whole thing, a little over 3 pounds!! What little scraps we had leftover I am having on a Greek salad today.  This recipe is soo easy, and it's so good to be able to come home and have a real meal that is better than most "crockpot recipes" out there!  I did sprinkle some rosemary over the lamb, but other than that, I followed the recipe, and came out with great flavors, and a super tender meat.  Thanks for breaking our 10 year fear of lamb!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chinese style ribs

sticky and yummy -- a multiple napkin meal.

1. combine soy sauce , marmalade , ketchup , and garlic
2. brush on both sides of the ribs
3. place in a crock- pot
4. pour remaining sauce over all
5. cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours
demonstrations.review:
I loved the taste of the ribs.  I do have to agree with some of the other comments that the ribs were not sticky.  Having said that, though, some of the comments were rather harsh, in my opinion.  Those that want stickier ribs can add about 1/2 more cup marmalade and the ribs will be stickier.  And to prevent "boiled" ribs, the brown the ribs in a pan first and drain or simply trim off the excess fat.  My ribs came out beautifully, and my whole family loved it.  You just have to use a little common sense!  
Thanks for a great recipe, Mirj!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot thai chicken thighs

throw six ingredients into the crock pot and 6 hours later enjoy a delicious treat!

1. put all ingredients in crock pot on low for 6-8 hours
2. garnish with cilantro , scallions , and peanuts
3. serve with jasmine rice made with half coconut milk and half water
demonstrations.review: I must admit it was not quite what I expected, but very good nonetheless.  I took sugarpea's advice and used the garlic cilantro salsa recipe.  Thanks for a great recipe!! This yielded a very tender and juicy meat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon snowflakes

this is an easy recipe that produces a tart and soft cookie. i believe that it was clipped from a taste of home magazine several years ago.

1. in a mixing bowl , combine cake mix , whipped topping and egg
2. beat with electric mixer on medium speed until well blended
3. batter will be very sticky -- and i can't even begin to tell you how sticky it is
4. :)
5. drop by teaspoonfuls into confectioner's sugar
6. roll lightly to coat
7. place on ungreased cookie sheets
8. bake at 350f for 10-12 minutes or until lightly browned on edges
demonstrations.review: I tried this recipe, not really expecting anything wonderful to result from it.  I thought maybe I would get a good last minute cookie recipe.  I'm glad to say that I was wrong!! This cookie has a wonderful lemony flavor without being tart (which I don't like) and the next day, it had the same chewiness and softness as the day before.  Unlike so many so called "soft" cookies that harden and dry out by the next day.  Thanks so much!!!

target.recipe_text:
chocolate orange fudge

this is so easy and yet it is probably the best fudge i've ever had. i usually omit the pecans. my niece used this recipe, substituting 3-4 drops peppermint extract for the orange zest, and earned a blue ribbon at the county fair. even my 12-16 year old 4h girls had no problems making it. note: make sure you use fresh orange zest. dried will make the fudge bitter. also make sure you don't get any of the bitter white part of the rind when you are zesting your orange.

1. line a 8x8x2-inch baking pan with lightly buttered waxed paper or aluminum foil
2. set aside
3. melt chocolate chips with condensed milk in the top of a double boiler or in a bowl in the microwave
4. stir until smooth
5. remove from heat and stir in pecans and grated orange peel
6. spread in prepared dish and chill until firm
7. carefully remove fudge from pan using the edges of the foil
8. cut into squares
9. store covered in refrigerator
target.review: I absolutely love how easy this is to make and it's really creamy and rich. I'm not crazy about orange and chocolate so I substituted about 3tsp of Peppermint extract (I say "about" because I was making a double batch and 6 tsp was almost the whole bottle of extract so I just dumped the rest in :) )Then I topped it with crushed peppermint pieces and OH MY GOSH!!! it was so good. I had to keep hubby and daughter off of it since I was making it as gifts..I let them have SOME, I'm not that mean. I was trying this out because I was wanting something that was easy but looked impressive and tatsed great to make for teachers and I definitely found it! This is going in my permanent file.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww skinny chimichangas

this is out of my weight watchers cookbook called "take-out tonight!" this is an excellent low fat chimchangas recipe. it is baked, instead of deep-fried. the burrito comes out crispy with a moist and flavorful filling. this has 4 points per serving. you can top these chimichangas with your favorite salsa and, for an extra 1 point per serving, 2 tablespoons fat-free sour cream.

1. preheat the oven to 400 degrees f
2. spray a nonstick baking sheet with nonstick spray
3. set aside
4. spray a medium nonstick skillet with nonstick spray
5. set over medium-high heat
6. add the turkey , onion , garlic , chili powder , oregano , and cumin
7. cook , breaking up the turkey with a wooden spoon until browned , about 6 miuntes
8. stir in the tomato sauce and the chiles
9. bring to a boil
10. reduce the heat and simmer , uncovered , until the flavors are blended and the mixture thickens , slightly , about 5 minutes
11. remove from the heat and stir in the cheddar cheese
12. meanwhile , wrap the tortillas in foil and place in the oven to warm for 10 minutes
13. spoon about 1 / 2 cup of the filling into the center of each tortilla
14. fold in the sides , then roll to enclose the filling
15. place the chimichangas , seam-side down , on the baking sheet
16. lightly spray the tops of the tortillas with nonstick spray
17. bake until golden and crisp , about 20 miuntes
18. do not turn
demonstrations.review: These were really good!! I'm not a big fan of ground meat of any kind so I used a can of 99%FF chicken chunks. I crumbled and squished them so they were shredded in consistency. A 12.5oz can of chicken weighed out to be 8oz without the water. Next time I will make extra and freeze for quick lunches. Thanks for this recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s spinach   four cheese manicotti  vegetarian

i have been making this recipe for years, it is *the best* manicotti recipe hands down! --- i have made this many times for dinner parties and have made it for socials and large gatherings increasing amounts of coarse, i have even served this at my thanksgiving and christmas holiday table as an extra dish along with a turkey or ham --- to save time i always mix up the filling a day ahead and refrigerate this will also give the flavors a chance to blend together, or you may prepare up to step #9 cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours --- don't forget to cook the spinach first before using for this recipe

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. butter a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. in a skillet , saute onion in oil for about 4 minutes or until softened
4. in a mixing bowl combine the ricotta cheese , 1-1 / 2 cup mozza cheese , cream cheese , 6 tablespoons parmesan cheese , italian seasoning
5. beat with a wooden spoon until smooth and well combined
6. season with white salt or seasoned salt and black pepper to taste
7. stir in onion mixture and spinach
8. mix well to combine
9. spoon into cooked and cooled manicotti shells
10. pour half of the pasta sauce into the prepared baking dish
11. arrange shells over sauce
12. top with the remaining sauce , use a spoon to spread the sauce over the shells
13. sprinkle about 1 / 4 cup parmesan cheese over the sauce
14. cover and bake for 25 minutes
15. uncover and top with mozzeralla cheese
16. bake 5 mins longer , or until cheese is melted
17. let stand 10 mins before serving
demonstrations.review: Outstanding! Really very yummy. I used fresh spinach because I do not like the taste of frozen spinach. I also cannot put just 2 tsp of garlic in ANYTHING so I added more of that.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetarian  meatballs

"meaty" vegetarian balls. try taking them to a pot-luck dinner and watch the suprised faces when the diners find out there's no meat in them. also great in spaghetti sauce or meatball stroganoff.  1/25/07 editor's note:  peta has a list of vegan products, and lipton onion soup mix is vegan.  www.petaworld.com/accvegan.asp

1. mix first five ingredients together in order
2. refrigerate for 30 minutes
3. form into 1-1 / 4 inch balls and place on baking sheet sprayed with pam
4. bake in 400 degree oven until brown , about 20 minutes
5. place meatballs in casserole and cover with 2-3 cups boiling water and 2-3 cubes or envelopes vegetarian brown broth
6. meatballs should be within 1 / 2 inch of being covered with liquid
7. bake , covered , at 350 degrees for 1 hour
8. or meatballs may be prepared in a crockpot on high setting for 1 hour
demonstrations.review:
My family loved these!!! I do not like walnuts as a rule and did not want chunks of them in the meatballs, so I threw them in my food processor and made walnut powder!! If I had not made them myself I would have thought they were beef. In fact, my hubby (he does not eat red meat) thought I was trying to feed him beef. I had to convince him otherwise. They were a bit salty, but I disagree with the other reviewers on the cause. The vegetarian broth powder is VERY salty...I really don't think it's the onion soup that does it. I think I will cut down on that next time and add some wheatgerm for consistency if needed. I used "authentic Italian Tomato Sauce" #92096 and they were very tasty
***Update: I have since made these for potluck dinners and NO ONE believes me when I tell them that they have no beef in them. My brother in law is a meat and potatoes kind of guy and declared to my sister that they were "the best meatballs he had ever had!" I decided to experiment a little and tried the mixture in a meatloaf...very tasty. My next experiment is to see if it can replace ground meat in tacos or chili. I will let you know

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy sun dried tomato roasted red pepper and artichoke pasta

my variation of a 

1. cook bowties according to package directions
2. reserve 1 cup of the cooking water
3. heat oil in a large pan
4. add garlic and onion , cook until translucent
5. add tomatoes and roasted peppers
6. cook for 3 minutes
7. stir in red pepper flakes
8. add artichoke hearts and cook for 3 minutes
9. add whipping cream and asiago cheese
10. allow to simmer until it starts to thicken
11. stir in basil and green onion
12. season with salt and pepper if desired
13. toss with bowties
14. add 1 cup reserved pasta water to make it saucier
demonstrations.review: This is absolutely to DIE for. The first time I made it I burned the sun-dried tomatoes a little bit but it still tasted great. I will make this time and time a gain. It has become a regular in our rotation of favorite meals

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave peanut brittle

note your microwave needs to be 750 to 950 watt. if your microwave is higher need to lower your cooking times and if your microwave is less you will need to increase your cooking time. i'm sorry i did not update this sooner.

1. mix sugar and corn syrup together and cook on high for 4 minutes
2. add peanuts mix well and cook on high for 3 minutes
3. add butter and vanilla and cook on high for 2 minutes
4. add baking soda and mix well , mixture will foam
5. spread on well butter foil
6. when completely cooled break in to pieces
7. store in air tight container
demonstrations.review: This is exactly like the recipe (except mine calls for 2 cups of peanuts...makes it very peanutty...also mine calls for micro-ing 5 min with just the corn syrup and sugar then an additional 4 min after adding peanuts and butter and then mixing in baking soda and vanilla...no micro-ing after that) I use and it has been a hit for many holiday seasons. I like it because with minimal work I can have something that tastes great and makes a lot for teacher gifts. I'm all into recipes that yield decent amounts! One variation that is on the recipe I use (I'm not sure where I got it) is to melt semi sweet chocolate and dip half of the peanut brittle pieces in it (scrape the back of the brittle against your bowl to get off excess chocolate)...this makes it look very fancy. my youngest daughter's 1:1 aide at school loves it so much that she wants a tin of just brittle this year instead of the variety I usually do! :)

target.recipe_text:
baked ham and cheese omelet roll

this is an easy way to serve omelets. in our house, it takes me forever to make breakfast on the stove top! baking this is soooo much easier. feel free to add or subtract to suit your tastes (bacon, sausage, onions, peppers, etc.)

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. beat eggs and milk until fluffy
3. add flour , salt and pepper and beat or whisk until smooth
4. pour into a buttered or greased 9 x 13 baking dish or pan
5. bake for 10 - 15 minutes or until eggs are just about set
6. sprinkle with chopped ham or lay slices of ham evenly on top
7. sprinkle with cheese
8. bake for about 5 minutes more or until cheese is melted
9. starting at short side , roll up omelet while still in pan
10. place seam side down on serving dish
11. cut into slices
target.review:
Hubby & I loved this! I made it for dinner and added green pepper and onion. When served, it was pretty enough for company. This recipe is a keeper! 
My Blog: http://lambaround.blogspot.com

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easter nests with jelly bean eggs

originally from a peanut butter company, these no-bake treats are easy and oh-so-fun for the kiddos! :o)

1. break chow mein noodles into small pieces
2. set aside in large mixing bowl
3. combine sugar and corn syrup in large saucepan
4. cook on medium heat until the sugar is melted and there are bubbles at the edge of the pan
5. add peanut butter and stir until smooth
6. pour peanut butter mixture over crunched up noodles
7. toss until completely coated
8. let cool slightly to avoid burns
9. butter hands lightly and use approx 1 / 4 cup mixture to form a compact ball
10. make indention in the middle of each ball to resemble a bird's nest
11. place on waxed paper and let cool completely
12. place 2-3 jelly beans inside each nest
13. serve on a bed of green-tinted coconut for extra festive look
demonstrations.review: I have a recipe that is very similar to this, but less unhealthy (uses Fiber One cereal and no corn syrup). There are step by step instructions and photos on my blog: http://lambaround.blogspot.com/2011/04/worlds-cutest-easter-recipe.html

demonstrations.recipe_text:
krispy kreme doughnuts

i got this from my child's high school home ec teacher! yum!

1. mix together ingredients for glaze
2. melt butter in hot milk , add 1 tsp sugar and salt
3. allow to cool
4. beat in yeast , nutmeg , eggs , remaining sugar , and 3 cups flour
5. add rest of flour
6. knead for 5 minutes then allow to rise for 1-1 1 / 2 hours
7. roll out dough , cut into shapes
8. do not re-roll dough , then allow to rise for 30-45 minutes
9. heat oil to 365 and fry 1 - 2 minutes on each side or until brown
10. toss in the doughnut holes first , let those cook , and then proceed to cooking the donuts
11. let them cool on a paper towel - helps get the glaze to stick
12. dip in warm glaze
demonstrations.review: These did taste just like Krispy Kreme doughnuts. They took sooooo long to make though! If you're looking for a quick doughnut fix, this probably isn't the recipe for you. I blogged about this recipe with step by step photos: http://lambaround.blogspot.com/2010/02/krispy-kreme-doughnuts.html

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean s dutch babies

a simple and tasty breakfast/brunch treat.
this is an adopted recipe from the recipezaar account, and i am delighted to be the new owner of such a winning recipe.
if you would like the inside of the finished dish to be a little less "egg-y" then cut the number of eggs down to 3, and many many reviewers also found that just 3 tablespoons of butter worked better for them. either way they did it, they all agreed that the taste was great. enjoy!

1. mix flour , salt and milk well
2. add sugar
3. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each addition
4. this can be done by hand or with a stand mixer
5. melt butter in an ovenproof dish or cast iron pan in the oven
6. when butter is completely melted and pan is hot , pour in batter
7. bake at 425 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
8. serve with maple syrup , jam or powdered sugar with a squeeze of lemon
demonstrations.review: This is my favorite thing to make for breakfast, especially if I have company. I posted a step-by-step guide, with photos, on my blog: http://lambaround.blogspot.com/2009/03/dutch-babygerman-pancake.html

demonstrations.recipe_text:
denny s style french toast

i do not remember where i got this recipe, but my husband says it tastes just as good as what he had at denny's. i am just amazed at all of the great reviews on this recipe!! my family loves it, so i thought i would share it here and i'm so glad i did because it seems you all love it just as much!!! thanks to all of you who have tried it!

1. mix together the eggs , milk , flour , sugar , vanilla , salt& cinnamon
2. heat a large skillet , or griddle
3. when the skillet is hot , add 1 tablespoon butter
4. if the butter smokes , your pan is too hot
5. turn down the heat
6. dip each slice of bread into the batter for 30 seconds on each side
7. let some of the batter drip off , then put in skillet
8. cook each slice 1 1 / 2-2 minutes per side until each side is golden brown
9. add more butter , if necessary , to cook all of the slices
10. to serve , put on plate , dust with powdered sugar
11. serve with butter & hot syrup
demonstrations.review: Mmmm! If anyone is wondering whether or not this will work with regular, whole wheat bread (all I had!), the answer is YES! I took step by step photos for this recipe and posted them on my blog: http://lambaround.blogspot.com/2010/02/dennys-style-french-toast.html

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick and easy pizza dough

a very quick way to make your own home-made pizza.  this dough rises up nice and has a very light flavour.  it can also be made in your bread machine on the 'dough' cycle.

1. mix 1 cup of flour with all other ingredients
2. gradually add 2nd cup of flour until it forms a ball
3. use your hands to form and knead the dough
4. let the dough rest 10-15 minutes in a bowl covered with a dish towel or saran to keep it warm
5. spread out onto greased pizza pan and top with your favorite toppings
6. bake at 375 degrees for approximately 15 minutes
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This recipe is a keeper! It was so quick and is easy to customize. I love this recipe so much that I even posted it on my blog: http://lambaround.blogspot.com/2009/04/15-minute-pizza-dough.html

target.recipe_text:
cabbage and potato fry

an indianised way to cook cabbage, and our favorite preparation of the vegetable. if you have a grinder, take the trouble to roast and grind the coriander seeds - the freshly roasted flavor is worth the effort.

1. quarter , core and shred cabbage
2. heat oil over medium heat
3. when hot , add cumin and mustard seeds and wait till they sputter
4. then add finely sliced onion
5. allow onion to soften and then throw in the shredded cabbage
6. add salt , turmeric and coriander powders
7. close pot , reduce heat slightly and allow to cook until cabbage wilts
8. as soon as cabbage reduces in volume , add small pieces of diced potatoes and continue cooking on medium heat till potatoes soften and cabbage is tender
9. if desired , add in shredded coconut with potatoes as allow to cook as in previous step
10. garnish with coriander sprigs
11. goes well as a low-fat option with parathas
target.review: I didn't have the coconut on hand, but the dish was delicious without it!!  Served it with a vegetarian roast and bread--yum!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried eggplant  aubergine

this recipe appeared in "cooking light" magazine. this is a non-traditional way to prepare eggplant, but it really cuts the calories.

1. combine first 2 ingredients , stir well
2. spread evenly over both sides of eggplant slices
3. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , and italian seasoning in a shallow bowl
4. dredge eggplant in breadcrumbs mixture
5. place eggplant on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray
6. bake@ 425 degrees for 12 minutes
7. turn eggplant over
8. and bake an additional 12 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe!  I used regular mayo and homemade breadcrumbs and this was still so much simpler and healthier than frying the eggplant!  I went on to use this in eggplant parmesan but this would also be wonderful on a sandwich!  I've made this three times, but this time I peeled the eggplant and used onion powder instead of minced onion to save time and it was the best yet!  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted french vegetables in hot balsamic and olive oil dressing

a fantastic medley of french vegetables - fennel bulb, onions, garlic, red peppers, aubergines & tomatoes; oven roasted in a balsamic vinegar, caper & olive oil dressing! simple yet impressive and adds a real splash of colour to any meal. i make loads of this, usually with the vegetables listed, but you can add anything you like which is in season, such as courgettes; it freezes very well and is used in numerous recipes of mine, such as vegetarian lasagne, vegetarian shepherds pie, pasta bakes, hot vegetable salad and also a great recipe which i will post, called french roast chicken & vegetables in wine! great all year around, the only proviso is what vegetables you have in season.......however, the fennel bulb & capers really adds that oooh la la!!!

1. pre-heat oven to 250c or 475f
2. you need a very strong and rigid roasting tin , one that will not bend in high heat
3. place all your prepared vegetables into the roasting tin
4. the vegetables should be roughly the same size so they cook evenly
5. mix together your balsamic vinegar and olive oil
6. season the dressing well with salt , preferably sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
7. add the capers
8. pour the dressing over the vegetables and then very carefully give them a stir with a wooden spoon
9. roast them in a pre-heated hot oven for about 30-45 minutes or until they are all charred at the edges , are soft but not too mushy - they should still hold their shape !
10. serve alongside your main meal , or use for lasagne , pasta & pasta bakes , hot salads and also couscous salads -- the list is endless !
11. they can be frozen as soon as they are cool in zip-lock bags or rigid plastic containers
12. p
13. s
14. keep the fennel bulb fronds of greenery as a lovely garnish
demonstrations.review: Delicious!!  A great quick and easy way to use up some of the bounty of fresh local veggies right now (July in Pa).  I didn't have any fennel so I used a TBS of fennel seeds or so and some garlic powder instead of cloves.  It was still fantastic and everybody loved it.  The vinegar really does add sweetness somehow.  Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: Delicious made "veg" using Quorn brand chicken breast substitute and sauteed 1/4 cup onions since I had no green ones.  Thanks for an excellent, fast recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s potato kugel

this is mostly served as a side dish with pot roast and gravy, i have even made this for sunday brunch and served it with eggs! --- to save time the potatos may be grated and kept refrigerated covered completely in cold water for up to 3 days ---i like to also add in some cayenne pepper for a little heat --- for a lighter fluffier textured kugel add in another egg with 1 teaspoon baking powder --- for passover subsitute matzo meal for the flour.

1. set oven to 400 degrees f (
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan , then pour about 3 tablespoons oil into bottom of the baking dish
3. squeeze out excess moisture from the shredded potatoes with hands , and place into a large bowl , then add in chopped onion
4. add in remaining ingredients with 3 tablespoons remaining oil
5. mix well to combine
6. adjust the salt and pepper if needed
7. the next step is only optional it will speed up cooking time and create a crispy bottom and sides
8. place the baking dish with the oil in the oven and heat the oil for about 6-8 minutes
9. carefully spread the potato mixture in the baking dish
10. this step is only optional otherwise just pour the potato mixture into the oiled cold baking dish
11. bake uncovered for about 1-1 / 4 hours , or until nicely browned on top
demonstrations.review: Delicious recipe!  I really liked the idea of using the hot oil to help brown the bottom--the crunchy potato and onion flavor was fantastic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
e z seasoned bread crumbs

if you are using this for breading such as salisbury steaks etc, use 1/2 the amount of crumbs and you will have a stronger spicier mix.

1. take 12 slices of stale bread and let air dry
2. crumble and grate until into crumbs
3. let dry again
4. add rest of the ingredients
demonstrations.review: As I noted in another review, I'm so grateful for this recipe!  I was right in the middle of making Recipe #30522 (Zucchini "Crab" Cakes) when I realized I was out of breadcrumbs, and this worked like a charm.  I was able to use super-healthy whole grain, high-fiber bread, too and everyone thought they were delicious!  I used these seasonings with the excellent method of heating to 400 degrees from Recipe #134615 (to save time).  Thanks for a great recipe!!

target.recipe_text:
peaches and cream cake

i don't remember where i got this recipe but it has been a family favorite ever since i made it 8 years ago! my father-in-law requests it all of the time. it is easy to make and tastes wonderful. everytime i take it somewhere, someone asks for the recipe. i use a butter flavored yellow cake mix.

1. drain peaches , reserving 1-3 t juice for the topping and set aside
2. combine cake mix , melted butter , and egg in medium bowl
3. a soft dough will form
4. this can be done by hand or with an electric mixer
5. press dough onto bottom and halfway up the sides of a 9x13 inch pan
6. cover dough with drained peaches
7. to make the topping , mix the cream cheese , sugar , and juice with electric mixer until creamy
8. spread over peaches
9. sprinkle with cinnamon
10. bake at 350 degrees for 30 to 35 minutes or until crust is golden brown
target.review: This was awesome. My Aunt came to visit and she loves peaches so here I come to Zaar to find something different, she took the recipe home with her. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lone star firesnackers

a spicy, "hot-as-you-want-it" snack cracker.  so easy to make and keeps well (if they last).  my son-in-law is addicted to these; he even asked for a batch of them for his birthday present.

1. empty crackers into a very large bowl
2. mix together the oil , dressing mix and cayenne pepper
3. pour over crackers and toss with hands until all are coated
4. let stand , tossing occasionally until crackers have absorbed all the mixture and are dry
5. store in a zip-lock bag or a large air-tight container
demonstrations.review: I didn't know how these would go over so I only made half a batch. What a waste of time. I've had to make them twice since. WE LOVE THEM! Only thing I do differently is I triple the cayenne and add some crushed red pepper flakes. Perfect with chili or anything else you eat a cracker with. we wont eat a plain cracker ever again. Thanks TxBluebonnet. We love em.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
freezer buttermilk biscuits

another one of my favorites from grandma's best-loved recipes.  biscuits that you make ahead and freeze so that you have biscuits any time you want them.  i used these for dinners, sausage gravy and biscuits or whenever i am in the mood for biscuits with jam or honey.  preparation time does not include freezing time.

1. to sour milk , place one tablespoon lemon juice plus enough milk to equal one cup into a 2 cup measure
2. stir , let stand 5 minutes before using
3. combine flour , baking powder , sugar , baking soda and salt in large bowl
4. cut in shortening with pastry blender or 2 knives until mixture resembles fine crumbs
5. stir buttermilk into flour mixture until mixture forms soft dough that leaves side of bowl
6. turn out dough onto well-floured surface
7. knead 10 times , roll into 8-inch square
8. cut dough into 16 squares
9. place squares on baking sheet lined with plastic wrap
10. freeze about 3 hours or until firm
11. remove squares and place in airtight freezer container
12. freeze up to 1 month
13. when ready to prepare , preheat oven to 400f
14. place frozen squares 1 1 / 2 inches apart on ungreased baking sheet
15. bake 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown , serve warm
16. bake 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown
17. serve warm
demonstrations.review: I liked this recipe and will make it again. The biscuits are good but are not quite as fluffy after they are frozen as they are when you just make them and bake them. But they are easy to make and just fine to take out of the freezer and bake and smother with some gravy for breakfast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ugly naked chicken

the sweet tangy sauce this chicken cooks in results in delicious, sweet, slightly sticky chicken that is just delicious. it may be the ugliest chicken you've ever seen (especially if you skin the chicken first, as i usually do), but it sure does taste good.i usually grab a "family pack" of select chicken parts or i use drumsticks and yank off all the skin with the help of kitchen shears. a serving is two pieces each. i originally found this in one of my favorite community cookbooks, "enough to feed an army" years ago.  this is my adaptation and i gave it the name "ugly naked" based on my method of skinning the chicken.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. place chicken pieces in a 9x13" casserole sprayed with nonstick cooking spray
3. generously sprinkle chicken pieces with garlic powder , salt and pepper to taste on both sides
4. bake , uncovered , for 40 minutes
5. meanwhile , in a microwaveable bowl , combine honey , soy sauce , butter , worcestershire sauce , and lemon juice and heat on high power for about 30-45 seconds , or until butter melts and you can easily stir ingredients together- watch carefully so you don't overheat it and end up with a melted butter mess in your microwave
6. after chicken has baked for the 40 minutes , pour the honey mixture all over the chicken and bake another 10 minutes , flip chicken over , bake another 10 minutes longer or until chicken is cooked all the way through and is tender
demonstrations.review: This was very good and we will be making again soon. I made it exactly as posted and from now on I'll let the sauce simmer on the stove top till it thickens just a bit. BF LOVED it. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
charlie s famous chicken salad with grapes

a really great guy i used to work with would make this and bring in to share. we all loved it so much and would beg for more! sounds strange with the grapes, but it's so good! allow time for salad to chill.

1. combine all ingredients
2. chill
3. serve with just about anything- crackers , chips , rolls , bread or bagel
demonstrations.review: I have made this several times and we just love it. Only thing different that I do is toast the nuts. It is awesome. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon blossoms  paula deen

these mini cupcakes are packed with lemon flavor.  a paula deen recipe.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. spray miniature muffin tins with vegetable oil cooking spray
3. combine the cake mix , pudding mix , eggs and oil and blend well with an electric mixer until smooth , about 2 minutes
4. pour a small amount of batter , filling each muffin tin half way
5. bake for 12 minutes
6. turn out onto a tea towel
7. make the glaze while the cakes are baking
8. sift the sugar into a mixing bowl
9. add the lemon juice , zest , oil , and 3 tablespoons water
10. mix with a spoon until smooth
11. with fingers , dip the cupcakes into the glaze while they're still warm , covering as much of the cake as possible , or spoon the glaze over the warm cupcakes , turning them to completely coat
12. place on wire racks with waxed paper underneath to catch any drips
13. let the glaze set thoroughly , about 1 hour , before storing in containers with tight-fitting lids
demonstrations.review: I've made these several times now and everybody just loves them. It's like little bites of lemon heaven. I love Paula Deen!! I like to double dip them for an even more yummy lemon treat.

target.recipe_text:
bloemkoolsoep  dutch cauliflower soup

this is a great soup to serve as a first course, or with salad and/or sandwiches.

1. clean cauliflower and separate into florettes
2. chop the tender part of the stalk
3. discard remainder of the stalk
4. bring the stock to a soft boil and cook the cauliflower until just barely tender
5. meanwhile in a sauce pan , melt butter , add flour and stir constantly about five minutes
6. slowly add some of the cauliflower stock to the flour mixture
7. continue to stir flour mixture and add enough stock to dissolve all flour and have a consistency you can pour into the stock to thicken it when the cauliflower is tender
8. add nutmeg and cream to the soup , stir , and serve hot
9. for variety , you can omit the nutmeg , and add paprika instead
10. you can also add 1 / 2 cup cheese when you are combining the flour and stock
target.review:
good stuff
i add grated parmesan and spring onion
 i add chives as a final garnish
love it mate!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef   bean khoresh  a persian beef stew

this is simply lean beef and kidney beans in a delicious cinnamon and cumin-scented stew, with lots of parsley and chives and a splash of lemon juice. the unusual color is from turmeric, and it's best served with rice.

1. in a large saucepan saute the onion in two tablespoons of the olive oil until golden
2. add stewing beef and cook for ten minutes more , until meat is browned on all sides
3. add the cumin , turmeric and cinnamon
4. cook for one minute , stirring , then add water and bring to a boil
5. cover and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes , stirring occasionally
6. heat remaining one tablespooon of oil in a small frying pan and saute parsley and chives about 2 minutes
7. add this mixture to the beef
8. also add the drained and rinsed kidney beans and lemon juice
9. season with salt and pepper
10. stir in one tablespoon flour whisked with a bit of hot water to thicken the stew a little
11. simmer uncovered for another 30 minutes , until meat is wonderfully tender
12. serve with rice
demonstrations.review:
lovely
persian food is highly underrated
more recipes please!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic mayo  ali oli

whenever i ask what i should bring to a gathering, this is always requested! it goes well with everything! steak, hamburgers, chicken, pork, on sandwiches, in potato salad, on sausages (brats, dogs, polish), and on fries. it keeps well in the fridge for about a week.

1. put the egg , garlic and salt in a food processor
2. turn on , and whir until garlic is completely blended--i sometimes mash it first , even before adding it to the machine
3. this is very important--add the oil in a thin steady stream--no thicker than spaghetti , especially at first
4. continue to add the oil in a steady stream until the mayo thickens
5. add the vinegar and process a couple seconds more
demonstrations.review:
delicious!
spaniards eat this with everything and i have just had it every day for a week in the canaries and never got bored
it was particularly nice with the fried lambs brain i enjoyed

demonstrations.recipe_text:
egg fried bread

my mother used to make this, it is quick and simple. we serve it with breakfast, sausages, bacon and tomatoes. it can however be eaten sweet with syrup or jelly (jam in u.k. english).

1. beat the eggs and milk
2. put into a bowl and add the bread and soak
3. heat the butter in a frying pan
4. fry the saturated bread until it is golden brown on each side
5. serve
demonstrations.review:
we used to call this gipsy toast.
Strangely where I grew up my Sikh neighbours were very fond of this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cottage pie  authentic irish recipe

hearty, stick-to-your-ribs pie.

1. pre-heat oven to 375 degrees
2. brown the beef in oil
3. remove from pan and set aside
4. drain most of the accumulated fat from the pan
5. saut onions until tender , and then add chopped tomatoes and cook for 2-3 minutes
6. add broth and stir in herbs and seasonings
7. return brown meat to skillet and continue cooking for 5 minutes
8. transfer all ingredients to an ovenproof casserole
9. top with mashed potatoes dot with butter and bake uncovered in 375-degree oven for 30-40 minutes
demonstrations.review:
irish food does NOT  have tomatoes in!
I am from dublin, I know!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gratin of brussels sprouts

always look for the smallest brussels sprouts you can find. they should be no larger than the tip of your thumb, firm and tightly closed. i hope you enjoy this recipe from everybody eats well in belgium cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 450
2. lightly butter a medium sized gratin dish
3. in a small saucepan , simmer the cream over medium heat until it is reduced to 3 / 4 cup , about 10 minutes
4. trim the base of the sprouts , discard the tough outer leaves , and rinse well
5. place the sprouts ina medium-sized saucepan with salt and cold water to cover
6. bring to a boil and continue boiling for 1 minute
7. drain and refresh under cold running water
8. saute the bacon in a small skillet until lightly brouwned , 2-3 minutes
9. drain on paper towels then coarsely chop
10. combine the sprouts and bacon in the buttered gratin dish and season with the salt , pepper and nutmeg
11. pour the cream over the top and sprinkle with the cheese
12. bake until nicely browned and crispy on top , about 15 minutes
demonstrations.review:
superb idea for a superb vegetable
thank you bev

target.recipe_text:
bok choy dumplings

this recipie is from about.com.  it's my favorite way to eat bok choy.

1. steam the bok choy until wilted
2. after it cools , drain it and finely chop it
3. make sure there is no excess liquid
4. place bok choy in a medium sized bowl
5. puree tofu and egg whites in a food processor
6. add this mixture to the bok choy
7. add scallions to bok choy mixture
8. combine the remaining ingredients , except for the wonton wrappers , in a small bowl
9. add this to the bok choy mixture and mix well
10. to form the dumplings: put about 2 teaspoons of the bok choy mixture into the center of a wonton wrapper
11. pull sides of dough up and pinch them together at three or four points , leaving the middle of the filling exposed at the top
12. steam the dumpling over boiling water for about 4 minutes or until they look cooked through
13. when eating , you can dip these in a little soy sauce or other asian sauces
target.review: These were very yummy. Everyone in the family loved them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linguine with mushrooms and ham sauce

this is a recipe i took in a coup de pouce (québec)

1. in a big skillet , heat oil at medium heat
2. add onion , garlic and cook , stirring from time to time , for about 5 minutes or until onion has soften
3. add mushrooms , sherry or wine and cook for about 5 minutes or until mushrooms have soften
4. sprinkle with flour and stir
5. with a whisk , add milk slowly and keep cooking , stirring from time to time , for about 12 minutes or until the sauce has thicken
6. add ham , parsley , salt and pepper and stir
7. in the meantime , in a big casserole with boiling salted water , cook pasta 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente
8. drain pasta and put back in the casserole
9. add the mushrooms and ham sauce and stir to coat well
