5. cut or divide each cheese slice into quarters to make 8 small squares of cheese
6. cut or fold one piece of cheese in half
7. stack the halves on top of each other and place them on the bottom end of one crescent triangle
8. roll triangle up starting with this end
9. fold the two side points of the dough towards the center of the dough so that all three triangle points are on the same side
10. place roll on the sheet with the points facing down
11. repeat for each dough triangle and bake for 11-13 minutes or until golden
target.review: mmmm, yummy! I used slices of marble cheese in them. We had them with some Hamburger Stew. Very very tasty! There's something about the crescent rolls that I don't care for, the cheese and garlic powder totally covered whatever it is I normally don't care for because I loved them so much I want more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
diet coke sloppy joes

you can use any diet cola type soda for this recipe. the soda gives the sloppy joes a sweetness rather than tang.  if your a weight watcher you can count 3 points for the sloppy joe but add points for whatever you serve it on. the recipe is core if you serve it over couscous or brown rice.

1. brown beef and onion in a large skillet
2. \
3. drain well
4. stir in remaining ingredients
5. mix well
6. cover and simmer 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Fantastic Sloppy Joes!! My family has always loved Sloppy Joes but I usually use the seasoning packets from the grocery store....no more! My husband and kids LOVED them, my husband has repeated several times "OMG those were the BEST Sloppy Joes ever!" Had with Bread Maker Hamburger Buns Bread Maker Hamburger Buns.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade baked potato chips

i made these saturday night for company, very big hit and lf.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. spray a baking sheet with non-stick cooking spray
3. in a small bowl
4. mix cheese , salt and garlic
5. slice potatoes thinly and place in a layer on the baking sheet
6. sprinkle both sides with the cheese mixture
7. bake 10 to 13 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I hate to give a bad rating so I will just comment instead of leaving stars.
I was disappointed with this recipe. They would not get nice and crispy in the oven, the few on the tray that did were stuck to the tray and crumbled in tiny pieces(even with plenty of spray). I was doing some in the microwave at the same time as the batch was in the oven, I was able to do 3 batches in the microwave that came out the perfect crispiness while the one batch was in the oven and never did come out properly, I had to finish them up in the microwave.
I will definitely be sticking with the microwave method.
If you don't care for then nice and crispy then this recipe is great, otherwise I don't recommend it.

And a tip for the one using her peeler, some people use a mandolin slicer to slice the potato, if you have a meat slicer it works fantastic too, that's what I am using and it's so fast and easy to slice them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fudgy orange brownies

these are just amazing, you may find it hard to quit eating them!

1. preheat oven to 325
2. mix together oil and sugar
3. add eggs , vanilla , zest , and juice
4. mix well
5. sift together dry ingredients
6. add to wet mixture , stirring gently until just combined
7. pour into greased 8x8 baking pan
8. bake 20-23 minutes until done
9. allow to sit at room temperature at least 30 minutes before cutting
10. let me know how long it took you to bake them
demonstrations.review:
These are really really fantastic! What a wonderful flavor with the orange in there. 
Time was way off for me, unfortunately I lost track of how many times I reset the timer for a couple of minutes, it was either 28 or 30 minutes that mine took. 
These were just as quick and easy as buying the boxes of brownie mix, but were so much better with a nice rich flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate eclair dessert

who would have thought something so easy could be so delicious!

1. mix together vanilla pudding mix and milk
2. fold in whipped topping
3. line 9 x 13 pan with one layer of graham crackers
4. put half of the pudding mixture over the graham crackers
5. place a second layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
6. put the remaining pudding mixture over the graham crackers
7. place a third layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
8. heat the tub of frosting in the microwave for 30 seconds to soften
9. spread frosting on the top of the last layer of graham crackers
10. cover with plastic wrap and let set a couple hours or overnight in the refrigerator
11. cut in squares
demonstrations.review:
This is a fantastic dessert! Super fast and easy to throw together, and if you use the lower fat/cal alternatives for the ingredients it still comes out great and leaves you feeling not quite as guilty. 

There seems to be a variance in preferences to how long to leave it sit, we have now had this after it has sat for only 2 hours, after about 7 or 8 hours, and after more than a day. It tastes great all ways, I personally preferred it when it was the full day and the crackers were really soft(they never went mushy, just soft!).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy no fail make anytime turkey gravy

i have been using this recipe for many years, my family loves this gravy and i have served it to dinner guests over the holidays and always receive rave reviews! --- you don't need to make this gravy using all pan drippings, if you do not have 4 cups of drippings you may mix with chicken broth to make the 4 cups, or it may be made with only chicken broth, please see note on the bottom of the recipe--- this may be made slightly ahead and kept uncovered on top of the stove until ready to serve, just whisk before using if you have any left over this gravy freezes very well or you may reduce all ingredients down to half and for a thinner gravy reduce flour by 1 tablespoon  --- also see my recipe#314890
for more of my recipes visit www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. drain the pan drippings for the roasted turkey through a fine strainer
2. let sit and then remove any fat from the top of the drippings
3. add in chicken broth or water to make 4 cups if necessary
4. in a medium saucepan , melt margarine or butter
5. add in lots of black pepper
6. add in 1 / 2 cup flour plus 3 tablespoons
7. constantly whisk for about 3 minutes over low heat
8. slowly add in the 4 cups turkey broth / drippings
9. whisk constantly over medium-low heat until bubbly and thickened
10. use right away or keep warm over lowest heat setting , whisk again before serving
11. options to make this gravy using all chicken broth prepare as directed using 4 cups low sodium chicken broth and 1 tablespoon chicken boullion powder ---- or you may add in low sodium chicken broth omitting bouillon powder to pan drippings to make up 4 cups
demonstrations.review: Love, love,love this gravy! Make it every holiday and it's loved by all! I could have a meal of just a plate of potatoes loaded with this gravy and nothing else, it's just that good!

target.recipe_text:
garlic walnut dip

this unusual, very inexpensive, quick, and easy dip or sauce uses whole wheat toast crumbs and walnuts for body. the flavor comes from our favorite--garlic, lemon juice and olive oil. it can be used as a sauce for fish or spooned over slices of fresh mozzarella and tomatoes. serve it in a small bowl surrounded by red pepper and zucchini strips. top it with chopped toasted walnuts or parsley.  imagine you are in greece!

1. place the toast in a food processor and process into fine crumbs , with the motor running , add the walnuts and garlic and process until they are ground fine
2. add the remaining ingredients with the motor running and process until smooth , adding more water if the mixture seems too thick
3. scrape the mixture into a bowl , and season to taste with salt and pepper
4. serve immediately ot it will turn dark in color
target.review: All I can say is that this is really, really good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomatoes provencales

an overabundance of vine-ripened tomatoes? lucky you! this is the recipe you want to make. from elizabeth david's 'a book of mediterranean food'.

1. preheat broiler in oven
2. have baking rack in centre rack of oven
3. with a sharp knife make several incisions crosswise in pulp of the tomatoes and in these , rub salt , pepper and crushed garlic
4. put tomato halves , cut side up , in baking pan just large enough to hold them
5. pour 1 tblsp olive oil over minced parsley and stir to coat
6. distribute parsley evenly over the 8 halves , pressing down lightly
7. drizzle a teaspoon of olive oil over each tomato half and cook under the grill until tomatoes have softened and are slightly charred on cut surface
8. serve with grilled or roasted meats
demonstrations.review: Fantastic and simple.  My 11 year old son who hates tomatoes enjoyed this.  Freshly grated pecorino or parmesan out of the broiler.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one pan oven greek chicken

this is a wonderful easy meal that gives comfort food a little zip!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in bowl mix oil , lemon pepper , garlic , and greek seasoning
3. cut potatoes into wedges
4. place in 9" x 11" dish along with other veggies
5. add half of lemon juice mixture and toss to coat
6. place chicken on top and brush with remaining lemon juice mix
7. bake for 1 hour or until juices run clear basting after 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very nice dish.  My family likes strong spices so I added quite a bit more lemon pepper.  After reading Erwin's review, I added 1 cup of chicken boullion and it turned out nice and moist.  My wife wants me to add this dish to the rotation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savoury mediterranean biscotti

good to serve along with a glass of wine.

1. in large bowl , beat eggs and sugar
2. add olive oil until smooth
3. in bowl , combine flour , baking powder , salt , pepper and basil and oregano
4. stir dry ingredients into egg mixture until blended
5. stir in cheese , sun-dried tomatoes and olives and combine thoroughly
6. divide dough into 2 pieces and shape each into a log about 10 inches long
7. place on parchment-lined cookie sheet and flatten tops slightly
8. bake in preheated 325f oven for 30 minutes or until pale golden and not quite firm to the touch
9. remove from oven and let cool on baking sheet for 3 minutes
10. transfer to cutting board and slice into 1 / 2 inch diagonal slices with serrated knife
11. place pieces on baking sheet and return to 325f oven for 20 to 25 minutes or until firm and dry
12. turn over partway through cooking time
13. cool on rack
14. makes about 3 dozen
15. store in airtight container
demonstrations.review: Excellent flavors.  Served with dinner as a side.  I must have cut mine a little thick since they didn't get real crispy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory lemon potatoes for two

this of coarse can de doubled!

1. combine butter , lemon juice , salt and garlic powder
2. place potatoes on lightly greased cookie sheet
3. brush butter mixture on the cut sides of potatoes
4. bake at 325 degrees for 30-40 mins , or until potatoes are done
demonstrations.review: Very nice combination of flavors.  Complemented Greek Baked Fish (recipe #76684) nicely.  Adapted to microwave cooking very easily.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tropical black bean salad

a favorite lunch salad of mine. the recipe was given to me by my best friend. original source unknown.

1. in a bowl , add lime juice , orange juice , olive oil , and garlic
2. stir to combine
3. add the beans and toss to coat
4. add the remaining ingredients
5. stir to combine
6. set aside for at least 30 minutes at room temperature so that the flavors can blend
7. can be put in the refrigerator but i prefer this at room temperature
8. i serve it on a bed of salad greens
demonstrations.review: Took this to a Hawaiian party as my dish to pass.  Got rave reviews from everyone, although I didn't much care for it.  Added 1c processed coconut for kicks.

target.recipe_text:
brussels sprouts in garlic butter

this is a recipe from joy of cooking... totally changed my mind about brussels sprouts! it's imperative that you use fresh sprouts, the texture would be way off with the frozen ones.

1. melt butter and olive oil in a medium skillet until butter is foamy
2. reduce heat to medium , add smashed garlic and cook until lightly browned
3. remove garlic and discard
4. add sprouts cut side down , cover , and cook without stirring on medium-low heat 10-15 minutes or until tender when pierced with a knife
5. the cut side of the sprouts should get nice and browned , with a nutty , buttery flavor enhanced by garlic
6. top with freshly grated parmesan and salt& pepper to taste
target.review: I made this as a side for Christmas Eve dinner and it disappeared fast.  I was quite suprised too!  If you need a different and easy veggie dish, this is it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s bakery buttercream  frosting icing

this is similar to bakery frosting and so much better than any canned!  ---  for extra fluffy frosting use heavy cream and make certain to beat for at least 3-5 minutes and remember to sift the confectioners sugar before using.  for flavor and color you can add 1-2 envelopes 3-grams each, duncan hines frosting creations flavor mix, any flavor desired.

1. in a large bowl using an electric mixer at medium speed beat together the shortening and margarine or butter with cream , salt almond extract and vanilla until smooth
2. add in sifted confectioners sugar starting with 4-1 / 2 cups
3. beat very well until smooth and fluffy , adding more confectioners sugar or cream or milk until you achieve desired consistency
4. add in the food coloring or flavor creation powder until the desired shade is achieved
demonstrations.review: I used this recipe to frost sugar cookies for my daughter's class. Perfect!  I actually made double because we love extra frosting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fannie farmer s classic baked macaroni   cheese

to me fannie farmer's recipe is the only "real" macaroni & cheese. it's from my 1946 edition of "fannie farmer's boston cooking school cookbook". with time on it's side - this recipe is hands down the best for traditional, homemade baked macaroni & cheese - comfort food.

please note: if you use cheap cheese you will end up with a bland and flavorless dish!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cook and drain macaroni according to package directions
3. set aside
4. in a large saucepan melt butter
5. add flour mixed with salt and pepper , using a whisk to stir until well blended
6. pour milk and cream in gradually
7. stirring constantly
8. bring to boiling point and boil 2 minutes
9. reduce heat and cook 10 minutes
10. add shredded cheddar little by little and simmer an additional 5 minutes , or until cheese melts
11. turn off flame
12. add macaroni to the saucepan and toss to coat with the cheese sauce
13. transfer macaroni to a buttered baking dish
14. sprinkle with breadcrumbs
15. bake 20 minutes until the top is golden brown
16. (you can also freeze this recipe in zip-lock bags for later use - once you have mixed the macaroni along with the cheese sauce allow to cool to room temperature before adding to your freezer - i generally pull it out the night before and allow macaroni and cheese to reach room temperature
17. i then add the macaroni and cheese to a buttered baking dish , sprinkle with bread crumbs and then bake for 20 to 30 minutes , until golden brown on top and bubbling
demonstrations.review: Best mac n cheese in the Universe.  First time I made this my kids almost died and went to Heaven.  They raved about it.  Now they want me to make it for all of their friends...kids?? LOL!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christina s killer dip

this is my sister's dip. she got the recipe while backpacking in europe a few years ago. she is now forced to make it at every party she has. people smell it cooking and stand drooling by the oven until it comes out! (many have not been able to wait for the cooling part and burned their mouths to get to it first).  you might have to make 2 portions.

**note: please check the sodium content before you choose a ranch dressing mix, because it will affect the flavor! some people have complained it is "too salty". please also make sure you are using only a 1 ounce packet; there are other sizes from various manufacturers. too much mix throws off the balance of flavors. my sister and i always use the hidden valley ranch original and we do not have any problems with it :)

you can also substitute half the sour cream for prepared ranch dressing and skip the dry mix. it will come out a bit wetter.

1. defrost the spinach
2. place it in a colander and press it until as much moisture as possible is removed
3. mix all ingredients , and blend well
4. put it in a shallow baking dish in the oven for 20 minutes at 350f
5. remove from oven
6. while still hot top it with remaining cheese , heat in oven again for 5 minutes
7. remove and cool below lava stage and serve
8. goes well with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: Eat this right away while it's hot with some small slices of french rolls.  Yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crumb topped banana muffins

these are so good. we love the topping.

1. in a large bowl , mix the flour , baking soda , baking powder , and salt
2. mix bananas , sugar , egg and melted butter
3. stir into dry mixture until thoroughly combined , then stop mixing
4. fill muffin cups 3 / 4 full
5. combine brown sugar , flour , and cinnamon topping ingredients
6. cut in cold butter until crumbly
7. sprinkle over muffins
8. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for about 20 minutes , until muffins test done
9. cool in pan for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made these today!!  Sooo good!  I made extra crumb topping by doubling the recipe for it and added extra cinnmamon to the banana mix.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: yummy

target.recipe_text:
spicy shrimp spread

simple to make and great to make ahead for parties and entertaining.

1. mix together the cream cheese and mayo until creamy
2. stir in the tabasco sauce , lemon juice , shrimp , parsley , bell pepper , onion , and garlic
3. place mixture into a serving bowl , and chill until ready to serve
4. serve with assorted party crackers
target.review: Haven't met a shrimp lover that doesn't like this recipe. It's really a good one. The garlic and tabasco give it such a zip you can't help but keep going back for more! Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bell s poultry stuffing seasoning

this recipe mix is as close as i could make to the original! =) easy to make with spices from your cupboard and no salt!

1. mix ingredients and store in an airtight container
2. sprinkle on poultry before roasting or make a stuffing
3. stuffing: melt 4 tbls
4. butter
5. saute 1 / 3 c
6. minced onion and 1 / 2 cup chopped celery until tender
7. salt to taste
8. add vegetables to eight slices of bread
9. add 1 / 2 cup water and 1 1 / 2 tsp of poultry seasoning to the bread mixture and toss
demonstrations.review: Thank you for a wonderful recipe that I needed in a pinch when I made recipe#84110 for Turkey Wings. It was excellent! This definitely is a keeper and I think buying poultry seasoning is yesturday's news.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
don t throw away that turkey carcass

don't throw away the turkey bones after you've demolished your bird! save them to make a fantastic turkey stock, which you can then use to flavor all sorts of soups and gravies. after you strain the stock you can freeze it in small tupperware tubs, or even in ice cube trays, very handy to have in the kitchen!

1. toss everything into a large stock pot
2. add enough water to cover
3. bring to a boil , then lower heat to a simmer
4. simmer for 1 hour
5. strain
demonstrations.review: This is just like I like to make mine. I hate to throw anything out. The only difference is I like to add a potato, and a few sprigs of fresh parsley from the garden, and a pinch of freshly ground sage. Wonderful, Mirj!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frugal gourmet s polish noodles and cabbage

this recipe is from "the frugal gourmet on our immigrant ancestors" cookbook. it's a great polish comfort food, easy to mix and serve, and it's easy on the pocketbook. i like to add sliced kielbasa to mix when done and serve with a tossed salad and good hard-crust bread.

1. melt butter in large skillet
2. add onion and saut until transparent
3. add cabbage and saut 5 minutes , or till tender but still crisp
4. stir in caraway seeds , salt and pepper
5. cook noodles in salted water as directed on package
6. don't overcook
7. drain well
8. stir noodles into cabbage and add sour cream
9. cook 5 minutes longer , stirring frequently
demonstrations.review: This one really took me back to when I was a kid! This was our Lenten special...I like the Kielbasa with it for other times though...great thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dirty shrimp in butter beer sauce

herby, spicy shrimp with a kick, in a buttery-beer "sauce". fast, easy and delicious, serve as an appetizer, or a dinner over rice or with lots of crusty french bread to soak up all the tasty, herbalicious sauce!

1. saute garlic and herbs in butter until garlic is slightly browned
2. add shrimp , stirring constantly , until shrimp are pink and done
3. pour in beer , simmer 1 minute more , and serve !
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful with the shrimp eaters at this house. I love the herbs that give it a wonderful flavor. That little bit of beer rounds out the herbs nicely. Very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas red enchilada sauce

this sauce can be used with beef or cheese enchiladas. the amount of "heat" in the sauce depends on the type and amount of chili powder you use.

1. melt butter / margarine in a sauce pan
2. make a roux by browning flour in melted butter / margarine
3. add spices and tomato paste
4. stir until well blended into roux
5. add water gradually , stirring constantly
6. heat until boiling
7. continue simmering and stirring until desired thickness is achieved
8. taste every so often and adjust spices as needed
9. once desired consistency and taste is reached , coat the bottom of a pan with the sauce , add freshly rolled enchiladas , then pour the remainder of the red sauce over enchiladas
10. place pan in oven and cook until enchiladas are done
demonstrations.review: This was very good and I could only wish there was just a tad more sauce. I did however add some oregano to the mixture but that was all I could see it needed. My dh loved it and I am sending it off to my sis as we speak. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe.

target.recipe_text:
six week raisin bran muffins

recipe can be made ahead and stored in the refrigerator for up to 6 weeks.   for an added treat melt one teaspoon butter and one tablespoon of brown sugar in each muffin tin before filling.   absolutley wonderful!
please note that this recipe is written to use with raisin bran flakes . . . if using all bran you will need to soak in water as noted by previous reviewers
this recipe is best if made in advance and stored in the refrigerator..

1. mix cereal with raisins , sugar , flour , soda and salt in a very large bowl
2. add oil , eggs and milk
3. allow to rest before use
4. store in a covered container and use as needed
5. fill muffin tins 2 / 3 full and bake at 400 degrees for 18-20 minutes
6. for an added treat melt one teaspoon butter and one tablespoon of brown sugar in each muffin tin before filling
target.review: Easy, easy.  Love just dumping a qt. of buttermilk in without measuring.  I like the idea of soaking some of the cereal in boiling water.  I had to use scale to measure the raisin bran.  I cooked about 25 minutes for the large muffins.  These were so tasty, and they disappeared fast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttery lemon squares

the title says it all. i ran across this yummy recipe in a booklet published by my local grocery store.

1. in a bowl with mixer , beat butter with 1 / 2 cup powdered sugar until mixture is smoothly blended
2. add 2 cups flour to butter mixture
3. beat until well mixed
4. pat dough into a ball
5. press evenly into a buttered and floured 9- by 13-inch pan
6. bake in 350f oven until golden , about 20 minutes
7. while dough bakes , in a food processor or bowl with mixer , whirl granulated sugar , remaining 1 / 3 cup flour , baking powder , grated lemon peel , lemon juice , and eggs to blend
8. pour onto hot crust
9. bake until the lemon mixture is no longer runny in the center , 35 to 40 minutes
10. remove from oven and dust with remaining 2 tablespoons powdered sugar
11. cool in pan on a rack
12. with a sharp knife , divide into 24 squares
13. store in airtight container up to 2 days or can be frozen to store longer
demonstrations.review: This will be a favorite.  I like LOTS of pudding, so I made an extra 1/2 of the pudding recipe.  Thanks for a sweet/tart treat!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kentucky biscuits

i got this recipe from a small free recipe book  from kfc    

1. preheat oven to 425
2. sift into mixing bowl flour , salt , sugar and baking powder
3. make a nest in the flour mix and add milk
4. add shortening and begin kneading with hands the vegetable shortening and flour in the milk until thoroughly mixed
5. add milk - if needed - to form , and mix
6. turn onto floured board , and knead gently 6 to 8 times
7. pat dough to 1 / 2" thickness
8. cut into biscuits
9. place on baking sheet and brown in oven 10-13 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was my first attempt at biscuits (other than with Bisquick), and I was so pleased.  I used the recommendation of the previous reviewer and cut the salt back to 1 t, and it worked out well.  I was surprised how quickly the shortening was incorporated just by using my hands.  Next time it will be a double recipe for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach  strawberry  mandarin salad with poppy seed dressing

this is a wonderful and refreshing salad that i got from best of bridge. i played around with it a bit and added a few other fresh fruits to it. this is yummy and great to offset a very rich main dish, such as my death to dieter's lasagna.

1. combine all dressing ingredients , mix well and refrigerate
2. make well ahead to allow flavors to blend
3. taste dressing and adjust sugar / vinegar for your sweet / tart taste preferences
4. tear fresh spinach into bite sized pieces , wash and pat dry
5. wash strawberries , drain , pat dry and cut in thirds
6. shake dressing container well and toss with spinach , strawberries , kiwi and mandarin orange sections just before serving , otherwise the spinach will wilt
7. this makes a wonderfully tart , slightly sweet and very colorful salad !
demonstrations.review: This was just outstanding.  My husband is on a soup/salad diet, so I am casting about for new recipes, and this is a keeper.  Not only was it delicious, it was a delight to the eye as well.  I left out the sesame seed and used fresh oranges because that is what we had on hand. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous greek salad

be prepared for the best greek salad on the planet! --- plan ahead the dressing needs at least 2 or more hours to blend the flavors, i sometimes add in 1/4 cup parmesan cheese to the dressing for a more cheesy dressing, all amounts may be adjusted to taste ----  to marinade the salad allow to sit at room temperature before serving, see bottom of instructions --- you will find this and many more of my recipes posted here http://kittencalskitchen.com/2009/04/13/kittens-famous-greek-salad/  ---also see my recipe #359292

1. for the dressing
2. in a processor or use a wire whisk process / whisk the olive oil with lemon juice , 2 teaspoons dried oregano , garlic , dried , basil , red wine vinegar , salt and sugar until smooth
3. season with black pepper
4. chill in fridge for a couple of hours before using to blend flavors
5. place the salad ingredients in a large bowl
6. pour dressing over
7. toss to combine
8. if desired allow the salad to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving , or you can refrigerate for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Redolent of my Mediterranean cruise, soft breezes,bright sun----seriously, this was so good. Sadly, I had to omit the cucumber because my DH cannot eat them, but this was one of those salads that made me feel as if I weren't deprived because I was not eating a "real" meal, that is, one with meat and potatoes. Just great...Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s buttermilk waffles

well, someone's grandma, but not mine. from gooseberry patch hometown favorites.

1. in a mixing bowl , add flour , baking powder , salt , and soda
2. stir to mix
3. add in eggs , buttermilk , and butter
4. mix well
5. pour batter into a preheated prepared waffle iron
6. cook until steaming stops and waffles are crisp and golden
demonstrations.review: This was a really good recipe. I refilled my waffle maker 6 times with one batch. My waffle maker is about 5 x 10 inches. Since I am only cooking for two, I think I would cut the recipe in half next time. It was a little on the salty side, so I just threw in 2T of sugar in the batter. I love the buttermilk flavor!

target.recipe_text:
liverwurst sandwich

my dad and i made up this sandwich one afternoon when i was a kid because we were the only ones in the house that liked liverwurst.  don't eat this if you don't want to offend anyone with your bad breath!

1. butter both sides of bread and toast until brown in toaster or in a 350 degree oven
2. spread mayonnaise on one slice of bread and top with onions and liverwurst
3. season with salt and pepper
4. spread mustard on other slice of bread and place on top of onions and liverwurst
5. smash down and enjoy
target.review: This is how I eat my liverwurst sandwich!  Never tried toasting it before - but should be great!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rose s world famous pancakes

these are truly world famous.  i have made them for guests from england and the netherlands as well as from nova scotia.  i remember the first time i ever made them. i was a fairly newly wed when my husband asked me for pancakes.  i very sweetly replied, " i can't make pancakes, i don't have any pancake mix." to which my husband answered, "don't you have a cook book?" thus begun my obsession of cooking things from scratch.  ( i was 14 when i learned you could make a cake from scratch).

1. preheat griddle
2. beat eggs and milk together
3. add dry ingredients and beat well
4. pour on griddle
5. cook until bubbles appear and flip over
demonstrations.review: Great recipe - DH says no more Bisquick!  Will be making these again!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sirloin steak kabobs

kabobs are a little more work, but are so worth it. great for company because everything can be prepared up to the grilling and you are good to go. cooking time is according to how you like your steak done.

1. mix together first nine ingredients for marinade
2. add meat , stir to coat , then cover and refrigerate overnight
3. alternate cubes of meat with pepper squares , small onions , tomatoes and mushrooms
4. place on charcoal grill , turning often until meat is done to your liking
demonstrations.review: AWESOME - Made this for dinner tonight and DH thought it was the best kabob I ever made!  Will be making this again to try on other meats!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortured chicken   beer can

i first saw these "tortured" chickens served at a bar-b-q. lined up on a serving platter, beer cans still in place! talk about a conversation starter!the dry rub sounds bizarre, but i guarantee the proportions blend into a delicious combination.

1. mix 4 dry ingredients together
2. use this rub inside and out of the cleaned , dry chicken
3. be generous
4. place 1 / 2 can of beer in center of roasting pan
5. position"bottom" of chicken over beer and slide chicken over the can of beer until the chicken is"sitting" upright in the pan
6. the fit will be snug and chicken will be secure
7. roast uncovered at 350 degrees for 1 hour
8. do not baste , do not turn pan
9. the beer will steam the chicken deliciously
10. when done , carefully remove can of beer from chicken and serve
11. chicken can also be carved while"sitting" on the beer can
12. i have"tortured" 2 or 3 chickens in the same roaster and did not have to adjust cooking time
13. this melt-in-your-mouth chicken will get rave reviews
demonstrations.review: I made this chicken tonight, and served it with Garlic Mashed Potatoes #117510, and Blue Cheese Chopped Salad #114912 - what a wonderful meal!!!  DH wants it again this week!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth chicken breasts

the mayonnaise make these chicken breast very moist and tender--enjoy!

1. mix mayonnaise or yogurt , cheese and seasonings
2. spread mixture over chicken breast and place in baking dish
3. bake at 375f for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Melt In Your Mouth is a perfect description of this recipe!  I made it tonight & everyone loved it.  Will be making this again - many more times!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate lover s cake

this is an absolute favorite of ours when we need a chocolate fix!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large bowl , mix together the cake and pudding mixes , warm water , sour cream , melted butter , and beaten eggs
3. stir in the chocolate chips and pour batter into a 12 cup bundt pan , sprayed well with non-stick cooking spray
4. bake for 50 to 55 minutes or until top is springy to the touch and a wooden toothpick inserted comes out clean
5. cool cake 20 minutes invert and remove from pan
6. you can top with a dusting of powdered sugar when cake cools if desired
demonstrations.review:
I make this cake - but my recipe is called "Cavity Causing Cake"!
It is wonderful!!!

target.recipe_text:
english cream of sorrel herb soup

sorrel is a very old herb that has been used throughout the centuries in england, as well as the rest of britain and europe - especially france. i have called this an english soup, as it does not contain any egg yolks, as french sorrel soup often does. it can be served chilled or hot, and is also delicious made with a combination of sorrel, watercress and other green herbs. you must try to use the small round tipped sorrel leaves, as the large pointed leaves are very bitter! sorrel is a purgative and an excellent detoxification herb, so you can enjoy your soup as well as cleansing yourself!! garnish with croutons and finely chopped sorrel leaves.

1. heat the oil and add the onion and potatoes , stirring all the time , cook them until they start to soften
2. add the stock & milk , season well with salt and black pepper and bring to the boil
3. simmer for 10-15 minutes until the potatoes are tender
4. 2 minutes before the end of cooking , add the sorrel & the creme fraiche or cream
5. liquidise the soup
6. serve it chilled or hot , with croutons and finely chopped sorrel leaves
7. to serve it chilled:
8. allow it to cool and store in a cool place such as the fridge
9. just before serving , add an ice cube to each bowl and pour the soup into the bowl
10. garnish as before
target.review: I found French Sorrel at the market yesterday and fell in love with the taste as I nibbled on a leaf.  I tried this recipe today and absolutely love this soup.  I added 4 cloves of fresh garlic along with the onion and potato.  I will make this soup again, thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free strawberry shortcake

this is a great recipe. it tastes just like the wheat containing sponge shortcakes that you can buy at the grocery store, during strawberry season. this recipe uses only 6 ingredients and you can find them all right in your kitchen.it is a great recipe for people that are trying to find an easy dessert to make for a celiac family member or friend, coming over for dinner. it's quick, its easy, and its really really yummy!!! try it, you won't be dissapointed!!!!!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. grease a 12-muffin pan
3. in a large bowl cream butter and sugar , using electric mixer
4. add the eggs and vanilla
5. beat until light and fluffy
6. in a small bowl mix the cornstarch and baking powder together and add slowly to the creamed mixture
7. mix until well blended
8. fill the greased muffin tins half full
9. bake for 15 minutes
10. remove from the pan while still warm
11. serve topped with strawberries , and whipped cream
demonstrations.review: Spring is here and the strawberries are amazing so I made this recipe for GF Shortcake and I love it!!  Fuss free and easy especially with my Kitchenaide stand mixer.  I used white sugar and added the eggs one at a time and mixing well....I thought I over mixed it but the batter was light and fluffy.  Perhaps they have too much baking powder in them? As they cooked the middles grew large and topped over the edge and there is an after taste of the baking powder, but you only notice it if you eat them plain.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey pot pie with stuffing crust  using leftovers

this is my favorite pot pie to use up those holiday leftovers. i tend to make more stuffing and gravy then i need for the meal so that i can use up the leftover turkey in this way. i love the crispy stuffing crust on the top. the gravy keeps the potpie from being dry.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. cook vegetable mix according to package instructions
3. drain well
4. mix together turkey , vegetables , garlic powder , sage , salt and pepper in a large bowl
5. if using a bottom pie crust , line a 9 x 13 rectangular cake pan with crust
6. prick all over and pre-bake until light brown
7. spoon vegetable and turkey mixture into the 9 x 13 rectangular cake pan
8. pour gravy over the vegetable / turkey mixture
9. top with stuffing , spreading evenly over all
10. bake for 30 minutes or until hot and the stuffing crust is brown and crispy
demonstrations.review: I made this pot pie recipe today with my Thanksgiving Dinner leftovers.  I used smashed red potatoes for the bottom layer. 3 cups of turkey, corn and lightly steamed broccoli for the vegetables. There wasn't any leftover gravy, so I combined a jar of alfrado sauce and a can of cream of mushroom soup plus about 1/2 can of milk. Topped with the stuffing and used the remaining sauce to drizzle over the top once assembled.  It made 4 lg pot pies and a small cassarole. I baked the cassarole for dinner tonight and froze the pot pies for future dinners. My suggestion is to be sure your pies are bubbly and browning before removing from the oven. I actually covered my cassarole for about 10 minutes during the baking time to heat thru the middle and not over brown the stuffing. Great recipe, thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best rice pudding

left over rice never had it so good ! this creamy pudding is the perfect way to use up the extra white rice from chinese take-out or from tonight's supper, and delicious enough to make you cook some up fresh, just so you can have this for dessert! tastes great warm or cold--enjoy!!

1. in large bowl , combine sugar , salt , cornstarch and nutmeg
2. add milk , egg yolks , and vanilla , using wire whisk to beat until smooth
3. add cooked rice , and pour into a 1 and 1 / 2 quart baking dish--you can also use a 9 x 9 square baking dish , but you'll need to decrease the cooking time by at least 15 minutes , if not more , so check carefully after the first hour
4. place baking dish into larger pan , and pour hot water into outer pan to create a 1 inch deep water bath
5. bake at 350 degrees , stirring occasionally , for 1 1 / 2 hours , or until pudding is creamy and milk is absorbed
demonstrations.review: The first time I made this pudding I loved the taste but it seemed too dry.  This time I cooked it for 15 minutes less, gave it a final stir and covered it with plastic wrap as it cooled to keep in the moisture. Very nice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet bread bread pudding

i got this from a coworker's wife years ago and it's always been my favorite bread pudding recipe. make sure the bread is as dry as possible - the drier the bread, the more it will soak up the custard.

1. grease a 9x12 pan
2. scald milk
3. add sugar and butter
4. mix until butter is melted
5. cool
6. break sweet bread into pieces
7. spread apple pie filling on top of the sweet bread
8. sprinkle raisins over the filling
9. combine cooled milk mixture with beaten eggs
10. pour liquid over the bread
11. sprinkle with cinnamon
12. bake at 350 degrees for 25 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This bread pudding turned out great!!  Next time I will cook it for 20-25 minutes so it will be moister. Serve it warm with vanilla bean ice cream

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet fuyu persimmon salad

got this off the internet. turned out to have a very nice flavor and was beautiful. i also enjoyed the textures together. be sure to use the firm, flat, non-astringent "fuyu" persimmon not the squishy dry out your mouth kind.

1. if you need to toast the pecans , you can do so in a dry frying pan on the stove top or in the oven on a cookie sheet
2. stove top would be over medium heat constantly stirring for a few minutes until lightly browned
3. oven at 350 for about 5 minutes , make sure to check after a few minutes and give them a toss
4. let cool
5. gently fold ingredients together
6. recommended to serve at room temperature
7. refrigerate leftovers
demonstrations.review: Excellent salad!!  Light and sweet with the crunchy nuts covering the crunch of pomegranate seeds, very nice

target.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
target.review: These are just awesome.  They come out of the oven perfectly crisp, but not oily, like you would get from frying.  I like to put salsa and sour cream when I plate them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger diane

we made this the other night and loved it!  i think next time we'll double the sauce...it's so good...

1. mix the ground round , salt and pepper together lightly and form into 3 1-inch patties
2. melt butter in skillet
3. remove from heat
4. blend mustard into butter , return to heat
5. saute hamburgers on medium heat about 5 minutes each side
6. remove and keep warm
7. add lemon juice and worcestershire sauce to pan and stir over low heat until well blended
8. return patties to pan and let simmer in juices a few minutes while spooning juice over the top occasionally
9. serve over toasted french bread
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I added garlic powder along with the salt and pepper before making the patties.  I had to drain the fat off the pan before adding lemon juice and W. sauce (plus more mustard) in the final step.  I doubled those ingredients and it made the perfect amount of sauce to spoon over the burgers.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy microwave mac and cheese

from "rush hour recipes".  nice and easy in the microwave.

1. in a medium saucepan , boil water
2. add macaroni and cook 8 minutes
3. drain
4. in a glass or microwave safe dish , melt butter for 30 seconds
5. blend in flour and salt
6. stir in milk until smooth
7. microwave 2 minutes , stirring with a fork after 1 minute , until thickened
8. stir in cheese until completely melted
9. pour well drained macaroni into cheese sauce , mixing well
10. microwave at medium-high heat for 3 minutes
11. if desired , sprinkle top with bread crumbs before serving
demonstrations.review: So creamy and so easy, I'll never make it out of 'The Box' again.  I added bread crumbs and cayenne pepper to give it a kick.  Just what I was looking for.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brady bunch pork chops

i think this recipe is an absolute gem. really, in all my years of cooking, i don't think i have ever made chops as delectable as these! crispy-crunchy on the outside, meltingly tender and moist on the inside. the key, i think, is the salty milk marinade/brine, and making sure not to overcook them. thanks to gourmet magazine for this one.

1. in a large shallow dish , like a 9x13 pan , stir together milk and first amount of salt
2. add pork chops and marinate , covered and in fridge , for at least one hour
3. turn chops once , halfway through marinating / brining time
4. when ready to cook chops , preheat oven to 200f and have ready an ovenproof platter
5. in a shallow dish , combine freshly made bread crumbs with garlic powder , rosemary , thyme and remaining amount of salt
6. remove chops from milk and let excess milk drip off , then dredge chops in bread crumbs , lightly patting crumbs onto both sides of chops so they adhere
7. place breaded pork chops on a tray , keeping chops in one layer
8. in a large 12-inch skillet over high heat , place butter and oil
9. saute chops , 2 1 / 2 to 3 minutes per side only
10. do not overcook , do not crowd chops in skillet , and turn only once
11. chops should be golden brown and just cooked through
12. place cooked chops on platter and keep warm in preheated oven
13. cook remaining chops
14. add more oil and butter to pan if necessary
15. i recommend serving with applesauce
demonstrations.review: Holy cow these are great!  I always had a hard time making pork come out juicy, and this recipe is perfect.  I leave the chops in the brine for at least an hour, then grind up fresh bread with spices for the coating.  I fry them in the pan with butter/EVOO for a few minutes each side, then put the pan in the oven at 400Â° for about 20 minutes.  My chops are too thick to pan fry the whole way, but they come out of the oven succulent and perfect.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I was looking for something to use up the hamburger in the freezer, and what a find!  I added tomatoes and green pepper to the meat mixture, and put olives on top before baking.  My husband went back for seconds, which he rarely does.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco bell taco meat for soft or hard shells

i use the top secret recipe cookbooks and have found the taco bell beef soft tacos taste pretty close, enough that we don't go there anymore!  i use this meat for crunchy homemade tacos as well.  this recipe calls for fat-free flour tortillas, and cheese.  i have made them both ways-fat full and fat free.

1. in a medium bowl combine the uncooked ground beef with flour and all the spices
2. use your hands to throroughly incorporate everything into the ground beef
3. preheat skillet over medium heat and add the beef mixture to the pan along with the water
4. brown the beef for about 5-6 minutes
5. use a wooden spoon to break up the meat as it cooks
6. you could heat up the tortillas a bit in the microwave by wrapping them in a moist cloth or paper towels
7. heat for about 25 seconds
8. spoon 3 tablespoons of meat into center of tortilla
9. place about 2 tablespoons of the shredded lettuce ontop
10. sprinkle about 1 tablespoon cheese over lettuce
demonstrations.review: This was very simple to make and quite good.  Following the advise of other reviewers, I only used 1 Tbsp of flour and added cumin, and I thought the taste came out perfect.  Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
yankee chili

thick and yummy chili. i call it yankee because it includes beans.

1. brown meat and onion and garlic in large pot
2. stir in remaining ingredients
3. stir over medium heat until mixture boils
4. reduce to simmer
5. simmer uncovered for about 90 minutes stirring occasionally
6. i like to serve with cheddar cheese and corn bread
target.review: I left out the beans because I'm Somersizing and shouldn't be mixing beans with meat.  I'm not a big fan of beans in chili anyway.  I upped the meat to 2 1/2 pounds, used a huge onion and about 6 cloves of garlic.  Since I'm from the Bronx, as is Richard, I'll call my adaptation of this recipe New York Yankee Chili (to be eaten while watching the World Series).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick vegetable soup

good and nutritious, great for a light dinner with bread or as a starter to any course.

1. chop up vegetables
2. dry fry onions
3. add chili powder and toss with wooden spoon
4. add stock and bring to a boil
5. add vegetables , cover , and cook 20 minutes
6. place mixture in blender and puree
7. reheat , if necessary , and add salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: So easy and delicious!  I quickly made this last night, using vegetable stock.  I left out the carrots, but added more zucchini and an extra onion, plus abour 4 large cloves or garlic.  I pureed the soup right in the pot using an immersion blender.  I've brought some leftovers in for lunch today, can hardly wait!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hreesa harissa  red pepper spice

used in tunisian cooking. hot!

1. mix all ingredients and place in a jar or lidded container
2. keep in refrigerator
3. used as needed
demonstrations.review: We are big fans of Moroccan harisa, this is the first time I've made it with caraway and am sorry to say we did not like the flavor much.  I'm sorry that I'm giving this a 2-star review, but based on personal taste the woody flavor of the caraway together with the heat of the cayenne and the cumin just did not go together.  Please don't let this review influence your trying out the recipe, as I said, it's personal taste and the flavor combination may work for you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
karfiol leves  hungarian cauliflower soup

pronounced kahr-fee-ol le-vesh.

1. place cauliflower in a pot with stock , milk , and salt and bring to a boil
2. cook until stalks can be easily pierced with a knife , but are still firm
3. in a small saucepan , make a roux , by heating the butter and mixing in the garlic and flour , stirring constantly until flour turns golden beige
4. add the parsley and white pepper
5. thin the roux with 1 / 2 cup of the cauliflower broth and slowly pour back into the soup
6. simmer until cauliflower is done and soup no longer tastes floury
7. let cool thoroughly
8. in a small bowl stir a little of the soup into the sour cream until smooth
9. return this to the remaining soup
10. reheat before serving
demonstrations.review: Big hit at my house last night.  I added a ton of Szeged Hungarian paprika, left out the sour cream and blended it all with my Thunderstick.  I don't mix meat with dairy, so I used soy milk instead of regular milk.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potsie s white trash trinity

the cajuns have a "holy trinity" of cooking which consists of celery, onion, and bell peppers. texas white trash (which i come from a long and distinguished line of)have our own holy trinity of cooking consisting of potatoes, onions, and okra. my family has been making this for years and i remember eating it while i was still strapped in a booster chair. if you love fried potatoes- if you love okra- and if you love onions- you will love this dish for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. may be served with ketchup but if you want real authentic white trash fare- serve smothered in creamy white gravy! you can get me to do some rather unpleasant things if you wave a plate of this at me.

1. pour oil into a skillet with a tight fitting lid and then add potatoes , onion , and okra and toss
2. heat your skillet over medium high heat
3. sprinkle with garlic powder and a generous amount of pepper
4. save salt for later
5. cover skillet with a tight fitting lid and cook over a medium high heat until potatoes are steamed soft , stirring about every 5 minutes
6. don't use a high heat yet -- you are not trying to brown the potatoes yet just get them soft
7. they should be soft in about 15-20 minutes , depending on the size of your cubed potatoes
8. i like to cube mine relatively small- i think the end result is a better texture
9. after potatoes are soft , remove the lid and turn the heat up to brown the potatoes
10. i usually only turn them two or three times because i like some of them browned and other ones still soft
11. when browned to your liking remove from skillet and salt to your taste
12. serve with ketchup if you must but a creamy white gravy is better
demonstrations.review: This was actually pretty good, and I don't even like okra!  I made up for that by adding another onion to the mix, and also adding some coarse-ground Hungarian paprika.  I have to put paprika in everything.  We actually had this for breakfast, with crusty rolls, lots of sweet butter and spicy matbucha (a Middle Eastern salsa).  Thanks for the cross-cultural experience, Potts!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice with a chilean flair

a chilean friend taught me how to make this. i was addicted to it for a long time. this dish is quite tasty when eaten with my other recipe 'dal curry'. enjoy!

1. clean rice
2. cover with plenty of water and boil until done
3. drain and rinse with cold water
4. saute chopped yellow onion in bottom of deep pot
5. when soft , add rice and salt and combine
6. reduce heat to low and let simmer awhile
7. prepare vegetable topping and let marinate
8. dish rice and top with vegetables
9. this dish is very good with dal curry
demonstrations.review: This rice is superb!  The only thing missing was a little hot pepper.  Instead of topping the rice with the fresh vegetables I mixed it in to the hot rice and let the heat cook the veggies a bit.

target.recipe_text:
weeknight thai beef  1 pan   3 carbs

my very "easy" favorite dinner. a 30 minute-meal that tastes better the 2nd day so leftovers are met with a cheer, not a groan! bet you already have all the ingredients in your pantry. this is so good even dh, who doesn't like peanuts, loves it, and my finicky 10 year old, too. it presents nicely on a bed of rice topped with fresh chives, and serve with asparagus bundles #111515 for a nice contrast of flavor. says serves 6, but serves my family of 4. i usually double the recipe. (f/uncle ben's) note-5/17-made tonight and doubled, and added rice to the final product, letting it simmer until cooked. even better! many thanks to lennie for photo.

1. start 6 servings of white rice cooking according to package directions
2. whisk together broth , peanut butter , soy sauce and lemon pepper in small bowl- set aside
3. heat large nonstick skillet on medium high-heat until hot , then add beef , onion powder , garlic powder and pepper to taste- cook and stir 5 to 7 minutes or until no longer pink
4. add green pepper and cook , stirring , 2 to 3 minutes or until tender- reduce heat to medium
5. stir in peanut sauce until well blended , and sprinkle with green onions
6. serve over hot rice- enjoy !
target.review: Yummy! I used smooth peanut butter just so the texture wouldn't turn off my daughter. Super easy! I added a bit extra soy sauce and broccoli. My husband (who is super picky) and my three year old both had thirds! Great for my low carb diet, although I think the sauce would be yummy over rice. I also thickened it up a bit with cornstarch and water.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
edamame dumplings

from the april 2006 issue of cooking light and adapted with the help of redmeatgirl.  we felt that the filling needed a little extra kick.  please adjust the seasonings to suit your own tastes.

1. to prepare sauce , combine the first 3 ingredients in a small bowl , stirring with a whisk
2. to prepare dumplings , cook edamame according to package directions
3. drain
4. rinse edamame with cold water
5. drain well
6. combine edamame , juice , sesame oil , cumin , red pepper flakes , garlic , and salt in a food processor , process until smooth
7. working with 1 wonton wrapper at a time , spoon about 1 teaspoon edamame mixture in center of each wrapper
8. moisten edges of dough with water
9. fold opposite corners to form a triangle , pinching points to seal
10. place dumplings on a large baking sheet sprinkled with cornstarch
11. heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
12. coat pan with cooking spray
13. arrange half of dumplings in a single layer in pan
14. reduce heat to medium
15. cook 1 minute or until bottoms begin to brown
16. turn
17. add 1 / 4 cup water to pan
18. cover
19. cook 30 seconds
20. uncover
21. cook 1 minute or until liquid evaporates
22. repeat procedure with the remaining dumplings and water
23. serve immediately with sauce
demonstrations.review: These had a really great kick to them with the fresh garlic and red pepper flakes. The dipping sauce was a bit strong, but maybe next time I'll use a low-sodium soy sauce so that the saltiness doesn't overpower. I left out the cumin per other suggestions. These reminded me of a steamed dumpling you'd find at any Chinese restaurant. I will make these for my vegetarian sister.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat californian rollwich

another recreation of a fun wrap i discovered at a box lunch restaurant while vacationing in cape cod. it makes me feel like i'm eating in a trendy cafe.

1. spread the mayonnaise on the tortilla , making sure to leave at least 1 / 2 inch around the outside
2. scoop the flesh from the avocado and mash , mixing with a dash of lemon juice to preserve color
3. you should end up with about 1 1 / 2-2 tablespoons mashed avocado
4. if your avocado is larger just save the rest for another sandwich !
5. spread avocado over mayonnaise
6. add the turkey and a thin layer of lettuce or sprouts
7. place the 3 tomato slices in a line down the center of the tortilla , if using
8. make sure you don't fill the tortilla too full or get too close to the edge , or it won't wrap properly !
9. carefully roll the tortilla into a wrap
10. cut into two pieces , if desired
11. enjoy a taste of sunny california
demonstrations.review: Yummy! Very healthy too! This was a good change up from a regualr turkey sandwich. I used whole wheat tortillas and since I don't care for raw tomatoe I used salsa, but my 4 year old ate it with tomatoes fresh from the garden. Hmm, she's never eaten one before, she must like this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ravioli with mushroom wine sauce  crock pot

a different meal for the crock pot, this dish is easily modified to fit your families tastes and you can add cooked sausage or ground beef to satisfy the meat eaters in your house.

1. combine mushrooms , rosemary , onions , red pepper , tomatoes , garlic , salt , wine , and water in crock pot
2. cover and cook on low for 4-6 hours
3. stir in ravioli after cooking has nearly finished and turn to high heat setting
4. if you are going to add any meat , this is the time to do so
5. cook for another 20 minutes
6. serve topped with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: This was good, but I agree it needed a bit more "oomph." I used white wine and added a bit of heavy cream after it was done to make more of a cream sauce. Using meat ravioi instead of cheese also adds some more flavor. Good basic recipe that allows for lots of alterations.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
emeril s mac and cheese

yum! i love making this.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
2. butter a 2-quart baking dish with 1 tablespoon of the butter and set aside
3. bring a large pot of salted water to a boil
4. add the macaroni and cook until al dente , about 10 minutes
5. drain in a colander and rinse under cold running water
6. drain well
7. melt the remaining 5 tablespoons butter in a heavy 3-quart saucepan over medium heat
8. add the flour , and stirring constantly with a wooden spoon , cook over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes , being careful not to let the flour brown
9. using a whisk , add the milk in a steady stream and cook , whisking constantly , until thick and smooth , 4 minutes
10. remove from the heat
11. add the salt , pepper , cayenne , and 2 cups of the cheese , and stir well
12. add the noodles and stir well
13. pour into the prepared dish
14. in a mixing bowl , combine the remaining 1 / 2 cup of cheese with the bread crumbs and essence
15. sprinkle evenly over the macaroni and bake until golden brown and bubbly , about 25 minutes
16. remove from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this and thought it was great. I used a blend of flavorful cheeses and added more essence to the milk/butter (just because I liked the flavor of the essence... alot!) and took note of another suggestion to add parmesan cheese to the breadcrumbs. This is not your boxed macaroni! My husband prefers Kraft, and I prefer this. I think it's the "grown up" version. Maybe I can use spiderman shaped pasta for him next time! :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
diet soup

nan

1. spray large stew pot with pam
2. saute garlic , onion , leek , zucchini , pepper , and mushrooms for 10 min , stirring frequently
3. thaw spinach in microwave until soft , add to vegetables
4. add remaining ingredients except blue cheese , bring to a boil , then reduce heat and simmer about 20 minutes
5. add about 1 tb of crumbled blue cheese to each serving
6. choice of vegetables can vary , depending on availability and personal preferences
demonstrations.review: Yummy!!! Quick, easy and full of good for you veggies. Made with a loaf of homemade pesto bread... warmed us up!

target.recipe_text:
swirl frosting

this is a family heirloom recipe. i most recently used this with mirjam's "ultimate chocolate cake"---with the filling she has in her recipe. this is just so good..........

1. combine corn syrup and sugar in saucepan
2. place over moderate heat and cook
3. heat till sugar dissolves and bubbles appear at edge
4. whip whites , salt and tartar till nearly stiff
5. pour hot syrup into whites , whipping constantly
6. add vanilla and whip until frosting stays in soft peaks
target.review: Loved it!! My ex mother in-law used to make me a cake for my birthday. And well since the divorce we don't share recipe's.. But this is the frosting. mmmmm its soooo good. I will make it often. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dark chocolate cake

while it takes slightly longer to prepare this recipe than a box mix, the resulting moist, delicious cake makes it very worth the little extra time. i consider this 'perfect' chocolate cake. this cake is excellent with  both with recipe #261024 and recipe #208959 (the dark flavor version). (i use recipe #95416 when i'm decorating the cake.) i love how the leftovers are still moist even a day or two later. (i store my loosely covered with plastic wrap.)
my father adores this cake with recipe #261024 on it. for his birthday, father's day etc. i make him cupcakes with the icing on them and individually wrap them. he keeps them in his freezer for when he wants "a piece of cake". he claims they are as good as when they are fresh. 
(even though it isn't where i got the recipe from so i can't vouch for it, reviewers have said it is the recipe on the hershey's cocoa can. i would recommend using their special dark cocoa if possible.)

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour two 9 inch round baking pans or one 13x9 inch pan
3. in large mixer bowl , stir together dry ingredients
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in boiling water by hand
7. i usually use between 2 / 3 & 3 / 4 cups
8. the cake is still very moist but it doesn't seem to "fall" as much as it cools
9. this might have to do with our high humidity or brand of flour or other factors so i don't know if it will work for everyone
10. pour into prepared pan
11. bake 30 to 35 minutes for round 9-inch pans , 35 to 40 minutes for rectangular pan or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. because they have a tendency to overflow if you fill them more than 2 / 3 full , i usually get about 27-28 cupcakes per batch
13. bake for approximately 18-20 minutes
14. cool 10 minutes
15. remove from pan to wire racks
16. please
17. chocolate drink mixes that you add to milk or water to drink will not work in this recipe
demonstrations.review: Not a bad recipe coming from Hershey!! I had to laugh when I reached for my box of cocoa and there was the recipe almost word for word... Here I was looking for a new recipe!! I love Hershey's but was looking for one with more a dark chocolate taste! Guess if ya can't beatem' you copy them right??? Becareful of copy right laws..

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic spaghetti sauce

i adopted this recipe from zaar some time ago and finally got round to trying it myself. it's quick and simple and full of fresh flavours. i prefer using basil but the original recipe stated parsley so i left it here for you to choose. try adding some sliced black olives, fried or marinated mushrooms or sun blush tomatoes at the end.

1. to make spaghetti sauce , cook garlic in butter and olive oil over medium low heat just until the garlic is soft but not browned
2. stir in the parsley or basil and cook for 2 minutes until the herbs are limp but still green
3. pour sauce hot over cooked spaghetti , toss lightly to coat and top with parmesan cheese
4. serve with french bread and extra parmasan cheese at the table
5. this garlic sauce will cover 3 / 4-1 pound of spaghetti or other pasta
demonstrations.review: This is the best!! My sister sent me the link and I am so greatfull. My hubby is picky but he loved it. I did add some sliced chicken breast to add some substance.. He has to have some kinda something in it.. LOL.. Anyways.. Thanks.. Will use over  and over..

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible peanut butter cookies

these are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!

1. mix peanut butter , sugar , and egg together until smooth
2. drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart
3. if desired , roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet
4. press with fork
5. press again in opposite direction
6. bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
7. do not brown
8. do not over bake
demonstrations.review: Omg, these are amazing. Like the last post I had seen this recipe here before but never tried it.. These are the fastest pb cookies ever. And mmm so good. I did 1/2 brown sugar and 1/2 white like some one else suggested.. Will never use another recipe again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple glaze for baked ham

posted at the request of my sister. glazing a ham while cooking is wonderful but the first person to the platter usually makes off the the glazed ends and the rest of the people get a "glazed rim". the solution in our house is to make lots of glaze and pour it over each slice!

1. place all ingredients in a small saucepan including the juice / syrup from the pineapple
2. turn heat on to medium and stir constantly to prevent burning
3. continue to heat until mixture thickens and comes to a boil
4. allow mixture to boil for approximately 1 minute
5. if mixture refuses to thicken , add more cornstarch- a little at a time
6. pour finished sauce into a serving bowl , complete with a ladle , and let your guests pour it over baked sliced ham
demonstrations.review: I couldn't find my moms recipe anywhere and I had forgot to put a glaze on while cooking.. This was perfect.. Taste just like it but not fus.. Thanks alot you were a life saver..

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brady bunch pork chops

i think this recipe is an absolute gem. really, in all my years of cooking, i don't think i have ever made chops as delectable as these! crispy-crunchy on the outside, meltingly tender and moist on the inside. the key, i think, is the salty milk marinade/brine, and making sure not to overcook them. thanks to gourmet magazine for this one.

1. in a large shallow dish , like a 9x13 pan , stir together milk and first amount of salt
2. add pork chops and marinate , covered and in fridge , for at least one hour
3. turn chops once , halfway through marinating / brining time
4. when ready to cook chops , preheat oven to 200f and have ready an ovenproof platter
5. in a shallow dish , combine freshly made bread crumbs with garlic powder , rosemary , thyme and remaining amount of salt
6. remove chops from milk and let excess milk drip off , then dredge chops in bread crumbs , lightly patting crumbs onto both sides of chops so they adhere
7. place breaded pork chops on a tray , keeping chops in one layer
8. in a large 12-inch skillet over high heat , place butter and oil
9. saute chops , 2 1 / 2 to 3 minutes per side only
10. do not overcook , do not crowd chops in skillet , and turn only once
11. chops should be golden brown and just cooked through
12. place cooked chops on platter and keep warm in preheated oven
13. cook remaining chops
14. add more oil and butter to pan if necessary
15. i recommend serving with applesauce
demonstrations.review: Made these for some of the hubbys co workes! Omg they are amazing.. Fast, easy & soo yummy.. ty will use this one forever..

target.recipe_text:
shrimp in white wine

this is again another recipe for world tour. off of greek cuisine again.

1. in a deep skillet , heat the olive oil and saute the chives for 2 minutes
2. add the mussels or shrimps , and cook for 1 minute
3. pour in the wine , and when it starts to boil , add the mustard , chili pepper flakes , half the parsley , and the water or stock
4. cook for about 3 minutes , then add the lemon juice , feta cheese , and the rest of the parsley
5. do not stir , but shake the pan to distribute the ingredients evenly
6. remove from the heat and add salt and pepper to taste
7. serve
8. it can also be refrigerated for 2 to 3 days
target.review: This was good, but I would reccomend using fish stock, or chicken stock to increase the flavour.  Thanx!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
domatosalta choritiki  greek tomato salad

this is a country styled tomato salad. use full ripe tomatoes for best result

1. wash tomatoes , remove the green stem part and cut into slices
2. wash chilis and cut into thin rings
3. if you like it hot use 2 chilis
4. if you like it mild use one or mild chilis
5. dice the olives
6. dice the feta cheese
7. arrange tomatoes on a large plate or bowl , sprinkle the chilis , olives , feta and capers over the tomatoes
8. if you like you can add anchovis , which you cut into thin stripes
9. make a vinaigrette of oil , vinegar , oregano
10. salt and pepper to taste
11. drizzle vinaigrette over tomato salad and serve
demonstrations.review: This was really tasty.  I added some sliced cucumber, and some sweet onion.  I will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortilla omelet wrap

another one for the omelet lovers among us!

1. whip eggs , half and half , salt and pepper to taste
2. warm tortilla in skillet and set aside
3. melt butter in a 10" non-stick skillet that has been coated with cooking spray and heat until bubbly
4. pour in egg mixture and pull eggs toward the center from all sides
5. remove from heat when the eggs are still moist , but no longer run
6. top with remaining ingredients , being sure to sprinkle over entire omelet
7. slide omelet onto the warmed tortilla and roll up bottom edge , then fold in sides about 1" and continue rolling until completely rolled
8. lay in plate seam side down
9. let rest for a couple of minutes and cut in half
10. serve with favorite salsa or relish
demonstrations.review: This was an awesome lunch!  I really like how it turned out! Mmm!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter and banana s mores

a new twist on an old favorite.

1. roast marshmallows until lightly browned and melted inside
2. spread or top each of the 4 honey maid honey graham squares with 1 / 4 of the filling
3. top each square with marshmallow
4. top with fruit and second graham square
5. press top lightly to secure
6. serve warm
7. microwave directions:
8. place 1 graham square on microwaveable plate
9. top with filling and 1 marshmallow
10. microwave on high 15 to 20 sec
11. or until marshmallow puffs
12. top with fruit and second graham square
demonstrations.review:
The only way to properly describe this is to put on your best BARRY WHITE voice, and repeat after me:
"oooooh yea baby"

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mango mania lassi

come summer time and mangoes it is in my house! we enjoy making this one quite alot. hope you too do!

1. put the yogurt , sugar and cold water in a blend
2. blend at high speed
3. add mango puree
4. mix well
5. take 2 glasses and put some crushed ice in them
6. pour your mango lassi over it and serve
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Made this for breakfast today...WOW!  This was awesome!!  The only problem is how fast I drank it..LOL  I added some sliced Nectarines, and strawberries on top. This was great.  Thanx for a keeper!
~Little Italy~

demonstrations.recipe_text:
just macaroni  and cheese

simply rich mac & cheese

1. in 2 quart sauce pan melt butter add flour cook stirring til starts to look like cornmeal
2. add hot half& half , add seasonings , stirring quickly with whisk
3. add cheese stirring til cheese melts
4. mix with macaroni in 2qt
5. casserole
6. toss bread crumbs with melted butter , sprinkle over top
7. bake 350f for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this tonight for dinner.  I love onion, so I added 1/4 cup of minced onion to the cheese sauce before pouring it on the macaroni, and omitted the bread crumbs...this was a whole new mouth watering experience! Thanks so much for posting! Mmmmm!!! :)

target.recipe_text:
sweet potato fries with cinnamon and maple syrup  light

from r. reisman.

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. spray rimmed baking sheet with cooking spray
3. cut sweet potatoes lengthwise in half and each half into 4 wedges
4. place on prepared baking sheet
5. in a small bowl , combine remaining ingredients
6. brush half of mixture over sweet potatoes
7. bake in centre of oven for 20 minutes
8. turn and brush with remaining maple syrup mixture
9. bake another 15 minutes or until tender
target.review: very good! I put them underneath a low broiler to try and crisp em up a bit...burned a few but the rest were delish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish rosie s irish soda bread

this irish soda bread recipe was passed on to me by a dear friend of my mother's who was born and raised in ireland. it's the best irish soda bread i have ever had. it is much higher, lighter and softer than most other recipes i have seen. it has an excellent flavor and texture, as well.

1. combine dry ingredients together in a large bowl
2. in a small bowl beat eggs and stir in sour cream
3. add the egg and sour cream mixture to the dry ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon
4. batter will be very thick
5. add the raisins and caraway seeds and stir well with wooden spoon or knead in with your hands
6. place batter in a greased 9 inch springform pan
7. dust the top with enough flour so that you can pat the batter like a bread dough evenly in the pan without it sticking to your hands
8. with a knife make a shallow crisscross on the top
9. bake for 50 minutes in a preheated 350f oven
demonstrations.review: I never reviewed this when i made it last year and here i am looking up the recipe again for our St. Patrick's day family dinner tomorrow night. It is the best soda bread i have ever had. Just the right sweetnes and it's not overly dense. Actually it's quite light which is really nice. I leave out the caraway seeds for my mom.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate banana cake

this is a very moist & very fudgey cake. it tastes best the second day.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. cream margarine with sugar and eggs
3. mix in banana and vanilla
4. mix flour with remaining dry ingredients
5. add flour mixture to margarine mixture in 3 parts , alternately with sour milk
6. begin and end with flour
7. spread in 2 greased 8" cake pans
8. bake in oven about 40 minutes
9. when cool , frost generously with chocolate butter frosting
demonstrations.review:
I'm enjoying a piece right now.
Very good cake....moist and not overly sweet with just the perfect chocolate/banana flavor.
Doesn't need any frosting, just plain or some powdered sugar is perfect. I baked in a 13 X 9 inch pan for 35 minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eye of round roast

this is a juicy, fall apart tender roast. the secret is in the baking, tightly covered and slow cooked with moist heat. can be made a day ahead, and just reheat for 30-45 minutes with the same excellent results.

1. place roast in a lightly greased dutch oven , and top with a mound of sliced onions
2. stir together remaining ingredients and pour over the top of the roast , covering all
3. before placing lid on dutch oven , cover with a double layer of aluminum foil , molding to pot
4. place lid on top
5. bake , tightly covered , at 325 degrees for 3 hours and 30 minutes or until tender
6. slowly cooked with moist heat is going to make this roast delicious
7. after baking , cool roast completely , remove from dutch oven , reserving the gravy
8. cut roast into slices , about 1 / 4 inch thick , and arrange in a 13 x 9 inch baking dish
9. i use an electric knife for perfect slices
10. pour gravy over sliced meat covering all , cover and refrigerate
11. to reheat: bake tightly covered , at 325 degrees for 30 minutes or until thouroughly heated
demonstrations.review:
This made a very flavorful and tender roast even though I overcooked it a bit to medium well..
I used cream of brocolli soup and au jus mix.  Cream of mushroom would have been better but the cream of brocolli tasted fine too.
I will follow your cooking instructions more closely next time.  I am always late in starting dinner so I roasted at 350 to speed up the cooking but you are right, slower is better.
We enjoyed this, my four year old and her grandmother both had three helpings. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
