target.review: This grape salad is a 10+.  Who would have imagined grapes in a mixture of cream cheese and sour cream and then topped with brown sugar and pecans.  I will be making this again for sure.  Thanks for this keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized chicken wings

nan

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. place chicken in a 9x13-inch baking dish
3. mix the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper and pour over the chicken
4. bake at 375f for one hour or until sauce is caramelized
demonstrations.review: These wings are the greatest and so easy to make.  Thank you for this keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple ranch house meatloaf

easy and tasty served either hot or cold, wonderful sliced cold for a picnic or sandwiches. we have enjoyed this basic meatloaf for many years.try a change, instead of the usual topping, try your favourite salsa brushed on top, a nice chipotle medium or hot salsa is wonderful on it.

1. mix all the meat loaf ingredients together
2. pack into a 5 x 9 loaf pan
3. bake at 325f degrees for 1 1 / 4 hours
4. remove from oven , turn out of pan and place on an ovenproof serving dish
5. topping: mix the topping ingredients
6. brush over the meat loaf and return to the oven for 30 minutes or longer
7. defrost and reheat or use sliced cold
8. alternate topping
9. 4 tablespoons chilli sauce
10. 3 tablespoons splenda
11. 4 tablespoons spreadable soft cream cheese - light
12. 1 tablespoon hot horseradish
13. 1 teaspoon dry mustard
14. combine all and brush on top of meatloaf instead of above topping
demonstrations.review: Should have known it was a 'Derf' recipe.  This is a very good, basic meatloaf.  I have grown tired of everything made with onion soup mix and mushroom soup, so this was a real treat!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma ila nelson s lemon dream bars

this recipe came from whitefish, montana and was given to me years ago by a dear friend.  it had been passed down from her family for generations.  i love the fragrance and flavor of lemons.  this is by far the easiest and best tasting lemon bar i have come across.  i have made it for bake sales, gifts, and simply to serve, and i always have requests for the recipe.

1. for crust: in medium sized bowl , stir together flour and powdered sugar
2. cut in butter with pastry blender or the tines of two forks
3. press into greased 10x15x1 pan
4. bake in 350 degree oven for 10-15 minutes
5. for filling: beat together eggs , lemon juice , zest and juice of fresh lemon , flour , sugar , baking powder and coconut
6. mix well and pour over hot crust
7. return pan to oven and bake uncovered for 25 minutes or until golden brown
8. cool completely on wire rack
9. for frosting: beat together butter , lemon juice , vanilla and powdered sugar
10. spread over filling when cool
11. cut into bars & serve
12. store covered
demonstrations.review: The only thing I did different was to sprinkle toasted coconut on top of the frosting because I had some.  This bar is decadent!!  Thanks so much for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanishing oatmeal raisin cookies

oatmeal raisin cookie recipe from the quaker oats box.  bar cookie variation included.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. beat together margarine and sugars until creamy
3. add eggs and vanilla
4. beat well
5. add combined flour , baking soda , cinnamon and salt
6. mix well
7. stir in oats and raisins
8. mix well
9. drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet
10. bake 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown
11. cool 2 minutes on cookie sheet
12. remove to wire rack
13. makes about 4 dozen
14. bar cookies: bake 30 to 35 minutes in ungreased 13x9-inch metal baking pan
demonstrations.review: This is how I remember oatmeal cookies and I love this recipe.  If you cook them a little less time they will be soft and chewey.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry crumble bars

anyone who likes cranberries is going to love these. i made them for christmas last year and will be making two batches this time. this came from one of my betty crocker cookbooks.

1. in 1 1 / 2-quart saucepan , mix granulated sugar , orange juice and water
2. heat to boiling
3. stir in all remaining cranberry filling ingredients
4. cook over medium heat about 10 minutes , stirring occasionally , until thickened
5. cool
6. heat oven to 400f
7. in medium bowl , mix brown sugar and butter
8. stir in all remaining bar ingredients until crumbly
9. press half of the crumbly mixture in ungreased rectangular pan , 13x9x2 inches
10. spread with filling
11. top with remaining crumbly mixture
12. press lightly
13. bake about 20 minutes or until light brown
14. for bars , cut into 8 rows by 6 rows while warm
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  These bars are so good that I am going to freeze a bunch of bags of fresh cranberries so I can make them all year.

target.recipe_text:
mrs  knobbes gooey butter cake

this is an ooey gooey delight straight from st.louis missouri.

1. mix the cake mix with 1 egg and the butter and pat into a greased cake pan
2. mix and pour the remaining ingredients over the cake
3. bake at 350f for 35 minutes
4. dust the top with powdered sugar
target.review: I made this cake and took it ot work--What a hit!!!  This is delicious and VERY EASY!  Thanks for sharing, I'll make this again, and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible peanut butter cookies

these are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!

1. mix peanut butter , sugar , and egg together until smooth
2. drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart
3. if desired , roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet
4. press with fork
5. press again in opposite direction
6. bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
7. do not brown
8. do not over bake
demonstrations.review: These cookies are great and soooo easy!!  What a great recipe to keep, when your sweet tooth is callin!!  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream of carrot soup

rich tasting, warm and comforting. i had a recipe i loved for this soup, but the original called for a lot more butter and 2 cups of heavy cream. i didn't really want to save this soup for special occasions only, so i attempted to reduce the fat & calories by reducing the butter and replacing the cream with evaporated milk - i have even tried evaporated skim milk with success (but it is better with whole evaporated milk). if i am serving this to guests, i use the half-n- half, but for just me i like it with the milk. i have never missed the cream in this.

1. in a large stockpot , melt butter and saute onion until soft and tender , about 5 minutes or so
2. add carrots , potatoes , chicken broth , and ginger powder
3. cover and cook on medium heat 30 minutes or until veggies are very tender
4. remove from heat and let cool 15 minutes
5. using a stick blender , puree the soup right in the pot
6. return to heat and add milk , rosemary , salt , and pepper
7. cook over low heat until heated through , maybe 5 minutes or so
demonstrations.review: This was my first attempt at carrot soup, and I must say it was wonderful!!  I followed the recipe exactly.  It was my preference to have a thicker soup, therefore I added a cup of instant mashed potatoes after immersion blending it, and that did the trick!!  Just my take on the consistency, and it worked great!  Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey tetrazzini

another favorite from the encyclopedia of creative cooking edited by charlotte turgeon. this is a good recipe use up, or stretch, that left over turkey. it's a good make-ahead dish too, as you can put it in the fridge and then cook it later that day, or the next. this last time that i made it, i was unable to get the sherry called for by the recipe. i substituted a rose, and while the taste was a little different, it worked just fine.

1. heat 4 tbsp butter and olive oil in a large saucepan
2. add mushrooms and saut for 5 minutes
3. remove mushrooms with a slotted spoon and reserve
4. add flour to pan juices
5. stir to form roux cook until bubbly
6. slowly add chicken broth and cook until thickened
7. remove from heat
8. add cream , sherry , parmasan cheese and nutmeg
9. stir until cheese melts
10. add turkey and mushrooms , stir well
11. turn into well greased 13x9x2 inch or 3 qt baking dish
12. melt 2 tbsp butter
13. toss with bread crumbs
14. sprinkle over casserole
15. bake , uncovered , in a pre-heated 375 degree oven for 25 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is such a lovely recipe.  I served it to my guests and they raved about it.  I followed the recipe exactly, and it was WONDERFUL!!  Thanks for sharing it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft as wonder   white bread

this is my standard loaf of white bread, good for anything.  very soft.  i mix it in the bread machine then bake it in the oven.
as with all my bread, i let it cool and then slice the whole loaf and put in a freezer bag and freeze and then i can take whatever i need out and have fresh bread. this does not include machine and rising time.

1. add ingredients in order given
2. select dough cycle
3. when done , take out dough and on a floured surface , shape into loaf and place in loaf pan
4. let rise in a warm place for approximately 40 minutes until doubled in size
5. bake on centre rack of preheated 350 degree oven for 25-30 minutes
6. cool on wire rack before slicing
demonstrations.review:
I made this bread and it was WONDERFUL!!  My DH loved the texture and the softness of the bread.  I usually prefer home baked bread on the day that I bake it, but 10 seconds in the microwave and this tastes like "fresh from the oven" no matter what day after baking.  
This will be my standard, easy to make bread recipe.  Thanks for posting.  My rating is really 10 stars!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
foil wrapped chicken tacos

this is quick and easy and oh so yummy for those that want a different take on the usual tacos.  i use taco sauce instead of salsa only per preference.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. sprinkle chicken with seasoning mix
3. place 1 / 2 cup of the potatoes on center of each of 4 large sheets of heavyduty foil
4. make sure foil is sprayed with cooking spray to prevent sticking
5. top evenly with chicken , salsa , and cheese
6. bring foil sides up
7. double fold top and both ends to seal packet
8. leave room for heat circulation inside
9. place on a 10x15 inch baking sheet
10. bake 30-35 minutes or until chicken is 165 degrees
11. remove packets from oven and let stand 5 minutes
12. cut slits in foil to release steam before opening
13. serve with sour cream or any other toppings
demonstrations.review: Sorry, forgot to rate stars!!

target.recipe_text:
skillet steak with mushroom sauce

this is delicious and quite easy to prepare, i have even made this recipe using pork tenderloin, the sauce recipe can be doubled if desired, make sure to brown the meat on both sides this will contribute to the flavour of the dish and make certain to leave the steak sit out to almost room temperature so plan well ahead --- this is very good!

1. season the steak with pepper , then let the steak sit out to almost room temperature , this will help relax the meat fibers and make for a more tender and flavorful steak
2. in a large skillet , melt half the butter over high heat
3. brown steak on both sides
4. transfer to a plate
5. reduce heat to med-high
6. add remaining butter to skillet
7. cook onions , mushrooms and thyme , stirring for 10 minutes , or until liquid is released , and the mushrooms are starting to brown
8. add in the garlic and cook for 2 minutes
9. add flour and cook stirring for 1 minute
10. gradually stir in beef stock , cream and horseradish
11. reduce heat , and simmer , stirring for 5 minutes , or until sauce is thickened
12. return steak , and any accumulated juices to pan
13. simmer for 5 minutes , or until steak is desired doneness
14. let steak rest for 5 minutes
15. season sauce with more salt and pepper to taste
16. slice steak thinly across the grain , and serve with the sauce
target.review: I gotta give this one another 5 stars. It was so good! I left out the onions but did use the garlic as well as fresh thyme. Wonderful flavor and the steak came out just right.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sahlab  middle eastern pudding

this is a quick and easy to prepare dessert. i usually always have the ingredients on hand. there are boxed versions of this pudding, but it is traditionally prepared at home. you can add more or less cornstarch if preferred. this dessert is so versatile that it can be served warm or chilled. i love to eat it both ways, when it chills it firms up.

1. combine cornstarch and water in a small cup and stir well
2. add milk to a soup pan or dutch oven pot
3. stir in cornstarch mixture in milk before it gets warm
4. add in vanilla and sugar
5. must stir constantly until it comes to a boil
6. let boil for 2 minutes , meanwhile still stirring
7. serve in dessert bowls
8. top with cinnamon and coconut or just chopped pistachios
9. it's traditionally eaten hot , but i like it cold too , once it cooled off and firmed up
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this. I served it warm with fruit. It was a comforting treat on a cold autumn day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fig balsamic glazed beef kabobs

this recipe is from the "beef - it's what's for dinner" web site. i haven't tried it yet but it looks tasty.

1. soak four 10-inch bamboo skewers in water 10 minutes
2. drain
3. cut beef steak into sixteen 1-1 / 4 inch pieces
4. alternately thread beef and onion pieces evenly onto skewers
5. set aside
6. combine preserves , vinegar , oil , garlic , 1 / 2 teaspoon salt and pepper in small bowl
7. reserve 1 / 4 cup for dipping
8. brush kabobs with some of remaining sauce
9. place kabobs on grill over medium , ash-covered coals
10. grill , covered , about 7 to 9 minutes for medium rare to medium doneness , turning and basting with sauce every 2 minutes
11. season kabobs with salt , as desired
12. serve with reserved sauce for dipping
demonstrations.review: We will double the recipe next time. Very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super easy  cheesy enchiladas

when you don't have a lot of time or money.  i made this for my family for around a dollar per serving.  if the only mexican food your kids will touch is cheese quesadillas (cheese melted on a tortilla), give this a try as a "step up".  my picky picky dd was okay with cheese enchiladas when we told her it was cheese in a tortilla with a sauce on top.  now she has been known to eat spinach enchiladas and chicken enchiladas! :)  she gave this recipe two thumbs up. :)

1. first , you want to mix the first four ingredients together until they are really well combined
2. seriously , you will not see any little shreds of cheese and it will have the texture of stiff play dough
3. preheat your oven to 350 and grab a pan
4. i used an 11x7 inch oval baking dish , but you can also use an 8inch square
5. pour about 1 / 4 of the enchilada sauce into the bottom of the pan and swirl the pan until the bottom is coated
6. reach in with your clean hands and grab about 2 tablespoons of cheese mixture in your hands and shape into a log
7. roll a tortilla around this log and place in the pan
8. repeat for the rest of the cheese and tortillas
9. pour the rest of the sauce on top , spreading it to cover
10. sprinkle the last 1 / 2 cup of cheese on top , and place in the oven
11. bake 20-30 minutes or until hot and bubbly
12. for oamc: freeze before cooking , thaw in refrigerator and bake according to directions
demonstrations.review: This was quick, tasty and inexpensive.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate mousse charlotte

i thought for sure i would have seen this posted already, as this has been a standby of my mother's for the last 30 years or so.  it is always a big hit and, best of all, takes little effort.

1. line a springform pan bottom and sides with ladyfingers
2. follow directions on pudding mix , using 2 cups of milk
3. add cream
4. beat until thick with heavy peaks
5. pour into ladyfinger-lined pan and let set
6. if you like , finish off top with additional whipped cream
demonstrations.review: What a great idea for a quick "mousse"! I can't believe I never thought of trying this before. Now my family wants me to make it in all their favorite pudding flavors.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brioche with chocolate chips abm

posting so i don't lose this one.  so rich, so good, so easy with an automatic bread machine.  this was given to me by a french work colleague who got it from a friend off of a french abm recipe site.  if the chocolate chips aren't frozen, or even if they are, they melt easily and you may wind up with chocolate swirl brioche, which is still good.  sometimes it works out ok for me and sometimes it doesn't. put in the order your machine needs and use the sweet bread setting.

1. put all in the bread machine in the order needed for your machine
2. the original recipe calls for 2 packets of vanilla sugar and 3 tbsp sugar
3. freeze the chocolate chips to stand a chance of them not melting and giving you swirl bread
4. use the sweet bread setting on your machine , time to cook will vary , for me , 3 hours and 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I prepared this in the bread machine and then baked it in the oven. It had a very nice, soft texture with a mixture of swirls and chips.

target.recipe_text:
easiest beef enchiladas ever

best enchilada recipe i've found. we love the spicy, cheesy flavor of these.

1. brown meat and onions in large skillet
2. add 1 cup enchilada sauce and 1 cup cheese
3. mix well
4. put filling along center of each tortilla
5. roll up and place seam side down in a 9x13 pan
6. pour remaining sauce over
7. sprinkle remaining cheese over
8. bake at 350f degrees for about 30 minutes till cheese is bubbly
target.review: My DH raved about this meal.....and it was really quick and simple!  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
still another tuna pasta salad        mom s tuna salad

a tasty tuna salad which is easy to prepare. i frequently make it during the summer for a light supper, after a day at the pool. also works well for picnics. amounts given are estimates, i usually prepare this 

1. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients
2. mix well to blend
3. if salad is too dry , add more mayonnaise
4. taste , and adjust seasonings to your preference
5. chill well before serving
demonstrations.review:
I love this...make it almost weekly....I ommitted the peppers...but otherwise followed the recipe exactly.  I am not a tuna liker but I like this!

Thanks for posting~Kristi

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon mushroom chicken

very easy to put together, and the result is fabulous. make sure to serve mashed potatoes or rice along side of this, to mop up the great tasting sauce!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. pour melted butter into a 9x13-in baking dish
3. add chicken , skin side down , sprinkle with seasoning salt and garlic
4. turn chicken over , season and lay bacon strips on top
5. sprinkle with mushrooms
6. bake in the preheated oven for 45-60 minutes , or until chicken is no longer pink and juices run clear
7. remove chicken , bacon and mushrooms to a platter and keep warm
8. pour juices from baking dish into a small saucepan and whisk together with cream over low heat until thickened
9. pour sauce over chicken and serve warm
demonstrations.review:
Loved the ease of this recipe.....but that it seems complicated to guests!  Made 2 changes...used boneless skinless chicken breasts, and used a lot more mushrooms and bacon.  The taste was incrediable...I will be making this again!

Thanks for posting~Kristi

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cube steak and gravy  crock pot

this dish is excellent when served with mashed potatoes or rice.

1. salt and pepper the steak to your liking , then dredge in the flour
2. fry steak until brown and place in crock pot
3. add water , soup , and gravy mix
4. cover and cook on low 6 to 8 hours
5. serve with mashed potatoes or rice
demonstrations.review:
Have made this about 4 times.  It is a crowd pleaser and oh so easy....just put it in the crockpot and you are done until dinner time.  served with mashed potatoes, buttered corn, and hot rolls...very filling!

Thanks for posting! Kristi

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese pot stickers

these pot stickers are 100% better than any you can buy and well worth the extra effort. i like to make them and then freeze them so all you have to do is the final steps just before you serve them. i make them every christmas to have as a quick appetizer. one review commented that she had trouble with them sticking together when she defrosted them -  i have not had this happen however to be sure it doesn't happen to you defrost them separated.  i have also fried them directly from the freezer. they only take a few seconds more to cook.

1. sprinkle salt over the shredded cabbage and let stand for 5 minutes , then squeeze out liquid
2. squeeze out any liquid from the shrimp
3. mix cabbage , shrimp , pork , soy , wine , onion , oil , ginger and garlic
4. on each wrapper place about 2 tsp of the mix and seal the edges , use a bit of water on the edge , try to press out all the air and ensure they are tightly sealed
5. in 2 large skillets heat 1 tbsp oil , fry 16 dumplings for 1 minute or until golden on one side add 1 / 4 cup of stock into the pan , reduce heat to low , cover and cook , without turning for about 7 minutes or until the dumpling is translucent and most of the liquid has evaporated uncover and on higher heat cook for another 5-7 minutes or until the bottoms are dark brown , drain put on a platter and keep warm
6. repeat for the remaining 32 dumplings
7. mix the dipping sauce and serve with warm or hot dumplings
demonstrations.review: These where pretty easy to make as far as pot stickers go.  I like them and so did DH.  They where tasty!  Went well with our veggie fried rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy coleslaw

my mom gave me this recipe, and i just love it! it's so easy to throw together, and tastes great.

1. toss together cole slaw and green onions
2. in a small mixing bowl , whisk together oil , vinegar , sugar , and ramen seasoning packet
3. pour over salad and toss together
4. just before serving , add ramen noodles , almonds and sunflower seeds and toss together
demonstrations.review: I love this coleslaw.....I did not put in the almonds as my mom is allergic.  But it was really good without them!

target.recipe_text:
kentucky steak marinade

this smells wonderful when you are grilling.

1. mix all the ingredients
2. marinate steaks for at least 2 hours but preferably longer
3. grill the steaks over an outdoor grill for best flavor
target.review: Excellent marinade.  I bought eye of round 2 inch steaks for a memorial day cookout and wanted them as tender as possible.  I marinated them in this for 8 hours prior to grilling.  They were melt in your mouth tender and had a wonderful flavor.  Happy that a less expensive cut of meat came out so great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red caldwell s prize winnin  pintos

this one is from chili pepper magazine. red caldwell has been winning cooking, grilling, and barbecueing compititions for the last 15 years. these are the absolute best tex-mex beans ever.

1. drain and rinse the beans
2. place the beans in a crock pot set on low , cover with water
3. add everything else
4. cook overnight
5. add any salt that is needed
6. serve
7. these freeze well and are even better when reheated
8. i had to cut this recipe in half to get it to fit my crock pot
demonstrations.review: Wowie ZZowie!  DH and I agree that these were the best kicked up pinto beans we have ever had.  I used leftover spiral sliced baked ham (just a tad left on a big ole ham bone) instead of the salt pork.  Made everything else as directed.  We ate off this for three days with cornbread and grated cheese.  Even froze some.  Thanks for sharing a super recipe.  This will be a regular in our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jack daniels chicken

yummy yummy yummy - what more can i say. this is delicious, you wont regret going to the trouble of making it. the sauce is thick and creamy, the taste is hard to describe, it is unique and very good.  you can just barely taste the jack daniels but it would not be the same without it.

1. saute chicken breasts in butter
2. wrap in foil and keep warm in 350 oven
3. saute shallots
4. add jack daniels and light with a match , flame will be high , let flame die down
5. add broth and tarragon
6. fast boil , uncovered , until sauce reduces to thick syrupy glaze
7. add lemon juice and cream
8. simmer until thickened
9. put chicken breasts into sauce to coat
10. serve with pasta or rice to utilize the yummy sauce
demonstrations.review: Made this last night...OMG...it was incredible.  Fabulous!  Will be making it again soon.  Thanks for such a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon cocktail weenies

this is my most requested recipe for parties. everyone is always stunned at how simple the ingredients are. if you are serving a large number of people, you may want to double the recipe, i have seen folks stumble over each other to reach the last weenie on the platter!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. spray 9x13 inch cake pan with non stick spray
3. open package of bacon and cut entire slab into thirds
4. wrap a third of a slice of bacon around each cocktail weenie and secure with toothpicks
5. place each bacon wrapped weenie in cake pan , making sure to crowd them together
6. liberally cover weenies with brown sugar , leaving only the toothpicks exposed
7. place weenies in hot oven
8. every 10 minutes or so , baste weenies with sugar / bacon grease mixture and break up any lumps of sugar
9. continue until sugar is completely melted and bacon is thoroughly cooked
10. when serving , be sure to drizzle sugar / bacon grease over weenies and on the platter
11. some people like to swirl their weenies in the syrup before cramming them in their mouths
12. i've never really timed this recipe , but i'm going to guesstimate the time at@30-40 minutes
13. servings also depend on the crowd you are feeding
14. my crew will argue that 15-20 weenies qualify as a serving !
demonstrations.review: How can you go wrong with these?  Bacon, sugar and wieners!  I lined my baking sheet with nonstick foil and am glad I did. The bacon fat and sugar combine to form a sort of salty sweet caramel and it is sticky. The smell while these were baking was intoxicating. I almost had to stand guard over the oven to protect them from DH. Made these a day ahead for Thanksgiving and stored in a heatproof pyrex bowl. I plan on reheating on a warming tray for the crowd. Absolutely certain they will be the first appetizer gone. Thanks so much for such a simple and delicious recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s swiss steak

i have also done this in the slow cooker at low for 8 hours with great success. add potatoes and carrots for a one pot meal.

1. preheat oven 350f degrees
2. brown steak lightly in olive oil
3. place in roast pan
4. saut garlic apple and onions
5. add to meat
6. place remaining ingredients in saut pan
7. bring to a boil
8. pour over meat
9. seal tightly with foil
10. bake 2 hours
demonstrations.review: Made this with london broil as directed.  Easy and tasty.  I like the fact that was not tomatoe based as most swiss steak recipes are.  I baked up perfectly in the oven and the fact that I baked it in the same pan I browned it in made clean up go fast.  DH loved it and it will go in our regular rotation.  Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jamaican jerk pork

this is really good-you can sub chicken for the pork if you like-and you can change the peppers if the heat is too much!

1. in a large bowl combine the first 7 ingredients
2. mix thoroughly
3. in a food processor combine green onions and garlic , peppers , onion , lemon juice , oil , soy sauce , malt vinegar and ginger
4. blend until very smooth
5. place pork in a glass bowl or large freezer bag , combine all ingredients and coat pork well
6. cover and stir or flip often
7. marinate for at least 8 hours
8. take out of the fridge 1 hour before grilling
9. preheat grill to medium high , skewer pork , 4 cubes to a skewer
10. cook for 6-8 minutes on one side , flip and 6-8 minutes on the other
demonstrations.review: Made this as pork kabobs along with steak kabobs that used another marinade.  This was gone in a flash, still have steak left over!  Everyone loved it, so flavorful and smelled unbelievable while grilling.  Thanks for sharing

target.recipe_text:
lemony black eyed pea and cilantro salad

this is delicious, low-fat and super-easy ... i like to load it up with extra cilantro and tomatoes. also try using lime juice in place of the lemon juice for a little different taste. it's a perfect vegetarian main dish salad, or serve it as a side dish with grilled or roasted pork or ham. prep time includes time spent in the refrigerator blending flavors; yield depends on whether salad is eaten as the main dish or as a side dish.

1. combine all ingredients in a bowl
2. let sit in refrigerator for a couple of hours to blend flavors
3. salad tastes best at room temperature
target.review: I LOVE this salad!!!  It is so quick and easy to make (I didn't peel or seed the tomato because I'm not into that...I feel like it just takes up extra time, and I like the tomato seediness) and it is sooooo good!  I used red onion, and two cloves of garlic.  I would recommend doubling the recipe, because it's so good you'll wish you had more!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy tuna or chicken noodle casserole

this is a delicious casserole that can be made using either tuna or 1-1/2 cups or more of cooked cubed chicken or even cooked turkey
 --- for a thinner sauce use 1 cup of milk or half and half instead of 3/4 cup, prep time includes boiling the egg noodles, if you are not a garlic-lover then you may omit the garlic powder and to zing the flavor up even more add in 1-1/2 tablespoons of lemon juice

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. grease a 2-quart casserole dish
3. cook the egg noodles in boiling salted water
4. drain then toss with 2 tablespoons butter
5. in a large saucepan , mix the undiluted mushroom soup , garlic powder , parmesan cheese milk or half and half , sour cream , salt , pepper , chopped onion , pimiento , bell pepper and celery
6. cook over low heat , stirring frequently for 15 minutes
7. add in the tuna or chicken
8. mix to combine
9. combine the mixture with the cooked egg noodles
10. transfer to prepared greased baking dish
11. sprinkle top with the broken ritz crackers
12. bake for about 25 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is delicious.  I used frozen peas instead of a green pepper, and I used milk and light sour cream.  The first time I made it, I forgot to mix the butter with the noodles, so I melted it and mixed it with townhouse crackers and parmesan cheese for the topping, and it was really good.  I would recommend cooking the onions till they're tender first and then mixing everything else in with them when you're making the sauce.  I'm making it again right now and I added some chopped tomatoes just because I needed to use them up...I'm sure it will still be amazing!  Thanks for the recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham and cheese pasta

a different way to do mac and cheese with the addition of ham and using colby cheese in the sauce. yum!

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. cook and drain pasta per package directions
3. melt butter over low heat and saute garlic in it for 30 seconds
4. whisk in flour and salt and pepper and cook over medium heat , stirring constantly until smooth and bubbly
5. gradually stir in milk and heat to a boil , stirring constantly
6. stir in mustard and colby cheese and cook , stirring occasionally until cheese is melted
7. stir pasta and ham into cheese sauce
8. pour into ungreased 2 quart baking dish
9. sprinkle with parmesan cheese and bake uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes or until bubbly
demonstrations.review: Mmmmm, this was sooo good!  I used 2 cups of cheddar cheese and one cup of colby jack, and I used about 12 ounces of pasta, and it was amazing.  My fiance says I need to save the recipe for when we have kids because they'll love it!  And it makes way more than two servings, we both ate all we could, and I still have enough for our lunches tomorrow.  Thanks for the yummy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic chicken thighs

this is a quick and easy recipe that never fails to please even my picky dds. since chicken thighs are usually inexpensive it makes a economical meal. i like to serve these with some type of rice side dish and a green salad.

1. spray large frying pan , preheat
2. rinse and pat dry thighs
3. season with salt and pepper
4. brown well on all sides
5. cover , reduce heat to medium and cook for approximately 25 minutes , or'til thighs are done depending on size
6. add shallots , cook for 2-3 minutes , until they soften
7. stir in balsamic vinegar , cook for about 1 more minute , turn chicken to coat thoroughly
8. spoon sauce over thighs to serve
demonstrations.review: Wow.  This was sooo good!  The only thing that I will do differently next time is to use a bit more balsamic vinegar, but that's just because I love it and I wanted more of that yummy sauce!!  I actually ate one cold out of the pan as I was putting the leftovers away, that's how good they are.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried sweet potato  kumara    coriander soup

this is so quick and easy because i can get pre-mashed kumara in tubs in the veggie section of my local woolworths supermarket. if it is not available to you prep time will obviously be much longer.

1. heat oil in saucepan over low heat
2. add onion , garlic and curry powder cook , stirring , for 2 minutes
3. add stock and mash and bring to the boil , stirring until smooth
4. reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes
5. add sour cream and coriander and season to taste with salt and pepper
6. served with warmed naan bread if desired
demonstrations.review: This soup was wonderful!  Very creamy and healthy and amazing and easy!  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jolean s cheese potato   smoked sausage casserole

this was another one of our favorites in the 70's  very inexpensive and very easy to make.  just recently found this recipe hand-written by my mom, and the warm feelings flood back to me, because this was a true favorite in our house.  little did i know that she was on such a tight budget, yet made things like this that we all loved!!  note:  the meat that was used in this recipe always varied, according to whatever we had available at the time.

1. cut skinless smoked sausage in half , lengthwise , and then chop into 1 / 2 inch "half moon" cuts
2. cook in a frying pan for about 15 minutes , turning frequently to slightly brown
3. meanwhile , put cooked & diced potatoes in 2 quart casserole
4. add cooked meat and give it a gentle toss
5. mix all remaining ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat until warm , melted and smooth
6. pour white / cheese sauce over potatoes and meat
7. sprinkle shredded sharp cheddar cheese on top , and then sprinkle paprika evenly over the top
8. bake in preheated 350f oven for 35-45 minutes
9. hot dogs , sliced into 1 / 2-inch slices or 1 / 2 lb
10. ham diced into 1 / 2-inch dices or 12 oz
11. can of spam diced into 1 / 2-inch dices , instead of the smoked sausage
demonstrations.review: This is amazing.  I love anything smoky, so I was sold on the recipe.  I threw in a chopped leek and a red bell pepper when I browned the sausage.  I boiled my potatoes but left them fairly firm, and I used freshly shredded cheddar cheese instead of Velveeta. (I'm not a huge fan of Velveeta.)  I made a white sauce first, and then I threw the cheese in after it was nice and hot, so I didn't have any melting problems.  I also used Penzeys Smoky 4/S Special Seasoned Sea Salt in place of regular salt, and put smoked paprika on top.  This is definitely not health food, but it used everything I already had on hand, and it's delicious!

target.recipe_text:
salmon pat

i have had this many times at a local restaurant, rotisserie for beef and bird, where it is their signature complimentary appetizer. it's an easy, yet impressive appetizer to make and disappears very quickly! printed in a local paper's food section for a recipe quest answer.  cook time is chill time.

1. combine cream cheese and butter in a mixing bowl and cream lightly
2. add salmon , garlic , sherry , green onions or chives and celery salt
3. blend well
4. transfer mixture into serving dish , cover , and refrigerate at least 2 hours at allow flavors to blend
5. serve with melba toast or thinly sliced rye bread
target.review: I made this for an hors d'oeuvre for Christmas dinner.  The color is beautiful.  I followed the recipe exactly, and it turned out wonderful.  I made it a day ahead, and the flavors really blended.  I would caution with the celery salt as the smoked salmon can be pretty salty at the get go.  Maybe add a little celery salt and taste as you go.  Very good stuff.  Made my socks roll!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carpetbagger steak

steak and oysters.

1. saut oysters , mushrooms , and parsley in the butter until the mushrooms are tender
2. drain off butter
3. stir in the bacon , cheese , and wine
4. set aside
5. make a pocket in the side of the steak
6. stuff pocket with the oyster mixture
7. secure with wooded picks
8. broil steaks about 6 inches from heat for about 8-10 minutes on each side or until desired doneness
9. top steaks with any leftover oyster stuffing
demonstrations.review: This recipe is incredible.  I have used thick rib eye steaks as well as New Yorks.  To top off the whole incredible dish, I added bernaise sauce over the steak.  Yummmmmmmm

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german sweet   sour cabbage

i grew up on this. this is my mother's recipe, and it has been a 

1. cook cabbage in water for 8-10 minutes
2. drain
3. fry bacon and remove from pan
4. add onion and saute until limp , 3-5 minutes
5. add sugar and flour to bacon fat
6. blend until smooth
7. add water , vinegar , and seasonings
8. cook until thick
9. add diced bacon , and cabbage
10. heat through
11. if bland , add more salt , sugar , or vinegar , whichever is needed
demonstrations.review: I've made this several times.  It's great.  Sometimes I add the flour sometimes I don't.  It works well either way.  Wonderful side for grilled brauts or just about anything except spaghetti.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with rosemary cream sauce

nan

1. cook the pasta until al dente
2. in the meantime , using a saucepan , saute the rosemary and garlic in olive oil over low heat for about 3 minutes
3. add the tomato puree , and season with salt and pepper
4. simmer for about 15 minutes
5. stir in cream and parmesan until heated through
6. drain pasta and toss with the sauce
demonstrations.review: Very simple to make, but I did not care for this dish.  I thought the sauce tasted akin to a canned spaghetti I used to eat when I was a kid.  The tomato puree was very acrid so I added a pinch of sugar to tone it down.  You might want to be careful when you stir the cream into the simmered puree.  If it's too hot, the cream could curdle.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
escargot a la bourguignonne

the simple and classic method for escargot.  :)  this is the way they are prepared at 13 coins in seattle.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
2. combine the butter , parsley , shallots , garlic , and brandy in a bowl and blend well
3. place a snail in each shell and fill the cavity with the seasoned butter
4. place on a baking pan and bake for twelve minutes
5. serve hot , as an appetizer , on individual snail dishes - or on small folded napkins on plates , to keep the shells from sliding about
6. also , small silver forks to easily eat them with are a good idea
7. make sure to have plenty of good bread alongside , to mop up the delicious butter sauce ! :)
8. also good with a bit of parmesan sprinkled on top of each
demonstrations.review: This one is a keeper.  I used this recipe rather than my old tried and true.  Hey, this one is now my tried and true.  I've never seen snail butter that calls for butter.  It's the brandy that puts this recipe over the top.  Don't leave it out.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffed french toast with cranberry sauce

baked french toast filled with orange flavored cream cheese and served with a maple cranberry sauce. prep time includes refrigeration overnight.

1. cut 1" from each end of the loaf and discard or use for another recipe
2. cut the loaf into 1" thick slices and halve each slice on the diagonal
3. cut in the diagonal side of each piece of bread to form a pocket
4. mix the cream cheese , 2 tbsp sugar , egg yolk , zest and 1 tbsp orange juice until smooth
5. fill each bread pocket with 1 tbsp of the cream cheese mixture
6. put bread slices in a 13" x 9" baking dish , overlapping slightly
7. whisk the eggs , milk and 1 tsp vanilla until frothy and pour over the bread
8. cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight
9. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
10. sprinkle bread with 1 tbsp sugar
11. bake for 35 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean
12. cranberry sauce: combine cranberries , maple syrup , 1 / 2 c sugar , 1 / 2 c orange juice and 1 tsp vanilla in a pot
13. cook over medium heat stirring as required until cranberries burst and mixture thickens , about 15 minutes
14. cool sauce and serve with toast
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful.  I made this for Christmas breakfast.  It was a complete hit.  I followed the recipe and wouldn't change a thing.  It's perfect.  Thanks, Pixie!

target.recipe_text:
the ultimate salmon fillets

living on the west coast, we have eaten a great deal of salmon. this is absolutely the best way we have found to cook it. it is so moist and the flavor is fantastic! many reviewers have said that they think the cheese, especially the cheddar is unnecessary, and i have to admit that i omit the cheddar cheese myself. the flavour is a little too strong and it is extra fat that is not needed. i do like the sprinkling of parmesan with the paprika because it looks so nice when it is broiled. using light mayonnaise and light sour cream or yogurt tastes just as good as the full fat versions and cuts down fat and calories even more. thanks for all the great reviews!

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. if frozen , partially thaw fillets and cut into serving size pieces
3. place in a greased baking dish
4. combine sour cream or yogurt , mustard , onion , dill , and mayonnaise
5. season with salt and pepper
6. spread mixture over fish
7. bake 20 minutes per inch of thickness of fish if frozen or 10-12 minutes if thawed
8. when just done , sprinkle with the cheeses and a dash of paprika
9. broil 1 minute or until the cheese is bubbly and flecked with brown
10. serve with lemon wedges
target.review: Used the highliner 4 in a bag salmon fillets and cooked from frozen, approx 25 minutes. Served with basmati rice, a bag of japanese veg mix and red lobster cheese biscuits (Recipe #11571). The biscuit recipe is good but I always have left over garlic butter so this time I used the remaining garlic butter from the biscuit recipe to toss and coat the veg mix theb topped  with toasted almonds. Additionally, for broiling I layered 1/2 cup crushed pecans/walnuts, 2 green onions and then the cheese. This was very good! Thank you for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chinese chicken balls with sweet and sour sauce

don't bother ordering chinese chicken balls make these at home they are just as good if not even better and the sweet and sour sauce is the same as what is served at your chinese restaurant!-- these are a great weekend snack or can be served as appetizers, if you want some extra flavor to you chicken batter feel free to add in some garlic or onion powder or spices of choice --- this makes a large amount so you may want to reduce the chicken ball batter amount by half (using 4 chicken breasts) --- note: the sauce recipe is one you may have to make a few times before you get the consistancy and sweetness to your liking, 1 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup lightly packed brown will give you a sweet sauce you may reduce the white sugar amount by a few tablespoons

1. to make the sweet and sour sauce sauce
2. in a saucepan combine the first 5 ingredients until combined
3. in a cup or bowl whisk the cold water or pineapple juice with cornstarch until smooth and well blended , then whisk vigorously into the ketchup mixture
4. bring to a boil stirring or whisking constantly over medium-high heat until bubbly
5. reduce the heat to medium-low and continue simmering and mixing until thickened remove from heat and allow to sit at room temperature while making the chicken balls or you may cool to room temperature then refrigerate until ready to use
6. to make the chicken balls: in a large bowl combine flour , cornstarch , baking powder , baking soda , garlic powder
7. add in water and sesame oil
8. whisk vigorously until smooth
9. add in chicken pieces
10. using clean handsand mix until well coated
11. heat oil in a deep-fryer or dutch oven to 375 degrees
12. carefully dip the battered chicken pieces in hot oil and fry until golden brown
13. remove to a paper towel
14. sprinkle with seasoning salt immediately after frying if desired
15. serve immediately with sweet and sour sauce
16. delicious !
demonstrations.review: This was fabulous! Time consuming but worth it. As written this does make allot but I wouldn't scale it down because then I would miss out on all those awesome leftovers. Many thanks for another great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cilantro dressing for salads

this dressing is great on a fresh veggie salad, chicken salad, crisp green salad, taco salads or any tossed salad. especially good on a salad that is accompanying a mexican entree.

1. using your steel knife in the food processor mix garlic and salt
2. process until it is a paste
3. add cilantro and parsley
4. process to a fine mince
5. add vinegar
6. process for 10 seconds
7. add oil in a slow steady stream with the processor on
8. add hot pepper sauce and a pinch of sugar
9. chill the dressing for several hours in a glass jar
10. shake to combine before using
demonstrations.review: Excellent and easy dressing, leftovers can also be used over pasta.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken divan  or turkey divan

there are a few similar recipes on zaar to this one, but none exactly the same. this is the one that my mom served when i was a child. the only change i have made is to use broccoli florets instead of frozen spears, which are difficult to cut when serving this up. i've also made this without the broccoli in a smaller dish. my mom always made this recipe with the chicken created when making chicken stock. feel free to substitute cooked leftover turkey in place of the chicken.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. cook broccoli until tender in the microwave
3. place broccoli in the bottom of a 9 x 11 casserole dish sprayed with cooking spray
4. spread chicken over broccoli
5. combine mayonnaise , soup , lemon juice and curry powder
6. spoon over chicken
7. sprinkle with cheese and bread crumbs
8. bake for 25-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was excellent! I made the recipe with leftover turkey from Christmas. The only change I made was to substitute the can of cream of chicken soup with turkey broth and I doubled the mayonnaise because I am allergic to MSG. Also my husband loves cheese so I used a cup of cheese instead. Thank you for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scallion sesame turkey burger

i found this in some random cookbook.  one of the best turkey burgers ever.  full of flavor.  make an extra for lunch the next day, reheats beautifully.

1. mix togeter , gently
2. the turkey , sesame seeds , soy , scallions , cilantro , garlic , sesame oil , 1 teaspoon of salt , and bread crumbs
3. form into patties
4. i usually mix all this together and make patties in the morning and leave in the refrigerator till i'm ready for them
5. sometimes that is the next day
6. brush with a little oil before grilling if desired
7. grill on the george foreman , in a grill pan
8. if you're using the outside grill increase the breadcrumbs a bit to insure they don't fall apart
demonstrations.review: This was very good. The burgers were exceedingly moist and flavorful. I served with this sauce on top: http://www.food.com/recipe/thai-peanut-dressing-from-cpks-thai-crunch-salad-383202.<br/><br/>Thank you for posting RifRaff

demonstrations.recipe_text:
just like loaded baked potatoes casserole

this is an awesome low-carb version of loaded baked potatoes, and tastes far better than any version of mock potatoes that i have tried. in fact, this dish is soooo good, you will not believe it!  i do not remember where i got this recipe, but it is a fabulous side to any low-carb meal. you will be pleased, i promise! yum! yum!

1. pre-heat oven to 350
2. chop cooked cauliflower into very small pieces
3. mix sour cream , 1 / 2 of the green onions , 1 / 2 of the cheese , 1 / 2 of the bacon , and salt and pepper to taste in medium bowl
4. stir in the cauliflower
5. place in medium baking dish and sprinkle remaining cheese and bacon on top
6. bake for 20 minutes
7. sprinkle the remaining green onions on top just before serving
demonstrations.review: Clear instructions and wonderful taste! I put it through the food processor before baking and the consistency was just right. Next time I think I will pipe it into hollowed out potato skins for that authentic look without the carbs. Thanks for sharing this keeper recipe :)

target.recipe_text:
yummy brussels sprouts with bacon   onion

i came up with this myself. since brussels sprouts have a similar flavor to cabbage, i have adapted my cabbage recipe for them. my husband thought he did not like brussels sprouts until i made these. i usually have to do a double batch and we end up fighting over the leftovers!!!

1. cook brussels sprouts according to package
2. i steam mine in the microwave
3. while sprouts are cooking , in a pot on the stove , cook your bacon and onion together
4. cook until bacon and onion are thoroughly done
5. add brussels sprouts to bacon & onion
6. add margarine and salt & pepper to taste
7. when margarine is melted , you are done !
8. i like to cook mine until the sprouts get a little brown on the bottom
target.review: Absolutely delicious! Will use this again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn muffin casserole

this is a wonderfully simple side-dish that tastes very similar to chi-chi's corn cake, which i have been missing so much since our chi-chi's closed:( could also be served for breakfast, with maple syrup drizzled over top...mmm!

1. in large bowl , combine first four ingredients well
2. stir in corn muffin mix
3. pour into 9x13-inch pan
4. drizzle melted margarine over top and sprinkle with sugar
5. bake in preheated 350f oven for 55-60 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a family favorite and so easy to make. I do skip the sugar on top. I find the Jiffy mix plus the 2 TBSPs of sugar are enough.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: I've been using this recipe for years now but just saw it on this site. This is the easiest way yet to cook a deliciously tender roast. We love it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ranch glazed baby carrots

five minutes is all you need to make this savory-sweet glaze for cooked carrots.

1. cook carrots according to package directions , drain well
2. in the meantime , melt butter in a large saute pan over low heat
3. add sugar and stir until dissolved
4. add carrots and ranch mix , stir until carrots are coated
5. increase heat to medium , and stir until carrots are hot and glazed , about 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: I've made this several times now and just now reviewing it. These carrots are just delicious. I love the "tang" of the ranch mix.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan pepper rice pilaf

i think this recipe originally came out of our local newspaper. its been several years. this is a great basic pilaf. you can add fresh vegetables such as mushrooms, bell peppers, etc.

1. in a medium saucepan , heat olive oil over medium high heat
2. add crushed red pepper and rice
3. stir well to coat rice with oil
4. cook for a minute or two until rice starts to look translucent
5. add the chicken broth and bring to a boil
6. reduce heat to low , cover and simmer for 20 minutes or until all broth is absorbed
7. remove lid , fluff rice with a fork
8. sprinkle with parmesan cheese and black pepper
9. cover just until cheese melts
10. serve
demonstrations.review: So delicious! I used Jasmine rice and it has the most wonderful aroma while cooking. I'll served baked Tilapia fillets over the rice. Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy baked shrimp

yummmmmmy!! spicy, so have plenty of cold beverages around.

1. combine first 7 ingredients
2. layer shrimp and lemon slices in a 13x9 inch baking dish
3. top with sauce
4. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes or until shrimp turn pink , stirring once
5. remove shrimp , reserving sauce
6. serve shrimp with reserved sauce and french bread
demonstrations.review: Living in Louisiana, I've had seafood about every way possible. I will rate this as one of the top recipes. We made piggies of ourselves. You must have crusty french bread to "sop" up the goodness!

target.recipe_text:
brussels sprouts in garlic butter

this is a recipe from joy of cooking... totally changed my mind about brussels sprouts! it's imperative that you use fresh sprouts, the texture would be way off with the frozen ones.

1. melt butter and olive oil in a medium skillet until butter is foamy
2. reduce heat to medium , add smashed garlic and cook until lightly browned
3. remove garlic and discard
4. add sprouts cut side down , cover , and cook without stirring on medium-low heat 10-15 minutes or until tender when pierced with a knife
5. the cut side of the sprouts should get nice and browned , with a nutty , buttery flavor enhanced by garlic
6. top with freshly grated parmesan and salt& pepper to taste
target.review: My new favorite way to prepare spouts! Couldn't stop eating them.  I used about 2 tsp of minced garlic (left it in and served it that way) and added about 1 tsp one lemon pepper to to the butter oil mixture instead of just pepper. I omitted the parm cheese. Awesome recipe -- thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: Very Tasty.  I love garlic and cheese and this came out very tender.  A little greasy so next time I will cut back on the butter a bit. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth chicken breasts

the mayonnaise make these chicken breast very moist and tender--enjoy!

1. mix mayonnaise or yogurt , cheese and seasonings
2. spread mixture over chicken breast and place in baking dish
3. bake at 375f for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: I enjoyed this recipe and will definitely make it again.  I would have rated it higher but as it came out it was too salty for us.  This may depend on the type of seasoned salt you use but mine is mostly salt and little seasoning.  Next time I will omit the season salt and instead add some minced onion or onion powder.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breast with honey balsamic glaze

4 pts from ww 2004 annual recipes for success

1. combine first 3 ingredients
2. sprinkle over both sides of chicken
3. heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
4. add chicken
5. cook 7 to 8 minutes on each side or until chicken is done
6. transfer chicken to a platter
7. keep warm
8. reduce heat to medium-low
9. add vinegar and honey to pan
10. simmer 1 minute or until glaze thickens
11. stir constantly
12. pour glaze over chicken
demonstrations.review: Excellent taste and very easy to make. I did not use the Tyme as I'm not a big fan of it.  I cut the breast into strips and sauteed in garlic and oil.  I also used one extra TBS honey in the sauce and next time may add a little corn starch to make a thicker glaze.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy and delicious ranch parmesan chicken

there are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, i find that hidden valley ranch dressing works the best but kraft or any other brand will do, i sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although i have only made this using breasts i imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *note* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
for low-fat option: use low-fat ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as smart balance 50/50 blend.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. in a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with parmesan cheese , seasoned salt , black pepper and garlic powder
3. dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides
4. coat in the breadcrumb mixture
5. place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil
6. lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast
7. if desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces
8. bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked)
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe -- tasty and easy to make.  I would have given 5 stars except my tasted salty.  Next time I make it I will omit the season salt and add a bit more garlic powder. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
legal seafood style baked scallops

whenever we get back to the boston area, it's a priority to to have a meal at legal seafoods.  i recently "re-discovered" this recipe buried in old newspaper clippings. i had tried to recreate it in the past but now know i was missing the most important ingredient - buttermilk. i made it again after posting the recipe so i have edited the original description. it's even better than i remembered, you might want to try just a dash (or more) of cayenne pepper. it's delightful !

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. place scallops in a bowl , season with salt and pepper , add thyme and buttermilk and toss to coat
3. place scallops , with buttermilk , evenly in the bottom of an oven proof dish , sprinkle with cracker crumbs and top with melted butter
4. bake for 20 minutes , squeeze lemon over scallops and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Easy to make and tastes great!  I used parsley as I'm not a big fan of thyme. Made my buttermilk with lemon juice and let the scallops sit in it (refrigerated) for about an hour.  No leftovers were to be found.  I plan on serving this again at an upcoming dinner party.

target.recipe_text:
fried salmon patties

we eat this dish for dinner or breakfast! for breakfast try them with grits.  for dinner try serving with sweet peas and rice.

1. add salmon to a medium bowl
2. remove bones
3. add the flour , eggs , onion and salt and pepper
4. beat with an electric mixer until well incorporated
5. in a large skillet , heat enough oil to cover the bottom of the pan
6. with a medium spoon , add salmon spreading them into round patties
7. let them cook on one side 10 minutes , then flip cook 10 minutes more
8. enjoy !
target.review: Hi Your cooking as always was wonderful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moist rosh hashana  new year  honey cake

my rebbetzin gave me this recipe a few years ago. i had a disastrous rosh hashana in the honey cake department, went to a break-the-fast at her place, and she had this amazing cake. i've made it every year since and make it in the off-season, too. this is one of those cakes that gets better as it ages, so if you want to make it a day or even two ahead, it'll actually taste better. she says it's based upon a recipe in marcy goldman's cake in a treasury of jewish holiday baking, but that thing's out of print. i did find a copy of it, purchased it for the recipe, and found that it was.. lacking.. in the spice department.

i haven't put in the optional whiskey to date, but i believe it's more traditional to use it. i've just never had it around.

i also like using bundt pans for this. did you know hadassah asked nordicware to make the original bundt pan?

1. preheat oven to 350f if you're using black or dark-colored pans , reduce to 325f
2. prepare a 10 inch bundt pan , or tube pan , or 3 8" x 41 / 2 loaf pans
3. grease and flour the bottoms of the pans - better yet , use baking parchment paper to line the bottoms of the pans: it makes getting your cake out in one piece easier !
4. mix all the dry ingredients in a large bowl or the bowl of your electric mixer
5. add wet ingredients and mix until well combined
6. pour slowly into prepared pans to avoid bubbles
7. tap pans against counter to free any bubbles
8. bake for 40 to 45 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
9. let the cake stand for at lease 15 minutes before you try and get it out of the pan
10. invert it on a wire rack and cool completely
11. wrap tightly in wax-paper , and then in foil to keep
12. this is one of those cakes that gets better the longer you let it sit
13. if you can make it 3 days in advance , that's actually ideal
14. it is also delicious right away
demonstrations.review: Hi this was a very good cake.  It is a good spice cake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savoury baked pork chops

adapted from an old german recipe. easy to do, it makes company think you've been at it all day. no extravagant extra ingredients. wine accompaniment: chardonnay or reisling

1. season chops with salt& pepper if you wish
2. roll in a plastic bag containing all-purpose flour and a little dried sage
3. let sit 5 minutes then dredge again
4. brown the chops in a small amount of oil , on top of stove
5. put chops into a casserole , in a single layer
6. blend together and pour over the chops: water , brown sugar , bay leaves , sour cream and wine or vinegar
7. bake in a 325-350f oven for 1 1 / 2 hours or until chops are tender and white inside
demonstrations.review: Hi! This was wonderful.  It was very tender. Made for Spring PAC 2009.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon cheese frittata

here's a tasty little number that doesn't require any special ingredients.  you'll feel like you're out for breakfast while cooking at home.  i substituted sausage in place of bacon because it's what i had.  recipe from taste of home quick cooking july/august 1999, courtesy of diana bullock who likes to prepare this for overnight guests.  she keeps cooked bacon in the freezer to cut down on preparation time.

1. in a bowl , beat eggs , milk , butter , salt , and pepper
2. pour into a greased 11x7x2" baking dish
3. sprinkle with onions , bacon , and cheese
4. bake uncovered at 350 for 25 to 30 minutes or until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Hi!  Your frittata was wonderful.  Thanks for sharing the recipe.  Although I did add a little green pepper and a bit of garlic.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken jambalaya packets

this is my spin on reynolds aluminum foil packet cooking.  for the utmost ease, cook the rice the night before and refrigerate.  reynolds quick & easy packet directions:  1.  center ingredients on a greased 12x18 inch sheet of heavy duty aluminum foil.  2.  bring up foil sides.  double fold top and ends to form a packet, leaving room for heat circulation inside.  repeat to make four packets.  3.  bake on a cookie sheet in preheated 450 degree oven.  4.  after cooking, carefullly open end of foil packet first to allow steam to escape.  then open top of foil packet.  tip:  for the easiest of clean-up, foil line baking sheet.

1. preheat oven 450 degrees
2. spray sheets of heavy duty aluminum foil with nonstick cooking spray
3. set aside
4. cut chicken into 1 inch strips and pat dry with paper towel
5. season chicken strips with cajun seasoning
6. in a small bowl combine tomato sauce , sugar , salt , garlic , dehydrated onions , fresh parsley , dried italian seasoning , cayenne and bell pepper
7. in a large bowl combine cooked rice , tomato mixture , seasoned chicken strips and smoked sausage slices
8. center one-fourth of mixture on each sheet of greased foil , leaving room for heat circulation inside
9. repeat to make four packets and place on baking sheet
10. two baking sheets may be required
11. bake 15 - 20 minutes
12. open packet as directed above and top with green onions
13. even better the next day !
demonstrations.review: Hi!  This was a very good recipe.  It is easy to make and very satisfying.  I would guess it would make a great camp out recipe too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cilantro garlic lime rice

i'm serving my crock-pot fiesta chicken over this tonight.  i am attempting a garlicky copycat of chipotle's cilantro lime rice, but my mom does not have any limes or real lime juice, so i'm having to make do with limemade.  i'm not sure how that will turn out, but the fiesta chicken will probably be too spicy for dh and maybe the sweetness of the limemade will balance it.

1. bring liquids to a boil
2. stir in rice , garlic , and cilantro
3. cover and remove from heat
4. let stand five minutes or until liquids are absorbed
5. fluff with fork and serve
demonstrations.review: Wonderful and easy to make.

target.recipe_text:
awesome baked pork chops

these chops remain moist and tender, and the sauce is to die for! you probably have all the ingredients in your kitchen to make this! serve these chops over rice!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. rinse pork chops , pat dry , and season with garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste
3. place the beaten eggs in a small bowl
4. dredge the pork chops lightly in flour , dip in the egg , and coat liberally with bread crumbs
5. heat the oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat
6. fry the pork chops 5 minutes per side , or until the breading appears well browned
7. transfer the chops to a 9 x 13 baking dish , and cover with foil
8. bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour
9. while baking , combine the cream of mushroom soup , milk and white wine in a medium bowl
10. after the pork chops have baked for an hour , cover them with the soup mixture
11. replace foil , and bake for another 30 minutes
target.review: Wonderfully Delicious! Used boneless chops & chicken broth instead of wine. Very moist & flavorful. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sugar free double layered chocolate pie

this is a delicious no-bake pie that is oh so simple!

1. in large bowl beat 2 cups milk and pudding mix with wire whisk for two minutes
2. spread in crust
3. in small bowl beat cream cheese and equal with wire whisk until fluffy
4. whisk in 1 tablespoon milk
5. fold in whipped topping
6. spread over chocolate pudding in crust
7. refrigerate at least 3 hours until set
demonstrations.review: Really good!! Cool & delicious treat. Easy to make & enjoy. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious oreo refrigerator cake  no bake

this has remained a long time favorite, i have even made this in the winter months and served it to guests many times, lemon flavor pudding mix is also very good to use in place of the chocolate --- you can make this well in advance, it can also be served as a frozen dessert just remove from freezer about 6 minutes before slicing this is just as delicious frozen!  if you are serving this at a kid's birthday party place mini oreo cookies into the topping of cool whip facing sideways --- i most always double the chocolate pudding mixture, you may also double the cream cheese mixture if desired --- this is very good!

1. crush oreo cookies
2. set 1 / 4 cup aside for topping
3. mix the remaining crushed cookies with the melted butter
4. press into the bottom of a greased 13 x 9-in baking pan
5. in a bowl , beat the cream cheese with the confectioners sugar on medium speed
6. fold in half of the cool whip topping
7. spread over cookie crumb layer
8. refrigerate 1 / 2 hour
9. in the meantime , combine milk with instant pudding mix
10. beat well , until smooth
11. pour over chilled mixture in the pan
12. refrigerate for 1 hour
13. spread remainder of cool whip topping on top of pudding layer
14. sprinkle with remaining reserved cookie crumbs
15. store cake in the refrigerator , covered tightly
demonstrations.review: SO AWESOME! Doubled the recipe for a party dessert. It was gone before i could even get any!! EVERYONE LOVED IT!! Very easy to make- my husband did it! This is definately my new party dessert!! THANKS!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious blue cheese broccoli casserole

this dish has been served every year at my holiday dinner table, i double the recipe and sometimes even triple depending on how many people i have at my table, there is never anything left and i always receive rave reviews all around! --- two small cloves fresh minced garlic may also be added in and sauteed for one minute in butter before adding in the flour--- you will also find this recipe on my food blog http://kittencalskitchen.com/2009/09/15/blue-cheese-broccoli-bake/

1. set oven to 350f
2. grease a medium casserole dish
3. steam broccoli florets until firm-tender drain well then pat dry with paper towels
4. in a large saucepan melt 2 tbsp butter over med-low heat
5. add in flour and stir for 1 minute
6. add cream cheese , blue cheese and milk
7. stir over low heat until melted and smooth , then add / stir in broccoli
8. mix 6 tbsp melted butter with the cracker crumbs until well combined
9. stir in 1 cup cracker mixture into the broccoli mixture
10. season with black pepper if desired
11. pour mixture into a casserole dish
12. cover with foil or a lid and bake for 15 minutes
13. remove from oven then sprinkle the top with remaining cracker crumbs
14. return to oven and bake uncovered for another 15 minutes
15. allow to cool for 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Awesome & Delicious!! Slight variation- I used Gorgonzola cheese instead of blue (tastes the same IMHO) and Gorgonzola crushed crackers. Really wonderful & ate by guests very quickly!! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pammy s crock pot chicken breast and gravy

my hubby (says 5 stars) and grand kids (very fussy) really like this.  this is one thing all 3 of the grand kids will actually eat.  the grand kids normally don't like gravy much but all of them like this gravy.  i serve with mashed potatoes, a veggie and homemade rolls.  hope you enjoy it! note added - you can use no sodium bouillon.
note added - i have also noticed sometimes when i make this it seems more salty then other times.  definately try to use low sodium or skip the boullion.  nov. 2007...my daughter used a package of ranch dressing instead of italian and a jar of gravy instead of a package.  she said they all loved it.  we don't care for ranch but thought maybe others would be interested.

1. spray crock pot with pam cooking spray
2. add the 2 tablespoons of olive oil to crock pot
3. put chicken breast in crock pot
4. sprinkle italian dressing mix , onion powder , garlic powder over the chicken breast
5. cook on low for 4 hours
6. sprinkle the 1 / 2 teaspoon bouillon in the liquid in crock pot
7. pour the cream of chicken soup over the breast
8. turn crock pot to high and cook 1 more hour
9. remove chicken , scraping the soup off the breast and back into the crock pot
10. add gravy mix to to 1 / 4 cup cold water and mix well , add to crock pot and mix well
demonstrations.review: Easy to make. Cooked chicken longer than 4 hours (because I wasn't home)- SO tender & delicious. Not as flavorful as expect. Will make again- but will add more spices. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
artichoke and chicken bake

this easy but elegant entree first appeared in "quick cooking" magazine. someone posted this at the somersize website, which is where i found it. i usually have this over a bed of fried spinach or zucchini ribbons.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. spray an 11x7 inch baking dish with pam
3. salt and pepper the chicken breast halves and place in the dish
4. in a bowl , combine the artichoke hearts , parmesan cheese , mayonnaise and garlic powder
5. mix well
6. spread artichoke mixture over chicken breasts
7. bake , uncovered , 30-35 minutes or until chicken juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Excellent, delicious recipe!! Very easy & quick to fix for dinner. Thanks for sharing the goodness!

target.recipe_text:
mushroom shrimp creole

nan

1. in a large skillet , cook bacon over medium heat until crisp
2. drain on paper towels
3. in the drippings , saute onions , green peppers and garlic
4. add the next 8 ingredients
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat
7. cover and simmer for 30-45 minutes
8. add the shrimp , mushrooms , butter , lemon juice and savory
9. cook 5-10 minutes longer or until thoroughly heated
10. discard bay leaf
11. stir in bacon
12. serve over rice
target.review: YUMMY!! My husband and I were very happy with the way this creole turned out. It is different from the way I usually make it but the flavors blended so well. Had just a hint of a sweetness in addition to the savory flavors. I liked that it was well seasoned but not hot with fire. Thanks for another winner, Nurse Di.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic shrimp

easy, yummy, and garlicy. doesn't get any better.

1. heat oil and butter in a large skillet
2. add garlic and shrimp
3. sprinkle with salt and pepper
4. saute 2-3 minutes or until shrimp turn pink
5. turn shrimp with spatula
6. cook shrimp 2 minutes longer on other side
7. remove shrimp to serving platter
8. garnish with lemon wedges
9. we give this a little squirt with the lemon wedge
demonstrations.review: Out of this world shrimp. I couldn't believe that something with a few simple ingredients could taste sooooo good. The garlic is potent and delicious. I served the sauteed shrimp over angel hair pasta. I sprinkled a little Parmesan on top. Delicious and can't wait to make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggs   rice

on saturdays my daddy made breakfast, he was famous for coming up with strange things. now years later, my family loves to eat this for breakfast or dinner. my daughter would not eat anything unless it had cheese so she use to call it cheese rice. you can add just about anything to this easy easy dish.

1. melt butter in a skillet
2. add left over rice
3. make sure rice is well heated and coated with butter
4. whisk eggs in a bowl then pour into the skillet
5. scramble the mixture until you feel it's done
demonstrations.review: My great grandmother and grandmother used to make this for breakfast when there was left-over rice. I always add a few sliced mushrooms, onion, and garlic. My family loves it. Glad to see this posted.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
granny s gingersnaps

another one of my grandmother's incredible recipes. this was a special treat when i was a little girl.

1. in a large mixing bowl , cream the shortening and sugar
2. beat in the egg and molasses
3. combine the flour , baking soda , ginger , cinnamon , and salt
4. gradually add to the creamed mixture
5. roll teaspoonfuls of dough into balls
6. dip one side of each ball into sugar
7. place with sugar side up on a greased baking sheet
8. bake at 350 degrees for 12-15 minutes or until lightly browned and crinkly
demonstrations.review: Just took these out of the oven and had to try one while they were still warm. Oh my goodness!! A little taste of heaven. Very tender and soft. Great gingery flavor. Smells wonderful too. Thanks Nurse Di, for another great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna salad jumbo shells

taste of home. a different slant on regular tuna salad. great for lunch.

1. cook pasta according to package directions
2. rinse in cold water and drain
3. in a bowl , combine mayonnaise and sugar
4. stir in the tuna , celery , onions , green pepper , carrot and parsley
5. spoon into pasta shells
6. cover and refrigerate
7. dressing: combine sour cream , sugar , vinegar , mayonnaise , celery seed , and onion powder
8. arrange lettuce leaves and shells on individual plates
9. drizzle with dressing
demonstrations.review: Made this for lunch today and it was soooo good. The filling and sauce had the best flavor. My husband and I spent spent a couple of hours outside doing yard work and we had worked up a sweat and an appetite. This tasted so good to me icy cold out of the refrigerator. Served atop a bed of leafy lettuce leaves. Thanks for another great one.
