quick pasty pie

this is my much quickened version of a pasty, put into pie form. for those who are unfamiliar with pasties, they are a pastry filled with meat, potatoes and onions, then folded into a half-circle. i live in an old mining town and these are still popular from the old days when the men would take them in their lunch boxes.

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. place crust in an 8-inch pie pan and press into bottom of pan
3. in a large bowl , thoroughly combine hash browns , ground beef , shredded onion , garlic , salt and pepper , and carrots
4. place filling into the pie pan and top with second pie crust
5. seal edges of crusts together and cut vents into the top crust
6. bake for 50-60 minutes or until meat is cooked through
7. serve topped with beef gravy or ketchup , if desired
target.review: A favorite!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thick chocolate pudding

this is the perfect chocolate pudding. it has a rich chocolate flavor, great texture and is not high in fat. i can't count the number of times i have made this. i hope you enjoy it as much as we do.

1. in a 2-qt
2. microwave-safe bowl , combine the first four ingredients
3. stir in milk until smooth
4. microwave , uncovered on high for 3 minutes
5. stir
6. microwave 4-6 minutes longer or until thickened , stirring after each minute
7. stir in vanilla
8. pour into individual serving dishes
9. cool
10. refrigerate
11. garnish with whipped topping if desired
demonstrations.review: Nice and creamy, Make sure your dish is BIG, mine overflowed too.  I had to eat part from inside the microwave. LOL

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cmp  chocolate  marshmallow  peanut  pie

this pie is inspired by the cmp sundae.  this is a great dessert for potlucks.  cook time includes baking crust plus cooling time.

1. for crust: mix graham crumbs , melted butter and chopped peanuts together in bowl
2. press into bottom of 13" x 9" baking pan
3. bake at 350 for 15 minutes
4. remove from oven and allow to cool---about 30 minutes
5. 1st layer: cream pb and cream cheese
6. beat in sugar
7. blend in 8 oz whipped topping
8. spoon scattered dallops on to cooled crust and gently spread evenly over the crust
9. 2nd layer: beat pudding mixes and milk until thick
10. spoon scattered dallops on top of first layer and gently spread evenly
11. 3rd layer: beat 12 oz
12. whipped topping with marshmallow fluff and spoon scattered dallops over 2nd layer---gently spread evenly over 2nd layer
13. sprinkle with chopped peanuts and / or chocolate chips
14. if desired
15. chill at least 1 hour before serving
16. store in refridgerator
demonstrations.review: Yum!Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker chicken cacciatore

monica perdue, personal chef, bon vivant

1. put chicken in the slow cooker
2. top with the spaghetti sauce , green bell peppers , mushrooms , onion , and garlic
3. cover and cook on low for 7 9 hours
4. serve with pasta
demonstrations.review: Very good and easy!  I have been making this for years.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegy pizza

this is a colorful, delicious dish that is great for an appetizer or potluck. everyone will love it and want the recipe!

1. unroll crescent rolls and lay on a greased cookie sheet
2. press the seams together
3. bake at 350 degrees for 7-10 minutes until lightly browned
4. leave in the pan and cool
5. mix the ranch dressing , mayo and cream cheese together and spread over the cooled"crust"
6. top with the chopped vegies- carrots , tomatos , broccoli , cukes- whatever you want to use !
7. serve for an appetizer or potluck dish and wait for the compliments !
demonstrations.review: Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk salad

my coworkers are great cooks. this is another great recipe from a former coworker. covered dish lunches at the office are a great way to discover new recipes. this is quick and easy. hope you enjoy this one!!!

1. heat undrained pineapple and jello in a saucepan till jello is dissolved
2. mix in buttermilk and cool whip
3. pour into mold or bowl
4. refrigerate for several hours or overnight
demonstrations.review: Sounds wonderful!  Bet it would be good with orange or lime jello.

target.recipe_text:
creamy potato salad

have you ever posted a recipe and just love reading the reviews for it?  this is my signature potato salad.  whenever there is a pot luck function at work, i am told that i have to bring the potato salad.  no one else is allowed to and i am never given a choice.  thank you everyone who ever tried this potato salad and for leaving such glowing reviews for it.  you all have made me look so good.  i personally can not stand eggs or raw onions, so i leave them out but i know most people don't think a potato salad is complete without them.  thanks again for so many wonderful reviews. (psssst....check out my recipe #123107 as well.  it shares the dressing with this recipe but tastes much much different because of the different ingredients) please see recipe #242966 for bacon bit tips.

1. cook potatoes in boiling , salted water until tender
2. drain well
3. peel and cube potatoes
4. transfer to a large bowl
5. add celery , onion , sweet relish and bacon bits
6. combine mayo , sugar , celery seed , vinegar , mustard , and salt
7. add mayo mixture to potatoes
8. toss lightly to coat potato mixture
9. carefully fold in the chopped eggs
10. cover and chill thoroughly
11. bacon bit
12. use a sharp knife and cut the frozen bacon into long strips about 1 / 4 inch wide
13. turn the bacon and cut the strips into pieces also about 1 / 4 in wide
14. you now have perfect raw bacon pieces to fast fry
15. no need to separate
16. they will separate during cooking
17. perfect bacon bits
target.review: I totally forgot to rate this recipe!  I have made it approximately three times and each time I have not had the celery or red onion.  I used yellow onion and omitted the pickle relish and sugar altogether.  I also add marinated artichoke hearts and aleppo pepper!  Thanks for a great potato salad recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
deli rotisserie chicken

i have a george foreman rotisserie and love the way everything comes out of it.  this recipe makes the chicken  juicy and skin crispy.  does not include marinade time.

1. remove the giblets from chicken and discard
2. wash chicken inside and out , drying with paper towels
3. rub chicken with a little olive oil
4. tie wings and legs with cooking twine
5. mix all the spices together well
6. rub all over chicken
7. place on plate and wrap with saran
8. put in fridge 4-24 hrs
9. , the longer the better
10. put chicken onto rotisserie bar
11. set timer for 1 1 / 2 hours
12. chicken is done at 160 and no longer pink
demonstrations.review: Most excellent!  My husband and I fixed two whole chickens on our grill rotisserie on our Broil King and cooked for a little over 1-1/2 hours.  This rub is fantastic!  Best rotisserie chicken ever!  I will definitely use this recipe all the time for rotisserie chicken!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate greek salad

this is the most delicious salad - fresh and wonderful-tasting.  fyi, lettuce can very much be a part of any greek salad - if you want it to.  we like lettuce in my family and i often add it.  it would not be 'authentic' in a horiatiki (village) salad, but who cares?

1. whisk dressing ingredients together until blended
2. season to taste
3. drain onion from ice water and pat dry with paper towels
4. combine all salad ingredients , except cheese , in large bowl
5. toss with dressing
6. sprinkle cheese over and serve
demonstrations.review: I liked this salad but my husband wasn't crazy about the dressing.  I thought maybe it needed more red wine vinegar to be a little tangier.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ultimate shrimp scampi linguini

this is a super simple recipe for shrimp scampi.  such a rich and elegant dish! for the white wine, i would recommend a pinot grigio.  this is my take on a tyler florence recipe from tyler's ultimate!

1. saute garlic , shallots and red pepper flakes in 2 tablespoons butter and 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium heat in large skillet
2. add shrimp to skillet , cooking until pink about 2-3 minutes
3. remove shrimp from pan
4. add wine and lemon juice to skillet
5. when mixture comes to a boil , add 2 tablespoons butter , 2 tablespoons olive oil
6. when butter melts , return shrimp to pan and add parsley , cooked pasta and 1 cup pasta cooking liquid
7. toss to combine
8. to be extra fancy: drizzle a little more olive oil over finished dish !
demonstrations.review: This is a wonderful shrimp scampi linguine.  The shallot and wine are a nice touch to the sauce.  The flavors are wonderful and of course, its even better the next day.  This will be my new recipe for shrimp scampi linguine.  Thank you for a wonderful recipe.  I just finished the last bit of it and still want more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: Kittencal, you got it going on with this recipe!  I totally loved it and my husband went on and on about it.  I used four cloves of garlic (didn't measure but it looked like alot).  I will definitely, definitely fix this again and again!  It was so yummy!  Thanks for the wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
okra and tomatoes  a k a   okra gumbo

i havent seen too many okra recipes on zaar, so i decided to post my favorite.  my grandmother taught me how to make this dish when i was 11, and i've been making it ever since.  its a great along side smothered steak and mashed potatoes, or rice.

1. fry bacon in a large skillet that can be covered , until crisp
2. remove from skillet and drain on paper towels
3. saute onion in bacon drippings until tender
4. add okra and tomatoes , stir to blend
5. cover , reduce to low heat
6. cook for about an hour , or until okra is tender , stirring occasionally
7. do not stir too much or too briskly , because the okra will fall apart
8. season with salt and pepper , to taste
9. my family doesn't like the bacon cooked into it because the bacon becomes soft
10. if you do it my way , you can sprinkle the bacon on right before serving
demonstrations.review: I have not made this recipe yet but my grandmother used to make this when she was alive and my mom also makes it.  It is fantastic.  It brings back such wonderful memories of my grandmother.  Thanks for the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
chocolate chip peanut butter oat cookies

i got this recipe from the inside lid of a metal box that had pictures of walt disney world and beauty and the beast and 2 12 oz. packages of nestles chocolate chips inside more than 5 years ago. when i first saw the recipe, i wasn't sure i would like it as it has oatmeal in it. well my daughter made them when i wasn't home and i was so glad she did because they were soooo delicious, rich, and yummy. i am posting this to share and for safe keeping.

1. preheat oven to 350 f
2. combine flour and baking soda in a bowl
3. beat butter , peanut butter , sugars , and vanilla in a large mixing bowl until creamy
4. beat in eggs
5. beat in flour mixture
6. stir in oats and chocolate chips
7. drop by mounded tablespoons onto a ungreased cookie sheet about 3 inches apart then bake for 10 to 15 mins
8. or until they are light brown
9. let stand on cookie sheets 3 minutes then remove to wire racks to cool
target.review: Absolutely delicious! They're the perfect pick-me-up at the end of a not-so-great day! They're a fantastic texture, and just the right balance of peanut butter, chocolate, and oats. I almost couldn't bear to dunk them in milk!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy crock pot chicken with noodles

this is a lifesaver when i've been on my feet all day.  it requires very little standing over the stove and makes a great meal.

1. trim any visible fat from chicken and cut each breast into thirds
2. in medium bowl , season chicken with lemon juice , pepper , celery salt and paprika , then place in crock-pot
3. in large bowl , mix soups with wine , thenp our over chicken
4. sprinkle w / parmesan cheese
5. cover and cook on on high 4 to 5 hours
6. serve over noodles
demonstrations.review: Delish! Used two cans of mushroom soup instead of one each celery & mushroom, and forgot the parmesan, but it was tasty just the same! Will be making it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized apple and chicken saute

apples, chicken, onions.....wow, this is a great combo, served with mashed potatoes and green beans.

1. in a shallow dish , combine flour , cinnamon , thyme and pepper
2. coat both sides of chicken with flour mixture
3. shake off excess flour
4. spray a non-stick skillet with no-stick cooking spray
5. melt 1-1 / 2 teaspoons of butter in skillet over medium heat
6. add chicken
7. brown 5 to 6 minutes on each side or until chicken is tender
8. remove from skillet and keep warm
9. melt remaining 1-1 / 2 teaspoons butter in skillet
10. add onions
11. saute 3 to 4 minutes or until golden brown
12. stir in apples and juice
13. bring to a boil
14. reduce heat and simmer 4 to 5 minutes or until apples are tender
15. add apple jelly
16. stir until melted
17. add chicken back to skillet and heat through
demonstrations.review: Made this for company, and it was a big hit. Forgot the apply jelly in the chaos of cooking all of dinner, but still turned out great. Can't wait to try it on a less crazy night.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot creamy chicken fettuccine

my children ask for this regularly. this is quick and easy to put together.

1. place the chicken in crock pot and sprinkle with garlic powder , onion powder and pepper
2. top with soup
3. cover and cook on low 6-8 hours or until chicken juices run clear
4. stir in cheese and olives
5. cover and cook until cheese is melted
6. meanwhile , cook fettuccine according to package directions and drain
7. serve chicken on top of fettuccine
demonstrations.review: Made lots of changes, but it was delicious all the same! Used eight chicken breasts, one teaspoon of garlic powder, a sprinkle of pepper, two cans CoChicken soup, some shredded parmesan, and poured it over some leftover rigatoni with alfredo sauce. Ready in seven hours, absolutely delicious. Very easy, I'll definitely use this recipe again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick   easy taco burger casserole

a new twist on an old favorite! feeds a family of 6-8, and is great on a cold winter night. i came up with this recipe when i was trying to get my husband to eat more family-style casserole dishes (he's not a fan of casseroles). i served it right out of the oven, bubbling hot, with a slice of crusty french bread and a small dinner salad. he ate three helpings and told me that i should definitely put "that one" in my recipe box.

1. cook macaroni noodles according to package directions for al dente , drain and rinse with cold water
2. set aside
3. in a large skillet , brown ground beef with onion , drain
4. return meat mixture to skillet , stir dry taco seasoning mix into meat mixture along with water
5. cook over medium heat , stirring occassionally , for 10 minutes
6. add the corn , tomato soup , cheddar cheese and cooked macaroni noodles to the meat mixture and stir until well blended
7. turn mixture into a greased , large oblong casserole dish
8. cover , and bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
9. remove cover and bake an additional 15 minutes or until bubbly
10. you may add extra grated cheese to top the casserole , if you wish , during the last 15 minutes of baking time
demonstrations.review: Family really enjoyed this! I doubled the meat and pasta for this, used rotini instead of macaroni, and omitted the corn. Really tasty and cheap to make, so it'll definitely be added to our big book of recipes! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect traditionally english roast potatoes

these are your standard traditional english roasties. imo there is an art to making these, at least the perfect golden crispy kind that i grew up with. the trick is to give 'em a good shake in a colander after par-boiling to rough up the edges of the potatoes. then once roasting; position spaced apart, turning only once or twice and basting in the hot oil every so often. if you don't manage the crispy texture (which you will, if you do the above!), they'll still taste excellent. you can't go wrong. i sometimes like to sprinkle rosemary/paprika/thyme or even a little garlic on top of mine for extra flavour.

1. peel and quarter potatoes
2. place in a saucepan with water and a pinch of the salt
3. bring to a boil and simmer them for 5-6 mins to slightly soften
4. meanwhile preheat your oven to 400f
5. when the potatoes have simmered drain them thoroughly in a colander shaking to roughen edges
6. let sit for a few mins to dry
7. pour just enough vegetable oil into a roasting pan to cover bottom and heat in oven for a few minutes
8. gently place potatoes into the hot oil and coat them with it evenly
9. sprinkle the salt and pepper over the potatoes
10. every so often baste the potatoes in the oil to prevent drying
11. turn potatoes once or twice halfway through to ensure even cooking
12. cook for 30-60 mins until gold and crispy
demonstrations.review: Outstanding potatoes. My boyfriend thought they were out of this world too, and is trying to figure out a way to get me to make these all the time. These are absolutely on par with the roast potatoes my English mother and grandmother make, and are straightforward enough that I could get them right every time. Thanks so much for sharing!!

target.recipe_text:
fluffy scones

these are the fluffiest scones ive ever made. they are so light and rise a lot, too. the key to getting them that way is to handle the dough as little as possible.
you can also turn them into fruit scones by adding a desired amount of dried cherries, cranberries or raisins.

1. preheat the oven to 200c / 400f
2. sift flour , baking powder and salt into a big bowl
3. using your finger
4. make a well in the center
5. whisk together milk and water and pour into the well reserving some liquid for glazing the scones
6. quickly stir until a dough forms
7. on a lightly floured surface pat down gently and cut out scones
8. the dough will be kinda sticky , but you should be able to form it without problems
9. if not , add some more flour
10. glaze scones with reserved water-milk-mixture and bake for 10-12 minutes
target.review: I cant say these were the best scones I have ever made.  They did not rise as nicley as my scones normally do.  They did taste lovely though.  I may give this recipe another go before I count it out.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jamie oliver s huge yorkshire puddings

another great recipe from jamie oliver. i made these a couple of times and everyone liked it!

1. mix all the ingredients , except the oil , to make a batter using an electric mixer
2. let it rest for 10 minutes
3. preheat oven at 450f
4. preheat a muffin tray and grease with a little oil
5. divide the batter into the tray
6. cook for 20 minutes at 450f
demonstrations.review: This recipe actually turned out very well!  I typically cant make YP to save my life, but I cant say that any more!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
award winning butter tarts

butter tarts are a canadian tradition. waaaay back in the 1970s, a national contest here in canada concluded that these butter tarts, originating from wilkie's bakery in orillia, ontario, were the best. i certainly think so and it's the only recipe i use. add a sprinkle of toasted walnuts when you add the raisins, if you wish, or use only walnuts if you don't like raisins.

1. prepare muffin pans by rolling out pie dough and cutting 4-inch circles
2. fit dough circles into muffin cups
3. set aside in fridge until ready to fill
4. in a small bowl , place raisins and cover with hot tap water
5. let stand on the counter for 30 minutes
6. in a large bowl , using a wooden spoon , mix together the soft butter , brown sugar , salt and corn syrup
7. stir well until sugar is dissolved and butter is creamed
8. add egg and vanilla and mix well
9. drain raisins
10. retrieve tart shells and divide raisins equally into all shells
11. then divide butter mixture into all tarts
12. bake at 400f for 15-20 minutes
13. filling will be lightly browned but still bubbling
14. canadians fall into two camps about butter tarts and are quite loyal to their favourite type: runny or firm
15. i like runny-- the type that dribbles when you bite into one
16. if you like firm , bake them for the full 20 minutes , even adding another minute or two if you wish
17. let cooked butter tarts cool in pans for 10 minutes after removing from oven
18. then remove and place on racks until completely cool
demonstrations.review: Ridiculously good.  If you do not want to hide in the pantry and scarf down 16 butter tarts by yourself DO NOT MAKE THIS RECIPE!  Being a good Canadian I decided to make these even MORE canadian by exchanging maple syrup for the corn syrup. A wonderful twist on an already great recipe. Now that you have been warned, go ahead and enjoy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wholesome homemade honey whole wheat bread

this is the most awesome wheat bread i have ever eaten. it is worth the extra effort and because this recipe makes 4 loaves, you can freeze them and have enough for awhile :) rising time included in prep.

1. dissolve yeast in warm water
2. in a large bowl , combine butter , molasses , honey and salt and mix well
3. add yeast mixture and then gradually add flours
4. turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth
5. place in buttered bowl and let rise until double
6. punch down and let rest for a few minutes
7. divide dough into 4 parts and shape into loaves
8. place in greased pans and let rise for about an hour
9. bake at 375 for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: Because our flour is a bit different here in Canada I did need to add an additional cup of flour.   Simply Lovely bread!!!  I followed anothers person suggestion and used this bread in making Recipe #133980 and it was  amazing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
golden  extra fluffy pancakes

these are my absolute favorite 'plain' pancakes. i love these so much that i can't put anything on them lol... i just eat them dry... i have to be careful.. i like them so much i could eat the whole batch lolol .. ok.. maybe not that many! hehe

1. in a small bowl , whisk milk , egg , and oil together
2. in a larger bowl , combine all dry ingredients
3. slowly add liquid mixture to dry mixture and whisk well
4. spray large frying pan with cooking spray , and heat to medium heat
5. wait until pan gets nice and hot
6. make pancakes whatever size you wish-- allowing top to form bubbles before turning over
7. cook until both sides are golden brown
8. these can be frozen and toasted in the toaster to be reheated
9. they are wonderful reheated !
10. serve with maple syrup , or whatever you wish to put on your pancakes !
demonstrations.review: This is the only pancake recipe that I ever use. I have been making it for at least a year now. It makes such yummy pancakes no one ever wants me to use the readymade powder mix.  It is so simple and easy that I don't mind.  For calorie sake, I do use splenda rather than sugar and 2tbsp of egg white rather than the egg. Elzmom, I think you need to try making these again because  you must have done something very wrong to not get fluffy pancakes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s sausage sawmill gravy  with biscuits

comfort food at it's best, this is a family favorite that goes back years! --- jimmy dean has a wonderful bulk sausage roll that will work great for this recipe, you may adjust the pepper flakes to suit heat level, my family likes extreme heat so i use 2 heaping teaspoons or you may use spicy sausage meat --- serve this over biscuits, i also like to serve it over mashed potatoes or fries :)

1. cook the sausage meat with onion in a large skillet over medium heat until sausage meat no longer pink
2. drain fat
3. add in crushed red pepper flakes and cook stirring until the meat is lightly browned
4. stir in 1 / 4 cup plus 2 teaspoon flour into the skillet and mix until dissolved with the meat
5. add in the cream and worcestershire sauce
6. cook over medium-low heat until thickened and bubbly
7. add in salt and ground black pepper
8. serve over biscuits
demonstrations.review: I added the onions and used Turkey sausage, the seasoning salt and 1% milk. I did not use the chillies.  I added 1 tsp of chopped fresh garlic and 1 tsp of chopped fresh ginger and 1/3 cup of no fat sour cream for a bit of extra flavor.  Absolutely wonderful!!! I will make it over and over again

target.recipe_text:
chicken curry in a hurry

watch out or you might get pulled over for a speeding ticket in the kitchen! ready in 20 minutes. :)

1. mix together flour , salt and cayenne pepper in a plastic bag
2. add chicken in small batches , shaking to coat
3. heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add chicken and cook until lightly browned
5. then add curry powder and toss to coat
6. remove from pan
7. add onion and garlic to pan , adding a little more oil if necessary , and cook for 2 minutes , then add broth , raisins , and tomato paste
8. return chicken to pan and simmer uncovered for 8 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and sauce has thickened
9. garnish with cilantro and a dollop of yogurt
10. serve with quick cooking minute rice , if desired
target.review: Both my DH and I have really enjoyed this recipe! I left out the raisins, but did everything else just like the recipe said. This makes a super-easy, fast, and delicious dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
treebeard s red beans  and rice

this recipe is quite a favorite at treebeards' restaurant in houston. it's posted in response to a request.  cooking time does not include the pre-soak or pre-boil time.  to make it south beach friendly, substitute low fat turkey smoked sausage for the regular smoked sausage, and serve with brown rice.

1. sort and wash red beans
2. in a large soup pot , add 2 qrts cold water and red beans
3. let soak overnight
4. do not drain water !
5. add onions , celery , and bell pepper to beans and bring to a boil
6. cover , and reduce heat to simmer about 1 1 / 2 hours , or until beans are soft
7. do not stir more than necessary
8. stir in seasonings and sausage
9. simmer 30 minutes more
10. meanwhile cook a pot of rice , and serve the beans over the hot cooked rice , garnished with shredded cheddar cheese and chopped green onion
11. if you want thicker beans , remove the lid during the last 30 minutes of cooking time , or remove 1 / 2 cups of the beans and mash them before returning to the pot
demonstrations.review: This was yummy! Both my husband and I were expecting more cajun tasting red beans (not ever having been to Treebeard's), but we really liked it after getting over that taste disparity. I made it exactly like the recipe, except without celery, b/c I don't like celery. I really liked it with the cheese and chives on top.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fluffy pancakes

i got this recipe from a good housekeeping recipe book years ago and have committed it to memory. my husband loves these and will eat no other kind.

1. mix all dry ingredients together in a bowl
2. mix milk , oil and egg in smaller bowl
3. mix liquid ingredients into dry ingredients
4. make 4 inch pancakes in a medium heated non-stick pan or griddle or use a small amount of oil in regular pan
5. cook until golden brown
6. serve with butter and syrup or your favorite topping
demonstrations.review: I was pretty disappointed with this recipe. I specifically wanted *fluffy* pankcakes, and these are very thin. They taste fine, but are just not what I was looking for at all. I followed the recipe exactly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
portable apple   cheese pleasers

most unusual cookies, but very tasty. my sil made this the first time about 25 years ago, the whole family loves it. especially because of how little sugar is in it. i think that she got it from the quaker oats company back then.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. combine flour , butter , sugar , egg , vanilla , cinnamon , baking powder and salt in a large bowl
3. mix well
4. add oatmeal , cheese and raisins
5. mix well
6. stir in chopped apple
7. drop by heaping spoonfuls onto an ungreased cookie cheet
8. bake 15 minutes or until golden brown
9. store in a tightly covered container in the refrigerator or in a loosely covered container at room temperature
demonstrations.review: My DH, who doesn't like sweets, gobbles these up! They're his new favorite cookie! Good job, Mysterygirl! I leave out the raisins, because he doesn't like them, but they are still delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot creamy italian chicken

nan

1. place the chicken breast halves in the crock pot
2. combine the italian dressing mix and water until smooth
3. pour over top of chicken
4. cover and cook on low for 3 hours
5. combine the cream cheese and soup until smooth and blended
6. stir in mushroom pieces
7. pour soup mixture over chicken
8. cook 1 hour more or until chicken is cooked through
9. serve over hot cooked rice or pasta
demonstrations.review: This was great! It was so nice to come home from work to a dinner already mostly made! I left out the mushrooms, b/c DH doesn't like them, but we both still enjoyed the meal. One thing I will do better next time is make sure the cream cheese and soup are smoothly blended before adding to the crockpot- the little lumps don't melt out as it cooks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach and onion couscous

colorful and a delicious side dish or main dish.

1. in a saucepan , cook and stir onion and garlic in hot oil until tender
2. add the broth and spinach
3. cook and stir frequently until the spinach thaws
4. bring mixture to a boil and stir occasionally
5. add in couscous
6. stir to combine
7. cover , remove pan from heat , and let stand 5 minutes or until liquid is absorbed
8. add remaining ingredients
9. stir to combine
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: WONDERFUL! I made this for dinner tonight, and I was a little nervous, because my husband doesn't usually like cooked spinach, but he raved over this recipe! I omited the pecans, simply because I didn't have them, and used lime instead of lemon juice, again because that's what I had, and it still turned out great.

target.recipe_text:
mean chef s raspberry mazurkas

i adopted this recipe after its original poster, mean chef (ihhdro), departed the site. mean posted it on jun 10, 2002.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. melt butter and cool
3. combine all dry ingredients in mixer with paddle
4. add melted butter until well combined
5. press half of the mixture in a half sheet pan and roll to firm
6. spread with jam to within 1 / 2-inch of edges
7. spread remaining mixture evenly on top and press down lightly
8. bake until golden brown
target.review: These are so delicious. Next time, however, I will spread the jam a bit thinner or, perhaps, use a little less because a couple of the center pieces had a little to much jam.  It surely didn't ruin the taste in any way, but they were to soft to hold together.....so I had to eat them all myself.  : )  I will surely be making these again.  Thank Mean!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple filling for pies

after just making this again i think some may find the filling too thick so i am changing the instructions to say 2-4 tablespoons of cornstarch. we like our apples diced so it takes 3-4 large apples to achieve 4 cups. i also used the micro.this time stirring every couple minutes. no chance of burning on the bottom that way.

1. sprinkle lemon juice over apples in saucepan
2. mix next four ingredients together and add to apples
3. mix well
4. add very hot juice to pan , cook , stirring constantly until thickened
5. remove from heat and cool
6. fill a well chilled 9 inch pastry lined pan and cover with top crust
7. bake on lowest rack at 425 for 10 minutes , and finish baking on center rack until bubbling , about 20 minutes more
demonstrations.review: With 15, 5-star ratings I knew this had to be fantastic...and it was.  I usually make one-crust pies (seems so much easier) but this recipe has surely changed my way of thinking.  So easy, and positively delicious.  Thank you Dorel, my friend, for sharing this wonderful recipe with us.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn pudding

this is the corn pudding recipe that has been served at our holiday dinner table for years. we would never think of switching. i hope your family enjoys it as much as we have.

1. combine sugar , flour , salt and pepper
2. add milk and slightly beaten eggs
3. stir in corn
4. dot with butter on top
5. bake in 375 degree oven , in pan of water for 1 hour
demonstrations.review:
Edited because I forgot to add stars the first time.

Bev, I can see this is going to be making it to our holiday table too. I've been searching for a corn pudding like one that is served at a local restaurant and I think I found it. No! I know I found it! Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy and tasty barbecue chicken sandwiches in the crock pot

this is almost too easy to be called a recipe, but i had to share it anyway. i came up with it one night when i wanted a nice meal but wasn't feeling too motivated. i love crock-pot cooking!

1. remove all visible fat from the chicken and toss it in the crock pot
2. place the onion slices on top of the chicken
3. pour the barbecue sauce over top
4. you may not need the entire jar , just enough to cover the chicken
5. cook it on low for 8 hours or until the chicken is nice and tender
6. shred the chicken with a fork and knife
7. scoop the mixture onto the bottom buns and top it with the top buns
8. or , if you're like my dad , you might prefer leaving the breasts whole and eating it that way
9. voila !
10. an easy weeknight meal that doesn't heat up your kitchen in the summertime !
11. i love this with potato chips and a carrot and raisin salad
demonstrations.review: I just purchased a slow cooker and was looking for an easy recipe....and this is it.  Very delicious too.   The chicken was tender and juicy.  Thanks for sharing Kree.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon dessert ww  2 points for entire recipe

for a sugar free, low fat dessert, this is really good.  tastes just like lemon meringue pie filling. be sure to use the cook and serve pudding mix, not instant.

1. add pudding mix to water and mix well
2. bring to boil
3. stir with a whisk until thickened
4. add box of jello and stir in well
5. pour into individual dessert dishes and refrigerate until set
6. top with fat free cool whip
demonstrations.review: I love 'anything' lemon so I was excited when I discovered this recipe. The 2 points made it very enticing too. Oh, how I would have loved to have given it 5 stars....if only it wasn't for the bitter aftertaste and the consistency.....which was more like a 'very thick' jello rather than a creamy lemon pie filling. BUT, that's not to say I won't be making it again. Once I topped it with Cool Whip the sweetness got rid of most of the bitterness leaving just enough lemony tartness, making it taste like lemon meringue pie. Now to figure out what I can do to make it creamier. I'm wondering if I used, perhaps, two packages of pudding if that would do it. It's certainly worth a try. Thanks for sharing the recipe Marie. I will be making it again, with a bit of experimenting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
twelve layer jello

kids and adults alike love this 'salad!' nice to slice & serve on a lettuce leaf (for presentation)- the colors can be varied to suit any holiday - greens & reds for christmas, varying shades of red for valentine's day, etc.. enjoy! this sounds like a lot of work, but it's really not. this is one i like to make when i'll be working around home all day, and can stop to do step after step. :)

1. add 1 cup boiling water to cherry jello
2. stir until dissolved
3. divide in half
4. to 1 / 2 the jello , slowly add 1 / 3 cup sour cream& stir until smooth
5. pour into a 9x13 pan
6. chill 25 minutes
7. add 2 tablespoons cold water to remaining jello& pour over first layer
8. let set 15 minutes
9. repeat process for each flavor , using flavors in given order for color effect
10. when completely cooled& firm , slice into squares& serve
demonstrations.review:
I haven't made this recipe as posted, but I would like to add another suggestion for presentation.  

My MIL use to make a similiar one in a large brandy sniffer-type glass with a stem base.

She would put in the first jello flavor and then set the stem of the siffer between the grates of her fridge so that the jello would gel at an angle.  She would then proceed with each additional flavor.  

It made an awe-inspiring presentation.

target.recipe_text:
peaches   cream pie

this pie is delicious! this is a great dessert to serve at a bbq cookout! i get compliments on it all the time!

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. place 3 cups fresh peaches into pie pastry
3. in a medium bowl , mix 1 cup sugar , 1 / 3 cup flour , and salt
4. add eggs and sour cream
5. blend well
6. spoon mixture over peaches
7. in a separate bowl , combine 1 / 2 cup sugar , 1 / 2 cup flour , and 1 / 4 cup butter until mixture resembles coarse meal
8. a pastry blender works well , but two forks or two knives will also work
9. sprinkle meal mixture evenly over pie
10. bake 60 minutes or until golden
11. garnish with fresh peach slices , if desired
12. refrigerate leftovers
target.review: I am not a peach pie fan...for some reason cooked peaches have a bit of a pucky taste to me...but this pie is excellent, esp. served cold (to avoid the pucky taste!).  I used 5 cups of fresh peaches and doubled all the rest of the ingredients.  Cook time took 1 hour and 20 minutes for the larger size pie pan (not sure of the exact dimension...maybe 10"???).  A perfect dense, slightly sweet, summer pie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta fazool   pasta and beans with sausage

this is a delicious dish that includes beans, pasta and sausage meat all in one, topped with cheese then baked in the oven, it's a very popular italian dish and there are many versions of this recipe, this one is a family favorite, i hope you enjoy this as much as my family does! --- if you prefer a dryer mixture then drain the tomatoes, ziti pasta works well in place of penne, please adjust the cayenne pepper to suit heat level, prep time includes cooking the pasta.

1. set oven to 400 degrees f
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. cook the pasta until just al dente
4. drain , do not rinse and immediately toss with 1-2 tbsp oil to prevent sticking
5. set aside
6. in a large fry pan , saut the sausage , ground beef , onion , garlic , dried oregano and thyme , over med-high heat , until the sausage and the ground beef are brown , crumbling with a fork while cooking
7. add in the undrained tomatoes , tomato paste and the cayenne pepper
8. simmer for 5-6 minutes
9. add in the kidney beans , and heat through
10. season with salt and pepper
11. add in the cooked pasta , parmesan cheese and parsley
12. toss to combine
13. transfer the mixture to a prepared baking dish
14. top with grated cheese
15. bake for 25 minutes , or until cheese melts and the mixture is hot and bubbly
demonstrations.review: Love, love, love this!  I'm sure my husband is going to label it as "chili"  which he does to anything of a tomato, bean and meat mixture, but I don't care - it was delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s spinach parmesan rice bake

this is a wonderful easy side dish to chicken or meat and any leftovers freeze wonderful,  it may also be baked in a 10-inch deep-dish pie plate and cut into wedges, this may be doubled but i would still only use one package or spinach or maybe 1-1/2 packages adding in too much spinach will overpower all other ingredients,  prep time does not include cooking the rice --- for freezing prepare recipe as directed but do not bake, wrap pan in plastic wrap then tightly in foil and freeze, to serve thaw over night in refrigerator, remove wrapping bake at 350°f for 25-30 minutes or until hot.

1. set oven to 350f
2. generously grease a 11 x 7-inch baking dish
3. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients with a wooden spoon , mixing very well to combine
4. season with salt , pepper and cayenne to taste
5. transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish then sprinkle with parmesan cheese
6. bake uncovered or covered for 25 minutes or until set
7. top with mozzarella cheese the last 5 minutes of baking
demonstrations.review: Excellent!  Besides requiring a bit of planning for prep time (mainly with cooking and cooling the rice, which took a little over an hour)I can't wait to make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peach crisp

i love the flavor of toasted oats...and combined with juicy peaches and cinnamon in a warm crisp, it's the ultimate comfort food. i have also made this recipe using half peaches and half apples...just as delicious!

1. place peaches in a 9 inch square pan
2. sprinkle with lemon juice and then drizzle with honey
3. in medium bowl , mix together remaining ingredients using a pastry blender or fork
4. sprinkle mixture evenly over peaches
5. bake in preheated 375 degree oven for 35-40 minutes or until top is golden brown
demonstrations.review: A good standard peach crisp.  I doubled the recipe to a 9x11 pan and had to cook 15 minutes longer.  I alos broiled on high for 5 minutes to get the topping to crisp up.  Think I'll add chopped pecans to the topping next time, yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
waffle ice cream sandwiches with the works

when i was young we used to make this all the time. use any flavor ice cream you desire. and the options are endless for the trim if you want.you can add a layer of peanut butter, fluff, preserves.....
july 4th.09 i made the waffles on the grill. a great way to keep it outdoors and yummy! when my guest smelt the waffles grilling they came running!

1. if using peanut butter , fluff or preserves spread a thin layer on one waffle
2. place the ice cream inside the waffles
3. then roll the optional garnishes along sides of the ice cream
4. and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Awesome treat for adults and kids!  Super easy and great customizable sweet goodness!  Had a craving for ice cream sandwiches, but didn't feel like making the cookies...this was a much better and way less work!  Try and get the waffles as crisp as possible without burning and it will remind you of a waffle cone.   I really suggest adding a thin layer of whipped topping to each waffle,  a small amount of chocoalte syrup and then what ever flavor ice cream you desire.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
demonstrations.review: Holy cow!  This pie is awesome, but super sweet!  I'm wondering if I accidentally put to much sugar into the apples...maybe next time I'll 1/2 the sugar.  Otherwse it was great, and I didn't even put the caramel sauce or nuts on top!

target.recipe_text:
one pot macaroni and cheese by consumer reports

years and years ago, cr reviewed boxed m&c products and came to the conclusion that this recipe was much less expensive and easy.  i have used it exclusively since the 70's, shared it with friends, and can tell you it is the best i have ever had.  of course, the prices are from about 30 years ago :)

1. using a two-quart saucepan , bring salted water to a boil
2. stir in the macaroni and return the water to a boil
3. stirring occasionally , continue boiling for four minutes
4. then lower the heat to medium and continue to boil the macaroni with frequent stirring for seven more minutes
5. add the remainder of the ingredients , stirring well until the cheese is melted
6. to modify and reduce saturated fat and salt , eliminate the salt , substitute low-cholesterol cheese and skim milk for the cheddar and the cream and add two teaspoons of fried onions
target.review: This is a great one pot macaroni recipe.  It's  so nice to find an easy and tasty recipe for  couples,  singles, and smaller families.  Thanks so much for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy skillet casserole

another recommendation from my grandmother!

1. brown beef in a large , deep pot with onion , garlic powder , salt , pepper and worchestershire sauce
2. cook macaroni separately according to package directions
3. when beef is cooked add tomato paste and prepared macaroni
4. mix throughly
5. cook over low heat until thickened
6. add grated cheese on top , if desired
7. cover and set aside for 5 mins before serving
demonstrations.review: I've been making this for years.  Sometimes I throw in a can of mixed vegetables or corn that has been drained.  It seems men and kids really like this dish.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bird s easy sweet corn

this is a simple way to dress up a can of corn. the flavor is spectacular.

1. melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat
2. add remaining ingredients
3. simmer uncovered and stir occasionally for about 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Old timers used to fix their corn and other vegetables like this.  By adding a little sugar they were able to get their children to eat vegetables.  This is good, but even less sugar and butter can be used.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake cherry cheesecake pie

this recipe is from grandma b. i am especially amused when i take it to a pot luck and people think i bought it because i can top it with the neat cover the ready-made crust comes with! very easy! be sure to chill well for a firm cheesecake.

1. blend cream cheese and sugar
2. fold in frozen dessert topping
3. press into graham cracker crust , spreading cream cheese mixture up sides
4. bottom will be covered and there will be a ring of cream cheese mixture about 1 inch wide around pie
5. pour cherry pie filling into center
6. chill at least 3 hours
demonstrations.review: My adult children still love this recipe from the 1970s.  They request it every Christmas.  We sometimes use Dream Whip instead of Cool Whip and make our own crust using graham cracker crumbs, butter and sugar.  This is a classic winner. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nestle toll house chocolate chip pan cookie

this recipe was in my paper recently and i made them for my co-workers. divine! i looked & looked and was surprised i couldn't find it already on zaar.

1. preheat oven to 375 grease a 15x10-inch jelly roll pan
2. combine flour , baking soda and salt in small bowl
3. beat butter , both sugars and vanilla in large mixer bowl
4. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each
5. gradually beat flour mixture into butter mixture
6. stir in chocolate chips and nuts
7. spread into prepared pan
8. bake 20-25 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: This is a wonderful classic recipe that I've been making for years.  The  recipe I received years ago indicated a 9x13 pan and that's what I've always used baking at 350 for about 27 min.  I follow the recipe exactly, but sometimes add an additional 1/4 c. of chips. Anyone who likes chocolate should like these pan cookies. The idea of adding peanut butter or M&Ms seems like fun. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simmered cabbage

once upon a time, my husband told me that he didn't like cooked cabbage. 

1. heat oil and butter in large heavy and wide saucepan or saute pan
2. add cabbage , salt , pepper , and stir over low heat for 5 minutes
3. add broth and bring to boil , cover and simmer over medium-low heat , stirring often , for about 15 minutes or until cabbage is tender
4. raise heat to medium , uncover and let juices reduce to about half
5. taste and adjust seasoning , serve hot
demonstrations.review: This is a very good recipe.  We don't use sherry, but add about 2 tsps. of sugar when cooking the cabbage.  We like it slightly on the sweet side.  Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
best pumpkin cookies

what can i say about these amazing pumpkin cookies... they are absolutely delicious! let me put it this way. i baked these every year at thanksgiving time for my job. my co-workers would come up to me two months in advance to make sure i was making them. one girl who resigned actually called me and asked what day i was bringing them in so that she could stop by - just for these cookies! another co-worker said she didn't even like pumpkin, but she loved these. the consistency is more cake-like than cookie. the glaze on top of these cookies is fabulous! at least, i think so. i noticed a few of you who rated this recipe said it was too sweet. that is why i suggested it may be omitted, or if you wish, use your own icing. lots of you have added nutmeg.. hey, make it all your own. that's what this is all about! : )

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. have ready some ungreased baking sheets
3. in a large mixing bowl , cream butter and the sugars together until light and fluffy
4. blend in pumpkin , egg and vanilla extract
5. in separate bowl , stir together flour , baking soda , baking powder , cinnamon , nutmeg and salt
6. mix flour mixture into butter-sugar mixture
7. drop tablespoonfuls 3 inches apart on ungreased baking sheets
8. bake the cookies for 10-12 minutes until golden around the edges
9. remove warm cookies and transfer to racks
10. let cool completely for a least one half hour , then frost with glaze
11. for glaze:
12. in a medium saucepan , heat butter and brown sugar over medium heat until bubbly
13. cook , stirring constantly , for one minute or until slightly thickened
14. beat in the milk
15. blend in confectioner's sugar until the glaze is smooth and spreadable
16. using a silicone basting brush , which i love and use religiously now , or a butter knife to spread glaze on cookies is the best
17. please
18. i suggest that you keep the saucepan over the stove on the lowest heat possible to prevent it from hardening
target.review:
I would love to give it 4 1/2 stars. They were really good! And one person who ate them swore they were the best cookies he had ever eaten! I really liked them and will defiantly make them again- I just can't say they are my favorite.
I made two batches- the first batch was the recipe followed to a tee- except for the glaze. I omitted the butter, added pumpkin pie spice and eyeballed it because I only wanted to drizzle it across the cookie. I must say, the cookies with more of the glaze were much better IMO- so next I will follow the glaze recipe. Anyway, this batch baked up really fluffy and cakelike. I smoshed some of the before I put them in the oven so they would bake more like cookies and less like muffin tops!
The second batch was made the next day with the remaining pumpkin (waste not, want not!)- which did not measure to one cup (I didn't even bother measuring it- but I would guess 1/2 cup). The batter was a good consistency, so I didn't think I needed to add any extra liquid to make up for the pumpkin. But I did mix in about a cup of chocolate chips to make up for less pumpkin flavor (if I had pumpkin flavoring I might have added that- yes they make it, King Arthur Flour.com carries it). These baked up much more like traditional cookies and less like muffin tops. I didn't glaze these.
I had some family members who preferred the original posted recipe and some who preferred it with chocolate chips! So I will make both again- it was a great way to use up the rest of the pumpkin.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whiskey marinade for london broil

this is a recipe is wonderful, it will make any kind of beef taste great. it is a family recipe that is over 50 years old and has been handed down in the family.leftovers make great sandwiches. enjoy

1. score meat with a knife of both sides
2. combine all ingredients together and marinade steak for 3 hours or longer in the refrigerator
3. broil or grill to desired doneness and slice on the diagonal
demonstrations.review:
Yummy!!!
Didn't have Accent but I did have Trader Joes 21 Salute Seasoning (which is really similar minus the MSG). I used 2 cloves of garlic because we LOVE garlic! And I used part balsamic and part white wine vinegar.
We BBQed the London Broil- hubbie stole a bit while it was cooking "just to see if it was done", and came back in say, "What did you put on that?? It tastes great!!" I knew then I had a winner!! 
I boiled the leftover marinade for a few minutes and we ate the London sliced thin over salad with the marinade as a dressing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
drunken garlic crock pot roast

don't be afraid of all the garlic in this! it gets really mild from the long cooking process and gives the meat a wonderful flavor. this is a favorite for me, and i hope it will be for you, too. different brands of beer will give you different amounts of sweetness ranging from bitter to malty (common beer characters). try going with less sugar until you know how your beer will taste (as most of them add some amount of sweetness regardless).

1. in a large skillet , heat 1 tablespoons of the oil and brown roast on both sides , seasoning with salt and pepper
2. remove to a platter and keep warm
3. add the remaining tbsp of oil to the pan and add the onions , cook until they just start to wilt then add the garlic , them cook until the onions are tender , a few minutes more
4. add the bouillon cubes to the hot water and stir to dissolve
5. add that to the skillet along with the beer , brown sugar , mustard , and vinegar
6. stir to mix well
7. pour mixture into the bottom of the crock pot
8. place roast on top of liquid , cutting into pieces if it doesn't lay flat
9. set the crock pot on low and cook for 7-8 hours
10. remove meat from crock pot and pour liquid into a pan on the stove
11. heat to a boil , and mix a slurry out of the cornstarch and water
12. thicken pan liquid with slurry to make a gravy
13. serve gravy over meat or with potatoes or noodles
demonstrations.review: I really liked this! I cut back on the the brown sugar and the beer a bit (as some guessed it made it "tangy"). And I used a mellow beer- "Spaten Oktoberfest" a beer from Munich. I served it with mashed potatoes and carrots, onions and celery that I roasted in the oven. This one goes in our "keep" pile.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
susan s version of old fashioned potato salad

from susan branch's "summer" book . . . a delicious family favorite!

1. slice potatoes into a large serving bowl
2. coarsely chop eggs with the potatoes
3. in a small mixing bowl , combine remaining ingredients
4. pour dressing over potatoes and eggs , stir gently to coat all
5. serve chilled or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: This is the potato salad that my mom has been making for years- and is my favorite by far! I substitute diced cucumber for the celery (not sure if it's in the original recipe or not, but it is on the handwritten copy I have) and it is the part that just makes it for me! And judging from the comments I get every time I make this for guests, it is often the part that sets this potato salad apart for everyone else too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed red potatoes with garlic and parmesan

the potatoes are ready in our garden, and this is the first recipe i reach for! these are so good!!

1. put potatoes and garlic in lg pan
2. cover with water
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes , until potatoes are tender
5. drain well
6. mash with the butter , milk , and salt
7. stir in the parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Dropping the garlic in with the potatoes is the best trick I've learned in a long time!! I love it! I usually roast the garlic in the oven while the potatoes cook- but then either I forget to put in until too late and the garlic isn't cooked enough or I overcook/burn it. This is the perfect solution!! The parmesan cheese was a unique addition. I added sour cream too. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic chicken livers

if you are reading this, then you probably like chicken livers! this recipe, however, may convert the 

1. combine the flour with the chili flakes in a resealable plastic bag
2. a few at a time , put the livers in the bag and shake to completely coat , remove and set aside
3. repeat with remaining livers
4. heat the oil in a large frying pan
5. pan-fry livers for 2-5 minutes each side depending on whether you like them rare or well-done
6. remove the livers from the frying pan
7. remove the pan from the burner , and wait about 30 seconds for the pan to cool slightly
8. add the balsamic vinegar to the pan , return to the heat , and scrape the juices and cooked bits up
9. add the butter , and continue to mix well
10. return the livers to the pan , coating them with the sauce and warming them through
11. serve , and enjoy
demonstrations.review: Yummmmm! I've always enjoyed liver a couple times a year,(usually beef liver sauted with onions) but was recently diagnosed with severe anemia and chicken liver is suppose to be one of the best foods to eat for it. I could easily eat this once a week!! Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
easy   yummy slow cooker chicken

this very easy recipe is great for a busy workday... just throw it all in the slow cooker in the morning, and have a wonderful hot and yummy sit-down dinner that night! i use frozen chicken breasts and add 2 cans of soup for lots of sauce. i make extra for a great work-day lunch for the next day. enjoy!

1. put frozen chicken into slow cooker
2. in a bowl , mix soup , onion mix , and milk
3. stir
4. add into slow cooker
5. add cut vegetables to the slow cooker and mix
6. cook on low for 7-9 hours , or high for 4-5 hours
target.review: YUM!  Another winner with the overly-picky hubby... I thought this tasted very "pot-roasty" and heavy... not expected from a chicken dish but VERY welcome!  I skipped the potatoes and served mine over egg noodles--- excellent!   I would highly suggest doubling the mushrooms and carrots (at LEAST, especially if not including potatoes in the pot)-- they soak up all that delicious flavor and I really wanted a lot more once I started eating them!   This is a keeper!  Thanks esm4877

demonstrations.recipe_text:
edna s apple crumble  aka  apple crisp

a simple and easy to make but oh so yummy recipe. known as apple crumble in the uk and apple crisp in the us

1. put apples in an 8 or 9 inch square baking dish
2. combine the rest of the ingredients in a separate bowl and mix
3. spread crumble mixture over apples and bake for 35 minutes in a 375f degree oven
4. for an added treat top off with a little english custard
demonstrations.review: Delicious--- just like the apple crisp my mom made growing up!  Delicious served hot with with some whipped cream on top!  I used a lot more cinnamon than the recipe calls for---  I sprinkled some on the apples before covering with teh topping... plus I tripled (at least) the amount in the topping itself.  YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek salad dressing

this is a scaled down slightly different version of a recipe i found. i use it on normal green salads and pasta salads, my wife even mentioned using it on sub sandwiches.

1. simply pour all ingredients into a container
2. shake vigorously until well mixed
3. store tightly at room temperature
demonstrations.review: Never been to Pano's in Buffalo, but it's very similar to other greek dressings in the Buffalo, NY area.  LOVE IT!  Wish it was less calorie, but it's so tasty.  I love the zing of the vinegar--- I prefer my greek dressings more "zingy" than "oily"

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco bell quesadillas

i used to love these when i was younger, i could eat two in one sitting! i haven't had fast food in a year or two, but these taste like i remember taco bell's quesadillas tasting. i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

1. combine sauce ingredients and stir until smooth
2. grill chicken in vegetable oil and cut into thin slices
3. preheat skillet over medium heat
4. one at a time , lay tortilla into hot skillet and sprinkle with 1 / 4 cup of each shredded cheese and 1 / 2 cheese slice on one side of the tortilla
5. arrange about 1 / 4 cup chicken slices over tortilla on the same half covered with cheese
6. on the empty side , spread about one tablespoon of sauce
7. fold over , and press gently with spatula
8. cook until cheese is melted and slice each into 4 pieces
demonstrations.review:
There is a LOT of cheese in this recipe!!  I wish there was a way to make it lower fat, but you gotta use all that cheese!

I didn't have jalepenos, so I made the sauce exactly as written but skipped the jalepeno step.  I used a whole packet of splenda instead of sugar, which made it a tad too sweet (though hubby loved it! lol)

I sauteed my chicken in a non-stick skillet with some taco seasoning sprinked over top--- put my tortillas on a Pam-sprayed electric griddle so I could get more done at once.  I made mine with some lovely sauteed onions, hubby's was without.  LOVED IT.  This is definitely in my "keeper" pile!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers parmesan chicken cutlets

this chicken tastes so great that it is great to have for dinner even when you're not on a diet.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. in resealable plastic bag , combine cheese , crumbs and all seasonings
3. shake well
4. transfer mixture to plate
5. dip each chicken breast in cheese mixture , turning to coat all sides
6. arrange on nonstick baking sheet
7. bake until chicken is cooked through , 20-25 minutes
demonstrations.review: Simple, easy to make, with ingredients I have in my kitchen all the time. Who knew that grated parm, when used in moderation, was fairly low calorie? Tasty, easy, and delicious. Thanks for an easy way to make chicken in my oven (I'm sick of grilled chicken!!!)  UPDATE:  This is now my go-to recipe for chicken--- whether for on a salad, with alfredo, with marinara, for sandwiches--- it's great all ways (and delicious cold!)  Irregardless of whether I'm dieting or not, this is my favorite recipe and SOOO easy with minimal ingredients (that I always have in the house!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled honey garlic pork chops

nan

1. combine ketchup , honey , soy sauce and garlic
2. set aside
3. lightly season pork with salt and pepper
4. brush each chop with sauce to coat
5. cook chops on greased grill 4 to 6 inches from medium-hot coals or on medium setting , basting with sauce often , for about 5 minutes on each side or until meat is cooked through
demonstrations.review: Agreed with the others--- I thought these would be wayyy too "ketchupy" but they weren't.  Tasted like a sweet and kinda tangy BBQ sauce.  We had ours on chicken (about 2 pounds worth) marinated our chicken for an hour with some of the sauce, then basted with the leftovers, and had a LOT left over--- I saved the leftovers for pork chops later this week!  Thanks!  Hubby was drooling from the sidewalk when I was grilling!

target.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth steak

add some zip to your grilled steak! cook time is to your desired doneness.

1. in a small bowl combine butter , garlic , onion powder , salt , parsley flakes and lemon juice
2. mix well
3. place mixture down the center of a 12 square piece of waxed paper and roll into a log
4. wrap tightly and refrigerate about 2 hours or until firm
5. season both sides of the steaks with pepper , broil or grill steaks
6. as the steaks are cooking place four thick slices of the seasoned butter on the steaks
7. just prior to serving place a slice of the buttered mixture on each steak
target.review: The steak sure does melt in your mouth.  Wouldn't use so much butter next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ginger rum marinade

this is a wonderful marinade. i loved it. this is good for up to 1 or 2 lbs of meat but i always make more. i like to have extra just incase.

1. mix all ingredients together
2. pour over meat and marinade in the refrigerator for 4 to 8 hours
3. i find this alot easier and it seems to marinade alot better this way
demonstrations.review: I used this for the pork and beef kebabs I made for camping. It was wonderful as my friends and I ate them up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory sweet crock pot chicken

you won't believe how flavorful this chicken is --and the ingredients are things you probably have on hand.

1. put all ingredients except for chicken in crock pot and stir
2. add chicken and spoon sauce over chicken
3. cook on low for 6 1 / 2 hours
demonstrations.review: Tasty chicken, with ingredients in your kitchen cupboards.  The sauce definately needs to be thickened up before serving with your side dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rum   mustard glazed ham

very simple but oh so good glaze. decorate the ham with pineapple & cherries, cloves etc if you really want a fancy ham. if you do not want to use rum substitute orange juice.

1. lightly score the ham- criss-cross and place in a roasting pan
2. mix remaining ingredients
3. spoon sauce over the ham and bake in 425f oven for 30 minutes
4. lower temperature to 375f and continue to roast for another hour
5. baste frequently
6. the top should be well browned and crispy in texture
7. allow to sit for 30 minutes covered with foil before carving
demonstrations.review: I used Bundaberg Rum and it was so good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fish with sour cream sauce

a low-carbohydrate main dish. simple, uncomplicated flavours combine well to make an easy main course.

1. melt butter in a skillet
2. saute onions in butter until lightly browned
3. arrange fish on top of onions and sprinkle with seasonings
4. add the water
5. cover , bring to a boil and then lower heat to low
6. cook for 45 minutes
7. divide fish onto two plates
8. stir sour cream into onions and liquid left in pan
9. serve sauce over fish
demonstrations.review: This is a good recipe for anyone on the Atkins Diet.  It is a simple and easy to make recipe that has some flavour.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham in a crock pot

what an easy recipe for beginning and busy cooks. a keeper! =)

1. place ham in crock pot
2. cook on low for 4 to 6 hours
3. sprinkle parmesan cheese and ground cloves on top of ham
4. pour can of pineapple slices and juice on top
5. cover and cook on low for an additional two hours
demonstrations.review: An easy recipe to follow where the aroma is mouthwatering and the ham, tender.

target.recipe_text:
caponata   eggplant and lots of good things

this i've been making for years and it 's never ever the same. this year i used balsamic vinegar and sundried tomatoes which brings the basic caponata up to date with our changing tastes. this if your are not familiar with this appetizer (relish) dip or spread it 's salty, sweet, tangy has lots of texture from celery, eggplant,onions, garlic, olive, capers, and pine nuts. this is very complex! serve it on fresh italian sliced bread or crackers or as a relish on a sandwich. you can even toss it into a small pasta to make a pasta salad. check out recipe #103124. in years gone buy i did can in boiling water bath for 10 minutes.i like to jar and give as gifts.

1. in a large hot pan heat oil and stir fry eggplant till golden brown about 10 minutes add celery , onions , garlic , and tomatoes cook till tender about 5 minutes
2. add remaining ingredients and simmer for 15 minutes
3. stirring occasionally !
4. jar or place in a sealed container and refrigerate over night
5. serve cooled
6. season with salt and pepper if needed
target.review: This is VERY good. I went to the store and bought rosemary vinegar, duh, when I made the recipe, I saw it said oil.I ended up heating the olive oil and adding some sprigs of rosemary. It was fine. This is so good, I started to munch on it before the overnight stay in the fridge. Thanks, Rita L

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black pepper onion bread   breadmaker 1 1 2 lb  loaf

this recipe comes from fleischmann's yeast company.

1. measure carefully , placing all ingredients in bread machine pan in the order recommended by the manufacturer
2. select basic / white cycle
3. use medium crust color
4. delay cycle can be used
5. remove baked bread from pan and cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: This recipe looked really tasty, but, it rose to only half the size of regular bread. I plan on trying it again with 1 1/2 tsp. of yeast. Maybe, try it like najwa with fresh onion and garlic.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach dip mozzarella pizza

my sil shared this with me when she was visiting from the frigid north. it was a huge hit at the pool party and a snap to prepare. this is a tasty appetizer but would also be a good lunch or light dinner recipe.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. place prepared crust on pizza pan
3. spread spinach dip over entire crust
4. sprinkle with water chestnuts if the spinach dip does not already contain them
5. if you can't find a good spinach dip in your local grocery deli there are many fine recipes here on zaar
6. sprinkle with mozzarella cheese
7. bake 10- 12 minutes until cheese and dip are bubbly and slightly browned
8. cool a few minutes before cutting
9. cut into wedges for lunch or dinner or cut into squares to use as an appetizer
demonstrations.review: This is a must try for anyone that likes spinach dip. I had the chore of making all of the appetizers for a party serving 100 people. This was one of the first to disappear. It was also had the highest requests for the the recipe. All that try this recipe will be pleased.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
snob pork chops

i got this online; sorry i don't know the original chef. it's very easy but tastes fancy.

1. brown chops on both sides in oil
2. remove from skillet
3. drain oil
4. add half the soup
5. replace chops on top of soup
6. mix rest of soup with wine and pour over chops
7. simmer 20 minutes
8. enjoy a glass of wine with dinner
demonstrations.review: My husband loves this, we add a package of dry onion soup mix, stick it in the crock pot, and dinner is served. I make it with mashed potatoes, but, rice or noodles would be good too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked potato cheddar soup

after a couple tries, my husband finally says this is the soup! i think it is the garlic that won him over.:) this soup can be seasoned to your taste with any number of spices!

1. in a large pot , melt butter and add flour
2. cook for 2 minutes
3. whisk in milk , stirring constantly , bring mixture to a boil to thicken
4. add potatoes , garlic , onions
5. simmer for 10 minutes add in cheese , sour cream , salt , pepper , old bay , and bacon
6. heat til cheese is melted and serve !
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is a really hearty soup. But, once you taste it, it will forever be in your memory. I worked at a restuarant that had it on the menu. ( No garlic in theirs, but, I love the garlic bulb. :) **Top the chopped green onions to the  soup, when it is to be served.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rigatoni puttanesca

if you like bland food, pass this one by. it is a lively dish..........true italian comfort food.

1. heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a heavy saucepan
2. add onion and garlic
3. cook over low heat for10 to 15 minutes , or until vegetables are wilted
4. crush tomatoes slightly
5. add to the saucepan along with their liquid
6. stir in tomato paste
7. cook for 5 minutes over medium heat
8. coarsely chop the anchovies and add to the saucepan along with their oil
9. stir in olives , capers , basil , oregano , red-pepper flakes and black pepper
10. stir gently and simmer over medium heat for 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
11. while sauce simmers , bring a large pot of water to a boil with remaining tablespoon of olive oil
12. add pasta and cook until just tender
13. for rigatoni , allow 10 to 12 minutes
14. drain pasta and serve topped with puttanesca sauce
15. pass the parmesan
demonstrations.review: This is the puttanesca sauce that I know and love. Do not omit anything! Anchovies are essential to this sauce, as are capers, and hot pepper flakes. Yummy!!

target.recipe_text:
brussels sprouts in garlic butter

this is a recipe from joy of cooking... totally changed my mind about brussels sprouts! it's imperative that you use fresh sprouts, the texture would be way off with the frozen ones.

1. melt butter and olive oil in a medium skillet until butter is foamy
2. reduce heat to medium , add smashed garlic and cook until lightly browned
3. remove garlic and discard
4. add sprouts cut side down , cover , and cook without stirring on medium-low heat 10-15 minutes or until tender when pierced with a knife
5. the cut side of the sprouts should get nice and browned , with a nutty , buttery flavor enhanced by garlic
6. top with freshly grated parmesan and salt& pepper to taste
target.review: This was a tremendous win at dinner. Two-third of my kids really liked them, and after gobbling them up, my husband and I agreed that we could make a meal of them. I've never enjoyed Brussels sprouts, and now I'm so excited that I'm planning to put them in my garden this year. I made them per the recipe, although I found I needed to add a little more butter at the end, and I held off on the parm because I wanted to enjoy the flavor without it the first time out. I think what I enjoyed most were the little roasted leaves that fell off of the sprout - crunchy and delicious.  These are just great. Thank you for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon garlic broccoli

a great basic recipe for a fast side dish - who doesn't like to dress up their veggies? i use regular olive oil as i haven't found the "o olive oil" called for in the recipe yet - but posted it as written.  also like to sprinkle with a little (light) bit of freshly shredded/grated parmesan cheese for a nice twist. another nice, quick and easy recipe from sandra lee on the food network - work night meals woohoo!!  check out the other recipes from this episode that compliment this well:lemon-herb butter-basted chicken, lemon chicken soup, lemon pudding brulee with blueberries, and a nice lemon cream martini.  yummy!!  ;)

1. add broccoli florets , lemon zest , minced garlic , lemon olive oil , and 1 tablespoon water to a microwave-safe bowl
2. stir to coat completely
3. cover bowl with plastic and microwave on high for 4 to 5 minutes
4. check for tenderness
5. cook 1 more minute if needed
6. sprinkle lemon juice over broccoli and toss to coat
7. season to taste with salt and black pepper (add a light sprinkle of parmesan cheese if desired)
8. serve immediately
9. enjoy !
10. )
demonstrations.review: From a girl who dislikes most veggies, thank you for this gem! I love how quick this is and the wonderful flavor the lemon adds. I normally don't mess with zest, but I'm glad I did :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken or turkey tetrazzini casserole

three flavors of canned soup takes the place of a creamed sauce for this recipe, i like to use 2 cans cream of mushroom and 1 can cream of chicken, i would suggest to add in salt if needed at the table as the creamed soups have enough salt already added . this is really good! :)

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. butter a 13 x 9-inch casserole dish
3. cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling water until al dente drain , then transfer to a large bowl
4. add in whipping cream and all three canned soups , cooked chicken or turkey , sour cream , parmesan cheese , 1-1 / 2 cup grated cheddar cheese and frozen peas toss well to combine
5. in a large skillet melt butter
6. add in the mushrooms and cook until all the liquid is removed
7. to the skillet with the mushrooms , add in onions , garlic and jalapeo pepper saut until onions are soft
8. add to the soup mixture
9. using a wooden spoon mix all ingredients together until well combined
10. season with seasoned salt and pepper
11. transfer to prepared baking dish
12. cover with foil and bake about 30-35 minutes uncover and sprinkle with about 1 cup grated cheddar cheese , return to oven and bake until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: Love this! I used a little celery seed since I didn't have a can of cream of celery, and used diced green chilis since that's what I had on hand. My kids prefer fettuccine noodles, and that worked great too. Kittenkal, thanks again for a marvelous recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy and delicious ranch parmesan chicken
