there are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, i find that hidden valley ranch dressing works the best but kraft or any other brand will do, i sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although i have only made this using breasts i imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *note* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
for low-fat option: use low-fat ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as smart balance 50/50 blend.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. in a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with parmesan cheese , seasoned salt , black pepper and garlic powder
3. dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides
4. coat in the breadcrumb mixture
5. place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil
6. lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast
7. if desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces
8. bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked)
demonstrations.review: Everyone gobbled this up tonight! My DH and 2 young sons cleared their plates in record time, and I love how easy this was. Mine was perfectly done in 30 minutes and was juicy as chicken can be. Very pretty too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best deviled eggs

these have been a favorite for years, when i serve these at my get togethers or make them for socials and large events they are always the first to go and everyone wants the recipe, i suggest to use large, extra large or even jumbo eggs for this, i like to make the yolk filling a day ahead and refrigerate this will blend the flavors --- for a nice presentation place each egg half in a colored paper muffin liner --- all ingredient amounts may be adjusted to taste --- see my recipe#259573

1. slice the eggs in half lengthwise
2. remove the yolks , and set whites aside
3. in a small bowl , mush yolks well with a fork , leaving no small lumps
4. add next 10 ingredients mix well to combine
5. spoon or pipe egg yolk mixture evenly into the whites
6. sprinkle with paprika
7. cover tightly with plastic wrap
8. store in the refrigerator until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: O my GOSH these were amazing! I used homemade mayonnaise (http://www.food.com/recipe/homemade-mayonnaise-71967) and substituted that mayo for the milk and otherwise made this as is. The eggs were from our backyard chickens (kept the eggs for about a week so I could peel them!) and these are hands down the absolute best deviled eggs I have had in my entire life. I'm taking them to a pot luck tomorrow and I know they're going to be a hit. The filling is so rich and full of flavor - really fantastic. Kittencal you are a food goddess - thank you for posting! Next time I make these I'm making lots of extra so I can keep a bunch for myself.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fantastic mushrooms au gratin

this is one of my family's all time favorite mushroom recipes, you can double the recipe, i have left the garlic as optional if you are a garlic lover i suggest to add in and you may adjust the amount to taste ---  you will love this! :)

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. grease a shallow baking dish
3. in a medium skillet saute the sliced mushrooms with butter over medium-high heat
4. in a small bowl , blend together sour cream , salt , pepper and flour
5. add to the mushrooms in the pan
6. heat until just beginning to boil
7. transfer to a baking dish
8. sprinkle with chopped parsley and cheese
9. bake for about 10-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was a huge win at dinner. My husband loves mushroom dishes, and when he took his first bite he gave me that look that he does when he's had a bite of something indescribably delicious, right before he tells me that I should make it as often as possible. I threw it together quickly, and I realized later that since I only had 8 oz of mushrooms and didn't measure, I used about 3x the amount of butter that I should have (I should have poured if off before adding the sour cream). Also, we've started eating Paleo, so I left out the flour - the dish turned out more watery than I think it will next time when I use the right amount of butter! I did use seasoned salt as the recipe recommends. I will definitely make this again - probably to serve over steak next time.

target.recipe_text:
marilyn s florida sunshine cake

i first had this cake at my in-laws (my sil is marilyn!)over the christmas holidays in denver, just after my husband and i were married. it is a deliciously moist cake, full of citrus flavor, that is like a taste of sunshine!

1. combine cake ingredients in large mixing bowl
2. blend till moistened
3. using mixer , beat on low speed until smooth , but do not overbeat
4. pour batter into well greased / floured bundt pan
5. bake at 325 for 45-60 minutes
6. remove cake from pan onto serving plate
7. top with orange glaze: mix orange juice and butter
8. add powdered sugar until a thin consistency is achieved
9. pour onto hot cake and keep spooning glaze back on so it seeps in
10. ileave the extra glaze on the serving plate to spread on each slice of cake !
11. yum !
target.review: This is a very nice cake that I will make again.  I baked it in a 9 by 13" pan to take to church.  It worked fine, I just added about 5 minutes to the baking time recommended on the cake mix box.  The cake has a nice flavor & is light & fluffy.  I had a bit of trouble with the glaze; following the directions  resulted in kind of a curdled appearance.  It was OK since it pretty much melted when applied to the hot cake.  I would recommend creaming the margarine & sugar together & then diluting it to the preferred consistency with the oj.  I poked holes in the top of the cake with a fork to allow the glaze to penetrate the cake better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flat cat cookies

poor kitty!

1. with an adult's help , preheat oven to temperature specified on package
2. sprinkle flour on a clean , flat surface and roll out cookie dough slightly thicker than what the package calls for
3. then , using butter knife , cut out cookies in the shape of a flattened cat
4. use a large spatula to carefully transfer cookies to cookie sheet
5. bake according to package directions
6. while they're cooling , count out enough cinnamon candies to put two eyes and a nose on each cat
7. carefully flatten between the front and back of two spoons and set aside
8. allow the cookies to cool on the cookie sheet for about 3 minutes and then press in eyes and nose
9. transfer to wire rack to continue cooling
10. dribble jam here and there on each cookie for blood
11. makes approximately 3 dozen kitty road kill
12. sicko serving suggestion: instead of making each cookie in a perfect cat shape , make a few that are missing a limb and / or tail
13. why not even sever a head or two ?
14. drip jam blood at stumps for an authentically dismembered look ?
demonstrations.review: Mirj, you are one sick cookie!  ;-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green beans with lemon and oil

you will love the fresh lemony taste of these greens beans.  enjoy!

1. cook beans in a 5-quart pot of boiling salted water until crisp-tender , about 5 minutes
2. drain in a colander and immediately transfer to a bowl of ice and cold water to stop cooking
3. drain and pat dry
4. toss beans with oil , salt , and pepper to taste , then toss with lemon juice and half of zest
5. serve beans sprinkled with remaining zest
demonstrations.review: These were very tasty green beans, Bev.  The lemon was a very good addition that I wouldn't have thought of on my own.  DD especially enjoyed them, & when you can get a kid to compliment you on the veggies, you know it's a good recipe!  I served them with Jewelies Tandoori Chicken Burgers with Creamy Chutney & some fresh fruit.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet potato  apple and onion gratin

posted by request. an adaptation i found from bon bon appetit, december 1991. times are estimates.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. butter 13x6 inch oval baking dish
3. melt butter in heavy large skillet over medium heat
4. add onions and saute until tender , about 10 minutes
5. toss apples with flour in medium bowl
6. arrange half of sweet potatoes in bottom of prepared dish
7. top with half of apple slices
8. arrange remaining potatoes and then remaining apples
9. cover with sauteed onions
10. pour stock over all
11. bake until sweet potatoes are tender , about 45 minutes
12. mix breadcrumbs , cheese and bacon in small bowl , then sprinkle mixture over potatoes
13. bake an additional 20 minutes
14. broil until topping browns , if needed
15. let cool 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This side dish utilizes some of my favorite foods & combines the sweet & savory flavors in a very nice way.  It smelled lovely in the oven.  The closest sized pan that I had was 9 by 13", so I did increase both the toppings & the chicken broth to accomodate the larger area of sweet potatoes, apples & onions to be covered.  The whole family enjoyed this one, thanks, Roosie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fantastic feta chicken

faboulous flavor in less than fifty minutes! compliments of athenos.

1. arrange chicken in 13x9-inch baking dish
2. drizzle with 1 tablespoon of the juice
3. sprinkle with oregano and pepper
4. top with cheese
5. drizzle with remaining 1 tablespoon juice
6. bake at 350f for 30 to 35 minutes or until cooked through
demonstrations.review: This was very tasty & couldn't have been easier.  I think next time I will drizzle just a bit of olive oil over the chicken, as skinless breasts can be just a bit dry if you aren't careful.  Very nice combination of flavors, thank you, Lorac.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemony salmon patties

enjoy.        

1. combine the first nine ingredients
2. mix well
3. spoon into eight greased muffin cups , using 1 / 4 cup in each
4. bake at 350 for 45 minutes or until browned
5. meanwhile , melt butter in a saucepan
6. stir in the flour to form a smooth paste
7. gradually stir in milk
8. bring to a boil over medium heat , stirring constantly
9. cook for 2 minutes or until thickened
10. remove from the heat
11. stir in lemon juice , salt and cayenne
12. serve over patties
demonstrations.review: Very, very nice!  I did end up making quite a few changes in the recipe as I went along, but the end result was a very nice dinner.  I had some leftover fresh salmon, so flaked & used that.  I didn't have any parsley (that would've been a nice touch - next time I'll make sure to have some on hand).  I decided to go with the White Worchester Sauce for no particular reason.   Halving the sauce recipe made plenty & I did double the lemon juice.  This was an easy, tasty meal which I will surely make again.  Thanks, Sean!

target.recipe_text:
easy chocolate chip pan squares

my mom made this for us all the time when we were little.  it is an easy recipe that makes a great treat.  freezing instructions (courtesy of the oamc tag game!): cut into squares, flash freeze and wrap in plastic, then place in a ziplock bag. be sure to label them!
to eat: thaw and enjoy!

1. combine margarine and brown sugar and beat well
2. mix in vanilla and flour
3. then add chocolate chips
4. spread onto lightly greased 9x13 pan and pat down gently
5. bake 10-12 mins or until light brown at 350f
target.review: This is a great fast and easy recipe. This would be really great for kids to do. A wonderful alternative to chocolate chip cookies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy delicious chocolate chip cookies

these chocolate chip cookies are great! it's hard to stop eating them! you can also drop them by rounded tbsp, and bake about 10 minutes.

1. preheat the oven to 375f for regular pans and 350 for dark pans
2. in a medium bowl , sift together the flour , baking soda and salt
3. in a large bowl , cream together the butter , both sugars , and vanilla until light and fluffy
4. add eggs and beat well
5. gradually add in the flour mixture
6. beat well
7. stir in the chocolate chips and nuts
8. drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets
9. bake in the middle of the oven about 8 minutes or until lightly browned
10. do not overbake
11. cool slightly
12. remove from the cookie sheets and cool completely on a wire rack
13. change the bread or apple every day or two
14. cookies may also be frozen for longer storage
demonstrations.review: Great flavor. nice and chewy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thick chocolate pudding

this is the perfect chocolate pudding. it has a rich chocolate flavor, great texture and is not high in fat. i can't count the number of times i have made this. i hope you enjoy it as much as we do.

1. in a 2-qt
2. microwave-safe bowl , combine the first four ingredients
3. stir in milk until smooth
4. microwave , uncovered on high for 3 minutes
5. stir
6. microwave 4-6 minutes longer or until thickened , stirring after each minute
7. stir in vanilla
8. pour into individual serving dishes
9. cool
10. refrigerate
11. garnish with whipped topping if desired
demonstrations.review: great pudding not too sweet I love the fact it can be done in the microwave.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oma s boterkoek  dutch buttercake

this is boterkoek (dutch buttercake) just like my oma (grandma) used to make. she passed away over a year ago now and i really started to crave it. i hope you like it as much as i did growing up! :)

1. in medium bowl , mix together butter , sugar and almond extract
2. add beaten egg except for 1 teaspoon
3. sift flour and baking powder , and add to bowl , mixing with wet ingredients
4. put dough in greased 9 inch pie plate
5. mix the reserved 1 tsp of beaten egg with 1 tsp of water , and brush over dough
6. sprinkle with sliced almonds , if desired
7. bake at 350f for 25-30 minutes or until done
8. this is a dense cake , but should be soft on the inside and hard on the outside , but not too hard !
demonstrations.review: Great almond flavour. Extremely quick and easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
funnel cake

i love to get funnel cakes at the fair, but a fair is not always in town. this recipe is very good and perfect for a quick snack for the kids.

1. in a large bowl , mix all dry ingredients
2. beat egg , milk , and vanilla together in a separate bowl
3. add milk mixture to dry ingredients beating until smooth
4. fill 8" skillet with 1 inch oil and heat to 375 degrees
5. cover funnel hole with finger and fill with about 1 / 4 cup of batter
6. hold funnel over skillet and remove finger moving funnel around to form patterns with the batter
7. fry until golden brown , about 1 or 2 minutes
8. turn over with tongs and continue frying another minute or two or until both sides are brown
9. remove from oil , drain on paper towels , and sprinkle with powdered sugar
10. serve hot
demonstrations.review: It is a good funnel cake but it needs to be thinned down just a bit.Very simple to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super quick pizza dough

only a 15-minute rise time! add a pinch of salt or garlic salt if you wish, but i never do. easy and quick dinner!

1. mix yeast in warm water until dissolved
2. stir in oil and flour until it forms a dough ball
3. cover bowl with a kitchen towel , place on top of your stove while the oven is warming up
4. let rise for 15 minutes
5. spread on pizza pan , jelly roll pan or baking stone
6. top with your favorite sauce , meats , veggies , herbs and / or cheeses !
demonstrations.review: Very fast pizza dough and very inexpensive to make.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s beer battered fish

a long time favorite i have used for over 25 years, plan ahead the batter needs to sit for one hour before using --- the amounts listed will be enough for 2 pounds of fish,  you may double but make certain to prepare two separate recipes in two bowls,  do not double into one bowl as the batter will not be as good --- you may wish to add in 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder and paprika to the flour mixture for extra flavor and for a little heat add in a pinch of cayenne pepper :)

1. sift flour and salt , add butter and egg
2. add beer gradually , add beaten egg white , stirring only until smooth
3. let stand for 1 hour in a warm place
4. in a deep fryer or heavy pot heat oil to 375 degrees
5. dip fish in batter then fry in hot oil until golden brown
6. allow to drain on a heavy brown paper bag or on double paper towels
7. it is best to use thinner pieces of fish if you intend to fry the whole piece or just cut into large chunks
target.review:
AWESOME fish batter.  Not too thick not too thin.  The batter really lets the fish taste come through but gives the fish a nice crisp outside.  If you are searching for a light weight, great tasting batter for fish this one is #1.  I used it on crappies and sunfish that my husband caught this weekend ice fishing her in Wisconsin.

Once again AWESOME receipe thank you so much for sharing it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best southern green beans

these are fantastic! this recipe was revised from an old family favorite! my southern roots come through on this one! either way the beans end up melting in your mouth and the cooked bacon adds more flavor! really tasty! good for cookouts or to compliment any meal!

1. put green beans in pot- if canned add juices , if frozen add water enough to see but not cover beans- cook on medium heat
2. fry bacon until cooked but not too crisp- drain on paper towel
3. cut onion in large slices and break rings apart in to beans
4. crumble or rip bacon apart add to beans
5. add spices to taste
6. let cook for a few hours on low heat
7. if want to serve sooner- turn heat up and cook until water boils down
8. or can put in crockpot on low all day long and let simmer
demonstrations.review: I make my greens beans this way - only way the family will eat them!  I add 2 chicken bullion cubes to the beans and it adds a wonderful flavor.  Great way to jazz up the greens beans!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best sticky chicken wings

for this recipe i strongly suggest to use fresh not frozen thawed wings as frozen will hold in too much water --- you may use 2 tablespoons minced fresh garlic in place of garlic powder but the fresh garlic tends to burn while cooking, the choice is up to you or you may use both the powder and fresh garlic, the butter will firm up only slightly when chilled but will melt and blend in with the other ingredients when baked --- plan ahead the wings need to marinate a minimum for 8-24 hours, overnight is better -- these wings are delicious!

1. in a large bowl mix together first 8 ingredients until well combined
2. add in wings
3. toss to coat
4. refrigerate for 8-24 hours
5. set oven to 350f
6. set oven rack to lowest position
7. place the wings on a large greased jelly-roll pan
8. bake for about 25-30 minutes or until cooked through
9. optional: for a crispy skin broil under broiler heat for about 4 minutes
demonstrations.review: This has to be one of the best chicken wing recipes I have made!  I've give it 10 stars if possible!!  Even my 2 younger girls - picky eaters - couldn't get enough of these wings.  Not too sweet - just the right flavor. Will definetly make these again.  I used 3 lbs of frozen wings (thawed them in water first) and the sauce was more then enough!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s milk boiled corn on the cob

a method i have been using for over 30 years, you will never boil corn in just water again once you try this, this method produces a very tender and sweet corn on the cob, i promise! --- do not add in any salt to the water as it will make the corn tough

1. fill a large stock pot half full with water
2. add in the cream , milk , sugar and butter
3. bring to a boil , then add in the corn cobs
4. reduce heat to a simmer and allow corn to cook for 7-8 minutes or until just tender , depending on size of corn try not to over cook the corn as it will become tough
5. using long tongs remove and place on a plate or in a bowl , then cover with foil until ready to serve
6. serve with butter and salt to taste
7. delicious !
demonstrations.review: I'd give it more then 5 stars if I could!  We had some very early sweet corn (I think it was probably field corn). We were so hungry for corn that we bought it and I used Kittencal's recipe.  It was delicious!!!  I will never boil corn in plain water again!  Thanks for an awesome recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast burritos  once a month cooking

great for that run in the morning breakfast. you can also take frozen burritos with you when going camping. just place the bag of frozen burritos into the ice chest, and by the time you're ready for breakfast the first morning, the burritos are fully thawed. then simply reheat them in a large skillet over the campstove or fire grate.

1. scramble eggs in large skillet until done
2. stir in cooked sausage and salsa
3. warm tortillas in microwave 20-30 seconds or until warm and flexible
4. place 1 / 2 cup egg mixture into tortilla
5. roll burrito-style
6. freeze burritos in single layer on lightly greased cookie sheet
7. when fully frozen , wrap burritos individually
8. place wrapped burritos in large zip-top freezer bags
9. freeze
10. to serve: unwrap burritos from foil or plastic wrap that you used for freezing
11. wrap in a paper towel
12. cook in microwave until heated through
13. or thaw burritos , wrap burritos in foil , and bake at 350 degrees for ten minutes
demonstrations.review: I just finshed making 24 burritos and 5 Egg McMuffins!  My husband had 2 of them right away. I had a lot of filling so I started putting more into the last ones and that's why I ended up with the McMuffins!  These will be excellent for breakfasts in the morning which I never seem to have time for. I can take it to work and heat it up and eat it at my desk when I get a few minutes.  My husband is off work for a few weeks so he can very easily pull these out of the freezer and nuke them for breakfast/lunch.  Even my fussy kids should like these!  What I used in mine was 1 lb of Jimmy Dean Pork Sausage and 10 chopped up sausage links, 16 eggs, 1 pkg of hashbrowns, colby and mozz. cheese, diced green peppers and mild salsa.  The only problem I had was getting them rolled into a burrito (have never been able to master that!).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast bagel sandwiches  oamc

while searching for a great make ahead breakfast i tried this and it worked great! hope you enjoy it too :)

1. slice each bagel in half
2. lightly butter each side
3. to cook eggs , lightly grease a mug or small bowl or ramekin
4. beat eggs in that bowl and microwave 30 seconds
5. remove egg in one piece and repeat for remaining eggs
6. or take swan valley tammi's idea and pre-cook the bacon , chop it up and add it to the eggs
7. pour into greased muffin tins
8. bake at 400 degrees fahrenheit for 12 minutes so all 12 egg / bacon 'patties' are done at the same time
9. on the bottom half of the bagel place cooked egg
10. top each egg with approximately 1 tablespoon grated cheese
11. stack bacon on top
12. complete sandwich with top of bagel
13. cool slightly
14. wrap in plastic wrap individually
15. place in a large labeled zipper freezer bag
16. to serve , remove 1 bagel sandwich from bag and remove wrapping
17. place upside down in microwave and heat for 30 seconds
18. place right side up and microwave for 30 seconds more or until heated through
19. time may vary in your microwave
20. eat warm
demonstrations.review: These are AWESOME!!!!  I made mine some with bacon, some with Jimmy Dean Sausage Patties and some with both.  They are a hit at our house!  It's hard to just eat one at a time.

target.recipe_text:
rumlicious rum cake

this cake is not for the weak of heart it's guaranteed to be a crowd winner. i always like to add a shot or two more than what the recipe calls for.

1. preheat oven 350 degrees
2. grease and lightly flour one bundt pan , and evenly distribute the the nuts on the bottom of the pan
3. in a large mixing bowl blend the cake mix , water , oil , 1 / 2 cup rum , eggs , and the instant vanilla pudding
4. pour batter into the greased bundt pan and bake for 1 hour or until a toothpick is instered into the center and it comes out clean
5. 5-10 minutes before the cake is removed from the oven , combine the remaining 1 / 2 cup rum , butter , and sugar into a sausepan
6. heat on stove until th butter melts and the sugar has dissolved
7. once the cake has been removed from the oven slowly pour the entire hot rum mixture over
8. let the cake rest for 10 minutes and then turn out onto a plate
9. cool
target.review:
Quite delicious.  I usually shy away from cake mixes, but this is an exception!  I used Captain Morgan's spiced rum.  I poked holes in the cake with a toothpick before pouring the glaze over.  Took to work for a party. Rave reviews! I will definitely make again.
Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green tomato cake with brown butter icing

i thought that this was an interesting use of green tomatoes.  the cake is rich made as directed, but i think that it could be lightened easily.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour a 12 cup bundt pan
3. beat butter and sugar with a mixer until creamy
4. add eggs , 1 at a time , beating well after each addition
5. combine flour , cinnamon , baking powder , salt , and nutmeg
6. gradually add dry ingrediens to butter mixture , beating well
7. stir in tomatoes , raisins , and walnuts
8. spoon batter into prepared pan
9. bake for 70 to 75 minutes , or until a tester inserted in center comes out clean
10. let cool in pan on wire rack for 10 minutes
11. remove from pan , and let cool completely
12. icing: in a medium saucepan over low heat , melt butter
13. cook 6 to 8 minutes , or until butter is lightly browned
14. whisk in confectioners' sugar until smooth
15. spoon browned butter icing over cake
demonstrations.review: Deliciously different way to use up my garden tomatoes that never ripened.  The only thing I did different was add a little vanilla to both the cake and frosting, and used regular raisins because that's all I had.  Yummy- and the frosting is terrific!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemony rice pilaf

this takes plain ol' rice to a new level. goes particularly well with chicken. if you don't use chicken stock, this side dish is vegetarian/vegan.

1. in a heavy saucepan , heat oil over mediumheat and cook onion for 5 minutes , or until softened
2. stir in rice , then stock , and bring to a boil
3. reduce heat and cover
4. let simmer for 20 minutes , or until rice is tender
5. stir in lemon zest , lemon juice , and parsley
6. taste and add pepper if you wish
demonstrations.review:
Very tasty.   I stirred a few times toward the end of cooking and used a short grain rice.  It turned out sort of creamy like a risotto.  I did add a little salt because I used a low sodium chicken broth. I also stirred in a dab of butter at the end.   Yummy served with fish.
Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quinoa black bean salad

this is really easy to make. there were no leftovers! what a great combination of flavors and textures. serve with tortilla chips on the side.

1. cook the quinoa in the water
2. allow to cool slightly
3. in a large bowl , combine the oil , lime juice , cumin , coriander , cilantro and scallions
4. stir in the beans , tomatoes , bell peppers and chilies
5. add the cooled quinoa
6. season with salt and pepper to taste
7. serve cold
demonstrations.review: Very good salad.  I only had white beans, and I added double the olive oil and one grated garlic clove. Can't wait for dinner!  Thanks for a good quinoa recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
traditional irish soda bread

this makes a fairly dense, rustic (ugly, even) loaf of bread that is tasty and not sweet. it is crusty and rough on the outside, chewy inside. nummy hot with lots of butter! note: sometimes (depending on humidity etc) it takes a bit more than the 1 1/2 cups of buttermilk--just keep adding a little bit at a time until it all holds together as stated in the recipe.

1. heat oven to 425 degrees f
2. brush a baking sheet with melted butter or spray with non-stick spray
3. combine dry ingredients in a deep bowl
4. gradually stir in 1 cup buttermilk , beating constantly , until dough is firm enough to be gathered into a ball
5. if dough crumbles , add up to 1 / 2 cup more buttermilk , 1 tbsp at a time , until it holds together
6. place on a lightly floured board and pat into an 8-inch flattened round loaf
7. place loaf on baking sheet and slash a 1 / 2-inch deep "x" into the top of the dough with a small , sharp knife
8. bake at 425 degrees f for about 45 minutes , or until the top is golden
9. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Very good, easy.  I would add a little more salt next time, but I love this simple peasant food.  Great with corned beef and cabbage dinner.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cauliflower cheddar soup

this is a modified recipe, originally called farmhouse cheddar soup, which i clipped out years ago. i make it often and freeze in individual servings to reheat. you can reserve 1 1/2 c of the cauliflowerets to saute in some butter and add after the soup has been pureed. i usually just puree it all in the soup pot with a hand blender.

1. combine water / stock , potatoes , cauliflower , onion , carrot and garlic in large pot
2. bring to a boil
3. simmer 15 minutes or until vegetables are tender
4. remove from heat and let cool 20 minutes
5. puree in food processor or blender or use hand blender
6. return to pan and stir in remaining ingredients until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I did double the seasonings- just personal preference .  I also left some chunks and didn't puree all of the soup.  Great topped with crumbled bacon!

target.recipe_text:
dandelion cookies

a drop cookie made with dandelion

1. cream together the shortening and sugars
2. when light and fluffy , add the vanilla and egg
3. beat well
4. mix in all the dry ingredients , including the dandelion petals
5. drop by spoonfuls or roll into balls about 1 / 2 inch round , and place on an ungreased cookie sheet
6. bake at 375 degrees f for about 7 minutes or until the edges are slightly brown
target.review:
Yum!
The hardest part was pulling all the dandelion petals from the flower, but my kids loved helping me do that.
This is a very nice "shortbready" cookie with a faint maple syrup taste: a bit hit in our Canadian house!  :P
We will be making these again soon... maybe a double batch!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy baked whitefish

this is a very easy, mild baked whitefish dish.  even my sons like it.

1. place whitefish in baking dish
2. spread mayonnaise over fish
3. sprinkle everything else over fish
4. bake at 500f for 17-20 minutes
5. serve , sprinkled with paprika for color
demonstrations.review: This was very good, and I don't like fish.  The sauce was of moderate strength (not too strong, not too weak) and the fish was tender.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesty chicken and pasta

zesty chicken and pasta from kraft canada

1. cook and stir chicken in 1 / 4 cup of the dressing in large skillet on medium-high heat 4 minute or until no longer pink
2. add broccoli , onion , red pepper and parsley
3. cook until tender , stirring occasionally
4. toss with pasta and remaining 1 / 4 cup dressing
5. sprinkle with cheese
demonstrations.review: Nice light supper pasta salad.  I'm looking forward to trying different dressings, veggies and cheeses.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chip sweet potato squares

from home cooking magazine (november-december 2004)

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray a 15x10x1 inch jelly roll pan with cooking spray
3. mash sweet potatoes with reserved syrup
4. in another bowl , whisk together flour , baking powder , allspice , cinnamon , cloves , and salt
5. beat together butter and sugars at medium speed for 2 minutes or until smooth and lightened in color
6. beat in eggs one at a time
7. on low speed , beat in half of the dry ingredients , followed by sweet potatoes , and finally the last of the dry ingredients
8. fold in chips and half of the pecans
9. spread batter evenly in pan
10. sprinkle remaining pecans over top
11. bake for 35-40 minutes or until lightly browned and the pecans are toasted
12. cool in pan on a wire rack before cutting into squares
demonstrations.review: Our first batch was gone before it cooled.  However, I did cook and mash my own yams, omitted the syrup, only put 1/2 cup of white and brown sugars, replaced the eggs, and skipped the pecans.  The chocolate chips (I like carob; the kids prefer semi-sweet) are a sweet addition: I didn't think I'd like them, but they are fun, and make this recipe out of the ordinary.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
okra stir fry

a fusion of the deep south and asia! i do not remember where i got it from but the taste works well (at least for me).
my japanese mom-in-law loves it!

1. marinate the chicken and peppers in the soy sauce , minced ginger , and balsamic vinegar
2. cut the heads and tails off the okra and cut into 1 / 4 inch rounds
3. dump them in a bowl and don't season them !
4. stir-fry the chicken until about 2 / 3 done , pull chicken out and set aside
5. add oil , then the okra
6. stir like crazy
7. your goal is little green things that look like they are trying to be a nice golden brown
8. if you cook the okra just right , it is great
9. under or over-cook it , it is great
10. throw the chicken back in and stir
11. add the peppers
12. toss in about a teaspoon of curry powder for fun
13. serve over rice or with mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: I couldn't find okra anywhere, but I used a packaged of frozen spinach instead.  It was great.  I forgot about putting potatoes or rice on, so boiled up some noodles quickly.  A fast, tasty meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry cream crowdie

crowdies are traditional scottish desserts, first served to celebrate the autumn harvest. naturally, they include whisky among their ingredients, but that can be omitted!  to keep your dessert course purely scottish, serve this raspberry cream crowdie with rich scottish shortbreads.  i am posting this recipe, from one adapted from an international masters '1001 recipes for pan or wok' recipe card, for the 2005 zaar world tour.  vary the berries to suit taste preferences.  crowdies may be largely prepared ahead, but are best assembled just before being served: that way the oats stay crisp.  the preparation and cooking times below do not include the several hours cooling time required after you have made the crowdies.

1. put the oatmeal or oats in a heavy-based , preferably non-stick , pan and cook over a low heat , stirring constantly until they are toasted and golden
2. allow to cool before use
3. meanwhile , pour the cream into a mixing bowl and whip until soft peaks form , then gradually whisk in the honey and whisky
4. set aside
5. after you have removed the stems , washed and carefully dry the raspberries , place a few raspberries in the base of 4 dessert glasses , top with a little cream mixture and sprinkle with some oatmeal or oats
6. continue layering the raspberries , cream and oatmeal , finishing with a layer of raspberries and oatmeal
7. chill until required
8. alternative: for slightly larger serves , with more of the creamy mixture , use 150ml of double cream and 150ml of yoghurt , mixed together , with honey and whisky then whisked into the blended cream / yogurt
9. the yogurt i always buy is a very creamy , slightly sweet greek yogurt which i get at a local delicatessen
10. when i make this recipe i intend using this instead of cream
demonstrations.review: Excellent - nice presentation and easy. I added more oats to mine, but that must be my Scottish roots showing!  I also tried to save time by using pre-made whipped cream with the honey and whiskey.  BAD IDEA.  It turned out gluey instead of fluffy, but the taste was still fantastic.  Thank-you so much for this recipe!

target.recipe_text:
chinese chicken noodle salad

if you love pasta salads that contain crisp veggies you'll love this. the dressing is really delicious. the flavors get better after 2 or 3 days in the fridge. i got this great recipe from a friend.

1. cook spaghetti in boiling water for 9 minutes
2. add sliced snow peas and cook for 1 more minute
3. drain and rinse under cold , running water
4. drain well
5. combine pasta mixture , chicken , green onions and bell pepper in a very large mixing bowl
6. set aside
7. in a separate bowl combine teriyaki sauce , sesame seeds , sesame oil
8. also salt , pepper and chili oil
9. pour over pasta mixture and toss well
10. serve at room temperature or chilled
11. keeps well in the fridge for up to a week
target.review: This was really good! As always, I couldn't leave well enough alone and changed things up a bit. I left out the sesame seeds because I didn't have any. Also, my bottled teriyaki sauce was too bitter for me (I used Kikkoman) so added about a tablespoon of honey, a good drizzle of soy sauce and a wee bit of sambal for heat. It's a good recipes for summer when I don't want to heat up the kitchen much. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef rouladen

this recipe, from the dec/jan 1996 issue of taste of home has been a family favorite since the first time i made it. it does require a little effort, but it's worth every minute. i make this on a regular basis, as well as when we have company over. i always serve homemade dinner rolls with it but traditionally it may have been served with potato dumplings. i usually will slice my 8 meat slices in half, lengthwise, to create 16 smaller slices, which are easier to handle.  *note:  most recipes include a dill pickle slice in each roll, and after trying it with pickles my family loves this recipe even more!  i've added the pickle as an optional ingredient.  :)

1. spread mustard on one side of each slice of meat
2. sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. place one strip of bacon , dill pickle slice , and a few onion wedges on each slice of meat
4. roll up and secure with wooden toothpicks
5. put oil in dutch oven or other large pan and brown meat
6. drain
7. add broth and bring to a boil
8. reduce heat and cover and simmer for 1-1 / 2 hours or until meat is tender
9. remove meat and keep warm
10. combine flour and water until smooth and slowly stir into broth
11. bring to a boil , stirring constantly until thickened
12. remove wooden pics from meat and return to gravy
13. heat through
14. sprinkle with parsley if desired
demonstrations.review: This recipe is almost just like my dad used to make. The gravy is ridiculously good, you must serve with mashed potatoes to soak it all up!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sour cream and ground beef layered casserole

this is a great casserole that i have been making for years, it's one of my family's favorite dishes. feel free to adjust all ingredient amounts to suit taste. i usually season the ground beef/onion mixture with seasoned salt and add in some cayenne pepper for heat but that is optional.

1. set oven to 350f
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. in a large skillet , cook the ground beef with onion , garlic and chili flakes over medium heat until meat is browned and no longer pink
4. drain fat then stir in the parmesan cheese
5. add tomato sauce and sugar
6. bring mixture to a boil
7. cover , reduce heat and simmer for about 30 minutes stirring occasionally
8. transfer meat mixture to a greased baking dish
9. set aside
10. in a bowl beat cream cheese and sour cream at low speed until smooth
11. add in green onions then stir to combine
12. spread the cream cheese mixture over the ground beef in the dish
13. top with cooked noodles , then sprinkle the shredded cheddar cheese over the noodles
14. sprinkle with paprika
15. bake for 25-30 minutes or until hot and bubbly
demonstrations.review: This worked out pretty well. I used Fat free sour cream and cream cheese and reduced fat Colby cheese on top. I also used macaroni noodle and built it upside down so the noodles were on bottom, I'm not a fan of crunchy noodles. Finally, I made the whole casserole the night before so I could just pop it in the oven when I got home from work. I usually have most of this stuff on hand so I'm sure I'll make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coca cola pork roast

there are lots of cola/meat recipes on this site, this one is a little different. i found this in a crockpot cookbook that my folks gave me for christmas. i tweaked it a bit, but still--great stuff!

1. rub the roast with salt and pepper then place it in the crockpot
2. add soup mix and coke
3. cook on low 8 hours or high for 4
4. before serving dump liquid from crockpot into a pot
5. skim fat
6. to the remaining juices add salt and pepper to taste and a dash of kitchen bouquet
7. bring mixture to a boil
8. remove a cup of the liquid and add corn starch to thicken
9. add corn starch mixture to the rest of the juices
10. cook until it reaches desired consistency
11. wonderful gravy !
demonstrations.review: I made this with a beef roast, it came really tender and fell apart. I was not a fan of the gravy, and I made sure to use classic coke as recommended. I didn't even bother saving the leftovers because I couldn't get over that gravy taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese pot stickers

these pot stickers are 100% better than any you can buy and well worth the extra effort. i like to make them and then freeze them so all you have to do is the final steps just before you serve them. i make them every christmas to have as a quick appetizer. one review commented that she had trouble with them sticking together when she defrosted them -  i have not had this happen however to be sure it doesn't happen to you defrost them separated.  i have also fried them directly from the freezer. they only take a few seconds more to cook.

1. sprinkle salt over the shredded cabbage and let stand for 5 minutes , then squeeze out liquid
2. squeeze out any liquid from the shrimp
3. mix cabbage , shrimp , pork , soy , wine , onion , oil , ginger and garlic
4. on each wrapper place about 2 tsp of the mix and seal the edges , use a bit of water on the edge , try to press out all the air and ensure they are tightly sealed
5. in 2 large skillets heat 1 tbsp oil , fry 16 dumplings for 1 minute or until golden on one side add 1 / 4 cup of stock into the pan , reduce heat to low , cover and cook , without turning for about 7 minutes or until the dumpling is translucent and most of the liquid has evaporated uncover and on higher heat cook for another 5-7 minutes or until the bottoms are dark brown , drain put on a platter and keep warm
6. repeat for the remaining 32 dumplings
7. mix the dipping sauce and serve with warm or hot dumplings
demonstrations.review: I made these exactly as directed except I left out the shrimp. I also froze them which worked out nicely. I didn't think they were as good as everyone else said. They seemed to be a little lacking in flavor, tasted like porks in a won ton. Is there something I'm missing?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian peasant soup

i found this in toh quick cooking magazine. i haven't tried it yet but it looks like something my family and i would love. plan on trying it soon.

1. in a large pot , cook sausage over medium heat until browned and no longer pink
2. drain
3. add onions and garlic
4. saute until tender
5. add chicken
6. saute and stir until no longer pink
7. add in the beans , broth , tomatoes , basil , and oregano
8. stir to mix
9. cook uncovered , for 10 minutes
10. add the spinach and heat just until wilted
11. serve with parmesan cheese sprinkled on top
demonstrations.review: This was really nummy! I totally forgot to thaw my chicken, so by the time I went to make it is was too late. I added some macaroni to the soup to beef it up in place of the chicken. still good!

target.recipe_text:
french pastry cream

pastry cream is a light, rich custard filling for any cake, fruit tart, puff or dessert crepe. lovely poured over fresh fruit cup. quick and easy to make.

1. in a medium saucepan , heat 2 cups milk to boiling
2. while milk is heating , whisk egg yolks , sugar and remaining 1 / 4 cup milk
3. whisk in cornstarch and flour until smooth
4. temper the egg mixture by slowly whisking in about 1 / 3 of the heated milk , then whisking in the remaining milk
5. return mixture to saucepan and cook over medium-high heat until mixture thickens and boils
6. whisk constantly
7. reduce heat to low and cook for another 2 minutes
8. remove from heat and stir in vanilla or other flavorings
9. pour into a bowl , press plastic wrap on the surface to prevent a skin from forming and cool to room temperature before chilling for at least 2 hours
target.review: It's a bit thinker than I wanted but adding more milk solved the problem.  I'll try leaving out the flour next time

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kristi s chicken noodle casserole

i started with kittencal's chicken noodle soup, next thing i knew, i had a casserole!

1. put first 6 ingredients in to a pot with a large opening
2. boil until liquid is reduced by roughly 1 / 4
3. add chicken and mushrooms , simmer for 45 minutes , or until chicken is done
4. preheat oven to 350f
5. assemble casserole in a shallow dish
6. dry rice to line the bottom , then uncooked veggies , then cooled broth with chicken and mushrooms
7. cook , uncovered , in oven for approx 1 hr , or until rice is fluffy and most liquid has boiled off
demonstrations.review: Boring!  Way too much rice, dry chicken and no flavour. Sorry but this is just my opinion.  Glad other enjoyed it though :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot cranberry port pork roast

this elegant dish is a family favorite

1. put the roast in slow cooker
2. mix in a bowl , cranberry sauce , port , and sugar
3. stir in lemon , raisins , garlic , ginger , mustard , salt , and pepper
4. pour over roast cover and cook on low 6-7 hours or until meat is 170f
5. remove roast and keep warm measure 3 cups of cooking juices and pour into saucepan
6. bring to a boil
7. in a cup dissolve cornstarch in cold water
8. stir into saucepan
9. cook , stirring until thickened
10. slice roast and serve over rice with sauce on top
demonstrations.review: This is DELICIOUS-a 5 star recipe!  I was a bit worried about the added sugar, but it's fine as is.  I might try it again without the added sugar.  Regardless, I will be making this again - we all loved it with mashed potatoes and carrots on the side. Thanks Tish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brussels sprout salad with walnuts

thinly sliced brussels sprouts make a delicate coleslaw texture, enhanced by a classic vinaigrette.

1. slice brussels sprouts across in 2 mm strips , using a food processor or slicer
2. discard cores
3. chop walnuts into 1 cm chunks
4. grate cheese
5. toss cheese with sprouts and nuts
6. whisk together mustard , oil , vinegar , salt and pepper , until blended
7. pour over salad , toss lightly , and serve
demonstrations.review: This is keeper!  I didn't remove the cores but instead of slicing them just once, I sliced them twice - kind of like julienning. The mix of flavours is perfect just the way it is.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ruth s chris sweet potato casserole

this is absolutely divine! ruth has done it again! note, the first time i made this i noticed there was a bit of extra liquid left over, next time i will adjust the amount of butter and/or add a bit more potato.

1. combine brown sugar , flour , nuts and butter in mixing bowl
2. set aside
3. preheat oven to 350 degrees
4. combine sweet potatoes , sugar , salt , vanilla , eggs and butter in a mixing bowl in the order listed
5. mix thoroughly
6. pour mixture into buttered baking dish
7. sprinkle the surface of the sweet potato mixture evenly with the crust mixture
8. bake for 30 minutes
9. allow to set at least 30 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was a good first try at Ruth's Chris sweet potatoe casserole.  Next time I'll leave out the vanilla and most of the sugar.  I baked it with the topping and it was fine.  Maybe a few mintues under the broiler would crisp it up a bit.  I wonder what it would be like with orange zest?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kelly s creamy cheddar pea salad

i'm not a big fan of peas, but like them in things. this salad is one of my favorites. happy to share!

1. in large bowl , combine mayo , relish , sugar , seas
2. salt and mustard
3. gently fold in rest of ingredients adding peas last so they don't get broken up and mushy
4. chill
5. if you like it extra creamy , double the sauce
demonstrations.review:
My son (14years) made this for his contribution to our Easter dinner.  He left out the sweet pickle relish because none of us like it and I wasn't about to buy some or visit a fast food joint to get some packets. He used dijon mustard because that's what we have in the house. Everyone except my son loved it.  I might reduce the amount of sauce a bit next time though or maybe make it with half mayo and half yogurt or sour cream.  It would make a nice Christmassy dish with a bit of red pepper diced up in it!
FYI - TRIED THE SOUR CREAM IDEA AND IT ISN'T AS GOOD AS JUST MAYO.

target.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot pork chops

i make this for my husband and daughter, and i have got nothing but smiles from this.  it's easy, cheap and oh so yummy!

1. combine cream of mushroom soup , 1 / 3 can water , softened cream cheese and garlic in a bowl
2. stir out most of the lumps , but the rest will cook out
3. pour in bottom of crock pot
4. put pork chops on top of mixture
5. add liberal amounts of salt and pepper
6. i'm usually heavy handed !
7. cook on low for 7-8 hours
8. serve over slices of warm bread or pasta of your choice
9. pork chops will fall apart
10. so tender you can cut with a spoon !
target.review: Made this tonight and it got a thumbs up from DD. I used Campbells Cream of Mushroom with Roasted Garlic Soup and added some diced onion as well. The gravy was actually a bit too thick so I added nearly a cup of milk at the very end to loosen it up a bit. Turned out perfect. Served it over mashed potatoes and just broke the pork chops up in the gravy. Next time, I will cut back to about 2/3 a block of cream cheese and add sliced mushrooms as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
monte cristo casserole

one of my sons could not get past the monte cristo sandwich at the blue bayou restaurant in disneyland. i made this casserole for him and he loved it. i hope you do to.

1. preheat oven to 375^f
2. pour milk in a microwaveable container and heat until hot
3. whisk eggs in small bowl and add hot milk to eggs , blend
4. cut french toast into 3 / 4 inch cubes
5. place in a large bowl
6. pour egg mixture over bread cubes , toss gently , set aside
7. combine ham , turkey , cheese and parsley in a bowl
8. spray a 13x9x2 inch baking pan with cooking spray
9. layer half the french toast cubes with half the meat mixture in bottom of pan
10. repeat
11. let stand for at least 10 minutes set at room temperature for a few minutes before baking-or bake a little longer if it's cold
12. bake 30-35 minutes until golden brown and set in center
13. cool 10 minutes
14. sprinkle with powdered sugar
15. slice strawberries
16. combine strawberries with strawberry ice cream topping in a small bowl
17. cut casserole into squares
18. serve topped with strawberry mixture
demonstrations.review: This is a good recipe. I enjoyed it.  I was hoping it would be a hit with my 5yr old daughter, but she didn't like it.  Truthfully, although the flavors are there...it can't compare to a real monte cristo sandwich.  A good substitute for those of us that don't have a Bennigans nearby. :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
striking strawberry cake

strawberries plus strawberry gelatin added to the mix packs this cake with tons of strawberry flavor. the cool-whip and strawberry frosting just adds to the delight!! very easy to make, and nice to take to picnics and potlucks. i have never made this as a layer cake, but i imagine that you may have to use a bit more cool-whip to frost the entire outside of the cake.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. beat together all cake ingredients and pour into greased and floured 9x13-inch cake pan
3. bake for 35 minutes , or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
4. make frosting by folding strawberries into cool-whip
5. spread frosting over cooled cake , and refrigerate until serving
demonstrations.review: This is my FAVORITE strawberry cake recipe! So moist and perfect for the warmer weather when you want something not as rich. Thought I'd lost mine and just knew I'd find it here. I always use the 9x13 pan, so I can't answer Prairie's question. I do use a different frosting though: Mix 1cup milk with 1 vanilla pudding mix til smooth then fold into 1 tub cool whip. Spread this over the cake and then garnish with Fresh sliced strawberries if desired.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mock chicken fried steak with milk gravy

my mother made these for us four girls. money was tight and she couldn't afford steak very often. these use ground beef. i use a 80/20 lean to fat. you can use ground round but it tends to be a little too dry. this is great with mashed potatoes. everyone i have ever made it for loved it. the first time my dh had it he never knew it was ground beef. he just commented on the tenderness of the steak!

1. mix 2 cups flour with salt and pepper
2. shape ground beef into four thin patties
3. dip patties into flour , then beaten egg , then flour again
4. put shortening , oil or lard into a heavy skillet over medium high heat
5. when a little flour sprinkled into skillet begins to sizzle , add patties
6. cook for about 5 minutes per side
7. remove and drain on paper towels
8. to make gravy:
9. remove all but four tablespoons of fat from skillet
10. stir in 4 tablespoons of dredging flour and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt
11. stir , scraping up browned bits , for about one minute till light brown
12. whisk in milk gradually
13. whisk until thick and bubbly
14. remove from heat
15. add 1 / 2 teaspoon black pepper or to taste
16. stir well
demonstrations.review: This was SO easy and very tasty! I loved how tender it was compared to using cube steak. The gravy was delicious. I seasoned my meat with some Montreal Steak Seasoning before making the patties and otherwise followed the recipe exactly. My DD is picky and she raved "Oh Mom, this is SOOOO good!" Anything that pleases her pleases me.. 5 stars! :D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: YUM! Made these this afternoon & just finished cutting them into bars. Recipe is SO easy. I only had chunky peanut butter, so made the mixture in my food processor to smooth out the peanuts. I followed other recommendations, and lined my pan with parchment paper. The whole thing lifted out perfectly, and made it easy to cut...plus, no dirty pan to clean. :-) I cut my bars in approx. 3/4" squares. 1 or 2 go a long way. Tastes just like a Resee's.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
avocado mandarin salad

toh; goes well with tex-mex menu.

1. in a bowl , combine oranges , onions , pecans , and pepper
2. refrigerate for 30 minutes
3. when ready to serve , place the greens in a salad bowl
4. top with orange mixture and avocado slices
5. drizzle with dressing
6. toss and serve
demonstrations.review: WOW!  Great combo of flavors that I wouldn't have ever thought of.  I LOVE the richness of the avocado, the sweetness of the mandarin oranges and the kick from the italian dressing.  First time, I made it as written...excellent!  Second time (the next night, lol) I added mediterranean (provolone, parmesan & feta) cheese crumbles.  Loved it both ways & will make it all summer.

target.recipe_text:
how i got my family to eat spinach  spinach casserole

if spinach scares you, this is one recipe that contains spinach that you do not have to be afraid of! it is so delicious that even my picky kids like it. my mother-in-law makes this for get-togethers and she passed the recipe on to me. you can also use broccoli instead of the spinach, which she does often, but i have never tried...it is great the way it is! she also eats this hot or cold, but i only like it hot :) enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. place spinach in strainer and squeeze all extra liquid from it
3. in a large bowl , combine spinach with the rest of ingredients , except croutons , and combine well
4. pour into a 2 quart casserole dish and top with croutons
5. bake for 35 to 40 minutes , or until bubbling around edges
target.review: It was a great recipe.  I needed a fast side dish to go with beer can chicken and roasted potatoes and I had all the ingredients on hand.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey garlic meatloaf

i just whipped this together one night with ingredients i happened to have on hand.  it turned out pretty good.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease an 8x10 glass baking dish
3. set aside
4. in a bowl , combine all ingredients then transfer to bakind dish
5. top with desired amount of ketchup
6. bake at 350 for 1
7. 25 hours
8. let stand for 3-5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: The meatloaf turned out great. My husband loves meatloaf and this recipe had the differnet twist with the honey and the garlic. I served it with scalloped potatoes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baklava salmon  salmon with honey  butter  walnuts  and mustard

one of my friends deemed this "baklava salmon" and the name stuck. the salmon & mustard go well with the honey, butter, and walnuts. we usually serve this with rice and steamed carrots or broccoli.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. line shallow roasting pan with non-stick aluminum foil , or spray with non-stick pan spray
3. in small bowl , blend butter , mustard , and honey , set aside
4. in another bowl , mix together bread crumbs , nuts , and parsley
5. place salmon fillets on prepared pan , sprinkle with salt and pepper , and brush with honey-mustard mixture
6. sprinkle tops with crumb / nut mixture
7. if any remains , press into sides of salmon
8. bake salmon 12-15 minutes in preheated oven , or until it flakes easily with a fork
9. serve with lime or lemon wedge
demonstrations.review: I made this a while back but have not had a chance to rate it until now. It had great flavor and the salmon stayed nice and moist.  Was really easy and fast to prepare.  Will make it agian for guests.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sea scallop and cod pie topped with mashed potatoes

a wonderful comforting irish dish. this is good for those of you that are fasting not eating red meat during lent. try it with shrimp in place of scallops.i made this again using bay scallops because that's all the store had and i enjoy the sea scallops so much more.

1. clean the scallops and cut in half , leave fish whole then simmer in the milk for 15 minutes
2. strain , reduce the liquid cooking for 5 more minutes
3. heat 2 tablespoon of the butter and stir in the flour , cook for about a minute , stirring , then add the milk gradually , stirring all the time to avoid lumps
4. season with salt and white pepper , add the sliced mushrooms and simmer for about 10 minutes longer
5. then add the sherry and finally the scallops and fish
6. when hot , transfer to an oiled 2 quart ovenproof dish and cover with mashed potatoes , making sure they cover the fish right to the edges
7. dot with the remaining butter sprinkle with paprika and bake in a moderate oven , 350f , for 20-30 minutes , or until the top is turning brown
8. 04 / 29 / 04- i made this again adding 2 sliced scallions and 1 / 4 cup green peas to the fish just before topping with potatoes
9. and used vermouth because i ran out of sherry
10. 3 ? 18 / 11 i made it this yer topped with recipe #367251
11. i also did add scallions and green peas
demonstrations.review: This recipe was very good.  I made a few changes by using Basa fish and shrimp.  It's great for the cold days of winter.  I will make this again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red lobster cheddar bay biscuits

don't you just love the copycat recipes? here's another one, and if you like red lobster's biscuits, this is the recipe for you. they may not be the exact biscuits, but you will not notice a difference in the taste.

1. heat oven to 450
2. combine baking mix , water and grated cheese in a bowl
3. roll out on a lightly floured surface , until 1 inch thick
4. cut biscuits , and place on an ungreased pan
5. melt butter and spices together
6. brush the biscuits with the butter and bake for 8 to 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Graet recipe easy to prepare.  I did not have bisquick on hand.  But if you click on the ingredient bisquick baking mix and it give you a substuition mix you can make at home.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gerry s meatloaf with dill pickle sauce

yet another of dad's recipes. this is a slightly different meatloaf, than what most people are familiar with.  excellent served with rice, potatoes or broad pasta & fresh peas.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. lightly mix meats with onions , bread crumbs , pickles , egg , salt and pepper until well blended
3. shape into a loaf and place in shallow pan
4. combine pickle juice , chili sauce or ketchup , water , sugar and worcestershire sauce
5. pour over meatloaf and place in 350f oven basting twice with sauce in pan for 40 minutes
6. continue baking without basting for additional 30 - 35 minutes , until meatloaf is really glazed
7. garnish with a pickle fan
8. dad always served this with brussels sprouts and tiny whole carrots
demonstrations.review: This recipe was a hit.  It was quick and easy to prepare and has lots of flavour.

target.recipe_text:
roasted lemon and garlic potatoes

i just love roasted potatoes, and this takes it to a new level, using lemon juice! this is an easy recipe! adapted from southern recipes.

1. spray an 9x13-inch baking pan with cooking spray , or coat bottom of dish with oil
2. preheat oven to 425f
3. combine potatoes with remaining ingredients in a bowl
4. toss to coat completely
5. let coated potatoes stand 10 minutes
6. spoon potato mixture into prepared baking pan in a single layer
7. bake for 35-40 minutes or until tender and lightly browned , stirring occasionally
8. i cook a little longer , because i like mine brown and crispy !
target.review: This recipe appealed to me because of the lemon (my son loves "lemony" potatoes).  Very simple and easy, will make again with a few herbs and pepper.  Made and reviewed for Dec. '08 NZ/AUS recipe swap.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ravioli in a dish

this is so good and so easy.  i always have stuff on hand to make this recipe.  it comes together so quickly for a weeknight meal.  i have served this to guests before and they thought i went to a lot of trouble because it was so good!  :)

1. boil the ravioli according to package directions
2. drain ravioli and pour back into the pot you cooked them inches
3. gently stir the alfredo sauce into the ravioli
4. pour the ravioli into ungreased 7x11 inch casserole dish
5. pour the spaghetti sauce on top of the ravioli and spread around the top with a spoon
6. top the casserole with the parmesan cheese and bake in 375f oven for 10-15 minutes until hot and bubbly and the cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: Family loved it, I love how easy it was!  Served this with a caesar salad and warm bread.  I did however use my own pasta sauce that is a family favorite.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandpa parker s french onion soup

another recipe from the 1980 version of the grace evangelical congregational church cookbook from muir, pennsylvania that was given to me by my nana when i became an adult.  this was submitted to the cookbook by my late grandfather - william parker.

1. heat butter and then add onion and simmer for 10 minutes
2. add bouillon and bring to boil and then simmer for 20 minutes
3. season to your taste with salt , pepper and worcestershire sauce
4. pour the hot soup into earthenware cups
5. on top of each , float a slice of sauteed french bread and sprinkle with grated cheese
demonstrations.review: DH loved it as well as I.  Kids not so much as they are not onion fans (I will not let that effect my rating).  I used both sweet and cooking onions.  I will need to double recipe next time.  (Made and reviewed for NZ/AUZ recipe Swap #21, Oct.2008)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moo shu vegetables

a great low-calorie vegetarian meal you can make in a flash at home!  this recipes uses pre-shredded veggies so it comes together quickly.  recipe from eating well.  they suggest serving with warm whole-wheat tortillas, asian hot sauce and extra hoisin if desired.

1. heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat
2. add eggs
3. cook , stirring gently , until set , 2 to 3 minutes
4. remove to a plate
5. wipe out the pan and heat the remaining 2 teaspoons oil over medium heat
6. add ginger and garlic and cook , stirring , until softened and fragrant , 1 minute
7. add shredded vegetables , bean sprouts , half the sliced scallions , soy sauce and vinegar
8. stir to combine
9. cover and cook , stirring once or twice , until the vegetables are just tender , about 3 minutes
10. add the reserved eggs and hoisin
11. cook , uncovered , stirring and breaking up the scrambled eggs , until heated through , 1 to 2 minutes
12. stir in the remaining scallions and remove from the heat
demonstrations.review: This was put together very quickly as you said. Quite a tasty light meal that is great on the fly. I didn't add the extra hoisin but added some julienned carrots and fresh pea pods.  Thank you January Bride. {Made and reviewed for Aus/NZ Recipe Swap #38, March 2010}.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my own coleslaw dressing

when made with slaw this is a great recipe to use with pulled pork barbeque. i have been making cole slaw this way for years. the slaw is simple to prepare using your food processor to shred the cabbage and carrot. i hope you enjoy it!

1. combine mayonnaise , lemon juice , celery seed , sugar and salt and pepper
2. for cole slaw , toss dressing with shredded cabbage and carrot
3. chill
demonstrations.review: Will make a again,  thanks Bev!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun crab spread  using imitation crab

this is one of my favorite snacks.  it can be served with crackers, or i like to eat it with the big corn chips (scoops) or serve it in jumbo pasta shells.  it's easily doubled if you want to use a whole brick of cream cheese and a pound of imitation crabmeat. this is fairly chunky; if you want it to be more spreadable, increase the amount of cream cheese/mayonnaise.  cook time is chill time.

1. in a small mixing bowl , beat cream cheese , mayonnaise , paprika , black pepper , garlic powder and ground red pepper with an electric mixer on medium speed till well combined
2. stir in the imitation crab , chopped tomato and green onions
3. cover and chill for 3-24 hours
demonstrations.review: Mailbelle, this was a tasty, quick cracker dipper that everyone enjoyed.  With the exception of using fresh chopped garlic instead of ground powder I made as written.  This was great.

target.recipe_text:
salisbury steak with mushroom and onion gravy

i combined the salisbury steak from one recipe and the gravy from another and made this hearty, filling, easy meal. mashed potatoes make a great accompaniment, i suggest making extra gravy for the potatoes.

1. combine ground beef , chopped onions , cracker crumbs , egg , horseradish , salt and pepper
2. shape into patties
3. heat 2 tablespoons butter in skillet
4. cook patties till no longer pink inside - approx 8 minutes each side
5. in separate pan , melt 3 tablespoons butter
6. saut onion rings and mushrooms til tender
7. remove patties from pan
8. stir flour into pan , scraping bottom of pan
9. add dash of salt and pepper
10. cook 2 minutes
11. stir in cream to form a thick paste
12. slowly stir in chicken broth - stir till thick
13. add a few dashes of worcestershire sauce and hot sauce
14. stir till mixed well
15. simmer 5 minutes add mushrooms , onions and patties
16. heat 10 minutes
target.review: After perusing what seemed like hundreds of recipes for salisbury steak this is what I settled on... am I glad I did!  This was a fantastic recipe and well received by the whole family.  Using what I had in the pantry and two pounds of ground beef, I mixed the meat w/ the egg and bread crumbs (doubled) and 1 envelope onion soup mix until well blended.  The gravy was fantastic!  We subbed beef broth as that was available and used whole milk with fantastic results.  If you want the gravy to have the classic deep brown color, use some browning sauce, or it'll have that classic milk gravy look.  Thank you so much for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy lemonade jello

i believe this recipe came from the taste of home magazine a few years ago. i have made this for many occasions and everyone raves over it. very easy to prepare and make aheads are always great!

1. dissolve jello in boiling water , then stir in lemonade concentrate until dissolved
2. chill until partially set
3. fold in whipped topping
4. pour into a 13 x 9 glass dish
5. chill until firm
demonstrations.review: Oh this is so devine!  I took the advice of another poster and used orange jello and juice~~ it tastes just like a push up (but doesn't melt!).  Folding the whipping cream in... well not so much for me!  It just wouldn't mix that way so I used a whisk and gently worked it in.  I used a 10x15 glass pan to have nice size squares and garnished them with sliced oranges and cherries, very pretty without the guilt!  Thanks for helping me make my party goodies super easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
calico beans   baked beans w  3 kinds of beans

this is one of my favorite cookout side dishs! my aunt char makes these all the time and i finaly got the recipe from her! they are a great side dish with hamburgers, hotdogs, potato salad...the list goes on and they are yummy!

1. fry bacon until crisp
2. drain
3. fry ground beef in fat until tender
4. combine onion , ketchup , salt , mustard , vinegar , brown sugar , and partly drain beans in a 3 quart oven container
5. mix well
6. add hamburger and crumbled bacon
7. bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wicked good beans!  Personal preferences took over the recipe in a few ways (don't they always?)!  I cut the sugar to 1/2 cup and still find them sweet.  I used about 3/4lb. of ground beef, subbed black beans for kidney beans because I don't like the latter and added another can of white beans to stretch out the batch.  Used the slow cooker and made them a day ahead of time since many reviewers of this and other recipes said they're better the next day.  They're soooo good now it's hard to imagine them better!  Thanks Jen!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
light blueberry sauce

a tasty blueberry sauce. low in sugar, so less calories than most recipes. good served over pancakes, ice cream or dessert. this is a small recipe, so you may want to double it.

1. combine all ingredients in a small saucepan
2. heat over medium heat , stirring , until thick
3. serve over pancakes , ice cream , cake or other dessert
demonstrations.review: I can't believe I've used this so many times and have neglected to review it!  This sauce is marvelous!  I usually leave out the sugar, or use stevia to taste making this a very low calorie sauce (the whole batch is 1.5 ww points, which is just wonderful!)  There's no compromise on flavor, in fact it's tastier than overly sweet sauces and the blueberry flavor just shines!  Thank you so much for sharing it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake rice krispies peanut butter granola bars  lower fat

this is a delicious lower fat bar if using reduced-fat peanut butter, these are perfect for kid's lunch boxes, feel free to add in some chopped nuts or sunflower seeds or coconut in place of the raisins,

1. lightly grease 11 x 7-inch , can use a 13 x 9-inch baking dish but you will have a thinner bar
2. in a large bowl combine rice krispies cereal , oats and raisins
3. in a saucepan stir the corn syrup or honey and brown sugar until just at a boil
4. immediately remove from heat and stir in the peanut butter and vanilla until well combined
5. pour over the dry ingredients in the bowl
6. mix to combine
7. mix in mini chocolate chips work fast the mixture hardens quickly
8. transfer the mixture into prepared baking dish , then using slightly wet hands push evenly down into the pan
9. while the mixture is still soft , for easier slicing take a sharp knife and slice into desired size bars
10. chill until firm
demonstrations.review:
These are the bomb!  I couldn't resist a little tweaking to suit our tastes ;).  We abhor rasins, so I used coconut there and added 1t. cinnamon to the dry ing.  Not fond of p'nut butter so I used almond butter instead (yum!).  I left out the choc. chips for a mixture of seeds and nuts.  Do mix the dry ingredients very well before adding the syrup mixture.  Also, press into the pan very firmly, compacting the mixture.  
I used a loaf pan sprayed with pam.  Once they were "set up" I sliced them fairly thinly with my electric knife (but a serrated knife would work fine).  This way they resembled the store bought ones my daughter goes ga ga over.
Then, I thought hmmm, wonder if you could make them crispy... so I sprayed the cookie sheet with pam and baked up the slices at 300 for 10 min. on each side -careful turning them.  Now I'm the granola bar goddess! 
Thank you a million times over Koechin!  I can hardly wait to fiddle with these again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pear and pecan pancakes with pear and ginger sauce

this recipe is from the september 7, 2005 edition of the food section of the chicago sun-times. enjoy!

1. to make sauce:
2. stir cornstarch with 2 tablespoons water in a cup
3. pour into a small , heavy-bottomed saucepan
4. stir in pear , crystallized ginger , cinnamon , sugar , and salt
5. cover and simmer for five minutes or until pear is tender and pulpy
6. remove from heat
7. stir in lemon juice
8. set sauce aside
9. to make pancakes:
10. stir together milk , melted butter , and egg in a small bowl
11. stir together flour , baking powder , sugar , and salt in a larger bowl
12. pour in milk mixture
13. mix just to combine ingredients
14. don't beat
15. stir in pear and pecans
16. coat a griddle or large heavy-bottomed skillet with oil
17. heat over medium heat for thirty seconds
18. add batter by 1 / 4 cup measure
19. cook pancakes until bubbles form on surface and edges are browned
20. flip over and cook second side until golden brown
21. drizzle ginger and pear sauce over pancakes and serve warm
22. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious and perfect for two!  I used whole wheat flour and left out the pecans (didn't have).  For the sauce, I added 1/4 cup water as my pear didn't really cook out a lot of juice so the "sauce" wasn't really saucy until water was added.  The flavor of these pancakes and accompanying sauce was just delicious, thank you hannah for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
hot quinoa breakfast with fruits

quinoa makes a great gluten free hot breakfast /porridge. 5 to 10 minutes and it is ready.

1. rinse the quinoa in water using a strainer , as you would was rice
2. add the quinoa to the water in a medium sized saucepan
3. bring to the boil , reduce heat and gentley simmer for 5 minutes
4. add the apples , raisins and cinnamon
5. simmer until the water has absorbed
6. serve with milk of your choice and sweeten with honey / rice syrup if desired
target.review: We made this for breakfast after our weekend run.  I had a cup of cooked quinoa left over from earlier in the week, so I cooked up 1/3c oats in 2/3 c water with half a chopped apple for each of us, then added 1/2 cup cooked quinoa.  Spiced it up with some cinnamon, honey, dried chopped figs and fresh blueberries, plus a splash of milk.  Will do this more often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my mother s version  weight watcher s 0 points vegetable soup

back in 1993 my dm and i became lifetime members of ww. she revised the 0 point soup recipe. she won 1st place with it at her office "soup cookoff" one year. i just dug it out because now i need it again. zaar is not kind to your waist line. i also have revised her revision. it called for a can of cajun stewed tomatoes which i can no longer locate. i now use 1 tsp cajun spice but food.com won't accept it. also changed a few other items to my liking.

1. spray large saucepan with cooking spray
2. saute' onion , carrots and celery until tender , approximately 5 minutes
3. combine beef broth , tomatoes , cabbage , bouillon cubes , garlic , cajun spice , and basil in the saucepan
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce heat
6. simmer approximately 30 minutes
7. add zucchini , continue simmering for another 10 minutes
8. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Tasty, filling soup!  It was also a great way to use up the veggies in my fridge and freezer at the end of the week.  Besides the listed veggies, I added some red bell pepper to the saute, and later some frozen oriental and california mix veggies, shelled edamame and spinach.  Instead of beef broth/bullion, I used 3/4 of a carton chicken broth, 2 cups of water and about 2 Tbs tomato paste.  Finally, I spiced it all up with some Tabasco sauce.  Delish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy african peanut soup

we served this on christmas eve to friends and family and it was a universal hit! very filling and its orange colour looks beautiful in a bowl.

1. heat the oil in a large saucepan over high heat
2. add pepper , ginger , carrots , garlic , onions and cayenne or chilies
3. cook for 2 minutes , then add potato and stock
4. bring to the boil and simmer 10 minutes
5. transfer the vegetables to a food processor and pure until smooth
6. return the pure to the saucepan and stir in peanut butter and tomato juice or mash the vegetables in the saucepan until slightly lumpy
7. add sugar , salt and pepper
8. serve sprinkled with green onions
demonstrations.review: My grandmother gave me a very similar version of this delicious recipe.  I used peanut oil to sautee the veggies, omitted the sugar, and added a teaspoon of ground cloves.
