I also used 4 cups of veg broth since that's what my recipe called for, but next time I'll try it with the tomato juice.  This is an outstanding dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steamed artichokes with garlicky dipping sauce

i grew up eating artichokes dipped in a garlic butter, which is delicious, but i wanted something i wouldn't feel so guilty about eating.  so, i came up with this recipe as a test, and it was really good.  i use non-fat greek yogurt, it is a little thicker, but you could use regular non-fat/low-fat yogurt, or even sour cream.  i make things for 2, so if you want more, just make twice as much dipping sauce.

1. trim bottom stalk of artichokes , leaving about 1 inch
2. cut off the first couple of inches of the top of the artichoke
3. if your artichoke is dangerously spikey , or you are serving these to kids / company , you may want to trim the
4. rinse the artichokes well , under running water
5. put about 2 inches of water in the bottom of a big pot , and place the artichokes top down
6. throw in the bay leaf and crushed garlic clove
7. cover and bring to a boil , then lower heat so the liquid is just simmering
8. steam like this for about 30-45 minutes
9. make the dip by putting the minced garlic , margarine , and lemon juice in a microwave safe bowl and heating for 30 seconds
10. add the dill , yogurt , and salt & pepper
11. if you want your sauce thick like this , then you are done
12. i like my dip a little runnier , so i add a little milk until it is the consistancy that i want
13. either way , cover and put in the fridge until the artichokes are ready
14. let artichokes cool off for about 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I bought some artichokes on sale and wanted to try something simple and light--this was perfect!  Loved the yogurt sauce as well, although I think I'll add more cayenne pepper next time, for a bigger zip.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lebanese meatloaf

"my father is lebanese. i remember the flat bread that his sister made, and grape leaves, and kibbeh—the foods we ate when we gathered as a family. kibbeh was sort of a steak tartare. my dad ate it raw; no one else would. we flattened it in a pan and baked it like meat loaf," says fiber artist dana boussard of arlee, montana. i got this recipe off a middle eastern food site.  it sounds so good and has  4 star rating.  i thought others might like it too.  i am posting this dish for world tour 2-middle eastern

1. place bulgur in a fine strainer and rinse thoroughly with cool water
2. in a food processor , finely chop the onions
3. add beef , 1 / 2 cup water , pepper , cumin , cinnamon , and 1 teaspoon salt
4. whirl until mixture is a smooth paste
5. add bulgur and 1 / 4 cup parsley
6. whirl just to mix
7. pat meat mixture evenly into a shallow 1- to 1 1 / 2-quart casserole
8. cut through meat mixture to make diamonds 2 to 3 inches wide
9. place a peppercorn in the center of each diamond
10. bake , uncovered , in a 425 oven until meat is no longer pink in center , about 25 minutes
11. sprinkle with remaining parsley and add salt to taste
12. to serve , cut diamonds apart and accompany with yogurt
13. yield: makes 4 servings
demonstrations.review: I made this with ground beef for an easy, healthy, flavorful weekday dinner, with a lebanese-style cucumber-tomato-mint salad on the side.  A keeper!  I'll have to try it with lamb in the future.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
semisweet chip rocky road frosting

i do not typically have milk chocolate chips so this is the rocky road version i use.  i put this onto sue b's chocolate cake.  the recipe is from chocolate from the cake mix doctor.  i have only used this for flat surfaces and not the sides of a cake.

1. place the sugar , butter , and milk in a small saucepan over medium-low heat and cook , stirring constantly , until the mixture comes to a boil , 3 to 4 minutes
2. boil , stirring constantly , for 2 minutes
3. remove the pan from the heat , add the chocolate chips , and stir until they are melted
4. let the pan rest off the heat to cool slightly but not completely , 3 to 4 minutes
5. fold in the peanuts and marshmallows until they are well combined and the heat from the frosting begins to melt the marshmallows
6. turn the frosting out onto the cooled cake , then spread evenly with a spatula until the frosting covers the entire cake
7. or spread onto cooled cupcakes
demonstrations.review: I needed a chocolate icing recipe for cupcakes at the last minute, using things I had in the cupboard.  This one worked pretty well.  I added the marshmallows, but didn't like the lumpy texture so I let them melt in all the way, and ended up with a nice, smooth chocolate glaze.  I left out the nuts since I didn't have any.  I was able to ice about 30 cupcakes (I was in a hurry and didn't let it cool, so it spread thin, which I didn't mind).  I have about 3/4 cup left in the fridge which, after I heat it up a bit, should make a nice, thick frosting for brownies.  Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
nan s classic mustard potato salad

i'm always asked to share this recipe, and people are often surprised to see how similar the ingredients are to their own recipe. while the ingredients may be similar to other posted recipes, the technique is the key to this outstanding potato salad. the specific ingredients are important, too. russets absorb the flavors best, but don't hold their shape well. dicing them after they are cold, and folding the other ingredients in gently, takes care of that problem. don't skimp on the mayo and other dressing ingredients. the potatoes will absorb a lot of moisture, and you want a creamy salad. another key to flavor and texture is the very fine chopping of the onion, celery and pickle. you want the flavors to disperse throughout the whole dish, but when you take a bite, you want to bite into potato, not an onion chunk. for smaller apetites and crowds, you can halve the quantity easily.  in louisiana and other states where they serve cajun food, potato salad is often served with gumbo.

1. boil potatoes in the peel with the whole eggs
2. remove the eggs after 10 minutes of boiling , and remove and drain the potatoes when just fork tender
3. let eggs and potatoes cool to room temperature
4. peel all and refrigerate whole potatoes and eggs until cold
5. the potatoes will dice and hold up better when cold
6. dice the potatoes into 1 / 4- 3 / 8" dice
7. place into a very large container with a lid
8. crumble the eggs and add to the container with the diced potatoes
9. very finely chop the onion , celery and pickles
10. add to the potatoes and eggs
11. gently stir to mix the ingredients evenly
12. in a separate bowl , mix the mayonnaise , mustard , dill pickle juice , cream , salt , pepper and sugar
13. whisk until creamy
14. pour over potato mixture
15. gently stir until the dry particles are coated with the creamy mixture
16. cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours
17. 6- 8 hours is even better
18. if you like color you can sprinkle some sweet paprika over the top
target.review: I enjoyed all the extra tips you gave in the directions.  Refrigerating the potatoes before peeling and cutting works great. I cut the recipe in half.  It was creamy and good, but I wanted a little more mustard.  Next time will add more mustard for our tastes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn souffle

this recipe came from my aunt who is a fabulous cook! she made this every year for thanksgiving and i use it for any special occasion. the recipe can easily be cut in half to feed about 6-8 people. i have also used fat free sour cream with no difference in taste.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. melt the 1 / 2 cup of butter in a large casserole dish in the microwave
3. mix the remaining ingredients in a large bowl until moistened
4. pour into the casserole dish
5. bake for 45 minutes to an hour or until it is golden brown on top
6. bake a little longer for a more cake-like consistency or a little less if you want it more like a pudding
demonstrations.review: This was great.  I cut in half and baked for 35 minutes at 350 degrees Convection Bake.  Turned out a perfect soft moist cornbread consistency.  I found the sweet canned cream corn added enough sweetness for me.  Didn't think it needed any extra sugar.  Was great with ribs!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach beef biscuit bake

this was one of my first successful cooking experiences. it came from the april/may 1999 issue of taste of home. this is a recipe you will want to make over and over again.

1. press and flatten biscuints onto the bottom and up the sides of a greased 11 x 7 x 2-inch baking dish
2. set aside
3. in a skillet over medium heat , cook beef and onion until meat is no longer pink , drain
4. in a bowl , beat eggs
5. add spinach and mushrooms
6. mix well
7. stir in the cheeses , garlic powder , salt , pepper , and beef mixture
8. mix well
9. spoon into prepared crust
10. drizzle with butter
11. bake uncovered , at 375 f for 25-30 minutes or until crust is lightly browned
demonstrations.review:
This was good and easy to make. 

I made it in an 8x8 dish and changed the proportions some.  Only used 1/2 lb ground beef, but used the full 10 oz of spinach, and all the feta cheese.  I also subbed black olives instead of mushrooms because thought they would be great with the feta. And they were.

After I put it in for about 10 minutes, I thought "that looks really dry"  Then realized I had forgot to add the drizzle of butter so drizzled some olive oil in middle of cooking, which took care of that problem.

Thanks for the easy recipe.  I usually have these ingredients on hand, so it will be a repeat for us!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious crock pot barbecue ribs

these can also be cooked in the oven and i have done so many times, prep time includes browning the ribs ;-)

1. set oven to 400 degrees f
2. season ribs with seasoned salt or white salt and pepper
3. place the ribs on a greased baking sheet
4. bake / brown for 20 minutes , then turn over and bake / brown for another 20 minutes
5. place the ribs in the crock pot
6. in a large bowl mix together ketchup , bbq sauce , brown sugar , apple cider vinegar , worcestershire sauce , tabasco to taste and garlic
7. mix well to combine
8. pour over the ribs then turn to coat with the sauce
9. cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours or until ribs are tender
10. delicious !
demonstrations.review: This was excellent!  I used your method and barbeque sauce with a couple changes.   I used the dry rub from fitmama's "Crock Pot BBQ Ribs" (minus the brown sugar) on this site and then roasted in oven as directed by your recipe, which I think works fantastic for getting excess grease out before putting in the crock pot.  I then used your barbeque sauce for putting on top in the crock pot (except I used Cattleman's smokehouse barbeque sauce instead of Materpiece, as it was on good sale this week).  I also made the chili sauce from Princess Buttercup's "Chili Sauce Substitute" recipe on this site, as I did not have a jar of prepared chili sauce on hand.  The sauce and ribs turned out fantastic.  Thanks for this recipe.  YUMMY!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground pork and potato balls

i got this recipe from a better homes and gardens cookbook that my mom bought in 1969. the recipe calls for 1/4 cup of chopped green onions, but i am not a big fan so i substituted with 1 tablespoon of onion flakes. this is great with mashed potatoes. i tried this for the first time tonight and my husband really surprised me not only did he go back for seconds....but thirds also!!!

1. mix egg , milk , bread crumbs , potato , onion , mustard , salt , and pepper together
2. add pork
3. mix well
4. make into 24 meatballs
5. heat shortening in skillet , add meatballs and brown
6. drain fat and remove meatballs from pan
7. dissolve bouillon cube in 1 cup of boiling water , return meatballs to pan
8. cover and cook on low for 20 minutes , turning occasionally
9. remove meatballs from pan again
10. reserve drippings
11. mix flour with 1 / 3 cup of water
12. stir into drippings
13. cook until thickened
14. serve with meatballs
demonstrations.review:
Ground pork is always on sale at our grocery store, and this was a different, easy, and yummy way to use it.

This was very good and fairly simple to make by shredding the potatoes in the food processor.  Added a little bit of minced garlic, used beef bouillion cause was out of chicken, made more gravy, and served over egg noodles.

A couple of my meatballs fell apart while browning, so just mushed those up to cook and they stayed in the gravy.  Probably will add a little more breadcrumbs next time to make sure they stay together.  Leftovers were good too!

Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lobster or crab bisque

rich and delicious seafood bisque!  i use chicken broth because it's cheap and easy to find, but if you are so inclined, you could use fresh lobster stock or  3 ounces of glace de fruits de mer gold reconstituted in 4 cups of hot water.

1. saute onion and carrot in 2 tablespoons butter until soft
2. set aside
3. in 4 quart saucepan , melt 4 tablespoons butter and add flour , whisking constantly over medium heat until roux becomes light brown
4. do not burn !
5. slowly add chicken broth , whisking constantly to ensure mixture stays smooth
6. add onions and carrots , cover , and simmer for 1 / 2 hour
7. add cream , sherry , lemon juice , worcestershire sauce , cayenne pepper , salt , and lobster or crab and simmer an additional 5 to 10 minutes
8. garnish with fresh minced chives if desired
demonstrations.review: This was excellent.  Based on the other reviews I did cut the sherry in half.  Nice spiciness to this, very rich.  I also used homemade chicken stock. Will definitely use this recipe again.  Only change I might make next time is using 1/2 and 1/2 instead of heavy cream next time.

target.recipe_text:
artichoke linguine

this is an easy, elegant and yummy pasta recipe. it has a mild flavor. it is my husbands favorite.

1. boil pasta according to directions
2. in the meantime , melt the 1 / 4 cup of butter with the 1 / 4 cup of oil in a small saucepan over medium heat
3. add the flour and stir until smooth , about 3 minutes
4. blend in the stock , stirring until thickened , about 1 minute
5. reduce heat to low
6. add the garlic , parsley , lemon juice , salt and pepper
7. cook 5 minutes , stirring constantly
8. blend in the artichokes and the 2 tbsp of parmesan cheese
9. cover and simmer over low heat for about 8 minutes
10. melt the remaining butter in a large skillet over medium heat
11. stir in the remaining oil , cheese , and salt
12. add linguine and toss lightly
13. arrange pasta on a platter and pour sauce over all
14. serve immediately
target.review: I added in capers and black olives as we really like them.  It was a great addition! Very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jasmine rice

soft, light, sweet and floral. goes well with asian dishes.

1. bring water , salt , and butter to a boil
2. stir in rice with a fork
3. bring back to a boil , then cut heat to simmer
4. cover and cook for 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: I love Jasmine rice and wasn't sure how to make it so I came on here to see if there was a quick recipe.  This one fit the bill!  So good.  The rice was nice and fluffy and everyone enjoyed it!  Will use this recipe from now on.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scallion sesame turkey burger

i found this in some random cookbook.  one of the best turkey burgers ever.  full of flavor.  make an extra for lunch the next day, reheats beautifully.

1. mix togeter , gently
2. the turkey , sesame seeds , soy , scallions , cilantro , garlic , sesame oil , 1 teaspoon of salt , and bread crumbs
3. form into patties
4. i usually mix all this together and make patties in the morning and leave in the refrigerator till i'm ready for them
5. sometimes that is the next day
6. brush with a little oil before grilling if desired
7. grill on the george foreman , in a grill pan
8. if you're using the outside grill increase the breadcrumbs a bit to insure they don't fall apart
demonstrations.review: MMMMmmm.  These burgers are so good!  We love these and have them often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk biscuits and pepper gravy

even though my mom came from "up north", she really could make great biscuits and gravy.  it has taken me this long to get the so called "recipe" down. she never measured anything, and as such, i had to guess at how she made them. i think i finally figured it out. so here it is. i hope you enjoy it. prep time includes 5 minutes sitting time if you have to make your own buttermilk. posted on october 12th 2005.

1. pre-heat oven to 425f
2. in a medium sized bowl , add flour and shortening
3. cut in shortening until it looks like coarse breadcrumbs
4. add buttermilk and stir until soft dough forms
5. pour onto a board floured with 1 / 3 cup flour
6. roll into a ball and lightly knead for about 5 minutes
7. gently pat out dough until about 1 / 3 inch thick
8. using a 1 1 / 2 to 2 inch round biscuit cutter , cut out biscuits
9. re-knead remaining scraps to make more biscuits
10. place on ungreased cookie sheet , about an inch apart
11. bake at 425f for 15 to 20 minutes or until desired color is reached
12. for gravy:
13. in a medium sized skillet , melt shortening until hot but not smoking
14. add 1 / 3 cup flour and stir until it looks like a paste
15. add 1 / 2 cup milk
16. stir until smooth
17. add rest of milk , stirring with wire whisk constantly until all lumps are gone
18. add salt and pepper to taste
19. turn off heat and let sit for 5 minutes to thicken
demonstrations.review: I used my biscuit recipe but made your pepper gravy.  Delicious with some Fried Chicken and Coleslaw!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey ginger grilled salmon

super easy, sweet and spicy!

1. in a large self-closing plastic bag , combine first six ingredients
2. mix well
3. place salmon in bag and seal tightly
4. turn bag gently to distribute marinade
5. refrigerate 15 minutes or up to 30 minutes for stronger flavor
6. turn bag occasionally
7. lightly grease grill rack
8. preheat grill to medium heat
9. remove salmon from marinade
10. reserve the marinade
11. grill 12-15 minutes per inch of thickness or until fish flakes easily with a fork
12. brush with reserved marinade up until the last 5 minutes of cooking time
13. discard leftover marinade
demonstrations.review: An amazing salmon dish with loads of flavors that we both really enjoyed!  DH says I can make it for him anytime, so it was a winner for us!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coca cola cake

-

1. combine flour , sugar , salt , cocoa and baking soda
2. in small saucepan , bring butter and coca-cola to a boil
3. add dry ingredients to mixture and then add buttermilk , eggs , and marshmallows
4. bake in 9x12 inch baking pan at 350 degrees for about 45 to 60 minutes or until tooth pick comes out clean
5. topping for coca-cola cake: combine butter cocoa and coke in a small saucepan and bring to a boil
6. pour over sugar and mix well
7. add nuts an vanilla
8. pour over cake while still hot
demonstrations.review: This cake should have a 100 ratings it is so good!  Rich, chocolately and especially good served with a big scoop of Vanilla ice cream!  I will now make this often.  Even the kids gobbled it all up and wanted seconds!

target.recipe_text:
chocolate mint cookies

i love chocolate mint anything, so when i saw this recipe, i had to try it.  of course i have not had time to make it, but i wanted to post it so that i would not lose it.  if anybody makes them, let me know.  i will try this week-end.....

1. combine flour , baking soda and cocoa together in a bowl and combine
2. in a separate bowl , combine brown sugar , sugar , butter , applesauce , vanilla , mint extract and egg white
3. beat with a hand mixer until well blended
4. combine flour mix with sugar mix to form dough
5. roll into a log and cover with plastic wrap
6. place in freezer for about 1 hour until firm
7. slice into quarter inch pieces and place on a baking sheet that has been sprayed with baking spray
8. bake at 350 for about 10 minutes
9. cool on wire rack
target.review: I just finished making these, and they are delicious! I was surprised at how good for you these cookies are while still being good, tasty cookies. My only problem was how messy it was to roll the dough into a log, since it was just so sticky. I think I might just refrigerate the dough in the bowl for a couple hours next time and just flatten the cookies after spooning them onto the baking sheet. Another variation of this would be a teaspoon of cinnamon in place of the mint...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft  spicy  heavenly ginger cookies

i found the original recipe for these cookies on allrecipes.com, and modified it to be vegan, as well as by changing the spices slightly. they are truly delicious cookies, and very easy to make.

1. in a large bowl , cream together the margarine and 1 cup sugar until light and fluffy
2. stir in the molasses
3. mix the water and baking soda and stir
4. sift together the flour , salt , and dry spices
5. add gradually to the sugar-margarine mixture
6. gradually stir the sifted ingredients , along with the ginger and raisins , into the molasses mixture
7. shape dough into walnut sized balls , and roll them in the remaining 2 tablespoons of sugar
8. place the cookies 2 inches apart onto an ungreased cookie sheet , and flatten slightly
9. bake at 350f for 10-12 minutes
demonstrations.review: Baked these last night, intending them to be for my fiance, since I usually don't care much for ginger cookies (molasses = eww), but I think I have already eaten more of them than he has! These are delicious! I made them non-vegan by using butter and an egg plus about 1 T of water in place of the 1/3C. Also used just slightly less sugar, and 3/4C whole wheat flour. The boy doesn't like raisins, so those were also left out. After mixing up the dough, I let it sit covered in the fridge overnight, and then only baked for about 8 minutes. This recipe will definitely have a permanent spot in my recipe box! Thanks pollen!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry jam buttercream

i love raspberry and this frosting did not disappoint. i used seedless raspberry preserves instead of jam. pair it with your favourite chocolate cake and you're in heaven. i added a couple drops of pink food colour to enhance the natural colour of the raspberry jam in the finished product. this recipe is from the culinary concoctions by peabody blog.

1. place butter and jam in a mixing bowl of an electric mixer fitted with a paddle attachment
2. cream butter and jam until well incorporated , about 2 minutes
3. add powdered sugar , one cup at a time until you reach desired consistency
4. if frosting gets too thick you can add a little milk to thin it out
5. if you are not satisfied with the pink colour from the jam / preserves alone add in a drop or two of red food colour to intensify it
demonstrations.review: This buttercream is great! I put it on chocolate chip cupcakes for Valentine's day, and it was delicious! I ended up using quite a bit more jam to get the flavor I was wanting, and added some vanilla as well. This also made waaayyy more than I was expecting, and I think I only used about half of it! I'm going to try using the rest in some sandwich cookies. Will definitely be using this recipe again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
havana beans

i adapted this from "500 fat free recipes". i make this a lot when i'm hungry and have no idea what to fix. i cook the rice while making the beans and then throw it all together.

1. spray a heavy pan with cooking spray
2. cook the onion , garlic , and pepper for about 3 minutes or until starting to get soft
3. add the tomatoes and pepper
4. cook and stir for 5 minutes
5. add the beans , cover , and simmer for 20 minutes
6. serve with rice
demonstrations.review: This turned out pretty tasty! I used a combination of red, yellow, and orange peppers that I already had chopped up, but I think it was around 1 cup, and about a can and a half of beans, though I did rinse them. I also added some red pepper flakes, chili powder, and cumin, because I wanted the extra flavor. Oh and I used a can of diced tomatoes instead of the fresh. I'll be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy apple muffins

these are super moist delicious healthy muffins my son loves them. i use frozen apples.

1. toss apple with splenda set aside
2. whisk egg , applesauce , & vanilla
3. add the remaining ingredients
4. mix well
5. add apple mixture
6. mix well
7. pour into 12 greased muffin tins
8. batke at 325 for 25-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I just finished making these, and they are amazing! I used regular sugar in place of the Splenda, and oat flour instead of whole wheat. I also decreased the salt to 1/4 t, and I added walnuts and raisins. I think that next time I will try using 1/4 c brown sugar and 1/4 c white to give it a slightly different flavor. Thanks, Mamawolfe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever eggless banana oatmeal muffins

these have to be the best banana muffins i've tasted! i found this recipe on allrecipes.com and tweaked it to make it egg-free and low-fat. these muffins taste best fresh from the oven, and also are the perfect, healthy way to start your day!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. in a bowl , combine flour , oats , sugar , baking powder , soda , and salt
3. in another large bowl , mix together milk , applesauce , and vanilla
4. add the mashed bananas , and combine thoroughly
5. stir the flour mixture into the banana mixture until just combined
6. lightly grease and dust 6 muffin cups , and divide the batter among them
7. bake at 400 degrees f for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I doubled this recipe and got two mini loaves and six muffins. The only changes I made were to use a full tsp of vanilla, add a tsp of cinnamon, and I used 3 bananas, without bothering to measure. The batter smelled (and tasted!) wonderful, but the finished product did not have nearly as much flavor as I expected, and the banana is only very faint. The texture is also rather gummy, which I half-expected, since this is basically a fat-free recipe. Though I wasn't overly impressed with this as-is, I will probably still play around with it to find something to more suit my tastes. Oh, and these are definitely better warmed up (or right out of the oven). Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
avocado   prawn risotto  gluten free

yummy risotto

1. place the stock in a saucepan , bring to the boil , then reduce heat to low and keep stock at a simmer
2. meanwhile , heat the butter and olive oil in a deep frypan over medium heat , add the onion and cook , stirring , for 1-2 minutes until softened , but not coloured
3. stir in the garlic , then add the rice and cook , stirring , for 1 minute to coat the grains
4. add the wine and allow the liquid to evaporate
5. add the stock , a ladleful at a time , stirring occasionally , allowing each ladleful to be absorbed before adding the next
6. continue until you have one ladleful of stock left - this should take about 20 minutes
7. add the prawns with the final ladleful of stock and continue to stir for 2-3 minutes until the prawns are cooked through
8. stir in the parmesan , then cover and remove from the heat
9. peel the avocados , dice and toss in the lemon juice
10. just before serving , carefully stir the avocado mixture into the risotto
11. serve in bowls topped with extra parmesan and chopped chives
target.review: My husband said it was the best risotto he had ever tried. I used seafood broth instead.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breast stuffed with feta cheese  sun dried tomato

a stuffed chicken breast where the sweetness of the sun-dried tomatoes harmonizes with the saltiness of the feta cheese.

1. saut garlic and red bell pepper , in olive oil , for about 3 minutes
2. put aside to cool
3. in a bowl , combine feta cheese , breadcrumbs , thyme , sun-dried tomatoes , and garlic and red pepper mixture
4. toss until well mixed
5. lay a flattened piece of chicken breast on a cutting board or your counter
6. put a 1 / 4 of the above mixture on the flattened chicken breast like you would be making a burrito and roll as tight as you can get it
7. secure it with a toothpick or butcher string
8. place chicken breast "roll" on a baking sheet , brush with olive oil , and season with salt and pepper
9. preheat oven to 350f
10. cook for about 35 minutes or until the internal temperature reaches 180f
11. i guess you could try it on a grill , but i never attempted it yet !
12. garnish with chopped green onion and serve hot
demonstrations.review: I forgot to put the olive oil on before baking and turned out dry, but that was my fault.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked cod with crunchy lemon herb topping

this is a very simple and quite delicious dish which can be made lighter and lower in calories and fat by using low fat crackers and light mayo.  from america's test kitchens' best recipes of 2007.

1. adjust an oven rack to the middle position and preheat the oven to 450f
2. lightly grease a rimmed baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray
3. set aside
4. in a medium bowl , combine the cracker crumbs and 1 tablespoon of the parsley , dill or basil
5. set aside
6. in a separate small bowl , combine the remaining 1 tablespoon parsley , dill or basil with the mayonnaise , garlic , and lemon zest and juice
7. set aside
8. season the fish fillets with salt and pepper to taste
9. place on the baking sheet , spacing the pieces about inch apart
10. brush the tops and sides of the fish with the mayonnaise mixture , then press the cracker crumbs into the mayonnaise
11. bake for 8 to 15 minutes , or until the crumbs are golden brown and the fish flakes apart when gently prodded with a paring knife
12. if the cracker crumbs brown before the fish is cooked , cover the fish with aluminum foil
13. serve hot with the lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: Fast solid recipe. Will save for a busy day but not amazing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot curried lamb and risotto

the lamb is fork tender and almost melts into the soft spicy rice. i love mango chutney and it's perfect to serve with this easy and delicious dish.

1. trim any fat from the roast
2. in a large skillet brown roast on all sides in the hot oil
3. in a 4 quart slow cooker , combine juice , uncooked rice , curry powder and salt
4. add the carrots and place the roast on top
5. cover and cook on low heat for 8-9 hours
6. add the green pepper to cooker
7. cover and let stand 5-10 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this for some family members who had never eaten lamb. I am also not known for being a good cook. They were impressed. Thanks for this one! P.S. I used only mild curry powder and regular v8 juice. Don't be afraid spicing on the hotter side

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jammin jerk chicken freezer dinner kit

great on the grill, yummy in the oven! heat and sweet! oh and this is a dump recipe! even better! thank you cuisine at home for this recipe. i broke it down to make it a dump recipe.

1. combine all ingredients in a large freezer bag
2. seal squeezing out as much air as you can
3. to cook
4. thaw completely
5. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
6. cover a baking sheet with aluminum foil or
7. spray a casserole dish with pam
8. place chicken in prepared dish reserving
9. marinade in a saucepan and bring to a simmer
10. roast for 30 - 40 minutes or until juices run clear
11. brush with remaining sauce just before serving
demonstrations.review: After our trip to Jamaica I was wondering what to do with the pickapeppa sauce and this was great. My husband was so impressed.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
commander s chocolate souffle cakes w  white chocolate sauce

a decadant single serving desert. the contrasting white sauce on chocolate cake makes for a very pretty presentation. i have had this dessert at commander's palace and it is divine!

1. --sauce--
2. bring cream to simmer in small saucepan
3. remove from heat
4. add white chocolate and whisk until melted
5. stir in rum
6. chill until just cool , whisking occasionally , about 30 minutes
7. --cakes--
8. preheat oven to 400f
9. butter six 3 / 4-cup souffl dishes
10. stir chocolate in top of double boiler over simmering water until melted
11. cool 10 minutes
12. mix sugar and eggs in processor until well blended
13. blend in butter
14. add flour
15. process until smooth
16. blend in chocolate
17. divide batter among prepared dishes
18. place on baking sheet
19. bake until cakes are puffed , tops look crusty and tester inserted into center comes out with wet batter still attached , about 18 minutes
20. run knife around sides of cakes
21. invert onto spatula
22. gently slide onto plates
23. spoon sauce around cakes
demonstrations.review: This recipe  is a decent chocolate cake but the only thing it had in common with a souffle was the dish. I liked the sauce the best

target.recipe_text:
crispy potato wedges with mustard

this was a super bowl recipe that came from the ny times, so it's suitable for a bunch of hungry guys:)  adapted from waldy malouf of the beacon restaurant.  you can either microwave this in about 30 minutes or bake it in about 60 minutes.  i microwaved and used my favorite brown mustard, koskiusko.  outside was tasty and crispy and inside was nice and soft.  careful lest your smoke detector goes off.  makes a great snack/appetizer though!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. pierce potatoes with a fork and bake them until almost cooked , about 30 to 40 minutes
3. leave oven on
4. in a large bowl , stir together mustard , olive oil , thyme , salt and pepper
5. when cool enough to handle , cut potatoes lengthwise into 4 wedges each
6. toss wedges in mustard mixture until thoroughly coated
7. raise oven temperature to 500 degrees f
8. lay potato wedges , with one cut side down , on a rimmed baking sheet and roast for 20 minutes , turning them onto the other cut side after 10 minutes
9. transfer to a warmed platter and serve
target.review: Excellent! I used baby red potatoes because that is all I had, and only used a dash of olive oil.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stir fried pork soup

from taste of home.

1. in a 3 quart saucepan , stir-fry pork , mushrooms , celery and carrots in oil until pork is no longer pink and vegetables are tender
2. add broth and spinach
3. combine cornstarch and water to make a thin paste
4. stir into soup
5. return to a boil
6. boil for 1 minute
7. quickly stir in egg
8. add pepper
9. serve immediately
demonstrations.review:
I made this tonight for my family. I didn't eat it (I've vegan) but they raved!
The only changes I made:
I marinated the pork (which was about 1lb.) in ginger, soy sauce, garlic and lemon grass.
I added some diced onion to the soup, also, because I mis-read and thought it required it.
The spoons clinked in the bowls to the last drops. 
Excellent, easy to follow recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my granola   dairy free

this is a combination that i came up with, based loosely on a nigella lawson one, when i was diagnosed as  lactose intolerant. this is one i adore, i eat this every morning with chopped fresh fruit and soy milk.

1. mix everything except the pears and ginger together in a huge bowl
2. i use a couple of large flat wooden spoons , but spatulas or slotted spoons work just as well - it's a really sticky mixture if you do it by hand --
3. spread the mixture in a large roasting pan - it will be about 2 cm deep
4. bake , uncovered , at 170c , checking and turning after 20 minutes , then every 10 minutes after that until it is golden brown and fragrant
5. you want it just golden brown as it will darken a bit more as it cools
6. remove it from the oven and allow to cool
7. chop the fruit , especially the ginger , finely and mix through the granola
8. store in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: Just a heads up - spelt is wheat-free but NOT gluten-free.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free multigrain miracle bread

it is hard to believe that something as ordinary as a loaf of bread could nearly bring tears to my eyes - but that is what happened the other night when i sliced into the loaf of fresh-baked bread i had just pulled from the oven. i can't take full credit - it's based on a recipe by a woman named laurie on the celiac.com forums. but this is really some stellar bread - hands down the best gluten-free bread i've had. it stays pliable and delicious without freezing or toasting. don't skip out on the flaxseeds, they add nutrition and texture without too much "flaxy" taste.

1. preheat the oven to 200f
2. sift the flours , yeast and all other dry ingredients together into a medium bowl
3. stir in flax meal and combine
4. combine the wet ingredients in a separate large bowl using a hand-mixer on low or medium speed
5. when fully combined , slowly add dry ingredient mixture and mix until fully blended , with no lumps
6. scrape the sides regularly
7. grease a 9x5" bread pan , and pour the dough into the pan
8. turn off the oven and immediately place the pan in it
9. do not open the door again , if possible
10. allow the dough to rise for 90 minutes
11. it should rise to the very top of the pan
12. increase heat to 350f and bake for approximately 40 minutes
13. the crust should be golden-brown
14. allow to cool slightly before removing it from the pan to finish cooling
15. do not slice until the bread is no longer hot
16. this loaf does not need to be frozen , but if there are leftovers after a few days , place slices in airtight bags and freeze
demonstrations.review: I had posted mine here (under Recipe #190906), but I am glad that you enjoyed it. It truly is a miracle! Great name :) (I'm Laurie from the celiac forums, just to clarify!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan fried cumin chile crusted fish

this only serves 2 but can easily be increased to serve how many servings you need. although the original recipe suggests using snapper, other white fish such as tilapia or grouper can be used. when i made this i used tilapia, as it is more readily available where i live. as there is not much oil used to cook the fish, it best to use a bit of pam in the skillet or a non-stick pan, as the fish tends to stick. recipe source: local newspaper

1. in a pie pan or shallow bowl combine first 5 ingredients
2. in a second pie pan or shallow bowl beat egg white
3. dip fish in egg white and then into flour mixture , coating well and shaking off excess
4. heat oil in skillet over medium high heat
5. saute fish for 3 minutes and then flip fish and saute for 5 minutes of other side or until fish is done
demonstrations.review: I made this tonight with tilapia and cornmeal instead of the flour. I didn't really measure the other things, but did equal amounts. I also added a dash of flax meal for some crunch. I know it wasn't the exact same, but I made it for my family and they loved every bite! Thanks for the inspiration - I'm sure this version is just as tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s sauteed mushrooms

i adopted this recipe from  mean chef.

1. in a large skillet , heat the oil over high heat
2. add the mushrooms
3. do not move the mushrooms until they have caramelized on the bottom
4. if you toss them too soon , they will release their liquid and begin to steam
5. when the bottoms are caramelized , toss them and continue to cook for about 5 minutes
6. add the butter and continue to cook and toss for 5 minutes , until beautifully browned
7. season with salt and pepper
8. add the garlic
9. saute another 2 minutes , and add the thyme and lemon juice
10. cook to evaporate the liquid
11. add the wine and reduce until the mushrooms are glazed with the sauce
12. toss in the parsley and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Really delicious, except I saved some calories by reducing the olive oil to 1 tbsp, and used 2 tbsp. dairy-free margarine instead. I also had to use dried thyme (that's all I had and I really wanted to make them). I served it with tilapia, and before the wine fully reduced, I drizzled it on the tilapia. Excellent!

target.recipe_text:
irish rosie s irish soda bread

this irish soda bread recipe was passed on to me by a dear friend of my mother's who was born and raised in ireland. it's the best irish soda bread i have ever had. it is much higher, lighter and softer than most other recipes i have seen. it has an excellent flavor and texture, as well.

1. combine dry ingredients together in a large bowl
2. in a small bowl beat eggs and stir in sour cream
3. add the egg and sour cream mixture to the dry ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon
4. batter will be very thick
5. add the raisins and caraway seeds and stir well with wooden spoon or knead in with your hands
6. place batter in a greased 9 inch springform pan
7. dust the top with enough flour so that you can pat the batter like a bread dough evenly in the pan without it sticking to your hands
8. with a knife make a shallow crisscross on the top
9. bake for 50 minutes in a preheated 350f oven
target.review: Thank you!!   I made it exactly as stated in the recipe.  It is delicious!  Leave this recipe as it is, it is delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s melt in your mouth scottish shortbread

this is a light, buttery flakey shortbread that is quite similar to the expensive brands that are sold in the stores, the success of this shortbread or any shortbread recipe will depend on the quality of butter that you use so purchase the best quality butter you can find, and use only salted butter, if you are using unsalted add in a pinch of salt, the almond extract is only optional -- the amount of sugar will give give a medium sweetness, if you prefer a sweeter shortbread then increase by 2-4 tablespoons, for brown sugar shortbread use brown sugar in place of white, i advise to make this a few days ahead to allow the flavors ripen --- servings is only estimated.

1. set oven to 300 degrees f
2. lightly butter an 8 x 8-inch baking dish or a 9-inch pie plate
3. using clean hands blend together all ingredients until well combined
4. press into prepared baking dish
5. prick holes all over the batter
6. bake for about 25-30 minutes or until golden on the edges
7. while the shortbread is still warm slice into squares or wedges if using a pie plate
demonstrations.review: Thanks for the recipe.  Everyone loved this shortbread.  The almond extract gave it a much richer flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
world s best pimento cheese

never liked pimento cheese until we ate it at papa robin's, a now-defunct restaurant in jasper, arkansas. this is a recreation of their marvelous pimento cheese.

1. puree till smooth in processor the mayo , cream cheese , garlic , parsley and sauces
2. turn into bowl
3. now , in food processor , process just till coursely chopped , 1 cup pecans
4. add pecans and pimentos , with juice , to mayo mixture
5. now grate cheese in food processor put into bowl with remaining ingredients
6. stir well to combine
7. let stand , refrigerated , at least 1 hour
8. even better the next day
demonstrations.review: Living in Oklahoma, pimento cheese is a staple.  We also have quite a few pecan trees.  This is my favorite recipe.  I do add 1 Tbl. worchestershire sauce and I toast the pecans in the oven at 300 degrees for 10-15 minutes (until toasted) Good stuff!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best almond paste bars

a dutch treat, these are better than any you will find in a bakery. be careful not to eat the whole pan ;)

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. beat together butter , flour , oil , first cup of sugar , baking powder , and first round of eggs until smooth and set aside
3. beat together the almond paste , second cup of sugar , second round of eggs and almond flavoring until smooth
4. combine both mixtures
5. grease a 9x13" pan , and evenly pour in mixture
6. bake for 30 to 45 minutes until toothpick comes out clean
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: These are WONDERFUL!! If you love almonds, you will love this!  It is much like an almond brownie.  It has the consistancy of a brownie or baked fudge.  These are wonderful.  I made a confectioner's sugar, light cream, and almond extract glaze to make them look as delicious as they taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fantabulous hot german potato salad

well, this cannot be good for you...

1. boil or microwave potatoes until tender
2. meanwhile , chop bacon and saute until cooked , but not crispy
3. reduce heat , saute onion until translucent
4. don't drain the fat
5. add vinegar , sugar , mustard , and mustard seed
6. whisk 2 tbs flour into stock , add to pan , bring to boil
7. taste mixture , and adjust sugar-to-vinegar ratio , if necessary
8. slice potatoes , and coat with dressing
demonstrations.review: Really delicious recipe.  I did add two boiled eggs to it, I just like them!  It is fantabulous of you to share!! I believe it is on its way of being a word, there are 31 fantabulous recipes on Recipezaar!!!! Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon white chocolate cake

this is a white chocolate layer cake, accented with saigon cinnamon. frost with recipe #122090 (i was going to add it but it was already on zaar) .

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. microwave chocolate and butter in medium microwavable bowl on high 2 minutes or until butter is melted
3. stir until chocolate is completely melted
4. cool chocolate about 5 minutes or until chocolate is lukewarm to the touch
5. beat cake mix , milk , eggs , cinnamon and chocolate mixture in large bowl with electric mixer on low speed just until moistened , scraping side of bowl frequently
6. beat on medium speed 2 minutes or until well blended
7. pour evenly into 2 greased and floured round cake pans
8. bake 25 to 28 minutes or until toothpick inserted in centers comes out clean
9. cool cakes in pans 10 minutes
10. rmove from pans
11. cool completely on wire racks
12. frost cooled cake
demonstrations.review: This is a wonderful cake.  Today is my partner's birthday and I decided to make your  cake.  He and I both loved it.  It was a nice alternative, the Saigon cinnamon gave it a nice flavor both in the icing and cake.  I used white chocolate chips because I was out of white baking chocolate.  It worked fine, will try it again with the proper chocolate soon.  Thank you for sharing.  Derek

target.recipe_text:
tacos de potatoes  tacos de hombre pobre

you can use just about any flavor of leftover mashed potatoes for these babies! the garnishes are given only as suggestions as the tacos are perfectly delicious all on their own! use mini-tortilla or tostada shells for a fun appetizer offering. what are you waiting for? ps>kids love tacos de papas!

1. steam or fry the tortillas
2. divide the mashed potatoes onto each tortilla and garnish each taco with your favorite toppings
3. servings and yield are estimated
4. for vegan , omit the cheese and the sour cream
target.review: I always make these and kids love them. I usually add a bit of cheese to smashed potatoes, stuff corn toritilla, roll it up and fry to crisp. Then I serve with Mexican Crema and Queso Fresco to make it even more delish. Always a hit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tangy and sweet aqua fresca

refreshing fruit drinks are popular all over mexico. you can use any fruit you like to flavor it.

1. in a blender combine water and fruit
2. puree until smooth
3. pour mixture through a sieve into a pitcher or serving container
4. stir in lemon or lime juice and sugar
5. add additional sugar to taste
6. garnish with a lemon or lime wedge
demonstrations.review: I make this all the time for our family mainly using watermelon, melon, and strawberries. I do omit the lemon and lime juice and cut down to 1 1/2 cup of fruit. I only add slight squeeze of lime to the strawberry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
milk rice horchata

horchatas are whitish refreshing beverages usually made with rice, but can also be made from ground almonds and/or cantaloupe seeds.

1. soak the rice overnight in the water with the cinnamon strips
2. next day discard cinnamon strips
3. process in blender in 3 batches with evaporated milk and soaking water
4. pass through sieve after each processing
5. pour into a pitcher , add theskim milk , sweeten , add vanilla and mix well by stirring
6. refrigerate until serving time
7. sprinkle a little cinnamon on each serving just before drinking
demonstrations.review: have this all the time at home love this drink

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican enchilada sauce

i got this recipe from by grmil who was born and raised in mexico city. the secret to its flavor is the cocoa

1. combine all dry ingredients in a small bowl
2. stirring constantly , slowly add enough of the water to make a thin paste
3. pour into pan and add rest of water
4. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until mixture thickens
5. stir in tomato sauce
6. use in your favorite enchilada recipe
7. the amounts on the ingredients are very flexible
8. for instance , if i am feeding my kids who do not like"spicy" , i will halve the chili powder and double the tomato sauce
9. experiment to suit your taste , but don't leave out the cocoa
10. for a quick meal , we will soften a corn tortilla in a bit of hot oil , drag it through the sauce , and lay it flat on a plate
11. cover it with grated cheddar cheese , sprinkle with chopped onions and sliced black olives
12. then cover with another softened sauced tortilla and melt the cheese in the microwave for 1 minute on high
demonstrations.review: I also like this sauce it didn't come out to thick as I like next time I will cut down water and maybe try tomatoe paste instead. I doubled cocoa powder and chili. Nice taste. Better than canned and not to spicey for the kids.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: YUMMMYY! I followed the recipe exactly. It turned out wonderfully moist. One of my boys did'nt care for the frosting but, I loved it and so did everyone else. I had never heard of banana cake but, this is one great cake and flavorful. The best part is how moist it is. I will make this for sure again. Thanks for posting. As my kids would say " this rocks".

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken salad for sandwiches

simple old-fashioned chicken salad which is perfect for sandwiches or stuffing tomatoes. although the recipe calls for boiling uncooked chicken leftover chicken would also work fine and give wonderful flavor to the chicken salad. recipe source: local newspaper

1. place chicken , celery stalk and onion in saucepan with water to cover
2. bring to a boil and simmer 20 minutes or until chicken is done
3. drain and discard onion and celery
4. let chicken cool
5. in a food processor chop chicken
6. in a medium sized bowl combine chicken with mayonnaise , salt& pepper , parsley , dill seed , chopped celery and lemon juice
7. cover and refrigerate until chilled
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe the kids gobbled this up quickly with no leftovers. The lemon juice was very tasty in this made the chicken salad very good. this recipe is a keeper.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot shredded chicken breasts for freezing   oamc

great to have on-hand for recipes. just place as many chicken breasts as you can fit into your crock pot as long as the lid fits on properly. i use bone-in, skin-on but i'm sure boneless, skinless would work too.

1. place the chicken breasts in the crock pot , mix water and spices together and pour over the chicken
2. cook on the low setting for 8-10 hours
3. remove chicken breasts , shred or pull the meat from bones , removing skin
4. place meat in individual freezer bags or containers and freeze until needed for recipes
5. defrost and add to any recipes that call for cooked chicken
6. great for casseroles , quesadillas , pizzas , burritos , pastas , soups , etc
7. or heat with bbq sauce for hot barbecue chicken sandwiches
target.review: Tried this today for the first time and it will now be the only way I will fix shredded chicken.  Very easy and the flavors are wonderful.  To be honest, I thought maybe this would be bland but it isn't at all!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kim s sweet potato casserole

this thanksgiving my boyfriend's step mom's daughter-in-law, kim, brought this sweet potato casserole for our feast. not being a huge fan of sweet potatoes, i was reluctant to try it. boy am i glad i did! it isn't as sweet as most sweet potato casseroles and doesn't have tons the marshmallow goop on it. i begged her for the recipe so that i could have it every holiday and decided to post it on *zaar so that i don't lose it. she stated on the recipe card that she always doubles the recipe and that when it does, it fills a 1 1/2 quart casserole dish.

1. mix all of the casserole ingredients together until well blended
2. spread into a buttered casserole dish
3. mix topping ingredients together and sprinkle over the casserole
4. bake uncovered in a 350 degree oven for 35 minutes
5. remove from oven
6. if topping with marshmallows , place them on the casserole and bake for an addition 5-7 minutes or until marshmallows have melted
7. serve
demonstrations.review: This was excellent!!  I tried it for Thanksgiving this year and it was everything and more; everyone enjoyed!  My sister wanted the marshmellow kind and I wanted the nut topping one so this pleased us both.  The sweet potato casserole is not overly sweet until you get to the topping and then not overly sweet, it is just enough!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican jumping beans  south beach diet phase 1 friendly

done in 20 minutes on the stovetop; i like to serve this with my low carb mexi baked chicken for a complete and festive low carb dinner. also a tasty, easy side dish to serve with your tacos, fajitas, etc.

1. in a medium saucepan , sautee the pepper , onion and garlic in olive oil until crisp-tender
2. add beans , water and seasoning
3. simmer on low to medium heat until thickened
4. top with cheese upon serving
demonstrations.review: Very flavorful & Yummy Beans!  Fixed this while on South Beach but whole family loved them.  Had to fix another pot for me to take for leftovers in lunch!  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
treebeard s red beans  and rice

this recipe is quite a favorite at treebeards' restaurant in houston. it's posted in response to a request.  cooking time does not include the pre-soak or pre-boil time.  to make it south beach friendly, substitute low fat turkey smoked sausage for the regular smoked sausage, and serve with brown rice.

1. sort and wash red beans
2. in a large soup pot , add 2 qrts cold water and red beans
3. let soak overnight
4. do not drain water !
5. add onions , celery , and bell pepper to beans and bring to a boil
6. cover , and reduce heat to simmer about 1 1 / 2 hours , or until beans are soft
7. do not stir more than necessary
8. stir in seasonings and sausage
9. simmer 30 minutes more
10. meanwhile cook a pot of rice , and serve the beans over the hot cooked rice , garnished with shredded cheddar cheese and chopped green onion
11. if you want thicker beans , remove the lid during the last 30 minutes of cooking time , or remove 1 / 2 cups of the beans and mash them before returning to the pot
demonstrations.review: One of the best beans that I have ever had.  So glad to have found it and learned about Not stirring them alot.  I think I stirred them a total of 4 times.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
20 minute chicken parmesan

this is a delightful meal. so quick and easy. serve it with pasta and a salad.

1. place chicken between two sheets of heavy-duty plastic wrap
2. flatten to 1 / 4-inch thickness , using a meat mallet or rolling pin
3. dip chicken in egg , and dredge in breadcrumbs
4. cook chicken in butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until browned on both sides
5. spoon spaghetti sauce over chicken
6. bring to a boil
7. cover , reduce heat , and simmer 10 minutes
8. sprinkle with cheeses and parsley
9. cover and simmer 5 additional minutes or until cheeses melt
demonstrations.review: This recipe is so good and easy, even on weekday nights after work.

target.recipe_text:
okra and tomatoes  a k a   okra gumbo

i havent seen too many okra recipes on zaar, so i decided to post my favorite.  my grandmother taught me how to make this dish when i was 11, and i've been making it ever since.  its a great along side smothered steak and mashed potatoes, or rice.

1. fry bacon in a large skillet that can be covered , until crisp
2. remove from skillet and drain on paper towels
3. saute onion in bacon drippings until tender
4. add okra and tomatoes , stir to blend
5. cover , reduce to low heat
6. cook for about an hour , or until okra is tender , stirring occasionally
7. do not stir too much or too briskly , because the okra will fall apart
8. season with salt and pepper , to taste
9. my family doesn't like the bacon cooked into it because the bacon becomes soft
10. if you do it my way , you can sprinkle the bacon on right before serving
target.review: I added corn to this, but otherwise made it according to this recipe.  It had a really nice flavor. I think that next time I may add pinto or cranberry beans, along with the corn. Very nice. Thank you for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oh my god the best fudgy brownies on earth

i have had many brownies and i have to say that these are by far the best brownies i have ever had (and they aren't difficult to make)!

1. preheat oven to 350f and spray a 9x9-inch square pan w / cooking spray
2. on the stove over medium-low heat , melt chocolate and butter in a medium pot
3. mix in eggs , vanilla and sugar until combined
4. add in flour , mix well
5. pour into prepared baking dish , and sprinkle w / chocolate chips if you want a true chocolate experience
6. bake for 20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near center comes out clean
7. allow to cool , cut into 16 bars
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
I have happily used another brownie recipe for 35+ years, but DS requested that I find a more â€œfudgyâ€� recipe.  I made half of this recipe, adding chocolate chips & nuts and baked in a 8 x 8â€� pan for 24 minutes. I heavily sprayed the pan & the batter, (after it was in the pan), with cooking spray as DS loves a crisp crust.  He likes this far better than my recipe.  It was indeed very â€œfudgyâ€� and I like it better than my old recipe as well. 
This recipe is very easy to mix up. I think I may add 2 T. instant coffee next time as I like Mocha. Caramel bits would be good too. There are so many possibilities!  This is my new brownie recipe!  
Thanks from both of us!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super tasty white sauce

there was a lack of sauces on recipezaar so i thought i would make a contribution. a very nice sauce with many uses. i will post some recipes where i use it.

1. place the butter in a preheated suacepan and melt the butter down
2. once the butter is melted down add the plain flour
3. stir well and cook the mixture of butter and plain flour which should go a bit lumpy and dry at this stage
4. very important that you cook this well
5. remove from heat and slowly , very slowly add the milk and stir in
6. the sauce should now be getting smooth
7. if it is lumpy you have been adding the milk to fast
8. keep adding the milk until the desired thickness is achieved
9. add the paprika for a bit of extra kick
10. any other herbs or things like lemons can be added for a bit of extra taste
11. this sauce is used in my fish and white sauce and my tuna mornay recipes as well so look for them
demonstrations.review: I doubled this, adding a bit of salt & pepper, and served it over sliced hard-boiled eggs on top of thick slices of toast for brunch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar brownies  blondies

an easy & yummy brownie that makes a nice no-chocolate treat! fun to vary the mix-ins - we like to add candy corn! it's a moist slightly cakey brownie that everyone will enjoy!

1. mix all ingredients well
2. bake in 9 inch square pan that you have sprayed well with pam at 350f for 25 to 30 minutes
3. cool before cutting
demonstrations.review: I made this with only 2/3 cup brown sugar, then added 1 cup walnut pieces and 1/2 cup shredded coconut.  Very good, with a cake-like texture, I will make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ratatouille

this is another recipe i made a lot before the-girl-who-hates-vegetables joined us. one of our favotite summer dinners with a nice hunk of bread. i also added some tomato paste to this to reduce the acidity. came from we're cooking now - an old cooking show circa 1985.

1. heat oil in dutch oven or large saucepan , cook garlic and onions until tender
2. cut vegetables into 1-inch pieces
3. add the eggplant , zucchini , pepper , oregano parsley and stir well
4. saute about 5 minutes
5. add tomatoes , cover and cook over low heat for about 45 minutes
6. serve hot or cover mixture and refrigerate to serve chilled
demonstrations.review: I have made this several times with no changes to the recipe.  It was very easy to make and I will make it again. DS likes it over pasta with Feta Cheese.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
luby s cafeteria chocolate chess pie

for those enchanted with cafeteria food. chocolate lovers will especially enjoy this richly flavored version of the south's classic chess pie.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in large bowl , combine sugar , flour , butter , and cocoa
3. mix well
4. add eggs one at a time , mixing well after each addition
5. add evaporated milk , corn syrup , chocolate , and vanilla
6. mix well
7. if using refrigerated crust , unroll and place into pie pan
8. pour batter into pie shell
9. bake 45 to 50 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out almost clean
10. do not overbake
demonstrations.review: Admittedly, taste is very subjective but this taste like Coco Wheats Cereal to me.  IF I make this again, I would make major changes starting with the type & amount of chocolate.

target.recipe_text:
ultimate pizza sauce

this pizza sauce recipe was given to me as a wedding present, written on the inside cover of a pizza cookbook. it is thick, saucy, spicy and delicious. i'll never use anything else on my homemade pizzas. i like to double or triple it and put it in ziploc bags in my freezer.

1. in a large skillet , melt butter with the oil
2. add the onion , celery and garlic and saute until soft and transparent
3. add tomato sauce and tomato paste and stir until smooth
4. add remaining ingredients and bring to slow simmer
5. simmer for 30-60 minutes
6. remove the bay leaf and spread the sauce on your prepared pizza dough
target.review: This sauce is the best! I have mad this several times, it is my 'go to' sauce recipe. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled ham with glaze

this delicious ham is a nice break from the burgers and chicken we do. the glaze is so good!

1. in small saucepan , bring first 3 ingredients to a boil
2. boil 1 minute
3. remove from heat
4. brush on the ham
5. grill over med hot coals , turning once , until hot
6. baste with more glaze
demonstrations.review: I cooked this last night and it was great! I had only enough ingredients to make 1/3 of the glaze, but it was plenty to brush on the ham, but not enough left over for dipping. This recipe is going into my weekly meal rotation. I couldn't believe how good it was, and how simple to make. Thanks for posting :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian style grilled tilapia

i have to put this recipe somewhere before it gets thrown away!! it was in the paper as a "quick meal". i just love tilapia!! feel free to add more garlic or ginger to this sauce....the more the merrier, right?

1. combine the soy sauce , sugar , garlic , lime juice , ginger and red pepper flakes in a wide , shallow baking pan that will hold all of the fish in a single layer
2. stir briefly to dissolve the sugar
3. add the tilapia , then turn it over so that it's coated all over with the marinade
4. set aside for 20 min or so
5. heat the broiler to high , and move the oven rack to position closest to heat
6. slide the pan into the oven , and broil the fish for 5 minute keep the oven door ajar so the broiler element stays lit
7. turn the pan around , and broil for 5 more minute
8. if the juices in the pan appear to burn , add a little water to the dry spot to prevent burning
9. the fish should be opaque and flaky
10. spoon the sauce over the fish when serving
demonstrations.review: Oh My, this was excellent! I cooked this for dinner tonight and wished I had cooked more. I used the exact recipe and grilled it on the charcoal grill. I reduced/cooked the marinade in the microwave for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring halfway through. I served it with my own recipe for Lemon Rice Pilaf (I have it posted) and an Asian salad with dried cranberries, won ton strips and sesame-orange salad dressing. I will be cooking this again! Thank you for posting. Jan

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best baked beans

the perfect addition to picnics and barbecues! simple and delicious. sure to become one of your favorites. my mother makes this for every family get together. ham could be added, or more ketchup if desired, but try it this way first - you'll love it!

1. cut bacon into bite size pieces
2. cook bacon in microwave , checking after each minute , or cook in a skillet , draining fat
3. don't let it get crisp
4. meanwhile , mix the remaining ingredients in a 3 quart casserole dish
5. add bacon and mix a little
6. bake uncovered for one hour at 350
7. it's best if they set out to cool for one hour before you serve them
demonstrations.review: Excellent!!! I cooked these for the second time today, this has become my standard baked beans recipe. I did decrease the brown sugar to 1/3 cup as others had mentioned, and they were perfect! Thanks for posting this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef patties in onion gravy

good 

1. combine all patty ingredients
2. mix thouroughly with your hands and shape into 4 patties
3. spray a non-stick skillet , and brown patties on both sides
4. add dry onion soup mix and 1 1 / 2 cup water
5. cover pan tightly and simmer for 20 minutes
6. remove patties to a plate
7. in a gravy shaker or jar , combine 1 / 2 cup water with 2 tbs
8. flour
9. stir flour and water into onion gravy
10. stir constantly with a whisk until it comes to a boil
11. boil 1 minute
12. return patties to pan
13. serve with mashed potatoes or hot cooked noodles
demonstrations.review: Very, very good! I loved it...cooked it for dinner tonight and served it with white rice and green beans. True comfort food.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
deep fry breading

deep fry breading for fried chicken, pork tenderloin, or fish. this will give you a nice substantial crispy breading for your deep fried foods

1. wisk together batter ingediients in a large mixing bowl until smooth
2. should be the consistency of runny pancake batter
3. put as much of your meat in the bowl with the batter as you can , and make sure it is all well coated with the batter
4. let it set for at least 5 minutes
5. combine the dry ingredients in a 9 x 13 baking pan , make sure they are well mixed
6. reserve 1 cup of dry mix and spread it evenly on a platter this keeps the pieces from getting soggy and pulling the breading off of each other
7. use the wet hand , dry hand method and take each battered piece and dredge it in the dry mix until well coated and then move to platter , do not stack the pieces
8. only prepare as many pieces as willl fit in your deep fryer in one batch
9. do each batch seperately just before putting in fryer and fry until medium brown following your fryers directions
10. don't try to stretch the dry mix , when it gets soggy and too clumpy , make a new batch of dry mix
demonstrations.review: Fantastic!!! I used cornmeal in place of the bread crumbs and fried sliced squash. Tonight I am using it to batter and fry green tomatoes. A keeper!!!!!

target.recipe_text:
bits n bites

an awesome snack! my mom used to make this every christmas, and give some away in christmas tins, or fancy jars. makes a great hostess gift, or teacher gift- but now i just make it for myself and my family, usually two batches each christmas!

1. mix all dry ingredients together in a large roasting pan
2. toss to mix
3. mix oil , garlic powder , seasoned salt and worcestershire sauce together in a large measuring cup
4. whisk together , it will want to separate , so keep whisking while you pour over dry ingredients
5. mix thoroughly
6. bake at 250 uncovered , for 1 1 / 2 hours mixing every 20 minute
7. allow to cool , enjoy !
target.review: So yummy!!  Think I will have to do another batch!  I did add a few drops of tobasco sauce for a little more zing.  Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pot pie w  puff pastry

this recipe is a favorite in our house. using the puff pastry makes it very quick and easy to prepare. i also use pie pastry when i don't have puff pastry on hand. i usually make this pie in a 9"x13" baking dish but when it's busy i just divide it into two 8" square dishes.   
notes:  if chicken breasts are frozen just boil them in water and remove skins.  you can always add your harder vegetables to cook with the chicken.  cubed carrots, potatoes, etc. 
a great tip if you're like me and don't tend to keep cream, buttermilk or whipping cream on hand. i buy these containers and divide them into muffin tins and freeze. then i pop them out and store them in resealable bags. each cube is about 1/4 cup.

1. thaw pastry according to package directions
2. heat butter in large saucepan
3. cook onion in butter until tender-crisp
4. add flour and seasonings , mixing until smooth
5. gradually stir in broth and milk
6. cook , stirring constantly , over medium heat until mixture comes to a boil and is smoothly thickened
7. stir in chicken and vegetables
8. cool slightly
9. spoon into baking dish
10. place rolled out puff pastry on top and make slits for steam to escape
11. you can brush with egg white
12. bake on lower rack in oven @ 375f
13. until filling is bubbling and crust is puffed and golden brown
14. 30-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was very good!  It didn't make nearly as much as the recipe states though.  I doubled the ingredients for the sauce mixture (flour, broth, etc) and still only used an 8 1/2" x 11 1/2" pan.  I also used 1% milk, added some garlic powder and only used 1/2 of the puff pastry.  Finally I doubled the amount of vegetables.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hubby s favorite onion rings

these are my hubby's favorite onion rings (and mine too.) they are really simple, and very fast to make. the onion rings are puffy and crispy, and a beautiful golden color. great with cheeseburgers or brats.

1. peel onions , cut into 1 / 4 inch slices , and separate into rings
2. combine dry ingredients
3. stir well
4. add eggs , milk , and 1 teaspoon oil , and beat until mixture is smooth
5. dip onions into batter
6. fry in deep hot oil until golden brown
7. drain on paper towels
demonstrations.review: I've been craving onion rings all week and decided to try this recipe.  They were good but not crispy like I had hoped.  They were quite doughy actually.  I also added cajun seasoning instead of the black pepper for a little kick.  I refrigerated the batter and added an extra tablespoon of milk.  The batter stuck to the onion rings quite nicely.  I just didn't care too much for the texture.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy stir fry sauce

a basic stir fry sauce that i've been using for years. i got the recipe from my mother, but i don't know where she got it from. i make no claim to authenticity.

1. combine all ingredients in a large glass jar with a lid
2. screw lid on
3. shake well
4. can store in fridge up to 2 weeks
5. shake well before using
6. to use sauce: stir fry your vegetables and meat as desired , add appropriate amount of sauce , bring to a boil , boil for 1 minute or until slightly thickened
7. serve
demonstrations.review: This was the yummiest stir fry sauce recipe ever!  The only thing I added was about a tsp of chili pepper flakes.  Everyone in our house loves it and it was definitely easy!  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
a mountain of make ahead mashed potatoes

creamy mashed potatoes for 12 lucky people. make ahead if desired, or bake right away. whichever you choose, this recipe is sure to be a hit at your next potluck.

1. place potatoes in large pot , cover with water , and bring to a boil
2. reduce heat , cover , and cook for 20-25 minutes or until potatoes are tender
3. drain potatoes , place in large bowl , and mash with sour cream , cream cheese , onions , salt , and 4 tablespoons of butter , stirring until butter and cream cheese have melted
4. spread potatoes into greased 13 x 9 baking dish
5. melt remaining butter and drizzle over potatoes
6. sprinkle with paprika , cover , and refrigerate until ready to use
7. refrigerated potatoes need to sit at room temperature for 30 minutes before baking
8. cover with tin foil and bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes , then remove foil and bake for another 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very rich but yummy!  These were great at Christmas!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli   cheese soup

a great soup, one of the deli classics.

1. saute onion and celery in butter in saucepan over medium heat until tender
2. add flour , and salt and pepper , cooking and stirring until mixture is smooth and bubbly
3. add broth and milk , stirring constantly until mixture comes to a boil and begins to thicken
4. add cooked broccoli , stirring until all is heated through
5. remove from heat and stir in cheese until melted and smooth
demonstrations.review: This soup was absolutely wonderful!  We loved loved loved it!  I made a pot for 2 of us last weekend and we ate the whole thing for lunch.  I think I'll make some more this weekend, lol.  I followed the recipe exactly except that I pureed about half of it for a thicker consistency.  Yum!  Thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
green kale with raisins   toasted pine nuts

nice combination of kale, raisins & pine nuts. i sometimes add a hint of cinnamon. loaded with iron.

1. to toast the pine nuts place them on a cookie sheet in a 325f oven for about 5 minutes , be careful they burn easily
2. bring water to boil in a skillet with a tight fitting lid , add kale and cook for approximately 5 minutes of until the kale is just tender , drain& set aside
3. rinse out the skillet , dry , add olive oil and heat over medium heat , add garlic and saute for 30 seconds , add raisins and stir for about 30 seconds
4. the raisins should be glossy and slightly puffed
5. add kale , stir , season and saute until heated through
6. garnish with the pine nuts and serve
target.review: This was so good!  Who would think the whole family would want a second helping of kale?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with shrimp and wine

this is one of the best pasta/seafood dishes i have ever tasted! i know the recipe came from a cookbook, but a friend gave it to me several years ago (xeroxed the page) and the title of the book doesn't appear. sorry i can't give credit!
i've made it with scallops, too, and it's just as good.

1. thaw shrimp , if frozen
2. in a saucepan , cook onion in 2 tblsp
3. butter and olive oil until tender but not brown
4. stir in wine , bouillon granules , basil , salt and pepper
5. bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer , uncovered , for 12 to 15 minutes or until about 1 / 3 of the liquid is evaporated
6. halve shrimp lengthwise and add to wine mixture
7. cover and simmer about 5 minutes until shrimp is just tender
8. stir in tomatoes and heat through
9. toss pasta with 1 / 4 cup butter , melted
10. add shrimp mixture , cheese and parsley
11. toss until pasta is coated
demonstrations.review: I've made this several times in the last 2 weeks since I found this recipe.  I don't usually repeat recipes that much.  My husband and son (5) keep asking for it.  It's very good plus quick and easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
radicchio and endive salad

a change for a salad.  very simple and so good!

1. in a large bowl , whisk together vinegar , oil , honey
2. season with salt and pepper
3. add radicchio and endive
4. toss to coat
5. serve
demonstrations.review: This was delicious!  A perfect quick salad with loads of flavor.  I never know what to do with radicchio and now I know.  I added some toasted walnuts and goat cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy baked tortellini   giada

i got this recipe from giada de laurentiis, on her cooking show. i saw her make this and had to make it myself, because it looked so good. and it is!!!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly oil an 8 x 8" baking dish
3. whisk the sauce , mascarpone cheese , parsley and thyme in a large bowl to blend
4. cook tortellini in a large pot of boiling salted water until just tender , about 2 minute drain
