5. add tortellini to the sauce and toss to coat
6. transfer the tortellini mixture to the prepared baking dish
7. top the mixture with the mozzarella and parmesan
8. cover and bake until the sauce bubbles and the cheeses on top melt , about 30 minute
demonstrations.review: This was so good.  I didn't have mascarpone so I substituted regular cream cheese.  I will definitely be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious tuscan style trout   in 25 minutes

my husband & i love baked trout & baked salmon. this is a lovely recipe which you can use either fish in or even haddock. it is very simple to make, ready in 25 miuntes & is truly delicious! this recipe uses a ready made rub but you can make your own by mixing 4 tbsp sun dried tomatoes (with the olive oil they come in) & 1 tbsp of fresh torn basil & a pinch of sea salt. blitz in a mini food processor or mortar & pestle.

1. preheat the oven to 190c cut 4 large squares of tin foil , each large enough to enclose the trout in a loose parcel
2. dive the courgettes equally between them & dot withthe butter
3. mix the rub with the olive oil & spreas over the trout fillets , rubbing it in lightly
4. put the trout on the vegetables & top with the slices of lemon
5. to wrap , fold the foil to make loose parcels with enough space inside allow the air to circulate
6. tightly seal the edges by folding over twice
7. put the parcels on a baking tray & cook in the oven for 20 mintes
8. serve with boiled new potatoes
demonstrations.review: I'm giving this a four star only because the zucchini turned out overcooked but the fish was delish!  Next time I'll just split them up.  I mixed up some sundried tomatoes, dried basil (all I had), evoo, and threw in a couple cloves of garlic.  I rubbed it on the fish, put in the packet and grilled on indirect heat for about 20 minutes.  Yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken stew with tomatoes and white beans

this is a delicious recipe and makes a comforting meal on a cold evening. bon appetit published this in 1999.

1. cook chopped bacon in heavy large pot over medium-high heat until crisp
2. using slotted spoon , transfer bacon to paper towel
3. sprinkle chicken thighs with salt and pepper
4. dredge chicken in flour , shaking off excess
5. add to drippings in pot and saut until brown , about 3 minutes per side
6. using slotted spoon , transfer chicken to large bowl
7. pour off all but 2 tablespoons drippings from pot
8. add chopped onion and minced garlic to pot
9. saut 4 minutes
10. add bacon , stewed tomatoes , chicken broth , red wine , basil and oregano
11. bring to boil , scraping up browned bits
12. return chicken and any accumulated juices to pot
13. cover and simmer until chicken is cooked through , about 20 minutes
14. add cannellini
15. simmer 10 minutes longer
16. season to taste with salt and pepper
17. makes 4 to 6 servings
demonstrations.review: This was very good.  I made a few "figure friendly" adjustments though.  I used boneless skinless chicken breasts cut up into chunks.  I dredged them in flour with salt and pepper added then browned in olive oil.  I also added a handful of real bacon bits for flavor but less fat.  It was still a yummy, easy, winter dinner that I will definitely make again.

target.recipe_text:
the best apple pie muffins ever

i got this  recipe from a friend.  i make these often and take them to many potlucks, office parties, the cottage, picnics, children's lunch and the list goes on. recipe from the cookbook "just the best."

1. cinnamon could be added to the batter
2. topping: in a small bowl toss together sugar , flour , butter and cinnamon until crumbly
3. set aside
4. muffins: in a large bowl whisk together brown sugar , oil , egg and vanilla until smooth
5. in a separate bowl , sift together flour , soda and salt
6. stir oil mixture into flour mixture alternately with buttermilk
7. fold in apples , mixing just until combined
8. spoon into greased muffin cups filling 3 / 4 full
9. sprinkle topping over evenly
10. bake at 350f for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown and tops spring back
target.review: Four stars only b/c of all the adjustments made to recipe; however, I will say this, if for no other reason, please please make this recipe for the simple fact that the entire house smells AMAZING afterward. We were very pleased with the *somewhat altered* results. Kids loved them. I made the night before for quick b-fast in the morning, but they sat by the oven and waited, split one for dessert before bed and begged for more!!! My 6 y.o. informed me that even though she has never done it before, she may be sneaking out of bed in the middle of the night to get another one before morning! Will make again and again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: Delicious! Hubby loved them. This will make a nice change into the typical meal rotation at our house!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oreo balls

my sister's co-worker brought these to a party and they were quite a hit. i don't know where the recipe came from originally.

"bark" is an artificial chocolate or vanilla candy coating/confectioner's coating used to make a treat called almond bark and can be found at most grocery stores near the chocolate chips. 

you can use chocolate chips and white chocolate chips if you don't have almond bark, but i have found that almond bark melts better and is easier to work with.

1. using a blender or hand held mixer , mix oreos and cream cheese together
2. roll into walnut size balls
3. chill for an hour
4. melt approximately 3 / 4 package of white almond bark
5. stick a toothpick in an oreo ball and dip it in the melted white almond bark
6. allow to harden on wax paper
7. takes about 15 minute
8. while waiting , melt about 1 / 4 package of chocolate almond bark
9. when oreo balls are no longer sticky to the touch , decorate with drizzles of chocolate and white almond bark
10. i just use a sandwich bag with a tiny hole cut in one corner to drizzle the almond bark
demonstrations.review: Phenomenal!!! Just wonderful. I wish I hadn't eaten more than I gave away, but they were just so tempting! Excellent holiday recipe for fod gifts!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon  garlic and basil shrimp skewers

use this recipe as a template for other shrimp skewers. if you don't have honey mustard, stir a little honey into dijon. limes would also work well instead of lemons. and if you're finding your home-grown chives or parsley getting out of hand, substitute them for the basil.
these need to marinate for 45 minutes before cooking.
recipe developed for food and drink by heather trim.

1. in a medium bowl , whisk lemon juice with oil , mustard , garlic and lemon peel
2. add shrimp and stir to coat
3. marinate , covered and refrigerated , for about 45 minutes
4. grease grill and preheat barbecue to high
5. thread shrimp onto skewers and sprinkle both sides lightly with salt
6. place on grill and barbecue until shrimp are pink , about 1 to 2 minutes a side
7. remove , place on a platter and sprinkle with basil
demonstrations.review: Everyone in family loved this marinade for shrimp. Will make again and again!!! My very picky eater who DOES NOT eat shrimp...ATE shrimp!!! This is a winner! Can't wait to do chicken and shrimp together. Flavor is still in my mouth. Loved it, loved it, loved it!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
island rice

we like to eat this rice when we are having a "tropical" meal.  this recipe comes from "burt wolf's menu cookbook".  i usually just put all the ingredients in my rice cooker and just add a little extra water but it can be cooked on the stove as described below.

1. bring water to a boil in a saucepan
2. add the rest of the ingredients and simmer , covered , for 20 minutes
3. remove garlic clove before serving
demonstrations.review: Would never have thought to put lime in rice,but so glad I tried it anyway. Made as a side to Lemon, Garlic and Basil Shrimp Skewers as an idea from another reviewer. Lime flavor was strong upon first bite, but more addictive bite by bite. My 4yo son who eats anything put his first bite in and tried to spit it out, but ate another and another and asked for more. Definately grows on you!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Such an easy recipe, and so versatile! It does look kind of gross but if you can get past the looks part, the taste is amazing. It was more watery than I expected, so a quick change of plans and it was served as "chicken stew~mexican style" the first night, and leftovers in tortilla wrap the next night as "enchiladas" (this made it sound like it was restaurant style...sometimes the wording is all I need to make the picky child eat! She loved it! I was also thrilled with the amount it produced, as it saved me a night of cooking as well.

target.recipe_text:
easy banana muffins

nan

1. mash bananas , add sugar and the slightly beaten egg
2. stir in melted butter
3. stir in dry ingredients
4. spoon into medium size muffin pan
5. bake 20 minutes at 350f degrees - 375f degrees
target.review: This recipe is amazing! Here are somethings I did to make it healthier. I used brown suger instead of white, and whole wheat flour instead of all-purpose and 2 egg whites. I also added some cinnamon and vanilla extract. I didn't use nuts due to my sisters nut allergy, but it was still amazing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chip or m   m oatmeal cookies

these are really good, i like to use red and green m and m's to replace the chocolate chips and serve them as christmas cookies.

1. cream the butter and both sugars
2. add eggs and vanilla
3. mix together with flour , oatmeal , salt , baking powder , and soda
4. add chocolate chips , and nuts
5. roll into balls and place two inches apart on a cookie sheet
6. bake for 10 minutes at 375 degrees
demonstrations.review: This was reallly good but they spread a lot because we didnt't put the cookies far enough on the pan and are pan was to small. But the cookies were delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven baked fries

excellent side dish.  any seasoning will do, these are just what i like.

1. cut potatoes into thin strips
2. you can leave the skin on , it's good for you !
3. spread in one layer onto a baking sheet
4. drizzle with olive oil and rub over potato strips
5. using your hands would probably be easiest
6. season with any seasoning of your choice
7. i prefer old bay , mrs
8. dash and seasoned salt
9. bake in oven at 350 degrees for 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender
10. then broil for another 10 minutes or until the "fries" are crispy
demonstrations.review: Excellent. THe Seasons were right on abd the fries crisped up so well. I served these for dinner last night andd my kids liked this better than te ones I fry. They are healthier too, which is also an up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fluffy eggless pancakes

i poached this recipe from cooks.com (it was submitted by dawn linke, so props to her). i'm mainly posting it here since this is the recipe site i use the most and i want to add it to my cookbook, and i was most happy with this recipe vs. other eggless pancake recipes i've tried, so i figured it was worth sharing. :)

1. combine dry ingredients and mix slightly
2. add milk , oil , water , and vanilla
3. whisk together until just combined
4. be careful not to over mix - it should still be slightly lumpy
5. set aside to rest for a few minutes
6. melt the butter
7. when fully melted , add the butter to the batter
8. take pan to stove and stir butter into batter
9. when pan is hot , with a measuring cup or ladle , pour 1 / 4 cup of batter into the skillet for each pancake
10. cook until bubbles form on the surface
11. carefully flip pancakes with turner / spatula and cook until golden brown
12. chopped fruit , nuts or chocolate chips can be added to batter before cooking for a unique treat
demonstrations.review: These were really good! Just like you suggested they fluffed up a lot. I promised everybody pancakes for breakfast yesterday, but we didn't have any eggs. NOBODY could tell that there were no eggs in it. My younger sister was asking how I got it so fluffy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanilla butter icing

this is my favourite icing. you can make it in vanilla or chocolate flavours.

1. place icing sugar and butter in a bowl and add boiling water slowly , stop when it is the consistency you want
2. stir until it spreadable and add vanilla essence
3. ices a 20cm cake
4. add 1 / 4 cup cocoa powder for a chocolate version
demonstrations.review: I am sure this is a good recipe but i did not have icing sugar so I used granulated sugaar and the icing was not very good and it did not have a good texture and tasted to much like butter. Anyway it is probably my fault.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanishing oatmeal raisin cookies

oatmeal raisin cookie recipe from the quaker oats box.  bar cookie variation included.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. beat together margarine and sugars until creamy
3. add eggs and vanilla
4. beat well
5. add combined flour , baking soda , cinnamon and salt
6. mix well
7. stir in oats and raisins
8. mix well
9. drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet
10. bake 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown
11. cool 2 minutes on cookie sheet
12. remove to wire rack
13. makes about 4 dozen
14. bar cookies: bake 30 to 35 minutes in ungreased 13x9-inch metal baking pan
demonstrations.review: This was awesome! I didn't have any cinamon but it was just fine! A wonderful cookie recipe! It was also very chewy!!!!!

target.recipe_text:
day after thanksgiving turkey and sausage gumbo

use up those leftovers right down to the carcass...and freezable, too.

1. to make the roux , in a large dutch oven over medium heat , combine the oil and flour
2. cook , stirring constantly until becomes a reddish-brown color , approximately for 30 to 40 minutes
3. be careful not to burn
4. add to the roux the onions , bell pepper and celery , stirring , about 5 minutes
5. add broth
6. bring to a boil , stirring to incorporate roux , then reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour
7. add salt , pepper and cayenne
8. add turkey and sausage then simmer an additional 30 minutes
9. should the gumbo become too thick , thin with additional broth or water
10. skim from the top any fat that surfaces
11. add the green onions and the parsley
12. serve over hot rice
target.review: Although it's nowhere close to Thanksgiving, I did bake a turkey for my husband last week---he loves having one around for sandwiches, or just "gnawin' " on a leg!  I used the carcass for this recipe, and it made a huge pot!  I'm freezing some, taking some to neighbors and husband's elderly parents, and there will still be a-plenty left to freeze for "The Carnivore"!  I used a bag of frozen gumbo vegetables that included corn, and instead of cayenne, I used red pepper flakes   some Cajun spice mix (quite a lot of that, actually).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic honey roasted root vegetables

this is an easy, inexpensive, stress-free recipe even a beginning cook could whip together. perfect for fall and winter. this dish is usually served hot, but is also very tasty cold, either by itself or mixed in with spring greens and a balsamic or "goddess" dressing. you can easily substitute other root vegetables if you don't have these on hand - try celery root, baking potatoes, red beets, etc.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. cut the bottom 1 / 4 inch of each garlic clove off but do not peel cloves
3. toss ingredients in a deep baking dish
4. roast , uncovered , for approximately 30 minutes or until all vegetables are soft throughout
5. toss vegetables and turn heat up to 400 degrees
6. roast until vegetables are browned and caramelized
7. serve hot or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: Tasty, tasty!  I used only what I had on hand---red beets, sweet potato, and parsnips---and subbed agave for honey.  Beautiful color and texture!  Excellent side for an otherwise "beige" meal---I served this with chicken loaf and pasta with Alfredo sauce.  Mmm!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked zucchini potato latkes

this is probably not at all traditional but it is way healthier and very tasty. easy and quick enough to throw together after work and it will use up some of the garden's bounty. i just eyeball this so all measurements are approximate. feel free to improvise. you can use more or less potato and zucchini, you just may need to add a bit more egg or flour to get it to come together nicely.

1. shred the potato and zucchini with a cheese grater , chop the onion
2. mix together with the salt and let sit for 10 min to draw out some of the liquid
3. drain the veggies well , give them a little squeeze
4. they don't have to be perfectly dry but do the best you can
5. mix in the remaining ingredients , preheat the oven to 425f and line a baking sheet with parchment paper
6. just greasing it wont work , they'll stick anyways
7. form the mix into little cakes about 1 / 2 inch thick by 2-3 inches around
8. bake for 10-15 min , flip and bake another 10-15 min or until crispy and browned on both sides
9. serve with sour cream with chopped green onion mixed inches
demonstrations.review: Tasty and simple to make! I subbed Parmesan cheese for the cheddar, as I'm not a fan of low-fat cheeses (although parm is naturally low-fat---I guess I mean I don't like tampered with versions of cheeses meant to have a certain fat content?) Instead of dill, I used an Italian blend. The lemon pepper/jalapeno idea sounds nice, Incredibore---will try that next time. A keeper, Spiritusancto!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy tuna or chicken noodle casserole

this is a delicious casserole that can be made using either tuna or 1-1/2 cups or more of cooked cubed chicken or even cooked turkey
 --- for a thinner sauce use 1 cup of milk or half and half instead of 3/4 cup, prep time includes boiling the egg noodles, if you are not a garlic-lover then you may omit the garlic powder and to zing the flavor up even more add in 1-1/2 tablespoons of lemon juice

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. grease a 2-quart casserole dish
3. cook the egg noodles in boiling salted water
4. drain then toss with 2 tablespoons butter
5. in a large saucepan , mix the undiluted mushroom soup , garlic powder , parmesan cheese milk or half and half , sour cream , salt , pepper , chopped onion , pimiento , bell pepper and celery
6. cook over low heat , stirring frequently for 15 minutes
7. add in the tuna or chicken
8. mix to combine
9. combine the mixture with the cooked egg noodles
10. transfer to prepared greased baking dish
11. sprinkle top with the broken ritz crackers
12. bake for about 25 minutes
demonstrations.review: My husband retains his childhood fondness for good ol' tuna casserole, and this is a nice twist on that "school cafeteria classic"!  I chopped up some leftover grilled yellow bell peppers and subbed these for the pimiento/green pepper combo, and used the golden mushroom/roasted garlic canned soup.  And the resident overgrown "little boy" insists on a can of sweet green peas added to the mix...good old-fashioned recipe, KC!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian summer squash

a delicious way to use zucchini and yellow squash. you can adjust the seasonings to your own taste, and add salt and pepper, if desired. be sure to use younger, 5 to 7 inch squash.

1. sautee garlic and onions in butter , until tender
2. wash and scrub squash
3. slice into 1 inch coins
4. place in pan with onions and garlic
5. cover and cook over medium heat 5 minutes
6. stir , and add spices
7. cover and cook 3 to 5 minutes more
8. do not overcook
9. squash should be a little firm
10. remove to bowl , sprinkle with cheese
demonstrations.review: A meal in itself!  Delicious.  We had this last night along with some fresh lima beans and baked tomatoes.  I made no changes to the ingredients and amounts, but did alter the prep slightly:  I sliced the vegetables thinner (1/4") and did not cover the pan, allowing the juices to evaporate somewhat.  I upped the heat a bit, which caramelized everything nicely. A true winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple and cheddar cheese casserole

this recipe comes from mobile, alabama via my in-laws. strange combination? yes. but it makes a sweet surprise for your holiday table or family dinner. for the cheese crackers use brands such as cheese-its or cheese nips.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a large bowl combine flour and sugar , then add 6 tablespoons of reserved pineapple juice
3. add butter , cheese and pineapple
4. mix until combined
5. pour into 13x9 casserole dish
6. bake 20 minutes at 350
7. top with crackers
8. reduce heat to 250 degrees and bake an additional 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Unusual, and always enjoyed.  I cut the sugar back to 1/2 cup, though!

target.recipe_text:
apple cinnamon overnight oatmeal

easy, easy, easy...t hat's what this is. put ingredients in crock pot the night before. upon serving, add more brown sugar to taste.

1. mix together the apples , cinnamon and brown sugar in bottom of crock pot
2. sprinkle oats over apples , then pour in water and salt
3. do not stir !
4. cook on low for 8-9 hours
target.review: This was pretty good, but it was a little bland. I think I'm going to play with it a bit to see what I can do. I think that it is a great starting point, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gnocchi

yum! that is all!

1. in large bowl , combine all ingredients and mix into a soft dough
2. turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead 20 times
3. divide dough into fourths and roll each quarter into a 12 inch long rope
4. cut each rope into inch pieces , and set on a floured surface
5. bring a large pot of salted water to a boil
6. roll each piece of dough across the tines of a fork to get groves on it and drop it into the pot of water
7. cook gnocchi until it floats to the top
8. drain and serve
demonstrations.review: Very simple, very flavorful gnocchi! Very similar to how they do it in Argentina. Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot chai chai chocolate

the spices in this hot chocolate are 

1. measure all ingredients up to marshmallows into a large bowl
2. with a fork , mash / mix the powdered ingredients
3. add marshmallows and chocolate chips
4. mix
5. measure approx
6. 1 / 3 cup into cup and add hot water to half fill cup
7. stir / blend vigorously
8. add hot water to fill cup and stir
demonstrations.review: We were very happy with this mix. I used fresh ground cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice and cloves. My wife really loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
warm orange spice drink for cold   flu

i created this drink when i felt a bad cold coming on, and wanted a tasty way to keep it at bay. oranges provide vitamin c, honey soothes sore throats, cinnamon helps relive nausea,  clove quells coughs, and ginger root aids in clearing the sinuses. also a delicious, warming beverage for those chilly winter days.

1. in a small saucepan , mix orange juice , water , ginger , cinnamon and clove over medium heat
2. once the mixture is hot , stir in honey until dissolved
3. pour into a mug and enjoy
demonstrations.review: This recipe couldn't have come at a better time for me. I have been fighting off a cold for a few days now and I can tell that this is definitely going to help me fight it off. I love the tangy flavor combination! Thank you for the great recipe! [Made & Reviewed for PAC Spring '09]

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maggiano s little italy chicken asiago soup  copycat

i am posting this recipe to try later.  i am always looking for great soups to make during winter months and this sounds different; but yummy!

1. in large pot over medium-high heat , heat oil
2. add onions and garlic and saute until light brown
3. lower heat and add celery , carrots , salt and pepper
4. saute until vegetables are tender
5. add rosemary and cook briefly
6. add broth and cooked chicken
7. stir in asiago and parmesan cheeses
8. simmer 10 minutes
9. adjust seasonings with salt and pepper if needed
10. serve immediately or cool in refrigerator
11. to serve: portion pasta , spinach and cheese for garnish into bottom of individual serving dishes
12. top with hot soup
demonstrations.review: This was really good. Next time I will probably cut down on the quantity of carrots and broth--to make it more to our family's taste. All in all, though, an excellent dish. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuscan sun pasta

a simple, quick and tasty pasta inspired by my meals in tuscany.

1. saute olive oil , peppers and herbs on medium heat for 4 minutes
2. add noodles and sauce , stir
3. continue to cook until just heated
4. strive for al dente noodles
5. serve
6. buon appetito !
demonstrations.review: Quick, Easy and Delicious! I roasted my garlic before adding it and it turned out great. Thanks for the great recipe! [Made & reviewed for PAC Spring 2009]

target.recipe_text:
the dagwood

this recipe originally came from 

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. butter bread and lightly toast
3. thinly slice the figs removing stems
4. cut loaf horizontally down the middle
5. spread all of the cream cheese on both sides of the bread
6. layer half of the figs , all of the ham , and turkey
7. add a small amount of olive oil and oregeno to taste
8. add all of the slices of cheddar and jack cheese on top
9. i criss cross them like a checker board
10. finally top with the remaining figs and put the top of the loaf on
11. cut vertically into 4-5 slices and serve
12. best served fresh while the bread is still warm from the toasting , but if you refrigerate and eat later , microwaving quickly seems to do the trick
target.review: Great sandwich.  Used yogurt cheese (labaneh) rather than cream cheese but otherwise followed the recipe.  Dh gobbled it.  Seems to qualify as good "dude food".  I'd recommend microwaving a little before serving whether you just toasted the bread or not.  It's not warm without it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rick s trout

this is what my husband makes that made me actually like trout, it is so easy and really very delicious, the green onion and cilantro give it an excellant flavor. for the serving size i will say 4 but obviously how ever many fish you have.

1. sprinkle the inside of the trout with salt and pepper and stuff with cilantro and onion
2. drizzle with oil
3. grill till done , approx 3-5 minutes each side
demonstrations.review: Easily prepared, great flavor and the best part was that Dh could  do it himself (with no coaching), including the grilling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab salad sandwiches

no this doesn't use real crabmeat but we think it is delicious nonetheless.

1. add the crabmeat , mayonnaise , green onions , and celery to a large mixing bowl
2. stir to combine
3. add the cheese , and salt / pepper to taste
4. stir to combine
5. spread the crab mixture over the bottom of the bread
6. replace top of bread
7. wrap sandwich in a big piece of heavy foil
8. bake at 400 for 20 minutes or until heated
9. cut into slices and serve
demonstrations.review: Got a surprize gift of a 6 oz cup of Dungeness crab that needed to be used right away.  Followed your reduced recipe w/ lowfat versions, spread it on Wasa (substantial wholegrain sandwich-sized crackers) and popped them under the broiler for a couple of minutes.  Lunch fit for a princess!  Soooo good, proportions are perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked beans don t get any better than this

these are my all-time favorite baked beans (and i've tried plenty). "it don't get any better than this".

1. fry bacon
2. remove from pan and set aside
3. when cooled , break up into small pieces
4. in the bacon grease , cook ground beef and onions until beef is no longer pink
5. mix all the ingredients together , stir well
6. pour in a 9 x 13 baking dish
7. bake at 350 for about 1 hour
8. these are sweet baked beans
9. you may cut back or eliminate the brown sugar according to your tastes
demonstrations.review: Who knew baked beans could be so easy to make with so few ingredients?  I used half the listed sugar and will use even less next time.  It was very hot here so I made them in the crockpot.  They were a bit soupy but that didn't seem to be a problem.  They're all gone.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole wheat pizza crust

this is so good. even my kids and dh will eat this crust.

1. mix water , oil , honey and yeast
2. add wheat gluton , garlic powder and two cups of the flour
3. if you are using a mixer like a bosch , dimension or a kitchenaid you add additional flour until the sides of the mixer come clean
4. knead about 7 minutes in your mixer
5. if mixing by hand add one cup at a time until the right consistence and knead until smooth and elastic
6. if you choose you can let the dough rise but i just divide the dough and half and roll out one on my pizza stone
7. after you roll the dough out pierce the rolled out pizza dough with a fork
8. bake the pizza crust 450 degrees for about five minutes
9. add your toppings such as sauce and cheese or whatever you want on pizza and then put back into the oven at 450 for about 10 minutes
10. repeat for the second crust
demonstrations.review: Very good crust.  This made two 12" pizzas of what I would consider medium thickness.  Mine only took 10 minutes to bake and I skipped the initial 5 minute baking time. I had minimal toppings, though.  I froze the second pizza for one of those evenings when I don't want to cook.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest ahi tuna ever

i came up with this the first time i purchased an ahi tuna steak to make at home.  for me, less is more when it comes to ahi because i really love the flavor of the fish.  this recipe is super easy and it makes a great presentation over a baby spinach salad.

1. rub the steak with one tbs of the olive oil
2. put the peppercorns on a plate and press the tuna steak into the peppercorns until it is coated
3. sprinkle the steak with salt to taste
4. heat the other tbs of olive oil in a non-stick pan on medium high heat
5. cook the steak 2-3 minutes per side
6. slice the steak into 1 / 4" slices and serve over salad or rice
7. cooking a tuna steak for 2-3 minutes per side will leave the middle quite rare , and barely warm
8. you could cook the fish longer until it is well done , but then you would basically spending a lot of money on a cut of fish that is meant to be served rare or raw
demonstrations.review: The title of this recipe should read Easiest and BEST Ahi Tuna Ever. We followed the recipe exactly except we used the grill.  The baby greens salad accompaniment is a wonderful suggestion. Wonderful.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
target.review: How have I not already reviewed this and given it 1,000 stars??  This recipe is absolutely incredible.  A staple in my house after having first made it 8 - 9 months ago.  Kittencal, you sir, are a magician.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review:
Excellent dish! I find myself craving this randomly throughout the day, lol.

A few things I've noticed:
I find that I need a lot more seasoning than the recipe calls for to coat my chicken pieces. I like to have them smothered in it.

Also, and this is a big one... Not all cajun seasonings are created equal! Some go from very mild to quite spicy. The reviewer below me a few places said their's tasted bland. I bet it was your seasoning. McCormack's seasoning (the line Safeway carries out west here) is very spicy, and perfect for this dish.
I made it once with another brand and was very disappointed! Was far too mild.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: Loved it!  Huge hit at work.  I use slightly less sugar, sligtly more crumbs for a denser bar.  I may also try using honey roasted PB next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic baked ziti

this baked ziti recipe is a simple italian casserole dish that my family enjoys.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large skillet , cook ground beef , onions , and garlic over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes or until beef is browned
3. stirring frequently
4. stir in spaghetti sauce , chicken broth , and oregano
5. reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes
6. stir 1 cup of the sauce into the cooked ziti noodles
7. spoon 1 / 2 of the ziti mixture into a 13x9x2-inch baking dish
8. sprinkle with 1 1 / 2 cups mozzarella cheese and 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese
9. top with 2 cups sauce , then remaining ziti mixture and remaining sauce
10. cover and bake 20 minutes
11. sprinkle with remaining mozzarella and parmesan cheese
12. return to oven and bake uncovered for 10 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: Amazing!  We used Classico brand garlic & onion pasta sauce for the sauce, and followed the rest of the recipe exactly.  Will definitely be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flawless sesame chicken  restaurant style

this is the recipe you've been looking for!  it makes a perfect sesame chicken.  this excellent recipe comes out perfect every time with little fuss and inexpensive ingredients you probably have on hand.  this recipe is truly restaurant quality... try it, you won't be disappointed! (recipe courtesy of "reykjaviky" at all recipes)

1. cut the chicken into 1-inch cubes
2. mix the marinade ingredients and marinate the chicken for 20 minutes
3. to prepare the sauce:
4. mix together all of the sauce ingredients
5. pour them into a small pot and bring to a boil , stirring continuously
6. turn the heat down to low and keep warm while you are deep-frying the chicken
7. to deep-fry the chicken:
8. add the marinated chicken pieces a few at a time , and deep-fry until golden brown
9. drain on paper towels and then place chicken in warm oven while you continue frying
10. repeat with the remainder of the chicken
11. just before you are finished deep-frying , bring the sauce back up to a boil
12. place the chicken on a large platter and pour the sauce over
13. sprinkle with sesame seeds
14. serve the sesame chicken with rice
demonstrations.review:
Excellent!!
I would suggest doubling the marinade recipe though if you're making 3 chicken breasts. Breadding lightly after marinading also works well. Will make again for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken stuffed poblano chiles

this is an attractive and tasty dish.  these are not your ordinary stuffed peppers.  serve on top of saffron rice with a side salad for a spicy meal.

1. while using gloves , wash the poblano chilies and using a sharp paring knife , cut a slit lengthwise from stem to
2. carefully cut away the seeds and membrane rinse the inside of the chilies and set aside
3. in a large skillet over medium high heat , warm 1 tablespoon of the olive oil , add chopped onions and garlic
4. cook until onions begin to turn golden , stirring frequently
5. add the diced chicken , sprinkle with seasoning salt and cook until chicken is almost cooked through
6. add tomato and mushrooms , continue to cook until chicken is done
7. preheat oven to 350 degrees and spray a 2 quart casserole dish with non-stick cooking spray
8. with remaining tablespoon olive oil , lightly oil the outside of the chilies and place them cut side up in casserole dish
9. pack the chicken mixture into chilies and push cheese into mixture along the slit
10. cover dish , place in preheated oven and bake for 35 to 40 minutes
11. remove cover the last 5 to 10 minutes of cooking
12. serve on top of a bed of saffron rice
demonstrations.review: Made these last night, and although they were good, they were lacking in....something.  Not at all bad, just a bit on the bland side for our tastes.  I will definitely make these again however, and try something different with spices.

target.recipe_text:
baked brie and red pepper jelly wrapped in phyllo pastry

this is a nice twist to the traditional baked brie in puff pastry. i find that the phyllo lends to a more elegant presentation. phyllo is not that tricky to work with - just keep the sheets that you aren't working with covered with plastic wrap and a damp towel. we traditionally use a 300 gram wheel of triple cream brie, which converts to about .66 of a pound. because of the size of the phyllo sheets (about 12" x 18"), you could likely use up to a pound of brie.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. place brie on flat surface and with sharp knife , slice brie in half horizontally
3. spread red pepper jelly on bottom half of brie and then replace top half of brie and set aside
4. using a pastry brush , brush butter on first sheet of phyllo , place a second sheet on top at roughly a 30 degree angle , brush with butter , place third sheet on top at roughly a 30 degree angle from the first , brush with butter and continue until all sheets have been used
5. place brie in centre of phyllo and gently pull all the sheets up and over the brie , twisting closed at the top
6. arrange the sheets in the"twist" in various directions
7. brush entire package with melted butter
8. bake for 30-35 minutes
9. set aside for 5-10 minutes before serving
10. serve with crackers or thinly sliced baguette
target.review: excellent awesome very sophisticated dish we all loved it even my red neck friends

demonstrations.recipe_text:
speedy white chicken enchiladas

this is a quick and simple chicken enchilada recipe.  don't remember where the original came from, as i have tweaked it over the years into this recipe.

1. mix soup and sour cream and set aside
2. heat butter in medium saucepan
3. add onions and chili powder and cook until onions are tender
4. add the canned chicken and chilis and 3 tablespoons of the sauce mixture
5. spread 1 / 2 cup of the soup mixture into a 9x13 pan
6. spoon mixture into tortillas , roll up , and place on top of the soup mixture
7. spread remaining sauce mixture on top , and cover with cheese
8. bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes -- or until cheese is bubbly and browning
9. suggestion: one can use chopped / shredded leftover chicken rather than canned chicken
10. suggestion: serve with salsa and chips for a great meal !
11. suggestion: this is a very forgiving dish
12. i have added black olives , used less chicken , doubled the sauce mixture , upped the spice factor , etc
13. you can easily tweak this recipe to your liking
demonstrations.review: excellent we love this recipe. I did not have 2 chicken soup cans so I used 1 chicken and 1 mushroom soup with that it even tasted good. will have this again and again and again ....... and again. awesome awesome

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bolla s peanut stew

when i was in college a friend of mine taught me how to make this. he was from "the gambia" and told me they make it there with either fish or chicken. i have only made it with chicken and every time i serve it to someone new they ask for 2 things. first they want seconds and second they want the recipe. i did see a very close recipe to this printed about 5 years after bolla taught me. it appeared in betty crocker's recipe cards. enjoy

1. in a large skillet over medium heat , saute the pepper and onions in oil until tender
2. while sauteing the veggies , in a medium bowl blend the tomato paste , peanut butter , broth and seasonings
3. add broth mixture and chicken to the onion and pepper still in the skillet
4. cook and stir over low heat until heated through
5. serve over rice
demonstrations.review:
It was ok. added garlic & hot sauce
Will I make it again? not sure. It was fun to try something that was from Gambia.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun jalapeno poppers

this recipe came from taste testing poppers all over. i combined what i liked and discarded the rest. you can use fresh peppers or prepackaged peppers (not recommended,to soft). if i use fresh, i sometimes like to slice them in half, leaving the stem, de-vein and seed them and saute' them in my favorite beer to soften them up just a little (2-4 minutes). another tip is to always use protective cooking gloves when dealing with peppers.

1. halve the jalapenos leaving the stem attached , de-vein and seed them
2. setting the halved jalapenos and bread crumbs aside , mix all of the other ingredients together
3. take your mixture and completely fill the jalepeno cavities to their brim and set aside
4. put bread crumbs on a flat plate
5. take jalapeno halves , one at a time , and roll cheese side only in bread crumbs and place cheese / crumb side up on a baking pan once completed if you like a thick crumb layer , you can repeat this step
6. if you do not intend to bake finished product skip the rolling part and just lightly sprinkle the top of the jalepenos with the bread crumbs
7. bake at 350 for 15 minutes or until mixture starts to bubble
8. i like to refrigerate at least 1 hour prior to baking sometimes i prepare the day before , cover and refrigerate
9. serve warm , room temperature or chilled with any or all of the recommended sauces
demonstrations.review:
loved it and so did all the other New York Giants fans on Super bowl sunday 
Feb 3, 2008
will make it again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best snickerdoodles i have ever eaten

"this must be one of the best cookies i have ever eaten." yep, that's what my mother said the first time i ever made this cookie. it is a great cookie recipe, and not difficult to make at all. i tripled the recipe and took it to school to sell... i sold all of them with in an 80 minute time span to only 4 people. they are good cookies, i can't resist them whenever i make them. and they turn out so nice whenever you bake them, it's hard to make an ugly snickerdoodle. lol. enjoy. (prep time is estimated)

1. in a large bowl , cream butter and sugars at high speed
2. add egg , vanilla , and beat until smooth
3. in another bowl , combine flour , salt , baking soda , and cream of tartar
4. pour dry ingredients into the wet ingredients , mix well
5. preheat oven to 300 while you let dough rest 30-60 minutes in fridge
6. in a small bowl combine topping
7. take about 2 1 / 2 tablespoons of dough and roll it into a ball
8. roll this dough in the cinnamon / sugar mixture and press onto greased cookie sheet
9. bake cookies 10-12 minutes , no more
10. cookies may seem undercooked but will develop
11. don't roll your dough into too big of a ball
12. they may not turn out in that much time if you do that
13. it happened to me
14. lol
15. if the cookies don't turn out , please try again
16. it's a very good cookie , it's just all a matter of getting the cooking time right
demonstrations.review:
These are the very best Snicker doodles I have ever made. Thank you so very much it made my day on December 15, 2008.
Did I say thank you oh I guess I did........ merry xmas

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken wellington  puff pastry wrapped chicken

this is not at all hard to put together, it's an amazing dish to serve to dinner guests and i have done so many times over the years and have always receive rave reviews from everyone at my table and you will too! --- to save time saute the onion, garlic and mushrooms up to a day ahead,  the cream cheese and dijon mustard mixture may be increased slightly -- i always serve this with recipe#149547 drizzled over or on the side of the plate, you will *love* this!

1. season the chicken breast with seasoning salt and pepper on all sides
2. heat butter and oil in a skillet
3. brown the breasts on all sides until almost completely cooked through
4. transfer to a plate
5. to the same skillet add in onions , garlic and sliced mushrooms
6. saute until the mushrooms lose their moisture and the onions are tender
7. stir in parsley
8. on a floured surface , roll out each puff pastry sheet to a 14-inch square
9. cut into four even 7-inch squares
10. place each breast over each puff pastry square
11. set oven to 375 degrees
12. in a small bowl combine the softened cream cheese with mustard , then spread over each breast
13. then top with about 2-3 tablespoons mushroom / onion mixture
14. brush the edges of each pastry square with water
15. wrap pastry around the chicken breast , pressing edges to seal tightly
16. place seam-side down on greased baking sheets
17. brush the tops with egg wash
18. bake for about 20 minutes , or until puffed and golden brown
19. serve with mushroom sauce over the wellington or on the side of the plate
20. delicious !
demonstrations.review: The best I made it for a family dinner Awesome. I did not use all the cream cheese. I will have this again and again, great flavor.

target.recipe_text:
easy black beans and rice

using canned beans makes this dish not just quick and easy but delish! and you have everything in your cabinet so make it now!

1. in a stockpot over medium-high heat , heat the oil
2. add the onion , pepper and garlic and saute for 4 minutes
3. add the rice and saute for 2 minutes
4. add the vegetable broth , bring to a boil , cover and lower the heat and cook for 20 minutes
5. add the spices and black beans
target.review: My husband had 2 helpings! It is a regular from now on! Thanks for the great recipe! M. Sutphen

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican rice casserole

a great way to use a pound of ground beef and make a dinner that all will love.  it's so easy too!  if you cannot find mexicorn by green giant, you can use a regular can of corn or frozen corn.  to control the heat of the dish, you can choose mild, medium or hot salsa!

1. place the 2 cups of water and long grain rice in a medium sauce pan and bring to a boil
2. reduce heat to a simmer , place a lid on , set timer for 20 minutes and cook rice until done
3. preheat oven to 350f
4. in a skillet , brown ground beef and drain
5. place in a large mixing bowl
6. in large mixing bowl , add the jar of salsa to the ground beef
7. also add chili powder , mexicorn , rice and salt
8. mix with a wooden spoon until combined well
9. spray a 2 quart casserole dish
10. put rice mixture into dish
11. cover with a lid or foil and bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes
12. at 30 minutes , take off lid / foil
13. add shredded cheddar cheese evenly over top and bake for an additional 5 minutes
14. remove from oven and serve
demonstrations.review: excellent! Try it soon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked brie in puff pastry with apricot or raspberry preserves

this baked brie puff pastry is rich, creamy, and dessert-like. it always disappears. i'm always asked for the recipe. raspberry preserves goes great in this as well. bringing in 2012 i made this using recipe #463563!

1. preheat oven to 425
2. lightly grease cookie sheet
3. roll puff pastry out slightly
4. place cheese wheel on top
5. place preserves on top of cheese
6. place almonds on top of preserves
7. bundle puff pastry up and around the cheese
8. bake for 20-25 minutes
9. let cool for five minutes
10. serve with your favorite crackers
demonstrations.review: Excellent !!! Used Mushrooms instead of jam, everyone scoffed it up! Thanks for a great treat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jan s reuben casserole

if you like the reuben sandwich you will love this casserole.

1. line bottom of 9x13 pan with frozen peirogie
2. spread sauerkraut on top
3. add the corned beef
4. top with thousand island dressing
5. top all with provolone cheese
6. bake at 350 deg
7. for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review:
My husband just loves all of the above items that composed this dish. He and I think it is a 5!
Thanks MewMew for a great dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet bbq pressure cooker  grilled chicken

this is a combination of two recipes that i have used.  i have been obsessed with my pressure cooker lately and thought this would bring tenderness and juiciness to grilled bbq chicken.  it turned out awesome!

1. combine nutmeg , cinnamon , ginger , salt , and pepper
2. rub into meat
3. in separate container combine beer , water , and chicken bouillon
4. pour into pressure cooker
5. place chicken into cooker and cook at 15 lbs pressure for 20 minutes
6. use the natural release method
7. put the chicken on the grill
8. cook for 10 minutes
9. brush chicken with barbecue sauce and cook for an additional 5 minutes
10. a little time consuming but worth the effort !
demonstrations.review: The best, you must try it1

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lori b s chili

i'm not a chili fan but a friend gave me this recipe and this is the only one i make now. it makes a big pot but it freezes well.

1. brown hamburger and onion
2. while browning hamburger , put the rest of the ingredients into a large pot
3. drain hamburger and add to pot
4. simmer on low heat for 30 minutes
5. can also be made in the crock pot
6. i normally make this without the chili sauce because i have the other ingredients on hand
7. put into soup bowls , sprinkle with some cheese and enjoy
demonstrations.review: Excellent! A very good keeper, handy to have from the freezer for unexpected friends who drop around!

target.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
target.review: Best apple pie I've ever tasted! Prebaked my crust 8-10 min, used 5 fugi apples & 4 Tbls of flour. Added the pecans in the last 10 min of baking to toast them a bit. Left off the caramel cause the pie was sweet enough although I will try it with some time. Fantastic! Thank you for sharing Wendy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christmas rum balls or bourbon balls

these balls are so quick and easy to make. they make a nice addition to the baked goodies that you give as gifts. make these about a week before you want to serve them as they mellow and the sharp strong alcohol taste blends  in more with the other ingredients. store in a tin with a tight lid.  this year i couldn't find the vanilla wafers so i used chocolate and i like them even more.  to form the balls i use two teaspoons as the dough is quite moist.  i store them in the freezer - they don't go hard and they are so good ice cold

1. sift the cocoa with 1 cup sugar
2. stir in the spiced rum mixed with the syrup
3. add crushed vanilla wafers and nuts
4. mix thoroughly
5. shape mixture into walnut sizes balls and dredge with remaining sugar or leave them plain
6. store in a tin
demonstrations.review: These were great! I made these as a last minute thought for a party- Since I didn't have time to let the rum mellow, I used Kahlua instead of rum and boy were they good! No mellowing time needed! The Kahlua was not too strong and the flavor mixed so well with the cocoa....I'm thinking to try Irish cream next. Thanks Bergy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted cauliflower   16 roasted cloves of garlic

i find it totally amazing, that children and men all  love this recipe!  as for the female of our species we just love this for the flavor and the health benefits it brings our families.
roasted brings out a wonderful sweetness in this dish. the garlic is roasted to a tan color is creamy good. you can just pop them in your mouth. or you can spread them on your florets or fresh bread. just be sure to scoop up some of the rosemary, olive oil and black pepper that may have escaped to the bottom of the dish.
for halloween check out recipe #396674 version of my recipe.

1. mix oil , rosemary , salt , pepper and garlic together
2. toss in cauliflower and place in a large casserole dish in one layer
3. roast in a preheated oven at 450 degrees for 20 minutes
4. give a toss and bake for 10 more minutes
demonstrations.review: Oh Rita! This was so good! I didn't have rosemary so I sub'd a combo of dried basil, oregano, parsley, cajun seasoning, & red pepper flakes and used 30+ garlic cloves. The amt of olive oil is perfect. Better flavor & healthier than other recipes I've tried yet so easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken  shrimp and andouille jambalaya

a cajun classic, meal in one pot! have the hot sauce ready to splash on. serve with some crusty french bread, a nice crisp salad, and some of your favorite wine. :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large pan or dutch oven , brown chicken in hot oil on both sides
3. remove and drain
4. add andouille , onion , celery , bell pepper , thyme , oregano , paprika , salt , and cayenne pepper to the pan , cooking and stirring for about 5 minutes until onions are tender
5. add rice , tomatoes with juice , and broth
6. bring to a boil
7. place rice mixture in a baking dish or oven-proof casserole
8. top with chicken
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees f for 40-45 minutes or until rice and chicken are done and tender
10. stir in shrimp , parsley , and green onions
11. cover and cook 5-8 minutes longer or until shrimp curl and turn bright pink and serve
demonstrations.review: Wow! This is the best Jambalaya recipe I've made. Tons of flavor. I added cumin & dried basil, 2 tbs of worcestershire sauce & 1 cup of frozen peas tossed in with my shrimp at the end. Didn't have andouille so I used precooked hot links & precooked turkey breast cubed up instead of chicken. It was easy to put together. Everyone at the table gave it a raving 5 stars! Thanks Sue!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
addictive mexican stew

my mother gave me this recipe.  she found it while clipping coupons.  it is from s&w.  this is the best stew i have ever eaten and my family requests me to make it quite frequently.  it has become a 

1. cook onion and garlic in oil in large saucepan until tender
2. add cooked chicken , taco seasoning , tomatoes , beans , corn and chilies
3. blend broth and cornstarch
4. add to saucepan
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes
7. stirring occasionally
8. serve with cornbread for a hearty meal
demonstrations.review: Wonderful 30 minute recipe that tastes like you cooked it all day. So versatile too. I used white canellini beans.  Next time I will try it with fresh tomatoes to cut down on the sodium. Served on some left over white rice. Everyone loved it. Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
uncle bill s whipped shortbread cookies

these are very easy to make shortbread cookies. they are so good that they melt in your mouth, you hardly have to chew them. i have been making them for over 35 years.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a mixing bowl and using an electric mixer , combine butter , flour , icing sugar and vanilla extract
3. mix until mixture is a smooth consistency
4. prepare cookie sheets with parchment paper
5. spoon out dough onto parchment lined cookie sheets by teaspoonfuls or by tablespoons for larger cookies , spacing about 2 inches apart
6. cut maraschino cherries into quarters and place one piece in the middle of each cookie , alternating with red and green cherries
7. bake in preheated 350 f oven for 13 to 15 minutes or until bottom of cookies are lightly browned , do not overbake
8. remove from oven and let cool on cookie sheet for about 5 minutes
9. transfer onto wire racks to finish cooling
10. store in a container with a lid and separate each layer with wax paper
11. use sprinkles , half an almond or half a cashew or chocolate to the top of the cookies before baking
12. a thumbprint in the cookie , filled with your choice of jam is very tasty
13. it has been suggested that the cookies be refrigerated for at least 1 / 2 hour before baking for a different texture
demonstrations.review: These were so easy to make. I made a small well and added a dollop of my homemade pineapple-apricot filling. They turned out great! I made mine a little larger so I doubled the recipe and got about 4 dozen. Thanks Uncle Bill!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot caramelized onion pot roast

this is one of our favorite recipes for crock pot roast. it's easy and a little different than the usual crock pot roasts. i got the recipe off the internet and i wish i could thank the original poster for a great recipe!

1. brown the meat , remove from frying pan to plate
2. add oil to pan and cook onions until brown
3. add broth , juice , brown sugar , vinegar and mustard to onions in pan
4. put half of the onion mixture in crock pot and place the roast on top
5. cover with the rest of the onions
6. cook on low 8 to 9 hours
target.review: Wonderful to come home to.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
aegean beans

a nice vegetable dish to go with lamb or fish.

1. 1
2. slice beans into bite-size pieces
3. 2
4. microwave 6 minutes
5. 3
6. chop tomatoes
7. 4
8. dice onions
9. 4
10. crumble cheese and mix with oil and lemon juice
11. 5
12. toss all ingredients together
13. 6
14. salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: Yummy.  Served with pork chops.  Nice change from just green beans.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked bourbon chicken

this is rich-tasting but fairly simple to make. i got this recipe from the houston chronicle sometime in the early 1990s. it was submitted by a retired chef named ken olszewski in response to a reader request or a recipe challenge. i like to garnish this with parsley so i can sing 

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. brown chicken in skillet
3. remove chicken from skillet and place into a baking dish
4. in the same skillet , combine garlic , cayenne , sugar , salt , sage , rosemary , thyme , and flour
5. add bourbon and whisk to combine
6. remove from heat
7. pour sauce over chicken in baking dish
8. cover dish and place in oven
9. bake 1 hour or until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: This was good, just not as wow as I expected (the smell while they cooked was fantastic).  Used large skinless chicken breasts, maybe they should have been cut smaller? Or maybe I should have basted them?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old time baked beans

these are the beans my french-canadian mother used to make. she never measured anything making these so i've estimated the amounts. these taste great with fresh bread. a good dish to keep in mind for pot-lucks. you can add pork or weiners to it if you like. bacon strips on top work well.

1. soak beans overnight in water , then boil until tender
2. drain water and put beans in a large heavy pot or crock
3. add all ingredients together and mix
4. add enough water to cover beans
5. cover and bake at 325 degrees for about 6 hours
6. check beans while they are baking to add water to ensure they do not go dry
demonstrations.review: These were too sweet for our taste, and no one wanted to eat them.  Extra salt really helped.  Next time I would half the brown sugar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingered strawberry tart

i saw this recipe in taste of home and it looked so pretty and delicious i couldn't resist trying it and posting it here to share. it is a very elegant looking dessert but so simple to make. the gingersnap crust is such a perfect complement to the strawberries. a scrumptious dessert without a lot of calories. i'm sure it will taste even more delicious when strawberries are in season. prep time does not include time for chilling.

1. in food processor , combine the gingersnaps , 2 t sugar and butter
2. cover and process until blended
3. press onto the bottom and up the sides of a 9-inch or 10-inch fluted tart pan with a removable bottom
4. set aside
5. in a large saucepan , combine the cornstarch , ginger if desired and remaining sugar
6. stir in the chopped strawberries and water
7. bring to a boil
8. cook and stir for 2 minutes
9. reduce heat
10. simmer , uncovered , for 4-6 minutes or until thickened
11. cool for 30 minutes
12. pour into crust
13. cover and refrigerate 2 hours or until set
14. arrange sliced berries over filling
15. in a small microwave-safe bowl , heat jam on high for 15-20 seconds or until pourable
16. brush over berries
17. remove sides from tart pan
18. top with whipped cream , if desired
19. refrigerate until ready to serve
20. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was desert on Mother's Day.  I skipped the crystallized ginger but it was still great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
canadian living s mushroom chicken

i am now using recipezaar to store recipes i want to try, including this one. what a great way to share!

1. in a clean plastic bag , combine flour and pepper
2. add chicken
3. shake to coat
4. reserve remaining flour mixture
5. in a large skillet , heat oil over medium-high heat
6. brown chicken all over , about 10 minutes
7. remove to plate and set aside
8. add onion and garlic to skillet
9. cook over medium heat for 3 minutes
10. add mushrooms , carrots , basil , and salt
11. cook for a few minutes , just until vegetables are tender
12. sprinkle in reserved flour mixture
13. stir in stock and vinegar and bring to boil
14. return chicken to pan
15. reduce heat , cover and simmer , stirring occasionally , for 35 minutes or until juices run clear when chicken is pierced
16. serve sprinkled with parsley
demonstrations.review: This recipe has been on my to-try list for months.  It's a keeper.  Great served with mashed potatoes.

target.recipe_text:
shelleys best ever caesar salad

this is a recipie that i invented by tase and error...my family would have this everyday for supper if i made it....i have only shared it with a few people and they all have ditched their other caesar salad recipies and now are using this one....its awesome and a real surprise full of taste ! the heat can be turned up or down and the garlic can be adjusted.....the amount i am posting feeds my son and husband each a very large bowl...enjoy

1. put everything into a jar or container and shake the heck out of it
2. place in fridge for at least an hour to blend
3. pour over salad and let sit for at least 10 minutes
4. add bacon bits , sliced mushrooms and croutons
5. top with fresh grated parmesan cheese --
target.review: Wow, what a great dressing!  I'm a salad lover anyway and this dressing was just wonderful!!!  Thank you for posting, and I look forward to seeing more of your recipes here!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple pecan coleslaw

this is a sweet tasting coleslaw, nice change for a hot summer day.  got the recipe from publix grocery store and just had to share

1. place pecans in a small saute pan on medium high , cook and stir 3 to 4 minutes or until fragrant
2. drain the pineable reserving 1 / 4 cup juice place the juice and the slaw dressing in a large bowl and whisk until blended
3. stir in the remaining ingredients until evenly coated
4. chill for 2hours , stirring often
5. if it seems dry add a bit more slaw dressing
6. it will create more juice the longer it chills
demonstrations.review: This coleslaw is easy to make and it is quite good.  It is definitely a sweet coleslaw, so if you aren't into the extra sweetness, you might skip this one.  I thought the pineapple was a quite good addition.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best deviled eggs

these have been a favorite for years, when i serve these at my get togethers or make them for socials and large events they are always the first to go and everyone wants the recipe, i suggest to use large, extra large or even jumbo eggs for this, i like to make the yolk filling a day ahead and refrigerate this will blend the flavors --- for a nice presentation place each egg half in a colored paper muffin liner --- all ingredient amounts may be adjusted to taste --- see my recipe#259573

1. slice the eggs in half lengthwise
2. remove the yolks , and set whites aside
3. in a small bowl , mush yolks well with a fork , leaving no small lumps
4. add next 10 ingredients mix well to combine
5. spoon or pipe egg yolk mixture evenly into the whites
6. sprinkle with paprika
7. cover tightly with plastic wrap
8. store in the refrigerator until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: Wonderful deviled eggs and easy too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barley soup

this recipe came from somewhere way in my past. it came from a family that my step-sister was going to marry into. it is a very comforting soup.  it was originally made with chicken stock, but i made it vegetarian for myself.  great soup.  takes awhile to cook but worth it.  freezes well. even better the next day.

1. wash barley and let soak in 1 cup of water for 1 hour
2. cook until soft and fluffy
3. while that is cooking in a skillet saute onion and garlic in the oil
4. take 2 / 3 of cooked barley and blend in blender , food processor , or hand blender
5. mix remaining barley with blended barley
6. add vegetable broth and milk
7. put back on stove and bring to a boil
8. mix cornstarch with water or milk and add to broth and milk
9. cook to desired consistency adding broth as needed
10. add salt and pepper to taste
11. ladle into bowls and serve with a sprinkle of vinegar on the top of soup
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I made this last week when it was chilly and grey outside. I loved it! So did my husband. We're both big soup fans and this one did not disappoint! Great as is. You could easily add other ingredients if you wanted. I love the milk added. I used rice milk so it would be a vegan dish. Terrific!  bbblampwork, you need to post more of these terrific recipes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hummus bi tahina

this recipe is slightly modified from "the complete cooking light" cookbook. this is great served with pita wedges or raw veggies. i like to garnish it with a spritz of olive oil and paprika.

1. drain chickpeas , reserving 1 / 4 cup liquid , and set aside
2. process garlic 10 seconds in food processor or until minced
3. add chickpeas , reserved 1 / 4 cup liquid , tahini , lemon juice and water
4. process 3 minutes or until smooth , scraping sides of bowl occasionally
5. spoon tahini mixture into a serving bowl
6. serve immediately or cover and chill
7. nutrition information : 44 cal , 1
8. 8 g fat , 2
9. 4 g pro , 5
10. 5 g carb , 1
11. 1 g fiber , 0 mg chol , 0
12. 7 mg iron , 74 mg sod , 28 mg calc , 1 ww point
demonstrations.review: This recipe is terrific! I like it much better than the stuff in the store.  It is less expensive, you know what you're putting in it and it tastes fabulous!  Thanks for the recipe Columbus!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple crumble tarts

i got this recipe in betty crockers cookbook, a reprint actually, that was from a very old book. it was for a pie and i only had 12 tarts so i changed it and modified it and yum yum....we had them for ukranian christmas dessert and my husband and son told me to write  it down before i forget what i did....so enjoy please...

1. pre heat oven to 375
2. peel and dice apples , put into bowl
3. mix next 3 ingredients together and pour over apples and stir well
4. fill uncooked tart shells high and place on cookie sheet
5. combine next 3 ingredients and crumble over filled tarts
6. sprinkle with chopped walnuts
7. bake for 20-25 minutes or until nicely browned
8. remove and place on wire racks
9. serve with your choice of ice cream , cheese or whipping cream or just eat as is --
demonstrations.review: Shelley you really should post more recipes as the ones I've tried for Spring PAC 2012 have been outstanding!! And this one is certainly not a disappointment.  The tarts came out wonderful and made my kitchen smell like heaven.  Plus they taste absolutely fabulous.  Definitely a 5 star recipe!

target.recipe_text:
boneless pork chops milanese

you can put these chops together, cover and refrigerate and cook at dinner time.  this is a really quick and delicious recipe courtesy of giada delaurentis.

1. coarsely crush the panko and place in a large shallow bowl
2. stir the cheese into the panko
3. lightly beat the eggs in another large shallow bowl
4. sprinkle the pork generously with salt and pepper
5. dip the pork , 1 piece at a time , in the egg , then dredge the pork in the crumb mixture , patting to coat completely
6. heat 1 / 4 cup of oil in a heavy large skillet over medium-high heat
7. add the pork to the hot oil and cook until golden brown and just cooked through , about 3 minutes per side
8. transfer to paper towels to drain
9. transfer the pork to plates and serve with lemon wedges
target.review: This was really good! I omitted the lemons and instead made a reduction of fresh lemon juice, white wine, capers and butter. I served it with broiled asparagus and peppers marinated in lemon juice, garlic, rosemary and olive oil. Perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy honey garlic ribs

you will love these there are better than any restaurant and the recipe may be doubled

1. set oven to 300 to 325 degrees
2. slice ribs into individual pieces
3. in a large bowl , combine honey , soy sauce vinegar , fresh minced garlic and brown sugar
4. stir until honey and brown sugar are completely dissolved
5. stir in the baking soda
6. transfer ribs to the bowl
7. turn to coat
8. cover a cookie sheet with foil , and arrange the ribs meat side up on the sheet
9. pour the excess sauce all over them , and sprinkle with garlic salt
10. bake for 1 hour , turning every 20 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Very good! Even though I omitted the brown sugar I found these started to burn a bit at 375 F so I lowered the temperature to 300 F and left them in a bit longer and they cooked up fine. 
Cheers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice noodles with ginger and snow peas

in this beautiful dish, nearly transparent noodles mingle with shimmering snow peas and shredded carrots. from vegetarian times cookbook.

1. soak or prepare the rice noodles according to the package directions
2. drain and set aside
3. heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat , and cook the ginger and garlic , stirring , for 1 to 2 minutes
4. add the scallions , chili , carrots and snow peas
5. cook , stirring , for 2 minutes
6. stir in the salt
7. add the noodles and toss to coat
8. remove from the heat
9. stir in the sesame and chili oil
10. garnish with cilantro or parsley
11. serve at once
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Very tasty and simple to make. I had no hot chili oil so I used tabasco sauce and it worked just fine. I'll be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seared ahi tuna glazed with wasabi butter

i've always loved wasabi with tuna, but usually the wasabi overpowers such a delicate fish. when this recipe came to me through a friend, who doesn't recall its origins, i finally found the perfect marriage of flavors. i can't make this often enough!

1. drizzle sesame oil on both sides of each tuna steaks
2. season with salt and pepper
3. combine remaining ingredients in a small sauce pan
4. heat over low heat until butter is melted , stirring constantly to mix and prevent scorching
5. while sauce is heating , heat a heavy frying pan on another burner with high heat
6. place tuna in pan and sear until crispy and brown
7. turn and sear on the other side
8. folks who like their tuna steaks more well-done may want to sear their tuna for 4-5 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: As others have mentioned, I found it a bit salty, but quite tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wonderful salsa

this is the best salsa recipe i've found so far and i've tried about a dozen. i got it from one of the local hospital cookbooks that are sold in my area. i changed it a bit and have been canning it for years. the reason i plant a garden is for this salsa. we would be lost without it. hope you like it as much as we do.  one of our members who is a food scientist took this salsa to work, tested the ph and found it measured under 4.0 (well within the safety limit for boiling water bath processing).

1. mix all together and bring to a slow boil for 10 minute
2. seal in jars and cook in hot water bath for 10 minute
3. this is a medium salsa
4. this is also a chunky salsa so if you want a smoother salsa cut your veggies into smaller pieces
5. yields 3-6 quarts or pints
demonstrations.review:
Outstanding - I added 1/2 cup of minced cilantro, and used poblano peppers (warm but mild) instead of sweet green peppers. I also cut the sugar to 1 tbsp as suggested by others. Result was TOO GOOD! Will freeze the rest, also suggested by others.
Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
all purpose stir fry sauce  brown garlic sauce

adapted from martin yan's chinese cooking for dummies. this is my favorite stir-fry sauce. it makes enough for two meals. having extra on hand makes for a quick meal. my son will actually eat vegetables he can dip in the sauce! warning about the amount of soy sauce. when i used kikkoman soy sauce, i found this sauce far too salty. i now use angostura, which is much lower in salt. when adding soy sauce, start with less than half the amount and slowly add more to taste. using vegetable broth makes this vegetarian. yield: 1 3/4 cups (couldn't get that amount entered)

1. in a bowl , combine soy sauce , broth , rice wine , sugar , sesame oil and white pepper
2. dissolve the cornstarch in 1 / 4 cup water
3. heat a pan over high heat
4. add the cooking oil , swirling to coat
5. add the garlic and ginger
6. cook , stirring , until fragrant , about 15 seconds
7. add the soy sauce mixture
8. bring to a boil
9. reduce heat to medium and cook for 1 minute
10. add the cornstarch solution and cook , stirring , until the sauce boils and thickens
demonstrations.review: Excellent. I made a double batch as we do stir fry quite often. I cut back on the soya just a bit and used powdered ginger. I also added a pinch of five spice powder and a fresh chopped jalapeno for the kick.

target.recipe_text:
thai tofu and squash curry

from canadian living magazine.  recommended for tofu lovers and/or fans of thai-inspired dishes.

1. pat tofu dry with paper towels
2. cut into 3 / 4-inch cubes
3. set aside
4. peel and seed squash
5. cut into 3 / 4-inch cubes to make 3 cups
6. set aside
7. in skillet , heat oil over medium heat
8. cook onion , garlic and curry paste , stirring occasionally , until onion is softened , about 5 minutes
9. add squash , coconut milk , stock , soy sauce , sugar , fish sauce and salt
10. bring to boil
11. reduce heat to low
12. partially cover and simmer until squash is almost tender , about 12 minutes
13. add red pepper
14. simmer for 5 minutes
15. add tofu
16. simmer until heated through , about 2 minutes
17. stir in cilantro and lime juice
18. sprinkle with peanuts
target.review: Super yummy, healthy, easy - what else could you ask for? We enjoyed the way some of the squash cubes "melted" and thickened the delicious sauce. Made it with fish sauce and added about 1 1/2 cup brocoli pieces (florets plus peeled and diagonally sliced stalk) in step 6, which was a lovely addition, both in terms of color and taste. Served it with jasmine rice. Thanks for a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gnocchi with butternut squash  squacchi perhaps

this is very tasty, simple and quick to make (what more can anyone ask for?).  the recipe uses bought gnocchi, but you could always make your own if you have time on your hands!  the original recipe comes from the latest sainsbury's magazine (april 2005 issue), but i've tweaked it a bit.  it'll take plenty more tweaking to suit your preferences too, just choose your favorite seasoning and herbs.
