3. stir vigorously until mixture leaves the side of the bowl
4. gather dough together and press into a ball
5. knead dough in bowl 10 times to make smooth then divide dough in half
6. on lightly floured surface roll each half into a 13-inch circle
7. place on pizza pan
8. turn up edges 1 / 2 inch and pinch
9. brush circles with remaining 2t of salad oil
10. add toppings and bake for 20-25 minutes or until it looks done
demonstrations.review: Great recipe - my family loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: thanks for sharing---the meatballs were great and  i added a couple of raisins to the mix.  Sounds alittle weird but they plump up and give a special sweet surprise.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage  peppers  and potatoes

lots of flavor in a very easy supper.

1. in 12 inch skillet , heat oil and brown sausage
2. remove from pan
3. add peppers , potatoes , onion mix and water
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce to low and simmer , covered 20 minutes
6. return sausage and simmer another 5 minutes , or until potatoes are done
demonstrations.review: Awesome!!! so easy and inexpensive...we loved it!!!   Doubled the recipe and it tunred out perfect-- thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast beef tenderloin with red wine   shallot sauce

this recipe from the december 2000 issue of canadian living was served in the posh dining cars of the royal canadian pacific! it is definitely dinner party fare but also good enough for your family!

1. sprinkle beef with peppercorns & salt , pressing to adhere
2. heat oil in roasting pan , over medium-high heat
3. sear beef all over
4. roast in preheated 375f oven for about 55 minutes or until meat thermometer inserted in centre registers 140f
5. transfer to cutting board , tent with foil & let stand for 15 minutes before carving
6. sauce: heat 2 tbsp pf the butter in a saucepan over medium heat
7. cook shallots , stirring occasionally , for about 10 minutes or until softened
8. stir in sugar & cook for an additional 10 minutes or until shallots are golden & caramelized
9. stir in garlic & thyme and cook for a further 5 minutes
10. add stock , wine , brandy & bay leaf , bring to a boil , then reduce heat and simmer for about 30 minutes or until sauce is reduced to about 2 cups
11. whisk cornstarch with 1 tbsp water , then whisk into sauce and boil until smooth & thickened
12. discard bay leaf
13. add roasting pan juices to sauce , bring to a boil , then whisk in remaining butter
14. serve with roast
demonstrations.review: Made it for the holidays and it was a HIT!! Thanks loved it!!

target.recipe_text:
william shatner s cappuccino muffins

i love william shatner and cappuccino; what could be better, hehe. these are on several sites, the goldmine again, where there are bunches of other celebrity recipes. i used instant coffee instead of espresso powder  cause where i live that's all there is.  it works fine.

1. preheat oven to 400 and grease muffin tins or line with paper baking cups
2. sift all dry ingredients together into a bowl
3. make a well in the center of the mixture
4. beat the egg together with the milk and the melted butter
5. add the vanilla
6. add to the dry ingredients along with the chocolate chips and mix until just moistened
7. spoon batter into prepared muffin cups , filling each 2 / 3 full
8. bake until just done , approximately 20 minutes
target.review: I have made these lovely, delicious muffins several times since I first saw the recipe a year ago.  I've baked these as the recipe is written.  These tasty gems have gone to work for morning coffee, to church for coffee time, and to the homes of several friends who needed a "cheer-up."  All who consumed these treats raved about them and wanted more.  These are easy to make and are a wonderful "go-to" recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
graham cracker coffee cake

this is good, i have made it many times over the years.

1. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
2. mix the first four ingredients together and put half of batter into pan
3. mix the remaining ingredients together and put half the crumb mix over the batter in pan
4. put remaining batter over the crumbs and last put remainder of crumbs on top
5. bake at 350 for 25-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This coffee cake is a huge favorite at work.  It disappears in minutes!  Thanks, RecipeMonster, for posting this yummy coffee cake!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mocha crumble bars

these are incredible!!! everyone who ate one at the party said "oh wow!" as soon as they put them in their mouth. bet you can't eat just one!!

1. preheat oven to 350f line a 15x10x1-inch baking pan with foil
2. in a medium bowl , using an electric mixer set on high speed , beat butter and brown sugar until light and creamy
3. on medium speed , beat in egg
4. in another bowl , combine flour , baking soda and 1 / 2 teaspoon cinnamon
5. gradually add flour mixture to butter mixture and mix until dough is smooth
6. stir in oats and walnuts
7. reserve 1 cup dough for topping
8. press remaining dough into bottom of prepared pan
9. in a medium saucepan , heat 1 1 / 2 cups chocolate chips , condensed milk , instant coffee and remaining cinnamon over medium heat
10. stir until smooth
11. spread mixture evenly over the dough in the pan , smoothing the surface with a spatula
12. crumble reserved dough on the top
13. sprinkle with the remaining chocolate chips
14. bake until lightly browned , about 20 minutes
15. cool completely on a wire rack
16. lift foil to remove from pan
17. cut into 2-inch bars
demonstrations.review: These bars taste fantastic!  The recipe is almost identical to my grandma's old Mennonite recipe for "Revel Bars"  (Her recipe didn't have coffee in it.)  I will definitely make these treats again. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blue ridge mountains chocolate chip cookies

these cookies have been served for over 75 years in the quiet village of orkney springs, va. we have stayed in this  retreat center called shrine mont where people come for rest, devotion, and fellowship. a couple of things set these cookies apart: butter and shortening ensure a thick cookie, soft in the middle, with a touch of almond extract.

1. i add the 1 / 4 cup making it 2 3 / 4 cups total
2. cream shortening , butter , sugars , then eggs and vanilla and almond extracts
3. blend dry ingredients and add to mixture
4. stir in chocolate chips
5. drop by large tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheet , leaving 2-inches room in between to allow cookies to spread
6. i press down lightly with a measuring cup to bake more uniform cookies)
7. bake at 375 for 10 minutes until lightly brown
8. makes 2-3 dozen cookies depending on size
demonstrations.review: I've had this in my cookbook for quite a while but just now made it. Had visitors for the holidays and decided to make a double batch. My visitors called them "divine" and ate them for breakfast! This is my new "go-to" chocolate chip cookie recipe...tender, delicious, and easy! I wasn't sure about the almond extract but it adds just the right flavor "boost". BTW, I used a cookie scoop and received 6 1/2 dozen cookies from the double batch.  Thank you, Roxygirl!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christmas rum balls or bourbon balls

these balls are so quick and easy to make. they make a nice addition to the baked goodies that you give as gifts. make these about a week before you want to serve them as they mellow and the sharp strong alcohol taste blends  in more with the other ingredients. store in a tin with a tight lid.  this year i couldn't find the vanilla wafers so i used chocolate and i like them even more.  to form the balls i use two teaspoons as the dough is quite moist.  i store them in the freezer - they don't go hard and they are so good ice cold

1. sift the cocoa with 1 cup sugar
2. stir in the spiced rum mixed with the syrup
3. add crushed vanilla wafers and nuts
4. mix thoroughly
5. shape mixture into walnut sizes balls and dredge with remaining sugar or leave them plain
6. store in a tin
demonstrations.review:
I made several batches of "Christmas Balls" for giving this year...

A double batch as the recipe is written (I used Rebel Yell whiskey) and

A single batch made with graham crackers, pecans, and Sailor Jerry spiced rum. I had to use raw honey instead of Karo for this batch when rainstorms kept me from going to town for supplies.

All of the Christmas Balls were received and consumed with happy hearts and happy taste buds! One tin of Bourbon Balls went to a "very senior" friend who loved the Bourbon Balls his late wife used to make. He was tickled pink when he opened the tin and caught a whiff of the whiskey fumes. :-)

Bergy, thank you for posting this delightful and delicious recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
snoopy thanksgiving

this is the thanksgiving meal that charlie brown served his friends.  snoopy was in charge of the toast and popcorn.

1. toast bread in toaster
2. butter toast , stack high
3. in large pot , over medium high heat , melt coconut oil
4. add in popcorn kernels and cover
5. shake pot virgorously
6. when popping begins , lift cover off just a smidge so steam escapes but popcorn does not
7. when popping slows to 1 kernel per second , remove from heat
8. add salt and pour into a large bowl
9. add butter if desired
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: My family's tradition for many years was to eat popcorn, toast and jellybeans (don't forget the jellybeans!) while watching the Charlie Brown Thanksgiving...now my husband and I do this. :-)  My husband is very tolerant of my silly quirks. ;-)  Thank you for posting this delightful menu for posterity, Snoopy Chef!

target.recipe_text:
chicken croissant bake

this makes a nice lighter style casserole. great for weekend brunches or light lunches. any of the cheeses are good, or even a combination. prep time includes refrigeration time before cooking.

1. arrange half of the croissant cubes in an ungreased square 8 x 8 baking dish
2. sprinkle with 1 / 2 cup of the cheese , all of the chicken and onions
3. arrange remaining croissants over the top
4. beat milk , eggs , mustard and salt
5. pour over casserole
6. cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours , but no more than 24 hours
7. bake uncovered at 325f for 1 to 1 1 / 4 hours , or until tests clean
8. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese
9. bake 2 minutes more , or until cheese melts
10. serve immediately
target.review:
I used all mozzarella cheese (cant beat that stringiness!)
Tasty and loved the croissant crunch, I obly had it in the oven for 1 hour and it was a little dry, will make it again but check sooner.
Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and gravy

easy weeknight supper.mashed potatoes are a perfect side,

1. combine flour , paprika , salt and pepper
2. coat chicken
3. save flour mixture
4. in large skillet , saute chicken in butter , turning and browning until done
5. remove and keep warm
6. in same skillet , saute mushrooms for 3 minutes
7. add onion , cook for 2 minutes
8. add 3 t of the flour mix to pan
9. cook and stir for 1 minute
10. add milk mixture , stirring until mixture comes to a boil
11. thin with more milk if neccesary
demonstrations.review:
Cut this accordingly for 4 servings, tasty dish.
Loved the gravy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pecan tassies

if you like pecan pie, you'll love these!

1. beat flour , butter and cream cheese in bowl
2. refrigerate 1 hour
3. roll into 1" balls
4. press each ball into greased wells of small muffin tin , forming cups
5. set aside
6. bring remaining ingredients to a boil
7. pour hot mixture , 1 tbsp at a time , into cups
8. bake in 400 oven for 12-15 minutes
demonstrations.review:
These are delicious with a capital 'D'..I have made these to include in my Christmas goody gifts...ahem ahem, I've eaten 3 in a row!
The pastry is melt in your mouth, the filling divine, thank you so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steak with blue cheese sauce

very assertively-flavored steak recipe that i learned about 12 years ago when i was learning to cook to impress my now-husband. adapted from betty crocker's new international cookbook. this spanish-influenced recipe can tend to be somewhat on the salty side, so be careful to use unsalted butter to saute the steaks, and a good-quality, not-overly-salty blue cheese in the sauce. serve simply, with a lightly-dressed salad, good crusty bread, and a nice red wine.

1. in a medium skillet , combine cheese , garlic , wine , and red pepper over low heat
2. stir frequently until cheese melts
3. remove from heat and keep warm
4. in large skillet , melt butter over medium-high heat , and cook steaks to your liking , turning only once
5. sprinkle pepper over steaks , remove from skillet and keep warm
6. add water to skillet and heat to boiling , stirring constantly to loosen browned bits
7. boil 2 minutes , then stir pan juices into cheese mixture
8. pour over steaks and sprinkle with parsley
demonstrations.review:
Wow oh wow, what a delicious steak recipe.
I was only cooking 2 steaks so cut the blue cheese to 4 ounces but kept everything else as stated, what a tasty sauce..first class, thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
emaw s goulash

as some of you know i have been attempting to record my mother's recipes for all eternity.  this has been one of my all time comfort meals all my life.  some of the ingredients would change depending on how much $$ we had at the time.  feel free to add any seasoning you might like.

1. prepare elbow macaroni according to directions on package till al dente
2. save a little of the pasta water in case you need it later to loosen the sauce
3. brown meat in a large skillet , drain the fat and add the onion and bell pepper half way through cooking
4. drain any ramaining fat when onion and pepper is done and add garlic , stir it about
5. add the meat mixture to the cooked macaroni , add the canned tomatoes , corn and sauce
6. mix all this together and add seasoning to taste
7. you may need to add some of the pasta water to loosen the sauce if it is too dry
8. this is really good the next day too
demonstrations.review:
Great tasting and easy to put together, I used frozen corn and premium beef (less fat) 
Perfect for a cold winters meal, thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked grated zucchini

another from "pacific fresh".  this is a simple and rather unusual side dish.  it is very tasty and one more way to use up that zucchini.  good served with roasted chicken!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. wash zucchini , leaving skins on , and grate either by hand or in a food processor
3. blot zucchini with paper towels to remove as much moisture as possible
4. place in an 8 inch square baking dish that has been sprayed with cooking spray
5. cut butter into small pieces and place evenly over zucchini
6. bake for 15 minutes , uncovered
7. remove from oven and pour off any liquid that has accumulated in the bottom of the dish
8. stir in sour cream , salt and pepper
9. sprinkle top with parmesan cheese and bake until zucchini is tender and cheese melts
10. about 5-10 more minutes
demonstrations.review: This is definitely outstanding, if I could give it 10 stars I would. What a delicious way to cook the humble zucchini, love the texture and the flavour. A definite favourite.

target.recipe_text:
creamy potato salad

have you ever posted a recipe and just love reading the reviews for it?  this is my signature potato salad.  whenever there is a pot luck function at work, i am told that i have to bring the potato salad.  no one else is allowed to and i am never given a choice.  thank you everyone who ever tried this potato salad and for leaving such glowing reviews for it.  you all have made me look so good.  i personally can not stand eggs or raw onions, so i leave them out but i know most people don't think a potato salad is complete without them.  thanks again for so many wonderful reviews. (psssst....check out my recipe #123107 as well.  it shares the dressing with this recipe but tastes much much different because of the different ingredients) please see recipe #242966 for bacon bit tips.

1. cook potatoes in boiling , salted water until tender
2. drain well
3. peel and cube potatoes
4. transfer to a large bowl
5. add celery , onion , sweet relish and bacon bits
6. combine mayo , sugar , celery seed , vinegar , mustard , and salt
7. add mayo mixture to potatoes
8. toss lightly to coat potato mixture
9. carefully fold in the chopped eggs
10. cover and chill thoroughly
11. bacon bit
12. use a sharp knife and cut the frozen bacon into long strips about 1 / 4 inch wide
13. turn the bacon and cut the strips into pieces also about 1 / 4 in wide
14. you now have perfect raw bacon pieces to fast fry
15. no need to separate
16. they will separate during cooking
17. perfect bacon bits
target.review: I can't believe anyone gave this less than 5 stars!  My husband hates potatoe salal, but yet asked me to make a second batch because there was no leftovers! I didn't have celery seeds onhand, but it still turned out yummy.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe.  I'll get a lot of mileage out of this one!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
three bean turkey burger bake

i was shopping with the kids and this was a sample. they made sure i got the recipe! a change from plain old baked beans. (would be good with sausage or hamburger too)

1. in a large skillet brown turkey and onions
2. drain if necessary
3. add lima beans and cook and stir until heated through
4. add remaining ingredients
5. mix well
6. bake uncovered at 350 for 35 minutes
demonstrations.review: The smell was making me hungry while it was cooking!  It was so easy to make and it tasted great!  I served with a salad and Dale's Deviled Eggs.  My husband loved it and was estatic that there was leftovers.  I didn't have lima beans, so I used northern beans instead.  Excellent recipe that anyone would love!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dales deviled eggs

named for my wife, who "invented" it

1. place eggs one layer deep in a large pan
2. cover with hot water by 1"
3. bring water to a gentle boil , lower heat and gently boil for 15 minutes
4. remove from heat and place pot under cold running water , as soon as eggs are cool enough to handle peel them under cold water
5. place on a paper towel to dry
6. cut eggs in half , put yolks into a medium bowl , place whites on a prepared tray
7. refrigerate whites
8. chop yolks with a pastry cutter , food processor or mash with a fork
9. add remaining ingredients , whisk thoroughly , adjust seasonings
10. add more mayo if a creamier texture is desired
11. pipe filling into whites , sprinkle more salt and paprika and serve
demonstrations.review: This is the easiest, best recipe for deviled eggs.  I use celery salt instead of celery seed.  I also have used regular mustard when I'm out of brown mustard.  This recipe is a no-fail recipe!  Thanks for a great one!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange marmalade curry chicken

an easy, change of pace recipe that tastes great! for a quick week-day dinner, i like to serve it with rice and a salad.

1. lightly flour chicken pieces
2. brown well in butter in frying pan
3. mix together marmalade , water , curry powder , salt and pepper
4. baste chicken well with this mixture
5. pour remaining mixture into frying pan with chicken
6. cover and cook for 30 minutes or until chicken is tender
7. remove cover for the last 5 minutes of cooking
demonstrations.review: I added more curry and used on chicken tenderloins.  It was a very good and healthy alternative to Chinese Orange Chicken.  I served over rice and it was delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chipped beef cheese ball

very easy to make when you are on short notice of company coming.

1. mix all ingredients together , reserving a couple ounces of the beef
2. shape into a ball and roll into reserved beef
3. chill for at least 2 hours
4. serve
demonstrations.review: I've made this for years!  It's so awesome and addicting.  It's definitely not an ordinary cheese ball, but everyone will love it and ask for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana cream supreme

this is a great banana dessert!

1. mix toghether graham cracker crumbs , margarine and sugar
2. mix well
3. press crumb mixture onto flat bottom of springform pan
4. in 2 quart
5. bowl whisk together sour cream and milk until blended
6. add pudding mix
7. whisk until pudding is dissolved
8. add whipped topping mixing until well blended
9. spread half of filling over crust
10. slice bananas
11. arrange over filling
12. spread remaining filling over bananas
13. grate pecans over top
14. chill
15. to serve , remove collar from springform pan
16. cut into wedges
demonstrations.review: This is very easy and very tasty.  When I was a Pampered Chef Consultant, I used this recipe in my demos.  It was always a hit and always disappeared.  I learned to make more!

target.recipe_text:
armenian herb marinade grilled chicken breasts

this is the most awesome grill marinade i've ever tasted in my life!  i don't know where my mom got this, but there is no match that i've ever known of...it is simplicity and freshness, yet rich, robust and succulent!  i haven't told you this one yet, because i was entering it in a grilling contest for a weber grill, but i can't hold back any longer!  it is wonderful for chicken breasts and also for lamb.  my mom used to make chicken and lamb kabobs with this marinade and we always wanted more!!!  note:  prep time does not include the 24-48 hours marinating time.  update:  my grill has died....so in desperation to taste this chicken again, i tried bobo3039's suggestion about baking it in a 350 degree oven...results were wonderful!!!  (still missed that charcoal essence, but one must "roll with the punches" and make do...in this case, bobo3039 was right on the money!)

1. mix all ingredients together and whisk thoroughly
2. put cleaned and dried meat in a large 8 x 11-inch glass baking pan and pour marinade over all , being sure to coat well
3. cover with plastic wrap and let marinate in refrigerator for 24 to 48 hours
4. drain meat and grill , basting with marinade until meat is cooked through
target.review: Fantastic, even after only marinating for 6 hours!  Husband and toddler approved! Served with acorn squash filled with rice, red onion and chopped baby spinach. Thanks for the winner :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory crock pot shredded beef

oh my goodness!  this beef is so delicious and the aroma while it is cooking is mouth watering.  it isn't difficult to prepare- just combine dry rub ingredients and pop in the crock pot.  there is no need to add water and the roast comes out so juicy, tender, and flavorful.  it is so nice to have an all purpose meat recipe to use in enchiladas, burritos, tacos, casseroles, or in sandwiches.  if you make sandwiches, you can leave the meat as is- it is tender and juicy or add your favorite barbeque sauce.  i like to freeze it to keep on hand.

1. halve roast to make sure meat cooks all the way through
2. combine all seasonings in a small bowl and mix thoroughly
3. run all over roast
4. place roast in crock pot sprayed with nonstick cooking spray
5. cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours or until meat is tender and cooked through
6. shred meat with a fork
demonstrations.review: This was outstanding, and SO easy.  Thanks for posting!  We loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek baked shrimp with feta

this is a delicious recipe, and one i have enjoyed many times. it would make an excellent appetizer for entertaining as well as a great dinner idea!

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. remove shells from shrimp , leaving last segment and tail intact
3. remove vein
4. rinse and dry
5. in a pan saute onion in oil until transparent , , add garlic and green onion and cook 2 minutes more
6. to the onions add the tomatoes , wine , half the parsley , oregano , and salt and pepper to taste
7. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 30 minutes until thickened
8. pour half the sauce into a shallow casserole , and arrange the shrimp on top
9. pour the rest of the sauce on , and sprinkle crumbled feta over the shrimp
10. bake at 450 degrees for 10-12 minutes or until prawns are pink and feta is lightly browned
11. garnish with remaining parsley and serve
demonstrations.review:
We loved this! My husband asked me to put it into rotation!
Thanks for an easy, delish shrimp dish :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese style sesame chicken

i say this is japanese-style because it is similar to the sesame chicken served at a japanese restaurant in my hometown. of course they set it on fire and all of that stuff, so it isn't quite as good, but it is close enough for home. my family loves this. i serve it with recipe #186399.

1. use the sesame oil to coat a wok or nonstick pan
2. add chicken and cook over low heat until almost cooked through
3. mix the ginger , onion powder , garlic powder , and sesame seeds in a small bowl
4. sprinkle over chicken and saute over medium-high heat
5. turn heat to high and add soy sauce , sauting until fully incorporated and the chicken is slightly seared
6. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Mine was a bit soupy :(

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot sausage and peppers

this is a very easy recipe i found and tastes yummy!  i serve it with french bread, or rice to soak up the juices. enjoy!

1. place onions and peppers , then sausage in crock pot
2. pour the stewed tomatoes on top of the sausage , then the spaghetti sauce
3. sometimes i add a touch of water to make more sauce
4. cook in crock pot for 6-8 hours on low , 3-4 hours on high
demonstrations.review: This sauce is a great base.  I used bulk mixed sausage, Ragu Light (no sugar added), a can of whole peeled tomatoes (instead of the stewed--what I had on hand), added a clove of chopped garlic, a tbsp of tomato paste and about a cup of red wine.  Delish!  Next time I would even add more Italian seasonings, maybe oregano.  Thanks for the inspiration.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic pork chops with mushroom

i have this great bottle of balsamic vinegar and was looking for recipes to use it best.  this is one. hope you enjoy it as much as i did.

1. pre-heat oven to 400f
2. heat oil in large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat 1 minute
3. sprinkle pork with salt and pepper to taste
4. brown pork chops 3 minutes per side
5. add vinegar , rosemary , and soy sauce
6. bake 15 minutes
7. transfer sauce to bowl and keep warm
8. add butter and mushrooms to skillet
9. cook over medium heat 2 minutes
10. spoon warm sauce over pork and mushrooms and serve
demonstrations.review: Easy and very tasty!  Thanks :)

target.recipe_text:
wonderful salsa

this is the best salsa recipe i've found so far and i've tried about a dozen. i got it from one of the local hospital cookbooks that are sold in my area. i changed it a bit and have been canning it for years. the reason i plant a garden is for this salsa. we would be lost without it. hope you like it as much as we do.  one of our members who is a food scientist took this salsa to work, tested the ph and found it measured under 4.0 (well within the safety limit for boiling water bath processing).

1. mix all together and bring to a slow boil for 10 minute
2. seal in jars and cook in hot water bath for 10 minute
3. this is a medium salsa
4. this is also a chunky salsa so if you want a smoother salsa cut your veggies into smaller pieces
5. yields 3-6 quarts or pints
target.review: Superb! I added some cilantro and homemade raspberry jam to some of the salsa and YUMMY--the flavors complimented each other nicely. Thanks for sharing the recipe, it is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh tomato soup with basil

this is delicious served hot or even so, on a warm day served ice-cold! with a crusty bread. please note, fresh basil is to be added towards the end of the cooking time, whereas when using dried basil, it needs to be added alongwith the tomatoes.

1. heat the butter or olive oil in a thick saucepan , and add in the chopped onion , garlic and potato and soften them gently without browning for about 10-15 minutes
2. add the tomatoes , if you are using dried basil then add it in now alongwith the worcestershire sauce , stir well and let them cook for a minute
3. pour in the stock and give it a good stir and season with salt and pepper and cover and simmer for 30 minutes
4. blitz the soup and then pass it through a sieve to extract the skins and pips
5. check seasoning , add in the fresh basil then return the pan to heat and bring to boil again
6. serve hot or ice-cold
demonstrations.review: yum! A few changes; I sauted my vegies in olive oil cooking spray to cut down on the fat..I used pico de pollo instead of chicken bullion (I think it adds more flavor...) I also skinned my tomatoes first instead of last.  Finally, I put some frozen shrimp in at the end---next time I will add carrots and maybe old bay seasoning. A wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cake mix oatmeal cookies

this recipe comes from a local church, fundraising cookbook. it was submitted by janice, by dear stepson's mom. these a good yummy comfort type cookies. great with that special cup of coffee or glass of milk. cook time is per cookie sheet.

1. combine first 3 ingredients in large bowl and mix together with spoon
2. combine oil , eggs& vanilla extract , beat slightly and then add to dry ingredients , stir well
3. stir in pecans and mix well
4. stir in chocolate morsels if you choose to add these and mix well
5. drop by teaspoonful on ungreased cookie sheet
6. drop about 2-inches apart
7. bake at 325f for 12 minutes or until lightly browned
demonstrations.review:
For cookies from a cake mix, yummy (although I think the serving size of 60 cookies is stretching it! :) 
I used vanilla, sugar free pudding along with taking the suggestion of using 1/2 apple sauce and 1/2 vegetable oil. I also used eggbeaters instead of whole eggs and only used 1/4 cup sugar.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy chicken  broccoli   rice casserole   no canned soups

i modified loves2teach's great recipe for cheesy broccoli rice (#67521) to make a main dish casserole without canned soups. enjoy!

1. boil water , adding bouillon cubes
2. add rice and broccoli and cook covered on low heat for 12-15 minutes
3. while rice is cooking , heat butter over medium heat in medium pan
4. add onions and cook until softened and just starting to carmelize , about 8 minutes
5. add garlic and cook an additional 2 minutes
6. turn off heat , add thyme , chicken , mayonnaise and milk , stirring to combine
7. once rice mixture is ready , remove from heat and dump in 9x11" glass pyrex pan
8. add chicken and sauce mixture , 1 1 / 2 cups of cheese and mix well
9. add salt and pepper to taste
10. sprinkle remaining cheese on top
11. cook at 350 degrees approx 25 minutes or until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: Yummy! What a quick and delicious meL.  I used two cans of canned chicken and didn't add the onion or butter because the kids don't like them. I would if it were just the hubby and I though.  Also, I will add cream cheese next time, just to kick up the richness and tinker (cause I can't leave a recipe alone :-). Thanks for posting, you saved us from a supper of PB&J!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian couscous

tonight i was making recipe #147775 and i needed a side dish with an oriental flair... i came up with this and got great reviews from the family!  (cooking time is the time the cous cous needs to sit.)

1. sautee onions and garlic in olive oil until tender
2. remove from oil
3. boil chicken broth
4. when broth has reached a boil , add cous cous and remove from heat
5. stir in onions and garlic
6. stir in remaining ingredients and let cous cous sit for five minutes
7. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Wonderful and quick. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon latte

these have become a sunday morning favourite for us. heavenly coffee to warm your tummy! the original recipe calls for ground cinnamon, but it also works very well if you put a couple whole cinnamon sticks or pieces of cinnamon bark in the cold milk. it will infuse the milk as it comes to a boil.

1. in a large pan , mix the cinnamon and sugar with a bit of milk
2. add the rest of the milk and bring to a boil
3. just as the mixture comes to a boil , take it off the heat
4. split your hot coffee between 4 mugs
5. pour in the milk and serve immediately
6. another variation is to leave out the ground cinnamon , but instead put a large cinnamon stick , some cloves and green cardamom pods in the milk
7. leave as it comes to a boil , set aside and let it infuse for a couple minutes
8. then strain out the seasonings and pour into the coffee
demonstrations.review: awesome, I do the core ww program and this So fits the bill!  I cannot believe how much like starbucks this thing tastes (the cinnamon dulce latte.) You rock, thanks for the great recipe!!

target.recipe_text:
savory cheese soup  slow cooker

i like to garnish this soup with popcorn, croutons, green onions or bacon bits.

1. in slow cooker , combine the first eight ingredients
2. cover and cook on low for 7-8 hours
3. combine flour and water until smooth
4. stir into soup
5. cover and cook on high 30 minutes longer or until soup is thickened
6. stir in cream cheese and cheddar cheese until blended
7. stir in beer if desired
8. cover and cook on low until heated through
9. serve with desired toppings such as croutons , popcorn , cooked crumbled bacon , sliced green onions
target.review: This was easily the best homemade soup I have ever made.  Perfect consistency, great flavour, and velvety in the mouth.  It is a little salty, so next time I will omit the added salt altogether.  In my opinion, this great soup doesn't need it--you get all the flavour you need by using old or sharp cheddar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was easy and really tasty.  It was filling too, so a whole pan fed me and the honey for two nights--very important on a budget!  Very interesting--I love Americanized Mexican food, and this was a great one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy baked chicken strips

these are delicious! and much more cost-effective than buying chicken nuggets. nice and juicy, yet crisp on the outside, too. yummy, yummy! for an italian twist, omit chili powder and substitute italian seasonings. makes two dinner servings, or 4 lunch/appetizer servings.

1. cut chicken breasts into thin strips , about one inch wide
2. longer sections can be cut in half to have uniform pieces
3. mix cracker crumbs and seasonings well
4. dip chicken pieces into egg mixture , then dredge in crumb mixture
5. place on baking sheet sprayed with cooking spray
6. bake at 375 degrees f , for 10-12 minutes , until crispy on outside and lightly browned
7. dip into favorite sauce , or enjoy just as they are !
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  Better than any storebought I have ever had.  Crisped up nicely and lots of flavour.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french dip roast beef for the crock pot

this is one of the best recipes i've come up with for beef roast. the cheapest cuts come out tasting like you slaved over a stove all day long. you can add potatoes and carrots to the recipe if you like, or shred it and serve it as a french dip sandwich with the au jus juice from the crock pot on the side. if you are watching your sodium, use the lite soy sauce and it will taste just as delicious.

1. place roast in a 5-quart slow cooker
2. combine soy sauce and next 6 ingredients
3. pour over roast
4. add water to slow cooker until roast is almost covered
5. cook , covered , on low for 7 hours or until very tender
6. remove roast , reserving broth
7. you may shred roast with a fork and serve on sandwich rolls with the broth on the side for dipping
demonstrations.review: I followed this recipe to the letter and the meat was not very flavorful.  I even added more of everything and it was still very bland.  The meat was kind of dry too, and I added all the water in the recipe.  I was expecting this to be really fantastic and I was disappointed.  Maybe I will try again with a different cut of meat and more seasoning.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
divine meatball sandwiches

the spread on these meatball sandwiches is what really sets them apart from others. you can experiment and customize by using your favorite meatballs, sauces and fresh bread. good for a party finger food, or for lunch or dinner. i promise no meatball sandwich will be the same again! cook time includes entire process.

1. in a large pot combine frozen meatballs and spaghetti sauce
2. heat over medium until meatballs are heated throughout
3. meanwhile , mix together cream cheese , mayonnaise , italian seasoning , pepper , and garlic powder and set aside
4. slice italian style bread loaves horizontally with serrated bread knife
5. cut loaves into three- or four-inch sections to make small sandwiches
6. spread cream cheese mixture on insides of each sandwiche's tops and bottoms
7. preheat oven to 350f
8. when meatballs are heated , spoon onto sandwiches and top with shredded mozzarella cheese
9. put sandwich tops on and place on a foil-lined baking sheet
10. bake about 10-15 minutes or until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review:
You weren't kidding when you said that the spread sets these incredible sandwiches apart. Hands down the best sandwiches I have ever had. I used Kaiser rolls instead of the suggested buns, and it turned out great. I had leftover spread as I was only feeding two people, and mixed that, the leftover meatballs and sauce, and leftover cheese together, and it made a great qucik lunch the next day.

Fantastic recipe, sure to be an instant classic in my house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy slow cooker roast beef sandwiches

i got this recipe from a co-worker who made it for a luncheon we were having at work one day. the meat comes out very moist and very flavorful.

1. place roast in crockpot
2. in bowl , mix together the sauces and the soup mix
3. pour sauce mixture over roast
4. add enough water to crockpot so that it reaches about three-fourths of the way up to the roast
5. cook on low 7-8 hours
6. shred beef and serve on sandwich buns
demonstrations.review: Meat was very flavorful.  I don't think I added enough liquid, as the meat was a tad dry, but that's no fault of the recipe.  Very simple and tasty.

target.recipe_text:
borden s mini cheesecakes

these are festive little cakes after cooled garnish with a sprinkle of cake sprinkles or get creative and use fresh berries; fresh sliced fruits; toasted coconut..... prep time unknown; baking time 20 minutes
the borden's eagle brand condensed milk provides the sweetness to the cheesecake mixture...sugar is not needed. (except for stated amount in crust.)

1. preheat oven to 300 degrees f
2. line cupcake tin with cupcake papers
3. combine crumbs , sugar and butter
4. press equal portions onto bottom of cupcake papers
5. in large mixing bowl beat cheese until fluffy
6. gradually beat in condensed milk until smooth
7. add eggs and vanilla
8. mix well
9. spoon equal amounts into prepared cups
10. bake 20 minutes or until cakes spring back when touched lightly
11. cool and chill
12. garnish with fresh berries or sliced fruits
13. chocolate shavings
14. toasted coconut
15. or cake sprinkles for a festive look
target.review: These were a big hit !! Made them for my husbands birthday. Who needs cake when you can enjoy these little gems!! I topped them with cherry pie filling. Thanks for a great recipe!!! Diana

demonstrations.recipe_text:
edna s apple crumble  aka  apple crisp

a simple and easy to make but oh so yummy recipe. known as apple crumble in the uk and apple crisp in the us

1. put apples in an 8 or 9 inch square baking dish
2. combine the rest of the ingredients in a separate bowl and mix
3. spread crumble mixture over apples and bake for 35 minutes in a 375f degree oven
4. for an added treat top off with a little english custard
demonstrations.review: Oh this is so yummy, I have made it twice now, in 1 week !! The first time as directed, the secon time, I added Werthers soft caramels to it. I layered the caramels on top of the applle layer, and then covered with the crumble mixture. Pure Joy!!! Thanks very much, Diana

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kafta  meatball shish kabobs

found this on another site...purported to be authentic lebanese cuisine. we think it's great!

1. soak wooden skewers in warm water for 30 minutes
2. mix all ingredients in a large bowl
3. divide into 6 portions and shape around one end of a skewer in a log shape , about 1 inch thick and 6 inches long
4. grill over high heat , turning several times , for 10-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Have made these twice, in just 2 weeks!! The first with skewers, the second made into little mini patties,perfect to place into pita pockets!!! Yummy thanks very much

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast beef horseradish spirals

very attractive looking appy! and good too. had some ladies over for a 

1. combine first 6 ingredients
2. place the two tortillas on work surface , spread half of cheese over each , top each with half of the roast beef slices , leaving a 1 / 2 inch border around edges
3. roll up , wrap tightly in plastic wrap
4. refrigerate until firm , 30 minutes or up to 1 day ahead
5. cut diagonally into 1 / 2 inch slices and serve
demonstrations.review: DELISH!!! The first thing to vanish at my sons BDay party, Thank You Very Much Diana

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate eclair dessert

who would have thought something so easy could be so delicious!

1. mix together vanilla pudding mix and milk
2. fold in whipped topping
3. line 9 x 13 pan with one layer of graham crackers
4. put half of the pudding mixture over the graham crackers
5. place a second layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
6. put the remaining pudding mixture over the graham crackers
7. place a third layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
8. heat the tub of frosting in the microwave for 30 seconds to soften
9. spread frosting on the top of the last layer of graham crackers
10. cover with plastic wrap and let set a couple hours or overnight in the refrigerator
11. cut in squares
demonstrations.review: WOW, WOW, WOW What a Wonderful Recipe, This is sooooooo Good. Made it for a family potluck, everyone loved  it, and asked for the recipe, Thank You So Much !!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s 5 minute cinnamon flop brunch cake

except for the the milk and small amount in the egg, the cake itself has very little fat and using low-fat milk will keep the fat to a minimum, i have stated the egg as optional, i strongly suggest to add it in for a more cake-like texture --  if you are looking for a fancy cake to serve then this is not it however for the ease of this cake it is darn good and makes a great weekend brunch cake, it's like a combination of a cake and cinnamon bun all in one,  ridiculously simple to make as it's all mixed by hand and takes like 5 minutes to throw together, try adding in some chopped strawberries, apples or blueberries, raisins or dried cranberries, this recipe is a blank canvas, so go ahead and add in fruit, nuts chocolate chips whatever you wish, and to kick this up a notch drizzle recipe#120835 on top :) --- servings are only estimated

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. prepare a greased 13 x 9-inch baking dish , or two 8 or 9-inch round cake pans
3. in a bowl mix the 2 cups flour , 1-1 / 4 cups white sugar , milk , vanilla or almond extract , baking powder , pinch of salt and egg until just combined careful not to overmix
4. pour into prepared baking pan / s
5. generously spread brown sugar and cinnamon on top
6. if desired sprinkle chopped walnuts or pecans over top
7. drizzle melted butter over top
8. bake for about 20-25 minutes for 8 or 9-inch round cake pan , and about 30 minutes for a 13 x 9-inch pan
demonstrations.review: Wow,wow,wow!!!This is sooooooo good. A hit with my family. Thanks so much.

target.recipe_text:
rice pilaf with herbs

especially good pilaf. the celery and onion add a nice touch.

1. in skillet , saute rice , celery , and onion in butter until the rice is browned
2. place in a greased 2 quart casserole
3. combine all remaining ingredients
4. pour over rice
5. cover and bake at 325f degrees for 50 minutes or until rice is done
target.review: Made this a while ago and it was great. Added carrots like a lot of other reviewers. The amount of rice is huge, fed about 8 people and still had leftovers. Love having a different variation for rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic batter waffles

this hearty waffle recipe comes from an issue of parent's magazine. ive made it every week for years and it comes out great every time. i double it and freeze the leftover waffles and reheat in toaster oven.

1. mix all dry ingredients together using a large whisk
2. mix the wet ingredients together
3. gently combine but don't overmix
4. cook as your waffle maker directs
5. sprinkle with powdered sugar
6. cover with toasted nuts , bananas , and real maple syrup
7. pour on log cabin and michele's maple cream syrup for my husband !
demonstrations.review: This was my 1st attempt at making waffles. They were delicious. I've been making them once a week since trying these. I didn't use the maple, but doubled up the vanilla and added cinnamon. I also used whole wheat flour, but even my picky clan couldn't tell. I love that they are perfectly crisp and still soft inside. It has a lot of texture and doesn't just dissolve in your mouth. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili s monterey chicken

from copykat.com (http://www.copykat.com)

this is traditionally served as a sandwich but may be served as is!

1. pound chicken breast until it is somewhat flattened , and season with salt and pepper
2. spray pam in a nonstick skillet , and cook chicken breast until it is done
3. transfer to a serving plate
4. top chicken breast with barbeque sauce , bacon , and cheese
5. broil chicken breast in the oven , or melt the cheese in a microwave
6. sprinkle with a small amount of cold chopped tomatoes and chives
demonstrations.review: I make this as a sandwich on bakery rolls made into garlic bread. So delicious. I have made this many times, just forgot to review it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: This was amazing!!! After reading all the reviews I decided on a reduced sodium brown gravy mix and used a 4 lb roast. It was not overly salty at all. It was perfect. I used a little too much water but nothing a little flour couldn't fix. It made an awesome gravy. Thank you so much. This is definitely my favorite roast recipe I've found.**I didn't think this recipe could get any better, until I tried it with a pork roast. It was even better than the beef. It retained more flavor and moisture. It was delicious. Now I have another way to make my favorite crock pot meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate cheesecake

this looks so pretty and tastes delicious!!! i can imagine it at a bridal luncheon or even as an untraditional wedding cake. great for canada day with the red/white of if you want to make a red-white-and blue cake for the 4th of july, make it one pint raspberries (or strawberries) and 1 pint blueberries. but make it over the summer, when fresh berries are readily available, for sure.

1. make crust: in processor , blend crumbs and almonds until almonds are ground fine
2. add butter and combine well
3. press into bottom and 2 / 3s up sides of 10 inch springform pan
4. preheat oven to 300 degrees f
5. make filling: melt chocolate
6. stir until smooth
7. in a large bowl , beat cream cheese until light and fluffy
8. add sugar and beat in whole eggs and egg yolks , one at a time , beating well after each addition
9. beat in the flour and the vanilla and add the melted chocolate in a slow stream , beating , until the filling is combined well
10. scatter raspberries over bottom of crust , pour filling over , and bake cheesecake for 1 hour , or until top is firm to the touch
11. turn off oven and leave cheesecake in closed oven for a further 1 / 2 an hour
12. let the cheesecake cool and then chill it , covered loosely , overnight
demonstrations.review: Used regular instead of clarified butter and put the berries on the side. Not sure if I used the right size pan because it collapsed in the middle, but the flavor was amazing. Everyone loved it and it was pretty easy. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory oven french fries

oh these are so simple and good! the salad dressing mix gives them a savory flavor.  enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. peel potatoes and slice for french fries
3. lay out on paper towel , pat dry
4. potatoes should be as dry as possible
5. put potatoes in a large bowl and drizzle with oil , tossing to coat evenly
6. lay in a single layer on a large baking sheet
7. sprinkle dry dressing mix and parsley over all
8. bake 25 min , then flip over only once
9. return to oven and increase temperature to 450f
10. cook 3 to 5 min longer until potatoes are tender and start to brown
demonstrations.review: These were so good my 4 & 1 year old ate them. I used the right dressing mix but instead of parsley used some fresh basil off my plant and some fresh shredded garlic over them. They have the best flavor. Thank you so much.

target.recipe_text:
real shepherd s pie

a traditional british dish, cottage pie may be made by the same method substituting lamb and lamb stock with beef and beef stock,it may also be topped with grated cheese and tomato before browning, my recipe serves 2 hungry people with good appetites,but it can serve 4.

1. brown meat and chopped onion together for about 5 minutes , add stock and simmer slowly , occasionally stirring until cooked , about 20 minutes
2. mix 2-3 teaspoons of flour or cornflour to a smooth cream with water and slowly add to meat mixture over a low heat stirring continuously until thickened
3. pour into ovenproof dish and set aside , allowing to cool , depending on the quality of the meat used you should not need to skim the fat , however , this is to personal taste
4. peel , boil and mash potatoes with salt , pepper , freshly chopped mint if required , and a generous knob of butter
5. cover the meat mixture with the potato and bake in a medium oven for 30-40 minutes
6. if required dish can be browned under a grill
7. serve with fresh vegetables
8. i also like thickly sliced fresh bread and butter with my real shepherds pie
target.review: Geesh...I just recommended your bubble and squeak recipe and lol lol here I am making shepards pie...with lamb and left over gravy.  Wish you would post some more no nonsense recipes.  This too was plain and simply good eating.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pea shoots  stir fried pea shoots    chow dau miu

pea shoots are the tips of the vines and the top set of leaves of the pea plant. i was introduced to these by my bil a couple of years ago. i found no recipes for it here or on line. which lead me to add my recipe.

1. rinse the pea shoots thoroughly in cold water twice , lightly drain
2. in a large wok or skillet over high heat , heat oils add ginger , garlic and sugar
3. toss and add shoots , soy , & oyster sauce
4. stir-fry for two to three minutes , or until the leaves soften and are tender
5. remove shoots leaving the liquid in pan
6. place shoots on serving dish
7. reduce the remaining liquid by 1 / 2
8. pour over shoots and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Quite good.  I also use pea sprouts in salads, sandwiches,  and I cook and blenderize for fresh pea soup  with yoghurt or sour cream and some frozen peas for looks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp  or chicken  with cashew nuts

this is so easy to prepare and the taste is incredible. i've adapted this recipe from more long-life chinese cooking from madame wong and though it calls for deep-frying the shrimp, or chicken, i usually stir-fry it to make it easier and more healthy. i love this recipe!

1. combine sauce ingredients and set aside
2. mix shrimp with cornstarch
3. heat oil
4. deep-fry shrimp until color changes
5. drain
6. remove
7. deep-fry cashews in large strainer until light brown
8. drain , remove
9. reheat 2 t
10. oil in wok
11. fry chilies until dark brown
12. add scallion and garlic
13. stir-fry 30 seconds
14. add onion , stir-fry 1 minute
15. add green pepper , stir-fry 30 seconds more
16. remove chilies
17. pour in sauce , bring to a boil
18. add shrimp and nuts
19. mix until shrimp and nuts are glazed
20. removed to serving platter
21. serve over rice
22. you don't have to deep-fry the shrimp and cashews , i usually stir-fry them in 1 t
23. oil i use peanut oil for this recipe
demonstrations.review: Yikes.....only ONE dried red chilli for me.  lol  and stir-fried.  why deep fry this at all??

demonstrations.recipe_text:
north croatian liver dumplings for soup

this is one of my favorite soup dumplings. the good thing is that you can freeze surplus and use them later for another meal. it can stay in refrigerator about 3 months at -20°c. the procedure with frozen dumplings is the same as with fresh when putting them into soup.

1. cover breadcrumbs with milk and wait until breadcrumbs soaks milk
2. mince garlic , onion parsley leaves and add marjoram
3. saut onion on butter until becomes translucent
4. mince the liver and saut them shortly on butter with onion and garlic
5. add eggs , parsley , marjoram , salt , pepper
6. mix well all ingredients and shape them into balls approximately 1 inch in diameter
7. cook them in hot soup 3-5 minutes
8. be careful , soup mustnt wildly boil otherwise dumpling will disintegrate
9. if you want to freeze them put them on foil on hard surface making sure they dont touch each other
10. freeze them completely and than put into bag
11. you can take them one by one and follow the above mentioned cooking procedure
demonstrations.review:
Only 4 star 'cause I tweeked it.  Was too bland for me.  Added more garlic and black pepper.  And I used some bottled browning (carmel). That dead grey colour gets me evertime!!  AND lol I had to muck around with quantities...one of these days I will get used to the metric system!!  We do use it in Canada but I am of an age that I am stuck between both systems... should have asked my granddaughter..lol
Also it didn't need all that much liquid.  But is a GOOD basic jump off recipe.  Thanks.

OOO and I must try that citrus jam of yours. Looks good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black risotto

it's original name is risotto nero,this dish from venice has become a classic, for its unusual black color and for its very delicate taste.

1. clean the cuttlefish by removing eyes , beak and transparent quill
2. remove and reserve ink sac
3. place cuttlefish in a bowl of cold water and soak for 30 minutes
4. peel off as much skin as possible , cut the cuttlefish into strips and wash in plenty of cold water
5. saute' onion and garlic in the oil until translucent
6. add the cuttlefish and cook over moderate heat until golden , stirring from time to time
7. add salt and pepper reduce heat , cover and cook for 30 minutes
8. add the rice and stir briefly over high heat to blend flavors
9. pour in several ladlefuls of boiling broth , the ink from the cuttlefish sac , and then little by little the rest of the boiling broth
10. reduce heat to low and cook for about 15 minutes , stirring constantly
demonstrations.review: darn not many people even seem to use cuttlefish...this is quite good but wayyy to long to cook the cuttlefish...max 2/3 minutes for me...or it goes rubbery. But still deserves 4 stars

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apollo potato pancakes

this recipe appeared on the web site 

1. soak shredded potatoes in cold water about 5 minutes
2. drain and squeeze dry in a linen kitchen towel
3. combine the potatoes with onion , eggs , flour , salt , baking powder and pepper
4. stir well
5. pour oil into skillet to a depth of 1 / 8 inch
6. place over medium heat
7. portion 1 / 2 cup potato mixture into pan
8. flatten slightly
9. cook 8 minutes until brown , turning once
demonstrations.review: Toooo funny...I have no idea where you got the idea it would serve 6!!   lol  Fed two...Soooo good. Actually glad the family wasn't over.  more for me

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s quick 5 minute chinese noodles

i make this often it's easy and a great way to use up leftover cooked spaghetti, after you chop the garlic and green onions this takes only about 5 minutes to make, the amounts listed are really only a guideline you may use any amount of spaghetti and adjust all other ingredients to suit your taste --- i have left the chili flakes as optional you may omit or adjust to heat level, we like spicy  so i always use lots! --- make certain to use only cold spaghetti for this, you may use cooked chinese soba noodles if desired in place of the spaghetti, i like to add in a few teaspoons sesame oil also while cooking, prep time does not include cooking the spaghetti

1. cook the spaghetti in boiling water until al dente drain then rinse well under cold water , then drain again
2. transfer to a bowl , cover and refrigerate until cold
3. heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add in the chopped garlic and chili flakes , cook stirring for 2 minutes
5. add in the cold spaghetti and toss using long tongs until the pasta is hot
6. pour the soy sauce over the hot pasta and continue tossing with tongs adding in more soy sauce if needed until you have the desired flavor that you want
7. season with black pepper if desired
8. transfer to a bowl then toss with chopped green onions
target.review: This is different and sounds delicious....I'll be tempted to toss in some nuts, but guess I'll try it the approved way first!  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fried portuguese style bay scallops

this is a simple, straight-forward way to prepare fresh bay scallops without distracting from their natural sweetness.  the larger sea scallops would work just as well here.

1. wash the scallops in cold water
2. spread on paper towels to dry
3. put flour in a small bowl
4. toss scallops in flour to coat completely
5. melt butter in a skillet over low heat
6. add the scallops and pan fry 3 to 4 minutes , moving and turning , until they are firm but not browned
7. add garlic and parsley and cook 30 seconds longer
8. remove to a serving plate and squeeze lemon juice over scallops and season with salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: For purists this is exactly right!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chicken tortilla soup

i'm in love with this soup!! a very good friend of mine made this for me recently and i fell in love. i'm very picky about my tortilla soup and this by far the best ever. she makes hers in the crock pot and i have to agree, that it's easy and tastes just wonderful!! whatever you do, do not skip the garnishes! they are the icing on the cake! update april 2010:  obviously i've made this so many times i never even look at the recipe anymore!  but i wanted to add some variations that i play around with that are great.  like many reviewers black beans and corn are great additions.  sometimes i add them to the leftovers (if there are any :-) so that is feels like something new the next day!  i have also made it several times with shredded pork which turns it into a pork carnitas type of soup.  if you like it on the spicy and smoke side buy a can of chipotle peppers in adobo sauce and mince up one or two and add it.  and lastly, a little swizzle of half and half or heavy cream just minutes before serving makes it a creamy tortilla soup that is wonderful and it is also a good way to tone down the heat if it got away from you...

1. throw everything except the garnishes in your crock pot and let it cook on high for 5-6 hours
2. dress with garnishes and give it a squeeze of lime and you're good to go !
3. enjoy !
4. if you are not using a crock pot , saute the garlic and onion in 2 tablespoons olive oil before adding the remaining ingredients
5. simmer for at least an hour so that the flavors mix together
demonstrations.review: I've never made tortilla soup in the crockpot before, but I like the convenience of concoct and forget.  It has a lot of flavor and I'm sure we'll love it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous greek salad

be prepared for the best greek salad on the planet! --- plan ahead the dressing needs at least 2 or more hours to blend the flavors, i sometimes add in 1/4 cup parmesan cheese to the dressing for a more cheesy dressing, all amounts may be adjusted to taste ----  to marinade the salad allow to sit at room temperature before serving, see bottom of instructions --- you will find this and many more of my recipes posted here http://kittencalskitchen.com/2009/04/13/kittens-famous-greek-salad/  ---also see my recipe #359292

1. for the dressing
2. in a processor or use a wire whisk process / whisk the olive oil with lemon juice , 2 teaspoons dried oregano , garlic , dried , basil , red wine vinegar , salt and sugar until smooth
3. season with black pepper
4. chill in fridge for a couple of hours before using to blend flavors
5. place the salad ingredients in a large bowl
6. pour dressing over
7. toss to combine
8. if desired allow the salad to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving , or you can refrigerate for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Absolutely perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemony salmon patties

enjoy.        

1. combine the first nine ingredients
2. mix well
3. spoon into eight greased muffin cups , using 1 / 4 cup in each
4. bake at 350 for 45 minutes or until browned
5. meanwhile , melt butter in a saucepan
6. stir in the flour to form a smooth paste
7. gradually stir in milk
8. bring to a boil over medium heat , stirring constantly
9. cook for 2 minutes or until thickened
10. remove from the heat
11. stir in lemon juice , salt and cayenne
12. serve over patties
demonstrations.review: Baked rather than fried -- what a great idea!  I added a little chopped celery along with the onion since I'm used to patties that way.   For the sauce I used chicken broth instead of milk in the white sauce.  Very Tasty!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesty polynesian scallops

this polynesian dish is reminscent of the uniquely tropical cuisines of hawaii and new zealand.  it's a very easy dish to prepare, and it makes a very elegant dinner, especially paired with a dry white wine or a tropical orange-mango blend fruit juice.  but remember to always take care not to overcook scallops or they will become tough. as soon as they lose their translucence and turn opaque, they are done.

1. broil the scallops for 4 minutes , then turn and broil 2 more minutes
2. in a large saucepan , saut the chopped onion in the olive oil until tender
3. add the sliced mushrooms , bell pepper strips , and chopped tomato
4. cook until all the vegetables are heated through
5. arranged the sauted vegetables on a platter
6. top with the broiled scallops
7. layer the avacado slices on top of the scallops , then spread mango salsa over the the avacado slices
8. top with sour cream , and garnish with green onion slices
demonstrations.review: Wow!  Delicious and elegant recipe.  Thank You.

target.recipe_text:
caramelized baked chicken legs wings

delicious! yummy  caramelized legs, kids love these! so quick and easy and no marinating required. just prepare the sauce, pour over the chicken and pop in the oven!  i actually like this with wings better ;-)
 

very important to leave it in the oven until it has caramelized to avoid disappointment. 

thank you to everyone for their positive reviews!

try adding sambal oelek as chef  #27416 has suggested in his review. what a great idea ;-)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit or 180 degrees celsius
2. place chicken in a 9x13 inch baking dish
3. mix together the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper
4. pour over the chicken
5. bake in preheated oven for one hour , or until sauce is caramelized
6. could also use wings or pork ribs
target.review: I made these tonight and they were wonderful!  Both DH and I were licking our fingers!  This recipe will go straight into my Favorites Cookbook!  I followed the recipe exactly and the legs were caramalised and lick smacking good.  I wouldn't change a thing.  Thank you for a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave poached egg on toast

this recipe came with my very first microwave 20+ years ago. it makes an easy, quick, no mess breakfast.

1. place the toast on a plate , butter it , flatten the middle down with the back of a fork
2. crack and carefully pour the egg into the flattened middle of the toast , not allowing it to spill over into the plate
3. prick the yolk quickly and carefully with the tines of the fork and bake in the microwave on a turntable for about 1 minute on 60-70% power , until the white is cooked through or desired doneness is achieved
demonstrations.review: I am diabetic so I have to eat breakfast, but in the mornings I never feel like cooking.  This morning I decided to try this and let me tell you I am hooked!  This took just a few minutes and I had breakfast!  Tasted so good.  I will be making this often.    Thanks Trisha !

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken hurry

a quick chicken recipe, serve with plain white rice and steamed baby carrots.

1. arrange chicken parts in a casserole dish
2. in a small bowl combine the ketchup , water , sugar and soup mix
3. mix together well
4. spoon over chicken , making sure the sauce is on every piece
5. bake covered at 350f for one hour
demonstrations.review: Made this tonight with some bone-in chicken thighs.  WOW - I will be making this often.  The sauce is yummy and the chicken is so moist!  Even DH liked it and asked that I make it again!  I think the sauce would be good on pork chops also - I will try that next and let you know.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian green beans in a snap

this is a yummy way to jazz up a can of green beans from the pantry :)

1. cook the onion and garlic in a little oil until tender
2. add the soy sauce and green beans , and cook until hot , stirring frequently
3. stir in bacon and serve
demonstrations.review: I made these tonight to go with recipe#145038 Caramelized Baked Chicken legs/wings.  They were so good and went great with the chicken.  The prep was so easy and turned a can of green beans into a dish that I could serve to guests and no one would know how easy it was. I know I will be making these a lot!  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and flour tortilla dumplings

these taste just like the one's your grandmother use to make. they are so thin and perfect. unless you tell i promise nobody will ever know they are flour tortilla's. if you want to make for a really big crowd, follow the same instructions just use a 6 qt pot and an additional small pack of 8.5 oz shells. also you can omit the chicken if you want and use canned chicken broth or bouillon cubes.

1. fill 4-quart pot half full with water
2. boil chicken until tender
3. while chicken is cooking , slice tortillas with a sharp knife 5 slices across and one slice through the middle
4. remove cooked chicken and shred with a fork or cut into cubes
5. place chicken , cream of chicken soup , butter , salt and pepper into boiling chicken broth
6. bring to a rolling boil
7. drop individual tortillas into pot one piece at a time
8. do not stir , you can pat the top of the dumplings and move them around slightly with a wooden spoon
9. boil medium / high heat for 12 minutes
10. remove from heat
11. add 1 cup of milk and move the dumplings around gently to mix the milk
demonstrations.review: I am so happy I tried this recipe.  My husband loves rolled dumplings, but frankly I am too lazy to even try to make them.  I saw this recipe and thought I would give it a try, I am so happy I did.  My husband loved it!  This is pure comfort food and I am sure I will make it often.  Thank you so much for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham barbecue sandwiches pittsburgh style

this is a recipe originally published in the pittsburgh post gazette for a regional favorite using local products, heinz ketchup and isaly's chipped ham, although shaved deli ham is a good substitute. this is a quick and easy crowd pleaser that can be doubled or tripled.  this is a favorite on football sundays watching our favorite team, the pittsburgh steelers.  they are great fresh or reheated.

1. combine ham , ketchup , and coke and heat over low heat until heated through
2. slow cooker: combine ham , ketchup and coke and heat for two to three hours on low , one hour on high
3. serve on buns
demonstrations.review: Oh my!  This is just as I remember from my childhood days growing up in Beaver Falls, PA, many, many years ago!   I am so happy to find this recipe.  It as been a very long time since I have had one of these sandwiches, but I promise it will be a regular at my house from now on.  Thank you for bringing back a memory from my childhood.

target.recipe_text:
special green bean casserole

great for holiday dinners.

1. saute onion in butter
2. add flour , salt , sugar and pepper
3. mix in sour cream , beans and cheese
4. pour into 9x13 baking dish
5. top with cornflakes
6. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes
target.review: Wonderful!!!!  This is sooo good and different from the ordinary.  I did top it with fried onions because DH requested it.  I also added some garlic to the sauteing shallot.  I will be making this again.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s pan fried asparagus

i like to make this as soon as asparagus season roles around ---try not to purchase thick asparagus as it tends to be tough, you may adjust the garlic amount to taste, i have left the chili flakes as optional i like to add them in for heat :)

1. in a large skillet melt butter with oil over medium heat
2. add in kosher salt , garlic and crushed chili flakes cook stirring for about 1 minute
3. add in asparagus and cook for about 8-10 minutes turning the spears to ensure even cooking
4. season with freshly ground black pepper
5. sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Thank you! Thank you!!  I finally got my Pickiest Eater to taste asparagus.  He actually ate a few pieces!  We will be making this again.  Another superb recipe Kittencal.  Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed potato pancakes southern style

on a rare occasion we have leftover mashed potatoes.  using recipe #27361 (the best), i added a modern twist to my mom's old southern recipe. increase or decrease onion, garlic, hot sauce, and s&p as to your preference. crispy on the outside, soft on the inside.  bet you can't eat just one!

1. in medium bowl combine all ingredients
2. whisk together until combined well
3. consistency should be similar to cornbread mixture
4. heat skillet with a light layer of oil on medium-high heat
5. spoon batter to form 3 1 / 2 to 4 inch rounds
6. brown each side to a rich dark golden brown
7. potato pancakes should look like a thick regular pancake
8. place on paper towel to drain excess oil
9. don't stack on top of each other or the bottom pancakes will become soggy
demonstrations.review: Found these to be tasty, but not worth the effort.  Family thought they were alright. They were a nice change from mashed potatoes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry margaritas

recipe courtesy rachael ray

1. combine all ingredients in a blender and blend on high
2. serve
3. if your blender is small or not high-powered , make the margaritas in 2 batches
demonstrations.review: I made this at Thanksgiving and it was a huge hit!  I did make this in two batches; it was sooo easy.  Will definately be making this again.  Made according to directions.  Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
campbell s 15 minute chicken  broccoli   rice dinner

nan

1. heat oil in skillet
2. add chicken and cook until browned
3. remove chicken
4. add soup , water , paprika and pepper
5. stir
6. heat to a boil
7. stir in rice and broccoli
8. top with chicken
9. season chicken with additional paprika and pepper
10. cover and cook over low heat 5 minute
11. or until done
demonstrations.review: This was a quick and easy meal.  It made a lot (I increased the water amount).  I did thaw the frozed broccoli a bit to quicken cooking time.  A good meal when you don't know what to fix and are in a hurry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
deb s italian noodle casserole

my sister gave this recipe to me and it is wonderful.  i usually cook a big meal for our family around the holidays and this was the recipe i chose last year.  it feeds a crowd and everyone loved it.  throw in a salad and a loaf of garlic bread and you've got a fantastic meal.  this is not a diet meal! :o)
new note: in an effort to get the fat out of some of my fav recipes, i made this today with all light ingredients and with whole grain egg noodles.  it was fantastic! we didn't miss the fat at all!

1. cook noodles according to package directions , set aside
2. brown ground beef and garlic in butter , drain
3. to the ground beef , add tomato sauce & sugar
4. in a seperate bowl , combine cottage cheese and cream cheese , add sour cream , onion and green bell pepper to the cheese mixture , stir thoroughly
5. in a greased 9 x 13 inch casserole dish , layer 1 / 2 of the cooked noodles , layer of cheese mix and then the rest of the noodles
6. cover the layers with the ground beef mixture and top with the cheddar cheese
7. bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Love this recipe.  Have made it for years especially when I needed to take a meal to a friend.  I usually play around with the spices (Italian and such); I love flavor.  You can substitute spaghetti sauce for the tomato sauce if you want.  This is a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
scallion sesame turkey burger

i found this in some random cookbook.  one of the best turkey burgers ever.  full of flavor.  make an extra for lunch the next day, reheats beautifully.

1. mix togeter , gently
2. the turkey , sesame seeds , soy , scallions , cilantro , garlic , sesame oil , 1 teaspoon of salt , and bread crumbs
3. form into patties
4. i usually mix all this together and make patties in the morning and leave in the refrigerator till i'm ready for them
5. sometimes that is the next day
6. brush with a little oil before grilling if desired
7. grill on the george foreman , in a grill pan
8. if you're using the outside grill increase the breadcrumbs a bit to insure they don't fall apart
target.review: This was unbelievably good. I followed the directions exactly, save for toasting the sesame seeds before I added then. It would be amazing even if I hadn't done that, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chipotle chicken salad tacos

nan

1. the filling: in a large bowl , whisk together the vinegar , olive oil and chipotles
2. season generously with salt , usually about a generous 1 / 4 teaspoon
3. add the cabbage , carrot , onion , cilantro and chicken
4. toss everything together and let stand for 15 minutes
5. taste and season with additional salt if necessary
6. finishing the dish: scoop the filling into a wide shallow serving bowl , dot with the cubed avocado and dust generously with the cheese
7. serve with warm tortillas
demonstrations.review: My friend requested we leave the carrots out in this, so I was worried it might turn out tasting odd, but my dad said this was the best chicken salad he'd ever had! I don't eat chicken salad often, but this is good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
harvest pumpkin apple bread

all the flavors of autumn combined into one scrumptious bread. this tastes great with coffee or tea! i make this using egg beaters and unsweetened applesauce in place of half the oil to make it healthier. prep time includes cooling time.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease and flour two 9 x 5-inch loaf pans
3. combine flour , cinnamon , baking soda and salt in large bowl
4. combine sugar , pumpkin , eggs , vegetable oil and apple juice in large mixer bowl
5. beat until just blended
6. add pumpkin mixture to flour mixture
7. stir just until moistened
8. fold in apples
9. spoon batter into prepared loaf pans
10. bake for 65 to 70 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
11. cool in pans on wire racks for 10 minutes
12. remove to wire racks to cool completely
13. to make using three 8 x 4-inch loaf pans: prepare as above and bake for 60 to 65 minutes
14. to make using five or six 5 x 3-inch mini-loaf pans: prepare as above and bake for 55 to 60 minutes
demonstrations.review: Good stuff! Lovely texture. Will add more apple next time, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese vinegared cucumbers

this is in response to a request. it is from "the complete asian cookbook" by charmaine solomon. it does require that it marinates a while before serving. there is no real cook time involved.

1. peel and slice in half lengthwise and remove seeds
2. cut into thin slices
3. combine all other ingredients and marinate cucumber in the seasonings for at least 1 hour
4. serve as a side salad or relish
demonstrations.review: This was good. Fresh and tart, but not too tart. I couldn't really taste the ginger, but that might be the fault of my own backwards tastebuds.
