demonstrations.recipe_text:
korean pork strips

quick and simple dinner for those busy weeknights that we all know and love! serve over steamed rice for a tasty meal.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. add all ingredients to ziplock bag , shake to mix , and marinate pork for 5 min , or up to 3 hours
3. spray 9x13 baking dish with cooking spray , then place pork in dish , pouring marinade over pork
4. bake 30-35 minutes
5. cut pork into thin slices before serving
demonstrations.review: Made a bunch of changes, and oh man, it turned out tasty! I didn't have reduced sodium soy sauce, so I halved it and made up for the rest with OJ, and used just a tablespoon of sugar. Then I didn't use onion flakes; I chopped up two onions and cooked them in the marinade along with the pork. Finally, I put in a teaspoon of red pepper flakes. Will be making this whenever I have pork loin around!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stir fried shrimp with spicy orange sauce

serve over rice or udon noodles. we just nibbled on them! quite yummy and love the sambal! from cooking light.

1. place shrimp in medium bowl , sprinkle with cornstarch , toss well to coat and set aside
2. combine juice , soy sauce , honey , vinegar , and sambal , stirring until well mixed
3. set aside
4. heat canola oil in large nonstick skillet over med-hi heat
5. add minced ginger and garlic , stir fry for 15 seconds or until fragrant
6. add shrimp mixture , stir-fry for 3 minutes
7. add juice mixture and onions , cook 2 minutes or until sauce thickens and shrimp are done , stirring frequently
8. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Amazing! We doubled the ginger, garlic, and onions, because we love all of those. We didn't have any sambal oelek, but we replaced it with sweet red Thai chili sauce, and I can't imagine it tasting any better. Will add orange zest next time to see if that improves on it. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
pepperoni

homemade pepperoni. you have to let it stand in the fridge overnight before baking.

1. combine all ingredients , mixing until thoroughly blended
2. divide in half into slender rolls about 1 1 / 3 inch in diameter
3. wrap in plastic or foil
4. refrigerate overnight
5. unwrap and bake on broiler pan at 200 f for 4 hours
6. store wrapped in the refrigerator
target.review: I'm going to use regular coarse salt, as I can't have nitrates that are in the curing salt. I will probably freeze it in small batches in lieu of that. I update how it went.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever  and most versatile  muffins

these are wonderful for just throwing in your favorite ingredients---i don't need any other muffin recipes. editing to add, based on a recent review: be sure not to overmix muffins; if you do, they will be tough. they should still be lumpy when you are finished mixing them.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. stir together the flour , baking powder , salt and sugar in a large bowl
3. make a well in the center
4. in a small bowl or 2-cup measuring cup , beat egg with a fork
5. stir in milk and oil
6. pour all at once into the well in the flour mixture
7. mix quickly and lightly with a fork until moistened , but do not beat
8. the batter will be lumpy
9. do not overmix
10. this will create tough / heavy muffins
11. pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups
12. variations: blueberry muffins: add 1 cup fresh blueberries
13. raisin muffins: add 1 cup finely chopped raisins
14. date muffins: add 1 cup finely chopped dates
15. cheese muffins: fold in 1 cup grated sharp yellow cheese
16. bacon muffins: fold 1 / 4 cup crisp cooked bacon , broken into bits
17. bake for 25 minutes , or until golden
demonstrations.review: Made this with blueberries and stevia instead of sugar.   They were very good. Totally gone before I could snap a picture!  I did have to add a bit more milk to get it to a muffin batter consistency. My flour may have been a bit dry-- being winter and all.  I am making these again today perhaps with cheese and bacon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome  and economical  chai concentrate

if you like the refreshing and spicy taste of chai half as much as i do, then you're going to love how easy and good this is! i make up a batch once of twice a month and then enjoy my chai.

1. pour condensed milk and spices into the blender and blend on high speed for a few seconds until the milk looks evenly "flecked" with spices
2. pour mixture into a clean jar or container with a lid
3. refrigerate at least 24 hours
4. alternatively , pour mix into ice cube trays and freeze
5. to use concentrate: brew a strong black tea or strong herbal tea of your choice
6. stir in 1 frozen concentrate cube or 1 / 2 to 2 teaspoons of chai concentrate mix per cup of freshly steeped tea
7. frozen cubes will keep up to one year in the freezer if you pop them out of the trays and store in a freezer bag
8. concentrate will keep in the fridge for up to 3 weeks
demonstrations.review:
This is better than store bought.  I've been putting it in coffee as well as tea.  I made my own sweetened and condensed milk using Splenda,as we are an Atkins family. I'm going to start using it in waffles and pancakes.
Thank you-- 
LisaJo

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb cheesecake

i came up with this recipe as i am on a low carb diet. its hard to find desserts to suit.

1. base: melt butter and blend the rest of the ingredients
2. pour into cake tin and cook for 30 minutes on 180f
3. once cooked allow to cool
4. filling: blend cream cheese , sour cream , vanilla essence , lemon and orange / mandarin juice and sugar together
5. once you've reached a smooth and creamy texture blend in one at a time the eggs
6. pour mixture onto base
7. decorate with strawberries
8. as a suggestion using diet jelly that is half set pour over strawberries and then chill cheesecake overnight
9. or if you like chocolate cheesecake just remove the citrus juices and add 1 / 3 cup cocoa powder
10. it really is a yummy treat
demonstrations.review:
THIS WAS GREAT!!!!  However I suspect the wonderful author of this recipe might be British(?)
I think the baking at 180 is for Celsius-- which I converted to 350 Fahrenheit.  I made my own Almond meal by grinding up almonds (I didn't know where to find it). The 125 Grams of melted butter is about 1 Stick, and the 750 grams chream cheese is about 16 oz.  I also shredded my own coconut-- because I couldn't find any that wasn't sweetened with sugar.
Thank you for this wonderful cheesecake.
LisaJo

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade sweetened condensed milk

got this from 

1. stove top version: combine in blender and blend til smooth
2. makes 1 14 oz
3. can
4. keep in fridge
5. micro-wave version in a 2 c
6. measurer , add water , sugar , and butter
7. microwave on high to 1 1 / 2- 2 minutes til boiling , stirring every 30 seconds
8. put in blender with powered milk
9. process til smooth
10. refrigerate
11. makes 1 cup
demonstrations.review:
I used Splenda instead of sugar-- and it's terric.  It didn't make a 14 oz can however.  I found I had to make three batches to get that equivalent.  It was very easy and convenient.
Thanks,
LisaJo

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese and meatball soup

my family loves this soup. 

1. meatballs: mix ingredients together thoroughly
2. shape into medium size meatballs
3. place uncooked meatballs and all other ingredients , except cheez whiz , in electric slow cooker
4. stir gently
5. cover and cook on setting # 2 for 8 to 10 hours
6. before serving add cheez whiz , stirring gently until well blended
demonstrations.review: My husband and I liked this very much. He will be taking it in his lunch this week.  The kids didn't like it!  I think they were all cranky.  I thought it was really delicious.  My 14 year old ate it--he is very adventurous.

target.recipe_text:
parmesan salmon

this is a great recipe for health watchers. use low fat mayo or such. i'm not a fish lover and even i liked this recipe!

1. combine first 4 ingredients in small bowl , adjusting worcestershire sauce to taste
2. mix until smooth
3. spray baking pan with nonstick spray
4. place salmon fillets on pan and coat with mayo mixture
5. bake at 450f for 12-15 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork
target.review: Tasty! I had 4 fillets (about 1 lb.) so I quadrupled the sauce. After coating the salmon on both sides, I spooned the excess on top. Delicious and company-worthy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple meatballs

this is a family favourite; my teenage son eats at least 2 servings himself. cooking time includes the browning of the meatballs, although you can brown them in the oven on a cookie sheet and make the sauce at the same time, saving yourself a little time.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. first , make the meatballs: combine all meatball ingredients in a bowl and mix well
3. shape into 1-inch balls
4. brown them in a nonstick frying pan until browned all over
5. drain on paper towel then place in a large ungreased casserole dish
6. to make sauce , combine brown sugar and cornstarch in a large saucepan , then whisk in the 1-3 / 4 cup pineapple juice / water combination until mixture is smooth
7. add vinegar , soy sauce and worcestershire sauce
8. stir
9. simmer , uncovered , on medium-low heat for about 8 minutes , or until thickened
10. pour sauce over meatballs and add pineapple tidbits
11. stir gently to combine until meatballs are coated with sauce
12. bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes
13. if you want a lot , this recipe doubles well
demonstrations.review: Yummy! Thanks for a great new recipe. I appreciated the clear, detailed way the directions were written, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy ham and potato soup

comfort soup at its finest!  i usually make this to use up leftover ham.  this is easy to adapt with other ingredients.  i don't put celery in mine.  i have added garlic sometimes as well.

1. combine potatoes , celery , carrots , onion , ham , and water / broth in stockpot and bring to boil
2. then cook over medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. stir in the chicken bouillon , salt , and pepper
4. in separate saucepan , melt butter over medium-low heat
5. whisk in flour and cook stirring constantly until thick
6. slowly stir in milk as not to allow lumps to form and all milk is added
7. turn up to medium heat
8. continue to stir until thick
9. add in cheese and stir until melted
10. stir the cheese mixture into the stockpot and cook until heated through
demonstrations.review: Yummy! This will be made again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy and delicious ranch parmesan chicken

there are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, i find that hidden valley ranch dressing works the best but kraft or any other brand will do, i sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although i have only made this using breasts i imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *note* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
for low-fat option: use low-fat ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as smart balance 50/50 blend.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. in a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with parmesan cheese , seasoned salt , black pepper and garlic powder
3. dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides
4. coat in the breadcrumb mixture
5. place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil
6. lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast
7. if desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces
8. bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked)
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I couldn't believe how moist it was inside and how crunchy outside! Next time I would probably use a little less salt, but overall this was amazing and I will definitely be making it again. Thanks Kittencal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot whole chicken

tender, fall-off-the-bone chicken! skip the overnight refrigeration if you are in a hurry. for variety, eliminate the onion and substitute a quartered lemon or two, stuffed into the chicken cavity.  chef shapeweaver had a good suggestion:  use fajita seasoning mix #28011 as another variation.  thanks!  the standard size slow cookers are a bit too small and a whole chicken won't fit.  you'll need a 6-quart slow cooker for this recipe.

1. in a small bowl , combine the spices
2. remove any giblets from chicken and clean chicken
3. rub spice mixture onto the chicken
4. place in resealable plastic bag and refrigerate overnight
5. when ready to cook , put chopped onion in bottom of crock pot
6. add chicken
7. no liquid is needed , the chicken will make its own juices
8. cook on low 4-8 hours
demonstrations.review: I think I cooked it too long (8 hours on low). The chicken was super mushy. I'll try it again sometime and maybe lessen or eliminate the cayenne pepper as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oat n  toffee cookies

to die for!!!

1. cream butter and sugars
2. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
3. beat in vanilla
4. mix flour , oats , baking soda , baking powder and salt
5. gradually add to creamed mixture
6. stir in toffee bits
7. drop by rounded tbs onto ungreased baking sheets
8. bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes , until light golden brown
9. cool 1 minute before removing from pans to wire rack
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious. I only had 8 ounces of toffee but the cookies are still amazing. I think this might be my new favorite cookie recipe!

target.recipe_text:
slow cooker cabbage roll casserole

yummy and less work than the real cabbage rolls.  there is no rice in this recipe, because i don't like rice in my cabbage rolls.

1. spary crock pot with nonstick cooking spray
2. crumble the raw ground turkey and spread along bottom of crock pot
3. add the onions , green pepper , garlic , salt , pepper , thyme and cabbage
4. pour the diced tomatoes over top
5. mix the sugar into the tomato sauce and pour over everything
6. if you like more sauce , add another 8-oz or 15-oz can of tomato sauce
7. cover and cook on low for about 8 hours or on high for about 4 hours
8. when done , remove lid and stir to mix well
target.review: I made this for dinner last night. I only had regular ground beef and I was afraid there'd be a boatload of grease if I didn't modify for that, so I precooked the meat about 70% in the microwave prior to adding it to my crockpot. Other than that I followed the recipe exactly and both my husband and I loved it. It was simple, uses a lot of fresh handy ingredients, smelled lovely cooking and tasted wonderful. Would have been great with rice, but we currently have a lot of squash and zucchini coming from the garden so we grilled some of them and made that our meal. Lovely, just lovely!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
daytona wings    baked teriyaki style chicken wings

growing up in a family of race fans, watching the daytona 500 on tv was something we always looked forward to. mom always made these wings to snack on during the race. once upon a time these were called wing dings, but somewhere along the way they were renamed daytona wings.

1. combine all ingredients except the wings in a large pitcher
2. mix well
3. place chicken wings in single layer in a 9" x 13" pan
4. pour the liquid mixture over the wings
5. marinate at least 2 hours , flipping wings once
6. keep wings refrigerated while marinating
7. bake at 350 degrees for 1 1 / 2 hours
8. flip once during baking
demonstrations.review: Made these last night for our Friday Night Bonfire and they were a hit with everyone. They were super easy to fix. I bought one of those 4 lb. bags of frozen chicken wings and mixed up the marinade and poured it in the bag the wings came in (still frozen) and then left them to marinate and thaw in the fridge until the next day when I cooked them. The taste was fantastic! Will absolutely be making these again. Thanks for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeno chicken wraps

i've been playing around with this recipe from taste of home back yard grilling and think i've got it right for our taste.  this is so good, it can be a meal in itself.  it's a little heat intense, but we like it that way.  we loved the combination of spices.  hope you try it.

1. cut chicken into 2 in strips that will fit the size of your pepper
2. in a large resealable plastic bag , combine the garlic powder , onion powder , pepper , seasoned salt and paprika
3. add chicken and shake to coat
4. place a chicken and onion strip in each jalapeno half
5. wrap each pepper with a slice or two of the shaved smoked ham , enough to cover the entire pepper and place on baking sheet
6. you will need toothpicks if you use bacon or the prosciutto
7. preheat oven to 350 degrees
8. bake peppers for 20-25 minutes or until the ham is slightly browned and chicken juice runs clear
9. you can also grill these:
10. spray your grill with pam
11. grill peppers uncovered , over indiredct medium heat for 20-25 minutes or until chicken juices run clear and ham is slightly brown
12. serve with blue cheese or ranch dressing
13. for a variety , try sprinkling some italian bread crumbs on top before adding the ham it adds to the flavor
demonstrations.review: I have made these twice for parties and they have been devoured! The first time I made exactly by the recipe, but the second time I made some changes. I did saute the onion the 2nd time (we like that better)and I stuffed a tiny bit of pepper-jack cheese into the mix because everything is better with cheese! Also, I wrapped some in ham, some in bacon. Next time I will use a leaner bacon, but other then that this is a GREAT recipe. Oh, and for what it's worth, I cook them and then stick in my crock pot on the warm or low setting and keep them toasty warm...and it gives them a roasted, tenderness that everyone seems to really enjoy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mini muffuletta kabobs

my aunt mary alice made these yesterday for a puppy shower we held at her house.  they were very yummy!

1. layer 1 slice each of smoked ham , provolone cheese , and genoa salami
2. tightly roll up , and slice into 4 equal pieces , repeat procedure 5 times
3. thread 24 wooden skewers with 1 of each: pepperoncini salad pepper , meat-and-cheese roll , 1 -inch-long roasted red bell pepper , and pimiento-stuffed spanish olive
4. place in a 13- x-9-inch baking dish
5. pour dressing over skewers , and chill 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe for our weekly bonfire party last night and everyone seemed to really enjoy them...there weren't any left at the end of the evening and that's usually a good sign that they were a hit! When a recipe is simple, takes just a few ingredients, and everyone likes it, I add it to my keeper list! Thanks for a neat recipe :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my own cube steak and gravy

this recipe is a old family favorite that i get asked to make at least twice a month and serve with my cream potatoes.

1. in a bowl or plastic bag add flour , salt , onion powder , garlic powder and black pepper
2. add cubed steak in flour mixture and coat well
3. heat oil and butter in a large frying pan
4. add cubed steak and brown on both sides for 15 minutes
5. remove cubed steak and drain grease out of pan , leaving some dripping grease in pan
6. add can of mushroom soup , water and heavy whipping cream or milk to the pan drippings and mix well
7. add cubed steak back to pan and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes
8. turning cubed steaks once during simmering
demonstrations.review: I made this last night for dinner, and everyone, including my picky teenage son, really loved it. It was relatively simple, used ingredients I had on hand, and got rave reviews from the family. I call that a success!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dads sausage  peppers and onions

my dads recipe, personally i can't get enough of this, very easy and fast too. it uses the jars of red peppers along with fresh.

1. remove casings from sausage
2. cook and crumble till brown in a large pot along with fresh bell pepper , onion and garlic
3. chop jarred red peppers smaller and add to sausage with their juice
4. simmer on low
5. prepare the linguini according to package instructions , drain
6. add to sausage mixture and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner last night. I had the ingredients on hand, and it was a relaxed Saturday evening. I didn't want to extend myself too much in the kitchen...so I put this together in just a few minutes, fixed some bruschetta to go along with, and it was excellent. I'm adding this to my "keeper" file!

target.recipe_text:
black eyed pea masala

this is a recipe that i adapted from a recipe my mil made while i was in india. it is fabulous, and is even served for breakfast quite often in her house! (i could eat it for every meal lol)  i donut know the actual name of the chilies they use, but at home i generally use either 2 of the small chiles labeled "hot green chiles" from the market, or i use serranos. the ginger i generally just run over my microplane.

1. drain your peas
2. heat oil / ghee in a medium heavy pot over medium heat and fry chiles , garlic , onion , and ginger for approx 6 minutes
3. add your curry powder / garam masala , turmeric and cumin , and then add the tomatoes
4. cook for approximately 3 minutes until it begins to thicken and add your peas and salt to taste , along with 4 cups of water
5. allow water to boil and then reduce your heat , cover and cook for approximately 2 hours until your peas are done and the sauce is nice and thick
6. after the peas are done , fold in your yogurt and cilantro , and serve
7. this goes well with rice or with chappati / roti
8. garnish with minced cilantro
target.review: This recipe completely exceeded my expectations!  I made this for new years day, thinking it would be fun to have black eyed peas for the new year.  I will be making this again before next year.  I used half indian curry & half garam masala.  This was a great slow cooked on the oven all day vegetarian dish that makes the house smell wonderful and you can't wait to eat.  Next time I might experiment with chickpeas, I think that would be great too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
noo s famous spiced green chicken skewers

this is a minimum effort maximum flavour recipe. every summer we barbecue as much as we can (well i do live in england!) and i always have to make loads of these to throw on the barbie. not only that, if i go to a friends barbie, i always get asked to bring some of my "green chicken thingies"--hence the name! they are so easy to do, but the flavours are great. i like to use little chicken fillets if i can, but strips of chicken breast are fine. you can of course just grill these off indoors, but itï¿½s not quite the same without that char grill flavour you get from a barbecue. they are also great hot or cold tucked into some pita bread with some salad ! nb-don't forget to soak the skewers if they are wooden! timings do not include marinating time.
i just have to add that this is now a prize winning recipe..having been submitted for a competition here in adelaide, i got invited along for a cook off with five others, and won a top of the range weber q barbecue and a stack of weber goodies to go with it...along with plenty of rave reviews!!
note: i don't recommend using all ground coriander and no fresh coriander..it really isn't the same at all.

1. cut the chicken lengthwise into strips
2. put the remaining ingredients into a food processor and whiz until smooth
3. in a bowl , coat the chicken in the marinade
4. cover and chill for at least two hours
5. when you are ready to cook , thread the chicken , concertina style onto the skewers
6. grill over hot coals , basting with any remaining marinade
demonstrations.review: These were delicious!  I doubled the chili's because I like spice.  I also did not bother pureeing everything in the food processor.  I just chopped everything up fine and marinated overnight.  I sprinkled some fresh cilantro on the chicken after I took it off the grill also.  This one is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s 1 gram low fat banana blueberry muffins

less than 1 gram of fat in each muffin  but you wouldn't even know they are low-fat, these are even better the next day, and are just as delicious without the berries, of coarse you can use full-fat sour cream or yogurt, flavored yogurts only add to the taste of these muffins, i like to sprinkle a sugar/cinnamon mixture on top of each muffin before baking but that is optional, see note on bottom for doubling the recipe. for greasing see recipe#78579 --- visit www.kittencalskitchen.com for more low fat recipes!

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease or line 12 regular-size muffin tins with paper liners
3. in a large bowl mix together flour , baking powder , baking soda , salt cinnamon , nutmeg and blueberries
4. in another bowl beat banana , sour cream , sugar , egg and vanilla until just blended
5. stir into the dry blueberry mixture just until combined
6. scoop / divide the mixture between the muffin tins
7. bake for 15-20 minutes or until the muffins test done
demonstrations.review: A great healthy muffin!  I made six x-large muffins with this recipe.  Next time I think I may try adding in some whole wheat flour also.  My only wish is that this recipe made more!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet and spicy empanadas

these are more sweet than spicy and there are a few surprise ingredients that really make these little beef bites quite delicious!  my husband is a "dipper" and created the tomato-based sauce that perfectly complements these non-traditional empanadas.  the recipe makes 24 bite-sized appetizers, or you can make them twice as big and eat them for dinner. :)

1. for the sauce:
2. combine all ingredients and whisk till smooth
3. for the empanadas:
4. take the pastry sheets out of the freezer 40 minutes before your empanadas will be ready to be filled
5. preheat the oven to 400 degrees
6. peel the potatoes and dice them fairly small
7. cover them with water and simmer for 10-15 minutes , or till tender
8. meanwhile , mince the onion and place in a large bowl with the beef , all the sugar and spices , and the milk
9. knead with your hands until the mixture is very soft
10. cook the meat mixture in a skillet over medium heat until the beef is browned
11. drain the potatoes and mix them in with the meat
12. drain any excess fat
13. cut the pastry into 24 equal rectangles and divide the mixture between them
14. divide the cream cheese into 24 portions as well and squish it on top of the meat so it evenly covers
15. fold the pastry over and seal the edges by folding or pinching
16. place on baking sheet and bake for 13-15 minutes , or until puffy and golden brown
17. remove from oven , place on serving plate , and dip in the sauce if you desire !
demonstrations.review: This was a really great recipe.  The dipping sauce set this over the top!  I tried blending the cream cheese in with the filling as another reviewer suggested.  I would not recommend this as it kind of gave the filling the appearance canned dog food.  Next time I think I may try spreading the cream cheese first or LIGHLTY tossing with the filling at the last minute.  Overall, this was a truly great and unique combo of flavors.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato pie tomato bread

locals make this with creole tomatoes.

1. preheat oven 350 degrees
2. thoroughly mix mayonnaise , cheddar cheese , minced onions , herbs and pepper
3. set aside
4. in large mixing bowl , mix together baking mix , baking powder , buttermilk and water
5. with floured fingers , pat mixture into the bottom and sides of a lightly greased and floured 9" pie pan
6. bake crust 10 minutes
7. remove from oven
8. arrange tomato slices on top of crust to completely cover
9. cut smaller pieces of tomato to fill in gaps
10. at this point you may want to lightly salt the tomatoes
11. spread mayonnaise mixture over tomatoes and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
12. bake until biscuit is nicely browned and top is bubbly , about 30 to 40 minutes
13. cut into wedges and served still warm or if made ahead , briefly reheat in low oven
14. refrigerate leftovers
demonstrations.review: I absolutely loved this with the biscuit crust instead of a pie dough crust.  This is definately the best tomato pie recipe out there.  I used half cheddar and half mozzarella cheese, and then realized I was out of Parm cheese.  Next time will make sure I have parm cheese as well.  Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese black rice orange and avocado salad

from: "whole grains every day, every way" by lorna sass. "china meets the southwest in this unusual fusion salad. glistening chinese black rice--usually sold under the label forbidden black rice--set off against bright orange segments and avocado's pale green gives the mixture striking visual appeal." *time does not include time it takes to cook rice.

1. in a bowl , combine the cooked rice , oranges , orange juice , pumpkin seeds , orange zest , salt , and chipotle
2. gently mix in the avocado
3. add more salt , if needed
4. place a lettuce cup on each plate and spoon the salad into the lettuce cups
5. garnish with orange wedges , if desired
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe with some leftover black rice I had from a previous meal.  This made a nice light lunch.  The contrast of flavors was excellent.

target.recipe_text:
penne with spicy vodka tomato cream sauce

i found this on another website, but haven't had a chance to try it yet.  hearty italian sausage sauteed with garlic and red pepper flakes are simmered with tomatoes and cooked with vodka and cream to make a rich, spicy sauce.  toss with penne and fresh parsley to serve.

1. bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil
2. add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente , drain
3. in large skillet , heat oil over moderate heat
4. add sausage , breaking up the meat , until brown
5. add garlic and red pepper and cook , stirring until garlic is golden brown
6. add tomatoes and salt
7. bring to boil
8. reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes
9. add vodka and cream and bring to boil
10. reduce heat to low and add pasta , toss for 1 minute
11. stir in fresh parsley and serve ,
target.review: This is an easy to make fabulous dish! Thanks for posting, my husband requests it often. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
biscuit topped creamy chicken or turkey casserole

this is a pretty simple basic comfort food recipe, but it's darn good! you can really add in any veggies that you like even corn niblets are good too...if desired mix the melted butter with garlic powder and then brush over the biscuits. make certain the the creamed chicken mixture is hot before putting it in the casserole dish otherwise the bicuits will get baked before the casserole gets hot and cooked.

1. set oven to 375 degrees
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. in a saucepan combine soup , cheddar cheese , parmesan , chopped onion and mayo
4. bring to a boil and simmer for 2-3 minutes , stirring occasionally
5. add in the cooked cubed chicken , frozen mixed veggies , mushrooms and cheddar cheese
6. mix to combine until heated through and the cheese has melted then season with black pepper
7. pour the hot chicken or turkey mixture into the prepared baking dish
8. separate the refrigerated biscuit dough into 8 biscuits , then arrange over the hot chicken mixture
9. brush each biscuit with melted butter
10. sprinkle finely grated cheese around each of the biscuits
11. bake for about 23-30 minutes , or until the biscuits are baked and the casserole is bubbly
demonstrations.review: This casserole is great! My DH loved it and requests it regularly. Thanks :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pappadeaux crawfish bisque

nan

1. boil crawfish in a large pot of water
2. drain and cool until crawfish can be handled easily , remove tail and save shells
3. refrigerate tail meat
4. heat oil in large sauce pan or dutch oven
5. add crawfish shells , paprika and cayenne
6. saute 5 minutes
7. add water and bring to boil
8. reduce heat and simmer 30 minutes
9. strain liquid into another pan
10. crush shells to remove remaining liquid and add that liquid
11. discard shells
12. return to heat and add onion , bell pepper , tomato paste , cream and tomato
13. simmer 1 hour , stirring frequently
14. add brandy and crawfish tail meat
15. simmer 10 minutes
16. serve hot
demonstrations.review: HALF the water to 1 quart and DOUBLE or TRIPLE the paprika and cayenne pepper. I did this and was MUCH BETTER!  This recipe has all the right ingredients, just the completely wrong amounts. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jo mama s world famous spaghetti

my kids will give up a steak dinner for this spaghetti. it is a recipe i have been perfecting for years and it is so good (if i may humbly say) that my kids are disappointed when they eat spaghetti anywhere else but home! in fact they tell me i should open a restaurant and serve only this spaghetti and garlic bread. in response to requests, i have posted the recipe for recipe #28559 that uses approximately 1/2 of the sauce from this 
recipe. have spaghetti one night and lasagna later!  thanks to all of you who have tried my recipe and have written a review.  i read and appreciate every one of them!  chef note:  after i posted this recipe i remembered a funny incident--my dear husband usually has a nice bottle of wine handy so when i make a batch of spaghetti i just help myself to a splash of it. on one occasion, there wasn't a bottle opened, but there was a bottle sitting on the counter so i got out the corkscrew and helped myself. for some reason, the spaghetti that night was the best ever. my husband asked what wine i put in it and i showed him the bottle. he nearly fell off the chair. i had opened a rather expensive bottle he had bought to give his boss. goes to show you--don't use a wine for cooking you wouldn't drink. you get the best results from a good wine!

1. in large , heavy stockpot , brown italian sausage , breaking up as you stir
2. add onions and continue to cook , stirring occasionally until onions are softened
3. add garlic , tomatoes , tomato paste , tomato sauce and water
4. add basil , parsley , brown sugar , salt , crushed red pepper , and black pepper
5. stir well and barely bring to a boil
6. stir in red wine
7. simmer on low , stirring frequently for at least an hour
8. a longer simmer makes for a better sauce , just be careful not to let it burn !
9. cook spaghetti according to package directions
10. spoon sauce over drained spaghetti noodles and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Fabulous! I used half sausage / half ground beef.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tater tot green bean surprise

the surprise is that this is delicious! this comes from my friend, shawna, and is ridiculously easy to make. it seems to get even better the second day.

1. brown ground turkey , season to taste , drain and set aside
2. heat oven to 425 degrees
3. line the bottom of an 11x13 rectangular baking dish with the frozen tater tots
4. layer the browned ground meat next , then the green beans
5. in a bowl or large measuring cup mix the soup and enough milk that when mixed with the soup makes it easy to pour but not excessively runny
6. pour mixture on top of the green beans and spread around to coat the top of the casserole
7. top with the shredded cheddar cheese
8. bake for 30-45 minutes until casserole is bubbly and the cheese is melted and starting to brown
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! I added onions to the meat and to the green beans for extra flavor. And French's fried onions to the top. DH really enjoyed!  So easy and tasty! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
alfredo shrimp tilapia

this is my version of ruby tuesday's new orleans tilapia. tilapia fillets are baked then topped with alfredo sauce, sauteed red peppers and garlic cooked shrimp. i'm not very good at copycatting recipes, but we had this last night and it was mighty fine.

1. preheat oven to 425
2. wash and dry tilapia filets , spread with olive oil and creole seasoning , to your taste
3. place in well oiled baking pan , bake for 8-10 minutes , until just white
4. while fish is baking , saute slivers of red pepper in 1 tbs butter , until cooked , about 5 minutes
5. warm alfredo in a small saucepan
6. in a frypan , melt 3 tbs butter , add minced garlic and cleaned , prepared shrimp , saute for about 5 minutes
7. when fish is ready , remove from pan from oven
8. carefully remove fillets , 4 per plate
9. place one quarter of the red pepper slivers and one quarter of the cooked shrimp on top of fillets
10. top with 1 / 4 cup of alfredo , sprinkle of grated cheese and a dusting of more creole seasoning
11. if you like , you can put this under the broiler for about a minute
demonstrations.review: Very tasty, I used more seasoning and garlic.

target.recipe_text:
instant iced cafe mocha latte

i make this using decaf coffee and my 7 year old loves it...and i do too!  an easy, awesome summer drink.

1. mix coffee granules and boiling water
2. add sweetened condensed milk and cold water until completely blended
3. mix in chocolate milk and add cold milk
4. chill at least one hour and serve over ice
target.review: OMG this was to die for!!!!! I have been on a Starbucks Mocho Frappachino kick lately and this was just as good and way cheaper. Thank you for saving my budget.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter cookies with chocolate chunks

a little bit different peanut butter cookie that tastes great.  half a bag of semisweet chocolate chunks can be used in place of the chopped semisweet chocolate.

1. mix flour , oats , baking soda and salt
2. beat peanut butter , brown sugar , butter , honey
3. egg and yanilla in large bowl until well blended
4. stir dry ingredients into peanut butter mixture in 2 additions
5. stir in chopped chocolate
6. cover and refrigerate until dough is firm and no longer sticky , about 30 minutes
7. preheat oven to 350
8. with hands , roll 1 heaping tablespoonful of dough for each cookie into 1 3 / 4 inch ball
9. arrange cookies on lightly greased baking sheets , spacing 2 1 / 2 inches apart
10. bake cookies until puffed
11. beginning to brown on top and still very soft to touch , about 12 minutes
12. cool cookies on baking sheets 5 minutes
13. transfer cookies to rack to cool completely
demonstrations.review: How can you go wrong with cookies! Yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
refried bean supreme

this is soooo good!

1. mix beans and half of the cheese in a microwaveable safe dish
2. cover
3. microwave on high for 3min
4. sprinkle with remaining cheese
5. microwave until cheese is melted
6. sprinkle with green onions and tomato
demonstrations.review: This was so good and cheesy. My whole family just loved it. Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french vanilla frozen coffee  drink

okay, so i really like iced coffee, so one day i tried putting it in a blender and this is what i came up with. very easy and yummy. enjoy. note: prep time doesn't include brew time or chill time on coffee. i brew it for hot coffee one day and take leftovers and put in fridge for this.

1. mix coffee , sugar and creamer
2. pour into blender and add ice cubes
3. blend until smooth
4. top with chocolate syrup and cool whip if you want
demonstrations.review:
YUMMMMMM YUMMMMMMM YUMMMMMM!!!
I made this on a hot 100+ degree day and it really hit the spot. Thank you for adding another iced coffee to my collection.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic blt sandwich

this is a sandwich that i crave a lot.  i am just posting it because i couldn't find it posted already on the zaar...i couldn't believe that!  my ex-dh wondered how i make these, so i decided to post it and send him the recipe.  nothing fancy -- just the real, simple, unabridged version.  update:  after reading peg629's review, i have tried it that way, with one slice of toast spread with yellow mustard, and i must say it really, really makes an exceptional blt!  such a subtle difference, yet genuinely makes a superior blt, in my opinion!  (thank you peg629 for that awesome suggestion!)

1. cook bacon until crispy , then drain on paper towels
2. toast the 8 slices of bread
3. spread 1 tablespoon mayo on each slice of toasted bread
4. add 1 slice of lettuce to 4 pieces of mayo-spreaded toast
5. add 2 slices of tomato on top of lettuce
6. arrange 3 slices of bacon evenly on top of tomato
7. add 1 slice of lettuce on top of bacon
8. put the remaining 4 pieces of mayo-spreaded toast on top to finish the sandwiches
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Absolutly PERFECT. I love BLT's and this is exactly how I make them... only I add avocado to my sandwich. Thank you for a great lunch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese stuffed hawaiian pizza

from taste of home's "cooking for 2", a good, quick & easy recipe with lots of possibilities.  i used deli ham and a mix of cheddar, monteray jack and mozzarella cheeses.  recipe says it yields 2 servings but i managed to eat most of it myself! enjoy!

1. place one tortilla on a baking sheet coated with nonstick cooking spray
2. sprinkle with 1 cup cheese
3. top with second tortilla
4. spread with pizza sauce
5. sprinkle with pineapple , ham and remaining cheese
6. bake at 375 for 15 minutes or until tortillas are crisp and cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: This was a great recipe. I love Hawaiian pizzas and don't get them that often because nobody else cares for them. I made this for my lunch and now I can make them often. Thank you.

target.recipe_text:
peanut butter banana muffins

i found this tasty muffin recipe in a magazine ad for quaker oats.

1. heat oven to 375f
2. grease 12 medium muffin cups , or line with paper baking cups
3. combine flour , oats , brown sugar and baking powder
4. whisk together milk , peanut butter , banana , egg , oil and vanilla
5. add to dry ingredients , mixing just until moistened
6. fill muffin cups 3 / 4 full
7. combine topping ingredients
8. sprinkle evenly over batter
9. bake 16 to 18 minutes or until golden brown
10. serve warm
target.review: Very yummy! It was the first time I was trying to make a quick bread with peanut butter and I must say, I'm impressed. However, I never found 1 tbsp of baking powder to work well, so I stuck to my usual - 1 tsp of baking powder, 1/2 tsp of baking soda. And because of the baking soda (it needs acidity), I replaced the milk with buttermilk. I made it into a loaf and baked about 40 mins.. I omitted the topping but it was still really yummy! Thank you so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate banana chocolate chip bundt cake

after first trying this years ago my 2nd son declared -who needs banana bread?! - and this became our favorite choice for doing away with overripe bananas. the recipe originally had an optional chocolate glaze, i've always skipped it and just added a light dusting of confectionary sugar. this is a pretty sturdy cake which makes it great for picnics, potlucks and lunch bags - the same son recently took 1/2 a cake with him for the drive back to s.ca!
 an extra note - seeing some of the comments - this is not a tall cake it only rises a littel  more than half way up the pan. ovens are different - go with a shorter cooking time and check to see if needs more.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees , grease or spray a bundt pan and lightly dust with cocoa powder
2. mix together dry ingredients , set aside
3. cream butter , add sugar and eggs , mix well , then add bananas and mix briefly
4. mix in dry ingredients until incorporated , don't over mix , stir in chocolate chips
5. pour into prepared pan and bake 50- 60 minutes until it tests done , cake will just start to pull away from edges
6. cool slightly then remove from pan
7. your supposed to let it cool all the way then dust with confectionary sugar , but my kids always slice it warm , which is good with vanilla ice cream
8. i always use a pan release spray and dust with the cocoa , and have almost never had a problem with the cake sticking
9. if greasing the pan - do it well and use a bit more cocoa as you would flour
demonstrations.review: WOW! This cake was awesome! I was looking for a banana chocolate chip cake to bake for my cousin when I found this. I made 12 cupcakes out of these cuz I did not have a bundt pan, and honestly it's the fluffiest cupcakes ever! My cousin devoured it like it was the best cake in the world! :) Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
30 minute dinner rolls

i made these one time to go with soup that we were having for dinner. i made the dough balls too big and/or let them rise too much and they ended up being huge, but they were good and they were easy to make.

1. mix warm water , oil , sugar and yeast
2. let rest for 10 minutes until yeast activates
3. add salt and beaten egg
4. blend well
5. add flour , one cup at a time until soft dough if formed
6. knead on a floured surface 5-10 minutes or until dough is smooth and elastic
7. shape into small balls and put into a greased baking pan
8. let rise at least 5-10 minutes
9. bake at 425 degrees for 15-20 minutes
10. if you have more time , you can let the rolls rise in the pan until they have doubled in size
demonstrations.review: I usually am a loaf-of-bread kind of girl, but since dad wanted some rolls and there wasn't any space in the fridge (most dinner rolls have to be refrigerated overnight),  I thought I'd give this recipe a try. These were awesome! Soft and fluffy! I let the rolls rise for about 35 mins and baked them for 20 mins. Thank you so much for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate banana bread

from a local volunteer cookbook

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease loaf pan
3. combine margarine , sugar , eggs and vanilla in a bowl
4. beat on medium speed until moistened
5. mash bananas and add with milk
6. beat on low to blend
7. add next five ingredients
8. beat on low until flour mixture is moistened
9. use a spoon to fold in the walnuts
10. pour batter into loaf pan
11. bake on centre rack 50-60 minutes
12. remove from oven and let stand 15 minutes on a wire rack
13. remove from pan
14. cool completely
demonstrations.review: This is EASILY my favorite bread! Very moist, very chocolatey, very very good! And I agree, it's even moister the next day! The minute I finished eating it, I had the urge of making it again. It was THAT good! :) Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white batter bread

this simple recipe will give you 2 beautiful, delicious loaves of bread. try it warm with butter and jam, wow!! prep time is the rising.

1. dissolve yeast in water , in a large bowl
2. add half the flour , and the sugar , salt , and shortning
3. blend at low speed , then beat 2 minutes at med speed
4. mix in remaining flour by hand
5. cover and let rise until doubled , about 45 minutes
6. stir the batter hard for 30 seconds
7. spread into 2 8in greased loaf pans
8. let rise until doubled , about 20 minutes
9. bake at 325 for about 45 minutes , until golden brown and done
demonstrations.review: I couldn't wait to try my hand at making a batter bread. This was the first time I was going to attempt something with yeast in it (I am always making quick breads) so I was nervous. But it was beautifully baked and just the right consistency and texture! :) Thanks for the recipe, MissNez!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
singin  the blues  muesli

late august is blueberry season here in newfoundland, and what better way to use them than in a fruity, oaty breakfast?

1. mix together the oats , soymilk and dates
2. do let soak overnight in the fridge
3. in the morning , dice and stir in the apple
4. cut the banana lengthwise into quarters , then slice
5. stir these small banana pieces along with the blueberries , into the muesli
6. it's totally delicious without any nuts or seeds , but i like them anyway for some crunch
7. my favorites here are pumpkin seeds
8. almonds are also good
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I can't believe how something so healthy can be sooooo delicious!! I have made this a total of  6 times and I just can't get enough of it! YUMMY! It's the best breakfast on earth :) Thanks a million!

target.recipe_text:
new england baked kidney beans in the crock pot

if you like kidney beans, then this is a recipe not to be missed!  rich in flavor and absolutely delicious!  serve with boston brown bread and you have one fabulous meal!  i use my 6 qt. crock pot and there is plenty of room. preparation time does not include soaking beans overnight.  the cooking time is approximate, so check your beans periodically.

1. rinse dry beans in cold water
2. place in a lg
3. bowl , and cover with 2" of cold water
4. let soak overnight in refrigerator
5. drain , and rinse beans
6. put beans in a lg
7. crock pot with the rest of the ingredients
8. cook on high 12-14 hours or on low for 24 hrs
9. , or until beans are soft , and juice is thick
10. stir occasionally
11. check water occasionally to make sure there is enough water in the beans , so they don't boil dry
12. if you use a smaller size crock pot cut the recipe in 1 / 2 , and cook until beans are done
13. i always use my large crock pot , so i'm not sure how long it takes
target.review: I always know where to go when I want good beans now that I have this recipe!  Wow were these awesome!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dusty s stuffed mushrooms

recipe from a late dear friend.

1. combine crab meat , breadcrumbs , egg , onion , green pepper , garlic powder , worcestershire sauce and diced mushroom stems
2. pack each mushroom cap with crab meat mixture and top with a pat of butter
3. broil until brown or bake at 350f for 20-25 minutes until heated through and the mushrooms are beginning to leak their water
demonstrations.review: I omitted the green peppers but made the same otherwise and they were delicious with a good squirt of lemon over the top before serving!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrot pineapple muffins

moist and light. these are the only way my toddlers will eat carrots.

1. stir together sugar and oil
2. stir in the eggs until well combined
3. stir in vanilla
4. in a separate bowl , combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , cinnamon and salt
5. stir into sugar mixture just until combined
6. stir in carrots and pineapple just until combined
7. spoon into greased muffin tin , filling to top
8. bake in a preheated 375f oven for 20 minutes or until done
9. cool in pan for 5-10 minutes , then remove to a rack to finish cooling
demonstrations.review: Added nuts to the mix and they were to die for good!  Wouldn't change a thing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s asian salmon

i wanted to try my hand at creating an asian style marinade for salmon.  this came out great and i wanted to share it with all of you.  i hope you will try it!  delish!  serve alongside your favorite asian inspired rice or noodle dish, and my recipe for recipe #218814, for one meal to remember!  we serve it with my son's recipe for recipe #318992 with some sweet soy sauce drizzled over the top.

1. mix together all the ingredients in a container big enough to fit the fish
2. add the fish to the marinade , and let sit in the refrigerator for 1 / 2 hours
3. preheat grill to medium heat
4. lightly grease grill rack with oil
5. remove salmon from marinade , reserving the marinade
6. grill 12-15 minutes per 1" of thickness , or until fish flakes easily with a fork
7. brush fish with reserved marinade while cooking , up until the last 5 minutes on the grill
8. dispose of any leftover marinade
9. plate , and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I would give this 10 stars if you had them!  The fish was incredibly flavored! A new favorite Asian dish for us and we will have it often when we feel like having fish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simply elegant salad with balsamic raspberry vinaigrette

i came up with this salad one day and loved it! now i bring this salad to dinner parties and it's always a huge hit. the two different vinaigrettes mixed together are a perfect combination of sweet, tart and tangy. for dinner parties with people i don't know well i usually leave the almonds and dressing on the side in case anyone has food allergies; only once has anyone passed on the almonds and dressing.  this salad is also great topped with grilled chicken to make the salad a complete dinner.

1. in a medium sized bowl mix the two vinegarettes and black pepper together , stir until well blended
2. set aside
3. in a large bowl toss lettuce , cuccumbers , onions , grapes , tomatoes and almonds
4. add to veggies the desired amount of dressing , cheese , and more almonds
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Great lunch salad with some chicken or shrimp added!  We love the Vinaigrette!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cole slaw on hot dogs

i have been eating these since my childhood.  normally i make these with leftover slaw so the ratio of slaw may be off.  the recipe was inspired by recipe #262230 which was posted by chef rickoholic83.  the dressing makes a wonderful dressing for coleslaw.  you may have leftover dressing, it can also be served on a fruit salad or lettuce wedges.

1. for the dressing , in a small bowl combine the mayonnaise and red wine vinegar
2. mix together the cabbage , carrot , red onion , and sun dried tomatoes
3. stir in enough of the dressing to moisten the cabbage mixture to your liking , add the ketchup and mix well
4. add salt and pepper to taste , refrigerate the coleslaw until ready to serve , 4 to 5 hours is suggested in order for the flavors to blend
5. boil hot dogs in water , place one in steamed bun top with generous amounts of slaw and enjoy
6. please
demonstrations.review: Yummy hot dogs.  We all loved the cole slaw addition.  We had with baked beans and homemade rolls.  Delicious!

target.recipe_text:
easiest beef enchiladas ever

best enchilada recipe i've found. we love the spicy, cheesy flavor of these.

1. brown meat and onions in large skillet
2. add 1 cup enchilada sauce and 1 cup cheese
3. mix well
4. put filling along center of each tortilla
5. roll up and place seam side down in a 9x13 pan
6. pour remaining sauce over
7. sprinkle remaining cheese over
8. bake at 350f degrees for about 30 minutes till cheese is bubbly
target.review: These are not enchiladas.. sorry

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chicken tortilla soup

i'm in love with this soup!! a very good friend of mine made this for me recently and i fell in love. i'm very picky about my tortilla soup and this by far the best ever. she makes hers in the crock pot and i have to agree, that it's easy and tastes just wonderful!! whatever you do, do not skip the garnishes! they are the icing on the cake! update april 2010:  obviously i've made this so many times i never even look at the recipe anymore!  but i wanted to add some variations that i play around with that are great.  like many reviewers black beans and corn are great additions.  sometimes i add them to the leftovers (if there are any :-) so that is feels like something new the next day!  i have also made it several times with shredded pork which turns it into a pork carnitas type of soup.  if you like it on the spicy and smoke side buy a can of chipotle peppers in adobo sauce and mince up one or two and add it.  and lastly, a little swizzle of half and half or heavy cream just minutes before serving makes it a creamy tortilla soup that is wonderful and it is also a good way to tone down the heat if it got away from you...

1. throw everything except the garnishes in your crock pot and let it cook on high for 5-6 hours
2. dress with garnishes and give it a squeeze of lime and you're good to go !
3. enjoy !
4. if you are not using a crock pot , saute the garlic and onion in 2 tablespoons olive oil before adding the remaining ingredients
5. simmer for at least an hour so that the flavors mix together
demonstrations.review: This recipe is wonderful.  I made it over the stove, adding some green chilies for an extra kick. Also added a splash of dry white wine.  Served it with homemade tortilla chips.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon wrapped garlic asparagus bundles

a bundle of asparagus is drizzled with garlic steeped olive oil, wrapped in bacon and roasted.  the flavor of this is outstanding.

1. saute garlic and parsley over low heat , then set aside to steep
2. remove ends from asparagus that are tough
3. lay 4 stalks of asparagus in the center of each strip of bacon and sprinkle with salt and pepper
4. drizzle garlic oil over each bundle
5. wrap bacon around the stalks and secure with a toothpick
6. place asparagus bundles on baking sheet and bake at 400 for 20 minutes or until asparagus is tender and bacon is crisp
demonstrations.review: Didn't change a thing- this recipe is perfect just as it is.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkish red lentil soup

another delectable entry for the zaar world tour from the enticing world vegetarian cookbook by madhur jaffrey.  this is simple enough to prepare midweek and comforting as the first cold air of fall arrives.

1. place the red lentils in a colandar and rinse
2. sift through to remove and debris or damaged beans
3. place the washed and cleaned lentils into a medium pot with the stock , potatoes , onions and paprika
4. bring the pot to a boil and reduce to a simmer
5. loosely place a lid on the pot leaving slightly ajar as to allow some evaporation
6. cook for 40-40 minutes until the lentils are tender
7. add salt and pepper to taste
8. place all but 1 cup of the soup into a blender or food processor and blend briefly
9. return blended soup to the pot with the reserved cup of soup
10. heat through
11. serve
demonstrations.review: A bit bland.. I added red chilies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican ceviche

this dish is a regular served on the beaches of mexico. serve it as a seafood appetizer or as a side salad dish. you can alter it to suit your own taste. make it as spicy or as mild as you wish. my friends all love it. i often use shrimp & fish or shrimp & scallops - when i do this i do not marinate the shrimp as the shrimp tend to get tough. i steam the shrimp and add them a few hours before serving as i mix all the ingredients together. in mexico when they make this they often add sea water (not recommened).  if you are using frozen fish, choose a firm-fleshed fish and make sure it is fully thawed with as much moisture as possible removed.

1. dice the fish
2. marinate fish in the lime juice in the fridge overnight
3. stir often
4. pour off most of the lime juice
5. add remaining ingredients except lettuce , avocado and olive
6. do this preferably a few hours before serving & refrigerate
7. toss well and arrange in individual serving bowls that are lined with the lettuce leaves
8. if you wish garnish with sliced avocado and sliced black olives
demonstrations.review: Reminds me of vacation.. I like to add steamed octopus as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan broiled flounder

this easy and delicious recipe is a classic!

1. place fillets in a single layer on a lightly greased or pan sprayed , shallow oven-to-table type broiler pan
2. brush with lemon juice
3. in a small bowl , combine remaining ingredients to make the cheese topping mixture
4. set aside
5. broil fillets 4 to 6 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork
6. remove fillets from oven
7. spread with parmesan topping
8. broil an additional 30 seconds or until cheese is lightly browned and bubbly
9. garnish with lemon twists and parsley , if desired
10. since the flounder in the recipe is not marinated , if the fish comes out mushy i suspect the results are the from overcooking
11. either the fish was left under the broiler for too long , the temperature of the broiler is too high , or the rack on which the the pan placed under the broiler is too close to the heat
demonstrations.review: I cannot give this recipe enough stars.  Works well with other mild fish too.  Fast and impressive tasting.

target.recipe_text:
mama s best  macaroni and cheese

my kids say this is better than 'the blues' and gobble it up, even when i toss in a handful of cooked veggies like broccoli, peas, carrots, etc.... make it a one dish meal with some tuna, cooked ham, etc... it is just as easy as the 'blue box' at least i think so and it is much healthier!

1. make a roux by melting butter in pan and adding flour
2. stir constantly and cook until it is the color of caramel candy
3. it burns easily so stir stir stir !
4. slowly and carefully add milk while stirring
5. when milk starts to steam add cheese and seasonings and stir until melted and well combined
6. pour over cooked macaroni noodles and serve
target.review: Great recipe! I did have slight problems, but it was my fault. Definitely will make again!! :) I followed it almost exactly - used a squirt of prepared mustard, as that's all I have; and used colby cheese instead of cheddar. Just bought the kids some Cars macaroni pasta and was looking forward to trying out a stovetop mac-n-cheese recipe. Even my pickiest ate some of it. For future reference, don't try to make this in a large pan.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pete s scratch pancakes

it was the fall of 1987 when pete nyhus walked into our office, just to visit. we started talking about breakfast, and he reached into a wastepaper basket and pulled out a scrap of teletype paper. he wrote out this recipe, and my family has never used pre-mix since.

1. mix the dry items first
2. combine the eggs and melted butter to the milk and slowly stir into the flour mixture
3. let sit at least 10 minutes while heating the pan
4. these will be high , but light and fluffy --
demonstrations.review: These were wonderful!! My kids went crazy over them. I used slightly soured milk and these turned out very close to Denny's pancakes, IMO. The only thing is I used salted butter and used the salt and the taste was a tad on the salty side, but evidently kids didn't mind. :) Next time I will only add a dash of salt with my salted butter. Wonderful with homemade caramel sauce!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
applesauce cereal snacks or bars

made this up to give my toddler a healthy and yummy snack--and to use up some of the millions of cheerios we seem to always have in the pantry!  great to take to play groups, no eggs or honey so even young babies can share.  substitute any cereal you want!

1. mix all ingeredients in a medium bowl until well blended
2. optional-throw a tbs or two of soy flour in to boost up the protine of a picky child's diet !
3. spray pan with cooking spay
4. to make bars press into a 9x9 pan
5. to make bite sized snacks , spread loosely onto a jelly roll pan
6. bake at 350 20-30 minutes unyil crisp and golden--watch the snacks , they cook faster
7. cut or crumble , cool and enjoy !
8. store in an air tight container , they never last more than a couple days at our house so i'm not sure how long they are shelf stable
9. servings are approximate
demonstrations.review:
Wow! These are good! I was a little skeptical while I was making them, I just knew that they would turn out to be a pile of mush, but they didn't!! It was a perfect blend of cereal and fruit!! Thanks for a great recipe that is an unlikely one!
I followed the recipe pretty much - used plain Cheerios and multi-grain Cheerios; raisins and dried berries; self-rising flour (because that's the only kind I ever buy) and natural applesauce.
Both of my kids even liked this! Okay, well picky 3-year-old just ate the Cheerios out of it, but hey. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jen s baked macaroni and cheese

i am very picky about mac n cheese - i won't touch that stuff in the box.  i like it to be creamy, yet do not like the flavor of the "processed" cheese which makes it creamy.  i played around with this quite a bit to get the right blend of creaminess and flavor, along with the topping i prefer on my mac n cheese.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease 2 quart casserole dish
3. cook macaroni al dente
4. drain
5. meanwhile , melt butter in a medium saucepan
6. remove from heat
7. stir in flour , salt , pepper , mustard , paprika and onion until smooth
8. gradually stir in milk
9. bring to a boil , strirring constantly
10. reduce heat and simmer for 1 minute
11. remove from heat
12. stir in velveeta and 1 c cheddar until smooth
13. fold macaroni into cheese sauce and pour into casserole
14. sprinkle with remaining cheddar
15. for topping , melt butter and toss with bread crumbs to coat
16. sprinkle mixture over macaroni
17. bake 30-40 minutes until brown and bubbly
18. let stand for 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review:
Loved this!! I did make a few changes...
Didn't have dry mustard, so used a squirt of prepared mustard. Didn't have paprika. Didn't use the onion. Used only 1 cup of cheese - and that was plenty - and it was a mix of colby, mild cheddar and Monterey Jack. Also, didn't use bread crumbs - used crushed saltine crackers.
My Velveeta was past date a little, but I still used it and it turned out great!
Thanks for this recipe, this was the first time I have ever made homemade mac-n-cheese. (Way better than MIL's version, which is just cooking macaroni and melting cheese and milk over it after it cooks.)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butterscotch banana bread waffles

ohhhh mannnn, these are good! i made these up by taking a basic waffle recipe and combining it with my butterscotch banana breaad recipe...ta da! these are so good with butter and maple syrup, or even plain!! these can also be served with ice cream for dessert.

1. sift together flour , baking powder , baking soda , salt , cinnamon , nutmeg and brown sugar in a large bowl
2. in another large bowl beat the egg yolks
3. add sour milk and mashed bananas
4. stir in the dry ingredients until well mixed
5. in a mixing bowl , whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form
6. fold into batter
7. gently stir in butterscotch chips
8. heat waffle iron and brush with oil
9. pour batter into iron and cook until golden brown
10. serve with maple syrup or butter , if desired
demonstrations.review: Great recipe!! They were so yummy, I had a hard time making myself stop eating them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy soft breadsticks

very nice to have with soups and salads.

1. mix flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
2. slowly add milk to form a soft dough
3. knead on a floured surface 4 times
4. roll into 10 inch by 5 inch rectangle
5. cut into 12 sticks
6. put butter in 13x9 baking dish
7. roll breadsticks in butter
8. sprinkle with sesame seeds
9. bake at 425 for 16 minutes , or until golden
demonstrations.review: Excellent!! I made these with half whole wheat flour/half unbleached all-purpose flour and sprinkled with garlic powder, dried parsely and parmesan before baking. Absolutely wonderful! I got 8 large breadsticks the first time I made them and 10 smaller, thicker breadsticks the second time. Thicker is definitely better! Will definitely be making these regularly - thanks for posting! :) Almost forgot - I baked at 425 for exactly 12 minutes and had perfection.

target.recipe_text:
best ever pumpkin pie

southern living. always served for thanksgiving dinner.

1. combine pumpkin and remaining ingredients in a large bowl
2. beat at medium speed with an electric mixer 2 minutes
3. pour into prepared piecrust
4. bake at 425 degrees for 15 minutes
5. reduce heat to 350 degrees
6. bake 50 additional minutes or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean
7. cool on a wire rack
target.review: My first time making a pumpkin pie - success!  I cooked and pureed my pumpkin (Australia doesn't have tinned pumpkin) and used the Delicate Shortcrust Pastry recipe for my base, which I blind baked.  Nice flavour without being overpowering, delicious served with a dollop of plain whipped cream. Looking forward to trying a piece (or two) tomorrow.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creme caramel

egg custards are quite simple to prepare, provided you follow the recipe directions! avoid using excessive heat which will ruin the texture, stir the mixture constantly when cooking over direct heat & watch the mixture carefully as it thickens. i'm making this on valentine's day - its one of my hubby's favourite desserts!!

1. melt 1 / 2 cup of the sugar in a small skillet over medium heat , stirring , until its a light brown syrup
2. pour into 8 buttered ramekins or custard cups
3. place ramekins into a shallow baking pan for easier handling
4. preheat oven to 300f
5. beat eggs , salt & remaining sugar in a large bowl with mixer at low speed until lemon coloured
6. gradually beat in milk & vanilla extract
7. divide the custard mixture among the ramekins
8. pour hot water into pan within 1 inch of top of cups
9. bake for 1 hour until a knife inserted in the centre comes out clean
10. remove ramekins from baking pan & cool on wire rack
11. refrigerate
12. to serve , loosen the custard from the cups with the
demonstrations.review: Quick and easy to make.  I made them in star shaped tins and they looked pretty special.  They are best made the night before, it gives the caramel a chance to colour the custard and liquify so it runs down the sides nicely.  Putting this one in my cookbook to do again... and again. Thanks for this great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate fudge from lonavala

everyone loves chocolate fudge, and my fondest memories of fudge are of those from lonavala, a tiny hill station in west india. no one visiting this place can leave without buying a generous amount of lonavala's famous chocolate fudge!

1. grease a shallow dish with butter
2. pour condensed milk into a thick-bottomed pan
3. add butter , sugar , cocoa powder and the chopped nuts into the pan
4. stir continuously on a low flame till the mixture leaves the sides of the pan
5. remove from flame and pour evenly into the prepared greased dish
6. allow to cool and set , and cut into 1 inch squares
7. store in an airtight tin in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: Quick and easy to make - I used cashew nuts, my favourite. It set perfectly. Even gets the thumbs up from my husband - I'll have to hide it!I will definately be making this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate beetroot muffins

saw this on a tv cookery programme. even beetroot haters will like these ...because they can't taste the beetroot, but it makes the muffins moist.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. line paper muffin cases in a 12-mould muffin tin
3. sift the cocoa powder , flour and baking powder into a bowl
4. mix in the sugar , and set aside
5. pure the beetroot in a food processor
6. add the eggs , one at a time , then add the vanilla and oil and blend until smooth
7. make a well in the centre of the dry ingredients , add the beetroot mixture and lightly mix
8. divide this mixture over the 12 muffin cases
9. bake for 20 to 30 minutes , depending on your oven , or until the top is firm when pressed with a finger
10. cool on a wire rack and dust with icing sugar to serve
demonstrations.review: Yum!  These turned out very moist and chocolatey, and quite easy to make - the only problem I had was converting the ingredients from oz to grams (I'm in Australia).  Amounts would have been a lot easier in cups.  I took them to a friends for after dinner last night and they went pretty quickly, so as we speak I am boiling beetroot to make some more! Definately making these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast pepper  cashew   chilli dip

this is a wonderful dip, it delicious, and refreshingly different from the usual dips. so many people comment on it when i serve it a parties, etc - but, why ask for the recipe when they can ask me make it & bring it!! you can store this in the fridge up to a week. go on give it a try.

1. preheat oven to 190 deg celsius
2. place the capsicum halves into a roasting pan & drizzle with olive oil
3. roast for 20 minutes , or until skin blisters
4. remove from oven , place in a bowl , cover with plastic wrap & leave to sweat
5. when capsicums are cool , the skins will peel off easily
6. place capsicum flesh , remaining oil , chilli sauce and tomato paste into the bowl of a food processor , process to combine
7. add cashews and process again until smooth
8. season with salt & pepper
demonstrations.review: A great dip - once the capsicums are roasted and peeled, it is so quick to make. I took it to a dinner party and ran out of dippers!!  I am going to make it again tomorrow and for any other get together we have. Very impressive.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red onion jam

this is wonderful with cheeses and cheese dishes, quiches and savoury pies, hamburgers, sausages, roast meats, lentil roast, and so much more.....  the flavours develop the longer you keep it, so make ahead to get the sweetest mellow taste.  this jam (or "confiture" if you want to be posh) keeps well in sealed sterilised jars and also makes a great gift at christmas time.  the recipe came from the december 2003 edition of the sainsburys magazine, but you don't need to wait for christmas to make this!

1. heat the oil in a wide shallow pan , then add the onions , sugar and salt and pepper: cook very gently for 30 minutes , stirring occasionally until most of the liquid has evaporated
2. add the sherry vinegar , grenadine and red wine: continue to cook , uncovered , at a gentle simmer for a further 30 minutes , stirring regularly until it reaches the consistency of jam
3. allow to cool before decanting and sealing in sterilised jars
demonstrations.review: I used olive oil instead of sunflower oil and a mixture of red wine vinegar and balsamic vinegar, it still came out fine.  It is very sweet but works great when combined with other flavours.  It is a very easy recipe that you don't need to spend much time attending to while it is cooking.  I have used some to make little tarts of puff pastry, onion, crumbled feta and pinenuts - recieved great compliments.

target.recipe_text:
pasta bows and chicken

from my aunt many years ago. really tasty and addictive!

1. chicken:
2. 1
3. melt butter
4. add onion and garlic
5. cook until onion is clear
6. 2
7. stir in chicken stock powder
8. 3
9. add chicken and cream , heat through but don't boil
10. add pepper
11. sprinkle with parsley
12. pasta:
13. 1
14. cook pasta , add 1 tbsp butter and 1tbsp chicken stock powder
15. 2
16. put on plate , pile chicken mixture on top
target.review: Great recipe! I tweeked this a little by cooking the cubed chicken breasts with the onions & garlic. When the chicken was almost done, I added the cream (using 1 1/2 cups) and about 1/4 cup of grated parmesan cheese. I let it simmer for it to thicken while the noodles finished cooking. I also used 'Better than Bullion' chicken paste (it uses half the amount of powder and *much* more flavorful). When the noodles were done, I drained them, added the pasta seasonings and tossed them into the skillet with the chicken. Served with homemade French bagettes. Yummy! NOTE: The sauce thickens upon standing, so don't fret if at first you feel it's too liquidy. This recipe is a terrific, quick, and easy weekday meal with a gourmet flair. Thanks so much for sharing your aunt's recipe. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nairobi meat  rub

this recipe is from kenya.

1. combine salt , black pepper , red pepper , sugar , and ginger , garlic powder , and onion powder
2. put into a storage container for barbecues
3. rub this mixture into the fatty parts of the ribs , pork , or skins of chickens with the fingers
4. cook meat over grill until done
5. meats should never be basted with sauces , or oil
6. if your meat appears to be dry , keep a light salad oil ready to brush on during cooking
demonstrations.review: We used this spice blend on some chicken legs that we broiled in the oven. I did add a smidgen of dry mustard powder to the mix to go with the sweetness of the sugar. This is a great rub that we will be using often. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frozen chocolate oreo souffles

an easy to make no-bake treat with instant chocolate pudding and oreo cookies, or substitute vanilla instant pudding and chips ahoy cookies. both versions are tasty anytime treats for children and adults too. the five hours is freezing time. another kraft canada goodie.

1. pour milk into medium bowl
2. add the two dry pudding mixes
3. beat with a wire whisk 2 minutes
4. gently stir in thawed whipped topping
5. spoon 2 tablespoons of the chopped cookies into each of eight paper drinking cups
6. cover evenly with half of the pudding mixture
7. repeat layers
8. cover with foil paper
9. freeze for 5 hours or until firm
10. remove from freezer about 15 minutes before serving
11. let stand at room temperature to soften slightly
12. peel away paper to unmold souffls onto dessert plates
13. top with a maraschino cherry
14. store any leftover souffls in the freezer
demonstrations.review: Quick and easy to make. Everyone enjoyed these.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simply delicious thousand island dressing

this is what i whip up when i need 1000 island. it is much better than store bought. goes great on reuben sandwiches, salads, burgers or as a dip with french fries. my family does not usually eat 1000 island but they love this! i love it with nick's mom's recipe #179493.

1. combine all of the ingredients together in a small bowl
2. mix well
3. cover and refrigerate until ready to use
demonstrations.review: This recipe is great. We will be using this from now on. Thanks for posting it. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
indian cornmeal   berry dessert

this unusual dessert was found in an american indian cookbook.

1. soak the cornmeal in the water
2. melt the butter in a large pot the add the cornmeal mixture
3. heat slowly , stir constantly for 15 minutes , or until thickened
4. add the juice , berries , & nutmeg then bring to a boil , stirring constantly
5. then add the cream & maple syrup , blending throughly
6. add the eggs & remove from the heat , stirring until the mixture stops bubbling
7. serve either hot or chilled
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I served this like warm grits and used frozen strawberries which I microwaved (to thaw) and thereby creating it's own juice. I made half the recipe and got about 3 cups from it, which made 2 servings. This is delicious and quick to make. It only took about 5 minutes to thicken. I only used half the maple syrup called for and sprinkled a bit of sugar and added more berries just before serving. Very unique, and very delicious, this would make a great fruit dip also!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tiajuana tacos

a recipe that i came up with a friend of mine hat we have tweaked a tad.

1. combine all ingredients except the last 5 in a slow cooker , and mix well
2. cover and cook on high for 2 hours
3. just before serving , fold in crushed corn flakes
