11. cook on high for 4 hours
12. when it's done , sprinkle remaining cheese on top , replace lid until cheese melts
13. cut into wedges with plastic spatula to serve
target.review: Easy and tasted great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham and cheese breakfast puffs

nice for a sunday breakfast or brunch. can be prepared several hours in advance, but baked when ready to serve. they will sink slightly when you remove them from the oven.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease two ovenproof dishes and line with the ham
3. beat together 2 tablespoons cheese , eggs and yogurt
4. mix in the green onions
5. divide evenly into the ham-lined dishes
6. sprinkle with the remaining cheese
7. bake for 25 to 30 minutes
8. run a knife around the rim , turn out , garnish with the parsley and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Made this for Sunday breakfast.  It was easy, I had all the ingredients and my family loved it. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry nut cornbread

i haven't tried this recipe yet, but it would make a nice side dish, or even a snack.  i plan on making it at christmas time, when fresh cranberries are plentiful in the market.  note:  i am writing the preparation directions  exactly as written in this recipe, but you may want to try using the method baby kato uses in his recipe# 85511, which describes soaking the cornmeal in the milk first to eliminate the grittiness some people don't like in their cornbread.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. lightly coat the bottom and about 1 / 2 inch up the sides of a 9x5x3-inch loaf pan , or two 7 1 / 2 x 3 1 / 2 x 2-inch loaf pans with cooking spray such as pam
3. set aside
4. in a large bowl stir together flour , cornmeal , sugar , baking powder and salt
5. make a well in the center of the flour mixture
6. set aside
7. in a medium bowl combine the egg , milk , oil and lemon peel
8. add egg mixture all at once to flour mixture
9. stir just until moistened
10. fold in nuts and cranberries
11. spoon batter into prepared pans
12. bake 55 to 60 minutes for the large loaf pan , or 45 to 50 minutes for the smaller loaf pans , or until a wooden toothpick inserted near center comes out clean
13. cool in pan on a wire rack for 10 minutes
14. remove from pan
15. cool completely on wire rack
demonstrations.review: I made these to go with a soup tonight.  They were very good.  I will sefinately make them again.  I didn't have fresh cranberries so, I used craisins.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
south beach muffin

an individual muffin that you can whip up fresh and hot for breakfast. no flour or sugar and only 3 net carbs!!! plus 7 grams of fiber. this little beauty is based on a recipe yogi told me about in the low carb forum. i have tweaked it to not use butter and to be a bit lighter in texture than the original. this recipe is suitable for phase 1 of the south beach diet (the 3 tablespoons of ground flax seeds count as the portion of nuts allowed per day). i find these are very filling and prevent me from feeling starving all morning.

1. spray a microwave safe ramekin or bowl with cooking spray
2. mix the egg and splenda until well combined , add the yogurt and blend well
3. mix in the ground flaxseed , cinnamon and baking powder until well combined
4. pour in ramekin and microwave on high for 1 minute 30 seconds
5. these taste best served hot
demonstrations.review: This was really good.  I didn't have ground flax so I substituted ground pecans.  The muffin had a great texture and flavor.  I will definately make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome blueberry muffins

this is a awesome blueberry muffin recipe. double it to make large muffins. i sometimes add cinnamon to the batter.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. grease muffin cups or line with muffin liners
3. combine 1 1 / 2 cups flour , 3 / 4 cup sugar , salt and baking powder
4. place vegetable oil into a 1 cup measuring cup
5. add the egg and enough milk to fill the cup
6. mix this with flour mixture
7. fold in blueberries
8. fill muffin cups right to the top , and sprinkle with crumb topping mixture
9. to make crumb topping: mix together 1 / 2 cup sugar , 1 / 3 cup flour , 1 / 4 cup butter , and 1 1 / 2 teaspoons cinnamon
10. mix with fork , and sprinkle over muffins before baking
11. bake for 20 to 25 minutes in the preheated oven , or until done
demonstrations.review: I make blueberry muffins about once a month. I have been using the same recipe for years. I tried this recipe for something a little different. Now it is my favorite blueberry muffin recipe. Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortilla crusted tilapia

i'm not fond of fish, but even i like this dish.  tilapia is mild, and the spicy crust is very appealing.  i like to make the crumb crust in bulk and freeze in meal sized amounts.  then this becomes a super quick weeknight meal.

1. preheat oven to 375f coat a baking sheet with cooking spray
2. place tortilla pieces , pepper , lime juice , cilantro and spices in blender
3. pulse until the mixture is uniform small crumbs
4. spread on plate
5. beat egg in shallow dish
6. dip each fillet in egg , then in crumbs , patting crumbs to adhere
7. place on baking sheet
8. bake until fish flakes , about 15 minutes depending on thickness of fillets
demonstrations.review: This was great.  I previously rated the wrong talapia recipe. This is the one I tried and my family loved it.  I will try the other one next.

target.recipe_text:
chile chicken enchiladas

these are delicious.

1. heat oven to 350
2. spray 13x9-inch glass baking dish with nonstick cooking spray
3. in medium bowl , combine chicken , monterey jack cheese , roasted peppers , chiles and sour cream
4. mix well
5. spread about 2 teaspoons enchilada sauce on each tortilla
6. top each with 1 / 2 cup chicken mixture
7. roll up tortillas
8. arrange , seam side down , in sprayed baking dish
9. top enchiladas with any remaining enchilada sauce
10. sprinkle with cheddar cheese
11. spray sheet of foil with cooking spray
12. cover baking dish with foil , sprayed side down
13. bake 45 to 60 minutes or until thoroughly heated
14. if desired , remove foil during last 5 minutes of baking time
15. if desired , serve with lettuce , tomato , avocado and additional sour cream
target.review: Very good I left out the red peppers and it came out great, thanks for the keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
very moist banana nut bread

this is a very easy, "no mixer" bread to make. it is very moist and a little heavy type banana bread. the really important thing to remember is using all black bananas to get my same results. i always use 5 medium sized bananas and this recipe makes 2 loaves. also, i've never used buttermilk, but sour milk instead..a little vinegar added to regular milk. i've used this recipe since 1972 and last year made 32 loaves to give away for christmas! it's truly a wonderful bread. i only bake it until the toothpick comes out almost clean, as we like it really moist. if you over bake it, or wait til the toothpick is completely clean, the bread will be a lot dryer. i realize some like it this way, so thats why i've given this hint. my family and friends would rather have it a little under done than over. it's so good with coffee, butter/jelly or i like mine just plain. i bake it in tin foil pans and it freezes wonderfully. i try to always have one or two in the freezer for company, or a little gift. this recipe came from a ladies club cookbook. the kind where everyone contributes recipes, they are made into a recipe book and sold to make money for charities. all the cooks are just plain "down home" country gals that produce miracles in the kitchen. it's my favorite cookbook and i've almost worn it out and it can't be replaced. i know there are many banana bread recipes here, so thanks for trying this recipe. i hope you enjoy it!

1. heat oven to 350
2. grease or spray 2 loaf pans
3. in a large bowl , mash bananas with a masher or by well washed hands
4. dissolve soda in buttermilk-- use a larger container as it will foam up quite a bit
5. mix all ingredients by hand and add in 1 cup chopped nuts
6. bake at 350 for 1 hour , or until toothpick comes out almost clean
7. totally clean will mean a dryer loaf
8. let cool 15 minutes after removing from oven and remove from pans
9. or , let cool , cover with foil , slide into freezer bags and freeze
10. great when using tin foil pans
demonstrations.review: The bread is very good but slightly eggy, I think next time I will try leaving out an egg or at least an egg yolk. Thanks for the keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: We really did not care for these, they came out eggy I guess, not something I'd use again but thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili s salsa

you can make this sauce easily at home. from copykat.com (http://www.copykat.com)

1. in food processor place jalapenos and onions
2. process for just a few seconds
3. add both cans of tomatoes , salt , sugar , and cumin
4. process all ingredients until well blended but do not puree
5. place in covered container and chill
6. a couple of hours of chilling will help blend and enrich the flavor
7. serve with your favorite thin corn tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: This was good, truly you are right, don't use pickled jalapeno's. My second batch (the right way, was good tasting, had a nice consistency, not exactly chili's and not hot enough for my sweet little family, maybe next time I will also lessen the cumin and up the garlic salt, thanks for a good one! Update tweaked it and now we love it. I put in 2 jalapenos, 1/2 belle pepper, 1 clove garlic, and left out the cumin and sugar, then I stuck it in the blender and froze it. Thanks again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden garlic alfredo sauce

this recipe is posted by request and was found on the net-no name attached.

1. in a medium to large saucepan melt the butter over medium heat
2. add the cream cheese and whisk to smooth and melted
3. whisk in the heavy cream
4. season with the garlic powder , salt and pepper
5. bring to a good simmer and whisk frequently until sauce thickens , around 25 minutes
6. remove from heat and stir in cheese
7. taste and adjust seasoning's
demonstrations.review: Very good, I put in 4 cloves of garlic, nice consistency and flavor will be making again soon. Thanks. UPDATE: Reheated this the second day and it was even better! It tastes just like olive garden!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian parmesan baked chicken

i had the chicken in the freezer and no idea what to do with it.  a search through the cupboard yielded a few helpful items

1. skin chicken if desired
2. combine dry ingredients in one pie plate and milk and beaten egg in another
3. wet drumsticks completely in milk and egg
4. coat them thoroughly with the breadcrumb mixture , turning so that the crumbs cover the leg
5. place legs in a lightly greased 9x13 , making sure that the legs do not touch
6. place in an oven preheated to 375 and bake 45-55 min or until juices run clear and chicken reaches an internal temp of 180
demonstrations.review: We liked it but next time we will use less bread crumbs more cheese and seasoning, it just came out slightly bland for our taste, but still very good. Thanks.

target.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
target.review:
Loved it! Had to have 3rds!

Would probably recommend you adding "follow the taco seasoning instructions", otherwise the meat is way to dry. You've got to add some water to that and simmer it for about 5 minutes.

I used more sour cream and would recommend using at least half a tub of it to be sufficient.

Baked for 22 mins in a gas stove and it turned out great

demonstrations.recipe_text:
island honey burgers

umm umm good!!

1. in a bowl , combine the first 7 ingredients
2. mix well
3. shape into 8 patties
4. grill the burgers , uncovered , over medium-hot heat for 3 minutes on each side
5. brush with soy sauce
6. contiinue grilling for 4-6 minutes or until juices run clear , basting several times
7. during the last 4 minutes , grill the pineapple slices until browned , turning once
8. serve burgers and pineapple on buns with lettuce and condiments of your choice
demonstrations.review: One of the best burgers I've ever had. I did not change the recipe one bit. Cooked in a skillet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
armenian herb marinade grilled chicken breasts

this is the most awesome grill marinade i've ever tasted in my life!  i don't know where my mom got this, but there is no match that i've ever known of...it is simplicity and freshness, yet rich, robust and succulent!  i haven't told you this one yet, because i was entering it in a grilling contest for a weber grill, but i can't hold back any longer!  it is wonderful for chicken breasts and also for lamb.  my mom used to make chicken and lamb kabobs with this marinade and we always wanted more!!!  note:  prep time does not include the 24-48 hours marinating time.  update:  my grill has died....so in desperation to taste this chicken again, i tried bobo3039's suggestion about baking it in a 350 degree oven...results were wonderful!!!  (still missed that charcoal essence, but one must "roll with the punches" and make do...in this case, bobo3039 was right on the money!)

1. mix all ingredients together and whisk thoroughly
2. put cleaned and dried meat in a large 8 x 11-inch glass baking pan and pour marinade over all , being sure to coat well
3. cover with plastic wrap and let marinate in refrigerator for 24 to 48 hours
4. drain meat and grill , basting with marinade until meat is cooked through
demonstrations.review: This was the greatest chicken I've ever had. After marinading for only 4 hours, I decided to start making it. It was so simple to make and the chicken turned out extremely moist. I did use some chicken mesquite rub and I highly recommend doing that to add some flavor to the chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review:
This was delicious, albeit, it looks a bit off when it's all finished up and the sauce is on.

I would recommend two things: First a little bit of oven time. It's never good when chicken isn't done!... I could see a bit of pink in mind when it was done. Secondly, dress it up a little bit to make it look more appealing. I don't know how we could do that, but I'm sure someone can figure that out.

Bottom line = The flavor is amazing, the look is missing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
california bbq chicken pizza

i know there are other recipes out there for bbq chicken pizza, but none like this! i just love this one!!!

1. saut chicken with garlic and onion in olive oil for 2-3 minutes
2. add 1 / 2 cup bbq sauce and continue to cook until chicken is done
3. cool slightly
4. prepare dough , if using
5. brush dough with additional bbq sauce
6. cover with about 4 ounces of cheese
7. top with chicken , pineapple , cilantro and remaining cheese
8. bake at 500 for about 10 minutes or until cheese is bubbly
demonstrations.review:
In one word: excellent.

In many words: The pizza was great, but be careful with the cilantro. First off, 1/2 cup of cilantro is a lot, and many people in the US aren't fond of the flavor, especially me. I would say 1/4 cup at most, and none at all if you don't like it (cause it's very potent).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern baked spaghetti

this is an easy, yet very tasty spaghetti casserole, which reminds me of the spaghetti they used to serve us in elementary school. i loved their spaghetti! i normally only brought my lunch, but not on spaghetti day!

1. cook spaghetti per package direcions
2. combine milk and egg , mix well
3. combine drained spaghetti , milk and egg
4. mix well
5. pour spaghetti mixture into a buttered 9x13 inch casserole dish
6. brown ground beef with onion , bell pepper and garlic in a large skillet
7. drain
8. return drained meat back into the skillet and add seasonings
9. cook for 2 minutes
10. stir in tomato sauce and cook for 2 more minutes
11. spread meat mixture over spaghetti
12. sprinkle with cheese
13. bake at 425f for 10 minutes or until cheese melts and is bubbly
14. remove from oven and let stand for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review:
This recipe I think has all the right ingredients, however I think it needs to be put together a bit differently.

When they spaghetti came out, the milk was runny still (even after overcooking it for an extra ten minutes) and there was hardly enough meat to satisfy my tonsils.

I would recommend: Use a bit less noodles. Use a bit more Tomato Sauce, but instead of "laying" the meat over the top, you could mix it together and it would be much better.

My only real complaint, (Since this recipe is VERY tasty) is that the noodles and the meat sauce didn't jive. I think they need to be mixed together, rather than separate. Some of you may like this, but I had a few complaints.

Great recipe overall!

target.recipe_text:
scallops with avocado salsa

this is an awesome accidental find that i came across on msn.com, credited to food & wine. i can't possibly express how delicious this dish is. each component is wonderful- it's almost a three-for-one deal- one recipe with 3 things that you can make just on their own. i hope you enjoy this as much as we did. couldn't wait to share with you all!

1. in a large bowl , combine basil , lime juice , olive oil , onion , jalapeno and garlic
2. with rubber spatula , gently fold in the avocados
3. season with salt and pepper
4. in a large skillet , heat the vegetable oil until shimmering
5. season the scallops with salt and pepper and cook over high heat until browned outside , but still rare in the center- about 2 minutes per side
6. transfer scallops to warmed platter- keep them warm
7. add water and tomatoes to the same skillet and cook over med-high heat , scraping up any browned bits from the bottom until the water has reduced- this happens in about 2 minutes
8. remove from heat and stir in the balsamic vinegar
9. season with salt and pepper
10. pour the tomato sauce over the scallops and serve with avocado salsa on the side
11. use the salsa and the sauce on steak , shrimp , with chips , in a sandwich -- the possibilities are endless !
target.review: This is a really simple preparation that ends up looking and tasting like it took a lot of time!  I used scallops that were pre-frozen so they released some water in cooking. If you do the same I would suggest skipping the water when you add tomatoes to the skillet. I ended up having to drain the tomato sauce to get the right consistency, but it still tasted great. As advertised, the avocado salsa can be added to anything-it is delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
summer orzo salad

simple salad is wonderful by itself or with some tuna for a simple salad lunch. recipe being submitted for rsc7 as a salad entree.

1. cook psta in boiling water for five minutes , add green beans to pasta and cook for 5 minutes longer
2. drain
3. put pasta and green beans in salad bowl and toss with oil and vinegar
4. add green pepper , capers , garlic and olives to pasta and toss
5. add tomatoes and feta chesse and toss
6. refrigerate before serving
7. this makes a good salad lunch when tossed with 1 small can white tuna
demonstrations.review: Really simple to put together, and it held up great when I made it the day before and refrigerated overnight. I chopped and added the tomatoes right before serving. I didn't add the tuna, but will try that next time. Guests and DH went back for seconds!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggplant dip

inspired by middle eastern's dip.

1. preheat the oven to 400 degrees f
2. cut the eggplant , bell pepper , and onion into cubes
3. toss them with the garlic , olive oil , salt , and pepper
4. spread them on lined baking sheet
5. roast for 45 minutes until the vegetables are lightly browned and soft , tossing once during cooking
6. let cool
7. place the vegetables in a food processor , add the tomato paste , and pulse to paste
8. taste for salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: This dip is wonderful. I made it one afternoon to try it out, and my DH ate it for dinner and would not stop exclaiming how good it was. I will definitely make it soon for a party. It's perfect as is, but definitely serves more than four.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian noodle bowl

probably the best asian type dish i have made yet. taken from a hannaford recipe card.

1. cook spaghetti according to package directions , drain and rinse
2. heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high hear
3. add oil and saute garlic and chili powder until golden , about 1 minute
4. add water and vegetables
5. cook until vegetables are tender-crisp , about 3 minutes
6. add the bbq sauce and peanut butter , stir until sauce is smooth
7. toss sauce and vegetables with spaghetti and garnish with chopped peanuts
demonstrations.review: I've made this recipe a few times, and it makes a great lunch reheated or cold the next day.  My DH adds extra pepper flakes, but I like the flavor as is.  I usually add some extra veggies though, 1 pkg frozen just isn't enough. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
warm salmon and couscous salad

a recipe from "clean eating" magazine, spring 2008.  this salad makes a wonderful lunch or light dinner, and has a spring-like freshness to it that makes it very appealing.  serve over a bed of baby spinach and garnish with lemon wedges if desired.

1. measure broth into a large microwave safe bowl
2. heat on high to boiling point then add couscous , chili powder , lemon zest and spinach
3. stir , cover tightly and let stand 5 minutes
4. add salmon , carrot , lemon juice , green onions , and walnuts
5. fluff with a fork and serve immediately on a bed of lettuce or spinach leaves
demonstrations.review: This was good, but a little light-it felt like something was missing. I chose to make it ino a salad with the salmon and couscous over a bed of baby spinach. Next time I'll drizzle a little vinaigrette over it to add some extra flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili brown rice with chicken  black beans and olives

a recipe posted in the 01/14/09 edition of the wichita eagle. i loved the combination of ingredients and the fiber content. an easy to make mexican meal made in one dish! i think this could easily be made into a oamc meal either cooked and frozen, or made as a "dump" meal.

1. heat the oil in a dutch oven over medium heat
2. add the rice
3. toast , stirring occasionally , until aromatic , 2-3 minutes
4. turn heat to low
5. push rice aside
6. stir in chili powder to taste , cumin and oregano
7. toast 15 seconds
8. gradually stir in water
9. stir in 2 cups of the salsa and the salt
10. taste
11. stir in more chili powder if you like
12. heat to a boil over high heat
13. cover
14. reduce heat to low
15. simmer until rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed , about 1 hour
16. stir in beans , chicken , corn and olives
17. if mixture seems dry , stir in more salsa
18. cover
19. continue cooking 1 minute
20. turn off heat
21. let rest , covered , 4 minutes
22. stir in avocado and cilantro
23. add lime juice , pepper and salt to taste , if needed
24. serve at the table with bowls of salsa , sour cream , cheese and onion
demonstrations.review: I loved this and it was really simple.  I used white rice because I didn't have any brown on hand, and it reduced the simmer time by about 25 minutes so be careful not to burn if you do the same.  Definitely had to add more salsa at the end because it got really dry. I also increased the chili powder to 3 tsps. but will probably add more next time. My DH likes a lot more spice. Thanks for a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
basic baking mix

just a quick baking mix recipe for pourable crusts, biscuits, pancakes.....

1. in a food processor or large mixing bowl combine all the dry ingredients
2. pulse to mix the ingredients or turn your mixer on low to mix well , 1 t at a time add the shortening-mixing well after each addition
3. this will keep for 6 weeks in your fridge , 4 weeks on the shelf
4. to make a pourable crust combine 2 / 3 cups baking mix with 2 eggs and 1 cup of milk
5. mix well
6. for biscuits , muffins or pancakes follow the directions in recipe#16813
target.review: This recipe works well for biscuits, but my only problem is the yield is very wrong. Another reviewer mentioned this as well. I expected 4 cups for another recipe, but when that didn't turn out well I came back and did the math, and the true yield on this is only 3 cups, not 4. It works well if you measure it out as you need it, but I should have double-checked beforehand.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brownie frosting

our favourite brownie frosting..

1. in a saucepan over med heat combine butter , sugar , milk , and cocoa
2. melt , and bring to a boil
3. when it has bubbles all the way across the top of surface now time
4. boil hard one minute only
5. remove from heat , add vanilla
6. let cool slightly , stir and beat until its like very thick corn syrup , and sticky to bottom of pot
7. i always use a spoon , so i can tell how it is thickening up
8. pour over brownies or cake
demonstrations.review: So easy! I subbed Splenda SugarBlend for the sugar, and ended up simmering for a few minutes longer after step 4. Mine turned out more thin, like a glaze, because of my sugar sub. But it was great over 1 Pan Fudge Cake! Definitely will make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect basic white rice

you do not need to be afraid of cooking rice again! lol real rice is so much better for you than instant. so here is a basic recipe that will have you cooking rice like a pro! check out the options too! your friends and family will think you're a star! 

1. in a saucepan with a good fitting lid bring water , salt and optional ingredients if desired to a boil
2. the salt and butter are simply for flavor
3. the vinegar keeps your grains separated and gives you a prettier dish
4. no one will taste the vinegar at all !
5. add rice and stir
6. cover and reduce heat to medium low
7. you will know that your temperature is correct if a little steam is visible leaking from the lid
8. a lot of steam means your heat is too high
9. cook for 20 minutes
10. do not lift lid !
11. the steam that is trapped inside the pan is what allows the rice to cook properly
12. remove from heat and fluff with fork
13. serve !
demonstrations.review: OHMYGOD. I am rice-disabled and this recipe makes me look like a superstar! I can't believe what a difference it makes to boil the water first, but my rice is light, fluffy, stick-free, and there is not a single grain stuck to my pot (and it's not even non-stick). Thank you!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bombay kidney beans

a can of beans, a can of tomatoes, some indian-style seasoning, serve over rice, and you've got yourself a quick and healthy vegetarian meal. use the higher amount of spices if you like your food a bit spicier. adapted from the vegetarian gourmet's easy low-fat favorites.

1. combine beans , tomatoes , honey and seasonings in a medium saucepan
2. bring to a boil , stirring occasionally
3. reduce heat , cover , and simmer 10 minutes
4. in a small bowl , stir together cornstarch and water so that cornstarch dissolves
5. add to saucepan
6. cook 2-3 minutes , stirring constantly , until slighly thickened
7. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: I've never posted a review, but after making this I had to! This is SOOOOO good! I'm a vegetarian and a new mom and this is delicious and simple and CHEAP. I usually have it over white rice. Definitely use the lesser amount of spices unless you like a LOT of heat. Thanks for posting this Fluffy, it's my new weekday staple!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sarah s secret chocolate silk pie  easy

for many years i kept the basic ingredient of this pie a secret, and for many years people wondered what was in it. cream? butter? both? well, for many years no one knew is that the main ingredient (besides chocolate, of course) is tofu! why tofu? not to be healthy or because i had anything against dairy, but because it's just easy. why didn't i tell people? because many of my picky-eater relatives wouldn't have eaten it if they'd known it was tofu. finally, one day, after everyone had enjoyed a piece of pie, i let the secret out... but you don't have to. make this pie, and let everyone think you spent more time making it out of cream and butter. one note: be sure to use silken tofu, not the meatier, textured tofu. make sure it says "silken" on the box.

1. melt the chocolate chips however you like to melt them
2. i heat them in a non-stick skillet over a low-heat burner , stirring often and keeping a close eye so to remove them when just melted
3. combine tofu and vanilla in a food processor
4. while processing , add the melted chocolate slowly
5. process until well combined
6. spoon into the pie crust
7. chill in the refrigerator for a couple hours until the pie has solidified
8. served chilled
demonstrations.review: Oh my GOD. This is the easiest, most chocolatey, satisfying desert ever! I always have tofu on hand and never would have thought of this. It actually sits in the pantry right next to the chocolate chips! THANK YOU for this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy chickpea   rosemary soup

we love chickpeas so this recipe from chef april bloomfield of the spotted pig "gastro-pub" in manhattan soon became one of our favorites.

1. in a large saucepan , heat the oil over medium heat and add garlic , rosemary and red pepper flakes
2. cook , stirring constantly , until the garlic starts to brown , about 1 minute
3. add chickpeas and cook 2 minutes , stirring constantly
4. add chicken broth and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat and simmer 30 minutes
6. let cool slightly
7. transfer soup to a blender
8. cover loosely , and puree until just smooth
9. return to the saucepan and stir in lemon juice and sea salt to taste
10. serve , garnished with a fresh rosemary sprig , or an additional drizzling of olive oil
demonstrations.review: I would have never thought of rosemary and chickpeas. The lemon makes it perfect! It is fantastic. I had some chickpeas to use up and found this; I'm so glad. My 1yo son even loves it! I used my immersion blender instead of transferring it, and that made it SOUPER easy (lol). One pan to clean, 30min from start to finish, who can beat it? This is going to be a staple for us. Thanks so much.

target.recipe_text:
weeknight easy beef enchiladas

this is off the back of a can...can't quite remember what the can contained but the recipe is so easy and tastes great!

1. preheat oven to 375
2. brown beef and onion until beef is thoroughly cooked
3. drain beef and stir in 3 / 4 cup enchilada sauce , the chopped green chilies and 1-3 / 4 cup cheese
4. spoon enchilada filing into tortillas
5. roll up and put seam side down in lightly greased baking dish
6. pour remaining enchilada sauce over top and sprinkle with remaining cheese
7. bake at 375 for 20 minutes
target.review: Perfectly tasty and easy! My husband loved these! Will be making these again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chicken in a skillet

easy and delicious!

1. heat oil in dutch oven or large skillet and brown chicken pieces
2. add tomatoes , with juice , and remaining ingredients
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for 40 minutes , stirring occasionally , until chicken juices run clear
demonstrations.review: I have made this 3 or 4 times now, and for some reason I never saw the onion soup mix! *stomp foot* Its still great though. My husband says its the best chicken I have ever made, so moist and absolutely PERFECT! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
monterey chicken bake

5 ingredients... talk about easy :) i found this on the helmans site and it turned out well for me.

1. preheat oven to 425
2. brush chicken with mayonnaise on all sides then dip in bread crumbs until evenly coated
3. arrange chicken in a 9x13" pan
4. bake 15 minutes
5. top with salsa then cheese
6. bake an additional 5 minutes or until cheese is melted and chicken is cooked thoroughly
demonstrations.review: Oh, this was so easy and so yummy! Absolute repeat in my house. I loved it! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
3 meat breakfast pizza

we love pizza--even for breakfast. feel free to add any of your favorite toppings too. this is very filling and great served with fresh fruit. also super as a light lunch or supper. i will make a couple of these on the weekend and wrap individual wedges that the kids grab to pop in the micro and eat as they wait for the bus.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. in saucepan add water and milk
3. whisk in gravy mix , and bring to a boil
4. simmer 2-3 minutes , stirring constantly til thick
5. cool slightly
6. in large skillet , melt margarine
7. beat eggs with milk and add to skillet
8. scramble eggs in skillet until set and in small chunks
9. place crust on pizza stone or cookie sheet
10. spread gravy evenly over the top
11. sprinkle meats over gravy
12. sprinkle eggs over meats
13. salt and pepper to taste
14. sprinkle cheese over eggs evenly
15. bake at 400f for 10-15 minutes until bubbly and cheese is melted and browning
16. cool slightly and cut into wedges
demonstrations.review: This was soooo good. I used sausage and bacon and added a little extra cheese. My family loved it! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
husker chops

nan

1. brown the chops well in small amount of fat
2. season both sides with salt and pepper , and place in 9" x 13" baking dish
3. mix together the remaining ingredients
4. pour mixture over chops and cover with foil
5. bake in a 325 degree oven for 2 hours
6. remove foil the last 1 / 2 hour of baking
demonstrations.review: Melt in your mouth good. My family LOVED these! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon roll toast

this is delicious and easy. takes cinnamon toast to a whole nother level.

1. sprinkle cinnamon on plain piece of bread
2. spread it in and around with a knife
3. butter that side of the bread
4. place buttered side down in a moderately hot skillet until lightly toasted
5. turn and leave on other side just long enough to keep it from feeling soggy
6. spread hot toast with glaze made with confectioner's sugar , water and vanilla
demonstrations.review: Oh, this was delicious, my kids were amazed and I will be making this again, the right way! The second time around, I messed it up trying to shorten the time by melting the butter and cinnamon together, then dipping the bread in it (like french toast). This was NOT a very good idea.

target.recipe_text:
pakistani dhal

vegan indian gourmet. vegetable stock can be used for added flavor.

1. heat water in pot until boiling
2. add lentils and boil for one minute
3. reduce heat to a simmer
4. simmer lentils until they resemble a thick paste
5. while lentils are simmering , heat oil in frying pan
6. add onion , garlic and ginger
7. fry until soft
8. add curry , chili , cumin , coriander , salt and pepper , saut for 2-3 minutes
9. add tomatoes and saut for another 3-5 minutes
10. add fried spice mixture into lentil paste , stir and cook an additional 15-20 minutes
11. serve as is or over basmati rice
target.review: This daal was delicious and healthy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best potluck pasta salad

this is a very good salad for a potluck, serves 16-18 as a side dish and can be made ahead of time; 12 to 24 hours. chill time not included.

1. cook pasta according to package directions
2. drain
3. rince with cold water
4. drain again
5. in a large bowl combine , pasta , squash , peas , sweet pepper , cheese , olives tomatoes , onion , and oregano
6. add dressing to pasta mixture
7. toss gently to coat
8. cover and chill for 2 to 24 hours
demonstrations.review: I love this recipe, so healthy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
achari fish

serve with rice or naan and raita

1. wash the fish well in salt water
2. apply the lemon juice to the fish and set aside for approximately 1 hour
3. fry the onions till they are light golden in color
4. remove with a slotted spoon and crush
5. in the same oil put the red chillies , onion seeds , turmeric powder , red chilly powder and garlic
6. stir and fry for a few minutes till the oil separates
7. add the tomatoes and again stir and cook till the oil separates
8. add the fish
9. coarsely grind together the aniseed , coriander seeds , fenugreek seeds and mustard seeds
10. add this to the fish along with the green chillies and cook over a low heat till the fish is done , about 10 minute min
demonstrations.review: Thanks for another great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seviyan   vermecilli dessert

a famous dessert made by muslims.

1. put sugar , 6 ounces water and honey in a pan and dissolve on a slow fire
2. remove from fire and keep aside
3. heat ghee and put in vermicelli and fry gently to a golden color
4. put in the prepared syrup and cardamoms
5. add the fried raisins
6. mix well and cook on a very slow fire until the water or moisture is all absorbed
7. when ready it should be separated and not mushy or sticking together
8. serve hot garnished with almonds
demonstrations.review: I had been looking for this recipe. This came out great. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pakistani fish curry

this recipe was submitted by christina lewis in this week's thursday magazine. looks very good! preparation time includes marinating time.

1. heat oil in a pot
2. add onions and saute until brown
3. grind the onions
4. put the ground onions in a large mixing bowl
5. add yoghurt to the ground onions
6. add fish pieces to this , mix well and marinate the fish in this mixture for 2 hours
7. in the same oil which was used to saute the onions , add the methi seeds
8. allow to sizzle a bit , then remove them once they turn brown
9. add ginger-garlic paste to the same oil
10. saute until the raw smell is gone
11. add red chilli and turmeric powders
12. mix well and continue to stir-fry for a few minutes
13. add the marinated fish pieces
14. add half a glass of water and mix well
15. keep on low flame for 10 minutes
16. garnish with corriander leaves
17. serve hot with chappatis
demonstrations.review: This recipe is easy and delicious. When I grind the onions, I also grind a tomato with it. I add curry leaves to the fish also whole green chilli for flavor. The curry fresh curry leaves have an amazing flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
karahi chicken

chicken is brought alive with this simple tomato-based spicy sauce that is added last-minute for a quick-to-cook curry. i love this from my local takeaway.

1. for the karahi curry sauce: heat the oil in a pan , add the onions , garlic and chillies and fry over a medium heat for approximately 10 minutes or until the onions are caramelised
2. add the cumin , coriander , turmeric , salt and garam masala and stir
3. mix in the ginger and pureed tomatoes and cook for 1 minute , stirring
4. add the water and cook for about 5 minutes or until the oil surfaces
5. remove from the heat and keep warm
6. for the chicken: heat the oil in a wok or heavy-based frying pan and add the chicken
7. stir-fry over a medium heat for 8-10 minutes or until the chicken is golden brown all over
8. stir in the karahi curry sauce and simmer for 2-3 minutes
9. garnish with cilantro leaves
demonstrations.review: This came out really tasty. I used cut up whole chicken in small pieces.

target.recipe_text:
moosewood mushroom barley soup

i'm posting this in honor of one of my best friends mom's who first served this to me during high school...my second jewish mother who always thought i should eat more. she used the moosewood cookbook for many a fine dinner. thanks eileen!

1. cook barley in 1 1 / 2 cup of the stock or water until tender
2. add remaining stock or water , tamari and sherry
3. saute onions and garlic in butter
4. when they soften , add mushrooms and 1 / 2 tsp salt
5. when all is tender add to barley , being sure to include the liquid the vegetables expressed while cooking
6. give it a generous grinding of black pepper and simmer 20 minutes , covered , over the lowest possible heat
7. taste to correct seasoning
target.review: Excellent! I used olive oil in place of butter, 1/2 shitake and 1/2 crimini mushrooms, and added 1 bunch of spinach. I will certainly make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato and green bean salad with balsamic vinaigrette

this is awesome! this salad will stay for several days, and improves in flavor. it may be served chilled or room temperature. preparation time includes cooking the potatoes and beans.

1. in a large bowl , combine the potatoes , green beans , onion and basil
2. mix / whisk all the vinaigrette ingredients togther
3. add in the balsamic vinaigrette mixture to the warm potato / bean mixture
4. toss well to coat
5. season with salt and pepper to taste
6. serve chilled or room temperature
demonstrations.review: everyone enjoyed this dish at the potluck I took it to.  I added halved cherry tomatoes, otherwise made as written.  I also found that it was too much dressing for the quantity of vegetables and only used about half the dressing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maw maw s thanksgiving dressing

this was my maw maw's recipe for homemade dressing. it is the best!!! my family has been using this particular dressing recipe for years!

1. pre-heat oven to 350f
2. in a very large mixing bowl , combine bread crumbs , crumbled cornbread , crumbled biscuits , yellow onions , celery , green onions , fresh parsley , sage , salt and pepper
3. toss well
4. add melted butter and eggs
5. mix
6. add chicken broth , a little at a time , mixing lightly , but well
7. add enough broth to make mixture extra moist
8. place mixture into a well-greased baking dish
9. bake about 45 minutes or until top is golden brown
10. ~
11. to bake , remove from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for about 30 minutes
12. then , remove foil and bake for about 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: was a hit last year, now my standard thanksgiving stuffing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
okra patties

my favorite way to use okra, and besides...it is good. i usually make this in the summer when okra is plentiful, but i have also used frozen okra successfully.
note:  i should have put this notice here before, but just didn't think!  okra should be chopped by hand. the food processor makes it way to slimey to work with.

1. combine okra , onion , salt , pepper , water , and egg and mix well
2. mix flour , baking powder , and cornmeal and add to okra mixture , mixing well
3. heat oil to medium-high , drop okra by heaping tablespoons into hot oil and cook until brown on both sides
demonstrations.review: I added garlic and cooked in olive oil. They were great. Next time I think I will either add something to then to make them spicy, or serve with a spicy sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese wafers  straws  cookies

a wonderful cheesy crispy cookie for a snack or make into straws and have with soup.  well seasoned for the "just right" taste and flavor.  do include all seasonings as they enhance the flavor.  we are a third generation family enjoying these cheese wafers or cheese krispies as some of us call them.  a great appetizer for parties or weddings.  they go well with coffee, fruit drink or a cocktail. note:  put only 1/2 teaspoon cayenne powder if you don't like it very hot.

1. blend softened butter with grated cheese
2. add salt , garlic powder , cayenne powder and worcestershire
3. stir in flour and rice krispies
4. for wafers: form by hand into balls and flatten with fork
5. for straws: flatten pieces of dough by hand on parchment paper and cut into 4 x 6 inch straws and separate
6. place on an ungreased cookie sheet
7. bake in a 325 degree oven for 17 minutes
8. watch carefully and do not overbake
9. let cool slightly and place on paper towels
10. store in an air tight container
demonstrations.review: I made these for a potluck and got rave reviews!  My husband loves spicy so I used a habanero cheddar.  They were really spicy, and I missed the sharp cheddar taste, so next time I think I will use 1/2 extra sharp cheddar, and 1/2 habanero cheddar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peach muffins

make with fresh or canned peaches.  can be made as a loaf, if desired.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease muffin tins or greased / floured 9" x5" bread loaf pan
3. in a large mixing bowl , combine the flour , salt , baking soda , sugars and cinnamon
4. make a well in the center
5. add the eggs , oil and vanilla and stir just until dry mixture is moistened
6. stir in almonds , if using them
7. stir in the chopped peaches
8. pour about 1 / 3 cup of batter into the muffin tins
9. bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes or until toothpick tests done
10. if baking in the loaf pan , bake at 350 for 1 hour or until done
demonstrations.review: I used half all purpose and half whole wheat flour, and added 1/4 tsp ground ginger.  Next time I will add 1/2 tsp ground ginger, and will use 1/2 the sugar as I found them to be quite sweet.

target.recipe_text:
coffee cake over night

this will go like hotcakes. i use to make it up just before a lake trip and take it along. was always gone in a matter of minutes.

1. grease 9x13 pan
2. in large bowl mix flour , sugar , brown sugar , shortening , buttermilk , soda , baking powder , cinnamon , salt , and eggs
3. blend on low speed of mixer
4. in small bowl mix brown sugar , granulated sugar , cinnamon , and nuts
5. pour half of the cake batter into pan
6. sprinkle half of the topping mix over
7. repeat a second time
8. cover and refrigerate overnight
9. pre-heat oven to 350f
10. bake at 350f for 30-40 minutes
target.review: I have to say this recipe is a good idea for a coffee cake, but there is far too much sugar topping listed in the recipee.  Other reviewers wrote about using less, there should just be less in the recipe for a good review.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my grandmother s fresh peach cobbler

my grandmother used this recipe every summer when the peaches were ripe. she got the recipe from her church cookbook. you can use any almost any kind of fruit in the cobbler, it will still be good.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. pour melted butter into an 8x8 pan
3. whisk together the flour , 3 / 4 cup of sugar , baking powder and milk
4. pour over melted butter
5. cover with peach slices
6. cover with 3 / 4 cup sugar
7. bake until batter rises to top and forms a nice brown crust , about 20 - 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This really tasted fabulous and my entire family liked it.  I added 1/4 tsp each of cinnamon and ginger to the final sugar as per other reviews.  I think it needed to cook longer.  It wasn't at all cakey.  After 30 mins it came out gooey and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rhubarb crisp

mom's recipe! easy to make and easy to eat.

1. combine rhubarb , sugar , flour and cinnamon and put into 8" x 8" x 2" glass baking dish
2. combine flour , brown sugar , rolled oats and melted butter and sprinkle streusel over rhubarb mixture
3. bake at 375 for 35 minutes
demonstrations.review: I thought this crisp either had not enough fruit or way too much goo.  It would taste great with less goo or more fruit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic baked ziti

this baked ziti recipe is a simple italian casserole dish that my family enjoys.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large skillet , cook ground beef , onions , and garlic over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes or until beef is browned
3. stirring frequently
4. stir in spaghetti sauce , chicken broth , and oregano
5. reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes
6. stir 1 cup of the sauce into the cooked ziti noodles
7. spoon 1 / 2 of the ziti mixture into a 13x9x2-inch baking dish
8. sprinkle with 1 1 / 2 cups mozzarella cheese and 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese
9. top with 2 cups sauce , then remaining ziti mixture and remaining sauce
10. cover and bake 20 minutes
11. sprinkle with remaining mozzarella and parmesan cheese
12. return to oven and bake uncovered for 10 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: This is very good.  Followed the recipee and it turned out great.  Just right, not too meaty, not too cheesey.  My kids enjoyed it and I'll make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
poverty meal

when i was a child, my family used to eat this at least once a week due to the fact that it is inexpensive and a little goes a long way. we also added fresh herbs or sometimes whole kernel corn. its even better the next day and it freezes well.

1. saute onions and garlic in olive oil until translucent
2. brown ground beef and drain
3. add ground beef , tomatoes , water , raw macaroni , salt and pepper to the onion and garlic mixture
4. cook for 15 to 20 minutes or until macaroni is tender
5. if desired , top with parmesan cheese
6. serve with crusty bread and a salad
demonstrations.review: I like the idea of this recipe, but it is very bland as is.  You need to season the meat while it is cooking and decide how to spice it up.  On the plus side it makes a huge hot meal, but not too tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
1 hour ham and bean soup

made this one up myself, from a mix of different recipes.  no need to wait for dry beans to soak. you get great homemade soup in about an hour!

1. heat vegetable oil in a soup pot
2. add carrots , celery and onion
3. saut for about 4 minutes , just until onion is beginning to soften
4. add ham , saut 2 minutes
5. add garlic , saut one more minute
6. add 3 cups stock , bring to a low boil for about 10 minutes , stirring once or twice
7. meanwhile , in a food processor , combine all but 1 / 2 of a can of beans , including juice , and the tomato sauce
8. process until smooth
9. add remaining stock to processor to thin mixture
10. process to combine
11. add mixture from processor into ham mixture
12. add remaining 1 / 2 can of beans , stir to blend , bring to a boil , lower heat , cover and simmer for 30 minutes
13. serve hot !
demonstrations.review: This was the best ham and bean soup I've ever made.  I added some sage because my mom always put sage in hers.  I have never put garlic in ham and bean soup before and it made all the difference.

target.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
target.review: This is my favorite meal in the WHOLE world!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Thank-you SO much for posting this awesome recipe!!!!! I will recommend this to everyone!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
libby s famous pumpkin pie

well, after looking for this recipe on here and not having any luck, i decided to find it and post it. in my opinion, this is the best pumpkin pie. make your own graham cracker crust or buy an already prepared one.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees fahrenheit
2. mix sugar , salt , cinnamon , ginger , and cloves in small bowl
3. beat eggs in large bowl
4. stir in pumpkin and sugar-spice mixture
5. gradually stir in evaporated milk
6. pour mixture into pie shell
7. bake at 425 degrees fahrenheit for 15 minutes
8. reduce temperature to 350 degrees fahrenheit
9. bake for 40 to 50 minutes or until knife inserted near center comes out clean
10. cool on wire rack for 2 hours
11. serve immediately or refrigerate
12. top with whipped cream before serving for best results !
13. do not overcook
14. overcooking leads to pie cracking in the middle
15. try to bake the day you will serve the pie
16. cooking in advance can make the crust soggy
17. if you have to bake a day before serving , pop the pie in the oven for 5 to 10 minutes and it should bring the crust back to life !
demonstrations.review: I got this recipe from a libby's pumpkin can. I made this for desert a few months ago. It was very easy to prepare. And all I can say is... YUM!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible peanut butter cookies

these are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!

1. mix peanut butter , sugar , and egg together until smooth
2. drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart
3. if desired , roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet
4. press with fork
5. press again in opposite direction
6. bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
7. do not brown
8. do not over bake
demonstrations.review:
They where pretty good.
These cookies are perfect for parties. thanks for submitting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon tea cookies

i love tart lemon desserts.  this is a recipe i found on betty crocker that looks very good.

1. in large bowl , beat butter , 1 / 3 c powdered sugar , and vanilla with mixer on medium speed until well blended
2. stir in flour until dough forms
3. cover
4. refrigerate 30 minutes
5. heat oven to 350f shape dough into 1" balls
6. place balls 2" apart
7. press thumb into center of each ball to make indentation
8. bake 8 to 10 minutes or until golden brown
9. remove to cooling racks and cool completely , about 30 minutes
10. in 1 qt saucepan , heat all filling ingredients over low heat about 25 minutes , stirring constantly , until smooth and thickened
11. cool about 15 minutes
12. fill each thumbprint with rounded 1 / 4 tsp filling
13. sprinkle 1 t powdered sugar over cookies
demonstrations.review:
I made the dough and followed all the directions but it was too dry so I added 1/4 cup of water, and it worked perfectly. Also........
I was string the filling on the stove for about 15 minutes then it smelt like it was burning and the color what used to be yellow was a brown. I think it was burnt. So I took it off the heat. When they were finished they tasted DELICIOUS!!! They are the best tasting cookies I ever made but also the longest time make cookie I ever made. Thanks for posting!!!!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy one bowl vanilla cupcakes

this recipe goes back over 20 years, i like the simplicity of this recipe and for a one bowl cupcake they are pretty darn good, 1-1/2 teaspoons almond extract may be used in place of the vanilla, using butter in place of shortening will alter the texture it is best to only use shortening --- if you don't have paper liners grease the tins generously or see my recipe#78579

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large bowl , mix together the flour with sugar , baking powder and salt until combined
3. add in the shortening cream or milk , vanilla and eggs
4. beat on medium speed of an electric mixer scraping the bowl constantly until just blended
5. pour into paper-lined regular size muffin tins filling under just three-quarters full
6. bake for 20-22 minutes or until the cupcakes test done
7. immediately remove from pans
8. cool completely before frosting
demonstrations.review:
They tasted REALLY good and moist, but they kept falling apart. They may fool you by what they look like but they taste delicious!!!

                familyof6

P.S. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: My friend and I love having cooking days and we decided to make this recipe. It was delicious!!! I like adding bacon and Mexican cheese on top! Thanks for posting it!!!

target.recipe_text:
fudge popsicles  fudgesicles

recipe from a friend.  without instant pudding mix.  kid approved!  prep time does not include freezing time.

1. in a small saucepan , combine sugar , cornstarch , cocoa , and milk
2. cook on medium until thick
3. remove from heat and add vanilla and butter and stir until combined
4. place in molds and freeze until firm
target.review: the whole family loved these including my daughter who does not care for chocolate!  My husband loved them so much I had to go out and get some more cocoa right away to make more!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bread machine cinnamon buns

bread machine cinnamon buns.

1. put yeast in bread machine first on bottom , then flour , sugar and salt
2. then melt butter in microwave
3. add beaten egg , milk and water
4. pour onto dry ingredients in bread machine on the dough setting
5. when dough is done , put it onto a lightly floured surface
6. knead in enough flour to make it easy to handle
7. if it is too elastic , cover and leave 10 minutes
8. use floured rolling pin to roll out dough on floured surface
9. roll out into rectangular shape to approx 1 / 4-inch thick
10. use filling and spread over entire surface of dough with spoon
11. roll up dough
12. cut into circle with a sharp knife about 1-inch thick
13. place these in a greased 9x13-inch pan
14. cover with a tea towel and leave in a warm place for approx 30 minutes , until double in size
15. bake in a 350 oven for about 25 minutes , light brown on top
16. when done , make glaze and swirl over buns
demonstrations.review: These were amazing.  Exactly the light soft texture I was looking for and craving.  It is by far the best recipe for cinnamon buns for the bread maker I have ever tried.  The recipe says to put the ingredients in a totally different order than my machine calls for but I followed the recipe anyway and it came out perfect.  The dough was easy to work with and the finished product lasted less than 24 hours in my house.  Thanks for a great new recipe, I will use it again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cauliflower cheddar soup

this is a modified recipe, originally called farmhouse cheddar soup, which i clipped out years ago. i make it often and freeze in individual servings to reheat. you can reserve 1 1/2 c of the cauliflowerets to saute in some butter and add after the soup has been pureed. i usually just puree it all in the soup pot with a hand blender.

1. combine water / stock , potatoes , cauliflower , onion , carrot and garlic in large pot
2. bring to a boil
3. simmer 15 minutes or until vegetables are tender
4. remove from heat and let cool 20 minutes
5. puree in food processor or blender or use hand blender
6. return to pan and stir in remaining ingredients until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: I made this to use up some cauliflower.  I liked that it had lots of other veggies and didn't call for a lot of milk or cream.  I used chicken broth in place of the water and it was very easy to make.  I gave if 5 stars because both of my kids ate it, including the picky one!  I served it with a sprinkle of cheddar and a small handful of balsamic croutons.   The croutons were amazing with it as they added some cruch and contrast!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey banana bread

i got this recipe from a friend, who got it at a weight watchers meeting. it's so delicious you won't believe you're eating low fat! it doubles perfectly (i never make just one loaf!) and if you don't have enough banana, just use applesauce for the balance. it works like a charm. enjoy!!! 2 points per 1/16 of a loaf.

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. grease an 8 x 4 loaf pan with nonstick cooking spray
3. combine flour , brown sugar , baking powder , baking soda and nutmeg
4. stir to mix well
5. in a separate bowl , combine banana , honey and milk
6. mix well
7. add liquid ingredients to dry , stirring just till dry are moistened
8. spread mixture evenly in pan and bake 45 to 50 minutes , or until a wooden toothpick inserted in center of loaf comes out clean
9. remove bread from oven and let sit for 10 minutes
10. invert loaf onto wire rack , turn right side up , and cool before slicing and serving
demonstrations.review: This is a nice tasting banana bread that I could feel good about baking. I was trying to find low fat and high fiber recipes that my husband and I could actually enjoy as a snack and I was very pleased with this. It was easy and came out great.  I skipped the nutmeg.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: I loved that this was a one bowl recipe.  I doubled the batch and they were perfectly done in 25 min. in my oven.  I didn't have any nuts or chocolate chips but as it was the day after halloween I cut up various mini chocolate bars (mars, peanut butter cups, M&Ms, etc.) and pressed them into the batter after spreading it in the pan. The candy sort of sunk in as it baked and the result was lots of yummy surprises.  My favorite was the peanut butter cups so next time I may try it with just lots of those!  Yummy and very chocolaty, requires a glass of milk wich is just how a brownie should be!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian peasant soup

i found this in toh quick cooking magazine. i haven't tried it yet but it looks like something my family and i would love. plan on trying it soon.

1. in a large pot , cook sausage over medium heat until browned and no longer pink
2. drain
3. add onions and garlic
4. saute until tender
5. add chicken
6. saute and stir until no longer pink
7. add in the beans , broth , tomatoes , basil , and oregano
8. stir to mix
9. cook uncovered , for 10 minutes
10. add the spinach and heat just until wilted
11. serve with parmesan cheese sprinkled on top
demonstrations.review: I love this soup.  I first had it at my Mom's at least a year ago and only tried it myself last month when I found the recipe here.  I used itallian turkey sausage to cut down on the fat and it was great.  I also used a 28ounce can of diced tomatoes instead of 14 1/2.  Tonight I served it to a group of friends and eveyone enjoyed it.  This is my new favorite soup!

target.recipe_text:
swiss cheese bacon smoked almond dip

awesome dip!!!  always the first to go at parties.  it is also great served in pre-packaged phyllo cups

1. fry the bacon
2. let drain and crumble
3. mix all ingredients
4. bake in 350 degree preheated oven for about 15 minutes
5. until golden and bubbly
6. top with some crushed almonds
7. for a twist , put the cold dip in pre-packaged phyllo cups and bake for about 15 minutes
target.review: I made this for our housewarming party and recieved more compliments on it than anything I have ever made! In fact, my husbands entire family stood around the counter gorging on it and barely had room for dinner. They have asked that I bring it to all family functions! I used chive cream cheese, as its what I had. I also used smoked apple flavored swiss and plain almond slivers. It was EXCELLENT!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy turkey tetrazzini

this is a great way to use leftover cooked turkey or chicken. it's also an easy one dish casserole that everyone in the family enjoys. the recipe started life as a cooking light recipe in a recent issue. i made modifications to suit our taste.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. melt butter in saute pan
3. add onion , celery , pepper , salt , carrots , and mushrooms
4. saute until vegetables are tender
5. add flour and stir until vegetables are coated
6. add wine , and stir quickly until flour is absorbed
7. gradually add broth , stirring constantly
8. bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes , stirring frequently
9. remove from heat
10. add 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese and the neufchatel cheese , stirring until cheese melts
11. add the peas , turkey and pasta
12. stir until blended
13. coat a casserole with non-stick spray and transfer mixture to the casserole
14. combine breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese
15. sprinkle mixture evenly over the top of the casserole
16. bake at 350 for 30 minutes until lightly browned
17. let rest for 15 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this with a lot of changes (picky husband). I didn't use any vegetables except onion and red bell pepper. I used vegetable flavored low-fat cream cheese and didn't remember the breadcrumbs. Anyway, it was delicious. I also used the spiral pasta noodles. I will make this again tonight and freeze it for busy days this month! Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy choco chip cookies

good chocolate chip cookie!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. line two cookie sheets with parchment paper
3. place flour , baking soda and salt in a mixing bowl
4. whisk to combine
5. set aside
6. in a large mixing bowl , beat butter and sugars , mixing until thoroughly blended
7. beat in egg , egg yolk and vanilla extract
8. add dry ingredients and beat at low speed with electric mixer just until combined
9. stir in chocolate chips
10. bake for 10 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Outrageously good! Chewier than any other recipe I've tried and just what I was lookin for!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
houston s spinach and artichoke dip

i try to avoid using 

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. place romano cheese in a food processor
3. while running , drop garlic in the feed tube
4. start the machine and add spinach , artichokes , cream cheese and eggs , process until thoroughly blended
5. turn into a casserole dish and fold in mozzarela
6. bake 20-25 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious! I will be serving this tonight for about 15 guests and I really don't care if they like it or not, I love it! I find it very flavorful and mine isn't all THAT green, its spinach for Pete's sakes!!! Its supposed to be green! Anyway, I used canned spinach (time crunch) and added a big dollop of sour cream. I will serve it (when re-heated) in a Hawaiian bread loaf. Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast  sticky  chicken

beautiful and delicious, this incredibly moist roasted chicken puts kenny roger's roasters, boston market, and other rotisserie style chickens to shame! please don't let the word 

1. blend all spices together and set aside
2. remove neck and giblets from chicken cavity , rinse well inside and out , and pat dry with paper towels
3. rub with spice mixture , both inside and out , then stuff cavity with onions
4. wrap in a resealable"food grade" plastic bag , tie closed , and refrigerate overnight
5. remove from plastic bag and place in a shallow baking pan
6. roast uncovered in a 250 f oven 5 hours
7. if the chicken contains a pop-up thermometer , ignore it
8. this recipe is safe
9. according to the united states department of agriculture food safety and inspection service , a whole chicken should reach an internal temperature of 180 f
10. for more info check out their"thermy" campign web site !
11. baste with drippings every 30 minutes after the first hour
12. let rest for 10 minutes before carving
demonstrations.review: I didn't add everything that was recommended, as a trip to the grocery store was not possible. I added the salt, paprika, garlic powder, black pepper, thyme and onions. I added lawrey's seasoned salt and garlic salt. I did not make this a day in advance or put it in the bag, but rubbed it into the chicken, stuffed the chicken and cooked it. I needed to cook it a lot longer than suggested because I stuffed the chicken, but when it was finally done it was delicious. I will make it again but perhaps use a smaller chicken and not stuff it! I also added water to the bottom of the pan.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pink stuff     cherry pie filling  pineapple dessert

my husband and children would literally die without this for the holidays!  and it is so easy!  my husband says it is a side dish.  i say it is a dessert.

1. combine all ingredients and mix well
2. serve chilled
3. your family and friends will go nuts
demonstrations.review: My husband's aunt made this for Thanksgiving and I immediately asked her for the recipe, and here it is!!! I think I added drained mandarin oranges too though. Delicious, simple, and should def. be a dessert (IMO)!!!

target.recipe_text:
tandoori white fish with a green chili rice

this is a very simple, quick and easy recipe to make, you can have it on the table in about 35-40 minutes and that time is only because, of the longer cooking time for the rice. it tastes very good, i serve mine with a yogurt sauce, which i will list ingredients below, but you can serve as is or with whatever is your preference.

1. combine paste with 80ml of the coconut milk place fish fillets in paste and leave in the fridge while making the rice
2. rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear
3. combine rice , water , chili , rind and remaining coconut milk in a saucepan , bring to the boil , reduce to a simmer and cook covered about 15-20 minutes stirring occasionally , until rice is tender
4. while the rice is cooking , heat the oil in a large frying pan add onion and carrot , cook stirring a couple of minutes
5. place fish fillets on top of vegetables , cook covered about 10 minutes uncover and cook a couple minutes more or until fish is cooked through
6. yogurt sauce
7. combine all the ingredients in a bowl and mix well
8. to serve: spoon some vegetables onto a plate top with fish and drizzle with yogurt sauce if desired
9. serve the rice on the side
target.review: I had to make a few substitutions, so that may be the problem, but I found the rice lacking in a little flavor.  I loved how easy it was to cook the fish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked rice and lentils

serve this instead of potatoes at your next dinner party. it can be vegetarian if vegetable stock is substituted for the chicken stock. this can also be served cold. the left overs can be frozen in one or two serving packages.

1. soak lentils in water for 2 hours then drain
2. combine lentils , rice and onions in large casserole
3. stir in remaining ingredients and cover
4. bake@ 425 for 25 minutes
5. stir and mix well and bake 20 minutes longer or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed
6. for vegetarian use the vegetable stock
demonstrations.review: Very easy and delicious. I also served it with steamed veggies. Next time I might spice it up a bit more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of ihop buttermilk pancakes by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com. these are my favorite pancakes...so light and fluffy.

1. preheat a skillet over medium heat
2. mix all of the ingredients til combined
3. melt a little bit of butter in the pan
4. pour the batter by spoonfuls into the hot pan , forming 5-inch circles
5. when the edges appear to harden , flip the pancakes
6. they should be golden brown
7. cook the pancakes on the other side until they are also golden brown
8. enjoy
demonstrations.review: This is my new staple recipe. Light and fluffy, wonderfully delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fat free asian salad dressing

a tangy dressing that you only need to use a tiny bit of because it's richly flavored. it's fat free and wonderful! if you must, then you can drizzle a little olive oil into your salad after tossing it with this dressing but, honestly, it doesn't need it to make a delicious salad! also a yummy dressing for sauteed tofu and vegetables. enjoy!

1. there are 2 options for preparing this dressing
2. you can either whir ingredients in blender , which makes it a little frothy- which i like
3. or , you can finely mince the garlic and ginger and whip the rest of the ingredients together with a wire whisk
4. either way , it's fabulous !
5. you can easily double this recipe- just keep the 2 to 1 ratio for the garlic and ginger and the soy sauce and vinegar
demonstrations.review: Solid Asian flavor. It was very strong and a little went a long way, which was actually nice to have a salad that wasn't drenched in dressing. I'll make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern black eyed peas

i love black-eyed peas! i'd much rather have fresh peas than dried, but i'll take them anyway i can get them. i don't remember where i found this recipe, but i really like it.  the original recipe used salt pork, but i use bacon. give me a bowl of these peas, a dash of tabasco, a slab of hot-from-the-oven cornbread, some green onions and tomato slices then stand out of the way!

1. in a 5 quart dutch oven , cook bacon until crisp
2. set aside to drain on paper towels
3. cook onion , celery and garlic in bacon drippings until tender
4. add broth , salt , pepper and peas
5. bring to a boil and skim top if necessary
6. lower heat to simmer
7. crumble bacon and add to peas
8. adjust seasonings to taste , cover and simmer until peas are tender
demonstrations.review: So tasty, just a few of us finished the whole pot! I think the bacon I used was a little too fatty and the broth tasted a bit oily, but delicious! We'll make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sour cream bran muffins with apples

this muffin recipe came from an advertisement for breakstone dairy products.  it is moist and flavorful and not too sweet.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. grease muffin tin
3. combine sour cream , butter and egg
4. add bran flakes , let stand till softened
5. add combined dry ingredients , mixing till just moistened
6. fold in apples
7. spoon into greased muffin cups , filling cups 3 / 4 full
8. bake at 375 25 minutes
demonstrations.review: I thought these muffins were good, they were dense and didn't rise very much, but they were tasty.

target.recipe_text:
brunch bake

i like this recipe for when we have overnight guests. you can serve a lot of people without spending all your time in the kitchen. and---it taste great!

1. in lg skillet , saute onion and garlic in butter for 1 minute
2. stir in ham and tomato
3. set aside
4. mix the biscuit mix and water
5. mix well
6. press onto bottom and halfway up sides of a greased 13x9 baking pan
7. spread ham mixture over crust
8. sprinkle with cheese
9. mix eggs , milk , dill , salt and pepper
10. pour over cheese
11. sprinkle with chives
12. bake at 350 for 30 minutes
target.review: Very nice flavor and not too much work except for the crust.  Getting it spread in the pan was impossible!  I never did get it half way up the sides.  The dough was just too sticky.  I'll make my own biscuit dough next time instead of using the Bisquick.  Otherwise I liked this recipe.  Nice combination of flavors and not too heavy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy bisquick coffee cake

very easy and perfect warm with a little pat of butter! :)

1. heat oven to 375f
2. grease round pan
3. prepare streusel topping and set aside
4. mix well bisquick , milk , sugar and egg
5. spread in pan and sprinkle with streusel topping
6. bake 18-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Probably because I don't have any fond childhood memories of making or eating this coffee cake, I found it rather disappointing.  It was kind of bland and a little dry, really nothing special.  I ended up feeding half of it to my dogs.  They loved it!  Nothing really wrong with it, just not worth the calories.
