I think it might be better with some blueberries in it. It was very quick and easy to make, but next time I'll probably do the extra work and make something from scratch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground pork with carrots and peppers

this is a variation on a recipe from an old friend. i added the carrots to save having to prepare an additional side dish and my family likes it better. the peppers are added in 2 stages, so some are still slightly crisp.

1. in a wok combine pork , onion and carrots
2. cook until no pink remains in the pork and carrots are tender crisp
3. drain off any fat
4. to pork mixture add pasta , soya , worcestershire and water
5. stir to coat
6. add approx 1 / 2 of the peppers
7. cover and simmer 10 minutes
8. toss and add remaining peppers
9. cover again and simmer an additional 5 minutes until sauce thickens and vegetables are tender
10. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent recipe: delicious, easy, inexpensive, and healthy. I made it as written except that I used rotini instead of angel hair.  Since it had pasta in it, I didn't serve it over rice.  Next time I think I'll add some celery.  My family liked this and wants to have it again.  This is going into my regular rotation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan heart attack chocolate doughnuts

nan

1. beat the egg replacer and sugar together until creamy in consistency
2. melt the margarine and chocolate together in a small saucepan over low heat
3. beat into the sugar mixture until well combined
4. combine the soy milk , vinegar and vanilla
5. stir this into the sugar / chocolate mixture
6. in another bowl , combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
7. stir this into the liquid mixture until it forms a dough
8. chill this for about 1 / 2 hour to make it easier to handle
9. roll 1 / 2 the dough out onto a lightly floured board to a 1 / 2" thickness
10. cut out the doughnuts with a 3" diameter doughnut cutter
11. let them rest for about 10 minutes before frying
12. repeat with the rest of the dough
13. deep fry in hot oil for about 90 seconds each , turning every 15 seconds
14. remove from the hot oil and allow them to drain on paper towels
15. cool , and ice , glaze or sprinkle with powdered sugar as per your desires
demonstrations.review: I was really excited about making vegan doughnuts -- chocolate to boot!  Unfortunately, even though I followed the recipe exactly, and kept my oil at 375, these were the worst culinary disaster of my life.  I got greasy globs with uncooked centers.  So bad I threw away more than half the dough. Not sure what went wrong, but I'm going to look for a different recipe.  Glad this works better for others, but it's not for me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
finnish pasties

growing up as a young girl, my best friend's mom would make these. she was born in finland and came over to america as a young girl and was raised in ishpeming, michigan. the family migrated out west after she married and had her own family. her kitchen always had the most wonderful aroma of good things baking. her pasties and braided bread were the best!

1. with a wire whisk , mix together flour and salt in a large bowl
2. cut in shortening
3. make a well in the center of the mixture and quickly stir in the ice cold water
4. form dough into a ball
5. set aside
6. dissolve the bouillon cube or beef base in the hot water
7. combine potatoes , carrots , onion , rutabaga , ground beef , pork , salt , pepper , and bouillon
8. roll out pastry dough into 6 x 8 inch rectangles
9. place about 1 1 / 2 cups of filling in the center of each rectangle
10. bring 6 inch sides together , and seal
11. cut a slit in the top of each pasty to vent
12. place on dull , not black , cokkie sheet
13. bake in 425 degree oven for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I used turkey instead of the beef and pork.  Otherwise, I followed the recipe as written.  Pasties were excellent.  The only reason I'm not giving this recipe 5 stars is that I didn't come out even with the dough and filling.  By rolling the dough out really thin, I was able to get 8 pasties, but I still had quite a bit of filling left.  I measured too!  I like a thicker crust, so next time, I'm going to double the amount of dough and make a dozen pasties.  I might increase the rutabaga and decrease the potato slightly, but that's just a personal preference detail.  These pasties were great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey tetrazzini casserole

this is a make-ahead meal: one of many i made in preparation for the birth of my daughter. this would be a great way to use leftover thanksgiving turkey.

1. this is a make ahead meal and there are three ways you can make these: individual pans
2. family casseroles
3. and company sized
4. cook linguine 3 / 4 of time recommended by manufacturer
5. rinse under cold running water until cool and let drain
6. combine everything but butter , breadcrumbs , and cheese
7. pour this mixture equally into whatever sized pan you have decided on
8. freeze uncovered while you make the breadcrumbs
9. melt the butter
10. stir breadcrumbs in and cook until light amber
11. spread hot crumbs on a plate and refrigerate about 30 minutes to cool
12. blend parmesan into cooled crumbs
13. spread crumbs evenly over pan
14. cover with foil and label
15. when ready to cook preheat oven to 400 and uncover pan
16. both the individual and family sizes take an hour to cook
17. the company size takes an hour and 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Kind of dry and bland.  My family didn't like it.

target.recipe_text:
herb coated cod

a very simple but yummy way to prepare cod.  the buttery flavor has saved more than one meal of frozen cod at our house.  i thank harriet stichter of milford, in for submitting this to toh, as it appears in the toh cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees fahrenheit
2. grease a 13-inch x 9-inch x 2-inch baking dish
3. crush butter-flavored crackers either in a ziploc bag with a rolling pin or bottle of sherry , or in a food processor
4. melt butter over low heat , and place in a shallow bowl
5. in another bowl , combine the crackers , cheese and seasonings
6. dip fillets in butter , then coat with crumbs
7. place coated cod fillets in baking dish
8. bake , uncovered , at 400 degrees fahrenheit for 15-20 minutes or until fish flakes easily with a fork
target.review: Delicious!  I used panko crumbs instead of cracker crumbs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolaty peanut butter banana bread

you have to try this!! what a great combination-how can you go wrong with peanut butter, chocolate, and bananas?? this recipe is from the better homes and gardens annual recipes cook book (1998).

1. grease the bottom and 1 / 2 inch up the sides of two loaf pans
2. set aside
3. in a medium mixing bowl stir together the eggs , bananas , sugar , peanut butter , and milk
4. stir in the flour just until moistened
5. fold in chocolate pieces and peanuts or pecans
6. spoon batter into the prepared pans
7. bake in a 350f oven about 45 minutes or until a wooden toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean
8. cool in pans on a wire rack for 10 minutes
9. remove loaves from pans
10. cool completely on a wire rack
11. wrap and store overnight for easier slicing
12. if you do not have self-rising flour , substitute with 2 cups all-purpose flour plus 2 teaspoons baking powder , 1 teaspoon salt , and 1 / 2 teaspoons baking soda
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe.  I made mini-muffins, and small loaves to include in my husband's lunch.  Perfect alternative to the same ol'banana bread.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory pot roast a la pressure cooker

the flavor of this pot roast is wonderful. the pressure cooker seems to force the seasoning right into the meat and vegetables.  sunday dinner after church in the south was fried chicken, but in the midwestern u.s. region, it was potroast.  yum.

1. coat roast with seasonall
2. in a non-stick pan , brown meat in olive oil , on high , on all sides to sear in juices
3. add carrots , celery and onions when meat is nearly browned
4. add water and worcestershire sauce
5. place potato halves on top of roast and add pepper , beef bouillon powder and bay leaves
6. lock pressure cooker lid in place and bring to pressure over medium-high heat
7. adjust heat to stabilize pressure at about medium pressure
8. cook for one hour
9. release pressure naturally - don't use quick release
10. as all pressure cookers are different , test meat and fork the potatoes to make sure they are done
11. if not , add water , if necessary , and return to pressure
12. when done , release pressure and serve
demonstrations.review: I love the way it turned out.  We didn't care for the flavor though.  Maybe it was the Worcestershire sauce?  I'm not sure.  I am going to use this as a base though and change the seasonings and try it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole foods  tarragon chicken salad

the whole foods here makes this *wonderful* chicken salad- but for $8/lb!!! this tastes about exactly the same for far less money.

1. bake or boil chicken breasts until tender and cooked through
2. cut breasts into bite-sized pieces
3. discard skin and bones if you did not use boneless , skinless breasts
4. whisk sour cream and mayonnaise together and pour over chicken
5. add celery , walnuts , tarragon , salt and pepper to taste and toss well
6. refrigerate and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: One word....DIVINE!  I love it!  Adding it to my Tried and True!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracker barrel green beans

this is the only way i can eat canned green beans!

1. in a 2-quart saucepan over medium heat , cook bacon until lightly brown but not crisp
2. when bacon has browned , add green beans
3. add salt , sugar and pepper and mix well
4. place onion on top of green beans
5. cover saucepan with a lid and bring to a light boil
6. turn heat down to low and simmer beans for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: A nice "dress up" for the everyday can of green beans!  Love them. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really really good candied sweet potatoes

we like sweet potatoes a lot, and don't wait for a holiday to fix these.

1. cover potatoes with water , bring to a boil
2. lower heat and simmer for 25 minutes , until done
3. when cooled , peel and cut into chunks
4. place in 2-qt baking dish
5. in small saucepan combine remaining ingredients , cook and stir until mixture boils
6. pour over potatoes
7. bake at 350f for 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: Oh wow!  So very yummy!  I love the addition of cinnamon and maple syrup!

target.recipe_text:
the most ultimate buttery cream cheese pound cake

this is the most ultimate rich dense buttery pound cake! no lein this cake but the eggs--- for best results this cake should be baked a day ahead and wrapped in plastic, or it can be frozen for up to 3 months, servings is of coarse estimated ---  this is wonderful served with a blueberry or strawberry sauce :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. generously grease two 8 x 4-inch loaf pans or a 4-quart tube pan
3. in a bowl cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
4. add sugar
5. beat until light and fluffy , about 5-7 minutes
6. add the eggs one at a time beating well after each addition
7. mix in vanilla
8. with mixer on low add the flour and salt in two additions
9. immediately pour in batter into prepared pan
10. tap pans to eliminate any large air bubbles in the batter
11. bake 60-75 minutes , or until cakes tests done
12. cool in pans for 10 minutes
13. turn out the cakes then cool completely with the tops up on a wire rack
target.review: Excellent pound cake recipe! I did have to extend the cooking time quite a bit but it was so worth it. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
individual cream cheese danish

small danishes that make a great addition to a brunch buffet. you can also make fruit and cream cheese danishes by adding a spoonful of your favorite pie filling prior to baking. there are never any leftovers when i make these.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. slice crescent roll dough into 1 / 4 inch slices
3. place slices of dough on cookie sheet and make slight indention in the middle
4. in a large bowl , mix together cream cheese , white sugar , lemon juice , vanilla extract and sour cream
5. add a tablespoon of filling to each roll
6. bake in preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes
7. in a small bowl , stir together confectioners' sugar , milk and butter
8. after danish has cooled , drizzle with icing
demonstrations.review: These have a nice flavor filling, but too (unnecisarily) sweet for me and I was dissapointed by the cresent rolls. They just tasted almost like canned biscuits. Next time I will make these with puff pastry, which will be just as easy, but much tastier and authentic. I probably won't make this recipe again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked ziti with spinach  sausage  and mozzarella

delicious ziti recipe with fresh spinach. easy!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. heat heavy large saucepan over medium heat
3. add sausage , onion , and garlic , and saute until sausage cooked through , about 10 minutes , breaking up meat with back of spoon
4. add tomatoes with juice to pan
5. simmer until sauce thickens slightly , stirring occasionally , about 10 minutes
6. stir in pesto sauce
7. season with salt and pepper
8. lightly oil 13 x 9 glass baking dish
9. combine pasta , spinach , mozzarella , and 1 / 3 cup parmesan cheese in large bowl
10. stir in hot tomato sauce
11. mix gently until spinach is wilted
12. transfer mixture to prepared baking dish
13. sprinkle remaining 2 / 3 cup parmesan cheese over top
14. bake until sauce bubbles and cheese melt , about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe. I have seen this one before on Epicurious.com and made it many times, I think it was originally from BonAppetite or Gourmet magazine. Anyhow, this is a tasty recipe. Thanks for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reduced fat alfredo sauce

this sauce is lower in fat than traditional alfredo sauce but full of flavour. great as a side with grilled chicken or double it for a meal with meat filled pasta.

1. the key here is patience , add all ingredients gradually !
2. melt butter in sauce pan on stove top with medium heat
3. gradually whisk in flour
4. this will create a yellow paste
5. gradually add milk , whisking until incorporated and no lumps are present
6. continue to whisk until hot
7. usually 3-5 minutes
8. the longer you cook the base the thicker the sauce will be
9. add parmesan slowly , again whisking until incorporated
10. add crushed garlic and pepper
11. cook for 2 minutes or until cheese is melted
12. remove from heat
demonstrations.review: Fast, tasty, and healthier! I love it. I added some diced shallots to the butter and let them cook down before I added the flour....it added another layer of flavor. Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bran flax muffins

recipe from bob's red mill.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix together flour , flaxseed meal , oat bran , brown sugar , baking soda , baking powder , salt and cinnamon in a large bowl
3. stir in carrots , apples , raisins and nuts
4. combine milk , beaten eggs and vanilla
5. pour liquid ingredients into dry ingredients
6. stir until ingredients are moistened
7. do not over mix
8. fill muffin cups 3 / 4 full
9. bake for 15-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe. These came out so tender and flavorful! I always buy Bob's Red Mill products, they are so high quality. Thanks for posting this great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barefoot contessa s turkey meatloaf

this is an ina garten recipe from the barefoot contessa cookbook. my husband is fussy about his meatloaf, but really likes the texture and flavor of this.

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. saute onions in olive oil until translucent , about 15 minutes
3. add salt , pepper , thyme , worcestershire sauce , chicken stock and tomato paste and mix well
4. allow to cool to room temperature
5. combine ground turkey , bread crumbs , egg and onion mixture in a large bowl
6. mix wll and shape into a rectangular loaf on an ungreased sheet pan
7. spread the ketchup evenly on top
8. bake for 1 1 / 2 hours until the internal temperature is 160f and the meatloaf is cooked through
demonstrations.review: Perfect! This is so very delicious and everyone LOVES it! I do add mustard to the ketchup topping but that is my only change. I can't say enough good things about this recipe. I have to agree with the previous review about the onions, it is a large amount but it does make this meatloaf delicious by keeping it moist and adding flavor.

target.recipe_text:
spicy catsup

i've been making this one for over 30 years now, and still have not learned that by the end of april it's all gone.

1. cook tomatoes , peppers and onions without adding water for 1 hour hard boil
2. press mixture through a strainer
3. return to heat and add salt , sugar and spices
4. boil rapidly until thick again
5. strain again to remove whole allspice and cloves
6. return to heat , bring to hard boil and add vinegar
7. boil till desired consistency
8. laddle into hot jars and seal immediately
9. can be processed in a hot water bath , boiling 5 minutes , i never do and have not had one spoil yet
target.review: This is outstanding! My only regret is that I didn't make enough. It's only October, and already I am down to my last two pints. Next year, I'll know to make a double batch. Thanks, Renate!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeno cheese grits

my husband's favorite. we eat this with just about everything, in place of mashed potatoes.

1. bring water and salt to rapid boil
2. add grits , reduce heat , and cook until grits are thickened , about 3-4 minutes
3. stir in butter and velveeta cheese until melted
4. mix eggs , milk , and black pepper together , and then add to the grits mixture
5. stir in the chopped jalapenos
6. pour into casserole dish
7. bake uncovered for 45 minutes or until set in a 300 degree oven
8. sprinkle jack cheese on top , and return to the oven for 15 more minutes
demonstrations.review: I love trying new recipes. Unfortunately, I made one recently, that while certainly exotic, ended up being completely inedible. I searched frantically through some recipes  that utilized the limited ingredients that I had on hand, and came up with jalapeno cheeese grits. Oh, my! These were absolutely divine. I actually served them as a main dish, with a green salad. I did end up using sharp cheddar in place of the velveeta, and also in place of the pepper/jack cheese. (It's all I had on hand) No matter. The result was pure heaven, and dinner was saved!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey thighs with olives and cherries   crock pot

cooking light oct 2003. use a cut up chicken if you can't find turkey thighs.

1. combine the first 9 ingredients in an electric slow cooker , stirring to combine
2. stir in 1 / 2 teaspoon salt
3. rinse turkey with cold water
4. pat dry
5. sprinkle with remaining 1 teaspoon salt and cumin
6. place in slow cooker
7. cover with lid , and cook on low 6 hours
8. discard cinnamon stick
demonstrations.review:
Wow. Wow. This is incredibly good! I used boneless skinless chicken thighs instead of turkey, but other than that, I made this exactly as written, and OMG!!!
Herty, sweet, spicy with the tang of kalamata olives.This just might be the perfect recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
golden tofu salad with carrots and hijiki

the mild hijiki is a great way to introduce seaweed to wary family and friends. this was my favorite recipe from the whole foods class i took in spring of 2003 at bastyr university. careful - the salad is highly addictive!

1. in a small saucepan , soak hijiki for 10 minutes
2. once rehydrated , simmer the seaweed uncovered for 20 minutes or until the water has evaporated
3. remove from heat and allow to cool
4. meanwhile , drain the tofu and slice the cake horizontally
5. place between sheets of paper towels and put on a cutting board with a heavy weight atop the tofu to press away excess water
6. a cast iron skillet or heavy book is ideal
7. drain the tofu for at least 15 minutes
8. cut into cubes and brown evenly on all sides using 1 tabblespoon of sesame oil
9. remove from pan and sprinkle with tamari
10. set aside to cool
11. in a large bowl , whisk together vinegar , oil , ginger , and salt
12. add seaweed , tofu , and veggies
13. toss well and allow flavors to marry for at least 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Addictive, indeed! I've made this three times already since discovering it here about a month ago. Nice contrast of textures, and a fresh clean flavor. Also, keeps well in the refrigerator for a few days. Thanks, BelovedRooster!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german potato cheese soup

nan

1. peel and prepare vegetables
2. in a large cooking pot , add water , chicken broth , chicken soup base , black pepper , carrots , potatoes , onions and bring to boil
3. reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes or until vegetables are tender
4. stirring occasionally
5. add celery , sweet red pepper and simmer for 5 minutes more
6. gradually add mayonnaise to hot soup , whisking until smooth
7. reduce heat to medium and add processed cheese , sharp cheddar cheese and swiss cheese and simmer for 5 minutes or until cheese melts and soup is creamy
8. stirring constantly
9. add instant mashed potatoes and stir well
10. let soup sit for 15 minutes before serving
11. this soup is very rich , but good
12. refrigerate any unused portion
13. serves 12
demonstrations.review: Coldest day of the year in Ohio, and I just wanted to stay inside, and make a big pot of soup. This was perfect! Initially, I was skeptical of the Miracle Whip, but it gave this soup that inimitable "something", that was just right. I'm not a red pepper fan, but instead, added some steamed broccoli and cauliflower, stirred in at the end. Also, something about this soup, just screamed for cayenne pepper. I'm glad I listened!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wild about creamy wild mushroom soup

sinfully rich! you can use veggie stock instead of the chicken stock.
use your favorite dried and fresh mushrooms.

1. soak dried mushrooms in 1 cup hot water till softened
2. remove mushrooms and drain liquid through cheesecloth and saving liquid and discarding sandy bits
3. chop mushrooms set aside
4. in the drained hot liquid and crushed pinch of saffron
5. set aside
6. in a large pot over medium heat melt 2 tablespoons oil and 2 tablespoons butter
7. saute onions , garlic and all the mushrooms season with thyme , salt and pepper about 5 minutes
8. optional carrot and celery may be added along with onions
9. add sherry reduce to half
10. add chicken stock and liquid reserved from mushrooms simmer 20 minutes
11. in a separate pot melt 4 tablespoons butter then add flour to make a thick paste whisk in 1 pint of cream
12. then whisk into soup
13. using a hand blender puree the soup to a nice consistency
14. let simmer 5 more minutes stirring so not to burn
15. serve with soup topped with a little extra sherry
demonstrations.review:
I was  looking for a recipe similar to O'Charley's wild mushroom soup, and decided that this recipe seemed the most likely. Actually, it turned out to be even better. More interesting, more depth of flavor.
 Ah, this soup is just perfect.

target.recipe_text:
peanut butter rice crispy bars

peanut butter and chocolate rice crispy bars.
i got the recipe from a friend of the family after years of begging for it. everyone loves these, they have always been a big hit at the school sporting event snack stands.

1. measure out rice crispies and set aside in large bowl
2. in saucepan combine sugar and karo
3. bring just to simmer , then add the peanut butter and stir
4. do not let the sugar mixture boil
5. stir peanut butter mixture into rice crispies and stir quickly
6. it will start to harden immediately
7. pour mixture into a 9x12 pan and flatten out evenly across pan
8. combine chocolate and butterscotch chips into saucepan and melt over a double boiler and stir constantly
9. when melted pour over peanut butter mixture
10. let it set
11. when set , cut into squares
target.review: these were pretty good, the only change i made was i only had choc. chips. So that is what i used for topping. They were also semi sweet, and i think milk choc. ones would have been better. But all and all i highly recomend these. I will be making again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my mil s coleslaw

my mil gave me the 'ingredients only'...........she never measured anything. after several attempts, i got it right. i made her proud. i prefer to chop the veggies rather than grate (like kfc's cole slaw - which this tastes like). servings are approximate.

1. in a food processor , chop cabbage , carrots , peppers and onion
2. chop them one-at-a-time-- not all together
3. put into a large bowl and add remaining ingredients
4. mix well
5. best prepared the day before you plan to serve to allow flavors to blend and juice to form
demonstrations.review: This was actually my first time making slaw, and this turned out yummy. Even better the next day. I ate some with supper last night, but have been nibbling on it today and it is even better. This is a keeper

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy baked shrimp

yummmmmmy!! spicy, so have plenty of cold beverages around.

1. combine first 7 ingredients
2. layer shrimp and lemon slices in a 13x9 inch baking dish
3. top with sauce
4. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes or until shrimp turn pink , stirring once
5. remove shrimp , reserving sauce
6. serve shrimp with reserved sauce and french bread
demonstrations.review: good taste, made a nice dish. May try this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oreo cookie turkeys

build an oreo turkey with oreos, candy and frosting. this would be a fun activity for (school-age) kids at a thanksgiving gathering to put these together.  they can display them at their dinner place and eat them for dessert....if they can wait that long.  the recipe i am listing will be to make one dozen turkeys.

1. place one oreo cookie as the base
2. put one teaspoon of chocolate frosting on top
3. place one small peanut butter cup on it's side so that the top and bottom are perpendicular to the base -- and stuck in the frosting
4. place a teaspoon of chocolate frosting on the top of the p-butter cup
5. for the second cookie
6. stick some candy corn into the oreo 'stuff' along one edge for the feathers -- pointy side down
7. they should fan out around the edge
8. if you have trouble doing this , you can help them stick with some white frosting
9. place this second oreo cookie on it's edge and sticking to a dab of brown frosting on the back of the peanut butter cup
10. place a dab of chocolate frosting on top of the peanut butter up
11. place a malted milk ball on top for the head
12. take a small amount of the white frosting in a separate dish
13. mix in red food coloring
14. use a toothpick with the white and red colors to place eyes , and wattle
15. you can pinch off the small pointy top of a candy corn and dip it in brown frosting for the beak
16. your turkey is complete !
demonstrations.review: i haven't made these yet, but i have to say this is one of the cutest things i have seen. I am definantly makeing these for my son to take to school next month. thanks for such a great idea.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan squash toss

a nice summertime side dish.

1. slice zucchini and yellow squash diagonally
2. saute' vegetables in olive oil in large skillet over medium-high heat 3 minutes or until crisp-tender
3. add cheese and remaining ingredients
4. toss gently
5. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: made a  nice change from breading and frying, I probably wont make this again as it was a little bland but like i said it was a change at least.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake peanut butter balls

can't get much easier than this! cook time is actually chilling time.

1. mix all ingredients
2. roll into 1-inch balls
3. roll in chocolate sprinkles , nuts , or confectioner's sugar if desired , then chill
demonstrations.review: me and my son made these and the taste was ok but very crumbly. He liked them more than i did. Will not be making agin, kinda made a mess was all.

target.recipe_text:
einstein bros bagels ultimate toasted cheese sandwich

calling all cheese fanatics! do you love cheese?  i think i may have the sandwich for you.  my local einstein brothers used to have this on their menu - if i recall correctly, it was around the year 2001.  back then, this sandwich cost about $6 or so, so i figured out how to make these for myself at home.  this glorious sandwich has since been pulled from the menu, probably because the fat content is enough to induce an instant heart attack!  ha ha, just kidding of course. anyway, i love this sandwich (in moderation) and it's very easy to make using a sandwich maker,grill or skillet. bon appetit!

1. lightly butter each slice of bread and place , butter side down on a plate
2. spread 1 tablespoon of chive and onion cream cheese on each slice
3. top one piece of bread with slice of tomato
4. layer with swiss , cheddar , provolone and pepper jack cheese
5. top with second slice of tomato
6. place second slice of bread on top so that buttered side faces out
7. place in lightly oiled skillet and grill on medium heat until lightly browned
8. turn over , and lightly brown the other side
9. cut in half and enjoy with a dill pickle !
10. these can also be made with a sandwich / panini maker or placed under the broiler until cheese is melted
target.review: OMG!!  This was awesome! Cheese heaven. I made exactly as written and even served with the pickles too!! Thanks so much for posting! Made for My 3 Chefs '08

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot pork chops

i make this for my husband and daughter, and i have got nothing but smiles from this.  it's easy, cheap and oh so yummy!

1. combine cream of mushroom soup , 1 / 3 can water , softened cream cheese and garlic in a bowl
2. stir out most of the lumps , but the rest will cook out
3. pour in bottom of crock pot
4. put pork chops on top of mixture
5. add liberal amounts of salt and pepper
6. i'm usually heavy handed !
7. cook on low for 7-8 hours
8. serve over slices of warm bread or pasta of your choice
9. pork chops will fall apart
10. so tender you can cut with a spoon !
demonstrations.review: These are "oh so yummy"! I used fat free cream of mushroom soup and fat free cream cheese. I also added a can of mushrooms. Very easy to throw together and I will be making these again as they were enjoyed by all. Thanks! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s  goulash  awesome   feed an army w  3 cheap  ingredients

tomato soup goulash: it's easy and takes no time to make!! this has fed a family of 4 boys and me with enough for seconds!!

1. while water is boiling for noodles cook and drain ground beef
2. add large can of soup to cooked and drained noodles
3. mix in meat
4. eat and get stuffed !
5. use the small can for leftovers- or add to taste
6. double the recipe for larger families
demonstrations.review: I tought a group of 4-H kids to cook this weekend and this was one of my choices.It turned out very good x7 and everyone enjoyed it. They also added garlic powder,which was a nice addition. We ended up using the extra small can of tomato soup to make it wetter while we were mixing it. I got phone calls from all families saying that they really enjoyed their dinner.(All the kids took their dishes home to feed their families.) My DD made this too and we topped ours with shredded mozzarella cheese. You couldn't be more correct with the name of this dish...it really does feed alot of people! Thanks for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon breaded fried chicken

if you like the taste of lemon, you will like this chicken. served with parsley potatoes and garlic green beans and you have a great meal.

1. place chicken and lemon juice into a zip-lock bag
2. refrigerate for 2 hours turning pieces occasionally
3. remove chicken from bag and pat dry with paper towels
4. in a medium mixing bowl , blend together salt and flour
5. place each chicken breast into flour and shake off excess
6. in another bowl , lightly beat egg
7. after chicken is dipped into flour dip it then into the beaten egg
8. in a skillet , brown chicken breasts in oil
9. the oil should be 1 / 4 inch at all times during frying
10. if you can't fry all the chicken at the same time , place cooked chicken on a warm platter in an oven preheated to 200f
11. cover cooked chicken with aluminum foil
12. place cut lemon wedges on platter with chicken before serving
demonstrations.review: This made for a wonderful dinner!! The breasts soaked in the refrigerator all day until dinner time. I followed the recipe except that I used egg beaters instead of an egg. I used Italian bread crumbs and added them in step 7. I dipped into the  flour mixture, egg and then the  breadcrumbs. I hope that's how it was supposed to go because it worked! :)  Thanks so much for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dorito dip

i great, hearty dip that goes great with those flavored tortilla chips. simple to prepare and a great addition to any party.

1. brown ground beef and drain well
2. mix all ingredients well
3. heat and serve
demonstrations.review: Everyone loved this dip! It was easy to put together. I used ground turkey because we don't eat beef. It went perfect with Doritos and was gone in a flash. Thanks so much for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
m   m dream bars

these are yummy! the original recipe called for red and green christmas m&ms, but i see no reason to relegate this delicious treat to just the holidays. :)

1. combine oatmeal , brown sugar , flour , coconut , baking soda , and salt
2. add melted butter and stir until moist
3. reserve 1 1 / 2 cups and press remaining crumbs into a greased 13x9-inch baking pan
4. bake 12 minutes at 375f
5. combine milk and peanut butter
6. carefully spread over baked crust
7. sprinkle on m&m's and chocolate chips
8. sprinkle reserved crumbs over chocolate pieces and lightly press crumbs down
9. bake 20 minutes , or until golden brown
10. cool completely before cutting
demonstrations.review: I've had this in my cookbook FOREVER and now I'm mad because I didn't make it sooner. First off, it's very easy to put together but I agree that you have to be very careful when putting on the peanut butter/milk layer. Secondly,I used Mega M&M's and they worked out great. I love the combo of all of the flavors. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
cream soup mix  replacement for cream of     soups  substitute

if you don’t have any cream soup on hand, (or maybe you just want to save money) try this—it’s  great.

1. mix all the ingredients together
2. store in an airtight container
3. for the equivalent of 1 can of cream soup , mix 1 / 3 cup of dry mix with 1 1 / 4 cups of cold water
4. cook in sauce pan until thick
5. entire recipe makes the equivalent of nine cans of cream soup
target.review: Thank you so much......for a cream-based lover turned dieter, this is heaven.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced beer batter

use for fish , chicken , vegetables , feta cheese or anything else you can come up with !

1. mix all the dry ingredients , add the oil and the beer
2. if you have the time , cover and leave to stand for a few hours , this will improve the texture of the batter{not in the refrigerator} just before you need it , beat the egg white stiff and fold it into the batter
3. whatever your choice of food , coat with flour first , dip in the batter , then deep fry
4. you can leave out the spices for a plain batter and use water instead of the beer
5. this is great for onion rings !
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! I fried chicken tenders and they're delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted edamame

i just discovered this recipe and can't wait to try this interesting way to use those wonderful edamame beans.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in small bowl , stir together oil , basil , chili powder , onion salt , cumin , paprika and black pepper
3. drizzle mixture over soybeans and toss to coat well
4. arrange beans in a single layer in a shallow baking dish
5. roast , uncovered , for 12 to 15 minutes , stirring once , until soybeans begin to brown
6. serve hot as a vegetable side dish or cooled as a snack
7. refrigerate any leftovers
demonstrations.review:
J-Lynn... to answer your question, no. There are ways to make them crispy, and you can buy them in natural food stores crispy, but edamame is traditionally like a cross between a soft bean and nut. 

As for the recipe, it's a different way to prepare edamame. I usually buy it fresh in the summer at the farmer's market and simply steam, but this adds a lot of flavor.

Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kentucky beer cheese

i grew up in central kentucky and now hold a kentucky derby party out here in california every year now.  it was approaching and i was jonesin for hall's beer cheese.  this was the recipe i settled on...

1. open beer and bring to room temperature it is desirable to get most of the gas out of the beer , but don't let it get stale
2. you can heat it in the microwave a bit if you are in a hurry , but don't boil it
3. grate cheese and garlic in a food processor
4. switch to the mixing blade and add remaining ingredients , mixing until thoroughly blended
5. refridgerate overnight
6. this really helps the flavors develop and meld properly
demonstrations.review: Living in Versailles, I really liked the idea of this recipe...love Hall's on the River. I made it tonight for the Season Opener tomorrow! I can't wait to take it tailgating. Go Cats!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh broccoli with spinach fusilli

excellent fresh tasting pasta with no heavy cream sauce.  i have also made with whole wheat pasta with excellent results. from the joy of pasta by joe famularo and louise imperiale.  serve with valpolicella or other dry medium bodied red wine.

1. in medium skillet heat olive oil
2. saute onion and garlic 2 minutes
3. add carrot and capers and cook 1 minute longer
4. add beef stock and pepper flakes
5. cook slowly for five minutes
6. meanwhile cook fusilli al dente
7. drain and return to pan
8. stir in sauce and broccoli into pasta and half the cheese
9. serve hot topped with the remaining cheese
demonstrations.review: Have to admit I used fresh spinach instead of spinach pasta...I had a couple of pounds of fresh spinach and a bunch of broccoli and I was looking for a veggie dish to go with some stuffed pork chops. It was so so good without the pasta, so I can only imagine how much better it would be with it! Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetable rice pancakes

nan

1. combine all ingredients except oil
2. form into 12 thin patties , pressing firmly with hands
3. in large skillet , cook patties in heated oil until brown , turning once
4. serve with dairy sour cream or yogurt , if desired
demonstrations.review: These were very tasty... I used regular flour, but will have whole wheat next time.... I used lots of fresh onion and garlic, and made them a little more pourable with milk. I fried them like fritters in hot olive oil and they were a total hit. Whole grain rice, organic veggies, olive oil....healthy, yet tastes really decadent. Thanks for posting a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
solo chicken breast teriyaki style

nan

1. slice chicken length wise into four pieces , and thread onto two thin sticks or sharpened chop sticks
2. mix the rest of the ingredients and use to marinate the chicken in a shallow dish for at least two hours
3. turn the meat at least once after the first hour
4. broil 5 to 6 inches from heat , turning once , or on a charcoal grill for about 10 minutes
5. heat marinade until it starts to bubble and pour over cooked meat after it has been removed from the sticks
6. serve over rice
7. 1 / 3 cup of raw rice grains , 2 / 3 cup of water
8. heat until it just starts to boil , cover and reduce flame to the lowest level
9. cook for 15 minutes without lifting the cover , and then let sit for an additional 5 minute with no heat before serving
10. this meal will go nice with a lettuce salad or a small side dish of vegetables
target.review: I would've never thought of using a shot glass to measure ingredients like this...I'll be passing this hint along to my readers!  Thanks, Bill!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat  green giant niblets corn in butter sauce

i had to come up with this quick. every thanksgiving my mom serves green giant niblets corn in butter sauce and i promised i would pick it up for her and bring it on thanksgiving day. when i went to the store, they were sold out! i made this recipe and brought it already prepared to thanksgiving dinner. nobody was the wiser! i saved some money too, because i used store brand corn! this recipe makes a lot...you may want to half it.

1. add corn to large sauce pan along with all ingredients except water and cornstarch
2. stir corn mixture over medium heat until butter is melted
3. combine water and cornstarch and stir until cornstarch is disolved
4. slowly add water to corn in sauce pan , stirring constantly
5. reduce heat to simmer and stir until sauce thickens
6. let simmer , stirring occasionally , until corn is tender , about 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Let me add my song of praise for this copycat.  I love corn, always have, always will, but usually it's out of my garden.  I couldn't find any our our frozen so I thought I'd just substitute a can I use for vegetable soup.  NEVER AGAIN will I snub my nose at canned corn, but only if it's fixed this way.  Thanks so much, Karen.  Now..if only to fool my parents with this dish...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sticky soy wings

a family favorite at the cabin.....

1. wash the chicken wings and dry as much as possible
2. preheat oven at 400 degrees
3. place chicken in a deep baking dish
4. mix all other ingredients together in a bowl
5. pour over chicken
6. place in oven or 1 1 / 2 hours or until chicken is done and sauce is sticky
7. important: due to the hot cooked sugar , chicken will be extra hot and easy to burn
8. be careful and let chicken sit for at least 15-20 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Made this with chicken tenders...pretty good, but the whang threw me at first.  I do have a suggestion, though.  Make these in one of those turkey oven bags and the clean-up is a cinch.  Don't tie the bag closed and the chicken comes out perfect just like the picture.  Hope this helps!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jack daniel s doodles

easy chocolate cookies with a kick!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. combine eggs , cake mix , oil , nuts and whiskey in batter bowl and mix well
3. chill dough overnight , or at least 3 hours
4. form into small balls and roll in powdered sugar
5. place cookies on ungreased baking sheet and bake for 10-15 minutes , until almost no indentation remains when touched
6. they will be soft when taken from the oven , but will crispen when cooled
7. bake for closer to 10 minutes if you like a softer cookie , closer to 15 for crispy ones !
8. if you want , sprinkle with a little more powdered sugar before serving
demonstrations.review: These were good, sort of like my tipsy cakes minus the coffee.  I am sure that I'll be baking these again, but trying rum and maybe a different whiskey.  Kudos, darlin...these were great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hopel popel

this dish could be served as a brunch dish, or for any light meal or snack.  when i came across this recipe tonight in a recipe book - the midweek cookbook: 200 ways with potatoes - i really hadn't looked at since the seventies, the name of this dish intrigued me.  a web search produced nothing  of relevance, just lots of references to dog breeding kennels! so unfortunately i know nothing of the origins of recipe's name.  i'm posting a c21st  adaptation here so that i remember to make it some time!  it's actually rather similar to what i've always referred to as a chip omelette, although i usually make that with diced raw potatoes.

1. saut the bacon , onion , garlic and mushrooms gently in the oil , preferably in a non-stick pan , then add the potatoes and allow them to warm through
2. beat the eggs , add the thyme , season to taste and pour over the potato mixture , sprinkle with grated cheese and cook slowly until the eggs have set
3. brown the top under the grill , cut into wedges and serve
demonstrations.review: This was good!  I halved the recipe (no need for a huge omelete when it's just me) and even halving the recipe, reduced the garlic (not a big garlic fan here).  I didn't boil the potato; I used some frozen hashbrowns.  I did enjoy this with a cup of coffee and will be putting this on the "Bed & Breakfast" list the next time I have guests.  KUDOS, Moonie!  This one is GREAT!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut milk ice cream

this is a merger of several recipes i found while researching for a special mothers day dinner. coconut is mom's favorite ice cream. this version is easy, not too sweet, smooth, creamy and quite tasty. it might be good with some coconut stirred in at the last. the cook time is freeze time and is variable depending on your machine. prep time does not include chill time for the coconut milk.

1. shake can of coconut milk to mix well
2. pour into large chilled bowl or pitcher
3. stir in cream , sugar and coconut rum until sugar is dissolved
4. pour into ice cream maker and freeze according to manufacturers directions
5. spoon into container , cover well and place in freezer to harden off
6. if desired , stir in flaked or toasted , flaked coconut before placing in freezer to harden
demonstrations.review: This was deeeelish!  I had some coconut milk leftover from another recipe in the back of my fridge and it was CRYING OUT to be used!  I did have to cut the recipe in half (which didn't effect anything but the quantity of my ice cream) because my little churn only makes a pint.  I didn't have anything but half-n-half, but it worked fine.  After it froze most of the way, I stuck it back in the freezer to firm up a bit more.  Absolutely a tropical treat!  Thanks so much for posting a great recipe!  I will definately be using this again!

target.recipe_text:
cream pasta sauce with zucchini

this is awesome pasta sauce! much different than alfredo-ish sauces, which i don't like. this one could be healthy, depending on which ingredients you use. i found the original version of this in a cookbook i received as a gift, but this is very different from that recipe.

1. melt butter in saucepan
2. cook minced garlic in butter for 3-4 minutes or until soft
3. stir in flour
4. cook for one minute , stirring constantly
5. add sour cream , milk , and lemon
6. cook until heated through
7. add zucchini , and cook just until bubbly
8. add to pasta
9. add parmesan and black pepper to taste
target.review: I used  a little less garlic and added some cheddar cheese as well, but it was a great sauce!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Really good and moist! I made muffins with this recipe too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wonton wrappers

i have posted this in response to a request. i have made them once, and found that they work fine. however, i usually find it easier to just buy them. still, it's a handy recipe to have around.

1. mix the salt and the flour
2. in a small bowl , add 1 / 4 cup water to the egg and beat gently
3. make a well in the middle of the flour , and add the egg-water mixture
4. mix into the flour , adding remaining water as needed
5. knead the dough into a ball
6. keep kneading until smooth
7. place the dough in a large bowl , cover with a damp cloth and let rest for 1 hour
8. cut the dough into quarters
9. place one of the quarters on a well-floured surface , and roll out with a rolling pin until very thin
10. cut the dough into the desired shapes
11. if stacking , dust the wrappers lightly with flour or cornstarch to keep them from sticking together
12. keep cut wrappers covered with plastic wrap to keep them from drying out too much
13. repeat with the other quarters
14. if not using immediately , wrap in plastic wrap and store in the refrigerator or freezer
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe - easy to do and works perfectly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sesame tofu

serve with steamed or sauteed vegetables and brown rice

1. wrap tofu with paper towels and place on a cutting board
2. put a heavy plate on top to press out liquid for approximately 20 minutes
3. stir sauce ingredients together in a saucepan
4. simmer sauce while you cook the tofu
5. dry drained tofu with paper towels and cube
6. dust very lightly with cornstarch
7. heat 1" oil in deep frying pan
8. fry tofu in 350 degree f oil until golden brown
9. place fried tofu in a large bowl and toss with 2 / 3 cup sauce , sprinkle liberally with sesame seeds and scallions
10. toss gently
11. serve remaining sauce for dipping or drizzled over vegetables
demonstrations.review: very good - especially the second day when the tofu had time to take in the sauce's flavour

demonstrations.recipe_text:
edna s apple crumble  aka  apple crisp

a simple and easy to make but oh so yummy recipe. known as apple crumble in the uk and apple crisp in the us

1. put apples in an 8 or 9 inch square baking dish
2. combine the rest of the ingredients in a separate bowl and mix
3. spread crumble mixture over apples and bake for 35 minutes in a 375f degree oven
4. for an added treat top off with a little english custard
demonstrations.review: Excellent - I don't usually use nutmeg, but it made it extra spicy and my guests loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fabulous honey white bread   bread machine

this recipe makes a loaf of bread that is high rising, soft textured, slices well, and keeps well too. all the qualities we get in store bought bread but, warm and fresh out of the bread machine, at a fraction of the cost too. i make this recipe 3 to 4 times a week. you will love this!!!

1. place ingredients in bread pan in order specified by your manual
2. use the white bread and light crust setting
3. press start
4. your dough should be slightly tacky to the touch and soft when you press down on it , like playdoe when you first open it
5. if too dry add warm milk 1 teaspoon at a time
6. if too wet add white flour 1 tablespoon at a time
demonstrations.review: This bread was wonderful! I made it for a pre-Christmas dinner with family and it was soft and fluffy and full of flavour - a welcome addition to any meal!

target.recipe_text:
cottage cheese jello

as our family expands each year with marriages, etc...we try to incorporate favorite dishes of the new in-laws to our holiday celebrations, so that they feel a part of our event and not an outsider.  this is a recipe my sister-in-law's grandmother always made and i am happy to add it to our collection.

1. combine cottage cheese and jello
2. add remaining ingredients
3. refrigerate until set
target.review: This has been at our family's thanksgiving since I can remember. It is as much tradition as the turkey and dressing.  My aunt always makes it with lime jello. One year she made it with a red jello (which is also very good) and lets just say she never did it again! lol! This is a light wonderful recipe. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican pizza like taco bells

this tastes exactly like taco bells mexican pizzas.

1. -using your hands , mix together beef , taco seasoning , and water
2. -brown the beef mixture in a skillet over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes , using a wooden spoon or spatula to break up the meat as it cooks
3. set aside
4. -in 375 degree oil , fry tortillas for 30-45 seconds per side , keeping as flat as possible and popping any bubbles that may form
5. drain on brown paper bags
6. -spread beans , then meat , then picante sauce / salsa over 4 of the tortillas
7. set aside
8. -spread cheese , then tomatoes , then onions over remaining tortillas
9. stack one of these tortillas on each of the others
10. -place pizzas under a hot broiler just until cheese has melted
11. i usually just brown the burger and add the beans in with it
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this. We left off the onions and added lettuce. We eat some kind of mexican dish every week. It was nice to add a different one that is a keeper. Thanks, Katie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
florida fruit smoothie

i love to drink these in the mornings. i'd rather drink this than eat in the mornings before i go to work, sometimes you're just not very hungry that early in the morning and this sticks with you through the day.

1. cut banana up into pieces into blender , or i have one of those smoothie machines
2. add yogurt
3. i use whatever yogurt is on sale that week , but usually use yoplait or the store brand
4. add frozen fruit , i like to use mixed kinds to get different flavors
5. use whatever kinds of fruits you like
6. it might take a few tries to get what you like
7. add juice
8. i usually use orange juice or the orange / peach / mango flavored variety
9. or i look in the mexican food aisle and buy guava and peach nectar for a different kick
10. i like this a lot better than those smoothies with milk or ice cream and think it's healthier too !
11. after blending and if it's too clumpy and thick add 2 or 3 more splashes of juice and blend some more till the consistency you want
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was really good. I used peaches for the frozen fruit. I liked this method and can't wait to try other fruit combinations. I did add some sweet and low because I like my smoothies sweet. The girls really enjoyed these too! thank you, Katie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
calypso cooler

yet another chili's recipe. this drink is really pretty, and very easy

1. fill a glass with ice and set aside
2. in a separate glass or shaker , ad the rum , schnapps and orange juice , shake or stir mixture
3. pour the rum mixture into the prepared glass filled with ice
4. float a splash of grenadine over the top
5. garnish with orange and cherry
6. sit back and sip up !
demonstrations.review: We don't do alcohol that often, but this had some of my favorites in it so we tried it and loved it. It was really good! Thank you, Katie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
catalina chicken breasts

this recipe came from kraft's "food and family" magazine.  the sauce is very thick, sweet and tangy.  if you like sweet and thick sauces on chicken breast, you'll like this.  (but honestly, i didn't care for it much!)

1. heat oil in skillet
2. add chicken and cook until browned , about 4 minutes on each side
3. mix dressing , soup mix , and jam in a separate bowl
4. put the chicken in a 3-qt
5. baking dish and pour the sauce on top
6. cook at 350 degrees for 45 minutes or until chicken is cooked through
demonstrations.review: My momma used to make this all the time when I was young.  This is what she served if we had company. It is a tangy and sweet chicken dish.  Now I get to make it for my girls.  We always had it with Greek noodles.  Thanks for the memories.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pepperoni pizza bites

this are terrific, and the kids can help too! they are bite sized pizza calzones.

1. for filling
2. combine cheeses , pepperoni and sauce , set aside
3. separate the biscuits
4. flatten to 3" circles
5. place one rounded tablespoon of filling in the center of each biscuit
6. bring edges of dough together , pinch edges of dough to seal
7. place , seam side down on greased baking sheet , brush with milk
8. sprinkle with parmesan cheese
9. bake in a 350 preheated oven for 12- 15 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: My kids loved this and so did the kids I make snack for at church. Will make many more times. Thanks for a great idea!!!

target.recipe_text:
grilled pineapple with nutella

this is another amazingly simple recipe from everyday italian. i love grilled fruit....it just makes the flavors of the fruit "pop." this isn't one of those "do ahead" deserts, it needs to be served as soon as it is prepared......but you can prep ahead by slicing the pineapple, and mixing up the mascarpone mixture and the nutella mixture, and having them ready. or, if your house is like mine, the kitchen is where everyone hangs out anyways...so put them to work mixing stuff while you grill the pineapple. would also be great dessert for a summer barbecue, since the pineapple could be grilled outside on the grill.

1. whisk the mascarpone cheese , vanilla and sugar till smooth and blended
2. set aside
3. combine the nutella with cream in a small saucepan , and stir constantly over low heat for about 5 minutes , till satiny smooth , and easy to pour
4. set aside
5. grill pineapple slices in a grill pan sprayed with pam over medium heat
6. grill slices about 3 minutes per side , so you get those nice"grill marks
7. "arrange the pineapple on a large platter or shallow serving dish
8. drizzle nutella over the pineapple
9. then snip the corner of the bag , and drizzle the mascarpone over the top
10. sprinkle the hazelnuts over the top , and serve immediately
target.review: I absolutely love this dessert.  It's perfectly sweet, and the pineapple tastes so nice when it's warm.  I've made this for my family, and they've all enjoyed it well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai style ground beef

a wonderful recipe from cooking light.  a delicious way to use ground beef.  you can make it spicier by using more red curry paste.

1. heat a large skillet over medium-high heat
2. coat pan with cooking spray
3. add leek
4. saut 5 minutes
5. add garlic
6. saut 1 minute
7. add beef
8. cook 7 minutes or until lightly browned , stirring to crumble
9. stir in curry paste and tomato sauce
10. cook until half of liquid evaporates
11. add milk and next 4 ingredients
12. cook 2 minutes or until slightly thickened
13. serve with the rice
demonstrations.review:
What a great way to use ground beef! So flavorful, and even though I ran out of red curry paste, I ended up using red garlic chili paste. It worked out perfectly and the BF said it tasted like Thai sloppy joes on rice :o).

Update:  I had to re-rate this at 5 stars--the hubby asks for it all the time, and I've made this more than I can count!  Even if I'm short on leeks, I can still pull everything else together--it's easy, fast and tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick sauteed mushrooms

adapted from a recipe by lanni (allrecipes). makes a wonderful side dish, especially for an italian meal. i think it would be wonderful as a burger topping.

1. melt butter with oil in a large skillet over medium heat
2. add balsamic vinegar , garlic , herbs , and mushrooms and saute for 20-30 minutes , or until tender
3. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Very nice and simple to prepare!  I used this as a side to some roasted chicken, and because I didn't realize that I was out of certain herbs, I ended up using Italian seasoning instead.  Thanks for this truly "quick" recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory zucchini

a simple side dish of zucchini and mushrooms. this is from "a hundred years of island cooking", and old cookbook from the hawaiian electric company.

1. wash zucchini
2. cut off ends
3. cut zucchini into lengthwise halves , then crosswise into 1 / 2-inch slices
4. in a large skillet , melt butter
5. saute mushrooms for 1 / 2 minute
6. add zucchini
7. saute 1 / 2 minute
8. stir in remaining ingredients and continue cooking on medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: I love recipes from that cookbook!  They seem to always put together a nice selection of recipes.  I really enjoyed this, and I think by cooking it for such a short amount of time, it kept the veggies in a nice cooked but fresh sort of state.  Thanks for posting, Chilicat!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rosy garlic sauteed cabbage

yum! if you like garlic and cabbage, this is for you! adapted from great good food cookbook.

1. in a large nonstick skillet , heat the oil over medium heat
2. add the garlic and saute for 3 minutes , stirring constantly
3. pour in 1 / 2 cup of chicken broth
4. stir , cover , and cook for 15 minutes
5. remove the cover and cook until all liquid has evaporated , stirring constantly as the last few tablespoons of liquid evaporates
6. stir in the cabbage
7. sprinkle with the remaining chicken broth , paprika , and pepper to taste
8. cook for 3-5 minutes or longer , until cabbage is wilted or to your liking , stirring constantly
9. move to a serving bowl and serve immediately
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: The calories are low, and the dish is simple and straightforward.  Like others, I seemed to have an abundance of cabbage, although I only used one head.  To even it all out, I just used a little extra chicken broth and all was well.  I can imagine that this would be easy to flavor differently, but was nice mild and garlicky as-is.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
iraqi cardamom cookies  hadgi badah

found this recipe while looking for an iraqi chicken and potatoes dish requested in the na/me forum.  (from chicken to cookies, yes my mind wanders.) saw this and thought it would be a great addition to 'zaar for all my cardamom loving friends.  the original recipe is from "the world of jewish cooking." posting for some future zwt.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. prepare baking sheets with a light coating of cooking spray , oil or butter
3. sift together the flour , cardamom , salt , and baking powder
4. using an electric mixer , beat the sugar and eggs until light and creamy
5. stir in the flour mixture , then the ground almonds
6. pinch off a small piece of dough and hand form into 1-inch balls , moistening your hands with rose water or orange blossom water , if desired
7. place on the prepared baking sheets and flatten slightly
8. press a whole almond into the center of each cookie
9. bake until lightly browned about 12 minutes
10. transfer to a wire rack and let cool
11. store in an airtight container at room temperature
demonstrations.review: I used this recipe as one of my Christmas cookies this year...the taste is SO good!  The hint of cardamom (and rose water) is perfect together.  Only thing, is this--my batter was quite runny, so I ended up adding another 1/2 cup of flour.  Also, I doubled the batch, and by no means are there 72 servings worth per batch.  Since they were a little on the runny side, I spooned them with an ice cream scoop and sprinkled a little bit of rose water on each.  Thanks for posting this tasty recipe--I'll definitely be making it again!

target.recipe_text:
cinnamon pumpkin empanadas   empanadas de calabazas

from esperanza's cafe (joe t. garcia's bakery), fort worth courtesy of texas monthly magazine.

1. for the filling: mix ingredients together and set aside
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees
3. combine water , sugar , salt , yeast , baking powder , and cinnamon
4. using an electric mixer , gradually blend in half of the flour
5. add shortening and thoroughly mix , then gradually blend in remaining flour
6. divide dough into 4 equal parts , then shape each of those parts into 4 dough balls
7. slap the dough balls between the palms of your well-floured hands until somewhat flattened , then roll out on a floured surface into circles approximately 4 inches in diameter and 1 / 8-inch thick
8. put about 1 1 / 2 tablespoons of pumpkin filling in the center of each circle , fold over , and seal edges by moistening slightly and pressing lightly with a fork on both sides
9. bake on a greased cookie sheet until golden brown , 18 to 20 minutes
target.review: No one had posted a picture of this recipe yet and I wondered why. Well, probably because they were gone as soon as they came out. I was quick to snap a photo before they were devoured! Very delicious. I added a couple of steps: 1.) The recipe did not indicate if the bread was suppose to rise (it had yeast) so I let it rise about 45 mins. 2.) I used pumpkin pie mix instead of the pumpkin filling because pumpkin pie mix already has most of the ingredients called for and tastes just as good. 3.) I brushed my empanadas with an egg wash before baking. This gave it a beautiful shine. Next time a will also try a pinnaple filling. Thanks for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panko coated chicken schnitzel with capers and lemon

chef thomas keller makes this at the french laundry restaurant.   it is the best schnitzel i have had and that includes in germany and austria.  the panko breadcrumbs really make this dish

1. set the flour , eggs and panko in three separate shallow bowls
2. season the chicken cutlets with salt and pepper
3. dredge the chicken in the flour , shaking off any excess , then dip in the eggs and coat thoroughly with the panko , pressing lightly to adhere
4. in each of 2 large skillets , heat 1 / 4 cup of the canola oil
5. add the chicken and cook over moderately high heat , turning once , until golden and crispy , about 3 minutes
6. transfer the chicken to a paper towel-lined baking sheet and sprinkle with salt
7. meanwhile , in a small saucepan , melt the butter and cook over moderately high heat until browned and nutty , about 4 minutes
8. stir in the capers , lemon juice and parsley
9. spoon over the chicken and serve
demonstrations.review: The crust on this was very good. I have never eaten capers before...until now. I think that the sauce really works well with the chicken. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
light pot roast

a tasty comfort meal provided by better homes and gardens: family favorites made lighter. this recipe recommends that you use half the meat for the meal, and chill the rest for sandwiches.

1. trim fat from roast
2. spray a dutch oven with cooking spray and preheat to medium
3. brown roast on all sides
4. drain fat
5. in a small bowl mix the 1 / 2 cup water , worcestershire sauce , bouillon granules , and basil
6. pour over the meat and bring to a boil
7. reduce heat , cover and simmer 1 hour
8. add potatoes , carrots , celery , and onion to the dutch oven
9. cover and simmer for another 45 to 60 minutes or until meat and vegetables are tender
10. add more water if needed
11. remove meat and vegetables to a platter and keep warm
12. pour the pan juices into a metal bowl and place the metal bowl in ice water to solidify the fat
13. skim off the fat
14. you need 1 cup of pan juices , so add water if necessary to make the full cup
15. whisk together the 1 / 4 cup water and flour until smooth
16. stir in the pan juices and return to the dutch oven
17. cook , stirring constantly , until thickened and bubbly
18. cook another minute and serve the gravy with the meat and veggies
demonstrations.review: Meat was very tender and tangy. Made it for my sister's family dinner (since she does not really cook) and they enjoyed it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted moroccan spiced chicken

i found this recipe online somewhere and i tried it and it was awesome!!  really easy and really good.  if you like spiced and flavorful food, this is a great recipe to try. 
a note to the cook: i always put the chicken in a pan with the juices and put it directly in oven.  you might have to cook it a few minutes longer, but it always comes out delicious.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. pat chicken dry and rub with flattened garlic cloves
3. place garlic in cavity
4. squeeze lemon into small bowl
5. place lemon in cavity
6. brush chicken with half of juice
7. mix spices and salt and rub over and inside chicken
8. tie legs together
9. heat oil in large ovenproof skillet
10. add chicken , breast side up
11. add remaining lemon juice to skillet
12. baste
13. chicken withpan juices
14. transfer to oven , and bake until juices run clear
15. baste occasionally
16. roast about 1 hour --
demonstrations.review: The spices were great on this chicken. I only had chicken legs so that is what I used and I roasted them in my cast iron skillet with new potatoes. When the chicken was done roasting, I placed my skillet back on the stove and I deglazed the pan with a little butter and lemon juice. This dish was wonderful! Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious cheesy baked potato   bacon soup

this is a delicious creamy thick soup. i make it quite often, it's a family favorite, i also add in some cayenne pepper, if you are not a lover of garlic you may omit--- it is so filling that i usually just serve it as a main meal with crusty bread on the side, and a salad.

1. in a large soup pot melt butter over medium-high heat
2. add in garlic
3. cook stirring for about 2 minutes
4. add in flour then stir until smooth
5. gradually add milk and half and half stirring constantly until thickened and smooth
6. add potatoes and onions
7. bring to a boil , stirring constantly
8. reduce heat
9. simmer for 10 minutes
10. add remaining ingredients
11. stir until cheese is melted
12. serve immediately
13. delicious !
demonstrations.review: it is a very thick hearty soup which my family enjoyed. It made alot of soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fish and chips bits

a traditional pub treat as an appetizer!  sprinkle with malt vinegar and salt for an authentic touch. when deep frying, the most important thing to monitor is the oil temperature. if you don't have a fryer with a thermostat, go to your local kitchen shop and purchase a good quality deep fry thermometer. from an old newspaper clipping.

1. preheat oven to 450f and lightly spritz a baking pan with baking spray
2. toss potatoes with 1 / 4 cup salad dressing
3. place in baking pan and bake for 25 minutes
4. preheat oil to 365f
5. combine flour , cornstarch , baking powder , 3 / 4 cup salad dressing and 1 / 4 cup water
6. dip fish into batter and fry a few pieces at a time in hot oil until golden , about 2 minutes
7. drain well on absorbent paper or paper towels
8. serve fish bits and french fries in miniature newspaper cones lined with waxed paper , for an authentic touch
demonstrations.review: My family liked this dish. The use of italian dressing is unique. The only thing is that I would probably decrease the amount of baking soda used becuase the taste is still present in the end result. I will preobably make again but with less baking soda. Thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
roasted brussels sprouts

i got this from the barefoot contessa cookbook. so good.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cut off the ends of the brussels sprouts and pull off any yellow outer leaves
3. mix them in a bowl with the olive oil , salt , and lemon-pepper seasoning
4. transfer them to a sheet pan and roast for 35 to 40 minutes , until crisp outside and tender inside
5. shake the pan from time to time to brown the brussels sprouts evenly
6. sprinkle with more kosher salt , if you like , and serve hot
target.review:
3 stars because while the basic recipe is great, this recipes calls for you to cook them waaaaaay tooooo loooong! These should be roasted at 450 for about 15-20 minutes, (preferably on an upper rack), stirred frequently, until they blacken. To the reviewer who said he/she can't imagine that blackened b. sprouts would taste good, oh, they do. They sooooo do! I hated b. sprouts until I tried these! My husband and kids even beg for them! Seriously, a 6 year old who says b. sprouts are his favorite?

To make this any time of year, cook directly from frozen. Just open the bag, throw the oil, salt and pepper right in the bag, toss and dump on the baking sheet. Just as good, if not better, because frozen veggies are frozen at their peak. Unless you get your sprouts from the farmer's market, they've probably been sitting around for a week or more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fluffy buckwheat pancakes

these are my favourites pancakes because they are delicious and healthy, fluffy and thick! if you wish you can use whole wheat flour adding some more liquid to the batter.

1. in a large bowl , sift together the flours , baking powder , salt and sugar
2. make a well in the center and pour in the milk , egg whites and melted butter
3. mix until smooth
4. heat a lightly oiled griddle or frying pan over medium high heat
5. pour or scoop the batter onto the griddle , using approximately 1 / 4 cup for each pancake
6. brown on both sides and serve hot with syrup or honey
7. it's possible to prepare batter the night before and refrigerate it covered overnight
demonstrations.review: Super great!  I make them about once a week and usually enough, (2 batches), to keep in the fridge and warm up for breakfast for several days.  I use 4oz. each, (by weight, a little extra), buckwheat and white whole wheat flour plus a little extra baking powder to increase the batch size.  Plus, one large egg, rather than 2 egg whites.  I've made the batter the night before, too, and though the pancakes come out just fine, the batter is really gummy and difficult to work with.  It's easier to just mix up the dry ingredients the night before and add in the wet in the morning.  I should probably just mix up a bunch at once and measure it out as needed....... :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beth s melt in your mouth barbecue ribs  oven

i almost didn't want to share this ribs recipe because this is one of the dishes that i make that keep my sons coming back home! these can be done with baby back or regular pork ribs. i have also made split chickens this way. the ribs are tender, moist and just slide off of the bone. i know that your family will love them just as much as my family does.
i noticed that some are unable to find hickory smoked salt. you can use smoked paprika or just brush the ribs with liquid smoke before applying the rub. the smoke flavor is nice because it helps give the ribs a cooked-on-the-grill flavor.
also, the easiest way to remove the membrane is to work a spoon, or i use the tips of my kitchen shears, into the bottom center of the membrane, work it back and forth to form a "pocket," then i slide my thumbs in and work the membrane off from the center outward to the ends.

1. preheat oven to 300 degrees f
2. line a baking sheet with two layers of foil , shiny side out
3. peel off tough membrane that covers the bony side of the ribs
4. season the ribs on both sides with salt and pepper
5. if using , divide the hickory liquid smoke evenly over the ribs
6. in a medium bowl , combine the light brown sugar , paprika , garlic powder and ground red pepper
7. apply the rub to all sides of the ribs
8. lay ribs on the prepared baking sheet , meaty side down
9. lay two layers of foil on top of ribs and roll and crimp edges tightly , edges facing up to seal
10. transfer to the oven and = bake for 2-2 1 / 2 hours or until meat is starting to shrink away from the ends of the bone
11. remove from oven
12. heat broiler
13. cut ribs into serving sized portions of 2 or 3 ribs
14. arrange on broiler pan , bony side up
15. brush on sauce
16. broil for 1 or 2 minutes until sauce is cooked on and bubbly
17. turn ribs over
18. repeat on other side
19. alternately , you can grill the ribs on your grill to cook on the sauce
demonstrations.review: Super easy and super good!  I used a prepared rub mixture because I was short on time.  With only 4 hours marinating, the meat was, indeed, falling off the bone, quite literally.  (Save for a couple of very thick, lean end pieces which, while falling apart, were a bit dry, something which probably could have been remedied with longer marination.)  We, too, finished them on the grill, with Trader Joe's Memphis BBQ sauce.  The ribs even outshone the blue crab!  Oh, an I used applewood smoked salt.  Yum.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
korean style short ribs  crock pot

i'm always looking for new recipes to make in my crock pot. here's another easy and tasty one. i finally got around to making this i used pork spare ribs. i cooked them longer till they were falling off the bone. the sauce has a very good flavor. my husband was pleasantly surprised at the flavor.i found this in family circle magazine.

1. blend soy sauce , sugar , oil , vinegar , ginger , garlic and red pepper in bowl
2. place ribs in 5 quart slow cooker , add sauce
3. cover , cook on high for 6 hours or low for 9 hours , until meat is tender
4. transfer ribs to a platter
5. skim and discard excess fat from liquid
6. combine cornstarch and 3 tablespoons water
7. blend with liquid in a saucepan
8. bring to a boil over high heat and cook for 2 minutes , stirring , until thickened
9. stir in carrots
10. top ribs with sauce , scallions and sesame seeds
11. serve over cooked rice
demonstrations.review: Really, really, really good and so very easy.  Hallmarks of an excellent recipe.  The meat is tender and flavorful  and the sauce rich.  To save some money, (and to make it a bit easier to eat), while preserving the flavor and mouthfeel, I use a chuck roast, sliced.  Then, I add some marrow bones to the pot.  Since short ribs are from the chuck end, anyway, the meat is similar in flavor and texture and the bones add the all-important flavor and gel to the sauce.  Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot  and cold thai  sesame noodle salad

got this off a 30 minute meal segment. i love the mix of flavors in this dish. this will last several days in the refrigerator. cook time is chilling time.

1. cook pasta to al dente , then cold shock it to stop the cooking process by running it under cold water in colander
2. drain the pasta very well
3. in the bottom of a large bowl , whisk together soy , peanut butter , vinegar , oil , sesame oil , and hot sauce
4. adjust to taste
5. add noodles and veggies and toss to combine the noodles and coat them evenly with sauce
6. sprinkle scallions and sesame seeds throughout the salad
7. tastes best if allowed to chill first
demonstrations.review: It was......eh.  "Sauce" was pasty.  Was awful as per the recipe.  Slightly improved with the addition of the brown sugar recommended by other reviewers.  Will most definitely not be making this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
finnish coffee bread  breadmaker recipe

finnish coffee bread for a 2 lb. breadmaker on dough setting, but can also be made in a 1 1/2 lb breadmaker. prep time includes rising time. recipe adapted from recipe printed on genealogia.org)

1. put all the ingredients in the bread machine on the dough setting , in the order specified for your machine
2. when the dough cycle completes , remove , divide in half and then split each part into 3 equal pieces
3. roll into long strands , and braid strands into 2 loaves
4. put loaves on greased cookie sheets
5. let rise until doubled in size
6. brush with second egg and sprinkle with sugar
7. bake at 375f for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown
8. immediately after taking them out of the oven , remove from pans
9. cool on racks
