demonstrations.review: Sooooooo goooooood.  It was actually the first bread I made in my bread maker and I have made it several times since then.  It did sorta fall once, but I think that was a breadmaker issue, not a recipe issue.  It was still delicious!  Try it with Nutella.  Yum.

target.recipe_text:
nestle toll house chocolate chip pan cookie

this recipe was in my paper recently and i made them for my co-workers. divine! i looked & looked and was surprised i couldn't find it already on zaar.

1. preheat oven to 375 grease a 15x10-inch jelly roll pan
2. combine flour , baking soda and salt in small bowl
3. beat butter , both sugars and vanilla in large mixer bowl
4. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each
5. gradually beat flour mixture into butter mixture
6. stir in chocolate chips and nuts
7. spread into prepared pan
8. bake 20-25 minutes or until golden brown
target.review:
Easy recipe, good cookies.  I doubled the servings and used 2 9x13 pans.  I had to bake a little longer than 25 mins because they were done on outer edges but middle wasn't.

Will make again.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: This was my first time ever making potato soup so I was a little nervous but this came out great.  My family is big eaters so I had to make a larger pot of soup.  I used 8 cups cubed potatoes, 6 cups of chicken broth, 2 chicken bullion cubes, generous amount of black pepper, 1 8 ounce pack cream cheese and half of another package(heated in microwave to soften first, helps with melting).  After potatoes were softened enough to mush, I added about 1 cup of shredded cheese and real bacon bits...not the crunchy ones.  This soup was great.  My teenage son swore he wouldn't like it but after tasting it he said "ok ok I LOVE IT, add it to my recipe book."  Thanks for great recipe.  Very easy for a new cook.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panini sandwiches

when i got my george foreman grill, i made up this recipe to be like the ones that i had bought. it has been a big hit with everyone.

1. start heating the grill
2. place 1 slice of mozzarella on each of 4 slices of bread
3. place 1 slice of provolone on each of the other 4 slices of bread
4. top the mozzarella with pepperoni , salami and pepperoncini
5. top the provolone with turkey , ham and cheddar
6. place the two halves of the sandwiches together
7. brush the top of the first sandwich with the melted butter
8. place the sandwich butter side down on the grill
9. brush the other side with melted butter
10. grill till bread is toasted and the cheese has melted
11. continue with the other sandwiches
12. a george foreman grill works great with these sandwiches but even a stove top grill would work
demonstrations.review:
Love this recipe. When I try something new, I can tell by the look on my hubby's face if it is a keeper.....he LOVED these. I didn't have a clue what pepperoncini peppers were so I used jalepeno peppers in some and banana peppers in the others. Both worked great. Thanks again for a great recipe :) Prissy

I do have one question I forgot to ask....Where do you get sour dough bread?  I couldn't find it anywhere in the bread section.  I used texas toast instead.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered pumpkin loaf

you'll love the surprise inside this delicious, smart-choice pumpkin bread: a creamy center.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease a nonstick 9x5-inch loaf pan
3. set aside
4. mix pumpkin , 1 cup granulated sugar , the brown sugar , 3 of the egg whites , milk and oil in large bowl
5. add flour , baking powder , pie spice and salt
6. stir just until moistened
7. set aside
8. beat neufchatel cheese , remaining 2 tablespoons granulated sugar and the remaining egg white with wire whisk until well blended
9. spoon half of the pumpkin batter into prepared pan
10. spoon neufchatel cheese mixture evenly over the batter
11. cover with remaining pumpkin batter
12. bake 1 hour to 1 hour 5 minute or until wooden toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
13. run knife or thin spatula around edges of pan to loosen bread
14. cool in pan on wire rack 10 minute
15. remove bread from pan to wire rack
16. cool completely
demonstrations.review:
I must have done something wrong even though I followed the recipe exactly.  The outer layer...the bread part tasted good but the center wasn't creamy at all.  It was clumpy and broke into pieces all over the place.  I will admit I am a somewhat inexperienced baker so could have been something I did wrong.  Doubt I will be making this again.

Thanks for submitting it, was worth a try for a pumpkin roll type dessert.

Prissy

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best twice baked potatoes

family favorite - tried and true - the only recipe we use.

1. microwave the potatoes until done
2. allow to cool a bit
3. slice about a 1" strip of the skin off the top of each potato
4. carefully scoop out the pulp , placing in a large bowl , and leaving potato shells intact
5. mash the potato pulp along with the margarine
6. add milk , sour cream , cheese , salt and pepper
7. combining well
8. spoon the mixture back into the potato shells , piling high
9. top with the crumbled bacon or bacon bits
10. bake at 400 for 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have made these before and somehow this time, the shells of potato wouldn't hold up so I mixed it all together...shells and all. So actually made twice baked MASHED potatoes. Family loves this. I have also made these with instant mashed potatoes. If you are pressed for time, its just as good and a lot easier.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortilla dip supreme

this recipe is very easy, and super delicious! this dish will definately disappear in a matter of minutes, everyone who tastes this dish, asks me for the recipe.

1. in a shallow baking dish , press cream cheese into botton , distributing evenly
2. spoon canned chili over this , top with cheese
3. place in a pre-heated 350 degree oven for 10-15 minutes or until cheese is bubbly
4. serve immediately with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review:
Awesome tasting and easy dish to make.  Instead of layering with cream cheese, I mixed the cream cheese and chili together, and added hot sauce for an extra kick.  A keeper!!!

Thanks for the great recipe.

Prissy

target.recipe_text:
momma s lemon berry bars

this was a lemon bar recipe i found in a church cookbook, but modified it a little to include raspberries and mulberries. it was a big hit with my family! you can use butter or margarine. if you don't have mulberries on hand just use all raspberries, or substitute other berries. the addition of the juice into the batter gives it a little added flavor.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a medium bowl mix crust ingredients
3. press into a jelly roll pan
4. bake crust at 350f for 12 minutes
5. in a large bowl combine sugar , flour , baking powder
6. mix well
7. to the flour mixture add eggs , lemon juice , and berry juice
8. mix well
9. gently fold in berries ,
10. pour the batter over the crust
11. bake in 350f oven for about 25 to 30 minutes just until the top begins to turn light golden
target.review:
This is a great recipe. I used only frozen blackberries and it turned out perfectly.
 I wasn't so sure about adding the juice to the filling as it turned an unappetizing color. The taste, however, changed my mind. Delicious!
To make it more beautiful :) I might experiment with adding more berries and more juice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rj s rice pudding

i think that i've come up with a great rice pudding recipe.  anyone who has tasted my rice pudding says so anyway.

1. combine the raisins and rice and place in a strainer
2. wash the raisin and rice mixture under hot tap water
3. in a pot with a tight fitting lid , bring 4 cups of water to a boil
4. add raw rice and raisins and stir
5. cover , reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes
6. meanwhile , in another pot combine the milk , sugar , egg yolks and corn starch
7. heat over medium high heat stirring mixture constantly to avoid burning until the mixture thickens to the consistency of thick cream
8. remove from heat , stir in the nutmeg and vanilla
9. in a large bowl , beat the egg whites until they are stiff enough for form peaks
10. then slowly whisk in the thickened milk mixture
11. when the rice and raisin mixture is cooked , stir into the creamy custard mixture
12. at this point , you can dish up the pudding in serving dishes and sprinkle lightly with cinnamon or , you can bake the pudding mixture in a 350f oven for about 45 minutes and then serve sprinkled lightly with cinnamon
demonstrations.review: Wow! Fluffy and yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chana dal curry  kerala style

can be used as a soup or a curry to be eaten with rice. my kids love this!
hing is asafoetida powder (the ingredient in bean-o). it can be found in asian and indian groceries

1. cook dal in 4 c of water until soft , adding more water as needed
2. drain and set aside
3. heat oil in another pan
4. saute cabbage and bell pepper over high heat , about 3 minutes
5. add ginger , jalapeno , hing , dry spices and tomato
6. saute until the oil separates from the ingredients in the pan
7. add 1 c of water and bring to a boil
8. add cooked dal and cook 10 minutes until gravy is thick
9. add the coconut milk and remove from heat
10. add lemon juice
11. serve with flat bread or rice
demonstrations.review: This is really yummy!  I only added half a can of coconut milk and skipped the hing.  It's really spicy, so I might do half the pepper next time. Thanks Jacqueline!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rainbow bean soup mix in a quart jar

this makes a great gift. i have made many welcome/gift baskets for my neighbors. when i give the gift, i add a can of crushed tomatoes and a package of soup crackers.

1. use a quart jar that has a wide mouth , but if you can't find one any quart jar will work
2. place each type of bean in jar in the order listed above
3. top with seasoning bag , gently flattened so it can be seen from all sides
4. place lid , decorate jar and attach recipe
5. put an expiration date: one year from time of assembly
6. directions to make rainbow bean soup:
7. remove seasoning packet from the jar and set to the side
8. rinse beans and place beans in large microwave-safe dish
9. cover with water 1" to 2" over top of beans
10. cover dish loosely with plastic wrap
11. microwave on high for 15 minutes , rotating after 7 minutes
12. drain and rinse beans very well
13. place in a large pot
14. add 8 cups water , one 15 ounce can crushed tomatoes and seasonings from packet
15. cover , bring to boil
16. lower heat , cover pan and simmer 1 1 / 2 hours or until beans are tender
17. stir occasionally
demonstrations.review: Very pretty presentation and easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kale chips

light and crunchy "chips" that are practically guilt free. found this recipe on radicalhealth.com.  i reduced the amount of salt called for in the original recipe thanks to some of the reviews.

1. cut kale into 2 to 3 inch pieces
2. mix vinegar , oil , and salt in a large bowl then add kale and mix by hand
3. try to get all the leaves covered
4. place on baking sheets and bake at 350 f until they are crispy
5. after about 20 minutes , if it looks like they are not sizzling a bit or getting a little crispy , turn up the heat to 400f
6. time for baking varies depending on the size of your chips and desired crispness
7. the outer edges cook quicker than the pieces from near the stem
demonstrations.review:
I was a little skeptical as I started this recipe but all the positive reviews intrigued me.
These are so interesting... and yummy.  I used balsamic vinager and about a tsp of salt. Still too salty.  Someone described these as having the texture of ashes- so light they fly away. True, but who knew ashes could be so tasty (not that I've ever eaten ashes...)!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera bread  black bean soup

this is my own version of panera bread's black bean soup. it tastes a lot like it, and i love it! use vegetable stock to make it vegetarian.

1. in a pot , combine the first six ingredients
2. simmer for 10 minutes
3. add half a can of beans , salt and cumin
4. cook for 5 minutes
5. puree soup
6. add the rest of the beans to the soup
7. combine the cornstarch with 1 1 / 2 tablespoons of water
8. add the lemon and the cornstarch to the soup
9. cook until thickened
demonstrations.review:
Yummy! I used dried black beans in this recipe instead of canned and it turned out great! I added less water in the veggies to account for the amount of water that the beans were soaking in. 
Thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
tortured chicken   beer can

i first saw these "tortured" chickens served at a bar-b-q. lined up on a serving platter, beer cans still in place! talk about a conversation starter!the dry rub sounds bizarre, but i guarantee the proportions blend into a delicious combination.

1. mix 4 dry ingredients together
2. use this rub inside and out of the cleaned , dry chicken
3. be generous
4. place 1 / 2 can of beer in center of roasting pan
5. position"bottom" of chicken over beer and slide chicken over the can of beer until the chicken is"sitting" upright in the pan
6. the fit will be snug and chicken will be secure
7. roast uncovered at 350 degrees for 1 hour
8. do not baste , do not turn pan
9. the beer will steam the chicken deliciously
10. when done , carefully remove can of beer from chicken and serve
11. chicken can also be carved while"sitting" on the beer can
12. i have"tortured" 2 or 3 chickens in the same roaster and did not have to adjust cooking time
13. this melt-in-your-mouth chicken will get rave reviews
target.review: Great easy chicken recipe. I made 2 chickens at the same time. One of the chickens refused to stand up, but turned out good because it cooked lying in the spilled beer. The chicken was tasty and moist.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey ginger grilled salmon

super easy, sweet and spicy!

1. in a large self-closing plastic bag , combine first six ingredients
2. mix well
3. place salmon in bag and seal tightly
4. turn bag gently to distribute marinade
5. refrigerate 15 minutes or up to 30 minutes for stronger flavor
6. turn bag occasionally
7. lightly grease grill rack
8. preheat grill to medium heat
9. remove salmon from marinade
10. reserve the marinade
11. grill 12-15 minutes per inch of thickness or until fish flakes easily with a fork
12. brush with reserved marinade up until the last 5 minutes of cooking time
13. discard leftover marinade
demonstrations.review: Good recipe. I marinated the salmon for 3 hours, and still felt like the end result was not overly flavorful. Served with rice and salad for a perfect dinner. Next time I might use fresh garlic and fresh ginger.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai coconut rice

creamy coconut combined with a little bite from red pepper flakes and ginger, create a delicious rice dish to accompany a wide range of entrees.

1. combine all ingredients in a saucepan , except the crystallized ginger and sliced almonds
2. stir well to combine
3. cook over medium high heat , stirring until mixture comes to a low boil
4. immediately reduce heat to low
5. cover and cook for about 18 minutes
6. fluff with a fork
7. the cover , and let sit for 5 more minutes
8. garnish the finished rice with the candied ginger and the sliced almonds
demonstrations.review: Great flavor, went really well with pineapple chicken (like apricot chicken but with pineapple preserves instead). Trying to be healthier, I used brown rice, the rice at the bottom of the pot got burned because of the longer cooking time. Next time I will make with white rice, and there will definitely be a next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bestest hamburger soup

i think this is our #1 all time family favorite and it's often requested for birthday dinners. it's the 'bestest' because my daughter described it as such when she was little.  this freezes well and i've added directions for that and for reheating.

1. in a large saucepan , brown meat , drain excess fat
2. add salt , pepper , oregano , basil , seasoned salt , and onion soup mix
3. stir in boiling water , tomato sauce , and soy sauce
4. cover and simmer for about 15 minutes
5. meanwhile , prepare celery , celery leaves , and carrots
6. then add to simmering mixture with split peas and continue to cook for 30 minutes
7. add macaroni and simmer for 30 minutes longer , adding more water if necessary and stirring occasionally
8. serve sprinkled with parmesan cheese over individual servings
9. to freeze: place soup in a rigid container and freeze
10. to reheat: remove from freezer and thaw
11. place soup in saucepan and heat , stirring , until hot
demonstrations.review: Very nice meal all in one, served it with cornbread.  I followed the recipe exactly. The reason why I am rating it 4 stars is because the split peas were under cooked, and the macaroni was over cooked. The overall flavor was delicious, will definitely make again, but will leave out the split peas next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked acorn squash with spicy maple syrup

nan

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. split the squash into thirds and remove the seeds
3. cut a slice off the bottom of each piece so that it sits evenly , skin-side down , in a 9 x 13-inch glass baking dish
4. in the hollow of each piece , place 1 teaspoon unsalted butter , 1 tablespoon maple syrup , cinnamon and nutmeg to taste
5. bake in the heated oven until fork tender , about 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Awesome and simple recipe. My husband loved it! I made exactly as directed. Will definitely be making this over and over again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek potatoes  oven roasted and delicious

these potatoes are a staple in our home. whether accompanying roast lamb or chicken, or just on their own, we have them a couple of times a week. they are delicious and the ones that get overly-brown in the pan and stick a bit are mine!  clean up is a little tricky with this recipe, unless you line your pans with foil, but i find that just filling the pan up with hot, sudsy water and forgetting for an hour (something i apparently have no problem doing ;-)) helps a lot.

1. preheat oven to 420f a reviewer has suggested spraying the baking pan with pam - that sounds like a great idea !
2. put all the ingredients into a baking pan large enough to hold them
3. season generously with sea salt and black pepper
4. make sure your hands are very clean and put them in the pan and give everything a toss to distribute
5. the garlic will drop into the water / oil solution but its flavour will permeate the potatoes , and this way , it won't burn
6. bake for 40 minutes
7. when a nice golden-brown crust has formed on the potatoes , give them a stir to bring the white underside up , season lightly with a bit more sea salt and pepper and just a light sprinkling of oregano
8. add 1 / 2 cup more water if pan appears to be getting dry , and pop back into oven to brown other side of potatoes
9. this will take about another 40 minutes
10. do not be afraid of overcooking the potatoes- they will be delicious
demonstrations.review: I was skeptical whether or not the water would cook off, and the potatoes would be crispy. But, it did to my suprise. They stuck to a sprayed pan terribly, which is part of the reason for my not perfect score. Also, I used 1 lemon and they tasted a little bit too lemony. I will make them again, but maybe tweak the recipe. They do not stay crisp if you don't serve them immeadiately out of the oven.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot apple crumb crisp

wanted to make something for dessert so i threw a few things together and came up with a simple apple crisp. you'll need just four basic ingredients to make this comforting dessert. started at 4:00 pm and had a warm dessert at 6:00 pm.  serve with whipped cream or al-a-mode.

1. place pie filling in large bowl
2. break up apples with a pastry blender / cutter
3. place half of cinnamon topping with apple filling and place in a 1-1 / 2 quart slow cooker
4. combine dry cake mix , 3 tablespoons of cinnamon topping and butter
5. sprinkle over filling
6. sprinkle with remaining cinnamon topping and walnuts if desired
7. cover and cook on low for 2-3 hours
8. serve in bowls
target.review: WOW - so easy and so good - the only thing I suggest is making sure you cook this in a 1.5 qt cooker - I used 1 quart and had to take some out - I should have followed directions but I thought it would be ok - I used pecans instead of walnuts as that is what I had on hand. Will make again! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers chicken and cheese casserole

this recipe came from a card that was handed out with my weekly weight watchers materials. it's comfort food for 6 points per serving.  note: substitute turkey for chicken if desired.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a large casserole , combine all ingredients , mixing well
3. bake , covered , 35-45 minutes
4. remove cover
5. bake 10-15 minutes longer
6. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: You can do so much with this casserole. I omitted the macaroni, used 1 can 98% fat free cream of chicken soup, 1 can 98% fat free cream of chicken & mushroom soup, 2% cheese and fat free milk. On one side, I added crushed butter crackers and sprayed them with spray butter for the kids. My whole family loved it. You could add fat free noodles, brown rice, broccoli...the possibilities are endless....Thanks for the recipe...I will use it often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oreo turkeys  thanksgiving snack

these are cute little turkeys made out of oreo cookies and candy pieces. they are even easy enough for young children to help make. gobble! gobble!

1. take 1 oreo apart
2. this will be the base
3. place the whole oreo on its side on the base , so that it sticks to white of the oreo
4. in front of the oreo on its side , place a malted-milk ball for the turkeys head
5. place candy corn , points down , in between the oreo cookie that is standing on it's side
6. use icing for eyes and waddle if you want
demonstrations.review: Madethese for my son's 3rd grade class at school for their Thanksgiving party - everyone loved them and of course they tasted good - they're OREOS!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon chicken

prep time depends on the thickness of your chicken breasts. my first preparation. gained a 

1. cook bacon in 12" skillet until crisp
2. crumble bacon and set aside
3. pour bacon grease out of skillet , but don't wash or wipe it
4. add butter and olive oil to the same skillet
5. cook chicken breasts in this mixture over medium heat , turning once , until chicken is done
6. place chicken in ungreased 12x8" baking dish
7. cook onion and garlic in drippings remaining in skillet until the onion is softened
8. stir in the pepper and cooked& crumbled bacon
9. spoon over chicken breasts and sprinkle with parsley and cheese
10. bake at 350 degrees for 10-15 minutes until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: My husband absolutely LOVES this recipe - he has raved to all his friends about it and asks often for me to make it. I think the cheddar cheese does make a difference, I grate the cheese myself and follow the recipe as given and it is perfect. Light up your spuse's taste buds and cook this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oriental mini meatloaves with honey garlic sauce

a yummy variation on traditional meatloaf. i have also made this mixture into meatballs as well.

1. meatloaves-combine all ingredients in a large bowl
2. mix lightly but throughly to blend
3. divide into 12 muffin cups
4. bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes
5. or remove from pan and serve with honey garlic sauce immediately
6. sauce-combine ingredients in a sauce pan
7. cook and stir on low heat until hot and bubbly
8. serve with rice or oriental noodles
demonstrations.review: My husband and 9 year old really liked these - thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pronto pups aka corn dogs

these are also known as corn dogs, but our school and church term for them are pronto pups. my family loves these friday nights, i can never seem to make enough for the kids!

1. combine cornmeal , flour , baking powder , salt , egg and sugar
2. add milk until batter has a pancake type consistency
3. dry off hot dogs with paper towels , coat with flour , and skewer through the center of the corndog
4. heat 2" deep oil to 370 degrees f
5. dip skewered hot dogs into batter mix and coat evenly
6. fry until golden brown about 2 1 / 2 minutes
7. let cool and drain on a paper towel
8. with left over batter drop like dumplings into the oil until golden brown and drain
9. serve with ketchup , mustard tarter sauce or a dressing of your choosing
demonstrations.review: My 2 boys (ages 7 & 9) are use to frozen corn dogs - I made these for them and needless to say, really liked them (bad for me as they do take longer than the microwave ones!) I didn't rate a 5 because I was hoping the batter would have more crunchy bits like I remember from going to a local ballpark but they were still delicious. Nice family Friday night meal! Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
basil walnut pesto

this is my favorite pesto recipe; rich but healthy due to 

1. place basil , olive oil , walnuts , garlic and salt in food processor
2. blend until thoroughly combined
3. add parmesan and butter and blend 5-10 seconds more
4. just before serving , add 2 tbsp of hot pasta water from cooked pasta
5. serve over pasta with bread and salad
target.review: I love pesto, but I don't usually keep pine nuts on hand, this was a perfect recipe I could make from what was already in the garden, pantry and fridge.  Even my picky kids liked this!  Loved it, Loved it, Loved it!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetable linguine

this is one of my favorite recipes from college.  even my meat-and-potatoes boyfriend likes this - he actually requests it for dinner.
don't be scared off by the number of ingredients and steps.  this really only takes a little longer then boiling the pasta.

1. steam the broccoli , zucchini , and asparagus until tender
2. cook the linguine according to package directions in plenty of boiling , salted water , and drain
3. while the linguine is cooking:
4. in a very large saucepan , saut the garlic and tomatoes in the olive oil for 2 minutes over medium heat
5. stir in the basil and mushrooms , and cook an additional 2 minutes
6. stir in parsley , salt and pepper to taste
7. add the butter and cook until melted
8. add the milk and cheese
9. blend well
10. raise the heat and let the mixture reduce by about one third
11. add the linguine and steamed vegetables
12. toss to combine
demonstrations.review: We really liked this pasta dish!  After making it, we now double, sometimes triple, the sauce, we have a family of four and the first time around there was not enough sauce for all of us. I now also add yellow summer squash to the vegetables.  This has earned it's spot in our normal dinner rotation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
won ton dough

nan

1. combine flour and salt and mound on pastry board
2. make an indentation in center of mound , add egg and mix with fingers
3. gradually add water to form dough
4. knead 10 minutes and form into a ball
5. cover with a dampened tea towel and let rest 20 minutes
6. roll out in several batches to desired thickness , in most cases as thinly as possible
7. cut in 4-inch squares or 3-inch rounds
8. dust dough pieces lightly with cornstarch , stack and cover with cloth to prevent drying out until ready to fill
9. yield: 1 pound , approximately 40 skins
10. regional cooking of china
demonstrations.review: I used these wraps for won tons and egg rolls and they were pretty well.  It took me a few trys to get them rolled out thin enough, the first few didn't turn out too well.  All in all they were good but in the future I'll probably just buy the premade wraps for conveniance sake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really deep dish pizza

bit like a pizza casserole but this has a crust so theoretically you could pick it up and eat it like regular pizza, but half of the toppings would probably slide off. the toppings listed are mostly suggestions try it this way or using your favorite toppings instead.

1. in a measuring cup or small bowl , dissolve sugar and yeast in water
2. combine flour , parmesan and salt in a large bowl and make a well in the center
3. pour yeast mixture and oil in well and stir into dry ingredients until dough forms
4. let rise 5 minutes
5. preheat oven to 350f
6. heat olive oil over medium heat , add hamburger , onions and garlic , season with chili powder and saut until onions are tender and meat is browned , about 10 minutes
7. grease a 9x12-inch cake pan , and press dough into pan
8. pour 1 / 2 of sauce onto dough , layer 1 / 2 of all remaining ingredients , top with remaining sauce , then layer on all remaining ingredients
9. bake at 350f for 20-25 minutes until the cheese is lightly browned
demonstrations.review: We have made this pizza five times in the last few weeks, it is excellent!  After the first time we made it we changed the toppings, we use italian sausage, pepperoni, olives and mushrooms and we are generous when we sprinkle on the fresh parmesan.  This is a new family favorite, thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free waffles

my husband, who is not gluten intolerant, and i have these every saturday morning. he likes these better than ones made with "real" flour! this recipe is easily halved or multiplied, as needed. these are also excellent to use as sandwich bread, sloppy joe open-face bread, (better if you omit the sugar and use regular milk instead of buttermilk); strawberry shortcake, etc. refrigerate any leftovers and warm about 15-20 seconds in microwave before filling with sandwich stuff.

1. mix all ingredients together with a whisk , and pour into waffle iron , in batches
2. add a bit more milk if too thick or a bit of rice flour if too runny
3. can be made without eggs , if necessary
4. just add a little more liquid to make up for them
demonstrations.review: We have dairy allergies at our house as well as gluten intolerance, so we used almond milk instead of buttermilk.   These waffles were amazing, there was not one left after my boys got to them!!  Yum, yum yum!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast casserole supreme

this is a wonderful almost do ahead breakfast. great for company or christmas morning.

1. melt margarine and place in the bottom of 9" by 13" baking pan
2. spread potatoes in bottom of the pan
3. sprinkle chopped vegetables over potatoes
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. sprinkle meat over potatoes and vegetables
6. pour beaten eggs over potatoes
7. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
8. remove from oven and sprinkle cheese evenly over top
9. bake another 5-10 minutes or until cheese is hot and bubbly
10. remove from oven and let set for approximately 5 minutes
11. cut into 2
12. 5"-3" squares and serve with a spatula
13. enjoy
demonstrations.review: So delicious!  I doubled the recipe in a huge baking dish and am freezing the rest in individual servings.  So excited to enjoy this dish for the next few weeks!

target.recipe_text:
stardust chocolate pancakes

these are just heavenly!

1. in a small bowl , combine milk , egg and butter
2. whisk until blended
3. in another bowl , combine flour , cocoa powder , sugar , baking soda and salt
4. mix well
5. add milk mixture
6. whisk just until dry ingredients are moistened
7. heat griddle over medium heat until hot
8. for each pancake , pour scant 1 / 4 cup batter into griddle
9. cook 1-2 minutes or until batter is set around edges
10. carefully turn over pancake
11. cook 1-2 minutes or until pancakes are cooked through
12. repeat with remaining batter
13. sprinkle pancakes with powdered sugar
14. serve warm with desired toppings
15. try using metal star shaped cookie cutters !
target.review: Love these pancakes. very tasty, I served them with raspberry preserves and whipped cream a very nice treat! Thanks Sharon for another great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy bran   flax muffins

lightly sweet and heart healthy.  uses oat bran and flax seeds which are high in omega-3 fatty acids.  this recipe is an adaptation of one we found on the university of virginia cancer center website.   this version adds heart healthy oat bran plus a few other yummy things like vanilla and orange peel.  diabetics could substitute the brown sugar for splenda & brown sugar mix.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. line muffin pan with paper liners or coat the muffin tins lightly with cooking spray
3. in a large bowl , combine dry ingredients and set aside
4. beat the applesauce , eggs , oil , brown sugar , vanilla and orange peel with a fork until well mixed
5. pour into dry ingredients and mix by hand being careful not to over mix
6. fold in nuts and dried fruit
7. spoon batter into muffin cups and if desired , sprinkle with a bit of oatmeal flakes
8. bake for 18-20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean
9. cool in the pan for 5 minutes before placing on a cooling rack
10. freezes well if placed in a zip lock bag
11. just microwave 15-30 seconds to reheat
demonstrations.review: Very good for you muffins. Love the texture of these. I ground the flax seed then measured a 1/4 cup. Also used canola oil. The orange zest gave it a nice fresh taste.  I got 11 nice sized muffins using a large scoop, baked up in 17 minutes. Thanks for sharing this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern baked spaghetti

this is an easy, yet very tasty spaghetti casserole, which reminds me of the spaghetti they used to serve us in elementary school. i loved their spaghetti! i normally only brought my lunch, but not on spaghetti day!

1. cook spaghetti per package direcions
2. combine milk and egg , mix well
3. combine drained spaghetti , milk and egg
4. mix well
5. pour spaghetti mixture into a buttered 9x13 inch casserole dish
6. brown ground beef with onion , bell pepper and garlic in a large skillet
7. drain
8. return drained meat back into the skillet and add seasonings
9. cook for 2 minutes
10. stir in tomato sauce and cook for 2 more minutes
11. spread meat mixture over spaghetti
12. sprinkle with cheese
13. bake at 425f for 10 minutes or until cheese melts and is bubbly
14. remove from oven and let stand for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Im going to add review number 123. If you havent tried this recipe, dont wait any longer My family loves this dish. Very good directions and wouldnt change a thing, its perfect for us. Love the blend of monterey jack and cheddar cheese. Served with a green salad and garlic bread recipe#132920

demonstrations.recipe_text:
big apple mojito

i was served a one of these delicious cocktails on our last visit to bonefish grill.  i thought it was so good that i would try recreating it for you! to make it super special, slide a little lime juice over the rim of your glass and dip into sugar!  i hope you will enjoy it!

1. crush mint leaves and lime juice in a tall glass
2. cover with simple syrup and fill glass with ice
3. add rum and lemon lime soda , stir well
4. add mint to garnish
demonstrations.review: *wow* I love this drink. Ive tried this with different kinds of mint leaves (apple,pineapple) very good. I used superfine sugar the 4 tsp is just right for me. I also used diet 7up. I used Bacardi big apple. Im not a rum drinker and I didnt even notice the taste of rum at all in this drink. Thanks Bev

demonstrations.recipe_text:
v b vodka water

a good friend on zaar thought it would be a great twist on my recipe #299834 with red ruby grapefruit vodka instead of mandarin.... then add simple syrup and some citrus..... turns out it's delicious. thanks "b" for the great idea ;) "throw some slices of fruit in it add some ice, shake your booty and your good to go!"

1. simple syrup:
2. bring water to a boil in a small saucepan
3. pour in sugar
4. stir until sugar is completely dissolved
5. remove saucepan from heat and allow contents to cool
6. refrigerate in a sealed container until ready for use
7. vodka water:
8. place ice cubes in an empty pitcher
9. squeeze juice of the orange , lime and lemon over the ice
10. cut peel into quarters and throw in the citrus -- it just gets better
11. add ruby red grapefruit vodka
12. fill with water , add 1 / 2 cup to 1 cup simple syrup and stir
13. pour into highball glasses with or without ice
demonstrations.review: I'm so thrilled to be the first to rate this recipe! I love absolut ruby red grapefruit vodka, so I knew I was going to love this drink. Love the orange, lime, lemon combination.  Be careful drinking these they tend to sneak up on you. I used a simiple syrup ratio of one cup sugar, one cup water and added one cup of simple syrup to the pitcher. Made this at my sisters appy night and was a *HUGE* hit. Thanks for sharing this recipe, one I know I will be making again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s vanilla buttermilk cupcakes

i adopted this recipe, which was originally submitted by mean chef. mean's original comment: "from sunset magazine"

1. beat butter and all the sugar on medium speed until well blended
2. add eggs and vanilla and beat on high speed until well blended
3. sift together flour , baking powder , and salt
4. with mixer on low speed , add one third of the flour mixture , followed by a third of the buttermilk repeat , alternating in thirds
5. when all the flour is incorporated beat mixture on medium speed just until well blended
6. fill paper-lined or buttered muffin cups about three-fourths full with batter
7. bake in a 350 oven until tops spring back when lightly touched in the center , 20 to 25 minutes
8. cool on racks 5 minutes
9. remove from pans
10. cool completely
11. decorate with your favorite frosting
demonstrations.review: Love these cupcakes. Not an overly sweet cupcake. I used clear vanilla and buttered the cupcake pans. Mine baked up in 18 minutes. I used recipe#80118 for the frosting. Made for "Share the love" muffin and cupcake challenge.

target.recipe_text:
apple bars

apples and oatmeal go so well together! (adopted recipe)

1. in a large bowl , mix together oats , flour , margarine , baking soda and brown sugar
2. blend well
3. spread half of the oats mixture in a greased 9 x 9-inch baking pan
4. press down firmly
5. in a separate bowl , combine apples , 2 t
6. margarine , sugar and cinnamon
7. spread over the oats mixture in the pan
8. cover with remaining oats mixture
9. bake at 375 f for 40-45 minutes
10. cut into bars
target.review: These are a pretty good option. I used a premade dessert product instead of the flour, and five spice blend in place of some of the cinnamon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini cobbler

if you don't tell it is zucchini, people will think it is apple...i promise!

1. in a large saucepan , over medium-low heat , cook and stir zucchini and lemon juice for 15-20 minutes or until zucchini is tender
2. add sugar , cinnamon and nutmeg
3. simmer one minute longer
4. remove from heat and set aside
5. for crust , combine flour and sugar in a bowl
6. cut in butter until mixture resembles course crumbs
7. stir 1 / 2 cup into zucchini mixture
8. press half of remaining crust mixture into a greased 15x10x1-inch baking pan
9. spread zucchini mixture over top
10. crumble remaining crust mixture over zucchini
11. sprinkle with cinnamon
12. bake at 375f for 35-40 minutes or until golden and bubbly
13. top with ice cream or whipped cream to serve , if desired
demonstrations.review:
Good enough to fool the taste buds. I used five spice blend and cucumbers. 
Recipe does not say to drain excess liquid-I did. It was still soupy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled chicken satay salad

a nice combination of chicken satay and salad. perfect for summer! posted for 'zaar world tour ii.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. arrange tortilla strips in single layer on ungreased cookie sheet
3. bake 7 to 11 minutes or until lightly browned
4. meanwhile , make peanut satay dressing
5. beat vinegar , peanut butter , peanuts , sugar , oils , soy sauce , ginger , and garlic in small bowl with whisk until smooth and creamy
6. place chicken in resealable plastic bag
7. add 3 tablespoons dressing
8. seal bag
9. turn to coat
10. refrigerate 1 to 2 hours
11. refrigerate remaining dressing
12. brush grill rack with oil
13. grill chicken covered , 10-15 minutes until juice is no longer pink
14. cut chicken into strips
15. toss remaining salad ingredients in large bowl
16. toss with chicken and remaining dressing
17. divide salad among 6 plates
18. sprinkle with tortilla strips
demonstrations.review: Nice way to use a tortilla. I'll be doing that again. Sounds cheaper and healthier than ramen, though I haven't done the math.. I made my own dressing and veg substitutions.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut buttery chewy gooey brownies

pb & chocolate - best combo ever, perfect for cravings and crappy days. this recipe is vegan friendly - and does not come out cakey (my pet peeve about vegan brownies).

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a large bowl , beat first 5 ingredients
3. stir in egg replacer and oil until combined
4. in a separate bowl , mix dry ingredients
5. add the dry mixture to the liquid , stirring only until combined
6. add chocolate chips / chunks
7. spread in a 9x13 dish
8. bake for 20-30 minutes (bake time varies depending on how chewy / cooked you want your brownies
demonstrations.review: I didn't add oil, but used more peanut butter and bananas. I also used  chocolate cookie crumbs instead of the chocolate chips and cocoa. I think cookies made with the amounts listed in the same pan size as the recipe specifies must be very thin. I used a 7x11 pan instead.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fruit   nut bread pudding

serve this warm with some vanilla ice cream or whipped cream - yum! (prep time includes chill time)

1. combine bread& sugar in a large bowl
2. in another large bowl , beat eggs , milk , cinnamon , salt& vanilla until foamy
3. pour over bread& sugar
4. mix well
5. cover& refrigerate 2 hours
6. preheat oven to 350f
7. grease a 13x9 baking pan
8. stir in remaining ingredients
9. pour into prepared pan
10. bake 45-50 minutes or until firm
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good as written. Will make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian pumpkin strata

got this from a carnation evaporated milk can. i have adapted slightly for my family's taste. one of my favorite fall meals.

1. in a large skillet , cook sausage , onion , peppers , and garlic in oil
2. crumble sausage into pieces
3. cook until sausage is no longer pink
4. drain
5. combine bread , cheese , and sausage mixture in a large bowl
6. mix together milk , pumpkin , eggs , salt , pepper , and seasonings
7. pour over bread mixture and stir gently until bread is moistened
8. pour into a greased 13x9 inch baking dish
9. bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes or until set
10. serve warm
demonstrations.review: This is one of my go to recipes. This time I used regular sausage, canned spinach, cheese bread, and rehydrated home-dried cottage cheese instead of milk, etc. I hadn't made it for a while, and could not find it in my recipe box or in the main collection. I contacted the site for help-got nothing. I actually knew all of the main ingredients, but used winter squash as my key words instead of pumpkin. Well, pumpkin is a winter squash, for those who don't know. Other types of winter squash even processed and sold as canned pumpkin, varieties are so similar.

target.recipe_text:
cheeseburger chowder from  cooking live

this thick and hearty chowder comes from sara moulton's old food network show "cooking live." perfect fare for a cold winter night!

1. in a saute pan brown the ground beef
2. drain and set aside
3. in same saute pan saute onion in 1 tablespoon butter until tender
4. add garlic , carrots , basil and parsley
5. saute about 3 minutes
6. add broth and beef and potatoes
7. bring to a boil
8. reduce heat and cover , simmer for 15 to 20 minutes or until carrots and potatoes are tender
9. meanwhile melt remaining butter in a small skillet
10. add flour and cook , stirring for 3 to 5 minutes
11. gradually add evaporated milk , stirring constantly , cooking and stirring for 6 to 8 minutes
12. gradually stir the sauce into the soup
13. bring to a boil and cook for 2 minutes
14. reduce heat to low
15. add cheese , salt and pepper
16. continue to stir until cheese melts
17. remove from heat and blend in sour cream
18. garnish each serving with chopped fresh tomatoes and dill pickle slices
target.review: I substituted a half cup of grated cheddar and used only 1 cup of processed cheese. Still a good soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no peek casserole

my mom gave me this when we hunted. it's the best winter comfort food! and it's soooo easy.

1. combine all ingredients well in 2 qt
2. casserole
3. cover& bake@ 300 for 3 hours
4. do not peek until done
5. serve over rice or noodles
demonstrations.review: Good way to use meat you don't really want. Tastes excellent with beef.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna fish junk

a great quick casserole that's real tasty and serves well over rice (my favorite), bread, noodles, etc.  also great for storing and reheating in the microwave - mix the rice throughout and add some water for best reheating results.

1. saut onion and celery in butter
2. remove from heat
3. blend in bisquick and salt
4. add milk
5. cook and stir until thick
6. blend in tuna and heat through
demonstrations.review: Reminds me of the creamed tuna of my youth, only a little lighter. I added frozen peas, just because I could.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy tomato soup with rice

this is a soup my mother used to make for me when i was a little girl and came home from school.

1. heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a small saucepan and brown flour , stirring constantly
2. slowly add the hot milk and bring almost to boiling , stirring constantly
3. turn off the heat and let it stand
4. in a 4-quart pot , heat 1 tablespoon of oil and saut onion , celery , carrot and garlic
5. add tomatoes and liquid and spices
6. add 2 cups water and bring to a boil
7. simmer covered 15-20 minutes and remove bay leaf
8. blend half of the soup at a time in a blender
9. return to the pot
10. add rice and boiled you can garnish each bowl with a little fresh dill
demonstrations.review: Basically taseteless.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork steak

my husband loves this pork steak. it is fork tender, tasty & easy to make.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat
3. brown steaks on each side
4. while browning , season steaks with salt , pepper , and garlic powder
5. transfer steaks to a 9x13 inch casserole dish
6. saut the onions and mushrooms in the same skillet
7. add water , worcestershire sauce , dry soup mix , and mushroom soup
8. mix together until sauce forms
9. pour sauce over steaks
10. cover dish with aluminum foil
11. bake in preheated oven for 90 minutes
demonstrations.review: Scaled this back to 2 servings, which doesn't always work. Pork was still excellent.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dana s sloppy joes

my daughter hates sloppy joes, i got her to try these and now this is the only kind she will eat.

1. in a large skillet , brown beef with onions
2. mix the rest of the ingredients together
3. add to beef and onions
4. cook for 1 hour over medium heat , stirring occasionally
5. serve on warm hamburger buns
demonstrations.review: For my family had to eliminate the vinegar.

target.recipe_text:
zucchini they will eat

quick and easy- hot and cheesy! seasonings, bacon and two cheeses make this a really yummy side that is sure to please the pickiest people! southern women will add bacon and cheese to any healthy veggie!

1. fry bacon until crisp and drain on paper towel
2. drain grease from pan leaving just a light coating
3. slice zucchini and add to pan
4. add basil , salt and pepper and sautee until crisp tender - or softer if you like
5. add onion , bacon and cheeses and heat just until cheese to begin to melt
6. if you like you can put it under the broiler for a few minutes to brown the cheese
7. serve~
target.review: I had 2 zucchini sitting in the crisper and waswondering what to do with them when I saw bluemoon downunder's review.  I cannot believe how easy and delicious this version is!  Thank you. I'll be making it this way many more times....Lee

demonstrations.recipe_text:
huzarensla  dutch meat and potato salad

this traditional dutch recipe is definitely a meal. we love it. the prep time does not include the chill time.

1. mix all the ingredients together
2. refrigerate for a couple of hours for best flavor
3. spread on a platter lined with lettuce leaves and smooth the top
4. decorate top and sides with dollops of mayonnaise , sliced hard boiled egg , sliced tomato , parsley and a dusting of paprika
5. serve with your favorite bread
demonstrations.review: I made 1//2 the recipe b/c I'm alone and the whole thing would be too much.  I used canned beets, more convenient for me. I was a bit sceptical about the beets, but it really turned out very nicely.  They gave a different texture and taste to the whole thing, and I like it! Didn't have pickled onions so used green onions.  Lee

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb waffles

so fast and easy for the low-carb dieter! this recipe comes from the south beach diet book that i have tweeked to our personal taste. you'll never miss the old waffle mix ever again!

1. process all ingredients in blender until smooth
2. heat waffle iron and spray with non-stick spray
3. pour desired amount on waffle iron
4. leave on longer for extra crispy waffle
demonstrations.review: When a serving of something has more than 10 Net Carbs, it is definitely NOT low carb!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
valentine cutouts

these are a fun gelatin treat that the kids and adults will enjoy.they can be a finger food for the little ones. you can use different shape and use for any holiday. time does not include chilling

1. in a bowl , dissolve gelatin in water
2. set aside for 30 minutes
3. in a small bowl , whisk milk and pudding mix until smooth , about 1 minute
4. quickly pour into gelatin
5. whisk until well blended
6. pour into an oiled 13x9x2 in dish
7. chill till set
8. cut into cubes or use a heart shaped cookie cutter
demonstrations.review: Just a suggestion. I line my pan with Saran wrap. The when it is gelled I can remove the whole thing from the pan and make my cutouts.  HTH

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy broccoli tomato cheese soup

this is an easy soup to make.  the tomatoes give it more of a "zing" than other broccoli soups.  i usually don't puree it completely smooth, but some prefer it that way.

1. place onion , broccoli , tomatoes , broth , pepper , and curry powder in a large soup pot
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat slightly and cook until broccoli is very tender
4. about 12-15 minutes
5. puree , using an immersion blender / blender / food processor , until desired consistency
6. return to soup pot over med-low heat and stir in milk and cheese
7. stir and cook until heated through and cheese is melted
8. add salt if needed , to taste
9. serve
demonstrations.review:
I made this soup since winter seems to have come back to New England!
It was great...but let me say I did change a bit. 1st)I added only enough broth to cover the ingredients after adding the tomatoes. I like thickish soups. 2nd) I used 1 cup heavy cream, yummy. I'm on low carb so no problem there. 3rd) I used extra sharp cheddar, and made sure it was finely grated, no curdle effect. 
No salt was needed. The soup had a wonderful full bodied flavor and was very satisfying. Thank you very much, I shall make this again. Though I have enough to freeze some!  Lee

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cabbage beef bake

low cal. 
can serve with cooked white rice or mashed potatoes and biscuits.

1. chop cabbage
2. brown ground beef and onion in skillet on medium heat
3. drain
4. season with salt and pepper to your liking
5. cover bottom of greased medium size casserole dish with half the cabbage
6. add beef and onion
7. put remaining cabbage on top of beef layer
8. mix tomato soup and water
9. pour over beef / cabbage mixture
10. cover and bake @ 375 for about one hour
demonstrations.review: This is basically a cabbage roll casserole.  All you need to do is add cooked rice to the beef and onion mix.

target.recipe_text:
beef patties in onion gravy

good 

1. combine all patty ingredients
2. mix thouroughly with your hands and shape into 4 patties
3. spray a non-stick skillet , and brown patties on both sides
4. add dry onion soup mix and 1 1 / 2 cup water
5. cover pan tightly and simmer for 20 minutes
6. remove patties to a plate
7. in a gravy shaker or jar , combine 1 / 2 cup water with 2 tbs
8. flour
9. stir flour and water into onion gravy
10. stir constantly with a whisk until it comes to a boil
11. boil 1 minute
12. return patties to pan
13. serve with mashed potatoes or hot cooked noodles
target.review: Wow, this was such a great meal. Very easy to throw together and tasted so comforting and home-y. I added some sauteed onions and served with white rice. The only change I would make next time is doubling the gravy -- it was so good, we could have definitely used more! I have one patty left for lunch tomorrow that I'm already looking forward to. This one is definitely going into the 'keep forever and make once a week' drawer. THANKS!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome baked pork chops

these chops remain moist and tender, and the sauce is to die for! you probably have all the ingredients in your kitchen to make this! serve these chops over rice!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. rinse pork chops , pat dry , and season with garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste
3. place the beaten eggs in a small bowl
4. dredge the pork chops lightly in flour , dip in the egg , and coat liberally with bread crumbs
5. heat the oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat
6. fry the pork chops 5 minutes per side , or until the breading appears well browned
7. transfer the chops to a 9 x 13 baking dish , and cover with foil
8. bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour
9. while baking , combine the cream of mushroom soup , milk and white wine in a medium bowl
10. after the pork chops have baked for an hour , cover them with the soup mixture
11. replace foil , and bake for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: my husband made these pork chops for dinner tonight and they were pretty good. he used very thin pork chops so we didn't need to bake them in the oven for every long (frying on the stovetop was sufficient). the breading was very flavorful but i wish it had been a little crispier. it got a little soggy after towards the end of the cooking. we really enjoyed the sauce -- it was creamy and slightly sweet (maybe b/c we used a riesling wine). served with grilled asparagus and brown risotto rice -- yum! thanks for a quick, easy and yummy dinner idea. we'll be adding this into our regular rotation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chili you will ever taste

this is the best chili recipe i have ever tried. i'm not sure where the recipe originated, but it is amazing! sometimes, i don't bother adding all four cans of the kidney beans and it still turns out wonderful. once anyone tastes this chili, they will be begging for the recipe!! enjoy!

1. heat oil
2. cook onions , garlic and meat until brown
3. add tomatoes , beer , coffee , tomato paste and beef broth
4. add spices stir in 2 cans of kidney beans and peppers
5. reduce heat and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
6. add 2 remaining cans of kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is the first time I made chili, and it came out fantastic. I halved the recipe and used ground turkey to make it healthier. I also followed the suggestions of other reviewers and reduced the brown sugar to 1 TB. I used 3 heaping TBs of chili powder because I didn't have any chili sauce and added about 5 dried chili peppers, including seeds (we're big fans of spicy). So yummy and spicy, and surprisingly easy to  make. I'm adding this to the permanent recipe collection. THANKS!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese cabbage salad   coleslaw

an asian twist to cole slaw!

1. chop cabbage in medium pieces , garlic , ginger , green onions , carrot and red pepper
2. brown noodles , sunflower seeds , sesame seeds , & almonds in butter
3. boil sugar , oil , sesame oil , vinegar , and soy sauce , cool completely
4. i`ve also skipped the boiling and just mixed with no problem !
5. toss everything together just before serving
6. doesn't stay crunchy if kept overnight !
demonstrations.review: Very refreshing and simple salad. I decreased the amount of oil used to 1/4 C of olive oil and 1 TB sesame oil (I think next time I will increase amount of sesame oil), and used apple cider vinegar instead of rice wine vinegar. I also skipped the browning step, as I wanted to save some calories and fat. I think next time I will add some grilled chicken to turn this into a main meal. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stir fry chicken with garlic sauce

nice and simple. prep time includes marinating time.

1. combine garlic , soy sauce , water , honey , 1 tablespoon oil , cornstarch and black / red pepper
2. stir chicken into marinade and mix to coat
3. cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours , stirring once to twice
4. in large skillet , heat remaining oil
5. using slotted spoon , transfer chicken to skillet
6. stir-fry about 5 minutes
7. add reserved marinade
8. continue to cook and stir about 30 seconds until thickened
9. remove to platter
10. garnish with green onion
11. serve with snow peas , if desired
demonstrations.review: Very easy and tasty stir-fry recipe! We used more garlic (about 5 cloves total), 1/3 cup soy sauce, less honey, 1/2 jalepeno and a lot more crushed red pepper flakes to give it more spiciness and flavor. I also added a lot of veggies (onion, bell pepper and mushrooms). Very versatile recipe so it's easy to modify it with additional meats or veggies. We'll be making this regularly. Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hawaiian chicken   white rice    made simple

this recipe is simple, delicious and can be prepared and cooked in one hour. it looks as if you spent the day in the kitchen cooking (at least my husband always thought so). i found this recipe in an american heart association cookbook back in the '70's.

1. skin , bone , and flour chicken breasts and place in covered casserole dish
2. mix together the soy sauce , sugar and all of the juice from the can of pineapple
3. pour liquid over chicken breasts and sprinkle the parsley on top
4. bake covered in a 350 degree oven for 45 minutes
5. add the pineapple chunks and continue cooking for an additional 15 minutes
6. prepare the white rice during the last 15 minutes the casserole is cooking
7. serve the chicken over the rice , also place fresh parsley sprigs on the plate
8. i usually make string beans to serve with this dish
demonstrations.review: This recipe is made regularly in our household! It generally takes me less than 10 minutes to throw everything into the oven. I usually add an onion and a few cloves of garlic to kick it up a bit. The chicken breast is extremely moist and the sauce is so flavorful! Thanks for sharing such a quick, delicious recipe!!

target.recipe_text:
emeril s spiced nuts

recipe courtesy emeril lagasse, 2003 10 minutes on the prep time is inactive.

1. mix spices and reserve
2. heat nuts in a dry skillet and cook , stirring frequently , until begin to toast , about 4 minutes
3. transfer to a small bowl and set aside
4. add the butter , sugar , water and spices to the hot skillet and cook , stirring , until a glaze forms , about 1 minute
5. return the nuts to the skillet and toss to combine with the glaze
6. cook for about 1 to 2 minutes , or until the nuts are glazed and golden brown
7. remove from the heat and transfer to a baking sheet lined with aluminum foil , separating with a fork
8. let rest until cooled and the sugar has hardened , about 10 minutes
9. store in an airtight container
target.review: I have been looking for a simple spiced nut recipe and have found the perfect one.  Not to sweet or spicy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
split pea soup    best pea soup ever

this recipe was developed by my partner, dean ramsey and everyone just raves about it, because it's the best pea soup you have ever tasted!

1. place all ingredients into a large stew pot
2. cover ingredients with water about 2 inches above the top of the ingredients
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for about 3 hours , or until peas are pureed and slightly thickened
5. serve with a crusty bread if desired
demonstrations.review: After the potluck at church for Easter there were ham bones and ham leftover and it was my job to come up with ways to use them.  My Pastor requested Split Pea soup and being I can stand the stuff I went in search for a recipe.  I title sold me on it and it didn't fail to be the Best Pea Soup.  In fact because the Sunday I chose to make it my pastor desided to do a continental breakfast during service I left him a cool whip container full and he informed my husband it wasn't enough to please him, he could have ate the whole pan alone.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon breakfast muffins

these are delicious muffins that are perfect for breakfast, brunch, or to serve with soup or salad.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a small skillet , cook green onions in butter until soft
3. remove from heat and set aside
4. in a small bowl , mix together flour , baking powder , salt , and sugar
5. set aside
6. in a medium bowl , beat eggs together with milk
7. add in bacon , cheese , and green onions / butter
8. stir dry ingredients into egg mixture
9. spoon mixture into prepared muffin cups
10. fill cups about 3 / 4 full
11. bake 25-27 minutes
demonstrations.review: Made these for a camp breakfast at family camp.  Some were sceptical but they ate all of them. Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best homemade mac n cheese ever

updated 9/27/12 with additional notes i've learned over time. this is a personal recipe based on traditional bechamel-based mac-n-cheese. super creamy and flavorful. i like mine in the microwave, but also tastes great in the oven. for my own taste, i like 1  1/2 cups sharp cheddar, 1 cup mild cheddar, and 1/2 cup italian blend. re: comment about "kicked up white sauce", not using enough cheese or only mild cheeses would certainly taste more like a white sauce, but that is why i have written the recipe to taste. there are so many combinations to try :)  please feel free to use your favorite cheese(s) and plenty of it! 3 cups is just what works for me.

1. boil macaroni according to package directions
2. cheese sauce
3. melt butter in saucepan over low heat
4. add flour gradually while whisking and cook for 1 minute , still whisking
5. add a small amount of milk to start the sauce then add all the spices
6. keep on whisking while adding the rest of the milk
7. turn up the heat to high or medium high depending on your stove , just be careful not to scorch the sauce
8. the more you whisk , the creamier the sauce will be
9. as sauce approaches a boil , begin to whisk in cheese one handful at a time , ensuring all cheese is melted before adding another
10. take off the heat and whisk vigorously one last time
11. pour over cooked macaroni in 13x9 pan and stir together
12. the last 1 / 2 cup of sauce may be too much depending on type and amount of pasta
13. sprinkle additional cheese over the top if desired
14. microwave on 70% power for 15:00 minutes or until set
15. if you prefer baking , it comes out well at 350 after about 30-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: I took this to the church potluck today.  I tripled the recipe and did not come home with a drop left.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef   fresh vegetable noodle bowls

i love this dish!  it's light, healthy and very easy to prepare!  i got this off the kraftfoods website.  i usually omit the tomato.  enjoy!

1. mix soy sauce and dressing in a measuring cup
2. in a large skillet heat olive oil , then add steak , garlic , snow peas , bell pepper and onions
3. stir fry for 3 minutes or until steak is cooked and veggies are crisp-tender
4. add soy sauce mixture and stir fry 3 more minutes
5. add tomato and parsley
6. serve in bowls over hot cooked pasta
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner last night and it was great.  I don't like all my veggies cooked and my son won't eat most veggies, and my husband loves stir-fry so finding a recipie that all three of us will enjoy can be difficult.  I made this and just before adding the tomatoes pulled out my son and my portions.  I will make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple  orange  and yogurt delight

i make these the night before for my husband and i to grab and go the next day.  the acid in the mandarin oranges keeps the apples from turning brown.  sometimes, i'll add half a banana to each one for more fruit.  i either use nonfat vanilla yogurt or plain nonfat greek yogurt with a little vanilla extract mixed in. and i don't peel the apples for the extra fiber. it's so simple to make....if you can cut up fruit, then you can have this simple recipe!

1. mix the partially drained mandarin oranges and the chunked apple together
2. here is where you can add half a banana too
3. if you like more juice , spoon some of the reserved juice into the mixture to make sure the apple is coated
4. this acid stops the apple from turning brown overnight
5. divide the fruit mixture into 2 containers
6. top each container with 1 / 2 cup of vanilla yogurt
7. if you are going to enjoy this the next day , cover at this step and put in the fridge
8. top one container with 1 / 4 cup wheat germ and 1 teaspoon of honey before enjoying !
demonstrations.review: Made these for a Father's Day potluck/breakfast at church today.  They were great.  The acid in the oranges really does keep the apples from turning brown.  I topped mine with granola and honey (no wheat germ).

target.recipe_text:
perfect chocolate brownies

this is the best brownie recipe i've ever used and i've used several!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 9x13" pan
3. melt shortening in a large saucepan over low heat , then stir in cocoa
4. remove from heat
5. mix in sugar and vanilla then mix in eggs one at a time
6. stir in remaining ingredients then stir in nuts
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. cool completely , before cutting into 2x2" squares
9. i have read all the great reviews and learned from them , thank you all
10. now i line my pan with buttered alumunin foil or parchment paper
11. this works very well
target.review: Easy to make and absolutely delicious!! I made mine with 1/2 cup of white choc. chips and 1/2 cup of chopped almonds instead of the walnuts. Will definitely be making these again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon squares

simple, yummy bar cookies filled with cinnamon-goodness! the heavenly scent they create while baking is a tantalizing prelude to their delicious taste!

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees
2. grease and flour a 15 1 / 2 x 10 1 / 2 x 1-inch pan
3. cream the butter , margarine , and sugar
4. add the egg yolk and dry ingredients
5. press the batter into prepared pan
6. beat the egg white until foamy and spread sparingly over batter
7. press on the nuts
8. bake at 325 degrees for 30 minutes
9. cut into squares
demonstrations.review: I agree with Merlot - I counldn't wait to try these and I was definitely not disappointed. I used 1 cup of finely ground almonds too. I would reduce the amount of cinammon slightly next time. The apple idea sounds great - I'll try that too

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4 ingredient sweet and spicy chicken wings

these are a great alternative to hot wings, which are not very family friendly :) with only 4 ingredients and even less steps, these are super easy and delicious.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. place wings in a greased 9 x 13 baking dish
3. combine sauces and honey and pour over the wings
4. bake for about an hour , or until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Wow! I've been encouraging my 14 year old son to cook supper from time to time and this was the perfect recipe, easy and delicious. The whole family raved about the taste. We used chicken wings and marinated them overnight before baking. Looking forward to trying this with chicken legs or thighs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate dipped shortbread cookies

these are an elegant addition to a christmas cookie plate.

1. cream butter and sugar , add flour and vanilla
2. pinch of 1 / 2" balls of dough , roll in sugar and place on cookie sheet
3. use the tines of a fork to flatten cookies
4. bake at 350f for 12-15 minutes
5. remove from baking sheet , cool 10-15 minutes
6. dip half of each cookie into melted chocolate
7. chill to set chocolate
demonstrations.review: Very easy to make and even better to eat. The first time I made them, I didn't even dip them in the chocolate and they were still great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream filled oat bars

i found this in a local newspaper. i tried it out on a night when my teenage daughters had a house full of friends over for a movie. i managed to grab a piece before the dish was grabbed and the bars inhaled. delicious!

1. heat oven to 375f
2. grease 9 x 9-inch square pan
3. mix milk , lemon peel and lemon juice until thickened
4. reserve
5. mix remaining ingredients until crumbly
6. press half of the crumbly mixture in pan
7. bake about 10 minutes or until set
8. spread milk mixture over baked layer
9. sprinkle remaining crumbly mixture on milk mixture
10. press gently into milk mixture
11. bake about 20 minutes or until edge is golden brown and center is set but soft
12. cool completely
demonstrations.review: This sounded great - but turned out to be far too sweet for our tastes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amish apple crisp

another wonderful amish inspired dish. we serve this for dessert, or for breakfast. very tasty!

1. place apple mixture in a deep dish pie pan
2. sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon
3. mix topping ingredients , except the cinnamon and butter , with a fork until blended
4. sprinkle topping over apples
5. drizzle melted butter over topping
6. sprinkle with cinnamon
7. bake at 375f degrees for 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was definitely a winner in our house. I used a combination of sliced apples, peaches and raisins. Served it piping hot with vanilla icecream - what a hit it was!! Thanks

target.recipe_text:
fresh peach cobbler  or berry cobbler

a fabulous cobbler recipe. it is quick to make and delicious every time.  if peaches are not in season--it is also wonderful with frozen sliced peaches--just be sure they are thawed through before you put it together and allow more time to cook.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. filling: mix peaches , sugar and flour together and pour into a 15-inch baking dish
3. batter: combine 2 cups flour , 1 cup sugar , baking powder , and salt in food processor
4. process to combine
5. add the milk and melted butter
6. process until smooth
7. spoon batter over the peaches , making sure you spread to edge of dish
8. sprinkle remaining 1 tablespoon sugar , nutmeg and cinnamon over the top
9. bake in center of oven about one hour
10. crust should be brown and crisp on the outside and cooked all the way through
11. let cool for 10 minutes before serving
12. serve with whipped cream or vanilla ice cream
13. variation: blackberry , blueberry or raspberry cobbler--omit cinnamon and nutmeg
target.review: After bringing this to work for a potluck meal, I am now being called the best baker in the department! Many have asked for the recipe and everybody loved it. Thank you for posting such a wonderful recipe that is so easy to make. -- posted Oct 5, 2005

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ruth s chris sweet potato casserole

this is absolutely divine! ruth has done it again! note, the first time i made this i noticed there was a bit of extra liquid left over, next time i will adjust the amount of butter and/or add a bit more potato.

1. combine brown sugar , flour , nuts and butter in mixing bowl
2. set aside
3. preheat oven to 350 degrees
4. combine sweet potatoes , sugar , salt , vanilla , eggs and butter in a mixing bowl in the order listed
5. mix thoroughly
6. pour mixture into buttered baking dish
7. sprinkle the surface of the sweet potato mixture evenly with the crust mixture
8. bake for 30 minutes
9. allow to set at least 30 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Absolutely perfect. We changed nothing and everyone loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach artichoke dip   look no further this is the one

i am not a fan of spinach but this is my favorite dip period! i have tried a lot of spinach artichoke dips and this is by far the best! look no further! make this now!

1. preheat oven to 350f in an 8x8 inch baking dish , spread the roasted garlic , spinach , artichoke hearts , alfredo pasta sauce , mozzarella cheese , parmesan cheese and cream cheese
2. cover and bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes or till cheeses are bubbly
3. serve warm with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: This recipe is fantastic. I have been searching for a good spinach-artichoke dip. My search is now over. Thanks for posting this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious cream corn

this makes a large amount but not to worry this will be eaten up in a flash it is *that* good!  make certain that the corn is completely thawed but not cooked. i like to mix in some parmesan cheese at the end of cooking ;-)

1. in a large saucepan combine thawed corn niblets , whipping cream , evaporated milk , salt and sugar
2. bring to boil over medium heat , stirring occasionally
3. reduce heat to low and simmer for 5-6 minutes
4. melt butter in the microwave or in a small saucepan over low heat
5. whisk in flour until smooth , then stir into the corn mixture until well blended and thickened
6. season with black pepper or cayenne to taste
demonstrations.review: With out a doubt just as good as that place in Texas. I didn't change a thing. Thank you for the post.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar bundt cake

my mom passed this recipe along to me. it is easy to make and has been a big hit at home and at the office. i get frequent requests for the recipe. it is very moist and delicious and makes a good breakfast cake as well as a dessert. increase nuts by another 1/3 cup if you like nuts!

1. grease a 10-inch bundt pan well and sprinkle pan with granulated sugar
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
3. combine cake mix , pudding mix , eggs , oil and water in large bowl and beat on medium speed until well mixed , about 4 minutes
4. add brown sugar and pecans and mix to combine well
5. pour batter evenly into prepared bundt pan and bake for 1 hour or until cake tester comes out clean
6. place bundt pan on wire rack and cool 15 minutes
7. invert cake onto rack and slip pan off cake
8. let cool on rack
9. can be stored covered at room temperature
demonstrations.review: This was a big hit at a party I recently attended. I made it as directed with no alterations.(unusual for me!) I'm already planning to bring another one to share with my coworkers. Thanks for posting this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab rangoon dip

i received this recipe from my sister-in-law. it is very good and hard to stop eating once you start.

1. dip: soften cream cheese in microwave
2. stir in rest of ingredients
3. spread in serving bowl
4. before serving , microwave to warm
5. top with sweet and sour sauce
6. to make wonton strips :
7. cut each wonton wrapper in half
8. spray with nonstick cooking spray and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
9. bake 5-7 minutes at 375 or until slightly brown
demonstrations.review: This was just perfect. I used the 1/3 reduced fat cream cheese and did not add the sweet and sour sauce since we like the flavor of the cream cheese mix by itself. This is just what I've been looking for. Thank you.

target.recipe_text:
tarragon chicken salad  whole foods

this recipe is from whole foods and is also gluten free.

1. fill a medium pot with water and bring to a boil over high heat
2. add chicken , cover and return to a boil
3. boil chicken for 2 to 3 minutes , then turn off the heat and let the chicken steep , covered , until no longer pink in the thickest part of the breast , 8 to 12 minutes
4. using a slotted spoon , transfer chicken to a plate and let cool for approximately 20 minutes
5. cut chicken into 1 / 2-inch cubes
6. skip 1-4 if you are using canned chicken
7. drain liquid from can
8. in a medium bowl combine celery , mayonnaise , mustard , onions , almonds , tarragon , lemon juice and pepper and stir to blend
9. fold chicken into the mayonnaise mixture
target.review: I really enjoyed this but I wasn't sure if it was fresh or dried tarragon and so I only used 1 tbsp dried.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s blueberry pie   option for freezing

this is so easy and it makes a wonderful blueberry pie, this filling freezes wonderful and will makes enough for one 9-inch pie,  the filling also makes a great topping for cakes and cheesecakes --- you may make the filling up to step 4 and then freeze in a plastic container, if you are doubling the recipe prepare two separate recipes and make in two saucepans, i do not recommend to double into one.

1. in a heavy saucepan mix the blueberries , sugar , lemon juice , cinnamon , nutmeg and salt
2. bring to a boil stirring frequently
3. mix the cornstarch with cold water
4. pour over the berries whisking vigorously
5. cook stirring until thick and smooth
6. cool slightly
7. at this point you may freeze the filling or continue with pie recipe
8. pour into unbaked 9-inch pie shell
9. place the top crust over and seal / flute edges as desired
10. make 2-3 small slits on the top of crust
11. if desired you may brush with cream then sprinkle sugar over top
12. place the pie on a baking sheet
13. set oven to 400f
14. bake for 10 minutes then reduce to 350f and continue to bake for about 30 minutes longer or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbly
demonstrations.review: I was very happy to find this recipe but had a couple problems. First, I forgot that pouring cornstarch paste into a hot mix can create cornstarch lumps (which it did) and it turned out thicker than I would have liked. I tried this recipe again but reduced the cornstarch from 1/3 to 1/4 cup and then mixed the dry cornstarch with the dry sugar and it turned out perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish rosie s irish soda bread

this irish soda bread recipe was passed on to me by a dear friend of my mother's who was born and raised in ireland. it's the best irish soda bread i have ever had. it is much higher, lighter and softer than most other recipes i have seen. it has an excellent flavor and texture, as well.
