1. combine dry ingredients together in a large bowl
2. in a small bowl beat eggs and stir in sour cream
3. add the egg and sour cream mixture to the dry ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon
4. batter will be very thick
5. add the raisins and caraway seeds and stir well with wooden spoon or knead in with your hands
6. place batter in a greased 9 inch springform pan
7. dust the top with enough flour so that you can pat the batter like a bread dough evenly in the pan without it sticking to your hands
8. with a knife make a shallow crisscross on the top
9. bake for 50 minutes in a preheated 350f oven
demonstrations.review: I've never tried soda bread with caraway seeds before and I'm so glad I finally decided to take a chance. This was a very hearty and delicious bread that tasted great with Irish Beef Stew with Guinness Stout (#809) and calconnon potatoes. The seeds were not overpowering and the raisins (I used currents gave just the perfect about of sweet) Thank you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shredded pork tacos

makes really delicious tacos. you can make this into shredded beef too, just use a beef chuck roast in place of the pork blade roast. vary your toppings as you like- add some fresh jalapenos and spice things up!

1. season and rub meat with salt , pepper , coriander , cumin , and oregano
2. place roast in a large saucepan and add water about halfway up the meat
3. add onions , peppers , and garlic to pan and bring to a boil
4. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 2 1 / 2- 3 hours or until very tender
5. carefully remove meat from liquid and place on a cutting board with adequate drainage
6. allow to cool until you can handle it , then shred the meat with 2 forks
7. set the meat aside and keep warm
8. warm crispy taco shells for 5 minutes at 350f or warm flour tortillas briefly in a hot skillet until pliable
9. build tacos on warmed shells or tortillas with some meat , lettuce , cheese , olives , sliced avocado , and a little salsa
10. serve at once
demonstrations.review: would you believe I used ground turkey? Dinner was late and ground turkey was thawed so I threw it in the skillet with your seasonings (minus onions and jalapenos which we use as condiments) Everyone loved the flavor and my husband was stunned; "THAT WAS GROUND TURKEY??" Tonight I'll be using the pork. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chunky navy bean soup

a nice thick version on regular navy bean soup. i usually serve with hot cornbread and butter, maybe a few green onions on the side. you could use bacon instead of the ham hock.

1. sort , wash , and soak beans overnight
2. drain beans
3. add ham hock , garlic and 4 cups water
4. bring to a boil , cover , reduce heat , and simmer for 3 hours
5. add remaining ingredients
6. cover and simmer for 30-40 minutes , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: sorry, I didn't really like this recipe. I used four cups water, four cups chicken broth so maybe that ruined it. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracker barrel old country store fried apples

nan

1. in a large skillet , melt bacon drippings
2. pour apples evenly over skillet bottom
3. sprinkle lemon juice over them , then brown sugar , then salt
4. cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes until apples are tender and juicy
5. sprinkle with cinnamon & nutmeg
demonstrations.review: Very delicious!! Even the kids wanted seconds. I will definitely make this recipe again!

target.recipe_text:
spinach gorgonzola cornbread  crock pot

what a great side dish.

1. coat crock pot slow cooker with nonstick cooking spray
2. mix all ingredients in medium bowl
3. pour batter into crock pot slow cooker
4. cover
5. cook on high 1 1 / 2 hours
6. sprinkle to with paprika for more colorful crust , if desired
7. let bread cool completely before inverting onto serving platter
8. cook only on high setting for proper crust and texture
target.review: I'll use Crockpot again, I'll try in my breadmaker too, I'll never make plain cornbread again. Think I could have done less time, it should have been moister & more fluffy. It didn't come out as bright orange either, maybe that was your lighting. I added the paprika at the beginning, maybe should have added it after, I was unsure reading the recipe, even though it does mention it after the cooking on high bit. Maybe this dried it too, I've nothing to compare it with, only store-bought cornbread & that is dry!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and dumplings   pressure cooker   instant pot   instapot

pressure cooker recipe for chicken and dumplings.
very easy to modify to stove top cooking.

this has become a family favorite, and is requested over grandma's
pennsylvania dutch recipe (shhhh).

1. combine the first 8 ingredients into pressure cooker
2. cover , lock , and cook on low pressure for 15 minutes
3. after 15 minutes , lower pressure with quick release method
4. remove chicken and cover to keep warm
5. combine dumpling ingredients as follows:
6. combine eggs , milk , salt and baking powder in large bowl
7. whisk until frothy
8. whisk in 1 cup of flour
9. stir in remaining flour
10. bring liquid in pressure cooker to a boil
11. drop teaspoon sized dumplings into boiling broth
12. cover , lock , and bring to high pressure over high heat
13. lower heat to stabilize , and cook for 5-7 minutes
14. shred chicken off bone as dumplings cook
15. after 5-7 minutes , lower pressure with quick release method
16. add shredded chicken back into dumpling pot , or serve directly into bowls and spoon broth and dumplings over it
demonstrations.review: I've given 5 stars because I loved the flavour-combination & especially the fluffy dumplings. There are some things I didn't do though. I have an Instant pot, but I haven't bought chicken with bones in for 30 yrs - if I did, I'd have to skin them to follow the recipe faithfully, wait for InstantPot to come down from temp twice at 10 mins a time, then shred the chicken, it was a few steps too far. In addition, chicken cooks so quickly, I don't think it needs a pressure cooker & British chicken (I used breast fillets) oozes some white goo out of it that I didn't want in the stock, so it had to be seared anyway first, as well as my not being that keen on boiled-from-scratch meat either. Accordingly, I seared large chunks of chicken & carrots, so the carrots were well-started on cooking, added the onions & celery, then more stock as was not using the Instant pot & the dumplings on top, it all cooked together then. I like the fluffy texture, not used bicarb in dumplings before & I'm very impressed, not just the texture, but they threatened to migrate out of my pot because the grew (perhaps they would not rise under pressure). Served with potatoes & cabbage.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy spaghetti pie

i went to a pampered chef party where this was served. many people asked for the recipe! update: i have revised this recipe due to people having trouble with the instructions. i hope this makes it easier to follow.

1. save out 1 / 4 cup of the parmesan cheese and 1 / 4 cup shredded mozzarella cheese
2. set aside
3. mix together green onions , garlic , chopped parsley , 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese , ricotta cheese , egg , butter , salt , italian seasoning , and 3 / 4 cup mozzarella cheese
4. mix cheese / egg mixture with cooked spaghetti and place on the bottom of a shallow casserole dish
5. in a bowl , mix spaghetti sauce with tomatoes
6. pour over spaghetti mixture
7. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 4 cup parmesan cheese and 1 / 4 cup mozzarella cheese that was set aside
8. bake about 30 minutes at 350 degrees
9. after pulling out of oven , garnish pie with chopped parsley
10. serve and enjoy !
11. pie will feel firm to the touch
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This looked appealing as I have never encountered this before. The recipe had lots of cheese in which is a big yes for me & it was as satisfying as I knew it would be. Like other posters, I added things, mushrooms & courgettes - next time I'll do green pepper & sweetcorn. I used basil not parsley as it was Italian based but coriander would also have worked well to cut through but still complement all that cheesiness, ahem, I did add more than directed! The only thing I was unsure about was a jar of 'spaghetti sauce'. We don't have such a thing in Britain, but there was a choice: Passata - sieved tomatoes that are a 'Christmas red' as the seeds are not liquidised with the pulp (which would make it orangey) or 'Pasta Sauce'. The latter is sold plain (which Americans may call tomato sauce - our tomato sauce is ketchup) or with added herbs/veg & I chose this (with red peppers) as I thought it the most appropriate & generally meant to be added to a 'quick' pasta dish. I used part full-fat ricotta & part cottage cheese, mostly the latter as I had put loads of fatty cheese in/on already. As sharfan posted, not enough stars!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
touchdown taco dip

this dip is to die for!!! i use jalapeno flavored refried beans and top the dip with fresh, seeded jalapenos, because my family likes it extra spicy! this dip is easy and certainly a crowd pleaser! i found this recipe in one of my pampered chef cookbooks.

1. spread the refried beans in a square stone baker
2. in a mixing bowl , combine cream cheese , sour cream , taco seasoning , and garlic
3. mix well with electric mixer
4. spread cream cheese mixture on top of refried beans
5. sprinkle cheddar cheese on top of cream cheese mixture
6. sprinkle olives , tomatoes , onions and cilantro on top
7. bake at 350 for about 15 minutes
8. serve hot with tortilla chips !
demonstrations.review: I loved this! This is the sort of thing that would be served on toast in the UK - we don't do the 'dip' thing. I had most of the ingredients, what I didn't have or know if it was sold here was 'Taco' seasoning. I googled it (I hope I can mention this?), & we do & even onion powder & garlic powder, but they are not mentioned on our recipe sites. I dry-roast garlic & onion in a dry-pan (what people used before electric air-fryers) & added to the other spices. I had some HUGE olives to cut, pitted them myself & served on toast. I made double quantity & will top a cottage pie tomorrow with it. Doing that reminds me of my son, then a teenager, who loves cheese as much as me, made cottage pie & a moussaka, both of which would have served 8 hungry people, & made/poured a thick mature Cheddar cheese sauce over it all. He made the sauce in a stockpot & it worked out at over a litre for a 4-portion pie, we still laugh about it, I love cheese, but my tummy, as in measurements, doesn't!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
african style grilled peanut butter chicken

peanuts are used widely in african cuisine.

1. combine all ingredients , if mixture is too thick , keep adding hot water until mixture is similar to cream
2. reserve 1 / 2 cup of marinade mixture for basting while grilling
3. place remaining marinade in zip loc bag , add chicken pieces , squish to combine , marinate for 2-3 hours
4. heat grill , lightly oil grates , place chicken on grate and brush with reserved peanutbutter mixture while grilling
5. grill until juices run clear
6. serve with rice or potatoes
demonstrations.review: I'm not sure what is supposed to be 'African-style' about this, other than it's served with the bones still in it. Mayonnaise & Sherry (or wine) are not African at all. Lime juice & coriander are Mediterranean to South-East Asian, as are peppers. Plantains, Cassava, Palm oil & Maize Porridge are traditional African foods, though I have found a reference to peanut sauces in West African cuisine. I've never met Africans who cook with them though other than using groundnut oil. Did you mean Arab, rather than Black Africa, as in, say, Morocco? It does seem more like Middle-Eastern cookery. It is lovely though, I never buy peanut butter, not a popular item in Britain, unless I'm making a sauce, I used the coarse-ground (and next time I'll make my own as I regularly make peanut burgers - mixed with maizemeal as it happens!). I used fillets as I never buy boney pieces & don't want fatty skin, & they were lovely. I grilled them (British grill is the space between the oven & hob, not an outdoor BBQ - most people don't have them). I made a spicy tomato rice as pictured & Recipes 406859 & 368435 (Black-eye-bean salad & Grilled Coconut Pineapple as well as suggested by another reviewer below. Onion, Tomato, Cucumber & Coriander Leaf Raita (yogurt) & Garlic Naan Bread completed the spread. I shall make this again soon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy zucchini boats with tomato   pepper jack

the garden is currently bursting with zucchini and tomatoes and this is one of my favorite ways to use it up.  these are cheesy, sweet, salty and spicy all in one bite.  i typically have them as a snack but they are also perfect as a side dish.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat
3. add the onions and cook until soft
4. add the garlic and cook for 1 minute longer
5. remove the onion with a slotted spoon and set aside
6. slice the zucchini in half lengthwise
7. using a spoon , scoop out the seeds from the middle of the zucchini to make the boats , leaving 1 / 2 inch of the zucchini intact
8. season the zucchini boats evenly with salt , pepper and basil
9. spread the onions out on top of the zucchini
10. place four sliced tomatoes on top of each boat
11. top with pepper jack cheese and add another layer of tomatoes
12. top with some more pepper jack cheese
13. bake in the oven for 30 to 35 minutes , or until the zucchini is tender
14. garnish with basil
15. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful!!! I made a lot more than 2 though. Served with salads, quiche, veggy cutlets, anything to suit the baking weather at the moment. As well as making as written for authenticity, I did some with Thersa M's suggestion, except I used veggy bacon.

target.recipe_text:
roasted butternut squash and shallots

the perfect combination, even my kids will inhale this!

1. preheat oven to 475
2. combine ingredients in bowl
3. pour into a lightly sprayed jellyroll pan
4. bake at 475 for 20 minutes or until tender , stirring occasionally
target.review: Delicious! I used butternut and acorn squash from the farmer's market and it baked up beautifully! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of red lobster cheddar bay biscuits by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com. the cold butter is the secret. it's not included in other copy cat recipes.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. combine bisquick and cold butter
3. don't combine too thoroughly
4. there should be small chunks of butter about the size of peas
5. add cheddar , milk and 1 / 4 tsp garlic
6. mix by hand until combined , but don't over mix
7. drop 9 equal portions onto greased cookie sheet
8. bake for 15-17 minutes or until tops are light brown
9. melt 2 tbsp butter in a bowl
10. stir in 1 / 2 tsp garlic powder and parsley flakes
11. use a pastry brush to spread garlic butter over tops of biscuits
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! These biscuits came out delicious, soaked up all the butter I could pour on them (and remained firm), and were proclaimed a "hit" by a hungry group of basketball-watching guys! Thank you for this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my favorite chocolate chip cookies

get a glass of cold milk ready! this has been my favorite chocolate chip cookie recipe of all time, found in a betty crocker cookbook years ago. once i made it for my hs latin class and it became a class tradition and a family favorite...thank you, betty!

1. cream shortening , butter , and sugars in large mixing bowl
2. blend in eggs and vanilla
3. combine dry ingredients and add to butter mixture
4. mix until well blended
5. stir in chocolate chips
6. drop by rounded teaspoon onto ungreased baking sheets
7. bake at 375 for 7-10 minutes until golden brown
8. i like chewy cookies and if you do too , adjust the baking time accordingly)
demonstrations.review:
Used this because I didn't have pudding mix on hand for other recipes - so glad I chose it! These got great reviews, and I froze half the dough to use later!
Tip: These go great with a glass of scotch; the vanilla in each is soo perfect together!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan roasted chicken and veggies

only one pan to wash with this wonderful casserole type dish which combines potatoes, rosemary, onions and garlic with quartered boneless chicken thighs and fresh spinach.

1. preheat oven to 475f
2. in large roasting pan , combine potatoes , onion , garlic , oil , salt , pepper and rosemary and toss to coat
3. roast veggies 25 minutes , stirring once
4. lightly salt and pepper chicken and add , tossing to coat and roast 15 minutes longer or until chicken is done
5. place spinach over chicken mixture and roast for 5 minutes longer or until spinach wilts
6. toss before serving
demonstrations.review: Good recipe.. it leaves a lot of "wiggle" room to personalize it, which I like. Doubled the recipe and added mushrooms (which the BF likes), marinated the chicken thighs as per the other reviewers in olive oil and lemon juice (then balsamic too, which the BF added). Used fresh rosemary since I didn't have dried, seared the chicken in a pan before adding (to cut my baking time), and loved the end result! Thank you Marie, for a great dinner staple!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
golden eggplant  aubergine  rounds

very good, crispy eggplant.

1. in shallow bowl , mix crumbs with parmesan cheese
2. put dressing in another bowl
3. dip eggplant slices in dressing , then into crumbs
4. put in a single layer on sprayed baking sheet
5. bake at 450 for 15 minutes , until golden brown
6. turn rounds once while baking
demonstrations.review: Very nice! I was looking for a quick and easy eggplant recipe and this was it :) I'm glad it also happened to be healthier than the fried version!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggnog cookies

"what a delectable treat for eggnog lovers everywhere! these cookies have a wonderful spicy aroma and are great tasting. the fragrance of nutmeg and cinnamon will infuse your home with holiday spirit as you bake these cookies. they make delicious gifts and are a welcome addition to cookie exchanges. "

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. combine flour , baking powder , cinnamon and nutmeg
3. cream sugar and butter until light
4. add eggnog , vanilla , and egg yolks
5. beat at medium speed with mixer until smooth
6. add flour mixture and beat at low speed until just combined
7. do not overmix
8. drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet 1 inch apart
9. sprinkle lightly with nutmeg
10. bake 20 to 23 minutes until bottoms turn light brown
demonstrations.review: The first batch of these I baked spread WAY more than I expected. After flouring my cookie sheet for round two, they came out much nicer. I, too, used the eggnog icing and it was splendid! These cookies are much more cakey than traditional cookies. I actually was able to cut them with a cookie cutter straight out of the oven!

target.recipe_text:
24k carrots

carrots coated with a yummy butter, brown sugar and ginger sauce. i grew up eating these in texas. easy, quick and yummy!-- great way to get kids to enjoy this veggie! if you like a lot of sauce double the sauce ingredients. i posted this less 'saucy' to keep the fat and calories down. the sauce is yummy and great on rice or just on a spoon! hope you enjoy it as much as we do!  i am so honored that this simple little recipe of mine has been so well received. thank you all for your reviews!

1. cook carrots until tender- or to desired doneness
2. melt butter and add brown sugar and ginger , stirring to blend
3. add sauce to carrots and stir to coat
target.review: I had this for lunch today. It was very good. This is one of the few ways that I like to carrots. Good Basic recipe. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sour cream salsa chicken for crock pot

this recipe has a smooth mexican taste.

1. spray liner of crock pot with vegetable spray
2. add the chicken breasts on the bottom
3. don't lay them on top of each other
4. sprinkle with taco seasoning mix with salsa poured on top
5. cook on low for 6 to 8 hours
6. when ready to serve , remove chicken from crock pot and place on meat platter covered with aluminum foil
7. mix together 3 tablespoons water and 2 tablespoons cornstarch
8. add to salsa mixture in crock pot and stir well
9. turn crock pot to high and sauce should begin to thicken in five minutes
10. next , stir in sour cream
11. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was easy, quick, and tasty. Next time I will not be adding the cornstarch because I thought the sauce became to thick. I will be making this again for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
enchiladas santa fe

my adaptation of a great recipe from baja cantina in park city, utah. don't miss out on experiencing these yummy enchiladas for yourself!

1. saute chicken in vegetable oil with garlic salt until just done
2. spread each tortilla with cream cheese
3. divide chicken , spinach , onion , and tomatoes between tortillas
4. roll enchiladas and place seam-side down in 9x13" baking dish that has been lightly sprayed with no-stick cooking spray
5. pour enchilada sauce evenly over enchiladas then top with grated cheese
6. bake at 350 degrees for 15 minutes until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I have made these 2 times now and each time they come out so good!! Easy to make!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq chicken pizza   california pizza kitchen style

if you've ever been to the california pizza kitchen and tried this pizza, you'll never want to go back to the greasy east coast style...

1. to make bbq chicken: in a large frying pan , cook the chicken in olive oil over medium-high heat until just cooked , 5 to 6 minutes
2. do not overcook
3. set aside in the refrigerator until chilled through
4. once chilled , coat the chicken with 2 tablespoons bbq sauce
5. set aside in the refrigerator
6. to make the pizza: place the pizza stone in the center of the oven and preheat to 500 degrees f for one hour before cooking pizzas
7. use a large spoon to spread cup bbq sauce evenly over the surface of the prepared dough within the rim
8. sprinkle 1 tablespoon smoked gouda cheese over the sauce
9. cover with cup shredded mozzarella
10. distribute half the chicken pieces evenly over the cheese
11. place approximately 18 to 20 pieces of red onion over the surface
12. sprinkle an additional cup mozzarella over the top of the pizza
13. transfer the pizza to the oven
14. bake until the crust is crisp and golden and the cheese at the center is bubbly , 8 to 10 minutes
15. when the pizza is cooked , carefully remove it from the oven
16. sprinkle 1 tablespoon cilantro over the hot surface
17. slice
demonstrations.review: This was excellent!! I used a pre-made pizza crust so it was really fast to put together. I also used KC Masterpiece Original BBQ sauce. Great Pizza!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kashmir lamb with spinach

a fragrant, not hot, curry. for a bit of kick add ground or fresh chopped chillies to taste.

1. heat the oil in a pan and over medium heat brown the lamb in batches
2. add the onions , garlic and ginger and cook , stirring often , for 3 minutes
3. add the spices and cook , stirring , for 1- 2 minutes until spices are fragrant
4. return the lamb and any juices to the pan
5. add the stock and bay leaves
6. bring to the boil and then reduce heat , stir well , cover and simmer for 35 minutes
7. add the cream , stir , cover and cook a further 20 minutes
8. add the spinach and cook until the spinach has softened
demonstrations.review: Amazing! Yummy! Delicious! Tender! These were just a few of the words my dinner guests used to describe this dish. This is a perfect dish for people who do not like spicy food but still enjoy fragrent food. Everyone was very impressed. The lamb was very tender and wonderful! I will be making this again and again for sure! Thanks so much for providing an excellent recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
most simple vegetarian white gravy

old family secret...best vegetarian gravy you'll ever have.  it'll turn meat-eaters into believers!  update:  i've reduced the amount of salt based on some of the comments.  enjoy!

1. mix all ingredients into a saucepan
2. whisk together over medium heat
3. continue whisking until the sauce thickens
4. if after about 5 minutes sauce isn't thickening still add more flour tbsp by tbsp until it is at your desired consistency
5. if sauce is too thick , add more milk
demonstrations.review: I use this gravy recipe to make biscuits and gravy. We probably put in a bit more pepper because we like peppery gravy :) Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
rice pudding for one

i'm passing this along for all the seniors and singles. i haven't tried it myself, but plan to soon as it sounds easy and tasty.

1. bring water to a boil and add rice
2. cover and simmer for 20 minutes
3. preheat oven to 350f degrees
4. whisk milk and egg together , then whisk in sugar and vanilla
5. stir into the hot cooked rice and then stir in raisins
6. pour rice mixture into a small greased casserole dish and bake , uncovered , for 20 minutes
7. serve warm with pouring cream
target.review: This was so tasty!  Great breakfast on a rainy morning - used whipping cream after baking to make it creamier.  Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked garlic corn on the cob

corn on the cob baked with olive oil and garlic!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. add oil and garlic to a 13x9 inch glass baking dish , bake until oil starts to sizzle and remove
3. add corn , season with salt and pepper and turn to coat
4. cover tightly with foil , bake 25-30 minutes turning once
demonstrations.review: Very good!  Only complaint is that a lot of the garlic pieces didn't "stick" to the corn, but it still tasted great!  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
prize winning chile cheese appetizers

these excellent little puffs won first prize at a chile festival in new mexico in 1984 by helen trujillo.

1. in a 13 x 9 pan , melt butter
2. beat eggs lightly in a large bowl
3. add flour and baking powder
4. combine
5. in another bowl , combine remaining ingredients , except salsa
6. combine cheese mixture to the flour
7. blend well
8. pour batter into pan and bake at 400f for 14 minutes
9. reduce heat to 350f and bake 35-40 minutes longer
10. cut into appetizer size squares and serve warm with salsa
demonstrations.review: Made this for a potluck at work and it got rave reviews - will definitely make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: I also added some dried thyme and just a pinch of Mediterranean oregano to this (forgetting to peel the potatoes, but it was still good!) I served it in some homemade bread bowls (see Recipe #36562) and it was great!!! Reminded me of the soup served at the Wildflower Bread Company (probably the Panera of the Southwest). Great recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
romano s macaroni grill chicken cannelloni

had this at the macaroni grill.  it was delicious.  this is a copycat version i found online.

1. dice the chicken breast into 1 / 2-inch pieces and place into a large mixing bowl
2. add spinach , tomatoes , ricotta , mozzarella , pepper and salt , and mix thoroughly
3. arrange precooked pasta sheets on a cutting board and place two or three rounded tablespoons of filling mixture down the center of each pasta sheet and carefully roll pasta around filling in a cigar fashion
4. place the rolled cannelloni , side by side , into an ovenproof shallow baking dish
5. place alfredo sauce and tomato sauce in bowl and mix until well incorporated
6. pour sauce over cannelloni covering completely
7. sprinkle grated parmesan cheese over top of sauce
8. cover with aluminum foil and bake at 350f for approximately 20 minutes
9. remove foil and continue to bake for an additional 20 minutes , or until an internal temperature of 165f is reached
10. remove from oven and serve family style or on individual plates garnished with fresh diced tomatoes , and basil or italian parsley
demonstrations.review: I used the pre-cooked chicken strips in the meat case - this was excellent!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic breadmaker machine bread

nan

1. put milk in bread machine , followed by salt , sugar , butter , flour , yeast
2. my preference is to process on the dough setting until dough is ready and take out and bake as a normal loaf
3. if not follow the instructions on your bread machine for a 1 1 / 2 lb loaf
demonstrations.review: I needed a bread bowl for the potluck Thanksgiving my family was invited to so I used this recipe for the dough and then shaped it and baked it in my convection oven at 375 for 22 minutes.  I added a couple of tablespoons of dill and garlic powder to it since its final destiny was to hold a flavored dip, and it was gone in an hour.  Great, great recipe - I love fresh bread but I'm not really wild about the shape of the loaves that my bread machine makes.  I will use this recipe again and again.  Thanks for posting!!

target.recipe_text:
oatmeal salmon patties

this is a very healthy and tasty recipe for salmon patties. it is also very fast and easy to make. what more could a chef want!

1. combined all ingredients except margarine
2. mix well
3. shape to form oval patties about 1 / 2 inch thick
4. pan fry the patties in margarine over medium heat for 3-4 minutes on each side or until golden brown and heated through
5. serve hot
target.review: I thought this was ok.  It was missing something for me......salt maybe?  They were ok.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
south beach salmon with creamy lemon sauce low carb

i found this in the "south beach diet book".. even if you're not dieting... it's great. just substitute real sour cream for the fat-free for a to die for experience. it's quick, simple and uses on hand ingredients.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. coat a baking sheet with cooking spray
3. heat the oil in a small saucepan over medium heat
4. add the garlic and cook for one minute
5. reduce heat to low
6. stir in the lemon juice , capers and lemon-pepper seasoning and cook for 5 minutes
7. add the sour cream and cook for 5 minutes or until heated though
8. meanwhile , place the salmon on the prepared baking sheet
9. bake for 20 minutes or until the fish is just opaque
10. serve with the sauce
demonstrations.review: This was really good.  I used tilapia instead of salmon, the sauce was really creamy and satisfying, I think it would be good over any fish.  Quick, easy and really yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
3 vegetable casserole

my bosses wife swears by this recipe for leftovers. i have used it many times, make a good meal or sidedish.

1. scald milk with margarine
2. remove from heat , add bread veggies , salt , eggs and 3 / 4 cup cheese
3. mix together and pour into a 4 quart greased casserole , top with remaining 1 / 2 cup of cheese
4. bake at 325 for 40 min
5. want some extra flavour use half evaporated milk
demonstrations.review: This recipes is really great!  I used some frozen veggies (corn, peas and spinach) wheat bread and mozz and it was mighty tasty.  I used it a side-dish along with some Aidells sausage, it was a fantastic meal and so simple only taking minutes to assemble.  I will definitely be making this again, it's a quick, tasty, versatile (ie; you can really make it with whatever you want!) meal. Thanks Tara!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bob s white chili

i don't know who bob is and i haven't tried this; it was emailed to me by my sil. sounds good!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. place chicken breasts on greased baking sheet and bake for 20 minutes
3. alternatively , saute chicken breasts on stovetop in a nonstick frying pan until almost cooked through
4. remove from heat and set aside
5. in a large pot , pour in 1 cup of chicken broth and add onion and garlic
6. bring to a simmer and cook until onion starts to soften
7. add the chilies , stir , then add remaining broth and beans
8. stir in the spices
9. bring to a boil and add chicken pieces , cut into cubes
10. cover and simmer for at least 30 minutes-- longer is better
11. taste and add more salt if necessary
12. serve in prewarmed bowls , garnished with sliced raw green onion
demonstrations.review: This was really good!  I had some bell pepper and mushrooms to use up so I chopped them up and threw them in.  I served it will sour cream, cheddar and green onions

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy crock pot salsa chicken

quick, healthy and delicious. just pop the four ingredients into the crock-pot in the morning and you'll have a great-tasting meal for dinner. this would also be great for larger gatherings.

1. place first four ingredients in crock pot
2. cook on low 6-8 hours
3. 30-60 minutes prior to serving , remove chicken , shred and return to crock pot
4. to serve , use chicken mixture as filling inside tortillas
5. add desired condiments
demonstrations.review: This was really, really good and so simple to make.  I ate in a corn tortilla taco style, I plan to eat the rest over rice tomorrow, this is definitely going into my rotation!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cottage cheese and tomato on toast

this is a healthy breakfast, or whatever meal you like. really yummy.

1. toast the bread
2. spread with cottage cheese
3. top with tomato
4. sprinkle with pepper if you want
5. enjoy
demonstrations.review: So simple and fresh tasting.  This has been incorporated into the breakfast rotation.

target.recipe_text:
santa s whiskers

from better homes and gardens new cook book. a woman in my husband's office makes these for him at christmas time. he just loves them.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. beat butter for 30 seconds
3. add sugar and beat until fluffy
4. add milk and vanilla and beat well
5. stir in flour , then cherries and pecans
6. shape into three 7-inch rolls
7. roll dough in coconut to coat outside
8. wrap in waxed paper or clean plastic wrap
9. chill thoroughly
10. cut into 1 / 4 inch slices
11. place on an ungreased cookie sheet
12. bake in 375 oven for 12 minutes or until edges are golden
target.review: Really enjoyed these, even tho I don't usually liked candied cherries.  I used half red and half green cherries, I feel the cookies are prettier this way.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4 layer pizza dip

i haven't tried it yet...just putting in here for safe keeping.  i changed it a little to be a bit more "low carb" friendly.  let me know what you think!  adapted from http://jaimesrecipes.com/.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a blender combine tomatoes , garlic , onion , italian seasoning , salt , and pepper
3. blend until pureed
4. set pizza sauce aside
5. in a medium bowl , combine cream cheese , sour cream and 2 ounces of shredded cheese
6. mix well until well combined
7. spread cream cheese mixture in an even layer over baking dish
8. pour blended pizza sauce over cream cheese mixture and evenly distribute with spatula
9. sprinkle remaining shredded cheese over pizza sauce
10. top pizza dip with bacon and pepperoni
11. bake for 20-25 minutes , until cheese is browned and bubbly
demonstrations.review: I really liked the concept of a pizza dip.  I would suggest cutting down  on the sour cream and I really wasn't sold on the taste of the homemade sauce, but this dip would be really good with your favorite store bought pizza sauce.  I skipped the bacon due to my families preference. I made this with regular sour cream and regular cream cheese because that is what I had on hand. My family won't go low fat yet.   I made this for My-3-Chefs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pepper steak and noodles

my mother-in-law wanda gave me this recipe, and i have made it for 29 years. we reheat half of it the next day, yum.

1. in large skillet , melt margarine , add beef and sprinkle with garlic powder
2. saute until browned
3. remove meat from skillet
4. saute onion and green pepper 2 minutes
5. return meat along with tomatoes and bouillon cube
6. simmer 20 minutes
7. blend together cornstarch , water , soy sauce , sugar and salt
8. add to skillet mixture and cook , stirring , until thickened
9. meanwhile , cook noodles and drain
10. mix noodles into skillet with meat mixture
11. sprinkle cheese on top and allow to melt
demonstrations.review: Very good.  I added the cheese, but would like it with or without the cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet potatoes

my grandmother's simple sweet potato recipe.  she made this every thanksgiving and christmas.  simple and delicious.

1. mix first 5 ingredients and put in buttered casserole
2. mix last 4 ingredients with fork
3. sprinkle crumbs on top of first mixture
4. bake 20 minutes at 350 degrees f
demonstrations.review: Five star rating only after adding  a generous amount of cinnamon to both the mashed sweet potatoes, and to the topping.  Made for My 3 Chefs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
upper crust potatoes

this is a outstanding potato gratin. it goes great with all grilled and roasted meats, poultry, and game. different textures can be achieved by coarsely or thinly grating, dicing, or julienning the potatoes. from new basics cookbook.

1. preheat the oven to 375f
2. oil the bottom of a shallow 2-quart baking dish
3. peel and very thinly slice potatoes
4. put them in a mixing bowl and add 3 / 4 cup of the cream
5. mix , and set aside
6. melt the butter in a skillet , and add the shallots and garlic
7. saute over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes
8. do not brown
9. add bay leaves and rosemary to skillet
10. whisk in the cream cheese , milk , and remaining 3 / 4 cup cream
11. simmer , whisking constantly , until smooth , 2 to 3 minutes
12. add the paprika and salt and pepper
13. discard the bay leaves and pour the mixture over the potatoes
14. toss gently
15. arrange the potato mixture in a baking dish , spreading it out evenly
16. sprinkle it first with the parmesan , and then with bread crumbs
17. bake until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden brown and bubbly , 1 to 1 1 / 4 hours
18. sprinkle the parsley over and serve immediately
19. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Really good but I also topped ours off with Sharp Cheddar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy rolled crescent reubens

these are absolutey delicious and so easy to make! you can even purchase the jumbo crescent rolls and double the amounts of the filling ingredients. you can omit the dressing if desired. just make certain to hand-squeeze the sauerkraut out well.

1. set oven to 425 degrees
2. prepare a slightly greased cookie sheet
3. unroll the crescent rolls and seperate
4. spread each triangle with about 1 teaspoon dressing
5. top with shredded corned beef , then grated cheese , and then the sauerkraut
6. roll up from large end to small end
7. place on cookie sheet with the point end facing downwards
8. bake for about 10-12 minutes , or until golden brown
9. delicious !
demonstrations.review:
My family really enjoyed these tasty, little crescents.  These are a nice treat to munch on while watching television, or playing a game of Poker.   
I made these in memory of John, Cookathon for Kittencal.

target.recipe_text:
tiramisu

a classical italian dessert , my boyfriend's favourite!

1. beat sugar and egg yolks until white and frothy
2. whisk egg whites until stiff
3. fold mascarpone into egg mixture
4. add egg whites carefully
5. pour coffee in a shallow bowl , dip biscuits in it , taking care not to soak them completely , and put them in a square tin in a single layer
6. cover with the cheese cream and continue layering the ingredients , leaving the cream on top , dust with cocoa
7. cover and refrigerate for a few hours or even overnight so that the biscuits have time to become moist and flavourful
target.review: Made this for the dessert bar at my wedding and it's so good!  I'm glad I got to bring some of it home so I could finish it off!!!  Thanks so much for sharing!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden capellini pomodoro

this is an incredibly easy, incredibly delicious dish. it is a takeoff from the olive garden original. i like more garlic, more basil,  and less oil than their recipe calls for, but you can go to their website and get the original. this is a real kid pleaser. if they hate tomatoes, leave them out. it's still delicious. 

i wanted to add that you almost can't put too much basil in this. i made this again last night and probably used 40 large basil leaves or more, and some fresh parsley that my son picked by mistake. i did note that when i used 6 cloves of garlic,  they were small to medium cloves. when they were large, i used only 4. garlic is a matter of preference, though and you may love 6 large cloves. you can also increase the amount of fresh tomato, but do increase your garlic in proportion. it always amazes me that this dish is so fast and sooooooooooooooo delicious!

1. boil pasta in salted water and drain
2. you may process garlic , olive oil , basil leaves , salt and pepper whole in mini chopper or food processor and then stir into drained noodles
3. or add garlic , olive oil , and basil
4. stir well
5. add salt , pepper , and tomatoes
6. adjust seasonings to taste
7. top with parmesan , romano , or asiago cheese
demonstrations.review: We LOVED this.  I added about a cup of baby spinach leaves to it to increase the protein and just chopped them in the food processor with the rest.  Thanks Heartsong!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden style chicken and gnocchi soup

this is very close to the olive garden soup. there's another recipe on the web, which was the basis of this recipe, however, i have changed it to use less cream. still tastes good! i did end up using a little cornstarch to thicken. i guess you could sub heavy cream for the half-and-half to make it a little thicker without using cornstarch. the gnocchi is usually in the spaghetti section of the grocery store.

1. saute the onion , celery , garlic , carrot in oil over medium heat until onion is translucent
2. add chicken , chicken stock , half and half , salt and pepper , thyme
3. heat to boiling , then add gnocchi
4. gently boil for 4 minutes , then turn down to a simmer for 10 minutes
5. add spinach and cook for another 1-2 minutes until spinach is wilted
6. ladle into bowls and serve !
demonstrations.review: This soup is DELICIOUS!  Not exactly the same as OG, but since the closest OG is 100 miles away, it's definitely an acceptable substitute!  I left out the celery since my hubby hates it, and used half a package of frozen spinach instead of fresh.  At first I thought it was a bit heavy on the thyme, but I let it sit for a few minutes prior to serving, and the flavors melded perfectly.  We sprinkled a bit of parmesan on the top of each bowl also.  Even most of the kids loved this one, and they're hard to please!  Great recipe, thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet potato casserole w coconut pecan topping

my partner's wife sent this last year to our thanksgiving luncheon at work. it was hit there and a hit at my house. i just love it!

1. mix all of the casserole ingredients in a mixer until smooth , then spread in a buttered dish
2. mix well topping ingredients and add melted butter
3. sprinkle on top of the potatoes
4. bake at 375 for 25 minutes
demonstrations.review: Huge hit at the family Thanksgiving this year!  I doubled the recipe and it was gone before anything else with everyone asking for the recipe!  Thanks for sharing!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken tortilla soup for dieters

my boss gave me this recipe when she was going to weight watchers. i tried it and was impressed with how easy it is to make and the great flavor. if you follow this recipe exactly this is only 3 points per serving. i myself never follow the serving and always tend to add more tortillas and chicken and cheese!

1. preheat oven to 200 degrees and thinly slice one of the tortillas and place it on a baking sheet and bake for about 15 to 20 minutes until crisp
2. crush the remaining 2 tortillas into small pieces
3. heat 2 tbs of the chicken broth in a pot and add your onion and garlic and cook about 2 minutes until softened
4. add the remaining chicken broth , crushed tortillas , tomato sauce , cilantro , cumin , chili powder , bay leaf and salt
5. bring this mixture to a boil , reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes
6. discard bay leaf and transfer the mixture to a blender and puree working in batches to avoid overflows
7. pour soup into 4 bowls and top each with tortilla strips , chicken , avocado and cheese
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: SO incredibly delicious in addition to being healthy!!!  This is a meal in our house at least a couple of times a month.  Thanks so much for sharing!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious broccoli   cheese crunchy bake

this is an uunbelievably simple side dish recipe which was taught to me by an american friend of mine who moved over here. we decided to celebrate thanksgiving with her to help her feel less homesick and she made this for us. i thought it was delicious, demanded the recipe which she gave me there and then and now it is a firm family favourite.

give it a chance, it sounds bizarre and yes, it is full of calories but it is perfect for a family dinner, or holiday celebration like christmas or thanksgiving or even easter.

i've tried this with normal cheese but it just doesn't have that same fix for me!

this is my first recipe listing so here goes nothing ha ha!!! please rate!!! i'd love any advice on changing or improving this!

1. 1
2. cut your broccoli into florets and steam until cooked how you like them
3. 2
4. pour the broccoli into a large oven proof serving dish
5. 3
6. crush the ritz crackers and sprinkle all over the top of the broccoli
7. 4
8. add the cheese squares to cover the dish
9. 5
10. cut the butter sticks into cubes and place across the top of the cheese
11. 6
12. pop into the over until the cheese is melted nicely
13. 7
14. remove from the oven and go nuts !
demonstrations.review: Made this for Thanksgiving with the extended family and it was AMAZING!  Will definitely be a repeat side at our house!  Thanks for sharing!!!!

target.recipe_text:
hungarian cabbage   noodles

some people use this as a main dish. i use it as a side dish.  my husband is a meat & taters man, so he has to have meat with his meal. this dish goes well with meatloaf.

1. in a large skillet , cook bacon until crisp
2. remove from skillet
3. drain on paper towel and crumble
4. stir sugar and salt into bacon drippings in skillet
5. add cabbage
6. stir till cabbage is coated
7. cook over medium heat until cabbage is tender , about 10 or 15 minutes
8. combine cabbage mixture , noodles and bacon
9. turn all into a 1 1 / 2-quart casserole
10. cover and bake in slow oven for 45 minutes
11. uncover
12. spoon sour cream over top
13. sprinkle with paprika
14. return to oven and bake 5 minutes more
target.review: This was a hearty and very rich dish.  Perfect comfort food for a cold day.  Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffing for christmas or thanksgiving

this is similar to my mom's recipe that she has made for years. she never measures and adds everything for our taste preferences. i have never been able to top her stuffing, but this comes very close. i don't measure the herbs. we like the sage flavor, so i tend to add more of that. i taste it until it tastes right to me. adjust the herbs to whatever your taste preferences are. your kitchen will smell wonderful as the herbs are cooking with the vegetables! if you like drier stuffing, adjust the amount of chicken broth. we like ours moist, so i use about 2 cans of swanson chicken broth. i always make several days ahead and freeze in ziploc bags with all the air squeezed out so that i'm not so rushed the day of the dinner.

1. if you're using bread , toast bread in a large shallow baking pan in middle of oven until just dry , 25 to 30 minutes
2. if you're using stuffing mix , you can skip this step
3. cook onions , celery , and herbs in butter in a large heavy skillet over moderately low heat , stirring occasionally , until celery is softened , about 10 minutes
4. stir together bread or stuffing mix , vegetables , broth , and salt and pepper to taste , then cool completely , uncovered
5. freezes extremely well
6. stuff in the turkey or bake at 350 for about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this for Thanksgiving and thought it was very good.  Will definately make again.  Thank you for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german onion pie

this is usually served when tasting wine and beer in germany. a good easy tasty recipe. serve hot, or room temp. bake in a large baking sheet, ( cookie pan with sides.)

1. line a large slightly oiled pizza pan with your favourite pizza yeast dough , about 1 / 4 inch thick
2. i usually use a large cookie sheet with low sides
3. press dough on bottom and give slight edges
4. fry onions slowly in the butter
5. do not brown the onions , make them transparent and cooked but not browned
6. beat eggs with the salt , sour cream , flour , and seeds
7. mix in the cooked onions and butter
8. pour over the pizza dough
9. bake at 350 degrees for 40- 50 minutes or until knife comes out clean
10. serve hot , or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: This was a good recipe.  A good snack food to make to eat while watching a game on TV.  Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken vindaloo

for the vegetarian version: use your favorite veggies, omit the cinnamon stick. this is my sister's recipe (thank you najla! xoxo), she made it on the stove top. it's really yummy!!

1. puree first 10 ingredients in a blender
2. pour into the crock pot , add tomato sauce , cinnamon stick and onion and mix well
3. add chicken and turn to cover
4. cook on low for 5 hours
5. sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving
6. serve with rice or rolls , enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was very good and with just the right amount of spice for my family and I.  Will definately make again.  Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy dill dip

it is so creamy and delicious.  good with recipe 109249.

1. in small mixing bowl , combine cream cheese , mayonnaise , sour cream , dill weed , onion and beau monde seasoning
2. blend well
3. cover and refrigerate overnight before serving
demonstrations.review: Very good. Served with prezels. Will definately make again.  Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herb roasted pork loin and potatoes

very good. i got this from an allspice recipe magazine.

1. 1
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
3. 2
4. in a pot with enough water to cover , boil the potatoes for about 10 minutes
5. drain , cool , and place in a bowl
6. toss with olive oil , 1 / 2 teaspoon thyme , 1 / 2 teaspoon garlic powder , chives , salt , and pepper
7. 3
8. rub the pork loin roast with 1 teaspoon thyme , 1 teaspoon garlic powder , and onion powder
9. sprinkle with salt and pepper
10. 4
11. place the roast on a rack in a shallow roasting pan , and cook 50 minutes in the preheated oven
12. arrange the potatoes around the roast , and continue cooking 50 minutes , to an internal temperature of 160 degrees f
13. remove from heat , cover with foil , and let sit 15 minutes before slicing
demonstrations.review: This was very good and will definately make again.  My family enjoyed it a lot.  Thank you for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
harvest pumpkin apple bread

all the flavors of autumn combined into one scrumptious bread. this tastes great with coffee or tea! i make this using egg beaters and unsweetened applesauce in place of half the oil to make it healthier. prep time includes cooling time.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease and flour two 9 x 5-inch loaf pans
3. combine flour , cinnamon , baking soda and salt in large bowl
4. combine sugar , pumpkin , eggs , vegetable oil and apple juice in large mixer bowl
5. beat until just blended
6. add pumpkin mixture to flour mixture
7. stir just until moistened
8. fold in apples
9. spoon batter into prepared loaf pans
10. bake for 65 to 70 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
11. cool in pans on wire racks for 10 minutes
12. remove to wire racks to cool completely
13. to make using three 8 x 4-inch loaf pans: prepare as above and bake for 60 to 65 minutes
14. to make using five or six 5 x 3-inch mini-loaf pans: prepare as above and bake for 55 to 60 minutes
target.review: I substituted half the oil for applesauce.  I didn't have apple juice, so I used water as suggested, and the bread could have been a little sweeter.  Next time, I will make sure to use apple juice.  Also, make sure to grease the loaf pans really well; I thought I had, but the bottoms of both loaves stuck to their pans.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: This banana bread turned out great.  I used five overripe bananas, and though I'm at high altitude (over 6000 ft.), I didn't have to adjust the recipe (e.g. flours, sugars) at all.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai chicken breasts

this recipe actually calls for breasts, but i used thighs and they were moist and lucious! goes well with steamed basamati rice.

1. combine the gingerrot , garlic and red pepper flakes in a cup and set aside
2. mix flour with salt and pepper to taste and dredge chicken pieces in this
3. heat the olive oil in a large skillet
4. saute the chicken until browned on both sides and cooked through
5. remove the chicken and put in a warm dish , set aside in low oven to keep warm
6. add the ginger-garlic mixture to the skillet and saute until lightly browned
7. add the soy sauce , brown sugar , vinegar and fish sauce
8. bring the mixture to a boil
9. reduce the heat and simmer , stirring frequently , until the sauce reduces and thickens
10. pour the sauce over the chicken pieces in the warm serving dish and keep warm until ready to serve
11. trim and shred the sugar snap peas diagonally
12. just prior to serving sprinkle the top of the chicken with the shredded snap peas
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious!  I took other reviewers' suggestions and substituted green onions, sliced diagonally, for the sugar snap peas.  I served these over jasmine rice with a side of edamame.  I'll be making this dish regularly from now on.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paula deen s layered mexican cornbread

this quite possibly might be the best cornbread you will ever have, it bakes out high, light and fluffy, it really should be called a corn cake lol! the jalapenos can be substituted with one small finely chopped green bell pepper, or one 4-ounce can green chilies, drained. since i prefer the taste of olive oil i used that instead of the melted butter, this is a recipe of paula deen's tweeked slightly i think for the better ;-)

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. butter a 8 x 8-inch or a 9 x 9-inch square baking dish
3. in a large bowl mix together cornmeal with flour , sugar baking powder , garlic powder , milk , eggs , seasoned salt and melted butter or oil until well blended
4. add in onion and creamed corn and thawed corn
5. mix to combine
6. pour half the batter into prepared baking dish
7. sprinkle the layer with grated cheese and jalapeno peppers
8. pour the remaining batter on top of the cheese and jalapeno peppers
9. bake for about 35-45 minutes or until golden on top and a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean
10. allow to cool slightly before slicing
demonstrations.review: I made this in a 9" x 9" glass Pyrex baking dish, and I had the same experience as a couple of other reviewers in that the cornbread was far from done at 35 min.  I recommend at least an additional 15 min. Also, make sure to grease the baking dish very well.  The cornbread was very moist and tasted great.  Next time I make this, however, I think I'll sub hot diced green chili for the jalapeno to suit personal tastes.  I served this with turkey chili.  Thanks for sharing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken scaloppine with lemon glaze   low fat and delicious

this is a wonderful lower-fat restaurant-quality dish that is easy to make, i also like to add in a few tablespoons of capers and cook with the lemon glaze if you are a lover of capers then add them in as it really adds to the flavour of this dish ---  this lemon sauce is not a heavy creamy sauce which is what makes this dish lower in fat, it is more like a glaze that soaks into the chicken, and i would strongly suggest to double or even triple the glaze i most always do, and please be certain to use only dry breadcrumbs as fresh will not stick to the chicken as well --- this is *very* good!

1. in a small bowl or shallow dish whisk together mustard and eggs
2. set aside
3. combine the dry bread crumbs with poultry seasoning , garlic powder and seasoning salt
4. spread on a piece of waxed paper
5. dip the breasts firstly in egg / mustard mixture then coat well with the crumb mixture , pressing downs with hands to adhear the crumbs to the breast
6. heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat
7. add in the chicken and cook for about 5 minutes on each side , or until it is no longer pink inside
8. remove and transfer to a plate to keep warm
9. for the glaze
10. in the same skillet add in the broth , lemon juice and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt bring to a boil scraping any brown bits from the pan
11. add in lemon slices and parsley
12. mix to combine for about 1 minute
13. spoon the glaze / sauce over chicken
14. delicious !
demonstrations.review: Good, healthy recipe.  I didn't have any capers, so I omitted that.  I served it over angel hair pasta with spinach salad, bread, and dipping oil on the side.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
szechuan green beans with ground pork

this is a bit spicy so you may want to decrease the pepper flakes and add more at the end for taste. i made this for a pot-luck chinese dinner that is why the serving size is for 8. can be cut in half. delicious over chinese white rice.

1. steam beans 5 minutes
2. combine the first 4 ingredients in a medium bowl
3. heat oil in a large non-stick skillet over med high heat
4. saute pork mixture until pork loses it's pink color - stirring to a crumble
5. add steamed green beans and garlic - saute for 3-5 minutes more
6. combine hoisin sauce , sugar , pepper flakes and soy sauce in a small bowl - stirring with a whisk to incorporate ingredients
7. pour mixture into pan with pork and green beans
8. cook another 3-5 minutes or until heated through , stirring frequently
9. serve over hot rice - enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I've made this twice now, and both times it's turned out fabulous.  It's pretty easy, too!

target.recipe_text:
easy microwaveable peanut butter fudge

i saw this on "good eats" on the food network.
it is easy, delicious and creamy.

1. ) put butter and peanut butter in a microwaveable bowl
2. cover with plastic wrap and microwave on high for 2 minutes
3. remove and pull up plastic wrap and stir thoroughly
4. replace plastic wrap
5. place back in microwave and microwave for 2 more minutes
6. ) remove from microwave and stir in powdered sugar and vanilla extract until mixed thoroughly
7. place in an 8x8 glass dish or metal pan lined with waxed paper , cover with waxed paper and flatten out top
8. place in frig for 2 hours then cut into 1inch squares
9. store in frig
target.review: I have made this.  I will never make any other pnutbtr fudge again.  It is smooth and creamy, has a wonderful flavor and is very easy.  I tried a canned frosting and pnutbtr microwave fudge that turned out more like candy once because it was easy... This is true fudge.  It was perfect.  My family an coworkers make me buy a gallon jar of pnutbtr every Christmas and make this fudge until the jar is gone...Lot of fudge, lotta flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb rich chocolate cake

this was created by barb goldstein from a low carb site. it is very rich and chocolatey and would make a special treat for valentine's day. the main sweetener is splenda and not sugar, and it contains no flour. if you can spare the carbs, top with whipped cream and berries.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. grease 8" inch round cake pan , and cut 8" parchment or wax paper round to fit inside , grease the top of the paper
3. microwave chocolate and butter on high one minute at a time until melted
4. whisk until smooth , then add vanilla , and set aside to cool for a few minutes
5. add eggs , one at a time and beat well
6. add splenda , incorporating until melted in
7. sift in cocoa powder and mix lightly
8. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in the center of the oven for 20 minutes unil a light crust is formed around the edges
9. cool on rack for 5 minutes
10. losen cake around the edges with a knife and invert on serving plate
11. cool completely before serving
12. can top with powdered splenda or whipped cream
demonstrations.review: I agree with Sausage on this cake.  It was very salty tasting and I won't be making it again.  Someone told me that Dutch chocolate will help prevent this... I used unsalted butter and figured I was o.k. but that was not so.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden   fettuccine with shrimp   zucchini

this is a recipe given to me one night when my family ate at the olive garden.

1. cut zucchini into 2 in by 1 / 4 in sticks
2. peel and devein shrimp
3. cook fettuccine according to package directions
4. while pasta is cooking , heat oil in large saute pan over medium heat
5. add chopped garlic and parsley
6. cook for 1 minute
7. add zucchini
8. cook additional minute
9. add shrimp , wine , salt , pepper and butter
10. stir well and cook shrimp for 5 minutes or until they are no longer opaque
11. add drained pasta to the mixture
12. toss all ingredients to mix
13. season with salt and pepper to taste
14. use tongs to pull pasta onto serving platter
15. top with shrimp , zucchini and seasonings
16. squeeze two lemon wedges over dish
17. garnish with remaining wedges and parsley
demonstrations.review: I made this dish last night before I saw recipe.  It was delicious.  I used evoo flavored with basil and sundried tomatoes and left out the parsley.  I also added yellow cauliflower and broccoli and topped with scallions.  I give it a 5 star. Taste was incredible and recipe was quite easy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
santa fe soup

this is so good! it's nice and cheesy and oh so easy to put together. really good with slices of hot cornbread. i got this recipe from my mother who is a wonderful cook. cook time is time it takes to melt the cheese in the soup mixture.

1. brown ground beef with onion
2. drain fat well
3. in a large pot combine ground beef , corn , beans and stewed tomatoes and ro-tel tomatoes
4. cube cheese and add to soup pot
5. stir over low flame until melted and blended
demonstrations.review: Please, please, please list your can sizes!  Believe me a 28 oz can of tomatoes makes a lot different soup than a 4 oz can does.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb sausage gravy

this is thickened with xanthan gum, which you can find in health food stores. be careful with it, as a little bit goes a long way, and it takes just a bit longer to thicken than flour or cornstarch, so do give it time.

1. brown sausage until cooked through and drain any excess fat
2. pour milk over crumbled sausage and season with salt and pepper
3. stir in coffee
4. sprinkle xanthan gum evenly over skillet , and stir over low heat until gravy thickens
demonstrations.review:
I liked the addition of coffee to this recipe.  Xanthan gum is a vegetable fiber and it actually thickens as it cools.  Rather than continuing to cook; I usually add it to room temperature liquid and then add the liquid to my dish just enough to warm it or for the flavors to meld.  Another trick I use with Xanthan gum is to put it in a salt shaker and shake it into my liquid as I am whisking.  This prevents the fiber from clumping.  You can measure then put in your shaker, or you can just estimate your "shake" measure.  I am so used to using it now that I estimate and eyeball it.
Thank you so much for posting low carb recipes, Evelync, I really look forward to trying all of them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb 3 minute chocolate cake

fast and delicious! the soy flour may be substituted with almond flour.

1. blend the flour , cocoa , baking powder , splenda together in a pyrex two-cup baking dish
2. add water , melted butter and egg and blend together thoroughly with a fork
3. cover with plastic wrap and cut a small vent in the top to vent
4. microwave on high for 1 minute or until a knife comes out clean
5. cool a bit and eat warm with whipped cream
demonstrations.review: I used golden flax meal -- same measurement, and added 2 tsp plain yogurt for moisture. This recipe turned out beautifully. For the topping I whipped one cup heavy cream, 1 heaping T cocoa powder and 2 pkts of Splenda with my power stick to a thick, stiff consistancy. Perfect balance to the dense cake and just the right sweetness. The cake cut in half and was perfect for 2 servings. I am already making recipe 263983 South Beach Muffin, which is pretty similar and it turns out great. I imagine "add ins" would work with this recipe, too. Thanks for dessert, Mercy.

target.recipe_text:
shanghai beef

this is actually one of my grandma's recipes. it is one of her newer ones (it's only about 20 years old). she doesn't cook that much anymore which is a pity because she is a great cook.

1. brown beef in hot oil in a skillet for about 5 minutes
2. add water chestnuts , capsicum , scallions , salt and pepper
3. cook 2 minutes longer
4. mix broth , water , soy sauce and cornstarch
5. stir into beef mixture
6. cook and stir until mixture thickens and comes to a full boil
7. stir in rice
8. continue cooking the dish until the rice is soft
9. remove from heat
10. let the dish stand 5 minutes
11. serve with parsley as a garnish
target.review:
i left out the water chestnuts as my family dont like them. 
they loved this meal thank you it was a winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dodo  chocolate holiday  cookies

i didn't know i was in need of a chocolate italian cookie, unitl i read a request for one on the discussion board. i felt a kinship with the recipe and immediately made it.the cookie tasted just like christmas to me. it is a beautiful addition to any cookie tray. kimd supplied this recipe found on the internet.these freeze well or stay for two weeks in a tupperware in the refrigerator.

1. sift the dry ingredients together
2. heat the milk until very warm but not boiling and melt the shortening in the milk
3. let it cool and add in the dry ingredients
4. add the nuts if desired
5. roll in 1-inch balls and bake in a preheated 375 oven for about 12 minutes
6. frost with the following recipe
7. frosting
8. 1-cup confectioners sugar
9. milk
10. 1-teaspoon anise or vanilla extract
11. mix confectioners sugar with enough milk to make the icing spreadable
12. mix in anise or vanilla extract and frost the cookies
demonstrations.review: i am cooking with the kids and trialing cookies for christmas and my kids loved these. they helped me make them and thought they were delicious. many thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pueblo pumpkin muffins

my quest for a good pumpkin led me to a bed and breakfast in nm, called "inn at the paseo." these bake up tall and with a golden orange color with a tender inside.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. mix together oil , sugar , eggs , pumpkin , and buttermilk , and extract
3. add flour , baking powder , baking soda , cinnamon , allspice , and beat until batter is smooth
4. stir in walnuts and raisins
5. spoon into greased muffin tins full and bake 10 minutes , reducing the oven to 350 and bake until toothpick comes out clean , about 15 additional minutes
demonstrations.review: my husband has sworn off of pumpkin for life. Yet he ate 3 of these little beauties and would of kept eating them had i not hidden the rest from him. they are great and my kids loved to help me make them. thank you for a real yummy recipe.. and like heather... i had some for breaky.. oh yum!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweetheart trifle

i love the chocolate/peanut butter taste! i found this in a cooking magazine, it originally called for nestle crunch bars, but i don't care for those, so i decided to use the peanut butter cups. try a different candy bar and find your favorite! i am not positive about the prep time, but it includes chilling.

1. prepare cake mix according to directions , let cool completely
2. in a heavy saucepan , combine chips , 1 / 4 c milk and the whipping cream
3. cook and stir over low heat until chips are melted
4. remove from heat
5. stir in vanilla and cool to room temp
6. place the remaining milk in a mixing bowl
7. beat in the pudding mixes on low speed for 2 minutes
8. to assemble , crumble half the cake into a 4 qt trifle bowl or large bowl
9. layer with 1 / 2 the peanut butter sauce , pudding , whipped topping and then repeat layers
10. at the end , add the crumbled peanut butter cups
11. cool for 3 hours
demonstrations.review: my hubby doesnt like peanut butter so i used choc bits and nestles crunch bars  and it was delious

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caesar chicken wrap

saw this on food tv.  looks delicious with a few different ingredients than the normal caesar salad wrap.

recipe courtesy the big wrap 
show:  $40 a day 
episode:  aspen

1. warm tortillas over a gas flame , in a low temperature oven , or in the microwave
2. in the middle of each tortilla , place 3 ounces grilled chicken , 1 / 2 cup black beans , 1 cup lettuce , 1 tablespoon each pumpkin seeds , feta , and red peppers
3. for dressing
4. add all ingredients to a blender
5. blend until smooth
6. refrigerate until ready to use
7. top wrap with caesar dressing and roll up
demonstrations.review: i left out the pumpkin seeds and black beans but added slices of tomato. it was a really delicous lunch. Just what i needed to surprise my famliy with when they came over for lunch. thank you

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s tuna casserole circa 1949

i remember the first time mother made this casserole, back in 1949. she and i really loved it. so we made it often. even the leftovers are good. in this version, i have doubled her recipe to feed a larger family.

1. bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil
2. cook pasta in boiling water for 8 minutes , or until al dente
3. drain
4. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
5. in a large bowl , thoroughly mix noodles , onion , 1 cup cheese , peas , tuna , soup and mushrooms
6. transfer to a 9" x 13" inch baking dish , and top with potato chip crumbs and remaining 1 cup cheese
7. bake , uncovered , for 15 to 25 minutes in the preheated oven , or until cheese is bubbly
demonstrations.review: this recipe was absolutely delicious. My family don't eat peas so i swapped them for a can of whole corn kernels. there were no left overs and my family are asking for it again. A great way to get fish into your kids diet .. you've won my vote

target.recipe_text:
vietnamese beef pho

this soup is served with a plate full of fresh garnishes as well as various sauces. this allows each person to season their serving to taste. the soup is somewhat unusual, because the meat is cooked in the bowl. the beef is sliced very thin, almost thin enough to see through. you might want to have the butcher slice it for you. the boiling hot broth is poured over the noodles and raw meat. the meat is quickly cooked in the hot broth in the time it takes to garnish the soup. from allrecipes.com

1. in a large soup pot , combine broth , onion , ginger , lemon grass , cinnamon , and peppercorns
2. bring to a boil , reduce heat , and cover
3. simmer for 1 hour
4. arrange bean sprouts , mint , basil , and cilantro on a platter with chilies and lime
5. soak the noodles in hot water to cover for 15 minutes or until soft
6. drain
7. place equal portions of noodles into 6 large soup bowls , and place raw beef on top
8. ladle hot broth over noodles and beef
9. pass platter with garnishes and sauces
target.review:
This is very good recipe.
I love this soup since I went to a Vietnamese restauran.  I crave this soup. I make it 1-2 a week.  
And is so healthy.!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
szechwan style eggplant  aubergine

tasty aubergine dish

1. in a wok or large skillet heat the vegetable oil over high heat until it is hot but not smoking and in it stir fry the eggplant over moderately high heat for 3 to 5 minutes , or until it is tender and browned
2. transfer the eggplant with a slotted spoon to paper towels to drain
3. in a small bowl dissolve the cornstarch in the broth
4. to the wok add the garlic , the gingerroot , the chili paste , the hoisin sauce , the vinegar , and the sherry and stir fry the mixture for 30 seconds
5. add the scallions and stir fry the mixture for 30 seconds
6. add the soy sauce , the brown sugar , the cornstarch mixture , stirred , the bell pepper , and the eggplant and stir fry the mixture for 1 minute , or until the eggplant has absorbed most of the liquid
7. remove the wok from the heat , add the sesame oil and salt and pepper to taste , and toss the mixture well
8. the eggplant mixture may be made 1 day in advance and kept covered and chilled
demonstrations.review: Best recipe I have found!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
puerto rican plantain tostones

a simple appetizer or snack. very tasty.

1. peel plantains and slice into 1 inch thick sections
2. place water , salt and garlic in a large baking pan
3. soak the plantain slices in the garlic mixture for 20 minutes
4. pour oil in a pan set at 365 degrees
5. fry plantains until they are golden brown on all sides
6. flatten each plantain between sheets of wax paper with a plate or the palm of your hand
7. dip flattened plantains into garlic mixture and place on a paper towl
8. place plantains into the oil once again and fry until crispy and golden brown
9. sprinkle with salt to taste
10. serve promptly after frying for best taste
demonstrations.review: I am from PR,  the only thing I do different is I dont soak the plantains in water.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
puerto rican style pernil  roast pork

pernil is roasted pork shoulder, seasoned to the max. it is served with rice and beans or sweet plantains. cold pernil is sliced thin paired with swiss cheese, pickles and ham to make the famous cuban sandwich. i found this recipe online and have made it twice now. i love it and so does my family.

1. in a bowl mix garlic , salt and oregano
2. with a sharp knife make deep cuts in to the pork only on meat side , and stuff the garlic mixture into the slits
3. the more cuts the better the flavor
4. sprinkle the other seasoning the adobo and the sazon all over the outside
5. then rub the seasonings in making sure the entire surface is covered
6. roast the pork in a pre-heated 350 degree oven for 4-6 hours uncovered in a pan with a rack
7. roast the pork skin side down for the first 2 hours and then turn skin side up for the remaining time
8. pork should be well done and tender
9. make sure all juices run clear before removing from oven
demonstrations.review:
this is a great recipe, the trick I use for crispy skin (chicharron) IS 
dont turn it, LEAVE IT ALONE).
i DONT USE SAZON, 
I MAKE A PASTE OF THE SEASONING WITH 3 TBPS OF OIL.
IS SOOO GOOD.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mofongo

monfongo is made by mashing tostones (twice fried plantains) with garlic, olive oil, and chicarrones or bacon.

1. first make tostones: cut plantains in wedges
2. fry until tender
3. flaten with a "tostonera" or with a second cutting board
4. fry for a second time , until light golden
5. using a mortar , crush garlic cloves and add adobo
6. in a medium bowl , mix together the garlic / adobo paste , olive oil and chicharron or bacon
7. mash the tostones , a few at a time
8. add some of the garlic mixture
9. mash tostones in separate bowls
10. this will allow the garlic mixture to spread evenly
11. if too dry , add more oil
12. shape like small balls
13. serve with pork meat , soups , seafood or solo
demonstrations.review:
This is the real thing.
You can also steam the plantains if you dont want to fry them.
I love this with a chicken soup on the side and fried pork chunks.
yummmy!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy asian cucumber salad

i received this via email update from america's test kitchen. i'm looking forward to employing some of our bumper cucumber crop on this.

1. bring vinegar and sugar to boil in saucepan over medium-high heat
2. reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until mixture reduces by half , 5 to 6 minutes
3. transfer to medium bowl and cool to room temperature
4. whisk in lime juice , ginger , chile , and sesame oil
5. toss in cucumbers , scallions , and basil
6. season with salt and pepper , and let sit for 10 minutes or up to 1 hour
7. serve
demonstrations.review:
Awesome, Delicious, Fantaboulus,
I love it!!!

target.recipe_text:
authentic puerto rican rice and beans

this is my family's recipe straight from aguada, puerto rico. in pr we make it from scratch (all the seasoning, but this recipe tastes the same, just easier than the all home-made version. this recipe is easy and serves 4, or 2 if you eat alot!! muy rico, come lo

1. made by goya brand and can be found in the spanish / latin section of your grocery store cook white rice as instructions on package of rice say to
2. make sure when you are done cooking to let excess water out of rice
3. in saucepan , heat oil on low-medium heat and put in the ham , salted pork , or canadian bacon
4. once it starts to sizzle , add the garlic powder and adobo seasoning
5. then add the sofrito and sazon con azafran seasoning , stir
6. next add red beans
7. mix and serve
8. (in puerto rico , it is traditional to serve rice and beans with almost every meal , but mainly with pork chops on the side)
9. enjoy
target.review: i have never seen this recipe without the tomato sauce. i made it as directed except i put tomato sauce in it as did that other poster. it was good. i always wondered what sazon was until one day i was pouring a sazon packet  into my pot and saw it kinda shined.
