"aha MSG!" i thought. i looked on the packet and sure enough MSG! i can't stop using them though. i guess you can't teach an old dog new tricks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s jello salad  strawberry

this dessert/salad brings back such fond feelings.  this is the recipe my grandmother served the kids 2-3 times a year when we were all together.  after she died no one could find her recipe for this.  i guess that is what the internet is for!  when i surprised the family with this recipe at christmas dinner, both my aunt and uncle cried.  i hope your family enjoys this dessert as much as mine has.

1. dissolve jello into boiling water
2. add frozen strawberries and stir until they are thawed and the mixture begins to thicken
3. add mashed bananas and pineapple
4. pour half the mixture into a 9 x 13 pan
5. chill in refrigerater until firm
6. spread sour cream over the top
7. add remaining jello mixture and chill until firm
demonstrations.review: My whole family loves this! I had the recipe and was going to post it but then I searched so I wouldn't post a double and here it is! This is a tradition in my fiance's family to make at Thanksgiving bet we just had it for Easter and I think I want it again at Christmas!!! Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
art s roast beef   anderson  indiana  copycat

shhh!!! this is a secret recipe and i have it on good authority that it's the real deal. problem is, it's just too good to keep to myself! don't ask who let me in on the secret, though, because i'll never tell. :)

1. bake roast in 350 degree oven until done
2. put water , sauce , onion , green pepper and spices in crockpot and allow them to cook on low while beef is baking
3. when beef is done , slice and put in crockpot with sauce
4. let beef cook in sauce for 2 hours
5. serve on french bread
demonstrations.review: Oh Art! You've ruined my diet! These sandwiches are so great! You really must try this recipe. The only things I did differently was to cook it in my crock pot on high until the beef became fall apart tender (after I transferred it from the oven) and used half the amount of pepper flakes. After the meat was done I filled mini sub rolls with the mixture (including the peppers) and sprinkled some mozzarella cheese on top and put the whole thing under the broiler to melt the cheese. I also put some ketchup on mine. It was really really great. The best recipe I have made for a long time. I bet this would be a great addition to any buffet or potluck. Just leave the meat on low and provide the fixins (rolls, cheese, condiments). Thanks! This one is a keeper for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy italian farmhouse chicken

totally healthy and delicious, true!
creativity can be up to you!
colourful, easy...people will think you did slave,
hope your review is also a rave!

1. combine cornflour , dried italian seasoning and pepper in bowl or ziplock bag
2. slice chicken breasts in half lengthways and then in 2 to 3 pieces across
3. flour chicken
4. shake excess off before
5. heat pan
6. then add oil
7. brown chicken and remove
8. saute garlic , onions , mushrooms and red or green pepper until soft
9. add diced zucchini , can of diced tomatoes with juice , red wine , lemon juice , lemon rind and brown sugar
10. bring to a boil , reduce to simmer
11. add chicken back into large pot on stove and simmer for 1 hour until chicken is tender
12. when done , add black olives and
13. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: OK! This is like a hearty chicken stew. I made it with all purpose flour instead of corn flour because that is all I had. I have been eating low fat and low cal for a while now and have been looking for recipes that have lots of flavour but are still healthy. This is it! Exceeded my expectations and I  will make again very soon! The only thing I will be changing is I will be adding more mushrooms and salt.  Thank you so much for posting this wonderful recipe. My mother Loved it too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blackberry cobbler

this is so great. my family can hardly wait for it to come out of the oven. nothing like it.

1. mix blackberries and sugar
2. let stand 20 minutes or until fruit syrup forms
3. mix together flour , baking powder , salt , and milk in ungreased 8 inch square pan
4. stir in butter until blended
5. spread evenly in pan
6. spoon blackberries over batter
7. bake at 375 degrees for 45-55 minutes or until dough rises and is golden
8. serve warm
demonstrations.review:
I made this recipe with REALLY sour blackberries so I used a whole cup of sugar. This was absolutely delicious. My mother said I should use the recipe for other fruits too she loved it so much! Thanks!
QKF

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chickpea cutlets

this is from veganomicon by isa chandra moskowitz and terry hope romero

1. mash the chickpeas and oil together until no whole chickpeas remain
2. add remaining ingredients and knead for 3 minutes until strings of gluten have formed
3. preheat large nonstick skillet over medium heat
4. divide dough into four equal pieces
5. flatten each piece and stretch to roughly 4x6 inches
6. add a thin layer of olive oil to to the pan
7. place cutlets in the pan and cook on each side for 6 to 7 minutes
8. they are ready when lightly brown and firm to the touch
demonstrations.review: I just made these tonight from the book and they are so good. I used their oven method which is to preheat the oven to 375, brush a baking with olive oil, brush both sides of the cutlets with olive oil. Bake them for 20 minutes and then flip the patties and bake for 8-10 more minutes. They are supposed to come out more toothsome and chewy this way. Mine were perfect! I didn't have lemon so I just used a squirt of lemon juice. SO DELICIOUS!

target.recipe_text:
uncle bubba s fried dill pickles

courtesy of pauladeen.com

1. drain the juice from the pickle jar and refill the jar with the garlic powder , hot sauce , and buttermilk
2. marinate the pickles for at least 30 minutes
3. in a dutch oven over medium-high heat , heat the oil to 350 degrees f
4. drain the pickles
5. put the fry mix in a large mixing bowl , and toss the pickles to coat thoroughly
6. shake off the excess mix by tossing lightly in a strainer and deep fry the pickles in batches for 3 to 5 minutes , depending on the size of the spears
7. when golden brown , remove the pickles from the oil with a clean strainer or slotted metal spoon and place on paper towels to drain off any excess oil
8. serve immediately
target.review: This was great! I used the remaining seasoned buttermilk (after I removed the pickles) to batter up some mushrooms too, and they were delicious! I was out of normal hot sauce so I combined some tobasco, some sriracha, and some spicy kimchi juice... it was awesome.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic fried catfish

from southern living magazine, 1982. excellent!

1. combine first 5 ingredients in a large shallow dish
2. sprinkle fish with 1 / 4 teaspoon salt
3. dredge in cornmeal mixture , coating evenly
4. pour oil to a depth of 1 1 / 2 inches into a deep cast-iron skillet
5. heat to 350 degrees
6. fry fish , in batches , 5 to 6 minutes or until golden
7. drain on paper towels
demonstrations.review: Southern Living... how can you ever go wrong with a Southern Living recipe??  The only substitution I made was to replace the wheat flour with gluten-free flour to suit my gluten sensitivity.  The fillets I had from the grocery store were thicker than I usually prefer, and ended up frying them for 10 minutes in my Fry Daddy.  Otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly, and they turned out fabulous.  My 9 year old said "Mmmm!  This tastes just like at a restaurant!"  Thanks Bev.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken mole

the traditional chicken mole is just delicious and this recipe makes it extremely simple to prepare using your crock pot. bhg's slow cooker recipes is the source.

1. in a blender container or food processor bowl , combine undrained tomatoes , onion , nuts , garlic , jalapeno peppers , cocoa powder , raisins , sesame seeds , sugar , salt and spices
2. cover and blend until mixture is a coarse puree
3. in the crock pot , place the tapioca
4. add chicken and then the sauce
5. cover , and cook on low for 9 hours
6. serve with hot cooked rice
7. and sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds
demonstrations.review: I would suggest going with the almonds instead of the pumpkin seeds.  I used the pumpkin seed  option, and there were very hard "shell" like bits in the sauce that were unpleasant and got stuck in our teeth.  Next time I make this I will definitely use almonds.  Otherwise, this tasted very good.  I used 2 fresh jalapeño peppers because I happened to have them on hand, and didn't have any canned.  It was a good amount of spice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lentil casserole with white wine

from fatfree.com, posted by leanne m. reidy.  i love baked lentil and rice dishes as they are so easy to make and taste great.  the wine in this dish gives it a very nice flavor, and i think that a white cheese that goes well with white wine tastes great with it (i used monterey jack but want to experiment with other more gourmet cheeses).  and of course, this recipe is no longer fat free when you cover it with cheese!  this was fully cooked at 1 and 1/2 hours in my oven.

1. combine all of the ingredients in a large bowl
2. pour the mixture into a 1-1 / 2 quart casserole
3. place the casserole into the oven and bake for 1-1 / 2 to 2 hours
4. remove when the casserole is moist but not runny
5. sprinkle with cheese and bake for another five minutes
demonstrations.review: I have made this several times, and it is very good. But I have to warn you, that you MUST stir this several times during cooking. DO NOT just "bake uncovered for 2 hours" or you will be seriously disappointed. All the rice and beans float to the top and dry out/burn. It is a disaster!!! Just don't forget to stir it. LOL (yes, I made that mistake once, it was not pretty.) Otherwise, it is delicious, nutty, fluffy, and very filling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy granola bars vegan  gluten free  egg free  dairy free

i have modified recipe #20184 to fit into our allergen free diet. everyone loves these!! these are free of milk, egg, gluten, corn, soy and so on!! 

sorry about missing changing the directions. i have been tweaking the recipe. everything should be correct now. 

you will have to read labels to be sure that the items you buy are allergen free. this recipe is quite forgiving but using regular rice flour helps them to stick together.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. oil 9x13 baking pan
3. in large bowl , beat sugar and shortening until light and fluffy
4. add honey , egg replace and vanilla
5. beat until smooth
6. in medium bowl , combine flour , gar gum , salt and baking soda
7. blend
8. add flour mixture to sugar mixture
9. mix until well combined
10. by hand mix in chocolate chips , nuts , rice cereal and oats
11. press firmly into pan
12. bake for 20 minutes , until brown
demonstrations.review: Thanks for the recipe, but no-can-do. I've been searching for a granola recipe that is corn free, and I was excited to find this one, but it includes Rice Krispies which contain high fructose corn syrup.  Most of these recipies contain some form of corn: corn syrup, marshmallows, rice krispies, etc. Even sweetened chocolate chips!  :*(  Well, it does look like a great recipe for a gluten-free or vegan diet.  Thanks anyway.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bisquick ham   cheese muffins

these are great breakfast handfuls.  my dh loved them. i wrapped them individually & refrigerated them & he kept snaking on them all day.  easy & good, the best kind. the original is on the bisquick website.

1. heat oven to 400f
2. spray bottoms and sides of 12 regular-size muffin cups with cooking spray
3. beat eggs slightly in medium bowl with fork
4. stir in bisquick mix , milk and oil just until moistened
5. stir in 3 / 4 cup of the cheese and the ham
6. divide batter evenly among muffin cups
7. sprinkle remaining 1 / 4 cup cheese evenly over tops of muffins
8. bake 18 to 20 minutes or until light golden brown
9. immediately remove from pan
10. serve warm
11. wrap and refrigerate any remaining muffins
12. high altitude no changes
demonstrations.review: This is a good "base" recipe, but as-is it is pretty bland.  The second time I made this, I increased the cheese to 2 cups because it seemed a little dry.  That helped (and made 18 muffins rather than 12), but it still needs something.  Next time, I will add some herbs (basil, rosemary, and parsley), and a dash of cayenne and garlic salt.  I think that will give it the complexity it seems to be missing.

target.recipe_text:
spinach   roquefort salad

this french inspired salad utilizes blue cheese, thinly sliced apples, and sunflower seeds to perk up a traditional spinach salad. artisanal cheese works best here as well as a tart apple.  recipe from vegetarian times.

1. make vinaigrette
2. combine vinegar , honey , salt , and pepper in a small bowl
3. whisk in oil and water to emulsify
4. stir in minced shallots
5. make salad
6. place sunflower seeds in medium skillet
7. toast over medium heat 5-6 minutes or until browned and fragrant
8. transfer to small bowl and let cool
9. thinly slice 1 large apple leaving peel on the apple for color
10. use one large tart apple or two small contrasting flavors of apple
11. just before serving , toss baby spinach , thinly sliced apple , crumbled roquefort , and cooled sunflower seeds with vinaigrette
12. divide among salad plates and serve
target.review: My 3 yo boy ate only this all dinner long, and kept saying, "mmm, I love this!" I added one more tablespoon of honey to tame the tanginess of the vinegar (used apple cider vinegar) and add a hint more sweetness. Used honey mustard, omited shallot, omited sunflower seeds, and used 4 small apples, and feta instead of Roq. Great! Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: Delicious. I used a 2:1 ratio of ground beef to turkey sausage and baked one inch sized meatballs for 17 min at 350. They were a hit!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast sticks   oamc

i got this basic recipe from another site but changed it a little for my family.  the original recipe called for orange juice as the liquid instead of milk.  i also added the vanilla as we think it gives it a nice flavor.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. cut each slice of bread into 3 pieces to make sticks
3. texas toast is a very thick sliced bread about 3 / 4" thick
4. you could substitute french bread if texas toast is not available
5. in a bowl , mix together melted butter , eggs , sugar , cinnamon , vanilla and milk
6. beat well
7. dip sticks into egg mixture and place on a cookie sheet that has been sprayed with cooking spray
8. if there is any dip left , you can drizzle it over the sticks
9. bake for 25 minutes on middle rack of oven
10. turn halfway through baking time
11. allow to cool
12. flash freeze on cookie sheet , remove and place in a ziploc bag
13. to reheat: place 3 sticks on a microwave-safe plate and heat on high for 1 minute until warm
14. serve with syrup
demonstrations.review: We all love this, including my 4 yo and 2 yo. I have so far only used orowheat original bread--the regular thin slices--and it's been delicious. I save time by not slicing them until after they are done in the oven. I found the individual dipping so time consuming. But if you are using thick bread, it might need it. I also nearly doubled the cinnamon. I did mine in the oven at 350 for 5-7 min. on each side. Thanks so much for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushroom and pea curry

this mushroom and pea curry is designed to be served as a side with three or four other indian dishes, but i like it served over rice just as well.

1. heat the oil in a large frying pan , until very hot
2. add the cumin seeds and sizzle for 10 seconds
3. add the garlic , mushrooms , ginger and chillies
4. cook , stirring until the mushrooms turn silken
5. put in the ground coriander and garam masala and stir for 30 seconds
6. now add the tomato pure , salt , peas and fresh coriander , and water or stock
7. stir well , bring to a boil
8. cover and simmer for five minutes
9. stir in the sour cream and cook gently for one more minute
10. eat immediately , either over boiled basmati rice or as a side dish with other indian dishes
demonstrations.review: I used fresh mushrooms and also did not need any stock/water. I didn't use chilies but did add some chili powder-minimal since I have toddlers. I used closer to 1/3 c of fresh tomato puree, and added more dry coriander since I didn't have fresh. I used plain yogurt. I ended up wanting more flavor so doubled the cumin, garlic, ginger, cor., and gar. mar. and it turned out great. My 21 month old gobbled it up, as long as the mushrooms were tiny enough.My 3 y old liked the peas part. I served it over brown rice. It's a good dish and maybe I'll make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: We found this pretty average. The vegetables were great. I had put the carrots and rutabaga strips under the roast. We have a 7 quart crock pot. I used 1 1/2c water with half the spices in it, the other half on the roast. Put it on simmer (temp is a little lower than low) for 4 hours and the 3 lb pot roast came out too done. Took out the roast, turned to high and added cornstarch, and made great gravy. Put the sliced roast back in with the veg and gravy and served from the pot.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco ritos

this recipe comes from denver fire fighters favorites cookbook published in 1976. this is a quick and very tasty dish and you can increase ingredients to make a larger batch, if needed. it's always been a big seller in my house.

1. brown ground beef and drain off grease
2. add refried beans
3. remove from heat
4. soften tortilla in microwave for 20-25 seconds
5. place 2 tbspns
6. of ground beef mixture and 1 tspn
7. of onion on tortilla and roll like a burrito
8. place in shallow roasting pan
9. repeat filling and rolling instructions until you fill approximately 8 tortillas
10. mix mushroom soup and green chile enchilada sauce together and pour over rolled tortillas in pan
11. top with both cheeses
12. bake in 375 degree oven for 20 minutes or until cheese is melted and everything is hot
13. allow to stand about 5 minutes
14. serve with toppings , as desired
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! I think next time I will put some cheese inside as well as on the top. I put some sauce under the tortillas before I laid them in the pan, which helped them to stick to the pan less. I think I will decrease the sauce some, maybe 1/3 less, because we had tons. I also sauteed my onions and then stirred them into the meat/bean mix. Thanks for a great recipe! My husband and I and my 3 yo and my almost 2 yo all liked it. The toppings sure were a great idea, adding some fresh crunchy goodness.

target.recipe_text:
parmesan parsley potatoes

nan

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. peel potatoes and starting at one end , slice into approximately one inch slices
3. melt butter in a glass baking dish
4. combine cheese , flour , salt and pepper into ziploc plastic bag
5. put potatoes into bag and shake to coat
6. put coated potatoes into prepared baking dish and bake 30 minutes
7. turn potatoes over and bake for an additional 20 to 25 minutes
target.review: I needed a quick to prepare side dish using some leftover yukon gold potatoes.  I substituted dried chives for the parsley.  Talk about yummy; golden and crispy!  I dove into the potatoes and never even ate my entree! Thanks for a great recipe, I can't wait to make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wicked baked beans

a quick and easy recipe for smokey, tangy-sweet baked beans to accompany anything smoked.  designed to be smoked in a smoker, hey you got the smoker fired up anyway, why not throw on some beans.

while not my original recipe, this recipe has received hundereds of rave reviews.

1. crisp bacon in a skillet , remove , leaving grease in skillet
2. saute' bell pepper , jalapeno , and onion until tender
3. combine all ingredients
4. if mixture looks drier than desired , add additional ketchup
5. pour into a 12x9 aluminum baking pan , or deep 9x9
6. smoke @ 225-250 for 2 1 / 2 hours uncovered
7. remove to oven and bake 1 hour @ 350 , or until beans reach a temp of 160
8. if desired , adjust the heat up or down with peppers , and mustard
demonstrations.review: Made this for a pot luck and it was a huge hit!  I did omit the green bell pepper only because I really don't like it. My cooking method was to heat the beans in a crock pot for about 4 hours on high and they turned out perfect.  Thank you for a recipe that I know I can always count on!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
supper

a big game hunting buddy of my husband's dreamed up this round steak dish. he puts it on before they go out hunting and it's ready when they come in for supper at night. it's very easy to prepare and can cook happily along in a crock as well as the conventional oven. it's a great dish for people who work all day. it's done when you get home-just slice some italian or french bread, throw a green salad together and sit down and enjoy.

1. trim fat from meat
2. sprinkle with minced garlic
3. mix cream soups with water
4. pour over meat
5. sprinkle dry onion soup over top
6. bake 325f oven for about 2 hours , or , place in crockpot in morning , low setting , 6-8 hours
demonstrations.review: A great, easy recipe!  I prepared it then popped it into the oven to cook while I was on the treadmill and the wonderful aromas filled the house.  Only change I made was to add a couple cups of halved fresh mushrooms.  I served it with whole wheat couscous and the results were so delicious.  Happily, I have enough for lunch today!  Thanks for an excellent recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pulled pork and bbq sauce

this is a thinner southeasten style pulled pork sauce that is designed to either be incorporated into pulled pork shreds, or as a drench on a pulled pork sandwich. it is very sweet and tangy.
be careful with the cloves, some are much stronger than others.  also, cayenne may be added for a little heat if desired.

1. combine all ingredients except butter and soy in saucepan
2. simmer 30 minutes stirring often
3. add butter and soy
4. stir until butter is incorporated
5. may be tossed into freshly pulled pork , or used on pulled pork sandwiches
6. to build the perfect pulled pork sandwich , put a slice of onion on a slice of white bread , add a layer of pulled pork , drench with sauce , repeat , cover with a slice of white bread , then pig out , mmmmessssy , but delish
demonstrations.review: The photo of the bbq'd bacon cheeseburger got to me.  Just HAD to try this sauce.  It's even better than it looks/sounds!  Next time I'll make a double batch! It's almost gone already and I just made it last night.  Dipped a patty melt in it for breakfast and will pour it over pork roast for lunch; YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dirty shrimp in butter beer sauce

herby, spicy shrimp with a kick, in a buttery-beer "sauce". fast, easy and delicious, serve as an appetizer, or a dinner over rice or with lots of crusty french bread to soak up all the tasty, herbalicious sauce!

1. saute garlic and herbs in butter until garlic is slightly browned
2. add shrimp , stirring constantly , until shrimp are pink and done
3. pour in beer , simmer 1 minute more , and serve !
demonstrations.review: I came across this recipe sort of by accident; was looking for a use for some precooked prawns in the freezer.  This was the perfect recipe for those little critters!  Between two of us we used almost a whole loaf of french bread for the sopping.  Can't wait to make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken souiza cornbread bake

this is one of our favorties and is a great crowd pleaser!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. grease 9x13 inch baking dish
3. melt margarine in a small skillet over med-high heat
4. saute onion and garlic until tender , 4 to 6 minutes
5. set aside
6. in a large bowl , combine corn , cream style corn , salt and eggs
7. beat in muffin mix
8. fold in cooked onion mixture
9. pour into prepared baking dish
10. in a large bowl , combine chicken , green chiles , sour cream , salt and pepper
11. spoon over corn mixture to within 1 inch from edge
12. sprinkle top with cheese
13. bake in preheated oven for 35 to 40 minutes , or until edges are golden brown
demonstrations.review: I'm so glad I tried this recipe because it is absolutely delicious!  Used two whole eggs in lieu of the substitute, and one fresh jalapeno pepper instead of the canned chilis.  Can't wait to have some of the leftovers for lunch; it is so savory and truly a "comfort" dish!

target.recipe_text:
barbecued country ribs

one of my families favorite

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees place ribs in a 13" x 9" baking dish season with salt and pepper combine remaining ingredients
2. pour mixture over ribs bake at 325 degrees for 30 minutes
3. turn ribs
4. bake 1 to 1 1 / 2 hours longer , until tender
5. skim off fat and spoon remaining sauce over ribs
target.review: Thank you for a great recipe.  Very easy to put together and the taste was great.  Will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german chocolate cake mix cookies

got this from the back of the cake mix box.i bought the mix just for the recipe. course i love anything chocolate, so my fate was sealed

1. pre heat oven to 350
2. mix all ingredients together
3. drop by teaspoon onto ungreased cookies sheet
4. bake for 10-12 minutes
5. let cool for for 2 minutes and remove
6. hide them , they will disappear !
demonstrations.review: These were fabulous.  I took some to work and everyone loved them.  They are just the right texture.  Gooey and chocaltey...who could ask for more.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lazy ravioli lasagna

this fast dish tastes like lasagna but is much easier! you can use cheese, spinach or beef ravioli.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. brown and strain beef
3. cover the bottom of a 9 x 13 pan with sauce
4. layer 1 / 2 of the frozen ravioli , 1 / 2 of the beef and 1 / 3 of the cheese in the pan
5. pour another layer of spaghetti sauce and repeat layers
6. save some cheese for the top , if you wish
7. bake uncovered for 45 minute or until heated all the way through
demonstrations.review: I have made this exactly as written and it is great.  My husband doesn't like red sauce so I have also made a variation of this recipe with sausage, alfredo sauce and cheddar cheese on top.  Either way, this recipe is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage gravy

this is a really easy and super deelicious recipe for sausage gravy over biscuits, you will want to make this one again and again!

1. cook sausage in skillet
2. drain fat
3. sprinkle flour over sausage and stir well
4. cook flour and sausage together for about 5 - 7 minutes
5. add milk
6. cook over medium heat until thickened
7. add pepper
8. serve over biscuits
demonstrations.review: I made this for my husband and he really enjoyed them.  It was so easy to make and had a lot of taste to it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awful potatoes

we called them awful potatoes in the hopes that others wouldn't try them and there would be more left for us. unfortunately, everyone in the family is on to us and digs right in.

1. cook potatoes in salted water until done
2. drain and put back into the pan
3. add sour cream , cream cheese and garlic salt
4. mash
5. turn into baking dish
6. sprinkle cheddar cheese on top
7. bake in a 350 degree fahrenheit oven for 45 to 50 minutes until puffed and golden brown
demonstrations.review: This was a wonderful dish.  My dh liked it alot.  Next time I think I will put bacon in it before baking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french bread rolls to die for

the title says it all! prep time does not include rising time.

1. mix together warm water , yeast and sugar and let stand for about 10 minutes
2. in large bowl , combine yeast mixture with oil , salt and 2 cups of the flour
3. stir well to combine
4. stir in remaining flour 1 / 2 cup at a time , beating well after each addition
5. turn out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic
6. lightly oil a large bowl and place dough in and turn to coat with oil
7. cover with cloth and let rise in warm place until doubled , about 1 hour
8. deflate the dough and turn out onto floured surface
9. divide dough into 16 equal pieces and form into rounds
10. place rolls onto lightly greased baking sheet at least 2" apart
11. cover rolls with cloth and let rise until doubled , about 40 minutes
12. preheat oven to 400 degrees and bake rolls for 18 to 20 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: These were wonderful.  My picky children loved them.

target.recipe_text:
irish potatoes  candy

there are no potatoes in this candy, they're just called that for some reason. these are very yummy and sweet, especially to coconut lovers. i got this recipe from my teacher in school, he would make these with the 6th and 5th grade on st. patrick's day. i'm not positive on the number of servings though.

1. mix cream cheese , sugar , and butter
2. mix in salt and vanilla
3. add coconut and gradually add milk until is in rolling consistency
4. form into balls
5. put a small amount of cinnamon in the plastic bag and put 2 or 3 balls into the bag
6. close the bag and shake a few times , make sure that he balls get covered with cinnamon
7. add more cinnamon to the bag if needed
8. take them out of the bag and add 2 ot 3 more , and repeat by shaking the bag until all the balls are done
9. enjoy !
target.review: My daughter made these for a white elephant gift along with another candy. They easy, quick and good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my crock pot spaghetti sauce

this is a spaghetti sauce recipe that i've developed over time. you may alter the ground meat as you please; sometimes i use all ground beef when i find a good sale but half beef/half pork is pretty tasty. my crock pot is my best friend at times when i'm having busy days at work but still want a decent meal on the table for my family. i serve spaghetti with crusty bread and a romaine salad. cook time is the crock pot cooking time. this recipe is for a 4 quart crock pot, halve it if your pot is smaller.

1. brown meats and onion in a skillet and drain well
2. transfer to your crock pot
3. add remaining ingredients and mix well
4. cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours
5. serve over hot spaghetti noodles
demonstrations.review: My family enjoyed this recipe very much. It is the only one we use now.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate toffee candy cookies  saltine candy

this simple candy shows up at all of my family gatherings .this recipe is quick and easy. the saltines may sound like a strange addition to something sweet, but i have never known anyone who made this recipe just once!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. cover cookie sheet with a single layer of saltines
3. boil butter , sugar , and vanilla for one minute
4. pour evenly over saltines
5. if needed , gently spread to make even
6. bake for 7 minutes
7. while toffee is still hot and bubbly , pour chocolate chips evenly on top of candy
8. when the chocolate chips begin to melt , gently spread chocolate over toffee
9. freeze for one hour
10. break into pieces and enjoy !
11. i have sprinkled nuts and / or drizzled white chocolate over the top of this candy to make it even better , but the basic recipe is outstanding as well
12. you can also change the type of chocolate that you use in the chips
13. white chocolate chips and milk chocolate both work , but make the candy incredibly sweet
demonstrations.review: My daughter made these for her white elephant gift they were easy, quick, and good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic herb burgers

a little surprise will greet you when you bite into these succulent burgers hot of the grill. you can make each recipe ahead of time and refrigerate the burgers for 24 hours or freeze them, tightly wrapped for 1 month

1. place the ground beef in a large mixing bowl , add 1 tbs of the soup mix and mix it in well
2. shape the hamburger into 12 1 / 2" thick patties in a medium mixing bowl , beat together the cream cheese , remaining soup mix and the green onions place 1 tbs of the cream cheese filling on a patty , and then cover with another patty , sealing the edges together
3. refrigerate the hamburgers for at least 1 hour before cooking
4. to freeze: flash freeze uncooked on a cookie sheet until solid then put into a ziplock bag or vacuum seal quantity desired
5. to cook: thaw in refrigerator and grill as usual
demonstrations.review: I didn't pay attention while making these burgers and just mixed everything together. Everybody liked them anyway. Next time I will remember to make a filling instead and try them that way.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian hamburgers

these tasty seasoned hamburgers are topped with tomato sauce and parmesan cheese. they make a quick and delicious meal. serve alone or over pasta.

1. combine the first seven ingredients
2. add beef and 3 tblsp
3. of parmesan cheese
4. mix well
5. shape into six patties
6. in a skillet , brown patties for 2 minutes on each side
7. combine the tomato saude and italian seasoning
8. pour over patties
9. reduce heat
10. cover and simmer for 10-15 minutes or until meat is no longer pink
11. sprinkle with remaining cheese
12. serve patties and sauce alone or over pasta if desired
demonstrations.review: I made these yesterday with two other burgers all went down very nicely. I use a mixture of ground beef, ground turkey and tvp in equal parts. Also with this recipe I put a small amount of Mozerella cheese in the middle. Next time I will leave out the green peppers since some of us here do not like them

demonstrations.recipe_text:
teriyaki pork chops  oamc

this recipe is very tasty and easy to make.  it's great having the chops in the freezer for an easy meal.  the recipe comes from 30 day gourmet.

1. combine all the ingredients except the pork chops in a pan and bring to boil
2. cook for 5 minutes
3. cool completely
4. when the marinade is completely cool , place the chops in a labeled freezer bag
5. pour the marinade over the chops and close the bag
6. make sure the marinade has reached all the pork chops
7. label , seal and freeze
8. to serve: thaw completely in the refrigerator
9. grill chops , discarding marinade , until completely cooked , about 7 or 8 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: Everybody loved this. I put all the ingredients in a freezer bag and the got it out the night before and then cooked it over charcoal grill. I made two sets so we can have it again later this month.

target.recipe_text:
the elvis

this is said to be elvis's favorite sandwich and i know i love it.

1. preheat a grill or griddle over medium heat
2. spread butter on one side of each slice of bread
3. spread the peanut butter on the other side of each slice of bread
4. slice the banana lengthwise to make 4 thin pieces and place on top of peanut butter on one slice of bread
5. top with bacon slices and thendrizzle with honey
6. place the sandwich on the griddle and cook about 3 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy
7. slice in half and serve and enjoy
target.review: Priscilla Presley has publicly stated that Elvis Did Not eat bacon in his PB & Banana sandwich! This was added by folks mainly after his death to poke fun at his increased weight.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot cocoa 1962

this is from frys cocoa powder can, the only difference is that i add the cornstarch which adds creaminess. i also add a pinch of cinnamon sometimes, to add another element of flavour.

1. blend the cocoa powder , sugar , cold milk and cornstarch together well
2. in a saucepot heat the one cup milk , to simmering point , and stir in the ingredients , and cook for one or two minutes , until dissolved and hot
3. stirring well
4. pour into cup , top with mallows or whipped cream
demonstrations.review: This is awesome! If you add the cinnamon like andy suggests, and froth it tastes just like Mexican Hot Chocolate. I've even added both the cinnamon and a small pinch of chili powder for that Aztec flavor. This should be your basic Hot Chocolate mix, not that store bought stuff! Way to go Andypandy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fish chowder

this is the best new england fish chowder ever. it is my mom's recipe. she is the best cook. it is simple and filling. whenever we came home from school and knew this was cooking it was a joyful day. hope you like it.

1. cook chopped bacon and onion in large pot
2. cook slowly
3. onion should be soft but not brown
4. remove onion and bacon from pot
5. set aside
6. leave 2 tablespoons bacon fat in pot
7. put potatoes in same pot
8. add just enough water to cover
9. cook 5-10 minutes
10. add fish to pot
11. cook until fish is flaky
12. remove skin from fish
13. thicken with flour mixed with a little water
14. bring to a boil
15. reduce heat until no longer boiling
16. add milk , bacon and onion
17. heat but do not boil
18. salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: This is very much like my family's recipe, except we use salt pork cut into lardons instead of the bacon. I like to add a can of peas, or sometimes a can of cream corn as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornflake penuche

this is a very crispy and crunchy candy. the trick to this candy is to keep the candy in the pan, covered loosely with wax paper for 2 days before you eat it. if you try it too soon, it will be tough and chewy.

1. spray a 8x8x2 pan with cooking spray
2. line the pan with aluminum foil and spray again
3. in a 4 quart saucepan over low heat , melt butter
4. add sugar and stir well with wooden spoon until sugar is dissolved
5. stir and slowly add evaporated milk
6. keep the heat on low and add the cornflakes
7. stir until well mixed
8. remove from heat and press into prepared pan
9. cover loosely with waxed paper
10. let stand for 48 hours in cool dry place
11. do not refrigerate
12. turn candy out on smooth surface
13. remove foil
14. break into eating-size pieces
15. store in airtight container for no more that 3-4 days
demonstrations.review:
Delicious and wonderful. I made it just as described, and it was a hit! 
The next batch I added a small pinch of Kosher salt to counter the sweetness.
Both batches were great. 
I can see adding chocolate chips or coconut to boost the flavor.
All around a great recipe Corn Flake Candy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice porridge with fresh eggs

good for unhappy bellies! i like it savory, so i eat this with soy sauce and sesame oil, but you can try it sweet as well.

1. combine rice , water and salt in a saucepan
2. bring to a boil , then reduce heat to a simmer
3. let simmer for anywhere from 30-45 minutes , stirring occasionally to keep the rice from sticking to the bottom
4. when the consistency is to your liking , crack the two eggs into a cup and whisk well to combine whites and yolks
5. slowly pour a thin stream of egg into the rice
6. stir the rice quickly for a well-combined , custard-like porridge or slowly for thin ribbons of cooked egg , like an egg drop soup
7. simmer another minute or two until the egg is cooked thoroughly , drizzle soy sauce and / or sesame oil on top then serve
demonstrations.review: This was very good. Any excuse I have to add another porridge recipe to my collection is fine with me. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potsie s famous fried bolony sandwich

i was raised on fried bolony sandwiches. i remember eating a simple version while strapped to my booster seat as a little boy. i outgrew my booster chair many years ago and i have modified the ingredients for a more adult palette... but i still love a fried bolony sandwich.

1. it ain't rocket science or quantum physics
2. just make the sandwich
3. i like to fry them until they are just a little blackened but still plenty greasy
4. if the grease doesn't drip down your arm and off your elbows then you have overcooked it
demonstrations.review: Fantastic! This is also how I make a grilled cheese. I fry the bologna, assemble the sandwich with American Cheese (NOT that Kraft yellow stuff, the REAL stuff, the white one, from the Deli). Then grill the whole shebang till GB&D. I like to serve with thousand island dressing as a dipping sauce.

target.recipe_text:
the last peanut butter cookies recipe you ll ever try

these are the most amazing cookies. they are crispy on the outside, soft on the inside and freeze so well. you can't even tell they were frozen! the best part - they are drop cookies, no shaping necessary. if you love nuts, use crunchy peanut butter and add the nuts, if not, use creamy pb and 2 cups of peanut butter chips. cook time is for one batch. dough keeps well in fridge so you can bake a batch every day and have fresh cookies!

1. cream peanut butter and margarine , add sugars and mix well
2. add eggs and mix until creamy
3. add remaining ingredients
4. chill for one hour-i usually skip this step and chill between batches
5. drop by teaspoonful onto cookie sheets- do not flatten
6. bake at 325f for 15 minutes
7. cool on cookie sheets for about 5 minutes then transfer onto newspaper- the newspaper soaks up extra grease so the cookies don't become crumbly , little trick i learned from my mil- this is also optional
8. edited to add - immediately after the cookies are completely cooled i always transfer them to an airtight container
9. several posters have mentioned the cookies get hard if you leave them out
10. i have never had that problem - these cookies have always stayed soft and moist if they are stored in an airtight container
target.review: Very good cookies, but there wasn't as much of a peanut butter taste as I had hoped.  Furthermore, after a day of being sealed in an air-tight tupperware, the cookies got hard.  Good cookies, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Excellent! I let it bake for 65 minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thick  soft  and chewy chocolate chip cookies

i moved out of the house in 1992 but my dad still insist i make his chocolate chip cookies for him. after much searching these are the ones we deemed "best". soft and chewy but with a lightly crisp outer layer. if you don't want the crispness, substitute more butter for the shortening. 

i have found that you need to follow the directions *exactly* to get the best cookies. not using real butter or all brown sugar, not beating the eggs in one at a time, not baking them at a higher temp than the "traditional" recipe, all make a difference in the end result. 

i have also found that land o' lake butter makes a better cookie than some generic brand butter. don't let the butter sit out too long. it needs to soften but if it sits until the moisture starts to separate from the butter, it is too soft and it will affect the resulting cookies. if that happens, refrigerate the dough for about an hour to help them not spread as much. it also helps to use the mixer on the dough in between batches going into the oven. it helps keep the dough from starting to separate if it is a warm day. 

another thing i've learned is you have to make sure there is plenty of circulation in your oven. when i moved, my cookies started turning out flat again. i finally realized that my oven was smaller at the new house and when i switched to smaller cookie sheets, my cookies turned out perfectly!

1. mix flour , baking soda , and salt in a small bowl
2. in a separate bowl , beat butter and shortening until creamy
3. add sugar and vanilla and beat with a mixer on medium speed until well blended
4. beat in eggs , one at a time , mixing well
5. add flour mixture , and beat slowly to incorporate , then beat to blend well
6. stir in chocolate chips and nuts
7. drop batter in 2-tablespoon portions about 2 inches apart on baking sheets
8. bake in a 375f preheated oven until edges of cookies are brown but an area about 1 inch wide in the center is still pale , about 10 minutes
9. if using 2 pans in 1 oven , switch positions at half-time
10. let cookies cool on pan about 5 minutes , then transfer to racks with a spatula
11. serve warm or cool
demonstrations.review: Like other bakers here, I have tried a plethora of chocolate chip cookies.  This is definitely the best recipe, and I will be sticking to it for a long time.  The baking time and temperature were perfect.  I did not find it necessary to flatten out the cookies before baking.  I find that they spread out sufficiently while cooking.  Letting them rest on the baking sheet for another ten minutes (while the second batch is baking), also helps them achieve the desired texture.  Thanks-these were great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dill and sour cream potato salad

a different twist on "traditional" potato salad, this one is simple to make and delicious to eat. cooking time includes overnight refrigeration.

1. put potatoes in a large pan , cover with water , and boil until tender
2. drain , and cut into bite-sized pieces , leaving skins on
3. combine remaining ingredients in a large bowl
4. add hot potatoes , and mix until well coated
5. refrigerate overnight before serving
demonstrations.review: This is my favourite potato salad recipe.  I love the taste of new potatoes, so I never want to overpower them with dominant flavours including mayo, eggs, and relish.  The mayonnaise in this recipe is subdued by the sour cream, giving it a nice, light flavour.  The addition of dill is perfect.  I make this all the time!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german chocolate icing

this is a recipe from my mom and the cake has always been a real hit when i make it. i do double this when i make it as i like a lot of icing on my cake.

1. put butter in a sauce pan and let it melt
2. add milk , sugar , vanilla and whisk in egg yolks
3. cook and stir over medium heat until mixture starts to bubble and then cook for about nine minutes stirring constantly
4. pour over coconut and pecans and mix
5. i usually put the nuts and coconut in a metal bowl and then poor the hot mixture over them to help with cooling
6. if you are in a hurry , put the mixture in the refrigerator stirring occasionally until it is cool and thick enough to ice your cake
7. i find that box cakes are just fine for this
demonstrations.review: Excellent icing!  The only additional thing I would point out is that the canned milk in the recipe is evaporated milk. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
loaded potato skins

i have gotten addicted to these! its a mix of other potato skin recipes with my own additions.

1. preheat oven to 475f
2. cut potatoes in half lengthwise , scoop out flesh leave a inch shell
3. place on a greased or lined baking sheet
4. mix together the oil , salt , pepper and paprika and brush all over the skins
5. bake in the oven for 7-8 minutes skin side up
6. turn over and bake again for 7-8 minutes
7. in the meantime mix together: cheddar cheese , red pepper , and chives
8. mix together in another bowl the garlic , mustard , hot sauce , sour cream and the egg , and then combine with the mix above
9. divide this mixture into the skins , sprinkle with bacon , return to the oven and bake for about 4-5 minutes
10. very nice served with more sour cream and green onions
demonstrations.review: Awesome potato skins. Everyone loved them-thanks!

target.recipe_text:
crab salad sandwiches

no this doesn't use real crabmeat but we think it is delicious nonetheless.

1. add the crabmeat , mayonnaise , green onions , and celery to a large mixing bowl
2. stir to combine
3. add the cheese , and salt / pepper to taste
4. stir to combine
5. spread the crab mixture over the bottom of the bread
6. replace top of bread
7. wrap sandwich in a big piece of heavy foil
8. bake at 400 for 20 minutes or until heated
9. cut into slices and serve
target.review: Oh so wonderful. I will be making this my number one Crab Salad.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef roast

very tender, very juicy. makes lots of gravy great over mashed potatoes simple to make. melts in your mouth everyone who's tried this recipe agrees you won't find an easier or better tasting beef roast recipe anywhere.

1. mix gravy , mushrooms , soup mix and italian dressing
2. pour over beef roast
3. bake , covered , for 1 hour 15 minutes per pound at 300f
4. add carrots and / or potatoes during last hour , if desired
5. cooking time is approximate , depending upon how big your roast is
demonstrations.review:
This was very good . The roast was very moist and tender. I used a slow cooker added potatoes and carrots.
Highly recommend this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
should be illegal oven bbq ribs

after not being able to find restaurant ribs that satified my hot sweet appetite, i carefully attempted various combinations of flavors until i found one that i and my family thought was perfect. hope you enjoy them too.

1. place all ingredients together in large roasting pan
2. cut ribs apart for easier serving
3. mix together making sure to coat all ribs with this semi-dry paste
4. spread ribs out evenly on bottom of pan
5. cover lightly with foil
6. bake at 375 degrees for approximately 1 hour
7. turning or stirring occasionally
8. you can use broiler for these ribs , just watch more closely , and adjust cooking time
9. these ribs are also great finished on the grill for a few minutes on each side
demonstrations.review: OH SO GOOD Loved it

demonstrations.recipe_text:
upside down fresh peach cobbler

a delicious, fast and easy dish, using fresh or canned fruit. a family favorite , handed down through the generations.

1. heat the peaches in saucepan with 1 / 2 cup sugar , til good and hot
2. melt butter in 2 qt baking dish
3. mix dry ingredients for batter
4. add 3 / 4 cup milk , beating until all the lumps are gone
5. pour batter onto melted butter
6. do not stir !
7. spoon hot peaches onto the batter
8. do not stir !
9. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes , or until top is golden brown
10. the batter will have risen to the top , making a beautiful golden crust
11. serve warm with cream or ice cream
12. delish !
13. this is also good with plums , boysenberries , apricots etc
demonstrations.review: This is so easy to make. An amazing, delicious Will definitely make it again!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger steak

very easy to make and simmered until it melts in your mouth. the gravy is delicious and goes well with potatoes, noodles or rice. 
this could also be eaten on a toasted bun, topped with the onions and some of the thickened sauce.

1. mix hamburger , 1 / 4 cup flour , garlic powder , salt and pepper
2. form into 4 square patties and brown
3. add onions to pan and saute
4. remove patties and onions from pan
5. mix 1 / 4 cup flour and water in pan
6. add beef cubes stir and heat until thickened
7. add salt , pepper and a little browning sauce if desired
8. add patties and onions back to pan and simmer for 30-45 minutes
9. serve with potatoes , noodles , or rice
10. if sauce is to thick or boils down add a little more water as it simmers
demonstrations.review: One of the best hamburger steaks I have had in a long time. Very easy to make. For the gravy I used a 12 oz.bottle of Heinz Bistro Au Jus with a 1/4 cup of flour and added a half of jar water salt and pepper to taste. Enjoyed this recipe very much thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast beef slather

also adds to the flavour of gravy made from pan drippings, or slice potatoes about 1/4 inch thick and place around roast for last 45 minutes of roasting, rub slices into pan residue around roast.
this slather is particularly good with recipe #27007.

1. this is enough for about a 3 lb roast and acts quite well as a tenderizer , and leaves a wonderful taste
2. increase ingredients for a larger roast
3. combine all ingredients
4. whisk together till well blended
5. smother entire roast with mixture , rub well into roast
6. let stand 15 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Never heard of a beef slather till I seen this recipe.Everyone loved It.One I  will be useing in the future.It left a very wonderful taste to the meat very easy to make.

target.recipe_text:
chicken breast with honey balsamic glaze

4 pts from ww 2004 annual recipes for success

1. combine first 3 ingredients
2. sprinkle over both sides of chicken
3. heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
4. add chicken
5. cook 7 to 8 minutes on each side or until chicken is done
6. transfer chicken to a platter
7. keep warm
8. reduce heat to medium-low
9. add vinegar and honey to pan
10. simmer 1 minute or until glaze thickens
11. stir constantly
12. pour glaze over chicken
target.review: I have made this several times and my guy loves it. I make it with Agave Nectar since I usually have that on hand instead of honey and it turned out great. I agree with other reviewers, I make extra glaze to go over the white rice. Next time I am going to try cutting my chicken into strips and serve with rice, spinich salad, and extra glaze.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanilla  buttercream frosting  from sprinkles cupcakes

my sister got this buttercream frosting off the box of a sprinkles cupcake mix, made famous by oprah.  my sister said this was amazing.  update:  i have finally gotten around to making this myself.  i will say, that i don't like my desserts overly sweet and. though this was very good, i think i would probably decrease the amount of sugar for my personal taste.  i'm glad everyone else has liked it as-is, though.  :)

1. in a bowl add sugar then add butter
2. beat till blended
3. next add salt
4. then add the milk and vanilla and beat for an additional 3 to 5 minutes or until smooth and creamy
demonstrations.review: I have been making this with Devil's food chocolate cake for birthdays and it hands down the creamiest, best frosting to go with devils food cake. P.S. to replace the liquid in my CAKE recipe I use cold strong coffee...delish

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato salad with chipotle peppers a man s salad

warning warning !! this tex mex salad is very spicy !!!  use your best judgment in how much chipotle peppers you use. taste as you add just don't dump them all in. each pepper has it's own heat level. yes us girls love it too! ;)

1. mix first 7 ingredients together
2. toss in remaining ingredients except 1 tablespoon bacon and salt and pepper
3. mix well
4. taste to see if you need to add salt and pepper
5. i myself like lots of pepper
6. top with bacon bits
7. chill& serve
demonstrations.review: Instead of scallions I used red onion finely diced in my cuisinart food prep. I also made extra dressing and let this sit over night then added my crumbled bacon to garnish. Fabulous, the family loved it with BBQ chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
devils food cake 1948 version

this is very moist, and takes on a bit of a red hue after cooling. you may use your favorite icing, the icing listed is my favorite, quick and tasty.

1. mix water , cocoa and baking soda , let stand while preparing the rest of the ingredients
2. cream butter and sugar , beat in eggs , add half the flour and half the milk beat well
3. add the cocoa mixture and remaining flour and milk and vanilla
4. bake in two greased and floured cake pans , at 350f for 30 minutes or until cake tests done
5. frost with icing:2 cups powdered sugar , 1 tsp vanilla , 1 / 2 to 3 / 4 cup milnot
6. beat milnot canned milk into powdered sugar a little at a time until spreadable
7. add vanilla
demonstrations.review: I use 1/2 c. cold, STRONG, coffee instead of water, and instead of 1/2 c. cocoa I add 3/4 c. If you don't have buttermilk you can sub with 3/4 c. milk plus 2 t. lemon juice or vinegar that sits for 10 minutes before using. Make this with Sprinkles Vanilla Buttercream frosting and it is perfect for a birthday.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fannie farmer s classic baked macaroni   cheese

to me fannie farmer's recipe is the only "real" macaroni & cheese. it's from my 1946 edition of "fannie farmer's boston cooking school cookbook". with time on it's side - this recipe is hands down the best for traditional, homemade baked macaroni & cheese - comfort food.

please note: if you use cheap cheese you will end up with a bland and flavorless dish!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cook and drain macaroni according to package directions
3. set aside
4. in a large saucepan melt butter
5. add flour mixed with salt and pepper , using a whisk to stir until well blended
6. pour milk and cream in gradually
7. stirring constantly
8. bring to boiling point and boil 2 minutes
9. reduce heat and cook 10 minutes
10. add shredded cheddar little by little and simmer an additional 5 minutes , or until cheese melts
11. turn off flame
12. add macaroni to the saucepan and toss to coat with the cheese sauce
13. transfer macaroni to a buttered baking dish
14. sprinkle with breadcrumbs
15. bake 20 minutes until the top is golden brown
16. (you can also freeze this recipe in zip-lock bags for later use - once you have mixed the macaroni along with the cheese sauce allow to cool to room temperature before adding to your freezer - i generally pull it out the night before and allow macaroni and cheese to reach room temperature
17. i then add the macaroni and cheese to a buttered baking dish , sprinkle with bread crumbs and then bake for 20 to 30 minutes , until golden brown on top and bubbling
demonstrations.review: There are probably easier, less adaptable, and flavorful recipes out there but I prefer this classic mac & cheese dish served with Paula Dean's Basic Meatloaf. Definitely use a good, rich cheese for flavor or it will be bland. I make this in a casserole dish sprinkled with Italian Breadcrumbs for texture.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey sausage and bell peppers weight watchers style

recipe comes from the new cookbook by weight watchers.
2 points per serving
serve with salad and garlic bread.

1. spray large skillet with pam cooking spray and heat skillet
2. add sausage and stir frequently until no longer pink 5-6 minutes
3. add bell peppers , onion , broth , garlic , pepper flakes and oregano
4. saute all together for 5 minutes or until liquid evaporates
5. reduce heat and simmer covered 5 minutes more
demonstrations.review: I make this just as listed, but I serve on top of baked potatoes, or whole wheat rotini pasta from Trader Joe's or Whole Foods. My guy loves it. Can't tell at all it is WW. Super tasty

target.recipe_text:
julie s bean dip or refried beans

easy and delicious!  the cream cheese and green onions really make this dish special.  this was originally a bean dip recipe, but we like it so much we serve it as refried beans too.

1. mix ingredients together and heat in the microwave until everything is melted and mixed well
2. if serving as a dip , place in crockpot on warm
3. tastes even better if you make it up ahead of time , refrigerate 'til needed then reheat
target.review: This was really yummy. My husband and I are on a diet, so I made it with all "Fat Free" ingredients and cut out 70 calories a serving : ) and practically no fat!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate strawberry shortcake

the perfect summer dessert. not your ordinary strawberry shortcake!

1. wash , stem , and cut strawberries in half
2. add sugar
3. toss to mix well
4. chill
5. beat cream cheese and powdered sugar well
6. fold in whipped topping and cake cubes
7. spread cake into an ungreased 13x9 dish
8. cover and chill for at least 2 hours
9. cut cake into squares
10. top with strawberries
demonstrations.review: Wowwy, Wow, Wow! Definately the best Strawberry Shortcake I've ever eaten!  I couldn't put it down. Thank you!  I'll surely be passing this one around!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
now don t go  eeewww    before you try this

the only way to eat fresh tomatoes! in anticipation of the impending tomato harvest, i share with you a family secret. this is the reason we look forward to the end of summer, to the time when our gardens and our friends gardens are bursting with little red-skinned treasures. when i tell anyone about this, besides my brother and sister -- we learned it from mom -- and my children -- now that i've gotten them to try it -- they think i'm weird (well...yes, i am, but this isn't why). people looked at me oddly when i made this in the college cafeteria. at least i thought that was the reason. it never tasted right, though. i think the foodservice tomatoes were plastic. my husband seems to shudder if he sees me or the kids consuming this treat, but then, he hates warm peanut butter. period. won't touch it. i haven't managed to get any of my in-laws to give it a try; my husband's dad just looks at me and shakes his head. come to think of it, i get a lot of that from him. so, what is this food that most people seem to find so repulsive that they won't even consider it? i just call it exactly what it is: peanut butter and tomatoes on toast. if you're intrigued, the extremely difficult and intricate recipe follows below. if you think i'm weird, get in line. grossed out? get over it, and try it already. i thought it was pretty gross the first time i saw my mom eating it, too, but she made me take a bite, and i was hooked.

1. spread peanut butter on hot toast
2. concerned with calories-- you don't have to lay it on really thick , just make sure you can taste it
3. now , completely cover the toast with tomato slices
4. cut sliced tomatoes in halves or quarters , if necessary , to accomplish this task
5. sprinkle liberally with black pepper , and add just a bit of salt , if desired
6. eat while toast is still hot
7. if it gets cold , throw away and start over
8. well , i'd probably eat it anyway , but it's not as good cold
9. try it , you'll like it
10. trust me on this-- the salty peanut butter is just wonderful with the tomatoes , and at least a little bit of pepper is necessary
11. i know , you're going eeewwwwww !
12. but if you give it a shot , who knows-- maybe this is how you can find your inner weirdo
demonstrations.review: Pretty good : )  My mom had me eating sliced tomatoes with sugar or tomato sandwiches with miracle whip and salt and pepper as a kid, so this wasn't much of a stretch for me.  I used light whole wheat bread, low fat jif and one store bought roma tomato.  I can only imagine it on a great white bread, with a full fat, thick layer of pb, and a deliciously ripe homegrown tomato.  Thanks for the recipe : )

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken gravy

yummmy gravy--good on anything.

1. bring chicken stock to a boil
2. add seasonings
3. set aside
4. in a deep pan , add butter until it starts to melt then add flour
5. whisk in chicken stock and cook until thickened
6. add whipping cream
7. don't let it come to a heavy boil , or cream will curd ! serve !
8. if you like a clear gravy omit the cream !
demonstrations.review: Simple. Perfect. =) used the 'clear' version - yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini lasagna  lasagne    low carb

great for anyone going low carb or who has so many zucchini, they don't know what to do!! :) we found the sauce to be very mild. i think it would be better with twice as much garlic. i boiled my zucchini slices for about 3 minutes so they were partially cooked. i wanted to make sure they were soft in the finished dish or i knew the kids wouldn't eat them. ;) the cottage cheese provides a slightly tangy note. i think we would have preferred ricotta, but that is personal taste. i use my 11x7 baking dish and got 6 pieces the size of what you see in my photos. both of the guys ate two so it fed 4 of us, and i double the meat. adjust the recipe accordingly for your family.

1. cook zucchini until tender , drain and set aside
2. fry meat and onions until meat is brown and onions are tender
3. drain fat
4. add next 8 ingredients and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat
6. simmer , uncovered 10 minutes or until reduced to 2 cups
7. in small bowl slightly beat egg
8. add cottage cheese , half of shredded cheese and flour
9. in baking-roasting pan arrange half of the meat mixture
10. top with half of the zucchini and all the cottage cheese mixture
11. top with remaining meat and zucchini
12. bake uncovered at 375 degrees f for 30 minutes
13. sprinkle with remaining cheese
14. bake 10 minutes longer
15. let stand 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Wow, I think I like this better than "normal" lasagna!  It's tender and sweet and just plain delicious!  (I used garden combonation Ragu instead of the sauce that was called for, 1/2 lb lean ground beef and 3 zucchini.)  My picky toddler LOVED it!  Thank you for a terrific and healthy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian pork loin for the slow cooker  crock pot

very simple great tasting, tender pork loin.  this is also great using, pork chops, chicken breast even beef.

1. place pork loin in crock pot
2. in bowl mix everything else
3. pour over chops
4. cook on low 6-8 hours
5. serve with cooked pasta , rice or mashed potatoes , salad and garlic bread
demonstrations.review: Oh my God, this was the MOST TENDER pork I've EVER had!  It was SO YUMMY, we had ours with mashed potatoes, and it will definately be a regular meal on our table!  Also pretty low fat if you use a lean cut, and fat free soup : ) ENJOY!

target.recipe_text:
cranberry  feta and walnut salad

a tasty and beautiful salad. you may choose to substitute the walnuts with almonds - just as good!

1. toss greens , cranberries , cheese and walnuts in large bowl
2. mix vinegar , honey , mustard and pepper with wire whisk until well blended
3. gradually add oil , whisking constantly until well blended
4. pour over salad
5. toss to coat
6. serve immediately
target.review: I made this for Thanksgiving dinner with my in-laws and it was a huge hit! I initially mixed the lettuce, cranberries, cheese, and walnuts together, but the mix-ins were so heavy that the fell to the bottom of the bowl. I ended up separating the lettuce from the other ingredients and just placing the cranberries, cheese, and nuts on top of the lettuce. I served the dressing on the side so the salad wouldn't become soggy by dinnertime. The sweetness of the cranberries paired nicely with the tang of the feta. Will be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean and tortilla bake

great quick and healthy dinner.

1. preheat oven to 350 f
2. spray a large skillet with cooking spray
3. add garlic , onions , tomato , green onion , cumin , and chili powder
4. cook on medium heat until onion is tender
5. add tomato sauce and cook 5 minutes more
6. stir in beans , cilantro , salt and pepper
7. spray a 9 inch square baking dish with cooking spray
8. layer 4 tortillas , 1 / 3 cheese , and 1 / 3 of the bean mixture
9. repeat 2 more times
10. top with reserved 2 tablespoons of cheese
11. bake 20 minutes , covered , then 10 minutes uncovered or until bubbly
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed this dish. It had good flavor and was very easy to prepare. I followed the recipe exactly, but didn't need as many tortillas as the recipe stated (I think I used about 5 or 6 six-inch tortillas). Next time I'll add some diced green or red pepper and cayenne to the bean mixture to add some texture and heat. Served with sour cream on the top.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
waffles perfect  vegan

yummy nutritious vegan waffles.  i made these for a cooking demonstration at my previous university and they were a hit!  this recipe was adapted from the newstart lifestyle cookbook.  keep them healthy by pouring fresh blended apples with some cinnamon on top or my recipe #239131.

1. process all ingredients in a blender until smooth
2. for small blenders , blend with less of the water , then pour into a pitcher and add remaining water
3. pour onto preheated , nonstick waffle iron , using enough batter to cover grids and edges
4. bake until steaming stops , from 7 to 14 minutes , depending on the waffle iron style
5. if batter gets too thick , add more water and blend before pouring
6. in my waffle iron i have to make sure to put a generous amount of batter on the iron or it will stick
7. waffles may be frozen and reheated in toaster or oven
8. for variation , blend in a banana
demonstrations.review: Very good waffles. I made these because I was trying to find a low-cholesterol recipe for waffles. I like that the base of this recipe is oats, it helps sneak in more fiber. The oats make the waffles pretty dense, though, which was the only drawback. I was worried about how thin my batter was once I blended it, but it worked just fine in my waffle iron.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lower fat creamy alfredo sauce white sauce

if you are searching for a delicious lower fat white sauce or alfredo sauce don't look any further this one is it! ---serve over cooked pasta passing more parmesan cheese at the table, adjust the garlic to suit taste

1. in a saucepan whisk together the broth with flour , garlic powder and a pinch cayenne pepper until smooth
2. mix in cream cheese spread , 4 tablespoons parmesan cheese and pinch nutmeg until smooth , bring to a simmer and cook about 3 minutes whisking / mixing continuously until combined , thickened and heated through
3. mix in remaining 2 tablespoons parmesan cheese
4. season with black pepper to taste
5. serve over cooked pasta
demonstrations.review: This was a great substitution for full-fat alfredo sauce. Even picky DH liked it! My sauce was pretty thin, even after cooking for additional time, so I had to thicken it with a little cornstarch. Great taste and it stuck well to the fettuccine noodles.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate chip breakfast cookies

this is like the baker's breakfast cookie.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. place all dry ingredients in a large bowl
3. place wet ingredients in a plastic cup , whip until fluffy
4. fold into dry ingredients
5. spray hands before forming each cookie
6. place on cookie sheet , leave room in between each one
7. cook 7-8 minutes for soft cookies , 10 for chewy
8. let cool , removed from pan on cookie sheets
9. place in tupperware , wax paper in between cookies when cool
demonstrations.review: Very good! It's a nice treat for breakfast. I used all-purpose flour (ran out of whole wheat), substituted Splenda for the sugar, and used 3 Tb of applesauce and 3 Tb of peanut butter. I'll leave out the chocolate chips next time--the cookie was already very sweet and indulgent. I'll also make the cookies smaller like lissa suggested, the cookies were still a little doughy in the middle after 10 minutes of cooking. Will be making these again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hershey s kiss peanut butter cookies

there are a few like these on here, but this particular recipe is my favorite. and i think it is the official version directly from hershey's.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. in mixer , beat shortening and peanut butter until well blended
3. blend in sugars and beat until light and fluffy
4. add egg , milk and vanilla
5. beat well
6. stir together flour , baking soda and salt
7. gradually mix in peanut butter mixture
8. shape dough into 1-inch balls and rollin additional sugar
9. place on ungreased cookie sheet and bake 8-10 minutes or until lightly browned
10. immediately place a hershey's kiss on each cookie and press down slightly
demonstrations.review: I made these for DH and used mini Reeses Peanut Butter Cups per his request (I'm not much of a cookie person). He told me that "these are the best things you've ever baked" (I'm not much of a baker!). So, five stars from DH!

target.recipe_text:
individual cream cheese danish

small danishes that make a great addition to a brunch buffet. you can also make fruit and cream cheese danishes by adding a spoonful of your favorite pie filling prior to baking. there are never any leftovers when i make these.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. slice crescent roll dough into 1 / 4 inch slices
3. place slices of dough on cookie sheet and make slight indention in the middle
4. in a large bowl , mix together cream cheese , white sugar , lemon juice , vanilla extract and sour cream
5. add a tablespoon of filling to each roll
6. bake in preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes
7. in a small bowl , stir together confectioners' sugar , milk and butter
8. after danish has cooled , drizzle with icing
target.review: I made these and they were great. Everyone loved them, even the dog. We left them on the plate to cool and went to the movies. When we came home our dog Lucy had licked the plate clean. Glad we all tried them before we left. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taste of home meatloaf wellington

a different delicious twist on meat loaf that is really easy. be sure to seal the ends of the meat loaf well or the cheese will be overflowing.

1. in large bowl , combine the egg , 1 / 3 cup spaghettie sauce , bread crumbs , salt and pepper
2. crumble beef over mixture and mix well
3. on a piece of heavy duty foil , pat beef mixture into a 12-inch by 8-inch rectangle
4. sprinkle 1 cup cheese and parsley to within 1 inch of edges
5. roll up jelly-roll style , starting with long sides and peeling foil away while rolling
6. seal seam and ends
7. place seam side down in a greased 13-inch by 9-inch by 2-inch baking pan
8. bake , uncovered at 350 degrees for one hour
9. drain
10. unroll crescent dough
11. seal seams and perforations
12. drape dough over meat loaf to cover the top , sides and ends
13. seal ends
14. bake 15-20 minutes longer or until a meat thermometer reads 160 degrees and crust is golden brown
15. let stand for five minutes
16. using two large spatulas , carefully transfer meat loaf to a serving platter
17. sprinkle with remaining cheese
18. serve with remaining spaghetti sauce
demonstrations.review: This is the only way I will eat meatloaf. I lost my recipe and its been a while since I made it. I am so happy to have found it. Thanks for posting! This is a MUST try recipe if you don't really care for meatloaf.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter oatmeal chocolate chip cookies

very yummy! a nice moist, chewy cookie. no heavy baking soda aftertaste!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. cream butter and sugars together
3. add peanut butter , egg , and vanilla
4. and mix well
5. in another bowl mix dry ingredients together and add to butter mixture
6. add chips and mix well
7. either drop onto pan or roll into small balls
8. bake for about 10-12 minutes
9. cool for 5 minutes on sheet
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I too added more oats and butter. I think I did 1 1/2 cups of oats and 3/4 cup butter. I decided more peanut butter would be nice and I also threw in some mini m&m's. they were heavenly. Didn't last long at all. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake fudge cookies

this recipe is from a church library book 

1. mix first 6 ingredients in a sauce pan and cook until it boils
2. boil for 1-3 minutes
3. remove from heat and add peanut butter and oatmeal
4. drop by teaspoonfuls on to wax paper
5. chill until set
demonstrations.review: I remember making these when I was a kid with my mother. These are our 2nd favorite peanut butter recipe that is posted on this site. Thanks for posting this. We love these cookies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s onion patties latkes

i have been making these for over 20 years, i usually get about 15 patties but it depends on the size of the batter that you drop in the pan, these are better if fried to very brown and crispy, you can make a double recipe, fry them then freeze them on a tray then pop them into freezer bags, then just warm them in the oven to crisp up, they are very addicting and i can tell you i eat half before they even get to the table lol!  if you plan on doubling the recipe then make two separate recipes in two bowls, i have doubled the recipe into one bowl and for some reason they just are not as good ---  if desired you could add in a slightly beaten large egg and reduce the milk by 1/4 cup --- you will *love* these!  also see my
recipe#186700 *and*
recipe#244592

1. chop the onions finely then place into a bowl
2. in another large bowl mix together the flour , sugar , baking powder , seasoning salt , cayenne , garlic powder and a small amount of black pepper
3. mix to combine well
4. add in the milk and whisk until thoroughly combined
5. add in the chopped onions and green onions and mix with a wooden spoon until combined
6. in a large non-stick frypan , heat a small amount of oil to medium-hot , adding in more oil as needed as the patties will absorb too much oil if you add in a large amount of oil at one time
7. drop the batter from a tablespoon into about 1 / 2-inch of hot oil
8. flatten slightly with the spoon or spatula
9. sprinkle with a little salt
10. fry until crispy and brown on both sides
demonstrations.review: YUM. This is my new favorite way to eat potatoes. these are so good they don't last for long. Thanks for posting another great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
why i joined zaar carrot cake
