on october 2, 2001, i discovered the recipezaar web site. i immediately joined so i could post a request for a recipe i had lost. in less than an hour, i had a reply: this recipe. unfortunately, i never posted it into the database -- until now. my mistake. this cake was the reason i joined, and the friendly response i received was the reason i stayed!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour a 9x13 inch pan
3. mix flour , baking soda , baking powder , salt and cinnamon
4. make a well in the center and add sugar , oil , eggs and vanilla
5. mix with wooden spoon until smooth
6. stir in carrots , coconut , walnuts and pineapple
7. pour into 9x13 inch pan and bake for about 45 minutes
8. don't panic , the centre will sink a little
9. allow to cool
10. when cool , ice the cake
11. you can certainly use your favourite cream cheese frosting to ice this cake , but the one i've included is highly recommended
12. to make the frosting: cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
13. add the icing sugar and beat until creamy
demonstrations.review: My husband is a huge fan of chocolate. He wont even try any other kind of cake. The day after I made this I made him try a bite. He LOVED it! I must say it is a good cake the day you bake it but it is soo much better the next day. My mom came over and stole a few pieces to take home with her. Thanks for a heavenly recipe.

target.recipe_text:
springfield mo cashew chicken sauce

cashew chicken sauce - springfield mo style

1. combine all ingredients except the and bring to a slow rolling boil
2. add corn starch to 2 / 3 c water and whisk thoroughly , then combine with boiling sauce base
3. whisk until thickened
4. this sauce is actually as close as i can come to mr
5. lee's sauce from oriental inn in marshfield , mo
6. he's made the "best" springfield-style cashew chicken in america since 1982
7. period
target.review: Looks fabulous! I consider myself lucky to live where I get to eat this unique and original style of chicken. For variety, try my Ozarks Cashew Chicken recipe on this site. Very similar, but more in line with the original Springfield-style cashew chicken developed by David Leong in 1963 at Leong's Tea House.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
penne with 5 cheeses ala barefoot contessa   ina garten

i was watching the barefoot contessa earlier this week, and she made this dish. the show was about preparing food ahead of time so that at dinner time, you have very little to do. when i went on the web to get the recipe, it was nowhere to be found. luckily, the show was repeated last night, so i was ready, pen in hand. the recipe below is exactly how it was described on the show; it looks delicious and i hope to try it soon. the amount given for the gorgonzola is a guess on my part, as it wasn't specified, nor was the type of cream specified (i'd use regular table cream). she also didn't specify how much basil she used, but it looked like about a quarter-cup. it was mentioned that no salt was needed, as the cheeses are salty enough.

1. preheat oven to 500f
2. bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook penne for just 4 minutes
3. drain well
4. meanwhile , in a very large mixing bowl , combine the cream , crushed tomatoes , cheeses and basil
5. on the show , very fresh buffalo mozzarella was used , and it was cut into slices and then slivered
6. i'm sure shredded mozzarella would work just fine
7. add cooked , drained penne to sauce and stir well
8. on the show , individual shallow serving dishes were filled with the pasta
9. i'm sure this could be done in a shallow casserole dish too , such as a 13x9 pan
10. either fill individual dishes with pasta , as above , or fill an entire shallow dish , then dot butter over surface in small pieces
11. bake in preheated oven for 7 to 10 minutes , until top is browned
12. on the show , the individual dishes were then refrigerated , uncovered , so that they could be reheated later in the evening
13. unfortunately , no information was given as to how the dish should be reheated so , really , your guess is as good as mine
demonstrations.review: This is a great cheesy penne dish!. Using fresh mozzarella makes all the difference.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
drew s homemade pimiento cheese   spicy or mild

you'll never buy pimiento cheese again! if you want a milder version, omit the cayenne pepper.  everyone asks for this very easy recipe. try this in a grilled cheese sandwich! yum.

1. chop pimientos into small pieces , or pulse in a food processor
2. in small bowl , stir all ingredients until well mixed
3. or put all ingredients into a food processor , and pulse until well-blended and pimientos are in small pieces
4. serve on crackers , with celery , or make pimiento cheese sandwiches !
5. you may prefer to add up to 1 / 2 cup mayonnaise to get the spreading consistency you like
demonstrations.review: I, the pimiento cheese addict, believe this is the pre-mo recipe. I grew up on it, crave it, devour it... and always serve it politely to my guests. We all know it is a Southern staple for entertaining and this is the best variation I have ever tried. The cider vinegar is the key and has taken my pimiento cheese to Nirvana level. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatloaf from good eats

this meat loaf from alton brown is moist and perfectly seasoned. my family has always been very picky when it comes to meatloaf. they loved this variation.

1. heat oven to 325 degrees
2. in a food processor bowl , combine croutons , black pepper , cayenne pepper , chili powder , and thyme
3. pulse until the mixture is of a fine texture
4. place this mixture into a large bowl
5. combine the onion , carrot , garlic , and red pepper in the food processor bowl
6. pulse until the mixture is finely chopped , but not pureed
7. combine the vegetable mixture , ground sirloin , and ground chuck with the bread crumb mixture
8. season the meat mixture with the kosher salt
9. add the egg and combine thoroughly , but avoid squeezing the meat
10. pack this mixture into a 10" loaf pan to mold the shape of the meatloaf
11. onto a parchment paper-lined baking sheet , turn the meatloaf out of the pan onto the center of the tray
12. insert a temperature probe at a 45 degree angle into the top of the meatloaf
13. avoid touching the bottom of the tray with the probe
14. set the probe for 155 degrees
15. combine catsup , cumin , worcestershire , hot pepper sauce , and honey
16. brush glaze onto the meatloaf afer it has been cooking for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: I've had this posted on site for a while. It truly is the best meatloaf recipe I've ever tasted. Thanks again, Alton!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ranch chicken thighs

needed a quick & easy weeknight meal. this is adapted from an old taste of home magazine. the chicken is tasty & juicy, with a nice crunchy crust. you won't miss the skin!  
eta -- some say this is too bland.  the ranch dressing is not enough seasoning.  i do add season salt to taste (nature's seasonings) to the bread crumb mixture for more flavor.  hopefully as a cook, you will know what to add to suit you and your family's taste.

1. in a shallow bowl , combine crumbs , parmesan cheese , cornmeal , italian seasoning , and seasoned salt
2. dip chicken into salad dressing , then coat with crumb mixture
3. place chicken in a greased 13x9 baking dish
4. bake , uncovered , at 375 degrees for 45 minutes or until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Thought this was good. I liked it, not loved it.  Decent family fare. Chicken comes out tender and juicy. I'm a ranch dressing fan, so thought it would have more flavor than it did. Used Panko breadcrumbs instead of dry, and used 2 tbsp. of Italian bread crumbs instead of cornmeal. Next time, I would use additional Italian seasoning.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frozen whiskey sour

my husbands favorite! no water is used for the blender is filled with ice. i give an optional choice to add water if you'd like it weaker.

1. in a large blender fill blender with cubed ice
2. add one frozen can of lemonade and orange concentrate
3. add the top shelf whiskey
4. add 1 / 4 cup cherry juice
5. add sugar
6. blend , high speed
7. taste if to strong for your taste add ice cold water
8. re-blend
9. pour into chilled glasses
10. fill each glass and garnish with a cherry and orange slice
11. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Wow!  The whiskey sour I've been searching for...................yum! I omitted the sugar and used only 6 oz. of whiskey (so I could have more than one!). Perfect!

target.recipe_text:
chili s salsa

you can make this sauce easily at home. from copykat.com (http://www.copykat.com)

1. in food processor place jalapenos and onions
2. process for just a few seconds
3. add both cans of tomatoes , salt , sugar , and cumin
4. process all ingredients until well blended but do not puree
5. place in covered container and chill
6. a couple of hours of chilling will help blend and enrich the flavor
7. serve with your favorite thin corn tortilla chips
target.review: So easy to prepare and we always have the ingredients on hand.  The flavor gets even better the 2nd day (if it lasts that long)!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nestle toll house chocolate chip pan cookie

this recipe was in my paper recently and i made them for my co-workers. divine! i looked & looked and was surprised i couldn't find it already on zaar.

1. preheat oven to 375 grease a 15x10-inch jelly roll pan
2. combine flour , baking soda and salt in small bowl
3. beat butter , both sugars and vanilla in large mixer bowl
4. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each
5. gradually beat flour mixture into butter mixture
6. stir in chocolate chips and nuts
7. spread into prepared pan
8. bake 20-25 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Yumm!  Quick and so easy to prepare.  Be careful not to overcook.  When cooked just right the cookies are sinful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grand prize chili

this is an actual grand prize chili recipe and it comes from the "texas bragging rights" recipe book.

1. in large pot , sear meat in a small amount of oil
2. add onion& garlic , cook until tender
3. add tomato sauce , paprika , cayenne pepper , bouillon cubes and enough water to cover
4. simmer 1 1 / 2 hours
5. add cumin , garlic powder , oregano , pepper and chili powder
6. add salt to taste
7. cook another 30 minutes or until meat is tender
demonstrations.review: This recipe is incredible.  I made it yesterday and the entire pot was devoured.  My husband was back for seconds (probably thirds) as a midnight snack and finished it off!  My kids (age 10 and 12) loved it.  They said it was spicy but loved the flavor and kept on eating, going for seconds too!  I followed the recipe except for only putting 3 tablespoons of chili powder and adding a can of beans.  This is a keeper!!!!  They are alreading asking when I am going to make it again!  THANKS for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate mallow fondue

a recipe from the dec/jan 2k1 issue of taste of home. so easy and great fun for the whole family!  to remove the marshmallow creme from the jar i use a rubber spatula & the fluff just sticks to it.  otherwise microwaving it for a few seconds at a time might make it release easier.

1. in a heavy saucepan , heat the first five ingredients just until melted
2. whisk until smooth
3. transfer to fondue pot and keep warm
4. serve with fruits and / or cake pieces
demonstrations.review: Heavenly! Made this for Christmas eve and it was a huge hit. Served it with marshmallows, bananas and Pepperidge Farm Sugar Cookies. Yummy. This recipe makes a large batch . . enough for leftovers (that won't last long). I melted ingredients on the stovetop and then transferred to my fondue pot. This is a keeper. Smooth and so sinful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
harvest pumpkin cheesecake

indulge!!

1. in a small bowl , combine cracker crumbs and sugar
2. stir in the butter
3. press onto the bottom and 2 inches up the sides of a greased 9-inch springform pan
4. bake at 350 degrees for 5 minutes
5. cool on a wire rack
6. in a mixing bowl , beat cream cheese , sugar and vanilla until smooth
7. add eggs , pumpkin and spices
8. beat just until combined
9. pour into crust
10. place cheesecake / pan in a large rectangular baking pan filled with 2 inches of hot water
11. place in a 350 degree oven and bake for 1 hour or until center is almost set
12. remove cheesecake from oven and water-filled pan and cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes
13. carefully run a knife around edge of pan to loosen
14. cool 1 hour longer
15. refrigerate until completely cooled
16. remove sides of pan just before serving
17. garnish with whipped cream
demonstrations.review: YUMM!  What a pleasant change from pumpkin pie!  This was a huge hit at Christmas dinner.  I beat the eggs with a fork before adding to the mixture, as this helps with the consistency.  I also doubled the cinnamon.  This recipe deserves all 5 stars!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome slow cooker pot roast

i found this on the all recipes site. this is a very easy recipe for a delicious pot roast. it makes its own gravy. it's designed especially for the working person who does not have time to cook all day, but it tastes like you did. you'll want the cut to be between 5 and 6 pounds.

1. in a slow cooker , mix cream of mushroom soup , dry onion soup mix and water
2. place pot roast in slow cooker and coat with soup mixture
3. cook on high setting for 3 to 4 hours , or on low setting for 8 to 9 hours
demonstrations.review: Great flavor.  So quick and simple.  I also threw in potatoes with the roast.  Cooked 6lb roast on low for 12 hours.  It fell apart when pulling it out of the crockpot.  I used the drippings to make an incredible gravy.  The trick to cooking roast - you can almost never overcook it.  I always undercooked my roasts and that is why they were so tough and chewy.

target.recipe_text:
cherry tomatoes marinated in vodka  in oversized martini glass

this was a real hit at a christmas party i went to last year. not only was the idea original and the presentation artistic, but everyone loved it! they are served in a large way- oversized novelty martini glass. they are absolutely delicious and reminded me of a bite of bloody mary

1. cut a shallow cross shape in the top of each tomato , put them in a large bowl and add the garlic , a little salt , tabasco and above all vodka
2. allow the tomatoes to soak up the vodka , stirring occasionally
3. let them soak overnight and after 24 hours they can be put in the refrigerator
4. once you are at the party pour into the large oversized martini glass and serve with a shot glass of lemon pepper for dipping and a shot glass with toothpicks
target.review: it actually gets 5 stars for the original presentation, but only 4 stars for the flavor. very original, half my guests loved it and half didn't. i guess you have to be a vodka lover. thanks for the original idea.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best banana bread

you'll never need another banana bread recipe ever again!

1. remove odd pots and pans from oven
2. preheat oven to 350 / 180
3. cream together butter and sugar
4. add eggs and crushed bananas
5. combine well
6. sift together flour , soda and salt
7. add to creamed mixture
8. add vanilla
9. mix just until combined
10. do not overmix
11. pour into greased and floured loaf pan
12. bake at 350 / 180 for 55 minutes
13. keeps well , refrigerated
demonstrations.review: the flavor was very good, however i found it a little too greasy,i will cut down on the butter a little and add a tsp of baking powder to give it a little lift.  All in all it does taste very good and will be using butter instead of shortening that called for in my other recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry feta pinwheels

from ocean spray and very good!

1. combine all ingredients except tortillas , mix well
2. divide and spread mixture evenly among tortillas
3. roll up tightly , wrap in plastic and refrigerate at least one hour
4. to serve cut into 12 slices
5. a nice variation is to add thin slices of ham on top of the spread before rolling
demonstrations.review: i placed kosher salt into a tray, covered it with plastic wrap. on top I positioned the rolls into an igloo shape and placed the perky olive penguins around it.  they were not only cute but edible too.  will definitely make again during the holidays

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perky olive penguins

these tuxedo-clad tidbits are actually ripe olives stuffed with a mildly seasoned cream cheese filling.

1. cut a slit from the top to the bottom of 12 jumbo olives
2. set aside
3. in a mixing bowl , combine the next six ingredients
4. mix well
5. fill a small heavy-duty plastic bag with cream cheese mixture
6. cut a small hole in the corner of the plastic bag
7. carefully pipe mixture into jumbo olives
8. set aside
9. cut a small triangle out of each carrot slice
10. press triangles into small olives for a beak
11. on each notched carrot slice , position a jumbo olive so the white chest is lined up with the notch for the feet
12. place the small olive , hole side down , over the jumbo olive so the beak , chest and feet are aligned
13. carefully insert a toothpick through the top of the head into the body and carrot base
14. wrap a pimento around the neck for a scarf
demonstrations.review: These are so cute and very good when made the day before. the cheese has time to absorb all the flavors. great to decorate around the cranberry feta rolls. I placed kosher salt on a tray (snow) covered it with saran wrap, placed the feta rolls shaped as an igloo and placed the penguins all around ...so cute

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best beef barley soup

this is one of my favourite recipes for leftover roast beef - its delicious on a cold winter night!!if you don't have leftover beef, substitute with 1 lb of extra-lean ground beef, to be cooked with the onions. "demi glace" or "au jus" can be found with the prepackaged gravies & sauces in the supermarket - you just won't get the same great flavour if you omit it!!

1. heat oil in large dutch oven
2. saute onions and garlic
3. add veggies and cook for about 10 minutes
4. add broth , water and barley
5. cover the pot and bring to a boil
6. add worcestershire , spices and beef
7. stir in demi-glace
8. lower heat and simmer for 30- 45 minutes or until veggies and barley are tender
demonstrations.review: very tasty soup.  I had leftover fondue meat so i browned it and used it for this recipe.thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked chicken stuffed with sun dried tomato pesto  goat cheese

this recipe is great for all phases of the south beach diet. but it's so yummy you can eat it even if you're not counting carbs!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. trim all visible fat and tendons from chicken breasts
3. pound chicken until 1 / 4 inch thick
4. put pesto , goat cheese , and chopped basil in food processor and buzz a few times until mixture is combined but not completely blended
5. spread 1 / 6 of pesto / basil / goat cheese mixture on each chicken breast
6. roll up chicken , starting with smallest end , tucking in loose pieces
7. put parmesan cheese in flat dish , and roll each rolled up chicken breast in the cheese , patting on so you get as much cheese sticking on as you can
8. spray glass casserole dish with nonstick spray and arrange chicken so pieces are not touching
9. bake 30-40 minutes , or until chicken is slightly browned and firm , but not hard to the touch
10. serve hot and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: made this and it was soooo good. very easy and tasty. thanks

target.recipe_text:
army   lou s soul food macaroni and cheese

i have had this mac and cheese and it truly is awesomely rich and creamy!  i had totally forgotten how good it was until i opened the june 2006 issue of midwest living and there it was.  no more trips to chicago to get it, here is the recipe!

1. let cheeses and butter stand at room temperature
2. cook macaroni according to package directions until almost al dente'
3. drain macaroni and transfer to a large bowl
4. add 1 cup shredded cheese and velveeta cubes to hot pasta and stir gently til cheeses start to melt
5. in a medium mixing bowl , whisk the eggs , butter , milk , soup , salt and pepper
6. stir this mixture into the cooked macaroni mixture
7. transfer half into a 13x9 sprayed baking dish
8. sprinkle with 1 / 2 cup of shredded cheese
9. top with remaining macaroni mixture
10. bake covered at 325 degrees for 30 minutes
11. uncover
12. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 2 cup of shredded cheese
13. return to oven and bake 15 minutes more until cheese is melted and bubbly brown
14. let stand 10 minutes before serving to meld flavors
target.review:
I love mac and cheese and can eat it alone!
I decided to try this recipe since it's number one under soul food section.
It was easy to prepare,but it was ok.
If I was to do this over again, I would only use two eggs, not three. Also, a tad more seasoning would help.
I will stick to my normal recipe for macaroni and cheese

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted brussels sprouts

quick, simple, and unbelievably tasty. this recipe could make even a self-professed brussels sprout hater change their mind. roasting at a high temperature with olive oil brings out the sweetness and reduces the cabbagey taste of brussels sprouts, caramelizing the edges.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. cut the bottom of each brussels sprout off and then slice in half lengthwise
3. toss all ingredients and place in a single layer on a baking dish
4. roast for 25 minutes or until brussels sprouts are slightly browned and tender throughout
5. serve hot or cold
demonstrations.review: Since September been in the process of eating more veggies.  I would eat Brussel Sprouts from time to time,but never made an effort to eat them.<br/>I pulled a small package out of the freezer and decided to check out recipes here.  The items needed are things always on hand and the reviews were great.<br/>I fixed this for dinner.<br/>OMG they are so yummy!  I chopped some garlic and placed it half way during the cooking.<br/>I love the taste with the slight burn on the end taste!  This will go into my veggie rotation!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mahogany beef stew

you will not believe the deeply satisfying flavour of this stew. this is our favourite wintry stew dish - comfort food to the max.  the cooking time is more or less accurate, but it really depends on the cut of meat used -  not everyone used chuck, and then, not all chuck is the same!  you really have to poke and prod and taste to get it to where you want it...but that's what cooking is all about, isn't it? ;-)

1. heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in heavy large pot over high heat
2. sprinkle meat with salt and pepper
3. add meat to pot
4. saut until brown on all sides , about 10 minutes
5. push meat to sides of pot
6. reduce heat to medium
7. add 2 tablespoons oil to pot
8. add onions
9. saut until golden brown , about 15 minutes
10. mix meat into onions
11. add 1 cup wine , tomatoes with juices , garlic , herbs , hoisin sauce , and bay leaves
12. bring to boil
13. reduce heat to low , cover pot and simmer 45 minutes , stirring occasionally
14. add carrots and 1 cup wine
15. cover
16. simmer 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
17. uncover , increase heat to high
18. boil until sauce is slightly thickened , stirring occasionally , about 15 minutes longer
19. reduce heat to medium , add cornstarch mixture and simmer until sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 8 minutes
20. discard bay leaves
21. season stew with salt and pepper
22. transfer stew to large bowl
23. sprinkle with parsley and serve
24. excellent with buttered egg noodles
demonstrations.review:
I love stew and this recipe was so amazing!
The flavors were a great combination!
I did add potatoes along with the carrots. I would suggest that if you do add veggies to place them with the other items at least one hour than the thirty minutes suggested in order for them to be cooked correctly.
I didn't eat it the same day that it was prepared (I will admit sneaking spoonfuls because it smell so wonderful!) because I wanted it to "season" overnight. It was so good at lunch the next day that my only regret was only bringing one bowl for lunch!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super easy honey curry chicken

i got this recipe for my mom and made it for my husband when we were just dating. he was convinced that i was the best cook ever! the recipe called for thighs, but i prefer boneless breasts. i usually serve this over a bed of rice with a steamed veggie medley or asparagus on the side.

1. dip chicken in sauce
2. place in casserole dish skin side up
3. bake at 375 degrees for 1 hour , basteing every 15 minutes
demonstrations.review:
This recipe was so yummy! It was a great mixture of spicy sweet.
I used chicken breast instead of thighs and used a tablespoon and half of curry. I also marinated the breast for around five hours while running errands. When returning home, placed in the oven to cook.
The smells were heavenly! I didn't baste until the last thirty minutes of cooking. To give it a nice caramelized topping, I placed it under the boiler for four minutes.
I will cook this again!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sauteed swiss chard  don t be afraid

incredibly yummy- slightly spicy with a bit of lemon zip. this is the most delicious swiss chard recipe ever! -i promise. (adapted from a recipe from bon appetit)

1. melt butter and oil in heavy large pan over medium-low heat
2. add garlic and crushed red pepper
3. saut until fragrant , about 1 minute
4. add swiss chard
5. stir to coat
6. cover and cook until tender about 8 minutes
7. squeeze juice from 1 / 2 lemon onto chard
8. season to taste with salt
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I'm at the point of eating better, esp with vegetable!  I've always seen Swiss Chard at the store and not sure how to prepare it.  I saw this recipe and said "Why not?".<br/>It was easy to prepare and very yummy!<br/>This will be on my green rotation!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken curry soup with coconut and lime

anything with coconut and lime just takes me right back to the tropics. i love this soup. it's actually a thai recipe and is very easy and quick create. plus, i usually have these ingredients on hand anyway, so it is also inexpensive. enjoy.

1. bring chicken broth , coconut milk , curry powder and chili to a simmer in a heavy medium saucepan over medium heat
2. add chicken and simmer until chicken is just cooked through , stirring frequently , about 5 minutes
3. mix in lime juice
4. season with salt and pepper
5. divide rice between 4 bowls
6. ladle soup over rice
7. sprinkle with green onions and cilantro
8. pass lime wedges separately
9. serve
demonstrations.review:
What a quick and easy recipe!
I love anything with curry and a great soup. There are times when a recipe state it's a quick one and end up being one that twice the stated time.
One thing that I always do prior to preparing a new recipe is to read all the previous reviews. I followed quite a few suggestions by other reviewers. I increased the curry to 1 tablespoon, added 2 tablespoons of fish sauce, 1 tablespoon of garlic and 1/2 tablespoon of red pepper.
It was so good that my only regret was not making extra!
I will be making this recipe quite often!

target.recipe_text:
jazzy new orleans chicken

tender rice, juicy chicken and lots of flavor from herbs and smoky sausage combined in an easy one-dish perfect for casual weekend entertaining.

1. in a bowl , dredge chicken in flour , turning to coat all sides
2. in large sauce-pan , heat oil over medium heat: brown chicken , about 8 minutes per side
3. transfer to a plate
4. in the same pan , cook sausage , garlic , onion , peppers , tomatoes , sugar , thyme , oregano , salt , allspice , and cayenne , stirring occasionally , for 10 minutes or until peppers are softened
5. stir in rice
6. add stock and bay leaves
7. nestle chicken into rice , bring to a boil
8. reduce heat , cover and cook for about 20-25 minutes , or until liquid is absorbed and juices run clear when chicken is pierced
9. remove bay leaves
10. serve sprinkled with parsley
11. garnish with lemon wedges
target.review: The prep work took no time at all, but the finished product tastes like real work went into it. I didn't have any oregano, but next time won't skip it. I used whole grain rice, more than a pinch of  cayenne,  and about 3/4 tsp salt. It took a little longer to cook, but I didn't mind.  The aroma filled the house with anticipation. It's a tasty dish and a nice change from the usual. I'll make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s seafood pasta salad

the amounts listed are only a guideline you may adjust all amounts to taste, fresh lemon juice only please, use fresh cooked crab meat or imitation, whatever you prefer to use, if using previously frozen then thawed shrimp hand squeeze out all excess moisture from the shrimp before using in the salad, plan ahead there is a chilling time before serving.

1. in a pot cook the shell pasta in boiling water until al dente drain , then rinse the pasta under cold water then allow to drain very well then transfer to a large bowl
2. add in cooked shrimp , crab meat , celery , red bell pepper , green onions , cubed mozzarella cheese and thawed peas or black olives toss to combine
3. in a bowl whisk together the mayonnaise with salad dressing , sour cream , garlic powder , lemon juice and old bay seasoning pour over the salad and toss to combine , then mix in the hot sauce
4. season with salt and fresh ground black pepper
5. if the salad is too dry for your liking then mix in some whipping cream or more mayonnaise
6. cover and chill for at least 4 hours or more before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this for the 4th of July and everybody liked it.  One of my guests, a graduate of culinary school, (oohlala :) gave it a big thumbs up.  I used 1 tblsp of Old Bay, but followed everything else as given. I'm making it for the office potluck tomorrow.  Thanks for another winner, Kitten.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my moms amazing parsley potatoes

my mom has the amazing ability to turn the mundane into something awesome. never fail, one of my 5 brothers or sisters would ask for this every night. simple, tasty, attractive and goes with just about anything. you can adjust the amounts to your liking as potatoes come in all sizes. southern all the way!

1. peel potatoes and cut into chunks
2. boil potatoes until tender
3. drain and stir in remaining ingredients
demonstrations.review: This is really good eating. I'll never look at plain old mashed potatoes the same way. Thanks for a real keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned country beans

this recipe is marked as a heritage recipe in the 1991 book, the black family reunion cookbook, recipes and food memories.

1. place bacon in large saucepan and cover with water
2. boil 20 minutes
3. add green beans , onions , salt , sugar and cayenne
4. boil 15 minutes
5. add potatoes
6. boil until potatoes are tender
demonstrations.review: I used a 1 lb. bag of frozen green beans, 3 slices of bacon, 1/2 onion, 1/2 tsp. salt, 3 white potatoes quartered (we like potatoes) and a pinch of sugar. I forgot the cayenne pepper and this was still delicious. Next time, I'll follow the recipe to the letter for even better results.  Thanks, Lennie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lebanese chicken wrap sandwich

during a trip to montreal, we had the tastiest chicken wrap sandwich at a little lebanese food stand. i had to come up with this recipe to keep my husband from hopping in the car and driving the 4 hours back to montreal for more.

1. in a large nonstick pan , heat oil and then add the chicken , chopped onion , minced garlic , 1 / 4 cup lemon juice , cumin , oregano and enough salt and pepper to taste
2. make sure chicken is well cooked and browned
3. in a small bowl mix the mayo , lemon juice and garlic powder
4. heat flour tortillas by steaming in microwave for 1 - 2 minute covered in a damp paper towel
5. assemble wrap by placing one tortilla on a piece of aluminum foil , then fill with chicken , garlic mayo spread , and then top with the optional toppings of tomato , onion , lettuce and / or tahini sauce
6. wrap closed with foil and twist foil end
demonstrations.review: The flavors dance in your mouth and there's a "Mmmm" with each bite.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best carrot cake

i made this cake for easter, and everone loved it, saying it was the best carrot cake ever.

1. combine flour , salt , soda , & cinnamon
2. set aside
3. combine eggs , sugar , & oil
4. mix until smooth
5. stir in flour mixture a little at a time until well blended
6. stir in carrots , walnuts , pineapple , & vanilla , mixing evenly
7. pour into a greased 9x13in pan
8. bake at 350 degrees for 45-55 minutes
9. --------------frosting----------
10. cream together , cheese and butter until smooth
11. add vanilla
12. add sugar a 1 / 4 cup at a time , until well blended
13. after frosting cooled carrot cake , sprinkle with toasted coconut
14. to toast coconut , put on cookie sheet , under broiler for about 1 minute
15. keep an eye on it to be sure it does not burn !
demonstrations.review: I can't say enough about this cake!! My co-workers BEG me to bake this cake and complain when it's all gone. It's funny watching a group of otherwise civilized folks, elbowing each other to get a slice of my cake. I love it! It's quite a compliment when, rather than not have a taste at all, someone scrapes the crumbs off of your cake plate at the office luncheon. UPDATE:  10/28/2009 I've sold 3 of these cakes for $25 each and I expect more orders with the holidays coming.  Thanks, Leslie!

target.recipe_text:
chicken and cornbread stuffing casserole

a easy and nice flavorable stuffing that doesn't need the bird. lol

1. heat oven to 400 degrees
2. spray 3-quart casserole with pam
3. heat soup and milk to boiling , stirring frequently
4. stir in mixed vegetables , onion , and poultry seasoning
5. heat to boiling , stirring frequently
6. remove from heat
7. stir in chicken and stuffing mix
8. spoon into casserole
9. sprinkle with pepper and paprika
10. bake uncovered for 15 minutes
target.review: I REALLY enjoyed this recipe.  I did not mix the stuffing in with the other ingredients instead I reduced the milk to 1/2 cup, took the stuffing mix and added 1/2 cup chicken broth and topped the veggies, chicken and soup mixture with the moistened stuffing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tossed salad with mandarin oranges

this salad goes good with any main dish and is especially nice with bbq. easy to carry to picnics or potlucks too! just 4 ingredients make it fast and easy! fits into many catagories for the zaar world tour especially sw.taken from a louisiana cajun french church anniversary cookbook.

1. in a large bowl tear lettuce into small pieces
2. drain oranges and reserve 2 tbsp of juice
3. mix reserved juice , vinegar , onion powder and garlic powder with miracle whip until smooth
4. add drained oranges and onions to lettuce
5. drizzle miracle whip mixture over all and toss to coat
6. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: My family enjoyed this recipe.  Even my 6 yo who said I'm not eating that ate every bite that was put on her plate (our rule is you have to try it - she did that and a lot more!).  I cut the recipe in half since there are only 3 of us and it came out great - thanks mama!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french dip crock pot recipe

a really nice fireside supper for friends. taste the aus jus first to make sure it's really "beefy" and add another bouillon packet if needed.
edit--if "heat bothers you" start with 1 teaspoon of black pepper.

1. coat roast in flour and garlic salt
2. braise the roast on all sides on pan prior to placing in crock pot
3. place all ingredients in a crock pot
4. cook on high for 5-6 hours or low for 8-10
5. remove the meat from the crock pot and place on a deep plate-to collect juices
6. strain the broth well so that it is clear and no spices or onions remain
7. add a few cups of water to create aus jus
8. place in a saucepan and keep warm
9. most people prefer to keep the broth as is but you can stir in a small amount of cornstarch mixed with cold water to thicken it up just a touch
10. heat hoaggie buns to warm and slice the meat thin
11. place a good amount of sliced meat in each of the buns and offer the aus jus in individual ramekins
demonstrations.review: My dh and dd both said they would like to eat this at least once a month - a definite keeper!  I served mine on toasted french bread slices which worked very well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic shrimp and pasta  low fat recipe

nan

1. in a medium saucepan , mix cornstarch , broth , garlic , parsley , lemon juice and pepper
2. over medium-high heat , cook until mixture boils and thickens
3. stir constantly
4. add shrimp
5. cook for 5 minutes or until shrimp turns pink
6. stir often
7. toss with spaghetti
demonstrations.review: I really enjoyed this recipe, it was light and tasty.  I did not have chicken broth on hand so I made my own with chicken bullion granulas/water which gave it a buttery flavor.  I think next time I would reduce the lemon juice a little though.  Also, I used penne pasta because it's what I had on hand.  Will probably make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornbread taco bake

a second place winner in the country woman magazine.

1. in a large skillet , cook beef over medium heat until no longer pink
2. drain
3. stir in the corn , tomato sauce , water , green pepper and taco seasoning
4. mix well
5. spoon into a greased 2-qt
6. baking dish
7. prepare corn bread mix according to package directions for corn bread
8. stir in half the onions
9. spread over beef mixture
10. bake uncovered at 400 degrees for 20 minutes
11. sprinkle with cheese and remaining onions
12. bake 3-5 minutes longer or until cheese is melted and toothpick inserted into corn bread layer comes out clean
demonstrations.review: I used Jiffy cornbread mix and I was not crazy about the sweetness of this particular mix in contrast to the rest of the recipe.  Also, it took longer to bake than suggested, about 10-15 minutes longer.  The base of the recipe (meat, corn, etc) was tasty though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
suzanne s caramel oatmeal bars

i received these from my christmas bake exchange and i just love these little treats! thanks suzanne for sharing the recipe with me.

1. press half of oatmeal mixture into a 9 x 13 pan bake at 350 for 10 to 15 minutes
2. remove from oven and sprinkle on enough chocolate chips to cover
3. then top with caramel mixture , then remaining oatmeal mixture
4. bake another 15-18 minutes
5. cool and cut
demonstrations.review: These were a hit at my house.  Very rich and chewy.

target.recipe_text:
fresh peach blueberry cobbler

a different cobbler...

1. preheat oven to 400
2. in a large bowl , combine peaches and lemon juice
3. mix gently
4. add blueberries , sugar , cornstarch
5. mix to combine
6. spoon into an ungreased 9" square pan and bake for 15 minutes
7. meanwhile , in a separate bowl , combine flour , sugar and baking powder
8. cut in margarine with a pastry blender or fingers
9. stir in milk and vanilla
10. drop batter in spoonfuls over fruit
11. bake for an additional 30 minutes , or until golden brown
target.review: We made this pretty much as written, the only substitutions being butter for margarine, and white flour for the cornstarch. It was fantastic. Served it with heavy whipping cream, and had it for dessert and breakfast the next morning! Highly recommended!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ma po tofu  from cooking light

tried this the other day and loved it! if you use a couple of 8 oz. packages of diced tofu, found in the produce section of your grocery store, and bottled minced ginger, this goes together in no time. a rice cooker does a great job with brown rice, too, and will keep the rice warm until serving. a quick, healthy dish from cooking light.

1. place tofu slices on several layers of paper towels , cover with additional paper towels
2. place a dinner plate on top of covered tofu
3. let stand 30 minutes
4. remove plate , discard paper towels
5. cut tofu slices into 1 / 2-inch cubes
6. combine broth , cornstarch , soy sauce , oyster sauce and chili garlic sauce , stirring with a whisk
7. heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
8. add pork
9. cook 4 minutes or until done , stirring to crumble
10. add ginger and garlic
11. cook 1 minute , stirring constantly
12. add tofu
13. cook 4 minutes or until golden , stirring frequently
14. add broth mixture to pan
15. bring to a boil
16. cook 1 minute or until mixture thickens
17. remove from heat
18. serve tofu mixture over rice
19. sprinkle with onions
demonstrations.review: Really liked this.  Made with 1lb of ground pork and about 10 oz. of rsff chicken broth.  Came out very well.  Will definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dandelion casserole

it seems like a lot of greens but they cook down to almost nothing.and if you want you can replace the dandelion with spinach. i use hot sausage which gives this a real kick, but if you rather go for mild or just use chopped beef.

1. blanch greens for 3 minutes and set aside
2. brown meats , onion and garlic , add bread crumbs , parsley , dried herbs , salt , pepper , egg , and milk
3. squeeze dandelion greens of all moisture
4. in a buttered casserole alternate layers of dandelions , pasta , crumbled browned meat mixture and tomato sauce
5. top with cheese and bake 350 degrees for 20-30 minutes
6. garnish with hot pepper flakes and parmesan cheese and serve with crisp fresh bread
demonstrations.review: I started with what seemed like WAY too many greens, but in the end it cooked down and became 'just right.'  I think one key to this recipe is the sausage... make sure you use a sausage you like.  The one I picked up at the store was questionable, and really cast an odd flavor over the whole dish.  The rest of my family didn't like it much, for which I mostly blame the meat.  Also, I went on the low side with the sauce, using only about 3 cups originally, and the dish came out really dry.  Part of the dryness was my noodles... I used whole wheat egg noodles and cooked them al dente; I think they still had some moisture to absorb.  We ate the 2nd half as leftovers, and I added an entire 3c. can of pizza sauce to the leftovers.  Then the liquid level came out about right.  To recap:  Lots of dandelion, be sure you like your sausage, don't undercook your noodles, and err towards the high side with the tomato sauce.  Overall quite good, and I will probably experiment with this some more.  One thing I liked was that, as it was baking, it evinced a wonderful buttery aroma.  I think that must have been from the dandelion, as I haven't experienced it from any of the other ingredients in the past.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy shrimp in coconut milk

steamed rice is perfect with this very tasty exotic dish.

1. heat oil in lg skillet on med-hi heat
2. add onions and stir cook for 3 minutes
3. add garlic and ginger , cook 2 minutes
4. add next 5 spices , cook 1 minute
5. add tomatoes , cook 1 minute
6. add coconut milk , water , and salt , and bring to a simmer
7. simmer until thickened 5-10 minutes
8. add shrimp , simmer , stirring for 5 minutes
9. stir in cilantro
10. serve with lime wedges
demonstrations.review: Pretty good.  Not really very spicy, overall quite bland at first taste.  I added some fish sauce, used 50% more coriander (fresh ground from seed), doubled or tripled the red pepper, and included a bit of red wine vinegar.  That plus the fresh lime juice squeezed on at the table made it acceptably tasty.  But I wouldn't call it spicy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple collards with yogurt and old bay

just a really easy experimental dish that turned out well.

1. cook the chopped collard greens in some water in a pot on your stovetop for about 15 minutes or until heated through
2. drain out some of the water , leaving about 1 / 2 cup
3. add the old bay seasoning , salt and pepper to taste , and yogurt
4. mix through
5. if mixture is watery , mix 1 teaspoons cornstarch with 1 teaspoons water , add to collards and cook until sauce is thickened
demonstrations.review: Not really to my taste, I suppose.  YMMV.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herbed shrimp and feta casserole

this recipe comes from the "come on in" cookbook, and if you are a shrimp lover like me, then you will *love* this! it's layers of angel-hair pasta covered with shrimp and salsa in a fantastic fluffy cheese/egg sauce mixture topped with melted mozzarella cheese, i could eat this whole casserole by myself it is just *that* good! :)

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. butter an 8" x 12" baking dish
3. in a bowl , blend eggs , milk , yogurt feta , swiss cheese , parsley , basil , oregano and garlic
4. spread half the pasta over bottom of baking dish
5. cover with salsa
6. add half the shrimp
7. spread remaining pasta over shrimp
8. pour and spread egg mixture over pasta
9. add remaining shrimp
10. top with mozzarella cheese
11. bake 30 minutes
12. remove from oven , and let stand 20 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Loved it!  It was funny; my wife and I wanted to make 'something with shrimp.'  I dug up a quiche recipe, an alfredo recipe, a cheesy shrimp-bake recipe, and a shrimp, feta & tomatoes recipe.  Then I came across this recipe, and it was almost like, "All of the above, mixed together."  We both thought it sounded crazy enough that it just might work.  And sure enough, it was great!  It was a hit with the kids too.  The only change we made was that we added some steamed broccoli to it.  Will definitely make this one again.

target.recipe_text:
glazed rosemary honey mushrooms

so easy and tasty!

1. preheat onven to 325 degrees
2. in a heavy bottom pan place oil through salt and pepper heat and whisk to blend and melt honey
3. add mushrooms and toss to coat
4. bake for 30-40 minutes stirring a couple times
5. serve with a sprig of rosemary
target.review: Super easy. Went overall well with enteraining friends -- toss in the toaster oven and enjoy this as an appetizer, round 2.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apricot ginger pork tenderloin

apricot-ginger pork tenderloin

1. in a small bowl , combine oil , oregano , salt , thyme , black pepper , red pepper and garlic
2. rub mixture on all sides of pork tenderloins , rubbing it into meat surface
3. place tenderloins in center of cooking grate
4. grill 25 to 30 minutes for medium and centers are still slightly pink , turning occasionally throughout grilling time to brown them evenly
5. meanwhile , make sauce:
6. in small saucepan , combine all sauce ingredients
7. cook over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes until jelly is melted and sauce is hot
8. remove from heat and keep warm
9. remove tenderloins from grill and let rest 10 minutes
10. slice and serve with sauce
demonstrations.review: This recipe is the one you whip out when guests come for dinner. Super easy and super impressive means happy dinner guests and more time for entertaining.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gambas al ajillo  shrimp w  garlic  catalonia

while this is usually served as a tapa, it is too good not to eat as a main course. after trying the ones that were posted here on zaar, i found myself still searching for the gambas we had in barcelona. finally i found the recipe with the flavor and creaminess of the dish we fell in love with in spain! the same dish can be made with squid, cut into rings, or scallops. serve with lots of warm crusty bread to sop up the sauce…. you will not want to waste a drop! (make sure you are "warming" the olive oil and the butter, not cooking it off..... cause you'll want every last bit of it for the sauce)

1. in a wide , shallow saut pan over high heat , warm the olive oil and the butter
2. add the shrimp and garlic and saut quickly for about 2-3 minutes
3. add the lemon juice , paprika , pepper flakes , and salt and pepper to taste
4. adjust seasonings to your liking
5. transfer to a warmed serving dish , sprinkle with the parsley and serve at once
demonstrations.review: Prepped everything beforehand, and then when guests arrived, I sauteed and served. Perfect little snack with good food and good conversation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: For me, this is a quick-and-easy go-to chicken dinner, especially since I practically keep all of these ingredients on hand, except chili peppers. In the grand scheme of things, Thai grilled chicken with chili honey glaze still ranks #1 in flavor (319611), but it cannot be made on a whim like this recipe, which gives this recipe a place in my recipe box.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bourbon  rum  balls  no bake cookies

these i make my request of my sis lydia. her favorite! i've also use walnuts. the food processor make this so very easy!

1. place wafers and pecans in food processor and pulse till crumbly
2. add remaining ingredients and pulse till smooth
3. shape into balls about 1 inch in diameter
4. roll in powdered sugar and chill
5. this mixture is sticky , so keep finger and palms of hands dusted with sugar while shaping cookies
6. it helps if hands and kitchen is cool
demonstrations.review: Love. Love. Love this recipe. The only thing hard about it is getting people to try it. Once they do, they're glad they did.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked brie in puff pastry with apricot or raspberry preserves

this baked brie puff pastry is rich, creamy, and dessert-like. it always disappears. i'm always asked for the recipe. raspberry preserves goes great in this as well. bringing in 2012 i made this using recipe #463563!

1. preheat oven to 425
2. lightly grease cookie sheet
3. roll puff pastry out slightly
4. place cheese wheel on top
5. place preserves on top of cheese
6. place almonds on top of preserves
7. bundle puff pastry up and around the cheese
8. bake for 20-25 minutes
9. let cool for five minutes
10. serve with your favorite crackers
demonstrations.review: A big hit. Don't be afraid to be a little creative with the shape of the dough to brie. Variations handle well (and they may be a bit easier if you are like me and don't have as much of a creative knack). I thought I'd like the raspberry better, but the apricot really compliments the brie best.

target.recipe_text:
franks chicken wing dip

hot or cold dip that really gives the taste of authentic buffalo wings

1. mix all ingredients together
2. you can eat this cold , as is-- or heat it up
3. to heat: bake in casserole dish at about 350 degrees for about 30-40 minutes until everything melts together
4. serve with crackers , tortilla chips or bagel chips
target.review: This is the best dip!  My family will devour it when I make it! Made it with blue cheese and ranch mixed and it was great!  Thanks karencooks1 for a recipe I will make again and again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized baked chicken legs wings

delicious! yummy  caramelized legs, kids love these! so quick and easy and no marinating required. just prepare the sauce, pour over the chicken and pop in the oven!  i actually like this with wings better ;-)
 

very important to leave it in the oven until it has caramelized to avoid disappointment. 

thank you to everyone for their positive reviews!

try adding sambal oelek as chef  #27416 has suggested in his review. what a great idea ;-)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit or 180 degrees celsius
2. place chicken in a 9x13 inch baking dish
3. mix together the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper
4. pour over the chicken
5. bake in preheated oven for one hour , or until sauce is caramelized
6. could also use wings or pork ribs
demonstrations.review: Sorry, but this was just OK to us.  It never caramelized and nobody ate more than one piece.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered chocolate brownie pudding trifle

this is a chocolate-lover's dream dessert! if you don't have a trifle dish then use a large glass bowl, i use my recipe#87925 for this, use your own favorite brownie recipe but must be baked in a 13 x 9-inch pan or use a packaged brownie mix. plan ahead the brownies must be baked and refrigerated until completely cold before slicing, i advise to make the brownies a day in advance. prep time does not include making the brownies. you can use all chocolate pudding if desired.

1. prepare a large glass trifle bowl or a large glass serving bowl
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. prepare the browninie mix according to package directions
4. bake in a 13 x 9-inch baking pan until brownies test done
5. cool to room temperature then refrigerate until completely cold
6. when the brownies are cold cut into about 2-1 / 2-inch squares
7. prepare chocolate and cream cheese pudding separately in two bowls using 2-3 / 4 cups milk for each
8. line the bottom of the trifle bowl with half of the brownie cubes
9. pour the prepared chocolate pudding over the brownies then sprinkle with 1 / 3 of the crushed cookies
10. cover with one 8-ounce container of the cool whip topping
11. layer the remaining brownie cubes over the cool whip , then pour the cream cheese pudding over the cool whip
12. sprinkle 1 / 3 of the crushed cookies over the cream cheese pudding , then top with the second 8-ounce container of cool whip topping
13. sprinkle the remaining crushed cookies over the cool whip
14. refrigerate until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: I made this twice in the last month and had none left over either time! This is so good! I used white chocolate and chocolate the first time and all chocolate the second. Everyone just loved it and ooood and ahhhhhd over it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy garlic penne pasta

this is a delicious, super quick side or main dish. i got it from the back of a pasta box and it is yummy!

1. melt butter and add garlic in a medium sauce pan
2. cook over medium for 1 minute
3. add flour and cook 1 minute , stirring constantly
4. stir in broth and milk and cook , stirring frequently , until sauce boils and thickens
5. add parsley , salt , pepper and cheese
6. stir until cheese is melted
7. toss hot pasta with sauce and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This is so good!!  We all just scarfed it up!  Very easy to fix and I fixed the recipe as is, but then I added some cut up chicken breasts to make it a whole meal!  My son went back after dinner and ate it cold and said it was really good.  We will be having this again and again and again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
champagne salad

nan

1. in a large bowl , cream together the cream cheese and sugar
2. fold in the pineapple , whipped topping and strawberries and mix well
3. stir in bananas and walnuts
4. 2 freeze for 4 to 6 hours or overnight
5. remove from freezer 1 to 2 hours before serving
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is a recipe I love.  It is easy to make and very delicious.  Just a hint...dice bananas into the pineapple juice so they won't darken.  Drain before adding to recipe! (Sorry...forgot the stars!!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panini sandwiches

when i got my george foreman grill, i made up this recipe to be like the ones that i had bought. it has been a big hit with everyone.

1. start heating the grill
2. place 1 slice of mozzarella on each of 4 slices of bread
3. place 1 slice of provolone on each of the other 4 slices of bread
4. top the mozzarella with pepperoni , salami and pepperoncini
5. top the provolone with turkey , ham and cheddar
6. place the two halves of the sandwiches together
7. brush the top of the first sandwich with the melted butter
8. place the sandwich butter side down on the grill
9. brush the other side with melted butter
10. grill till bread is toasted and the cheese has melted
11. continue with the other sandwiches
12. a george foreman grill works great with these sandwiches but even a stove top grill would work
demonstrations.review: These are the best sandwiches.  I made these a lot while at the beach this past summer.  Easy to make, and everyone loves them.  Didn't change a thing!

target.recipe_text:
joe s crab shack crab dip

copy cat recipe from google search. posted in reply to a request.

1. mix cream cheese , mayo , sour cream , and butter until smooth
2. blend in salt and paprika
3. stir in onion , green pepper , cheese , and crab meat
4. bake at 350f for 10-15 minutes , until bubbly
target.review: Yummy dip and true to Joe's. Next time I will use lump crab meat instead of canned.  I thought the canned meat kinda "got lost" in the dip.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this exactly as written. We liked this and will definitely make it again! It is a tad salty so I can only give it 4 stars.  Next time I will try lower sodium items. Thanks for a keeper recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatball subs  crock pot

one of my kids' favorite meals. the meatballs can be prepared ahead of time and frozen, if desired.

1. place first seven ingredients in large bowl
2. mix thoroughly with your hands just until combined
3. shape into approximately 30 1-inch balls
4. bake in an ungreased oblong pan in a 400f oven until light brown , 20-25 minutes
5. or: microwave meatballs in an ungreased baking dish , 6 minutes on high , turning once
6. or: cook over medium heat in frying pan , turning occasionally , until brown , about 20 minutes
7. place cooked meatballs and spaghetti sauce in crock pot
8. cook on low for about 2 hours
9. if you cook longer , stir every hour or so
10. place meatballs and sauce in buns / rolls and top with mozzarella cheese
demonstrations.review: What a easy and delicious sandwich! I hollowed out sub buns, used sliced mozarella and ran it under the broiler til the cheese melted. This recipe is definitely a keeper. Thanks Marg!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
island kielbasa

my mother gave this recipe to me and it's a quick and easy recipe to make. take it along to your next pot luck...it's always a favorite

1. slice kielbasa into 1 / 2 inch slices and place in crockpot
2. add ketchup , brown sugar and the can of pineapples
3. stir until thoroughly blended
4. cook on low in crockpot for approximately 4-5 hours
demonstrations.review: This was dee-lish! Since there are only two of us I 1/2'd the recipe but didn't change any ingredients.  This is definitely going in my "keep" file!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dad s casserole

complete comfort food. great on a cold day.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. spray 2-3 quart casserole with non-stick cooking spray
3. cook noodles as directed on package
4. brown beef with garlic until cooked through
5. drain
6. add salt , sugar and tomato sauce and simmer for 5 minutes
7. combine sour cream , cream cheese and onion
8. layer 1 / 2 of the noodles then 1 / 2 of the meat mixture in casserole dish
9. spread with sour cream mixture
10. top with remaining noodles and the tomato sauce
11. bake for 30 minutes
12. sprinkle grated cheese on top and bake for another 5 minutes
13. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I have to agree with others. Making the recipe exactly as written my family thought there was WAY too much sour cream/cream cheese.  I might try it again and 1/2 the mixture and see if I can up my rating.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seasoned goldfish crackers

i can't believe no one has posted this yet! these are so good. my 3 year old won't eat the plain ones out of the bag anymore because of this!

1. place crackers in a large bowl
2. combine the remaining ingredients
3. drizzle over crackers and toss to coat evenly
4. transfer to a large baking pan
5. bake at 250 degrees for about 15 - 20 minutes stirring occasionally
6. cool completely and store in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: These were a hit at a recent party. I made these exactly like the recipe said. I had lots of compliments for such a simple little snack!

target.recipe_text:
family favorite crock pot meatloaf

found this recipe many years ago in my very first crockery cookery cookbook. if you like meatloaf either hot or for cold sandwiches this has a real nice flavor especially with sweet sauce on the top!

1. combine eggs with milk , bread crumbs , onion , salt , and sage , and meat
2. mix well and shape into a 9x5 inches
3. rectangle or oval
4. carefully place into slow cooker pot
5. cook on low for about 6-7 hours
6. combine sauce ingredients and pour over meat loaf and cook on high for about 15 minutes
target.review: So easy and so good!!!  Even the neighbor kid, who is SUPER picky loved it!!  I was in shock, he doesn't like anything!!!  So it has to be good!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simply sour cream chicken enchiladas

easy to assemble, deliciously creamy and a great choice for once-a-month cooking. and there is no canned cream soup in my enchiladas -- hope you give them a try!

1. in a frying pan , cook chicken and onion together in oil over medium-high heat until chicken is just done
2. divide cooked chicken evenly between 8 tortillas
3. add 1 1 / 2 tablespoons cheese to each tortilla
4. roll enchiladas and place seam-side down in a 9x13" baking dish that has been lightly sprayed with no-stick cooking spray
5. melt butter in a medium saucepan
6. stir in flour to make a roux , stir and cook until bubbly , and gradually whisk in chicken broth then bring to boiling , stirring frequently
7. remove from heat
8. stir in sour cream and green chilies
9. pour sauce evenly over enchiladas
10. top with remaining 3 / 4 cup cheese and bake at 400 f for 20 minutes until cheese is melted and sauce near edges of baking dish is bubbly
demonstrations.review: Made with leftover turkey and add a can of black beans.  Awsome!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach garlic soup

this soup turns to a brilliant green color. my kids take leftovers to school for lunch and ask me to often make this easy soup. i have substitued skim milk for the cream with good results

1. in a 5qt dutch oven , bring spinach , broth and carrots to a boil
2. reduce heat
3. simmer 5 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. remove from the heat
5. cool to luke-warm
6. meanwhile , in a skillet , saute onion and garlic in butter until onion is soft , about 5-10 minutes
7. add flour
8. cook and stir over low heat for 3-5 minutes
9. add to spinach mixture
10. puree in small batches in a blender or food processor until finely chopped
11. place in a large saucepan
12. add cream , milk , and pepper , heat through but do not boil
demonstrations.review: Super good!!!!  Made it for dinner last night on a chilly Indiana evening and everybody gobbled it up!  Will be making this frequently around here.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple or pear cake

absolutely the most delicious, moist cake ever with a decadent topping. very simple to make, my family just loves this!

1. cake:
2. mix all cake ingredients by hand in order given
3. pour in a greased 9 x 13 inch pan or springform pan
4. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes and remove
5. topping:
6. in saucepan mix all ingredients and bring to a slow boil for 3 minutes
7. pour over cake and return to oven for 4 minutes
demonstrations.review: Sooo good!!!!   Made as stated and cake was gone in less than two days!!!  Wi

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato phyllo pizza

this was great and easy meal, and a nice way to use up phyllo dough.
points 1.

1. spray jelly roll pan with cooking spray
2. place sheet of phyllo on pan and spray generously with spray
3. repeat with remaining sheets phyllo
4. sprinkle mozzarella cheese and onion over phyllo
5. arrange tomato slices on top
6. sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper
7. sprinkle with parmesan cheese and herbs
8. bake pizza at 375f until phyllo is browned and cheese melted , about 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Oh sooo good!!!  Added some fresh garlic to it and it was fantastic!!!  Very good use for garden fresh tomatoes.  Made for a good light meal.  Will be making again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the sweetest blueberry muffins

very tasty and sweet.

1. heat oven to 375
2. grease 18 regular-size muffin cups
3. in bowl , mix butter until creamy
4. add sugar and beat until pale and fluffy
5. add eggs one at a time , beating after each
6. beat in vanilla , baking powder and salt
7. with spoon , fold in half of flour then half of milk into batter
8. repeat
9. fold in blueberries
10. spoon into muffin cups and sprinkle topping onto each muffin
11. bake 15 to 20 minutes , until golden brown and springy to touch
demonstrations.review: Oh my 8 yr old and I are so addicted to these.  Yummy!!!

target.recipe_text:
restaurant teriyaki sauce

you know the nice, sweet, thick teriyaki sauce you get from your favorite takeout joint? now you can have it at home.

1. mix all but cornstarch and 1 / 4c water in a sauce pan and begin heating
2. mix cornstarch and cold water in a cup and dissolve
3. after sauce is simmering , add cornstarch and water mixture , whisking well until sauce thickens
4. heat until sauce thickens to desired thickness
5. add water to thin if you over-thick it :)
target.review: I'm giving the recipe five stars for flavor. I didn't make the sauce as directed because I just needed teriyaki marinade for stir-fry beef. I didn't add the cold water/cornstarch, but instead added a splash of sesame oil. I added the mixture to thinly sliced steak and marinated for a hour before stir frying. Wonderful flavor!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
top secret recipes waffle house waffles by todd wilbur

try the recipe that has sold millions of waffles. if you prefer pecan waffles, add 1/4 cup chopped pecans before pouring the batter onto the waffle iron

recipe created by todd wilbur www.topsecretrecipes.com

1. combine flour , salt and baking soda in a medium bowl and stir to combine
2. lightly beat the egg in another medium bowl and combine with sugar , butter , and shortening , mixing well until smooth
3. add the half & half , milk , buttermilk and vanilla and mix well
4. add the dry flour mixture to the wet mixture while beating and mix until smooth
5. if you can , cover and chill overnight , though the batter can be used right away
6. rub a light coating of vegetable oil on a waffle iron , and preheat it
7. leave the batter out of the refrigerator to warm up a bit as your waffle iron is preheating
8. spoon 1 / 3 to 1 / 2 cup of batter into the waffle iron and cook for 3 to 4 minutes or until the waffles are light brown
demonstrations.review: Great Recipe! Worked Perfectly :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
avocado and egg salad

this recipe was my wonderful mother's. having been raised in california, we ate avocados every day. this is one of my husband's favorites. it can also be used on a sandwich and recently i actually smashed it up and filled eggs with it. a big hit with my friends.

1. cut ripe avocado into chunks
2. hard boil egg and chop
3. add to avocado
4. add remaining ingredients
5. let stand or refrigerate for a little while , but not too long as avocados may turn
6. serve on a bed of lettuce for salad
7. sprinkle a little paprika on top for color
demonstrations.review: This was "okay". It was prepared as written, other than I used 2 large eggs, and less garlic than called for. One teaspoon of garlic seemed extreme, and even the 1/4 teaspoon I did use was overpowering.  I love egg salad and avocados, but I guess I don't love them together.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever peanut butter fudge

peanut butter lovers, this is perfect for you. very rich flavor. can't stop eating.....

1. grease 9x13 cake pan
2. mix sugar , evaporated milk , and butter in pan
3. stir constantly over medium heat
4. bring to a full boil and stir for 4 more minutes , or until a candy thermometer reads between 234 and 240 degrees f , or until a small amount of syrup dropped into cold water forms a soft ball that flattens when removed from the water and placed on a flat surface
5. remove from stove and stir in peanut butter , vanilla , and marshmallow cream
6. spread evenly into pan and chill in fridge until firm
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was good, just not exactly what I was looking for. I followed the directions EXACTLY, and it still seemed a just bit too crumbly and soft. Great flavor though. It is, as another reviewer mentioned, very light colored. I think I'll try it again, using half brown sugar/half white sugar, and cooking for five minutes instead of four.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the last peanut butter cookies recipe you ll ever try

these are the most amazing cookies. they are crispy on the outside, soft on the inside and freeze so well. you can't even tell they were frozen! the best part - they are drop cookies, no shaping necessary. if you love nuts, use crunchy peanut butter and add the nuts, if not, use creamy pb and 2 cups of peanut butter chips. cook time is for one batch. dough keeps well in fridge so you can bake a batch every day and have fresh cookies!

1. cream peanut butter and margarine , add sugars and mix well
2. add eggs and mix until creamy
3. add remaining ingredients
4. chill for one hour-i usually skip this step and chill between batches
5. drop by teaspoonful onto cookie sheets- do not flatten
6. bake at 325f for 15 minutes
7. cool on cookie sheets for about 5 minutes then transfer onto newspaper- the newspaper soaks up extra grease so the cookies don't become crumbly , little trick i learned from my mil- this is also optional
8. edited to add - immediately after the cookies are completely cooled i always transfer them to an airtight container
9. several posters have mentioned the cookies get hard if you leave them out
10. i have never had that problem - these cookies have always stayed soft and moist if they are stored in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: These were OK, but I guess not exactly what I was looking for. Followed recipe exactly, but ended up increasing the oven temp to 350 with subsequent batches; the cookies were not finished cooking at 325 in 15 min. The cookies were thin and the peanut butter flavor was mild. I was looking for "Grandma's" big, thick, extra peanut buttery cookies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marvellous mini meatloaves  with options   oamc

a perfect addition to your oamc collection because you can start with the base recipe and then make 1 or all of the variations so that you don't feel like you are eating the same thing for every dinner. this recipe is great for singles too because the mini loaves are individual servings and you can take out as many or as few as you need.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. mix meat , stuffing mix , or bread cubes , water , and seasoning until well blended
3. press evenly into 12 greased muffin tins
4. make a small indentation in the middle of each with the back of a spoon
5. fill the indentation with your choice of filling
6. bake for 30 minutes or until loaves are cooked through
7. top with the cheese specified in the recipe of your choice and bake 5 minutes or until cheese is melted
8. let stand 10 minutes before removing from baking pan
9. for oamc: remove from baking pan and let cool
10. flash freeze on a cookie sheet until frim
11. transfer to a labeled ziploc bag
12. to serve: defrost overnight , then reheat in oven or microwave until heated through
demonstrations.review: I wanted to try this recipe, but I couldn't figure out what to do with the 1 cup of water listed in the base recipe. Maybe I'm missing it, but it doesn't seem to specify in the recipe if you mix it in with the ground beef and stuffing (which I would assume?). Hmmmmm....

target.recipe_text:
my secret ingredient coleslaw

this is my own recipe for cole slaw. my secret ingredient gives it a little extra taste that everyone seems to like.

1. chop cabbage , carrots , onion and apple in food processor and transfer to large mixing bowl
2. add celery seed , sugar , vinegar and mayonnaise to bowl
3. salt and pepper to taste
4. stir until well blended
5. refrigerate until chilled and ready to serve
target.review: This is now our favourite coleslaw recipe, even the kids like it!  I left out the onions and used the dressing ingredients as specified with 1/8 tsp. salt and pepper, but with 1/2 head of cabbage.  Great recipe, thanks for sharing!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate chip cranberry oatmeal cookies

i originally made these at the request of my old chorus director john kelleher, who also worked at seattle area starbucks (i think he'd had the combo in a cookie there, once). i was surprised but very pleased they came out so tasty! these days, these are pretty much the only cookies which are requested and i make on a fairly regular basis.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in a large bowl using an electric mixer combine the sugar , brown sugar and butter
3. mix well to cream together
4. add in egg and vanilla extract and mix until combined
5. add the cinnamon , baking soda , salt and flour and mix well
6. fold in the oatmeal , dried cranberries and white chocolate chips- making sure that all ingredients are uniformly distributed
7. roll dough into 1-inch balls and place 3 inches apart onto a greased cookie sheet and bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes , just until the edges are lightly golden
8. remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes on the cookie sheet , then transfer cookies to cooling rack
demonstrations.review: I followed the recipe exactly and these cookies turned out excellent!  They are easy enough for my teenage daughters to make and have become a favourite in our household.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
great canadian potato salad

i got this wonderful summer recipe from the kraft canada website. this salad is exactly how my grandma used to make it! yum! :)

1. combine salad dressing , mustard , celery seed , salt and pepper
2. add remaining ingredients
3. mix lightly
4. refrigerate until ready to serve
5. best if potato salad is stored in the fridge for at least a couple of hours before serving to let the flavours combine
demonstrations.review: I just made this potato salad and we liked it so much that I was going to post it on Recipezaar, but then I realized that it's here already.  I made the salad exactly as directed, and it turned out great!  I will definitely be making it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s vegetable bake

this is my favorite thing to eat at thanksgiving, but it is good any time! usually the first thing to disappear at our house.

1. cook vegetables according to package directions and drain
2. place cooked vegetables in ungreased 9x13" pan
3. mix cheese , mayonnaise and onions together and pour on top of vegetables
4. top with crushed crackers and then melted butter
5. bake uncovered 35 minutes at 350
demonstrations.review: I made this dish over the holidays when we had family over and everyone loved it!  I followed the recipe exactly and it turned out great.  I'll definitely be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I prepared this recipe as directed, and it turned out great!  It was a hit with the whole family, including my two teenage daughters who are fairly particular eaters.  I baked the casserole in a 9x13 pan and used low fat soup and sour cream.  Makes great leftovers!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry oatmeal muffins

nan

1. heat oven to 400f
2. line 12 medium muffin cups , 2 1 / 2x1 1 / 2 inches , with paper baking cups , or grease bottoms only of muffin cups
3. mix all ingredients except blueberries just until flour is moistened
4. fold in blueberries
5. divide batter evenly among muffin cups
6. bake 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown
7. immediately remove from pan
8. high altitude : heat oven to 425f
9. decrease brown sugar to 1 / 3 cup
10. bake about 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: These muffins turned out wonderfully!  Really nice and moist, and they freeze very well.  Definitely a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
ww 0 point weight watchers cabbage soup

you can eat as much of this 0-point weight watchers cabbage soup as you like. it's so good for you.

1. spray pot with non stick cooking spray saute onions carrots and garlic for 5 minutes
2. add broth , tomato paste , cabbage , green beans , basil , oregano and salt & pepper to taste
3. simmer for a about 5-10 minutes until all vegetables are tender then add the zucchini and simmer for another 5 or so minutes
4. i have tried different variations
5. leaving out green beans
6. adding chopped green onions in addition to the yellow onion
7. all very good
8. you can customize it a bit
target.review: Made it JUST like the instructions but added cajun seasoning instead of salt & pepper-gave it a little oomph. we loved it. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reese s peanut butter cups

nan

1. combine everything but the chocolate chips , and press in a greased 8x8" pan
2. spread melted chocolate chips over top with a spatula , covering entire surface
3. chill 2 hours
demonstrations.review: Yes, these are super good.  Make them once, and you will crave them forever...
