demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest ever pizza dough

this is so easy to make -- no long rising times and all in one bowl! and, if you don't feel like pizza, try just brushing the dough with olive oil, and topping with olives, parmesan cheese and rosemary to make foccacia bread. i have also topped it with a mixture of oil, finely chopped fresh herbs (parsley, basil, oregano) and garlic paste.

1. throw all ingredients into a bowl and mix together with a food processor or by hand
2. the dough will be fairly sticky but don't add any more flour
3. instead scrape it into an oiled bowl , cover with a cloth and leave to rise for 30 minutes or until doubled in size
4. i like to let my dough rise in an ever-so-slightly warmed oven or in an airing cupboard
5. when dough is finished rising , pre-heat oven to 400 f degrees
6. turn onto a floured surface and work in a bit more flour until the dough loses its stickiness -- you shouldn't need too much -- then roll out to desired size , keeping the dough about 1 / 2 inch thick
7. leave to rise for about 10 minutes , before topping with your favourite ingredients
8. put on a baking sheet sprinkled with flour or cornmeal and bake for 10-15 minutes in a very hot oven until lightly browned
9. our standard is 230-240 c in a fan oven for 10 minutes on a top shelf
demonstrations.review: Very good. Very easy. I didn't want it too thick, so I just used the dough to make one pizza and a few breadsticks for my pizza hating son (seriously-I have a son who does not like pizza, I know, that's weird)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my no roll pie crust

the only pie crust i will use anymore. its flaky and slightly sugary and oh so easy to do. note: due to some major discrepencies please use a good quality oil, preferably a vegetable and a good name brand like mazola, it may not seem like it will make a difference but in the end it will, also use new oil not something that has been sitting around for a while.

1. mix dry ingredients together with a fork in a pie pan
2. make a well in the center and add the oil and milk
3. mix with a fork til it makes a ball
4. flatten and press into the pan in pie crust shape and flute the edge
5. bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes until golden
6. one crust pie , excellent for cream pies and crumb topped baked pies
demonstrations.review: Yeah, this is really good and easy. All they payoff of a homemade crust with half the work. Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
calves liver and onions

i think this dish has an undeserved reputation. when it's cooked up nice and crisp it's really wonderful. i had kids eating this like crazy, because i didn't tell them what it was!

1. cut liver in small serving size pieces
2. salt and pepper pieces
3. in a 12 inch skillet heat vegetable oil
4. make sure it is good and hot
5. lightly roll pieces in flour
6. saute in hot oil till brown on one side , turn and brown the other side
7. about 4 minutes per side
8. remove from skillet and keep warm
9. add onions to skillet and fry about 5 minutes till crisp tender
10. put onions over liver and serve
demonstrations.review: This was a smash hit, and I have to admit I was skeptical. But the family loved it. My husband told me it was the best liver and onions he has ever had! High praise from a man who usally remarks "I'm choking it down, aren't I?" when asked if he is enjoying his dinner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
friendly oven stew

i call this a friendly oven stew for two reasons - a friend where i used to work gave me the recipe, and it's cook friendly - you can add whatever and how much of any vegetable you want to the basic mix.  keep in mind if you add a large amount of extra veggies, you may need to increase the amount of tomato juice & tapioca.  (i  suggest 1/2 cup juice and 1/2 tablespoon tapioca per 1 cup veggies).  i have also used v-8 successfully for a spicier taste.  remember - no peeking!

1. preheat oven to 325
2. spray a casserole dish with cooking spray
3. put the meat in the bottom of the casserole
4. add the chopped vegetables
5. now is the time to add any & how much of any vegetable you want
6. sprinkle with tapioca , salt and pepper
7. pour in tomato juice & cover tightly with foil before placing casserole lid on
8. bake @ 325 for at least 3 1 / 2 hours
9. remember not to peek during cooking time
demonstrations.review: I love this stew! Make this stew, it is everything stew should be, meaty, rich, hearty... except without babysitting it on the stove. You just slice the stuff up, mix it up, stick it in the oven and then at supper time, tada- it's ready!

target.recipe_text:
very yummy spicy dilly beans

my hubby makes these and they are sooooooo yummy!

1. trim the green beans evenly and wash
2. boil vinegar , water , and salt in a large pot
3. in each of 4 one-pint jars , pack the green beans
4. to make this job easy we set the jar on it's side and put the beans in so they look pretty in the jar
5. put one piece of dried hot pepper , one clove of garlic in each jar and top with a head of dill
6. pour the boiling liquid over all leaving 1 / 4 inch headspace
7. remove air bubbles , adjust caps and process in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes , starting the counting from the time the water comes back to a boil
8. after 10 minutes turn off the heat and let the jars 'settle' in the hot water for about 5 minutes , remove to a towel to cool for 24 hours
9. try to wait for at least two weeks before you eat them since the flavors mellow out in that time
target.review: In desperation at having too many beans and not enough freezer space. I put all the excess into jars using this recipe.. they are excellent. I put them out with cheeses as a platter for guests and they just disappear. Also chopped finely into mayonnaise they make a terrific tartare type sauce to go with cooked fish. thankyou for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
summer squash pickle

a nice change from cukes-

1. cut onion slices in half and peppers into 1 / 4 inch by 1 inch strips
2. combine squash , onions and peppers and sprinkle with salt , cover with water and let stand 2 hours
3. drain , rinse , drain well
4. combine vinegar , sugar , and remaining ingredients in a large pot
5. bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer 10 min
6. add veg and return to a boil-remove from heat immediately
7. quickly ladle veg and liquid into clean hot jars
8. leave 1 / 2 inch head space
9. seal
10. process 10 minutes in a boiling water bath
demonstrations.review: I'm drowning in zucchini and squash at the moment and any recipe that uses up  large quantities is a life saver. This looks great in the jar and has  good flavour. Would definately make this again. Thanks! Allie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini salsa  canned

this recipe is from a friend's, daughter's mother-in-law (kinda like a 5th cousin twice removed and it is delicious! if you want it "hot" just add a dozen finely chopped jalapenos.  i do not water bath the jars but i am very careful with sterilizing and make sure the lids are sealed.  i you feel better waterbathing them do it for 15 minutes.

1. day one:in a large bowl combine
2. zucchini , onions , green pepper , red pepper and the salt mix together cover and let stand over night
3. day two
4. next day rinse , drain well and put into a large pot then add mustard , garlic , cumin , vinegar , brown sugar , pepper flakes , salt , cornstarch , nutmeg , pepper , 1 tablespoon salt , tomatoes and tomato paste
5. bring to a boil and simmer for 15 minutes
6. pour into sterilized jars and seal
7. water bath jars for 15 minutes if they have not sealed properly
demonstrations.review: Easy recipe to follow. Doubled the mix and split it in half again for cooking, to make a batch each of hot and mild salsa. Substituted 3x 800gm cans of tomatoes in juice, for the fresh tomatoes. For colour and a bit more of a lift in flavour, added about 10 diced pickled gherkins to each batch and would have added some canned pineapple if I'd had any left in the pantry, have made 4 batches of this and given many jars and the recipe to friends and family..Zucchini are a bountiful plant! This is a keeper recipe..Allie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
plum good pickled plums

this is really good with bbq (mmmmm lamb chops) has a nice tang to it

1. wash the fruit and prick each plum with a fork
2. put all the other ingredients into a saucepan and bring to a gentle boil , stirring until the sugar has melted
3. add plums and cook for 3-4 minutes
4. put plums into sterilized jars
5. keep boiling the syrup until it thickens , pour over plums
6. check the jars are sealed , keep for 2 months before using
demonstrations.review: Bergy, I am loving the recipes you are sharing. This has colour, sex appeal, ( in the jar lol!) warmth and a fab palate.. I know I have to leave these for two months however, I am betting will give in and try one jar earlier. Have used the fortune plums , smaller with a yellow flesh and deep red/purple skins. I will make sure to update when the 2 months have passed and making another batch today anyway..have a feeling this is one of those recipes I'll hand down to the kids.. Allie :) UPDATED.. I left these for quite a few months before using.. the family loves it with the BBQ.. will be making this again .

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mild red pepper jelly

we are not so fond of hot sauces or hot peppers as such; it is a cultural thing, i presume. on the other hand, mild peppers are a treat and we love them. so, for the mild pepper lovers of recipezaar, here is my favorite pepper jelly. it can be done with red peppers or green or orange ones or a mix of peppers!! we have this on bagels spread with cream cheese or on anything that you wish, such as ham, roast, crackers, sandwiches, etc.. as a family secret, i will add that to avoid the sticking in the bottom of the pots when preparing ketsups and chutneys, we always put 3 equally-spaced pennies on the burner. nothing sticks to the bottom of the pots this way. try it!!

1. prepare the peppers by deseeding , cuting away the membranes and pass them in a food processor or through a food mill
2. put the grounded peppers in a bowl , add the coarse salt and let stand for 4 hours at room temperature
3. after that time , rince thoroughly under cold water
4. drain well
5. in a dutch oven , put the peppers and the rest of the ingredients and bring to boil , then lower the heat to medium so that the preparation cooks with small bubbles
6. cook 30 minutes counting from the time it started to boil , stirring occasionally
7. the color will be a wonderful dark red and the peppers will be slightly transparent
8. pour boiling in your sterilized jars and close the lids
9. count the "pocs" of the jars to be sure that they are well sealed
10. wait until the jelly is cooled down before eating
demonstrations.review: Super quick, easy and seal of approval from the teenagers, I bought two boxes of capsicums from the grocer that were getting on a bit and starting to wrinkle ( they were cheap!). Good colour and flavour, excellent with cream cheese and crackers. Highly recommended recipe. Thanks! Allie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salsa with  zucchini with a hint of lime

this is spicy and thick. no one will know there are 6 cups of shredded zucchini in this! a great filler and way to use all the extra garden grown zukes! 
use a mixture of tomatoes from green to ripe but not over ripe or bruised.
remove the skin by dipping tomatoes into boiling water for 30-60 seconds or until skins split. check this http://www.recipezaar.com/bb/viewtopic.zsp?t=223941
forum for peeling tomatotes. here is step x step pictures http://www.recipezaar.com/bb/viewtopic.zsp?p=4073734 and directions on making this.

1. place tomatoes in a strainer over a bowl to catch all the juices
2. very lightly oil a large heavy bottom pot , add shredded zucchini and 1 / 2 teaspooon salt , saute to release juices and reduce the liquid
3. add the tomato juice to the reduced zucchini and cook for 10 minutes or till most liquid is gone
4. add onions , all the peppers and chili`s , garlic , tomatoes , spices , salt , black pepper , sugar , lime juice and zest , vinegar , and paste
5. simmer over medium heat for 30 minutes
6. stir in fresh basil or cilantro
7. fill into hot sterile jars with hot salsa leaving 1 / 2 inch head space
8. being careful not to leave any salsa on the rims
9. wipe jar rims with a clean , damp paper towel
10. put on lids and screw on metal bands
11. process for 10 minutes in a hot water bath
12. label and store in a dark place
13. use with 1 year
demonstrations.review: Great recipe thankyou. Great for using up green tomatoes too. I think this would also double as a pasta sauce :)

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
target.review: great meatballs! very flavorful and moist.  I used 2lb ground beef and formed them into about 40-50 small balls.  cooked them in a 350 degree oven over 15 minutes and then put them in a crockpot of wonderful sauce 'jo mama's spaghetti sauce' (#22782) low for a couple hrs and they were perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wild west coleslaw

this may seem like an odd mixture, but the flavors blend very well.  i like it because it is traditional cole slaw with a twist.  this is best when you let the flavors mingle for a couple of hours before serving.

1. in a large bowl combine cabbage , apples , grapes , and onion
2. add raisins , walnuts and pickles
3. in a small bowl use a wire whisk to combine mayonnaise , sugar , vinegar , mustard , and salt and pepper , to taste
4. add to cabbage mixture
5. lightly toss until coated
6. cover and refrigerate 2-6 hours before serving
7. cover and refrigerate leftovers
demonstrations.review: this was delicious. such a nice  version of cole slaw. liked it with craisens instead of raisens. thanks for the great recipe m&m!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best pumpkin cookies

what can i say about these amazing pumpkin cookies... they are absolutely delicious! let me put it this way. i baked these every year at thanksgiving time for my job. my co-workers would come up to me two months in advance to make sure i was making them. one girl who resigned actually called me and asked what day i was bringing them in so that she could stop by - just for these cookies! another co-worker said she didn't even like pumpkin, but she loved these. the consistency is more cake-like than cookie. the glaze on top of these cookies is fabulous! at least, i think so. i noticed a few of you who rated this recipe said it was too sweet. that is why i suggested it may be omitted, or if you wish, use your own icing. lots of you have added nutmeg.. hey, make it all your own. that's what this is all about! : )

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. have ready some ungreased baking sheets
3. in a large mixing bowl , cream butter and the sugars together until light and fluffy
4. blend in pumpkin , egg and vanilla extract
5. in separate bowl , stir together flour , baking soda , baking powder , cinnamon , nutmeg and salt
6. mix flour mixture into butter-sugar mixture
7. drop tablespoonfuls 3 inches apart on ungreased baking sheets
8. bake the cookies for 10-12 minutes until golden around the edges
9. remove warm cookies and transfer to racks
10. let cool completely for a least one half hour , then frost with glaze
11. for glaze:
12. in a medium saucepan , heat butter and brown sugar over medium heat until bubbly
13. cook , stirring constantly , for one minute or until slightly thickened
14. beat in the milk
15. blend in confectioner's sugar until the glaze is smooth and spreadable
16. using a silicone basting brush , which i love and use religiously now , or a butter knife to spread glaze on cookies is the best
17. please
18. i suggest that you keep the saucepan over the stove on the lowest heat possible to prevent it from hardening
demonstrations.review: made these today and they turned out really good. my youngest child said it was like eating pumkin pie with your fingers. didn't have the confectioners sugar to make the glaze for the top but they tasted great without it. will try it next time. thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken tetrazzini  freezer friendly

i got this recipe from a friend at my bridal shower. it freezes well and is one of my favorite dishes. you could also substitute cut up cooked turkey for the chicken.

1. cook spaghetti as directed on package
2. drain
3. heat butter in a large skillet until melted
4. stir in flour , salt , and pepper
5. stir constantly until smooth and bubbly
6. remove from heat
7. stir in chicken broth and half & half
8. heat until boiling , stirring constantly
9. boil and stir 1 minute
10. stir in spaghetti , chicken , & grated parmesan cheese
11. pour into a greased 9x13-inch pan
12. top with fresh shredded parmesan cheese
13. to serve immediately: bake at 350f for about 30 minutes until bubbly
14. or to freeze for another day: after topping with the parmesan cheese , do not bake right away
15. cover dish with plastic wrap and freeze
16. thaw completely and bake as directed on serving day
demonstrations.review: I have made this 2x in the past couple weeks and it turned out great each time. very good for potlucks. easy to follow recipe and made with few ingredients. I did add some dry chicken seasoning (chef paul's poultry seasoning) as I used canned/unseasoned chicken.  perfect! thanks munchkinland for the great recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
denny s style french toast

i do not remember where i got this recipe, but my husband says it tastes just as good as what he had at denny's. i am just amazed at all of the great reviews on this recipe!! my family loves it, so i thought i would share it here and i'm so glad i did because it seems you all love it just as much!!! thanks to all of you who have tried it!

1. mix together the eggs , milk , flour , sugar , vanilla , salt& cinnamon
2. heat a large skillet , or griddle
3. when the skillet is hot , add 1 tablespoon butter
4. if the butter smokes , your pan is too hot
5. turn down the heat
6. dip each slice of bread into the batter for 30 seconds on each side
7. let some of the batter drip off , then put in skillet
8. cook each slice 1 1 / 2-2 minutes per side until each side is golden brown
9. add more butter , if necessary , to cook all of the slices
10. to serve , put on plate , dust with powdered sugar
11. serve with butter & hot syrup
demonstrations.review: this is quick and easy. I just sprayed my pan with a non- stick olive oil spray instead of butter and left out the powdered sugar topping. it still turned out delicious. thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best marble cake

i found the recipe of the cake some time ago on duncan hines. while the icing comes from one of the books of bhg. it is the best marble cake i ever had. made on several occasions for company, and they couldn't stop eating it.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. spray bundt cake with non-stick
3. microwave chocolate with 20-30 sec intervals
4. stir and repeat until most of the chocolate is melt but not all
5. i usually do not let it melt completely , which creates a nice effect in the cake
6. combine cake mix , eggs , vanilla extract , sour cream , vegetable oil , sugar and water
7. beat on high for around 3 minutes
8. stir third of the batter into the melted chocolate , mix well
9. spread half of the vanilla batter in the pan , then the chocolate batter and then the rest of the vanilla batter
10. swirl the batters with a butter knife to create the marble effect
11. bake for 35-40 minutes , cool for 20 minutes in pan , remove from pan and cool completely
12. for the icing: melt the chocolate and butter
13. cool the mix for 5-10 minutes , add sour cream and then the powdered sugar 1 cup at a time
14. spread the icing on the cake when it has cooled completely
demonstrations.review: the cake was very good-everyone loved it. very easy to make. but everyone thought the frosting was too sweet.  will make the cake again but with a different frosting. thanks!

target.recipe_text:
mansion on turtle creek mop sauce

when chef dean fearing was executive chef at the mansion on turtle creek in dallas, texas he showed this recipe on a local television show.  this sauce can be used as a bbq mop sauce but the one he showed that i used was pan searing beef filets in this sauce just until desired doneness. i did make a couple of adjustments.  the original recipes called for 1 cup malt vinegar which you will see i tweaked.  also, instead of the thyme i used parsley and added grated garlic to taste.  this is truly wonderful but you must use shiner bock beer.  i thought i lost this recipe and it is no longer posted.  just found it and putting it here for safe keeping.

1. in medium bowl add all ingredients and stir to combine
2. brush over any item being grilled
3. or pan fry meat in this sauce added
4. do not cook at a high temperature as you don't want the sauce to burn
target.review: The ribs were Outstanding!  I smelled them cooking in the oven and it just about drove me crazy. I used one rack of baby back ribs and the dry spice rub from recipe #104075 and a bottle of Corona beer.  (no shiner on hand)  I put the spice rub on 24 hours earlier and put the ribs in the frig.  I mop basted at the start then about every 15 minutes their after.  The last 30 minutes I just dumped some Cookies Bar B Q Sauce on them, OUTSTANDING!   Had a lot of mop sause leftover and put it in the frig.  It will make a good marinade for other meats.  Thank You for the Mop Sauce Recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sourdough banana bread

i enjoy finding interesting different things to make from alaskan sourdough starter (see recipe #7020 for instance), so i was so happy when i was able to adopt this recipe!  :)

1. cream together the shortening and sugar , add egg and mix until blended
2. stir in bananas and sourdough starter
3. add orange peel or vanilla
4. stir flour and measure again with salt , baking powder and soda
5. add flour mixture and walnuts to the first mixture , stirring until just blended
6. pour into greased 9 x 5-inch loaf pan
7. bake in 350 degree oven for 1 hour or until toothpick comes out clean
8. cool to cold before slicing
demonstrations.review:
Yummy! The Best Banana Bread, that I have made.
Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gwen s butter rich dinner rolls

i have used this recipe for over 30+ years. i first saw it in a cookbook put together by factory workers. i received this cookbook as a gift and have since made it my main and favorite cookbook. it is so ragged and well used. i hope you enjoy them as much as i have making them.

1. soften yeast in warm water
2. in large mixing bowl combine sugar , butter , salt and milk
3. cool to luke warm
4. stir in eggs and yeast
5. gradually add flour to form a stiff dough , beating well after each addition
6. knead methold: knead on floured surface until smooth and satiny
7. cover
8. let rise in warm place until doubled , about 1 hour
9. work done , cover , let rise again until about double , put into rolls and let rise again for another hour
10. bake for 12 to 15 minutes at 350 degrees
demonstrations.review: The rolls tasted great! Made them 4 times already. thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashion buttermilk pie

this is so easy to make and is wonderful.

1. preheat oven to 300 degrees in a mixing bowl , cream butter and sugar
2. stir in eggs , flour , buttermilk , and vanilla
3. pour into pie shell
4. bake until knife
5. cool slightly before serving
demonstrations.review: What a surprise! I don't like to drink buttermilk, but wow it made an excellent pie! Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sharon s ono barbecue beef

ono is hawaiian for tasty. my friend, sharon, always takes this to potlucks at work. she also brings copies of the recipe because people always ask for it. i'm generally not a barbecue fan, but i really enjoy this recipe. it is great on buns or over rice.

1. place chuck roast into a crock pot
2. combine remaining ingredients in a mixing bowl
3. pour barbecue sauce over meat
4. cover& cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or high for 4 to 5 hours
5. remove roast from crock pot& shred meat with two forks
6. place shredded meat back into crock pot& stir to coat meat with sauce
7. cook for 15 or 20 minutes with lid off on high to reduce sauce
demonstrations.review: This is good really good! The BBQ sauce was mild and not over powering.  We followed the recipe exactly.  We will keep this recipe as a favorite in our recipe box.  Thank you for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shortcake biscuits

i love sweet warm bisquits topped with fresh strawberries and whipped cream.

1. sift together dry ingredients
2. cut in butter until it resembles course crumbs
3. mix in 1 beaton egg and milk , add all at once to dry mix
4. stir just until moist
5. knead gently on floured surface for 1 / 2 minute
6. pat or roll to 1 / 2 inch thickness
7. cut into 6 bisquits with floured 2 1 / 2 inch cutter
8. bake on ungreased baking sheet at 450 for 10 minutes
9. split and butter bottoms , fill and
10. serve warm
demonstrations.review: Great biscuits!  I substituted 1/2 cup of sourdough for the milk and they turned out perfect.  Will  make these again.  Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
mama stamberg s cranberry relish

heard this recipe on npr and was pleasantly surprised that the strange ingredients garnered such a great cranberry dish. 
all credit must go to npr's susan stamberg who shares this recipe on air every year at thanksgiving time.

1. grind the raw berries and onion together
2. - it should be chunky not a puree
3. add everything else and mix
4. put in a plastic container and freeze
5. early thanksgiving morning , move it from freezer to refrigerator compartment to thaw
6. the relish will be thick , creamy and shocking pink
target.review:
I, too, got this recipe from NPR years ago and have made it with great success. I can guarantee you that it is delicious. The color is a bit surprising (the same shade of pink as Pepto-Bismol!) but the taste is wonderful: the tartness of the cranberries, the bite of the onion and horseradish mellowed by the coolness of the sour cream and sweetness of the sugar.

Try this one, folks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
helen s cabbage salad

a light, tasty cabbage salad that, unlike many others, has no ramen noodles in it.  cooking time is chilling time.  you can easily eat on this salad for a week, and have done this many times in the past.  this recipe was given to me by helen marcum.

1. combine the shredded cabbages and onions in a large bowl
2. add the bean sprouts , shredded chicken meat and almonds
3. toss until well mixed
4. mix the dressing ingredients in a quick-shake or similar container until well blended
5. pour dressing over the cabbage mixture , this could take two bowls , because of the amount of ingredients
6. do not be concerned once the cabbages come in contact with the dressing , it will be able to store in a large bowl
7. cover and refrigerate over night or 6 hours minimum
demonstrations.review: This salad is yummy and makes great leftovers.  I really like to use napa & savoy cabbages and this recipe fills both bills.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggnog for one

good for those with an itch for eggnog just for one, singles and such...  and its so tasty, vary microwave time to each persons mi cro otherwise you can have a mess!!

1. beat egg , sugar and vanilla with wire whisk
2. pour into large mug
3. add milk and mix well
4. microwave for about 2 1 / 2 minutes , stirring every 30 seconds
5. do not boil
6. sprinkle with nutmeg
7. serve immediately for those who enjoy warm or cool otherwise
demonstrations.review: D-girl, this recipe sure brings back memories.  My fanatically religious mother used to make this delicious eggnog for us every Sunday morning as an inducement to get us out of bed and ready for church.  Although I turned out to be an atheist, I still have fond memories of her eggnog - church notwithstanding!  Thanks for the memories! ~Chef  289860.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quiche in pepper cups

this is fabulous! there are lots of leftovers if you are only cooking for two, but they reheat very well. pick small peppers or the cups will be too big and the edges will burn.

1. cook peppers in boiling water
2. drain well
3. saut green onions , green peppers and garlic
4. stir in herbs
5. add tomato and orzo
6. spoon into peppers and sprinkle with cheese
7. place in a baking pan
8. beat eggs with milk until foamy
9. pour over peppers
10. bake at 350 until set and a knife inserted in the center comes out clean
11. about 45 minutes
12. serve hot
demonstrations.review: What a great idea, Dicooks!  I love quiche of all kinds but never envisioned cooking them in red pepper shells.  The variations on this recipe are virtually endless!  Thank you! ~Chef 289860.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornbread souffle   simple

the best thing about this recipe is that it is quick and yummy.  i have had many people request this recipe after they have tried it.

1. drain whole kernel corn , mix all ingredients together
2. pour into greased baking dish
3. bake at 375 for 1 hour
demonstrations.review:
This is an excellent, easy side dish.  For caloric reasons, I usually substitute low-fat/fat-free yogurt for the sour cream which does not affect the outcome a bit.  

Thanks for this recipe, Missa. Thus spake Chef #289860.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mixed vegetables in a spicy tomato sauce

a good low calorie vegetable main dish! again adapted from a recipe i found on the net

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. in a casserole put in the aubergine , zucchini , onion and mushrooms
3. mix the rest of the ingredients with the tomato paste and the water pour over the vegetables and mix well
4. bake in preheated oven till the aubergine is tender , stirring occasionally
5. add water as necessary if reqd , but the dish should turn out relatively dry , and slightly browned at the edges
demonstrations.review: This very much reminds me of an Indian take-off of one of my fave vegetable stews, ratatouille.  It's a nice twist with a great spicy taste.  Plus, this recipe is extremely Weight Watchers friendly.  Mad props to Girl from India. ~Chef 289860~

target.recipe_text:
green cilantro rice

this is wonderfully flavored mexican rice. i love to serve it with chicken enchiladas. it is a must try if you love cilantro.

1. saute in butter the garlic , onion and jalapenos until soft
2. add uncooked rice
3. stir constantly until rice is slightly brown
4. pour in chicken broth
5. stir in the cilantro , cumin , salt and pepper
6. pour in a baking dish if you pan is not oven friendly
7. cover with a tight fitting lid
8. bake at 350 for 30- 45 minutes until rice is soft
9. fluff and serve hot
target.review: This is a nice change from Spanish rice and I will use it regularly.  I used what I had on hand to make this recipe so I only had about half of the cilantro called for and I also used canned green chilies because that is what I had in the pantry.  The dish was still good, but next time I will make sure I have enough cilantro and will use a jalapeno as I thought it could use more flavor.  Prep note:  I did transfer rice to a baking dish before putting in the oven.  The dish I used was a deep dish casserole and the cooking time was more like 70 minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork roast over sweet potatoes for the crock pot

my husband always requests this recipe. i cook it 11 hours so the meat barely holds together. works for low glycemic index diets.

1. combine first 6 ingredients
2. rub into pork
3. put potatoes in the crock pot
4. place pork on top of potatoes
5. pour broth over all
6. cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours
demonstrations.review: This is a delicious and easy way to cook pork roast.  I can never seem to get them just right in the oven, but I won't ever have to roast one again now that I have this recipe.  I did use a larger pork roast (about 3.5 lbs) so used more spices, browned it before putting it in the crock pot, and halved the sweet potatoes as others have suggested.  It cooked for about 10 hours and the meat was fall apart tender and the sweet potatoes held their shape.  My husband said I should make it often and I've already passed the recipe along to my non-cooking friends as a great way to fix an impressive but easy meal.   Thank you for sharing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chili chicken

great on those cold fall days!

1. remove excess fat from chicken
2. mix onion , garlic , broth , cumin , oregano , salt and pepper sauce in 3 1 / 2 to 6 quart slow cooker
3. add chicken
4. cover and cook on low heat setting 4 to 5 hours or until chicken is tender
5. remove chicken from slow cooker
6. use 2 forks to remove bones and shred chicken into pieces
7. discard bones
8. return chicken to slow cooker
9. stir in beans , corn , lime juice and cilantro
10. cover and cook on low heat setting 15 to 20 minutes or until beans and corn are hot
demonstrations.review: I agree that this is flavorful as written which my husband liked.  (I added some chopped jalapeno to mine as a garnish.)  Instead of using the crock pot, I sauteed the onions and garlic in a little oil then added the broth, spices, and chicken and cooked it for about 45 minutes before proceeding with Step 5.  It was very good and even better as leftovers when all the flavors came together even more.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked cauliflower

we love to eat cauliflower made this way.

1. in a large skillet , saute onion and garlic in 2 tablespoons butter and oil until onion is tender
2. add the cauliflower , salt , pepper , and saute for 2 minutes
3. transfer to a greased 1-qt
4. baking dish
5. melt remaining butter and toss with bread crumbs
6. sprinkle over cauliflower mixture
7. cover and bake at 350 for 15 minutes
8. uncover and bake for 10 minutes or until heated through
9. sprinkle with cheese and bake 3-5 minutes longer or until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: I recently tried a very similar recipe given to me by a friend.  The only difference was the addition of 1/8 tsp nutmeg to be added in Step 2.  I liked the addition of the nutmeg which brightened up the dish and added just a little something different and unexpected, but this recipe would be good without it.  I also steamed some fresh cauliflower instead of using frozen and reduced the amount of butter and oil by about half for health reasons.  Thanks for  posting this recipe.  I will definitely keep it and use it many times in the future.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious bread stuffing

i don't remember where i got this recipe, but i've been making this stuffing for quite a few years now, and it's delicious. it has something for everyone. this makes alot, i usually get a 13

1. heat oven to 325
2. in a large saute pan , heat the butter and oil
3. add onions , green onions , and celery
4. saute until tender
5. add mushrooms and saute 2 minutes more
6. remove from heat and pour mixture into a large mixing bowl
7. add remaining ingredients and any optional ingredients at this point
8. stir well
9. spoon into shallow baking pan , cover with foil , and bake 45 minutes
10. remove foil and bake for another 15 minutes , until crusty and golden brown
demonstrations.review: I made this stuffing the first time last Thanksgiving because I was only cooking for my husband and me so I decided to try something new instead of using the recipe that everyone else is used to and which I find kind of boring. I was a little hesitant about the canned soups, but I was intrigued by the use of the citrus juices so I gave it a try. I made it exactly as written and I added the cranberries. The citrus juices freshened and brightened the taste...it was so good. We had lots of leftovers but we liked it so much, that was no problem. I'm going to make it again this Thanksgiving because I don't think it's so different from traditional that the rest of the family will dislike it, but it is different too. Thank you for posting this delicious recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curry rice

this is a stable at our house and the rice compliments a wide range of meat and chicken recipes. the curry mellows and the rice is not spicy at all.

1. heat small sauce pan and add oil over medium / hot heat
2. cook onions until soft
3. add curry and and rice and saute for 1-2 minute
4. add salt and broth and let come to a boil over high heat , as soon as it boils turn heat all the way down and cover for approx 20 min , until done
5. keep the lid on and try to avoid to peek too many times
6. remove from heat and let sit of 5-10 minute
demonstrations.review: This was an easy and tasty way to make rice.  I had it with eggplant curry for a vegetarian meal so used vegetable broth.  I only used 1 tsp of curry and think I'll use the full 2 teaspoons and more onion next time.  Thank you for posting, I will definitely make it again.

target.recipe_text:
dreamsicle jello salad

this recipe has been a big hit at family gatherings and potlucks for years! it could also be used as a light dessert. i have also used french vanilla pudding mix. it makes a large amount so make sure to use a very large mixing bowl.

1. combine the pudding , jello and boiling water and dissolve completely
2. add the mandarin oranges
3. fold in the cool whip
target.review: This has become a family favorite.  I make it with sugar free/fat free pudding and jello and cool whip lite or free.  I like to add a can of crushed pineapple as suggested by another reviewer.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
it s a tuna salad wrap

try something new for lunch! adapted from the ultimate weight solution cookbook by dr. phil mcgraw.

1. combine the tuna , celery , dill relish , mayonnaise , onion , lemon juice , dill , salt , and pepper in a bowl
2. cover and set in refrigerator for up to 24 hours
3. to make the wrap , spoon 1 / 2 cup filling into each tortilla and roll it up
4. enjoy !
5. you may make this to go , but you must keep the filling and the tortilla separate so the tortilla doesn't get soggy over the course of the morning
6. store the filling in the fridge , so the mayonnaise doesn't spoil
demonstrations.review: Really good!  Perfect combo of flavors.  I like it with or without lettuce.  I wouldn't change a thing.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy parmesan roasted potatoes

this dish is a snap to put together and tastes great.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. place the potato pieces in a medium-sized tupperware bowl and add all other ingredients
3. place the tupperware top on the bowl and shake until well combined
4. dump out onto an ungreased cookie sheet and spread out into one layer
5. bake for 20 minutes and turn the potato pieces
6. bake for another 15-20 minutes or until potatoes are cooked through and browned
demonstrations.review: My family begs me to make these all the time now!  The first time I didn't change a thing and they were perfect.  Now I usually use less olive oil and it turns out just as well.  We like these with baked chicken nuggets.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with black beans and rice

this is a variation of a cuban dish. the balsamic vinegar gives it an exceptional flavor!

1. in a large pan , heat olive oil and add red pepper flakes
2. add onion and garlic , and cook until onion is tender
3. increase heat , add chicken , stirring until cooked
4. lower heat to medium , add 1 tsp oregano , 1 tsp cumin , and simmer 1 minute
5. add black beans , pimentos , remaining spices , and balsamic vinegar
6. blend and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes , reseasoning if needed
7. while beans are simmering , bring broth to boil in a pan , add rice
8. lower heat to simmer , cover , and cook 20 minutes until rice is fluffy
9. serve bean mixture over rice
demonstrations.review: We loved it and will make it many more times.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers garlic mashed red potatoes

even mashed potato aficionados won’t be able to tell that these creamy, garlicky potatoes have been slimmed down with nonfat sour cream and skim milk. 3 points per serving.

1. combine potatoes and garlic in a large saucepan and pour in enough water to cover
2. set pan over high heat and bring to a boil
3. reduce heat slightly and boil until potatoes are fork tender , about 8 minutes
4. drain water from saucepan
5. add sour cream , milk and chives to pan
6. mix until combined
7. mash mixture with a potato masher until smooth
8. season to taste with salt and pepper
9. yields about 1 / 2 cup per serving
demonstrations.review: These were yummy and I will make them again.  I didn't have chives so I used parsley, I'm sure chives would be even better.  Mine ended up needing a bit more milk/sour cream but it also made more than 4 servings of 1/2 cup so maybe my version of 8 small potatoes was off.  These worked well for leftovers too.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: Very good!  I used light cream cheese and it turned out fine.  I didn't use season salt but did add a bit of garlic powder and about 1/2 cup of lean diced ham.  I put in all the red and white pepper, but next time I might reduce the red because it was a bit spicy for the kids.  Next time I will also use low sodium chicken broth - it was  a tiny bit too salty for us.  Thanks for this easy and yummy recipe!

target.recipe_text:
portabella mushroom with spinach and feta lasagna  vegetarian

this is a wonderful vegetarian dish! if desired, regular mushrooms may be substituted for the portabellos, but the regular mushrooms should be sautéed first to release any moisture, to make things easier, you may classico pasta sauce for this recipe or just use your own favorite sauce --- prep time includes boiling the pasta.

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. cook the lasagna noodles until soft
4. meanwhile in a saucepan , stir together the tomatoes , tomato sauce , tomato paste , vinegar and seasonings
5. heat till a medium boil
6. reduce the heat , cover , and simmer for 20-25 minutes
7. in a medium bowl , stir together 1-1 / 2 cups mozzarella cheese , feta cheese , spinach and the egg
8. in the bottom of the prepared baking dish , spread 1 / 3 of the sauce on the bottom
9. layer 3 pieces of cooked lasagna noodles on top of the sauce
10. then 1 / 2 of the cheese mixture
11. then 1 / 2 of the sliced mushrooms
12. then another 1 / 3 of the sauce
13. repeat
14. top with the remaining pasta , then the balance of the sauce and then mozzarella cheese
15. cover with foil
16. bake for 25 minutes , uncover , and bake for 5-7 minutes longer , or until the cheese melts
target.review: We really enjoyed this recipe, and the portabellos give 100% meaty satisfaction to this lasagne.  For dietary reasons I used fat free cheeses and egg substitute without a problem.  The sauce could benefit from a little wine, broth or water to thin it a bit and stretch it, as I too found myself a little short on the sauce.  Great recipe Kitten, thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted mustard potatoes

nan

1. preheat oven 400f degrees
2. spray roasting pan with cooking spray
3. whisk all ingredients , except potatoes , in a bowl
4. prick potatoes with a fork
5. toss with the mustard mix
6. place in the pan
7. bake 45 minutes to 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Delicious flavor and a unique way to prepare potatoes.  I especially liked the fact that other than the intial spray of the roasting pan, there was no added oils making this heart healthy.  Thank you Stephanie for sharing the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
edamame dumplings

from the april 2006 issue of cooking light and adapted with the help of redmeatgirl.  we felt that the filling needed a little extra kick.  please adjust the seasonings to suit your own tastes.

1. to prepare sauce , combine the first 3 ingredients in a small bowl , stirring with a whisk
2. to prepare dumplings , cook edamame according to package directions
3. drain
4. rinse edamame with cold water
5. drain well
6. combine edamame , juice , sesame oil , cumin , red pepper flakes , garlic , and salt in a food processor , process until smooth
7. working with 1 wonton wrapper at a time , spoon about 1 teaspoon edamame mixture in center of each wrapper
8. moisten edges of dough with water
9. fold opposite corners to form a triangle , pinching points to seal
10. place dumplings on a large baking sheet sprinkled with cornstarch
11. heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
12. coat pan with cooking spray
13. arrange half of dumplings in a single layer in pan
14. reduce heat to medium
15. cook 1 minute or until bottoms begin to brown
16. turn
17. add 1 / 4 cup water to pan
18. cover
19. cook 30 seconds
20. uncover
21. cook 1 minute or until liquid evaporates
22. repeat procedure with the remaining dumplings and water
23. serve immediately with sauce
demonstrations.review: Loved this recipe.  Based on the posters opening comments, I added some freshly grated ginger to the filling and fresh ginger, pepper flakes and a bit of rice vingegar to the dipping sauce.  I especially liked that fat that these were not fried, and only a quick spray of cooking spray was neede to initally brown them.  Thank you Ms_Bold for shairng the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuscan pork chops  or chicken  with rosemary

i just love this sauce, and it is so easy to put together, too. though i haven't tried it with chicken yet, i think it would be great with 4 chicken breast fillets substituted for the pork chops--simply increase the simmering time (in step number 6).

1. in a small saucepan , cover the sun-dried tomato pieces with chicken broth and madeira
2. bring to a boil , remove from heat and allow to stand about 10 minutes to plump the tomatoes
3. heat the olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-heat
4. add the pork chops and brown on both sides
5. remove from skillet and set aside
6. add shallots and garlic to the skillet and cook briefly
7. stir in tomatoes with the liquid and chopped rosemary
8. return the chops to the skillet , cover tightly and cook over low heat for 5 to 6 minutes until they are cooked through
9. remove the meat from the skillet to serving platter
10. combine water and cornstarch
11. add to the skillet
12. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until the sauce thickens
13. top the meat with the sauce and serve
demonstrations.review: We found this meal to be delicious.  I chose to make the recipe using boneless skinless chicken breast.  I used a heavy skillet and was able to omit the oil and just brown the chicken until it released from the pan.  The rest of the components of the recipe made a lovely and healthy pan sauce.  Thank you Flemish Minx for sharing the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chipotle spiced black beans

posted in response to a recipe request.  sound yummy to me; i'll be trying them soon!

1. saute onion and garlic for 5 minutes or until onion is tender and lightly browned
2. add remaining ingredients
3. reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes , uncovered
4. serve topped with crumbled mexican cheese , queso blanco , and sliced green onion or maybe even a dollop of pico de gallo
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this recipe.  As each chipotle can have its own level of heat, I would recommend testing before adding the additional pepper flakes.  In my case, one chipotle was mild, the other was 5 alarm (both coming from the same can) so I omitted the additional chili flakes.  I served this as a side to fajitas, and the leftovers made a perfect burrito filling the next day.  Thank you Impera Magna for sharing the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp diablo for two

a quick and easy meal with a spicy kick.

1. in a large saute pan , melt butter over medium heat
2. saute onion and jalapeno about 3 minutes
3. add garlic , crushed red pepper and shrimp and cook until shrimp is opaque , about 2 minutes
4. add tomatoes , lemon juice and white wine and reduce until sauce thickens , about 2 minutes
5. divide cooked linguine into two bowls and spoon sauce over
6. serve immediately and pass grated parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: This was delicious, surpirsingly filling and very satisfying.  I did use olive oil (and less of it)instead of the butter and without a problem.  Based on other reviews I increased the jalapenos & garlic.  I was afraid if I followed the isntructions that the shrimp would be rubbery, so I removed them while letting the sauce simmer and returned them just befor serving.  Thank you PanNan for sharing the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
bake or break nutella oatmeal cookies

i have a wonderful relationship with nutella.  it's manna from heaven.  it's ambrosia straight from the elysian fields.  it's delicious in cakes, ice creams, spread on bread and licked off a loved one's fingers.  i found this recipe on a favorite food blog, bake or break.  it had the magic word it in:  nutella!  the minute i read the blog entry i knew i had to try these out.  these are amazingly easy-to-make cookies with a powerful nutella flavor.  you would think that with nutella in the recipe that would be enough, but noooooooooo!  there's also a heavy, heady dose of cocoa in there, so it's chocolate overload.  and what's so bad about that?  i find it very hard to share these cookies, i really have to love you to let you have one out of my stash.

1. in a saucpan , over medium-high heat , combine the butter , milk , sugar and cocoa
2. bring to a boil , stirring constantly
3. a wooden spoon works best
4. reduce the heat and continue boiling for 3 minutes
5. keep stirring
6. don't stop stirring
7. remove from heat and add the almond liqueur
8. i've also used chocolate liqueur
9. add the nutella and mix well with the wooden spoon
10. add the oats and mix well
11. very quickly now , drop by the teaspoonfull onto parchment paper
12. the original recipe calls for wax paper , but i don't use that stuff
13. i don't even know anyone who uses that stuff
14. allow the cookies to set
15. share if you dare
target.review: Make sure you use real sugar! I tried to use Splenda to cut some of the calories and realized all too late that the sugar is a pretty important part of these setting up correctly! However, I got some sinfully sweet oatmeal out of the deal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican casserole   6 5 weight watcher points

this is a delicious mexican casserole recipe with only 6.5 weight watcher points per large serving!  yum!  (on the new, points plus system of weight watchers, this recipe is 9 points)

1. brown ground beef and chopped onions in large skillet
2. brown 10 to 12 minutes or until thoroughly cooked , stirring constantly
3. drain well and rinse with warm water to remove all fat
4. return beef / onions to skillet
5. add corn , black beans , tomatoes , chilies / jalapenos and taco seasoning mix
6. mix well
7. reduce heat
8. simmer 5 minutes
9. meanwhile spray 12x8-inch baking dish with nonstick cooking spray
10. cut each tortilla in half
11. place 8 halves in bottom of sprayed baking dish , overlapping slightly
12. spoon half of beef mixture evenly over tortillas
13. spoon sour cream over beef mixture
14. spread evenly
15. top with remaining 8 tortilla halves and remaining beef mixture
16. heat oven to 350f
17. bake at 350f for 25 minutes
18. remove from oven
19. sprinkle with cheese
20. cover
21. let stand 5 minutes or until cheese is melted
22. sprinkle with chopped cilantro and serve with fresh chopped lettuce , tomatoes , salsa , black olives , etc /
23. makes 6 large servings at 6
24. 5 weight watcher pts / each
demonstrations.review: Really easy, really filling, and reheats beautifully! Another bonus is that this is made with ingredients I often have on hand. I will be making this often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with sausage  tomatoes  and cream

delicious and satisfying... i don't remember where this recipe comes from, but it's a pleaser! easily doubled.  also, works well with gf pasta and sausage

1. heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat
2. add sausage and crushed red pepper
3. cook until sausage is no longer pink , stirring frequently , about 7 minutes
4. add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until onion is tender and sausage is light brown , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
5. add tomatoes , cream , and salt
6. simmer until mixture thickens slightly , about 4 minutes
7. cook pasta in large pot of boiling water
8. drain
9. bring sauce to a simmer
10. add pasta to sauce and cook until pasta is heated through and sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 2 minutes
11. divide pasta between plates
12. sprinkle with parsley
13. serve , passing parmesan separately
demonstrations.review: This is so easy... and my husband asks for this dish specifically quite often! It's fancy enough for company and easily doubled, tripled or quadrupled! I love to take the leftovers for lunch...this is a definite keeper. PS I use Land O Lakes fat free "half and half" instead of cream to keep the fat content reasonable and it still turns out great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hg s crazy good cold sesame noodles   ww points   4

this was a featured recipe in an email from hungry girl today.  sounds yummy!  sesame treat!  
cold sesame noodles with half the fat and a fraction of the calories compared to the average order? give us forks asap -- and let the noodle-swirling begin!  serving size: 1 bowl (entire recipe) 
calories: 198 
fat: 10g 
sodium: 494mg 
carbs: 19g 
fiber: 6g 
sugars: 4g 
protein: 9g 

points® value 4*

hg alternative! if you use better'n peanut butter instead of reduced-fat pb, your crazy-good cold sesame noodles will clock in with 137 calories, 3.5g fat, 18g carbs, 4.5g fiber, and 6g protein (points® value 2*). woohoo!

1. rinse and drain noodles well
2. pat very dry with paper towels
3. place noodles in a microwave-safe bowl , and microwave for 1 minute
4. drain excess liquid from noodles , and pat them again until thoroughly dry
5. cut noodles into spaghetti-length pieces
6. set aside
7. in a separate small dish , combine peanut butter , soymilk , soy sauce , sesame seeds , garlic and sweetener
8. mix well
9. feel free to season this sauce to taste with salt
10. pour sauce over noodles
11. mix thoroughly
12. top with chopped scallions and mix again
13. allow to chill in the fridge
14. then enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I love this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate coconut iced coffee

a ridiculously quick & simple refreshing iced coffee drink that is super low in calories.

1. combine instant coffee granules with water in a tall glass and stir until dissolved
2. add the almond breeze , syrups and sweetener and stir
3. add ice cubes and if desired top it off with whipped cream and a little chocolate sauce !
demonstrations.review: Made exactly as written except I added 4 ice cubes...made a lot and was delicious! This will be my new morning drink of choice!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot triple chocolate mess

a good dessert for the chocoholic!

1. spray crock pot with non-stick spray
2. mix all ingredients and place in crock pot
3. cook on low for 5-6 hours
4. try not to lift the lid
5. serve with ice cream
demonstrations.review: I made this without oil, with light sour cream, sugar free chocolate Jello pudding and half a 15 oz bag of Ghiradelli dark chocolate chips-- along with the requisite 4 eggs. For a "lighter" version of the original, it turned out extremely well...I think it tasted best while still warm and gushy, four hours into bake time-- while it was still puddingish and gushy. An easy dessert that borders between pudding and cake! A winner! I can't wait to try this with white cake and white choc. chips! Maybe with some raspberries added for fun!

target.recipe_text:
orzo a la melanie

a colorful pasta dish, which can be served as a side dish, as a lunch and is particularly good for a buffet as it does not mind sitting around and tastes just as good at room temperature. i like this recipe because everyone in my house likes it (a rare occurrence) and because any vegetable can be substituted as long as it is cut up small. for vegetarians substitute vegetable stock.

1. cook orzo with salt according to packet instructions
2. heat the oil in a large frying pan
3. saut red pepper and carrot on a low heat for 10 minutes until softened
4. increase heat to medium and add green onions and garlic and saut for 2 to 3 minutes
5. add the squash , zucchini and tomato and cook for a couple of minutes more
6. add the tomato sauce and stock
7. when the sauce comes to a simmer , turn heat to low and stir
8. stir in the drained orzo
9. stir in the cream
10. stir in parmesan cheese
11. remove from heat
12. add salt and pepper to taste
13. can be served immediately , or at room temperature
target.review: I cooked this last night for my fiance.  I made a few adjustments for the ingredients I could not find in Greece but it turned out wonderful!  A double recipe cooks up just as well as the original.  Thanks for a great meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with yogurt and caramelized onions from kassos

according to diane kochilas, author of the glorious foods of greece, from whom i adapted this recipe, you can find this dish, makarounes tis kassou, in many of the dodecanese islands.  she says it's one of the best and easiest dishes in greek cooking--i don't know if that's true, but i know this is delicious--sweet onions, tart yogurt, lovely texture.  the key is the right yogurt--use greek yogurt if possible, sheep's milk yogurt is the best, or use plain yogurt that you sit in a sieve and drain until it becomes lovely and thick.  the only thing missing from this dish is a bit of color and i have found that adding some fresh greek oregano or some fresh thyme does wonders both in terms of taste and presentation.

1. in a large skillet , melt the butter over medium high heat
2. add the sliced onions and stir to coat with the butter
3. reduce heat to medium and continue to cook the onions , stirring occasionally for about 45 minutes or until they are really brown and soft
4. meanwhile , bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook the pasta to desired doneness
5. mix the yogurt with 1 / 2 cup of the pasta water and mix well
6. add the yogurt mixture to the onions and stir in until the onions are evenly coated with the yogurt mixture
7. add the drained pasta and about half the cheese and toss
8. transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with the rest of the cheese and the herbs
demonstrations.review: YUMMY!!  I am not fond of creamy sauce for pasta but I gave this recipe a try because I am in Greece and was happy to finally find a recipe that I could find all the ingredients to.  I was pleasantly suprised by the fact that I really really liked this pasta.  Next time I think I would add half the cheese though.  Thanks for a delicious meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted garlic mashed potatoes   the best you ve ever had

nan

1. separate head of garlic into individual cloves
2. toss in olive oil and wrap tightly in small piece of aluminum foil
3. bake in 350f oven for 45 minutes
4. when the garlic has cooled to the touch you should be able to squeeze it out of the 'paper' shell of the individual cloves
5. mash the roasted garlic with a fork , or force through a fine strainer
6. if you use a ricer as recommended below , simply rice the garlic along with the potatoes
7. peel and boil potatoes in salted water until tender
8. force the cooked potatoes through a ricer or mash by your usual method
9. put the riced potatoes , garlic , sour cream , butter , and salt and white pepper in a mixer bowl , and whip at medium speed until smooth
10. add cream or milk to adjust consistency
demonstrations.review: Yummy yummy!!  We really enjoyed these.  I know the recipe says the quality of the potatoes is a prime factor but I used old red spuds and it was still great.  Mmmm mmmm good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato yogurt  soup

i threw this together for my infant son and my 

1. first peel and slice potatoes and rinse in cold water
2. place potatoes in a heavy large pan and cover with water , just to cover
3. boil until soft but not mushy
4. pour about half of the water off of the potatoes , but save half , the starch that boils off the potatoes helps the soup to thicken and holds more nutrients
5. add yogurt and spices and simmer 5-10 minutes to let the flavors mingle , and serve
6. i like a little shredded cheese in mine , grew up with cheddar , but like mozzarella now
demonstrations.review: This recipe was great!  Very easy to make with ingredients found in most kitchens.  A great meal for a cool fall day!!  I added a cup of chicken broth and a bit of evaporated skimmed milk to up the creaminess of the soup.  I also cooked the garlic before adding it.  Thanks for a great meal!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan fried onion dip

from the barefoot contessa cookbook. this is great for parties. we have really enjoyed this recipe. great with chips or veggies!

1. cut the onions in half and then slice them into 1 / 8-inch thick half-rounds
2. heat the butter and oil in a large saute pan over medium heat
3. add the onions , cayenne , salt , and pepper and saute for 10 minutes
4. reduce the heat to medium-low and cook , stirring occasionally , for 20 more minutes until the onions are browned and caramelized
5. allow the onions to cool
6. place the cream cheese , sour cream and mayonnaise in the bowl of an electric mixer fitted with the paddle attachment and beat until smooth
7. add the onions and mix well
8. taste for seasonings
9. serve at room temperature
demonstrations.review: A great dip.  My family inhaled it. The spicyness was perfect.  Next time I think I would use less mayo as it was a little sweet.  This will be a frequent visitor to special events in our life.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jolean s cheese potato   smoked sausage casserole

this was another one of our favorites in the 70's  very inexpensive and very easy to make.  just recently found this recipe hand-written by my mom, and the warm feelings flood back to me, because this was a true favorite in our house.  little did i know that she was on such a tight budget, yet made things like this that we all loved!!  note:  the meat that was used in this recipe always varied, according to whatever we had available at the time.

1. cut skinless smoked sausage in half , lengthwise , and then chop into 1 / 2 inch "half moon" cuts
2. cook in a frying pan for about 15 minutes , turning frequently to slightly brown
3. meanwhile , put cooked & diced potatoes in 2 quart casserole
4. add cooked meat and give it a gentle toss
5. mix all remaining ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat until warm , melted and smooth
6. pour white / cheese sauce over potatoes and meat
7. sprinkle shredded sharp cheddar cheese on top , and then sprinkle paprika evenly over the top
8. bake in preheated 350f oven for 35-45 minutes
9. hot dogs , sliced into 1 / 2-inch slices or 1 / 2 lb
10. ham diced into 1 / 2-inch dices or 12 oz
11. can of spam diced into 1 / 2-inch dices , instead of the smoked sausage
demonstrations.review: This is great!  We eat sausage once a week and I am always looking for new ways to cook it.  This was wonderful.  I used shredded cheddar instead of the Velveeta but that was the only substitution I made.  My hubby loved it too.  He said it was kind of like a Nigerian stew, so it tasted a bit like home for him.

target.recipe_text:
cake batter ice cream

i made this recipe after falling in love with coldstone and carvel's cake batter ice cream.

i recommend using splenda instead of sugar since there is sugar in the cake mix.

you can use 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract if you please. you can also use 3/4 cup of cake mix.

this recipe is to use with an ice cream maker (mine is by cuisinart)

1. place freezer bowl of ice cream maker into the freezer
2. it is better to keep it in there 24 / 7 that way it is always ready
3. in a medium bowl , whisk the milk and granulated sugar until the sugar is dissolved
4. stir in the heavy cream and vanilla to taste
5. stir in cake mix , making sure there are no lumps
6. pour mixture into the freezer bowl and let mix until it has thickened
7. remove ice cream from freezer bowl and place into a separate container
8. place freezer bowl and the ice cream into the freezer to further harden
target.review: I got the Kitchenaid ice cream maker attachment, and wanted an easy recipe to try out - I picked an AWESOME one for my first batch!  I made some slight modifications - used half & half for whole milk, used light cream, and added 2t of vanilla.  It was delicious!  Next time I try this (and there WILL be a next time) I'll probably add a bit more cake mix, but not a whole lot.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey wheat bread like outback

you know that bread they serve at outback steakhouse? well, topsecretrecipes.com has got the recipe pretty close. if you want the exact color, you will have to use food coloring, but the taste is very good. serve warm with whipped butter.

1. place all ingredients in a bread machine in the order listed above and use the dough setting
2. when it is done , let it rise for about an hour
3. when the dough is twice its original size , punch it down and split it into rolls
4. if you want authentic outback size , make about 8 tubular loaves
5. i prefer to make 12 rolls
6. the dough is sticky , so make sure you use a well-floured cookie sheet and plenty of flour on your hands
7. sprinkle the entire surface of the loaves with cornmeal and then let them rise again
8. bake for 20-24 minutes at 350
demonstrations.review:
I've made this so many times, I just assumed that I had rated it already...  This bread is so yummie and flavorful! Every time I make it for any occasion, I get a barrage of requests for the recipe.

I've used the lemon juice trick on the dough, and am currently making 48 dinner sized rolls (24 to a 9x13 pan) PLUS a medium sized loaf.

This is practically the only bread we eat...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon cookies iii

i made this at christmas last year and they were a big hit, especially with me and my mom. the frosting is a must.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. blend the white sugar and shortening until light
3. beat in the eggs , milk , vanilla and 1 teaspoon lemon extract
4. mix until well blended
5. combine the flour , baking powder and salt
6. add the flour mixture to the shortening mixture
7. mix until combined
8. drop spoonfuls of dough onto parchment paper lined baking sheets
9. bake for 8-10 minutes
10. let cookies cool on cooling rack
11. to make icing: combine the confectioner's sugar , water and lemon extract to taste
12. beat until smooth and make icing thick enough to spread on cooled cookies
demonstrations.review: These were really good!  I made them as directed, and everyone loved them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef barley soup

hearty, easy one dish meal that cooks itself while you're gone. serve with salad and bread, and you have a whole meal.

1. in skillet brown beef
2. place carrot , celery , green pepper , onion , corn and green beans in crock pot
3. put meat on top
4. combine tomatoes , barley , parsley , bouillon , salt and basil
5. pour over meat
6. add water
7. do not stir
8. cover and cook on low for 10-12 hours
demonstrations.review: I added a cup of water, as others suggested, and it turned out AWESOME!  DH loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingerbread  for cookies or a  gingerbread house

this dough is very easy to work with.  we use this gingerbread to make our annual gingerbread houses.  one recipe makes 3 fair sized gingerbread houses.  this is also works excellent for gingerbread people. from good housekeeping dec 94

1. in a medium saucepan , heat sugar , molasses , ginger , allspice , cinnamon , and cloves to boiling , stirring occasionally
2. remove from heat
3. stir in soda
4. stir in margarine till melted
5. with a fork , stir in egg , then flour
6. on a floured surface , knead dough till mixed
7. divide dough in half , wrap half with plastic wrap
8. set aside
9. roll half the dough , with a rolling pin , slightly thinner than 1 / 4 inch
10. cut with cutters
11. bake at 325f on a cookie sheet for 12 minutes
12. cool on a wire rack
13. makes about 3 dozen 3" gingerbread people
demonstrations.review: I made two DOUBLE batches of this because I was trying to make enough pieces for 6 houses, and I came up short (My fault - I kept eating the dough; it was so yummie!).  The first batch was tougher to roll - it was a dry day, and I think I had added too much flour.  The second batch I ran out of molassas and had to add corn syrup - that batch came out stickier (it was also raining), and it fluffed up the cookies a little bit more.  The cookies SMELL great, and the pieces I've nibbled on (from the sixth piece, which we didn't use) are very good - not as tasty as they smell, but still very good!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple sweet scones

this is a simple perfectly delicious recipe my mom used to make for our family. it origioually came from a biscuits and scones recipe book, this one was always my favorite of all the recipes.

1. heat oven to 425f
2. put flour , baking powder and salt into a large bowl
3. stir mix well add butter and cut in with a pastry blender or rub in with your fingers , until the mixture looks like fine crumbs
4. add sugar
5. toss to mix
6. add milk and stir with a wooden spoon until dough forms ,
7. place dough on floured counter and knead gently until the dough comes together in a ball
8. pat or roll into a circle about 1 1 / 2 inches thick
9. cut each circle into 6 or 8 wedges
10. place wedges on a greased cookie sheet- slightly apart for crisp sides , touching for soft
11. bake about 12 minutes , or until medium brown on top
demonstrations.review: I was given the task to make scones for my department's Christmas High Tea, and having never made scones before, I came here to find good recipes.  I made both the Simple Sweet Scones (#66409) and the Cranberry Scones (#13067), and I got RAVE responses from my coworkers!  THANK YOU, THANK YOU, THANK YOU!!

target.recipe_text:
carrot pancake

i always try to make meals as "healthy" as possible for my 1 and a half year old daughter. so, for breakfasts i've played around with ideas for pancakes. i decided to be adventurous and add carrots. your first reaction might be "gross!" but it actually tastes rather good. my daughter loves them and eats them up.

1. in a bowl , mix together the dry ingredients [flour , sugar , b
2. powder , salt
3. ]
4. mix in the milk , egg , and applesauce
5. put raw , uncooked carrots in a food processor until very fine
6. stir the carrots in with the batter
7. spray your griddle or frying pan with cooking spray , then heat to 375 or medium heat
8. use 1 / 4 cup to measure out your pancakes
9. cook pancakes until bubbly on top , then flip over until the other side is also cooked and golden
target.review: I made one as intended, then added vanilla, cinnamon & raisins to the batter and cooked the rest that way, which I found tastier. This is a very moist pancake and tasty--especially for being so healthy. I used almond breeze for the milk & opted for applesauce instead of oil. I made a cream cheese spread for the topping made with 4 oz reduced fat cream cheese,  1/4 cup powdered sugar, 3 tbsp milk & 1 tsp vanilla.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter truffle brownies

for those of us who crave peanut butter and brownies together! from the betty crocker website.

1. heat oven to 350f grease bottom only of 13x9-inch pan with cooking spray or shortening
2. in medium bowl , stir brownie mix , pouch of chocolate syrup , water , oil and eggs until well blended
3. spread in pan
4. bake 28 to 30 minutes or until toothpick inserted 2 inches from side of pan comes out almost clean
5. cool completely , about 1 hour
6. in medium bowl , beat filling ingredients with electric mixer on medium speed until smooth
7. spread mixture evenly over brownie base
8. in small microwavable bowl , microwave topping ingredients uncovered on high 30 to 60 seconds
9. stir until smooth
10. cool 10 minutes
11. spread over filling
12. refrigerate about 30 minutes or until set
13. for brownies , cut into 9 rows by 4 rows
14. store covered in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: These are my new favorite brownie. They are perfection!! An offset spatula really helps with spreading the filling (since it is fairly thick and hard to spread) and topping (since it has to be spread very thin).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole wheat cornbread

this bread is great with chili or stew

1. combine the corn meal , flour , baking powder , and salt
2. add the honey , oil , milk and eggs
3. mix just enough to moisten the batter
4. pour the batter into an oiled 9 by 13 inch baking pan
5. bake at 375 degree oven for 20-35 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Yum! I made this for my Dad, who is a cornbread fanatic, but I couldn't help myself from nabbing a piece before I delivered the pan to him.  Can't say that I'm sorry, b/c it turned out really yummy.  I'll definitely be making this again--and not just for my Dad, either!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one point pumpkin pie  crustless

i got this recipe from my weight watchers group. i admit i do prefer traditional pumpkin pie but this is pretty good. all the ingredients are core, too, even though baked goods don't qualify as core due to abuse potential.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. combine all ingredients
3. spray 9" pie plate with pam
4. pour mixture into pie plate
5. bake at 400 f for 15 minutes
6. reduce heat to 325 f and continue baking for about 45 minutes or until a knife comes out clean
7. slice into 8 pieces
demonstrations.review: I make this pie every winter--I love it! Today I made it using butternut squash puree and it's just as good as the pumpkin. The only thing I do different is add 1/2 cup self-rising flour.  I've never tried it without.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the elvis

this is said to be elvis's favorite sandwich and i know i love it.

1. preheat a grill or griddle over medium heat
2. spread butter on one side of each slice of bread
3. spread the peanut butter on the other side of each slice of bread
4. slice the banana lengthwise to make 4 thin pieces and place on top of peanut butter on one slice of bread
5. top with bacon slices and thendrizzle with honey
6. place the sandwich on the griddle and cook about 3 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy
7. slice in half and serve and enjoy
demonstrations.review: I've been wanting to try this sandwich for years, and I finally got around to it!! I found it to be very tasty but I wouldn't make it again.  I'd eat it again if someone offered it to me, but it's just not my preferred type of sandwich so I probably will never make it again.  It is such a fun sandwich, though, and I did really enjoy it while it lasted.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole wheat pumpkin cornbread

higher in fiber and nutrients than the usual cornbread. makes a good breakfast item. original from an old mag, but i don't know which one.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray a 9 inch square baking pan with nonstick cooking spray and coat lightly with flour
3. combine the first 8 dry ingredients
4. in another bowl , beat the butter and sugar together until fluffy
5. add eggs and pumpkin and combine thoroughly
6. add dry mixture and milk alternately until all are incorporated and the mixture is smooth
7. pour into pan
8. bake 60-70 minutes , until tester inserted in center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Yum! I was making pumpkin puree today, wondering how in the world I would use it all (I made about 15 pounds!), when I came across this recipe and decided to give it a try.  I was already making a batch of cornbread for my father, so I whipped this one up along with it.  It's a very hearty bread b/c of the whole wheat (and I used stone-ground cornmeal as well), but moist and sweet. I'm thinking about making this to serve with Thanksgiving dinner.  The only thing I changed in the recipe was I substituted buttermilk for the milk since that's all I had, but it turned out great, nonetheless!

target.recipe_text:
awesome baked pork chops

these chops remain moist and tender, and the sauce is to die for! you probably have all the ingredients in your kitchen to make this! serve these chops over rice!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. rinse pork chops , pat dry , and season with garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste
3. place the beaten eggs in a small bowl
4. dredge the pork chops lightly in flour , dip in the egg , and coat liberally with bread crumbs
5. heat the oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat
6. fry the pork chops 5 minutes per side , or until the breading appears well browned
7. transfer the chops to a 9 x 13 baking dish , and cover with foil
8. bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour
9. while baking , combine the cream of mushroom soup , milk and white wine in a medium bowl
10. after the pork chops have baked for an hour , cover them with the soup mixture
11. replace foil , and bake for another 30 minutes
target.review: I've made this several times but am just now getting around to reviewing it - sorry!!  This is an excellent recipe.  So, so good.  Never have been able to produce decent pork chops in the past, but now I can.  It's the only way I make them now.  I sub cream of chix soup as DH can't tolerate mushrooms in any form, but other than that I follow the recipe to the letter.  Thank you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate toffee candy cookies  saltine candy

this simple candy shows up at all of my family gatherings .this recipe is quick and easy. the saltines may sound like a strange addition to something sweet, but i have never known anyone who made this recipe just once!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. cover cookie sheet with a single layer of saltines
3. boil butter , sugar , and vanilla for one minute
4. pour evenly over saltines
