2. mix together cucumbers , green onion , yellow pepper , cilanto and vinegar
3. cover and chill at least 1 hour
4. just before serving add strawberries
5. sauce
6. in small sauce pan over low heat , melt butter with garlic
7. stir in honey , soy sauce and lemon juice
8. cook 2 minutes , then set aside
9. grill
10. prepare charcoal grill
11. when coals are ready , oil a fish grilling rack
12. brush sauce on salmon pieces and place on well-oiled rack
13. place rack over coals
14. grill salmon about 4-5 minutes on each side
15. brush fish with sauce after turning , and again when done
16. place grilled fish on warm platter and top with salsa
demonstrations.review: Went to visit my son on Sat.with a couple of my lady friends, he made us Planked Atlantic Salmon ans used your Strawberry Salsa recipe, it was awesome, nothing but good comments from everyone, as a matter of fact, it was the main topic of conversation on the 11/2 hr. drive home.LOL This is a keeper for sure. Thank You Dee.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey roasted pork loin

very yummy! we really enjoyed this.

1. preheat the oven to 375
2. season the pork and place in a roasting pan
3. in a separate bowl , mix together the honey , juice , oil and thyme
4. pour over the pork
5. add the broth to the pan
6. bake until internal temperature reaches 150
7. baste frequently
8. strain the pan juices into a saucepan small amount gravy flour
9. reduce until slightly thickened
10. serve over the sliced pork
demonstrations.review: Wonderful recipe, I had a pork loin roast that I had bought on sale, I knew it was very dry,I had already cooked one (i had bought a couple).Iused this recipe this time, added the garlic and tarragon, rubbed the roast with the spices, poured on honey, orange mix and let sit in fridge overnight. popped it in the oven in the morning in a look cooking bag, then sliced and let it sit in the gravy for a few hours. it was terffic. Thanks Lisa

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review:
Made this meatloaf for DH and myself for dinner tonight, I thought it was awesome, DH thought it was a little Tomato Sauceee. (Just a Little) I will certainly use it again. Thanks Nita.
Jess96

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili jack oven omelet

awesome! great for breakfast, brunch or supper. this recipe is from a bed and breakfast.

1. beat eggs with whisk until fluffy
2. stir in water , powdered milk , salt , seasonings , cheese and peppers
3. pour into a lightly buttered 9-inch pie pan
4. bake at 350f for 35 minutes or until puffed and golden brown
5. cut into wedges
6. serve immediately
demonstrations.review:
Made this for Sun. breakfast this morning, a wonderful recipe, will certainly use again and use for guest.

Thanks nurseDi

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced sweet roasted red pepper   feta hummus

middle eastern style spread for pita bread. this recipe is very tasty and easy to make. this is a very popular dish in this region. the base is usually chickpeas and tahini, but the flavor added to the base vary widely from one chef to the next. tahini is a sesame paste, you can usually find it in the mediterranean section of your grocery store.

1. in an electric blender or food processor , puree the chickpeas , red peppers , feta , lemon juice , tahini , garlic , cumin , cayenne , and salt
2. process , using long pulses , until the mixture is fairly smooth , and slightly fluffy
3. make sure to scrape the mixture off the sides of the food processor or blender in between pulses
4. transfer to a serving bowl and refrigerate for at least 1 hour
5. sprinkle the hummus with the chopped parsley before serving
demonstrations.review:
Made this today (Thurs.) to take to a get together on Saturday, will probabley have to make another one befor Sat.I love Hummus and I love Red pepper dip, so this is a keeper in this house.
I found it very easy to make, next time Imay cut back a little on the cayenne if i'm making it for a variety of people. I love hot but I know some of my friends don't, but its an excellent recipe.
Thank you.

target.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
target.review: I thought this recipe was great. It went together easily. Even my non-fish loving daughter ate it with enjoyment

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered greek dip

from better homes and gardens magazine... may 2008 issue

1. in medium mixing bowl , beat cream cheese , lemon juice , italian seasoning , and garlic with electric mixer on medium speed until smooth and combined
2. spread cream cheese mixture into a deep 9-inch pie plate or shallow serving dish
3. evenly spread hummus on cream cheese layer
4. top with cucumber , tomato , olives , feta cheese , and green onions
5. cover and refrigerate 2 to 24 hours
6. serve with pita chips
demonstrations.review: I love this dip. It is so fresh tasting and a nice change from the Mexican layered dips. I used the Sabra brand hummus because it's the creamiest I could find. I agree with the previous review, it is a really festive-looking holiday dip. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted chicken and vegetable soup

my favorite comfort food on a cold day.  it makes your house smell amazing!  it makes a huge batch, however can be 1/2ed or doubled easily depending on your groups size.  you can used leftover turkey or rotisserie chicken too, great way to use up leftover meats and veggies.  i serve this with my loaded foccacia bread and everyone's happy!  i made the seasoning amounts a little vague because you should taste the soup as you season so it works according to your tastes.

1. place water in a large pot
2. add the chicken base and stir well
3. add all vegetables and turn on medium heat , bringing to a boil
4. turn down to a simmer
5. cook for about 30 minutes add seasoning and bring back to a boil
6. dump in pasta and cook till tender / firm
7. add the diced chicken and cook about 5 more minutes
8. freezes well
demonstrations.review: This is by far the best homemade chicken soup I have ever made or had. I wouldn't change a thing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot  chicken swiss bake

this recipe was gotten "somewhere" off the internet and tweaked by me :). i've made this many times and it's one of those i always have the ingredients on hand, it's simple and everyone i've ever served it to loves it. make a salad or some green beans in the microwave and dinner is served!

1. place chicken breasts in crock pot and sprinkle with salt and pepper
2. cover with swiss cheese
3. empty soups into bowl , but keep one of the soup cans
4. fill the empty soup can 3 / 4 full with the port wine and add milk for the last 1 / 4 to make one full can and add this to your soup mixture in the bowl
5. mix well and pour on top of swiss cheese
6. top with dry stuffing
7. slice butter into pats and place on top of stuffing
8. cover and let cook on low 4-6 hours
demonstrations.review:
When I put my boneless breast in the crockpot they still had some ice crystals on them and I was afraid it would skew the cooking time, but 6 hours was perfect. 
The chicken cut with a fork easily. I would make this again in a heartbeat. I've already passed it along to a couple friends.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chicken marsala

i got this recipe off of the back of a bag of frozen chicken breasts. it was really easy, but tasted very "gourmet". i know you will enjoy it as much as we did. the original recipe called for a 8 oz. can of tomato sauce, but i used the bigger can to make it more saucy.

1. in plastic bag , combine flour , salt , and pepper
2. add chicken
3. shake to coat
4. heat oil over medium heat and add chicken
5. cook until no longer pink in center
6. remove and set chicken aside
7. in the same skillet add garlic and mushrooms
8. cook 2-3 minutes
9. stir in tomatoes , tomato sauce , wine , and basil
10. reduce heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes
11. return chicken to skillet and simmer for an additional 5 minutes
12. serve over hot linguine
demonstrations.review: This was a nice variation on the traditional chicken marsala. I used chicken cutlets, and added 1 T. butter to my pan when cooking the mushrooms because my pan was too dry. I also let the chicken simmer a little longer than 5 min. to make sure it was cooked through. The dish had great flavor. I'll definitely be making this on again...and again. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggs   rotel  bake

here is another easy and quick breakfast casserole.  dave really liked this one.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly oil a 10 inch pie plate
3. beat the eggs in a large mixing bowl
4. stir in the monterey jack , cottage cheese , butter , flour , baking powder , salt and rotel tomatoes
5. pour into the baking dish , and bake for 40-45 minutes , or until the eggs are set
6. cool for 10 minutes
7. cut into squares and serve with salsa
demonstrations.review: What a nice tasty dish. I made it for a quick dinner and my family loved it. I usually have trouble with the cooking time for oven egg dishes like this, they never seem to be done in the suggested time, but this was perfect at 40 minutes. This is definitely a make-again. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s sausage sawmill gravy  with biscuits

comfort food at it's best, this is a family favorite that goes back years! --- jimmy dean has a wonderful bulk sausage roll that will work great for this recipe, you may adjust the pepper flakes to suit heat level, my family likes extreme heat so i use 2 heaping teaspoons or you may use spicy sausage meat --- serve this over biscuits, i also like to serve it over mashed potatoes or fries :)

1. cook the sausage meat with onion in a large skillet over medium heat until sausage meat no longer pink
2. drain fat
3. add in crushed red pepper flakes and cook stirring until the meat is lightly browned
4. stir in 1 / 4 cup plus 2 teaspoon flour into the skillet and mix until dissolved with the meat
5. add in the cream and worcestershire sauce
6. cook over medium-low heat until thickened and bubbly
7. add in salt and ground black pepper
8. serve over biscuits
target.review: Kitten I've loved  your  recipes forever, however if you happen to find Tennessee Pride sausage in your  area, stock up!  This sausage is sooo full of flavor!  And if you  can't  find  TN Pride add  a  few  dashes of  Louisiana  Hot  Sauce....melds through  the gravy better

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green beans from a can that don t taste like it

as fast as you can heat a can of veggies you can have this special side ready to serve! i hate canned green beans yet this is one veggie my dd will eat without complaint. this forced me to find a way to make us both happy. hope you enjoy this one!

1. heat entire contents of the canned green beans
2. drain
3. place butter in the bottom of a serving bowl and add drained green beans , stirring gently until butter is melted
4. sprinkle with parmesan and serve
demonstrations.review: Forget the butter ...Add bacon drippins and at least 1 Tbs diced onion

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: Kittencal, I've loved your recipes for years. Thank you for all your efforts. I have made these with crushed french fried onions, and they are fabulous.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple tomato sandwich

i am only posting such a simple recipe because i actually somehow lived 29 years of life before my husband introduced me to the tomato sandwich. if you've only used tomatoes as an accessory in your sandwiches, and not as the featured ingredient, you are truly missing summer as it was meant to be tasted. note: after many years, i have solidly converted to mayo for this sandwich, with fresh ground black pepper too.  (oct 2012)

1. toast bread
2. slice tomato
3. when bread is adequately toasted , liberally spread both sides with miracle whip
4. lay tomato slices on one side of bread
5. salt tomato to taste
6. slap that baby together and savor summer at its best !
demonstrations.review:
There is nothing better in this world than a fresh Ripley TN tomato sandwich!  Add a few leaves of fresh basil and ONLY Dukes or Hellman's real mayo. Nothing tastes as bad as a sweetened miracle yuck! 
 BTW  salt your tomatoes slabs lightly before  building your  slabwich. Brings  out  the flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker beef short ribs

you won't believe how good these ribs are!!! i think we could have these every other night with no complaints! they're yummy!!!!

1. put flour , salt and pepper in a bag
2. add ribs and shake to coat
3. brown ribs in butter in a lg skillet
4. put in slow cooker
5. in same skillet , combine remaining ingredients
6. bring to a boil , stirring
7. pour over ribs
8. cover and cook on low for 9 hours
demonstrations.review:
OMG Nezz...made this tonight and still going back to nosh again and again. Made just few changes, cut back the brown sugar to 1/4 c. used 1/4 c balsamic vinegar plus 1 c red wine.Added one pack of brown gravy mix. And added one small can pieces and stems mushrooms. This was tremendous!!!!!!
Used wide egg noodles and after skimming off the fat, just poured them in to soak up the goodness!
Something to pack away in the FOREVER recipes.

Thank you MizzNezz

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: This was to DIE FOR ! Prepared as is, I already had 4 cups of chicken thigh meat. But this was soooo easy to prepare, literally from start to oven was 40 mins? And if you use regular soup bowls, the Pillsbury crusts placed in the bottom of the bowls and then filled with the mixture will wrap over and leave just enough space for the steam to escape. Thank you so much Vincy for a taste of my childhood.

target.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
target.review: This is a very good recipe, and a new twist to Chicken Adobo, which is a family favorite.  I used boneless, skinless thighs, and added in a hand full of chopped green onions during the last couple of minutes of cooking.  The flavor was wonderful, and I'll be making this time and time again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden garlic alfredo sauce

this recipe is posted by request and was found on the net-no name attached.

1. in a medium to large saucepan melt the butter over medium heat
2. add the cream cheese and whisk to smooth and melted
3. whisk in the heavy cream
4. season with the garlic powder , salt and pepper
5. bring to a good simmer and whisk frequently until sauce thickens , around 25 minutes
6. remove from heat and stir in cheese
7. taste and adjust seasoning's
demonstrations.review:
UPDATE: I just wanted to come back and update this.  I still absolutely love this recipe, but I've changed it up a little by decreasing the amount of butter to 5T and using 1/2 & 1/2 instead of heavy cream (I also use low-fat cream cheese).  It's significantly less greasy this way, and still just as good.

I've tried so many Alfredo recipes that claim to be a clone of Olive Garden's recipe, but none of them have ever come close.  That is, until I tried this one.  This recipe hits it spot on, and is so delicious and easy.  One batch makes enough to cover 16 ounces of boiled pasta, and feeds my husband and I, plus our 4 children, with some left over.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger noodle bake

this is almost like a lasagna. very good!

1. brown hamburger , onions , and spices until cooked
2. add tomato sauce and simmer 15 minutes
3. mix cream cheese and sour cream
4. in 2-quart casserole , put 1 / 3 noodles , 1 / 3 cream mix , 1 / 3 meat mix
5. repeat twice
6. sprinkle cheddar on top
7. bake at 350 for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a new family favorite!  I did modify it a little, I didn't layer it, I just mixed it all together, including half the cheese, and topped it with the other half, I doubled the amount of cheese.  I also used a full 16 oz package of pasta and there was plenty of sauce for it.  My 6yo son is a very light eater, but it was so good even he came back for seconds.  Thank you for sharing this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with lemon  spinach  parmesan and bread crumbs

this is the specialty of the house in cucina biazzi, in ashland, oregon. bread and pasta seem to have a natural affinity for each other. this is delicious.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. toss bread crumbs with 1 tbs oil in large bowl to coat
3. spread evenly on rimmed baking sheet
4. bake until breadcrumbs are golden , about 5 minutes
5. cool
6. sprinkle with salt
7. cook pasta in large pot of boiling salted water until tender , but still firm to the bite , stirring occasionally
8. drain , reserving 1 / 2 cup cooking liquid
9. meanwhile , heat remaining 6 tbs oil , thinly sliced garlic , lemon juice , and dried crushed red pepper in heavy small saucepan over medium heat
10. cook oil mixture until garlic turns golden , about 5 minutes
11. toss pasta , oil mixture and spinach in large bowl until spinach wilts , adding reserved cooking liquid as needed to moisten
12. sprinkle breadcrumbs over
13. serve pasta , passing grated parmesan cheese seperately
demonstrations.review:
This is such a wonderful recipe! I made a few changes, just to use what I had available in the house. I didn't have fresh french bread, but did have a baguette that was a day past it's prime. I cut it in chunks and processed it in the food processor to make bread crumbs, then added 2 splashed of rice milk to moisten it back up. I then added a teaspoon of each onion and garlic powder to the crumb mixture with the olive oil, tossed to together and baked as directed. I didn't have linguine pasta, so I just used angel hair, and I omitted the red pepper flakes (I think I'll add them in on a night when my husband is here to eat this with us though). I also significantly decreased the oil used, (I used about 1T with the bread crumbs, and about 2-3T with the lemon juice mix) and just increased the amount of pasta water to compensate. And one last thing, I let the pasta cool for about 10 minutes before adding in the spinach, because I don't care for cooked spinach, and this way the pasta was still warm enough to warm the spinach, but not hot enough to wilt and cook it.

Goodness, when you type that all out it sounds like a lot of changes, but it really wasn't, and the dish was absolutely wonderful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: This is an absolutely delicious recipe.  I slightly change it by not using pie crusts.  I just make the filling as directed, pour it into baking dish and top it with a rolled out batch of home-made buttermilk biscuits.  There's something about the buttermilk biscuits that my family and I all love with this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4th of july grilled salmon  or chicken

a friend of mine made this at last year's 4th of july celebration, and after much begging and groveling, shared this super-easy, fun, and very yummy recipe, which you can easily double or triple for a big crowd!   the cold left-overs (if any) the next day are fabulous!  try this with chicken!!  grill 4 chx breasts 4-5 min ea side, then finish in 350 degree oven in covered pan with butter & olive oil for +/-20 min.  oh!  magnificent (great sandwiches w/tomato, cream cheese, and avocado).

1. into a large zip-lock bag , make marinade out of peanut oil , soy sauce , vinegar , onions , brown sugar , garlic , ginger , red pepper flakes , sesame oil and salt
2. combine well , and insert fish or chicken
3. seal and marinate in refrigerator 4-24 hours
4. oil and preheat grill on medium-high heat
5. grill fish ~5 minutes per side , until fish just flakes with a fork
demonstrations.review: Wow!!  My husband and I made this for dinner last night, and it was wonderful!  All 4 of our kids gobbled it up, even the one that doesn't normally like fish.  We marinated it for 6 hours, and I think I'll do it longer next time just to help the thicker part of the fillet soak in the flavors.  Thank you for sharing this recipe!

target.recipe_text:
zucchini or yellow squash casserole

this is different from your usual squash recipe.a friend of mine brought it to a pot luck dinner 15 years ago and it has been a family favorite since then.

1. saute onions&bell pepper in margarine for 5 minutes , add squash that has been sliced and cubed
2. saute 5 min more , add tomatoes , cook 5 more minutes
3. add bread cubes and seasonings
4. put in 2 quart casserole , sprinkle top with parmesan cheese
5. bake at 350 for 30 to 40 minutes
target.review: Can't imagine anyone giving this less than 5 stars. Fantastic just as submitted, but I've also made it with Ro-Tel tomatoes since my family likes the extra heat. Fantastic the next day as well. This is a lighter version of one of my all-time favorites, Tomato Vegetable Casserole from Giada DiLaurentis which is posted on recipezaar also. Thanks for posting, Connie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
santa s whiskers

from better homes and gardens new cook book. a woman in my husband's office makes these for him at christmas time. he just loves them.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. beat butter for 30 seconds
3. add sugar and beat until fluffy
4. add milk and vanilla and beat well
5. stir in flour , then cherries and pecans
6. shape into three 7-inch rolls
7. roll dough in coconut to coat outside
8. wrap in waxed paper or clean plastic wrap
9. chill thoroughly
10. cut into 1 / 4 inch slices
11. place on an ungreased cookie sheet
12. bake in 375 oven for 12 minutes or until edges are golden
demonstrations.review: Having lost several Christmas cookie recipes in a move, I was so happy to make this recipe and find that it's exactly like my favorite! The directions are complete and easy to follow. I've always loved that you make the dough and bake later, and the slice and bake makes it a great one for huge quantities for cookie exchanges. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my chicken parmigiana

this is a family favorite meal and one i make for special occasions, such as birthday dinners. the cooking method of this particular version is different from the conventional chicken parmigiana recipes i always used to make. once i tried this much easier and moister version, i never went back to the "old" method. i often use homemade sauce in this, but a good-quality bottled sauce, such as classico or barilla, is perfectly acceptable as well. i serve this chicken atop mounds of freshly cooked pasta with some additional heated sauce. i have often chosen to replace the mozzarella with thin slices of provolone cheese. note: edited to add that pounding the chicken is not necessary with this method.  part of what is unique about this recipe is that even the meatier pieces of chicken get so moist & tender as it braises in the sauce.

1. beat egg and set into a rimmed plate
2. set bread crumbs in a second rimmed plate
3. dip chicken breasts into the egg , then into the crumbs , coating both sides and shaking off excess
4. melt butter or margarine over medium heat in a large , deep skillet
5. add chicken breast halves to the pan and brown on both sides - just enough to brown the chicken , not to fully cook it yet
6. pour spaghetti sauce into the pan , immediately reduce heat to low , cover , and simmer until the chicken has cooked all the way through , about 15-20 minutes but the time will vary depending upon the thickness and size of your chicken breasts
7. sprinkle with parsley and cheeses , re-cover , and simmer just until cheese melts- about 5 minutes
8. serve with cooked spaghetti
demonstrations.review: Chicken Parmagiana without turning on the oven..fantastic! I did use my homemade sauce and was unable to break my habit of double-dipping the chicken, but the method is the magic of this recipe and otherwise I followed it to the letter. Thanks so much for letting your chicken parm become my chicken parm.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s balsamic vinaigrette

this dressing goes with my recipe #211266 you may double this recipe if desired. plan ahead this needs to chill for a minimum of 2 hours before using. this is very good!

1. in a bowl whisk together garlic , salt , dijon , honey and balsamic vinegar
2. add in olive oil in a slow steady stream until emulsified
3. season with more salt if needed and black pepper
4. chill for a minimum of 2 hours before using
demonstrations.review: Once again, Kittencal comes through for her RecipeZaar friends! I made this for sandwiches (balsamic chicken with fresh mozzarella, fresh basil, and roasted pepper on ciabatta bread) and used it as both marinade and dressing to save time. Great flavor even without the black pepper which my daughter dislikes. Thanks Kittencal, you're the best!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s started in texas buttermilk biscuits

i have been making these biscuits for years and love the almost creamy texture. they always remind me of the time when i was quite young and was cramped on time. i grabbed some bisquick and snuck some of those onto the table. my in laws being ever so gracious declared them the best they ever ate (thinking i needed encouragement!)

1. heat oven to 450
2. mix the dry ingredients in medium size bowl
3. cut in the shortning until it looks like little peas
4. stir in the buttermilk and plop it onto a floured surface
5. work in just enough flour to pat the dough into a circle about 1 / 2 inch thick
6. take a drinking glass about 3-inches across and cut out your biscuits
7. leftover dough is easy to roll back out to sqeeze out a couple more !
8. place on cookie sheet about 1-inch apart and bake for 10-12 minutes until the crust is just brown
9. in a pich , use buttermilk powder or even milk
10. serve warm- we don't even bother with butter but it is your choice
11. makes great leftovers if heated in the microwave for 10-15 seconds and topped with jam
demonstrations.review: I grew up with a mom and sisters who make biscuits without measuring anything. I always relied on canned biscuits but was never happy with them because they didn't taste like homemade. I made this recipe today for a birthday dinner and the family devoured them. They mixed up as quickly and easily as described and the taste and texture was fantastic. Really soft and tender, flavor like my mom's, and browned beautifully. I printed the recipe and taped it inside a cabinet door. Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salad asian salad  crunchy salad  tsunami salad   it s all good

this is a different twist from the every day traditional salads. give this a try, you will want to make it again and again.  it will go with just about any meal! this recipe came from a friend in monclova, ohio. she made it for her kids and they asked for it all the time.

1. dressing: combine ingredients and shake well
2. shred 1 head of napa cabbage and add 4 green onions , sliced thin
3. set aside
4. melt 1 stick of butter in a frying pan on medium heat and break up the 2 packages of ramen noodles , add to butter and cook until golden brown
5. add 1 / 2 cup slivered almonds and 1 / 2 cup sesame seeds
6. drain on paper towels
7. just before serving , add noodle mixture and dressing to cabbage and toss together
demonstrations.review: Thanks so much for a wonderful, wonderful recipe. I did alter it to try to recreate a recipe I lost and for dietary restrictions, but I know it would have been fantastic just as you've written it. The changes I made are to substitute coleslaw mix for the napa cabbage, use less butter, and sunflower seeds instead of sesame seeds. Also, I reduced the sugar to 1/2 cup and omitted the soy. Thanks for a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
dutch baby

i've had these a lot at b&b's, probably because they're delicious and dependable if the right technique is used. this dish is puffy around the outside and flat in the center offering the perfect nest for sliced fresh fruit. it's airy, light and makes a beautiful presentation. the batter can be made up to a day ahead and refrigerated.

1. fifteen minutes before baking preheat the oven to 450
2. have a pie plate or oven-proof skillet ready
3. whisk together the milk , flour , eggs , sugar and vanilla
4. put the butter in the pie plate or skillet and place the pan in the oven just until the butter is melted
5. with a brush coat the rim and entire inside of the pan
6. slowly pour batter into hot pan
7. bake for 20 minutes
8. reduce heat to 350 and bake another 8-10 minutes , until pancake is well-browned
9. remove from oven and sieve confectioners' sugar over the top
10. serve immediately with fruit spooned into the center of the pancake
target.review:
Yum Yum.   These are sweet enough that you don't need syrup.   

I was to lazy to look for the recipe I have .  I just picked two different recipes from zaar and wow am I glad I did.    You can be sure that this one is going in my recipe box.    

Next time I'm going to try putting some canned peaches in the butter and pour the batter over Then bake as usually.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic batter waffles

this hearty waffle recipe comes from an issue of parent's magazine. ive made it every week for years and it comes out great every time. i double it and freeze the leftover waffles and reheat in toaster oven.

1. mix all dry ingredients together using a large whisk
2. mix the wet ingredients together
3. gently combine but don't overmix
4. cook as your waffle maker directs
5. sprinkle with powdered sugar
6. cover with toasted nuts , bananas , and real maple syrup
7. pour on log cabin and michele's maple cream syrup for my husband !
demonstrations.review: They were light and fuffy without having to whip the egg white.    I also subtituted rum extract since I did not have maple.    May have to get some now I know these waffles are so gooooooood.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wholesome homemade honey whole wheat bread

this is the most awesome wheat bread i have ever eaten. it is worth the extra effort and because this recipe makes 4 loaves, you can freeze them and have enough for awhile :) rising time included in prep.

1. dissolve yeast in warm water
2. in a large bowl , combine butter , molasses , honey and salt and mix well
3. add yeast mixture and then gradually add flours
4. turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth
5. place in buttered bowl and let rise until double
6. punch down and let rest for a few minutes
7. divide dough into 4 parts and shape into loaves
8. place in greased pans and let rise for about an hour
9. bake at 375 for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I cut the receipe in 1/4 and made in the bread machine.  

This bread has the right amount of sweetness for us.   

I didn't think that it toasted very well but there really not that much left over to toast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy vanilla almond french toast

i haven't made this yet,i saw it on 30 minute meals and it looked really good. she also topped it with fresh fruit and and orange liqueur i've left that out ot the recipe but you can try it if you like.

1. pre heat oven to 350
2. in a shallow dish , beat together with a wire whisk: eggs , half-and-half , vanilla , salt , nutmeg , cinnamon
3. in a second shallow dish combine flakes and nuts
4. add 2 tablespoons butter to warm skillet
5. place a cookie sheet lined with foil near the stove
6. coat 4 to 6 slices of bread in egg , depending on the size of your skillet , then coat bread in cornflakes and nuts
7. cook slices 2 minutes on each side and transfer toast to cookie sheet
8. repeat with remaining slices and transfer toast to oven
9. bake 10 minutes
demonstrations.review:
The flavor was excellent.  I added the same dry spices to the connflake mixture.

I had half the egg mixture left over which I used in a baked oatmeal.

I found the cornflakes to be a little tough.  Next time I crush them a little finer.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
south beach oatmeal pancake

this big pancake can be eaten during phase ii of the diet and is very filling. you can use a low sugar syrup if you would like; i prefer it with just a few spritzes of trans free margarine spray and a few sprinkles of splenda. this recipe is courtesy of the south beach diet book.

1. in a blender or a food processor , blend together all ingredients until smooth
2. spray a medium sized skillet with cooking spray and set heat to medium
3. add the pancake batter to skillet and cook until sides are lightly browned
4. top with a low sugar syrup , trans free butter and / or a few sprinkles of a sugar substitute and serve with fresh fruit
5. blueberries or strawberries are allowed and would go nicely
demonstrations.review: I added some oat flour to thinken it to be more like pancake batter and 1/4 Bakeing powder.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the easiest  bestest focaccia bread ever

this focaccia bread is sooo easy and tastes wonderful! tons of herbs and seasonings, and tons of flavor!! great to make sandwiches with! you can alter the toppings to your liking. i have made this with caramelized onions and sliced tomato on top...mmmmmm!!!

1. mix the yeast and water in a small bowl
2. let proof for 10 minutes
3. in large bowl , stir together flour , salt , sugar , garlic powder , oregano , thyme , basil , and black pepper
4. add the yeast mix and vegetable oil to the dry ingredients and combine
5. when dough has pulled together , turn out onto lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic
6. lightly oil a large bowl , place dough in bowl , and turn to coat with oil
7. cover with damp cloth and let rise in warm place 25 minutes
8. preheat oven to 425 degrees
9. punch dough down , place on greased baking sheet
10. pat dough into 1 / 2-inch thick rectangle
11. using your knuckle , make indentations in the dough about 1 / 2-inch apart , then prick dough with fork
12. brush top with olive oil , then sprinkle with parmesan and mozzarella cheese
13. bake for 13-15 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review: I have made a few times now.  and just love it.    Sometimes I use  1 T italian seasoning for the oregano, Thyme and basil.      Thanks you yor sharing and thanks you all for rating this.

target.recipe_text:
pumpkin cream cheese muffins

made these for my future in-laws, who will be visiting this weekend. we tried one and they are fabulous. i think toasting the nuts really helped the flavor as well (see my note below).

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. grease and flour 18 muffin cups
3. filling: beat cream cheese until soft
4. add egg , vanilla and brown sugar
5. beat until smooth
6. set aside
7. streusel topping: mix flour , sugar , cinnamon and pecans
8. add butter and cut it in with a fork until crumbly
9. set aside
10. muffin batter: in a large bowl , sift together flour , sugar , baking powder , cinnamon and salt
11. make a well in the center of flour mixture and gradually incorporate eggs , pumpkin , olive oil and vanilla
12. beat together until smooth
13. fill cups with pumpkin mixture until they're about 1 / 2 full
14. carefully add one tbsp of the cream cheese mixture right in the middle of the batter
15. if you're using paper cups , try to keep cream cheese from touching the paper
16. sprinkle on the streusel topping
17. bake at 375 degrees for 20 to 25 minutes
target.review: These are quick and easy to make considering how spectacular they appear.  Got great reviews from eveyone at work.  Next time I will use real sugar rather than the substitute stuff because it gave my batch a funny taste that only I seem to have noticed.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
portabella mushroom with spinach and feta lasagna  vegetarian

this is a wonderful vegetarian dish! if desired, regular mushrooms may be substituted for the portabellos, but the regular mushrooms should be sautéed first to release any moisture, to make things easier, you may classico pasta sauce for this recipe or just use your own favorite sauce --- prep time includes boiling the pasta.

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. cook the lasagna noodles until soft
4. meanwhile in a saucepan , stir together the tomatoes , tomato sauce , tomato paste , vinegar and seasonings
5. heat till a medium boil
6. reduce the heat , cover , and simmer for 20-25 minutes
7. in a medium bowl , stir together 1-1 / 2 cups mozzarella cheese , feta cheese , spinach and the egg
8. in the bottom of the prepared baking dish , spread 1 / 3 of the sauce on the bottom
9. layer 3 pieces of cooked lasagna noodles on top of the sauce
10. then 1 / 2 of the cheese mixture
11. then 1 / 2 of the sliced mushrooms
12. then another 1 / 3 of the sauce
13. repeat
14. top with the remaining pasta , then the balance of the sauce and then mozzarella cheese
15. cover with foil
16. bake for 25 minutes , uncover , and bake for 5-7 minutes longer , or until the cheese melts
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!  This doesn't taste like anything vegetarian that I would expect - it tastes great!  As another layer to my lasagna I add provencal roasted olives (seasoned of course) and the combination beats any real-meat lasagna I've had in a restaurant.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pattypan squash fritters

pattypan is very mild-flavored, so my husband will eat it. and it's abundant, too, so we're always looking for ways to serve it. served with fresh corn and sliced tomatoes, this is a meatless meal. try a horseradish sauce for the fritters.

1. before shredding , cut out the stem of the squash , but there's no need to peel it
2. if the squash is large , more than 4 inches across , you may wish to cut out the bigger seeds
3. preheat about 1 / 2 inch oil over medium-high heat in a deep skillet
4. beat the eggs , milk and oil into the squash in a large bowl , then add the flour , baking powder and salt and mix until combined with a few strokes
5. drop tablespoons of batter into hot oil-- in a big skillet , you can cook up to 8 at a time
6. cook until brown , turn with a spatula and cook the other side until brown
7. drain on newspaper or other suitable draining surface
8. serve with horseradish sauce , ketchup or whatever catches your fancy
demonstrations.review: This was a great and easy recipe when I used some of the excess squash I had from another recipe.  I did add some of Franks hot sauce, but that just made it even better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot potato chowder

another of my aunt's recipes. great for those cold nights.

1. combine potatoes , onion , broth , and cream of chicken soup in crock pot
2. cover and cook on low 8-10 hours or until potatoes are tender
3. add cream cheese and blend
4. top with bacon and chives before serving
demonstrations.review: Fantastic!  I only had 3 large russet potatoes, so I used 3 sweet potatoes and the combined flavor was out of this world!  This has become one of my go-to recipes.  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried poached eggs

wonderful taste to start your day! from readers' digest

1. fill medium saucepan with about 3 inches of water
2. stir in coriander , curry powder , cumin , turmeric , salt and pepper
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat to a gentle simmer
5. break one egg into a small dish
6. gently slip egg into water
7. repeat with remaining eggs
8. cook in barely simmering water for 3 to 5 minutes
9. remove eggs with a slotted spoon and drain well
10. serve immediately on crisp buttered toast
demonstrations.review: Thank you for the step by step instructions that were fool proof for poaching eggs. I used a 1/2 cup measuring cup to drop the eggs into and then slid the eggs into the water. I also was expecting more flavor and was a little sad when I did not get the curry fix I was desiring. However, This recipe sure beats regular poached eggs. It also has a very nice color and aroma. Just wish the flavor was there to back it up. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: I put the dried mixed through the blender for a finer crust and better adhesion to each piece of chicken.  Then I also put the minced garlic, garlic powder, and butter through the blender. Both clung to the chicken pieces perfectly and tasted unbelievably good.

target.recipe_text:
lemon pudding pie

nan

1. cream butter well in large mixing bowl
2. add 3 / 4 cup sugar in 2 additions , beating 1 minute after each portion added
3. blend in the egg yolks , 1 at a time , beating well after each addition
4. beat in the lemon juice and rind
5. beat in flour and cream
6. beat egg whites on moderately high speed in small deep bowl until frothy
7. add cream of tartar
8. continue beating until soft peaks form
9. add remaining 1 / 4 cup sugar
10. beat until firm but moist peaks form
11. stir in small spoonful of the egg whites into lemon mixture
12. then fold in remaining egg whites
13. gently , pour filling into baked pie shell
14. bake at 400 degrees 10 minutes , reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees and continue baking about 25 minutes or until top is well risen and firm to the touch
15. transfer to cooling rack
16. cool completely
17. then refrigerate 6 hours before serving
18. makes one 9" pie
target.review: Very easy recipe. I added more lemon juice, because it just didn't taste like lemon pie. My family loves it. I have made it 2 times already. :) Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry cream cheese pie

easy yummy dessert. make your own cherry mix if you want but sometimes it's nice to take a shortcut. i use e.d. smith pie filling. this is another no fail recipe.

1. whip cream cheese with sugar until fluffy
2. blend in vanilla
3. fold in whipped cream
4. blend thoroughly
5. spoon into pie shell
6. spread cherries over the top
7. refrigerate over night , covered
demonstrations.review: This was so yummy. I added a 12 tsp. of lemon extract to the topping and it was so good I could have eaten the whole pie. This one is a keeper! Thanks. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sahlab  middle eastern pudding

this is a quick and easy to prepare dessert. i usually always have the ingredients on hand. there are boxed versions of this pudding, but it is traditionally prepared at home. you can add more or less cornstarch if preferred. this dessert is so versatile that it can be served warm or chilled. i love to eat it both ways, when it chills it firms up.

1. combine cornstarch and water in a small cup and stir well
2. add milk to a soup pan or dutch oven pot
3. stir in cornstarch mixture in milk before it gets warm
4. add in vanilla and sugar
5. must stir constantly until it comes to a boil
6. let boil for 2 minutes , meanwhile still stirring
7. serve in dessert bowls
8. top with cinnamon and coconut or just chopped pistachios
9. it's traditionally eaten hot , but i like it cold too , once it cooled off and firmed up
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: top stuff!!! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ambrosia pudding

this recipe was originally made into a 9" pie, but i sometimes enjoy the simplicity of using it as a pudding! the junket brand danish dessert also comes in a raspberry flavor, if you can find it on the grocery shelf! preparation time does not include time needed to chill.

1. prepare junket danish dessert , as a pudding , according to directions on package , then allow to cool slightly
2. fold in orange segments , pineapple & bananas
3. pour into serving bowl , & chill at least 4 hours until firm
4. if desired , garnish with toasted coconut just before serving
demonstrations.review: top stuff!!! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana blueberry pudding pie

nan

1. line a 9 inch pie plate with vanilla wafers , reserving any excess for garnish
2. layer bananas and blueberries on top of the vanilla wafers
3. in a large bowl beat softened cream cheese with an electric mixer on medium speed until fluffy
4. add sweetened condensed milk and beat until smooth
5. beat in water and instant banana pudding mix
6. chill for 10 minutes
7. in another bowl beat cream with an electric mixer on medium speed until soft peaks form
8. fold into the chilled pudding mixture
9. pour mixture into the prepared pie crust
10. garnish with excess vanilla wafers
11. chill
demonstrations.review: Yummy! This banana with cream cheese pudding is soo tasty. It is much better than the boxed mix. Soo melt-in-your-mouth good. I have a few suggestions though.. You MUST add strawberries or some sort of fruit (preferably berries)! It's absolutely a match made in heaven. Yum! Delicious! Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red velvet cupcakes

a beautiful cupcake for christmas -- or valentine's day.  the cake has become almost traditional for the upcoming season and now here is an individual-sized serving to highlight a dessert tray.  the recipe came from a book of cupcake recipes and decorating ideas.  i'm sorry to say i know neither the name of the book nor the author but am grateful to have gotten such a great recipe!  note that the recipe for a suggested frosting is included at the end of the recipe, but any white frosting of your choice may be used.
edited to add:  the recipe comes from the book "hey there, cupcake!" by clare crespo.  it contains lots of decorating ideas.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. grease 12 cupcake cups or line with paper liners
3. cream butter and sugar until fluffy
4. add eggs and blend well
5. make a paste of cocoa and food coloring and add to the butter mixture
6. sift flour and salt togethr into this mixture
7. one at a time , add the following ingredients: buttermilk , vanilla , and water
8. in a small bowl , combine the vinegar and the baking soda
9. fold it into the cake batter
10. make sure it's incorporated , but don't beat it
11. pour the batter into the cupcake cups
12. bake for 15 to 20 minutes , until the cake springs back when touched
13. remove from oven and let cool for about 10 minutes , then turn out of pan and onto a rack to finish cooling completely
14. cream cheese frosting: blend together the following: 1 package cream cheese , softened , 1 / 2 cup unsalted butter , softened , 1-1 / 2 cups powdered sugar , and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
15. blend until smooth
demonstrations.review: These were fantastic! I brought them to my family and my relatives couldn't get enough. I'll definitely make them again. The cream cheese frosting that I used was a perfect compliment! :)

target.recipe_text:
easy oatmeal raisin cookies

quick cookie made with a cake mix. really good when you need fast cookies without the hassle. from cake mix magic in minutes.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. line cookie sheets with parchment paper
3. combine cake mix , egg whites , oats and oil in a large bowl
4. beat at low speed until well blended
5. stir in raisins
6. drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto cookie sheets
7. bake 7-9 minutes until lightly browned
8. cool on sheets 1 minute
9. remove and cool completely
target.review: Sorry to be the voice of dissent: I found these cookies to be rather doughy and too spicy. I like the convenience of starting out with a cake mix, but maybe that was the problem: I like my oatmeal cookies crispier.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy pumpkin spice cookies  cake mix

in a hurry?  cake mix and canned pumpkin - that's it!  amazingly simple and they taste wonderful -honestly they're great!  moist and chewy inside, slightly crispy outside.  there are other cake mix cookie recipes on zarr and they're all very good, but this one is my family's favorite.  beginner and experienced chefs can all appreciate the ease of this recipe, plus they sell quickly at bake sales, and children love them.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray cookie sheets lightly with vegetable spray
3. in a large bowl , mix together the cake mix and pumpkin with a fork or mixer until well blended
4. stir in nuts or raisins , if desired
5. drop by large rounded spoonfuls onto the cookie sheet
6. they don't flatten out much so however you place them on the sheet is pretty much how they'll look after baking
7. bake for 8 to 15 minutes , depending on the size of your cookies
8. allow cookies to cool on baking sheet for up to 5 minutes before removing to a wire rack to cool completely
9. frost , if desired
10. how many cookies you get depends on how large you make them of course - just increase your baking time if making larger cookies
11. mine , made with a medium size cookie scoop , take 13-15 minutes to bake and yield about 3 dozen
demonstrations.review:
Great Muffins, but not exactly cookies
I followed another poster's recommendation of adding 2 eggs and water. Batter was too runny for cookies, but made tasty muffins.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pillsbury pine nut pesto appetizer

my best looking  appetizer looks like you bought it from a greek bakery!  this is so easy and sure to please! takes just a few minutes to spread pesto, sprinkle cheese, nuts, in between layers of prepared pie dough,  and into the oven.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. place first round of dough onto greased cookie sheet and bake for 8-10 minutes
3. spread pesto , sprinkle cheese and place second round of dough on top and seal edges with a fork
4. brush top of crust with a little milk
5. sprinkle pine nuts evenly and dust with paprika
6. bake about 15 minutes or until lightly browned
7. cool slightly and cut into wedges
demonstrations.review: Pretty good, and SO quick and easy! I think it needs more pesto, however. I also added garlic powder before baking. Pine nuts toasted up nicely. Used egg white on top instead of milk (personal pref.) Next time I'll try it with filo dough. Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried garlic chicken

i gave this recipe from the "365 ways to cook chicken" cookbook an a+! it's easy and you'll probably have most of the ingredients already on hand.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a shallow bowl , blend together bread crumbs , parmesan cheese , parsley , salt , and pepper
3. in a small saucepan , heat butter and garlic over very low heat until butter melts
4. remove from heat
5. brush chicken pieces with garlic butter , then roll in bread crumb mixture to coat
6. place chicken skin side up on a large foil-lined baking sheet
7. mix together any remaining crumb mixture and butter and sprinkle over chicken
8. place in oven and bake 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I used fresh skinless, boneless chicken breasts and olive oil instead of melted butter. Chicken was moist and tasty! Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pesto potato salad

just like regular potato salad- but with a little extra touch. this recipe works well with additions of other herbs and spices, or vegetables and is great with a few sprinkles of parmesan. enjoy!

1. in a small bowl , mix together mayo , pesto , salt & pepper , and garlic
2. in a large bowl , combine potatoes , celery , eggs and onion
3. stir dressing into potato mixture
4. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Absolutely Fab! Perfect hot weather side dish. Second time I made it cooked potatoes after dinner one night and refrigerated. They were fine the next day- ready to be tossed with dressing. It was a real time saver. Also used that new olive oil mayonnaise (low fat and delicious!)

Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy granola

this granola makes a great, filling snack. good dry or with milk. it is very addictive, but it's good for you, so enjoy!

1. heat oven to 275 degrees f
2. line 2 cookie sheets with parchment paper
3. combine brown sugar and water in a 4 cup microwave proof cup
4. microwave on high 5 minutes until sugar is completely dissolved
5. remove from microwave and stir in vanilla and salt
6. in large mixing bowl , mix oats , nuts , and brown sugar mixture
7. mix thoroughly
8. spread onto cookie sheets and bake 45 minutes-1 hour until golden brown
9. when granola has cooled completely , add fruits if you wish and store in airtight container
demonstrations.review: Absolutely awesome! Hubby and I are addicted! Great with vanilla yogurt or milk. It doesn't last long at our house! Only changes I've made are to use walnuts instead of almonds, and about 1/4 cup of real maple syrup with the brown sugar water. So many ways to tweak and enhance! Thanks for a great granola!

target.recipe_text:
ex mother in law s pork chops with cream of mushroom

this was the one good memory i have of my first marriage- going to my ex-mother-in-law's and smelling this cooking! of course, i begged for her recipe and have been making it regularly ever since. her son was not a keeper for me, but her pork chops sure were! this recipe may be halved by using 4 pork chops, one can of soup, and two tablespoons of butter with the lawry's seasoning.

1. in skillet with melted butter , sprinkle both sides of pork chops with seasoned salt and seasoned pepper to taste and brown
2. put into 9 x 13 inch glass casserole and spoon mushroom soup and smear all over pork chops
3. cover and seal tightly with heavy aluminum foil and put into pre-heated 350 degree oven for 1 hour
4. remove foil last few minutes
5. serve over rice or noodles
6. yummmmm !
target.review: This was sooooooo good!!  I only changed it slightly, but it does not take away from the basic recipe.  First, I only needed 3 chops, so I used 1 can of soup.  After removing the chops from the skillet, I tossed in a half cup of sliced fresh mushrooms and sauteed them for a moment before adding the soup to the pan.  I scraped the bits from the bottom of the pan.  After this was stirred smooth, I mixed in a splash of milk.  This I poured over the chops and continued as written.  Served over wheat egg noodles and a broccoli medly on the side.  This was just mouthwatering, and the chops were sooo juicy.  My 13 year old wanted me to make it tomorrow, or the next day, or the next day after that.  We were licking our plates!  Thanks sooo much!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lentil soup with swiss chard

i purchased swiss chard the other day and was looking for something to do with it.  i stumbled upon a recipe which i promptly revamped.  this has a little "kick" provided by the cayenne pepper.  the kick can be enhanced by serving jalapeno pepper sauce on the side.  hope you enjoy!

1. place all ingredients in a 5 to 6 quart crockpot , stir , and cook for 4 hours on high or 6 to 8 hours on low
2. lentils and other vegetables should be cooked but not overly soft
3. remove bay leaves , stir and serve with fresh baked cornbread and jalapeno pepper sauce on the side
demonstrations.review: This was great soup.  I couldn't find swiss chard at the grocery and so used turnip greens instead.  This had great flavor.  My only issue is that the lentils did not soften as much as we like, even after cooking on low for 10+ hours.  Next time I'll start it on high for 3-4 hours, then turn down to low until dinnertime.  Served with cornbread and hot sauce. Thanks for a great healthy soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fantastic feta chicken

faboulous flavor in less than fifty minutes! compliments of athenos.

1. arrange chicken in 13x9-inch baking dish
2. drizzle with 1 tablespoon of the juice
3. sprinkle with oregano and pepper
4. top with cheese
5. drizzle with remaining 1 tablespoon juice
6. bake at 350f for 30 to 35 minutes or until cooked through
demonstrations.review: This recipe was delicious.  I scaled the recipe down to 3 servings.  I sliced a vidalia onion and placed the slices in the botton of the baking dish, to keep the chicken from sitting in the juices.  I then salted and peppered both sides of the breasts before placing them on top of the onion.  I chopped up some garlic chives from my garden as well as 2 sprigs of fresh oregano.  I juiced a whole lemon for the drizzling.  I also chopped up some dry-packed sun-dried tomatoes and put them on just before the feta.  This was so yummy, and quick for a week night meal.  I'm sure to make this again.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy egg rolls

i love egg rolls and these are vegetarian and low fat!

1. spray a baking sheet with cooking spray
2. dissolve one tablespoon of the cornstarch into 1 / 4 cup water and set aside
3. lightly spray a wok or large saute pan with cooking spray and heat over low heat
4. combine cabbage , carrots , mushrooms , celery and ginger in the pan
5. cook for five to seven minute or until vegetables begin to wilt , stirring constantly to keep from burning
6. stir in cornstarch mixture and soy sauce
7. cook until the sauce thickens
8. add green onions at very end to keep them crisp
9. dissolve the remaining tablespoon of cornstarch in 1 / 4 cup water
10. brush onto egg-roll wrappers and fill with vegetables
11. bake in a 350-degree oven for 15 minutes or until brown
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Thanks for making my first attempt at eggrolls an easy one.  This is a great recipe.  I accidentally cooked my cabbage a bit too long so the insides were not as crunchy as I would have liked, but that was my mistake.  I only used teh cornstarch/water mixture to moisten the edges of the wrappers before folding/rolling them up.  Next time I make these, I think I will brush them with a bit of olive oil before baking.  I served these with Thai Dipping Sauce #33113 as a side to Panda Express Orange Chicken #103215.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish rosie s irish soda bread

this irish soda bread recipe was passed on to me by a dear friend of my mother's who was born and raised in ireland. it's the best irish soda bread i have ever had. it is much higher, lighter and softer than most other recipes i have seen. it has an excellent flavor and texture, as well.

1. combine dry ingredients together in a large bowl
2. in a small bowl beat eggs and stir in sour cream
3. add the egg and sour cream mixture to the dry ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon
4. batter will be very thick
5. add the raisins and caraway seeds and stir well with wooden spoon or knead in with your hands
6. place batter in a greased 9 inch springform pan
7. dust the top with enough flour so that you can pat the batter like a bread dough evenly in the pan without it sticking to your hands
8. with a knife make a shallow crisscross on the top
9. bake for 50 minutes in a preheated 350f oven
demonstrations.review: This was my first attempt to make Irish soda bread and WOW, it sure was a hit with the family!  I followed the recipe to a "T" and couldn't be more pleased.  My DH stated that he wanted another loaf next weekend!  I served this with Corned Beef and Cabbage in Guinness Recipe #86868 and our family of 5 enjoyed a wonderful St. Patty's Day feast.  This recipe combo will become our annual keeper feast.  Thanks so much for a great recipe 1Steve.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot  chicken tortilla soup

a quick, no-fuss version of chicken tortilla soup! all you do is put everything into the slow cooker, and turn it on. then garnish with baked corn tortilla strips. what a dish.

1. place chicken , tomatoes , enchilada sauce , onion , green chilies , and garlic into a slow cooker
2. pour in water and chicken broth
3. season with cumin , chili powder , salt , pepper , and bay leaf
4. stir in corn and cilantro
5. cover , and cook on low setting for 6 to 8 hours or on high setting for 3 to 4 hours
6. garnish with fresh tortilla strips or tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: I would make this 5 stars with my changes.  I thought I had chili powder, but didn't.  So instead used about 1-1/2 Tbs peppers in adobo (pureed) and instead of adding corn, I added drained and rinsed black beans.  It was delicious topped with sour cream, shredded cheese, crushed tortillas, avocado, sliced black olives, etc.  Very easy and will definitely do this one again!

target.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
target.review: This recipe was terrific!  I used an onion brown gravy mix, all of the ranch dressing mix, and about 3/4 of the italian mix.  Mixed the ingredients and rubbed them onto a chuck eye roast and whenever it wouldn't stick to the meat any more I poured the rest of the mixes on top of the meat.  I put about 3/4 cup of water around the meat and cooked on low for about 8 1/2 hours and it was delicious.  As for the comments about being too salty, it was salty tasting, but not too salty for this family!  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory chuck roast

one of the best pot roasts i have ever made. it has a thick rich gravy and amazing flavor.

1. cut 8-10 slits in roast , sprinkle with vinegar and garlic salt then dredge in flour
2. brown roast on all sides in hot oil
3. transfer to baking pan or slow cooker
4. stir together soup mix , sherry and coffee
5. pour over roast
6. add mushrooms
7. bake at 350 for 3 hours
demonstrations.review: It was the best chuck roast I've ever had.  My husband loved it and my children, who normally would not eat anything like a roast, liked it.  White vinegar is listed as an ingredient, however, there is no mention of it in the directions.  I stirred it in with the soup mix, sherry, and coffee.  I assume that was correct because it sure was good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oh my d lux chocolate chip cookies

these are definitely not your standard chocolate chip cookies! they are of the "oh my" variety, which is what you'll say after the first bite! the addition of rice krispies may seem odd, but these are great and a favorite of kids of all ages. an extra plus...this recipe make about 7 1/2 dozen cookies :) (don't worry, you'll have no problem getting rid of them all!)

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cream butter and add sugar , beating at low speed until light and fluffy
3. add eggs and vanilla and beat well
4. combine flour and baking powder and add to creamed mixture until well combined
5. stir in remaining ingredients
6. drop by heaping teaspoonfuls onto baking sheets
7. bake for 10-12 minutes or until lightly browned
8. cool on wire racks
demonstrations.review: These are a great variation of the chocolate chip cookies I normally make.  The Rice Krispies and coconut make them very crispy.  Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate caramel cashew chewies

these bars are so good! if you love cashews, chocolate (who doesn't) and caramels, you will love these. they are pretty easy and come out looking and tasting like they were difficult to make :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 9 x 13 inch pan
3. in a large bowl , beat brown sugar and butter until light and fluffy and then beat in egg
4. stir in flour and oats and blend well
5. press into prepared pan
6. bake for 15- 18 minutes until light brown
7. in a medium saucepan combine caramels and half and half and cook over low heat until caramels are melted and mixture is smooth , stirring occasionally
8. pour caramel mixture over baked crust
9. sprinkle with cashews and chocolate
10. bake an additional 8- 10 minutes or until chocolate is softened and caramel begins to bubble around edges of pan
11. cool completely and refrigerate to set chocolate
12. cut into bars
demonstrations.review: How can I put a proper rating on this?....sinfully delicious!!  This is so easy to make and a great recipe for kids to help out!  Don't want to unwrap all those caramels?  It was a great and enjoyable job for my 4 and 6 year old children.  Very scrumptious!  Will definitely be a new entry into my cookbook!  Thanks for the great recipe Karen!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pasta supreme

moist and saucy chicken with great flavor.

1. cook fettuccine according to pkg directions
2. cut chicken into 2 inch pieces
3. in skillet saute chicken in butter until browned and no longer pink
4. add cream , basil , parmesan and pepper flakes
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer 3 minutes , stirring often
7. drain fettuccine well
8. toss with sauce to coat well
demonstrations.review: As usual, absolutely wonderful!  I love your recipes!  The only thing I did differently was to saute the chicken in olive oil instead of butter.  Thanks for another terrific recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the world s best sugar cookies

i found this recipe in the houston chronicle, and i think it really is the best sugar cookie recipe! it's the best one i've tried!!!

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. beat oil and butter until blended
3. add powdered sugar and 1 cup sugar
4. beat well
5. beat in eggs and vanilla
6. sift flour , soda , cream of tartar and salt together
7. stir into sugar mixture
8. mix well
9. chill at least 2 hours
10. roll into 1-inch balls
11. roll balls in sugar
12. place cookies on ungreased cookie sheet and flatten with bottom of glass dipped in sugar
13. the cookies should be flattened to 2-inch rounds
14. don't flatten too thin
15. bake for 10-14 minutes or until brown around the edges
demonstrations.review: This recipe is terrific!  We loved the taste and texture and it's a great recipe to let kids help out.  I rolled some of the cookies in sugar with cinnamon and they were even better, but we really like cinnamon.  Thanks for a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
the classic french bistro sandwich   croque monsieur

my two versions of this classic french café/bistro sandwich - oven baked for large quantities and ease.......or, the traditional frying pan/skillet method! you can always rely upon the french to add a certain "je ne sais quoi" to even the simplest food ...including the humble cheese and ham sandwich. the croque-monsieur (which becomes a croque-madame if you top it with a fried egg) is a great favourite in french cafés & bistros, and there are as many methods of crafting it as there are cafés! this one works for me. but, please be warned ... it's not for calorie-counters, the cholesterol police or those of a nervous disposition!!

1. spread the bread with some of the softened butter , make 4 sandwiches , each with one slice of ham and one slice of cheese
2. press them firmly together
3. beat the eggs with the water , add the salt and pepper to taste , and dip the sandwiches into the egg mixture , coating all sides well
4. heat the rest of the butter in a heavy- bottomed frying pan / skillet , when it has melted and is very hot - but not brown , fry the sandwiches for about 5 - 8 minutes , turning once
5. serve immediately
6. if you prefer , although it is not traditional , you may place the croque-monsieur into a very well-buttered baking pan and bake in a moderately hot oven - 175c / 350f - turning once , for about 10 to 15 minutes
7. it is easier to prepare a larger number this way and keep them warm until you are ready to serve them
target.review: This was a recipe that my French teacher suggested we try.  It is a great ham and cheese sandwich with french toast sides.  I added some chives and capers to my sandwich for a little added flavor.  Made for ZWT5 for the Genies of Gourmet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french pie pastry

my daughter in law is from france and this is how she makes her pie crusts. i think this is far superior to the ones made with shortening and the crust is much flakier. hope you like it!

1. place flour and salt in food processor and pulse a couple times
2. add butter and process until mixture resembles coarse crumbs
3. add water 1 t at a time through top feeder and pulse briefly until dough begins to form a ball
4. remove from processor and place on floured surface
5. form into a ball
6. allow dough to rest at room temperature for 30 minutes before rolling out
7. on lightly floured surface , roll out dough to fit pie pan
8. place in pan , flute edges and prick bottom of dough several times with a fork
9. place in freezer for 15 to 20 minutes
10. preheat oven to 425 degrees
11. bake pie shell for 15 to 20 minutes or til light brown
demonstrations.review: As a big fan of french desserts, this is splendid!!! I'm a believer!! Why would anyone ever make any other kind of crust. Crusts with shortening are hard to roll and they fall apart alot but this was elasticy and very easy. It was like I popped the ingredients in the processor and VOILA! Perfect ball of pie crust. Thank you very much for submitting this recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey sesame pork tenderloin

we love this variation of pork tenderloin. it's excellent served over rice.  delicious! the prep time does not include marinating, which is 2 hours.
enjoy!

1. combine soy sauce , ginger , garlic and sesame oil
2. place tenderloin in a resealable plastic food storage bag and pour the soy sauce mixture into it
3. marinate for 2 hours in the refrigerator
4. i do not recommend marinating this any longer than 2 hours - as the pork will become too salty tasting
5. preheat oven to 375 degrees
6. remove pork from marinade and pat dry with a paper towel
7. mix honey and brown sugar on a plate
8. place sesame seeds on another plate
9. roll pork in honey mixture and then roll in the sesame seeds
10. roast in a shallow pan for 20 to 30 minutes or until meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part registers 160 degrees
11. suggested to serve over rice
demonstrations.review:
I made this for a dinner for my family.  MY family loved it especially me and my brother.  We will make this a lot.
Made for PAC Spring 2010.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon tea cookies

i love tart lemon desserts.  this is a recipe i found on betty crocker that looks very good.

1. in large bowl , beat butter , 1 / 3 c powdered sugar , and vanilla with mixer on medium speed until well blended
2. stir in flour until dough forms
3. cover
4. refrigerate 30 minutes
5. heat oven to 350f shape dough into 1" balls
6. place balls 2" apart
7. press thumb into center of each ball to make indentation
8. bake 8 to 10 minutes or until golden brown
9. remove to cooling racks and cool completely , about 30 minutes
10. in 1 qt saucepan , heat all filling ingredients over low heat about 25 minutes , stirring constantly , until smooth and thickened
11. cool about 15 minutes
12. fill each thumbprint with rounded 1 / 4 tsp filling
13. sprinkle 1 t powdered sugar over cookies
demonstrations.review: These are very good, very tart. The reason I give this 4 stars and not 5 is mostly because the lemon glaze is really hard to keep control of. If I made these again I would add a bit more cornstarch I think, because the glaze ran out of the holes that were a pain to make as the dough kept sticking to my fingers and disfiguring the cookies. But here I am just giving my mom a hard time. xD Don't listen to me. Great cookies. Made for ZWT5.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy oatmeal chocolate chip cookies

a friend brought these to a picnic. after one taste of the warm-from-the-oven cookie, i knew i had to have the recipe. these are now the most requested cookie by my family. the recipe makes a huge batch of big cookies, but they do freeze very well. the 5 dozen amount is a guess, i've never counted! we love these and hope you will too!

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees f
2. cream together , using a stand mixer: butter , sugar and brown sugar
3. add the eggs , one at a time , and the vanilla
4. blend well
5. blend 2 1 / 2 cups of the oatmeal in a food processor or blender
6. in a separate large bowl , mix together: flour , all of the oatmeal , salt , baking powder and baking soda
