7. add the dry mixture , on low - a bit at a time , to the wet ingredients and blend together until fully incorporated
8. add the chocolate chips and blend in on low
9. scoop balls onto cookie sheets , spaced a few inches apart
10. i like to make them about 1 inch balls
11. bake for about 10 minutes , depending on your oven
12. get the gallon of milk ready !
demonstrations.review: Dad and I made these for our church's weekly Kids' Club.  It made at least six dozen, so we froze some for later weeks, ate some at home, and sent some to Dad's work. They're terrific and everybody loves them.  Made for PAC.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lasagna in a skillet   in about 30 minutes

what i love about this recipe, is that it's possible to have lasagna within approx. 30 minutes and only have one pan to wash! it's an easy weeknight recipe to prepare. comfort food with ease. :)  this is an adaption from cook's illustrated. *note: i use preshredded cheeses for quick prep. the 30 minute time is what the original recipe states, and the time it takes me to prepare - however, the time is an approximation and may take a bit longer. enjoy!

1. cook meat in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat , breaking it into pieces with a wooden spoon , for about 5 minutes
2. drain meat and return to skillet
3. stir in garlic , red pepper flakes and 1 / 2 t
4. salt and cook over medium-high heat until fragrant
5. sprinkle broken lasagna noodles into the skillet , then pour in marinara sauce and water over the top
6. cover and cook , stirring often and adjusting heat as necessary to maintain a vigorous simmer , until noodles are tender
7. take the skillet off the heat source and stir in half of the mozzarella and half of the parmesan
8. season with salt and pepper
9. dot heaping tablespoons of ricotta over the noodles , then sprinkle with remaining mozzarella and parmesan
10. cover and let stand off heat until the cheeses melt
11. sprinkle with basil before serving
demonstrations.review: My family loved this.  We love lasagne and this was a quick and easy way to get it.  Made for PAC Spring 2010.

target.recipe_text:
mongolian beef

this is a good one for mongolian beef.

1. combine meat , soy sauce , cornstarch , oil , sugar , salt , and pepper and refrigerate at least 1 hour
2. in 375 degree wok , cook garlic and ginger in oil for 3-5 minutes
3. add remaining ingredients , including meat mixture
4. stir fry for 5-10 minutes , or until meat is cooked through
target.review: This was a wonderful addition to my "Chinese" night.  Great success.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate surprise cake

this is best, in my opinion, served warm right out of the oven. i like to make in individual dishes. i just divide the 

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. melt the chocolate and butter together over hot water
3. meanwhile , sift together 1 1 / 4 cups of the sugar , sifted flour , baking powder and salt
4. stir the dry mixture into the chocolate mixture and blend
5. stir in milk and vanilla
6. pour into a greased , square 9 by 9-inch cake pan
7. mix brown sugar , remaining 1 / 4 cup sugar and cocoa powder and sprinkle over the batter
8. pour coffee over and bake for 40 minutes
9. serve warm or cold from the pan
demonstrations.review: I made this in coffee cups.  Turned out GREAT!!  LOL, Just as good as when you make it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bergy dim sum  5  steamed shrimp dumplings

the right name for this appetizer is har gow. this can also be part of a dim sum brunch.for a dim sum brunch you would usually serve about 8-10 dishes different dishes, depending on the appetites of your guests. this recipe can be frozen and when you wish to serve it take it frozen and steam them over very high heat. i prefer to freeze them unsteamed. these are tasty!

1. sift flour and salt into a bowl of mixer fitted with the dough paddle and quickly add the boiling water
2. mix until springy
3. when cool enough to touch , knead a few times on an oiled surface
4. if you do not have a mixer , after you have added the water to the flour / salt work the dough with the handle of a wooden spoon until it is cool enough to knead by hand
5. then knead on an oiled surface until springy
6. cover with a damp cloth and set aside
7. mix shrimp , water chestnuts , soy sauce , sugar and cornstarch with your fingers until sticky
8. refrigerate for 30 minutes
9. roll the dough out into a long sausage and cut off pieces
10. roll out each piece into a thin round
11. place a teaspoon of the filling on each round and pinch the edges together
12. oil your steamer and place the dumplings in it and steam over high heat for 8-9 minutes
13. serve with a spicy chili sauce or soy mixed with hot mustard
demonstrations.review: Bergy, I can't believe Lali hasn't rated this.  She is the one who told me about it.  This was one of my dishes on "Chinese" night.  A Great Success!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
p  f  chang s chicken lettuce wraps by todd wilbur

update: this recipe was created by todd wilbur for his cookbook "top secret restaurant recipes 2" (penguin random house 2007). www.topsecretrecipes.com. 

another version of the chicken lettuce wraps.

1. make the special sauce by dissolving the sugar in water in a small bowl
2. add soy sauce , rice wine vinegar , ketchup , lemon juice and sesame oil
3. mix well and refrigerate this sauce until you're ready to serve
4. combine the hot water with the hot mustard and set this aside as well
5. eventually add your desired measurement of mustard and garlic chili sauce to the special sauce mixture to pour over the wraps
6. bring oil to high heat in a wok or large frying pan
7. saute chicken breasts for 4 to 5 minutes per side or done
8. remove chicken from the pan and cool
9. keep oil in the pan , keep hot
10. as chicken cools mince water chestnuts and mushrooms to about the size of small peas
11. prepare the stir fry sauce by mixing the soy sauce , brown sugar , and rice vinegar together in a small bowl
12. when chicken is cool , mince it as the mushrooms and water chestnuts are
13. with the pan still on high heat , add another tbsp of vegetable oil
14. add chicken , garlic , onions , water chestnuts and mushrooms to pan
15. add stir fry sauce to pan , saute mixture a couple minutes then serve in lettuce leaves
demonstrations.review: These were so good and easy to make.  I too made both Chili's and these.  They are so close to the same.  Can't say which is best. Thanks Lali.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma bessie s beef stew

grandma's beef stew. this was passed down from grandma's mother to grandma to my mom to me.

1. if it is cool or cold weather , it is best to put this in the oven and let cook for a while
2. take a large pot on med high heat and add whole bottle of ketchup
3. fill empty bottle with water and rinse out bottle with it , pour this water in pot with ketchup
4. add carrots , celery , potatoes , garlic and onion
5. when all of this has been cooking for a 1 / 2 hour or so , coat meat with flour and brown in large pan with a little oil
6. cover with a lid and let this simmer for a few minutes
7. meat will be soooooo tender
8. add meat mixture to the veggies
9. mix well
10. add the salt and pepper
11. let this cook until it is thick and the veggies are tender
12. the"secret" is the ketchup
13. the stew doesn't taste a thing like ketchup though
demonstrations.review: Thanks Lali, this turned out so very good.  We had company over and Everyone Raved about this.  Not much in the way of leftovers either.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot german potato salad

this was passed down from my great-great-grand mother who came from germany in the 1800's.

1. dice and fry bacon
2. in a small bowl , add eggs , salt , mustard , sugar , vinegar and cayenne pepper
3. beat well and pour into hot pan with bacon and bacon grease stirring till thickened
4. add diced cooked potatoes and sliced onion
5. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Thanks for sharing Lali.  This turned out as good as I've EVER had.

target.recipe_text:
the ultimate lime margarita

you can't have a summer gathering without the great taste of margarita's and chips with salsa. make these ahead of time and they will be ready to serve when the party starts!

1. combine first 4 ingredients in a 4-cup measuring cup
2. for blended margaritas: fill blender halfway with ice cubes
3. add half of margarita mixture
4. blend until mixture is thick and icy
5. divide between two glasses
6. repeat with more ice cubes and remaining margarita mixture
7. for margaritas on the rocks: fill four glasses with ice cubes
8. divide margarita mixture among glasses and serve
9. do-ahead
10. cover and refrigerate
target.review: These are REAL good!  I added alittle more sugar, but my husband likes his drinks sweet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best roast beef

this came from the april 1998 chatelaine magazine. since then, its the only recipe i have used for a good cut of beef. the cooking time indicated here is for a3 lb roast.

1. take roast out of refrigerator- allow time for it to reach room temperature
2. preheat oven to 325f
3. if roast is very moist , pat dry with paper towels& place in a roasting pan
4. in a small bowl , combine butter , mustard , horseradish& garlic
5. using your fingers or a small palette knife , cover outside of roast with the mixture
6. roast , uncovered , in the centre of oven
7. allow about 20 minutes per pound for medium rare to medium
8. if you did not bring roast to room temperature , increase the time to 25 minutes per pound
9. remove to cutting board , tent with foil& allow to rest for 10 minutes before carving
demonstrations.review: Just had to drop a note.  I made this for the second time last night.  We had dinner guest and everyone loved it.  I used a eye of round roast.  The favor was unforgetable.  Loved the topping and the presentation was beautiful.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy baked potato skins

these are easy and yummy seasoned potato skins filled with bacon and cheese!

1. cut potatoes in half lengthwise
2. scoop out pulp and discard leaving 1 / 4-inch shell
3. place on a greased baking sheet
4. combine oil , parmesan cheese , salt , garlic powder , paprika and pepper and brush all over potato skins
5. bake at 475 for about 8 minutes and turn over
6. bake for another 8 minutes or so and then turn right side up
7. sprinkle bacon and cheddar evenly inside of skins
8. bake 2 minutes longer or until cheese is melted
9. top with sour cream and onions , if desired
demonstrations.review: My husband and I were recovering from colds and where tired of soup.  Found this recipe, the only one I had all the ingredients for, and we loved it.  I think the next time I make it I will add with the cheese some taco meat and make it a full meal.  It was easy to do and looked beautiful.  Would serve to company.  Also, very good warmed up the next day for lunch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bleu cheese beef tenderloin

if you like bleu cheese...you should love this easy meal. prep time is the length of time to let the meat marinade as well as to create the final sauce. (this is a copykat with a few adjustments but for the life of me i don't know where i got it)!

1. place beef in a shallow dish
2. combine , teriyaki sauce , red wine& garlic
3. pour mixture over beef and allow to marinate for at least 30 minutes turning at least once
4. place tenderloin on broiler pan and cook in preheated oven at 450 degrees for 15 minutes
5. reduce heat to 375 degrees and cook for 30 to 40 minutes longer
6. allow to set for appx 10 minutes before slicing keeping in mind it will continue to cook as it sets
7. in a saucepan over low heat , combine the bleu cheese , mayo , sour cream and worcestershire sauce
8. stir until smooth and creamy and serve over the sliced tenderloin
9. when i made this , i saved the marinade , minced some garlic and added a little more of each ingredient
10. i then put it in a saucepan with a sprig of rosemary and small red potatoes and let them simmer while the meal cooked
11. as always , garlic and bleu cheese can be overpowering for some but you can indeed adjust these to taste
demonstrations.review: This was the best, especially the sauce!  Will definely make it again and again.  Would be great for a dinner party.  Easy and quick!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sea scallops

this makes a great dinner for 4, or an appetizer for 8 and is a wonderful light dish. adapted from diabetic recipes 2003

1. heat olive oil in skillet , add garlic , stir
2. add scallops , cook 2-3 minutes until opaque , set aside
3. add orange juice to the skillet , add tea leaves , soy sauce , honey and any reserved scallop liquid reduce heat and simmer to thicken
4. strain sauce in fine mesh , add liquid back to pan , discard solids
5. add scallops back to pan , coat with sauce
6. serve over rice noodles
demonstrations.review: This is a keeper is what my DH said when I served this one!  So easy to make.  Had the sauce all made up early in the day and when dinner time came I was ready.  My in-laws are coming this weekend and DH wants me to make this for them.  I used bay scallops, just personal taste, and served over pasta.  Very elegant dish.  Thanks for posting this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barbecued fish steaks

i doubled this to 12 servings (for 8 people) and had absolutely no left-overs. another one for my diabetic dinner guests, yet well received by all!

1. saut onion and garlic in butter or margarine until tender
2. add ingredients through ground peppercorn and simmer for about 7 minutes , stirring occasionally
3. cool
4. pour liquid into a zip-lock type storage bag
5. add salmon
6. marinate in refrigerator 45 minutes , turning after about 20 minute intervals
7. remove fish from marinade
8. place on well-greased , hinged wire grill
9. cook 2 inches from coals for 3 minutes , basting frequently with sauce
10. turn and cook for about 5 minutes longer , or until fish is done
demonstrations.review: This was exceptional!  I don't usually fix fish, but DH is on a special diet, in fact, I don't know how to fix fish.  It was so nice and moist.  The flavor was unbelieveable.  Will definely do this one again.  I used Salmon fillets.  Thanks for this one!

target.recipe_text:
simple caribbean jerk chicken

i like jerk chicken but often don't have all the exotic ingredients. this simplifies the mix by using dry italian dressing. yummy on the grill!

1. mix all ingredients except chicken in bowl
2. pour over chicken
3. cover and marinate 1 hour or over night in fridge
4. grill it !
5. enjoy !
target.review: Definitely a keeper. Paired with rice and plantains, makes a perfect meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fruit salad with pudding

i get compliments on this fruit salad wherever i take it. it is super easy to make and a great dish to bring to a potluck or family party. kids love it too. everyone asks "what's in the sauce"? the secret ingredient is the vanilla pudding mix.

1. in a large bowl , combine peaches , pineapples , and vanilla pudding mix
2. this includes the juices from the cans
3. mix well until pudding is dissolved
4. stir in strawberries , banana , blueberries , grapes , and sugar if desired
5. chill
demonstrations.review: I did not care for the taste of this either... the pudding was a bad idea to me because it covered the taste of the fruit and gave it a fake taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon pepper chicken breasts on a bed of rice

a simple great tasting recipe that makes enough to feed the family. it has a wonderful robust flavor, but not too overpowering. this dish also makes good leftovers. try it out and see for yourself!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. sprinkle lemon pepper on both sides of breasts
3. sprinkle the lemon pepper to your own taste
4. using a non-greased 9"x13" glass baking dish place the chicken , and melted margarine inside
5. cover
6. bake for 30 minutes
7. remove from oven
8. remove chicken and set aside
9. add one cup of long grain white rice , one can of chicken broth
10. stir together and cover tightly with foil
11. put pan back in the oven
12. bake 30 minutes
13. remove from oven , and place chicken back inside
14. cook for another 15 minutes
15. this update to the recipe brings it back to its roots and eliminates the problems people were having with under cooked rice / overcooked chicken
demonstrations.review: I liked the taste of the rice a lot. However, I think I'm going to shave off some of the oven cooking next time, because I thought the chicken tasted way too dry because it was in the oven too long.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
favorite scallops

this is my favorite way to prepare scallops. recipe adapted from bon appetit ( october, 1981).

1. melt butter in skillet over medium heat
2. stir in garlic , tarragon and oregano
3. add scallops and season with paprika , salt and pepper
4. squeeze lemon juice over scallops and saute for 5 minutes or until scallops turn opaque
5. increase heat to medium-high and add sherry cooking until there is almost no liquid in pan
6. transfer to serving dish
7. sprinkle with paprika , parsley and lemon slices
demonstrations.review: It was good, but I used bay scallops, so they cooked superfast, and I did not have time to evaporate the liquid any. I'm sure the recipe is a lot better with sea scallops instead!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chow gai laan  jade green broccoli

adapted from a chinese cookbook by jim lee that was published around 1970. this is one of my all-time favorite cookbooks; i was introduced to it by friends who were chinese students i knew at university of virginia. the gai laan which the chinese eat is not actually broccoli, but broccoli is a good substitute which works well in america, where most of us don't have access to gai laan.

1. mix together sugar through soy sauce plus 1 / 2 cup water and put aside
2. heat oil in a skillet or wok over medium heat and add the garlic
3. when garlic is golden brown , add the broccoli
4. turn the heat up and stir-fry 2 minutes
5. add sherry , cover quickly and cook 2 minutes
6. lift cover& add the soy sauce mixture
7. when sauce thickens , remove and serve
demonstrations.review: My husband said he could eat this every single day! Thanks for spicing up our broccoli.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
charlie s famous chicken salad with grapes

a really great guy i used to work with would make this and bring in to share. we all loved it so much and would beg for more! sounds strange with the grapes, but it's so good! allow time for salad to chill.

1. combine all ingredients
2. chill
3. serve with just about anything- crackers , chips , rolls , bread or bagel
demonstrations.review: Awesome! I used regular mayo instead, and also added about 1/4 teaspoon of ground white pepper in the mix. Perfect lunchtime food!

target.recipe_text:
thin swedish pancakes

a very delicious breakfast for the whole family.   serve with eggs and bacon.

1. for pancakes
2. beat eggs , flour , salt , and sugar until smooth
3. beat in milk , and vanilla
4. fry in well buttered skillet
5. serve with strawberries , and jelly
6. for the syrup
7. boil ingredients until clear
8. add butter and serve hot
target.review: These were pretty good ... I had to add a little bit more flour as they kept tearing when folding. We served these with a peach compote and drizzled the syrup on top. Thanks for a good breakfast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
summer berry grunt

mmmm berries stewed with vanilla and sugar, topped with steamed dumplings.  a traditional dessert in the new england area and one of my favorite.  i like this combination, but you can use any berries you like, and regular sugar if you don't have vanilla sugar.

1. in a large skillet , combine the berries , water and 1 / 3 cup vanilla sugar
2. set the skillet over medium-high heat and bring it to a simmer
3. while the berries are cooking , combine flour , baking powder , salt and remaining sugar in a medium bowl
4. mix with a fork to combine
5. in a separate bowl , whisk together milk and vanilla and add to dry ingredients
6. mix together with a fork until dry mixture comes together in a soft dough
7. drop the dough by heaping spoonfuls onto simmering berries , making 8 dumplings
8. cover pan and cook 10 minutes , until dumplings are puffed up and cooked through
demonstrations.review: This was so easy and tasted really good. I used strawberries instead of the other berries and orange juice concentrate instead of triple sec. I like the dumplings but do wish there were more berries and sauce. I will either double that next time or reduce the dumpling mixture by half. This would also make a great dessert or breakfast while out camping.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
skinny gravy

low fat chicken or turkey gravy, great for the holidays, and your waistline!

1. shake can of stock and pour into a sauce pan , add beef cube , olive oil and bring to a simmer
2. in a small bowl combine the corn starch with some water about 4 tablespoons , and stir
3. when stock comes to a boil add corn starch slurry
4. whisk
5. the mixture will start to become thick , when the consistency is to your liking remove from heat
6. if it doesn't thicken enough repeat step 2 , by adding another portion of slurry
demonstrations.review: After reading the other reviews I thought I would try it with chicken flavored cube instead of beef. We liked the flavor but it was a bit too salty. Will try again and experiment more. Thanks for the post.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic grilled pork chops

this has been a favorite of the family for years. i use this for both pork chops and pork tenderloin. it is really tender and flavorful.

1. combine all ingredients in a large bowl
2. marinate 4 to 6 hours in refrigerator
3. grill 5 inches from heat , basting with marinade several times
demonstrations.review: These were not only tasty but super easy. I let them marinate overnight. The only change I made to the recipe was I only used a few drops of oil not 1/2 cup and they still turned out great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raisin bread  lite bleu

this bread qualifies for part of a meal plan. if your not dieting, enjoy and serve freshly baked, cut into thick slices and smeared with lots of butter. all lite-bleu recipes are meals or recipes that we designed for our weight loss diet. please visit our homepage for more info.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. in a large bowl sift together the flour , sugar , cinnamon , salt and soda
3. mix in the dried fruit
4. make a well in the center and pour most of the milk in at once
5. using one hand , mix in the flour from the sides of the bowl , adding more milk , if necessary
6. the dough should be soft , not too wet and sticky
7. when it all comes together , turn it out onto a floured board , knead lightly for a few seconds
8. pat the dough into a round about 1 1 / 2 inches deep and cut a deep tic
9. tac
10. toe pattern on it
11. bake in a hot oven for 15 minutes , then turn down the oven to 400 degrees f
12. and bake for another 30 minutes or until cooked
13. if you are in doubt , tap the bottom: if it is cooked it will sound hollow
demonstrations.review: This is a dense bread that is easy to make. I actually shaped mine into a heart and it only baked for 23 of the last 30 minutes. I added extra raisins and will probably add cinnamon next time to spice it up a bit - maybe some vanilla too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple nut bread pudding

bread pudding that has a flavorful aroma while cooking.  great for a fall-winter evening.

1. place bread cubes , apples , and pecans in a greased slow cooker , and mix together gently
2. combine sugar , cinnamon , and nutmeg
3. add remaining ingredients
4. mix well , and pour over breadmixture
5. cover , cook on low 3-4 hours or until knife inserted in center comes out clean
6. serve with ice cream
demonstrations.review: It wasn't very sweet which my dd and dh liked better then our normal treats. I don't care for nutmeg and wished I had left it out, even though it was a small amount. I didn't plan my time very well so I ended up cooking this in the oven at 350 for 55 minutes. I think it would be better in the crockpot and will make that it that way next time.

target.recipe_text:
black bean chipotle soup

i found this recipe in a magazine and modified it to my liking. very delicious and super easy! my family enjoys the recipe often!

leaving out the sausage, for a meatless soup is also great!

1. in a medium sauce pan , heat the olive oil on medium high heat , add onion and saute until soft , about 3 minutes
2. add garlic , chipotle , cumin , oregano , and cook for additional 1-2 minutes
3. add black beans and chicken stock and bring up to a boil , then reduce heat to medium to medium low , cover and simmer for 15 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. while the soup is simmering , in a large skillet , brown the sausage
5. after the soup has simmered for 15 minutes , coarsely smash the beans and add the browned sausage
6. stir in the juice from one 1 lime and cilantro
7. simmer for an additional 5 minutes
8. if you'd like , garnish with sour cream , cheese , extra lime and cilantro
target.review: thanks for posting, this is a great soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rosemary parmesan sourdough bread

while visiting my local quiznos decided to try to make my own.  used a couple of my favorite zaar recipes as the starting point.   made two loaves yesterday . . . friends stopped in and we devoured one loaf with cheese.   it was deemed ready for the public!   next time may try adding a couple tablespoons of sun dried tomatoes.

1. proof starter over night before making bread
2. to kitchen aid mixing bowl add all the ingredients
3. using dough hook mix until a satin ball is formed
4. adding additional flour as needed
5. remove dough to greased bowl , turning once to coat
6. cover and allow to rise until doubled
7. form into 1 large or 2 smaller free-form loaves and place on parchment paper or pizza peel dusted with corn meal
8. cover and allow bread to rise until double in size
9. preheat oven to 375 dgrees
10. lightly beat 1 egg white with 1 tablespoon water
11. brush top of loaves with egg wash and then sprinkle with fresh parmesan
12. bake a 375 deghrees for 30-45 minutes , depending on the size of the loaves
demonstrations.review:
Great bread, was a pleasure to work with, and slices beautifully, making it a great sandwich bread
Thanks so much for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy molasses crinkle cookies

this recipe is wonderful. easy, tasty, perfect-looking cookies every time, and the way your house smells while they're baking is heavenly. let the kids help by rolling the dough into balls and into the granulated sugar.

1. heat oven to 350
2. in large mixer bowl , beat the sugar , shortening , molasses and egg at medium speed until well blended
3. add the remaining ingredients and mix at low speed until a soft dough forms
4. shape dough into 1-inch balls
5. roll balls in a dish of granulated sugar and place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie / baking sheets
6. bake 10-12 minutes
7. let cool and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: great great cookie !! It was the scent of heaven while baking, and with a cup of tea, it was a taste of heaven

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sourdough sams

nan

1. sift dry ingredients , stir into liquid , roll out and cut with regular donut cutter
2. then heat some oil in a deep fryer to 390 degrees f and fry
3. just before serving dust with powdered or cinnamon sugar
4. these doughnuts are virtually greasless
5. and if you want you can make several batches at a time and freeze
6. they keep well and to me taste after a while in the freezer
7. take out as many as needed and thaw and put sugar on or eat plain
demonstrations.review: This has become my # one go doughnut recipe ! My mom use to make one similar, but has long since lost the recipe, and she says she doesn't remember using a starter, if her memory holds true, she says. But for me you gave some good memories to recollect! Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy beans n  greens in a bowl  kale soup

a light and delicious fast fix meal that is easy on the waist and the pocketbook! this comes together very fast and will fill you up with just a few tasty but healthy ingredients. the quantity listed leaves you with a soupy, brother bowl of yum! you could add another batch of kale if you like, there is that much broth. also great with all kinds of beans. to me this dish seems like a beautiful marriage between italian and southern cooking. hope you enjoy! ps: if you use a vegetarian 'chicken' broth this will be completely vegetarian friendly! skip the parm or use a vegan parm and you have a vegan friendly dish! the portion is very generous! adjust time if you are using more tender greens so they are not over cooked.

1. heat a dutch oven and spray with cooking spray
2. add olive oil and then the onion and garlic
3. saute just until it begins to soften , add chicken broth and allow to continue cooking while you begin the next steps
4. wash whatever greens you choose to use and remove any hard stalks
5. stack the leaves one on top of the other , roll like a cigar and slice into 1 / 4 inch slices , then cut the pieces in half
6. this will give you nice ribbons that are not too wide or long
7. add greens , sugar and nutmeg to the pan
8. stir to combine
9. rinse and drain beans and add to pan
10. stir gently
11. simmer for 20 minutes or until greens are al dente or as soft as you would like
12. toss in spinach just to wilt
13. ladle each serving into a bowl and top with a generous sprinkling of freshly grated parmesan cheese and additional cracked pepper if desired
14. crusty bread is also a great accompaniment for all the yummy broth that is swimming in the bowl
15. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: great soup, enjoyed with some home made bread. thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
molasses oat  bread

a diabetic exchange is 2 1/2 starch  per slice.

1. in a bowl combine first 6 ingredients
2. cool to 110f
3. add yeast and mix well
4. add enough flour to form a soft dough
5. knead on a floured board til smooth about 6-8 minutes
6. place in greased bowl turning once to grease top
7. cover and let rise in a warm , draft free place til doubled
8. punch dough down and divide into 3
9. form 3 loaves and place in well greased loaf pans
10. cover and let rise til doubled
11. bake 350f 45-50 minutes or til golden brown
12. allow to cool on wire racks
demonstrations.review: great bread! toasted, used for a sandwich, or just with butter..or not..tasty no matter what !!

target.recipe_text:
garlic spinach with white beans

warm comfort food.  fast & easy.  very healthy and yummy.

1. heat a large skillet
2. add oil
3. saut garlic 1 minute
4. add all the spinach
5. lower heat to med and cover
6. cook just long enough to wilt spinach
7. add beans & stock and heat through
8. serve
target.review: So delicious!!  Quick and easy to make and goes with anything you could think of - and healthy!!!  Thanks conniecooks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basil shrimp with feta and orzo

i got this recipe from cooking light.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. spray the inside of the foil bag with cooking spray and place on a large shallow baking pan
3. cook the pasta in boiling water for 5 minutes
4. drain
5. place the pasta in a large bowl and stir in 1 teaspoon of the oil and the next 7 ingredients
6. place the orzo mixture in teh foil bag
7. combine the shrimp and basil
8. arrange shrimp mixture on the orzo
9. fold edges of bag to seal
10. bake at 450 degrees for 25 minutes
11. cut open the bag with a sharp knife and peel the foil back
12. drizzle with remaining 1 teaspoon of oil
13. serve
demonstrations.review: This was FABULOUS!!!  I made it for my family and even my low-carb uncle raved about it!!!  I'm making it again tonight - only one week later than the first time!!  Thank you soooo much, Kim!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
provencial black olive and fresh thyme mashed potatoes

this is another recipe from oprah.

1. put potatoes in a large saucepan and cover with cold water and bring to a boil
2. reduce heat to med and cook until potatoes are very tender when stabbed with a fork , about 15 minutes
3. drain well
4. return to the saucepan and add the cream and butter
5. with a hand mixer , blend until just smooth
6. add the olives and thyme
7. garnish with fresh thyme
8. season generously with salt and pepper
9. according to oprah this serves 12 to 15
demonstrations.review: This is fabulous!!  My DM - who eats like a bird on her best days - had SECONDS!!  This reinvents the mashed potato and makes it the most elegant and succulent side dish ever!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli with browned butter

simply delicious.

1. remove broccoli floweret clusters from stems
2. separate flowerets
3. peel stems , then cut into inch thick slices
4. steam broccoli until crisp-tender
5. cook butter with garlic in large skillet over medium-low heat until foam subsides and butter is nut-brown
6. immediately remove from heat and discard garlic
7. stir in lemon juice
8. add broccoli and toss to coat
9. season and serve
demonstrations.review: The nutty flavor of the browned butter with the hint of garlic and the lilt of lemon juice.  YUMMY!!  Thanks evelyn!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon olive bacon cheese meatballs

lemon olive bacon cheese meatballs

1. partially cook the bacon , keeping it from curling
2. mix all the other ingredients except bacon
3. shape the mixture into 12 balls
4. wrap a bacon slice around each ball
5. fasten with a toothpick
6. arrange in a baking dish
7. bake in a preheated 350f oven for about 40 minutes , turning once or twice
demonstrations.review: The blend of flavors is so unusual and so good!! It's a great party food! Thanks Miller!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken chalupa casserole

easy

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray large casserole dish with cooking spray
3. lay two tortillas in bottom of dish , overlapping slightly
4. top with a layer of chicken , a layer of cheese , and a layer of salsas
5. repeat layers until dish is full , finishing with a layer of salsa
6. bake until hot and bubbly
7. garnish with olives and cilantro , if desired
demonstrations.review: So easy to do - store bought ingredients that come together to make a really good meal!!  I even found low carb tortillas!!  Thanks littleturtle, this is definitely a keep and do often recipe!!!

target.recipe_text:
smoked sausage cassoulet

one of my favorites from bon apetit. very hearty and so delicious. tastes better with every day that passes.

1. heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large ovenproof dutch oven
2. add sausages
3. saute for 25 minutes or until browned
4. transfer sausages to a paper-towel lined platter and let drain
5. add leeks and garlic to same dutch oven
6. saute for 8 minutes or until they begin to soften
7. add in apples , rosemary , and sage
8. mix well
9. add brandy and simmer 5 minutes or until mostly evaporated
10. add canned tomatoes with juice , beans with 1 / 2 cup of reserved liquid , lima beans , 1 cup broth , tomato paste , and cloves
11. mix well
12. return sausages to pan
13. season to taste with salt and pepper
14. bring mixture to a boil
15. cover and place dutch oven in a 350 degree oven for 30 minutes
16. heat 1 / 4 cup olive oil in a large skillet
17. add bread and saute for 25 minutes or until golden brown , stirring frequently
18. mix together tomatoes and parsley in a large bowl
19. add in the bread
20. mix well
21. season to taste with salt and pepper
22. spoon bread mixture evenly on top of cassoulet
23. bake uncovered for 15 minutes
target.review: This was a fairly easy dish to pull together, and I had all the ingredients on hand. I liked the way it looked, BUT (and its just me I guess, because my son and husband liked it enough to finish what was on their plates)  the smell turned me off. To me, the sage and cloves smelled like a Christmas tree was cooking in my oven. I just couldn't get past that smell! I'm sure its just me and my own really sensitive nose, because it rates well w/ others! If I were to make this again, I would omit the spices, and just use more garlic and maybe instead of all the beans(I love Northern Beans!), I would use pasta. But then it would be an Italian meal, not so French!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanish bar cake

moist and tasty spice cake. reminds me of the ones a&p grocery stores made when i was a child :)

1. mix first 8 ingredients together in an electric mixer
2. mix well
3. add next 3 ingredients
4. raisins should be added last
5. bake at 350f in 9x13 inch pan for 30-35 minutes
6. tube pan 40-45 minutes
7. cool thoroughly and frost if desired
8. for frosting:combine frosting ingredients in bowl
9. beat well , adding more milk or confectioners' sugar to make it smooth and easy to spread
demonstrations.review:
(( YUM ))

I am looking for Spanish food recipes to help my son's school celebrate the upcoming 'Memphis In May' celebration whereby we honor a chosen country every year. This year it is Spain.
I don't know if this is a real Spanish cake or not-I'm clueless to the origin of it, but I came accross your recipe while searching the site, and decided to try it. 
Now, I grew up in Pennsylvania, and I remember A & P stores ( ahhh-the good ole' days!), and I swear as soon as I took a bite of this cake I was 8 again! I remembered it!!
 I made two cakes, one for us to eat at home, and one for my husband to take to work to try out on his employees. Everyone loved it according to him, and said that it would be just as good without the icing. I made them in bundt cake pans and I have to tell ya', this was one of the moistest cakes I have ever eaten! Thanks 1Steve for the fantabulous recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dutch baby

i've had these a lot at b&b's, probably because they're delicious and dependable if the right technique is used. this dish is puffy around the outside and flat in the center offering the perfect nest for sliced fresh fruit. it's airy, light and makes a beautiful presentation. the batter can be made up to a day ahead and refrigerated.

1. fifteen minutes before baking preheat the oven to 450
2. have a pie plate or oven-proof skillet ready
3. whisk together the milk , flour , eggs , sugar and vanilla
4. put the butter in the pie plate or skillet and place the pan in the oven just until the butter is melted
5. with a brush coat the rim and entire inside of the pan
6. slowly pour batter into hot pan
7. bake for 20 minutes
8. reduce heat to 350 and bake another 8-10 minutes , until pancake is well-browned
9. remove from oven and sieve confectioners' sugar over the top
10. serve immediately with fruit spooned into the center of the pancake
demonstrations.review:
Wow! This was wonderful presentation piece for Easter breakfast.
My oven runs hot-so I baked it 425 for 15 minutes, and then at 350 for about 10minutes. 
Topped it off with peaches, blueberries, raspberries and blackberries.
My family will be keeping this recipe!
Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate salmon fillets

living on the west coast, we have eaten a great deal of salmon. this is absolutely the best way we have found to cook it. it is so moist and the flavor is fantastic! many reviewers have said that they think the cheese, especially the cheddar is unnecessary, and i have to admit that i omit the cheddar cheese myself. the flavour is a little too strong and it is extra fat that is not needed. i do like the sprinkling of parmesan with the paprika because it looks so nice when it is broiled. using light mayonnaise and light sour cream or yogurt tastes just as good as the full fat versions and cuts down fat and calories even more. thanks for all the great reviews!

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. if frozen , partially thaw fillets and cut into serving size pieces
3. place in a greased baking dish
4. combine sour cream or yogurt , mustard , onion , dill , and mayonnaise
5. season with salt and pepper
6. spread mixture over fish
7. bake 20 minutes per inch of thickness of fish if frozen or 10-12 minutes if thawed
8. when just done , sprinkle with the cheeses and a dash of paprika
9. broil 1 minute or until the cheese is bubbly and flecked with brown
10. serve with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review:
(( Wow))
 I am so used to making Salmon on the grill using a sweet marinade w/soy sauce.
 These were fabulous! 
I am so glad to have a new recipe for salmon to add to my repotoire!
The fish was moist and so tasty.I did not have any dill weed on hand, so I added a teaspoon of Herbes de Provence to it as it has dill weed in it. Served it on a bed of lettuce w/ a side of parmesean cous-cous-yum!
Thank you Paja for the fabulous recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
almond poppy seed muffins

i had almond poppyseed muffins at a restaurant called yoders in shipshewana, in. a few years ago and they were the best muffins i've ever eaten. i searched on the internet and found this recipe. not sure what site it came from. i hope you like them.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease , spray , or placed liners in muffin tins to hold 24 muffins
3. combine flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
4. add milk , eggs , oil , and almond extract
5. whisk until smooth
6. gently stir in poppyseeds
7. fill muffin tins and bake for 25- 30 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Outstanding!
I halved the recipe the first time I made it as I was low on flour, but I upped the almond extraxt to 1.5 TBS and upped the poppyseed count to 3.5 TBS and they were perfect! Everyone here loved them, and they freeze nicely too! Great for a quick snack or breakfast add-on.
Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ultimate pizza sauce

this pizza sauce recipe was given to me as a wedding present, written on the inside cover of a pizza cookbook. it is thick, saucy, spicy and delicious. i'll never use anything else on my homemade pizzas. i like to double or triple it and put it in ziploc bags in my freezer.

1. in a large skillet , melt butter with the oil
2. add the onion , celery and garlic and saute until soft and transparent
3. add tomato sauce and tomato paste and stir until smooth
4. add remaining ingredients and bring to slow simmer
5. simmer for 30-60 minutes
6. remove the bay leaf and spread the sauce on your prepared pizza dough
demonstrations.review:
(((( Yummm! ))))
This was a real good recipe for pizza sauce-tastes BETTER than store bought by a mile, and was really easy to make. I made a double batch and paired it with 'Easiest Ever Pizza Dough' recipe from this site, #23137.
I did not add any celery or fennel, as I didn't have any on hand. I did however add a pinch or two of celery salt in place of the celery and fennel. - I gotta' tell ya'- It was wonderful anyway!
I had a little left over and I froze it to use at a later time. Thank you SAMS_CLUB- I will use this all the time now!

target.recipe_text:
tortillas de harina  flour tortillas

my late grandma's tortillas. delicious as a stand alone snack or mexican side

1. mix flour , shortening , baking powder , salt , and sugar
2. gradually stir in water until crumbly dough forms
3. work with hands until dough holds together
4. on a floured board , shape into a ball and knead until smooth
5. divide dough into 12 roughly equal parts
6. roll into sphere and let stand for 15 minutes
7. use a rolling pin to flatten into 8 inch circles
8. cook on ungreased griddle on medium heat , to cook , when it starts to bubble , flip it over , when it starts to bubble , pat it down with a clean towel or spatula , when the entire tortilla starts to inflate , take it off the grill
target.review:
This is such an easy recipe, and the tortillas had a good flavor.  I think this is the easiest recipe I've ever seen -- and I had all the ingredients on hand.  We used them for quesadillas and they were better than store bought, for sure!

One problem I seem to have with tortillas is keeping them soft after cooking.  Mine usually end up like flat bread  Any suggestions?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white wedding cake

one of my friends makes wedding cakes and this is her recipe. i like using it for birthday cakes, especially ones i am doing something creative with as the cake holds together quite well.

1. grease and flour 2 9-inch cake pans
2. set aside
3. beat all ingredients on low speed until mixed
4. batter will be thick
5. beat on medium speed about 2 minutes
6. batter will be slightly lumpy
7. pour into greased and floured pans
8. bake at 350 for 30- 35 minutes or until cake tests done
9. do not overbake
demonstrations.review: Fixed this for my great grandmother's birthday, as she requested white cake with chocolate frosting.  Everyone LOVED it.  The almond extract really adds a little something extra to it.  Very moist, easy to frost, and tasty!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot baked cinnamon apples

these cinnamon apples taste like a cobbler or pie without the crust. i was looking for a recipe for cinnamon apples and all i could find were recipes for baking the whole apple - not what i wanted. after much searching i finally came across this recipe - i unfortunately cannot remember the site. it can easily be reduced to 2 or 3 apples, just watch it as it cooks. we serve this over ice cream and it is delicious. it can also be used on pancakes, waffles, or all by itself.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. place cut and peeled apples in a mixing bowl and gently mix all the ingredients together
3. put apples in a non-stick pan
4. cover and place in the oven
5. bake for 45 minutes , stirring at least once every 15 minutes
6. once they are soft , cook for another few minutes to thicken the cinnamon sauce
7. i like to put everything into my baking dish and then mix it since there is less to clean up
demonstrations.review: Made your apples as a last minute thing on Thanksgiving, and they were absolutely WONDERFUL!  It was so easy and the apples had such a great flabor.  Thank you SO much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sue b s chocolate cake

i adopted this recipe.  i had prepared it for a holiday function prior to the adoption. the comments from my original review stated, "this dense, rich chocolate cake is intensely moist. it baked perfectly and made a lovely layer cake. i will be using this recipe again for chocolate cake needs."  the cake in my photo has recipe #44126, between the layers, and is frosted with recipe #31809 before being covered with my recipe #105466.  it was a huge hit, and i have made this cake many, many times since.

1. mix cocoa and boiling water
2. mix buttermilk , oil , eggs and vanilla together
3. mix dry ingredients together
4. mix dry ingredients into buttermilk / oil mixture
5. mix in cocoa
6. bake at 350 degrees fahrenheit in two greased and floured and parchment lined 9-inch round pans
7. bake until tester comes out clean , approximately 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Needed a cake to impress the boyfriend and his family for his birthday, and this definitely did the trick.  Preparation was easy and the cake rose to perfection for a dual layer cake in exactly 30 minutes.  Flavor was good (not too sweet), cake was moist, and it turned out perfectly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted garlic potatoes

these tasty spuds, spiced with garlic herbs, will feel right at home alondside breafast, lunch, or dinner entrees. (this recipe is from the cookbook "how it all vegan".)

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. place the cubed potatoes in a medium bowl and add the rest of the ingredients and stir together
3. lay evenly onto a cookie sheet or lasagna pan and bake in the oven for 30-40 minutes , until potatoes are golden brown and can be easily pierced with a fork
demonstrations.review: These were wonderful!  They came out perfectly and had a great flavour.  I couldn't stop eating them.  I broiled them for 8 minutes at the end to crisp them up a bit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peppermint bark

this is a copycat of the william sonoma bark that costs $22 a lb. i have never tried their version, but when my mom told me she liked it, i went on a search to find the recipe. make sure to buy white chocolate chips that contain cocoa butter to get a smooth melt- otherwise, you will end up with clumpy chocolate. use good quality chocolate chips (belgian, semi-sweet, or bittersweet)  for the best results.this recipe is so simple and delicious  my only hope is that i'm able to save a piece for my mom. recipe by rita nader heikenfeld.

1. preheat oven to 250
2. line a 9x13 pan with foil , letting it hang over the sides
3. spray foil
4. pour the chocolate chips in an even layer on the foil
5. place in oven for 5 minutes or until almost melted
6. remove from oven , smooth with an offset spatula or knife
7. place in refrigerator until cold and firm , about 20 minutes
8. melt white chocolate chips in a double boiler or in a metal bowl over simmering water , until chocolate is almost melted
9. if you are daring , you can use your microwave
10. remove bowl from water and stir until completely melted , stirring in extract
11. let cool a little bit so it doesnt melt the chocolate layer when you pour it on top
12. pour this over chocolate layer , and , working quickly , spread to cover
13. sprinkle with crushed candy
14. chill until both layers are firm
15. lift foil out of pan and shake off excess candy
16. trim edges
17. cut into 2 wide strips
18. peel bark from foil and cut each strip as desired
19. chill in covered container
20. makes about 2 pounds
demonstrations.review: This was so easy and so good!  I do have to say that the Kroger chips with cocoa butter were definitely the best for the job.  We also used ghirradelli semi-sweet, and everything adhered nicely.  The ghiradelli white chocolate chips didn't melt as smoothly, and the Target semi-sweet choclate chips did not adhere.  Either way, the recipe is EASY and tasty!!!

target.recipe_text:
bobbie q sauce  barbecue sauce

a versatile barbecue sauce - sweet and spicy. kind of like magic -- anything i prepare with this sauce disappears! it's a hit with all ages. i've started preparing it with xylitol, also known as birch sugar, instead of sugar, and it works just great, plus it's easier on blood sugar levels.

1. combine ingredients , bring to a boil and simmer over low heat for 5 minutes
2. use this as a basting sauce for barbecue , or combine with chopped or shredded beef , chicken or pork , and simmer until heated throughout and flavor is well through the meat
3. if you want to make up a batch of this to keep in the freezer , leave out the water , and it will not freeze solid
4. you can take out the container and just scoop out however much you need
5. i sometimes make it up by the gallon just to have it on hand for easy meals
target.review: I really loved this!! Will make this for all my BBQ dishes! So simple and easy to make, thanks so much for sharing this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome blueberry muffins

this is a awesome blueberry muffin recipe. double it to make large muffins. i sometimes add cinnamon to the batter.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. grease muffin cups or line with muffin liners
3. combine 1 1 / 2 cups flour , 3 / 4 cup sugar , salt and baking powder
4. place vegetable oil into a 1 cup measuring cup
5. add the egg and enough milk to fill the cup
6. mix this with flour mixture
7. fold in blueberries
8. fill muffin cups right to the top , and sprinkle with crumb topping mixture
9. to make crumb topping: mix together 1 / 2 cup sugar , 1 / 3 cup flour , 1 / 4 cup butter , and 1 1 / 2 teaspoons cinnamon
10. mix with fork , and sprinkle over muffins before baking
11. bake for 20 to 25 minutes in the preheated oven , or until done
demonstrations.review: I loved these, I used Splenda Granular in place of the sugar for both the batter and topping. (Splenda also does well with banana nut bread, but not cookies).  I also throwed in cinnamon and chopped pecans in both batter and topping. Thanks for posting this yummy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my famous chocolate covered cherries

these are so good. i have to make 2 dozen for my grandmother every christmas and she refuses to share them.  she actually hides them and pulls them out one at a time!  i really have no idea how many this makes as i usually double or triple the recipe.  also it depends on how much of the center you like . update: some people have had difficulty with the filling being to runny....adding more powdered sugar is not going to alter the taste so feel free to add another 1/2 c to a cup with out worry :)

1. combine the first 5 ingredients until well blended and smooth and place in fridge until firm
2. meanwhile spread out the drained cherries on a cookie sheet and freeze for at least 1 hours
3. scoop out about 1-2 teaspoon of filling and form into a ball around a cherry
4. place on a wax paper lined cookie sheet and freeze for 1 hr after you have formed them all
5. melt dipping chocolate and using your hands dip each cherry placing it on a wax paper lined cookie sheet and chill in fridge until chocolate is solid
6. remove cherries carefully as not to break them open and loose the center
7. place in an airtight plastic container and keep in a cool dry place for up to 1 month
demonstrations.review: I thought these were very very good, it was nice to just dip these and make more at a time instead of using a candy mold with only a few cavitys.  I don't really like the taste of the melting chips at the stores around here so I used Nestle's Tollhouse Milk Chocolate Chips and used 1/2 Tbs of shortening per 2 Cups of chips instead of the parrifin wax.  These are going in my "favorites" recipe folder! Thanks for sharing this!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the sweetest blueberry muffins

very tasty and sweet.

1. heat oven to 375
2. grease 18 regular-size muffin cups
3. in bowl , mix butter until creamy
4. add sugar and beat until pale and fluffy
5. add eggs one at a time , beating after each
6. beat in vanilla , baking powder and salt
7. with spoon , fold in half of flour then half of milk into batter
8. repeat
9. fold in blueberries
10. spoon into muffin cups and sprinkle topping onto each muffin
11. bake 15 to 20 minutes , until golden brown and springy to touch
demonstrations.review: Oh my goodness! These ARE the best! My 10 yr old found this recipe and made them herself, she did excellent! It made exactly 6 jumbo muffins with the jumbo muffin pan and they came out looking beautiful like from a coffee shop or bakery! I am keeping this recipe in my special

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas sheet cake

this is an extremely moist chocolate/cinnamon cake that tastes almost like fudge! it's thick, sweet, and perfect with vanilla ice cream . . . or by itself!

1. mix in large bowl and set aside the two cups of flour and two cups of sugar
2. in saucepan , bring 1 stick of margarine , four tablespoons of cocoa , and 1 cup of water to a boil
3. pour boiled mixture over dry ingredients and mix well
4. add 1 / 2 cup buttermilk , 1 teaspoons baking soda , 2 eggs , 1 teaspoon vanilla , and 2 teaspoons cinnamon
5. mix well
6. after mixed , pour into 9 1 / 2 x 13 1 / 2 baking pan
7. bake 25 minutes @ 400 degrees
8. as cake comes from oven , pour icing mixture over the top - do this while the cake is hot hot hot !
9. make the icing !
10. boil 4 tablespoons cocoa , 1 stick margarine , and 6 tablespoons of milk together for 1 minute
11. add to powdered sugar and vanilla
12. blend / stir until the lumps are gone , and pour over hot cake
13. let sit for 30 minutes until cool
14. this cake freezes beautifully !
demonstrations.review: My grandmother used to make this cake for my birthday when i was little, and tastes just like it! I made it today but halfed the recipe to make in an 8x8 pan. Yum! I also plan to make reviewer Fatima Rose's variation with the maraschino cherries! That sounds delicious too!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s chocolate popcorn

love making recipes with add-ins to my popcorn, and this one is sure to please young and old alike!  you can add nuts too if you like them.  i especially like peanuts, cashews and pecans with this recipe.  cooking time does not include time taken to pop popcorn.

1. preheat oven to 250f
2. place popped popcorn in a large roasting pan
3. set aside
4. in a saucepan , over medium heat , cook sugar , corn syrup and butter , stirring constantly , until sugar is dissolved
5. remove from heat
6. stir in chocolate chips and vanilla
7. stir until melted
8. pour over popcorn , and mix together well
9. put in oven and bake for 1 hour , stirring occasionally
10. if adding nuts , do so now , and mix into mixture with a large spoon
11. spoon onto waxed paper to cool , stir to separate
12. store in a large plastic container or put into baggies
demonstrations.review: WARNING!! DO NOT ATTEMPT TO MAKE IF YOU ARE ON A DIET, YOU WILL LOSE CONTROL! We made pigs of ourselves, we loved it so much! Thanks!!!!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s grilled chicken caesar salad

for ease i have listed bagged lettuce, all ingredient amounts may be adjusted, this recipe will yield four if you are serving more then double amounts, once the chicken is cooked and the dressing is made this takes little time to put together, i strongly suggest to use my dressing from recipe#116849 --- prep time does not include grilling the chicken ----your family and/or guests will be licking their plate clean!

1. season the chicken breasts as desired grill until thoroughly cooked remove from heat and cool for 10 minutes
2. slice the breasts into about 1 / 2-inch slices
3. in a large bowl toss the lettuce with parmesan cheese , red grape halves , onions and croutons
4. add in the caesar dressing and toss to coat
5. season with fresh ground black pepper if desired
6. divide the salad between 4 serving bowls and top with sliced chicken
7. delicious !
target.review: OMG THIS WAS FABULOUS!!!  I made exactly as written and threw in some tomatoes and cucumbers.  I really feel like the addition of the grapes and green onions really makes this salad Extra Special!  This is now a family favorite!  Thanks kitten!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green chile chicken soup

a new mexican favorite.

1. in a large pot , melt butter
2. add flour and stir paste over medium heat
3. add milk and chicken broth and whip to eliminate lumps
4. bring to a boil and reduce heat to simmer
5. add remaining ingredients
6. stir well , cover and simmer for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: My MiL makes green chile soup almost exactly like this.  My Goodness this stuff is too die for!!!  My absolute favorite soup.  Really good for a cold winter evening.  The only thing different is I added two small cans of chopped green chilies and Tony Chachere's cajun seasoning which really adds to the flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
glazed carrots dijonnaise

one of my favorite ways to prepare carrots.  "yummo!"

1. cook carrots until soft
2. while carrots cook , mix together all other ingredients
3. when carrots are soft , drain excess water and then add sauce and keep on low heat until sauce is warm and butter is melted
4. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
This is my family's new favorite way to eat carrots!!!  These were so delicious and I have added this recipe to my favorites list.

thanks so much

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatloaf with sun dried tomatoes

does the world really need another meat loaf recipe? yes...this one! i have converted three meat loaf haters into meat loaf lovers with this recipe. it's now the only recipe i use, and i make it with turkey. if you are lucky enough to have leftovers, you will enjoy a really delicious meat loaf sandwich.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. grease a loaf pan , preferably glass
3. heat oil in skillet over medium heat
4. add onion and saute for 5 minutes
5. add celery and continue cooking until veggies are very tender , about 15 minutes longer
6. transfer to large bowl
7. add all remiaining ingredients except ketchup to vegetables in bowl
8. mix thoroughly
9. transfer to prepared pan and press mixture down well , smoothing the top
10. bake for 1 hour
11. spread ketchup on taop and bake about 15 minutes longer
12. let sit for 5 minutes
13. slice and serve
demonstrations.review:
My Families new favorite meatloaf!!!I did change a few things. I used one pound of lean ground beef and added Italian breadcrumbs instead of fresh.  I omitted the sage and oregano.  I used the vegetables in amounts called for.  The results, a perfect meatloaf that will replace my old.  

Thanks so much!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate strawberry shortcake

the perfect summer dessert. not your ordinary strawberry shortcake!

1. wash , stem , and cut strawberries in half
2. add sugar
3. toss to mix well
4. chill
5. beat cream cheese and powdered sugar well
6. fold in whipped topping and cake cubes
7. spread cake into an ungreased 13x9 dish
8. cover and chill for at least 2 hours
9. cut cake into squares
10. top with strawberries
demonstrations.review:
This was so delicious!!!!  Served to guests who went back for THIRDS!!!
My husband who doesn't really care for desserts loved this!!!  I will never make strawberry shortcake any other way but this.  Followed the recipe exactly and the only thing I would change is add more strawberries.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous caesar salad

i developed this dressing years ago, and i can honestly say that you won't be able to keep your spoon out of the fridge for a taste, it is *that* good! --- although i do think the dressing is better with the anchovy it can certainly be made without them. in a pinch i have even substituted buttermilk for the half and half cream, just use about the same amount --- this dressing gets stronger with refrigeration time so a small amount of fresh garlic goes a long way! ---- usually one recipe without doubling is perfect for one large romaine lettuce, if you are serving a large crowd of people you might want to double -- salad dressing will not work for this use *only* mayonnaise, i find hellman's brand mayonnaise works the best and for the  perfect companion to this salad see my recipe#125034-------------lower-fat option use reduced fat mayonnaise and fat-free half and half or low-fat milk --- also see my recipe#66596

1. in a small 2-cup mini food processor , process / mince the anchovy fillets and garlic together until finely minced
2. add in the remaining ingredients , and process for 30 seconds , or more until well mixed
3. adjust seasonings to taste
4. thin with buttermilk for a thinner consistency if desired
5. store in fridge , covered in a glass container for 3 or more hours before using
6. toss desired amount of dressing with romaine lettuce and croutons
7. sprinkle with more grated parmesan cheese if desired
demonstrations.review: OMG the Caeser dressing was the best I have ever had!  I made exactly as written throwing one extra head of garlic in.  I couldn't stop licking the bowl even before putting in the refrigerator for a few hours.  The flavor really does intensify after a few hours.  Just the best dressing ever!!

target.recipe_text:
baked ham   noodle supper

good comfort food and easy to make.

1. combine the butter , flour& mustard in a saucepan
2. add milk gradually , stirring constantly
3. cook until thick
4. add the ham , salt , pepper& celery
5. then stir in the noodles
6. pour into a greased baking dish
7. sprinkle with bread crumbs and dot with butter over the top
8. bake at 350 degrees for 30 to 45 minutes
target.review:
This worked out quite well. Even my wife, who is not a big ham fan, liked this. My 4 yr. old loved it.
Just for kicks, I added 2 hard-boiled eggs I had in the fridge. For some reason, after I smelled the ham-mustard sauce, it just sounded right. You know, eggs and mustard in egg salads, and ham and eggs. Anyway, the addition of diced eggs allowed the richness of the yolks to blunt the mustard's astringency somewhat. 

Didn't work all that well with a Mouton-Cadet bourdeaux, but that's all I had. try with a gooed reisling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq ribs

this is an excellent dish for a barbeque party. make the ribs in advance, and when your guests have arrived, all that's left is to grill them. you'll have them wondering how they got so tender and tasty so fast.

1. place ribs in a large skillet
2. cover with salted water and bring to a boil
3. reduce heat and simmer over low heat for 1 hour , or until meat is tender , but not falling off the bone
4. melt the butter in a saucepan and saute the onion and garlic until the onion is tender
5. remove from heat and pour into a blender with all remaining ingeredients
6. puree for 1 minute , then pour back into saucepan
7. bring to a boil , then remove from heat
8. place the boiled ribs in a shallow dish and pour sauce over them
9. place in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours
10. barbeque ribs on an outdoor grill over moderately hot coals , basting with the sauce and turning often until well browned
demonstrations.review: Decent sauce, but boiling then grilling is no substitute for slow-cooking. Keep the sauce, but try grilling/baking the ribs on low,low heat for 4-6 hours. The meat was OK, but the tissue (fat, fascia) that melts and provides juice and flavor during slow cooking remained chewy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
refried beans  crock pot

very easy to make! makes a great side dish or filling for burritos. enjoy!

1. sort and rinse dried beans
2. place in crockpot and cover with water and soak overnight
3. in the morning , drain and rinse beans
4. return beans to crock pot , and add 6 cups water and the salt
5. cover and cook on low for 10-12 hours or until beans are nice and tender
6. drain cooked beans , reserving cooking liquid
7. mash beans and return to crock
8. in a small skillet , saute onion and garlic in lard or butter until tender and lightly golden
9. add to crock pot
10. stir in chopped green chillies and ground cumin , adding some of the reserved cooking liquid to adjust the consistency as desired
11. cover crock , and cook on high for 15-30 minutes or until heated through nicely , stirring occasionallly
12. adjust salt , if necessary , before serving
13. garnish with cheese or chopped onion , if desired
demonstrations.review: Pretty decent! The gold standard  of refrieds are the ones at Ojeda's in Dallas, redolent with smoky bacon flavor. These come close if you add a packet of Goya ham stock/boullion.  With a bit of onion and Goya stock, they taste much like the beans at Taco Cabana, a better-than-avg. fast food joint we patronized we patronized when we lived in Texas.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cactus paddle salad relish or ensalada de nopalitos

i like this and use in tacos and fajitas. give it a try!

1. if the cactus is in big chunks dice to 1 / 2-1 / 4 inch pieces
2. toss together with the tomato , onion and cilantro
3. whisk together the dressing ingredients and toss with the salad
4. serve
demonstrations.review: Quite good. Makes a good salsa for chips. I'm taking this to a 4th of July party to freak out my Yankee neighbors.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
authentic italian tomato sauce

this is a recipe i got from my father who got it from a little old lady he knew from italy. i always simmer this sauce with my meatballs (recipe posted). you can also add sausage if you like. this sauce is to die for!!!!

1. in a large pot , saut onion and garlic in olive oil
2. empty plum tomatoes into large bowl and squash with your hands
3. add all ingredients to pot and simmer for 3 hours
demonstrations.review: Quite a good sauce. Rich and tomatoey. Cloves add a nice subtle flavor to the sauce. I, too, questioned the lack of oregano, but resisted the temptation to add some. The sauce was good w/o it. I did,l however, add a bit more garlic and onion. Cheese gives the sauce a subtle creaminess that echoes some pink (tomato & cream) sauces I have tried. Very good with your meatball recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pakistani kima  hamburger curry

a really easy one skillet meal made with ingredients i can find in my wisconsin kitchen. full of flavor and not too spicy; my kids love this. from mennonite cookbook more-with-less.

1. saute onion and garlic in butter till soft
2. add meat and brown well
3. stir in curry powder and seasonings , and remaining vegetables
4. cover and simmer 25 minutes , stirring several times and adding more water if needed
5. serve with rice
demonstrations.review:
Quite good. This is quite easy and flavorful, and is good for a quick weeknight meal.
Seems like an Indian version of S. Tex. picadillo . I followed the other poster's advice, and added the garam masala, and a few pepper flakes.  No extra potatoes were added, but I did toss in some extra water as it simmered.

target.recipe_text:
amy s pumpkin chocolate chip cookies

i've been making these cookies ever since i was a little girl.  they are so good and moist!  i usually use home-canned pumpkin, but if you are using store-canned pumpkin, just add 2 tablespoons of water to the recipe.  makes 30 large cookies.  enjoy!

1. mix sugar , pumpkin , oil and egg
2. add vanilla
3. mix dry ingredients and then add to pumpkin mixture
4. i usually cheat and just add directly to pumpkin mixture
5. add chocolate chips and mix
6. spoon onto pans , cook at 375 for 10-12 minutes
7. makes 30 cookies
target.review: Excellent!  I used home-cooked pumpkin and they were delicious.  Thanks, Amy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer batter fried mushrooms

i love fried mushrooms! i learned how to make these from a chef at a 5-star restaurant about a year ago. you can also use the batter to make fried onion rings. yum!

1. pour about 3 inches of oil into a large pot
2. heat until it reaches about 375 degrees farenhieght
3. meanwhile mix beer , flour , garlic powder , salt , pepper and parsley flakes in a large bowl
4. mix until smooth and well blended without any lumps
5. dip mushrooms into batter and coat well
6. fry mushrooms in batches in oil until crispy and brown
7. time will vary depending on temperature of oil and the amount of mushrooms being fried
8. i usually do about 10 mushrooms at a time and it takes about 8 minutes
9. when done , remove mushrooms to a plate or bowl lined with paper towels to drain off excess oil
10. place in a shallow bowl sprinkle with salt and toss to coat evenly
11. serve with favorite dipping sauce !
demonstrations.review: Really good recipe.  I used baby button mushrooms and cooked them about 4 minutes.  The batter was perfect and the mushrooms were perfectly cooked.  I used 1 pound and halved the recipe.  WONDERFUL!  Dipped 'em in a little soy sauce and enjoyed!  Thanks so much! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern quinoa vegetable casserole

this is a pretty good healthy and easy to prepare dish

1. preheat oven to 400
2. combine all ingredients except cheese and sour cream in a 2 quart casserole
3. cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes
4. remove and stir
5. bake for another 20 minutes or until all liquid has been absorbed and quinoa is tender
6. cover with cheese and broil till cheese is melted
7. serve with sour cream
demonstrations.review: Quick, easy and healthy.  Who can ask for more?!  Oh, and it tasted really great, too!  I'm not big on "health food", but this tasted more like a comfort food.  I used a can of corn rather than frozen corn and 1/2 tsp beef bullion plus 1/2 cup water instead of the broth.  Turned out very flavorful.  I skipped the toppings as I'm trying to "be good" and it was still fabulous!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracked wheat buttermilk bread with sunflower seeds

this is a nutritious, hearty bread with a nice nutty taste. it makes great toast! cracked wheat can be found in a bulk food store.

1. put cracked wheat into a small pot with 1 to 2 cups of water
2. bring to a boil , reduce heat to medium and boil for 6 minutes
3. remove from heat and drain well
4. let cool about 15 minutes
5. put cooked wheat into bread machine
6. add all other ingredients as listed except for the sunflower seeds
7. if you don't have buttermilk , you can make a substitute by adding 1 tbsp lemon juice to one cup of whole milk
8. stir and let sit for 5 minutes
9. use amount called for in the recipe
10. set bread machine for whole wheat bread
11. press start
12. add sunflower seeds at'addition' beep
demonstrations.review: This recipe is great!  I made it twice--the first time with sunflower seeds as mini loaves and the second time without as a regular loaf.  I preferred it without the sunflower seeds.  I also prefer to use the bread machine on the dough cycle and then make the bread in a bread pan in the oven because I don't like the shape of bread machine dough, but that's just my preference.  If you want to do that--the recipe makes 5 mini loaves (350 degrees for 20 minutes) or 1 big loaf (350 degrees for 45 minutes).  I live at a high altitude, over 7,000 feet, and this recipe turned out great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced crabapples

posted by request. original recipe from 

1. combine sugar , water and vinegar in a large stainless or enamel saucpan
2. break up cinnamon and tie up with allspice and cloves in a large square of cheesecloth and add to pan
3. bring to a boil and boil for 10 minutes
4. add prepared crabapples and return pan to a boil , reduce heat and boil gently for 10 to 15 minutes
5. remove spice bag
6. pack into clean hot jars to 3 / 4 inch from rim and add boiling syrup to cover , leaving 1 / 2 inch head space
7. do the jar thing
8. process in a boiling water bath for 20 minutes at altitudes up to 1000 feet
demonstrations.review: Changes:  5 c. sugar; only boil with crabapples for a couple of minutes.  I only gave this recipe 3 stars because even though I pricked the apples with a fork they were really mushy after boiling 10 minutes.  I ended up pulling them out of the brine, discarding them and starting with new apples.  I only boiled them a few minutes until they were just barely tender then processed in a boiling water bath.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mustard sauce for corned beef

my mother's recipe is a family favourite.

1. mix the egg , mustard and sugar together
2. add the vinegar and beef liquor
3. heat gently without boiling
4. serve hot or cold with hot or cold corned beef
demonstrations.review: I'm not issuing stars because I'm not sure what happened with my sauce.  It never sat up and it tasted way too much like vinegar.  I used 1/2 cup broth from my corned beef, 1/2 cup apple cider vinegar and everything else exactly like the recipe said.  Let it boil forever then finally added a teaspoon of cornstarch dissolved in a little cool water to thicken.

target.recipe_text:
cream of garlic  onion  and mushroom soup

this is a creamy, rich, dinner party type soup. yet it's so easy to make and so delicious that i make it often. don't be put off by the amount of garlic, as it cooks so long it becomes mellow and smooth tasting. i got the original recipe for this from the epicurious website, but have made several changes and additions.

1. saute chopped mushrooms in olive oil over high heat for 2-3 minutes
2. stir as little as possible so that they brown , not steam
3. remove from pan and set aside
4. melt butter over medium-low heat
5. add onions and garlic
6. cover and cook for about 10 minutes , stirring occasionally
7. add the flour and cook , stirring , for 3 minutes
8. add the broth , half and half , sherry , thyme , and bay leaf
9. stir well and bring to a boil
10. lower heat and cook uncovered for 15 minutes
11. add the bread pieces , stir well , and simmer for another 5 minutes
12. discard the bay leaf
13. using an immersion blender , puree the soup until the bread has dissolved and the soup is smooth
14. add the reserved mushrooms to the pureed soup and heat through
15. add salt and pepper to taste
target.review: Wonderful Soup...my family thought they were back in Germany. I didn't use Half and Half but whole milk with a spoon full of sourcream. Dry red wine 1/4 cup. Only had white Mushrooms, but will try with portobellos next time because I just love them. I didn't puree because I added the mushroom to soon, but I whisked the soup to break up the bread.  I thought the soup was wonderful will make it again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herbed zucchini noodles  low fat

recipe courtesy of juan carlos cruz from the low calorie commando on the cooking network.
posted for the low fat holiday challenge!

1. carefully drag a vegetable peeler the length of the zucchini to create
2. long strands
3. discard centers with the seeds
4. heat a large nonstick saute pan over medium heat with the butter
5. add the zucchini and quickly toss to coat with the butter
6. add parsley , thyme , oregano , and lemon pepper
7. toss again and warm through , about 1 minute
8. add the egg noodles
9. toss once again until pasta is warmed through but zucchini
10. remains crisp tender
11. taste and adjust flavor with salt and pepper
12. sprinkle with parmesan
demonstrations.review: Everyone in the house loved it!!! Added in Carrots also used the peeler to make long strands.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lentil veggie soup  crock pot

this soup is easy to put together with basic food items that most of us have around. i found the recipe in better homes and gardens biggest book of slow cooker recipes, and i did some adjustments with the vegetables and herbs used. i was surprised at how good this very simple soup turned out.

1. rinse lentils
2. place all ingredients except the pepper into a 4-6 quart slow cooker
3. cover and cook on low for at least 12 hours , or high for at least 5 hours
4. season with pepper and remove the bay leaves before serving
demonstrations.review: This is soup is wonderful!!! Easy to make and great after a long day of work and school.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
school cafeteria peanut butter bars

remember those flat peanut butter bars you used to get in your school cafeteria lunches? well, here they are!

1. combine flour , baking soda , and salt and set aside
2. cream together the butter , peanut butter , granulated sugar , brown sugar , and vanilla in a large bowl
3. beat in egg
4. gradually beat in flour mixture
5. spread batter into a 13x9x2 inch pan
6. bake at 375f for 15 to 18 minutes
7. let the bars it cool in the pan on a rack then cut into bars
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican corn soup

this is perfect for a cold day! the cheese and sour cream make this soup delicious and if you want to make it extra special add some avocado! recipe courtesy ingrid hoffmann.

1. if using fresh corn , scrape kernels from cobs using small sharp knife or spoon
2. place half of the corn kernels in blender with tomatoes , 2 cups of broth , and oregano
3. puree until smooth
4. set aside
5. in a large saucepan over medium heat , cook bacon , turning once until brown and crisp , about 10 minutes
6. remove bacon to a paper towel lined plate to drain
7. set aside
8. add onion to bacon fat in saucepan and cook , stirring frequently until onion is soft and translucent
9. add garlic and stir for another minute
10. add tomato-corn puree to saucepan with remaining 2 cups of broth and cayenne pepper if desired
11. bring to a low boil and add remaining whole corn kernels
12. simmer over medium-low heat until thickened , about 20 minutes
13. stir occasionally and remove any foam as it develops with a large flat metal spoon
14. season with salt and pepper
15. if using parsley or cilantro mix that in along with the cream , and heat through
16. to serve , garnish with crumbled bacon , remaining parsley or cilantro , crumbled cheese , tortilla chips or strips and avocado
