1. to make the fondue: in a bowl toss together cheeses and cornstarch
2. rub inside of a heavy 3- to 4-quart saucepan with garlic halves , leaving garlic in pan , and add wine and lemon juice
3. bring liquid just to a boil and stir in cheese mixture by handfuls
4. bring mixture to a bare simmer over moderate heat , stirring , and stir in kirsch , nutmeg , chilies , and pepper to taste
5. transfer fondue to a fondue pot and set over a low flame
6. stir in fried shallots , scallions , and / or bacon if using and serve fondue with accompaniments for dipping
7. to make the fried shallots: in a heavy 10- to 12-inch skillet cook shallots in oil moderately high heat , stirring , until golden brown
8. transfer shallots with a slotted spoon to paper towels to drain and season with salt
9. makes about 2 / 3 cup
target.review: I was first served this at one of Mimi's many parties.  That night I was introduced to several variations of fondue including this one.  It was fantastic.  Last weekend, I attempted to duplicate this fabulous recipe.  I will admit, it is a great deal of work, but the final out come is worth it and is sure to impress you and your guests.  I did have a difficult time trying to locate the chipotle chiles in adobo, which I eventually found. (GOYA Section of food store)  I will make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
confetti appetizers

go nuts! have a party! and at your next special occasion where an appetizer is on the menu, maybe you'd like to give these a try! (i said, "go nuts..." but there are no nuts in the recipe) :)

1. combine all ingredients , except mini-bagels
2. mix well
3. spread on mini-bagel halves
4. broil until cheese is melted
5. option: use 24 party bread slices toasted instead of the mini bagels
demonstrations.review: I made this as well as some other stuff for the superbowl.  Can you believe the guys actually at this and liked it?  Well they did.  very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingerbread waffles

nan

1. put the butter and molasses in a pan and heat until it boils
2. remove from the fire and stir in the milk and soda along with a well beaten egg
3. don't forget to sift the rest of your dry ingredients and add them to your milk mixture
4. bake in a hot waffle iron for 1 minute , turn off the power and leave them in the iron for another 2 to 3 minutes
5. serve with fruit of whipped cream / cool whip
demonstrations.review: I love these, as does my husband.  I think the children are not grown enough to appreciate this.  Between the cheese waffles and these waffles - I wouldn't know which to pick.  They are both so fantastic.  I just make them both!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gourmet beef burgers

nan

1. heat oil in large , non-stick skillet until hot
2. add onion
3. cook and stir until onion is browned , about 10 minutes
4. add green pepper and mushrooms
5. cook and stir until mushrooms are browned , about 8 minutes
6. stir in wine
7. simmer until reduced
8. stir in beef broth , thyme , salt and pepper
9. simmer , covered , until green pepper is limp
10. divide beef into 4 equal parts
11. shape beef into patties to match the shape of the french rolls
12. broil beef patties 4 inches from source of heat 4 minutes
13. flip patties
14. broil 4 minutes longer for rare , or until desired doneness
15. place patties on half of each roll
16. top each patty with 3 / 4 cup mushroom mixture
demonstrations.review: This is hands down the best recipe for burgers known to man.  The combiniation of onion, pepper, wine and thyme is a delight to the palate.  Will be making this again and again!  That's for certain.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ginger s  dorito  soup  spicy tomato soup

i invented this recipe completely on my own on a cold winter day when i craved something spicy but simple. i've never made plain tomato soup since :) it's a truly wonderful change, spicy but creamy, warm and smooth..and kids love it. if your children are particularly sensitive to spiceiness, you may want to reduce the hot pepper sauce and possibly eliminate the red pepper flakes. my boyfriend and his son actually came up with the name 

1. in saucepan , combine tomato soup , water and milk
2. stir until reasonably blended
3. add grated cheese , hot pepper sauce , crushed red pepper and black pepper
4. heat over medium heat , stirring often
5. continue heating until cheese has melted into soup
6. add salt , stir well
7. pour into bowls or cups , and serve with crackers
demonstrations.review: Very very good.  Nice and hot.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steak with lemon butter   caesar salad

nan

1. this recipe makes 4 servings
2. save leftovers to use in salads , sandwiches or to topped baked potatoes
3. stir together butter , lemon juice , green onion , parsley , and pepper
4. if necassary , chill about 20 minutes or until firm enough to shape
5. shape into a 1-inch thick log
6. wrap in plastic wrap and chill
7. slightly , slash fat on edges of the steaks at 1-inch intervals
8. if desired , sprinkle steaks with seasoned salt
9. place steaks on the unheated rack of a broiler pan
10. broil 3 to 4 inches from the heat to desired doneness , turning once
11. slice lemon butter into 8 slices
12. place 1 or 2 slices atop each steak
13. while steak is cooking , prepare salad mix as directed on package
demonstrations.review: The lemon flavor on the steak was fantastic.  We are used to that with a seafood combo, but it never occured to me to try it on red meat.  I will be making this again.

target.recipe_text:
chicken caesar wrap

try this easy wrap when you have left over chicken.

1. mix all ingredients except tortillas
2. toss to coat
3. place on softened tortillas and wrap
target.review: We love this as a snack or a light dinner... Very satisfying!!!  It's a great change from the normal Caesaer salad... I like to add in some sliced tomatoes sometimes just for the extra veggies...  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
applebee s veggie patch pizza

whenever we go to applebee's we have to get a veggie patch pizza!  i discovered this recipe on recipe goldmine.  i hope you will enjoy it!

1. pizza: in a hot saut pan or on a griddle , place sliced mushrooms and butter-flavor oil and season with salt , pepper and garlic
2. cook until hot
3. brush tortilla with oil and place on griddle
4. spread spinach and artichoke dip evenly on top of tortilla to within 1 / 2 inch of the edge
5. top with mushrooms , when cooked , italian seasoning and diced tomatoes
6. sprinkle shredded mozzarella cheese over pizza and remove from griddle and place on a pizza pan in an oven preheated to 350 degrees f
7. remove from oven when cheese is melted and top with shredded parmesan / romano cheese
8. cut into wedges and serve
9. spinach and artichoke dip: combine ingredients thoroughly in a bowl and spread mixture into a small baking dish
10. bake in an oven preheated to 350 degrees f for 30 minutes or until cheeses are bubbling and melted
11. serve as the "sauce" for the vegetable pizza or as a dip for chips
demonstrations.review: I have been enjoying this yummy appy for years at Applebee's and am so glad I can prepare it at home now!  I made this several times now... it's great when you get the munchies and want something hot.  I like to make this pizza whenever I have some leftover pinach and artichoke dip so I don't have to waste time preparing that day.  This is so easy and tasty... Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic butter rice

i love rice. i  also love garlic and cook with it a lot. it took a few tries to get the correct measurements for this recipe in order to submit it. i don't always use measurements when i cook.  this is very easy to make. this is a very moist and buttery rice with a good,  but not overpowering garlic flavor. for rice with less moisture, use less water and for a less garlicky flavor, use less garlic.  i read in an article on an internet medical site, that if garlic is cooked too long, it loses some of  its healthful benefits. they said not to cook garlic any longer than 3-6 minutes. i have also noticed that it loses some of its flavor if it's cooked too long. therefore,  i add the garlic towards the end of the cooking time to get more of a garlic flavor and more healthful benefits from the garlic.  i will sometimes have this for breakfast with a fried egg. i just put some of the rice on a plate and put a fried egg on it and mix it together. it is really good that way. i also serve the rice with gravy over it as a side dish with some meat.  it is also good just by itself. the chicken bouillon is optional but it adds to the flavor of the rice. if you have to or are watching your sodium intake, you might want to omit the bouillon or use less of it.  i have found that jasmine rice gives the best results for this recipe but you can also use white rice. prep and cooking times are estimates. note: due to the first review, i have edited this recipe. thank you lauralie41,

1. melt the butter or margarine in a 10" skillet over med-high heat
2. add the rice and stir
3. add the bouillon cube and stir until softened or dissolved
4. i use a spoon and break the bouillon cube apart while it is dissolving so that it dissolves faster
5. watch closely so that the rice does not start to brown
6. you might need to lower the heat if the rice starts to brown or appears to be cooking too fast
7. add the water and stir
8. cover with a lid and bring it to a boil
9. lower the heat to med to med-low and cook for 10 minutes or until rice is almost tender and a lot , but not all , of the water / butter mixture has been absorbed
10. this comes out better if it is "slow cooked"
11. add the garlic and stir
12. put the lid back on the skillet and continue cooking for 5 more minutes or until the rice is tender and all of the water has been absorbed
13. there may still be some melted butter at the bottom of the skillet , but that is okay
14. stir well and turn the burner off
15. let the skillet sit on the burner until you are ready to serve the rice
demonstrations.review: When I first read this recipe, I thought there was no way it was going to produce an edible rice...  more like rice porridge.  Well, I am happy to say I was wrong!  I just couldn't see how 1/2c rice would absorb 1.5c of water/broth... but it did.  I used only 2 Tbs of butter and toasted my rice (Jasmine) slowly in that.  It was plenty for us... I didn't want an oily rice...  I added in 1/2 a bouillon cube for a subtle chicken taste and water for the liquid...  I added in 2 cloves of garlic ( thinly sliced) at the beginning of the cooking and then stirred in another 2 cloves at the end...  My rice turned out fluffy, tender and dry... meaning that there was no liquid in the pan when I finished cooking.  It was the best rice I have ever had!!!  My BF also liked it a lot... he finished off the pan!  We will make this often... thanks for a great recipe that deserves a lot more than 5 stars...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco bell taco sauce

you can have this taste at home!

1. place in sauce pan and stir well , simmer at a very low temperature for 15- 20 minutes
2. remove and cool
3. may be kept in refrigerator for several days
demonstrations.review: Just finished making a half batch to go along with Recipe #59812 for tonight's quick and easy dinner.  Tastes great and just the right amount of spice for my wimpy BF!  I will be adding a drop or two of tabasco to mine, but now we don't have to run out to the store when we run out!!!  Thanks for posting!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paula deen s taco salad

i am posting the recipe as written by paula deen but i made a few changes.  i used shredded taco cheese instead of cubed cheddar cheese.  i mixed in a cup of salsa instead of topping each serving.  i also used regular tostitos instead of doritos to mix in.  the salad is great and very quick to make on a busy night.

1. combine the tomatoes , cheese , onion , lettuce and ground beef in a large bowl
2. add the salad dressing and mix well
3. just before serving , add the taco chips and toss
4. top each serving with salsa and serve with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: My BF's mother made us this salad for dinner this past weekend.  I have never had Catalina dressing before and found it a little sweet on it's own, but with some medium salsa to top it off, really was perfect.  The only thing she added was a can of drained kidney beans, which was a great addition.  Love this version of taco salad now, and we will be making it often!  Thanks for sharing!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
trattoria salad

this salad is so good you will not be able to stop eating it! recipe found on the internet.

1. combine all ingredients including marinade from artichokes except for romaine lettuce
2. add black pepper to taste
3. let marinate in the refrigerator until serving time
4. toss in lettuce at serving time and serve with hot french bread
demonstrations.review: A great change from your usual green salad!  These are ingredients I usually have in the fridge or the pantry, so putting this salad together was very easy.  Marinating the ingredients is very important, I have to agree... When I first tasted the salad when I mixed it together, it was not very tasty... but after the marination... fabulous!!!  I also used only a 1/4 lb of pasta to cut down on some of the carbs.  Then I used about 4 oz of buffalo mozarella (which was plenty for us), and a full pint of cherry tomatoes from my garden.  So fresh and tangy! I served this salad along with my rock salt crusted roast beef, yukon gold mashed potatoes and rolls... I am going to eat the leftovers tomorrow with some shredded roasted chicken... Thanks for posting!!!

target.recipe_text:
ritz crackers   egg

if you need a fast, easy and different  appetizer, try this. make ahead and pop in oven for the 5 minutes. they are always a winner.

1. combine hard cooked eggs , mayonnaise , chili powder , and salt & pepper
2. spoon on the crackers and top with a dab of the taco sauce
3. bake in 375 degree oven for 5 minutes
target.review: OMG!  This was SOOO good!  Exactly what I was craving....I knew it would be tasty, just because of the ingredients, but I had no idea it would be THAT tasty!  So addictive....Had to hard-boil 4 more eggs just to make it again -- doubled -- because my kids were mad at me that I wouldn't share it!  Good, simple snackies...and in my cookbook now.  Thank you!  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
montreal baked fish

yummy sauce, good and cheesey, easy to make- what more could you ask for?

1. pre-heat oven to 400
2. spray 9x9 pan with cooking spray and put fish in pan
3. mix butter , onion , montreal seasoning , and miracle whip and spread on top of fish
4. bake for 10 minutes per inch thickness of fish
5. top with cheese and bake til melted
6. serve with rice to use up all the delicious sauce
demonstrations.review: Very nice!  Such an easy recipe, and I was a bit skeptical about using Miracle Whip (since I'm a Hellman's Mayo gal), but I made this recipe exactly as written, and the sauce was AMAZING!  Really creamy and delicious and a perfect compliment to the fish.  I like my fish a little overcooked too, so I ended up baking it for 20 minutes like your note said.  Even an ex-DH who happened to be visiting loved this fish recipe.  And SO easy to prepare!  Thanks, didyb, for yet another Keeper in my house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tacos from scratch  way better than a packet and just as easy

those "taco seasoning" packets are usually so high in sodium and contain all kinds of unecessary junk.  give this one a try.  you can adjust the seasoning to your liking, add onions when you brown the beef or not, whatever you like.  i like to add fresh jalapenos when i add the sauce.  consider this a base recipe.  enjoy!

1. in a saute pan , brown ground beef
2. while beef is browning , combine the remainder of ingredients in a small bowl
3. drain beef
4. return to pan
5. add the sauce
6. stir , and add some water if desired
7. simmer uncovered until meat reaches desired consistency
8. serve on heated taco shells with cheese , sour cream , lettuce , tomatoes , olives , and hot sauce or however you prefer to use seasoned taco meat
demonstrations.review: Jackieblue, I absolutely LOVE this recipe!  I can't believe how good the sauce was!  It's the first time I've ever tried coriander, and WOW!  Beautiful flavor, almost like a subtle lemon-pepperish taste, accompanied by the smoky flavor of cumin -- MUCH better than the "Old Elpaso" taco seasoning I'd tried before...Even my 7 year old (who proclaims to dislike tacos) loved this, and even asked me if he could have a little more of the sauce to eat without the taco shell!  (I added hot sauce to mine only, because the kids don't like it -- but it was a great addition!)  Thank you for sharing this...It's a keeper!  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon   tomato spaghetti carbonara

pasta with bacon and tomatoes

1. in large frypan cook bacon until crisp
2. drain , reserving 2 tbsp drippings
3. set bacon aside
4. combine drippings and butter
5. set aside
6. in large saucepan , cook spaghetti according to package directions
7. drain
8. return to saucepan
9. add butter mixture , eggs , cheese and parsley tossing to combine
10. cook and stir over low heat until mixture is creamy and slightly thickened
11. stir in tomatoes and bacon
12. add salt and pepper to taste
13. serve immediately sprinkled with additional parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: OMG! This is absolutely OUTSTANDING!!! I wish I could give you 10 stars! It was so simple to prepare, with ingredients that I already had on hand...And although the kids grumbled when I muttered the unfamiliar word "Carbonara", they scarfed it down like there was no tomorrow! YES!! 5 stars from all the kids!!! The simple spices and cheese are perfect compliments to the bacon in this recipe, and it tastes so fresh that I felt like I was eating at the Olive Garden! (I did add about 1/4 tsp. minced garlic to the butter & bacon drippings mixture.) Thank you so much for sharing this "Newly Found Favorite" recipe! I'll be making this weekly, Brenda! TY! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesty biscuit bean bake

this came from pillsbury's harvest time cook book. my husband and i can almost eat the whole thing ourselves - it is sooo good.

1. heat oven to 375 degrees f
2. in 10-inch ovenproof skillet , brown ground beef and onion
3. drain
4. reserve 1 t seasoning mix
5. set aside
6. add remaining seasoning mix , beans , brown sugar and catsup to ground beef
7. heat until hot and bubbly
8. separate biscuit dough into 10 biscuits
9. place cheese cube in center of each biscuit
10. fold dough over cheese , covering completely
11. seal well , shaping into balls
12. roll each biscuit in reserved seasoning mix
13. arrange biscuits on hot meat mixture
14. bake at 375 degrees f for 20 to 25 minutes or until biscuits are a deep golden brown
15. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: We really loved this!  The only thing I changed, was that I put shredded cheddar cheese on top of the biscuits instead of inside...But we loved the flavor and the ease of preparation was wonderful for me!  We will definitely make this again, as my kids cleaned their plates! Thanks for sharing this, Sugar!  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy eggs

yummy way to have your eggs!

1. beat eggs and milk together
2. add salt and pepper to taste
3. cook over medium-high heat with the cream cheese
demonstrations.review: OMG!  Diggy, this is SO wonderful!  Oh, YUM!  I would have never thought of adding cream cheese to eggs, but Man, is it good!  Kinda sinful, really...Thank you so much for sharing!  YUM YUM YUM!!!

target.recipe_text:
alex s favorite beef and cheese pie

this is the #1 all-time most requested meal that my two boys grew up on. now adam is 27 and alex has passed away, so i'm posting this in alex's memory. so easy, and you won't be dissapointed! also very good cold the next day. i got in the habit of making 2 pies so there would be leftovers! i got this recipe from a small cookbook i picked up at a truckstop while driving across country called "cooking for the king of the road"

1. brown beef , onion and green pepper
2. drain fat off
3. add tomato sauce , green beans and garlic salt
4. simmer 10 minutes
5. while the beef mixture is simmering , spread separated crescent rolls into a pie plate , pressing edges together to make a thin crust with an edging around the rim
6. mix 1 cup cheese with beaten egg , spread on bottom of crust
7. pour in beef mixture
8. sprinkle with paprika and parsley
9. spread 1 cup cheese on top
10. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes , or until bubbly and cheese begins to brown
11. remove from oven
12. let stand for 10 minutes
target.review: Very good and easy to make comfort food at its best

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nana s chocolate cherry cake

this was one of my nana's signature cakes...we all loved cherry cordials and received them for christmas quite a few times!  this cake was my nana's way of giving us that same simple pleasure, but in a more healthy (???) way!  yum-o!!!

1. mix cake mix , eggs and flavorings until well-blended
2. fold in cherry pie filling
3. spread batter into a 8" x 12" pan that has been greased and floured
4. bake at 350 degrees until done
5. frost with dark chocolate frosting
demonstrations.review: This made a great cake I made it for my wife for mothers day and everyone loved it

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tater tot taco bake

this recipe reminds me of chili cheese fries. (i have reduced the amount of milk after reading the reviews. i hope this helps.)

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees then spray a 8x8 glass baking dish with cooking spray
2. brown the beef in a skillet until no longer pink , drain excess grease
3. stir in the rest of the ingredients except the tater tots
4. pour the mixture into the baking dish then top with the tater tots
5. bake for 25 minutes then turn on broil & cook another 5 minutes
6. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Very easy to make and the kids loved it.Thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: Wow its what a Reeses Cup wants to be when it grows up.I used dark chocolate chips and turned out super good

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled reuben sandwiches

these are terrific! even my sauerkraut hating dh liked these! i like to use my george foreman grill for these. serve with potato salad and crispy dill pickles.

1. spread each slice of bread with thousand island dressing
2. top 4 of the bread slices with sauerkraut , cheese and corned beef
3. place remaining bread slices on sandwich
4. spray butter flavored papm on the outsides of each sandwich
5. heat a large skillet over medium high heat
6. grill until browned , then turn and grill until heated through , and cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: I love this recipe. I had to improvise some I used wheat bread instead of rye and I forgot to get swiss cheese and used cheddar instead but it still came out to make a wonderful sandwich.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered mexican chicken

this is a recipe i got on the weight watchers web site. it is so good and only 6 points for a hearty serving. even if you aren't watching your weight, it is a great and filling dish.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. coat a lasagna pan with cooking spray
3. place chicken in medium saucepan and fill with enough cold water just to cover chicken
4. set pan over high heat and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat to medium and simmer until chicken is cooked through , about 10 minutes
6. drain
7. when chicken is cool enough to handle , cut into 1-inch pieces
8. transfer chicken to a large bowl and add beans , sour cream , 1 cup of shredded cheese , chilies , cumin , and pepper
9. mix well and set aside
10. arrange half of tortillas in bottom of prepared lasagna pan , overlapping pieces to cover surface
11. top tortillas with half of chicken mixture , layer with remaining tortillas and then top with remaining chicken mixture
12. sprinkle with remaining cup of cheese
13. bake until filling is bubbly and cheese is melted , about 30 minutes
14. let stand 5 minutes before slicing into 12 pieces
15. serve with salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: Very tasty even my picky son loved it. Thanks for sharing

target.recipe_text:
tenderest pork roast ever

this is the easiest recipe ever. you will have people raving over this recipe. a definite crowd pleaser. i will never make this roast any other way. the chicken broth tenderizes the pork like you would never believe and adds so much flavor to the pork. this also makes the best dipping sauce ever. this is a perfect recipe because you can just throw it in the crock pot and sleep for 8-10 hours or you can prepare it the night before and turn the crock pot on as you are walking out the door to start your busy day.

1. place pork roast in crock pot and poke as many holes as you can in the pork roast with a sharp knife or fork
2. pour dale's seasoning and chicken broth over the roast
3. sprinkle minced garlic or garlic powder
4. sprinkle with black pepper
5. bake on low for 8-10 hours
target.review: This was terrific. Put it in the crock pot last night about nine to eat at noon today after church with some mashed potatoes. Poured in flour/water to thicken it and will eat it as "stew" tomorrow. Great flavor!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled cheese sandwich pie

when you're not in the mood to cook, this is the recipe.  not a sandwich-no bread; not a quiche; not a pie-no crust; just good, plain and fast to do. and only one dirty bowl.  just be sure to grease the pie plate very well. this also lends itself to any number of additions.  a great lunch. or, on the side, a few slices of tomatoes or a small salad and voila!  dinner!  from my collection of really "olde" recipes.

1. in small mixing bowl , combine egg , flour , salt , pepper , 1 / 2 cup milk
2. using hand rotary beater , beat until smooth
3. add remaining 1 / 2 cup milk
4. beat until well blended
5. stir in 1 / 2 cup shredded cheese
6. pour into well-greased 8" pie pan
7. bake at 425 degrees fahrenheit for 30 minutes
8. sprinkle with 1 / 2 cup shredded cheese and bake about 2 minutes more
9. cut into 4 slices
10. variations:
11. grilled pizza sandwich: stir 1 / 2 cup finely chopped pepperoni or salami and 1 / 2 teaspoon italian seasoning into batter
12. grilled mexican sandwich pie: taco seasoning , mexican blend cheese and some chopped black olives , a few leftover black beans ?
13. crumbled cooked bacon ?
14. i'm sure you'll have some other ideas
demonstrations.review: Very good-- made it for main dish and added a pound of bacon that I fried and crumbled. Definitely make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smothered pork chops and sausage

saw emeril lagasse prepare this on foodtv and i could practically smell it and taste it through the screen. it was as fabulous as i thought it was going to be. i think you could use the same basic sauce for chicken and shrimp dishes as well. the sauce is to die for! adapted from recipe in "new new orleans cooking" by emeril lagasse and jessie tirsch.

1. mix ingredients for seasoning mix together in a small bowl and sprinkle generously on both sides of pork chops
2. heat the oil in a dutch oven or large pot over medium-high heat
3. add the pork chops , a few at a time and cook them until they are lightly browned on both sides
4. remove the pork chops to a platter and set aside
5. reduce the heat to medium
6. add the flour and stir constantly until the roux is the color of peanut butter , about 4 minutes
7. add the onions , salt , and pepper
8. cook , stirring , until the onions are slightly soft , about 5 minutes
9. add the garlic , bay leaves , chicken broth and water
10. bring to a boil
11. return the pork chops to the pot
12. reduce the heat to medium-low , cover and simmer for 45 minutes
13. add the smoked sausage and the potatoes
14. bring to a boil , and then reduce the heat to medium-low and cook , uncovered , stirring occasionally , for 30 minutes
15. serve with either steamed white rice or rice pilaf
demonstrations.review: These were great. The only change I made was to leave out the onions, since we don't like them...and I did cook them slightly differently. I realized I wouldn't have time to finish them on the stovetop and eat before church, so after the sauce was made, I added the potatoes and sausage back early and put it all in the oven at 200 degrees and cooked for about 2 hours. The sauce was terrific--caught my husband pouring it off the plate into his mouth! I was a little bit more decorous. I mopped mine up with a piece of bread :D Definitely a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy deep fried hush puppies

i have not tried this, but it just sounds soooo good to me!

1. in a mixing bowl , combine cornmeal , onion , flour , salt , baking soda , black pepper and cayenne pepper
2. in a small bowl , whisk together evaporated milk , egg and lemon juice
3. fold into cornmeal mixture , along with cheese
4. mix just until blended
5. in a large pot or an electric frying pan , pour in vegetable oil to a 2-inch depth
6. heat to 350f
7. drop batter by rounded tablespoons into hot oil
8. turn to brown evenly
9. cook , turning frequently , for about 3 minutes or until golden brown
10. remove with slotted spoon
11. drain
12. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I really liked these. Had them with blackened catfish. I also made them a bit too big, but they were delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon brownies

yummy twist on the traditional brownies.

1. combine cocoa and baking soda
2. blend in 1 / 3 cup margarine
3. add boiling water , stirring until thickened
4. stir in sugar , eggs , vanilla and rest of butter
5. add flour , cinnamon and salt
6. fold in chocolate chips
7. pour into a greased 9x13 pan
8. bake at 350 for 40 minutes
9. cool
10. frosting:
11. cream butter
12. combine cocoa , sugar , and cinnamon
13. add to butter with milk
14. beat well
15. add vanilla
16. mix well
17. spread over brownies
demonstrations.review: I asked my step-daughter how many satrs to give this recipe. I think she said five, but her mouth was so full of brownie I"m not sure! These were terrific and will definitely be made again and again and again around here.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paula deen s baked beef stroganoff casserole

i love making casseroles, and i love beef stroganoff.  this is one of my family's favorite meals.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease a 13x9x2-inch baking dish
3. in a large skillet , cook ground chuck , onion , and garlic over medium heat until meat is browned and crumbles
4. drain
5. return meat to skillet and stir in worcestershire , mushrooms , and beef broth
6. bring to a boil , reduce heat , and simmer for 15 minutes
7. stir in soup , sour cream , salt and pepper
8. remove from heat
9. combine hot cooked noodles and butter , stirring until butter melts
10. combine noodles and meat sauce
11. spoon into prepared baking dish
12. bake for 30 minutes
13. top evenly with fried onions and bake for 10 more minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good. I also used beef stew meat and I didn't cook the noodles before adding them. Just cooked them with a foil covering and they were fine. Definitely be making it again because it's so easy.

target.recipe_text:
quinoa tahini cookies

these cookies resemble oatmeal cookies, but they are crispier and have a unique taste.  they don't contain any wheat, gluten, common headache triggers, milk or eggs.  they're a nice treat for someone on a restrictive diet like mine, but i think they'll appeal to others too.  (it didn't take long for my husband to ask for a second one, and he can eat anything.)  i've only made this recipe at high altitude (5200 feet), so you'll have to test my low altitude suggestions.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. combine first four ingredients
3. mix until creamy
4. add remaining ingredients
5. mix well
6. spoon rounded teaspoonfuls of batter onto cookie sheets
7. bake for 10 - 14 minutes , or until they start to turn golden brown
target.review: Not bad, but not good either.  I subbed half white and half wheat flour for the rice flour, and used half tahini and half peanut butter.  They tasted like peanut butter cookies with sand in them.  I don't have any allergies and am not on a restrictive diet...just wanted to use up some quinoa.  The recipe didn't say to cook the quinoa beforehand..maybe that would have made a difference?  They came out fine, just don't taste great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really good vegetarian meatloaf  really

high in fiber and protein, low in fat, easy and really yummy! i've always thought meatloaf looks and smells so delicious and savory so, as a vegetarian, i decided to make a no-meat version! this is basically our favorite meatloaf recipe but with cooked mashed lentils instead of ground meat. the result is a very tasty dinner!

1. add salt to water and boil in a saucepan
2. add lentils and simmer covered 25-30 minutes , until lentils are soft and most of water is evaporated
3. remove from fire
4. drain and partially mash lentils
5. scrape into mixing bowl and allow to cool slightly
6. stir in onion , oats and cheese until mixed
7. add egg , tomato sauce , garlic , basil , parsley , seasoning salt and pepper
8. mix well
9. spoon into loaf pan that has been generously sprayed with pam or well-greased
10. smooth top with back of spoon
11. bake at 350 degrees for 30- 45 minutes until top of loaf is dry , firm and golden brown
12. cool in pan on rack for about 10 minutes
13. run a sharp knife around edges of pan then turn out loaf onto serving platter
demonstrations.review: Really delicious! I'm not vegetarian, but really love creative vegetarian meals -- this one gets the honor of going in the Recipe Box. So easy to make! It tastes like meatloaf, without the heavy "gut bomb" feeling afterwards.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon cornbread

from the family suppers cookbook which i sent to my swap partner floridanative.  this is super!!  i just had to try it.  you can also make it a spicy cornbread by subbing out the cinnamon and adding 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes and reducing the sugar to 3 tbls instead of 1/3 cup.  we loved it as cinnamon cornbread!  i do not have a skillet, so i melted the butter in an 9-inch round baking stone (first step).

1. heat oven to 450f in an 8 or 9 inch cast iron skillet , melt butter
2. tilt pan to coat the bottom and then pour the remaining butter into a glass measure
3. in a medium bowl , stir together the cornmeal mix , flour , sugar and cinnamon
4. add eggs and milk and stir until just blended
5. then stir in remaining butter
6. using a rubber spatula , scrape the batter into the skillet and smooth the top
7. bake until golden and springy to the touch in the center , about 15 minutes
8. let cool in pan for 10 minutes before cutting and serving
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  Worked great in the cast iron skillet.  I cut sugar to 1/4 cup and no cinnamon (personal preference) - it was great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chile vinegar turnip greens

cookin' down greens takes on a spicy twist!

1. heat oil in stockpot over medium-high heat
2. add garlic and saute 30 seconds or until lightly browned
3. add greens and saute 5 minutes , or until wilted
4. add remaining ingredients
5. bring to a boil , cover , reduce heat , and cook 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: The only flavor that really came through was the vinegar.  Probably needs more garlic and chili paste than the recipe says.  Ours was also very bitter, but that may have been due to the greens we used.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrot beet ginger soup

this soup is surprisingly good.  the ginger is very subtle and the color is beautiful.  when you want to use up garden produce in the fall, make this and freeze in zip lock bags for winter eating.  full of fiber and vitamins. this recipe is from cdkitchen.com i am guessing on prep time as i pulled the carrots and beets from the garden, etc.

1. peel beets and cut into chunks
2. fry onions in oil
3. add carrot chunks
4. fry for 10 min
5. add ginger , garlic , and orange peel
6. add stock or water
7. slow boil for about 50 minute or until veg are soft
8. puree
9. add salt and pepper
10. serve with sour cream
demonstrations.review: My husband came home with a bunch of fresh beets and carrots and I didn't know what to do with them.  I NEVER would have thought I would like beets, but this was GREAT!    I was a little confused on the directions...I guess you saute beets with carrots and onions.  Also, I thought it was lacking in a little flavor so I added more garlic and ginger (I used water, so it may be better with broth instead).  I pureed most of it, but left some chunks in for more texture.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baba ganoush   the best in the world

this baba ganoush recipe is from williams-sonoma's small plates by joanne wier, published 1998

1. prepare a medium-hot fire in a charcoal grill
2. preheat an oven to 375f
3. prick the eggplant with a fork in several places and place on the grill rack 4 to 5 inches from the fire
4. grill , turning frequently , until the skin blackens and blisters and the flesh just begins to feel soft , 10 to 15 minutes
5. transfer the eggplant to a baking sheet and bake until very soft , 15 to 20 minutes
6. remove from the oven , let cool slightly , and peel off and discard the skin
7. place the eggplant flesh in a bowl
8. using a fork , mash the eggplant to a paste
9. add the 1 / 4 cup tahini , the garlic , the 1 / 4 cup lemon juice and the cumin and mix well
10. season with salt , then taste and add more tahini and / or lemon juice , if needed
11. transfer the mixture to a serving bowl and spread with the back of a spoon to form a shallow well
12. drizzle the olive oil over the top and sprinkle with the parsley
13. place the olives around the sides
14. serve at room temperature
demonstrations.review:
Delicious!!
I made it in the magic bullet (it was easier to blend that way than mashing with a fork).
I sprinkled a little crumbled feta cheese on top for more flavor and garnish - yum!!

target.recipe_text:
to die for make ahead mashed potatoes

these are the best mashed potatoes ever! and they are so user-friendly because you can make them the night before. i never take these anywhere without people begging me for the recipe. once you make these, you will never want to make them any other way. also great in twice-baked potatoes. and, if you need really easy, buy pre-cooked mashed potatoes, add from these ingredients, stir, and re-heat in microwave. tastes almost as good as home-made! my favorite way to cook these are in the crockpot! edit: please note that i have always cooked these in the crockpot and have never baked them; i have gotten new feedback that they taste far better if cooked in the crockpot, so this is now my only recommendation for cooking source.

1. boil potatoes until tender
2. beat softened cream cheese and sour cream in mixing bowl
3. add hot potatoes and beat until smooth , adding small amounts of milk as needed
4. add butter , chives , salt , pepper and onion powder and beat until well-mixed
5. add garlic , green onions , and marjoram and beat until well-mixed
6. pour into either casserole dish or crockpot
7. dot with additional butter and sprinkle with paprika
8. bake for 25 minutes in 350f oven or cook on low in crockpot for 2-3 hours
9. if cooked in crockpot , add a few additional drops of butter and stir , just before serving
10. sprinkle with bacon bits or crumpled bacon just before serving
target.review:
My family loves mashed potatoes! One could say they are connoisseurs as they are very picky on the type and "add-ins" for the potatoes. I was a little nervous trying this but because I was going to be under a time crunch for preparation, I decided to give it a whirl. First off, I didn't tell anyone I was doing anything different to see if I could get a reaction. I didn't want to taint their views by knowing they are trying a new recipe. I just put it out there just like every year. They were delicious!! Making them in the crock pot is brilliant as these are always the last thing I prepare for any meal. Using the crock pot enables me to prepare them ahead of time and then not take time away from the guests/family right before meal time. I prepared them the night before exactly as written in the recipe. The next morning, I plugged in the crock pot. I was afraid they might be dry so I added a thin layer of chicken broth (about 1/2 inch) on top. As the potatoes warmed, I stirred in the broth. I would caution those who aren't onion/chive fans. This has a strong onion flavor. If you rather not have the onion, just use plain cream cheese.

This is our new staple for mashed potatoes. I must admit that I am not crazy with the added calories but the taste is outstanding! Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy soba noodles with chicken and peanut sauce

very fast, easy recipe. i use rotissiere chicken, kick the seasoning up with added chili paste.  goes very well with a quick veggie stir fry

1. shave carrot lengthwise into thin strips using a vegetable peeler
2. combine 1 / 3 cup broth , peanut butter , ginger , soy sauce , honey , pepper , and garlic
3. stir with a whisk until smooth
4. place chicken in a large saucepan
5. add 1 2 / 3 cups broth
6. bring to a boil
7. reduce heat , and simmer 4 minutes or until chicken is done
8. remove from heat
9. let stand 20 minutes
10. drain
11. cut chicken into 2-inch pieces
12. combine carrot , peanut sauce , chicken , and noodles in a large bowl
13. toss to coat
14. sprinkle with onions and peanuts
demonstrations.review: The sauce was great.  We usually like soba noodles that we get at restaurants, however, those that we bought had a strong buckwheat flavor.  We cannot hold that against this recipe!  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dry rub pork ribs

a simple, no hassle, no mess and delicious method for 

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. cut pork ribs into sections of 3 or 4 bones
3. mix remaining ingredients well , sprinkle on both sides of ribs and rub into the meat
4. seal rib sections in foil with a tablespoon of water in each package , and bake for 2 hours on a cookie sheet in the center of the oven
5. open foil carefully as steam escapes
6. can be crisped on a hot bbq if desired but will be great just the way it is
demonstrations.review: Very good.  As others have said - good balance of spicy and salty...  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef  cheese  and noodle bake

from cooking light, february 2006. yummy, filling casserole.

1. preheat over to 350
2. cook pasta , drain and set aside
3. saute onion , carrot , and garlic for about 3 minutes
4. add ground beef and brown breaking up the meat
5. add tomato sauce , 1 / 2 tsp salt , and pepper
6. continue to cook for about 2 minutes
7. add macaroni
8. put mixture into a 11 x 7 baking dish that has been sprayed with cooking spray
9. heat milk , flour , remaining 1 / 2 tsp salt , and nutmeg over medium heat whisking constantly for about 2 minutes , until smooth and thickening
10. stir in 1 cup of grated cheese until smooth
11. pour cheese mixture over pasta and stir in to blend
12. spread remaining cheese over the top
13. bake for 20 minutes or until cheese is starting to brown
14. let sit for about 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: So much better than Hamburger Helper!!  I also love sneaking in the carrots.  We did add some green pepper.  My only comment is that I would not add as much black pepper next time.  It just seemed too much.  Thanks so much!  Definitely a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious irish cream  no eggs

this recipe contains no eggs which makes it safe for the elderly, this is very good!

1. in a blender combine all ingredients
2. blend on high power for about 20-30 seconds
3. store tightly sealed in the refrigerator
4. shake well before using
demonstrations.review: Very Very good...  Made 5 batches and decorated mason jars to take to a St. Pats party, with a bunch of beer drinkers (I didn't know - arg!!)  Once they tried it, they loved it.  I did a couple of small things to try to reduce calories - I mixed the whipping cream with half and half (saving a huge amount of calories).  I used fat free sweetened condensed mild and light chocolate syrup.  STILL WONDERFUL!!  Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I agree --- this is one of the best.  Get this --- my DH doesn't like cream cheese, black beans or mexican --  but once he tried it, he was sold.  I serve it with rice.  My kids rolled it into tortillas.  I agree with AmyZoe about throwing in some chilies and red peper to add some additional spice but for kids - it is just perfect when I used Medium salsa.

target.recipe_text:
easiest tastiest barbecue country style ribs  slow cooker

i threw this together one morning before going out for the day. it was super easy because only three ingredients are needed! not only did the house smell heavenly when we came home, but dinner was ready and it was awesome!

1. place all ingredients in crock pot
2. cook on low for 6 to 8 hours
3. meat starts to fall off the bones-- be careful of the small ones in the juices !
target.review: This is the first time I have ever made ribs and they were absolutely fantastic! So tender and fell right off the bone! DH ate seconds and thirds! Served with Recipe #102305 and Recipe #42564

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: This is awesome! I added a package of onion soup mix as well. So delicious. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best grilled pork chops

this is a simple recipe i have adapted from company's coming.it is simple to throw together the marinade in the morning before going off to work and coming home to an easy dinner to prepare at night.

1. in deep bowl mix all marinade ingredients
2. marinate at least 2 hours
3. remove from marinade and cook over medium-high heat on greased grill for no more than 15 minutes or until done
4. cooking time for second side is shorter by 1-2 minutes
5. 3 / 4" or thinner , 5-6 minutes maximum per side , thicker than 3 / 4" 6-7 minutes maximum per side
6. do not over_grill , chops will become tough
7. after 2 minutes grilling on a side , rotate chops 45 degrees for even cooking
8. turn over when juices pool on upper surface and meat appears to be cooked half-way through
demonstrations.review: WOW! I can see why this is rated so highly! I had some porkchops to use up and we wanted to grill them but I didn't have a recipe so I did a quick search and came up with this one -- soo yummy! Next time we are going to try stuffing them with Gouda cheese. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortilla crusted tilapia

i'm not fond of fish, but even i like this dish.  tilapia is mild, and the spicy crust is very appealing.  i like to make the crumb crust in bulk and freeze in meal sized amounts.  then this becomes a super quick weeknight meal.

1. preheat oven to 375f coat a baking sheet with cooking spray
2. place tortilla pieces , pepper , lime juice , cilantro and spices in blender
3. pulse until the mixture is uniform small crumbs
4. spread on plate
5. beat egg in shallow dish
6. dip each fillet in egg , then in crumbs , patting crumbs to adhere
7. place on baking sheet
8. bake until fish flakes , about 15 minutes depending on thickness of fillets
demonstrations.review: Our local grocery store sells  already prepared Tortilla Crusted Tilapia and I LOVE it, so I thought I'd try to find the recipe -- this is a pretty close match! I don't bake a lot of fish but this was very easy to prepare and super yummy -- not "fishy" tasting at all. Best of all? My picky 1 year old gobbled it up. That alone makes it worth 5 stars in my book!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy baked sweet potato  fries

this recipe is adapted from a weight loss websites newsletter. posted for 2006 zaar world tour - mexico

1. preheat oven to 450f with aluminum foil or parchment paper , line a cookie sheet
2. in a medium bowl , combine sweet potatoes with olive oil and seasonings
3. mix well to evenly coat potatoes
4. place potato strips on the foil or parchment lined cookie sheet and leave space between strips for even baking
5. bake for approximately 15 minutes or until potatoes become crispy
6. turn strips every 5 to 7 minutes as needed
7. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I was looking for a different, healthier alternative to french fries to serve with our burgers the other night and gave these a try. Very good! They definitely have a different taste, but we really liked them. I felt like there was just a little something missing but I couldn't put my finger on it. Maybe more salt? I don't know, but I'll definitely be making it again and possibly experimenting a little! Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy potato chip chicken breasts

this has been a long time favourite in my house, it's a great way to use up any leftover potato chips ;-) you can season the crushed potato chips with black pepper if desired.

1. grease an 8 x 8-inch baking dish
2. set oven to 425 degrees
3. place sour cream in a medium bowl
4. coat all sides of the chicken in sour cream
5. coat with crushed potato chips
6. place chicken in greased baking sheet
7. bake for 5 mins , then reduce heat to 375 degrees , and bake for 10-15 mins longer
8. while the chicken is baking , melt butter
9. add garlic powder to butter , mix
10. set oven back to 450 degrees
11. remove chicken from oven
12. brush with melted butter / garlic mixture
13. return to oven and bake for additional 5 mins , or until chicken is golden brown
14. delicious !
demonstrations.review: I actually originally got this recipe from my mother-in-law who has made this for years -- it isn't very healthy so I don't make it often, but it is a treat when I do -- it tastes fantastic! :) I normally cut the chicken breast into strips before coating but otherwise the recipe is the same! It's one that will please the whole family!

target.recipe_text:
warm cheesy potato soup

here's a warm, hearty, easy to prepare soup for those chilly days of winter. if found this recipe in a senior spotlight newspaper. i used skim milk and fat free, low sodium chicken broth. the cheese i added for zip! (so much for extra calories, but it was worth it!!)

1. in a large saucepan over medium-high heat , sautee ham and onions in the butter , until the onions are translucent
2. stir in the mustard , then pour in the chicken broth
3. add the potatoes , bring to a boil and cook until the potatoes are tender
4. add to the potato mixture and heat until warm , but not boiling
5. add seasonings
6. serve with warm bread or rolls
7. combine the milk and cream of celery soup in a small saucepan
8. add the cheese and melt , stirring frequently
target.review: GOOD STUFF...thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger spaghetti for 50

this is good for a huge gathering of hungry people.

1. cook spaghetti in boiling salted water until tender
2. drain
3. brown the meat and minced onions
4. mix the tomatoes , salt , pepper and the cup of oil drippings together then mix it into the spaghetti ,
5. add and mix in the fried hamburger and onions
6. spread out into baking pans
7. cover with buttered bread crumbs
8. bake at 300f for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review:
OH MY GOODNESS....could this have been any easier to feed a hungry youth group and 8 starving adults???  I think NOT!

Thanks Shirl for saving my "bottom end" when it was my turn to cook for the church group.  This recipe turned out GREAT and I'll never be able to relay all of my thanks!

:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old time waldorf salad

the old fashioned waldorf salad has very few ingredients. this is the old timey way to fix it.

1. as soon as apples are diced , mix the mayonnaise into the apples so they will not turn brown
2. add celery and nuts
3. combine well
demonstrations.review:
It doesn't get much easier or better than this recipe.  Mom fixed it for Thanksgiving this year and we all devoured it.
The combination of flavors and textures are really good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
toffee oatmeal cookies

yummy! 8)

1. preheat oven to 300
2. line cookie sheets with parchment paper
3. in medium bowl , cream butter and brown sugar
4. stir in egg and vanilla extract until smooth
5. sift together flour , salt and baking soda
6. stir this into the other mixture
7. blend in oats and toffee bits
8. drop rounded tablespoonfuls onto cookie sheets
9. flatten slightly
10. bake 10-18 minutes in the preheated oven
11. cookies will look dry when finished baked
demonstrations.review: Very very good.  Thank you for a new recipe for my family and friends.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh peach french toast cobbler

from the michigan cook book comes this yummy sounding recipe from the hanson house in grayling michigan. i haven't tried this, but there's nothing like good fresh peaches! prep time is a bit of a guess and includes letting the bread soak for 2 hours.

1. slice bread into 8 slices and arrange in a shallow baking pan
2. in a bowl whisk together eggs , milk , baking powder and vanilla
3. pour mixture over bread , turn slices to coat evenly , then cover with plastic wrap and let stand 2 hours at room temperature or refrigerate overnight
4. preheat oven to 450 degrees
5. grease a 9x13 inch baking pan
6. mix sugar , cinnamon and cornstarch in a bowl and then fold in peaches , coating well
7. ifusing frozen peaches that are sweetened you might want to add less sugar spread peach mixture in the greased baking pan and cover with the egg-soaked bread slices , wetter side up , wedging the bread in tightly
8. brush the top of the bread slices with melted butter
9. bake 20-25 minutes or'til toast looks golden and the peaches buble around the edges of the pan
10. place toast on plates and spoon the peach sauce over the top and sprinkle with powdered sugar
demonstrations.review:
Made this last night for Spring 2007 PAC.  It went together quickly and the 2 hour soak time was plenty of time for the bread to absorb the egg mixture.
I used frozen peaches as there aren't any good fresh ones ready here yet.  NEXT TIME, I will add more sugar to the peaches as mine weren't sweet enough for our tastes.
Mark too the remainder of the pan to work with him this morning and called to declare that the pan had been licked clean within 15 minutes.
Thanks Ree' for another great addition to my recipe file.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jello pudding pecan pie

another oldie but goodie from the 

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. in a large bowl mix pudding mix and corn syrup
3. gradually add evaporated milk and egg until well blended
4. add pecans and pour into pie shell
5. bake until top of pie is firm and just starting to crack , about 40 minutes
6. cool at least 3 hours
demonstrations.review:
The flavor of this pie was wonderful but mine baked for almost an hour and never did set. That fact didn't seem to bother anyone though as they ate it out of a bowl with a spoon.
I'll try again and maybe add another egg to firm it up.

target.recipe_text:
simple sweet scones

this is a simple perfectly delicious recipe my mom used to make for our family. it origioually came from a biscuits and scones recipe book, this one was always my favorite of all the recipes.

1. heat oven to 425f
2. put flour , baking powder and salt into a large bowl
3. stir mix well add butter and cut in with a pastry blender or rub in with your fingers , until the mixture looks like fine crumbs
4. add sugar
5. toss to mix
6. add milk and stir with a wooden spoon until dough forms ,
7. place dough on floured counter and knead gently until the dough comes together in a ball
8. pat or roll into a circle about 1 1 / 2 inches thick
9. cut each circle into 6 or 8 wedges
10. place wedges on a greased cookie sheet- slightly apart for crisp sides , touching for soft
11. bake about 12 minutes , or until medium brown on top
target.review: Really good!  My children loved them.  I think they ate them all before my husband even had a chance to try them.  I guess I'll have to make them again. I will probably add some cinnamon to the batter next time.  YUMMY!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simplicity chocolate cake

a quick, easy and extremely good chocolate cake. my mother often baked this cake for the jackaroos (cowboys) when she was a cook on the cattle stations (ranch) in outback australia. be careful not to overcook this cake and it will stay moist and fresh for days. enjoy. i use this recipe on a regular basis.

1. melt the butter
2. put all the other ingredients into a large bowl and pour the melted butter on top on them
3. beat on high for 3 minutes only
4. pour the mixture into a prepared cake tin and bake in a moderate oven
5. the baking time will depend on the size and shape of your cake tin
6. be careful not to overcook this cake and it will be deliciously moist and fresh days after it is baked
7. ice with your favourite chocolate icing / frosting or top with fresh or mock cream sweetened and flavoured with vanilla or rum , and cover with grated chocolate or nuts
demonstrations.review: I made this for my son's birthday.  It was so easy and very moist.  Good recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeno popper burgers

oh boy, these are good-good-good! if you like stuffed burgers and poppers, you'll love these. :)

1. mix meat , worcestershire sauce , salt , garlic powder , and pepper
2. shape the mixture into 12 thin patties , each about 4 inches in diameter
3. mix the cream cheese , ancho chili powder , cumin , dried onion , and minced jalapeno
4. top 6 patties with the cheese mixture , spreading it to within 1 / 2-inch of the edge
5. cover each patty with one of the remaining 6 patties , sealing the edges well
6. broil or grill the patties , turning only once if possible , until preferred doneness and cheese is melted , about 10 to 15 minutes
7. low-carb serving: top with a bit of grated cheddar , guacamole , and enjoy !
8. high-carb serving: eat with a bun and other condiments
demonstrations.review: Yummy!!!  I made these for my husband and got rave reveiws.  I will definately make these again.  The only change I would make is to add more jalapeno peppers.  We like it spicy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanilla rum balls

this no bake and gift cookie is from www.mightycool.com and these are - to die for! try 'em, they're addictive! make ahead, and store in an airtight container(we don't want the tantalizing vapors to vanish!) for at least a week, to enjoy these best! pls. note- brandy or bourbon can be substituted for rum. also, pls. note - the yield is a guess. honestly, i feel it depends to a gigantic extent on your power to resist these:)

1. in a large bowl , sift together the cocoa and confectioners' sugar
2. in a food processor or blender crush / crumble the vanilla wafers
3. add the crushed vanilla wafers to the sugar mixture and combine
4. add the remaining ingredients
5. form the mixture into 1 inch balls with your hands
6. the balls should hold together easily and retain their shape
7. if the mixture is too dry to hold together or too wet to form balls , you can easily adjust the consistency by adding rum / sugar accordingly
8. sprinkle the extra cocoa or ground chocolate on a flat surface and roll the balls in to coat
9. have 'em on your cookie tray this year and watch 'em vanish before you know it !
demonstrations.review: WOW!!!  I took these to party last weekend and got rave reviews!  There were many requests for this recipe.  I suggest letting the rum balls rest for a few hours before devouring them.  If you eat them right away the texture is a little grainy.  When you allow them to rest they become incredibly creamy and even more yummy.  The flavor is delicious either way.  This is a KEEPER!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome blueberry muffins

this is a awesome blueberry muffin recipe. double it to make large muffins. i sometimes add cinnamon to the batter.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. grease muffin cups or line with muffin liners
3. combine 1 1 / 2 cups flour , 3 / 4 cup sugar , salt and baking powder
4. place vegetable oil into a 1 cup measuring cup
5. add the egg and enough milk to fill the cup
6. mix this with flour mixture
7. fold in blueberries
8. fill muffin cups right to the top , and sprinkle with crumb topping mixture
9. to make crumb topping: mix together 1 / 2 cup sugar , 1 / 3 cup flour , 1 / 4 cup butter , and 1 1 / 2 teaspoons cinnamon
10. mix with fork , and sprinkle over muffins before baking
11. bake for 20 to 25 minutes in the preheated oven , or until done
demonstrations.review: YUMMY! YUMMY! YUMMY! I used 1/3 a cup of applesauce and a little dash of oil in place of the oil and I added 1/4 cup of wheat germ with 1 1/4 cup of flour.  I am always on the lookout for healthy muffins for my kids to grab on the way to school.  I tried using whole wheat flour for 1/2 the flour a different time but they came out to heavy.  This time they turned out wonderful(very moist).  My kids keep asking for more! I will make these again soon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried chicken tea sandwiches

these tea sandwiches have chewey dried cranberries and crunchy pecans, the sweetness of apple and the spiciness of curry on heart-shaped bread.

1. combine the fist 6 ingredients thru green onions
2. combine mayonnaise , lime juice and curry powder
3. add to chicken mixture and stir to coat
4. cover and refrigerate until ready to serve
5. cut each slice of bread with a 3" heart-shaped cookie cutter
6. top with lettuce and chicken salad
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  Yummy!  Yummy!  My friend's and I loved this recipe.  Wow!   It was a wonderful addition to my tea party.  Very pretty too.  MMMMMM....

target.recipe_text:
big grandma s best peanut butter cookies

this is my husband's grandmother's recipe that is cherished by the family. they are the best cookie that melts in your mouth. they don't have the normal peanut butter fork crossing...but more of a crackled sugar type cookie... my husband comes from a huge family - and these are one of the cherished recipes!!

1. cream together the sugars , crisco , peanut butter
2. add the eggs and vanilla
3. sift the dry ingredients together and add gradually until blended well
4. roll into tablespoon size balls
5. roll cookie dough balls into sugar
6. place on cookie sheets- do not mash with fork in normal "peanut butter cookie" fashion !
7. bake at 350 oven for 11-13 minutes
target.review: I made these this morning to take to a cookie exchange. I used crunchy p.b.  Once I had the dough mixed I tasted it and decided to add about 1/2 cup more peanut butter, and about 3/4 cup mini semi-sweet chocolate chips to boost the flavor. I also squished them w/a fork dipped in sugar, like traditional p.b. cookies. I only did this from failure to read thoroughly as it was way TOO early! The cookies came out excellent! EVERYONE loved them and asked for the recipe! Thanks so much for such an easy and delicious cookie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pete s scratch pancakes

it was the fall of 1987 when pete nyhus walked into our office, just to visit. we started talking about breakfast, and he reached into a wastepaper basket and pulled out a scrap of teletype paper. he wrote out this recipe, and my family has never used pre-mix since.

1. mix the dry items first
2. combine the eggs and melted butter to the milk and slowly stir into the flour mixture
3. let sit at least 10 minutes while heating the pan
4. these will be high , but light and fluffy --
demonstrations.review: The kids and husband LOVED these pancakes!!  We will not go back to the boxed mixes again!  THANKS for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot black bean salsa chicken  oamc

i was trying to think of ways to make my oamc recipes for crock pot use...you know they sell those crock pot box recipes at the grocery now. this is one of the ones i found that work and is simple. there may still be some fiddling but it's pretty good as is. hope you will give it a try.

1. for immediate cooking:
2. mix corn , beans and 1 cup of salsa together and put in the bottom of the crock pot
3. add the chicken
4. salt and pepper to taste if desired
5. added 1 more cup of salsa over the top of the chicken
6. cook on low for 6 hours add 8 oz of cream cheese- cubed and stir in until melted
7. for oamc:
8. you can dump everything into a freezer bag except for the cream cheese and freeze
9. dump in the crock pot
10. cook on low for 8 hours
11. add cream cheese when you are done
12. good served over cooked rice and dipped into with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: This was easy to prepare and tasted exceptional!  My 9,3,and 1 1/2 yr olds all asked for more!! Thanks for a great change of pace recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy granola

this granola makes a great, filling snack. good dry or with milk. it is very addictive, but it's good for you, so enjoy!

1. heat oven to 275 degrees f
2. line 2 cookie sheets with parchment paper
3. combine brown sugar and water in a 4 cup microwave proof cup
4. microwave on high 5 minutes until sugar is completely dissolved
5. remove from microwave and stir in vanilla and salt
6. in large mixing bowl , mix oats , nuts , and brown sugar mixture
7. mix thoroughly
8. spread onto cookie sheets and bake 45 minutes-1 hour until golden brown
9. when granola has cooled completely , add fruits if you wish and store in airtight container
demonstrations.review: This was my first attempt at making granola. I found the recipe so simple that my 2 & 4 yo helped make most of it. I used tin foil lined sheets and decreased the temp 1/2 way through cooking to 250 for fear of burning. I used 7 grain mix for oats and added some milled flax and sunflower seeds, but followed the recipe other than that.  My kids liked it but thought it needed to be sweeter. I added some dried cranberries to some and it was good.  I think with the additions that I made  it created a more "nutty" flavored mix (which I loved) but the next time I make it I will add a little more brown sugar mixture.  I used natural brown sugar this time, so it may be that doesn't produce as sweet a flavor. All in all a very good and easy recipe! Thanks for a great way to save some $$ and skip the highpriced store stuff!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best banana bread

you'll never need another banana bread recipe ever again!

1. remove odd pots and pans from oven
2. preheat oven to 350 / 180
3. cream together butter and sugar
4. add eggs and crushed bananas
5. combine well
6. sift together flour , soda and salt
7. add to creamed mixture
8. add vanilla
9. mix just until combined
10. do not overmix
11. pour into greased and floured loaf pan
12. bake at 350 / 180 for 55 minutes
13. keeps well , refrigerated
demonstrations.review: This recipe was simple to throw together with a fantastic result! My whole family woofed it down quickly, even the pickiest 2 y.o. Thanks so much for the perfect flavor and texture bread!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef patties in onion gravy

good 

1. combine all patty ingredients
2. mix thouroughly with your hands and shape into 4 patties
3. spray a non-stick skillet , and brown patties on both sides
4. add dry onion soup mix and 1 1 / 2 cup water
5. cover pan tightly and simmer for 20 minutes
6. remove patties to a plate
7. in a gravy shaker or jar , combine 1 / 2 cup water with 2 tbs
8. flour
9. stir flour and water into onion gravy
10. stir constantly with a whisk until it comes to a boil
11. boil 1 minute
12. return patties to pan
13. serve with mashed potatoes or hot cooked noodles
demonstrations.review: Quick and easy meal! My whole family gave it five stars. Thanks for a real kid/man pleaser!

target.recipe_text:
bev s spaghetti sauce

this is a recipe i have developed over a number of years. this is the only spaghetti sauce my family will request! very easy to make. i hope your family enjoys it as much as mine does!

1. brown the ground beef , onion and garlic in olive oil with bay leaves , oregano , basil , italian seasoning , salt and pepper
2. add tomato paste , tomato sauce and diced tomatoes
3. stir well and bring to a simmer over medium heat
4. cover and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
5. use sauce to top your cooked spaghetti
6. top with sauteed mushroom
7. pass the parmesan
target.review:
Great spaghetti sauce! 
Due to time constraints we sometimes use sauce from a jar and spice it up.  My husband said this one was taking too long and therefore not worth the trouble, but he changed his mind after tasting it. Made it as written and we both loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breasts with rosemary

this is so easy to make and can be served over pasta, rice, etc.

1. pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt& pepper
2. dip chicken in flour and shake of excess
3. heat butter and cook chicken 4-6 minutes per side or until no longer pink in the center and lightly browned
4. remove from pan
5. discard any fat from the pan
6. return pan to heat
7. add chicken stock and rosemary
8. cook 2 minutes
9. add cream and mustard
10. bring to a boil
11. cook 4-5 minutes until slightly thickened
12. season to taste with salt and pepper
13. return chicken to pan
14. coat with sauce and heat thoroughly
demonstrations.review: I wanted something easy and saw this recipe. My friend had given me fresh rosemary so I chose this chicken dish, and I'm so glad I did. I doubled the sauce, using lowfat milk and dijonnaise since that's what I had. My sauce ended up being thin, even after cooking it a little longer than stated, but I'm sure that was from my substitutions and my old electric stove. Also, based on another reviewer's comment, I put 3 rosemary sprigs in while cooking and then took them out before serving. It was easier, plus I wasn't sure what my husband would think of the rosemary, He loved it and said it had the perfect amount of seasoning. I served it over rice, and the leftovers I served over fried potatoes from another meal. Both were equally as good. Thanks for a great recipe that I will definitely make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic green beans

this is a quick and easy way to spruce up green beans. and they disappear fast. my family devours these. i created this when i was looking for something different to do with green beans in a hurry. a nice side for company too!

1. place green beans in microwave safe dish with the butter
2. cover and cook on high for five minutes
3. add vinegar and parmesan cheese
4. cook on high five more minutes
5. stir to make sure the beans are well coated with the vinegar mixture
6. serve and enjoy !
7. these would work well with fresh green beans too
8. you would just need to adjust the cooking time
9. ingredient amounts can be adjusted to suit your taste
10. i will sometimes increase the parmesan cheese and use 2 tablespoons of butter
demonstrations.review: To cut calories I didn't use the cheese, so I added some garlic and heb seasoning instead and these were very good. I used 16 oz. of frozen  haricot verts so I cooked them a couple of minutes longer. I'm sure with the cheese they'll be even better!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pot roast in a crock pot

once you have removed the yummy meat and veg make a gravy from the juices-an awsome fall and winter dish. serve with hot bread and a salad. (and the rest of the wine!)

1. place 1 / 2 of the vegetables in the crock pot
2. place the meat on top of the vegetables
3. add the other half of the vegetables on top of the meat
4. add the beef stock and the wine
5. add the salt and pepper and herbs
6. cook on low for 8-10 hours
demonstrations.review: Very good flavor! I added garlic and since I had no peas I added frozen green beans. Now I have lots of leftovers for the week. Yum. Will definitely make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffed small red potato appetizer

a great make ahead appetizer,
can also be an accompaniment to an entree,
or serve them with a salad.
this is the best recipe for stuffed small potatoes, try it and see.....
this wonderful recipe was found on a beautiful website: www.finedinings.com

1. cook whole unpeeled potatoes in boiling water until fork-tender but not mushy
2. place in cold water to stop cooking
3. carefully cut each cooked potato in half
4. with a melon baller or small spoon , scoop out centers , leaving a 1 / 4-inch shell of pulp in skins
5. in a small bowl , combine sour cream , bacon , seasoned salt , pepper and chives
6. spoon sour cream mixture evenly into centers of cooked potatoes
7. sprinkle tops with cheese
8. arrange on a baking sheet
9. when ready to serve , preheat broiler
10. place stuffed potatoes under broiler until cheese melts
11. arrange broiled appetizers on a platter or serving plate
12. garnish with parsley
demonstrations.review: I've made these a couple of times for holiday parties. This time I prepared them the day before so I only had to pop them under the broiler for a few minutes. Served them as a side to beef filet and salmon, and they were gone in no time. I didn't add the scooped out potato to the mix, but will try that next time. I also like another reviewer's twist of adding shrimp and crushed red pepper on top. Will have to try that too. Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corned beef and cabbage in guinness

the irish butcher at my market gave me a new (to me anyway) recipe for corned beef & cabbage; he told me to cook it in guinness draught. (guinness stout will make the dish bitter).  since everyone raved about it, i thought i'd share the recipe he gave me. 

note: some reviewers have mentioned that the broth/sauce is very salty. it is important to rinse your corned beef in cold water before cooking it to remove some of the excess salt from the corning process. (i usually soak mine in cold water for a bit depending on the brand - some are much saltier than others).  --- i have tried 5 times today to change the wording of the last ingredient on the list from "1-2lbs carrot, peeled and cut into 3-inch pieces" to "1 - 2 pounds of carrots, peeled and cut into 3-inch pieces". every time the change "goes through," it does not reflect the new wording. grrrrrrr!

1. rinse corned beef under cold water , and pat dry
2. in a dutch oven , or other large pot with a cover , brown corned beef well on all sides over high heat
3. pour guinness over the meat , and add enough water to just cover the brisket
4. add the onion , garlic , bay leaf , cinnamon , cloves , allspice and pepper to the pot
5. bring pot to a boil and skim off any foam
6. reduce heat to a simmer
7. cover pot and simmer for 3 hours
8. add carrots , then potatoes and then the cabbage wedges to the pot
9. cover pot , and continue cooking until meat and vegetables are tender
10. remove meat and vegetables to warm serving platter / dishes , leaving the cooking liquid / sauce in the pot
11. over high heat , bring the cooking liquid to a boil , and cook until the amount of liquid is reduced by half
12. slice the corned beef
13. serve with the vegetables and the sauce on the side
demonstrations.review: I had friends over and made this in the crockpot, adding the potatoes and carrots toward the end. It cooked about 8 hours. I had no room for the cabbage, so I transferred everything to a big stock pot the last half hour or so. I added the seasonings as stated, except that in place of allspice I used equal parts of cinnamon and nutmeg. I also used the seasoning packet that came with the beef. To cover the beef I used two mexican beers that I had on hand. Next time I'll use the Guiness. I served the horseradish sauce from Corned Beef and Cabbage Dinner for the Slow Cooker. It turned out great and I got compliments all around!

target.recipe_text:
opal s pumpkin pie

this recipe makes 2- 9" pies.  if you make one large pie instead you will have to add time to the baking to get it done.  this recipe was given to me by opal beebee, several years ago. this is a handed down family recipe. it was once prepared in the white house for one of the former presidents. opal's daughter had served in the national guard and had met a pastry chef who later worked at the white house and called opal to ask for the recipe for thanksgiving dinner at the white house. do not eliminate the heavy cream in the pie...the cream and the amount of spices listed is what makes this pie so special. it is good hot or cold. i never tasted hot pumpkin pie until i tasted this one.  

i found out this past christmas (2009) that this bakes well without a crust as well.

i had to make 3 pumpkin pies to take to my son's home.  i had enough mixture left over make another pie but not enough pie dough for a 4th pie.  so i spray oiled a round casserole dish, filled with mixture and baked.

1. combine first 8 ingredients in a large bowl , mixing well
2. combine the evaporated milk and the heavy cream in a small saucepan
3. heat the milks to the scalding point
4. add scalded milks to the other ingredients , mixing well
5. pour equally into the two unbaked pie shells
6. bake 350 degrees for about 1 hour
7. pie is done when a knife inserted into the middle comes out clean
8. top with desired topping
target.review: I made quite a few alterations to this recipe, only because I live in Italy and I had some trouble finding the proper ingredients.  I used two whole, small baking pumpkins and microwaved them to soften them enough to puree.  I also halved the amount of brown sugar (my family had used it without telling me, so I didn't have as much as I thought I did on hand) and as I couldn't find evaporated milk or heavy cream I used 1 part fresh cream, 1 part natural yogurt, and 1 part skim milk... it turned out great!
