I loved the spices and the flavor.  I baked it in a pan about the size of a spring-form, so it made one large pie.  Great recipe... I can't wait to try it back in the states with the proper ingredients!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butterscotch apple pecan cobbler

with fall just around the corner, here's a perfect apple dessert. this smells awesome as it bakes in your oven!

1. preheat the oven to 375
2. in a small bowl , combine butterscotch morsels , brown sugar , flour and cinnamon
3. set aside
4. place apples in a 13x9 inch baking pan-sprinkle morsel mixture over the apples
5. bake for 20 minutes
6. to make the topping , combine the flour and brown sugar
7. cut in butter with pastry blender or two knives till mixture is crumbly
8. stir in pecans and oats
9. sprinkle over apple mixture
10. bake 30-40 minutes or until apples are tender
11. serve warm with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream
demonstrations.review: Oh wow!  I made this last night for a family dinner and it was fantastic!  It's really rich, but well worth it.  My family is already asking when I'm going to make it again!  Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun style green beans with tabasco

a recipe i found on the floor of a department store while shopping. the mcllhenny company, they of celebrated tabasco fame, included for promotion a free recipe with the purchase of a men's necktie. i have been making this every thanksgiving for close to ten years now. can be made vegetarian with the use of vegie soysage or "facon."

1. steam the green beans until just done but still maintaining their bright green color
2. drain
3. keep warm
4. in the meantime , in a small pan over medium-high heat cook the salt pork or bacon until crisp
5. reserve the fat
6. reduce heat , add the minced celery stalks and cook about 2 minutes
7. adding the garlic and cooking another minute longer
8. stir in vinegar , dijon mustard , sugar and tabasco sauce
9. heat through
10. remove from heat
11. stir in celery leaves
12. toss with beans to coat
13. season with salt and pepper and adjust seasonings if necessary
demonstrations.review: I served this at Thanksgiving and it was devoured... even by the kids!  I kept the green beans a little crunchier to contrast with all the soft things I was serving and I really liked it that way.  Next time I will probably double this recipe, since it went so fast at Thanksgiving!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marie callender s lemon cream cheese pie by todd wilbur

recipe created by todd wilbur www.topsecretrecipes.com.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. make the crust by combining the graham cracker crumbs with melted butter and sugar in a small bowl
3. press the crust mixture into an 8-inch pie pan
4. prepare the cream cheese filling by mixing cream cheese with 1 / 4 cup sugar , vanilla and an egg using an electric mixer
5. mix well until smooth
6. pour cream cheese filling into graham cracker crust and bake for 30 to 35 minutes or until center is cooked
7. a knife stuck in the middle of the filling should come out mostly clean
8. as the pie cools , make the lemon filling by combining 1 / 2 cup sugar with cornstarch , salt and water in a small saucepan
9. set mixture over low heat and bring to a simmer , stirring often
10. whisk in egg yolks , then add lemon juice and butter
11. when mixture simmers again remove it immediately from the heat
12. pour the lemon filling over the cream cheese filling , and let the pie cool
13. when cool , chill pie in the refrigerator for several hours before serving
14. slice into 6 pieces to serve restaurant-size portions
demonstrations.review: I made this for Thanksgiving dinner, as an alternative to pumpkin pie, and everyone liked it best.  I added a bit too much lemon juice, so there was a slghtly bitter aftertaste, but my family still thinks it's the best lemon pie they've ever had.  I also made it for my church's pot-luck.  Unfortunately, I added to little lemon juice (after my first mistake) and I didn't cook the lemon mixture long enough so it didn't set properly.  However, it was still everyone's favorite dessert at the party, so it is definitely a new stand-by for me.  Any recipe that can still be a hit even when I screw it up deserves  10 stars!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple butter cookies

so simple to make and so yummy.  the dough will quite happily sit in the fridge for a week, so you can bake off as much as you want when you want.

1. put butter and sugar together in a bowl and beat until light and fluffy
2. add flour and using your hands , gradually work it until the mixture forms a smooth dough
3. roll into a sausage shape about 30cm long
4. pat the sides to form either a square or a triangular log
5. sprinkle a thick layer of demerara sugar on a piece of baking parchment
6. press each side of the dough into the sugar to coat it
7. wrap in cling film and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes until firm
8. when ready to bake , preheat oven to gas 3
9. remove dough from cling film and cut into thick slices
10. place slightly apart on a non-stick baking tray
11. bake for 20 minutes , until they are just starting to brown
demonstrations.review: I made these this afternoo as a snack for the girls while we decorated the Christmas tree and everyone loves them!  The recipe was sooo easy and they turned out great.  I used salted butter and I really like the tang it gives the cookies.  Thanks for a great recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown gravy mix

posted in response to a request.

1. combine all ingredients and store in an airtight container
2. to make gravy , measure 3 tablespoons mix into a saucepan
3. add 1 1 / 2 cups water
4. bring to a boil and simmer 1 minute
demonstrations.review: Really easy to make and handy, since you only have to mix it once and then you have lots of the mix left in the jar.  I had a little trouble getting the exact amount of water and gravy mix... other than that, it's great!

target.recipe_text:
cheese enchilada chowder

from bhg. a slow-cooker chowder.

1. add the black beans , tomatoes , frozen corn , onion , bell pepper , and jalapeno pepper to a 4 quart slow-cooker
2. stir to combine
3. in a mixing bowl , add the enchilada sauce and cream soup
4. whisk together
5. gradually whisk in the milk until mixture is smooth
6. pour over vegetables in slow-cooker
7. cover and cook on low heat for 6-8 hours
8. add cheese and stir until melted
9. ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls and top with sour cream , guacamole and broken tortilla chips if desired
target.review: Very easy and has great flavor.  Thanks for a great recipe!  I will definately make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caesar pasta salad

this recipe is from the june 2004 issue of gourmet magazine.  has a nice zing!  this will serve about 4-6 people as a main course or over 8 as a side or starter.

1. whisk together the lemon juice , mustard , anchovy paste , garlic and olive oil in a large bowl
2. add pasta , romaine , cheese and croutons
3. toss to combine
4. season with salt and pepper to taste
5. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: A nice change with the addition of the pasta.  I doubled the dressing and added more romaine.  I also added vinegar to the dressing for added flavor.  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy chili seasoning

nan

1. combine the first six ingredients
2. store in an airtight container in a cool dry place
3. yield: 4 batches
4. to prepare chili: lightly brown steak in oil in a dutch oven
5. add 3 teaspoons of the seasoning mix and toss to coat
6. add ground beef
7. cook until meat is no longer pink
8. add onion
9. cook until tender
10. add tomatoes and 2 more teaspoons of mix
11. stir in one can of chili beans
12. place the other can in a blender cover and process until smo oth
13. add to chili
14. cook on low for 30-40 minutes or until meat is tender
demonstrations.review: Great seasoning.  I spiced it up a bit more and added more cumin because I am a cumin addict.  Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey and rice casserole

this is a tasty, simple and convenient way to use leftover turkey and/or leftover rice, and a great casserole to take to a potluck.
note:  edited on 1/1/08 to reduce milk in ingredient list from 1 3/4 to 1 1/4 cups.  i actually just fill a soup can with milk, but the ingredient list requires a measurement, and i took a guess.

1. combine 1st 4 ingredients and 1 / 2 can of fried onons
2. combine mushroom soup with soy sauce , cajun seasoning and milk
3. stir til combined
4. mix into remaining ingredients in casserole dish
5. top with remaining onions and bake at 350 for 30 minutes or until bubbly
demonstrations.review: Comfort food!!!  We really enjoyed this casserole.  I did not have 2 cans of mushroom soup on hand so substituted one can for cheddar cheese soup.  I left half of the casserole turkey free being a vegetarian.  Thanks for a great recipe PanNan!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broiled parmesan tilapia  low carb

you'll love this fish recipe! i have also made this with other meaty fish fillets too, works well with basa fillets also!

1. set oven to broiler heat
2. grease a broiler pan , then line with foil and grease the foil slightly
3. in a small bowl mix together parmesan cheese , butter , mayo , lemon juice and garlic
4. add in all the remaining seasonings and salt if using
5. mix well and set aside
6. arrange the fillets in a single layer on the prepared pan
7. broil a few inches from the heat for about 2-3 minutes
8. turn the fish over and broil a couple minutes more
9. remove from oven and cover them with the parmesan mixture on the top side only
10. return to oven and broil for about 2 minutes more or until the topping is browned and the fish flakes easily
demonstrations.review: This was fabulous.  Our daughter is allergic to egg so I substituted sour cream for the mayo.  I also grilled it in foil instead of broiling.  The fish had a wonderful flavor and we all really enjoyed it.  I will make this again.  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken bombay   lighter

ww-friendly adaptation of the delicious recipe posted by *pamela* (recipe #123104).  changed ingredients to reflect lower fat variations like changing chicken pieces to boneless chicken breast and changing/reducing butter to olive oil as well as reducing amount of meat per serving in order to be ww friendly.  (5 ww points)

1. combine all ingredients , except chicken , in a small sauce pan
2. heat over medium heat until smooth and slightly warmed
3. roll each piece of chicken into the sauce and place in a greased , 9 x 13-inch baking pan
4. bake uncovered for 30 minutes at 375f
5. spread remaining sauce over chicken and bake for a few more minutes until chicken is done
6. to freeze: prepare sauce ingredients in a small zip-top bag
7. put chicken breasts in a larger zip-top freezer bag
8. put both bags together into another bag with cooking directions inside as well
9. label and freeze for up to 4 months
10. to serve: thaw overnight in refrigerator
11. drain chicken and proceed with step 2 above
demonstrations.review: This is a nice sauce. Easy to toss together because the ingredients are those you normally have on hand.  I used it on chicken and salmon.  It actually seemed like a glaze on the salmon.  Our 2 yr old even liked it.  If I were just making it for adults I might double the curry.  But it is great the way it is written.  Thanks for a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
a1 cowboy up tart  a1

a.1. original sauce recipe contest entry.  this a1 original sauce recipe contest entry uses a few leftovers revitalized with a1 original sauce on a spiced up pastry crust and topped with cowboy staples: steak, potatoes, corn, tomatoes. yum!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees and line baking sheet with parchment paper
2. roll out pastry to 9 x 11 rectangle
3. place on baking sheet and bake 20-25 minutes until golden
4. remove from oven and cool on wire rack
5. beat cream cheese , sour cream and 3 tablespoons of a1 original sauce together until smooth
6. using a spatula the cooled tart
7. place the steak and potatoes on a microwave dish and heat 30 -60 seconds to warm
8. sprinkle onto tart
9. now add the tomatoes , corn , and peppers
10. sprinkle with the cheddar cheese and drizzle with the reserve4d a1 original sauce
11. season to taste
target.review: Giddy Up that looks good!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
charge me up a1 steak   egg veggie breakfast wrap  a1

a.1. original sauce recipe contest entry.  this is one heck of a healthy breakfast sandwich that is low in carbs and packing tons of protein.  after eating this for breakfast you will be charged up for the rest of day, i guarantee.  enjoy!

1. combine 1 / 2 a
2. 1
3. sauce with olive oil , garlic and thyme leaves in a small mixing bowl
4. brush both sides of steak with sauce
5. heat up non-stick skillet to medium high heat
6. cook steak for 3-4 minutes on each side until desired doneness
7. remove and rest for 5 minutes
8. slice thin slices against the grain
9. meanwhile , whisk eggs in small mixing bowl
10. add salt and pepper flakes , mix well
11. meanwhile heat up non-stick skillet to medium heat , add butter
12. scramble eggs to a minute or so until desired doneness
13. combine remaining a
14. 1
15. sauce and mayonnaise in a small mixing bowl
16. place wraps on flat surface
17. on the bottom 1 / 3 of wraps spread a
18. 1
19. and mayonnaise mixture followed by spinach leaves , scrambled eggs , tomatoes , goat cheese and steak slices
20. fold in corners of wrap and roll like a burrito
21. wrap in plastic wrap or parchment paper until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: A wrap never looked so good!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon granola chicken salad  rsc

ready, set, cook! hidden valley contest entry.  this recipe is so tasty using slightly sweet granola on chicken breast.  it locks in the juices keeping the chicken breast nice and moist.  the combination of the other ingredients makes this a dish, your family, will ask you to make over and over again.

1. 1
2. in large skillet heat about 1 / 4 cup olive oil on medium heat
3. 2
4. slice chicken breasts in half creating 6 pieces , season with salt and pepper
5. 3
6. in small bowl combine egg and dressing , beat
7. 4
8. in additional small bowl combine ground granola and bread crumbs , season with salt and pepper
9. 5
10. dip each chicken breast into egg / ranch then coat in granola / bread crumbs , covering completely
11. 6
12. add to skillet and brown on each side until done
13. 7
14. squeeze lemon juice over top of chicken
15. 8
16. serve on top of fresh spinach , dressing and favorite salad ingredients
demonstrations.review: Looks Great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
california bacon ranch pizza  rsc

ready, set, cook! hidden valley contest entry.  a delectable pizza with an avocado ranch white sauce, chicken and bright notes of tomato and citrus!  i came up with this recipe to use up some avocado for a friend who wanted something a little different!

1. pre-heat oven to 350f
2. in a heavy skillet , heat olive oil
3. while oil is heating , season chicken with salt , pepper , and lemon zest
4. stir well to combine
5. brown chicken in skillet until no longer pink , 6-7 minutes on medium high
6. remove chicken with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels
7. set aside and keep warm
8. mix together avocado , lemon juice , ranch dip mix , mayonnaise , greek yogurt and cream cheese
9. set aside to flavor for 5-10 minutes
10. while avocado ranch sauce is sitting , spread pizza dough out onto a large pizza pan bake pizza crust 6-7 minutes or until just starting to brown on top
11. remove from oven
12. spread avocado ranch sauce generously onto warm crust
13. sprinkle cooked chicken , diced red onion , bacon pieces and diced tomatoes on top of ranch sauce
14. top with both cheeses
15. return pizza to oven
16. bake an additional 10-15 minutes or until cheese is melted and pizza is hot through
demonstrations.review: Bacon and Ranch - Yummy!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
a 1  cherry cobbler tart   a1

a.1. original sauce recipe contest entry.  tangy a1 ganache takes a creamy cherry cobblet tart to new heights!

1. in a saucepan , cook cherries over medium heat for 6-7 minutes until reduced and cherries have popped
2. set aside
3. cut 1 sheet puff pastry in 9 equal squares
4. spray a 12 muffin tin with nonstick cooking spray
5. press each square of puff pastry in 1 muffin compartment
6. press dough up sides
7. combine mascarpone cheese , 1 tablespoon brown sugar and vanilla in bowl
8. spoon mixture evenly between 9 puff pastry cups
9. top mascarpone cheese mixture with cherries
10. in a small bowl , combine flour , 2 tablespoons brown sugar and butter until combined and crumbly
11. top cherries with mixture evenly among cups
12. bake at 400 degrees for 15 minutes
13. remove from oven and let cool until room temperature
14. place chocolate in a bowl
15. heat heavy cream and a1 sauce in a saucepan over medium heat until hot and almost boiling
16. pour over chocolate
17. whisk until melted and combined
18. to serve: drizzle ganache on plate
19. top with tartlet and top with more ganache
20. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Wow I never would have put those together but it sounds fun and amazing!!!  Nice job!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheery cherry cream puffs with a 1  ganache drizzle  a1

a.1. original sauce recipe contest entry  quick and easy, this dessert tastes as wonderful as it looks! it features flaky pastry, a creamy cherry filling and a rich chocolate ganache flavored with a.1. original sauce! it will wow all who taste it!

1. bake puff pastry shells at 425 degrees f
2. for 18 minutes according to package directions
3. use a fork to remove the top halves and soft pastry underneath
4. allow to cool
5. bring 1 cup heavy cream to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium heat
6. remove from heat
7. stir in a
8. 1
9. origianal sauce and chocolate chips
10. stir until well blended and smooth
11. set aside
12. to make the filling , place remaining 1 / 2 cup heavy cream in a medium bowl
13. beat on high speed
14. once cream begins to thicken , add cherry juice , vanilla and sugar
15. continue to whip until cream is thick and stiff
16. fold in maraschino cherries
17. to assemble , spoon cream mixture onto pastry shell bottoms
18. place pastry tops over cream
19. drizzle with the a
20. 1
21. ganache
22. sprinkle with chopped walnuts
23. serve immediately and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Yum!!

target.recipe_text:
lemon cream cheese pie with berries

special dessert for company or special occasion. make it at least once through berry season. easy no-bake recipe.

1. beat the cream cheese until fluffy slowly pour the condensed milk into the cream cheese as you continue beating
2. beat until smooth whisk in lemon juice , lemon zest and vanilla
3. pour into prebaked 8 inch crust puree 1 / 3 cup of the berries drizzle on top of prepared pie run a knife throughout the pie to make a swirl effect
4. refrigerate for 3-4 hours
5. to serve , top with remaining berries
target.review: So creamy and yummy.  MMMMMM - thanks Derf!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple ranch house meatloaf

easy and tasty served either hot or cold, wonderful sliced cold for a picnic or sandwiches. we have enjoyed this basic meatloaf for many years.try a change, instead of the usual topping, try your favourite salsa brushed on top, a nice chipotle medium or hot salsa is wonderful on it.

1. mix all the meat loaf ingredients together
2. pack into a 5 x 9 loaf pan
3. bake at 325f degrees for 1 1 / 4 hours
4. remove from oven , turn out of pan and place on an ovenproof serving dish
5. topping: mix the topping ingredients
6. brush over the meat loaf and return to the oven for 30 minutes or longer
7. defrost and reheat or use sliced cold
8. alternate topping
9. 4 tablespoons chilli sauce
10. 3 tablespoons splenda
11. 4 tablespoons spreadable soft cream cheese - light
12. 1 tablespoon hot horseradish
13. 1 teaspoon dry mustard
14. combine all and brush on top of meatloaf instead of above topping
demonstrations.review: This is a very simple, yet delicious meatloaf.  Moist and flavorful.  As Derf indicated you can change around the topping for different tastes.  Will make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic bread pudding

perfection, from sunset magazine.

1. trim crusts off bread and cut loaf cross-wise into 3 / 4 inch thick slices
2. arrange 8 to 10 slices diagonally in a buttered 8-inch square pan you may have to overlap them on each other and push and tug a bit to get them to fit without overlapping the edges of the pan
3. whisk the eggs , half-and-half , sugar , nutmeg and vanilla together until well blended , then gently pour over the bread and soak for about 30 to 40 minutes until its al soaked up you may need to coax it a bit by spooning some of the liquid over the top
4. bake in 350 oven for about 30 minutes , or until custard is cooked in the center
5. if desired , run the pan under the broiler about 3 to 4 inches from the heat for a golden and crusty top
demonstrations.review: Gee - this didn't turn out for me it was so-so at best.  It was dry (I even added another egg and an extra cup of half and half) and lacked flavor.  I really wanted this to work out.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best cornbread ever

this is the best cornbread i've ever had. the cottage cheese melts into the batter and tastes great. try the optional add-ins. this is a great complement to chili.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. combine all ingredients and mix well -- it will be thicker than you expect
3. pour into buttered 9" x 13" casserole dish
4. bake in oven for 35-40 minutes until golden brown
5. this cornbread is very moist and dense
6. for a little variation , add one or more of the following: a can of chopped green chiles , 1 cup of cheddar cheese , 1 cup of pepperjack cheese , 1 / 2 cup chopped fresh cilantro
7. let it cool for 10 minutes for best flavor
demonstrations.review: OK - This IS the best cornbread ever!  Dense and moist, mmmmm. I substituted sour cream for the cottage cheese and it worked great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pete s scratch pancakes

it was the fall of 1987 when pete nyhus walked into our office, just to visit. we started talking about breakfast, and he reached into a wastepaper basket and pulled out a scrap of teletype paper. he wrote out this recipe, and my family has never used pre-mix since.

1. mix the dry items first
2. combine the eggs and melted butter to the milk and slowly stir into the flour mixture
3. let sit at least 10 minutes while heating the pan
4. these will be high , but light and fluffy --
demonstrations.review: Made these for breakfast last weekend and added some blueberries.  Family loved it.  Fluffy, light and easy to make.  Will make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon jello cake

don't know where this recipe came from but my great-grandmother used to make it!

1. mix cake ingredients together for 4 minutes
2. bake in metal non stick 9x13 inch pan @350 for 40 minutes
3. or , if using a glass baking dish bake @325 for 45 minutes
4. poke holes all over the cake while hot
5. mix together icing: powdered sugar and lemons
6. pour this over the cake immediately , while it is still hot from the oven
7. serve warm or cold
demonstrations.review: Yum Yum.  Very moist and flavorful.  I substituted fresh squeezed lemon juice for the water in the recipe just cuz I love lemons that much!  Turned out fantastic.

target.recipe_text:
fresh blueberry cobbler

easy and too good for words.

1. add flour , 1 / 2 cup sugar , salt , and baking powder to a mixing bowl
2. stir to combine
3. add in milk and butter
4. stir to combine
5. spread batter into a greased 8-inch square baking pan
6. sprinkle blueberries evenly over batter
7. sprinkle with 1 / 3 cup sugar and drizzle with vanilla
8. bake at 350 for 40-45 minutes or until a pick comes out clean
9. can serve plain or with ice cream on top
target.review: This is yummy! The only thing I did different was to mix the vanilla with the sugar before sprinkling it on the berries. I didn't think I'd have much luck drizzling a tsp of vanilla. =) updated- I just had to give this 5 stars, it doesn't deserve anything less!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
poached chicken

i do about 12 breasts at a time and freeze for sandwiches or wraps or i use it for stirfry's.

1. place chicken in a large saucepan
2. add water and remaining ingredients , and bring to a boil
3. reduce heat , and simmer , uncovered , for 5 minutes or until chicken is done
4. remove from heat , let stand , uncovered , 20 minutes
5. place chicken and poaching liquid in a large bowl
6. cover and chill , or , put just the chicken in freezer bags and freeze for another time
demonstrations.review: This is a wonderful way to cook lean, moist and wonderful tasting chicken.  I will make this again and again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry rhubarb dessert bars

i use this one every year during rhubarb season. a pennsylvania state fair butter cookie contest winner, originally found on the land o' lakes website. times do not include cooling time.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease the bottom of a 13x9 inch baking pan
3. combine rhubarb , strawberries , and lemon juice in a 2-qt saucepan
4. cover and cook over medium heat , stirring occasionally , 8 to 12 minutes or until fruit is tender
5. combine granulated sugar and cornstarch in a small bowl , then mix into the fruit mixture
6. keep cooking , stirring constantly , until mixture comes to a boil
7. continue boiling until thickened
8. remove from heat and set aside
9. combine all crust ingredients in a large mixing bowl
10. beat on low speed , scraping bowl often , for 1 to 2 minutes or until mixture is crumbly
11. set aside 1 1 / 2 cups of crumb mixture
12. press remaining crumb mixture onto bottom of prepared pan
13. spread fruit filling over crust , and sprinkle evenly with reserved crumb mixture
14. bake at 350 degrees f for 30 to 35 minutes , or until crust is golden brown
15. cool completely
16. mix drizzle ingredients in a small bowl
17. drizzle over cooled bars
18. cut into bars
demonstrations.review: SO YUMMY!  I wanted something fresh and fruity to take to work and this was it!  I printed the recipe to take along just in case and I had to make copies!  Thank you, Muffin Goddess!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
edna s apple crumble  aka  apple crisp

a simple and easy to make but oh so yummy recipe. known as apple crumble in the uk and apple crisp in the us

1. put apples in an 8 or 9 inch square baking dish
2. combine the rest of the ingredients in a separate bowl and mix
3. spread crumble mixture over apples and bake for 35 minutes in a 375f degree oven
4. for an added treat top off with a little english custard
demonstrations.review: yummy!  I use golden delicious apples as that is what I had on hand and it was so good!  Plenty of topping, (my favorite part!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
1 pan fudge cake

this is my favorite chocolate cake. no fuss, no mess and very moist. back in the early days when it was paycheck to paycheck, this simple dessert made it into his lunchbox many a day because it was cheap and simple. no eggs, no milk.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in an ungreased 9 x 13 pan- yes ungreased , sift all dry ingredients
3. add the liquids and stir just until blended
4. bake for 25 minutes
5. frost with your favorite frosting , cake is extremely moist so care must be taken that you don't tear up the top of the cake
demonstrations.review: This turned out really well, even though I forgot to add the vanilla, and midway through dumping eveything in the pan I discovered I didn't have baking soda.  I substituted 1T baking powder and replaced the vinegar with applesauce to lower the acid.  Topped it with Easy Chocolate Fudge Frosting and it turned out great!!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s easy peanut brittle

my mom got this recipe years ago from someone she worked with...she made it at christmas and holidays quite a bit. i have never made it, but i know it tastes yummy!! if you like alot of peanuts to candy ratio, use the whole 1 1/2 cups peanuts (or more if you like)...it's purely personal preference!

1. stir syrup , water and sugar together in large , heavy pan to hard ball stage
2. stir in butter and peanuts until golden brown
3. stir in vanilla and soda
4. pour into 2 buttered pizza pans , just shaking pan to even out mixture
5. cool and break into pieces
demonstrations.review: This was wonderful.  As my mom says, "This is Peanut Brittle, not Peanut Brutal."  It has a nice crunch without being too hard.  It's not super sticky either.  Thank you, Troop Angel!

target.recipe_text:
engagement chicken

a chicken with ultracrisp skin and a subtle lemon flavor. rumor has it that if you cook this for your boyfriend he will propose.. here's to hoping. :o)

1. place rack in upper third of oven and preheat to 400 degrees
2. wash chicken inside and out with cold water , remove the giblets , then let the chicken drain , cavity down , in a colander until it reaches room temperature pat dry with paper towels
3. pour lemon juice all over the chicken season with salt and pepper
4. prick the whole lemons three times with a fork and place deep inside the cavity
5. place the chicken breast-side down on a rack in a roasting pan , lower heat to 350 and bake uncovered for 15 minutes
6. remove from oven and turn it breast-side up
7. return it to oven for 35 minutes more
8. test for doneness - a meat thermometer inserted in the thigh should read 180 , or juices should run clear when chicken is pricked with a fork
9. continue baking if necessary
10. let chicken cool for a few minutes before carving
11. serve with juices
12. serve with boiled new potatoes tossed with olive oil and fresh chopped parsley and / or steamed asparagus with butter
13. enjoy
target.review:
I made a very similar recipe...also added garlic and rosemary!  It was a great chicken!  And so simple!  I sliced the lemon in half before putting it in the cavity!

Seems like it was so time consuming...and skilled!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy pretzels

my daughter got this recipe from her friends mom . the small pretzels work the best. and for some reason , the oil definitely makes a difference! we've made them with crisco, and we've made them with other brands, and they don't taste the same!
*** seems to be too hot for a few people , please adjust the cayenne pepper if you don't like hot***

1. put pretzels in a roaster pan
2. mix together the crisco oil , dressing mix , salt and cayenne pepper
3. pour over pretzels
4. toss thoroughly !
5. bake at 200 for 1 1 / 2- 2 hours
6. stir about every 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: These are awesome!  I've made them 3 times!  It was too much cayenne for us so we started to cut it in half for our second batch!  My DH thinks every bar should serve these to up their beverage sales!  My DH and BIL would give more than 5 stars if they could!  Very easy and very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brady bunch pork chops

i think this recipe is an absolute gem. really, in all my years of cooking, i don't think i have ever made chops as delectable as these! crispy-crunchy on the outside, meltingly tender and moist on the inside. the key, i think, is the salty milk marinade/brine, and making sure not to overcook them. thanks to gourmet magazine for this one.

1. in a large shallow dish , like a 9x13 pan , stir together milk and first amount of salt
2. add pork chops and marinate , covered and in fridge , for at least one hour
3. turn chops once , halfway through marinating / brining time
4. when ready to cook chops , preheat oven to 200f and have ready an ovenproof platter
5. in a shallow dish , combine freshly made bread crumbs with garlic powder , rosemary , thyme and remaining amount of salt
6. remove chops from milk and let excess milk drip off , then dredge chops in bread crumbs , lightly patting crumbs onto both sides of chops so they adhere
7. place breaded pork chops on a tray , keeping chops in one layer
8. in a large 12-inch skillet over high heat , place butter and oil
9. saute chops , 2 1 / 2 to 3 minutes per side only
10. do not overcook , do not crowd chops in skillet , and turn only once
11. chops should be golden brown and just cooked through
12. place cooked chops on platter and keep warm in preheated oven
13. cook remaining chops
14. add more oil and butter to pan if necessary
15. i recommend serving with applesauce
demonstrations.review: Nice easy recipe!  I was planning on having them for dinner and put them in the milk and salt at lunchtime.  Dinner was canceled, but after 6 hours in the marinade, I had to cook them!  I used pre-made bread crumbs.  My chops were thinner than 1/2 inch, but cooked them for the 2 1/2 minutes each side, adjusted the temp to medium after the first batch started to burn!  I sealed them each individually and my DH had 2 the next day!  He loved them!  I had one 3 days later and they were still very good!  I am going to freeze the last few!  I can't wait to try them right out of the pan!  Thanks for posting this great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate kiss peanut butter cookies

valentine cookies for the one you love!!! a kiss in each cookie. this makes a lot of them.

1. cream butter and peanut butter
2. gradually add sugar and brown sugar , at medium speed until fluffy
3. add eggs and vanilla , beat well
4. combine dry ingredients
5. add to creamed mixture , mixing well
6. shape dough into 1-inch balls
7. place on ungreased baking sheets
8. bake at 350 for 8 minutes
9. press a kiss into top of each cookie
10. bake 2 more minutes
11. cool on wire racks
demonstrations.review: My all time favorite cookies!  I often cheat and make them with the PB cookie mix!  But these are my favorites!   While the cookies are baking, be sure to unwrap a Kiss for each cookie!  You need to put them on the cookies right out of the oven!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soda cracker buttercrunch

a candy lover's dream! easy to make and delicious to eat!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease , or cover with parchment paper , a 15 x 30 inch cookie sheet
3. line pan with the crackers
4. combine butter and brown sugar in a medium-sized saucepan
5. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until mixture comes to a boil
6. continue cooking 3 more minutes , still stirring
7. pour mixture over crackers
8. place baking sheet on rack in upper third of oven
9. bake 12 to 15 minutes--if mixture starts to burn remove from oven immediately !
10. sprinkle right away with chocolate chips
11. let stand 2-3 minutes and then spread melted chocolate out more evenly
12. chill in refrigerator until set
13. when cooled thoroughly , break into ragged shapes and chunks
demonstrations.review: Thanks for the awesome recipe.  There are a few here, but there are some little differences.  Your directions were very clear and easy to follow.  I used 40 saltine crackers and also added nuts on top of the melted chocolate.  Thanks again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed the taste of this recipe.  But was surprised that after more than 6 hours in the crock pot, it wasn't very tender.  It was a little better the second day for leftovers.  We just expected it to be almost fall apart tender!  But because of actual flavor I gave this a 4 instead of a 3!  Thanks for the recipe!  EDIT:  We made this again with a different cut of meat!  I had to bump up the stars!  It was wonderful!  Falling apart tender!  That is what I was looking for!  We just bought another roast to make it again!  We used an actual "Pot roast" this time!  I think it was shoulder!  The first time I think it was a round roast!  What a difference the shoulder roast made!

target.recipe_text:
roti de pore a la boulangere

fancy name for pork loin roast with potatoes and onions.  this dish has been around forever and it's always a winner.  if you can catch a pork loin on sale, then is the time to buy and freeze for special company dinners.  this one is sure to wow them!

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. with garlic , crush one clove and mix with the salt
3. rub mixture over pork
4. place fat side up in a large roasting pan
5. roast 30 minutes
6. meanwhile , thinly slice potatoes and coarsely chop onion
7. crush other garlic clove
8. toss with potatoes , onion , butter , seasoned salt , and pepper
9. after pork has roasted 30 minutes , spoon potatoes around meat
10. roast one hour and 15 minutes longer , stirring potatoes around twice , until temperature on a meat thermometer reaches 150 degrees
11. let stand before carving and garnish with parsley
target.review: This is so good! The house smelled great while the pork loin was cooking. The garlic flavor was excellent and the the pork loin was nice and tender. The juices from the meat made a nice gravy for the potatoes, too. The only change I made was that I used a garlic pepper blend instead of seasoned salt. The recipe is simple with great results!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cilantro lime baked chicken

i don't really remember why i decided this would be good to try. the family loved it so i kept fixing it. i also do these on the grill/smoker sometimes. if using a grill set up for indirect cooking. you could also use lemon, but my dil seems to love the lime taste.

1. wash chicken and pat dry
2. place lime quarters in the cavity of the chicken
3. stuff the remainder of the cavity with cilantro
4. salt and pepper to taste
5. bake at 350f according to your favorite chart until juices run clear
6. serve with american southwest , mexican , or se asian side dishes
demonstrations.review: I made mine in the crockpot. I added a 1/2 cup of chicken broth to the crockpot and rubbed the outside of the chicken with butter and Adobo seasoning. I cooked it on high for about 4 hrs. It was delicious. I can't wait to try this on the grill!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flaky chicken wraps

i ran across this recipe a few years back from pillsbury and i have enjoyed it since then. i love to make this when i need a quick dinner idea. it's so quick and easy and the results are delicious! hope you enjoy them as much as we do.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. lightly grease a cookie sheet
3. in a small bowl , combine the oil and 1 tbs of the salad dressing mix and combine thoroughly
4. separate your dough , press and roll them out to form a 6-inch circle
5. spread a very light amount of the salad dressing / oil mix onto each biscuit
6. arrange 3 or 4 strips of chicken in the center of each biscuits
7. bring the ends of each biscuit over the chicken and overlap them and pinch them together to form a seal
8. repeat this step until all biscuits and chicken are used
9. brush each biscuit with melted butter and sprinkle some of the dry ranch dressing on top sparingly
10. bake for 18- 22 minutes or until light golden brown
11. meanwhile , in a small bowl combine the sour cream and mayonnaise and the remaining salad dressing together and mix well
12. serve this dipping sauce with your chicken wraps
13. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: My boys like Hot Pockets, so I saved this recipe. Wow! These are much better than Hot Pockets. I added a little grated Mexican Blend cheese in with the chicken when filling the dough. This recipe is fast easy and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with honey

this dish is a native of africa. the chicken and honey mix to make a wonderful dish.
hope you enjoy!

1. in pan , heat butter and oil
2. brown chicken in this mixture
3. season with salt & pepper if desired , remove
4. in remaining fat , cook onion and garlic until clear
5. add ground or crushed almonds , basil , pepper , and honey and cook , stirring , until mixture is well blended
6. combine broth and cornstarch and add to pan
7. cook , stirring , over high heat until sauce thickens
8. remove from heat , stir in lemon juice
9. place chicken in a casserole dish , spooning sauce over
10. bake , covered , at 350 degrees for 1 hour , or until chicken is tender
demonstrations.review: Great recipe Leslie! I love the flavor of the lemon, honey and almonds together. I could almost eat the sauce with a spoon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushrooms in spanish sherry

i made up this recipe when i was over at mom's house one evening preparing dinner. she didn't have any white wine so i raided the liquor cabinet and found an old, unopened bottle of spanish cream sherry (jerez). the sweetness of the sherry was a nice balance with the meatiness of the mushrooms.

1. heat a skillet to medium-high and add the olive oil and butter being careful not to burn
2. add the mushrooms and saut for about 5 minutes
3. gently stir to distribute the olive oil / butter evenly over the mushrooms
4. add minced garlic and cook another minute
5. next add the cream sherry and cook down mushrooms until softened but not slimy
6. about 2-3 minutes
7. season mushrooms with salt and pepper
8. garnish with fresh parsley leaves
9. serve as an appetizer , a side dish or over pasta
demonstrations.review: DEElicious... I used baby bellas and they were yummy. These mushrooms would be awesome on top of big juicy steak. We will be having these often because we love mushrooms and these are great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini stuffed chicken breast

the skin of this chicken makes a natural pocket to hold the stuffing mixture in. this is a great recipe for a dinner party, quite easy to make, and very delicious.

1. set oven to 375 degrees f
2. butter a 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. in a skillet , melt butter
4. saute onion , parsley and basil until onion is tender
5. add garlic zucchini and cook 2 minutes longer
6. remove from the heat
7. stir in bread crumbs , egg , cheese salt and pepper
8. carefully loosen the skin if chicken on one side to form a pocket
9. stuff each chicken breast with the zucchini mixture then place in a greased dish
10. bake for 35-45 minutes or until chicken is cooked through
demonstrations.review:
I was looking for recipes to make with stuff I had on hand and came across this one. It is great. We especially like the stuffing. Everyone commented on how good it was. I only had boneless breasts, so I put the stuffing on the underside and folded them in half. I put the extra stuffing in the dish around the breasts.
Very nice recipe Kittencal.

target.recipe_text:
cajun rubbed pork chops

really moist and tasty chops! just add garlic mashed potatoes and corn on the cob for a perfect meal.

1. combine spices , mix well
2. rub mixture thoroughly onto both sides of each chop
3. pan fry in oil , cooking both sides , until done
target.review: This was so delicious, simple and quick.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli with horseradish sauce

from southern living, a nice sauce to jazz up some broccoli. time includes chilling time.

1. combine all ingredients except broccoli
2. stir well
3. chill 3 to 4 hours
4. separate broccoli into spears
5. cook , covered , in a small amount of boiling water 8 to 10 minutes or until crisp-tender
6. arrange in a dish
7. top with sauce
demonstrations.review: WOW!!!!!  We made this for dinner the other night and everyone loved this!!!  Thanks for such a WONDERFUL recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing chicken marinade

this recipe came from allrecipes (ruth crickmer). my whole family loved it even though it cooked too fast. the original recipe said 'high heat' on the grill, which my husband did. it ended up cooking 8 minutes total, charred but not burnt tasting, and very juicy and flavorful. we'll turn down the heat next time for texture, but this is a keeper in our home!

1. in a large , non-reactive container , whisk together ingredients beginning with cider vinegar through salt
2. then whisk in olive oil and pepper
3. place chicken in the mixture
4. cover and marinate chicken in the fridge 8 hours or overnight
5. remove chicken from marinade just before you turn on your grill or broiler to let come up a few degrees
6. discard marinade
7. lightly oil your grill or broiler pan
8. grill or broil about 10 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: Amazing!!  The chicken was so moist and tender.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: YUMMY!!!!  My fiance made this for dinner after a long day at work and let me tell you it really hit the spot.  We did not have any cheddar cheese so we used an italian blend and we really loved it like this.  We had a hard time imagining how cheddar cheese would be any better.  Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted beets with honey balsamic glaze

i made this for dinner tonight & well...i should have made a lot more.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. trim & scrub beets leaving root & 1" stem intact
3. place on a sheet of foil , drizzle with 1 / 2 tb olive oil & wrap loosely but tightly
4. place on a baking sheet
5. bake for 1 hour & let cool enough to handle
6. remove stems & roots , peel & slice beets
7. place in bowl
8. combine glaze ingredients in a small saucepan
9. bring to a boil for 1 minute
10. pour over beets
demonstrations.review: Wow!!!  These were so good.  I truly feel that beets are one of the most under utilized and appreciated vegetables out there.  This is such an easy and tasty way to serve them.  However, I did cut the cooking time way down by peeling and cutting beets into half moon slices and roasted them like this.  Much quicker cook time.  The glaze is SOOOO yummy.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sea islands grouper

a tasty way to fancy up grouper that's super easy!

1. stir together bourbon , oil , salt , pepper , lime juice and honey until emulsified
2. pour into shallow dish
3. lay grouper filets in bourbon mixture
4. turn to coat and refrigerate for 1-4 hours
5. pour crushed pecans into another shallow dish
6. pour enough olive oil into deep frying pan to cover bottom and preheat on medium-low
7. dip filets into pecans , pressing firmly to coat evenly
8. turn over and coat other side
9. fry in pan until pecans turn golden brown
10. gently turn over and cook other side
11. approximately 10 minutes per side
12. can also use with other firm-fleshed fish or chicken
demonstrations.review:
The flavor of this dish was absolutely wonderful and it got rave reviews from my family.  Also-I reduced the marinade in the same pan that I cooked the fish in and then poured it over the fish once done...this was delicious.
The only reason I did not give it 5 stars was because the pecans didn't stick to the fish very well which made it somewhat difficult to cook in the pan.  Maybe I should have crushed the pecans more, but I did do it in a food processor.  Thanks for a GREAT recipe...loved the flavors

target.recipe_text:
dana s homemade kahlua

this is a recipe i came up with since i enjoy white russians soo much, and also i like kahlua in my coffee too. let me know what you think if it is too strong, weak or is missing something..thanks!!

1. boil water , coffee , sugar
2. simmer for 3 hours
3. let cool and add vanilla and vodka
4. bottle and cap tightly
target.review: I used the instant espresso powder as well.  Turned out fabulous!  It's 5:00 somewhere....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fruit salad with pudding

i get compliments on this fruit salad wherever i take it. it is super easy to make and a great dish to bring to a potluck or family party. kids love it too. everyone asks "what's in the sauce"? the secret ingredient is the vanilla pudding mix.

1. in a large bowl , combine peaches , pineapples , and vanilla pudding mix
2. this includes the juices from the cans
3. mix well until pudding is dissolved
4. stir in strawberries , banana , blueberries , grapes , and sugar if desired
5. chill
demonstrations.review: Made this as a quick dinner side.  It was delicious.  I had to use what I had, so no strawberries or blueberries (Next time I will).  I did add a can of mandarin oranges and omitted sugar.  You really don't need it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy crock pot dinner

nothing can be easier than this scrumptious dinner! it cooks unattended until the last 5 minutes of cooking. add a salad or green vegetable for a complete meal. this recipe will work for any size roast (beef or venison), just cook larger ones a little longer and smaller ones a little less.

1. place roast in crock pot
2. add potatoes and carrots
3. if using mushrooms , add them now
4. pour dry soup mix , black pepper and bouillon into 2-cup measuring cup
5. gradually add water , stirring to mix soup and water , adding enough water to make 1-1 / 2 cups
6. add sherry until mixture reaches 2-cup mark
7. pour liquid over and around veggies and meat
8. cover and turn crock pot to desired temperature: low or high or until roast is tender
9. during the last hour of cooking , i slide the veggies from atop the roast into the hot juices so they get additional flavor
10. to serve: remove roast and veggies from crock pot and place on serving platter to rest
11. to make gravy: put 1 / 4 cup water in small jar
12. add cornstarch and stir to dissolve
13. pour cold slurry into hot crock pot and stir until gravy is thickened , about 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: Good roast flavor. changed a few things....used shiraz instead of sherry and added 1 can Campbells beefy mushroom soup.  Great gravy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irondale cafe s fried green tomatoes

absolutely southern tradition.

1. slice tomatoes into 1 / 4-inch slices and set aside
2. combine cornmeal , flour , salt and pepper in a shallow dish
3. pour buttermilk into a bowl and add some of the tomatoes , being careful not to stack
4. remove slices from bowl and let excess buttermilk drain off
5. dip slices into cornmeal mixture
6. repeat until all slices are coated
7. fry in 1 / 2 inch of hot oil until brown , turning once to brown other side
8. place in a colander to drain
9. serve hot
10. serves 5 to 6
demonstrations.review: We made these with milk in lieu of buttermilk.  It worked fine.  Added a bit of garlic powder to the salt and pepper.  Be sure to salt these babies again once they come out of the frying pan.  These are a WONDERFUL addition to any southern supper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooked korean beef

this is based on a recipe i saw in chatelaine magazine.  it is hands-down the best slow cooker recipe ever!  it's great served over mashed potatoes, but my favourite way to serve it is in kaiser buns, with the yummy shredded beef piled high on top.  i put out toppings like arugula or lettuce, horseradish, mayonnaise, and sliced dill pickles, and let people fix their own bun the way they like it.  make sure to drizzle some of the wonderful sauce on each bun too, and also some of the onions too.  sooooo good!

1. stir all ingredients but meat together in the bowl of a slow cooker
2. remove string from roast
3. cut roast in half
4. place meat in the soy mixture and turn to coat
5. cover and cook until beef is fork-tender , 5-6 hours on high or 8-10 hours on low
6. remove beef from slow cooker and shred with a knife and fork , then return it to the sauce
7. pile onto mashed potatoes , or buns with toppings
8. dee-licious !
demonstrations.review: Followed recipe pretty much exactly, amazing flavor. <br/>I did sear the roast in veg oil before putting in the crockpot on High for 5 hours.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potsie s creamed chicken and biscuits casserole

this is a wonderful and simple to prepare comfort food using things you probably already have around. kids love it- but so do adults. at least, in this home. try it. it is one of my quick and easy favorites. this is my first submitted recipe... be kind.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease the bottom and sides of an 11x7 inch baking dish or 10 inch quiche dish
3. chop the onion
4. heat butter in a small nonstick skillet and saute until tender
5. combine cooked onion , soup , chicken , milk , pimiento , and mayo in a bowl and then turn into the prepared baking dish
6. bake for 15 minutes and remove from oven
7. sprinkle 1 cup of the cheese over the baked mixture
8. arrange biscuits decoratively in a single layer and sprinkle remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese over them
9. return casserole to oven and bake until biscuits are golden brown and sauce is bubbly , usually about 20 minutes longer
10. the last time i made this i used a 1 / 4 cup of fat free mayo and 1 / 4 cup of sour cream
11. i think it was delicious ! also -- i took the suggestion of adding a cup of cooked green peas
12. what a terrific idea ! i loved it ! i think i might add two cups next time
13. thanks to you all for making my humble recipe and leaving your suggestions
14. you greatly improved a recipe i was already proud of
15. thanks so much
demonstrations.review: POTSCRUBBER... This is unbelievably Delicious!  Yes, pure comfort food.  So nice to make a meal where everyone wants not just 2nds but 3rds!!!  The empty casserole dish bought JOY to my heart.  I only made few changes--added 1/2 c. sour cream, no pimentos or red peppers, subbed monterey jack cheese for cheddar and used onion powder ( for my picky eaters).  I used the Grands flaky biscuits and the eight in there were perfect for my 11x7 dish.  Thank you, this is going in the keeper folder for sure!

target.recipe_text:
rhubarb crunch

nan

1. mix flour , rolled oats , brown sugar , margarine and cinnamon until crumbly: press half of this mixture into a 9" greased pan
2. cover with chopped rhubarb
3. combine sugar , cornstarch , and water
4. cook until thick and clear in a small saucepan
5. remove from heat and add vanilla
6. pour over rhubarb
7. top with remaining crumbs
8. bake at 350f for 1 hour
target.review: I 1½ timed this recipe to make it big enough for a 9X13 pan. It is great, so yummy. I followed the other suggestions to increase the sugar in the sauce. I have been enjoying it without ice cream but know it would be so good with some.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon muffins

muffins are good anytime of the day.

1. mix flour , sugar , baking powder , salt , nutmeg and allspice
2. add egg , milk and butter
3. stir into dry ingredients until moistened
4. spoon into greased or paper-lined muffin cups
5. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes or until done
6. for topping combine sugar and cinnamon
7. brush top of warm muffin in butter and dip top of muffin into sugar / cinnamon mixture
demonstrations.review: I am pleased with this recipe. I doubled it and added a chopped apple. The only thing I didn't double was the nutmeg because I find it overpowering sometimes. I got 12 large and 12 mini muffins by doubling the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s air buns  rolls

this recipe for light, soft, buns did not come from my mom, but it is so good that i dedicate it to all moms who bake bread..or anyone who bakes bread for that matter! i will give the original recipe, but i admit that i now use the abm to knead the dough, and will give instructions for this variation at the end. preparation time is the length of time for the "dough" cycle on my bread machine. for anyone wishing to make 100% whole wheat buns,(a variation of this recipe, and equally delicious imho), i have submitted it as recipe #168802 with minor alterations.

more tweaking...i now like mom's 100% whole grain air buns, recipe #186744 even better for a healthier version.

1. mix the 1 / 2 cup warm water , yeast , and 1 tsp sugar , and allow to proof
2. melt the lard , and mix in sugar , salt , vinegar , and warm water
3. when body warm , add the proofed yeast , and beat in 1 1 / 2 cups flour
4. let rest for 15 minutes
5. knead in approximately 3 cups more flour
6. let dough rise till double
7. deflate dough , and form into buns , any size , or loaves
8. rise till double
9. bake buns at 350f for approximately 20 minutes
10. for abm , in my machine , on the "dough" cycle , i use 2 teaspoons of bread machine yeast , and i reduce the water to about 1 1 / 2 cups , the flour to 4 cups , adding a tad more water or flour as it kneads to get a smooth , soft ball of dough
11. i leave the other ingredients as posted
demonstrations.review: I have baked buns for many years and tried many recipes and I think this is the best recipe I have ever tried!! Made my first batch yesterday and have another one rising right now. I will definitely be making them again and will double the recipe for a bigger batch:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
short ribs with sauce

simple to make sauce really makes this good.

1. heat oven to 350
2. place ribs in 13x9 baking pan
3. add water
4. cover and bake for 2-1 / 2 hours
5. pour off water
6. in small saucepan , mix all other ingredients
7. bring to a boil
8. reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes
9. set in refrigerator until needed
10. when done , uncover ribs and spoon sauce over
11. bake , uncovered , for 1 / 2 hour , turning often to coat with sauce
demonstrations.review: We had this for supper and it was delicious. I took the ribs directly from the freezer to the oven so baked them longer-probably close to 3½ hours. I didn't have cider vinegar so used part regular and part rice. The sauce smelled  sharp but was very yummy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
award winning butter tarts

butter tarts are a canadian tradition. waaaay back in the 1970s, a national contest here in canada concluded that these butter tarts, originating from wilkie's bakery in orillia, ontario, were the best. i certainly think so and it's the only recipe i use. add a sprinkle of toasted walnuts when you add the raisins, if you wish, or use only walnuts if you don't like raisins.

1. prepare muffin pans by rolling out pie dough and cutting 4-inch circles
2. fit dough circles into muffin cups
3. set aside in fridge until ready to fill
4. in a small bowl , place raisins and cover with hot tap water
5. let stand on the counter for 30 minutes
6. in a large bowl , using a wooden spoon , mix together the soft butter , brown sugar , salt and corn syrup
7. stir well until sugar is dissolved and butter is creamed
8. add egg and vanilla and mix well
9. drain raisins
10. retrieve tart shells and divide raisins equally into all shells
11. then divide butter mixture into all tarts
12. bake at 400f for 15-20 minutes
13. filling will be lightly browned but still bubbling
14. canadians fall into two camps about butter tarts and are quite loyal to their favourite type: runny or firm
15. i like runny-- the type that dribbles when you bite into one
16. if you like firm , bake them for the full 20 minutes , even adding another minute or two if you wish
17. let cooked butter tarts cool in pans for 10 minutes after removing from oven
18. then remove and place on racks until completely cool
demonstrations.review: I have made this recipe several times to rave reviews every time. Love it!!  I always double the recipe and put in 24 purchased 3" shells.( Fit perfectly on a large cookie sheet) I have just used raisins but need to try with the walnuts as I am sure that would be yummy, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rhubarb cake

this is a great use for rhubarb straight from the garden. the first time i had this, i thought it was apple, not rhubarb.

1. cream 1 / 2 c butter and white sugar
2. add the buttermilk , vanilla and beaten egg
3. mix well
4. mix the flour , baking powder , and salt
5. add the rhubarb to the flour and stir
6. fold the flour mixture into the egg mixture
7. put in a greased 8 x 8 pan
8. blend the brown sugar , cinnamon and 1 / 4 c butter
9. sprinkle on top
10. bake for 45-60 minutes at 350
11. sides should pull away from pan
12. best served hot with whipped cream or vanilla ice cream
demonstrations.review: This cake was a big hit with the group I served it to this evening. I 1 and a half timed the recipe and baked it in a 9X13 pan. Worked well. I know you can't use 1 1/2 eggs--just used  two.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot potato chowder

another of my aunt's recipes. great for those cold nights.

1. combine potatoes , onion , broth , and cream of chicken soup in crock pot
2. cover and cook on low 8-10 hours or until potatoes are tender
3. add cream cheese and blend
4. top with bacon and chives before serving
target.review: This was very good and so easy to make!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin coffee cake

please don't pass this by because of all the ingredients. it's really very easy and quick. it's also very delicious

1. grease or spray the bottom of a 9x13 pan
2. mix together first 8 ingredients
3. pour 1 / 2 of the mixture in the 9x13 pan
4. prepare the pumpkin exactly like the pumpkin pie recipe on the can of pumpkin except you only use 1 / 2 cup of evaporated milk or just mix together the next 8 ingredients
5. pour all of the pumpkin mixture over the batter in the 9x13 pan
6. pour the remaining half of batter over the pumpkin make the topping , put over batter
7. bake in a 325 degree over for 50-60 minutes
8. let cool completely
9. enjoy
demonstrations.review: This was great - like eating coffe cake with a  slice of pumpkin pie in the middle.  Delicious!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate caramel candy

my mom decided to try these snickers-like candy, and our family fell in love with them!!! they are very rich, so cut into small pieces!!! also, each layer has to be refrigerated before adding the next, so plan ahead. the time is worth it though!!

1. combine the first three ingredients in a small saucepan
2. stir over low heat until melted and smooth
3. spread onto the bottom of a lightly greased 13-in
4. x9-in
5. x2-in
6. pan
7. refrigerate until set
8. for filling , melt butter in a heavy saucepan over medium-high heat
9. add sugar and milk
10. bring to a boil
11. boil and stir for 5 minutes
12. remove from the heat
13. stir in the marshmallow creme , peanut butter , and vanilla
14. add peanuts
15. spread over the first layer
16. refrigerate until set
17. combine the caramels and cream in a saucepan
18. stir over low heat until melted and smooth
19. spread over the filling
20. refrigerate until set
21. in another saucepan , combine chips and peanut butter
22. stir over low heat until melted and smooth
23. pour over caramel layer
24. refrigerate for at least 1 hour
25. cut into 1-in
26. squares
27. store in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: This fudge is awesome!  It is a bit time consuming to make due to the different layers, but well worth the effort.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s fettuccine alfredo

nan

1. set small frying pan in mid-high heat
2. add the butter and the cream to the frying pan and mix well
3. stir the sauce frequently and add the black pepper , salt and nutmeg , boil and immediately lower the heat and stir frequently until the sauce becomes heavier , it should take a few minutes of constant stirring
4. add the pasta to the boiling water along with some salt and cook to your liking
5. once the pasta is cooked , drain the pasta and add the sauce to it
6. mix well
7. add the grated cheese to the sauce and pasta , and mix until the cheese is absorbed by the sauce
demonstrations.review: This was easy to make and tasted great.  I liked that the sauce only coated the fettuccine.  Next time I will use less nutmeg (I think my pinches were a bit too generous).  But overall an outstanding recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
deep dish taco squares

nan

1. combine biscuit mix and water , stirring with a fork until blended
2. press mixture in bottom of a lightly greased 12x8x2" baking dish
3. bake at 375 degrees for 9 minutes
4. cook ground beef , green pepper , and onion in a large skillet until meat is browned , stirring to crumble meat
5. drain well
6. stir in tomato sauce
7. spoon over crust
8. combine sour cream , cheese , and mayonnaise in a medium bowl
9. spoon over meat mixture
10. sprinkle top evenly with paprika
11. bake at 375 degrees , uncovered , for 25 minutes or until casserole is lightly browned
12. cut into squares to serve
demonstrations.review: This was easy to make and tasted great!  The only change I made was to add a packet of taco seasoning mix whenever I stirred in the tomato sauce.  I plan on making this often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter cup cookies  tarts

i first saw these at a bake sale and was so impressed. you bake a ball of dough in a mini-muffin tin, bake, and press a reese's peanut butter cup into it after you take it out of oven. you are left with a picture-perfect tart, receiving "oohs and aahs" and "how did you do it?" you could even use the refrigerated sugar/peanut butter cookie dough too.

1. cream peanut butter , butter , sugar and brown sugar until fluffy
2. add egg , vanilla , flour , baking soda and salt' mix well
3. roll into 1-inch balls and place in miniature muffin tins or in mini cupcake wrappers)
4. bake 8-10 minutes at 375f
5. when tins are removed from oven , immediately press 1 peanut butter cup into the center of the cookie
6. allow to cool completely before removing cookies from the tin
demonstrations.review: These were so easy to make and so delicious.  What I loved the most (besides tasting so great) was how easy they were and how nicely they turned out.  I did manage to get about 4 dozen out of this recipe, and one bag of reese's wasn't quite enough (if anyone is wondering how much to buy.)  I will definitely be making these again and again.

target.recipe_text:
amish baked apples

very good version of baked apples.

1. place apples in greased 9 x 13 inch dish
2. mix remaining ingredients together in order given , in pan and bring to a boil
3. simmer , stirring until thick
4. pour syrup over apples and bake at 350 for 35 to 40 minutes or until tender
target.review: Brought me back a few years to when I was young and my grandma would make these for me.  I love the cinnamon.  Nothing better served with a big scoop of French Vanilla ice cream!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
john s cucumber sweet onion salad with lime pepper dressing

this is wonderful on a hot summer night. the flavours are amazing. the longer you marinade the salad the better it is...try to let it sit for 24 hours...you will not be disappointed.

1. run a fork down the cucumbers , all over , making slight indentations
2. cut the cucumber in half , lengthwise
3. scoop out all the seeds
4. cut the cucumber halves into 1 / 8" strips
5. peel the onion and cut lengthwise into quarters
6. slice the quarters crosswise into thin strips
7. in a large bowl , combine cucumber and onions with lime juice , salt and sugar
8. toss well
9. add hot pepper flakes , olive oil , vinegar and water , toss well
10. cover and refrigerate for 24 hours
demonstrations.review: I used pickling cucumbers for this for some added crunch, and what great taste to this salad!  Loved the dressing!  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s tomato and cucumber mix

i made this last night for dinner and thought i would share it with you... one of my own recipes that i created years ago... it's delish!

1. cut up tomatoes and cucumbers , and put in a med
2. sized bowl
3. in a separate bowl , add italian seasoning , oil , and vinegars
4. mix in the liquid with the vegetables
5. mix well
6. add salt and pepper
7. let marinate for a few hours in the refrigerator
8. mix every once in awhile while marinating
9. serve
demonstrations.review: Nothing tastes better than fresh tomatoes and crispy pickling cucumbers in this mix!  Make sure you marinate them for a few hours so the flavors really fuse together.  Awesome salad and something different for all to enjoy!  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun maple mahi mahi

this is so good!  i looked for a good recipe for maple glaze for chicken or fish or *whatever* that had the ingredients that i had on hand, but i just couldn't find the right one, so i created this extremely simple recipe myself and it was a success.  i guess sometimes, to find the right answers, you have to look within!

1. mix all ingredients together except for fish
2. spoon mixture over fish
3. place fish into shallow pan and sautee with onions if desired for about 3-5 minutes on the first side and 2-3 minutes on the second side
4. add more of the syrup mixture if you want
5. best served with rice
6. can also marinate fish for a few hours for maximum flavor
demonstrations.review: I used filet of sole and it turned out great.  So delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cookie jar peanut butter cookies

my favorite peanut butter cookies! crispy on the outside, chewy on the inside--just the way i like them. from sheila lukins usa cookbook, a great book!

1. heat oven to 350
2. sift together the flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt , set aside
3. cream the butter , shortening , and both sugars in a large bowl with an electric mixer at medium speed until light and fluffy
4. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each addition , then mix in the peanut butter
5. add the flour mixture by the cupful and beat at low speed to mix well
6. shape the dough into 1 inch balls and place on ungreased baking sheets about 2 inches apart
7. press each cookie twice in each direction with a lightly floured fork to make a crosshatch design
8. bake 10-12 minutes
9. do not overbake--they will still be a bit pale , but if you overbake , they won't be chewy on the inside
10. use a spatula to transfer to a rack to cool
demonstrations.review: These are awesome!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barnaise butter

a simple recipe for a spiced butter

1. boil wine , vinegar , onion , tarragon , garlic salt and pepper in small saucepan over medium-high heat until liquid evaporates , about 2 to 3 minutes
2. combine onion mixture with butter
3. place in bowl or shape into a small log and refrigerate a minimum of 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed it on some grilled steak, but I think there is too much tarragon and next time I will cut it down to about 1 tsp.

target.recipe_text:
simple chicken and dumplings

this is my sister debra's recipe and my kids always love it when she cooks it for them.  it is simple, easy, basic...and very good! you can add a vegetable to the creamy broth if you would like (frozen peas or broccoli), but we like it just the way it is. *i always double this recipe because they always come back for 2nd helpings.

1. melt shortening in dutch oven
2. blend in flour and salt
3. add milk and chicken broth
4. cook , stirring constantly until smooth and thickened
5. stir in onions and chicken
6. blend well
7. dumplings-mix dry ingredients with shortening and milk
8. stir only to moisten
9. drop by spoonfuls into boiling chicken mixtures
10. cover with lid
11. cook for 15 minutes over low heat
12. do not lift cover until cooking time is up !
target.review:
Very good recipe! I cannot review the dumplings, because I wanted to try out another recipe. I used a rotisserie chicken from the grocery stored, shredded into small pieces. Also added a can of corn and a sprinkle of pepper (personal preference). I also added a touch more milk.
Overall, very simple and delicious! Our family's favorite recipe now.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate coconut pots de creme

this is the world’s best dessert. i think i’ve been searching for it ever since i was born, and the desire to taste this kind of magnificence is what has led me to spend so many hours of my life in the kitchen.

more than anything else i love chocolate. and i really love soft, succulent, rich and melty chocolate with a high fat content and a deep, intense but sweet flavor. before i created this dessert i always had to choose between flavor and texture, it seems i could never get the exact right combination…until now.

it is even richer than a silk pie, more luscious than a mouse, far richer than pudding, and infinitely more delicious than just plain chocolate. if chocolate had a soul, this would be it. from: 
http://voraciouseats.com/2010/05/14/chocolate-pots-de-creme-the-best-dessert-in-the-world/

1. - break the chocolate up into pieces , put it into a food processor along with the agave nectar , vanilla , nutmeg and cinnamon dont process it yet ! just wait
2. - bring the coconut milk up to a simmer on the stove , and then pour it over the ingredients in the food processor
3. - blend everything together until smooth and creamy , pour into ramekins or coffee cups if that is all you have , and chill for about 5 hours until firm and creamy
4. i am the worlds foremost hater of all things coconut , but coconut milk is really growing on me
5. it is light and fragrant and not at all coconuty
6. believe me , in this dessert you cant even taste it !
demonstrations.review: These were very good! Perfect if you don't like things that are very rich. These are not super sweet, either. There is a very, very slight taste of coconut, so I'm not sure if I would serve them to someone who doesn't like coconut. Overall, these were delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bisquick danish

alright, you caught me.... i hate using store bought mixes but i had some bisquick in my pantry and needed a treat real fast one night when i ran out of flour so this is what i came up with!

1. stir butter , sugar and bisquick together until crumbly
2. gently add in coffee creamer and half and half or milk until dough just starts to form
3. drop about a heaping tablespoonsful dough onto a greased baking sheet
4. make an indent into each danish
5. fill indent with a small amount of preserves
6. bake at 425 degrees fahrenheit for 10-12 minutes , or until just starting to turn golden
7. while they are baking make the glaze by combining the powdered sugar , coffee creamer or milk , and corn syrup
8. drizzle glaze over warm danishes
demonstrations.review: These were very good, although they're not quite like the Danishes that I'm used to. I used milk instead of half-and-half, since that's what I had on hand. I also had fresh raspberries to use up, so I mashed them, added a little sugar and cornstarch and cooked them down. I used that instead of any preserves. I think I got about 14 Danishes in a batch. The glaze was also very good and didn't make the Danishes too sweet. Everyone loved them so much that I had to make another batch the next day. Will be making again (as soon as I get more Bisquick). Someone also suggested that they would be good with coconut added. I'm not sure about this, but may try it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cutout cookie decorator icing

this frosting works well on decorated cookies because it hardens when cool.

1. place sugar into mixing bowl
2. combine milk , corn syrup and vanilla , and blend
3. add liquid mixture to powdered sugar and mix thoroughly
4. add softened butter and blend until thoroughly incorporated
5. divide frosting into several cups , and add food coloring to each
6. if using liquid coloring , add a little more powdered sugar until it reaches good spreading consistency
7. spread onto cookie with knife , or place in zip-loc sandwith bags with the corner nipped off 1 / 16" to pipe onto cookies
8. decorate with sprinkles or colored sugars
9. once cookies are decorated , place on flat surface to allow frosting to dry
10. store cookies in covered container
11. sugar can be added or milk lessened to achieve the best consistency
demonstrations.review: This icing is very good. I really like the flavor and the fact that it hardened, allowing me to stack the finished cookies. I did have to add a bit more milk to get the right consistency. I used it to ice cow shaped cookies that I made with the "White Velvet Cutout Cookie" recipe. They were a big hit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white velvet cutout cookies

this is in response to a request. the recipe is from the taste of home magazine. it is a cream cheese cutout cookie.  frost with recipe #48001.

1. in a mixing bowl , cream butter and cream cheese until light and fluffy
2. add sugar , egg yolks and vanilla: mix well
3. gradually add flour
4. cover and chill 2 hours or until firm
5. preheat oven to 350f
6. roll out on a lightly floured surface to 1 / 4-inch thickness
7. cut into 3-inch shapes
8. place 1 inch apart on greased baking sheets
9. bake for 10-12 minutes or until set
10. cool for 5 minutes
11. remove to wire racks to continue cooling
12. frost after completely cool with white velvet buttercream cookie frosting
demonstrations.review: These cookies were very good! I cut them into cow shapes and iced with the "Cutout Cookie Decorator Icing" recipe for a 4-H club meeting. They were a big hit with all of the kids (adults, too)! I have been told that I should enter them into the county fair, because they would win Grand Champion. I have also already been asked for the recipe. The taste and texture were both excellent. Can't wait to make them again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meaty slow cooker chili

big flavor and lots of meat make this the perfect chili for those who want to hide the beans. a slow cooker makes for easy work and the time needed to blend flavors for amazing chili. i serve with shredded cheese and corn chips on top for a big meal.

1. brown ground beef and pork sausage with the onion and garlic
2. drain well
3. add all the ingredients to a slow cooker
4. stir and let simmer on low for 6-8hrs or on high for 3-4hrs
5. top with fixins - sourcream , cheese , green onion , corn chips , or rice
6. you choose
7. mix it up for a new flavor combo everytime
demonstrations.review: I am picky about my chili, and I liked this one! I had to made some substitutions (just didn't have some of the ingredients).
