V8 juice in place of tomato soup and water, grilling beans in place of pork and beans, kidney beans in place of black beans, etc. I didn't change anything with the spices. All in all, a good chili.

target.recipe_text:
jake s chickaladas  chicken enchiladas

you all know of my love of jake and his family.  one of jake's favorite foods was "chickaladas" which is a 4 year old's word for enchiladas.
god bless you jakeydoodle, i miss you.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a large bowl , mix chicken with 1-1 / 2 cans soup , 1 can chopped green chilies , and 8 oz sour cream
3. spread mixture down the center of each tortilla and sprinkle with cheese
4. roll each tortilla up and place in baking dish coated with nonstick cooking spray
5. combine sauce ingredients in a large bowl , 1 1 / 2 cans cream of chicken soup , remaining 8 oz sour cream , and 4 oz can chopped green chilies
6. pour sauce over enchiladas
7. top with remaining chicken mixture and cheese
8. bake in preheated 350f oven for about 30 to 40 minutes or until heated through and bubbly
target.review: WOW! made this today to have for the weekend as I am working. Well let me tell you they are GREAT. I was waiting for them to cool to cover & refridgerate & the smell made me take a tiny taste, and another, & and another. Had to cover them & get them in the fridge. Thanks for an easy & wonderful recipe. True comfort food.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oriental spareribs

ribs a little different. prep time includes marinading time.

1. combine crushed garlic with all other ingredients and stir well to get a thick marinade
2. rub all over the ribs , cover and leave to marinade for 20-30 minutes
3. preheat oven to 400f degrees
4. place the ribs in roasting dish and bake for 20 minutes
5. turn the ribs , add 1 / 2 cup boiling water to the pan and roast for a further 20 minutes
6. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Fantastic--the smell of garlic filled the house while these were cooking, yet was not overpowering to the taste. Very easy to make & so good. Great change from the usual red sauce!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork and vegetable lo mein  easy and delicious

my family loves this hearty main dish. i get requests for it often. it's very quick and easy to prepare, great for when you're in a hurry. you can buy a couple of the ingredients already prepared in the produce section of the grocery store, if you like.

1. already shredded--a real time saver
2. heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet or wok
3. saut pork , onion , garlic and pepper flakes until meat is no longer pink
4. remove this mixture from pan and keep warm
5. add remaining tbsp of oil to pan and saut cabbage , bok choy or celery , carrots and peppers until crisp tender
6. add spaghetti to cooked veggies in the pan
7. stir in soy sauce and add pork mixture back to the pan
8. cook for 5 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: OH WOW, this is fandamntastic......I found this very easy & the flavor was/is outstanding....I did add some sliced mushrooms being a 'shroom nut...other than that it is perfect....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicago chicken casserole

this is a terrific recipe to make when you have left over chicken. saves a step, cuts down on the prep time and uses up that chicken.

1. poach chicken in water , when cool enough to handle pull apart into bite-size pieces
2. in a large 9x12 casserole layer cooked chicken , drained corn and broccoli
3. mix soup with milk , cheese , mushrooms and pimentos
4. heat and pour over chicken
5. sprinkle top with ritz crackers which have been mixed with enough butter to moisten
6. if prepared ahead and refrigerate , do not top with the ritz until ready to bake
7. bake for 1 hour or till bubbly and hot
8. do not fill casserole to full
9. this cooks over easily
demonstrations.review: Hope you don't have to live in Chicago to eat this..I don't but this made a fantastic casserole..easy-peasy with the chicken I roasted the day before.. & it's full of flavor without being heavy...this has gone unreview till now--hope others give it a go--they won't be disappointed...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese chicken with black pepper sauce

for shae, who discovered this on a chinese buffet. i had found this on a buffet also. it is a great little dish, with a little bite of pepper that is quite addictive!

1. mix together sauce ingredients in a small bowl and set aside
2. cut chicken into a small dice , about 1 / 4-inch
3. heat 1-2 cups peanut or other cooking oil in your wok
4. place cornstarch in a small bowl and begin to dust chicken pieces , shaking off excess
5. fry in hot oil in small batches until crispy and golden , about 2-3 minutes
6. drain
7. remove oil from wok and discard
8. heat 1 tbsp oil in wok and stir-fry onion about 1 minute
9. add peas and carrots and cook another 30 seconds
10. add sauce mixture to wok along with chicken pieces and stir to coat everything evenly
11. serve at once with hot steamed rice
demonstrations.review: This is excellant, easy, fast, & sooooo good....Actually I have made it twice...the second time using broccolli which lends itself to this very well. Either way the dish is flavorful & perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish rosie s irish soda bread

this irish soda bread recipe was passed on to me by a dear friend of my mother's who was born and raised in ireland. it's the best irish soda bread i have ever had. it is much higher, lighter and softer than most other recipes i have seen. it has an excellent flavor and texture, as well.

1. combine dry ingredients together in a large bowl
2. in a small bowl beat eggs and stir in sour cream
3. add the egg and sour cream mixture to the dry ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon
4. batter will be very thick
5. add the raisins and caraway seeds and stir well with wooden spoon or knead in with your hands
6. place batter in a greased 9 inch springform pan
7. dust the top with enough flour so that you can pat the batter like a bread dough evenly in the pan without it sticking to your hands
8. with a knife make a shallow crisscross on the top
9. bake for 50 minutes in a preheated 350f oven
demonstrations.review:
adding my 5* to the rest...this is excellant, crusty, light & flavorful. The only adjustment I made was to 'plump' the raisins..covering with boiling water for 2 min. then draining before adding to the batter...I find this not only adds to the appearance but makes them softer.
Thanks for a great recipe...

target.recipe_text:
italian breaded tilapia

this is an easy recipe for a weeknight. low fat and kid approved!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. mix breadcrumbs , parmesan cheese , and garlic powder in a quart size ziploc bag
3. pour italian dressing in a different quart size ziploc bag
4. '
5. place tilapia , one piece at a time , into the bag with italian dressing and shake
6. then put in the bag with the breadcrumb mixture and shake
7. repeat with other fillets
8. mound any unused breading on top of fish
9. bake in 400 degree oven for 20 minutes , until fish is done and topping is browned
target.review: This was delicious.  I sprinkle a little lemon on tip to brighten up the flavour once it was out of the oven.  The coating on the underside was a little soggy for my tastes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rosemary and orange chicken breasts

while thumbing through a magazine at the doctor's office (my home away from home), i found this recipe.  others call for whole chickens or too much rosemary, which i think overpowers most dishes it's in.  i always end up leaving out most of it.  this was just right, though.  i wanted to post it so i didn't lose it, since i wrote it on a prescripton pad.

1. in a nonstick 12 inch skillet , melt butter over med-high heat
2. add garlic
3. add chicken and sprinkle tops with rosemary , pepper , and 1 / 2 teaspoons salt
4. cook 6 minutes
5. turn chicken over
6. reduce heat to medium
7. cover and cook 8 minutes or until juices run clear when thickest part of chicken is pierced with
8. meanwhile , squeeze 1 / 2 cup juice from 1 orange
9. cut peel and white pith from remaining orange
10. cut orange in half from stem to blossom , then cut each half crosswise into 1 / 4 inch thick slices
11. in a cup , mix orange juice , cornstarch , salt and 1 / 4 cup water until blended
12. transfer chicken to warm platter
13. to the same skillet , add orange juice mixture
14. heat sauce to boiling over med-high heat
15. cook stirring constantly , 1 minute or until sauce thickens slightly
16. stir in orange slices
17. heat through
18. spoon sauce over chicken on platter
demonstrations.review: My husband loved this so much, it has been added to the "Again" list.  Very easy to prepare.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
penne with cannellini beans

this is a quick, 5 ingredient recipe. it comes from light and tasty.  you should definitely be using the italian-style diced tomatoes that come already seasoned with herbs for flavor. if you use plain diced tomatoes, just add some herbs to  your liking when putting this recipe together.

1. cook pasta according to package directions
2. in large saucepan , combine the tomatoes and beans , and bring to a boil
3. reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes
4. add spinach , cook and stir for 2 minutes , or until spinach is wilted
5. drain pasta , top with the tomato mixture
6. sprinkle with cheese
demonstrations.review: Quick, and I used my homemade roasted tomatoes.  The 4 year-old gobbled it up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bar  b  barn ribs

this is a copy kat recipe from the famous bar "b" barn restaurant in montreal. simmer the ribs early in the day and then refrigerate until ready to bbq. this recipe is for pork but beef ribs can be substituted with no problem.

1. in a large saucepan or stock pot , cover ribs with cold water
2. add thyme , salt , pepper , bay leaf , celery and onion
3. bring to gentle boil
4. cover , reduce heat and simmer for about 45 minutes or until ribs are tender
5. remove ribs place in shallow glass dish
6. set aside
7. sauce
8. in small saucepan , combine all the sauce ingredients , bring to gentle boil
9. reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes to blend flavors
10. let cool
11. cut strips of ribs into serving portions of 3 to 4 ribs
12. pour sauce all over ribs in dish and marinate for 3 to 4 hours in refrigerator or for 30 minutes at room temperature
13. remove ribs from sauce , reserving any remaining sauce
14. cook ribs on greased grill over medium-hot coals or medium setting , turning and brushing occasionally with reserved sauce , for about 20 minutes or until meat is browned
demonstrations.review: Well my husband has announced that we can make this every night.  Very good!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian style cauliflower

i expected this to have a much stronger vinegar taste, but i was surprised to find it was really rather subtle, and just enhanced the cauliflower rather than truly flavoring it.  i like to taste my veggies, and not cover them up, so you can bet i enjoyed this.  from southern living.

1. remove outer leaves and break cauliflower into flowerets
2. arrange cauliflower in a steaming rack
3. place over boiling water
4. cover and steam for 5-8 minutes or until it reaches the tenderness that you like
5. transfer to a serving dish and keep warm
6. combine the remaining ingredients in a saucepan and cook over medium heat until hot
7. pour this mixture over cauliflower and toss
demonstrations.review: Delicious!!  We uswd fresh yellow cauliflower from out local farmer's market and it worked well.  Also wonderful cold the next day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dilly sole

my dh developed an allergy to white fish many years ago, but this was a dish we both loved; i served it often in the early 80s. it doubles easily if you want to feed more people.

1. preheat oven to 450 f
2. spray an eight-inch baking dish with nonstick cooking spray and set aside
3. with paper towel , pat fish dry
4. spread mayo on the broad half of each fillet and season with the salt and pepper
5. tear toast into pieces and place in a food processor
6. whirl toast until it is in crumbs
7. with processor running , drop garlic clove down chute and let process until chopped
8. add butter , dill and lemon zest to processor and process until combined
9. sprinkle this crumb mixture evenly over the fillets where you spread the mayo , then fold the narrow end of the fillets over the crumb mixture to form a roll
10. place in prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for 10 minutes , or until the sole flakes when tested with a fork
11. serve with steamed rice , broccoli , and fresh lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: Delicious!!  My 18 month old slurpped it right up.  It did take 15 minutes to cook completely tough, most likely due to my fikkets being thicker.

target.recipe_text:
grilled chicken kisses

foil packets for the grill shaped like a big
candy kiss. very easy clean-up and great tasting too. you can use your own preferences for the veggies and indiviualize each kiss to suit anyone. i just love to make these they are sooo good. this is how i make mine.

1. tear off 6 sheets of heavy duty aluminum foil about 20 inches long
2. spray center of foil with cooking spray
3. place sliced potatoes , about one potato per packet , onto center
4. season with cajun spice and pepper , to your taste place about 1 / 2 cup of baby carrots onto potaoes
5. put about 1 / 4 of a cup of the barbecue sauce on top
6. then , place a chicken breast on top of potatoes , carrots , and sauce
7. season chicken with the cajun spices and pepper
8. place onion rings , as many as you like , on top of chicken
9. finish off the packet with another 1 / 4 cup of the barbecue sauce over the onions
10. gather up the foil around the chicken and veggies , and twist the top tightly to seal
11. it should resemble a big candy kiss
12. repeat steps for all packets
13. place on a medium hot grill
14. mine is gas , i have it at about 350
15. i just leave them on the grill for 45 minutes all of these portions can be easily adjusted to each packet
16. be careful when opening them
target.review: I made this last night.  It is quick, simple and tastes great. You can add practically any combo of vegetables and still have a winner.  I added half a cob of corn to each packet(eating the corn was a little messy tho).  Next time I'm going to try a variety of red, green and yellow peppers. I did it in the oven at 375 degrees for 50 minutes with the "kisses" on a large cookie sheet. 5 stars definitely!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
muddy brownies

i make these occasionally when i really want a chocolate fix.  a few people on the site have requested that i post this.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease a 9x13 inch pan
3. in a large saucepan over medium heat , melt 1 cup of butter
4. remove from heat and stir in cocoa until smooth , then transfer to large mixing bowl
5. mix in the white sugar , eggs and 2 teaspoons vanilla
6. mix in the flour , then fold in chocolate / peanut butter chips and marshmallows
7. spread evenly into the prepared pan
8. bake for 25 to 30 minutes in the preheated oven , until brownies start to pull away from the sides of the pan
9. let cool in pan
demonstrations.review: Loved this, for those of you having problems, try freezing the marshmallows first and taking them out of freezer and dump them directly in.( no counter time so they can defrost.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: This was the best banana bread I have ever tried.  I added chopped pecans, cooked the directed amount of time and it was perfectly moist and delicious, even better the second day when we finished it off at breakfast.  It is so quick and easy I will buy extra bananas just so I can let them get overripe and make this again and again.  For those of you who had problems with the timing, I suggest making sure your oven temp is reading correctly. I always have an oven thermometer inside to make sure mine is right.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut cream cake

easy recipe that starts as a box mix with a little added flair.

1. when cake is done , punch holes all over the top
2. pour cream of coconut over the entire cake and let cake cool completely
3. beat together the cream cheese and whipped topping
4. spread over cake and sprinkle with coconut
5. refrigerate until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: I made this cake tonight. When I got to the frosting I really didn't think it was sweet enough with just the Cool Whip and cream cheese but I went ahead and followed the directions, covered it with coconut and put it in the fridge.  Anyone who bakes knows it's hard to not at least taste something you've never made before, so 3 hours later at 12:30am I got it out and took just a corner square bite, then I called my husband upstairs and gave him the same size bite (knowing he doesn't like coconut).  His first comment was, "Is that all I get??"  Needless to say, we both ended up eating another larger piece.  We absolutely love this cake.  It has just the right amount of sweetness and is a very light, enjoyable dessert, not to mention very easy.  I am so glad I tried this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry cheese bars

i ripped this recipe from a magazine a long time ago.  i made it many times and it always turned out delicious as well as beautiful.  since then, i misplaced my box of recipes torn from magazines until the other day.  i had previously tried to find this recipe on zaar, but couldn't so i was happy to find the clipping so now i can share the recipe with all of you.  since the layers are baked separately, the cook time and the prep time overlap somewhat.  prep time does not include refrigeration time.  i have used low-fat cream cheese and it turns out just as good.  enjoy!

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease a 13x9x2-inch pan
3. coarsely chop 1 / 2 cup nuts for the topping
4. set aside
5. finely chop remaining 1 / 2 cup nuts
6. combine flour and brown sugar
7. cut in shortening until fine crumbs form
8. add finely chopped nuts and coconut
9. remove 1 / 2 cup of this mixture and set aside
10. press remaining crumbs in bottom of pan
11. bake at 350f for 12-15 minutes until edges are lightly browned
12. beat cream cheese , sugar , eggs , and vanilla at medium speed until smooth
13. spread over hot , baked crust
14. return to oven and bake 15 minutes longer
15. spread cherry pie filling over cheese layer
16. combine reserved nuts and reserved crumbs
17. sprinkle over cherries
18. return to oven and bake 15 minutes more
19. cool
20. refrigerate several hours
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe. I made it yesterday and my husband and I have eaten almost all of it.  The crust is awesome and for those reviewers who said they don't like coconut, the crust is such a different one from others and you know it's special but you won't even know the coconut is in there, unless you put more in it next time like I intend to try. I love, love, love this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nestle  toll house walnut pie  aka black cat pie

this recipe is adapted from the nestle' toll house heritage cookbook (1980) and posted at the request of a zaar member.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees
2. in a large bowl , beat eggs until foamy , beat in flour , sugar , and brown sugar until well blended
3. blend in melted butter
4. stir in nestle' semi-sweet real chocolate morsels and walnuts
5. pour into pie shell
6. bake 1 hour
7. serve warm with whipped cream or ice cream , if desired
demonstrations.review: Oh my my my. I baked this pie this evening and my husband and I were in chocolate heaven. This is a chocolate lover's dream. I didn't change a thing, followed instructions to the letter.  It was perfect except for one thing, the extra inches it's going to put on my waistline.

target.recipe_text:
oven baked coconut shrimp  low fat

there is almost no fat in this recipe, please make certain to generously grease your baking pan, i use the non-stick foil for this --- this complete recipe can be doubled to about 52-53 shrimp, enough to feed a crowd! if your coconut flakes are very large, then just chop them slightly, they will stick to the egg whites better. cooking time is estimated depending on size of your shrimp  --- serve the shrimp with pineapple or a fruit salsa --- your going to love this shrimp! ;-)

1. set oven to 375 degrees f
2. rinse the shrimp under cold water and pat dry with paper towels
3. in a shallow dish combine the cornstarch with salt and red pepper
4. stir to combine
5. place the egg whites in a medium bowl
6. beat using an electric mixer on high speed until frothy
7. place the coconut in a shallow dish
8. working one shrimp at a time dredge the shrimp firstly in the cornstarch mixture , then dip in egg whites and then in shredded coconut
9. place the shrimp on a foil-lined baking sheet that has been generously coated with cooking spray
10. repeat with remaining shrimp
11. lightly spray the shrimp with cooking spray
12. bake for about 20 minutes or until the shrimp are done , turn the shrimp after 10 minutes of cooking making that 10 minutes per side
target.review: Wow!  These were better then deep fried, you could actually taste the shrimp and the coconut and not grease!  I put them on my silpat and had no trouble with sticking or breading falling off.  I will make these again and again.  Awesome!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yogurt hollandaise sauce

who would have thought? a guilt free hollandaise sauce that does not compromise on flavour!!! this is our go-to recipe and we find it better than the sauces filled with butter. sauce can be made in advance and refrigerated for up to 1 week. from 'smart cooking'  byanne lindsay.

1. use double boiler or like me - place a strainer / sieve over a sauce pan of water and place a bowl in the sieve
2. beat yogurt , lemon juice , egg yolks well
3. heat over simmering water , stirring frequently , until sauce has thickened , approx 15 min
4. remove from heat and stir in salt , mustard , pepper and dill / parsley
demonstrations.review: What a great "cheat"!!  This was yummy on my Valentine's Day filet!  I did add some fresh tarragon for more of a bernaise sauce flavor.  Would have done the whole shallot and vinegar thing but was short on time. Sauce was great and I will use this again and again! Love being able to enjoy this without the guilt and calories of the original.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized onion and asiago beer batter bread

a quick beer bread.  delicious with soups and stews.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. heat olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat
3. add onion and 1 t sugar , and saut 15 minutes or until tender and caramelized
4. cool to room temperature
5. combine flour , 2 t sugar , baking powder , and salt in a bowl
6. make a well in center of mixture
7. add onion , cheese , and beer
8. stir just until moist
9. spoon batter into a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan coated with cooking spray
10. drizzle evenly with butter
11. bake for 55-60 minutes , or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. cool 5 minutes in pan on a wire rack
13. remove from pan
14. cool completely on wire rack
demonstrations.review: This was soooo good and very easy to put together.  I will be making this again and again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caribbean black bean soup   slow cooker

a filling easy soup to make...takes a little preparation if you use dried black beans, but worth the effort.

1. soak beans overnight in 4 quarts water
2. drain
3. combine beans , onion , green pepper , garlic , ham , oil , cumin , oregano , thyme , salt , pepper , and 3 cups of fresh water
4. stir cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours or on high 4-5 hours
5. for thick soup , remove half of cooked bean mixture and puree until smooth in blender or mash with a potato masher
6. return to cooker
7. if you like it souper , leave it as is
8. add vinegar and stir well
9. debone the ham hock if you used one and cut into bite sized pieces , and return to the soup serve in soup bowls with a dollop of sour cream in the middle of each serving , topped with fresh cilantro
demonstrations.review: First time doing black bean soup in a crock pot.  Worked great!  I added extra cumin as we love it here. Also had more ham than it called for but it turned out perfect.  I had to cook it for about 5 1/2 hours to get the beans as tender as I like them.  Served it was some pickled onions on top, hubby loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I thought this was a good recipe. It was so easy and took no time at all to throw in the crock pot. I love that you use frozen chicken!I did add some cumin, garlic powder, oregano, just a pinch of salt and some pepper.  I served it over rice and my husband loved it!  I also used some homemade fresh salsa instead of jarred.  It is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
korean beef  bulgogi in lettuce wraps

this recipe is another winner from toronto star - we made it tonight and just loved it. a fun way to have the kids eat their lettuce, too. beef needs to marinate 2-12 hours, so plan ahead when making this meal

1. combine first 9 ingredients
2. slice the steaks across the grain into thin slices
3. place beef in resealable ziplock bag and pour soy mixture over
4. let marinate in refridgerator for 2-12 hours , turning bag occoationally
5. heat large non-stick skillet or wok over medium-high to high heat
6. pour beef and marinade into the skilled and cook until mixture is almost dry , 6-8 minute
7. toast sesame seeds and garlic in hot pan
8. serve with lettuce leaves , toasted sesame seeds and toasted garlic cloves and perhaps some hot sauce if you like it hot
9. you roll the beef and condiments up in the lettuce leaf and eat like a roll with your hands
10. serve with white rice
demonstrations.review: I did not slice my flank steak since I wanted to grill it.  Turned out perfect!  I did cook down the marinade and used it as a sauce and they devoured it!  Very good, nice flavor will make again and again!

target.recipe_text:
lasagna soup

i couldn't believe how easy and tasty this recipe is.  i love the half-melted pieces of cheese in the soup!  this is from cuisine at home.

1. brown sausage in a large saucepan over medium-high heat
2. add onions and carrots
3. saute 3 minutes
4. stir in mushrooms and garlic , and saute another 3 minutes
5. add broth , stewed tomatoes , and tomato sauce , and bring to a boil
6. drop in pasta and simmer until cooked , about 10 minutes , or according to package directions
7. stir in spinach and cook until wilted
8. place 1 / 4 cup cheese into serving bowls and pour soup on top
9. garnish with parmesan and basil
target.review: Sharlene - This soup is really good. My husband even gave it a thumbs up-after he looked at me and said "This really does taste like lasagna". The only thing different I did was put the stewed tomatoes and carrots in a blender so that I wouldn't have to chop the carrots up. thanks for the great soup

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamed spinach  like boston market

this is by far the best creamed spinach recipe that i have ever tasted! my mother got married in early nov and my brother (a chef) served bar-b-qued filet mignon, oven roasted red potatoes, this creamed spinach, salad and garlicy cheesy bread - talk about heaven!! the creamed spinach stole the show and 1/2 the guests left with the recipe! he found the recipe on the internet, it is a copy cat recipe of boston market's creamed spinach. (i think it's better).

1. in a saucepan over medium low heat , melt 3 tbls butter
2. stir flour and salt into pan until creamed together
3. slowly stir in cream , then stir in cream cheese , increase heat to medium
4. constantly whisk until mixture becomes thick and smooth , remove from heat and set aside
5. in a saucepan over medium-high heat , saute onions and garlic in remaining butter until transparent
6. add spinach and water to pan , reduce heat to low , cover
7. cook , stirring occasionally for 8 minutes
8. stir prepared sauce and parmesan cheese into pan , stir until completely blended
demonstrations.review: The Chart House in Newport, Ky. has a creamed spinach on their menu that tastes just like this. It has the perfect balance of garlic with the parmesan cheese. Loved this. This will be my new addition for Thanksgiving. I didn't alter a thing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wild addicting dip

wow, the name says it all. we had a huge buffet dinner for new years eve one year and people could not leave this alone. the recipe is also easily 1/2 sized.

1. spread each layer evenly in order given
2. cover and chill before serving
3. serve with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: I make this dip alot. I have people who sit in front of the dish and don't move. I would make one suggestion: that you pat dry the tomatoes so it does not get runny.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy  yummy  hummus  hummos  hummous   however u spell it

i got this idea to use yoghurt from my friend nasreen.  i used to work at a lebanese restaurant that had the best hummous and i could not get the recipe out of the owner!! he he he. i just loved it and wondered how they got the hummous to be so light in color compared to most hummouses... well, my friend nasreen showed me how to make baba ghanoush one day and she added yoghurt to it and told me to add yoghurt to hummous also to get a lighter color.  i finally figured out it was yoghurt!!  it is best to let this sit in the fridge for at least a couple hours to overnight for the flavors but is still good to eat as soon as it is done. 

thank you for all of the reviews of the recipe  ;)

1. if you have the patience , peel the "skins" off all the chickpeas , but this step is optional
2. peeling helps with the creaminess
3. boil chickpeas for 10 minutes
4. drain but reserve about 1 / 2 cup of the boiling liquid in a separate cup
5. in a food processor or blender , add all the other ingredients and the chickpeas and blend till smooth
6. if you find it is difficult to blend or too thick pour in some of that reserved boiling liquid -- just little at a time until you get the right smooth consistency
7. garnish with a good serving of extra virgin olive oil , and chopped tomatoes , onions , and a little paprika
8. it is even better the next day !
demonstrations.review: Ameera - Great hummus! I have attempted to make hummus numerous times with the results a thick, greasy, chunky mess.  This was perfect. Taking off the "shells" of the chickpea was something I would have never thought of. I did have to add a little liquid to mine. I think it is a texture thing.  I also added some cheyenne pepper. Perfect! Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s best stuffing

a thirty year old recipe that just seems to get better with time. i went to visit my daughter 3000 miles away and i still had to make the stuffing for dinner.

1. saute sausage until brown
2. remove from pan and cut into small bites
3. in a large skillet , melt butter and cook onion , celery , and mushrooms over medium heat for 3 minutes or until softened
4. transfer sausage and veggies , including any butter that is left in the pan to a bowl
5. add stuffing mix , bread cubes , sage , thyme , poultry seasoning , salt , pepper , pecans , turkey stock , and eggs
6. toss well and adjust seasoning
7. stuffing should be moist but not soggy
8. add more stock if needed
9. transfer to a baking dish
10. bake in a 325 degree fahrenheit oven for 20 minutes covered and 10 minutes uncovered until heated through and crust forms on top
11. or better yet stuff it into a big fat turkey
demonstrations.review: After 4 years of trying different stuffing recipes I finally found one that we all liked.  I made this for Thanks giving this year and everyone in my family loved it-I was told not to try anything different. I made this exactly to the recipe. Thanks crazymom-this is the whip

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: Kitten - Loved your meatball recipe. My 3 year old helped me shape them, he has perfect size hands for them. They turned out great and the recipe was easy. Thanks

target.recipe_text:
southwest spaghetti squash

i found this recipe in a low-carb cookbook. the sweetness of the squash mixes well with the spice of the other ingredients. low-carb and vegetarian!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cut squash in half lengthwise
3. remove and discard seeds
4. place squash , cut side down , in greased baking pan
5. bake 45 minutes to 1 hour or until just tender
6. using fork , remove spaghetti-like strands from hot squash and place strands in large bowl
7. add tomatoes with juice , beans , 1 / 2 cup cheese , cilantro , cumin , garlic salt and pepper
8. toss well
9. spray 1 1 / 2 quart casserole with nonstick cooking spray
10. spoon mixture into casserole
11. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 4 cup cheese
12. bake uncovered , 30 to 35 minutes or until heated through
13. serve immediately
target.review:
This was wondeful!!! The flavours blended so nicely. Definitely a keeper. The only extra thing I add was a little cayenne pepper.
Thank you for the sharing Cyn.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s spinach parmesan rice bake

this is a wonderful easy side dish to chicken or meat and any leftovers freeze wonderful,  it may also be baked in a 10-inch deep-dish pie plate and cut into wedges, this may be doubled but i would still only use one package or spinach or maybe 1-1/2 packages adding in too much spinach will overpower all other ingredients,  prep time does not include cooking the rice --- for freezing prepare recipe as directed but do not bake, wrap pan in plastic wrap then tightly in foil and freeze, to serve thaw over night in refrigerator, remove wrapping bake at 350°f for 25-30 minutes or until hot.

1. set oven to 350f
2. generously grease a 11 x 7-inch baking dish
3. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients with a wooden spoon , mixing very well to combine
4. season with salt , pepper and cayenne to taste
5. transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish then sprinkle with parmesan cheese
6. bake uncovered or covered for 25 minutes or until set
7. top with mozzarella cheese the last 5 minutes of baking
demonstrations.review: What a wonderful dish! and a great why to get some spinach in your diet. I used 2% milk (because that's all I had on hand) otherwise followed as is. (although I must have put more garlic..there is no such thing as too much garlic!)Thanx Kittencal for sharing one of you creations.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sparkling pineapple lemonade

lightly fizzy with lots of flavour. my boys love it. i refrigerate it in a 2 litre(1/2 gallon) pop bottle - keeps the fizz in it. ds#1 calls it 

1. stir together sugar and the juices until the sugar is dissolved
2. put in the pop bottle
3. slowly pour in the ginger-ale
4. screw on the cover and lightly shake bottle to blend everything
5. keep refrigerated , or serve on ice
demonstrations.review:
This is by far the best lemonade I have ever tasted!! and it's so easy to make!
.. thanx MaeEast for sharing it with us!
•Savannah

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai tofu and squash curry

from canadian living magazine.  recommended for tofu lovers and/or fans of thai-inspired dishes.

1. pat tofu dry with paper towels
2. cut into 3 / 4-inch cubes
3. set aside
4. peel and seed squash
5. cut into 3 / 4-inch cubes to make 3 cups
6. set aside
7. in skillet , heat oil over medium heat
8. cook onion , garlic and curry paste , stirring occasionally , until onion is softened , about 5 minutes
9. add squash , coconut milk , stock , soy sauce , sugar , fish sauce and salt
10. bring to boil
11. reduce heat to low
12. partially cover and simmer until squash is almost tender , about 12 minutes
13. add red pepper
14. simmer for 5 minutes
15. add tofu
16. simmer until heated through , about 2 minutes
17. stir in cilantro and lime juice
18. sprinkle with peanuts
demonstrations.review:
Thank you so much Roosie for this wonderful recipe! It's absolutely delicious. And it really is hard to find such good tofu recipes. I followed everything as is.. using what looked like an Australian Blue Squash. I had broccoli and spinach on-hand so I added that in.
I did however leave out the peanuts. Served this with brown-rice.. even my 5 year old nephew enjoyed it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
halibut with mushrooms

quick and elegant topping for fish and delicious too! tasty combination. adapted from canadian living magazine.

1. in a bowl , mix together , mushrooms , onions , mayonnaise , parsley , lemon juice , ginger , salt and pepper
2. set aside
3. place fish on greased rimmed baking sheet or broiling pan
4. broil for 5 minutes
5. with a lifter , turn fish over
6. spread mushroom mixture evenly over fish
7. broil until mushroom mixture is golden brown and fish flakes easily when tested , about 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: Lovely recipe, makes a change from what we usually have. I added garlic (because everything needs garlic :D ) and a little cayenne pepper.. but other than that, I made as is. Thank you for the wonderful recipe Derf.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
m   m dream bars

these are yummy! the original recipe called for red and green christmas m&ms, but i see no reason to relegate this delicious treat to just the holidays. :)

1. combine oatmeal , brown sugar , flour , coconut , baking soda , and salt
2. add melted butter and stir until moist
3. reserve 1 1 / 2 cups and press remaining crumbs into a greased 13x9-inch baking pan
4. bake 12 minutes at 375f
5. combine milk and peanut butter
6. carefully spread over baked crust
7. sprinkle on m&m's and chocolate chips
8. sprinkle reserved crumbs over chocolate pieces and lightly press crumbs down
9. bake 20 minutes , or until golden brown
10. cool completely before cutting
demonstrations.review:
Oh my!.. can you guys see my extra butt.. rich indeed, but oh so wonderful!! Gayla, this is an above 5 star recipe..not only because it tastes so good, but so easy to make. Thank you very, very much!!
Tips for others: be gentle when spreading the peanut-butter mix (so the base doesn't lift off), and you will definitely love making 'bar' cookies, if you FOIL the pan. (no oil/grease, no sticking, and you don't even have to wash the pan)

target.recipe_text:
light wheat bread or rolls  abm

very light and good tasting wheat bread that kids love. another standard on our dinner table. sometimes i'll make dinner rolls with this recipe. hope you like it with your meals! cook time is estimated if you bake in your oven and not in your bread machine. also makes 15 rolls

1. sift flours , salt , sugar and dry milk
2. add to bread machine with liquids first then flour mixture- yeast should be last
3. set on light / med setting
4. often i will set just on dough setting and knead and raise last time to bake in my own oven at 375 degree oven for about 25-30 minutes
target.review: This is a very good recipe. I tried it out on daughter and son-in-law last night. I am making again today for dinner club. Yesterday I used 1 cup wheat flour and 3 cups white flour. I just didn't think they would be "wheaty" enough. Today I am using the recipe as is, I believe I was wrong.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
glazed cinnamon rolls   bread machine

the bread machine makes these rolls easy! i usually make them at night and refrigerate them to bake for the next day's breakfast. adapted from betty crocker's bread machine cookbook. prep time listed includes the dough mixing time and rising time.

1. place water , 2 tablespoons butter , bread flour , 1 / 4 cup white granulated sugar , salt and yeast in the bread machine and start on dough cycle
2. once dough is complete , roll out into a 9" square on a lightly floured surface
3. mix 1 / 3 cup sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon together
4. spread 2 tablespoons softened margarine over the dough and sprinkle with the cinnamon mixture
5. roll up tightly into a log and pinch the edges to seal
6. cut into 1" slices and place in a greased 9"x9"x2" square pan
7. cover loosely with plastic wrap and let rise 1 hour or so until double , or in refrigerator overnight if making for breakfast
8. preheat oven to 375f and bake 20 minutes or until golden brown
9. mix powdered sugar , vanilla and milk to make glaze , drizzle over rolls and serve warm
demonstrations.review: Fantastic! These turned out perfectly! I undermeasured the yeast so they were slow to rise but very much worth the wait!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy veggie soup

nan

1. melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat
2. add onion
3. cook 5 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. add broth , potato and carrots
5. bring to a boil over high heat
6. reduce heat and simmer uncovered 5 minutes
7. add broccoli , salt and pepper
8. cook 5 minutes
9. place flour in a medium bowl
10. gradually stir in milk , mixing well
11. add milk mixture to soup
12. bring to a simmer
13. simmer uncovered 5 minutes or until vegetables are tender and soup has thickened
14. for chicken vegetable soup , stir in 2 cup diced cooked chicken breast
demonstrations.review: Very nice and so simple! I added celery with the onion. Used whole milk. Sprinkled with parsley. Next time I hope I have some chicken ready. I really want to use my homemade broth next time. A definite keeper with my go to recipes. Thank you for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thick  soft  and chewy chocolate chip cookies

i moved out of the house in 1992 but my dad still insist i make his chocolate chip cookies for him. after much searching these are the ones we deemed "best". soft and chewy but with a lightly crisp outer layer. if you don't want the crispness, substitute more butter for the shortening. 

i have found that you need to follow the directions *exactly* to get the best cookies. not using real butter or all brown sugar, not beating the eggs in one at a time, not baking them at a higher temp than the "traditional" recipe, all make a difference in the end result. 

i have also found that land o' lake butter makes a better cookie than some generic brand butter. don't let the butter sit out too long. it needs to soften but if it sits until the moisture starts to separate from the butter, it is too soft and it will affect the resulting cookies. if that happens, refrigerate the dough for about an hour to help them not spread as much. it also helps to use the mixer on the dough in between batches going into the oven. it helps keep the dough from starting to separate if it is a warm day. 

another thing i've learned is you have to make sure there is plenty of circulation in your oven. when i moved, my cookies started turning out flat again. i finally realized that my oven was smaller at the new house and when i switched to smaller cookie sheets, my cookies turned out perfectly!

1. mix flour , baking soda , and salt in a small bowl
2. in a separate bowl , beat butter and shortening until creamy
3. add sugar and vanilla and beat with a mixer on medium speed until well blended
4. beat in eggs , one at a time , mixing well
5. add flour mixture , and beat slowly to incorporate , then beat to blend well
6. stir in chocolate chips and nuts
7. drop batter in 2-tablespoon portions about 2 inches apart on baking sheets
8. bake in a 375f preheated oven until edges of cookies are brown but an area about 1 inch wide in the center is still pale , about 10 minutes
9. if using 2 pans in 1 oven , switch positions at half-time
10. let cookies cool on pan about 5 minutes , then transfer to racks with a spatula
11. serve warm or cool
demonstrations.review: A new mixer came by UPS today so I had to have a recipe to try it out. I specifically set out to find a cookie recipe with no white sugar, as I was out. This one fit the bill and they were (are)wonderful! I very simple recipe, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ruby s vinegar pie

this is my aunt ruby's recipe. it is remarkably easy, and delicious. among my in-laws, ruby is famous because of this recipe.

1. preheat oven to 300 degrees f
2. mix all ingredients well
3. pour into unbaked pie shell
4. bake for 55-60 minutes
demonstrations.review: YUM! Just like my grandmother used to make! I am so happy to have found this recipe. It was fun fixing it for hubby who hates vinegar! = )

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chicken crescent roll casserole

this will also work great with turkey; if you do not have chicken breasts, then use any leftover cooked chicken. if desired you can fill the crescents just with the filling mixture and omit the soup, just brush with butter before baking. they are wonderful just stuffed with the filling! a few members have experienced a soggy bottom, so you might want to consider just drizzling half (or even a little less) of the soup mixture on top and a little around the sides of the crescents, then save the rest of the soup mixture for another time (this will help prevent a soggy bottom). you may use the jumbo crescent rolls and stuff with more chicken mixture :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. butter a casserole dish
3. in a saucepan , mix half and half cream , 3 / 4 cup grated cheese and undiluted chicken soup
4. heat just until the cheese melts
5. for the filling --- in a bowl , mix the soft cream cheese with butter until very smooth , then add in garlic powder
6. add in the chopped chicken , onion and cheddar cheese
7. mix well until combined
8. add in 2 tablespoons whipping cream or mayonnaise
9. mix to combine
10. season with seasoned salt or white and black pepper to taste
11. unroll the crescent rolls
12. place 1 heaping tablespoon chicken mixture on top of each crescent triangle , then roll up starting at the thicker end
13. drizzle a small amount of soup mixture on the bottom of the dish
14. then place the crescent rolls seam-side down on top of the creamed mixture in the casserole
15. drizzle the remaining sauce on top and sprinkle with 1 cup grated cheese , or amount desired
16. bake for about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I remember these from 20 years ago! We were visiting friends and this was one of the meals we had. YUM! And BTW, I love them a little soggy. Reminds me of dumplings.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s bakery buttercream  frosting icing

this is similar to bakery frosting and so much better than any canned!  ---  for extra fluffy frosting use heavy cream and make certain to beat for at least 3-5 minutes and remember to sift the confectioners sugar before using.  for flavor and color you can add 1-2 envelopes 3-grams each, duncan hines frosting creations flavor mix, any flavor desired.

1. in a large bowl using an electric mixer at medium speed beat together the shortening and margarine or butter with cream , salt almond extract and vanilla until smooth
2. add in sifted confectioners sugar starting with 4-1 / 2 cups
3. beat very well until smooth and fluffy , adding more confectioners sugar or cream or milk until you achieve desired consistency
4. add in the food coloring or flavor creation powder until the desired shade is achieved
target.review: Excellent recipe!! It was very easy to make and decorate with. And it tastes great too. I used butter and coconut oil (which has the consistency of shortening). I added red food coloring to make pink valentines cupcakes. Thanks for another great one :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick lemon and garlic quinoa salad

refreshing! good potluck pick, too!

1. boil the water in a large stock pot
2. add salt and quinoa and boil for 10 minutes
3. drain in a strainer
4. prepare dressing in a large bowl
5. add carrots , seeds , parsley , and cooked quinoa , and toss well
demonstrations.review:
This was my first time making a dish using quinoa, and it was fantastic!!!! I used the dressing recipe, in which I reduced the oil to 1 tbsp. I prepared the quinoa as directed. For the salad itself I used finely chopped cucumber, diced tomato's seeds removed, and quartered grape tomatos. I added a sprinkle of feta cheese on top of each serving. It was great, the dressing was a perfect combo of flavors and it really made the salad a hit!!!!!Thanks!!!!

I just made this salad again, but I omitted the oil completly and added black beans!!! It was great, a complete meal without the added fat from the oil!! Yummy

demonstrations.recipe_text:
get my day started granola

this granola is what gets my family started nearly every day. i experimented with different ingredients until i hit upon the combination we like best. i've tried using different amounts of oil and honey to make it as healthy as possible and the amounts shown here are the lowest i've been able to go without sacrificing flavor. if you want to omit a nut for lower fat content, omit walnuts since they are the highest in fat.  i mix 1/3 cup of this with a fat free vanilla yogurt and my metabolically blessed husband devours a big bowl of this with just milk. this granola will clump somewhat if that's how you let it cool, but if you want clumpier granola you'll need to increase the wet ingredients.

1. stir together oats , nuts , coconut , seeds , banana chips , and wheat germ in a large bowl
2. in a separate small bowl , mix the raisins and cranberries and set aside
3. combine oil and honey in a microwaveable bowl and microwave on high for about 2 and a half minutes
4. immediately pour over oats mixture , stirring as you go
5. stir to coat dry ingredients
6. divide mixture and spread on two ungreased cookie sheets
7. bake one pan at a time for 20 minutes in a preheated 325 degree oven on the center rack
8. immediately after removing from oven , stir half of the raisin mixture into each pan
9. be sure to release the granola from the cookie sheet or it will stick as it cools
10. let cool , then store in an airtight container
11. i store this at room temperature in two big canisters
12. it's always gone within a couple of weeks and i've never had it become stale
13. i'm not sure about the number of servings , but just gave it my best guess
demonstrations.review:
Made for PAC spring 2008. Good granola that is easy to prepare. I did have to do a few things differently.  I used slow oats, that I soaked for 12 hours then rinsed and drained well. I soaked the oats to make them more digestible (as I do with all grains, seeds, and nuts). I used pumpkins seeds, and slivered almonds. I did have to cook for a lot longer, because of the soaking. I cooked it for 1 hour at 325, mixing every 20 minutes. Then I reduced the heat to 170 and let it cook for another 2 hours without touching it. It came out lovely and crunchy
with a nice sweet taste. It is a lot quicker than my soaked granola recipe, the end result is different but still good. I will use this recipe when I don't have time to make my other one (which takes 2 1/2 days). Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry muffins

yummy low-fat blueberry muffins

1. preheat oven to 350 and use flour version of cooking spray a 12 cup muffin pan
2. combine dry ingredients
3. combine all other ingredients , except blueberries
4. combine slowly , as with other muffin recipes
5. fold in blueberries
6. fill muffin cups 1 / 2 way
7. bake in preheated oven for 25 mins or until golden brown , and springy to touch
demonstrations.review: Made for PAC spring 2008. Nice muffins, easy to make with a nice blueberry flavor. I liked that they were not too sweet. I did add 1/2 tsp baking soda to make them rise a little more. I made one batch to recipe (with 1/2 tsp baking soda added) and got 12 regular sized muffins. I also made I batch with whole wheat flour and raw cane sugar, which did not rise as much. These I made as mini muffins and got 36, these took about 18 minutes. They tasted great for me and my kids but we are used to eating health food. So if you want to make these healthier, the option is there. :) :) Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moist white cake

this was originally a recipe i got from a friend and i altered it so much that it became my own. makes a very nice, moist cake or cupcakes. i like it best with homemade buttercream frosting.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in small bowl , beat egg whites , 1 / 4 c milk , vanilla , and almond extract
3. set aside
4. in another bowl , mix together dry ingredients
5. add butter and 3 / 4 c milk to dry mixture
6. mix on low speed until mixed well , scraping the sides of the bowl as necessary
7. add egg white / milk / vanilla mixture slowly while mixing at low speed
8. mix on low speed or by hand until well mixed
9. bake 22 - 32 minutes until toothpick inserted into center comes out clean
10. be careful ! this cake does not brown as much as most cakes so be careful not to overbake !
11. wait until completely cooled before frosting
demonstrations.review: Made for PAC spring 2008. This turned out really nicely, but it was very heavy for a cupcake. It would work better as a layer cake. With that said my family did really enjoy it!! I halved the recipe and got 24 perfect mini cupcakes, they took 10 mins in my oven. You really do have to use the toothpick trick, because they do not look done. I iced them with a cream cheese icing, and then my family devoured them!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best carrot cake  in the world

was in a paper cutting my aunt gave me from an usa newspaper back in the 80's.. i have adapted it over the years to be yummier :) it is a very large cake that needs to be cooked in a roasting dish.. very moist and best iced with cream cheese frosting.

1. preheat oven to 180c and grease and line a large roasting dish
2. sift together the flour , baking powder , cinnamon , baking soda
3. add salt
4. beat eggs in a large bowl , add sugar and oil
5. mix in carrot and pineapple until blended
6. incorporate sifted flour mix bit-by-bit and stir until just combined
7. bake in oven for 1 hour 1 hour 15 minutes or until cake starts shrinking from sides
8. insert skewer , if it comes out clean then its cooked
9. rest cake in tin for 15 minutes and then turn onto wire cooling tray
10. frosting
11. beat butter , vanilla and cream cheese together in a mixer
12. add icing sugar slowly until the frosting is a smooth consistancy
13. frost cake when cold
demonstrations.review: Made for PAC spring 2008. Well the results are in, my carrot cake loving DH says to give this recipe 100% (which I took to mean 5 stars). I followed the recipe, but did add 1 cup of walnuts (DH loves walnuts). I cooked it for 1hour 20mins. Cooled it and topped with cream cheese icing. It was a big hit, I'll be making it again. Thanks for a great recipe :)

target.recipe_text:
best beer margarita

i make these all year around for my parties they are the best margarita,  don't worry you won't even taste the beer, you can double or triple this recipe if desired, if the mixture tastes too sweet you can add in a little more water, use the limeade can to measure out all ingredients

1. pour the limeade , tequila , seven-up , water and beer into a large glass pitcher
2. stir with a long-handled spoon until completely blended and the frozen limeade has completely melted
3. add in lots of ice
4. adjust with extra water if the mixture is too sweet
5. serve each glass with a lime wedge on the end
target.review: This is just delicious! It's very refreshing and not too sweet. I did add about a half a cup of triple sec and I'm drinking it over ice. I'm on my third one and I'm not planning on sharing with anyone! This will be in my fridge all summer! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
unbelievable baked buffalo wings

here's a healthy alternative to fried wings: one of my famous recipes! the meat will fall off the bone! unbelievable!

1. fill a large pot half way with water and then add the first 4 ingredients
2. bring water mixture and wings to a boil and then boil for 15 minutes
3. transfer wings to an oven safe container coated with cooking spray
4. bake wings on "broil" for 15 minutes on each side
5. while waiting for wings , combine the hot sauce and margarine in a microwave safe container and cook in microwave for 2 minutes or until melted
6. when wings are done , shake 'em up with the sauce and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: We LOVE these wings! They are quick, easy and delicious! Our 22 year old son said that these were the best wings he's ever had. Friday night is pizza and wings night at our house and these are on the menu for tonight. I'm also going to try this cooking method for making bbq wings. Thanks for sharing a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
now don t go  eeewww    before you try this

the only way to eat fresh tomatoes! in anticipation of the impending tomato harvest, i share with you a family secret. this is the reason we look forward to the end of summer, to the time when our gardens and our friends gardens are bursting with little red-skinned treasures. when i tell anyone about this, besides my brother and sister -- we learned it from mom -- and my children -- now that i've gotten them to try it -- they think i'm weird (well...yes, i am, but this isn't why). people looked at me oddly when i made this in the college cafeteria. at least i thought that was the reason. it never tasted right, though. i think the foodservice tomatoes were plastic. my husband seems to shudder if he sees me or the kids consuming this treat, but then, he hates warm peanut butter. period. won't touch it. i haven't managed to get any of my in-laws to give it a try; my husband's dad just looks at me and shakes his head. come to think of it, i get a lot of that from him. so, what is this food that most people seem to find so repulsive that they won't even consider it? i just call it exactly what it is: peanut butter and tomatoes on toast. if you're intrigued, the extremely difficult and intricate recipe follows below. if you think i'm weird, get in line. grossed out? get over it, and try it already. i thought it was pretty gross the first time i saw my mom eating it, too, but she made me take a bite, and i was hooked.

1. spread peanut butter on hot toast
2. concerned with calories-- you don't have to lay it on really thick , just make sure you can taste it
3. now , completely cover the toast with tomato slices
4. cut sliced tomatoes in halves or quarters , if necessary , to accomplish this task
5. sprinkle liberally with black pepper , and add just a bit of salt , if desired
6. eat while toast is still hot
7. if it gets cold , throw away and start over
8. well , i'd probably eat it anyway , but it's not as good cold
9. try it , you'll like it
10. trust me on this-- the salty peanut butter is just wonderful with the tomatoes , and at least a little bit of pepper is necessary
11. i know , you're going eeewwwwww !
12. but if you give it a shot , who knows-- maybe this is how you can find your inner weirdo
demonstrations.review: I have enough food addictions - now I've added another one!! At least this seems fairly healthy! This is really good! I can hardly wait to see if me peanutbutter, tomato loving daughter will try it. Thanks for sharing such a great snack!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked ham and cheese omelet roll

this is an easy way to serve omelets. in our house, it takes me forever to make breakfast on the stove top! baking this is soooo much easier. feel free to add or subtract to suit your tastes (bacon, sausage, onions, peppers, etc.)

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. beat eggs and milk until fluffy
3. add flour , salt and pepper and beat or whisk until smooth
4. pour into a buttered or greased 9 x 13 baking dish or pan
5. bake for 10 - 15 minutes or until eggs are just about set
6. sprinkle with chopped ham or lay slices of ham evenly on top
7. sprinkle with cheese
8. bake for about 5 minutes more or until cheese is melted
9. starting at short side , roll up omelet while still in pan
10. place seam side down on serving dish
11. cut into slices
demonstrations.review: This was great! Quick, easy, light, Fluffy and delicious! Thanks for sharing, this is a keeper! I did have a lot of flour lumps in mine, so I just put it in my blender and it worked great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of mcdonald s shamrock shake by todd wilbur

recipe adapted from todd wilbur's version of mcdonald's shamrock shake www.topsecretrecipes.com. i used to absolutely love it when mcdonald's brought out their shamrock shakes around st. patrick's day. the past couple of years i haven't been able to have it because of the dairy, so i was thrilled when i found this copycat recipe! just use the soy ingredients to make it dairy-free.

1. combine all ingredients in a blender and blend on high speed until smooth
2. stop blender to stir with a spoon if necessary to help blend ice cream
3. pour into 12-ounce cups and serve each with a straw
4. happy st patrick's day !
demonstrations.review: Made four batches of this for the family, everyone loved it! Even my picky husband!  I'm sure I'll be making this often, thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb slaw

this recipe supposedly earned its name because it is so addictive and i agree! i absolutely love this stuff. you can just eat it with a fork or make lettuce wraps out of the mix. simple and delicious! i say 4 servings here but really, my husband and i could polish off the batch with no problem!

1. brown ground beef and season with salt and pepper to taste
2. remove from pan and set aside
3. heat up sesame oil and saut garlic , onions , and slaw in sesame oil until cabbage cooked to desired tenderness
4. stir in the soy sauce , sriracha sauce , splenda , ginger and vinegar
5. add back in hamburger
6. mix well and serve !
7. serve with additional sriracha sauce on the side for people who want to add spice
demonstrations.review: This is SOOO good! I used red pepper flakes - 2 ts, just the right amount of heat for me but a little too much for my 13yr old son. I use one lb of ground beef but double everything else. I think I could live off this stuff. Thanks for sharing a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
andrea s oatmeal raisin cookies

i love oatmeal raisin cookies, but they have to be homemade. this is the way i make them.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. mix brown sugar , lard , milk , and vanilla
3. stir in remaining ingredients
4. drop the dough by tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheet
5. bake 15 minutes
6. immediately remove from cookie sheet and cool
target.review: don't change a thing in this recipe....just fantastic

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian chicken cacciatore

the smell of this makes me "weak in the knees". ha! italian is my heart.:)

1. sprinkle the chicken with the salt , pepper , and flour , shaking to remove the excess flour
2. heat 4 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large non-stick high-sided frying pan set on high heat
3. add the chicken to the pan and cook until well-browned , about 3 minutes per side
4. transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside
5. save the chicken fat left in the pan , adding enough of the oil to make 4 tablespoons cook the onion and bay leaves over medium heat till tender
6. add the garlic , pancetta , red pepper flakes , and half of the parsley
7. cook for 3 minutes
8. pour in the wine and cook for 3 minutes , stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan
9. add the tomatoes and their juice , the chicken stock , tomato sauce , and browned chicken pieces
10. break the tomatoes into smaller pieces
11. bring to a boil , reduce heat , simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes
12. transfer the chicken to a serving dish
13. cook the sauce 5 more minutes
14. taste for salt and pepper
15. pour the sauce over the chicken
16. sprinkle the remaining parsley on top and serve
demonstrations.review: very good very yummy on a cold day

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chive dumplings

these are the dumplings i use for my recipe #248713.

1. cut the shortening into the flour , baking powder and salt until mixture looks like fine crumbs
2. stir in milk and chives
3. drop onto hot chicken
4. cook uncovered 10 minutes , then covered 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: have with a beef stew and you've got a complete meal very good daved it to my favorites

demonstrations.recipe_text:
joe s chili

my best friend's husband made this up. i only had it once, but i loved it!

1. put cut-up chuck roast in dutch oven with oil , salt , and pepper
2. brown meat
3. add everything else
4. simmer for 2-3 hours on low
5. keep checking it often to stir
demonstrations.review: great to have on a cold winters day warm you to your toes

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic chicken for crock pot

i got a similar recipe of this a long time ago, got bored with it back then, and changed some ingredients. my husband and daughter get so excited when we're gonna have this for dinner. i don't measure some things, so if you need me to explain further, let me know. the liquid is so good that i keep sipping it! ha!

1. put the first 7 ingredients in a crock pot and cook for 4-5 hours on low
2. cook the rice or pasta separately
3. when chicken is done , remove the bones and skin and throw them away
4. put either rice or pasta in a bowl and then ladle the balsamic chicken on top with some of the liquid from the crock pot
demonstrations.review: when I cook this...they come running..great dish never any left overs

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with balsamic vinegar

this is a low-fat way to make chicken with lots of flavor.

1. cut all the chicken breasts in chunks
2. season them with salt and pepper
3. lightly dust with flour , shaking off the excess
4. heat oil in non-stick frying pan
5. lightly brown the chicken on all sides over high heat , about 2 minutes on each side
6. add vinegar and bring to a boil
7. reduce heat to simmer and cook until the vinegar is reduced by two-thirds
8. add the chicken broth and continue simmering , uncovered , until the chicken is tender , about 10 minutes
9. transfer it to a platter
10. boil the sauce until reduced , about 10 minutes
11. spoon the sauce over the chicken and sprinkle with parsley
12. serve over rice
demonstrations.review:
this is the best chicken I ever had
over rice oh my goodness I am just drooling thinking about it
yuuuuummmy

target.recipe_text:
low carb cheesecake mousse

this dessert keeps you on the straight and narrow with your low carb diet and is actually very refreshing. try different flavors, like cranberry.

1. melt sugar free jello in boiling water
2. stir well to dissolve and cool slightly
3. beat softened cream cheese until smooth and stir in cooled jello
4. lightly fold in heavy cream until well mixed
5. pour into serving dishes and put in fridge to chill at least 3 hours
target.review: Finally a low carb dessert that tastes good! Just a little advice, I mixed up my recipes while I was making it, I used 1/2c. water intsead of the 1/4c. like it called for. When you use 1/2c. it turns more into a firm jello. So next time I will for sure only use a 1/4c. of water. Thanx for the idea.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
anne of green gables raspberry cordial

this recipe is from the anne of green gables cookbook by kate macdonald. 

1. put the unthawed raspberries into a saucepan and add sugar
2. cook on medium , stirring occasionally until all the sugar ahs dissolved
3. using a potato masher , mash the raspberries and syrup thoroughly
4. pour the mixture through a strainer , extract all the juice
5. squeeze two of the lemons and strain the juice , add it to the raspberry juice
6. add the boiling water to the raspberry juice
7. allow the cordial to cool , then chill it in the refrigerator
8. serve cordial with a thin slice of lemon in each glass
demonstrations.review: I have to confess, the idea of the Raspberry Cordial had me so excited. I have been a huge fan of Anne of Green Gables since I can remember. This is a little time consuming to make, and the taste is very different.  I can't decide if I like it or not. It's unlike anything I have ever had before in my life.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chicken crescent roll casserole

this will also work great with turkey; if you do not have chicken breasts, then use any leftover cooked chicken. if desired you can fill the crescents just with the filling mixture and omit the soup, just brush with butter before baking. they are wonderful just stuffed with the filling! a few members have experienced a soggy bottom, so you might want to consider just drizzling half (or even a little less) of the soup mixture on top and a little around the sides of the crescents, then save the rest of the soup mixture for another time (this will help prevent a soggy bottom). you may use the jumbo crescent rolls and stuff with more chicken mixture :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. butter a casserole dish
3. in a saucepan , mix half and half cream , 3 / 4 cup grated cheese and undiluted chicken soup
4. heat just until the cheese melts
5. for the filling --- in a bowl , mix the soft cream cheese with butter until very smooth , then add in garlic powder
6. add in the chopped chicken , onion and cheddar cheese
7. mix well until combined
8. add in 2 tablespoons whipping cream or mayonnaise
9. mix to combine
10. season with seasoned salt or white and black pepper to taste
11. unroll the crescent rolls
12. place 1 heaping tablespoon chicken mixture on top of each crescent triangle , then roll up starting at the thicker end
13. drizzle a small amount of soup mixture on the bottom of the dish
14. then place the crescent rolls seam-side down on top of the creamed mixture in the casserole
15. drizzle the remaining sauce on top and sprinkle with 1 cup grated cheese , or amount desired
16. bake for about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Not sure if this was my favorite meal. I didn't put the cream sauce on the bottom of the casserole dish just buttered it. I have to say it's really filling meal though. Just not one of my favorites.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pepsi pork roast

this recipe sounds strange and tastes wonderful. we have experimented with other brands of soda, but none worked as well. you can also cook potatoes and carrots with the roast for a complete meal.

1. place roast in crock pot
2. mix soup mix with soup
3. add cola to soup mixture and pour over roast
4. cook on high for 4-5 hours
5. when done , remove roast and thicken juices with cornstarch for wonderful gravy
demonstrations.review: Sheer Perfection! I followed the recipe except used coke instead of pepsi (we're a coke family). after 8 hours of low heat crock pot cooking it removed the roast, poured the liquid into pan and thicken with corn starch, alittle extra salt, pepper and garlic powder and it was good to go. Cut up roast ( I could have used my hands it was so tender) placed the meat into the skillet with the thicken liquid/gravy and let it simmer on low heat until my husband got home; the picky eater who went back for 3rd which is a feat in itself. In 6 years I've never seem him do that! Thank you Mysterygirl!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon cheeseburger potato pie

my husband and father-in-law love this! it's a bit time-consuming, but worth the spectacular results. truly a handsome dish! from one of those pillsbury mini-magazine things you buy at the supermarket. please note that you can use leftover mashed potatoes as well, or make homemade if you really hate instant!

1. heat oven to 375 degrees f
2. combine ground beef , breadcrumbs , onion , ketchup , mustard and salt and mix well
3. press hamburger mixture in bottom and up sides of an ungreased 9 inch pie pan to cover completely
4. bake in preheated oven for 15 minutes
5. while meat mixture is baking , cook bacon until crisp
6. drain on paper towel , cool , and crumble
7. discard bacon drippings or save for another recipe
8. in a medium sauce pan , combine water , margarine and garlic salt
9. bring to a boil
10. remove from heat and add milk
11. with a fork , stir in potato flakes
12. then stir in 1 / 2 cup of cheddar cheese
13. remove partially baked"crust" from oven , pour off any fat
14. spoon potato mixture into crust evenly
15. return to oven for another 10-15 minutes or until meat is thoroughly cooked , and potatoes are heated through
16. remove pie from oven
17. top with tomato , remaining cheese and crumbled bacon
18. return to oven , and bake for 5 minutes longer , until cheese is melted
19. remove from oven , top with green onions
20. let stand 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good. I would have liked the "hamburger crust" to be a little more cooked through. I like my hamburger meat WELL done. Next time I'd cook the crust longer for my taste. I also used real mashed potaotes as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cake mix christmas cookies

this is quick and easy! chilling makes handling these easier.  option for a lemon glazed cookie--all you have to do is in place of the water use the frozen lemon concentrate for a real tart cookie and/or use lemon cake mix. then mix a bunch of powdered sugar with the frozen lemon contentrate thats at room temperature for a nice tart icing!
pictures uploaded here on nov 27 using carrot cake mix, 1/4 cup coconut, 1/4 cup chopped nuts then sprinkled with cinnamon sugar before and after baking.
dec 10 used chocolate cake mix and chocolate mint chips.

1. mix all together
2. shape in 1" balls and roll in powdered sugar
3. you may want to chill dough before rolling
4. place on parchment lined baking sheet
5. bake 10-12 minutes at 375f
demonstrations.review: No need to wait until Christmas to make these cookies. The possiblities are ENDLESS!! I made strawberry (cake mix) with chocolate chips, my 3 yr old son helped, and had alot of fun. PLUS! he kept stealing them after they were cooked so I know he liked them :o)

target.recipe_text:
gingerbread  for cookies or a  gingerbread house

this dough is very easy to work with.  we use this gingerbread to make our annual gingerbread houses.  one recipe makes 3 fair sized gingerbread houses.  this is also works excellent for gingerbread people. from good housekeeping dec 94

1. in a medium saucepan , heat sugar , molasses , ginger , allspice , cinnamon , and cloves to boiling , stirring occasionally
2. remove from heat
3. stir in soda
4. stir in margarine till melted
5. with a fork , stir in egg , then flour
6. on a floured surface , knead dough till mixed
7. divide dough in half , wrap half with plastic wrap
8. set aside
9. roll half the dough , with a rolling pin , slightly thinner than 1 / 4 inch
10. cut with cutters
11. bake at 325f on a cookie sheet for 12 minutes
12. cool on a wire rack
13. makes about 3 dozen 3" gingerbread people
target.review: WOW!!!  This is the ONLY gingerbread recipie I'll ever need!!!  I made 5 batches (yup, 5) today for a 'house' party I'm having.  No substitutions needed, easy dough to work with (great for 4 yr olds), great flavor and texture!  I did cut windows and used crushed butterscotch candies for that 'glow from within' look.  I'll send pics of the finished masterpieces...thanks SO much for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese ball with everything

this savory variation belongs in every serious cook's repertoire. serve these to a crowd you want to impress! caution..this makes alot, the two small balls are as big as baseballs! i have been making these for years from a recipe i clipped from a magazine and they are always a hit. cook time is chill time.

1. let swiss and cheddar cheeses come to room temperature
2. in a large bowl beat together cream cheese and sour cream till fluffy
3. beat in swiss cheese , cheddar cheese , onion , undrained pimiento , pickle relish , half of the bacon , 1 / 4 cup of the pecans , salt and pepper
4. cover and chill till firm
5. shape into 1 large or 2 small balls on wax paper
6. in a small bowl combine remaining bacon , pecans , parsley , and poppy seeds
7. turn mixture out onto clean clean sheet of waxed paper
8. roll cheese balls in seed mixture to coat
9. wrap and chill
10. let stand 30 minutes at room temperature before serving
11. serve with crackers
demonstrations.review: very good...this was my man's favorite cheese ball last night for new year's eve!  thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oreo balls

my sister's co-worker brought these to a party and they were quite a hit. i don't know where the recipe came from originally.

"bark" is an artificial chocolate or vanilla candy coating/confectioner's coating used to make a treat called almond bark and can be found at most grocery stores near the chocolate chips. 

you can use chocolate chips and white chocolate chips if you don't have almond bark, but i have found that almond bark melts better and is easier to work with.

1. using a blender or hand held mixer , mix oreos and cream cheese together
2. roll into walnut size balls
3. chill for an hour
4. melt approximately 3 / 4 package of white almond bark
5. stick a toothpick in an oreo ball and dip it in the melted white almond bark
6. allow to harden on wax paper
7. takes about 15 minute
8. while waiting , melt about 1 / 4 package of chocolate almond bark
9. when oreo balls are no longer sticky to the touch , decorate with drizzles of chocolate and white almond bark
10. i just use a sandwich bag with a tiny hole cut in one corner to drizzle the almond bark
