demonstrations.review: Had to rename this for my 4 yr old, who really really wanted COAL for his Thomas the trains for Christmas...Zachariah's Lumps o' Coal...LOL  Big hit in all my goodie boxes this year.  Will become a staple on the goodie list!  I dipped them in candy quick - smoother and not as thick as regular choco chips.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed potatoes with ham

my polish grandmother could work magic with a few simple ingredients. a refreshing change from the the complex and highly seasoned foods of modern cuisine.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. beat egg yolks with mashed potatoes and season with salt and pepper
3. add sour cream and ham
4. beat egg whites until stiff and fold into potato mixture
5. place in a buttered casserole , dot with butter and bake 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Went looking on the 'zaar for something to do with leftover ham the other night.  This is what I found and it's delish!!!  My men didn't even know that they were eating leftovers...LOL

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry cardamom cookies

these are a very soft delicious cookie. i made 8 dz for a cookie exchange at christmas last year and they were a hit. these have to be one of the family's favourite. the first batch was gone in no time. the cream cheese adds a nice flavour to this cookie. if you like cherries you can add more by pressing 3 or 4 dried cherries into the tops of cookies before baking.

1. heat oven to 350 f
2. toss chopped cherries and 2 tbsp flour: set aside
3. beat butter , sugar and cream cheese in large bowl with electric mixer on medium speed until fluffy
4. beat in egg , buttermilk and vanilla
5. beat in 2 1 / 3 cups flour , the cardamom , baking powder and baking soda on low speed just until flour is moistened
6. stir in cherries
7. shape dough into 1 inch balls and place 1 1 / 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet
8. bake 12 to 14 min or until bottoms are light golden
9. remove from cookie sheet to wire rack
10. cool
11. sprinkle with powdered sugar
demonstrations.review: Very good!  We love cardamom and this was something new.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish soda bread 1

i just love it!!!!!!!!!!!!!! you tell me what you think????!!! filled with dried cranberries and raisins and flavored with the black caraway seeds are so good. you can use regular but the black tops this. these black seed is also known as black cumin, habbatul baraka (the blessed seed), and by its botanical name "nigella sativa".

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. pump up dried fruit:
3. place raisins and cranberries in a glass bowl 1 / 4 cup pour water or whiskey over it
4. cover with plastic wrap or paper towel and microwave it for 1 minute
5. let sit to cool
6. add salt , baking powder , sugar , and flour to food processor and pulse 3 times to sift
7. add the buttermilk , butter and eggs and mix till it comes to a doughy ball
8. mix in seeds and drained raisins , and cranberries
9. you may need to do this step by hand
10. don`t worry if you can knead the dough into a ball it still will be very good
11. at times my dough is moist because of moisture in the air
12. place the dough into a well buttered pan using hands well floured shaping the dough
13. pat down in center for even baking
14. mark a cross on top and brush with more melted butter
15. bake in 350 degree oven for 50-60 minutes
demonstrations.review: So delicious!!!  I finally have gotten around to posting after making this many many times.  I omit the cranberries as I usually don't have on hand.  Even my mother, who swears by her recipe, asked me for this recipe!  A great way to use up that last bit of buttermilk.  I serve this with pork roast & saurkraut (both with tons of caraway).  BTW - I just shape a flattened ball on a cookie sheet.  Thanks for sharing!  (ps - I'm a Rita too)

target.recipe_text:
shredded potato baskets with cheese and bacon  5fix

5-ingredient fix contest entry - this is my tasty version of a popular appetizer served at a local restaurant.  the crispy yet chewy "baskets" made with the shredded potatoes (hashbrowns) takes this side dish to the next level and is a family favorite.

1. heat oven to 375 degrees f
2. generously coat 2 6-compartment non-stick muffin tins with cooking spray
3. set aside
4. in a large bowl , combine the potatoes , egg and flour , adding just enough flour so mixture "sticks together"
5. divide evenly among the prepared muffin compartments
6. using the back of a spoon , firmly press potato mixture into bottom and up sides of each compartment , making a "well" in each
7. place in oven and bake for 20-25 minutes or until just starting to brown
8. remove from oven and divide shredded cheese evenly among cups and top each with crumbled bacon
9. return to oven and bake another 5-10 minutes or until "baskets" are golden brown and cheese and bacon is hot , melted and bubbly
10. remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes
11. to serve: gently run the
12. release each basket and place on serving platter
target.review: These are so cute and amazing! I love it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy potato   italian sausage balls  5fix

5-ingredient fix contest entry.  who knew that 5 ingredients could pack such a punch of flavor!  these little treats scream mama mia that's a tasty tater ball!  they are crispy on the outside and soft and gooey on the inside. they are the perfect appetizer for any occasion. the best thing about these delightful balls of yumminess is that the kids will flip over these as well as the grown-ups.

1. combine potatoes , sausage , cheese , pesto and 1 / 2 cup of bread crumbs in a mixing bowl
2. mix thoroughly
3. with wet hands , roll potato mixture into 1 1 / 2 inch balls
4. place remaining bread crumbs on a large plate
5. roll each potato ball in bread crumbs
6. make sure they are evenly coated
7. place poatao balls on a large plate or pan and put in fridge for at least 30 minutes or until ready to use
8. meanwhile , preheat oven to 380 degrees
9. place potato balls on a large non-stick cookie sheet
10. bake for 20 minutes and golden brown
11. serve with your favorite marinara sauce
demonstrations.review: You are an amazing cook. These sound awesome!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheddar stuffed potato cake and egg  5fix

5-ingredient fix contest entry.  sharp cheddar cheese stuffed inside of a crispy and delicious potato cake.  "egg"cellent plated with an "over easy" egg.  so easy to make and prepare.  have dinner on the table in minutes.

1. 1
2. in large skillet heat oil , medium heat
3. 2
4. open package to mashed potatoes
5. with a knife divide into 10 equal parts
6. 3
7. add shredded hash browns in separate bowl
8. 4
9. drop one piece of mash into bowl of hash browns , pressing lightly
10. add chunk of cheese to center , folding over potatoes to seal
11. flip cake over to cover
12. make sure entire cake is covered with shredded hash browns
13. 5
14. add to hot oil
15. when cake is brown on one side flip and brown on opposite side
16. 6
17. poach eggs , serve one egg on each potato cake
demonstrations.review: Glad the phot is up because this is pretty and sounds delicious too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab ranch gorgonzola slaw  rsc

ready, set, cook! hidden valley contest entry: this is not your ordinary coleslaw.  the combination of the creamy ranch gorgonzola dressing, sweet and succulent crab meat makes this extra special. you will soon make this your 2-go-2 slaw for any occasion.

1. combine dressing ingredients in a large mixing bowl
2. mix well
3. fold in 1 / 2 of the crab meat , tomatoes , parsley and chives
4. chill in fridge for at least 1 hour
5. when ready to serve , top slaw with remaining crab meat and fried garlic
demonstrations.review: My tounge is dancing in my mouth with anticapation of eating this recipe!~ Roberta

demonstrations.recipe_text:
california bacon ranch pizza  rsc

ready, set, cook! hidden valley contest entry.  a delectable pizza with an avocado ranch white sauce, chicken and bright notes of tomato and citrus!  i came up with this recipe to use up some avocado for a friend who wanted something a little different!

1. pre-heat oven to 350f
2. in a heavy skillet , heat olive oil
3. while oil is heating , season chicken with salt , pepper , and lemon zest
4. stir well to combine
5. brown chicken in skillet until no longer pink , 6-7 minutes on medium high
6. remove chicken with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels
7. set aside and keep warm
8. mix together avocado , lemon juice , ranch dip mix , mayonnaise , greek yogurt and cream cheese
9. set aside to flavor for 5-10 minutes
10. while avocado ranch sauce is sitting , spread pizza dough out onto a large pizza pan bake pizza crust 6-7 minutes or until just starting to brown on top
11. remove from oven
12. spread avocado ranch sauce generously onto warm crust
13. sprinkle cooked chicken , diced red onion , bacon pieces and diced tomatoes on top of ranch sauce
14. top with both cheeses
15. return pizza to oven
16. bake an additional 10-15 minutes or until cheese is melted and pizza is hot through
demonstrations.review: Great yummy recipe Noelle!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mac  n cheese and spinach strata  sp5

official contest entry: simply potatoes 5fix.  a combination of 2 of my favorite foods, this creamy, cheesy casserole is made with simply macaroni & cheese and layered with chopped spinach.  buttery and cheesy breadcrumbs top this delicious dish and give it an added punch of flavor.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees f
2. coat a 2-3 quart glass baking dish with cooking spray
3. set aside
4. transfer 1 package of the heated simply macaroni and cheese to the bottom of prepared baking dish and spread evenly
5. top evenly with spoonfuls of spinach
6. cover spinach with 2nd package of macaroni and cheese and spread evenly
7. in a small bowl , combine the breadcrumbs , butter and cheese
8. sprinkle over casserole
9. bake for 30-35 minutes or until hot and bubbly and crumbs are just starting to brown
demonstrations.review: This sounds delicious!

target.recipe_text:
blueberry apple crisp

serve this with vanilla ice cream!!

1. combine the blueberries and the apples in a bowl and sprinkle with about 1 tablespoon of the flour
2. toss
3. spoon into 6 custard cups
4. combine the remaining flour and sugar in a bowl
5. cut in margarine until mixture is crumbly and resembles coarse meal
6. add oats , cinnamon and nutmeg
7. sprinkle flour mixture over the fruit
8. bake at 400 degrees for about 30 minutes or until bubbly
9. let stand for 10 minutes
10. serve warm
target.review: Superb!  We ate this warm straight from the oven with french vanilla ice cream.  Just sinful.  I made mine in a casserole dish instead of custard cups and also doubled the topping.  Looking forward to another bowlful later this morning!  Made for ZWT4.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh summer sour cream green beans

this is a very old family recipe. really brings back fond summer memories!!

1. saute onion and parsley in butter , then stir in flour
2. add 1 / 2 cup liquid from beans to flour paste and cook , stirring constantly until thickened
3. stir in rest of ingredients except bacon
4. pour sauce over beans
5. sprinkle top with crumbled bacon
demonstrations.review: I wasnt sure I would care for this very much but OK I can admit when I'm wrong, wrong, wrong!  These green beans were fabulous!  I was skeptical about the sour cream/green bean mix but boy were these a great combination of flavours!  I'll make this one again and again.  Straight to my veggie cookbook for this one!  Made for ZWT4.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven cooked bacon with black pepper and brown sugar

nice and smokey, spicy and easy clean up. if you like it sweet try some brown sugar sprinkled on it too.

1. line a cookie sheet with parchment paper
2. preheat oven to 400 degrees fahrenheit
3. lay bacon on paper
4. sprinkle bacon generously with optional black pepper , chiptole pepper and brown sugar
5. bake 10 minutes then drain fat from pan
6. bake 5 more minutes or until it's as crisp as you like
demonstrations.review: We had this morning for breakfast and with tongue in cheek, I will say that we piggishly enjoyed this very much.  I had never made bacon in the oven before but now I know this is will be the only way to make it from now on.  I did not use the brown sugar because the bacon I use is Maple Syrup Bacon, so it's already on the sweet side and I was afraid it would be too sweet.  Thank you for posting Rita!  Made for ZWT4.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salad with parmesan cheese  salata ma jibna

from the african cookbook, by bea sandler. posted for zwt4.

1. toss salad ingredients together in a large salad bowl
2. whisk together dressing ingredients and drizzle over salad , tossing lightly again
3. serve in small bowls sprinkled with mashed garlic and parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: A nice refreshing salad with a bit of a kick.  Very quick and easy to prepare.  Just right for a summer salad side dish!  Made for ZWT4.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
alberta flank steak

canadian way to eat steak.

1. combine soya sauce , wine , oil and ginger or garlic in a shallow bowl
2. score meat with shallow cuts , criss-cross-style at 2-inch intervals and add to marinade , turning to coat meat
3. cover and refrigerate for at least four hours but preferably overnight , turning occasionally
4. remove meat from bowl , reserving marinade
5. barbecue over medium-hot coals or at medium-high setting , brushing occasionally with marinade , 4 to 6 minutes per side , or until cooked to desired doneness
6. remove from barbecue and let stand for 5 minutes , then cut diagonally across the grain , in extra-thin slices
7. wrap well and chill
demonstrations.review: With only 4 ingredients I was afraid this wouldnt deliver tastewise.  Boy was I wrong!  I was only able to marinate for 4 hours but next time I'll marinate overnight so that more of this yummy flavour will be absorbed.  Simplistic but wonderful!  Only change I made was to increase the garlic as we are crazy about garlic on our steaks!  Will make again.  Made for ZWT4.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted cajun potatoes

these are nice and crispy with just the right amount of kick!

1. cut each potato lengthwise into eight wedges
2. in a large bowl , combine the oil , shallots , garlic , salt , paprika , cayenne and pepper
3. add potatoes and toss to coat
4. place in greased roasting pan
5. bake , uncovered , at 450 degrees f for 45-50 minutes or until tender and golden brown , turning every 15 minutes
6. sprinkle with parsley
demonstrations.review: I love this recipe.  It's a favourite of mine that I first saw in a TOH cookbook.  I've made it many times.  It's so easy to make and super delicious too.  I actually use russet potatoes most of the time because I have those on hand and they are just as good!  Also, I cook them about 10-15 minutes longer because we like ours a bit crispier.

target.recipe_text:
chilekeesh

this is my first recipe post, so i wanted it to be a good one! i adapted this recipe from one i clipped from the l.a. times in 1978. the original recipe called for canned diced green chiles and monterey jack cheese instead of fresh chiles and cheddar. it is tasty both ways. it is a good brunch or light dinner dish. i like to serve it with salsa and sour cream. my co-workers request it when we have a brunch potluck.

1. preheat oven to 350 deg f
2. in oven , melt butter in 8-inch square pan , tilting pan to grease sides
3. beat eggs in a bowl
4. add flour , baking powder , melted butter , chiles , cottage cheese and cheddar cheese
5. mix well
6. pour into prepared baking pan and bake for 35 minutes or until golden
target.review: This is gorgeous!  My hsuband and I were a bit sceptical when we saw how easy this recipe is, but we both loved it!  It's better than regular quiche because it's cheesier and the texture is just lovely.  I don't normally like jalapeno's (I prefer green chillies), but they were perfect in this.  It was especially good straight out of the oven, but we enjoyed the left-overs for lunch the next day too.  Thank you Clare - we will be making this very often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
it s a whole meal keema curry  beef  potatoes and veg

i originally found this recipe in a dutch language curry cookbook, but have changed it up somewhat. it tastes great, is quick and easy to prepare, is an entire meal, and not much to clean up afterwards. i would say the leftovers taste terrific cold the following day, but we rarely have anything to save!

1. in a small bowl or coffee cup combine the turmeric , cinnamon , cumin , cardamom , ginger and chili powder
2. in a large frying pan , saute onion , pepper and garlic in the oil until the onion softens
3. add the spice mix to the vegetable mixture in the frying pan and combine well
4. add the ground beef , stirring well and often to incorporate the spice mix with the beef and brown thoroughly
5. add the water and the tomato paste , again mixing well
6. cook this at a low to medium simmer until most of the water has cooked off
7. mix in the potatoes and the green beans , then the coconut milk
8. simmer till everything is heated through , and serve
demonstrations.review: Great recipe!  I doubled the quantity of tomato paste, addes salt and brown suger for a more intense flavour.  There was enough to feed 2 of us for dinner and have the left-overs in a wrap for lunch the next day.  Yum!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage for those who dislike cabbage

this is so much nicer than plain steamed or boiled cabbage. try it on the cabbage haters in your family and see if it converts them.

1. in a large skillet , heat butter and oil over medium heat
2. add cabbage , garlic and brown sugar to pan
3. saut until the cabbage is limp , about 5 minutes or so
4. reduce heat to medium-low and stir in vinegar
5. cook , stirring very often , for approximately 20 minutes
6. taste and if cabbage is too crunchy for you , continue to cook for a few more minutes
7. add salt and pepper to taste and serve
demonstrations.review: Gorgeous!  Works well with red caggabe too.  I only sauted for 5 minutes since I like my cabbage to retain some texture.  Thank you for this wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lime cayenne mayonnaise

these go perfectly with chicken mashed potato fritters! easy and good with almost anything!

1. stir together all ingredient
2. cover and chill until ready to serve
3. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was very yummy.  Next time I think I'll try to make it with greek yoghurt so I don't feel so guilty about eating so many calories!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic glazed tuna steaks

my brother is a deep-sea fisherman, whenever he gets the chance and brings home hundreds of pounds of tuna! this is our absolute favorite way to fix this delicacy! i make the sauce way ahead of fishing season and store in the freezer. even the kids give it two thumbs up! a fancy way to entertain guests and make it seem like you slaved all day. give thanks to beulah's in port aransas, texas for this winner!

1. wrap bacon around tuna steaks and secure with toothpicks
2. salt and pepper
3. for sauce: combine all ingredients in a sauce pan and heat on medium until reduced by half
4. sauce should be made ahead of time and can be refrigerated up to one week
5. sauce can also be frozen and thawed in refrigerator before reheating
6. when warm and reduced , whisk in one tablespoon of butter until melted
7. spoon some sauce on plate add grilled steak and drizzle sauce over the top
8. grill tuna steaks 4 minutes per side over hot coals
demonstrations.review: I hate to blaspheme - but OMG - that was a fantastic meal!  The bacon was a fantastic addition.  I didn't add as much soy sauce (I ran out) and I pan fried the tuna wrapped in bacon.  I doubled up on the bacon and fried for 4 minues per side on a high heat.  this ensured the bacon was good and crispy, but the thinner steaks were over-cooked so make sure to use thick ones.  The sauce was amazing!!  Thanks Mostrah!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
three cup chicken

this is a traditional taiwanese dish that we always order in our favorite chinese restaurant. i begged the chef for this recipe and he very reluctantly gave it to me! i just made it for dinner tonight and couldn't wait to post this to share it with all of you!

1. heat up the sesame oil in a wok or a large skillet on high heat
2. add garlic , ginger and serrano peppers , stir fry until fragrant , about 2 minutes
3. add the chicken pieces and cook until it's white in color , about 5 minutes
4. stir together the soy sauce , rice wine and sugar in a bowl , pour over chicken
5. bring to a boil , then turn down the heat to low
6. let cook , uncovered , until sauce thickens , about 30 minutes
7. turn heat back up to high and add basil and scallions , cook for another 2 minutes
8. serve over steamed rice
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  We used pale dry sherry instead of rice wine since it's a really good substitute in Chinese recipes.  Also we used one cup of basil and one cup of cilantro.  Lastly, we did all up to step 5 in the morning to let the chicken marinate all day in the sauce and then resumed with step 6 in the evening.  Next time I won't simmer for quite as long so we don't lose too much of the sauce.  Will defintiely make again!

target.recipe_text:
greek feta burgers

a nice alternative to ground lamb, which can be very expensive. serve with cucumber sauce, recipe #492963

i found this recipe online and haven't had a chance to try it yet.

1. prepare recipe #492963 set aside
2. in a medium bowl , combine ground beef , cheese , parsley , garlic , and pepper
3. shape mixture into two 1 / 2-inch-thick patties
4. in a large nonstick skillet , cook patties over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side or until desired doneness
5. i like mine medium to medium rare
6. your choice , of course
7. line cut sides of bun halves with spinach
8. top with burgers , tomato slices , and sauce
9. if desired , garnish with red onion
target.review: I made these tonight for hubby & I. Wonderful flavor! I have to say upfront, I'm not a big fan of Feta... but being mixed into the burger it brought out a new flavor for hamburgers. I did not have fresh parsley, so I used 1/2 teaspoon of dried. I also used pre-packaged salad mix containing spinach. Stupid me... before even tasting it, we melted some cheddar slices on them (sorry, force of habit)... next time I will not :) I toasted some pretzel buns on the flame of my stovetop  (pretzel buns are cheap at Aldi's), and added some pre-cooked bacon (Oscar Mayer) to them. (I did not make the Recipe #492963... but maybe next time. I just used my mustard & mayo dressing). This turned out to be one of the best pan-fried burgers I've had (I normally pan fry or oven bake, and hubby does the grill). Thanks for a new take on a burger. (Made for ZWT9)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s marinated flank steak

another great recipe my brothers & i grew up on...  the outside gets a little but crispy and seals in the succulent juices inside - yum!

it's as delicious the next few days as it is hot off the grill - make a bunch, store in a ziplock in the fridge & snack for days!

1. combine all ingredients in ziplock bag or possibly glass dish
2. marinate steak overnight for best flavor
3. grill on barbecue or possibly broil to taste - i usually eat steaks med rare but i find this tastes best med / med well
4. slice thin against grain
demonstrations.review: This was excellent! I marinated last night, and made this for lunch today. I actually made 2 smallish flank steaks, but there was more than enough marinade for them both. (I turned and tossed them a few times in the baggie over the course of approx 15 hours). I used another reviewers advice and cut the seasoning salt down to 1 tablespoon. I'm glad I did. Between the beef broth, seasoning salt and soy sauce, it was plenty salty! I made them under my oven broiler (since it is storming here), but they worked out great! I sliced one thinly, across the grain, and used it on top of crisp, fresh salads for hubby and I. we both loved it. The other I am saving to have for dinner tomorrow night and eat as a "steak". I plan to make some fried onion slices in EVOO and Lawry's seasoning salt (those are the best) to serve over the top. Thank you for posting such a terrific marinade. I plan to use it again. (Made for PAC - Spring 2013)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
negima   beef scallion rolls

the most difficult part of making negima is said to be slicing the meat thin enough to wrap around the scallions. worth asking a butcher for ultra-thin cut sirloin.  maybe freezing the meat a bit first would make it easier to slice at home.  possibly easier is using pork, chicken, or veal sold as thin cutlets.  with a little pounding they're thin enough.  from bittman's best recipes in the world.

1. start a charcoal or wood fire or preheat a gas grill or broiler
2. the fire should be quite hot
3. mix together the first 3 ingredients , then soak the scallions or chives in the this mixture while you prepare the meat
4. place the meat between 2 layers of wax paper or plastic wrap and pound it gently with a mallet , the bottom of a cast-iron pan , or rolling pin until it is about 1 / 8 inch thick
5. brush one side of each piece of meat with a little soy sauce
6. remove the scallions or chives from their soaking liquid and cut them into lengths about the same width as the meat
7. place a small bundle of them at one of the narrow ends of each slice , on the soy-brushed side
8. roll the long way , securing the roll with a toothpick or two
9. brush the exterior of the roll with a little of the soaking liquid
10. grill or broil until brown on all sides , a total of about 6 minutes for chicken , 4 to 5 minutes for pork or veal , 4 minutes or less for beef
demonstrations.review: Made these tonight for dinner.  Quite tasty, and very easy to make (These are made using the same technique as my Rouladen). I used the Soy sauce/ mirin/ rice vinegar mixture on all of the scallion greens, but then brushed half of them with Soy Sauce, and Teriyaki sauce on the rest. Both were good. I used a thin cut round steak and pounded the heck out of it (just like I normally do). They took about 6 minutes to get done on the grill. I will try and get the pic posted. Made for CQ 2015 Family Picks for LBOB's

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jamaican bbq sauce

this is one of my mom's tattered recipes from her well-used collection. it says 1998 and is from heloise. very nice sauce for chicken, ribs, or whatever. we had this at almost every family gathering by the grill. you can double the recipe and store in the refrigerator for up to one month. cooking time is refrigeration time.

1. mix together all ingredients
2. let chill in refrigerator at least two hours
3. use or store in refrigerator in sealed jar up to one month
demonstrations.review: I'm attempting to review this... again (the first time it did not post). Anyway, I made this a couple weeks ago, and finally got around to using it this past week. I marinated some chicken wings for a few hours in a baggie with 1/2 of the recipe, removed the wings to a sheet pan and then tossed the marinade portion away. While they were baking, I used the remainder of the sauce for basting. I was afraid of them possibly burning from the brown sugar, but they turned out great! The only thing I was a bit leery of was that the recipe called for tomato puree. Depending on which country you live in, it can be confusing. I used tomato sauce, since it already called for catsup. I think that is correct. It worked, either way. Thanks for posting. (Made for Football Pool Week 4 win)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smores fondue  the melting pot

i came across this recipe and i just had to post it.  taste just like the melting pot's.

1. melt the chocolate in the top of a double boiler set over simmering water , stirring constantly
2. transfer to a fondue pot
3. spoon the marshmallow crme into the center of the chocolate
4. do not stir
5. add the rum to the pot and ignite carefully , using a long wooden match or lighter
6. allow the flame to burn out and stir gently to combine
7. sprinkle with the graham cracker crumbs
8. keep fondue warm over low heat
demonstrations.review: I made this to have as a snack during the football games yesterday. It was enjoyed by all (even the grand-kids... LOL... DO NOT PANIC... the alcohol had burned off). A very fun fondue. I used "Kraft Marshmallow Fluff", "Nestle Milk Chocolate", "Keebler Grahams" and "Bacardi" to make the fondue. I served it with whole graham crackers, large marshmallows, banana and granny smith apple slices. Thanks for a nice recipe. I will be using this at our Christmas get-together. (Made for "My 3 Chefs")

demonstrations.recipe_text:
devil dogs

i bake the cookies while my kids are in school and they frost them when come home. kids love them. i got this recipe from a realtor in our area.

1. mix together shorting , egg , and sugar
2. then add milkand vanilla
3. mix again , then add flour , cocoa , salt , and baking soda
4. mix throughly
5. drop by tablespoons on ungreased cookie sheet
6. bake for 10 minutes at 350 degrees
7. filling mix ingresents together throughly
8. add a small amount of water to make it stir easier
9. put filling between between 2 cookie
demonstrations.review: I made this today (expecting the grand-kids tonight). They are not coming, so it's up to hubby and I to rate these. I will start by saying that the cookies themselves are alright, but the filling seemed off. I'm not sure if it was because of an entire cup of shortening combined with the marshmallow fluff, but it just seemed so very greasy. I did not double the filling portion, no need to. It is very sweet, a little goes a long way. I don't think I will try this recipe for Devil Dogs again, but thank you for posting. (Made for My 3 Chefs)

target.recipe_text:
jalapeno popper burgers

oh boy, these are good-good-good! if you like stuffed burgers and poppers, you'll love these. :)

1. mix meat , worcestershire sauce , salt , garlic powder , and pepper
2. shape the mixture into 12 thin patties , each about 4 inches in diameter
3. mix the cream cheese , ancho chili powder , cumin , dried onion , and minced jalapeno
4. top 6 patties with the cheese mixture , spreading it to within 1 / 2-inch of the edge
5. cover each patty with one of the remaining 6 patties , sealing the edges well
6. broil or grill the patties , turning only once if possible , until preferred doneness and cheese is melted , about 10 to 15 minutes
7. low-carb serving: top with a bit of grated cheddar , guacamole , and enjoy !
8. high-carb serving: eat with a bun and other condiments
target.review: These were soooo good. i have made them 3 times!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizza getti

feeding a dozen hungry men or your kids this easy meal is a hit. but make two pans for the guys!! freezes well if there are leftovers.  note:  standard is 1 cup cheese = 4 ounces (1/4 pound) shredded/grated/crumbled cheese

1. cook spaghetti according to package and drain
2. mix eggs with milk and 1 / 2 of each of the cheeses in a large mixing bowl
3. mix with spaghetti and pour into greased 9x13 pan
4. bake 30 minutes at 350 degrees
5. remove from oven and pour spaghetti sauce over it
6. cover sauce with pepperoni slices
7. add the remainder of the cheeses over pepperoni
8. bake 30 minutes longer
9. let stand 5 minutes
10. serve
demonstrations.review: Yummy and super easy. we only had to feed 4. so i split it in half. still will have left overs for lunch tomorrow!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s juicy hamburger burger

we all have our different tastes for burgers i like mine flavorful and juicy this recipe will give you the best of both! see the bottom of the recipe for tips on even more extra juicy burgers! --- making a indentation in the middle of the uncooked burger will prevent the burgers from puffing up into meatballs shapes while cooking and keeps them flat --- do not add any salt into the burger mixture as the dry onion soup already has a lot of salt content, you can sprinkle some on towards the end of cooking if needed, if desired you may add in 3-4 tablespoons of your favorite barbecue sauce to the ground beef mixture

1. in a bowl crumble the ground beef with clean hands
2. add in the dry soup mix , egg , garlic , breadcrumbs or crushed soda cracker crumbs , worcestershire sauce , black pepper and hot sauce
3. using clean hands mix until combined , add in more breadcrumbs or cracker crumbs if needed to just hold the mixture together
4. divide the ground beef into 6 equal patties
5. using your large finger or the back of a small spoon make a shallow dent into the center of each patty
6. place the patties onto a large plate or a small cookie sheet
7. cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for a minimum of 6 hours or up to 24 hours to blend flavors
8. grill or pan fry the burgers as desired until cooked through
9. serve burgers in toasted buns with choice of condiments
demonstrations.review: These were good, not great. I did not have time to let them sit and marinate-that was probably what was missing. That was the only pice that i changed, so i only recommend if you can plan in advance.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s extreme chocolate brownies

if your looking for an everyday run-of-the-mill cake-style brownie then pass this by, this is a a moist chewy extreme chocolate bakery-style brownie that takes little time to make and tastes even better the next day, it's everything a good brownie should be!  --- i have even made these using half brown sugar and half white sugar, the amount of sugar listed will give you a sweet brownie you may reduce the sugar by 1/4 cup or more if desired or if you have a sweet tooth use amount stated --- add in a couple of tablespoons of coffee-flavored liqueur in place of the vanilla if desired -- according to a reviewer oil may be used in place of the butter successfully --- these brownies freeze very well,  they are so simple to make just mix everything by hand, they bake out so rich and sinful! --- see recipe#89207

1. set oven to 325 degrees f
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. in a heavy saucepan , bring butter , sugar and water to a boil , stirring constantly until the butter is melted and sugar is dissolved
4. remove from the heat , with a wooden spoon , stir in 2 cups chocolate chips until melted
5. cool slightly , beat in vanilla
6. in a mixing bowl , whisk eggs , gradually add in the chocolate mixture , beating with a wooden spoon until completely mixed
7. mix together flour , baking soda and salt
8. add to the egg / chocolate mixture
9. mix well to combine
10. stir in the remaining chocolate chips
11. spread into prepared baking pan
12. bake for 35-40 minutes
13. cut into squares
demonstrations.review: YumYum! this was delicious and easy to make it. I split it in half because we didnt need that many-totally wish i had made the whole recipe. these were the first thing gone!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sour cream and ground beef layered casserole

this is a great casserole that i have been making for years, it's one of my family's favorite dishes. feel free to adjust all ingredient amounts to suit taste. i usually season the ground beef/onion mixture with seasoned salt and add in some cayenne pepper for heat but that is optional.

1. set oven to 350f
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. in a large skillet , cook the ground beef with onion , garlic and chili flakes over medium heat until meat is browned and no longer pink
4. drain fat then stir in the parmesan cheese
5. add tomato sauce and sugar
6. bring mixture to a boil
7. cover , reduce heat and simmer for about 30 minutes stirring occasionally
8. transfer meat mixture to a greased baking dish
9. set aside
10. in a bowl beat cream cheese and sour cream at low speed until smooth
11. add in green onions then stir to combine
12. spread the cream cheese mixture over the ground beef in the dish
13. top with cooked noodles , then sprinkle the shredded cheddar cheese over the noodles
14. sprinkle with paprika
15. bake for 25-30 minutes or until hot and bubbly
demonstrations.review: This was ok. Everybody ate it, but noone ate the leftovers. i used rice instead of noodles-we arent usually noodle eaters. maybe that would have made a difference.  I am stll a huge fan of Kittencal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: very easy and very good. served over rice!

target.recipe_text:
simple oatmeal cookies or cowboy cookies

these are some cookies that i made for my sil when she was having issues with fibre in her diet.  she was encouraged to have oatmeal and so i tried to find her a "good" oatmeal cookie.  this was attempt number two.  this recipe is adapted from the fannie farmer cookbook.  i have included two versions of a great cookie.  when i make the cowboy cookies, i make them big.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. to make simple oatmeal cookies: mix the flour , baking soda , cinnamon and salt together in a large bowl
3. stir in the remaining ingredients
4. arrange by teaspoonfuls on unbuttered cookie sheets
5. leave about 1 inch in between
6. they do spread a wee bit
7. not too much though
8. bake until the edges are brown , about 10-12 minutes
9. for cowboy cookies: add in coconut and chocolate chips when you add in the rest of the ingredients
10. drop them by the full tablespoon on a cookie sheet
11. bake for 14-17 minutes or until mostly brown
target.review: These cookies are awesome. I made the cowboy cookies and everyone raved about them. I will be making these on a regular basis. Thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana oat muffins

nan

1. combine first 6 dry ingredients in large bowl
2. mix well
3. beat egg , banana and melted butter together in small bowl until smooth
4. add banana mixture to dry ingredients
5. stir just until moistened
6. stir in nuts , if desired
7. fill greased muffin cups almost full
8. bake at 375f for 20-25 minutes , or until top springs back when lightly touched
demonstrations.review:
All I can say is YUM THESE ARE THE BEST MUFFINS EVER!!!!
I make them exactly as the recipe states. The only thing is we don't have those particular oats where I'm from so I just use whatever brand I have on hand. I don't think you could improve on these - they are already perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon muffins

muffins are good anytime of the day.

1. mix flour , sugar , baking powder , salt , nutmeg and allspice
2. add egg , milk and butter
3. stir into dry ingredients until moistened
4. spoon into greased or paper-lined muffin cups
5. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes or until done
6. for topping combine sugar and cinnamon
7. brush top of warm muffin in butter and dip top of muffin into sugar / cinnamon mixture
demonstrations.review:
Yum yum yum. These were absolutely delicious!!!
The only changes I made were to add a teaspoon of cinnamon as suggested by previous reviews and increased the sugar by a quarter of a cup. Excellent muffins

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moroccan chickpea and vegetable stew with couscous

this is delicious stew. very flavorful from the spices, but not too spicy, just right. there is no meat in it, and you most likely won't miss it, as the chickpeas are very "meaty" themselves. but i don't see why you couldn't add some meat if you really wanted to. it also goes from prep to table in about 30 minutes, great for weeknight dinners. from cooking light.

1. heat the oil in a large skillet on medium high heat
2. add the zucchini , onion , carrot and garlic
3. saute 5 minutes
4. stir in the broth , and the next 9 ingredients , and bring to a boil
5. cover , reduce the heat , and simmer for 8 minutes or until tender
6. stir occasionally
7. while the stew simmers , bring the 1 1 / 2 cups water to a boil , stir in couscous , and remove from heat
8. cover and let stand for 5 minutes
9. serve stew over couscous
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this. I try to make 2 to 3 vegetarian recipes a week and this one fit the bill nicely. I added extra spices as we like a stronger flavour and a pinch of sugar. It was delicous and everyone including my toddler ate a hearty portion. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry yogurt muffins

a nice simple recipe for a fruited muffin, this time strawberry...my sister is a strawberry fanatic and always asks for this when she comes for a visit...this recipe has been updated to substitute oil for the butter and substitute egg beaters (egg whites) for the whole egg...it may seem (to some) a little denser than the usual muffin but its an excellent breakfast or snack item nonetheless :d

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. in med bowl , stir together all flour , baking soda , baking powder , salt and sugar
3. in sm bowl , beat together egg beaters , vegetable oil and yogurt
4. gently fold yogurt mixture into flour mixture until completely incorporated
5. do not beat
6. fold in strawberries , lemon rind and walnuts
7. spoon batter into 9 well-greased muffin cups
8. chill in refrigerator 1 hour
9. bake muffins in preheated 400f oven for 25-30 min until they are golden brown
10. remove from oven
11. let muffins stand 5 min , then turn out of pan
12. serve warm or at room temperature
13. variations: change the flavor of the yogurt to something else for a two fruit flavored muffin
14. we stand by this recipe , unequivocally
demonstrations.review:
These muffins were so delicious and very easy to make. I followed the recipe exactly except I left out the nuts so my young toddler could eat them. I will be making this again and would even like to try this recipe with some different fruit as I feel it would adapt itself well to other flavours. Definitely a keeper!

I wrote the above in Jan 2006 and am editing today - Feb 2008... When I orginally made this the recipe called for real egg and fresh strawberries. Also, if memory serves, it had butter not vegetable oil and the yoghurt was natural. I can't find my original print out but I would love to see the option of those ingredients returned to the recipe. It was delicious as it was and I will continue to make it as I remember.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thanksgiving pumpkin pie  uses fresh pumpkin

this is the one pumpkin pie recipe i keep coming back to year after year. i was at a military ladies' coffee when i first tasted this pie, and it was the most moist & eggy pumkpin pie i had ever eaten. i asked the hostess, barb, for the recipe, and she shared the recipe with me - which i believe came from her mother. i made my own changes to the recipe over the years and now i have written down my changes so that i can share my version with you. i only use fresh pumpkin in this recipe and it is well worth the little bit of extra effort. please note: this recipe calls for a deep dish pie plate and intended to be a egg custard textured pie.  even using a deep dish pie plate, you may still find you have a small amount of extra batter, as some deep dish pans are larger and deeper than others (mine fits all of the batter in one pie). you can use whole milks in this if you prefer, however i like the lighter taste of the skim in this. if you only have small pie plates, then you might want to prepare an extra pastry round and divide the batter between two smaller pies.

1. preheat oven to 400f and have ready a pie shield and a large rimmed cookie sheet
2. line a deep dish glass pie plate with the pie pastry round , fluting the edges decoratively as desired
3. combine in order the pumpkin , sugar , salt , cinnamon , ginger , nutmeg , and cloves
4. lightly beat eggs together with both milks , then add to the pumpkin mixture , stirring well to combine--it will be rather thin
5. pour as much filling as you can into unbaked pie pastry and bake at 400f for 50 minutes
6. if there is any extra filling use to fill a smaller mini pie plate or discard
7. if the pie edges start overbrowning , place a pie shield or a ring of foil over the edges--this will be needed or not depending on the type of pastry you use
8. pie should be served chilled and should be stored in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: My first attempt at a pumpkin pie and I have to say it was a total success. I made 2 pies out of this and recieved many complements from all those who partook of its glorious flavours -lol.

target.recipe_text:
green salad with dried figs and nuts

from the oct. 23, 2009 issue of athens plus magazine.

1. cut greens into large pieces and place in a bowl
2. add the shallots and mix
3. add half the figs and walnuts
4. put all the dressing ingredients in a glass jar , close the jar tightly and shake until well blended
5. pour the dressing over the salad , mix well and transfer to a platter
6. sprinkle the rest of the figs and walnuts on top and serve immediately
target.review: Very nutritius and delicious salad. The figs and walnuts blend well with the lemon-honey dressing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yellow confetti rice salad

turmeric gives the rice its yellow color. striking looking salad.

1. in a saucepan , heat the oil over low heat
2. add rice
3. stir to blend
4. sprinkle with turmeric and cumin
5. stir to coat
6. add in the water and salt
7. bring to a boil
8. stir once
9. cover and cook over medium-low heat , without stirring , for about 15 minutes or until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender
10. let the rice stand , uncovered , until cooled , about 20 minutes , do not stir
11. meanwhile , to make the dressing: in a small bowl , whisk the oil and lemon juice together
12. add the dressing , green onions , and bell peppers to the cooled rice
13. stir gently to combine and you are ready to serve
demonstrations.review: Yummy! Very good salad and easy to make and perfect for lunch or barbecue.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuscan bread salad  panzanella

this is the family recipe, from italy. it's very different from the others i've seen here, so i decided to post it.  crucial elements: extra virgin, first press, unfiltered olive oil and fresh mozzarella.

1. boil a large pot of water , and dip the tomatoes in for five seconds each
2. peel while still warm
3. seed the tomatoes , and cut into chunks
4. put them in a large bowl , sprinkle lightly with salt , and set aside for five minutes
5. add the bread , mozzarella , basil , parsley and garlic to the tomatoes in the bowl
6. sprinkle with salt and pepper , toss
7. beat the vinegar into the olive oil
8. add water until you have two cups of liquid
9. pour the liquid over the bread salad
10. at this stage it should look pretty wet
11. add a little more water if it doesn't
12. toss well , cover the bowl with a towel , and set aside for an hour
13. taste and adjust salt and pepper
14. serve as a side dish with grilled meat
demonstrations.review: Ah, where shall I begin: loved the taste, loved the texture, loved just about everything. This was so good, so easy to prepare!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kiwi jam

goodie, goodie, yum-yum.

1. combine kiwi , pectin and pineapple juice in a large saucepan
2. bring to a boil stirring constantly
3. add sugar , stirring until disolved
4. return to a rolling boil
5. boil hard for 1 minute , stirring constantly
6. remove from heat-skim off foam
7. ladle into clean hot jars leaving 1 / 4 inch head space
8. process 10 minutes in a boiling water bath at altitudes up to 1000 feet
demonstrations.review: First jam i ever tried and it was so easy and so delicious! Even gave some glasses to my friends and all of them loved it as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk bran loaf

fibre, anyone? this is very easy and good, too. sometimes i lose track of the point and replace the raisins with chocolate chips.

1. mix together all the dry ingredients
2. stir in the buttermilk and let stand in a warm place for 1 / 2 hour before scraping into an oiled loaf pan
3. preheat the oven to 350f
4. bake for 30 to 40 minutes , until a toothpick comes out clean when inserted in the middle
demonstrations.review: This bread is truly fantastic, rich taste, very filling and healthy! Exchanged the raisins with pumpkin seeds.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
farfalle tuna salad

i used barilla plus multi-grain pasta that is omega rich. loaded the salad with veggies. this can be a side or a complete meal.

1. cook pasta in salted boil water for 9 minutes add peas for 1 minute and drain well
2. meanwhile place remaining ingredients in a large bowl tossing to blend
3. add pasta and toss to coat
4. chill for at least 2 hours
5. garnish with parsley sprig
6. enjoy
demonstrations.review: I love pasta salads and this one was very good. Made a perfect lunch today. Added a lot of seeds like sesame seeds.

target.recipe_text:
easy roasted potatoes

i usually throw this mixture in the pan with whatever else i'm baking (like a meatloaf or a roast).  it's really easy and great when i'm low on time to make another starchy side.

1. wash and cut potatoes into cubes
2. put potatoes , seasoning , and oil in a bowl and toss to coat
3. put potatoes into baking dish
4. bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour
5. stir half way through to brown potatoes evenly
target.review: Fantastic recipe!  The only thing I would change for next time is I used a glass serving dish to bake them in and I didn't spray the dish first so I had a lot sticking to the dish.  The flavor and color were great though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: To quote my husband, "This is the best meat you've ever made!"  The flavor in this is incredible.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cauliflower polonaise

simple, tasty way to serve cauliflower that lets the vegetable shine.

1. break cauliflower into flowerets
2. cook in boiling water or steam until tender , drain
3. heat margarine until lightly browned
4. stir in breadcrumbs , basil , parsley and seasoning
5. spoon over hot cauliflower and serve
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe!  Simple and very tasty.  I'm not a huge cauliflower fan and my 7 year old step-daughter isn't either, but we both loved it!  I did make a couple of changes based on what I had in the house.  Instead of parsley and Mrs. Dash I used It's a Dilly seasoning and lemon pepper.  I also added a little sale and some lemon juice to the cauliflower before I poured the mixture on top.  Thanks again for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy 5 minute almost cheesecake dessert

this is a wonderful easy dessert and if you chill it overnight it's similar to a very creamy cheese cake but much easier and much quicker to make, you can whip this up in about 5 minutes,  the ingredients may be easily be doubled and baked in a 13 x 9-inch baking pan, see note on bottom --- serve this warm or cold, it  will  "ripen" in  flavor have a cheesecake texture after it is chilled for 24 hours

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease an 8 x 8-inch square baking dish
3. in the baking dish melt the butter inside the oven
4. remove from oven
5. sprinkle the cracker crumbs in the melted butter , stir well
6. press on the bottom of the baking dish to form a crust
7. bake the graham crust in a 350 degree oven for 7 minutes
8. remove and set aside
9. in a medium bowl , mix together the sweetened condensed milk , sour cream and lemon juice
10. spread evenly over the crumb / crust
11. spoon the pie filling evenly over the cream layer
12. bake on lowest oven rack for 25-30 minutes , or until set
13. serve warm or chill overnight
14. this dessert is very good so you might want to consider doubling it -- this can be easily doubled and baked in a 13 x 9-inch baking pan , double the canned pie filling too and bake it for just a couple minutes longer
demonstrations.review: Easy to make and tastes great!  It even gets better the longer is stays in the refrigerator.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peppercorn crusted filet mignon with port jus

a lost cooking light recipe

1. the beef should be cut into four 4 ounce servings one inch thick
2. if you can't find a good port use a sweet red wine
3. cut the butter into small pieces
4. heat a cast iron skillet over medium high heat
5. rub pepper evenly over steaks
6. sprinkle the salt in the pan
7. add steaks and cook 2 minutes each side or until browned
8. remove steaks and set aside
9. stir in port and broth and scrape pan to remove browned bits
10. reduce heat to medium and return steaks to pan then cook for 2 minutes each side or until done as you desire
11. remove steaks from pan
12. add butter to pan
13. stir with whisk until melted
14. drizzle sauce over steaks
15. 1 tbsp jus for each steak
demonstrations.review: Absolutely magnificant!  The combination of the peppercorns with the rich sweetness of the port was unbelievable.  I highly recommend trying this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ant  kelly s london broil marinade

my niece shwana loves this!  she always writes my name "ant" kelly when we play rummy or scrabble - started when she was little and stuck.  
i always make this when we go tubing in wisconsin.  

prep time includes does not include time to marinate.

1. mix all marinade ingredients together
2. lightly score meat in a diamond pattern on each side
3. place meat in a resealable bag
4. pour in marinade
5. squish meat and marinade around to get all the nooks and crannies
6. marinate in refrigerator 2-3 hours or up to 24 hours , rotating occasionally
7. can be frozen in the marinade too
8. 20-30 minutes before cooking take meat out of the refrigerator to come up in temperature
9. cook in the broiler or on the grill on high heat for 5-7 minutes per side depending on thickness and desired doneness
10. i have been asked about roasting temperatures , i have never done this , always grill or broil
11. for camping - place the fresh london broil and marinade in a zipperbag , squeeze out as much air as possible , seal , place inside a vacuum pack bag
12. vacuum pack and freeze
13. put frozen in the camping cooler , after a day or two it is defrosted and can be cooked on the grill with minimal preparation and mess
demonstrations.review: We tried this the other night.  The flavor was great.  I marinated it for about 6 hours - next time I think I'll marinate longer to really let the flavors into the meat.

target.recipe_text:
chicken haleem

serve hot with fried onions, garam masala powder, fresh mint, and coriander leaves.

1. heat oil in a pan
2. put meat in the pan , add garlic , garam masala powder , red chili powder , coriander powder , turmeric powder , and salt
3. cook on medium heat
4. in a separate pan boil wheat grains with lots of water , add salt
5. when the grains become tender and mushy add a pinch of soda and cook further for 15 to 20 minutes
6. now mix the wheat grains with the meat and mix well
7. stir continuously so that both are mixed properly
8. now grind the lentils in a food processor
9. make it into a thick paste by adding 2 cups of water while processing it
10. pour the lentil paste into the meat and wheat mixture and stir to mix well
11. place the pan on a heavy tava or griddle on low heat and cook for 30 to 40 minutes
12. fry the sliced onion in oil and drain on absorbent paper towel
13. when the haleem is cooked , sprinkle fried onions , garam masala powder , fresh mint , and coriander leaves
14. garnish with cumin and ginger
15. keep a little of the seasoning separate and serve with haleem
target.review: I  made 1/2 recipe for dinner today just to give it a try and I now regret I only made a half. I used cracked wheat instead of whole. When dish was almost ready I thought it lacked a flavor and added fried onions,diced chili,cilantro and mint to the dish and mixed it well. That made a huge difference. My husband also liked it. I thought it could also be used without any meat as a vegetarian alternative. Very good for you too:lentils,wheat,can't go wrong. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soutzoukakia  greek meatballs in a tomato sauce

lovely, delicately seasoned meatballs in a tomato sauce done in the style of the greeks from smyrna. this is a warming, hearty dish, great year round, but especially in winter.

1. soak the bread in the wine for about 5 minutes , or until thoroughly softened
2. then , squeeze out and reserve the excess wine
3. in a large bowl , combine the ground meat with the wine soaked bread , onion , garlic , egg , parsley , grated cheese , cumin , and salt and pepper to taste
4. mix the ingredients until thoroughly blended
5. cover and chill for 1 to 2 hours
6. dampen your hands , pinch off small portions of meat mixture , about the quantity of a teaspoon or just over , and shape into approximately 20 oval rolls
7. dredge them in flour
8. heat olive oil in a large frying pan
9. add the meatballs and fry until browned all over , turning occasionally and allowing time for the meat to cook thoroughly
10. remove from the pan using a slotted spoon and set aside
11. strain the oil you fried the meatballs in through a fine sieve into a cooking pan
12. add all the sauce ingredients , and the reserved wine
13. bring to a boil and simmer until the sauce is thick
14. drop in the meatballs , stir to cover all over with the sauce , and simmer covered for 15 minutes
15. serve hot with rice , french fries , or mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: I made my meatballs using ground beef,parmesan and crushed tomatoes for the sause. Meatballs are very delicate and difficult to turn when frying ,they are easily fall apart. I made these meatballs in hope they would taste like the ones we had in Athens 2 weeks ago but they didn't. They were not bad but just did not taste autentically Greek.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sauted green apples and leeks

found this german recipe on one of my favorite vegetarian websites.  leeks & apples go quite well together so i'm looking forward to trying this.  when i do get to it, i'm thinking of adding a bit of fresh sage. posted for the zaar world tour

1. split the leeks in half lengthwise and trim the bottoms , leaving a little of the root end intact so that they stay together
2. wash well several times and dry
3. cut lengthwise into thin strips , about 2 inches long
4. in a medium skillet over medium heat , melt teaspoon of margarine
5. add the leeks and cook until soft , about 3 minutes
6. remove from the pan and set aside
7. in the same pan , melt the remaining teaspoon of margarine and add the apple slices
8. turn the heat to high and cook until the apples are lightly browned and softened , about 3 minutes
9. return the leeks to the pan and toss together to combine
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Good taste but I thought that leeks were a little too chewy. Not sure I'll make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato  basil  yogurt tart

this recipe is made with yogurt instead of milk or cream. with tomatoes & basil in season this recipe makes a perfect summertime meal. best served at room temperature, so it is great to bring along on a picnic. recipe comes from stonyfield farm.

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees
2. in a large bowl , combine the yogurt , eggs , 1 / 4 cup basil , black pepper , salt and parmesan cheese
3. beat well
4. place crust into 9" tart pan or pie pan and trim of excess crust from edges , or crimp edges
5. bake for 10 to 15 minutes , until a very light golden brown
6. pour the mixture into the tart shell , top with tomato pieces , and sliced basil
7. sprinkle lightly with parmesan cheese and bake 20-30 minutes or until cooked , let cool 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Great tasting light and easy to make tart. I did  not have frozen pie shell,so I had to make my own crust,using recepie # 18103. It came out looking exactly like on photo. Next time I will put a little less basil (maybe 1/3 cup).I found that it is hard to taste tomatoes because of strong basil taste. Thanks for the recepie, my husband loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oriental drumsticks

this old favorite is always prepared during the warm summer months for family gatherings.

1. combine all ingredients , except chicken , into a large covered tupperware
2. cover and shake till combined
3. add chicken
4. chill 24 hours , turning often
5. discard marinade and place drumsticks onto 1 or 2 cookie sheets
6. bake in a 350 degree oven for 45 minutes , or till cooked through
7. either serve immediately , or place into a crock pot and keep on low to stay warm
demonstrations.review: Excellent, we liked it a lot. I made the marinade exactly as directed.I give it 4 stars only because I marinated drumsticks for 48 hours in refrigerator and cooked them in my rotisserie,so they can be crispy on the outside and juicy inside. Thank you. Will make it again,super easy and delicious meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frank and potato bake

i like this recipe because it's so simple to make. it's from better homes and gardens low-cost cooking.

1. in saucepan cook onion in butter till tender but not brown
2. blend in flour and salt
3. add milk all at once
4. cook and stir over medium heat till thickened and bubbly
5. add cheese , stirring to melt
6. stir in parsley and mustard
7. fold in potatoes and frankfurters
8. place in a 1 quart casserole
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees for about 35 minutes or till heated through
10. prep time does not include cooking and cooling of the potatoes
demonstrations.review: Good comfort food, very easy to make. I used low fat cheddar cheese, low fat milk  and olive oil spread instead of butter. I also added a little black pepper. It made a nice dinner after a busy day at work.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s marinara pasta sauce  vegetarian

this is a basic simple marinara but big on flavor, it can be ready in 1 hour or you can cook it longer and even tastes better the next day that is why i strongly suggest to make this sauce 1-3 days ahead and refrigerate as the flavors will blend and intensify ---this freezes well so make a double recipe and freeze a batch for the next meal, you may omit the wine but i strongly suggest to add it in, it really adds flavor to the sauce --- please make certain to purchase only good-quality canned italian roma (plum) tomatoes for this it will make a huge difference to the flavor of the sauce ---  all ingredients may be adjusted to suit taste, this sauce can also be simmered for a longer time in a crockpot, throw in some fresh mushrooms also if desired ---  also see my recipe#71273

1. in a heavy-bottomed stockpot or dutch oven heat oil over medium-high heat
2. add in onions , garlic and dried red pepper flakes , basil and oregano
3. saute for about 3-4 minutes
4. add in the tomato paste and stir for 2-3 minutes
5. add in the roma tomatoes with juice and wine
6. simmer uncovered over low heat for 1-2 hours stirring occasionally
7. season with salt and pepper and add in sugar if desired
target.review: this is my new favorite marinara! BF loved it. i let it simmer while i made meatballs (#69173) then threw them in after they cooked. what a great super simple delicious meal! :) definately using again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: this was amazing! bf even asked if he could eat it 2 nights in a row which never happens! thank you for posting. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizza egg rolls

the crisp wrappers and flavorful pizza filling make these taste so good.

1. in a large skillet , cook the sausage , green pepper and garlic over medium heat until meat is no longer pink
2. drain
3. stir in the tomatoes , tomato paste and seasonings
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce heat
6. cover and simmer for 10 minutes
7. uncover and simmer 10 minutes longer
8. remove from the heat
9. cool for 20 minutes
10. stir in cheese
11. place 1 / 3 cup sausage mixture in the center of each egg roll wrapper
12. fold bottom corner over filling
13. fold sides toward center over filling
14. brush remaining corner with egg
15. roll up tightly to seal
16. in an electric skillet or a deep fryer , heat 1 inch of oil to 375
17. fry egg rolls in batches for 1-2 minutes on each side or until golden brown
18. drain on paper towels
demonstrations.review: These were so good! I used pizza sauce I had instead of tomatoes & paste & mixed in pepperoni pieces with the sausage. Everyone is begging me to make them again. Thanks for posting! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wild mushroom risotto

i originally made this as a side dish for osso bucco.  the leftovers were fantastic all by themselves!  mushroom broth or vegetable broth can be substitutes.

1. bring chicken broth to simmer in medium saucepan
2. reduce heat to low
3. cover and keep broth hot
4. melt 3 tbsp butter with olive oil in heavy large saucepan over medium heat
5. add chopped shallots
6. saut 1 minute
7. add wild mushrooms
8. cook until mushrooms are tender and juices are released , about 8 minutes
9. add rice and stir to coat
10. add sherry and simmer until liquid is absorbed , stirring frequently , about 8 minutes
11. increase heat to medium-high
12. add 3 / 4 cup hot chicken broth and simmer until absorbed , stirring frequently
13. add remaining hot chicken broth 3 / 4 cup at a time , allowing broth to be absorbed before adding more and stirring frequently until rice is just tender and mixture is creamy , about 20 minutes
14. stir in parmesan cheese and chopped fresh thyme
15. serve warm
16. you may not need to use all the broth
demonstrations.review: this was so good! i served with bourbon chicken (recipe #45809) and the flavors were amazing! thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic bread

an unusual garlic bread. this one uses mayonnaise. try it, you'll like it! (really)

1. preheat broiler
2. mix mayonnaise , parmesan , garlic and herbs in bowl to blend
3. arrange bread , cut side up , on baking sheet
4. butter generously
5. broil until crisp and golden-brown
6. spread parmesan mixture over bread
7. broil until puffed and golden-brown
8. cut into wedges and serve
demonstrations.review: this is by far the most amazing garlic bread i've ever tasted. bf begs for this with everything. thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: i used beef & pork, wrapped the balls around cubes of jack cheese & baked for 20 min @ 350. wow. these were soooo good! served them with marinara sauce (#136292). everyone loved them! :) thanks kittencal!!!

target.recipe_text:
bisquickie cinnamon rolls

these are soooo yummy and easy. they start with bisquick and there is no yeast involved! truly a delicious breakfast treat, dessert or to serve with coffee or tea. enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. mix baking mix , milk and egg until a soft dough forms
3. turn dough onto lightly floured surface and knead gently until smooth
4. pat or roll dough into an 8 x 10 rectangle
5. combine cinnamon and sugar
6. spread dough with butter and sprinkle with cinnamon and sugar mixture
7. roll up tightly , beginning at 10 inch side
8. pinch edge of dough into roll to seal
9. place sealed side down on an ungreased cookie sheet
10. cut at 1 inch intervals almost through to bottom , using scissors or sharp knife
11. bake about 20 minutes or until light brown
12. mix powdered sugar and water until spreading consistency
13. spread over warm roll
target.review: Absolutely loved them. What a treat to sit down to after a long, hard day. Will definitely be making these on a regular basis.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate orange chocolate chip cookies

these cookies are super-packed with intense flavors.

1. heat oven to 350
2. beat 1 cup sugar , butter , 1 tablespoon grated orange peel and the egg in large bowl with electric mixer on medium speed , or mix with spoon
3. stir in flour , cocoa , salt , baking powder and baking soda
4. stir in pecans and chocolate morsels
5. shape dough into 1 1 / 2-inch balls
6. mix 1 / 3 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon grated orange peel
7. roll balls in sugar mixture
8. place about 3 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet
9. flatten to about 1 / 2-inch thickness with bottom of glass
10. bake 9 to 11 minutes or until set
11. cool slightly
12. remove from cookie sheet
13. cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: Exellent cookies! I must admit though, that I didn't roll them in the sugar mixture. My only problem is that I'm the only one in the family who liked them; they're all such picky eaters 'cos they didn't even try them, the combination of orange and chocolate didn't appeal to them. Can't understand why?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tasty buns

these are so good we eat them plain. no butter needed, though if you want to go through all the trouble of getting it out of the frig and getting a knife, etc. be my guest. actually got this recipe from allrecipes.com (but that was before i found this website...i'll never go back!) ha!

1. mix 2 c flour& yeast
2. in a separate bowl , heat milk , water , oil , sugar& salt to lukewarm in microwave
3. add all at once to flour mixture and beat till smooth
4. mix in enough flour to make a soft dough
5. mix well , then turn out onto floured surface and let rest under a bowl for about 10 minutes
6. shape dough into 12 slightly flat balls and place on greased baking sheet to rise till doubled in size
7. bake in preheated 400 degree oven 12-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Unbelievably delicious! I never thought bread making could be this easy. I can't stop thinking of all the different variations I'd like to try, wholewheat, sultanas, etc. Thanks for a great recipe Yogi.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry crunch

something different to do with cranberries.

1. mix cranberries and apples and place on bottom of ovenproof dish
2. melt margarine in microwave-safe bowl
3. add oats and brown sugar and mix well
4. pour on top of cranberry-apple mixture
5. do not pat down
6. bake at 350 for 30-45 minutes
7. serve warm or cold
demonstrations.review: Great easy and tasty dessert. This is much easier than the crumble that I normally make. I made one small change - I added cinammon to the apple mixture. Thanks Caryn

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bisquick

oh yes, it's a copycat and it works!!! saves $ also. di

1. combine all dry ingredients in a large bowl
2. add the shortening and mix with an electric mixer on medium speed until all shortening is blended with the flour
3. use the mix as you would the real thing
4. pancakes-stir 2 cups of your bisquik with 1 cup milk and 2 eggs in a bowl until blended
5. waffles-stir 2 cups of your bisquik with 1 1 / 3 cups milk , 1 egg and 2 t veg oil
6. biscuts-preheat oven to 450 stir 2 1 / 4 cups your bisquik with 2 / 3 cup milk
7. makes 9
demonstrations.review: This was so easy to put together Di, I always have these ingredients at hand. Now I can get down to trying all the recipes here that call for Bisquick. I just made BisQuickie Cinnamon Rolls (#31607) and they were unbelievable.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salmon with tomatoes

this savoury dish is very popular in andalusia, spain. you can use red pepper flakes (to your taste) in place of the hot pepper and any firm whitefish can be a substitute for the salmon. great with rice and a green vegetable.

1. in a medium sized frying pan , heat oil and saute onions , garlic& peppers over medium heat for about 10 minutes
2. add remaining ingredients , bring to a boil , then lower heat& simmer for 5 minutes
3. place the fish into a greased medium sized casserole dish
4. pour the tomato mixture over the fish& bake , uncovered , in a preheated 350f oven for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was so delicious and so easy to make. I also used slices of salmon fillet, my family don't particularly like the bones. I didn't use the hot pepper 'cos we're not too crazy about spicy food, but I did add some cayenne pepper instead.

target.recipe_text:
excellent carrot cake

chock full of flavor, this is the best carrot cake! it tastes even better the next day after the flavors meld. a tad more time consuming than the average carrot cake, but well worth it!

1. combine first 5 ingredients
2. beat well
3. mix flour , soda , salt and cinnamon
4. add to creamed mixture
5. stir well
6. add carrots , walnuts , pineapple and coconut
7. stir well
8. pour batter into greased and floured 13x9 baking pan
9. bake at 350 for 55 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
10. buttermilk glaze: combine first 5 ingredients in large saucepan
11. bring to a boil
12. cook 4 minutes on medium heat
13. remove from heat
14. add vanilla
15. pour buttermilk glaze over warm cake
16. let cake cool
17. cream cheese frosting: mix cream cheese and butter
18. beat until smooth
19. gradually add sugar , beating until light and fluffy
20. stir in vanilla
21. spread cream cheese frosting on top of cooled cake
target.review: Wow! Are you kidding me? I love carrot cake and this is the BEST I have ever tasted: commercial or home-made. Lasts and tastes great even days later. Couldn't thank you enough. 5 stars X a million.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry feta pinwheels

from ocean spray and very good!

1. combine all ingredients except tortillas , mix well
2. divide and spread mixture evenly among tortillas
3. roll up tightly , wrap in plastic and refrigerate at least one hour
4. to serve cut into 12 slices
5. a nice variation is to add thin slices of ham on top of the spread before rolling
demonstrations.review: Excellent, easy. Would be great with turkey inside also.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: Wow, I made this for 70 people and it was a hit. I had 25 lbs of ground beef and increased the serving units accordingly. I used 1 1/2 cup of yogurt in place of 1 1/2 cup of milk since there is a question of mushiness. I also added some extra herbs, italian seasoned crumbs instead of plain bread, kitchen bouquet. Definately increase the sauce. It goes quickly. The crowd loved it and I had NO leftovers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach balls  appetizer

very handy to have in the freezer for the holidays - easy to make

1. cook spinach according to instructions , drain in a sieve , use back of a wooden spoon to press the spinach against the sieve to get as much moisture as possible out in a bowl combine the spinach , stuffing mix , cheese , eggs , butter , salt& pepper mix thoroughly& roll into small balls 3 / 4 to 1" size
2. place on a cookie sheet& freeze
3. when frozen place in a plastic zip lock bag
4. to serve place frozen balls on a cookie sheet and bake at 350f 10-15 minutes or until lightly browned if you are doing them fresh or thawed only bake for 7-10 minutes
5. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Same as previous comment: thought they would be better, cooled quickly. They were very stuffing tasting and dry. Sorry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet hawaiian yeast bread  bread machine

this is a great bread machine recipe that substitutes pineapple juice for the usual water, making it extra flavorful. the ingredient list is for a 1.5 lb loaf.

1. place ingredients in bread machine container in order directed by manufacturer
2. cycle: white , sweet , no timer
3. setting: light
demonstrations.review: This is excellent and easy! I only had 1/2 cup pineapple juice so use apple for the rest. 1/2 whole wheat flour and 1/2 white. Excellent! Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
unusual dip

first experienced this "bi-zaar" and extremely tasty concoction on a women's retreat. the ingredients seem very strange, but the end result is fantastic! go ahead, be brave, & give it a try!

1. mix all ingredients together and leave in refrigerator overnight to blend flavors
2. serve with raw veggies or crackers
3. preparation time includes refrigeration
demonstrations.review: It looks very unappealing but has interesting flavor. I love that you can make it ahead. Nice texture.

target.recipe_text:
pesto tuna
