i had tuna, but none of the usual ingredients i mix in. i found pesto in the back of the fridge. it's unusual i know, but we really liked the flavour combination, even my husband who hates trying new things :-) note: the cook time is for refrigeration.

1. make sure the tuna is as well drained as possible , i squeeze mine in a sieve
2. mix with pesto and pepper to taste
3. if you want a more"spreadable" consistency , mix in the mayonnaise
4. a little lemon juice adds some zing if you like a more tangy flavour
5. refrigerate for at least 20minutes to allow flavours to meld
6. serve either as a sandwich or on crackers
target.review: This was very good! I used basil walnut pesto since that is what I had. I had some plain and some on a sandwich. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry oat cookies

these yummy drop cookies are quick to whip up and are actually good for you. great for when you want a treat without the guilt!

1. preheat oven to 375
2. in a large bowl , mix the oil and sugars together
3. stir in the egg , milk and vanilla
4. in another bowl combine oats , flour , baking soda and salt
5. add to sugar mixture and stir until combined
6. stir in cranberries and drop by tablespoons onto greased baking sheets
7. bake for 10-12 minutes or until lightly browned
8. cool for a couple minutes and remove to wire racks
9. let cool or enjoy warm !
demonstrations.review: VERY good! I made a few changes, none of which I consider too major. I used 1/4 cup of egg beaters for the egg, soy milk, and rolled oats instead of the quick. I baked them on parchment paper for 10 minutes exactly. I got 29 cookies out of this using tablespoonfuls. They are chewy and very tasty. I do recommend eating at least a couple warm out of the oven. Yum....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
deviled chicken salad

created for rsc#10. if you like tangy, this is for you. eat it on it's own, in a sandwich or atop a nice crisp bed of lettuce.

1. combine salad ingredients
2. stir together dressing ingredients
3. combine dressing with salad
demonstrations.review: I liked this a lot! Nice savory and spicy flavor. I used green olives and would recommend them (if you like them of course). I used light mayo and sour cream, and they worked quite well. Quick and easy too. I served it on whole wheat bread. I would recommend chilling it for at least an hour to blend the flavors. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetable brown rice

this recipe comes for august/september 2004 light & tasty. it makes a wonderful side dish or with all the veggies and nuts it can stand alone as a light main dish.

1. in a medium size saucepan , bring the water to a boil
2. add the rice and basil stirring well
3. reduce heat to low
4. cover and simmer for 45 minutes or until rice is tender and the water has been absorbed
5. in a large non-stick skillet , stir-fry the carrots , onion , and green onions in hot oil for 5-7 minutes or until vegetables are lightly browned
6. add peas and salt
7. cook for 1 minute or until vegetables are tender
8. stir in pecans , raisins and rice
9. heat through
10. please
demonstrations.review: I made this a while ago and I loved it! I did make some substitutions, according to what I had on hand. I used almonds instead of pecans and dried cranberries in place of the raisins.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brownie for one

chocolaty indulgence at in it's simplest form! ((for a lower-calorie version, replace sugar with splenda or other artificial sweetener, and replace 1 tablespoon of oil with applesauce. this eliminates around 300 calories- if you're afraid of losing flavor, try one or the other variation or replacing just half the sugar))

1. combine all ingredients in a mug
2. mix well
3. microwave on high for 45-60 seconds , be sure not to overcook
4. brownie should still be wet on sides and in the middle when done
5. let stand to cool for a few minutes
6. grab a fork and dig in !
demonstrations.review: This is SOOOOO good! It's way too easy. I cut down on the sugar and it was still fabulous. I also added a little vanilla. I made it in a ramekin and it fit perfectly. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetarian burritos

provides the perfect protein combination....beans and corn. this is a recipe from the moosewood restaurant.  (i've updated the # of servings...i agree with longhorm mama....1 burrito is reasonable serving..thanks for the input)  the filling also freezes well.  i make a big batch and freeze the filling in ziploc bags and then assemble and bake when needed.

1. drain the cooked beans and save the liquid
2. saute the garlic and onions in oil for several minutes until onions are translucent
3. add the peppers and all of the spices and continue to saute until peppers are tender
4. cover the vegetables , remove from heat , and set aside
5. mash the beans with a potato masher adding enough of the reserved liquid to reach the consistency of mashed potatoes
6. mix the mashed beans , vegetables , corn , olives , and cheese
7. salt to taste
8. preheat oven to 400f
9. place each tortilla flat on the counter
10. spoon about 1 / 2 - 3 / 4 cup bean mixture onto the tortilla half closest to you
11. roll the tortillas from the bottom up , putting pressure on the fililng so that it will be evenly distributed and will reach the open edges of the rolled tortilla
12. place the burritos , rolled edge down in an oiled baking pan
13. brush will oil , cover with a damp cottom cloth , and bake , tightly covered with foil for 45 minutes
14. uncover the pan , remove the cloth , sprinkle with additional grated cheese and bake 5 more minutes
15. serve the burritos topped with sour cream
demonstrations.review: These were great! I used homemade whole wheat tortillas. I served them with salsa along with the sour cream. I thought that they were even better the next day! Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
herbed corn on the cob grilled in foil

corn already seasoned so this is very easy to take for a picnic.no need to bring butter or salt. just keep corn on ice till ready to cook because the sugar will turn to starch if it sits around. more reason to buy fresh as possible. can be doubled or cut in half. feel free to change the herbs.

1. place one corn on each foil
2. mix remaining ingredient together and rub into each cob
3. wrap foil up around the corn and grill 15 minutes turning often
target.review: We loved this!  I made it for a family and friends barbeque along with some regular "buttered and salted" corn.  Some were skeptical at first but after they gace it a shot- it was a hit!  The sweet and salty tastes together were fabulous!  There are so many different ways to vary this recipe....omitting the sugar and using red pepper, cumin and taco seasoning maybe...hmmmm...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic tomato couscous

we had a potluck to attend where we had been asked to bring a side dish.  i was craving couscous though i knew few (if any) of my friends would be willing to try it.  never mind, i moved forward!  this is a slight adaptation of one i found in one of my favorite cookbooks "500 almost fat free pasta recipes."  and truth be told, i brought very little home and got asked for the recipe!

1. in a medium pan , bring the broth to a boil
2. when it is boiling add the basil and garlic and stir
3. then add the couscous , cover the pan , and remove it from the heat
4. let sit 5-10 minutes
5. chop the tomatoes
6. in a small bowl mix the balsamic vinegar , the oil , and the pepper
7. add the tomatoes
8. when the couscous is ready add the tomato mixture and mix well
9. serve hot or cold
demonstrations.review: Wonderful flavor!  I LOVE couscous and am always looking for a new way to make it.  This was quick, easy and a hit with my family- even my two year old!  You could easily add chopped cucumbers to this or small cubes of mozerella and a few basil leaves for a 'Couscous Caprice' kind of feel!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato and  artichoke chicken breasts

very easy topping to your basic chicken breast - found this in woman's day magazine :)

1. mix flour , salt and pepper in gallon-size plastic food bag
2. add chicken , close bag and shake to coat
3. heat oil in large non-stick skillet
4. add chicken and , turning once , cook 8 - 10 minutes or until golden and barely pink in center
5. remove to a serving platter and cover to keep warm
6. in pan , add diced tomatoes , artichoke hearts and balsamic vinegar
7. bring to a simmer , cook 3 minutes to blend flavors
8. spoon on chicken , sprinkle with parmesan cheese and serve
demonstrations.review: This recipe was fantastic! I used sun dried tomatos (canned in olive oil and patted dry) instead of canned and added my own spices to them.  This recipe will be a consistant for our family.  Wonderful flavors!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baklava salmon  salmon with honey  butter  walnuts  and mustard

one of my friends deemed this "baklava salmon" and the name stuck. the salmon & mustard go well with the honey, butter, and walnuts. we usually serve this with rice and steamed carrots or broccoli.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. line shallow roasting pan with non-stick aluminum foil , or spray with non-stick pan spray
3. in small bowl , blend butter , mustard , and honey , set aside
4. in another bowl , mix together bread crumbs , nuts , and parsley
5. place salmon fillets on prepared pan , sprinkle with salt and pepper , and brush with honey-mustard mixture
6. sprinkle tops with crumb / nut mixture
7. if any remains , press into sides of salmon
8. bake salmon 12-15 minutes in preheated oven , or until it flakes easily with a fork
9. serve with lime or lemon wedge
demonstrations.review:
My family and I absolutely loved this recipe!  I have shared it with a number of people and it makes a lovely and classy dinner when you have company!  This recipe is great every time!
-Megan

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers milk shake  flex or core

this is from a very old weight watchers pamphlet for week one of the diet. i love this milk shake. it's surprisingly thick and tasty.

1. place all ingredients in blender
2. blend until all ice is crushed and milk shake is thick
3. it really does become thick
demonstrations.review: My family thought this was very good for what it was.  I used one cup of Vanilla light soy milk, about 6 ice cubes, 4 packs of "Purevia" (stevia based powdered sweetner like Splenda...maybe I have too much of a sweet tooth but 2 packs didn't make it sweet enough for me) and I also added 2 tablespoons of frozen strawberries.  I know the berries had sugar in them so it added another 1-2 points.  I'll try it again with fresh berries or "splenda sweetened" peaches.  I thought it was definitely worth the 4 points as it was SO good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick butternut squash soup

here's a quick, light and creamy soup that warm you on the coldest night. add some hearty whole grain bread and a tossed salad to make a very satisfying meal.

1. add oil , garlic and onion to large stockpot over medium heat
2. saute for 3-4 minutes
3. add sage , salt , pepper , broth and squash
4. bring to a boil
5. cover , reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes
6. use stick blender to lightly puree , leaving some chunks , or puree half of the soup in a food processor or blender and return to pot
7. garnish with parmesan cheese and more fresh sage
demonstrations.review: My family and I LOVE this soup!!!  My husband, who is "anti-any kind of sqash" requests it regularly.  We buy a 2 pound container of peeled and cubed butternut squash at Costco for $5 and put the whole thing into the stockpot with 4 cups of chicken broth and TONS of dried sage from my mother's garden. After I use the stick blender, I always add a can of washed black beans.  It adds a little something and makes the soup stick to your ribs a bit more. ;-)  Quick, healthy and absolutely FABULOUS!!!!  Thanks for posting!!

target.recipe_text:
tsr version of girl scout thin mints recipe by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com. i love these cookies when girl scouts sell them, and i just found the recipe on tsr! i can't wait to make them, but i thought i'd share them first!

1. combine the cookie ingredients in a large bowl , adding the water a little bit at a time until the dough forms
2. cover and chill for 2 hours
3. preheat oven to 350 degrees
4. on a lightly floured surface , roll out a portion of the dough to just under 1 / 16 of an inch thick
5. to cut , use a lid from a spice container with a 1 1 / 2-inch diameter
6. arrange the cut dough rounds on a cookie sheet that is sprayed with a light coating on non-stick spray
7. bake for 10 minutes
8. remove the wafers from the oven and cool completely
9. combine chocolate chips with peppermint extract and shortening in a large microwave-safe glass or ceramic bowl
10. heat on 50 percent power for 2 minutes , stir gently , then heat for an addition minute
11. stir once again , and if chocolate is not a smooth consistency , continue to zap in microwave in 30-second intervals until smooth
12. use a fork to dip each wafer in the chocolate , tap the fork on the edge of the bowl so that the excess chocolate runs off , and then place the cookies side-by-side on a wax paper-lined baking sheet
13. refrigerate until firm
target.review: I made these a while back seeing as my husband is a thin mint FREAK.  He loved them, as well as I, and the only reason I haven't made them since then is because they are very time consuming, as well as the fact that I have very little counter space to work on.  You know you have to pay for these recipes now!?!?!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
not just another cream of mushroom soup

a friend made this and i was thrilled by how wonderful it tasted. i never thought i would like just mushroom soup. she served it with fresh hot bead and butter. mmmmmmmmmm

1. slice enough mushrooms to measure 1 cup
2. chop remaining mushrooms
3. cook and stir sliced mushrooms in 2 tbls of butter in a 3qt
4. saucepan over low heat until golden brown
5. remove with slotted spoon
6. cook and stir chopped mushrooms and onion in remaining butter until onion is tender
7. stir in flour , salt and pepper
8. cook over low heat stirring constantly , about 1 minute then remove from heat
9. stir in broth and water
10. heat to a boil , stirring constantly
11. boil and stir for 1 minute
12. stir in half-and-half and sliced mushrooms
13. garnish with parsley
demonstrations.review: Very very good, took it to a Thanksgiving potluck, and it was wonderful. It is a thin soup wich I like!  THanks for the great, easy recipe.  I added a dash of Italian seasoning and some cayenne for a little boost of flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry orange muffins

i love the taste of cranberry, and these muffins are an excellent combination of cranberries and oranges!

1. combine dry ingredients
2. stir in cranberries
3. beat egg , orange juice , oil and orange rind
4. add to dry ingredients all at once
5. stir just to moisten
6. spoon into greased muffin cups
7. sprinkle tops lightly with a bit of sugar
8. bake 400f 15-20 mins until lightly browned and firm to the touch
demonstrations.review: I made this with those little "Cuties" mandarin oranges that were about to turn, and rehydrated craisins.  I had 3/4 c orange juice, and 1/4 c heavy cream to bind everything together then placed in a bundt pan.  Yummmmmmy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
waldorf astoria red velvet cake

i haven't even tried it, but it looks good.

1. cream shortening , sugar and eggs
2. make a paste of food coloring and cocoa
3. add to creamed mixture
4. add buttermilk alternating with flour and salt
5. add vanilla
6. add soda to vinegar , and blend into the batter
7. pour into 3 or 4 greased and floured 8" cake pans
8. bake at 350f for 24-30 minutes
9. split layers fill and frost with the following frosting
10. frosting: add milk to flour slowly , avoiding lumps
11. cook flour and milk until very thick , stirring constantly
12. cool completely
13. cream sugar , butter and vanilla until fluffy
14. add to cooked mixture
15. beat , high speed , until very fluffy
16. looks and tastes like whipped cream
demonstrations.review: I'm sorry, but I wasn't crazy about this recipe. I followed the recipe exactly, and it came out too dry for my taste.  I'm an avid baker, and this just didn't hit the mark.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing giant chocolate toffee cookies

these are wonderful and oh so chocolaty! the toffee adds a really nice flavor to the cookies, too. these are big cookies--probably 4" diameter. so, you can make them smaller if you prefer. prep time doesn't include time to chill dough.

1. combine flour , baking powder and salt in a small bowl , whisk to blend
2. stir chocolate and butter in top of a double boiler over simmering water until melted and smooth
3. if you don't have a double boiler , you can use a sauce pan over low heat
4. remove pan from over water and cool to lukewarm
5. beat sugar and eggs in a bowl until thick using an electric mixer
6. beat in chocolate mixture and vanilla
7. stir in flour mixture , then toffee and nuts
8. chill batter until firm
9. preheat oven to 350
10. drop batter by 1 / 4 cupfuls onto parchment-lined cookie sheets , 2 1 / 2" apart
11. bake just until tops are dry and cracked but cookies are still soft to the touch , about 15 minutes
12. cool on cookie sheets
demonstrations.review: All I have to say is that these sound absolutely wonderful!  I will let you know what I think as soon as I try them...  I am excited to try this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best snickerdoodles i have ever eaten

"this must be one of the best cookies i have ever eaten." yep, that's what my mother said the first time i ever made this cookie. it is a great cookie recipe, and not difficult to make at all. i tripled the recipe and took it to school to sell... i sold all of them with in an 80 minute time span to only 4 people. they are good cookies, i can't resist them whenever i make them. and they turn out so nice whenever you bake them, it's hard to make an ugly snickerdoodle. lol. enjoy. (prep time is estimated)

1. in a large bowl , cream butter and sugars at high speed
2. add egg , vanilla , and beat until smooth
3. in another bowl , combine flour , salt , baking soda , and cream of tartar
4. pour dry ingredients into the wet ingredients , mix well
5. preheat oven to 300 while you let dough rest 30-60 minutes in fridge
6. in a small bowl combine topping
7. take about 2 1 / 2 tablespoons of dough and roll it into a ball
8. roll this dough in the cinnamon / sugar mixture and press onto greased cookie sheet
9. bake cookies 10-12 minutes , no more
10. cookies may seem undercooked but will develop
11. don't roll your dough into too big of a ball
12. they may not turn out in that much time if you do that
13. it happened to me
14. lol
15. if the cookies don't turn out , please try again
16. it's a very good cookie , it's just all a matter of getting the cooking time right
demonstrations.review: Incredible, easy, crispy, and chewy.  I will make these again, and again. I make these for my church newcomers, and get many requests.

target.recipe_text:
fire and rice

rice....with a kick!! this is really, really good.  the "kick" in it is determined by if you use 1 or 2 jalapenos.  if you like a little kick-in-the butt, you'll love this flavorful rice! i don't know where this origional recipe comes from.  i've had it for 20 years plus!

1. heat oil in large skillet until hot
2. add onions , cilantro , garlic and pepper
3. cook and stir 5 to 7 minutes or until onion is tender
4. add rice and stir until blended
5. cook 3 minutes sor until thoroughly heated
target.review:
Made for a good side dish...
I used the 2 jalepeno peppers, I will use a 3rd next time or a small whole chilli pepper in the oil to give more heat. Thanks for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marinated goat cheese rounds with crostini

this is a simple appetizer that is meant to be eaten at leisure with friends!  you can make crostini out of day old bread, and you can use any flavor of bread you like, but don't make them too far ahead, they are best served warm. cook time is marinating time. from cooking with caprial cookbook.

1. goat cheese rounds:
2. roll the cheese into a 4" long log
3. slice into 1" thick rounds and place in a shallow dish
4. in a small bowl , whisk together vinegar , garlic , thyme , pepper , olives , and olive oil until well blended
5. pour over the goat cheese and marinate , refrigerated , for 2 hours to 1 week
6. before serving , let warm to room temperature , about 30 minutes
7. crostini:
8. preheat the broiler or grill
9. drizzzle the bread with olive oil , and grill or broil until golden brown
10. when the crostini come out of the oven or off the grill , rub them with a bit of the minced garlic
11. then cut in half on the diagonal
12. serve the warm crostini with the goat cheese
13. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Great use of goat cheese!
Made as written, with the addition of toasted pine nuts.
Great on crostini and as a salad topper!
Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mustard crusted roast new potatoes with shallots and garlic

a flavour packed roast potato recipe which results in crisp and crunchy little new potatoes with caramelised shallots in a wholegrain mustard crust. wonderful for dinner parties as well as bbq's. these are so easy to prepare, no peeling required and they can be prepared ahead of time; just let them sit in the mustard and oil marinade until they need to be roasted..

1. pre-heat the oven to 200c / 400f / gas 6
2. par-boil the potatoes for 3 to 5 minutes and then drain well
3. place the potatoes into a large bowl with the oil , mustard , salt , pepper , shallots and garlic and mix well
4. toss the potatoes well so they are all evenly coated with the seasonings , oil and mustard
5. transfer them to a roasting tray and roast them in the pre-heated oven for 35 to 45 minutes or until the mustard forms a golden crust and the potatoes are crisp and cooked
6. gently toss them in the tin before serving hot with chicken , sausages , roasts , stews or with burgers and pies
demonstrations.review:
Good recipe, but needed something.
The wife, daughter and I all agree.

Maybe some rosemary?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fiery pork loin

pork loin marinated in a spicy chipotle mixture and grilled or rotisseried.  this has some fire to it!  pork can also be roasted in oven.  prep time includes marinating.

1. place all marinade ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth
2. if pork loin needs to be tied , do so now
3. place pork in a large zipper-type plastic bag
4. pour marinade over roast and seal bag
5. turn it several times to get meat covered
6. refrigerate for at least 4 hours , turning occasionally
7. prepare grill or indoor rotisserie
8. remove roast from marinade and put on spit
9. cook roast 1-1 1 / 2 hours , or until internal temperature reaches 150f baste occasionally with marinade
10. let roast rest 10 minutes before carving
11. put reserved marinade in small saucepan and heat to boiling
12. serve with sliced meat
demonstrations.review:
WOW!  Great flavor combinations and I love the heat factor!

Next time I make this  ( and I will ) I will bump up the garlic a little, maybe to 4 cloves.

Cooked this over a fire in the back yard on a spit. I turned it every 15 minutes until it was done.

Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tex mex potato skins

these just scream....football! the guys will love you if you have these ready on monday night!

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. cut baked potatoes in half lengthwise
3. scoop out cooked potato , leaving 1 / 4-inch shell
4. place potato shells on an ungreased baking sheet
5. in a skillet , brown sausage
6. drain of all fat
7. add salsa to skillet , and cook for 2 minutes , mixing well with meat
8. spoon sausage mixture into shells , and top with nacho cheese sauce
9. bake 10-15 minutes or until heated through
10. serve topped with sour cream , some green onions , and a few ripe olives , if desired
demonstrations.review:
One word:

Great!

Used Chorizo from local butcher!

Next time I will add a little Stiton cheese to the sauce with a little hot pepper flakes.

Thanks for a great recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jim s country ribs

this is how my family has come to like "meaty" ribs.  the meat just falls off the bones and is finger licking good. it's also easy to prepare.

1. fill a 12 quart pot 2 / 3 full with water
2. add all ingredients except bar-b-que sauce
3. bring to a boil over high heat
4. as soon as water begins to boil , lower heat to simmer and simmer for 45-60 minutes , stirring occasionally
5. drain off liquid
6. place ribs in a baking pan
7. pour bar-b-que sauce over ribs
8. cover with foil and bake in a 350 degree oven for about 30-45 minutes
9. option: instead of baking in oven , put ribs on the grill and baste with sauce
demonstrations.review:
JIm sorry this review is so late, my machine died and I was unable to post.

These ribs had excellent flavour and texture! I like the boil method to infuse the flavours.
Real nice recipe, will be used often!

target.recipe_text:
easiest mac  n  cheese

the easiest and tastiest macaroni and cheese recipe...so easy my 10 year old can make it! also the only mac and cheese my very picky 7 year old will eat. make sure to use extra sharp cheddar, it makes all the difference. best of all, no need to pre-cook the noodles! adapted from moosewood low fat favorites.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. place cottage cheese , buttermilk , and mustard in a mixing bowl
3. using a stick blender , puree until smooth
4. add cheddar cheese and uncooked macaroni to pureed mixture and stir until well mixed
5. spray a 8x11 baking dish with non-stick spray , then pour mixture into dish
6. in a small bowl , mix together bread crumbs and parmesan cheese
7. sprinkle over top of mixture in the baking pan
8. bake for about 45 minutes , until edges are nice and bubbly and top is browned
target.review: This is a keeper for sure, it's sooo cheesy and sooo easy to make and it always comes out perfectly.  Everybody loved it!  Made one little change:  had no buttermilk so used yogurt instead. Great practical mac'n'cheese and great taste too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sour cream and onion burgers

another betty crocker favorite of mine.

1. heat the coals or gas grill for direct heat
2. mix all the ingredients except the buns and lettuce
3. shape into 8 patties 1 / 2" thick
4. cover and grill patties 4-6" from heat for 10-15 minutes till juices run clear
5. serve with lettuce and buns
demonstrations.review: I don't like modifying recipes and then rating them but this was a minor change, I used leftover onion sour cream dip, same taste, same effect.  Amazing, moist, tasty burger.  One of the best I've ever had.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy sausage and pasta bake

creamy, cheesy pasta with italian sausage pieces. a family favourite and wonderful comfort food!

1. cook and slice italian sausage , set aside
2. lightly sautee green onions , mushrooms and peppers in butter
3. in the meantime cook pasta in generous amount of salted water , drain
4. prepare sauce:
5. melt butter on medium setting in a large pot
6. slowly add flour to make a thin paste , stirring constantly
7. slowly add milk
8. add all cheeses , salt and black pepper
9. simmer until partially thickened , adding more milk if neccessary
10. transfer pasta , sliced sausages and mushroom / pepper mixture to the pot , mix
11. transfer all to casserole dish
12. top with bread crumbs
13. bake at 350 degrees until heated through
14. serve with side salad and garlic bread
demonstrations.review: Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oh my d lux chocolate chip cookies

these are definitely not your standard chocolate chip cookies! they are of the "oh my" variety, which is what you'll say after the first bite! the addition of rice krispies may seem odd, but these are great and a favorite of kids of all ages. an extra plus...this recipe make about 7 1/2 dozen cookies :) (don't worry, you'll have no problem getting rid of them all!)

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cream butter and add sugar , beating at low speed until light and fluffy
3. add eggs and vanilla and beat well
4. combine flour and baking powder and add to creamed mixture until well combined
5. stir in remaining ingredients
6. drop by heaping teaspoonfuls onto baking sheets
7. bake for 10-12 minutes or until lightly browned
8. cool on wire racks
demonstrations.review: Excellent, sweet, crunchy and soft!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange mashed potatoes

here's a nice variation on regular mashed potatoes. i really enjoy them with a pork loin roast and fruit salad.

1. melt butter and saute onions
2. cook peeled potatoes until tender
3. mash and add sour cream and orange juice using mixer
4. stir in onions and salt
5. garnish with orange zest
demonstrations.review: Good but a bit bitter and not very creamy.  I will retry it adding cream and/or something sweet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s ground beef fried rice

a long time family favorite! --- you can substitute the broccoli florets for one 6-ounce package frozen pea pods if desired --- make certain the the cooked ground beef is very well browned and well drained, also make certain to use only *cold* cooked rice, cooking time does not include cooking the rice --- you will love this! :)

1. in a wok or a large skillet brown the ground beef with garlic and ginger over medium heat breaking up into small pieces
2. drain the fat , then transfer to a bowl
3. heat 2 tablespoons oil in the same skillet over medium-high eat until hot
4. add in bell pepper and pea pods
5. cook for 3 minutes or until bell pepper is crisp-tender , stirring occasionally
6. stir in the cold cooked rice , soy sauce and sesame oil
7. return the cooked ground beef back to the skillet
8. toss to combine and heat though , then stir in the chopped green onions
9. season with salt and pepper and more soy sauce if desired
demonstrations.review: Great, easy recipe for leftover rice and inexpensive too!

target.recipe_text:
chicken breasts with hot honey mustard sauce

came up with this after looking at several other recipes.  chicken was tender and quite tasty.

1. in small bowl , mix olive oil , honey , mustard , orange marmalade , paprika , pepper flakes , garlic and stock
2. if you want , use a hand blender to get all the ingredients combined well
3. set aside
4. heat olive oil in large skillet over medium-high heat
5. if breasts are big , cut in half horizontally
6. season flour with salt and pepper , and dredge chicken in flour
7. fry in pan about 2-3 minutes each side
8. pour sauce around chicken and cover
9. lower heat to medium and simmer for about 10-12 minutes
10. remove chicken to plate and pour sauce over top and serve
11. it contains ingredients such as molasses , brown sugar and jalapeno peppers
12. you can use a similar type of mustard if you can find one or just use dijon
13. however , i think that a bold flavored mustard like the one i used is what really brought this dish together
14. if you try this recipe and review it , please let others know what type of mustard you used
target.review: I followed this recipe exactly using "inglehoffer" sweet hot mustard. The recipe is simply delicious. I served it with baked potato and steamed asparagus. Perfect Dinner!!!!  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ro tel chicken spaghetti

easy, easy, easy!!! i got this recipe from an aunt who made it for a family reunion. it has a great flavor and makes alot. very good! does not include cooking time for the chicken.

1. in a bowl mix together the soup , broth& ro-tel tomatoes
2. in a 13x9 greased casserole dish layer as follows: spaghetti , chicken , soup mix , cheese
3. bake in a preheated 350 degree oven until heated through and cheese melts about 30-45 minutes
4. as soon as you remove from the oven stir to mix well , adding salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: Thank you for this recipe. I had not ever eaten chicken spaghetti let alone made it. It was delicious and very easy to make. I followed the recipe exactly.Thank you again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
camper s hobo dinner

my kids had this at their summer camp. my version's a bit easier, they had to peel the potatoes with their teeth!

1. place veggies and hamburger pattie in middle of large sheet of aluminum foil
2. sprinkle with seasoned salt
3. bring up the two long sides of the foil to meet above the food , fold the foil several times until it is snug against the food
4. fold the short ends of the foil several times until snug against the food
5. this will seal the food in and prevent leakage
6. place package directly on hot charcoal and cook for about 15 to 20 minutes each side
7. make as many packages as needed
demonstrations.review:
This is a good dinner especially when only cooking for one. I used a 5 oz. piece of pork loin instead of the hamburger patty and sprinkled with sage and pepper instead of seasoned salt. MMMMMMM good.
Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sauteed salmon

very classy salmon. one we have at least twice a month. this is soooo goood!!!

1. in 12 inch skillet , heat 3 tbsp butter
2. add filets , skin side down , and saute on low heat for about 10 min turning often
3. add salt and pepper to taste
4. sprinkle with lemon juice and dill
5. remove to serving plate
6. add 2 tbsp butter , and cream
7. cook and stir 1 minute
8. pour over salmon
9. serve with lemon slices
demonstrations.review: This was so good. The only thing I did differently was use 1/2 and 1/2 instead of cream. Followed everything else exactly. I will be using this quite often.  Thank you

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon pepper bay scallops

fresh and tangy, perfect with some roasted red potatoes and steamed broccoli.  also very good tossed into a caesar salad, or folded into pasta and vegetables.  this is another one of my college-kid attempts at cooking something that doesn't come from box, and it turned out well!

1. rinse and dry scallops
2. spread olive oil on the bottom of a saute pan , and add minced garlic
3. heat garlic on medium in olive oil until oil is warm
4. add scallops , and turn heat to medium-high
5. season generously with salt and pepper
6. keep the scallops moving for 4 minutes , or until opaque and tender
7. with one minute to go , squeeze lemon into the pan and continue to toss scallops around the pan
8. serve right out of the pan , very hot
demonstrations.review:
Bay Scallops is one of my favorite seafoods. I have made this twice. The fresh taste cannot be beat. The last time I served it with broccoli salad, whole grain brown rice and white wine. It was sooo good. 
Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black eyed pea cakes

got this recipe from southern living. i served these at one of our bbqs and they were a big hit.

1. saute onion in 1 t hot oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until tender
2. process onion , 1 can of peas , and next 4 ingredients in a blender until mixture is smooth , stopping to scrape down sides
3. pour mixture into a large mixing bowl
4. stir in hush puppy mix , and gently fold in remaining can of peas
5. shape mixture by 2 t into 3-inch patties
6. place patties on a wax paper-lined baking sheet
7. cover and chill 1 hour
8. cook patties , in batches , in 3 t hot oil , adding oil as needed , in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 1 / 2 minutes on each side or until patties are golden brown
9. drain patties on paper towels , and keep warm
10. serve with desired toppings
demonstrations.review: I found the recipe very easy to follow. The taste was superb. I used corn relish instead of green tomato; either would be good. I fried them in an iron skillet. I gave some to neighbors that used hot pepper relish; they too were very complimentary of the taste. It is a very good recipe and is very close to the Black Eyed Pea Cakes served at The Stable Cafe located on The Biltmore Estate.

target.recipe_text:
english flapjack

this is my recipe for flapjack, inherited from my english mother. it doesn't have golden syrup in it, but you could try using 3 oz of lyles with 3 oz brown sugar and seeing how it turns out. i'm sure it would work quite well.   

1. melt butter in saucepan over very gentle heat
2. mix in the sugar , oats and salt
3. stir well and turn mixture into greased swiss roll tin and press lightly together
4. smooth top surface with the back of a metal spoon and bake at 190c for 30-35 mins in centre of oven
5. when golden brown remove from oven and allow to cool for a few minutes before cutting into square slices
6. cool completely before serving
target.review: I used 50/50 sugar/syrup. Because I like my flapjaks to be quite moist I also used a can of cherries in syrup, let a lot of the syrup drain of, spread a thin layer of flapjack mix into the baking tin, then a layer of cherries in syrup and covered it with the rest of the mix. They were absolutely delicious and non survived the day! I might use a little less sugar next time as it was quite sweet!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy lemon pound cake

i have used this cake for so many different things. its great if you need something at the last minute. its always comes out good. it's good just as a pound cake, without the drizzled lemon. we like it for strawberry shortcake.

1. mix together 1 cup sugar and butter
2. add eggs and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice
3. mix well
4. add salt , flour , and baking powder to mixture
5. add milk
6. bake at 325f in a well greased loaf pan for 1 hour , or until golden brown
7. mix 1 / 3 cup lemon juice and 1 / 4 cup sugar
8. use a toothpick to make holes in top of cake and drizzle lemon juice and sugar mixture over the top of the cake when removed from the oven
9. serve warm or cool
demonstrations.review: I used oil instead of butter and got a very dense moist cake. The dough was more like a batter and as I'm not sure it was meant to be that way. That's why I'm only leaving a comment and no rating. I'll try this recipe again and will make it as stated, because I really like the flavour, so i'll update this review next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marble cheesecake

nan

1. combine crumbs , sugar , and margarine
2. press onto bottom of 9-inch spring- form cake pan
3. bake at 350 degrees f
4. , 10 minutes
5. combine cream cheese , sugar and vanilla , beating at medium speed on electric mixer until well blended
6. add eggs , one at a time , mixing well after each addition
7. blend chocolate into 1 cup batter
8. spoon plain and chocolate batters alternately over crust
9. cutting through batters with knife several times for the marble effect
10. bake at 450 degrees f
11. , 10 minutes
12. reduce oven temperature to 250 degrees f
13. continue baking 30 additional minutes
14. loosen cake from rim of pan
15. cool before removing rim of pan
16. chill
demonstrations.review: A great looking cheesecake with a very rich, creamy taste. We don't have Graham Crackers or Graham Cracker crumbs here, so I used Caramel flavoured biscuit to make the crust, reducing the sugar as they were already quite sweet. Otherwise I followed the recipe exactly as written. I had to bake mine for an extra 10-15 minutes until it was properly set. It was enjoyed by everyone. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dutch almond cookies  amandel koekjes

this is another dutch recipe with almond paste. it's very traditional - yummy, too.

1. cream butter and sugars together
2. then beat in the eggs
3. add the flour and soda and then mix in the almond paste
4. if dough gets too stiff andd a few drops of water
5. mix in the nut meats
6. drop by teaspoonful on greased cookie sheet
7. bake in 325 oven for 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: These are really good. I reduced the white sugar to 1/4 cup, because I thought they would be very sweet with the almond paste, and they turned out just right for my taste. Very easy to make as well. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bechamel   basic white sauce

formula for making a thin, medium and thick white sauce.

1. scald the milk with the onion , bay leaf and peppercorns
2. cover and let infuse off heat for 10-15 minutes
3. in a heavy based saucepan , melt butter , whisk in flour and cook , stirring , until the flour is foaming but not browned- about 1 minute
4. off heat , strain in the hot milk
5. whisk well , then bring to a boil , whisking constantly until the sauce thickens
6. season with salt , pepper and nutmeg and leave to simmer slowly for 1-2 minutes
7. for a "thin" bechamel use 2 tbs
8. butter and 2 tbs
9. flour
10. for a "thick" bechamel use 4 tbs
11. butter and 4 tbs
12. flour
demonstrations.review: Infusing the milk gave this bechamel a really nice subtle flavour. Thanks Meanie for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with seven spices

this chicken creates quite an aroma while roasting!  you can leave the skin on and just peel it back to rub the spices on the chicken.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. remove chicken skin
3. rinse chicken and pat dry
4. remove giblets and neck
5. lightly spray the inside of a roasting back with nonstick cooking spray
6. place chicken , breast side up , in the plastic oven bag in a shallow roasting pan
7. in a small bowl , stir together remaining ingredients
8. rub this mixture evenly over chicken
9. tie the oven bag closed
10. roast in oven 1 to 1 1 / 4 hours , or until chicken is tender and no longer pink
demonstrations.review: After reading the previous review by LMillerRN, I decided to leave the skin on the chicken and roast it the usual way. I really liked the combination of spices and the flavour it added to the chicken. It wasn't that strong, but well balanced. I sprayed my chicken with olive oil and rubbed the spice mix all over. I also stuffed it with a lemon, cut in half to give it extra moisture and instead of using garlic powder in the mix, I used a couple of fresh garlic cloves that I peeled and slipped under the skin. The result was a yummy, wonderfully coloured and very moist chicken. I baked it for 20 minutes per lb, plus an extra 20 minutes. Thanks for sharing

target.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
target.review: These were a big hit in my boxes of Christmas cookies.  I lined my pan with foil, which made it easy to pull the whole thing out of the pan and cut into small bites.  Yum.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
east african braised chicken

this is a wonderful dish i found in "cooking light" magazine. this dish if full of flavor and despite all the ingredients, it is very easy to make. it's good served with rice and a flat bread. braising in a this highly aromatic liquid yields an exceptionally flavorful and tender result.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. sprinkle chicken with salt and black pepper
3. heat oil in a dutch oven over medium-high heat
4. add chicken , cook 4 minutes on each side or until golden brown
5. remove the chicken from pan
6. add the onions to pan
7. reduce heat to medium-low , and cook for 10 minutes , stirring frequently
8. add the ginger and next 5 ingredients , cook for 1 minute
9. stir in chicken , broth and the remaining ingredients , and bring to a boil
10. cover and bake at 350f for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Both DH and I loved this dish.  The chicken was tender and flavorful, and it smelled exotic and wonderful while cooking.  We did everything exactly as the recipe said, and I used Rex Goliath Pinot Grigio as the wine.   The rest of the bottle was delicious with the chicken.  DH usually does not care for curry, so instead of typical yellow curry powder, we tried McCormick's Red curry powder.  As a curry lover, I felt it was the perfect choice and even DH agreed.  This is a very good dish that I anticipate making on a regular basis.  Thanks, L. Duch.  I see this recipe has been on this site for quite a while and it has not been tried by very many people.  To all you who are interested - give it a try.  I don't think you'll be disappointed as the flavors meld together beautifully.  It has an exotic flair with all the elements of comfort food.  Yum.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
three not so blind mice

the cutest, delicate mice you ever saw! everyone remarks about them. i give trays of assorted cookies each year and place them on top.  they just make it!  it actually is a help when the kids can put on the almonds.  i don't remember where i got the recipe, so i gave the best measurements i can recall. it sounds like it could be a hershey's recipe!? for adults you can strain the cherries, then add rum or almond liquor and soak overnight drain and dry proceed with recipe. save the rum for drinks.

1. melt chocolate and paraffin double boiler
2. dip whole cherry holding tail , set on waxed paper
3. attach one kiss to opposite end of tail , it`ll be the head
4. make sure the tail lies along the waxed paper
5. don`t forget it`s to be a mouse
6. then put almonds for ears between chocolate kiss and cherries
7. tube tiny eyes above the nose then apply mini kisses over icing
demonstrations.review: Take a tray of these to a party and everyone will be cooing over them.  I use a variety of chocolate kisses - the ones filled with a creamy cherry filling, with almonds, or even the Truffle Kisses.  Tubes of decorating icing work well for white eyes and black noses.  Fun!  KK

demonstrations.recipe_text:
puffing  crab

here in southern maryland we eat a lot of crabs.  this is an interesting way to use your leftover crab meat (we pick our own crab meat).  i don't remember where i found it.  you can also use canned pasteurized crab meat.

1. melt butter in sauce pan
2. cook 5 minutes
3. gradually sir in milk and bring to the boil
4. cool mixture 5 minute
5. fold in beaten yolks
6. fold in mayonnaise
7. add crab meat
8. season to taste
9. add cayenne
10. fold in stiff beaten egg whites to crab mixture
11. put into buttered casserole
12. dust with paprika
13. bake in 400f oven until browned and puffed , approximately 20 minutes
demonstrations.review:
First Review 8/07: This recipe is very good, and would be a fantastic meal to serve to guests - you'll wow them with elegance. The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is my personal preference for creamy dishes as opposed to light, fluffy ones. I'll try this recipe again using whole eggs (not beating the whites) as all the elements are here that are perfect with crab! If you like dishes with this texture, you will adore this recipe. I always advocate using the best crab you can find when preparing any crab dish.
Second Review 3/08: I made this dish again for a big party, placing it on a table with many other dishes, and it was a huge hit.  I'm revising my review to 5 stars, although I still expect to try this dish 'creamy' style.  The seasoning is perfect - thanks again, Sandy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
triple lemon ripple cake

every time i've made this cake, it's gone over extremely well. lemon cake with a lemony cream cheese swirl and lemon glaze ... what's not to like?

note:  because this recipe is from a minute maid frozen lemon juice booklet, it does call for just lemon juice, and i like the mild flavor.  however, many like a stronger lemon flavor, and have added some grated lemon rind to the batter, with excellent results.  you should, however, use either frozen or fresh; reconstituted doesn't work as well in this cake.


1. prepare the filling by beating the cream cheese and sugar in a bowl
2. beat in the egg until the mixture is fluffy
3. add the flour until well blended and stir in the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. preheat the oven to 350 and spray a 12-cup tube or bundt pan with the non-stick spray
6. cream the butter and sugar , then beat in the eggs until the mixture is very light and fluffy
7. add the lemon juice and beat just until blended in
8. combine the dry ingredients& add to creamed mixture alternately with the milk
9. pour half of batter into the prepared pan
10. cover the batter in the pan with the cream cheese filling and pour in the remaining batter
11. gently swirl a knife through the batter a few times to make a swirl
12. bake for 50-60 minutes until cake pulls away from the side of the pan
13. cool in the pan for 10 minutes , then turn out and cool completely
14. prepare the glaze by stirring the 2 tbs
15. of lemon juice into the confectioner's sugar and blending until smooth
16. drizzle over the cooled cake
demonstrations.review:
Most cakes I make get rave reviews from my family and friends, but this one was very bland and not as interesting or exciting as the recipe sounded or the previous reviews indicate. I used fresh lemon juice and also added two tsp of zest to the batter. Made this for Mother's Day, but I need to find another recipe and make another Lemon Cake to make Mom happy. It does have a good texture that we liked - slightly different than most cakes, but it just didn't make up for the lack of flavor.
2 Days later:  The lemon came out more and the cake was better after it sat for 2 days, but I don't think I'll make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tipsy boursin cheese

creamy, smooth, with more than a hint of garlic. this recipe was in a cookbook my mom made for me. if you put this out at a party, you probably won't have leftovers to think about, but just in case, it keeps well, wrapped tightly in the fridge.

1. place all ingredients into a food processor or mixer , and whirl
2. pack into a crock , fancy cup , or dish or form into logs
3. refrigerate and serve with crackers and get ready for raves !
demonstrations.review: I made this exactly as written for a large party, but forgot to serve it, so it was shared with friends and used in place of expensive Boursin in two reipes I like to make.  To be honest, I like it better than Boursin, except it doesn't have the buttery/melty quality of the real thing when you're eating it on a cracker.  It's delicious, though, and this is an excellent recipe.  Thanks for such a useful recipe that will save me a lot of money.

target.recipe_text:
pasta with bacon and spinach

a nice simple supper.

1. cook pasta according to package directions
2. drain , reserving 1 / 2 cup cooking water
3. in a large skillet over medium heat , cook bacon until crisp
4. remove and drain on paper towels
5. drain drippings but do not clean pan
6. in same pan over medium heat , heat olive oil 1 minute
7. increase heat to medium-high and add spinach , wine and reserved cooking water
8. cook and stir until heated through
9. toss pasta and cheese with sauce
10. season with pepper to taste
11. crumble bacon over pasta
target.review: This was excellent. I used thick cut pepper bacon and garlic basil fresh pasta for this dish. I did end up adding 2 tablespoons of half and half to the dish, but it would have been just as delicious without. Will definately make again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
warm chicken spinach salad

a quick and healthy salad for a perfect lunch or light dinner. at 172 calories a serving and 6 grams of fat this recipe is perfect for those who are watching what they eat and don't want to compromise flavor. this recipe is better homes and gardens editor's top ten healthy heart recipe.

1. in a large salad bowl , combine spinach , leaf lettuce , sliced red onion , and pepper strips
2. cover and chill salad up to 2 hours
3. cut chicken into bite-sized strips
4. toss chicken with rosemary and lemon-pepper seasoning
5. in a wok or 10-inch skillet stir-fry chicken strips and garlic in hot oil over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes or until chicken is tender and no longer pink
6. remove chicken from skillet
7. add to salad mixture
8. for dressing , add vinegar and water to skillet , stirring to scrape up any browned bits
9. pour dressing over salad
10. toss gently to mix
11. transfer to individual salad plates
12. garnish with fresh rosemary , if desired
demonstrations.review: I made this tonight for dinner and my fiance and I really enjoyed it! I halved the recipe because it was just him and myself. I added a little mixed spring greens, more balsamic (twice as much) and added the garlic right at the end to give it more POW! The only thing he said was it would be even better with a little crumbled bacon. Yet we all know that everything is better w/ bacon! Thanks! Will make again, maybe even for a dinner party.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy peanut butter cream pie

this can be a rich dessert for peanut butter lovers.  can be spiffed up with the addition of bailey's or kaluha - or try amarula for a nice flavor, 2 tablespoons is minimum i think!!

1. mix together the first 5 ingredients and fold in cool whip
2. scoop and smooth into graham crust then garnish with drizzled chocolate syrup
3. put in refrigerator 1 hour or longer before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this dish for my fiance's birthday BBQ this last Tuesday evening and everyone really loved it. I added chopped up peanut butter cups to the bottom of the pie to give it more chocolate goodness and it was wonderful. I used the oreo crust and garnished the pie with chocolate syrup and chopped peanuts. I'm sure I will make it again and again. Next time I'll try a little Baileys.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun ponchartrain sauce

from my friend haguepoo in my new orleans recipe group. i serve this as a first course or over a little pasta for lunch.

1. in a medium saucepan , saute mushrooms and garlic in 1 teaspoon butter until tender
2. stir in shrimp and cook until pink
3. transfer to bowl
4. in same saucepan melt remaining 2 teaspoons butter
5. slowly mix in cream
6. stir in shrimp and mushroom mixture and black pepper
7. simmer over very low heat until thick
8. just before serving stir in wine
demonstrations.review: I made this sauce this past weekend for a dinner party. I grilled some catfish and poured this sauce over it. I served it with white rice and wilted spinach and red bell peppers. It was AMAZING! I think next time I'm going to try and get some red fish and pan fry it to put the sauce over. Great work!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon herb butter basted chicken

another lemony based creation from sandra lee's sumptuous collection of recipes.  this one is simple, tasty, and when paired up with lemon chicken soup,lemon garlic broccoli, lemon pudding brulee with blueberries, and a lemon cream martini you have an elegant spread that everyone will think you slaved over - without adding to your non-existent grey hairs!! lemon haters, need not apply!!  ;)  yummy!

1. preheat broiler
2. in a small pan over medium heat , melt butter
3. stir in sauce mix and lemon juice , cook 1 minute
4. remove from heat
5. set aside
6. rinse chicken with cold water and pat dry
7. season with garlic salt and lemon pepper
8. place chicken on foil lined baking sheet or broiler pan
9. broil chicken for about 15 minutes per side basting with butter sauce every 5 minutes or until desired crispness and color
10. serve with a crisp salad , lemon chicken soup , lemon garlic broccoli etc
11. enjoy !
12. )
demonstrations.review:
This was gorgeous! That's really the only word I can use. I was lazy and used whole chicken breasts, baking them upside down in the sauce so they would be moist. I flipped the chicken over and put them under the broiler for a few minutes to crisp the skin up before serving. Once the skin was nice and crispy brown I poured a good spoon full of the lemony butter sauce over the top before serving. Easy, moist and flavorful!
Great simple chicken recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kabak mcveri  turkish zucchini fritters

fritters are very popular in the middle east. they are eaten hot or at room temperature as a vegetable side dish or a meze. it couldn’t be simpler to make, but you can dress it up with optional garnishes of black olives, tomatoes, or hard-boiled egg. the perfect use for small, sweet new zucchini. serve alone or with a creamy garlic-lemon yogurt sauce for a perfect complement to any spicy or grilled foods that call for a cooling accompaniment.

1. grate the zucchini and place in a colander
2. sprinkle with salt and let drain for 30 minutes
3. squeeze out moisture and pat with paper towels
4. place the zucchini in a bowl and add the green and yellow onions , dill , parsley , cheese , eggs , flour and salt and pepper to taste
5. mix well
6. in a large saut pan over medium-high heat , pour in oil to a depth of inch
7. when the oil is hot , drop the batter by heaping tablespoonfuls into the pan , allow space in between fritters
8. fry for 2 minutes on the fist side , then turn to brown on the second side for about 3 minutes
9. using a slotted spatula transfer to paper towels or newspaper to drain
10. repeat with remaining batter
demonstrations.review: I do believe I've found a new favorite side dish! These were wonderful!!! I added a little red bell pepper for color and had to use dry dill. The flavor and texture was wonderful. I used a good extra virgin olive oil, and sprinkled with kosher salt when finished. I also made a quick sauce out of garlic, greek yogurt and lemon juice to serve on the side. Thank you for this wonderful recipe!

target.recipe_text:
baby finger food   apple turkey loaf or sticks

i found this recipe on wholesomebabyfood.com and i am posting it for safe keeping. it is recommended for babies that are 6 months and older, but they also advise speaking to your pediatrician before starting your baby on solids. also, remember to follow the rule of four (wait 4 days after introducing new foods) and make sure your baby has had no allergic reactions to any of the foods in this recipe before serving it!

1. place ground turkey in a large mixing bowl
2. add the egg / yolk , carrots , applesauce , spices , bread crumbs and bran
3. mix well - if this mixture appears too dry , add more carrots or applesauce
4. if this mixture appears too wet , add more bran and / or bread crumbs
5. place mix into a lightly oiled loaf pan and bake at 350f for approximately 45 minutes or until an inserted knife comes out clean
6. you may wish to cover with foil to prevent the top from burning
7. when finished baking and cooled , remove loaf from pan and slice as you would for bread
8. break into small bits for finger feeding or mash or chop gently for younger babies
9. this recipe may also be made into "turkey sticks" for toddlers and older babies who are able to handle more textured / chunky finger foods
target.review: My 10 month old daughter loved these! She tends to not like most things with meat. I made them into a fishstick shape and cooked them for about 30 minutes and they were done.  I froze them and now I can reheat one or two for dinner or a snack. I plan on trying this with different combinations, like ground chicken and ground beef and other veggies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted red potatoes with rosemary

from quick fix meals with robin miller on the food network

1. preheat oven to 400
2. combine all ingredients in a large bowl and toss to coat potatoes
3. transfer potatoes to a large baking sheet
4. roast 25-30 minutes or until tender and golden
demonstrations.review: I've made this recipe quite a few times now and it is so delicious.  I usually use baby red potatoes and I have substituted dried rosemary during the winter when I don't have fresh on hand it is still good

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy mostaccioli

this recipe is from an old pampered chef cookbook. simple and something my kids will eat. freezes well. see note for oamc instructions.

1. prepare the pasta according to the package directions
2. rinse and drain
3. in a non-stick skillet , cook and stir the beef over medium-high heat until meat is browned
4. drain
5. add in spaghetti sauce , soup , pepper , and italian seasoning
6. stir to combine
7. in a large bowl , mix together the pasta , sauce , and 2 cups cheese
8. transfer mixture to a greased 4-quart baking dish
9. sprinkle remaining 1 cup cheese over the top
10. bake at 350 for 40 minutes or until heated through
11. seal with foil or place in a zip top bag
12. freeze
13. to serve: thaw in fridge overnight
14. bake as directed
demonstrations.review: Yum we will make this again, great winter comfort food.  My kids ate it well and DH liked it except the carrots I chopped up and put in it to get some veggies with our meal easily, I didn't mind them nor did the kids though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry cheesecake cookie pizza

this is a great desert.  easy to make also.  from bh&g christmas cookies 1995.

1. beat the butter in a large mixing bowl with an electric mixer on medium to high speed for 30 seconds
2. add the 3 / 4 cup sugar and beat till combined
3. beat in egg yolk and vanilla till combined
4. beat in as much of the flour as you can with the mixer
5. stir in any remaining flour with a wooden spoon
6. spread dough in a lightly greased 12 or 13 inch pizza pan
7. bake in a 350-f oven about 25 minutes or till golden
8. meanwhile , beat together cream cheese , 1 egg and the 1 tbl sugar till smoth
9. spread over hot crust to within 1 / 2 inch of the edge
10. dollop preserve on top
11. with a knife , carefully swirl preserve to marble
12. sprinkle with almond
13. bake 5 to 10 minutes more till filling is set
14. cool in pan on a wire rack
15. cut in wedges
16. store in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: This was good, I would have liked more cheesecake and preserves I think though.  I heated up my preserves and they seemed to marble very well.  I also cooked my cookie bottom for 20 minutes and then the topping took almost 10 minutes to set and I think the cookie was still a bit harder then I would have liked.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheddar turkey bake oamc

i haven't made this yet but it sounds great. it uses 2 cans cheddar cheese soup and rice, mmm. i think i  might add shredded carrots or spinach to the rice mixture before cooking. i also think it would be great with chicken.

1. in a large saucepan , bring the broth , water and onion to a boil
2. reduce heat
3. add rice , cover and simmer for 15 minutes
4. remove from the heat and fluff with a fork
5. divide the rice between 2 greased 9 inch square baking pans
6. sprinkle each with peas and turkey
7. in a bowl combine the soup , milk and salt until smooth
8. pour over the turkey
9. combine the cracker crumbs with the butter and sprinkle over the top
10. cover and freeze
11. from frozen: thaw the casserole overnight in the refrigerator
12. bake uncovered at 350 degrees for 45-50 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: MMM this was really good!  One of the better casseroles I have made lately.  We used chicken and brown rice and my kids ate it up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy layered tomato dip

great for superbowl parties.

1. mix cream cheese spread and garlic until well blended
2. spread onto bottom of 8- or 9-inch pie plate or on serving plate
3. top with tomatoes , onions and cheese
4. cover
5. refrigerate several hours or until chilled
6. serve as a dip with the crackers
demonstrations.review: I love this recipe.  I first made it off of the wheat thins box during the holidays last year and it was a big hit, you definatly have to be a garlic lover to like it though.

target.recipe_text:
magic omelette

this isn't so much a recipe as a tip. most of us make omelettes the same way: wait until the eggs are nearly cooked, then add cheese, vegetables, meat, etc., counting on the heat of the eggs to heat them, and in doing so unnecessarily overcooking the eggs. if, instead, you cover your egg pan with a pot lid, you can add the omelette filling from the outset and it cooks with the eggs, so your omelette's already done at the point where you'd normally add the filling. and get this - you never have to touch a utensil! try it and i bet you'll never cook an omelette without a lid again.

1. heat a non-stick skillet until butter sizzles
2. scramble eggs
3. add to skillet
4. sprinkle eggs evenly with cheese , ham , chives , salt and pepper
5. cover and cook over low flame until eggs solidify , about 5 minutes
6. slide from skillet to plate , folding omelette in half with edge of skillet
target.review: This rocks, I'm going to do this, and so appreciate the tip,,,saves on all that fiddling.   Five stars, best in show, etc.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome thai chicken coconut curry

this recipe introduced me to the fantastic flavour of coconut milk and curry paste, its insane how good it is, don't even think of skimping on any of the ingredients, you need them all. fish sauce is super cheap and you can find it in the asian food isle in your supermarket. i hope you enjoy this as much as i do.

1. heat the oil in a large wok , add the garlic , saute
2. add the curry , ginger and the thicker cream on top of the can of coconut milk to the wok , whisk
3. now add the rest of the coconut milk in along with everything but the chicken and pineapple , whisk
4. bring to a slow boil for 7 minutes , then discard the lemongrass add the chicken and pineapple and cook till the chicken is no longer pink inside , about 7-9 minutes
5. serve over jasmine rice and top with green onion
6. soooooooooooooo yummy !
demonstrations.review:
Wow. I took the leftover can juice from the pineapple chunks, and added a tablespoon of wasabi mayo (found in the Asian market when I went to get these ingredients). Used this as a dressing / marinade for cucumbers. Wow ! Anyway, the red curry paste that I bought didn't really provide the "heat" my family likes, in fact, hardly any at all. I used the 2 teaspoons of this red curry paste, and then added a teaspoon of crushed red pepper flakes (for more moderate, you might try 1/2 teaspoon of pepper flakes).
That did the trick. Added the pineapple chunks just before the final heating, and a sliced baby bok choy & some flat peas.
Thanks for this recipe - will be making again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oriental ramen broccoli coleslaw

this recipe comes from my aunt. someone from their church had sent over this dish while i was in visiting my family. we all had a fit over it. wanted to share and have for my own reference too. 
note: can use splenda in place of sugar

1. before opening noodles , crush into 1 inch pieces
2. open packages and set aside flavor packets
3. place noodles in bottom of large serving bowl
4. top noodles with broccoli slaw , then sprinkle with almonds and sunflower kernels , and green onions
5. in a separate bowl combine sugar , oil , vinegar , and flavor packets from noodles
6. pour over slaw , cover and chill up to 24 hours
7. toss before serving
demonstrations.review:
It's a good thing I didn't make this for a crowd because I would have eaten the entire bowl by myself before it even got to the event. This is so good, so nutty-crunchy and full of subtle flavors and nutrition. I reduced the sugar to 1/3 cup and it was sweet enough without overwhelming any of the other flavors. If any of this dish does make it to a party I am sure I will be the talk of the gals...thanks so much...excellent, and thankfully I did find a store with the bagged broccoli slaw, so it will be a frequent favorite.
FIVE BIG STARS

demonstrations.recipe_text:
favorite corn muffins

fluffy, light, just sweet enough.

1. in bowl , combine first 5 ingredients
2. add milk , eggs , and oil
3. beat for 1 minute
4. pour into greased muffin tins
5. bake at 400 for 20-25 minutes
demonstrations.review: OK, this worked,,,these are really good.   Perfect blend of the sugar / salt and baking powder.  The recipe says 6-8 muffins so I assume these would be jumbo,,because the recipe completely filled all 12 wells of my muffin pan, which has generous wells.  I t hought they would rise and flow over, but they didn't,,,stayed nice and mounded......love these....and thanks for taking the time to post this wonderful keeper............

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic flat bread

this bread-machine recipe has a great taste and impressive presentation. it is perfect for a dinner party or pot-luck.

1. in bread machine pan , place the first six ingredients in order suggested by manufacturer
2. select dough setting
3. when cycle is completed , turn dough onto floured surface
4. roll into 12-inch circle
5. transfer to a 14-inch pizza pan coated with non-stick cooking spray
6. cover
7. let rise in a warm place until doubled , about 30 minutes
8. in a small skillet , cook garlic in butter over medium heat for about 5 minutes , stirring frequently
9. with the end of a wooden spoon handle , make indentations in dough at 1-inch intervals
10. top with garlic butter and sprinkle with cheeses
11. bake at 400 degrees for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown
12. remove to a wire rack
13. cut into wedges or squares and serve warm
demonstrations.review: I came here because earlier today I was in the supermarket.  They had a display of flat  breads, oval in shape about 12 inches by 6 inches (that's all you get) a variety of flavors like roasted tomato, garlic, etc....,,so here's the good part, the price for each of these was $ 4.89.  Kid you not.  Would serve maybe four.  I said to myself,,,I'm headed to zaar, run don't walk !   I will make this lovely recipe just to be able to thumb my nose at the "artisan bread" people out there...........

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rosemary ranch chicken kabobs

this is my favorite recipe that i snagged from allrecipes.  i've changed things a bit...but the flavor is incredible!  i've cooked this on the grill (in a grill basket lined with foil so as not to lose any of the incredible sauce!), on the stovetop and in the oven.  oven and grill are by far the best methods.  i serve this over white rice and the flavor is super!!  i usually use dried rosemary, but fresh is best!  i also cut the sugar in half and use low fat ranch.  i also completely omit the salt since i don't feel it needs it.  my kids have been eating this since they were 19 months old!  when i bake these in the oven i bake them on 450 degrees for about 20-30 minutes.  lean toward 20 so as not to overcook.  yum!

1. in a medium bowl , stir together the olive oil , ranch dressing , worcestershire sauce , rosemary , salt , lemon juice , white vinegar , pepper , and sugar
2. let stand for 5 minutes
3. place chicken in the bowl , and stir to coat with the marinade
4. cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes
5. preheat the grill for medium-high heat
6. thread chicken onto skewers and discard marinade
7. lightly oil the grill grate
8. grill skewers for 8 to 12 minutes , or until the chicken is no longer pink in the center , and the juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Wow, why doesn't this have 2000 5-star reviews?  I had this at a retirement party last night.  Very easy, and the kebabs were moist and very tender, and so tasty.  Everyone wanted the recipe.  Food.com'ers, you have to try this one....10-stars

target.recipe_text:
turtle ice cream cake

great for making a head and keeping in the freezer for unexpected company!

1. combine first 5 ingredients and spread on a cookie sheet in a thin layer
2. bake at 400 degrees until crumbs are golden
3. check often to prevent it from burning !
4. crumble into 1-13 x 9 pan or 2-8x8 pans reserving some of the crumbs for the top
5. drizzle 3 / 4 cup caramel sauce on top of crumbs
6. scoop vanilla ice cream on top and spread evenly
7. drizzle the rest of the caramel sauce and top with the reserved crumbs
8. freeze until firm or overnight
9. if storing for an extended time , cover well to prevent freezer burn
target.review: This was great!  I made it ahead for Valentine's Day - wonderful.  This would be great to have for unexpected company - if you can keep it that long.  Thanks for the great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
st  louis toasted ravioli

got this recipe from a st. louis bar and grill. my dh and his friends love it. i usually have to double the recipe.

1. combine milk and egg in a small bowl
2. place breadcrumbs and salt in a shallow bowl
3. dip ravioli in milk mixture , and coat with breadcrumbs
4. pour oil to depth of 2 inches into a dutch oven
5. heat to 350 degrees
6. fry ravioli , a few at a time , 1 minute on each side or until golden
7. drain on paper towels
8. sprinkle with parmesan cheese , and serve immediately with warm spaghetti or pizza sauce
demonstrations.review: perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wonderful salsa

this is the best salsa recipe i've found so far and i've tried about a dozen. i got it from one of the local hospital cookbooks that are sold in my area. i changed it a bit and have been canning it for years. the reason i plant a garden is for this salsa. we would be lost without it. hope you like it as much as we do.  one of our members who is a food scientist took this salsa to work, tested the ph and found it measured under 4.0 (well within the safety limit for boiling water bath processing).

1. mix all together and bring to a slow boil for 10 minute
2. seal in jars and cook in hot water bath for 10 minute
3. this is a medium salsa
4. this is also a chunky salsa so if you want a smoother salsa cut your veggies into smaller pieces
5. yields 3-6 quarts or pints
demonstrations.review: this is the best receipe i have ever found also - i use 2T honey instead of the sugar - mmmmm

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade white bread  non bread machine

delicious, basic bread recipe. yummy! when i make this recipe, i bake one, and freeze the other two loaves, then use them later. to use later, i simply thaw in greased bread pan & let rise above & continue to follow same directions as posted. enjoy!

1. in large bowl , mix sugar , yeast , melted lard and warm water
2. stir and let stand approximately 2-5 minutes , until bubbly
3. add salt and flour
4. stir , then mix well
5. let stand for 30-60 minutes
6. punch down , then knead
7. shape into three loaves
8. place into greased loaf pans and let rise until rounded above pan
9. bake at 350 for 30 minutes or until done
10. remove from pans and butter tops , if desired , for a softer crust
demonstrations.review: Doesn't come any easier than this.  I baked all three then froze two.  Next time I will freeze unbaked as suggested.  Texture is great - was not so sure it would be with only one knead cycle.  Thanks WJ for a great recipe.  So much better than bread machine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dirty shrimp in butter beer sauce

herby, spicy shrimp with a kick, in a buttery-beer "sauce". fast, easy and delicious, serve as an appetizer, or a dinner over rice or with lots of crusty french bread to soak up all the tasty, herbalicious sauce!

1. saute garlic and herbs in butter until garlic is slightly browned
2. add shrimp , stirring constantly , until shrimp are pink and done
3. pour in beer , simmer 1 minute more , and serve !
demonstrations.review: we missed with this one - not sure why - made for special Valentine's dinner - did not care for spice combination

demonstrations.recipe_text:
filet de boeuf en croute

(filet mignon in puff pastry) i prefer not to eat out on valentine's day, hate fighting the crowds, the noise, the usually bad service because the restaurant is jam packed, the expense...could i have a little cheese with my "whine"? lol! here's what i made for the main course last year, and it was to die for. almost too pretty to eat....almost! enjoy!!! *prep-time does not include chilling time.

1. trim any fat from the steaks , sprinkle with pepper , spread tops of each with 1 tbl butter
2. in shallow roasting pan , bake in pre-heated oven , buttered side up , at 425 for 10 minutes
3. place in fridge til cold
4. roll out puff pastry a little and cut in half
5. spread steaks with garlic , top with cheese
6. place cheese side down onto center of pastry squares , fold pastry over , moisten edges and seal well
7. place seam-side down onto baking sheet lined with parchment paper
8. prick top with a fork , cover with plastic wrap , and re-chill for 1 hour
9. beat egg with oil , and brush pastry with it
10. bake in center of pre-heated 425 oven for 25 minutes for med-rare
11. serve with horseradish sauce if desired
12. serves 2
demonstrations.review:
Wildflour thanks for making Valentine's Day easy and special.  Did exactly as posted - next time, and there definetely will be a next time, I will replace the cheese with fresh sliced mushrooms.  Let's see - when is the next special occasion.
Did not fix the sauce - I actually forgot about it until now when posting the review.  I guess we didn't miss it but will try to remember next time.

target.recipe_text:
pineapple meatballs

this is a family favourite; my teenage son eats at least 2 servings himself. cooking time includes the browning of the meatballs, although you can brown them in the oven on a cookie sheet and make the sauce at the same time, saving yourself a little time.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. first , make the meatballs: combine all meatball ingredients in a bowl and mix well
3. shape into 1-inch balls
4. brown them in a nonstick frying pan until browned all over
5. drain on paper towel then place in a large ungreased casserole dish
6. to make sauce , combine brown sugar and cornstarch in a large saucepan , then whisk in the 1-3 / 4 cup pineapple juice / water combination until mixture is smooth
7. add vinegar , soy sauce and worcestershire sauce
8. stir
9. simmer , uncovered , on medium-low heat for about 8 minutes , or until thickened
10. pour sauce over meatballs and add pineapple tidbits
11. stir gently to combine until meatballs are coated with sauce
12. bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes
13. if you want a lot , this recipe doubles well
target.review: I just made this recipe and it is wonderful.  Very easy to follow the directions (I did however double the sauce).  Made no changes whatsoever and we all loved it.  I am now trying to think of the different "fruit" variations to use.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s juicy hamburger burger

we all have our different tastes for burgers i like mine flavorful and juicy this recipe will give you the best of both! see the bottom of the recipe for tips on even more extra juicy burgers! --- making a indentation in the middle of the uncooked burger will prevent the burgers from puffing up into meatballs shapes while cooking and keeps them flat --- do not add any salt into the burger mixture as the dry onion soup already has a lot of salt content, you can sprinkle some on towards the end of cooking if needed, if desired you may add in 3-4 tablespoons of your favorite barbecue sauce to the ground beef mixture

1. in a bowl crumble the ground beef with clean hands
2. add in the dry soup mix , egg , garlic , breadcrumbs or crushed soda cracker crumbs , worcestershire sauce , black pepper and hot sauce
3. using clean hands mix until combined , add in more breadcrumbs or cracker crumbs if needed to just hold the mixture together
4. divide the ground beef into 6 equal patties
5. using your large finger or the back of a small spoon make a shallow dent into the center of each patty
6. place the patties onto a large plate or a small cookie sheet
7. cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for a minimum of 6 hours or up to 24 hours to blend flavors
