8. grill or pan fry the burgers as desired until cooked through
9. serve burgers in toasted buns with choice of condiments
demonstrations.review: I should have known with your name on it these would be wonderful.  This is the very best burger I have ever, ever cooked.  So juicy.  I followed the recipe exactly and I did add the Worcestershire sauce.  I don't think I will make burgers any other way again.  Thanks Kitten.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey bbq chicken

awesome bbq flavour on tender chicken pieces.  i make extra sauce so the kids can put it on their mashed potatoes.

1. spray a 9x13 pan with cooking spray
2. lay the chicken in the pan ,
3. blend the remaining ingredients , pour over the chicken pieces
4. bake covered at 350 for 30 min's
5. turn chicken over , bake uncovered for another 30- 40 min's until done
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe last night and my family loved it.  It will be a keeper in our house.  This was made with love for Chef Dee.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: I am making this for dinner and realized that I did not review it the first two times I made it.  Not that this recipe needs another review.  My family loved this pot roast.  I did add additional water to mine although to say how much would be a guess on my part.  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no cook divinity

i've never tried to cook divinity, but i've heard stories about others trying and failing, so when i saw this recipe i had to post it for safe-keeping.  cooking time is the drying time overnight.  haven't tried it yet---i bought a box of old quick cooking magazines at a flea market and am posting the recipes i want to keep as i go through them.

1. in a large mixing bowl , combine the frosting mix , corn syrup , 2 tablespoons boiling water and vanilla
2. beat on high speed for 5 minutes
3. gradually add sugar , 6 tablespoons hot water and nuts
4. mix well
5. drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper
6. let stand at room temperature overnight or until dry to the touch
7. store in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: This is the recipe I always use and it works perfectly for me.  Everybody loves it.  However you cannot make this when the weather is humid.  I was going to make this Christmas again this year but I can no longer find the frosting mix.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
icing in the cake cake

this recipe comes from a community church cookbook. it is easy and delicious. i have friends that have made this with other flavor combinations and the result has always been good thus far. the best part is since it is not 

1. mix all together with mixer
2. bake in a well-greased bundt pan at 375 for 45-55 minutes
3. cool 20 minutes before turning out on cake plate
demonstrations.review: WOW!!  This is fabulous.  And what variety this recipe has to offer.  This will become a staple in our family.  Thanks for posting such an easy, tasty cake.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy tuna or chicken noodle casserole

this is a delicious casserole that can be made using either tuna or 1-1/2 cups or more of cooked cubed chicken or even cooked turkey
 --- for a thinner sauce use 1 cup of milk or half and half instead of 3/4 cup, prep time includes boiling the egg noodles, if you are not a garlic-lover then you may omit the garlic powder and to zing the flavor up even more add in 1-1/2 tablespoons of lemon juice

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. grease a 2-quart casserole dish
3. cook the egg noodles in boiling salted water
4. drain then toss with 2 tablespoons butter
5. in a large saucepan , mix the undiluted mushroom soup , garlic powder , parmesan cheese milk or half and half , sour cream , salt , pepper , chopped onion , pimiento , bell pepper and celery
6. cook over low heat , stirring frequently for 15 minutes
7. add in the tuna or chicken
8. mix to combine
9. combine the mixture with the cooked egg noodles
10. transfer to prepared greased baking dish
11. sprinkle top with the broken ritz crackers
12. bake for about 25 minutes
target.review: This recipe was just as I had hoped it would be! I wanted to make my mom's recipe, but when I couldn't find it in my recipe book, I turned to Kittencal. The only thing I would do next time is cut down on the onion. I LOVE onion, but for this recipe it's a little much- that's why I gave it four stars. Other reviews said that it was too dry after baking so I added a little extra milk (about 1/4 cup) to be on the safe side and it was perfectly moist! Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot garlic brown sugar chicken

the house smells wonderful while this is cooking!

1. place chicken in crock pot
2. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over chicken
3. cook on low for 6-8 hours
4. serve over rice or noodles
5. you can thicken the juices after cooking with a little cornstarch
demonstrations.review: I'm so confused as to what happened with my recipe! After reading all of these rave reviews I was so excited to make this. I was SO disappointed! The flavor was awful- very sour and tangy. I used apple cider vinegar, thinking maybe that was where I went wrong, but I read other reviews who also used acv. I went back and triple checked that I used the right amount of vinegar and I know that I did. I don't know what happened, but this was not good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: I forgot to rate this recipe, 5 stars of course!! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy and delicious ranch parmesan chicken

there are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, i find that hidden valley ranch dressing works the best but kraft or any other brand will do, i sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although i have only made this using breasts i imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *note* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
for low-fat option: use low-fat ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as smart balance 50/50 blend.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. in a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with parmesan cheese , seasoned salt , black pepper and garlic powder
3. dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides
4. coat in the breadcrumb mixture
5. place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil
6. lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast
7. if desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces
8. bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked)
demonstrations.review: THIS WAS SO GOOD! My SO and I devoured this chicken, it was so tender and juicy! This will be a regular recipe in our household. Thank you for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean cous cous salad

qeth .... a quick, easy, tasty and healthy middle eastern dish. note:   i agree with reviewers that this salad needs to be kicked-up-a notch, so i've made some revisions as of 7/1/09.

1. bring chicken broth to boil in a 2 quart or larger sauce pan and stir in the couscous
2. cover the pot and remove from the heat
3. let stand 5 minutes
4. in a large bowl , whisk together the olive oil , lime juice , vinegar and cumin
5. add green onions , red pepper , cilantro , corn , optional tomatoes and beans
6. toss to coat
7. fluff the couscous well , breaking up any chunks
8. add to the bowl with the vegetables and mix well
9. season with salt and pepper to taste and sprinkle feta cheese on top
10. serve at once or refrigerate until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: I have made this recipe so many times I can't even count. It is so simple, delicious, refreshing, and SO healthy! I usually throw in ingredients that I have on hand, but the original recipe is my absolute favorite. Cilantro, red onions, cumin, corn, black beans.... mmm it is so tasty! Thank you for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanish chicken   rice bake

a throw-it-together and pop it in the oven supper. use more chili powder or add hot sauce if you really want to spice it up!
i just want to add:  many people who have tried this recipe have had to cook it longer than i have specified. a hint:  i always use a casserole dish with a heavy tight-fitting lid. i sometimes presoak my rice in cold water for 10 minutes or so.  hope this helps! =)  barb
ps...to freeze : cool, portion and freeze in a ziploc bag.
to reheat: thaw, place in a covered casserole dish and bake until heated through.

1. mix soup , salsa , water , corn , and beans and rice in 2-quart shallow baking dish
2. top with chicken and sprinkle with chili powder
3. cover tightly with casserole lid or foil
4. bake at 375f for 45 minutes or so
5. sprinkle with cheese
demonstrations.review: For starters, I used brown rice instead of white and I'm sure this contributed to my problem. I read a lot of other reviews and anticipated that 45 minutes would not be enough time to cook the rice fully, so I cooked it for an hour and 20 minutes in a 2 quart dish. Even after that long of cooking time the rice was still very chewy. I give it 4 starts because the flavor was actually really good and I think I would make it again, maybe just cook the rice partially beforehand.

target.recipe_text:
shrimp sahanaki with greek cheeses and tomatoes

this is a fantastic greek appetizer/main dish. serve with a glass of chilled white wine and lots of bread for the sauce.

1. heat 1 / 3 cup oil in medium saucepan over medium heat
2. add onion and saut until golden-brown , about 12 minutes
3. add tomatoes , 4 tblsps parsley , garlic , cayenne and ouzo
4. season to taste
5. bring to boil
6. reduce heat , cover and simmer until sauce thickens , about 25 minutes
7. add shrimp to sauce and cook for a further 6-8 minutes , until shrimp are cooked through
8. remove from heat
9. sprinkle feta , kasseri and parsley over and cover with lid of saucepan
10. allow to sit for 5 minutes , until cheeses have started melting
11. give a gentle stir to distribute cheeses and distribute amongst serving plates
12. use crusty bread to dip into the delicious sauce
target.review: We enjoyed this recipe and want to thank you for sharing it. It was simple, quick and very filling. I tossed it with some pasta. The sauce was delish and the shrimp were nice and tender.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s tuna melt sandwich

trust me you will be craving this often once you try it! --- you may use regular white salt but the seasoned salt is better, also use as much cheese and tomato slices as desired, i sometimes add in some chopped sweet yum yum pickles to the tuna filling too --- low-fat mayonnaise and cheese may be used :)

1. set oven to broiler heat
2. in a bowl mix tuna , mayo , lemon juice celery , green onions and parsley
3. mix well
4. add in seasoned salt and lemon pepper to taste
5. place the bread slices on a baking sheet and broil for 1 minute or until lightly toasted
6. remove from heat , divide and spread the tuna mixture on top of each bread slice
7. place one cheese slice over the tuna , then one tomato slice then another slice of cheese on top
8. return the layered bread to oven and broil for about 3 minutes , or until the cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: This is a keeper. I'm not too fond of tuna, but this recipe makes it enjoyable to eat...maybe even crave! I was out of green onions and swiss so was forced to use provolone cheese and a finely grated vidalia onion as substitutes. Still came out delish.  Thanks kittencal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bushka burgers

these burgers have evolved over a very long time of trying different ingredients and techniques. they got the name 

1. combine in a large bowl , the beef , egg , onion , garlic , ketchup , 2 tbsp butter , parsley , liquid smoke , dijon mustard , worcestershire sauce , salt and black pepper
2. form into 8 equal-sized flatter patties
3. separate each burger with wax paper , stack and put into the freezer to firm them up
4. preheat grill to medium-high
5. grill burgers to desired doneness turning only once
6. brush burger buns with the remaining cup melted butter and grill cut side down until crisp and golden brown
demonstrations.review: Flavorful burgers...love the liquid smoke. However, I can't seem to agree with the freezing technique because 1) they still fell apart after storing them for 3 hrs in the freezer and 2) meat sears/grills better when it's close to room temperature. UPDATE: Made these a second time. Since the flavors work well together, I added bread crumbs to the mixture instead of eliminating any ingredients. The burgers stayed intact and didn't need freezing. Still came out tasty. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apfelklosse  german apple cake

this is a traditional german recipe.  it is considered a 'cake' there, but more akin to what we know as bars.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. combine 2 cups flour , 1 / 2 cup sugar , 1 / 2 teaspoons salt and baking powder
3. cut in butter as for pie crust
4. add egg yolks
5. press half in the bottom of a 10 x 15 inche jelly roll pan
6. combine apples , 1 / 2 cup sugar , 1 / 4 cup flour , cinnamon and nutmeg
7. spread over the bottom
8. crust
9. crumble remaining crust over the filling
10. brush with egg whites and bake for 30-40 minutes
11. serve with a vanilla custard sauce or ice cream
demonstrations.review: I used gala apples and thought during the process that I might not have enough crust for the topping, but it worked out fine. We loved that it wasn't over done with sweetness. I would like to try this again using a tad less butter for the pastry, just because we thought it was too buttery for our tastes. I was greedy enough to stash some in the freezer (cut it up into squares and wrapped in foil) and they still tasted good after defrosting and reheating.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek potatoes  oven roasted and delicious

these potatoes are a staple in our home. whether accompanying roast lamb or chicken, or just on their own, we have them a couple of times a week. they are delicious and the ones that get overly-brown in the pan and stick a bit are mine!  clean up is a little tricky with this recipe, unless you line your pans with foil, but i find that just filling the pan up with hot, sudsy water and forgetting for an hour (something i apparently have no problem doing ;-)) helps a lot.

1. preheat oven to 420f a reviewer has suggested spraying the baking pan with pam - that sounds like a great idea !
2. put all the ingredients into a baking pan large enough to hold them
3. season generously with sea salt and black pepper
4. make sure your hands are very clean and put them in the pan and give everything a toss to distribute
5. the garlic will drop into the water / oil solution but its flavour will permeate the potatoes , and this way , it won't burn
6. bake for 40 minutes
7. when a nice golden-brown crust has formed on the potatoes , give them a stir to bring the white underside up , season lightly with a bit more sea salt and pepper and just a light sprinkling of oregano
8. add 1 / 2 cup more water if pan appears to be getting dry , and pop back into oven to brown other side of potatoes
9. this will take about another 40 minutes
10. do not be afraid of overcooking the potatoes- they will be delicious
demonstrations.review: Superb! This dish is simple to prepare and so savory. I serve these straight out of the oven while they're still nice and crispy. The leftovers are still delicious and can be rewarmed in the oven to bring back the crispiness.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesto pesto

ok, the name's silly, but this version of pesto is really good!  the recipe makes enough to generously sauce 1 lb of your favourite pasta.  developed for rsc #6.  (edited to add that this recipe eventually won ready, set, cook! #6.   i am so proud of this creation and all the favourable reviews it has received - thanks to all who have tried it.)

1. mince and mash the garlic to a paste with salt and peppercorns
2. in a processor or blender , puree spinach with basil , oil , wine , cashews , parmesan , lemon zest and garlic paste
3. the pesto keeps , covered with a thin film of olive oil and chilled , up to 2 weeks
4. this makes enough for 1 lb of pasta
demonstrations.review: This pesto tastes light and is so refreshing! I used a little less olive oil (just added the oil until it came to the right consistency.) I served it with linguine and the family actually favored this dish more after the pasta had cooled, kind of like a pasta salad. Next time, I'll serve the pesto & pasta as a side dish instead of a main meal because I think chicken, fish or steak would go great with this. I'll also try adding this pesto to crostinis and maybe top them with a little feta. Thank you for sharing your recipe.

target.recipe_text:
dad s casserole

complete comfort food. great on a cold day.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. spray 2-3 quart casserole with non-stick cooking spray
3. cook noodles as directed on package
4. brown beef with garlic until cooked through
5. drain
6. add salt , sugar and tomato sauce and simmer for 5 minutes
7. combine sour cream , cream cheese and onion
8. layer 1 / 2 of the noodles then 1 / 2 of the meat mixture in casserole dish
9. spread with sour cream mixture
10. top with remaining noodles and the tomato sauce
11. bake for 30 minutes
12. sprinkle grated cheese on top and bake for another 5 minutes
13. enjoy !
target.review: We liked it, the kids ate it well. It's not really to our normal dinner tastes, but it WAS good. It's very similar to a pasta dish with Gouda cheese that I have so in a lot of ways it tasted, to me, like I forgot the best part of my dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: I've made this multiple times and we ALL love it. I've shared it with everyone, and can't believe that I FINALLY have a pot roast recipe that turns out perfectly every time. My kids love it and I know they will ALWAYS finish their dinner when this is being served. Thank you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeno popper burgers

oh boy, these are good-good-good! if you like stuffed burgers and poppers, you'll love these. :)

1. mix meat , worcestershire sauce , salt , garlic powder , and pepper
2. shape the mixture into 12 thin patties , each about 4 inches in diameter
3. mix the cream cheese , ancho chili powder , cumin , dried onion , and minced jalapeno
4. top 6 patties with the cheese mixture , spreading it to within 1 / 2-inch of the edge
5. cover each patty with one of the remaining 6 patties , sealing the edges well
6. broil or grill the patties , turning only once if possible , until preferred doneness and cheese is melted , about 10 to 15 minutes
7. low-carb serving: top with a bit of grated cheddar , guacamole , and enjoy !
8. high-carb serving: eat with a bun and other condiments
demonstrations.review: I love these. I kept eating LONG after I was full. Which is the sign of true tastiness.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooked shredded beef tacos

nan

1. place beef and onion in slow cooker
2. combine water and seasoning mix in small bowl
3. pour over beef and onion
4. cook on low for 6-8 hours or until tender
5. shred beef with two forks
6. place beef in large bowl
7. stir in taco sauce and chiles
8. fill warmed taco shells with beef mixture
9. top with lettuce , tomato , cheese , and sour cream
demonstrations.review: Oh my, oh my! My family (and I) have become spoiled on this one. The easiest and best taco dish ever! I do not think we'll ever eat tacos with ground meat again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spaghetti with zucchini and garlic

simple and elegant, a great way to use zucchini!

1. pile up 2 or 3 layers of paper towels on a work surface
2. working on the paper towels , shred zucchinis using a grater holding the zucchini at an angle
3. heat a large skillet over moderate heat
4. add extra-virgin olive oil to the pan add chopped garlic to the oil
5. when garlic starts sizzling in oil , add shredded zucchini
6. season zucchini with salt and pepper
7. saute shredded zucchini 7 to 10 minutes
8. add hot , drained pasta to the pan
9. toss spaghetti with zucchini and garlic oil
10. add a couple of handfuls of grated cheese to the pan
11. adjust seasoning and serve
demonstrations.review: I have loved this recipe ever since I saw it on Rachel Ray's show. She always has the quickest and best recipes! The kids love it too. I grate the cheese myself and it melts nicely over noodles and zucchini.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marshmallows  french laundry

i was surfing the internet and found this recipe for marshmallows.  i have since tried a few others and i wished i hadn't wasted my time and ingredients. for one thing, this recipe is extremely easy to follow. (you don't even need a candy thermometer.)secondly, this recipe is foolproof and super easy to make.  the only suggestion i have is to use a quality vanilla extract as the aroma and flavor is unbelieveable! if you've never had homemade marshmallows before, you are in for a real treat!  the texture is so much softer and the flavor is well, ummmm....  marshmallow melting moment.  yummy.  i have a lot of fun making these with my two year old daughter.  i love watching her lick the beaters.  have some fun in your kitchen for a change.  these are wonderful with your favorite hot cocoa.  the list goes on.

1. in a large mixing bowl , sprinkle gelatin over 1 / 2 cup cold water
2. soak 10 minutes
3. meanwhile: combine sugar , corn syrup , 1 / 4 cup water in a small saucepan
4. bring to a boil
5. boil hard for 1 minute
6. pour the boiling syrup into gelatin and mix at high speed
7. add the salt and beat for about 10 - 12 minutes
8. add the vanilla and incorporate into mixture
9. scrape into a 9 x 9 inch pan lined with oiled plastic wrap and spread evenly
10. don't skip the plastic wrap step or the marshmallow mixture will stick and you'll have a very delicious mess !
11. after pouring marshmallow mixture into pan , take another piece of plastic wrap lightly oiled on the side which you will be placing on top of the marshmallow mixture and lightly press marshmallow mixture till flat and even into the pan
12. let marshmallows sit up for about 2 hours
13. remove from pan , dredge whole slab with confectioners sugar and cut into squares
14. each time you cut or slice you will need to keep using the confectioners sugar and dredging each piece so they will not stick to each other and your knife
15. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: So easy and SO fun to make with the kids.

target.recipe_text:
molasses spice spritz

this isn't something i would do just for the heck of it anymore but for the holidays....maybe. i'm posting this as a cathartic thing. i'm passing on my non-diabetic goodies to folks who can offer them a good home. i just can't abandon them without a chance to become good little recipes for someone else. this could go on for some time, i have a lot of recipes! it's been a long time since i made these and i don't honestly recall how long it took to make and press them out so i'm taking my best guess. *please note*: as written the recipe will yield a milder spice flavor. if you prefer a stronger spicy flavor double the spice amounts (or to taste).

1. preheat oven to 400 f
2. stir together flour , baking powder , nutmeg , cinnamon , cloves , and ginger
3. set aside
4. in a large mixing bowl beat together margarine until smooth
5. add molasses and brown sugar and beat until fluffy
6. add egg and vanilla
7. beat well
8. gradually add flour mixture until all combined
9. prepare cookie press with desired design
10. fill press and place cookies two inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet
11. bake in oven for about 6 minutes or until the edges are firm but not browned
12. remove and cool completely on wire racks
target.review:
The dough made it difficult to spritz, but rolling it out and using a cookie cutter made these a true winner!  My husband has been gobbling these for days!  I need to send them to friends ASAP or I'll be making another batch!

NOTE:  If you want to low carb this recipe, try whole wheat flour.  I kept the molassas and brown sugar as-is.  THE BEST COOKIE AROUND!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin cream cheese muffins  like starbucks

these delicious muffins are very close to the kind you can get at starbucks. if you want to cut back on the fat, substitute some or all of the oil with natural unsweetened applesauce.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. mix cream cheese with one egg and 3 tablespoons of sugar
3. put the entire mixture on a piece of wax paper or parchment paper and shape it into a long log
4. put it in the freezer while you mix and fill the pans , up to an hour
5. unwrap and cut with a sharp knife so each cream cheese disk equals 1-2 teaspoons
6. if the cream cheese disks are too big around , cut thick slices and then cut them in half
7. this lets you push it down into the batter easier
8. mix all ingredients together
9. fill muffin tins half full
10. put cream cheese disc in the middle , pressing down
11. sprinkle with 1 tsp chopped nuts
12. bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes , until a toothpick comes out clean from the muffin part
13. let cool in pans for 5 minutes , then remove to racks to cool completely
14. do not touch the cream cheese until it cools
demonstrations.review: Silly me, I didn't read the other comments so didn't know to add sugar to my cream cheese.  That part was not very good at all.  The actual muffin, however, was good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal crispies

i got this recipe out of an old cookbook of my mothers. we like crispie cookies and this one is just the ticket. cook time is per cookie sheet.

1. thoroughly cream shortening , brown sugar and granulated sugar
2. add eggs and vanilla and beat well
3. add sifted flour , salt , soda , oats and nuts
4. mix all well and drop by teaspoons full onto greased baking sheet
5. bake@ 350 degrees f for 10 minutes or until light brown
6. you may make these up into rolls and wrap with wax paper and store in fridge
7. take out and cut 1 / 4" thick and cook
demonstrations.review:
Outstanding recipe, delicious!  Tried to plug in the nutritional facts on my own based on ingredients and was WAY off.  Maybe shortening wasn't added?  I am a carb, calorie, and fat counter.

Either way, FABULOUS!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana cream crepe filling

this goes well with any crepes or you can use this with recipe #209247. cook time is an estimate.

1. combine flour , sugar , cornstarch , and salt in a small saucepan
2. add milk gradually
3. cook , stirring , over low heat until thickened
4. blend a little of the hot mixture into egg yolks
5. stir yolks into saucepan
6. cook 1 minute
7. remove from heat
8. add vanilla and butter
9. cool
10. when ready to serve fold in diced bananas
11. place a small amount of filling on each crepe and roll
demonstrations.review: Not sure what happened.  Tasted too starchy!  But it was good overall.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb almond cookies

during the holidays my family has a longstanding tradition of baking cookie trays for family and friends.  this year, my circle includes a friend who has been advised by her doctor to dramatically reduce her carbohydrate intake. not wanting to leave her out of the cookie circle, i tracked this recipe down on the web and have posted it here for others interested in low-carb baking. the resulting cookie is a little crumbly like a shortbread with a soft nutty flavor. i like the variation, my own, of adding the egg as the cookie holds together more and has a thin marzipan like center. a bit too rich for my low-fat taste buds but a certain hit for a low-carb diet. according to the recipe these have about 2.7g carbs per cookie.

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. using and electric mixer blend softened butter for a minute
3. add remaining ingredients and mix together
4. form dough into walnut sized balls and place onto ungreased cookie sheet
5. the oil from the butter and almond flour grease the sheet as the cookie bakes
6. bake for 5 minutes
7. press down lightly with fork , then continue to bake another 18 minutes
8. the cookies do not brown
9. let cool on sheet for 5 minutes before removing
10. for a more festive look , you can drizzle a little melted chocolate on top
demonstrations.review:
Out of this world good!  Low carb or not, my new favorite cookies!  WOW!!!  

NOTE:  I didn't do the chocolate stuff on top.  I did used blanched almonds for garnish.  NICE!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb snickerdoodles

a cinnamon cookie treat for low carbers or people allergic to wheat flour.  cooking time includes the chilling time.

1. in a mixing bowl beat butter with an electric mixer on
2. medium to high speed for 30 seconds
3. add about half the flour , the 1 cup splenda , the egg , vanilla , baking soda , and cream of tartar
4. beat until thoroughly combined
5. beat in the remaining flour
6. cover and chill for 1 hour
7. combine the 2 tablespoons splenda and the cinnamon in a small bowl
8. shape dough into 1 inch balls
9. roll balls in the splenda-cinnamon mix and place 2 inches apart on an ungreased cookie sheet
10. bake at 350f for 10 to 12 minutes
demonstrations.review: OH-MY-GOSH!  These taste even better than my sugary snickerdoodles.  HANDS DOWN A KEEPER!  Great work "Mercy!"

target.recipe_text:
chicken stroganoff   crock pot

nan

1. put frozen chicken in bottom of crock pot
2. mix soup , sour cream , and onion soup mix
3. pour over chicken
4. cook on low for 7 hours
5. serve over rice or noodles
target.review: This was delicious and as easy as it gets!! I used the "fat" versions, as my family sniffs out fat free in a heartbeat. I added onions at the start, mushrooms (fresh, sliced) halfway through. I made a complete meal dish by adding steamed peas, and fusilli(sp?) pasta. SO good, comforting, filling. Thanks!! -Joanna

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tiny cinnamon rolls

southern living. my kids adore these tiny little treats. we have fun making them together.

1. unroll dough , and separate into 4 rectangles
2. pinch seams together
3. stir together sugar and cinnamon
4. sprinkle evenly over rectangles
5. roll up jellyroll fashion , starting with a long side
6. press edges to seal
7. cut each log into 5 slices and place slices , cut side down in a lightly greased 8-inch round cakepan
8. bake at 350 degrees for 12 minutes
9. stir together powdered sugar , milk , and vanilla in a small bowl until smooth
10. drizzle over warm rolls
demonstrations.review: I was surprised at how good these were-given their simplicity! They sure are small, and mine didn't come out as pretty as some of the photos, but they are yummy! I added a bit more than a tsp of milk for the icing, Also, these took more like 10 minutes prep than 30! Note: at least for me, these were much more puffy than crusty buns

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Delicious! Very tasty, super easy to make-a quick and yummy meal. Served with a cool cucumber salad. It didn't have "heat" as I was expecting-which was great as I don't like spicy!-but the boyfriend just added some more freshly ground pepper atop. I definitely think this would be great with shrimp as well, and plan on adding a little more green onion and sun-dried tomatoes next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flawless sesame chicken  restaurant style

this is the recipe you've been looking for!  it makes a perfect sesame chicken.  this excellent recipe comes out perfect every time with little fuss and inexpensive ingredients you probably have on hand.  this recipe is truly restaurant quality... try it, you won't be disappointed! (recipe courtesy of "reykjaviky" at all recipes)

1. cut the chicken into 1-inch cubes
2. mix the marinade ingredients and marinate the chicken for 20 minutes
3. to prepare the sauce:
4. mix together all of the sauce ingredients
5. pour them into a small pot and bring to a boil , stirring continuously
6. turn the heat down to low and keep warm while you are deep-frying the chicken
7. to deep-fry the chicken:
8. add the marinated chicken pieces a few at a time , and deep-fry until golden brown
9. drain on paper towels and then place chicken in warm oven while you continue frying
10. repeat with the remainder of the chicken
11. just before you are finished deep-frying , bring the sauce back up to a boil
12. place the chicken on a large platter and pour the sauce over
13. sprinkle with sesame seeds
14. serve the sesame chicken with rice
demonstrations.review: This dish was just amazing! I just made a batch and my brother finished every last bite in 10 minutes. As a new cook, I've never successfully fried anything before. This was EASY and the sauce thick and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mars bars rice krispies squares  no bake

i have been making ever since my son was small and even though my son is all grown up now they are still requested --- these bars are best if eaten the same day.

1. melt butter and mars bars over med-low heat in a large saucepan until smooth
2. remove from heat
3. stir in rice krispies cereal , and nuts ,
4. press into a greased 8x8 pan
5. top with chocolate chips , and place under broiler for 30 seconds remove from oven and spread chocolate evenly over squares
6. store in fridge
7. cut into squares , and serve
demonstrations.review: These were pretty yummy treats! I found that they could have done with a little less butter, the bottom was a bit greasy. I give them 4 stars because, while they tasted good, they were very hard. I almost wonder if the bottom might have been better if prepared with marshmallows, like a traditional rice krispie treat? Something to consider for next time. Will post if I give it a try.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy and tasty barbecue chicken sandwiches in the crock pot

this is almost too easy to be called a recipe, but i had to share it anyway. i came up with it one night when i wanted a nice meal but wasn't feeling too motivated. i love crock-pot cooking!

1. remove all visible fat from the chicken and toss it in the crock pot
2. place the onion slices on top of the chicken
3. pour the barbecue sauce over top
4. you may not need the entire jar , just enough to cover the chicken
5. cook it on low for 8 hours or until the chicken is nice and tender
6. shred the chicken with a fork and knife
7. scoop the mixture onto the bottom buns and top it with the top buns
8. or , if you're like my dad , you might prefer leaving the breasts whole and eating it that way
9. voila !
10. an easy weeknight meal that doesn't heat up your kitchen in the summertime !
11. i love this with potato chips and a carrot and raisin salad
demonstrations.review: TOO easy! I put in a bottle of Bullseye (what I had), added a bit of ketchup (like a little sweetness), and used half a vidalia onion. I set it for about 6.5 hours, shredded it at 4 or so, and my brother is currently eating his third sandwich! I put them on toasted buns with a slice of cheese, served with green beans and almonds and some Pirate's Booty! Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
authentic no refrigeration bakery frosting icing

a frosting just like the bakeries use on their cakes and there is no refrigeration required--it may be kept for 3 months covered in the refrigerator  just bring to room temperature before using.  recipe yields 8 cups of frosting.  you will love this!

1. in a large mixing bowl beat the shortening creamer and extracts
2. gradually beat in the confectioners sugar
3. add in enough water until frosting reaches desired consistency
4. add in food coloring until the desired shade is achieved
target.review: I am an experienced cake decorator - who was looking for a non dairy frosting recipe.  This recipe was awesome - I did substitute butter extract for almond though

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin gooey butter cake   paula deen

i originally submitted this without trying it, as it was in response to a request.  i finally got around to trying it last week, and realized there was a mistake, as the ingredients in the cake part should have read: 8 tablespoons butter, melted.  also, you can't "pour" the cake into the pan it has to be patted into the pan like a pie crust.  anyway, here is the revised version.  i also cut down on the sugar, using about 12 ounces or 3/4 of the box.  this is awesome-a paula deen classic!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. to make the cake: combine all of the ingredients and mix well
3. pat batter into a lightly greased 13x9-inch baking pan with hands into an even layer
4. prepare filling
5. to make the filling: in a large bowl , beat the cream cheese and pumpkin until smooth
6. add the eggs , vanilla , and butter , and beat together
7. next , add the powdered sugar , cinnamon , nutmeg , and mix well
8. spread pumpkin mixture over cake batter and bake for 40 to 50 minutes
9. make sure not to over bake as the center should be a little gooey
10. serve with fresh whipped cream or cinnamon-flavored ice cream
demonstrations.review: I brought this to a party and it was gone.  It was delicious.  I love pumpkin, but hate pumpkin pie because of the texture.  This had all the pumpkin flavor I love without the texture if pumpkin pie.  I made exactly as written and used Dunkin Hines yellow cake mix.  I will definately make this recipe many more time in the future.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker crock pot cranberry pork loin roast

if you like lots of gravy then double the whole cranberry sauce and french dressing, for a a larger roast adjust cooing time ---  this also may be made successfully cooked in the oven at low temperature.

1. using a strainer separate the dried onions from the dry powder
2. place the dry onions in a small bowl
3. heat about 3 tablespoons oil in a skillet over medium heat
4. rub the roast all over with 2 tablespoons oil , then season the pork loin with the onion soup powder , black pepper and garlic powder
5. brown the roast on all sides in hot oil then allow to cool slightly or enough for easy handling if stuffing with the garlic cloves
6. make small slits all over in the roast , then stuff with garlic cloves
7. place the roast in the slow cooker
8. in a bowl whisk the french dressing with the cornstarch until smooth then add in the cranberry sauce and dried onions
9. mix until combined
10. pour the mixture over and around the pork
11. cover and cook on high heat for 4 hours or on low for about 7-8 hours or until the pork reaches internal temperature of 160 degrees f
demonstrations.review: I rather enjoyed this recipe.  I made it a while ago but forgot to rate it.  I made it exactly as listed and it was awesome.  None left at all!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s molasses cookies

these are my absolute favorite cookies. every time i go home my mom makes a batch.

1. mix together brown sugar , crisco , molasses and egg
2. add in flour , soda and spices , mix well
3. cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour
4. preheat oven to 375
5. shape dough into walnut-sized balls
6. dip tops in granulated sugar
7. place sugar-side up about 3" apart on cookie sheet
8. bake 10-12 minutes
9. remove immediately from cookie sheet and let cool
demonstrations.review: These cookies are delicious!  I will be making them again for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marvelous middle eastern marinated yogurt lemon chicken

a tangy rich tenderizing marinade recipe for grilled, sauteed or baked chicken.  i adapted it from a lebanese restaurant's marinated kabobs.
you will receive many many compliments!

1. mix the yogurt with the seasonings place in a plastic bag with the chicken
2. marinate for 2 hours to overnight
3. pound chicken in the bag with the marinade to 1 / 2 thick and grill , saute , skewer or bake until lightly browned and cooked through
4. serve with rice or pasta and salad and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This chicken was so tender and so delicious.  Would make again.  Even my little ones ate it all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground chicken ranch burger

i don't remember where i got this recipe but i make the patties ahead and freeze them. they can be cooked frozen on the grill. serve on crusty rolls with your favorite condiments. can also use ground turkey but not even close to as tasty as the chicken. no other seasoning is needed other than the ranch dressing mix.

1. mix all ingredients together
2. mixture will be wet
3. be sure to spray or oil grill and do not turn chicken patties until well browned
4. form into patties and grill or pan fry
5. i usually cook about 3-4 minutes on each side , a little longer may be needed if frozen
6. juice will run clear when done
demonstrations.review: These were yummy - made with chicken breast meat ground.  Only added chopped onions which made them even greater.  We will be making these again!!

target.recipe_text:
blt chicken salad

really good as a light meal served with crusty rolls. easy and quick to make.

1. in a small bowl , combine the first 5 ingredients
2. mix well
3. cover and chill until ready to serve
4. place salad greens on a large serving platter
5. sprinkle with tomatoes , chicken and bacon
6. garnish with eggs
7. drizzle with dressing
target.review: This was really good.  I used ranch dressing instead of the mayo like Chris suggested.  My whole family enjoyed this salad.  The only change that I made is that I added some cubed cheddar cheese.  This salad tastes like a club salad but better!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oat n  toffee cookies

to die for!!!

1. cream butter and sugars
2. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
3. beat in vanilla
4. mix flour , oats , baking soda , baking powder and salt
5. gradually add to creamed mixture
6. stir in toffee bits
7. drop by rounded tbs onto ungreased baking sheets
8. bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes , until light golden brown
9. cool 1 minute before removing from pans to wire rack
demonstrations.review: Chewy and delicious!  I used Skor bits because that's what I had on hand.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
world s best butter cookies

i tested 8 different butter cookie recipes, looking for the "perfect" butter cookie. it had to be buttery, a little crumbly (like shortbread), and not too sweet. this is the winner. i think these are the worlds best butter cookie, courtesy of chef alice medrich.

1. beat the butter , sugar , salt and vanilla together until smooth and creamy
2. mix in the egg yolk until well incorporated , scraping down the sides of the bowl at least once
3. add the flour and mix just until incorporated
4. scrape onto a lightly floured board and knead a few times , just until the dough smooths out
5. turn onto a sheet of plastic wrap and roll into a log , wrap up and refrigerate for several hours or freeze
6. before baking , preheat the oven to 325f
7. line your baking sheets with parchment
8. slice the dough into slices about 1 / 8" thick and place them on the sheets about an inch apart
9. bake until just beginning to turn golden around the edges , about 16-18 minutes
10. you could roll the dough out and cut shapes
11. you could slice them even thinner and sandwich them with chocolate or jam or lemon curd
12. you could make them and then dip them half into chocolate
13. you could just make them and eat them , which is my favorite
14. whatever you do , they will be delicious
demonstrations.review: Wonderful buttery cookies with a flakey texture that were not too sweet (just like PetitFour described them).  The flavor of these cookies reminds me of those Danish butter cookies that come in a round tin and are sold mostly during the holidays.  My kids loved these cookies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dutch apple bread

the crumb topping on this bread makes it extra special. it's an old taste of home recipe.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease a 9x5x3" loaf pan
3. in a mixing bowl , cream butter and sugar
4. beat in eggs and vanilla
5. combine flour , baking soda and salt , and stir into the creamed mixture alternately with the buttermilk
6. fold in apple and nuts
7. pour into prepared pan and sprinkle topping evenly over the bread
8. bake for 55 to 60 minutes , or until knife inserted into bread comes out clean
9. cool in pan for 10 minutes before removing to a wire rack to cool completely
10. topping:
11. combine the flour , sugar , brown sugar and cinnamon well
12. cut in butter until the mixture is crumbly
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed this mildly flavored and lightly sweet bread.  I substituted half of the white sugar for brown sugar and I used one cup of finely chopped granny smith apples.  We warmed up buttered slices of the bread for breakfast.  We especially liked the crumb topping.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic blondies

traditional blondies, tastes a little like cookie dough even after baked. always asked for the recipe!!!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 inch pan
3. cream butter & sugars until pale brown and thick
4. add the eggs one at a time and then add vanilla
5. with a wooden spoon , stir in chocolate chips , then add the flour , baking powder & salt
6. spread into the prepared pan
7. bake for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very tasty.  I used half butter and half margarine and the blondies turned out like a cross between a cookie and a cake.  I doubled the amount of chocolate chips because we love chocolate.  The blondies were quite tall.  The next time that I make this recipe, I am going to try dividing the batter between a 9x13 pan and an 8x8 pan.  These were especially good heated up in the microwave for a few seconds and then topped with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.....pure heaven!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butterscotch pumpkin cake

a great bundt cake recipe from the good people at nestle.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease 12-cup bundt pan
3. microwave butterscotch chips in small , microwave-safe bowl on medium-high power for 1 minute
4. stir
5. microwave at additional 10-20 second intervals , stirring until smooth
6. cool to room temperature
7. combine flour , granulated sugar , baking powder , cinnamon , salt and nutmeg in medium bowl
8. stir together melted chips , morsels , pumpkin , vegetable oil , eggs and vanilla extract in large bowl with wire whisk
9. stir in flour mixture
10. spoon batter into prepared bundt pan
11. bake for 40 to 45 minutes or until wooden toothpick inserted in cake comes out clean
12. cool in pan on wire rack for 30 minutes
13. remove to wire rack to cool completely
14. sprinkle with powdered sugar if desired
demonstrations.review: Wonderful flavor!  I made two loaves of pumpkin bread with this recipe.  After reading Jo Ann L's review, I decided to melt the chips over a double boiler with 1 tbs milk.  After the chips were melted, I incorporated the pumpkin.  This cooled the chips without making them lumpy.  I also added the rest of the bag of unmelted butterscotch chips to the recipe and that caused the bread to stick to the bottom of the pan.  I don't think that there would have been a problem with the bread sticking if I had not added  the extra chips.  Lastly I added 1/3 cup of finely chopped nuts.  I am very pleased with the results of this recipe.

target.recipe_text:
chili s monterey chicken

from copykat.com (http://www.copykat.com)

this is traditionally served as a sandwich but may be served as is!

1. pound chicken breast until it is somewhat flattened , and season with salt and pepper
2. spray pam in a nonstick skillet , and cook chicken breast until it is done
3. transfer to a serving plate
4. top chicken breast with barbeque sauce , bacon , and cheese
5. broil chicken breast in the oven , or melt the cheese in a microwave
6. sprinkle with a small amount of cold chopped tomatoes and chives
target.review: Scrumptious chicken! I had this at another restaurant than Chilis and loved it so I was looking for a recipe.  I'm glad I found this one. It was so good my DH said how good it was 3 different times.  Thanks for posting it and I'll definitely serve it again.  Nancy

demonstrations.recipe_text:
home fried potatoes

nan

1. peel and cube potatoes
2. cook in oil in covered skillet , turning often about 5 minutes
3. add onions , salt and pepper to taste and continue to cook over l ow heat until potatoes are almost cooked , turning often
4. remove cover and continue cooking until well browned and slightly crisped
5. serves 2 to
demonstrations.review: This is the way my Granny always made her potatoes so I'll go ahead and rate it as scrump-dilly-ishous!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spaghetti sauce mix

yum

1. combine the first eight ingredients
2. store in an airtight container in a cool dry place up to 1 year
3. to use: stir in 1 / 4 cup spaghetti sauce mix , water and tomato paste
4. bring to a boil
5. boil and stir for 2 minutes
6. reduce heat
7. cover and simmer for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I made this for dinner the other night since I didn't have any pre-made sauce.  We loved it and it was so quick and easy. I always have the ingredients on hand I will be making this and using it from now on.  Not only was it delicious but will also be a cost-efficient meal. Thank you for posting this great recipe.
Nancy

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dry ranch dressing mix

easy to make and wonderful to have on hand. a real money saver. great to give bottles of these great dry mixes as shower gifts.

1. put crackers through blender on high speed until powdered
2. add parsley , minced onions , and dill weed
3. blend again until powdered
4. dump into bowl
5. stir in onion salt , garlic salt , onion powder , and garlic powder
6. put into container with tight-fitting lid
demonstrations.review: This is the BEST! I made it using only 1/2 the dill because I was afraid it would be too much. (Personal taste) I added some Hormel Real Bacon Bits to make it into Bacon Ranch and it tasted even better than my favorite that costs about $4.00 a jar. This will be my fav from now on. No more store-bought second best for me! Thanks a bunch Barbara.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas best cheese dip  chile con queso

this is a delicious cheese dip that my daughter makes.  the cream cheese gives it a wonderful consistency. all the fresh ingredients make this a dip that you will be asked for over and over again! please note i have put "to taste" on alot of the ingredients as it depends on how big your bunch of veggies are.  if you actually get lucky enough to have any left it keeps in the fridge a good while and reheats great. i usually serve/take this dip in a crockpot so it stays warm.

1. melt cheeses together in microwave or on stove top
2. stir in all other ingredients
3. serve warm
demonstrations.review:
I made this at work today and served it to 6 people.  Almost all of it was eaten and one of the girls, who is from Africa, said she will make this at home and eat it for breakfast, lunch and dinner. I only put 2 jalapenos because some didn't like it too hot but I left the seeds in and when I make it at home I will put more. The hotter the better!  Everyone gave it 5 stars and if there were more so would it score!
Thanks so much for a delicious dip, much better than plain old rotel dip.  Nancy

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the lady and sons easy peach cobbler   paula deen

it was an instant hit on the first day paula deen offered this dessert at the lady & sons, and remains so today. this delicious cobbler can be found on their dessert trays at both lunch and dinnertime.
 it's so easy to make you won't believe it! cooks notes: if they are available by all means use fresh peaches. in a saucepan, mix two cups fresh peach slices with one cup sugar and one cup water. bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. an almost equally good product is frozen peach slices. simply follow the instructions for the fresh peach slices. note: this is an adopted (late in 2006) recipe and there was already some discussion about the amount of butter necessary in reviews made previous to my inheriting this recipe: now that i have made it myself, i can say that for me at least, 60 grams (1/4 cup) of butter was fine, (by all means use a little less if you prefer) and my dumplings didn't turn out doughy at all... what i did mess up was using a larger can of peaches (non-metric sizes of canned fruit don't translate perfectly into metric ones), so i thought that the extra wouldn't matter much, mine was swimming rather a lot in the juice at the bottom and next time i will use all the peaches but only half or 3/4 of the juice from my metric sized can.. taste was excellent and guests devoured it. i'm delighted to have inherited this recipe, so to both paula deen and the previous zaar owner: thanks for an excellent recipe !!!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. place butter in oven in a 2-quart baking dish to melt
3. stir sugar and flour together and mix well
4. slowly add milk and continue to stir to prevent the batter from lumping
5. being careful not to burn yourself , remove hot baking dish containing melted butter from oven
6. pour batter directly over butter in baking dish
7. spoon fruit on top of batter , then gently pour syrup on top
8. sprinkle with cinnamon , if using
9. the most important part of this dish is not stirring the mixture
10. bake for 30 to 45 minutes or until golden brown
11. your batter will rise above your fruit , producing the most wonderful of crusts
12. serve warm with vanilla ice cream or fresh whipped cream
demonstrations.review: This turned out beautifully for me.  I've made similar recipes many times and had doughy results so was frustrated.  One of the women I worked with used the same type recipe and I asked her why hers wasn't doughy and she gave me a great tip.  I hope some of you will try it that like your dumpling part to be firmer.  Put your peaches and their juice in a sauce pan and bring to a boil before pouring them into the batter.  I think you'll be as pleasantly surprised as I was  Thank you for sharing this recipe.

target.recipe_text:
slow cooker chicken  tomato and white bean soup

love the ease of my slow cooker! also from low carb slow cooker book by broihier and mayone.

1. place vegetables , garlic , salt and pepper in crock pot
2. top with the chicken pieces , butter , broth and bouillon
3. do not stir
4. cover and cook on low for 7 1 / 2 hours
5. stir in drained tomatoes and beans
6. continue to cook 1 / 2 hour more
7. before serving , stir in parsley and tabasco sauce
target.review: This was excellent. Loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chinese chicken balls with sweet and sour sauce

don't bother ordering chinese chicken balls make these at home they are just as good if not even better and the sweet and sour sauce is the same as what is served at your chinese restaurant!-- these are a great weekend snack or can be served as appetizers, if you want some extra flavor to you chicken batter feel free to add in some garlic or onion powder or spices of choice --- this makes a large amount so you may want to reduce the chicken ball batter amount by half (using 4 chicken breasts) --- note: the sauce recipe is one you may have to make a few times before you get the consistancy and sweetness to your liking, 1 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup lightly packed brown will give you a sweet sauce you may reduce the white sugar amount by a few tablespoons

1. to make the sweet and sour sauce sauce
2. in a saucepan combine the first 5 ingredients until combined
3. in a cup or bowl whisk the cold water or pineapple juice with cornstarch until smooth and well blended , then whisk vigorously into the ketchup mixture
4. bring to a boil stirring or whisking constantly over medium-high heat until bubbly
5. reduce the heat to medium-low and continue simmering and mixing until thickened remove from heat and allow to sit at room temperature while making the chicken balls or you may cool to room temperature then refrigerate until ready to use
6. to make the chicken balls: in a large bowl combine flour , cornstarch , baking powder , baking soda , garlic powder
7. add in water and sesame oil
8. whisk vigorously until smooth
9. add in chicken pieces
10. using clean handsand mix until well coated
11. heat oil in a deep-fryer or dutch oven to 375 degrees
12. carefully dip the battered chicken pieces in hot oil and fry until golden brown
13. remove to a paper towel
14. sprinkle with seasoning salt immediately after frying if desired
15. serve immediately with sweet and sour sauce
16. delicious !
demonstrations.review: This was so amazing!  I am an American living over seas and was craving some Chinese food.  This was better then the real thing.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potsie s creamed chicken and biscuits casserole

this is a wonderful and simple to prepare comfort food using things you probably already have around. kids love it- but so do adults. at least, in this home. try it. it is one of my quick and easy favorites. this is my first submitted recipe... be kind.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease the bottom and sides of an 11x7 inch baking dish or 10 inch quiche dish
3. chop the onion
4. heat butter in a small nonstick skillet and saute until tender
5. combine cooked onion , soup , chicken , milk , pimiento , and mayo in a bowl and then turn into the prepared baking dish
6. bake for 15 minutes and remove from oven
7. sprinkle 1 cup of the cheese over the baked mixture
8. arrange biscuits decoratively in a single layer and sprinkle remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese over them
9. return casserole to oven and bake until biscuits are golden brown and sauce is bubbly , usually about 20 minutes longer
10. the last time i made this i used a 1 / 4 cup of fat free mayo and 1 / 4 cup of sour cream
11. i think it was delicious ! also -- i took the suggestion of adding a cup of cooked green peas
12. what a terrific idea ! i loved it ! i think i might add two cups next time
13. thanks to you all for making my humble recipe and leaving your suggestions
14. you greatly improved a recipe i was already proud of
15. thanks so much
demonstrations.review: This was quick and easy.  Next time I will add mixed veggies but other than that it was very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker beans

this can easily make into a meal.  very filling and satisfying.

1. brown beef and onion , set aside
2. mix together bacon , oil , catsup , worcestershire sauce , vinegar , mustard , salt and brown sugar
3. add to beef
4. stir in b eans
5. pour mixture into a slow cooker
6. heat on high for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Easy and I loved it and so did my toddlers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese ravioli with pumpkin sage sauce

creamy homemade alfredo sauce, fresh cheese ravioli and a luscious pumpkin-sage sauce combine for this quick and easy meal! great served with a crisp green salad and a crusty baguette, -or- may be served as a starter. notes: this dish from the mantua region of northern italy is traditionally eaten on christmas eve. you can add a bit of fruit chutney, and sub pistachios for the pine nuts. enjoy!

1. prepare ravioli according to package directions
2. drain the ravioli and set aside , keep warm
3. meanwhile , in a skillet saute the green onions in the wine and butter over medium heat until the onions are softened and the butter is melted and begins to foam
4. stir in the pumpkin and heat through
5. remove from heat and blend in the cream , parmesan cheese , salt , pepper , and the sage leaves , stirring well to combine
6. to serve:
7. spoon the warm sauce over the ravioli
8. garnish with parmesan cheese , snipped parsley and toasted pine nuts
demonstrations.review: I didn't have any sage but this still turned out excellent.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot low country shrimp and grits

from one of gooseberry patch's newest cookbooks ("fall, family & friends") comes this very southern recipe for shrimp & grits.  now i am not southern (my dh is), but we both love grits. i do know this dish is very traditional in the southeast.  in a check on amazon, i discovered a cookbook devoted entirely to shrimp & grits, can you believe it?  this is an easy version to be made in the crock pot. y'all,  i haven't try it yet, but as soon as i find the grits (scarce here in the southwest) i'm going to -- dh can't wait!

1. combine chicken broth , salt and grits in the crock pot
2. cover and cook on low 6-8 hours
3. two hours before serving , saute the peppers , onions , garlic , and shrimp in the 2 tablespoons butter until tender
4. add this mixture to the crock pot along with the cheeses , tomatoes with chilies , and cayenne , if using
5. continue to cook on high an additional 2 hours
demonstrations.review: Very nice, a little spicy for the kids but good.  I will try without the chiles next time.

target.recipe_text:
awesome bacon tomato dip

oh, you have to try this one!! my family loves dips and spreads, and even the guys got really into this one. i even caught my uncle (who thinks guys are too "macho" for dips), eating it straight from the bowl with a spoon!! best when made day of, and lettuce added just before serving. it gets soggy:(

1. in medium bowl , with mixer , blend sour cream , mayonnaise , cream cheese , cheddar cheese , chopped onion and green pepper , garlic powder , and black pepper
2. crumble bacon into small pieces and add to mixture
3. add chopped tomato and stir well
4. garnish with shredded lettuce just before serving , if desired
5. serve with townhouse crackers or wheat thins
6. also good served in a bread bowl with bread cubes to dip
target.review: Great dip recipe!  This was so delicious.  It has a taste like homemade Thousand Island dressing, which I love!  Thanks for this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steak san marino

nan

1. combine flour , salt , and pepper in small bowl
2. dredge each steak in flour mixture , then place in bottom of crockpot
3. combine remaining ingredients in small bowl
4. pour over meat in crockpot
5. cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours , or high for 4 to 5 hours
6. serve steaks and sauce over hot cooked rice
7. besure to discard bay leaf before serving
demonstrations.review: I love easy crockpot meals, and this is a great one!  It smells wonderful while it's cooking too!  The meat was sooooo tender and the spices are perfect.  Thanks for sharing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
charlie s famous chicken salad with grapes

a really great guy i used to work with would make this and bring in to share. we all loved it so much and would beg for more! sounds strange with the grapes, but it's so good! allow time for salad to chill.

1. combine all ingredients
2. chill
3. serve with just about anything- crackers , chips , rolls , bread or bagel
demonstrations.review: I really enjoyed this, it's a different and delicious way to prepare chicken salad.  I left out the nuts because I don't care for them.  I love the extra 'wang' that the grapes and Worcestershire add.  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat potato vegetable chowder

nan

1. bring liquid to boil in a deep soup kettle
2. add all vegetables and seasonings
3. turn down heat to simmer and partially cover the pot
4. simmer until vegetables are tender
5. serve hot with crusty whole wheat bread and a light fruit dessert
6. variation: almost any vegetable but onions , tomatoes , and the potatoes can be substituted for another vegetable
7. don't use the cabbage family because the flavor is too radically changed
8. green peas and baby lima beans are a great addition , as is 1 / 2 cup of corn kernels
demonstrations.review: This was delicious and had a great, rich tomato flavor.  I more than doubled the recipe so that I would have lots of leftovers to eat.  Thanks for sharing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta and spinach

delicious meat-free dinner. its the only way i can get my kids to eat spinach! sometimes, to please hubby, i'l add cooked chicken or italian sausage.

1. cook pasta according to directions for al dente , or just barely tender
2. meanwhile , in a large bowl , combine the 2 / 3 c
3. parmesan cheese and all the other sauce ingredients
4. mix well
5. drain the pasta , toss it with the sauce , and turn it into a greased 9x13 baking dish
6. sprinkle the 2 tbs of parmesan over the top , and bake at 375 for 25 to 30 minutes , or until bubbly and lightly browned on top
demonstrations.review: This is really good!  I only used one package of frozen spinach and it was plenty for us.  This is definately a keeper!  Thanks for the new recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
exceptional potato salad

this recipe is the result of endless attempts to recapture the taste of my mother's wonderful potato salad! it is basically your traditional potato salad with some added elegance.

1. sprinkle potatoes with the vinegar , salt , sugar and celery seed
2. add onion , celery and sweet pickle
3. mix dijon mustard and miracle whip salad dressing together well and gently mix into ingredients
4. fold in the hard-cooked sliced eggs
5. sprinkle top of salad very lightly with paprika , overlap three hard-boiled egg slices in a circle and place sprig of parsley in center chill and serve
demonstrations.review: WOW!  This is exceptional potato salad, I really like the sugar in it it's something different I've never had in potato salad.

target.recipe_text:
rich  rich  rich   vanilla and  fig squares

these lovely treats melt in your mouth, they simply disappear, they are so delicious, i can never seem to keep them around for even an afternoon. 

come on,  try them, i dare you, i double dare you! 

the vanilla sugar adds so much to the squares. it's very easy to make, here is a great recipe that i used ... recipe #22071

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees
2. in a large bowl cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy
3. add egg yolks , one at a time , beating well
4. next add the vanilla and orange rind
5. now slowly beat in the flour , until well blended
6. spread the crust batter evenly into an ungreased 13 x 9 " pan
7. bake in a 375 degree oven for 15 minutes , remove and set aside to cool until needed
8. reduce heat in oven to 300 degrees
9. in a medium size pot , add the figs , raisins , 1 / 2 cup coconut , orange rind , sugar , vanilla extract , boiling water and butter
10. boil over medium heat for about 30 minutes until the filling is thick and resembles jam
11. spread the filling over the crust and bake in a 300 degree oven for 10 minutes
12. remove squares from oven and place on rack , sprinkle with the remaining coconut , cool , then cut and enjoy !
target.review: I loved this recipe, DH said 'so-so', the crust was very goopy.  No flour is listed in the ingredients but it is in the directions.  I added some but I guess not enough.  Please say how much.  I used the vanilla suagr.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatball sub casserole

wonderful take on the italian meatball sandwich. taken from "quick cooking" magazine.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. in a bowl , combine onions , bread crumbs and parmesan cheese
3. add beef and mix well
4. shape into 1-inch balls
5. place on a rack
6. in a shallow baking pan , bake for 15-20 minutes or until no longer pink
7. reduce oven temperature to 350
8. meanwhile , arrange bread in a single layer in an ungreased 13x9x2" baking dish
9. combine cream cheese , mayo , italian seasoning and pepper
10. spread over the bread
11. sprinkle with 1 / 2 cup mozzarella
12. combine sauce , water and garlic
13. add meatballs
14. pour over cheese mixture
15. sprinkle with remaining mozzarella
16. bake , uncovered at 350 for 30 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: Very good. Thank you.  I used Italian Eggplant Balls #306857 instead of the meat and the casserole came out perfectly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mmmm mushroom gravy

load your mashers with taste...not with guilt! a scrumptious gravy recipe of the realage webbi....it being so healthy is simply a plus ;)

1. heat oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat
2. add onion and garlic
3. cook , stirring often , until softened , about 5 minutes
4. add mushrooms and cook , stirring often , until they begin to release their juices , about 10 minutes
5. add broth , tamari , thyme and sage
6. simmer for 10 minutes
7. mix cornstarch and water in a small bowl
8. stir into the sauce and simmer , stirring often , until slightly thickened , about 10 minutes more
9. season with pepper
10. if you prefer a smooth gravy , pass it through a fine sieve
11. enjoy hot
demonstrations.review: Very tasty. Will be making this again. Thanks natsxox

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s best ever banana nut bread

this is dark, rich and moist.  it is sweet and flavorful and i am told unlike any other people have tasted.  some liken it mimi's cafe, but say it is better.  my mother, belen, who passed away at the age of 100 had been making this for as long as i can remember.   please follow the instructions regarding putting the vinegar in the milk in one cup and the baking soda in warm water in another before mixing it with other ingredients.   it makes a difference.

1. mix together 4 tablespoons milk with 1 teaspoons white vinegar in a cup
2. mix together 1 ts
3. baking soda with 1 tablespoons warm water in a separate cup
4. beat sugar and margarine until blended
5. add eggs and bananas and mix
6. add everything else
7. prepare a large
8. large loaf pan by coating it with shortening ,
9. flour and lining the bottom with waxed
10. paper
11. bake at 325 degrees for 1 to 1 hours
12. toothpick test for doneness
demonstrations.review: This is the only banana bread recipe I use, it's that good.  I've reduced the sugar to 1/2 cup and will try less next time.  The technique for making the bread reminds me of the original Toll House cookie recipe. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian eggplant patties  polpettti de melanzane

very good meat alternative!  great as an appetizer, sandwich, or main meal topped off with good  chunky tomato sauce.  comes from my mother adelia who has been making these forever.  try these, you will love them!

1. place the diced eggplant and in a small deep bowl
2. season with salt and compress with heavy object
3. let it stand for approximately 1 hour
4. squeeze out excess juice and set aside
5. in a small frying pan , begin to heat 6 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil , 2 cracked garlic cloves , hot pepper , eggplant for approximately 3 minutes until garlic brown and crisp
6. discard the garlic
7. in a bowl , beat eggs , add grated cheese , remaining 2 tablespoons of extra-virgin olive oil , chopped fresh basil , and parsley
8. add the eggplant , , 2 garlic finely chopped cloves , and bread crumbs , and mix thoroughly
9. heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick frying pan or skillet
10. wet your hands and begin to scoop 1 / 2 cup of mix to make patties
11. start to fry when oil is very hot
12. cook for 4 minutes on each side until golden brown
13. remove from pan and place on tray lined with paper towels to cool and absorb excess oil
14. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: With the eggplant from the garden, I tried this last night and had good results.  It worked, the patties stayed together.  Just used a shake of crushed red pepper, I'm a coward, instead of the diced chili pepper and it was fine.  Very tastey.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffed baby eggplant

this is a recipe my aunt passed on to me.  she's been making these for as long as i can remember, and everyone loves them.  you can use whatever bread is on hand.  recipe works well with white, wheat, or italian bread crumbs.  if you are in a hurry, you can skip the final step of baking in the oven, and cook the eggplants on top of the stove.  this dish is also great topped with tomato sauce and sliced mozzarella cheese just before placing in the oven.  just be sure to cover the pan with aluminum foil before baking, venting with a few knife slits.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. prepare eggplants by slicing them in half lengthwise
3. scoop out the inside of the eggplant and cut into cubes
4. lay cubes on several paper towels and squeeze any moisture out of them by hand
5. boil shells in a large stockpot for 2 minutes and allow to cool
6. place a tablespoon of olive oil in a hot skillet
7. add eggplant , onion , and garlic and saute
8. in a large mixing bowl , stir the saute mixture into the remaining ingredients and combine well
9. add a second tablespoon of water if mixture is too dry
10. if mixture is too loose , add more bread crumbs
11. fill the cooled eggplant shells with the mixture
12. add a tablespoon of olive oil to a hot skillet
13. place eggplants top side down in skillet and brown over medium heat
14. place browned stuffed baby eggplants in a baking dish
15. drizzle with remaining olive oil and bake for 30 minutes in a 350 degree oven
demonstrations.review: Have made this twice already because the recipe is very good.  Thank you.

target.recipe_text:
cheyenne s fudgy dutch cocoa brownies   fudge icing

this is a recipe that my 13 year old daughter came up with after trying different recipes over the past month...we all deemed it a "keeper" in our house and will keep making brownies this way from now on!  so simple, and i didn't even have to go to the store to buy any more ingredients!  looks cake-like, but tastes so fudgy and chewy...really good brownies!  p.s. my baby, cheyenne, took all of the pictures herself while i was at work!!!  awwww!  :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease an 8x8x2-inch glass pan
3. in a medium saucepan , melt butter or margarine
4. remove melted butter or margarine from heat , add cocoa , and stir until well blended
5. add sugar and mix well
6. add eggs , one at a time , and beat well
7. stir in vanilla , flour and salt
8. do not overbeat
9. fold in nuts , if desired
10. spread in prepared glass pan and bake 25 to 30 minutes , or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean , but sides are not yet hard and crusty
11. cool completely before topping with icing
12. fudge icing:
13. in a small bowl , beat melted butter , cocoa , corn syrup and vanilla until blended
14. add powdered sugar and water , and beat until spreading consistency
15. after spreading icing onto cooled brownies , cool in fridge for at least 45 minutes
target.review: The best brownies I've EVER had. I didn't use the nuts because I didn't have any, and I just used the unsweetened cocoa powder I had in my pantry instead of the Dutch-processed kind. I've never made from-scratch brownies before, and I'll never make another boxed one again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
imitation crab cakes

don't let the title fool you, these are so good! i adapted them from a regular crab cake recipe on allrecipes when our grocer had imitation crab on sale. the crab cakes may need 2 eggs as reviewers have noted, it depends on how moist your imitation crab is and how finely you flake it. the cakes won't seem to hold together well but they will cook up nicely, just be sure to make them small and carefully flip them when they're nice and brown on the bottom. 

i've also made these with finely diced red pepper and cilantro, omitting the green onions, and that is probably our new favorite way to prep.

1. heat 1 tablespoon oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat
2. saute green onions briefly until tender
3. combine crabmeat , sauteed green onions , egg , mayonnaise , dry mustard , crushed crackers , cayenne pepper , garlic powder , old bay seasoning , lemon , salt and pepper with your hands
4. work the ingredients together so they start to stick together
5. form into 1 / 2 inch thick patties
6. heat 1 tablespoon oil in the non-stick skillet over medium-medium high heat
7. works really well on a flat griddle
8. cook cakes until nicely browned on each side
9. drain briefly on paper towels and serve hot
demonstrations.review: These were fantastic! I didn't have Old Bay so I used some Creole seasoning. They had LOTS of flavor. YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab bisque in 20 minutes

quick corn and crab bisque. wonderful on a cold night when your in a hurry! easily doubled, leftovers freeze well.

1. combine all ingredients except crabmeat in a medium-sized saucepan over low heat
2. heat until hot approximately 10-15 minutes , but do not overheat or it will scorch !
3. add crab and heat through
