4. remove bay leaf before serving
demonstrations.review: I used 2 cans of crab meat instead of the imitation crab, because it was less expensive and I don't really like the flavor of fake crab. Other than that the recipe was great, quick and easy. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wasabi sesame tuna

if you like the flavor of wasabi you will like this recipe. these do not come out of the pan fiery hot, but with wasabi flavor. you can always add more heat if you wish.

1. in a shallow dish , combine the soy sauce , wasabi paste and cracked black pepper
2. mix well
3. add the tuna and turn until thoroughly coated on both sides
4. let sit for 10 minutes or plan ahead and let marinate overnight in a zipper bag or foodsaver bag
5. coat a pan with nonstick cooking spray and preheat over high heat
6. place the sesame seeds in another shallow dish , add the tuna and turn to coat completely
7. grill the tuna for 1 to 2 minutes per side , or until browned or cooked to desired doneness
8. slice thinly and serve with rice or stir fry
9. remember fish cooks fast and will be dry and chewy if overcooked
demonstrations.review: I didn't taste any wasabi, but it was otherwise ok.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new england clam chowder

very rich and creamy chowder served at skipjack's restaurant in boston, massachusetts

1. bring bottled clam juice and potatoes to boil in heavy large saucepan over high heat
2. reduce heat to medium-low
3. cover and simmer until potatoes are tender , about 10 minutes
4. remove from heat
5. melt butter in heavy large pot over medium heat
6. add bacon and cook until bacon begins to brown , about 8 minutes
7. add onions , celery , garlic and bay leaf and saut until vegetables soften , about 6 minutes
8. stir in flour and cook 2 minutes
9. gradually whisk in reserved juices from clams
10. add potato mixture , clams , half and half and hot pepper sauce
11. simmer chowder 5 minutes to blend flavors , stirring frequently
12. season to taste with salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: Very tasty! The only thing i did differently was I used 2 10oz cans of clams. It seemed like a perfect amount. Everything else stayed the same. So good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashion berry cobbler

very good served slightly warm with ice cream and recipe has been in family for over 100 years

1. cream butter and sugar together , then add milk on slow speed
2. sift dry ingredients together and add to wet a couple of tablespoon at a time , until smooth
3. batter should be very thick paste , turn out into greased 13 x 9 x 2 inch pan , put berries on top of batter , sprinkle with remaining 1 1 / 2 cups sugar , and pour 2 1 / 2 cups boiling water over top , dot with remaining 3 tbsp butter
4. bake at 425f for 30 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Yum! I used this recipe to use up the wild mulberries we have in our back yard. 1 and 1/2 cups sugar on to of the berries seemed like way too much. I only used 1/2 cup and it was perfectly sweetened.

target.recipe_text:
chocolate eclair torte

i always get asked to bring this to pot-luck type dinners.

1. line bottom of 9x13-inch dish with crackers
2. mix pudding and milk
3. fold in whipped topping
4. spoon layer of pudding mixture over crackers
5. add another layer of crackers , then pudding mix again then final layer of crackers
6. spread chocolate frosting over top
7. chill in refrigerator for at least 2 hours
target.review: This is the standard dessert for every family function.  I rarely have leftovers.  Everybody loves it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot chocolate  cocoa blocks

simply swirl these blocks of chocolate into a mug of steaming hot milk for a special treat!  another great recipe from king arthur flour.

1. 1) line an 8" x 8" pan with parchment paper or aluminum foil
2. 2) heat the cream and condensed milk over low heat until steaming
3. 3) remove from the heat and add the chocolate
4. allow it to gently melt
5. 4) after about 10 minutes , return the chocolate mixture to low heat to completely melt the chocolate
6. 5) whisk vigorously until the mixture is thick and shiny
7. 6) pour the chocolate mixture into the pan
8. shake the pan gently to level
9. 7) set aside overnight to slowly set up
10. 8) run a knife around the edge of the pan and turn out onto a clean cutting surface
11. 9) slice into 1 " cubes
12. heat a knife in hot water and wipe dry before each cut , for smoothest cuts
13. 10) stick a wooden stick into the center of each block
14. 11) wrap in waxed paper , parchment , or plastic wrap to store
15. 12) you can also add a few drops of flavoring oil to the mixture , or roll the blocks in cocoa or crushed candy canes , to kick it up a notch
demonstrations.review: These blocks are yummy and very easy to make.  I gave them away as gifts too, which received raves and requests for the recipe.  I will be making them every year and in between.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage gravy

this is a really easy and super deelicious recipe for sausage gravy over biscuits, you will want to make this one again and again!

1. cook sausage in skillet
2. drain fat
3. sprinkle flour over sausage and stir well
4. cook flour and sausage together for about 5 - 7 minutes
5. add milk
6. cook over medium heat until thickened
7. add pepper
8. serve over biscuits
demonstrations.review: This an awesome recipe.  I needed a gallon of gravy so I had to times it by 4.  I also used pork and bacon sausage by Farmland--very flavorful.  I also added some salt as a personal preference.  It will sit overnight for the brunch tomorrow, so I know the flavor will be even better.  I am now going to make simple biscuits using heavy cream and recipe #263699.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate spritz cookies

from an ad for nestle chocolate chips.  prep time includes chill time.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. melt over hot water chocolate chips
3. remove from heat
4. set aside
5. in a bowl , combine butter , sugar and vanilla
6. beat until creamy
7. add eggs
8. beat well
9. stir in melted chocolate
10. gradually add flour
11. chill 30-45 minutes
12. place dough in cookie press
13. use star
14. place cinnamon candies on each cookie
15. bake for 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: These cookies were great! Instead of the press, I formed small balls, rolled in ground pecans, and pressed a M&M into them.  My 4-year old granddaughter helped me make them and she ate several.  Great recipe.  Kathy

demonstrations.recipe_text:
make ahead burritos

i needed to use up some leftover chicken, and i didn't want to feel like i was "eating chicken again".  it was the fastest burrito i've ever made, and i'm going to freeze the leftovers individually.  who needs to purchase frozen burritos when you can make your own with ingredients you have on hand.  the only thing i did differently is i used around 7 ounces of green chilies and instead of the burrito seasoning mix i added my own seasoning (fresh cilantro, garlic, cumin, and chili powder).  recipe from america's best church supper recipes/jennifer shafer (durham, nc).

1. in a large skillet or saucepan , combine meat , salsa , beans , chilies , seasoning , and water
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes or until heated through
4. spoon abour 1 / 3 cup off-center on each tortilla and top with a cheese strip
5. fold edge of tortilla nearest filling over to cover
6. fold ends of tortilla over filling and roll up
7. wrap individually in aluminum foil
8. freeze for up to 2 months
demonstrations.review: One star only because there are no directions on what to do with them when they come out of the freezer. Are they heated or not?   Recipe does sound delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jj s beer cocktail meatballs

simple, fast, 4 ingredients, taste wonderful. i first had these at my friends wedding reception 40 years ago, and fell in love with them.

1. make your meatballs about quarter sized , and either fry or bake them draining grease well
2. in a deep saucepan or crock pot put in the sugar , ketchup , and add beer
3. mix well until sugar is pretty well dissolved
4. add in the cooked meatballs , and simmer with lid ajar on stovetop for 30-45 minute or simmer in crockpot on low for 1-1 1 / 2 hours
5. be sure to stir a couple of times
6. sauce will thicken , and smells almost like sweet and sour sauce
7. my friends like them over spaghetti noodles , and mashed potatoes
8. these freeze well for future use
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I used frozen meatballs from market and used 2/3 cup xylitol instead of sugar.  I will make it again.

target.recipe_text:
linzer torte bars

named after a classic austrian dessert, these bars have a great raspberry filling and are so easy to make. they make a great addition to the cookie jar.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. mix together flour , sugar , walnuts , cinnamon , and butter in a bowl until crumbly
3. press 2 / 3 of mixture into an ungreased 9x9-inch baking pan
4. spread preserves over crust
5. sprinkle remaining crumb mixture over the top of preserves , patting mixture down lightly
6. bake at 375f for 20-25 minutes or until light golden brown
7. cool completely before cutting into bars
target.review:
Today is a snow day from school and I find myself trying new recipes with my kids.  I made three different cookies and had the children rate the cookies.  This recipe by far, came out in front every time.  I was amazed at how easy it was to make and how fast the kids cleaned out the pan!  I will pass on this recipe and I will DEFINITELY make it again and again!
Thanks for Sharing SUE

demonstrations.recipe_text:
danish cookies  press cookies

this is another old recipe of my mothers. it's at least 50 years old or more. i don't know where she got it but it is very good and buttery.i am going to guess on the amount of cookies it makes. i know it makes a lot. they also freezes well.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. cream together sugar and butter
3. add eggs which have been slightly beaten
4. add salt and flour
5. add vanilla
6. mix well
7. form into fancy shapes by using a cookie press
8. place on ungreased cookie sheet
9. bake 8 to 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: I am so sorry that it has taken me so long to post this recipe - - I must say that this recipe is fantastic.  I got extremely creative with this and put it into a fluted cookie silicone pan.  Baked for 10 minutes and topped with apricot jam and sliced almonds.  Put back in the oven for approximately 8 more minutes until the almonds toasted.  Deeeeee-Lish!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
demonstrations.review:
This recipe is FANTASTIC.  My kids absolutely LOVE this recipe.  I love recipes that don't take an enormous amount of time to prepare.  I can make this in the afternoon and have a hot meal on the table when the kids get in from their sporting activities.

Great recipe and I'll make this again and again!!!

Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
norwegian crowns

adapted from the cookie book, edited by ruth berolzheimer, 1949. i haven't tried these, but they seem to be a good way to use up egg yolks, both hard boiled, and raw. btw, you can freeze any raw egg white in freezer safe containers as is, just defrost in the fridge overnight to use in meringues or angelfood cake. i would not advise freezing cooked egg white. feel free to halve the recipe if that is more convenient for you. 1 1/2 cups butter equals 12 oz. i am not sure of the preparation time, but have excluded the time for boiling the eggs. the cooking time is for one batch.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. press the hard cooked egg yolks through a sieve , into a mixing bowl
3. add the sugar , salt and uncooked egg yolks , and beat thoroughly with mixer
4. add the butter and flour alternately in small amounts , mixing in after each addition
5. cover and chill until stiff
6. roll the dough into ropes 1 / 4 inch in diameter and 5 inches long
7. form rings by crossing the ends and pressing slightly
8. dip , first into egg white , and then into the sugar , and place on cookie sheets with some space between them
9. bake at 400 degrees f for 8 to 10 minutes , but check slightly earlier to make sure they aren't browning too fast
10. remove from sheets and cool on racks
demonstrations.review:
This is the recipe that my Norwegian grandmother had taught me to make some-odd 43 years ago. I've been making them ever since.  The only thing I DON'T do is to egg wash and put sugar on them. These also work well with a cookie press.

She used to make these cookies with a chocolate meringue cookie so she could use up her egg whites.
TRY THESE - - YOU WON'T BE SORRY!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate dipped shortbread cookies

these are an elegant addition to a christmas cookie plate.

1. cream butter and sugar , add flour and vanilla
2. pinch of 1 / 2" balls of dough , roll in sugar and place on cookie sheet
3. use the tines of a fork to flatten cookies
4. bake at 350f for 12-15 minutes
5. remove from baking sheet , cool 10-15 minutes
6. dip half of each cookie into melted chocolate
7. chill to set chocolate
demonstrations.review: I left myself a note on my personal notes to TRIPLE THE RECIPE IF YOU'RE MAKING THEM AGAIN - -Pushed through a piping bag and made them all a uniform size. (2") melted chocolate with 2 TB. shortening and put a thin layer of chocolate in the middle of the two cookies. Slapped them together and I will tell you that they are the closest things to MILANO cookies that you'll find...BUT BETTER

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s creamy greek feta salad dressing

plan ahead the dressing needs a few hours chilling time before serving,  you may want to adjust some ingredients after you make this, i would suggest to start with the stated amounts and add in more after mixing, you may use 3 tablespoons freshly grated parmesan cheese in place of the feta cheese --- if you are not a lover of garlic then i suggest to pass this by! --- servings are only esitmated.

1. in a food processor or blender process all ingredients together except the salt and pepper until blended and smooth
2. add in a little more crumbled feta cheese if you prefer a chunky-style dressing
3. season with salt and black pepper
4. refrigerate for at least 2 or more hours before serving
demonstrations.review:
This dressing is just tremendous! I mixed grilled chicken in the salad for a light and easy dinner.

Once again Kittencal...you made me shine!

target.recipe_text:
rochester quiche

a robust "man's" quiche! bacon, mushrooms, onions, blue cheese & swiss cheese.

1. preheat oven 425f degrees
2. in skillet fry bacon til crispy , drain on paper towel
3. remove most fat from skillet then saute' mushrooms and onions til browned
4. in bowl combine eggs , half and half , pepper
5. crumble bacon onto bottom of prepared pie shell
6. then add the onions and mushrooms
7. sprinkle crumbled blue cheese over all
8. top with the grated swiss cheese
9. pour egg mixture carefully over contents
10. bake at 425' for 15 minutes
11. reduce heat to 350' bake another 20-25 minutes til center is set and knife inserted in center comes out clean
target.review: I made a modification of this recipe for my husband's family last weekend and everyone loved it!!  I used Gouda instead of swiss, since I had some already and used a whole container (16oz) of egg substitute, three eggs worth would not be nearly enough.  This increased the cooking time about 20 minutes.  Fabulous combination of flavors.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hummus amongus

there's a large middle eastern population in bayridge brooklyn and amazing restaurants line the avenues...hummus is served with every dish on the menu...it's one of my favorite things in the whole wide world...if you haven't tried it, please do. i think you'll love it!

1. drain beans
2. reserve water
3. in a food processor or blender add beans and all the ingredients
4. process until smooth
5. if mixture is too thick , add some of the reserved liquid from the beans to dilute to a desired consistency
6. serve at room temperature with pita bread , grilled pork , lamb or chicken
demonstrations.review: Yummus Hummus!!  I have wanted to make this for a while and finally got around to it and it is soooo gooood.  I used roasted garlic cloves for softened garlic flavor.  Using the food prcessor made this light and creamy.  I can't wait to try some new combinations, like sundried tomato.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic lime chicken

from leanne ely's book, saving dinner (fall). serve with garlic mashed potatoes, steamed broccoli, or baked sweet potatoes.  the seasonings are relatively mild. you could probably safely add any seasoning left over after sprinkling breasts to the pan without it being too spicy.

1. on a plate , mix together first seven ingredients
2. sprinkle mixture on both sides of chicken breasts
3. in a skillet heat butter and olive oil together over medium-high heat
4. saute chicken until golden brown and done through
5. remove chicken and add lime juice and chicken broth to the pan , whisking up the browned bits off the bottom of the pan
6. keep cooking until sauce has reduced slightly
7. add chicken back to the pan to thoroughly cover and serve
demonstrations.review: Very flavorful dish, we loved it!!  We eat a lot of chicken and this was a great recipe to break the monotony.  I think this would also work well fish, like Tilapia.  It's a great low calorie dinner. One of our new favs, thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
love me tender nut burgers

concocted by the first class nuts team for the zwt3!
"if you're lonesome tonight, stop in at our heartbreak hotel for a one-of-a-kind "love-me-tender nut burger" that we're sure elvis himself would've danced in his blue suede shoes for! peanut butter is the secret ingredient for our tender, juicy burger that's topped with all the best southern trimmin's! including bbq sauce, bacon, creamy coleslaw, and much, much more! ya'll come down and see us now, ya hear?!"

1. in large bowl , combine well the hamburger , peanut butter , garlic and finely chopped onion
2. if you prefer , you can top your burgers with thinly sliced onion instead
3. shape into four patties
4. sprinkle each side with salt and pepper if desired
5. place on hot grill and grill til almost done , turning once , about 3 minutes per side
6. spread top of each burger with half of the bbq sauce and turn , top other side with remaining bbq sauce
7. grill for 1 minute , turn burgers over , and top each with cheese
8. grill one minute longer or til cheese has started to melt
9. during this time , toast buns if desired
10. place burgers on bottom buns
11. top with the rest of the ingredients in order divided evenly , breaking bacon slices in half and topping each with 2 half slices
12. spread inside of top buns with spicy mustard and place on top of slaw
13. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Made these at the pool yesterday for the fam and everyone loved them!!  No one cuold guess the secret ingredient and they couldn't believe it was peanut butter when I told them!  Made with groud turkey and worked out reat!  Can't wait to make them again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortilla casserole  oamc

i went on a missions trip almost 13 years ago with teen missions international and this was one of the meals served. i made sure to come home with the recipe as it was a team favourite!

1. fry ground beef and onions until meat is cooked through
2. add taco seasoning and water and cook until thickened
3. line the pan or casserole dish with 3 tortillas , then layer with 1 / 2 of the meat , 1 / 2 of the beans , 1 / 2 of the sour cream and 1 / 2 of the cheese
4. repeat
5. if you like it spicy , then top it with some hot sauce or salsa
6. bake at 350 until bubbly
7. oamc directions: after baking , place in rigid container and seal with a lid
8. place in freezer
9. when ready to eat , thaw , place in baking dish , and reheat in 400 degree oven for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was a great quick dish to throw together, already had everything on hand.  We eat a lot of tacos at our house and this was a nice variation.  I substituted ground turkey and black beans and it turned out great.  Thanks for the yummy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome beef or chicken taco soup

this is a recipe i got from a friend of mine. it's great for making when you're feeding a lot of people. also fantastic for warming you up when it's cold!

1. mix together all ingredients
2. simmer for 30 minutes
3. serve with tortilla chips , cheese , and cornbread if desired !
demonstrations.review: If you like Paula Deen, you will love this recipe.  It is almost exactly like her Taco Soup.  One our favorites!!

target.recipe_text:
buttered wine rice

from a women's weekly dinner party cookbook.
a nice change from plain rice!
if you have any leftovers, add some cooked peas, canned tuna & some cream for an easy tuna rice dish, yum!

1. heat butter in a pan , add onion and cook gently until onion is tender and lightly golden
2. add rice and stir for 3 minutes
3. add 1 cup of hot chicken stock to pan and stir until almost completely dissolved
4. add remaining stock & wine , bring to the boil , reduce heat & simmer gently for approximately 10 mins until rice is tender
5. season with salt & pepper & serve
target.review: This was so tasty, We will be making this again for sure.  We served ours with Thai Chicken Breasts, thanks for a great recipe :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried sausages

curried sausages are quite popular comfort food in australia, this is my recipe that i have made commercially for many years and have had lots of compliments for.

1. cover the sausages with cold water
2. bring to the boil and simmer about 5 minutes
3. drain , cool , remove skins and cut each into 4 or 5 pieces
4. heat the oil in a large saucepan and fry the onion , garlic and ginger , carrots and potatoes , stirring until the onions are soft
5. add the curry powder and cook a minute or two
6. add the tomato paste , chutney , apple sauce , stock and coconut milk
7. stir well , then return the sausage chunks to the saucepan
8. bring too the boil then cover and simmer about 45 minutes
9. remove the lid and allow to cook about 15 minutes more to reduce the sauce a bit
10. if you cant be bothered , mix two tablespoon cornflour with 2 tablespoons water and stir this through to thicken
11. 1 cup of peas can be added in the last 15 minutes as well
12. season with salt and pepper and serve garnished with copped fresh coriander
demonstrations.review: yummy yummy, i made it exactly to your recipe and found it very tasty, will definately be a regular in our household, best thing there was left over for hubbys lunch.  Thank you Jan. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple and rhubarb crumble

another magazine recipe, really nice pudding.

1. place filling ingredients into an ovenproof casserole dish
2. pulse crumble ingredients until mixture resembles breadcrumbs
3. sprinkle the mix evenly over the rhubarb and apple mixture
4. bake at 170c degrees for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Thanks for a great recipe, cooked it exactly as said and served it with whipped cream, it was loved by all.  :-) xoxo

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta bake

i've been making this since my boys could eat solids! and it's still a favourite. add carrot, celary, bell pepper if you wish, or tinned tomatoes in place of all or some of the soup. i really just make it with what i have or need to use. i also love the custard on mashed potatoes or pumpkin baked in the oven.

1. heat the oil in a large frypan over medium heat
2. fry the onion until golden and tender
3. add the garlic and cook a couple of minutes more
4. add the beef and cook , breaking up the lumps with a fork , until all the meat has changed colour
5. add remaining sauce ingredients , stir well
6. simmer for about 30 minutes or until the sauce has thickened
7. mix in cooked pasta and pour into a 2 litre casserole
8. topping: whisk together the cream and egg , and season to taste
9. pour gently over the meat / pasta mix
10. sprinkle over cheese , scatter this with the bacon
11. cook in a moderate oven until custard is set and golden
12. about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was great!!!! Very simple to make and had such a great taste, the topping was scrummy, I added some mushrooms to ours, thanks for another great recipe, will be making this again for sure :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai chicken breasts

this recipe actually calls for breasts, but i used thighs and they were moist and lucious! goes well with steamed basamati rice.

1. combine the gingerrot , garlic and red pepper flakes in a cup and set aside
2. mix flour with salt and pepper to taste and dredge chicken pieces in this
3. heat the olive oil in a large skillet
4. saute the chicken until browned on both sides and cooked through
5. remove the chicken and put in a warm dish , set aside in low oven to keep warm
6. add the ginger-garlic mixture to the skillet and saute until lightly browned
7. add the soy sauce , brown sugar , vinegar and fish sauce
8. bring the mixture to a boil
9. reduce the heat and simmer , stirring frequently , until the sauce reduces and thickens
10. pour the sauce over the chicken pieces in the warm serving dish and keep warm until ready to serve
11. trim and shred the sugar snap peas diagonally
12. just prior to serving sprinkle the top of the chicken with the shredded snap peas
demonstrations.review: WOW!!! This was so good, words cannot describe how yummy this was.  The only thing I changed was instead of crushed red pepper flakes (can't get them here) I used 1/8 teaspoon of chilli powder.  We served it on Buttered Wine Rice.  Thanks for a excellent recipe :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
why i joined zaar carrot cake

on october 2, 2001, i discovered the recipezaar web site. i immediately joined so i could post a request for a recipe i had lost. in less than an hour, i had a reply: this recipe. unfortunately, i never posted it into the database -- until now. my mistake. this cake was the reason i joined, and the friendly response i received was the reason i stayed!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour a 9x13 inch pan
3. mix flour , baking soda , baking powder , salt and cinnamon
4. make a well in the center and add sugar , oil , eggs and vanilla
5. mix with wooden spoon until smooth
6. stir in carrots , coconut , walnuts and pineapple
7. pour into 9x13 inch pan and bake for about 45 minutes
8. don't panic , the centre will sink a little
9. allow to cool
10. when cool , ice the cake
11. you can certainly use your favourite cream cheese frosting to ice this cake , but the one i've included is highly recommended
12. to make the frosting: cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
13. add the icing sugar and beat until creamy
demonstrations.review: WOW!!! I never thought I'd be able to make a carrot cake this yummy, the best I have ever tasted by far, this recipe is definately a keeper, thank you very much :-)

target.recipe_text:
fantastic taco casserole

i originally found this taco casserole recipe in a taste of home magazine.  since then, i have made this recipe at least 50 times.  i love it because the ingredients list isn't complicated and, based on the layers, i can readily remember all ingredients when i am at the store without my recipe card.  i have served this for myself and had wonderful leftovers or many times i have made it for company with a nice green salad to accompany it.  i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

1. brown ground beef and drain
2. add taco seasoning and cook according to package directions , adding proper amount of water
3. put corn chips on bottom of 8x8" dish
4. cook refried beans on stove until hot
5. add 1 cup cheese and 1 cup salsa
6. stir until combined
7. pour beans over corn chips in dish
8. add beef to top of beans
9. sprinkle remaining cheese over top
10. sprinkle green onions and black olives over cheese
11. bake in a 375 degree oven until the cheese is sufficiently melted
12. take out of oven and sprinkle chopped tomatoes on top
13. wait 1-2 minutes and then serve
target.review: Leilani, I can see why you've made this recipe at least 50 times!  It's tasty and a snap to make.  A great standby for busy days.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
semisweet chocolate icing

this is the icing for the vanilla-fudge marble cake recipe #45104.  don't have the golden syrup?  well if you must, you can try substituting it with 2 parts light corn syrup and 1 part molasses or equal parts of honey and light corn syrup.

1. combine all ingredients together in a small saucepan
2. heat over low heat , stirring until chocolate melts and mixture is smooth
3. use immediately to top the vanilla-fudge marble cake recipe #45104
demonstrations.review: Made this to top the Vanilla-Fudge Marble Cake, and it was very good.  I used one Tbsp. each of corn syrup and honey which, for me, made the perfect consistency.  I will use this again.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect southern fried chicken

this is an outstanding recipe. when i found this i decided i didn't need to look for the perfect fried chicken recipe any more - i already had it.

1. soak chicken in water and salt at least 2 hours in the refrigerator
2. mix buttermilk , eggs and season all and dip chicken pieces in this mixture
3. combine 1 cup flour , 2 tbsp corn meal , 2 tsp dried oregano , and 2 tsp season all in a bag
4. drop two pieces of dipped chicken in the bag at one time
5. shake to coat
6. place on wire rack to rest
7. heat a shallow layer of oil or shortening to 360 f in a jumbo chicken skillet or an electric skillet
8. place the chicken in the pan , trying not to crowd the pieces
9. cover for the first five minutes
10. check the chicken
11. when golden brown , turn
12. cover for the next five minutes
13. remove cover and cook uncovered , turning occasionally , as needed for a total of an additional 20 minutes or until cooked through
14. watch carefully , and don't allow it to get too dark
15. if it's frying too fast , reduce heat slightly
demonstrations.review: Great recipe--my husband said it reminded him of the fried chicken he ate while growing up.  I especially liked your method of covering during the first five minutes--worked great!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken fried chicken with milk gravy

this one is for all the men in my family. they would eat this every day!!! they even love it for breakfast, with biscuits!

1. pound breasts a little to flatten
2. roll breasts in flour , then egg , and back in flour
3. heat oil in large skillet on med hi
4. add breasts and cook and turn until golden brown and juices run clear ,
5. remove and keep warm
6. to skillet add flour , stir until light brown and bubbly
7. add a little more oil if needed
8. mix the milks together
9. slowly pour half the milk mix into skillet , stirring hard
10. continue adding milk and stirring until as thin as you like
11. add salt and pepper
12. let boil 1 minute
13. spoon over chicken
demonstrations.review: You're right--this is a man-pleasin' dish and one I will surely make again (and again).  I did not have any evaporated milk, so I substituted chicken stock for it and will probably continue to do so.  Thanks for another great recipe, MizzNezz!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
a better reuben sandwich

this is the very best way to use up left over corned beef or a great dinner using deli corned beef slices.

1. combine mayonnaise , chili sauce and horseradish in a small bowl
2. set aside
3. spread one side of each slice of bread with butter
4. generously spread the mayonnaise mixture on the other side of each slice of bread place 1 slice of cheese on 4 slices of bread on top of the mayonnaise spread
5. arrange corned beef over cheese
6. top corned beef with saurkraut
7. place another slice of cheese over the saurkraut
8. close sandwiches with the rest of the prepared bread , mayo side down and butter side up
9. cook on a pre-heated griddle or large skillet over medium-low heat for 4 or 5 minutes per side until bread is toasted and cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: Great Reubens, and we really liked the sauce--especially my horseradish-loving husband.  I'll make them this way from now on.  Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracker barrel green beans

this is the only way i can eat canned green beans!

1. in a 2-quart saucepan over medium heat , cook bacon until lightly brown but not crisp
2. when bacon has browned , add green beans
3. add salt , sugar and pepper and mix well
4. place onion on top of green beans
5. cover saucepan with a lid and bring to a light boil
6. turn heat down to low and simmer beans for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good green beans!!  This will really come in handy when cooking for a large group.  Thanks, mcb22902!!

target.recipe_text:
oven baked fish

this fish dish goes well with my recipe #53227 and garlic green beans. enjoy!

1. melt butter in large glass pyrex measuring cup and add lemon juice , spices and sugar
2. place bread crumbs in a shallow bowl or platter
3. spray a shallow baking dish with vegetable spray
4. cut fish into individual serving pieces
5. dip fish into butter and then coat each fillet well with bread crumbs
6. place bread coated fillets into baking dish
7. repeat until all fish fillets are covered
8. spoon the remaining herb butter mixture over fish
9. i also use a pastry brush to lightly tap the tops of the breaded fish to make sure it is all cover
10. you may need to melt more butter to coat fish
11. bake , uncovered , for 15 minutes at 400 degrees
12. fish is done when fish flakes easily with a fork
target.review: Just used your recipe for dinner tonight and it was delicious.  I stuck pretty close to your recipe, just substituted cayenne for the basil (we use cayenne in just about everything) and used basa fish.  I was just making 2 filets, so I cut the recipe in half.  As you suggested I used a brush to tap the butter on top and had some butter left that I didn't use.  I cooked it exactly as the recipe suggeted and it came out fantastic.  It was crispy and very flavourful.  My husband says its a definite keeper.  Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
enchilada sauce

this is a very easy, quick enchilada sauce to use instead of the canned variety. we prefer to eat freshly made foods without alot of preservatives. this has a wonderful flavor.

1. heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat
2. add the garlic and saute for 1 to 2 minutes
3. add onion , oregano , chili powder , basil , ground black pepper , salt , cumin , parsley , salsa and tomato sauce
4. mix together and then stir in the water
5. bring to a boil , reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes
6. use in place of canned enchilada sauce
demonstrations.review: Great sauce.  I made it on the weekend for a Mexican dinner party we hosted for our Dinner Club.  It had a bit of a kick to it that everyone loved.  I followed the recipe exactly, because it was the first time I ever made enchilada sauce.  I was worried because it was thin, but after simmering it boiled down and was perfect.   I have never tasted the canned variety and I know I won't even bother trying it now.  Why would I when your recipe is this good and easy to make my own.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesty salsa for canning

i got this years ago from the lady in our church who canned it. i've never made it but i've eaten lots of it! it's the best salsa i have ever had. especially good with lime tortilla chips or on taco salad (recipe #102234).

1. combine all ingredients except tomato paste in large sauce pot
2. simmer until desired thickness
3. stir in tomato paste
4. ladle hot salsa into hot jars leaving 1 / 4 inch head-space
5. process 15 minutes in a hot water bath
6. it depends on how hot your peppers are and how hot you like your salsa
7. i never get close to 2 1 / 2 cups for our mild salsa
demonstrations.review: Just finished canning salsa using this recipe.  It is fantastic!  We tripled the recipe to use up tomatoes that were given to us and ended up with 32 - 500 ml jars.  Followed the recipe except for the amount of hot pepper, we used much less as we were using jalapenos and didn't take out the seeds.  It has a nice bit of heat...probably a cross between and medium and a hot salsa.  I was worried about the amount of bell pepper, but we used the amount called for using a mix of green, red & yellow peppers and it tastes great...the peppers weren't too overpowering.  I have canned salsa before using another recipe, but this one is far superior and will be the one I use in future.   Thanks Marg...another great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nacho dip

a yummy dip,great for get togethers....very addictive. i have also seen this dip with a layer of ground beef spiced with taco seasoning added in ! yum!

1. blend first three ingredients together
2. spread over 12 inch pizza pan or other large plate or platter
3. chill for one hour
4. add salsa sauce over top
5. alternate cheese , green peppers , onions , tomatoes
6. cover& chill
7. serve with nacho chips for dipping
8. regular or bite sized
9. very addictive !
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic!  I took your tip regarding the ground beef.  I didn't have mayo, so I used cream cheese and sour cream and mixed some of the taco seasoning in with it...that made for a tasty base.  Then I spread the cooled ground beef which I had browned with some taco seasoning.  Then follwed the rest of the recipe, except substituted lettuce for green pepper and layered with tomato, cheese and onion.  Served it with nacho chips at a potluck BBQ and it was gone in a flash.  Thanks for the recipe...yum yum.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pareve brown rice pudding

i wanted rice pudding and decided to try my hand at a recipe of my own.  enjoy!

1. in medium size sauce pan over medium-high heat combine soy milk with sugar , vanilla , and cinnamon bring to a boil while constantly stirring
2. in a separate bowl large enough to accommodate the hot liquid beat the egg with a whisk while slowly adding the hot liquid a little bit at a time until all of the liquid has been added to the egg
3. place the 2 cups of cooked rice into the pan used to cook the soy milk mixture
4. add the soy milk mixture to the rice in the pan and return heat to medium-high , stir constantly until the mixture comes to a boil then reduce heat to simmer
5. simmer mixture for 15-20 minutes , stirring every 5 minutes until the mixture is a creamy consistency
6. remove from heat , cover top with wax paper and place in the refrigerator to cool
demonstrations.review: I have used this recipe many times, it's one of my favorites for breakfast or snack, and keep forgetting to rate it.  I always have leftover brown rice hanging around, so it's an easy and delicious way to use it up.  I've made it using 1%,  skim, almond or soy milk and  they all turn out great.  I usually substitute 4 egg whites (4 Tblsp. if using a carton of egg white), 4 Tblsp. maple syrup instead of sugar and always add raisins (cause I love them)and it is yummy.   Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chai latte

my latest addiction!

1. chill 1 / 3 cup of the evaporated milk in the fridge until very cold
2. combine remaining evaporated milk , tea bags , water and honey in a small saucepan over medium heat , simmer 5 minutes
3. beat chilled 1 / 3 cup evaporated milk , sugar and vanilla until thick and frothy
4. strain tea into warmed mugs
5. spoon frothy mixture over top
6. sprinkle with cardamom or nutmeg and chocolate shavings
demonstrations.review: Love, love, love this recipe.  I made it with chocolately chai tea bags, used some leftover whipped cream for the topping and it was fantastic.  It was so good I had to run a to-go cup over to my friend so she could rave about it with me.  I won't be buying expensive chai lattes at the coffee shop anymore.  Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
acorn squash medley

one of nature's finest creations: squash. squash appeals to most pallets and pairs well with virtually every food category. i served this with a glass of merlot, black seedless grapes and banana-walnut-cranberry bread--a heavenly combination. enjoy!

1. halve both acorn squash and remove and discard seeds
2. place upside down on microwaveable dish and cook on high for 8-10 minutes until softened
3. scoop out squash leaving approximately 1 / 4 inch on shells to retain their shapes
4. set aside
5. cook sausages , cool and cut into 1 / 2 inch size bites
6. saute thinly sliced garlic , shredded carrots and chopped peppers in olive oil for 3-4 minutes until softened
7. stir in spinach , mushrooms and seasonings and cook 3-4 minutes more
8. remove from heat , combine with cooked rice , sausage and squash
9. fill each half of the acorn shells with equal amounts of the filling
10. bake in 350 degree oven for 20 minutes
11. cool five minutes before serving
12. enjoy
target.review: A perfect winter comfort food. Loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
protein powered oatmeal breakfast

breakfast should be your most nutrition packed meal of the day. oatmeal combined with protein powder, nuts and berries provides plenty of energy enhancing antioxidants to get you through a vigorous morning workout or day.

1. boil oats and 1 cup of milk in saucepan for 2 minutes
2. add 1 / 4 cup milk , protein powder and cinnamon
3. divide equally between two bowls and garnish with 1 / 4 cup of blueberries and 1 tablespoon of sliced almonds each
4. pour remaining milk equally over both bowls and serve while still warm
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Substituted dried cranberries for the blueberries and added a little almond milk. A nutritious and quick breakfast!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french cabbage soup from door county  wi

this recipe is a popular soup served at the summer kitchen near ephraim, wi. it is thick and delicious. i've modified it somewhat by adding the thyme and pepper for even more flavor. it freezes very well. for culinary quest participants - it's typical of the hearty soups served throughout central europe.

1. make a white roux with 6 tbsp butter and 1 / 2 cup flour by melting the butter in a medium skillet , stirring in the flour and simmering 3- 5 minutes while stirring constantly
2. avoid browning
3. set aside
4. melt 2 tbsp butter in a stock pot , or dutch oven
5. add diced onions and carrots
6. saute until tender
7. add chicken broth , diced smoked sausage , diced potatoes and chopped cabbage to the pot
8. stir and simmer for 20 minutes
9. add white roux , thyme , salt and pepper to the pot
10. stir until smooth
11. simmer for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Just made it yesterday. Excellent!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken fingers and fries

fast food perfected! and, it's much better for you too! trust me, this recipe's a keeper!

1. tenderize chicken breast and marinade in oyster sauce overnight
2. peel and cut potatoes with a french fry cutter
3. toss with olive oil coating evenly
4. place single layer on a cookie sheet
5. bake in 350 degree oven for 30 minutes , turn all and bake ten minutes more or until golden brown
6. meanwhile , stir together the flour , cornstarch and remaining spices
7. cut chicken breasts in 1 / 2 / inch strips
8. soak strips in milk then coast completely with flour mixture
9. beat eggs well and coat floured chicken strips in the egg
10. fry in olive oil on medium high heat for 15 minutes , turning regularly until all sides are golden brown
11. drain on paper towel
12. serve with ketchup and cold beer
13. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Better than fast food and more nutritious too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nutritious nachos

nachos can be a healthy snack choice if made with fresh vegetables and low fat cheese. topped with a slathering of salsa and garlic powder and you're ready to indulge! enjoy!

1. spread out tortilla chips on a dinner plate or serving platter keeping chips touching , exposing very little of the plate
2. top with cheese then the remaining ingredients
3. heat in microwave on high for 1 to 2 minutes
4. serve warm
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Best if made in smaller individual size portions as a baked snack eaten quickly. So good I have them weekly!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy no rise pizza crust

you will not believe how easy and quick this is to make.  just stir ingredients together, let sit for ten minutes, then press into baking pan. add your favorite toppings and bake.  pizza in no time!

1. dissolve yeast in warm water in a medium bowl and add rest of ingredients
2. beat vigorously 20 strokes and let rest 10 minutes
3. press dough onto greased 11x17" baking sheet and add topping ingredients of your choice
4. bake at 425 for 15 to 20 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: Really Good and Simple!

target.recipe_text:
easy beefy crescent squares

i came up with these when i needed something quick and easy to make for supper. hubby and i enjoy them and i hope you will too!

1. brown hamburger , drain , and add pasta sauce
2. press 4 crescent rolls in the bottom of greased 8x8 pan , add meat / sauce mixture , cheese , and remaining 4 crescent rolls on top
3. bake in preheated 350f oven for 12-15 minutes and enjoy !
target.review: This was very good and EASY! That is such a wonderful combination.  I had to double mine, for my large faimly and I did a layer of cheese, meat, then cheese.  Next time I am going to add veggies and make it a one dish meal. Thanks for the recipe Loves2Teach!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caesar pork chops

i am always looking for new and delicious ways to prepare pork chops.  these are delicious, easy to put together and use things that are in most people's pantries.  a real family pleaser.  serve with rice pilaf and a green vegetable.

1. heat oven to 375f
2. spray a 12 x 8 inch glass baking dish with cooking spray
3. in pie pan or shallow dish , mix flour and italian seasoning
4. pour dressing into another pie pan or shallow dish
5. coat both sides of each pork chop with the flour mixture
6. dip into dressing , coating both sides well
7. place in baking dish
8. sprinkle with cheese
9. discard any remaining flour and dressing
10. bake uncovered , 35 to 40 minutes or until pork is no longer pink in center
demonstrations.review: Good flavor on the chops, but the kids did not really enjoy.  More of an adult taste I guess.  Will make again, but smaller amount for just the adults.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy tater tots casserole

my mom used to make this when i was little and i've always loved it. it's so easy to make and is always a big hit in our house.

1. cook ground beef and drain grease
2. pour ground beef in bottom of ungreased 8x8 pan
3. drain green beans and layer on top of ground beef
4. smooth cheddar cheese soup over the green beans
5. place tater tots strategically to cover entire casserole
6. if desired , sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese over tater tots
7. bake in the oven using the directions from the tater tot bag
demonstrations.review: My family did not go wild over this.  They liked the taste of the meat and soup mix, but they did not like the tots on top.  I may change to just potatoes on top instead.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy caramel apple cinnamon dump cake

i have tried several variations of dump cake and made up my own one day when i needed some comfort! ;)  this one is by far the favorite of anyone i have served it to.  i make several different flavors and fillings at work potlucks and since i made this one, that is all everyone requests!  once you make it, you'll know why, just make sure you have your favorite vanilla ice cream on hand to go along with it. :)

1. pour both cans of apple pie filling into a 13x9 glass cake pan
2. add cinnamon and stir
3. depending on what type of caramel topping you have , you may have to heat it in the microwave to get it to pour
4. once it is ready to pour , then drizzle in a checkerboard fasion all over the pie filling , first up and down , then side to side
5. sprinkle dry cake mix over the top of the pie filling
6. cut small slices of butter and place randomly all over on top of dry cake mix , ensuring that most areas are evenly covered
7. bake at 350 for about a 30 minutes , watch it , when it is brown and bubbly it is ready to go
8. serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream , drizzle more hot caramel over ice cream and dessert
9. enjoy ! :-)
demonstrations.review: This was wonderful!  I used cinnamon apples instead of apple pie filling (what I had on hand) and I added a little brown sugar to apples.  Followed everything thing else just the same and got lots of compliments!  I am going to make this for the holidays instead of apple cobbler!  Thanks Kassi!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger noodle bake

this is almost like a lasagna. very good!

1. brown hamburger , onions , and spices until cooked
2. add tomato sauce and simmer 15 minutes
3. mix cream cheese and sour cream
4. in 2-quart casserole , put 1 / 3 noodles , 1 / 3 cream mix , 1 / 3 meat mix
5. repeat twice
6. sprinkle cheddar on top
7. bake at 350 for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good to eat and on the budget!  I doubled the order for my large family of 8.  I did make one change, I did not read the directions well and I added the sour cream and the cream cheese to the tomato sauce mixture.  Then I layered sauce and noodles, toped with cheese. Despite my inability to read directions it still turned out wonderful!  Thanks, will be making again!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy creamy sour cream chicken casserole

this is one of the first recipes i really "mastered" when i was learning how to cook. my husband got to enjoy this recipe at least twice a month because it was one of the few dishes i knew how to make. now, that i'm a much better cook, we still have this delicious dinner on our menu at least monthly. it is so easy to put together and very good. if you like your casserole's creamy, then this is one you've gotta try! i hope you enjoy it as much as we do!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. boil chicken breast until tender
3. drain and cube
4. spread evenly over the bottom of a square casserole dish
5. salt and pepper to taste
6. mix sour cream and chicken soup in a separate bowl
7. spread the sour cream and soup mixture over the chicken in the casserole dish
8. crush the ritz crackers and spread over top of the casserole
9. spoon melted butter on top over all
10. bake in a 350f oven until top is golden brown , approximately 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I did this, but added rice as I wanted to have one less dish.  Great and easy, just my kind of meal.  Added Green beans on the side and dinner was done! Thanks KC for posting!

target.recipe_text:
jo mama s world famous spaghetti

my kids will give up a steak dinner for this spaghetti. it is a recipe i have been perfecting for years and it is so good (if i may humbly say) that my kids are disappointed when they eat spaghetti anywhere else but home! in fact they tell me i should open a restaurant and serve only this spaghetti and garlic bread. in response to requests, i have posted the recipe for recipe #28559 that uses approximately 1/2 of the sauce from this 
recipe. have spaghetti one night and lasagna later!  thanks to all of you who have tried my recipe and have written a review.  i read and appreciate every one of them!  chef note:  after i posted this recipe i remembered a funny incident--my dear husband usually has a nice bottle of wine handy so when i make a batch of spaghetti i just help myself to a splash of it. on one occasion, there wasn't a bottle opened, but there was a bottle sitting on the counter so i got out the corkscrew and helped myself. for some reason, the spaghetti that night was the best ever. my husband asked what wine i put in it and i showed him the bottle. he nearly fell off the chair. i had opened a rather expensive bottle he had bought to give his boss. goes to show you--don't use a wine for cooking you wouldn't drink. you get the best results from a good wine!

1. in large , heavy stockpot , brown italian sausage , breaking up as you stir
2. add onions and continue to cook , stirring occasionally until onions are softened
3. add garlic , tomatoes , tomato paste , tomato sauce and water
4. add basil , parsley , brown sugar , salt , crushed red pepper , and black pepper
5. stir well and barely bring to a boil
6. stir in red wine
7. simmer on low , stirring frequently for at least an hour
8. a longer simmer makes for a better sauce , just be careful not to let it burn !
9. cook spaghetti according to package directions
10. spoon sauce over drained spaghetti noodles and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
target.review: I have made this soooo many times. I am absolutely in love with it....so much so that I decided to can it, so I can have it on hand whenever I want. I do leave out the water completely as I love thick sauces. I will let everyone know how I did it, if the canning works out. Wish me luck!UPDATE:I over canned the sauce and it doesn't have the texture it usually does. Also the flavors are kind of mellowed. I will try this again without over pressure canning it and adding the herbs on top of the jar...I guess this is supposed hold in the flavor of the herbs better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tilapia

nan

1. combine oregano , chili powder , cayenne pepper , and salt
2. in a shallow bowl combine the melted butter and lemon juice
3. dip fish into butter mixture , then press into the spice mixture
4. place in a shallow casserole sprayed with non-stick cooking spray
5. bake at 450 degrees for about 15 minutes , or until fish flakes when pressed
demonstrations.review: I made this tonight! Delish

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herbed orange roughy

we love grilled fish. here is another great recipe.

1. in a small bowl , combine the first seven ingredients
2. dip fillets
3. grill , covered over hot coals for 5 minutes on each side or until fish flakes easily with a fork
demonstrations.review: I broiled this and it turned out awesome.  My 3 and 5 yr olds devoured it.  Will definitely make over and over again.  Also left out the lemon peel I didn't have any and I dumped the sauce stuff over the fish as it broiled.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortellini tomato spinach soup

really healthy soup, good to use when there's no time to spend in the kitchen!

1. in a soup pot , heat olive oil over medium high heat
2. saute the onion and garlic , stirring often until onions are translucent , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. add broth and tomatoes , turn heat up to high , and bring to a boil
4. add the tortellini and cook according to package instructions
5. when tortellini is almost done , add spinach and taste , adjusting seasonings with salt and pepper
6. serve immediately
7. garnish each serving with a sprinkling of parmesan
demonstrations.review: OH MY!!!! I thought this would be healthy, but kind of bland, but I tried it anyway. It is sooooo yummy!!! My kids love it too. We are over in Germany and eat it with Brotchen, a crusty roll. We also add an extra clove of garlic and use a 28oz can of diced tomatoes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
7 layer bean dip

this 7 layer bean dip is great for super bowl parties, work parties, other gatherings! pretty easy to make...you can use store bought guacamole if you can't find ripe avocados.

1. mix avocados , lemon juice , salt , and pepper
2. mix mayonnaise , sour cream , and taco seasoning mix
3. layer ingredients as follows
4. bottom layer: bean dip
5. second layer: avocado mixture
6. third layer: sour cream mixture
7. fourth layer: tomatoes
8. fifth layer: onions
9. sixth layer: olives
10. seventh layer: cheese
11. top with extra sour cream / olives / salsa , etc
12. if desired
13. serve with tortilla chips
14. this seems to be a little bit better if you can chill it for a few hours or over night to let the flavors intensify
demonstrations.review: Absolutely the best I have had.  I used salsa because I didn't have tomatoes on hand.  EXCELLENT!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon swirl quick bread

this rich quick bread is a favorite with my family. i often give my husband a few slices to take with him on his commute to work, along with a tall travel mug of coffee.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a large mixing bowl , beat together butter , 1 cup sugar , and egg
3. combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
4. add the flour mixture to the egg mixture alternately with the buttermilk
5. in a small bowl , combine the cinnamon and remaining 1 / 3 cup sugar
6. pour a third of the batter into a greased 8x4x2-inch loaf pan
7. sprinkle a third of the cinnamon sugar on top of batter
8. repeat layers twice
9. bake for 45-50 minutes , until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean
10. cool in pan for 10 minutes
11. remove from pan to a wire rack to cool completely
demonstrations.review: Completely AWESOME.  Just don't put too much sugar on the top.

target.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth pumpkin bread

i got this recipe out of a church cookbook many years ago. it is a simple and delicious pumpkin bread. my daughter who hates coconut loves this bread. it is so moist and tasty that it really does melt in your mouth.

1. mix oil , eggs and pumpkin
2. combine remaining ingredients and add to pumpkin mixture
3. bake in a 9x5x3-inch pan at 325 for 1 hour
target.review: This bread is so wonderful! It is very moist and melts in your mouth.  It could also be served for dessert. A keeper that I will be making again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot special

this is from a handwritten recipe card, so i don't know where it is from.  i do know that it is simple and delicious.  great served over egg noodles, mashed potatoes or rice.

1. mix soups together
2. place roast in crock pot and pour soup mixture over
3. cook on low 8-9 hours
4. serve over egg noodles , rice or mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: Loved it!  So easy and tasty, I threw this together in the crock pot on my way out the door to work!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sauteed fennel

this recipe came from the foodtv.com kitchens

1. heat a medium saute pan over medium-high heat until just smoking
2. add the oil , garlic , fennel , and start tossing , to coat fennel in oil
3. season with salt and pepper , to taste
4. as the fennel starts to caramelize , add a splash of water to steam for 1 minute
5. remove from the heat
demonstrations.review: I love, love, love fennel!!!  This was quick easy and delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple blue cheese dip

from the book, recipes and rememberances. pineapple and blue cheese seem like they'd go well together. i think it would also look very pretty in a hollowed-out pineapple as the recipe describes below. time includes time to serve in the hollowed-out pineapple.

1. mix ingredients together
2. looks nice served in a hollowed out fresh pineapple
3. serve with potato chips
demonstrations.review: This dip was excellent!Serve it with crackers. It needs to be refrigerated for at least 2 hours.  When I first made it, I thought it was very bland and I would never make it again.  After it was refrigerated I was shocked at how delicious it was! This is now a new favorite cracker spread!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s porcupine meatballs in sweet and sour tomato sauce

if you don't mind the idea of using canned soup this is a delicious tomato sauce, because of the instant rice in the meatballs it will need about 1-1/2 to 2 hours of cooking time , i sometimes remove about 1/2 to 3/4 cup of the simmering sauce cool slightly then mix into the ground beef mixture before shaping into meatballs, you may need to adjust the brown sugar and vinegar amounts during cooking --- for meatballs i use my recipe#69173

1. for the meatballs
2. mix the ground beef with ingredients stated in the recipe
3. mix in 1-1 / 2 cups instant uncooked rice
4. shape into about 1-1 / 4--inch balls or as desired , then place onto a plate
5. for the sauce
6. in a pot heat oil over medium-high heat
7. add in onion , oregano and basil
8. cook stirring for about 3-4 minutes or until softened
9. add in garlic and chili flakes
10. cook stirring for 2-3 minutes
11. add in all remaining sauce ingredients
12. bring to a simmer stirring over medium heat until well combined
13. place the meatballs into the simmering sauce
14. bring back to a simmer
15. reduce heat to low or to a low simmer and cook uncovered for about 1-1 / 2 to 2 hours stirring frequently after the 25-30 minutes of cooking time
16. adjust the brown sugar and vinegar amounts if needed , then season with more salt and black pepper
demonstrations.review: This was delicious!!! This is a keeper and I will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
northwoods inn purple cabbage salad

the restaurant northwoods inn or clearmans serves this slaw.  i normally do not like cabbage, but this salad is delish!

1. combine oil , vinegar , sugar , salt , seasoned salt , pepper and onion powder in a bowl
2. pour over cabbage
3. chill for at least 2 hours or overnight
demonstrations.review: I have eaten at the restaurant many times and this recipe is almost better than the original!!

target.recipe_text:
white pasta sauce

nan

1. melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat
2. whisk in flour until smooth
3. slowly add the milk whisking continuously until smooth
4. bring to a boil and boil for about 1 minute or until the sauce is as thick as you like
5. add the salt , pepper and cheese
6. stir
7. add the pre-cooked shrimp
8. serve over pasta
9. you can also add any other seafood that you like to this sauce or leave it out
10. i have also added chicken that was sauteed in garlic and olive oil
11. this recipe also doubles well
12. sprinkle chopped parsley over to garnish
13. top with extra grated parmesan cheese
14. jan
target.review: the sauce is pretty good. I ended up adding more than 2 tablespoons of flour in because the sauce is not thickening.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled chicken wings

the marinade is simply wonderful and so easy. if you bite into one of these hot off the grill the rest may not make it into the house! make extras because the kids will eat them cold the next day. i marinated the wings for 6 hours to overnight.  i also use 1 tablespoon of fresh ginger finely grated instead of ground ginger.

1. cut the chicken wings into three pieces and discard
2. mix remaining ingredients into a bowl
3. add wings and stir
4. cover and marinate for 45 minutes
5. place pieces on the grill and brush with remaining mixture
6. grill over medium-hot coals about 15-20 minutes , turning once
demonstrations.review: great flavor. Everybody loves it for tonight BBQ.  I used wings and breast both on the grill. The wings seem to taste better, very moist. I love it. I think I will do it again in our family BBQ next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jumbo shrimp with sweet and sour sauce

a simple and delicious shrimp dish.  the sauce can be made ahead of time.  i decreased th marmalade after reading kitz review because 1/2 cup was my typo.  should be 1/4 cup marmalade, but feel free to add more if you like it sweeter.

1. for the sauce:
2. in a small saucepan warm the peanut oil over medium heat
3. add the ginger and garlic
4. cook until golden brown , about 60 to 90 second , stirring often
5. add the marmalade , rice vinegar , dijon mustard and soy sauce and stir until the marmalade has melted
6. remove from heat and set aside at room temperature
7. if made ahead , warm the sauce over medium heat until the marmalade has melted again
8. shrimp:
9. in a large bowl mix the oil , salt , chile powder , paprika and pepper
10. add the shrimp to the bowl and mix thoroughly to coat the shrimp evenly with the spices
11. thread shrimp onto metal skewers or you can also use a fish basket
12. heat grill to 500 to 550 degrees
13. with the grill lid closed , grill shrimp over direct high heat until just opaque in the center and firm to touch , 3-5 minutes , turning once
14. serve warm with as much sauce as you like drizzled over the top or use as a dipping suace
demonstrations.review:
Thanks for the great recipe. The sauce is not as thick as I want it to be because I used orange juice instead of marmalade.  And I added some corn starch to thicken it. 
Great tasty sauce to shrimp.  It is really creative.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade cough medicine

this is a home remedy for that horrible cough that you just can't get rid of, and best of all: you probably already have all of the ingredients!

1. mix ingredients
2. take by the teaspoon as often as needed for cough
3. do not give to infants under 12 months due to the honey
demonstrations.review: oh my, I was skeptic at first so I had my 5-year-old tried it last night.  He had 1 tablespoon and I had a big glass of water ready for him. He still coughed a bit after the first dose.  Then I gave him the 2nd tablespoon and he didn't cough for the entire night. It works like miracle. This is amazing!  It works better than the Vicks that I rubbed on the bottom of his feet. Anyway, thanks for the recipe. My DS doctor said his cough is called night time asthma and it is caused by allergy.  Now, I know what to give him for cough instead of Delsym. Thank you so much for this great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
monkey meat

this recipe goes real well with my lumpia recipe. this came from the same party as the lumpia did. awesome, tender and very tasty. no monkeys were harmed in any way in the preparation of this recipe. enjoy!

1. mix 7up , soy sauce and garlic in a large bowl
2. place pork loin strips in bowl
3. cover and refrigerate overnight
4. weave meat on skewers
5. grill until done
6. for me , it takes about 15 minute to cook
7. delicious !
demonstrations.review: I am sorry to say that I don't really like this recipe. It tasted like soy sauce on soy sauce.  Too salty and don't have any other favor.  Maybe I have done something wrong...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: Thanks Kittencal again for another great recipe.  DH and DS tried it tonight for dinner and all of them were pleased. DH said he wants the leftover for lunch tomorrow!

target.recipe_text:
roasted rosemary potatoes with garlic

this italian favorite pairs up especially well with the recipes i posted for mediterranean roasted green beans with slivered amonds recipe #21300 and/or roasted asparagus recipe #21148. from the mediterranean vegan kitchen.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. place the potatoes and garlic in a shallow baking dish large enough to hold them in a single layer
3. drizzle with the oil and toss well to evenly coat
4. sprinkle with the rosemary , salt and freshly ground pepper
5. toss again
6. roast , uncovered , for 40-50 minutes , depending on size , turning halfway through cooking time , or until the potatoes are nicely browned and tender through the center
7. serve hot
8. serves 6
target.review: Delicious....I folloewed the recipe to a ree.  My 10 year old whodoesn't eat potatoes ate these. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coq au vin  chicken braised in red wine

elegant but hearty chicken and wine dish. a nice blend of burgundy, herbs, and garlic. i serve this with hot cooked noodles, crusty french bread, and a salad for a wonderful company meal. and don't forget the wine!

1. mix flour , salt and pepper and put in paper or plastic bag
2. drop chicken pieces into bag and shake to coat
3. in large skillet fry bacon until crisp
4. drain and reserve bacon bits
5. brown chicken in bacon drippings
6. remove to a plate
7. add onions and mushrooms to skillet and cook until onions are tender
8. drain off fat
9. return chicken pieces to skillet
10. add remaining ingredients , including bacon bits
11. cover and simmer about 1 hours
12. or until chicken is tender
13. remove bouquet garni before serving
14. skim off excess fat
15. if desired , sprinkle with snipped parsley
demonstrations.review: We loved the sauce and I loved that the chicken didn't have to marinate over night. Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
company pork roast

this is very tasty and have received rave reviews. i serve the liquid from the roast, in a small bowl, to spoon over the meat.

1. place roast , fat side up , in foil lined roasting pan
2. mix remaining ingredients and brush on all sides of roast
3. cover with foil and bake at 325f for 2 1 / 2 hours basting frequently
4. uncover the last 45 minutes to brown roast
demonstrations.review: One word saya it all....DIVINE. The roast came out succulently. This recipe will definately become a family tradition. Thanks for sharing :).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
applebee s garlic mashed potatoes  copycat

applebee's has the best mashed potatoes. i found this knock-off recipe on e-cookbooks.net. we had it last year for christmas and it was just heavenly.

1. place a single layer of garlic cloves on a sheet of heavy-duty aluminum foil and wrap tightly
2. roast in 400f degree preheated oven for approximately 45 minutes or until soft
3. unwrap and let cool until touchable
4. peel cloves and mash with potatoes when they are ready
5. wash and rinse potatoes under cold water
6. it is not necessary to peel potatoes , unless you desire
7. in large sauce pan , bring red potatoes to a slow boil for approximately 20 minutes
8. remove from heat and drain in colander
9. in pan or bowl , combine potatoes , peeled and roasted garlic cloves , and all other ingredients and mash with a potato masher
10. keep warm
demonstrations.review: Delicious...one word says it all, the garlic adds great but subtle flavor. It took almost a whole bulb of garlic to get a quarter cup though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic shrimp

easy, yummy, and garlicy. doesn't get any better.

1. heat oil and butter in a large skillet
2. add garlic and shrimp
3. sprinkle with salt and pepper
4. saute 2-3 minutes or until shrimp turn pink
5. turn shrimp with spatula
6. cook shrimp 2 minutes longer on other side
7. remove shrimp to serving platter
8. garnish with lemon wedges
9. we give this a little squirt with the lemon wedge
demonstrations.review: Delicious and soooo very easy.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizzeria pizza sauce

this quick and easy sauce tastes like that which you would find at your neighborhood pizzeria! i found the original recipe on the internet, but adapted it to my families taste.

1. in a medium saucepan , saut garlic in oil until golden
2. add tomato paste , water , sugar , oregano , basil , cheese and wine
3. season with salt and pepper , to taste
4. simmer for 10 minutes over medium low heat
demonstrations.review: doubled recipe & used only about1/2 the amount of red wine.Thanks for sharing..

target.recipe_text:
broccoli roasted with garlic  chipotle peppers and pine nuts

this is so easy and full of great flavor from the broccoli being roasted with garlic spiciness and smokiness from the chipotles and creaminess from the pine nuts. keep in mind if you don't use seasoned salt and use regular salt you don't need so much.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. place the broccoli in a roasting pan so all will be 1 layer
3. mix all the remaining ingredients together then pour over the broccoli
4. place in oven for 10 minutes
5. toss and return to oven for 10 more minutes give an other toss for 5 -10 more minutes
6. enjoy !
target.review: Yum!!  Great flavor, loved it.  I used the pre-cut broccoli florets in the produce section, and subbed a dash of red pepper flakes for the chipotle peppers.  Definitely my favorite way to eat broccoli!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green beans in garlic tomato sauce

i found this in an old family circle magazine. it has become a staple at easter. i serve with ham and twice baked potatoes.

1. cook green beans till tender-crisp
2. saute onion and garlic in butter
3. when onion is soft , about 3 minutes , stir in flour and paprika until well blended and cook for a minute
4. if it is too thick add some of the tomato juices
5. cook till slightly thickened , stirring constantly about 2 minutes
6. add tomatoes and green beans , breaking up the tomatoes with the back of a spoon
7. stir till coated , stirring constantly , about 5 minutes
8. simmer for 1 hour on the stove or put in crock pot for 2-3 hours if so desired
demonstrations.review: I absolutely LOVED this recipe!  I used frozen green beans (French style).  I used olive oil instead of butter, and I only had one can of tomatoes, so i subbed one 8-oz can of tomato sauce for the other.  Family loved it!  It's a keeper for sure.  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chili ever

this recipe is wonderful and easy. i throw everything in my crockpot and a few hours later - homemade chili! i also top with onions, cheese or salsa. delicious!

1. brown ground beef and drain
2. combine all ingredients in a large pot and simmer for 2-3 hours
3. you can also put all ingredients in crock pot and simmer on low for up to 9 hours
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  Even my picky dh liked it :)  I did leave out the celery and substituted canned diced tomatoes for the fresh.  Will definitely be using this one again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat banana chocolate chip muffins

here is a moist, lowfat alternative for those who love a banana chocolate chip muffin

1. combine sugar and egg and blend well
2. add the mashed bananas , applesauce , and yogurt and stir to combine
3. stir in chocolate chips and set aside
4. in another bowl , combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
5. add to the wet mixture and stir until just blended- the batter will be lumpy
6. pour the batter into muffins tins
7. bake at 375 for 10-15 minutes- be careful not to let them get too brown
demonstrations.review: Yum! Made a couple substitutions, but this recipe was delicious!! Kids loved it. One warning...these really puff up, so leave a little room in the top of your muffin tins...mine spilled over during baking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best yellow cake ever

a bit unusual mixing technique assures a perfect cake every time. frost with 1 1/2 batches of my semi classic butter-cream frosting, any flavor will do, but we like the milk chocolate best.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease two 9-inch x 1 1 / 2 inch cake plans line bottoms with parchment paper grease bottom and flour entire pan
3. in a medium bowl lightly combine the yolks , 1 / 4 cup milk , and vanilla
4. in a large mixing bowl combine the dry ingredients and mix on low speed for 30 seconds to blend
5. add the butter and remaining 3 / 4 cup milk
6. mix on low speed until the dry ingredients are moistened
7. beat for 90 seconds at medium speed to develop cake structure
8. stop mixer , scrape down the sides
9. gradually add the egg / milk / vanilla mixture in 3 batches , beating 20 seconds after each addition
10. stop mixer , scrape down the sides and give it a final mix by hand
11. pour the batter in the prepared pans and smooth surface
12. bake 25 to 35 minutes or until toothpick inserted in cake comes out clean and the cake springs back when pressed lightly in center
13. cool the cakes in the pans for 10 minutes , then invert onto a buttered rack
14. reinvert cakes so that tops are right side up
15. cool to room temperature and wrap tightly with plastic wrap
demonstrations.review: It had a really good flavor, but was a little too dry for my taste.  Still, a good recipe.  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ultimate brownies

from the 1990 collection 

1. preheat oven to 325f degrees
2. melt chocolate and butter together in large bowl
3. add sugars
4. mix well
5. add eggs and vanilla , mix well
6. add flour and salt
7. stir until blended
8. add walnuts
9. pour into greased 13x9 pan
10. bake 25 minutes
11. let cool
12. make frosting-------------
13. melt chocolate and butter together
14. stir in milk
15. add powdered sugar
16. beat for 3 minutes or until smooth
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  My dh loved it.  I didn't have any walnuts, so I omitted them, and topped with chopped almonds.  A big hit.  :)  I also had to bake for about 40 minutes, 25 wasn't nearly enough.

target.recipe_text:
stir fried asian vegetables

as with most stir-fries i add and delete ingredients depending upon what i have on hand. this is a good basic veggie stir-fry from cooking light. prep all of the ingredients before you start cooking because the cooking phase is quick.

1. combine first 5 ingredients in a small bowl
2. stir with a wire whisk until well-blended
3. set aside
4. heat oil in a wok or large nonstick skillet over high heat
5. add carrot , celery , and onion
6. stir-fry 2 minutes
7. add snow peas , corn , and mushrooms
8. stir-fry 2 minutes
