9. add broth mixture
10. stir-fry 1 minute or until thick and bubbly
target.review: This was even better than we imagined it would be! We ended up leaving out the baby corn and used sliced fresh mushrooms instead of canned. We also added some broccoli and sliced peppers. We did make the sauce exactly as stated though, and it was so tasty. Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
three cup chicken

this is a traditional taiwanese dish that we always order in our favorite chinese restaurant. i begged the chef for this recipe and he very reluctantly gave it to me! i just made it for dinner tonight and couldn't wait to post this to share it with all of you!

1. heat up the sesame oil in a wok or a large skillet on high heat
2. add garlic , ginger and serrano peppers , stir fry until fragrant , about 2 minutes
3. add the chicken pieces and cook until it's white in color , about 5 minutes
4. stir together the soy sauce , rice wine and sugar in a bowl , pour over chicken
5. bring to a boil , then turn down the heat to low
6. let cook , uncovered , until sauce thickens , about 30 minutes
7. turn heat back up to high and add basil and scallions , cook for another 2 minutes
8. serve over steamed rice
demonstrations.review: Well, I first have to say that I didn't follow the recipe exactly, but I stayed pretty close to it, and my family thought it was delicious! I guess the only changes that I made, was that I didn't add any Thai basil, because I didn't have any, and I also didn't have any scallions. Also, instead of using sugar, I used honey. I served it with brown rice and an Asian salad and it made for a very tasty dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern barbecued beef tips

a southern classic that is delicious and easy to make. the sauce is a sweet and tangy barbecue sauce that cooks with the meat, flavoring both the sauce and meat. my family loves this dish! thanks barbiann!

1. in a large skillet over medium heat , saute onions in butter , when onions are tender add meat and cook until browned
2. mix in mustard , worcestershire sauce , vinegar , salt , pepper , sugar and catsup
3. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 45 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: These were actually pretty good! I admit, I was a little bit skeptical, even after reading the good reviews, but the meat turned out nice and tender and the sauce had good flavor. I will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
heathier banana pumpkin spice bread

this is a delicious wholesome bread that is perfect for breakfast or snack. the whole house will smell of the wonderful aroma of this freshly baked masterpiece that turns out perfectly every time. very rich in vitamin a. optional to add wheat germ, walnuts, or grated zucchini as it is a very forgiving recipe. enjoy. may do muffins or mini loafs.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease a large loaf pan (approx
3. 8 1 / 2 x 2 1 / 2 x 2 1 / 2
4. in a large bowl , whisk together mashed bananas , pumpkin puree , oil , eggs and vanilla until combined well
5. in a medium bowl , whisk together flour , erythritol , baking powder , baking soda , cinnamon , ginger , allspice and salt
6. add flour mixture to wet ingredients in large bowl and stir until just combined
7. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
8. bake until top is deeply browned and springs back when touched gently , about 70 to 85 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was delicious!! I did have to make two changes though...I only had one banana, so in place of the second banana, I used about 1/4 cup of sour cream to add moisture. Also, I didn't have any allspice, so I used some nutmeg instead. Thanks for the recipe. I'll definitely be making it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy ginger beef

if you like sweet, spicy, crispy chinese food- this is for you. adapted from a recipe i saw on "fixing dinner" with sandi richard.

1. place cornstarch in a large bowl
2. add water gradually while whisking
3. beat eggs into cornstarch mixture
4. toss in beef and stir to coat
5. pour 1 inch of oil into wok , heat until boiling hot , but not smoking
6. add a quarter of the beef to the oil
7. seperate with a fork and cook , stirring frequently , until crispy , remove , drain on paper towel and set aside
8. repeat until all the beef is cooked
9. drain off all oil except for about 1 tablespoons and add carrots , onion , ginger , and garlic in that order
10. stir fry briefly over high heat
11. combine last 5 ingredients and add to vegetable mixture
12. bring to a boil and then add beef
13. heat thorough and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Made this last night and my husband LOVED it. Said it tasted just like the stuff you get at the restaurant. I used flank steak and it was super tender. I was a little bit disappointed because the beef didn't come out quite as crispy as I would have liked, but I guess I'll just have to cook it a little bit longer next time. Either way, it tasted great. As a slightly more healthful option, next time I may try just stir-frying the beef instead of dipping it in the batter and deep-frying it. I served this with some brown rice. Will definitely keep this one in the rotation. Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground beef gyros

this is a great summer meal and quick and easy to put together and tastes wonderful. refreshing served with the cucumber sauce and is even low in fat. i think this came from quick cooking. it's a favorite in our house.

1. in a bowl , combine first 5 ingredients
2. cover and refrigerate
3. in separate bowl , combine ground beef and seasonings
4. mix well
5. shape into 4 patties
6. grill , covered , over medium to high heat for 10 to 12 minutes or until meat is no longer pink , turning once
7. cut patties into thin slices
8. stuff into pitas
9. add lettuce , cucumber , tomato , and onion
10. serve with yogurt sauce
demonstrations.review: These were great! We will definitely make them again. Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
denny s style french toast

i do not remember where i got this recipe, but my husband says it tastes just as good as what he had at denny's. i am just amazed at all of the great reviews on this recipe!! my family loves it, so i thought i would share it here and i'm so glad i did because it seems you all love it just as much!!! thanks to all of you who have tried it!

1. mix together the eggs , milk , flour , sugar , vanilla , salt& cinnamon
2. heat a large skillet , or griddle
3. when the skillet is hot , add 1 tablespoon butter
4. if the butter smokes , your pan is too hot
5. turn down the heat
6. dip each slice of bread into the batter for 30 seconds on each side
7. let some of the batter drip off , then put in skillet
8. cook each slice 1 1 / 2-2 minutes per side until each side is golden brown
9. add more butter , if necessary , to cook all of the slices
10. to serve , put on plate , dust with powdered sugar
11. serve with butter & hot syrup
target.review:
Very easy and delicious! However, I found that no matter how low I set my stove, my slices were burning when I used butter to cook them. I switched to canola oil and things came out much better. I'd recommend just putting some butter on top when serving for that butter flavor (even better, whipped butter like Denny's does), or use only clarified butter to fry these up in your frying pan.

Mixing the dry ingredients together in a small bowl then adding to the egg mixture helps it all combine with no lumps.

I used Whitewheat bread, which was perfect -- just enough crust, thickness and chewiness to it, and did not soak up too much batter. I also added a tiny splash of orange extract (could also use orange juice,) since I've noticed when eating french toasts at restaurants, there's often hint of orange flavor that adds a bit of unexpected and sophisticated yumminess.

This recipe is a total keeper! Thank you for sharing it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek seasoning mix

i used this mix tonight on a couple of cornish hens...yum!!

1. combine all ingredients
2. store in an airtight container
3. serve with red meat , pork , poultry , or fish
4. yield: 1 / 4 cup
demonstrations.review:
Absolutely amazing!! I needed "greek seasoning" for a pan-seared spice rubbed pork chop recipe. I made this mix and added a tsp of cumin to it and WOW, best pork chops ever. My husband was blown away.

In the bowl it smelled a bit unusual, with the cinnamon & nutmeg, but once it was rubbed on the meat it smelled perfect! So don't let yourself be put off by the cinnamon & nutmeg -- it starts off smelling overpowering but once you start cooking, it becomes a subtle & interesting background flavor.

I will use this regularly. I can't wait to try it for making other greek & mediterranean dishes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hush puppies justin wilson style

these are absolutely the greatest and go great with fried fish. this recipe is from the late justin wilson

1. combine all dry ingredients
2. add egg , buttermilk and onions
3. mix well
4. drop in deep hot oil by spoonsful and brown on all sides
demonstrations.review:
Wow, these taste like something you'd get from a restaurant! The only tweak I made was to add a bit of Nature's Seasoning spice blend for a bit more flavor.

Only needed 3/4c of buttermilk for the batter to come together, and they fried up great in peanut oil at around 350F.

This recipe is a definite keeper.Thanks for posting it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera bread  black bean soup

this is my own version of panera bread's black bean soup. it tastes a lot like it, and i love it! use vegetable stock to make it vegetarian.

1. in a pot , combine the first six ingredients
2. simmer for 10 minutes
3. add half a can of beans , salt and cumin
4. cook for 5 minutes
5. puree soup
6. add the rest of the beans to the soup
7. combine the cornstarch with 1 1 / 2 tablespoons of water
8. add the lemon and the cornstarch to the soup
9. cook until thickened
demonstrations.review:
Ohhh, this recipe is SO GOOD. Tastes just like Panera. They probably wonder why I stopped showing up every day. It's beacuse I'm at home, eating huge bowls of this with some fresh baked French bread!

An immersion blender really helps get the right consistency.

It also freezes perfectly. I make a huge batch and freeze half of it.

So good, and good for you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken curry in a hurry

watch out or you might get pulled over for a speeding ticket in the kitchen! ready in 20 minutes. :)

1. mix together flour , salt and cayenne pepper in a plastic bag
2. add chicken in small batches , shaking to coat
3. heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add chicken and cook until lightly browned
5. then add curry powder and toss to coat
6. remove from pan
7. add onion and garlic to pan , adding a little more oil if necessary , and cook for 2 minutes , then add broth , raisins , and tomato paste
8. return chicken to pan and simmer uncovered for 8 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and sauce has thickened
9. garnish with cilantro and a dollop of yogurt
10. serve with quick cooking minute rice , if desired
demonstrations.review:
Wow, what an awesome recipe! Comes together quickly and easily, and really does taste as good, if not better than anything we've had in a number of Indian restaurants! I also love how the ingredients are surprisingly basic and simple to prepare -- I've spent a lot more time on curries in the past.

I served this yummy curry with jasmine rice made with cumin seeds (cooked easily with the help of my rice cooker), some peas (from frozen), and some Trader Joe's naan. Husband ate so much that he looked like he would explode!

This recipe has immediately been elevated into our rotation of favorite go-to meals. Next time I will probably use about half the amount of cayenne and/or swap in ancho chili powder instead, because it was a bit too spicy for me to enjoy as much as I would like (though my husband thought the spiciness was perfect.)

Thanks for sharing such a mind-blowing recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dark chocolate cake

while it takes slightly longer to prepare this recipe than a box mix, the resulting moist, delicious cake makes it very worth the little extra time. i consider this 'perfect' chocolate cake. this cake is excellent with  both with recipe #261024 and recipe #208959 (the dark flavor version). (i use recipe #95416 when i'm decorating the cake.) i love how the leftovers are still moist even a day or two later. (i store my loosely covered with plastic wrap.)
my father adores this cake with recipe #261024 on it. for his birthday, father's day etc. i make him cupcakes with the icing on them and individually wrap them. he keeps them in his freezer for when he wants "a piece of cake". he claims they are as good as when they are fresh. 
(even though it isn't where i got the recipe from so i can't vouch for it, reviewers have said it is the recipe on the hershey's cocoa can. i would recommend using their special dark cocoa if possible.)

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour two 9 inch round baking pans or one 13x9 inch pan
3. in large mixer bowl , stir together dry ingredients
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in boiling water by hand
7. i usually use between 2 / 3 & 3 / 4 cups
8. the cake is still very moist but it doesn't seem to "fall" as much as it cools
9. this might have to do with our high humidity or brand of flour or other factors so i don't know if it will work for everyone
10. pour into prepared pan
11. bake 30 to 35 minutes for round 9-inch pans , 35 to 40 minutes for rectangular pan or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. because they have a tendency to overflow if you fill them more than 2 / 3 full , i usually get about 27-28 cupcakes per batch
13. bake for approximately 18-20 minutes
14. cool 10 minutes
15. remove from pan to wire racks
16. please
17. chocolate drink mixes that you add to milk or water to drink will not work in this recipe
demonstrations.review:
Whoa! I used this recipe for my first attempt at making chocolate cake from scratch, and, I kid you not, my results were as good or better than a professional bakery's?!?!?! My husband and I have gotten chocolate cake and cupcakes many times from lots of bakeries over the years, so to have something come out of my oven that I whipped up on a whim one afternoon is incredible.

As suggested by other reviewers, I used only 2/3 cup boiling water and mixed in 1 tsp of espresso powder for the coffee flavor. The batter was thinner than I'm used to seeing with boxed cake mixes but it baked up fantastic!

I made cupcakes and my total baking time was about 25 minutes -- however, I did overfill the liners so the 20 minute estimates from other reviewers might be closer to the mark when I next make these.

They tasted kind of bland when they first came out of the oven, even with icing smeared on it (I couldn't wait.) However, once they cooled for 2 hours or so and I piped straight all-butter buttercream they tasted better. Then once they had a chance to sit overnight in a container and the icing crusted up just a bit? OMG, PERFECTION. Richly chocolatey but not overwhelming, not too sweet so biting into it with icing doesn't make you feel instantly toothachey, and the density and crumb are just right.

Seriously just blown away how this recipe is professional, bakery quality. And not much harder than a box of cake mix, just requires a few more measuring cups and spoons. Total keeper!

target.recipe_text:
all american hamburgers

been making  1/4 pound burgers like this forever, and dont think its ever been posted here.  one of our all-time favorites on the summer grill! we also love these with a slice of cooked bacon for a bacon cheeseburger.

1. in a large bowl , combine beef , soup mix and worcestershire sauce
2. mix just until blended dont overwork the meat
3. shape into eight patties
4. grill over medium coals to desired doneness or until no longer pink in the center and a minimum temperature of 160 degrees , brushing frequently with barbecue sauce
5. top with cheese
6. continue grilling until cheese is melted
7. for each serving
8. fill bun with lettuce , pickle slices , tomato and hamburger patty
target.review: These were good. We try not to eat much carbs around here, so we didnt use a bun, but I did fry up some bacon for my DH and kiddos and they ate it like that. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast sticks   oamc

i got this basic recipe from another site but changed it a little for my family.  the original recipe called for orange juice as the liquid instead of milk.  i also added the vanilla as we think it gives it a nice flavor.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. cut each slice of bread into 3 pieces to make sticks
3. texas toast is a very thick sliced bread about 3 / 4" thick
4. you could substitute french bread if texas toast is not available
5. in a bowl , mix together melted butter , eggs , sugar , cinnamon , vanilla and milk
6. beat well
7. dip sticks into egg mixture and place on a cookie sheet that has been sprayed with cooking spray
8. if there is any dip left , you can drizzle it over the sticks
9. bake for 25 minutes on middle rack of oven
10. turn halfway through baking time
11. allow to cool
12. flash freeze on cookie sheet , remove and place in a ziploc bag
13. to reheat: place 3 sticks on a microwave-safe plate and heat on high for 1 minute until warm
14. serve with syrup
demonstrations.review: I am rating this on behalf on my 5, 3, and 1 year old boys...They loved these! Perfect breakfast idea for my 5 year old starting K in 2 days. Will always make sure I have these in the freezer! Thank you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stardust chocolate pancakes

these are just heavenly!

1. in a small bowl , combine milk , egg and butter
2. whisk until blended
3. in another bowl , combine flour , cocoa powder , sugar , baking soda and salt
4. mix well
5. add milk mixture
6. whisk just until dry ingredients are moistened
7. heat griddle over medium heat until hot
8. for each pancake , pour scant 1 / 4 cup batter into griddle
9. cook 1-2 minutes or until batter is set around edges
10. carefully turn over pancake
11. cook 1-2 minutes or until pancakes are cooked through
12. repeat with remaining batter
13. sprinkle pancakes with powdered sugar
14. serve warm with desired toppings
15. try using metal star shaped cookie cutters !
demonstrations.review: I am rating these for my three boys...ages 5, 3, and 2, since chocolate really isnt my thing. My boys LOVED these. I knew my husband would too, but hes getting over the stomach flu so he didnt try them :( Put some reduced sugar strawberry preserves on it, then sprinkled powdered sugar on top. We have 5 leftover so with some eggs again thats a super simple breakfast for me to fix them. Thank you!!!!! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tarragon chicken casserole

this is so easy, and so good. no browning, just put the chicken in and pour the sauce on, and bake!! the tarragon makes it an elegant entree.

1. in 13 x 9 inch baking pan , place chicken pieces
2. do not overlap
3. place onion rings over top
4. mix seasonings with cream of chicken soup and milk and spoon over chicken
5. bake , uncovered , in 375 degree oven for 40 minutes
6. sprinkle chicken with almonds , if desired
7. bake 10 minutes more or until chicken is tender
demonstrations.review: I cant rate this based on me because  I am sick and everything is bland:( BUT I can rate based on my DH & my 3 boys ages 5, 3, and 1 and they LOVED this chicken. I made mashed potatoes with it, and used the sauce as the gravy. Will make this again, so I

demonstrations.recipe_text:
inside out stuffed green bell peppers

this is a lot easier to make than the regular stuffed green peppers. my husband just loves it this way.

1. in a skillet , brown beef
2. drain
3. transfer to a greased 2-quart casserole dish
4. add the next 8 ingredients
5. cover and bake at 350f for 1 hour or until rice is tender
6. uncover and sprinkle with the cheese
7. return to the oven until cheese melts , about 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is SOOOO good! I did make a few changes. 1) instead of stewed tomatoes, I used FIRE ROASTED diced tomatoes 2) For the rice, I used the Ben's Spanish Rice that you microwave in a packet for 90 seconds 3) I added a can of tomato sauce, and used chicken broth instead of water because I had some leftover from dinner last night. I also mixed everything up in a seperate bowl and just dumped it all in. Only took about 30 mins in the oven because the rice was pre cooked. Oh, :) and added some cumin and garlic powder to the ground beef. Thanks so much! I will be sending this recipe to my mom.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic baked ziti

this baked ziti recipe is a simple italian casserole dish that my family enjoys.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large skillet , cook ground beef , onions , and garlic over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes or until beef is browned
3. stirring frequently
4. stir in spaghetti sauce , chicken broth , and oregano
5. reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes
6. stir 1 cup of the sauce into the cooked ziti noodles
7. spoon 1 / 2 of the ziti mixture into a 13x9x2-inch baking dish
8. sprinkle with 1 1 / 2 cups mozzarella cheese and 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese
9. top with 2 cups sauce , then remaining ziti mixture and remaining sauce
10. cover and bake 20 minutes
11. sprinkle with remaining mozzarella and parmesan cheese
12. return to oven and bake uncovered for 10 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: This was amazing!! The fact that my 4 year old, 2 year old, and 1 year old boys all loved this really makes me wish I could rate a lot more stars! I used whole grain penne pasta, used about 4 garlic cloves, and added a bit more cheese on the top. My two oldest kept saying "mmmmm!!" and my 1 year old ate a lot more than I expected. Thanks so much! I will be making this again and again!

target.recipe_text:
mango cobbler

this is delicious, especially warm. you can serve it with ice cream or whipped cream but i like it plain.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. combine mangoes , lime juice , and nutmeg in a mixing bowl
3. stir until mango is coated with lime and nutmeg
4. spoom fruit into a greased 8 inch square pan
5. in another bowl combine flour , baking powder , salt and brown sugar
6. mix well
7. using a pastry cutter , cut the butter into the dry mix until it resembles a course meal
8. stir in milk , mix until smooth
9. spread batter evenly over fruit
10. bake at 375f for 20-25 minutes or until lightly browned on top
target.review: I am inundated with mangoes right now and have been searching for recipes to use them.  This was tasty.  The topping turned out different than I expected but it was still good.  Two of us managed to eat the whole thing in 3 days.  I have big mangoes so I had to place a cookie sheet under my pan to catch the drippings.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
authentic margarita mix

reportedly the origional "authentic" margarita mix, from scratch, and easy too!  this came from tijuana (baja california, mexico) and was named after the inventers daughter.

1. place ingredients in blender and blend well
2. for an authentic magarita , mix three parts mix , 1 part tequila and 1 / 2 part cointreau or triple sec and serve in a glass with salted rim
3. (to salt the rim , wipe rim of glass with lime skin and dip upside down in a plate of salt
4. to make bartenders simple syrup , used in bars since it won't cloud or settle in your drink , take 1 cup water , 2 cups sugar and simmer or nuke until the sugar is dissolved , cool to room temperature keep on hand
demonstrations.review: Quite tasty!  I had to use more lime because my limes were on the small side.  Hubby says, "woo hoo!" so this recipe is a keeper.  Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate margarita

with all these mexican dishes i have posted, i figured i needed to add some drinks along with them, so here is the first of many.

1. rub the rims of 2 martini glasses with a lime wedge , then dip the rims in a dish of course salt
2. refrigerate the glasses if desired
3. in a shaker , combine the lime juice , tequila , and orange liqueur
4. add ice and shake 10 to 15 seconds , then strain into the prepared glasses
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  This was so easy and so good.  I used Cointreau and I love the orangy taste.  My only problem is I want another one don't have any more limes.  I'll definitely stock up on limes at the market from now on.  :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
condensed cream of soup mix   homemade substitute

i found this interesting recipe by request.  it's great to have on hand and you can adjust the seasonings to suit yourself! =)

1. using an air tight container combine dry milk , cornstarch , onion flakes , pepper and chicken bouillon
2. if desired also add basil and thyme
3. mix well
4. when using the mix combine 1 / 3 cup of the mix with 1 1 / 4 cups of water in saucepan
5. cook and stir until thickened
demonstrations.review: Thank you so much for posting this recipe.  Canned soups are so expensive here and most of the crock pot recipes I look at making call for cream of _____ soup.  I haven't made it yet but am so excited I found this I had to leave a comment.  Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
boiled maine lobster

move over martha stewart. simple is better. let the natural flavor of the lobster come through and watch your guests' eyes glaze over.

1. bring to a roiling boil a large kettle of salted water
2. place lobsters in boiling water head first
3. cover and cook for 15 minutes
4. remove and serve with melted butter
5. how to eat: twist off the claws
6. crack each claw with a nut cracker
7. separate the tail piece from the body
8. bend back and break the flippers off the tail piece
9. insert a fork where the flippers have been broken off and push out the meat
10. separate the back from the body
11. open the remaining part of the body by cracking apart sideways
12. there is some good meat in this section
13. the small claws are excellent eating ! the meat sucked out like like sipping through a straw !
demonstrations.review: Thank you so much for this simple yet delicious recipe!  I was a little intimidated about cooking the lobsters my husband caught yesterday but since you included the instructions how to eat them it worked out great.  I've only ever had lobster that had been cracked open for me in a restaurant and even though this was a little more work this tasted better than the restaurants!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: I was home alone and wanting some comfort food and this did the trick!  I halved the recipe because I didn't have enough cream cheese for a full recipe.  After reading a lot of the comments I added extra potato.  It was delicious!

target.recipe_text:
venison marsala

found this online a few years ago(don't remeber where).  a great way to do something different with venison.

1. trim meat and cut into 1 / 4 inch slices
2. combine flour , cheese , and salt
3. dredge meat into flour mixture and shake off excess
4. melt 2 tbsp butter in skillet and brown meat 1 min on each side
5. set aside and keep warm
6. add to skillet remaining butter and melt
7. add onions and mushrooms , saute until tender
8. add consomme , lemon juice , and wine
9. mix well
10. return meat to skillet and cover
11. simmer for 10-15 minutes or until tender
12. to serve , pour pan juices over meat and sprinkle with parsley
13. nice served over rice , but that's up to you
target.review: Wow! This was fantastic! Well worth the effort it takes for an elegant, delicious meal. We have made this several times and also used venison steaks and chops. Both work very well. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese style noodle and pork soup

yummy!
low sodium, low cholesterol, low cal.

1. cook noodles according to package directions , or until of desired consistency , drain
2. meanwhile , in a large pot combine all remaining ingredients
3. stir in the cooked noodles
4. bring to a full boil over high heat , stirring occasionally
5. boil for about 10 minutes
6. sprinkle each serving with chopped green onions if desired
demonstrations.review: This was very good and so easy to make. Make sure your noodles are a little undercooked before you add them to the soup mixture since they will continue to cook. Also, I used Bok Choy cabbage and it was wonderful. Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
unbelievable chicken and rice

kids and adults alike love this dish! its easy and its so delicious. i've been making it since college days (1966) friends still request it!

1. melt butter in a 13x9 baking dish
2. add the rice and all three soups
3. mix well
4. this will look like a gloppy mess at this point but thats how it should look
5. put the chicken breasts on top of the soup mixture and season with paprika , garlic salt and pepper
6. cover with foil and bake in a 350 oven for one hour
7. remove foil and bake another 30 minutes
8. remove from oven and let it sit for about 10-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: A true comfort food in my opinion. I had to cook it about 15 minutes longer because some of the rice around the edges wasn't quite done. What a great flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible quiche

easy, quick quiche recipe using bisquick as a base. you can subsitute other veggies for the mushrooms if you prefer.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease a 9-10 inch pie plate
3. sprinkle mushrooms , cheese , and onion evenly over bottom of pie plate
4. place remaining ingredients in blender , cover , and blend on high for 1 minute
5. pour into pie plate
6. bake until golden brown and knife inserted in center comes out clean
7. let stand 5 minues before cutting
8. refrigerate leftovers
demonstrations.review: I thought this was great. Easy and will work with almost any veggie and meat combo. I fried up some leftover sausage, added onions and mushrooms. I also didn't have enough cheddar cheese, so I used a little cheddar, a little Muenster and a little Feta. Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked pasta with sausage and tomato pesto

the smoked gouda can sometimes be hard to find, but it adds a great flavor and texture.  the hot italian sausage adds some spice.  got this one from "the best american recipes 2003-2004."

1. in a large dutch oven over medium-high heat , add the sausage and onion
2. cook , breaking sausage up with a spoon , for about 5 minutes , or until softened , stirring frequently to cook onion evenly
3. add garlic and cook for 1 more minute
4. add marinara sauce and reduce heat to medium
5. simmer for 10 minutes , or until sauce begins to thicken
6. stir in pesto and season with salt and pepper to taste
7. set aside
8. cook penne in a large pot of salted boiling water for about 10 minutes , or until al dente
9. drain well
10. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
11. oil a 9-x-13-inch baking dish
12. spread a thin layer of sauce over bottom of dish
13. in a large bowl , combine pasta with remaining sauce , the gouda or mozzarella , 1 / 3 cup of the parmesan , and spinach , mixing well
14. spoon mixture into prepared dish and sprinkle with remaining 2 / 3 cup parmesan over top
15. bake for about 30 minute or until casserole begins to bubble and cheese is browned
16. serve hot
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic! I used a shredded Italian blend of cheeses as I couldn't find any smoked Gouda. I also use hot turkey italian sausage to bring down the fat grams. It was very flavorful and easy to put together.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice   spinach bake

nan

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. cook and drain spinach
3. mix spinach , cooked rice , cheese , eggs , margarine , rosemary , milk , onion , worcestershire sauce and salt
4. place in a 10 x 6-inch casserole dish and bake 20 to 25 minutes
demonstrations.review:
This was great! Light and very flavorful. I've served it twice. Once with grilled chicken and the other time with a pork roast. Easy to put together.
Yummy!

target.recipe_text:
savory microwave new potatoes

easy, fast and delicious. a great side dish with any meat.

1. place margarine in 2-quart microwave safe casserole
2. microwave on high for 30 to 45 seconds until melted
3. add potatoes , leeks and red pepper , toss to coat
4. cover tightly
5. microwave on high for 6 to 8 minutes until potatoes are tender , stirring once halfway through cooking
6. sprinkle with parmesan cheese
target.review:
Very good-very easy.  Potatoes in a pinch. I also omitted the leeks only because I've never purchased/eaten them.  Couldn't even tell you what they look like. 
But I did add onions to take their place and we liked this recipe alot. 
Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my egg salad

plain and simple, my favorite.

1. chop eggs , place in bowl
2. add all other ingredients , and mix well
3. serve on desired bread
4. great on rye
demonstrations.review:
Just add some shredded lettuce and you've got MY Egg Salad, too!!

Just a nice light, lunch.  Yum.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome baked pork chops

these chops remain moist and tender, and the sauce is to die for! you probably have all the ingredients in your kitchen to make this! serve these chops over rice!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. rinse pork chops , pat dry , and season with garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste
3. place the beaten eggs in a small bowl
4. dredge the pork chops lightly in flour , dip in the egg , and coat liberally with bread crumbs
5. heat the oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat
6. fry the pork chops 5 minutes per side , or until the breading appears well browned
7. transfer the chops to a 9 x 13 baking dish , and cover with foil
8. bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour
9. while baking , combine the cream of mushroom soup , milk and white wine in a medium bowl
10. after the pork chops have baked for an hour , cover them with the soup mixture
11. replace foil , and bake for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review:
One word for ya...OMG!!!  
(I guess that's three.)
I have never had a recipe taste this great! EVER!  The only thing I changed was that I added an envelope of LIPTON GOLDEN ONION SOUP MIX to the soup/milk/wine mixture. I also listened to the other reviewers and cooked the chops in the pan for only 3 and a 1/2 minutes per side.  Then for only 48 minutes for the first bake; and then only 25 minutes for the final bake. 
HOLY CRAP this is the BEST pork chop recipe IN THE WORLD!  
I will never even look to improve this one! 
Wow...wow. Yum.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ambrosia

ambrosia

1. drain fruit well
2. mix all ingredients together
3. refrigerate for 24 hours
4. be sure fruit is well drained or ambrosia will be mushy
demonstrations.review: I added a cup of coconut like some others.  I also ran just short on maraschino cherries so I used the leftover CANDIED cherries from my Christmas baking and they worked great here!  It's REALLY hard to not eat the entire batch!!!  It reminds me of the holiday fruit salad that my mom used to make when I was a kid...but we just called it 'FRUIT SALAD'!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini ribbons with basil butter

found this in a magazine! made it with the garlic excellent!   also instead of boiling the ribbons, i fried them in butter until tender. wow! that was excellent also! very easy either way.

1. bring pot of water to boil
2. mean-while , with vegetable peeler-slice zucchini lengthwise into ribbons
3. add zucchini to boiling water
4. cook until tender , 30-60 seconds
5. drain and transfer zucchini to serving bowl
6. add butter , oil , parmesan , basil , and red pepper flakes
7. gently toss until butter is melted and zucchini are coated
8. i also added 1 / 2 tsp of garlic powder to this !
demonstrations.review: Wow! This is a new favorite! It made itself a spot near the front of my recipe "Faves" book! Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
arizona hobo potatoes

easy dish to accompany steaks, burgers, chops, ribs, etc. on the grill.

1. grills vary widely , so you may need to experiment with the heat setting
2. for my propane grill , i use medium-high heat , or even high heat , high enough to sear / brown the meat dish when i throw them on the grill
3. )
4. wash potatoes and cut into slices 1 / 4 inch or so with skin intact
5. slice onion into thin slices , then separate into rings
6. on heavy duty aluminum foil , about 18" to 24" long , put in the center a layer of potatoes
7. follow with a layer of onion rings
8. sprinkle with salt , pepper , and a hint of garlic
9. repeat layers , dotting each second layer with butter
10. wrap the foil securely around the layers
11. should make a packet about 15"-18" long and 10" wide
12. put the foil package on the grill about 45 minutes to an hour before the intended serving time
13. its okay if the bottom layer caramelizes
14. some will love those bottom pieces !
demonstrations.review: Simple and delicious!  However, I just layered the ingredients in a baking dish, covered with foil and baked @ 350 for about 40-50 minutes.  Take the foil off and bake for another 15-20 minutes. Mmmmm.

target.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
target.review: Soooo good and easy.  Thanks.  Loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted brussels sprouts

i got this from the barefoot contessa cookbook. so good.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cut off the ends of the brussels sprouts and pull off any yellow outer leaves
3. mix them in a bowl with the olive oil , salt , and lemon-pepper seasoning
4. transfer them to a sheet pan and roast for 35 to 40 minutes , until crisp outside and tender inside
5. shake the pan from time to time to brown the brussels sprouts evenly
6. sprinkle with more kosher salt , if you like , and serve hot
demonstrations.review: My new favorite way to cook brussel sprouts.   YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thick and creamy new england clam chowder

this is the best chowder i've ever had. i've had chowder at legal seafoods in boston, which i have to say is good, but mine is better! if you like thick chowder, you'll love this one!!

1. add bacon to sauce pan and cook on medium low heat until crispy
2. add onion and cook until translucent
3. add clam juice from both cans
4. add potatoes
5. cook and cover until potatoes are fork tender , about 15-20 minutes
6. stir occasionally so potatoes won't stick
7. add clams , soup , cream , milk , and dill weed
8. stir together
9. add butter and let melt into the chowder
10. cook for about 30-45 minutes or until thickened
11. stir occasionally
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herbed top round roast

taken from the everyday low-carb slow cooker cookbook

1. pour the red wine and water into the slow cooker crock
2. set aside
3. in a small bowl , combine the herbs , pepper , salt , and olive oil
4. stir to combine
5. using clean hands , rub the oil and herb mixture all over the beef roast
6. place the roast into the slow cooker crock
7. sprinkle the garlic and onions aroudn the raost and lay the bacon strips over the top of the roast
8. cover and cook on low for 10 hours
9. before serving , flip the roast over in the slow cooker , then turn the slow cooker off and let the roast rest in the slow cooker for about 15 minutes
10. remove roast to a platter and let it drain for a few minutes
11. to serve , use a sharp knife to slice the meat against the grain
12. if you like , dip the roast slices into the cooking juices before serving , or serve the cooking juices alongside the beef
demonstrations.review: Sorry....I just didn't like it.  Way too herby and not tender.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marshall field s chicken salad  with sandwich variations

love the combination of flavors and textures in this savoury salad.  delicious also as a sandwich (leaving out the grapes).  try it cold or a yummy hot variation: on one slice of sweet, whole-grain bread, spread 1/2 cup of chicken salad and put under broiler until heated, but not bubbly; top with 3 slices of bacon and 1 slice of provolone cheese.  return to broiler until cheese is melted.  yum!

1. mix all dressing ingredients together in large bowl
2. add chicken , green onion , pecans , and grapes if you are using them
3. mix well
4. cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours
5. arrange lettuce leaves on plates and top each with a scoop of salad
6. chef's
7. i shred my chicken the easy way using the plastic blade in my food processor and just giving it a few short pulses
demonstrations.review: Just made this chicken salad this afternoon.  Gave my hubby a spoonful and asked what it needed......absolutely nothing.  I made it for sandwiches tonight.  Don't know if I can wait that long.  I only had some chicken my husband had smoked so I used that.  Yummy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttery shrimp and pasta

this is a really simple dish to make and it's quite elegant.

1. have pasta ready
2. in lg skillet , heat butter
3. add shrimp and garlic
4. saute 4 minutes , remove shrimp from skillet
5. add half and half
6. bring to a boil
7. reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes , stirring frequently
8. add shrimp , basil , cheese , pepper and pepper flakes
9. pour sauce into a bowl
10. add pasta and toss well
demonstrations.review: Just plain ol' yummy!

target.recipe_text:
green chili casserole

i found this in one of my mothers' old recipe books. this is one easy dish to put together and now my family loves it!

1. brown meat with onion
2. drain well
3. dip tortillas in hot oil just long enough to soften
4. drain on paper towel until needed
5. mix soup , chilies and milk in mixing bowl
6. cut tortillas into fourths
7. layer in 3 quart casserole dish
8. cover with layer of meat mixture , layer of soup mixture and layer of cheese
9. repeat
10. cover
11. bake 300 for 30-40 minutes
target.review: yummy & easy. I went with another suggestion & added a can of diced tomatoes with green chili's. I didn't have mozzarella cheese, but used cheddar cheese & it tasted great :)Very tasty. Served alongside tortillas & salsa. Thank you for the easy & yummy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I have made this a few times, but this time was the best!!! I added 4 tbsp of cream cheese, fresh basil, garlic & some flour to thicken the sauce. WOW....such a great, easy, restaurant quality dish!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe. Tasted like a giant Reese's. Was easy to make & very good. Would definetally make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kickin  buffalo dip

hot wings with a cracker. soooo simple to make. if you like wings & blue cheese, you will love this dip. i like to layer it, but you can just mix it all together and dip your favorite cracker right in. my grandson says,"you know how i know you love me mom mom? it's the kickin' buffalo dip you make just for me" hope you enjoy.

1. mix cream cheese & 1 / 2 of blue cheese dressing together
2. spread on the bottom of oven proof dish
3. toss chicken in wing sauce & place on top of cream cheese mixture
4. add hot sauce to taste
5. sliced scallions to taste
6. pour remaining blue cheese dressing on top
7. top with shredded cheese
8. place in 400 oven for about 20 minutes or until bubbly & golden
9. munch away
10. you are going to want to double this
11. if you like hot , use jalapenos or more hot sauce
12. i didn't care for the hot wing sauce
13. do not cheap out on the blue cheese
14. cheap blue cheese is sour tasting
demonstrations.review: Awesome & easy :) I would use a wider dish, instead of a deeper dish next time. Very tasty, we can't wait to make again. Thank you for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked texas jalapeo peppers

another recipe submitted by a co-worker for our chili cook-off at work. these were gone in nothing flat!

1. cut jalapeo peppers in half lengthwise
2. remove seeds
3. place peppers in boiling water for 5 minutes
4. drain well
5. combine cream cheese , cheddar cheese and worcestershire sauce
6. stir well
7. place one heaping teaspoon cheese mixture on each pepper half
8. sprinkle with bacon
9. place on a baking sheet
10. bake at 400f for 5 minutes or until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: Wonderful & easy! Made it for 4th of July & they were gobbled up! Will definitely make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jo mama s world famous spaghetti

my kids will give up a steak dinner for this spaghetti. it is a recipe i have been perfecting for years and it is so good (if i may humbly say) that my kids are disappointed when they eat spaghetti anywhere else but home! in fact they tell me i should open a restaurant and serve only this spaghetti and garlic bread. in response to requests, i have posted the recipe for recipe #28559 that uses approximately 1/2 of the sauce from this 
recipe. have spaghetti one night and lasagna later!  thanks to all of you who have tried my recipe and have written a review.  i read and appreciate every one of them!  chef note:  after i posted this recipe i remembered a funny incident--my dear husband usually has a nice bottle of wine handy so when i make a batch of spaghetti i just help myself to a splash of it. on one occasion, there wasn't a bottle opened, but there was a bottle sitting on the counter so i got out the corkscrew and helped myself. for some reason, the spaghetti that night was the best ever. my husband asked what wine i put in it and i showed him the bottle. he nearly fell off the chair. i had opened a rather expensive bottle he had bought to give his boss. goes to show you--don't use a wine for cooking you wouldn't drink. you get the best results from a good wine!

1. in large , heavy stockpot , brown italian sausage , breaking up as you stir
2. add onions and continue to cook , stirring occasionally until onions are softened
3. add garlic , tomatoes , tomato paste , tomato sauce and water
4. add basil , parsley , brown sugar , salt , crushed red pepper , and black pepper
5. stir well and barely bring to a boil
6. stir in red wine
7. simmer on low , stirring frequently for at least an hour
8. a longer simmer makes for a better sauce , just be careful not to let it burn !
9. cook spaghetti according to package directions
10. spoon sauce over drained spaghetti noodles and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: This is awesome & a family favorite. It makes a lot of sauce, so we froze half of it & had it a few weeks later. It was even better the second time! I am craving it again :)

target.recipe_text:
creamed ground beef sos

i loved it when mom used to make this for us! i have no idea if she originally made it for dad, who had been in the army, or if she just liked it because it tasted good and was a budget stretcher. a traditional favorite, good ol' sos.  note: the title of this recipe specifies that it is made ground beef, rather than chipped beef; "authentic" sos is generally made with chipped beef, however many folks also refer to the ground beef version by the same name.

1. in a large skillet over medium heat , brown the ground beef and onion
2. stir in the flour , granulated bouillon , salt , pepper , and garlic and onion powders
3. saute all together until flour is absorbed , about 5 minutes
4. gradually stir in the worcestershire sauce and milk
5. bring it all to a simmer , stirring , and cook until thickened , about 5 to 10 minutes
6. serve over toast , biscuits , noodles , rice , or potatoes
7. delicious !
target.review: Excellent! So easy and was fabulous! Did everything as stated and didn't add the optional cayenne! Served on top of egg noodles. Will make again...thanks for a fantastic recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
puppy chow candy

unlike it's title, this recipe is for children, not the family puppy. i received this recipe from a friend of mine who runs a dayhome. it's a big hit at her house, and when i made it for my kids, they loved it! and it's sooo easy to make!

1. melt chocolate chips , peanut butter and margarine in a pot over low heat on the stove stirring until smooth
2. stir in vanilla
3. in a large tupperware bowl with a lid , first pour in cereal , and then add chocolate mixture , stirring until cereal is well coated
4. sprinkle icing sugar , one cup at a time , onto coated cereal , seal with lid , and shake until cereal is well coated
5. cereal should look white by the time you are done
6. keep stored in a tightly sealed bowl
demonstrations.review: Excellent! This is easy and great! Thanks for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage lover s cabbage quickie

i'm doing the nutrisystem diet, and since cabbage is listed as a 

1. spray a heavy skillet with the nonstick spray
2. put the whole bag of shredded cabbage in the skillet and sprinkle with generous amount salt and pepper
3. stir and toss until wilted and just beginning to brown a bit
4. serve hot
demonstrations.review: WONDERFUL!! I cooked on medium for about 20 minutes and added a few sprays of butter. When it started to brown I turned up the heat for about 10 more minutes....Delish and healthy...Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy potato bites

i thought of this the other week when i was tired of the same old potato dishes. similar to what my mum used to make. my dh has requested twice since.

1. preheat oven to 220c
2. dice potatoes into bite size pieces
3. pour olive oil& melted butter into ovenproof dish
4. toss diced potatoes in oil& butter
5. season to taste
6. sprinkle cheese& breadcrumbs over potatoes
7. toss mixture til potatoes are covered in cheese& bread crumbs
8. cook in oven for approx 30 mins turning once half way thru
9. secrets to success , make sure oven is hot& adding the olive oil stops the butter from burning
demonstrations.review: I followed the recipe but maybe did something wrong. They baked for almost an hour and did not ever get as cripy as I thought they were supposed to. Still had a good flavor though! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven baked mostaccioli

great make ahead meal for parties and family dinners.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in large skillet , combine beef , green peppers and onion
3. cook until meat has browned
4. stir in spaghetti sauce , tomato sauce and water
5. bring to a boil , then simmer 5 minutes
6. pour 1 cup of meat sauce mixture into the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish
7. top with half of the pasta
8. then a layer of 2 cups of mozzarella cheese and all of the parmesan cheese
9. for the next layer , add 2 cups of sauce , remaining pasta and mozzarella cheese
10. top with remaining sauce
11. bake at 350 degrees for 30-45 minutes or until hot and bubbly
12. cook the assembled meal right before serving
13. you may have to add some cooking time because of the refrigeration
14. to make clean up easier , consider foil lining the baking dish
15. easy clean up is so nice when entertaining !
demonstrations.review: Wonderful Donna! This was my very first time making mostaccioli and thought this was a perfect recipe. Only thing I did different was added a little sugar to my sauce mixture and only used mozzarella cheese and no parmesan. Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taffy apple pizza

a pampered chef winner! one of my favorites. the crust is sugar cookie dough! did you know taffy originated in germany? and apples are used extensively in germany too! i guess that makes this a german recipe!(lol)

1. put sliced apples into the lemon-lime soda to soak so they won't brown
2. preheat oven to 350
3. roll cookie dough into a 12-inch circle on a 13" baking stone that has been lightly floured
4. bake approximately 5 minutes longer than directions on package say
5. let cool
6. in a bowl , mix peanut butter , cream cheese , sugar and vanilla
7. spread over cooled cookie crust
8. then drain apples and arrange in a spiral , to cover entire "pizza"
9. srinkle with cinnamon and pour over caramel topping
10. it's ready to serve !
11. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Made this for work this morning and was wonderful! I did use 1/2 c. peanut butter (personal preferance) and sprinkled with cinn. and sugar mixture...Perfect recipe to us up some apples! Thanks

target.recipe_text:
wild rice mushroom stuffing

a very easy but beautiful stuffing to serve with your bird for the holidays or anytime of the year.

1. rinse and cook wild rice to package instructions
2. set aside
3. spread cubed french bread in a single layer on a baking sheet
4. broil 5 to 6 inches from heat for 4 minutes or until lightly toasted , stirring after 2 minutes
5. set aside
6. preheat oven to 325f
7. melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat
8. add onion and garlic
9. cook and stir for 3 minutes
10. add mushrooms
11. cook for 3 more minutes stirring occasionally
12. add sage , thyme , salt , pepper and cooked rice
13. cook for 2 minutes stirring occasionally
14. stir in broth
15. add pecans and toasted bread cubes
16. toss lightly
17. transfer to very large casserole dish
18. cover with lid or foil
19. bake for 40 minutes or until hot
target.review: My family loved this stuffing. I don't tend to like stuffing so I haven't tried it yet but I made this and they loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
little bear s  seafood soup

this is a creation for my 4 year old  boy, hunter, inspired by his favorite tv show, "little bear". 

you could use any fish in this recipe, but catfish seems to have the best texture when cooked and holds together better than more flaky fish. 

it may seem like a lot of work, but really does go together easily and even the kids like it! its a bit of a cross between a soup, a stew, and a gumbo, with a slight tomato base and a bit of spice. 

the measurements are not very exact, just do what seems right and adjust to taste.

1. saute onion and garlic in olive oil over medium heat until onion is almost tender
2. sprinkle in 2 tablespoons old bay seasoning and stir constantly for about 30 seconds
3. add in chicken stock , red wine vinegar , oregano , parsley , and tabasco
4. bring to almost boiling over medium heat
5. while this is heating , lay out frozen seafood mix , shrimp , and catfish on a cutting board
6. sprinkle with the juice from one lemon
7. then sprinkle with remaining one tablespoon old bay seasoning and black pepper
8. let this stand while mixture is heating
9. when liquid is almost boiling add in the seafood mix , rice , tomato soup , canned tomatoes and okra
10. be sure to add all liquid from both the tomatoes and okra
11. lastly , add in the gumbo fil
12. simmer for 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: Very good... I changed it a little didn't measure everything but it turned out great my husband has had jambalaya in red lobster and a few other places but definitely perfers this one!! Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delilah s macaroni and cheese

this is delilah winder's mac and cheese as featured on oprah and throw down with bobby flay in which she came a very close second.

1. preheat oven to 325
2. bring a large sauce pan of salted water to a boil
3. add the macaroni and cook until al dente
4. drain and set aside to keep warm
5. whisk the eggs in a large bowl until frothy
6. combine the velveeta , butter , and 2 cups of the half and half in a large bowl
7. add the warm macaroni and toss until the cheese is melted and the mixture is smooth
8. add the remaining half and half , 3 cups of the yellow cheddar , the remaining grated cheeses and the salt and pepper , tossing until completely combined
9. pour the mixture into a 9x13 inch casserole or baking dish and bake for 30 minutes
10. sprinkle the remaining 1 cup of yellow cheddar cheese and bake until golden brown on top , about 30 minutes more
11. serve hot
demonstrations.review: My little brother is a huge noodles and company mac & cheese fan, but I made this for Thanksgiving dinner and he said that noodles and company must step aside cause there is now a better!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thanksgiving turkey brine

brining the turkey with this recipe makes a very moist turkey!  delicious!

1. combine all ingredients in a stock pot , bring mixture to a boil , lower heat and simmer for 15-20 minute allow brine to cool completely
2. rinse turkey under cook running water , inside and out
3. pat turkey dry with paper towels , then immerse turkey in cooled brine
4. turkey should be completely submerged in liquid
5. my pot wasn't big enough , so the
6. cover the pot and refrigerate for 8-10 hours or up to 24 hours
7. remove turkey , rinse , pat dry and roast as usual
demonstrations.review: Fantastic Brine I didn't boil it as to the fact we had nothing big enough to boil it in.  We had put all the makings in a big home depot bucket and left it in the snow for two days... only bringing in when it was too cold! It was the BEST TURKEY my family has ever had.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin pie dip

this is different and really delicious. great for fall parties.

1. beat cream cheese and sugar at medium speed with an electric mixer until smooth
2. add pie filling , cinnamon , and ginger , beating well
3. cover and chill 8 hours
4. serve with gingersnaps and apple slices
demonstrations.review: Dangerously yummy!! My mom and I make it every year this time for any party or gathering we have and we always end up sending atleast one person home with the recipe. Ahhh now i need to make some!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barbecued asparagus

nan

1. trim the bottoms of the asparagus and place in a shallow dish
2. pour the olive oil , salt , pepper and lime juice over the asparagus and toss well to coat thoroughly
3. grill over hot coals for 2 to 3 minutes , or until tender
4. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: YUMMY! Have made twice now and both times was wonderful!

target.recipe_text:
fresh peach cobbler  the absolutely best ever

a wonderful version of the old classic, this peach cobbler has a glazed finish to the top.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. in a mixing bowl , combine tapioca , peaches , sugar , cinnamon and nutmeg
3. mix thoroughly
4. pour the fruit mixture into a buttered 9" x 13" baking dish
5. in a bowl mix thoroughly the ingredients for the cobbler dough
6. spread over the fruit mixture
7. in a medium mixing bowl , stir together dry cobbler topping ingredients
8. sprinkle evenly over the cobbler dough layer
9. then pour the boiling water evenly over the cobbler
10. bake for 1 hour and 20 minutes or until knife inserted comes out clean and top has a golden crust
target.review: This cobbler is delish.  The best I've ever had?  No.  But, it is in the top 3.  I fed it to my wife who rated it "damn good".  That is high praise indeed.  Made it with canned peaches.  It will be sinful with fresh ones.  If you love peaches, you owe it to yourself to try this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
opal s pumpkin pie

this recipe makes 2- 9" pies.  if you make one large pie instead you will have to add time to the baking to get it done.  this recipe was given to me by opal beebee, several years ago. this is a handed down family recipe. it was once prepared in the white house for one of the former presidents. opal's daughter had served in the national guard and had met a pastry chef who later worked at the white house and called opal to ask for the recipe for thanksgiving dinner at the white house. do not eliminate the heavy cream in the pie...the cream and the amount of spices listed is what makes this pie so special. it is good hot or cold. i never tasted hot pumpkin pie until i tasted this one.  

i found out this past christmas (2009) that this bakes well without a crust as well.

i had to make 3 pumpkin pies to take to my son's home.  i had enough mixture left over make another pie but not enough pie dough for a 4th pie.  so i spray oiled a round casserole dish, filled with mixture and baked.

1. combine first 8 ingredients in a large bowl , mixing well
2. combine the evaporated milk and the heavy cream in a small saucepan
3. heat the milks to the scalding point
4. add scalded milks to the other ingredients , mixing well
5. pour equally into the two unbaked pie shells
6. bake 350 degrees for about 1 hour
7. pie is done when a knife inserted into the middle comes out clean
8. top with desired topping
demonstrations.review: This pie is GREAT!  So creamy and delicious.  We will have this one from now on.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
big grandma s best peanut butter cookies

this is my husband's grandmother's recipe that is cherished by the family. they are the best cookie that melts in your mouth. they don't have the normal peanut butter fork crossing...but more of a crackled sugar type cookie... my husband comes from a huge family - and these are one of the cherished recipes!!

1. cream together the sugars , crisco , peanut butter
2. add the eggs and vanilla
3. sift the dry ingredients together and add gradually until blended well
4. roll into tablespoon size balls
5. roll cookie dough balls into sugar
6. place on cookie sheets- do not mash with fork in normal "peanut butter cookie" fashion !
7. bake at 350 oven for 11-13 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wow!! These are the best peanut butter cookie I've ever had. Love the crispy/chewy combination. Thanks a million!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chicken crescent roll casserole

this will also work great with turkey; if you do not have chicken breasts, then use any leftover cooked chicken. if desired you can fill the crescents just with the filling mixture and omit the soup, just brush with butter before baking. they are wonderful just stuffed with the filling! a few members have experienced a soggy bottom, so you might want to consider just drizzling half (or even a little less) of the soup mixture on top and a little around the sides of the crescents, then save the rest of the soup mixture for another time (this will help prevent a soggy bottom). you may use the jumbo crescent rolls and stuff with more chicken mixture :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. butter a casserole dish
3. in a saucepan , mix half and half cream , 3 / 4 cup grated cheese and undiluted chicken soup
4. heat just until the cheese melts
5. for the filling --- in a bowl , mix the soft cream cheese with butter until very smooth , then add in garlic powder
6. add in the chopped chicken , onion and cheddar cheese
7. mix well until combined
8. add in 2 tablespoons whipping cream or mayonnaise
9. mix to combine
10. season with seasoned salt or white and black pepper to taste
11. unroll the crescent rolls
12. place 1 heaping tablespoon chicken mixture on top of each crescent triangle , then roll up starting at the thicker end
13. drizzle a small amount of soup mixture on the bottom of the dish
14. then place the crescent rolls seam-side down on top of the creamed mixture in the casserole
15. drizzle the remaining sauce on top and sprinkle with 1 cup grated cheese , or amount desired
16. bake for about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wonderful.  Tasted like chicken pot pie.  The grandkids ate like they were starving.  We will be having this one again.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever pumpkin pie

southern living. always served for thanksgiving dinner.

1. combine pumpkin and remaining ingredients in a large bowl
2. beat at medium speed with an electric mixer 2 minutes
3. pour into prepared piecrust
4. bake at 425 degrees for 15 minutes
5. reduce heat to 350 degrees
6. bake 50 additional minutes or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean
7. cool on a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Pretty good pie.  Different from the traditional pumpkin pie.  We liked it.  Wife said it was too sweet, but that didn't stop us from inhaling it.  Next time I will cut down on the sugar a little bit.  Also, the 50 minute cook time was too much for me as well.  Will have to cut back some next time.  And there will be a next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese cinnamon crescents

these are so yummy.  would be perfect for breakfast or brunch or anytime!  i just made a batch late this evening.  a parent brought these in for a teacher's luncheon and everyone loved them.

1. roll out one can of crescent rolls in bottom of 9x13 pan
2. i sprayed pan with cooking spray
3. cream together: 2 8oz
4. cream cheese
5. 1 cup sugar
6. 1 teaspoon vanilla
7. spread this mixture over crescent rolls
8. lay second tube of crescent rolls over mixture
9. melt 1 / 2 cup butter , mix in 3 / 4 cup sugar ,
10. 1 teaspoon cinnamon , and pour over top
11. bake at 350 for 30-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: So good its addiction in a pan. DW says its a 10 star recipe. I agree. Its nice to get wonderful flavor in such an easy and quick recipe. Thanks a million.

target.recipe_text:
chicken pot pie with 2 crusts

this is old-fashioned, from scratch, comfort food. this has been a family favorite for years. i like to take this to other families when they are in need of a meal. it's always a winner. i like making it with leftover turkey, too! i often add some cooked diced potatoes.

1. heat butter over low heat until melted
2. blend in flour , onion , salt and pepper
3. cook over low heat , stirring constantly until smooth and bubbly
4. remove from heat
5. stir in broth and milk
6. heat to boiling
7. stirring constantly
8. boil and stir one minute
9. stir in chicken and veggies
10. reserve
11. line pie plate with prepared bottom crust
12. pour in filling
13. top with top crust
14. cut slits in center to vent
15. flute edges
16. cook uncovered in 425f oven until crust is brown
17. approximately 30-35 minutes
target.review: This was great! Better than any frozen pie. My oven was broken so I cut the recipe in two and used a small pan that I use for hot dips (i.e. spinach and artichoke) and it was just enough for two. I used frozen carrots and peas and threw in a little poltry seasoning.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
absolute best ever lasagna

my family's favorite. this is a very meaty lasagna. we prefer it with cottage cheese, but you can easily substitute ricotta.

1. brown ground meat , onion and garlic
2. add salt , pepper , parsley , oregano , basil , chopped tomatoes with juice
3. stirring until well mixed
4. cover and simmer 1 hour
5. cook lasagna noodles according to package directions
6. drain and set aside
7. spray a 13 x 9" baking pan with cooking spray
8. combine riccota cheese , eggs , pepper , 2 tablespoons parsley , parmesan cheese and 1 / 2 1lb of mozzarella cheese
9. in a lasagna pan , layer noodles , meat sauce , and cheese mixture
10. repeat
11. top off with layer of noodles
12. sprinkle evenly with remaining mozzarella cheese
13. make sure to cover noodles completely
14. bake at 375f for 40-60 minutes , or until cheese mixture is thoroughly melted
15. (i cover w / foil for about 40 minutes , then uncover for 15-20 minutes
16. let sit for 15-20 minutes before cutting and serving
demonstrations.review: I have to say that this was my first lasagna. I brought it to a friend who just had a baby, she and her husband loved it! They were so amazed that it was my first one. This is my new go to Italian dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream pie  chocolate  coconut  and banana variations

hands down, the best cream pie recipe i've ever tasted!  it was passed down from my mom, who got it from a neighbour while living briefly in los angeles way back in 1969.  the chocolate variation has been the universal birthday 'cake' in my family for almost as long as i can remember.  i've adapted it to be more microwave friendly and even less time-consuming than the original.  (cooking time is cooling time)  in case you don't have a microwave or just want to try this on the stovetop, see my cousin crystalb's recipe#108268 for the method.

1. in a microwavable bowl , mix sugar , flour , and salt
2. in a separate bowl , whisk milk and eggs or egg whites
3. add to dry ingredients
4. microwave for two minutes and stir
5. return to microwave for one minute intervals , stirring in between , until custard starts to cook
6. remove from microwave and add margarine and vanilla
7. cool slightly and pour into pie crust
8. cover with wax paper and refrigerate 2 hours before serving
9. chocolate cream pie: add 1 / 2 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips with margarine and vanilla and mix until chips are completely melted
10. pour into crust
11. banana cream pie: slice 2 or 3 bananas into bottom of pie crust before pouring pie filling over top
12. coconut cream pie: add 1 / 2 cup coconut with margarine and vanilla and pour into pie crust
13. serve with whipping cream and garnishes of your choice
demonstrations.review: OMG! I made this recipe and everyone loved it! I made the chocolate version but, I added 1 cup of chips instead of 1/2 cup. It was so rich and creamy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marshall field s chicken salad  with sandwich variations

love the combination of flavors and textures in this savoury salad.  delicious also as a sandwich (leaving out the grapes).  try it cold or a yummy hot variation: on one slice of sweet, whole-grain bread, spread 1/2 cup of chicken salad and put under broiler until heated, but not bubbly; top with 3 slices of bacon and 1 slice of provolone cheese.  return to broiler until cheese is melted.  yum!

1. mix all dressing ingredients together in large bowl
2. add chicken , green onion , pecans , and grapes if you are using them
3. mix well
4. cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours
5. arrange lettuce leaves on plates and top each with a scoop of salad
6. chef's
7. i shred my chicken the easy way using the plastic blade in my food processor and just giving it a few short pulses
demonstrations.review: I made this for tea sandwiched at a bridal shower tea party and they were great. My husband loved it too and ate all the leftovers. From what I can remember... it was very good. I left out the nuts cause husband is allergic.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern fried salmon patties

salmon patties are quick and easy.  i got this recipe from my son's babysitter many years ago.  my son is now 20 and we still eat these at least a few times a month.  these are very moist when done.

1. open salmon and drain thoroughly
2. place drained salmon in mixing bowl and flake evenly with a fork
3. add onion , corn meal , flour , mayonnaise , and egg
4. stir until well blended
5. shape the mixture into patties about the size of an average burger or less
6. cook in oil in skillet over medium heat until browned on each side
7. turn once while frying
demonstrations.review: These were fantastic! I have been eating salmon burgers since I was a little girl and these were by far the best ones I've ever eaten. My husband was very skeptical but even he asked if I would make them all the time. I used 3 small cans of skinless and boneless salmon instead of one big can.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed red potatoes with garlic and parmesan

the potatoes are ready in our garden, and this is the first recipe i reach for! these are so good!!

1. put potatoes and garlic in lg pan
2. cover with water
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes , until potatoes are tender
5. drain well
6. mash with the butter , milk , and salt
7. stir in the parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: My family loved these, no changes. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
corn dogs

here's a good basic recipe for corn dogs. i'm looking forward to trying some of the suggestions from reviews as to adding dry mustard or other seasonings to the batter.

1. combine cornmeal , flour , baking powder , salt and egg
2. mix well
3. stir in milk to make a thick batter
4. place in a tall narrow glass
5. let stand 4 minutes to thicken
6. meanwhile , heat oil to 375 degrees f
7. pat hot dogs dry
8. dust with flour if desired
9. insert sticks in hot dogs
10. dip into batter
11. let excess drip off
12. fry until golden brown , about 5-6 minutes
13. drain on paper towel
target.review: I followed directions to the letter, and wound up with naked cooked hotdogs, and a bunch of cornmeal swimming around them.  I did put it all in a bowl, put some mustard in it and it tasted good, it just didn't stick to the dogs at all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp cocktail mexican style

i got this recipe from a friend that tried something similar in a restaurant on south padre island.

1. place shrimp in a large bowl
2. stir in garlic , red onion and cilantro
3. mix in clamato , ketchup , lime juice , minced serrano and horseradish
4. season with salt
5. cover and refrigerate 2-3 hours
6. stir in avocado when ready to serve so it doesn't get too mushy
demonstrations.review: This was wonderful. I used vegan shrimp, and it was perfect.  The part that I made with real shrimp tasted just like what I had on SPI myself, which was what I was looking for.  I didn't have any horseradish, but I did have some shrimp cocktail sauce, so I just used 1/4 cup of that instead. Exactly what I wanted it to be, thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
trisha s easy fried rice

quick and easy fried rice recipe that is good and does not have to have all the veggies.

1. melt butter or margarine in non-stick skillet
2. add onions and carrots , and fry until onions are transparent and carrots are crisp
3. add peas and cook for 1 minute more
4. push veggies to one side and scramble eggs in empty side of skillet
5. add soy sauce
6. spoon in rice and mix until well blended
7. fry until steamy and serve
demonstrations.review: This was the easiest fried rice recipe I have ever made.  Very tasty.  I added some rice wine while frying the rice in, and that added some flavor.  We used low sodium soy sauce and that didn't hurt the flavor at all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn  tomato  and black bean salsa

this is an excellent dish alone or as a side dish for both hot and cold entrees. best if allowed to stand at least an hour in order to marinate the flavors. can even be made a day or two ahead, as the flavors get even better.

1. to make red chile honey: mix honey , red chile powder , cumin and garlic salt
2. combine all ingredients in a small saucepan on low heat and cook for 1 minute , stirring constantly
3. to make salsa: lightly saute the onion and garlic in the olive oil until soft
4. mix the chopped cilantro , cumin seed , jalapeno , vinegar , honey , and salt together in a large mixing bowl
5. add the corn , tomatos , black beans and sauteed ingredients
6. stir to combine thoroughly
demonstrations.review: This is a good salsa recipe, easy to make, and it goes with a lot of different kinds of dishes, as well as being a kind of salad on its own.  I did also cut back on the honey, but then I used all the mix, instead of just the 1/3 tbsp required for one cup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy  speedy spaghetti sauce

a tasty sauce you can throw together on those nights that you don't have much time or have unexpected company drop in. you can add meats, veggies or whatever your preference is to the sauce.

1. stir all ingredients in a saucepan and simmer for 15-30 minutes
2. serve over spaghetti
3. sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Amazing easy sauce! I cut the sugar in half, and added a dash or so of red wine, and have been making this sauce weekly by popular demand for months now. Finally got around to reviewing. I have also, in a pinch, used a tablespoon of italian seasoning mix, in place of the mix of spices. I use minced garlic, but the garlic powder works great too! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai cucumber sauce  nam chim taeng kwa

a traditional condiment often served with satay and spring rolls.

1. place vinegar , water , sugar , and salt in saucepan
2. heat over medium heat , stirring until sugar and salt dissolve
3. bring to a boil and remove from heat
4. allow to cool
5. pour over cucumber , and sprinkle cayenne pepper on top
6. serve
demonstrations.review: I have been searching for years for this recipe.  I added 1/4 of a small red onion, sliced paper thin.  I also added one single, seeded, Thai pepper.  It was perfect, took me straight back to my favorite Thai restaurant!

target.recipe_text:
is it a baked potato or potato salad

it was 1987, i was living in my first apartment, and i had invited my first company over for dinner, a friend from work and his girlfriend.  i had planned on providing everything for dinner that night, and i was completely shocked when my company brought some food with them.  her potato salad tasted so much like baked potatoes, only it was cold and required no effort on my part to make it ready to eat.  it was so good that i had to ask for the recipe.  i have made it this way ever since.  this recipe is forgiving.  so, try to keep the general proportions correct and don't be so worried about exact measures.

1. wash your potatoes and cut them into approximately 1-inch thick wheels
2. cover wheels in a pot of water and boil until the potatoes are tender
3. drain and cool potatoes in a large mixing bowl
4. when potatoes have cooled , combine all remaining ingredients in the bowl with the potatoes
5. if you want to season the entire batch before serving , consider including any combination of the following before mixing all the ingredients together - salt , pepper , lemon pepper , garlic powder
6. and remember a little bit of seasoning in the mix tends to go further than seasoning added to each serving
7. if you are lucky enough , you will get everything evenly combined and still have some chunks of potato in the mix
8. if you don't , it still tastes great
9. cover and chill for at least two hours before serving
10. this can be made a day or two in advance of serving
11. prep time includes cooling the potatoes and chilling the salad
