I actually mashed the squash and eggs in the Kitchen Aid Mixer on a slow speed, then added diced roasted vegies, garlic and Mexican blend grated cheese and mixed slowly. I put it into a pan, topped it with a little cheese, warmed it up and YUM!

target.recipe_text:
angel hair pasta with simple garlic   basil

i adore angel hair pasta, and such a fine pasta doesn't always need a big sauce.  serve with some kind of cheese or "cheez" if you wish, sprinkled on top. my children like it with sliced olives.  there are many versions of this simple recipe, this one i adapted from www.cookingnook.com.  this would probably be good for 4 as a side dish or 4 for lunch with a salad.

1. bring a large pot of salted water to boil over high heat
2. meanwhile , heat the olive oil up a large saute pan over medium heat
3. once warm add the garlic and cook until it just begins to brown -- too long or too high and the garlic will burn
4. remove the pan from the heat and deglaze by pouring in the wine
5. return the pan to the heat and cook for a few minutes
6. the wine should reduce by about half
7. add in lemon juice , chopped tomato , and sea salt to taste
8. stir once or twice then remove the pan from the heat again and set it aside to wait for the pasta
9. add the pasta to the boiling water and cook until desired tenderness , following package directions
10. drain , then add the cooked pasta to the pan with the garlic & tomato mixture , along with the basil and some freshly ground pepper
11. toss well ,
12. generally they say 2 ounces of pasta is one serving , but for larger appetites this might not be enough
target.review: A very quick and simple recipe for pasta.  I used it as a side with breaded chicken. I forgot the lemon juice, though, and I had some Italian dressing mix that I threw in there for some extra flavor.  Also, I didn't have any white wine so I just used chicken broth.  This recipe is versatile enough to accommodate whatever you have in your pantry :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for chicken marsala

a must have for anyone that loves italian food. this is a extremely easy recipe and it is great for dinner parties or a romantic dinner with your honey. try it and let me know what you think! i buy pre-sliced mushrooms and pre-made broth and it really cuts down the time you spend preping.

1. place chicken breasts between two pieces of plastic wrap
2. with a meat tenderizing mallet , pound chicken breast until they are 1 / 4 inch thick
3. dredge breasts in flour until all sides are coated
4. heat olive oil in a large skillet or frying pan
5. cook breasts until almost done , about 3-4 minutes on each side
6. remove from pan being sure to keep warm
7. deglaze pan with marsala wine , making sure to scrape bottom of pan to loosen all browned bits that may be stuck on
8. add broth , mushrooms and garlic
9. cook on medium / high for 10 minutes or until reduced by half
10. add breasts back to pan and cook for another 10 minutes
11. serve over angel hair pasta
demonstrations.review:
I thought it was pretty good, and my hubby liked it too, which is saying a lot. However, my picky daughter didn't care for it. And the plain pasta noodles I made to eat with it didn't do it for her either. Any ideas on how to kick up some pasta noodles without clashing with the chicken?

Oh, and I didn't use mushrooms because my family doesn't care for mushrooms. I just substituted onions for the mushrooms in the sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
30 minute chicken noodle soup  from foodtv  rachael ray

from show of 5/16/02.

1. place a large pot over moderate heat and add extra-virgin olive oil
2. work close to the stove and add vegetables to the pot as you chop , in the order they are listed
3. add bay leaves and season vegetables with salt and pepper , to taste
4. add stock to the pot and raise flame to bring liquid to a boil
5. add diced chicken tenderloins , return soup to a boil , and reduce heat back to moderate
6. cook chicken 2 minutes and add noodles
7. cook soup an additional 6 minutes or until noodles are tender and remove soup from the heat
8. stir in parsley and dill , remove bay leaves and serve
9. this is a thick soup
10. add up to 2 cups of water if you like chicken soup with lots of broth
demonstrations.review: Very good, I added 1 chicken bouillon cube and skipped the parsnips but otherwise made exactly as directed.  Good, quick easy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
minced beef with chilli  garlic   holy basil

putting this here for safe keeping.

1. heat oil in a wok and stirfry small chillies and garlic until they begin to colour
2. add palm sugar , fish sauce , sweet soy and oyster sauce
3. mix well and add minced beef
4. gently cook until sealed , continually mashing with a wooden spoon
5. then add lime leaves and cup stock
6. mix well and cook for another 10 minutes taste for seasoning and add holy basil and long red chillies
7. stir and cook until wilted
8. sprinkle with spring onion and serve with steamed rice on the side
demonstrations.review: I did not have the fish sauce, so I was missing a key ingredient, unfortunately.  But yummy nevertheless.  Even hubby ate it, and he is a picky eater.  Of course, being the unusual sort he is, he turned his into a taco by eating it with tortilla chips, cheese, and some salsa verde.  Go figure.....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s chocolate cupcakes

this recipe was given to my mom by a next door neighbor many years ago. it makes a wonderful dark chocolate cupcake, or double the recipe for a sheet or layer cake. it has become a family favorite and is always requested at birthdays.

1. mix all ingredients together until moist and well blended
2. put in cupcake cups and bake for 20-25 minutes at 350 degrees f
3. frost with your favorite icing
4. to make a layer cake , double the recipes and put in 2 round cake pans
5. increase baking time to about 35 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Pretty simple to make, which is good for me because I'm not much of a baker.  Made these for Father's Day....added a tad bit more sugar, and chocolate chips after reading reviews.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Oh my....so good!  I was a bit dubious about this combination of ingredients but, I must say.....very very good.  Thanks for posting, this one's a keeper

target.recipe_text:
calico beans   baked beans w  3 kinds of beans

this is one of my favorite cookout side dishs! my aunt char makes these all the time and i finaly got the recipe from her! they are a great side dish with hamburgers, hotdogs, potato salad...the list goes on and they are yummy!

1. fry bacon until crisp
2. drain
3. fry ground beef in fat until tender
4. combine onion , ketchup , salt , mustard , vinegar , brown sugar , and partly drain beans in a 3 quart oven container
5. mix well
6. add hamburger and crumbled bacon
7. bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes
target.review: Excellent!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken schnitzel

i tried this recipe from the every food magazine and dh and i just loved it. the flavor, with garlic, parmesan, and a wine sauce, take it beyond the average schnitzel recipe. it's also fairly quick and easy enough for a week night meal.

1. beat eggs in a shallow bowl with garlic , parsley , salt and pepper
2. in a separate shallow bowl , combine breadcrumbs and parmesan cheese
3. dip each cutlet into egg mixture to coat completely , then dredge in breadcrumb mixture , patting it on to help it stick
4. for each 2 cutlets , heat 2 tbsp oil in a large non-stick skillet over med-high heat
5. cook 2 cutlets at a time until golden brown and cooked through , about 3 minutes per side
6. transfer the cooked chicken cutlets to an oven-proof platter or pan , and keep warm in the oven while cooking the remaining cutlets and making the sauce
7. wipe the skillet clean with paper towels
8. heat butter until melted and add wine
9. heat 30 seconds and stir in broth and lemon juice
10. season with salt and pepper
11. simmer 2 minutes
12. pour broth mixture over cutlets and serve
13. garnish with parsley and lemon slices
demonstrations.review:
This is MY FAVORITE DISH!!
I just love loved it and have made it numerous times now..It's one that will stay in my kitchen for years!  Thank you so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crescent topped casserole

i found this in taste of home's casserole cookbook, and it's delicious!!! the beef mixture and crescent roll topping make for a real hearty meal!

1. in a large skillet , cook beef and onion until meat loses its pinkness
2. drain
3. stir in tomato sauce and spaghetti sauce mix , then reduce heat
4. simmer , uncovered , for 5 minutes
5. remove from the heat
6. stir in sour cream , and spoon mixture into a greased 13" x 9" x 2" baking dish
7. sprinkle with mozzarella cheese
8. unroll the crescent roll dough into one rectangle , and seal seams and perforations
9. place over the cheese
10. brush with butter and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
11. bake , uncovered at 375f for about 25 minutes , or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: This meal is a great one for those of us moms who work full time..easy prep and in 30 minutes it's hot on the table!  Thank you for this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome blueberry muffins

this is a awesome blueberry muffin recipe. double it to make large muffins. i sometimes add cinnamon to the batter.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. grease muffin cups or line with muffin liners
3. combine 1 1 / 2 cups flour , 3 / 4 cup sugar , salt and baking powder
4. place vegetable oil into a 1 cup measuring cup
5. add the egg and enough milk to fill the cup
6. mix this with flour mixture
7. fold in blueberries
8. fill muffin cups right to the top , and sprinkle with crumb topping mixture
9. to make crumb topping: mix together 1 / 2 cup sugar , 1 / 3 cup flour , 1 / 4 cup butter , and 1 1 / 2 teaspoons cinnamon
10. mix with fork , and sprinkle over muffins before baking
11. bake for 20 to 25 minutes in the preheated oven , or until done
demonstrations.review:
This recipe is wonderful!

I doubled it and put it into a 9x11 oblong pan.  I baked it on 350 for 1 hour.
It's definitely a keeper in my book..Very moist and tasty!!  Thank you Debbie!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
claude s baked beans

updated on september 16, 2009. i posted this recipe on apr 22, 2001 and am embarrassed to say that just today i found out that the recipe is missing an ingredient! i talked to 'claude' and she (claudia, actually) said that the recipe needs to include 1 can of condensed tomato soup. i have added the soup to the ingredients list.  the recipe received several 5-star ratings before i corrected the ingredients list so i guess that goes to show that this is a really good recipe!  here is my original recipe description:

these beans are delicious. even those who don't like baked beans love these. this is the recipe that i am requested to bring to every potluck. i've made them in the slow cooker also but i think they cook best in the oven. they are a thicker consistency when baked in the oven.

1. brown sausage , celery , and onions put on side
2. mix remaining ingredients and then mix with sausage mixture
3. bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: These beans are OUTTA SITE!!!!  My hubbie can't keep a spoon out of them!!!  Thank you Marie!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best spinach salad

my mom got this recipe from a friend, and it has quickly become a family favorite. delicious!

1. saute in the butter , until lite brown , the package of ramen noodles and the slivered or sliced almonds
2. these are the"crispies" and will keep in a baggie in the freezer if you have any leftover
3. combine all the dressing ingredients in jar and shake to mix
4. this makes enough salad for 2-3 bags of baby spinach or baby romaine or spring greens , your choice
5. toss the salad with some crispies and dressing right before serving
6. works well to serve with tongs
7. add optional sliced green onions if you wish
demonstrations.review: This recipe is great!!!!

target.recipe_text:
lebanese lentil salad

the lemon and mint are the secret to giving these basic lentils their middle eastern flavor.

1. in saucepan , bring lentils and water to a boil , cook 30 minutes until tender , drain
2. add pepper , onion and mint
3. refrigerate at least 30 minutes or until ready to serve
4. just before serving , add oil , lemon juice , garlic and feta
5. toss and serve
target.review: I made this recipe to take to a softball club BBQ.  It was an outstanding success and voted best salad at the BBQ.  So would recommend it as an economical, easy to make and delicious dish with a colourful presentation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried savoy cabbage soup with mushrooms

my parents grow a lot of vegetables. although i live quite far away from them and neither of us has a car, i sometimes see my sister. last time i saw her she gave me a savoy cabbage from my parents. not being a big fan of cabbages, i was quite happy to find this curried cabbage soup in the new edition of the swiss cooking magazine called 'kochen' (november 2005). i love spices and i enjoy nearly every dish with curry powder or paste in it. i used a recently bought sri lankan curry powder, which - as i found out - happens to be very very hot. the second time i prepared this soup i used half a tablespoon of the sri lankan and half a tablespoon of a mild curry powder. this soup makes a lovely starter or a nice meal.

1. cut the savoy cabbage into wedges , core and shred it
2. chop the onion
3. remove leaves from the thyme sprigs
4. peel and cube potato
5. heat half of the butter in a high pan until butter melts
6. lower heat and add the shredded savoy cabbage and onion
7. cook for 3-4 minutes , stirring frequently
8. add curry powder and mix
9. add chopped potato , thyme leaves and stock
10. increase heat , add a lid and cook on low / medium heat for 25-30 minutes
11. slice the mushrooms and chop the parsley
12. blend the soup with a hand blender
13. add the cream
14. check if more water or curry is needed
15. season with salt and pepper if necessary
16. warm the soup , but don't heat it too much , as the cream may curl
17. heat the remaining butter in a skillet and fry the mushrooms
18. season with salt and pepper
19. add parsley when mushrooms are cooked
20. serve:
21. pour soup into bowls and top with mushrooms
demonstrations.review:
"Seriously good soup" is what hubby had to say when I made this for lunch today.  I used the left-over broth from a beef pot roast from the night before as a stock.  My variations were to add a stalk of celery chopped which along with the cabbage and onion, I cooked al dente in the microwave oven before adding to the broth.  I increased the potatoes to 2 large and added a potato sized piece of sweet potato (yam).  Instead of curry powder, I used a small jar of ready-made tikka marsala sauce. Instead of the 1/2 and 1/2 cream, I used low fat evaporated milk (Carnation) and chopped coriander in place of the parsley.
Excellent.  Next time I want to try it with low fat coconut milk as I think it would work well with this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean couscous salad

this is a delicious salad containing all four food groups ( if you use the red kidney beans)

1. cook couscous in 1 cup of water
2. cool to room temperature
3. whisk together lemon juice and olive oil
4. pour over other ingredients combining well
5. season with fresh pepper
demonstrations.review: An interesting salad.  I was looking for something to make using kidney beans and came across this salad.  I had never come across the combination of couscous and kidney beans before.  I followed the recipe except for omitting the pine nuts (didn't have any) and I used Danish Feta which has a softer texture and tastes not unlike a mild goats cheese.  It really was delicious and everyone commented on how good it tasted.  I will make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut slice

this can also be made as a chocolate coconut slice.  one for the lunchbox or with a nice cup of tea or coffee.  ice/frost with your favourite lemon icing for plain version or chocolate icing/frosting for the chocolate variation.

1. sift together the self raising flour and salt into a bowl
2. add the sugar , coconut , and melted butter
3. mix well
4. stir in the beaten eggs and milk
5. spread mixture into a slice tin and bake in a moderate oven 350'f / 180'c for 25-30 minutes
6. when cold ice / frost with either lemon or chocolate icing / frosting
7. sprinkle some extra coconut over top of icing / frosting if liked
8. cut into bars or squares
demonstrations.review: A nice moist slice, easy to make and I used the frozen chocolate icing I had left over from birthday cakes (reheated in the microwave), which made the whole thing even easier.  I think some walnuts in the mix would work well too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vidalia three bean salad with mustard dressing

this is our family's favorite bean salad. it is the sweet vadalia onion that makes it special. please feel free to use canned (home/store) beans in this recipe.

1. place vegetables in a serving dish
2. add dressing and toss
3. cover and refrigerate for several hours
demonstrations.review: Quite tasty.  I took Dave_in_CO's advice and cut back the olive oil to 1/3 cup, substituted lemon juice for the vinegar (but gave it a quick shot of vinegar too).  As we don't get vidalia onions where I come from, I used a french shallot instead.  I also substituted canned corn kernels for the yellow beans as we don't get them either.  Kidney beans are not a great favourite in our household, but this salad was well received.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lasagne a la courgette

the humble zucchini gets a lovely make-over in this beautiful lasagne. it is impressive enough to serve to guests, but easy enough to make for your family on a busy night, as it does not require you to pre-boil your lasagne noodles. i keep one in my freezer "just in case".
it makes a filling supper when coupled with a salad - the meat-eaters in your life won't even notice it's vegetarian!

1. pre-heat the oven to 350 degrees
2. prepare vegetables if you have not done so already
3. place them in a large bowl , salt them lightly and set aside
4. blend ricotta cheese , egg and all spices in a food processor or beat by hand until smooth
5. add cheese mixture to zucchini and blend to incorporate
6. add water and pasta sauce , stir to combine
7. add 1 cup of thinned sauce to the bottom of your lasagne pan , spreading it out to evenly coat the pan
8. now , begin layering uncooked lasagne noodles , then a third of the zucchini mixture , then another cup of sauce
9. repeat until you run out of noodles
10. cover the pan tightly with tin foil and bake for one hour
11. just before serving , sprinkle with shredded parmesan and return to the over to bake uncovered for an additional 15 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly
demonstrations.review: I made a few adjustments to the recipe in that I used fresh herbs which I pureed with the sweated zucchini, egg and ricotta cheese.  I also added a finely chopped shallot to this mix.  For the tomato sauce, I used half a jar of pasta sauce, a tin of tomato soup and the 1 cup of water.  After putting it all in the lasagna dish, I used freshly grated parmesan to top. The family thought it tasted good and it was easy enough to make.  I like the idea of using asparagus - might try that next time. If I were to make this recipe again, I would use 2 - 3 garlic cloves instead of the garlic powder.  I feel this would give it a bit more taste.

target.recipe_text:
a famous chicken salad sandwich

after enjoying an arby's sandwich i could not help but try to make one similar because it was that good. i think this is pretty close, but better because all the fruits are fresh.  

i don't really measure so, the measurements are guesses, and it's more of getting a desired consistency.  also use your own favorite type of bread.  i preferably use whole grain wheat.

1. drain chicken and put in bowl
2. add some mayo so that it does not have that dry appearance
3. next , start adding the apples , grapes , celery , and pecans
4. next , chop up the egg and add it to the salad
5. spread the salad on the bread with lettuce and tomato
6. enjoy !
target.review:
Loved it! Sweet & crunchy
I will make this again for sure. I used walnuts since that was what I had on hand and used leftover baked chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ex mother in law s pork chops with cream of mushroom

this was the one good memory i have of my first marriage- going to my ex-mother-in-law's and smelling this cooking! of course, i begged for her recipe and have been making it regularly ever since. her son was not a keeper for me, but her pork chops sure were! this recipe may be halved by using 4 pork chops, one can of soup, and two tablespoons of butter with the lawry's seasoning.

1. in skillet with melted butter , sprinkle both sides of pork chops with seasoned salt and seasoned pepper to taste and brown
2. put into 9 x 13 inch glass casserole and spoon mushroom soup and smear all over pork chops
3. cover and seal tightly with heavy aluminum foil and put into pre-heated 350 degree oven for 1 hour
4. remove foil last few minutes
5. serve over rice or noodles
6. yummmmm !
demonstrations.review: I made this dish last night and had a few people over everyone loved it. I did slice some potatoes and onion and put them under the pork chops and added a cup of milk. It really turned out well. Great recipe! Yummy!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked tilapia with veggies  herbs  and wine

delicious, fast, easy, and low-fat. what more could you want?

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. spray a baking dish and arrange filets in a single layer
3. overlap slightly if necessary
4. sprinkle with salt and paprika
5. set aside
6. in a small skillet , heat olive oil
7. quickly saute portabello , green onion and yellow pepper , about 2-3 minutes
8. add sherry and tarragon , and simmer 2-3 minutes more
9. if this mixture is very wet , simmer to reduce another minute or two
10. spoon contents of skillet over fish
11. bake@ 450f 20-30 minutes , depending on the thickness of your filets
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe for fish and chicken too. My sister cannot eat seafood so I made fish in one dish and chicken in another. The chicken was wonderful too. I did have to use regular mushrooms because I didn't have portabello on hand. Thanks for posting a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrot and raisin salad with pineapple

quick and easy

1. toss raisins , carrots , and pineapple together lightly
2. set aside
3. stir together mayonnaise , lemon juice , salt and sugar and add to the raisin mixture
4. refrigerate until served
demonstrations.review:
This is a very good recipe. I love carrot and raisan salad. I did add in some apple to give it a little more crunch. It was great with The copycat Chilis Ribs recipe #54234.
Thanks!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
camping burgers in foil

here's an old standby i use often. you can use other little goodies as well, such as mushrooms, real sliced onions, etc. if real potatoes are used, the cooking time will be longer.

1. separate meat into 4 patties
2. place each patty in the center of a square of foil
3. top with equal portions of sliced carrots , potatoes and peppers
4. season with dehydrated onions , worcestershire sauce , salt and pepper
5. seal foil
6. check for leaks
7. place on hot coals for 12 to 15 minutes
8. turn and cook an additional 10-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Have been making this for years! Everyone loves it. I use a few more spices like garlic and season-all. Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of chili s grilled baby back ribs by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com posted in response to a request. the recipe was given to me by miller, who is still with us in spirit. thanks miller!

1. make the barbecue sauce by combining all of the ingredients for the sauce in a medium saucepan over medium heat
2. when it comes to a boil , reduce heat and simmer sauce , stirring often , for 45 to 60 minutes or until sauce is thick
3. when you're ready to make the ribs , preheat the oven to 300 degrees
4. brush sauce over the entire surface of each rack of ribs
5. wrap each rack tightly in aluminum foil and arrange the packets on a baking sheet with the seam of the foil facing up
6. bake for 2 to 2 hours or until the meat on the ribs has pulled back from the cut ends of the bones by about inch
7. when the ribs are just about done , preheat your barbecue grill to medium heat
8. remove the ribs from the foil and grill them on the barbecue for 4 to 8 minutes per side or until the surface of the ribs is beginning to char
9. brush sauce on both sides of the ribs a few minutes before you remove them from the grill
10. just be sure not to brush on the sauce too soon or it could burn
11. serve the ribs with extra sauce on the side and lots of napkins
demonstrations.review: Oh My! This was wonderful. The meat just fell off the bone. The flavor of the sauce was excellent. I did add just a little more brown sugar because my family loves sweet BarBQ sauce. Make sure and have plenty of napkins on hand you will need them. This will be the way I make ribs from now on. My Family said this is a Keeper! Thanks!!!!

target.recipe_text:
chickpea curry  garbanzos

with a picture! a delicious, easy, stovetop vegetarian indian curry that makes a yummy lunch! based on a recipe i got from mrcurrys.com with a sample of their wonderful curry seasoning powder.

1. saute onions in olive oil for 3 minutes
2. add ginger , garlic and curry powder , stir and cook for another minute or so
3. add chickpeas and salt and a tablespoon or so of water
4. cook and stir about a minute
5. add tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes , stirring gently
6. add another spoonful of water if it seems dry or if it's burning or sticking
7. serve with flatbread and rice
target.review: I ended up using this as a base recipe for my final result; had other items in the fridge I wanted to use up, plus wanted to have leftovers for lunches later in the week.  So I added a diced zucchini, some pre-cooked grilled chicken chunks, a few mushrooms, and some chili paste for some extra heat. Then I included a can of coconut milk because we like plenty of sauce to soak up the rice. I forgot the garlic, so would definitely add it next time, but the result was still good. It just needed a little more salt, no big deal really.  My husband and I both thought this was yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jambalaya for the crock pot

try this for your next crock pot adventure. wonderful flavor!

1. cut chicken into 1 inch pieces
2. put all ingredients in crock pot
3. cover
4. cook on low for 8 hours
5. add shrimp the last 20 minutes of cooking
6. stir in rice before serving
demonstrations.review:
I finally realized after the umpteenth time of trying to cook chicken breasts in a crock pot that it just doesn't work well. It always dries out and has the same funny taste, no matter what other ingredients I use. And I've tried a LOT of different liquid/spices combos.

However, where this recipe is concerned, I substituted turkey sausage for the shimp (DH isn't a huge shrimp fan), and I really loved that part of it. I would make this again, and next time substitute the sausage for the CHICKEN, and keep the shrimp. That would be absolutely great. I liked everything else about this, other than the icky dried-out chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of mcdonald s shamrock shake by todd wilbur

recipe adapted from todd wilbur's version of mcdonald's shamrock shake www.topsecretrecipes.com. i used to absolutely love it when mcdonald's brought out their shamrock shakes around st. patrick's day. the past couple of years i haven't been able to have it because of the dairy, so i was thrilled when i found this copycat recipe! just use the soy ingredients to make it dairy-free.

1. combine all ingredients in a blender and blend on high speed until smooth
2. stop blender to stir with a spoon if necessary to help blend ice cream
3. pour into 12-ounce cups and serve each with a straw
4. happy st patrick's day !
demonstrations.review: I LOVE shamrock shakes, and spend every March periodically reminding myself to drive to McDonalds and get one, but then forgetting after the fact.  I was so excited to see this recipe - it's super easy to make, it tastes just like the "real" thing, and for a fraction of the price!  Since I always have 3 of the ingredients on hand, the only thing I had to buy was a bottle of peppermint extract for $4, and now I can make them for myself ANY time of the year.  What's not to love?  (My husband loves it too...he devoured his just now. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cheesy ham and pasta

this is based off of my creamy bacon & leek pasta.  it's adapted for my husband and son who both prefer more simple meals.  i love it because it takes less than 30 minutes to make and it pairs very nicely (as most pasta dishes do) with a salad and some bread.  i hope you enjoy!

1. bring a pot full of water to a boil
2. meanwhile add butter to skillet and melt
3. once melted , add onion , garlic and ham
4. saut until onion is soft or ham is slightly browned
5. once water starts to vigorously boil , add pasta
6. meanwhile add flour to mixture one tablespoon at a time stirring constantly
7. add in milk 1 / 2 cup at a time
8. once sauce consistency is a little runnier than you like , add cheese and salt
9. reduce heat to simmer while you drain pasta
10. mix drained pasta together with sauce and serve with salad and bread for a complete quick meal !
11. this meal is very versatile and you can change the quantities of the pasta or type of pasta to suite your own family's needs
demonstrations.review: Very good!  I used sour cream and 1% milk because that's what I had...also added some shredded monterey jack cheese, and didn't need to add salt because the other things gave it enough flavor.  DH definitely gave it two thumbs up, and it will make great leftovers for his lunch.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot  super garlic chicken legs

i love garlic, and i love chicken cooked in the crock pot (so tender it falls right off of the bones), so this is a perfect combo of the two.  i have some cooking in the crock pot right now, and i am longing for it to be done! :-) i never measure the spices, so these are estimates - please feel free to experiment.  it is cooked with loads of garlic, so loving garlic is a plus!

1. place garlic cloves in crock pot
2. mix spices together in med bowl
3. pour oil into separate med bowl
4. dip chicken legs in oil , then roll around in spice bowl , until chicken is nicely coated in spices
5. place chicken legs in crock pot with garlic cloves surrounding it
6. pour chicken broth over all ingredients
7. cook on low for 8 hours
demonstrations.review: I placed the chicken legs in a large ziplock with olive oil and minced garlic and gave them a nice coating, then sprinkled the spices on and added the broth. (Added a bit of basil as well.) I cooked it 4  hours on high, then broiled the chicken a few minutes on each side and it was perfect.  The aroma it created while cooking was amazing. This is the only way I'll cook chicken in a crock pot from now on - it seems like every other time my chicken comes out dry with a weird aftertaste.  I also made gravy out of the leftover juices to go over red mashed potatoes, which was great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tex mex fusilli

this is a family favourite that comes from an old milk calandar. even dh, who doesn't like anything tex-mex raves about this one. i always make it with the ham, but the if you have left over chicken, i bet it would be just as good.

1. cook pasta according to package directions
2. meanwhile , in a medium sauce pan , melt butter over medium heat
3. stir in flour until blended
4. gradually whisk in milk and salt , making sure there are no lumps
5. stir and bring to a boil
6. reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 1 minute
7. reduce heat to low , add cheese a handful at a time , stirring until melted
8. stir in chicken or ham , corn , green onions and salsa
9. heat through
10. to serve , drain pasta
11. turn into a large bowl
12. toss sauce with pasta and sprinkle with additional grated cheddar cheese , if desired
demonstrations.review: This was the perfect way to use leftover diced ham.  I had already exhausted the other possible dinner options, so decided to give this a try.  And so glad I did.  My hubby and I agreed that it was missing a little something (but not enough to keep us from looking forward to the leftovers).  Maybe something to give it a little more "kick" (and we did use medium salsa to begin with)...maybe more salsa, or cheese, some hot sauce or red pepper flakes?  Any (or even all) of the above would probably put it right at the perfect-o mark.  Also, I was a little worried about the green onions, but they were a great addition. Love this recipe!

target.recipe_text:
simple caribbean jerk chicken

i like jerk chicken but often don't have all the exotic ingredients. this simplifies the mix by using dry italian dressing. yummy on the grill!

1. mix all ingredients except chicken in bowl
2. pour over chicken
3. cover and marinate 1 hour or over night in fridge
4. grill it !
5. enjoy !
target.review: This recipe is great! I only put half of the crushed red pepper in, thought it might be to spicy for us. We have made this twice now and it gets rave reviews each time. We will be making this again real soon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breasts with spicy honey orange glaze

nan

1. in small bowl , combine honey with juice concentrate , orange zest , garlic , salt and red pepper flakes
2. rinse chicken with cold water and pat dry
3. season lightly with salt
4. in large non-stick skillet , heat margarine and oil over medium-high heat
5. add chicken and cook about 4 minutes , until seared
6. turn chicken , cook another 4 minutes until just cooked through
7. pour honey mixture over chicken and cook , turning chicken to coat as sauce begins to thicken , about 2 min
8. serve chicken breasts with honey-orange glaze spooned over the top
demonstrations.review:
This is really good and easy to make. I did make some changes, I used garlic powder since I didn't have minced. Used less of the red pepper flakes. We don't like things real spicy hot. Next time I will double the sauce and cut the chicken up in small pieces.
Thanks for sharing such a good and easy recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizza hut cavatini copycat

i got this from copykat.com. pizza hut cavatini copykat

1. cook noodles according to box directions
2. heat sauce & combine with cooked hamburger and cooked sausage
3. in a 11 x 13 pan , sprayed with pam cooking spray , layer noodles and sauce
4. top layer with pepperoni , onions and green peppers , mushrooms and cheeses
5. make about 3 layers and top with cheese
6. bake at 350 degrees for about 45 minutes or until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: We really like this recipe. I have been making it for a few years now. Because of DH I leave out the green peppers. I also got this recipe from CopyKat. It's a keeper in our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marion s michigan sauce for hot dogs

recipes for this northern new york specialty are closely guarded like barbecue down south.  try this with chopped onions on your hot dogs for a new taste treat.

1. finely chop onions and saute in a little olive oil until tender
2. add ground beef and cook until browned
3. separate meat so it is broken into very fine pieces of meat
4. add rest of ingredients , mix , and cook over low heat on the stove 1 hour or more
5. this could be cooked in a crockpot on low for six hours
6. serve as a topping on hot dogs
demonstrations.review:
This is great when you want to add something to hotdogs. It is so easy to make which makes it even better. We will be making this one a lot.
Thanks so much for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest beef enchiladas ever

best enchilada recipe i've found. we love the spicy, cheesy flavor of these.

1. brown meat and onions in large skillet
2. add 1 cup enchilada sauce and 1 cup cheese
3. mix well
4. put filling along center of each tortilla
5. roll up and place seam side down in a 9x13 pan
6. pour remaining sauce over
7. sprinkle remaining cheese over
8. bake at 350f degrees for about 30 minutes till cheese is bubbly
demonstrations.review: I was not pleased with the taste and was surprised because of all of the rave reviews. It was very pland for our taste. Very easy to make. I might try again and add something like taco seasoning for added flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review:
These were very good. Next time I will try fixing, on just the stove as others has suggested. We do not eat pork that often. With this recipe we will be having it more often.
Thanks for the recipe.
Beth

target.recipe_text:
roasted pork tenderloin with garlic mushrooms and tomatoes

this is best with the summer tomatoes.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. rub pork on all sides with salt and pepper
3. place pork on one side of a large roasting pan
4. in a large bowl combine mushrooms , tomatoes , oil , garlic , and salt and pepper to taste
5. mix gently
6. spoon vegetables into pan with pork , spreading in an even layer
7. roast until meat thermometer inserted in the middle of the pork registers 160 degrees f
8. cut pork into thin slices
9. top with garlic mushrooms and tomatoes
target.review: I made this to the recipe but I found the mushrooms and tomato mixture to be really "wet" and the pork to be a little bland.  I guess I just like spicier food!  Glad I tried it though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best pork tenderloin

this is the best tenderloin i've ever had. it's a friends recipe and i love how simple it is! great for those summer months when it's too hot to turn on the oven. cook time does not include marinade time.

1. combine soy sauce , lime juice , oil , garlic and red pepper flakes in a 13" x 9" pan or ziplock bag to make marinade
2. add the tenderloin and marinate for at least 4 hours , or overnight
3. grill on bbq over low heat , turning regularly and basting with marianade until internal temperature reaches 160
4. it should be crusty on the outside and tender on the inside - delicious !
demonstrations.review: I liked the flavour of this marinade.  I cooked it with pork loin steaks on the george foreman grill, so it was a little drier than I would have liked but the taste was very nice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tiger prawns in garlic butter

these are incredable!! you will never have enough and everyone will want the recipe!! make lots for a full meal or serve as a first course. from mexican, healthy ways with a favourite cusine.

1. rinse the prawns in a colander , remove their heads and leave them to drain
2. heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan , add the garlic and fry over a low heat for 2 to 3 minutes
3. add the lime rind and juice
4. cook , stirring constantly , for 1 minute more
5. add the prawns and cook them for 2 to 3 minutes until they turn pink
6. remove them from the heat , sprinkle with coriander and serve with the warm tortillas
7. give each guest a finger bowl filled with water and a slice of lemon , for cleaning their fingers after shelling the prawns , and provide lots of paper napkins !
demonstrations.review: Made these for a dinner with friends last night and they were gobbled up in entirety.  Cooked up in a flash and as you say...there were not enough!  Thanks for the "simply" delicious recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scalloped potatoes with herbed cheese

i clipped this recipe from our local newspaper quite some time ago and i have been making it ever since. it goes great with baked ham but try it with any other meat that strikes your fancy.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. butter 9-inch casserole dish
3. in medium saucepan , melt butter
4. whisk in flour
5. cook 2 or 3 minutes at medium heat without browning , stirring constantly
6. gradually whisk in milk
7. bring to a boil
8. reduce heat
9. simmer gently 5 minutes
10. add cream cheese , swiss cheese , salt , pepper and nutmeg
11. stir until cheese melts
12. layer potatoes and butter sauce alternately in buttered dish , ending with sauce
13. sprinkle with parmesan
14. bake 1 hour and 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender
15. let stand 5 to 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I prepared these for an Easter dinner I was attending (and sacrificed a piece of my finger slicing the potatoes on a mandolin!)and really liked the look of the recipe.  However, I was surprised to find the taste pretty bland for my taste.  I also added a thinly sliced onion with the layers of sauce and potatoes and even that didn't add much zip.  Thanks for posting, however.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red bell pepper pork boulettes  meatballs

the original recipe came from my dd's culinary school education packet, however she reworked it to her taste. she served it at home with a creamy sauce served on a bed of homemade pasta. our family loved them plain right out of the refrigerator. the recipe makes 24 one inch balls, but you may want to double it and freeze the extras.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. sweat onions , bell pepper , green onions and garlic until tender in 2 tbsp of butter
3. remove from heat and allow to cool
4. once cool combine vegetable mixture , ground pork , egg , bread crumbs , and salt / pepper
5. mix until well incorporated
6. cook a test patty to see if seasoning needs to be adjusted
7. form meatballs to desired size about 1"
8. dredge meatballs in flour and shake off any excess
9. heat pan with oil over medium high heat and place a meatball in , if it does not sear or if it burns adjust your heat
10. once the pan is ready brown your meatballs and place on a baking sheet and pop them in the oven
11. cook until they reach an internal temperature of 165 degrees or when you cut one in half and there is no visible sign of pink
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: My 7 yr old and I really enjoyed these.  I did make a few changes.  Left out the green onion and did not dredge the balls in flour.  Fried in a non-stick pan rather than roasting.  Very nice texture and flavour- not too strong.  Great paired with a green salad and sheila's best balsamic drsg from the site.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian banana chai bread

never tasted it, don't know what it's like, but sounds interesting. not as nice as the easiest (non-machine) white bread in the world. i've tasted that, its gorgeous, as is the chef.

1. in a medium bowl mix together flour , baking powder , and salt
2. in a separate bowl mix sugar , cream cheese , and eggs until light and fluffy
3. mix mashed bananas and chai into cream cheese mixture
4. add flour mixture and mix until smooth
5. pour mixture into a greased 9x5 inch loaf pan
6. bake in a preheated 350 degree f oven for 60 minutes
7. cool on rack
8. remove from pan after 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Hi.  I haven't made this yet, either, but I have often wondered what happened between you two!  I stumbled across Scar's review of your bread and thought it was a fearless ( and slightly nutty) thing to do.  So glad it worked out for you!  Keep us posted!

target.recipe_text:
chocolate  chocolate  chocolate  bundt cake with chocolate glaze

need i say more...chocolate! decadently rich and moist. add a scoop of vanilla ice cream and you're in heaven.

1. cake: preheat oven to 350
2. grease and flour bundt pan , set aside
3. in large mixing bowl , combine cake mix , pudding mix and chocolate chips
4. in another bowl , combine water , eggs , and vanilla mixing well
5. add egg mixture to dry mixture and mix with spoon until just blended
6. pour into prepared pan
7. bake for 50 to 55 minutes or until cake tests done when wooden pick in center comes out clean
8. cool 15 to 20 minutes before removing cake from pan
9. when completely cool , drizzle cake with chocolate glaze
10. chocolate glaze: combine all ingredients in bowl
11. mix with spoon until smooth
target.review: I saw the recipe and my daughter made it for me (13yrs) and it was fantastic!!! Moist, and lots of chocolate flavor, really rich, a smaller piece goes a long ways and I would definately serve it with ice cream or whipped topping to cut the richness a little. Also, I love the darker flavor but at the famiy's request would be using milk chocolate cocoa next time. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek tzatziki sauce

this is a delicious sauce that can be used in many greek recipes.  we like to use it when making gyros, or other mediterranean recipes that are wrapped in pitas. it tastes just like the sauce we've had in restaurants such as "hell's" in tarpon springs in florida.  it's a funny name, but the restaurant is known for having some of the best greek food and greek pastries in florida.

1. place yogurt in a coffee filter or piece of cheesecloth , and place in a strainer over a dish
2. let drain for 2-4 hours in the refrigerator
3. if using greek yogurt you do not need to drain it , as it is already a thick consistency
4. meanwhile , put the chopped or grated cucumber in a tea towel and squeeze to remove liquid
5. discard liquid
6. sprinkle with 1 teaspoon salt and mix into the cucumber
7. set aside 20 minutes
8. rinse a little to wash out the extra salt , if you want to
9. then squeeze again to express as much liquid as possible
10. draining the yogurt and cucumber make for a thick and authentic consistency of tzatziki sauce
11. combine the drained yogurt and cucumber , sour cream , pinch of salt , olive oil , red wine vinegar , mint and garlic
12. it made for an overpowering and almost bitter taste , so now i stick to only 1 clove
13. place sauce in the refrigerator for 1 hour or more to meld flavors
14. stir before serving
15. the sauce can be stored in the refrigerator for up to one week
16. makes 1 1 / 4 cups
demonstrations.review: yummmm..just made this and my picky son (who never eats anything easily) LOVED this..could have used it as a side salad..Anyway, most Kroger's carry the greek yogurt and wasn't sure about the olive oil? So didn't use all of it. Turned out fabulous. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cocoa mix  extra large batch

i like this cocoa for many reasons, only one of which is because it has a delightfully creamy texture. it makes an extra-large batch of cocoa mix, great for gift-giving or large groups. running the powdered milk through the blender powders it, decreasing the odds that it will float to the top of the mix. the number of servings are approximate, as it will depend on how much mix you use per serving. i estimated at 2-tablespoons per serving. adjust for personal taste.

1. mix all ingredients in a large bowl and blend with a whisk
2. store in airtight container
3. combine , to taste , with hot water or milk
demonstrations.review: Made this for christmas gifts..everyone loved it. I did change a couple of things. I used 1/2 Vanilla pudding and 1/2 milk chocolate pudding and also used chocolate flavored coffee creamer. Doubled it once..and then had to make another double batch. Sent some over to a friend in IRAQ and he shared it with his buddies..he got one cup and went back and there was no more left. I guess I'll be sending more that way. :) The kids loved it and the one comment I keep hearing back over and over is how creamy it is. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
killer baked beans

it is a recipe i came up with by playing around and everyone loves them. i have them when i have barbecues or with a catfish or chicken fry!!! as far as taste it all blends in and is just awesome.

1. mix pork and beans , brown sugar , onion , worcestershire sauce , mustard , barbecue sauce , and liquid smoke together in baking pan
2. place bacon on top
3. bake at 350 degrees fahrenheit for an hour or so !
4. yummmmm !
5. hope you enjoy
6. we have people over for barbecues and they are gone in no time
7. can never seem to make enough !
demonstrations.review: Yummy. Made these for a family reunion where about half are vegetarian of some sort or another..so I made them using Bush's Veg. Baked Beans as a base, I used ground turkey browned instead of bacon. Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce, Walla Walla Onions for a bit of natural sweet and flavor. I made too much this recipe feeds way more than 5 so be careful. I was feeding 25 and only doubled the stuff and we ate beans for 3 days. Comments I heard, I don't like beans and I can't stop eating these!! OMG these are the best beans I ever had they are really really good, Wow, can I have the recipe?? Will make these again and again..thanks for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
30 minute chicken noodle soup  from foodtv  rachael ray

from show of 5/16/02.

1. place a large pot over moderate heat and add extra-virgin olive oil
2. work close to the stove and add vegetables to the pot as you chop , in the order they are listed
3. add bay leaves and season vegetables with salt and pepper , to taste
4. add stock to the pot and raise flame to bring liquid to a boil
5. add diced chicken tenderloins , return soup to a boil , and reduce heat back to moderate
6. cook chicken 2 minutes and add noodles
7. cook soup an additional 6 minutes or until noodles are tender and remove soup from the heat
8. stir in parsley and dill , remove bay leaves and serve
9. this is a thick soup
10. add up to 2 cups of water if you like chicken soup with lots of broth
demonstrations.review: This was Fantastic! Only subs were I used the squeeze tube of dill and basil. It was fast and easy and everyone wanted refills:-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
puffy french toast

my dh did not like french toast until i found this recipe in an old book. now he loves it. it works best with day old bread.

1. stir dry ingredients in a medium sized mixing bowl
2. in another bowl , blend milk and egg
3. add milk and egg mixture gradually to dry mixture
4. beat until smooth
5. dip bread slices in batter
6. turn to coat both sides evenly
7. fry in greased skillet until golden brown on both sides
8. serve with syrup if desired
demonstrations.review: We loved it, it was kind of like a cross between pancakes and french toast. Yum. We are just making again for the second time. Thanks for the post.

target.recipe_text:
gluten free oreo cookies

what's your favorite way to eat an oreo cookie? some of us celiac's may have forgotten our favourite way ... or tried really hard to forget oreo cookies even exsisted. well forget no more, you will never have another craving for an oreo cookie. these taste exactly like the real wheat containing oreo cookie. split these cookies apart and lick the frosting from each side, or dip them in milk, they are so similar! slip these cookies into your children's lunches for a real treat.  they won't feel different from the other kids eating these, infact the other children will definetly be envious of them for once! note: if you have a cookie stamp, press onto sliced cookies before baking to give a more authentic look to the cookies.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a medium bowl , whisk together the flour mix , xanthan gum , egg replacer , cocoa , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
3. set aside
4. in the bowl of the mixer , cream the margarine and sugar until light
5. add the egg and vanilla and beat well
6. add the dry ingredients in 3 additions
7. if the dough becomes too stiff , add the milk as needed
8. shape the dough into two 10"x1-1 / 2" rolls
9. wrap in foil and chill
10. chill for about 15-20 minutes
11. cut into 1 / 8" slices , if you have a cookie stamp , you can at this point press in onto the sliced cookies before baking
12. bake these cookies on an ungreased cookie sheet for 10 minutes
13. let cool for only a few minutes before removing from the cookie sheet
14. cool thoroughly on a rack
15. for the filling , combine confectioners' sugar , shortening , vanilla and hot water
target.review: First try was a great success. I brought them to my sister's house for treats for the kids. They were enjoyed by all and only one celiac among us! Outstanding dough - so easy to handle. I started slicing the roll of dough as suggested, but found myself reshaping the dough. I decided to make walnut size balls and flatten them with my hand. Worked out great! If you prefer a chewier cookie, cook 1 minute less. The icing was right on the money! Tastes just like the real thing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free cornmeal muffins

this is my adaptation of the recipe on the package of the brand of cornmeal i use.  a family favorite that disappears quickly!

1. combine cornmeal and milk in a microwave safe bowl
2. microwave on high for one minute , and let stand
3. preheat oven to 400f line muffin tin with paper baking cups , and spray with oil or non-stick spray
4. combine remaining dry ingredients in a separate bowl
5. add egg and oil to cornmeal mixture
6. add cornmeal mixture to dry ingredients , and stir with a fork until blended
7. do not over mix
8. fill cups 2 / 3 full , and bake for 20 - 25 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very easy to prepare.  I tested at 20 minutes and tester came out dry.  Muffins were tasty, texture a bit chewy.  Will make again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weekend baked hash browns

are you looking for a great thanksgiving or christmas morning meal? this awesome-tasting one-dish breakfast can be made in advance and refrigerated until needed. it uses simply potatoes® brand hash browns. they are refrigerated, not frozen, and come in a green bag.

1. cut bacon into 1 / 2" pieces
2. fry in large skillet until crisp
3. remove and drain on absorbent paper
4. discard all but a very small amount of bacon fat from skillet
5. add vegetable oil to lightly cover bottom of skillet
6. heat to medium-high
7. add hash browns and fry until brown
8. remove hash browns from skillet , spreading them into a 9x13 baking dish that has been lightly sprayed with no-stick cooking spray
9. spread half the bacon and half the cheese over the hash browns
10. beat eggs , milk , onions , salt , pepper , and hot pepper sauce together then pour over the hash browns , bacon , and cheese
11. press the bacon and cheese evenly down into the hash browns and egg mixture with the edge of a spoon or clean finger
12. bake at 450 for 8 minutes
13. reduce oven temperature to 350 and continue baking for an additional 12-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this for a quick dinner one nite - It came together quickly and easiy. I served it with a green salad to get some veggies in.  I found it a bit dry and may add a bit of milk next time. The kids loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free dutch sugar cookies

these cookies are very yummy. they are crisp on the outside and alittle soft on the inside. they remind me of those wheat containing animal crackers, that i used to eat as a kid(before i was diagnosed with celiac disease.)these cookies are very yummy and lots of fun to make and decorate.i like making them with coloured sugar or shaking alittle powdered sugar on them.they also keep very well in a sealed  container.last year i made them to take up to my cottage on our week of holidays. everyone loved them, and couldn't believe that they were gluten free!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. have on hand 2 ungreased cookie sheets
3. in a small bowl , whish together the flour mix , baking powder , xanthan gum , and salt
4. set aside
5. in the bowl of your mixer , cream sugar and crisco
6. beat in the egg and vanilla
7. add the dry ingredients , mixing enough to combine
8. the dough will be a soft ball
9. with your hands , knead in enough of the potato starch to make the dough easy to handle and roll out
10. using about half at a time , place a piece of plastic wrap over the ball and roll out to about 1 / 8 inch thickness
11. cut into desired shapes and place on pan
12. decorate with coloured sugars before baking or use frosting to decorate after baking
13. just scrape them together and roll out again
14. they will not get tough
15. bake for about 13 minutes
16. cool very slightly before removing from the pan
demonstrations.review: I found this recipe in one of B. Hagman's cookbooks and made them for Christmas. They were very good. Crisp on outside with a nice chewy center. The kids enjoyed decorating them. The dough was incredibly easy to work with. My 6 year old was rolling it out and cutting cookies! Great family recipe and activity.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free awesome chocolate chip cookies

gluten free? you might not think so because these even fooled my husband! chewy, crunchy or how ever you like them - these are a real treat.

1. by hand blend margarine , sugars , egg , & vanilla until creamy
2. in a separate bowl blend flours , baking soda salt
3. combine both bowls and mix well
4. add chocolate chips and mix
5. roll into balls
6. bake at 375 for 12-15 minutes on a lighty greased preheated cookie sheet
demonstrations.review: Wow!!! I made these with BH featherlite flour mix.  They were unbelievable!  We took them to a Christmas party and they were gone in a flash.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon ricotta almond cake   gluten free

this is a beautifully rich gluten-free cake that unlike many gf cakes will stay moist for days. it's based on a cake from the blog lucullian delights. the delicate tastes of almond and lemon compliment each other in a really wonderful way. this would taste great with fresh fruit. i prefer the almond meal/flour from bob's red mill, which can be bought at most health food stores or online. make sure the gluten-free flour mix you use contains xanthan or guar gum! pamela's works best.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. whisk eggs and sugar
3. add almond meal and butter , and stir well
4. pulse ricotta in blender or mash by hand , and then add to batter
5. stir thoroughly to combine before folding in pamela's baking and pancake mix
6. lastly , add the lemon zest , lemon juice and lemon extract and mix the batter to blend
7. grease 8" round cake pan
8. pour batter into the cake pan , and bake for 30 minutes
9. cool for 10 minutes before slicing and serving warm
10. dust with powdered sugar and / or garnish with fruit
demonstrations.review: This was delicious and very easy. My entire family enjoyed it. It is a great lunchbox treat. I changed the recipe just a bit to tone down the lemon taste. (I love the lemon, but my celiac kid does not.) I added almond extract instead of the lemon extract. Keeper! 10.5" round 22 mins.

target.recipe_text:
caramelized baked chicken legs wings

delicious! yummy  caramelized legs, kids love these! so quick and easy and no marinating required. just prepare the sauce, pour over the chicken and pop in the oven!  i actually like this with wings better ;-)
 

very important to leave it in the oven until it has caramelized to avoid disappointment. 

thank you to everyone for their positive reviews!

try adding sambal oelek as chef  #27416 has suggested in his review. what a great idea ;-)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit or 180 degrees celsius
2. place chicken in a 9x13 inch baking dish
3. mix together the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper
4. pour over the chicken
5. bake in preheated oven for one hour , or until sauce is caramelized
6. could also use wings or pork ribs
target.review: YUM!!!!  super easy, and the house smelled soooo good while it was cooking!  i made it with mac and cheese and lima beans, but TRUST me next time...rice or mashed potatoes to put the sauce on...VERY GOOD

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest tastiest barbecue country style ribs  slow cooker

i threw this together one morning before going out for the day. it was super easy because only three ingredients are needed! not only did the house smell heavenly when we came home, but dinner was ready and it was awesome!

1. place all ingredients in crock pot
2. cook on low for 6 to 8 hours
3. meat starts to fall off the bones-- be careful of the small ones in the juices !
demonstrations.review: Super tender ribs!  The meat fell apart, and had great flavor.  We prefer ribs on the grill, but we dont always have time.  This hit the spot when I was short on time because of work and sports, and and was craving ribs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jolean s italian sausage casserole

my mom used to make this for us, after she was just a little too old to stand in the kitchen for too long...it was one of her favorites that was easy to make, yet tasted like good old-fashioned comfort food...sure do miss my mom!!!

1. in a 2 quart , ungreased casserole dish , layer twice: 1 / 2 cooked macaroni , 1 / 2 cooked sausage , then 1 / 2 sauce , 1 / 2 mushrooms , 1 / 2 shredded cheese
2. do the same layering again
3. sprinkle romano cheese on top
4. bake in a preheated 350 degree oven for 30-40 minutes , until cheese is slightly browned and casserole is bubbly
demonstrations.review: This was so good and easy to make!  I will definitely be making this again..thanks for a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamed chipped dried beef on toast or waffles

i've had this recipe for years given to me by my mother. i have to at least triple this when i make it. the recipe says 4 servings, but we like a lot on our toast. we love it for breakfast with fried eggs. yummy! i also add ground black pepper to mine, but that's just how i like it. cook and prep times are approximate.

1. put shredded beef in pan , sprinkle with flour , add butter , and slightly brown
2. add milk and stir until thick
3. serve on toast or waffles
demonstrations.review: OH YUM!  My mother used to make this for me, I love it....thanks for submitting this, now I make it.  Truely comfort food for me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli cheese salad

nan

1. place all salad ingredients in bowl
2. mix dressing ingredients until smooth and pour over salad
3. chill
demonstrations.review: I have been making this salad for years!  It is always a hit at potlucks....I use half broccoli and half cauliflower to give it a nice color.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tasty collard greens

would be equally as good with turnip or mustard greens or even kale.  *i do the cooking of the smoked turkey leg a day ahead, refrigerate and then skin the congealed fat off the top of the broth.  this is our favorite method of cooking greens.

1. heat oil in a large pot over medium heat
2. saute garlic until light brown
3. add turkey leg and chicken broth , cover and simmer until turkey leg is tender
4. remove turkey leg and cool slightly so comfortable to remove and chop meat and return turkey meat to pot
5. add collard greens and turn heat up to medium-high and let the greens cook down for about 45 minutes , stirring occasionally
6. reduce the heat and season with salt , pepper and red pepper flakes
7. continue to cook until greens are tender - about 45 to 60 minutes
8. drain greens and reserve liquid to reheat leftovers
9. i often freeze some of the liquid and use with frozen greens at another time
demonstrations.review: These were SOOO good!  The only difference is that I used 10 cups chicken stock, 2 smoked turkey legs and I chopped up onion to brown with the garlic.  I also added some hot sauce and put a bay leaf in it as well.  I don't drain the liquid, I like to drink it.  The "pot liquer" is GREAT to sip out of a mug on a cold day and is so healthy full of vitamins.

target.recipe_text:
beef  cheese  and noodle bake

from cooking light, february 2006. yummy, filling casserole.

1. preheat over to 350
2. cook pasta , drain and set aside
3. saute onion , carrot , and garlic for about 3 minutes
4. add ground beef and brown breaking up the meat
5. add tomato sauce , 1 / 2 tsp salt , and pepper
6. continue to cook for about 2 minutes
7. add macaroni
8. put mixture into a 11 x 7 baking dish that has been sprayed with cooking spray
9. heat milk , flour , remaining 1 / 2 tsp salt , and nutmeg over medium heat whisking constantly for about 2 minutes , until smooth and thickening
10. stir in 1 cup of grated cheese until smooth
11. pour cheese mixture over pasta and stir in to blend
12. spread remaining cheese over the top
13. bake for 20 minutes or until cheese is starting to brown
14. let sit for about 5 minutes before serving
target.review:
Great recipe,thanks for posting it!

I was trying to come up with something different to do with ground sirloin.We were all getting tired of the usual things to use it for chili,tacos,spaghetti sauce,burgers etc.It was very cold here today and this was warm, filling comfort food.I really loved the fact that it was low in calories per serving.(I didn't tell my husband or little one that though;)I left out the carrots because as one other reviewer said,I have a couple of hawk eyes here.LOL! I only used 1/4 tsp of pepper(I figured we could add more when serving)and it was perfect.My daughter gobbled hers up without a complaint and believe me thats 5 stars right there because she's VERY fussy!Thanks again for this recipe I will definitely make it again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chick   egg krispies nest easter treats

i make these little treats for my son to take to school.  it's a perfect, cute little easter treat.  i serve them in the individual over-sized cupcake papers.  you could use plain rice krispies and/or omit the chick.....still just as cute.  prep time does not include cooling and setting time.

1. lightly spray 2 cupcake / muffin tins w / nonstick cooking spray
2. in a large saucepan , over low heat , melt margarine
3. add marshmallows , and stir frequently over the low heat until melted and mixed well with melted margarine
4. remove from heat
5. stir in rice krispies and mix to coat well
6. immediately spoon into muffin / cupcake tins to almost full , but not packed down
7. with greased or wax-paper-covered thumb , or greased shot glass , press down on center of the krispies treats to form nest shape
8. allow to cool and set completely---about 20 minutes
9. remove to extra-large foil muffin / cupcake liners
10. place 2 or 3 egg-shaped candies in each nest
11. separate the marshmallow peep chicks and gently press a chick on top of each nest
demonstrations.review: So cute what a brillant idea! We made these for my 3 year old daughters playgroup as a easter treat for snack time.The teachers were really impressed and the kids loved them. Thanks for posting a great recipe Parsley!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the clockmaker s caramel coated popcorn  a haunted recipe

in 1921, a german born clockmaker quit his well respected job to open a popcorn stand in chicago’s wicker park district. the clockmaker’s typical fare was freshly popped popcorn drizzled with warm butter and sprinkled with salt; but his favorite, and most beloved popcorn, was his caramel coated popcorn. the recipe he used to make it was given to him from his only true love, who tragically died four years earlier during world war i. the tattered and torn recipe, which was scribbled on the inside of an old playbill, was carefully framed and sealed in an exquisite frame. the clockmaker faithfully took the framed recipe with him everywhere he went.  

by the summer of 1924, the clockmaker’s caramel coated popcorn had captivated the entire city’s attention; everyone was frantically lining up at his busy stand to buy the sweet, sticky confection. a few months later, just as the clockmaker was preparing to close his stand for the day, a small fire ignited near the stove. the clockmaker instinctively ran out to call for help. when he returned, just seconds later, he remembered leaving the framed recipe hanging on the wall. the clockmaker quickly ran into the burning stand to retrieve the recipe, but he never made it out.

when the fire inspectors went into the charred ruins to investigate the accident, they found the clockmaker’s frame lying in a pile of smoking debris. the frame was in pristine condition; not a dent, nor a blemish, could be seen on it. however, the recipe was gone.  

the recipe for the clockmaker’s caramel popcorn recently surfaced and is beginning to circulate around the globe. unfortunately, many people think the recipe is haunted because it is believed that if your clock stops running after making the recipe it’s because the clockmaker has paid you a visit in hopes of reclaiming his long, lost recipe.

note:  this recipe, as written, results in a sticky, chewy caramel popcorn.  if you prefer a crunchier caramel popcorn, bake it in the oven at 250 degrees for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.

1. in a large pot , heat the margarine , brown sugar , karo syrup , and salt together over medium heat
2. while stirring , bring mixture to a boil and allow to boil for five minutes
3. remove from heat
4. add baking soda and vanilla
5. mix well
6. pour over freshly popped popcorn
7. stir until the popcorn is well coated
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Great recipe and fun story to go with it ;)I used butter in place of margarine and baked in oven on two greased cookie sheets for the full hour stirring and breaking up every 15 min as directed. Delicious, tastes like crunch n munch popcorn which I love. Next time I'll add some cashews or salted peanuts for extra yumminess!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
avocado smoothie

ok...here in the us avocados are used in savory salads...but in brazil we eat them sweet.  this is known as "creme de abacate", when blended with sugar and milk this comes out to be a creamy goodness, trust me!  before making this make sure you chill the entire avocado so it is nice and cold.

1. put everything in blender , and blend until smooth and free of lumps
2. taste the smoothie if you think you need more sugar add it
3. it will really depend on the size of the avocado
4. this is best eaten right away , because if you store the smoothie in the fridge it will turn a slight brown on top and alter the taste
demonstrations.review: yum! this was such a fast and easy breakfast smoothie.It was creamy fresh and sweet,thanks for a new way to use avocado as I love them and always have them in my house:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cinnamon buns

what a treat for the kids when they come home from school or for a sunday brunch. there will never be any of these left over! they are crispy on the outside and lovely and soft inside. very tasty

1. spray a 9 inch baking pan and preheat oven to 425f
2. in a small bowl mix the filling ingredients together , mixing well
3. in large bowl combine the sugar , raisins , flour , salt , baking powder and baking soda
4. add yogurt and oil , mix well together until you have formed a dough
5. on a lightly floured surface knead the dough 8-10 times
6. roll the dough out to a 8" x 10" rectangle
7. brush dough with margarine and sprinkle the filling evenly over the dough
8. roll up jelly roll fashion , pinch seam to seal
9. cut into 12 1-inch pieces
10. place rolls slightly touching in the prepared baking pan
11. bake for approx 17 minutes or until golden
12. place on wire rack for 10 minutes
13. serve warm
demonstrations.review: Quick, easy and tasty! what more could you ask for? I didn't have and plain yogurt but I had vanilla Greek yogurt so I used that. I also used butter in place of the margarine as we only had butter. Other than that I followed the recipe as written.They turned out great and I know I will use this this recipe again. We had some leftover homemade vanilla frosting in the freezer so I spread a little over top of them and my family gobbled them up. Thanks Bergy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
double chocolate banana muffins

nan

1. in a large bowl , combine the first six ingredients
2. in a small bowl , combine bananas , oil and egg
3. stir into dry ingredients just until moistened
4. fold in chocolate chips
5. fill greased or paper lined muffin cups three fourths full
6. bake at 350 deg f for 20-25 minutes or until muffins test done
demonstrations.review: Yummmmm,I made these this morning and I think there is maybe 1 left from 12 muffins? <br/>yes, we are a bunch of chocolate lovin' pigs and we know it! I used 4 badly spotted banana's because I hate wasting food,and I only had about 3/4 of a cup of regular sized semi sweet choc chips so I used those,otherwise followed recipe and everyone loved them.Thanks for a new "get rid of those icky looking bananas" recipe;)

target.recipe_text:
marvelous marinated london broil

this steak turns out moist and flavorful.  i found this recipe in my local newspaper many years ago.

1. pour the honey into a 2-cup glass measure
2. microwave the honey , uncovered , at high , 30 seconds to make it pour easily
3. remove the measure from the microwave and add the oil , worcestershire sauce , soy sauce , lime juice , garlic and onion powder
4. whisk to blend well
5. place the meat in a gallon-size zipper-top plastic bag
6. whisk the marinade once more and pour it over the meat
7. seal the bag and turn the bag several times to cover the meat with marinade
8. refrigerate 8 to 24 hours , turning the bag at least once , if possible
9. turn on a gas grill to medium high
10. remove the meat from the marinade and discard the marinade
11. grill the meat , covering the grill to the desired doneness , 7 to 10 minutes per side for medium-rare , depending on the thickness
12. do not overcook
13. remove from the grill and slice across the grain
14. serve at once , or let stand until ready to serve
15. refrigerate leftovers , covered , up to 3 days
target.review: I had to use lemon juice in place of the lime, but it was fabulous! For the first time in my life I made a great steak. From now on, this is how I'll always do it. It was too easy and the family gobbled it up! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soupa avgolemono  egg lemon soup

this tasty soup is very popular in greece and cyprus. i remember my father making it on chilly winter days, especially when there were colds and flu in the household! sometimes he would add chopped, cooked chicken to the soup, and other times he would serve it plain.  this is a taste of my childhood.

1. bring broth to boil in saucepan , and add rice or orzo
2. cover and cook on medium low heat for 20-25 minutes or 10 minutes
3. while the rice cooks , lightly beat the eggs and the lemon juice together
4. remove the broth from heat
5. slowly mix about one cup of the hot broth into egg-lemon mixture
6. add to the soup gradually while stirring
7. place saucepan back on the heat , and stir until soup is heated through
8. serve
demonstrations.review: This was very simple and delicious, but it didn't go over as well as I had hoped with my family, hence only four stars. I loved it, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
someone s grandma s brisket

from a community cookbook.  sounds easy and yummy with honey, ketchup, mustard powder, onion, paprika, red wine and coke!  imagine that! i love brisket so i can't wait to try this one. best if marinated overnight.

1. put the oil , coke , wine , honey , ketchup , mustard , onion and paprika in a food processor or blender and "chop" mixture
2. pour over the brisket
3. marinate overnight if you have time
4. cook in a roasting pan with the liquid , at 350 degrees f
5. , loosely covered , until fork tender
6. when brisket is cool , slice meat against the grain , and return to the pan with the gravy
7. reheat when ready to serve
8. to make the gravy thicker , you can pour the pan juices into a saucepan
9. add 1 tablespoons flour and let cook until half the liquid is reduced
10. pour over sliced meat and serve
demonstrations.review: Couldn't rate this recipe, because I haven't tried it. Just wanted to point out that as it is, it's not kosher for passover. You should specify kosher for passover wine and ketchup, and Coke is not kosher for passover, though diet Coke might be. Looks like a great recipe, and I'll try it after the holiday.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kukkakaalilaatikko

hehe....i had to post this recipe just because the name was so amazing...plus it sounds pretty good! i think it means cauliflower rye casserole.  it is from sundays at moosewood.

1. at least an hour before cooking , pour the beer into a shallow bowl until it becomes flat
2. dry the bread cubes on a baking sheet in a 300f oven until they are crisp but not browned , about 15-20 minutes
3. saute the cauliflower in the butter with the carraway seeds until just barely tender
4. combine the bread cubes and cauliflower with the grated cheese
5. spread the mixture into a buttered 2-qt casserole dish
6. mix the eggs , mustard , coriander , and black pepper in a blender or by hand with the flat beer and pour the mixture into the casserole dish
7. bake at 350f for 30-45 minutes until puffed and golden
demonstrations.review: We liked this a lot. I skipped the caraway seeds because I used seeded rye and I thought the kids might not like so many. I also skipped the butter because I steamed the cauliflower. Will make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracker barrel potato casserole hash browns casserole   copycat

i love cracker barrels hash brown potatoes/potato casserole so i thought i would share this recipe i found on copykat.com.

1. spray a 13" x 9" x 2" baking pan with non-stick cooking spray
2. set aside
3. in a bowl , combine soup , cheese , butter , onion , salt , and pepper
4. gently fold the potatoes into the mixture and pour into prepared pan
5. bake in a 350 degree oven for 35-40 minutes , until heated through and top is browned
demonstrations.review: I made this last week and the whole family loved it, so I'm making it again tonight. I was afraid you had forgotten to say "thaw the potatoes first", but I went ahead and followed the directions exactly, and it was perfect! I have also tried the recipe that calls for sour cream, but this is much closer to Cracker Barrel, and cheaper and easier to boot!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jiffy corn muffin mix copycat

makes 8.5 ounces (equal to 1-box of jiffy corn muffin mix), 1-1/2 cups of mix, or 6 corn muffins.
recipe source: www

1. combine first 5 ingredients in a bowl , mix well
2. whisk in vegetable oil and mix until dry mixture is smooth and lumps are gone
3. if another recipe is calling for a box of jiffy corn muffin mix , add the above mixed ingredients to that recipe
4. to make corn muffins , preheat oven to 400f , spray muffin pan with non-stick cooking spray
5. optional: to mix , add any combination of optional ingredients you prefer
