demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate  chocolate  chocolate  bundt cake with chocolate glaze

need i say more...chocolate! decadently rich and moist. add a scoop of vanilla ice cream and you're in heaven.

1. cake: preheat oven to 350
2. grease and flour bundt pan , set aside
3. in large mixing bowl , combine cake mix , pudding mix and chocolate chips
4. in another bowl , combine water , eggs , and vanilla mixing well
5. add egg mixture to dry mixture and mix with spoon until just blended
6. pour into prepared pan
7. bake for 50 to 55 minutes or until cake tests done when wooden pick in center comes out clean
8. cool 15 to 20 minutes before removing cake from pan
9. when completely cool , drizzle cake with chocolate glaze
10. chocolate glaze: combine all ingredients in bowl
11. mix with spoon until smooth
demonstrations.review: Out of this world.  And no oil.  It was moist and dense.  It really satisfied my chocolate needs.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brings back memories tuna casserole

my sister used to make this all the time, but had to lie to me about the cream of mushroom soup because when i was little i thought i didn't like mushrooms! she would tell me it was cream of chicken soup (which you can substitute if you wish). i loved this comfort food and am so glad i found the recipe again. now trying to get my kids to eat it might prove to be a feat :)

1. prepare egg noodles as directed on package
2. drain and rinse
3. preheat oven to 375 degrees
4. combine soup and milk and mix well
5. in a large bowl , combine cooked noodles , soup mixture , tuna and peas and stir gently until well coated
6. turn into a buttered casserole or baking dish and sprinkle evenly with crushed potato chips
7. bake for 25 minutes or until bubbly
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed this but it seemed sort of dry.  I think that I will double the soup next time.  And might try bread crumbs instead of chips.  But overall this was exactly what we were craving (ie not cheese)  Thanks for a great stepping off point.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
all american hamburgers

been making  1/4 pound burgers like this forever, and dont think its ever been posted here.  one of our all-time favorites on the summer grill! we also love these with a slice of cooked bacon for a bacon cheeseburger.

1. in a large bowl , combine beef , soup mix and worcestershire sauce
2. mix just until blended dont overwork the meat
3. shape into eight patties
4. grill over medium coals to desired doneness or until no longer pink in the center and a minimum temperature of 160 degrees , brushing frequently with barbecue sauce
5. top with cheese
6. continue grilling until cheese is melted
7. for each serving
8. fill bun with lettuce , pickle slices , tomato and hamburger patty
demonstrations.review: I thought these were just okay.  I solid burger but not exactly to our taste.  I thought the onion soup added a funny, off taste to the burger.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttery bread machine rolls

these golden, fluffy, butterfy rolls are great hot from the oven. the dough is very easy to shape. this recipe is from a quick cooking magazine

1. in bread machine pan , put all ingredients in order suggested by manufacturer
2. select dough setting
3. when cycle is completed , turn dough onto a lightly floured surface
4. divide dough into 24 portions
5. shape dough into balls
6. place in a greased 13 inch by 9 inch baking pan
7. cover and let rise in a warm place for 30-45 minutes
8. bake at 350 degrees for 13-16 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: These are amazing.  Absolutely my go to roll now.  I have made these every week for the last month.

target.recipe_text:
cheesy shrimp   grits casserole

delightful addition to a beautiful brunch or perhaps a light supper with a salad. from southern living

1. bring 4 cups chicken broth and 1 / 2 teaspoon salt to a boil in a large saucepan
2. stir in grits
3. cover , reduce heat , and simmer 20 minutes
4. stir together grits , 3 / 4 cup cheddar cheese , and monterey jack cheese
5. melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat
6. add green onions , bell pepper , and garlic , and saut 5 minutes or until tender
7. stir together green onion mixture , grits mixture , shrimp , and next 3 ingredients
8. pour into a lightly greased 2-quart baking dish
9. sprinkle top with remaining 1 / 4 cup shredded cheddar cheese
10. bake at 350 for 30 to 45 minutes
target.review: delicious. I added bacon, some Tabasco and paprika also.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tarragon chicken casserole

this is so easy, and so good. no browning, just put the chicken in and pour the sauce on, and bake!! the tarragon makes it an elegant entree.

1. in 13 x 9 inch baking pan , place chicken pieces
2. do not overlap
3. place onion rings over top
4. mix seasonings with cream of chicken soup and milk and spoon over chicken
5. bake , uncovered , in 375 degree oven for 40 minutes
6. sprinkle chicken with almonds , if desired
7. bake 10 minutes more or until chicken is tender
demonstrations.review: I made this for the first time a few weeks ago and made it again tonight. Very elegant, simple and it tastes delicious. Didn't have any almonds, served over rice with veggies. Even my picky two year old was asking for seconds. He did the same thing last time I made it, therefore it is definitely a keeper. Thanks papergoddess!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot whole chicken

tender, fall-off-the-bone chicken! skip the overnight refrigeration if you are in a hurry. for variety, eliminate the onion and substitute a quartered lemon or two, stuffed into the chicken cavity.  chef shapeweaver had a good suggestion:  use fajita seasoning mix #28011 as another variation.  thanks!  the standard size slow cookers are a bit too small and a whole chicken won't fit.  you'll need a 6-quart slow cooker for this recipe.

1. in a small bowl , combine the spices
2. remove any giblets from chicken and clean chicken
3. rub spice mixture onto the chicken
4. place in resealable plastic bag and refrigerate overnight
5. when ready to cook , put chopped onion in bottom of crock pot
6. add chicken
7. no liquid is needed , the chicken will make its own juices
8. cook on low 4-8 hours
demonstrations.review: So easy to make, moist and delicious. I will leave off the cayenne next time for the sake of children. I didn't let it sit overnight, only put on the rub before cooking, and it worked great. I also did not have lemon or onion...but will definitely use the lemon next time. I also put under broiler for a few minutes to crisp. The dripping made great gravy! Yum. I will make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortellini with garlic cream sauce

yum! this is so so good--i hope you like this as much as we do.

1. cook tortellini according to the package directions
2. set aside
3. in a large pan , heat oil and butter
4. saut garlic 2 minutes
5. in a cup stir together half and half , broth , and cornstarch
6. pour into skillet
7. bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer 3 minutes
8. stir in the herbs , olives , garlic , and tortellini
9. cook 2 minutes to heat through
10. serve
demonstrations.review: Thanks. I basically used your ingredients and added a pinch of this and that...I used heavy cream and rosemary I had in fridge. Topped with some cheese, omitted olives. Very quick, easy and filling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic chicken thighs

full of flavor and very easy. substitute chicken breast for a low fat version.

1. place chicken between 2 sheets of plastic wrap and pound lightly with a mallet or other heavy flat object to flatten slightly
2. season with salt and pepper to taste
3. heat oil in a heavy nonstick pan over medium high heat
4. add rosemary and crushed garlic
5. saut 1-2 minutes , pressing down on rosemary and garlic to release flavor
6. remove with a slotted spoon and discard
7. saut chicken 5 minutes per side , turning frequently until browned and cooked throughout
8. stir in minced garlic during last 2 minutes of cooking
demonstrations.review: pretty good. Easy and good flavor. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft batch chocolate chip cookies

a soft & chewy cookie. one of my favorites

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. mix butter , sugar , brown sugar , vanilla and eggs together until creamy
3. add the remaining ingredients and blend well
4. bake until lightly browned
5. store in an air tight container
demonstrations.review: Wonderful chocolate chip cookie recipe. I tried a few others, and this one definitely tops all the others. I made exactly as instructed, made about 40 good sized cookies.

target.recipe_text:
garlic and parmesan sourdough bread

this is one of those recipes that you can taste with your imagination! i haven't made it yet, but i will soon. i just know it is going to be really yummy with my next italian dinner!

1. starter must be proofed overnight or up to 12 hours before making bread
2. add ingredients to bread machine in the order recommended by your machine's manufacturer
3. select dough cycle and start
4. when dough has finished kneading , but before it goes into the rise , remove from machine and shape into loaf or loaves
5. you could do standard loaves , or a free-form round or oval , or elongate
6. let bread rise until double in bulk , covered
7. for a nice touch , lightly beat 1 egg white with 1 tbsp water and brush top of loaf with this egg wash , and then sprinkle with fresh parmesan , finely shredded
8. bake at 375 degrees f for 30 to 45 minutes , depending on the size of loaves
target.review: Like others, I wish there were a rating higher than 5 stars. I found that only 3 cups of flour and a cup of milk was about right. I also substituted molasses for honey for a more distinct flavor. I made a "tear&share" like Jenny (great idea by the way!) and sprinkled it with mozzarella cheese and spread sun-dried tomato and basil tapenade on it, then stuck it back in the oven so the cheese would melt. My husband loved it. If he weren't already married to me, I feel certain this would've cinched the deal. The sourdough loaf I made also came out great. I plan to make this next time company comes. WONDERFUL!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yangtze chicken skewers

tasty marinated chicken and pineapple skewers. prep time does not include marinate time.

1. combine the soy sauce , ketchup , wine , marmalade and honey in a glass or ceramic dish large enough to hold all the chicken
2. cut the chicken breasts into 2 inch cubes and add to the dish , stirring to coat the chicken well
3. marinate for at least 1 hour in the fridge
4. preheat a grill rack or bbq
5. could also be broiled , your choice
6. drain the marinade and discard it
7. thread the chicken cubes and pineapple cubes together onto the skewers
8. if you are using wooden skewers you should soak them first
9. cook until done , turning occasionally
10. about 15 minutes
11. you could use canned pineapple pieces if fresh is not available
demonstrations.review: Delicious. And you can sub in any other jelly, too. Peach or apricot work best, I think. I also prefer to add a bit of lemon juice instead of white wine. Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthier fresh apple cake

a few changes to lower the fat and calories, while still keeping the flavor.  leaving on the apple peel doubles the fiber. one serving is approximately 225-250 calories.  cooking time includes cooling time,.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. spray bottom only of 9x13 inch pan with cooking spray
3. in a large bowl , beat sugars , buttetrmilk , oil , vanilla , and eggs with mixer on low speed for 25 seconds or until blended
4. add rewmaining ingredients except apples , and walnuts , and beat on low speed about 1 minute or until blended
5. stir in apples and walnuts , and spread batter into pan
6. bake 40-45 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
7. cool in pan on cooling rack for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Lovely.  I wanted something to take to a friend's house, and this fit the bill by being healthy for me and edible for others.  I don't keep buttermilk on hand, so I substituted almond milk and yogurt in a 30-70 ratio.  I also didn't use whole wheat flour because we're currently out.  I used all brown sugar, no granulated... and it came out great: 40 minutes on the dot.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted garlic mashed potatoes and cauliflower

a great way to disguise cauliflower! the kids and adults love it! to roast garlic cut pointed end off bulb rub olive oil on wrap in foil and bake 375 for 1 hour.

1. boil potatoes and cauliflower together till tender
2. drain and mash potatoes , cauliflower , oil and butter
3. add rest of ingredients mix through
4. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I think I'll always put some cauliflower in my mashed potatoes. The texture is slightly lighter and the flavor difference is subtle. I even added a bit of broccoli and it was hardly noticeable. I also didn't use any butter or sour cream but added some part-skim ricotta (lower in fat) to add richness. Paprika, salt, pepper, and garlic were just perfect. Thanks for the great idea!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy mushroom bread

nan

1. reconstitute dried mushrooms in one cup of hot water
2. set aside
3. dissolve yeast in the 1 / 4 cup warm water and add sugar
4. set aside
5. warm the cottage cheese and put in bowl
6. add yeast mixture , egg , salt , soda , 2 1 / 2 cups flour and chives and stir until springy
7. cover bowl with towel and let rise to double ,
8. turn onto floured board and knead in the drained , chopped and blotted mushrooms and remaining one cup flour ,
9. place in oiled 2-quart casserole and let rise to double , about 45 minutes
10. bake at 375 degrees for 35 minutes
11. butter top crust while still hot , remove from pan , serve immediately
demonstrations.review:
This bread was delicious! Hubby approved, too.  I didn't have chives, so I did sub in diced onion and parsley.  I also used low-fat cottage cheese and fresh mushrooms.
We're having it with steaks, but it was also fabulous dipped in olive oil and spices---just like somthing you'd get at a restaurant and a great New Year's Eve treat. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy soft breadsticks

very nice to have with soups and salads.

1. mix flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
2. slowly add milk to form a soft dough
3. knead on a floured surface 4 times
4. roll into 10 inch by 5 inch rectangle
5. cut into 12 sticks
6. put butter in 13x9 baking dish
7. roll breadsticks in butter
8. sprinkle with sesame seeds
9. bake at 425 for 16 minutes , or until golden
demonstrations.review: These were good, quick to make and didn't need too much butter. I did have trouble getting the full size breadsticks out of them. I only got 3/4 of the yield and they weren't that long. My husband and I both thought they tasted like biscuits, so while we enjoyed them and will make them again, they weren't as soft as we were expecting.

target.recipe_text:
marinade for beef

this marinade gives an 

1. combine all ingredients in a glass deep or large zip-lock bag and mix well
2. add beef and marinate for several hours
3. grill steaks , basting with marinade to desired doneness or place roast along with marinade in a baking dish and bake@ 350 degrees for 40-50 minutes for rare
4. if whole tenderloin cook 45-60 minutes@ 425 degrees for rare
5. i bake the tenderloin@ 350 degrees for about 2 hours for medium well
6. let sit about 10 minutes before slicing
target.review: We will use this marinade often in the coming months, as we love steak on the grill and with this recipe for the marinade, now we can have perfectly grilled delicious flavored meat!  Kudos to you Anita for this winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chuck wagon potatoes

from the next food network star rory schepisi.  potatoes with onion, garlic, bacon, butter, and cheese.  what could be better?

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. wash and cut potatoes into bite-size pieces
3. place potatoes in a medium sized roasting pan
4. add diced onion , shallots , garlic and bacon
5. mix potatoes and other ingredients with softened butter until ingredients are coated thoroughly with butter
6. cover with foil and cook approximately for 1 hour or until the potatoes are almost fork tender
7. remove foil
8. season with salt and pepper and place back in the oven for 20 to 25 minutes or until potatoes have a nice golden brown color
9. garnish with grated cheese and chives
demonstrations.review: MMMmmmm!  Potatoes don't get any tastier than these.  We loved them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry sweetheart streusel muffins

for a romantic touch, bake these in heart shaped muffin tins.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. grease bottom and sides of 18 cup muffin tin / s
3. mix together ingredients for streusel and set aside
4. mix together for the muffins the flour , sugar , and baking powder
5. separately , mix together the milk , melted butter , beaten eggs and vanilla
6. gently mix the wet ingredients into the flour mixture
7. fold in lightly floured chopped strawberries
8. pour mixture into prepared muffin tins and top with streusel mixture
9. bake at 375f for 25-30 minutes until toothpick comes out clean
10. allow muffins to cool for 10 minutes before trying to remove them fom the pan
11. finish cooling muffins on a wire rack
12. to make strawberry butter , mix together thoroughly the soft butter and powdered sugar
13. fold in the strawberries and toasted pecans
14. chill until needed and soften before serving on split muffins
demonstrations.review: My DH and I thought these muffins were scrumptious to say the least!  We loved the strawberries in the muffins and the topping was to die for!  What made it even better was the delicious Strawberry Butter.  The muffins were moist and tasted great and everything about them couldn't have been better.  This is not only a winner in the contest but it is the best recipe I have made on Zaar to date.  Good Luck!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
virginia fried soft shell crabs

nan

1. dress fresh crabs or thaw frozen crabs
2. rinse in cold water
3. drain
4. combine eggs , milk , and salt
5. combine flour and crumbs
6. dip crabs in egg mixture and roll in flour / crumb mixture
7. for heavier breading , let crabs sit several minutes and repeat dipping / rolling procedure
8. additional spices , such as cayenne pepper and garlic , may also be added
9. place crabs in a heavy frying pan which contains 1 / 8 to 1 / 4 inch of fat , hot but not smoking
10. fry at moderate heat
11. when crabs are brown on one side , turn carefully and brown the other side
12. cooking time is approximately 8 to 10 minutes
13. drain on absorbent paper
demonstrations.review: This is a great basic recipe for you to experiment with.  I added some Tony Chachere's Cajun Seasoning and a little Old Bay to the flour.  It was a great addition for the crab.  We loved them!  I am saving this for future use!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: I made these meatballs to go in my spaghetti sauce, and they had a wonderful flavor!  The sauce wasn't the best, but the meatballs were!  I used a beef and pork mix this time, and may try all beef next time, and I will make them whenever I need meatballs.  They were so tender and delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kenny s brain spread

this is a great appetizer for your next halloween party!  if you don't have a brain mold, you can substitute by lining a med. size round bowl with saran wrap and making your mold. once the mold is set, you can take the round end of a knife or a pencil eraser and create your crevices and creases to make your brain, as in the picture i have posted.  takes a little more time, but works well.  when done designing your brain, peel off the saran wrap, and plate to serve along with your crackers, chips etc.

1. heat soup , undiluted , and mix in the cream cheese
2. stir in softened gelatin , and blend well
3. fold in remaining ingredients , and pour into a lightly-oiled brain mold
4. chill until firm , and serve with your favorite crackers , pita or bagel chips or scoops
demonstrations.review:
Excellent!  I used shrimp for this recipe, and it went over very well at thi years Halloween Party!  Thank you for this recipe Linda.  I will be making it again for sure.

Megan

target.recipe_text:
amish soft honey whole wheat bread

i've been looking for a soft all whole wheat bread, and i finally found it!  this is in an amish cookbook that i have, and i am writing it as it is written. i mix it with my kitchenaid. :)  this is our sandwich bread that we have all the time on hand and the recipe can easily be cut into 1/3 to make just one loaf. :) 10/8/07 corrections made to make bigger loaves.  i usually use recipe #185778 to have a great rise.

1. mix water with yeast and sugar and let sit until foamy
2. in the meanwhile , put the 3 eggs in a bowl of hot water
3. put flour , salt , and gluten in bowl
4. pour in yeast mixture and stir until combined
5. add in honey , eggs , and crisco until combined , scraping sides
6. add more wheat flour and knead until smooth
7. let set in warm place for about an hour until double in size
8. divide into 3 loaves
9. let rise again in warm place until doubled
10. bake as regular bread
11. enjoy !
target.review: I am a sucker for whole wheat homemade bread. Ahhh...the smell of it baking in the oven just makes my mouth water and I can't wait to open the oven and devour slices of it with or without butter. The kids also have their school lunches made with this bread and enjoy it too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
down home macaroni and cheese

my kids don't like most homemade macaroni and cheese dishes, but they love this one. it is creamy and cheesy!

1. melt 3 tablespoons of the butter in large saucepan on low heat
2. blend in flour and salt
3. cook and stir 1 minute
4. gradually add milk
5. cook , stirring constantly , until thickened
6. add prepared cheese product and 1-1 / 2 cups of the shredded cheese
7. stir until melted
8. stir in macaroni
9. pour into lightly greased 1-1 / 2-quart casserole
10. melt remaining 1 tablespoon butter
11. toss with bread crumbs
12. sprinkle casserole with remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese and bread crumb mixture
13. bake at 350 degrees f for 20 minutes or until thoroughly heated
demonstrations.review: Yum, yum! I just had some the other night and it was delicious. So very cheesy and creamy. Everyone loves this and asks for more. This is so much better than the recipe my mother used.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zippity do dah baked ziti

i have had this recipe for a couple of years and got it from another site, but i did several modifications to the original.  it makes a lot!  great oamc recipe!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. cook ziti according to package
3. drain
4. cook italian sausage along with garlic and onion until browned
5. drain
6. return sausage mixture to pan
7. add in spaghetti sauce , sugar , and spices
8. stir
9. combine sour cream and cottage cheese
10. grease 13x9 with cooking spray
11. layer in the pan 1 / 2 of noodles , 1 / 2 of sauce , all of the provolone , all of the sour cream / cottage cheese mixture , 2nd 1 / 2 of noodles , 2nd half of sauce , mozzarella , and parmesan
12. bake in oven for 20-30 minutes or until heated through and cheeses are melted
demonstrations.review: This is so much easier than lasagna and just as delicious. Serve with garlic bread and a tossed green salad (don't forget the feta cheese and Italian olives) and you have a great meal for a crowd. How about some Spumoni ice cream for dessert? I love Italian dishes like this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s chicken curry

we love this dish.  it is fast and easy, too!  my mom would usually serve it with a variety of condiments to go on top like coconut, pineapple, raisins, bacon, peanuts, etc.

1. saute onion in butter with curry powder
2. blend in flour and other seasonings
3. cook on low until smooth
4. stir in broth and milk slowly with whisk to make sure to get all the lumps out
5. bring to boil
6. boil for one minute or until thickened while stirring
7. stir in chicken and lemon juice
8. serve over rice
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is a delicious curry meal and everyone enjoys adding their own special condiments, which I like to have at least 5 choices. Here are some more choices that can be used: dates, chopped egg, sweet or sour pickles, sliced avocado, and chutney. Baked Bananas for dessert is a nice finish to this meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
springtime asparagus medley

this is a taste of home recipe with lots of delicious taste.  i made this for my mom and i for lunch and we were slurping up the dressing.  :)  i put the recipe as written, but my changes are in parentheses.)

1. in large saucepan , bring water to oil
2. add aspargus
3. cover and cook for 3-5 minutes or until crisp-tender
4. drain
5. add tomatoes
6. cover and keep warm
7. in a blender , combine vinegar , worcestershire sauce , sugar , onion , salt and paprika
8. cover and process until smooth
9. while processing , gradually add oil in a steady stream
10. pour over asparagus mixture and toss to coat
11. transfer to serving bowl
12. sprinkle with almonds and blue cheese if desired
13. serve warm
demonstrations.review: The asparagus was so tender and delicious. The blue cheese added a wonderful zing to the dish, and the dressing was SO...good that you don't want to miss one drop!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweetslady s chocolate peanut butter brownie trifle

this is one of my most requested recipes.  it is something i came up with one day as i love the combination of peanut butter and chocolate.  you can make this with brownies from the box; however, i make mine from scratch.  this is my husband's other favorite dessert.

1. brownies:
2. preheat oven to 350
3. grease 13 x 9-inch baking pan
4. combine dry ingredients in large mixer bowl
5. stir
6. add wet ingredients and stir well
7. spread into prepared baking pan
8. bake for 18 to 25 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out slightly sticky
9. let cool completely
10. trifle:
11. mix cream cheese and powdered sugar until smooth
12. add in peanut butter and milk
13. combine
14. fold in cool whip until combined
15. take half of the brownies out and crumble in large glass bowl , if you have one , or in a 13x9 pan
16. add a layer of the peanut butter mixture
17. take the other half of the brownies out and crumble on top of the peanut butter mixture
18. put the last half of the peanut butter mixture on top
19. drizzle chocolate syrup on top
20. add the chopped peanut butter cups on top
21. refrigerate until serving time
22. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Wonderful combination of my favorite ingredients, chocolate and peanut butter! You can't go wrong here! Try it for yourself and see if you don't agree!

target.recipe_text:
grilled ham and cheddar sandwich

this sandwich sizzles with flavor.  these go great with a nice spicy tomato soup, too.

1. mix mayonnaise , steak and worcestershire sauces , dry mustard , and cayenne in small bowl
2. spread 4 slices bread with thin layer of grainy mustard and top with layer of onion , 2 pieces of ham , and the cheese
3. spread mayonnaise mixture over remaining bread and place on sandwiches
4. brush both sides of sandwiches with butter
5. heat large skillet over medium heat
6. add sandwiches and fry , turning once , until golden , about 3 m inutes each side
7. serve hot
target.review: wow this is good  didnt use the onions

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef over rice

simple 4 ingredient meal that tastes great.  good for a busy night.  my mom used to make this all the time, it is one of my dad's favorite meals.  i put my rice in a rice cooker, so that's the amount of water i listed in the ingredients.  it normally takes about 25 minutes to have it on the table, less if you use precooked beef.

1. cook the rice as you would normally
2. saute' onion , and cook ground beef over medium heat in a large skillet , drain off the fat
3. return to skillet
4. add onion soup mix and water , bring to a boil and simmer until slightly thickened , about 5-10 minutes
5. serve warm over rice
6. the extra liquid will soak into the rice and flavor it
demonstrations.review: good

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dijon mustard marinade for grilled fish

this marinade is delicious on firm, white flesh grilled fish, such as grouper or mahi-mahi.

1. mix all ingredients well
2. to prepare your fish , marinate your fish fillets for several hours
3. prepare your grill
4. once it is hot , grill your fish until it flakes easily
5. baste the fish with the marinade while it is grilling
6. delish !
demonstrations.review: this is wicked good

demonstrations.recipe_text:
patty melt

another easy sandwich that my boys liked.   they had trouble with onions, but i chopped them really fine and i don't know that they knew they where there, did you guys, lol.

1. saut onions until golden in 2 tablespoons butter until translucent and lightly golden
2. remove from the pan
3. form the meat patty so it will fit the bread
4. grill to desired doneness
5. butter bread on one side
6. put buttered side down on hot griddle , put 1 slice cheese followed by onions then cooked patty , followed by cheese
7. butter one side of the other slice of bread and place on top buttered side out
8. fry until bread is crisp but not burned , turn over and do the same thing on the other side
9. cheese should be well melted
10. slice on the diagonal
demonstrations.review: this is a great sandwich

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cockrel breast with lemon carrots

it is really a chicken breast guys; just thought the name was cute. danish, very simple, served with white rice. zaar tour 6. i just made this in crockpot and will tell how i did versus old recipe .i really liked this and its pretty . i used bone in chicken breasts but this calls for frozen breasts

1. cut lemon in half
2. heat oil in skillet
3. add chicken
4. brown
5. add onion
6. saute
7. take out chicken
8. add carrots
9. saute with sugar
10. squeeze lemon juice over
11. add chicken back to pan
12. add water
13. poach with the lemon peel
14. cook until chicken and carrots done
15. arrange carrots in a circle
16. put chicken on top of carrots
17. squeeze 2nd half of lemon over top
demonstrations.review: simple  i like the lemony taste

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma florence s fruit cookies

this was my great grandma's recipe.  it is a family fav and uses that bacon grease people save. this is a soft cookie that spreads out while its cooking

1. sift all dry ingredients into bowl
2. stir liquid into well of flour
3. add raisin and nuts stir drop cookies onto pan will spread out 400 oven 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: these are sweet  and the bacon adds to the taste i love these

target.recipe_text:
vegetarian hominy chili with beans

adapted from a cooking light recipe i found years ago. this is quick, hearty and delicious, which is great considering it can be made in less than 30 minutes, simmer time included. pretty much involves peeling some garlic and opening cans, but of course, you can use fresh tomatoes and pre-soaked beans if you want. the hominy adds a great texture, as does the tvp if you choose to include it. like most chili it tastes even better the next day and freezes well. serve with sour cream and sprinkle with a good sharp shredded cheddar.

1. saute garlic in the canola oil in a large sauce pan or small pot
2. stir in the remaining ingredients and bring to a boil
3. reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes
4. if using tvp , add water if chili gets too thick as tvp will absorb liquid pretty quickly
5. garnish with cilantro , shredded cheddar cheese , sour cream
target.review:
Wonderful!
I happened to have the large TVP on hand and wow! Even my DH who normally turns his nose up at meat substitutes had seconds.
Thank you for a great addition to my cookbook!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amaretto almond liqueur

i have not tried this out, but i found it on a copycat recipe site and it is supposed to be comparable to di saronno brand liqueur.

1. combine the water and the sugars in a saucepan
2. heat until boiling over medium heat and until all the sugar is dissolved
3. remove from the heat and let mixture cool for about 15 minutes
4. add the vodka , almond extract and vanilla extract
5. store in a sealed bottle
demonstrations.review:
WOW!
As I sip a little taste of this, I can't believe I actually made it!
So easy, so cost-friendly and so very delicious!
Great recipe!
Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut crumb cake  made with vanilla wafers

the food section of my local newspaper says this super easy cake is "super moist, super simple and super good with cold glass of milk!" i haven't tried it yet; let me know what y'all think....

1. preheat oven to 325f grease and flour a bundt pan - i used the pam cooking spray with flour already in it
2. place vanilla wafers in a food processor and pulse until you end up with fine crumbs
3. combine crumbs with coconut , sugar and pecans in a large bowl
4. mix
5. in a medium bowl , whisk eggs , butter and milk together
6. pour egg mixture over dry ingredients and mix well
7. batter will be thick
8. pour batter into prepared pan
9. bake 1 hour and 35 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I made this early this am - it's hot in VA and wanted to get the baking over with early! Anyhow, the cake is good, but we thought it needed more flavor - maybe some coconut or vanilla extract. Because the cake was baked when we discovered this, I made a XXX sugar glaze (orange flavored) and it provided just the perk the cake needed. Actually reminds me now of an orange slice candy cake my dad's sister used to make. Quite good! Next time, I'm going to add dates and orange slice candies-chopped-and see what happens.
Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing taco seasoning

this taco seasoning is just perfect!  i make three or four batches at a time and put them in ziploc bags for convenience.  once you try this you'll never buy a packet of taco seasoning at the grocery store again!  msg gives me a headache, so years ago i went on a quest for a great taco seasoning recipe.  this is what i found (i just don't remember where).  this will season a pound of ground whatever (or a bag of morningstar farms veggie crumbles- nobody will ever know it's meat-free).  hope you like it!

1. mix ingredients
2. pour over browned , ground meat in a pan over medium heat
3. i'm sorry i don't have an amount of water to recommend adding to the seasoning
4. i usually just wing it and then simmer it down if i get too carried away with the water
5. i think about a half cup ?
6. simmer until it looks good !
7. dig it
demonstrations.review:
This IS amazing! We just loved it, even with my omitting the salt!!
It tastes just like or better than anything like it I've ever purchased.
Merlissa, thank you soooo much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy mushroom rice pilaf

this recipe is from the back of a brown rice package.  so easy and excellent as a side dish!!

1. combine all ingredients in 3-quart saucepan
2. bring to boil
3. reduce heat to low
4. cover and simmer for 50 minutes
5. remove from heat and let stand , covered for 10 minutes
6. stir and serve immediately
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Served this at a dinner party and everyone loved it! How pretty it looked on the table! I used beef broth because we were having steak and it just seemed the thing to do LOL
Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
walnut meatballs  vegan

a very healthy alternative to meatballs.  i'm always looking for yummy vegan food and i'm especially looking forward to trying this one.  many of my favorite vegan recipes come from the micheff sisters, brenda walsh, cinda sanders and linda johnson, on 3abn.  this is one of brenda's recipes.  suggestions: these walnut balls can be made ahead of time and frozen. can also use them in other sauces such as spaghetti sauce. try making them a little smaller and using them for an appetizer. for “crispier” texture, fry them in a little canola oil instead of baking them.

update:  we finally tried this and were not disappointed!  made this with my quick vegan pesto alfredo sauce (recipe #246616) and onion herb foccacia bread (recipe #246431)and it tasted terrific!  i could see how frying them in a little oil would make them taste better plain, but i couldn't tell that much of a difference with them in the sauce and it's so much healthier having them baked.  i'm going to try to make these again this weekend with a vegan gravy and hope it turns out just as good! i've had it now with sweeet and sour sauce and it tasted really nice.

1. in food processor , pure the water and onion until smooth
2. pour into large mixing bowl
3. add all the remaining ingredients , mixing well until mixture holds together
4. coat hands with nonstick cooking spray
5. shape mixture into 1-inch balls
6. place on a baking sheet and bake for 30 minutes at 375 degrees
7. remove from oven and place meatballs on a platter
8. garnish with fresh parsley
9. serve hot with a variety of dipping sauces , such as sweet and sour , marinara , or your favorite
demonstrations.review:
Awesome recipe!
I didn't have any kind of sauce to serve, so I whipped up a batch using a glob of apricot preserves (low sugar), a squirt or two of ginger from a tube and a little apple cider vinegar.
The Meatballs are filling and totally yummy!
I will make this many times in the future. Thanks for sharing!!

target.recipe_text:
parmesan and basil orzo

this is a great recipe....tastes great and it is so quick and easy to make!  plus it goes with a wide range of meats, making it a great weeknight side dish.  this is from the cookbook "june fete fare".

1. saute the orzo in butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat , stirring constantly until golden
2. add the chicken broth and bring to a boil
3. cover , reduce heat , and simmer for 20 minutes or until the orzo is tender and the liquid is absorbed
4. stir in the parmesan cheese , julienned-sliced basil , and salt and pepper to taste
target.review: This really was a great side-dish for pretty much anything I sauteed it with two garlic cloves and some paprika for extra flavor, and because I love garlic in almost everything. Only other changes I made were using dried leaves of basil (that's all I had in the house), using less of it, and adding some mozzarella in addition to parmesan. Delicious! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oat peach muffins  small batch

these are a tasty change of pace from regular muffins.  they are lower in fat than most muffins.  from betty crocker's "new choices" cookbook.  recipe can easily be doubled to make 12 muffins.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. spray medium muffin cups with nonstick cooking spray
3. mix oats and yogurt in bol
4. beat in brown sugar , oil , molasses , vanilla and egg white
5. stir in remaining ingredients , except peaches , just until flour is moistened
6. fold in peaches
7. divide batter evenly among muffin cups
8. sprinkle with sugar if desired
9. bake about 20 minutes or until golden brown
10. immediately remove from pan
demonstrations.review: These were good but not great. I would have preferred them a bit sweeter to complement the more tart (but still mildly sweet) taste of the peach. Also this recipe does not state whether to peel before slicing the peach. I peeled and wouldn't have done it any other way. Just in case anyone was wondering!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry banana nut bread

this one came from an old school cook book. really good bread. great for bake sales and gifts. you can add cool whip for a dessert, or slice it for a really interesting sandwich.

1. in a bowl , sift the first 4 ingredients
2. set aside
3. mix the next 4 ingredients together in another bowl
4. fold flour mixture with orange juice mixture , then stir in bananas , cranberries and nuts
5. pour into 2 lightly greased loaf pans
6. bake at 350 for 45 minutes to 1 hour , or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean
7. i suggest checking at 30 minutes to be on the safe side
demonstrations.review: This was really, really, really good... with a few small changes. Looking at this recipe and other similar recipes, it seemed like an awful lot of sugar, so I omitted one of the cups. I also replaced 1.5 cups of the flour with whole wheat flour. Finally, I don't have loaf pans so I tried this in a springform pan. On 350 it took about an hour and a half and came out perfect (don't trust me on this--I tested every 10-15 minutes for the last 45 minutes and my oven runs a little cool). It's just slightly dense in a good way (thanks, whole wheat flour!). I could really taste the orange juice in the batter (the batter was delicious) but not so much in the finished product. When I make this again I might experiment with adding orange zest. Still, the banana and cranberry flavors stand on their own.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baklava muffins

i love baklava and this is a delightful treat that brings the same flavors through.    from how to be a  domestic goddess by nigella lawson.

1. preheat oven to 400f degrees
2. mix all the filling ingredients together in a small bowl , set aside
3. in a large bowl , mix together the flour , baking powder , baking soda and sugar
4. mix the egg , melted butter and buttermilk
5. make a well in the dry ingredients and add gently mix in the wet ingredients
6. fill 12 miffin cups 1 / 3 full , add a scant tablespoon of filling , cover with more muffin mixture until 2 / 3 full
7. sprinkle any remaining filling on top of the muffins
8. bake for 15 minutes
9. put the muffins onto a rack to cool and drizzle with honey
demonstrations.review: These were awesome. I followed the recipe pretty closely, the only change being I used three tablespoons of vegetable oil instead of butter in the batter, simply because I didn't feel like melting more butter. The taste was still exceptional. I also had no problem whatsoever getting them out of my cupcake tins after I sprayed the heck out of them with some Pam. My method for filling the cupcake tins was precisely this: one heaping tablespoon of batter followed by one rounded teaspoon of the filling covered by another tablespoon of the batter. This made (barely, but it did!) exactly 12 muffins. And they are delicious and taste as close to baklava as I can get without actually having baklava. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sage and parmesan rice

a nice side dish for poultry.  i made a change in the rice/broth ratio, and cooking method on recommendation of some of the reviewers, and after trying it myself again.  this changed the servings to 4 instead of 2.  thanks to all reviewers for your input!

1. melt butter in saucepan and stir in the sage
2. turn off heat and let sit
3. in another sauce pan heat broth to boiling
4. add rice and lower heat
5. simmer , covered until rice is tender , 15 to 20 minutes
6. put rice into serving dish and toss with sage butter and parmesan
demonstrations.review: This seemed a bit heavy, actually, for a side dish, but it was tasty! I used the same measurements here except I simplified to one cup rice, two cups water, one chicken bouillon cube. I cannot see how 1 cup of water would be enough for 3/4 cup rice, especially at just 12 minutes. Don't be a afraid to put more liquid into this recipe! The spices are perfect though! The cheese just makes it a little heavier than I expected. It was fine since I ate it as a main course.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ora s deep dark chocolate cake

sinful, sensational, and luscious, this cake is too easy to make to be this good! my grandmother gave me this recipe when i got married. make it and you'll see why she kept it such a secret.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour two 9-inch round baking pans
3. in large bowl , stir together sugar , flour , cocoa , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla: beat on medium speed of electric mixer for 2 minutes
5. stir in water
6. pour batter evenly into prepared pans
7. bake 30-35 minutes or until wooden toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
8. cool 10 minutes
9. remove from pans to wire racks
10. cool completely
11. prepare ora's favorite frosting
12. spread between layers and over top and sides of cake
demonstrations.review: First off, this exact recipe is on the back of the Hershey cocoa powder box. Secondly, it really just did not taste that good to me. And it was horrible coming out of the pan! It stuck so badly. I would definitely recommend using shortening or parchment paper.

target.recipe_text:
turkish meatballs  kofta

these are the well-known turkish kofta, delicious little meat balls or patties. you can make them with beef, but lamb is traditional and makes them very special.

1. make the bread crumbs by breaking up 2 slices of stale but not dried out whole wheat bread into the bowl of a food processor
2. whizz until finely crumbed
3. add the ground lamb and the egg , and process until blended
4. add the spices , garlic and parsley
5. process the meat well to achieve a fine texture
6. roll the mixture into small meatballs or finger shaped patties using dampened hands
7. you may cook them at once , or refrigerate the mixture for several hours
8. heat the oil in a heavy skillet , and fry the balls or patties until cooked through and evenly browned
9. the meatballs should be stirred several times , the patties turned once
10. remove them with a slotted spoon to drain
11. serve the meatballs hot or at room temperature as an appetizer
12. lovely with a yogurt or tahini sauce , on a bed of rice or in a pita
target.review: Delicious! I used fresh dill instead of dried mint as one of the other reviewers suggested. I didn't put in allspice. After I browned the kefta, I minced some garlic and onions, sauteed them with hot sauce, salt, pepper, chili flakes and tomatos and boiled and then simmered with a bit of water. Delish! My husband finished the whole plate (a sure sign that it's a winner!!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
twisted sisters creamy cucumber salad

when i arrived in iceland, this was my dh’s 1st food request & i went thru a lot of rz cucumber salad recipes to be sure it wasn’t a duplicate. siggi & my sister named this because it was original w/me & because of my twissis internet identity. for best results, don’t make this a dy ahead, but do allow at least 2 hrs for the flavors to blend & the “cream” to develop from the finished ingredient mix. i promise you’ll like this. (stated time does not include refrigeration time)

1. peel & slice cucumbers in 1 / 2 in thick slices
2. then half ea slice & transfer all slices to a lrg mixing bowl
3. roughly dice red onion & add to the bowl
4. quarter tomatoes , remove seeds , rough dice the tomato meat & add to the bowl
5. thinly slice 1 / 2 green pepper , cut slices in 1 in strips & add to the bowl
6. toss prepared veggies to achieve a good distributional mix
7. add last 6 ingredients to bowl , mix well & refrigerate at least 2 hrs
8. if thinly sliced , most cucumbers wilt & do not retain their crunch
9. -- when all ingredients have been combined , the mixture will appear dry & lack a creamy texture or appearance
10. do not panic that will begin to change almost immediately
11. if you reduce further , you will likely lose any salt component in the mix
demonstrations.review: I really like this! It's a very pretty salad, and very easy to make! Also...very tasty! I used a bit of fresh dill and filled in the rest with dried - otherwise followed it to a "t!" Thank you for a good one! I'll plan to take a pic, too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy turkey burger

this burger is tasty and the shredded cheese gives it a great flavor. i've used cheddar cheese, co-jack, or a mexican cheese mixture. you may need more breadcrumbs, depending on how moist your turkey is. i like to serve this with veganaise or mayo on the side.

1. mix all ingredients together in large bowl
2. add more bread crumbs if necessary
3. should form a firm ball
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. shape into six patties , not too thin
6. pan-fry , broil , or grill inside or out until lightly browned and cooked through , about 5 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: I love this burger! I added fresh minced onions and garlic and didn't put celery seed. I used mozzarella cheese and the burgers were delish and very easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic roasted potato salad

easy and different potato salad. great with bbq. it's a modification of a recipe from my aunt. she adds pickle relish and red onions to hers. i add parsley and scallions instead. it's up to you.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a bowl , toss potatoes , garlic , and olive oil together to coat
3. place potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet
4. sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste
5. place in 350 degree oven for 15-20 minutes , or until tender , allow to cool for 10 minutes
6. combine mayonnaise , creole mustard , lemon juice , parsley , and scallions
7. add to potatoes
8. add salt or pepper to taste
9. serve cold or room temperature
demonstrations.review: Really delish! The potatos had to cook for more like 20-22 min. I didn't need all that olive oil, and I used horesradish mustard instead of creole mustard. It was a bit hit for father's day paired with Cilantro Salmon Burgers!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy slow cooker applesauce

i came up with this recipe after i had bought too many apples for me to eat before they started getting soft.  i didn’t want to waste them or my money so i used what i had in my house for spices and poof!  out came this recipe.  you can really use any kind of apple you want, mac’s are usually less expensive than most other kinds of apples.  the coriander and lemon juice add great brightness to the apples.
i like to eat it plain, but it’s great stirred into hot cereal, or on top of your favorite vanilla ice cream with a little caramel sauce on the side, it tastes like an apple turnover!  i know that the spices seem minimal, but they add such a great flavor that’s not overpowering.

1. peel , core , and slice apples into bite sized pieces
2. pour 1 / 8 c of water and apples into the slow cooker
3. add salt , maple syrup , cloves , coriander , ginger , and lemon juice and stir so all apple slices are coated
4. place cinnamon sticks so that they are sticking into the container on three sides
5. turn the slow cooker on low and let cook for 6-7 hours or until the apples are very soft to pierce and most of the liquid is evaporated
6. turn off the slow cooker and take out the whole cinnamon sticks
7. for a chunky texture , mash with a potato masher , for a smooth texture , put into a food processor / blender or use an immersion blender until you reach the desired texture
demonstrations.review: So easy - so delish! It's a very easy recipe and the hardest thing is slicing the apples! I used 2 tsp ground cinnamon instead of the sticks, and I ground the cloves and coriander myself. I used lime juice instead of lemon, and added 1 tbsp of sugar to the pot. The results were wonderful! Slow cookers are amazing and I'm so glad to add this recipe to my collection!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
drunken mushroom soup

mushrooms and vermouth - who knew they'd taste so good together? very good, broth-based soup where the mushroom flavor really shines, since there's no cream or milk. it's also vegetarian but could be made vegan (substitute olive oil for butter and vegetable broth for chicken broth). we usually have this all year round, but like it especially to start a thanksgiving or christmas dinner. especially nice since you can make it in advance! adapted from 

1. melt butter in large saucepan , and cook onions , sugar , and thyme slowly until golden , about 30- 45 minutes
2. add mushrooms and saute for about 5 minutes
3. stir in flour and stir until smooth
4. cook for about 2 minutes , stirring constantly
5. add water and stir until it's smooth and well blended
6. add the rest of the ingredients and heat until the soup comes to a boil
7. reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 10- 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: I really liked it. I used low-sodium chicken broth and substituted extra broth for the vermouth. I found that the soup needed more salt and some parsley. It was delicious!

target.recipe_text:
spicy sweet snack mix

this recipe is posted by request.

1. in a large bowl combine the popcorn , pretzels , oyster crackers and pecans
2. in a microwaveable safe bowl combine the brown sugar , butter , cinnamon and cayenne pepper
3. microwave on high for 1 to 1 and 1 / 2 minutes-until butter is well melted and bubbly
4. remove from microwave , mix well and drizzle over popcorn mixture
5. toss well to coat snack piece's
6. allow to cool-pack into jars
target.review: YUM! Made this for my husband to take to work and the both of use ate half of it right away. Very addictive, love the spicy after taste you get. Planning to make some more soon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger spinach casserole

my husband's favourite weekday meal (really i could make it any day of the week, weekend included!). serve with mashed potatoes or over short-cut pasta. adapted from a recipe found on another site. originally posted by micha in az.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. in a non-stick fry pan , soften onion , then brown hamburger
3. add frozen spinach , cover and cook until spinach thaws , scraping spinach as it melts
4. stir in soup , soy sauce , pepper , cajun seasoning and 1 / 3 cup cheese
5. cook until cheese melts , then place in a greased 2-quart casserole
6. sprinkle with the 1 / 4 cup cheese and bread crumbs
7. bake at 400f for about 10 minutes or until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: Simple to make and delicious! Served it over small shell macaroni. Will keep this recipe for sure, Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stir fried garlic beef with broccoli

broccoli and beef just seem to go together. this recipe with garlic just enriches the flavor

1. slice the steak very thinly , the easiest way to do this is to have it half frozen when you slice it
2. put sliced steak in a bowl with the sherry , soy sauce and the cornstarch , and a little salt , let it rest for 20 minutes
3. put 2 tbsp oil in a skillet
4. add garlic , stir fry for 1-2 minutes
5. add mushrooms stir fry 2 minutes
6. remove and keep warm
7. put 2 tbsp of oil in the skillet and stir fry the beef until nicely browned , remove and keep warm
8. add 1 tbsp oil and stir fry the green onions for 1 min , remove and keep warm
9. pour in the chicken stock , heat to bubbling add broccoli cover and steam for 3- 4 minutes
10. remove lid and put all the ingredient together
11. heat through but do not over cook
12. serve over rice or noodles
demonstrations.review: Excellent! I've made this twice and my whole family enjoys this. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smothered chicken italiano

from light & tasty.  will make soon because i love cheese and tomatoes with chicken!!

1. in a small bowl , combine the oregano , garlic powder , 1 / 8 tsp salt and 1 / 8 tsp pepper
2. rub over chicken
3. in a large nonstick skillet coated with nonstick cooking spray , brown chicken in oil for 3-4 minutes on each side
4. transfer to an 11x7 inch baking dish coated with nonstick cooking spray
5. combine ricotta cheese and remaining salt and pepper
6. spoon over chicken
7. top with tomatoes
8. bake , uncovered , at 350f for 15 minutes
9. top with cheese
10. bake 5-10 minutes longer or until cheese is melted and chicken juices run clear
demonstrations.review: I was looking for a change of pace with using chicken breasts. So glad I tried this. Very simple and delicious! A great low carb recipe. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet and spicy sweet potato bake

this is a must at your holiday dinner table, it has just the right balance of sweet and spicy --- cooking time will vary depending on the size you cut the sweet potatoes you will love these!

1. in a resealable plastic bag toss the cubed sweet potatoes with melted butter or oil
2. add the rest of ingredients
3. toss well to coat
4. transfer to a greased baking dish
5. bake uncovered at 400 degrees for about 22-25 minutes , or until sweet potatoes are tender but not too soft
6. delicious !
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! I've made this twice now and love it. Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cassoulet soup

inexpensive and tasty soup based on a french classic. fast and easy to make and everyone always loves it.

1. saut onion and sausage in large saucepan until browned
2. add thyme , stir one minute
3. add wine , boil until slightly reduced , about 2 minutes
4. stir in broth , 1 cup of the beans , and the chicken
5. mash the rest of the beans and add to pot
6. partially cover and simmer for 10 minutes
7. season to taste with salt and pepper , garnish with chopped parsley
demonstrations.review: Very Good! I left out the white wine and added some salt. It was gone fast. Will make this again, thank you!

target.recipe_text:
copycat recipe for carrabba s chicken marsala

a clone dish from carrabba's restaurant. i have not tried this yet, but will soon and add more comments. sounds wonderful!

1. pound chicken breasts to even out thickness and lightly salt and pepper
2. in large skillet , saute chicken in 2 t melted butter until lightly browned , about 2 minutes per side
3. remove from pan and set aside
4. melt remaining butter in pan and add shallots and mushrooms
5. cook until mushrooms are lightly browned
6. add marsala and bring to a boil , scraping browned bits from bottom of pan
7. add cream and lemon juice and return to a boil
8. season with salt and pepper
9. return chicken to pan for about 3 minutes to reheat and finish cooking
10. serve with buttered fettucini
target.review: This dish was simply amazing.. I have several recipes for Chicken Marsala, and honestly this is the only one that I have made twice in one week!!! The only thing different I did was cut the chicken up into nugget size pieces before I cooked, and when I was browning the mushrooms, I added a couple of slices of prosciutto chopped up. It gave it the best flavor!!! I would give more stars if I could!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar meatloaf

i use chili sauce or salsa instead of ketchup to give a nice contrast to the sweetness of the brown sugar.  a lighter version can be made using splenda brown sugar blend, skim milk, and egg beaters. got this one from the allrecipes website. it's one of their most popular recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease a 5x9 inch loaf pan
3. press the brown sugar in the bottom of the prepared loaf pan and spread the ketchup over the sugar
4. in a mixing bowl , mix thoroughly all remaining ingredients and shape into a loaf
5. place on top of the ketchup
6. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until juices are clear
demonstrations.review: This recipe was very good. I only used about a 1/4 cup of brown sugar, and I mixed 1/4 cup of Ketchup with a 1/4 cup of Chili Sauce. I put the brown sugar and sauce on the bottom and the top of the meatloaf, and I ended up having to bake mine for about an hour and a half. The meatloaf held together very well, and was super tasty. My husband (who is a VERY picky eater) loved it! We will be using this for our regular meatloaf recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin layer cheesecake

an easy to make pumpkin cheesecake that tastes great. my wife found this recipe on a box of philadelphia cream cheese.

1. mix together the cream cheese , sugar , and vanilla until well mixed
2. add the eggs and mix well
3. separate one cup of the batter from the rest
4. pour the rest of the batter into the crust
5. mix the pumpkin and spices into the one cup of batter and then pour this onto the rest of the batter in the pie shell
6. bake at 350 degrees for 35 to 40 minutes
7. allow to cool and then refrigerate for at least 3 hours
demonstrations.review: This pie is the best. It is super easy. I have made it three times, and every time I make it, it is gone the same day. With the cream cheese layer you don't even need whipped cream like most people have with plain pumpkin pie. Awesome!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy potato salad

have you ever posted a recipe and just love reading the reviews for it?  this is my signature potato salad.  whenever there is a pot luck function at work, i am told that i have to bring the potato salad.  no one else is allowed to and i am never given a choice.  thank you everyone who ever tried this potato salad and for leaving such glowing reviews for it.  you all have made me look so good.  i personally can not stand eggs or raw onions, so i leave them out but i know most people don't think a potato salad is complete without them.  thanks again for so many wonderful reviews. (psssst....check out my recipe #123107 as well.  it shares the dressing with this recipe but tastes much much different because of the different ingredients) please see recipe #242966 for bacon bit tips.

1. cook potatoes in boiling , salted water until tender
2. drain well
3. peel and cube potatoes
4. transfer to a large bowl
5. add celery , onion , sweet relish and bacon bits
6. combine mayo , sugar , celery seed , vinegar , mustard , and salt
7. add mayo mixture to potatoes
8. toss lightly to coat potato mixture
9. carefully fold in the chopped eggs
10. cover and chill thoroughly
11. bacon bit
12. use a sharp knife and cut the frozen bacon into long strips about 1 / 4 inch wide
13. turn the bacon and cut the strips into pieces also about 1 / 4 in wide
14. you now have perfect raw bacon pieces to fast fry
15. no need to separate
16. they will separate during cooking
17. perfect bacon bits
demonstrations.review: Made this last weekend while camping, and it turned out awesome, everyone loved it! There were no leftovers!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chip butter bites

very easy cookie recipe that doesn't require eggs.  from bev bennet, "30 minute meals for dummies."

1. preheat oven to 350
2. cream butter and sugar
3. blend in salt and vanilla
4. add the flour , 1 / 4 cup at a time , until batter is light
5. stir in chips by hand
6. spoon out batter by1 / 2 teaspoon measure
7. cool into marble-shaped balls and arrange 1" apart on ungreased cookie sheet
8. bake 12-15 minutes or until cookies are fairly browned
demonstrations.review: I followed the recipe exactly, but, they ended up as flaky little flat cookies. I think there wasn't enough flour in the recipe. I liked the flavor, so I will try again using more flour to hold it all together!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oyster crackin s  ranch crackers snack

these are different from the other recipes on zaar for seasoned oyster crackers because they don't include dill and they do include parmesan cheese. my mom always makes these at christmas and they can be very addictive.

1. mix oil , dressing mix and cheese in a large bowl , add crackers and mix well
2. let stand a couple hours , stirring occasionally
3. will store a couple of weeks covered
demonstrations.review: LOVE these!!! I make them at least once a month! Super easy and very tasty!

target.recipe_text:
applesauce  bread

this makes the most moist bread.  i made these in mini loaf pans for gifts one christmas and the were quite popular.  it's also a great way to use your applesauce!

1. cream butter and sugar till light , beat in egg
2. stir in flour , soda , spices , and salt
3. beat in applesauce , then raisins and nuts
4. pour into greased 9 by 5 inch loaf pan
5. bake 350 for 1 hour
6. cool in pan 10 minutes , remove from pan , may sprinkle with powdered sugar
7. makes one loaf
target.review: Loved the bread! Moist, flavorful, and easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus

this recipe was one of my aunt ely's favorite veggy dishes to make for her family. i hope you enjoy it as much as we have.  this recipe is also in my family's cookbook, the one i revised 2 yrs ago for our family reunion.

1. cut off the hard ends first
2. lay asparagus in shallow baking dish
3. drizzle with 2 tablespoons of olive oil
4. 2 teaspoons chopped fresh thyme , 1 / 2 teaspoons salt and 1 / 8 teaspoons of black pepper
5. then roast in a 425 degree f oven for 15 minutes
6. then serve and enjoy
demonstrations.review: This is the fastest asparagus recipe I have ever had.  Very hands off.  The asparagus is outstanding.  My family loves it and we have found a new way to cook asparagus.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marvelous broccoli salad

you may want to make a double batch of this salad. there won't be any left!!

1. combine all ingredients for salad
2. combine dressing ingredients
3. add to salad just before serving and toss
demonstrations.review: This is a nice simple salad that is easy to make. As I was eating it I was thinking that next time I will add slivered almonds. I really don't care for broccoli but mixed with all the ingredients it tasted fine! Will make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no fail easy cake mix brownies

these are similar to a packaged  brownie mix, they have a great brownie texture and take only minutes to make, just dump everything in a bowl, mix and bake! if desired frost with my recipe#89207

1. set oven to 375 degrees
2. grease an 11x7 or a 13x9-inch baking pan
3. in a large bowl using an electric mixer beat all ingredients except walnuts or chocolate chips until smooth
4. add in walnuts of chocolate chips mix to combine
5. spread into the prepared baking dish
6. bake for about 25-30 minutes
7. cool completely before frosting
demonstrations.review: My whole family loved these brownies! We prefer these over the brownie box mix. Thank you for an easy recipe that turns out delish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate chip cranberry oatmeal cookies

i originally made these at the request of my old chorus director john kelleher, who also worked at seattle area starbucks (i think he'd had the combo in a cookie there, once). i was surprised but very pleased they came out so tasty! these days, these are pretty much the only cookies which are requested and i make on a fairly regular basis.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in a large bowl using an electric mixer combine the sugar , brown sugar and butter
3. mix well to cream together
4. add in egg and vanilla extract and mix until combined
5. add the cinnamon , baking soda , salt and flour and mix well
6. fold in the oatmeal , dried cranberries and white chocolate chips- making sure that all ingredients are uniformly distributed
7. roll dough into 1-inch balls and place 3 inches apart onto a greased cookie sheet and bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes , just until the edges are lightly golden
8. remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes on the cookie sheet , then transfer cookies to cooling rack
demonstrations.review: Mmmm...I wish I doubled this recipe, it was great. I liked that I didn't have to use two separate bowls to make these cookies! Very simple basic but super yummy cookies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stove top mac n cheese by alton brown

this is from alton brown's good eats show and it's an easy and good mac n cheese recipe to have on hand. you won't be buying the boxed stuff again after eating this. (edited 8/15/2008 - this was initially posted with 3/4 tsp of dry mustard but after making this a few times i agree with the reviewer that said this amount is too much so i've reduced it to 1/2 tsp.)

1. in a large pot of boiling , salted water cook the pasta to al dente and drain
2. return to the pot and melt in the butter
3. toss to coat
4. whisk together the eggs , milk , hot sauce , salt , pepper , and mustard
5. stir into the pasta and add the cheese
6. over low heat continue to stir for 3 minutes or until creamy
demonstrations.review: Delicious! This is the first recipe that I was able to make mac n cheese successfully! Even my DH who doesn't really care for mac n cheese loved it!

target.recipe_text:
chicken  shrimp and andouille jambalaya

a cajun classic, meal in one pot! have the hot sauce ready to splash on. serve with some crusty french bread, a nice crisp salad, and some of your favorite wine. :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large pan or dutch oven , brown chicken in hot oil on both sides
3. remove and drain
4. add andouille , onion , celery , bell pepper , thyme , oregano , paprika , salt , and cayenne pepper to the pan , cooking and stirring for about 5 minutes until onions are tender
5. add rice , tomatoes with juice , and broth
6. bring to a boil
7. place rice mixture in a baking dish or oven-proof casserole
8. top with chicken
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees f for 40-45 minutes or until rice and chicken are done and tender
10. stir in shrimp , parsley , and green onions
11. cover and cook 5-8 minutes longer or until shrimp curl and turn bright pink and serve
target.review: This Dish was absolutely delicious and easy to prepare. My whole family cleaned their plates. I gave it 4 stars because the rice wasn't cooked all the way so next time i will boil the mixture a little longer. Thank you Sue

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked ziti

good italian comfort food!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. cook ziti according to package directions
3. drain
4. set aside
5. mix ricotta , egg , parsley , 1-1 / 2 cups of the mozarella cheese , and parmesan cheese in a large bowl
6. mix cooked sausage and pasta in with ricotta mixture
7. mix in 3 / 4 jar of sauce
8. transfer mixture into a 2 quart casserole dish
9. top with the rest of the sauce and mozarella cheese
10. bake for 30 to 35 minutes , or until hot and bubbly
11. to freeze: cover dish with foil and freeze
12. when frozen you can pop it out of the container and put in a freezer bag if desired
13. to heat: thaw
14. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
15. cover and bake for 20 minutes
16. uncover and bake for 10-15 minutes more
demonstrations.review: This was a great recipe!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with sausage  tomatoes  and cream

delicious and satisfying... i don't remember where this recipe comes from, but it's a pleaser! easily doubled.  also, works well with gf pasta and sausage

1. heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat
2. add sausage and crushed red pepper
3. cook until sausage is no longer pink , stirring frequently , about 7 minutes
4. add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until onion is tender and sausage is light brown , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
5. add tomatoes , cream , and salt
6. simmer until mixture thickens slightly , about 4 minutes
7. cook pasta in large pot of boiling water
8. drain
9. bring sauce to a simmer
10. add pasta to sauce and cook until pasta is heated through and sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 2 minutes
11. divide pasta between plates
12. sprinkle with parsley
13. serve , passing parmesan separately
demonstrations.review: I tried this recipe tonight and for some reason it didnt turn out well. I followed the recipe as written but it had no flavor although it did smell good while cooking. Wont try again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I made this tonight and OMG it was delicious even my 5 year old loved it and my son said it should be a dish at olive garden. Definitely will be making this again maybe with mushrooms and fresh tomatoes. Thanks for sharing. just to add i just had this reheated today and it was even better

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach and bacon quiche

an easy and delicious quiche. this comes courtesy of paula deen & her show on televion food network, 2003.

1. preheat the oven to 375f
2. combine the eggs , cream , salt and pepper in food processor or blender
3. layer the spinach , bacon and cheese in the bottom of the pie crust
4. the pour egg mixture on top
5. bake for 35-40 minutes until the egg mixture is set
6. cut into 8 wedges and serve
demonstrations.review: this recipe was very delicious i was scared of the swiss cheese but so happy i didnt change it...the kids had seconds...i will be making this again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my sister s sweet potato bread

this is my sister barb's recipe. it is the first thing i ever made for my husband when we first met and he flipped over it. he ate a whole loaf driving home from my house!

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees
2. in a large mixing bowl , combine sugar , oil , egg , sweet potatoes and vanilla
3. in a separate bowl , mix dry ingredients together well and add to wet ingredients
4. stir until just combined
5. fold in walnuts
6. pour into 2 standard loaf pans
7. bake for 75 minutes or until thin knife inserted in center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: This bread was not good to my family and friends at all and i followed the recipe exactly as it is written so i'm not sure if i made an error or what.

target.recipe_text:
taco bell taco seasoning clone copycat

this copycat recipe is on many websites, but wasn't on zaar, so i posted it. better than those storebought packages.

1. combine and store in an air-tight container
2. add seasoning mix and 3 / 4 cup of water
3. bring to a boil then reduce heat
4. simmer uncovered , 10 minutes , stirring occasionally
target.review: DH and I both enjoyed this.  He noticed I switched something but couldn't figure it out and said the switch was neither better nor worse than what he's used to.  I found this mix to be mild in the "spicy" category which is what I prefer.  I'm personally kind of sensitive to Cumin and find it can be overpowering in many recipes but not so with this mix.  With that said, I can take lots of "heat" and think I will use a Medium Hot Chili Powder next time.  All in all, a good mix and one I'll keep.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetable pancakes

paula deen's recipe for these vegetable pancakes are by far the best i have ever had

1. in a mixing bowl stir together the flour , baking powder , salt and pepper
2. in another bowl , beat together the egg , milk , carrots , zucchini , and onions
3. add this to the dry ingredients and stir until combined
4. using a large skillet , heat 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat
5. pour the batter by tablespoons into the pan , making a few pancakes at a time
6. cook about 2 minutes on each side and golden brown
7. add the remaining oil to the pan as needed
8. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: DH really enjoyed these with dinner last night but I thought they were just a tad flat.  I have a couple left over and might put them back in a hot skillet to reheat and serve with some hot sauce.  Otherwise, they were very easy to make, held together beautifully and made a nice presentation.  I'll make these again but will try adding something for a more zippy flavor (maybe some finely chopped jalapeno or some cayenne pepper).  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian style cucumber salad

a quick and easy asian style salad - nice and light, with a little kick!

1. trim ends off cucumber and cut into 1 inch chunks
2. combine rice vinegar with soy sauce , vegetable oil , sesame oil , salt , sugar , hot chili paste and garlic
3. mix dressing with cucumbers and serve at room temperature
demonstrations.review: This was really yummy!  We don't care much for Sesame Oil and even though I thought I had some apparently I threw it out so that was ommitted.  I also added some of those crunchy Chinese Noodles because I like them.  The flavors blended nicely and DH and I agreed it would probably be good with thinly sliced onion.  Next time I will let it marinate a bit as I served it almost immediately.  Very tasty side dish!  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon apple coleslaw

from the february 2005 issue of southern living. posted in response to a request. cooking time is chilling time.

1. combine cabbage , apples , and carrots in a large bowl
2. whisk together mayonnaise and next 6 ingredients
3. toss with cabbage mixture
4. cover and chill 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I've been making this recipe for a couple of years now.  It's my Go-To slaw recipe during the summer months.  The lemon is so refreshing and adds such a lightness to a dish that can sometimes seem heavy with mayonnaise and sugar.  You can't go wrong with this one!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I'm almost embarassed to post this review because it has gotten so many high ratings but it just didn't work for us.  It's everything we love and we were very surprised to find that it really fell flat and did not meet our expectations at all.  If I do this one again I may leave out the corn and add some chipotle peppers and/or adobe sauce.  But thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s apple brine

i adopted this recipe from mean chef. "mild brine for turkey, chicken or pork."

1. bring apple juice , sugar and salt to a boil over high heat , skim foam , let cool to room temperature
2. add remaining ingredients
3. brine turkey for 24 hours
4. quantity is sufficient for a 14 pound turkey
demonstrations.review: This is the same recipe I've used for the past two years.  If you're short on fridge space, like we always are, we fill a cooler half way with ice and place a clean and sterilized 5 gallon paint bucket inside ($5 at the hardware store) then pack any empty spaces with remaining ice.  Once the brine is cooled pour it in the bucket and put the bird in.  I weight the bird down with a small landscape stone that is double bagged in ziplocks then cover the bucket with aluminum foil to keep out any dust.
