Works like a charm everytime and everything is still very cold the next day.  You will have the most beautiful, juicy bird you've ever had and literally tons of drippings for gravy.  No more fighting over the gravy boat, promise!

target.recipe_text:
stuffed pecan pie french toast

i have many versions of french toast, but i have to say this is one of my favorites. so easy to make and tastes great. the pecans give it a nice crunch and the bread stays moist. it's like eating pecan pie for breakfast. yummy! easy to double for more hearty eaters...

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. heat butter and brown sugar to a boil in small saucepan over medium heat
3. remove from heat and stir in pecans
4. set aside
5. grease a baking sheet with butter
6. place the bread slices on the baking sheet
7. bake for 5 minute or until lightly toasted
8. remove from sheet and set aside
9. beat milk , eggs , granulated sugar and vanilla in medium bowl
10. dip 8 slices toast into the batter and place on baking sheet
11. spread a heaping tablespoons of the pecan mixture onto each
12. dip remaining slices toast into batter and place over nut filling to form a sandwich
13. bake for 20 minute or until hot
14. sift confectioners' sugar over toast
15. serve immediately
target.review: I can't say enough good things about this recipe. I make it every weekend - it's a HUGE hit in our house! I've used the rasien bread, regular bread and homemade bread - it's all amazing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate martini

this is served at the bar in the tides hotel, south beach, miami, fl. incredible.

1. wet the rim of a chilled martini glass with water , then dip the rim in cocoa powder
2. in a cocktail shaker half filled with ice , add the vodka and creme de cacao
3. shake vigorously and pour into the martini glass
4. drop a hershey's kiss into the glass and top with a splash of godiva chocolate liqueur
demonstrations.review: I made this for Valentines Day and it was delicious! Loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
legal seafood style baked scallops

whenever we get back to the boston area, it's a priority to to have a meal at legal seafoods.  i recently "re-discovered" this recipe buried in old newspaper clippings. i had tried to recreate it in the past but now know i was missing the most important ingredient - buttermilk. i made it again after posting the recipe so i have edited the original description. it's even better than i remembered, you might want to try just a dash (or more) of cayenne pepper. it's delightful !

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. place scallops in a bowl , season with salt and pepper , add thyme and buttermilk and toss to coat
3. place scallops , with buttermilk , evenly in the bottom of an oven proof dish , sprinkle with cracker crumbs and top with melted butter
4. bake for 20 minutes , squeeze lemon over scallops and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I followed the recipe exactly and it was amazing! I love scallops and these were the best I've ever had!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome chocolate butterscotch chip cookies

these are delicious cookies and easy to make. something a little different from regular chocolate chip! they also freeze well.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. combine butter and sugar and beat until fluffy add egg and vanilla and mix very well
3. gradually add flour , salt and baking soda while mixing until smooth
4. stir in chips by hand
5. drop by teaspoonfuls on lightly greased baking sheet
6. bake until just browned approximately 10-13 minutes
7. watch them closely near the end to prevent butterscotch chips from burning !
demonstrations.review: Excellent cookies! I didn't use butterscotch chips and used all semi-sweet chocolate chips instead. They turned out perfectly - thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted parmesan garlic cauliflower

yummy and different way to prepare cauliflower. a must try! number of servings is a guess.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. grease large casserole dish
3. place olive oil and garlic in large resealable bag
4. add cauliflower and shake to mix
5. pour into prepared casserole dish
6. bake for 20 to 25 minutes , stirring halfway through
7. top with parmesan and parsley and broil for 3 to 5 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Loved this. I burned the cheese accidently but it was still good. Can't wait to make this one again - thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
burritos  black bean

since beans and rice together make a complete protein (http://www.vegez.com/shopper/beans.asp), this recipe is great for breakfast.  it make a lot and is good to have on hand for ready-made meals from the refrigerator or freezer.  it is adapted from breaking the food seduction: the hidden reasons behind food cravings---and 7 steps to end them naturally.

1. soak beans overnight , if using dried
2. cook beans , if using dried
3. cook brown rice
4. heat water and oil in a large saucepan
5. when hot , add onion and saute until soft
6. add bell pepper , garlic , and cumin and cook 2 minutes more , adding more water , if necessary to prevent sticking
7. stir in beans , mushrooms , tomatoes , and salsa
8. cook about 10 minutes , until mushrooms are soft
9. warm the amount of lavash breads or tortillas you are using
10. add rice and pepper , hot sauce , and salt or tamari
11. spoon onto the lavash or tortilla , allowing room for rolling into the burrito shape
12. freeze any filling you won't use by the end of the week in individual portions
demonstrations.review: This was really good. It was a lot of work, but our family really enjoyed it. Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
puerto rican pork a la criolla

this is a really flavorful roast pork, with lots of garlic and black pepper. it doesn't require overnight prep, just about 5 minutes of seasoning and an hour and a half in the oven. leftovers make great sandwiches!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. combine pepper , garlic , oregano , vinegar , olive oil and salt in a small bowl , then rub this mixture all over the pork roast
3. place roast in a shallow baking pan and roast , uncovered , at 350 degrees f for about 1-1 / 2 hours
4. meat thermometer should read 165 to 170 degrees f
5. remove from oven and let rest 10 minutes before slicing
target.review: Very flavorful roast, loved the simplicity of the rub.  Easy to make but bursting with flavor.  I only had a 1.80 pound roast, but I still used the amount of spices called for a 3 pound roast.  I would never have thought to use cider vinegar, so glad you posted this.  Thanks, Crabzilla

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zingy rice casserole

this one-pot meal could be a side dish, or it could be a meal on its own.

1. in a large and deep frying pan , cook sausage , cumin , garlic , green peppers and onions , stirring often
2. drain any excess fat
3. dissolve bouillon cube in water and add to skillet
4. stir in jalapenos and rice , bringing to a boil
5. reduce heat and simmer , uncovered , until water is absorbed and rice is cooked , about 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I'm giving this recipe 5 stars even though I did not use the sausage and I halved it for two people.  I was very concerned that the onions and peppers would be too much, but my worries were unfounded.  This made a scrumptions side dish to my London Broil and sauteed yellow squash, carrots and green beans.  I used two cloves of garlic and one whole large jalepeno (I'm sick, I admit it, we all know I like it "hot").  This is a keeper and it's a recipe that you can play around with to suit your tastes.  You could throw in some red bell pepper, a little celery, whatever suits your tastes.  Thanks Sackville!!!  Superb in my book.  Crabby

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous greek salad

be prepared for the best greek salad on the planet! --- plan ahead the dressing needs at least 2 or more hours to blend the flavors, i sometimes add in 1/4 cup parmesan cheese to the dressing for a more cheesy dressing, all amounts may be adjusted to taste ----  to marinade the salad allow to sit at room temperature before serving, see bottom of instructions --- you will find this and many more of my recipes posted here http://kittencalskitchen.com/2009/04/13/kittens-famous-greek-salad/  ---also see my recipe #359292

1. for the dressing
2. in a processor or use a wire whisk process / whisk the olive oil with lemon juice , 2 teaspoons dried oregano , garlic , dried , basil , red wine vinegar , salt and sugar until smooth
3. season with black pepper
4. chill in fridge for a couple of hours before using to blend flavors
5. place the salad ingredients in a large bowl
6. pour dressing over
7. toss to combine
8. if desired allow the salad to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving , or you can refrigerate for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Really enjoyed this, however, I did add twice the amount of vinegar called for simply cause we love our dressings more vinegary than most.  Thanks for posting, will definitely make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s onion patties latkes

i have been making these for over 20 years, i usually get about 15 patties but it depends on the size of the batter that you drop in the pan, these are better if fried to very brown and crispy, you can make a double recipe, fry them then freeze them on a tray then pop them into freezer bags, then just warm them in the oven to crisp up, they are very addicting and i can tell you i eat half before they even get to the table lol!  if you plan on doubling the recipe then make two separate recipes in two bowls, i have doubled the recipe into one bowl and for some reason they just are not as good ---  if desired you could add in a slightly beaten large egg and reduce the milk by 1/4 cup --- you will *love* these!  also see my
recipe#186700 *and*
recipe#244592

1. chop the onions finely then place into a bowl
2. in another large bowl mix together the flour , sugar , baking powder , seasoning salt , cayenne , garlic powder and a small amount of black pepper
3. mix to combine well
4. add in the milk and whisk until thoroughly combined
5. add in the chopped onions and green onions and mix with a wooden spoon until combined
6. in a large non-stick frypan , heat a small amount of oil to medium-hot , adding in more oil as needed as the patties will absorb too much oil if you add in a large amount of oil at one time
7. drop the batter from a tablespoon into about 1 / 2-inch of hot oil
8. flatten slightly with the spoon or spatula
9. sprinkle with a little salt
10. fry until crispy and brown on both sides
demonstrations.review: Very tasty, we really enjoyed these.  Thanks for sharing!  Crabby

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory potato bake

this recipe is an internet find and the delicious flavor surpassed my expectations. try to use potatoes of equal size if possible for best results.

1. butter a 9 x 9 inch baking dish
2. cook potatoes whole in boiling salted water until tender
3. drain and let cool
4. preheat oven to 375f
5. in the same pan as you boiled the potatoes in , saute onion in butter over medium heat until tender and golden , about 5 minutes
6. stir in all of the flour and the pepper , mixing well
7. add the water and the bouillon cube and bring to a boil
8. boil for one minute , stirring
9. remove from heat
10. whisk in all of the mustard and the horseradish
11. slice the potatoes 1 / 2 inch thick , and layer them in the baking dish
12. cover the potatoes with the sauce and sprinkle with the bread crumbs
13. bake for 15 to 20 minutes , until hot and bubbly
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this recipe.  It is very simple to prepare and has a great taste.  I was a little leary about the mustard but it turned out just fine.  I made everything ahead of time and put the bread crumbs on at the last minute.  I used packaged Progresso plain bread crumbs and I think that homemade would be much better.  Thanks for a keeper and thanks FlemishMinx for responding so quickly to my question!  PS:  We're in the 1960/Champions area.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan chili corn on the cob

roast this one on the grill!  it's awesome!

1. husk the corn
2. spread with mayonnaise
3. sprinkle with chili powder and parmesan cheese
4. wrap in foil
5. roast on the grill until cooked
6. when it's roasted , spread with butter and sprinkle with salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: Just love it!!  I would never have thought of using mayo, but it adds a nice touch, I also used some cayenne pepper, a keeper for sure!  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
strawberry coffee cake

good for a special occasion breakfast.

1. in a mixing bowl , add the flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
2. stir to mix
3. in a second bowl , add the egg , milk and butter
4. stir to mix
5. add to dry ingredients and stir just until moistened
6. pour mixture into a greased 8-inch square baking dish
7. place strawberries evenly over the top of batter
8. to make the topping: combine the flour and sugar in a bowl
9. with a pastry blender , cut in the butter until consistency of coarse crumbs
10. stir in pecans
11. sprinkle mixture evenly over the strawberries
12. bake at 375 for 30-35 minutes or until wooden pick comes out clean
target.review: Definately 5 stars!!!  I was actually looking for a recipe for the last of my fresh-picked strawberries.  Instead of the usual strawberry cake,  I thought this coffee cake really sounded good. Although somewhat apprehensive about baked strawberries, I decided to try something different after reading the many reviews.  Very easy to make,  very moist with a crunchy topping, and very delicious!!!  My co-workers said it was awesome.  I substituted walnuts for the pecans, and doubled the recipe for a 9x13" pan which I baked for about 40 minutes.  After cooling,  I drizzled a powdered sugar glaze (1/3 cup powdered sugar, 1/4 tsp vanilla, and 1-2 tsps. milk) .   I will make this recipe again!! Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rich and chewy low fat brownies

amazingly rich and chewy, you would never know these are low fat.  i have people asking me for this recipe whenever i make it.  the applesauce is the secret ingredient in these delicious brownies!  one suggestion i have to make them fudgier is to use a very high quality cocoa.  i usually use watkins or epicure selections and found a big difference from that and the kind you can buy in the store.  it makes them a real dark chocolate in the middle and they are rich and chewy!  this recipe also doubles well and will fit into a 9x13 pan.

1. cream butter and sugar in a large bowl using a hand mixer
2. add egg whites , applesauce and vanilla
3. mix all other ingredients in a separate smaller bowl and add to the wet ingredients in the large bowl
4. do not overmix !
5. spray 8x8 dish with pam and bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is a good brownie considering it is low fat. However, I could detect a subtle taste of the applesauce which was off-putting. I also decreased the amount of sugar to 1 1/2 cups . I would make this recipe again, but as another reviewer suggested, I will try adding some mini-chocolate chips to enhance the chocolate flavor of a brownie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fantastic twinkie refrigerator strawberry shortcake

plan ahead this needs to chill for a minimum of 2 hours before serving, purchase the ready-made glaze for this, if you like a lot of cream topping then use a 12-ounce container of cool whip topping, 16 servings is only estimated i can eat this whole cake myself lol! --- see note on bottom for a thinner twinkie crust -- you will *love* this! :)

1. prepare a 13 x 9-inch pan
2. mix the strawberry slices with the glaze
3. chill until ready to use
4. place the whole twinkies into the bottom of the pan , pressing down slightly
5. in a bowl using an electric mixer at medium speed beat softened cream cheese with condensed milk until smooth
6. fold in the 8-ounce container using a spatula until combined
7. spread the cream cheese mixture over the twinkies
8. spoon the berries over the cream cheese mixture
9. cover with plastic wrap and chill for a minimum of 2 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: Too sweet :-(

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swanson quick chicken   vegetable stir fry

i have been making this for years. got it off a can of something swanson.

1. in bowl mix cornstarch , broth , soy and ginger until smooth
2. set aside
3. in medium skillet over medium heat , heat oil
4. add vegetables and stir-fry until tender-crisp
5. stir cornstarch mixture and add
6. cook until mixture boils and thickens , stirring constantly
7. add chicken and heat through
8. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: Quick and easy with ingredients I had on hand. I added 1/2 tsp minced garlic and  cut up chicken tenders that I had previously cooked.  I did add a bit more water to thin the sauce as it cooked for a thinner sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
better homes and gardens banana bread

from the better homes and gardens red plaid cookbook.  the best banana bread out there!  i always add some cinnamon sugar on top before baking, which adds a subtle but delicious difference.  makes a yummy, crispy top crust! try it... you won't be disappointed!

1. grease the bottom and 1 / 2 inch up the sides of an 8x4x2-inch loaf pan
2. set aside
3. in a medium mixing bowl combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , cinnamon , and salt
4. make a well in the center of the dry mixture and set aside
5. in another bowl combine egg , bananas , sugar , cooking oil , and lemon peel
6. add egg mixture all at once to dry mixture
7. stir just until moistened
8. fold in nuts if desired
9. spoon batter into the prepared pan
10. sprinkle with some cinnamon sugar
11. bake in a 350 degree oven 50-55 minutes or till a wooden toothpick inserted near center comes out clean
12. cool in pan on a wire rack for 10 minutes
13. remove loaf from pan and cool on rack
demonstrations.review: I have used this banana bread recipe for many years. I also reduce the amount of sugar to about a 1/2 - 2/3 cup. Before baking, I sometimes sprinkle the top with a few walnuts instead of mixing them into the batter. I lightly press the nuts onto the top of the batter with the back of a spoon so they will stick to the bread as it is baking. This recipe is flavorful and moist with minimal vegetable oil as some other quick bread recipes call for. This recipe is deserving of its 5 star rating!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brownie mallow bars

nan

1. prepare brownie batter according to package directions for fudge-like brownies
2. pour into a greased 13x9 inch baking pan
3. bake at 350f for 28-30 minutes
4. top with marshmallows bake 3 minutes longer
5. cool on wire rack
6. in a saucepan , combine the chocolate chips , peanut butter and butter
7. cook and stir over low heat , stir in cereal
8. spread over brownies
9. refrigerate 1-2 hours or until firm before cutting
demonstrations.review: So sweet and rich.... cut into small squares!!   I decreased the chocolate chips to 1 1/2 cups.  I also used 1/2 milk chocolate and 1/2 semi-sweet chocolate chips.  The taste of the chocolate chip and rice cereal mixture seemed to over power the brownie and marshamallow layers.  I would make these bars again.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot caramelized onion pot roast

this is one of our favorite recipes for crock pot roast. it's easy and a little different than the usual crock pot roasts. i got the recipe off the internet and i wish i could thank the original poster for a great recipe!

1. brown the meat , remove from frying pan to plate
2. add oil to pan and cook onions until brown
3. add broth , juice , brown sugar , vinegar and mustard to onions in pan
4. put half of the onion mixture in crock pot and place the roast on top
5. cover with the rest of the onions
6. cook on low 8 to 9 hours
target.review: What a wonderful rich tasting roast!  I also did mine in the oven (300 degrees for about 4 hrs.)  I thickened the gravy at the end, great the next day for sandwiches.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn puffs caramel corn

a favorite in this household.  so addicting!!!
o-keedoke carries this kind of cornpuff.

1. place corn puffs in a large roasting pan
2. cook together butter , brown sugar , corn syrup for two minutes , stirring constantly
3. add baking soda to the mix
4. this will cause the mixture to foam so make sure you use a 2 quart saucepan
5. pour caramel mixture over corn puffs and stir until mixed
6. place in a 250 degree oven for 45 minutes
7. stir at least every 10-15 minutes
8. remove from oven and pour on wax paper and break apart
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: These are so good.  My sister has been making this for years and it is truly adicting to eat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potluck broccoli salad

this salad is perfect for summer bbq's and potlucks.  it is sweet and tangy.

1. cut broccoli into small pieces
2. dice green onions
3. crumble crisp bacon
4. add all other ingredients for the salad
5. combine all ingredients for the dressing in a separate bowl and whisk until smooth
6. pour dressing over salad just before serving
demonstrations.review: This is one of my favorite salads to take along.  It is simple to make and there is never any left over.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bountiful harvest  shake n bake  fruit pie filling

got a bushel or two of peaches, apples, berries, etc? oamc!!! a fresh fruit ready (home)made pie filling that you simply defrost, pour into pie crust and bake for wonderful pies, cobblers, etc. great for gift giving also. i've done this tequnique for years and it's always been a no fail recipe. this recipe multiplies easily so double, triple, etc. away depending on how much fruit you have to use.

1. to the ziploc bag , add all ingredients to bag except fruit
2. mix well , then add the fruit
3. blend well by tossing , shaking , and gently kneading the bag until all the fruit is coated
4. careful as not to bruise the fruit
5. place flat in the freezer
6. repeat and stack in freezer till your bounty is used up
7. when ready , just place into a pie crust , lay top crust over , and bake as a frozen pie
8. to bake: take out a bag of fruit filling and thaw on counter
9. when thawed , pour filling into pie crust
10. top with additional crust if using
11. preheat oven to 400f bake for about 40 minutes or until top crust is golden brown
12. place on rack to cool
demonstrations.review: What a great recipe!  I tried this last year and I am using it again this year.  I buy big bags of "deer apples" in the fall (apples that have hit the ground in the orchards and they can't sell as perfects so the sell them as deer feed) much cheaper than in the stores and I make my pie filling and applesauce from them as they get cut up anyway. Around here deer apples sell for about $7.00 for 25 - 30#.  Anyhow this filling is very good... I add a little more cinnemon and nutmeg along with some mace to mine.  Thanks for sharing this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon cheesecake bars   caren s variation on alabamagirl71 s

i made alabamagirl71's recipe (#51329) for lemon cheesecake bars and asked for feedback from my friends.  this is the recipe i developed, which is really only a minor variation on the original (thicker cheesecake layer and more graham cracker crumbles on top).

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. prepare 13x9-inch baking pan by spraying with non-stick cooking spray
3. combine graham cracker crumbs , pecans , sugar , and melted butter
4. mix well
5. reserve 1 / 2 cup crumb mixture
6. press the rest into a 13x9-inch baking pan
7. bake for 8 minutes
8. allow to cool
9. while the crust is cooling , beat cream cheese until it's fluffy
10. gradually beat in the sweetened condensed milk
11. add eggs until mixture is just combined
12. add the lemon juice and vanilla and mix until just combined
13. pour mixture into prepared crust
14. sprinkle the reserved crumb mixture over the top of the cheesecake layer
15. bake for about 50 minutes
16. cool for about 1 1 / 2 hours , then cut into bars
17. store in your refrigerator
demonstrations.review: Very good cheesecake and so easy to make.  I did add the zest of one of the lemons just to amp up the taste.  Everyone loved it and asked for the recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
holiday dinner rolls 2016   walker style

i make these with "after-dinner turkey sandwiches" in mind - my family's favorite part of the day. so, i roll them out, cut with a large cookie cutter or drinking glass, dip in melted butter and fold in half, filing the cookie sheet.  raise to double size and bake until golden. brush with butter & pile on the leftovers!

1. use 1 / 2 c of the warm water to soften yeast
2. sprinkle with a little bit of sugar to help the yeast work
3. combine all other wet ingredients in mixing bowl
4. add flour a cup at a time , along with softened yeast until dough is soft
5. mix with dough hook
6. dough will just barely stick to your fingers
7. remove from bowl and roll out the dough on floured surface
8. cut with large , round cookie cutter , dip in melted butter , fold over and place on lightly greased cookie sheet , just touching each other
9. let rise until doubled
10. makes about 2 dozen
11. bake at 350 degrees for 12 minutes
12. remove from oven and brush tops with butter
13. cool on wire rack , if they last that long
14. serve right out of the oven , if you can time it right !
demonstrations.review: These are terrific!  I don't use a bread machine so I mixed them in my KitchenAid, let rise once then formed into rolls and let them raise again.  I did add some dried minced onion to the second batch I made and it added a nice flavor.  We didn't think these were too sweet ,just plain delicious.

target.recipe_text:
bisquick buttermilk pie  half recipe

i ate this in a local restaraunt and asked a 'connection' there for the recipe. i couldn't believe how easy it was. and how fattening!! omg! *lol* but, they put it on their buffet and it's always gone. it's very good .. no crust! kind of a custardy, pudding type dish. i guess this was on the bisquick box years and years ago. don't look at the calorie count and enjoy!!! ;-) (by the way, the recipe i'm posting is half ... to fit into a 13x9 pan instead of the buffet pans!)

1. mix all ingredients until smooth
2. pour into a sprayed 13x9 pan
3. bake at 350 until the top cracks and is golden brown
4. approx 70 minutes
5. is best to monitor instead of relying on the time
6. it's not always done in the same amount of time for me
7. you want it to jiggle a bit and not be too dark brown on top
8. enjoy
target.review: This was wonderful!  My family wooed and aughed!  Wow-and so easy!  I love buttermilk pie-and this one is great!!!  Thank you for sharing this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy baked shrimp

yummmmmmy!! spicy, so have plenty of cold beverages around.

1. combine first 7 ingredients
2. layer shrimp and lemon slices in a 13x9 inch baking dish
3. top with sauce
4. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes or until shrimp turn pink , stirring once
5. remove shrimp , reserving sauce
6. serve shrimp with reserved sauce and french bread
demonstrations.review: This was great! I also doubled the garlic.  I served this with roasted asparagus, yukon gold potatoes and baguette bread.  This would be a nice valentines day dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry pretzel jell o

a crisp salty pretzel crust complements the creamy marshmallow-fluff-like "white" layer, with a  tangy topping of strawberries in gelatin. much like a strawberry cheesecake, but with the surprise of pretzels!  for best results, make strawberry pretzel jell-o only one day in advance, to preserve the  crunchy texture of the pretzels.

1. crust: combine pretzels , butter , and 1 / 4 cup sugar
2. press into 9" x 13" baking dish and bake at 350 for 10 minutes
3. cool to room temperature
4. white layer: cream together cream cheese and 1 cup sugar
5. fold in cool whip
6. spread over pretzel crust
7. red layer: dissolve gelatin in boiling water
8. stir in frozen strawberries , chill until partially set and spread over white layer
9. chill until set and serve
demonstrations.review:
This is a great summer dessert. I love the salty/sweet mix. I guessed at the amount of cool whip to add. Also, next time I will crush my pretzels a little more than I did.
Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ellen s yummy pasta salad

this recipe can be played with. you can use all, or just a few of the vegetables. choice of pasta goes the same. i even tried it with tortollini and it was delicious. i just suggest that you do not substitute on the dressing and salad seasoning. i have given out this recipe before and have to stress that since many did not use those. using an assortment of peppers is great for the color.

1. cook and drain pasta of your choice according to package directions
2. drain and rinse with cold water
3. may also place in an ice water bath
4. toss pasta with 1 / 2 bottle salad seasoning , or to your taste
5. add chopped veggies and dressing
6. chill for at least 2 hours before seving
demonstrations.review: I love this pasta.  It has the perfect blend of flavors.  I like it best with Penne pasta.  Next time instead of buying the seasoning that goes in it I will use the salad supreme seasoning recipe (#24917) in it!  Thanks for sharing this great pasta salad dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pernil  puerto rican pork shoulder

this is a delicious way to cook pork.  i got this recipe from my boyfriend who is from puerto rico. this also makes excellent, moist meat for cuban sandwiches.

1. wash the pork shoulder
2. with a sharp knife , make 1 inch deep cuts into the pork
3. with mortar and pestle crush garlic , oregano and black pepper together
4. add olive oil , vinegar and salt
5. mix well
6. spoon some of the garlic mixture inside the small cuts around the pork , and spread remaining mixture all over the pork
7. place pork in an aluminum turkey pan
8. cover with aluminum foil tightly
9. refrigerate at least 8 hours
10. bake in pre-heated 325 degree fahrenheit oven for about 5 to 6 hours
11. remove aluminum foil and bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for another hour or until skin is crisp
12. closely watch this so you don't burn the skin
13. pork should be well-done and tender
demonstrations.review: This was excellent.  I had a 3 lb pork shoulder.  I used about 8 cloves of garlic (minced), and kept the rest of the ingredient amounts the same (used sea salt).  I cooked it 3 hours at 325 degrees and uncovered it and cooked it one hour more.  It was so tender and juicy and bursting with flavor!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern stuffed bell peppers

simple preparation & delicious taste! use a mixture of red, green, yellow & orange peppers for a colourful presentation. recipe #2642 instead of store-bought taco seasoning mix--it makes this dish even better!

1. combine beef , onion , seasoning mix and egg in a large bowl
2. add rice and mix well
3. cut peppers in half lengthwise
4. remove seeds and membrane
5. spread tomatoes on the bottom of an ovenproof 12 x 9 inch baking dish
6. the liquid from the tomatoes will reduce during cooking so if you like lots of sauce , add about a cup of water
7. this also helps make the peppers softer
8. place peppers , cut side up , on top of the tomatoes
9. spoon beef mixture into peppers , mounding as necessary
10. top each pepper with salsa
11. bake in preheated 375f oven for 40-45 minutes or until beef is cooked thoroughly and peppers are soft
12. cover each pepper with cheese and return to oven , under the broiler , until the cheese melts- less than a minute , so watch carefully !
13. serve with sour cream and additional salsa
demonstrations.review: These were great!  I made as directed but I used spaghetti sauce instead of diced tomatoes.  My husband loves stuffed peppers and he said these were the best that he has ever had.

target.recipe_text:
foolproof standing prime rib roast  paula deen

this is from paula deen of food tv and is what i fixed for christmas dinner 2005.  i was tempted to open the oven to check how things were going, but i resisted...waiting until it had cooked 40 minutes at the final stage of cooking.  i had a 9+ pound roast and the final temperature at that point was 129°f.  it was wonderful!  i'd definitely cook it the same way again.  see recipe #57340 for seasoning.

1. allow roast to stand at room temperature for at least 1 hour
2. preheat the oven to 375f
3. rub roast with house seasoning
4. place roast on a rack in the pan with the rib side down and the fatty side up
5. roast for 1 hour
6. turn off oven
7. leave roast in oven but do not open oven door for 2-3 hours
8. about 30 to 40 minutes before serving time , turn oven to 375f and reheat the roast
9. important: do not remove roast or re-open the oven door from time roast is put in until ready to serve
10. cover with foil and let stand for 15 minutes before cutting
11. cook it rare
12. if anyone wants it done medium , dip their slice in a pot of simmering au jus for 1 minute
target.review: I made this last night with a 6.5 rib roast in a gas oven. I cooked it an hour, left it in for 3 hours and then cooked it another 30 mins and it turned out medium rare. Perfectly cooked and melt in your mouth delicious!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet potato  yam  casserole with marshmallows

this is a compilation of a couple of different recipes i found on the web. my husband loves sweet potatoes with lots of marshmallows and wanted a casserole like one of his aunts used to make. after a few trials, this was the final incarnation. it is now a thanksgiving staple for both his and my family's dinners.

1. spray 1 quart baking dish with pam
2. heat oven to 350 degrees
3. mash yams in a large bowl and add brown sugar , salt , cinnamon , egg , and melted butter
4. mix well
5. place 1 / 2 mixture in baking dish
6. top with a layer of marshmallows , then add remaining mixture
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. remove from oven and top with remaining marshmallows
9. turn oven to broil and move casserole to the upper middle rack
10. broil for approximately 5 minutes or until marshmallows are lightly browned
demonstrations.review: This was delicious!  I made it for Thanksgiving and everyone loved it.  I goofed and used a 29oz can of sweet potatoes thinking I was supposed to have 30oz.  The only thing I changed was the amount of marshmallows.  I didnt put the middle layer in because I thought it would be too sweet and it came out perfect!  The next time I used the 40oz can of sweet potatoes and it came out good also but I almost think I prefer the smaller can.  I love how the marshmallows puff up and get really chewy.  My dh is away for 3 weeks so last night I made this just for myself, comfort food. Awesome dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy mashed potato casserole

oh so good and so easy! a favorite at our home!

1. cook potatoes in boiling water until tender
2. drain
3. mash
4. stir in cream cheese , sour cream , onions , melted butter , salt , garlic powder and pepper
5. place in a 2-quart casserole dish
6. sprinkle with paprika and dot with butter
7. bake , uncovered , at 375 for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was absolutely delicious!!! I only made a few changes.  I added sauteed onions instead of green onions because thats all I had.  Then I added shredded cheese to the top and then sprinkled french's french fried onions on top.  I baked it for 15 mins, until the onions got brown, turned the oven off and left it in for the other 15 mins so they wouldnt burn.  WOW!  It was awesome!!!! There was only 2 of us and we ate 3/4 of the whole thing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raw brownies

i found this recipe online and really wanted to try it. it comes from a website called 28 cooks. you may substitute the dates and cherries for other dried fruits. the cooking time is freezing time.

1. process all ingredients in a food processor or blender
2. press into a small square baking pan and freeze for 1 hour
3. slice brownies into 12 pieces
4. store in fridge
demonstrations.review: These were really delicious!  I am just switching to raw foods and I have to say they were very surprising.  They had just enough tartness in the cherries and sweetness in the dates and honey.  I used cocoa and honey.  Im not real fond of carob. Thanks for a great raw dessert!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kwick kielbasa hash

kall me the kielbasa kween! my polish genes are responsible for my love of polish sausage.

1. in 10-inch skillet melt butter until sizzling add potatoes and onion
2. cook over medium-high heat , stirring occasionally , until potatoes are lightly browned
3. add sausage and continue cooking , stirring occasionally , until sausage is heated through
4. stir in cheese and serve
demonstrations.review: This was awesome!  I did double it like one person suggested and I am glad I did.  The only thing I did different was use the o'brien potatoes with onion and green peppers.  Thats all they had at the store.  I still added the onion and it was delicious!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brussels sprouts in garlic butter

this is a recipe from joy of cooking... totally changed my mind about brussels sprouts! it's imperative that you use fresh sprouts, the texture would be way off with the frozen ones.

1. melt butter and olive oil in a medium skillet until butter is foamy
2. reduce heat to medium , add smashed garlic and cook until lightly browned
3. remove garlic and discard
4. add sprouts cut side down , cover , and cook without stirring on medium-low heat 10-15 minutes or until tender when pierced with a knife
5. the cut side of the sprouts should get nice and browned , with a nutty , buttery flavor enhanced by garlic
6. top with freshly grated parmesan and salt& pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: I have to say I never have liked brussels sprouts until now.  This is one of my favorite side dishes.  The only thing I did different was, I didnt discard the garlic.  After the brussels sprouts were done, I chopped up the browned garlic and added it back.  They are sooo delicious that they are actually my favorite veggie now.  Thanks for this wonderful recipe!

target.recipe_text:
french breakfast puffs muffins

a french coffee house treat prepared in a flash with a food processor, then baked and rolled in a delicious butter sugar and cinnamon mixture :)

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease muffin tins with cooking spray
3. in a bowl , sift together the flour , baking powder , salt and nutmeg
4. in a food processor , with steel blade , pulse the cold butter with the 1 / 2 cup sugar with on / off method , until creamed
5. add in the egg and vanilla , mix until combined
6. feed alternately through the tube , the dry ingredients and the cream
7. fill greased muffin tins 2 / 3 full
8. bake for 20-25 minutes , or until golden brown
9. remove from the muffin tins , and roll in melted butter , then in mixture of 1 / 2 cup sugar , and 1 tsp cinnamon
10. these can be frozen or refrigerated , and when reheated , roll in the butter and the sugar mixture , the puffs will get hard and crusty if rolled in the butter then reheated serve hot-- delicious !
target.review: Very good,  fast to make. Light and very tastey............YUMM

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized butternut squash

this is a delicious butternut squash recipe from ina garten / the barefoot contessa. we really enjoy this during the holidays. it is best when the squash is cut in medium to large chunks so that the outside gets a maple-flavored crust, and the inside stays soft and delicious.

1. preheat the oven to 400f
2. cut off the ends of each butternut squash and discard
3. peel the squash and cut in half lengthwise
4. using a spoon , remove the seeds
5. cut the squash into 1 1 / 4" to 1 1 / 2" cubes , and place them on a baking sheet
6. add the melted butter , brown sugar , salt and pepper
7. with clean hands , toss all of the ingredients together and spread out in a single layer on the baking sheet
8. roast for 45 minutes to 55 minutes , until the squash is tender and the glaze begins to caramelize
9. turn the squash while roasting a few times with a spatula to be sure it browns evenly
10. adjust seasonings if needed
11. serve hot
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was excellent.  I will definitely make this again.  Had it at our Christmas dinner and it was a hit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my favorite sauteed kale

i love kale and this is how i like to  make it almost every time.  i'm a hot pepper flake chick, but if that's too much for you, just leave it out!  great as a side dish, but i can eat this as my main meal, maybe just add some chickpeas or cannelini beans in at the end, amazing!

1. heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat
2. add crushed red pepper flakes , if using , and let them sizzle a bit in the oil
3. add the garlic and cook until soft , but not colored
4. raise heat to high , add the stock and kale and toss to combine
5. cover and cook for 5 minutes
6. remove cover and continue to cook , stirring until all the liquid has evaporated
7. i like the kale to still remain bright-ish green
8. season with salt and pepper to taste and add vinegar
demonstrations.review: very good.  Wanted to try kale,  and found that I love it coked this way....thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s chocolate fudge frosting

another recipe from my grandma. i still remember making this with her as a little girl. rich and creamy!

1. put first three ingredients in a sauce pan
2. bring to a boil , while stirring constantly
3. remove from heat and add chips
4. with a wire whip beat until creamy and cooled
5. add chopped pecans if desired
demonstrations.review: Very Good.  Will make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Good and fast easy dinner.  Will be making this again.  I used corn tortillas.  I like that flavor.  maybe next time I may add corn to the mix.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the great green vegetable medley

a perfect make ahead dish. this is excellent !! i usually have to double this. guaranteed you will make this over and over. it comes from a christmas cookbook i believe, my friend gave me the recipe and it is a great dish !!!!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. steam or boil broccoli , beans and peas together until tender , drain and set aside
3. cook1 / 2 cup onions in 2 tbsp of butter till tender
4. add cornstarch , salt , pepper and sour cream
5. mix well
6. stir in green vegetables
7. put in a greased 2 qt casserole dish
8. mixture can be refrigerated overnight at this point and finished before cooking
9. top with grated cheese
10. combine remaining 2 tbsp of butter and cracker crumbs
11. sprinkle over cheese
12. bake 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a good way to get the vegetables down.  But I just guess you have to like them to begin with in order to get 5 stars, sorry.

target.recipe_text:
candied almonds

nan

1. bring water , sugar and cinnamon to a boil
2. stirring constantly
3. add almonds and toss to coat
4. remove almonds with slotted spoon
5. arrange on greased baking pan
6. bake at 350 for 20 minutes , basting twice with reserved syrup
7. cool
8. store airtight
target.review: Wow these are good :)  I always buy candied almonds at the mall around Christmas time (who can resist that heavenly smell?!) But now I can have them year round thanks to this awesome recipe!!  There goes my diet :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned corn and potato chowder

this really is old fashioned! it comes from 

1. combine , in a large pot , all ingredients except milk and flour / water
2. cook until potatoes are fork tender
3. add milk and flour / water , stirring well
4. bring to a boil and allow to cook for 10 minutes
5. serve with chopped green onion and shredded cheese as a garnish
demonstrations.review: This soup is fantastic & so super easy to make!!  My oldest boy was in raptures over it :)  Thanks for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
double chocolate banana muffins

nan

1. in a large bowl , combine the first six ingredients
2. in a small bowl , combine bananas , oil and egg
3. stir into dry ingredients just until moistened
4. fold in chocolate chips
5. fill greased or paper lined muffin cups three fourths full
6. bake at 350 deg f for 20-25 minutes or until muffins test done
demonstrations.review: Why have I not reviewed this recipe yet?!  I've been making these for years!!  Oh man, they are delicious :)  One of our most favorite muffin recipes!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: 1000 amazing reviews, and now I know why!!  I love a recipe that's easy **and** delicious!!  Thanks sooooo much for posting!!  This was a hit with the entire family :)  I'd rate it 10 stars if I could!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick soft breadsticks

our family likes these breadsticks because they are soft and chewy. i like to make them when i am in a hurry because they rise quickly.

1. make dough using your favorite method- bread machine , mixer or by hand
2. roll out into a 10x12 inch rectangle
3. cut into strips about 3 / 4 inch wide
4. give each strip a twist and place on a greased cookie sheet
5. let rise for at least 20 minutes or more if you have time
6. bake at 375 for 10-15 minutes
7. brush with butter and sprinkle with garlic salt and parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Wow!!  These are great!!  Thank you so much for posting such a wonderfully delicious and easy recipe :)  Followed everything exactly except that I combined the garlic salt & parmesan cheese before sprinkling for even distribution.  We will be having these breadsticks on a regular basis!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best cherry pie

this is called best cherry pie because it is a blue ribbon winner at the county fair in vicksburg, ms (according to the cookbook 

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. drain cherries , reserving 1 / 2 cup juice
3. combine sugar , cornstarch and salt
4. combine cherry juice , food coloring , almond extract and lemon juice
5. add to dry ingredients , mixing well
6. add cherries and mix well again
7. add butter and let stand for 15 minutes
8. pour cherry mixture into pie crust and finish top with lattice work pie crust
9. bake for 50 to 55 minutes
demonstrations.review: Oh my gosh, your recipe is amazing!!  This was the first time I've ever made a cherry pie, so I was really pleased that it turned out so well!!  I didn't change a thing... it made a devilishly good "Vam-Pie" for my Halloween party :)  I'm gonna go eat another slice right now!!

target.recipe_text:
chocolate guinness layer cake

a very moist dense chocolate cake that gets even better with age! the dark beer is what gives this cake an intense flavor! this cake will not fit into a regular size 12-cup bundt pan.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease three 9 or 10-inch round cake pans then line the bottoms with parchment paper , then butter the paper
3. bring 2 cups stout beer and 2 cups butter to a simmer in a large saucepan over medium heat
4. add in cocoa powder and whisk until mixture is smooth
5. cool slightly
6. in a large bowl whisk the flour , sugar , baking soda and 1-1 / 2 teaspoons salt
7. in another bowl using an electric mixer beat eggs until thick and lemon coloured add in the sour cream and beat until well combined
8. add the stout / chocolate mixture to the egg mixture
9. beat just to combine
10. add in the flour mixture and beat on low speed until combined
11. divide the batter equally among the three pans
12. bake for about 35 minutes , or until the cakes test done
13. cool in pans for 10 minutes , then remove to plates
target.review: Great option for a not-too-sweet chocolate cake; the stout flavor of the beer came through very nicely.  I used half a recipe which fit into a bundt pan nicely (baking time about 40 min @ 350F)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican layered ground beef enchiladas

authentic mexican recipe from a friend of the family.  posted for zwt 3- mexico.

1. in a medium saucepan , heat oil over medium low heat
2. stir in flour until blended and light brown in color
3. slowly pour in broth and whisk to make smooth gravy
4. add chili powder , cumin , and garlic powder
5. bring to boil and reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes
6. remove from heat and cool slightly
7. pour gravy into a medium size bowl in which to dip tortillas
8. brown ground beef in large skillet
9. drain excess fat
10. add one package of taco seasoning and tomato sauce and stir to combine
11. bring to boil and then reduce heat to low and simmer 8-10 minutes
12. remove from heat and set aside until ready to assemble layers
13. spray bottom of 9 x 13 baking dish with non stick spray
14. dip two tortillas into gravy and place into baking dish
15. cover with one fourth of ground beef , cheese and onion
16. repeat 3 times
17. bake for 50-60 minutes at 350 degrees f
demonstrations.review: Wow, the roux really is the secret to a great enchilada casserole!  Corn tortillas work as well as flour tortillas, and I've even swapped out the red sauce with mole sauce. Tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetarian sweet potato stew

you wouldn't think this would taste as good as it does by looking at the ingredients.  we were very surprised and pleased.

1. heat oil in large saucepan
2. add onions and garlic , cook until lightly browned
3. add bell peppers , cook for 5 minutes
4. stir in water , tomatoes , sweet potatoes , beans , chiles , tomato sauce , chili powder and cumin
5. cook over medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes or until thickened and potatoes are cooked through
6. season with salt and ground black pepper
demonstrations.review: The sweet & spicy comination ROCKS, thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amaretto apricots with walnuts teriyaki

you can serve this with cocktails or on a dessert tray. they are both sweet and savory. from the new carry-out cuisine. it is hard to stop nibbling on these!

1. line a jelly-roll pan with foil
2. spread the nuts on the foil lined pan
3. combine the remaining ingredients for the walnuts , except the kosher salt , in a saucepan and heat until the sugar is dissolved
4. pour the sauce over the nuts , making sure to coat them well
5. bake at 350 for 15-20 minutes
6. place the toasted nuts on lightly oiled foil and sprinkle with the salt if desired
7. assembly: add the amaretto to the cream cheese and mix well
8. place a teaspoon of the cheese on each apricot and top with a walnut
demonstrations.review: A new staple for us - even enjoyed at a picnic recently.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rumaki polynesian

this is a party favorite. a very nice recipe that you can keep in a crock pot for those holiday festivities or anytime that you want to have finger foods. while the water chestnuts are unexpected, they are a hit surprise!

1. cut the bacon slices into halves
2. wrap the water chestnuts with the bacon pieces
3. secure with wooden picks
4. place in a shallow 9x13 inch baking dish
5. bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes
6. drain
7. combine the ketchup , worcestershire sauce , soy sauce , hot sauce and sugar in a bowl
8. mix well
9. pour over the water chestnuts
10. bake for 30 minutes longer
demonstrations.review: These were a hit - the water chestnuts made for a great texture that really lets you appreciate the flavor of bacon & sauce.  The only change I made was to replace Worcestershire sauce with extra soy sauce to avoid problems for those with fish allergies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice vinegar cucumber salad

the rice vinegar gives this salad a great flavor.  it's  milder and more flavorful than regular vinegar, and delicious. i found this recipe a few years ago and it has become my standard cucumber salad recipe.  i always have to double this recipe because it disappears in my house.  even the kids love it!

1. mix sugar , vinegar , oil , salt and pepper and dill in a serving bowl
2. peel cucumbers , if desired , then thinly slice and add to bowl , stirring to mix and coat
3. let marinade
demonstrations.review: Simple, elegant, yummy!  I'm not a fan of normal cucumbers, but the smaller diameter, thinly sliced Japanese cucumbers work beautifully. Very reminiscent of the cucumber salads in Japan.  Even if you're not a cucumber fan (as I wasn't), this one is worth a try.

target.recipe_text:
simply sour cream chicken enchiladas

easy to assemble, deliciously creamy and a great choice for once-a-month cooking. and there is no canned cream soup in my enchiladas -- hope you give them a try!

1. in a frying pan , cook chicken and onion together in oil over medium-high heat until chicken is just done
2. divide cooked chicken evenly between 8 tortillas
3. add 1 1 / 2 tablespoons cheese to each tortilla
4. roll enchiladas and place seam-side down in a 9x13" baking dish that has been lightly sprayed with no-stick cooking spray
5. melt butter in a medium saucepan
6. stir in flour to make a roux , stir and cook until bubbly , and gradually whisk in chicken broth then bring to boiling , stirring frequently
7. remove from heat
8. stir in sour cream and green chilies
9. pour sauce evenly over enchiladas
10. top with remaining 3 / 4 cup cheese and bake at 400 f for 20 minutes until cheese is melted and sauce near edges of baking dish is bubbly
target.review: Enchiladas may also grow spicy with sour cream, cheese, chicken, and flour tortillas even when baked.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese chicken drumettes

i received this recipe from my friend karen, when i lived in california.  these are good served hot or cold.  they are so tasty.

1. rinse off chicken
2. combine all ingredients , except chicken , and bring to a boil
3. leave on a low boil for 15 minutes
4. add in chicken drummettes
5. let boil for one hour or more until it all thickens and becomes sticky
6. then let it stand for about ten minutes and then refrigerate
7. can serve warm or cold
8. sprinkle with sesame seeds once arranged on platter and garnish with parsley
demonstrations.review: A simplified alternative to teriyaki is made with chicken grilled to perfection.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy midnight soup

my best friend made this the other day and i just had to have the recipe. it's filling and soooo good! the recipe can easily be halved. this recipe comes from a german cookbook and a german packet of leek soup is enough for 3 cups of water. as far as i can tell from looking on the internet that's the same for knorr leek soup in the us. if i am wrong please use enough of the soup mix to make 9 cups. if you add the optional ingredients you might want to reduce the amount of whole kernel corn, otherwise the soup becomes really thick. where i live you can buy cans of whole kernel corn that have some kidney beans added, those work really well. can easily be prepared ahead and reheated.

1. heat the butter in a large stock pot and fry the turkey or chicken chunks until very nearly done
2. add the curry powder and fry for a further couple of minutes , if you are using leek you can add it at this stage
3. add the water , bring to the boil , add dry soup mix and stir until disolved
4. add all other ingredients , apart from the cream and the spices , and simmer for 5-10 minutes until everything is heated through
5. add the cream and season to taste with chili powder and cayenne
6. serve with crusty bread
demonstrations.review: This spicy, flavor-rich soup is a cream-based vegetarian meal made with real chili and served as dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato kielbasa skillet

a very hearty, tasty supper. this is very easy to make and a real pleaser.

1. in dutch oven , brown potatoes , kielbasa , onion and peppers in oil
2. add seasonings and water
3. bring to a boil
4. cover tightly and cook for 20 minutes on low , stirring occasionally
5. uncover and put cheese on top
6. simmer until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: A crisp alternative to the gratin, this side dish is made with real potatoes and sausage, enriched with real cheese melted to red-hot perfection and eaten with other vegetables.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
midnight mozart

don't you just love that name! for zaar world tour, coffee and kahlua both come from mexico.

1. brew coffee
2. stir in liqueur's
3. serve topped with whipped cream
demonstrations.review: I can sometimes suggest this drink with the use of sugar as preparation, and peppermint syrup for drizzling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer pastrami sandwich

saint patty's day and/or superbowl food. of course, this goes along with lots of cold beers. enjoy!

1. preheat the broiler to high setting
2. in a saucepan , over medium heat , combine the broth , beer and worcestershire sauce and bring to a boil , then reduce heat to low
3. separate the slices of pastrami and drop each into the sauce , allowing the pastrami to heat through
4. place open buns on an ungreased cookie sheet or half-sheet
5. place pastrami slices on one side of the bun ,
6. place cheese on the opposite side of the bun
7. broil for 1 to 2 minutes until cheese melts
8. remove from broiler and spread mustard on pastrami
9. serve , cut into pieces and with bowls of the sauce for dipping
demonstrations.review: It has just had pastrami infused with beer and is great with other side dishes.

target.recipe_text:
easy pizza pasta casserole  oamc

this is a kid pleaser-very cheesy and topped with pepperoni. it makes 2 large (9x13) casseroles or 4 small ones; i often divide it in fourths and freeze 3. this originally came from toh's quick cooking.

1. brown ground beef , onion , garlic and seasoning in oil
2. drain
3. while beef is browning , cook pasta according to the packaging
4. stir in pasta , spaghetti sauce and 3 cups cheese
5. place mixture in 2 greased 9x13x2 inch baking pans or 4 square pans
6. sprinkle with remaining mozzarella
7. top with pepperoni
8. cover and freeze up to 3 months
9. to cook now: bake uncovered at 350 degrees for 25-30 minutes , until heated through
10. to bake frozen casserole: thaw in refrigerator overnight and bake at 350 for 35-40 minutes , till hot
target.review:
Fantastic. I added peperoni (personal love) and that was it. The thing disappeared faster than rain drops in Tucson...

Excellent and easy! Thanks for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken  shrimp and andouille jambalaya

a cajun classic, meal in one pot! have the hot sauce ready to splash on. serve with some crusty french bread, a nice crisp salad, and some of your favorite wine. :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large pan or dutch oven , brown chicken in hot oil on both sides
3. remove and drain
4. add andouille , onion , celery , bell pepper , thyme , oregano , paprika , salt , and cayenne pepper to the pan , cooking and stirring for about 5 minutes until onions are tender
5. add rice , tomatoes with juice , and broth
6. bring to a boil
7. place rice mixture in a baking dish or oven-proof casserole
8. top with chicken
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees f for 40-45 minutes or until rice and chicken are done and tender
10. stir in shrimp , parsley , and green onions
11. cover and cook 5-8 minutes longer or until shrimp curl and turn bright pink and serve
demonstrations.review:
WOW! This was a huge hit at my house last night. I made this long with cheddar biscuits (256914) and my family is still singing my praises this morning.

The flavor mixture is marvelous. I also went with kielbasa and it worked out terrific. Very filling, very easy, very delicious. Prepared as directed.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy meat and cheese stromboli

this is from 30 minute meals on food network.  a simple, quick snack for the sunday football game or movie night.

1. pre-heat oven to 400 degrees
2. break open the tube of dough and remove it from container
3. dust your hands and lightly coat the dough with cornmeal then roll out onto work surface
4. stretch out dough , then cut the thin rectangular dough into 4 equal square pieces
5. cover each piece of dough with: 6 slices pepperoni , 1 1 / 2 slices cheese , 1 1 / 2 slices hot ham and 2 slices genoa salami
6. roll each piece on an angle from corner to corner making a long roll that is thicker in the middle and thinner on each end
7. brush rolls with extra-virgin olive oil then mix sesame seeds , cheese and seasonings in a small cup , sprinkle and pat the mixture into the dough
8. bake until evenly golden , 12 to 15 minutes then serve
9. if desired , serve with marinara sauce
demonstrations.review:
Made these yesterday after having stromboli for the first time on a cruise ship last week. They were terrific. I did mix and match using many meat and vegetable combinations. Ultimately my favorite included red onion, mushrooms, green pepper and red bell pepper. I also added 1/4 cup of shredded mozzarella to each one. 

Truly outstanding recipe... Thanks for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of red lobster cheddar bay biscuits by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com. the cold butter is the secret. it's not included in other copy cat recipes.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. combine bisquick and cold butter
3. don't combine too thoroughly
4. there should be small chunks of butter about the size of peas
5. add cheddar , milk and 1 / 4 tsp garlic
6. mix by hand until combined , but don't over mix
7. drop 9 equal portions onto greased cookie sheet
8. bake for 15-17 minutes or until tops are light brown
9. melt 2 tbsp butter in a bowl
10. stir in 1 / 2 tsp garlic powder and parsley flakes
11. use a pastry brush to spread garlic butter over tops of biscuits
demonstrations.review:
Mades these last night to go with a fantastic Jambalya recipe (28165) and they were terrific. Made them exactly as described. The only downside was my over sized pinch of salt but even salty they were delicious. 

Thanks for posting this, I have been looking for this recipe for a very long time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best sweet and sour sauce

this came from taste of home's quick cooking and is much better than anything i've created on my own. the sauce is thick and gooy and goes well with so many things.

1. combine all ingredients in a sauce pan
2. cook over medium heat until thick , stirring constantly
3. pour over chicken , meatballs , smoked sausage , veggies , etc
demonstrations.review: Outstanding! I prepared according to the instructions and thought when I put it in the pan it was too runny - however - a minute later it thickened right up and it was delicious. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked spanish rice

this "kicked up" rice dish is a family favorite. if you have some saffron threads, add in a good pinch for even extra flavor. make certain to use only converted rice for this recipe. if you do not like it spicy then use only a pinch or omit completely.

1. in a oven-proof dutch oven or a large frypan with an oven proof tight fitting lid , melt the butter
2. saute the onions , garlic , celery and green pepper until soft
3. add in the converted rice and mix with a wooden spoon for about 3 minutes
4. carefully add in the chicken broth and diced tomatoes along with all the remaining ingredients
5. stir to combine , and simmer on top of the stove on low heat for 5-6 minutes
6. set oven to 350 degrees
7. cover with an oven-proof tight fitting lid and place in oven to cook for about 30-35 minutes or until the rice is at desired tenderness
8. fluff with a fork
9. delicious !
demonstrations.review:
Excellent recipe, very tasty and simple. I'm not a huge green olive fan so I will cut it in half next time. 
I made this with my own carne asada recipe and it was a terrific dinner. Thanks Kit for posting it.

target.recipe_text:
szechuan carrot soup

excellent recipe from the manchester highlands inn, manchester, vermont

1. in a large heavy saucepan cook onion , celery , and garlic in oil over moderately low heat , stirring , until onion is softened
2. add carrots , ginger root , red pepper flakes , and broth and simmer , covered , until carrots are very tender , about 45 minutes
3. stir in remaining ingredients and , in a blender or food processor , puree mixture in batches
4. return soup to pan and heat over low heat until hot , being careful not to let boil
5. serve soup drizzled decoratively with sour cream mixture
target.review: Very Easy and very good!! This soup was simply delicious!   I read all the reviews and cut back on the sesame oil like I was advised and it tuned out great! I used 1% milk and just used low fat sour cream, to cut back on the calories, However I did cook the onions and garlic in butter,  Next time I make it I might add some hot sauce for some added heat!  This soup will be added to my weekly soup rotation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry chicken salad sandwich

i love the combination of textures in this sandwich. its classic chicken salad changed up with the addition of dried cherries and pecans.

1. combine chicken , cherries , pecans , and onion in a bowl
2. mix mayo , yogurt , and lemon juice
3. pour over chicken mixture
4. toss to mix
5. refrigerate salad for 1-2 hours
6. split croissants and divide chicken evenly
7. sprinkle with black pepper before serving
demonstrations.review: This is my go too  sandwich!! I bring them to everything!!   I instead of 1/4 cup of mayo I mix 1 tablespoon of Mayo with 1 tablespoon of Miracle whip.  I always serve it on Mini- Croissants with Boston Bib!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
poor man s lobster   mahi mahi

i found a similar recipe on the internet and then i personalized it. i just love mahi mahi and this recipe really hits the spot. simply decadent!

1. cut fillets into 2 inch chunks and drizzle with the lemon juice
2. pour the beer into the bottom of a saucepan and place a collapsible vegetable steamer over the beer
3. bring the beer to a boil , place the fish chunks in the steamer , cover and steam for 5 to 10 minutes , dependent upon the thickness of the fish
4. the fish will be rubbery if it is overcooked
5. meanwhile , heat the butter with the garlic and salt
6. remove the fish from the steamer and discard the beer / liquid / rind
7. serve the fish chunks with the garlic butter dipping sauce
demonstrations.review: I made this to serve with a surf and turf. It was good and real easy to make, although not very flavorful. It not my favorite was to make Mahi Mahi, but it was the easiest.  I marinated the fish in some Beer and lemon for about an hour. I used Heineken, and the fish was a wild caught, same day :) I'll make it again,  .  I cooked the butter  till it was clear and garlic was soft and mushy

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rachael ray s linguine with red clam sauce

rach's cupboard red clam sauce. lots of clams and lots of flavour.

1. bring a large pot of salted water to a boil , then add the pasta and cook until al dente
2. while the pasta cooks , prepare the sauce: heat a large skillet over medium-low heat , add the evoo and the anchovies and cook until the anchovies melt into the oil
3. add the crushed red pepper flakes , oregano , thyme and garlic and cook for 1 minute , then add the onion , raise the heat to medium and cook , stirring frequently , for 3 to 4 minutes , until the onion begins to soften
4. add the wine and cook 1 minute , then stir in the clams with their juice plus the drained clams
5. cook , stirring , for 1 minute to concentrate the flavors
6. stir in the tomatoes and cook until heated through
7. season with salt and pepper to taste
8. drain the linguine , return it to the pot and add the sauce
9. add half the parsley and toss
10. adjust the salt and pepper and plate the pasta
11. garnish it with the remaining parsley and a little lemon zest
demonstrations.review: I made about two years ago and I have made it about 20 times since!  This is by far my favorite Red Clam Sauce!  I even made it with fresh clams ( left over from a family picnic) and got rave reviews!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herb roasted pork tenderloin

got this recipe from southern living magazine. oh so good and easy.

1. stir together first 11 ingredients in a shallow dish or heavy-duty zip-top plastic bag
2. prick pork with a fork , and place in marinade , turning to coat
3. cover dish , or seal bag
4. chill 2 hours
5. remove from marinade , discarding marinade
6. place pork on a rack in a roasting pan
7. bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes or until a meat thermometer inserted into thickest portion of pork registers 160 degrees
demonstrations.review:
Absolutely the best! This will be a staple for my Sunday Dinners menus, Very Moist and juice!  
I add extra marinade in the last 15 minutes of cooking and sliced the Poke in to slices. I served it with Garlic Butter Baby Potatoes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan eggs

simple, easy to prepare, different, and good. from the belle de jour inn in healdsburg, ca. we like this with toasted italian bread for breakfast.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an individual ramekin , then dust with 1 tablespoon of cheese
3. break egg into ramekin and cover with cream
4. sprinkle with remaining cheese
5. bake 10 to 15 minutes , until white is set
6. serve hot in ramekin
demonstrations.review: This was so good! I loved it! A great and easy way to make an egg! I served it with fresh hot french bread!

target.recipe_text:
no bake hershey s bar pie

this is soooo yummy and rich with chocolate. it is also super easy to prepare and comes out looking and tasting delicious. chill time not included.

1. heat milk and marshmallows in top of a double boiler
2. add hershey bar and stir until melted and combined
3. allow to cool to room temperature
4. whip cream until stiff
5. fold the whipped cream into the chocolate mixture and pour into the graham cracker crust
6. chill at least one hour or until firm
target.review: I made this and it was a huge success at Thanksgiving.  I did change it up a little.  I cooked a pie shell prior to adding the filling and then I covered the chocolate filling with fresh whipped cream with chocolate kisses on top in the middle for garnish. Very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fantastic crispy tempura batter

whenever i have tempura at a restaurant it is always so light and crispy, the boxed store-bought stuff is okay providing you rush to the table within minutes to eat it or it gets soggy and soft, i have tryed many tempura recipes over my 35 years of cooking i have to say this one is the best, it produces a very light crispy coating that holds up well --- i have used this to make tempura veggies and froze them after deep-frying in this batter, and just reheated them in a small amount of oil, also with bite-size meaty pieces of fish and with about 15 large peeled shrimp cooked about 3 minutes --- remember the tempura must sit out at room temperature for 10 minutes before using, if you want to make a double recipe of tempura, then make two exact recipes using two separate bowls, do not double the recipe and make it all in one bowl it will not work --- use only rice flour for this anything else will not work the same and use only a light-coloured beer.

1. in a bowl whisk beer with the rice flour until very smooth
2. add in salt and garlic powder and cayenne
3. let sit out at room temperature for 10 minutes
4. heat oil to 375 degrees
5. dredge the fish or veggies into the batter coating completely with batter , letting any excess drip off
6. deep-fry turning once until golden
7. transfer to a piece of brown paper
8. season with seasoning salt
demonstrations.review: Went looking for an easy and well rated Tempura batter recipe today and found this one by Kittencal and knew this would be a good one because she has never failed me yet...I was not wrong.  This recipe was easy and fantastic.  My husband is still raving.  Thanks for another great recipe Kittencal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy one bowl milk chocolate fudge cupcakes

if you are looking for a dark chocolate cupcake then these are not for you, they rise simply beautiful and come out just perfect, they' re so easy to make everything is mixed in one bowl with a wooden spoon! --- top these with my recipe#89207

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. line 12 regular size muffin tin with paper liners
3. in a medium-size mixing bowl , mix together the flour , brown sugar , sifted baking cocoa , baking powder , baking soda , salt and cinnamon
4. mix with a wooden spoon to combine
5. in a two-cup measuring cup or bowl whisk together the milk , egg , oil and vanilla
6. add the milk / egg mixture to the dry ingredients
7. mix very well with a wooden spoon to combine well
8. mix in the chocolate chips and nuts
9. divide the batter evenly between the lined muffin tins
10. bake for 22-25 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean
11. cool , and frost with favorite chocolate frosting
demonstrations.review: My family loves these.  We don't even put frosting on them...So moist and great it doesn't need it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chocolate cake  really

i made this cake for my little brother's 12th birthday with the request of a chocolate cake. it was truly amazing- weeks later my family (nonetheless after being stuffed with a huge dinner and dessert) was still talking about how fabulous the cake was! nice and moist and the frosting...oooh. recipe for a 9"x13" pan, but can be made as a wonderful layer cake. prep time includes cooling and frosting (with some extra leeway). from www.donogh.com

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. melt chocolate , either on the stove or in the microwave and set aside
3. beat butter in large mixer bowl then add brown sugar and eggs , and beat until light and fluffy , about 5 minutes
4. add vanilla and melted chocolate , and beat to combine
5. combine flour , baking soda , and salt and add to chocolate mixture gradually , alternating with sour cream , beating after each addition
6. stir boiling water into the batter - the batter will be thin
7. pour into two 9 inch round cake pans which have been greased and floured
8. bake for 35 minutes , until cake centre springs back when touched
9. cool for 10 minutes before removing from pans
10. allow to cool completely before applying frosting
11. for the frosting
12. combine brown sugar , butter and milk in a small saucepan and bring to a boil
13. continue to boil , stirring constantly , for 3 minutes
14. cool to lukewarm
15. stir in icing sugar and continue to stir until the right consistency to spread
16. spread over cooled cake
demonstrations.review: I am very happy that I found this recipe.  I don't often take the time to add a review, even though they often deserve one, but this one I just had to take the time.  I can't stop eating this cake and my entire family is addicted.  I agree that you would need at least an additional 1/2 of the icing recipe.  This one will become a family staple.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
waldorf astoria red velvet cake

i haven't even tried it, but it looks good.

1. cream shortening , sugar and eggs
2. make a paste of food coloring and cocoa
3. add to creamed mixture
4. add buttermilk alternating with flour and salt
5. add vanilla
6. add soda to vinegar , and blend into the batter
7. pour into 3 or 4 greased and floured 8" cake pans
8. bake at 350f for 24-30 minutes
9. split layers fill and frost with the following frosting
10. frosting: add milk to flour slowly , avoiding lumps
11. cook flour and milk until very thick , stirring constantly
12. cool completely
13. cream sugar , butter and vanilla until fluffy
14. add to cooked mixture
15. beat , high speed , until very fluffy
16. looks and tastes like whipped cream
demonstrations.review: I had never made a Red Velvet cake before and so this was very fun and different.  I replaced butter for the shortening, like many others and only used 1 ounce of red food coloring not 2, which still made it very red.  Only filled up 2 8 inc. pans, and it took a little longer than 30 minutes for them to cook all the way though in the middle, but that may just be my oven.  I iced it with cream cheese icing made purple (on request) for my son's  birthday cake.  Altogther this was a great experience and look forward to making it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: This recipe was amazing.  Followed it pretty much as stated, but added some crushed red pepper.  Cooked it in the simmering sauce (not the oven)...the entire family LOVED it and said that this should be our go forward recipe for spaghetti.  I had enough left over for meatball hoagies later in the week.  Thanks Kittencal again for the inspired recipe!

target.recipe_text:
tilapia al ajillo  garlic tilapia

you can do this with any white fish, sea bass is great this way. fish is often served this way in the canary islands, though usually it is the whole fish instead of fillets. yum!

1. season tilapia fillets with salt and pepper
2. heat oil in a skillet over medium heat
3. put fillets in first , and when they start to turn color a bit add garlic slices
4. continue cooking about 4 minutes or so , then flip fillets
5. fry until cooked through , and fish flakes easily with a fork-- this will depend entirely on the thickness of your fillets , so you will need to watch them carefully
6. the garlic should turn a dark golden brown , but not be burned , if you notice that the garlic is starting to burn , spoon it over the fish , so it is no longer in contact with the pan
7. serve with freshly squeezed lemon juice and garnish with chopped parsley
target.review: This was delicious! Will definitely make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamed tuna fish on a shingle
