oh how i love this comfort food.  this has been a staple piece in my diet since i was a little girl- it makes me happy.... best on a cold winter night!

1. melt butter over med heat in small sauce pan
2. add flour slowly , stirring constantly until well combined
3. add milk slowly , stirring in between each addition till all is smooth and not curdled looking
4. add salt and pepper
5. lastly , add the tuna fish and bring to a low boil
6. if sauce is too thick for your liking , add more milk -- too thin , add more flour
7. sauce will thicken a bit as it simmers
8. i like to add more pepper- towards the 1 / 2 teaspoons mark- but add to your liking
9. toast 6 slices of bread in toaster , immediately upon removing from toaster put a large spoonful of tuna mixture on top of toast and spread evenly over top
10. grate desired amount of cheese on top and serve !
demonstrations.review:
I grew up eating this, minus the cheese. LOVE IT! People always think I'm weird when I make it for them, but then they take a bite and I get to watch their eyes roll to the back of their heads.     For a bit more zip, I like to add a little garlic,..simply because I'm obsessed with garlic. Either way, it's super simple, super easy and super tasty. I'm so glad you posted this recipe.
A fellow Minnesotan,
-Meredith

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
demonstrations.review: These were good. I personally prefer a bit more flavor, but my boyfriend absolutely loved them. I'll be making these again. The recipe is quite simple to make, the only thing I may do differently would be to add more of the Old Bay seasoning, a bit more pepper sauce and maybe fresh grated garlic.  I think the garlic would really compliment this dish especially with the cheese and mayo mixture that browns and melts so nicely over the fillets.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy stove top  rotini and cheese

this is a quick and easy way to avoid the box mac and cheese. i found this recipe in a cooking light magazine and really liked it. i did substitute wheat flour and wheat pasta rather than regular macaroni and white flour.

1. cook pasta according to package directions , omitting salt and fat
2. drain and set aside
3. while pasta cook , place wheat flour , salt , and pepper in a large saucepan
4. add milk , stirring with a whisk until well blended
5. drop cream cheese by teaspoonfuls into milk mixture
6. bring to a boil over medium-high heat , stirring constantly
7. reduce heat
8. simmer 2 minutes or until thick and cream cheese melts , stirring occasionally
9. stir in mustard , worcestershire sauce , and garlic
10. simmer 1 minute
11. remove from heat
12. add cheddar cheese , stirring until cheese melts
13. combine pasta and cheese sauce in a large bowl
14. toss well
demonstrations.review: Yummy!! I love garlic, and in my opinion you can almost NEVER have too much, so I added some more garlic but other than that, delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
should be illegal oven bbq ribs

after not being able to find restaurant ribs that satified my hot sweet appetite, i carefully attempted various combinations of flavors until i found one that i and my family thought was perfect. hope you enjoy them too.

1. place all ingredients together in large roasting pan
2. cut ribs apart for easier serving
3. mix together making sure to coat all ribs with this semi-dry paste
4. spread ribs out evenly on bottom of pan
5. cover lightly with foil
6. bake at 375 degrees for approximately 1 hour
7. turning or stirring occasionally
8. you can use broiler for these ribs , just watch more closely , and adjust cooking time
9. these ribs are also great finished on the grill for a few minutes on each side
demonstrations.review: Excellent sauce! Finger licking good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bulgogi  korean bbq

a wonderfully marinated korean beef dish. kimchi, white sticky rice, whole cabbage leaves and assorted pickled vegetables make a wonderful accompaniment. optionally, add an assortment of vegetables to beef marinade.

1. mix beef& sugar , let rest 2 minutes , then add remaining ingredients
2. toss well and let stand 1 hr at room temp or overnight in the refrigerator to allow the meat to mature- better the longer it marinates !
3. preheat a large , heavy skillet over moderate heat for 2 minutes
4. add beef , a few slices at a time , and sear without oil for 2-3 minutes at most
5. or , grill beef in very hot gas or electric broiler
6. serve immediately with white sticky rice and an assortment of side dishes
demonstrations.review: I cannot say one bad thing about this recipe.  Delicious! It's the closes I've tasted, home-cooking wise, to what they serve in a Korean restaurant.  If I didnt make this again, I'd have a lot of unhappy friends and an unhappy ME!

target.recipe_text:
quiche

my sisters and i used to make this for our family for dinner when we were young. not only is this a very easy recipe to make but it is quite tasty as well.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. layer the swiss cheese , mozzerella cheese , pepperoni , and onion in the pie crust
3. in a small bowl , mix together the milk , eggs , salt , oregano , and garlic powder
4. pour this mixture over the cheese in the pie crust
5. bake for 45 minutes
target.review: I used spinach and bacon in this instead and it was tasty, however it didn't set.  It was soupy and the crust got soggy so my family didn't eat too much of it although they did say it had a good taste.  I always use skim milk and wonder if that may be why it was soupy.  I think next time I will cut the milk down to 1/2 cup and add an extra egg instead and see if my results turn out any better.  Will definitely keep this thanks :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maryland crab salad

this is a personal recipe -- tried and true -- made time and time again. i use this in the good ol summa' time, but can be used during the rest of the year as well. normally, i buy "cold  steamed blue crabs" from our local fish market, that are bursting with flavor after resting in the unique maryland seasoning. i pick the meat, and make this cooling, refreshing salad. it is also great served on a saltine or toast points. usually though, i just place atop a garden fresh lettuce leaf, and grab a cracker or two with it. if you get the time, marinate the crab meat in 1 tablespoon of italian dressing for about 1 hour prior to gently folding together. if you don't get the time, that's okay too! just *enjoy*  you can substitute lobster, shrimp, or even conch meat.

1. carefully comb through crab meat for any extra shells
2. making sure not to break up crab , marinate crab pieces with italian dressing for about 1 hour
3. but if you don't get a chance , ten minutes works well too
4. mix all other ingredients in a medium bowl thoroughly
5. add crab meat mixture to mayonnaise mixture and mix with spatula , again not to break up pieces
6. you can either cool in fridge for an hour or two , or you can eat directly
demonstrations.review: My hubby and I absolutely love this recipe.  I've been craving Crab Salad a lot with it becoming summer and this is one of the best I've tried.  I haven't used the real blue crab with it yet, but the imitation crab meat goes very well with this so I can't wait to try it with the real thing.  Definitely a keeper in our house.  Thanks Andi for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
deluxe potato casserole

a creamy potato dish sure to please your family. excellent at potlucks too! if you want to dress it up. add cruched corn flakes with melted butter on top the last 30 minutes of baking.

1. in lagre mixing bowl add ingredients listed
2. mix well
3. put into a casserole dish and bake for 1 hour at 350 degrees
demonstrations.review: This was heavenly!  I had a recipe similar to this given to me a few years back but lost it so I'm glad you have this one posted.  Loved it and so did DH and DS. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herb roasted whole chicken

i make this a lot,i let it bake until the skin is brown and crispy.

1. combine oil , water , herbs , salt and pepper
2. stir
3. pour or brush over the whole chicken before baking
4. the oil and water dosen't mix very well but thats ok
5. the water keeps it moist and the oil makes it crisp
6. any other herbs you like can be used in place of these
7. cover with foil and bake at 350 about an hour or until crispy and brown
demonstrations.review: I mixed together rosemary, thyme, basil and oregano in some olive oil and spread it on the bird.  Then I sprinkled on a little Garlic powder and salt.  I put a tablespoon of margarine up under the skin of the breast on each side, added a little water to pan and baked at 300 for 4 hours.  I took off the foil about 30 minutes before cooking time was finished so that the bird could get brown and crispy and it was simply delish!  My husband said it was the best baked chicken he ever had and the juiciest.  Will definitely make again thanks :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot hamburger  n potato casserole

easy and inexpensive, but so yummy!

1. spray crock pot with non stick vegetable spray
2. layer potatoes , onions and hamburger until all is used , sprinkling each layer very lightly with salt and pepper
3. mix soup and milk together and pour over top
4. cook 3 to 4 hours on high
demonstrations.review: I made this just like the directions said except I sprinkled some cheese in with the layers.  It was really good.  My husband liked it a lot so it will definitely be made again in this household. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked mashed potatoes

this recipe is from a pbs telethon cooking show. this casserole is loaded with mashed potatoes, cheese, butter and hard salami, then baked till hot and cheesy! it sounds wonderful. i have not made this recipe, it is a recipe request.

1. to the warm mashed potatoes , add 6 tablespoons butter and all the milk
2. whip until smooth
3. add both cheeses and the salami
4. stir to blend
5. add salt and pepper to taste
6. use 1 tablespoon of the remaining butter to grease the bottom and sides of a tall sided casserole dish
7. coat the greased casserole with the bread crumbs
8. spoon the potato mixture into the casserole dish and , dot the top with the remaining tablespoon of butter
9. bake at 350f until the top of casserole is golden brown
demonstrations.review: This was a perfect side dish!  My DH loved the salami, my son was skeptical at first, but liked it too.  I will definitely be making this again.  Thanks for the recipe. :)

target.recipe_text:
chuck roast barbecue

this is a really good recipe for when you are having a lot of people over. it is simple to put in crock pot or oven. has really good flavor. i put in crock pot over night and just shred the beef in the morning and let it go on low until needed.

1. brown meat
2. mix soup , ketchup , vinegar , brown sugar , sauce , mustard , and salt in bowl
3. put meat in crock pot , then onion and celery
4. pour sauce on top
5. cook until meat shreds with fork
6. crock pot 8-10 hours low-medium
7. oven: covered 6-8 hours 250 degrees
target.review:
I halved the recipe, left out the
mustard, and used celery seed 
instead of celery.  This was great
over rice, and my husband liked
it on hoagie rolls for lunches.
I cut the meat into chunks for a
quicker cooking time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot chocolate marshmallow coffee

easy and oh so good! adapted from a coffee site.

1. stir together the coffee and hot chocolate
2. mix until blended
3. top with the marshmallow whip
4. add a dash of cinnamon if desired
5. serve hot
demonstrations.review: I like to substitute a small amount of vanilla ice cream for the marshmallow whip.  Yummy way to start the morning!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
katharine hepburn s brownies

another of my celebrity recipes. when i make this, i leave out the nuts.

1. preheat oven to 325f degrees
2. butter and flour an 8-inch square baking pan
3. melt the chocolate with the butter in a saucepan over low heat
4. remove from heat and stir in sugar
5. next , stir in the eggs and vanilla and mix until smooth
6. add the flour , salt and nuts and stir until smooth
7. pour into prepared pan and bake until a toothpick inserted in centre comes out clean , about 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: These are my favorite childhood brownies; not too sweet and perfectly chewy.  My hubby and three boys love them, too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
prudhomme s cajun cauliflower in garlic sauce

a wonderful, flavorful vegetable courtesy of chef paul prudhomme.

1. steps: bring 1 quart of water to a boil in a large pot
2. blanch the cauliflower just until tender-crisp , about 3 minutes
3. drain well and set aside
4. place the butter in a large skillet over high heat
5. as soon as the butter begins to sizzle , add the garlic
6. cook , stirring almost constantly , until the garlic is thoroughly coated with butter , about 30 seconds
7. add the cauliflower and cook , stirring occasionally , just until the cauliflower is slightly browned , about 4 minutes
8. remove from the heat , stir in the pepper sauce , cilantro and cajun spice blend , and mix gently but thoroughly
9. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I found this recipe while searching for something southern for my son's Louisiana school regional food feast.  We're not from this area, so I needed a little help in the idea category.  My son's teacher told the class no one, so far, is bringing a vegetable dish.  My son told me he hasn't come across anything cajun that he has liked so far.  Well, although I didn't have fresh cilantro, I had some fresh cauliflower and all the other ingredients, so I decided to try a halved amount of everything.  It is a very easy recipe, especially since I cooked the cauliflower in the microwave instead before it was added to the butter and garlic in the skillet, which I should add that my son of 11 had prepared.  He added the cauliflower and pretty much completed the rest.  And... he tried it and liked it!  We made this yesterday, and today he requested some more for dinner!  He did the same thing as yesterday and ate even more today... amazing, since he doesn't eat many vegetables.  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked mozzarella cheese sticks

nan

1. in a small bowl , beat eggs& water
2. in a plastic bag , combine bread crumbs , italian seasoning , garlic powder , and pepper
3. coat cheese sticks in flour , then dip in egg mixture and bread crumb mixture
4. repeat egg and bread crumb coatings
5. cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight
6. place on an ungreased baking sheet& drizzle with butter
7. bake , uncovered , at 400 degrees for 6-8 minutes or until heated through
8. allow to stand for 3-5 minutes before serving
9. use marinara or spaghetti sauce for dipping
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Thank you for this recipe!  I made these for myself and one of my sons as we are the baked cheese stick eaters in the family.  I followed the recipe exactly as stated with perfect results.  I was lucky to get one or two of these from my son; he just inhaled them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
big chocolate chip birthday cookie

my neighbor marilyn gave me this recipe several years ago; not sure where she got this...but marilyn....this recipe has 'served me well' over the years!!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. spray a 15 inch flat pizza pan or 10 inch springform pan with pan spray to prevent sticking
3. mix flour , soda and salt , set aside
4. beat butter and shortening in a large bowl with a mixer on medium speed to just combine
5. mix in sugars
6. beat with electric mixer until mixture is smooth
7. mix in egg and vanilla on low speed until blended thoroughly
8. add flour mixture , mixing just until incorporated
9. mix in chocolate chips , stir by hand
10. using fingers , spread dougn into a 10 inch circle on the pizza or springform pan
11. smooth edges
12. if using the pizza pan , bake cookie about 14 minutes , until edges are light brown and center is golden
13. if using the springform pan , bake for about 18 minutes , until evenly light brown
14. loosen the edge of the cookie from the pan , cool thoroughly
15. remove sides of springform pan
16. optional: put spoonfuls of peanut butter on top of the cookie as it's cooling
17. allow it to 'melt' slightly and then spread around
18. sprinkle with chocolate chips , allow those to melt and spread around
demonstrations.review: I made this for my teenager because he did not want cake and he only had a short time for an informal celebratory goodie.  I used two tablespoons of coconut oil instead of the shortening.  I also added some chocolate chips on top and spread them around, which made a very nice topping that was superb with some decorative icing and really made the cookie special.  My three boys and a teen guest with cooking experience all said this was much better than store-bought large cookies that have been purchased and tasted in the past.  I will definitely make this again, and it is a very versatile recipe.

target.recipe_text:
ooey  gooey  chewy chocolate chip cookies

i have had so many requests for this recipe so i thought i'd better share. these cookies bake up fat and chewy with just the right amount of crisp! the quick oats give these cookies their incredible texture. and you would never guess there were oats anywhere in these cookies. i make these every sunday night- a family tradition.

1. cream butter and both sugars
2. mix all dry ingredients in a separate small bowl
3. add 2 eggs , one at a time , to creamed ingredients
4. add vanilla
5. mix well
6. add dry ingredients a little at a time until it's all well incorprated
7. mix in chocolate chips
8. i roll these into about golf ball sized balls and bake at 350 for 12-13 minutes
9. take them out just as they are barely beginning to brown
10. the key is to not overbake these ! let them cool for 2 minutes on the cookie sheet and then transfer to wire rack
11. hint: if your cookies spread too much while baking , try putting the dough in the fridge for a while before baking up the next batch
12. if that doesn't work , add a bit more flour to it
target.review: Oatmeal has been the secret to my Chocolate Chip Cookies for years.  I highly recommend this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
harvest pumpkin pie

this is a delicious pumpkin pie recipe. very simple and a nice presentation.

1. beat eggs
2. add pumpkin , spices and salt
3. blend in milk
4. pour into pie crust
5. bake 425f for 15 minutes
6. reduce heat to 350f and bake for 45 minutes
7. test center of pie with toothpick , must come out clean
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I have used  this recipe 45 years.  After trying several variations, I still go back to this version.  We think it is  the best!  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: I made these  last  weekend  and  have had nothing but raves.  Everyone loved them.  Will definitely  make  them again.........I think I am going to try the mini muffin papers for the holidays   and make individual ones.   Also  will add parchment   or wax paper to the pan so I can lift the bars out  of the pan before I slice them..........Thanks for sharing this fantastic  recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mix in the pan chocolate cake

when you don't think that you have enough time to make a homemade cake, don't even think about using a cake mix. instead make this easy homemade chocolate cake that is mixed in the pan it is baked in. top this moist cake with any type of frosting you want or no frosting at all. i got this recipe from martha stewert's everyday food magazine from november 2009.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a square 9 inch pan stir together flour , sugar , cocoa , baking soda , and salt
3. add oil , vinegar , water , and vanilla
4. mix until combined , making sure there are no clumps of flour mixture
5. spread batter evenly in pan
6. bake until toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean , about 35 to 40 minutes
7. let cake cool completley on a cooling rack
demonstrations.review: I got this recipe from my grandmother when I was a teenager.  I am 68 years old and still use it on occasions.  It is really easy and very tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
1 pan fudge cake

this is my favorite chocolate cake. no fuss, no mess and very moist. back in the early days when it was paycheck to paycheck, this simple dessert made it into his lunchbox many a day because it was cheap and simple. no eggs, no milk.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in an ungreased 9 x 13 pan- yes ungreased , sift all dry ingredients
3. add the liquids and stir just until blended
4. bake for 25 minutes
5. frost with your favorite frosting , cake is extremely moist so care must be taken that you don't tear up the top of the cake
demonstrations.review: My grandmother taught me how to bake this cake when I was  a little girl......She called it a Finger Cake, because she mixed it with her hands........I am 70 plus and still use this recipe and mix it with my fingers!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked pork chops and apples

i found this in a pamphlet from the orchard (about maryland apple orchards) a few years ago when we were picking apples. it is one of the tastiest things i have ever made!

1. peel , core , and slice the apples
2. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
3. melt the butter in a skillet
4. brown the pork chops on both sides in the butter
5. grease a large baking dish
6. put the apple slices in the bottom of the dish
7. mix the brown sugar and cinnamon
8. sprinkle the cinnamon and sugar over the apples
9. place the pork chops on top of the apples
10. cover with foil and bake for 1 and 1 / 2 hours
demonstrations.review: I used bone in Pork Chops about 1 inch thick.  The apples turned to mush and the Pork Chops were soooooooo dry.  I have been cooking for 52 years and should have known that the Pork Chops will cook in 20 minutes in the oven.  The next time I try this recipe, I will slice the apples a lot thicker and check them after 30 minutes to make sure they are done.  I know the Pork Chops will be done.

target.recipe_text:
best ever pumpkin pie

southern living. always served for thanksgiving dinner.

1. combine pumpkin and remaining ingredients in a large bowl
2. beat at medium speed with an electric mixer 2 minutes
3. pour into prepared piecrust
4. bake at 425 degrees for 15 minutes
5. reduce heat to 350 degrees
6. bake 50 additional minutes or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean
7. cool on a wire rack
target.review: Awesome pie! Sweeter than your traditional Libby's pie, and every bit as delicious. Everyone loved it and asked for more. What better compliment can you get?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chickpeas and rice

this is a recipe that i got from a vegetarian cookbook and made a few modifications to.  we have fallen for this dish and now make it a few times a month.  my two year old also loves it.  we tried it out on some non-vegetarians and they all loved it.

1. cook water , rice , thyme , and bay leaf and set aside
2. heat olive oil and half of the butter in a skillet and then add chickpeas
3. when chickpeas start to lightly brown add parsley and the sun-dried tomatoes and cook for an additional 5 minutes
4. add oregano , basil , salt , and pepper and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes
5. remove from heat and mix rice and chickpeas together until rice is a golden color
6. mix in remaining butter and parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: We love this dish. I always add nearly a whole bunch of fresh asparagus, and a little extra cheese. I make this at least once a month. Before this dish I had never eaten chickpeas, except in hummus, and now I eat them all the time!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fluffy 7 minute frosting

this was my absolute favorite frosting when i was growing up. it is so light, fluffy and fat-free too.

1. combine sugar , water , egg whites , corn syrup , and salt in the top of a double boiler
2. blend
3. place over simmering water
4. using an electric mixer , beat the mixture constantly at high speed for 7 minutes or until the mixture triples in volume and holds firm peaks
5. remove from heat
6. beat in vanilla
7. spread on cooled 2 layer cake
demonstrations.review: Without a doubt, the most beautiful frosting I've ever made. The consistency is so fluffy it smooths out all my sloppy knife strokes and looks like something out of a magazine! I had to cook/whip mine for about 15 minutes (maybe a few more actually) so it had me worried for a few minutes there. Came out beautifully, though. It's not as sweet as some other recipes, but it has a lovely flavor, and everyone raved about it. Again, it's stunningly beautiful--shiny, satiny finish. Will definitely make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
little debbie oatmeal cream pie

i found this on the web, and since they're the absolute favorite of my grandson, i made them for him. we couldn't tell the difference! the only thing is-these are a lot fresher!

1. in large bowl , cream margarine , sugars , molasses , vanilla , and eggs
2. combine flour , salt , baking soda , and cinnamon
3. add to the creamed mixture
4. mix in the oats
5. drop dough by tbsp on ungreased sheets
6. bake at 350f
7. bake for 10-12 minutes , or until just starting to brown around the edges
8. they will look moist
9. don't overcook
10. while the cookies bake prepare the filling
11. in small bowl , dissolve the salt in the hot water
12. allow this to cool
13. combine marshmallow cream , shortening , powdered sugar , and vanilla in med bowl
14. mix on hi until fluffy
15. add the cooled salt water and mix well
16. spread filling on flat side of one cookie , press 2nd cookie on top
demonstrations.review: These are awesome! I have made them following the recipe and they're great. Today I made a gluten free batch, using Pamela's Artisan Flour Blend (her pancake/baking blend would be great too). I used 1/2 cup oat flour (just grind the oats in the food processor) and just under 2 cups of the GF flour blend, plus 1/2 tsp xanthan gum and an additional 1/2 tsp baking soda. Took me a few tries to get them to turn out just right, but those measurements did the trick. Delicious, as always!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chess pie

very rich, chocolaty and delicious!

1. preheat oven to 325f degrees
2. combine sugar , cocoa , flour , and salt
3. blend in milk
4. beat in eggs 1 at a time
5. add butter and vanilla , beat until smooth
6. pour into prebaked pie shell
7. bake in 325 oven for 55-60 minutes
demonstrations.review: If you're looking for a new twist on your old chess pie, you'll be very pleased...but if you're looking for a chocolate fix, you might want to go for a more traditional chocolate pie. I thought it was more chessy than chocolatey, but it was very tasty either way. Shared the rest of the pie with co-workers and it disappeared immediately.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers chocolate chip blondies 3 points

didn't know a diet could taste so good:)

1. preheat oven to 350f in a small bowl , combine flour , baking powder and salt
2. in a large bowl , beat brown sugar and butter until fluffy
3. add egg whites and vanilla
4. gradually beat in flour mixture alternating with water
5. stir in chips
6. spread into a foil-lined 9- x 13-inch baking pan
7. bake until golden , about 20 to 25 minutes
8. cool on wire rack
9. remove foil and cut into 24 two-inch squares
demonstrations.review: If I hadn't made them myself I would never have guessed they're a lower fat/cal dessert. They're awesome!

target.recipe_text:
muffin size passover vegetable kugels

some weeks ago chia helped me with suggestions of how to make smaller sized kugels. and lo and behold, while browsing on the net i found this recipe. tweaked it a bit to my liking and immediately tried it. such a good idea to use muffin tins. besides passover, matzohmeal can of course be substituted for flour. thanks chia for the initial suggestions.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. grease 12 muffin tins or ramekins
3. heat oil in a skillet
4. saute onion , celery , carrots and peppers 2-3 minutes , or until onion is translucent
5. place drained spinach in a bowl
6. add eggs , sauteed vegetables and matzoh meal
7. season with salt and pepper
8. mix well
9. spoon into prepared tins
10. bake 35-40 minutes
target.review: These were really good.  I made them as instructed and the texture was perfect.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked red snapper with citrus   tomato topping

this is a slightly alterd recipe from epicurious. the spicy hot topping makes a nice change for baked fish.

1. preheat oven to 475 degrees
2. coat the red snapper on both sides with some of the olive oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. place the fish in a 9-inch glass pie dish
4. mix remaining oil , tomatoes w / green chilies , tangerine pieces , green onions and cilantro in a small bowl
5. season topping to taste with salt and pepper , and fish herbs
6. spoon the topping over the red snapper
7. bake until snapper is just opaque in center , about 15-20 minutes
8. can be cooked through if preferred
9. sprinkle almonds on top of each serving
demonstrations.review: I made this fish using Orange Roughy instead of snapper and it was really good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maureen s chicken schnitzel lite

easier and a lighter version of traditional schnitzel. credited to maureen clancy in cooking light magazine.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. place chicken breasts between 2 sheets of heavy plastic wrap and pound to 1 / 2" thickness
3. salt and pepper to taste
4. place flour in shallow dish
5. combine egg and mustard in another shallow dish
6. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , parsley , chives and garlic in another shallow dish and mix to blend
7. dredge each chicken breast in flour
8. then in egg mixture
9. then in breadcrumb mixture to coat evenly
10. heat olive oil in heavy ovenproof skillet over med-hi heat
11. saute chicken on one side until browned about 2 1 / 2 minutes
12. remove from heat
13. and turn chicken to place unbrowned side down in skillet
14. place in oven and bake for 10 minutes or until chicken is done and browned on underside
15. serve with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic. I put the recipe into the Weight Watcher Calculater and it computes to 6 pts. I loved the mustard and parmesan combination, and baking it kept it nice and juicy.  My family loved this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken drumsticks pierre

this is a very easy recipe for a chicken dish that will suit people who like their chicken spicy, but not too hot. served on a bed of rice, it is colorful and elegant enough for company. update:  i suggest that you not substitute regular mustard for dry mustard. regular mustard is made by mixing dry mustard with a substantial amount of vinegar and will completely change the flavor of the dish.

1. mix together the flour , salt and pepper
2. dust the drumsticks with the seasoned flour
3. melt the butter in a skillet with a lid
4. brown the chicken over medium heat on all sides
5. remove the chicken from the pan and drain on absorbent paper
6. in the same pan , combine the tomatoes thru hot pepper sauce
7. bring to a boil
8. reduce the heat and return the chicken to the pan
9. cover and simmer about 45 minutes
10. serve with pan juice
11. good over white or brown rice
demonstrations.review:
I have made this several times now and realized I did not rate it.  It is one of my family favorites.  I have used both drumsticks and boneless breasts.    I found the recipe easy to follow and quick to prepare.

This sauce is so good I am going to try it on other meats/fish.  Thanks for the post.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey cutlets with balsamic brown sugar sauce

i think this recipe would work with thin chicken cutlets as well or maybe even pork.

1. combine first four ingredients in a shallow dish , stir well
2. dredge turkey cutlets in flour mixture
3. heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
4. add cutlets and cook 3 minutes on each side or until done
5. remove cutlets from pan , set aside , and keep warm
6. reduce heat to warm
7. add shallots to pan and saute for 1 minute
8. stir in wine and broth , scraping pan to loosen brown bits
9. bring to boil , reduce heat and cook 5 minutes
10. add balsamic vinegar , sugar , and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt
11. bring to a boil
12. reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes
13. return cutlets to the pan to warm through
14. serve sauce with cutlets
demonstrations.review: Very nice flavor but I would recommend that if you are not serving right away to keep the sauce on the side.  The cutlets have such a nice crisp coat and when they sit in the sauce they tend to get a little soggy.  Thanks for the post.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
plain roasted artichoke hearts

can't believe it, but there's no other recipe like this on recipezaar (unless i somehow missed it).  these babies are so, so good.  i roasted canned artichoke hearts in connection with another recipe i invented, and was so pleased with the way they came out even without the topping, so i'm posting a plain(er) version.  if you want the topped version, go to recipe no. 144997.  i found that roasting them enhanced the taste and texture - made them more tender on the inside:d  one of these "throw it in the oven and ignore while you are fixing other parts of dinner" recipes!

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. drain artichokes in colander and rinse a bit to remove brine
3. mix gently with garlic and olive oil in a bowl
4. pour artichoke mixture in a metal roasting pan and roast for about one hour , tossing a few times if desired
5. sprinkle with salt and pepper , and add lemon juice and butter
demonstrations.review:
I roasted these and mixed with other roasted vegetables red, yellow and orange bell peppers, carrots, and asparagus.  They were really good.

Thanks for the post.

target.recipe_text:
best banana pudding

this is very yummy and simple.

when my husband has a potluck at work everyone asks 
for this luscious pudding.

1. whip cream until thick
2. beat milk , water and pudding with a wire whisk
3. chill 5 minutes
4. fold in cream
5. put1 cup pudding mixture in bottom of a large glass bowl
6. now a layer of cookies
7. now a layer of sliced bananas
8. repeat layers with cookies on top
9. chill 24 hours
target.review: This was a big hit tonight after dinner! I'll be making this one again! It was super easy, and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
unbelievable baked buffalo wings

here's a healthy alternative to fried wings: one of my famous recipes! the meat will fall off the bone! unbelievable!

1. fill a large pot half way with water and then add the first 4 ingredients
2. bring water mixture and wings to a boil and then boil for 15 minutes
3. transfer wings to an oven safe container coated with cooking spray
4. bake wings on "broil" for 15 minutes on each side
5. while waiting for wings , combine the hot sauce and margarine in a microwave safe container and cook in microwave for 2 minutes or until melted
6. when wings are done , shake 'em up with the sauce and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: These are awesome. They were a huge it even with my picky eaters! I will be making these again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
big hit meatloaf

this recipe is a combination of many failed attempts to make a meatloaf my husband will love.   this one hit the mark!  great with garlic green beans and green salad.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. combine all ingredients in a large bowl
3. mix well
4. shape into rectangle and place into greased loaf pan
5. bake for 1 hr and 10 min or until thermometer reads 165
6. drain and let sit for ten minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was very quick and easy. My whole family loved it. This is the first time that we have not had leftover meatloaf! We will certainly make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy refried refried beans

my sister-in-law who was born and raised in mexico city shared this recipe for sprucing up canned refried beans. they taste like you've been cooking them for hours.

1. gently fry the bacon until near crisp
2. add onion to the bacon grease and saute until tender
3. add the refried beans and water
4. stir and simmer until creamy and heated through
5. place in a serving bowl and top with shredded cheese
6. the heat of the beans will melt the cheese
7. serve with hot tortillas and / or tostada chips
demonstrations.review: So easy, and so good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick   easy garlic chicken with parmesan

quick? easy? garlic? parmesan?

really? do you guys need anymore encouragement? try this one! you can't go wrong.

1. melt butter
2. add garlic to butter
3. place chicken in a single layer in a baking dish
4. mix cheese & seasonings
5. cover chicken with cheese mixture
6. pour garlic butter over the top
7. bake at 350 until chicken is no longer pink
demonstrations.review: This was so easy, and so good! I will be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed red potatoes with garlic and parmesan

the potatoes are ready in our garden, and this is the first recipe i reach for! these are so good!!

1. put potatoes and garlic in lg pan
2. cover with water
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes , until potatoes are tender
5. drain well
6. mash with the butter , milk , and salt
7. stir in the parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: This were so quick, easy, and yummy! I plan to make this again!

target.recipe_text:
chocolate torte

i've been making this for years.  it's very rich and always a special occasion when this is served!

1. preheat oven to 250 degrees
2. grease a springform pan
3. dust with cocoa
4. line bottom with kitchen parchment
5. in 2 qt saucepan over low heat , melt chocolate with butter
6. in large bowl , with wire whisk beat egg yolks and vanilla
7. slowly beat warm chocolate mixture into yolk mixture until blended
8. in small bowl with mixer at high speed , beat egg whites until soft peaks form
9. gradually beat in 1 / 4 cup powdered sugar until sugar dissolves and whites stand in stiff peaks
10. fold beaten egg whites into chocolate mixture , one third at a time
11. spoon batter into pan spreading evenly
12. bake torte 1 hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out almost clean
13. cool torte in pan
14. when torte is cool , remove side of pan then remove torte from pan bottom
15. discard parchment
16. cut torte in 12 wedges
17. sprinkle 6 wedges with cocoa , remaining 6 wedges with confectioners sugar
18. arrange wedges alternately on cake plate
target.review: This was excellent and very easy to make (didn't even take 1/2 hour of prep time unless you have trouble separating the eggs).  Per another review, I also used bittersweet chocolate, the Trader Joe's Pound Plus which is excellent quality, and it was delicious!  I skipped the powdered sugar and cocoa topping and didn't miss it.  I used a 9 inch springform (the recipe doesn't specify, but it's the only one I had), and it was perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
divine vanilla cupcakes

these cup cakes are little bites of heaven. moist and super delicious. from 'kitchen for kids' they are great to bake along side little ones.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. line 2 muffin tins with paper liners
3. sift flour , baking powder and salt int a bowl and mix
4. in another bowl cream sugar and butter , stir in eggs
5. gradually add milk and vanilla and spoon flour mixture in until all mixed and smooth
6. spoon batter into liners to about 3 / 4 full
7. bake 27-28 min until tops are golden and spring back or a toothpick comes out clean
demonstrations.review: This recipe makes really good cupcakes although I did follow the suggestions of other reviewers. 1 cup of sugar is plenty even if you don't plan to use frosting, and if you are going to frost these, definitely don't use the full 1 1/2 cups. I also doubled the vanilla and I think if you used just what was called for, it probably wouldn't have as much flavor. The texture was crumbly but not too much so and they were quite moist and just dense enough to be satisfying but not so dense that they were too heavy. Even my daughter, who is a chocoholic and doesn't get excited about vanilla anything, gave them a major thumbs up. Plus, what I really liked is that they had a great texture on the outside that made them a breeze to frost. This made 20 cupcakes that went just to the top of the muffin cup. If you want really big cupcakes, it will probably only make about 14 or so.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken divan

the only prep work is a little chopping--the crock pot does the rest and in only a few hours. no broccoli or cheese (unless you want to add them, but it doesn't need it). i double the curry powder since we have strong palates.

1. cut chicken , celery and onion into bite-size pieces and put in crock pot
2. add rest of ingredients and stir to combine well
3. cover and cook on high for 2-3 hours or low for 6-8 hours
4. serve over rice or noodles
demonstrations.review: Delicious and so easy!!  I followed the recipe for cream of chicken soup referenced above but substituted margerine and rice milk since I am dairy free, and it still came out great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork cider stew

my family loves this hearty stew. easy because it is made in a slow-cooker.

1. cut pork shoulder roast into 1-inch cubes
2. add meat cubes , potatoes , carrots , onions , apple , celery , and tapioca to a large slow-cooker
3. add in the remaining ingredients
4. stir to combine
5. cover and cook on low for 8-10-12 hours
demonstrations.review: Very flavorful and easy to make.  I didn't have tapioca, so I used cornstarch and it came out just fine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana bread with coconut milk

i came up with this last night. it is a good way to use up leftover coconut milk. like all banana breads, the flavor is much better the second day.

1. mix wet ingredients , and dry ingredients
2. mixture will be lumpy
3. pour mixture into a greased loaf pan , and bake at 350 for 30-40 minutes , or until a cake tester inserted in the middle of the loaf comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Delicious.  I can't have dairy so this was perfect.  Easy to make too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole wheat hamburger and hot dog buns  bread machine

this is from bread machine magic. the best bun we ever had. when barbecuing, i usually divide the dough in half and make 4 burger buns and 6 hot dog buns.

1. place all ingredients in bread pan , select dough setting , and press start
2. when dough has risen enough , the machine will beep
3. remove bread pan , and turn out dough onto a floured countertop
4. gently roll and shape the dough into a 12-inch rope
5. with a sharp knife , divide dough into 8 pieces for hamburger buns or 12 pieces for hot dog buns
6. grease a baking sheet
7. roll pieces of dough into balls and flatten for hamburger buns or shape into 6-inch rolls for hot dog buns
8. place on prepared baking sheet
9. cover and let rise in warm oven 10 to 15 minutes until almost doubled
10. preheat oven to 400f bake 10 to 12 minutes until golden brown
11. remove from oven and cool on racks
12. when ready to use , split buns horizontally
13. these will keep in plastic bag in the freezer for 3 to 4 weeks
demonstrations.review: These buns are awesome and so incredibly easy to make. I followed other suggestions and used 1 1/2 c of apf and wwf and 1/4 c of olive oil, and they came out just perfectly. My kids had a blast rolling the dough and shaping it into buns. What I liked most about them is that they are very light, flaky and moist. The texture is wonderful. Thanks for a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
cheese sauce  vegan

this is the simplest and best tasting vegan cheese sauce recipe we've found.  we got it from our cousin diana p. who got it from who knows where.  we like it best for nachos.  it works well for mac'n'cheese as well as enchiladas or any recipe that calls for a cheese sauce.

1. rinse cashews with hot water while combining the remaining ingredients in a blender
2. add cashews to blender and process on high for 1-2 minutes
3. cook in a sauce pan over medium heat , stirring constantly , until thick
4. add chiles and serve or use in other recipes that call for cheese sauce
target.review: OMG this is awesome!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
finger lickin good bbq sauce

this is sooo delicious makes me lick my fingers!

1. put olive oil in a sauce pan on medium heat and cook onion and garlic until they are soft
2. then add the white vinegar , ketchup , brown sugar , worcestershire sauce , chili powder , and cayenne pepper
3. let this simmer for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was gooood!!! I used accidentally used smoked paprika instead of chili powder (oops!). I added 1tsp ancho chile powder hoping it would balance it out... turned out great!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chili you will ever taste

this is the best chili recipe i have ever tried. i'm not sure where the recipe originated, but it is amazing! sometimes, i don't bother adding all four cans of the kidney beans and it still turns out wonderful. once anyone tastes this chili, they will be begging for the recipe!! enjoy!

1. heat oil
2. cook onions , garlic and meat until brown
3. add tomatoes , beer , coffee , tomato paste and beef broth
4. add spices stir in 2 cans of kidney beans and peppers
5. reduce heat and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
6. add 2 remaining cans of kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was good but I tweaked it to make it better (in my family's opinion) and I won a chili contest! I changed/added the followingI used 1 1/2lb beef sirloin, 2 canned diced tomatoes instead of 1, 1 larger can Guinness beer, 1 cup Starbucks drip coffee with a shot of espresso added in, 4 Tbsp chili sauce - "Homemade" brand in ketchup aisle (round glass jar w/white lid), added 1/4 tsp cinnamon, 3-4 shakes of red pepper flake, added 1 can pinto or white northern beans. I cook it in the crockpot on low overnight or for 8-10 hours during the day then I put it in the fridge for 8-10 hours before reheating and serving for the first time. Excellent out of the freezer too. Thanks for posting!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
san diego style champagne margarita

i found this on the cook's champagne website for cocktails. they have many great recipes there. yummy!

1. combine together lime juice , tequila , triple sec and champagne in a festive glass
2. garnish with citrus
3. serve with fiesta dip , chips and salsa
4. enjoy !
5. )
demonstrations.review: It was good but I'm not sure I'd make it again unless I had people over - personal preference, no fault to the recipe. I used Hornitos tequila, Bols triple sec, fresh lime and Ballatore champagne. Great idea though!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted brussels sprouts

i got this from the barefoot contessa cookbook. so good.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cut off the ends of the brussels sprouts and pull off any yellow outer leaves
3. mix them in a bowl with the olive oil , salt , and lemon-pepper seasoning
4. transfer them to a sheet pan and roast for 35 to 40 minutes , until crisp outside and tender inside
5. shake the pan from time to time to brown the brussels sprouts evenly
6. sprinkle with more kosher salt , if you like , and serve hot
demonstrations.review: I wasn't too crazy about this one. Maybe my brussels sprouts were too large or maybe my oven just sucks but they didn't turn out any different than any other type of bs I've made before. They were definitely nothing like popcorn - the outside wasn't crispy at all and I cooked them for about 40 minutes. BUT the leaves that fell off during cooking were crispy and yummy.... made me think of Kale Chips I make all the time.... maybe I will peel off all the leaves and then roast them! Crispy and yummy like potato chips. Overall I was disappointed that these didn't turn out as well as everyone said but I'll keep trying!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal cottage cheese pancakes

these are wonderful and are almost too healthy to be true. lots of calcium, protein, fiber, etc. i usually eat them without any topping and just keep popping them in my mouth! yum. but a good jam will do them nicely as well.

1. blend all ingredients in blender
2. spray skillet with cooking spray and cook just like"silver dollar" pancakes , a few small ones at a time
3. top with your favorite pancake topping !
demonstrations.review: These are sooo good! I add 1/4 cup quick oats and 1/2 tsp cinnamon. Great recipe!!

target.recipe_text:
lunchroom tamale pie

this is one of those old recipes that tastes like the school lunchroom tamale pie. i always ate in the lunchroom on the day they served this. it is also one of the recipes that i just do, so prep time is an estimate only.

1. brown ground chuck
2. add onion , bell pepper , and cook until tender
3. add chili powder , black pepper , garlic powder , 1 teaspoons
4. salt and tomatoes
5. simmer for 10 minutes and keep warm
6. mix cornmeal with cold water
7. add boiling water and cook about 10 minutes , or until thick
8. add 1 teaspoons salt , stir well
9. spray a 9 x 13-inch casserole dish with cooking spray
10. use 2 / 3 of cornmeal mixture on bottom& sides of casserole dish
11. pour meat mixture into casserole dish
12. spread the remaining 1 / 3 of cornmeal mixture over meat mixture
13. dot with margarine
14. bake at 375f for 40 minutes
target.review: I have been looking for a recipe like this one! Definitely a keeper! I used ground turkey and a seasoning packet which was not as spicy as I hoped. Next time I will REALLY *spice* it up and maybe use salsa as a timesaver instead of chopping the onions & green peppers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli   cheese soup

a great soup, one of the deli classics.

1. saute onion and celery in butter in saucepan over medium heat until tender
2. add flour , and salt and pepper , cooking and stirring until mixture is smooth and bubbly
3. add broth and milk , stirring constantly until mixture comes to a boil and begins to thicken
4. add cooked broccoli , stirring until all is heated through
5. remove from heat and stir in cheese until melted and smooth
demonstrations.review: Woweee!!!! This was SO, SO, SO good!!!! I have been wanting a good recipe for this soup and my search is over! Sue, I never heard of steaming the broccoli first but it sure did preserve the BRIGHT green of the broccoli and made it look so much more appetizing than the gray-green color it fades to after extended cooking. I followed the recipe exactly except for the addition of about 1/4 c. of diced ham that I needed to use up. Next time I will double the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy peanut butter fudge

i got it from my friend, already tried it a few times.

1. grease a 9x13 inch baking dish
2. in medium saucepan over medium heat , combine sugar , brown sugar , butter and evaporated milk
3. bring to a boil
4. stirring constantly , boil for 7 minutes
5. remove from heat
6. stir in marshmallow creme until well incorporated and melted
7. stir in peanut butter and vanilla until smooth
8. spread in prepared pan
9. let cool before cutting into squares
demonstrations.review: Wonderful fudge! This reminds me of the peanut butter balls my grandma used to make. I don't usually care for fudge, but this one is a winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect punch

this is a really easy punch to do. i always make it when we are having alot of people over. it's good for kids and adults.

1. puree orange juice and lemonade concentrates in a blender with water
2. pour into large container
3. add pineapple juice
4. puree frozen strawberries and combine with other juices
5. when ready to serve , pour half the juice mixture into punch bowl
6. add half the sherbert and half the soda
7. stir gently and serve
8. when the bowl is empty repeat with remaining ingredients
demonstrations.review: Tongue-tingling good and fun to make! I made this for my family's Christmas celebration. I omitted the strawberries and used twice as much lemon-lime soda.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fat free lemon herb roasted veggies

i made this to satisfy one of my constant roasted-veggie cravings! you won't believe how filling this is; it'll do for lunch along with a fruit or juice, honest! if you like a stronger lemon flavour, use more of the concentrate. the combination of herbs is really quite wonderful, if i do say so myself :-) enjoy! (note: prep. time includes marinating time).

1. peel and chop the veggies as directed and place them in a large ziplock bag
2. in a non-metallic bowl , mix together the marinade ingredients and mix well
3. pour the marinade into the ziplock bag , seal it , and shake it well such that all the veggies are coated with the herb marinade
4. let it sit for at least 30 minutes
5. preheat oven to 200 degrees celcius
6. spray a casserole dish or baking sheet lightly with cooking spray
7. remove the veggies from the ziplock bag and arrange them on the dish / tray
8. bake on the top rack of the oven for 35 to 40 minutes , or until the veggies are as done as you want them
9. turn once or twice during baking
10. alternately , you can also grill the veggies in skewers , i prefer that way !
11. after they're done , pile the veggies onto a large plate , season with extra salt and pepper if required , pour yourself a tall glass of cold fruit juice , and sit down to a shockingly healthy and light lunch !
demonstrations.review: I used russet potatoes, sweet potatoes, onions, yellow & red bell peppers and tomatoes and 2 TBSP Reconstituted lemon juice. I will use less next time because although it was AWESOME, I think it interfered with the natural sweet roasted flavor of the veggies. I LOVE that this is fat-free! This recipe proves you don't necessarily need the oil for roasting veggies!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab stuffed chicken  aka fancy chicken

i was searching the internet 2 valentines days ago for a romantic, not too foo-fooey recipe and found this (don't remember what site). this is now my bh's version of comfort food, whenever he feels down he asks me to make "that fancy chicken". i like to serve it with garlic mashed potatoes.

1. combine cream cheese , crabmeat , and soup mix , set aside
2. cut a 'pocket' into the side of each chicken breast
3. fill each pocket with the cream cheese mixture and close the opening with toothpicks
4. dip chicken breasts in flour-> eggs-> breadcrumbs
5. in large skillet , melt oil and butter over medium-high heat
6. add chicken to skillet , cook for 10 minutes , or till golden brown , turning once
7. transfer chicken to 13x9 pan and bake in a 350f oven , uncovered , for 15 minutes or until chicken is done
demonstrations.review: This was my first experience stuffing chicken and it was SO easy! I will make this again, most def! My husband LOVED this, my brother was very impressed and I was pleased as punch to serve it and eat it! I pounded the chicken breasts flat with a meat mallet and discovered a creative outlet for stress! I also used imitation crabmeat- the results were fabulous!

target.recipe_text:
zucchini parmesan with lemon

and now for something completely different................

1. cut zucchini in half crosswise , then cut each half into 4 lengthwise sticks
2. heat oil in a heavy nonstick skillet over medium high heat
3. saut zucchini and lemon peel about 3 minutes , stirring frequently , until zucchini is lightly browned
4. mix in parmesan cheese and pepper to taste
target.review: Great tasting and so good for you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican fiesta casserole

i adopted this recipe in february 2005.  while i'm not much of a casserole person, this one looks to be pretty good.

1. preheat the oven to 375f
2. cook the ground beef in a large skillet until browned
3. drain off the excess fat
4. season the meat with the salt and pepper
5. set aside
6. mix together the cheese , sour cream , mayonnaise and onion
7. set this mixture aside
8. stir the biscuit mix and water together until a soft dough forms
9. with floured fingers , pat the dough into the bottom of a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan , pressing the dough about 1 / 2-inch up the sides of the pan
10. layer the browned ground beef , tomato slices , green pepper , and sliced olives over the dough layer
11. spoon the sour cream and cheese mixture over the top
12. bake , uncovered , until the edges of the dough are light brown , 25 to 30 minutes
13. cool 5 minutes and then cut into squares to serve
demonstrations.review: Very good. Since I'm on a low fat diet I used all reduced or no fat ingredients and it was still very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hearty baked bean casserole

i typically use the tinned maple baked beans in this; if you use regular baked beans you may want to add an extra tbsp of brown sugar. this is great on a cold day.

1. preheat oven to 300f degrees
2. in a large skillet , cook bacon until crisp
3. remove and drain fat from skillet
4. crumble bacon and set aside
5. in the same skillet , brown the ground beef and onion
6. drain off any fat
7. combine all ingredients in a casserole dish and bake for 2 hours
8. i keep it covered during the first hour , then remove the cover and stir , and leave the cover off for the last hour of cooking , although the original recipe did not specify this
demonstrations.review: Very good way to use left over baked beans.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon toast rollups

i make these at the cottage and the kids like to grab a few with some fruit to eat on the dock in the mornings......fast and easy....

1. stir together first 3 ingredients
2. unroll crescent rolls
3. brush with melted butter , and sprinkle evenly with sugar mixture
4. separate dough into triangles
5. roll up each triangle , starting with shortest side
6. place on a lightly greased baking sheet
7. bake at 350 degrees for 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown
8. remove to a wire rack to cool
demonstrations.review: Easy and tasty.  Quick breakfast on school mornings.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted mustard potatoes

nan

1. preheat oven 400f degrees
2. spray roasting pan with cooking spray
3. whisk all ingredients , except potatoes , in a bowl
4. prick potatoes with a fork
5. toss with the mustard mix
6. place in the pan
7. bake 45 minutes to 1 hour
demonstrations.review: very good and so easy to make. we loved them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter corn flakes cookies

mom has made these every year during the holidays since i was a child. the family loves them and they are quite simple to make.

1. bring sugar and corn syrup to boil
2. remove from heat
3. add peanut butter and mix well
4. pour mixture over corn flakes
5. mix into balls onto waxed paper or spread into buttered pan
demonstrations.review: GREAT!!! I hardly got to taste them.  My son ate most of them first.

target.recipe_text:
weight watchers bbq pork sandwich w coleslaw

so good and so easy!!  only 6 points per serving. this recipe came from the ww website, so if you doubt the points value, check their site.

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. line a shallow roasting pan with nonstick foil
3. or coat pan with cooking spray
4. place pork in pan and brush with 2 tablespoons of barbecue sauce
5. roast until an instant read thermometer inserted in center of pork registers 160f for medium , about 25 minutes
6. transfer pork to a cutting board
7. cover loosely with foil and let stand 10 minutes
8. meanwhile , whisk mayonnaise , water , vinegar and pepper together in a medium bowl until smooth
9. add coleslaw mix and scallions
10. toss to mix and coat
11. slice pork into 20 slices
12. for each sandwich , place 5 slices of pork on the bottom half of each roll and drizzle with 1 teaspoon of barbecue sauce
13. top with 1 / 2 cup of coleslaw and cover with top half of roll
14. yields 1 sandwich per serving
target.review: Really good light version of a pulled pork sandwich.  I added one packet of Splenda and some celery seed to the cabbage.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork tenderloin with balsamic cranberry sauce

nan

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. melt 1 / 2 tablespoon butter in heavy large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat
3. sprinkle pork with salt and pepper
4. sear pork on all sides , about 2 minutes
5. place skillet with pork in oven
6. roast pork until thermometer inserted into center registers 155f , about 10 minutes
7. meanwhile , melt remaining 1 tablespoon butter in heavy medium skillet over medium-high heat
8. add onion and rosemary
9. saut until onion softens , about 3 minutes
10. add broth , cranberry sauce and vinegar and whisk until cranberry sauce melts , about 2 minutes
11. transfer pork to work surface
12. scrape any juices from large skillet into cranberry mixture
13. boil until sauce has reduced enough to coat spoon thickly , about 6 minutes
14. season with salt and pepper
15. slice pork and serve with sauce
demonstrations.review: This recipe is a family favorite.  I use it for easy entertaining as does my daughter-in-law.  Great substitute for T-day turkey for two.  Goes well with stuffing and other Thanksgiving sides.  I always double the sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast apple bake

this is a great make-ahead breakfast that will fill your home with the holiday aromas of cinnamon, spice and apples. it is a "soak overnight" casserole that mimics the flavors of french toast. call it bread pudding if you like, but i know you'll call it delicious. it makes holiday morning cooking a breeze. i think i must have gotten this recipe from taste of home.

1. in a skillet over medium heat , melt butter and add apples
2. stir occasionally until tender
3. add brown sugar and corn syrup
4. cook over low heat until sugar is dissolved
5. pour into buttered 9-by-13-inch baking pan
6. arrange bread slices over apple mixture
7. in bowl , beat eggs , milk , vanilla , salt and cinnamon until blended
8. pour mixture evenly over mixture in pan
9. cover with foil or plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight
10. next morning , preheat oven to 375 degrees
11. remove cover and bake for 35-45 minutes or until firm and brown
12. cool for 5 minutes , then flip onto large platter or foil covered cookie sheet with 1-inch edge
demonstrations.review: This has been a Christmas morning tradition  in our family for many years.  I now use cinnamon bread from a great local bakery instead of French bread.  Even better that way.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
braised red cabbage

nan

1. cut out core of cabbage and discard any tough or discolored outside leaves
2. slice cabbage in half or quarters , then slice lengthwise into 1 / 8-inch shreds
3. you should have about 12 cups
4. toss cabbage and onion in large nonstick skillet and add currants , vinegar , sugar , salt , pepper , oil and stock
5. bring to boil over high heat , then cover
6. reduce heat to medium and braise , stirring occasionally , until there is only a small amount of liquid left and cabbage is moist and just slightly crunchy , about 40 to 45 minutes
7. adjust seasonings and serve
8. comments: you can vary this dish to suit your taste or ingredients on hand
9. use regular or savoy cabbage
10. add minced garlic , apple slices or caraway seeds
11. or use part red wine or apple cider in the braising liquid
demonstrations.review: Used dried cherries instead of currants.  A simple dish with lots of flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4 minute spicy garlic shrimp

recipe is originally from the food network courtesy of rachael ray, but i tweaked it to fit our tastes. very quick & easy shrimp recipe that's done on the stovetop. if your tastes desire spicy & garlic, then this recipe is just for you.

1. heat a large skillet over medium high heat
2. add olive oil , garlic , red pepper flakes , and shrimp
3. season with grill seasoning or salt & pepper
4. cook shrimp 3 minutes or until just pink
5. toss with lemon zest , juice , & chopped parsley
6. remove shrimp to a serving platter , leaving the garlic cloves in the pan
demonstrations.review: This has become my go to shrimp recipe.  I dredge the shrimp lightly in flour and saute in a separate pan.  Then I add them to a pan in which I've heated the olive oil, pepper flakes and minced garlic. Then proceed as posted. Can't bear leaving the garlic behimd.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible french apple pie

not exactly gourmet, but very good.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees f
2. grease pie plate , 10" x 1 1 / 2"
3. mix apples and spices
4. turn into plate
5. beat remaining ingredients except for streusel till smooth
6. 15 seconds in blender or 1 minute with hand beater
7. pour into plate
8. sprinkle with streusel
9. bake till a knife inserted in the center comes out clean , 55-65 minutes
10. cool
11. for the streusel--------------------
12. mix bisquick , chopped nuts , brown sugar and margarine till crumbly
demonstrations.review: Turned out great for me.  Used a whole grain baking mix and increased the butter a bit to compensate.  Had some wonderful Golden Delicious apples that stayed firm.  That the bottom crust is not like a regular pastry is not an issue for me.

target.recipe_text:
strawberry soup

this soup is cold and is so refreshing on a summer day.

1. clean and cut strawberries in to pieces
2. reserve 1 1 / 2 cup of the cut strawberries
3. chill until serving time
4. add the strawberries , water and sugar to the blender and process until soupy
5. run mixture through a fine strainer to get all the liquid
6. discard the seeds and solids
7. pour into a large bowl and add the amaretto , stir
8. cover and place chill
9. in a small bowl mix sour cream with 1 / 4 cup powder sugar
10. cover and chill until serving time
11. to serve mix reserved strawberry pieces into soup
12. ladle soup into bowls
13. serve with a spoon of sour cream mixture in the middle
14. you may use equal amounts of splenda in place of the sugars
target.review: What an excellent and refreshing recipe. My first time ever trying or hearing of strawberry soup but I am very impressed. This would be excellent on a warm summer day. I loved it a lot, as did my family , and I can only imagine all of the yummy variations you could so of this dish. Thanks for a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lucky sweet and sour sauce

my most favorite sweet and sour sauce. i often add pineapple, sliced green pepper and maraschino cherries. you can use it as a dipping sauce or add it to cooked meat or poultry.

1. mix juice and cornstarch
2. heat oil in a small saucepan and add remaining ingredients and cornstarch mixture
3. cook over medium to medium high heat , stirring until sauce thickens
demonstrations.review: This is a great and easy recipe. I made thsi and poured it over Chinese Wontons (from this site). What a FANTASTIC combo. I used water instead of pineapple juice because my mom isnt a huge pineapple fan. Out of many dishes, the wontons and this sauce were the first to empty. Surprisingly, my mom loved the sauce, the first sweet and sour sauce she ever liked. Will certainly make again. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s rouladen

this is my mom's recipe for rouladen as taught to her by my dad's mother, with a couple of flavour enhancements from me.

1. lay the cutlets on a flat surface
2. spread each one with mustard , then sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. divide the pickles , bacon and onion evenly between the cutlets
4. roll up jelly roll style and secure with wooden toothpicks
5. heat the oil in a large saucepan
6. add the rouladen and brown well on all sides
7. pour in the broth and add the peppercorns and bay leaf
8. cover , simmer for 1 hour and 20 minutes
9. remove the rouladen
10. keep warm
11. blend the cornstarch with the cold water and add to the broth in the pan
12. bring to a boil and cook until thick and bubbly
13. stir in the sour cream and heat through
14. adjust the seasonings and serve
demonstrations.review: What an awesome recipe. My first attempt at rouladen and it was so simple. Your directions are really clear and this is a super tasty recipe. Everyone loved this recipe, even a friend of mine who's mother is German. I think the Dijon mustard really adds to the flavour. Definite make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry cheesecake tarts

delicious, impressive looking little tarts! you can use any type of berry you want, just make sure you use the same type of preserves as berries.
adapted from oregon strawberry recipes.

1. combine cream cheese , sour cream , sugar and lemon peel in small bowl
2. beat until smooth
3. spread evenly into tart shells
4. top with sliced strawberries , pressing into cream cheese mixture slightly
5. refrigerate about 4 hours
6. before serving , spread the strawberry preserves evenly over the filling
7. optional: drizzle melted chocolate over top !
demonstrations.review: Wonderful, wonderful recipe! Just like a strawberry cheesecake but in bite-sized form. Everyone was ooing and awing over these little tarts and all went back for more! I have had many requests for this recipe already. Simpe to make with fabulous results! Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hidden valley bacon and cheddar dip

this is always a hit and is simple to make! hope you like ranch!!!!

1. mix ranch dip with sour cream
2. add bacon bits and cheese
3. mix together well
4. serve with your favorite chips
demonstrations.review: Made this for Christmas Eve when my aunts and uncles came over. This went really fast and my aunt kept asking me for the recipe. The thing I canèt belive is how EASY it is to make. I can remeber this recipe having only made it once. Am sure to make it many more times. Nothing but pluses for this super dip. I serevd this with fresh cut up veggies. Thanks for a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple krispie cookies

perfect for those after school or late night snacks.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. in large bowl , mix all ingredients well
3. roll into 1-inch balls
4. place 2 in apart on lightly sprayed cooking sheet
5. bake for 10-12 minutes
6. cool for 1 minute
7. remove and cool completely
demonstrations.review: Made these a while back to give as Christmas gifts and am only getting around to reviewing now. This is an extremely simple yet totally awesome recipe. JUST DONT EAT THEM RIGHT AWAY! I gave my mom a cookie to sample when they were fresh out of the oven and her comment was that the cookies were "so-so". However, that night my mom samples another and declared that they were delicious. Much tastier and crispier than fresh out of the oven. Im sure the people on my Xmas list will be thrilled to be receiving these little gems. Thanks for a great, quick recipe.

target.recipe_text:
mushroom alfredo

this recipe came from a soup can label - it is easy to fix and quite tasty.   

1. in saucepan , combine soup , milk , red pepper , cheese , garlic and parsley
2. bring to boil at medium heat , stirring often
3. reduce heat and simmer for 5 mins
4. pour sauce over noodles and sprinkle with pepper and additional cheese if desired
5. i usually increase the garlic to 2 plus cloves
target.review: I was pretty impressed!!! I had started with some meatballs from costco with red pepper,and zucchini. had mushroom soup and didnt know what to do so found this recipe.it turned out pretty good!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffed any way you want hamburgers

you've got lots of options for stuffing these burgers!  :)  (please note:  this is an adopted recipe and needs some editing.)

1. mix all ingredients except the fillings
2. shape mixture into 12 thin patties , each about 3 1 / 2-inches in diameter
3. top each of 6 patties with a filling , spreading to within 1 / 2-inch of the edge
4. cover with a remaining patty , sealing the edges firmly
5. broil or grill patties 4-inches from the heat , carefully turning once , to the desired doneness , about 10 minutes
6. peppy cheese filling: mix all ingredients
demonstrations.review: These tasted awesome! But the only thing is, is I could not get the patties to stick together.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
2 in 1   herbed chicken   leftover chicken salad

this may be a first for recipezaar - two recipes in one! i had leftovers from the herbed chicken with no takers (if you know what i mean). this is delicious hot, but leftovers lose its appeal. hating to see food go to waste, i created an out-of-this world recipe for herbed chicken salad. (from now on, i will make sure i have leftovers for the chicken salad.) i doubled the original herbed chicken recipe to accommodate the chicken salad. if you like traditional chicken and chicken salad, search elsewhere. this is for those who are looking for unique flavors.

1. herbed chicken :
2. mix margarine with spices
3. coat chicken with herb mixture
4. place in baking dish skin side up bake in preheated 375 degree oven for 30 to 40 minutes or until done
5. for leftover chicken salad:
6. mix all leftover ingredients together
7. delicious served on a plate of lettuce- suppose you could put in a sandwich
8. probably would be best served the next day to let flavors blend mine didn't last that long
demonstrations.review: So I thought I would be smart and just dump all the butter/herb mixture overtop the chicken. Needless to say I had some very spicy chicken LOL. BUT the taste was awesome!!! Even my DH commented on how good it was! I also made the chicken salad but didnt have the onion or black olives but it was stil to die for!! Even if I just want chicken salad I will definately be using this recipe again. It's under my favorites now :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cook down home pork chops and gravy

i don't even like pork, but was tricked into tasting this dish when i was told it was chicken. wow! the meat was sooo tender and juicy; so tender in fact, that it was literally falling apart! it was like nothing i'd ever tasted before! definitely not like my mother's hard, crusty pork chops! lol! this recipes goes hand in hand w/ some mashed potatoes. just pour the leftover gravy on the taters' and enjoy!

1. combine 1st four ingredients in a shallow dish
2. dredge chops in flour mixture and set aside
3. combine what is left of the flour mixture w / the chicken broth and pour into your crock pot
4. pour oil into a large skillet and cook the chops in hot oil until browned on both sides
5. place chops in crock pot and cook covered on high for about 2 to 5 hours or until tender
6. serve w / hot rice and / or mashed potatoes
7. ++if the gravy becomes too thick just add a little water
8. if you accidentally add too much water then add a little more flour
9. season w / salt and pepper too your taste
demonstrations.review: Sorry to say but I was not fond of these at all and neither was my hubby. The sauce had no flavor at all. This recipe didn't really meet my expectations.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: Oh man Karen...if I could give this recipe more than 5 stars I would. These are to die for!!!!! My hubby even took some with him to work last night and everyone just loved them. Thanks for the awesome recipe. I will make these over and over again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken or turkey salad

this is very good served over a bed of lettuce or as a sandwich. it's a good way to use up left over turkey at thanksgiving. i am basing prep and cook time on using left over meat. cook time is actually the chill time.

1. combine chicken and celery in bowl
2. mix salad dressing , salt , poultry seasoning , onion salt and pepper
3. pour over chicken and celery
4. toss
5. cover
6. chill at least 2 hours
7. for variation , fold in one of the following: 1 cup chilled fruit or: 1 / 4 cup chopped sweet pickle or: 4 slices bacon , crsply fried and crumbled or: 1 / 3 cup chopped nuts
demonstrations.review: very good!!!

target.recipe_text:
aussie pepper steak   steak with creamy pepper sauce

this sauce is so tasty and is great with chips or mash. i looked on zaar for a pepper steak recipe but only found stir-fry's with capsicum so i came up with my own. i have said that this recipe is for 2 servings because i have 1 steak and my fiance has 2. it also makes a lot of sauce which we like so you could easily cook another 1 or 2 steaks and still have enough sauce to cover them all as well as the chips.

1. season raw steaks with salt and freshly cracked pepper
2. melt butter with oil in pan , add steak and cook to you liking
3. remove and set aside
4. turn heat to medium
5. add flour to the pan to make a roux with the pan juices , let cook for 1 minute
6. begin adding the stock bit by bit , whisking constantly so it doesn't get lumpy
7. it will be quite thin once all the stock is added
8. add pepper steak seasoning to your taste and mix in to the gravy
9. keep whisking
10. add cream and thicken to your liking on a low / medium heat
11. re-heat steaks in the micorwave for about 30 sec's if you haven't kept them warm
12. serve with chips or potato mash
target.review: I made this really great recipe last night. My picky husband loved the sauce and requested I make this again today! I definitely will because I also loved it!! I put the extra sauce over potatoes and it tasted great too. Thanks for this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
miss daisy s deviled eggs

these are the best deviled eggs i have ever tried. i usually have to double this recipe because they are gone almost as soon as i put them out.

1. cut eggs in half lengthwise , remove yolks , and reserve whites
2. mash yolks until smooth
3. combine yolks , mayo , worcestershire sauce , mustard , salt , pepper , and mix until smooth
4. stir in onion , and pickle relish
5. spoon mixture into center of egg whites
6. sprinkle tops with paprika
