demonstrations.review: Very good! Didn't change a thing and everyone loved them! I will definitely makes these again :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
toffee dip with apples

i served this at a party and people kept raving about it and asking for the recipe. i must admit, i was addicted and was hoping for left overs - but it was all gone.

1. combine first 4 ingredients in a bowl
2. beat at medium speed of a mixer until smooth
3. add toffee bits and mix well
4. cover and chill
5. combine juice and apples in a bowl
6. toss well
7. drain apples
8. serve with dip
demonstrations.review: So so yummy!! I could have eaten the whole thing my self! Everyone loved this and kept asking what was in it. I will definitely make this over and over! I'm craving it right now but I don't have cream cheese :(   Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
toll house butterscotch chip cookies

these are my absolute favorite cookie. ever. i have licked many a beater after mixing these cookies up. they are of course from the back of the toll house package.

1. mix together the flour , salt and baking soda in a small bowl , set aside
2. cream the sugars and butter together , add the vanilla
3. add the eggs one at a time
4. slowly add the flour mixture
5. when completely mixed , add the butterscotch chips
6. drop by the spoonful onto an ungreased cookie sheet
7. bake 8-10 minutes at 375f degrees
demonstrations.review: Very good!! I used 1 cup butterscotch chips and 1 cup chocolate chips and everyone loved them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best pumpkin cookies

what can i say about these amazing pumpkin cookies... they are absolutely delicious! let me put it this way. i baked these every year at thanksgiving time for my job. my co-workers would come up to me two months in advance to make sure i was making them. one girl who resigned actually called me and asked what day i was bringing them in so that she could stop by - just for these cookies! another co-worker said she didn't even like pumpkin, but she loved these. the consistency is more cake-like than cookie. the glaze on top of these cookies is fabulous! at least, i think so. i noticed a few of you who rated this recipe said it was too sweet. that is why i suggested it may be omitted, or if you wish, use your own icing. lots of you have added nutmeg.. hey, make it all your own. that's what this is all about! : )

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. have ready some ungreased baking sheets
3. in a large mixing bowl , cream butter and the sugars together until light and fluffy
4. blend in pumpkin , egg and vanilla extract
5. in separate bowl , stir together flour , baking soda , baking powder , cinnamon , nutmeg and salt
6. mix flour mixture into butter-sugar mixture
7. drop tablespoonfuls 3 inches apart on ungreased baking sheets
8. bake the cookies for 10-12 minutes until golden around the edges
9. remove warm cookies and transfer to racks
10. let cool completely for a least one half hour , then frost with glaze
11. for glaze:
12. in a medium saucepan , heat butter and brown sugar over medium heat until bubbly
13. cook , stirring constantly , for one minute or until slightly thickened
14. beat in the milk
15. blend in confectioner's sugar until the glaze is smooth and spreadable
16. using a silicone basting brush , which i love and use religiously now , or a butter knife to spread glaze on cookies is the best
17. please
18. i suggest that you keep the saucepan over the stove on the lowest heat possible to prevent it from hardening
demonstrations.review: Wow! These are so good! Definitely love the glaze. I used 2 cups confectioners suger. These are really nice and soft and I can't wait to make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy potato salad

have you ever posted a recipe and just love reading the reviews for it?  this is my signature potato salad.  whenever there is a pot luck function at work, i am told that i have to bring the potato salad.  no one else is allowed to and i am never given a choice.  thank you everyone who ever tried this potato salad and for leaving such glowing reviews for it.  you all have made me look so good.  i personally can not stand eggs or raw onions, so i leave them out but i know most people don't think a potato salad is complete without them.  thanks again for so many wonderful reviews. (psssst....check out my recipe #123107 as well.  it shares the dressing with this recipe but tastes much much different because of the different ingredients) please see recipe #242966 for bacon bit tips.

1. cook potatoes in boiling , salted water until tender
2. drain well
3. peel and cube potatoes
4. transfer to a large bowl
5. add celery , onion , sweet relish and bacon bits
6. combine mayo , sugar , celery seed , vinegar , mustard , and salt
7. add mayo mixture to potatoes
8. toss lightly to coat potato mixture
9. carefully fold in the chopped eggs
10. cover and chill thoroughly
11. bacon bit
12. use a sharp knife and cut the frozen bacon into long strips about 1 / 4 inch wide
13. turn the bacon and cut the strips into pieces also about 1 / 4 in wide
14. you now have perfect raw bacon pieces to fast fry
15. no need to separate
16. they will separate during cooking
17. perfect bacon bits
demonstrations.review: This was very yummy! I didn't use celery or onion because I dislike them but it was still a big hit at our 4th of July bbq.

target.recipe_text:
froggy pie

i watched this years the national pie championships held by the american pie council(2006) and was just in awe at the creative recipes that were entered. this southern entry  had the pickiest of judges raving. i have found conflicting information on who entered this pie...when i figure it out i will return with the right name.

1. in a saucepan mix the gelatin and water let sit 1 minute
2. cook over low heat until dissolved , stirring constantly
3. in a mixing bowl , combine the gelatin mixture , marshmallow , and creme de menthe and mix well
4. refrigerate until mixture mounds when dropped from spoon
5. in a separate mixing bowl , whip cream until soft peaks form
6. fold whipped cream into gelatin mix
7. add candies and mound into pie crust
8. garnish with whipped cream and additional candies , optional
9. refrigerate overnight
target.review: Green & Minty - perfect for the office St. Patrick's Day potluck.  This pie was very tasty and EASY to make.  I've been asked to share the recipe and will do so.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linguine with clam sauce

quick easy, and cheap! dinner for 6 for about $5.00.

1. heat oil in skillet over menium heat
2. add onion and chopped garlic and cook till the onion is tender
3. add clam juice to skillet and add all the seasonings
4. simmer over low for 5 minutes
5. when pasta is ready , add clams , and remove from heat
6. pour sauce over drained pasta , toss together
demonstrations.review: SO TASTY!  The flavor combinations are great and it's a meal that I can put together in the time it takes to cook the noodles.  Love that it's lowfat and inexpensive too.  I will make this often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mahogany beef stew

you will not believe the deeply satisfying flavour of this stew. this is our favourite wintry stew dish - comfort food to the max.  the cooking time is more or less accurate, but it really depends on the cut of meat used -  not everyone used chuck, and then, not all chuck is the same!  you really have to poke and prod and taste to get it to where you want it...but that's what cooking is all about, isn't it? ;-)

1. heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in heavy large pot over high heat
2. sprinkle meat with salt and pepper
3. add meat to pot
4. saut until brown on all sides , about 10 minutes
5. push meat to sides of pot
6. reduce heat to medium
7. add 2 tablespoons oil to pot
8. add onions
9. saut until golden brown , about 15 minutes
10. mix meat into onions
11. add 1 cup wine , tomatoes with juices , garlic , herbs , hoisin sauce , and bay leaves
12. bring to boil
13. reduce heat to low , cover pot and simmer 45 minutes , stirring occasionally
14. add carrots and 1 cup wine
15. cover
16. simmer 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
17. uncover , increase heat to high
18. boil until sauce is slightly thickened , stirring occasionally , about 15 minutes longer
19. reduce heat to medium , add cornstarch mixture and simmer until sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 8 minutes
20. discard bay leaves
21. season stew with salt and pepper
22. transfer stew to large bowl
23. sprinkle with parsley and serve
24. excellent with buttered egg noodles
demonstrations.review: I loved this stew - I added a couple of diced potatoes, some mushrooms and a parsnip along with the carrots.  I also simmered the meat with a couple of beef soup bones to flavor the broth and it was one of the best stews I've ever made.  The hoisin sauce definitley made this stew. Give it a try - you won't be sorry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was a hit at the Mexican themed Super Bowl party.  I followed pretty closely except for adding about 1/2 lb. of chorizo to the ground beef when browning and I used 8 oz. of sour cream instead of just the four.  As other people have said you can play around with adding/substituing and using lowfat substitutions.  It's a great recipe and I will be making it again - EASY too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butterflied leg of lamb with lots of garlic and rosemary

a butterflied leg is usually of uneven thickness. when it is grilled, there will be rare(125-130 degrees, medium rare 130-145 degrees, and medium-well 145 and up sections to satisfy everyone.

1. trim any excess fat from the lamb and place it in a 9-by-13-inch nonreactive pan
2. whisk together all the marinade ingredients in a bowl
3. scoop out and reserve 1 / 4 cup of the marinade and pour the remainder over the lamb
4. massage into meat
5. cover and refrigerate overnight
6. remove the meat from the refrigerator and allow to come to room temperature
7. preheat grill to medium heat
8. place the lamb on the grill rack and cook , turning once and basting frequently with the reserved 1 / 4 cup marinade , for 15 to 18 minutes on each side for medium-rare
9. my favorite !
10. transfer to a platter , season with salt and pepper , and tent with aluminum foil
11. let rest for 10 minutes before slicing , then place on a cutting board and slice thinly
12. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Even guests who didn't know it was lamb thought it was a tender, juicy beef cut.  I love lamb and this preparation was top knotch.  Great flavor - followed directions and had a great meal off the grill!  If you like lamb you will enjoy this and it was so easy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: The dry bread crumbs made the topping taste stale - maybe fresh would be better.  I followed exactly and it was just okay - I have a parmesan chicken recipe that uses fresh and it crisped up better without getting mushy on the bottom.

target.recipe_text:
copycat olive garden minestrone soup by todd wilbur

from http://www.topsecretrecipes.com it's finally here! what everyone's been waiting for! just in time for winter, this soup is sure to warm your soul with it's savory flavor and wonderful aroma. i've asked many an olive garden waiter for this recipe, but none gave it to me in detail. one waiter told me the secret ingredient was to add a little red wine to the stock, but i'll leave that up to you to try.

1. heat three tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat in a large soup pot
2. saute onion , celery , garlic , green beans , and zucchini in the oil for 5 minutes or until onions begin to turn translucent
3. add vegetable broth to pot , plus drained tomatoes , beans , carrot , hot water , and spices
4. bring soup to a boil , then reduce heat and allow to simmer for 20 minutes
5. add spinach leaves and pasta and cook for an additional 20 minutes or until desired consistency
6. makes about eight 1 1 / 2 cup servings
target.review: yum yum!!! i love OG's minestrone and this was even tastier! i didn't have any celery so i put a bit more onion instead...i also used 2 cans of beans (instead of 4) and just a handful of thawed spinach. it tasted marvelous!!! thanks for posting this :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
home baked bagels

these bagels are better than any store bought or frozen varieties. they are so fresh and the possibilities are endless :) have lots of real butter and cream cheese on hand! oh...and you might want to double the recipe...they never last long around here.

1. mix yeast , sugar and warm water together and let stand 3 minutes
2. mix 2 cups of flour with the salt in a large bowl and add the yeast mixture
3. stir until combined and slowly mix in the rest of the flour
4. knead on a floured surface for 5 minutes , adding additional flour if needed , dough should be firm
5. place dough in a greased bowl , cover and let rise until double
6. after rising punch down and divide dough into 12 balls
7. allow to rest for 4 minutes
8. bring 2 quarts of water to boil
9. with your thumb , make a hole in each ball of dough and pull open about 2 inches , making a bagel shape
10. preheat oven to 350 degrees
11. place the shaped dough onto a cookie sheet and cover for 10 minutes
12. lower heat under water for it to be simmering
13. drop 2 or 3 bagels at a time into the water for about 45 seconds , turning each once
14. drain and place on greased baking sheets
15. brush tops with beaten egg white and top with optional toppings
16. bake for 35 minutes , turning once for even browning
17. bagels are done when they are golden brown and shiny
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! :) The only thing I would change is the very yeasty flavor of the bagels, but that could be because of a measuring error (and is quickly corrected by spreading on some butter--totally masks the yeast flavor). Thanks for a pretty much foolproof recipe! All purpose flour and brown sugar can be used providing excellent results.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gambas al ajillo  shrimp w  garlic  catalonia

while this is usually served as a tapa, it is too good not to eat as a main course. after trying the ones that were posted here on zaar, i found myself still searching for the gambas we had in barcelona. finally i found the recipe with the flavor and creaminess of the dish we fell in love with in spain! the same dish can be made with squid, cut into rings, or scallops. serve with lots of warm crusty bread to sop up the sauce…. you will not want to waste a drop! (make sure you are "warming" the olive oil and the butter, not cooking it off..... cause you'll want every last bit of it for the sauce)

1. in a wide , shallow saut pan over high heat , warm the olive oil and the butter
2. add the shrimp and garlic and saut quickly for about 2-3 minutes
3. add the lemon juice , paprika , pepper flakes , and salt and pepper to taste
4. adjust seasonings to your liking
5. transfer to a warmed serving dish , sprinkle with the parsley and serve at once
demonstrations.review:
Te amo. ¡Cásate conmigo!* This was a wonderful dish. Very good with lots of fresh, crusty bread. I am going to make this again tonight and serve it over pasta with red sauce. mmmm!!

Muy bien! 

*I love you. Will you marry me?!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jumbo shrimp parmesan

i made these for dinner tonight and they are scrumptious! can be made ahead up to and including the breading stage and refrigerated. then drizzle with butter and bake. found on the global gourmet website.

1. preheat oven to 475 degrees
2. peel and devein shrimp , leaving tails intact
3. mix together olive oil , garlic and salt and pepper in a bowl
4. add shrimp and toss lightly to coat
5. refrigerate 30 minutes to an hour
6. in shallow bowl , combine bread crumbs and parmesan cheese
7. place each shrimp in bread crumb mixture and turn them to lightly coat both sides
8. arrange shrimp so that they aren't touching each other in a ungreased 9 x 13 pan
9. drizzle with melted butter
10. place pan on the center rack of oven and bake for 10 minutes or until done
11. serve immediately with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: ooh lala! i used large shrimp and had fantastic results. prepared the shrimp with all the same ingredients, but made adjustments where necessary to get them nice and covered in the marinade. i loooooove garlic so i added 4 cloves, and the flavor was perfect. this one deserves more than 5 stars! even my picky BF thinks so-- thank you marie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review:
These were fabulous. They tasted much better than Reese's...especially if you splurge on extra decadent chocolate chips! (I used Godiva and it was worth the extra $1!!)
I didn't have a 9x13 inch glass pan on hand so I used an 8x8 and double layered the squares and I think this made them super tasty. Thank you :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun style oven fries

you gonna' dun like diss, i garontee! :)

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. in a small bowl , combine oregano , thyme , paprika , cayenne , black pepper , sugar , cumin , salt , garlic powder , onion powder , tabasco sauce , and oil
3. mix well into a paste
4. line a large baking sheet with aluminum foil
5. pour a small amount of oil onto foil and spread with a paper towel
6. peel potatoes and slice into french fry shapes
7. place fries in a plastic bag with paste and work paste onto fries
8. alternatively you can do this in a bowl , but the bag method is easier
9. place fries on lined baking sheet , trying not to let edges touch
10. bake in preheated oven for approximately 30-35 minutes
11. turn once during cooking to brown underside
demonstrations.review: i've made these several times and each batch was delicious with the perfect amount and mix of spices! :) thanks for the recipe and thank you also for posting a photo for my beans--that was very nice of you :) (i would have messaged you but i'm on a free account, hehe)

target.recipe_text:
beef stroganoff casserole

a delicious recipe that is very easy to make! you may use steak, ground beef, ground turkey or venison.

1. saute onion and butter in skillet
2. add and saute beef until cooked through
3. add flour , spices , and mushrooms
4. simmer for 5 min
5. add soup and water
6. simmer for 10 min
7. remove from heat and stir in sour cream
8. add parsley and extra paprika for garnish
9. serve over noodles , pasta , rice or serve as a main dish by itself
10. easy and fast !
target.review: i made a vegetarian version with veggie stock....it was very very good. i then made hubby the meat version and he as well loved it! i did add some stock to his too though and FYI it gave it a BEAUTIFUL flavor!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
skillet okra and rice

this is from a march 1994 betty crocker cookbooklet.  my garden is doing great and i was looking for new and different ways to prepare okra.  this is a nice low-fat version.

1. in a 10-inch nonstick skillet , heat the oil over medium-high heat
2. add the rice and cook about 3 minutes , stirring frequently or until lightly brown
3. add the onion , bell pepper and garlic
4. cook 5 minutes , stirring frequently , or until onion begins to soften
5. stir in remaining ingredeints except for the okra
6. heat to boiling , reduce heat
7. cover and simmer until rice is tender
8. add the okra , cover and simmer 10 minutes longer or until okra is tender
9. remove bay leaf and serve
demonstrations.review: not a fan...very bland

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq chicken with spicy yogurt

this recipe is recommended by "american health" as heart smart. it's tasty too!

1. mix crumbs and seasoning
2. dip chicken in the yogurt and crumb mixture
3. brush oil over the bbq grill
4. grill 15 minutes turn and grill an other 10-15 minute
5. use low to medium heat on gas bbq
6. watch you don't burn the crumbs
7. cooking time will vary depending on the thickness of the breasts
8. they're done when fork tender
demonstrations.review: another beautiful recipe by Bergie!!!!!!!! hunny this is to die for!!! thanks for a spledid recipe my whole dinner party was RAVING about!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
south african vegetable curry

an awesome african recipe that will be a hit ten fold, especially if you like indian food. great served with cous cous.

1. cut carrots into 1 / 2 inch thick slices
2. cut beans into 1 / 2 inch pieces
3. cut cauliflower into 1 1 / 2 inch florets
4. cut pepper and peaches into 1 inch pieces
5. in a 5 to 6 quart pan over medium high heat , stir oil , onion , ginger , garlic and cinnamon sticks until onion is limp , 5 to 7 minutes
6. add curry powder and turmeric , stir 30 seconds
7. add broth , carrots , beans , cauliflower bell peppers , peaches and cabbage
8. bring to a boil over high heat
9. cover and simmer over low heat , stirring occasionally , until carrots are tender when pierced , 20 to 25 minutes
10. add salt to taste
demonstrations.review: this was to die for!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caesar salad dressing  low cal

much to my joy, i adopted this recipe last year!
after making this, the only change i made was to note, soft-silken tofu works very well!  next time i will try the firm.

1. in small saucepan of simmering water , poach tofu for 2 minutes
2. drain , chop coarsely and let cool
3. in blender , blend lemon juice , mustard , garlic , anchovy , salt , sugar and pepper
4. with blender running , gradually add tofu , cheese and oil
5. transfer to small jar and refrigerate covered , for up to 2 days
demonstrations.review: wasnt good at all

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low cal indian yogurt and spinach salad

this is a very quick and simple, yet tasty indian recipe, great for summer. it goes great with any veggies or even regular hot french bread, or simply as a side dish.

1. in a shallow frying pan , heat the oil
2. when hot , add the mustard seeds and fry till they start crackling
3. at this point add the chopped green chillies
4. now add the boiled spinach and saute till the oil seperates
5. let the mixture cool to room temperature
6. in a seperate bowl , beat the yogurt with the garlic paste and salt
7. now simply mix the spinach and voila , a yummy low cal salad is ready
demonstrations.review: i loved this recipe...indian food is one of my favorites and this one hit a home run!

target.recipe_text:
sweet chicken bacon wraps  paula deen

hey you paula deen fans, she has a new magazine, "cooking with paula deen"--this recipe is from the premier issue.  it was so yummy looking, i couldn't wait to try it.  i added another 15 minutes to the cooking time suggested (30-35 minutes) and it was just right, but oven temperatures vary, so check on it during the last few minutes of cooking time.  i'm also going to add a few dashes of cayenne pepper next time for something hot and sweet!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cut chicken breasts into 1-inch cubes
3. cut each bacon slice into thirds
4. wrap each chicken cube with bacon and secure with a wooden pick inserted on the diagonal starting where bacon seam overlaps
5. stir together brown sugar and chili powder
6. dredge wrapped chicken in mixture
7. coat a rack and broiler pan with non-stick cooking spray
8. place chicken on rack in broiler pan
9. bake at 350f for 30 to 35 minutes , or until bacon is crisp
target.review: I love these! I make your recipe all the time and everyone enjoys them. We throw them on the grill in the summer. So simple and so good. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crook s corner shrimp and grits

crook's corner is a restaurant in chapel hill, nc. this is a dish served at the restaurant and i found the recipe in the latest southern living magazine. i made this last night for dinner and my husband and i went nuts for it, it's the ultimate comfort food. don't let the long list of ingredients throw you off, this goes together quickly and easily.

1. bring first 4 ingredients to a boil in a medium saucepan
2. gradually whisk in grits
3. reduce heat and simmer , stirring occasionally , 10 minutes or until thickened
4. add cheddar cheese and next 4 ingredients
5. set aside but keep warm
6. cook bacon in a large skillet until crisp
7. remove bacon and drain on paper towels , reserve 1 tablespoon of drippings in skillet
8. crumble bacon and set aside
9. sprinkle shrimp with pepper and salt
10. dredge in flour
11. saute mushrooms in hot drippings in skillet 5 minutes , or until tender
12. add green onions and saute 2 minutes
13. add shrimp and garlic and saute 2 minutes or until shrimp are lightly brown
14. stir in chicken broth , lemon juice and hot sauce and cook 2 more minutes , stirring to loosen browned bits from skillet
15. divide grits into 4 large , shallow soup bowls
16. divide shrimp mixture into four servings and place on top of grits
17. top each serving with crumbled bacon and serve with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: OOOH WEEE! This was SO good. My husband made this for dinner one night and I havn't stopped asking him to make it again. He didn't change anything about it and it was fabulous! This is a new favorite. one of my sons who claimed to not like shrimp is  saying how much he likes shrimp now. Thanks for the great recepie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb pizza

i got this delicious recipe from www.atkinsdietbulletboard.com the orginal chef is bikergoddess. we all thank her for creating this great recipe. it's not exactly like pizza, but it's pretty close. i like it alot. i've made it twice now, and will be making it over and over again.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. beat together cream cheese and eggs until smooth
3. add cream , parmesan , chives , italian seasoning and garlic
4. spray 9x13 pan with cooking spray or oil
5. place 2 cups mozzarella cheese in bottom of pan
6. pour egg mixture over cheese
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. remove from oven and spread sauce over baked mixture
9. add toppings of choice
10. cover with remaining mozzerella cheese
11. bake until bubbly and brown
12. let stand for 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: My husband and I really liked this  recepie. It was a great break in our diet that made it seem like we were having a little fun. We didn't miss the crust at all. The only thing we did different was add a little pizza seasoning to the top of our tomato sauce. Thanks for posting the recepie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry cheesecake ice cream  for electric ice cream machine

posted by request. recipe is from the recipe book that came with my ice cream machine. prep time includes 1 hour chilling and 1/2 hour freezing times.

1. blend all ingredients until smooth
2. chill ingredients for about 1 hour , or until cold
3. turn on ice cream machine and set it to chill the freezing / mixing bowl for 5 minutes
4. spoon the cooled mixture into the freezing / mixing bowl of machine
5. set the freezing timer to the 30 minute maximum setting
6. push start button
7. when timer rings , spoon ice cream into dishes and enjoy
demonstrations.review: This is a new favorite in my house now! I doubled the recepie add gramcracker and strawberry syrup swirls. Yummy! Thanks for the recepie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: I loved this meatloaf and so did my family. I will be making this often. I used shallots instead of vidalia onions because thats what I had and sauteed them in butter before adding them to the mixture. Otherwise I made it as directed. I was very pleased with the fact that my meatloaf was moist, I use 4% fat beef and it can be very dry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my chicken parmigiana

this is a family favorite meal and one i make for special occasions, such as birthday dinners. the cooking method of this particular version is different from the conventional chicken parmigiana recipes i always used to make. once i tried this much easier and moister version, i never went back to the "old" method. i often use homemade sauce in this, but a good-quality bottled sauce, such as classico or barilla, is perfectly acceptable as well. i serve this chicken atop mounds of freshly cooked pasta with some additional heated sauce. i have often chosen to replace the mozzarella with thin slices of provolone cheese. note: edited to add that pounding the chicken is not necessary with this method.  part of what is unique about this recipe is that even the meatier pieces of chicken get so moist & tender as it braises in the sauce.

1. beat egg and set into a rimmed plate
2. set bread crumbs in a second rimmed plate
3. dip chicken breasts into the egg , then into the crumbs , coating both sides and shaking off excess
4. melt butter or margarine over medium heat in a large , deep skillet
5. add chicken breast halves to the pan and brown on both sides - just enough to brown the chicken , not to fully cook it yet
6. pour spaghetti sauce into the pan , immediately reduce heat to low , cover , and simmer until the chicken has cooked all the way through , about 15-20 minutes but the time will vary depending upon the thickness and size of your chicken breasts
7. sprinkle with parsley and cheeses , re-cover , and simmer just until cheese melts- about 5 minutes
8. serve with cooked spaghetti
demonstrations.review: This was very easy and yummy. I wouldn't change a thing.

target.recipe_text:
honey grilled pork chops

these tasty chops have a bit of an oriental flair! can easily be done under the broiler if you don't wish to grill outdoors, or if it suddenly rains! prep time does not include marinating time.

1. trim excess fat from chops
2. then prick with a fork on both sides and set aside
3. combine soy sauce , ginger and garlic in a small bowl
4. pour half of this in a shallow pan and add the chops
5. pour remaining sauce / marinade over the chops , then refrigerate for up to 8 hours , turning occasionally
6. prepare grill
7. spray grill rack with non-stick spray before heating
8. combine sugar , honey and sesame oil in a small saucepan
9. cook on low until sugar dissolves then remove from heat
10. remove chops from marinade and discard marinade
11. drizzle chops lightly with peanut or other oil on both sides , and grill directly over coals or heat until lightly charred
12. turn chops and do opposite side
13. then move away from direct heat
14. brush chops with honey glaze and cover grill
15. turn and baste chops several times , until meat checks done , about 30 minutes or a cut towards the bone section shows no blood and only pale pink to browned meat
target.review: I tried this last night and it was great. I doubled the recipe and also put in skinless chicken thighs. the pork chops and the thighs were absolutely fantastic. I'm thinking of trying it on some sort of grilled fish. I will get back to you on the results.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp escabeche with ginger grilled pineapple

traditionally escabeche is made by pickling fried fish. susser's quick version features sautéed shrimp in a cilantro marinade with tangy grilled pineapple. liberal use of local citrus and tropical fruits and juices makes it easy for allen susser to add bright flavor to both savory and sweet dishes without using lots of fat. his philosophy at chef allen's in miami is simple: don't try to cut out oil and rich foods altogether; just use small amounts and make sure they're top quality. 
this low calorie (161 a serving) - low fat (4.6 gm) recipe was created by allen susser, the famed caribbean-latin-euro fusionist of miami's chef allen's. wine: wine because ginger, lemons and spices can overwhelm dry, subtle wines, look for a simpler aromatic white, such as a west coast riesling. the 1994 hogue cellars dry johannisberg riesling or the 1993 trefethen white riesling are acidic enough to stand up to the tartness and fruity enough to magnify the flavors of the shrimp and the snapper. 30 minutes to marinate.

1. heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet
2. season the shrimp with salt and pepper and cook over high heat for 1 minute
3. add the onion and garlic and cook , stirring occasionally , until the shrimp are cooked through , about 2 more minutes
4. stir in the orange juice , 2 tablespoons of the lime juice , the scallion and cilantro , transfer to a bowl and let cool
5. meanwhile , in a bowl , combine the remaining 2 tablespoons lime juice with the ginger , sesame oil , 1 / 2 teaspoon salt and 1 / 4 teaspoon pepper
6. brush the pineapple with the mixture and let stand at room temperature for 30 minutes
7. in a dry skillet , toast the sesame seeds over high heat , shaking the pan , until fragrant , about 2 minutes
8. light a grill or preheat the broiler
9. grill or broil the pineapple for about 2 minutes per side , turning once , until lightly browned
10. cut each quarter crosswise into 6 pieces and arrange the pieces on 6 plates
11. set 2 shrimp on each plate , spoon on a little of the orange juice marinade and sprinkle with the sesame seeds
demonstrations.review: My son is attending Johnson & Wales Univ. to be come a chef. He has already owned his own resturant so he is not a novice. He made this for one of his classes and his Prof asked for the recipe! He made it at home first, so I got to taste it. It says six  servings but we ate all of it. It was just the two of us.So thanks ncmystery shopper for sharing and helping my son keep his 3.9 GPA!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
company pork roast

this is very tasty and have received rave reviews. i serve the liquid from the roast, in a small bowl, to spoon over the meat.

1. place roast , fat side up , in foil lined roasting pan
2. mix remaining ingredients and brush on all sides of roast
3. cover with foil and bake at 325f for 2 1 / 2 hours basting frequently
4. uncover the last 45 minutes to brown roast
demonstrations.review: I thought this was the most tender and flavorful pork roast I've ever had. Thank you so much for sharing Garnet. Too bad I had to stop at 5 stars!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian rice and peas

this rice is a little moister than most rice dishes. it goes well with other veggies. it is a speciality of venice

1. melt 2 oz of butter in a saucepan
2. add chopped onion and celery , cook until just translucent
3. add rice , cook a few minutes more , stirring to coat the rice with butter
4. add wine , 1 cup of boiling water and crumbled stock cubes
5. bring to a boil , add peas
6. reduce heat , simmer uncovered until the water has evaporated
7. add another cup of boiling water , cook until evaporated
8. add the final cup of boiling water
9. keep cooking until the water is almost absorbed
10. overall cooking time is about 20 minutes
11. stir in the parmesan cheese and 1 oz butter
12. add salt& pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: I was looking for something to serve as a side dish and found this. Oh Boy! I picked this mainly because I had all ingredients on hand. I am so glad I tried it. It is absolutely wonderful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy barbecued corn on the cob

adapted from semi-homemade cooking with sandra lee, this is yummy!

1. preheat outdoor grill or preheat oven to 400f
2. shuck corn
3. if desired , leave husks attached to cob to use as holders
4. in a small bowl , combine softened butter , chili powder , and powdered cheese packet or creamy cheese sauce
5. spread butter on corn and wrap each ear individually in foil
6. place on the grill and close the lid or place in the oven
7. cook 25 to 30 minutes , turning every 5 minutes , or until corn is tender
8. remove foil and serve
demonstrations.review: This is GOOD ! did you know you can get the cheddar cheese powder from King Arthur?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned cocoa

you'll never go back to instant cocoa again!

1. in a small pan , combine cocoa and sugar , whisk in half and half till smooth
2. over low heat , whisk in milk and vanilla , bring to a simmer
3. pour into hot mugs and top with cream and chocolate
4. to add variety add cinnamon and nutmeg before adding milk , or use peppermint extract in place of vanilla
demonstrations.review: Reminds me of Rumplemyer's in NYC>

target.recipe_text:
creamsicle in a glass

this is a wonderful creamy creation.  this takes only seconds to prepare.

1. peel and break apart the orange and add to blender along with the zest , soy milk , tofu , vanilla , sweetner and ice cubes
2. blend until smooth and frothy , about 30 seconds
3. pour into tall , chilled glasses and garnish with an orange slice if desired
target.review: Thank you so much for sharing the recipe!!! YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paula deen s praline french toast casserole

very easy to make and delicious. make it up the day before and set in refrigerator over night. this is a great recipe from a great southern cook, paula deen.

1. generously butter a 13 x 9 inch casserole dish
2. mix the eggs , half and half , maple syrup , and sugar in a large bowl
3. place the bread slices in the prepared casserole dish and cover with the egg mixture: cover with plastic wrap and let soak overnight in refrigerator
4. preheat oven to 350 degrees
5. remove the casserole from refrigerator
6. make the topping: melt the butter in a saucepan
7. add sugar and maple syrup and cook for 1 to 2 minutes
8. stir in pecans
9. pour the mixture over the bread and bake for 45 to 55 minutes , allow to cool 10 minutes before serving , enjoy
demonstrations.review: I used a non stick pan and greased it thoughly but it still was very hard to serve.  The pralines were great but it is not french toast!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amish sour cream apple pie

i found this recipe in my files. i dont remember where i got it, but it's good. i love the simplicity of the recipe.

1. beat sour cream and egg together
2. add flour , sugar , salt and vanilla
3. mix until smooth
4. stir in apples
5. bake at 400 degrees for 25 minutes
6. mix the crumb topping ingredients until crumbly
7. remove pie from oven and spread with crumb topping
8. bake 20 more minutes
demonstrations.review: Very unusual taste for an apple pie! Got lots of raves!  Will make again!!  Thank you for listing it!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buckingham palace garden party cucumber sandwiches

cucumber sandwiches are made with fresh springy white or brown bread, lightly buttered, and with the crusts cut off – the perfect cool summer snack to go with your afternoon tea. this recipe idea came from a friend who was lucky enough to attend a garden party at buckingham palace - she swears this is how they made them! cucumber sandwiches achieved literary notoriety in oscar wilde’s play the importance of being earnest (1895) when algernon devours an entire plate full in the first act and there are none left for his aunt, lady bracknell. they are presented by jack as being a delicacy: “hallo! why all these cups? why cucumber sandwiches? why such reckless extravagance in one so young? who is coming to tea?”

1. peel cucumber and slice in paper-thin rounds
2. salt rounds lightly and place in colander for 15 minutes to drain
3. press to release water
4. pat dry with paper towels
5. spread sliced bread with softened butter
6. put 2 layers of cucumber slices on bottom slice , sprinkle with finely chopped mint , salt and pepper to taste , and top with another buttered slice
7. press lightly with palm of hand
8. cut all crusts off with a sharp knife
9. cut sandwiches in half diagonally and then again into quarters
10. serve in alternate rows of brown and white bread sandwiches , points facing up !
demonstrations.review: Loved them!  I love everything English lol This is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet sour red cabbage salad

the recipe comes from my german grandmother. i like it,since it is refreshing in summer and taste good with all kind of poultry.

1. cook bacon until crips
2. crumble
3. measure 3 teaspoons of bacon fat into skillet
4. stir in remaining ingredients , leaving out cabbage
5. cook mixture over medium heat , stirring constantly , until mixture is smooth and clear
6. cool to room temperature
7. put cabbage into salad bowl
8. pour cooled dressing over it
9. add crumbled bacon
10. chill
demonstrations.review: I used 3 teaspoons of olive oil instead and it was great!  Thanks for recipe!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
make ahead mashed potato casserole

time saver casserole and the taste is excellent! originally from canadian living magazine.

1. in a large pot of boiling water , cook potatoes for 20 minutes or until tender but not mushy
2. drain and let cool slightly , peel
3. with a potato masher , mash until smooth , do not use an electric mixer , blend in cream cheese and butter until melted
4. mix in onions , sour cream , parsley , marjoram , and salt and pepper to taste
5. transfer to 8 inch baking dish , smooth top
6. sprinkle with crumbs , bake in 400 degree oven for about 20 minutes or until heated through and top is lightly golden
demonstrations.review: Great make ahead recipe!!!! Thank you so much!!!  I will make this again and again for company. Saves so much time the day of the dinner party!!!

target.recipe_text:
sunrise breakfast casserole  prepared night before

a johnsonville recipe that we served this at my sister's wedding brunch, this is a great breakfast prepared the night before.  especially good for morning entertaining.  prep time does not include overnight refrigeration.  cooking time includes sausage cooking.

1. put sausage on a 15x10x1 inch baking pan
2. bake at 375 degrees for 15-20 minutes or until the sausage is no longer pink
3. drain , then slice into 1 / 4 inch coins
4. in a large bowl , combine the eggs , milk , mustard , salt and pepper
5. add the hash browns , sausage , cheese , sweet red pepper and green onions
6. mix well
7. pour into a greased 13x9x2 inch baking dish , cover and refrigerate overnight
8. remove from refrigerator 30 minutes prior to baking
9. bake uncovered at 350 degrees for 65-70 minutes or until set and golden brown
10. let stand 10 minutes before serving
11. serve with salsa or picante sauce , if you like
target.review: Made this last night for breakfast today.  A nice change from the usual eggs/meat/pancake fare.  I cut the recipe in half as there are 3 of us and it fit perfectly into a 2-qt casserole dish.  The store was out of green onions, so I used onion powder; I had a jar of roasted red peppers so I used those.  The dish took longer to bake than directed, but my hashbrowns weren't quite thawed when I put it together and I think the extra moisture from the thawing was the culprit.  The dish itself is fairly bland but lends itself well to the addition of salsa (dh) or ketchup (dd).  If you know your family likes things a little spicy, I would recommend trying a hot sausage and/or adding red pepper sauce/flakes to the mixture.  I call recipes like this 'blank canvas' as they are easy to prepare and the add-in possibilities are endless; change up the cheese, add veggies, try different meats, maybe flavored hashbrowns, serve with a spicy gravy or even maple syrup, etc.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simply baked chicken parmesan

this is an easy chicken parmesan that is completely baked in the oven - no browning in oil.  i do use a tiny spray of margarine over the top before baking.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. dip each chicken piece into eggs
3. coat with bread crumbs
4. place into casserole dish
5. bake uncovered for 30 minutes
6. remove chicken and pour marinara sauce into bottom of dish
7. lay chicken over the sauce and sprinkle the two cheeses on the pieces of chicken
8. bake an additional 20 minutes until cooked through
demonstrations.review: YUM!  Very easy and quick.  This will be seeing many repeat performances at our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna egg chicken salad dressing  all purpose

i used to be fussy about my tuna salad dressings, since most of the time they tasted too "tinned" or "fishy." this all-purpose dressing from "cook's illustrated" is fabulous on all three types of sandwich fillings. listed are the variations suggested for each filling. recipe makes 1/4 cup (enough for one 6 ounce can tuna) but  can be doubled or tripled.

1. in medium bowl using a fork , stir together all the ingredients , until completely smooth
2. cover and refrigerate until ready to use
3. variations:
4. barbecue : omit the lemon juice and add 1 tablespoon prepared barbecue sauce
5. basil : add 1 tablespoon minced basil and 2 tablespoons seeded , diced tomato
6. buttermilk : substitute buttermilk for the sour cream and add 1 tablespoon minced scallions or chives
7. just before serving stir in 2 tablespoons fried , crumbled bacon
8. chipotle : add 1 / 2 to 1 -1 / 2 teaspoon chipotle in adobo sauce
9. chutney add 1 tablespoon mango chutney
10. club : add 1 tablespoon each diced avocado and seeded , diced tomato
11. just before serving stir in 2 tablespoon fried , crumbled bacon
12. curry add 1 teaspoon curry powder , pinch ground ginger , and honey to taste
demonstrations.review: I used this for tuna sandwiches.  I cut it in half for one can of tuna and used Greek yogurt, plain mustard as we're not mustard fans.  I found I was out of honey but added a bit of Splenda.  I loved it!  I had never thought of adding a bit of sweetness to "any type" salad fillings, but I think it will become my secret ingredient.  I just dumped everything in with the tuna and next time I will mix up the dressing first and let it meld for awhile in the refrigerator.  I might just have to buy a jar of Dijon mustard...now that's a FIRST!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sunday chicken and dressing casserole

this is from the chocolate biscuit tearoom cookbook.  it's good comfort food and very easy and quick to throw together.

1. saute onions and celery in butter
2. mix together the broth and soups
3. heat and pour over cornbread
4. add onions and celery and mix well
5. season with salt and pepper to taste
6. pour 1 / 2 dressing mixture in 3-quart casserole dish
7. top with chopped chicken
8. pour on rest of dressing
9. bake at 350 degrees for 50-60 minutes
demonstrations.review: Once again, this is my review of a recipe not quite followed. :-)  First of all, I thought I was opening a container of chicken broth - it was BEEF broth!  But I did use Cream of Chicken soup (just one can as I was cutting recipe in half) and it was good!  Then I used Stove Top and added some chopped up onion.  I made the stuffing a little more 'wet' than I would usually, put it all together and baked for 1 hour.  Got high reviews from both dh and dd.  Served with broccoli and cheese sauce.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy sausage stuffing  make ahead

it wouldn't be the holidays without it! my mom's recipe and an easy holiday tradition using packaged stuffing mix. the first steps can be done ahead of time and refrigerated.

1. prepare a small dice of celery and onion , and saute with butter until soft
2. remove from pan and reserve
3. add crumbled sausage to pan and cook through
4. drain sausage on paper towels and combine with celery mixture
5. this can now be refrigerated until you are ready to stuff the turkey
6. when you are ready to stuff the turkey combine celery mixture , sausage , stuffing mix and sage in a large bowl
7. add chicken broth a little at a time just until stuffing is moist , not mushy or runny
8. rinse turkey and empty the cavity
9. place turkey in roasting pan
10. fill the body cavity with stuffing mixture
11. also fill the cavity at the neck under the skin with stuffing
12. pat any additional stuffing between the turkey legs
13. prepare turkey as desired
14. to cook in a casserole dish instead of stuffing the turkey , place stuffing mixture in a greased casserole dish and bake according to package directions
15. if stuffing is drying out dot with butter and add small amounts of broth to moisten
demonstrations.review: We had just the three of us for Thanksgiving dinner this year so this fit the bill exactly.  We liked it a lot.  Would definately recommend.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanish 7 layer casserole   a pantry recipe

i am publishing a series of recipes that use items from your pantry. these recipes are good for emergency survival, camping, job loss and other situations where surviving off staples may be needed. most of these are also good as a quick dinner when you dont feel like cooking. since these recipes require canned or packaged goods they may not be as good as if you use fresh - but feel free to substitute fresh for packaged.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. if your corn and salsa are really juicy omit the water
3. mix cream of chicken soup and 1 / 2 of the salsa together
4. mix the cheese soup and half the salsa together
5. place ingredients in casserole dish in the following order
6. rice , water , corn , cream of chicken / salsa mixture , beans , chicken breast , and cheese soup / salsa mixture
7. cover and bake 45 minutes
8. uncover and cook another 15-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I would like to try this, but need to know if the 1 C of rice is cooked or uncooked.  I'm thinking uncooked due to the time in the oven...but I've been wrong before (not that I let my husband know that...) Please advise. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
mom s gingersnaps

everyone in my family loves these. dad keeps asking me to make them and send them over. great ginger and molasses flavour.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. combine dry ingredients and set aside
3. in a large bowl beat butter till soft , gradually add sugar
4. beat in egg and molasses
5. stir in flour mixture
6. roll into balls , then roll in sugar
7. bake 10- 12 minutes
8. cooking time depends on the size of cookie
9. i have small children so i make them quite small and the baking time decreases
10. the yield is not correct- it depends on the size of the cookie- i do not know the amount it will make ?
target.review: these were pretty good...i think that I like a stronger flavored gingersnap but if you are looking for something with a mild flavor, give these a try!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chipotle copycat lime rice recipe

this is a copycat recipe i found for this amazing rice, it works perfectly with a nice savory pulled pork that i use for making burritos. but it really is good enough to have on it's own. *edit* i will have to revisit this recipe soon and come up with more precise measurements and possibly using more generic rice.

1. in a 2-quart heavy saucepan , heat oil or butter over low heat , stirring occasionally until melted
2. add rice and lime juice , stir for 1 minute
3. add water and salt , bring to a full rolling boil
4. at boiling , cover , turn down to simmer over low heat until rice is tender and the water is absorbed , about 25 minutes
5. add in the cilantro and fluff rice with a fork
demonstrations.review: Flavor is definetly spot on!  I made the rice with the additional liquid and it ended up a bit mushy.  I'm sure it will be great if I reduce the liquid next time.  YUMMY!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat olive garden minestrone soup by todd wilbur

from http://www.topsecretrecipes.com it's finally here! what everyone's been waiting for! just in time for winter, this soup is sure to warm your soul with it's savory flavor and wonderful aroma. i've asked many an olive garden waiter for this recipe, but none gave it to me in detail. one waiter told me the secret ingredient was to add a little red wine to the stock, but i'll leave that up to you to try.

1. heat three tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat in a large soup pot
2. saute onion , celery , garlic , green beans , and zucchini in the oil for 5 minutes or until onions begin to turn translucent
3. add vegetable broth to pot , plus drained tomatoes , beans , carrot , hot water , and spices
4. bring soup to a boil , then reduce heat and allow to simmer for 20 minutes
5. add spinach leaves and pasta and cook for an additional 20 minutes or until desired consistency
6. makes about eight 1 1 / 2 cup servings
demonstrations.review: Fantastic!  This was spot on compared to Olive Garden!  I have already emailed this to everyone I can think of.  Now I just have to master those breadsticks...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blue baby shower punch

posted in response to a request for pastel blue punch on the boards a long while back, i figured i should probably go ahead and post this one officially so the recipe wouldn't get lost.  pink punch is easy enough to make, for little girls, but blue is a bit more elusive.  :)

1. mix together the kool-aid , water , and sugar according to the package directions
2. in a punchbowl , combine the prepared kool-aid , thawed pina colada mix , and 7-up or sprite
3. add scoops of vanilla ice cream
4. serve and enjoy !
5. :) it's to make the punch a pastel color , rather than bright blue
6. it's up to you whether or not you use it , but i think it's tasty !
demonstrations.review: Perfect for the baby shower I just hosted!  It was a hit and everyone wanted the recipe.  I used pineapple sherbert rather than ice cream.  Also would recommend not making large batches at a time because the kool aid/sugar/sherbert or ice cream starts to almost gel after awhile.  BUT....PERFECT for a little boys shower!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white trash candy snack

no, not your new neighbors; this no-bake candy treat is the perfect holiday snack! time listed includes refrigerator time.

1. mix all of the dry ingredients in a large bowl
2. melt the white chocolate chips in the microwave and then pour into the bowl with the dry ingredients
3. lay the mixture flat on cookie sheets and refrigerate until hardened
4. remove from refrigerator and break the mixture apart
demonstrations.review: I make this with Almond Bark rather than white chocolate chips, and then toss in reece's peanut butter minis rather than the chocolate chips.  And I throw in some Honeycomb cereal and popcorn as well.  It is never lasts very long!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggnog cookies

"what a delectable treat for eggnog lovers everywhere! these cookies have a wonderful spicy aroma and are great tasting. the fragrance of nutmeg and cinnamon will infuse your home with holiday spirit as you bake these cookies. they make delicious gifts and are a welcome addition to cookie exchanges. "

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. combine flour , baking powder , cinnamon and nutmeg
3. cream sugar and butter until light
4. add eggnog , vanilla , and egg yolks
5. beat at medium speed with mixer until smooth
6. add flour mixture and beat at low speed until just combined
7. do not overmix
8. drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet 1 inch apart
9. sprinkle lightly with nutmeg
10. bake 20 to 23 minutes until bottoms turn light brown
demonstrations.review: I got a little excited early this year for Christmas and made these.  Everyone really liked them, but they really do need icing or sprinkles to make them look a little more exciting.  I made icing and put eggnog in it as well.  Great for eggnog lovers!

target.recipe_text:
shrimp quesadillas

this is a great change from the usual sandwich for lunch. i've often thought i could try baking them all at once in the oven but i have'nt tried it yet. if anyone does, let me know how they turn out.

1. heat 10" non-stick skillet over med-high heat
2. place 1 tortilla in skillet and sprinkle with 1 / 4 cup cheese and 1 / 4 of tomato , bacon and shrimp
3. sprinkle with additional 1 / 4 cup cheese
4. top with another tortilla
5. cook 1-2 minutes or until bottom is golden brown
6. turn
7. cook 1-2 minutes longer or til bottom is golden brown
8. repeat 3 more times
9. cut each quesadilla into wedges
10. to keep quesadillas warm , place on a ungreased cookie sheet in oven
target.review: Easy to fix and a very tasty recipe. I used fresh shrimp and it was good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cheesy pork chops

one pan! quick prep! don't remember where it came from but it really is great!

1. using an electric frying pan , brown pork chops in olive oil
2. remove from pan
3. lower heat and add can of cheese soup , then fill can with milk and add
4. stir with whisk until smooth
5. add pork chops , potatoes and onion
6. bring temperature up to simmer
7. simmer covered for 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
8. serve in a casserole dish
demonstrations.review: I enjoyed fixing this recipe and my family enjoyed eating it.  I did not have the cheddar cheese soup so used a fiesta cheese soup that I had on hand.  It made it a little hot but very enjoyable.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flank steak fajitas

our family loves mexican food, and this is one of our favorites.

1. place beef in a slow cooker
2. in a bowl , combine the tomatoes , garlic , jalapeno , cilantro , chili powder , cumin and salt
3. pour over beef
4. cover and cook on low for 7-8 hours
5. stir in red and green peppers
6. cook 1 hour longer or until meat and peppers are tender
7. thicken juices if desired
8. using a slotted spoon , place about 1 / 2 cup beef mixture down the center of each tortilla
9. fold sides over filling
10. serve with sour cream , salsa and cheese if desired
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe and easy to fix.  My family really enjoyed it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe.  All of my family liked it and it was easy to make.  Definitely a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cottage cheese enchiladas

oh my!!! these enchiladas are too good to be true! i found this recipe on another recipe site and i just had to tell others about it! all of my guests love this dish. just be careful, they're filling!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. to make meat mixture: heat oil in medium saucepan , add either cooked shredded chicken or ground beef
3. add onion and saut and add taco seasoning and prepare according to package directions
4. to make cheese mixture: combine sour cream , cottage cheese , salt , and pepper in a medium bowl
5. to assemble enchiladas: take a bit of the meat mixture , cheese mixture , and shredded cheese and roll
6. place the enchiladas in a 9x13 baking dish , with folded edge on bottom of pan
7. top tortillas with any remaining meat or cheese mixture or shredded cheese
8. pour the enchilada sauce over tortillas
9. bake at 350 for 20-30 minutes or until bubbly
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: The absolute best recipe for enchilidas that I have ever tasted.  My family raved over it and my stepson said "this is definitely a keeper"  MMMMMM MMMMMM  Good

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk citrus shakes

i love making shakes for my boys after school, snack and drink in one. this beauty came from cuisine at home.

1. combine sugar and hot water in a small bowl
2. stir until dissolved
3. puree all ingrdients in a blender
4. be sure to add the ice last so it doesn't lock the blades
5. garnish each serving with 1 teaspoons crushed cookies , 1 / 2 teaspoons zest , and a lemon slice
6. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Very refreshing taste and not at all what I expected.  All the kids liked it.

target.recipe_text:
rub a dub t bones

this is the standard rub used in a restaurant located in buffalo gap, texas.  makes ½ cup. will cover 4-10 steaks, depending on size and flavor preference.

1. blend all dry ingredients together and rub into both sides of at least 4 t-bone steaks
2. heat 1 tablespoon canola oil in large skillet at fairly high heat
3. cook steaks for 5 minutes
4. turn , drop heat to medium and continue cooking for approximately 10 minutes for medium-rare , depending on the thickness of your steaks
target.review: very good, even my 6-and 3-year olds loved it! Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry orange pancakes

made with fresh or frozen cranberries, these pancakes have a hint of orange that makes for a tasty breakfast! original recipe is from the joy of cranberries: the tangy red treat, with a small tweak from yours truly! various syrups do well with these, but when they're topped with a cranberry syrup like recipe #304229, well . . .

1. in a small bowl , mix cranberries , sugar & zest & set aside
2. in large bowl , mix flour , baking powder , baking soda & salt
3. in another small bowl , mix egg , buttermilk , oj & butter , then add this mixture to flour mixture , stirring until just combined [batter should be lumpy]
4. fold cranberry mixture into the other mixed ingredients
5. heat a lightly greastd griddle or heavy skillet over medium heat
6. pour about 1 / 4 cup batter onto hot griddle for each pancake
7. cook pancakes until golden brown , then turn to cook other side
8. serve hot !
demonstrations.review: This one is a keeper! The kids and DH did not enjoy this, but I will be keeping this in my "Just-for-me" file. We can have those, right??

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chipotle roast for tacos   sandwiches

crock pot recipe. beware - this is spicy, but is an excellent shredded beef for tacos, sandwiches or enchiladas!

1. place chuck roast in large crock pot and sprinkle with the salt and pepper , chili powder and cumin
2. add the remaining ingredients and simmer on high for 5 hours or on low for 7-8 hours
3. shred the meat with a fork and simmer on high for additional 10-15 minutes
4. serve in enchiladas , tacos or on crusty rolls with the juice for dipping
demonstrations.review: I would give this ten stars if I could! My whole family loved this-I did omit chipoltes for the kiddos and used regular salsa. Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
snickerdoodle coffee mix

from gooseberry patch more gifts for giving.

1. combine all the ingredients together
2. store in airtight containers
3. instructions: add 3 tablespoons coffee mix to 3 / 4 cup boiling water
4. stir to dissolve
demonstrations.review: From my giftees (I don't like frill in coffee): This mix was gone in three days by two people. I am now making more for my DH. Great job!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
v8 chili

this is a real easy chili for picky eaters.

1. brown hamburger and garlic
2. drain hamburger and add to crockpot
3. while hamburger is browning , put can of chili beans , kidney beans , and v8 into crock pot
4. add chili powder
5. cook on high for 3 hours
6. before serving , add cayenne
7. shredded cheddar for topping
demonstrations.review: I was looking for a chilli recipe without actual tomatos for my dh, and this fits! He loved it, and since he works a rotating shift, I make it for him every time he goes in on nights ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter truffle brownies

for those of us who crave peanut butter and brownies together! from the betty crocker website.

1. heat oven to 350f grease bottom only of 13x9-inch pan with cooking spray or shortening
2. in medium bowl , stir brownie mix , pouch of chocolate syrup , water , oil and eggs until well blended
3. spread in pan
4. bake 28 to 30 minutes or until toothpick inserted 2 inches from side of pan comes out almost clean
5. cool completely , about 1 hour
6. in medium bowl , beat filling ingredients with electric mixer on medium speed until smooth
7. spread mixture evenly over brownie base
8. in small microwavable bowl , microwave topping ingredients uncovered on high 30 to 60 seconds
9. stir until smooth
10. cool 10 minutes
11. spread over filling
12. refrigerate about 30 minutes or until set
13. for brownies , cut into 9 rows by 4 rows
14. store covered in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: I like my chocolate rich! And these were amazing!!! Be prepared: this is the ultimate sweet tooth recipe.

target.recipe_text:
old fashioned corn fritters

this recipe brings back memories. my mom and older sister used to make these and they are yummy!

1. combine flour and powder in a large bowl
2. in a medium bowl , beat eggs and milk
3. stir in corn and butter
4. stir gradually into dry ingredients until just blended
5. in a deep fryer , electric frying pan or chicken fryer , heat oil until 375 degrees
6. drop batter into heaping teaspoonfuls into hot oil and fry for 2- 3 minutes
7. you can also do this using less oil in a skillet , just flatten them a bit with the back of the spoon and then turn them like pancakes
8. drain on paper towels
9. some people put confectioner's sugar or syrup on these , we eat them plain
target.review: my son made these for dinner the other night ( he's 11 ) and they turned out beautifully, so thank you on his behalf for sharing this recipe and for giving us a light and simple meal - which my son says he will definately make again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
guacamole with sour cream

my guacamole is very free-form, but here are the basics:  figure about 1/2 large avocado per person. i don't care whether i'm using haas or regular avocados - some people do. pick ones that give to mild pressure but are not mushy. if you can't find any that are ripe, get hard ones and keep them in a paper bag for a couple of days until they ripen.

1. cut the avocado in half , scoop out the flesh with a spoon
2. mash 3 / 4 of it well and chop the remaining 1 / 4 coarsely
3. mix it into the mashed portion
4. mix all remaining ingredients together
5. serve immediately , or cover with plastic wrap , pressing wrap firmly to surface of guacamole and refrigerate up to 4 hours before serving
demonstrations.review:
YUM!!! Thank you for sharing this simply, yet delicious recipe. 

My son, who unlike my other 3 kids usually thoroughly dislikes avocado, ate this without a second thought and even asked if he can help make it next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato  pumpkin and ham bake

we make this at work, sometimes substituting sweet potato for the pumpkin.

1. cook the potato and pumpkin in boiling water until just tender , drain
2. heat oil in a frypan over a medium heat and cook onion and ham for 2 minutes
3. combine with the potato and pumpkin in an oven proof baking dish
4. combine the remaining ingredients except the extra cheese
5. pour over the potato and pumpkin
6. sprinkle with extra cheese and bake in a 180c oven 35-40 minutes until golden brown and set
demonstrations.review: As always, your recipes are delicious and easily followed. I've been introducing my son ( he's 11 )too the wonders of cooking and this was his second attempt at making dinner for the family. Using your recipe, he was able to make a delicious and simple recipe which really boosted his self esteem in the kitchen. Thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dad s lasagna

like my father's rib recipe which i've also posted, this is a recipe which some old buddies of mine recently requested that i post. back when we all were a little younger, the guys used to come over everytime my dad made his lasagne. maybe it was the free meal or maybe it was just that good but this recipe is the reason why lasagna has always been one of my favorite foods. i know that you can substitute ground beef for the sausage (or use both combined) with equal success. i've posted this as 6-10 servings but i know from experience that 4 big guys can polish this off and still ask for more.

1. remove sausage skins and break up the sausage in frying pan
2. brown meat slowly and spoon off excess fat
3. add garlic , basil , 1 1 / 2 teaspoons salt , tomatoes and tomato paste
4. simmer , covered for 15 minutes
5. stir often
6. set aside when finished
7. meanwhile , cook noodles in boiling salted water until tender
8. drain
9. rinse
10. in a large bowl , beat eggs
11. add ricotta , parmesan , parsley , pepper and a tsp of salt
12. mix well
13. now in a 13x9x2 inch baking dish
14. layer half the noodles
15. spread with half the ricotta cheese / egg mixture
16. add half the thinly sliced mozzarella and then half the meat sauce
17. repeat
18. bake at 375 f degrees for about 30 minutes
19. alternatively , you could refrigerate until later and then bake for 45 minutes
20. either way let the lasagna stand for 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Awesome recipe. Kudos to you and your dad for this wonderful and now permentant addition to my household meal roster.. my son who is not a big pasta fan came back for 3 servings of this lasagna and then asked when I was making it again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon latte

these have become a sunday morning favourite for us. heavenly coffee to warm your tummy! the original recipe calls for ground cinnamon, but it also works very well if you put a couple whole cinnamon sticks or pieces of cinnamon bark in the cold milk. it will infuse the milk as it comes to a boil.

1. in a large pan , mix the cinnamon and sugar with a bit of milk
2. add the rest of the milk and bring to a boil
3. just as the mixture comes to a boil , take it off the heat
4. split your hot coffee between 4 mugs
5. pour in the milk and serve immediately
6. another variation is to leave out the ground cinnamon , but instead put a large cinnamon stick , some cloves and green cardamom pods in the milk
7. leave as it comes to a boil , set aside and let it infuse for a couple minutes
8. then strain out the seasonings and pour into the coffee
demonstrations.review:
Quick, easy and delicious.

I used the same ingredients for the milk, but added it too hot chocolate for my kids and they loved it. Thank you for sharing this recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
guinness pub burgers

from the great big burger book

1. in a bowl , gently mix the beef , beer , mustard , ginger , garlic , salt , and pepper together
2. form mixture into 4 patties , each inch thick
3. melt the butter in a large skillet over med-high heat
4. cook the burgers 3-5 minutes per side for medium or until desired doneness
5. remove patties from skillet
6. add in the scallions
7. cook 1-2 minutes , stirring , until just wilted
8. serve patties on toasted sesame seed buns with some pan sauce on top
demonstrations.review:
I've been slowly working my way through the recipes you have posted here and trying out different ones, I've yet to come across a meal I haven't enjoyed ( or my kids for that matter ) and this one is no different. My son loved the texture and flavour, making sure to give me all the help in the kitchen I could stand, by making sure I followed you directions to the letter , lol.

My daughter also enjoyed it, even if she was initially put off by seeing some of the ingredients used. Thanks for sharing another awesome meal idea!!

target.recipe_text:
hershey s s mores sandwich bar cookies

oh. my. god.
*moan*
these are so decadent, like richer, cookie-ish, layered s'mores.
i love everything hershey's, and this is no exception.
this recipe is courtesy of the hershey's kitchens site, so you know it's good!
this is my favorite diet cheat...beware, though. 
once you start eating these, you will not be able to stop.
enjoy!

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease 8-inch square baking pan
3. beat butter and sugar until well blended in large bowl
4. add egg and vanilla
5. beat well
6. stir together flour , graham cracker crumbs , baking powder and salt
7. add to butter mixture , beating until blended
8. press half of dough into prepared pan
9. bake 15 minutes
10. unwrap chocolate bars
11. arrange over baked layer , breaking as needed to fit
12. sprinkle with marshmallows
13. scatter bits of remaining cookie dough over marshmallows , forming top layer
14. bake 10 to 15 minutes or just until lightly browned
15. cool completely in pan on wire rack
16. cut into 16 bars
17. yum !
target.review:
This was finger smacking good!  
One egg was omitted from the ingredient list but is still mentioned in the instructions.  Yum

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato spinach slow cooker soup   0 points

from weightwatchers.com.  each 1 cup serving has 0 points.  perfect for a light meal or snack.

1. place all ingredients in a slow cooker
2. cover and cook on high for 5 hours or low for 8-10 hours
3. remove bay leaves , stir and serve
4. yields about 1 cup per serving
demonstrations.review: Good slow cooker soup recipe.  I used and 8oz bag of spinach and chicken broth instead of vegetable.  I ended up adding about 1.5-2 C of vegetable juice (V8) because my soup seemed a little to watery for my taste.  Tasted great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bev s macaroni and cheese

this is the recipe i have been using for macaroni and cheese since the beginning of time! truly a classic and a staple on our family table. i hope you enjoy it as much as we do. a great side dish to be served with my meatloaf barbecue style!

1. melt butter in medium saucepan
2. stir in flour , salt , mustard and pepper until smooth
3. remove from heat and gradually stir in milk until smooth
4. stirring constantly , cook over medium heat until thickened
5. remove from heat
6. stir in 1 1 / 2 cups cheese until melted
7. combine cheese mixture with macaroni in greased 2 quart casserole
8. sprinkle remaining cheese on top
9. bake in 375 degree oven for 25 minutes or until lightly browned
10. makes 6 servings
demonstrations.review: Oh yeah, this is the stuff dreams are made of!  I added a couple of slices of white American cheese for fun.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cauliflower   sweet potato curry soup

this is a wonderful soup, creamy and warm with just a hint of curry, it's quite enjoyable.

1. in a large saucepan sprayed with vegetable spray , heat the oil
2. saut the garlic and onion until softened , about 5 minutes
3. add the curry powder , cinnamon , salt , pepper , cauliflower , stock , sweet potatoesand honey and bring to a boil
4. cover , reduce the heat and simmer for 25minutes or until the potatoes are tender
5. transfer to a food processor or blender and pure until creamy and smooth
6. return to the saucepan and thin with more stock ifdesired
7. ladle into bowls
8. garnish with a dollop of sour cream and cilantro
demonstrations.review: This was super tasy and very fast and simple to make.  I used my immersion blender, and the followed the recipe exactly.  I'll be making this one again, thanks for posting kelly in TO!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade hamburger buns  bread machine

you will never want to buy hamburger buns again after trying this recipe. easy to do using a bread machine and so awesome! you can also top rolls with sesame seeds after brushing with melted butter.

1. place all ingredients , except butter , in pan of bread machine according to manufacturer's directions
2. select dough setting
3. when cycle is complete , turn out onto floured surface
4. cut dough in half and roll each half out to a 1" thick circle
5. cut each half into six 3 1 / 2" rounds with inverted glass as a cutter
6. place on greased baking sheet far apart and brush with melted butter
7. cover and let rise until doubled , about one hour
8. bake at 350 for 9 minutes
9. some reviewers baked these anywhere from 12 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I use a little less sugar, but other than that these buns are so, so good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brownie caramel layer bars

i got this recipe at a bake sale. they disappeared so fast! make sure you cut them into smaller squares because they can be very rich.

1. combine caramels and the first 1 / 3 cup evaporated milk
2. cook over low heat until melted
3. grease and flour 13x9 inch pan
4. in a large bowl combine cake mix , butter , second 1 / 3 cup evaporated milk , and nuts
5. stir until dough holds together
6. press half of the dough on the bottom of the pan , bake for 6 min at 350 degrees
7. sprinkle chocolate chips over crust
8. spread caramel over crust
