9. press the last half of cake mixture gently on top of the caramel
10. bake for 15-18 minute
11. cool slightly and refrigerate
12. cut into squares and serve with cool , creamy milk !
demonstrations.review: I substituted dark chocolate cake mix, but followed recipe for the rest.  Very good.  Very brownie like and gooey, but not over the top sweet.  Good with vanilla ice cream and a cup of hot coffee!

target.recipe_text:
mustardy fried chicken breasts

i got this recipe from an ex-boyfriend's mother.it gets rave reviews every time i make it.just be careful not to overcook the chicken.i usually use italian style bread crumbs and yellow mustard, but you could use any combination of bread crumbs and mustard that you have. i've used dijon mustard as well with very good results.you could also bake it in the oven, just be sure to cover it so it doesn't dry out.

1. wipe down chicken breast with paper towel
2. sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. in bowl , beat egg and mustard
4. in separate bowl combine cheese and bread crumbs
5. dip each breast in egg mixture then coat with cheese mixture
6. let set 10 minutes
7. saute chicken in oil for 15-20 minutes or until tender
target.review: Awesome chicken recipe! I made this exactly as the recipe states and I got the most tender, juicy and flavorful chicken breasts I've ever made. I'll be making this again without a doubt. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
never fail  biscuits

easy to make and hard to mess up!

1. mix dry ingredients
2. cut in butter
3. beat egg and milk slightly in separate bowl
4. milk together
5. kneed on floured surface
6. roll till desired thickness
7. cut out with a glass or cookie cutter
8. bake 350 for till golden brown
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe! I did have to add about 1/3 cup more flour, but it's been raining like crazy, so maybe the humidity played a part in that. These tasted so great. The dough rolled really nicely and was easy to work with. I'll have to print it again because my sister snagged the first recipe print. Thanks for a great recipe! ~Sheila

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no roll pie crust dough

i love to bake, but i'm terrible at rolling out pastry. the pie crust dough was my salvation! there's a total of 45 minutes resting time for the dough before baking.

1. melt butter
2. add both sugars and stir to combine
3. stir in flour
4. cool 15 minutes
5. use immediately by pressing into 10 inch pie plate and fluting edges
6. refrigerate atleast 30 minutes !
7. this can be blind-baked at 300f for 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a terrific recipe! I was using this crust in a savory pie, so I left out the sugars and added salt instead. Worked perfectly! I will be making many more pies in the future thanks to this recipe. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: These brownies are spectacular! I added 3/4 of a pound bag of mint chocolate M & M's. Oh pure heaven! This recipe is a sure keeper! Thanks Karen! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frosted zucchini brownies

absolutely the best way to use zucchini! moist and fudgy, worth the calories. my mother in law will do almost anything for me if i make her these! from taste of home.

1. combine zucchini , sugar , vanilla and oil
2. add dry ingredients and mix well
3. pour into a greased 9x13 pan and bake at 350 degrees f for 35-40 minutes
4. cool 30 minutes
5. for frosting , melt butter in a saucepan on medium heat
6. stir in sugar and milk , and bring to a boil , stirring frequently
7. boil and stir 1 minute , then remove from heat
8. stir in chocolate chips and marshmallows until melted
9. add vanilla and quickly spread over brownies
10. sprinkle with walnuts if desired
demonstrations.review: Spectacular! I had shredded zucchini out the wazoo and gave this one a try. I'm sure glad I did! It sort of reminded me of my favorite Texas Sheet Cake recipe. YUM! I was out of chocolate chips so I added 3 T. of cocoa to the frosting and a few extra tablespoons of sugar. It still came out wonderfully. Husband gave this is big thumbs up and it goes in to the make-again folder. Thanks for the terrific recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the absolute best applesauce spice muffins with spice topping

this is one of my all time favorite muffin recipes! --- you can substitute one large finely chopped apple for the nuts, increase the spices if desired --- some of the butter can be replaced with more applesauce for a lower fat muffin :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. set oven rack to second-lowest position
3. butter 12 muffin tins or line with paper liners
4. for muffins: in a small bowl mix together first 7 dry ingredients
5. in another large bowl whisk together eggs and brown sugar until well combined
6. add in melted butter whisking continuously until mixture is creamy
7. stir in applesauce
8. fold in flour mixture until just combined
9. stir in nuts
10. divide the batter evenly between muffin tins
11. to make the topping: stir together all ingredients then sprinkle over tops of muffin batter
12. bake for about 20-22 minutes , or until muffins test done
13. cool in pan for 5 minutes then remove to a rack to cool
demonstrations.review: Made a double batch of these today. One for my banker and one for my family. Superb! I did not add any nuts or raisins since I was not sure of taste preferences or allergies at the bank. Nice spice combo and I thought the sweetness level was right on the money. Easy, quick and yummy. Will make again for sure. Thanks Kittencal! ~Sheila

target.recipe_text:
oven fried garlic chicken

i gave this recipe from the "365 ways to cook chicken" cookbook an a+! it's easy and you'll probably have most of the ingredients already on hand.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a shallow bowl , blend together bread crumbs , parmesan cheese , parsley , salt , and pepper
3. in a small saucepan , heat butter and garlic over very low heat until butter melts
4. remove from heat
5. brush chicken pieces with garlic butter , then roll in bread crumb mixture to coat
6. place chicken skin side up on a large foil-lined baking sheet
7. mix together any remaining crumb mixture and butter and sprinkle over chicken
8. place in oven and bake 1 hour
target.review: This is definitely an A+++!  Even my extremely picky 6 yr old inhaled it with a "Mommy, make this tomorrow night too."  Needless to say, I am all smiles.  Instead of cutting the chicken into bites, I used 4 skinless boneless chicken breast, slowly nuked the butter/minced garlic in the microwave, and dredged each breast into the butter mixture and then bread crumb mixture (you know, to save on clean up time).  Baked in an oven dish for recommended time and viola.  Awesome!  Thanks for the new recipe :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan bow ties

kid favorite.

1. cook noodles according to package directions
2. drain
3. transfer to a serving bowl
4. add the remaining ingredients
5. toss to coat
demonstrations.review: As my extremely picky 6 yr old said, "     " NOTHING!  She was too busy stuffing her mouth full. She HATES salads and salad dressings, but didn't take notice to this dish!  Made the pasta as a side dish exactly as stated.  THANK-YOU for a keeper!  I will make this often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco bell quesadillas

i used to love these when i was younger, i could eat two in one sitting! i haven't had fast food in a year or two, but these taste like i remember taco bell's quesadillas tasting. i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

1. combine sauce ingredients and stir until smooth
2. grill chicken in vegetable oil and cut into thin slices
3. preheat skillet over medium heat
4. one at a time , lay tortilla into hot skillet and sprinkle with 1 / 4 cup of each shredded cheese and 1 / 2 cheese slice on one side of the tortilla
5. arrange about 1 / 4 cup chicken slices over tortilla on the same half covered with cheese
6. on the empty side , spread about one tablespoon of sauce
7. fold over , and press gently with spatula
8. cook until cheese is melted and slice each into 4 pieces
demonstrations.review: DH and I want to give this more stars!!  It was absolutely delicious.  Considering the fat content, I've only made it three times in the last 2 weeks!!! The first 2 times I followed the recipe exactly, the last time I sub. the mayo for fat free mayo, used fat free Kraft American processed cheese and Kraft Mexican shreddred cheese and we couldn't really taste a difference.  This recipe is definitely a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: This is absolutely delish!  I added carrots and halved red potatoes and the flavor was out of this world!  In fact, I can hardly wait to make it again because the meat was extremely tender and the food disappeared off my VERY picky childrens plates.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bruschetta chicken

i got this recipe from a local cable tv cooking show.

1. place flour and lighlty beaten eggs in separate containers that are large enough to accommodate each chicken breast
2. dip chicken in flour then in egg and place in greased 9x13 pan
3. combine the cheese , breadcrumbs & butter and sprinkle over chicken
4. loosely cover dish with foil & bake at 375 for 20 minutes
5. meanwhile combine remaining ingredients
6. uncover the chicken and bake an additional 5-10 minutes longer until top is browned
7. spoon tomato mixture over chicken , return to oven for 3-5 minutes or until just heated through
8. plate each breast and garnish with 2 or 3 whole basil leaves
demonstrations.review: I didn't disclose the name of this dish to my DH beforehand.  After his first bite, I asked him what it tasted like and he promptly said, "BRUSCHETTA!" with a huge smile!  In a week, I've made this twice and he is already asking me for it again.  This is definitely a great recipe!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
excellent carrot cake

chock full of flavor, this is the best carrot cake! it tastes even better the next day after the flavors meld. a tad more time consuming than the average carrot cake, but well worth it!

1. combine first 5 ingredients
2. beat well
3. mix flour , soda , salt and cinnamon
4. add to creamed mixture
5. stir well
6. add carrots , walnuts , pineapple and coconut
7. stir well
8. pour batter into greased and floured 13x9 baking pan
9. bake at 350 for 55 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
10. buttermilk glaze: combine first 5 ingredients in large saucepan
11. bring to a boil
12. cook 4 minutes on medium heat
13. remove from heat
14. add vanilla
15. pour buttermilk glaze over warm cake
16. let cake cool
17. cream cheese frosting: mix cream cheese and butter
18. beat until smooth
19. gradually add sugar , beating until light and fluffy
20. stir in vanilla
21. spread cream cheese frosting on top of cooled cake
demonstrations.review: Thank-you for my new very moist and delicious carrot cake recipe.  I made it for Easter and it was a huge hit!  Definitely cannot go wrong with this one!

target.recipe_text:
apple pecan pork chops

found in the newest issue of bh&g easy family food.

1. sprinkle chops with salt & pepper
2. set aside
3. in a large skillet , melt butter over medium heat until it sizzles
4. add apples
5. cook and stir for 2 minutes
6. push apples to side of skillet
7. add pork chops
8. cook for 4 minutes
9. turn chops over , moving apples aside as needed
10. spoon apples over chops
11. sprinkle with pecans & brown sugar
12. cover and cook for 4 to 8 minutes more or until an instant read thermometer inserted in centers of chops registers 160
13. spoon apples & cooking juices over chops
target.review: This was not only wonderful, but easy as well - flavorful, tender and moist.  I didn't change a thing except to scale down the recipe for two people and used bone-in pork loin chops as a personal preference.  My other half, who thinks chops can only be grilled, loved it and asked when I would make it again while eyeing the half that I couldn't finish!  Of course, I gave it to him  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops smothered in green beans

i got this dish from my mother's friend. this dish does tend to be more soupy than creamy but it also produces extremely moist pork chops.

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees
2. spray a baking pan with cook spray
3. mix the soup , sour cream , spices , & beans together
4. place the chops in the pan then pour the soup & bean mixture over the chops
5. cook in the oven for 30 minutes or until the chops are no longer link inside
6. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Going on NELady's comment, I used two 9 x 9 Pyrex and made half the recipe as per the instructions and the other half by adding 1/4 cup each FF sour cream and 2% cottage cheese.  Both were tasty, but the additional creaminess from the S/C and Cottage Cheese made it even better, as I prefer a creamy sauce.  Next time I'll add sliced mushrooms, diced celery, carrots, broccoli, fresh green beans and get all our veggies in one dish!!  Mahalo for the great meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
limoncello   lemoncella

this is a great lemony flavored vodka that is great for sipping after dinner, or anytime. i always try to keep some in the freezer.

1. wash the lemons well with a vegetable brush and hot water to remove any residue of pesticides or wax
2. pat the lemons dry
3. using a vegetable peeler , peel the lemons
4. if you do get some of the pith with the zest , carefully scrape it away with the
5. fill the jar with one bottle of the vodka and the zest
6. cover the jar and let it sit forty days at room temperature in a dark cabinet
7. combine the sugar and water in a saucepan , bring it to a boil and cook until thickened , about five minutes
8. let the syrup cool before adding it to the limoncello mixture , along with the other bottle of vodka
9. cover and return to the cupboard for another 40 days
10. strain the limoncello into bottles and discard the lemon zest
11. store them in a cupboard or the freezer
demonstrations.review:
Delish!
As I'm writing this I'm sipping on a small glass the strained and refrigerated first batch. I cut the recipe in 1/3 and now (like most) wish I had made the full portion. Already have lemons and vodka bought for the next batch of liquid sunshine. Mahalo for the recipe and you can bet I'll be gearing up to make this for Holiday gifts this year.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
decadent baked scallops

this recipe came from a co-worker of my best friend. it's absolutely delicious and somewhat rich.
please don't be put off by the ingredients. i promise you they are great if you like scallops and rich seafood. 
perfect when having guests.they will never guess how simple they are to make. 
i have had lots of compliments on these and have given out the recipe to many. they in turn have shared. 
trust me these are wonderful!
i haven't tried it yet, but you could probably add other fish as well.
i would like to try haddock (i'm a maine-iac) and lobster.

1. rinse scallops in cold water and drain well
2. toss flour in a quart plastic bag or put in bowl
3. dredge scallops in flour
4. and shake off excess
5. in casserole dish , place scallops in single layer
6. pour chicken broth around scallops until almost covered
7. pour melted butter over all
8. add pinch of thyme
9. top with enough crushed ritz crackers to thinly cover
10. bake 350 degrees approximately 40 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I *love* scallops and this sounds interesting enough to be delish....and will trust in your promise of yumminess. Since you suggested adding fish, I'm going to make this recipe 1/2 as posted and 1/2 with ono. Your a maine-iac and I'm one local kine wahine sitting in the middle of the Pacific ocean, lol! Have you tried fish? lobster?
You can bet I'll return with a full on review! Mahalo for positng.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green tortilla pinwheels

delicious, easy and everyone loves them! i know there are a few other recipes out there, but these pinwheels are to-die-for! the green salsa and the corn tortillas are the trick. mmmmmmm.... and i mean it! --use the amount of ingredients to your liking, you can't go wrong!

1. if you can find fresh tortillas , use them- they make all the difference !
2. over an open gas flame , place one tortilla at a time onto burner
3. cook for 10-15 seconds per side and flip with tongs
4. smear tortilla with cream cheese , add about half of a teaspoon of chiles and a plop of salsa
5. roll up tortilla and slice it into single bite servings- or better yet , eat it up all by yourself
6. 0)
demonstrations.review: Herdez green is the *best* !!!  Made half with corn torts and half with spinach torts due to picky eaters and while the spin torts were good, I preferred the corn!   Served with sour cream mixed with smushed avocado, taco seasoning & grated onion as well as a jalapeno relish (green Herdez  fresh jalapenos and onion, processed smooth & chilled 12-24 hours prior).  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
versatile mustard dip sandwich spread

this is such a versatile dip!  it goes wonderfully as a dip for most any kind of appetizer:  vegetables, chips, breadsticks.  one of my favorite ways to use this is as a dip for 
recipe #46078.
it's also great to keep on hand to use as a quick and delicious sandwich spread… you won’t believe how good it is on a ham and cheese sandwich or your favorite sub!

1. combine all ingredients in mixing bowl
2. transfer to a plastic air-tight container
3. keep refrigerated
4. will keep in refrigerator for up to 4 weeks
demonstrations.review: Made as directed the first time and it did indeed taste better after refrigerating a couple days (not that it tasted bad to begin with).  Second time I made it, I increased the mayo and decreased the sour cream (personal preference), used sriracha instead of chili powder, fresh garlic and just a dash of agave nectar for that one-two sweet & spicy punch.  Mahalo for a great recipe - and I'm also saving your sausage ball recipe for the next potluck party we attend!

target.recipe_text:
shrimp buongusto

a tasty shrimp dish in a red sauce which is very easy and quick to prepare (if you buy pre-cleaned shrimp). serve with pasta or rice. add a tossed green salad and crusty (garlic) bread to round out the meal.

1. wash and dry shrimp and roll them in flour
2. heat oil in a large skillet
3. brown shrimp on both sides in hot oil
4. remove oil from skillet and set aside
5. add wine to shrimp and cook until wine is reduced to half
6. put reserved oil into a small saucepan , add tomato paste , water , salt , pepper and cayenne and cook for 3 to 4 minutes
7. pour sauce over shrimp and add the parsley , scallion and truffle to the skillet
8. cook for 4 minutes
9. remove from pan and add lemon juice
10. serve with rice or pasta
target.review: Very good made it with tiger shrimp they turn blue when you remove the shell very strange, but they turn a normal shrimp color when heated. I was not sure of this recipe with basicaly just flour and wine but it was great. Served it over brown rice. I used some dry crushed red pepper instead of cayenne. I did not have any scailions so I used dry onion flakes and dry parsley.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
inside out chocolate chip cookies

these chocolate chip cookies are inside-out because they're chocolate cookies with white chocolate chips. i found this recipe in a booklet at the grocery store years ago.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. using a hand mixer , cream sugars , butter and shortening together until well mixed and fluffy , about 2 minutes
3. add vanilla and eggs and mix well
4. stir flour in it's container and spoon lightly into the measuring cup and level off when measuring
5. stir flour , cocoa , baking soda and salt together in a bowl
6. add flour mixture to creamed butter mixture and mix until well combined
7. stir in white chocolate chips and nuts
8. drop dough by rounded tablespoonfuls or a small cookie scoop about 2-inches apart onto ungreased or a parchment paper lined cookie sheet
9. bake 10-12 minutes or until set when you touch the tops
10. cool slightly
11. remove form cookie sheet
12. cool on wire rack
13. that's one of my cookie baking secrets
demonstrations.review: Great cookies they break real easy, but then the broken pieces don't have any calories....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetarian pasta e fagioli  pasta and beans

this is one of my many variations of the old italian standby. please feel free to adjust the types and/or amount of the dried herbs to suit your taste

1. in a large heavy pot , heat olive oil over medium high heat
2. stir in onion with a pinch of salt and pepper , and cook for 2 minutes
3. add dried herbs and red pepper flakes into the oil and toss to coat to bring out some of the dried herbs' flavors
4. stir in garlic , and then celery , and carrots and cook for about 3 minutes
5. stir in tomatoes and stock and bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes
7. if necessary add an additional cup of stock or water and stir in beans and tiny pasta
8. simmer for 6-8 minutes or until pasta is tender
9. stir in parsley and serve hot with grated parmesan and freshly ground black pepper
demonstrations.review: very good I added some chopped cooked chicken

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sugared asparagus

one of my favorites. brings out the sweetness of the asparagus.

1. in a skillet over medium-high heat , melt butter and brown sugar until sugar is dissolved
2. add asparagus
3. saute for 2 minutes
4. stir in chicken broth
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat
7. cover and simmer for 8-10 minutes or until asparagus is crisp-tender
8. remove asparagus to a serving dish and keep warm
9. cook sauce , uncovered , until reduced by half
10. pour sauce over warmed asparagus and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Very good not as sweet as I thought it was just right.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with artichokes and lemon

one-dish, low-fat, tasty and gourmet...does it get any better than that?! so elegant that your guests will never guess it was this easy! originally from 

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. spray shallow 2-quart casserole or baking dish with non-stick cooking spray
3. add ingredients in order given
4. mix gently
5. cover and bake 40 min , or until chicken breasts are tender to fork
6. for thicker sauce , remove cover for the last 15 min of cook time
7. may be made earlier in the day and stored in refrigerator until time to cook
8. also freezes for up to 6 wks
demonstrations.review:
WOW this is fantastic.  The chicken was sooooo tender you could cut it with a fork. I thought it would have too much lemon, but it was just right.
GREAT recipe..

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange sherried sweet potatoes

this goes very well with poultry or ham. the sherry can be substituted with ginger, maple syrup orcrushed pineapple if desired.

1. cook potatoes in boiling water until tender , about 30 to 40 minutes
2. drain , cool slightly and peel
3. while still warm mash with butter , orange rind , orange juice , sherry , sugar , nutmeg , salt and pepper
4. return to saucepan and heat over medium heat until hot
demonstrations.review: This was very good next time I will not put so much orange juice the orange taste was a little strong.

target.recipe_text:
tomato bread   bread machine

a fragrant, fabulous bread. i serve it with any sort of homemade soup, with an italian meal slathered in garlic butter, or...my favorite...make a grilled cheese sandwich with this bread!

1. place all ingredients in the order listed
2. set the machine for: 1 pound size
3. light crust
4. when bread is done , remove from the pan and let cool for 1 hour before slicing
target.review: this ended up being delicious. it is a bit small for my bread machine, so i will make a 2lb loaf next time. i ended up having to mix the dry ingredients to make sure it all got in there. i think it could also use a bit more spice. we at it with cheddar beer soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bird s creamed potatoes with roasted garlic

this is my most requested dish for mashed potatoes.

1. to roast garlic: cut the top off of an entire bulb of garlic just to expose the tops of the cloves and place in center of a small sheet of aluminum foil
2. drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and black pepper
3. fold edges of foil up around garlic cloves to form an open bag
4. roast in 350f oven until garlic is tender , about 1 hour
5. allow garlic to cool
6. turn bulb over and squeeze out the garlic cloves
7. mash with tines of fork
8. potatoes: place potatoes and onions a large pot
9. cover with enough water and add a little salt and bring to a boil over high heat
10. reduce heat to medium-high and cook until tender
11. drain potatoes and onions and then return them to the pot or a mixing bowl
12. add remaining ingredients and beat until smooth
13. serve to the table in a large serving bowl with a pat of butter in the center and sprinkled with some fresh chopped parsley
demonstrations.review: we love these! the roasted garlic is perfect (sometimes we use the whole bulb, sometimes not. depends on who all is eating.) they come out so smooth. i usually leave out the onion as my husband doesn't like them much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jamaican lentil stew with coconut

1 pot, 1 hour = simple, incredibly tasty vegetarian meal.  truly a delightful change from ordinary lentil stew or soup.  make sure you have a hunk of great bread to sop up the stew juices or you'll end up using your fingers!  add a salad for a complete meal.

1. make a thick paste by mashing ginger and garlic together using a pestle and mortar or a small bowl and the heel of a wooden spoon
2. heat vegetable oil over medium heat in a large saucepan , add the onion and saute until transparent
3. add the garlic ginger paste and saute another 2 minutes until fragrant
4. lower heat and stir constantly to avoid burning the paste
5. add the spices and saute for a minute more
6. stir in the coconut milk , stock , lentils , sweet potato and pumpkin puree
7. simmer over medium - low heat for 40 - 50 minutes or until sweet potato is soft and almost melting into the stew
8. be sure to stir occasionaly
9. before serving , stir in the red curry paste if you are using it or adjust seasoning with black pepper
10. if you prefer a lighter soup then add more stock to thin the base , or try adding more cocount milk for a very savory and unique taste
demonstrations.review: This was delicious! We had company over and served this soup with a simple salad and some potato latkes. Was a very balanced, filling soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
refreshing mojito  by the pitcher mojitos

this is a refreshing cuban drink. it's hard to stop drinking these on a hot summers day. i made these for the fourth of july and we went on to 3 yes 3 pitchers! if you don't have a muddle stick try a mortar and pestle or the end of a wooden rolling pin. please use fresh lime if you cannot go ahead and try the already bottled lime juice but if you do think about that when you rate this recipe! i did both and there's nothing like fresh! same goes for the fresh mint if you need to you can use frozen but i don't recommend extract. and for the sugar real granular is what helps muddles the lime and extract the mint oils from the leaves.

1. place lime juice , mint and sugar into a pitcher
2. using a muddle stick mash to release mint oils , and dissolve sugar into juice
3. add rum and lots of ice topped with club soda
4. adding more club soda to glasses if a lighter drink is desired
5. garnish with fresh mint and lime slices
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious, particularly with more rum and less soda.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really good vegetarian meatloaf  really

high in fiber and protein, low in fat, easy and really yummy! i've always thought meatloaf looks and smells so delicious and savory so, as a vegetarian, i decided to make a no-meat version! this is basically our favorite meatloaf recipe but with cooked mashed lentils instead of ground meat. the result is a very tasty dinner!

1. add salt to water and boil in a saucepan
2. add lentils and simmer covered 25-30 minutes , until lentils are soft and most of water is evaporated
3. remove from fire
4. drain and partially mash lentils
5. scrape into mixing bowl and allow to cool slightly
6. stir in onion , oats and cheese until mixed
7. add egg , tomato sauce , garlic , basil , parsley , seasoning salt and pepper
8. mix well
9. spoon into loaf pan that has been generously sprayed with pam or well-greased
10. smooth top with back of spoon
11. bake at 350 degrees for 30- 45 minutes until top of loaf is dry , firm and golden brown
12. cool in pan on rack for about 10 minutes
13. run a sharp knife around edges of pan then turn out loaf onto serving platter
demonstrations.review: this was pretty good. it was a little dry for us, but the flavor was tasty. i think the onions needed to cook a bit longer. we did like the flavor though and will try it again with a little fiddling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tillamook beer cheese soup

this is from the tillamook cheese factory - some of the best cheese in the world!!!!! of course i'm biased cause they're in my home state :-) this is my fave beer cheese soup -- you can use other cheese, just make sure it's extra sharp!

1. heat butter in saut pan
2. add flour and cook on low heat
3. stir mixture until it starts to bubble
4. do not allow to brown
5. pull off fire and set aside
6. heat milk in sauce pan until it is just ready to boil
7. add garlic , salt and pepper and crushed chilies
8. stir mixture until just before boiling
9. add half of flour / butter mixture and stir with wire whisk until at a low simmer
10. additional roux may be added to thicken
11. stir constantly to avoid burning
12. turn down heat and add cheese and beer
13. stir to allow cheese to melt
14. texture should be smooth to the touch
15. may be reheated on low temperature
demonstrations.review: love it!!!! will probably add some finely chopped caramelized onion next time.  you do have to be very careful not to overheat it.

target.recipe_text:
taco ring  from pampered chef

i attended a pampered chef party and had this taco ring.  i had ate them many times but was always to scared to make one.  it's so easy--took me a few times to make it look pretty but it's really simple to do, just experiment around with it.  my kids now request these instead of regular tacos.  i was out of black olives tonight, so i used green--the toppings are your personal choice really!  makes 16 rolls but we can't eat just one!

1. cook ground beef in large skillet over medium heat 7-9 minutes or until beef is no longer pink
2. drain
3. remove pan from heat
4. stir in taco seasoning mix , cheese and water
5. preheat oven to 375f
6. unroll crescent dough
7. separate into triangles
8. arrange triangles in a circle on classic round pizza stone with wide ends overlapping in center and points toward outside
9. i use my pampered chef pizza stone , but any flat round pan should work--perhaps even a pizza sheet , but i'd spray it with pam before adding the crescent rolls
10. scoop meat mixture evenly onto widest end of each triangles up over filling and tuck under wide ends of dough at center of ring
11. bake at 20-25 minutes or until golden brown
12. shred lettuce and chop tomato , onion , olives , and bell pepper
13. if you want to do something fancy , scoop out a bell pepper and fill with salsa and put into center of ring
14. add your toppings to top of ring and finish with more shredded cheese and sour cream
15. this is great with a salad
target.review: A great recipe and a perfect taco dish for the whole family.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white fish in herbed butter

frequently requested, easy to make.

1. mix all but fish in small bowl
2. heat skillet
3. add butter mixture
4. add fish and saute for about 6-7 minutes on each side
5. garnish with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: This fish is so amazing. I added a touch of lemon juice and it was divine. I'll be making it again, as soon as I can!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jambalaya for the crock pot

try this for your next crock pot adventure. wonderful flavor!

1. cut chicken into 1 inch pieces
2. put all ingredients in crock pot
3. cover
4. cook on low for 8 hours
5. add shrimp the last 20 minutes of cooking
6. stir in rice before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this for my picky husband who dislikes spice and it was so good and even with the spicy kick we both loved it. No leftovers here!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ginger me up chicken  low fat honey   ginger chicken breasts

this is a recipe i have been making for yonks now.....i first devised it about 18 years ago, when i was following rosemary connely's "hip & thigh diet"!! it's a very easy low fat chicken dish, which can be pan fried or baked in the oven - i prefer the latter method, it's much easier! serve it with a medley of gently steamed vegetables, rice or pasta. (nb: please note, one of the reviewers has stated that she cooked this in a crockpot!! i would never suggest cooking this recipe in a crockpot, that's why it is not mentioned as a cooking method anywhere in the recipe - only pan-fried or oven baked. thanks! )

1. preheat the oven to 180c or 350f
2. select a sturdy oven dish - preferably non-stick
3. place the chicken breasts into the baking dish
4. mix the honey , mustard , water , ginger & crushed garlic together in a measuring jug
5. pour over the chicken breasts , easing them up slightly so the mixture runs underneath them
6. season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste and bake in the oven for 45 to 60 minutes
7. serve one chicken breast per person with some of the cooking sauce drizzled over the top of the chicken
8. garnish with chopped parsley & serve with a medley of steamed vegetables & pasta
9. to pan fry , heat up a frying pan and add the chicken breasts - dry fry them briefly to give them a bit of colour and add the cooking sauce , mix well and cook for about 20- 30 minutes over a medium heat
10. serve as before
demonstrations.review: This came out delicious. Very tender, a hint of spice but nothing overpowering. I think next time I'll lower the amount of mustard I use just for personal taste but it was a pleaser!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple caribbean jerk chicken

i like jerk chicken but often don't have all the exotic ingredients. this simplifies the mix by using dry italian dressing. yummy on the grill!

1. mix all ingredients except chicken in bowl
2. pour over chicken
3. cover and marinate 1 hour or over night in fridge
4. grill it !
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I wasn't expected much of this recipe since it wasn't the way I'm used to preparing jerk chicken but it was so delicious! My husband requests this recipe now and it was great. It's not as spicy as some jerk chicken recipes but it's a great meal that is on my dinner table often now.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
substitution for pumpkin pie spice

out of pumpkin pie spice and only need a little to get you through until you buy more? from hamilton beach web site a few years back.

1. stir or shake ingredients together
2. store in a closed small container
3. use in place of"pumpkin pie spice" in your recipe
demonstrations.review: This is the perfect blend. I just used it in pumpkin doughnuts and it was delicious.

target.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
target.review: This turned out super delicious.  It was fairly simple to throw together, and the instructions were very easy to follow.  The sauce was wonderful, and everything turned out perfect.  Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai chicken pizza

an easy version of the california pizza kitchen favorite. i like to use the italian pizza crust (boboli) because it is quick, but you could also adapt it to use your own favorite pizza crust. a good one i like here on zaar is recipe  #8497 posted by steve sickenberger.

1. in food processor or blender , combine peanut butter , vinegar , soy sauce , chili oil , ginger , honey and sesame oil
2. set aside
3. season chicken to taste with salt and cayenne pepper
4. saute in olive oil until done
5. cut chicken into bite sized pieces and coat with 2 tablespoons of the peanut sauce
6. spread peanut sauce over the surface of the italian pizza crust
7. scatter chicken pieces over top and sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions
8. sprinkle with 1 / 2 cup of mozzarella cheese and 1 / 2 cup of the monterey jack cheese
9. bake , uncovered in 400f oven for 12 minutes
10. remove from oven and sprinkle with shredded carrot and cilantro
demonstrations.review: I really loved the sauce!  This turned out really great.  Even my husband liked it, and he isn't generally a fan of Thai food.  Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nestle toll house chocolate chip cookies  high altitude

it took me almost two years to clue into the fact that most of my formerly successful baking recipes were failing because i moved to a high altitude location. i've yet to try this high altitude recipe for chocolate chip cookies (from the back of the toll house bag), but certainly plan on it the next time as the cookies i've baked with the regular toll house recipe turn out flat as can be. the recipe specifies high altitude as 5,200 feet (or 1,585 meters). feel free to substitute your favorite baking chip -- i like the chocolate caramel swirled kind.

1. preheat oven to 375 f / 190 celsius
2. combine flour , soda and salt in a small bowl
3. cream together butter , sugars and vanilla extract in a large bowl
4. add eggs , one at a time , to butter mixture , beating well after each addition
5. gradually beat flour mixture and water into the wet ingredients until well combined
6. stir in morsels and nuts
7. drop by rounded tablespoon onto ungreased baking sheets
8. bake 8-10 minutes or until golden brown
9. cool on baking sheets 2 minutes , then transfer to wire racks
10. for a pan cookie : grease pan , prepare dough as indicated above , spread into pan and bake 17-19 minutes
demonstrations.review: Hey thanks for posting this!  These were the first cookies that I have made here in the "mountains" that have actually turned out as well as the ones I used to make in the desert.  This is my favorite cookie recipe by far....and the best cookie dough  =)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
restaurant teriyaki sauce

you know the nice, sweet, thick teriyaki sauce you get from your favorite takeout joint? now you can have it at home.

1. mix all but cornstarch and 1 / 4c water in a sauce pan and begin heating
2. mix cornstarch and cold water in a cup and dissolve
3. after sauce is simmering , add cornstarch and water mixture , whisking well until sauce thickens
4. heat until sauce thickens to desired thickness
5. add water to thin if you over-thick it :)
demonstrations.review: We all really liked this.  It had a good flavor and was a lovely consistency.  We used it as a glaze over our kabobs, and as a dipping sauce.  Thanks for posting such a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried garlic chicken

i gave this recipe from the "365 ways to cook chicken" cookbook an a+! it's easy and you'll probably have most of the ingredients already on hand.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a shallow bowl , blend together bread crumbs , parmesan cheese , parsley , salt , and pepper
3. in a small saucepan , heat butter and garlic over very low heat until butter melts
4. remove from heat
5. brush chicken pieces with garlic butter , then roll in bread crumb mixture to coat
6. place chicken skin side up on a large foil-lined baking sheet
7. mix together any remaining crumb mixture and butter and sprinkle over chicken
8. place in oven and bake 1 hour
demonstrations.review: We just finished dinner, and this turned out really good!  I used chicken breast, and might have added a bit more garlic, but otherwise followed the recipe pretty exactly.  Even my husband liked it, and he isn't usually that fond of garlic.  Thanks for posting this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
most incredible no fail pie crust

this is absolutely the best pie crust i have ever used. it never fails me and always comes out flaky and perfect. this recipe is enough for 2 - 9" crusts.

1. cut together flour , shortening and salt until it resembles small peas
2. combine the egg , water and vinegar and gradually add to flour mixture
3. stir just until moistened and a soft dough forms
4. divide into 2 disks
5. wrap and refrigerate until ready to use
6. roll out and use with your favorite pie recipe !
demonstrations.review: This is the same recipe that my mom taught me when I was a kid, and it is definately the best.  It always turns out so well, tastes great and is so easy to work with.

target.recipe_text:
chicken curry in a hurry

watch out or you might get pulled over for a speeding ticket in the kitchen! ready in 20 minutes. :)

1. mix together flour , salt and cayenne pepper in a plastic bag
2. add chicken in small batches , shaking to coat
3. heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add chicken and cook until lightly browned
5. then add curry powder and toss to coat
6. remove from pan
7. add onion and garlic to pan , adding a little more oil if necessary , and cook for 2 minutes , then add broth , raisins , and tomato paste
8. return chicken to pan and simmer uncovered for 8 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and sauce has thickened
9. garnish with cilantro and a dollop of yogurt
10. serve with quick cooking minute rice , if desired
target.review: This is certainly not the typical curry that I am used to but this is still great! I've never cooked curry before as it's very time consuming but after reading all the reviews here, I just have to give this recipe a try. DH who can't stand the smell of curry is also a fan of this dish and that is a major WOW! Thank you very much, Sue!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer battered fish  for fish n chips

i love fried fish.. always have. when dining out, nine times out of ten, i will order fish n'chips. it's getting to be very hard to find a restaurant that serves good fish n'chips anymore..so i just had to learn to make them myself.

1. sift together flour , salt , and paprika
2. stir in enough beer to make batter so it is barely thick enough to coat a spoon
3. usually somewhere between one and two cans
4. set batter aside while you heat your deep-fryer or deep pan of oil to 375 degrees
5. use a candy thermometer if you need to
6. peanut oil is best but any vegetable oil will do
7. cut the cod fillets diagonally into 2 inch wide strips , and remove any pin bones from fish
8. lightly coat fish in flour and shake off excess
9. this will allow batter to stick to fish
10. when oil is heated , dip fish in batter , let excess drip off , then fry fillets 2 or 3 at a time until golden brown
11. drain on paper towels
12. serve with fries and tartar sauce
demonstrations.review: Fabulous! Big hit with hubby and he said it's better than some restaurants. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
big sandwich spread

great for a party or a potluck meal. i usually make my own french bread but i've also used store bought french bread before and it works well too.

1. mix all the spread ingredients together
2. slice a loaf of french bread lengthwise
3. spread mixture on the inside of both halves
4. top bottom half with any combination of sandwich meats that you desire
5. can also be topped with pickles if you wish
6. place top half of bread on the sandwich and slice into individual servings
demonstrations.review: Very very good sandwich spread, better than some restaurants! I half the amount as there's only DH and me and it's MAJOR YUM! I was worried that it would be too 'cream cheesy' but boy was I wrong. All the ingredients melded together beautifully and gave such amazing taste. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super creamy and cheesy mac and cheese

i always make a big batch of this because my husband and i both love this and always want more.

1. cook the macaroni and set aside
2. in a pot , melt the butter and mix in salt and pepper
3. slowly add in the flour , stirring continuously
4. gradually add the milk and stir the mixture until smooth
5. add the cheese on a low heat and melt into the mixture
6. once the mixture is at your desired consistency , mix in the drained macaroni
demonstrations.review: Thank you, little_spoon! DH really loves this recipe! Changes I made were; I scaled everything down to half, added half teaspoon of dry mustard and garlic powder each; added 3 strips of streaky bacons. Awesome!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese chicken noodle salad

if you love pasta salads that contain crisp veggies you'll love this. the dressing is really delicious. the flavors get better after 2 or 3 days in the fridge. i got this great recipe from a friend.

1. cook spaghetti in boiling water for 9 minutes
2. add sliced snow peas and cook for 1 more minute
3. drain and rinse under cold , running water
4. drain well
5. combine pasta mixture , chicken , green onions and bell pepper in a very large mixing bowl
6. set aside
7. in a separate bowl combine teriyaki sauce , sesame seeds , sesame oil
8. also salt , pepper and chili oil
9. pour over pasta mixture and toss well
10. serve at room temperature or chilled
11. keeps well in the fridge for up to a week
demonstrations.review: Hubby and I both love this. Thank you for such a wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steak  or chicken  fajitas

these are so quick and tasty. you can use strips of boneless chicken breast instead of the beef. feel free to double the marinade. the flavor is so great for such a short marination time. you can can do them up ahead of time and have the meat sit longer if you wish.

1. slice steak into thin strips
2. in bowl , mix together 1 tablespoons olive oil , lime juice , garlic , chili powder , cumin , hot pepper flakes , black pepper & salt
3. add beef strips and stir to coat , set aside
4. wrap tortillas in foil and place in 350 oven for 5-10 minutes or until heated through
5. cut onions in half lengthwise and slice into strips , cut your peppers into strips
6. in large non stick skillet over medium high heat , heat remaining tablespoons of olive oil
7. add onions & peppers stirring for 3-4 minutes , until softened
8. transfer to a bowl and set aside
9. add beef to skillet , cook , stirring for 3-4 minutes or until they lose their red color
10. return onions and peppers to skillet
11. stir for about one minute
12. to serve , spoon a portion of the beef mixture down the centre of each tortilla , top with your desired toppings , fold bottom of tortilla up over filling , fold the sides in , overlapping
demonstrations.review: What can I say that others have not said? AMAZING! I followed the recipe and didn't change a thing. I did use Recipe #16892 as chili powder, I think it's better and hey, it's also cheaper as I got everything on hand. Personally, this recipe is restaurant quality and what makes it even better is the fact it is soooo darn easy to make! Thank you, Rhonda for sharing this great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
impossible peanut butter cookies

these are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!

1. mix peanut butter , sugar , and egg together until smooth
2. drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart
3. if desired , roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet
4. press with fork
5. press again in opposite direction
6. bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
7. do not brown
8. do not over bake
target.review: YOU WILL NEVER NEED ANOTHER P.B. COOKIE RECIPE!  My 6 year old can make these alone.  So simple and so delicious.  We always add 1 t of vanilla and on special occasions top with chocolate kisses.  This is a family favorite!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot whole chicken

tender, fall-off-the-bone chicken! skip the overnight refrigeration if you are in a hurry. for variety, eliminate the onion and substitute a quartered lemon or two, stuffed into the chicken cavity.  chef shapeweaver had a good suggestion:  use fajita seasoning mix #28011 as another variation.  thanks!  the standard size slow cookers are a bit too small and a whole chicken won't fit.  you'll need a 6-quart slow cooker for this recipe.

1. in a small bowl , combine the spices
2. remove any giblets from chicken and clean chicken
3. rub spice mixture onto the chicken
4. place in resealable plastic bag and refrigerate overnight
5. when ready to cook , put chopped onion in bottom of crock pot
6. add chicken
7. no liquid is needed , the chicken will make its own juices
8. cook on low 4-8 hours
demonstrations.review: I loved the ease of this recipe.  However, I do not care for white pepper and wished that I had left it out.  I find that it has a very unique flavor and something that you have to acquire a taste for.  I think I will like the chicken better if I leave it out.  It was very tender and moist.  Wonderful to come home to dinner being done!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best seller caramel corn

when i used to regularly do christmas craft shows, i always sold this packaged up in christmas tins; it was a big seller for me. my sil always hoped it wouldn't sell well, though, so she could eat what didn't sell! based on a bonnie stern recipe.

1. when i make this recipe , it's the only time i haul out my hot-air popcorn popper
2. use 1 / 3 cup popcorn to achieve the 8 cups of popped corn
3. preheat oven to 275f
4. have ready a jelly roll pan
5. place popped corn in a very large bowl
6. in a large , heavy saucepan over high heat , combine the sugar , butter and corn syrup and bring to a boil
7. let boil for two minutes , stirring continuously
8. remove from heat
9. add baking soda and vanilla to sugar mixture and combine well
10. pour this mixture over popped corn and combine , then spread mixture out onto jelly roll pan
11. bake in preheated oven for 40 minutes , stirring well every 10 minutes
12. let cool before eating
demonstrations.review: Absolutely addictive!!!  We made it for the holidays and it was gone just as quickly as it was coming out of the oven.  Way better than anything you could ever buy in a store!  This recipe is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amaretto cow

similar to a brown cow, but using amaretto.
serve over ice....delicious change of pace!

1. fill an old-fashioned glass with ice , add amaretto and cream , stir
2. garnish with maraschino cherries on a plastic sword or stick
3. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Amaretto and cream?!?!  Can life get any better?  Delish!  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: My kids think that there a few recipes on this web site that deserve more than 5 stars.  This is one of them.  I made this so qickly for an impromptu gathering.  AND they were gone just as quickly as I could cut them.  People loved this and I loved the simplicity!  Thank you for a new addition to my cookbook

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s juicy crock pot turkey breast

this method creates a very moist flavorful turkey breast, the low slow cooking will create juice if you want more juice just add in a can of low-sodium chicken broth undiluted although you really don't need to --- do not add in any extra salt the onion soup mix is salty enough --- for best flavor i recommend not to use previously frozen then thawed turkey breast, use fresh if possible, since every crock pot cooks differently the cooking time is only estimated, a bone-in breast will need slightly longer to cook --- see my  recipe#145064

1. rinse the breast under cold water , then pat dry using paper towel
2. lightly rub vegetable oil all over the turkey breast
3. in a small bowl mix together the onion soup mix with garlic and black pepper , then rub all over the breast and underneath the skin
4. cover and cook on high for 1 hour
5. reduce the heat to low and cook for about 5 hours for a 6-pound breast , for a larger breast increase cooking time slightly
demonstrations.review: This is a NO FAIL recipe without question.  Deliciously moist!!!  *****Fatastic*****

target.recipe_text:
broccoli chicken dijon  south beach diet

this recipe comes from krafthealthyliving.com.  i haven't tried it yet, but it looks wonderful!  as soon as i get a chance to make this dish, i'll let you all know how it is.

1. mix chicken broth and soy sauce
2. set aside
3. cook and stir broccoli and garlic in hot oil in large skillet on medium-high heat until crisp-tender
4. remove from skillet
5. cover to keep warm
6. add chicken to skillet
7. cook and stir 3 to 4 minutes or until cooked through
8. add broth mixture
9. mix well
10. bring to boil
11. reduce heat to medium-low
12. stir in mustard until well blended
13. return broccoli mixture to skillet
14. mix lightly
15. cook until heated through , stirring occasionally
target.review: Wonderful!! I cooked in reverse, chicken first, like another reviewer. My only changes were adding a bit of sesame oil and mushrooms. Served over rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy grilled herbed fish

a little dish i created a couple of years back. extremely healthy. the fish turns out really moist, and the juice is out of this world. i usually add a little more garlic, but i am crazy about garlic. has become such a staple with my family that it is requested for at least once a month. don't worry about adding any salt, i personally feel that it isn't needed. the herbs and juices mixed together makes it all natural and tasty enough. but if you feel some salt is lacking, just sprinkle a little before digging in. enjoy!

1. cut a piece of tin foil big enough to wrap round the fish twice
2. brush the middle portion of foil with olive oil
3. place the fish fillet on top of the greased foil
4. rub ginger juice into fish
5. sprinkle a pinch of pepper on top of fillet
6. spread the oregano and basil evenly over the top of fillet
7. sprinkle the finely chopped garlic over the top of herbs
8. rest the tomato slices on top
9. arrange the onion rings over the fillet
10. squeeze the juice of both the orange and the lemon over the whole fillet
11. grate the zest of both the orange and lemon on the top
12. wrap up the fish with all the ingredients in the foil
13. place the envelope in the grill and grill at 400f for 20 minutes
14. turn the grill off and let it sit in the grill for another 10 minutes
15. remove the envelope , cut an "x" on the top , place on plate and serve
demonstrations.review: Fabulous! I used tilapia and substituted ground ginger for the ginger juice. Otherwise, followed recipe exactly and it came out perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s chocolate fudge frosting

another recipe from my grandma. i still remember making this with her as a little girl. rich and creamy!

1. put first three ingredients in a sauce pan
2. bring to a boil , while stirring constantly
3. remove from heat and add chips
4. with a wire whip beat until creamy and cooled
5. add chopped pecans if desired
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!! Very rich! I made ahead and stored in fridge. It did harden like fudge. I just needed to microwave slightly to soften it up to frost the cake. I added Heath bar bits to the top. Get any toppings on quick because frosting will harden again into a creamy fudge frosting! Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy bacalao   puerto rican fish stew

mmmm...serve with crusty rolls to soak up the juices! this quick version of puerto rican stew from eating well magazine uses tilapia or any white flaky fish. the traditional dish uses bacalao, or salted dried codfish.

1. heat oil in a large high-sided skillet or dutch oven over medium heat
2. add onion and cook , stirring occasionally , until softened , about 2 minutes
3. add garlic and cook , stirring , for 1 minute
4. add fish , tomatoes and their juices , chile pepper , cilantro , olives , capers , oregano and salt
5. stir to combine
6. add up to 1 / 2 cup water if the mixture seems dry
7. cover and simmer for 20 minutes
8. remove from the heat
9. serve warm or at room temperature , garnished with avocado if desired
demonstrations.review: Loved this exactly as the recipe is written! Serve with bread because you won't want to leave a drop of the stew in your bowl!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy indian eggplant spread

a nice spread.  you can easily adjust the heat by varying the amount of cayenne pepper.  it smells wonderful while simmering!  i found this recipe in the sunday paper.  serve warm with pita, naan, tortilla or pita chips!

1. toss eggplant with 3 tablespoons vegetable oil and spread on a long baking sheet prepared with nonstick cooking spray
2. place on bottom rack of oven and turn oven onto 400f roast for 20 minutes , until golden brown
3. stir eggplant and roast for an additional 5 minutes
4. heat remaining oil in a skillet and add onion
5. saute until onion is golden , then stir in garlic and ginger for just a moment
6. add garam masala , cumin , and cayenne pepper
7. once spices are fragrant , about another 30 seconds , add eggplant , tomatoes , and water to skillet
8. simmer for 10 minutes , partially covered , before removing from heat
9. stir in cilantro and salt , if desired
10. optional: run spread through food processor or blender if you prefer it to have a smoother consistency
demonstrations.review: This was fabulous!!!!! One of the most flavorful recipe I've found on this site. I substituted the canned tomatoes with fresh chopped. I also added 8 oz tomato sauce and simmered it on low for a long time until eggplant soft (my preferences). The flavors were divine! I served as side dish to Chicken Masala and served with naan. Yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fried broccoli

my friends and i used to make this for every barbeque when i was growing up. it is an adaptation of a recipe my girlfriend's dad saw on tv. although i have no idea what that original recipe was, this one tastes soooooooooo good with barbequed anything!  it is broccoli so it tastes like broccoli.  if you're expecting something else then this recipe won't please you :)

1. in a frying pan heat olive oil
2. put in a pinch of rosemary and saute until the scent gets very pungent
3. add broccoli and a couple of dashes of white pepper
4. saute until the broccoli gets very green but looks crunchy / cooked
5. lastly , toss in bread crumbs a bit at a time while still sauteing
6. the crumbs will start to stick into the broccoli
7. once all or most of the crumbs are in the broccoli , saute for 1 or 2 minutes longer to brown
8. serve right away
demonstrations.review: This was fabulous! I followed some of the other suggestions to add some garlic and butter. So simple and delicious!

target.recipe_text:
southwest vegetarian bake

this is a good hearty winter meal. it can easily be made healthier by using low fat sour cream and cheese.

1. in a large saucepan , bring rice and water to a boil
2. reduce heat
3. cover and simmer for 35-40 minutes , until tender
4. in a bowl , combine beans , corn , tomatoes , salsa , sour cream , cheddar , pepper and rice
5. transfer to a 2 1 / 2 quart baking dish coated with nonstick spray
6. sprinkle onions and olives over top
7. bake , uncovered , at 350f for 30 minutes
8. sprinkle mexican cheese over top
9. bake 5-10 minutes longer , until cheese is melted
10. let stand 10 minutes
target.review: This really good and satisfying. Our family is cutting back on meat and this filled everyone up and we didn't miss the meat.......although it would probably be really tasty with some shredded chicken for those that aren't vegetarians

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato soup mix in a jar

here's a very inexpensive recipe for 

1. in a medium bowl mix dry ingredients well and pour into a 1 quart jar
2. seal and attach: place 1 / 2 cup of soup mix in a bowl
3. add 1 cup boiling water and stir to smooth
4. season with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: This is really good. My older kids seem to like it. I will be making this for gifts for our family and friends. I like that fact that is something that the kids can fix for themselves if they need a snack or quick meal.  My husband finally tried and loves it.  I now keep a gallon jar of it on hand.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic buttermilk waffles

rich and delicious, easy and satisfying; my favourite waffle recipe. no sugar, but you don't really miss it, especially when drizzled with syrup! and yes, one *tablespoon* of baking powder is correct! cook time is per waffle in my iron. from the cookbook 

1. sift together the dry ingredients
2. add the buttermilk , eggs and melted butter , mixing until there are no more lumps
3. this will make a very thick batter
4. bake in a waffle iron according to the manufacturer's directions
demonstrations.review: I ended up making 3 batches of these. My kids just kept eating them.  I did thin the batter down with a little bit more buttermilk so the batter would fill the waffle iron.  I also make extra for the freezer.  This will more than likely be our first choice for waffles.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pickled garlic

this is my dad's recipe.  they can be eaten right out of the jar, but they also work well in many recipes.

1. bring vinegar , water and spices to a boil
2. add garlic and bring back to a boil
3. pour into clean , sterilized jars
4. seal tight and store in cool place
5. keep sealed for 3 weeks before using to get best flavor
6. separating garlic into cloves and soaking them for 2 or 3 hours makes the outer skin easier to remove
demonstrations.review: My son and I love this.  My hubby doesn't like me eating them right before bed though.  I found peeled garlic at my grocery store so it makes the process alot easier. These would be good in a viniagrette but I love them straight out of the jar.  The hardest part is waiting 3 weeks to try them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
julie s extra special holiday chex mix

my mix is based on a recipe that my childhood best friend's mother, mrs. harper, had for chex mix. it became an annual ritual for me to call her to ask for the recipe yet again. :) this mix is so very, very yummy and decadent! good thing i only make it once a year...

1. fry up the bacon until it's nice and crisp
2. it depends on the bacon you use
3. then place the cooked bacon in a container and reserve it for another use- it's the leftover drippings you're after !
4. pre-heat the oven to 250 degrees f
5. melt the butter and bacon drippings together in a saucepan , then stir in the seasonings to make a nice , buttery mix
6. in a very large bowl , combine the mix ingredients
7. gradually stir in the buttery seasoning mix until the dry mix is evenly coated
8. spread on cookie sheets and bake for 1 hour , turning every 15 minutes
9. spread on paper towels to cool
10. store in airtight container
11. makes about 14 cups chex mix snack
demonstrations.review: Oh my goodness this is really good.  I made a double batch for us to take on vacation.  We had both bag finished by the second day.  I've made it couple more times since.  This is the best chex mix I've ever had.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
alice s zucchini cheese casserole

your neighbor just brought you a sack of zucchini and you need help with how to cook them into something good your family will enjoy. you won't be sorry with this easy to put together casserole. this is just one of my many zucchini recipes. this is from aunt alice in oklahoma in the 1970's.

1. saute zucchini , onion , and garlic in meltedbutter in a large skillet 5 minutes or until vegetables are crisp tender
2. remove skillet from heat
3. sprnkle flour and salt over sauteed vegetables , tossing gently to combine
4. stir in evaporated milk , sour cream and cheese
5. spoon zucchini mixture into a 1-quart casserole
6. bake at 350 degrees for 30 to 35 minutes or until cheese melts and mixture is hot and bubbly
7. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Our family (and we have a couple of self proclaimed zucchini haters) loved this. This is my first go to when the zucchine plants are producing more than we can eat. I often print out this recipe and put in the bags of zucchini I take to the neighbors.

target.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
target.review: I was having a dinner guest last night.  I wanted to make something new, so I chose this recipe.  It was so yummy!  I used nacho cheese soup instead of cream of mushroom.  I added a can of petite diced tomatoes to the meat mixture and 4 shakes of hot sauce.  We added black olives to the top.  My daughter who is 10, is learning to cook, and she assembled this dish for me, and thought it was quite fun.  We served it with a side salad and Mexican rice.  Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
saucy bacon roll ups

these are very easy to make for a buffett or appetizer party. i usually double this, because they go fast!  note:  the last time i made these, i fried the bacon after i cut it into thirds until it was almost done, cooled slightly on paper towels then wrapped around the water chestnuts and secured with toothpicks.  the sauce was a lot less greasy.  i cooked for about 5 minutes less.  enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. seperate bacon into slices
3. cut each slice in thirds
4. wrap each cut slice of bacon around a water chestnut
5. secure with a toothpick
6. place in a baking dish
7. in a bowl combine chili sauce , mayonnaise , and brown sugar
8. pour sauce over bacon roll ups and bake in the preheated oven for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I love this appetizer and have made it many times.  I always make a double or triple batch when I take them to a party. I usually make them and put them in the crock pot to stay warm, even though they are usually gone quickly!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vidalia onion bake

i had this at a friends house this week and had to have the recipe! it is so good! she made it with pam butter flavored spray instead of the butter and it was still fabulous!

1. slightly hollow out each onion
2. arrange onions in small baking dish
3. place 1 bouillon cube in each onion , top with butter and 1 tsp brown sugar
4. bake at 350 for 30 minutes
5. these can also be made on the grill
6. just double wrap in aluminum foil and grill until tender
demonstrations.review: Fantastic!  This is now my new favorite food to grill.  I omitted the brown sugar, and substituted a little garlic, just because I don't like sweet foods.  I grilled with marinated pork chops.  Next time, I will try this when I grill steak and corn-on-the-cob.  Thanks for the great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chicken thighs

i came across this recipe when i was looking for something easy using the ingredients i had on hand. prep time includes marinating

1. combine all ingredients in a large pot
2. cover and marinate for 1-3 hours
3. bring to a boil , then lower heat
4. cover and let simmer for 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
5. uncover and simmer until sauce is reduced and thickened and chicken is tender , about 20 more minutes
6. serve with rice
demonstrations.review: Delicious! Very easy to make.  I marinated my chicken for 6 hours.  As another reviewer suggeted, I turned the heat up pretty high for the last few minutes to thicken the sauce.  I served it over rice.  Next time, I'll add some Oriental veggies to the rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bow ties with sausage  tomato  and cream

a very easy pasta dish for busy evenings. i like it served with crusty bread (to dip in the sauce) and a tossed salad. i have even doubled the recipe and served it to guest on a casual evening.

1. bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil
2. cook pasta in boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes , or until al dente
3. drain
4. heat oil in a large , deep skillet over medium heat
5. cook sausage and pepper flakes until sausage is heated and browning around the edges
6. stir in onion and garlic , and cook until onion is tender
7. stir in tomatoes , cream , and salt
8. simmer until mixture thickens , 8 to 10 minutes
9. stir cooked pasta into sauce , and heat through
10. sprinkle with parsley
demonstrations.review: Great dish.  Even my picky 10-year-old DD loved it.  Didn't have red pepper flakes, so used some Cajun spice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country white bread or dinner rolls  bread machine

we think this is the best white bread recipe ever! it is a tender bread with a slightly sweet taste. my dinner rolls using this dough are so good, everyone always loves them. it doesn't take to long to make them when the bread maker does most of the work. the cook time is listed for the rolls only because everyone's bread makers cooks at different rates. mine is older and a regular loaf will take 4 hours and 10 minutes. i have found that 15 balls of dough fit perfectly in the 9x13 pan with sides touching after raising the 2nd time but they can be made whatever size you want. i hope you enjoy this great bread as much as we do.

1. in bread machine pan , place all ingredients from flour through yeast in order as recommended by the manufacturer
2. select the basic bread setting
3. check dough after 5 minutes of mixing , if needed add 1-2t of water or flour
4. bake as normal
5. for dinner rolls
6. mix in bread machine but use only the dough option
7. lightly grease a 9 x 13 baking pan
8. when dough is finished shape into 15 uniformly sized balls
9. i always grease my hands with shortening to smooth the dough out and it helps keep the dough from drying out
10. cover and let the rolls rise in a warm , draft free place until risen to the desired size
11. i let them about double in size
12. bake in a 350 oven about 12-15 minutes until golden brown
13. after removing from the oven , brush the tops of the rolls with melted butter
14. take out of pan and let completely cool before storing
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe.  Like others have stated, it rose to the top of my bread machine and was pushing the lid open!  Next time, I will sub some wheat flour in for the white, just for a change.  Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
tacos de pescado  baja style fish taco

this is a great fish dish that even my fish hater of a husband likes. posted for zaar world tour 05

1. pat the fish filet strips dry with paper towels
2. mix the flour , salt , pepper , vegetable oil and egg yolks to form a batter
3. beat the egg whites until stiff , and fold into the mixture
4. in a large skillet , heat oil with a depth of no more than 1 inch
5. dip each fish strip in the batter , fry quickly on one side , turning to fry the other until golden brown
6. this should only take a couple of minutes on each side
7. drain on paper towels
8. arrange pieces of fish in softened tortillas and serve at once , accompanied by the shredded cabbage , marinated onions , guacamole sauce , and a selection of salsas
target.review:
OMG do I love these! I have been making them this way for years, very tasty!
Tip, for a to die for sauce, try mango salsa...........WOW!
Good Post!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry bites

my dad is responsible for this recipe. he would make these for me as after-school snacks and now i make them for after-work snacks!they're just simple and good!

1. roll bread flat with rolling pin
2. mix the next 3 ingredients together and put about 2-3 tablespoons of mixture onto the bread
3. fold the bread into a square and press around edges to hold together
4. brush the butter around the edges
5. bake at 400 degrees about 5 minutes each side
demonstrations.review: These were not what I had hoped for. I would almost bet that with less cream cheese, some sugar and a touch of cinnamon on top it might be a lot better. I liked the idea, cream cheese with fruit is an all time hit around my house, but this just was not a hit.  Any suggestions? SORRY!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ukrainian lokshyna and ham  noodle and ham casserole

any leftover meat or mushrooms may be used in this dish.

1. cook the noodles as directed in the recipe for ukrainian lokshyna
2. mix the drained noodles with the melted butter
3. mix in the ham and cheese
4. combine the egg , cream , and salt , and add to the mixture
5. if the ham is very salty , reduce the salt or omit it
6. spoon into a buttered baking dish and top with the buttered bread crumbs
7. bake in a moderate oven for about 45 minutes , or until done
demonstrations.review:
I made this with leftover x-mas ham (I ground it in the food processor)
WOW! I thought I died and went to Heaven!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade deep dish sausage pizza

this came out of quick cooking magazine. it is delicious. it is new to our family but will be a much repeated recipe. kids love it too. :)

1. on a lightly floured surface , roll and stretch dough into a 9 inch circle
2. cover with plastic wrap
3. let rest for 10 minutes
4. roll and stretch the dough into a 12 in circle
5. sprinkle corn meal into a greased 9 inch springform pan
6. place dough in pan and press 1 inch up the sides of pan
7. spread pizza sauce over crust
8. top with sausage , 1 cup cheese , oregano and green pepper
9. sprinkle with remaining cheese
10. bake at 425 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until crust is golden brown
11. remove to a wire rack
12. let stand for 5 minutes before removing sides of pan
demonstrations.review: This has become my standard "I am too lazy to cook" meal. I love how the cornmeal gives the crust a nice nutty crunch. This recipe is so flexible! I have used pepperoni, sausage, hamburger..I even once used SteakUms from the freezer section with onions, mushrooms and peppers for a Philly Cheesteak Pizza!! WOW!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tastes like apple pie apple squares

from my favourite church cookbook, where all the recipes are tried and true!  **like most of the reviews state, if you don't want to fight with the pastry to make it fit a cookie sheet - make 1.5x the dough recipe or use a smaller pan.

1. mix flour and salt and cut in shortening
2. add egg and milk mixture and mix till it forms a ball
3. divide dough in half
4. roll first half in 17 x 12 inch rectangle
5. place in cookie sheet and bring pastry up sides
6. cover pastry with apples and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon
7. roll out second half of dough and place on top of apples
8. moisten edges with milk and pinch together
9. beat egg white until stiff and brush on crust
10. bake at 400f for 1 hour
11. mix glaze ingredients together and brush on crust
12. this square freezes beautifully
demonstrations.review: I took Chef Trumpies hint and made extra dough, this was very good! Great treat for those who LOVE apple pie (ME!). I had a few extra apples so I used a little more than the recipe called for, it worked fine. I served these cut up on a platter with pieces of cheddar cheese and it made a lovely presentation as well as a great snack. My son enjoyed this too, which was a surprise because he wanted no part of apple pie at Christmas. I think this appealed more to him because it was "finger food". That is fine with me because these do not have too much sugar. I think it would be very interesting to mix up the fruit a bit, try pears, raisens ect. THANK YOU SOOOOOO MUCH!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stroganoff

this recipe was used by both my mother and my mother-in-law. it's been a favorite of our families for years, and is both easy and delicious.

1. brown beef in large skillet
2. add onions and cook until onions are translucent
3. drain grease
4. stir in condensed soup , then garlic powder , salt , and pepper
5. allow to simmer until all other parts of meal are prepared
6. minutes before it's time to serve , stir in the sour cream completely and heat through
7. serve over egg noodles
demonstrations.review:
Easy enough, though as listed it is very bland. But to be fair I gave it a second run with the following adjustments.
