1. heat one tablespoon of the butter and one tablespoon of the oil over medium and add both types of onion and a little salt and freshly ground black pepper
2. cook , stirring , until crispy and brown , about 15 minutes , then set aside
3. mash together the remaining 2 tablespoons butter , the cheese and mustard and set aside
4. rub the steaks with salt and pepper
5. heat the remaining 1 teaspoon olive oil in a medium cast-iron skillet over high heat
6. when very hot , add both the steaks and cook without disturbing for 2 minutes
7. flip and brown the other side for 2 more minutes- this will give you medium doneness but still pink meat
8. place the steaks onto the roll bottoms , top each with half the butter mixture and then smother with onions
9. top with the roll tops and eat with ice cold , alcoholic beverages on a friday evening
target.review:
Really really good! 
The changes I made were to leave the dijon out of the gorgonzola butter. Instead I mixed it with an equal amount of sour cream, slathered onto toasted roll topped with shredded romaine. The crispy fried onions are fantastic :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
guinness and filet mignon chili

if you're not watching your sodium intake, use regular instead of low-sodium ingredients. this recipe is based on chili served at gallagher'ss steak house, 228 west 52nd street, new york city, with just a couple of very minor alterations.

1. heat up cup of the butter in a large sauce pot over medium high heat until very hot
2. add diced filet and cook until seared and browned around the edges
3. add ground beef and cook until all of the beef is browned thoroughly
4. remove the meat and set aside , draining off of the fat
5. add the diced onions and chile pepper to the pot and cook until soft , about 3 minutes
6. add the meat back to the pot
7. add the guinness and let boil for 1 minute
8. add the flour and stir constantly for 1 minute
9. add the crushed tomatoes , tomato paste and the beef stock and stir thoroughly
10. reduce the heat to a low simmer and add both of the beans , the chili powder , cumin , salt , white pepper and brown sugar
11. let the chili simmer for 30 minutes , uncovered , stirring occasionally
12. finish by stirring in cup more of the butter and the shredded cheddar cheese
13. garnish or serve with any of the following: sour cream , diced red onions and pepper , shredded cheddar cheese , diced tomatoes , fresh chopped cilantro
demonstrations.review: The BEST chili I have ever tasted!  The only change I made was to halve the recipe...Big Mistake!  The next day everyone fought over the leftovers and there wasn't enough to go around.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christmas chocolate cherry cookies

this is a great recipe for a christmas cookie. i make it every year for the family. my kids like the chocolate chips while the grownups prefer the maraschino cherries and coconut.

1. cream shortening and sugar in large bowl with electric mixer until well blended
2. add eggs and almond extract , beating on medium speed until light and fluffy
3. about 2 minutes
4. combine flour , baking powder and salt
5. add to creamed mixture gradually , beating on low speed just until blended
6. fold in chips , coconut and cherries
7. drop dough by spoonfuls onto greased cookie sheets
8. bake at 350 for 12-15 minutes or until lightly browned around edges
demonstrations.review: mmmm...Tasty and Really Pretty too! I left out the coconut and they still turned out great. Thanks villagemom.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of applebee s oriental chicken salad by todd wilbur

this recipe is from www.topsecretrecipes.com. this actually tastes like the salad from applebees. it is a bit of work, but worth every second!!

1. preheat oil in deep fryer or deep pan over medium heat
2. you want the temperature of the oil to be around 350 degrees
3. blend together all ingredients for dressing in a small bowl with an electric mixer
4. put dressing in refrigerator to chill while you prepare the salad
5. in a small , shallow bowl beat egg , add milk , and mix well
6. in another bowl , combine flour with corn flake crumbs , salt and pepper
7. cut chicken breast into 4 or 5 long strips
8. dip each strip of chicken first into egg mixture then into the flour mixture , coating each piece completely
9. fry each chicken finger for 5 minutes or until coating has darkened to brown
10. prepare salad by tossing the chopped romaine with the chopped red cabbage , napa cabbage , and carrots
11. sprinkle sliced green onion on top of the lettuce
12. sprinkle almonds over the salad , then the chow mein noodles
13. cut the chicken into small bite-size chunks
14. place the chicken onto the salad forming a pile in the middle
15. serve with salad dressing drizzled over it or on the side
demonstrations.review: We like this recipe BETTER than Applebees! If you are in a hurry, try using cut-up chicken tenders from your grocer's deli and packaged cole slaw mix from the produce dept. Or, hit KFC drive thru and pick up some popcorn chicken to throw on top. Mmmmmm!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
andes chocolate mint cookies

nan

1. heat oven to 350f
2. over low heat , combine butter , sugar and water
3. heat until melted and add chocolate chips until partly melted
4. remove from heat and stir
5. pour into large mixing bowl
6. let stand 10 minutes to cool slightly
7. beat in eggs one at a time on high speed
8. reduce mixer to low speed and add flour , salt and baking soda
9. beat until well-blended
10. chill one hour
11. roll into balls , place two inches apart on parchment paper-lined baking sheets
12. bake for 10 minutes
13. place an andes mint half on top
14. allow to melt slightly and spread with a spoon
demonstrations.review: mmm...minty! Added 1/2 tsp. pure peppermint extract to the melted butter/chocolate mixture. Rolled into 43 golf ball sized cookies and slightly underbaked, just eight minutes.. finally topped with a whole andes mint, used a toothpick to spread melted candy. Yummy :)  Thank you recipenut!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible peanut butter cookies

these are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!

1. mix peanut butter , sugar , and egg together until smooth
2. drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart
3. if desired , roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet
4. press with fork
5. press again in opposite direction
6. bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
7. do not brown
8. do not over bake
demonstrations.review:
Great recipe. 
 When they first came out of the oven, I was dissapointed...   they tasted like a spoonful of dough. 
After setting up for a few hours they were perfect! I topped them with a broken hershey bar while still warm.
Addictive :)

target.recipe_text:
chicken breasts with rosemary

this is so easy to make and can be served over pasta, rice, etc.

1. pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt& pepper
2. dip chicken in flour and shake of excess
3. heat butter and cook chicken 4-6 minutes per side or until no longer pink in the center and lightly browned
4. remove from pan
5. discard any fat from the pan
6. return pan to heat
7. add chicken stock and rosemary
8. cook 2 minutes
9. add cream and mustard
10. bring to a boil
11. cook 4-5 minutes until slightly thickened
12. season to taste with salt and pepper
13. return chicken to pan
14. coat with sauce and heat thoroughly
target.review: I made these last night.  I had to cook my chicken breasts a little longer because they were really thick and I also added about 1 tbsp more of butter.  It was great!  My husband LOVED it and said it was a keeper!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple or pear cake

absolutely the most delicious, moist cake ever with a decadent topping. very simple to make, my family just loves this!

1. cake:
2. mix all cake ingredients by hand in order given
3. pour in a greased 9 x 13 inch pan or springform pan
4. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes and remove
5. topping:
6. in saucepan mix all ingredients and bring to a slow boil for 3 minutes
7. pour over cake and return to oven for 4 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this cake yesterday.  We did not care for it at all.  I followed everything like the recipe said and it came out very dry.  Everyone else was saying how moist this cake is and mine was very dry.  I don't know what went wrong.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kale with caramelized onions and garlic

a quick and simple side dish made with an amazing vegetable.

1. heat oil in large pan
2. add chopped onions and garlic
3. saut until onions are clear and begin to caramelize
4. stir often
5. do not allow garlic to burn
6. add torn kale
7. toss with onions and garlic
8. cook until kale is wilted
9. sprinkle with a tiny bit of balsamic vinegar if desired
demonstrations.review: I made this last night.  It was quick and easy and tasted great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter in my chocolate no bake cookies

kids love these and you can whip them up in less than 10 minutes. they are a cross between a cookie and a candy.

1. stir sugar , cocoa , margarine and milk together in saucepan
2. bring to a boil and boil for 1 minute , stirring frequently
3. remove from heat
4. stir in vanilla , peanut butter and oats
5. drop by teaspoonfuls on waxed paper
6. should be kept refrigerated
demonstrations.review: Loved it!!  It was really easy to make and my DH loved them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french potatoes

this is a no-fuss microwave potato dish that really makes a hit. i serve it for special occasions, as well as any old time. it's from the book microwave cooking by beverley piper.

1. put the potato slices to soak in cold water
2. put the onion rings into a bowl
3. cover with plastic wrap , and pierce
4. microwave on high for 1 minute
5. grease a five cup casserole dish with a little of the butter
6. layer the drained potatoes and onions in the dish , starting and finishing with the potatoes
7. season each layer with salt and pepper
8. pour the milk over the potatoes and dot with the rest of the butter
9. sprinkle the top with paprika
10. cover with plastic wrap , and pierce
11. microwave on high for 13 minutes
12. rotate half-way through cooking time
13. allow to stand , covered , for 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Great recipe.  Simple and tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
canadian living s best chocolate chip cookies

these truly are the best chocolate chip cookies that i've ever made. the  chilling instructions before baking and the standing afterwards are very  important steps. the texture turns out perfect.

1. in a large bowl , cream together butter and shortening
2. gradually mix in sugars , creaming thoroughly
3. beat in eggs and vanilla
4. combine flour , baking soda and salt
5. blend into creamed mixture
6. stir in chocolate chips and nuts
7. chill for a few minutes or let stand at cool room temperature for 30 minutes
8. drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto lightly greased baking sheets
9. flatten slightly and smooth edges to make 1 / 2-inch thick cookie
10. bake in a 375f oven for 8-9 minutes or until golden brown around the edges and still slightly under-baked in the centre
11. let stand on baking sheet for 5 minutes
12. remove to racks to let cool completely
demonstrations.review: These cookies tasted wonderful.  I don't know what I did wrong but mine came out really crunchy (overcooked) at 375 for 8 minutes.  Next time I will probably reduce the temp to 350F.

target.recipe_text:
whole wheat bread machine bread

a great every-day bread, good for toast and sandwiches. i have dark, coated metal pans, so i bake it at 350. this came from a great frugality blog called wanting what you have. the author recommends putting the dry ingredients in a ziploc (in reverse order), then storing several batches in the freezer, to streamline the process.
prep time includes dough cycle on my bread machine and rising time.

1. place ingredients in your bread machine hopper in the order listed
2. make a small well to rest the yeast inches
3. coat a loaf pan with cooking spray and set aside
4. place hopper in the machine and select the dough cycle for a 1
5. 5 lb loaf
6. when the cycle has completed , turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface shape the dough into a uniform loaf
7. place the dough into the prepared bread pan
8. cover with a damp towel and let rise to double it's size
9. preheat your oven to 375 degrees
10. bake the bread for 30-40 minutes , until the crust is browned and makes a hollow sound when tapped
11. allow to cool before slicing
target.review: Bread was good. But there are better recipes on here for a everyday bread.  I really like breads wth flax and bran added. Thank you so much for posting the blog address! I have really enjoying it! I'm going to use lots of her ideas! livingonadime.com is also a good site!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dad s homemade chocolate pudding

my dad used to make this for us when i was little..if you are a chocolate lover you will love this...it's even good on a piece of bread..really!!

1. -combine all dry ingredients until all lumps are gone and blended well
2. -add milk and place on burner turned to high -- stir constantly until desired thickness
3. -remove from heat and add vanilla , stir well and serve
4. enjoy
demonstrations.review: Very, very good! 5 stars from my hubby, kids, and ME! My youngest daughter and I are the chocolate lovers of the family. We really enjoyed it. My husband thinks it tastes really rich. He described it as having frosting like richness to it. He was suprised to find out it was lowfat. Thanks for sharing this!!!! We will be making his often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really easy  really good french bread

a dear friend gave me this recipe, swearing that it is too easy to mess up- and she was right!  it was delicous, better than anything fresh from the bakery!

1. dissolve yeast , warm water , and sugar in a small bowl
2. in a large bowl or stand mixer , combine hot water , granulated sugar , salt , and oil
3. add 1 1 / 2 cups of flour to the mixture in the large bowl / mixer and mix well
4. stir in yeast mixture
5. add 1 1 1 / 2 cups more flour and mix until well blended
6. leave in bowl and let rise for 1 hour , mixing a few strokes a couple of times during the hour
7. divide dough into 2 pieces
8. roll out each piece on a floured surface into the length desired then roll up length wise like a jelly roll
9. put on a greased cookie sheet , sealed side down , and tuck the ends under
10. slash the top diagonally across the top every couple of inches with a sharp knife
11. brush with egg white
12. preheat oven to 400 degrees fahrenheit
13. let loaves rise 30 more minutes
14. bake for 25 - 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good! So much better than store bought! Will be using this a lot! Thanks for the recipe and thank your dear friend too!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ramen noodle egg foo yung

i can't believe i like this dish as much as i do. i was surprised. this is a variation of a rather bland scrambled egg mix that i found on the net but turning it onto an egg foo yung is really special.  add your own favorite things but this is a good start. if you add water chestnuts, ham, shrimp, pork, whatever- then you will have to adjust the cooking time. this is a basic recipe-  make it your own. but an easy recipe to amend- as soon as the egg is set- then it is done! i really love this and it is so good for a family on a budget or a bachelor short on time. if you want a terrific egg foo yung sauce then try this one recipe#45270 .

1. cook ramen noodles according to package instructions for 3 minutes blah blah and drain well in a colander
2. if you don't know how to cook ramen noodles you are too stupid to cook
3. call dominos and have them deliver you a pizza
4. whisk eggs , onions , the seasoning packet , sesame oil , soy sauce , and baking powder with a fork in a small bowl and toss in the cooked ramen noodles
5. heat butter on med high heat in an 8 inch nonstick skillet
6. throw the ramen noodle / egg mixture in the skillet and cook it
7. i reiterate if you don't know to to cook ramen noodles call dominos because you are obviously , stupid
8. :(
9. flip the patty over and cook the other side until the egg is set , about two more minutes
10. flip over again and cook about 1 minute more
11. serve with soy sauce if you wish or an egg foo yung sauce
demonstrations.review: Great recipe. I lowered the butter and subbed smart balance.  Will be using this often! Thanks!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ultimate pizza sauce

this pizza sauce recipe was given to me as a wedding present, written on the inside cover of a pizza cookbook. it is thick, saucy, spicy and delicious. i'll never use anything else on my homemade pizzas. i like to double or triple it and put it in ziploc bags in my freezer.

1. in a large skillet , melt butter with the oil
2. add the onion , celery and garlic and saute until soft and transparent
3. add tomato sauce and tomato paste and stir until smooth
4. add remaining ingredients and bring to slow simmer
5. simmer for 30-60 minutes
6. remove the bay leaf and spread the sauce on your prepared pizza dough
demonstrations.review: SO VERY GOOD!!! I have made this so many times now. My family loves pizza so I make it about once a week. But I make this awesome Sauce once a month. I usually triple it and freeze it in dinner portions. Costco has a great deal on a huge can of tomato sauce. Also, I add ground flaxseed too it. And I have never used the bay leaf it calls for. Like some of the other reviewers, I also grind all the spices together (magic bullet works great). For the dough I use recipe #251840. This is a very budget friendly meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate angel food cupcakes

once they taste these cupcakes, no one will believe that they are low in calories. less than 50 calories a serving!
adopted from the recipezaar account.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. in small saucepan , stir cocoa and 1 / 3 cup water over low heat about 1 minute until mixture thickens and just begins to boil
3. remove from heat and stir in vanilla
4. in large bowl , with electric mixer at high speed , beat egg whites and salt until soft peaks from when beaters are lifted
5. add sugar , 1 tbsp at a time , beating well after each addition until stiff peaks form when beaters are lifted
6. quickly add cocoa mixture and beat 20 seconds until just blended
7. in a small bowl , combine flour and baking powder
8. fold into egg white mixture , one fourth at a time
9. spray 12 regular muffin cups with vegetable cooking spray
10. divide batter evenly between muffin cups
11. bake 10-15 minutes until cupcakes begin to pull away from sides of pan
12. remove from oven and cool on wire rack for 10 minutes
13. run a knife around edge of cupcakes to loosen
14. remove cupcakes and cool on wire rack
15. invert onto serving plate
16. garnish each with a little whipped cream and a strawberry , if desired
demonstrations.review: Quite tasty. I used ww pastry flour and regular unsweetened cocoa. And I doubled the recipe. Sure glad I did...they went very fast. Mine didn't fall. We topped them with a light vanilla frosting. It did increase the calories a bit but still each treat ended up being under 100 calories! Will make again!

target.recipe_text:
cola ribs

i know there are a bazillion recipes for ribs available, but my husband is never satisfied unless i make these. serve with lotsa napkins!

1. in a small bowl , combine soy sauce , brown sugar , garlic , worcestershire sauce and black pepper
2. rub mixture onto rib pieces
3. layer ribs and onions in a dutch oven and pour cola over all
4. cover and bake at 250f for 4 hours
5. remove pan from oven and pour off cola juices
6. add bbq sauce , cover and return to oven for 1 hour more
target.review: Great!!! I used KC Masterpiece BBQ sauce that had a smoke flavor. Tasted like they might have been prepared over a hickory wood camp fire.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy sausage penne

this luscious pasta dish is one i've avoided making recently; it's not exactly a lowfat dinner and i feel guilty serving it to my husband -- neither of us should be eating such a high calorie meal. but it's so, so good! even though i can't claim it's part of a healthy diet, i hope you try it at least once -- it's a fast, easy dish, after all! i serve this with a simple green salad.

1. bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook the penne until al dente
2. drain well and do not rinse
3. after you put the water on to boil , remove sausage meat from the casings , crumble , and set aside
4. in a large skillet , heat olive oil over medium-high heat
5. add garlic and cayenne and saute for approximately 30 seconds , then add sausage meat to skillet
6. cook until sausage meat is no longer pink
7. add cream , salt , pepper and nutmeg to skillet and turn heat to high to bring mixture to a boil
8. reduce heat and simmer , gently , until the cream reduces and the sauce thickens a bit
9. it takes about 10 minutes
10. place cooked penne in a large serving bowl and pour sauce over
11. add butter and cheese to bowl and combine all well
12. taste
13. add more salt and / or pepper if you wish
14. sprinkle chopped herbs over top and serve
demonstrations.review: Very good!My son & I enjoyed this by itself, Need suggestions for side dishes & deserts. Would like to serve to dinner guests.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
world s best butter cookies

i tested 8 different butter cookie recipes, looking for the "perfect" butter cookie. it had to be buttery, a little crumbly (like shortbread), and not too sweet. this is the winner. i think these are the worlds best butter cookie, courtesy of chef alice medrich.

1. beat the butter , sugar , salt and vanilla together until smooth and creamy
2. mix in the egg yolk until well incorporated , scraping down the sides of the bowl at least once
3. add the flour and mix just until incorporated
4. scrape onto a lightly floured board and knead a few times , just until the dough smooths out
5. turn onto a sheet of plastic wrap and roll into a log , wrap up and refrigerate for several hours or freeze
6. before baking , preheat the oven to 325f
7. line your baking sheets with parchment
8. slice the dough into slices about 1 / 8" thick and place them on the sheets about an inch apart
9. bake until just beginning to turn golden around the edges , about 16-18 minutes
10. you could roll the dough out and cut shapes
11. you could slice them even thinner and sandwich them with chocolate or jam or lemon curd
12. you could make them and then dip them half into chocolate
13. you could just make them and eat them , which is my favorite
14. whatever you do , they will be delicious
demonstrations.review: If I could give this recipe a 10 I would!! Beautiful to look at & a wonderful texture. The taste is delicious.Easy to prepare. My son had asked for butter cookies from the grocers & I forgot them. It was ok to forget this time, nothing I could have bought could have been as good. I think this will make good cookies for my grandson to paint.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern grits

hubby says these grits are fit for a southern tea room. no higher compliment than that! it is not a mistake to use quick cooking grits, and cook them for almost half an hour. these grits have body!

1. in a small pot , bring water , milk , and salt to a boil
2. slowly stir grits into boiling mixture
3. stir continuously and thoroughly until grits are well mixed
4. let the pot return to a boil , cover pot with a lid , lower the temperature , and cook for approximately 30 minutes stirring frequently
5. add more water if necessary
6. grits are done when they have the consistency of stiff cream of wheat
7. stir in butter
8. serve with additional butter on top of each portion , or serve with fruit or with a savory meal
demonstrations.review: My family enjoys grits with fried crumbled sausage or crumbled bacon, and topped with shredded cheddar cheese. Good for breakfast or a quick supper on a cold night.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gizzards and noodles

we grew up on 

1. rinse and cut in half each gizzard
2. simmer in water and 2 tsp salt for about 3 hours or until very tender
3. cook noodles until done , drain and add gizzards , butter and salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: When my sons were little guys and with only one income I prepared "cheap food". My boys called this dish Lizard Stew. Even today as grown men they talk about Mamas delicious Lizard Stew. If available, I added chopped celery and a boullion cube to make it more flavorful. Sue

demonstrations.recipe_text:
little dixie pound cake

a tiny pound cake made in a mini-loaf pan, perfect for just the two of you (or just the one of you with the need for pound cake! ;o) also great for gift baskets or dinners for shut-ins. from toh.

1. cream butter and sugar together
2. beat in egg
3. combine flour and baking soda
4. alternately add flour mixture and buttermilk to creamed mixture
5. add extracts
6. pour into greased 5-3 / 4" x 3" x 2" loaf pan
7. bake at 350f for 35 min or until tester comes out clean
8. cool for 10 min , remove to wire rack and cool
demonstrations.review: Very easy,very tastey. Quick to make. I mixed it in a 2 cup measuring cup.Only a few utensils to clean up.

target.recipe_text:
buttery farm biscuits

this is an easy never fail recipe. you don't even use a rolling pin! change it to suit the meal you are serving them with - add 2 tbsp parmesan cheese and a bit of basil & oregano, try 1 tsp grated orange peel, or just before baking sprinkle the top with cinnamon & sugar use your own imagination

1. combine flour , baking powder& salt
2. cut the butter into the flour using 2 knives or a pastry blender , keep cutting until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs
3. with a fork stir in the milk , very gently , until a soft dough forms
4. don't over mix
5. place the dough on a baking sheet and with floured hands press it into a 9" x 9" square
6. use a spatula or the dull side of a knife and cut the dough into 12 biscuits without actually cutting them apart
7. bake in 400f oven for about 15-20 minutes or until they are golden
8. transfer to a wire rack& cool for about 10 minutes
9. serve with homemade fruit jam or anything else that takes your fancy
target.review: These are very good. We had them 2 days in a row!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
5 minute fudge

my favorite is the butterscotch but i have done the chocolate, too and they both turn out great.

1. mix milk , sugar and salt in a heavy saucepan , over med-high heat
2. heat to boiling
3. cook 5 minutes , stirring constantly
4. remove from heat , and add other ingredients
5. stir until marshmallows are all melted
6. pour into buttered 9" square pan
7. cool and cut into squares
demonstrations.review: I used peanut butter chips. We loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple and mandarin orange dessert

i made this up myself to add fruit to my husband's diet. he is diabetic and this satisfy's his cravings for something sweet. even non-diabetics enjoy this. it is quick and you can add drained cherries for more flavor or color!

1. mix pudding mix and cool whip together well , fold in drained fruit
2. chill for 2-3 hours before serving
3. great for diabetics !
demonstrations.review: A very nice dessert. Not too heavy, with a good texture and flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato kielbasa skillet

a very hearty, tasty supper. this is very easy to make and a real pleaser.

1. in dutch oven , brown potatoes , kielbasa , onion and peppers in oil
2. add seasonings and water
3. bring to a boil
4. cover tightly and cook for 20 minutes on low , stirring occasionally
5. uncover and put cheese on top
6. simmer until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: This is total comfort food! This was a major hit with my husband, the cheese melted on top made it very good! Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fudge filled bars

i like to make these when i need something that travels well. very good! very easy!

1. mix oats , flour , brown sugar and salt
2. add butter and mix until crumbly
3. stir in pecans
4. set aside 1-1 / 2 cup for topping
5. press remaining into a greased 13x9 baking pan
6. in saucepan combine milk , chips and shortening
7. cook and stir over low heat until melted
8. spread over crust in pan
9. sprinkle with reserved topping
10. bake at 350f for 20-25 minutes , until edges golden are brown
demonstrations.review: We LOVED these!!! This recipe went into my favorites folder! Delicious, creamy and crunchy at the same time. Very easy, thanks for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate strawberry shortcake

the perfect summer dessert. not your ordinary strawberry shortcake!

1. wash , stem , and cut strawberries in half
2. add sugar
3. toss to mix well
4. chill
5. beat cream cheese and powdered sugar well
6. fold in whipped topping and cake cubes
7. spread cake into an ungreased 13x9 dish
8. cover and chill for at least 2 hours
9. cut cake into squares
10. top with strawberries
demonstrations.review: This rocks!! It was a major success, everybody loved it! Thanks for recipe!!!

target.recipe_text:
bombay kidney beans

a can of beans, a can of tomatoes, some indian-style seasoning, serve over rice, and you've got yourself a quick and healthy vegetarian meal. use the higher amount of spices if you like your food a bit spicier. adapted from the vegetarian gourmet's easy low-fat favorites.

1. combine beans , tomatoes , honey and seasonings in a medium saucepan
2. bring to a boil , stirring occasionally
3. reduce heat , cover , and simmer 10 minutes
4. in a small bowl , stir together cornstarch and water so that cornstarch dissolves
5. add to saucepan
6. cook 2-3 minutes , stirring constantly , until slighly thickened
7. serve over rice
target.review: Excellent! I added the following private note to my saved copy:<br/><br/>1) Sautee 1 chopped onion and several cloves of minced garlic with spices before adding beans and tomatoes<br><br/>2) Double the rice and beans<br><br/>3) Triple spices and salt to taste<br><br/>4) Add 1/2 tsp of cayenne<br><br/>5) Reduce honey<br><br/>6) Add kale or other greens during the 10-minute simmer<br><br/>7) Dissolve 1/2 vegan bouillon cube AND a tsp of arrowroot in 1/2 C hot water and add it to the pot with the greens<br>

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage sausage supper

this is a very good and hearty old-fashioned dish that i think came from taste of home. it's almost like a stew or even a soup. i have tried it with keilbasa but it wasn't as good. i like to serve it with rye bread.

1. in a dutch oven or soup kettle , cook sausage and onion over medium heat until sausage is lightly browned and onion is tender
2. drain
3. add the cabbage and water
4. cover and cook on low for 10 minutes
5. stir in carrots and potatoes
6. cover and cook for 25 to 30 minutes or until vegetables are tender
demonstrations.review: The smoked sausage sounded so good, but I only had uncooked Italian chicken sausage. So I cooked that up with the onion and a little bit of Liquid Smoke. Instead of potatoes (we avoid them because of their glycemic index) I added sliced, unpealed sunchokes (Jerusalem artichokes). I also added a few de-ribbed and chopped collard greens because I didn't have a full head of cabbage, a chopped apple, and a Creole seasoning blend. I don't like overcooked cabbage, so all the veggies went into the pot at the same time. Since there is no grain in this dish, I served it with slices of whole wheat bread. Excellent!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tofu jerky

this is a nice substitution for beef jerky, as it provides the saltiness and smoky flavor (it has been a long time since i've had real beef jerky, though, so i may not be the best judge).  the texture will not be the same, of course, but it is chewy and satisfying. enjoy!

1. cut the cube of tofu horizontally into four pieces , and then slice it into strips
2. the strips should be about 4 millimeters in thickness
3. they're going to shrink a lot in the oven , so they should start out pretty thick
4. mix all the other ingredients together
5. arrange the tofu in a single layer in a shallow baking pan or cookie sheet and pour the marinade over it
6. let it soak for several hours or overnight
7. drain excess liquid and dry tofu in food dehydrator or 200 f oven
8. this will take 4 to 8 hours , depending on the weather
9. flip the tofu over hourly so it dries evenly
10. dry the jerky until it is very chewy , but not crispy
demonstrations.review: I made this with low sodium soy sauce and several people sampled it and liked it. I'll try regular soy sauce when I make it to take backpacking. I used a dehydrator for 7 hours at 195 F, and the texture came out nice -- not really chewy, but not crispy either. It made the house smell smoky for a couple days, but it's a pleasant smell. When I laid it out to dry, I made sure some of the marinade solids (garlic and pepper) was on each piece.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot millet salad

a fresh way to enjoy millet, which is very good for you, inexpensive and easy to cook. this recipe contains many different textures, which helps avoid that heavy, "healthy-tasting" kind of grains dish vegetarians know so well . . .

1. fry onion and garlic in oil until tender
2. add millet
3. cook three minutes , stirring well
4. add two cups of water , bring to a boil , then lower heat to medium-low and cook , covered , for 25 minutes
5. while millet cooks , chop other ingredients
6. when millet is finished cooking , turn off heat and add chopped ingredients to the pot
7. stir well
8. serve on two big plates and sqeeze lemon juice liberally on top
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I love millet, and this recipe is perfect! I make my own tamari almonds by toasting them on medium heat in a dry skillet, then adding tamari to the skillet when the nuts are hot. Use enough tamari to coat the nuts. Keep stirring while you're toasting and as you add the tamari because both will burn easily. When the tamari evaporates, dump the almonds out of the pan onto a plate to cool.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
persian kidney beans

this is for the bean lovers!

1. saute the chopped onion in oil
2. add the garlic , cumin and cinnamon
3. add the lime juice , then the tomato paste and the water
4. simmer for 5 minutes
5. add the beans and the chili pepper and simmer for another10 minutes
6. it's done when it's quite dry ,
7. serve stuffed into pita bread
demonstrations.review: With the only fresh veggies in the house being onions and mixed baby kales, I had to whip up something fast. I already had this recipe set aside as one I wanted to try. We include fresh greens in most meals, so I added a couple handfuls of the baby kale just after I added the canned beans. We also love spices, so I doubled the cumin and added two hefty shakes of cinnamon. I used a teaspoon of red pepper flakes instead of a fresh chili, and used nearly a whole bulb of chopped garlic. We ate it on corn tortillas since we didn't have any pitas. I think it would be excellent on cornbread. We'll definitely be eating this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
almond spice rice pudding from leftover rice

i just made up this recipe.  i had a lot of leftover jasmine rice, and decided to try an experiment.  my mom used to make rice pudding from leftovers all the time, but i added my own flavors for this one.  the quantities are approximate, and you can modify according to your taste or according to the amount of leftover rice you have.

1. put cooked rice , sugar , and milk in a saucepan
2. add extracts , cardamom , and flax
3. heat to just before boiling , or to an early boiling point , stirring constantly
4. remove from heat , cool , and serve
5. store remaining quantities in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: I didn't have flax seeds or almond extract, but I made this with coarse ground almonds, agave instead of sugar, nonfat milk, and raisins. It was easy, satisfying, and tasty!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
target.review: Had really high hopes but this was just okay. Gave the third star for ease of preparation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked pork chops and apples

i found this in a pamphlet from the orchard (about maryland apple orchards) a few years ago when we were picking apples. it is one of the tastiest things i have ever made!

1. peel , core , and slice the apples
2. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
3. melt the butter in a skillet
4. brown the pork chops on both sides in the butter
5. grease a large baking dish
6. put the apple slices in the bottom of the dish
7. mix the brown sugar and cinnamon
8. sprinkle the cinnamon and sugar over the apples
9. place the pork chops on top of the apples
10. cover with foil and bake for 1 and 1 / 2 hours
demonstrations.review:
This is a keeper! Made only minor changes.
I seasoned my pork chops with sage, onion powder, no salt seasoning and pepper. In place of the sugar I used splenda.
Both the apples and pork were tender enough to cut with a fork and the family raved about it well after dinner. I will be making this again. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy pizza pasta casserole  oamc

this is a kid pleaser-very cheesy and topped with pepperoni. it makes 2 large (9x13) casseroles or 4 small ones; i often divide it in fourths and freeze 3. this originally came from toh's quick cooking.

1. brown ground beef , onion , garlic and seasoning in oil
2. drain
3. while beef is browning , cook pasta according to the packaging
4. stir in pasta , spaghetti sauce and 3 cups cheese
5. place mixture in 2 greased 9x13x2 inch baking pans or 4 square pans
6. sprinkle with remaining mozzarella
7. top with pepperoni
8. cover and freeze up to 3 months
9. to cook now: bake uncovered at 350 degrees for 25-30 minutes , until heated through
10. to bake frozen casserole: thaw in refrigerator overnight and bake at 350 for 35-40 minutes , till hot
demonstrations.review: *I use recipes as a springboard for my own creativity*<br/>This one ROCKED! I used Italian sausage in place of the ground beef, wheat rotini, pizza seasoning, added fresh shredded spinach (how else would I get my kids to eat it), and canned mushrooms. OhMyGoodness! Had to force my family from the table as opposed to them running off. Can't wait to eat the one in the freezer. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot potato chowder

another of my aunt's recipes. great for those cold nights.

1. combine potatoes , onion , broth , and cream of chicken soup in crock pot
2. cover and cook on low 8-10 hours or until potatoes are tender
3. add cream cheese and blend
4. top with bacon and chives before serving
demonstrations.review: Following some of the reviewers suggestions, I added thyme, basil, minced garlic, and a bag of frozen corn. The suggestion to temper the cream cheese before adding worked like a charm. Instead of removing potatoes and broth to thicken it I grabbed my mixing wand and after a few pulses it was ready to go.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast roll ups

from mr. food...cooking time is really the freezing time.

1. in a medium bowl , beat the cream cheese , egg yolk , and 1 / 4 cup sugar until smooth
2. set aside
3. cut the crust off each slice of bread then roll out each slice with a rolling pin
4. spread the cheese mixture over the bread , distributing evenly
5. roll up each slice jelly roll-style and place seam side down on a baking sheet
6. in a shallow dish , mix the remaining 3 / 4 cup sugar and the cinnamon
7. brush the butter over the roll-ups then roll them in the cinnamon-sugar mixture , until completely coated
8. repeat with the remaining roll-ups , placing them on the baking sheet after coating
9. cover and freeze for at least 2 hours , or up to 2 months
10. just before serving , preheat the oven to 400f
11. bake the roll-ups for 10 to 12 minutes , or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Tastes a lot like a churro!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy chocolate or gingersnap cookie crumb pie crust

very easy pie crust to put together. use either chocolate wafers or gingersnaps, depending on your need.

1. preheat oven , 350 degrees
2. process cookies in food processor until crumbed
3. mix crumbs , sugar , vanilla , and butter
4. if desired , reserve 2 tablespoons of crumb mixture for garnish
5. press mixture firmly and evenly against bottom and side of 9-inch pie pan
6. bake 10 minutes
7. cool
demonstrations.review: After moving to a "culinarily"  challenged region of the world I was ecstatic to find this recipe. Unfortunately I underestimated the shrinkage issue and ended up with 2 pie crust that barely covered the sides of my pie pans and not enough oreos to try it again. Initially I was going to rate 3 stars but after tasting my family and I decided that it deserved the 4th star. Needless to say, I will have to wait until tomorrow to make another attempt but will place in a springform pan instead. The end results were just too good to quit after 1 try.

target.recipe_text:
macaroni grill s bread

i found this at ehow.com and i promise you it is exactly like the original.

1. in a medium / large bowl , mix yeast with warm water
2. wait five minutes
3. add the sugar , flour , salt , and oil
4. knead until light
5. add herbs and pepper
6. knead into dough until blended
7. place dough in well oiled bowl and allow to rise for 1 hour
8. after one hour , punch dough down and let rise for another 30 minutes
9. place on baking sheet in a loaf shape
10. sprinkle top with a bit of salt and rosemary
11. bake at 370 f for about 25-35 minutes , or until top is golden
target.review: Thank you for posting this recipe!!  You are right, it tastes EXACTLY like Macaroni Grill's bread.  I cheated, though, by using frozen bread dough -- just added the spice to the dough, kneaded it in, let it rise, and baked.  I can't even express how good this was.  Good thing I made two loaves, because the first one is GONE!  Thanks again, it completely took my meal over-the-top.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quickie cinnamon rolls

these impressive pastries are so simple using refrigerated crescent rolls and a few pantry staples. based on pillsbury recipe.

1. unroll dough in one long rectangle and press to seal perforations
2. combine cinnamon and sugar and sprinkle over dough
3. roll up jelly roll style <like a log> starting from the short end and pinch seam to seal
4. using a serrated knife slice into 4 equal slices
5. (i use unwaxed dental floss threading underneath the 'log' and then crossing the ends above the 'log' pull ends to draw floss through to cut dough
6. makes a cleaner cut
7. )
8. place rolls pinched side down in ungreased muffin tin
9. bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes or until brown
10. cool for 5 minutes then transfer to wire rack
11. mix powdered sugar and orange juice to make a thin glaze
12. drizzle over the warm rolls and serve
demonstrations.review: I woke up to a cinnamon roll kinda morning...and this recipe had the easiness I needed!  My only change was that I used brown sugar.  My family was very happy with the results!!  THANK YOU.  =)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pot roast cooked in beer so tender it falls apart

it's fall apart good. serve with my roasted garlic mashed potatoes and cauliflower  recipe #46925 or mashed potatoes with roasted garlic and caramelized onions recipe #93000 





1. in a dry cast iron pot brown fat side down , then continue to brown all sides
2. your kitchen will be smokey !
3. season with salt and pepper
4. add 1 can beer
5. and pour the other can for yourself !
6. add rest of ingredients except butter and flour
7. put pot with cover into 325 degree oven for 3 hours
8. melt butter in micro and flour
9. remove roast and vegies from pan
10. add some drippings to butter then add back to pan
11. cook 5 minutes till nice and thick
12. add veggies back to sauce
13. plate the sliced roast {if it`s not already falling apart} top with the veggies and serve with your or my favorite side !
demonstrations.review: Absolutely AMAZING! I was a little concerned about the beer taking over the taste, but it did not.  It was very simple to make, very tender, and I have already forwarded the recipe to others!  Thanks so much for posting, it's a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun chicken alfredo pasta

this dish can be made two ways: 1. the easy weeknight throw together way, 2. the good for company restaurant style way. i thought this way extremely spicy, my husband thought it was perfect so, spice to taste. serve with salad and bread! i made the cream cheese a range, i prefer it with less but have added more to cut the spiciness when making it for both of us, so taste and add as desired.

1. prepare noodles according to package directions and set aside
2. trim chicken breasts of fat and cut into bite sized pieces
3. saute chicken in butter
4. if you are doing restaurant style us only 1-2 tbsp of butter , reserving the rest
5. add cajun seasoning to chicken while it sautes , adding the ingredients to taste , you can always add more later
6. for family style , once chicken is cooked , stir in half and half or cream and cheeses
7. bring to a low boil and stir until melted and creamy
8. toss with pasta and serve !
9. for restaurant style , melt remaining butter in a medium sauce pan , add half and half or cream
10. melt in cheeses , stir to combine
11. toss with pasta and place chicken on top
demonstrations.review: Sooooooo very, very GOOD!  We had this over cheese ravioli, only used 4 oz of cream cheese.  We thought the spice was wonderful, as we love spicy food.  I actually forgot the parmesan, and honestly we didn't miss it.  I added mushrooms, red onion, and omitted the onion powder (personal preference).  Thanks for posting.  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork loin with wine sauce

this makes a superbly tender loin. have also used recipe with venison loin and the results are excellent. when i use a venison loin, i marinate in salt water, beer or other marinade for several hours to remove wild game taste and use meat tenderizer before cooking.

1. heat oil in a large skillet and brown loin on all sides
2. remove loin from skillet , add onion and cook until tender
3. add flour
4. cook and stir until lightly browned
5. add chick stock , wine , garlic , bay leaf , minced parsley , salt and pepper
6. cook and stir over low heat until sauce is thoroughly blended
7. place browned loin in small roasting pan
8. pour wine sauce over top
9. cover and cook at 325 degrees for 2- 2 1 / 2 hours depending on size of loin
10. remove loin and slice thinly
11. to serve , arrange loin on platter and drizzle with reserved sauce
12. pass remaining sauce
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful!  Very easy to make, and there wasn't a bit left.  My entire family loved it!  thanks =)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easier than perogy casserole

i love perogies but not all the work it takes to make them.  i decided there had to be an easier way and this is what i came up with.

1. cook noodles as directed on package
2. drain
3. mix cheese , mashed potatoes , salt , onion salt and pepper together
4. line bottom of 9x13 pan with one third of the noodles
5. next layer one half of the cheese / potato mixture , then another layer of noodles , another layer of cheese / potatoes and ending with a layer of noodles
6. melt butter in frying pan and saute onions slowly until clear and soft
7. pour over noodles
8. cover
9. bake 30 minutes in 350 degree oven
10. let stand 10 minutes before cutting
11. serve with sour cream
demonstrations.review: soooo very, very good.  the taste is exactly like my Gram's pierogies.  I've never made them from scratch before, but I'm assuming that this is much easier.  Thanks so much for this recipe.

target.recipe_text:
super spicy boiled peanuts

you cant get boiled peanuts up where im at currently(upstate ny) and i love boiled peanuts  and extremely spicy food . so here is my version of these

1. add all ingredients to a large pot
2. stir well
3. set on high heat to boil
4. once boiling reduce heat to a low simmer
5. simmer until soft usually about 3 hours stir occasionally
target.review: Deliciously spicy!  I omitted the cayenne pepper, used only 1T red pepper.  They turned out a very nice hotness.  I can't imagine the full dose!  I'm from Syracuse, NY and these are my first taste of boiled peanuts!  After tasting these, I decided I like roasted peanuts better.  I tossed my pre-shelled boiled spanish peanuts in the oven for about 10 min and now they're incredibly delicious (five stars)!  I won't officially rate this recipe since I'm evidently not a fan of boiled peanuts.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy chicken in rice

this recipe was one of the 'usuals' at my house when i was little- even so, we never got tired of it! it is a super easy recipe, and you can play around with it: for the soup, you can either use two cans of cream of mushroom, or one can each of cream of mushroom and cream of celery. for the chicken, you can use boneless skinless chicken breasts, or chicken legs. i truly hope you enjoy!

1. rinse off chicken pieces
2. mix rice and cans of soup together
3. add 1 / 2 cup of milk , if you wish
4. place the chicken on top of rice mixture
5. sprinkle 1 / 2 of the dry onion soup mix on top of the chicken , or just sprinkle salt and pepper as desired
6. cover with foil and bake at 350 degrees for one hour
7. remove foil for the last 10 minutes
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: The chicken was wonderfully tender, but I didn't like the flavor of the onion soup (2 stars from me); my husband did enjoy it (4 stars from him).  Also, I thought the dish was too creamy.  Maybe I'll add more rice next time and flavor the chicken with just the salt and pepper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot shredded chicken breasts for freezing   oamc

great to have on-hand for recipes. just place as many chicken breasts as you can fit into your crock pot as long as the lid fits on properly. i use bone-in, skin-on but i'm sure boneless, skinless would work too.

1. place the chicken breasts in the crock pot , mix water and spices together and pour over the chicken
2. cook on the low setting for 8-10 hours
3. remove chicken breasts , shred or pull the meat from bones , removing skin
4. place meat in individual freezer bags or containers and freeze until needed for recipes
5. defrost and add to any recipes that call for cooked chicken
6. great for casseroles , quesadillas , pizzas , burritos , pastas , soups , etc
7. or heat with bbq sauce for hot barbecue chicken sandwiches
demonstrations.review: I used about 2.5 lb chicken breasts and doubled everything else.  Without that extra water, there was no liquid for it to cook in since I have a very large crock pot.  With the extra water, the top of each piece of chicken looked dry when it was done cooking, but it did not taste dry.  Great flavor, very useful.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
traditional chai tea

this is a spicy, creamy tea that i make every christmas. its more my tradition than the authentic tea. its tasty and sure to warm you from the inside out. great for those with a cold or flu... clears your sinuses and settles your tummy.

1. in large saucepan combine first nine ingredients
2. bring to a boil over high heat
3. reduce heat to low and simmer ten minutes
4. remove from heat and strain with fine sieve or through coffee filters
5. return to pot and add honey until melted
6. add milk and heat through , but do not boil
7. serve in clear mugs with a pinch of cinnamon on top
8. merry christmas !
9. you can also store the tea without the honey and milk in the fridge , then just reheat and add milk and honey to taste
10. this is a nice tea to serve with gingerbread or shortbread cookies at gatherings
demonstrations.review: I agree, excellent mix of spice and sweet.  It smelled like way too much nutmeg as it boiled (I am not a huge fan of nutmeg), but the recipe as is actually turned out amazing!  I added the tea bags only in the last 4 minutes of simmering since I usually steep my tea 4 min.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy yellow rice

taken from cooking today and changed dramatically, i like this dish! i've upped the spices!

1. heat a medium skillet , add butter and melt
2. add the onion , green pepper , and garlic
3. saute about 5-8 minutes , or till tender
4. add the rice , stirring gently
5. now , add the water or broth , and the rest of the spices
6. bring the mixture to a boil , cover , reduce heat , and cook for about 20 to 25 minutes , allowing the rice to become tender and the liquid to absorb
7. enjoy !
8. serves 6
demonstrations.review: Delicious flavor!  I actually had no turmeric, so I substituted 6 drops of yellow food coloring.  I halved the butter and substituted 1/8 t ground chipotle pepper for the hot sauce; it turned out nice & spicy.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut krispies ice cream bars

a delicious recipe that my mom has made since i was little. it is my favorite ice cream dish. anyone who loves ice cream and coconut will love this recipe!

1. melt margarine and brown sugar together over low heat , stirring often
2. remove from heat
3. add rice krispies and coconut to mixture
4. stir until cereal is evenly coated
5. place 1 / 2 of the mixture in the bottom of a 9x13-inch pan
6. spread ice cream over mixture in the pan
7. place the remaining 1 / 2 of the mixture on top of the ice cream
8. cover and freeze until serving
9. when serving cut into 12 pieces and top with chocolate syrup
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  We added 1/2 c chopped pecans on top as well.

target.recipe_text:
no knead batter dinner rolls

absolutely delicious and so easy to make. recipe found on the internet.

1. pour water into large mixing bowl , add yeast and let stand a few minutes
2. stir to dissolve and add half the flour , sugar , salt , softened shortening and egg
3. mix on medium speed of mixer for about 1 to 2 minutes or until smooth
4. add rest of flour and stir in by hand
5. cover bowl and let rise in warm place until doubled , about 30 minutes
6. grease 18 large muffin cups
7. stir batter and spoon into muffin cups , filling 1 / 2 full
8. let rise in warm place until batter reaches top of muffin cups , about 20 to 30 minutes
9. bake at 425 for 10 to 15 minutes or until done
target.review: Believe it or not, I never thought to make this as rolls!  I used to make it at a coffee house I used to have as "Batter Bread"!  Just shows to go you what a little imagination can do.  Thanks for the idea.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shortcrust pastry dough

this is in response to a request for homemade pastry. i am the world's worst baker, but my pastry came out right on my first attempt! (prep time includes refrigeration time)

1. in a large mixing bowl , sift together the flour and salt
2. add the butter and cut into flour until the mixture resembles fine bread crumbs
3. mix in enough cold water to hold mixture together
4. form into a ball
5. wrap in wax paper or plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator for 30-45 minutes
6. assembly: preheat the oven to 350 degrees
7. spray a baking sheet , muffin tray , etc
8. with nonstick cooking spray or grease with shortening
9. remove pastry from refrigerator
10. lightly sprinkle work surface with flour
11. roll out pastry to about 1 / 8-inch thickness
12. cut into circles , squares , or any shape and size that you like
13. use any filling that you want
14. to"join" separate pastry pieces together , moisten the edges with beaten egg and gently crimp the edges together
15. if your dish is to have pastry on the top , brush the top of the pastry with beaten egg
16. place on prepared baking sheet , muffin tray , etc
17. and bake for 50 minutes or until golden brown on top
18. pastry freezes extremely well
demonstrations.review: I love this one!  It's quick and easy.  A suggestion?  Why not try putting ingredients in a large reclosable plastic bag, massage to mix and shape before refrigerating?  Would this work-anybody?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade sausage seasoning blend

a dry herb blend for giving any ground meat a 

1. blend all ingredients together in a spice grinder or mini-food processor
2. store in an airtight container until ready to use
3. to use , mix with 1 pound ground meat
4. chill seasoned meat 3 hours before using
5. or you may also use this in any recipe calling for sausage seasoning
demonstrations.review: A good blend I've used many times.  Kept in a pepper mill, I grind as needed.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gigi s oven baked doughnuts

my grandma (gigi) received monthly recipe cards from the montana-dakota utilies co during world war ii.  this was a recipe from the month of "april"  year unknown.  the comment on the card states: bake your doughnuts--and give your fat to the war effort.  majority of time is the dough rising.  **it takes a few minutes less when "proofed" in higher heat with fairly high humidity**

1. soften yeast in lukewarm water
2. scald milk and pour over shortening , sugar and salt
3. cool to lukewarm
4. add yeast , beaten eggs , flour and spices
5. let double in size
6. roll out to 1 / 2 inch thickness
7. cut into 3 inch rounds , place on pans , grease tops and let rise 20 minutes
8. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes
9. spread with butter and sprinkle with sugar while warm
demonstrations.review: I enjoy a good recipe, and this one is excellent. The only problem is the time it takes to let rise. I enjoy the taste, especially when I sprinkle in Peanut butter chips.  I mix the dry ingredients in a reclosable plastic storage bag.  Less mess.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
authentic jamaican jerk sauce

i found this recipe on www.jamaicans.com.  we tried this and wow was it awesome.  i did not have allspice berries so i substituted ground allspice using one full tablespoon.

1. put content in a food processor or blender and liquify
2. pour sauce in a jar and keep refrigerated
3. the sauce will keep forever if kept refrigerated
4. to increase spiciness blend pepper and pimento and add to sauce the hot peppers at any time
5. marinate meat at least 2 hours
demonstrations.review: Now THIS is authentic.  However, if you want a truly HOT sauce, substitute Habenero for Scotch Bonnet peppers.  Or go medium with Jalapeno.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brisket of beef

this is a very simple, easy no brainer way to make a delicous fall apart beef brisket.

1. put brisket in roasting pan
2. dump onion soup mix on top
3. pour water over about 1 / 2 inch into pan
4. stir a little
5. cover tightly with foil
6. put into oven at 250 degrees-middle rack
7. forget about it for at least 5 hours
8. take it out , cut against the grain , it should fall apart and be very tender
9. season with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review:
I've made it this way at home.  Commercially, for the larger ones, I cover it on the fat side with 1 cup of mixed with 1/4 cup black pepper. Then roast in a hot oven to rare before slicing off most of the fat and the salt mix.
I seldom get any at home because everyone digs in.

target.recipe_text:
black bottom banana bars

delicious and very moist. even better the second day.

1. in a mixing bowl , cream butter and sugar
2. add egg and vanilla
3. beat until thoroughly combined
4. blend in the bananas
5. combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
6. add to creamed mixture and mix well
7. divide batter in half
8. add cocoa to half
9. spread into a greased 13-in x 9-in pan
10. spoon remaining batter on top and swirl with a knife
11. bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes or until the bars test done
12. cool
target.review: Very moist, easy and delicious!YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review:
To quote my husband, "This is the BEST meatloaf I've ever had!!"

2 thumbs up for this recipe! The glaze would work very well on other meats.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
icing in the cake cake

this recipe comes from a community church cookbook. it is easy and delicious. i have friends that have made this with other flavor combinations and the result has always been good thus far. the best part is since it is not 

1. mix all together with mixer
2. bake in a well-greased bundt pan at 375 for 45-55 minutes
3. cool 20 minutes before turning out on cake plate
demonstrations.review: DELISH!!!!! My 11 Y/O DD made this with chocolate cake and chocolate frosting..YUM!!! Thanks Anni!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet potato casserole iii

nan

1. combine sweet potatoes , sugar , butter , eggs , vanilla and milk
2. mix well
3. spoon into a 2 quart casserole
4. combine topping ingredients and sprinkle over sweet potatoes
5. casserole can be refrigerated at this point for up to 2 days
6. bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes or until heated through
7. makes 8 sinful servings
demonstrations.review: I made it as listed for Easter except I did the traditional marshmallow topping..DELICIOUS!!! This is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oh my d lux chocolate chip cookies

these are definitely not your standard chocolate chip cookies! they are of the "oh my" variety, which is what you'll say after the first bite! the addition of rice krispies may seem odd, but these are great and a favorite of kids of all ages. an extra plus...this recipe make about 7 1/2 dozen cookies :) (don't worry, you'll have no problem getting rid of them all!)

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cream butter and add sugar , beating at low speed until light and fluffy
3. add eggs and vanilla and beat well
4. combine flour and baking powder and add to creamed mixture until well combined
5. stir in remaining ingredients
6. drop by heaping teaspoonfuls onto baking sheets
7. bake for 10-12 minutes or until lightly browned
8. cool on wire racks
demonstrations.review: VERY good cookie recipe! I used chopped almonds and milk choc chips...The only thing, it didnt make nearly as much as it said it did unless you make very teeny cookies.My cookies,when cooked,were about 2 inches in diameter.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheddar cheese   ham soup

a great winter soup! serve with a pan of hot biscuits or onion scones.

1. melt butter in a large , heavy saucepan
2. brown carrots , celery , onion , ham and mushrooms over high heat
3. turn heat to medium and cook until tender
4. sprinkle in flour , paprika , dry mustard
5. stir over low heat about 5 minutes
6. gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk
7. stir until slightly thickened
8. add cheese and whisk until melted
9. do not boil
10. season with salt and pepper
11. top w / parsley
demonstrations.review: This is the best soup Ive ever had! Heaven in a bowl!! Dont know what part of Aroostook County youre from but I will be sharing this recipe all over Fort Kent!!! Thanks for sharing this!!

target.recipe_text:
lasagna casserole

i love this recipe! it's quick and delicious! i got it years ago from my good friend danielle.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. prepare pasta according to package directions
3. in bottom of casserole dish spread drained , cooked pasta
4. fry beef , add onion , garlic , salt& pepper , seasoning and tomato sauce
5. simmer for 15 minutes
6. pour over noodles
7. spread sour cream on and top with cheese
8. bake uncovered for 30 minutes
target.review: This was wonderful! I fixed this for lunch yesterday and had my two daughters over.  They loved it also.  I had to make sure we didn't finish it, so I would have some to feed my husband for supper that night.  This is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon blossoms  paula deen

these mini cupcakes are packed with lemon flavor.  a paula deen recipe.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. spray miniature muffin tins with vegetable oil cooking spray
3. combine the cake mix , pudding mix , eggs and oil and blend well with an electric mixer until smooth , about 2 minutes
4. pour a small amount of batter , filling each muffin tin half way
5. bake for 12 minutes
6. turn out onto a tea towel
7. make the glaze while the cakes are baking
8. sift the sugar into a mixing bowl
9. add the lemon juice , zest , oil , and 3 tablespoons water
10. mix with a spoon until smooth
11. with fingers , dip the cupcakes into the glaze while they're still warm , covering as much of the cake as possible , or spoon the glaze over the warm cupcakes , turning them to completely coat
12. place on wire racks with waxed paper underneath to catch any drips
13. let the glaze set thoroughly , about 1 hour , before storing in containers with tight-fitting lids
demonstrations.review: I also made these by Paula Dean, after watching her make them on her show and had to try them.  They are wonderful! I served them on Christmas day and my daughter said it was like a taste of summer in her mouth!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
twinkie strawberry surprise

this is a no bake, no cook recipe that tastes like strawberry shortcake and starts with twinkies!! it is very easy to prepare, but it does need to chill several hours, so plan ahead :)

1. slice twinkies in half lengthwise and lay evenly flat side up in a 9 x 13 inch pan
2. pour strawberries all over the top
3. in a large bowl , mix pudding , milk and whipped topping until well combined
4. spread over strawberries
5. cover and refrigerate several hours overnight
demonstrations.review: I loved how easy this was to make and still taste wonderful! I also used the Sarahlee pound cake instead. It was still good for several days in the frig.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
demonstrations.review: I have been searching for the perfect sloppy joe recipe for some time and this it. Thanks so much for sharing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
speedy baked beans

great if you're in a hurry. i usually have all the ingredients on hand. i've only used the microwave version.

1. combine all ingredients
2. mix well
3. bake at 350 degrees for 30-40 minutes , or microwave on high 7- 9 1 / 2 minutes , stirring twice-cover with wax paper while cooking
demonstrations.review: these beans were wonderful and easy! My kind of cooking. I baked it in the oven. Plan on having again with weiners in it and serving it for main dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot sausage and sauerkraut dinner

great for those chilly fall evenings.

1. in 3 1 / 2 or 4-quart crock pot , combine potatoes , carrots and onion
2. in medium bowl , combine brown sugar , mustard , and caraway seed
3. mix well
4. stir in sauerkraut and kielbasa
5. spoon sauerkraut mixture over vegetables in cooker
6. cover
7. cook on low setting for at least 8 hours or until vegetables are tender
demonstrations.review: I fixed this for my husband and me,we loved it.I left out the caraway seed because I didn't have any. I aready been to the store and had these ingredients on hand.  I love using the crockpot.  This recipe was easy to follow. It's a keeper for us. Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
target.review: I know this recipe has a lot of very positive reviews, and I don't like to be difficult, but I honestly didn't like it.  I didn't like the bottom (peanut butter) portion - it didn't have the peanut butter taste I was expecting.  I probably would have let my own opinion slide, but when my 8 year old and 6 year old wouldn't eat them (and they are not picky eaters), I thought I should probably mention it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetarian spaghetti and lentil sauce

an easy stand by meal that the kids love. i usually double the recipe and pop it in the freezer for an instant meal when time is at a premium.

1. cook onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes until onion is soft
2. add lentils , chili , salt and pepper , and water
3. simmer 30 minutes
4. add stock , basil , oregano , tomatoes , tomato paste , and vinegar
5. simmer uncovered approx one hour , stirring occasionally
6. serve on spaghetti and sprinkle with cheese
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent recipe. I was looking for something for my vegetarian son, but it was very popular among the four non-vegetarians in the family as well. We have added this one to the family recipe book.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
three pepper pizza

a colorful pizza.  a great way to use up summer produce. you can use a store bought pizza dough or make your own.  from williams-sonoma with some minor changes to fit our taste.

1. roll out the dough into a 12 inch round and lay the dough on top of a lightly greased pizza pan
2. lightly brush the dough with the olive oil and spread the tomatoes evenly on top , leaving a 1 / 2 inch border
3. lay the cheese slices evenly over the tomatoes
4. scatter the bell peppers and sausage evenly over the cheese
5. sprinkle with half of the oregano and season with salt and pepper
6. bake at 450 degrees f until the bottom of the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbly , about 15 minutes
7. remove from the oven and sprinkle with remaining oregano
8. let cool for 5 minutes , then cut into slices and serve
demonstrations.review:
Wonderful pizza!  With the olive oil and tomatoes instead of tomato sauce it had the feel of a gourmet pizza.  I would strongly recommend including all the tomato called for in the recipe, as it gives the pizza a sweet flavour.

We will certainly use this recipe again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best vegan oat   walnut waffles  or pancakes

our sunday tradition entails that my hubby make waffles for me and the boys (3 and 5). we tried this recipe this morning and it was the best waffles he's made by far!  this recipe is from moosewood resturant and is listed exactly as they wrote it. here are my adaptions: we omitted the walnuts due to allergies. we used all unbleached flour. we decreased the soy milk by 1/3 cup and added a glob of vanilla yogurt instead. we used sugar instead of maple syrup. lastly, we doubled the recipe for the four of us because we love leftovers for the next morning! (though i only added one tbsp of oil instead of two) this could be used for pancakes also. follow-up: since posting this recipe, i tried as pancakes. while the taste was good, i prefer the waffles.

1. if toasting walnuts , toast in a single layer on an unoiled baking tray at 350 for 5 to 10 minutes , until fragant and golden brown
2. in a large bowl , sift the flours , salt , baking powder , cinnamon , and nutmeg , stir in the walnuts and oats
3. in a separate bowl , stir together the milk , oil , and maple syrup or sugar
4. make a well in the dry ingredients and pour in the wet ingredients
5. stir until just combined
6. do not overmix the batter
7. when combining wet and dry ingredients , it is better to leave a few lumps than to stir too much
8. after mixing , let the batter sit for a few minutes until bubbles form on the top
9. this 'rest' gives the baking powder time to start working so the waffles will be lighter
10. preheat waffle iron and lightly oil to prevent sticking
11. use 1 / 3 cup of batter for each waffle and bake accoring to the directions for your waffle iron
demonstrations.review: I made these according to the recipe, except I used 2% milk instead of soy (I'm not a vegan - just a dude who ran out of eggs).  I have to disagree with a couple of other posts in that I didn't miss the eggs at all.  The waffles were just as crispy as any others I have made.  My suggestion to anyone making waffles of any type is not to stack them after they're cooked.  That makes them soggy.  I wouldn't recommend this recipe to anyone who doesn't like walnuts (which I do), as that seemed to be the dominant flavour to me.  We liked them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick and easy cinnamon rolls  yeast free

i made these today in 'home ec' class. these are super yummy and quick to make because they have no yeast, so you don't have to wait hours for them to rise.
my friend is vegan so our group used powdered milk instead of actual milk.
you do not need to use a mixer at all ^_^
sorry for the form of measurement, the recipe was written in ml's instead of cups-tsp-tbsp.

1. preheat oven to 250c
2. mix flour , sugar , salt , and baking powered in large bowl
3. cut in margarine until mixture looks like oatmeal or small peas
4. add milk gradually , stirring with a fork
5. dough should come away from sides of bowl
6. knead 3-4 times and then roll into a rectangle on lightly floured counter
7. -filling-
8. smear margarine over dough coating it not to thick but not to thin
9. sprinkle desired amount of cinnamon on top
10. sprinkle desired amount of brown sugar on top
11. sprinkle desired amount of raisins
12. roll up like a jelly roll , starting from the long edge
13. slice into 1-inch slices and place cut side down in a grease muffin tin
14. bake 12-15 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good.  Tasty, but texture wasn't quite as good as some other recipes I have tried.  Also, the glaze didn't turn out at all.  Not sure whether I did something wrong.  I had to throw that out and make my own.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jeannette s jam  bread machine

posted in response to request. from bbonline.com . i have not yet tried this. yield is estimated.

1. place all ingredients in bread pan
2. set to jam cycle and start
3. spoon into containers and refrigerate
demonstrations.review: We really liked this jam.  We used 8 ounces of frozen strawberries (cut into big chunks) and 8 ounces of frozen blueberries.  We also halved the sugar, and found the sweetness about right for our tastes.  The recipe yeilded a half a mason jar of jam.

target.recipe_text:
thai drunken master noodles  pad kee mow

this is my closest attempt at recreating our favorite thai dish. the key is the fresh wide rice noodles that can only be found at an asian market.

1. heat a wok with several tablespoons of cooking oil
2. seperate rice noodles and stir fry noodles until they soften
3. when oil is absorbed add a few tablespoons of soy sauce and finish cooking
4. remove noodles from heat , place noodles on a plate and keep them in a warm oven
5. add a few more tablespoons of cooking oil to the skillet and stir fry onions , garlic , green onions , peppers and basil until softened slightly
6. add chicken and cook until slightly browned
7. combine all ingredients for sauce in a medium sized bowl and whisk everything together ,
8. add noodles and sauce to skillet
9. stir fry for several minutes
10. remove from heat and enjoy
target.review: We enjoyed this dish very much. We used tofu instead of chicken, and our veggies included red bell pepper, onion, carrot, and zucchini. We used 14 oz of 3mm rice sticks, which we boiled for 5 min and then stir-fried briefly. The amount of sauce seemed like you could have even more, as the noodles soaked everything up. We will definitely make this again. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon swirl quick bread

this rich quick bread is a favorite with my family. i often give my husband a few slices to take with him on his commute to work, along with a tall travel mug of coffee.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a large mixing bowl , beat together butter , 1 cup sugar , and egg
3. combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
4. add the flour mixture to the egg mixture alternately with the buttermilk
5. in a small bowl , combine the cinnamon and remaining 1 / 3 cup sugar
6. pour a third of the batter into a greased 8x4x2-inch loaf pan
7. sprinkle a third of the cinnamon sugar on top of batter
8. repeat layers twice
9. bake for 45-50 minutes , until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean
10. cool in pan for 10 minutes
11. remove from pan to a wire rack to cool completely
demonstrations.review: Absolutely scrumptious and so easy to make!  We used Saigon cinnamon (much stronger cinnamon flavor), 1/2 tsp. vanilla extract, and 1/4 tsp almond extract. Wow!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry summer sensation dessert

my kids saw this in kraft's "what's cooking magazine" and decided to make it for dessert when we had their teachers over for lunch. this is a simple make-ahead dessert that appeals to the eye and the stomach! cook time is freezing time.
