1. line a 9x5 inch loaf pan with foil , spoon sorbet into pan and put in the freezer for 10 minutes
2. pour milk into a large bowl and add dry pudding mix
3. whisk until well blended and fold in whipped topping
4. spread pudding mixture over sorbet in pan
5. freeze for at least 3 hours or overnight
6. wrap securely and label if freezing longer than 24 hours
7. unmold loaf pan onto a serving platter and top with fresh raspberries just before serving
8. it will be easier to cut if it rests for 15 minutes
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Super easy to make and a great summer dessert!  We brought this to a "summer vegetables" themed dinner. We used chocolate pudding mix and really enjoyed how it complemented the raspberry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chip apple cookies

delicious moist and flavourful cookies. because the apple is grated, it is not obvious there is apple in these cookies.

1. in a large bowl , cream together margarine and sugar
2. beat in egg
3. in seperate bowl , mix flour , baking soda and cinnamon
4. stir flour mixture into creamed mixture
5. stir in apples , chocolate chips and oats
6. drop mixture by rounded teaspoons onto cookie sheets
7. bake at 350f for 12-15 minutes
8. makes 2 1 / 2 dozen
demonstrations.review: Excellent! These are great to make during apple season when you have a lot of apples to go through. I really enjoyed the cinnamon and chocolate combo.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lentil salad with roasted sweet potatoes and queso fresco

from about.com, posting for zwt 7, south america. this combines two of my favorite things, lentils and sweet potatoes! recipe is credited to marian blazes, who says "toss it all together and serve warm, adding a few baby spinach leaves for something green. this is a healthful salad that everyone will enjoy. " servings are a guess...please help me if this needs correcting!

1. preheat the oven to 400 degrees
2. toss the cubed sweet potatoes and the chopped red onion with 2 tablespoons olive oil , the sazongoya seasoning packet , and salt and pepper
3. place vegetables in a roasting pan and roast , gently stirring every 10 minutes or so , until potatoes are starting to brown around the edges and appear slightly crispy
4. let cool
5. while potoatoes are roasting , bring the lentils to a boil in the 2 cups of water with 1 teaspoon salt
6. simmer lentils gently until tender , about 25 minutes
7. drain lentils well , and let cool completely
8. place lentils in a bowl and toss with 1 tablespoon olive oil , 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar , and the juice of one lime
9. stir in the sweet potatoes and onions , chopped red pepper , and queso fresco , and gently toss to mix
10. season with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: Awesome!  Made a great lunch, and we'll be making it again this week for dinner.  We used a generous amount of smoked paprika, and the flavor was excellent.  We liked the queso fresco, and this week we will try feta.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
divine macaroni and cheese

i found some long lost recipes yesterday.  i'm posting them here for safekeeping.  from december 1999 southern living.

1. melt butter in a dutch oven over medium heat
2. add garlic , and saute until tender
3. add milk , and cook until thoroughly heated
4. gradually stir in 1 / 2 c parmesan cheese and next 6 ingredients until smooth
5. stir in spinach
6. add pasta , tossing to coat
7. spoon into a lightly greased 13 x 9 baking dish
8. bake at 400 for 7 minutes
9. remove from oven
10. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 2 c parmesan cheese and breadcrumbs
11. reduce oven temp to 350 and bake for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Best macaroni and cheese ever! It is very rich and filling.  Perfect in the winter, and makes great leftovers for lunch!   I don't usually like gorgonzola cheese, but I loooove this dish!!!

target.recipe_text:
fusion avocado

had this in texas a couple of years ago! my sil kathie turned me on to it!
sushi without the fish, nori, and trouble of making it! ok she just had the soy but darn the pickeled ginger is so good! this is so quick and easy!!!!! it'll satisfy that i want sushi need!  i myself can eat one a day!

1. take a spoon between the meat and skin to loosen
2. pour 1 / 2 teaspoon soy sauce over each half of avocado
3. scoop out with a spoon and enjoy !
4. using optional wasabi or ginger to taste is a great healthy option !
target.review: I loved this snack.  Also tried it as a previous reviewer suggested with balsamic vinegar and it was wonderful too!  Thanks for the great keeper

demonstrations.recipe_text:
still another tuna pasta salad        mom s tuna salad

a tasty tuna salad which is easy to prepare. i frequently make it during the summer for a light supper, after a day at the pool. also works well for picnics. amounts given are estimates, i usually prepare this 

1. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients
2. mix well to blend
3. if salad is too dry , add more mayonnaise
4. taste , and adjust seasonings to your preference
5. chill well before serving
demonstrations.review: My hubby works is a contractor and during the summer heat, the last thing he wants is a heavy meal.  THIS WAS PERFECT!!  I doubled the recipe, left out the eggs (only because i was out), added red AND green pepper, Old Bay Seasoning and a little thyme.  I served it on a bed of romaine with halved grape tomatoes and it made a perfect main dish.  This will definately become a staple in our "summer fare". Thanks for a wonderfully light addition to the cookbook!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb spaghetti squash alfredo

this is a very good and comes from george stella's low carb and loving it. i did change the way to cook the squash as it is much faster and less clean up.

1. slice spaghetti squash in half lengthwise , scoop out seeds with a spoon
2. place squash cut side down in microwave safe dish with 1 / 3 cup water
3. cook about 15 minutes or until tender when tested with a fork
4. scoop out the cooked squash from its skin , discard skin
5. use a fork to fluff and separate the squash into"spaghetti"- like strands
6. you can use your hands
7. reserve the cooked squash and heat in microwave just before serving
8. melt half the butter in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat
9. add cream and reduce for about 2 minutes , then add garlic and cheese , whisk quickly , heating through
10. stir in the rest of the butter and parsley
11. place spaghetti squash in a large serving bowl , and , pour alfredo sauce over squash , garnish with basil and tomatoes , serve and enjoy
demonstrations.review: This was a wonderful low carb recipe.  We have become huge fans of all squash, so i was excited to see a recipe showcasing another way to use spaghetti squash.  Even my kids loved it.  Thanks for a keeper!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot pork chops

i make this for my husband and daughter, and i have got nothing but smiles from this.  it's easy, cheap and oh so yummy!

1. combine cream of mushroom soup , 1 / 3 can water , softened cream cheese and garlic in a bowl
2. stir out most of the lumps , but the rest will cook out
3. pour in bottom of crock pot
4. put pork chops on top of mixture
5. add liberal amounts of salt and pepper
6. i'm usually heavy handed !
7. cook on low for 7-8 hours
8. serve over slices of warm bread or pasta of your choice
9. pork chops will fall apart
10. so tender you can cut with a spoon !
demonstrations.review: This recipe was tasty and VERY simple.  I used cream of celery instead of mushroom and as suggested added sliced potatoes and onions to the bottom of the pot, covered with soup mixture, and then added the chops.  They were very tender and while not a "five star" recipe, i will definately fix again.  My three year old absolutely LOVED this dish, and anything she will eat well is a keeper in my book.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun seafood pasta

293 five star reviews caught my interest in this pasta dish when i was searching the net. shrimp and scallops in a cream sauce with parmesan and swiss served over your favourite pasta.

1. cook pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water until al dente
2. meanwhile , pour cream into large skillet
3. cook over med
4. heat , stirring constantly , until just boiling
5. reduce heat , add herbs , seasoning , and veg's
6. simmer 8 minutes , or until thickened
7. stir in seafood , cooking until shrimp is no longer transparent
8. stir in cheeses , blending well
9. drain pasta , top with seafood sauce
10. opt
11. you can make this hotter to suit your tastes by doubling the pepper and red pepper flakes
demonstrations.review: This pasta had a wonderful flavor and my DH, who is neither a pasta or a seafood guy, loved it.  My kids liked the pasta and the sauce but picked around the seafood. OH WELL!  The sauce was a little thin, but nothing a piece of garlic bread can't take care of.  I used shredded parm instead of grated because it was all i had.  I used dried thyme and fresh basil and parsley.  This was definately good enough for a company meal and i will be fixing it again soon!!  Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffed celery snacks  low carb

this is a great low-carb snack!

1. in a small bowl , combine cream cheese and seasonings
2. stuff into celery
3. cover and chill for at least 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I love celery and cream cheese, and this adaptation was great.  I also love to mix the cream cheese with organic salsa and use the celery sticks to "dip" with!  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
watermelon yogurt mint smoothie

there's nothing more refreshing on a hot summer's day than watermelon, the base for this yummy summer smoothie from the meals for you website.  the recipe specifies non-fat lemon yoghurt, but i always use creamy greek yoghurt, and because i love lemony flavours, i add the juice of half a lemon.  the honey counter-balances this superbly.

1. puree the watermelon , honey and mint quickly -- do not over blend
2. pulse in the yogurt and cinnamon until just smooth
3. transfer to serving glasses
target.review: I began to make this and realized I didn't have mint (fresh or dried).  A quick google search shows that you can substitute basil for mint in sweet dishes, so I tried that.  Not too bad!  I don't think of basil as a sweet seasoning, but it actually worked out pretty well - I'd do it again.  I also used plain yogurt.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ma  cristina s tortilla eggs

this recipe was handed down from my late mother-in-law and it is a simple yet delicious quick breakfast. my son loves them. any salsa will work, store bought or homemade, you choose the heat, i prefer the chunky kind. i've also added ham or sausage with the salsa for good results.

1. tear the tortilla into bite sized pieces
2. in a hot dry skillet , fry the tortilla pieces until they just start to brown
3. while they are cooking , beat the eggs with a little water
4. lower the heat to med and stir in the salsa
5. cook for 2 or 3 minutes
6. add the eggs and salt to taste
7. continue cooking and stirring until the eggs are just set
8. the eggs will continue cooking after you take them off the heat
9. mmmmmm
demonstrations.review: I found this recipe years ago, and I make it regularly making modifications as needed.  I often make this by using the crumbs from a bag of tortilla chips instead of fresh tortillas, and I mix them in with the egg and water and let them sit for a few minutes.  I then cook the egg-tortilla mix first, and add the salsa when the eggs are set.  Delicious either way!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
three minute brown sugar fudge

cut this into small squares as it is a very rich and sweet candy.

1. heat together first five ingredients in a large heavy bottomed saucepan
2. boil hard three minutes
3. add vanilla and nuts
4. beat until thick and pour into grease 9x9 pan
5. cut when cool using a knife dipped in hot water
demonstrations.review: Mine tasted like hard-packed brown sugar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy japanese slaw

this salad uses jalapenos to jazz it up. you may omit them if you don't like it spicy.

1. in large bowl , combine cabbage , green onions , cilantro , and jalapenos
2. remove noodles from soup mix and break into small bite sized pieces
3. add to cabbage mixture
4. in a small bowl , whisk oils with vinegar , sugar and contents of seasoning packet from soup mix
5. pour over salad and toss thoroughly
6. add sesame seeds and salt and pepper to taste
7. toss to mix
demonstrations.review: I made this with a little extra spice (didn't de-seed the jalapenos, and substituted one habanero for a jalapeno).  It tasted a little unbalanced, so I threw in a can of mandarin oranges.  Perfect!  I'm happy I found this recipe.  I have salads like this at potlucks and never tried making my own until now.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker cheddar polenta

an easy and delicious breakfast, lunch, or dinner! add a little pinch of cayenne for a kick! from the cabot cheese folks!

1. mix water , polenta , olive oil , salt and pepper in slow cooker
2. whisk until well blended
3. add cheddar cheese and whisk again
4. cover and cook on high setting for about 2 hours , or until liquid is mostly absorbed
5. stir together well
6. if not serving right away , pour onto buttered baking sheet with sides , spreading into an even layer
7. cover with plastic wrap and let cool
8. when ready to serve , cut into rectangles and saut in nonstick skillet with olive oil until golden on both sides
demonstrations.review: I used a mix of water and chicken broth, Â½ polenta and Â½ cornmeal.  Used 2Â½t hot salt and omitted pepper.  Only had about 2 c shredded cheese, though.  Still turned out delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy layered chicken bake

easy, economical and comfort food! this is a hit in our house and i have even done a version of it in my crockpot on busy days. for a lower fat version, substitute half fat cream soup.  you won't taste the difference. to make it faster, keep chicken breasts whole and increase baking time to 45 mins. i got this from a kraft recipe magazine.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. place chicken in 13x9 baking dish
3. sprinkle with poultry seasoning
4. combine stuffing mix with 1 cup water
5. mix soup with milk and spread over chicken
6. spread green beans over next
7. sprinkle with cheese
8. top with stuffing
9. bake 30 mins or until chicken is cooked through
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!  I was looking for a simple dinner recipe and this was it.  I didn't have green beans so I used sliced celery, and I used leftover stuffing instead of stuffing mix (minus the water).  I also kept the chicken whole.  Perfect, easy.

target.recipe_text:
african chicken in spicy red sauce

this recipe is from the october 2006 issue of cooking light.  it's very tasty! the original recipe calls for using breast halves, drumsticks and thighs.  i just used skinned, boneless breasts. also, used olive oil instead of cooking spray.  this is their description - " this flavourful ethipian-inspired chicken stew uses berbere, an ethiopian spice blend.  store extra spice mix covered in a cool, dark place for up to two weeks. use leftovers on salmon, flank steak, or chicken for fiery flavour.  serve with basmati rice.  **prep time includes marinating time
*additional tip*- maidinafrica suggested swirling a bit of plain yogurt on top just before serving so we tried that - it's really good and the contrast of colours swirled together makes for a very pretty presentation!

1. berbere:
2. combine all ingredients in a small bowl
3. yields 1 / 4 cup
4. serving size is 1 teaspoons
5. chicken:
6. place chicken in a shallow dish
7. drizzle with juice , and sprinkle with 1 / 2 tsp salt
8. cover and marinate in refrigerator for 30 minutes
9. heat a large pot over medium heat
10. add olive oil
11. add onion and garlic
12. cook 5 minutes , stirring frequently
13. add 2 tsp berbere , remaining 1 / 4 tsp salt , butter , ginger , nutmeg , and cardamom , cook 1 minute
14. add wine , broth , and tomato paste
15. stir until well blended
16. add chicken mixture
17. bring to a boil
18. cover , reduce heat , and simmer 50 minutes or until chicken is tender , turning chicken occasionally
19. stir in cilantro
20. serve with lemon wedges
target.review: Wow, that was a surprise! I'm an Indian and Thai curry lover, but had never tried anything like this, fantastically fragrant and rich flavour. This is one I definitely will be making again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken   butternut pasta with creamy sage sauce

tasty and quick.

1. heat the oven to 400f toss the squash in 1 tsp oil and
2. roast in the oven for 25 mins stirring half way through
3. while the squash is cooking , heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan , throw in the onion and saut for 5 mins until soft , add the chicken and cook for a further 5 mins until browned all over
4. pour in the broth and simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the broth has reduced
5. while the chicken is cooking , cook the pasta according to the pack instructions then drain
6. add in the roasted squash to the chicken then the sage and cheese stir well
7. add 2 spoonfuls of the sauce to the pasta and stir inches divide the pasts between 4 plates and top with the chicken
demonstrations.review: Great taste and easy to make, liked the combination of the butternut texture combined with the soft pasta and chicken. I used dried sage instead, which gave the menu quite a sweet and fragrant flavour.... Will defiantly be making this again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with banana curry sauce   caribbean

from food & wine.

1. heat the oven to 450
2. in a food processor or blender , puree the bananas , curry powder , coriander , dry mustard , butter , lime zest , lime juice , salt , pepper , and 1 / 4 cup of the water
3. make a few deep cuts in each chicken breast and put the breasts in a roasting pan
4. pour the curry sauce over the chicken , making sure the sauce gets into the cuts
5. roast in the bottom third of the oven until the chicken is just done , about 20 minutes
6. remove the roasting pan from the oven and remove the chicken breasts from the pan
7. there should be plenty of thick sauce in the bottom of the pan
8. set the pan over moderate heat and whisk in the remaining 1 / 2 cup water
9. continue to whisk until the sauce is heated through , adding more water if you want a thinner sauce
10. serve the chicken breasts with the sauce over them
11. sprinkle with parsley if you like
12. serve with steamed rice
demonstrations.review: What an absolutely delicious alternative to an Indian curry. I added more lime as I'm a fan of slightly acidic flavour combined with the sweetness of the banana. Served with basmati rice, and chopped cucumber and tomato. Top marks !

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon raisin bread for the bread machine

nan

1. add all the ingredients in order given except the raisins
2. add raisins in on the "add in" beep
3. bake on "sweet bread" setting
demonstrations.review: Tasted great, but unfortunately it didn't rise. Will definitely be trying again, but will activate the yeast first and reduce the salt as it was a bit too salty.... But that's perhaps because it didn't rise?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
magic chocolate mug cake  microwave

note added jan 27, 2012:  please note that this is not a serious cake recipe! it is a fun recipe, for a quick choc snack. it may work for you, or you may have to make adjustments, or it might not work for you. please do not judge this little recipe as if it is a chocolate cake -- as you will see from the reviews, they range from "great!" to "awful!" lol! 

original intro: this recipe is doing the e-mail rounds! i do not know where it originated, but if you have kids, teenagers, or a sweet tooth yourself, it works!!  a chocolate cake in a mug, for one person! do use a large mug!  i never, ever post recipes like this which i have not made, and i'm not a microwave fan, but this one, for parents of the above-mentioned people, just has to be posted. delicious with whipped cream, ice cream or custard, they say! it must be great to mix a choc cake in a mug, and have a hot "cake" within 3 minutes!!

1. in a small bowl , mix the flour , sugar , cocoa , tiny pinch baking powder and tiny pinch salt
2. add egg and mix into dry mixture
3. add oil and milk and mix well
4. grease a tall , large mug , and pour in this mixture , scraping out with a spatula
5. place in microwave on high for 2 1 / 2 - 3 minutes
demonstrations.review: I never knew it was possible to make cake like this in the microwave. It worked well, but was rather bland... Not sure what it missed though. Nevertheless went down well with custard

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: Simple, tasty and quick.... What a great combination, my only problem was getting the sauce to thicken. Added a little extra dried chilli to the sauce, but that's just a personal preference. Great served with rice and mixed fried veg.

target.recipe_text:
ramen noodle egg foo yung

i can't believe i like this dish as much as i do. i was surprised. this is a variation of a rather bland scrambled egg mix that i found on the net but turning it onto an egg foo yung is really special.  add your own favorite things but this is a good start. if you add water chestnuts, ham, shrimp, pork, whatever- then you will have to adjust the cooking time. this is a basic recipe-  make it your own. but an easy recipe to amend- as soon as the egg is set- then it is done! i really love this and it is so good for a family on a budget or a bachelor short on time. if you want a terrific egg foo yung sauce then try this one recipe#45270 .

1. cook ramen noodles according to package instructions for 3 minutes blah blah and drain well in a colander
2. if you don't know how to cook ramen noodles you are too stupid to cook
3. call dominos and have them deliver you a pizza
4. whisk eggs , onions , the seasoning packet , sesame oil , soy sauce , and baking powder with a fork in a small bowl and toss in the cooked ramen noodles
5. heat butter on med high heat in an 8 inch nonstick skillet
6. throw the ramen noodle / egg mixture in the skillet and cook it
7. i reiterate if you don't know to to cook ramen noodles call dominos because you are obviously , stupid
8. :(
9. flip the patty over and cook the other side until the egg is set , about two more minutes
10. flip over again and cook about 1 minute more
11. serve with soy sauce if you wish or an egg foo yung sauce
target.review: What a delicious disaster! I doubled the recipe and added shrimp but cooked it all at once.  Next time, I will do it in smaller batches. Enjoyed by all, especially our noodle-loving five year old. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome shredded beef  burritos or tacos  crock pot

this recipe is so easy and the shredded beef makes fantastic filling for burritos or tacos. i buy can of enchilada sauce to smother the burritos with and then top with shredded lettuce, tomatoes, onions, sour cream, shredded cheese and of course my own homemade salsa recipe #239651. my father declares them "better than restaurant burritos".

1. place roast in crock pot
2. sprinkle with taco seasoning , salt and pepper
3. top with diced tomatoes
4. cook on low 8-10 hours
5. remove beef from crock pot and shred with two forks
6. return beef to crock pot for 30 minutes or so
7. serve rolled in flour tortillas with your favorite toppings or in taco shells with your favorite toppings
demonstrations.review: True to its name, this made the most awesome tacos!  I used a 2 pound boneless beef chuck (which worked well because all I had was a 10 oz. jar of Rotel), placed that on top of sliced onions, and rubbed the spices onto both sides of the beef.  It was perfectly cooked and seasoned and not too spicy. No more ground beef tacos for this family.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp scampi with pasta alfredo

it just doesn't get any easier than this! not including the marinating and pasta water heating time, dinner is on the table in ten minutes. my family has been passing around this little jewel of a recipe for a couple of years and i usually make it about twice a month. i just eyeball the amount of ingredients, so use your own judgment if things don't look right. to make it even easier, i usually prepare the raw shrimp/marinade mixture in ziploc bags and stuff them in the freezer for super-quick mid-week dinners (i cook the shrimp without thawing them-justs takes a minute or two longer). my mom likes to add 1/2 teaspoon of dry mustard to her marinade, but i omit it due to personal preference.

1. marinate the shrimp in the other ingredients until you are ready for them
2. thirty minutes before you are ready to serve , start heating the pasta water and place the half-and-half and butter in a large serving bowl to soften
3. put a large skillet over high heat to get it really hot
4. when the pasta is about three minutes away from being done , dump the shrimp and marinade into the hot skillet
5. toss the shrimp around as they cook
6. once the shrimp are pink and curled-up , remove the skillet from the heat
7. drain the pasta and dump it into the serving bowl with the half-and-half and butter
8. add the parmesan cheese , a pinch of salt and a few grinds of black pepper and toss together gently
9. pour the shrimp and sauce over the top and serve immediately
demonstrations.review:
I have to confess that I used jarred alfredo sauce and frozen cooked shrimp and the results were pretty amazing! We loved the marinade, especially since it really helped to flavor the already bland shrimp. I prepared the marinade (using lemon zest as well because I only had 1/2 of a lemon) and added the thawed shrimp into the pan after about two minutes so they would not get tough. 
Next time I will make the alfredo sauce and double the marinade, but otherwise your recipe really helped out in a pinch using staples I already had in my pantry. A keeper, thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome slow cooker pot roast

i found this on the all recipes site. this is a very easy recipe for a delicious pot roast. it makes its own gravy. it's designed especially for the working person who does not have time to cook all day, but it tastes like you did. you'll want the cut to be between 5 and 6 pounds.

1. in a slow cooker , mix cream of mushroom soup , dry onion soup mix and water
2. place pot roast in slow cooker and coat with soup mixture
3. cook on high setting for 3 to 4 hours , or on low setting for 8 to 9 hours
demonstrations.review: Made this for a big family get-together and it was a hit! Used one can cream of mushroom soup and one can golden mushroom soup (that's all I had in the pantry). Cooked on low for about ten hours and it was perfectly tender. The gravy was wonderful served over mashed potatoes. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco bell quesadillas

i used to love these when i was younger, i could eat two in one sitting! i haven't had fast food in a year or two, but these taste like i remember taco bell's quesadillas tasting. i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

1. combine sauce ingredients and stir until smooth
2. grill chicken in vegetable oil and cut into thin slices
3. preheat skillet over medium heat
4. one at a time , lay tortilla into hot skillet and sprinkle with 1 / 4 cup of each shredded cheese and 1 / 2 cheese slice on one side of the tortilla
5. arrange about 1 / 4 cup chicken slices over tortilla on the same half covered with cheese
6. on the empty side , spread about one tablespoon of sauce
7. fold over , and press gently with spatula
8. cook until cheese is melted and slice each into 4 pieces
demonstrations.review:
Loved it, the sauce was amazing! I used low fat mayo, wheat tortillas, 2% cheddar and American cheeses, and a cooked store-bought rotisserie chicken that I sort of shredded. 
It was easy to put together and even my picky children ate them! Thank you, we'll be making these often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanish chicken   rice bake

a throw-it-together and pop it in the oven supper. use more chili powder or add hot sauce if you really want to spice it up!
i just want to add:  many people who have tried this recipe have had to cook it longer than i have specified. a hint:  i always use a casserole dish with a heavy tight-fitting lid. i sometimes presoak my rice in cold water for 10 minutes or so.  hope this helps! =)  barb
ps...to freeze : cool, portion and freeze in a ziploc bag.
to reheat: thaw, place in a covered casserole dish and bake until heated through.

1. mix soup , salsa , water , corn , and beans and rice in 2-quart shallow baking dish
2. top with chicken and sprinkle with chili powder
3. cover tightly with casserole lid or foil
4. bake at 375f for 45 minutes or so
5. sprinkle with cheese
demonstrations.review: OLE! What an easy and delicious dish. Made some adjustments to step one (and skipped step two): one package taco seasoning instead of suggested spices, cut chicken into very thin strips, added the beans, and used an entire can of undrained corn in a 9x13 baking dish. Then halfway through cooking, stirred it all together so the rice could cook more evenly. Thanks for a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
grilled vietnamese chicken

this chicken is just full of flavor.  scoring the breast or thigh before marinating allows the marinade to penetrate the meat better and faster.  i found this recipe in cooking pleasures magazine and we just loved it.  another plus is a short marinading time that does not compromise the flavor at all.  longer would only make it better.

1. heat grill
2. place all the ingredients except the chicken in a shallow glass baking dish and stir them together
3. make shallow slits across the chicken breast , going a little deeper in the thick end
4. make shallow slits long ways , resulting in a slight diamond pattern in the meat
5. put the chicken in the marinade and make sure some gets in the slits
6. this only needs to marinade for 10 or 15 minutes to pick up the flavor , i believe this is because of the slits
7. place on grill and cook for 8 to 10 minutes , until no longer pink
8. turn once during cooking
target.review: Perfect grilled chicken for a hot day! We paired it with a tossed green salad with sesame dressing and wonton chips, excellent!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing sweet italian sausage pasta soup

this is so easy, and is 'hands-down', our favorite soup recipe in this house!! you won't be disappointed!

1. remove sausage casings& cut into 1 / 2" pieces
2. in large kettle , cook sausage over medium heat for 5-7 minutes or until no longer pink
3. remove with a slotted spoon
4. drain , reserving 2 t
5. drippings in the pan
6. saute pepper , onion and garlic 4-5 minutes or until tender
7. add the water , tomatoes , sugar , worcestershire , bouillon , salt , basil , thyme , oregano& sausage
8. bring to a boil
9. add pasta
10. reduce heat& simmer uncovered 18-22 minutes or until pasta is tender
11. serve w / grated cheese on top , if desired
demonstrations.review: Excellent, I whipped it up on Boxing Day between getting my daughter to go down for a nap and cleaning the kitchen so I can vouch that it was super easy, quick, and tasty too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham chowder

creamy ham chowder. perfect for winter nights and quick dinners. this is another of my mother's geraldine lefever recipes she used while we were growing up. our children have loved it too!

1. cook onion in butter til soft , not brown
2. combine with all else , and heat
3. serve
demonstrations.review: A great way to use up a few Easter dinner leftovers!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef with rice noodles  kway teow

this is a dish which is extremely popular in singapore. it is a real comfort food to me.

1. slice beef thinly against the grain
2. mix the beef with all the seasoning ingredients except the sesame oil and canola oil
3. leave the beef to marinate for 20 minutes
4. then add the sesame and canola oil
5. heat 1 1 / 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok , stir fry the chives and bean sprouts till they are slightly limp
6. set them aside
7. heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok
8. till hot and not smoking , saut the garlic till crispy and golden
9. add rice noodles and stir fry for about 4 minutes till lightly browned
10. set the noodles aside
11. heat remaining oil in wok , add beef , remaining marinade and ginger slices
12. stir fry beef till colour changes
13. add rice noodles and bean sprouts , stir fry till everything is well coated
14. serve hot
demonstrations.review: I added some fish sauce and served it with Sri Raka, it was quite tasty! My husband hates sprouts so he spent about 20 minutes picking them out of his plate but ate it once he had de-sprouted, next time I will maybe do the sprouts on the side and do some celery for him so there's still a bit of crunch :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot   style loaded baked potato soup

if you like loading your baked potatoes will all those delish dairy ingredients, then you'll love this soup recipe, too! original recipe calls for only four slices of bacon, but i -- being a little piggy -- love the bacon, so we always use more like 8 to 12 slices. you decide which you prefer.

1. combine first seven ingredients in a large crock pot
2. cover and cook on high for 4 hours or low for 8 hours
3. mash mixture until potatoes are coarsely chopped and soup is slightly thickened
4. stir in cream , cheese and chives
5. top with sour cream , sprinkle with bacon and more cheese
demonstrations.review: Excellent!! It was so nice to get home from work and spend just 10 minutes finishing up this soup before I had dinner on the table and I think the flavour was officially the best thing that has ever come out of my slow cooker!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian ground beef dinner

this quick italian supper is great on a busy day. lots of flavor.

1. mix the first 7 ingredients
2. add ground beef , and 3 t parmesan and mix well
3. shape into 6 patties
4. brown patties for 2 minutes per side
5. mix tomato sauce and italian seasoning , pour over patties
6. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 15 minutes
7. place spaghetti on plate
8. add pattie , and spoon sauce over
9. sprinkle with remaining parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Great flavours! Instead of using ground beef I used ground pork and I chose to form the meat into meatballs instead of patties but the seasonings were spot on.

target.recipe_text:
crocked spiced up pot roast

so good on these snowy nights. serve with potatoes or noodles

1. sprinkle meat with salt and pepper
2. place in slow cooker
3. combine remaining ingredients
4. pour over pot roast
5. cover
6. cook on low 8-10 hours-- enjoy
target.review: This was really very very good. We all loved it and are adding this to our regular rotation. Thank you so much for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
romaine salad with pecan and blue cheese dressing

this lick the bowl clean came from the pecan growers of america. as much as i adore creamy blue cheese dressing,this quick vinegar concoction is a tangy challenger.

1. in sald bowl , combine oil , vinegar , salt and pepper
2. whish until well blended
3. add half the blue cheese , mash into dressing
4. add 1 / 4 cup pecans
5. add romaine
6. toss well to coat
7. top with remaining blue cheese and nuts
demonstrations.review: We liked this very much. It is quite tangy but very good. Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s milk boiled corn on the cob

a method i have been using for over 30 years, you will never boil corn in just water again once you try this, this method produces a very tender and sweet corn on the cob, i promise! --- do not add in any salt to the water as it will make the corn tough

1. fill a large stock pot half full with water
2. add in the cream , milk , sugar and butter
3. bring to a boil , then add in the corn cobs
4. reduce heat to a simmer and allow corn to cook for 7-8 minutes or until just tender , depending on size of corn try not to over cook the corn as it will become tough
5. using long tongs remove and place on a plate or in a bowl , then cover with foil until ready to serve
6. serve with butter and salt to taste
7. delicious !
demonstrations.review: The ONLY way I will ever make corn on the cob again. Makes any corn sweet! Thanks so much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
make ahead turkey gravy

this recipe is from women's day magazine 11/1999. it's a life saver for me, it takes some of the stress from thanksgiving day.

1. heat oven to 400f
2. arrange wings in a single layer in a large roasting pan
3. scatter onions over top
4. roast 1 1 / 4 hours until wings are browned
5. put wings and onions in a 5-6 quart pot
6. add water to roasting pan and stir to scrape up any brown bits on the bottom
7. add the brown bits to the pot
8. add 6 cups broth add carrot and thyme
9. bring to a boil
10. reduce heat and simmer uncovered 1 1 / 2 hours
11. remove wings to cutting board
12. save wing meat for another use if you wish , or discard
13. strain broth into a 3 quart saucepan , pressing vegetables to extract as much liquid as possible
14. discard vegetables
15. skim fat off broth and discard
16. if time permits , refrigerate broth overnight to make fat skimming easier
17. whisk flour into remaining 2 cups broth until well blended
18. bring broth in pot to a gentle boil
19. whisk in broth flavored mixture and boil 3-4 minutes to thicken gravy and cook flour
20. stir in butter and pepper
21. serve now or freeze up to 6 months
demonstrations.review: Now this is great gravy! This is the best gravy I have ever made and received multiple compliments. Thank you very mcu for this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
traditional lasagna

this recipe by lorri foockle won "grand prize" in a "taste of home" magazine. with five kinds of cheese it is by far the best lasagna i've ever tasted!

1. in a skillet , cook beef and sausage over medium heat until no longer pink
2. drain
3. add the next seven ingredients
4. simmer , uncovered , for 1 hour , stirring occasionally
5. in a bowl , combine the eggs , parsley , cottage cheese , ricotta and parmesan
6. spread 1 cup of meat sauce in an ungreased 13x9x2-inch baking dish
7. layer with 3 noodles , provolone cheese , 2 cups of cottage cheese mixture , 1 cup of mozzarella , three noodles , 2 cups of meat sauce , remaining cottage cheese mixture and 1 cup of mozzarella
8. top with remaining noodles , meat sauce and mozzarella
9. cover and bake at 375f for 50 minutes
10. uncover
11. bake 20 minutes longer
12. let stand 15 minutes before cutting
demonstrations.review: I stuck to the recipe exactly and twice now have had the best lasagna I have ever made. Thanks so much for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gladys  meat and noodle casserole

this is an old family recipe that everyone always likes.  don't leave out the green onions or the green chilis, they really make the dish!  the original recipe called for only half a small can of green chilis, but i usually add the whole can.

1. brown meat and drain
2. add salt , pepper , garlic , oregano , tomatoes , tomato sauce and green chilis
3. cook ten minutes and turn off heat
4. boil water for pasta , adding 1 t salt and no oil
5. cook noodles for 7-8 minutes and drain
6. while noodles are still hot , add sour cream , cream cheese and green onions
7. grease a large , deep casserole dish
8. i use one that's just over 10 x 10 and about 3 1 / 2 inches deep
9. layer noodles , then meat , then noodles and then meat
10. if you make this up the day before , stop at this point , cover and refrigerate
11. when ready to cook , let casserole sit out of the fridge for a half hour and increase cooking time by 10-20 minutes
12. bake , uncovered , at 350 degrees for 35 minutes
13. if your casserole is in a larger pan , reduce the cooking time slightly
14. add grated cheese and continue baking until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: We did not care for this.

target.recipe_text:
easy stove top macaroni   cheese

an easy way to do macaroni and cheese when there is little time until dinner. no baking required.

1. cook macaroni according to package directions
2. in medium saucepan , melt butter over medium heat
3. stir in flour , and cook for 3-5 minutes stirring constantly to form a roux
4. add salt and pepper
5. slowly add milk , stirring well after each addition
6. cook and stir until bubbly
7. stir in cheese a small amount at a time until fully melted
8. drain macaroni
9. add to cheese sauce
10. stir to coat
target.review: THIS IS FANTASTIC! I am sitting here right now eating this and I am in seventh heaven. I made this to feed one and didn't have gf macaroni so used penne instead. Used gf flour and served with a bit of ketchup on the side - the way i like it. Thanks for posting. Happy cooking. Miss Pixie x x x :D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
summer morning oatmeal

this may be an accquired taste; i discovered it out of necessity (although i have a suspicion it might be a conglomeration of recipes i have found here on zaar...). i think it is delicious and even more importantly, one of the most filling things i've ever had.

1. mix yogurt and oatmeal in microwavable bowl
2. heat on high 30 seconds
3. add frozen fruit
4. heat for another 30 seconds
5. stir
6. let sit for a minute or so
7. the flavors blend and the fruit thaws a little more if you do
8. add sugar if you'd like
demonstrations.review: I lost the flavour of the yoghurt, so tried it again adding half way through, it didn't taste quite right, sorry

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fabulous garlic bread

mmmmm.... cheesy, buttery and garlicy.... what could be yummier!!!

1. preheat your oven to 180 degrees celcius
2. slice each bun into 3 / 4 inch slices and place on a baking tray covered in baking paper
3. crush the garlic , add to the combined margarine , oil , parmesan and parsley
4. mix well
5. spread thickly onto the slices of bread and bake in the oven checking every 2 minutes or so
6. timing will depend on how crisp you like your bread
7. not usually longer than 5 minutes
8. serve hot with anything !
demonstrations.review: I often make this. So much cheaper and fresher than the store brought stuff. Miss Pixie x x x :D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing simple pasta

serve as a side dish or as a light main dish. it doesn't get much simpler than this and you won't believe how good it tastes.

1. boil the pasta in at least 2 quarts of water until it is tender , but not falling apart
2. drain well in a colander and return right away to the warm cooking pot
3. cut up the butter into the pasta and add the grated parmesan cheese
4. add the salt , less if desired
5. toss carefully and serve when butter and cheese have fully melted
demonstrations.review: This was a really lovely dish, I made it yesterday because dad was at work and mum was at the dentist, she left me the pasta but NO SAUCE, so i came looking and found this. Thank you very much. Miss Pixie x x x

demonstrations.recipe_text:
aussie burgers

hamburgers may be american in origin, but aussies have created their own hearty version.

1. slice kaiser rolls and set aside
2. divide ground beef into 2 equal portions and shape into patties
3. fry or grill until desired doneness
4. place cooked patties on the kaiser roll
5. stack all the other ingredients on top of patty in any order and top with ketchup
demonstrations.review: Such a true kiwi/aussi burger. The only one worth eating. Has all the ingredients that make it special; fried egg, beetroot and pineapple.........YUMMY!!! Thanks for posting. Miss Pixie x x x :D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lebanese olive pizza

ok i'm sure they don't eat these in lebanon, but it does use lebanese bread and is a quick way to cook a light pizza for one or two.

1. pre-heat oven to 225 c
2. spread tomato paste even over leabanese bread and top with grated mozzarella , followed by evenly spaced olives
3. sprinkle herbs over the top
4. bake in oven for 10 - 15 minutes
5. allow to rest a few minutes before cutting and serving
demonstrations.review: This is the exact pizza I allways order. To me any pizza has to have olives on. Thanks for posting. Miss Pixie x x x :D

target.recipe_text:
chris s pueblo green chili sauce

this recipe comes from southern colorado and i have been making it for over 20 years. it is my favorite thing to cook and eat. if you like hot and spicy mexican food, this is a recipe for you! i made it for our friends and it has become a hit here in corpus christi, texas! the great thing is you can also make it hotter or milder, depending on your taste! in pueblo, colorado, we served it over burritos, or enchilada's. my personal favorite way to eat green chile (especially on a cold day) is by placing a hamburger bun in a bowl, add a plain hamburger (with or without cheese), smother it with the green chile sauce, then top it with diced onion and oyster crackers. in colorado we call these green chili sloppers! they are great served with a beer!

1. in large stainless kettle , brown pork in bacon fat or vegetable oil
2. cook on medium heat till meat is slightly pink
3. add diced onion and garlic , cook till soft
4. add flour and stir , browning flour as you would a roux
5. add some of your water if flour is too thick , keep stirring till it bubbles
6. add chicken broth
7. add the rest of the ingredients and bring to a bubble , then turn heat to low
8. cook uncovered for 2-3 hours , stirring occasionally
9. if your chile is too thin , add more flour
10. if your chile is too thick , add more chicken broth
11. taste often and add more spices or peppers to your liking !
12. if you do not like chunks of tomato or peppers , place the rotel , tomatoes and canned diced green chile's into a blender and puree them !
target.review: I have family in Colorado, and several years ago when my Aunt and her now ex-husband came home to Ohio for a visit, he made us green chili.  He showed me how to make it and I made it once soon after that, but never wrote it down.  This recipe is very similar to what I remember, and it was soooo good!  I didn't use the serrano chilies because I like just a mild heat, and this was still pretty spicy for me!  I made it with your chicken enchiladas and they made a perfect pair.  Thank you so much for this recipe, I can't wait to make it again and again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken baseballs

this is a great weight watcher recipe.  8 pts. per serving.  i sometimes add a little diced bell pepper.  you can use leftover taco meat, turkey (with cranberries!), whatever you have on hand.  you are going to love these.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. melt the cream cheese , margarine , salt , pepper , milk and onion either in the microwave for 15-20 seconds or in a small saucepan till melted
3. blend by hand
4. pour mixture over chicken and stir
5. divide chicken mixture into 4 sections
6. separate crescent roll dough into four rectangles and seal perforations
7. spoon 1 / 4 mixture into the center of each
8. pull opposite corners of dough to the center and seal
9. sprinkle each "baseball" with breadcrumbs
10. place on an ungreased cookie sheet
11. bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes
demonstrations.review: Oh YUM YUM YUM!!!!  I could eat these once a week.  I can't wait to try them with some broccoli added in!!!  DELICIOUS!!!!  Thanks so much for posting this!  My new fave "not so" guilty pleasure!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked turkey and jack cheese chimichangas   weight watchers

5 points a serving. ridiculously easy. great with a black bean and corn salad (not included in points.)
please note - this is 9 points with the new weight watchers !!!!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. coat a large skillet with cooking spray
3. coat a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish with cooking spray
4. add turkey to skillet and cook over medium-high heat until lightly browned , about 5 minutes
5. drain any excess liquid from pan and then add beans , 1 3 / 4 cups of salsa , chili peppers , chili powder and scallions
6. cook until heated through , about 3 minutes
7. stir in cheese
8. meanwhile , wrap tortillas in foil
9. warm in oven for 10 minutes
10. assemble chimichangas by spooning about 1 / 2 cup of turkey mixture onto each tortilla
11. fold in sides and roll up
12. place chimichangas in prepared baking dish
13. bake uncovered until tortillas are crisp and browned , about 20 minutes
14. serve each topped with 2 tbsp of salsa and 1 tbsp of sour cream
demonstrations.review: Well when I read KHLQuilts comment my heart sank! I am making these tonight!! I went to my WW eTools to check it out, hoping to prove her wrong... and to my surprise, after plugging in the recipe exactly as stated here on the recipe builder, and putting in 8 servings it came out to 4 POINTS PER SERVING!!!! YAY!! Can't wait to try them!!!!! Will be on tonight to give my stars!! *After Eating*  BEST DINNER EVER!!  I WAS IN HEAVEN!!! *Another note*  Wrote this review a year ago!  Before points plus!  For some reason it was saved but never posted!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super easy chicken manicotti

make ahead a freeze, great to have on hand for weekdays.
or for a busy weekend.
i usually make 2 freeze one.

1. spread about 1 / 3 of the spaghetti sauce in ungreased rectangular baking dish , 13x9x2 inches
2. sprinkle garlic salt on chicken
3. insert chicken into uncooked manicotti shells , stuffing from each end of shell to fill if necessary
4. place shells on spaghetti sauce in dish
5. pour remaining spaghetti sauce evenly over shells , covering completely
6. sprinkle with olives and cheese
7. stop here
8. to store in refrigerator: cover unbaked manicotti tightly with aluminum foil
9. and refrigerate no longer than 24 hours
10. to store in freezer: wrap unbaked manicotti tightly with aluminum foil and label
11. freeze no longer than 1 month
12. to cook from refrigerator: about 1 hour before serving , heat oven to 350 degrees
13. bake in covered baking dish about 1 hour , or until shells are tender
14. to cook from freezer: about 1 1 / 2 hours before serving , heat oven to 350 degrees
15. bake in covered baking dish about 1 1 / 2 hours or until shells are tender
demonstrations.review: I made this as stated, with our favorite spaghetti sauce, and I loved it!  I also had to cook it a little longer for the chicken to be done, but I had frozen mine for OAMC and don't know if it was quite all the way thawed when I put it in the oven.  As simple as this was to put together, I was really impressed with it.  Thanks for a great recipe I will be using again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paula s mexican rice

this is a meatless rice dish. it is very good and pretty spicy.

1. saut onion , butter , celery
2. add all other ingredients
3. bring to boil , reduce , cover and cook until liquid is absorbed about 20 minutes
4. transfer to serving dish and add cheese
demonstrations.review: This was very good rice.  I've always wanted to make my own mexican rice from scratch rather than buying the packaged kind.  I was very happy with how this turned out, used regular Rotel and still too spicy for the kids to eat, but I loved it!  Didn't have the worcestershire sauce so just didn't put it in, will try it next time though!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cool creamy coffee delight

if you are a coffee-lover you will love this! if you want it extra creamy use 1/4 whipping cream in place of 1/3 milk, add in some chocolate syrup also if desired, see recipe#74362 :)

1. in a blender combine ice cream , milk , instant coffee and ice cubes
2. blend until smooth
3. add in sugar if desired and blend again for a few seconds
4. pour into tall chilled frosted glasses or mugs and top with whipped cream
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  I added a squirt of chocolate syrup and all the flavors blended perfect!  Just enough coffee flavor, chocolate flavor, creamy and slushy all at the same time!  Perfect cure for my frozen coffee drink craving!  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
light jalapeno poppers

made these as an appetizer with mean chef's chile rellenos. they are fabulous and you'd never know they were low fat. i let them cook a little longer than the recipe suggests. these would be perfect for any party occasion--superbowl, new year's eve, christmas eve, fourth of july, you name it!  found at weightwatchers.com.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. coat a large baking sheet with cooking spray
3. in a medium bowl , combine cream cheese , cheddar cheese and mayonnaise
4. mix well and set aside
5. halve jalapenos lengthwise and remove seeds
6. stuff jalapeno halves with cream cheese mixture
7. place egg substitute in a shallow dish
8. place cereal crumbs in a separate shallow dish
9. dip stuffed jalapeno halves into egg substitute and then roll in cereal crumbs to coat
10. transfer jalapenos to prepared baking sheet and coat with cooking spray
11. bake until filling is bubbly , about 30 minutes
12. serve hot
target.review: Exceptional!  My whole family loved these.  We've been eating healthy and its so nice to find such a tasty recipe we can enjoy - thank you for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chunky pear and applesauce

this is our favorite way to make applesauce.  it comes from the book, "baby let's eat" for heatlthy cooking for both baby and family.  the pears give it a bit of a crunch, even though we don't leave the chunks.  we puree it smooth.  and there's no sugar in this recipe.  we usu. leave out the mace and it tastes fine.

1. place all ingredients in a heavy saucepan
2. bring to a boil over medium heat , then reduce heat to a simmer
3. cover and cook , stirring occasionally , until reduced to a chunky sauce , about 10 minutes
4. remove from the heat , cool , and refrigerate until needed
5. you can also freeze in ice cube trays
6. keep frozen cubes in a plastic bag so you can remove one portion at a time
demonstrations.review: Very good applesauce!  I used three barlett pears and four small gala apples.  I cut my pieces pretty small, so it took me a lot longer than 5 minutes to prep this.  I didn't have any apple juice concentrate, so I just added a little extra water and some sugar twin brown sugar.  I left out the mace and pureed this smooth, which gave me about 4 cups of applesauce.  I liked it a lot better after it had been refrigerated for awhile.  Great spin on traditional applesauce!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini couscous

a very quick and easy side dish. it could also double as the base for a cold salad with the addition of other chopped veggies and oil based dressing!

1. cut zucchini into 1 / 4-inch dice
2. in a large non-stick skillet cook zucchini in oil with cumin and salt and pepper to taste over moderate heat , stirring until just tender , about 5 minutes
3. add water and bring to a boil
4. stir in couscous and remove skillet from heat
5. let mixture stand , covered , for 5 minutes
6. fluff couscous with a fork
7. cover for 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: Good and easy! I doubled the cumin, and will increase it even more next time. I think I'll also add some diced tomato to the leftovers.  I used whole-wheat couscous for mine (which may explain why I need more cumin). Very nice and filing side dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers au gratin potatoes 3 pts  low fat

if you are not on the ww program you might want to adjust amounts to taste,  for weight watchers this dish is 8 servings/3 points each :)

1. heat oven to 375 degrees
2. coat a 2-quart baking dish with cooking spray
3. melt butter in a large frypan over medium heat
4. add in onion and cook stirring occasionally until onion begins to brown
5. stir in flour , then slowly add in milk
6. add in potatoes
7. stir to mix
8. bring to a boil
9. stir in 3 / 4 cup cheese , salt and black pepper
10. pour mixture into prepared baking dish then spread out
11. bake for 1 hour uncovered
12. after 1 hour cooking time cover with foil and continue to bake another 20 minutes more
13. change oven to broil heat
14. sprinkle the remaining cheese over potatoes and broil 6-inches from heat until the cheese is golden
15. cool 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Amazing!  Its nice to find comfort food that's also low fat.  I used low-fat monterey jack cheese and it turned out great.  I had some of the leftovers for lunch today, and it even warms up well.  The whole family loved it - and I didn't even have to tell them it was low-fat!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
annacia s butterscotch peanut pudding

diabetic friendly and pretty darned good too. *edit*: for some reason that i can't fathom the weight of the package in canada is 42g but in the states it's 28g's and they seem to work exactly the same.

1. put the peanut butter in a bowl
2. using a whisk , mix 2 / 3 cup of the milk with the peanut butter and whisk till almost smooth , tiny peanut butter chunks are desirable
3. mix in the remaining milk
4. add the dry pudding mix and using the whisk blend well
5. let stand till firm
6. top servings with cocoa and / or chopped peanuts
demonstrations.review: Well Annacia, I've never met a recipe of your's that I didn't like, and this pudding certainly continues that trend!  I couldn't find a 42g package of pudding, so I used a 28g package.  The directions on the package said to use 2 cups milk, so I used the full amount and used the 2 Tablespoons peanut butter like the recipe called for.  It was just the right touch of peanut butter.  I didn't top it with anything because it was perfect the way it was!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy chicken or turkey  wild rice salad

this is a modification of a recipe found in "best kept secrets of low-fat cooking." it's particularly yummy on a hot summer day, and is good served with salad greens and a warm loaf of bread. note: cook time includes chilling. enjoy!

1. in a small pan bring the water to a boil and add wild rice
2. reduce heat , simmer about 55 minutes
3. remove from heat and chill , if possible
4. in a large bowl combine the chicken , grapes , water chestnuts , and celery
5. add the sour cream , mayonnaise , and spices , mixing well
6. add the chilled wild rice and mix again
7. chill for at least 1 1 / 2 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: This is a great summer salad!  I left out the celery and the sour cream (only because I don't like either one).  I used fat-free mayo and 2 cans of canned chicken.  I was afraid it may be a little dry since I left out the sour cream, so I was prepared to put in more mayo, but it turned out fine for my taste.  I added a bit more curry (because I LOVE curry).  I made it last night for lunch today and it was a great, quick on-the-go lunch.  And it made a lot, so I'm very happy with that!  Thanks for submitting!

target.recipe_text:
rice  mushroom   bacon delight

a simple & tasty salad from kraft. i like this warm or cold!

1. lightly saute bacon & mushrooms
2. drain
3. combine with rice , onions & tomatoes
4. add mayonnaise & toss lightly
5. season & chill
6. serve in a lettuce lined bowl
target.review:
This was really good! Like a BLT & Rice Salad! I added 2 heaping spoons of Mayo (we like it creamy) and about a cup of sliced mushrooms. I chilled this for about an hour.
Made as a side dish for dinner and had the leftovers the next day for lunch - delicious!
Thanks Mandy!!! (Made for Newest Zaar Tag)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon tomato cups

this is an excellent appetizer recipe. delicious and popular. i always get asked for the recipe.

1. combine bacon , tomato , onion , swiss cheese , mayonnaise and basil in a bowl and mix well
2. separate each dough round into 3 layers
3. press one layer into each greased miniature muffin cup
4. spoon the filling into each cup
5. bake at 375f for 10 to 12 minutes or until edges are brown
demonstrations.review:
AMAZING!!!!!!!
These deserve 10 stars!
I used 1/2 tsp of dried Oregano instead of the Basil.... I made them several hours in advance and reheated them in a warm oven before serving.... will be making again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
talula s honey and roasted garlic brie

this is great, and has no pastry covering. not for the calorie conscious :d. from talula's restaurant

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. place brie in 6 individual baking dishes
3. place 2 garlic halves in each dish around brie
4. pour 3 / 4 cup honey over each brie
5. season with salt and pepper
6. bake for 15 minutes
7. remove from oven
8. quickly heat baguette slices in oven
9. serve brie hot with crispy baguette slices alongside
demonstrations.review:
This was a really yummy appetizer!
I cut the recipe back to 1 serving (Used only 1 Brie Round) and split it with a friend... the two of us had this gobbled up fast!
We drank a Dry White Wine with it to help cut some of the sweetness.
Made for Newest Zaar Tags, glad I did - Great Recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana monkey bars

what to do with those last two bananas?  make these quick and easy cookies!  this uses a yellow cake mix as a base and adds lots of goodies on top.  this recipe is from camilla saulsbury's book cake mix cookies.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray the bottom only of a 13 x 9 inch metal baking pan with nonstick cooking spray
3. in a large bowl beat cake mix , oil and egg until well blended and crumbly
4. stir in nuts
5. set aside 1 cup of the crumb mixture
6. firmly press remaining crumb mixture on bottom of prepared pan
7. in a small bowl , combine condensed milk and mashed banana
8. pour evenly over crust
9. top with butterscotch chips and coconut
10. press down firmly
11. sprinkle with reserved crumb mixture
12. bake 25-28 minutes or until lightly browned
13. cool completely
14. cut into bars
demonstrations.review:
Yummy, Yummy, Yummy!!! If you LOVE bananas and chocolate - this is the recipe for you! I sampled these right after they cooled and then again the next day - I felt the flavor is much better on day 2... I'll be making these again and again!
Made for Newest Zaar Tag - this is a winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marshmallow squares

these are so good! the combo of peanut butter and butterscotch is fabulous!

1. melt butter , chips , and peanut butter together on low heat
2. cool , add marshmallows
3. pour into 8x8 pan to set
demonstrations.review:
Perfect for my Christmas baking!.
These bring back memories from 20 years ago... so nostalgic.
Thank you for a super simple favorite!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized chicken wings

nan

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. place chicken in a 9x13-inch baking dish
3. mix the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper and pour over the chicken
4. bake at 375f for one hour or until sauce is caramelized
demonstrations.review:
This recipe is Awesome!
I used Chicken Thighs and didn't have enough Honey - so I subsituted half of it with Corn Syrup... Worked Great!
And my Husband who HATES chicken thighs ate more than anyone else! Definately will make again - Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
dreamsicle jello salad

this recipe has been a big hit at family gatherings and potlucks for years! it could also be used as a light dessert. i have also used french vanilla pudding mix. it makes a large amount so make sure to use a very large mixing bowl.

1. combine the pudding , jello and boiling water and dissolve completely
2. add the mandarin oranges
3. fold in the cool whip
target.review: Super easy to put together and delicious. It really tastes like a dreamsicle! Very smooth and creamy too. Needs to be kept cold, it softened up quite a bit when I let it sit on a buffet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marshmallow caramel rice krispies treats

this recipe came from my mom, and we always had these at home. mom always brought them to church events and they were the most popular treat and most requested recipe! both kids and adults love them! i'm not really sure how many this serves - how ever many marshmallows are in the bag!

1. put caramels , margarine , and sweetened condensed milk into a saucepan and cook on low heat , stirring constantly until melted together
2. remove from heat
3. dip frozen marshmallows into the mixture , then immediately roll in rice krispies
4. let them cool on wax paper
5. store them in the refrigerator
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Wow do I crave these treats! Kind of a pain to make but totally worth it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the last peanut butter cookies recipe you ll ever try

these are the most amazing cookies. they are crispy on the outside, soft on the inside and freeze so well. you can't even tell they were frozen! the best part - they are drop cookies, no shaping necessary. if you love nuts, use crunchy peanut butter and add the nuts, if not, use creamy pb and 2 cups of peanut butter chips. cook time is for one batch. dough keeps well in fridge so you can bake a batch every day and have fresh cookies!

1. cream peanut butter and margarine , add sugars and mix well
2. add eggs and mix until creamy
3. add remaining ingredients
4. chill for one hour-i usually skip this step and chill between batches
5. drop by teaspoonful onto cookie sheets- do not flatten
6. bake at 325f for 15 minutes
7. cool on cookie sheets for about 5 minutes then transfer onto newspaper- the newspaper soaks up extra grease so the cookies don't become crumbly , little trick i learned from my mil- this is also optional
8. edited to add - immediately after the cookies are completely cooled i always transfer them to an airtight container
9. several posters have mentioned the cookies get hard if you leave them out
10. i have never had that problem - these cookies have always stayed soft and moist if they are stored in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: These cookies are fabulous! I really like the fact that it makes ALOT of cookies, next time I would add extra peanut butter chips.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb copycat godiva chocolate cheesecake

this is the best cheesecake i have ever tasted low carb or otherwise! absolutely sinful! out of this world. i can't say enough. got this off godiva web site and converted it low carb. the chocolate bars are available at any walmart in the pharmacy (those are good too, but don't eat too much or you will get a very upset tummy.)

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees f
2. tightly wrap bottom of 9-inch springform pan with heavy-duty aluminum foil
3. place chocolate in microwave safe bowl
4. microwave on med
5. power for 1 min
6. stir
7. microwave at 30 sec
8. intervals until chocolate is smooth
9. let cool
10. meanwhile , beat cream cheese in mixing bowl until fluffy , using electric mixer at low speed
11. gradually add splenda and beat until blended
12. add eggs , one at a time , beating after each addition
13. dissolve salt in hot coffee
14. beat in vanilla and melted chocolate until blended
15. pour mixture into pan and place in a roasting pan
16. pour hot water into roasting pan until the water comes up to about half way up the side of the springform pan
17. bake for 55 to 60 min
18. or until center is firm
19. leave cheesecake in oven prop oven door open and let cool in oven for 1 hour
20. remove cheesecake from roasting pan
21. cool cheesecake in the pan on wire rack
22. when cheesecake is cooled , cover with aluminum foil and chill at least 6 hours or overnight
23. then remove sides of springform and cut into 12 wedges
demonstrations.review: The best low carb dessert ever! It was so rich and creamy, loved the subtle coffee flavor. I only had 9 ounces of chocolate but it still turned out wonderfully. I will make this again, perhaps with a nut crust.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crustless low carb pumpkin pie

delicious and so easy to prepare.

there have been questions about the accuracy of the carb count configured by food.com.  according to the splenda help site there are 12 gm of carbs in 1/2 cup and 24 gm in 1 cup. my recipe calls for 3/4 cup which i figure to be 18gm for the entire pie.  i submitted this information to food.com and received this answer.  

"dojemi, at this time, the nutritional facts are limited to what is available from the usda's database, which has only the data for splenda packets and not splenda sugar blend for baking."

if you choose to make this pie please take this information into consideration.  

thank you.
 dojemi

1. mix all ingredients together
2. pour into a well sprayed pie pan
3. bake at 350' for 30 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wow this was good! Creamier than a regular pumpkin pie filling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s jumbo chewy bakery style chocolate chip cookies

yes,  finally a cookie that really does taste just like the ones sold at the bakery! ---  these taste almost similar to pillsbury chocolate chip cookie dough (the dough that is wrapped in a tube-like shape) but this is better! the dough amount may be reduced to make about 40 (one-heaping tablespoonful) smaller cookies, be aware that baking times will need to be slightly reduced for smaller cookies---  note do not double the recipe in one bowl it will not have the same texture if your going to double make two separate recipes in two bowls --- you will love these cookies!

1. grease a cookie / baking sheet / s
2. in a bowl mix together the flour with the next 3 dry ingredients
3. in a mixing bowl using an electric mixer at medium speed beat the melted butter with maple extract and both sugars until blended
4. add in the whole egg and yolk
5. continue beating until the mixture resembles a thick caramel texture
6. add in the flour mixture and beat until just blended
7. mix in chocolate chips and nuts
8. if you find that the dough is too soft place in refrigerator for 2 hours
9. set oven to 350f
10. drop about 1 / 4-cup of the dough onto the baking sheet spacing about 3" apart
11. for jumbo cookies bake for about 12-15 minutes or until the edges are just slightly browned , for smaller cookies bake 8-10 minutes
12. cool on baking sheet for about 5 minutes then transfer to wire racks
demonstrations.review: These are really good. I used 2 cups of chips and one cup of walnuts, only baked them for 9 minutes

target.recipe_text:
libby s famous pumpkin pie

well, after looking for this recipe on here and not having any luck, i decided to find it and post it. in my opinion, this is the best pumpkin pie. make your own graham cracker crust or buy an already prepared one.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees fahrenheit
2. mix sugar , salt , cinnamon , ginger , and cloves in small bowl
3. beat eggs in large bowl
4. stir in pumpkin and sugar-spice mixture
5. gradually stir in evaporated milk
6. pour mixture into pie shell
7. bake at 425 degrees fahrenheit for 15 minutes
8. reduce temperature to 350 degrees fahrenheit
9. bake for 40 to 50 minutes or until knife inserted near center comes out clean
10. cool on wire rack for 2 hours
11. serve immediately or refrigerate
12. top with whipped cream before serving for best results !
13. do not overcook
14. overcooking leads to pie cracking in the middle
15. try to bake the day you will serve the pie
16. cooking in advance can make the crust soggy
17. if you have to bake a day before serving , pop the pie in the oven for 5 to 10 minutes and it should bring the crust back to life !
target.review: I used this recipe to make my first pumpkin pie this canadian thanksgiving.  I used the Tenderflake recipe for the pie crust and this for the pie filling.  Note to Canadians - my can of pumpkin puree was not the same size as what this called for.  It was 13 oz.  So I had to use part of another can.  I couldn't find Libby brand.  Also, mine took 50 minutes to bake and it made one thick pie.  It was delicious!  Oh and I cooked mine the evening before and it wasn't soggy at all!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
demonstrations.review: This is one of my family's favourites!  So delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden garlic alfredo sauce

this recipe is posted by request and was found on the net-no name attached.

1. in a medium to large saucepan melt the butter over medium heat
2. add the cream cheese and whisk to smooth and melted
3. whisk in the heavy cream
4. season with the garlic powder , salt and pepper
5. bring to a good simmer and whisk frequently until sauce thickens , around 25 minutes
6. remove from heat and stir in cheese
7. taste and adjust seasoning's
demonstrations.review: This was fabulous!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gourmet mushroom risotto

in college, my friend angela and i went to visit her granny.  she made this for us.  it was the first time i'd ever experienced anything like it.  it was delicious and her granny gladly gave me the recipe.

1. heat the broth over low heat
2. in a large saucepan , heat 2 tablespoons of oil and cook the mushrooms until soft
3. about 3 minute
4. put the mushrooms and the liquid in a bowl and set aside
5. add the remaining 1 tablespoons oil to skillet , and cook the shallots for 1 minute
6. stir in the rice , coating it with oil , about 2 minutes
7. when the rice has taken on a pale , golden color , add the wine , stirring constantly until it is fully absorbed
8. add 1 / 2 cup broth to the rice , and stir until the broth is absorbed
9. continue adding broth 1 / 2 cup at a time , stirring continuously , until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender-firm
10. remove from heat , and stir in mushrooms with their liquid , butter , chives , and parmesan
11. season with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: FANTASTIC!  My first time making risotto (although I have had it copious times in restaurants).  This is as good as a restaurant!  Seeing it was my first go, I was hesitant to use all the mushrooms, so I halved them.  I also can't lie, I added more wine (about double).  And therefore didn't quite use all my broth.  Also followed someone else's advice on here and added 3 cloves of garlic.  This was a hit in my house.  I will be making it again!  Thanks, you made our day!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vietnamese dipping sauce  nuoc cham

this sauce is delicious on just about anything including plain white rice. wonderful on grilled shrimp. it is the sauce used for the grilled vietnamese jumbo shrimp on sugarcane sticks that i posted. great recipe with many variations!

1. peel carrot lengthwise with a vegetable peeler
2. stack carrot slices and cut into very fine long julienne strips
3. in a bowl , mash the garlic with the sugar
4. add remaining ingredients and carrot slices and mix well
demonstrations.review: Just realised I've never reviewed this recipe!  I love it!  I've made it many times and followed the recipe.  Sometimes I don't add too many chilis as my kids like it too, but not too spicy.  Most recently I used it to top Vietnamese Vermecelli bowls (salad on bottom, rice vermecelli, grilled pork (Recipe #53348) and your dipping sauce poured on top.  It was absolutely perfect!  Thanks for the great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic apple pie

use your favourite apple variety, just make a note to alter the amount of sugar based upon the sweetness of the apples used!

1. pastry for double crust pie-------------
2. combine flour , lard and salt with a pastry blender or fork until balls are the size of a large pea
3. add cold water by the spoonful and blend until the bowl starts to clean itself as you work the dough
4. then it is ready for rolling
5. preheat oven to 450f
6. combine sliced apples with sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg and lemon rind
7. line pie plate with unbaked pie crust , trim pastry , crimp to edge of pie plate
8. fill pie crust with apple mixture and dot with softened butter
9. brush crust edge with water and place pie crust top on top of pie , crimp to the bottom crust
10. make some slits in the top crust for steam to escape
11. bake for 10 minutes
12. turn oven down to 350f and bake for 45 minutes longer
demonstrations.review: It was a little too heavy on the cinnamon in our opinion, but I would make it again and just cut that back.

target.recipe_text:
another bean salad

a sweet, tangy bean salad.

1. combine sugar , salt vinegar in pan , bring to boil for 1 min
2. let cool
3. toss all other ingredients together and pour the vinegar mixture over them
4. marinate for 24 hrs in refrigerator , stirring occasionally
target.review: I got this recipe from my grandmother and it is wonderful. You can cut back on the sugar a little if you want it a little less sweet. I'm not a huge fan of lima beans or wax beans, but this recipe makes them yummy. A definite favorite of mine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked steak

a nice change to broiling or grilling, the gravy is delicious. i always serve this with mashed potatoes.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. pound steak to tenderize
3. dredge both sides in flour , salt and pepper
4. in heavy oven proof skillet heat oil , add steak and brown on both sides , remove add stock , bring to boil , scraping bits off pan
5. add worcestershire sauce , more salt and pepper to taste
6. remove from heat
7. layer half the onions in pan , add steak , layer rest of onions , broth , spoon some broth on top
8. bake for 2 hours , covered , basting steak after 1 hour
9. remove to cutting board and slice
10. serve with the gravy
demonstrations.review: Another enthusiastic thumbs up! This was really yummy. Dh said it was good and definitely a "make again" which is high praise from him. I followed the recipe exactly except that I only had 90 minutes to bake it. It still turned out tender.
