The only thing I would do differently next time would be to add more broth half way through the baking time. We really didn't have enough leftover to use as gravy. Thanks for sharing such a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttery yeast rolls

these are the absolute best dinner rolls. they are light and fluffy and buttery. the dough can also be shaped in many other ways, so use your imagination. makes awesome cinnamon rolls too!

1. place all ingredients except the 1 / 4 cup butter into bread machine in the order recommended by the manufacturer
2. select the dough cycle and start machine
3. shape dough into 20 to 24 balls and place in buttered pan
4. melt the 1 / 4 cup butter and brush it over the tops of rolls , saving the excess for brushing on after baking
5. cover and let rise in a warm place about 1 hour , or until double in bulk
6. bake at 375 degrees f for 15 to 18 minutes
7. brush baked rolls with remaining butter
demonstrations.review: These rolls were so good! They tasted like some of the rolls I have gotten in restaurants. This is for sure my new roll recipe. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the very best salisbury steak

this is our favorite salisbury steak recipe. i always make enough extra sauce to serve over potatoes. tastes like it took all day to cook.

1. in a large bowl , mix together 1 / 3 cup condensed french onion soup with ground beef , bread crumbs , egg , salt and black pepper
2. shape into 6 oval patties
3. in a large skillet over medium-high heat , brown both sides of patties
4. pour off excess fat
5. in a small bowl , blend flour and remaining soup until smooth
6. mix in ketchup , water , worcestershire sauce and mustard powder
7. pour over meat in skillet
8. cover , and cook for 20 minutes , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: This recipe just wasn't to our liking. Everything cooked up nicely and it was very easy to prepare. We just didn't care for the flavor the ketchup imparted to the sauce. It wasn't what we had in mind when we were thinking salisbury steak.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
key lime cheesecake squares

this is a delightful and refreshing dessert. i found a recipe 15 years ago that is similar to mine, but i modified it to have a very good blend between the lime juice and sugar. my crust enhances the taste of the cheesecake.

1. crust---------
2. preheat oven to 350 f degrees
3. in a mixing bowl , combine graham wafer crumbs , vanilla wafer crumbs and ground almonds
4. cut in butter using a pastry blender or a fork until mixture is crumbly
5. prepare a 9 inch x 9 inch oven-proof casserole dish by spraying inside with a vegetable spray
6. press wafer mixture firmly in bottom of casserole dish
7. bake in preheated 350 f oven for 15 minutes
8. filling----------
9. in a mixing bowl using an electric mixer , beat softened cream cheese , sugar and egg until smooth
10. add lime juice , grated lime zest and tapioca starch and beat until smooth and creamy
11. spread mixture evenly over baked crust
12. return to oven and bake at 350 f for 25 to 30 minutes or until set
13. cool on wire rack
14. chill in refrigerator for at least 1 hour before cutting into squares to serve
15. if desired , decorate top of cheesecake with pieces of lime or halved small fresh strawberries or quartered maraschino cherries
16. you can also use regular lime juice or use bottled key lime juice
demonstrations.review: These were fabulous!! I did make the following changes: Used a 9 in springform pan, used 1 1/2 cups of cookie and graham cracker crumbs since we don't like nuts, doubled the cheesecake filling and used 1/4 cup of lemon juice instead of lime. The result was a wonderful, light cheesecake bar. I loved the blend of flavors in the crust. I topped it with some whipped cream with a little bit of instant lemon jello mixed in. My friend asked for the recipe and said that her DH doesn't like cheesecake but he loved this. This will certainly become a regular around here. Thanks Uncle Bill!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate chunk cookies

these are impossible to stop eating.

1. cream the butter and peanut butter together until fully incorporated
2. add the sugars and cream on medium speed
3. add the egg and vanilla and mix until completely incorporated
4. add the flour and baking soda , mix until no white remains , then add the chocolate and mix on low just until everything comes together
5. drop by teaspoonfuls onto parchment-lined baking sheets
6. bake at 350 for 9 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: These cookies were very good. My husband is a big peanut butter fan and he gave them a thumbs up. The only change I made was to use 1/2 cup peanut butter instead of 3/4 and they still had lots of PB flavor. I did think they were a little greasy/oily (not sure how to describe it) and a little flat for my taste in cookies. When I make these again I think I will use 1/4 cup of butter and 1/4 cup of shortening and a little more flour just to plump them up a little. Thanks for a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
bread salad

something different for your next cookout.

1. combine bread , tomatoes and basil in large bowl
2. in food processor with metal blade , chop garlic and salt
3. add rosemary , hot pepper flakes and vinegar
4. add olive oil in a stream to emulsify
5. toss bread mixture and dressing
6. allow to stand for at least 20 minutes so the bread can absorb the dressing
target.review: This was pretty tasty. It almost seems like it would be better served hot cassarole style, with some parmesan cheese sprinkled over the top...Next time I may try it that way. Thanks for a unique  new taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot garlic brown sugar chicken

the house smells wonderful while this is cooking!

1. place chicken in crock pot
2. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over chicken
3. cook on low for 6-8 hours
4. serve over rice or noodles
5. you can thicken the juices after cooking with a little cornstarch
demonstrations.review: The chicken had nice flavor. I added butter to the sauce, which made it a bit richer. By the end of the cooking time, I needed to put the liquid into a frying pan to reduce it and added cornstarch and water mixed to the pan to thicken the sauce. It was pretty good but not sure I would make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: Very tasty! I added 1/4 cup of brown sugar the second time I made these.. made the sauce sweeter and thicker. Pinapple may enhance the flavor even further.. but very yum, as directed, too! Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef barley soup

hearty, easy one dish meal that cooks itself while you're gone. serve with salad and bread, and you have a whole meal.

1. in skillet brown beef
2. place carrot , celery , green pepper , onion , corn and green beans in crock pot
3. put meat on top
4. combine tomatoes , barley , parsley , bouillon , salt and basil
5. pour over meat
6. add water
7. do not stir
8. cover and cook on low for 10-12 hours
demonstrations.review:
Very good! I plan to add more meat and corn the next time, just because they are my favorite ingredients in this recipe.. I need to dice everything smaller, too.
Oh, so good! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon shake up

this recipe was found on the net per a recipe request. no name was attached.

1. in a 16 oz glass pour in sugar
2. squeeze lemons to juice them and then add the squeezed halves
3. add ice , then water to fill
4. cover and"shake" until sugar is dissolved
demonstrations.review: Tart and Sweet! Oh so good! Very refreshing. I put some in the freezer to have shaved ice later.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
onion salad

posted this recipe as a request on the message board. i found the recipe in the 

1. slice the onions very thin and place them in a plastic or glass dish
2. combine the vinegar , water , sugar , and salt
3. mix well to dissolve the sugar and salt
4. pour over the sliced onions and mix well
5. put a plate on top of the onions and set a weight on it
6. a plastic bottle of oil and vinegar works well
7. let the onions sit on the counter all day- overnight is best
8. drain the onions
9. combine the dressing and celery seed and toss with onions
10. put in a serving bowl and serve
demonstrations.review: I used white onions and followed the recipe. I put the mixture into a zip-lock bag left it a few inches un-zipped, set it into a bowl in case of overflow, there was none. I let it marinate over night. WOW!!! I thought what does this taste like? Then it dawned on me, sweet pickles but with an onion taste. I later added thinly sliced celery for extra crunch. I think these onions would work like a "top secret" special ingredient in potato salad! Shhh! It's our secret lol!

target.recipe_text:
weepless meringue

i dont like tears on my pies.

1. mix together cornstarch and cold water
2. add to 1 / 2 cup boiling water
3. cook over low heat until it thickens
4. set aside to cool
5. beat egg whites , dash of salt , and sugar until stiff
6. add cooled cornstarch mixture to beaten egg white mixture
7. put on pie , making sure it covers the edges well
8. bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes or until golden brown
target.review: This was my first meringue attempt...I don't think it turned out like it was supposed to. It never did "fluff up"....I think maybe I should have beat the egg whites before adding the sugar and salt? Tasted good though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracker barrel grilled chicken tenders

this is such an easy recipe and taste just like cracker barrel chicken tenders. you can not find an easier recipe for chicken tenders.

1. mix dressing , lime juice and honey
2. pour over chicken tenders
3. marinate for 1 hour
4. cook tenders in a non stick pan or grill until golden in color , but not dry
demonstrations.review: We really liked these. Made them exactly as recipe calls for. I'll make them again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli casserole

had this recipe for years, not sure of it's origin. every occasion i have used it for, it's always been a success and i always get asked for the recipe!!

1. put broccoli into baking dish
2. mix other ingredients
3. pour mix over broccoli and sprinkle with a little cornbread topping or muffin mix
4. top with cheese
5. bake in preheated 350 degree oven for 30 minutes
6. recipe easily doubled
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! I used cream of celery, turned out perfect. Topped with Ritz crackers/butter. Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best orange creamsicle cake

this is by far one of the best cake recipes.  you simply must try it! 8) very fun, refreshing, wonderful cake for summer! enjoy!

1. bake cake as needed in 9x13-inch pan
2. when baked and cooled , poke holes all over cake with meat fork
3. mix large box of jello with the waters and just let it start to set up
4. slowly pour over the cooled cake and allow to run into holes all over cake
5. chill cake until jello is set
6. in large bowl , cream the cheese until creamy
7. add the dry jello powder , pudding mix , milk and the vanilla extract
8. beat well
9. fold in cool whip
10. spread on cake and chill until served
11. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Made this last night for my little boy's 3rd birtday (he specifically asked for an orange cake with orange frosting). It was really good! The cake tasted like a Push-up-Pop. Very easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage velveeta slow cooker dip

this dip is a favorite for parties at work, everyone always requests it. hope you enjoy it!

1. brown sausage and drain
2. cube velveeta
3. add all ingredients to slow cooker
4. cook on low for 1-2 hours , stirring occasionally until melted and blended well
5. if you have a "keep warm" setting on your slow cooker , then set to this temp until ready to serve
6. serve with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: This was great! I made it exactly as the recipe shows. I'll definately make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy and delicious ranch parmesan chicken

there are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, i find that hidden valley ranch dressing works the best but kraft or any other brand will do, i sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although i have only made this using breasts i imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *note* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
for low-fat option: use low-fat ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as smart balance 50/50 blend.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. in a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with parmesan cheese , seasoned salt , black pepper and garlic powder
3. dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides
4. coat in the breadcrumb mixture
5. place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil
6. lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast
7. if desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces
8. bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked)
demonstrations.review: Made this last night, and it turned out PERFECT. I've never used breadcrumbs, and I bought the Panko ones based on your recommendation- I loved it! The coating came out crisp and delicious. I just realized I forgot to drizzle any butter, but honestly, I don't think it needs it since it was so yummy without it. Everything else I did exactly as written. Thanks for an awesome recipe!

target.recipe_text:
toffee apple french toast

you make this recipe the night before and then cook it the following morning. from toh casseroles, slow cooker and soup cookbook.

1. place half of the bread cubes in a greased 13-inch x9 in x 2inch baking dish
2. top with apples
3. in a large mixing bowl , beat the cream cheese , sugars , 1 / 4 cup milk and 1 teaspoons vanilla until smooth
4. stir in toffee bits
5. spread over apples
6. top with remaining bread cubes
7. in another bowl , beat the eggs and remaining milk and vanilla until blended
8. pour over bread
9. cover and refrigerate overnight
10. remove from the refrigerator 30 minutes before baking
11. bake , uncovered , at 350f for 35-45 minutes or until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean
target.review:
This has a great combination of ingredients and a really good taste.
 I halved the recipe by cracking the five eggs into a measuring cup, beating them, and adding approximately half. (and of course, halving the other ingredients as well.)
I think I added the right amount of liquid, but the bread cubes on top were a little crunchy, and I was wondering if this was the way it was supposed to be.
I want to make this again because I wasn't entirely pleased with the way it looked, and I thought it could be improved by a second attempt.
My husband liked this a lot. We didn't need any syrup, it probably would have masked the wonderful taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baby shower pink cloud punch

this makes a wonderful punch for a baby girl's baby shower or a little girl's party! ---since this has such a wonderful colour it is best served in a large fancy punch bowl and should be served as soon as possible as the scoops of sherbet tend to get soft but don't worry if they melt in the punch it really makes the punch taste even better! --- this takes little time to prepare and is *so* good! if you should decide to add in any ice just make ice cubes out of any extra lemon-lime soda i have little fancy ice cube container shapes that i use just for punch and fancy drinks, if you prepare the ice cubes days in advance and just store them in a ziploc plastic bag it really saves time --- if you are using frozen concentrate lemonade for this recipe you might want to reduce the water amount slightly and increase the sugar amount but this is only optional, you will love this! --- also see my recipe#292039

1. in a large glass punch bowl , mix the lemonade and lemon-lime soda
2. add in half of the sherbet , and stir well to make frothy
3. add in small scoops of the remaining well-frozen little sherbet balls
4. and the lemon and / or orange slices
5. serve immediately
6. also make certain that your lemonade and soda are very cold , so you do not have to add any ice to the punch when serving , although of coarse ice may be aded if desired
7. delicious !
demonstrations.review:
This was the punch I served recently at my Daughter's bridal shower.
Everyone absolutely Loved this punch.
It's simple to make, with a beautiful pink color and a delicious taste.
I had several people ask me for the recipe.
It was the perfect choices for a day that was all about the ladies!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh fruit breakfast parfaits

we were served this at a b&b in grass valley, ca. it is so simple and so tasty! you can use any mix of fruit you have on hand.

1. place of the bananas and of the strawberries in each of 2 parfait glasses
2. sprinkle 1 teaspoon of brown sugar over each
3. top with each with of the yogurt and serve
demonstrations.review: Very easy and quick to make. Simple ingredients and very pretty. Nice for breakfast or brunch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot baked cinnamon apples

these cinnamon apples taste like a cobbler or pie without the crust. i was looking for a recipe for cinnamon apples and all i could find were recipes for baking the whole apple - not what i wanted. after much searching i finally came across this recipe - i unfortunately cannot remember the site. it can easily be reduced to 2 or 3 apples, just watch it as it cooks. we serve this over ice cream and it is delicious. it can also be used on pancakes, waffles, or all by itself.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. place cut and peeled apples in a mixing bowl and gently mix all the ingredients together
3. put apples in a non-stick pan
4. cover and place in the oven
5. bake for 45 minutes , stirring at least once every 15 minutes
6. once they are soft , cook for another few minutes to thicken the cinnamon sauce
7. i like to put everything into my baking dish and then mix it since there is less to clean up
demonstrations.review:
This is a great recipe because it's so easy and versatile. Plus, it's less calories than pie with the crust.
Everyone I described this too was salivating, and they were just imagining it, I hadn't actually made it for them yet!
I did make it for my husband, and he loved it. I put it over lower calorie ice cream, and made it like a sundae with whipped cream.
I bought fresh apples to make it with, but found a can of sliced apples which I wanted to use up in my cabinet. This worked just as well and made it even easier.
I will be trying it with fresh apples as well. 
It is wonderful to smell this baking on a cold fall night, and even better to eat.
You can also use this as a topping  for pancakes or waffles.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breaded breast of chicken  chicken cutlets

very simple chicken recipe, but one my family is quite fond of. they love when there are leftovers, so they can make sandwiches!

1. pound chicken to flatten
2. sprinkle salt and pepper on each
3. dip into beaten eggs and then coat with bread crumbs
4. in a large skillet , heat oil over medium heat
5. saute garlic until golden and then discard
6. place chicken in skillet and brown on both sides , cooking about 5 minutes on each side , or until chicken is fork tender
7. cooking time will vary depending on how thick your chicken is
demonstrations.review: Love these! Can't wait to make chicken sandwiches with the leftovers. Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast applesauce for pancakes  french toast or waffles

my grandpa made us kids pancakes and waffles whenever we'd visit.  and he'd serve this apple sauce on the side - we'd eat it as is or top our waffles.  good!

1. in a sauce pan mix sugar , flour & water
2. add the apples
3. cook over medium heat until it bubbles
demonstrations.review: This was delicious and easy to make. I added 1/2 tsp. cinnamon because I like that combination of ingredients and it was very flavorful.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
target.review: This was a great dish!! Kittencal, you should open your own restuarant!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot barbecue country ribs

makes a sweet sauce that is nicely sticky so have lots of napkins! great for days when the weather isn't good enough to grill outside!

1. place ribs , onion and garlic in crock pot
2. cook on low for 8-10 hours , or until pork is cooked through and tender
3. drain ribs and onion from crock pot
4. discard any juices from crock pot and return meat and onions to crock pot
5. stir together barbecue sauce and jam until blended
6. pour over ribs , stirring lightly to coat
7. cook on high for 30 minutes or until sauce has thickened and ribs are glazed
demonstrations.review: With all the good reviews I wasn't too impressed. Good but needed more sauce or something.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
john and erin s beer butt chicken   beer can

this was our first attempt at beer butt chicken and it was awesome! you can change the flavor a bit by changing the beer you use.

1. mix dry ingredients together and rub chicken inside and out
2. open can of beer , pour half into a spray bottle and add orange juice , olive oil and vinegar to spray bottle
3. insert the can into the cavity of the chicken
4. with the chicken resting on the can , cook for about 2 hours over medium-hot grill with grill cover on spray chicken with the basting spray while cooking
5. when done , carefully lift the chicken off the grill and remove the can-- be careful , liquid is hot !
demonstrations.review: Great Bird!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven ranch chicken  low fat

this is a wonderful recipe that my children love. i love it too because it's only 4 points per breast if you're living a lifestyle that requires you to assign points to your food.  pair this up with cole slaw and baked beans... yummy!!!

1. heat oven to 375 degrees f
2. spray cookie sheet with non-stick spray
3. in shallow dish combine bread crumbe & dressing mix
4. dip chicken in sounr cream , then crumb mixture
5. place on cookie sheet , spray chicken with cooking spray
6. discard any remaining bread crumbs & sour cream
7. bake at 375 for 30-35 minutes or until chicken is fork tender and juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Yum! This is a keeper for a quick weekday dinner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Gross. not yum, I don't know why the heck everyone thinks this is so great. No flavor at all and watery! :(

demonstrations.recipe_text:
emeril s creamed spinach

i saw this recipe on food tv's web site and had to try it. i love his recipes and this one is no exception. i make it several times a year.

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees
2. lightly grease a 6 cup casserole
3. in a large saute pan , melt the remaining butter
4. add the onions and season with salt and pepper
5. saute for about 2 minutes , or until the onions are soft
6. add the spinach
7. season with salt and pepper
8. saute for 3 to 4 minutes
9. add the garlic and cream
10. mix well
11. season the mixture with salt and pepper
12. bring the liquid to a boil and reduce to a simmer
13. simmer the mixture for 6 minutes
14. remove the pan from the heat and turn into the prepared pan
15. add 1 / 2 of cheese to casserole and stir
16. sprinkle the top with the remainder of the grated cheese and place in the oven
17. bake for about 4 to 6 minutes or until the cheese is slightly brown and bubbly
demonstrations.review: yum, yum yum, big hit with the DH and myself, will be making this again!!! I did notice that all that spinach (I used baby spinach) gave off some excess water so I would recommend draining off any excess liquid before adding the cream.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s extreme chocolate brownies

if your looking for an everyday run-of-the-mill cake-style brownie then pass this by, this is a a moist chewy extreme chocolate bakery-style brownie that takes little time to make and tastes even better the next day, it's everything a good brownie should be!  --- i have even made these using half brown sugar and half white sugar, the amount of sugar listed will give you a sweet brownie you may reduce the sugar by 1/4 cup or more if desired or if you have a sweet tooth use amount stated --- add in a couple of tablespoons of coffee-flavored liqueur in place of the vanilla if desired -- according to a reviewer oil may be used in place of the butter successfully --- these brownies freeze very well,  they are so simple to make just mix everything by hand, they bake out so rich and sinful! --- see recipe#89207

1. set oven to 325 degrees f
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. in a heavy saucepan , bring butter , sugar and water to a boil , stirring constantly until the butter is melted and sugar is dissolved
4. remove from the heat , with a wooden spoon , stir in 2 cups chocolate chips until melted
5. cool slightly , beat in vanilla
6. in a mixing bowl , whisk eggs , gradually add in the chocolate mixture , beating with a wooden spoon until completely mixed
7. mix together flour , baking soda and salt
8. add to the egg / chocolate mixture
9. mix well to combine
10. stir in the remaining chocolate chips
11. spread into prepared baking pan
12. bake for 35-40 minutes
13. cut into squares
target.review: These brownies are truly fabulous!  They are so fudgy and delicous! They are easy to make as well. I did not top them with the chocolate buttercream, because they are over the top already...but that doesn't mean that I won't someday!  I made one recipe with 1 tsp.or so of instant coffee granules for just a hint of a mocha flavor for my husband's family Christmas get-together, and they were devoured. I am THRILLED to have this recipe to use again and again!  Thanks once again Kitten!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan   garlic damper rolls

simple & oh so tasty. a great one to serve with a big bowl of soup!

1. sift flour into a bowl , rub in butter with finger
2. make a well in the centre of the mixture , add combined water & milk all at once reserving about 2 teaspoons
3. mix quickly to a soft dough , turn onto a lightly floured surface , knead gently & form into 6 rounds
4. arrange on a baking paper lined tray
5. cut a cross in the top of each roll & brush with remaining milk mixture , sprinkle with extra cheese
6. bake at 220
7. c for 15-20 mins or until hollow when tapped
demonstrations.review: These were delicious!  They remind me a good bit of my Mom's homemade biscuits with cheese, garlic and chives added. They were BIG, so next time I might make more than 6. I also might add a touch more garlic and cheese, or try using a stronger flavored cheese and adding a little garlic powder with the fresh garlic.  This is a winner! Made for ZWT3.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken lasagna  lower fat lower calorie

this is healthy, but still rich and delicious.

1. spray a frying pan with nonstick spray and saute the onions , green pepper , and mushrooms until tender
2. add the soup , milk , and chicken breast
3. in a 9x13 pan that has been sprayed with nonstick spray , layer:
4. 3 noodles
5. cottage cheese
6. 3 noodles
7. 1 / 2 of the chicken sauce
8. chedder cheese
9. second 1 / 2 of the chicken sauce
10. parmesan cheese
11. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
12. remove from oven and let sit for 10 minutes before cutting
demonstrations.review: We had this last night, and I have to agree that there was not enough sauce to make 3 layers. When I saw how little the sauce looked in the pan, I added my leftovers from recipe#137667. This made enough sauce. I did add a little mozzerella with the cheddar as well. It was quite tasty. Firmed up after about 15 minutes resting time, and tasted better the more it cooled. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned chocolate filling and frosting

yummy, rich filling and frosting, enough for a 3 layer cake! this comes from my grandmom's collection of recipes...it really is old-fashioned :)

1. melt the chocolate and butter together in top of a double boiler
2. mix the cornstarch with the milk
3. add slowly to melted chocolate , stirring until thick and smooth
4. add 1 1 / 2 cups confectioners' sugar and salt to egg yolks
5. add to chocolate mixture
6. continue to cook while while beating until smooth
7. add vanilla and cool
8. usehalf of the mixture to fill or spread between layers of the cake
9. use the other half for frosting by adding remaining 2 cups of confectioners' and the cream slowly to the mixture and beat until smooth
demonstrations.review: What a fantastic fudgy filling! I am not rating the frosting part of the recipe, because I did not finish the frosting. I made the recipe through step 5, and stirred in 2 heaping Tablespoons of peanut butter. I made recipe#87205 as a 3 layer 9 inch cake, and used almost all of this delicious filling between the layers. I used recipe#87058 to frost the top and sides. This was absolutely the BEST chocolate peanut butter cake I have EVER had! I can't WAIT to make this again exactly as directed for a yellow cake, or a peanut butter cake.  Thanks so much for EXACTLY the rich, decadent filling I was looking for!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet salsa dump chicken   oamc

the theory is you dump this in a bag and freeze to pull out later. there are many variations which i will post separately but it's amazingly easy to make these up and have a different 

1. for immediate cooking: pre-heat oven to 350f place all ingredients into a large baking dish , turn chicken to coat
2. bake until chicken juices run clear
3. for freezing: place all ingredients into a 1 gallon freezer bag
4. lay flat in freezer
5. to thaw and cook: take the bag out of the freezer the night before , make sure the baggie is completely closed
6. place the bag on a refrigerator shelf to thaw
7. preheat the oven to 350f empty the contents of the bag into a large baking dish and bake until the juices run clear
demonstrations.review: New family favorite! I used boneless chicken breasts, peach jam, and didn't have taco seasoning but had fajita seasoning, so I used it and add a touch extra cumin. I froze first, then just dumped partially thawed into a slow cooker on high for 1 hour, then low for about 6 hours. I added rice the last hour, but I won't do that next time, because it wasn't minute rice and it never really got soft, but stayed a little crunchy. The flavor was infused in every bite of chicken, and the sauce was delicious, not too sweet at all. I will make it again and thicken the sauce to serve over the chicken, or cook the rice separately to put the sauce over. Thanks so much for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mansiikka kiisseli  strawberries

a finnish recipe perfect for an easy dessert when strawberries are in season!

1. in a pot we put the juice , the water and the sugar
2. we wait until the sugar is dissolved stirring a little
3. remove from heat
4. we wash well the strawberries
5. add the cornstarch in the pot over medium heat stirring well until we have a cream
6. then we put the strawberries inches
7. serve !
demonstrations.review: What a simple, perfect dessert! This came together even more quickly than the time indicated! My sons who claim not to like strawberries loved it, as did DH and I. This is wonderful alone, and would also be great served over shortcake/poundcake, or even pancakes for breakfast! Thank you, Katia, for posting a new family favorite! Made for ZWT3.

target.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
target.review: I may be in the minority, but my husband and I just didn't care for this. I thought I would since I love burritos and this was super simple, but I think our disliking this was due to the tortillas becoming mushy and doughy in the casserole. I didn't care for that texture. Maybe it would be better if you put a layer of rice or a layer of tortilla chips instead of flour tortillas. Also I didn't think the mushroom soup complimented the flavors very well, I would look for a different flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian turkey sausage and peppers with bow tie pasta

i just threw this together one night with ingredients i had on hand. we loved the flavor and it's now a favorite after work meal.

1. saute onion , peppers and pepper flakes in olive oil until onions start to brown
2. add garlic , salt , pepper , basil and oregano
3. set aside
4. prick sausage links with a fork
5. saute in skillet with a little olive oil over medium heat until brown
6. add wine vinegar and canned tomatoes
7. add the sauted vegetable mixture
8. cover and simmer for 20 minutes
9. meanwhile cook pasta al dente
10. add cooked pasta to sausage and pepper mixture
11. stir and serve
demonstrations.review: This was really good! I used whole wheat penne instead of bow ties, also used half a red pepper plus half of a yellow pepper. The vinegar was new to me and had an interesting flavor, next time I think I will add a little red wine to the sauce as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chorizo black bean soup

this is adapted from a recipe i found on the weight watchers site. the original recipe calls for cooking in a crockpot. instructions for the crockpot version are included at the bottom. it makes about 5 servings--not a huge potfull.

1. remove the casing from the chorizo and begin to break it up and brown it in a medium saucepot
2. after a few minutes add the onion , garlic and green pepper and cook the mixture for about five minutes total
3. add the beans and broth , then the cumin and bay leaf
4. let it come to a boil and then simmer about a half hour
5. add the lemon juice
6. for crockpot use , follow the first step , then transfer all the ingredients into the crockpot and cook on low about 3 hours
7. garnish with cilantro if desired
demonstrations.review: This was really easy and pretty good, even better the next day though. I used about 1/2 a pound of chorizo, 3 cups of chicken broth, and added corn and cayenne pepper. I also used the optional sherry. I served it with tortilla chips, shredded cheese and sour cream. It was similar to chili but easier and quicker. I definitely would add cayenne if you like spicy food, otherwise I probably would have found it just a little bland. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
good and garlicky sweet and sour pork

the flavors of this dish mix really well together. we like this served over brown rice, it makes a nice dish.

1. for the sauce , combine all the sauce ingredients in a small dish
2. set aside
3. trim the tenderloin of any visible fat , and cut into 1-inch cubes , and set aside
4. coat a large nonstick skillet with nonstick cooking spray , and preheat over med-high heat
5. add the garlic and the pork , stir fry for 5-6 minutes , or until pork is browned
6. drain the juice from the pineapple , reserving both the juice and the fruit
7. add the juice to the pork mixture , and bring to a boil
8. reduce the heat to low , cover , and simmer for 6-8 minutes , or until pork is tender and cooked through
9. add the pineapple chunks , bell pepper , onion , and carrot to the pork mixture
10. cover and simmer for an additional 3-4 minutes , or until the veggies are crisp-tender
11. stir the sauce to mix , and add it to the skillet
12. cook , stirring constantly , until the sauce is thickened and bubbly
13. serve hot , with brown rice
demonstrations.review: I made this tonight for dinner. Although I had to use chicken instead of pork because my husband doesn't eat pork, I thought it was very good. I was looking for a good, healthy recipe and was very pleased with this. I also added a small yellow bell pepper, and I think next time I may also add some red pepper and maybe water chestnuts. It isn't like the typical sweet and sour that you get at buffets and such, but actually I much prefer this style. Thank you for a very nice recipe, I'm sure I'll be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww core   bubbling pizza casserole

this delicous weight watcher core program recipe counts as 4 point per serving to the the core member.   you can really add any vegetables to taste to this recipe.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in skillet , brown meat over medium heat , stirring to crumble
3. stir in onion , tomato sauce , basil , garlic , and italian seasoning
4. add veggies
5. add quartered biscuit dough to the pan of sauce & meat
6. stir gently until biscuits are covered with sauce
7. spray a 9 x 13" casserole dish with cooking spray
8. dump the mixture into the dish
9. bake for 25 minutes
10. sprinkle with cheese , and bake an additional 10 minutes or until biscuits are done
11. let stand 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I thought this recipe was ok. There was really nothing special about it, but it was quick and easy, also made a ton of food fairly inexpensively. I like the idea of using biscuits in a casserole and I think I may play around with that and make different kinds, like maybe a chicken casserole with biscuits instead of the rice I usually use.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: I have made these twice. The first time I followed the recipe exactly, though I thought 1 cup of chocolate chips ended up being too much. Also my brownies did not get done at 350 for ~35 minutes. They were still way too gooey, though they tasted great. This time I substituted one ripe banana for 1/4 cup of the butter and only put in about 1/2 cup chocolate chips, and I baked at 375 for 10 minutes, then turned it down to 350 for the remaining 20. They turned out perfect! A little more cakey and definitely a some banana flavor, but I like that and esp. like reducing the fat. They were still very moist. Next time I may try substituting Splenda granular for some of the sugar, too, to reduce the calories further. This is definitely a great basic recipe and fun to play around with.

target.recipe_text:
almond pound cake

very rich! one of my favourite cakes. this is good dressed up with frosting, served plain, or with fruit. i quadrupled this recipe, and baked it in two 9"x13" pans to make a cake for my father's 65th birthday party. note: be sure the almonds are finely ground; if they seem somewhat coarse you should run them through the food processor until quite fine. 

1. preheat the oven to 325f
2. butter and flour a loaf pan or small square pan
3. cream the butter and sugar
4. beat in the eggs one at a time
5. beat in the almond extract and the water
6. stir together the flour , ground almonds and baking powder
7. stir this into the wet ingredients
8. pour evenly into the prepared pan
9. bake for 45 minutes for a loaf pan
10. bake for 50 minutes in the square pan , or in either case until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean
target.review: This makes an outstanding cake, perfect balance of sugar and butter and almond flavor.  I wasn't sure about it as first, it looked a little "rustic" coming out of the oven.  But as soon as I tasted it I was hooked!  Took it to work and everyone there is begging for me to make it again.  This is a hit!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas trash

not your ordinary snack mix! a big, bold flavor just like the state of texas! this can be doubled, tripled or quadrupled successfully. you can also add other ingredients, just keep the proportion of spicy butter to the dry ingredients the same as in the recipe. i usually add goldfish crackers to mine.

1. preheat oven to 250
2. mix the first 7 ingredients in a cup with a spout
3. mix all dry ingredients in a baking pan
4. pour the butter and seasonings over the dry mix , stirring until each piece is coated
5. bake for 1 hour , stirring every 15 minutes
6. cool
7. stir in an air tight container
8. freezes well
demonstrations.review: I made this a couple of days ago, and will be making it again today since my husband has eaten all of the first batch!  We absolutely love this, and the spice was just right to us (we're pepper heads--I may even kick it up!).  I made another Texas Trash recipe first, but this one was by far the best.  This one is definitely going in my permanent cookbook.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
multi grain bread

this very easy bread requires zero kneading, yet the result is a nice high risen moist and crumbly loaf.  recipe from power eating.

1. combine cereal and boiling water in a microwavable bowl , set aside for 10 minutes
2. stir honey and oil into the cereal
3. heat until hot
4. in a separate large bowl , mix 1 cup whole wheat flour with the all purpose flour , oat bran , yeast , sugar and salt
5. beat in hot cereal mixture and egg
6. using electric mixer beat for 2 minutes at high speed
7. stir in enough remaining whole wheat flour to make a stiff batter
8. with floured hands , pat dough in a 9x5 sprayed or lightly greased loaf pan
9. cover lightly with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel
10. let rise until doubled , 40-60 minutes
11. remove wrap , bake at 375f 35-40 minutes or until bottom sounds hollow when tapped
12. remove from pan , cool on a rack
demonstrations.review: I LOVE this bread!  I made it a couple of weeks ago and forgot to save the recipe, and I've been searching the website for it ever since.  Today the site was having traffic issues and I couldn't get the recipe to open, but I sat here trying over and over for about 10 minutes and when it finally did, it paid off.  Yay, it's my recipe!  I love how crumbly this is, and I toast it in the mornings and enjoy it on the way to work.  My only wheat bread recipe from now on, and thanks for sharing it with us!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
golden crunchy pickled onions

from yahoo group. description states: "you should allow two weeks after preparing these before eating. they’ll be tasty right away, but they’ll be sublime if you exercise two weeks’ worth of patience!"

1. to each prepared pint jar add 6 cloves , 6 peppercorns , 1 tsp mustard seed and 1 / 2 tsp celery seed
2. set aside
3. peel and slice the onions into 1 / 4 thick rings
4. separate the onion rings carefully and divide among the jars
5. in a large nonreactive saucepan , stir together the vinegar , water , sugar , salt , turmeric and cinnamon over high heat
6. heat the syrup to boiling and then allow it to simmer for 2 minutes
7. pour the hot liquid over the onion rings being sure to leave 1 / 4 of headspace
8. use a chopstick or skewer to remove air pockets that might be in the jars by running it along the inside wall of the jar
9. if needed , add more hot syrup to maintain the 1 / 4 headspace
10. process jars in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes
11. adjust time according to your altitude
demonstrations.review: If you haven't made these yet...what are you waiting for?  These are outstanding!  We love them on sandwiches, or sprinkled over a salad.  Really great in a panini, too, since they keep their crunch and it adds some additional texture to your sandwich.  They are a little sweet, a little sour, a little spicy from the cinnamon and tumeric, with the great onion flavor remaining at the base.  They are beautiful in the jar, and make great gifts.  I buy a box of onions at our local produce stand every year to make these, as people often request them.  One of my favorite condiment recipes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese wontons

these appetizers disappear quickly! they are also great dipped in a mixture of soy sauce and worcestershire sauce.

1. combine pork , garlic , ginger , soy sauce , sesame oil , and vegetables in a bowl
2. separate wonton skins
3. place a heaping teaspoon of filling in the center of the wonton
4. brush water on 2 borders of the skin , covering 1 / 4 inch from the edge
5. fold skin over to form a triangle , sealing edges
6. pinch the two long outside points together
7. heat oil to 450 degrees and fry 4 to 5 at a time until golden
8. drain and serve with sauce
demonstrations.review: These are sooooo good!  I think my fiance liked them even more than I did, they were great.  I love the combination of the vegetables in the stuffing, that really added something.  I made up some hot mustard to dip them in, and needless to say there weren't any leftovers!  I froze half the batch to cook at a later date, and I'm already wanting to get them out of the freezer.  Thanks for posting this, it's a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy green chili and cheese soup

this sounds perfect for cold nights!  potatoes, green chiles, cream and cheese!??  doesn't get much better than that!
source:  internet

1. melt butter in medium saucepan over medium heat
2. add onion , garlic and oregano
3. cook for 10 minutes
4. add chicken broth , potatoes and hot pepper sauce
5. bring to a boil
6. cook for 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender
7. add green chiles , cream and cheese
8. heat until cheese is melted
9. season with salt and black ground pepper to taste
10. garnish with cilantro
demonstrations.review: Oh my goodness, this is soooooo good. I had dental surgery and am on a soft/liquid diet for a few weeks so I made this, and it totally hit the spot. Very filling and flavorful. I used hot Hatch green chiles because I like a lot of heat, and it did not disappoint. I'll have a hard time ever eating the traditional potato soup now. This recipe is definitely a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
papaya salsa

a great accompaniment to grilled fish and chicken for summertime grilling!

1. peel , split , and seed papaya
2. chop coarsely
3. mix together all ingredients in a bowl
4. serve over grilled fish such as ahi tuna , swordfish
5. also grilled chicken
target.review: This was terrific on grilled fish!!!  Thanks!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rhubarb dumplings

granma's rhubarb dumpling recipe modernized

1. in 2 quart micro-safe dish with cover combine sugar and cornstarch , stir in water til smooth
2. add rhubarb and butter
3. cover and microwave on high 5 minutes , stir , microwave 3 minutes til rhubarb is tender and sauce is thickened
4. meanwhile combine flour , sugar , baking powder , milk and butter
5. drop batter in eight mounds onto rhubarb around edges of dish
6. cover microwave on high 2 minutes
7. rotate dish a quarter
8. microwave 3 more minutes , or til toothpick inserted in dumpling comes out clean
9. combine sugar and cinnamon sprinkle over dumplings , serve warm with cream , whipped cream or icecream
demonstrations.review: These were great!!! Definitely something we'll fix whenever we have rhubarb!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with bulgur

a tasty middle-eastern style recipe, and one of my favorite ways to fix chicken!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. mix together the salt , cinnamon , allspice , and pepper
3. rub mixture into chicken
4. in a heavy , wide frying pan over medium-high heat , heat the oil
5. add the chicken pieces and cook , turning , until all sides are browned
6. remove the chicken from the pan and set aside
7. discard the pan drippings but do not wipe out the pan
8. melt the butter in the pan you cooked the chicken in
9. add the onion and cook , stirring , until soft
10. add the uncooked bulgur and currants and stir to coat well with butter
11. spread the bulgur mixture in the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking pan
12. place the chicken pieces on top
13. pour the water , then the broth , over the chicken
14. cover the pan tightly with foil and bake in a 375 degree oven for 40 to 45 minutes or until juices run clear and bulgur has absorbed all liquid
15. garnish with sprinkled parsley and mint and serve
demonstrations.review: This is a GREAT RECIPE!!! I loved the mix of spices and it was really easy to make. It was the first time Ive cooked bulgur and it was GOOD!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet brie

this is a very elegant appetizer. make sure to 'gently' pat down the brown sugar (perhaps sprinkling would be better). the first time i made it i was not gentle and the crust was much to hard (but still delicious).  some reviewers have suggested using less sugar which sounds like a good option. you be the judge.  either way, it's sure to be a hit at your next get together.

1. preheat broiler
2. place brie in 10-inch quiche dish or other oven-proof dish or pie plate and sprinkle with nuts
3. cover top and sides with sugar , patting gently with finger
4. broil on lowest rack until sugar bubbles and melts , about 3 minutes
5. serve immediately with crackers
demonstrations.review: I've made this many times in the past and its really really good!!!  Really easy to make and people are impressed and go home and make it themselves at their next party.  I think thats a compliment!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy pesto shrimp

ridiculously easy to make, this shrimp is oh-so-wonderful-tasty and rich. not for those watching your fat intake, but hey... everything in moderation, right?

1. cook linguini according to package directions
2. drain and set aside
3. in a large skillet , melt butter over medium heat
4. toss in the minced garlic , shallot , mushrooms , and reconstituted sundried tomatoes and saut for 2 to 3 minutes , then stir in half and half and season with pepper
5. cook 6 to 8 minutes , while stirring
6. stir the parmesan into the creamy mixture , stirring until well mixed
7. stir in the pesto , and cook for about 5 minutes , until thickened
8. stir in the shrimp and cook until they turn pink , about 5 minutes
9. re-heat the linguini and serve shrimp and sauce over the hot pasta
10. garnish with grated romano and freshly ground black pepper
demonstrations.review: Wow! These prawns are rich! I didn't have a shallot and so used white onion, but did the rest of the recipe the same.  I'll be making this one again!!!!! Thanks Julesong! It made for a great romantic dinner!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sherry buttered shrimp

this is so very simple, and so very tasty. elegant and perfect for a nice, romantic dinner.

1. in large skillet , cook mushrooms , garlic , and shallot in butter until tender
2. add shrimp , basil and pepper
3. cook and stir until shrimp are pink
4. stir in sherry
5. simmer for 3 minutes
6. serve with cooked rice
7. makes 4 servings
demonstrations.review: The mother in law took the kids and we had a night alone for a romantic dinner and I fixed this for my wife.  It was great!!!

target.recipe_text:
vegan mayo

this is great on sandwiches, wraps and veggie burgers

1. place the soy milk in a blender , and with the belnder still running , slowly drizzle in the oil
2. continue adding the oil until it is all absorbed
3. transfer to a large bowl , and whisk in the vinegar , mustard , agave nectar , hot sauce , salt and pepper to taste
4. the mayo will keep in the refrigerator , covered , for up to a week
target.review: Perfect!  I had been having a devil of a time getting other vegan mayo recipes to get thick enough but followed directions on this and it was literally too thick to blend in those seasonings - that's why you have to transfer to a bowl and hand mix them in.  PERFECT texture, amazing taste.  Thanks for a home run recipe!<br/><br/>Edited to add - I have made this dozens of times now and have only had this turn out runny twice - both when using almond milk.  Stick to soymilk for the best results.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy bean sprouts

this is a great side to serve with an asian inspired main.

1. wash sprouts & drain well
2. heat butter in a pan and saute ginger & garlic 1 minute , add onions and cook for 3 minutes
3. add remaining spices and cook 3 mins before adding bean sprouts
4. combine all ingredients well and cook for a further 3 minutes
demonstrations.review: not my cup of tea at all, which surprised me as I love all the ingredients separately.  So it wasn't a total toss out I doctored it to our tastes by adding a bit of sugar and balsamic and a generous sprinkling of ground peanuts.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese curry  wafuu

this recipe comes from saveur magazine, and it tastes just like the curry we had in japan.  it seems to be a forgiving recipe: i used a sprinkle of dry ginger instead of fresh, left out the bay leaf, used 1/2 cup of apple sauce instead of a grated apple, used chicken bullion instead of stock and used ketchup instead of crushed tomatoes.  serve with freshly steamed rice.  it doesn't take a long time to make, and isn't complicated although it has a long list of ingredients.  edit - a few reviewers think that 1/2 cup of applesauce makes it too sweet, so please adjust to your tastes if you decide to substitute it for the apple :-)

1. bring chicken stock to a simmer
2. meanwhile , season chicken with salt and pepper , and brown in oil
3. after approx 4 minutes , remove to a separate dish and set aside
4. melt the butter and add ginger , garlic , and onion
5. cook a few minutes until done
6. sprinkle in the flour and cook until browned add curry powder and tomatoes , stir well
7. mix in 1 / 2 cup hot stock , making sure to scrape the stuff off of the bottom of the skillet
8. pour the mixture into the simmering stock
9. add the chicken , onion , potato , and carrot
10. simmer 30 minutes
11. add the apples , soy sauce , and honey
12. allow to cook for 5 more minutes , remove from heat and serve with rice
demonstrations.review: Delicious.  Made per recipe except made it vegan, so subbed margarine, left out chicken and put in edamame.  Kids inhaled this.  Will definitely do this again.  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan pumpkin pie

this comes from the vegetarian times complete thanksgiving cookbook.

1. to make the crust , in a medium bowl , combine flours , salt , sugar and baking powder
2. in a small bowl , mix oil and soy milk mixture
3. pour liquid mixture into dry ingredients and mix with a fork until dough holds together in a ball
4. if it is too dry , add some water , a little at a time , until dough is moist enough to roll
5. roll out dough on lightly floured surfaced with a floured rolling pin , forming an 11-inch circle
6. line a 9-inch pie pan with the dough
7. flute or crimp the edges with your fingers or a fork
8. cover with plastic and refrigerate until ready to use
9. pre-heat oven to 425f
10. to prepare the filling , in a large bowl , mix all remaining ingredients until smooth and blunted
11. pour into prepared crust and smooth top
12. bake 10 minutes , then reduce oven temperature to 350f and bake until filling is set , about 50 minutes
demonstrations.review: Another review just reviewing the filling - I had grown pumpkins this year so wanted to try a pie.  Used 2.5 c fresh pumpkin in lieu of the canned.  The filling was so amazingly tasty uncooked my kids would have done shots of it had I let them.  I didn't have any molasses, so just used 1/2 T of dark brown sugar as a substitute.  End result was a very good pie.  I used Food.com recipe 51537 for a no-roll pie crust which was a super easy perfect compliment to the filling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cauliflower and or broccoli soup  ww 0 point soup

delicious soup to use leftover broccoli or cauliflower.  i have used both - alone and together.  it's easy and 0 point if you are following the weight watchers plan!

1. dice cauliflower and / or broccoli
2. slice 2 cups carrots , chop 1 / 2 cup onion
3. in a 5 quart saucepan , add all ingredients except salt and pepper
4. cover and simmer until vegetables are tender
5. strain off and reserve most of the liquid
6. place vegetables in a food processor and puree
7. {or mash vegetables , still in pan with potato masher til of desired consistency}
8. add pureed vegetables and reserved liquid back into the pot
9. add salt and pepper and re-heat
demonstrations.review: It's a good soup but I altered it to kick it up a notch for my liking.  Without substantially altering its WW Zero point status, add 2T of apple cider vinegar to give it a little tang, 1 t of thyme and a few cloves minced garlic (sauteed in with the onions first before boiling up the lot) to bring it up.  I used cauliflower and broccoli in mine 2:1 ratio.  I'm thinking I would leave out the broccoli and just go cauliflower next time.  Also to give it cheesy goodness without the calories and fat of cheese, think about sprinkling on a tablespoon or so of nutritional yeast flakes (about 10 cals) to garnish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seitan and mushroom stroganoff  vegan

this is the best vegetarian or vegan stroganoff i've tried yet.  it came from farm sanctuary's guide to vegan living and i've only slightly changed it.  one way i improved it for our taste is by using mckay's chicken seasoning broth instead of vegetable broth or water and adding 3 tablespoons of vegan sour cream.  we will be making this often from now on.  hope you enjoy it!

1. gravy: stir cornstarch and soy sauce together in a 2-quart saucepan and make a thin , smooth , paste
2. whisk in the broth or water and garlic granules
3. cook over medium-high heat , stirring constantly until it thickens and comes to a boil
4. remove from heat and beat in the tahini and vegan sour cream
5. cover the saucepan and set aside
6. place oil in a large skillet and heat over medium-high
7. when the oil is hot , saut the onion and garlic for 10 minutes
8. add the mushrooms and cook , stirring often , for 5 to 7 minutes
9. stir the seitan strips and the reserved gravy into the onions and mushrooms
10. reduce heat to low and stir often , about 5 to 10 minutes , until the seitan is heated through
11. season the stroganoff with ground pepper
12. serve at once over egg-free noodles
demonstrations.review: So good!  I had no seitan on hand so just made this with extra mushrooms.  I didn't have veg. sour cream so used 2.5 T vegan alfredo with .5 T lemon juice.  I was raised on beef stroganoff and this brought childhood back but in a much, much healthier way.  Thanks for sharing this great recipe.  Truly a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
iowa salisbury steak

i got this from the covered bridges cookbook. it's a family favorite.

1. combine 1 / 3 of the soup , ground beef , bread crumbs , onion and egg
2. mix well
3. shape mixture into 6 patties
4. brown patties in skillet , 3-4 minutes each side
5. pour off fat
6. combine remaining soup with water and pour over patties in skillet
7. cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes or until meat is done , stirring and shifting occasionally
target.review: One time when I was missing my family and longing for some old time comfort food, I searched on Iowa (where I was born and raised) and this recipe was one that came up.  I made it for dinner and felt like I was at my parents home.  Ahhhh, the memories! Eventually, I wanted to lighten it up a bit. Now a days, I use a 20 oz. package of ground turkey, forgoing the 1/3 can of soup (Healthy Request or Low Fat version) in the meat mixture, since there's 1/4 lb. less meat.  Brown the patties and remove them to a plattter, sautee some onions and fresh mushrooms in the skillet.  Mix 1/2 cup hot water with 1/2 to 1 teaspoon beef base and use some to deglaze the skillet, leaving 1/3 cup remaining.  I let the beef broth reduce with the onions and mushrooms, add the soup, remaining broth, stir and return the patties to the "gravy".  Cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes. Heaven.  Thanks, Wendy for bringing a bit of home to me in CA!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the real chocolate chip cookies   neiman marcus   copycat

this is the same cookie recipe that was posted on the neiman marcus web site.

1. cream the butter with the sugars until fluffy
2. beat in the egg and the vanilla extract
3. combine the dry ingredients and beat into the butter mixture
4. stir in the chocolate chips
5. drop by large spoonfuls onto a greased cookie sheet
6. bake at 375 for 8-10 minutes or 10-12 minutes for a crispier cookie
demonstrations.review: This past year, I discovered the NM Chocolate Chip Cookie recipe on their website http://www.neimanmarcus.com/store/service/nm_cookie_recipe.jhtml.  I have taken them to several book club meetings, dinner parties and get togethers and everyone has raved about these cookies.  My friend, Erin, says these are the best cc cookies that she has ever had.  One of the things that differs from your recipe is the baking temperature and time.  The recipe on the NM website has the cookies baking at 300 degrees for about 20 minutes.  I tried it and discovered that this makes for the most perfectly baked cookie EVER.  Yes, it takes longer, but it is well worth it!  I highly recommend that you try it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
keema

this, surprisingly, is a requested dish from the kids. it is unusual, spicy and very indian.

1. heat large skillet over medium-high heat
2. add beef and cook , stirring until browned , about 5 minutes
3. add next 7 ingredients
4. reduce heat to medium and cook , stirring , until onions are translucent , 3 minutes
5. add broth and peas
6. cook until broth is reduced and peas are are hot
7. 2 minutes
8. serve with rice and condiments: chutney , chopped peanuts chopped fresh cilantro and sour cream
9. we keep minced ginger in a small container in the freezer compartment and make chicken broth from the bones whenever we have chicken and keep a bottle of chutney around just for this dish
10. one small jalapeno is sufficient if not generous for the amount
11. warning
12. this dish is too small for our family of eaters
13. we double it and have extra food the next day
demonstrations.review: Ever have one of those days when you hardly have any food in the house, have no time to go grocery shopping and need to get dinner on the table now?!  Today was that day for me.  I made this substituting a 1.25 lbs. package of ground turkey for the beef, a 15 oz. can of garbanzo beans (drained and rinsed) for the peas and 25% increase in the seasonings and it was REALLY GOOD.  DH called me at class to ask if he had to save me some!  Thanks for saving my day; I will be making this again.  PS  While the garbanzo beans were good in a pitch, the peas are much better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
huli huli bbq chicken

jumped out at me while leafing through the august '08 issue of "cuisine at home."  according to the article, this grilled chicken is cooked and sold from roadside stands in hawaii. i haven't tried it yet, but it sounds wonderful.   at first sight it looks like a lot of work, but i bet it isn't. just a lot of ingredients. if you make it before me, let us all  know how it is, o.k?

1. whisk all ingredients together in a bowl
2. place drumsticks in half the pineapple juice mixture in a large resealable plastic bag
3. refrigerate 1 hour
4. reduce remaining mixture in a saucepan over medium-high heat until thickened
5. set aside for basting
6. preheat grill to high
7. when hot , turn off one burner , leaving the other lit
8. remove drumsticks from marinade
9. arrange on unlit portion of the grill
10. cook chicken to an internal temperature of 165 degrees
11. baste with reserved glaze regularly
12. turn after 20 minutes
13. continue basting until done
demonstrations.review: Wow!  My DH and I just finished eating grilled chicken using this recipe and I couldn't wait to review it.  I have been trying lots of different grilled/barbecued chicken recipes lately and this one is THE WINNER.  Since we like things spicy sweet, I did substitute 1 Tbsp. of the ketchup for Asian Chili Garlic Sauce (sriracha).  It gave it the perfect amount of heat for us.  Thanks for this recipe; we will be making this often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey curry with raisin rice

i haven't been a huge fan of curries, but i absolutely adored this one from a diane mott davidson book (the killer pancake), so now i'm trying out other curries from this site.  since i don't see this great one already posted, i'm adding it for your culinary enjoyment.

i didn't make my own stock, i bought a box at the store, but chicken broth would probably work just as well. it's mostly just to add flavor to the rice. the recipe originally listed white rice, but i substituted brown since i rarely use white rice. i bet popcorn rice would also be good. for the new year's party that i was attending, it was easier to just stir the meat and the rice all together and take it as a casserole rather than serving it as two items, and that worked out just fine. i used skim milk and non-fat dry milk to keep fat content lower, and did not notice any affect on the finished product.

i suggest getting the rice started before preparing the curry since it takes a while to cook.

1. turkey curry: saute the ground turkey until evenly browned
2. drain fat and set aside
3. in a greased or non-stick skillet , saute the apple and onion over medium heat , stirring frequently , until the onion is translucent
4. set aside
5. reduce heat to low and heat the olive oil
6. stir in the flour and curry powder until the flour begins to bubble
7. combine the bouillon granules , milk and dry milk
8. whisk until combined
9. gradually add the milk mixture to the curry mixture , continuing to stir over medium-low heat until the mixture thickens
10. when the mixture is thick , add the turkey and the apple-onion mixture
11. stir well and heat through
12. serve over raisin rice
13. raisin rice: in a large nonstick skillet , toast 1 cup raw rice over medium heat , stirring frequently , until most of the rice is brown
14. stir in raisins and chicken stock
15. bring to a boil , reduce heat to low , cover the pan , and cook for 25 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed
demonstrations.review: I don't understand why more people haven't tried this recipe; it so easy and so GOOD!  I didn't have the dry milk, so I left it out but otherwise made as directed.  My DH and I loved it!  We love curry, so after trying it as is, I did add some more due to our personal preference.  Thanks for posting this; it's perfect for an easy weeknight dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with spinach  feta and olives

mediterranean-inspired salad served warm. also delicious cold. don't add salt - the feta, olives and capers provide plenty. a short sturdy pasta works best such as bowties, shells, elbows.

1. in a large bowl , whisk olive oil , vinegar and garlic
2. add remaining ingredients and toss to mix
3. the spinach will wilt from the hot pasta
4. season with pepper to taste
5. garnish with more cheese crumbles if desired
6. though it's delicious refrigerator cold , i think it tastes best when served warm
demonstrations.review: I have a very similar recipe from Cooking Light that I have been making for years.  The only minor differences in our recipes are my calls for penne pasta (we like whole wheat), the garlic is crushed and the pepper is omitted in mine.  My family loves it.  I like a "wetter" pasta, so I often double the olive oil and balsamic vinegar and add a bit extra crushed garlic.  I've misplaced this recipe a couple of times, so thank you, Kathy228, for posting.

target.recipe_text:
philadelphia truffles appy

another recipe from the best of cooking by arne kruger & annette wolter ... love the idea, name & make-ahead or emergency quick-fix! (time shown does not include the 2 chilling periods & pls see note at end of prep) *enjoy*

1. mix 1st 5 ingredients & chill for 30 minutes
2. crumble the pumpernickel bread as finely as possible
3. form the cheese mixture into sml balls & coat w / the pumpernickel crumbs
4. chill for a further 30 minutes & serve
5. open freeze till solid , then pack in layers w / dividers in a rigid container
6. allow to defrost to room temp when ready to serve
7. "
target.review: This is a very tasty appetizer! I followed the recipe closely (the only exception was that I used low fat cream cheese), and  I wouldn't change anything the next time around. I used my hand-blender to make the bread into crumbs; I don't think I would have gotten small enough crumbs otherwise. I got 24 cheese balls out of this (each was the size of a rounded teaspoon). Thanks for sharing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried tuna rice salad

my mom used to make this dish as a meal for hot summer evenings.

1. combine mayo , curry , lemon juice and salt
2. chill
3. combine tuna , rice , carrots , celery and onion
4. toss with mayo mixture and chill at least 2 hours
demonstrations.review: I really liked this a lot. This yielded four quite large and filling servings, so it would probably serve a lot more people with smaller appetites than my own. :) I followed the recipe exactly as written, with the exception of using low fat mayo instead of the full fat stuff. I wouldn't change anything the next time I make it (I'd use low fat again). This was good on its own, but it also makes a nice sandwich filling (I ate it in a tortilla). Thanks for sharing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quinoa black bean salad

this is really easy to make. there were no leftovers! what a great combination of flavors and textures. serve with tortilla chips on the side.

1. cook the quinoa in the water
2. allow to cool slightly
3. in a large bowl , combine the oil , lime juice , cumin , coriander , cilantro and scallions
4. stir in the beans , tomatoes , bell peppers and chilies
5. add the cooled quinoa
6. season with salt and pepper to taste
7. serve cold
demonstrations.review: Delicious and light. I used a little extra lime juice, coriander, and cumin, and replaced the bell pepper with corn. This was so easy to make...I bet I'll make it again later this week (a double batch this time). Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate and orange buttercream pound cake

the buttercream is so good you will want to eat it by itself! prep time includes chilling. enjoy

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. place wax paper on ungreased bottom of a 91 / 2x51 / 2 inch loaf pan
3. chocolate cake: put all ingredients in a large bowl
4. beat 5 minutes with electric mixer , starting at low speed and increasing to high when flour is no longer visible
5. pour into pan and bake 45-50 minutes or until center of cake springs back when touched lightly with your finger
6. cool 10 minutes and loosen sides with metal spatula
7. cool completely on a cake rack then slice horizontally into 3 layers
8. orange cream: cream butter at high speed with electric mixer until light in color
9. add heavy cream , 1 tbsp at a time , beating well after each addition
10. add orange jam 1 tbsp at a time
11. spread mixture between cake layers
12. topping: pour whipping cream in a bowl and freeze 40 minutes before beating
13. beat at high speed with electric mixer for 2-3 minutes or until thick and spreadable
14. use to ice layer cake
15. drizzle with liquid chocolate over icing
16. decorate top center with canned mandarin oranges
17. chill until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: Awesome cake! The orange frosting and rich chocolate cake combo were really great. I made a few small changes, as follows: I used an 8-inch square cake pan, I didn't use the mandarin orange or chocolate syrup toppings, and I added a little bit of sugar to the whipped cream frosting. Thanks for sharing this recipe; we really loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious cauliflower n cheese sandwich filling

this is a personal favourite of mine. i found this recipe in anjali vellody's foodcourt column of the weekend magazine. hope you enjoy it!

1. heat oil in a non-stick pan
2. add onion and stir-fry until its transparent
3. add cauliflower and stir-fry for 4 minuts
4. add corriander , cumin , garam masala and red chilli powder
5. mix in the grated maggi cube powder
6. add few tbsps
7. of water to cook the cauliflower
8. cook until the mixture is dry
9. add chopped corriander , mint and grated cheese
10. mix well
11. transfer this filling onto a plate and allow to cool
12. divide it into 2 portions
13. place each portion between 2 bread slices
14. toast in a sandwich toaster
15. serve hot
16. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was even better than I expected! I wasn't too sure about using cheddar with Indian spices, but the combo was really quite good. I used flour tortillas instead of bread and used a little more cheddar than called for, but otherwise followed the recipe closely. Thank you for posting; I'm sure I'll be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bisquick chocolate chip bars

so easy, incredibly yummy and chewy. the recipe calls for 1 cup of chocolate chips but i use about 1 and a half.  ***update***just an added note, i've used a copycat version of bisquick and it turns out very greasy so you might want to reduce the oil content if you are using a homemade baking mix.

1. combine all ingredients except chips
2. spread in a 13 x 9-inch pan , greased and floured
3. sprinkle chocolate chips over top
4. bake 25-30 minutes at 350
demonstrations.review: This recipe turned out absolutely perfect for me. I used "Heart Smart" Bisquick (I don't know, really, why it is heart-smart, but it claimed to be healthy and I bought it :) ), 1/4 cup oil, 1/2 cup brown sugar, and 1 cup white sugar. I also mixed in the chocolate chips. These were chewy and delicious...they didn't last long. Thanks for posting this!!

target.recipe_text:
real crab bisque

adapted from best of the best of georgia. a recipe supposedly from elizabeth of 37th restaurant. a nice way to serve this is in hollowed out individual bread rounds as bowls.

1. melt butter over low heat
2. mince green onion , celery , and carrot in food processor , then add to the butter , cover& sweat until tender , approximately 5 minutes
3. whisk in flour and cook 2 minutes , stirring constantly
4. whisk in chicken broth and milk
5. bring to a boil , whisking often
6. when it comes to just a boil , quickly stir in cream , seasonings , sherry and crabmeat
7. heat through , then serve
target.review: This was an amazing dish!  Very big hit with the family and friends. The only things I changed were to put more carrots in it for more color and I used regular chicken broth and butter instead of unsalted because it was a little bland the first time I made it. Definitely going in my recipe box!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
upside down berry crostada

from giada de laurentiis -  everyday italian...yummy!

1. to make the crust , combine the flour , 2 tablespoons sugar , lemon zest , and salt in a food processor and pulse to blend
2. add the butter and pulse until the mixture resembles a coarse meal
3. add the ice water , 1 tablespoon at a time , and pulse until moist clumps form
4. gather the dough into a ball then flatten into a disk
5. wrap the dough in plastic and refrigerate until firm , about 1 hour
6. preheat the oven to 400f
