demonstrations.review: Oh boy--these are fantastic. I used russets and sweet potatos and doubled up on the spices. Really delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave poached egg on toast

this recipe came with my very first microwave 20+ years ago. it makes an easy, quick, no mess breakfast.

1. place the toast on a plate , butter it , flatten the middle down with the back of a fork
2. crack and carefully pour the egg into the flattened middle of the toast , not allowing it to spill over into the plate
3. prick the yolk quickly and carefully with the tines of the fork and bake in the microwave on a turntable for about 1 minute on 60-70% power , until the white is cooked through or desired doneness is achieved
demonstrations.review: I poach eggs in the microwave all the time because it is so quick and requires no added fat. I would suggest putting the egg in a bowl with a T or 2 of water, pricking the yolk, and cooking for about 60 seconds or so. Just watch it until it is done, as each microwave is different. Meanwhile toast up the bread in a toaster and butter it up a bit (or not). When the egg is done, drain the water off and put it on top of the toast. You can also put the egg and some mayo in between two slices of bread for a to-go sandwich. Nothing fancy, but it is quick and tastes good enough.

target.recipe_text:
poppy seed chicken baseballs weight watchers style

this is a variation on the popular, weight watchers cult-like recipe, chicken baseballs.  i am told the basic recipe is 8 points per serving.  paired with a green salad, this makes a fantastic dinner.  

i tried this variation based on an old, but very high fat recipe that my family loved - this lighter recipe really tastes great, and the kids love it, too!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. add cream cheese , margarine , salt , pepper , milk , and poppy seeds in small bowl
3. microwave for about 30 seconds and stir
4. pour mixture over cooked , finely cubed chicken and stir
5. divide chicken mixture into 4 portions
6. separate dough into four rectangles , careful to seal perforations
7. two triangles will make up each rectangle
8. lay each rectangle over a pinch of the cracker crumbs to keep them from sticking to your work surface , then add 1 / 4 of the chicken into the middle of each , pull up the corners , then seal the edges to make a "baseball" shape
9. then sprinkle a small amount of cracker crumbs over the entire area of the dough , and place seam side down on parchment lined cookie sheet , or an ungreased cookie sheet
10. bake for 20 minutes or until lightly browned
target.review: I was going to give this a three or four since I did not care for them much when they were warm.  But I got one out after they were chilled and they made a seriously yummy chicken salad in nice doughy pastry puff.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers baked potato soup

i had this for lunch today and really liked it. i hope you do, too! it is 5 points per serving.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. wrap entire garlic bulb tightly in foil
3. place garlic and potatoes in oven
4. bake garlic until soft when squeezed , about 45 minutes
5. remove from oven and let cool
6. continue baking potatoes until tender when pierced , about 15 minutes more
7. let potatoes stand until cool enough to handle
8. meanwhile , cook bacon in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until browned , about 6 minutes
9. place bacon on paper towels to drain off any fat
10. chop bacon
11. unwrap garlic and squeeze pulp from bulb with hands into a large saucepan
12. peel potatoes and add to saucepan
13. mash with a potato masher until smooth
14. gradually stir in broth , thyme , salt and pepper until blended
15. place saucepan over medium heat and cook until hot , stirring occasionally , about 5 to 10 minutes
16. spoon about 1 1 / 3 cups of soup into each of 6 soup bowls
17. top each with 1 tablespoon of sour cream , 1 tablespoon of cheese , 1 rounded tablespoon of bacon and 1 tablespoon of scallions
18. grind fresh pepper over top if desired
demonstrations.review: Maybe I missed something when I was making the soup, but it came out fair. I ate it and it was not terrible, but if I were out to eat it would not be something I would order again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fig preserves

this recipe is posted by request.

1. wash figs gently in cold water
2. place in a large bowl , fill with cool water and soak for 20 minutes
3. make a syrup by boiling the sugar and water together in a large saucepan
4. when syrup is clear and just thick , around 15 minutes add figs and lemon slices
5. bring to a boil over high heat
6. boil hard 1 minute
7. lower heat and simmer for 30 minutes
8. remove from heat
9. carefully pour into a blender and pulse to grind figs and lemon slices
10. you may want to cook down for 10 or 15 more minutes to desired thickness
11. ladle into clean hot sterile jars and process in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was so easy to make and was totally scrumptious. I liked that I did not have to peel the figs. Fantastic recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super easy general tso chicken

this is not authentic general tso's chicken, but it's a recipe i developed and it tastes quite similar.  it's easy and requires no "odd" ingredients.  you can either batter your chicken before adding to the sauce or just stir-fry your plain chicken, it's up to you.  this makes plenty of sauce- i don't like dry general tso's. after reading several reviews,  i would just like to add that i must use very mild hot sauce, because i am definitely not someone who likes super-hot stuff and several have complained that it's too hot.  i would have to say that it probably varies according to your brand of hot sauce, so be warned!  :-)

1. mix the soy sauce , water , hot sauce , sugar , boullion , and ginger in a saucepan and heat until boiling
2. cut the heat down and simmer while you prepare the chicken
3. take your chicken and cut into bite-size cubes
4. now , at this point you can either use a boxed batter mix to add a coating on it , or you can just stir-fry your plain chicken in a little oil until thoroughly cooked
5. going back to your sauce , use the cornstarch in water to thicken it
6. then add your cooked chicken
7. if you battered your chicken , it's ready to eat
8. if you stir-fried plain chicken , use this time to simmer it awhile and prepare your veggies and rice
9. serve this chicken over the veggies and rice
demonstrations.review: This was really authentic tasting with minimal fuss. I tweaked for personal  taste and it was fantastic. I added green onions, some pepper flakes and less tobasco sauce, a splash or rice vinegar and some minced garlic. I also did not use real sugar, I used the natural sweetener erythritol. This was served over brown rice. I will soooo be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted chickpeas   ww core

these are a wonderful alternative to nuts.  snack on them, or use them to top salads.  you can easily double this recipe, store them in zip-top bags or airtight containers.  you can also experiment with various spices or seasoning mixes in addition to the garlic powder.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. rinse and drain chickpeas
3. lightly coat baking sheet with nonstick spray
4. spread chickpeas on baking sheet and sprinkle with garlic powder , salt and pepper
5. toss to coat
6. bake on bottom rack of oven , shaking pan every 15 minutes
7. bake 45 to 50 minutes , until browned and crunchy
8. cool completely before serving
demonstrations.review: I was not to thrilled with this recipe. My daughter tried them and told me they tasted like partially popped popcorn kernels. I tasted them again and she was right. If you are into the last of the popcorn kernels, you might really like them, but it is not really for me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers milk shake  flex or core

this is from a very old weight watchers pamphlet for week one of the diet. i love this milk shake. it's surprisingly thick and tasty.

1. place all ingredients in blender
2. blend until all ice is crushed and milk shake is thick
3. it really does become thick
demonstrations.review: If you are expecting a McDonald's milkshake or Arby's- it is not going to happen. But, if you are on WW Core or Flex this will be a surprisingly wonderful treat. It is thinner then a regular milkshake, but still has a great ice cream taste. I added a little more ice and some sugar-free pudding to thicken it up. Then I topped it with lf whipped topping. I will so be making this again!

target.recipe_text:
no fail crock pot beef stew

this stew tastes like you've been slaving and it's the easiest recipe ever! i usually throw everything in the crock pot right before i go to bed.

1. layer vegetables in the crock pot as listed above , then add beef
2. mix the soups and water together and pour over all
3. put crock pot on low
4. cook all night and the next evening your beef stew will be ready
5. be sure and check in the morning to see if a little water needs to be added
target.review: Wonderful Stew!  I followed the basic recipe but added mushrooms, 4 or 5 glugs of shiraz wine, and in the last hour @ 1/2 a bag of frozen peas.  I did screw up the timing so instead of over night and all day, I had it in the crock pot on high for 3 hours and on low for 4 hours - it was done and turned out wonderful.  This recipe is obviously very adaptable.  Will make it often and not worry about adding additional ingredients/seasonings.  Maybe next time some garlic? chopped onions or pearl onions instead of quarters? mixed veggies instead of peas? no peas?  I'm rambling. It was very good and deserves 5 stars.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mini ham   cheese cups

these are tasty little appetizers that are enjoyed by both kids and adults. they are also easy to make.

1. in a bowl , combine the first six ingredients
2. set aside
3. divide crescent roll dough into 24 portions
4. press into greased miniature muffin cups
5. spoon 1 tablespoon ham mixture into each cup
6. bake at 350 degrees for 13-15 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: I Love These! Fantastic taste, easy to make, and popular with the crowd! Used cheddar/monteray jack cheese cause that's all I had.  Although. I must have a heavy hand with tablespoons.  I tripled the recipe and should have had enough filling for 72 roll cups.  I eeked out 40 instead.  That's okay, I'll know better next time.  I filled the rest with mixtures of cheese and garlic and cheese and bacon bits.  Thanks for the great recipe!  It's a keeper!  Kris

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange splash

a refreshing drink for the kids on a hot summer day. works great for an after school snack. how about a morning drink for the whole family!

1. put ice cubes into electric blender , start so that the cubes break up
2. put the remaining ingredients into blender and blend until smooth
3. serve
demonstrations.review: Well now you went and did it! I love OJ, but have bad reactions to it (Can you say tomato face?) Made Orange Splash for Easter Breakfast. How Refreshing! (and DELICIOUS). Drank way more than I should have - I just couldn't resist. The blend of OJ, milk, and almond extract is a wonderful combination that is just too enticing.  I'll be making it again soon.  Thanks Charlotte

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy baked potato wedges

we love these potatoes, they are simple to make and taste great!

1. wash potatoes , cut into wedges
2. place potatoes skin down in a baking dish
3. mix the next 6 ingredients together and brush onto potatoes
4. bake at 350 for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Heaven! I'm in Heaven! Made these tonight with sweet potatoes and good ole Idahos.  The Idahos were good and deserved 5 stars.  The sweet potatoes were MAGNIFICENT!  Sweet and spicey, melt in your mouth taste.  I'll make these again as soon as I buy more sweet potatoes!  Used olive oil, fresh parmesan, bottled garlic powder, salt, black pepper & sweet paprika.  Didn't have a brush, so I mixed everything in a small bowl, dipped the end of the wedges in the mix & smoothed on the mixture with a spatula.  Worked great & had plenty of the mixture.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kaleidoscopic vegetables

this is a delightful dish to serve during the fresh vegetable harvest time. it can be prepared ahead of time and baked just before serving.

1. clean and cut mushrooms in half
2. slice zucchini and yellow squash in 1 / 2 slices
3. slice onion into 1 / 4 inch rings
4. place butter in glass measuring cup or any microwave safe bowl
5. melt in microwave on high
6. add dill , tarragon , salt and pepper to butter and mix well
7. place veggies in flat 3 quart oven-safe casserole
8. pour butter mixture over veggies and toss to coat
9. bake at 325 degrees for 30 minutes
10. vegetables will still be semi-crunchy
11. you may bake an additional 15-20 minutes if you prefer your vegetables not crunchy
demonstrations.review: Great dish! Nice mixture of color and taste. Transported to our Thanksgiving dinner. Cut up veggies the night before. Followed recipe exactly except only used 3 zucchini & 5 yellow squash and 1/2 lb. mushrooms. The tomatoes & onion amount I kept the same as the recipe.  The 9"x13" pan was HEAPING with veggies. Split them between Two (1 gallon)ziploc bags, melted butter and seasonings, poured onto veggies in bags, sealed and mixed.  They sat for 6 hours before I dumped them into the pan and baked them. Enjoyed by all. Fed more than 8 people - and still had some left over.  Received compliments from everyone.  Thanks Susie! NOTE: Very easy to transport using the ziploc bags.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cucumber salad swedish style

a very different way to fix cucumbers. a great go-a-long with summer meals.

1. wash cucumbers , dry off and remove the ends
2. score the skins with the tines if a fork , dragging it the length of the cuke
3. repeat all the way around
4. slice cucumbers very , very thin
5. place in a bowl
6. sprinkle with salt and sugar
7. add vinegar and press slightly with back of a spoon
8. cover and refrigerate overnight
9. keeps well in a covered jar
10. the end result is similar to an uncooked pickle
demonstrations.review: My Mom made this also.  I think it's one of the reasons I like cucumbers so much.  It's refreshing and because of the sugar is not sour. Really perks up your mouth with a nice tang.

target.recipe_text:
gnocchi   tomato bake  with freezing instructions

this sounds good for anybody looking for a quick and tasty meal. it is vegetarian too which is always great in my books. i originally found this recipe in the september 2008 copy of the bbc good food magazine.  the recipe states that the dish can be frozen for up to a month.  it says to just defrost and bake in a medium oven for 20 - 30 minutes until piping hot.

1. heat grill / broiler to high
2. heat the oil in a large frying pan , then soften the onion and pepper for 5 minutes
3. stir in the garlic , fry for 1 minute ,
4. bubble for 10 to 15 minutes , stirring occasionally , until gnocchi is soft and the sauce has thickened
5. season , stir through the basil , then transfer to a large ovenproof dish
6. scatter with the mozzarella , then grill / broil for 5 to 6 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden
7. this dish can be frozen for up to a month
8. just defrost and bake in a medium oven for 20 - 30 minutes until piping hot
target.review: This is incredibly easy, especially if you use a mini food processor to chop the onions and pepper.  It's tasty, but just a small step up from pouring pre-made sauce on gnocchi... nothing special.  I used a 14.5 oz bag of frozen gnocchi straight out of the freezer and cooking it in the sauce worked just fine.  I made the recipe even easier because I didn't bother broiling it in the oven - the cheese melted when I added it to the frying pan and I didn't feel the need to make it golden or crispy.  I used more mozzarella than called for, since it came in an 8 oz package... why not use it all?  Next time I will increase the sauce.  I may try adding other things... mushrooms, broccoli, artichokes...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried cauliflower bake

southern living; this is a wonderful way to use garden fresh cauliflower. also very quick and easy.

1. cut cauliflower into floweret
2. cook in boiling water to cover with 1 / 2 t
3. salt 10 minutes or until tender
4. drain
5. arrange cauliflower in a lightly greased 8-inch square baking dish
6. mix together soup , cheese , mayo , butter , and curry powder
7. pour over cauliflower
8. bake at 350 for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very simple and yummy.  The curry isn't the main event... it contributes a nice, subtle flavor.  That makes this side dish easier to pair with a main dish; it doesn't clash with a lot of flavors like some of the other curry cauliflower recipes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate s mores fudge cake

i had this at my parents house today. my daddy made it and we all loved it.  if you love peanut butter and chocolate, you will love this!!! great for church socials and other gatherings. ***note*** wherever you see "(*optional)", that is where my daddy added that little something extra into the original recipe. i hope you try it and like it!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease and flour a 9-by-13-inch pan
3. combine sugar , flour , baking soda and "optional" pudding mix in bowl
4. in a saucepan over medium heat , bring butter , vanilla , cocoa , water , buttermilk and eggs to a rolling boil , stirring occasionally
5. pour over dry ingredients and mix well
6. bake 25 minutes , until center bounces back when lightly touched
7. cool cake completely
8. combine peanut butter and peanut oil in bowl and spread over cake
9. sprinkle with marshmallows
10. prepare chocolate fudge frosting:in a saucepan over medium heat combine butter cocoa buttermilk vanilla and optional karo
11. bring to a boil , stirring constantly
12. remove from heat and stir in confectioners' sugar
13. stir or whisk until smooth
14. while still warm , pour over evenly over marshmallows
15. allow frosting to set 5-10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Not bad, but I think I'm spoiled from having the classic Rocky Road Fudge bars, which are brownies with S'more toppings instead of cake.  I found myself wanting the base to be more dense and less cakey.  Love the layer of peanut butter and followed another reviewer's advice to just nuke it into spreading consistency (who wants to my peanut oil just for one recipe?).  FYI, substitution for buttermilk: put 1/2 Tblsp of cider vinegar or lemon juice in 1/2 cup measuring cup and add enough milk to fill the cup..  For the 6 tablespoons of buttermilk, I added 1 tsp of cider vinegar to 1/3 cup and added the milk... then dolloped in just a little extra since 1/3 cup is a little short.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked orzo with fontina and peas

a giada recipe, it looked so good i had to put it here for safe keeping.

1. preheat the oven to 400 degrees f
2. butter a 9 x 13 baking dish
3. bring the chicken broth to a boil over medium-high heat in a medium saucepan
4. add the orzo and cook until almost tender , about 7 minutes
5. pour the orzo and the broth into a large bowl
6. set aside
7. meanwhile , melt the butter over medium heat in a medium skillet
8. add the oinions and saute until tender , about 3 minutes
9. add the mushrooms and continue to saute until the mushrooms are beginning to turn golden around the edges , about 7 minutes
10. add the marsala
11. scrape the brown bits off the bottom of the pan and cook unti lthe marsala has reduced by half , about 5 minutes
12. add the mushroom mixture to the orzo in the large bowl
13. add the cream , fontina , mozzarella , peas , salt & pepper
14. stir to combine
15. pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish
16. in a small bowl combine the bread crumbsd , parmesan , and dried thyme
17. sprinkle the bread crumb mixture on top of the pasta
18. bake until golden , about 25 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This has a fantastic flavor, but I wanted more stuff in the orzo. The second time I made this, I doubled both the mushrooms and the peas and I was much happier. I also decided since I couldn't buy less than 8 oz of Fontina, I might as well just use all Fontina and leave out the mozzarella. This also worked well. The marsala and thyme are a lovely combination.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome penne spinach bake

spinach and pasta mixed with the most delicious cream sauce, topped of with a breadcrumb/cheese topping, then baked in the oven. your gonna love this one! prep time includes boiling the pasta.

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 13" x 9" baking pan
3. cook the pasta only to firm-tender according to package directions
4. drain , set aside
5. in a heavy-bottomed saucepan , melt the butter over med-high heat
6. add in the chopped onion and the garlic
7. saute for 5 minutes
8. whisk in the flour , thyme , nutmeg and black pepper
9. cook for 2 minutes , stirring constantly
10. gradually whisk in the half and half
11. cook for 4 minutes , until thick and bubbly
12. add in the grated swiss cheese , and the parmesan cheese
13. mix well over low heat , until the cheese has melted , and the sauce is hot and bubbly
14. remove the saucepan from the heat
15. in a large bowl , combine the cream / cheese sauce , 1 / 2 cup of the remaining swiss cheese , chopped tomato , and the spinach
16. stir well
17. spoon the mixture into a prepared greased baking pan
18. in a small bowl , combine the breadcrumbs , melted butter and the parmesan cheese
19. sprinkle the mixture over the casserole in the baking pan
20. bake for 30 minutes , or until hot and bubbly
demonstrations.review: This was pretty easy to make, but I found it to be a bit bland... it just needed a little tang from something. When something has that much cream and cheese, it needs to knock my socks off. I cooked the sauce in the same pot as I used to cook the pasta. Then I skipped the extra bowl and just mixed everything in the pot before pouring into the baking dish. I used the whole tsp of thyme and 3 plum tomatoes, but it still needed something more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curry  feta  and garlic dip

this is a great dip, very easy to prepare and a big hit at parties and get togethers. i get asked for this recipe quite alot...hope you like it! serve with crackers or fresh veggies.

1. mix all well with food processor or mixer until smooth
2. more or less garlic and curry may be added according to taste
3. refrigerate well , and serve with crackers or fresh veggies
demonstrations.review: Wonderful flavor. I kept adding a little more curry, tasting and adding just a bit more. I probably only got to about 3/4 tsp and decided that was enough tweaking for the first try. Next time, I'll go to a full tsp. I will caution that the dip was gritty right out of the food processor, but I let it age overnight and all the gritty was gone the next day. Aging lets the flavors blend better anyway.

target.recipe_text:
best roast potatoes ever

i can hear you thinking “everyone knows how to do roast potatoes”, but bear with me; following this recipe has given me the best never-fail perfect roast potatoes ever!  golden and crisp on the outside, soft and fluffy inside.  there are other recipes posted on recipezaar, but i’ve checked them and these directions are different!  obviously it helps if you use a variety of potato that is especially suitable for roasting (such as maris piper, king edward or desiree), but this recipe really will give you beautifully roasted potatoes that don’t stick to the pan - the secret to success is in step 2.

1. preheat the oven to 400 f , 200 c , gas mark 6
2. peel the potatoes and cut them into evenly sized halves or chunks
3. put the potatoes into a large saucepan , cover with cold salted water and bring to the boil
4. drain the water off as soon as it comes to the boil - this step isnt to cook the potatoes: it heats them through so they start roasting more quickly - return the potatoes to the hot pan and dry them over the heat
5. slide a large baking tray into the oven to heat up for a few minutes , add the vegetable fat to the potatoes in the hot pan and let it melt
6. turn the potatoes in the melted fat until they are shiny and well coated , then
7. place the tray in the oven for about 45 minutes
8. add the bay leaves , if using , 15 minutes into the cooking time
9. turn and baste the potatoes a few times during cooking
10. to serve , lift the potatoes from the baking tray with a slotted spoon , sprinkle with sea salt if desired:
target.review: Thank you Mrs B! I've tried a few other recipes but never got the right texture. These are indeed crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. I used butter flavored crisco since that's all I had. This is a great recipe on it's own but next time I think I may add some chives, lemon and oregano or ranch dressing powder.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
better than sex cake iii

it is my understanding that there are a variety of recipes masquerading under this name, but this is the one that my friends like most.  overnight chilling not included in preparation time.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease and lightly flour 13" x 9" cake pan
3. mix cake as directed on package
4. bake the cake about 35 minutes or until it tests done
5. as soon as it comes out of the oven , poke holes all over it with a fork and pour sweetened condensed milk evenly over the cake , followed by caramel sauce
6. refrigerate overnight
7. shortly before serving , spread whipped topping over cake and sprinkle with crushed heath bars
8. enjoy
demonstrations.review: Served this cake at a dinner party, I liked it a lot but wasn't over the moon about it. However when I threw my next party I had a few guests actually call to ask if I could make it again and asked for the recipe. So for me that makes it a 5 star recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken thighs with lemon garlic

don't be put off with large amount of garlic, this recipe is really full of flavour and has excellent sauce.  i used on the bone chicken thigh cutlets because i think the chicken has much more flavour if it's kept on the bone and it is much tender. the original recipe comes from ‘taste of the sun’ by jacqueline clark & joanna farrow but i twinkled with it to suit our family.  if you don't like a lot of salt in your diet you could use salt reduce liquid chicken stock but this will alter the flavour.

1. to make the "garlic flavoured chicken hot stock" put the stock into a pan and bring to the boil
2. add the garlic cloves and simmer gently for 40 minutes
3. strain the stock and reserve both stock and garlic
4. preheat the oven to 190oc / 375of / gas 5
5. fifteen minutes before stock is ready , heat large saut or frying pan , then add the butter and oil and allow the butter to melt
6. add the chicken thighs and cook gently on both sides until golden brown
7. transfer them to an ovenproof dish
8. distribute the garlic and lemon slices among the chicken pieces in the ovenproof dish
9. add the flour to the pan which you browned the chicken and continuously stirring for one minute
10. add the extra chicken stock , stirring constantly and scraping the bottom of the pan , and then add the hot stock to the same pan
11. stirring , until the sauce has thickened and is smooth
12. season with salt and pepper
13. then pour the sauce over the chicken , cover and cook in the oven for 40 minutes
14. serve chicken on dinner plates and garnish with chopped parsley
15. you could serve with boiled new potatoes or rice
demonstrations.review: Just ate it minutes ago, it was good, not great. The photo looked a lot more appetizing than it tasted. By the end of the cook time my sauce was runny from mixing with the natural juices from the chicken. It was very moist but despite all the garlic and lemon it wasn't the most flavorful chicken I've had lately.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast sticks   oamc

i got this basic recipe from another site but changed it a little for my family.  the original recipe called for orange juice as the liquid instead of milk.  i also added the vanilla as we think it gives it a nice flavor.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. cut each slice of bread into 3 pieces to make sticks
3. texas toast is a very thick sliced bread about 3 / 4" thick
4. you could substitute french bread if texas toast is not available
5. in a bowl , mix together melted butter , eggs , sugar , cinnamon , vanilla and milk
6. beat well
7. dip sticks into egg mixture and place on a cookie sheet that has been sprayed with cooking spray
8. if there is any dip left , you can drizzle it over the sticks
9. bake for 25 minutes on middle rack of oven
10. turn halfway through baking time
11. allow to cool
12. flash freeze on cookie sheet , remove and place in a ziploc bag
13. to reheat: place 3 sticks on a microwave-safe plate and heat on high for 1 minute until warm
14. serve with syrup
demonstrations.review: This makes a great breakfast for my toddler. I omitted the sugar and some of the butter to make it a healthier recipe. I also used regular organic wheat bread instead of texas toast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
alton brown s baked macaroni and cheese

this is in reply to a request for mac and cheese. i copied this from alton brown "good eats" from the food network. does take a bit of work, but well worth it. you can add tuna, hot dogs or any other kinds of additions you want.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large pot of boiling , salted water cook the pasta to al dente
3. while the pasta is cooking , in a separate pot , melt the butter
4. whisk in the flour and mustard and keep it moving for about five minutes making sure it's free of lumps
5. stir in the milk , onion , bay leaf , and paprika
6. simmer for ten minutes and remove the bay leaf
7. temper in the egg
8. stir in 3 / 4 of the cheese
9. season with salt and pepper
10. fold the macaroni into the mix and pour into a 2-quart casserole dish
11. top with remaining cheese
12. for the topping , melt the butter in a saut pan and toss the bread crumbs to coat
13. top the macaroni with the bread crumbs
14. bake for 30 minutes
15. remove from oven and rest for five minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Alton always gets it right. It's just fact. This was very very good. I've made a handful of highly rated recipes from this site and they were just ok. Nothing measured up to the mac and cheese I had as a kid. Even with my substitutions (2% fat cheese and skim milk although it doesn't specify and no egg) it shined.  My favorite part was the breadcrumbs. I even hid some shredded carrots in my daughter's portion.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best apple pie muffins ever

i got this  recipe from a friend.  i make these often and take them to many potlucks, office parties, the cottage, picnics, children's lunch and the list goes on. recipe from the cookbook "just the best."

1. cinnamon could be added to the batter
2. topping: in a small bowl toss together sugar , flour , butter and cinnamon until crumbly
3. set aside
4. muffins: in a large bowl whisk together brown sugar , oil , egg and vanilla until smooth
5. in a separate bowl , sift together flour , soda and salt
6. stir oil mixture into flour mixture alternately with buttermilk
7. fold in apples , mixing just until combined
8. spoon into greased muffin cups filling 3 / 4 full
9. sprinkle topping over evenly
10. bake at 350f for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown and tops spring back
demonstrations.review: Made this for a playdate with some new friends. I got compliments all around. I'm craving them again already. I think next time I'll add more apples. Also for I did change the topping. I recommend equal parts sugar, flour and butter. I couldn't stop eating the topping!

target.recipe_text:
jackie s m   m chocolate bars

these tasty treats are loved by all who like chocolate and sweets!  great for the kids and adults alike.  don't forget these luscious morsels on your cookie trays for the holidays!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a large mixer bowl , combine butter , sugars , pudding mix and vanilla
3. beat in eggs
4. add flour and baking soda , and mix well
5. stir in chocolate chips , nuts , and half the m&m candies
6. mix well
7. pour into a greased 9x13" baking pan
8. top with remaining m&m candies
9. bake for 20-25 minutes
10. cool , then cut with a sharp knife
target.review: I saw this recipe and was very excited.  I started making it and realized that there is an ERROR.  Ing. list says paking powder and the directions say baking soda.  I added baking soda, but not sure which it was suppose to be.  Typical cookie recipe calls for baking soda.  No stars because I am not sure if the chef makes it with the powder.  Mine came out great, very soft.  I also added an extra 1/4 cup of brown sugar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chunky brownie cookies

fast, easy, and so yummy! i had a brownie mix to use up, and my 4 year old was sick and needed a pick me up. thank you duncan hines! these would be great for kids to make. just 5 ingredients, and you've got great chocolate-chocolate chip cookies. and don't forget the ice cold milk to have with these!

1. heat oven to 375 , line cookie sheet with parchment paper , or grease cookie sheet
2. mix the brownie mix , egg , water and oil in a large bowl
3. stir until blended , fold in chips
4. drop by teaspoons , 2 inches apart onto prepared cookie sheet
5. bake 7-8 minutes until they are set in the center--do not overbake !
6. cool 1 minute on sheet before moving to cooling rack
demonstrations.review: Holy Chocolate Batman!  If you like chocolate then these are for you!  Very simple to make...I added some walnuts, toffee chips and chocolate chips as my brownie mix was just a milk choc mix.  Hard to tell when done.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
denny s style french toast

i do not remember where i got this recipe, but my husband says it tastes just as good as what he had at denny's. i am just amazed at all of the great reviews on this recipe!! my family loves it, so i thought i would share it here and i'm so glad i did because it seems you all love it just as much!!! thanks to all of you who have tried it!

1. mix together the eggs , milk , flour , sugar , vanilla , salt& cinnamon
2. heat a large skillet , or griddle
3. when the skillet is hot , add 1 tablespoon butter
4. if the butter smokes , your pan is too hot
5. turn down the heat
6. dip each slice of bread into the batter for 30 seconds on each side
7. let some of the batter drip off , then put in skillet
8. cook each slice 1 1 / 2-2 minutes per side until each side is golden brown
9. add more butter , if necessary , to cook all of the slices
10. to serve , put on plate , dust with powdered sugar
11. serve with butter & hot syrup
demonstrations.review:
Like this one needs another five stars, but I have a TIP!!
Mix all ingredients in the blender!  After reading some tips of the food processor, and i not having one, whipped out the blender.  When done poured in a nice round bowl to dip...great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s bakery buttercream  frosting icing

this is similar to bakery frosting and so much better than any canned!  ---  for extra fluffy frosting use heavy cream and make certain to beat for at least 3-5 minutes and remember to sift the confectioners sugar before using.  for flavor and color you can add 1-2 envelopes 3-grams each, duncan hines frosting creations flavor mix, any flavor desired.

1. in a large bowl using an electric mixer at medium speed beat together the shortening and margarine or butter with cream , salt almond extract and vanilla until smooth
2. add in sifted confectioners sugar starting with 4-1 / 2 cups
3. beat very well until smooth and fluffy , adding more confectioners sugar or cream or milk until you achieve desired consistency
4. add in the food coloring or flavor creation powder until the desired shade is achieved
demonstrations.review: ok so i am finally giving my 2 cents, not as though this needs any more wonderful reviews, but I have made this countless times and have found a few helpful tips...During the 1st step of combining I found that if I combined the ingredients as listed while i mix with my mixer it  splatters, and I mean splatters!  So i combined crisco and marg, then the other ingredients with 1 cup of the p suger.  I find that this helps keep the mess down...But the mess is definately worth it!!!!  This pipes wonderfully! and holds int he fridge for a week wonderfully.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger   steaks  with onion gravy

came up with this after trying to figure out what to do with some ground beef that needed to be cooked. i paired this with orzo, but would be equally good with mashed potatoes.

1. in a large bowl mix together beef , egg , bread crumbs , 1 package soup mix , and worcestershire sauce
2. form into 8 balls and flatten into patties
3. mix flour salt and pepper
4. dredge patties in flour mixture
5. heat large skillet over med-high heat
6. fry the patties 4 minutes each side , then remove patties to a platter
7. heat oil and saut onions until translucent , about 10 minutes
8. add the rest of the flour mixture to onions and stir to coat
9. mix broth and last package of onion soup and add to the onions
10. stir well
11. return the patties to the pan , cover and reduce heat to low
12. simmer 15-20 minutes until beef is cooked through
13. stir occasionally to make sure gravy is not sticking to bottom of the pan or clumping
demonstrations.review: This takes regular hamburger steaks to a whole new dimension!  These are fabulous!  Served with mashed taters and corn...HINT!  only had one package of onion soup mix.  Used it for the gravy portion and used dried onion, beef boulion cube mashed up, little bit of sugar ( as called for in the copycat recipie).  Also didn't have beef broth, so I used 3 cups warm water crushed a beef cube and added the onion soup mix...yummmm

demonstrations.recipe_text:
luscious lemon lush

cool and refreshing. a perfect dessert. and so quick to put together.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. mix butter , flour and 3 / 4 cup nuts
3. press into a 9 x 13 inches glass baking dish
4. bake 15 - 18 minute
5. mix cream cheese , powdered sugar and 1 cup cool whip
6. spread over cooled crust
7. mix milk and lemon pudding
8. spread over cream cheese
9. spread 1 cup cool whip over pudding layer and sprinkle with 1 / 4 cup chopped nuts
demonstrations.review: This has always been a family favorite.  I had lost this recipe...thank goodness for Zaar!!  we will also make this after a big dinner...it's so light and refreshing

target.recipe_text:
chicken and black bean enchiladas

easy to make and a definite family pleaser.

1. julienne chicken
2. saute bacon until crisp , reserving 2 tbsp drippings
3. saute chicken and garlic in drippings until chicken is opaque
4. add 1 / 2 cup picante sauce , beans , red bell pepper , cumin and salt
5. simmer 7-8 minutes , until thick
6. stir in green onions and crumbled bacon
7. top each tortilla with 1 / 4 cup chicken mixture and 1 tbsp cheese
8. roll up and place in baking dish
9. top with remaining 1 cup picante sauce
10. bake at 350f for 15 minutes
11. top with remaining cheese and bake 3 minutes more
12. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
target.review: This is so good. We used the picante sauce and then also put a can of enchilada sauce on it too cause we like them saucy and it was a bit dry for us but other than that is was a awesome dinner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dipping oil for bread

i could eat an entire loaf of bread dipped in this tasty oil!! this is a versatile recipe, adjust the herbs and spices to your taste. this can be kept in the fridge for up to a month, bring it to room temperature and stir it before serving.

1. in a jar with a lid , combine oil , vinegar , cheese , basil , salt , pepper and garlic
2. stir , or cover and shake to blend ingredients
3. pour into small , shallow bowls or rimmed plates
4. slice or tear bread into pieces and dip into oil to eat
demonstrations.review: This is so good and easy to make. It's a great dish for to make for yourself or to take as your dish to pass at a party. I took it to a dinner party and everyone raved about it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s creamy broccoli casserole  make ahead

this is a wonderful broccoli recipe which takes only minutes to prepare once your broccoli is steamed, and may be completely made and refrigerated for up to 48 hours in advance until ready to bake. add in some cooked crumbled bacon also if desired --- the exact 
measurements do not really matter with this recipe, you can adjust all ingredients to taste, no matter how much you use the casserole will still be delicious. you will love this!

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. butter a 2-quart casserole dish
3. steam or boil the broccoli florets until just fork tender drain well then pat dry with paper towels
4. in a medium bowl combine the mayonnaise with sour cream , melted butter , garlic powder , seasoned salt , black pepper , cheddar cheese cubes and onion
5. mix well to combine
6. add in the well drained broccoli florets and mix gently with a spatula
7. transfer to prepared baking dish
8. sprinkle with grated parmesan cheese
9. bake uncovered for about 20-25 minutes or until bubbly
demonstrations.review: This was good and it did get eaten but nobody touched the leftovers. One service was enough. It was too something for me, I can't quite put my finger on what the something is but it was. Maybe too tangy or too heavy, not sure but I didn't really care for this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh orange muffins

i got this recipe from one of my sils after having them at her house. next time i make them i think i will add miniature chocolate chips!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. spray a muffin tin with non-stick cooking spray like pam and set aside
3. put orange quarters in food processor along with orange juice and process or blend until pureed
4. add egg and butter to food processor and combine
5. pour into large bowl
6. combine dry ingredients together in a separate bowl , then add all at once to orange mixture
7. stir to combine
8. fill muffin cups about 3 / 4 full
9. bake in preheated oven for 20 minutes
10. remove from oven and let stand in tin for 5 minutes before removing muffins
demonstrations.review: These were really good. I was worried about the peel so I only used half of the peel. Also I had some cherries that were on their last leg so I put about 8 cherries in too. The color was green so they didn't look that appetizing but they were good. I brought them to a meetup with kiddos and they all got gobbled up! The kids just devoured them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awful potatoes

we called them awful potatoes in the hopes that others wouldn't try them and there would be more left for us. unfortunately, everyone in the family is on to us and digs right in.

1. cook potatoes in salted water until done
2. drain and put back into the pan
3. add sour cream , cream cheese and garlic salt
4. mash
5. turn into baking dish
6. sprinkle cheddar cheese on top
7. bake in a 350 degree fahrenheit oven for 45 to 50 minutes until puffed and golden brown
demonstrations.review: This was very easy to make and prefect for making ahead but there was something about it that I just didn't like. They were too something, tangy maybe? I will say they all got eaten, there were no left overs but I don't think I'll be doing this again, something in there I didn't like. Thanks for sharing though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww 0 point weight watchers cabbage soup

you can eat as much of this 0-point weight watchers cabbage soup as you like. it's so good for you.

1. spray pot with non stick cooking spray saute onions carrots and garlic for 5 minutes
2. add broth , tomato paste , cabbage , green beans , basil , oregano and salt & pepper to taste
3. simmer for a about 5-10 minutes until all vegetables are tender then add the zucchini and simmer for another 5 or so minutes
4. i have tried different variations
5. leaving out green beans
6. adding chopped green onions in addition to the yellow onion
7. all very good
8. you can customize it a bit
demonstrations.review: I love this soup, I make it all the time. Sometimes (I'm not on weight watchers so I'm not worried about points) I'll put a little pasta in it too, yum!

target.recipe_text:
balsamic asparagus

my fav way to serve asparagus

1. prepare asparagus by washing and snapping off tough end
2. heat oil in frying pan
3. add asparagus and keep moving around in pan until changes colour add balsamic vinegar and the pepper sprinkling over all of the asparagus
4. remove from heat and cover for a few minutes to let flavours develop
5. serve
target.review: This was sooooo good! Thank you for a new way to do asparagus!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
safe to eat raw chocolate chip cookie  dough

i was searching the web for something like this. i doubled this recipe for my son's bake sale. i labeled if 

1. cream butter , and sugars together
2. blend in milk and vanilla
3. add flour and salt and mix well
4. stir in chocolate chips
demonstrations.review: This was great! Thank you for a yummy cookie dough that is safe to eat raw!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ghirardelli award winning brownies

this recipe came from the can of ghirardelli brand sweet ground chocolate and cocoa (found with the baking supplies). they were so great that i made them twice in one day! i omitted the walnuts but added the chocolate chips.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. using a spoon , stir eggs , sugar , and vanilla
3. add butter
4. sift together sweet ground chocolate , flour , salt and baking powder
5. stir into egg mixture
6. add nuts and / or chocolate chips
7. spread into 8" or 9" square baking pan
8. bake 20-30 minutes
9. for chewy brownies use 8" pan and less baking time
10. for cake like brownies use 9" pan and more baking time
11. cut into squares
demonstrations.review: ever since I found this recipe on the Ghirardelli can, it's the only brownies I make. I always omit the nuts, but that's personal preference. I tend to double the chocolate chips, which is also personal preference :)  they tend to dry out after a day, so make sure everyone eats them up fast!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy risotto

from the "better homes & gardens new cookbook"

1. melt butter in a medium saucepan
2. add onion and saute 1 minute
3. add rice , then cook and stir for 2 minutes more
4. stir in water , bouillon , and pepper
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat , cover , and simmer for 20 minutes
7. remove saucepan from heat and let stand , covered , for 5 minutes
8. rice should be tender but slightly firm , and the mixture should be creamy
9. stir in parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Very good. Found this in my BH&G cookbook and I use it for a quick side dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salmon and asparagus in foil

this is a quick and easy dinner.  pop the packets into the oven while you set the table and in 15-minutes you have a nutritious dish with virtually no clean up.  serve this with a rice or couscous dish and extra lemon on the side.  this recipe was found at another web site.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. snap the ends off asparagus spears and divide into 4 equal portions
3. spray the center of each foil sheet with non-stick cooking spray
4. place one salmon fillet in the center of each sheet , top with a serving of the asparagus and drizzle with lemon juice
5. sprinkle with fresh ground pepper and salt or seasoning blend as desired
6. bring up the sides of foil and fold top over twice
7. seal ends , leaving room for air to circulate inside the packet
8. place packets on a cookie sheet and cook in oven for 15 to 18 minutes or until salmon is opaque
9. serve with lemon wedges on the side
10. please use caution when opening the foil packs , as the steam is very hot
demonstrations.review: We loved this! We make salmon a lot, usually with teriyaki and maple on the grill. This is now in the rotation! Making for the second time right now. The first time I had pretty thick asparagus, and it didn't quite cook enough; this time I'm using thin, white asparagus. I can't wait to try this out with different veggies and flavors - tonight I sprinkled on some sweet ginger Asian seasoning at the request of my hubby. Thanks for such a great, easy recipe, with minimal work and miniscule clean up!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked tilapia parmesan

tender, flakey tilapia with a creamy herb parmesan sauce.  yum-o

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. grease baking pan
3. in small bowl , mix together the cheese , butter , mayonnaise and lemon juice , basil , onion powder , salt and pepper
4. arrange fillets in a single layer in prepared pan
5. bake for 20 - 30 minutes until done and flaky
6. remove fillets from oven and cover them with the cheese mixture on top side
7. place under broiler for 2 minutes or until the topping is browned
8. be careful not to overcook the fish
demonstrations.review: This was really good. The cheese flavor was a bit rich, but I liked that. My husband thought it needed to be a bit crispy, so next time I'll try some breadcrumbs in the mix. Very easy to make, too. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
peanut butter oatmeal chocolate chip cookies

very yummy! a nice moist, chewy cookie. no heavy baking soda aftertaste!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. cream butter and sugars together
3. add peanut butter , egg , and vanilla
4. and mix well
5. in another bowl mix dry ingredients together and add to butter mixture
6. add chips and mix well
7. either drop onto pan or roll into small balls
8. bake for about 10-12 minutes
9. cool for 5 minutes on sheet
target.review: The absolutely best chocolat chip cookie ever!  Easy to prepare and and you will have to fight off everyone who wants to hog them.  I have a secret cache where I store mine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bev s spaghetti sauce

this is a recipe i have developed over a number of years. this is the only spaghetti sauce my family will request! very easy to make. i hope your family enjoys it as much as mine does!

1. brown the ground beef , onion and garlic in olive oil with bay leaves , oregano , basil , italian seasoning , salt and pepper
2. add tomato paste , tomato sauce and diced tomatoes
3. stir well and bring to a simmer over medium heat
4. cover and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
5. use sauce to top your cooked spaghetti
6. top with sauteed mushroom
7. pass the parmesan
demonstrations.review: Absolutely fantastic!  Everyone (inclulding pickey eaters) said it was the best spaghetti sauce they had ever eaten.  Added 1/2 tsp of crushed red pepper flakes and tripled the garlic (we all love garlic), otherwise followed the recipe exactly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blue mountain blueberry pie

nan

1. have an 8-inch double crust pie shell ready
2. sort , rinse and drain blueberries
3. sprinkle lemon juice over berries
4. combine sugar , flour , lemon peel , cinnamon , nutmeg and salt
5. toss this mixture gently with the blueberries to coat well
6. put berry mixture into pie shell
7. dot with margarine
8. place second crust on top of pie , seal edges and cut 3 slashes in top to allow steam to escape
9. bake in preheated 450f oven for 10 minutes
10. lower heat to 350f and continue baking 30-35 minutes more
11. cool pie before slicing
12. it is important to use the freshest blueberries you can find
demonstrations.review: Best blueberry pie I ever made or tasted.  The only change I made was to use Splenda instead of sugar (due to a diabetic in the family), and I swear on my mother's grave that you couldn't tell the difference.  After you make this pie be sure to have a good hiding place for it!  It's that good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s fried cabbage with bacon

this makes a wonderful side dish to pork or beef, you may omit the chili flakes if desired or adjust amount to suit taste

1. in a large skillet over medium heat cook the chopped bacon until crisp and browned
2. remove to a bowl or plate and set aside
3. add in onion
4. cook stirring until softened
5. add in cabbage and broth or water and sugar
6. cook stirring until the cabbage wilts season with salt and pepper towards the end of cooking
7. stir in the cooked bacon
demonstrations.review: Made this for my "Southern Boy" exactly as written.  I had to cook it a bit longer than the recipe suggest, as SB likes it that way.  I, on the other hand, had never fried cabbage, nor tasted fried cabbage, and I was very pleased with the results.  SB said, "This is the best fried cabbage I've ever had!"

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fried green tomatoes   just like granny s

i first tried fried green tomatoes at my friend's granny's house, who lived in lousianna, about 10 years ago. boy were they good! i got her recipe and now i enjoy them every spring!

1. wash and slice tomatoes to 1 / 4-inch thick
2. in a shallow bowl , combine flour , cornmeal , salt , pepper and cajun seasoning
3. dip each tomato slice into the egg , then coat in the cornmeal mixture
4. fry on each side until golden
5. drain on paper towel
demonstrations.review: My husband declared this recipe for FGT the best he ever ate.  He actually used a word I have never heard out of his mouth to describe them, and that word is "superb."

demonstrations.recipe_text:
legal seafood style baked scallops

whenever we get back to the boston area, it's a priority to to have a meal at legal seafoods.  i recently "re-discovered" this recipe buried in old newspaper clippings. i had tried to recreate it in the past but now know i was missing the most important ingredient - buttermilk. i made it again after posting the recipe so i have edited the original description. it's even better than i remembered, you might want to try just a dash (or more) of cayenne pepper. it's delightful !

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. place scallops in a bowl , season with salt and pepper , add thyme and buttermilk and toss to coat
3. place scallops , with buttermilk , evenly in the bottom of an oven proof dish , sprinkle with cracker crumbs and top with melted butter
4. bake for 20 minutes , squeeze lemon over scallops and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious and easy.  MUST use fresh lemons!

target.recipe_text:
green beans with cherry tomatoes

this makes for a pretty dish and is easy to assemble. if you don't have the fresh vegetables on hand, you can easily adapt with canned goods. i get requests for the recipe all the time.

1. cook beans in water , until tender
2. in a fry , melt butter and add garlic salt , sugar , basil , salt and pepper
3. swish cherry tomato halves around until barely soft and heated , but not squishy
4. add the drained beans and mix well
target.review: I used 2 cloves fresh pressed garlic, substituted Splenda for the sugar, 1/2t dried basil for fresh(it's late winter here) and used 3/4lb fresh green beans. I'm not sure how many pints 2c of tomatoes are, but 2c are what I used. Excellent!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops and sauerkraut

the apple and wine (or rum) add a slight sweetness to the dish which counteracts the bite of the sauerkraut. goes nicely with herb-roasted potatoes.

1. season the pork chops with salt and pepper
2. heat a skillet and oil lightly
3. brown chops on both sides , and remove them from skillet
4. in remaining oil and residue , saute the onion and apple , till they begin to color
5. add the white wine or rum to the skillet
6. add the sauerkraut with about half of its liquid to your pan
7. combine well with onion-apple mixture
8. add the chops back to the pan , atop the sauerkraut mixture
9. cover and simmer for approximately 20 minutes
10. remove cover and cook off any remaining liquid , moving chops to the bottom of the pan for final browning on both sides
11. when all the liquid is gone , the dish is ready to serve
demonstrations.review:
When I prepped the vegetables and looked at the onion vs. apple ratio, I decided to double the apple. The dish smelled wonderful, but the meat was not as tender as I would hope.

I also didn't use the recommended spirit; I used Apple Schnapps, which should have made it taste even more rich.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
english toffee cookies

a simple bar cookie with nuts pressed into the top.

1. in a bowl with a mixer , beat butter with sugar until smoothly blended
2. beat in egg yolk
3. add flour to butter mixture
4. beat until well mixed
5. evenly press dough into buttered and floured 10- by 15-inch pan
6. in a bowl with a fork , beat egg white to blend
7. spread over dough with pastry brush
8. sprinkle chopped nuts over dough , then press them in
9. bake in a 275 f oven until golden brown , about 45 minutes
10. cut while hot into 1 1 / 2-inch squares
11. use a small spatula to lift from pan
12. let cool
13. serve or store airtight up to 4 days , or freeze to store longer
demonstrations.review: I'm afraid these did not taste great ~ at least to us. Perhaps more sugar, or the use of brown sugar would have helped. They were not toffee-like at all. I also had trouble brushing the egg white over the unbaked crust - crumbs kept coming up with the brush. I'm sorry that I couldn't give a more positive review.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butterfinger bars

another delightful combination of peanut butter and chocolate! easy to make cookies that taste so good! i got this recipe from a friend whom i consider the cookie goddess.

1. mix margarine , sugars and oats together and press into a greased 9x13" pan
2. bake at 350 f for 12-15 minutes
3. melt chocolate chips and peanut butter together over low heat
4. spread mixture over oatmeal base
5. allow to cool well and cut into bars
demonstrations.review: My little brother's best friend's Mom gave our Mom this recipe years ago, and I was so glad to find it again! It's good, and easy. I'll be making it for my husband this weekend with Adam's No-Stir Peanut Butter (btw, I never experienced trouble with the PB/chocolate mixture being too soft). Thanks for posting this, Whisper!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corned beef and cabbage in guinness

the irish butcher at my market gave me a new (to me anyway) recipe for corned beef & cabbage; he told me to cook it in guinness draught. (guinness stout will make the dish bitter).  since everyone raved about it, i thought i'd share the recipe he gave me. 

note: some reviewers have mentioned that the broth/sauce is very salty. it is important to rinse your corned beef in cold water before cooking it to remove some of the excess salt from the corning process. (i usually soak mine in cold water for a bit depending on the brand - some are much saltier than others).  --- i have tried 5 times today to change the wording of the last ingredient on the list from "1-2lbs carrot, peeled and cut into 3-inch pieces" to "1 - 2 pounds of carrots, peeled and cut into 3-inch pieces". every time the change "goes through," it does not reflect the new wording. grrrrrrr!

1. rinse corned beef under cold water , and pat dry
2. in a dutch oven , or other large pot with a cover , brown corned beef well on all sides over high heat
3. pour guinness over the meat , and add enough water to just cover the brisket
4. add the onion , garlic , bay leaf , cinnamon , cloves , allspice and pepper to the pot
5. bring pot to a boil and skim off any foam
6. reduce heat to a simmer
7. cover pot and simmer for 3 hours
8. add carrots , then potatoes and then the cabbage wedges to the pot
9. cover pot , and continue cooking until meat and vegetables are tender
10. remove meat and vegetables to warm serving platter / dishes , leaving the cooking liquid / sauce in the pot
11. over high heat , bring the cooking liquid to a boil , and cook until the amount of liquid is reduced by half
12. slice the corned beef
13. serve with the vegetables and the sauce on the side
demonstrations.review: This was the first time I'd seared a corned beef brisket before immersing it in liquid, and I think it made a big difference. I did use a "point' cut rather than a 'flat', since that what's was on sale this week. I also reserved the liquid from the package, and added the seasoning package that came with the brisket. We have cans of Guinness draught at home,  so that's what we used. But as for as the reduced sauce...that did not turn out well.  It smelled great, especially with the extra cinnamon, allspice, and cloves. The meat and the vegetables were wonderful, but the sauce was exceedingly salty.  Even if without any reduction, I don't think it would've been edible.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple tomato sandwich

i am only posting such a simple recipe because i actually somehow lived 29 years of life before my husband introduced me to the tomato sandwich. if you've only used tomatoes as an accessory in your sandwiches, and not as the featured ingredient, you are truly missing summer as it was meant to be tasted. note: after many years, i have solidly converted to mayo for this sandwich, with fresh ground black pepper too.  (oct 2012)

1. toast bread
2. slice tomato
3. when bread is adequately toasted , liberally spread both sides with miracle whip
4. lay tomato slices on one side of bread
5. salt tomato to taste
6. slap that baby together and savor summer at its best !
demonstrations.review: My Mom made this while we were growing up, and when I'm sick, I still crave it along with a cup of tea. Fresh, ripe tomatoes, mayonnaise, and the most refined white bread you can find come together wonderfully (though I always added a grind of pepper). Some might prefer wheat breads, but cheap, soft white breads don't compete with the tomato. Thanks so much for posting this, Ann Louise!

target.recipe_text:
vegetarian portuguese kale soup

recipe courtesy gertrude's gallery in newport, ri via $40 a day with rachael ray. here is a vegetarian version of this delicious soup.

1. in a large stock pot , heat the olive oil over medium-high heat
2. add the garlic , onions , turnips and carrots and cook for 5 minutes
3. add the kale , chorizo , bay leaves , parsley and thyme and mix well
4. add the veg
5. stock , beans and tomatoes
6. bring the soup to a boil , and then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes
7. meanwhile , in a medium saucepan , bring the salted water to a boil and add the diced potatoes
8. cook until tender , about 10 minutes
9. drain the potatoes and add them to the soup
10. remove the bay leaves and serve hot
11. enjoy !
target.review: I made this with the kale that came in my CSA box. Used some organic chicken sausage, left out the beans, added sweet potato, and didn't cook the potato separately.  Turned out really tasty. I like the flexibility of adding whatever vegetables I have.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chai spiced butternut squash soup with apple cream

whole foods

1. first , make the apple cream: combine the crme fraiche , apple cider and cinnamon in a small bowl
2. cover and refrigerate to allow the flavors to combine
3. melt the butter in a large soup pot over medium-high heat
4. add the onions and cook , stirring frequently , until translucent , about 6 minutes
5. stir in cloves , nutmeg , cinnamon , allspice , ginger and cardamom
6. cook until fragrant , stirring constantly , about 1 minute
7. stir in butternut squash , fennel , chicken stock and apple cider
8. cover , reduce heat to medium and cook until the butternut squash is tender , about 15 minutes
9. take from heat and let cool
10. blend the soup in small batches until a smooth puree is obtained
11. return to pot and stir in milk and salt
12. bring soup to a simmer
13. taste and adjust seasoning , adding more spice if desired
14. serve soup with a generous drizzle of apple cream
demonstrations.review: I really like the flavor of this soup. It had a good combination of squash, spice and apple. My only complaint was that it took a lot longer than 15 minutes to cook the squash. I make a lot of squash soup, so I'm sure to make this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach mushroom cheesy quiche

this is a really garlicious, cheesy recipe that only takes 5-10 minutes prep time

1. heat olive oil in a saute pan , toss spinach until it cooks down
2. combine fresh garlic , onions , milk , eggs & grated cheese
3. mix parmesan and garlic powder together
4. spread spinach out in the pie crust
5. pour egg mixture into crust
6. arrange mushrooms and feta over the top
7. sprinkle with parmesan / garlic mixture
8. bake for one hour at 350
demonstrations.review: I made it without a pie crust and used all cheddar cheese because I don't like feta. The flavors were good, but I will use a lot more garlic next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous barbecue sauce for chicken and ribs

this is the best barbecue sauce, and trust me i have experimented with hundreds of different combinations over the years,  this is even better than any of the popular bottled sauces! ---plan ahead this sauce must be made one day in advance to allow the flavors to blend and intensify, don't even think about using it the same day it is made,  this sauce will take on a whole different flavor when simmered for 1 hour and left overnight in the fridge--- the ingredients can easily be doubled but keep the garlic amount no more than 2 tablespoons, and for the best flavor use only heinz ketchup and a good quality brand of yellow mustard, i use french's mustard it really will make a difference in the taste, please do not omit the liquid smoke --- yield is only estimated as the sauce will reduce after simmering for 1 hour or more  ---*note* for a smoother low fat sauce omit the oil, onion and fresh garlic, then in the saucepan mix all remaining ingredients together and add in 1 teaspoon each garlic powder and onion powder then simmer for 1 hour -----you will love this sauce!

1. heat oil over medium heat
2. add in onion and saute for about 3 minutes , then add in garlic and saute for 2 minutes
3. add in chili powder , paprika , cayenne , salt and black pepper
4. stir for 1 minute
5. add in all remaining ingredients
6. bring to a boil stirring with a wooden spoon to combine
7. reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered stirring occasionally for 1 hour over low heat
8. cool to room temperature then cover and refrigerate for 24 hours or more before using
demonstrations.review:
used only 1/2 cup Ketchup, subbed 12 oz. tomato paste 1/4 water. Used Sucanat instead of brown sugar.
Used it on grilled chicken thighs, delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic skillet potatoes

an alternative to mashed or baked potatoes. great with steaks.

1. in large skillet , heat oil
2. add potatoes , onion , garlic powder , seasoned salt , pepper , and sugar
3. cook uncovered over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes or until potatoes are tender and browned
4. sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley
demonstrations.review: I made this with russet potatoes, and I cut them in skinny chunks instead of wedges, hoping they would cook quickly and evenly. I used granulated onion and garlic. The potatoes got nicely browned and crunchy with good flavor. Its a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple thai chicken spinach salad

i found this in toh and made it for dinner last night.  the dressing is especially good and the whole meal is very healthy and satisfying!

1. in a large skillet or wok , stir fry the chicken pieces in oil until juices run clear
2. remove and keep warm
3. in the same pan , stir fry the carrots and bell pepper until crisp-tender
4. in a large serving bowl , toss the spinach , green onions , and cilantro
5. set aside
6. in a blender , combine the dressing ingredients and process until well blended
7. add chicken , carrots , bell pepper , and dressing to the spinach bowl and toss to coat evenly
8. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I made this for guests last night, everybody liked it. I used some leftover chicken that I tossed is a skillet for a few minutes with the vegetables. I added more peanut butter & water to the dressing because the vinegar was a little too strong for me. But loved the combination of flavors and textures.

target.recipe_text:
our favorite grilled salmon sauce

quick, easy and delicious - who could ask for more?

1. in a small saucepan , combine ingredients
2. cook and stir until sugar is dissolved
3. brush on salmon while grilling
target.review:
Quick and easy and very tasty.
Baked the salmon in foil on the Bar-B-Q and it was great. Thanks Claudia.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy crispy sesame chicken

this chicken is *very* good!

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. in a large bowl , coat the chicken well with mayonnaise all over
3. mix the crushed honeynut cornflakes , sesame seeds , salt and pepper in a shallow dish
4. roll / coat the chicken pieces in the mixture until well coated
5. place in an baking dish
6. bake for about 50-60 minutes , or until chicken is done
demonstrations.review: Very good. Chicken was crispy on outside and moist on the inside. Used 3 large skinless, boneless breasts and cut into strips for cooking and chunks for serving. Prepared a catsup and creamed horseradish sauce for dipping. Doubled up on the sesame seeds. Thanks Kittencal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange jello salad aka st   joseph salad

easy and delicious and it does taste like baby aspirin. cook time is chill time

1. dissolve jello in boiling water
2. drain mandarin oranges and crushed pineapple
3. mix all ingredients thoroughly in large mixing bowl
4. transfer mixture to a serving bowl
5. cover and chill overnight
demonstrations.review: Made on several occasions and always a hit.I do leave out the walnuts however.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pepsi ranch pot roast

i was never a fan of pot roast, but i tried this recipe once because it was fast and easy. my husband says it was the best meal i ever made him, and we fought over leftovers!

1. place roast in the bottom of crock pot
2. if you are adding onions and / or potatoes , cut these now and place on top of the roast
3. pour cream of mushroom soup over roast
4. sprinkle full pkg of ranch mix on top of the soup
5. pour pepsi over all
6. i use enough pepsi to mostly cover all ingredients , and because it makes the best sauce / gravy i have ever tasted !
7. bake in crock pot all day , and enjoy a wonderful supper ! if you want to start eating sooner , just cook on high
demonstrations.review: My wife prepared this for her parents. Everyone enjoyed it.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christina s killer dip

this is my sister's dip. she got the recipe while backpacking in europe a few years ago. she is now forced to make it at every party she has. people smell it cooking and stand drooling by the oven until it comes out! (many have not been able to wait for the cooling part and burned their mouths to get to it first).  you might have to make 2 portions.

**note: please check the sodium content before you choose a ranch dressing mix, because it will affect the flavor! some people have complained it is "too salty". please also make sure you are using only a 1 ounce packet; there are other sizes from various manufacturers. too much mix throws off the balance of flavors. my sister and i always use the hidden valley ranch original and we do not have any problems with it :)

you can also substitute half the sour cream for prepared ranch dressing and skip the dry mix. it will come out a bit wetter.

1. defrost the spinach
2. place it in a colander and press it until as much moisture as possible is removed
3. mix all ingredients , and blend well
4. put it in a shallow baking dish in the oven for 20 minutes at 350f
5. remove from oven
6. while still hot top it with remaining cheese , heat in oven again for 5 minutes
7. remove and cool below lava stage and serve
8. goes well with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: Served for appetizer before Thanksgiving.  Very good but very rich.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hidden valley ranch chicken

i got this recipe from the back of a bottle of hidden valley ranch dressing. it's simple to make (a must for me) and tasted delicious. i lost the recipe but from memory, here it is.

1. rinse and pat dry chicken breasts
2. in a small dish or on a plate , combine the ranch dressing and the flour
3. dip each breast in the mixture until well coated
4. transfer to baking dish
5. cover breasts with the cheddar cheese and bake at 350f for 35 minutes or until cooked through
demonstrations.review: Very good and very easy to prepare.  Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot stifado

a tasty greek stew, made easy with a crock pot.

1. heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown beef-- in batches if necessary , adding more oil if needed
2. transfer beef to crock pot with a slotted spoon
3. reduce heat to medium and add onions to skillet , cooking until soft
4. add garlic , cinnamon and allspice and cook for 1 minute
5. add vinegar , tomato sauce , sugar and bay leaf and stir well to combine
6. pour mixture over meat
7. cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or on high for 4 to 5 hours , until beef is tender
8. add feta cheese , cover again , and cook on high for 10 minutes
9. discard bay leaf and serve over hot buttered pasta or mashed potatoes
target.review: I made this yesterday for my family, they said it was good, although my husband advised me not to eat it as I get heartburn really bad.  I tasted a bite and knew I would die if I ate it.  Still very good he did say though!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tony roma s blue ridge smokies sauce by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com

1. combine all of the ingredients in a medium saucepan over high heat , and whisk until smooth
2. bring sauce to a boil , for 2 minutes then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 30-40 minutes or until sauce has thickened
3. use on pork spareribs -- as cooked with the method from the book top secret restaurant recipes -- or any of your beef , pork or chicken recipes
demonstrations.review: This was very good, I am sad to say though that I substituted syrup for the molasses and also used chili sauce instead of ketchup.  It was good but I think it would have been great if I had followed the recipe exactly.  Very easy!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked pork chops

this is a super easy pork chop recipe that tastes like you slaved over a hot stove for a few hours to achieve its tender flavor.

1. combine cracker crumbs , cheese , salt and pepper in a bowl
2. dip pork chops in flour , this way , the coating will stick
3. beat egg and milk in shallow bowl
4. coat pork chops in crumb mixture
5. dip in egg mixture and into crumbs again
6. pour melted butter into baking dish
7. arrange pork chops in prepared dish
8. bake at 350 degrees for about 30 minutes on each side
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner last night and it was so easy and really very good.  I used thin pork chops so I only cooked them for 20 minutes on each side and it was perfect.  My parmesean rice and green beans went with it great too.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amish white bread

this is my favorite home baked bread recipe. i got it from an amish cookbook years ago and no other bread recipe i have tried beats it. it is a standard in our house with beef stew.

1. dissolve yeast in 1 / 2 cup warm water
2. in large bowl , combine sugar , salt , 2 cups water and shortening
3. stir in yeast mixture
4. gradually add flour to form a soft dough
5. turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth
6. place in a greased bowl and cover and let rise for about 2 hours
7. punch down and divide into 2 portions and form loaves
8. place in greased 9 x 5 loaf pans and prick tops with fork
9. let rise until higher than pans
10. bake at 375 degrees for 25 to 30 minutes
11. cool for ten minutes
12. rub butter all over tops of loaves
13. place pans on sides until loosened
14. remove bread from pans and cool completely on racks
demonstrations.review: Easy to make, great smell to the house, wonderful taste!!  My husband said it tasted like the bread he used to get at the amish roadside stands as a kid!  I served mine with a Penn. dutch corn soup...I'll post it soon!  I made four loaves, my husband and kids ate one mini (not really so mini)loaf before dinner.  Very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best authentic spanish rice

if you like the kind of spanish rice served in mexican restaurants, you will love this recipe. browning the rice gives it that fluffy and nutty taste that makes it so good. the flavor is not meant to be overpowering, so it goes very good with spicy entrees. this recipe was given to me by a friend who makes the best authentic mexican dishes ever.  enjoy!

1. pour rice into a deep pot and stir in enough oil so that every grain is coated
2. cook rice on medium and constantly stir , using a spatula , until it becomes a light toasted color , be careful not to burn
3. add onion and green pepper , cook until they become soft , add more oil if needed
4. stir in tomato , cook for 2-3 minute
5. tilt pot , remove any excess oil w / spoon
6. sprinkle bouillon and garlic salt over rice
7. pour water over rice , then cover
8. bring to a boil , then lower heat and cook for 25-30 min , or until most liquid evaporated
9. pick out large pieces of veggies w / a fork and discard ,
10. this rice actually tastes better when cooled , and then heated in the microwave , as any remaining liquid is evaporated
demonstrations.review: I make this recipe all the time, it has turned into our family favorite.  I usually cut it in half unless we have people over as it makes a lot.  I wasn't clear if the measurements for the boullion were for each or total so I just started using a little more than a tablespoon of each when I make the full recipe.  Go easy on the oil, doesnt take much at all.  Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot old south pulled pork on a bun

this is a great dish for weekends in the country, friday night dinners or evenings when you have a house full of teenage boys who can't get enough of the rich, smoky sauce.

1. in a skillet , heat oil over medium heat
2. add onions and cook until soft
3. add garlic , chili powder and pepper and cook , stirring , for 1 minute
4. add chili sauce , brown sugar , vinegar , worcestershire sauce and liquid smoke
5. stir to combine and bring to a boil
6. place pork in slow cooker stoneware and pour sauce over
7. cover and cook on low for 10 to 12 hours or on high for 6 hours , until pork is falling apart
8. transfer pork to a cutting board and pull the meat apart in shreds , using two forks
9. return to sauce and keep warm
10. when ready to serve , spoon shredded pork and sauce over warm buns
11. make ahead: this dish can be partially prepared the night before it is cooked
12. complete step 1
13. cover and refrigerate sauce overnight
14. the next morning , continue cooking as directed
15. the 150 best slow cooker recipes j finlayson
demonstrations.review: FANTASTIC!  I truly enjoyed this!  I cooked it in the crockpot and it was just perfect.  Really easy as well!  We had some left over so I put it in the freezer for another day.  Can't wait!  The whole family enjoyed it!

target.recipe_text:
sue b s chocolate cake
