i adopted this recipe.  i had prepared it for a holiday function prior to the adoption. the comments from my original review stated, "this dense, rich chocolate cake is intensely moist. it baked perfectly and made a lovely layer cake. i will be using this recipe again for chocolate cake needs."  the cake in my photo has recipe #44126, between the layers, and is frosted with recipe #31809 before being covered with my recipe #105466.  it was a huge hit, and i have made this cake many, many times since.

1. mix cocoa and boiling water
2. mix buttermilk , oil , eggs and vanilla together
3. mix dry ingredients together
4. mix dry ingredients into buttermilk / oil mixture
5. mix in cocoa
6. bake at 350 degrees fahrenheit in two greased and floured and parchment lined 9-inch round pans
7. bake until tester comes out clean , approximately 30 minutes
target.review: Yup, this cake is absolutely amazing! I needed to make a chocolate cake for a dinner party. I usually have a cake mix on hand, but looked in the pantry and didn't find one. So I came on to zaar to find a good chocolate cake recipe. Here it is. Perfect, dense, moist. Thanx so much for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham   cheese quiche

you can serve this for dinner or for breakfast. delicious.

1. beat eggs with milk , salt and pepper in bowl
2. add ham and cheese
3. pour into pie shell
4. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
5. let stand for several minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: yum! my mom hosted a baby shower... we had a brunch and I made three different kinds of quiche. This one was wonderful! thanx for a great recipe, really easy to make! used my own pie crust...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas country potato salad

recipe from the paula deen food network show.

1. cook bacon until crispy , drain and crumble
2. reserve a tablespoon of the bacon drippings
3. place potatoes in a large saucepan , cover with cold water , add reserved bacon grease , some salt and cook until potatoes are tender , about 15 to 20 minutes
4. drain and let cool , then cut into bite size pieces
5. mix together mayonnaise , mustard , salt and pepper for dressing in a separate bowl
6. mix together potatoes , green onion and egg and toss with dressing
7. add bacon and chill until serving time
demonstrations.review: Very yummy potato salad! I've never added bacon to my potato salad before but from now on I'll definitely be doing that! Thankyou for posting such a great recipe! I'll be making this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot family favorite casserole

i work nights and crock pot recipes are life savers.  this one is often requested by my family. my family doesn't much care for peas so i increase my potatoes and carrots to equal 1 1/2 c to substitute. the cream of celery soup really makes this good. i have used cream of chicken or mushroom and my family makes comments.

1. spray crock pot with pam
2. fry beef and onion , drain
3. place in crock pot
4. combine all ingredients except milk and macaroni
5. cover , cook on low 8-10 hours , or cook on high 4 hours
6. during the last 30 minutes of cooking add the milk and the macaroni and stir well
7. reduce the heat to low
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good. I left out the peas and carrots... I wish I would have put them in there, next time I will, though! This cooked in exactly 4 hours on high. My dad really liked it, my  brother didn't care for it but he's pretty picky. I'll use this one again, thanx.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
waldorf astoria red velvet cake

i haven't even tried it, but it looks good.

1. cream shortening , sugar and eggs
2. make a paste of food coloring and cocoa
3. add to creamed mixture
4. add buttermilk alternating with flour and salt
5. add vanilla
6. add soda to vinegar , and blend into the batter
7. pour into 3 or 4 greased and floured 8" cake pans
8. bake at 350f for 24-30 minutes
9. split layers fill and frost with the following frosting
10. frosting: add milk to flour slowly , avoiding lumps
11. cook flour and milk until very thick , stirring constantly
12. cool completely
13. cream sugar , butter and vanilla until fluffy
14. add to cooked mixture
15. beat , high speed , until very fluffy
16. looks and tastes like whipped cream
demonstrations.review: My grandma always makes red velvet cake for Thanksgiving and Christmas. It's my Dad's favorite cake so I decided to make him one for his bday.. I used to have the recipe for my Grandma's but I lost it. So I looked this up and this is exactly like hers. It's the best red velvet cake ever! Thanx for helping me out!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic beef enchiladas

enchiladas with a unique garlic flair, unlike any other enchilada i have ever tasted. the house smells wonderful when these are baking. although they do take some time to prepare, the work is definitely worth the reward! the ingredients are mostly things that you probably already have stocked in the cupboard. (cook time includes stovetop and baking times)

1. in saucepan , cook beef or turkey and onion until browned
2. drain
3. add flour and seasonings
4. mix well
5. stir in tomatoes and bring to boil
6. reduce heat , cover , and simmer 15 minutes
7. in another saucepan , saute garlic in butter
8. stir in flour until blended
9. gradually stir in broth and bring to boil
10. cook and stir for 2 minutes until bubbly
11. stir in tomato sauce and seasonings and heat through
12. pour 1 1 / 2 cup sauce in 13x9 inch pan
13. spread about 1 / 4 cup beef mixture down center of tortilla and top with 1-2 tbsp cheese
14. roll up tightly and place seam side-down over sauce in pan
15. repeat with remaining tortillas and top all with remaining sauce
16. cover with foil and bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes
17. sprinkle with remaining cheese and bake uncovered for 10-15 minutes until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: I've made these b4 and they are really good! Great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
dave s  special  black forest cake

my mother makes this cake for my husband when we go to visit her. he will eat two or three pieces of this over the course of the evening! it is very rich and moist. simple to make.

1. mix cake according to package directions and bake in a 9x13 inch pan
2. as soon as you remove from the oven , poke holes in the cake with the handle of a wooden spoon
3. pour the sweetened condensed milk and cream of coconut over the cake
4. make sure the milk& cream of coconut go down in the holes
5. refrigerate cake for 20-30 minutes
6. remove cake from refrigerator and spread the can of cherry pie filling on top
7. refrigerate again for 30 minutes and then spread the carton of whipped cream over the top of the cake
8. refrigerate several hours or overnight before serving
target.review: This cake is wonderful; thanks for posting. I changed the topping slightly: I mixed 1 cup milk with 1 box chocolate pudding mix, and folded the whipped topping into this mixture. It was 'wow!'

demonstrations.recipe_text:
milk tart

this is a very popular south african teatime treat/dessert a plus in its favour is it can be made in advance.the traditional version is made with a puff pastry base but i find a short crust type base makes it much easier to cut and handle.the filling can also be put into custard cups and served as a milk pudding.

1. cream the margarine and sugar together and beat in the egg
2. add the flour and salt and knead until a soft dough is formed
3. press the mixture into a greased circular pie dish and bake at 350f / 180c for 15 minutes
4. bring the milk and margarine to the boil
5. cream the sugar , eggs , maizena , flour and vanilla essence
6. add some of the hot milk to the creamed mixture , then pour it back into the pot and heat gently until it thickens
7. do not boil
8. pour the filling into the pie crust and cool
9. refrigerate until required and sprinkle with cinnamon to serve
demonstrations.review: I've been making milk tarts for many years, and I've found that by separating the eggs, beating the whites until fluffy, and folding them into the milk mixture at the end makes the tart a lot lighter. (Just remember to mention to your pregnant guests that the tart contains uncooked eggwhites)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swiss cashew tossed salad

this is always a huge hit at potluck meals.

1. in a blender , combine the vinegar , sugar , mustard , onion , and salt
2. cover and process until well blended
3. while processing , gradually add oil in a steady stream
4. stir in poppy seeds
5. in a salad bowl , combine the romaine , cashews , and swiss cheese
6. serve with dressing
demonstrations.review:
This simple salad is really very good. I thought the dressing needed a bit more of a kick, so I upped the vinegar to 1/2 cup and changed the mustard to 1 1/2 Tablespn Dijon.
The flavors compliment each other amazingly well and nothing else is required to make this salad great!
In fact, this dressing is so good I made extra and keep it on hand in the fridge for every day use on our salads.
Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing chicken marinade

this recipe came from allrecipes (ruth crickmer). my whole family loved it even though it cooked too fast. the original recipe said 'high heat' on the grill, which my husband did. it ended up cooking 8 minutes total, charred but not burnt tasting, and very juicy and flavorful. we'll turn down the heat next time for texture, but this is a keeper in our home!

1. in a large , non-reactive container , whisk together ingredients beginning with cider vinegar through salt
2. then whisk in olive oil and pepper
3. place chicken in the mixture
4. cover and marinate chicken in the fridge 8 hours or overnight
5. remove chicken from marinade just before you turn on your grill or broiler to let come up a few degrees
6. discard marinade
7. lightly oil your grill or broiler pan
8. grill or broil about 10 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: This really is a wonderful marinade. I diced the chicken before marinading, and before grilling stuck it on wooden skewers with diced green pepper, onion and mushrooms for the best kabobs we ever had.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
granny s banana cream pie

so delicious !!

1. in a saucepan , combine sugar , flour , and salt
2. stir in milk and mix well
3. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until the mixture thickens and comes to a boil
4. boil for 2 minutes
5. remove from the heat
6. stir a small amount of cream mixture into egg yolks
7. return all to saucepan
8. cook for 2 minutes , stirring constantly
9. remove from the heat
10. add butter and vanilla
11. mix well
12. allow to cool slightly
13. slice the bananas and place evenly in pastry shell
14. pour cream mixture over bananas
15. cool
16. before serving , garnish with whipped cream or cool whip and bananas
17. refrigerate any leftovers
demonstrations.review:
I like this pie, but I realized that the custard is a standard recipe and that there is an easier way with no dirty saucepan to clean.
Mix the sugar, salt and flour, then add a few drops of the milk at a time until a paste is formed. Then add the egg yolks to this paste. Boil the milk in the microwave, add a small amount to the flour mixture,mix well, then add the flour mixture to the hot milk whilst whisking. Cook for a minute or so in the microwave. Continue as per recipe. (I also added some artificial banana flavoring with the vanilla for better flavor)
For the topping, I mixed 1 box banana pudding mix with 3/4 cup milk, and folded in 8oz whipped topping. This is a lot lighter than whipped cream.
I will definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin white chocolate cake

i got this recipe from a resident's grand-daughter. she made it as a birthday cake and everyone inhaled it. i was thrilled when i found out it started out with a cake mix.

1. cake: preheat oven to 350 degrees grease and flour 12 cup bundt pan , i use bakers joy spray
2. in a large bowl
3. combine cake mix , eggs , pumpkin , evaporated milk and oil
4. beat on low speed until moistened
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in chips
7. pour into prepared pan
8. bake for 45 minutes or until wooden toothpick inserted in cake comes out clean
9. cool in pan for 25 minutes then invert on wire rack to cool completely
10. place on serving plate
11. glaze when completely cool glaze: heat evaporated milk in small saucepan over medium heat until it just starts to come to a boil
12. remove from heat
13. stir in white chocolate chips and stir until smooth
14. add cinnamon and stir in well
demonstrations.review: I really liked this cake; the texture was great. The only changed I'd like to suggest: before adding the chocolate chips, pour some of the batter in the baking pan; I didn't and the chocolate chips touching the sides and bottom of the bundt pan burnt and stuck to it.

target.recipe_text:
ruth s chris steak house creamed spinach

love their steaks, and i love their version of this classic side dish to a thick, juicy steak. sometimes i cheat and use 2 10 ounce packages of frozen, chopped spinach which i thaw and drain.

1. melt 4 tablespoons butter in heavy medium saucepan over medium heat
2. add flour and stir until light golden , about 7 minutes
3. stir in onion , bay leaf and clove
4. gradually whisk in milk
5. whisk until mixture boils and thickens , about 10 minutes
6. reduce heat to low and simmer 5 minutes longer , whisking frequently
7. remove bay leaf and whole clove
8. cook spinach in large pot of boiling water just until wilted and tender , about 2 minutes
9. drain
10. transfer spinach to bowl filled with ice water to cool
11. drain well
12. roll up spinach in kitchen towl and squeeze out as much liquid as possible
13. transfer spinach to processor and finely chop
14. add spinach to warm sauce , simmer over low heat until spinach is heated through , stirring often , about 5 minutes
15. stir in remaining 2 tablespoons of butter
16. season to taste with salt and pepper and serve
target.review: I made this with chopped beet greens and it was delicious!  I had everything but the clove, so I am looking forward to trying it with that addition in the future, but even without it, the dish was terrific.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick yellow cake

you can mix this up in a hurry.

1. heat oven to 350
2. mix dry ingredients in lg bowl
3. add shortening , milk and vanilla
4. beat on med for 2 minutes
5. add eggs and beat for 30 seconds more
6. bake in greased 13x9 pan for 35 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Wow!  I was craving cake and didn't have time to make my usual two-layer Martha Stewart cake recipe, so I gave this a try.  It  was excellent!  My only change was to use butter instead of shortening, which I always do.  It was fast, easy, moist and delicious.  I think it even gave my Martha cake a run for it's money!  Thank you Mizz  Nezz.  : )

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fannie farmer s classic baked macaroni   cheese

to me fannie farmer's recipe is the only "real" macaroni & cheese. it's from my 1946 edition of "fannie farmer's boston cooking school cookbook". with time on it's side - this recipe is hands down the best for traditional, homemade baked macaroni & cheese - comfort food.

please note: if you use cheap cheese you will end up with a bland and flavorless dish!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cook and drain macaroni according to package directions
3. set aside
4. in a large saucepan melt butter
5. add flour mixed with salt and pepper , using a whisk to stir until well blended
6. pour milk and cream in gradually
7. stirring constantly
8. bring to boiling point and boil 2 minutes
9. reduce heat and cook 10 minutes
10. add shredded cheddar little by little and simmer an additional 5 minutes , or until cheese melts
11. turn off flame
12. add macaroni to the saucepan and toss to coat with the cheese sauce
13. transfer macaroni to a buttered baking dish
14. sprinkle with breadcrumbs
15. bake 20 minutes until the top is golden brown
16. (you can also freeze this recipe in zip-lock bags for later use - once you have mixed the macaroni along with the cheese sauce allow to cool to room temperature before adding to your freezer - i generally pull it out the night before and allow macaroni and cheese to reach room temperature
17. i then add the macaroni and cheese to a buttered baking dish , sprinkle with bread crumbs and then bake for 20 to 30 minutes , until golden brown on top and bubbling
demonstrations.review: Very easy and super delicious!!  I had to practically force my 15 month old twins to stop eating it.  We'll be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanilla scented granola

great snack for everyone, or the for kids lunches or even as an after school treat! serve for breakfast with yogurt and fruit or over ice cream for dessert. watch your time in the oven because sometimes it cooks a little quickly. this recipe came from bon appetit, march of 2002.
a few baking tips i have learned from making this recipe often: i use a jelly roll pan so the granola will have maximum exposure while cooking.  also, if you do like your granola to clump, do not stir while baking.  allow to cool in pan for about 10 minutes or so, then run a spatula between granola and the pan to loosen.  you will have so many clumps you will have to break them with your hands ; )

1. position rack to middle of oven and preheat to 300
2. lightly spray large baking sheet with nonstick spray
3. mix next 5 ingredients in large bowl
4. combine oil , honey and sugar in small saucepan
5. bring to simmer over medium heat
6. remove from heat
7. stir in vanilla
8. pour hot liquid over oat mixture
9. stir well
10. using hands , toss mixture until thoroughly mixed
11. spread granola on prepared baking sheet
12. bake until golden brown , stirring occasionaly , about 30 minutes
13. transfer sheet to rack
14. cool granola completely
15. makes about 8 cups
demonstrations.review: Very, very yummy!  I do suggest, however, that you use organic coconut oil, which is SO much healthier than vegetable oil, and tastes excellent in granola.  Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the simple but perfect pancake

this recipe is from king arthur's all-purpose baking book and my family's current favorite recipe. they have a spongy texture and soak in the syrup.

1. beat the eggs , milk , and vanilla until light and foamy , about 3 minute at high speed of a mixer
2. stir in butter or oil
3. whisk the dry ingredients together and gently , but quickly , mix into the egg and milk mixture
4. let the batter relax while griddle is heating the batter will thicken upon resting
5. grease and preheat griddle
6. the griddle is ready if a drop of water will skitter across the surface , evaporating immediately
7. drop cupfuls of batter on the lightly greased griddle
8. cook on one side until bubbles begin to form and break , then turn the pancakes and cook the other side until brown
demonstrations.review: My hubby made this recipe the other morning and I tried not to like it, really I did, as I am the pancake queen and "how dare he try to de-thrown me with some sad pancake recipe he found on the internet"...but I loved it!  The pancakes were belgian waffle-like, super fluffy with a crispy edge, and just the right flavor.  This will replace my tried and true recipe for sure!  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Super easy and delicious!  The whole family loved it, toddlers included.  I made my own cajun seasoning with a recipe from this site and the dish turned out just as I had hoped.  Thanks Lorac!

target.recipe_text:
slow cooked italian stew  crock pot

have always been a fan of slow cooked meals and with my new crock pot, i'm equiped to try some new ones.  the original recipe comes from "the slow cooker bible" and includes my intended modifications.  as i have not yet tried this dish, feedback is especially welcome.

1. coat slow cooker with a light layer of cooking spray
2. add carrots and onions
3. top with chicken cubes and chicken sausage
4. top with peppers and zucchini
5. mix together the tomatoes , broth , rosemary , garlic and oregano
6. pour on top of ingredients in the crock pot
7. cook on high for 3 to 4 hours or low for 6 to 7 hours
8. vegetables should be tender and chicken cooked but not falling apart
9. turn cooker to high and stir in cannellini beans and re-cover slow cooker
10. cook and additional 10 to 15 minutes until beans are heated through
11. ladle stew into bowls and garnish with basil
target.review: Our Families all LOVED this dish!  The children even asked for seconds.  A Wonderful Slow Cooker recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn and clam chowder from the really good food cook book

every time i have made this soup someone asks for the recipe. you will go crazy over it!

1. in a large soup pot saute bacon until almost crisp
2. add onions
3. continue sauteing until onions are clear
4. add the flour 1 tbsp
5. at a time to make a roue
6. add the cans of clams and their juices
7. mix well
8. add the cans of corn and their juices
9. mix well
10. with a wooden spatula scrape the bottom of the pot until it is clear
11. add the diced potatoes
12. cook , covered , over medium-low heat until potatoes are fork-tender
13. add the butter
14. mix until it is melted
15. add the cream and milk
16. blend well
17. bring the chowder to just under a boil
18. remove from heat
19. salt and pepper to taste
20. allow this thick , creamy , flavors-from-the-sea-and-earth soup to rest for 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: The best Clam Chowder I have ever tasted.  And no wonder with all the heavy cream.  Easy to make and a real  pleaser!  Mine came out a bit thin, If I were making this again I would add in more flour about twice as much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole grain baking mix

similar to bisquick, but with whole-grain goodness. i have used this mix cup for cup for bisquick recipes and it turns out pretty well. you can substitute whole wheat flour for all the flour, if you like, though your baked products may be a little denser.

1. mix all ingredients together well , using a pastry blender
2. store in air-tight container , in a cool dry place
3. for biscuits: 3 cups mix , 1 cup water
4. mix well
5. divide into 16 biscuits
6. use greased baking sheet and bake at 425 f for 10-12 minutes
7. for pizza crust: 1 tbsp yeast , dissolved in 1 / 2 cup hot water
8. add 2 1 / 4 cups mix
9. knead on floured surface
10. let rise 10 minutes
11. spread on greased pizza pan sprinkled with cornmeal
12. bake at 425 f for 10 minutes , then add sauce and toppings of choice
13. return to oven and bake until hot and the cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: A Great Multi Grain Mix!! I made peach cobbler with it first, so I added in some milk, eggs and sugar.  The top was yummy enough to eat alone!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
light and fluffy pancakes

from the "best recipe" cookbook by america's test kitchen. fabulous pancakes like the ones in restaurants! perfect basic recipe for embellishing

1. whisk milk and lemon juice in a medium bowl and set aside to let thicken
2. in a separate bowl , whisk dry ingredients together - flour , sugar , baking powder , baking soda , salt
3. whisk the egg and melted butter into the milk mixture
4. create a little "well" in the center of dry ingredient bowl and pour the milky mixture in the center
5. whisk gently until just combined , there should still be lumps
6. heat a pan or griddle to medium heat and coat with butter or vegetable oil
7. pour pancake mixture by 1 / 4 cups and heat until large bubbles come to the top
8. flip the pancake and wait another 1-2 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wonderful Pancakes!  Served them with strawberry compote and whipping cream to my family of 5 and there were no leftovers!  Next time I will double the recipe.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
debbie s spanish rice

this is a creamy, cheesy, vegetarian version of spanish rice...a great side dish! the recipe was given to me by a friend.

1. saute the onions , chiles and garlic in a small amount of olive oil , over medium heat , until the onions are soft
2. set aside until cool
3. when the vegetables and rice are cool , combine all the ingredients in a bowl and mix well
4. pour into a buttered 1 1 / 2 quart baking dish
5. bake , covered at 375 degrees for 30 minutes
6. uncover and bake 10 minutes more
demonstrations.review: Loved this dish.  Used equal parts Cheddar and Pepper Jack cheeses.  Next time will add in shredded beef, chicken or turkey to make this a main dish.  Great Family Food!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irene stewart s ham   macaroni casserole

this recipe is from the archives of pioneer lodge, a seniors residence. this is an easy recipe, quick to put together and then just bake it. serve with a salad.

1. heat together the soup , milk , cheddar cheese , celery salt , and worcestershire sauce until bubbly , stirring frequently
2. add ham
3. add mixture to cooked macaroni
4. pour into a 2 quart greased casserole dish
5. top with cornflake crumbs
6. bake at 350 degrees fahrenheit for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Simple and yummy! I added broccoli and it whipped together quickly.  This will become a standard recipe around here. Thanks

target.recipe_text:
brie bread

this is an outstanding addition to your tapa table and so easy to make. i received this recipe from my friend pat who i had met in sint maarten.

1. melt the butter in a sauce pan and onion and basil
2. cut the brie into small pieces and add to the butter mixture
3. stir until the brie is melted
4. slice the french bread in half lengthwise
5. take each half and cut almost all the way through into slices about 1 1 / 2 inches each
6. spread the melted brie mixture over each half of the loaf
7. place each half of the under the broiler until the cheese is bubbly
8. tear the individual pieces completely off the loaves and place on serving platter
target.review: Have to say I agree with the previous review of there being too much butter.  I could have written that review as I also used onion flakes.  The taste was there and I will definitely make this again but with half the amount of butter.  Oh and I may try it on the Garlic Bread from Costco with the whole cloves of garlic baked in.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
touchdown pepperoni pizza sandwich

this is a hybrid of a pizza and a sandwich--in one handy little package.  mix-n-match to adjust for your own personal tastes.  i dreamed this up while in line at the check-out knowing i needed something quick to satisfy ds who was anxious to get over to his friend's to watch the game on the big screen tv.  dh and the peanut gallery thought this rated five stars!  hope you do, too!  idea:   use the toaster oven or a panini-maker to get these sammies to the peak of perfection!!!

1. spread mayonnaise on one slice and pizza or spaghetti sauce on the other slice
2. lay pepperoni slices on the pizza sauce and the cheese over the top of that
3. sprinkle parmesan on the mayonnaise slice
4. pop both pieces into the toaster oven until cheese is bubbly and melted
5. fold sides together , and serve while warm
6. variation: try this with your favorite pizza toppings or cheeses
7. serving suggestion: cut on point into four pieces and use as "appetizers" or little kid-wiches
demonstrations.review: Very good simple recipe.  I changed it up a bit but don't think that it altered the results much.  I made these on hoagie buns using provolone cheese.  I also mixed 1/4 c mayo with 1/4 shredded parmesan, 1/2 tsp italian seasoning and 1/2 tsp garlic powder and spread that on the top half of the buns(I made 4 sandwiches).  The bottom I spread spaghetti sauce on, then topped with pepperoni slices and the slices of provolone.  I put them under the broiler until the cheese was melted and had a few 'golden' spots.  These were super yummy, easy and will be enjoyed by us again! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s creamy mushroom risotto bake

the rice must be cold so use leftover cold rice or make a day ahead and refrigerate, i use converted rice for this but white long grain will do fine as long as the rice is semi-firm and not overcooked  see my recipe#350260 --- if you prefer a thicker rice casserole then omit the milk or reduce to 1/4 cup. the complete recipe may be doubled, this is *really* good! :)

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. butter a 2-quart casserole dish
3. in a skillet heat butter over medium heat until melted
4. add in onion , celery and green bell pepper
5. cook stirring over medium heat until softened or until well softened adding in garlic the last 2 minutes of cooking , place the mixture into the bowl
6. add in soup , milk , drained canned mushrooms mayonnaise , sour cream , black pepper , garlic powder and cooked cold rice
7. mix with a wooden spoon until well combined adjusted black pepper and adding in a small amount of salt to taste
8. transfer to prepared casserole dish
9. sprinkle parmesan cheese evenly over the rice mixture
10. bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was easy to make.  Very creamy and very, very tasty.  Made as a side dish to pork chops.  My one year old and I ate this the next day for lunch as well.  Will make this again soon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek tzatziki sauce

this is a delicious sauce that can be used in many greek recipes.  we like to use it when making gyros, or other mediterranean recipes that are wrapped in pitas. it tastes just like the sauce we've had in restaurants such as "hell's" in tarpon springs in florida.  it's a funny name, but the restaurant is known for having some of the best greek food and greek pastries in florida.

1. place yogurt in a coffee filter or piece of cheesecloth , and place in a strainer over a dish
2. let drain for 2-4 hours in the refrigerator
3. if using greek yogurt you do not need to drain it , as it is already a thick consistency
4. meanwhile , put the chopped or grated cucumber in a tea towel and squeeze to remove liquid
5. discard liquid
6. sprinkle with 1 teaspoon salt and mix into the cucumber
7. set aside 20 minutes
8. rinse a little to wash out the extra salt , if you want to
9. then squeeze again to express as much liquid as possible
10. draining the yogurt and cucumber make for a thick and authentic consistency of tzatziki sauce
11. combine the drained yogurt and cucumber , sour cream , pinch of salt , olive oil , red wine vinegar , mint and garlic
12. it made for an overpowering and almost bitter taste , so now i stick to only 1 clove
13. place sauce in the refrigerator for 1 hour or more to meld flavors
14. stir before serving
15. the sauce can be stored in the refrigerator for up to one week
16. makes 1 1 / 4 cups
demonstrations.review: This was very, very good.  I followed the recipe with two exceptions.  The first being that I subbed dill for mint as a personal preference.  The second thing, I only just now realized I did.  I completely ignored step 2.  It was still thick and oh so tasty.  Made to go with recipe #160830 and #81725.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy asian beef   noodles   ww recipe

this is delicious. it satisfies my craving for lo-mein. i have made with chicken and shrimp as well, just adjust the ramen noodle flavor to match.  from ww cookbook cooking for two, it makes a huge 10 points serving.  i am satisfied with 1/2 a serving.

1. trim fat from steak
2. cut steak diagonally across grain into thin slice
3. heat 1 tsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium high heat
4. add steak and green onions
5. stir fry 1 minute
6. remove steak mixture from skillet
7. keep warm
8. heat remaining 1 tsp oil in skillet over medium high heat
9. add slaw
10. stir fry for 30 seconds
11. remove slaw from skillet and keep warm
12. remove noodles from packages
13. reserve 1 seasoning packet for another use
14. add water and remaining seasoning packet to skillet
15. bring to a boil
16. break noodles in half
17. add noodles to water mixture
18. cook noodles 2 minutes or until most of liquid is absorbed , stirring frequently
19. stir in steak mixture , slaw , and soy sauce
20. cook until thoroughly heated
demonstrations.review: Made this last night for a quick and lowfat dinner.  Used a leftover t-bone and a combination of garlic and chili oil since I was out of sesame oil. Added button mushrooms that I sliced in half.  Husband, 1 year old and I all loved it. Husband asked me to make this again and I definitely will.  I may try oriental flavored ramen next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground beef gyros

this is a great summer meal and quick and easy to put together and tastes wonderful. refreshing served with the cucumber sauce and is even low in fat. i think this came from quick cooking. it's a favorite in our house.

1. in a bowl , combine first 5 ingredients
2. cover and refrigerate
3. in separate bowl , combine ground beef and seasonings
4. mix well
5. shape into 4 patties
6. grill , covered , over medium to high heat for 10 to 12 minutes or until meat is no longer pink , turning once
7. cut patties into thin slices
8. stuff into pitas
9. add lettuce , cucumber , tomato , and onion
10. serve with yogurt sauce
demonstrations.review: We thought the tzatziki was right on the money.  It was fantastic and I will use this recipe for it from now on.  However, the beef was really bland and we were very disappointed with that.  I had a hard time getting them sliced "thinly."  We may try these again adding more spice.  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
white chile con queso

in the 80's, julio's in juarez served a delicious chili con queso much like this. the original recipe was adapted from an old el paso newsletter.

1. saute onion in oil until tender
2. add chilies , jalapenos , pepper and garlic powder and cook for 5 minutes , stirring often
3. add water and pimentos , mix , and add evaporated milk and cheese
4. reduce heat and stir as needed until cheese melts
5. serve with tortilla chips
target.review: Thank you, thank you!  Its been many years since I've eaten at Julio's.  I love this queso recipe, and so does everyone I serve it to!  10 stars for you :]

demonstrations.recipe_text:
absolute best ever lasagna

my family's favorite. this is a very meaty lasagna. we prefer it with cottage cheese, but you can easily substitute ricotta.

1. brown ground meat , onion and garlic
2. add salt , pepper , parsley , oregano , basil , chopped tomatoes with juice
3. stirring until well mixed
4. cover and simmer 1 hour
5. cook lasagna noodles according to package directions
6. drain and set aside
7. spray a 13 x 9" baking pan with cooking spray
8. combine riccota cheese , eggs , pepper , 2 tablespoons parsley , parmesan cheese and 1 / 2 1lb of mozzarella cheese
9. in a lasagna pan , layer noodles , meat sauce , and cheese mixture
10. repeat
11. top off with layer of noodles
12. sprinkle evenly with remaining mozzarella cheese
13. make sure to cover noodles completely
14. bake at 375f for 40-60 minutes , or until cheese mixture is thoroughly melted
15. (i cover w / foil for about 40 minutes , then uncover for 15-20 minutes
16. let sit for 15-20 minutes before cutting and serving
demonstrations.review: Made for friends and family to rave reviews.  What a delicious lasagna!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers mexican zero points soup

from the ww website for my 'zaar buddies!
the following are variations that can be added along with the appropriate points values:
we used points tracker to calculate the following additions to an individual 1-cup serving: 
¼ cup corn kernels, points value: ½ 
¼ cup black beans, drained and rinsed, points value: ½ 
2 oz cooked shrimp, points value: 1 
2 oz shredded or diced white meat chicken, points value: 2 
2 tbsp reduced-fat sour cream, points value: 1

1. put snap beans , garlic , zucchini , tomatillos , jalapeno , diced tomatoes , green chili pepper , onion , green pepper , cumin , oregano and vegetable broth into a large soup pot
2. puree roasted peppers with chipotle in adobo sauce in a blender or food processor , and add to soup
3. stir to combine
4. cover and bring to a boil over high heat
5. reduce heat to low , and simmer , partly covered , for about 10 minutes
6. stir in salt , lime juice and cilantro
7. serve
8. serving size: about 1 cup
demonstrations.review: Delicious. What a nice change from the usual 0 point soups.  Thank you for posting this scrumptious recipe.  My whole family loves its, and the fact that it is Weight Watchers is my little secret.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet sweet potatoes

this is a wonderful recipe that goes back years, the addition of orange juice seems to bring out the flavour --- to save time you can even cook the potatoes a day ahead,  and this may easily be doubled or even tripled to serve a large dinner party --- this is so delicious! :)

1. set oven to 425f
2. butter a medium-size baking dish
3. in a saucepan cook sweet potatoes in boiling water for about 8-10 minutes , or until just firm-tender
4. drain well and transfer to baking dish
5. mix together brown sugar , cinnamon and salt in a small bowl or cup
6. sprinkle the potatoes with the brown sugar mixture and toss gently to coat
7. drizzle with orange juice
8. dot with butter all over
9. bake uncovered for 15 minutes
10. remove from oven and sprinkle with marshmallows
11. return to oven and bake for another 2 minutes longer , or until marshmallow are puffed and golden coloured
12. delicious !
demonstrations.review: Doubled the recipe and made for Christmas dinner.  So delicious.  It disappeared, and my family loved it so much I made it again the next night to eat with leftovers!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s no fail buttery flaky pie pastry crust

i don't think you will find a better pie pastry, not only is this easy to handle but bakes outs flaky and light and has a rich buttery flavor! --- you could use 3 cups all purpose flour but the crust will not be as flaky --- here's a tip, to prevent a soggy pie crust brush a thin layer of egg white over the bottom crust before filling --- *note* this can also be made using a processor with great results, which is the way i most always do (see instructions below the recipe) if you are making this on a food processor cube the butter and lard into about 1-inch pieces and then partially freeze.

1. mix both flours , sugar and salt in a large bowl
2. with a pastry cutter cut in the very cold butter and lard until the consistency of tiny peas
3. in a small bowl whisk the egg yolk , vinegar and water
4. stir the egg / water mixture into the flour mixture until moistened and dough holds together
5. gather into a ball then divide into two
6. cover with plastic wrap and store in the fridge for 30 minutes
7. processor method: whirl the flour , sugar and salt for a couple of seconds
8. in a small bowl mix the egg , vinegar and water together
9. set aside
10. add in the partially frozen butter cubes and lard to the flour mixture
11. pulse until well mixed , then add in the water / egg mixture
12. process / pulse just until the dough holds together
demonstrations.review: Another fabulous recipe from Kittencal. The best pie crust recipe ever...so light, flaky and buttery!  Thank you so much for sharing. I'll never use any other pie crust again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced apples

found this recipe on the internet. serve it cool or warm. it is pretty easy and tastes good. i have served it warm with vanilla ice cream

1. peel , core , and slice apples
2. place all ingredients in microwave-safe bowl
3. microwave on high for 15 minutes , stirring each 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: I served the spiced apples with pork chops to my family and a friend to rave reviews. I added cinnamon and it was delicious.  Thank you for sharing this yummy recipe.

target.recipe_text:
buttery baked chicken

this chicken makes a scrumptious sauce while it bakes. perfect for a dinner party. top it with toasted almonds for for a real treat.

1. place flour in shallow bowl
2. combine butter and spices
3. coat chicken with flour
4. roll in butter
5. place in greased baking dish
6. mix crumbs with cream , and any remaining butter mixture
7. pour cream around chicken
8. bake , uncovered , at 350f for 30 minutes , or until juices run clear
target.review: Nothing so easy should taste so good! What a great dinner, thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french country chicken stew

a stew typical of rural france. good served with a crusty bread

1. prepare the chicken but don't skin
2. salt the pieces and dredge them lightly in the flour , brushing off and saving the excess
3. trim off and discard the bacon rind
4. slice the bacon across the width into 1 / 4 pieces heat the oil in a large kettle and brown the bacon lightly
5. remove and set aside
6. brown the chicken pices in batches , removing them as they finish browning
7. remove and discard all but 3 tbs of the fat
8. add the onion , pepper , tarragon , and the remaining flour
9. scrape these back and forth in the hot fat until the onion is transparent
10. add the tomatoes and their juice and continue the scraping action until most of the juice has evaporated
11. add 1 1 / 2 cups of water , the wine , and the crumbled bouillon cube
12. add the bacon , chicken , peas , and carrots
13. cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes scrub the new potatoes under cold water and pare off a one inch strip around the middle of each one , leaving the peel on the ends
14. add them to the stew and simmer for 20 minutes
15. stir in the parsley
16. salt to taste , and serve hot
demonstrations.review: Try using fresh tarragon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chipotle oven fried chicken

this is one of my favorite ways to make chicken.

1. using a food processor , blend together the chipotle chile , mayo , salt and pepper until the mixture is smooth
2. in a baking dish arrange chicken in one layer and coat coat with entire mayo mixture
3. chill the chicken covered for at least 1 hour or overnight
4. using a large bowl , combine bread crumbs , cayenne pepper , salt and pepper
5. then coat each piece of chicken with the mixture
6. place chicken on roasting racks and bake them at 425 in the oven
7. for thirty minutes
8. reduce the temperature to 375 and bake for 15 minutes more , or until it is cooked
demonstrations.review: I ended up baking it without the breadcrumbs, etc., and it worked pretty well. I had made and spread on the mayo mixture the night before, woke up sick the next day and I didn't feel like doing any additional steps. I just covered the baking dish it was already in with foil and baked it for 1 hour at 450. It was nice and moist with a little burn on the aftertaste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cauliflower baked with tomatoes and feta

something a little different

1. heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a heavy based fry pan and saute the onion and garlic for 3-4 minutes , or until the onion has softened
2. add the tomatoes , cinnamon and oregano and season with the salt and pepper
3. stir then simmer covered for 5 minutes
4. preheat oven to 375f degrees
5. add cauliflower to the tomato mixture , cover and simmer for a further 10 minutes , or until cauliflower is just tender
6. remove from heat
7. transfer mixture to a large shallow dish and drizzle over the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil
8. sprinkle over the lemon juice and crumbled feta
9. bake for 40 minutes or until the cauli is soft and cheese has melted
demonstrations.review: This was a really great and different side dish. I wanted to use up ingredients that I already had, so I made this with frozen cauliflower that I microwaved first and a can of stewed tomatoes. My husband really liked it, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon herbed roasted chicken  crock pot

nan

1. rinse chicken well and pat dry
2. remove any excess fat
3. place onion in the cavity of the chicken and rub skin with butter
4. place in crock pot
5. squeeze the juice of the lemon over the chicken and sprinkle with remaining seasonings
6. cover and cook on low 10 hours
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner tonight for us and our friends that are staying with us. Everybody loved it and the best part was it took me 10 minutes to put together this morning. Thanks so much for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked brie stuffed with strawberry preserves and toasted almonds

an easy impressive do ahead appetizer.  update 9/15/2006 - adopted from the recipezaar account.

1. carefully lay the cheese on its side and using a long , sharp knife , horizontally cut in half
2. spread the preserves on the cut side of the bottom layer of cheese
3. sprinkle on the nuts
4. replace the top half of the brie
5. roll out the puff pastry into a circle , about double the diameter of the wheel of brie
6. place the brie in the center of the pastry
7. gather up the edges and decoratively twist together
8. refrigerate for at least 1 hour or up to 24 hours wrapped in plastic
9. preheat the oven to 375f
10. spray a large baking sheet with cooking spray
11. beat the egg yolk and brush over the pastry
12. bake about 40 minutes , until the pastry is evenly puffed and brown
13. serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: I made this for a dinner party with some old friends. I couldn't get the puff pastry to roll into a circle so I just used it as a big square. I cut the brie horizontally with an electric carving knife (my dad's suggestion). Everyone loved this! I served pie-like wedges on plates with a fork and crackers and let everyone decide whether to eat it on the crackers or just eat it. If you are looking for something impressive and easy this is it!

target.recipe_text:
low carb fauxtatoes

another variation on a cauliflower for potatoes recipe. we really like the flavor of the cream cheese and touch of garlic. you can also use this instead of mashed potatoes for shepherd's pie - it's really good this way!

1. chop cauliflower and steam with garlic until very soft
2. discard garlic clove
3. process cauliflower and other ingredients in food processor
target.review: Delish! And the best thing - this was too easy, so I wasn't too sure at first about it.  HAD to add another big fat garlic clove, tho. SO, now I'm going to make it with the green-colored (broccoli) cauliflower, the orange-colored - which has a 25% higher Vitamin A content... and the purple-colored cauliflower also for beautiful colors.  Thanks, Barb!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
papa bear s baked italian lemon  chicken

this recipe was given to me by a great guy we called "papa bear". this is easy and really good.  hi papa bear, if you're out there. :)

1. place chicken between plastic wrap and pound to flatten just a little
2. place chicken in glass pan and marinate in lemon juice for about 10 minutes
3. turning a few times
4. sprinkle chicken with lemon pepper and olive oil turn to coat and let marinate for another 15 minutes
5. put bread crumbs on plate and coat chicken on both sides
6. fold chicken in half and place in a glass baking dish
7. bake at 350 degrees for 8-10 minutes then flip over and bake another 8-10 minutes
8. do not overbake
9. :)
demonstrations.review: Thank you for such an easy scrumptious chicken recipe!  Used thighs, with skin.  Then, made a combo of black, wild and jasime rice, in the rice cooker.  Topped the rice with the Watercress Cilantro Sauce found on Recipezaar, (but I didnâ€™t save it and canâ€™t find it againâ€¦ there was yogurt in it, I remember).  Anyway it was mmmm mmmm good.  Next time I might just have to throw in some jalpenos somewhere there!  Will use Papa Bearâ€™s recipe when chicken is called for in salads.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green sauce  grne sauce

german cookery (hans karl adams). serving size is a guess

1. wash the herbs in cold water , dry , and chop finely
2. mix with other ingredients
3. you may want to add a lettuce or leeks
4. this sauce is good with cooked beef , fish , poultry , hard or soft boiled eggs , and is a real delicacy with cooked asparagus
demonstrations.review: For something without garlic in it, this is just as wonderful! Could not find sorrel, and the 2nd time I used 1/2 mayo and 1/2 yogurt - the 3rd time I used sour cream instead of yogurt.  I feel like putting every green herb on earth in the next sauce, just to experiment! Will make this often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli and ritz

this is not the cassarole recipe!!!  it is a fantastic version that usually requires a double batch for family functions.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. mix butter and crackers
3. press with the back of a spoon onto the bottom of a baking dish
4. add broccoli in an even layer
5. put velveeta slices covering entire top
6. bake for 15 minutes or until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: Loved this! A combination of healthy and fattening! I steamed fresh broccoli in a double boiler and used grated "Mexican Cheese blend" found in grocery cheese aisle... couldn't bring myself to buy the Velveeta which isn't healthy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mrs  g s garlic cilantro pine nut hummus

i made up this recipe from another hummus recipe.  i really make it to taste, and it seems to be a little different each time...so add or delete as you see fit!  i like a lot of garlic i've gone as high as 15 cloves, but i think 10 is probably the right amount.  sometimes this comes out thicker than i'd like (sometimes not)...if so, i add a bit more water and/or olive oil.  if you don't like cilantro, you could use parsley. i love this as a dip, or with pita or naan and tomatoes and cucumbers!!  served this one as an appetizer at my wedding!  yum!

1. on a cutting board mince and mash the garlic to a paste with the salt
2. in a food processor puree the chick-peas with the garlic paste , the tahini , the lemon juice , the oil and water , scraping down the sides , until the hummus is smooth
3. add water / oil , if necessary , to thin the hummus to the desired consistency
4. add salt to taste
5. add cumin and blend , taste and adjust if necessary
6. add cilantro and process until chopped into mixture
7. add toasted pine nuts and process until blended -- or you can just add them on top , whole , as garnish
8. transfer the hummus to a bowl and serve
demonstrations.review: I liked the thickness!  This was very good as a celery stuffer w/a little paprika sprinkled on it.  Have to admit that I added 4 jalpenos to make it spicy but will add even more next time!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soda cracker pie

my grandmother was a wonderful cook.  even in her "town" house (as opposed to her farm house) she had two kitchens.  one on the main floor for day to day cooking, and another in the basement for canning and preserving.  after her death, my mother and i were cleaning out the cupboards in the basement kitchen.  we found recipe box after recipe box.  when my mom found this recipe, she almost did a cartwheel!  i looked at the recipe and thought, "ok, this doesn't really sound all that good...."  mom told me, "wait til you try it!!"  it's now one of my favorite desserts.  the crust is dense and somewhat salty, which perfectly balances the creamy sweetness of the topping.

1. preheat oven to 325f and grease a 9" pie pan very well
2. beat egg whites , slowly add sugar
3. beat until stiff
4. add the rest of the ingredients
5. pour into prepared pie plate
6. bake for 40 minutes
7. when cool , top with mixture of whipped cream and strawberries
demonstrations.review: Wow I had this when I was little too - completely forgot about it... thanks for the reminder!  It's very good, easy, unusual (and memorable). Will experiment w/other fruit toppings.  The walnuts are essential.

target.recipe_text:
cabbage for those who dislike cabbage

this is so much nicer than plain steamed or boiled cabbage. try it on the cabbage haters in your family and see if it converts them.

1. in a large skillet , heat butter and oil over medium heat
2. add cabbage , garlic and brown sugar to pan
3. saut until the cabbage is limp , about 5 minutes or so
4. reduce heat to medium-low and stir in vinegar
5. cook , stirring very often , for approximately 20 minutes
6. taste and if cabbage is too crunchy for you , continue to cook for a few more minutes
7. add salt and pepper to taste and serve
target.review: I already love cabbage but this was a good alternative to the way my southern grandmother made cabbage.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hoisin pork

i always get compliments when i serve this. make it with fried rice or lo mein

1. combine marinade ingredients in small bowl
2. place tenderloin in shallow bowl , pour in the marinade
3. refrigerate 4 hrs
4. preheat oven to 425
5. roast 15 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: I used bone-in pork chops which I.M.O gives it more flavor.  It was fall off the bone delicious.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy oven baked beans and pork chops

this is an easy but really tasty pork chop dish --- purchase the thicker size pork chops or you may use 2-3 larger pork steaks, the thinner chops tend to fall apart when baked as they bake too fast, if desired you can top with shredded cheddar cheese the last 15 minutes of baking, also chopped fresh garlic may be added also to the bean mixture -- this may also be cooked in a crockpot, just brown the chops firstly in a skillet.

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. brown the chops in a frypan on both sides with salt , pepper and garlic powder
3. set aside
4. grease an dutch oven or a oven-proof casserole dish
5. in a bowl mix together the pork and beans , chopped onion , chopped green pepper , bbq sauce , ketchup , brown sugar and cayenne pepper
6. layer half of the bean mixture on the bottom of dutch oven
7. lay the pork chops on top of the bean mixture
8. top with remaining bean mixture
9. bake covered or uncovered for about 1 hour and 15 minutes , or until the chops are tender
10. delicious
demonstrations.review: Kittencal can do no wrong in my eyes!  This was another home run and thanks for sharing it with us all!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mixed vegetables casserole

simple side dish and goes with so many things.  source - internet

1. preheat oven to 350-degrees
2. cut vegetables into bit-size chunks
3. over medium heat , saut in olive oil in a large ovenproof skillet until crisp-tender
4. add tomatoes and cook 15 minutes until some of the liquid evaporates
5. top with parmesan cheese and mozzarella cheese
6. bake for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I had some leftover homemade meat sauce from a lasagna I'd made a couple of days before and added it to the veggies.  My sweety loved it so much he had seconds and is not much of a vegetable eater.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
demonstrations.review: The fish came out so tender and juicy and we loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: These brownies came out so good!  I've always bought boxed brownie mix because I could never find a recipe that was fudgy enough.  After eating these I will never have to buy boxed brownie mix again.  I made them without any add-ins but next time I may try some white chocolate chips to take them over the top.  Thanks for a great recipe and keep on baking.

target.recipe_text:
chicken waldorf sandwiches  diabetic

from diabeticrecipes.com, this looks really good.

1. place the chicken breasts in a pan and cover with broth
2. bring to a simmer and cook until done , about 8 to 10 minutes
3. allow to cool in the broth , then cut into small dice
4. in a small bowl mix together the mayonnaise , sour cream , orange zest , and juice
5. add the dressing to the chicken
6. stir in the apple and celery
7. place a leaf of lettuce on each of 6 slices of bread
8. top with chicken salad and top with a second piece of bread
9. refrigerate wrapped in plastic wrap , until ready to serve
10. cut each sandwich in half
11. exchanges per serving: 3 very lean protein , 2 carbohydrate
12. nutrition facts: 286 calories , 34 g protein , 4 g total fat , 30 g carbohydrate , 2 g dietary fiber , 67 mg cholesterol , 479 mg sodium
target.review: Holy smokes, this is good! I didn't have any celery and added orange juice concentrate instead of the juice and zest and it was delicious! Loved it on whole wheat bread for a great weekend lunch. Mmmm.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wisconsin cauliflower cheese soup

so rich, your guests won't believe it's made with milk instead of cream. use a blender not a food processor to puree the soup for an extra-smooth texture.  kids and adults alike will love this soup.

1. in 4-quart saucepan , melt butter over medium heat
2. add onion and cook until golden , about 10 minutes , stirring occasionally
3. stir in flour , salt and garlic
4. cook 2 minutes , stirring frequently
5. stir in milk , chicken broth , red pepper , and 1 1 / 2 cups water
6. add cauliflower and heat to boiling over high heat
7. reduce heat to low
8. cover and simmer until cauliflower is tender , about 10 minutes
9. in blender or with immersion blender blend cauliflower mixture at low speed until very smooth
10. return cauliflower mixture to saucepan
11. remove saucepan from heat
12. stir in mustard and 1 1 / 2 cups cheese until melted and smooth
13. garnish soup with remaining cheese to serve
demonstrations.review: We are having a soup supper tonight at church for Easter, and I decided to make this. And it was AMAZING. I decided not to bother with the water but instead used a full carton of Swanson's chicken broth, did not puree the cauliflower in the blender but used a potato masher to break it up, and then added a can of Campbell's cheddar cheese soup that I found in the pantry to take it over the top and I am SO glad that I did. I took one bite and I just about fell over in delight! My taste buds began to sing the Hallelujah chorus! This is an amazing soup and it will certainly be showing up at our house again soon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken  broccoli and wild rice

this is delicious. one would never know this is crockpot style---it is very creamy and yummy!!!!! your meal is practically done when work day ends. i encourage anyone to try---if you like all the ingredients, it will be a favorite at your house. it is at my house. :)

1. in a 3 1 / 2 quart slow cooker , combine all the ingredients
2. mix well
3. cover and cook on low setting for 6 to 10 hours
demonstrations.review: I found that when I made this, the rice completely turned to mush. I really wanted to like this, but I wasn't that crazy about it. Maybe cooking it for less time would do the trick, but I got smooshy, unappetizing rice after 6 hours and we tossed out the leftovers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
round steak   onions

this is one of my favorite recipes. it takes a little longer to cook than some recipes, but is very worth it. the gravy you'll make is wonderful served over mashed potatoes.

1. cut steak into four pieces
2. on a plate , mix salt , pepper , marjoram , and flour
3. dredge steaks in flour
4. pound mixture into steaks till steaks are about double in diameter and about 1 / 4" thick
5. in a heavy skillet , heat butter over medium heat
6. add onions
7. saute 10 minutes or till golden brown
8. lift out onions , set aside
9. add steak to hot skillet
10. brown over med-high heat
11. add broth and onions
12. cover and simmer over very low heat 1 hour or till tender
13. remove steaks to warm platter
14. stir sour cream into pan drippings
15. whisk till smooth-- do not boil !
16. pour over steaks and serve
demonstrations.review: I don't know what the other reviewer was talking about with this needing a little boost in the flavor department - it was amazing! I did not use the marjoram (forgot about it) and cooked the steaks for probably a bit over an hour. I cannot believe how delicious this turned out...my husband says it has to go on our regular rotation! Thanks for a great recipe. This one's a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sam s favorite boneless pork loin chops

from "just cook this" with sam the cooking guy.  prep time does not include overnight marination.  he describes the marinade as the food cousin of the little black dress :)

1. put soy , brown sugar , ginger , and newcastle in a container , mix well then add the chops
2. refrigerate overnight
3. heat grill to medium-high and put on the chops
4. grill until done to about 160 degreessomewhere around 10-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: OK, this was seriously amazing! I put my chops in to marinade during the day on Friday on the pretense that we'd be having them for dinner on Saturday night - but I forgot that my husband had band practice, so that left them until tonight. I was a little worried that they might taste a little off or something, but I was not disappointed at all - and neither was my husband! I used big, thick boneless pork chops and they were so juicy and amazing...you have GOT to try this! "Little Black Dress" for pork chops indeed!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy indian style skillet chicken biriyani

if you are a lover of indian food, then you will love this dish! this is a skillet version of the indian biriyani, no need to bake in the oven it is all made in a skillet with the same authentic flavors, do not use low-fat yogurt for this or it will curdle, use whole milk yogurt. if you have any saffron add in a pinch to the rice when it is cooking, along with a very small pinch cinnamon and 2 teaspoons salt, use 3 cups water or chicken broth with 1-1/2 cups basmati rice. you can adjust the jalapeno peppers and chili flakes amount to taste and also use as much curry as desired.

1. sprinkle the chicken with about 1 teaspoon salt and 1 / 2 teaspoon black pepper
2. heat oil with butter over medium heat
3. add in the chicken and cook for about 6-7 minutes or until cooked through , remove to a bowl , cover with foil to keep warm
4. add in onions and cook for about 10 minutes or until lightly browned
5. add in garlic , chili flakes , curry powder , ginger , cardamom and jalapeno peppers
6. cook stirring for 3 minutes
7. add in yogurt , cook stirring constantly for 2 minutes
8. add in chicken and raisins
9. cook for about 3-4 minutes or until heated through
10. add in cooked rice
11. stir to combine
12. season with more salt and black pepper to taste
13. sprinkle with chopped cashews
demonstrations.review: So good! I have never had biriyani before so I don't really have anything to compare it to, but this was delicious. I did not have fresh ginger or jalapenos, so I used powdered ginger, some cinnamon (I loved the sweet edge it gave it!) and added a second packet of crushed pepper flakes left over from getting pizza. I also did what one of the other reviewers did and add craisins instead. I will definitely be making this again - great comfort food and even better the second day for lunch. Mmmm. :)

target.recipe_text:
swedish roast potatoes

these make a nice change from traditional roast or baked potatoes.

1. preheat the oven to approx 210c
2. cut across the potatoes at around 1 / 8 inch intervals , slicing about 3 / 4's through the thickness of the potatoes
3. put a baking tray on the hob and heat up the butter and olive oil until sizzling
4. turn the potatoes in the fat well
5. arrange cut side up and again spoon over the fat
6. sprinkle well with the sea salt and put in the oven for approximately 1 hour and 10 minutes until the flesh is soft
target.review: I make these potatoes often, they are really excellent.  For a "switch-up" try sprinkling with steak spice instead of sea salt.  This recipe also works well in a foil pouch on the bar b q, just remember to turn them often so they don't burn.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sheila s best apple crisp  no oats

this is the apple crisp from my childhood (there is no oatmeal in the topping).  if i could only pick one dessert to make the rest of my life, this would probably be it.  mom always made this in her beautiful copper au gratin pan.  i bought the same pan when i got married, just so i could make this dessert.  originally from the 1966 version of the "woman's day encyclopedia of cookery", mom adapted it slightly over the years (with a little help from cooks illustrated i think).  cutting the apples into "cubes" (instead of slices)  helps the apples keep the apples firm throughout. i have made this with pecans or walnuts.  i have also made it without nuts.  i like it best with pecans, but all versions are yummy!!  i love it warm or cold.  you can serve it with ice cream, but i usually only do that for dinner parties.

1. cut cold butter into small cubes
2. place in freezer to chill further
3. prepare apples
4. peel apples
5. cut an apple into quarters
6. cut out core
7. cut each apple slice one more time so that there are 8 slices
8. cube the apple by cutting each slice the "short" way 2 or 3 times
9. apple chunks should be no smaller than 1 inch
10. cube the remaining apples
11. put apples into an 8 1 / 2 x 12 inch au gratin casserole dish , or an equivalent baking dish
12. pour water over apples
13. prepare topping:
14. in the food processor put the sugar , nutmeg , cinnamon , salt and flour
15. pulse until combined
16. remove butter from freezer and put into food processor
17. pulse to blend
18. topping should be smaller than peas but not as fine as cornmeal
19. add 3 / 4 cups chopped pecans pulse too mix
20. sprinkle topping over apples evenly
21. cover dish with foil
22. bake at 350 for 30 minutes
23. uncover
24. bake for 30 more minutes
25. cool before serving
demonstrations.review: Thanks for this, I have never put a recipe for this in my book because I had an old fashioned home ec book from my youth that had the only one we've ever used.  My late husband made this for our sons, and he made it so often that he committed the recipe to memory - I didn't know he had absolutely ruined the book that it was in.  He loved to cook, and this has brought back so many great and wonderful memories!  This is "his" recipe, and it is just as good as I remember it being!  Thanks again!  It is now going in my book, finally!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pina colada slush

what a way to make yourself feel like your in the tropics and cool! pineapple, coconut and rum!

1. blend first 2 ingredients till smooth add to a large bowl or pot
2. add the rest of the ingredients to bowl
3. stir to mix
4. place in 2-3 freezer bags and freeze overnight
5. bring to room temperature 1 hour before serving
6. give a mix to blend and scoop into glasses and serve
demonstrations.review: This is excellent - I agree with dukeswalker - more rum though!!! :smile:

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kfc original recipe breading mix  copycat

my reverse-engineered recipe for replicating kfc's 'original recipe' chicken breading mix. yields one batch fried chicken (8-10 pieces, or up to 16 drumsticks). for a bulk mix of this same recipe for quick and easy breading, use recipe #453973. follow link to recipe #393795 for complete brining, preparation and frying instructions. please note: the nutritional information listing here is inaccurate -- since only a fraction of flour and salt actually end up in the finished product. so be aware -- the suggested sodium, sugar, carb and calorie levels are ridiculously exaggerated!

1. msg is in the actual original recipe , but may be omitted if necessary
2. egg white powder is sold in health food stores
3. you may substitute egg white powder with cornstarch
4. finely grind required herbs and spices separately in a clean spice mill or coffee grinder
5. use a pepper mill to medium-grind tellicherry peppercorns
6. i recommend mccormick brand tellicherry black pepper and ground ginger , spice islands brand ground sage and cardamom , spice appeal brand ground savory , and williams-sonoma brand ground tahitian vanilla bean
7. measure the base mixture and 11 secret herbs and spices into a large re-sealable container
8. break up any clumps using the back of a spoon
9. seal the container
10. shake container to mix well
11. store container sealed and store in a cool dry place
12. when ready to use , combine seasoning mixture with the 2 cups unbleached breading flour into a large re-sealable container
13. seal the container with flour and seasoning
14. shake well until thoroughly combined
15. follow link to recipe #393795 for complete brining , preparation and frying instructions
16. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is another killer recipe by the "spice guru" himself.  Would love to hear the story about the changes over time because this site isn't loving me these days.  ~nudge~nudge~

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork  nut   vegetable noodles

if you like noodles try this one.  my daughter loves this one.

1. cut the pork into 1 / 2 slices & place in a shallow dish
2. mix the soy sauce & cornflour together & pour over the pork mixing evenly
3. cover with clingfilm & leave to marinate in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours
4. stir fry the cashew & peanuts in a dry wok until toasted
5. reserve
6. combine all the vegetables , garlic & ginger
7. heat a wok with 1 / 2 of the frying oil & stir fry the vegetables until the celery & peppers have softened
8. remove from wok & keep warm
9. drain the pork reserving the remaining marinade
10. using the remaining oil heat in the wok until nearly smoking & stir fry the pork for around 5 minutes or until browned
11. add the chicken stock & remaining marinade to the wok & simmer hard until the sauce has reduced by around 2 thirds as you don't want the pork too wet when adding the noodles
12. add the vegetables , cashew & peanuts , freshly cooked noodles & chopped coriander
13. stir fry for 3 minutes & serve immediately with fresh crusty white bread
demonstrations.review: I made this for our family, LOVED IT.  I'll make it again for sure.  I used steamed noodles that I bought fresh in the grocery store.  Lots of really great flavors.  Good left over, no bean sprouts to go soggy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato relish recipe

posted for a recipe request.

1. to prepare the tomatoes peel them by soaking them in boiling water for a couple of minutes , the skin shoould peel off easier
2. remove the seeds and chop them
3. combine the sugar , vinegar , celery seeds , salt and pepper in a large bowl
4. stir until the sugar is dissolved
5. now add the chopped tomatoes , onion and green pepper
6. store the relish in an airtight container in the refrigerator overnight
demonstrations.review: This is a fresh and welcome relish when it is snowing and there is no sign that spring is coming, and probably at the height of tomato season too. It is fresh and light. I made as instructed (but I didn't bother to peel the tomatoes because we don't mind the skin) and I will process a small jar as I would any tomatoe preserve. I added some chili flake to the remainder as we are having an meal that will require some spice. It is excellent as is and not at all like a salsa. Thankyou for a new and speedy addition to brighten up our long winter!  I will make it again, but won't cut the tomatoes quite so small next time - maybe 3/4" chop.  Thanks again.

target.recipe_text:
skillet parmesan chicken

this is real comfort food. a family favorite. if you can, buy the fresh mozzarella. you won't believe the difference and it's worth it. the texture isn't rubbery like the typical mozzarella. i got it from watching an emeril show on the food network.

1. pound the chicken breasts between two slices of plastic wrap until about 1 / 4" thick
2. season with salt and pepper
3. dredge chicken in flour and shake off excess
4. dip in egg / milk mixture , then in breadcrumb / parmesan mixture
5. heat the butter and olive oil in a large deep skillet
6. brown the chicken breasts over medium heat until golden on each side
7. remove to a plate and keep warm
8. add the marinara sauce to the skillet
9. heat to boiling and simmer 10 minutes
10. add the chicken breasts to the sauce and sprinkle parmesan over them
11. place a slice of mozzarella on each piece of chicken
12. cover and simmer about 8- 10 minutes or until the cheese has melted and the chicken is tender
13. serve with your favorite pasta- we like linguine
target.review: This was one of the best chicken parm recipes ever!  So easy to make, especially without the hassle (and cleaning) of an extra oven dish.  I sliced the breast in half instead of pounding it thin.  The chicken came out so juicy and tender.  I didn't have any milk on hand so I used a little water in the egg mixture and it was just fine.  I also used part skim shredded mozzerella cheese instead of the fresh and didn't add the extra sprinkling of parmesan cheese, but was still great and cheesy!  I served it with a side of thin spaghetti tossed in the the simmered sauce.  This is the only Chicken Parm recipe I will ever make again!  Thanks PanNan!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: This was a great Meatloaf recipe!!  I used ground Turkey and for the first time (thanks to this recipe) the turkey did not turn out dry!  I added some garlic powder, sage and a shot or two of Worcestershire sauce but otherwise followed the recipe to the tee and it was wonderful, thank you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
veal osso buco  yummy

this is a very tender italian veal dish with a flavorful tomato and herb sauce. it takes a while to prepare, but does not require much attention while cooking. original recipe makes 6 to 8 servings, but i scaled it down to make 2 servings. it is delicious!!!

1. in a shallow dish , stir together flour , salt , and black pepper
2. dredge meat in seasoned flour
3. in a large skillet , melt butter with oil over medium heat
4. brown meat in skillet
5. remove meat from pan , and set aside
6. add onion , carrots , celery , and garlic to drippings in pan
7. cook and stir for about 5 minutes
8. stir in tomato sauce , water , basil , thyme , parsley , and bay leaf
9. return meat to pan
10. bring to a boil , and reduce heat to simmer
11. cover , and cook for 2 1 / 2 hours
12. serve the delicious sauce over meat , a bed of rice , or mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: This is very similar to my friend's recipe, he's a chef.  I first had it at his restaurant and it was amazing.  This recipe is almost an exact match and ohhh sooo good, thanks for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chicken cordon bleu with mushroom sauce

this is a great dish to serve to guests. this is also one of my husband's favorite dishes and it is treat to serve it to him as well.

1. use a meat pounder to flatten the chicken breats
2. place 1 slice of ham and 1 slice of cheese in the center of each breast
3. roll up and place seam side down in a casserole dish
4. securing with a toothpick if necessary
5. bake , covered , for 20 minutes at 350 degrees or until the chicken is no longer pink and juices run clear
6. while it is baking , mix together remaining ingredients
7. pour over cooked chicken and bake until sauce bubbles
8. i usually serve this over egg noodles
demonstrations.review: This recipe was so yummy.  I had to make a few substitutions, such as I didn't have sour cream so I used non-fat plain yogurt and I didn't have sliced mushrooms so I omitted.  Other than that, I added some pepper and sage to the sauce and that added great flavor.  I increased the baking time to 25 minutes and cooked the sauce for about 15 minutes.  A very delicious meal, thank you Pamela!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled herbed chicken thighs

this is my own recipe i dreamed up this summer. i've got an abundance of fresh herbs and wanted to try this out. turned out really good. i also use this mixture on grilled steaks. the amounts of the ingrediets are an estimate (i didn't measure anything out) so feel free to use your own judgment. hope ya like it.

1. starting with the herbs , mix all ingredients together into a rub mixture
2. rub mixture into chicken , under and on top of skin
3. set aside for an hour to let flavors soak into meat
4. leave longer if you have time
5. preheat your grill to hot
