here is a fast microwave chicken dish. it takes no time to prepare and is on the table in less than 30 minutes. this is good cold as well.

1. combine soy sauce & cornstarch in 8" baking dish
2. stir well & add sherry , ginger , garlic & cayenne
3. place chicken in dish and coat with soy mixture
4. cover with wax paper
5. microwave on high 6 minutes
6. turn pieces over , stir sauce & spoon over chicken
7. sprinkle with paprika
8. cover again & microwave on high 6-8 minutes
9. rest 5 minutes , spoon sauce over chicken & serve
demonstrations.review: This recipe was great!  Yesterday I worked in the yard all day and early in the morning had taken the boneless chicken thighs out of the freezer.  I needed something simple and easy to prepare, and I did not want to go to the grocery store for ingredients.  This was the perfect recipe.  I served it with my Rice Pilaf, which I prepared in the microwave, and broccoli. This was super easy and super delicious!  My DH and I enjoyed it very much. We have leftovers for tonight.  I followed AuntSana's suggestion and cooked the thighs in the oven according to her directions.  Thanks Tebo for this wonder recipe and AuntSana for your suggestion!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old time waldorf salad

the old fashioned waldorf salad has very few ingredients. this is the old timey way to fix it.

1. as soon as apples are diced , mix the mayonnaise into the apples so they will not turn brown
2. add celery and nuts
3. combine well
demonstrations.review:
I like the simplicity of this recipe.  It is very easy to put together and is also very delicious.  i added a little Greek yogurt to the mayonnaise and also added some dried red currants.
I am serving this dish with dinner tonight (our son and family are coming over) but DH & I could not resist sampling it at lunch time.  Thanks Darlene, for such a nice recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french baby beans  baby brown pearl mushrooms topped with almond

the food store had these baby vegies i just had to buy. i they were tender crisp! the mushrooms i know will be hard to find and i see no reason why you can't use any mushroom. simple and good!

1. in a large pan heat oil add onions , mushrooms , beans , garlic , red pepper stirring till onions are translucent
2. add sugar , salt and pepper and 1 / 8 cup water cover and let simmer till water is gone
3. plate and top with almonds
demonstrations.review: DH, SS, and I throughly enjoyed this recipe.  It was the perfect side dish to accompany Roasted Salmon and Rice Pilaf.  It really looked elegant and tasted even better!  I blanched the beans for about 4 minutes and added the beans after I sauteed the   onion, garlic, mushrooms, and red bell.  Did not have any almonds.  The recipe was great even without them.  Thanks, Rita, for posting the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled salmon and smokey tomato chipotle sauce

my favorite fish salmon is one of the richest, strongest flavored fish available, it combines well with piquant sauces. this one is made with tomatoes and chipotle chiles. you can find these chipotles canned in dark red adobo sauce.

1. to prepare the sauce: in a medium saucepan , warm the olive oil over medium-high heat
2. add the onions and cook until soft , 4 to 5 minutes , stirring occasionally
3. add the garlic and oregano , and cook until the garlic is light brown , about 1 minute , stirring occasionally
4. add the tomatoes and the chile
5. season with the sugar , salt , and pepper
6. bring the sauce to a boil , then lower heat to a simmer
7. cook for 30 to 40 minutes , stirring occasionally and crushing the tomatoes with the back of a large spoon as they soften
8. carefully pour the sauce into a food processor
9. puree and return to the pan
10. keep warm over low heat
11. generously brush or spray the salmon fillets with olive oil
12. season with salt and pepper to taste
13. grill the fillets , flesh side down , over direct medium heat until you can lift them off the grate with tongs without sticking , 7 to 8 minutes
14. turn the fillets and finish cooking them , skin side down , for 2 to 3 minutes
15. slip a spatula between the skin and flesh , and transfer the fillets to serving plates
16. serve warm with the sauce
demonstrations.review: The sauce in this recipe is incredibility delicious.  The seasonings and ingredients are just right.  My DH thought it was super!    I have left over sauce today and plan to use it with a black bean and chicken recipe.  I am sure it will be delicious!  This sauce could be used on almost any type of meat.

target.recipe_text:
best hot wing sauce in america

this sauce is simply the best one that i have ever used!  my family really enjoys this on wings and other things.  try something off the wall and fry up some potatoes and put this sauce on for a treat, or try using it as a toasted bread dipping sauce for a unique treat!

1. melt the butter in the pan
2. add the garlic and saut for 3 to 4 minutes
3. add the flour and whisk until smooth , cook for 1 more minute
4. add the franks and the vinegar , bring to a boil
5. if desired add the pepper flakes and simmer for 2 or 3 minutes
6. pour over the food of your choice and enjoy
target.review: I tried this sauce and it was Darn good. Works on alot of the stuff I cook. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flat dumplings

i got this recipe from my mom. i don't like fluffy dumplings, but these are flat and i love them.

1. mix together 1st four ingredients
2. then mix eggs with milk and add to mixture to form dough
3. roll out on floured surface about a 1 / 8 inch thick and cut into desired strips
4. boil in a broth of your choice for 10 minutes with lid off , then finish for 10 minutes with lid on
5. eat and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe, just like Mom used to make. I also like the fluffy ones but these are more filling. They go great with beef and gravy to.  Thanks again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shannon s hominy egg pita

my mom helped come up with this one. it's a good way to sneak in a serving of vegetables plus it's tasty.

1. spray small skillet with non stick cooking spray
2. heat to medium and add egg beaters and hominy
3. scramble egg
4. spread mayonaise inside of pita , and place tomato slices , cheese slices then egg hominy mixture inside
5. enjoy
demonstrations.review: Was easy and very Yummy!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned hot open faced roast beef sandwich

tasty and easy.

1. slice the roast into thin or thick slices as desired
2. warm the slices of roast in microwave or oven
3. heat the gravy in the microwave or on the stove top
4. add minced , sauteed onions and seasonings to the warmed gravy , if desired
5. lightly toast or leave untoasted the sliced bread
6. lay two slices of the sliced bread side-by-side on each plate
7. lay one slice of warmed meat on each slice of bread
8. pour desired amount of warmed , seasoned gravy over both slices of bread and meat
9. serve at once or reheat each plate in the microwave
demonstrations.review: Now yur talkin', this is my kind of sandwich. I used turkey but its still the same, yummy and fills the hole!! Throw some taters and a vegi on the plate and yur good ta go. Thanks !!!    Jimmbob

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cauliflower  brie and bacon soup

this is one of my favorite soups.  i absolutely love brie cheese because it's so creamy, and the flavor with cauliflower and bacon...wow!  this recipe came from lhj or bh&g.

1. fry bacon in a large pot until browned but not crisp
2. drain on paper towels , then coarsely chop
3. remove all but 2 tablespoons of drippings from the pot
4. add onions and saute until translucent , about 7 minutes
5. stir in cauliflower , broth , and celery soup
6. bring to a boil , reduce heat , and cover and simmer for 45 minutes or until cauliflower is soft
7. cool soup 10 minutes before adding bacon and cheese
8. when cool enough to handle , puree in batches in a blender until smooth , pouring pureed soup into another pot or storage container
9. garnish with parsley and or red pepper
demonstrations.review: This is a GREAT! soup! I bumped it up abit with my own chicken broth along with the soup and a shredded carrot and twice the cheese! Thanks for a good one. Jim...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yer basic barbecued spareribs

don't mess with basic - as in basically delicious!  adapted from good food magazine, june 1987.  if you don't have a jar of hot peppers, you can substitute 2 t. cider vinegar mixed with 2 t. hot red pepper sauce for the liquid drained from the jar of hot peppers.

1. cut spareribs between bones into single-rib pieces and trim excess fat
2. rub chili powder and salt into ribs
3. let stand at room temperature 30 minutes to 2 hours
4. heat 2 t
5. oil in 3- to 4-quart dutch oven or casse3role over medium-high heat
6. add as many ribs as will fit in single layer without touching
7. brown well on all sides and remove to paper towels to drain
8. repeat with remaining ribs , adding more oil if needed
9. pour off all but 1 t
10. fat from dutch oven
11. add garlic and onion
12. cook , stirring frequently , until lightly browned , about 5 minutes
13. stir in remaining ingredients and heat to simmering over medium heat
14. tuck ribs into sauce and simmer uncovered until meat is no longer pink near bones , about 20 minutes
15. let cool to room temperature
16. prepare grill or heat broiler
17. grill ribs , turning as needed , about 4 inches from heat until brown and crusty on all sides , about 10 minutes
18. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! Just the way I do mine. I sometimes par boil mine if real fatty. Im doing these tonite. Yur welcome to stop by for a plate. Thanks, Jimmbob

target.recipe_text:
zesty skillet chicken altered by mep

obviously got this off a can of del monte tomatoes, but i fiddled around with it a bit. it's a great weekday meal to throw together, especially if you have everything cut up ahead of time. i make this pretty often.(i also like a little frank's hot sauce on my plate) you can also throw in a can of black beans or whatever. be creative!

1. in a large skillet saute chicken , onion and garlic in oil until chicken is no longer pink
2. season with salt and pepper
3. add tomatoes , corn , green pepper , and green chilies and simmer till liquid is somewhat reduced
4. serve over rice and add cheese
5. garnish with cilantro if desired
target.review: I didn't have a can of green chilies, but still enjoyed this recipe.  As other reviews, I did add l/2 can of drained black beans.  I cooked the rice in chicken broth spiked w/chili powder and a bit of chunky salsa to taste and served it on the side, along with warmed flour tortillas, in case we'd want to stuff the filling as a burrito.  Made in memory of MEP, who will be missed by so many of us.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kielbasa   pasta skillet dinner

one-dish family pleaser.  this freezes and reheats very well.

1. cook pasta according to package instructions
2. in a large skillet , saute over medium heat , the sausage and garlic in butter
3. combine cornstarch and low-fat milk until smooth
4. gradually add the cornstarch mixture to the skillet
5. bring to a boil over medium high heat and cook for 2 minutes , stirring constantly or until thickened
6. drain pasta and add to skillet
7. stir in peas and cook over medium heat until they are tender
8. reduce heat to medium low , add cheese and cook until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: I exactly halved this recipe because it was for two of us.  I liked it a lot but DH asked me to make another batch of sauce because he thought it needed it. So, I did, added some cracked pepper, and enjoyed it a lot (with or without the extra sauce!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled chicken with avocado salsa

great summer meal! this works well with pork too.

1. in a small bowl , combine onion , lime juice , jalapenos , oil and cumin
2. pour 1 / 2 cup into a plastic zipper bag
3. add chicken
4. seal bag and turn to coat
5. refrigerate 2 hours
6. set aside 1 / 3 cup of the remaining marinade
7. place the remaining marinade in a large bowl
8. add the avocados , tomatoes , cucumber , green onions , cilantro , honey , salt and pepper
9. cover and refrigerate until ready to serve
10. in a small saucepan , combine jelly and 1 / 3 cup marinade
11. bring to a boil
12. cook and stir until slightly thickened , about 2 minutes
13. coat grill rack with nonstick spray before starting the grill
14. drain and discard marinade from chicken
15. grill , uncovered , over medium heat 4-6 minutes each side , until juices run clear , brushing occasionally with jelly mixture
16. serve with the salsa
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful! I made as written, except used 4 boness chicken breasts rather than the pork tenderloin given in the ingredient list. I'll make it over and over, since we live near family who grow avacadoes and we always need new recipes. I can't wait to make it again and invite them! (The salsa can also be used with many other dihes...perhaps adding lime or other experiments!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: I've never cooked meatballs without browning them first before adding them in the sauce.  What a mistake!  I'll never take extra time to do that again!  All I did was add 1 tsp. crushed fennel seed to the meat mixture then threw them in the pot for succulent, tender meatballs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate orange chocolate chip cookies

these cookies are super-packed with intense flavors.

1. heat oven to 350
2. beat 1 cup sugar , butter , 1 tablespoon grated orange peel and the egg in large bowl with electric mixer on medium speed , or mix with spoon
3. stir in flour , cocoa , salt , baking powder and baking soda
4. stir in pecans and chocolate morsels
5. shape dough into 1 1 / 2-inch balls
6. mix 1 / 3 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon grated orange peel
7. roll balls in sugar mixture
8. place about 3 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet
9. flatten to about 1 / 2-inch thickness with bottom of glass
10. bake 9 to 11 minutes or until set
11. cool slightly
12. remove from cookie sheet
13. cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: Cookie baking is not one of my favorite pastimes, so I only usually bake them at XMas.  These fantastic cookies will change my ways though, since I have now formed an addiction to them!  At least double the recipe, since they will FLY out of the cookie jar! I used fresh orange zest and loved the flavor so much I'll add a little more to the batter and sugar coating next time. A FABULOUS cookie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tropical miracle cake

this recipe was given to me by my bachelor brother, after he made it, so i figured i had to post this (my brother never cooked).  it's very simple; uses a cake mix and whipped topping.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease and flour a 13" x 9" glass baking pan
3. combine cake mix , eggs , oil and pineapple in a mixing bowl
4. blend on low speed , then beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
5. stir in nuts , if using them
6. pour batter into the prepared 13 x 9 baking dish
7. bake for 30 to 35 minutes or until cake tests done with a toothpick
8. cool
9. for topping , blend all topping ingredients , mixing well
10. spread evenly over cooled cake
11. refrigerate cake after cake is topped
demonstrations.review: It's a warm day today and a pineapple lemon cake sounded so refreshing.  I'm a lemon lover, so added some juice to the cake batter and a little more than what was called for in the topping, but either way is wonderful. I've never used condensed milk added to a topping, and it really made the cake different and delicious -- one that I will make again and again.

target.recipe_text:
orzo a la melanie

a colorful pasta dish, which can be served as a side dish, as a lunch and is particularly good for a buffet as it does not mind sitting around and tastes just as good at room temperature. i like this recipe because everyone in my house likes it (a rare occurrence) and because any vegetable can be substituted as long as it is cut up small. for vegetarians substitute vegetable stock.

1. cook orzo with salt according to packet instructions
2. heat the oil in a large frying pan
3. saut red pepper and carrot on a low heat for 10 minutes until softened
4. increase heat to medium and add green onions and garlic and saut for 2 to 3 minutes
5. add the squash , zucchini and tomato and cook for a couple of minutes more
6. add the tomato sauce and stock
7. when the sauce comes to a simmer , turn heat to low and stir
8. stir in the drained orzo
9. stir in the cream
10. stir in parmesan cheese
11. remove from heat
12. add salt and pepper to taste
13. can be served immediately , or at room temperature
target.review: Good base. I made the recipe exactly as stated. It takes time for the flavors to marry, so let it sit somewhere for at least 15 minutes. I would have liked a bit more flavor. I'll try throwing in crushed red pepper and maybe some oregano next time, but it was definitely something that will be easy to build on.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zippity dooo daaaa orzo salad

this is a fabulous salad that is sure to please all of your guests.  it is easy to increase or decrease the size of the recipe to suit your needs.
dont use extra virgin olive oil for this salad.  use an olive oil suitable for salads.  i really hope you enjoy my creation!!!

1. first cook your orzo pasta per package directions , cooking until al dente , and drain
2. in a medium sized , nonreactive bowl , gradually beat together the lime zest , lemon juice , salad quality olive oil , basil , garlic , and mustard until an emulsion forms
3. then season the oil mixture with salt and pepper to taste
4. mix your pasta , feta cheese , peppers , tomatoes , capers , kalmata olives , and chopped red onion together in a bowl
5. pour the vinaigrette over the pasta mixture and mix to combine
6. add oregano and green onions , toss , and then add extra salt and pepper to your tastes
7. chill salad for 1-2 hours for best results
8. you can make this in the morning and even serve it in the evening , but dont save it for too long
demonstrations.review: I used goat cheese instead of feta, since I didn't have any feta around. It made for a creamy base. The mustard and capers make a tangy dish. My mom LOVED it

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk pancakes

this is our favorite pancake recipe. i got it from williams-sonoma site. try it.. it's great.

1. in a bowl , using an electric mixer , beat the eggs on medium speed until frothy
2. add the buttermilk , melted butter and vanilla and mix well
3. add the flour , sugar , baking powder , baking soda and salt , and beat on medium speed just until blended
4. you can also mix this together using a wooden spoon or whatever you have
5. heat lightly greased griddle at 350 degrees
6. pour about 1 / 3 cup of the batter onto griddle for each pancake
7. cook until the tops of the pancakes are covered with tiny bubbles and the batter is set , about 4-6 minutes
8. flip pancakes and cook until the undersides are golden brown , about 4 minutes more
9. repeat with remaining batter
demonstrations.review:
Brilliant, fluffy, and amazing :) I was on the prowl for a good recipe and I knew Zaar wouldn't let me down. The praise showered on this recipe is totally deserved. I do a few things differently, though:
(1) When greasing the pan, remember to wipe up the excess. The pancakes will come out much more golden and delicious-looking. Also, don't forget to grease between each pancake.
(2) Keep an oven-safe plate in a 175-degree oven and keep all your pancakes in there until serving time.
(3) In everything I do that calls for vanilla, I double or triple the amount. Here, I only doubled.
(4) Try different spices in the batter. I added 1 tsp of nutmeg (it's the holiday season) and it was awesome - just an undertone of seasonal tastiness
Try pancakes with lemon curd. Evidently, it's a Brit thing.. But it's delicious

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai grilled chicken thighs

this is my first recipe - please be kind! my kids love it and when i take it to a bbq everyone wants the recipe. it is a variation on one i found in epicurious a while ago. it is very easy and very yummy!!

1. combine all ingredients except chicken in a bowl
2. mix thoroughly
3. add chicken and leave to marinate at least one hour , preferably longer
4. grill chicken on the bbq , hotplate or in the griller until golden brown and cooked through
5. ususlly you would expect 12 thigh fillets to feed 4 to 6 people- in my family the kids eat 4 each so this recipe serves 3
demonstrations.review: I don't know what it is in the marinade that makes it happen, but the texture of the chicken becomes.. slippery. It definitely wasn't slimy, but I really couldn't get over the texture. I grilled one batch, then pan-seared and baked another batch. I baked to see if it would change the texture. I preferred the baked a bit more, but the chicken did retain the texture, so I'm assuming it's the marinade that gave the chicken the texture it had.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon garlic marinade for chicken

i'm not sure where i got this recipe but it is very good. i usually throw some chicken breasts in a ziploc bag and add this marinade and then freeze. all i have to do for a quick meal is thaw and toss on the grill. this makes enough marinade for about 1-1.5 pounds of chicken breasts. cooking time reflects marinating time.

1. place chicken breasts in a large ziploc bag
2. mix first five ingredients together and pour over chicken
3. marinate at least one hour , longer if possible
4. cook chicken as desired
5. i prefer to grill mine
6. this is wonderful served on a caesar salad
demonstrations.review: This was incredibly easy and really delicious. I think I've made it through at least half of all of Recipezaar marinades and this is easily one of my favorites. I used four cloves of garlic, 1-2 teaspoons of cumin, and marinaded 1 1/2 lbs of chicken breast, then grilled it an hour later. The hour was just right and everything came out juicy and delicious. I will definitely make this again :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
walnut crusted trout fillets

looking for a new way to prepare your trout? look no further! this wonderful recipe comes from the greunke's first street inn restaurant and bon appetite.

1. using fork , stir flour , sage , salt and pepper on large plate to blend
2. whisk eggs in medium bowl
3. place walnuts on another large plate
4. sprinkle trout fillets with salt and pepper
5. dredge trout in flour mixture , then dip in eggs to coat
6. press both sides of trout in walnuts to coat
7. melt 1 tbs butter with 1 tbs oil in each of 2 heavy large skillets over medium heat
8. add 2 trout fillets to each skillet
9. cook until coating is lightly browned and trout are cooked through , about 5 minutes per side
10. transfer trout to plates
11. squeeze 1 lemon wedge over each fillet , sprinkle with parsley , and serve
12. serves 4
demonstrations.review: Great flavor! I used candied walnuts and it added a bit of sweetness that my guests and I really enjoyed. I think I had the oil heated too high, as it was smoking and I definitely ended with a blackened version, but it was great!

target.recipe_text:
easy carrot dip with a bite

i made petroushka's recipe #207860 yesterday and thought -- the food processor is already dirty, so i might as well make something else. after a bit of experimentation, this was the end result. i took it to office drinks today and it got two thumbs up from everyone. i used a tin of baby carrots, but you can make this recipe harder for yourself by cooking 250 grams (8 ounces) of sliced fresh carrots until they are tender, draining them and then following the rest of the recipe. i'm sure you could double or triple this for a crowd. use yogurt only if you need to reduce the heat.

1. drain the carrots and put all ingredients in a food processor or blender
2. add the yogurt only if you want to reduce the heat
3. buzz until you have the desired consistency
target.review: Thanks for the recipe, was quick n easy.  I enjoyed it but we didn't feel it rated 5 stars.  Took it to a pot luck supper, served it with another dip, crackers, corn chips, carrot & cauliflower crudites, the carrot dip wasn't gobbled up whereas the other dip disappeared in no time.  I didn't have cayenne pepper so replaced this with chilli powder, also cooked my own carrots, not sure if the change would have made a huge difference???  It wasn't hot at all, so perhaps thats the substitution diference.  Will try again with cayenne because I did enjoy it even if it wasn't a huge hit.  Thanks again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic machine french bread

this is my winner with tammiev and our friends. this recipe is for a 2 pound loaf and has never failed me. i think it is the lack of oil and sugar that they like in this one.

1. add to the bread pan in the order yours needs
2. for mine it is water first
3. then i add half the flour and the salt followed by the rest of the flour and the yeast on top
4. this will run well on the normal , rapid , and delay start cycles
demonstrations.review: Thank you very quick and easy to get together.  Popped it on at lunchtime with a delayed start for tea.  Was great.  Looking forward to making it on the dough cycle and rolling into a french stick to bake in the oven.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blue cheese and roasted garlic dip spread

this is the most amazing dip that is also wonderful spread on grilled steaks and burgers and also wonderful served on the side with raw veggies --- fresh garlic may be used, but be cautious only to use a small amount 1 teaspoon minced or less of fresh will do fine as it will overpower the other ingredients, i use about 1 tablespoon roasted for this, start by adding in a small amount at a time, and increase the amount of roasted garlic (fresh or roasted) as this dip gets stronger when left left to chill for the full 24 hours, so you might want to start with a small amount of garlic and add in more the following day if desired --- this is a dip i created years ago and still serve it today at get togethers it is the first to completey go so i always make a double batch --- gorgonzola cheese can be replaced with blue cheese for a milder flavor --- plan ahead this dip needs to chill  8-24 hours before using,  you may adjust all ingredients to taste, if you prefer a more creamy dip increase the sour cream slightly, but start with the stated amounts, you will love this dip! :)

1. mix all ingredients in a medium size mixing bowl
2. using an elctric hand mixer mix until well blended
3. cover and chill for 8-24 hours or up to 3 days
demonstrations.review: Was looking for something to use up some blue cheese that would also help dilute the blue cheese flavour for a work shout.  Blue cheese lovers enjoyed/loved this, non blue cheese fans were still not converted.  I used 75g creamy blue cheese, 1/4 cup Mayo and Sour Cream eacg, 1 tsp minced Garlic, 1/2 cup Cream Cheese, about 2-3 Tbsp sliced spring onions & 5 drops Tabasco, freshly ground black pepper.  Chill overnight and served with carrots and crackers.  Thanks from the blue cheese lovers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: Thanks for another great recipe.  Cooked these in  Recipe #92096 Italian Sauce, which we made into subs.  Looking forward to leftovers tomorrow with pasta.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy lemon self saucing pudding

been looking for the lemon delicious recipe i cooked many years ago but somewhere along lost the clipping (before zaar time) and this seems to come close to it though called a pudding (maybe searching in the wrong area) but it was good though sweeter than i remember (would need to work on the sugar content), certainly don't remember having the sprinkle sugar on top as per this recipe but i believe that what gives it its crispy top in this recipe.  serving suggestion was 4 but i think could be easily stretched to 6 served with cream and or icecream.  i found that 1 lemon gave me the rind and juiced that but needed to juice a second lemon to get the full 1/2 cup (got a little more than that and added the lot).

1. preheat oven to 180c
2. grease a 4 to 6 cup casserole dish
3. batter base - sift flour and a pinch of salt together and then add sugar and grated lemon rind , mixing well together
4. stir in melted butter , vanilla and milk mix and stir until all flour mix is incorporated
5. pour into prepared casserole dish
6. sauce - sprinkle the mixture with the sugar and lemon rind
7. combine the boiling water and lemon juice and carefully spoon some of over the batter and sugar topping , until fully covered and then pour the rest of the mix over the back of the spoon
8. bake for 30 to 40 minutes and let stand for 5 to 10 minutes before serving
9. serve with cream and or icecream
demonstrations.review: Tasty, easy to make.  Accidently mixed the sugar in with the hot water but it still turned out fine.  I did find that the sauce was quite runny I never have success in getting a thick self saucing pudding so could just be me or the sugar accident mentioned.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot cowboy beef   baked beans stew

this is always a hit with the kids. based on a betty crocker recipe.

1. mix stew meat , potatoes , onions , salt and pepper in crock pot
2. spread beans over meat mix
3. cover and cook on low heat 8-10 hours until beef is tender
demonstrations.review: Very quick and easy to prepare.  Didn't have beans in bbq sauce, so added 1/3 cup bbq sauce and 1 Tbsp Brown sugar.  Loved how the potatoes cooked up and tasted.  Meat was extremely tender.  Thanks.

target.recipe_text:
like mom s pineapple upside down cake

my mom made the best pineapple upside down cake and unfortunately no one in the family has the recipe.  i found this recipe on the internet somewhere, and its taste like my mom's recipe.  it is so yummy and no yellow cake mix.  note:  this was edited from when it was first posted,  i accidently added all the butter with the brown sugar for top coating.

1. use a 9 or 10 inch cast iron skillet or pan
2. melt 1 / 4 cup of the butter over low heat in skillet , add brown sugar make sure evenly coats bottom
3. take pan off of the heat , arrange pineapple slices on top of brown sugar
4. in a large bowl , cream other 1 / 4 cup of butter with the sugar
5. add eggs , one at a time , mix until blended
6. add juice , milk if using , and vanilla
7. beat until sugar is well dissolved
8. sift flour , baking powder and salt and mix with the egg mixture until well blended
9. pour batter into the skillet / pan
10. bake at 350 degrees for 35 minutes
11. let cool for 10 minutes and then put plate over skillet / pan and flip over
target.review: This is a great recipe! I took into account some of the other reviews and loosely packed the brown sugar for measuring and also only used 1 cup with the melted butter. I used crushed pineapple since that's all that was all I had. Instead of creaming butter and sugar, I mixed sugar and coconut oil. I find coconut oil is so good in baking; it adds a softness and hit of coconut flavor. I used mostly pineapple juice (added about 10% soymilk for richness). I don't have a mixer, so hand mixed everything together. I poured it all in a round cake pan (don't know if it is 8" or 9"), but the batter came almost to the top. Luckily it didn't spew out in the oven. I have a small convection oven, so I adjusted temp and baking time. Overall, wonderful cake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
1 pan fudge cake

this is my favorite chocolate cake. no fuss, no mess and very moist. back in the early days when it was paycheck to paycheck, this simple dessert made it into his lunchbox many a day because it was cheap and simple. no eggs, no milk.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in an ungreased 9 x 13 pan- yes ungreased , sift all dry ingredients
3. add the liquids and stir just until blended
4. bake for 25 minutes
5. frost with your favorite frosting , cake is extremely moist so care must be taken that you don't tear up the top of the cake
demonstrations.review: I've made this a lot, but don't think I've ever commented. I'm originally from the US, but am currently living in S. Korea. The cakes here just aren't quite what I'm used to eating, so whenever I get a hankering for cake, I make this. The ingredients are so easy, no mess, delicious cake, and everyone loves it. I have substitued coconut oil for the veggie oil (nice coconutty flavor, especially since I don't frost it), and I have tried 1/2 milk, 1/2 water. Very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
granny s fried green tomatoes

a southern staple! these are the best!

1. slice tomatoes 1 / 4 inch thick
2. sprinkle with salt and lemon pepper
3. let stand for 10 minutes
4. mix cornmeal and flour well
5. coat tomato slices with cornmeal mixture
6. heat oil over medium heat
7. fry tomatoes for 4 minutes per side , until tender and golden brown
8. drain on paper towels
demonstrations.review: These were very good. I actually was out of lemon pepper, so I substituted Everyday Seasoning. I was struggling to have enough cornflour/flour coating stay on the tomatoes until I read the review stating to coat, then dip in egg, then coat again. Those turned out wonderful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pink lady squares

this is another of our family favorites that makes for an excellent addition to the serving tray. looks very appealing on the holiday platter and great for special occasions. i often substitute the graham crumbs with crushed nillas. just as good untinted - but as my mom reminds me " always make the icing using the juice from a real lemon" - realemon will work but she's right ... that lemon juice makes for awesome!

1. base: in large bowl mix graham wafer crumbs , butter and flour and press into a greased 9x9 inch pan
2. bake at 275 degrees five minutes , take out of oven and cool
3. topping: mix the eaglebrand condensed milk , coconut and pecans and spread over base
4. bake at 325 for 20 to 25 minute being careful not to over bake
5. cool and ice with lemon icing
6. lemon icing: in medium bowl beat together the butter , cream and lemon juice
7. add in the icing sugar , adding more if needed for desired consistency and add just a small amount of food coloring to make for pale pink
demonstrations.review: I just realized I have not rated these. It has been a while since I made these squares (since last Easter), but I remember they were excellent. They were sweet with a nice lemon zing, and a not-too-gooey, still-chewy texture. I followed the recipe exactly, except for making a few different batches of icing and changing the colors to fit with Easter (pink, blue, purple...)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
2 minute microwave fudge

all i have to say, is that i'm obsessed with this recipe... i've never tasted better fudge! it's so good... although it's very sweet and very rich! prep time includes chill time.

1. sift powdered sugar , cocoa , and salt into a 1 quart microwave safe bowl
2. stir in milk and vanilla
3. mix well
4. place butter on top
5. microwave on high , 2 minutes
6. beat with wooden spoon until smooth
7. stir in nuts
8. spread in 8 x 8 x 2 inch baking pan
9. chill about 1 hour or until firm
10. cut into 36 pieces
demonstrations.review: I am making for the second time right now, it is in the freezer. The first time I made it I can't remember if I used unsalted butter or coconut oil instead of regular butter, but it hardened so fast that I didn't even need to refrigerate it. My husband thought it was a little too sweet, but I loved it. I followed the recipe exactly this time, and I noticed that it was a lot more liquefied.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry dreams

this recipe was a big hit with my toughest critics, my in-laws. i am always in charge of making the dessert for family gatherings and i needed something new for this year's fourth of july. so with some creativity and good fortune i came up with strawberry dreams. the red, white & blue finish is enticing to the eye and even more pleasing to the taste. enjoy!

1. wash strawberries
2. cut out small hole / core in tops of strawberries
3. blend cream cheese , sour cream , powdered sugar& extract in a bowl on medium speed until light and fluffy
4. fold 2 tbsp of grated chocolate into cream mixture
5. spoon mixture into a decorating bag with decorating
6. squeeze the cream mixture into the holes / cores of the strawberries
7. finally , top each strawberry off with a blueberry
8. best if chilled for at least an hour before serving
demonstrations.review: i loved these strawberries (and so did everybody else!) half of them i made like above, the other half i cut completely in half, laid them flat, then put the cream on top (i did this because i had more cream than strawberries). next time i make these i will leave them in halves, b/c they are easier to eat that way, and maybe drizzle chocolate over the top for more color. great recipe, thanks!

target.recipe_text:
bread machine cinnamon buns

bread machine cinnamon buns.

1. put yeast in bread machine first on bottom , then flour , sugar and salt
2. then melt butter in microwave
3. add beaten egg , milk and water
4. pour onto dry ingredients in bread machine on the dough setting
5. when dough is done , put it onto a lightly floured surface
6. knead in enough flour to make it easy to handle
7. if it is too elastic , cover and leave 10 minutes
8. use floured rolling pin to roll out dough on floured surface
9. roll out into rectangular shape to approx 1 / 4-inch thick
10. use filling and spread over entire surface of dough with spoon
11. roll up dough
12. cut into circle with a sharp knife about 1-inch thick
13. place these in a greased 9x13-inch pan
14. cover with a tea towel and leave in a warm place for approx 30 minutes , until double in size
15. bake in a 350 oven for about 25 minutes , light brown on top
16. when done , make glaze and swirl over buns
target.review: The buns were good, and the filling was fantastic. However, I did not like the texture of the dough. I found it very tough. This may be my fault though, as I found the buns also did not rise & fill out like in the pictures provided.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon swirl quick bread

this rich quick bread is a favorite with my family. i often give my husband a few slices to take with him on his commute to work, along with a tall travel mug of coffee.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a large mixing bowl , beat together butter , 1 cup sugar , and egg
3. combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
4. add the flour mixture to the egg mixture alternately with the buttermilk
5. in a small bowl , combine the cinnamon and remaining 1 / 3 cup sugar
6. pour a third of the batter into a greased 8x4x2-inch loaf pan
7. sprinkle a third of the cinnamon sugar on top of batter
8. repeat layers twice
9. bake for 45-50 minutes , until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean
10. cool in pan for 10 minutes
11. remove from pan to a wire rack to cool completely
demonstrations.review: Amazing recipe! It is simple to make, smells delicious in the oven, and the taste is phenomenal. It will be the first recipe I turn to when there is buttermilk sitting around! The loaf is wonderfully moist and perfect for a brunch menu.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wholesome homemade honey whole wheat bread

this is the most awesome wheat bread i have ever eaten. it is worth the extra effort and because this recipe makes 4 loaves, you can freeze them and have enough for awhile :) rising time included in prep.

1. dissolve yeast in warm water
2. in a large bowl , combine butter , molasses , honey and salt and mix well
3. add yeast mixture and then gradually add flours
4. turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth
5. place in buttered bowl and let rise until double
6. punch down and let rest for a few minutes
7. divide dough into 4 parts and shape into loaves
8. place in greased pans and let rise for about an hour
9. bake at 375 for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: This bread is fantastic! It was the first bread recipe I ever tried, and everything turned out perfect. I've made it for every family holiday since, both as loaves and as buns. I usually half the recipe, which is the perfect amount even when my relatives can't resist having a second slice! The sweetness is just right. Makes fantastic leftover-turkey sandwiches.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rhubarb sticky buns

my aunt used to grow tons of rhubarb and i wish i had it now, finding it these days isn't always easy. this recipe is very old, and you can use fresh or frozen rhubarb.

1. in a bowl , cut butter into brown sugar till crumbly
2. stir in rhubarb
3. spoon mixture evenly into 12 well greased muffin cups
4. set aside
5. in a mixer bowl , cream butter or margarine , and sugar
6. beat in egg
7. combine dry ingredients and add to creamed mixture alternately with cream
8. spoon batter over rhubarb filling cups about 3 / 4 full
9. bake 350 for 15-20 minutes
10. cool 5 minutes and invert onto serving tray
11. serve warm
demonstrations.review: This recipe is fantastic - my family hasn't stopped talking about it! I added half a cup of strawberries to the topping, used cinnamon instead of nutmeg & skim milk instead of cream. These were fantastic warm, nice and gooey, but also great chilled on a hot day. I will be making these again, for a long time to come!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
heather s stir fry sauce

my sil is a newlywed, and she's turning into quite a good cook -- we have even started sharing recipes. this is her stir fry sauce, and i love its basic goodness. you can add ingredients (i'll add a few spoonfuls of black bean sauce sometimes, for example) or change them around (i often use brown sugar instead of white, and sometimes i use rice wine vinegar instead of the white). i keep losing the piece of paper i have this scribbled on, so it's time to bring it to zaar!

1. whisk all ingredients together until smooth
2. add to stir fry just at the end , stirring well into the dish and let sauce come to a bubble
3. let simmer until sauce has thickened , then serve
demonstrations.review: A good basic recipe, with ingredients that are readily available. I used beef stock instead of water and rice vinegar, but still found the taste a little bland (although my family liked it). Next time I would add some garlic and maybe a little more soy sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon oatmeal poppy seed muffins

these breakfast muffins are perfect with your morning cuppa. the oatmeal makes them tender, but with a unique, nubby texture. a delicious way to eat your grains.

1. heat oven to 400 degrees
2. line 12 muffin cups with baking cups or lightly grease bottoms only
3. mix streusel and set aside
4. muffin: combine dry ingredients and mix well
5. add liquids and mix just until dry ingredients are moist
6. fill muffin cups
7. sprinkle streusel over muffins and pat gently
8. bake 18-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Fantastic oatmeal muffin recipe. I doubled the recipe and used a whole lemon (juice   zest) and the lemon taste is perfect. As I didn't have poppyseeds on hand, I omitted those and added frozen blueberries. I would definately make these again as they're perfect for a healthy breakfast.

target.recipe_text:
oh my god the best fudgy brownies on earth

i have had many brownies and i have to say that these are by far the best brownies i have ever had (and they aren't difficult to make)!

1. preheat oven to 350f and spray a 9x9-inch square pan w / cooking spray
2. on the stove over medium-low heat , melt chocolate and butter in a medium pot
3. mix in eggs , vanilla and sugar until combined
4. add in flour , mix well
5. pour into prepared baking dish , and sprinkle w / chocolate chips if you want a true chocolate experience
6. bake for 20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near center comes out clean
7. allow to cool , cut into 16 bars
8. enjoy !
target.review: "Oh my God" is right on!  Chocolate lovers... you MUST try these brownies.  I made these as a valentine present for my mother who loves chocolate like I do, and since she also loves raspberries, I added chocolate-raspberry swirled chocolate chips. Also, I added about a half teaspoon of raspberry flavoring.... we thought we'd died and gone to heaven.  It also took mine about 24 or 25 minutes to bake in an 8" square pan.  PEOPLE... you have to try these brownies!  You won't regret it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new england toll house muffins

adapted from joy of muffins cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. coat 12-cup muffin tin with baking spray
3. mix all the dry ingredients , flour to baking soda , in a large bowl
4. add chocolate chips , and stir to coat with flour
5. in another bowl , mix egg , milk , yogurt , butter , and vanilla
6. make a well in the dry ingredients and add wet ingredients , blending lightly , until just moistened
7. spoon batter into prepared muffin tins , filling batter to rim of muffin cup
8. bake 18-20 minutes or until tester comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Wonderful muffins!  I used mini-chips and I didn't have vanilla yogurt so I used sour cream and added an extra 1/2 teaspoon of  vanilla.  The texture was very light and taste was absolutely wonderful right out of the oven.  I'll definitely make these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amish baked oatmeal

this recipe came from an old amish cookbook of mine.  it tastes like an oatmeal cookie.  it stores well in the refrigerator and can be reheated in the microwave and served with milk.  this has to sit overnight, so plan accordingly.  it is well worth the wait, however!

1. melt butter
2. grease 1 1 / 2 quart baking dish and drop in eggs and beat well
3. add brown sugar , baking powder , vanilla , nutmeg or cinnamon , and salt
4. mix well , no lumps
5. whisk in butter and both measures of milk , then add oats
6. stir well , and refrigerate overnight
7. bake , uncovered , at 350 for 35-45 min , or until set in the middle
8. serve hot with warm milk poured over
demonstrations.review: We loved this. There are so many variations that you can make with this basic recipe.  The only things I did different were to add raisins and I only used 1/4 cup (half stick) of butter.  I'll try it again with dried cranberries, or maybe a small can of crushed pineapple, or maybe even some chocolate chips.... the combinations could be endless.  Thanks Aurora for a delicious start to our day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey zucchini bread

this is a great, spicy zucchini bread that is sweetened only with honey. make this on a saturday morning to enjoy with your coffee.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. butter two 8 x 4 inch loaf pans
3. beat eggs well
4. add oil , then honey and vanilla
5. stir in zucchini
6. mix dry ingredients together
7. stir into zucchini along with nuts
8. pour into the prepared loaf pans
9. bake for 45-55 minutes , or until tested done
10. cool in pans for 15 minutes before turning out
demonstrations.review: A great way to use all that zucchini that you have this time of year.  I made muffins and baked about 18 minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  Don't change a thing, except you might want to double the recipe and make a 9 x 13" pan.  Very moist and CHOCOLATEY!  Thanks Karen for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
triple treat chocolate muffins

this great recipe comes from one of the australian women's weekly cookbooks. i always make these when i want to treat my kids.

1. preheat oven to 190c oven
2. grease a 12 hole muffin pan
3. combine all ingredients in a large bowl , stir with large metal spoon until just combined
4. spoon mixture into prepared pan
5. bake 190c oven for about 25 minutes
6. cool on a wire rack
demonstrations.review: We thoroughly enjoyed these muffins.  What's not to like with 3 kinds of chocolate!  I followed the recipe as written and got 14 muffins... but I only baked for 20 minutes at 375.  I will make these again.

target.recipe_text:
auntie anne s pretzels   copycat

from copykat.com http://www.copykat.com

1. sprinkle yeast on lukewarm water in mixing bowl
2. stir to dissolve
3. add sugar , salt and stir to dissolve
4. add flour and knead dough until smooth and elastic
5. let rise at least 1 / 2 hour
6. while dough is rising , prepare a baking soda water bath with 2 cups warm water and 2 tbsp baking soda
7. be certain to stir often
8. after dough has risen , pinch off bits of dough and roll into a long rope and shape
9. dip pretzel in soda solution and place on greased baking sheet
10. allow pretzels to rise again
11. bake in oven at 450 for about 10 minutes or until golden
12. brush with melted butter
13. toppings: after you brush with butter try sprinkling with coarse salt
14. or for auntie anne's famous cinnamon sugar , try melting a stick of butter in a shallow bowl and in another shallow bowl make a mixture of cinnamon and sugar
15. dip the pretzel into the butter , coating both sides generously
16. then dip again into the cinnamon mixture
target.review:
This really hit the spot.The taste brings me back to the mall.
Such an easy dough to work with. I used 1 1/4 tsp yeast and they were fine. YUM O.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brats and sauerkraut

had this at a farm sell. the sauerkraut on top of the brat was just great! this can easily be made for a large crowd and keep in a roaster.

1. saute onions in butter
2. when the onions are caramelized add garlic , saute for 1 minute
3. add undrained sauerkraut , sugar , celery seed and bay leaf
4. cover and simmer 1 / 2 hour
5. add meat and simmer for 45 minutes
6. serve on bun and top with sauerkraut
demonstrations.review:
I've always poached my sausages and this recipe does just that. Only the sausage is poached in the liquid from the sour kraut . I  sauted the onions and garlic , added both to the kraut , sugar mixture . Started the brats in beer with a tab of butter and some sliced onion cooked added the kraut mixture and cooked  as directed and it was perfect . Thanks for a great recipe 
 Debbie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
company pork roast

this is very tasty and have received rave reviews. i serve the liquid from the roast, in a small bowl, to spoon over the meat.

1. place roast , fat side up , in foil lined roasting pan
2. mix remaining ingredients and brush on all sides of roast
3. cover with foil and bake at 325f for 2 1 / 2 hours basting frequently
4. uncover the last 45 minutes to brown roast
demonstrations.review: Company ? ha !They wont't get near it . LOL .   This is a real family pleaser. We love the flavor and the tenderness of the roast . I basted every 15 mins, and tripled the sauce . So Fine . Debbie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frijoles negros  cuban black beans

ay caramba, these are good!

1. fry the onion and pepper in a little oil
2. add the garlic and saute a little
3. introduce a little of the bean liquid until all previous ingredients are soft
4. add the beans with the remaining liquid
5. add spices and simmer about 30 minutes
6. add the vinegar just before serving
7. these are quite good when served over a bed of rice seasoned with just lime
demonstrations.review:
I did double the recipe, LOL . Had to put up police line tape to keep hubby from devouring it all . The best we've had yet and so simple . 
 Thanks so much for posting it

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cube steaks au poivre

this is just plain good. i cannot remember where i had found this recipe, but i thank whoever came up with this!!!

1. sprinkle steaks with salt and pepper to taste
2. in a large skillet , melt butter and cook steaks 2 at a time on medium-high heat until browned on both sides , about 4 minutes for each set of steaks
3. reserve drippings in pan
4. arrange steaks on a platter and keep warm
5. into pan drippings , over medium high heat , add remaining ingredients
6. stirring often to losen brown bits on bottom of skillet , heat until warm
7. pour over steaks and serve
demonstrations.review:
Cube steaks were on sale this week. I really didnt care for them.Your recipe changed that!
Now I wish I had bought more.
  We Loved the pepper. I added mushrooms and onions, tripled the sauce.Savory and delish.I also made gravy with beef broth as suggested by another reviewer.
Thanks Michelle for the recipe and thanks all you reviewers for the great tips.
Debbie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cube steak with onion mushroom gravy

made this last night. hubby really enjoyed this one. serve with mashed potatoes. mmmmm.

1. mix flour & pepper and place on a flat plate
2. add cube steaks covering with mixture well
3. in a large fry pan with a lid , brown the cube steaks in oil
4. add onions , mushrooms & garlic
5. saute about 1 miniute
6. add stock & worcestershire sauce and bring to a low boil , scraping the pan to loosen brown bits
7. cover pan & lower heat to a low simmer
8. stirring occasionally
9. cook 1 1 / 2 hours
10. serves 2-4
demonstrations.review:
Sublime ! All it needed in spite of the beef broth I used was a little salt.We loved the easy gravy.
Thanks
Debbie

target.recipe_text:
outstanding shrimp casserole

got this recipe from a friend in florida. my family adores this. very cheesy/creamy/oniony.

1. prepare rice mix according to package directions
2. in a medium saucepan , melt butter
3. saute green pepper , celery and onion for about 5-10 minutes or until tender
4. in a very large bowl , combine the cooked rice , cooked vegetable mixture , mushroom soup , cheddar cheese , swiss cheese and pepper
5. stir in the cooked shrimp
6. spoon mixture into a 3-quart rectangle baking dish
7. bake , covered with foil , at 350 degrees for about 40 minutes or until heated through
8. let stand 10 minutes before serving
target.review: This was comfort food for me. We thought the casserole was rich and creamy, just like you said. Not real spicy as in hot, but still well seasoned. It was easy for me to make and something that I would make again. Family loved it too. I used Paulette's menu and served with salad, french bread and white wine. Superb.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili cornbread salad

i have taken this to many potlucks. always popular.

1. prepare corn bread batter according to package directions
2. stir in the chilies , cumin , oregano , and sage
3. spread in a greased 8-inch square baking dish
4. bake at 400 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until tests done
5. cool
6. in a small bowl , combine mayo , sour cream and dressing mix
7. set aside
8. crumble half of the cornbread into a 13x9 inch dish
9. layer with half of the beans , mayonnaise mixture , corn , tomatoes , green peppers , onions , bacon and cheese
10. repeat layers
11. cover and refrigerate for 2 hours
demonstrations.review: Had a big, hungry crowd to feed over Labor Day. This salad was a monstrous hit with everyone. My dish was just about overflowing but I managed to get everything in there. Makes a lot but there wasn't one morsel left at the end of the day. A winner in my book. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken piccata

always looking for ways to duplicate the fine dishes i find in various restaurants, here is another "tweaked till true" recipe of mine. i serve this dish with bow tie pasta and drench the whole plate with the sauce.

1. season flattened cutlets with a thin coat of flour
2. salt and pepper them to taste
3. spray a saut pan with nonstick spray
4. add vegetable oil and heat over medium-high
5. saut cutlets 2-3 minutes on one side , then 1-2 minutes covered on the other
6. move to a warm plate and cover with foil
7. pour off fat from pan
8. deglaze pan with wine and add minced garlic
9. cook until garlic is slightly brown and liquid is nearly gone , about 2 minutes
10. add broth , lemon juice and capers
11. return cutlets to pan and cook on each side 1 minute
12. finish with butter and lemon slices
13. once butter melts , pour sauce over cutlets
14. garnish with parsley and serve
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent recipe. Restaurant quality in my opinion. Very easy to follow directions with better than expected results. Nice balance of lemon, garlic, wine and butter for a sumptious flavored sauce. I served it with linguine noodles. Deserves more than 5 stars. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken burritos

southern living; family favorite

1. remove chicken from bones , discarding skin and bones
2. chop chicken
3. place chicken and seasoning mix in a large zip-top bag
4. seal and shake to coat
5. spread beans evenly down center of tortillas
6. top with chicken , cheese , tomato , and onion
7. roll up burrito style
8. wrap each burrito in foil
9. bake at 350 degrees for 15 minutes
10. serve with salsa
demonstrations.review: These burritos made a very yummy but quick and easy supper for me and my family. I used Tyson whole roasted chicken which was delicious. The taco seasoning gave just the right amount of spicy flavor. Fast, easy, and family pleasing. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lime tea

love this so much. great summertime drink. add sugar to taste.

1. pour 5 cups boiling water over tea bags
2. cover and steep 5 minutes
3. remove and discard tea bags
4. add sugar , stirring until dissolved
5. stir in limeade concentrate
6. chill
7. serve over ice
demonstrations.review: We drink iced tea by the gallons. This was a new and exciting concoction that my family loved. We like our tea sweet but I found that 1/2 cup of sugar was plenty for us. Perfect blend of sweet and tart flavors. I served this with Manda's Beef Enchiladas, your Mexican Corn Bread and a salad. We had an incredible meal. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili salad

another main dish salad that may remind you of a taco salad but its not!

1. in salad bowl , combine all but the chili
2. heat chili until bubbly
3. pour over salad , tossing lightly to coat
4. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: A big hit at our house. I did like the other reviewer and used chili-cheese fritos. Very, very good and so quick to put together. My family loved it too. How exciting. Thanks Laurie.

target.recipe_text:
garlicky tomato bruschetta

this is a wonderful summertime appetizer. i keep a bowl of the topping in the refrigerator (it keeps for days!). really delicious and not too heavy. remember to make ahead - it needs to sit at least 8 hours.

1. bread: slice bread into 1 / 2" slices
2. brush oil on one side
3. broil briefly just until it barely starts to brown
4. you have to watch it !
5. cool
6. store in zip lock bag
7. topping: in a medium bowl , mix tomatoes , basil parmesan , olive oil , garlic and a little salt and pepper to taste
8. cover and chill in the refrigerator for 8 hours or overnight
9. spread a spoonful on toasted rounds and serve
target.review: Excellent! Comparable to the Bruschetta in our favorite resturants. (My son said better! and he doesn't even like tomatoes) I had fresh basil on hand and used that in place of the dried and it worked well, however I didn't have quite enough and need to use more next time. I used Kraft Grated Parmesan cheese in the container instead of grating fresh and this worked good as well. I think next time I will top it with some fresh chives after broiling. This will remain a staple in our refrigerator for quick, nutrious and easy snacking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lynn s favorite jerk chicken

this recipe came from my brother-in-law with a few variations from me.
wonderful and flavorful with very few carbs.  if you like your jerk chicken spicey, add more crushed red pepper flakes and cayenne pepper. cooking time does not reflect marinating time.

1. mix all ingredients , except chicken , in a medium bowl
2. cut each chicken breast into 4-6 long pcs
3. add marinade to chicken breasts
4. marinate at least 4 hours or overnight
5. can be grilled on barbecue or in broiler
6. cook just until done , do not overcook
7. this will dry out if overcooked
demonstrations.review: I am sorry but this tastes nothing like Jerk chicken. The flavor was ok. I followed the recipe exactly. All I could really taste was the cinnamon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: AMAZING!!! 20 STARS!<br/>I beyond love these!! I made them exactly as the recipe calls for and cooked them in the red gravy :) My best friend is Italian directly from the Tuscan Region, she said these are very similar to hers. I can't get enough of them!! Do yourself a favor people and make these!! Thank you so much for sharing this recipe :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey roasted pork loin

very yummy! we really enjoyed this.

1. preheat the oven to 375
2. season the pork and place in a roasting pan
3. in a separate bowl , mix together the honey , juice , oil and thyme
4. pour over the pork
5. add the broth to the pan
6. bake until internal temperature reaches 150
7. baste frequently
8. strain the pan juices into a saucepan small amount gravy flour
9. reduce until slightly thickened
10. serve over the sliced pork
demonstrations.review: This was really simple to make. I contemplated using lemon juice in place of the orange juice to cut down on the sweetness of the honey. I will try lemon juice next time, my kids loved it but I found it much too sweet for my taste. The tenderloin was wonderfully tender, I shredded it with forks then put the meat back into the reduced sauce and served it over brown rice. I added garlic to the sauce when it was reducing and will maybe try worchestershire the next time to cut down the sweetness. But overall it is a good recipe, thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek pork loin

i printed this years ago from about.com who listed it from the national pork producers council. this is a great recipe and when my grill was out of commission, i tried in my crock pot as well. i am glad i fought the temptation to increase the lemon and garlic, because the amounts listed are just right.

1. place pork loin in a large zip-loc bag
2. combine remaining ingredients and pour over pork in bag
3. seal and refrigerate overnight
4. remove pork and discard the marinade
5. grill over indirect heat on a covered grill until meat thermometer registers 155f , about 1 to 1 / 2 hours
6. let rest 10 minutes before slicing thinly to serve or proceed as above except place roast in crock pot with 1 / 4 cup good chardonnay and 2 tablespoons water
7. cook on low for 6 to 8 hours
demonstrations.review: I'd give this one 10 stars. OUTSTANDING! Thank you Deborah for posting it. My sisters and I are making a recipe book for a new bride to be and I'm adding this one! - I did mine in my slow cooker and threw in a few chunks of potato and some baby carrots cut in half - fantastic! My son (who is very picky about roasts) kept asking for more I can't wait to try it on the grill. Thank you again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot whole chicken

tender, fall-off-the-bone chicken! skip the overnight refrigeration if you are in a hurry. for variety, eliminate the onion and substitute a quartered lemon or two, stuffed into the chicken cavity.  chef shapeweaver had a good suggestion:  use fajita seasoning mix #28011 as another variation.  thanks!  the standard size slow cookers are a bit too small and a whole chicken won't fit.  you'll need a 6-quart slow cooker for this recipe.

1. in a small bowl , combine the spices
2. remove any giblets from chicken and clean chicken
3. rub spice mixture onto the chicken
4. place in resealable plastic bag and refrigerate overnight
5. when ready to cook , put chopped onion in bottom of crock pot
6. add chicken
7. no liquid is needed , the chicken will make its own juices
8. cook on low 4-8 hours
demonstrations.review: Although this recipe was tasty I am going to rate it just "Good"<br/>3 different peppers calling for 2 1/2 in total is an awful lot of pepper. I cut that back to 1/2, 1/2 and a few turns of my pepper mill.<br/>The fact that this recipe didn't call for any liquid whatsoever had me very skeptical so I did add a bit of water and chicken broth to the bottom. My chicken was completely thawed, maybe you are using a frozen chicken? That would make sense then that it makes its own liquid. Other than that I followed the recipe to a T, including the onion at the bottom. However, it was burnt to a crisp on the bottom due to no liquid. And I do mean burnt. I did cook it on low for about 6 - 7 hours while I was at work.<br/>I will try this again as I do like the flavor of the spice mixture (minus all the pepper it calls for) and will add some white wine, chicken broth and vegetables as other reviews have suggested.

target.recipe_text:
betty white s chicken wings

from my celebrity recipe collection; they sound perfect for a football party!  the smell while these sticky wings bake in the oven is amazing.

1. arrange wings in shallow baking pan
2. heat butter , soy sauce , sugar , water mustard and garlic powder if using , until butter and sugar melt
3. cool
4. pour over wings and marinate at least 2 hours , turning once or twice
5. bake in same pan at 375f for 1-1 / 4 to 1-1 / 2 hours , turning occasionally
6. drain on paper towels and serve
target.review: This must be the "Sue-Ann Nivens" side of Betty White, not the "Rose Nylund"! These are awesome wings! I used a 3 lb package of the frozen "drummettes" and it worked out perfect! Sweet and slightly salty...a nice change of pace from the "hot" buffalo wings everyone else serves...and you don't need a dippping sauce to cool your mouth down!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
off the shelf pasta salad

ok .. a couple of the ingredients are fresh, but this is a very quick and tasty salad for a pot luck.

1. cook pasta according to package instruction , and drain
2. add the rest of the ingredients , and allow to cool in the refrigerator for one hour
3. stir , and serve
demonstrations.review: I have to admit, I didn't make this myself-the chef himself, Bill Hilbrich and I actually work at the same company, and he brought this to our company picnic/potluck last month.  It was so simple, yet all the ingredients married beautifully into one sensational taste!  This salad is great as is, with basic ingredients mostly everyone would have on hand; hence the title says it all "Off The Shelf Pasta Salad"...OR you could only be limited by your imagination...I can see pepperoni or salami, different cheeses, artichoke hearts, fresh mushrooms, basil or pesto.  Thanks Bill-I'll be sure to use this when I have to make a fast salad that's tasty and simple!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean broccoli salad

easy to make ahead, rich in monounsaturated fat, everyone will enjoy this colorful and tasty salad.

1. combine dressing ingredients in jar or bowl and set aside
2. in salad bowl , combine broccoli with all other ingredients
3. whisk together the dressing ingredients and pour over the vegetables
4. gently stir to combine
5. refrigerate until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: This was very good.  It was a little too "tangy" for my taste.  Next time I might reduce the amount of vinegar and or the feta cheese just a tad.  It is very eye appealing, with the red peppers, green broccoli, white feta, and black olives.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach artichoke cheesy tortellini

this is from rachael ray, and oh soooo good!! like having artichoke dip in a pasta. my son even ate his on top of toasted french bread!

1. heat a deep skillet over medium heat with the oil and butter
2. when butter melts , add garlic and grated onion
3. saute for 5 minutes
4. sprinkle the flour into the skillet and cook for 1 minute
5. whisk in the broth , then the cream and bring to a bubble
6. season the sauce with nutmeg and reduce heat to low
7. separate spinach into pieces as you add it to the sauce
8. stir in the artichokes and cheese and season to taste with salt and pepper
9. cook the tortellini in salted boiling water according to package directions , about 7 minutes
10. drain and toss with the spinach artichoke sauce
11. serve immediately with additional grated cheese and diced tomatoes , if desired
demonstrations.review:
I made this for dinner last night....and it was so fantastic This was so easy to put together, and as written it really does only take 30 minutes! I followed the recipe exactly, except I used 1/2 pound of fresh baby spinach leaves, and 1 carton of chopped baby portebella mushrooms. I also threw in some leftover rotisserie chicken that I had the night before. But what really sent this out into orbit for me was the crumbled up 5 pieces of cooked bacon that I sprinkeled over the top of the dish. This is my favorite new "go to meal" when I want something fast and easy and good enough to impress company!!! Thanks so much for posting this winner!


.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paprika chicken with mushrooms

an easy, quick dinner that i often make on busy weeknights. there is nothing like the heavenly scent of paprika slowly simmering into chicken! this goes very well with pasta or rice. from original at allrecipes.com.

1. pound chicken breasts to 1 / 2 inch thickness
2. sprinkle both sides of each chicken breastliberally with paprika , salt , pepper , and garlic powder
3. in a large skillet , melt the butter over low heat
4. add the chicken breast , cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes
5. turn chicken breasts over and layer the thinly sliced onions and mushrooms on top of the chicken
6. cover and cook for 10 minutes
7. remove lid and mix onions and mushrooms into the butter sauce , reduce heat to low and cook uncovered for 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: S'kat, this was wonderful!  I used real Hungarian Paprika (sweet) for this.  Next time I'll be brave and try it with the hot!  I served this over a bed of egg noodles.  Pure comfort food!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooked short ribs

this makes lots of sauce but that is how we like it.

1. in a large zip-top plastic bag , combine the flour , salt , and pepper
2. add ribs in batches and shake to coat
3. in a large skillet , brown ribs in oil or butter
4. transfer to a large slow cooker
5. in the same skillet , combine the remaining ingredients
6. cook and stir until mixture comes to a boil
7. pour over ribs
8. cover and cook on low for 9-10 hours or until meat is tender
demonstrations.review: My local grocery had a sale on short ribs and I knew I had just added this to my cookbook so I snatched them up.  These are the hands down, the best short ribs I have ever made!  The sauce is wonderful!!!  Had enough to spoon over homemade mashed potatoes.  This is pure comfort food!  I wouldn't change a thing about this recipe!  Thanks Nurse Di!

target.recipe_text:
caramel bread pudding

as my son says, it is like eating french toast for dessert. :) it is very much like french toast with a lovely caramel sauce on it. we all like it warm best. make sure you use a 2-quart dish. trust me, it will boil over in your stove in a 1 1/2-quart one. oops! and don't worry, it will fall a little bit as it cools.

1. place bread in greased 2-qt
2. baking dish
3. combine water and brown sugar
4. pour over bread
5. combine remaining ingredients
6. pour over bread
7. bake at 350 degrees f for 50-60 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean
8. serve warm or cold
target.review: The recipe directions were clear and easy to follow, and the bread pudding turned out just right -- a nice texture and not too sweet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate coconut bundt cake

i found this recipe about 25 years ago in a magazine. i realize it isn't a 

1. can use a chocolate glaze if you prefer
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees
3. grease and flour a 10" bundt pan
4. filling: in a small bowl , beat egg whites till foamy
5. slowly add sugar while beating whites until stiff peaks form
6. stir in flour and coconut and set mixture aside
7. cake batter: in a large bowl , mix remaining ingredients
8. beat for 2 minutes with mixer at medium speed
9. pour about 1 / 3 to 1 / 2 of the batter into the pan
10. spoon the coconut mixture evenly on top of the batter
11. fill the pan with the remaining batter
12. bake at 350 for 50-55 minutes , or until cake tester inserted into center comes out clean
13. let cake cool in the pan for about 15 minutes , remove from pan and finish cooling on rack
14. when cool , top with glaze
15. confectioner's sugar glaze: in a small bowl , gradually stir milk into sugar , glaze should be thick enough to stay on the top of the cake , yet"drip" down the sides a bit
demonstrations.review: It's easy to make, comes out of the pan very nicely, is moist and not too sweet.  Also looks very pretty!  Would make a nice gift.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corned beef with mustard glaze

i cut this out of my newspaper years ago and prefer it to many others i have tried over the years.

1. rinse corned beef cut in cold water , place in a large , heavy pot and add cold water to cover
2. add peppercorns , bay leaves , onion studded with 4 cloves , garlic , carrot and celery
3. bring to a boil over medium-high heat and skim off any foam that rises to the surface
4. reduce heat to low , cover pot and barely simmer until the beef is tender , about three hours
5. while beef cooks , turn it over every 30 minutes
6. let meat cool in cooking water about 15 min
7. preheat oven to 350 degrees and transfer drained beef to a shallow roasting pan , fat side up
8. whisk together the mustards in a small , heavy saucepan
9. stir in remaining glaze ingredients and simmer for 5 minutes , stirring constantly
10. spread glaze evenly over top of brisket
11. bake in center of the oven , basting every 15 minutes , until heated through and beef has a deep , rich color , about 20 to 30 minutes
12. let meat rest for about 10 minutes
13. slice it across the grain and serve
demonstrations.review: I thought this recipe was great!  It's just what I have been looking for because I want to cook the corned beef by itself without potatoes.  The meat is very tender and tasty.  And the glaze is not overpowering.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zippy beef casserole

this a great quick easy meal. kids love it because of the addition of the potato chips on top. add a green salad and biscuits....yummy

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. cook and stir meat until brown
3. drain off fat
4. prepare elbows as directed on package
5. drain
6. in ungreased 2 quart casserole mix all ingredients except potato chips
7. cover and bake for 40 minutes
8. uncover , sprinkle with potato chips and bake and additional 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: Taste is similar to beef stroganoff.  It was nice, but tasted a bit salty and "heavy".

demonstrations.recipe_text:
walnut chicken

this recipe was found on the net and posted by request. original recipe was from helen chen's "peking cuisine". you can also use shrimp in place of chicken.

1. add marinade ingredients to chicken and mix well
2. marinate for 10 minutes
3. while marinating chicken mix together the sauce ingredients
4. set aside
5. heat wok on high with the oil
6. add the garlic and stir for a few seconds
7. add the chicken and cook to 80% done
8. reduce heat to medium and add the sauce , giving it a good stir
9. cook for 1 minute
10. add the walnuts and sesame oil
11. cook for 1 minute more
