this is the perfect consistency to hold on to pasta, don't omit the dryed thyme it is what makes this sauce and you may also add in a pinch cayenne pepper also if desired --- i'm a an extreme garlic-lover and i find that 1 heaping tablespoon is plenty for this recipe if you like an extreme garlic flavor then go ahead and use more! --- the recipe may easily be doubled but i suggest to keep the garlic at no more than about 1-1/2 tablespoons for a double recipe --- have plenty of mouthwash handy after this lol! :)

1. in a medium heavy-bottomed saucepan melt butter over medium-low heat
2. add in the garlic and thyme
3. whisk for about 2 minutes
4. add in flour and stir for 1 minute
5. add in table cream and heavy whipping cream
6. bring to a boil and simmer over low heat , whisking constantly until thickened , about 2 minutes
7. continue to simmer for about 2-3 minutes over low heat stirring continuously until bubbly and thickened
8. mix in the parmesan cheese
9. stir to melt the cheese
10. season with salt and black pepper to taste
11. serve over pasta and sprinkle with more parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: This is outstanding. I followed the recipe to the letter and it made the best, richest, creamiest alfredo I have ever tasted. Bravo!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bev s spaghetti sauce

this is a recipe i have developed over a number of years. this is the only spaghetti sauce my family will request! very easy to make. i hope your family enjoys it as much as mine does!

1. brown the ground beef , onion and garlic in olive oil with bay leaves , oregano , basil , italian seasoning , salt and pepper
2. add tomato paste , tomato sauce and diced tomatoes
3. stir well and bring to a simmer over medium heat
4. cover and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
5. use sauce to top your cooked spaghetti
6. top with sauteed mushroom
7. pass the parmesan
demonstrations.review: YUM! I love this sauce. I followed the recipe exactly, except I added about two tablespoons of sugar and skipped the mushrooms. Makes a TON of sauce...I froze about half of it for later meals. Inexpensive and delicious! I'll never go back to the jarred sauce. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken rice bowl

i love rice bowls!  this recipe is adapted from the internet.

1. combine teriyaki sauce and sugar in measuring cup , stirring until sugar dissolves
2. remove 3 tablespoons of mixture and set aside
3. pour rest of marinade over chicken in large plastic food storage bag
4. press air out of bag
5. close top securely
6. turn bag over several times to coat pieces well
7. marinate 15 minutes
8. add enough water to remaining 3 tablespoons teriyaki sauce mixture to measure 2 / 3 cup
9. blend in cornstarch
10. heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat
11. add chicken and saute 5 minutes or until chicken is thoroughly cooked through
12. add teriyaki sauce mixture
13. cook , stirring , about 1 minute , or until sauce boils and thickens slightly
14. spoon chicken and sauce over rice in large individual serving bowls
15. serve vegetables on top of rice or on the side , as desired
demonstrations.review: This was so yummy! I used chicken thighs instead of breasts...cheaper and more flavorful (IMO). For veggies, I steamed fresh green beans, broccoli, and chopped carrots for 4 minutes and then stir-fried them in the sauce with the chicken. HEAVENLY.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot beef broccoli soup

a comforting thick soup that is cooking for you all day while you are busy doing something else. i was very pleased with the results of this recipe and hope you all feel the same. it also fits into my new "lower" carb lifestyle.

1. brown ground beef and garlic , crumbling very well
2. drain off fat and add to crock pot
3. add remaining ingredients to crock pot and give it a good stir
4. cook on low 8-10 hours
5. leftovers freeze well
target.review: This was too easy to be so delicious.  I made it exactly as written on Sunday and ate it for lunch all week.  The smell of it cooking and then being reheated in the microwave at work drove my co-workers crazy.  Had to give everyone the recipe 'cause I wasn't sharing.  LOL!  Deserves more than 5 stars for taste and ease of preparation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh spinach mushroom frittata

i had some fresh spinach that i needed to use and this recipe was born. uses all the good stuff that i always have on hand.

1. melt butter in an oven proof skillet
2. add garlic , onions and mushrooms cooking until onions are translucent
3. add spinach , sautee for 2 minutes
4. beat eggs , salt& pepper together
5. pour over mixture in skillet , stirring to combine
6. cook eggs for about 4 minutes , eggs will be almost but not quite set still moist on top
7. sprinkle with cheese and put in oven
8. broil 6" from heat for 3-4 minutes or until eggs are set and cheese is lightly browned
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent frittata. I had to use up some fresh spinach and found this wonderful recipe.  Also, I added 3 strips of leftover bacon (chopped) to the egg before I poured over the onion-mushroom mixture.  It was my first time, too, making a frittata.  This is low carb and excellent!  I prepared as written except for adding the bacon.  I really enjoyed this recipe and will be enjoying it for lunches this week!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my own cube steak and gravy

this recipe is a old family favorite that i get asked to make at least twice a month and serve with my cream potatoes.

1. in a bowl or plastic bag add flour , salt , onion powder , garlic powder and black pepper
2. add cubed steak in flour mixture and coat well
3. heat oil and butter in a large frying pan
4. add cubed steak and brown on both sides for 15 minutes
5. remove cubed steak and drain grease out of pan , leaving some dripping grease in pan
6. add can of mushroom soup , water and heavy whipping cream or milk to the pan drippings and mix well
7. add cubed steak back to pan and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes
8. turning cubed steaks once during simmering
demonstrations.review: Yum! I used pork cubed steak and it was wonderful. Prepared exactly as written. Served with elbow macaroni. Delicious!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with oyster mushrooms

from 1001 more low fat recipes. i can get the most beautiful oyster mushrooms at the local asian market!

1. separate oyster mushrooms into pieces
2. saute mushrooms and garli in butter in a large skillet until soft , about 5 minutes
3. stir in flour
4. cook 1 minute
5. add milk , broth , and lemon juice to skillet
6. heat to boiling
7. reduce heat and simmer , uncovered , until liquid is reduced by half
8. stir in tomato , salt and pepper
9. cook over medium heat until hot
10. spoon over pasta and top with cheese
demonstrations.review: Absolutely awesome recipe. I, too, have a favorite Asian market here in Tucson and bought the oyster mushrooms this morning wondering what to do with them when I got home. Made this recipe EXACTLY as posted. I served over cheese tortellini. FABULOUS!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
down home sunday green beans

southern beans just like grandma made, healthier!

1. put turkey necks , broth , garlic , onion , and seasonings in a pot and bring to a boil
2. turn heat down and let simmer for 45 minutes to an hour
3. add green beans
4. bring back to a boil
5. turn down heat and simmer til fork tender or to taste
6. adjust seasonings to taste
demonstrations.review: I halved the recipe and used water instead of broth and omitted the salt.  Oh my goodness - all I can say is YUMMMMMOOOOO. Enjoyed with skillet jalapeno cornbread.  Definitely a repeat dish for me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smothered cube steaks low carb

nan

1. dredge cube steaks in a combination of pork rind flour , garlic powder & salt
2. fry in butter
3. when done , remove steaks from heat , and scrape all browned bits from pan
4. add water , and cream , and stir as it comes to a boil
5. cook till thickened
6. season to taste with salt , pepper& garlic powder place steaks back in cream sauce
7. pepper and salt to taste
8. serve with sauted mushrooms& onions
demonstrations.review: I used a little less than a pound of cubed steak (2 steaks cut in half to make 4 pieces).  I dredged in 3 heaping tbs. of flour seasoned with 1/2 tsp. garlic powder and pepper.  I fried in 1/4 cup of butter.  Made the sauce exactly as written (used another 1/2 tsp. garlic powder) except kept the precious drippings and bits for the sauce.  This was fantastic!  Wish I coulda had it with mashed taters but being on a low carb diet, it was awsomeness by itself! I definitely will adapt the cream sauce with other meats/fishes!

target.recipe_text:
mushroom muenster chicken

awesome...all i can say is awesome!

1. in a shallow bowl , beat eggs
2. place bread crumbs in a large resealable plastic bag
3. dip chicken into eggs , then place in bag and shake to coat
4. in a large skillet , cook chicken in oil over medium heat until almost done
5. transfer chicken to a greased 13x9-inch baking dish
6. sprinkle with cajun seasoning
7. top with mushrooms and cheese
8. cover and bake at 350f for 30-35 minutes or until chicken juices run clear
target.review: Yummy two of my favorite things: mushrooms and muenster cheese!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
demonstrations.review: yum!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortellini tomato spinach soup

really healthy soup, good to use when there's no time to spend in the kitchen!

1. in a soup pot , heat olive oil over medium high heat
2. saute the onion and garlic , stirring often until onions are translucent , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. add broth and tomatoes , turn heat up to high , and bring to a boil
4. add the tortellini and cook according to package instructions
5. when tortellini is almost done , add spinach and taste , adjusting seasonings with salt and pepper
6. serve immediately
7. garnish each serving with a sprinkling of parmesan
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I didn't add all the spinach and I added some italian spicy seasoning.  Great Recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
split pea soup  crock pot    dairy free

very little prep, just layer in crock pot/slow cooker, leave it for the day and a filling, delicious soup will be ready for dinner.

this recipe is a very versatile base split pea soup.  for a vegan option, omit the meat. i have made this recipe using ham, ham hock, and bacon. i have used veggie broth, chicken broth and water... each tasting different but yummy! i have reduced the salt but have not adjusted the recipe as written. this soup is even better the next day, it freezes well. this tends to be a thicker soup (especially once it has cooled) so adjust liquid after cooking to desired thickness.

1. layer ingredients in crockpot
2. pour in water , so don't stir
3. cover and cook on high 4-5 hours or on low for 8-10 hours
4. remove bay leaf
5. serve with some nice crusty bread or buns
demonstrations.review: Yum!! Absolutely delicious!  Roommates loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican crock pot roast

add some ole! to your pot roast. you can adjust the spice by using hot or mild salsa and you can substitute jalapenos for the chilis.

1. combine salsa , paste , water , seasoning mix and chilis
2. spoon 1 / 2 the mixture into the bottom of a crock pot
3. add the roast and top with the remaining mixture
4. cover and cook 8-10 hours on low
demonstrations.review: Absolutely Fantastic!  This is a keeper in my cookbook.  I put in  mushrooms as well just to add a little something extra.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese enchilada chowder

from bhg. a slow-cooker chowder.

1. add the black beans , tomatoes , frozen corn , onion , bell pepper , and jalapeno pepper to a 4 quart slow-cooker
2. stir to combine
3. in a mixing bowl , add the enchilada sauce and cream soup
4. whisk together
5. gradually whisk in the milk until mixture is smooth
6. pour over vegetables in slow-cooker
7. cover and cook on low heat for 6-8 hours
8. add cheese and stir until melted
9. ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls and top with sour cream , guacamole and broken tortilla chips if desired
demonstrations.review: Fantastic!

target.recipe_text:
creamy beef  noodle casserole

i made this for a potluck and it got wiped out immediately. just a very simple recipe, but good!

1. in large , deep skillet , cook beef , onion and pepper til done
2. drain grease
3. add manwich , soup , brown sugar and mushrooms , mix well
4. heat til bubbly , stir in 1 cup of the cheese
5. gently fold in noodles well
6. pour into lightly greased 4 qt casserole , pan or crock pot
7. sprinkle top with cheese
8. turn crockpot on low , cover and bake for about an hour til heated through
9. or bake , covered , in 350 oven for about 35-40 minutes
10. this makes 1 large pan , or 2 pans
11. canmake half a batch
target.review: Very good.I also halved it. Everyone in my family loved it. Great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger noodle bake

this is almost like a lasagna. very good!

1. brown hamburger , onions , and spices until cooked
2. add tomato sauce and simmer 15 minutes
3. mix cream cheese and sour cream
4. in 2-quart casserole , put 1 / 3 noodles , 1 / 3 cream mix , 1 / 3 meat mix
5. repeat twice
6. sprinkle cheddar on top
7. bake at 350 for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: My MIL and I made this one night but doubled the recipe. and it turned out AWESOME. my hubby says he can eat it every night.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy chicken   broccoli macaroni

here's a great recipe from the inside of a velveeta box!

1. cook and stir chicken in large skillet sprayed with no stick cooking spray 2 minutes or until no longer pink
2. stir in broth
3. bring to boil
4. stir in macaroni , reduce heat to medium low
5. cover with tight fitting lid
6. simmer 8 to 10 minutes or until macaroni is tender
7. add cheese and broccoli
8. stir until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: Rrally good.We will defiently make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger hash browns hotdish

this recipe is from an old cookbook from my mother's home town. very hearty and tasty.

1. butter a 9x13-inch pan
2. cover bottom of pan with hash browns
3. add hamburger , salt pepper and onions
4. sprinkle peas on top
5. mix soup and milk together and pour over peas
6. top with cheese
7. cover with foil and bake at 350f for one hour
8. sprinkle with french fried onions and return to oven for ten more minutes
demonstrations.review: We've made this about 5 times in the past few weeks. Didnt like peas so we used french cut green beans. Yummy! Thanks for the great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger   tots green bean casserole

makes a lot, so this is perfect for potlucks. quick and simple to make also.

1. brown hamburger
2. mix hamburger , soup and green beans
3. put this mixture in a buttered 9x13-inch cake pan
4. layer the tater tots over the top
5. bake at 350f for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: i made this last night and was very impressed on how simple it was.i will keep this stuff on hand so i can make it when we are in a hurry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potsie s creamed chicken and biscuits casserole

this is a wonderful and simple to prepare comfort food using things you probably already have around. kids love it- but so do adults. at least, in this home. try it. it is one of my quick and easy favorites. this is my first submitted recipe... be kind.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease the bottom and sides of an 11x7 inch baking dish or 10 inch quiche dish
3. chop the onion
4. heat butter in a small nonstick skillet and saute until tender
5. combine cooked onion , soup , chicken , milk , pimiento , and mayo in a bowl and then turn into the prepared baking dish
6. bake for 15 minutes and remove from oven
7. sprinkle 1 cup of the cheese over the baked mixture
8. arrange biscuits decoratively in a single layer and sprinkle remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese over them
9. return casserole to oven and bake until biscuits are golden brown and sauce is bubbly , usually about 20 minutes longer
10. the last time i made this i used a 1 / 4 cup of fat free mayo and 1 / 4 cup of sour cream
11. i think it was delicious ! also -- i took the suggestion of adding a cup of cooked green peas
12. what a terrific idea ! i loved it ! i think i might add two cups next time
13. thanks to you all for making my humble recipe and leaving your suggestions
14. you greatly improved a recipe i was already proud of
15. thanks so much
demonstrations.review: I fixed this last night and everyone loved it. I didnt have any cream of chicken soup so i tried cream of mushroom. And added peas.A total keeper!

target.recipe_text:
bird s easy shrimp scampi

this is a very simple and versatile recipe.

1. dry shrimp on a layer of paper towels to remove excess moisture
2. place shrimp in a bowl and toss with paprika
3. set aside
4. heat oil and butter in a large saute pan over med-high heat
5. add garlic and saut for 1 minute
6. add wine , salt and pepper and reduce by half
7. add shrimp and cook on one side about 2-3 minutes to sear
8. do not shake the pan at this point and it's important not to overcrowd the shrimp to sear and caramelize properly
9. after one side is seared , begin to shake the pan and toss shrimp to continue cooking another minute or two
10. sprinkle with parsley and saute' / toss one more minute
11. garnish with lemon wedges and serve
target.review: I'm not a huge fan of shrimp, but I enjoyed this.  My hubby however really liked it.  I did add a bit extra garlic and paprika

demonstrations.recipe_text:
belgian carrots

here's an interesting carrot recipe -- if you can, try making it a day ahead of time & give the flavor time to develop! they do reheat well!

1. in a medium saucepan , cover carrots with 1 inch of water & bring to a simmer for 10-12 minutes , until carrots are tender
2. drain water from pan & toss carrots with remaining ingredients
3. over low heat , stir carrots until sauce is heated through & serve
demonstrations.review: These are amazing! I love carrots to start with, but this was an exceptionally tasty dish.  Very easy to make and the flavors blend wonderfully.  I will definately be making these a lot.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turtle tarts

after receiving these as part of a christmas baking exchange i just had to have the recipe! these tarts are simple to make and so delicious.

1. bake tart shells according to directions
2. break up pecan pieces and place a small amount in each tart shell
3. you can make the filling fill more tart shells if you use more pecans melt margarine in a saucepan and then add the rest of the ingredients
4. bring to a boil , stirring a few times with a whisk
5. let boil for 2 minutes
6. while mixture is still hot fill tart shells and top with 1 chocolate melting wafer or a few chocolate chips
7. or melt chocolate in a ziploc bag , cut off one end , and drizzle over tarts
8. cool and enjoy !
9. these also freeze well
10. place cooled tarts in a tupperware container or a ziploc bag
11. label and freeze
12. to serve: remove tarts from container and let come to room temperature and then enjoy !
demonstrations.review: These were a little sweet for myself, but a huge hit with friends.  They have been begging me to make another batch for them.  Very easy to make too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ice wine infused peaches

from the television show "man-made food"  i was waiting for our fresh ontario peaches to try this recipe and oooooh, how i enjoyed this wonderful dessert! topped each dessert dish with a few leaves from my chocolate mint plant and served with some tiny crisp sugar cookies... hmm, hmm good!

1. in a sauce pan combine water , sugar and ice wine
2. simmer over low heat and until the sugar has dissolved
3. cook syrup for 3 additional minutes , take off the heat and set aside until needed
4. in a glass bowl , place peach halves and pour ice wine syrup on top and refrigerate to allow the flavors to mix
5. serve chilled in a small bowl and garnish with a drizzle of icing sugar
demonstrations.review: I served this over vanilla ice cream, topped with lightly whipped cream, and garnished with a sprinkle of edible gold leaf.  It was just lovely.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry peach cobbler

a nice seasonal cobbler.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. combine the fruit in a bowl with the sugar , cinnamon and orange liquor and pour into a 9x13 inch or 4 quart casserole dish
3. in a mixing bowl combine the flour , sugar , baking powder , and salt
4. after the dry ingredients are thoroughly blended , add the buttermilk , 1 / 2 cup heavy cream , and cold butter in quick succession , combining only briefly , to leave the mixture as lumpy as possible
5. pour dough onto a lightly floured board and flatten gently with a rolling pin into a shape approximately 1-inch thick and just large enough to cover the top of the fruit in the dish completely
6. place dough over fruit and seal edges so that the fruit is enclosed
7. make 1 or two vent holes depending on the size pan used
8. brush the dough with melted butter , and sprinkle the top with sugar
9. bake for 30 minutes , or until the pastry top is nicely browned
demonstrations.review: The filling was delicious, but I did have issues with the crust.  It wasn't nearly as flaky as I would like, though that is likely an issue more with the chef than the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kahlua chocolate cake

this is a chocoholics dream cake. this is very impressive and delicious. either dust powdered sugar on it, or try my recipe #200078  which goes perfectly with it.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease or butter bundt pan
3. mix all ingredients well in a large bowl
4. pour into a greased , 12-cup bundt pan add 12 walnuts to top of cake and bake until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out with crumbs clinging to it , about 45 minutes
5. cool in pan and serve on a platter with powdered sugar lightly sifted over the top
demonstrations.review: This was great!  Super easy to make and delicious.

target.recipe_text:
family favorite macaroni and cheese

i found this recipe in a taste of home publication awhile back.  i had written it out and stuck it in my 'to try' binder. a few months ago i made it for the first time... it's now my absolute favorite baked macaroni and cheese recipe! (with it tweaked for my own tastes). enjoy!

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. cook elbow macaroni as directed on package
3. while macaroni is cooking , melt butter in a 3 quart saucepan over low heat
4. stir in flour , salt , pepper , mustard and worcestershire sauce
5. cook over medium-low heat , stirring constantly , until mixture is smooth and bubbly
6. remove from heat
7. stir in milk
8. heat to boiling , stirring constantly
9. boil and stir for 1 minute
10. stir in cheese
11. cook , stirring occasionally , until cheese is melted
12. drain macaroni when done
13. gently stir macaroni into cheese sauce and pour into ungreased 2 quart baking dish
14. mix together bread crumbs and parmesan cheese
15. sprinkle over macaroni and cheese
16. bake , uncovered , for 25 minutes or until bubbly
target.review: A nice recipe.  I made it for our lake party and doubled the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic stir fry sauce

this is a good basic sauce. feel free to add ,perhaps a little lime juice, a pinch of cilantro, some peanut butter? have fun!

1. combine all ingredients except cornstarch in a small bowl or a 2 to 4 cup liquid measuring cup
2. place the cornstarch in a separate small bowl , and whisk in the mixture from step 1
3. just before mixing in to vegetables and / or meat , whisk the mixture one more time
4. add about 2 / 3 of the way through stir frying
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: We felt this sauce was bland, which surprised me considering all the great ingredients.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili s guiltless grill chicken sandwiches by todd wilbur

this recipe came from "top secret recipes, lite!" prep time includes the marinading time.

1. prepare the chicken marinade by combining the ingredients in a medium bowl
2. add the chicken fillets , cover , and refrigerate for several hours
3. overnight is even better
4. when the chicken has marinated , cook the fillets on a preheated barbecue or indoor grill set to a high temperature for 4-7 min per side or until done
5. while the chicken is grilling , make the fat-free dressing by mixing together the ingredients in a small bowl
6. build each sandwich by first stacking 1 / 4 of the lettuce on the bottom hamburger bun
7. stack the tomato slice on the lettuce
8. stack the chicken fillet on the tomato
9. cover each sandwich with the top bun and serve with honey mustard on the side
10. 8 points per serving
demonstrations.review: I can't believe I haven't rated this recipe.  It's really good and I've made this many times!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger hot pot  crock pot

this is very good, and inexpensive to prepare

1. in skillet , lightly brown ground beef , drain well
2. add seasonings
3. set aside
4. place half the potatoes and onions in greased crock pot
5. add browned beef
6. top with remaining potatoes and onions
7. combine mushroom soup and water and spread over top -- being sure to moisten and cover evenly
8. cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours
demonstrations.review: Very nice!  I split the recipe in half putting 1/2 in a crock pot and the other in the freezer for another day.  I used 98% ff cream of mushroom soup which turned out very well.  I also recommend lots of pepper.  Next time I think I'll throw some peas in for color and additional taste.  We put a little ketchup on top at the table.  Tx

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tilapia al ajillo  garlic tilapia

you can do this with any white fish, sea bass is great this way. fish is often served this way in the canary islands, though usually it is the whole fish instead of fillets. yum!

1. season tilapia fillets with salt and pepper
2. heat oil in a skillet over medium heat
3. put fillets in first , and when they start to turn color a bit add garlic slices
4. continue cooking about 4 minutes or so , then flip fillets
5. fry until cooked through , and fish flakes easily with a fork-- this will depend entirely on the thickness of your fillets , so you will need to watch them carefully
6. the garlic should turn a dark golden brown , but not be burned , if you notice that the garlic is starting to burn , spoon it over the fish , so it is no longer in contact with the pan
7. serve with freshly squeezed lemon juice and garnish with chopped parsley
demonstrations.review: DH says I don't like fish only the thought of eating it.  WELL, this recipe is great!  I'll def make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet pickled banana peppers

i love these peppers on hot dogs, hamburgers or what ever. they are so easy to make. you can double the recipe with no problem. i have never water bathed these pickles the jars have always sealed securely and i have used them a year or so later, just be sure that the top has sealed and you have heard it pop. if the jar does not seal fully store in the fridge and use within a couple of months. as you can see from the picture, i often mix hot jalapeno, anaheim, banana and any other peppers on hand - the result is  medium hot pickled peppers.

if you are at all concerned about food safety and would feel better water-bathing them, by all means do so -  just follow the instructions is any canning book - i recommend 15 minutes in the water-bath.

1. sterilize 2- 1 / 2 pint jars
2. bring the vinegar , sugar , mustard seed and celery seed to a rolling boil
3. place peppers in the 1 / 2 pint jars
4. pour on the hot pickling juice and bring liquid to within 1 / 2" of the top
5. be sure the edge of the jar has no juice on it
6. place lids and screw on bands finger-
7. seal jar and leave for 2 weeks
8. this is an heirloom recipe that uses a method no longer recommended by the usda / nchfp
9. current guidelines recommend processing in a boiling water bath at least 10 minutes at sea level to 1000 feet in elevation and left to cool , upright and undisturbed , on a cloth-protected counter for 24 hours
10. check for seal
11. if the jar hasn't sealed , either re-process the jars within the 24 hours or refrigerate and use first
demonstrations.review: Oh so good Bergy!!!  Never made sweet banana peppers before and it won't be the last.  Thank you much for the recipe!!

target.recipe_text:
layered tortilla pie

this is a quick and easy meal. serve with a salad. adults and children love this one.

1. in a skillet , brown ground beef and onion
2. drain fat
3. add tomato sauce , garlic , chili powder , salt and pepper and black olives
4. mix well and simmer for 5 minutes
5. lightly butter tortillas on one side only
6. place one tortilla , buttered side down , in a 2-qt
7. round casserole dish
8. spoon about 1 / 2 cup of meat mixture on the tortilla , then sprinkle with about 1 / 3 cup cheese
9. r
10. repeat layers , ending with cheese
11. pour water around the sides of casserole
12. cover and bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes or until heated through
13. let stand 5 minutes before cutting
target.review: Pretty tasty.  I think I may try it with a can of enchilada sauce instead of tomato sauce next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttery cut out christmas cookies

these are delicious. the cream cheese in the cookie dough really adds a softness, and makes the cookies taste really flaky and rich. they're a great addition to one's christmas cookie recipes.

1. combine the first five ingredients in a large mixing bowl
2. beat at about medium speed until well combined and creamy , about 3-4 minutes
3. gradually add flour , and beat until well mixed , about 2-3 minutes more
4. divide dough in half , and wrap each on in plastic wrap
5. refrigerate until firm , at least two hours
6. preheat oven to 375
7. roll out dough half on a lightly floured surface to about 1 / 4" thick
8. keep the other half in the fridge until ready to use
9. cut out the shapes your prefer , using a 2 1 / 2 inch cookie cutter
10. place 1" apart onto ungreased cookie sheets
11. if i'm making christmas cookie shapes , i sprinkle the cookies with red , green , or multi-colored sugars before baking
12. bake for 7-9 minutes or until edges are just slightly browned
13. these cookies may also be baked plain , and decorated with icings after they are cooled
demonstrations.review: This year I decided to try making cutout cookies one more time before I gave them up for good.  This recipe sounded easy, so I gave it a try.  They turned out beautifully!  The dough is nice and firm allowing me to even be able to punch out the more delicate designs like reindeer without having their legs or antlers break off!  The dough might could use a tad bit more sugar to give it a little bit sweeter flavor.  Thanks for the super easy recipe!  Now I don't have to give up on them for good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon cheeseburger meatloaf  paula deen

this recipe comes from a "cooking with paula deen" magazine (may/june 2006).  my family loves this served with macaroni and cheese.  the leftovers made a delicious sandwich the next day, topped with your favorite burger toppings.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray a baking dish with non-stick cooking spray
3. in a large mixing bowl , combine the first 9 ingredients , mixing well by hand
4. in a small bowl , combine ketchup and mustard
5. stir in 1 / 4 cup ketchup mixture into the meat mixture
6. place meat mixture in baking dish and shape into a loaf
7. spread remaining ketchup mixture over meatloaf
8. bake for 40 minutes
9. remove from oven and top with french fried onions
10. return to oven and bake 10-15 minutes longer , or until meat is no longer pink
demonstrations.review: This was actually pretty good considering I'm not a fan of meat loafs.  My husband really enjoyed it.  We had french fries with ours.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sugar cookie icing

this recipe is quick, easy, dries hard and shiny and tastes good too. i originally got if from allrecipes.

1. stir the powdered sugar and the milk until smooth
2. beat in corn syrup and vanilla until icing is smooth and glossy
3. if it's too thick , add more corn syrup
4. divide icing into separate bowls and stir in food coloring as desired
5. you can dip the cookies , paint them with a paint brush or spread them using a knife or the back of a spoon
demonstrations.review: Worked out quite well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken tortilla soup for dieters

my boss gave me this recipe when she was going to weight watchers. i tried it and was impressed with how easy it is to make and the great flavor. if you follow this recipe exactly this is only 3 points per serving. i myself never follow the serving and always tend to add more tortillas and chicken and cheese!

1. preheat oven to 200 degrees and thinly slice one of the tortillas and place it on a baking sheet and bake for about 15 to 20 minutes until crisp
2. crush the remaining 2 tortillas into small pieces
3. heat 2 tbs of the chicken broth in a pot and add your onion and garlic and cook about 2 minutes until softened
4. add the remaining chicken broth , crushed tortillas , tomato sauce , cilantro , cumin , chili powder , bay leaf and salt
5. bring this mixture to a boil , reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes
6. discard bay leaf and transfer the mixture to a blender and puree working in batches to avoid overflows
7. pour soup into 4 bowls and top each with tortilla strips , chicken , avocado and cheese
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was delicious!  I added some diced red bell peppers and celery to give it a few more veggies and loved it!  It was just as good as some of the mexican restaurants' soup.  Thanks for sharing!  We will be having this again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dirt cake iii

this is a joke, a bit of whimsy to lighten up your next party. the cake is really a quick mix dessert made with oreo cookies and soft squishy stuff. the trick is to capture everyone's attention with an announcement of some sort, and as you are speaking, trowel out some of the dirt from the flower pot around the flowers and eat it. may be followed by a worm dug out of the 

1. you may substitute vanilla pudding for the chocolate if you want , and use up to 20 oz of oreos
2. please use a clean new plastic flower pot or take the precaution of lining a clay pot with foil and wrap the stems of live flowers if you use them in order to prevent any toxins from entering the dessert
3. crush the cookies until they resemble potting soil
4. set aside
5. cream the butter or margarine , cream cheese , sugar and vanilla until smooth and fluffy
6. set aside
7. combine the pudding mix and milk until well blended
8. then fold in the whipped topping
9. gently fold the cream cheese and pudding mixtures together
10. to put the "cake" together , layer one-third of the cookie crumbs followed by 1 / 2 of the pudding mixture , 1 / 3 of the crumbs , the rest of the pudding mixture and topping with the balance of the crumbs
11. refrigerate 10-12 hours before serving
12. remove from refrigerator , decorate with flowers
13. serve by digging out portions with the trowel
demonstrations.review: I had forgotten how delightful and simple dirt cake could be!  I used 1 chocolate pudding and 1 french vanilla.

target.recipe_text:
chicken  shrimp and andouille jambalaya

a cajun classic, meal in one pot! have the hot sauce ready to splash on. serve with some crusty french bread, a nice crisp salad, and some of your favorite wine. :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large pan or dutch oven , brown chicken in hot oil on both sides
3. remove and drain
4. add andouille , onion , celery , bell pepper , thyme , oregano , paprika , salt , and cayenne pepper to the pan , cooking and stirring for about 5 minutes until onions are tender
5. add rice , tomatoes with juice , and broth
6. bring to a boil
7. place rice mixture in a baking dish or oven-proof casserole
8. top with chicken
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees f for 40-45 minutes or until rice and chicken are done and tender
10. stir in shrimp , parsley , and green onions
11. cover and cook 5-8 minutes longer or until shrimp curl and turn bright pink and serve
target.review: 5 stars, easy and delicious!  Everybody ate 2 plates, even my more picky 6 year old.  We will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon walnut granola

got this from a nutritionist friend of mine.  it has flax seed, and walnuts are good for you - the only nut that has omega 3's.  sometimes i'll also add a cup of sunflower seeds.  my daughter loves it and a 8 yo friend was over and tried it.  his comment: "this is tasty!"  i gave the recipe to his mom and she made it for a school function and it was a hit!  i use rolled oats, but you could use quick oats too.  i use this on top of fruit and yogurt for a healthy breakfast.

1. preheat oven to 275f in big bowl , combine oats , raisins , nuts and flaxseed
2. in microwavable bowl , blend together brown sugar , oil , honey and cinnamon
3. cook on high in microwave until mixture starts bubbling
4. remove , add vanilla and stir
5. pour over oat mixture and mix well
6. thinly spread on baking sheet
7. bake for 15 minutes
8. stir , return to oven for addtl 15 minutes or until oats are toasted
9. cool thoroughly
10. store in airtight container
11. i keep in fridge if not eaten right away
12. you could also pack into a pretty container and give as a christmas gift
demonstrations.review: Wonderful.  I'm so happy to have a healthy granola to feed my family.  It's not overly sweet.  I added a lot more raisins & walnuts than the recipe called for.  Left out the flax seed b/c we didn't have any in the house, but will add the next time I make it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato basil tortellini soup

this is very easy and tasty soup.  it certainly is a staple for our family.  my kids love it.

1. over medium heat cook garlic in oil until fragrant
2. stir in broth and tomatoes
3. bring to a boil
4. add tortellini , reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes
5. stir in basil , salt and pepper
6. simmer for 3 minutes longer
demonstrations.review: Super easy and tasted great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: We love these brownies!  They are so easy to make, my 8 year old is always wanting to help me. The last time I made them I used orange extract since I was out of vanilla and they were very good.  We have aded many things to them including marshmallows, nuts and chips.  I probably make these once a week and have shared the recipe several times.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate dessert quesadillas

these sound really good!  i have added them for zwt5.

1. lightly butter both sides of each tortilla
2. place each tortilla in a medium-hot skillet and sprinkle 1 / 4 of the chocolate chips on each tortilla
3. sprinkle cinnamon and sugar to taste on top
4. as the chocolate starts to melt and stick to the tortilla , fold over and brown lightly on each side
5. cut into wedges and serve with vanilla yogurt
demonstrations.review: Such a smart idea!  We make quesadillas all the time but I never though to make them chocolate.  My kids were thrilled.  I used milk chocolate and butterscotch chips mixed together, no need to add the sugar.  Yummy and quick... 2 of my favorite things :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooked baked apples

oh my!  it is apple season here and what a recipe to have.  while you are cooking, canning, reading a book, listening to music, dancing,  what better way then to make in the crockpot?  bonus-  your house smells divine!
(cookbook swap  2008, alskann)

1. scoop out center of each apple and and leave cavity about 1 / 2 in from bottom
2. peel top of apples down about 1 in and brush lemon juice on top
3. in bowl , combine craisins , pecans , brown sugar , cinnamon , and butter
4. spoon mixture into apple cavities
5. pour 1 / 2 c water in sprayed crockpot and arrange apples inside
6. cover and cook on low 1-3 hrs or until tender
7. serve warm or room temperature with carmel ice cream topping
demonstrations.review: Turned out great, didn't have any craisins so just added extra pecans.  My boys are loved them & so did I!

target.recipe_text:
better than boston market creamed spinach

after trying several recipes and even the frozen stuff from boston market(yuck!!!) i decided to "invent" my own. the amounts of ingredients are all guesstimates. so please feel free to adjust to your personal liking.

1. mix everything together
2. place in casserole dish
3. bake at 350 degrees in oven for 20- 30 minutes , or until cheese is bubbly
target.review: I have never tasted BM's creamed spinach but this was absolutely delicious. I used Neufchatel cheese in place of the creamed cheese to reduce the calories. Scrumptious! Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan burgers or burgerdogs

adapted from a grocery store circular. for a fun twist, you can form these into the shape of a hot dog.

1. mix all ingredients in large mixing bowl
2. form either 4 patties or 6 hot dog shaped links
3. grill , fry or broil depending on preference , until done
4. serve with your favorite condiments
demonstrations.review:
Very tasty burger. I used only half the Worcheshire and it was still quite tasty.
Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
you bring the macaroni salad   macaroni salad

whenever we go somewhere for a back yard bbq, i am asked to bring my macaroni salad. i think the "secret" that makes this macaroni salad different from others is the mixture of miracle whip and mayo. you know, some people like mayo...some like miracle whip. this way, everybody is "half" pleased!! this is another one of my "throw together" recipes, so i have tried my best to give some type of measurements.

1. honestly , i never measure "exactly
2. "
3. also , use as much or as little cheese as you would like
4. cook macaroni according to directions
5. when draining , run cold water over to keep it from sticking together and to "chill" it
6. mix mayonnaise , miracle whip , onion , pickle juice and sugar together to make "sauce
7. "
8. after macaroni is completely drained , mix macaroni , "sauce" , eggs and cheese until everything is coated and mixed well
9. the longer it chills , the better it gets !
demonstrations.review: Truly excellent. So easy to make. All I had was elbow macaroni and that worked great. My DH could not stop eating it. Mixed in a can of tuna to the left over for lunch at work. Super! Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot meatball stone soup

in the child's story, stone soup is literally made with a stone plus other soup ingredients neighbors might have and a delicious soup is made.  in this version, the stone is omitted but you still end up with a delicious soup, and one that is easily made as well.

1. combine all ingredients in a 4-quart crockpot
2. cover and cook on lo heat 9-11 hours or until vegetables are tender
3. stir in the frozen vegetables which have been thawed
4. cover and cook on hi heat 1 hour
5. serve with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Fabulous! DH was just diagnosed with Diabetes so I am collecting recipes to accomodate. This was simply delicious. I made my own mini meatballs using very lean ground beef. I also added 1/2 cup of barley. DH ate 2 bowls.  Thanks for the help!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fried chicken breast without breading

i make this as part of a quick dinner or lunch.

1. slice chicken breasts into strips or flat rounds , whichever you like
2. sprinkle all seasonings over one side of the chicken lightly , then flip and sprinkle the other side
3. in a large frying pan , pour in just enough vegetable oil to coat the bottom
4. heat the vegetable oil until good and hot
5. turn the heat to medium
6. add chicken and cook for 3 minutes on one side then flip
7. turn heat to low and cover
8. continue to cook for 5-10 minutes until the chicken is done
demonstrations.review: Marvelous taste is all I can say! A delicious low fat recipe. Followed the recipe as written and it was great. Thanks so much for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic butter rice

i love rice. i  also love garlic and cook with it a lot. it took a few tries to get the correct measurements for this recipe in order to submit it. i don't always use measurements when i cook.  this is very easy to make. this is a very moist and buttery rice with a good,  but not overpowering garlic flavor. for rice with less moisture, use less water and for a less garlicky flavor, use less garlic.  i read in an article on an internet medical site, that if garlic is cooked too long, it loses some of  its healthful benefits. they said not to cook garlic any longer than 3-6 minutes. i have also noticed that it loses some of its flavor if it's cooked too long. therefore,  i add the garlic towards the end of the cooking time to get more of a garlic flavor and more healthful benefits from the garlic.  i will sometimes have this for breakfast with a fried egg. i just put some of the rice on a plate and put a fried egg on it and mix it together. it is really good that way. i also serve the rice with gravy over it as a side dish with some meat.  it is also good just by itself. the chicken bouillon is optional but it adds to the flavor of the rice. if you have to or are watching your sodium intake, you might want to omit the bouillon or use less of it.  i have found that jasmine rice gives the best results for this recipe but you can also use white rice. prep and cooking times are estimates. note: due to the first review, i have edited this recipe. thank you lauralie41,

1. melt the butter or margarine in a 10" skillet over med-high heat
2. add the rice and stir
3. add the bouillon cube and stir until softened or dissolved
4. i use a spoon and break the bouillon cube apart while it is dissolving so that it dissolves faster
5. watch closely so that the rice does not start to brown
6. you might need to lower the heat if the rice starts to brown or appears to be cooking too fast
7. add the water and stir
8. cover with a lid and bring it to a boil
9. lower the heat to med to med-low and cook for 10 minutes or until rice is almost tender and a lot , but not all , of the water / butter mixture has been absorbed
10. this comes out better if it is "slow cooked"
11. add the garlic and stir
12. put the lid back on the skillet and continue cooking for 5 more minutes or until the rice is tender and all of the water has been absorbed
13. there may still be some melted butter at the bottom of the skillet , but that is okay
14. stir well and turn the burner off
15. let the skillet sit on the burner until you are ready to serve the rice
demonstrations.review: Trying to find something comparable to Uncle Ben's Garlic butter rice, this surely came close. I used chicken broth to cook the rice in and at the end I added salt and peeper. Adding the salt was a mistake. My bad! Other wise it was quite good. Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
show off roast pork

my favorite do-ahead party dish. excellent taste, very easy to make, and perfect for everything from a casual to a formal dinner party, or even a buffet. it's great served with braised belgian endive or lightly sauteed broccoli rappe, green salad, wine, and even pasta. versatile and easy dish. my go-to dish when we've got friends coming over, and i can't think of what to make.

1. mix together butter , prosciutto , garlic , rosemary , parmesan , and black pepper and set aside
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
3. cut slits about an inch or so long and a half inch or so deep all over the top of the roast
4. spread butter mixture over the roast , using the handle of a spoon to get it into the slits you made earlier
5. put prepared roast in a roasting pan , pour wine slowly over it , and cook for about 1 1 / 4 to 1 1 / 2 hours , depending on the size of the roast , basting about every 30 minutes or so with pan drippings
6. remove from oven , cover with aluminum foil and let rest for about 15 minutes
target.review: This was very good. As always, I followed the recipe as stated.   I think that next time I will use less rosemary (a little too strong for our tastes). Although my husband and son liked this dish, my 11 year old daughter did not.  I served this with another recipe from this site called Golden Potatoes (excellent), and fresh asparagus.  Overall, pretty good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
golden potatoes

i haven't tried this, but surely intend to! looks rich and creamy-just the way i like my spuds. recipe does not specify number of servings so i'm guessing 10-12. enjoy!

1. cook the peeled and cubed potatoes in large pot with salted boiling water just until tender
2. about 15 minutes
3. drain
4. in a seperate saucepan combine butter , soup and sour cream , heat until just melted
5. layer in a spray coated 13x9" baking dish
6. potatoes , soup mixture , cheese and onions
7. bake uncovered in a 350 degree oven for 30-40 minutes
8. let cool 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious!!  I will make this again for sure.  My family and I all agreed that this one is a keeper.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef patties in onion gravy

good 

1. combine all patty ingredients
2. mix thouroughly with your hands and shape into 4 patties
3. spray a non-stick skillet , and brown patties on both sides
4. add dry onion soup mix and 1 1 / 2 cup water
5. cover pan tightly and simmer for 20 minutes
6. remove patties to a plate
7. in a gravy shaker or jar , combine 1 / 2 cup water with 2 tbs
8. flour
9. stir flour and water into onion gravy
10. stir constantly with a whisk until it comes to a boil
11. boil 1 minute
12. return patties to pan
13. serve with mashed potatoes or hot cooked noodles
demonstrations.review: I don't really know what was wrong, but I just know that none of us here really cared for it.  I think that maybe it need more flavor.  Perhaps I should have added some mushrooms ect.  It was OK, but not something I would rush to make again.  Sorry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and stuffing bake

a long time favorite that i just found again.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. prepare stuffing according to package directions , but do not let stand
3. spoon stuffing across the center of a 2 quart shallow baking dish
4. arrange 3 chicken breast halves on each side of the stuffing , overlapping if necessary
5. combine soup , milk and parsley
6. pour over chicken
7. cover with foil and bake for 15 minutes
8. uncover and bake 10 minutes longer or until the chicken is no longer pink
9. you may need to lift some pieces of chicken so that you can check all of it
10. stir sauce before serving
demonstrations.review: I followed the recipe exactly as stated and felt that the stuffing mix was the only ingredient that had any flavor.  The chicken and the soup mixture were very bland for my family's taste.  This recipe was just okay for us.  If I were to make it again, I would add garlic and other seasonings as suggested by some of the other reviewers.  Also, I would definately double up on the soup and stuffing for my hungry family of 4.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ice water potatoes

just like the broasted potatoes i had at monterey restaurant for every birthday i had as a kid.

1. prepare the potatoes by cutting each into wedges lengthwise about 8 wedges for each potatoes
2. place in a bowl with ice cubes and add water to cover
3. place in fridge for at least 45 minutes
4. drain and pat with paper towels to dry
5. melt butter with minced garlic salt and pepper
6. i usually use a cast iron skillet , but any oven-proof pan will do
7. pour butter over potatoes in skillet , the butter mixture will stick because the potatoes are so cold !
8. bake in a 425 degree oven about 25 minutes
9. broasted !
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe.  I used red skinned potatoes and followed the recipe exactly as stated.  Everyone loved these potatoes.  I  will definately be making this recipe again.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot whole chicken

tender, fall-off-the-bone chicken! skip the overnight refrigeration if you are in a hurry. for variety, eliminate the onion and substitute a quartered lemon or two, stuffed into the chicken cavity.  chef shapeweaver had a good suggestion:  use fajita seasoning mix #28011 as another variation.  thanks!  the standard size slow cookers are a bit too small and a whole chicken won't fit.  you'll need a 6-quart slow cooker for this recipe.

1. in a small bowl , combine the spices
2. remove any giblets from chicken and clean chicken
3. rub spice mixture onto the chicken
4. place in resealable plastic bag and refrigerate overnight
5. when ready to cook , put chopped onion in bottom of crock pot
6. add chicken
7. no liquid is needed , the chicken will make its own juices
8. cook on low 4-8 hours
demonstrations.review: This was very good. This was the second time I have made this recipe.  The first time I used the rub with the exact ingredients as listed and cooked in the oven.  We all  thought that it was a little too spicy, so the second time I made this recipe I omitted the cayenne pepper and used the crockpot.  It is an incrediblely easy recipe and the meat very tender and juicy  Both times I used a 5 - 6 pound Perdue Oven Stuffer Roaster with pop-up timer.  I agree with a suggestion from one of the other reviews... after removing the chicken from the crockpot, pop it in the oven to add a little crispness.  My family and I agree this was a very flavorful and delicious chicken.

target.recipe_text:
layered hummus dip

the mediterranean version of the ever popular mexican layered dip. instead of using garlic salt, i mix a large clove of pressed garlic with the hummus. serve with toasted pita, flat bread or tortilla chips.

1. combine hummus and cumin , spread on the bottom of a 9 inch pie dish
2. top with a layer of tomatoes , seasoned with garlic salt
3. add the cucumbers and sprinkle with pepper
4. add a layer of feta topped with olives , then parsley
target.review:
I've made this several times and it's a hit every single time!

To avoid the liquid caused by the tomatoes and cucumbers, I dump them separately into mini-strainers overnight after preparing them according to the recipe plus a tiny bit of extra salt.  The amount of liquid strained out is amazing.

Leftover dip is delicious for lunch the next day on either crackers or French bread. Only had leftovers once, though!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek shrimp with rigatoni

if you love shrimp, tomatoes, & feta cheese, this one is for you. it is similar to others in the zaar database, but enough different that i think it is worth posting. it is from the local newspaper, the yellow newsprint a testiment to how many years it's been in my files.

1. preheat the oven to 400 degrees
2. heat 1 tablespoon oil in skillet , and add the garlic
3. cook briefly , stirring , then add the tomatoes
4. cook about one minute and add the salt , pepper , wine , basil , & oregano
5. cook over medium heat , about 10 minutes
6. sprinkle the shrimp with salt& pepper
7. heat the remaining 4 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet and add the shrimp
8. cook quickly for about 1 minute , just until the shrimp turns red
9. sprinkle with the red pepper flakes
10. spoon the shrimp& any pan juices into a small baking dish
11. sprinkle the shrimp with the crumbled feta cheese
12. spoon the tomato sauce over the shrimp& cheese
13. bake for 10 minutes
14. meanwhile , cook the rigatoni according to the directions on the package and drain
15. do not overcook
16. serve the rigatoni with the shrimp mixture spooned over it
demonstrations.review: Judy this is delicious!  I did follow FlemishMinx's idea to put the shrimp in the sauce instead of the oil.  I'll use Roma tomatoes next time as the ones I used were watery.  DH said "This is a keeper; make it again."  It goes into "My Favorites" cookbook.  Thank you for sharing it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy macaroni salad

this is my own macaroni salad.  i did not get it from my mother or my grandmother and i did not get it out of a book or off the internet. it is not amish, cajun, mexican or any other description of the various macaroni salads that are posted on the internet.  it is my own made up salad.  it is designed after my own recipe #20155 that i have posted on recipezaar (with 121 high reviews, thank you very much to those that have tried it).  the dressing is mostly the same, but there are a few other ingredients in this salad that is not in my potato salad.  i hope some of you will enjoy it as much as you did the other.

1. mix cooled macaroni , celery , onions , bell pepper and green olives together in a large bowl
2. in a separate bowl mix together the mayonnaise , mustard , vinegar , pickle relish , sugar , salt , pepper and celery seed , stirring well
3. stir dressing into the macaroni mixture
4. stir in the crumbled bacon
5. serve chilled
6. for another variation , omit the green olives , add sliced black olives and a container of grape tomatoes
7. for a meal type salad , add diced cooked chicken or tuna fish
demonstrations.review: Nice and tasty and makes enough to take to a potluck.  I discovered too late that our onions had gone bad, so I substituted a quarter cup of chopped shallots.  Thanks Karen for a great recipe that ended my hunt for a wonderful macaroni salad.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rumlicious rum cake

this cake is not for the weak of heart it's guaranteed to be a crowd winner. i always like to add a shot or two more than what the recipe calls for.

1. preheat oven 350 degrees
2. grease and lightly flour one bundt pan , and evenly distribute the the nuts on the bottom of the pan
3. in a large mixing bowl blend the cake mix , water , oil , 1 / 2 cup rum , eggs , and the instant vanilla pudding
4. pour batter into the greased bundt pan and bake for 1 hour or until a toothpick is instered into the center and it comes out clean
5. 5-10 minutes before the cake is removed from the oven , combine the remaining 1 / 2 cup rum , butter , and sugar into a sausepan
6. heat on stove until th butter melts and the sugar has dissolved
7. once the cake has been removed from the oven slowly pour the entire hot rum mixture over
8. let the cake rest for 10 minutes and then turn out onto a plate
9. cool
demonstrations.review: If you love rum, you'll love this cake.  We make it with pecans instead of walnuts (allergic); make sure to use butter in the glaze not a substitute.  This was my Mom's favorite cake so it brings back warm memories.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian spiced roasted baby carrots

the packages of the peeled baby carrots that you find the your grocery cuts back on the prep time for these babies!! a sara moulton recipe.

1. preheat the oven to 450f
2. combine the carrots , oil and salt in a medium bowl
3. spread the carrots on a rimmed baking sheet and roast , stirring once , until tender and starting to brown , 20-25 minute
4. meanwhile , combine the soy sauce , butter , ginger , cumin , vinegar , sesame oil , and pepper in a large bowl
5. when the carrots are tender , add them to the soy sauce mixture and toss until the butter melts and the carrots are completely coated
6. serve immediately
demonstrations.review:
This is a wonderful method to roast baby carrots! My DS & I loved it after I added about a tablespoon of brown sugar.  

My DH hated this recipe but he hates cumin so if you don't like cumin, I'd suggest making a different recipe!  

Easy to make, I recommend it with the addition of brown sugar to balance the flavors.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Even though there are already 58 reviews of the wonderful recipe, I just had to add my 5 stars as well.

I made it exactly as the recipe details except for softening the block of cream cheese in the micro, adding a couple of large spoonfuls of sour cream, and dropping dollops of the mixture over the chicken at the end.  After 20 minutes on "warm" I mixed everything together: the sauce was thick.

I also served this with rice the first night and turned it into chicken wraps the second by shredding the chicken, mixing it with the sauce, lots of shredded sharp cheddar cheese, and wrapping it all in flour tortillas.

Two wonderful easy meals.  This one went into "My Favorites" cookbook.

target.recipe_text:
fresh apple cake with nut topping

my aunt made this cake and shared the recipe with my mom. i have made this cake and its nice and moist.

1. preheat oven to 350 deg f
2. grease and lightly flour a 13 x 9 inch cake pan
3. mix together sugars , eggs and shortening
4. dissolve soda in buttermilk
5. mix together the dry ingredients , adding to the sugar mix alternately with the buttermilk
6. after mixing the above well , fold in apples and pour into prepared cake pan
7. mix topping and sprinkle over batter
8. bake for 35- 45 minutes
target.review: This is an extraordinarily yummy, easy to make, scrumptious cake.  I made it for a work breakfast tomorrow, and I've already had a "little" bit for myself.  The spices are great, the texture is perfect, and the topping just makes it even better.  Definitely a keeper that I'll make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: This soup tastes incredible, is really simple and quick to make, and it's so filling that one pot fed me at lunch for a solid week.  I added a few more potates than what was called for, and the flavor was out of this world.  Other than that, I did it exactly as the recipe said and I wouldn't change a thing.  Highly recommended.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: These were scrumptious and incredibly easy and quick to put together.  The people I made them for raved and said that it was just as good, if not better, than anything they've had at their favorite Mexican restaurants.  The flavor and spicyness was just right and considering what you're eating they're reasonably healthy too.  Gotta love that.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate lovers deluxe fudgy brownies

rich and chocolaty, these brownies satisfy even the most hardcore chocolate lover. these are always the first thing to sell out at a bake sale! great with a glass of cold milk.  enjoy!

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease an 8 square baking pan with non-stick cooking spray
3. in medium bowl stir together butter , sugar , eggs and vanilla
4. add flour , cocoa and salt stirring just until blended
5. mix in half of the walnuts , if desired
6. spread mixture and sprinkle with remaining walnuts
7. bake about 30 minutes , until top appears dry and center is set
8. cool brownies in pan on wire rack
9. to wrap , cut brownies into squares
10. bake in 350 degrees oven stirring occasionally , about 10 minutes or until lightly browned
11. remove from oven and cool completely
12. my dh has also added chocolate chips to the batter with wonderful results !
demonstrations.review: These were VERY yummy, and yes... EXTREMELY fudgy.  Someone that I had try them even said that they were too chocolaty for him.  I didn't know such a thing was possible!  :)  I'll be making these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese delight

this recipe came from one of my clients, when i dropped over on a chilly winter morning, and i smelled it throughout her lovely home. yum!

1. grease 9x13 pan
2. preheat oven to 350f
3. spread one can of crescent dough on bottom of pan
4. mix softened cream cheese , 1 cup of sugar and vanilla until smooth , and spread on top of crescent dough
5. spread 2nd can of dough on top of cheese mixture
6. be careful not to leave too many gaps in dough
7. pour melted butter all over crescent dough
8. mix 1 / 2 cup sugar with 1 teaspoons of cinnamon
9. sprinkle on top of butter
10. use all of it--it looks like a lot , but it's just right
11. bake for 30 minutes
12. allow to cool before cutting
13. serve with coffee , milk or ice cream !
demonstrations.review: I made these for a brunch gathering a few days ago.  I didn't have any because I don't eat a lot of sweet stuff (stinks because I love to make it), but they were a HUGE hit.  People were smacking the table going "GAH these are fabulous" as their eyes rolled in the back of their heads.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin pie dessert squares

great holiday dessert! took this to a company dinner. gone in a flash!

1. grease bottom only of a 13 x 7 inch pan
2. reserve 1 cup cake mix for topping
3. combine remaining cake mix , butter , & egg
4. press into pan
5. prepare filling by combining all ingredients until smooth
6. pour over crust
7. for topping: combine all ingrediants
8. sprinkle over filling
9. bake at 350 for 45 to 50 minutes
10. until knife inserted near center comes out clean
11. if desired serve with whipped topping !
demonstrations.review: I make this all the time with the Pumpkin Pecan Butter that you can get at Williams Sonoma, and they are HEAVENLY.  They're really nice to have with a little cider or hot chocolate, and the pumpkin taste combined with the cake and cinnamon is deadly.

target.recipe_text:
drew s homemade pimiento cheese   spicy or mild

you'll never buy pimiento cheese again! if you want a milder version, omit the cayenne pepper.  everyone asks for this very easy recipe. try this in a grilled cheese sandwich! yum.

1. chop pimientos into small pieces , or pulse in a food processor
2. in small bowl , stir all ingredients until well mixed
3. or put all ingredients into a food processor , and pulse until well-blended and pimientos are in small pieces
4. serve on crackers , with celery , or make pimiento cheese sandwiches !
5. you may prefer to add up to 1 / 2 cup mayonnaise to get the spreading consistency you like
target.review: I have been looking for a good pimiento cheese recipe forever.  Always just not quite right. Now I have it.  Added 2 jalepenos to it and cut back just a touch on the vinegar (I used apple cider vinegar) because of the peppers being in vinegar. Absolutely perfect.  Thanks BeachGirl. Now Mrs. Price will be loosing a customer for good.  No more over priced stuff for me, and so much better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
twisted sisters creamy cucumber salad

when i arrived in iceland, this was my dh’s 1st food request & i went thru a lot of rz cucumber salad recipes to be sure it wasn’t a duplicate. siggi & my sister named this because it was original w/me & because of my twissis internet identity. for best results, don’t make this a dy ahead, but do allow at least 2 hrs for the flavors to blend & the “cream” to develop from the finished ingredient mix. i promise you’ll like this. (stated time does not include refrigeration time)

1. peel & slice cucumbers in 1 / 2 in thick slices
2. then half ea slice & transfer all slices to a lrg mixing bowl
3. roughly dice red onion & add to the bowl
4. quarter tomatoes , remove seeds , rough dice the tomato meat & add to the bowl
5. thinly slice 1 / 2 green pepper , cut slices in 1 in strips & add to the bowl
6. toss prepared veggies to achieve a good distributional mix
7. add last 6 ingredients to bowl , mix well & refrigerate at least 2 hrs
8. if thinly sliced , most cucumbers wilt & do not retain their crunch
9. -- when all ingredients have been combined , the mixture will appear dry & lack a creamy texture or appearance
10. do not panic that will begin to change almost immediately
11. if you reduce further , you will likely lose any salt component in the mix
demonstrations.review: Yes!!!!!!!!!!!!Yum!!!!!!!This was really, really good. Neighbor agreed, I had to share and show it off. Unlike most I make as the recipe states and do not substitute. How do you know its good if you do not make it as listed? I don't understand. I absolutely loved this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ospidillo cafe italian salad dressing

i always offer two dressings on the table here at the ospidillo cafe; the stone pipe inn salad recipe #136181 and this one. when i place salads on the table, my guests typically query, "where's that good salad dressing that you make?" i just point to the two carafes and about half take one and half take the other; they taste nothing alike.

1. blend all ingredients in a mixer for 20 minutes
2. refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving
3. when dressing gets too cold it will solidify somewhat , due to the olive oil , so allow it to set out 1 / 2 hour or so if this happens
4. also , i prefer to use tupelo honey when i have it available which is much higher quality in flavor than regular clover honey
5. for the italian spices , i use 2 teaspoons of dee514's italian blend spice mix recipe #38293
6. here it is:
7. 2 tablespoons basil , 2 tablespoons marjoram , 1 tablespoon garlic powder , 1 tablespoon oregano , 1 tablespoon thyme , 1 tablespoon rosemary , 1 tablespoon crushed red pepper flakes
demonstrations.review: Really a good dressing. Went perfectly with dinner tonight. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
authentic italian meatballs

meatball recipes are often challenged by chefs who claim, "mine are the best!" even though my meatballs are the best, i will make no such claim. try them for yourself! this meatball recipe was given to me by my father who got it from a little old lady from italy that he knew. it's amazing that she gave up her recipe to him, but i sure am glad she did!

1. mix all ingredients in a large bowl by hand
2. use your bare hands for best results
3. roll meatballs to about the size of a golf ball
4. drop raw meatballs into large pot of sauce
5. simmer for about 3 hours
demonstrations.review: I think everybody has already said it, Outstanding!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blue ribbon stuffed mushrooms

these very easy mushrooms won a blue ribbon at the arizona state fair in the early 90's. these are great appetizers or even for a meal itself.

1. brown pork sausage and crumble well
2. drain sausage from skillet leaving a thin coating of oil behind and saut chopped onions until slightly wilted
3. return sausage to pan with onions and add cream cheese
4. over low heat stir sausage , onions , and cream cheese until well blended
5. remove stems from mushrooms and stuff each mushroom cap with the mixture
6. top with parmesan if desired
7. bake at 350f for 20-25 minutes until heated through and the mushrooms are beginning to leak their water
demonstrations.review: I must have read it wrong? 10 servings? Does that mean I just consumed 2270 calories in 8 minutes? Working on a second batch, just getting warmed up. These are to die for. Had to have a sample. LOL. Made exactly except sprinkled with a little garlic salt and paprika just for appearance. Thanks Scrubber another winner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy potato salad

have you ever posted a recipe and just love reading the reviews for it?  this is my signature potato salad.  whenever there is a pot luck function at work, i am told that i have to bring the potato salad.  no one else is allowed to and i am never given a choice.  thank you everyone who ever tried this potato salad and for leaving such glowing reviews for it.  you all have made me look so good.  i personally can not stand eggs or raw onions, so i leave them out but i know most people don't think a potato salad is complete without them.  thanks again for so many wonderful reviews. (psssst....check out my recipe #123107 as well.  it shares the dressing with this recipe but tastes much much different because of the different ingredients) please see recipe #242966 for bacon bit tips.

1. cook potatoes in boiling , salted water until tender
2. drain well
3. peel and cube potatoes
4. transfer to a large bowl
5. add celery , onion , sweet relish and bacon bits
6. combine mayo , sugar , celery seed , vinegar , mustard , and salt
7. add mayo mixture to potatoes
8. toss lightly to coat potato mixture
9. carefully fold in the chopped eggs
10. cover and chill thoroughly
11. bacon bit
12. use a sharp knife and cut the frozen bacon into long strips about 1 / 4 inch wide
13. turn the bacon and cut the strips into pieces also about 1 / 4 in wide
14. you now have perfect raw bacon pieces to fast fry
15. no need to separate
16. they will separate during cooking
17. perfect bacon bits
demonstrations.review: I have found the perfect potato salad! Outstanding!

target.recipe_text:
lemon butter bars

i found this recipe in a friends cookbook, but i tweaked it to my liking. i love a rich lemon flavor so feel free to cut back if it is too much for you. these are divine and a hit with everyone i shared them with!!

1. heat oven to 350f
2. in a small mixer bowl combine all crust ingredients
3. beat indgredients at low speed scraping the bowl often , until mixture is crumbly
4. press crust to the bottom of an 8" square greesed baking pan
5. bake for 10 to 15 minutes , or until the edges are lightly browned
6. meanwhile , in a small mixer bowl , combine all filling ingredients
7. beat at low speed , scraping the bowl often , until all ingredients are well mixed
8. pour the filling over the hot crust
9. continue baking for 18 to 25 minutes or until the filling is set
10. sprinkle with powdered sugar
11. cool , cut , and enjoy !
target.review: I liked that these were easy to make with ingredients I always have on hand. I think next time I might add a little more sugar to the crust to make them just a bit sweeter. A graham crust might also be good with the lemon filling on top. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and potatoes with pesto

i wanted to use up the rest of a bottle of pesto sauce and this is how i did it.  me and my family think it's pretty good.  easy to make too.

1. mix 3 tbsp pesto with potatoes and onions
2. place into casserole dish
3. top with chicken
4. evenly rub 1 tbsp pesto on top of the chicken breasts
5. season with salt , pepper , garlic and italian seasonings
6. top with cheese
7. bake at 400f for 40 minutes
8. if the cheese begins to brown too fast , loosely cover w / foil then remove foil during the last 5-10 minutes
9. serve with garlic bread and a salad
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This turned out so-so for me. It seemed to lack something - maybe adding some other spices or some sun-dried tomatoes would help. I do think it is a helpful base recipe though, and I will play around with it in the future.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shredded salsa verde beef  crock pot

if we are watching our carbs very carefully we eat this piled with shredded lettuce, shredded cheese and sour cream. if not we wrap it in flour tortillas (low carb or not) with shredded cheese and have burritos. or brush the outside of the burritos with butter after they are rolled and bake in a 425 degree oven for 15 minutes for chimichangas. then top the burritos or chimichanga2 with shredded lettuce, salsa, sour cream and shredded cheese. delicious!

1. place roast in crock pot
2. sprinkle with salt , pepper and garlic salt
3. pour salsa verde over roast
4. cover , and cook on low for 8 hours
5. when done , the roast should shred easily with a fork
demonstrations.review: I have made this many times and it is SO good. I'm not even a big fan of beef but I can' get enough of this stuff.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef stroganoff  italian meatball
