this is one of the first vegan recipes i ever tried. while it does not imitate grilled cheese, it has become one of our favorites. gooey and glorious! (from vegan vittles)

1. the cheeze keeps well in the fridge , so if pressed for time you can double or triple it , and microwave for a few seconds to soften before spreading
2. if you don't have a nonstick pan you can lightly butter the bread
3. combine all remaining ingredients , water to salt , in a small pot over medium-high heat
4. whisk together as it comes to a boil and immediately turn down to low , stirring continuously for a minute or two , till the cheeze is thickened and creamy
5. remove from heat
6. heat a non-stick skillet , or regular if using margarine , on medium
7. spread it on the bread to make sandwiches
8. this makes quite a bit of cheeze for two sandwiches , so you might want to spread it over three
9. grill on preheated skillet till golden , then flip and do other side
10. serve immediately
11. great with a salad or veggie sticks and dip
demonstrations.review: Great sub for a grilled cheese graving! Of course I only had hamburger buns on hand, and no regular bread so I didnt get the full effect, but I can't wait to have it with tomato soup!

target.recipe_text:
sweet italian chili

nan

1. brown ground beef in a dutch oven
2. drain and return to pan
3. add bell pepper , parsley , onion and celery
4. saute until onion is clear , approximately 5 minutes
5. add remaining ingredients and simmer 1-1 / 2 to 2 hours
target.review: I'm making this for the fourth time today in two months. I tripled the recipe for a small party and there were no leftovers - everyone loves it. This is now a staple in our house. It's hearty and robust for Dad, and not spicy and sweet for Mom. I don't add water since we like our chili thick. I always cook my meat seperately from my onions so I don't have to worry about under/over cooking them. Everything goes in the crockpot once the chili is assembled for at least three hours.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bev s spaghetti sauce

this is a recipe i have developed over a number of years. this is the only spaghetti sauce my family will request! very easy to make. i hope your family enjoys it as much as mine does!

1. brown the ground beef , onion and garlic in olive oil with bay leaves , oregano , basil , italian seasoning , salt and pepper
2. add tomato paste , tomato sauce and diced tomatoes
3. stir well and bring to a simmer over medium heat
4. cover and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
5. use sauce to top your cooked spaghetti
6. top with sauteed mushroom
7. pass the parmesan
demonstrations.review: The best sauce I've ever made. And I've made a bunch of different ones. I love thick, robust, and meaty sauces. I added a little less than 1/4 cup of sweet red wine and let it cook in crock pot for 4 hours. Didn't add any Parmesan cheese since I don't like it. Will keep in the cookbook and made again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate glaze  that hardens when cool

iso: chocolate glaze that dries hard using cocoa and without... saw this and found the answer.  this would be good now with valentine's day is near.  try using it like those chocolate dips they have in ice cream shops; it hardens into a shell on the ice cream.  or use it to top your favorite cookie, cupcake, cheesecake, brownie, etc..

1. combine melted margarine or oil , cocoa , and hot water
2. blend in confectioners' sugar and vanilla
3. pour or spread on brownies or cake
4. glaze will harden when cool
demonstrations.review: I doubled the recipe and put it on a bundt cake without tasting it first. Big mistake. Way too vanilla-ey. I don't know if it's because I used clear vanilla extract or doubled the recipe. I might try it again with regular vanilla extract and less of it. It came out with a soft icing consistancy also. I wanted more of a thinner glaze to pour over.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
almost like papa john s pizza dough

i found this via the net and am posting it in response to a request for it.

1. in a large bowl , combine 1 cup flour , sugar , undissolved yeast , and salt
2. blend well
3. gradually add water and oil to mixture
4. blend at low speed until moistened , then beat for 2 minutes at medium speed
5. by hand , add 1 1 / 2 to 2 cupa flour until dough pulls away from sides of bowl
6. on floured surface , knead in 1 / 4 to 1 / 2 cup flour until dough is smooth and elastic
7. cover loosely with plastic and let rest in a warm place for about 15 minutes
8. press out dough onto 12-inch pizza pans
9. prick randomly with a fork
10. let rest again in a warm place for 10-15 minutes
11. brush crusts lightly with oil then prebake them in a 450 degree oven for 5 minutes
12. top as desired , then bake again in 450 degree oven for 4-5 minutes , or until desired doneness
demonstrations.review: I made this with Papa John's Pizza Sauce (#108447) and was shocked how fast my pizza's got eaten. Normally we only need 2 pizzas and still have leftovers. I doubled the recipe and made 3 large pizza's, they were gone! My mom said it was the first time in a long time pizza didn't give her heart burn. I will definitly make again! I did under cook one since it was on the bottom rack, but it crisped up nice under broil.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crockpot chicken quesadillas

nothing is better than coming home and having your dinner practically waiting for you! this chicken could also be used on nachos, in tacos, or in some sort of mexican casserole. it is moist and delicious and literally falls apart in the crock pot. i found this recipe posted by a molly day on another cooking site. enjoy!

1. combine chicken , salsa , corn , and taco seasoning in a crock pot
2. cook on low for 6-8 hours
3. before serving , shred chicken with a fork
4. spray a skillet with cooking spray and add a tortilla
5. on half , add chicken mixture
6. top with cheese
7. fold tortilla over and let brown
8. after 1 minute , flip to other side
demonstrations.review: Pretty good. I used bone-in legs on high so it would get done faster. I should have made some quesadilla sauce, since I thought this was a little bland.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
papa john s pizza sauce

found on the net and thought i would share with everyone here!!

1. combine ingredients in a small saucepan over medium heat
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this with Almost Like Papa John's Pizza Dough (#177072) and was shocked how fast my pizza's got eaten. Normally we only need 2 pizzas and still have leftovers. I doubled the recipe and made 3 large pizza's, they were gone! My mom said it was the first time in a long time pizza didn't give her heart burn. I will definitly make again!

target.recipe_text:
cauliflower ham bake

this is from the company's coming christmas cookbook, it would be good with broccoli too. i have made it for a couple christmas dinners with raves. plus that way you get your ham with your turkey. if you don't have fresh ham get a slab of black forest ham from the deli 1 inch thick. if having for a big meal you can easily serve 10 as a small side. it can be made a day ahead and baked the next day. can also be a meal.

1. cook cauliflower in boiling water until tender crisp and drain
2. add ham and mushrooms and mix well
3. melt butter in saucepan , mix in flour and salt and gradually whisk in milk until it boils and thickens
4. add cheese
5. stir until melted , add sour cream and stir until smooth
6. put cauliflower mixture in 3-quart casserole , pour sauce over top and sprinkle with crumbs bake uncovered at 350f for 30-40 minutes
target.review: Yummy, did not have any sour cream so left it out and still tasted good. Will add this to my Leftovers collection.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted butternut squash  red grapes and sage

if you want something different to do with the season's harvest of winter squash, try this delicious roasted side dish.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. in a large bowl , combine the squash , grapes , onions and sage
3. drizzle in the oil and melted butter
4. season generously with salt and pepper and toss to coat everything well
5. spread the mixture on a large rimmed baking sheet and roast until squash and onion begin to brown -- about 50 minutes
6. sprinkle with pine nuts and serve
demonstrations.review: This is sooo good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic broccoli with cranberries

this takes only minutes to make and is a healthy, but yummy alternative to a side dish.  your kids will eat this any day over plain broccoli!  this recipe uses dried cranberries and is just super!  sometimes i add cooked pasta for a filler, and i'll add 2 cups cooked, chopped chicken for a complete meal!

1. heat oil in large skillet over medium heat
2. add garlic and saut 1 minute
3. add broccoli and cranberries , saut 5 minutes or until broccoli is crisp and tender
4. season to taste with salt and pepper
5. serve warm or cold
6. add chicken and or pasta to make a meal
demonstrations.review: Nice variation yet easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lasagna cupcakes

i love these. you can make them fancy for your next dinner party or simple for the kids. they are so fun to do and great to make a day or so ahead.    you can use any fillings you like. i prefer hamburger meat but you could use anything from spinach to sausage.  i haven't had luck in finding round wonton wrappers to i cut the square ones and then line my cupcake pan. when you are done layering you can pipe ricotta on top to make it look like a real cupcake....i don't do that and found it is just as good.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. to start the lasagnas: cook hamburger meat , season to taste , drain
3. reserve 8 tablespoons of parmesan and 8 tablespoons of mozzarellathis will be the topping
4. the remaining cheese will be used in the lasagnas
5. start assembling the lasagnas
6. line each cupcake mold with a round wonton wrapper
7. put a little parmesan , a little mozzarella , and a little ricotta into each mold
8. top with a little meat and a spoonful of sauce
9. repeat layers of wonton wrappers , cheeses , meat and sauce , creating 6 layers in all , and ending with sauce
10. sprinkle each lasagna with reserved parmesan and mozzarella
11. bake until the lasagnas are nicely browned , about 20 minutes
12. serve warm garnished with cherry tomatoes and basil leaves
demonstrations.review: Cute yummers!  Mini lasagnas.  Made these tonight. Cheated and used meat sauce instead of browning meat.   Wonder if you could freeze them -raw- and then bake later?    Thank you KT.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered summer salad

a little fresh basil in the dressing brings this make-ahead salad up-to-date. substitute torn romaine lettuce for the spinach, if you like. for a dramatic presentation, serve this salad in a clear glass bowl. the salad must refrigerate for 5 hours, which is included in preparation time. this recipe is by kraft.

1. layer spinach , 1 cup of the cheese , the mushrooms , onions , tomatoes and peas in 3-qt
2. serving bowl
3. mix mayo , sour cream and basil
4. spread over salad , completely covering top of salad
5. cover
6. refrigerate at least 5 hours
7. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese and the bacon just before serving
demonstrations.review: Perfect!  Loved that I could assemble ahead and is so pretty in glass bowl.  We liked the 1 tablespoon basil amount.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
overnight blueberry coffee cake

a make ahead recipe my mother gave me from an old taste of home magazine-1995.  notice that you refrigerate the batter, then let it get to room temperature in 30 minutes before baking.  if you have celiac disease, zori's review might be helpful to you-- she wrote" dr schar's gluten-free cake flour + 2tbsp potato starch (it makes gf flour stronger) and corn oil in stead of butter."

1. in a bowl , beat egg , and 1 / 2 cup sugar
2. combine flour , baking powder , and salt in medium sized bowl
3. alternate adding egg mixture and then the milk to flour mixture
4. beating well after each addition
5. stir in melted butter
6. fold in blueberries
7. pour into a greased 8 inch square pan , sprinkle with 2 tablespoons of remaining sugar
8. cover and refrigerate overnight
9. next morning , remove from refrigerator and put on counter for 30 minutes
10. preheat oven to 350 degrees
11. bake for 30-35 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Family loved this!  Added a bit more butter as previous reviewer suggested.

target.recipe_text:
beef meatballs

these are a great addition to spaghetti! the have the best mix of spices and meat that i've found yet!

1. combine all ingredients in a bowl
2. shape mixture into balls about 1 1 / 2"
3. place on broiler pan that is coated with cooking spray
4. bake at 400 degrees for 15 minutes or until done
target.review: Very good and easy meatballs.  I especially liked it that they are baked in the oven.  I used fresh herbs from the garden instead of Italian seasoning and doubled the garlic...a big hit!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herb roasted pork tenderloin

got this recipe from southern living magazine. oh so good and easy.

1. stir together first 11 ingredients in a shallow dish or heavy-duty zip-top plastic bag
2. prick pork with a fork , and place in marinade , turning to coat
3. cover dish , or seal bag
4. chill 2 hours
5. remove from marinade , discarding marinade
6. place pork on a rack in a roasting pan
7. bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes or until a meat thermometer inserted into thickest portion of pork registers 160 degrees
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious and very easy with readily available ingredients...good enough for me to figure out how to write a rated comment in Recipezaar.  Good enough for company and easy enough to prepare with short notice that company will be coming for dinner.  Good enough for my 'permanent recipe file' and sure to become a favorite in our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peachy mango salsa  canned for chris

chris aka chef #1118755 made and reviewed my recipe #68547 and asked about canning it. this is the result of that recipe. i did add garlic and or ginger to it. yes an optional choice. used fresh jalapenos in place of the canned green chilies. be sure not to use over ripe mango's, they need to be firm but fresh. if they are so soft you can't peel with a vegetable peeler they are too soft.

1. sterilize ball jars rims and screw tops
2. place all the ingredients in a large pot
3. bring to a boil over high heat , stirring to dissolve sugar
4. reduce to simmering , and simmer 5 minutes
5. do not overcook
6. fill into hot sterile jars with hot salsa leaving 1 / 2 inch head space
7. being careful not to leave any salsa on the rims
8. wipe jar rims with a clean , damp paper towel
9. put on lids and screw on metal bands tightening firmly and evenly
10. do not over tighten
11. put the sealed jars in the canner and keep them cover with at least 1 inch of water and boiling
12. boil them for at least 20 minutes
13. lift the jars out of the water and let them cool them in a draft-free place overnight
14. you can then remove the rings if you like
15. once the jars are cool , you can check that they are sealed verifying that the lid has been sucked down
16. just press in the center , gently , with your finger
17. label and store in a cool place out of direct light using within 1 year
demonstrations.review: I have used this recipe three times with wonderful results.  I have made it once with just Mango and twice with both Mango and Peaches...both delicious and a staple for our winter pleasure.  It is a versatile recipe...add more lime juice, cilantro or garlic...add ginger in addition to the garlic...use white wine vinegar...use red peppers, green peppers and more jalepenos if you like it spicier.  I will make this every year as soon as the peaches smell like peaches in the store and the mangoes are firm yet with just the right amount of give.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mandarin orange chicken

not very authentic or traditional...just delicious.

1. place flour in a small bowl
2. dredge chicken in the flour to lightly coat
3. heat olive oil and butter in a medium skillet over medium heat , and saute the chicken breasts until no longer pink and juices run clear
4. set aside , and keep warm
5. stir hoisin sauce , red pepper flakes and orange juice into the skillet , and scrape up the browned bits
6. let cook for a few minutes until sauce thickens slightly
7. return chicken , mandarin oranges , green onions , and cashews , to the skillet
8. continue cooking just until all ingredients are heated through
9. serve over hot rice
demonstrations.review: Very enjoyable and easy to prepare. I used fresh mandarin oranges rather than canned which were good and very pretty in the dish.  I used one whole bunch of green onions, doubled the cashews and used the two to top the dish before serving.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot leg of lamb

i love the flavour combination of lemon, garlic and herbs with lamb and this recipe fulfills my taste buds' expectations! this is not meant to be a roast, but is meant to be fall apart soft - almost like a mediterranean flavoured "pulled lamb".

1. using the crock pot's ceramic dish , mix together oil , lemon juice , garlic , oregano and nutmeg
2. immerse leg of lamb into the mixture and cook on high for 6- 8 hours until falling apart
3. just before removing meat from crock pot , mix together mint , sugar and vinegar in dish and microwave for 30 seconds until vinegar is hot enough to melt sugar
4. remove meat to serving platter and pull apart with forks until you have chunky shreds of meat
5. drizzle over mint vinegar and serve piping hot
demonstrations.review: Very good and easy.   I trimmed the fat from a boneless leg of lamb before cooking, thickened the gravy with flour and served over rice.  I served the mint sauce on the side which was very nice drizzled over the lamb and gravy.  We will certainly be having this again as it was very enjoyable.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot lamb shanks

modified version of a recipe i found on the 'net that i thought turned out great. apart from a few small changes to seasoning the original recipe called for a cup of wine rather than beer, sometimes i feel with tomato that makes things a bit rich when slow-cooked and i thought the beer substitution worked well. if you don't want to use beer try a cup of beef stock instead of the stock powder / beer. also whole garlic cooked this way doesn't taste strong at all, if you want it to have a strong garlic taste you'd need to crush some of it.

1. heat oil in pan over medium to high heat and brown lamb shanks on all sides
2. season lamb shanks with pepper
3. place sliced onions at bottom of crock pot and put lamb shanks on top drizzled with remaining oil and juices from the pan
4. place mushrooms and garlic cloves over the top
5. mix beer , worcestershire sauce , stock powder , tomatoes , oregano , basil , thyme and bay leaf in a bowl
6. pour mixture over the top of lamb shanks
7. cook in crock pot on low for 6-8 hours depending on your crock pot
8. remove bay leaves
9. serve with vegetables and juices poured over the top of the shanks
10. i served over wholegrain bread but mashed potatoes would be the best match
demonstrations.review: Very hearty, but the lamb flavor was overpowered by the many strongly flavored ingredients.

target.recipe_text:
greek potatoes  oven roasted and delicious

these potatoes are a staple in our home. whether accompanying roast lamb or chicken, or just on their own, we have them a couple of times a week. they are delicious and the ones that get overly-brown in the pan and stick a bit are mine!  clean up is a little tricky with this recipe, unless you line your pans with foil, but i find that just filling the pan up with hot, sudsy water and forgetting for an hour (something i apparently have no problem doing ;-)) helps a lot.

1. preheat oven to 420f a reviewer has suggested spraying the baking pan with pam - that sounds like a great idea !
2. put all the ingredients into a baking pan large enough to hold them
3. season generously with sea salt and black pepper
4. make sure your hands are very clean and put them in the pan and give everything a toss to distribute
5. the garlic will drop into the water / oil solution but its flavour will permeate the potatoes , and this way , it won't burn
6. bake for 40 minutes
7. when a nice golden-brown crust has formed on the potatoes , give them a stir to bring the white underside up , season lightly with a bit more sea salt and pepper and just a light sprinkling of oregano
8. add 1 / 2 cup more water if pan appears to be getting dry , and pop back into oven to brown other side of potatoes
9. this will take about another 40 minutes
10. do not be afraid of overcooking the potatoes- they will be delicious
target.review: these were absolutely the best potatoes i've had in a long time... i too did them on the bbq along with ribs... such goodness should be sinful.... thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek pasta salad

this salad is easy to make and tastes fantastic. great for family barbecues!

1. boil pasta according to directions , drain
2. in a small bowl prepare dressing and set aside
3. in a large bowl mix pasta with prepared vegetables , toss and then add crumbled feta cheese
4. add the dressing and stir
5. best if allowed to refidgerate for an hour before serving
demonstrations.review: This was absolutly delightful.  It's the first time ever making a pasta salad.  The dressing is something really special.  I only wish I had more friends around to taste it and I can't wait for a party to make it again.  Definately a keeper.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: You are right to call this THE BEST EVER BANANA CAKE - it is soooooo good. I made it at my daughters house and compliments just kept coming.  Thanks for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oh so good cabbage rolls

i have adjusted and tweaked this recipe to make it truly my own. during the last part of cooking the sauce becomes thick and delicious. for the adventurous, add a dash of louisiana hot sauce when serving.

1. blanch cabbage for approximately 10 minutes
2. when cool enough to handle , separate into leaves
3. combine meat , salt , pepper , rice , shredded cabbage , shredded potato , eggs , onions , bell pepper , garlic and parsley and small can of tomato sauce
4. mix well
5. place equal portions of meat mixture in center of each cabbage leaf , fold ends over , roll up and fasten with toothpicks
6. add one tablespoon oil each to two large skillets and place cabbage rolls sided by side in skillets
7. to the two small cans of tomato sauce add the brown sugar and lemon juice and pour over cabbage rolls
8. cover skillets and simmer for 30 minutes , basting occasionally
9. uncover and continue cooking 30 minutes more , basting occasionally
10. sauce will thicken and become a wonderful sauce that adheres to cabbage rolls
11. dash of louisiana hot sauce can be added to top of cabbage rolls for those that enjoy it
demonstrations.review: i really enjoyed this recipe... the taste is fantastic... i think the lemon added gave the right kick... thanks for posting...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: omg, omg, oh my god.... these are the best ever. just made them today with 1 1/2 cup of milk chocolate chips. they are the best brownies i have ever, ever had. thank you so much for posting. loved them and not too sure i'll share them....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s cream of potato soup or broccoli soup

this recipe has a slight smoky flavor due to the deli bacon. broccoli can be substituted for potatoes for cream of broccoli soup.

**this recipe can also be used for clam chowder.  eliminate the broccoli and use chopped clams.

1. empty cans of chicken broth in pot
2. add cubed potatoes and bring to a boil
3. while potatoes are starting to cook pan fry bacon until crisp and add bacon grease to chicken and potato broth
4. crumble bacon and add to broth
5. add diced ham to broth
6. in a sauce pan melt butter and add diced onion , celery and carrots
7. pan fry until soft
8. when potatoes are done add the celery , carrot and onion mixture with butter to broth
9. reduce heat to medium and add about 1 / 4 to 1 / 2 of the quart of heavy cream
10. be careful not to have soup at a heavy boil or cream will curdle
11. add enough cream to make soup look creamy throughout
12. add cheese
13. mix corn starch with very cold water and add to soup
14. continue medium boil until soup thickens
15. if it isn't thick enough repeat corn starch and add slowly
16. remove from heat and enjoy
17. soup will thicken when it gets cold
18. can add milk or water to thin out
demonstrations.review: I loved this soup. I made it exactly as the recipe was written except I added 1/2 Velveeta Cheese to it. My husband hates broccoli but really enjoyed this version. Thanks so much for posting it.

target.recipe_text:
lick the bowl clean bacon broccoli salad

first time i had this at a church potluck, another lady and i were nearly fighting over the last serving--it was so good!  so we took the empty bowl and went looking for the owner to beg for the recipe.   here it is!

1. fry the bacon
2. break into pieces
3. set aside
4. trim broccoli stems , cut into 1 / 2 - 1-inch pieces
5. cut flower ends into small pieces , too
6. put into a large serving bowl
7. slice green onions into the broccoli
8. add raisins and nuts to the broccoli and onions
9. tossing well
10. add bacon now or wait until serving time if you don't like it to get soggy-ish
11. dressing: mix dressing ingredients in a small bowl until sugar dissolves
12. add dressing to the broccoli mixture
13. stir well to coat everything
14. if you didn't add the bacon earlier , add it now
15. best served at room temperature
16. options: leave out the raisins or nuts or bacon--just don't leave them all out at the same time
17. instead of 3 bunches of broccoli , add some cauliflower--very pretty , too !
target.review: Made this already few times; did not have bacon so I replaced bacon with leftover Italian sausage thinly sliced. Also I replaced nuts (can not bring them to nut-free school with chick peas)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled or baked salmon with lavender

i noticed very few recipes here on zaar which use edible lavender so i decided to find some really good ones and post them! i didn't even know you could eat lavender until i read rita l's page long ago. now i notice that one of my fave restaurants uses it! brazosbelle.com this recipe is from greenemporium.com

1. place all ingredients except salmon , in saucepan over moderate heat , stirring with a wire whisk at all times until ingredients are reduced by one-third , to create a sauce
2. when sauce has cooled slightly , brush on salmon filet
3. grill salmon , basting with sauce occasionally , setting some aside to top when served
4. salmon is cooked when fish flakes
5. to bake salmon , preheat oven to 350
6. cover salmon with sauce , setting some aside to pour on salmon before serving
7. bake for 10 minutes or until salmon is flaky , basting occasionally
8. wonderful with rice or potatoes
demonstrations.review: We liked it. I had people for supper and they went for seconds and triples. I would suggest to pick up some lavender of the fish, as I personally found that it had little bit of bitter after taste, but only if you eat the lavender itself. I liked the aroma lavender gave to the meal. I used wild arctic chard instead of salmon. Will defendly make it again, thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh peach brown sugar pie

i adopted this recipe from the recipezaar account. i can't wait to try this one! i love peach pie. yum!

1. preheat oven to 425
2. stir dry ingredients together
3. sprinkle peaches with lemon juice and almond extract
4. add dry ingredients and toss gently to mix
5. dump into pastry lined 9" pie pan , dot with butter and add top crust
6. cut vent holes
7. bake until bubbles and crust is browned
8. about 35-45 minutes
demonstrations.review: The pie was exceptional. I used caned peaches and it still turned out great. The almond extract is a must -  adds such satisfaction note to the peaches. I added egg wash and sprinkled cane brown sugar on top. Was very pleased with the results. Would be making it again very soon. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simply awesome baked pork chops

tender and delicious!!

1. brown chops in butter
2. place in baking dish
3. sprinkle with soup mix
4. pour cream over all
5. bake , tightly covered , at 375 for 45 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: I followed the recepie exactly. It turned out great. Very easy and fast.  My husband loved it. I will be making it again for sure. Thank you for wonderfull pork chops.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kohlsuppe   cabbage soup

this afternoon i put some broth and cabbage into the crockpot, and when my husband came home he said, 

1. put the chopped cabbage and the broth in the crockpot , on high
2. simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
3. in a saut pan , cook the bacon slices until crisp
4. remove , chop roughly , and set aside
5. saut the onion in the bacon drippings until soft
6. add the chopped bacon , onion , potato , and salt and pepper to the crockpot
7. cook on high for an additional 1 to 1 1 / 2 hours hours , until the cabbage reaches the texture you prefer
8. serve with a dollop of sour cream
demonstrations.review:
I made this soup tonight. Was sceptic but decided to give it a try because I had all the ingreidients on hand (had a cabbage for over a month in the fridge and could not decide what to do with it). I followed general direction with some alternation. I used already cooked and crumbled bacon. I added 2 more cups of chicken broth. I used pressure cooker instead of slow cooker: saute onions and bacon bits in pressure cooker, added cubed potatoes, broth and chopped small cabbage, bring to  boil, close cover, wait until pressure monitor is activated, lower heat to medium, cook under pressure for 10 minutes, take off the heat, let the pressure to fall by itself. Soup was ready under 20 minutes and it tasted fantastic. Who knew cabage can be this tasty?!
Thanks for posting your discovery.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest beef enchiladas ever

best enchilada recipe i've found. we love the spicy, cheesy flavor of these.

1. brown meat and onions in large skillet
2. add 1 cup enchilada sauce and 1 cup cheese
3. mix well
4. put filling along center of each tortilla
5. roll up and place seam side down in a 9x13 pan
6. pour remaining sauce over
7. sprinkle remaining cheese over
8. bake at 350f degrees for about 30 minutes till cheese is bubbly
demonstrations.review: It was good week day supper. I added more whole seed cumin and sliced black olives on top of the cheese. Also next time I would put some sauce on the bottom of dish before putting tortillas down, because mine were sticking to the bottom. Thanks for the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
angel hair pasta with tomato lemon and garlic

this is a nice, light summer dish.  it's easy to prepare too.

1. put the olive oil and garlic in a saute pan and cook over medium heat till the garlic begins to brown
2. add the broth and cook till it's reduced in half
3. stir in lemon juice , tomato and basil
4. cook angel hair pasta till done
5. drain , and add to the tomato mixture
6. top with cheese and pepper
target.review:
I thought this was great dish.  I changed some things only because of personal preference but the base is delicious as written.
I added more extra-virgin olive oil, more garlic, I used 1/2 cup of fresh Basil and fresh grated Parmesian and Romano cheese.  I cooked my Angel Hair just until lightly tender to the tooth.
I'm going to try it a couple more time this summer, once using sun-dried tomatoes finely chopped, and another time I'm going to try just basil, fresh lemon zest & juice, and olive oil with the cheeses.
Thanks for a great base meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato and basil bruschetta

my first culinary 

1. whisk together chopped garlic , vinegar , salt , pepper , and basil
2. when combined slowly drizzle in oil
3. add tomatoes and let sit for 20 minutes at room temp
4. meanwhile back at the bat cave , toast the bread
5. this can be done either in the toaster or under the broiler
6. when the bread is toasted rub each piece , on one side , with the whole garlic pieces
7. place the bread on a cookie sheet and top with tomato mixture
8. sprinkle on a little cheese and broil till the cheese melts
9. serve immediately
10. the tomato mixture also makes a wonderful vinegrette for an an
11. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I just want to say "upfront" that this is a delicious recipe for Brushcetta.  And contrary to anothers somewhat unfair comment I think one should know that TRADITIONAL Bruschetta flavoring in other countries is VERY BLAND, since Bruschetta itself basically means "grilled bread".  This recipe for the Bruschetta 'topping' one has some flair and some flavor and I think you've done a great job.  People need to be more considerate of the history of a food culture when commenting, or kinder at least. Personal tastes are MEANT to vary.  If one prefers more flavor, I think the key would be to simmply 'double' this recipe for this thick a bread, or slice your bread thinner.  I liked it, though yes, I doubled it, and I've had Bruschetta all over our nation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy no bake cookies

i played around with my family's no bake cookie recipe and produced a single portion of this cookie that i feel is healthy enough to eat as a meal.  they’re still very good but are much healthier. i keep getting asked for the recipe, so i finally decided to measure out the exact portions and post the recipe. this recipe is very flexible! when i make them i never measure out anything and i often add more or less of ingredients and they still taste great.  i sometimes leave out the wheat germ and flax seeds and just add more oatmeal.  i have made these replacing the sugar with about 3 tablespoons of honey.  i have changed the recipe from 1 tsp. to 1 tbsp. of cocoa powder.

1. heat milk , sugar and cocoa powder over high heat until boiling , stirring constantly
2. take off heat and stir in vanilla and peanut butter
3. stir until peanut butter has melted completely
4. stir in wheat germ and oatmeal
5. drop by large spoonfuls onto wax paper or eat immediately
6. as i
7. if you don't have wheat germ or flax seed , just use more oatmeal
8. the recipe above should work out just perfectly and does most of the time , but if your cookies come out crumbly , use less oatmeal next time
9. if they never set , use more oatmeal next time
demonstrations.review: ShaGun, these are delightful cookies!!!  I did fuss with it ever so slightly but not enough to offer help, I simply personalized it a bit for us.  You've done a great job in giving a twist healthy option!!!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken kelaguen   in depth

this is a spicy (hot) chicken dish from guam.  this version is more work than my other one, but is richer in flavor, in my opinion.

be careful with the hot peppers!  wear gloves if possible, and wash your hands thoroughly after, not touching your face.

1. mix soy sauce with lemon juice
2. add finely chopped onion and peppers
3. let sit a few days in the refrigerator to let the flavors blend
4. marinate the chicken in the finadene sauce overnight
5. grill / broil the chicken , basting with the sauce
6. after it is done , cool the chicken , debone and shred it
7. open the coconut and discard the liquid inside
8. grate the coconut meat
9. after the coconut is grated , pick it up in your hands and squeeze it over a bowl to collect the milk
10. mix the milk with an equal amount of lemon juice and chill
11. mix the green onions , peppers , and coconut meat to the chicken
12. slowly mix the coconut milk and lemon juice into the chicken , stirring well
13. serve warm on or in pita bread
demonstrations.review: THIS is true Chicken Kelaguen.  Boonie peppers would have been the kicker over the top.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
guam fried rice

being a military family we get the pleasure of meeting people from all over the world. my girlfriend who lives in guam gave me this recipe. so that i don't misplace it i'm putting it into my cookbook for later use.

1. fry bacon until crisp
2. remove bacon and pour off half the bacon fat , reserve a little to add to pan after cooking your egg
3. sometimes the egg will absorb every bit of bacon fat and sometimes it leaves behind enough to coat the rice
4. fry garlic in bacon fat until golden , remove and discard
5. fry onion in the same bacon fat
6. remove onion from pan and add to bacon
7. spread eggs on bottom of pan as if preparing an omelet
8. fold over
9. remove to cutting board or plate
10. cut into strips
11. add reserved bacon fat and cold rice to pan , stir until all grains are coated with grease and grains are no longer sticking together
12. add bacon , onion and ham
13. mix well
14. always scraping bottom of pan to prevent sticking
15. turn heat to low and add sliced egg pieces
16. add cooked shrimp
17. heat 1-2 minutes , just until shrimp is warmed
18. remove from heat and serve
demonstrations.review: We lived in Guam for four years while in the USAF and this is not truly Guam Fried Rice.  Theirs is a very basic recipe that sometimes will include ham and shrimp but seldom does it include bacon.  I made this recipe and found it to be tasty but to complex for anything but trying to use it as  a main meal basically.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot  slow cooker  french dip roast beef sandwiches

i have another tried and true french dip recipe and also use another great one here on 'zaar, but when i went to make it the other day, i was lacking all of the ingredients to make either...so the following was born.  turns out everyone liked it better than either of my previous ones, so i figured i better post it for posterity!

1. place roast in 4
2. 5 - 6 quart slow cooker
3. sprinkle with onion soup mix and then pour onion soup and beer over it
4. drop bouillon cubes in different spots into the liquid and sprinkle pepper and salt to taste over all
5. cook on high for 4-5 hours
6. remove meat and slice or shred
7. return to slow cooker and cover
8. turn to low and let meat soak up the juices until ready to serve
9. our favorite way to serve: open rolls and place a slice of provolone on one side of each
10. place under broiler until cheese is almost melted
11. spoon beef on top with slotted spoon and serve sandwich with a side cup of au jus
demonstrations.review: I'm sorry, the concept of this recipe is wonderful, BUT...the sodium content in this recipe is above and beyond the necessary.  The simplicity of using packets of seasoning is great, but not at the cost of my families health.  I found that creating my own seasoning combo's and using those made this recipe equally delicious and succulent WITHOUT the ridiculous amount of salt.

target.recipe_text:
mrs  knobbes gooey butter cake

this is an ooey gooey delight straight from st.louis missouri.

1. mix the cake mix with 1 egg and the butter and pat into a greased cake pan
2. mix and pour the remaining ingredients over the cake
3. bake at 350f for 35 minutes
4. dust the top with powdered sugar
target.review: Out of this world delicious. A good cross between a butter cake and cheese cake. Has a decadently rich and creamy top layer. I made this for my family but am going to make it again and take it to my next ladies bible study meeting. Might have to pass around the insulin syringes cause this stuff is rich and sweet--Yum!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
los rios stew

they serve this at a little cantina near where i live. doesn't look so good, but the taste is fabulous.

1. in a dutch oven , heat oil
2. saute beef until browned on all sides
3. add remaining ingredients except for cheese
4. bring to a boil
5. lower heat and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours or until meat it tender
6. ladle stew into individual serving bowls
7. top with cheese
8. i usually serve this with corn bread
demonstrations.review: Excellent stew, Nurse Di. I have just about burned my family out on my standard beef-vegetable stew. This was something different that we all loved. I also used the extra-spicy rotel tomatoes and all the cumin. Wonderful Tex-Mex flavor and chunky texture. Didn't have time to make cornbread but will have to try that next time. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cool blue martini

we had out-of-town guests that shared this recipe with us. we have some funky martini glasses and this drink looked so cool in them. tasted great and we sure had a fun and crazy time.

1. in a shaker filled with ice , add first four ingredients
2. shake well , then strain into 2 martini glasses
3. garnish with lemon twists
demonstrations.review: I love this drink. It has a true  martini flavor with a calming cool blue color. My husband and I kicked back and enjoyed a beautiful sunset while sipping on these martinis. Thanks for a memorable evening.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creepy body bits dip

i adapted this from bhg's halloween magazine. i tried it out on my family and am going to serve this at our halloween bash.

1. in a skillet , cook sausage and onion over medium heat until sausage in no longer pink
2. drain
3. transfer sausage mixture to a 4-quart slow cooker
4. stir in weiners , tomatoes , and cheese
5. cover and cook on high for 1 to 2 hours until cheese melts , stirring after 1 hour
6. to serve , keep warm on low setting , stirring occasionally
7. serve with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: Ooh yes. I made this "creepy" dip on Halloween night. Our kids and their friends were in and out all night so we just served this to keep the festive mood going. Delicious tasting but kind of slimy looking which is the whole idea. Thanks for a fun and interesting dip recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven denver omelet

you can make this the night before and it will be ready to put in the oven in the morning. it's a nice light, fluffy omelet.

1. beat eggs and half and half until light and fluffy
2. stir in the cheese , ham , green pepper , onion and parsley
3. pour into a greased 9in square baking dish
4. bake at 400 for 25 minutes or until set
demonstrations.review: Wonderfully easy and a delicious brunch dish. The onions, pepper, and ham are a great combination and we enjoyed the taste immensely. I added some salt and pepper but that was all. Thanks for an easy and classy dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetarian taco soup

this is a quick and healthy meatless soup. i usually serve it with cornbread.

1. drain and rinse first six ingredients in a large colander
2. put in a crockpot or large pot
3. add all other ingredients , stirring to mix well
4. simmer about 30 minutes to an hour or cook in your crockpot on high for 2 hours
demonstrations.review: This soup is fabulous and so easy to make. All those different beans gave an interesting flavor and appearance. The seasoning with the taco mix and ranch mix was quite good. We ate on this a couple of days and then I froze the rest for later. Thanks Junebug. My family and I love this soup.

target.recipe_text:
tex mex breakfast hash and eggs

here's a nice change of pace for breakfast, you control the heat!

1. in a large skilled cook the chorizo over medium heat until browned and done
2. drain reserving 3 t
3. drippings , setting sausage aside
4. return drippings to the pan and over medium heat saute the onions and garlic for 4-5 minutes
5. add the chiles and stir well
6. add the potatoes , reduce heat to medium low and cook for 20 minutes , stirring often
7. add the tomatoes to heat through
8. spoon onto plates , top with eggs and offer salsa at the table
9. garnish with chopped cilantro and cheese if you wish
target.review: This recipe was awesome.  I didn't have a can of green chilies or a fresh tomato so I just used a can of Rotel diced tomatoes with green chilies instead.  I served this with over-easy eggs.. delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super moist chocolate mayo cake

chocolate cake that's so moist, it barely needs icing. (but have it anyways)made simple by using a cake mix.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. blend all ingredients
3. bake as directed on cake mix box
demonstrations.review: My daughter always requests a chocolate cake for her birthday so I found this recipe and decided to try it. I'm glad I did. It was so easy and it turned out moist and delicious. I frosted it with a vanilla buttercream frosting I found on this site (Recipe #222188). Thank you for posting this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breaded southern fried pork chops

had these for supper last night, reminded me how good they are!

1. mix flour , salt , pepper , and boullion cube
2. heat oil on med-hi in large skillet
3. roll chops in flour mixture
4. add to hot skillet
5. cook and turn for 20 minutes , until chops are done and golden brown
demonstrations.review: These pork chops were simple to make and they came out delicious!  I used thick boneless pork chops and they still came out moist and tender.  My husband loved these. I will make them again soon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple crab cakes

if you have a little leftover crab, this is the perfect recipe.  it makes 2 delicious crab cakes.
time includes 15 minutes for chilling.

1. combine the crabmeat , mayo , mustard , worcest
2. sauce , old bay seasoning , bread crumbs , and beaten egg
3. put bowl with mixture in freezer to chill for 5 minutes
4. take bowl out and shape mixture into 2 patties
5. wrap the patties with plastic wrap and put back in the freezer for 10 minutes
6. in a skillet , heat butter and oil over medium heat
7. dredge patties carefully in flour and place in pan
8. cook for about 6 minutes , until browned
9. then carefully turn patties and cook the second side about 4 minutes
demonstrations.review: I liked this recipe because it was easy to put together. I didn't use the Old Bay seasoning because I didn't have any so I used seasoned breadcrumbs. I would make this recipe again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quesadillas breakfast style

we love these and make them for brunch or sometimes dinner.

1. lay out 6 tortillas on 2 cookie sheets
2. evenly distribute the scrambled eggs , then sausage , the fried onion / pepper mixture , cheese and top with remaining tortillas
3. bake in a hot oven-450 is good , for 5 minutes-you want the tortillas crisp and the cheese all melty
4. remove and plate up with salsa , sour cream and cilantro
demonstrations.review: I love quesadillas! I tried these today and will be making them again soon! I didn't have any of the peppers but still tasted great without them. Thanks for the great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
15 minute garlic lemon chicken

so quick and so good.

1. flatten chicken slightly
2. dust with flour
3. salt and pepper chicken
4. fry in hot oil 5 minutes each side
5. remove chicken from pan
6. to pan add broth , garlic , lemon juice and butter
7. cook 2 minutes
8. pour over chicken
demonstrations.review: This recipe is wonderful! I made it for my mom and she really loved it. It's so quick and easy, yet delicious. I sprinkled some lemon pepper on the chicken but otherwise followed the recipe exactly. I will make this again. Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
low carb pizza

i got this delicious recipe from www.atkinsdietbulletboard.com the orginal chef is bikergoddess. we all thank her for creating this great recipe. it's not exactly like pizza, but it's pretty close. i like it alot. i've made it twice now, and will be making it over and over again.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. beat together cream cheese and eggs until smooth
3. add cream , parmesan , chives , italian seasoning and garlic
4. spray 9x13 pan with cooking spray or oil
5. place 2 cups mozzarella cheese in bottom of pan
6. pour egg mixture over cheese
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. remove from oven and spread sauce over baked mixture
9. add toppings of choice
10. cover with remaining mozzerella cheese
11. bake until bubbly and brown
12. let stand for 5 minutes
target.review: This was fantastic, I tweaked a bit....here's what I did: First, after spraying PAM on a 16" pizza pan, I sprinkled about 4 T of Bob's Red Mill coarse ground corn meal before the Mozzarella. This makes more of a 'pizza hut' type crispy crust in the end. Then I added 2 T of soy flour and 2 T of golden flax meal (golden flax has a milder taste) and 1/2 tsp of xanthan gum (to bind so it wouldn't be crumbly). These elements added a 'crust' effect I felt was missing the first time I tried the recipe. I used a 16" pizza pan and put the cheese in for 5 minutes (before adding egg mixture) as previous reviewers have. To understand low carb baking, you must know that  you have to replace gluten when cooking with low carb flours (flax, soy, almond, etc). You may do this by any number of methods, the lowest carb being eggs or xanthan gum. You need an extremely small amount of xanthan gum (1/4-1/2 tsp) to achieve this, or eggs, or a combination of the two. I used all the eggs called for in this recipe PLUS 1/4 tsp of xanthan gum with the additional flours. Next time I'm using almond flour and soy flour and I'll let y'all know how it goes! THANK YOU for this recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb spinach cheese  bread

makes a great sandwich wrapper.  make thick or thin, depending on your desires.  stays flexible, yet is sturdy enough to stand up to fillings.  add herbs or spices to vary the flavor - caraway seeds give the illusion of a rye type bread.  my favorite way is to make thin for a wrap, seasoned with some garlic and cayenne pepper.

1. thaw spinach , then squeeze out as much liquid as you can
2. place the dry spinach in a bowl and break up into small clumps
3. preheat oven to 350
4. line a baking sheet or pan with parchment paper , or spray well with non-stick spray
5. add remaining ingredients to spinach and stir to break up the spinach into small pieces and combine the ingredients well
6. spread batter evenly into prepared baking pan
7. bake about 20 minutes , or until dry and turning golden brown
8. remove from oven , loosen from parchment paper , let cool
9. cut into desired serving sized pieces
10. i usually use a cookie sheet that measures 10x13 , the batter spreads out to about 1 / 4 inch in this pan
11. when it is cooked it makes a thickish wrapper that can be rolled up around whatever ingredients
12. you can use a smaller pan to have thicker "bread" if desired
13. keeps well in a plastic bag for a couple of days
14. i have never had enough to last longer than that , it usually gets eaten by the second day
demonstrations.review: Just made this but I replaced the mozzarella cheese with 1/2 freshly grated sharp cheddar and 1/2 grated parmesan (not the stuff from the can) in addition to the stuff in the can. I also added sun dried tomatoes. When I first took it off the parchment paper, I let it cool on a rack and then cut it into four squares, all the while I was a bit apprehensive. Oh. My. God. I just had a bacon, lettuce and turkey sandwich on it. Seriously, it tasted like italian focaccia bread!! This is my new go-to bread!! I found a similar recipe (without spinach) for pizza on this site that was nowhere in the same galaxy as this!! This is NOT eggy at all. Bet if you got sick of spinach you could use grated eggplant or summer squash too! Wonder what would happen if you put a little baking powder and a scoop of either whey protein isolate or almond flour in? Tell you what, I'll try it this week and let you know. Thanks for a GREAT recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one minute flax muffin   low carb

got this recipe from a message board for low carb'ers and wanted it here for my reference. sadly, i don't know who the originator of this recipe is. this is quick easy, healthy, very low carb and high fiber.  works great as a sweet muffin as well as savory muffin (just omit the sweetener - goes well with soups).  original called for one packet of splenda as a sweetener.  i only use stevia. add in options; fruits, nuts, flavored sweeteners/syrups, cheese, bits of ham, vegetables or spices ... get creative and enjoy!

1. mix all ingredients in a coffee mug
2. micorowave for one minute on high
3. if using frozen berries , microwave for 1:30 on high
4. smooth on some butter and enjoy !
5. it will be moist at first , but as the muffin cools it goes away
demonstrations.review: Although I would rate mine 3 stars, I gave the recipe five stars because I didn't make it exactly as written. I didn't use stevia powder, I used a stevia packet and it wasn't sweet at all. Next time I'll use 2 packets of stevia, a little vanilla, some nutmeg and maybe a little pumpkin in place of oil and put some cream cheese on it. Like another reviewer said, the possibilities are endless, if you sweeten the cream cheese these would be like cinnamon rolls. I mean, not even close to cinnabon but, I've tasted enough sugar in my life, I'd rather stay on track, and this recipe is a great way to do just that!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
unbelievable baked buffalo wings

here's a healthy alternative to fried wings: one of my famous recipes! the meat will fall off the bone! unbelievable!

1. fill a large pot half way with water and then add the first 4 ingredients
2. bring water mixture and wings to a boil and then boil for 15 minutes
3. transfer wings to an oven safe container coated with cooking spray
4. bake wings on "broil" for 15 minutes on each side
5. while waiting for wings , combine the hot sauce and margarine in a microwave safe container and cook in microwave for 2 minutes or until melted
6. when wings are done , shake 'em up with the sauce and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: 5 star ranking is TOTALLY DESERVED! Husband called it a home run. Crispy, flavorful, a little spicy...do not be afraid of the cayenne and red pepper flakes, they just add a little spice. I did as Alton Brown does and let them sit in the fridge for 90 minutes on a paper towel lined baking sheet to dry out after boiling. Then broiled them, then tossed them in sauce. Next time I'll do this but cut the broiling time in half on each side and toss them in sauce and then throw them on the grill with the corn (they go great with corn on the cob). DELICIOUS! Thanks WhoDat...shoulda known with a name like 'WhoDat" (as in, Who Dat say they gonna beat dem Saints) that you'd come up with a delicious traditional spicy wings recipe....THANKS!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry oatmeal muffins  low sugar

these blueberry muffins came from cooking light, february 2006, but i made a couple of variations to lighten the sugar and fat load even more.  taste great!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. put oatmeal into a food processor to process until resembles course meal
3. mix all dry ingredients together well with wire whisk
4. make a well in center of dry ingredients
5. in a separate bowl mix well buttermilk , prune baby food , lemon zest , and egg substitute
6. stir wet ingredients into dry ingredients stirring slowly until just combined
7. mix blueberries and 2 tbs flour together to coat blueberries
8. carefully fold blueberries into batter
9. spoon batter into a prepared muffin tin
10. bake at 400f for 20 minutes or until cooked
11. let cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: Just made these. Didn't have buttermilk so I used fat free half and half, fat free greek yogurt and a dash more of lemon juice. Didn't have prune puree either so I just threw in a little more yogurt. I took them out of the oven and my husband inhaled two and I KNOW he wants to go back for a third. We are both on weight watchers and these are 3 pts apiece. Absolutely delicious and so healthy! Thanks so much for this recipe, I will be making them again and again, next time I'll do apples or blackberries and use the prune puree or applesauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb kfc coleslaw

i adapted this recipe from todd wilbur's version at www.topsecrets.com.

1. chop the cabbage into very fine pieces about the size of rice kernels
2. i use the shredder on my food processor and then use the grater attachment
3. i find this works just perfectly
4. then i process the carrot and onion at the same time
5. dump all this into a large bowl
6. combine the splenda , salt , pepper , milk , mayonnaise , buttermilk , vinegar , and lemon juice and whisk together until smooth
7. add the dressing to the cabbage mixture and mix well
8. cover and refrigerate for at least two hours before serving
demonstrations.review: This is delicious! Just made it for our super bowl Sunday (GO STEELERS!) and it's perfect. Tangy and sweet. Gonna go great with ribs. We aren't eating anything with cheese this superbowl....ha ha. Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
sausage gravy

this is a really easy and super deelicious recipe for sausage gravy over biscuits, you will want to make this one again and again!

1. cook sausage in skillet
2. drain fat
3. sprinkle flour over sausage and stir well
4. cook flour and sausage together for about 5 - 7 minutes
5. add milk
6. cook over medium heat until thickened
7. add pepper
8. serve over biscuits
target.review:
This was my 1st attempt at sausage gravy and it was super easy and tasted great.  My husband said it's better than his mom's (and that is always a good thing!)

Thanks a lot!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
softest ever bread machine bread

my sister gave me this recipe soon after i brought home my bread machine. it's a staple in our house. soft and fluffy and great for sandwiches or just to eat fresh out of the oven!
update 3/25/2005 - i made this using the dough cycle of my bread maker today but baked it in the oven and it turned out perfectly! i baked it at 350°f for 25-30 minutes.

1. place the water , sugar and yeast in the pan of the bread machine
2. let the yeast dissolve and foam for 10 minutes
3. add the oil , flour and salt to the yeast
4. select basic or white bread setting , and press start
5. you can also use the dough cycle of your bread maker and then place in a greased loaf pan
6. punch down and let rise again and then bake at 350 for 25-30 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: This is the best bread recipe ever!  It doesn't taste much like Challah, but I have never had a lighter, fluffier loaf come out of my bread machine.  We make this once a week - at least!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican enchilada sauce

i got this recipe from by grmil who was born and raised in mexico city. the secret to its flavor is the cocoa

1. combine all dry ingredients in a small bowl
2. stirring constantly , slowly add enough of the water to make a thin paste
3. pour into pan and add rest of water
4. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until mixture thickens
5. stir in tomato sauce
6. use in your favorite enchilada recipe
7. the amounts on the ingredients are very flexible
8. for instance , if i am feeding my kids who do not like"spicy" , i will halve the chili powder and double the tomato sauce
9. experiment to suit your taste , but don't leave out the cocoa
10. for a quick meal , we will soften a corn tortilla in a bit of hot oil , drag it through the sauce , and lay it flat on a plate
11. cover it with grated cheddar cheese , sprinkle with chopped onions and sliced black olives
12. then cover with another softened sauced tortilla and melt the cheese in the microwave for 1 minute on high
demonstrations.review: Fabulous!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pete s scratch pancakes

it was the fall of 1987 when pete nyhus walked into our office, just to visit. we started talking about breakfast, and he reached into a wastepaper basket and pulled out a scrap of teletype paper. he wrote out this recipe, and my family has never used pre-mix since.

1. mix the dry items first
2. combine the eggs and melted butter to the milk and slowly stir into the flour mixture
3. let sit at least 10 minutes while heating the pan
4. these will be high , but light and fluffy --
demonstrations.review: These were really great!!  They tasted just like homemade buttermilk pancakes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dry rub pork ribs

a simple, no hassle, no mess and delicious method for 

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. cut pork ribs into sections of 3 or 4 bones
3. mix remaining ingredients well , sprinkle on both sides of ribs and rub into the meat
4. seal rib sections in foil with a tablespoon of water in each package , and bake for 2 hours on a cookie sheet in the center of the oven
5. open foil carefully as steam escapes
6. can be crisped on a hot bbq if desired but will be great just the way it is
demonstrations.review: This was my first time making ribs and it turned out fabulous!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tropical apple date bread

we love loaf breads at our house, and i make them a couple times a week...i have collected hundreds of loaf bread recipes over the years, here is another winner from my 5 star folder. (note: the dates can be replaced with raisins if desired)

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan , or mini loaf pans
3. sift together , the flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
4. stir in coconut
5. mix together the milk , egg and vanilla
6. combine with the dry mixture
7. mix in chopped dates and apples
8. mix well until combined
9. spoon mixture into a prepared loaf pan
10. bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe.  The loaves turned out beautiful!

target.recipe_text:
rachael ray s spanakopita burgers

i'm always looking for a good turkey/chicken burger and this is wonderful.  juicy, full of flavor and not a bland thing about it.  serve with a yogurt cucumber sauce if you like.  works very well on the george foreman.

1. heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat
2. to one side , add a little extra-virgin olive oil and a tablespoon of butter
3. when butter melts , add the chopped garlic and chopped red onion and cook 5 minutes
4. transfer the onions and garlic to a bowl to cool
5. return pan to heat
6. squeeze all the water out of the thawed spinach
7. separate the spinach as you add it to the bowl with cool onions , garlic and season with 1 teaspoon of oregano
8. add in feta crumbles then chicken or turkey , grill seasoning and a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil
9. mix and form into 4 patties , 1-inch thick
10. raise heat on pan to medium-high
11. add patties and cook 6 minutes on each side
target.review: These are, without a doubt, the best burgers I have ever had. They are so flavorful and are pretty easy to make as well. Because I love cheese, I add a slice to the top as well. It tastes even better when served on rolls that have been lightly buttered and grilled. Scrumptious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey mustard crock pot chicken

super easy to make and a fantastic family or entertaining dinner if served with fluffy white rice and some buttered sugar snap peas. makes great next-day leftovers.

1. mix all the sauce ingredients together in a bowl or pyrex measuring cup
2. pour over chicken in the slow cooker
3. cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours
demonstrations.review: I liked this quite a bit. I needed something easy that used ingredients that I had on hand. That being said, I did not have any honey, so I searched for and found a substitution (1/2 cup sugar, 1/8 cup water). I decreased the amount of curry powder by half because I don't really like the taste. Also, based on other reviews, I lowered the cook time to 6 hours to get a less-brown chicken product. After removing the chicken from the crockpot, I added some cornstarch to thicken the sauce, which I served over the chicken and some mashed potatoes. Kudos!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really awesome macaroni and cheese

this is another dish that i would rather have than dessert. it truly is comfort food at its finest.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter a 13x9x2 inch glass baking dish
3. in a large pot of boiling salted water , cook macaroni al dente
4. drain and place in the buttered dish
5. add the cubed cheddar and combine
6. whisk flour , salt , mustard , pepper , cayenne and nutmeg in a medium bowl until no lumps are visible
7. gradually whisk in half-and-half , followed by the whipping cream and finally the sour cream
8. add eggs and worcestershire sauce
9. whisk well to blend
10. pour mixture over macaroni and cheese mixture
11. sprinkle with the grated cheese
12. bake in the center of the oven , 25 minutes until edges are set but center is still liquid
13. remove from oven and let stand about 10 minutes to thicken sauce
14. the sauce will still be creamy
demonstrations.review: I think this rating has to do more with my personal tastes than the actual recipe. The sauce was a little chunky (not with cheese) and I'm not sure why (I probably did something wrong). Also, the sauce didn't really taste all that cheesy, which I had expected based on reading the other comments about the richness of the sauce. It IS rich, but not cheesy. I liked the amount of sauce that the recipe made, but I guess I was expecting something different. Does anyone have any suggestions on how to make the sauce itself cheesier?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nutter butter cream cheese pie

very good i made for thanksgiving by the end of the day it was gone

1. get a bowl
2. mix cream cheese , peanut butter , powder sugar and vanilla with electric mixer on medium speed until well blended
3. take the nutter butter cookies break them in chunks big and small chunks and fold into same mixture bowl
4. spoon into gram cracker pie crust and spoon your whip cream topping on top of the filling ,
5. garnish with remaining nutter butter cookies and crumb the edgesof the pie
6. before serving put it in the freezer for one hour
demonstrations.review: This is a fantastic recipe. Another thing you can do as a variation is, instead of doing a graham cracker crust, to take the same amount of Nutter Butter cookies, crush them finely and mix with 3 tablespoons of melted butter, press into a pie plate to make a Nutter Butter crust. Doing this is more time consuming and does make the crust more difficult to slice through, but I figured I'd mention it. Thanks for the recipe! I had completely forgotten about it until I saw it here.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bruschetta chicken bake   weight watchers

dh and i both loved this. makes 4 servings at 5.5 ww points each. serve with salad or green beans for a complete meal.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. saute chicken with spices , onion and garlic until lightly browned , but not cooked through
3. place chicken in a casserole dish and sprinkle with cheese
4. in a bowl , mix tomatoes and stuffing mix , until stuffing mix is moistened
5. spread stuffing and tomato mixture over chicken and cheese
6. bake for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was good. After reading the review from greeneggs (but not having Italian diced tomatoes), I added salt and garlic powder and also baked it instead of sauteeing the chicken and spices first (I was feeling lazy). When I mixed the tomatoes and stuffing mix, I also added some Parmesan cheese to give it a little more flavor. If I make it in the future, I will use a smaller can of tomatoes because I think they made the stuffing mix bland. Either that or I will use more stuffing mix or more cheese, thus making the recipe NOT weight watchers. Oh well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
5 cheese macaroni and cheese

decadent! everyone raves about this dish. so cheesey and full of flavor. good southern comfort food. wonderful with pork chops or fried chicken. originally i got the base of this recipe from nell carter on some tv show. i had to spice it up a bit.

1. cook 2 cups macaroni noodles in salted boiling water for only about 6 minutes > do not over cook as they will continue to cook in the oven
2. while noodles are cooking: mix eggs , milk , cream cheese , melted butter and spices together in large mixing bowl
3. drain noodles
4. add noodles and all the shredded cheese to egg mixture
5. pour into a greased 9x13 baking pan
6. bake in a 325 degree oven for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was great and easy to make. I liked the cheese sauce that this recipe produced. I used a cheddar that had garlic in it, so there was quite the garlicky touch (which I like). The only other change I made was to sprinkle some breadcrumbs on top. Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
make ahead sandwiches

this is adapted from an old toh quick cooking recipe that has saved my tail many times. i keep them on hand in the freezer for those crazy busy times when i don't have time to cook.

1. in a saucepan , add the beef , onion , and garlic
2. cook and crumble up the meat until the meat is not pink
3. drain
4. add in the ketchup , pickles , salt , pepper , and hot sauce
5. stir and heat through
6. add in cheese
7. stir to combine
8. to serve immediately: spoon 1 / 3 cup mixture into buns and serve
9. to freeze and serve later: fill buns with 1 / 3 cup mixture
10. wrap individually in heavy-duty foil
11. seal tightly
12. will freeze up to 3 months
13. to use frozen sandwiches: bake at 400 in foil for 30-35 minutes or until heated
target.review: Loved how fast and easy this recipe was.  I made it as directed but we found it too sweet, so next time I will reduce the pickes.  The kids said they'd be great in their lunches for school.  Just ad some fruit and they're good to go.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy ground beef roll

this is a great recipe that i use often. the kids love it. the ground beef is rolled in a lovely dough. when baked, the dough has a light sconey texture to it. a 'must try' when you are tired of all the stock-standard ground beef options.

1. for filling: heat oil and fry bround beef until color changes
2. add onion and garlic and saute for a few minutes
3. season with salt , pepper and parsley
4. add chutney and leave to cool slightly
5. for dough: sift flour , salt and sugar
6. rub in margarine or butter and add cheese
7. beat egg and milk , add dry ingredients , and mix to a soft dough
8. roll out into into a 20cm x 30cm rectangle
9. spoon meat evenly onto dough , roll up like a swiss roll and place on a greased baking tray
10. make a few incisions in the roll and brush with beaten egg or milk
11. bake in pre-heated oven at 180c or 350f for 40-50 minutes or until browned
12. cook when needed
demonstrations.review: This tastes good and I was happy to use up some leftover ground beef in a new recipe.  I didn't have chutney, so I subbed a combination of apricots, pineapple, nutmeg and brown sugar.  Because I couldn't follow the recipe exactly I wont click the stars, but I would give it a 4/5.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tgi friday s mandarin orange sesame dressing copycat

this came from an e-cookbook that features recipes from famous restaraunts. i hope you enjoy this!

1. measure the marmalade , cayenne pepper , ginger , garlic powder , vinegar , oil , soy sauce , sesame oil and honey into a blender container
2. cover and blend on medium speed for 30 to 45 seconds
3. then transfer to a small bowl and add the chopped orange sections
4. stir to mix , cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days
5. serve on a bed of mixed greens , topped by sliced grilled chicken breasts
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I had to make a substitution, but it still tasted delicious.  I didn't have any marmalade or fresh mandarins, so instead I used one 10 oz can of mandarin slices with the juice.  It may not have been as sweet as it would be with marmalade, but still very tasty.  The second time I made it I omitted the soy sauce just to keep it from being such a dark colour - my children were more willing to try it on their salad with the lovely orange colour.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted french onion   onion

my mother gave me this recipe. she states she saw it on a cooking show. i decided to give it a try and fell in love with it. i love onions any way -- roasted, carmelized and even fresh. i am giving her credit and putting it here for others to enjoy!

1. cut the ends off the onion , just enough that it will rest flat on its root end
2. peel off outer dry layers
3. cut into wedges leaving the root end intact
4. place on a square of heavy foil
5. top with boullion and butter
6. wrap securely , be sure that you do not poke holes in the foil-- you want the juices to stay in there with the onion
7. bake at 350 for 45 min to 1 hour
8. remove from foil into a serving bowl and top with cheese while hot
9. enjoy with a piece of crusty french bread
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I had a small onion, so I halfed the recipe and had it as a snack.  I will try this at work for lunch by cooking it in the microwave.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country hamburger lentil soup   crock pot

i created this on a busy hockey weekend - i wanted something warm to come home to after spending a long day at the hockey rink.  this was just the ticket... and i got to clean out my cupboards too!

1. brown ground beef
2. combine all ingredients in 4-5qt crock pot
3. cook on low at least 12 hours or high for 6 hours
4. i do a combination of high / low , when i made this i did low for 5 hours and high for 4 hours
5. remove bay leaves before serving
6. it made very yummy leftovers !
demonstrations.review: I had a crazy day coming at me and this recipe was just what I needed.  I didn't have dried lentils, so I used 2 cans of kidney beans which made my soup more brothy.  I followed the rest of the ingredients and cooked on low for 8 hours.  Then I picked up some fresh buns on the way home and dinner was served.  It fed our family of 4 with no leftovers.  Thank you for an easy and healthy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
london fog  my low cost  low fat version

the london fog is a popular cafe tea made with earl grey tea, steamed & frothed milk and vanilla syrup. i have neither the time nor the money to get all fancy but i love the taste, so i came up with this and a friend requested i post it. i steep my tea by the pot (in my coffee maker), but i'll break it down to one cup. feel free to post comments. i have switched this recipe to skim milk but i have made it with skim milk powder. most people don't care for powder but i live in the middle of nowhere and sometimes i run out of fresh and that's where the original recipe was created one day when i really needed a nice comfort bevvie on a cold winter day and if i add just enough vanilla & honey it helps to cut the taste of the powder :-)  blessings ♥

1. place tea bag in a measuring cup and add boiling water , steep for at least 3min
2. in your favourite mug , mix together honey , vanilla & milk
3. heat in microwave for 30 seconds
4. remove bag from tea and pour in your mug with the heated milk
5. stir
6. enjoy
7. careful , it's hot !
demonstrations.review: Love this as a nice treat in the morning.  I've also made it with Rooiboos tea when I ran out of Earl Grey.

target.recipe_text:
best oatmeal cookies

this is a family favorite that i have been making for years. it's the most requested oatmeal cookie recipe i've ever made. i found it somewhere years ago, but have lost the source. the secret is soaking the raisins which makes all the difference.

1. this is a very important first step that makes the cookie: combine eggs , raisins and vanilla and let stand for one hour
2. cream together butter and sugars
3. add flour , salt , cinnamon and soda and mix well
4. blend in egg-raisin mixture , oatmeal , and chopped nuts
5. dough will be stiff
6. drop by heaping teaspoons onto ungreased cookie sheet , or roll into balls and flatten slightly
