i had to make 3 pumpkin pies to take to my son's home.  i had enough mixture left over make another pie but not enough pie dough for a 4th pie.  so i spray oiled a round casserole dish, filled with mixture and baked.

1. combine first 8 ingredients in a large bowl , mixing well
2. combine the evaporated milk and the heavy cream in a small saucepan
3. heat the milks to the scalding point
4. add scalded milks to the other ingredients , mixing well
5. pour equally into the two unbaked pie shells
6. bake 350 degrees for about 1 hour
7. pie is done when a knife inserted into the middle comes out clean
8. top with desired topping
demonstrations.review: Best pumpkin pie ever! I used deep dish pie shells because this recipe made a whooole lot of filling. My baking time fell somewhere between 65 and 70 minutes. I garnished the pies with whole pecans when they had cooled, and they looked gorgeous. The only thing better was how they tasted! Thanks for the recipe - this one's a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
quick n  easy salmon patties

i have used this recipe for many years and my family loves it, especially my husband. i think i got the recipe off of a crisco can when they still used paper wrapping on the cans.

1. drain salmon
2. set aside 2 tbsp of the juice
3. in a medium mixing bowl , mix salmon , egg and onion until sticky
4. stir in flour
5. add baking powder to salmon juice and stir into salmon mixture
6. form into small patties and fry until golden brown in hot crisco
7. serve with tartar sauce
target.review: Very good - I added 1/4 C mayo and covered with slice of american cheese.  mmm--

demonstrations.recipe_text:
schnitzla   polish meatballs

nothing fancy here, just an old family recipe.

1. chop onion and saut in 1 stick margarine until very soft
2. drain and reserve margarine
3. mix raw pork , ground round , cooked onion , 1 / 4 box finely crushed cracker crumbs , and 2 eggs
4. form patties with 1 1 / 2 to 2 tablespoon meat
5. crush another quarter box of the saltines into very fine crumbs , coat each meatball in the crumbs and gently flatten very slightly
6. fry in reserved margarine , keeping margarine level in pan to at least 1 / 4 inch
7. drain and enjoy
demonstrations.review: Very Good.  I did add a little olive oil to the meat mixture prior to shaping the balls.  This produces a juicier meatball.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot stuffed green bell peppers

this can be made the night before, put into the refrigerator. then put into the crock pot before going to work, or what ever you want to do the  day. try this recipe, you wont be sorry, and it won’t heat up your house in the summer.

1. cut the tops of the peppers , cut below the stem crown , dont toss the tops yet
2. cut around the stem , and chop the pepper part into small peaces
3. remove the seeds from the peppers
4. in large frying pan brown hamburger , onion , mushrooms , and small chopped pepper from the stem
5. when browned , drain grease , add rice , and one half of the sauce
6. heat , and stir till it is hot again , and it is mixed well
7. put filling in green peppers
8. cover the peppers with around one table spoon , or more of sauce
9. dump the rest into the crock pot
10. cover , and cook on low for 8 hours
11. side
12. the small , deep crock pots wont work
13. you can also make it this way , and cook it in the oven
demonstrations.review: Worked and tasted great

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn muffin casserole

this is a wonderfully simple side-dish that tastes very similar to chi-chi's corn cake, which i have been missing so much since our chi-chi's closed:( could also be served for breakfast, with maple syrup drizzled over top...mmm!

1. in large bowl , combine first four ingredients well
2. stir in corn muffin mix
3. pour into 9x13-inch pan
4. drizzle melted margarine over top and sprinkle with sugar
5. bake in preheated 350f oven for 55-60 minutes
demonstrations.review: Delicious and so easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach quiche

this quiche is my favorite. my children love it too, and it's a great way to get them to each spinach without complaining.

1. cook the spinach and drain well
2. mix remaining ingredients and add to spinach
3. put in unbaked pie shell
4. sprinkle 1 / 4 cup cheese on top
5. bake at 400 degrees for 40 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Delicious - and EASY!

Used evaporated milk for a richer taste.

Didn't have cheddar cheese, used 1/2 mozzarella and 1/2 colby jack with about 1/4 C parmesan

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy potatoes w  corn flakes

this is a staple at our summer grill-outs.  it's easy and can be prepared the day before, then baked when you need it.  i use reduced fat cheddar cheese, light sour cream and 98% fat-free cream of chicken soup.

1. take hash browns out of freezer , keep in bag , set aside
2. in microwave , melt 1 stick of butter in large bowl
3. mix in sour cream , cheese and cream of chicken soup
4. in 9x13 pan , spread hash browns
5. spread sour cream , cheese , and soup mixture on top
6. melt 1 / 2 stick of butter on stovetop , mix in corn flakes , stir until butter is absorbed
7. you may need / want to add more corn flakes
8. sprinkle corn flakes on top of sour cream , cheese and soup mixture
9. bake 1 hour at 350
demonstrations.review:
Made this for a potluck breakfast at work ---

Everyone loved it --

The best part was it was so easy to fix the night before and just heat in the microwave at work.

I did add carmelized onions to the potatoes and a handful of additional cornflakes for the topping.

target.recipe_text:
sweet and spicy sweet potato bake

this is a must at your holiday dinner table, it has just the right balance of sweet and spicy --- cooking time will vary depending on the size you cut the sweet potatoes you will love these!

1. in a resealable plastic bag toss the cubed sweet potatoes with melted butter or oil
2. add the rest of ingredients
3. toss well to coat
4. transfer to a greased baking dish
5. bake uncovered at 400 degrees for about 22-25 minutes , or until sweet potatoes are tender but not too soft
6. delicious !
target.review: Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kevin s best corned beef

this is the best corned beef you will ever have. 

1. use a 14 to 20 qt
2. pan
3. coarsely chop enough onions and carrots to make 1 cup each
4. in pan , place onions and carrots , corned beef with any liquid from meat , vinegar , stout , mustard seed , coriander , peppercorns , dill , allspice , and bay leaves
5. add water to barely cover beef
6. cover pan and bring to a boil over high heat
7. simmer till meat is tender when pierced , 2 1 / 2 to 3 hours
8. meanwhile , cut remaining onions into wedges
9. cut remaining carrots into 2 inch lengths , halve them lengthwise if large
10. cut cabbage in half through cores , then into wedges
11. scrub potatoes
12. add onions , carrots and potatoes to tender corned beef , place cabbage on top
13. cover and return to simmering over high heat
14. reduce heat and simmer till cabbage is tender when pierced , 15 to 20 minutes
15. with slotted spoon , scoop out vegetables onto warm serving dishes
16. using tongs and a slotted spoon , remove beef to a cutting board
17. cut off fat
18. slice meat across grain , place on warm platters
19. serve meat and vegetables with mustards
demonstrations.review: Good

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s black chicken

this is a super easy summer dinner. doesn't need to marinate for long. pair it with grilled corn and sliced summer tomatoes and you have a great summer dinner.

1. rinse chicken and pat dry
2. marinate all ingredients together for at least 1 hour
3. grill over medium heat
4. sprinkle with sesame seeds when done
demonstrations.review: Excellent!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin and chickpea ratatouille

recipe from womens weekly magazine and stated to be from the ww "pantry" cookbook. a simple vegetarian recipe. be sure to drain and rinse your chickpeas to get rid of the brine

1. preheat oven to 220c
2. place the pumpkin in a single layer onto an oven tray
3. drizzle with half of the oil
4. roast uncovered for 20 minutes or until tender
5. remove any skins
6. heat the remaining oil in a large saucepan
7. cook the onion and garlic , stirring , until the onion softens
8. add the tomato paste and cook a further minute
9. add the vinegar , undrained tomatoes , water , allspice , chickpeas and pumpkin
10. bring to the boil and then simmer for 5-10 minutes
11. serve ratatouile over couscous or quinoa
12. garnish by sprinkling over some fresh herbs such as parsley or basil
demonstrations.review: Tried this last night and it was delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetarian pitas

a healthy lunch or light supper.

1. slit open the pitas
2. spread the insides of each pocket with hummus
3. stuff each pita with half of remaining ingredients
4. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Tasty and simple! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate strawberry desserts

chocolate pudding layered with strawberry flavored whipped cream. yum! simple and easy for when you need a last minute dessert.

1. beat milk and pudding mix till thick and smooth and set aside
2. drain strawberries and place berries in a blender
3. cover and process until smooth
4. in a mixing bowl , beat cream and sugar until stiff peaks form
5. gently fold in strawberry puree
6. divide half of the chocolate pudding among four dessert dishes
7. top with half the strawberry mixture
8. repeat layers and garnish with strawberry slices
demonstrations.review: really good

target.recipe_text:
chocolate cherry cookies

a hidden cherry under the chocolate makes a sweet surprise when you bite into these wonderful chocolate cookies.

1. combine flour and cocoa
2. set aside
3. beat butter in a med bowl on med speed until softened
4. add sugar , baking soda , baking powder and salt
5. beat until well mixed
6. beat in egg and vanilla , scraping the side of the bowl
7. gradually beat in flour mixture
8. shape dough into 1-inch balls
9. place 2-inches apart on an ungreased cooking sheet
10. press down the centers with your thumb
11. drain cherries , reserving juice
12. place a cherry in the center of each cookie in the depression you made with your thumb
13. combine chocolate pieces and condensed milk in a small saucepan
14. cook and stir over low heat until the chocolate is melted
15. stir in 4 teaspoons of the reserved cherry juice
16. spoon about 1 teaspoon of the chocolate and milk mixture over each cherry , spreading to cover cherry
17. if the frosting is too thick , thin with additional cherry juice
18. bake in a 350f oven for about 10 minutes or until edges of cookie is firm
19. cool on cookie sheet for 1 minute
20. transfer to a wire rack to finish cooling
target.review: I made thise as part of my cookie tray. My son and daughter inhaled them.  This recipe is a keeper!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s sausage sawmill gravy  with biscuits

comfort food at it's best, this is a family favorite that goes back years! --- jimmy dean has a wonderful bulk sausage roll that will work great for this recipe, you may adjust the pepper flakes to suit heat level, my family likes extreme heat so i use 2 heaping teaspoons or you may use spicy sausage meat --- serve this over biscuits, i also like to serve it over mashed potatoes or fries :)

1. cook the sausage meat with onion in a large skillet over medium heat until sausage meat no longer pink
2. drain fat
3. add in crushed red pepper flakes and cook stirring until the meat is lightly browned
4. stir in 1 / 4 cup plus 2 teaspoon flour into the skillet and mix until dissolved with the meat
5. add in the cream and worcestershire sauce
6. cook over medium-low heat until thickened and bubbly
7. add in salt and ground black pepper
8. serve over biscuits
demonstrations.review: Yummy--I substituted scallions, and some cream because I had them---great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate mint syrup

this was sent to me as a use for the amazing mint bounty we are currently experiencing. the mint chocolate chip ice cream fetist in the house approves. from miri rotkovitz, for about.com. thank you miri!

1. in a small saucepan , combine the cocoa powder and cold water , and whisk together until smooth
2. add the sugar and torn mint leaves and place the saucepan over medium heat
3. bring the mixture to a boil , stirring constantly to melt the sugar
4. as soon as the syrup begins to boil , reduce the heat and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes , until it begins to thicken and turn glossy
5. remove from the heat and allow to cool
6. when the syrup has cooled to near room temperature , strain it through a fine mesh sieve into a clean jar
7. cover and store in the refrigerator
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is a terrific way to use fresh mint.  The mint taste is very light.  I am making a large quantity of this to give as gifts.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot german potato salad

this was passed down from my great-great-grand mother who came from germany in the 1800's.

1. dice and fry bacon
2. in a small bowl , add eggs , salt , mustard , sugar , vinegar and cayenne pepper
3. beat well and pour into hot pan with bacon and bacon grease stirring till thickened
4. add diced cooked potatoes and sliced onion
5. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Excellent --Made it for the 4th of July!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern hamburger quiche

i got this recipe from my mom.i added a few ingredients to it to change it up a little. my husband loves it!!!!!

1. brown hamburger meat
2. add chopped onions
3. cook until meat is browned
4. add green chiles , ro-tel tomatoes , black beans , cumin and chili powder
5. simmer for 5 minutes
6. beat eggs in a bowl
7. add salt , pepper and worcestershire sauce
8. add sour cream and whisk together
9. add egg mixture to the meat mixture and stir to blend together
10. add shredded cheese
11. pour equal amount of mixture into the unbaked pie crust
12. bake at 375 degrees for 1 to 1-1 / 2 hours
demonstrations.review: My family and I really enjoyed this recipe.  I omitted the chilis and added sweet green pepper instead. The quiche browned very fast.  I only baked it for 55 minutes because I thought it was going to burn.  I will make this again!  I also used light sour cream without any problem!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish rosie s irish soda bread

this irish soda bread recipe was passed on to me by a dear friend of my mother's who was born and raised in ireland. it's the best irish soda bread i have ever had. it is much higher, lighter and softer than most other recipes i have seen. it has an excellent flavor and texture, as well.

1. combine dry ingredients together in a large bowl
2. in a small bowl beat eggs and stir in sour cream
3. add the egg and sour cream mixture to the dry ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon
4. batter will be very thick
5. add the raisins and caraway seeds and stir well with wooden spoon or knead in with your hands
6. place batter in a greased 9 inch springform pan
7. dust the top with enough flour so that you can pat the batter like a bread dough evenly in the pan without it sticking to your hands
8. with a knife make a shallow crisscross on the top
9. bake for 50 minutes in a preheated 350f oven
demonstrations.review:
Not that this recipe needs another review....I just want to put my 2 cents in. This bread is terrific!! I really wanted to purchase a loaf of Irish Soda Bread at a local bakery (and they make great soda bread)... but I figured I would give this recipe a shot since it had so many terrific reviews. I am so glad I did. This bread is so easy to make especially with my Kitchen Aid mixer and it so moist. I did adjust it slightly. I soaked the raisins in Irish whiskey (hey --St. Patrick's Day is almost here!!) and only put in 1 Tbs of caraway seeds and used light sour cream. I'll be baking this bread for St. Patty's Day instead of buying it!! Thanks for a great recipe!! Happy St. Patrick's Day to all!!

UPDATE --I made this again ---in fact I made 2 loaves. I almost bought the irish soda bread at my local bakery because I was getting lazy! I didn't. This bread is so easy to make!! I added 2 T of caraway seeds in each --so glad I did. I again soaked the raisins in Irish Whiskey --- YUM!!. When I made the second loaf I didn't have any sour cream and I didn't want to run to the store so I used 2% greek plain yogurt instead. SO SO glad I did. My second loaf turned out even better. I don't know if this was a fluke but I will try it with greek yogurt again. I also made homemade butter - all I can say is YUM!!! This is one of my FAVORITE recipes.

target.recipe_text:
curried chicken salad with fruit

a lovely twist on chicken salad, with a delicious blend of flavors.  i adapted this from a clipping from cook's country that my mom gave me.  it works as a sandwich or wrap filling, and i also enjoy serving it over some fresh greens.  adjust the curry powder to your taste - i have found that different brands have different strengths.

1. combine the mayonnaise , lime juice , curry powder , cumin and coriander
2. mix well
3. add chicken , celery , onion , pineapple and cranberries and toss to cover all with the sauce
4. add salt and pepper , to your taste
target.review: I found this recipe while searching for a curried chicken salad, having recently enjoyed one from a restaurant salad bar.  The pineapple & cranberries really compliment the curry.  This salad is great and if you are a curry lover as I am, I hope you'll try it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with shrimp and wine

this is one of the best pasta/seafood dishes i have ever tasted! i know the recipe came from a cookbook, but a friend gave it to me several years ago (xeroxed the page) and the title of the book doesn't appear. sorry i can't give credit!
i've made it with scallops, too, and it's just as good.

1. thaw shrimp , if frozen
2. in a saucepan , cook onion in 2 tblsp
3. butter and olive oil until tender but not brown
4. stir in wine , bouillon granules , basil , salt and pepper
5. bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer , uncovered , for 12 to 15 minutes or until about 1 / 3 of the liquid is evaporated
6. halve shrimp lengthwise and add to wine mixture
7. cover and simmer about 5 minutes until shrimp is just tender
8. stir in tomatoes and heat through
9. toss pasta with 1 / 4 cup butter , melted
10. add shrimp mixture , cheese and parsley
11. toss until pasta is coated
demonstrations.review: We have been enjoying this recipe for a couple of years now...time to tell others to try it!  I usually half it, because there are only two of us.  I have only added a clove of crushed garlic with the onion; other than that, leave it alone.  I serve it on top of little bird nests of angel hair pasta.  Be sure to use the fresh parsley.  It is wonderful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracked wheat buttermilk bread with sunflower seeds

this is a nutritious, hearty bread with a nice nutty taste. it makes great toast! cracked wheat can be found in a bulk food store.

1. put cracked wheat into a small pot with 1 to 2 cups of water
2. bring to a boil , reduce heat to medium and boil for 6 minutes
3. remove from heat and drain well
4. let cool about 15 minutes
5. put cooked wheat into bread machine
6. add all other ingredients as listed except for the sunflower seeds
7. if you don't have buttermilk , you can make a substitute by adding 1 tbsp lemon juice to one cup of whole milk
8. stir and let sit for 5 minutes
9. use amount called for in the recipe
10. set bread machine for whole wheat bread
11. press start
12. add sunflower seeds at'addition' beep
demonstrations.review: This makes the most amazing bread!  I have modified the recipe to use olive oil instead of butter, omit the sunflower seeds, and use my stand mixer with dough hook.  I found I needed a bit more flour because the dough was too soft; knead with the dough hook until dough leaves the sides of the bowl, about 6-10 min.  Let rise in a bowl sprayed with Pam, covered about 45 min.  Deflate and form in a loaf and let rise, covered for another 45 min.  Bake 40-45 min. @ 350, tenting with foil after 20 min. to prevent over-browning.  Delish! p.s. Buy the cracked wheat from MySpiceSage.com

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marinated broccoli slaw

great change from mayo-based slaws!  i use a bag of pre-shredded broccoli slaw that includes shredded broccoli stalks, carrots, and red cabbage.  but i bet the marinade would be great for a cabbage slaw, too.  this gains flavor as it sits--best after a day in the refrigerator, but still good with a few hours to chill.  time does not include chilling.  i estimated six servings.  its probably several more than that, but *some* of us had rather large portions.

1. empty the bag of shredded veggies into a very large mixing bowl
2. in a small sauce pan , combine the vinegar , salt , garlic powder , pepper , brown sugar , soy sauce , and mustard
3. cover and bring to a boil
4. remove from the heat and add the sugar and oil , stirring or whisking to dissolve
5. allow the marinade to cool , then pour over the veggies and mix thoroughly
6. refrigerate and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I have been looking for a marinade for red cabbage salad...this is fantastic!  Just toss with sliced cabbage and refrigerate overnite.  I messed up and put all of the ingredients in a saucepan and then read again about adding the oil & sugar after the other ingredients came to a boil.  I let it all come to a boil, used my hand blender to emulsify and it was perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry pudding loaf

like a slice of pudding. very very moist and dense--in loaf form. make a tasty dessert or mid-morning snack with a hot cup of tea.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in very large mixing bowl , cream butter and cream cheese with mixer on medium speed until creamy and blended
3. add sugar , sour cream and vanilla
4. mix until fluffy
5. add eggs , one at a time , mixing well after each
6. in large mixing bowl , combine flour , baking soda , baking powder and salt
7. add gradually to butter / cream cheese mixture
8. and blend well
9. add blueberries
10. stir only to distribute
11. batter will be very thick
12. put batter into two greased and floured loaf pans
13. bake for 50-60 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
14. cool in loaf pans for 10 minutes before removing to wire rack to cool
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe! I used fresh blueberries, and light sour cream because that's what I had. It took 1 hr. 5 min. in my oven, and turned out beautifully.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberries and cream ice cream

if you are a blueberry lover, you are in for a real treat!  this rich and creamy ice cream  is sure to  satisfy your sweet tooth!  using fresh blueberries is always best, but you can use frozen (see note below).  cook time reflects chill time.  from williams-sonoma.

1. in a heavy medium saucepan , combine blueberries , water and sugar over medium high heat , bring to a boil and stir occasionally to dissolve sugar
2. reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 1 minute
3. remove from heat and allow to stand for 30 minutes
4. transfer blueberry mixture to food processor and process till smooth , 1 minute
5. strain through a fine mesh sieve into a bowl
6. cover and refrigerate about 3 hours to 24 hours , until well chilled
7. add cream and lemon juice to blueberry puree and stir to combine
8. transfer mixture to an ice cream machine and process according to manufacturer's directions
9. transfer the ice cream to freezer safe container , cover and freeze until firm , about 3 hours
10. make the sugar syrup by combining the water and the sugar in a saucepan , bringing to a boil over medium high heat , cooking until clear , about 1 minute
11. put the frozen berries in a heatproof bowl and pour the syrup over them
12. allow to cool and then transfer to the food processor and proceed with recipe
demonstrations.review: Wonderful favor and creamy texture.  I tried it with Splenda granular instead of sugar and fat free half and half instead of heavy cream and it is still exceptionally good!

target.recipe_text:
shrimp fra diavolo

i use this recipe to make both shrimp fra diavolo and lobster fra diavolo, just substitute the shrimp with lobster meat.  we usually serve it over linguine.  if you like it hot just increase the red pepper flakes we always do!

1. in a large bowl , toss the shrimp with 1 teaspoon salt and the red pepper flakes
2. in a large , heavy skillet , heat the oil over a medium high flame
3. add the shrimp and saute until just cooked through , about 2 minutes
4. using a slotted spoon , transfer the shrimp to a large plate and set aside
5. add the onion to the same skillet and saute until translucent , about 5 minutes
6. add the tomatoes with their juices , wine , garlic , and oregano , and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly , about 10 minutes
7. return the shrimp and any accumulated juices to the tomato mixture and toss to coat
8. remove from heat and stir in the parsley and basil
9. season with more salt to taste and serve over linquine or your favorite pasta
target.review: I have made this twice now.  The first time I followed the recipe exactly.  The second time, I did not saute the shrimp with the red peppers because I wanted to make the sauce ahead of time.  I made the sauce and then put it in the blender to make it smooth.  We liked it better this way.  Next time I will not use as much crushed red peppers(DH head was sweating lol).  Either way you can't go wrong!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian bread dip

we've had this in the finer italian restaurants here in michigan and it's a must have when eating italian recipes. if you are a garlic lover, you will love this and adjust the garlic to your preference. my hubby & i usually share a plate of this and i'll have 5-6 pressed cloves of garlic on my side alone!

1. pour olive oil onto salad sized plate
2. place pressed garlic all around the edges of the plate to form a ring of garlic
3. drizzle balsamic vinegar over garlic& olive oil
4. sprinkle parmesan cheese , oregano , & black pepper over entire plate
5. dip italian bread or french baguette until your garlic loving heart contents
demonstrations.review: Neither my husband or I was impressed by this recipe.  Maybe if the garlic had been roasted...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dirty shrimp in butter beer sauce

herby, spicy shrimp with a kick, in a buttery-beer "sauce". fast, easy and delicious, serve as an appetizer, or a dinner over rice or with lots of crusty french bread to soak up all the tasty, herbalicious sauce!

1. saute garlic and herbs in butter until garlic is slightly browned
2. add shrimp , stirring constantly , until shrimp are pink and done
3. pour in beer , simmer 1 minute more , and serve !
demonstrations.review: It was very good.  I used half of the red pepper flakes, cayenne pepper and black pepper.  It was still plenty hot enough.  Next time I will use only half of the thyme.  It seemed to overpower.  I used Killian's Red and tossed the shrimp with flour first.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best oatmeal cookies

this is a family favorite that i have been making for years. it's the most requested oatmeal cookie recipe i've ever made. i found it somewhere years ago, but have lost the source. the secret is soaking the raisins which makes all the difference.

1. this is a very important first step that makes the cookie: combine eggs , raisins and vanilla and let stand for one hour
2. cream together butter and sugars
3. add flour , salt , cinnamon and soda and mix well
4. blend in egg-raisin mixture , oatmeal , and chopped nuts
5. dough will be stiff
6. drop by heaping teaspoons onto ungreased cookie sheet , or roll into balls and flatten slightly
7. bake at 350 degrees for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned
demonstrations.review: delightful!  smelled so wonderful while baking.  crispy on the outside, chewy on the inside. mmmmm i may back off the sugar a lil next time.  i don't have quite a cup of raisins, so i added some chocolate chips to half of the dough.  both ways were good, but next time i will make sure i have enough raisins and maybe add extra :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple succulent shrimp scampi

this recipe is easy, quick, and gives the impression of a gourmet chef! the ingredients are simple, but the taste is truly 

1. first , peel shrimp and devein if desired
2. then , saute garlic in olive oil for about 1 to 2 minutes
3. next , add the butter and shrimp
4. cook until shrimp are somewhat pink
5. finally , stir in wine and red pepper
6. reduce heat and allow shrimp fully cook
7. when finished , sprinkle with parsley and serve over pasta or rice
8. a few
9. i recommend the following: 1 / 4 tsp of crushed red pepper1 / 4 cup of fresh or 1 / 8 cup of dried parsley
10. add more butter if you'd like
11. serve over angel hair pasta
demonstrations.review: Delightful!  I added lemon juice then parmesan cheese just before serving.  Served over rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheddar bay biscuits  red lobster style

i found this "copycat" recipe from a website. it is soooo easy and incredibly good! i've made this several times for my family and friends and they just love them. they think these are better than the ones served in the restaurant! i add extra cheese on top (maybe that's the key) ; ) hope you enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. combine garlic butter ingredients , mixing well
3. combine biscuit ingredients in a medium bowl
4. mix until well combined
5. drop approximately 1 / 4-cup portions of the dough onto an ungreased cookie sheet
6. brush garlic butter on top before baking
7. ps: sprinkle extra cheese on top as well
8. if you would like
9. )
10. bake for 14-16 minutes or until the tops of the biscuits begin to turn light brown
11. serve warm
demonstrations.review: These were great.  I mad a few simple changes.  I used buttermilk and 1/4 tsp of garlic powder in the batter.  I baked them then topped them with the garlic butter and popped them back in the oven to crisp.  Delicious!

target.recipe_text:
awesome baked ham

i love this recipe because it is so easy and it calls for hardly any ingredients, and i always have these ingredients in my pantry. this recipe came from a good friend's mother, who was always asked to bake the ham for get-togethers and family dinners. now i get those requests. people who ordinarily aren't too fond of ham rave over this one. after i carve, i spoon a little of the glaze over the meat in the platter - yummmm!

1. in a medium size mixing bowl , mix yellow mustard and brown sugar until you have a thick"paste"
2. take all wrappers off of ham and trim away excess fat
3. line baking pan with aluminum foil
4. place ham on foil and spread brown sugar / mustard paste on top
5. fold and seal foil
6. do not open again until ham is done
7. bake at 350 for 4 hours
8. let set for about 1 hr then carve
9. one of the best tasting hams you will ever have !
target.review: OMG!!!  Until I tried this recipe, I wasn't wild about baked ham.  Besides pizza, it would probably be one of the last things I'd really ever have a craving for.  However, hams were on sale, and I remember my mom used to bake a ham, then use the remaining bone to put in a pot of red beans, which being from Louisiana, red beans and rice is a traditional weekly meal, and one of my favorites.  I had a 9 lb. half ham, so I adjusted the recipe accordingly.  The only addition I made was to put some ground cloves into the brown sugar/mustard paste, then right before it was done, I opened the foil, decorated it with pineapple and cherries, and returned it to the oven, uncovered, and under the broiler for about 5 minutes more, to try to caramelize it a little.  Boopster, I will NEVER bake a ham any other way from now on!  Because of your recipe, I love baked ham!!  It was so moist and juicy, and just deeeeeeeeeelicious!  Thank you very much for sharing! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry ice cream like ben  and jerry s

good enough to be served at ben & jerry's.  use fresh, good-quality ingredients.  i love to make this during strawberry season.  plan to refrigerate berries in sugar for 1 hour before making ice cream.

1. combine strawberries , lemon juice , and 1 / 4 cup sugar in a mixing bowl , set aside in fridge for 1 hour
2. in large mixing bowl beat eggs until light and fluffy , about 2 minutes
3. gradually add 3 / 4 cups sugar , mixing well
4. stir in milk and vanilla and mix well
5. add strawberries with juice and mix well
6. gently stir in whipping cream just until combined
7. pour into ice cream maker and follow manufacturer's instructions
8. i use a donvier ice cream maker that doesn't require ice or salt and it works great !
demonstrations.review: Absolutely, the BEST Strawberry Ice Cream, ever!!  The only thing I did differently was, instead of using 2 cups of whipping cream, I used 1 cup of half and half, and 1 cup of whipping cream.  The texture was very light and fluffy!  Just perfect for me!  Thank you for sharing! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best chinese fried rice with egg

the secret to the best chinese fried rice is onions, garlic and sesame oil, you may add in cooked chicken, beef, pork or shrimp, also you may add in some frozen thawed peas or fresh sauteed or canned mushrooms, whatever you have handy in your fridge! --- for this recipe it is best to use slightly undercooked rice that is more firm that soft the best recipe is the firm option on my recipe#350260 the amount of egg does not matter, if you like lots of egg then use as many eggs as desired, if you like a little heat then add in some cayenne pepper, i most always do you and you will probably need to adjust the soy sauce to your liking ---  you will love this rice!

1. in a small bowl beat the eggs with water
2. melt the butter in a large skillet or a wok over medium heat or until sizzling
3. add in eggs and leave flat for about 2 minutes or until cooked through
4. remove to a plate then chop
5. heat oil in the same skillet
6. add in onion and saute until softened
7. add in cold rice , soy sauce , sesame oil and black pepper
8. stir-fry tossing continuously for about 5 minutes
9. stir in the egg and green onion
demonstrations.review: Super good recipe!!!  I added shrimp and used left over rice, which works great because it has a chance to dry out, keeping it from being mushy.  Thanks for posting! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and spinach manicotti or shells

we were treated to this at a friends house for dinner. very good! recipe can easily made ahead  and be halved. what i especially like about it it, it is not too cheesy! easy to make and easy to serve. i prefer making the shells for that reason.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in large bowl , combine chicken , ricotta cheese , spinach , 1 / 2 cup half and half , bread crumbs , garlic , basil , oregano , salt and black pepper
3. mix well
4. spread 1 / 4 c sauce on bottom of 13x9-inch baking dish
5. stuff chicken & cheese mixture into manicotti
6. line up shells in the baking dish
7. combine remaning marinara sauce and remaining 3 / 4 cup half and half
8. pour over stuffed manicotti
9. top with mozzarella cheese
10. bake 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated
demonstrations.review: Ok, I made this last night.  It was very tasty, but I made an alfredo sauce, instead of a marinara sauce.  I really should have stuck with the marinara, because it was just too rich with the alfredo.  I'll try it again, exactly as written.  Again, thanks for sharing.  Other than my alfredo sauce accompaniment, it was delicious!  My mistake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
addictive chicken

its so good it's addicting, hence the name. it's easy and delicious.  serve with green beans and rice or potatoes to make a delicious meal your whole family will be begging you to make again and again.  also try using chicken wings or with fish.

1. 1
2. first , preheat the oven to 350f
3. 2
4. then combine the grated cheese and the seasonings
5. line a shallow baking pan with foil
6. 3
7. melt the butter in a shallow bowl or pan
8. 4
9. dip each piece of chicken into the butter , and then into the seasoned cheese , coating well
10. 5
11. arrange in the foil lined pan
12. bake for 30-45 minutes at 350f
13. 6
14. then -- kick yourself that you didn't make a double recipe !
demonstrations.review: This was delicious, but after reading other reviews, I totally omitted the salt.  Parmesan cheese is very high in salt, so with that, it was plenty enough.  Thanks for sharing!   Will definitely make again! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar meatloaf

i use chili sauce or salsa instead of ketchup to give a nice contrast to the sweetness of the brown sugar.  a lighter version can be made using splenda brown sugar blend, skim milk, and egg beaters. got this one from the allrecipes website. it's one of their most popular recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease a 5x9 inch loaf pan
3. press the brown sugar in the bottom of the prepared loaf pan and spread the ketchup over the sugar
4. in a mixing bowl , mix thoroughly all remaining ingredients and shape into a loaf
5. place on top of the ketchup
6. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until juices are clear
demonstrations.review: This was my third time making this meatloaf.  I absolutely love this recipe!  I didn't have any ketchup, so I used brown sugar barbecue sauce in it's place.  I also substituted Ritz crackers for the saltines.  I have problems digesting black pepper, so I used cayenne and added a bit more for some zing.  Also added 3 cloves chopped garlic.  It was excellent and the only way I'll make meatloaf since trying it the first time. :)

target.recipe_text:
michael symon s homemade pizza sauce

this recipe is from the chew.  posting it for safe keeping.

1. combine the drained tomatoes , garlic , and dried herbs in a blender or food processor
2. pulse until the desired consistency
3. i like to leave this one a little bit course
4. pour into a bowl and season with salt and pepper
5. this is a raw pizza sauce , meant to be cooked on the pizza
target.review: Super easy pizza sauce!  You can't beat throwing a few ingredients into a blender and having a flavorful sauce ready to go in no time.  This has lots of flavor and tastes great.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
party roll ups   an american  an englishman  and an italian

cold cuts and cream cheese are a staple in our refrigerator, so when i'm not in the mood for bread, i like to make these 

1. for each roll-up , spread the cream cheese as evenly as possible across the slice of meat
2. then spread or sprinkle the other filling on top
3. roll it up
4. make as many as you want
5. eat or serve as is or cut on the horizontal into pinwheels
6. optional: garnish with toothpicks securing a cranberry for each american , a dried apricot for each englishman , and an olive for each italian
7. feel free to add additional seasonings: some like the american with a little mayo in it , some like the englishman with a touch of dijon mustard , and some like the italian with garlic powder -- horseradish might go in there somewhere !
demonstrations.review: Fun and delicious!  I have frequently made salami with cream cheese, so the fun twists and variety of this combo was a delightful addition to our appetizer table.  I used homemade cranberry sauce in the American and the option of the pepperoncini pepper for the Italian.  We loved the flavors.  Thanks for sharing!  PARTY '10

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scottish cream crowdie with raspberries

this is a name that isn't really known on these shores, although there may be a small group or two of people of scottish descent who use it. it is an anglicized version of an old gaelic (scottish) word for curd. a crowdie was a porridge (or pudding) and was usually eaten for breakfast. this version is one that was used on special occasions at harvest time. although a crowdie doesn't traditionally include fruit, it, like any breakfast cereal, is certainly lifted to another level when it is included. adapted from  king arthur flour.

1. toast the oatmeal in a 400f oven for 8 to 10 minutes
2. let cool
3. beat the cream until it is soft , not stiff
4. add and gently beat in the sugar and vanilla
5. fold in the cooled oatmeal and raspberries
6. put into a serving dish , cover and chill
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is a wonderful dish.  So delicious.  I followed the directions to a T this time around, but I can see that other berries would be great and look forward to trying them.  Thanks for sharing!  ZWT6

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek shrimp with rigatoni

if you love shrimp, tomatoes, & feta cheese, this one is for you. it is similar to others in the zaar database, but enough different that i think it is worth posting. it is from the local newspaper, the yellow newsprint a testiment to how many years it's been in my files.

1. preheat the oven to 400 degrees
2. heat 1 tablespoon oil in skillet , and add the garlic
3. cook briefly , stirring , then add the tomatoes
4. cook about one minute and add the salt , pepper , wine , basil , & oregano
5. cook over medium heat , about 10 minutes
6. sprinkle the shrimp with salt& pepper
7. heat the remaining 4 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet and add the shrimp
8. cook quickly for about 1 minute , just until the shrimp turns red
9. sprinkle with the red pepper flakes
10. spoon the shrimp& any pan juices into a small baking dish
11. sprinkle the shrimp with the crumbled feta cheese
12. spoon the tomato sauce over the shrimp& cheese
13. bake for 10 minutes
14. meanwhile , cook the rigatoni according to the directions on the package and drain
15. do not overcook
16. serve the rigatoni with the shrimp mixture spooned over it
demonstrations.review: Thanks for a delicious recipe!  I left the skins on the tomatoes and cooked the shrimp in the tomato mixture.  I also omitted the salt since feta has such a strong salty flavor already.  It made a lovely meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden pollo limone  lemon chicken

this recipe originally came from the olive garden website but i have changed a few of the steps after trial and error in my home chicken. we have a thing for lemony chicken in my house and this is one of the favorites.

1. pound chicken to 1 / 4 inch thickness
2. season chicken with salt and pepper
3. heat 1 teaspoon of the oil over high heat
4. lightly coat chicken with flour shaking off excess
5. cook in skillet until brown and nearly cooked through
6. remove chicken and reserve on the side
7. add 1 / 2 tsp oil to the skillet reducing heat to low
8. saute green onions and garlic until tender
9. deglaze the pan with broth and wine
10. add lemon juice and parsley
11. bring mixture to a boil over high heat
12. add lemon peel and salt and pepper to taste
13. return chicken to skillet and coat with sauce
14. cover skillet for 5 minutes over medium-low heat turning chicken once
15. plate the chicken and top with sauce and parsley for garnish
demonstrations.review: Thanks for a delicious recipe!  The chicken was so moist and the sauce had a wonderful, light lemon flavor.  I served it over pasta and with steamed broccoli.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blt creamy mac  n  cheese  rachael ray

a 30 minute meal from rachael ray.  a mac n cheese for grown-ups.  yum.  one of the reviewers on her website said that next time they may add a can of drained diced tomatoes to the top instead of the cherry tomatoes. . .just a thought!

1. preheat the oven to 500
2. bring a large pot of water to a boil , salt it , add the pasta and cook until al dente
3. drain , reserving 1 cup pasta cooking water
4. while the pasta is working , in a large skillet , heat a drizzle of evoo over medium-high heat
5. add the bacon and cook until crisp at the edges , 3 to 5 minutes
6. add the leeks and cook until softened , 3 minutes
7. add the garlic and crushed red pepper and cook , stirring , for 1 minute
8. stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute
9. stir in the cream cheese until melted
10. stir in half of the shredded cheese , then the reserved pasta cooking water
11. add the pasta to the sauce and toss
12. pile into a casserole and top with the tomatoes and remaining shredded cheese
13. bake until browned on top , 7 to 8 minutes
14. in a large bowl , toss the arugula and basil with the lemon juice and a drizzle of evoo
15. serve on top of the pasta
demonstrations.review: This is wonderful!  I used penne, low fat cream cheese, and the diced tomatoes on top.  Very filling and enjoyable.  Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
rhubarb sticky buns

my aunt used to grow tons of rhubarb and i wish i had it now, finding it these days isn't always easy. this recipe is very old, and you can use fresh or frozen rhubarb.

1. in a bowl , cut butter into brown sugar till crumbly
2. stir in rhubarb
3. spoon mixture evenly into 12 well greased muffin cups
4. set aside
5. in a mixer bowl , cream butter or margarine , and sugar
6. beat in egg
7. combine dry ingredients and add to creamed mixture alternately with cream
8. spoon batter over rhubarb filling cups about 3 / 4 full
9. bake 350 for 15-20 minutes
10. cool 5 minutes and invert onto serving tray
11. serve warm
target.review: These were so good, Im making a second batch right away!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best oatmeal cookies

this is a family favorite that i have been making for years. it's the most requested oatmeal cookie recipe i've ever made. i found it somewhere years ago, but have lost the source. the secret is soaking the raisins which makes all the difference.

1. this is a very important first step that makes the cookie: combine eggs , raisins and vanilla and let stand for one hour
2. cream together butter and sugars
3. add flour , salt , cinnamon and soda and mix well
4. blend in egg-raisin mixture , oatmeal , and chopped nuts
5. dough will be stiff
6. drop by heaping teaspoons onto ungreased cookie sheet , or roll into balls and flatten slightly
7. bake at 350 degrees for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned
demonstrations.review: very good! Im on a bit of a mission to get hubby to like rasins! this recipe is a help!!! I underbaked them a bit to get a shoft chewy cookie : )

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ryan s sandwich

a simple but good sandwich made by my student, ryan, for the sandwich making contest.

1. slice bread
2. cook bacon
3. place bacon on bread
4. place ham on bread
5. place turkey on bread
6. place cheese on bread
7. eat and enjoy
demonstrations.review: just had for lunch very good

demonstrations.recipe_text:
joan s pear tart

this is a delicious as well as impressive dessert to make for your guests. it always gets lots of oohs and ahhs when you serve it because of the pretty presentation. plus it tastes great! recipe given to me by my friend nancy and is from her stepmother joan.

1. beat the first 4 ingredients together until well blended and then add the pecans to the mixture and mix well
2. press into an 11 inch round tart pan
3. beat together the cream cheese , sugar , eggs and vanilla for the filling and pour over the crust
4. arrange the drained pear halves in a pretty design on top and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar
5. bake at 450 degrees for 10 minutes and then turn the heat down to 400 degrees and bake for an additional 25 minutes
6. remove side from tart pan to serve
7. serve warm and if desired garnish with whipped cream
demonstrations.review:
Very soft and fluffy. Easy to eat with braces! I put the pears in first then poured the custard on top. They came out very soft and full of flavour.
* Update I have made this twice since I got the recipe, It is VERY GOOD .We had friends over for a slice, they ended up taking the rest of the tart home with them they liked it so much : )

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one loaf white bread

tasty white bread.

1. mix the butter , sugar , and salt into the warm water
2. stir in 1 tablespoon flour and the yeast
3. wait 5 minutes
4. if yeast does not bubble buy new yeast
5. put flour in a large bowl
6. stir in yeast mix
7. stir thoroughly
8. turn onto a floured board and knead
9. knead in as much of the flour as possible to make a satiny dough
10. if dough is sticky add more flour a tablespoon at a time
11. put dough in a greased bowl and turn to coat
12. cover with a clean damp towel and let rise til double
13. punch down
14. shape into loaf and put in greased loaf pan
15. let rise
16. bake at 375 for 50 minutes or until bottom sounds hollow when thumped
17. can also be shaped into 12 dinner rolls or 8 hamburger buns
18. bake for less time if using these shapes
demonstrations.review: didnt turn out as a loaf (might have been yeast)so bought more and it made great buns!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white cake

this is a very moist and fluffy cake recipe that i got from my sister-in-law. it has never failed me yet. i have used it for different occasions and holidays and its always a big hit.

1. preheat oven to 375f degrees
2. mix butter& sugar until fluffy
3. add eggs& vanilla
4. add flour , little by little
5. add baking powder& salt
6. add milk , little by little until consistency is right
7. pour in a 9x13 or cupcake pan , lightly greased / sprayed& floured
8. bake for 30-33 minutes or until toothpick inserted into middle comes out clean
demonstrations.review: my swettie loves this cake its very moist !! and super easy

target.recipe_text:
basic icebox cookie dough

this is a nice basic cookie dough that you can expand upon as you wish. very versatile. *for variation, add chocolate chips, shredded coconut, toffee chips, whatever suits your taste buds!

1. in large bowl , combine the first 5 ingredients and beat well
2. stir in the next 3 ingredients , blend well
3. if using nuts , add them now
4. divide dough into 3 equal parts and shape each part into a 1 1 / 2" diameter roll
5. wrap the rolls in saran wrap and put in fridge until firm , at least 2 hours
6. at this point , you can do one of three things: bake , freeze , or refrigerate
7. to bake: cut dough into 1 / 4" slices and bake 1 inch apart on ungreased cookie sheet at 425f for 5-7 minutes , or until golden
8. remove immediately from sheets and cool completely
9. to refrigerate:leave in saran wrap and use within 2 weeks
10. to freeze: leave in saran wrap and use within 6 weeks
target.review: This was an ok recipie, not hard to make and the cookies turned out ok. They just didn't have that delicious factor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed plantains with leeks and fresh herbs

adapted from bon appetite magazine. plantains are those big bananas in the supermarket. often used in caribbean cooking. they are a starch and must be cooked before eating. in this recipe they are an alternative to mashed potatoes. the original recipe basically had more  butter and sour cream. increase those if you want a richer dish.

1. bring 7 cups water and broth to boil in heavy , large pot
2. add plantains
3. reduce heat to medium , cover and simmer until plantains are very tender and yellow-orange , about 20 minutes
4. drain , reserving 1 cup cooking liquid
5. cool plantains 10 minutes
6. remove peel using hands or small paring knife
7. transfer plantains to large glass bowl
8. add 1 / 2 cup of reserved cooking liquid and mash plantains until smooth , adding more liquid by tablespoonfuls to thin mixture , if desired
9. set aside
10. melt butter with olive oil in medium nonstick skillet over medium heat
11. add leek and saut until tender but not browned , about 6 minutes
12. stir in thyme and parsley
13. add leek mixture to mashed plantains
14. stir to blend
15. mix sour cream and cumin into hot plantains
16. season with salt and pepper
17. if using last tablespoon of butter , cut into small cubes
18. scatter butter and pecans over
19. serve
demonstrations.review: I didn't add the broth back in thanks to the other reviews and the recipe turned out well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of popeyes red beans   rice by todd wilbur

www.topsecretrecipes.com. this is a copycat recipe for my favorite fast-food side dish...unbelievably simple to make and quick enough to satisfy my regular cravings! this recipe is from todd wilbur's book more top secret recipes.

1. pour the beans with their liquid into a large saucepan
2. turn the heat to medium
3. add the pepper , paprika , butter and garlic powder
4. when the beans begin to boil , use a fork to mash some of them against the side of the pan
5. stir the mixture constantly
6. in about 20 minutes , the beans will reach the consistency of refried beans
7. prepare the rice , using the butter and garlic salt to season instead of per package directions
8. to serve , pour 1 / 2 cup of beans into a serving bowl and using an ice-cream scoop , scoop the same amount of rice on top of the beans
demonstrations.review:
Not hard to make, tastes awesome, it was a little more spicy than popeyes- but it was the best I've ever had! 
UMMM will be making again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sourdough  bread starter

this is your basic sour dough bread starter to be used over and over again. look for the sour dough bread recipe to make use of this starter.
there are two ways to make sour dough starter one without yeast where you feed the starter daily and this recipe where you just let the yeast do the work and  let it sit for 3 or 4 days. be sure that you clean the jar well before putting the saved starter back in it.

1. dissolve yeast in 1 / 2 cup warm water , rest for ten minutes
2. mix in flour , sugar& remaining water
3. allow to stand , loosely covered , in a warm place for 3 or 4 days
4. use a large bowl as it will rise considerably
5. every time the batter is used to make a product set aside 1 cup to be used as a"starter" for another batch
6. keep covered in the fridge
7. to make it into a basic batter again , add another 2 cups flour& 2 cups warm water and allow to stand at room temp overnight it is now ready to use , but again reserve a cup of the starter
demonstrations.review: The directions aren't complete as it don't tell you you need to feed it every couple days and such but the recipe does work.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked pears

this recipe is from the delforge place bed & breakfast in fredericksburg, texas.  use the best ripe pears you can find!   great as dessert or for christmas morning or anytime you want to do something special for your friends and family.

1. core pears but do not peel
2. place in greased 9" square pan
3. combine oats , sugar , spices and butter until crumbly
4. stuff pears letting excess fall into pan
5. pour 3 / 4 cup apple juice into pan
6. bake at 350 degrees for one hour , basting after 30 minutes
7. add more juice if necessary
8. cool 30 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: 5 stars don't even beging to describe it- these are the most wonderful pears I've ever had.. LOVE THEM. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
snickerdoodle biscotti

so yummy and quite healthy: 84 calories each, 1 g of fat. from cooking light's november 2000 issue (my favorite issue)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. measure flour into a large bowl using the scoop and level method
3. add 1 cup sugar , baking powder and salt
4. mix oil , vanilla and whole eggs in a small bowl , and add to the large bowl
5. turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead 7 or 8 times
6. divide in half
7. shape each portion into a roll about 8 inches long , and place them six or so inches apart on a cookie sheet lined with parchment
8. flatten each roll to 1 inch thick
9. combine the 2 tablespoons sugar and cinnamon , then gently brush the tops of the rolls with the egg white and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar
10. bake at 350 for 30 minutes
11. remove from the sheet and cool for 15 minutes
12. cut diagonally into 1 / 2 inch slices and lay them cut sides down on the cookie sheet again
13. reduce oven temp to 325 degrees f and then bake 10 more minutes , turn over and bake 10 more
14. they'll be soft in the middle but will harden as they cool
15. cool completely on a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Easy to make and tastes great!! The whole family loved it! Thanks

target.recipe_text:
indian lentil soup  dal shorva

an inexpensive, easy-to-make and delicious soup. this slightly modified recipe stems from mumtaz khan at mumtaz paan house in bradford, england. mung beans is the exquisite choice, but red or yellow lentils also make a delicious result (green lentils are not recommended). the chicken stock can be replaced with vegetable stock for a vegetarian variety. this recipe can also be made with less liquid and served as a stew.¨

improvement, a little off tradition, but works even better: 1) fry the lentils/beans for a few seconds in ghee before adding the spices and liquid. 2) add just a little tomato purée (1 tsp) to the soup. 3) add one diced potato together with the lentils/beans.

1. rinse the beans or lentils
2. bring to a boil with the stock , turmeric , cayenne , cumin , cardamom and curry / bay leaves
3. let simmer until the beans or lentils are very soft
4. if using bay leaves , remove them now
5. curry leaves can be left in the soup
6. run the soup quickly in a blender to a not too smooth consistency
7. sautee the garlic and mustard seeds lightly in the fat and add to the soup
8. let simmer for another 5 minutes
9. add salt , pepper and squeezed lemon to taste
10. serve hot with pita or paratha bread
target.review: This was very good!  I made the recipe pretty much as written.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
currant squares

i have two irish sisters inlaw and both say this is one of their favorite desserts.  especially when its make with home made flakey pastry

1. to make pastry:
2. freeze butter or margarine for half an hour before grating
3. sift flour and salt , then add butter or margarine
4. mix into flour with palette knife
5. add iced water until a dough is formed
6. wrap and chill in fridge for 30 minutes
7. put all filling ingredients into a saucepan and bring to boiling point
8. set aside to cool
9. preheat oven to 200c / 400f roll out half the pastry very thinly and line a swiss roll tin
10. pour on currant filling , spreading evenly , then cover with the rest of the pastry
11. glaze with egg or milk and bake for 30 minutes or until light gold in colour
12. dust with caster sugar and cut into squares when cool
13. makes 20 squares
demonstrations.review: I made this after picking lots of blackcurrants and needing to find recipes for them.  It was quite good, but I might reduce or leave out the lemon juice next time.  It was VERY tart and acidic.  Good overall, and I will try making it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breaded pollock fillets for 2

this is a nice baked fish. i enjoy making this with garlic mashed potatoes :-) (prep time does not include time to thaw frozen fillets)

1. if your fillets are frozen , thaw in advance
2. when your fillets are ready to prepare , preheat your oven to 350f degrees and lightly grease a shallow pan
3. melt your butter , and set aside
4. take a large plate and pour breadcrumbs on to plate
5. add spices to breadcrumbs and mix through with your fingers
6. add butter to breadcrumbs and mix through with fingers again
7. melt the other 1 / 2 teaspoon butter
8. take melted butter and lightly spread over the fillet and then roll fillet in breadcrumbs
9. pat breadcrumbs into both sides of the fillet over and over again until nicely coated
10. put fillets on pan and bake for 20 minutes , or until fish flakes nicely
11. enjoy alone or with your favorite sauces !
demonstrations.review: This made a nice, easy dinner.  It was a bit bland, I might spice up the breadcrumbs a little more next time!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slightly spicy  black bean burgers

this is a twist on recipe #111177. very good and cheap.

1. place beans in a large bowl and sit aside
2. heat oil in a large frying pan
3. add onion , garlic , corn and cumin
4. saut about 2-3 minutes over medium heat
5. add your green chili sauce and saut another minute or two
6. place in bowl with beans , let cool and mash with stick blender , it is okay if not every piece is mashed
7. add salsa , chili powder , flour and breadcrumbs
8. stir to blend ingredients with a rubber spatula
9. form in 4 patties and place on wax paper
10. store in tupperware until ready to cook
11. to cook , spray on one side and saut on medium heat until browned , repeat on other side
12. i serve these on toasted burger buns with pepperjack cheese , mayo , lettuce and tomato but serve it as you like
demonstrations.review: This is a new family favorite for us!  We eat the patties on whole grain bread with vegan mayonnaise, avocado, salsa, tomatoes, and alfalfa sprouts.  Yum!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kat s quiche  basic recipe

my sis is selling this at her restaurant for $4-$5 a slice. (hope she is not reading.) 4 ingredients...what a cheap, fast, and easy treat or brunch dish. hope you enjoy.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. sprinkle a small amount of cheese in the shell
3. beat eggs then add in the whipping cream
4. mix until incorporated
5. add remaining cheese and stir lightly
6. pour in frozen pie shell
7. bake 40-50 minutes until set
8. just be sure to lightly saute any fresh vegetables before adding
9. sprinkle filling into pie shell before adding eggs mixture
10. redistribute filling gently with rubber spatula
demonstrations.review: I made this with light cream and light cheese, broccoli, onion, and a small green pepper.  Nice!  This makes a good base for any kind of quiche you want to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
instant potato gnocchi

a quick and easy version of a robust italian winter dish. it's versatile - use these "dumplings" as a pasta or a foundation for the entree (maybe my smothered mushroom chicken? #113125). this recipe doubles or triples and works well with a simple tomato sauce, butter and sage, or with butter or good olive oil add a grind of black pepper and some parmesan cheese. for my smothered mushroom chicken recipe, this should be tripled.

1. put the potato flakes or buds in a medium-size bowl and add the boiling water
2. stir until blended then let cool
3. fold in the egg and salt with a wooden or plastic spoon or spatula
4. add flour slowly , folding with the spatula , until you have a fairly firm dough that doesn't stick to the bowl
5. turn dough out onto a well floured surface and knead lightly into a ball
6. you want just be able to work with the mixture without it sticking unduly- but too much flour will result in gnocchi that are more lead than light
7. cut dough in half and roll each half into a long cylinder about the thickness of your thumb
8. cut into bite-size pieces
9. you can dust lightly with flour or semolina and set aside for a few hours
10. to cook- put 6 to 8 gnocchi in a few quarts of boiling , salted water
11. as the gnocchi rise to the top of the pot , remove them with a slotted spoon and put them in a sieve over a plate to drain further until you are ready to serve
12. repeat until all are cooked
demonstrations.review: I had never made gnocchi before so I wasn't sure how this would turn out.  They were light and fluffy and delicious!

target.recipe_text:
my mama s meat sauce

this is probably the first thing that i ever learned to cook. my mother used to cook it while i took a nap as a child, and the smell would wake me up. it's really garlicky and the wine gives it a nice flavour. it also freezes really well. enjoy!

1. saut onions in oil
2. add beef and brown before stirring in all seasonings
3. add tomatoes , paste , and cloves
4. stir and add alcohol if using
5. cover and let cook on a low fire for 2 hours or more
target.review: This is a great recipe. It is easy to follow and tastes great. I added a few other ingredients to my sauce that were not listed. I added some red pepper flakes for a bit of heat, and I also sauted red, yellow and green peppers. I always freeze the extra sauce in portion sized containers and just reheat when needed. It makes a great 15 minute meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
light and spicy pumpkin pie tarts

these are so light and delicious, they give a new spin to traditional pumpkin pie!  these are great to bring to potlucks and parties.  they are a real eye catcher with a dollop of whipped cream on top.  the batter can also be poured into a 9 inch pie shell rather than the tart shells.

1. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients gently with a spatula
2. spoon batter into tart shells and place onto an ungreased cookie sheet
3. bake at 425 degrees for 15 minutes
4. then reduce heat to 350 degrees and bake for another 30 minutes
5. remove immediately from cookie sheet onto cooling racks
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Easily my favorite recipe that I have tried from recipezaar! I am Celiac and have not had pumpkin pie in two years until I tried this! I have made both tarts and pies with this recipe, and I've had compliments everytime I've made it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled lime chicken

nan

1. combine all ingredients except chicken in a shallow baking dish
2. add chicken , turning to coat
3. cover and marinate in refrigerator for 1 day
4. remove chicken from marinade , reserving marinade
5. coat grill rack with pam , place rack on grill over med-hot coals
6. place chicken on rack , and cook 5 minutes on each side or until done , basting with reserved marinade
demonstrations.review: I love lime, but I really did not enjoy this recipe at all. I found that the wine was just too much in this recipe. I would not make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: I converted these to a gluten free recipe by using an all-purpose celiac mix for flour, and they were fantastic. I used a little over a cup of marshmellows, and I am guessing that is why they were so moist (GF food isn't always moist). I will definitely make this recipe again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
penne with shrimp  asparagus   sun dried tomatoes

absolutely delicious and pretty quick! adapted from an epicurious.com recipe. quick and flavorful pasta that's special enough for company.

1. heat oil reserved from tomatoes in heavy large skillet over medium-high heat
2. add asparagus and saute until crisp-tender , about 5 minutes
3. using slotted spoon , transfer asparagus to bowl
4. add sundried tomatoes , shrimp , 1 / 4 cup basil , garlic , oregano , and crushed red pepper to same skillet and saute until shrimp are just opaque in center , about 3 minutes
5. transfer shrimp mixture to bowl with asparagus
6. add broth , wine and tomato paste to same skillet
7. boil until sauce thickens slightly , stirring occasionally , about 6 minutes
8. meanwhile , cook pasta until al dente
9. drain , return pasta to same pot
10. add shrimp mixture , sauce , remaining 1 / 4 cup basil and cheese to pasta
11. toss over medium heat until warmed through and sauce coats pasta
12. season with salt& pepper and serve
demonstrations.review: Very good flavour. I followed the recipe exactly and it turned out great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
loaded baked potato soup  gluten free

this soup is so easy to make and yet so delicious. you can very easily whip up a bowl for lunch or dinner when you are in a big hurry. leftovers of this soup reheat beautifully for lunch or dinner the next day. just save some of the toppings for sprinkling or spooning on the next day. i really love this soup. as a celiac i often eat soup for lunch. this is one of my favourite soups. i hope that you enjoy it as much as i do!

1. pierce potatoes
2. microwave on high for 5 minutes , turning over after 2 1 / 2 minutes
3. cut potatoes in chunks
4. combine potatoes , broth and milk in large microwaveable bowl
5. microwave on high for 6 minutes , stirring after 3 minutes
6. slightly crush potatoes with a potato masher
7. reserve 2 tablespoons each of bacon and cheese and 1 tablespoon of the onions for topping
8. set aside
9. add remaining bacon , cheese and onion to soup
10. serve topped with reserved bacon , cheese , onions , and sour cream
demonstrations.review: The ingredients were great together. I must say I didn't completely follow your directions. I ended up peeling and dicing the potatoes, and then boiling them in the chicken broth. I then scooped about 1/2 of the potatoes out and blended them with milk, added them back in with the broth and then continued as normal, but it was delicious! Tasted better the next day.

target.recipe_text:
amazing homemade pizza rolls

my dh loves those frozen tony's pizza rolls....i'll eat them too, but....what exactly is in them?? we probably don't want to even know! these are much better and at least we know what we're eating!! buy extra sauce for dipping if you'd like, but they really don't need it. also, add/omit any ingredients you like or don't like. make them to your own taste of course. this is what we like in them.

1. combine above ingredients except wrappers
2. place a cup filling in center of each egg roll
3. fold bottom corner over filling
4. fold sides toward center over filling
5. moisten remaining corner w / water and roll up tightly to seal
6. fry in 1 of 375 oil for 1-2 minutes til golden brown
7. serve with addition pizza sauce for dipping if desired
target.review: I WILL NEVER BUY STORE BOUGHT PIZZA ROLLS AGAIN! These were sooo good and ssooo easy.  Me and the kids made these over the weekend.  I was thinkin about baking them to cut out some of the fat....but I figured if we're gonna do it we better do it right. And we were so glad we did! Fried is the only way to make these.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one pan potatoes and pepper steak

i found this recipe a long time ago in a magazine in a laundry mat and tore it out. the page is so old and creased and faded that i can't hardly read it anymore. it is a delicious and easy one pan meal for a fast dinner.

1. partially cook potatoes in water , or microwave them
2. while potatoes are cooking , mix together the garlic powder and pepper
3. toss beef with the garlic mixture
4. heat oil in a large skillet over high heat
5. add beef and stir fry for 3 minutes
6. remove beef and add bell pepper to the pan
7. stir fry for 3 minutes
8. add partially cooked potatoes and saute 5 minutes
9. add beef and fry until heated through and meat is at desired doneness
10. season with salt
demonstrations.review: Pretty good dish. It was just  a little on the bland side so I added some garlic salt and onions. Over all is was very good and I will be making it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili s fajitas by todd wilbur

update: this recipe was created by todd wilbur for his cookbook "top secret restaurant recipes" (penguin random house 1997). www.topsecretrecipes.com. 

serve on flour tortillas with cheese, guacamole, sour cream, tomatoes, and lettuce.

1. combine the lime juice , water , oil , garlic , soy sauce , salt , liquid smoke , cayenne pepper , black pepper and either the sirloin or the chicken in a tupperware container , cover , and refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight
2. discard leftover marinade
3. grill meat over medium flame 4-5 minutes on each side
4. cut meat into thin strips
5. set aside and keep warm
6. combine the 2 tbls
7. water , soy sauce , lime juice , salt , pepper and olive oil
8. set aside
9. cook onion and peppers in oil until brown
10. remove from heat
11. pour reserved mixture over onions and peppers
12. combine meat , onions , and peppers
demonstrations.review: Very good! I used chicken instead of steak to cut down on the fat.  The marinade was very good but I think it would have been better if I would have marinated it over night like some others suggested.  The only mistake I made was not making enough veggie sauce.  There didnt seem to be enough to cover all the meat and veggies so it was just a little dry.  I also like a little more kick to my fajitas so I think I will add just a pinch of red pepper next time.  Over all very great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  The glaze was amazing!  The only thing I didn't care for was I am not much on bone-in meat....especially chicken.  Next time I think I will try thigh peices so keep the juciness of the dark meat.  This would probably be very good on chicken breat too but I dont think it would be as tender. Over all , AMAZING DISH!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel marshmallow apples

these sell well at bake sales....you will need 6 wooden craft sticks

1. wash apples and remove stems
2. insert sticks and set aside
3. place wax paper on a baking sheet and spray with non stick spray
4. combine caramels , marshmallows , and water in medium pan
5. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until caramels melt
6. remove from heat and cool slightly
7. dip in caramel mixture and place on prepared baking sheet
8. refrigerate till firm
9. can be drizzle with melted chocolate or rolled in chopped nuts , marshmallows , m&m's--use your imagination
10. i sometimes use candy corn at halloween
11. grandchildren love these
demonstrations.review: I LOVED the taste and texture of the caramel but it was just a little too thick for my taste. They were a big hit at our house last night with the family.  I dont know if it was something I did or if the marshmallows made them like this.  Next time I may try puttting less marshmallows.  This was also my first time making them so it could of very well been something on my end. All in all, very tastey!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot oniony pork chops with creamy mustard sauce

if you like onions, do try this crock pot dish. note that you will have a lot of sauce.

1. in a skillet , heat oil over medium-high heat and brown pork chops on both sides
2. place in bottom of slow cooker when browned
3. in same skillet , reduce heat to medium and saute onions until softened
4. add garlic , dry mustard , salt and pepper , and cayenne and cook , stirring , for 1 minute
5. add flour and cook , stirring , for 1 minute
6. add vinegar and wine and cook until thickened
7. pour this mixture over pork chops , put lid on crock pot and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours or on high for 2 to 2-1 / 2 hours , or just until pork is tender
8. remove pork chops from slow cooker and place on a warmed platter
9. stir dijon mustard and whipping cream into juices in slow cooker
10. when well combined , turn slow cooker off and pour sauce over chops on platter and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I am always look for a good crock pot recipe and this is def a great one! For some reason the first time I made it the onion mixtured turned out really thick so there wasnt much for the chops to absorbe but I made it again last night and it was perfect! I think the white wine is what makes it. Thanks Lennie!

target.recipe_text:
apple yum

i am not sure where i got this recipe, but i am glad i did find it, everones favorite. points 4.

1. combine raisins and amaretto in a bowl
2. microwave athigh 1 1 / 2 minutes
3. drain
4. combine raisins , apple , sugar , flour , and cinnamon in bowl
5. toss well and set aside
6. place 1 phyllo sheet on work surface
7. lightly coat with pam
8. add remaining sheets on top of each other
9. one at a time coating each with pam in between
10. cover with plastic wrap , press to seal sheets together , throw away plastic
11. spoon apple mixture along 1 long edge of phyllo leaving 2 inches all the way around
12. fold over the short edge to cover 2 to 3 inches of filling
13. starting at the long end , roll up like a jelly roll
14. do not try to roll tightly , the juices need time to expand
15. place sturdel , seam side down , on a jelly-roll coated pan sprayed with pam
16. cut small slits in top of the dough
17. bake at 350 for 35 minutes or until golden
18. serve warm with low fat ice cream or yogurt
target.review: I made this and took it to work.  It was a huge hit and everyone asked for either more--or the recipe.  I made it with 1/2 t almond flavoring since I am allergic to almonds.  I also didn't use the yogurt--which would've probably put it over the top!  Very easy to make.  I probably won't peel the apples next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal bake

perfect breakfast on the go or snack. for those of us on weight watchers, it's only 3 points for one big slice!

1. mix oatmael and powder
2. add remaining ingredients and mix well
3. pour into sprayed 9" pie pan or sprayed muffin tins
4. bake 45 min at 350f
demonstrations.review: This was very good and the pieces are huge.  The nutrition values shown don't match WW or FitDay.  I get 3 WW points, 173 cal, 2 g fat, 5 g fiber, and 9 g protein.  It is actually quite healthy.  I used Splends brown sugar blend and also dried berries in place of the raisins.  The recipe also lends itself to being cut in half.  I would definately make again using a variety of different dried fruit--like peach, mango, etc.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana nut bread
