this is an incredibly moist and tender banana nut bread.  the addition of the instant banana pudding gives it an extra banana "kick". i find baking it at a lower temperature avoids burning the edges.  my dh likes it for breakfast served under two eggs over easy.

1. preheat oven to 300
2. grease two 9 x 5 loaf pans
3. cream butter and sugar well
4. add buttermilk , eggs and vanilla and mix well
5. add instant pudding , salt , baking powder , baking soda , and cinnamon , mixing well
6. slowly add flour , one cup at a time , until well mixed
7. peel bananas , mash and add to mixture
8. add pecans and mix until blended
9. pour batter into prepared pans and bake for 1 hour and 10 minutes or until toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: This was a very good bread and easy to make.  I used butterscotch instant sugar free pudding, Splenda, light margaine, egg beaters, light soy milk, and a combination of pecans and walnuts.  I had enough to take it to a church social, the office, and give some to my cleaning person.  Everyone said this recipe is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple strudel baklava

i made up this recipe while wanting to use up phyllo dough and apples.  the result is a wonderfully fragrant apple dessert with a traditional baklava honey syrup poured over top.

1. mix together apples , brown sugar , lemon juice and zest and apple pie spice
2. set aside
3. brush 9x13 pan with butter
4. carefully unfold phyllo dough package
5. take one sheet , lay it in pan , brush with melted butter
6. repeat four more times
7. top with apple mixture and sprinkle chopped pecans on top
8. take the remaining five sheets of phyllo and place on top of apples / pecans , one at a time , brushing each with melted butter
9. brush top with melted butter and sprinkle with additional apple pie spice
10. with a very sharp knife , cut the top phyllo sheets into triangles
11. bake at 350 for 30-40 minutes
12. meanwhile , put sugar , honey and water in saucepan
13. over medium heat , bring to a boil while stirring
14. turn to low and keep warm
15. pour warm syrup over apple strudel
16. serve warm or cold
demonstrations.review: This took me longer than 15 min to prep--I guess I am slow on the apples.  I used dried lemon zest and made my own spice mix.  I also used butter flavored spray instead of the the butter as well as Spenda Blend for the brown sugar.  If I had sugar free honey (yes there is such a thing), I'd have used that.  This is really good.  I think I'd like a little more nuts in it next time, but it is a keeper.  I am taking it to church for our Sunday brunch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scottish eggs

this is a post in response to a request. i do remember my mom making these once though and think these would be a wonderful addition to a brunch or a scottish-themed meal!(prep/cook time does not include time to hard-cook eggs)

1. peel hard-cooked eggs
2. make sure the eggs are well-chilled so that the sausage meat will cling to them more easily
3. combine sausage , parsley , sage , and pepper in large bowl
4. mix well
5. press meat mixture evenly around eggs , keeping the oval shape
6. sprinkle eggs with flour , coating lightly all over
7. dip into beaten egg
8. then roll in bread crumbs to coat
9. pour oil into deep-fryer , or large heavy saucepan , to fill 1 / 2 full
10. heat to 350 on deep-fat frying thermometer
11. cook 1 egg at a time , for about 4-5 minutes until meat is well-browned
12. drain on paper towels
13. cool
14. refrigerate
15. slice to serve
demonstrations.review: I got a very similar recipe from a co-worker.  This is great if you are on a high protein, low carb diet and is very easy to make.  I made this with maple flavored sausage and omitted the spices.  I first divided the meat into 6 portions, so there was enough to cover all the eggs.  You can also dip them in crushed crackers or corn flakes for a crispier coating.  Since I like to be lower fat, I baked these at 350 for 45 minutes instead of deep frying.  To reheat, microwave for 30 seconds or less.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my stuffed bell peppers soup

i've had 'stuffed pepper soup' at different eating establishments...but we prefer mine.  we like spice and lots of bell peppers!!

1. in a large stock pot brown beef and onions
2. add peppers
3. cook approx 5-10 minutes
4. add all ingredients except cooked rice
5. simmer for 30 minutes on low
6. add rice and serve
demonstrations.review: This was very thick with an excellent flavor.  We liked it thick, but if you want soup, use 2 packages of onion soup and more water.

target.recipe_text:
hamburger and rice a roni

easy kids love it.

1. brown hamberger
2. drain grease
3. follow the directions on rice-a-roni
4. when you add the water mix in the hamberger
5. cover continue to cook at simmer 15-20 min or
6. until rice is tender
target.review: Thanks for this recipe! I needed something quick and easy and my kids a really picky! But they loved this meal and wanted more!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chilean salad

this salad is traditionally served with any type of grilled meats.
an excellent accompaniment to the main dish at your next barbecue.
from food and drink magazine.
hope you enjoy!

1. mix tomatoes , onion , salt and pepper together on a platter
2. combine oil and lemon juice and pour over salad
3. sprinkle with coriander leaves on top
demonstrations.review: This was great and very easy to prepare.  Even the kids enjoy it!! Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple no bake mountain bar cookies

it doesn't get any easier than these. kids love these!

1. mix first four ingredients in sauce pan
2. boil one minute
3. remove from heat
4. stir in oats
5. add remaining ingredients
6. drop onto wax paper and let cool
demonstrations.review: This was so easy to make and the kids raved over them for days!! It makes alot of cookies but never enough!! Thanks for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy peezy pizza dough  bread machine pizza dough

this is a really easy way to make a good "yeasty" pizza dough! as well as using this recipe for when i'm making pizza, i also use it for when i'm making a focaccia or a calzone. (the preparation time i have given includes the time it takes to make the dough in the machine and the time it takes for the pizza dough to proof - after removing it from the bread machine, 30 minutes.)

1. some pizza topping ideas
2. caramelised onions and roasted garlic
3. mozzarella cheese , camembert , romano and feta
4. equal parts of basil pesto and olive oil mixed together with parmesan or romano cheese
5. plus some roughly chopped sundried or semi-dried tomatoes , sliced black olives and lots of grated mozzarella cheese , salt and lost of freshly ground black pepper !
6. cranberry jelly , shredded chicken , sliced brie !
7. mozzarella cheese , shredded chicken and sliced avocado !
8. the bread
9. place all the above ingredients in the order i have listed into the bread machine
10. select the dough cycle and press start !
11. when the dough cycle is complete , take the dough out of the machine and place in well greased bowl , and roll the dough around thus 'coating' it in oil
12. cover and leave to rise in a warm place for about 1 / 2 an hour
13. knead the risen dough lightly
14. to shape and bake: roll the dough into a circle
15. place on well greased baking tray or pizza pan
16. then add a topping of your choice and bake at 225'c
demonstrations.review: This was great!! I had added 2tsp. of oregano to the dough and that made it extra yummy!! Thanks for posting it!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
egg drop soup  restaurant style

i came up with this recipe while searching for the perfect "egg drop soup". my picky 9 year old likes it, so i feel it is kid friendly.

1. reserve 3 / 4 cup of chicken broth , and pour the rest into a large saucepan
2. stir the salt , ginger and chives into the saucepan , and bring to a rolling boil
3. in a cup or small bowl , stir together the remaining broth and cornstarch until smooth
4. set aside
5. in a small bowl , whisk the eggs and egg yolk together using a fork
6. drizzle egg a little at a time from the fork into the boiling broth mixture
7. egg should cook immediately
8. once the eggs have been dropped , stir in the cornstarch mixture gradually until the soup is the desired consistency
demonstrations.review: Very good soup!! Everyone just loved it!! I'll be making this again:) Thanks for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker split pea soup

this split pea soup is almost as easy as opening a can, and twice as yummy. hope you enjoy it!

1. mix all ingredients except ham in 5 qt slow cooker , then add ham
2. cover and cook on low heat 8 to 10 hrs or on high heat 6 to 7 hours until peas are tender remove ham from cooker
3. place on cutting board
4. pull meat from bones , using 2 forks
5. discard bones and skin
6. stir ham into soup
7. stir well before serving
demonstrations.review: This was amazing! The flavour was excellent and the aroma was through out the house!! Mmmmmmmm!! Even the kids loved it! Thanks for posting

target.recipe_text:
irish beef stew with guinness stout

hearty beef stew for the irish-minded

1. heat a 6 quart stove top casserole or oven proof pot and add the oil and the bay leaves
2. cook the bay leaves for a moment and then add the meat
3. brown the meat on both sides on high heat
4. add the onion and cook for a few minutes until it is clear
5. reduce the heat to low and add the garlic , thyme , rosemary and flour and stir until smooth
6. add the beef stock and stout
7. simmer , stirring until the stew thickens a bit
8. add the remaining ingredients and cover
9. place the pot in the oven at 275 f: for about 2 hours , stirring a couple of times
10. check for the salt and pepper before serving
target.review: The house smells gorgeous. I found this recipe today in the midst of a Toronto snow storm. I had been making this stew for a number of years until I lost my recipe. What a delight to find your recipe on this very day! I add parsnips rather than carrots and add an entire can of Guinness as well as one small tin of beef broth. My original recipe called for fresh thyme and no rosemary. I add three stocks of thyme while it cooks and then add picked thyme leaves at the very end as well as the parsley. All in all a fantastic meal. I serve it with Perfect Traditionally English Roast Potatoes by Kellogs recipe number Recipe #109070. Absolutely lovely!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green beans with feta cheese

a wonderful greek style side dish that can be served hot or at room temperature.

1. saute onion and garlic in olive oil for a minute- be careful not to burn
2. add tomatoes , olives and oregano and simmer for about 5-8 minutes
3. add green beans and simmer for another 5 minutes
4. just before serving sprinkle feta cheese on top
5. these are delicious hot or cold
demonstrations.review: Fresh green beans in January are terrible so I bought frozen and then found your recipe...we just LOVED it. The addition of the feta produced a very rich tasting dish. I switched the oregano for basil simply because I had marinated chicken in oregano, lemon, and garlic before I found your recipe (and didn't want to go into oregano overdrive). Next time (and there will be many next times) I will use the oregano, it will definitely produce the requisite Greek flavour. Thank you for the marvelous recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
leftover beef enchiladas

great way to use left over roast. i usually put in a couple of chopped jalapeno peppers but it depends if you like it hot or not

1. saute the onion & garlic until the garlic is fragrent & the onion is soft
2. add the sweet peppers for a minute
3. remove from heat add beef and 1 / 2 cup taco sauce
4. spoon about 3 / 4 cup of the meat mixture down the middle of each tortilla
5. sprinkle with 1 tbsp of cheese
6. fold the tortilla sides up so they overlap slightly
7. place them side by side , seam side down , in a 11x7 baking dish
8. spoon the remaining taco sauce over them
9. spoon the sour cream in a line down the middle
10. sprinkle with the remaining cheese
11. bake in 350f degrees oven for about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wonderful, quick and different! We had a large leftover BBQ'd steak which I cubed. Followed your directions except for the addition of cumin to the onion/pepper medley. Purchased an excellent green salsa and added to the mixture. Poured a red salsa over the assembled batch and topped with fat free sour cream. Very filling indeed!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory pork chops

this one is for mustard lovers only.

1. in a bowl , combine the first 4 ingredients
2. dredge pork chops in flour mixture
3. in a skillet over medium heat , brown chops in oil on both sides , about 8 minutes
4. combine the sauce ingredients
5. pour over chops
6. cover , reduce heat , and simmer until meat is tender , about 20 to 30 minutes
7. spoon sauce over chops when serving
demonstrations.review: Mmm, mmm, mmm! I am a mustard freak so I actually added extra Dijon and ground mustard. I purchased a lovely boneless pork rib end which was at least two inches thick so it simmered for 40 minutes. The reduced sauce was just lovely however I found that it required salt to perk it up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect traditionally english roast potatoes

these are your standard traditional english roasties. imo there is an art to making these, at least the perfect golden crispy kind that i grew up with. the trick is to give 'em a good shake in a colander after par-boiling to rough up the edges of the potatoes. then once roasting; position spaced apart, turning only once or twice and basting in the hot oil every so often. if you don't manage the crispy texture (which you will, if you do the above!), they'll still taste excellent. you can't go wrong. i sometimes like to sprinkle rosemary/paprika/thyme or even a little garlic on top of mine for extra flavour.

1. peel and quarter potatoes
2. place in a saucepan with water and a pinch of the salt
3. bring to a boil and simmer them for 5-6 mins to slightly soften
4. meanwhile preheat your oven to 400f
5. when the potatoes have simmered drain them thoroughly in a colander shaking to roughen edges
6. let sit for a few mins to dry
7. pour just enough vegetable oil into a roasting pan to cover bottom and heat in oven for a few minutes
8. gently place potatoes into the hot oil and coat them with it evenly
9. sprinkle the salt and pepper over the potatoes
10. every so often baste the potatoes in the oil to prevent drying
11. turn potatoes once or twice halfway through to ensure even cooking
12. cook for 30-60 mins until gold and crispy
demonstrations.review: My Dad made these most Sundays with our roast. Absolutely lovely! Try them with a Guinness stew. Sublime....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
another mock mashed potatoes  mashed cauliflower  low carb

i saw this recipe made on the new low carb cooking show on food network. i tried the recipe tonight and it is really so good - this is my spin on the recipe. this time, i omitted the rosemary and used raw minced garlic, but you may also use a few cloves of roasted garlic if you prefer. this version is different from many others as there is no sour cream and no mayonnaise. real comfort without all that starch. (note: smart balance is a lower calorie, cholesterol reducing butter substitute).

1. bring a medium-large pot of water to boil
2. cut cauliflower into smaller pieces , add to the pot , and boil until fork tender , approximately 6 minutes
3. drain well
4. using a stick blender or potato masher , mash the cauliflower with the cream cheese , garlic , rosemary , parmesan cheese , butter , and bouillon powder
5. add some salt and pepper to taste- test and adjust seasonings as needed
demonstrations.review: I have made this dish a few times and realized I had not reviewed it. (blush!) As a follower of a low GI diet this is my potato fix. Yesterday I was lucky enough to find an outrageously mammoth cauliflower for 99 cents (it was the smallest of the bunch). I did not have cream cheese on hand so I substituted a cup of old white cheddar and a couple of glugs of half and half. I normally add rosemary but decided to try it with garlic and fresh thyme. The outcome was amazing. This recipe is so simple, versatile and wonderful. Two of us ate the entire pot. Oink, oink!

target.recipe_text:
white fish in herbed butter

frequently requested, easy to make.

1. mix all but fish in small bowl
2. heat skillet
3. add butter mixture
4. add fish and saute for about 6-7 minutes on each side
5. garnish with lemon wedges
target.review:
This was good and very easy! I did change it up a little though. I melted the butter with probably about 1/4 cup or maybe a slight more of white wine. Then I added some cut up steamed asparagus to the butter and wine combo. After slightly reducing, I added the fish. My Hubby really liked it and I did too! Since I didn't have any lemon, the white wine added that little tartness that the lemon would have.

I will surely be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jello cake

this is the moistest cake you will ever eat. i love it with strawberry jello and garnished with fresh strawberries. the cool whip makes such a pretty pure white and creamy frosting. it was my mom's favorite birthday cake. prep time is also chill time

1. prepare cake according to package instructions
2. allow to cool completely in pans
3. using a fork , poke holes all over the top of the cake through to the bottom
4. prepare jello according to package instructions except do not allow it to set yet
5. pour jello slowly over the entire surface of the cooled cakes
6. chill cakes until jello sets completely
7. to remove cakes from pans , set the pan in a dish of hot water for 1 minute
8. remove to a serving platter
9. frost with the cool whip
10. garnish with fruit pieces
11. keep any uneaten cake covered and chilled
demonstrations.review:
This was a hit at my Easter dinner!  My family loved it.  I used strawberry jello.  I accidently added too much jello, 6 ounce instead of 3 ounce, and I was so worried that I messed up the cake. To my suprise, it actually turned out great and I wouldn't make it any other way.
This was so yummy and I can't wait to make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
korean roast chicken thighs

not sure where i found this recipe, but make it monthly for my family. i have used vegetable oil in place of the sesame oil and it still tastes great.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. place chicken skin side down in a large baking dish
3. combine the remaining ingredients in a bowl and then pour on top of the chicken
4. bake uncovered for 45 minutes
5. turn the chicken over in the dish and bake for another 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: This recipe was pretty good. didn't blow me outta the water, but it was tastey.  thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops dijon

nan

1. trim excess fat from chops
2. spray a 10-inch skillet with nonstick spray coating
3. brown chops on both sides in hot skillet
4. remove chops
5. add onions
6. cook and stir over medium heat 3 minutes
7. push onions aside
8. return chops to skillet
9. combine mustard , dressing and pepper
10. spread over chops
11. cover
12. cook over medium-low heat 15 minutes or till meat is tender
demonstrations.review: I really liked this!  It had a really good flavor.  I didn't want to add any salt, but it was missing something so I added about a tablespoon of soy sauce and it really added a good flavor to it.  I didn't have Italian dressing so I used Wishbone Ramano basil vinigrette. So good! I caught myself spooning the left over sauce straight into my mouth. Yums!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade baked macaroni and cheese

this is a very easy recipe that my mom used to make when i was growing up-you can change the types of cheese to add a different flavor too. i like it spicy !

1. grease or spray with non-stick cooking spray a casserole dish
2. melt butter in medium saucepan
3. when melted , add flour , stirring constantly for about 1 minute
4. whisk in hot milk , cook for 3 minutes
5. add 1 cup each of the cheeses , and stir until smooth
6. cook macaroni , drain , rinse under cold water , and drain again
7. combine everything together and pour into casserole dish
8. sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top , and bake at 400ffor 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I'm not sure if I did something wrong, I followed the directions exactly, but it turned out quite grainy.  It wasn't creamy at all, and I used 1/2 a cup of extra cheese. I think it may have been the flour that caused the grainy texture.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gg s baked scallops

how can you go wrong with scallops, seasoned bread crumbs, i prefer italian croutons, crushed, garlic and fresh grated parmesan cheese.  ummmm

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. pour melted butter into a 2 quart oval casserole dish
3. distribute butter and scallops evenly inside the dish
4. combine the bread crumbs , onion and garlic powder , paprika , parsley , garlic and parmesan cheese
5. sprinkle this mixture over the scallops
6. bake in the oven until scallops are firm , and bread crumb mixture is lightly browned , about 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: I really liked this recipe, my hubby did not =(, that is why I gave it a 4 star.  I thought the recipe was quick, easy, and full of flavor.  I used panko bread crumbs because I didn't have regular seasoned bread crumbs and it turned out really good.  I'll be making this again, at least for myself ;)

target.recipe_text:
korean roast chicken thighs

not sure where i found this recipe, but make it monthly for my family. i have used vegetable oil in place of the sesame oil and it still tastes great.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. place chicken skin side down in a large baking dish
3. combine the remaining ingredients in a bowl and then pour on top of the chicken
4. bake uncovered for 45 minutes
5. turn the chicken over in the dish and bake for another 15 minutes
target.review: I've made this a few times - and finally time to review. One of my family's fave meals. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven crisp chicken wings

this is a very tasty way to make wings. you can dip them in your favorite sauce when baked or they are yummy as-is. recipe from cd kitchen on the internet.

1. cut wings at joints
2. preheat oven to 425 degrees
3. be sure wings are thawed and dry them well with paper towels
4. combine flour , paprika , garlic salt , black pepper and cayenne pepper in a plastic bag
5. shake to mix ingredients and add wings
6. line a large baking sheet with release foil and melt the butter on it
7. add wings to pan and turn to coat
8. bake for 30 minutes
9. turn wings over and bake for 15 more minutes or until crispy and done
demonstrations.review: GREAT wings! My crew loved these!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chocolate frosting icing

a wonderful frosting i have used for years made in very little time with perfect results and 100% better than any canned, this frosting is so good you will find yourself eating a fair amount of it before even using it to frost with! --- choose the amount of cocoa powder you desire for either a light, medium or dark frosting, and make certain to sift the cocoa powder and the confectioners sugar before using for the recipe--- this frosting *freezes* very well so double the recipe and freeze one batch for next time --- *note* for an ultra creamy fluffy milk chocolate frosting add in 1 to 1-1/2 cups thawed cool whip topping at the end of mixing the frosting and beat on low speed until blended ------- also see my recipe#80118 ---- recipe#282040 --- recipe#90142

1. cream the butter in a small bowl
2. blend in the cocoa powder , vanilla , confectioners sugar , alternately with the cream
3. beat with an electric mixer , until the desired texture is achieved
demonstrations.review: Delicious and so easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steak  or chicken  fajitas

these are so quick and tasty. you can use strips of boneless chicken breast instead of the beef. feel free to double the marinade. the flavor is so great for such a short marination time. you can can do them up ahead of time and have the meat sit longer if you wish.

1. slice steak into thin strips
2. in bowl , mix together 1 tablespoons olive oil , lime juice , garlic , chili powder , cumin , hot pepper flakes , black pepper & salt
3. add beef strips and stir to coat , set aside
4. wrap tortillas in foil and place in 350 oven for 5-10 minutes or until heated through
5. cut onions in half lengthwise and slice into strips , cut your peppers into strips
6. in large non stick skillet over medium high heat , heat remaining tablespoons of olive oil
7. add onions & peppers stirring for 3-4 minutes , until softened
8. transfer to a bowl and set aside
9. add beef to skillet , cook , stirring for 3-4 minutes or until they lose their red color
10. return onions and peppers to skillet
11. stir for about one minute
12. to serve , spoon a portion of the beef mixture down the centre of each tortilla , top with your desired toppings , fold bottom of tortilla up over filling , fold the sides in , overlapping
demonstrations.review: So delicious! Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian peasant soup

i found this in toh quick cooking magazine. i haven't tried it yet but it looks like something my family and i would love. plan on trying it soon.

1. in a large pot , cook sausage over medium heat until browned and no longer pink
2. drain
3. add onions and garlic
4. saute until tender
5. add chicken
6. saute and stir until no longer pink
7. add in the beans , broth , tomatoes , basil , and oregano
8. stir to mix
9. cook uncovered , for 10 minutes
10. add the spinach and heat just until wilted
11. serve with parmesan cheese sprinkled on top
demonstrations.review: Delicious! My husband says it's the best soup he's ever had.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken scaloppine with lemon glaze   low fat and delicious

this is a wonderful lower-fat restaurant-quality dish that is easy to make, i also like to add in a few tablespoons of capers and cook with the lemon glaze if you are a lover of capers then add them in as it really adds to the flavour of this dish ---  this lemon sauce is not a heavy creamy sauce which is what makes this dish lower in fat, it is more like a glaze that soaks into the chicken, and i would strongly suggest to double or even triple the glaze i most always do, and please be certain to use only dry breadcrumbs as fresh will not stick to the chicken as well --- this is *very* good!

1. in a small bowl or shallow dish whisk together mustard and eggs
2. set aside
3. combine the dry bread crumbs with poultry seasoning , garlic powder and seasoning salt
4. spread on a piece of waxed paper
5. dip the breasts firstly in egg / mustard mixture then coat well with the crumb mixture , pressing downs with hands to adhear the crumbs to the breast
6. heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat
7. add in the chicken and cook for about 5 minutes on each side , or until it is no longer pink inside
8. remove and transfer to a plate to keep warm
9. for the glaze
10. in the same skillet add in the broth , lemon juice and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt bring to a boil scraping any brown bits from the pan
11. add in lemon slices and parsley
12. mix to combine for about 1 minute
13. spoon the glaze / sauce over chicken
14. delicious !
demonstrations.review: So delicious! My family loved this (all of them - picky ones included!). Used panko as suggested and should definitely have made extra lemon sauce. We'll be having this again!

target.recipe_text:
brown sugar sauce

this is just another of the sauce recipes i wanted to keep in recipezaar file for faster finding! you can make this sauce in the microwave or saucepan

1. in a saucepan , combine the sugars , cornstarch , cinnamon , mace and salt
2. whisk in the water , then add the remaining ingredients
3. cook over medium heat , stirring until the mixture boils and thickens , about 4-5 minutes
4. serve hot over steamed puddings
5. microwave method , in an 8 cup glass measure , combine the sugars , cornstarch , cinnamon , mace and salt
6. whisk in the water , then the remaining ingredients
7. cover tightly with plastic wrap
8. microwave 3 minutes on high
9. whisk , and microwave 3 minutes longer
target.review: I use this alot to put on chocolate cake fresh from the oven even though I don't use the brandy. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot and spicy nuts  smoke house almonds

if you love smoke house almonds then you will love these! they are great for serving at holiday season or for get-togethers, or just to munch on at any time...better make lots these will go fast!

1. set oven to 350f
2. mix all ingredients except the nuts and kosher salt
3. mix well
4. add nuts
5. toss to coat
6. arrange on cookie sheet
7. bake until nuts are toasted
8. toss with kosher salt
9. store in an airtight container or freeze for up to 3 months
demonstrations.review: I wish I could give more than five stars because these are excellent!!!! Thanx for sharing kitten!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mc donald s secret sauce   c  1968 69

this recipe is from the 1968 mcdonald's manager's handbook put out in 1969 (1968 year) they quickly removed the recipe after realizing they had a very appealing "secret sauce." it was included as an emergency recipe in the event a particular store ran out of the pre-made sauce. enjoy!

1. mix everything very well in a small container
2. microwave 25 seconds , and stir well again
3. cover , and refrigerate at least 1 hour before using
4. makes about 1 cup -- enough for about 8 big macs !
demonstrations.review: Been making this for a while now. Very close to the real thing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s orange scones

source: "berries: a country garden cookbook"

1. preheat oven to 425
2. mix dry ingredients in cuisinart
3. add butter and process to cornmeal consistency
4. dump into bowl
5. whisk egg and cream together
6. add egg and cream mixture to flour and mix with fork until just blended
7. if it appears too dry , add a bit more cream
8. knead dough for 1 minute and roll to 8 x 14 inch rectangle on a floured board
9. brush dough with melted butter , sprinkle with sugar and zest
10. roll thge long side up jelly roll fashion , seal seam
11. with your hands , even up the roll and trim off the ends
12. cut into 4 even pieces
13. place cut side down on parchment lined sheet pan
14. press slightly to flatten
15. bake about 15 minutes or until golden
16. if bottoms brown too quickly , double-pan
17. the scones are done when you can just lift them off of the sheetpan without having them fall apart
18. serving ideas: serve with berries and whipped cream
demonstrations.review: These smelled great when they were in the oven. I think next time I might try adding brown sugar and cinnamon to the zest to make it more of a cinnamon bun type filling. This is a great recipe. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paula deen s ginger cookies

these are easy to make and taste very similar to ginger snaps.  yum!

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
2. line cookie sheets with parchment paper or nonstick baking mats
3. using an electric mixer at low speed , cream the shortening and sugar until thoroughly combined
4. add the egg and molasses and beat until completely incorporated
5. sift together the flour , baking soda , cinnamon , ginger , cloves and salt and add to the mixture
6. stir until combined
7. roll the dough into balls about 1-inch in diameter
8. roll the balls in sugar
9. place 1 / 2-inch apart on the prepared cookie sheets
10. flatten the balls slightly with your finger
11. bake for 8-12 minutes
12. cool on wire racks
demonstrations.review: so good!!! mom and I could eat a whole batch by ourselves! thanx for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kadju badun   sri lankan deviled cashews

i love the peppy-salty seasoning on this wonderful snack or party nibble, and i was pleasantly surprised to find that fried cashews are not greasy at all. i don't know if this is authentic to the recipe, but i also like to let the finished nuts cool just a bit then toss them in a bag with some garlic salt before serving.

1. combine the cashews , paprika , turmeric , salt and water together in a bowl and let stand for 1 hour
2. heat the vegetable oil in a skillet and fry the cashews until they're browned evenly
3. remove from the oil , drain on paper towels and let cool slightly
4. in a plastic zipper bag , combine the chili powder and garlic salt to taste
5. toss the nuts around in the mixture and serve
demonstrations.review: excellent treat for the family!  thanx  for posting.

target.recipe_text:
feta burgers with grilled red onions

from bon appetit, july, 2007.  these newfangled burgers are stuffed with feta cheese. pressing the center of the raw hamburger to form a slight indentation prevents the burger from puffing up in the center when cooking. here for safe keeping and sharing.

1. break up beef in large bowl
2. sprinkle feta , oregano , salt , and pepper over
3. toss
4. divide into 8 portions
5. form each into 4 1 / 2-inch burgers , pressing in center to form slight indentation
6. do ahead can be made 1 day ahead
7. cover
8. chill
9. puree garlic in processor
10. with machine running , gradually add 1 / 2 cup oil
11. process 30 seconds
12. do ahead can be made 1 day ahead
13. cover
14. chill
15. spray grill rack with nonstick spray
16. prepare barbecue
17. brush onion with 1 tablespoon oil
18. sprinkle with salt and pepper
19. place burgers and onions on grill
20. cover
21. cook 5 minutes
22. turn onions and burgers
23. cook until onions are charred in spots and burgers are medium-well , about 4 minutes longer
24. transfer to plate
25. brush cut sides of buns with garlic oil and place buns , cut side down , on grill
26. toast about 1 minute
27. turn buns
28. cook until heated , about 1 minute
29. place burgers on bun bottoms and top each with onion , tomato , and bun top
target.review: These were excellent!  We really enjoyed them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old stand by deviled eggs

this has become the perfect deviled egg recipe for our family - the only one we use.

1. cut the boiled eggs lengthwise and gently remove the yolks
2. mash the yolks with a fork , but do not pack
3. add remaining ingredients
4. replace the filling , back into the egg whites
5. you can do it with a spoon , or decoratively with a cake decorating / icing pump
6. sprinkle with extra paprika and garnish as desired with olives , pimentos , etc
demonstrations.review: I cut up some pickles instead of using relish cuz I can't get it here and I know that probably had to do with why I just "liked it."  Thanks for the recipe, I will try it again when I can get relish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the simple but perfect pancake

this recipe is from king arthur's all-purpose baking book and my family's current favorite recipe. they have a spongy texture and soak in the syrup.

1. beat the eggs , milk , and vanilla until light and foamy , about 3 minute at high speed of a mixer
2. stir in butter or oil
3. whisk the dry ingredients together and gently , but quickly , mix into the egg and milk mixture
4. let the batter relax while griddle is heating the batter will thicken upon resting
5. grease and preheat griddle
6. the griddle is ready if a drop of water will skitter across the surface , evaporating immediately
7. drop cupfuls of batter on the lightly greased griddle
8. cook on one side until bubbles begin to form and break , then turn the pancakes and cook the other side until brown
demonstrations.review: Awesome pancakes!  This is now the only recipe I use.  I even make it gluten free for my husband by adding rye and rice flour.  Very easy to make and I love the fact that the batter can be left over night!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican layered beef and bean casserole

this is delicious creamy ground beef, bean and corn mixture layered between crushed tortilla chips and cheddar cheese then topped off with more cheese, tomatoes and green onions, if you like extreme spice then add in some cayenne pepper and use spicy salsa as well as the jalapeno peppers :)

1. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
2. in a skillet over medium heat brown the ground beef with garlic , onion , green bell pepper and jalapenos drain fat then add in taco seasoning , salt and black pepper to taste
3. heat stirring for 1-2 minutes
4. transfer the mixture into a large mixing bowl
5. add in black beans , corn , sour cream and salsa
6. mix until well combined
7. spoon 1 / 3 of the ground beef mixture or enough to cover the bottom of the dish
8. arrange half of the crushed tortillas on top of the ground beef mixture , then sprinkle about 1 cup shredded cheese
9. spoon another 1 / 3 of meat mixture on top of the cheese
10. cover with remaining half of crushed chips then sprinkle with 1 cup shredded cheese
11. spread the final layer of meat mixture on top then sprinkle with 1 cup cheese
12. top the casserole with green onions and then chopped tomatoes
13. bake at 350 degrees for about 40 minutes
14. let sit for 15-20 minutes before slicing and serving
demonstrations.review: Very easy to make and everyone loved it!  Thanks so much!  We will make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country chicken and vegetables  crock pot

wonderful creamy chicken without heating up the kitchen. great to come home to.

1. cut chicken breasts in half crosswise
2. in crockpot , put potatoes , carrots and onions
3. top with the chicken
4. in small bowl , mix gravy mix with the next 5 ingredients until smooth
5. pour over chicken
6. cover and cook on low for 8 hours
7. remove chicken and vegetables
8. whisk sour cream into drippings
9. serve over chicken
demonstrations.review: I took this to a church function and everyone was asking me for the recipe! I cut the chicken up smaller so that it would go farther with all the people there. We had left overs that I froze and pulled out yesterday and my hubbie commented AGAIN how that I had made a hit with this one!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan zucchini

my husband dislikes zucchini, but even he gladly eats his servings of this at dinner!

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
2. clean the medium zucchinis well , cut the ends off , and slice them lengthwise into quarters so that you have eight pieces
3. coat the bottom of a baking dish with the olive oil and place the zucchini pieces in the dish
4. sprinkle with the seasoning salt , then with the parmesan cheese
5. place uncovered in the oven and bake for 20 minutes on 350 degrees f
6. serve two pieces to each person as a side dish , and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: My husband said these were to die for!  Very good, thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
country chuck roast with onion gravy

this was originally my great grandmother's recipe and was passed on to my grandmother. my memaw made this dish for many family get-togethers and always accompanied it with mounds of mashed potatoes, cole slaw and green beans, all fresh from her garden. the brown sugar is the magic that makes this roast utterly divine.

1. rub the salt , pepper , and brown sugar into all the sides of the roast
2. place the meat and the whole onion into an roasting pan
3. roast in a 450f oven for 15 minutes , flip the roast over and roast for an additional 15 minutes
4. whisk together the water , flour , 1 1 / 2 teaspoon salt and pepper
5. pour the flour mixture into the roasting pan and reduce the oven heat to 350f and roast for 2 hours or roast for 3 hours at 300f , flipping the roast over once at the midpoint of the cooking time
6. cover the pan if the meat looks like it is drying out
7. chop the onion into the gravy before serving
target.review: This was the best ever...change nothing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried southern style cinnamon honey chicken

while watching foodtv, i saw a piece about amy ruth's restaurant in new york where the owner made fried chicken dipped in a honey cinnamon mixture. it looked so good i began searching on the web for a recipe which approximated it... and after much browsing of webpages i put together a recipe that i thought might taste something like it. i don't fry my chicken, so here's a baked version, tweaked to my own tastes.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. spray a large roasting pan lightly with cooking spray
3. combine the flour with the salt , cinnamon , turmeric , black pepper , and a pinch nutmeg
4. coat the chicken pieces well with the flour mixture
5. beat together the egg and milk
6. dredge the flour-coated chicken pieces in the egg mixture , then into the breadcrumbs
7. arrange pieces skin side up in the sprayed roasting pan , making sure that the pieces are not touching each other to ensure they bake crispy
8. spray chicken pieces with oil spray or sprinkle with 2 tablespoons oil and place the chicken in the oven to bake
9. while the chicken is baking , in a saucepan over medium low heat combine the butter , honey , pinches of cinnamon , and lemon juice
10. after the chicken has baked for 25 minutes , pour the butter and honey mixture generously over the pieces
11. bake for an additional 15 minutes or until the juices run clear and the chicken is crisp and brown
demonstrations.review: My whole family loved this chicken...ages 5 and up. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wonderful curried sweet potato soup

this is a wonderful soup. and look at the list, just a few ingredients! i came up with lots of great ideas for the contest, but when i asked my friends what they liked best, they always mentioned this humble soup! how funny is that? the rum really makes a difference. it is added at the very end, so if you have kids at the table and you're worried about it, just serve them first and add the rum later. you may want to leave it out altogether, but just let me tell you one more time that the rum is a lovely addition. i use patak's curry paste which is available in asian stores where i live. madras is labelled as a hot paste and korma as mild. i've also tried a patak's paste called hot/tres epice which i do not recommend.

1. soup:
2. in a soup pot , heat oil over medium-low heat
3. add curry paste and onions and cook for 4 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. reduce heat if necessary
5. add garlic clove and ginger and cook for another 1-2 minutes
6. add sweet potatoes and pepper
7. mix
8. add stock
9. cook for 15 minutes or until vegetables are very soft
10. puree the ingredients in batches in a blender or puree the whole amount directly in the pot with a hand blender
11. check if you like the consistency of the soup
12. add more stock or water if desired and adjust the seasonings
13. you can add more curry paste if desired , but most pastes need to be cooked first before adding to a dish
14. add rum if using
15. serve:
16. serve in individual bowls and top each with a tablespoon of sour cream and a sprinkle of sweet paprika
demonstrations.review: My husband just loved this soup. I really like it to but it was a little to pudding like for me....but did have great flavor. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sauteed swiss chard

swiss chard is not a common veggie in most of north america. it is very rich in iron.some people say you need to acquire a taste for it. it is rather like strong cabbage. very low calorie

1. swiss chard should be chopped into pieces about 2" square
2. heat oil in a wok or skillet
3. saute garlic for about 1 minute
4. have high heat and saute the swiss chard for about2-3 minutes
5. toss until just wilted and getting soft
6. season with pepper and serve
demonstrations.review: We tried this dish and maybe I did something wrong but out of 6 only one liked it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scallops on asparagus spears with wine reduction

this is a perfect light dish for spring or summer.  i used bay scallops and reduced the cooking time to 2 minutes per side.  an easy way to season the scallops is to put them in a plastic bag along with the coating mixture, and just shake the bag a few times.  if you need the old bay, dib's recipe #15562 is good.  this recipe's source is mccormick.

1. cook asparagus in boiling water in a large skillet 3 minutes or until crisp tender
2. drain on paper towels and set aside
3. keep warm
4. combine flour , old bay , and paprika in a shallow pan
5. stir to blend thoroughly
6. add scallops and coat with flour mixture
7. dry skillet with a paper towel , and place over medium-high heat until hot
8. add 2 tablespoons of butter
9. when butter is melted , add scallops and cook 4 minutes , turn and cook 4 minutes longer or until opaque in center
10. top asparagus with scallops and cover to keep warm
11. add wine and dill weed to pan residue
12. bring to a boil and cook 1-2 minutes or until liquid measures about 1 / 3 cup
13. remove from heat
14. stir in remaining 1 tablespoon butter and stir until completely melted
15. pour sauce evenly over scallops
16. garnish with lemon wedges , if desired
demonstrations.review: My family loves asparagus but they did not like this at all. Sorry. As far as everything else it was great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: The best, easy and tasty, whole family loved it.

target.recipe_text:
apple or pear cake

absolutely the most delicious, moist cake ever with a decadent topping. very simple to make, my family just loves this!

1. cake:
2. mix all cake ingredients by hand in order given
3. pour in a greased 9 x 13 inch pan or springform pan
4. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes and remove
5. topping:
6. in saucepan mix all ingredients and bring to a slow boil for 3 minutes
7. pour over cake and return to oven for 4 minutes
target.review: This is SOOOOOOOOOOOO good...the very best, moistest apple cake you will ever taste. If I could I would give it 10 stars.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry rhubarb pie

an excellent pie to make when strawberries and rhubarb are at their peak. this delicious fruit-filled pie is a recipe from canadian living magazine, may 1993. you can substitute a plain top crust instead of the lattice top if you like; brush with the egg glaze and cut steam vents. tip: keep a clear plastic quilt ruler with your baking and cooking supplies to measure pastry strips for lattice pies, to measure squares or strips of dough, pastry, or pasta, or as a guide for cutting squares evenly.

1. in a bowl , combine rhubarb , strawberries , sugar , cornstarch , lemon juice and cinnamon
2. on lightly floured surface , roll out half of the pastry and line a nine-inch pie plate
3. spoon in filling
4. roll out pastry for top crust
5. using pastry wheel or knife , cut into 1-inch wide strips
6. brush pastry rim with some of the beaten egg
7. gently weave strips over the pie to form lattice
8. trim and flute the edge
9. brush lattice with beaten egg
10. sprinkle top with sugar if using
11. bake on a baking sheet with sides in a 425 degree fahrenheit oven for 15 minutes
12. reduce heat to 375 degrees fahrenheit and bake for 50 to 60 minutes longer or until rhubarb is tender , filling thickened , and the crust is golden
13. let stand for 15 to 20 minutes before cutting
demonstrations.review: Not too tart, not too sweet............absolute perfection. I sprinkled a good bit of coarse sugar on top of the egg washed crust before baking. I always do this for fruit pies because it just adds that little something extra and a little crunch to the crust.  Delicious!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: Soooooooooo Good.  As others have stated it took my cake almost 2 hours to bake but the results were worth it. I substituted coffee cream with a little lemon juice for the buttermilk because that's all I had and it turned out great.  Will be making this again. Update........since first making this cake I have made it many times. The last time I skipped the freezer part and it turned out just as moist and delicious.......just thought I'd let everyone know.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german cream of vegetable soup

hey, where's the cream? no, no cream here, only delicious healthy soup. this is a very healthy, low calorie soup. my family loves it. i serve it with thick slices of german bread.

1. bring the stock to simmer
2. the taste of the soup will be different depending on which stock you use
3. you can also use 2 quarts water + boullions
4. clean and slice the leek , white / light green part only
5. clean and chop the celery
6. peel the carrots and potatoes and dice them
7. put everything in the simmering stock
8. add salt , marjoram , oregano and basil
9. simmer for 1-1 / 2 hour
10. take out a big bowl to hold the soup while you use the blender to puree / liquify it
11. very important ! only fill the blender container half full and make sure the steam can escape on top
12. i usually hold a paper towel over the top to prevent splatter
13. you can also let the soup cool a bit before you puree / liquify it
14. put the pureed / liquified soup back in the pot and reheat
15. taste and add salt and pepper if needed
16. if you have fresh basil around , chop some and sprinkle over the soup
17. serve with delicious fresh bread
demonstrations.review: When I first made this soup, (using purchased Campbells vegetable stock), I thought "pretty good for a vegetable soup that tastes like Campbell's vegetable soup" (I did not puree it) Since I am not a big fan of that tomatoey kind of vegetable soup, I thought it was good but not something I would make again.  Then last night we had some for dinner and I threw in a generous handful of grated cheese (motzarella & parmesan mix) and lo and behold a whole new flavour, more reminicient of minestrone.  Next time I will add some kidney beans and maybe a little pasta and I will definitely add cheese.  Very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really good vegetarian meatloaf  really

high in fiber and protein, low in fat, easy and really yummy! i've always thought meatloaf looks and smells so delicious and savory so, as a vegetarian, i decided to make a no-meat version! this is basically our favorite meatloaf recipe but with cooked mashed lentils instead of ground meat. the result is a very tasty dinner!

1. add salt to water and boil in a saucepan
2. add lentils and simmer covered 25-30 minutes , until lentils are soft and most of water is evaporated
3. remove from fire
4. drain and partially mash lentils
5. scrape into mixing bowl and allow to cool slightly
6. stir in onion , oats and cheese until mixed
7. add egg , tomato sauce , garlic , basil , parsley , seasoning salt and pepper
8. mix well
9. spoon into loaf pan that has been generously sprayed with pam or well-greased
10. smooth top with back of spoon
11. bake at 350 degrees for 30- 45 minutes until top of loaf is dry , firm and golden brown
12. cool in pan on rack for about 10 minutes
13. run a sharp knife around edges of pan then turn out loaf onto serving platter
demonstrations.review: My vegetarian husband loves this loaf. I made this with two 10 oz cans of soy beans in tomatoe sauce in lieu of the lentils and added about 1/8 cup of ketchup in lieu of the tomatoe sauce. I also added about 1/4 cup of chopped green pepper to the mix. A winner....Thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
very low carb hamburger bun

i found this recipe on a low-carb forum when googling different low-carb websites--it sounds crazy, but the end result is amazing!  to quote the original post:

"this makes a wonderful hamburger bun, it tastes like a whole wheat bun. it's very sturdy and holds up well with all the juiciness of a hamburger with all the fixings."

note: you may need to add more ground flaxseed/flaxseed meal--the consistently of the "stuff" pre-microwaved should be thick and sort of pasty, like brownie batter, not liquidy.

1. mix all ingredients together in a microwave safe bowl or container
2. put the bowl / container in the microwave and nuke for 1 minute or until center is set
3. it will billow up in the bowl
4. leave it in the bowl for another minute then turn it out on a cooling rack and let it cool
5. once it has cooled take a long bread knife and slice the bun in half and make your hamburger as usual
demonstrations.review: I tried this recipe and could not believe the texture....just like grainy bread. It tasted just like bread too. I sliced mine into four circles and made little ham and cheese sandwiches with a tiny bit of grainy mustard. Delicious. My only problem is that as good as it tasted, I'm concerned with the fat content..........I could almost feel my arteries getting plugged up....figuratively of course. There is another low carb bun on this site which only calls for two tsp of olive oil. I will try that one next and hopefully it will taste as good with less saturated fat. I am giving this recipe 4 starts for taste minus 1 for the high fat content.

target.recipe_text:
the most incredible chicken spaghetti

from a local community cookbook; family favorite,

1. in a large dutch oven , fill 1 / 2 full with water
2. add salt and pepper if desired
3. add chicken breast halves
4. bring to a boil
5. cover and reduce heat
6. simmer 1 hour or until chicken breasts are done
7. remove chicken breasts , reserving broth , and allow chicken to cool
8. chop chicken meat into bite-size pieces and set aside
9. return chicken broth to a boil
10. add spaghetti noodles and cook until desired doneness
11. drain and set aside
12. saute onion and green pepper in butter until tender
13. combine onion mixture , cream of chicken soup , mushrooms , and cheeses
14. mix well
15. add spaghetti and chopped chicken
16. mix well
17. pour into a lightly greased 13x9 inch baking dish
18. bake at 375 degrees for 45 minutes
target.review: We loved this recipe!  I have made it before but wanted to try this recipe.  I used a can of cream of mushroom soup and also added some of the broth before baking so it would not be dry.  It was delicious!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sea bass on a bed of swiss chard and browned rosemary potatoes

pan seared chilean sea bass arranged on a bed of wilted garlic swiss chard (or spinach) with browned crisp potatoes arranged around it and teased with a garnish of sweet diced sun dried tomatoes. do i need to say more?

1. preheat oven for 375 degrees
2. lightly season the fish with salt and pepper , then coat with flour , shaking off the excess
3. heat two tablespoons oil in a skillet over medium-high heat , add the fish pieces and cook just until lightly browned , about 1 minute on each side
4. transfer to a casserole dish and place in oven for 10-15 minutes
5. add the onion and 3 cloves garlic to the skillet and cook , stirring , until beginning to soften , 1 to 2 minutes
6. slice pre boiled potatoes and add to the onions browning on both sides add rosemary , salt and pepper
7. meanwhile heat 2 tablespoons rosemary oil and toss in 3 minced cloves of garlic till almost browned add the swiss chard till wilted about 3 minutes , season with salt and pepper
8. place wilted chard on platter place cooked fish on top
9. arrange browned potatoes around the swiss chard
10. sprinkle with diced sun dried tomatoes
11. garnish with fresh rosemary
demonstrations.review: We really loved this delicious recipe!  Our filets were done in about 12 minutes.  It has a lovely presentation and was really good.  I followed the recipe as is.  I will probably use spinach next time, just a personal preference.  Thanks for the new addition to my favorites!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jewish penicillin  judy s chicken with matzoh

this recipe was given to my mil by her great grandmother, who immigrated from poland. i swear this soup has magical powers, as it has nursed my husband to health from countless colds, flus, and even a total hip replacement!! this also freezes very well, so make in advance of flu season!

1. in large stew pot , add all soup ingredients
2. cover with water , top pot with lid and simmer until chicken falls off bone
3. remove celery and onion
4. bone chicken and reserve
5. add matzoh dough to simmering broth , cooking until done
6. add chicken to broth: serve hot
7. matzohball directions: mix fat and eggs together
8. add matzoh meal and salt
9. when well blended , add soup stock / water
10. cover bowl and place in refrigerator 20 minutes
11. into simmering soup , drop matzoh mixture by tablespoons
12. they will form balls and float to the top
13. cover pot and cook about 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: This a beautifully simple recipe and so delicious!  I love that you shared where it came from.  I used thighs (what I had on hand) and my husband and 6 year old daughter each asked for seconds.  Now we don't have to look for a deli!  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with mushroom garlic sauce

this recipe is for garlic lovers.it is a quick easy meal when you are rushed and want some comfort food

1. in a skillet melt 2 tbsp butter
2. add garlic , allow to brown , then add mushrooms , basil , salt& pepper
3. cook until the mushrooms are just tender
4. add remaining butter and olive oil
5. stir and remove from heat
6. when pasta is cooked reheat the sauce add parsley
7. mix with pasta and enjoy
demonstrations.review: LOVED IT!!!!  I have made this many times and cannot believe that I forgot to rate it.  It is fabulous and one of my family's favorite dishes.  I followed the recipe as is and it is just great!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing chicken marinade

this recipe came from allrecipes (ruth crickmer). my whole family loved it even though it cooked too fast. the original recipe said 'high heat' on the grill, which my husband did. it ended up cooking 8 minutes total, charred but not burnt tasting, and very juicy and flavorful. we'll turn down the heat next time for texture, but this is a keeper in our home!

1. in a large , non-reactive container , whisk together ingredients beginning with cider vinegar through salt
2. then whisk in olive oil and pepper
3. place chicken in the mixture
4. cover and marinate chicken in the fridge 8 hours or overnight
5. remove chicken from marinade just before you turn on your grill or broiler to let come up a few degrees
6. discard marinade
7. lightly oil your grill or broiler pan
8. grill or broil about 10 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: We really loved this marinade.  I used what I had--rice vinegar, bottled lime and lemon juice and this mustard called "bone sucking" mustard (it is a spicy mustard with jalapenos in it).  I marinated for about 3 hours.  The result was delicious, juicy and tender chicken.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
luby s cafeteria beef liver and onions

this is a most requested recipe from the luby's cafeteria posted in response to a request. prep time includes soaking time.

1. soak liver in cold salted water for 15 to 20 minutes
2. in 10-inch skillet , melt butter over medium heat
3. add onion and cook , stirring occasionally , until tender and lightly browned
4. sprinkle with salt
5. keep warm
6. in a shallow bowl , whisk together milk and eggs until well blended
7. place bread crumbs in separate shallow bowl
8. rinse liver under cool running water
9. pat dry with paper towels
10. dip into milk mixture , then into bread crumbs , coating evenly
11. heat oil in large skillet over medium heat
12. add liver and cook 2 to 3 minutes on each side or until cooked through
13. top with onions
demonstrations.review: Thanks Miss Annie!  We love Luby's and their liver and onions is awesome!  My husband said it tasted JUST LIKE LUBY"S! The liver I bought was sliced a little thicker--I think that thinner is better--but it was great anyway.  Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
cajun garlic pork roast

a lovely cooking light recipe.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a small bowl mix the oregano , garlic , black pepper , seasoned salt , chili powder , cumin and red pepper together
3. rub evenly over roast
4. place on a broiler pan coated with cooking spray
5. bake for 1 1 / 2 hours or until a thermometer register 155-160f
6. let stand 10 minute before slicing
target.review: This was really good!  Was full of flavor and stayed moist.  However, I was afraid it would dry out so I loosely covered it with tin foil for about half the baking time.  I got a smaller roast (about one pound) because it's just my husband and I.  I served this with Spinach, apple and pecan salad #29765.  They went very, VERY well together!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach  apple and pecan salad

spinach, apples, red onion & pecans in a sweet-tart dressing.  to make this salad extra special, i like to glaze the pecans by stirring them with 1 tablespoon sugar in a medium non-stick frying pan over medium heat, stirring constantly until sugar melts.  pour them out on waxed paper and separate with your spoon while still warm.  if you do this, you don't need to toast the pecans.  it takes about 5 minutes or so for the sugar to melt.

1. in serving bowl , whisk oil , vinegar , mustard , sugar , salt and pepper until thick
2. add apple and onion
3. toss until apples and onions are covered with dressing
4. place spinach on top , then pecans
5. just before serving , toss
demonstrations.review: WOW!  If I could give this 10 stars I would!  We just absolutely loved this!!!  I followed the directions exactly and glazed the pecans in the skillet with sugar like you mentioned.  This is definitely going in my "make it again" cookbook!  Excellent!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crescent roll breakfast casserole

i got this recipe from having a pampered chef party and it was enclosed with my purchase of the deep dish baker.  i've made this many times and it's easy and quick and can even be made for supper.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. separate crescent dough into 2 large rectangles
3. place in an ungreased deep dish baker
4. press over the bottom and half way up the sides to form a crust
5. seal perforations
6. slice sausages and arrange over crust
7. sprinkle with cheese
8. combine the remaining ingredients and pour over the cheese
9. bake 20-25 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Made this on saturday for breakfast, we loved it!  I didn't have sausage so I just used bacon.  I just fried the bacon and crumbled it into bite size pieces.  Very good and simple.  Thanks for the recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one dish spicy chicken macaroni and cheese   or ham

looking for something new and different? tired of the same old thing? try this quick and easy stove top one dish meal that uses top quality  pantry items and staples and cooks in one pot! less dishes, less time, equals a happy mama! this is also great with some cooked ham rather than chicken! note: instead of the box mix you can use my homemade recipe for mac and cheese recipe #135662 also, when using a lot of pantry items you can up the taste and freshness level by adding some fresh ingredients like fresh parsley or other herbs, fresh cheese or even sneak in some fresh veggies like a little diced/minced  celery, bell pepper, garlic or onion. some green veggies like peas or broccoli would be a great addition here too! consider this recipe as a spark to light your creativity!

1. spray large skillet with cooking spray and saute chicken on medium-high heat for about 5 minute or until cooked through
2. drain liquid from tomatoes into a 2 cup liquid measuring cup and add enough hot water to measure 1-3 / 4 cups
3. add macaroni , tomatoes and the tomato liquid mixture to the pan and mix well
4. bring to boil and reduce heat to medium-low
5. cover and simmer 9 to 10 minute or until macaroni is tender
6. remove from heat and stir in cheese sauce from mac and cheese package and sour cream until well blended
7. sprinkle with shredded cheese on top and cover
8. let stand 1 to 2 minute or until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: This was just ok for me even though my husband really liked it.  I thought it was too cheesy.  I will definitely make this again but not add the shredded cheese at the end.  The cheese sauce that comes with the shells and cheese macaroni is cheesy enough.  Great way of spicing up the ol' macaroni though!  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
charlie s famous chicken salad with grapes

a really great guy i used to work with would make this and bring in to share. we all loved it so much and would beg for more! sounds strange with the grapes, but it's so good! allow time for salad to chill.

1. combine all ingredients
2. chill
3. serve with just about anything- crackers , chips , rolls , bread or bagel
demonstrations.review: I can't believe I never rated this!  I've made this about 3 times now and we all LOVE it!!!  I didn't change a thing.  Thanks for the awesome recipe Sherri35!  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pesto chicken

this recipe is simple, fancy and yummy.

1. cut a slit in the chicken breasts
2. mix the pesto , dijon and half of the mozzarella
3. stuff chicken breasts with half the mixture and spread the other half over the top
4. bake at 400 for 20-25 minutes
5. sprinkle remaining mozzarella over top of chicken breasts in last few minutes of cooking
demonstrations.review: I can't believe I forgot to review this!  This is an awesome recipe, I have made it several times now.  It is so easy to throw together after a long busy day.  I also thought that this was too mustardy so I cut the mustard in half now when I fix this.  Such an AMAZING taste!!!  Thanks for posting herby!

target.recipe_text:
braised lamb shanks

now there are just 2 of us, i'm going to cook shanks occasionally. they are way too expensive for a crowd. i found this on an australian abc site.

1. pre-heat oven to 160c
2. heat the oil in a big , heavy-based , oven-proof pan
3. brown the shanks well on all sides , remove , fry the garlic , onions and carrot until they are softened
4. add the tinned tomatoes and their juice to the pan , sit the shanks on top , then add the remaining ingredients
5. use enough stock to just barely cover the shanks
6. put the un-covered pan in the oven
7. braise for about 2 hours , checking it every 30 minutes or so
8. turn the shanks each time you check , and replace the liquid to bring it to half-way up the shanks
9. the shanks are done when the meat is beginning to fall of the bone
10. remove them and place on a warmed serving dish strain the liquid , pressing with a spoon to get all the juices out
11. skim and discard as much fat as you can , then reduce the remaining liquid to a nice gravy consistency
12. pour over the shanks and serve
target.review: This was extremely tasty.  After browning the shanks I added the remainder of the ingredients to the crock pot and cooked it for about 7 hours. Plenty left for freezing.  I forgot to rate this earlier and as the weather has turned cool today, I am having them for dinner tonight! Oh, and wine was GOOD!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
good every dang time seafood stuffed shells

giant pasta shells stuffed with a seafood cheese mixture. alfredo sauce is poured over all and baked to perfection! reheats nicely. we like it served with sourdough french bread (#111856)inexpensive enough to have on our regular menu but nice enough to serve at special occassions. enjoy!

1. boil giant pasta shells in salted water until they are pliable but not quite completely cooked
2. while they are cooking , you can make your sauce
3. melt butter in skillet
4. add garlic and saute for 3 minute being careful not to burn it
5. add the cream , milk , salt , lemon zest and bring to a boil
6. turn heat to low
7. wait 2-3 minutes and add cheeses
8. when cheese has melted , add the lemon juice
9. stir over med
10. heat for 2-3 minutes
11. make a slurry of water and cornstarch , mixing it well
12. add to the sauce and cont
13. to cook until it thickens nicely
14. be sure to keep an eye on it , and to stir it , because it will thicken quickly
15. don't overcook it or you will have a paste
16. it stays nice and creamy even when baked
17. drain your pasta shells and run under cold water until you can handle them
18. stuff with the cheese and seafood mixture
19. pour the sauce over all and bake 30 minute in a 350 degree oven
demonstrations.review: I was really disappointed with this recipe... it was rather bland and needed  more flavour.  I feel some herbs may lift it but worth experimenting with it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy parmesan chicken

someone posted this to a somersize recipe list i was on several years ago. it's perfect for level 1 somersizers, and tasty for everyone else, too!

1. brown chicken breasts over medium heat in a skillet with a little bit of olive oil , about 2 minutes per side
2. add remaining ingredients
3. cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes , or until chicken is cooked through
4. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner tonight.  Great taste for a minimum of fuss.  I added some garlic to the oil and used fresh sliced mushrooms as I had them on hand.   I did halve this recipe for the sauce as I only cooked 1 chicken breast.  So easy and a good recipe for dinner in a hurry..  So glad I tried this one... Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan seared veal chops with rosemary

this is a wonderful veal dish. it doesn't take very long to make.

1. rub the chops with 1 tbsp
2. oil , garlic , rosemary , salt and pepper and let sit on a plate for 15 minutes
3. heat a large cast iron skillet over medium high heat and add remaining oil
4. add chops to pan and cook until golden brown on one side , and flip
5. remove chops from pan to a baking dish , brown side down and roast at 375f
6. for 10 minutes
7. add wine and stock to cast iron pan and stir up brown bits from the bottom
8. serve chops with juice from pan
demonstrations.review: This was great!  First time I tried it, I used the red wine and mushrooms as one or two of the reviews suggested.  Was a winner here... Made it again tonight and used white wine and a little cream...  Red wine is definitely the winner....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled salmon with lime butter sauce

from the back of the salmon package. lime and butter beautifully highlight the flavor of grilled salmon. this sauce takes just 5 minutes to make and can be made a day ahead and chilled.

1. in a blender , puree the garlic , lime juice , salt and pepper until smooth
2. add melted butter and blend another 30 seconds
3. season salmon fillets all over with salt and pepper
4. grill over medium heat on lightly oiled grill rack 4 to 6 minutes i used the flavorwave oven
5. turn fillets over and grill until just cooked through , 4 to 6 minutes more
6. sprinkle fillets with lime zest and cilantro and then top with the lime butter sauce
demonstrations.review: This recipe was so good & easy.  The sauce was excellent with the lime & cilantro. I would recommend not substituting lemon juice as the lime just seems to lift the flavour & makes it taste so fresh.  I cooked this inside and it took about 6 mins.  I will definitely make this again & will add this to my dinner party list.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fantastic apricot chicken

the best apricot chicken recipe in the world. you will love it as much as everyone i know that has tasted it. yummy, yummy, yummy, yummy need i say more?

1. cut the chicken breasts into cubes
2. place the cornflour and pepper in a small plastic bag so that you can shake the cornflour onto the chicken pieces
3. start cooking your pasta so that it is ready when the chicken is
4. shake the cornflour onto the chicken pieces
5. place the oil into a frying pan and cook the chicken so that it is fully cooked
6. mix the french onion soup and apricot nectar together and add to the chicken in the frying pan
7. cook and stir for a couple of minutes
8. add the apricot halves and the juice from the apricot halves
9. stir continually and cook for a further 10-15 minutes so that the flavor can be absorbed by the chicken
10. serve
demonstrations.review: I made this with chicken drumsticks and cooked it a little longer without stirring it.  Otherwise I didn't change anything..  We really enjoyed this and quite enough left to freeze which was eaten a few days ago and husband said.... mmmm,, We will have that one again... I served it with homemade fried rice.  I already have chicken waiting to be cooked this way again..  A winner

target.recipe_text:
steak wine marinade

a super marinade for any steak. great not only in the summertime, but year-round.

1. in a heavy-duty plastic food bag , mix all ingredients well
2. place steak in marinade and seal bag tightly
3. place in refrigerator for at least 4 hours , inverting bag every hour
4. marinade can be used to baste steak while grilling
target.review: This was really great. I marinated some steaks for about 7 hours. I also added two garlic cloves and a tsp of minced ginger. Next time I would marinate overnight as this is a great tenderizer.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: Jan, I cooked this tonight and it turned out perfectly.  I followed the directions completely without changing a thing. I made sure I had the heat up to it's highest point and this resulted in a beautiful sticky silky dark glaze. I served this on a bed of jasmine rice with the glaze drizzled over.  Absolutely delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rissoles

this is an old classic aussie meal. when i was growing up, we always had rissoles and onion gravy at last once a week. give it a try and let me if you like this old favourite. cook time does not allow for cooking the gravy or the vegetables.

1. mix all the ingredients together , this is best done with your hands
2. shape into 4 or 6 round balls and dust with the flour
3. heat the oil on high in a heavy based frying pan until the oil is very hot
4. place the rissoles in the hot oil
5. don't over crowd your pan
6. make sure the rissoles do not burn
7. turn the rissoles over when one side is browned and slightly crispy
8. cook the other side the same way , turn the heat down to medium and cook through
9. depending on the thickness of the pan and the size of the rissoles , it may take about 3-4 minutes to cook the rissoles on each side
10. do not over cook the rissoles
11. the cooking time would be similar to cooking american hamburgers
12. serve with brown meat gravy and mashed potatoes with minted peas
demonstrations.review: I made these last weekend and they were absolutely delicious. I made them exactly as the recipe suggested. For the herbs I used thyme and parsley from my garden. These rissoles have a lovely savory flavour and they held together beautifully while cooking. I served them with onion gravy, mashed potatoes and corn on the cobb.  Everybody loved them and there were no leftovers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy sweet potato salad

refreshing and colorful, this novel combination is a tasty alternative to regular potato salad! prep time does not include chill time.

1. in a bowl , blend mayonnaise , buttermilk , lemon juice , mustard and sugar until smooth
