2. in a large bowl , combine sweet potatoes , peas , pepper and onions
3. pour dressing over all
4. toss to blend
5. chill 2 hours or overnight
6. to serve , spoon salad into a large bowl lined with spinach
7. top with bacon
demonstrations.review: I made this for Xmas lunch and not only did it taste delicious but looked really festive too with all the different colours. I roasted the sweet potatoes and although it was somewhat time consuming and more expensive than your regular potato salad I still highly recommend it. It was a huge hit here.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers baked chicken

this is another tasy way to prepare chicken that is good for you. this recipe is 3 points per serving. there is a total of 4 servings. you could also make this with white fish fillets or turkey cutlets in place of the chicken.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. coat a small , shallow roasting pan with cooking spray
3. season both sides of chicken with salt and pepper
4. transfer chicken to prepared pan and drizzle with oil
5. sprinkle with lemon juice , rosemary and parsley
6. pour broth around chicken to coat bottom of pan
7. bake until chicken is cooked through , about 30 to 35 minutes
8. garnish with fresh lemon and serve
9. yields 1 chicken breast half per serving
demonstrations.review: This was really simple to make and very delicious.  I also added some chopped garlic, it's packed with flavour and the herbs really stand out.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
magnificent 1st prize risotto

this recipe was part of what helped me win a cooking competition at school against 7 other people. i got it out of an excellent appetizer book and continue to make it!! excellent served with any meal. (vegetarians can substitute vegetable stock for chicken stock)

1. bring stock to a boil , then reduce to a low simmer
2. ladle a little stock into a small bowl
3. add the saffron threads and let infuse
4. melt 4 tablespoons of butter in a large sauce pan until foaming
5. add onions , stirring frequently , and cook for 2 minutes , then add garlic and cook for 1 more minute
6. cook only until softened , not brown
7. add the rice and stir until the grains start to swell and burst
8. then add a few ladles of stock , saffron liquid , and salt and pepper to taste
9. stir over low heat until liquid has beed absorbed
10. keep adding stock , letting the rice absorb the liquid before adding more
11. stir constantly test frequently just for the hell of it !
12. after about 20-25 minutes , the rice should be just tender and the risoto golden and creamy
13. take off heat and add 2 / 3 cup parmesan cheese and remaining 1 tablespoon butter , mixing until butter has melted
14. season to taste
15. transfer to serving plates and serve hot
16. sprinkle remaining parmesan cheese
17. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was a really delicious risotto. I used my homemade chicken stock and the infused saffron gave a wonderful subtle yet distinct flavour with a glorious colour. It's important not to skimp on the final step of adding butter and parmesan because it makes all the difference in the creaminess.  After that I put the lid back on and just let it sit untouched for 2 minutes before serving.  Fantastic, simple recipe, thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
chicken wellington  puff pastry wrapped chicken

this is not at all hard to put together, it's an amazing dish to serve to dinner guests and i have done so many times over the years and have always receive rave reviews from everyone at my table and you will too! --- to save time saute the onion, garlic and mushrooms up to a day ahead,  the cream cheese and dijon mustard mixture may be increased slightly -- i always serve this with recipe#149547 drizzled over or on the side of the plate, you will *love* this!

1. season the chicken breast with seasoning salt and pepper on all sides
2. heat butter and oil in a skillet
3. brown the breasts on all sides until almost completely cooked through
4. transfer to a plate
5. to the same skillet add in onions , garlic and sliced mushrooms
6. saute until the mushrooms lose their moisture and the onions are tender
7. stir in parsley
8. on a floured surface , roll out each puff pastry sheet to a 14-inch square
9. cut into four even 7-inch squares
10. place each breast over each puff pastry square
11. set oven to 375 degrees
12. in a small bowl combine the softened cream cheese with mustard , then spread over each breast
13. then top with about 2-3 tablespoons mushroom / onion mixture
14. brush the edges of each pastry square with water
15. wrap pastry around the chicken breast , pressing edges to seal tightly
16. place seam-side down on greased baking sheets
17. brush the tops with egg wash
18. bake for about 20 minutes , or until puffed and golden brown
19. serve with mushroom sauce over the wellington or on the side of the plate
20. delicious !
target.review:
I love this recipe!  I made this last night with rave reviews from all.  My DH hates mustard, so instead I mixed some basil, thyme and garlic powder into the cream cheese mixture.  We made it with the mushroom sauce and green beans.
It is a bit time consuming but I did everything at once versus some of it ahead of time.  Cooking the chicken or mushroom mixture ahead of time would make it come together faster.  Thank you for posting it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rustic italian bread abm

this is the one i make all the time.  i use the bread machine to make my dough and then bake in oven to get that rustic look. it rises nice and the crust and texture is great--give it a try.  prep time includes the total bread machine and rising time.


you can also make this in your kitchenaid mixer instead of the bread machine, using you kneading hook.  oil bowl cover let rise in a draft free spot.

1. add flour , oil , salt , sugar , yeast and water to your bread machine according to its instructions
2. set on dough setting
3. always follow your machines instructions , when mixing open it and keep check on the dough
4. dough should be in a nice round soft sticky to the touch ball
5. if it is not add more water , or add flour which ever is needed
6. remove when signal beeps and cycle is done
7. preheat oven to 375f
8. sprinkle cornflour or cornmeal onto a baking sheet
9. punch dough down and form into a long or oval loaf
10. cover and let rise for 25 more minutes
11. it should be doubled again by this time
12. uncover and slash the top with a sharp knife or razor
13. brush all over with the beaten egg white
14. bake 25 minutes to 35 minutes , until hollow sounding when tapped on bottom
15. cool
demonstrations.review: Excellent bread with great flavor and texture!  My DH raved as he loves bread that does not have a really hard exterior.  Earlier in the day I placed some olive oil in a ramekin with a smashed garlic clove, fresh rosemary and fresh thyme.  It was wonderful "dipping oil" for the bread.  I served the bread with salmon with balsamic glaze (Recipe #118010), asparagus and roasted baby potatoes (Recipe #133526).  One of the best meals I've made in a long time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple pecan dessert squares

one of my favorite desserts, doesn't last long at my house. if you like pecan pie, you are sure to like this!

1. heat oven to 350f degrees
2. stir together 1 cup flour , 1 / 2 cup melted butter , and 1 / 4 cup brown sugar until mixed well
3. pour into 8-inch square baking pan and press onto the bottom with fingers
4. bake for 5 minutes , then remove and set aside
5. turn oven up to 400f degrees
6. combine maple syrup and 2 / 3 cup brown sugar in saucepan , bring to a boil , then simmer for 5 minutes
7. cool to lukewarm and stir in butter until melted
8. stir in eggs
9. stir in pecans , vanilla , and flour until mixed well
10. pour mixture over partially baked crust
11. bake at 400f for 5 minutes , then reduce heat to 350f and continue baking another 20 minutes until the top bubbles
12. let cool
13. serve with whipped cream or ice cream if desired
demonstrations.review: Wonderful bar recipe that brought plenty of "oohs", "ahhs" and other happy taste bud noises! I toasted the pecans before adding them and refridgerated the bars overnight.  The cold really seemed to firm up the crust and make them much easier to get out of the pan.  Fabulous!  Thanks for sharing Terri!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seared salmon with balsamic glaze

i saw this on sara's secrets and couldn't wait to try it! the sauce brings out the sweetness in the fish. enjoy!

1. stir together balsamic vinegar , water , lemon juice , and brown sugar in a small bowl
2. pat salmon dry and season with salt and pepper
3. heat oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium high heat , not smoking
4. increase heat to high , add salmon skin side up , and sear until well browned , about 4 minutes
5. turn fish over and sear until just cooked through , 3 to 4 minutes more
6. transfer salmon to plates and carefully add vinegar mixture to skillet
7. simmer , stirring , until thickened and reduced to about 1 / 3 cup , about 2 minutes
8. spoon glaze over salmon
9. serve and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was a tasty and easy recipe.  I made it with roasted baby potatoes (Recipe #133526), broiled asparagus and rustic italian bread (Recipe #95086).  My DH raved.  The salmon took longer than 8 minutes to cook completely.  This recipe is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun seafood pasta

293 five star reviews caught my interest in this pasta dish when i was searching the net. shrimp and scallops in a cream sauce with parmesan and swiss served over your favourite pasta.

1. cook pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water until al dente
2. meanwhile , pour cream into large skillet
3. cook over med
4. heat , stirring constantly , until just boiling
5. reduce heat , add herbs , seasoning , and veg's
6. simmer 8 minutes , or until thickened
7. stir in seafood , cooking until shrimp is no longer transparent
8. stir in cheeses , blending well
9. drain pasta , top with seafood sauce
10. opt
11. you can make this hotter to suit your tastes by doubling the pepper and red pepper flakes
demonstrations.review:
I have been searching for a great creamy pasta sauce and now I need look no further!  This was fantastic!
I used 1 lb of shrimp, skipped the onions, used dried basil and a handful more of swiss.  Next time I may add some garlic but it is tough to think of much that could improve this recipe.  Thanks for sharing Chef Dee!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homestyle beef stroganoff

this is a real fast and easy way to make great stroganoff, the meat is very tender and delicous!

1. saut onion in olive oil until softened
2. add steak to the skillet and simmer meat covered for 30 minutes
3. remove 3 / 4 of the juice from steak
4. add red wine , cream of mushroom soup , salt and pepper and cover lid again
5. in separate pan saut mushrooms in butter , add parsley and paprika
6. when done add sauteed mushrooms to the steak and bring to a boil
7. add 4 tbls of sour cream to steak
8. serve over medium or wide egg noodles
demonstrations.review: Wonderfully full flavored recipe!  I followed as written except added some beef broth to the meat mixture before adding the sour cream to thin it out a bit.  I also used about 1 lb. of mushrooms since they cook down so much.  The meat was super tender!  Thanks for the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
peanut butter oatmeal no bake cookies

(no wheat / no egg) cookies in five minutes!  no wheat or egg so these are great for wheat or egg free diets.  a friend gave me the original recipe that called for white sugar and they were great that way.  i tried it with brown sugar and that is the only way i'll fix them now!  totally a new level.  only takes 10 minutes total to prepare these.

1. mix together the first three ingredients
2. set aside
3. stir together sugar , milk , and butter in medium saucepan
4. cook over medium heat stirring occasionally - full boil for one minute
5. immediately pour over oatmeal mixture and stir thoroughly but rapidly
6. spoon cookie size scoops onto waxed paper or plastic wrap and let set until firm
target.review: I just made them and the mixture didn't even hit the wax paper before I started eating it all up.  The brown sugar makes them very sweet, the peanut butter taste is just enough and these are really easy and very quick to make.  Love them and I know my kids would have too if it weren't for me hiding the rest so I can eat them later :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jelly bean cookies

a great easter treat (or any other time)! cookies baked with jelly beans in them. the kids, old and young will love this one.

1. mix butter and both sugars until smooth
2. stir in egg , baking soda , baking powder , salt and vanilla and mix well
3. stir in flour and oats until well blended
4. stir in jelly beans
5. drop by spoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet about 2" apart
6. bake at 375 degrees for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: It's a 5 star cookie for it being unique but I must say I was a little frustrated with how they stuck to the cookie sheet so I pulled out the silpat (if I even spelled that right) and that worked wonders.  Needless to say I think they'll be a big hit at the Easter party

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry chocolate chip bread

this is a really sweet bread. i made it to share with co-workers and to use up my extra cherries. it tastes great with a cup of coffee or tea.

you can put in up to a cup of chocolate chips, cherries or nuts; depending on your tastes. i generally use 1 cup of cherries and 3/4 cup of chocolate chips.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. soften butter , and cream with tightly packed brown sugar
3. stir in milk , eggs , and almond extract
4. in a seperate bowl , combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
5. add to milk mixture and stir until all ingredients are moistened
6. with a spoon , stir in chocolate , cherries , and nuts
7. add batter into a greased 9x5 baking pan
8. bake for 50-60 minutes , or until toothpick comes out clean
9. let cool before removing from pan
10. you may serve it warm , cold , or re-heated
11. store in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: Ohh not one of my favorites but regardless my husband and kids ate it right up.  I honestly didn't think it was that sweet at all, or not sweet enough.  The sweetness that was there came mostly from chocolate chips.  It baked well though and I was happy to see a sweet bread recipe using fresh cherries.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate chip cookies

i love these rich, very sweet, addictive cookies. i adapted this recipe from one i found and loved on allrecipes.com. i have altered it somewhat to suit my tastes and my preferred baking techniques but this is based on the recipe known there as aunt cora's world's best cookies. cook time is per batch, cooking one sheet at a time.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees f
2. have ready at least 2 baking sheets lined with parchment paper
3. cream butter until smooth
4. add peanut butter and both sugars and beat until combined well
5. add egg and beat well
6. stir in flour and baking soda gradually until well combined
7. stir in chocolate chips by hand
8. using a meatball scooper or a spoon , scoop out small portions of dough and drop onto parchment lined cookie sheets , leaving 2" gap between each cookie
9. bake for about 15 minutes or until cookies are just firm around the edges- don't overbake- if you wait until they are brown on top , they will be too hard
10. slide parchment sheet , cookies and all , carefully off pan and onto your counter , set a new piece of parchment paper onto your baking sheet and repeat until all dough is baked
11. meanwhile , as the next batch bakes , remove baked cookies from the parchment and let cool completely on wire racks
12. wipe off the crumbs from the old sheet of parchment and you can reuse it for your next batch
13. these will keep about 3 days stored in a cookie tin or an airtight plastic container
demonstrations.review: I knew it was a 5 star recipe when I couldn't stop eating the batter.  Easy to make and very flavorful.  Outstanding recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini coconut cobbler

here's one answer to the zucchini glut-taste's just like...............apple cobbler!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. grease a 9x13 inch pan and set aside
3. in a medium sauce pan add together the zucchini and lemon juice
4. cook over medium high heat for 15 minutes stirring often , or until zucchini is tender
5. add 3 / 4 cups sugar ,
6. 1 t
7. cinnamon ,
8. and the 1 / 2 t
9. nutmeg
10. simmer for 1 minute
11. remove from heat and set aside
12. in a large bowl combine the flour and 1&1 / 2 cups sugar
13. cut in the butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs
14. stir in the coconut
15. stir 1 / 2 of the coconut crumb mixture into the zucchini mixture
16. press half the remaining crumbs into the bottom of the prepared pan
17. spread the zucchini mixture on top of the bottom crust
18. add the remaining cinnamon and nutmeg to the remaining coconut topping and crumble on top of the zucchini mixture
19. bake for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown and bubbly
demonstrations.review: My 4yo is loving this!! Such a huge hit with us.  Great recipe for a Zucchini dessert.  Well worth the 5 stars

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker chuck roast barbecue

i found this in my southern living ultimate quick and easy cookbook and made it last night for the first time.  this one's definitely a "keeper," as my husband puts it.  even our notoriously picky 3 year old loved it, if that tells you anything!

1. chop onions and place in bottom of 4 quart slow cooker
2. trim all visible fat off of roast , cut in half to ensure even cooking , and place on top of onions
3. mix cola , worcestershire sauce , vinegar and minced garlic
4. reserve 1 / 2 cup for use later , and pour the rest over the meat
5. cover and cook on high for 6 hours or on low for 10 hours
6. when meat is done cooking and is very tender , remove meat and onions from the slow cooker with a slotted spoon
7. discard cooking liquid in slow cooker
8. add reserved sauce mixture and 1 / 2 cup bottled barbecue sauce to slow cooker and cook uncovered on high for 10 minutes
9. meanwhile , shred roast with two forks
10. when sauce is finished , return shredded beef and onions to slow cooker , stir well , cover , and cook until heated through--about 10 minutes on high
demonstrations.review: Oh Yum, this was a "keeper" in my house too.  My husband was surprised I pulled it off and my little kiddos too were eating it all up.  I must add though I used PORK ROAST instead and it came out very tasty.  The BBQ sauce complemented the meat well and wasn't overwhelming in taste.  The pork was very easy to shred and it tasted superb on hamburger buns

target.recipe_text:
ex mother in law s pork chops with cream of mushroom

this was the one good memory i have of my first marriage- going to my ex-mother-in-law's and smelling this cooking! of course, i begged for her recipe and have been making it regularly ever since. her son was not a keeper for me, but her pork chops sure were! this recipe may be halved by using 4 pork chops, one can of soup, and two tablespoons of butter with the lawry's seasoning.

1. in skillet with melted butter , sprinkle both sides of pork chops with seasoned salt and seasoned pepper to taste and brown
2. put into 9 x 13 inch glass casserole and spoon mushroom soup and smear all over pork chops
3. cover and seal tightly with heavy aluminum foil and put into pre-heated 350 degree oven for 1 hour
4. remove foil last few minutes
5. serve over rice or noodles
6. yummmmm !
target.review: This is so easy and so good.  I rarely make anything with 'Cream of Whatever' soup, but I was tired and wanted something really simple to make.  I had 3 chops for 3 people. Seasoned them with Lawry's and McCormick Grill Seasoning pepper mix and then browned them in butter with and bit of olive oil.  I sliced up some onion and put it on top of the chops in the baking pan before spreading out 1 can of fat-free cream of mushroom soup. Both Hubby and Son loved it as did I.  Thanks for the recipe, it is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: This is delicious.  Yesterday I boiled a whole chicken and picked the meat off today.  I saved the broth from cooking, skimmed off the fat, and used it for this recipe too.  I added some rubbed sage and fresh thyme, frozen peas, and used evaporated milk in place of half-and-half.  There was way too much to fit in to a normal pie pan, so I poured it in to a deep round baking dish and topped it with one pie crust.  Brushed the crust with an egg wash, sprinkled with sea salt and some garlic powder, and baked.  So good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick   i mean quick  herb rolls

i made these with just about any meal--very buttery-good! my grandmother's recipe.

1. melt butter in 9-inch cake pan
2. mix herbs and cheese together and stir into butter
3. let stand 10-15 minutes
4. cut biscuits into halves and swish around in herb butter to coat all sides
5. place into 9-inch cake pan
6. bake at 425f for 12-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: So good!  I couldn't find Hungry Jack so I used original flaky grands. Only 1/3 C. butter, parsley flakes, a pinch of dill, 1/4 tsp. of dried rosemary, and 2 tsp. on onion powder.  We will make this often to go with our weekly soup dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato slices made like potato skins

potatoes are sliced and baked, then topped with the makings of your favorite potato skins. serve as a side dish or even as appetizers. these are so yummy!

1. preheat oven to 400
2. brush both sides of potato slices with butter and place on an ungreased baking sheet
3. bake for 30 to 40 minutes or until lightly browned on both sides , turning once during baking
4. remove from oven and top with bacon , cheese and green onions
5. return to oven and bake until cheese melts
6. serve topped with a dollop of sour cream
demonstrations.review: Awesome!  I made these along with some other finger foods for New Year's Eve.  These were a big hit with hubby and son. I used only one potato and sliced, buttered, and browned the slices earlier today. I just stuck them back in the oven for less than 5 minutes with the cheese, bacon, and green onions on them.  So good...thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
incredible oven fried chicken

this recipe is the most flavorful home made fried chicken i have ever had. also great picnic food.

1. whisk buttermilk , oil , hot pepper sauce , mustard , garlic , 1 tsp salt and 1 / 2 teaspoon pepper in a large bowl
2. add the onion and then the chicken turning to coat each piece with the marinade
3. cover
4. chill at least three hours or up to one day turning the chicken occasionally
5. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , flour , thyme , paprika , cayenne and 1 tsp salt in a large baking dish
6. remove the chicken from the marinade and roll in the breadcrumb mixture
7. set chicken on a rack to dry for about 30 minutes
8. preheat oven to 400f degrees
9. place chicken in large baking dish and pour butter over the chicken
10. bake until crisp and brown , approximately 50 minutes
demonstrations.review: Just delicious!  I made only 4 big bone-in thighs and cut down the ingredients. I sliced the onion into 3 thick slices and soaked it with the chicken and then rolled it in the breading and baked it along with the chicken.  Kind of like onion rings...so good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: I made this again tonight with a few changes and it was very good.  I pounded the chicken and let it soak in low fat buttermilk for about 90 min.  Then, instead of butter I dipped the chicken in more buttermilk seasoned with garlic, garlic powder, seasoned salt, black pepper, and parsley flakes.  I used panko bread crumbs with Monterey jack cheese.  Yummy!

target.recipe_text:
tilapia tacos

this meal comes together in about a half hour total but when i am feeling especially lazy i will buy prepared mango/peach salsa at the store and use a package of prepared cole slaw mix plus the lime juice.  enjoy!

1. in a small bowl combine all salsa ingredients and toss gently
2. place in fridge for at least 15 minutes to allow flavors to combine
3. in a medium bowl combine cabbage , cilantro , mayonnaise , and lime juice
4. mix to combine
5. preheat oven to 450 degrees and spray a 13x9 baking dish with cooking spray
6. rinse and pat dry fish
7. cut into 3 / 4 inch pieces and lay in a single layer in baking dish
8. sprinkle with cumin , garlic and onion powder
9. bake for 10 minutes or until fish flakes with a fork
10. for each taco place a small amount of cheese on the bottom of shell , top with tilapia pieces , salsa , and cabbage mixture
target.review: This is excellent.  We dredged the tilapia in cornmeal and fried it, and bought the peach salsa.  The slaw is fabulous with this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana orange bread

the beauty of this recipe is its versatility.  experiment as you wish with the ingredients.  some people like raisins or currant in their loaves (i do not, but that should not stop anyone).  this recipe is a delicious, healthy version of an old standby, and one which the entire family can enjoy.  the following recipe has batter sufficient for one loaf; i have doubled the ingredients to create two loaves and bake them at the same time.  eat one, and freeze the other.  enjoy.   

important:  please note nut ingredients.  omit nuts if there are allergy implications. 

this recipe was originally created by tracy holly, general manager of the cory holly institute.  she writes for national magazines and is a lifestyle coach, lecturer and emcee.  tracy is a health and fitness activist and believes in natural medicine. tracy is the author of "the athlete's cookbook", teaches latin and ballroom dancing, and competes in masters' level ms fitness and natural body building.

tracy's recipe appears in the current issue of vista magazine; a canadian health publication.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. mix all the dry ingredients together in a large bowl
3. add all wet ingredients in a blender and mix for 15 seconds
4. add the blended ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix well
5. pour mixture into a well-greased bread pan and place on middle rack in preheated oven
6. bake for approximately 45 minutes
7. insert toothpick to test for doneness
8. cover the loaf with foil if it is starting to brown too quickly on top
9. let cool for 30 minutes and then enjoy
demonstrations.review: This is wonderful stuff, and totally guilt free.  I make mine in a bundt pan.  It's the only banana bread I ever make.  Just as good as the fattening kind.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon butter sauce for fish

this was the first way i learned to cook fish. my favorite fish for this is tilipia, but any white fish filets would work. it is perfect with rice and a green vegetable.

i found a website that has a picture of the knorr seasoning (it doesn't seem to have swiss in the name anymore). you can see a picture of it here:
http://www.germandeli.com/048001704022.html

1. melt the butter and add remaining sauce ingredients
2. pour sauce over tilapia filets
3. bake at 350f for 20-30 minutes
4. serve with rice
demonstrations.review: This was excellent.  I hate fish.  I ate the fish.  I had seconds.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingersnap gems

i think that these are just about the untimate ginger cookies. if you don't over bake them they will maintain a softness that is so toothsome. warning! these cookies are telepathic and will call to you from the cookie jar to come and get them.

1. in a bowl , stir together flour , baking powder , baking soda , cinnamon , cloves , ginger and salt
2. set aside
3. in a large mixing bowl , beat the 1 cup sugar and shortening with an electric mixer till well combined
4. beat in molasses
5. beat in the egg
6. add the flour mixture and beat till combined
7. shape the dough into 1-inch balls
8. roll balls in sugar and place 2 inches apart on an ungreased cookie sheet
9. bake in a 375 degree f oven for 8 to 10 minutes or till edges are set and tops are crackled
10. cool on a cookie sheet for 1 minute
11. transfer to wire racks to cool completely
12. makes about 45 cookies
demonstrations.review: These were great and easy to make.  Didn't have molasses, used a slight 1/4 cup of brown sugar instead.  Just a wonderful little cookie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean salad

i love creating salads and this is one of my latest discoveries. it has a lot of traditional mediterranean ingredients and is very healthy for you as well as colourful and easy to make. it serves two as a main dish or more if you're making it as a side to a bigger meal.

1. put half the olive oil in a frying pan and saut the sliced peppers for 3-5 minutes until the skins start to blister and the peppers soften
2. take off the heat and leave to cool slightly for a few minutes
3. meanwhile , put the chickpeas , artichoke hearts , avocado and tomatoes in a large bowl
4. when the peppers have cooled slightly , add them to the other ingredients in the bowl
5. sprinkle over the zaatar seasoning , or make a reasonable substitute by combining thyme , marjoram , and sesame seeds with a bit of salt
6. make the dressing by mixing up the other half of the olive oil and balsamic vinegar
7. pour the dressing over the salad and mix well
8. season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with the parsley
9. serve either at room temperature or chilled
10. if you are making this ahead of time , leave out the avocados until just before serving or they will discolour
11. you can also spice up this salad by using a chilli-infused olive oil
demonstrations.review: This is really, really good stuff.  I mean really good!  I didn't have the spice, so I used 1 tsp marjoram and thyme, 1 tbsp sesame.  I also replaced the avocado with an english cucumber.  Absolutely wonderful.  Served with spinach pie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb pizza

i got this delicious recipe from www.atkinsdietbulletboard.com the orginal chef is bikergoddess. we all thank her for creating this great recipe. it's not exactly like pizza, but it's pretty close. i like it alot. i've made it twice now, and will be making it over and over again.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. beat together cream cheese and eggs until smooth
3. add cream , parmesan , chives , italian seasoning and garlic
4. spray 9x13 pan with cooking spray or oil
5. place 2 cups mozzarella cheese in bottom of pan
6. pour egg mixture over cheese
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. remove from oven and spread sauce over baked mixture
9. add toppings of choice
10. cover with remaining mozzerella cheese
11. bake until bubbly and brown
12. let stand for 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: Marvelous.  The "crust" is not eggy at all.  We made a Green style pizza, absolutely wonderful.  Weird, but wonderful!

target.recipe_text:
raspberry filled almond shortbread with almond glaze

nan

1. in a medium mixing bowl
2. cream butter and sugar
3. mix in the almond extract
4. gradually mix in flour until the dough forms a ball
5. cover and refrigerate for an hour for easier handling
6. preheat oven to 350 degrees
7. roll into 1 1 / 2 inch balls and place on a ungreased cookie sheet
8. using a wooden spoon handle make and indention in the middle of the ball
9. fill with the raspberry jam
10. bake at 350 degrees for 14-18 minutes depending on your oven
11. add aditional raspberry jam if desired
12. remove and place on wire racks for cooling
13. mix the glaze ingredients
14. using a butter knife letting the glaze run off the butter knife , zig zag the mixture across the cookies creating a continuing z
target.review: Made these today, melt in your mouth shortbread consistency, nice almond flavour.  I didn't get 36 cookies, more like 28, perhaps made them too big, but they were delicious anyway.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome slow cooker pot roast

i found this on the all recipes site. this is a very easy recipe for a delicious pot roast. it makes its own gravy. it's designed especially for the working person who does not have time to cook all day, but it tastes like you did. you'll want the cut to be between 5 and 6 pounds.

1. in a slow cooker , mix cream of mushroom soup , dry onion soup mix and water
2. place pot roast in slow cooker and coat with soup mixture
3. cook on high setting for 3 to 4 hours , or on low setting for 8 to 9 hours
demonstrations.review: Took me a while to get to posting this recipe.  This recipe is easy and makes a tender roast.  I did not use the amount of water listed.  I cut that in half - it made a thicker gravy.  I used 1 can regular cream of mushroom and 1 can mushroom with garlic soup.  Very tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy one bowl vanilla cupcakes

this recipe goes back over 20 years, i like the simplicity of this recipe and for a one bowl cupcake they are pretty darn good, 1-1/2 teaspoons almond extract may be used in place of the vanilla, using butter in place of shortening will alter the texture it is best to only use shortening --- if you don't have paper liners grease the tins generously or see my recipe#78579

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large bowl , mix together the flour with sugar , baking powder and salt until combined
3. add in the shortening cream or milk , vanilla and eggs
4. beat on medium speed of an electric mixer scraping the bowl constantly until just blended
5. pour into paper-lined regular size muffin tins filling under just three-quarters full
6. bake for 20-22 minutes or until the cupcakes test done
7. immediately remove from pans
8. cool completely before frosting
demonstrations.review: They truly are wonderful!  I used your Buttercream Icing recipe (# 80118) to top them off.  Definitely a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornbread sausage stuffing

we eat this year round

1. in microwave or pan , brown sausage , casing removed
2. remove sausage to plate , add onion and celery , saute until soft
3. drain , add butter , melt , add veggies , cornbread , sausage , chicken broth , sage toast pecans , add to mix
4. preheat oven to 350f
5. bake covered 30-45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Used this for Thanksgiving dinner, was a hit, will definitely make again.  I used hot Italian sausage, removed the casings, and crumbled the meat.  I also added chopped jalepeno peppers for some more spice.....was delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tasty sangria

there's a cuban restaurant in atlanta that my wife and i love called mambo. after enjoying their sangria, i had to try to make it myself. this is a good approximation of their delicious libation. since you're going to pour juice and sugar into it, don't waste a good bottle of wine. buy the cheapest one you can find at the grocery store.

1. pour the bottle of wine into a pitcher
2. reserving one of the oranges , juice the other three oranges and all of the limes into the pitcher
3. stir the sugar into the wine / juice mixture until dissolved
4. peel the other orange and remove the pith
5. core the pear
6. you can peel the pear if you want , though it's not necessary
7. slice the orange and the pear into small , roughly 1 / 2 inch chunks
8. put them into a large ziploc bag
9. add the cinnamon and nutmeg to the pear and orange chunks in the bag
10. shake lightly to coat the fruit with the spices
11. empty the contents of the bag into the pitcher
12. stir
13. put the pitcher in the refrigerator for at least four hours , and up to overnight , to let the flavors marry and let the fruit become saturated with the liquid
14. taste and stir in more sugar if you feel you need to
15. serve over ice
demonstrations.review: Great - I used blood oranges, limes, lemons.  Easy and refreshing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chocolate frosting icing

a wonderful frosting i have used for years made in very little time with perfect results and 100% better than any canned, this frosting is so good you will find yourself eating a fair amount of it before even using it to frost with! --- choose the amount of cocoa powder you desire for either a light, medium or dark frosting, and make certain to sift the cocoa powder and the confectioners sugar before using for the recipe--- this frosting *freezes* very well so double the recipe and freeze one batch for next time --- *note* for an ultra creamy fluffy milk chocolate frosting add in 1 to 1-1/2 cups thawed cool whip topping at the end of mixing the frosting and beat on low speed until blended ------- also see my recipe#80118 ---- recipe#282040 --- recipe#90142

1. cream the butter in a small bowl
2. blend in the cocoa powder , vanilla , confectioners sugar , alternately with the cream
3. beat with an electric mixer , until the desired texture is achieved
demonstrations.review: Very smooth, chocolately!  I used 1/2 cup of cocoa.  I had to double the recipe to frost 24 cupcakes.

target.recipe_text:
wild game   moose sloppy joes

a recipe for wild game..

note: 
to freeze: cool. place in a freezer bag, seal, label and freeze. 
to serve: thaw in fridge overnight. reheat on stovetop until bubbly and serve.

1. brown moose and onion in skillet and drain
2. add other ingredients and simmer for 5 minutes
3. serve over buns or any other type of bread
4. you can also use venison / red deer hamburg in this recipe
target.review: This sure made the moose meat taste yummy...hubby thought it was on the sweet side...made for "What's on the Menu" tag game...=)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato bacon chowder

a satisfying comfort food that can be jazzed-up with the same toppings you would put on a baked potato (cheese, green onions, bacon).  this is a great soup for a pot-luck, because it is universally enjoyed by kids and adults.  note:  the original version called for half 'n half, but i've found that milk works just fine.

1. prepare vegetables
2. dice onion and celery
3. peel and dice potatoes into small pieces
4. saute onion and celery in butter about 8 minutes over low heat until softened
5. add potatoes and chicken broth
6. simmer 15-20 minutes until potatoes are tender
7. add cream cheese to soup
8. add chopped bacon and milk
9. option - add a pkg
10. of frozen broccoli , cooked , drained and chopped , or a package of frozen corn
11. season with salt and pepper
12. serve with additional toppings
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this. The flavor is very similar to my WW baked potato soup but this has more fat etc. I made the soup before the recipe was changed and the direction were different. So I have some yellow corn added into my soup. I used half-and-half which the recipe called for before the change. Very delicious soup. Thanks for posting. Made for PAC Fall 2008

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp coriander salad

a nice light salad with a lime vinaigrette - sounds good!

1. combine and mix shrimp , tomatoes , avocados , green chilies , celery and coriander leaves
2. quickly mix oil , sugar , salt and lime juice and pour over shrimp mixture
3. toss together and chill
4. serve on a bed of lettuce
demonstrations.review: This has to be one of my most favorite salads...it is so refreshing and easy to prepare...loved it! Made for "1st Time" tag game...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green    deviled  eggs  n  ham

just want sam-i-am to know i do like green eggs 'n' ham, & one of the easiest ways to enjoy 'em is by making a recipe like this! obviously this recipe is for a group [or someone who really, really likes green eggs]! [i use only del monte brand sweet pickle relish, 'cause many of the other brands have a large amount of hig fructose corn syrup.] the 23-minute cooking time for the hard-cooked eggs is not included in preparation time.

1. carefully cut eggs into halves lengthwise
2. just as carefully , scoop out yolks & into a bowl
3. mash yolks well , then mix in mayo , mustard & relish
4. add green food color one drop at a time , mixing well after each drop , until desired intensity of green is achieved
5. add chopped ham & lemon pepper & mix well
6. carefully spoon & slightly mound yolk mixture into each hollowed egg white half
7. if using paprika , sprinkle lightly over the green deviled eggs & serve
demonstrations.review: Yep! These tasty little guys deserve 5+ stars. Easy to prepare. Love the presentation. This will be great on St Patty's day with green beer. What a great appetizer. Thanks for posting. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jamaican chicken stew

found this in a cooking light magazine and have put it on my list of recipes to try.

1. prepare rice according to package directions , omitting salt and fat
2. while rice cooks , heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
3. add onion and garlic , saute 3 minutes or until tender
4. combine chicken and spices in a bowl
5. add chicken mixture to pan and saute 4 minutes
6. stir in wine , capers , beans , and tomatoes
7. cover , reduce heat , and simmer 10 minutes until tender
8. serve over rice
9. one serving equals 1 1 / 2 cups stew and 3 / 4 cup rice
demonstrations.review: Wow! This has lots of flavor. The only thing missing was some salt. I made as posted. Came out delicious. Served it with a side of corn bread and dinner was ready. This is quick and easy to prepare.What more can you ask for. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caribbean chicken with pineapple salsa

from:  valerie lindsey
this delicious recipe has a little kick from the jalapeno peppers and sweet from the pineapple and juice.  our family loves this dish.  be sure to cook it on the grill to do it justice!  
healthy, low fat, low sugar.  this is a guilt free dish.  delicious served with baked sweet potato and green salad with a sweet vinaigrette dressing.

1. make salsa first
2. combine all salsa ingredients except cilantro and refrigerate up to one day
3. add cilantro just before serving
4. puree all ingredients for chicken marinade and put in plastic ziploc bag with chicken
5. marinade no more than 30 minutes
6. grill and serve
demonstrations.review: Delicious! What a refreshing dish. Due to our need for heat I just used the other half of the jalapeno instead of a quarter of it in the salsa. That's the only change I made. This can easily serve 4. Just cut the breast in half lengthwise prior to marinading. There is plenty of salsa to go around. Made this on a very cool... just got here... spring day. Can't wait to make this on a hot summer day. I served it as suggested with baked sweet potatoes and green salad. This is a keeper. Thanks for posting. Made for Spring PAC 2011.

target.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
target.review: Hard to say if this is banana bread or banana pudding, it is so moist and creamy hot out of the oven.    I thought I had ruined it since 60-65 minutes is a bit long and mine had turned dark brown after about 45 minutes, but with all that banana in it it was still moist inside while the outside is caramalized.  I did a few changes, I used half whole wheat flour/half white flour, a teaspoon of vanilla, plus a dash of cinnamon and nutmeg.  Definitely good enough to let bananas get over ripe on purpose!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry oatmeal muffins

these are moist, tasty muffins which are especially nice to serve around christmastime.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. soak oats in yogurt or sourcream just enough to make it moist
3. sift dry ingredients into a bowl
4. in a separate bowl , add oil , sugars , and egg
5. beat until well blended
6. gradually fold in dry ingredients
7. add chopped cranberries and orange zest
8. put in greased muffin tins
9. bake for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have been on a search for the perfect muffin and these get close.  I have made them with both raisans and cranberries, plus I usually add chopped almonds or pecans as well.  I use this now as the basis for my muffin experiements.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fettuccini alfonso

afredo's healthy brother.

1. thaw corn kernels
2. place the corn , soy milk , tahini , and seasoning in a blender and process until completely smooth
3. pour the blended mixture into a medium saucepan and warm over medium-low heat , stirring often
4. while the sauce is heating , cook the fettuccini in a large pot of boiling water until al dente
5. drain well and return to the pot
6. add the hot sauce and toss until evenly coated
7. serve immediately , topping each portion with pepper , if desired
demonstrations.review: This recipe looked odd to me at first but I decided to try it (partly because the other reviewer didn't really make this recipe).  I stuck to the recipe with minor exceptions.  I added chopped garlic as well as onion powder plus I added some corn starch to thicken the sauce a bit.  I used a heavy dose of pepper but only a tiny fraction of the salt, plus I used the optional tahini.  The results were very good though not spectacular.  I added more pepper on top and a bit of grated paramasian cheese.  The pepper helped but the cheese didn't add much.  This sauce does have great potential, I think it would be great with curry for a shrimp or chicken curry dish.  For those not on a low salt diet I think this would be even better with the normal salt quanity.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ginger lime salmon

this recipe was featured in the june 2001 issue of shape magazine.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. rub a 10 ounce skinless salmon fillet with just enough olive oil to coat
3. place in a 10-inch nonstick skillet with an ovenproof handle
4. season with salt and pepper , a squeeze of lemon or lime , and freshly grated ginger or garlic to taste
5. bake 12-15 minutes or until firm to the touch or to your liking
demonstrations.review: I have made this twice.  The first time I left out the oil and used the lime/ginger mix as a marinade (1/2 hour) and baked the salmon.  It was okay but the lime over-powered the fish.  I can see where it would work for grilling but not for baking.  The second time I tried the recipe as written, with a lemonlime mix and ginger.  It was [b]very[/b] good and I'll keep it in my cookbook.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet   sour zucchini

quick easy and tasty. don't peel the zucchini

1. saut the zucchini in oil until still crisp but hot through
2. remove and keep warm
3. add remaining ingredients to the pan and simmer 3 minutes
4. put zucchini back in the pan for 1 minute and serve
demonstrations.review: It was a little too sweet, but I used rice vinegar, a stronger white vinegar would be better.  I added no salt just pepper and I didn't miss the salt.  A good recipe, might be nice to add giner for a bit more kick.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean orzo salad

nan

1. mix beans , olives , tomatoes , onions and cilantro in large bowl
2. mix oil , lime juice , cumin , pepper and salt
3. toss with bean mixture
4. stir in pasta
5. let stand for 1 hour to blend flavors
6. serve at room temperature as a side dish or on spinach
demonstrations.review: I love orzo but all of the salads recipes I have use cheese and I wanted one without.  This one was excellent, I really liked the black beans with the orzo.  I like keeping something in the frig for eating on the run and this was great for that, it kept well and was a great snack for between errands.

target.recipe_text:
sausage brunch braid

this is great when friends are coming over or when ever. serve with fruit and you have a complete meal.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a skillet cook , sausage , onion , celery , green pepper and garlic until meat is no longer pink and vegetables are tender , drain
3. add cream cheese , green onions and parsley
4. cook and stir over low heat until cheese is melted , set aside
5. unroll crescent dough on a greased baking sheet , press perforations together
6. roll in to an 12x10 rectangle
7. spoon mixture within 3 inches of sides and 1 inch of ends
8. on each long side cut 3 / 4 in wide strips
9. starting on one end , fold alternating strips at an angle , forming a braid
10. brush dough with egg and bake for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown
target.review: I had this recipe from a magazine years ago and had lost it.  Made again today for a trial run before making for brunch tomorrow at church.  It's as good as I remembered!  Don't be tempted to use more than the 12oz of sausage or you wind up with the bread spread too thin.  I also used red pepper instead of green; we like the flavor better.  Impressive looking easy brunch item!  Thanks for posting J9!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fruit salad   ambrosia style

my mother made this salad for every thanksgiving and christmas dinners.  i remember looking forward to this the most, as a kid, as i loved the marshmallows and the fruit.  my mom made a big bowl of this and added shredded coconut to half of it and left the other without for those of us non-coconut lovers.  this is so quick and easy yet so tasty and refreshing, especially with a big heavy holiday meal.  i also found out that this is a common hawaiian luau side dish.  time does not include chilling time.

1. drain all cans of fruit
2. in a large bowl add drained fruit , marshmallows , sour cream and coconut if using
3. mix well to combine
4. refrigerate for at least 6 hours , overnight if possible
5. this allows the juices to blend with the marshmallows and sour cream
6. one hour before serving , slice bananas and add to rest of the fruit , stir to combine
7. if it seems to dry add a little more sour cream
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: We'll jump on the 5 star bandwagon for this one diner!  I made this yesterday to refrigerate overnight and we had it for dessert tonight.  I halved the recipe for the 2 of us and made as directed except for using the refrigerated fruit in jars because I had in on hand.  I also used coconut because I love it!  Definitely plan on refrigerating this overnight or so for the best flavor melding.  I snuck a bit or two when mixing and the flavor definitely changes when it has had time to meld.  Often we see a variation of this here made with cool whip or the such, but we liked the tang of the sour cream--I used light.  Made for "I Recommend" Tag Feb-10

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory spaghetti

i made this without the meat, and it was still terrific.  i love how fast it comes together and the noodles cook right in the pan.  i used fresh garden tomatoes and added a hot pepper for extra flavor.  delicious!  recipe courtesy of betty crocker best-loved recipes and marie mckell of ukiah, california.

1. brown beef and pork in large skillet over medium heat
2. add onion and green pepper and cook 5 minutes
3. add olives , mushrooms , and tomato sauce and mix lightly
4. stir mixture of tomatoes , water , salt , pepper , worcestershire sauce , and tabasco into meat mixture
5. add uncooked spaghetti and bring to boil
6. cover tightly and reduce heat to low
7. simmer about 40 minutes , stirring occasionally
8. uncover and simmer 15 minutes longer
demonstrations.review: My mom's old Betty Crocker New Picture Cookbook (circa 1961) had this recipe and she made it often when we were growing up.  I hadn't had it in ages and while I have been visiting her she thought it sounded good.  I accidentally put in 3/4 lb. beef and I used about 4oz fresh mushrooms, but the rest was by the recipe.  In the future I would find a way to give this more spice (maybe seasoned tomatoes or Italian sausage instead of just ground pork), but my mom is really sensitive to spice during her chemo, so this worked out well.  Thanks for posting AmyZoe! **update** tonight I made this with sweet Italian sausage and seasoned diced tomatoes--really yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus  oven roasted

cooking asparagus in the oven will give you a crunchy result and it seems to enhance the flavor. use any of your favorite herbs if you don't like italian seasoning or omit herb altogether.

1. heat an oven proof pan in a hot oven for 5 minutes
2. pour in the oil& italian seasoning
3. coat the whole pan
4. roll the asparagus in the oil to coat all sides
5. bake in 400f degrees oven for 5-7 min do not over cook !
6. the asparagus should just be heated through but still very crisp
7. remove from oven , drizzle with the vinegar
8. add salt& pepper
9. sprinkle with parmesan
10. serve immediately or serve at room temperature
demonstrations.review: As an earlier reviewer stated, this is a good recipe with very good directions.  I didn't use the parmesan cheese because another dish we had for dinner had a fair amount of cheese.  I haven't had asparagus with balsamic vinegar and it was an interesting taste.  I loved the Italian seasoning!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana pudding cake

instead of making banana bread to use up those ripe bananas, why not try this instead?

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease a bundt pan and set aside
3. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients and beat with your electric mixer for 3 minutes
4. pour into prepared pan and bake for 50-55 minutes , or until a tester comes out clean
5. cool for 15 minutes before removing from pan
6. if desired , combine 1 cup of sifted icing sugar with a little milk and drizzle this over the cake
demonstrations.review: I'll just add to the great reviews!  I made this slightly differently than the posted recipe, taking other reviewers' advice and using 1 cup mashed ripe banana.  I also used 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce instead of the 1/4 vegetable oil and 1/4 cup of the water.  The result was a very moist and tasty cake.  I might cut back next time on either my amount of banana or applesauce to get a slightly drier cake, but that was my doctoring and not the recipes fault!  I didn't glaze at all and served for a fellowship on the lawn after church.  It was well recieved and DH says to make it again!  Thanks for the great recipe to use up those old bananas!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cheesy spinach and ham quiche pie

in the oven with only 10 minutes of prep, this hearty quiche is one of my favorites!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. spray pan with pam and cook mushrooms , onions and ham until onions are tender
3. thaw spinach and squeeze out excess water
4. add to pan
5. in a large bowl , mix mayo , milk , eggs and cheddar cheese
6. cool hot mixture slightly and add to bowl with liquids
7. pour into pie shell and top with parmesan cheese
8. bake for 45 minutes until set and golden brown
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Our CSA boxes each week have had a dozen eggs and even with giving a dozen away, the two of us are having a hard time keeping up with eggs, so I went on a search for recipes to use them up.  This is a keeper!  I made as written with the exception of using light mayonnaise, 2% Mexican Blend cheese instead of the cheddar, and fresh mushrooms instead of canned.  I also used a 5th egg because my farm eggs were not all what I would consider large.  Since I was a bit liberal on the filling, I might be wrong here, but I would recommend a deep dish pie shell over a regular one.  I had enough mixture leftover after filling the pie shell to put into a ramekin which I baked alongside the quiche.  I resisted my urge to add seasoning to the mixture, and that was a great decision as the flavor was perfect as it was.  A great mixture of flavors without any one being too overwhelming.  A great supper with salad! Besides, any recipe that gets that many veggies into DH and that he rates 5 stars is a keeper!  Thanks Trishypie for a wonderful recipe!

target.recipe_text:
chocolate snowflake cookies  chocolate crinkles   crackles

this makes a lot of cookies, perfect for gift-giving.

1. combine sugar , oil , and melted chocolate in a large mixing bowl
2. beat at medium speed of an electric mixer until blended
3. add eggs and vanilla , mixing well
4. combine flour , baking powder and salt in a medium bowl
5. add about one-fourth of dry mixture at a time to chocolate mixture , mixing after each addition
6. cover and let chill at least 2 hours
7. shape dough into 1-inch balls , and roll in powdered sugar
8. place cookies 2 inches apart on lightly greased cookie sheets
9. bake at 350 degrees f
10. for 10 to 12 minutes
11. cool on wire racks
target.review: I've used this exact same recipe for years...it's always a HUGE hit. Makes a great addition to gift baskets. I like to cook them til they are just done (don't overcook). :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice krispies chocolate dream bars

i made this for church fellowship gatherings and it was always the first to go. i have used various flavoured chips and it always turns out delicious.

1. bottom layer
2. in mixing bowl cream butter or margarine with sugar until light and fluffy
3. add vanilla and eggs one at a time beating well after each addition
4. mix together flour , cocoa , baking powder , salt and chopped nuts
5. stir into egg mixture until well combined
6. spread mixture in bottom of greased 13 x 9 pan
7. bake at 350f for 15-20 minutes
8. middle layer
9. sprinkle marshmallows evenly over bottom layer
10. bake an additional 3 minutes
11. let cool
12. top layer
13. in small saucepan combine chocolate chips and peanut butter
14. cook over low heat stirring constantly until melted
15. stir in cereal and spread evenly on top of cooled marshmallow layer
16. refrigerate 2 hours or until firm
17. cut into bars
demonstrations.review: I have a guilty confession...I wanted to make these as one of the desserts for Thanksgiving dinner at my MIL's, but I didn't have all the ingredients to make the bottom layer. Looking at it, the bottom layer looked basically like brownies to me...and I had a brownie mix. So I substituted that, baking it according to the package directions except that a used a pan a little larger than a 9x13 (maybe 12x13?). I baked it for 20 minutes, then sprinkled the marshmallows over the top of the brownie layer (along with about an extra cup of marshmallows due to larger pan size). I also doubled all the ingredients in the top layer...both due to pan size and because it was so good! Okay, despite all the changes and the fact that I didn't make the recipe exactly according to directions...everybody loved it!!! They disappeared as quickly as I could put them out! One of my SIL's has severe autism and normally is rather reserved about taking any food from me. I gave her one of those and she popped the whole thing in her mouth, grinning and her eyes widening with glee. She did the same thing with two more of them! I can tell you now that if she could she would have given you 20 stars! LOL And I'm inclined to say I'd have to agree with her. Loved the topping and marshmallow combination, along with the brownie. I would like to make this again soon and intend to try it with the original bottom layer. Thanks for a great recipe, Dorel! ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rich fudge ribbon bundt cake

this cake is moist and rich! i love the cheesecake filling in the middle!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease and flour , , 10 bundt cake pan well
3. prepare cake mix according to package directions ! adding instant pudding mix , not prepared to the package directions)
4. pour batter into pan
5. set aside
6. in mixing bowl , beat cream cheese , butter and cornstarch until fluffy
7. slowly beat in sweetened condensed milk
8. beat in egg and vanilla , beating til smooth
9. spoon evenly over cake batter
10. bake 50-55 minutes til toothpick comes out clean
11. cool 10-15 minutes , carefully remove from pan onto cake plate
12. you may have to tap sides quite a bit to loosen , and i also ran a knife around edge to help loosen
13. sprinkle with powdered sugar or drizzle with white chocolate and / or chocolate glazes if desired
demonstrations.review:
I didn't get the beautiful ribbon that Chef~V got in her photos...(how DID you do that?!?), but this was a really good cake. I iced it with a mocha icing. Mental notes to future self: Don't try to ice it on a platter that's "just the right size"...especially if it has scalloped edges. I had a terrible time trying to get it to stay on the platter...it kept trying to drip off around the scalloped sides. However, the cake was great, and I'd make it again in a heartbeat! :D  PS: Fwiw, I've found it's best when they've had a chance to sit in the fridge overnight and let the flavors meld. Update 5/27/08: Okay...guilty confession time. I went to a church retreat last weekend. We were supposed to bring a large dessert to share over the weekend. So I planned on making two of your cakes (in two 20" x 20" pans) and Chef~V's Recipe #303413 (changes I made noted in my review). I was racing around getting stuff done and needed to multi-task. So I tossed the cakes in the oven and raced down to drop my sleeping bag off at the laundromat. Realized I needed to get the espresso for the frosting. :evil: So I did that on the way back. Got back...and had been longer than I realized. Opened the front door to smell scorched cake. :evil: I REALLY didn't have time to remake them, but my neighbor agreed to run down to the store for me to pick up the supplies. While the neighbor was gone, I decided to try a piece of the cake, as there were some spots that weren't as dark. Used a 3-tined salad/meat spork to cut a piece out, cutting the scorched part off of the bottom as I did it. Hmmm...not bad. The inside and top didn't actually taste scorched. Too bad I couldn't serve it as the icing was already done and sitting there.

Hmmmm...

Grabbed a large piece of aluminum foil and set my cake rack on top. Continued to "spork" the pieces of cake out, in about 3"x3" squares, laying them upside down on the rack (ragged edge up). Salvaged what I could from both pans...not getting any that was too dark. Spooned the mocha ganache over the top. Let it set. Placed it on a serving tray and carefully covered it. They were absolutely TDF. I had a number of people come up and comment on them, begging me for the recipe. Nobody ever knew how close I came to just scraping both pans out and skipping it. :D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coffee punch

looking for something a bit different for your next gathering? this is a real crowd pleaser! smooth and tasty! a sprinkling of cinnamon or nutmeg on top is nice. cook time is for chilling.

1. combine coffee , milk , sugar and vanilla , stir well
2. place in refrigerator and chill thoroughly
3. place ice-cream in large bowl
4. pour coffee mixture over ice-cream
5. stir gently
6. top with dollops of whipped cream
demonstrations.review: July 29th, 2004: This sounds wonderful! I am imagining it with, perhaps, some Hershey syrup (maybe 1/2-1 cup) and a quality french vanilla ice cream. And if you\'re feeling really flush/adventurous, maybe a few well-placed sprinkles of cinnamon on top of the whipping cream. (Sorry, MizzNezz...no offense. I am one of those incurable recipe tinkerers. I have been very impressed, however, with the quality of your recipe collection. Kudos! And thanks for sharing!) ;o) August 1, 2005: It took me just over a year to get around to trying this recipe, although it's been rattling around in my brain since I first read it! And it was just as good as I imagined it would be! I made this last night to take to my DH's boss's potluck birthday party, and you should have seen and heard the reactions of people when they tried it! It would have warmed your heart! I had numerous people ask me for the recipe, and it is such an easy recipe to put together, I was able to rattle it off from memory. The coffee wasn't quite as chilled as it should have been, but it didn't seem to affect the punch overall. I made the punch exactly as the recipe called, except after it was assembled I sprinkled some grated sweet chocolate (I used Hershey's) over the top of the whipped cream dollops. It made for a very nice presentation, and the little bits of chocolate were fun to run into when drinking the punch. My DD, who had arrived at the party separately from us, tried it and fell in love with it. She came up to me later, wide-eyed and effusively said, "I didn't know YOU brought that punch...can you make that for our wedding reception?!?" (she's getting married this October). Thank you so much, MissNezz, for a wonderful ten star recipe...one that will be going into my personal, handwritten cookbook! :D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
you will get better soup

this is a cold remedy and really works! from the ny times. cheese is optional, if you really feel yucky.

1. combine stock , garlic , jalapenos , and herbs in pan , bring to a boil
2. reduce and simmer until garlic is soft , about 30 minutes
3. transfer to a blender , puree until smooth
4. season with salt , serve in mugs , topped with cheese
demonstrations.review: This soup was delightful! I made it because I've got a chest cold, and just "felt the need" to make something spicy to help clear my chest. I had tucked it away in my cookbook awhile back, figuring it would be there if I needed it. This last weekend...I needed it! I made a few changes, based on what I had on hand, which I'll document both for others and to remind myself what I did later... :D I used 8 cups of a very good quality chicken broth (I used Kitchen Basics brand), the 2 full heads of garlic, 2 very large, plump jalapenos (about 4-5" long each), 1  1/4 tsp. oregano leaves, 1 tsp. ground thyme, and grated "Mexican cheese" (4 cheese mix) from Costco. I skipped the salt by choice...tasted fine without it. Re. preparation, I didn't have any gloves, so I CAREFULLY used chicken tongs and a knife to cut the peppers lengthwise, then used the tongs and knife to cut the seeds (the hottest part) out. I left the peppers in quarters and didn't chop them...didn't want to risk it. After simmering the soup, I discovered my blender blade had "grown legs" (gotta love kids and DH's)...so I took all the solids out of the pot and transferred it to my food processor. I pulsed it a few times, then gradually added about 1 1/2 cups of broth to help it puree. Worked fine. Poured it back into the pot and stired. I have to agree with Miss Diggy on the flavor of this soup. It is absolutely delightful, and I guarantee I'll make it again! In fact, I went to Costco today and picked up a six-pack of chicken broth (I use two boxes per batch) so I can make some more. DH made all sorts of sad faces when he discovered he wasn't getting any of the last batch...figured I'd better make some for him since he was the hero that picked up the supplies for me when I wasn't feeling well. Thanks for an incredibly good recipe...and thanks for making me feel better when I was feeling icky.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven scrambled eggs for a crowd

cooking for a crowd? a really big crowd? use this easy recipe for an easy egg dish.

1. divide butter among four 13 x 9 inch baking dishes
2. combine eggs and salt
3. mix well
4. gradually stir in milk
5. pour evenly into baking dishes
6. bake , uncovered at 350f for 10 minutes
7. stir
8. bake 10-15 minutes more or until eggs are set
9. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Very tasty! I made a few adjustments for taste and the size crowd I was working with: I divided the recipe in half; reduced the salt to approx. 2 1/2 teaspoons (instead of 4 1/2); I cooked it in one deep (steam-table) pan; added cooked, chopped bacon; added approx. 39 slices of cheese; also, it was cooked in a convection oven. I stirred the bacon and approx. 24 slices of cheese in at the halfway point (had to double the initial time to 20 min), stirred til melted, then laid the remaining 15 slices on top. I covered it with a lid and put it back in the oven for  approximately 5 minutes, then put it in the steam table (on high) to finish while I finished cooking. They were a huge hit! The kids and staff kept coming in to see when snack was going to be ready...and one of the teens, upon hearing the boy next to him wasn't getting any eggs (seconds) said, "Are you crazy? Those eggs are kickin'!" :D All changes aside...you still have a great recipe, Miss Annie...thank you very much! :D

target.recipe_text:
cottage cheese banana breakfast delite

my own creation...i eat this every day for breakfast. very healthy, low-fat/cal, and filling (especailly when using whole-wheat bread). also a great breakfast for diabetics

1. toast bagel , english muffin , or bread
2. top with sliced banana
3. spread cottage cheese evenly over top
4. sprinkle sugar substitute and cinnamon over top
5. enjoy !
target.review: This was really so much better than I would have ever thought. I like cottage cheese, but would have never thought to use it like this! Thanks so much. (I can't imagine eating anything every day, but this will be in the rotation nonetheless!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy wild rice soup with smoked turkey

this came from cooking light 2001 magazine and it has been our favorite since i found it. it is the best cold, rainy, gloomy, any day soup ever!!

1. melt butter in a dutch oven over med high heat
2. add carrot and next 5 ingredients
3. saute 8 minutes or until brown
4. stir in broth scraping pan to loosen browned bits
5. stir in turkey and rice
6. cover and simmer 1 hour 15 minutes or until rice is tender
7. combine flour and milk in a small bowl stirring with a whisk
8. add flour / milk mixture to pan and cook over medium heat about 8 minutes or until thick
9. stir in sherry and salt
demonstrations.review: This soup is fantastic!  A keeper for sure!  I used up leftover turkey from the freezer.  I also used already cooked wild rice, and just used less broth (not sure I just eyeballed it). I also doubled the pepper, but I just like pepper.  Thanks for this great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hello dollies

these are rich, yummy layered squares that require no bowl or mixing. they are very easy to make and come out wonderful. (i have no idea where the name came from...got these out of a 30 year old women's club cookbook.) 12/23/08: butter amount changed to reflect the advice and opinions in reviews.  thanks!

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees fahrenheit
2. spread melted butter in a 9 x 13 pan
3. sprinkle with graham crumbs
4. add the nuts , chips and coconut , sprinkling evenly over crumbs
5. cover all with condensed milk
6. bake for 25 minutes
7. allow to cool and cut into squares
demonstrations.review: Wow, these were delicious!  Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken for chering

just cher and i are doing the south beach diet and she asked me to share a chicken recipe i created. how could i resist not calling it chicken for chering. get it?

1. combine spinach and ricotta
2. roll each piece of chicken with an equal amount of stuffing , secure with toothpick
3. sear chicken in non-stick pan--about three minutes on each side
4. transfer seared chicken to baking dish and bake at 350 for about 30 mins or until juices run clear and chicken is done
5. meanwhile combine all sauce ingredients in a small sauce pan
6. bring to a boil and stir
7. reduce heat and simmer sauce stirring occasionally
8. serve sauce over chicken
demonstrations.review: Followed exactly, and just wasn't wowed by this dish. It was edible and we didn't throw it away, but will not be making it again. Thanks anyway.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
demonstrations.review: I made this for a cookout with a bunch of friends and my brother.  I wish I would have made a couple, because my brother just about ate half the pie himself. Everybody raved, and my brother just oohs and ahhs anytime I even think about making another one, he keeps begging!  All the guys at the cookout told my boyfriend they are jealous as well! I used pretty thin slices of the apples, which I thought was perfect.  Nice touch with the caramel and pecans. Thanks for this awesome recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Well I don't think this needs another review, but hey, what is one more.  As a general rule I don't eat beans, never have, mostly because I don't like the texture of beans.  Beans are however, well a cheap source of protein so I have been scouring the websites for bean recipes that I might actually eat.  This recipe fits the bill.  Although I did not think it was the best thing since sliced bread, it is a good solid recipe.  I used frozen corn, and I cut up the chicken into pieces (not frozen) and decreased the cooking time and served over rice.  I think next time I will use the leftovers (with the rice) in a tortilla.  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
breakfast burritos  once a month cooking

great for that run in the morning breakfast. you can also take frozen burritos with you when going camping. just place the bag of frozen burritos into the ice chest, and by the time you're ready for breakfast the first morning, the burritos are fully thawed. then simply reheat them in a large skillet over the campstove or fire grate.

1. scramble eggs in large skillet until done
2. stir in cooked sausage and salsa
3. warm tortillas in microwave 20-30 seconds or until warm and flexible
4. place 1 / 2 cup egg mixture into tortilla
5. roll burrito-style
6. freeze burritos in single layer on lightly greased cookie sheet
7. when fully frozen , wrap burritos individually
8. place wrapped burritos in large zip-top freezer bags
9. freeze
10. to serve: unwrap burritos from foil or plastic wrap that you used for freezing
11. wrap in a paper towel
12. cook in microwave until heated through
13. or thaw burritos , wrap burritos in foil , and bake at 350 degrees for ten minutes
target.review: Made these just as directed and added a chopped onion, 1/2 of a green pepper, and about a cup of mushrooms. Yum! I made these for my DH to eat before work but he's going to have to share!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bread maker hamburger buns

this is a recipe that i put together myself and ever since i have never bought any.

1. add ingredients in order listed , except for the egg and 1 t
2. water that is for the egg wash later
3. select dough / pasta setting when cycle is complete , remove dough from machine to a lightly floured surface
4. divide dough into 3 equal portions , divide each portion into 6 balls
5. turn balls in hands folding edge under to make a circle
6. press ball flat between hands
7. place on greased cookie sheet pressing to a 31 / 2 inch circle
8. let rise 30 minutes or until double in volume
9. combine 1 slightly beaten egg with 1 tblsp
10. water and brush on buns
11. sprinkle with sesame seeds
12. perfect buns every time
13. bake at 350 for about 10 minutes or until lightly brown
demonstrations.review: I cut this recipe in half and made 4 large buns for dinner and wrapped the remaining dough around hot dogs for the kids. Everyone loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible peanut butter cookies

these are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!

1. mix peanut butter , sugar , and egg together until smooth
2. drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart
