3. if desired , roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet
4. press with fork
5. press again in opposite direction
6. bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
7. do not brown
8. do not over bake
demonstrations.review: Made these this afternoon, I used creamy pb, half brown sugar and half white sugar and added a tablespoon or so of vanilla. They were good but way too sweet for our tastes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blender quiche   or whatever you have in your kitchen leftover

the great part is you can use whatever leftovers (well...almost) you have on hand. this dish can be served hot or cold. freezes very well! use any cheese of your choice.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. generously grease a 9 inch pie pan
3. spread shredded cheese across bottom of pie pan
4. cover cheese with meat and vegetables
5. in a blender , combine eggs , baking mix , salt , garlic powder , onions , parsley , and milk
6. blend until smooth , then add olive oil
7. blend until combined , then pour mixture over meat and vegetable layer
8. sprinkle with paprika
9. bake in preheated oven for 40 minutes
10. cool 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I hesitate to post a review since I really didn't follow this recipe...I just used what I had, but I think that's the point of the recipe. I used a bit of leftover cornish hen meat, left over spinach, only 1/4 cup of olive oil, omitted the parsley, and used pancake mix for the baking mix. The cheese I used was mild cheddar that was left over from taco salad night. I also got to use up the last of the milk that was about to expire. I was super happy to use up all these things but a little concerned about how it would actually taste. It was awesome. Definitely not what I would serve as a real quiche, but great for leftovers. My husband ate 3 large pieces!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lorraine s luscious and lovely limoncello

my friend lorraine b gave me this wonderful recipe when i was looking for an interesting hostess gift. one of the best things about this recipe is that it only takes one week to infuse, as opposed to up to a month that i've seen in other recipes. i actually made a quadruple recipe and got 6 bottles to give as gifts (i kept one for myself, of course!). at last night's preliminary tasting (2 hours after bottling) i can tell you that this is a very refreshing tipple! i'm also going to try this with oranges this winter.

1. wash the lemons , using soap , rinse well
2. peel the lemons
3. i used my microplane zester and got lovely lemon zest , but you can also use a potato peeler
4. make sure not to get any of the bitter white pith
5. place the peel into a bowl and cover with the vodka
6. i used a large tupperware bowl with a cover
7. let the lemons infuse in the vodka for one week
8. line a strainer with paper towels and strain the lemony vodka into a bowl that will hold more than twice its volume
9. mix the sugar with the water in a pot and let it come to a boil
10. boil for 2 minutes , giving it an occasional stir
11. let cool
12. add the sugar syrup to the lemon vodka and mix
13. place in your favorite bottle
14. keep the limoncello in the freezer
demonstrations.review: I doubled this recipe. I have 2 quart glass containers in the freezer to give as gifts tomorrow. Plus 2 750 ML bottles for us. Plus whatever we drank while bottling it...LOL This stuff is good and worth the wait...I'm excited to give it out as gifts! I added two limes to mine and a few more lemons, but otherwise followed the directions.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
instant chai tea mix

spice this up even further by adding 1 teaspoon each nutmeg and allspice, and 1/4 teaspoon white pepper.  you may choose to omit the french vanilla creamer, and use 2 teaspoons vanilla extract instead. to do so, mix the vanilla into the sugar, let it dry, then break the sugar into small lumps. follow the same procedure as above. a quick, but very appreciative thank you to the reviewers who aren't receiving zmail!

1. in a large bowl , combine milk powder , non-dairy creamer , vanilla flavored creamer , sugar and instant tea
2. stir in ginger , cinnamon , cloves and cardamom
3. in a blender or food processor , blend 1 cup at a time , until mixture is the consistency of fine powder
4. to serve: stir 2 heaping tablespoons chai tea mixture into a mug of hot water
5. store dry mixture in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: I made this exactly as directed, using the extra spices, and grinding it up fine in my coffee grinder. I originally intended it to go in my Christmas Morning baskets that I'm giving out this year....but I've had to make 3 batches just to get enough for 4 gift bags... Because my family keeps drinking it all up! I had to hide the last batch from them. I also have had a cup every day. This stuff is just really good. I've never had a "real" chai from a coffee shop before but I've bought those little instant mix packets at the store, but this is better and much cheaper. I mix two heaping tbsp in hot water and then add a few splashes of vanilla soy milk to top it off and make it creamier. It's wonderful!

target.recipe_text:
chicken cutlets with bacon  rosemary and lemon

from cook's country.

1. fry bacon in large skillet over medium-high heat until crisp , about 5 minutes
2. transfer bacon with slotted spoon to plate lined with paper towels
3. spoon off all but 2 tablespoons bacon fat
4. meanwhile , place flour in shallow dish
5. season chicken with salt and pepper , dredge in flour , and shake to remove excess
6. add butter to reserved bacon fat in skillet and heat over high heat , swirling to melt butter
7. when foam subsides , reduce heat to medium-high and cook chicken until browned on both sides , 3 to 4 minutes per side
8. transfer chicken to plate and cover loosely with foil
9. reduce heat to medium and add garlic , rosemary and pepper flakes
10. cook until garlic is browned and crisp , about 2 minutes
11. add broth and lemon juice , scrape up browned bits from bottom of skillet with wooden spoon and simmer until slightly thickened , about 4 minutes
12. return chicken and bacon to pan and simmer , turning chicken once or twice , until sauce is thick and glossy , 2 to 3 minutes
13. adjust seasonings and serve immediately
target.review:
I made this for dinner last night and everyone love it! It was fast and easy but had that Wow factor that I like to have on a Sunday night!
Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon chewsies  chewy lemon bars with lemon frosting

moist and chewy citrus bars.

1. cream together butter , sugar , salt , and baking soda
2. then blend in the remaining bar ingredients
3. spread in well-greased and floured 15x10" pan
4. bake at 350f for 20-25 minutes or until light golden brown
5. combine all frosting ingredients , and beat until smooth and creamy , adding more juice if necessary
6. frost bars while still hot
demonstrations.review:
Wish I could give this more than 5 stars! My boys beg me to make these and are now a "must" for the Christmas dainty platter.
Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown rice and lentil casserole

this is a great meal that we eat here often in the winter time. with some dark bread and maybe a salad it is a really hearty meal, though we have been known to eat just this for dinner. the recipe is adapted from amy dacyczyn's "the complete tightwad gazette"

1. preheat the oven to 300 degrees
2. mix all ingredients except the cheese in a baking dish
3. cover with foil and bake for 1 hour 10 minutes
4. then remove the foil , add the cheese , and bake for an additional 20 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I know there is already plenty of great reviews, but I need to add mine!
This recipe has it all; easy, fast, inexspensive and best of all delicious!
Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrot pineapple cake with buttermilk glaze

if desired you may omit the buttermilk glaze and frost with your favorite cream cheese frosting,  see my recipe#90142   ---- prep time includes making the buttermilk glaze.

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. in a bowl beat eggs with sugar , oil , buttermilk and vanilla for about 5 minutes
4. in another bowl mix together flour , baking soda , cinnamon , nutmeg and salt
5. add to the egg mixture beating at low speed until blended
6. fold in carrots , drained pineapple , raisins and walnuts
7. mix with wooden spoon until combined
8. transfer to prepared baking dish
9. bake for about 30 minutes
10. remove from oven and cover the pan loosley with foil to prevent excess browning
11. return to oven and bake for another 12-13 minutes more , or until the cake tests done
12. to make the buttermilk glaze
13. in a heavy saucepan bring the sugar , baking soda , butter , buttermilk and corn syrup to a boil over medium-high heat
14. cook for about 4 minutes or until the mixture is golden brown
15. remove from heat and stir in vanilla
16. drizzle the buttermilk mixture glaze over the cake
17. cool completely in the pan then frost with cream cheese icing
18. delicious !
demonstrations.review:
Yum!!!
This was a definite hit in our house - everyone had seconds and then some. I served it with just the glaze and it was perfect. Thanks for sharing another outstanding recipe Kittencal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sinful red velvet cookies

this is based on a paula deen recipe, so it's quite rich ;) this is by far the most luxurious cookie i make. they never last long. they're painfully easy to make, which may be bad news for your waistline.

1. in a large bowl with an electric mixer , cream the cream cheese and butter until smooth
2. beat in the egg
3. beat in the vanilla extract
4. beat in the cake mix
5. cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to firm up so that you can roll the batter into balls
6. i've chilled batter overnight and it comes out fine
7. after batter has chilled and you're ready to make the cookies , preheat the oven to 350f
8. roll the chilled batter into tablespoon sized balls and then roll them in confectioner's sugar
9. place on an ungreased cookie sheet , 2 inches apart
10. bake 12 minutes
11. the cookies should remain soft and gooey
12. cool completely and sprinkle with more confectioners' sugar , if desired
13. to make these devilishly rich , i also top the cookies with cream cheese frosting , which is simple to make
14. i use bev's cream cheese frosting , but double the vanilla
15. or , if i'm making them for people i know have more of a savory tooth than sweet , i'll triple it to a full tablespoon
demonstrations.review:
If I could give these cookies 10 stars I would! As my 11 y/o son said "Oh My Gosh, these cookies are excellent"
Thanks so much for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sarah s tilapia

ok, here it is! my first recipe post to the site, this recipe was given to me by my mom, i have no idea where she got it, but it is just awesome, simple to make, and it is the only fish my picky, picky 11 year old daughter will eat, she loves it! she actually begs me to make it. update: after reading the reviews, i just want to emphasize the importance of using panko breadcrumbs in this recipe. it makes a huge difference! i also have never baked this fish, so cannot predict the results. for those who have commented that the breading isn't sticking well, i have found that this happens to me as well, when i have used too much of the mustard/mayo combo. a thin coating is best! i hope you all enjoy this recipe, and thanks for taking the time to review it!

1. heat oil in large non-stick skillet over med
2. heat
3. combine mayo and mustard in small dish
4. combine next 4 ingred
5. on a plate and mix well
6. brush thin coating of mustard mayo combo on to both sides of each fish fillet
7. press each coated fillet into panko crumb mixture , coating well
8. press more crumbs into any bare areas
9. saute fillets in hot oil until lightly browned , turn and saute other side until lightly browned and fish is opaque
10. serve with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: My family loves this recipe - all 3 boys fight over the last piece. I switch it up and sometimes use cajun seasoning with the panko crumbs and sometimes Italian seasoning. Its fast & healthy ( I bake it in the oven) - saves me on a busy hockey night.

target.recipe_text:
olive bread  for the bread machine

my local bakery occasionally makes an absolutely fabulous olive bread which i have attempted to clone. this is the closest i can come to it and it is a very nice version though not as great as the original. as usual, the best ingredients make the best bread so get the best olives you can find - it really makes the difference.

1. first prepare the onion
2. sprinkle the slices with salt and allow to sit for 5 minutes
3. then rinse and squeeze to drain
4. the onion will be softer and not as sharp tasting
5. finely chop , you should have around 2 tablespoons
6. pit the olives with a sharp knife and roughly chop
7. add the olives , chopped onion , oregano , garlic and tomato paste together and grind in a little black pepper to taste
8. set the bread machine on the basic cycle which is around 3 hours
9. add the remaining ingredients into the bread machine in the order recommended by the manufacturer , and then add the olive mixture at the beep for extras
10. bake with a medium crust or dark if you like it that way
11. this bread is wonderful with a greek salad or spread with tarama or eggplant dip
target.review: Two years ago I was in Winnipeg for business and the hotel that I stayed at served this bread, I've been obessed in finding a recipe to recreate that memory.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic glazed chicken

this is from rachael ray’s 365: no repeats. it is great! easy and fast to make. i served it with sour cream mashed potatoes. the leftovers are great over pasta or plain polenta.

1. heat a large skillet over medium-high
2. add 2 tablespoons of olive oil an cook the chicken
3. transfer to a platter and cover with foil
4. return the pan to the heat and add the remaining tablespoon of olive oil , onions , thyme , rosemary and garlic
5. saut for 4-5 minutes
6. add the balsamic vinegar , honey and chicken stock
7. cook until reduced by
8. turn off the heat and add the butter
9. stir until the butter melts
10. add the chicken back to the pan and coat it in the glaze
demonstrations.review: It was almost like Chinese chicken only not as salty.  This was great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy shrimp   tortellini salad

a creamy tortellini salad that's fit to serve company. i came up with this on an extremely warm day when i wanted to prepare dinner early and serve something cool. this can be adjusted according to amounts or type herbs you prefer.you can substitute chicken for the shrimp.reduce fat by using low fat mayo and sour cream. serve this one with a green salad and a glass of your favorite white wine.cook time is prep and chill time

1. cook tortellini according to package directions
2. drain and set aside to cool
3. mix together sour cream , mayonnaise , basil and chives
4. stir in lemon pepper and garlic powder and salt
5. add sour cream dressing mixture to the cooked tortellini and shrimp
6. gently toss
7. chill at least 2 hours
demonstrations.review: I have made this three times already.  All three times there was nothing left.  Including Labor Day where my friend's husband begged his longtime friend's mother to make her "famous pasta salad" that everyone loves.  After all the dust cleared, this salad was gone, Momma's was still in the bowl no one touched hers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I found this recipe yesterday, printed it out for myself and another woman in my office.  Both of us made it for our families... I thought I would have some for lunch today. There wasn't a drop of this left.  I used only one cup of heavy whipping cream for the two of us and used chopped garlic instead of the garlic power.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet  broccoli salad

this is a recipe i got from my sister who is the best cook i know. this a great recipe for a cook-out or picnic.

1. combine first 4 ingredients in a large bowl and mix
2. combine remaining ingredients to make dressing
3. pour dressing over broccoli mixture and mix well
4. refrigerate
5. if this is going to sit a while before serving , i suggest you wait to add the bacon until just before you serve to keep the bacon crisp
demonstrations.review: I have never personally made this recipe but I have a friend who has this exact same recipe and this is her signature dish to bring.  She brought it yesterday to a BBQ and it was gone in a matter of minutes.  She sometimes puts Feta cheese in instead of cheddar.  Either cheese that gets put in it, makes the salad great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amaretto sour cream strawberries

strawberries dipped in this cream mixture are so light, refreshing and good!  you can play with amounts used but i love it as directed.  leave on the strawberry tops to use as a handle to dip.  enjoy!

1. mix sour cream , amaretto , and powdered sugar together
2. chill
3. wash strawberries , keeping the tops on to use as a dipping handle
4. dip as you eat
demonstrations.review: These are great to have poolside.  I put a bowl full of ice under the the dip bowl and put it under the shade.  It was perfect coolness on a hot day.

target.recipe_text:
why i joined zaar carrot cake

on october 2, 2001, i discovered the recipezaar web site. i immediately joined so i could post a request for a recipe i had lost. in less than an hour, i had a reply: this recipe. unfortunately, i never posted it into the database -- until now. my mistake. this cake was the reason i joined, and the friendly response i received was the reason i stayed!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour a 9x13 inch pan
3. mix flour , baking soda , baking powder , salt and cinnamon
4. make a well in the center and add sugar , oil , eggs and vanilla
5. mix with wooden spoon until smooth
6. stir in carrots , coconut , walnuts and pineapple
7. pour into 9x13 inch pan and bake for about 45 minutes
8. don't panic , the centre will sink a little
9. allow to cool
10. when cool , ice the cake
11. you can certainly use your favourite cream cheese frosting to ice this cake , but the one i've included is highly recommended
12. to make the frosting: cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
13. add the icing sugar and beat until creamy
target.review: 1st time I make Carrot Cake because it aways seemed so complex....OH MY GOD! I followed the recipe to a T and the icing recipe and it was by far just as good as those expensive bakery carrot cakes! Will make again! Loved it! Thx for sharing:)<br/>Question: so I have made this about 5 times and I have discovered that the carrots turn green after a day? The carrots inside the cake? I have researched this and found it could be a reaction with baking soda???  Can anyone help me out with this issue? I love the cake and want to make but don't wAnt guests to be frightened by green carrots!!! Help my email is <br/>dabkeh@hotmail.com

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek potatoes  oven roasted and delicious

these potatoes are a staple in our home. whether accompanying roast lamb or chicken, or just on their own, we have them a couple of times a week. they are delicious and the ones that get overly-brown in the pan and stick a bit are mine!  clean up is a little tricky with this recipe, unless you line your pans with foil, but i find that just filling the pan up with hot, sudsy water and forgetting for an hour (something i apparently have no problem doing ;-)) helps a lot.

1. preheat oven to 420f a reviewer has suggested spraying the baking pan with pam - that sounds like a great idea !
2. put all the ingredients into a baking pan large enough to hold them
3. season generously with sea salt and black pepper
4. make sure your hands are very clean and put them in the pan and give everything a toss to distribute
5. the garlic will drop into the water / oil solution but its flavour will permeate the potatoes , and this way , it won't burn
6. bake for 40 minutes
7. when a nice golden-brown crust has formed on the potatoes , give them a stir to bring the white underside up , season lightly with a bit more sea salt and pepper and just a light sprinkling of oregano
8. add 1 / 2 cup more water if pan appears to be getting dry , and pop back into oven to brown other side of potatoes
9. this will take about another 40 minutes
10. do not be afraid of overcooking the potatoes- they will be delicious
demonstrations.review: Make all the time! Love it, big hit, I   Add extra garlic!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kafta  meatball shish kabobs

found this on another site...purported to be authentic lebanese cuisine. we think it's great!

1. soak wooden skewers in warm water for 30 minutes
2. mix all ingredients in a large bowl
3. divide into 6 portions and shape around one end of a skewer in a log shape , about 1 inch thick and 6 inches long
4. grill over high heat , turning several times , for 10-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent recipe...you can also broil it in the ovenif you want or make it on the skilt...either or is fine.  I also toast Lebanese bread or pita bread and brush some olive oil and garlic on it and place the kafta on top!  Yummy:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crepe batter

crepes have been a favorite in our family for years on sunday mornings. this recipe is the best we've found.

1. combine flour , milk , salt and eggs in a blender
2. blend for 15 seconds
3. scrape down sides
4. blend again and add butter while blending
5. blend 10 seconds
6. cover and let rest 1 hour in refridgerator
7. when ready to cook , heat and season crepe pan
8. pour enough batter onto a hot pan to coat
9. pour remaining batter back into the blender pitcher
10. cook over medium heat until edges just begin to brown
11. use a butter knife or spatula to remove crepe from pan
12. flatten and allow to cool slightly before filling
13. delicious sprinkled with sifted powdered sugar , or fill with your favorite fruit or pie filling and topped with whipped cream
demonstrations.review: Easy and delicious! Was nervous at first because there was clumps in the batter..but once I poured the batter onto the pan...they came out great!!!!!!!! thx:)  I spread nutella all over the crepe along with almonds, sliced bananas, strawberries and closed the crepe and placed powered sugar on top! sooo goood:)  I think next time I will make sure to use a BLENDER and Not a food processor...I think that is why it was clumpy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: I simmer the meatballs in the suace .and they turn out PERFECT! I add extra garlic:) Thx for sharing! LOVE this recipe:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best lebanese garlic sauce  by kay

last fall when leaving the u.s. to return home, we stopped-over in minneapolis for a family mini-reunion w/my aunt, uncle, their 7 children + various grandchildren i had not seen in 18+ yrs or even met b4. they are so lucky to all still live in the same city, but talk about the real *luck of the irish* - mike (my cousin) brought his lebanese heritage wife *kay* into our irish family & substantially raised the level of the cooking bar (already set pretty high). kay is a great cook & made the the most wonderful lebanese meal for us that included hummus, stuffed grape leaves, marinated + grilled lamb/chicken skewers & the most incredible garlic sauce i have ever tasted (just to mention a few). thank goodness the garlic sauce was not a recipe shrouded in generations of secrecy because i had to have it to share w/you. *enjoy* ! (see notes below)

1. place ingredients in a blender , blend till smooth & chill for several hrs b4 use to allow the full flavor to develop
2. done !
3. i have no patience for that
4. when i have tried it that way , i could never get my garlic sauce thick
5. adding the egg whites is technically cheating , but it works every time
6. i used the euro shopper brand corn oil , kay's recipe + the thin stream addition of the oil method w / excellent results ~ a richly garlic-flavored & thick sauce
7. i did add some seasoning salt to better match the icelandic garlic sauce that is sold commercially & very popular to serve w / lamb
8. :-)
demonstrations.review: I make this too.  I am a true GARLIC lover.  However, I do NOT put any EGG WHITES.  The key is to put the garlic and salt in a  food processor, and SLOWLY VERY SLOWLY drizzle the corn oil in....as you drizzle you will notice the garlic to become WHIPPED and not liquidy.  As, you finish putting in the corn oil, you add the lemon juice and  notice the color of the garlic sauce/dip to be even more WHITE(due to the lemon juice) If this is toooo strong for you..you may add a can of cooked potatoes to the food processor and it will be JUST AS good and whippy too!  Enjoy with your favorite meat and CHICKEN!

target.recipe_text:
easy creamy sour cream chicken casserole

this is one of the first recipes i really "mastered" when i was learning how to cook. my husband got to enjoy this recipe at least twice a month because it was one of the few dishes i knew how to make. now, that i'm a much better cook, we still have this delicious dinner on our menu at least monthly. it is so easy to put together and very good. if you like your casserole's creamy, then this is one you've gotta try! i hope you enjoy it as much as we do!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. boil chicken breast until tender
3. drain and cube
4. spread evenly over the bottom of a square casserole dish
5. salt and pepper to taste
6. mix sour cream and chicken soup in a separate bowl
7. spread the sour cream and soup mixture over the chicken in the casserole dish
8. crush the ritz crackers and spread over top of the casserole
9. spoon melted butter on top over all
10. bake in a 350f oven until top is golden brown , approximately 20-30 minutes
target.review: This was terrific!  I actually added half a pound of pasts, cooked al dente, 1/2 cup of shredded jack cheese, about 1/3 cup of milk to compensate for the noodles and used evoo instead of butter and it was terrific!!!  I was just very pleased.  I couldn't decide between this or the chili dog casserole thing I found so I made both full sized casseroles and 4 adults ate EVERYTHING!!!  So you know it was good!  I will definitely be making this one often.  Thanks! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean guy s general tso s chicken

this is an adoptee.  i have made it many many times and want to be able to help people out when they make it!  one of the best i've ever had.  takes some time, but oh so worth it.   good eats ;-)

1. in a large bowl , thoroughly blend the 1 / 2 cup of cornstarch and the eggs
2. add the chicken and toss to coat
3. if the mixture is too thick , add some vegetable oil to separate the pieces
4. in a small bowl , prepare the sauce mixture by combining the 2 tsp cornstarch with the wine , vinegar , sugar and soy sauce
5. first-stage frying: heat 1-2 inches of peanut oil in a wok to medium-high heat
6. fry the chicken in small batches , just long enough to cook the chicken through
7. remove the chicken to absorbent paper and allow to stand
8. second-stage frying: leave a tablespoon or two of the oil in the wok
9. add the pepper pods to the oil and stir-fry briefly , awakening the aroma but not burning them
10. return the chicken to the wok and stir-fry until the pieces are crispy brown
11. the general's favorite sauce: add the sauce-mixture to the wok , tossing over the heat until the sauce caramelizes into a glaze
12. serve immediately
13. serves 4 , along with steamed broccoli and rice
demonstrations.review: I made a big error making this one, but even with my goof up it still ended up tasting good.  I forgot to brown up my chicken and just put my liquid mixture into the pan without chicken being in there...well it turned into a big huge jello-ish ball lol  I have no clue what happend but nothing I did would thin it down..I tried some more wine, water, chicken stock lol  it just got bigger and bigger...so strange!  So I threw my chicken on top of my blob and just mixed it all in...and it still turned out good!  I'll definitely make this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy shortbread tart crust  no roll

looked and looked on zaar for just the shortbread crust and found many delicious crusts, but just not the one i was looking for.  perhaps i didn't key in the right search, but i found this recipe on the web and it's just what i was looking for...simple.

1. blend ingredients to make a soft dough
2. pat into a 9 or 10 inch tart or pie pan
3. prick crust well with fork
4. bake in 350 degree oven for 15-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was a delicious crust...it tasted good before I even cooked it!  The only reason I am giving it 4 stars was because I found it almost impossible to press it into my pan!  It wouldn't stop sticking to my fingers so I put a little water on my hands and that didn't work..Pam..didn't work...then I used the back of a measuring cup and that didn't work either!  So I basically just gobbed it together and did the best I could.  I also used this for the Blueberry sour cream pie and it was cooked perfect even without prebaking it.  I will try this again...I just have to figure out why it was sticking to me!  Oh, I also tried adding a tad more flour...didn't work!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted grape tomatoes

these tiny tomatoes give a burst of concentrated tomato flavor to just about anything... pizza, salads, pasta sauces, as an accompaniment to roasted meat or fish, or just plain, hot out of the oven... i can eat them like popcorn! i especially like them atop a salad of spring greens with warmed goat cheese... divine! and since these little tomatoes are available year round, it's a great way to enjoy tomatoes even in the winter.

1. heat oven to 250-275
2. toss all ingredients in bowl , stirring to coat
3. line baking sheet with parchment or foil
4. spread tomatoes in single layer on baking sheet
5. bake for approximately one hour , or until skins have shriveled slightly and juices are caramelized
demonstrations.review: So I found this recipe maybe an hour and a half ago...I made 2 pints of roasted grape tomatoes...and before their cooking time was over they were all gone..LOL!  They were GREAT!  I too ate them just like I would popcorn!  I bought six pints that were a quarter each at the store and was trying to find a recipe to use them up...this is it!  Tomorrow I'll roast the rest for dinner...I just wanted to see how good they would be tonight!!  I added some Tastefully Simple Garlic Garlic, other than that I followed exact.  Delish, sooooo happy I came across this!  I've been eating too many desserts, so this was a nice change of pace :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best rice pudding

left over rice never had it so good ! this creamy pudding is the perfect way to use up the extra white rice from chinese take-out or from tonight's supper, and delicious enough to make you cook some up fresh, just so you can have this for dessert! tastes great warm or cold--enjoy!!

1. in large bowl , combine sugar , salt , cornstarch and nutmeg
2. add milk , egg yolks , and vanilla , using wire whisk to beat until smooth
3. add cooked rice , and pour into a 1 and 1 / 2 quart baking dish--you can also use a 9 x 9 square baking dish , but you'll need to decrease the cooking time by at least 15 minutes , if not more , so check carefully after the first hour
4. place baking dish into larger pan , and pour hot water into outer pan to create a 1 inch deep water bath
5. bake at 350 degrees , stirring occasionally , for 1 1 / 2 hours , or until pudding is creamy and milk is absorbed
demonstrations.review: I accidentally made 5 times too much rice yesterday (realizing as I was pouring water on top of it lol) so today I have been making all things rice...and this was my winner choice for dessert and omg it isn't even out of the oven yet and it's delish!  I stirred it a little about half way through and mmmmm!!  It's great! I made curry for dinner, so I used coconut milk (all I have is skim milk) to see if it would work and so far it is!  I also added some cinnamon and I'm going to top it with toasted coconut flakes.  Thanks for this delicious recipe! It was super easy to throw together too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my own coleslaw dressing

when made with slaw this is a great recipe to use with pulled pork barbeque. i have been making cole slaw this way for years. the slaw is simple to prepare using your food processor to shred the cabbage and carrot. i hope you enjoy it!

1. combine mayonnaise , lemon juice , celery seed , sugar and salt and pepper
2. for cole slaw , toss dressing with shredded cabbage and carrot
3. chill
demonstrations.review: I am a fairly new Coleslaw lover...I wanted something different and I feel like I keep finding the KFC copy cat recipes but I like how simple this is!  I loved the lemon instead of vinegar, you could really taste the tang when served over top of pulled bbq chicken sandwiches!  I didn't have any celery seed (which if I did I prob wouldn't use b/c I hate them) so I microplaned about half a stick of celery to put a little bit of celery flavor in it.  I also added some of the zest of the lemon...loved it!  Will definitely use this as a go to recipe for coleslaw!  Another great thing is that this is all stuff I keep on hand all the time!  Thanks :)

target.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
target.review: Nice texture. Very chocolatey. I added m&m's and raisins. The raisins paired surprisingly well with the chocolate.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
artichoke bruschetta

a really great tapa that will get you many compliments. really simple to make. the original recipe was by roxanne. i have served this at many of my "wine and tapa" parties and was always pleased by the response.

1. preheat the broiler
2. place the bread slices on a baking sheet and toast lightly under the broiler
3. in a medium bowl , mix marinated artichoke hearts , romano or parmesan cheese , red onion , crushed garlic , diced tomato and mayonnaise
4. top the lightly toasted french baguette slices with equal amounts of the artichoke heart mixture being careful to spread the mixture over the entire surface
5. the edges of the bread will tend to burn if not covered by the artichoke mixture
6. arrange slices in a single layer on the baking sheet
7. broil in the preheated oven 2 minutes , or until toppings are bubbly and lightly browned
demonstrations.review: My husband loved this soo much, he kept reminding me to leave feedback !!! This deserves every 5 star rating it has got. Simple ingredients, easy to make and very delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted cauliflower   16 roasted cloves of garlic

i find it totally amazing, that children and men all  love this recipe!  as for the female of our species we just love this for the flavor and the health benefits it brings our families.
roasted brings out a wonderful sweetness in this dish. the garlic is roasted to a tan color is creamy good. you can just pop them in your mouth. or you can spread them on your florets or fresh bread. just be sure to scoop up some of the rosemary, olive oil and black pepper that may have escaped to the bottom of the dish.
for halloween check out recipe #396674 version of my recipe.

1. mix oil , rosemary , salt , pepper and garlic together
2. toss in cauliflower and place in a large casserole dish in one layer
3. roast in a preheated oven at 450 degrees for 20 minutes
4. give a toss and bake for 10 more minutes
demonstrations.review: My kids suggested I make this with 2 cauliflowers the next time :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cucumber and garbanzo bean salad

a friend of mine gave me this recipe. i love having this during the summer time.

1. in a medium bowl , combine beans , cucumber , onion , parsley and olives
2. in another bowl or jar combine remaining ingredients , mix well
3. pour over salad and toss
4. serve immediately or chill for up to 24 hours
demonstrations.review: I was really not sure about 3 tablespoons of red wine vinegar and 1 tablespoon of sugar. It all went together very well and tasted surprisingly good !

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I thought it was a wee bit too salty, but my kids LOVED it !! I think the cajun seasoning I added already had salt in it. My advice would be taste the sauce first and salt at the very end, if required.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
denny s style french toast

i do not remember where i got this recipe, but my husband says it tastes just as good as what he had at denny's. i am just amazed at all of the great reviews on this recipe!! my family loves it, so i thought i would share it here and i'm so glad i did because it seems you all love it just as much!!! thanks to all of you who have tried it!

1. mix together the eggs , milk , flour , sugar , vanilla , salt& cinnamon
2. heat a large skillet , or griddle
3. when the skillet is hot , add 1 tablespoon butter
4. if the butter smokes , your pan is too hot
5. turn down the heat
6. dip each slice of bread into the batter for 30 seconds on each side
7. let some of the batter drip off , then put in skillet
8. cook each slice 1 1 / 2-2 minutes per side until each side is golden brown
9. add more butter , if necessary , to cook all of the slices
10. to serve , put on plate , dust with powdered sugar
11. serve with butter & hot syrup
demonstrations.review: This always gets rave reviews from my kids.

target.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
target.review: Yummy! It was the bomb. I made it exactly as written with the additional of finely chopped green peppers and mushrooms. So good...this will be made again and again. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeo chicken crescent pinwheels

a 2004 pillsbury bake-off winner

1. heat oven to 375f in small bowl , mix all ingredients except dough until well combined
2. set aside
3. unroll dough
4. separate into 2 long rectangles
5. place 1 rectangle on long cutting board
6. press perforations to seal
7. spread half of cream cheese mixture on dough rectangle to within 1 / 2 inch of edges
8. starting with one long side , roll up rectangle
9. press seam to seal
10. cut roll into 16 slices
11. place slices , cut side down , on ungreased cookie sheet
12. repeat with remaining dough rectangle
13. bake at 375f for 14 to 16 minutes or until light golden brown
14. immediately remove from cookie sheet
15. serve warm
demonstrations.review: I have made this once and will make again with tweaks: the filling needs to be spread on thicker all the way to the edge and I will add a little hot sauce to the mix and less jalepeno. Definately something to play around with because it is really good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crescent layer bars

this simple to make recipe came from pillsbury annual recipes 2008. it includes some of my favorites - cashews and of course....chocolate (both white and semisweet)!

bars like these that contain sweetened condensed milk can be stored at room temperature.

i just made these bars this morning and have not actually tried them yet. but they look great & smell wonderful!  please let me know what you think...

1. 1) heat oven to 375 degrees
2. grease bottom and sides of 13x9 pan
3. unroll dough into 2 long rectangles
4. place in pan
5. press over bottom and 1 / 2 inch up sides to form crust
6. bake 5 minutes
7. 2) remove partially baked crust from oven
8. sprinkle white chocolate chips , chocolate chips , almonds and cashews evenly over crust
9. pour sweented condensed milk evenly over top
10. 3) bake 20 to 25 longer or until golden brown
11. cool 10 minutes
12. run knife around sides of pan to loosen
13. cool 1 hour
14. refrigerate 30 minutes or until chocolate is set
15. cut into 6 rows by 6 rows
demonstrations.review: We had this at a get together recently and it was really good and the recipe is so easy. They actually look and taste like an elaborate recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy chicken  bacon   tater tot crock pot bake

this is a simple throw-together dish i came up with that is great for a sunday after-church meal. note: you can fry your own bacon for this recipe. i like the taste of bacon but cannot handle the lingering smell it leaves in the house when you fry it, so i just buy the jarred bacon for the few times a year i use it.

1. grease the bottom of the crock pot
2. layer 1 / 2 the tater tots on the bottom of the pot
3. sprinkle with 1 / 4 of the jar of bacon bits
4. combine the two cheeses , and sprinkle 1 / 3 of it over the bacon and tots
5. top cheese with the chicken breasts
6. sprinkle chicken with salt and pepper to taste
7. top chicken with another 1 / 3 of cheese
8. sprinkle with another 1 / 4 of the jar of bacon bits
9. add remainder of the tater tots
10. top with final 1 / 3 of the cheese
11. pour milk over the top
12. set crock pot to high and cook 3-4 hours
demonstrations.review: This is awesome! So good and easy to prepare. My only change next time will be to use boneless skinless chicken thighs, and dice them up. The chicken can get a little dry using the white meat. Also, used the Oscar Meyer Bacon pieces in the pouch, yummy! Such a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork steak

my husband loves this pork steak. it is fork tender, tasty & easy to make.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat
3. brown steaks on each side
4. while browning , season steaks with salt , pepper , and garlic powder
5. transfer steaks to a 9x13 inch casserole dish
6. saut the onions and mushrooms in the same skillet
7. add water , worcestershire sauce , dry soup mix , and mushroom soup
8. mix together until sauce forms
9. pour sauce over steaks
10. cover dish with aluminum foil
11. bake in preheated oven for 90 minutes
demonstrations.review: I had always prefered chops over steaks, until now. This is a keeper. One of my favorite pork dishes...highly recommend!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I  followed the recipe to a "t" and it was so good. I will make it again soon.

target.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
target.review: Sorry, but my family didn't enjoy this as much as I expected.  It wasn't the flavor of what was there, it just that there was something missing.  I served it with salsa, sr crm, and lettuce and still seemed like it needs a sauce of some sort.  Maybe an enchilada gravy. It did crisp up nicely. I followed the recipe exactly, no substitutions except salsa instead of picante.  I may try again using shredded beef instead of chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy double chocolate chip cookies

i got this recipe from my best friend, and we sat down and ate quite a few. you can not stop at one, they are very chocolaty and additive. yummy!

1. cream together the butter , sugar , then add the eggs and vanilla
2. blend in the cocoa and add baking soda , salt and blend well
3. add the flour into the creamed mixture and fold in the chocolate chips
4. bake at 350 for 8-9 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I have named these my mmmm Good, Got Milk cookies.  These are truely one of the best cookies I have tried.  Here are the changes I made to the recipe.

1.  Substituted 1 cup Crisco + 3 Tbl water + 1/4 cup butter for margarine.  This eliminated the problem others talked about with the cookies being too oily.  I also cooked on parchment paper.

2. Used 1 cup sugar and 1 cup brown sugar per others suggestion.

3. Used hershey's premium dark cocoa.

4.  Used 1 cup white chocolate chips and 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips per others suggestion.

5.  Make sure to really blend well in step 3 so the eggs actually fluff up the batter some. And don't blend much when adding the flour or your cookies will be tough.

I made larger cookies (slightly over flowing #50 scoop) and baked for 14 minutes.

They came out soft and chewy and oh so delicious. THANK YOU Tweety Grams for a terrific recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: We all really liked these meatballs.  I made them with seasoned salt.  The only thing I may change next time is swapping out the oregano for basil.  I did fry them and used them in #26947 Mama Iuliucci's Sauce.  It was excellent.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: We all really enjoyed this. I made it on the stove as outlined in several previous posts.  I added thick sliced onions the last 5 minutes. It was extreemly tender.  I didn't want it to seem like a chinese meal so I served it with noodles instead of rice.  It still had a chinese flavor because of the ginger but the onions and sauce where very tasty on the noodles.  There were no leftovers. It's a keeper.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade hamburger buns  bread machine

you will never want to buy hamburger buns again after trying this recipe. easy to do using a bread machine and so awesome! you can also top rolls with sesame seeds after brushing with melted butter.

1. place all ingredients , except butter , in pan of bread machine according to manufacturer's directions
2. select dough setting
3. when cycle is complete , turn out onto floured surface
4. cut dough in half and roll each half out to a 1" thick circle
5. cut each half into six 3 1 / 2" rounds with inverted glass as a cutter
6. place on greased baking sheet far apart and brush with melted butter
7. cover and let rise until doubled , about one hour
8. bake at 350 for 9 minutes
9. some reviewers baked these anywhere from 12 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed these.  No more preservative flavored, half stale buns, in my household.  They were a huge hit when I made bbq pork and chicken sandwiches. THANKS!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat kfc coleslaw  the real thing

i am an avid collector of recipes. a young lady, a former kfc employee, was looking at my recipes one evening when she discovered this one. she told me that the recipe was close, but that i should remove the vinegar and lemon juice and replace them with tarragon vinegar. tarragon vinegar is the secret. note: this is one of the recipes i adopted in the great 'zaar orphan adoption of 2005. i hope you enjoy it.

1. mix oil , onions and sugar
2. add tarragon vinegar
3. fold in miracle whip
4. pour over grated carrots and cabbage
5. fold in well
6. refrigerate in an air-tight covered dish
7. best if made the night before serving
8. the tarragon is the secret seasoning
9. compare with the real kfc coleslaw
10. enjoy
demonstrations.review:
I used Kraft Light Mayo (it's what I had on hand) and I think if I would have used Miracle Whip this would have gotten a 5. It just needed a little "tang" to it. But it still was very good and I will definately make this again (the right way). I only used 1 really large head of cabbage and it was plenty.

UPDATE - Made with Miracle Whip and it was perfect.  Updated it to 5 stars.  BEST EVER.  Even better after 2 days.

target.recipe_text:
country white bread or dinner rolls  bread machine

we think this is the best white bread recipe ever! it is a tender bread with a slightly sweet taste. my dinner rolls using this dough are so good, everyone always loves them. it doesn't take to long to make them when the bread maker does most of the work. the cook time is listed for the rolls only because everyone's bread makers cooks at different rates. mine is older and a regular loaf will take 4 hours and 10 minutes. i have found that 15 balls of dough fit perfectly in the 9x13 pan with sides touching after raising the 2nd time but they can be made whatever size you want. i hope you enjoy this great bread as much as we do.

1. in bread machine pan , place all ingredients from flour through yeast in order as recommended by the manufacturer
2. select the basic bread setting
3. check dough after 5 minutes of mixing , if needed add 1-2t of water or flour
4. bake as normal
5. for dinner rolls
6. mix in bread machine but use only the dough option
7. lightly grease a 9 x 13 baking pan
8. when dough is finished shape into 15 uniformly sized balls
9. i always grease my hands with shortening to smooth the dough out and it helps keep the dough from drying out
10. cover and let the rolls rise in a warm , draft free place until risen to the desired size
11. i let them about double in size
12. bake in a 350 oven about 12-15 minutes until golden brown
13. after removing from the oven , brush the tops of the rolls with melted butter
14. take out of pan and let completely cool before storing
target.review: These are, literally, the best rolls I have ever had. It made exactly the amount of beautiful rolls you said it would, perfect for a 9X13 pan. We had the rolls with dinner and made sandwiches with them the next morning. Wonderful texture and taste; I will make these again and again! UPDATE: I make these at least once a week now. EVERYONE loves them! I use them to make sandwiches frequently, delicious with a little meat and cheese!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s creamy chicken gravy

this should yield about 3 cups gravy, if you don't use it all you can freeze it, use a good-quality chicken broth for this

1. in a heavy saucepan melt butter over medium-high heat
2. whisk in flour and stir constantly for 1 minute
3. slowly add in broth , chicken bouillon powder , half and half or milk , pinch garlic powder and dryed onions
4. stir / whisk over medium heat until smooth and thickened
5. add in lots black pepper and salt if desired
6. delicious !
demonstrations.review: I wanted a classic (and-dare I say-yellow) creamy chicken gravy and this was perfect. Very reminiscent of classic diner type chicken gravy. Kittencal's recipes never let me down!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous barbecue sauce for chicken and ribs

this is the best barbecue sauce, and trust me i have experimented with hundreds of different combinations over the years,  this is even better than any of the popular bottled sauces! ---plan ahead this sauce must be made one day in advance to allow the flavors to blend and intensify, don't even think about using it the same day it is made,  this sauce will take on a whole different flavor when simmered for 1 hour and left overnight in the fridge--- the ingredients can easily be doubled but keep the garlic amount no more than 2 tablespoons, and for the best flavor use only heinz ketchup and a good quality brand of yellow mustard, i use french's mustard it really will make a difference in the taste, please do not omit the liquid smoke --- yield is only estimated as the sauce will reduce after simmering for 1 hour or more  ---*note* for a smoother low fat sauce omit the oil, onion and fresh garlic, then in the saucepan mix all remaining ingredients together and add in 1 teaspoon each garlic powder and onion powder then simmer for 1 hour -----you will love this sauce!

1. heat oil over medium heat
2. add in onion and saute for about 3 minutes , then add in garlic and saute for 2 minutes
3. add in chili powder , paprika , cayenne , salt and black pepper
4. stir for 1 minute
5. add in all remaining ingredients
6. bring to a boil stirring with a wooden spoon to combine
7. reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered stirring occasionally for 1 hour over low heat
8. cool to room temperature then cover and refrigerate for 24 hours or more before using
demonstrations.review: This sauce is excellent! It's a little spicy, a little sweet,  smokey and super thick! I used dried onions and garlic (I had no fresh) but otherwise followed the recipe exactly. I have used it on ribs and chicken so far and love it on both. My friends have used it on their burgers and said it was wonderful there as well. For reference, you really DO have to let this sit in the fridge for a day. Don't worry, its WELL worth the wait. Thanks Kittencal, I just LOVE all of your recipes I've tried!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect blueberry pie filling

i love the the texture and flavor this technique produces in making blueberry filling. if you are tired of the overly processed and overly cornstarched taste of blueberry pie filling, give this a try. method produces a "fresh blueberry" taste.

1. combine 1 cup berries with 3 / 4 cup sugar in pan
2. simmer on low heat until sugar is melted and mixture is very liquid
3. about 5 minutes
4. combine cornstarch and water in bowl
5. add to pan with blueberries
6. cook over medium heat until mixture comes to full boil and is clear and thick
7. pour hot mixture into large bowl
8. cool until warm
9. fold in remaining 3 cups of blueberries , lemon rind , cinnamon , nutmeg and butter
10. let cool before adding to pie crust
11. add top crust and brush with egg wash , sprinkle with sugar
12. preheat oven to 400f but reduce heat to 375f when you put pie in oven
13. bake about 40 minutes
14. check pie halfway through baking
15. cover edges with a strip of foil if edges are getting too brown
16. this technique works for any delicate fruit such as raspberries or strawberries
demonstrations.review: Fabulous! I tripled it with great success. Thanks for the easy, delicious, GF (gluten free) recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian pork balls with napa cabbage

two of my most favorite ingredients in one recipe...sesame oil and sherry. what more could you ask for? i found this recipe online when i was low-carbing (just omitted the cornstarch and thickened the sauce by boiling it down) and then i tweaked it a little bit to suit my tastes.

1. mix together the first seven ingredients and form into golf-ball sized balls
2. place the pork balls on a baking sheet and bake at 375f for 25 minutes
3. place the pork balls in a large pot with the 1 cup of chicken broth , the 1 tablespoon soy sauce and the 1 tablespoon sherry and bring to a boil
4. cover , reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes
5. add the napa cabbage , cover , and simmer for 10 more minutes
6. dissolve the 1 tablespoon cornstarch in the 2 tablespoons cold water
7. remove the pork balls and cabbage from the liquid and arrange on a serving platter
8. stir the cornstarch slurry into the remaining liquid and bring it back to a boil
9. once the sauce has thickened , pour it over the pork balls and cabbage
demonstrations.review: This was very good. Followed the recipe exactly (except I added some chopped green onions to the cabbage...oops not exactly, I guess!) and I was very happy with the results. We will be adding this to our regulars! Thanks for posting such a great recipe. P.S. Reminds me of Chinese Lion's Head!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade hershey s chocolate syrup

i started making this to use in my daughter's chocolate milk, since i am not a fan of hfcs, and a teeny bottle of organic chocolate syrup was over $4.   i double the batch and store in a 32 oz rubbermaid "chug" bottle.  you can store this in the fridge in any clean container with a spout for several months.

1. whisk cocoa powder and milk together thoroughly in a large saucepan
2. heat and whisk to dissolve the cocoa
3. add the sugar and stir / whisk to dissolve
4. be sure the sugar has dissolved before continuing on , so your syrup is not grainy
5. bring to a boil and boil for 3 minutes
6. be sure to watch this very carefully
7. mine has a tendency to want to boil over immediately , so i have to continuously take it on and off of the burner
8. remove from heat and stir in salt and vanilla extract
9. let cool completely and skim off any skin that may have formed
10. pour into a clean / sterile jar with a spout and store covered in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: From the bottom of my heart: THANK YOU for posting this recipe. It is fantsasic. I made exactly as listed and wouldn't change a thing. I'll never buy nesquick or hersheys ever again, This was so simple, tasty, and cheap! I had 2 glasses of chocolate milk before this even cooled (oops, shame on me!) Highly recommended!

target.recipe_text:
olive garden style chicken and gnocchi soup

this is very close to the olive garden soup. there's another recipe on the web, which was the basis of this recipe, however, i have changed it to use less cream. still tastes good! i did end up using a little cornstarch to thicken. i guess you could sub heavy cream for the half-and-half to make it a little thicker without using cornstarch. the gnocchi is usually in the spaghetti section of the grocery store.

1. saute the onion , celery , garlic , carrot in oil over medium heat until onion is translucent
2. add chicken , chicken stock , half and half , salt and pepper , thyme
3. heat to boiling , then add gnocchi
4. gently boil for 4 minutes , then turn down to a simmer for 10 minutes
5. add spinach and cook for another 1-2 minutes until spinach is wilted
6. ladle into bowls and serve !
target.review: As suggested in other reviews, I cooked the gnocchi until light and fluffy. Sauteed the vegetables, along some diced, thin slices of red and green pepper in a dab of butter and a couple splashes of olive oil. Substituted shredded bacon-crusted turkey breast deli slices for the diced chicken. Despite using only skim milk to cut calories, the soup was delicious. I also thought this soup is as good or better than OG's. Thanks for posting this recipe Anne.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan fried trout

this adoptee is the way we make trout on our backpacking trips, we take corneal and butter packets and hope we catch dinner.  just as easy to make at home, its a taste of the outdoors.

1. rinse the trout under cold running water
2. pat dry
3. sprinkle with salt and pepper
4. melt the butter in a large heavy skillet on medium-high heat
5. coat the trout in corn meal and shake off the excess
6. when the butter is melted , place the coated trout , flesh side down , in the skillet
7. fry 4-5 minutes , then turn and fry 4-5 minutes or until the flesh is golden brown and flaky
demonstrations.review: So easy and delicious, especially when served with homemade tartar sauce!  I also add the seasonings mentioned by other reviewers. I rarely try another recipe to pan fry walleye -- this one is perfect for my family.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bottom banana bars

delicious and very moist. even better the second day.

1. in a mixing bowl , cream butter and sugar
2. add egg and vanilla
3. beat until thoroughly combined
4. blend in the bananas
5. combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
6. add to creamed mixture and mix well
7. divide batter in half
8. add cocoa to half
9. spread into a greased 13-in x 9-in pan
10. spoon remaining batter on top and swirl with a knife
11. bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes or until the bars test done
12. cool
demonstrations.review:
Thanks Debster for a delicious recipe. Cut out most of the fat by using 1/3 c. of applesauce and about a Tbsp. of margarine (although butter probably would have been more flavorable). Cut the sugar to 3/4 cup and used 1 cup of flour. After baking, added a light dusting of powdered sugar on top.

This recipe is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tasty ramen broccoli cole slaw

a really nice blend of crisp broccoli, nuts and a tangy sweet dressing!  friends and i have differing opinions on this one.....i like it best when it's first made and the noodles are crunchy, some seem to like it best after a day or two in the fridge when they are softer....it's really good either way!

1. heat butter and olive oil in large saute pan
2. crush ramen noodles and add to pan along with almonds
3. saute for approx 5-7 minutes or until noodles and almonds are lightly browned
4. set aside
5. in very large salad bowl , combine broccoli , broccoli slaw and sunflowers
6. add toasted noodle / almond mixture and toss
7. make dressing by whisking together in a small bowl: vegetable oil , brown sugar , apple cider vinegar and the ramen noodle seasoning packet
8. pour dressing over salad and toss
9. top with chopped green onions
10. serve immediately for crisp noodle slaw , or refrigerate for one day for softer noodle slaw
demonstrations.review: I brought this dish to a family reunion and everyone that tried it wanted the recipe. When we make it at home it barely lasts two days between my husband and I. We just can't stop eating it. Have ommitted the onions sometimes, but we found there is even better flavor with them. To cut down on sodium, I often omit the ramen seasoning in the dressing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornbread   sausage stuffing

got this recipe from a sausage ad - very good for thanksgiving, or anytime.

1. cook sausage in large skillet until browned
2. remove with slotted spoon& drain
3. saute onion& celery in remaining sausage drippings until tender
4. combine sausage , sauteed vegetables , bread cubes , cornbread , sage , marjoram& pepper in a large mixing bowl
5. blend well
6. moisten with chicken broth
7. mixture can be stuffed into turkey , or placed into a greased 13x9 baking dish& dot with butter
8. cover& bake 20 minutes at 350f
9. uncover& bake 10 minutes more , or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: I've never been a fan of dressing and I picked this recipe for my husband. I'm now a fan! I used light dry rye bread cubes and sage sausage. Made the recipe the day before and baked for 20 min. and finished baking the next day.  Cut the recipe in half because we were having smoked turkey and the stuffing was going to be a side dish -- this stuffing was delicious and I would love to have more leftovers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy stove top stuffing meatloaf

threw this together one night.  i see several variations out there.  this one is super easy and delicious.

1. mix first four ingredients in a large bowl
2. pat into an 8 x 8 square pan
3. spread a thin layer of ketchup on top
4. bake at 350 for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Use a cornbread stuffing mix. Love, love this recipe. I stopped looking for an alternative.

target.recipe_text:
cranberry hazelnut biscotti

these extra-crisp cookies contain no butter or oil. great with watermelon. i got this recipe out of bon appetit.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. line large baking sheet with parchment paper
3. beat eggs and sugar in bowl until thick
4. beat in peel and vanilla
5. slowly beat in flour , baking soda and salt
6. beat in cranberries and nuts
7. using floured hands , divide dough into 2 balls
8. flatten each to 1 inch thickness
9. brush beaten egg whites
10. sprinkle with additional sugar
11. bake for 20 minutes or until golden brown , reduce heat to 320 and cut on a diagonal line every 3 / 4 inches
12. arrange cut sides down on baking sheet
13. bake until bottoms are brown about 7 minutes
target.review: This recipe was excellent - low fat and very tasty.  However, it was way too sweet, I'll reduce the sugar to 2/3 cup the next time.  Substituted lemon juice for the vanilla, and lemon peel for the orange peel.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter banana muffins

i found this tasty muffin recipe in a magazine ad for quaker oats.

1. heat oven to 375f
2. grease 12 medium muffin cups , or line with paper baking cups
3. combine flour , oats , brown sugar and baking powder
4. whisk together milk , peanut butter , banana , egg , oil and vanilla
5. add to dry ingredients , mixing just until moistened
6. fill muffin cups 3 / 4 full
7. combine topping ingredients
8. sprinkle evenly over batter
9. bake 16 to 18 minutes or until golden brown
10. serve warm
demonstrations.review: Very good but a little on the heavy side.  I added 1/2 tsp baking soda and substituted butter milk for the milk and it turned out beautiful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggplant  aubergine  pepper kugel

this is a savory hearty winter kugel, from cooking light.

1. heat oven to 450f
2. pierce eggplant several times with a fork
3. line a baking sheet with tin foil , place eggplant on foil
4. bake for 20 minutes until tender
5. cool , peel , and chop , place in a large bowl
6. heat oil in a skillet
7. add onion , green pepper , and nuts
8. cook 5-10 minutes until veggies are tender
9. add to eggplant with salt , pepper , and eggs
10. mix well
11. add matzoh meal , stir well
12. coat a baking dish with cooking spray , add mixture , and then sprinkle with paprika
13. bake for 35-45 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Very delicious and easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christmas mincemeat squares

because of the whole wheat flour, i've always felt these squares were somewhat healthy. maybe i'm kidding myself, but i definitely can say they're delicious, and perfect for any holiday goodie platter.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. grease a 13x9 pan and set aside
3. in a large mixing bowl , combine the flour , oats , sugar and baking soda
4. stir in melted butter and mix together until mixture appears crumbly
5. firmly pat half the crumb mixture into prepared pan , then cover evenly with mincemeat
6. sprinkle remaining crumb mixture over mincemeat and pat lightly
7. bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until squares appear golden brown
8. cool before cutting into squares
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe. I reduced the sugar to only 1/4 cup because the mincemeat filling was extremely sweet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry banana oat muffins

these tasty muffins are a good way to use up over-ripe bananas and are great for those who are allergic to dairy products as they can be made with either butter or non-dairy margarine. this recipe was developed in the test kitchens of robin hood multifoods.

1. combine the first six ingredients in a mixing bowl
2. mix well
3. beat together egg , bananas and melted butter or margarine until smooth
4. add to dry ingredients
5. stir to blend
6. stir in cranberries just until combined
7. spoon batter into prepared muffin pan , filling almost to the top
8. bake at 375 degrees f for 20 to 25 minutes or until the top springs back when lightly touched
demonstrations.review: Excellent tasting and healthy muffins.  I serve these regularly at our B & B.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
english christmas pudding ii

nan

1. mix all dry ingredients , fruit , raisins , nuts and suet
2. add molasses and then milk to rinse all molasse s into the mixture
3. mix well
4. grease and flour a 3 pound empty crisco can or similar size , smooth sided can
5. put mixture into can
6. cover with double thickness of aluminum foil
7. tie foil on with string
8. set can in large pot or kettle half full of water
9. cover and steam 2 1 / 2 hours after water boils
10. serve slices covered with hot vanilla sauce and real whipped cream
11. bring 3 1 / 2 cups milk and vanilla bean to a boil
12. whip sugar and yolks over hot water to lukewarm
13. stir in cornstarch to remaining cold milk
14. add the cornstarch mixture to the boiling mixture and bring to a full boil
15. pour the boiling starch-milk over the lukewarm egg-sugar mixture , whisking forcefully
16. keep warm on steam table or double boiler
17. this sauce is good over puddings and souffles
demonstrations.review: Excellent pudding with an aromatic and spicy flavour.  I'll increase the amount of candied peel and raisins the next time as we all like it loaded with dried fruits.

target.recipe_text:
mexican yellow rice and black beans

this recipe is adapted from american diabetes association cookbook--diabetes & heart healthy cookbook.  it is a delicious blending of southwestern flavors that is so simple to prepare.

1. bring the vegetable or chicken stock to a boil
2. stir in the turmeric and brown rice
3. bring rice to boiling , stir once , lower heat and cook 40 to 45 minutes or until done and liquid has been absorbed , adding more liquid if needed
4. heat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat , add 1 teaspoon of olive oil , warming slightly
5. to the warmed pan , add the onion , jalapeno , bell peppers , and red pepper flakes
6. cook for 4 minutes or until beginning to brown on the edges , remove from heat
7. stir the drained beans and cumin into the mixture adding salt to taste
8. let stand covered for 5 minutes
9. stir in the remaining 2 teaspoons of olive oil
10. to serve , divide the rice into 4 equal portions and place on individual plates
11. top the rice with bean mixture , sprinkle with cheese and snipped cilantro
12. serve lime wedges on the side to squeeze over all
target.review: This is a great recipe.  I found it from the same book and it's a keeper for my dh and I who are diabetics.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marinated tofu for meat eaters who hate tofu

this is the tofu recipe that opens everyone's closed minds about this much maligned ingredient. the texture of the tofu was described as "similar to chicken and fish but not." i came up with it after many (failed) attempts at creating the perfect meatlover's tofu dish. the key is in the freezing of the tofu, so make sure you plan ahead. prep time does not include freezing time.

1. place the tofu into the freezer for at least 24 hours
2. keeping it in there longer doesn't hurt it
3. remove the tofu from the freezer and defrost by bringing a pot of water to a boil and placing the frozen block of tofu in the pot for 10 minutes or until defrosted
4. remove the tofu from the packaging and cut the block laterally in half so you have two block-sized slabs that are half the width
5. slice each slab lengthwise into three and place on a clean dish towel or paper towels
6. cover the six pieces with another dish towel and place a cutting board or baking tray or other flat object on top
7. place heavy cans or books onto the board and let sit for 15-30 minutes
8. cut the tofu lengths into cubes and place into marinade for a minimum of 30 minutes
9. remove from the marinade and dust the tofu cubes with flour
10. heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat
11. shallow fry the cubes until all sides are golden brown and crispy
12. serve hot with rice or couscous and a puddle of the marinade as a dipping sauce
demonstrations.review: I'm rating this 4 stars because while I just thought it was ok, my dh seemed to really like it. I think it was probably me.  I didn't notice I was to cut into cubes before marinating, so I marinated it in 2 blocks.  I think the taste would have been better if it had been in cubes surrounded by the marinade.  I also had trouble getting it crisp enough, the flour and bits of marinade came off and stuck to the pan. I fried it in 2 batches, removing the pan from heat and scraping off the stuck stuff and then adding more oil and frying the rest.  I used peanut oil and a spicy Jamaican BBQ and Dipping Sauce from Nanny's Jamaican Kitchen.  I served it with rice (both white and brown).  My dh really liked it and surprisingly the spicy sauce..as he doesn't usually care for spicy food.  So I will fix it again and I think I'll do better with it next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tofu and scallions

an excellent yet simple tofu recipe that brings out the essential creaminess of soft tofu by contrasting it with bright touches of ginger and rich shitake mushrooms.  we eat this for breakfast several times a week.

1. first cover the mushrooms in roughly four cups of boiling water and soak while you're preparing the rest of the ingredients
2. mince the ginger , slice the tofu into 1 inch cubes , julienne the scallions
3. mix the thickener in a small bowl
4. heat a nonstick frying pan or wok on the stove
5. when it's hot add the oil and then the ginger
6. when the ginger starts to turn golden then add the tofu and shitake mushrooms
7. almost immediately add about a cup of the mushroom soaking liquid and soy sauce
8. cook for 5 minutes turning once
9. toss the scallions on top , stir in the thickener and cook until the arrowroot turns clear
10. serve with steamed rice
demonstrations.review: I had some tofu I needed to use up and so I tried this recipe. I didn't have fresh mushrooms,ginger or oyster sauce, so I used canned mushrooms, ground ginger and fish sauce. And we STILL liked it! :-) Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
filipino eggplant  aubergine  adobo

i found this for the zaar world tour.  it reminds me of my favorite dish at my favorite restaurant in chinatown.

1. spread eggplant on paper toweling and sprinkle with salt
2. let drain for 30 minutes
3. rinse and pat dry
4. in a non-stick skillet , fry eggplant in oil until brown and set aside
5. in a small saucepan , simmer soy sauce , vinegar , garlic and pepper for 5 minutes
6. add eggplant , cover and cook over low heat for 7 minutes , stirring occasionally
7. serve hot
demonstrations.review: I really like this recipe.  My dh is Filipino and he likes it too.  I chopped up some tomato and sweet onion and added it to the finished dish.  Very good! I served it with grilled fish and rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
leftover roast beef casserole
