demonstrations.review: I made these today and they are easy to make and delicious.  I tried them right out of the oven, cooled off, and then refrigerated.  I prefer them after being chilled.  They come together more and it becomes truly fudgy.  Thanks for a great recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
they could be sliders  if eaten with eyes closed    white castle

a slightly "mock" rendition of white castles sliders, but we think only better. great "kid" sized burgers or even better for "adult" sized snacks! note: since posting this recipe i have found out that pepperidge farm no longer makes the small rolls in the pans so therefore use your own disgression on which rolls are available to you but i do suggest that you use a small size like a dinner roll in order to get the full "white castle" affect!

1. brown ground beef , and drain
2. stir in cheese , soup and onion , til cheese melts
3. cut buns in half
4. spread burger mixture on buns
5. wrap in foil
6. bake 350 for 15-20 minutes
7. open from foil and top each with pickle slice
8. serve immediately , with eyes closed
demonstrations.review: I made these for me and three other former New Jersey people.  We called White Castle food, rats and tails.  These were so easy to make and absolutely delicious and tasted like a ratburger should. My friends husband wants his wife to make these for dinner now.  I couldn't find the dinner rolls so I used hotdog rolls cut in half.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast beef horseradish spirals

very attractive looking appy! and good too. had some ladies over for a 

1. combine first 6 ingredients
2. place the two tortillas on work surface , spread half of cheese over each , top each with half of the roast beef slices , leaving a 1 / 2 inch border around edges
3. roll up , wrap tightly in plastic wrap
4. refrigerate until firm , 30 minutes or up to 1 day ahead
5. cut diagonally into 1 / 2 inch slices and serve
demonstrations.review: I made these for Christmas Eve.  I ended up using four 8" flour tortillas. Very easy to make. These were awesome.  The flavor is incredible.  These would make a great lunch.  Will definitely make again.

target.recipe_text:
cucumber with feta cheese and mint

this is for the world tour. this is from greek cuisine.

1. wash and dry the cucumber and cut it into very thin crosswise slices
2. place the slices in a salad bowl , sprinkle with feta cheese and mint
3. in a small whisk the oil and lemon juice with the salt and pepper to make a vinaigrette made with lemon juice
4. pour over the salad and toss thoroughly
5. serve immediately
target.review: If you like feta you will love this recipe! It is a very crisp and refreshing salad mixture.I didn't have fresh mint leaves so I used the bottled kind and it was still really good. If adding olives, I would suggest reducing the amount of mint as the two flavors may overpower one another.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ginger chicken asparagus stir fry

this is a delicious stir-fry recipe and a really quick and easy dinner. although the original recipe calls for asparagus, i have used fresh green beans (cut into 1-inch pieces) in place of the asparagus. the amounts for this recipe serves really only about 3 people, however all ingredients can easily be doubled to serve more. this is delicious!

1. in a small bowl , combine the lemon juice , soy sauce , fresh ginger and garlic
2. mix / whisk to combine
3. toss the chicken pieces well with about 3 tablespoons of the lemon / soy mixture
4. reserve the remaining mixture
5. dissolve / whisk the cornstarch in chicken broth
6. heat the oil in a wok or frying pan until hot
7. add in mushrooms and chicken
8. stir over high heat until chicken looses the pink colour
9. add in asparagus and green onions , continue to stir over high heat until veggies at crisp-tender
10. add / stir in broth / cornstarch mixture and reserved soy sauce mixture until thickened
11. sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds
12. serve over rice or cooked pasta
demonstrations.review: Fresh and flavorful, loved it! I sent my husband to the store who came back without asparagus... so I ended up using a bag of frozen brocolli and cauliflower instead and it came out great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken tenders  w w 4 pts

yumm i really felt like i was getting away with something when i had these with my ww frenchries!) serving size is 3 chicken fingers and 1 1/2 tbsps barbeque sauce.

1. pre heat oven to 450
2. place a large baking sheet in the oven to preheat
3. in a shallow dish , whisk together mustard and buttermilk
4. place breadcrumbs in a seperate dish
5. dip chicken in mustard mixture then into bread crumb mixture
6. remove the hot baking sheet from oven and coat with cooking spray
7. place chicken on baking sheet and bake 6 minutes , flip and bake until golden and all the way cooked , about another 6 minutes
8. serve the chicken tenders with barbeque sauce
demonstrations.review: These were easy to make and great for only 4 WW Pts. I too had to use double the mustard mixture and triple the breadcrumbs. Maybe the mustard mixture is supposed to be thinner? Mine was fairly thick with the buttermilk.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick mushroom cream pasta

very easy and so delicious! i received this e-mail from a cooking village e-mail. it's such a nice side dish or we even eat it as the main course.

1. combine mushrooms and wine in a large skillet
2. bring to a boil over medium heat
3. cook until wine is reduced to 1 / 4 cup
4. add cream and tarragon to mushroom mixture in skillet
5. cook until sauce is thickened , about 5 minutes
6. stir in green onions , lemon juice , salt and pepper
7. remove from heat
8. meanwhile , cook pasta according to package directions
9. drain well
10. place pasta in a large serving bowl
11. top with sauce and toss gently to coat
demonstrations.review: This was so simple and very delicious! I didn't use tarragon because I'm all out, instead i used about a tbsp of garlic powder and a tsp of thyme, and it still came out very well.I served this with lemon slices on the side and I would  recommend drizzling the juice all over the pasta, it just adds on to the really tasty flavor. Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp parmesan

my husband favorite. a one dish meal. you can prepare everything up to putting in the oven, chill, till ready to heat. serve with a nice crusty bread. or skip the pasta and make shrimp parmesan sandwiches. check out the step x step for this recipe http://www.recipezaar.com/bb/viewtopic.zsp?t=223776

1. open the shrimp up like a book and remove the dark vein
2. in a zip lock bag , place flour seasoned with salt and old bay toss in shrimp and shake to coat
3. remove shrimp
4. to the same bag with the rest of the flour add panko , breadcrumbs , and parmesan cheese
5. in a small bowl whisk well eggs and mayonnaise
6. dip floured shrimp into egg mixture then bread crumbs
7. in a large heavy bottom pan heat oil
8. brown shrimp in batches and drain on paper towel to remove excess oil
9. spread 1 / 3 the sauce on bottom
10. spread cook pasta on top of sauce
11. spoon 1 / 3 sauce on pasta
12. lay shrimp in a baking dish 1 layer
13. sprinkle with with mozzarella cheese
14. top with rest of sauce
15. top with grated parmesan cheese
16. bake in 350 degree oven till cheese is melted
17. about 15-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Not that this recipe needs another five star rating, but my husband and I have both agreed it deserves more than five! This is great for last minute dinner guests or dinner parties as it makes a lot and is very filling. We enjoyed with a greek salad (recipe by kittencal). Don't pass this up!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek style slow cooker sausage and artichokes

this mediterranean-inspired main dish is brimming with a medley of tastes; savory lemon, pungent oregano and tender artichokes. the recipe comes from weight watchers. points per 1 2/3 cup is 4 points.

1. coat 12-inch nonstick skillet with cooking spray
2. season turkey with salt and sage
3. shape into 1 inch balls , add to skillet and brown on all sides , about 3 to 5 minutes
4. remove and place in 4 to 5 quart slow cooker
5. add potatoes , frozen artichokes hearts , oregano , pepper and broth
6. cover and cook on high heat 5 to 6 hours
7. about 15 minutes before serving
8. spoon cornstarch into a cup , add 1 tablespoon of the slow cooker liquid and lemon juice
9. stir well
10. stir into slow cooker , cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes more
demonstrations.review: This was different from the usual crock pot meal and I think the whole family appreciated that. I would serve on fettucine also in agreement with the last viewer, this would be great with pasta but omit the potatoes.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot creamy italian chicken

nan

1. place the chicken breast halves in the crock pot
2. combine the italian dressing mix and water until smooth
3. pour over top of chicken
4. cover and cook on low for 3 hours
5. combine the cream cheese and soup until smooth and blended
6. stir in mushroom pieces
7. pour soup mixture over chicken
8. cook 1 hour more or until chicken is cooked through
9. serve over hot cooked rice or pasta
target.review:
Best tasting crock pot recipe I have tried here! I used the Garlic and Herb envelope instead of Italian. I also used a portabella mushroom sliced instead of the canned. The chicken was so moist and the spices from the dressing were perfect with the mushrooms.
It is now in my 5 top recipes. Thanks so much.....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
russian apple pie

cheap and very easy to make, low on sugar but has a great taste

1. remove core from the apples , cut in large chunks 2" , lay parchment paper on the bottom of your baking form
2. lay the apples on top of parchment paper
3. let eggs warm up for 10 minutes , then mix till light yellow and foamy
4. add sugar in , small portions at a time , let sugar dissolve
5. add flour
6. mix till you see air bubbles , pour mixture on the apples
7. it will soak throughout , do not mix apples with batter
8. bake for 55 minutes on 375f
9. when pie is done flip upside down , apples will be on the top
10. enjoy
demonstrations.review: This recipe is fantastic. I am so tired of the deathly sweet recipes so often found. This recipe lets the sweetness of the apples be truly appreciated.  People who are accustomed to eating sugar laden pastries will not be fond of this recipe. I believe they are now conditioned to expect something repulsively sweet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Great recipe! 1st time did recipe exactly as stated. 2nd time I sprinkled chicken with a little hot curry spice before adding vegetables. Also used a bag of frozen corn instead of canned. At the end I used 1/2 block of neufchatel cheese and squirted a bit of tomato paste. Came out fantastic!  This recipe is great, as you can tweak it as you wish.
Thank you Jen

demonstrations.recipe_text:
very moist banana nut bread

this is a very easy, "no mixer" bread to make. it is very moist and a little heavy type banana bread. the really important thing to remember is using all black bananas to get my same results. i always use 5 medium sized bananas and this recipe makes 2 loaves. also, i've never used buttermilk, but sour milk instead..a little vinegar added to regular milk. i've used this recipe since 1972 and last year made 32 loaves to give away for christmas! it's truly a wonderful bread. i only bake it until the toothpick comes out almost clean, as we like it really moist. if you over bake it, or wait til the toothpick is completely clean, the bread will be a lot dryer. i realize some like it this way, so thats why i've given this hint. my family and friends would rather have it a little under done than over. it's so good with coffee, butter/jelly or i like mine just plain. i bake it in tin foil pans and it freezes wonderfully. i try to always have one or two in the freezer for company, or a little gift. this recipe came from a ladies club cookbook. the kind where everyone contributes recipes, they are made into a recipe book and sold to make money for charities. all the cooks are just plain "down home" country gals that produce miracles in the kitchen. it's my favorite cookbook and i've almost worn it out and it can't be replaced. i know there are many banana bread recipes here, so thanks for trying this recipe. i hope you enjoy it!

1. heat oven to 350
2. grease or spray 2 loaf pans
3. in a large bowl , mash bananas with a masher or by well washed hands
4. dissolve soda in buttermilk-- use a larger container as it will foam up quite a bit
5. mix all ingredients by hand and add in 1 cup chopped nuts
6. bake at 350 for 1 hour , or until toothpick comes out almost clean
7. totally clean will mean a dryer loaf
8. let cool 15 minutes after removing from oven and remove from pans
9. or , let cool , cover with foil , slide into freezer bags and freeze
10. great when using tin foil pans
demonstrations.review:
OMG! The absolute BEST banana bread I ever made, or have eaten!! I substituted almond milk with some vinegar for the buttermilk, as I am not a baby cow.. and used only over a cup of sugar.
I accidentally forgot the vanilla and I used 5 black bananas. Great banana flavor. My new favorite recipe! Actually this was the only recipe that did not use a ton of butter. It was extremely moist and had the best taste ever. Thank you so much for this great recipe...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best blueberry crisp

this is wonderful served warm with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream --- you will love this crisp!

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. prepare an 11 x 7-inch baking dish
3. spread the blueberries in the bottom of the prepared baking pan
4. in a small saucepan over medium heat combine the sugar , cornstarch , water and 2-3 tbsp lemon juice
5. cook and stir until thick and clear , then add in the vanilla
6. pour over , then gently stir in the cooked mixture with the blueberries
7. in a bowl combine the flour with oats , brown sugar and cinnamon
8. add in the melted butter
9. mix until crumbly
10. sprinkle over the top of blueberries
11. bake for 30-35 minutes , or until blueberry mixture bubbles and the topping is brown
12. serve with ice cream-- enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
I followed the recipe exactly. It was fantastic. I didn't think it needed any more sugar. It's blueberry season now and I plan on freezing lots of blueberries to make this later
in the year. Just delicious, and so easy...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
authentic italian tomato sauce

this is a recipe i got from my father who got it from a little old lady he knew from italy. i always simmer this sauce with my meatballs (recipe posted). you can also add sausage if you like. this sauce is to die for!!!!

1. in a large pot , saut onion and garlic in olive oil
2. empty plum tomatoes into large bowl and squash with your hands
3. add all ingredients to pot and simmer for 3 hours
demonstrations.review: I made the recipe exactly as posted and I found it way too sweet for my taste. I will continue to search for the perfect sauce.

target.recipe_text:
garlic roasted asparagus with parmesan

such a wonderful and simple presentation of one of spring's best vegetables with the irresistible flavor of garlic. so easy to make- (but no one has to know how easy it is!!!)

1. heat oil and garlic in a small saucepan over low heat until garlic becomes golden- several minutes
2. allow oil to cool
3. bend asparagus gently at a natural point and when it snaps , discard end pieces
4. place asparagus on a lipped roasting pan and toss with infused olive oil and garlic , coating all pieces
5. line up asparagus and push together , season with salt and pepper , then sprinkle with grated parmesan
6. roast in a preheated oven at 400f for 12 minutes or until cooked to your liking
7. serve at once
target.review: This rocks.  Sue, you are my new hero.  So tired of same old boring asparagus and this was wonderful.  Even my "asparagus haters" ate this one.  Will make often, thanks a million. ~Messy44

demonstrations.recipe_text:
heart smart oatmeal date chocolate cookies

from health, january 2008.  i made these with dried figs (soaked thoroughly in water) in place of the dates.  very chewy and delicious cookies and plenty sweet.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. melt butter in a small saucepan over low heat
3. remove from heat and add brown sugar
4. stir until smooth
5. in a medium bowl , combine all-purpose flour , whole-wheat flour , baking soda , oats , and salt
6. combine the butter mixture with the dry ingredients , and add egg , vanilla , and chopped dates
7. fold in bittersweet chocolate
8. mix well and spoon mixture by tablespoon-fulls out onto lightly greased baking sheets
9. bake for 12 minutes , until tops are dry to the touch
demonstrations.review: There is a recipe in the Cooking Light Jan/Feb 2011 issue that is identical to this one - except for 1/4 tsp less baking soda and uses dried cherries in place of the dates. I was going to post but it is so close to this one, I changed my mind! Made these with the dried cherries and they are wonderful. Have also made with figs and they were AWESOME.  Can't wait to try them with dates. Yummmm. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast beef horseradish spirals

very attractive looking appy! and good too. had some ladies over for a 

1. combine first 6 ingredients
2. place the two tortillas on work surface , spread half of cheese over each , top each with half of the roast beef slices , leaving a 1 / 2 inch border around edges
3. roll up , wrap tightly in plastic wrap
4. refrigerate until firm , 30 minutes or up to 1 day ahead
5. cut diagonally into 1 / 2 inch slices and serve
demonstrations.review: Really good.  Took to a casual dinner at a friend's house and they were the first thing gone.  Only change was that I used arugula in place of parsley.  I served with some horseradish sauce for dipping.  Mine made 3 10 inch tortillas, but perhaps I didn't spread it thick enough.  Will make again.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesty oven baked fries

as good as fried and more healthy to boot!

1. heat oven to 450
2. spray a baking sheet with cooking spray
3. combine all dry ingredients and combine with potatoes , tossing to coat
4. drizzle with oil , tossing again to coat
5. arrange potatoes in a single layer on baking sheet and bake for 35 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Thunbs up - very tasty.  Will make again.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
giant soft pretzels

these are so yummy! even if a bit messy to make. you can also shape the pretzels into letters or numbers. kids love to do that. you can also brush with butter after you take the out of the oven and sprinkle cinnamon sugar over them. my kids love them that way.

1. preheat oven to 425
2. place water , flour , sugar & yeast in a large bowl
3. mix and knead dough for 5 to 10 minutes
4. turn dough onto a lightly floured surface
5. divide into 8 balls
6. roll each ball out into 20-inch ropes and form into pretzel shape
7. in a large sauce pan , bring water and baking soda to a boil
8. drop pretzels into water 2 at a time , boil for 10-15 seconds
9. remove with slotted spoons and drain on paper towels
10. place pretzles on a greased baking sheet and bake at 425 for 8-10 minutes or until golden brown
11. spritz or lightly brush with water
12. sprinkle with salt and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Love. Easy and produced a lovely result.  Eaten heartily and quickly by the crew.  Will make more, and often.  No changes - perfect as is. Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tibetan potato curry

i've had this long enough to forget where it came from.  thought i'd share....

1. precook the potatoes in water until almost , but not quite , done
2. drain thoroughly
3. while the potatoes are cooking , saute the fenugreek seed in the oil on medium heat until light brown , being careful not to burn them
4. add the onion and continue cooking for five minutes
5. add the ginger and garlic and cook another five minutes
6. add the spices and saute briefly to release their flavors
7. add the tomato , the dried whole peppers , and a little water
8. simmer until the flavors meld together , about 30 minutes
9. gently add the potatoes , stir , and reduce heat
10. cook until potatoes are tender , adding water if the sauce gets too dry
11. if the sauce is too runny , simply crush one of the potatoes to thicken it
demonstrations.review: I adopted this chef for PAC Fall 2007 and I am so glad I did!!!  I loved this recipe!  Very easy to make and a nice mild curry flavor.  I could not find fenugreek seeds in my area, so I used 1/4 tsp. ground fenugreek instead. I made no other changes.  My family enjoyed this and it was a refreshing change for us on a weeknight.  I was not sure how much water to add.  Next time I will add just a bit more water to make more sauce, and will add 2 dried peppers (I chose to add just one for my first attempt).  This one is going in the book.  Thanks, Elmotoo!

target.recipe_text:
seven layer magic bars

nan

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in 13x9" baking pan , melt butter in oven
3. sprinkle crumbs over butter
4. pour sweetened condensed milk over crumbs
5. top with remaining ingredients in order listed
6. press down firmly
7. bake 25 minutes or until lightly browned
8. cool
9. chill if desired
10. cut into bars
11. store covered at room temperature
12. when bars are baked , cool
13. lift of edges of foil to remove from pan
14. cut into individual squares
15. lift off of foil
16. keebler / realemon / borden
target.review: These tasted just like the ones my grandmother used to make!  They were also really easy & quick.  The one drawback was that they didn't quite hold together as well as I'd hoped.  (They cooled about 24 hours before serving, but the chocolate never quite hardened again.)  As Sherry F. mentioned, I might try changing the order of the chips/nuts next time I make 'em, and I definitely will be making them again! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cassoulet soup

inexpensive and tasty soup based on a french classic. fast and easy to make and everyone always loves it.

1. saut onion and sausage in large saucepan until browned
2. add thyme , stir one minute
3. add wine , boil until slightly reduced , about 2 minutes
4. stir in broth , 1 cup of the beans , and the chicken
5. mash the rest of the beans and add to pot
6. partially cover and simmer for 10 minutes
7. season to taste with salt and pepper , garnish with chopped parsley
demonstrations.review: I've never made a soup with smoked sausage before, and I thought it would be a little strange.  But, it turned out to be SO good!!  The smoky flavor couples beautifully with the wine, and creates several lovely "levels" of flavor.  The mashed beans added a rich, velvety texture that was VERY satisfying.  I doubled the recipe, and it still turned out beautifully!  (The bigger batch required some extra simmering time.)  My husband loved it as well -- I will definitely make this again!  Thanks for posting the recipe! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pear apple chutney

my mom made this chutney and i asked her for the recipe because i liked it so well. i had no idea it used such a bizzare combination of ingredients. i added it on top of cheese, ham, and crackers. spi-cy.

1. tie the peppercorns up in a piece of cheesecloth
2. add the peppercorns and the rest of the ingredients to a large pot
3. bring mixture to a boil
4. lower heat , and simmer , uncovered , for 2 hours , stirring occasionally
5. remove peppercorns in cheesecloth
6. pour mixture into hot sterilzed jars , leave 1 / 4 inch headspace
7. remove air bubbles
8. wipe jar rims
9. cover at once with metal lids , and screw on bands
10. process jars in boiling water bath for 10 minutes
11. let cool
demonstrations.review: Absolutely LOVED it... and you're not kidding about it being "spi-cy"! ;)  I used the conversion tool for 2 half-pints (1 pint) to see how it would work.  I didn't have cider vinegar, but the balsamic that I had, worked wonderfully with the other ingredients.  Also... I was too lazy to cook it for 2 hours!  (Instead, I nuked it for about 30 minutes, stirring every once in awhile.  After a few minutes of standing, it was perfect.)  I was also too impatient to let it cool, and slapped a bit on my veggie burger at dinner... YUM!  I might just go for the whole 4 pints next time I make it, 'cause the 1 pint isn't going to last long around here! :)  Thanks SO much for sharing this awesome recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma knorberg s pork chops casserole

my grandma used to make these and she said if you every left her house hungry that is your fault. excellent family meal.

1. place pork chops in 9x13 pan
2. sprinkle with salt , pepper and sage
3. mix all the remaining ingredients
4. pour over the chops
5. bake 1 hour at 350f
demonstrations.review: The reason I chose to try this recipe is the addition of the veggies, which rounds the dish out perfectly.  Made this for dinner last night, and LOVED it!  I would advise anyone making this recipe NOT to skip the sage, as it seems to really release its flavor during cooking & makes a great-smelling, great-tasting savory sauce -- I also added just a splash of white wine to my sauce mixture (about 1/4 cup).  Served it over stuffing, and my husband just *inhaled* it.  This is definitely a keeper!!  Thanks for posting, Shirl! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my spaghetti sauce

i have made my sauce this way for years.  it is very easy and i think really good.  the italian dressing mix is the key--the longer this simmers the better it is, but it can be made quickly too. i have also made it in the crock pot!

1. in olive oil saut onion , red pepper and garlic till soft
2. add italian dressing mix
3. stir
4. add cans of tomato sauce and stewed tomatoes
5. stir in basil and pepper and garlic powder
6. let simmer--the longer the better stirring often
7. towards the end , add the meatballs and simmer till they are done
8. stir in mushrooms
demonstrations.review: My husband really liked this sauce!  Because of our tiny crockpot, I had to take out half of the sauce about an hour into the cooking time.  I'm already planning how to use the leftovers. :)  I used a roasted red pepper (from a jar) in place of the fresh one, which gave it a wonderfully zingy, slightly smoky flavor.  The 1 drawback was the whole tomatoes; I'd hoped that they'd fall apart in the crockpot -- I love a nice chunky sauce, but my husband prefers a smoother texture.  Next time I make this sauce, I'll use 2 cans of sauce, or puree.  I'll definitely make this one again, as it is yummy & SUPER easy! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot western omelet casserole

a perfect make ahead dish for when you have overnight guests or when you expect a crowd for breakfast!

1. spray the inside of the crock pot with nonstick spray
2. place a layer of frozen potatoes on the bottom of the crock pot
3. add layers of ham , onions , green peppers and cheese , in the order listed
4. repeat the layering process two or three times , ending with a layer of cheese
5. beat the eggs , milk , salt and pepper together
6. pour over the layers , cover and turn on low
7. cook for 10-12 hours , or overnight
demonstrations.review: Another clever idea from Yooper!  I halved the proportions (except the onion and pepper, which I used one of each), chose to use cheddar cheese and ham with this.  I felt that the ham had enough salt as it was, so omitted the extra salt.  Some of the "texture" comments worried me a little, but the eggs turned out just fine here.  Smelled great as it was cooking, almost too hard to resist! :)  Next time I have a full house for breakfast, I'll be sure to fill my crockpot with this the night before!  Thanks Yooper!! :)

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken vindaloo

for the vegetarian version: use your favorite veggies, omit the cinnamon stick. this is my sister's recipe (thank you najla! xoxo), she made it on the stove top. it's really yummy!!

1. puree first 10 ingredients in a blender
2. pour into the crock pot , add tomato sauce , cinnamon stick and onion and mix well
3. add chicken and turn to cover
4. cook on low for 5 hours
5. sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving
6. serve with rice or rolls , enjoy !
target.review:
we liked this recipe, and was very easy to put together but it needed a little something extra.  I think will try again and add some red chili powder or more ground chilis for extra kick, we like really spicy food.

I may also try cooking it on stove top to build the flavor a little better by adding things in stages.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mahogany beef stew

you will not believe the deeply satisfying flavour of this stew. this is our favourite wintry stew dish - comfort food to the max.  the cooking time is more or less accurate, but it really depends on the cut of meat used -  not everyone used chuck, and then, not all chuck is the same!  you really have to poke and prod and taste to get it to where you want it...but that's what cooking is all about, isn't it? ;-)

1. heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in heavy large pot over high heat
2. sprinkle meat with salt and pepper
3. add meat to pot
4. saut until brown on all sides , about 10 minutes
5. push meat to sides of pot
6. reduce heat to medium
7. add 2 tablespoons oil to pot
8. add onions
9. saut until golden brown , about 15 minutes
10. mix meat into onions
11. add 1 cup wine , tomatoes with juices , garlic , herbs , hoisin sauce , and bay leaves
12. bring to boil
13. reduce heat to low , cover pot and simmer 45 minutes , stirring occasionally
14. add carrots and 1 cup wine
15. cover
16. simmer 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
17. uncover , increase heat to high
18. boil until sauce is slightly thickened , stirring occasionally , about 15 minutes longer
19. reduce heat to medium , add cornstarch mixture and simmer until sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 8 minutes
20. discard bay leaves
21. season stew with salt and pepper
22. transfer stew to large bowl
23. sprinkle with parsley and serve
24. excellent with buttered egg noodles
demonstrations.review: love this! had great flavor. I am cutting carbs and trying to eat more veggies, so I used about 2 lbs of some really lean looking chuck roast and trimmed as much fat as I could and added a lot more veggies (5 big carrots, 3 celery stocks, 1 red pepper, 1 green pepper   a lil extra onion). I think all the water from the veggies diluted it so I skipped the second cup of wine, it was very watery. Thickened up beautifully with cornstarch and was delicious and flavorful! Will make again for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: very good! i figured 1000 people cant be wrong and i followed the recipe closely and enjoyed a lot. I did hold off on the salt as my cajun seasoning i use is already salty. Will make this again for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
secretly delicious spinach pie

the tortilla adds a delicious crunchy shell and it smells so good while it is cooking. i actually made up this recipe from items in my kitchen and couldn't believe how wonderful it tasted! it is now a hit in my family and so easy to make. please rate and give feedback.  


update: since i first made this five years ago, we still enjoy this at least once a month. i have found that i can alternate the ingredients to use up items i have in the fridge. i have used mushrooms, sauteed onions, cherry tomatoes and even feta cheese instead of cheddar cheese. and it always comes out fantastic. i have also found that there are times i need to use more or less eggs depending on the ingredients. also, a glass pie pan is so much better than a metal as it toasts the tortilla just right. such an easy recipe with gourmet taste!

1. mix the first six ingredients in a bowl
2. set aside
3. lay the flour tortilla in a glass pie dish , press gently - does not need to lay perfectly flat against dish
4. i don't spray it prior and have never had any issues with it sticking
5. especially when made using a glass pie pan
6. sprinkle only 1 / 2 cup cheese on tortilla
7. sprinkle remaining cheese and the spinach onto tortilla in layers , and press gently
8. i don't chop or tear the spinach but you might opt to do this
9. pour egg mixture evenly over spinach , be careful not to pour any outside of tortilla as this causes it to stick to pan
10. bake in oven at 365 degrees for 35 to 45 minutes
11. insert fork in center and it should come out clean
12. use sharp knife to cut into pie slices and serve hot
13. other options: instead of garlic , you can use 1 / 4 cup onions
14. for added flavor , serve with homemade salsa
demonstrations.review: this was great. i tweaked it a little due to time and what i had. Just threw this together for a last minute dinner. Used garlic powder instead of real roasted garlic (no time) and deli ham instead of baccon. Otherwise followed everything else. Two of us ended up eating the whole thing! It baked up beautifully and was so little effort. Will make again for sure

demonstrations.recipe_text:
addictive mexican stew

my mother gave me this recipe.  she found it while clipping coupons.  it is from s&w.  this is the best stew i have ever eaten and my family requests me to make it quite frequently.  it has become a 

1. cook onion and garlic in oil in large saucepan until tender
2. add cooked chicken , taco seasoning , tomatoes , beans , corn and chilies
3. blend broth and cornstarch
4. add to saucepan
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes
7. stirring occasionally
8. serve with cornbread for a hearty meal
demonstrations.review: was fast, easy and delicious will make again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
snickerdoodle blondies

i've seen this recipe on several food blogs and was obsessed with them.   being a big fan of snickerdoodle cookies, i knew the moment i saw these i had to give them a whirl. what impressed me most about this recipe was that it was super basic, no need to run out and buy anything special, just raid your fridge and pantry and bake away! these are super easy to make and will have your house smelling heavenly in 10 minutes. these bars go great with a cup of piping hot coffee! now get obsessed with these bars and get to baking!  my hats off to julia of dozen flours who i adapted this from and tweaked to create this new favorite of my family and friends :) now everyone asks me for the recipe! i have not seen a recipe on zaar like this, so i am posting it here to share!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. lightly grease and / or line a 913 inch pan
3. combine the flour , baking powder , cinnamon , nutmeg and salt and set aside
4. in large bowl , beat together butter and brown sugar for 3-5 minutes
5. add in the eggs one at a time , then the vanilla , and beat until smooth
6. stir in the flour mixture until well blended
7. spread evenly in prepared pan
8. combine the granulated sugar and cinnamon , in a little bowl
9. evenly sprinkle cinnamon sugar mixture over the top of the batter
10. bake 25-30 minutes or until surface springs back when gently pressed
11. cool before cutting
12. makes 20-24 bars
demonstrations.review: these were just ok. Im a big fan of snickerdoodles and these didnt live up. They were rather doughy even after an extra 10 minutes in the oven. I followed the recipe exactly.

target.recipe_text:
white bean chowder

a lovely, filling soup with sweet and spicy flavors from the sweet corn and spices.  i found this in a dairy favorites card at the grocery and made a few tweaks for our preferences.  you can also sub white cannellini beans for the great northern - i just find it easier to locate the great northerns in my area.

1. heat oil in a large pan over medium heat and saute the onion and garlic until onion is softened
2. add one can of beans and mash roughly
3. stir in remaining can of beans , green chilies , corn , carrots , celery , and broth
4. bring soup to a simmer and stir in the cumin , chili powder , and cayenne pepper
5. combine milk and cornstarch , stirring well
6. stir the milk mixture into the soup , bringing it gradually to a boil
7. reduce heat and allow soup to simmer until veggies are tender , about 5 minutes
8. stir frequently
9. stir in 3 / 4 c of the cheese , reserving the remainder for use as garnish , and remove from heat
10. serve garnished with cheese and cilantro
target.review: Fabulous chowder. I loved the spiciness. It was just enough, without being overpowering. Even my kids, who don't typically like beans, ate this soup and talked about how good it was. I'm packing some of the leftovers for my lunch today! Made as is and it was perfect. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wasabi ae  broccoli with wasabi sauce

you can turn this into a one-dish meal by adding some protein of your choice, such as blanched and cut-up tofu, or poached and shredded chicken breast. the sauce is great with either. use less wasabi if you find it too strong. from the blog "just hungry" . cooking time is approximate

1. bring the water and salt to a boil
2. cook the broccoli until it's crisp-tender and still a bright green in color
3. drain , and refresh very briefly with cold running water
4. in the meantime , mix together all the remaining ingredients except the wasabi in a small pan , and stir over a low heat until the sugar is melted
5. let cool , and add the wasabi , reserving 1 / 2 tsp or so
6. mix well until the wasabi is dissolved
7. pour the sauce over the broccoli and mix well
8. serve at room temperature or chilled , optionally with a little additional wasabi on the side for people to mix into the broccoli as they eat it
demonstrations.review: This was a great broccoli recipe. I thought it had the right amount of wasabi. The only thing I would do differently next time is to cut down on the amount of sauce. This broccoli would be a great addition to any Japanese meal! Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar roasted salmon with maple mustard dill sauce

simple roasted salmon coated in brown sugar and glazed with a maple-mustard-dill sauce. taken from salmoninseconds.com and posted for zwt.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. combine brown sugar , cracked black pepper and kosher salt in bowl
3. mix well
4. rub salmon filets with brown sugar mixture , making sure to use all of mixture
5. let stand for 15 minutes in refrigerator covered lightly with plastic wrap
6. combine maple syrup , mustard and fresh dill in small mixing bowl
7. set aside
8. coat bottom of baking pan with 1 tbsp olive oil
9. place salmon fillets in pan and drizzle with remaining oil
10. bake for 12 minutes or until cooked to desired temperature
11. remove from baking pan and drizzle salmon with maple-mustard-dill sauce
demonstrations.review: My husband is still talking about this salmon - the morning after our dinner. It's safe to say that I'm tucking this recipe into my best-of-the-best file. It's absolutely delicious! I skipped the dill, but otherwise kept the recipe the same (using the Dijon option). The flavors are absolutely wonderful. I served the salmon and sauce over brown rice. Yum. Made during Family Picks for the Soup-A-Stars ZWT9

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple savory turkey burgers with zucchini relish

a "burger of the month" from everyday with rachael ray.  i switched up the recipe a bit, as i don't keep fresh herbs on hand.  the relish is good, but you can certainly serve the burger without and it will be just as yummy!!!  sometimes instead of topping them with the cheese, i stuff them with swiss or cheddar cheese. . .so good!  and sometimes i make them into sliders, making 6 burgers instead of 4.

1. in a medium bowl , combine the ground turkey , grill seasoning , mustard and poultry seasoning
2. form 4 patties
3. using your thumb , make an indentation in the center of each to prevent bulging while cooking
4. let the patties sit so the flavors blend while you make the relish
5. in a small bowl , combine zucchini , bell pepper , onion , hot sauce , lime juice , tomatoes and salt to taste
6. set aside
7. spray your large skillet with cooking spray and place it over med-high heat
8. add the patties and cook until the juices run clear , which is about 5 minutes on each side
9. during the last minute of cooking , top each burger with a cheese slice so that it melts
10. toast and butter the english muffins
11. set a lettuce leaf and burger on each muffin bottom and top with a spoonful of zucchini relish and the muffin top
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
This recipe made it into book#234156!
Hands-down the best turkey burger I have ever had. For years I've been trying different turkey burger recipes and they always left me just wanting a good ol' hamburger instead. I'm happy to announce that this recipe surpassed my high expectations for a turkey burger. It is delicious, full of flavor and pretty darn healthy, too! Notes: 1.When reading "grill seasoning" in the recipe, I would have ordinarily used a chicken grill seasoning BUT since JanuaryBride had noted that she used a steak seasoning, I decided to give that I try. I believe it's a KEY ingredient. The black pepper and mixture of spices in the steak seasoning (I used 'Montreal Steak Seasoning') hit the perfect flavor notes with the turkey. 2. I used a stoneground mustard vs. dijon and it was perfect for this recipe. 3. Definitely follow the directions in terms of toasting the english muffins OR buns. It does make a difference. *I used toasted whole wheat buns. 4. For the 2 family members who like cheese, I used plain American cheese (it was delish) and went without cheese for the 2 who don't care for it. Everyone gave it rave reviews! 5. I really loved the relish, but also think the turkey burger can stand alone! Great recipe. Thank you!!!! ~Aussie/NZ Swap #16

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nif s asparagus stuffed chicken breast with hollandaise sauce

you'll think that you are being spoiled in a nice restaurant with this recipe. this was a sandi richards recipe that i changed just a little. enjoy!

1. asparagus stuffed chicken: smear 1 / 2 teaspoon garlic on rough side of each chicken breast
2. lay 3 spears of asparagus on top of garlic , roll the breast around the asparagus and secure with toothpicks
3. heat oil in a large flat frying pan at medium-high heat
4. brown all sides of the rolled chicken
5. add wine and chicken broth to pan after all the breasts have browned
6. let simmer at medium heat , turning once , until liquid evaporates
7. remove toothpicks !
8. hollandaise: beat egg yolks with a whisk in a small stove top pot
9. add lemon juice , dry mustard and tabasco to yolks
10. whisk together to combine
11. melt butter until liquid , about 10 seconds
12. very slowly drizzle the butter into egg yolks while whisking
13. now place on medium-low heat
14. slowly whisk in milk until smooth
15. heat through while whisking
16. remove from heat
17. add a little more milk if you want it thinner
18. serve chicken with hollandaise sauce drizzled over top
demonstrations.review:
Delicious combination of flavors. The hollandaise sauce is a must!
I added salt & pepper to my chicken/asparagus.  
Such a beautiful presentation, too. This recipe would be lovely to serve to guests. Merci!
~ZWT5 Epicurean Queens~

demonstrations.recipe_text:
daily detox ritual  2  breakfast meal replacement green smoothie

this is a great smoothie to add to your morning routine...countless variations can be made by using different fruits and fresh greens. use what you have on hand, or what you may have a surplus of in the fridge. citrus fruits and greens are the magic combo, as fruits high in vit c help your body absorb more iron from the greens.lemon and lime juice are great alkalizers, and enhances the taste of the smoothie. add stevia or coconut nectar if needed. i like using frozen low gi fruits to keep the smoothie cold without adding ice (papaya, pears, apple) !
try adding a combination of the fruits listed, not all are necessary each time-if you are in a hurry try just one or two fruits (pineapple and papaya have the most enzymes so i try to keep these on hand).

1. start with water , you can use 1 cup to start , blend in about one small handful each of spinach and kale
2. blend until smooth if using a regular blender , try frozen organic chopped spinach
3. vita mix: add all ingredients in order , no need to blend greens first
4. add in 1 / 2 orange , cut into a few smaller pieces , try leaving a little rind ! make sure you take all seeds out
5. break celery into chunks , and blend smooth
6. add in harder fruits first , banana and lemon / lime last
7. if too thick , add in cold water until desired thickness , remember , it's a smoothie-not a juice:)
8. add stevia and sweeten to taste , and try a pinch of dry or fresh mint if you find it strong for your palate !
demonstrations.review: Wow! I'm actually surprised by how much I enjoyed this for my breakfast this morning. I'm used to juicing with greens (usually kale, celery, broccoli, spinach, apple or pear, ginger) but I've never done a green smoothie and wasn't sure if I would like it. I halved the ingredients (1/2 C water was the perfect amount for half of recipe) for one smoothie and included 1/2 a packet of stevia. I loved the flavor AND knowing that my breakfast was nutrition packed. It was filling, too. I didn't need anything else for breakfast (well, I did finish eating the other half of orange and banana). As a side note: I completely forgot about my usual morning coffee! It occured to me a few hours later that I missed my coffee and hadn't even thought about it. Made for Spring Pick A Chef in the contests/events forum.

target.recipe_text:
unknownchef86 s very best dinner rolls

these rolls are very soft and light. they make children and husbands very happy. my husband asked, "can you make these all the time?"

1. sprinkle the yeast over the warm milk and let sit for approximately 5 minutes to proof
2. add sugar , 1 / 2 cup melted butter , salt and eggs
3. mix well
4. add flour and mix well
5. blend at medium-low speed for about 5-10 minutes , scraping down sides once or twice
6. cover bowl with plastic wrap and a towel
7. let rise in bowl about 1 hour or til doubled
8. remove the towel and plastic wrap and turn mixer on low to"punch down" the dough
9. if you wish , you can let the dough raise a second time as it makes for a more flavorful roll
10. remove the dough from the bowl and divide into 36"plops"
11. the dough will be very sticky
12. place"plops" , edges just touching , in a buttered 9x13 baking pan
13. don't bother trying to smooth out the"plops"-- they will smooth out as they raise
14. cover pan with plastic wrap and let rise til doubled , about 30-40 minutes
15. melt the reserved butter and drizzle over the top of the rolls before baking
16. bake at 400f for 10-15 minutes or until golden
target.review: I have baked a lot of bread but never used my bread hook so I was hesitant to make these. . . but the great reviews encouraged me.  I made them just as the recipe instructed - let them rise twice before shaping.  It made two  9 x 13 pans of rolls.  I baked them in my convection oven at 350 degrees for 20 minutes.  Very easy bread recipe -not the prettiest rolls I have ever made. . . but very good - esp. for the minimal effort that it takes to make them.  I am going to freeze most of them for the holidays and will definitely make this recipe again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s caramel apples

no caramels to unwrap for these there easy and fun to make and the best caramel apples,  you may roll the caramel apples in mini m&m's,  nuts, chocolate, cereal or just about anything just make certain to roll while the caramel is still soft on the apples --- i made these often when my son was growing up especially around halloween time, and also for many birthday parties,  for me this has been the best recipe and i have tryed my share when my son was young --- kids of all ages just love these!

1. insert 1 wooden stick into each apple
2. in a heavy saucepan , combine the butter , brown sugar , corn syrup and milk
3. bring to a boil over medium-high heat
4. cook and stir until a candy thermometer reads 248 degrees about 30-40 minutes and for a softer caramel cook just to a few less degrees
5. remove from heat
6. stir in vanilla
7. dip each apple into hot caramel mixture
8. turn to coat
9. holding by the stick , sprinkle with nuts or whatever you desire while the caramel is still warm
10. set on generously buttered wax paper to cool
demonstrations.review: Very good tasting caramel.  Follow directions - stir the entire time and keep your heat on medium.  And use parchment paper -NOT waxed paper.  Only problem I had was that I tried to dip TOO much caramel onto the apple and it slid off of the apples as they cooled.  Next time I will use this recipe but try dropping the apples in boiling water to get rid of the wax prior to dipping.  That may help the caramel "stick" better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sandra s key lime pie

i saw this in the food section of the cincinnati enquirer october 30 2002 pg e3. by chef sandra wilson. i really like key lime pie and until this recipe have never found one that satisfied me.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. beat softened cream cheese until creamy
3. add sweetened condensed milk and beat to incorporate
4. add egg yolks and beat well
5. add lime juice and beat till combined
6. pour mixture into pie crust and spread with spatula until evenly distributed
7. place on cookie sheet and then into the oven and bake for 10 min
8. until the filling begins to set
9. remove from oven and allow to cool on rack at room temp
10. then place in the refrigerator for at least an hour
11. two works better
12. cut into 8 slices and serve with a generous helping of whipped cream
demonstrations.review: My husband is a fifth generation Floridian and I have always made his mother's key lime pie recipe - authentic and no cream cheese!  But I made this for fun and we call it our "restaurant recipe" key lime pie --  it keeps longer than the authentic recipe - retains its shape a little bit better - and the taste is excellent.  Don't tell Mom but I think I prefer this one!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious corn muffins

these delicious corn muffins were served at kenny roger's restaurant. i found the recipe on "top secret recipes". i love to serve them with bbq. they are so good it is almost like eating a dessert.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. mix butter , sugar , honey , eggs , and salt into a large bowl
3. add flour , cornmeal , and baking powder and blend thoroughly
4. add milk while mixing
5. add corn to mixture and work into mixture
6. do not mash corn , the whole kernel is baked into the muffin
7. fill a muffin pan with 12 paper / foil muffin cups and fill 2 / 3 full with batter
8. bake for 20-25 minutes until muffins are light brown
demonstrations.review: These are DANGEROUS!!!!  I make them as mini-muffins and it's so easy to pop one in your mouth and devour it!  Delicious!  I make them just as the recipe says.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana chocolate chip muffins

wow! get this...a very low-fat muffin recipe that actually tastes great!! after failing at many attempts to create a really tasty, low-fat muffin, i came across this recipe, and it is really good...great for dieters!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly coat 12 muffin tin liners with cooking spray and place in muffin tin
3. in large bowl , mash bananas with fork
4. whisk in egg , milk , granulated sugar , and brown sugar
5. in separate bowl , combine flour , baking soda , and salt
6. add flour mixture to banana mixture and combine well
7. fold in chocolate chips and walnuts
8. spoon equal amounts of batter into 12 muffin cups
9. bake 20 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
10. allow to cool slightly in pan , then remove to wire rack
demonstrations.review: Used 1/4 cup milk chocolate chips and no nuts. Substituted splenda for sugar and added 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce and 1/2 cup old fashioned quaker oats. With these changes, it made 18 muffins and when I put it through the WW recipe builder it came to TWO POINTS per muffin. These are delicious and "point-friendly" for a filling, good-sized muffin. I will be using all my ripe bananas for these!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww 1 point cheese soup

easy cheesy soup (1 cup = 1ww point)

1. in a saucepan add vegetables , chicken broth and tomatoes
2. bring to a boil , reduce heat , simmer 45 minutes
3. add the cheese and stir until melted
4. yield: 10 cups
demonstrations.review: The five stars are because it's a low-point WW food that really makes you feel like you ate something!!  This is so flavorful - if you don't like spicy beware of the Rotel - it really has a kick!  I used one pound of cal-blend veggies and thought it was enough.  If you're counting points you need to try this -- if you don't like spicy use brocolli only, leave out the rotel and have a great brocolli cheese soup for ONE POINT.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken  gravy and stuffing

nan

1. season chicken breasts with salt and pepper and place chicken breasts in crock pot
2. pour chicken broth over breasts
3. put one slice of swiss cheese on each breast
4. combine both cans of soup and milk
5. cover chicken breasts with soup mixture
6. sprinkle stuffing mix over all
7. drizzle melted butter on top
8. cook on low for 6 hours or high for 3
target.review: Very easy and very flavorful

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked pork chops and apples

i found this in a pamphlet from the orchard (about maryland apple orchards) a few years ago when we were picking apples. it is one of the tastiest things i have ever made!

1. peel , core , and slice the apples
2. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
3. melt the butter in a skillet
4. brown the pork chops on both sides in the butter
5. grease a large baking dish
6. put the apple slices in the bottom of the dish
7. mix the brown sugar and cinnamon
8. sprinkle the cinnamon and sugar over the apples
9. place the pork chops on top of the apples
10. cover with foil and bake for 1 and 1 / 2 hours
demonstrations.review: Sorry, my family did not care for this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked balsamic chicken

love balsamic vinegar, hope you enjoy this chicken. note; i have found that it's better with boneless, skinless  chicken breast or  boneless, skinless thighs. baking time may be less due to size.

1. preheat oven 400 degrees
2. arrange the chicken bone side down in a 9-by-13 inch glass or ceramic baking dish
3. pour the vinegar over them and sprinkle evenly with the oil , oregano , salt and pepper
4. bake the chicken 20 minutes and baste with the vinegar juices
5. bake 20 minutes more or until juices run clear
6. serve chicken with juices spooned over them
demonstrations.review: It was moist but it didn't have a lot of flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cake batter ice cream

i made this recipe after falling in love with coldstone and carvel's cake batter ice cream.

i recommend using splenda instead of sugar since there is sugar in the cake mix.

you can use 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract if you please. you can also use 3/4 cup of cake mix.

this recipe is to use with an ice cream maker (mine is by cuisinart)

1. place freezer bowl of ice cream maker into the freezer
2. it is better to keep it in there 24 / 7 that way it is always ready
3. in a medium bowl , whisk the milk and granulated sugar until the sugar is dissolved
4. stir in the heavy cream and vanilla to taste
5. stir in cake mix , making sure there are no lumps
6. pour mixture into the freezer bowl and let mix until it has thickened
7. remove ice cream from freezer bowl and place into a separate container
8. place freezer bowl and the ice cream into the freezer to further harden
demonstrations.review: My son loves this

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy turkey burger

this burger is tasty and the shredded cheese gives it a great flavor. i've used cheddar cheese, co-jack, or a mexican cheese mixture. you may need more breadcrumbs, depending on how moist your turkey is. i like to serve this with veganaise or mayo on the side.

1. mix all ingredients together in large bowl
2. add more bread crumbs if necessary
3. should form a firm ball
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. shape into six patties , not too thin
6. pan-fry , broil , or grill inside or out until lightly browned and cooked through , about 5 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: I am sorry but my family really didn't care for this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s slow cooker eye of round roast with gravy

slow cooking is the best method for an eye of round roast, i have cooked eye of round many times in a crock-pot with fantastic results, and you can use blade roast in place of the eye of round. the gravy from this roast goes well with mashed potatoes. do not add in any extra salt to this recipe and use only low sodium beef broth for this. if you are an onion lover, then you could add in a small chopped or sliced onion if desired. remember, do not lift the lid of the crock-pot while cooking. each time you do, the heat is lost and you will need to cook it for a longer time.

1. in a bowl combine the mushroom soup with beef broth , dry onion soup mix , fresh garlic and worcestershire sauce
2. mix until combined , then transfer into a 5-6-quart crock pot
3. in a small bowl mix together flour with black pepper and garlic powder
4. dredge the roast in the flour / black pepper mixture
5. heat oil in a skillet over medium heat
6. add in the roast and lightly brown on all sides
7. transfer the roast to the slow cooker and generously spoon the broth mixture on top of the roast
8. cover and cook on low for 8 hours or until the roast is tender
9. for a thicker gravy , after cooking remove gravy to saucepan and thicken with water / cornstarch mixture
demonstrations.review: Really good

target.recipe_text:
cedar planked salmon with sweet mustard vinaigrette

preparation time does not include the four+ hours soak time for the cedar cooking plank (available online or at many kitchen stores).  this is a combination of a recipe from food network and the other bobby flay.  great served with our without the vinaigrette.

1. at least 4 hours before , place the cedar plank in water to soak
2. place a heavy object on it to submerge completely
3. vinaigrette:
4. whisk the vinegar , mustard , and shallot together in a medium bowl
5. gradually whisk in the honey , then the oil , until the dressing is emulsified
6. season to taste with salt and pepper
7. salmon:
8. remove skin from salmon fillet
9. remove any remaining bones
10. rinse the salmon under cold running water and pat dry with paper towels
11. generously season the salmon with salt and pepper on both sides
12. lay the salmon on the cedar plank and carefully spread the mustard over the top and sides
13. place the brown sugar in a bowl and crumble between your fingers , then sprinkle over the mustard
14. set grill for indirect grilling and heat to medium-high
15. place the cedar plank in the center of the hot grate , away from the heat
16. cover the grill and cook until cooked through , around 20 to 30 minutes
17. the internal temperature should read 135 degrees f
18. remove the fish to serving plates or a platter and spoon a few tablespoons of vinaigrette over each fillet
19. serve immediately
target.review: Forgot to soak the cedar plank so had to grill without it but is was still great! I followed the recipe exactly but with half the vinaigrette.  We can't wait to try it on the plank.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caribbean rice and black bean salad

if you like some spice then add in some cayenne pepper. you can make this hours in advance and chill, and the complete recipe can be doubled to 5 cups cooked rice. prep time does not include cooking the rice.

1. in a small bowl whisk together oil , vinegar , dijon , cumin and garlic until well blended
2. season with salt and pepper to taste , add in some sugar if you find that the dressing is too strong
3. in a medium bowl combine the cooled or cold cooked rice , black beans , corn niblets , bell peppers and green onions
4. add in enough dressing to moisten
5. toss to combine
6. season once again with salt and pepper
7. can be made hours ahead , cover and chill
demonstrations.review: Very good!  I threw in some cilantro and everyone loved it!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach   feta stuffed chicken breast  quick   easy

this is the best chicken i have ever had!  it's so fast and easy and it tastes like something you would get at a fancy dinner somewhere nice!  my husband raved about it and my friends love it too!  it's a keeper!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. prepare chicken for stuffing
3. cook spinach in garlic and oil on top of stove until done
4. add in feta cheese and mix well
5. distribute spinach mixture onto each chicken breast
6. wrap chicken around mixture and secure with a toothpick
7. roll each breast in bread crumbs until well coated
8. place in glass baking dish and pour butter over them
9. cook for 30 minutes and serve
10. i usually have spinach mixture left over and just serve it as a side dish
11. it's so good that people always want more !
demonstrations.review: We loved it!  I followed the recipe exactly--don't change a thing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wasabi tuna steaks with green beans

i love this recipe so much. a delicious wasabi/sesame tuna steak and sweetened green beans. serve with basmati rice for a fabulous date night meal - but quick and easy enough for a family too. (i think i got this recipe from epicurious, but its been so long ago that i dont remember) - laurah

1. mix soy , wasabi and garlic powder in a glas 8x10 baking dish
2. add tuna and turn several times to coat
3. let stand 15 minutes each side
4. cook beans in a large pot of boiling water for about 4 minutes
5. heat sesame oil at med-high
6. when hot , sear tuna 2 minutes each side- pepper each side before searing
7. remove tuna steaks and add the marinade , brown sugar and beans
8. cook until reduced - about 4 minutes
9. serve with white or brown rice
demonstrations.review: Very tasty. DH said 3 stars but I gave 4, probably would have been better if I used the whole amount of wasabi. I measured 1 tsp and that seemed like a lot but couldn't taste it at all in the final dish.  I also subbed 2 packets of truvia for the brown sugar and the sweetness was perfect.  Next time I'll use the whole 3 tsp of wasabi and will update my review. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
costa rican tilapia

this recipe is from www.tastycooking.com.  authentic costa rican dish!

1. for the tilapia marinade , combine lime juice , 1 tablespoon olive oil , 2 tablespoons cilantro , 1 teaspoon garlic , 1 / 2 teaspoon salt , and sugar in a shallow dish
2. add tilapia and marinate 15 minutes , turning once
3. to prepare the bean and rice mixture , cook the rice according to package and keep warm while the tilapia is marinating
4. preheat oven to 400 degrees
5. in a large , skillet or saucepan , heat 2 tablespoons olive oil on medium heat
6. add remaining garlic and onions
7. saut until translucent , about 5 minutes , stirring
8. add 2 tablespoons cilantro , oranges , tomatoes , beans , oregano , 1 teaspoon salt , pepper , and cayenne
9. cook , uncovered , until hot , 7 to 8 minutes , stirring occasionally
10. transfer hot rice to a 9 by 13 inch baking dish
11. spoon the bean mixture on top of rice and gently blend
12. slightly overlap tilapia fillets on top and scrape marinade over fillets
13. bake 16 to 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: We love this with tilapia, but last night we made it with a pound of shrimp instead-INCREDIBLE!!!  Thanks so much for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled cilantro lime pork chops  bbq

shop rite recipe card to the rescue!

1. heat grill to medium direct heat
2. meanwhile , sprinkle chops with garlic pepper seasoning and onion salt
3. rub to coat
4. set aside
5. blend remaining ingredients in a small bowl
6. place chops on grill and cook 3 minutes per side , covered
7. brush with oil mixture
8. turn chops over and grill 3-5 minutes per side or until internal temperature is 160f brush with remaining oil mixture and turn once
demonstrations.review: Love the citrus with the pork, a big hit!

target.recipe_text:
salsa stoup and double decker baked quesadillas

this comes from rachael ray’s 365 cookbook. this looks like just our thing! we usually have all of these ingredients in the house. yum-o!

1. preheat the oven to 300
2. heat a medium soup pot over medium high heat
3. add the vegetable oil and the jalapenos , bell peppers , onions , celery and garlic
4. season with salt and pepper , then saut the veggies for 5 minutes
5. add all the tomatoes and stock and bring to a bubble
6. reduce the heat to a simmer and stir in the cilantro
7. paint one side of 2 tortillas with oil and place them , oil side down , on a large cookie sheet
8. mix the cheddar with the scallions and divide them between the tortillas evenly
9. top with another tortilla and top each of these with equal amounts of pepper jack cheese
10. set the last tortillas on top and brush the tops with oil
11. bake the quesadillas for 10 minutes , and then cool for 5 minutes to set
12. cut each into 6 wedges
13. serve each bowl of stoup with 3 wedges of quesadilla and sour cream for topping either
target.review: I got this from my Rachael cookbook as well. We loved the quesadillas, they wereas Rachael would say, delish! The stoup was good, it was perfect for dipping the quesadillas into, but we decided we wouldn't be able to just sit and eat it with a spoon. It is very good as a dip though!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy  tortilla soup vegetarian

i came up with this after reading a tip from a can of refried beans.  i first made my chicken version and then thought it would be great with black beans instead of the meat.  so easy to put together and a delicious soup.

1. combine tomatoes , broth , beans and corn in medium saucepan
2. stir together and bring to a boil
3. reduce and bring to a simmer till heated through
4. turn off heat and stir in the cilantro
5. top each bowl of soup with cheese and crushed tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: Probably the easiest soup I have ever made and SO good! My husband doesn't even care for soup and he said this is his new favorite soup! It was a little spicy and had really good flavor. I topped it with Santa Fe style tortilla strips. Will be making again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smashed potatoes for two

this is such a simple side dish that i use often.  you can adjust the butter and sour cream amounts to satisfy your taste and diet.  my measurements here are pretty rough estimates--i usually eyeball it, so keep that in mind.

1. wash potatoes
2. prick potatoes for baking
3. bake in microwave until soft and cooked through
4. place cooked potatoes in mixing bowl , add all other ingredients , and mash with potato masher until at desired consistency
demonstrations.review: These were very simple and pretty good. Just like a baked potato all smashed up in a bowl. I used a spread instead of the butter and I would definitely use more of that next time. I microwaved mine for 8 minutes and they could have used a couple more minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
three cheese shortbreads

these are great paired with any kind of cream soup.  my favourite is with a great cream of broccoli and cheese soup.  the preparation time includes the time to refrigerate the dough.

1. beat the butter until light and fluffy
2. stir in the three cheeses , cayenne pepper , mustard powder , and flour
3. mix well
4. if the dough is too crumbly , add milk tablespoon by tablespoon , until the dough holds together
5. pat the dough into a disc and refrigerate for 1 hour
6. preheat the oven to 300f
7. roll the dough out into a large 1 / 4-inch thick circle
8. use a scalloped cookie cutter to cut out the shortbreads
9. place on a greased cookie sheet and bake 30 to 35 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review:
These were pretty good. I did find that I was out of cayenne after I started making them, so I subbed chili powder. I will try these again with the cayenne, and possibly some other spices as well. I did have a bit of trouble rolling the dough out at first, but after sprinkled a bit of flour on my work surface it got easier. Overall these were quick, easy!
Made for PAC Fall 2008

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cilantro lime rice

delicious rice dish......fresh lime juice and cilantro wake up your taste buds....eat alone or with your favorite mexican dishes.

1. once your rice is cooked fluff with fork
2. add lime juice , zest , cilantro and salt
3. stir well
4. serve warm
5. enjoy
demonstrations.review: I forgot to add the lime zest, but this was still really good. We used it to make our own copy cat Chipotle burrito bowls.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salsa stoup   rachael ray 30 minute meals

this is actually a really good end of the week-use up all the veggies kind of stoup.  it makes a great lunch!  i added black beans i had leftover from taco night and i also added rice.  the jalapeno doesn't make it too hot either.  if you don't like the heat of a jalapeno, they can definately be omitted all together and this would still be great!

1. heat a medium soup pot over medium-high heat
2. add 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil , 2 turns of the pan and the jalapenos , bell pepper , onions , celery and garlic
3. season with salt and pepper then saute veggies 5 minutes
4. add tomatoes , crushed tomatoes and stock and bring soup to a bubble
5. reduce heat to a simmer and stir in cilantro
demonstrations.review: We thought this was ok, it was good as a dip, but we didn't really enjoy eating it as a soup. It did go really well as a dip to the quesadillas recipe that goes with this one in Rach's cookbook though!

target.recipe_text:
french toast with pears  brie  and cinnamon

a delicious twist on french toast that can be made-ahead and chilled for up to 24 hours. great for brunch, holidays, and special occasions.

1. grease a 9x13 baking dish
2. set aside
3. in a large skillet cook pears , brown sugar , and rosemary in 2 t butter over medium heat for 4-5 mins or until pears are tender
4. arrange 7 or 8 bread slices in a single layer in prepared dish
5. spoon pear mixture and arrange brie on bread slices
6. top each stack with a bread slice
7. brush bread with melted butter
8. combine sugar and cinnamon
9. sprinkle evenly over bread
10. in a medium bowl whisk together milk , eggs , vanilla , and salt
11. slowly pour over bread slices
12. cover and chill for 1-24 hours
13. preheat oven to 375f bake , uncovered , for 40-45 mins or until edges are puffed and golden
14. let stand for 10 minutes
15. serve warm with maple syrup , berries , and honey , or cranberry conserve
target.review: I made this for guests over the holidays and it was a hit!  I made it exactly as submitted.  The pears and rosemary are a great combination.  The leftovers heated up nicely the next day in the microwave.  Some guests suggested syrup with the leftovers and that tasted great too.  Thanks for an awesome recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mary s zucchini bread

this is my mother-in-law's favorite recipe and for very good reason!  this recipe makes two very moist and flavorful loaves.  i hope you will enjoy it!

1. place eggs , oil , zucchini and vanilla extract in blender and puree
2. sift together sugar , flour , baking soda , salt and baking powder and cinnamon
3. pour liquid ingredients into dry and mix
4. add nuts
5. divide batter into two loaf pans
6. bake at 325f degrees for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: This bread turned out beautifully.  It rose nicely in the loaf pans and it was very moist.  I usually have trouble with zucchini bread getting done in the center, but this recipe was right on.  Nice in the center and not burnt on the outside.  This is my "keeper" recipe for zucchini bread.  Thanks Bev!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot round steak

nan

1. combine all ingredients in crock pot
2. cook on low for 8-10 hours or on high for 5-6 hours
3. goes well with mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: This recipe was delicious and so easy!  I omitted the mushrooms as my husband doesn't like them, and added some sliced onions to the soup and dried onion soup mixture.  I browned the meat before I put it in the slow cooker, seasoning with pepper.  I didn't find it bland at all.  As a matter of fact, I didn't salt anything because of the salty taste of the dried onion soup mix.  The meat was very tender and flavorful.  I served it with mashed potatoes and the gravy was excellent.  I'l  make this dish again.  Thanks for posting it, Clairissa!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swiss ham potato scallop

imho this is the best ham casserole ever.  the swiss cheese adds divine flavor.  i got this recipe from my school principal's wife.  thanks, eunice!  this is perfect for potlucks or sit-down  dinners or as a treat for a sick neighbor.  it's a little more work but the flavor makes you glad you made it!

1. if you do not have leftover cooked red potatoes , cook them first
2. cool them enough to handle and cube them
3. shred the cheese and cube the ham
4. preheat the oven to 400 degrees
5. butter a 1-1 / 2 quart casserole
6. reserve
7. saute the onion in the 2 tablespoons butter until tender , not browned
8. blend in flour , salt and pepper
9. add the milk
10. cook and stir until thickened and bubbly
11. add the cheese and when melted , stir in the ham and potatoes , being gentle with the stirring
12. turn into prepared casserole
13. prepare the topping
14. combine the crumbs and melted butter
15. sprinkle on top of casserole
16. bake in preheated oven for 25 to 30 minutes or until lightly browned and bubbly
demonstrations.review: Great recipe!  I made this just as is and hubby loved it.  I think this recipe would taste good no matter what cheese you used.  Thanks Lorraine!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
better than sex cake iii

it is my understanding that there are a variety of recipes masquerading under this name, but this is the one that my friends like most.  overnight chilling not included in preparation time.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease and lightly flour 13" x 9" cake pan
3. mix cake as directed on package
4. bake the cake about 35 minutes or until it tests done
5. as soon as it comes out of the oven , poke holes all over it with a fork and pour sweetened condensed milk evenly over the cake , followed by caramel sauce
6. refrigerate overnight
7. shortly before serving , spread whipped topping over cake and sprinkle with crushed heath bars
8. enjoy
demonstrations.review: This cake is easy to prepare, rich, gooey, and oh sooo good!  I mixed the sweetened condensed milk and caramel together before pouring over cake and this worked out well. Thanks for a great recipe.  It's a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacardi rum cake

this bacardi rum cake is lovely and moist. i usually make it around new years, makes a nice looking dessert for a buffet and the taste is rich and wonderful. from a magazine add, many years ago.

1. sprinkle nuts over bottom of greased 10 inch tube pan or 12 cup bundt pan
2. stir together cake mix , pudding mix , eggs , water , oil and rum
3. pour batter over nuts
4. bake at 325 in oven for 1 hour
5. cool 10 minutes in pan
6. invert onto serving plate and prick top
7. glaze-----------------
8. melt butter in saucepan
9. stir in water and sugar
10. boil 5 minutes , stirring constantly
11. remove from heat
12. stir in rum
13. brush glaze evenly over top and sides of cake
14. allow cake to absorb glaze
15. repeat until glaze is used up
demonstrations.review: I served this over the holidays and it was a great success!  The rum flavor is wonderful and the nut crunch on top is delicious.  Very easy to prepare.  This will be my only recipe for rum cake from now on.  Thanks Derf!

target.recipe_text:
quick and easy chicken parmesan

an absolutely tasty and versatile dish. i have prepared this for two of us and for 100 men on a men's retreat and with the same consistency of flavor.

1. wash and pat the chicken breasts dry and then coat them with the breadcrumbs
2. after the chicken breasts are breaded , fry them either in a teflon skillet or with a little olive oil
3. fry the breasts until they are completely cooked
4. pour 1 / 2 of the spaghetti sauce into a 9"x5" casserole dish
5. place the cooked chicken breasts on top of the sauce
6. pour the remaining spaghetti sauce on top of the chicken breasts
7. sprinkle both cheeses on top put the dish into a 400 degree oven for 30 minutes , or long enough to warm all the sauce and breasts throughly and melt the cheese
8. serve over spaghetti
target.review: This was delicious, but the breading thing was a wreck without the egg (why didn't I read the reviews ahead of time??).  Tasted great, though, and all 3 of my kids ate it well!  My son is almost 7, and he was falling asleep eating a third helping!  That's evidence of a good meal! :)  Thank you for sharing this recipe!  It's one my family will enjoy in the future, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
noodles   herbs

this is a yummy little side dish that goes really well with beef roast, pork, and lots of other things.

1. cook noodles
2. drain and set aside
3. using pan you cooked your noodles in , put butter and spices in pan , melting butter and stirring spices into the butter
4. stir in noodles and coat well with the butter mixture
5. serve hot
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe for families who are in a bind for time!  I was looking for a quick, easy, convenient recipe to go with dinner, and came across this.  It was all 3! Thanks for sharing it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked acorn squash with spicy maple syrup

nan

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. split the squash into thirds and remove the seeds
3. cut a slice off the bottom of each piece so that it sits evenly , skin-side down , in a 9 x 13-inch glass baking dish
4. in the hollow of each piece , place 1 teaspoon unsalted butter , 1 tablespoon maple syrup , cinnamon and nutmeg to taste
5. bake in the heated oven until fork tender , about 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: My husband was none to pleased when I announced we were having acorn squash at dinner, but he couldn't shut up about it once he was eating it!  Delicious!
