An added bonus was that not only my husband loved it, but also my 2 year old daughter and my 8 month old (he ate some sections withOUT the syrup)!  It's a keeper! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy eggs

yummy way to have your eggs!

1. beat eggs and milk together
2. add salt and pepper to taste
3. cook over medium-high heat with the cream cheese
demonstrations.review: I made these eggs with whipping cream instead of milk (really desperate on a Saturday morning - out of milk).  I added about 1/3 cup of whipping cream instead of milk, and I used 7 eggs (just because I was feeding 3 people).  My 2 year old is STILL sitting at the table asking for a third helping of the eggs!  I'm fond of them, too!  They have a rich taste from the cream cheese.  Very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry pizza dessert

nan

1. mix flour , almonds and melted butter , press in a pizza pan
2. bake at 350 degrees for 15 minutes
3. let cool
4. combine cream cheese , powdered sugar and cool whip
5. spread over cooled crust
6. slice strawberries and combine with strawberry glaze
7. spread mixture over filing
demonstrations.review: I made this dessert about a week ago for company, and everyone gobbled it up.  Very easy, and just delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
penne with swiss chard   asiago cheese

quick and very good. from the local newspaper

1. in a large pot of boiling salted water , cook penne 8 to 10 minutes or until tender but firm
2. add 8 cups coarsely chopped swiss chard , cook 1 minute
3. drain well
4. in a large serving bowl , combine remaining ingredients
5. add pasta mixture
6. toss well
7. season to taste
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I added some cubed chicken to make it a rounded out meal, and to keep from taking away from the dish.  I used spiral pasta instead of the penne because it was what I had on hand, and this was delicious!  What a great, easy recipe to enjoy swiss chard!  Thanks for this recipe! :)  My 2 year old LOVED it!

target.recipe_text:
potatoes with leeks and rosemary

this is a quick potato dish - i love the addition of leeks!

1. in a wok , heat olive oil and butter over medium-high heat until hot , swirling to coat sides of pan
2. add potatoes and leek and cook , stirring and turning potato slices until hey turn translucent , 6 to 8 minutes
3. add chicken broth , wine , rosemary , salt , and pepper
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce heat to medium-low , cover , and cook until potatoes are tender , 20 to 25 minutes
6. uncover and cook , stirring occasionally , until most of liquid is absorbed , about 4 minutes
target.review: This was a delicious recipe. My potatoes never did get translucent - manybe I sliced them too thick. But, they were yummy anyway.  I couldn't toss out the green tops from the leeks, so I added them towards the end of the cooking.  They added a nice color and a bit of a crunch. I've just discovered the leek and I love it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chili you will ever taste

this is the best chili recipe i have ever tried. i'm not sure where the recipe originated, but it is amazing! sometimes, i don't bother adding all four cans of the kidney beans and it still turns out wonderful. once anyone tastes this chili, they will be begging for the recipe!! enjoy!

1. heat oil
2. cook onions , garlic and meat until brown
3. add tomatoes , beer , coffee , tomato paste and beef broth
4. add spices stir in 2 cans of kidney beans and peppers
5. reduce heat and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
6. add 2 remaining cans of kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: We love this recipe.  The only change I make is to reduce the amount of brown sugar by half.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
golabki  polish stuffed cabbage rolls   vegetarian version

pronounced gaw-wump-kee, literally meaning 'little pigeons'. probably the best known polish food. the ground meat & rice type in tomato sauce are the most common, but the seasonings and stuffings vary from region to region and there are many other varieties, including vegetarian versions like the one listed here.

1. slice through the base of the cabbage and cook in lightly salted boiling water until tender
2. when the leaves are tender , peel off
3. boil the rice until just tender
4. drain and set aside
5. fry the onions in the butter until softened
6. dice the mushrooms and fry lightly with the onions , and the worcestershire sauce , if using
7. mix with the rice and season with salt , pepper , garlic , paprika and parsley
8. place a tablespoonful of the rice mixture in each cabbage leaf
9. carefully , tuck in sides and roll to cover rice
10. heat the oven to 400f
11. grease a roasting pan and place cabbage rolls seam side down in pan , packing them tightly together
12. pour enough juice or stock over the top to cover them
13. sprinkle lightly with remaining paprika
14. cover and bake in oven for 20 minutes
15. remove cover and bake for another 10 minutes to brown the cabbage lightly
demonstrations.review: I was extremely apprehensive about making this dish, but it proved to be easier than I thought and was very tasty.  I wasn’t sure what was meant in Step 1 by “slice through the base of the stem, so I just cored the head. Then, I  used kitchen shears to snip away any remaining tough parts at the stem before filling the leaves.  Step #2: Little turtle was right, I had to immerse the head into the boiling water several times so that, each time the outer leaves were done to just the right tenderness.  I made the rice filling the night before and refrigerated it and I think that improved it – allowing the spices to blend better.  Everyone enjoyed this dish, even the meat eaters among us.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy moist salmon steaks

this recipe goes back years, the mayo is the secret to this recipe it's what locks in all the moisture in the fish,  you can also use large thick salmon fillets in place of the steaks, i like to use atlantic salmon fillets, but any salmon will do fine, this can easily be doubled, adjust the salt and pepper amount to taste, these also may be made on the grill placed on a pan

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. butter an 8 x 8-inch baking
3. rinse the salmon steaks and pat dry
4. in a bowl mix / whisk the melted butter , mayonnaise , lemon juice , worcestershire sauce , salt , pepper , paprika and garlic powder
5. add to the glass baking dish
6. add in the salmon steaks
7. turn to coat well and evenly in the butter / mayo mixture
8. bake for about 20-22 minutes , or until the fish flakes with a fork
demonstrations.review: Score another winner for Kittencal!  This was delicious.  I thought I had plenty of mayo, but as usual the boys left the jar nearly empty.  So, I used a little mayo and some homemade plain yogurt.  The recipe was very tasty and made a big hit with the gang.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thanksgiving pumpkin pie  uses fresh pumpkin

this is the one pumpkin pie recipe i keep coming back to year after year. i was at a military ladies' coffee when i first tasted this pie, and it was the most moist & eggy pumkpin pie i had ever eaten. i asked the hostess, barb, for the recipe, and she shared the recipe with me - which i believe came from her mother. i made my own changes to the recipe over the years and now i have written down my changes so that i can share my version with you. i only use fresh pumpkin in this recipe and it is well worth the little bit of extra effort. please note: this recipe calls for a deep dish pie plate and intended to be a egg custard textured pie.  even using a deep dish pie plate, you may still find you have a small amount of extra batter, as some deep dish pans are larger and deeper than others (mine fits all of the batter in one pie). you can use whole milks in this if you prefer, however i like the lighter taste of the skim in this. if you only have small pie plates, then you might want to prepare an extra pastry round and divide the batter between two smaller pies.

1. preheat oven to 400f and have ready a pie shield and a large rimmed cookie sheet
2. line a deep dish glass pie plate with the pie pastry round , fluting the edges decoratively as desired
3. combine in order the pumpkin , sugar , salt , cinnamon , ginger , nutmeg , and cloves
4. lightly beat eggs together with both milks , then add to the pumpkin mixture , stirring well to combine--it will be rather thin
5. pour as much filling as you can into unbaked pie pastry and bake at 400f for 50 minutes
6. if there is any extra filling use to fill a smaller mini pie plate or discard
7. if the pie edges start overbrowning , place a pie shield or a ring of foil over the edges--this will be needed or not depending on the type of pastry you use
8. pie should be served chilled and should be stored in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: Thanks so much for posting.  This may be the first pumpkin pie I've made that didn't sink in the center.  It looks creamy and yummy.  I think even the pumpkin haters in the family will take a slice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garden primavera fettuccine

from simple and delicious - boy i love this magazine!  submitted by t. perrault.  i love how she combined cauliflower, broccoli and zucchini within this recipe.  just a lovely combination.  feel free to use already prepared alfredo sauce or your own recipe for alfredo sauce.  i made this once as a side dish and realized it makes a large amount, so then the next time i added some cooked chicken to make it a main meal.  serve with crusty bread and you are done!

1. in a large saucepan , cook fettuccine according to the package directions
2. add vegetables during the last 4 minutes of cooking pasta
3. drain and return all to the pan
4. add alfredo sauce and basil , tossing to coat
5. cook over low heat for 1-2 minutes or until heated through
6. sprinkle with parmesan cheese to your taste right before serving
demonstrations.review: This was very nice and refreshing - even with store bought Alfredo sauce.

target.recipe_text:
creamy pasta with bacon

i have to admit whenever i first saw this i was skeptical...but after one bite, i was hooked. it has a flavor that i didn't expect, especially after hearing the ingredients. i don't know where it originally came from as i got this recipe from my mom. unsure of serving amount...makes quite a bit though.

1. cook pasta and drain
2. fry bacon , drain off grease , and crumble into small pieces
3. saute mushrooms , garlic , and green onions in bacon grease
4. add pasta , parmesan , bacon pieces , whipping cream , and black pepper to sauted mushroom mixture
5. simmer until slightly thickened
6. enjoy !
target.review: This was outstanding! I cut the recipe in half and made it for dinner for DH and me; the only change I made was to add way more mushrooms. This was a breeze to prepare and cooks up pretty fast too. We both wolfed it down; it was absolutely delicious. There was plenty for the two of us and there would have been leftovers if hubby hadn't polished it all off!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s fettuccine alfredo

nan

1. set small frying pan in mid-high heat
2. add the butter and the cream to the frying pan and mix well
3. stir the sauce frequently and add the black pepper , salt and nutmeg , boil and immediately lower the heat and stir frequently until the sauce becomes heavier , it should take a few minutes of constant stirring
4. add the pasta to the boiling water along with some salt and cook to your liking
5. once the pasta is cooked , drain the pasta and add the sauce to it
6. mix well
7. add the grated cheese to the sauce and pasta , and mix until the cheese is absorbed by the sauce
demonstrations.review: There are no stars here, not because my dinner wasn't five-star quality, because it was. It was fabulous. It's just that I made some significant changes to the recipe. In my largest skillet, I melted the butter first--and sauteed two minced garlic cloves in it--before I added the cream. I only had 1/2 cup heavy cream (I thought I had more), so I had to use half-and-half as well. I increased the parmigiano-reggiano to a full cup, plus added about 3/4 lb cooked king crab legs (shelled) to the sauce just before I tossed it with the drained pasta (I tossed everything in the skillet in which the sauce had cooked). Speaking of pasta, I used 300 grams of spaghettini, rather than the full pound of fettucine. The sauce was heavenly, thick but still ethereal -- every strand of pasta was coated and there was no little puddle at the bottom of the serving bowl like you typically expect with thin sauces. My dinner served 3 perfectly. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marmalade glazed ham

simple but oh so good. garnish the ham with slices of fresh orange and parsley

1. heat oven to 325f'score the fat on the ham into diamonds
2. bake uncovered for 1 1 / 2 hours
3. combine the remaining ingredients and mix well
4. during the last 20 minutes of baking time increase the oven temp tp 400 degrees f
5. spoon half the glaze over the ham covering the sides as well
6. return to oven for 10 minutes
7. spoon the rest of the glaze over the ham bake a final 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic; I may not use another recipe again. The orange flavour suited me perfectly, and it was so easy to whip together using ingredients I always have on hand. I followed the recipe exactly, except my ham was a little bigger so I lengthened my cooking time a bit. Thanks so much for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate cake brownies with splenda

this recipe is posted in request. i found it in a booklet published by splenda. i have not tried it, so i hope you will enjoy it.

1. mix tog splenda , flour , cocoa , baking powder and salt
2. and set aside
3. beat tog margarine , eggs and vanilla for 1 minute
4. add applesauce and beat until blended
5. add flour mixture and nuts until blended
6. spread evenly in a greased 8 inch square cake pan
7. bake at 350 deff for about 15 minutes or until tester inserted in centre comes out clean
8. cool on rack
9. store in a coverd container in the fridge
demonstrations.review: This was my first experiment using Splenda, in anything. Both my DH and I agreed that this was much more of a cake than a brownie, not that there's anything wrong with cake of course! On the positive side, the recipe was easy to put together (note to others: it may look curdled at first, when mixing, but don't worry, it all comes together just fine); baked up very quickly; has a wonderful appearance, all dark and chocolatey-looking; and cut nicely after cooling. The taste was good--not great or exceptional, but good. Very moist, too. On the negative side, the Splenda is so expensive that this recipe, which you would think wouldn't cost a lot to make, unfortunately does; I also detected an aftertaste I didn't like, which could possibly have come from the applesauce but I suspect came from the Splenda. I will definitely be passing this recipe on to my MIL, who has been diagnosed as a borderline diabetic. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked mustard chicken

something easy and delicious. you can serve it either hot or cold. goes great in chicken salad.

1. brush chicken with mustard and dredge in bread crumbs
2. place in a 13- x 9- x 2-inch baking dish
3. combine margarine , lemon juice , and wine
4. drizzle 1 tablespoon over each piece of chicken and pour remainder in dish
5. cover and bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
6. remove cover , sprinkle with paprika , and bake an additional 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Truly easy, truly delicious. This made for a simple, tasty dinner tonight (with white rice and steamed green beans) that was enjoyed by the entire family. Note that the nutritional analysis is a little off, as there will be a residue of butter/margarine left in the bottom of the pan that isn't eaten. I mixed brown mustard and dijon together, and next time I'll likely try a spicy mustard. This is a yummy dish that will become a staple in my home.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ugly naked chicken

the sweet tangy sauce this chicken cooks in results in delicious, sweet, slightly sticky chicken that is just delicious. it may be the ugliest chicken you've ever seen (especially if you skin the chicken first, as i usually do), but it sure does taste good.i usually grab a "family pack" of select chicken parts or i use drumsticks and yank off all the skin with the help of kitchen shears. a serving is two pieces each. i originally found this in one of my favorite community cookbooks, "enough to feed an army" years ago.  this is my adaptation and i gave it the name "ugly naked" based on my method of skinning the chicken.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. place chicken pieces in a 9x13" casserole sprayed with nonstick cooking spray
3. generously sprinkle chicken pieces with garlic powder , salt and pepper to taste on both sides
4. bake , uncovered , for 40 minutes
5. meanwhile , in a microwaveable bowl , combine honey , soy sauce , butter , worcestershire sauce , and lemon juice and heat on high power for about 30-45 seconds , or until butter melts and you can easily stir ingredients together- watch carefully so you don't overheat it and end up with a melted butter mess in your microwave
6. after chicken has baked for the 40 minutes , pour the honey mixture all over the chicken and bake another 10 minutes , flip chicken over , bake another 10 minutes longer or until chicken is cooked all the way through and is tender
demonstrations.review: So, everything's on the table for dinner and my 20 yr old son walks into the room. "What's for dinner?" "Ugly naked chicken," I say. I get THAT LOOK. "Hey, I don't make these things up," I tell him. "You're all on crack," he announced...and then proceeds to demolish the dinner. He wolfed it down! (So did hubby and I, too.) So, despite the name giving him cause to wonder at the sanity of us all (LOL), dinner was a huge hit. I used skinless boneless breasts and so cut the oven time back. I only used 6 breasts, but kept the sauce amount the same (DH and I like lots of sauce, anyway). This was so easy to prepare, with simple ingredients. When the chicken was done, I poured all the sauce into a pan, brought it to a boil and then thickened it with a wee bit of cornstarch dissolved in cold water, then strained the sauce (to get out the chicken bits) into a gravy boat. Served it with rice and broccoli; there wasn't a speck of anything left. Thanks so much for posting this, Heather; I've found a new family favourite!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot tangy rump roast

this recipe couldn't be easier! the "tang" comes from the cranberry sauce (one of the just 5 ingredients used in this recipe).

1. sprinkle the onion soup mix in the bottom of the crock pot
2. place the rump roast in next
3. spoon the cranberry sauce around and over the roast
4. cover and cook on low 8 - 12 hours
5. remove roast from crock pot and allow to rest while you thicken the gravy
6. turn the crock pot up to high
7. blend the softened butter and flour into a paste and whisk it into the gravy
8. cover and cook on high for about 10 minutes , until thick
9. slice the roast into 1 / 4" thick slices and serve with the gravy
10. the left-over slices may be frozen in the gravy in plastic freezer bags
target.review: Super easy and super good, my husband loved the gravy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked pork chops and apples

i found this in a pamphlet from the orchard (about maryland apple orchards) a few years ago when we were picking apples. it is one of the tastiest things i have ever made!

1. peel , core , and slice the apples
2. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
3. melt the butter in a skillet
4. brown the pork chops on both sides in the butter
5. grease a large baking dish
6. put the apple slices in the bottom of the dish
7. mix the brown sugar and cinnamon
8. sprinkle the cinnamon and sugar over the apples
9. place the pork chops on top of the apples
10. cover with foil and bake for 1 and 1 / 2 hours
demonstrations.review: I put all kinds of vegies under the chops along with the apples and a slice of lemon on top of the chop. Yummm

demonstrations.recipe_text:
just like loaded baked potatoes casserole

this is an awesome low-carb version of loaded baked potatoes, and tastes far better than any version of mock potatoes that i have tried. in fact, this dish is soooo good, you will not believe it!  i do not remember where i got this recipe, but it is a fabulous side to any low-carb meal. you will be pleased, i promise! yum! yum!

1. pre-heat oven to 350
2. chop cooked cauliflower into very small pieces
3. mix sour cream , 1 / 2 of the green onions , 1 / 2 of the cheese , 1 / 2 of the bacon , and salt and pepper to taste in medium bowl
4. stir in the cauliflower
5. place in medium baking dish and sprinkle remaining cheese and bacon on top
6. bake for 20 minutes
7. sprinkle the remaining green onions on top just before serving
demonstrations.review: Yummmm! Definately a keeper and easily gluten free. The califlower I got was small so I added some left over steamed carrots-turnips-beets and all was chopped about 1 inch square to maintain some crunch. I steamed the fresh califlower 15 minutes. Used Jennie O turkey bacon. My husbands testimony..."tell them I ate it before I ate my meatloaf." Very colorful, it would be a great pot luck dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled balsamic london broil

prep time is 5 minutes. the rest is time marinating.

1. put all ingredients , except meat , in a container fitted with a lid
2. cover and shake
3. pour the marinade over the top round steak and cover
4. marinate in the refrigerator for 4 hours or overnight , turning the meat occasionally
5. grill or broil until done as desired
6. slice thinly
demonstrations.review: We used a london broil...BBQed...awsome.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted eggplant and feta

this is a greek recipe.  this can be used to top a salad of baby spinach or other greens, pasta, couscous or any other similar thing.  or, scoop it up on small bites of good crusty bread, or serve as a variation of eggplant bruschetta.  it can be served as an appetizer, a side dish, or a meatless main course.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. place eggplant cubes in a shallow baking pan
3. toss with 1 / 2 cup olive oil , salt to taste , bake until cubes are soft but not mushy -- about 30 minutes
4. set aside to cool
5. whisk together the remaining 1 / 4 cup olive oil , lemon juice , onion , garlic , and oregano in a small bowl
6. season to taste with salt and pepper
7. toss about half the dressing with eggplant
8. put eggplant mixture on top of salad leaves , cooked pasta , couscous or slices of bread or toasts
9. sprinkle with cheese and olives , drizzle with remaining dressing
10. garnish with fresh oregano sprigs if desired
demonstrations.review: Very good, I also roasted bell peppers and onions with the eggplant. Added cherry tomatoes as a final touch on top. Served on hearts of romaine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
round steak in beer

i got this recipe from cece, a sweet lady at a campground in lebanan mo. i was living in a 5th wheel camper with my dh for his job. we became friends and spent plenty of time together while my dh was off working. being a newlywed i was always looking for good cheap meals to fix for us. we like to eat this with mashed potatoes or egg noodles.

1. flour steak then brown in oil in skillet
2. then place meat in a 2 quart casserole dish
3. in the skillet brown onion
4. stir in tomatoes , oregano , basil worcestershire sauce , beer salt and pepper
5. bring to a boil for 1 minute
6. pour sauce over meat in casserole dish
7. bake covered in a 350 oven for 1 1 / 2 hours
demonstrations.review: I made it in the crock pot and used italian stewed tomatoes instead of pureed tomatoes. great leftovers too. ( :

target.recipe_text:
panera broccoli cheese soup

a very good broccoli cheese soup. served with crusty bread.

1. saut onion in butter
2. set aside
3. cook melted butter and flour using a whisk over medium heat for 3-5 minutes or until you see a noticeable golden brown color in your pan
4. slowly add in the chicken stock and whisk again to combine
5. simmer contents covered for 20 minutes on medium heat
6. add the broccoli , carrots and the sauteed onions , into the pot
7. stir , add the milk and half & half
8. cook covered over low heat 20-25 minutes but do not bring to a boil
9. this may cause the milk to curdle
10. add salt , pepper & nutmeg
11. continue to cook the soup on low heat and slowly add the grated cheese a handful at a time and stir to avoid clumps
12. once all the cheese has been added is melted , remove from heat , and serve immediately
13. suggestion: serve with crusty bread or in a breadbowl
14. refrigerate leftovers after they have cooled and store in a airtight container up to 5 days in the refrigerator
target.review: Really delicious.  I can't wait to make this again.  I made it exactly as the recipe indicated and I have no complaints.  If you want to thin it down a bit, leave the lid on when simmering or add a little milk.  I used an immersion blender to break up some of the larger pieces of broccoli. Wonderful soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country chuck roast with onion gravy

this was originally my great grandmother's recipe and was passed on to my grandmother. my memaw made this dish for many family get-togethers and always accompanied it with mounds of mashed potatoes, cole slaw and green beans, all fresh from her garden. the brown sugar is the magic that makes this roast utterly divine.

1. rub the salt , pepper , and brown sugar into all the sides of the roast
2. place the meat and the whole onion into an roasting pan
3. roast in a 450f oven for 15 minutes , flip the roast over and roast for an additional 15 minutes
4. whisk together the water , flour , 1 1 / 2 teaspoon salt and pepper
5. pour the flour mixture into the roasting pan and reduce the oven heat to 350f and roast for 2 hours or roast for 3 hours at 300f , flipping the roast over once at the midpoint of the cooking time
6. cover the pan if the meat looks like it is drying out
7. chop the onion into the gravy before serving
demonstrations.review: Fantastic!  This recipe could not be any easier and it is delicious.  Only thing I did diffrently was sear all sides of meat in cast iron skillet and then I added a few whole cloves of garlic in the roasting pan along with the whole onion.  I used an immersion blender to chop the onion and garlic up into the gravy.  This is a great recipe. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
faux ground beef stroganoff  turkey

this is made with ground turkey, which has a lot less calories and fat than ground beef. even people who don't like ground turkey like this! as usual, fast, easy and tasty, and a nice comfort food.

1. brown turkey well in a large frying pan
2. when brown , add the brown gravy mix , water , herbs and pepper bring to a boil , then reduce heat and let slow boil for 15-20 minutes to thicken the sauce
3. add sour cream , mix well and serve
4. you can add mushroom , peas , onions or whatever to this
5. if i add onions and mushrooms , i usually saute them with the turkey
6. serve over egg noodles , with a big salad and a slice of french bread
demonstrations.review: I didn't bother with the gravy mix and I added a good splash of white wine!  This was good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cucumber sandwich filling

creamy cucumber filling for sandwiches that is wonderful. the dill and garlic give it pizazz. this can also be used for an appetizer if used on the party rye bread.

1. press the cucumber through a colander to remove excess moisture
2. process cream cheese and mayonnaise in a blender or food processor until smooth
3. combine mixture , cucumber , dill and garlic salt chill until ready to use to allow flavors to blend
demonstrations.review: I made the mixture without the cucumber, spread it on the bread and then added slices of cucmber to make cucumber sandwiches for 60 at a tea party.  I wanted the texture of full slices of cucmber, rather than having it all blended together.  I just let the cream cheese sit out for a short time to soften and then mixed it with my hand mixer, which worked fine.  You can adjust the garlic and dill to suit your tastes.  We cut off the crusts and cut the sandwiches into triangles and got good reviews!  Everyone loved them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat olive garden minestrone soup by todd wilbur

from http://www.topsecretrecipes.com it's finally here! what everyone's been waiting for! just in time for winter, this soup is sure to warm your soul with it's savory flavor and wonderful aroma. i've asked many an olive garden waiter for this recipe, but none gave it to me in detail. one waiter told me the secret ingredient was to add a little red wine to the stock, but i'll leave that up to you to try.

1. heat three tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat in a large soup pot
2. saute onion , celery , garlic , green beans , and zucchini in the oil for 5 minutes or until onions begin to turn translucent
3. add vegetable broth to pot , plus drained tomatoes , beans , carrot , hot water , and spices
4. bring soup to a boil , then reduce heat and allow to simmer for 20 minutes
5. add spinach leaves and pasta and cook for an additional 20 minutes or until desired consistency
6. makes about eight 1 1 / 2 cup servings
demonstrations.review: Very good.  As others suggested, I used only 2 cans of beans and did not drain the tomatoes.  I added a a generous splash of red wine! My DH and I really enjoyed this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
most refreshing lemonade you will ever taste    quick   easy

this is the best tasting, most satisfying, easiest homemade lemonade you will ever drink. what could be more satisfying on a hot summer day than the cool, brisk refreshing taste of lemonade? this is so easy with the help of a citrus juicer to juice the lemons.

1. combine lemon juice , sugar and club soda stirring well to dissolve sugar
2. add sliced lemon to pitcher
3. chill
4. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Great. Easy. Refreshing. Lemonade is fizzy or sparkling in England, so this was perfect for the non-tea drinkers at an English tea party we just held. It all went in a very short time! If you like a strong lemon flavour, you can add extra lemon juice and it is still delicious.

target.recipe_text:
ribs my way

this is the way i always prepare my bbq ribs. they result in fall off the bone tender ribs, and they are always a hit. the spices listed are what i submitted for this recipe, however i probably never use the same thing twice. play around with those ingredients you enjoy the most. prep time includes marinating time.

1. mix brown sugar , garlic powder , and cayenne together in bowl
2. add salt and pepper if you wish
3. rub spice mixture onto ribs , both sides
4. wrap ribs in aluminum foil , using two sheets of foil
5. place ribs in fridge for at least 24 hours
6. remove ribs when ready to prepare and place in oven on warm
7. (my oven goes from warm to 250f , so i say place on warm , if your oven does have temps
8. lower than 250f , i would suggest 200f bake ribs on warm for at least 4 hours , up to 6 hours
9. remove ribs , and let them sit in foil , allowing them to cool to almost room temperature
10. place ribs on hot fire , and baste with your favorite sauce
11. let ribs cook on grill for approx 15 minutes or until hot
12. remove ribs and let them rest for approx 10 minutes before serving
target.review: We've made this recipe twice so far (exactly as written) and my husband has declared them his favorite.  Thanks for the recipe, it's excellent!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted garlic mashed potatoes   the best you ve ever had

nan

1. separate head of garlic into individual cloves
2. toss in olive oil and wrap tightly in small piece of aluminum foil
3. bake in 350f oven for 45 minutes
4. when the garlic has cooled to the touch you should be able to squeeze it out of the 'paper' shell of the individual cloves
5. mash the roasted garlic with a fork , or force through a fine strainer
6. if you use a ricer as recommended below , simply rice the garlic along with the potatoes
7. peel and boil potatoes in salted water until tender
8. force the cooked potatoes through a ricer or mash by your usual method
9. put the riced potatoes , garlic , sour cream , butter , and salt and white pepper in a mixer bowl , and whip at medium speed until smooth
10. add cream or milk to adjust consistency
demonstrations.review: Lives up to it's name!  Very good recipe, definitely worth the time.  I used a very large head of garlic (I love the stuff) and didn't need extra cream for a good consistency.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan bow ties

kid favorite.

1. cook noodles according to package directions
2. drain
3. transfer to a serving bowl
4. add the remaining ingredients
5. toss to coat
demonstrations.review: Simple and tasty dinner.  We like this best after it's been in the refrigerator overnight and always serve it cold.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
favorite squash   cheese

harvest time! a great alternative to mac & cheese. we made this several times last season when our garden was producing squash, squash & more squash. this recipe is from one of my very favorite cookbooks, 

1. preheat oven to 350
2. boil squash and onion in small amount of salted water until tender
3. drain
4. while squash in cooking , prepare topping:
5. melt 1 / 2 c
6. butter in skillet
7. saute crushed crackers in butter until crisp and brown , set aside
8. make a white sauce using 1 / 4 c
9. butter , cornstarch , and half& half
10. add cheese
11. stir until melted and sauce is smooth
12. arrange squash in 9 x 13 inch glass baking dish
13. pour sauce over squash
14. top with cracker topping
15. bake 25 minutes or until hot& bubbly
demonstrations.review: I LOVED this recipe!  I followed the recipe exactly and it was just perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach ricotta pie with a hint of feta

we've got a new local dairy (in such a small country, local also means national), that makes some of the best cheeses (and soy milk and soy puddings). this recipe really showcases their ricotta and feta cheeses. this is a great vegetarian dish to serve, we usually have some kind of variation after the yom kippur fast day. i also like to add some za'atar in with the oregano.

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees f
2. heat the oil in a heavy pot over high heat
3. add the onion and saute until translucent , about 3 minutes
4. add the spinach in batches , if necessary , and saute until the ribbons are just wilted
5. lightly beat the ricotta and the eggs together in a bowl
6. add the spinach mixture , feta , oregano and salt and pepper
7. mix thoroughly
8. pour the batter into a greased 9 x 13 inch pan
9. bake for about 40 minutes , until the top is lightly browned
10. serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: These flavors go exceptionally well together.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ranch pasta primavera

nan

1. steam veggies together and cool
2. cook pasta in broth
3. drain and cool
4. combine with veggies
5. add basil and dressing and toss
6. sprinkle with cheese and parsley
demonstrations.review: Excellent and simple pasta recipe bursting with flavor.  We added some cherry tomatoes for a finishing touch.  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
thai rice noodles with chicken and asparagus

oooooooh this is good! my husband said he now has no reason to leave me for an asian woman.  thanks alot!! i got this off of a rice noodle box. i like spicy food so its not too spicy for me but it does have chili sauce in it and also, i used salt instead of fish sauce.

1. pour noodles into bowl and cover with very hot tap water
2. soak for 15-20 minutes
3. heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add garlic and stir fry until golden
5. add fish sauce or salt and chicken
6. stir fry until done
7. add soy sauce , chili pepper sauce , and brown sugar
8. mix until sugar is dissolved
9. drain noodles and add to skillet along with asparagus
10. stir fry noodles until firm but tender
11. serve and enjoy !
target.review: Fabulous!  Made it just as written and it had just the right amount of heat and full of flavor!  Nice and fast too! Thanks for this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini couscous

a very quick and easy side dish. it could also double as the base for a cold salad with the addition of other chopped veggies and oil based dressing!

1. cut zucchini into 1 / 4-inch dice
2. in a large non-stick skillet cook zucchini in oil with cumin and salt and pepper to taste over moderate heat , stirring until just tender , about 5 minutes
3. add water and bring to a boil
4. stir in couscous and remove skillet from heat
5. let mixture stand , covered , for 5 minutes
6. fluff couscous with a fork
7. cover for 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was so fast and easy.  I had lots of zucchini from the garden and just found another way to use it.  The cumin gave it so much interesting flavor and it was ready in no time.  Served it to company and they raved about it as well. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country pork ribs

these hearty ribs feature a lip-smacking sauce that's deliciously tangy with just the right hint of sweetness. prep. time does not include refrigeration time. great with other meats too.

1. in a bowl , combine the first 10 ingredients
2. mix well
3. pour 1-1 / 2 cups marinade into a large resealable plastic bag
4. add the ribs
5. seal and turn to coat
6. refrigerate for at least 4 hours
7. cover and refrigerate remaining marinade
8. drain and discard marinade from the ribs
9. grill , covered , over indirect medium heat for 20 minutes on each side
10. meanwhile , in a saucepan , combine the honey , brown sugar and reserved marinade
11. bring to a boil
12. cook and stir for 2 minutes or until slightly thickened
13. baste ribs with some of the sauce
14. grill 15-20 minutes longer or until a meat thermometer reads 160 degrees , turning and basting occasionally
15. serve with the remaining sauce
demonstrations.review:
Love this marinade/barbecue sauce! Fruity, spicy, and interesting!  (Well, actually, I left out the horseradish because I'm not fond of it - and it was even good without it!)  Grilled them on the barbecue just as you suggested...mmmmm!
Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free french bread

this french bread is amazing!! it tastes so similar to the wheat containing french bread. plus it freezes wonderfully!!! it's crusty on the outside, and soft and tender within. it is fabulous alone, or made as little brushetta', using 'joanne's creamy brushetta' recipe(#108383).you can make it from start to finish in about one hour!!

1. in the bowl of a heavy-duty mixer , place flours , xanthan gum , salt , and egg replacer
2. blend with mixer on low
3. in a small bowl dissolve the sugar in the water , and add yeast
4. wait until the mixture foams slightly , then blend into the dry ingredients
5. add the butter , egg whites , and vinegar
6. beat on high for 3 minutes
7. to form loaves , spoon dough onto greased and cornmeal-dusted cookie sheets in two long french-loaf shapes or spoon into special french-bread pans
8. slash diagonally every few inches
9. if desired , brush with melted butter
10. cover the dough and let rise in a warm place until doubled in bulk , 20 to 25 minutes
11. preheat oven to 400 degrees
12. bake for 40 to 45 minutes
13. remove from pan to cool
demonstrations.review: This was my first attempt at gluten-free bread.  I made it for a friend who was coming to dinner!  She really liked it so I guess it was a hit!!  Very easy!  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy orange chicken with vegetables

i use kraft signature asian sesame dressing with this recipe, it can be served over noodles if you prefer.

1. heat large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat , add chicken
2. stir-fry 5 to 7 minutes , or until done
3. remove chicken , add dressing and orange juice to skillet
4. bring to a boil , add vegetables
5. cook 10 minutes , or until crisp-tender
6. return chicken to pan , toss well
7. serve over cooked rice or noodles sprinkled with peanuts
demonstrations.review: Yumm!! What a great recipe!  Nice to simmer the vegetables in the orange juice sauce rather than more oil.  Great taste!  I added just a smidgeon of chili garlic oil (1/2 tsp.) to give it some heat but it was so awesome. DH loved it. I'm sure we'll be making this again soon. (Used chopped cashews on top as a garnish 'cuz that's what I had.)  Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish steel cut oatmeal

now here's a breakfast that's healthy, low fat  and sodium and cholestrol free. it's also a  great source of fibre which does a body good or should i say great! good health to you all!

1. pour the cinnamon and oats into boiling water until and stir until it begins to thicken
2. lower the heat until it begins to simmer and cook for 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
3. it's important not to overcook the oats so that you get a nice nutty flavour
4. add the remaining ingredients and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  Hearty & Wholesome!  (I halved the recipe and followed Chef #1382175's suggestion to bring to a boil the previous night.  When I awoke and flipped on the burner to low, it didn't take long at all to finish it off.)  Thanks.

target.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
target.review: This will now be my crockpot roast recipe. AWESOME!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker pulled pork

saw on another site; it sounds good and easy with just 3 ingredients!

1. place the pork tenderloin in a slow cooker
2. pour the root beer over the meat
3. cover and cook on low until well cooked and the pork shreds easily , 6 to 7 hours
4. drain well
5. stir in barbecue sauce
6. serve over hamburger buns
demonstrations.review: This is the recipe I always use.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fast  microwaved  pan  fried  potatoes

easy and fast way to make pan fried spuds.

1. wash and cube potato
2. place in microwave and microwave for 4 minutes
3. heat oil and butter over medium high heat
4. add potatoes and fry until crispy
5. add optional seasonings
6. stir to combine
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I just realized I have not reviewed this. We enjoy this shortcut.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy strawberry banana smoothie

this recipe is so easy and delicious! you'll make it in 2 minutes!

1. pour all the ingredients into a blender
2. blend for about 30 seconds or until it's the way you like
3. you may add any vitamin you like to make your smoothie healthy ,
demonstrations.review: Made this in my new ninja, but used more OJ rather than pineapple juice since not on hand

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy baked salmon

this recipe is so delicious, yet it takes less than 5 minutes to prepare.  it's a perfect dinner for a busy night!  for even more flavor, marinate for up to one hour.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees
2. mix together soy sauce , lemon juice , and spices
3. place salmon in a shallow baking dish , and pour liquid mixture over the filets
4. bake about 25 minutes or until salmon is flaky
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed and I liked the easy prep. I think we will cut down the cinnamon next time due to our preference.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave poached egg on toast

this recipe came with my very first microwave 20+ years ago. it makes an easy, quick, no mess breakfast.

1. place the toast on a plate , butter it , flatten the middle down with the back of a fork
2. crack and carefully pour the egg into the flattened middle of the toast , not allowing it to spill over into the plate
3. prick the yolk quickly and carefully with the tines of the fork and bake in the microwave on a turntable for about 1 minute on 60-70% power , until the white is cooked through or desired doneness is achieved
demonstrations.review: Tasty. I did mine in a 1200W microwave for 45 seconds at 60%. Yolk was hard so will try 40s next time.

target.recipe_text:
italian countryside beef soup for the crock pot

i find that i keep collecting more an more mediterranean recipes. italy isn't at the bottom of my list and that's because everything is just so good!  this is no exception and it makes a big batch so you'll have leftovers if you have a smaller family. leftovers are good as they are always better on the second day for lunch. i served with crusty multi-grain rolls and a simple green salad.

1. trim fat from meat , cut meat into 2-inch pieces and set aside
2. in a 4- to 5-quart slow cooker , combine potatoes , carrots or parsnips , onion , and fennel
3. add meat
4. sprinkle with rosemary
5. in a medium bowl , whisk together broth , wine , tomato paste , tapioca , pepper , and garlic
6. pour over mixture in cooker
7. cover and cook on low-heat setting for 8 to 10 hours or on high-heat setting for 4 to 5 hours
8. just before serving , stir in basil
9. makes 6 to 8 servings
target.review: So good! Perfect for Fall. I cut my meat and vegies in big chunks. I used russet potatoes cut into chunks. I added both basil and baby spinach. I added a splash of worcestershire at the end. Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lebanese spiced potatoes  batata harra

similar to the flavourful potatoes you can purchase in lebanese restaurants throughout ottawa, canada. this goes really well with recipe#44858 marinated chicken breast, recipe #409286, and a garlic sauce like, recipe#108234 without the cilantro and a little balkan yogurt to lighten it up, along with, recipe#254171, for a meal like the restaurants only way better! recipe modified from a recipe found on http://homemade-recipes.blogspot.com

1. heat canola oil and fry medium size cubed potatoes until crisp
2. remove onto a paper towel lined plate
3. in another pan heat olive oil and add finely chopped onion , minced garlic , cayenne , ground coriander and finely chopped cilantro , saute then add the potatoes sea salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
4. mix well and add lime juice
5. serve immediately with garlic sauce such as recipe#108234 without the fresh cilantro added
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Very good potatoes!!! I left out the onions, cuz I have an onion hater. I also cubed the potatoes and nuked them in the micro until almost done. Then pan fried.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red cabbage with apple and bacon

found this in taste of home magazine and i think the combination sounds so good i wanted to save it.  they recommended serving with sauerbraten, but i'm thinking it'd go great with pork chops.  haven't tried it yet, but it's going to be on my fall menu plan soon.

1. in dutch oven , cook bacon over medium heat until crisp
2. using a slotted spoon , remove to paper towels to drain
3. in drippings , saute onion and apple until tender
4. stir in the remaining ingredients
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce ehat
7. cover and simmer fo r30 minutes or until tender
8. stir in reserved bacon
demonstrations.review: Loved the red cabbage! I added more sugar than called for, cuz I like mine pretty sweet. Made for ZWT and the Saucy Silervados.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy garlic mayonnaise

this comes from the cuisine of california cookbook and was given to me by --sheri-- in the last cookbook swap.  this is great to kick up any kind of sandwich.  i've also used it on a shrimp and avocado salad.  it may be kept up to 5 days in refrigerator.

1. immerse pimiento or red pepper in a pan of boiling water and boil 2 minutes
2. remove from water with a slotted spoon
3. reserve
4. while motor is running , add garlic cloves to a food processor fitted with the steel blade
5. process until pureed
6. add pimiento or red pepper and process until blended
7. add egg yolks and blend
8. with blades turning , slowly pour in olive oil in a fine steady stream until sauce is thick and smooth and all oil is added
9. add salt , pepper and cayenne
10. taste for seasoning
11. refrigerate in a tightly covered container until ready to use
12. serve cold
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I roasted my bell pepper over the open flame of my stove and diced it up!!! Yummy on a sandwich!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish buttermilk scones   cheese   herb scones

perfect to go with your morning coffee or a great afternoon snack with hot tea. the secret to making good scones is a quick, light hand when mixing, and a hot oven.

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. sift flour with salt and rub in butter or margarine
3. for cheese& herb scones add mustard , cheese and herbs to the dry ingredients at this point
4. make a well in the centre and pour in the egg and most of the buttermilk
5. mix quickly to form a soft dough , adding a little extra buttermilk if necessary
6. turn out onto a floured surface and roll out lightly until 1" thick
7. working quickly , cut into 2" rounds
8. glaze with egg or milk and set on a floured baking sheet
9. before baking , dust scones with cinnamon sugar for buttermilk scones or sprinkle a little grated cheese on top of each scone for cheese& herb scones
10. bake for 15-20 minutes until light brown
demonstrations.review: These were good. I had to add quite a bit more flour and I didn't use all the buttermilk. I did the savory scones and added basil and parmesan cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
african chicken curry

this is an african (mozambique) curry that can be done with chicken, shrimp, or crab. goes well with tomato chutney and onion hot sauce. for shrimp or crab, use 1 pound."  i found it on another site while researching recipes for zwt 2011 the african tour.

1. heat olive oil in a large , heavy skillet over medium heat
2. stir in the onion , garlic , and bay leaf , and saute until onion is lightly browned
3. mix tomatoes , curry powder , and salt into the skillet , and continue cooking about 5 minutes
4. mix in the chicken , and cook 15 to 20 minutes , until no longer pink and juices run clear
5. reduce skillet heat to low
6. stirring constantly , gradually blend in the coconut milk over a period of about 10 minutes
7. mix in lemon juice just before serving
demonstrations.review: Mmmmm. Delicious!!! I left the wings and legs whole, and cut up the thighs and breasts. I partially cooked them a little first. I let this simmer a while, and added a little half and half to thin it back out. Great over some rice! Made for the Saucy Silverados for the ZWT!

target.recipe_text:
soup a l aille

this is the best garlic soup ever.  it's from my much used & loved 'feast of soups' cookbook by jacqueline heriteau.

1. separate the garlic cloves & scald 1 minute
2. slip off & discard skins & scalding water
3. in a kettle over medium heat , combine cold water , garlic , salt , pepper , cloves , parsley , & oil
4. bring to a boil , cover , reduce heat , & simmer 30 minutes
5. remove from heat
6. with a slotted spoon , lift out the cloves , parsley , & garlic
7. discard parsley & cloves
8. puree the garlic with 2c of broth , in a blender or food processor , or press through a sieve
9. in a medium bowl beat the egg yolks until thick
10. whip in the butter , then the garlic puree , then 1c broth
11. whip this mixture into the kettle
12. reheat to just below boiling , but do not boil
13. to serve: place a piece of french bread , toasted & buttered in the bottom of each soup bowl & sprinkle generously with cheese
14. ladle the soup over the bread
15. to make ahead: complete through step 3 , then finish just before serving
target.review: A note, you have actually written "wing soup" here.  To say garlic soup you would write "soupe Ã  l'ail."  No matter what the name, it sounds nice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave english muffin bread

my neighbor makes this all the time and i love it. a neat way to have bread without heating up the oven (too much). cook time includes rise time.

1. combine 3 cups flour , yeast , sugar , salt and soda in large bowl
2. heat milk and water until warm but do not boil
3. add to flour mixture and mix well
4. stir in rest of flour
5. grease 2 glass , 8-inch loaf pans , sprinkle each with cornmeal
6. divide batter into two equal parts and carefully place in pans
7. place pans in large rectangle with water
8. place in oven one warm
9. let rise 35-45 minutes or until dough rises to top of pan
10. place in microwave and bake on high for 6 1 / 2 minutes
11. remove and cool 5 minutes
12. remove from pan and slice
13. wrap in foil and store in freezer
demonstrations.review: This is so easy and so good; why have I not done this before???  Who knew that bread could be so easy and quick?  My roommate and I recommend toasting slices before eating.  The english muffin flavor didn't come through really really strongly but it's certainly a nice, fluffy white bread.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice flour banana bread  wheat free

i always seem to have rice flour on hand (for vietnamese and thai food), and am always looking for ways to use it up. this recipe is from the incomparable beatrice ojakangas' "great whole grain breads" (simon & schuster, 1984,1993). the recipe calls for small loaf pans, probably to reduce the baking time. might be possible to use a large pan, but i haven't tried.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. in a large bowl , beat the butter and sugar until creamy
3. beat in eggs , one at a time
4. stir in buttermilk and lemon extract and mix well
5. combine rice flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt and add to the butter mixture
6. stir in bananas and coconut and mix well
7. spoon the mixture into two greased mini loaf pans
8. bake 50 to 55 minutes , or until a wooden pick inserted into the center of the bread comes out clean
9. cool in pans 2 minutes , then turn out and cool completely
demonstrations.review: we also loved it, the flavor is so good! instead of lemon extract, i used the zest of a half of a lemon.  i tried to counteract the crumbliness by baking at 400 for about 40 minutes.  it kind of worked.  next time i would add more oil to try to get it less crumbly.  this made a beeeaaautiful loaf and i was so pleased to see a gf recipe without one million types of flours and gums!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
all bran banana bread

i made this yesterday from the recipe on the all-bran packet. i just love this banana bread! it has a great taste and is low fat and high fibre! perfect for morning tea or a snack. i like mine with just a little jam or peanut butter spread and served warm.

1. preheat oven to 180 degree c
2. combine dry ingredients and add egg , water , milk and banana
3. mix until well combined
4. spoon into a greased loaf tin
5. bake in oven for 30-45 minutes or until cooked when tested
demonstrations.review: I found this recipe to be ok.  Like ShaGun, I made 12 muffins but i had to bake them for a lot longer than she did, 25 minutes total at 350F. I would add a lot less sugar the next time that i make it; the muffin tops were almost instantly sticky after coming out of the oven.  I used the sticks version of all-bran, maybe that made a difference.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
any muffins recipe

this basic muffin recipe can make hundreds of different types of muffins,just by adding your choice of additions!  easy to memorize, you too can be called "the muffin queen" by your friends like i am!  comes from "the tightwad gazette."

1. heat oven to 400
2. grease 12 muffin cups , or 24 mini muffin cups
3. combine dry ingredients , including dry additions and spices
4. combine wet ingredients , including wet additions
5. spoon batter into muffin cups , filling about 2 / 3 full
6. bake for 18-20 minutes
7. to make non-sweet muffins , such as bacon and cheddar , just cut back on the sugar to 1 tablespoon
8. you can make your own "jiffy" corn muffins by substituting 1 / 2 cup corn meal for 1 / 2 cup of the flour , and using 2 tablespoons of sugar
9. substitute peanut butter for the oil to give your muffins a peanutty taste
10. if your additions are very wet then use up to 1 / 2 cup more flour , to equal up to 2 cups total flour
11. play around with this ! it's easy and quick !
demonstrations.review: This was so easy and good and didn't require anything but very basic ingredients.  However, being a student, sometimes I don't even have the most basic ingredients though so I mixed a third of a cup of dry nonfat milk in with my dry ingredients and added water with the wet.  It worked out great.  I also added pumpkin spice, cinnamon and 3 Tbs (ish) of molasses for flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
juneann s chewy bisquick brownies

i came across this on the net while browsing. a quick and easy one bowl dessert, especially great for moms who work, or for those young, up and coming chefs in your family.

1. put all ingredients into one bowl and mix with a hand mixer until blended good
2. the batter will be thick
3. put into 9x13 pan and bake at 350 for 18-25 minutes
demonstrations.review: I'm not sure if this recipe is correct.  I made it as written and came up with a clump rather than a batter.  I added about 1/4 cup of milk to make it a thick batter. Possibly because of my addition, I had to cook it a lot longer (and it was still undercooked).  The taste was good in the end but I don't think that the recipe was any easier than a normal brownie recipe.  It basically omitted only the salt and the leavening agent, two things that are not difficult to measure.

target.recipe_text:
chicken breasts   stuffed

whole chicken breasts stuffed with crab, a delicate flavor with the crab meat adding a delightfully different taste and  texture

1. cut a pocket into each chicken fillet
2. melt butter in a pan , adding the spring onions , cook for 2 minutes stirring
3. add drained crab meat , lemon juice and cream , cook for 1 minute and season
4. allow to cool
5. fill the pockets with the stuffing , heat oil in pan and add the chicken browning until golden
6. place in a greased dish and bake in a moderate oven 180c for 25 - 30 minutes
7. can be served either with salads , or new potatoes , fresh vegetables and a sauce of your choice
target.review: Sounds really good thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zippy stir fried baby bok choy

easy to make, this side dish adds a colorful green vegetable to a meal and is a bit spicy and tangy.  my dh loves it. if you choose to substitute fresh garlic and/or gingerroot, cook them in the hot oil before adding the cabbage.  this side dish goes well with most asian-spiced meats and poulty.  fried garlic (in jars) can be found at most asian grocers, and imparts a bit of a roasted flavor to this dish.

1. mix well first seven seasoning ingredients in small glass dish
2. set aside
3. heat oil in wok or large skillet over medium-high setting
4. add cabbage and stir fry until done but not soggy
5. reduce heat to low , stir in seasoning mix well , and cover
6. allow flavors to meld for 1-2 minutes
7. optional: add sesame seeds or cashews before serving
demonstrations.review: Will definately try this , thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green beans in dill walnut sauce

serve at room temperature or chill for wonderful picnic fare.

1. heat a large pot of water to boiling
2. add the green beans and cook until crisp-tender
3. drain immediately , then immerse in a large bowl of ice water to prevent further cooking and to retain the bright green color
4. meanwhile , make the sauce: place the scallions , dill , parsley , walnuts , and lemon juice in a blender or food processor fitted with the steel blade
5. process until smooth
6. with the machine running , pour the olive oil in a t hin , steady stream through the feed tube to make a thick green sauce
7. add salt and pepper to taste
8. drain the beans and dry wit h a towel
9. toss the beans with the dressing
10. serve slightly chilled or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: sounds good thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced lentils

this is really yummy. it can be used as a stuffing for mini pumpkins or tomatoes. i served it over some plain brown rice with mango chutney. it does make lots of leftovers and is pretty good cold the next day.

1. in a large saucepan , heat oil
2. add onions and garlic and cook until golden
3. stir in tomatoes , sugar , and spices
4. add lentils and broth
5. cover and cook until lentils are tender
6. drain if needed
7. season with salt , pepper and cayenne
demonstrations.review: sounds really good thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato corn salsa

this is a great salsa! cutting the veggies small makes it easier to get more salsa on your chip. the flavors need to mingle before serving, so let sit overnight. serve with salty tortilla chips. this would be good as a baked potato topping.

1. blanch and drain the corn
2. in a large bowl , combine all of the ingredients and set aside for the flavors to blend
3. serve at room temperature
demonstrations.review: made this with Trader Joes frozen roasted corn, excellent! Thank you! Easy too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick sesame chicken

i picked this up from "cook right 4 your type," which i picked up for only 25 cents. i haven't tried this, but it sounds too good and simple to be true.

1. put chicken in baking dish
2. sprinkle soy sauce on each piece
3. rub crushed garlic on each piece
4. sprinkle seeds over the top of the chicken
5. bake at 375f for 50 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: Sounds  great and easy too, thanks!

target.recipe_text:
sausage and potato soup

i just tried this recipe as a new meal tonight and it will definately be a keeper.
i got it out of a " taste of home quick cooking" book.
was easy to make and big on taste! 
i tweeked it just a bit but the end results are still the same.

1. brown sausage in a skillet
2. drain and set aside
3. in large stock pot , add begetables , seasonings , and broth
4. bring to a boil and simmer till soft
5. add sausage , milk , and cheese
6. cook on low heat setting till hot
7. serve with crusty bread
target.review: have made this at least 1/2 dozen times and everytime we LOVE it!! Really satisfying and filling on its on, but with a loaf of hot, crunchy french bread, its then supreme!! The key is to really brown up the kielbasa. It adds the flavor that it needs. Great recipe, thanks for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
avocado  feta and pancetta bruschetta

bruschetta derives from the italian 'bruscare' meaning "to roast over coals”.  at its most authentic, italian country-style bread is toasted over coals, rubbed with garlic and seasoned while hot with sea salt and fruity, virgin, cold-pressed olive oil. more commonly in english-speaking countries, the toasted garlic bread is topped with tomatoes and summery herbs. this version, without tomato, is a little different and is perfect for a casual lunch for 2 people, or as an appetiser for 4 people.

1. prepare all ingredients just before planning to eat
2. in a medium sized bowl combine the feta cheese , avocado , rocket , basil , pine nuts and 2 tablespoons olive oil
3. add an extra tablespoon of olive oil to further moisten this mixture if preferred
4. saute the bacon or pancetta in a little oil until crisp , then chop finely and add to the feta cheese / avocado mixture
5. set topping mixture aside while preparing the bread
6. toast the bread over hot coals , on the bbq or under the oven grill / broiler , until crusty and golden brown on the outside , but warm and soft inside
7. keep an eye on it as it can suddenly burn !
8. while the toast is still piping hot , rub one side of each slice with the cut side of a garlic clove , then quickly brush each slice with a tablespoon of olive oil
9. spoon the topping mixture on to the toasted bread , and season with freshly cracked black pepper - depending on the saltiness of the feta and bacon you use , you probably won't need to season with salt
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Loved it!! All said and done i prob doubled the pine nuts and pancetta but that only added to the goodness that filled my mouth!! That said it was a little salty but I'm sure that was due to the whopping amount of pancetta! Would for sure make again. My avocado was super ripe so it didn't really stay in the small chunk form, it was more mashed but that made it all the more spreadable on my toasted baguette. thanks!! gonna eat it again for lunch today, can't wait!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish kielbasa chowder

this yummy chowder will really fill your family up!  serve it with a big loaf of bread and you'll be in heaven!

1. heat the oil in a large dutch oven over medium-high heat
2. add the garlic and kielbasa and brown them well , turning often
3. add the next three ingredients to the cooking pot and bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for for 20 minutes
5. add cabbage and cook for 10 minutes or until tender
6. whisk the flour and milk together and add to to soup
7. simmer for 10 minutes , stirring often
8. add cheese and cook , stirring until cheese is melted and soup is heated through
demonstrations.review: made it for new years and it was super delish! cheated and threw potatoes and cabbage in food processor and chopped fine. Also used 2 cups 1/2 & 1/2 and 1 cup heavy cream ( bad girl!) but i have tons leftover from the holidays and i needed to use it. Just finished the last bowl today for lunch. Would def make again! thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
benihana japanese fried rice

source: www.topsecretrecipes.com

1. cook rice following instructions on package
2. pour rice into a large bowl to let it cool in the refrigerator
3. scramble the eggs in a small pan over medium heat
4. separate the scrambled chunks of egg into small pea-size bits while cooking
5. when rice has cooled to near room temperature , add peas , grated carrot , scrambled egg and diced onion to the bowl
6. carefully toss all of the ingredients together
7. melt butter in a large frying pan over medium / high heat
8. when butter has completely melted , dump the bowl of rice and other ingredients into the pan and add soy sauce plus a dash of salt and pepper
9. cook rice for 6-8 minutes over heat , stirring often
demonstrations.review: I have made this several times and LOVE it!! the whole family does too. Whenever i make rice i always double the amount purposely so i can make this. Super easy and so delish. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked ham and cheese omelet roll

this is an easy way to serve omelets. in our house, it takes me forever to make breakfast on the stove top! baking this is soooo much easier. feel free to add or subtract to suit your tastes (bacon, sausage, onions, peppers, etc.)

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. beat eggs and milk until fluffy
3. add flour , salt and pepper and beat or whisk until smooth
4. pour into a buttered or greased 9 x 13 baking dish or pan
5. bake for 10 - 15 minutes or until eggs are just about set
6. sprinkle with chopped ham or lay slices of ham evenly on top
7. sprinkle with cheese
8. bake for about 5 minutes more or until cheese is melted
9. starting at short side , roll up omelet while still in pan
10. place seam side down on serving dish
11. cut into slices
demonstrations.review: Soo good! I followed it exactly and used deli ham slices and colby jack slices and my husband and i gobbled it all down for lunch. We covered it in Trader Joes salsa and it was devine!! It didn't want to roll very easily so we just kind of flopped both sides towards the middle. Super for any meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrots lyonnaise

a change from potatoes lyonnaise and colorful, to boot!  don't skimp on the onions.

1. pare carrots & cut into julienne strips
2. dissolve bouillon cube in 1 / 2 c boiling water
3. cook carrots covered in bouillon 10 minutes
4. melt 1 / 4 c butter in large skillet
5. add 3 medium onions , sliced , and cook covered 15 minutes , stirring occationally
6. stir in flour , salt , pepper , and 3 / 4 c water
7. bring to a boil
8. add carrots with liquid
9. simmer , uncovered , 10 minutes
10. add pinch of sugar
demonstrations.review: I really surprisingly enjoyed this! I ended up eating the bulk of it since my family didn't concur with my opinion. Hubs just doesn't enjoy cooked carrots no matter how i prepare them i guess. I could've eaten them alone as my entire meal. Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
nutmeg log cookies

i received these as part of a christmas bake exchange. the person who brought these said they are her most favourite christmas treat. i am glad she decided to share  the recipe :)

1. cream together first 3 ingredients and then slowly add sugar
2. blend in egg
3. add flour and nutmeg gradually and mix well
4. shape dough on lightly floured surface into long longs 1 / 2 inch in diameter
5. cut into 2 inch lengths
6. bake at 350 degrees for 12- 15 minutes or until golden
7. drizzle with melted chocolate
8. these freeze very well
target.review: Very easy and very good! I also used them for a cookie exchange, the quantity was perfect. TFS

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot apple butter

this is just one of my comfort foods. i love it slathered on homemade biscuits. mmmmmmmm...so good.

1. place apples in a large bowl
2. combine sugar , cinnamon , cloves and salt
3. pour over apples and mix well
4. place in crock pot , cover and cook on high for 1 hour
5. decrease heat to low
6. cover and cook on low for 9-11 hours or until thickened and dark brown
7. stir occasionally
8. uncover and cook on low for 1 hour longer
9. if desired , whisk until smooth
10. spoon into freezer containers , leaving 1 / 2-inch head space
11. cover and freeze
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe! I would try a bit less sugar next time, though. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wholesome homemade honey whole wheat bread

this is the most awesome wheat bread i have ever eaten. it is worth the extra effort and because this recipe makes 4 loaves, you can freeze them and have enough for awhile :) rising time included in prep.

1. dissolve yeast in warm water
2. in a large bowl , combine butter , molasses , honey and salt and mix well
3. add yeast mixture and then gradually add flours
4. turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth
5. place in buttered bowl and let rise until double
6. punch down and let rest for a few minutes
7. divide dough into 4 parts and shape into loaves
8. place in greased pans and let rise for about an hour
9. bake at 375 for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I love this recipe, I have made it several times. I love that it makes 4 loaves! I have always found that I need to add alot more flour.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili maple glazed dump chicken oamc

i love dump recipes and this one is an easy 4 ingredient one!

1. for immediate cooking: pre-heat oven to 350f place all ingredients into a large baking dish , turn chicken to coat
2. bake until chicken juices run clear
3. for freezing: place all ingredients into a 1 gallon freezer bag
4. lay flat in freezer
5. to thaw and cook: take the bag out of the freezer the night before , make sure the bag is sealed completely
6. for the oven: preheat the oven to 350f empty the contents of the bag into a large baking dish and bake until the juices run clear
7. for the crockpot: cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 4-6 or until done
8. on the grill: cook over medium heat until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Loved this! Did not use salt, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy bisquick chicken pot pie

this is so good and easy to make.  the recipe came from the back of the bisquick mix package.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees fahrenheit
2. bottom crust:
3. cut 2 tablespoons butter into 1 cup bisquick baking mix until mixture resembles fine crumbs
4. stir in 2 tablespoons milk until mixture begins to form a ball and cleans side of bowl
5. pat dough on bottom and up to rim of an ungreased pie plate
6. bake for 5 minutes
7. heat remaining butter in 2 quart saucepan until melted
8. stir in 1 / 4 cup bisquick baking mix , onion and pepper
9. cook , stirring constantly until mixture is bubbly , remove from heat
10. stir in chicken broth
11. add vegetables
12. heat to boiling , stirring constantly
13. boil and stir 1 minute
14. stir in chicken
15. heat through
16. pour chicken mixture into bottom crust
17. mix remaining ingredients until smooth
18. pour evenly over chicken mixture , spread gently to edge
19. bake 25 minutes or until golden brown
20. let stand 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Very easy and very good. We really liked the flavour as is, but it would be great with some extra spice as well! I had to double as it didn't seem like it would serve 6, after doubling we had about a third left (with 2 adults and 2 kids). Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken thighs with lime and honey  oamc

adapted from "entertaining on ice" by t. hayward. if not making for oamc, this recipe can be cooked after letting chicken marinade for at least 5 hours or overnight.

1. combine lime juice , lime zest , honey , ginger , and garlic in a large ziploc bag
2. add chicken and combine well
3. squeeze out as much air as possible and freeze
4. remove from freezer the night before serving and defrost all day in the fridge
5. chicken will marinate as it defrosts
6. transfer thighs to a roasting pan and bake at 350 for 25-30 minutes , or until chicken is cooked through
7. you can also cook this chicken on the bbq / grill if desired
demonstrations.review: Great! I would use slightly less ginger next time, but my husband and I loved it!

target.recipe_text:
copycat  green giant niblets corn in butter sauce

i had to come up with this quick. every thanksgiving my mom serves green giant niblets corn in butter sauce and i promised i would pick it up for her and bring it on thanksgiving day. when i went to the store, they were sold out! i made this recipe and brought it already prepared to thanksgiving dinner. nobody was the wiser! i saved some money too, because i used store brand corn! this recipe makes a lot...you may want to half it.

1. add corn to large sauce pan along with all ingredients except water and cornstarch
2. stir corn mixture over medium heat until butter is melted
3. combine water and cornstarch and stir until cornstarch is disolved
4. slowly add water to corn in sauce pan , stirring constantly
5. reduce heat to simmer and stir until sauce thickens
6. let simmer , stirring occasionally , until corn is tender , about 10 minutes
target.review: I am too cheap to have ever purchased the real one, but we tried b/c of all the rave reviews.  VERY very good.  This dish and the mashed potatoes was the only thing my picky 5 yo DS ate at Christmas dinner.  Ha.  This will be the way I make corn from now on.  Also, I used two cans of Green Giant Sweet Whole Kernel Corn instead of frozen.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mock skor bars

taste just like skor bars. these are great and very addictive.

1. preheat ove to 350
2. line a 13 x9 inch pan with parchment paper for easy clean up
3. arrange crackers evenly in pan
4. in saucepan over medium heat melt butter
5. stir in brown sugar until melted and smooth
6. bring mixture to a boil stirring constantly until mixture is smooth and bubbly
7. boil for 2 minutes and then pour mixture evenly over cracker
8. bake in oven for 5 minutes
9. sprinkle chocolate pieces evenly over caramel mixture
10. return to oven just long enough for chocolate to melt
11. spread chocolate evenly with spatula
12. place pan in refrigerator or freezer until chocolate is firm
13. cut or break into pieces
14. cooking time is cooling time
demonstrations.review: Good.  I think I messed up the caramel layer b/c it was pretty grainy, but it was still out of this world.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese ball with everything

this savory variation belongs in every serious cook's repertoire. serve these to a crowd you want to impress! caution..this makes alot, the two small balls are as big as baseballs! i have been making these for years from a recipe i clipped from a magazine and they are always a hit. cook time is chill time.

1. let swiss and cheddar cheeses come to room temperature
2. in a large bowl beat together cream cheese and sour cream till fluffy
3. beat in swiss cheese , cheddar cheese , onion , undrained pimiento , pickle relish , half of the bacon , 1 / 4 cup of the pecans , salt and pepper
4. cover and chill till firm
5. shape into 1 large or 2 small balls on wax paper
6. in a small bowl combine remaining bacon , pecans , parsley , and poppy seeds
7. turn mixture out onto clean clean sheet of waxed paper
8. roll cheese balls in seed mixture to coat
9. wrap and chill
10. let stand 30 minutes at room temperature before serving
11. serve with crackers
demonstrations.review: Made it exactly like the recipe states and it was fabulous!  It is my stand-by cheese ball recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese delight

this recipe came from one of my clients, when i dropped over on a chilly winter morning, and i smelled it throughout her lovely home. yum!

1. grease 9x13 pan
2. preheat oven to 350f
3. spread one can of crescent dough on bottom of pan
4. mix softened cream cheese , 1 cup of sugar and vanilla until smooth , and spread on top of crescent dough
5. spread 2nd can of dough on top of cheese mixture
6. be careful not to leave too many gaps in dough
7. pour melted butter all over crescent dough
8. mix 1 / 2 cup sugar with 1 teaspoons of cinnamon
9. sprinkle on top of butter
10. use all of it--it looks like a lot , but it's just right
11. bake for 30 minutes
12. allow to cool before cutting
13. serve with coffee , milk or ice cream !
demonstrations.review: OMG!  This is to-die-for!  My DH ate half the pan all by himself.  I only had one roll of crescents so I halved the recipe and stuck it in an 8 X 8 square glass pan and they came out perfect!  Crispy and crusty and totally yum.  This is going in my keeper file!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot lemonade with rum

a delicious hot beverage that is perfect in cold weather and for holiday entertaining. also a wonderful drink if you are feeling a bit under the weather as well! tastes especially good with ginger-bread cookies! be sure to spike it with high-quality dark rum. this version can also be chilled. recipe adapted from suzanne lombardi from star cookies.

1. in a medium saucepan combine water , lemon juice and sugar and simmer over low heat , stirring frequently , until sugar dissolves
2. stir in the rum
3. pour into warm mugs , garnish with lemon slices & candy swizzle sticks
demonstrations.review: Made this for my sick little DS.  He wouldn't touch it, so I sipped on it - for the next three nights.  Kept just fine in the fridge and warmed up in the microwave.  I am going to make another batch.  Great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chi chi s seafood enchilada   copycat

supposedly this is the same as chi chi's "cancun"

1. in mixing bowl , stir together soup , onion , nutmeg and black pepper
2. in another bowl , place half of the soup mixture , crab and 1 cup of the jack cheese
3. set aside
4. wrap the tortillas in paper towels , microwave on 100 percent power for 30 to 60 seconds
