5. place 1 / 3 cup mixture on each tortilla and roll up
6. place seam side down in greased 12 x 7-1 / 2 dish
7. stir milk into the reserved soup mixture , pour over enchiladas
8. microwave , covered , on high for 12 to 14 minutes
9. sprinkle with remaining cheese
10. let stand for 10 minutes
11. add a dash of hot pepper sauce to soup mix if desired
demonstrations.review: Well, I had flashbacks.  They tasted so much like the original.  The only thing that I would do differently would be to saute the onions in butter before I added them.  Even though I am an onion lover and I liked the taste, I don't remember that in the ones I ate at the restaurant.  They are very very very rich.  My kids only ate a bite or two, but I thought they were delicious.  I used Cream of Shrimp and added a dash of dry sherry as the reviewers recommended.

target.recipe_text:
tennessee banana black walnut cake with caramel frosting

this is a very good moist cake, with a yummy icing. you can substitute english walnuts for black walnuts*. the recipe is courtesy of paula deen

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour 2 cake pans
3. for the cake: in a medium bowl , stir together flour and baking soda
4. set aside
5. using an electric mixer , cream together shortening and sugar in a bowl until light and fluffy , about 2 to 3 minutes
6. add eggs 1 at a time , mixing well after each addition
7. mix in mashed bananas , buttermilk , and vanilla
8. add flour mixture and mix until just combined
9. stir in walnuts
10. pour into prepared pans , bake until a toothpick inserted comes out clean , about 35 minutes
11. cool in pans on a cooling rack , remove from pans and cool completely
12. while cake is baking , prepare frosting
13. melt butter in a small saucepan
14. add brown sugar and 1 / 3 cup cream
15. cook over medium-low heat until sugar is dissolved , about 2 minutes
16. remove from heat and add vanilla
17. transfer to a large bowl
18. using a hand mixer , beat in confectioners sugar a little at a time until smooth
19. sandwich 2 layers of cake with frosting
20. frost outside of the cake
21. press chopped walnuts on sides of cake , if desired
target.review: I have Paulas' book and have tried this cake.. the cake is rich and dense..but I was not fond of the icing...she does say in the book NOT to substitute English walnuts.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon garlic chicken and potatoes

found this in todays parent. so simple and so good!

1. pour about half of the olive oil into a large skillet or dutch oven and place over high heat
2. add the chicken breast chunks , sprinkle with some of the salt and pepper and cook quickly until slightly browned
3. remove chicken from pan , leaving as much oil as possible
4. pour the rest of the olive oil into the pan and return to high heat
5. add the potatoes , carrots , garlic and oregano and cook , stirring , for 2 to 3 minutes
6. now add the chicken broth , lemon juice and sprinkle in the flour , stirring until blended
7. bring the mixture to a boil , then cover the pan and lower the heat to medium
8. add the browned chicken chunks , adjust the seasoning with more salt and pepper , if necessary and continue to cook , covered , for 7-10 minutes , stirring occasionally , until the potatoes are tender
demonstrations.review: Very good!!  Easy and quick to prepare.  I used a bit more chicken broth and a combination of chicken breast and boneless thighs..I will make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornmeal and cumin pork loin

a nice crunchy crust on a moist tender roast.

1. season pork with salt and pepper
2. mix cornmeal and cumin together
3. turn pork in this mixture to coat
4. heat oil in a skillet til hot but not smoking
5. brown pork , turning , about 3 minutes
6. transfer pork to a roasting pan
7. roast at 350f for 25 to 30 minutes until internal temperature registers 155f
8. let stand 10 minutes loosely covered
9. slice and serve
demonstrations.review: This recipe was not only very easy to prepare but delicious as well....it was crusty on the outside and moist and juicy on the inside. Not at all spicy..cumin does not have a spicy flavor..very pleasantly seasoned ...will absolutely make this again!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
applesauce cake

this recipe came from king arthur flour, its wonderful, the molasses really add to the rich flavor.

1. in a mixing bowl , beat together the oil , eggs , molasses and applesauce till smooth
2. add the flour , sugar , salt , baking powder , soda , cinnamon and nutmeg
3. beat till smooth
4. pour batter into a lightly greased and floured 9x13 in baking pan
5. place cake in a preheated 375 degree oven
6. bake for 25 minutes or until it tests done
7. remove and cool completely ona wire rack
8. just before serving dust with powdered sugar
demonstrations.review: Easy...delicious. I decreased the oil to 1/4 cup and increased the applesauce to 1 1/4 cups..may omit the oil completely next time and use 1 1/2 cups applesauce...but WILL make it again...thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mostaccioli broccoli bake

a tasty little side dish you could serve with chicken, fish or whatever you like. from the loma linda dental auxiliary cookbook.

1. cook mostaccioli according to package directions
2. drain and rinse in cold water
3. in a medium saucepan , melt margarine
4. stir in flour until blended
5. add milk
6. cook until thickened , stirring constantly
7. stir in parmesan cheese , salt , garlic powder , thyme and nutmeg
8. in a large bowl , combine mostaccioli , cheese sauce and broccoli
9. spoon into 12" by 9" baking dish
10. sprinkle swiss cheese over top
11. bake at 375 degrees for 10- 15 minutes until heated through
demonstrations.review: This was very good..the sauce was nicely seasoned..it was easy to make..the one thing I found was that it was just a bit dry for my taste..next time I'll start with 3 cups of milk and adjust the seasonings accordingly and I think that will make it perfect...Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave crumb potatoes

these are the easiest potatoes ever and they taste great.  nothing is better than an easy recipe that gets rave reviews

1. combine crumbs and cheese , if using
2. roll potatoes in butter , then crumbs
3. arrange in 9" square microwaveable baking dish
4. cover with plastic wrap and cook on high 7-8 minute
5. let stand 5 minute
demonstrations.review: These were easy but very bland. If I make them again I will make changes to the recipe.  Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
slow cooker 4th of july chuck roast barbecue sandwiches

i made this for the 4th and it was an easy dinner to put together while my family was able to spend some time together. it doesn't have to be cooked just for the 4th of july.

1. place roast in a 3 1 / 2 or 4 quart electric slow cooker
2. add onion
3. combine cola and next 7 ingredients
4. cover and chill 1 cup sauce
5. pour remaining sauce over raost
6. cover with lid
7. cook on high for 1 hour
8. reduce heat to low
9. cook 8 hours or until roast is very tender
10. if time doesn't permit , you can omit cooking it on high for 1 hour
11. just add two hours to the low cooking time
12. remove roast with chopped onion from cooker using a slotted spoon and shred meat with 2 forks
13. combine reserved sauce , ketchup and butter in a saucepan
14. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until thoroughly heated
15. pour sauce over shredded meat , stirring gently
16. spoon meat mixture on buns
target.review: This was really good!  It fed a large group of hungry people with even some for left overs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
renshaw dip

i fell in love with this dip 7 years ago when i had it at a work function. it was made by my supervisor, julie renshaw and had been dubbed simply 

1. mix it up and keep it in the frig for as long as you want before the party
2. a couple of days will get it really hot !
3. serve with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: This dip was "ok" - I guess I was expecting more bang for my buck.  It was tasty - but fell a little flat for me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic chicken for crock pot

i got a similar recipe of this a long time ago, got bored with it back then, and changed some ingredients. my husband and daughter get so excited when we're gonna have this for dinner. i don't measure some things, so if you need me to explain further, let me know. the liquid is so good that i keep sipping it! ha!

1. put the first 7 ingredients in a crock pot and cook for 4-5 hours on low
2. cook the rice or pasta separately
3. when chicken is done , remove the bones and skin and throw them away
4. put either rice or pasta in a bowl and then ladle the balsamic chicken on top with some of the liquid from the crock pot
demonstrations.review: Thought it was way too sweet. We couldnt even eat it and ended up ordering pizza.  :(

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review:
I have never been a fan of meatloaf, I guess one of those things that I was made to eat as a kid and just ended up with a bad taste in my mouth for it....lol
I tried this recipe on a whim for my husband and I actually liked it!  It was very moist and filling.  And set up well enough for my husband to be able to make meatloaf sammiches with as.  Thanks for posting a cool recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peachy crock pot pork chops

quick, easy and tasteful way to make pork chops in your crockpot!

1. place browned pork chops in crock pot
2. season with salt and pepper
3. place peaches on top of pork chops
4. mix brown sugar , cinnamon , tomato sauce , syrup and vinegar
5. pour over pork chops and peaches
6. cook on low for 4-6 hours
demonstrations.review: Oh My God, this was AWFUL!!!  There was something about tomato sauce and peaches?  I let it cook for the alotted time and did not tweak the reciepe at all, and we didnt even bother to put it on our plates.  One taste of it out of the crock pot and we threw it away and ordered pizza!  Now Im a pretty experienced cook and I love to try something new but this is NOT the thing for a newbie with a crock pot - it would sour them from using their crock ever again!  SORRY!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kfc and kentucky fried chicken biscuits

this is the kfc biscuit recipe from the website, they are wonderful.

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. sift together flour , salt , sugar and baking powder into mixing bowl
3. make a well in the flour mix and add the milk
4. add shortening and begin kneading with hands the vegetable shortening and flour in the milk until thoroughly mixed
5. add milk , if needed to form , and mix
6. turn onto floured board , and knead gently 6 to 8 times
7. pat dough to 1 / 2-inch thickness
8. cut into biscuits
9. place on baking sheet and brown in oven 10-13 minutes
10. makes about 9 biscuits
demonstrations.review:
I was so excited to try this biscuit recipe!  When they came out of the oven, I could barely wait for them to cool, and when I popped a bit in my mouth...all I tasted was SALT!!  There is way too much in the dough.
I threw them out and made another batch just to be sure that I didnt do something incorrectly..and again the salt was so overwhelming that I threw them away.  3rd time's the charm,  cut the salt to 1/2 teaspoon and they came out moist and delicious.....  I recommended fixing the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
streusel topped banana nut muffins

this is the best way to use your over ripe bananas. these are especially good because of the crunchy brown sugar streusel on top. a regular in my house.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. prepare a 12 cup muffin pan with paper muffin cups
3. in a bowl combine the brown sugar , 1 / 4 cup of the flour , oats , melted butter , and 1 / 2 tsp of the cinnamon , mix and press together with a fork until it looks crumbly , and set aside
4. in another mixing bowl , combine the remaining 1 1 / 2 c flour , baking powder , baking soda , 1 / 4 tsp cinnamon , and 1 / 8 tsp salt
5. set aside
6. in another bowl combine the egg , mashed bananas , sugar , and oil , mix well then add to the flour mixture
7. stir until just moistened , fold in the walnuts
8. spoon batter into each muffin cup , about 2 / 3 full each
9. top each batter filled cup with the streusel topping , enough to cover so you cant see the batter
10. bake at 350 degrees 20-25 min , or until toothpick test comes out clean
target.review: What to do with ripe bananas?  Make these muffins, of course.  These were fantastic.  The taste, texture, and crumb topping make them worthy of comparison with any boutique bakery muffin.  I added some chopped walnuts to the crumb topping.  Yum!!!  I'm going to try jumbo muffins next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
korean sirloin

a tasty korean style steak.
prep time does not include marinade time.

1. stir together in a small bowl soy sauce , ginger , brown sugar , sesame oil , cayenne and garlic
2. pour marinade into a large ziploc bag , then add steak and turn to coat
3. refrigerate for 1 to 4 hours turning bag several times
4. heat a ridged grill pan over medium-high heat until very hot
5. remove the steak from the bag , pour the marinade into a 1-quart saucepan and reserve
6. pat the steak dry with paper towel and cook for 6 to 8 minutes per side for a medium rare steak
7. remove steak to a cutting board and let stand for 10 minutes
8. add 2 tbsp of water to the marinade in the saucepan and heat to boiling over high heat , boil for 2 minutes
9. slice steak into thin strips diagonally against the grain
10. serve with the cooked marinade
demonstrations.review: This was a big hit at our house.  I didn't have cayenne pepper so I added a small amount of crushed red pepper flakes.  It just melted in our mouths and will be made again and again.  I served it with Jasmine rice, stir-fried broccoli, and an Asian inspired tossed salad.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken scallops with spinach and blue cheese

wilted fresh spinach with a little olive oil has lots of flavor to complement the blue cheese and pine nuts. most of the work can be done ahead of time and the dish completed in the oven just before serving.

1. preheat the oven to 400f
2. pour half the olive oil into a very large frying pan to film the bottom
3. over low heat , gradually add the spinach by handfuls , cover , and stir from time to time as it cooks down
4. when all the spinach is barely wilted , put it in a sieve and press out most of the moisture
5. spread the spinach in a wide , shallow ovenproof dish and set aside
6. salt and pepper the chicken cutlets on both sides
7. add the remaining oil to the pan and over medium-high heat saute the chicken , turning to color it golden on both sides
8. when the chicken is done , lay the cutlets on the spinach
9. in a small bowl , mix together the pine nuts and blue cheese
10. scatter this mixture over the chicken
11. bake the chicken until the cheese is melted and bubbling and the chicken and spinach are piping hot , about 15 minutes
12. serve at once
demonstrations.review: My husband and I just loved this.  It was easy to adjust ingredients to serve two.  I didn't have pine nuts so I used slivered almonds.  I also sauteed some sliced mushrooms and garlic and added that to the cooked spinach.  I will make this again.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
avocado and mandarin orange salad

given to me by a society matron who used this as her "presentation salad" at luncheons.  i recommend cutting back on the oil a bit.

1. make dressing: combine vinegar , oil , orange juice , mustard , orange peel , lemon juice , sugar , and salt
2. drain mandarin oranges
3. slice onions into very thin slices
4. combine mandarin oranges , sliced avocados and onion rings
5. cover orange / avocado / onion mixture with dressing and refrigerate
6. immediately before serving , break up lettuce and spoon orange / avocado mixture over lettuce
demonstrations.review: Wonderful, light, refreshing salad.  I will make this again. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gulliver s creamed corn

gulliver's is an old world english resturant located in the heart of orange county, california. they are best known for their prime rib, creamed corn and spinach souffle

1. combine all ingredients except last two in a pot and bring to a boil
2. simmer 5 minutes
3. blend butter with flour
4. add to the corn
5. mix well and remove from heat
6. variation:
7. put finished corn in heat proof casserole , sprinkle with parmesan cheese and place under a broiler until evenly brown
demonstrations.review: This is one of my husband's favorites that we serve whenever we cook a prime rib roast.  Back in the 1980's we used to dine at one of their restaurants near the San Francisco Airport, but it may be closed now.  Funny thing, I had an entire dinner dumped down my back one evening.  They were very gracious about it.  Anyway, I'm making it again on Christmas Day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fast fixin  chocolate chip cake

this is an easy little recipe that i found that can also be used as a cherry cake, just sub 1 20 oz. can of cherry pie filling for the chocolate pudding and chips. also, if you want the cherry kind, use only 1/2 cup of water as the cherry filling will be liquid enough for the recipe.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. pour oil into a 13x9x2 inches pan
3. tilt the pan to cover the bottom with oil
4. put remaining ingredients into pan and stir with a fork or spoon until blended
5. scrape sides and spread batter evenly in pan
6. bake at 350 for 35-45 minutes until toothpick inserted near center comes out clean
7. cooled cake may be sprinkled with powdered sugar
8. use a knife to loosen cake from sides
9. cut and serve directly from pan
10. store leftover cake loosely covered
demonstrations.review: I've been making this for almost 30 years using a Duncan Hines recipe torn from a magazine.  I think that any brand of cake mix is interchangeable in this recipe.  It's always a big hit at pot-lucks.

target.recipe_text:
red wine crock pot roast

yes, another roast recipe, but so very good!!! try it!

1. place roast in crock pot and season with pepper
2. mix rest of ingredients together and pour over roast
3. cover and cook on low 6-7 hours
4. remove roast to rest on platter
5. turn crock pot to high
6. whisk cornstarch into juices to thicken
7. this makes a wonderfully tasty au jus , or over mashed potatoes
8. enjoy !
9. you can easily make additions to this: garlic , pearl onions , mushrooms etc
target.review: At first we thought this was okay and then we notice the red wine was just was overpowing for this. I will try one more time with adding a can of beef broth to the mix.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot garlic rosemary chicken breast

this is a nice simple way to prepare chicken in the crock pot, but it tastes like you put a lot of work into it!

1. place butter and garlic in microwave-safe bowl and heat until butter is soft
2. blend together
3. roll chicken breasts in garlic-butter mixture and place in crock pot
4. sprinkle chicken breasts with salt , pepper , parsley and rosemary
5. add broth to bowl with remaining garlic-butter , reheat if necessary to allow smooth blending , and add mixture to crock pot
6. cook on low setting for 6 - 8 hours
7. serving size is approximately half a chicken breast and a small amount of sauce
demonstrations.review: Maybe I just did something wrong but these were horrible. I love rosemary so I really thought these would turn out great. However, my husband who loves chicken couldn't even eat these. As for tenderness the chicken was falling apart. It had a great aroma while it was cooking but it had a bad taste to it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jambalaya for the crock pot

try this for your next crock pot adventure. wonderful flavor!

1. cut chicken into 1 inch pieces
2. put all ingredients in crock pot
3. cover
4. cook on low for 8 hours
5. add shrimp the last 20 minutes of cooking
6. stir in rice before serving
demonstrations.review:
This is wonderful. I fixed this for alot of family and everyone wanted the recipe! Thank You!
The only changes was I omitted shrimp and added italian sausage and added a little bit more salt and pepper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review:
My family loves this roast. I have made it many times and can't believe I have not rated this yet!
Only thing I do different is instead of water, I use chicken broth. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy and tender crock pot pork chops

these are the most tender chops i have ever had! i usually cook some apples to go on top of the chops and use the sauce in this recipe to put over rice. i found this recipe in one of my favorite cookbooks 'fix it and forget it.' hope you enjoy!

1. brown chops in oil in skillet
2. transfer to slow cooker
3. discard oil
4. combine then add remaining ingredients to cooker
5. cover
6. cook on low 8-10 hours
7. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: These were so yummy! I don't care for pork chops that much but these may have changed my mind. The only changes I made to the recipe is used green bell pepper instead of green pepper and added some red pepper flakes and a clove of minced garlic. I also didn't brown mine. Thanks for a wonderful and now favorite recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey roasted pork loin

very yummy! we really enjoyed this.

1. preheat the oven to 375
2. season the pork and place in a roasting pan
3. in a separate bowl , mix together the honey , juice , oil and thyme
4. pour over the pork
5. add the broth to the pan
6. bake until internal temperature reaches 150
7. baste frequently
8. strain the pan juices into a saucepan small amount gravy flour
9. reduce until slightly thickened
10. serve over the sliced pork
demonstrations.review: I thought with all the good ratings this would be outstanding. However, maybe I did something wrong but my family did not like this to well. I made exactly as recipe says but it did not have much flavor.

target.recipe_text:
broiled steelhead

i stole this one from a family member, it's super easy to make and so delicious. steelhead is kind of a cross between salmon and trout. this recipe can easily be substituted with salmon, and can be done on the bbq as well be sure to use foil and or a bakesheet. leftovers make great sandwiches!

1. rinse and thouroghly pat dry steelhead or salmon
2. place skin side down on bake sheet that has been foiled and sprinkled with olive oil
3. combine mayo , dill , seasoning , lemon , salt and pepper in a bowl and mix with a wisk
4. spread mixture evenly over the fish
5. pre-heat the broiler
6. place in the oven on the middle rack
7. broil on high and check for doneness after 10 min
8. test the center of the fillet with a fork , fish should flake easily
target.review: I live in steelhead country, and although they are great fun to catch, not many people like to eat them.  Other than smoking them, this is the only way that I'll eat it.  I don't use Old Bay, but either lemon or lime pepper and a bit of garlic.  I think there's something about the mayonnaise(I always use Hellmann's) that takes away the strong fishy taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled parmesan broccoli

this delicious grilled side dish will add nutrition and flavor to any meal. recipe is from light and tasty’s april/may 2005 issue. i love broccoli anyway, and grilling veggies always kicks them up a notch.

1. place broccoli in large bowl
2. combine next four ingredients , drizzle over broccoli , and toss to coat
3. let stand for half an hour
4. spray grill rack before preparing grill for indirect heat
5. toss broccoli again and drain marinade
6. place parmesan in large ziploc bag and shake broccoli , a few pieces at a time , with the cheese to coat
7. grill broccoli , covered , over indirect medium heat for 8-10 minutes on each side or until crisp-tender
demonstrations.review: I've never grilled broccoli before, but this is delicious.  I used a bit less parmesan and added some asiago and garlic.  I used flowerettes and a grill pan with the holes in it.  It was more like an appetizer/finger food than a side dish.  I'll definitely be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect basic white rice

you do not need to be afraid of cooking rice again! lol real rice is so much better for you than instant. so here is a basic recipe that will have you cooking rice like a pro! check out the options too! your friends and family will think you're a star! 

1. in a saucepan with a good fitting lid bring water , salt and optional ingredients if desired to a boil
2. the salt and butter are simply for flavor
3. the vinegar keeps your grains separated and gives you a prettier dish
4. no one will taste the vinegar at all !
5. add rice and stir
6. cover and reduce heat to medium low
7. you will know that your temperature is correct if a little steam is visible leaking from the lid
8. a lot of steam means your heat is too high
9. cook for 20 minutes
10. do not lift lid !
11. the steam that is trapped inside the pan is what allows the rice to cook properly
12. remove from heat and fluff with fork
13. serve !
demonstrations.review: This worked great, even when I quadrupled the recipe.  The tip from  atlfitgirl to remove from heat and let sit covered for 5 minutes really did make it fluffier.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous greek salad

be prepared for the best greek salad on the planet! --- plan ahead the dressing needs at least 2 or more hours to blend the flavors, i sometimes add in 1/4 cup parmesan cheese to the dressing for a more cheesy dressing, all amounts may be adjusted to taste ----  to marinade the salad allow to sit at room temperature before serving, see bottom of instructions --- you will find this and many more of my recipes posted here http://kittencalskitchen.com/2009/04/13/kittens-famous-greek-salad/  ---also see my recipe #359292

1. for the dressing
2. in a processor or use a wire whisk process / whisk the olive oil with lemon juice , 2 teaspoons dried oregano , garlic , dried , basil , red wine vinegar , salt and sugar until smooth
3. season with black pepper
4. chill in fridge for a couple of hours before using to blend flavors
5. place the salad ingredients in a large bowl
6. pour dressing over
7. toss to combine
8. if desired allow the salad to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving , or you can refrigerate for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I made this to accompany Pork Souvlaki #39526.  I followed the instructions to a tee.  It was absolutely delicious!  Everyone especially loved the dressing.  Thanks SO much for such a wonderful recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new red potato salad

we can't wait for those lucious little new red potatoes to be ready in our garden so we can fix this great potato salad!!

1. bring a large pot of water to a boil
2. drop in the new potatoes and reduce to low
3. cover and cook for 20 min , or until potatoes are done
4. dice potatoes into a lg bowl
5. add onion
6. mix all remaining ingredients in sm bowl
7. pour over the potatoes and mix well
8. best if refrigerated for 1-2 hours
demonstrations.review: This was very good.  It's different than my usual potato salad and I wasn't  sure that my DH would like it, however he said it was very good, which is about the best praise he ever gives.  I halved the amount of sugar called for and added a teaspoon of horseradish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast ii

here's the way french toast has been made in my family for at least 4 generations - but until i got into high school, we called it 

1. whisk the eggs till frothy
2. add remaining ingredients , and mix well
3. over medium heat , lightly grease skillet with shortening
4. i use a paper towel , so i can use it repeatedly , with every 2 or 3 pans of french toast
5. dip each slice of bread into the egg mixture , on both sides
6. do this quickly , so as not to completely soak the bread
7. cook in skillet over med / med-high heat for approx 5 min per side
8. you may need to flip more than once to get th e desired golden-brown color
9. serve with butter and powdered sugar , or preserves or syrup
demonstrations.review: This is how I always make French Toast.  Although I do use a pinch of salt and nutmeg and half the amount of cinnamon.  Everyone has always loved it.

target.recipe_text:
black bean and mandarin orange salad

nan

1. drain oranges , reserving 1 / 2 tbsp per serving of the liquid
2. mix well: the reserved liquid , vinegar , oil , mustard , cilantro , cumin , and pepper in a large bowl
3. add oranges , cheese , onions , garlic and beans and toss well
target.review: Outstanding!  We loved this salad, the only problem we had was that I didn't double it!  Will be making this over and over again!  It's gorgeous and tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buffalo chicken soup

wow this is good! tastes just like buffalo chicken/hot wings in a creamy and filling soup! fast and simple too! i am not usually a fan of anything with canned cream soups but when i tried this i just had to have the recipe. there are lots of recipes here on zaar for substitutes for canned cream soup that could be used with great results. i have listed that this makes a gallon, actually it makes just shy of a gallon of soup. from toh with tweaks from mama.

1. stove top: combine all ingredients in a large pot and cook on stove until hot and flavors have blended
2. stir often to dissolve everything and to keep from scorching on the bottom
3. at least 30 minutes
4. crock pot: follow same directions above using crock pot
5. just put everything in , stir well to combine everything and then cook on low for 4 hours
6. adjust hot sauce to your liking and / or serve additional sauce on the side to allow each person to adjust their own bowl
7. garnish with an additional dollop of sour cream , ranch or blue cheese dressing / dip and a celery stick
8. would also be good with some shredded cheese on top
9. if you want to stretch it to feed more try serving it over a scoop of white rice
demonstrations.review:
Fantastic!  This was THE perfect soup to have for dinner on a snowy miserable night!  I used 2 cream of chicken and 1 cream of celery, and I only used 1/8th of a cup of hot sauce, and that was PLENTY for us.  Yes, we have wussy mouths! :o) 
We garnished ours with a dollop of sour cream and a sprinkling of Mexican Blend cheese.  
Thank you for posting this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned sausage and peppers

nan

1. divide oil between 2 large skillets with lids
2. heat over medium heat
3. divide garlic , onion and peppers between skillets and cook , stirring as needed , until onion is translucent , about 5 minutes
4. add sausages , 4 to a skillet , and cook about 4 minutes more until sausages begin to brown
5. add tomatoes , wine , oregano and a pinch of salt to pans
6. cover , bring to simmer for about 25 minutes , until peppers are soft
7. season with salt and pepper
8. serve with crusty bread
demonstrations.review: FANTASTIC!  My husband, who normally just tolerates Italian Sausage, LOVED this!  Acutally, we all did...it's delicious!  I used a sweet Italian sausage coil that I cut into bun sized pieces, and I too used a whole can of crushed tomato.  I can't wait to make this again and again...THANK YOU for sharing this recipe! Mmmmmm....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy oven baked beans and pork chops

this is an easy but really tasty pork chop dish --- purchase the thicker size pork chops or you may use 2-3 larger pork steaks, the thinner chops tend to fall apart when baked as they bake too fast, if desired you can top with shredded cheddar cheese the last 15 minutes of baking, also chopped fresh garlic may be added also to the bean mixture -- this may also be cooked in a crockpot, just brown the chops firstly in a skillet.

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. brown the chops in a frypan on both sides with salt , pepper and garlic powder
3. set aside
4. grease an dutch oven or a oven-proof casserole dish
5. in a bowl mix together the pork and beans , chopped onion , chopped green pepper , bbq sauce , ketchup , brown sugar and cayenne pepper
6. layer half of the bean mixture on the bottom of dutch oven
7. lay the pork chops on top of the bean mixture
8. top with remaining bean mixture
9. bake covered or uncovered for about 1 hour and 15 minutes , or until the chops are tender
10. delicious
demonstrations.review: Really loved this! (Even though my chops turned out dry)  I used boneless, and I think I will try this again with bone-in chops.  Actually my kids (11 &15) threw this together for dinner, and said it was very easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was AMAZING!!!  My family of 4 devoured the whole pan!  It was a perfect meal for a cold winter's night!  Thank you so much for sharing this fantastic recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot cheesy ravioli casserole

i work nights and crock pot recipes are lifesavers. here is another one. update: this recipe is also good frozen then thawed and reheated.

1. spray crock pot with pam
2. in a large skillet heat oil over medium heat , add onion and garlic and cook for 4 minutes stirring occasionally
3. stir in pasta sauce , tomato sauce and italian seasoning
4. place 1 cup of sauce in crock pot
5. add 1 package of the ravioli , top with 1 cup of the cheese
6. top with remaining package of ravioli and 1 cup cheese
7. pour remaining sauce over the top
8. cover and cook on low for 5-6 hours
9. sprinkle with parsley before serving
10. makes 10 servings
11. update
12. for oamc this recipe is good frozen
13. i put them into sealable freezer bags and reheated in bag and all in boiling water
demonstrations.review: Loved this! Easy too. It reminded me of canned ravioli, only 1000 times better! Next time I make it I will try 1/2 beef and 1/2 cheese ravioli. This would be a great pot luck dish as it makes a lot!

target.recipe_text:
roasted cauliflower   16 roasted cloves of garlic

i find it totally amazing, that children and men all  love this recipe!  as for the female of our species we just love this for the flavor and the health benefits it brings our families.
roasted brings out a wonderful sweetness in this dish. the garlic is roasted to a tan color is creamy good. you can just pop them in your mouth. or you can spread them on your florets or fresh bread. just be sure to scoop up some of the rosemary, olive oil and black pepper that may have escaped to the bottom of the dish.
for halloween check out recipe #396674 version of my recipe.

1. mix oil , rosemary , salt , pepper and garlic together
2. toss in cauliflower and place in a large casserole dish in one layer
3. roast in a preheated oven at 450 degrees for 20 minutes
4. give a toss and bake for 10 more minutes
target.review: So tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy bean soup with kale

we've all heard how anti-oxidants fight cancer, save eyesight, and prevent clogged arteries. turns out lutein, a delicious 7 mg dose of which is supplied with each serving of this recipe, is even more beneficial than beta carotene. it delays lung aging and combats arthritis to boot! who knew improving your health could be so quick and easy, and taste so good? try it -- you'll see!
p.s. since i felt this lacked enough elements to chew on, i've been adding canned, sliced carrots (fast, easy & healthy!) for quite a while, and thought i'd update the recipe. also, sometimes i add another can of beans, for the same reason. glad so many of you have been enjoying this. there's a container in my frig right now - yum!

1. in a large pot , heat olive oil
2. add garlic and onion
3. saute until soft and the onion is transparent
4. wash the kale , leaving small droplets of water
5. saute , stirring , until wilted and a lovely emerald green , about 15 minutes
6. add 3 cups of the broth , reserving 1 cup , 2 cups of the beans , reserving 1 cup , all of the carrots , tomatoes , herbs , salt and pepper
7. simmer 5 minutes
8. in a blender or food processor , mix the reserved beans and broth until smooth
9. stir into the soup to thicken it nicely
10. simmer 15 more minutes
11. ladle into bowls
12. sprinkle with chopped parsley and shredded parmesan
13. serve with a nice loaf of crusty bread to soak up all the yummy broth !
14. for vegetarian use the vegetable broth
demonstrations.review: This soup is so great!  It taste wonderful, it is good for your body, and it keeps you warm on a winter day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot swedish cabbage rolls  the best

my husband has tried many different recipes for cabbage rolls and swears these are the best he has ever had.

1. immerse cabbage leaves in large kettle of boiling water for about 3 minutes or until limp
2. drain
3. combine egg , 1 / 4 cup of sauce , onion , salt , pepper , beef , and cooked rice
4. place about 1 / 4 cup meat mixture in center of each leaf
5. fold in sides and roll ends over meat
6. place in slow-cooking pot
7. combine tomato sauce with brown sugar , lemon juice and worcestershire sauce
8. pour over cabbage rolls
9. cover and cook on low 7-9 hours
demonstrations.review: Yummy and easy, but a bit too sweet.  Next time, we will cut the sugar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chicken crescent roll casserole

this will also work great with turkey; if you do not have chicken breasts, then use any leftover cooked chicken. if desired you can fill the crescents just with the filling mixture and omit the soup, just brush with butter before baking. they are wonderful just stuffed with the filling! a few members have experienced a soggy bottom, so you might want to consider just drizzling half (or even a little less) of the soup mixture on top and a little around the sides of the crescents, then save the rest of the soup mixture for another time (this will help prevent a soggy bottom). you may use the jumbo crescent rolls and stuff with more chicken mixture :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. butter a casserole dish
3. in a saucepan , mix half and half cream , 3 / 4 cup grated cheese and undiluted chicken soup
4. heat just until the cheese melts
5. for the filling --- in a bowl , mix the soft cream cheese with butter until very smooth , then add in garlic powder
6. add in the chopped chicken , onion and cheddar cheese
7. mix well until combined
8. add in 2 tablespoons whipping cream or mayonnaise
9. mix to combine
10. season with seasoned salt or white and black pepper to taste
11. unroll the crescent rolls
12. place 1 heaping tablespoon chicken mixture on top of each crescent triangle , then roll up starting at the thicker end
13. drizzle a small amount of soup mixture on the bottom of the dish
14. then place the crescent rolls seam-side down on top of the creamed mixture in the casserole
15. drizzle the remaining sauce on top and sprinkle with 1 cup grated cheese , or amount desired
16. bake for about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Yummy!!! If you do not want the bottoms of the cresents to get soggy you can line them with the cheddar cheese. Melt the cheese in the oven for a few seconds and then spoon the filling into the rolls.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken scaloppine with lemon glaze   low fat and delicious

this is a wonderful lower-fat restaurant-quality dish that is easy to make, i also like to add in a few tablespoons of capers and cook with the lemon glaze if you are a lover of capers then add them in as it really adds to the flavour of this dish ---  this lemon sauce is not a heavy creamy sauce which is what makes this dish lower in fat, it is more like a glaze that soaks into the chicken, and i would strongly suggest to double or even triple the glaze i most always do, and please be certain to use only dry breadcrumbs as fresh will not stick to the chicken as well --- this is *very* good!

1. in a small bowl or shallow dish whisk together mustard and eggs
2. set aside
3. combine the dry bread crumbs with poultry seasoning , garlic powder and seasoning salt
4. spread on a piece of waxed paper
5. dip the breasts firstly in egg / mustard mixture then coat well with the crumb mixture , pressing downs with hands to adhear the crumbs to the breast
6. heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat
7. add in the chicken and cook for about 5 minutes on each side , or until it is no longer pink inside
8. remove and transfer to a plate to keep warm
9. for the glaze
10. in the same skillet add in the broth , lemon juice and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt bring to a boil scraping any brown bits from the pan
11. add in lemon slices and parsley
12. mix to combine for about 1 minute
13. spoon the glaze / sauce over chicken
14. delicious !
demonstrations.review: This was WONDERFUL!  I have been talking about it for weeks.  I will make this for my boyfriends mother, who is an amazin chef, to impress her when she visits next.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fish with lemon  butter  caper sauce

i've been making this "sauce" to serve over fish for years. i like it over simple pan fried fish, but you could serve it over crumbed fish too.

1. combine the flour , salt and pepper
2. coat the fish in the seasoned flour , shaking off the excess flour
3. heat half the butter to foaming over medium high heat in a heavy based pan
4. cook the fish to your liking and remove to serving plates
5. add the remaining butter , juice , zest , capers and parsley
6. heat for a minute then serve over the fish sharing the capers between the plates
demonstrations.review: This is decent. I've had much better. Next time, I would coat the fish in Dijon and clarify the butter.

target.recipe_text:
ground pork  peas  and rice casserole

this is based on a great recipe from ken hom's book, quick & easy chinese cooking. he says, "this is a typical chinese dish, designed to comfort, to satisfy, and to relax the body and soul. it reheats very well (when it is perhaps even tastier), and is a meal in itself. serve it with a favorite salad, and you will have a spendid, complete meal."

1. add rice and water to a large , heavy saucepan and bring to a boil
2. continue boiling for 10 minutes , or until most of the surface liquid has evaporated
3. the surface of the rice will be uneven and look like a pitted crater
4. at this stage , cover the pan with a tight-fitting lid and set the heat to low
5. meanwhile , prepare the rest of the dish
6. if you went the fresh peas route , blanch them in boiling water for 2 minutes , drain , and set aside
7. otherwise , thaw frozen peas at room temperature
8. add the oil to a heated wok or skillet
9. add the pork and stir-fry for 1 minute , then add the peas , soy sauces , oyster sauce , and rice wine
10. continue to cook for another 2 minutes , then add the green onions
11. place this cooked mixture on top of the rice , cover , and continue to cook over the lowest possible heat for another 15 minutes
12. serve immediately , drizzling additional oyster sauce over the top of the casserole if desired
target.review: I can't explain why but this dish was very dry. If I try it again I'd have to add more liguid.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp shau mai  dim sum dumpling

this is yummy, and pretty easy to put together, the wrapping wll be a little wrinkly. it not only has a shrimp filling, but a whole shrimp in it as well.  came from a recipe book i have that is written in half chinese and half english. updated as per chef flower's comments in directions.

1. chop shrimp coarsely
2. combine wine , sesame oil , cornstarch , sugar , salt and pepper
3. chop coriander and combine with chestnuts and lard / pork fat
4. mix all together with the chopped shrimp
5. place a tablespoon of the filling on top of a wonton skin
6. place a shrimp on top of the filling
7. wet the edges of the wonton skin , then cover shrimp with another wonton skin letting the tail stick out between the two skins
8. wrap around the filling , making sure the edges are sealed (use little more water if edge is to dry
9. do this til all are done
10. place the finished shau mai in a steamer for 8 minutes over high heat , serve alone or with your favorite dipping sauce
demonstrations.review:
Excellent taste.  Note to serve them immediately when ready.
Served with chili sauce and hot mustard on side. I took the tail shell off the shrimp and chopped the shrimp in halfs or thirds. Easier to make better looking shu mai, more uniform  Had fun with this and was delicious

demonstrations.recipe_text:
indian almond koftas with yogurt

wonderful tasty spicy kaftas to enjoy as a starter or to  accompany a good curry. kofta is very popular in asia. these can be made with lamb or chicken. koftas are usually fried these however are cooked in the oven.
i am posting this recipe for my friend, an indian lady who is a zaar member.

1. preheat oven to 190c
2. to the minced meat add the ginger , green chilie , coriander , curry powder , crumble the stock cube into the mixture
3. add 1 tbsp of yogurt and half of the milk powder , mix well to incorporate the ingredients
4. divide the mixture into 12 and shape into balls
5. roll the balls in the flaked almonds and place on a baking sheet , spaced out to allow them to expand while cooking
6. stir together the remaining yogurt , milk powder , sugar , oil and chilli powder and a little salt to taste
7. spoon the yogurt mixture over the koftas , coat them well
8. bake in the oven , uncovered for 30 minutes , the almond coating should be golden and toasted
9. serve with drinks , salads , curries or just as they are
demonstrations.review: I missed the "C" after the oven temp in the recipe and stupidly cooked it at 190 F. The sauce was great and when I cooked the second batch at the right temp, it turned out fine. Tasty but heavy and dense.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my mama s meat sauce

this is probably the first thing that i ever learned to cook. my mother used to cook it while i took a nap as a child, and the smell would wake me up. it's really garlicky and the wine gives it a nice flavour. it also freezes really well. enjoy!

1. saut onions in oil
2. add beef and brown before stirring in all seasonings
3. add tomatoes , paste , and cloves
4. stir and add alcohol if using
5. cover and let cook on a low fire for 2 hours or more
demonstrations.review: This was even better than expected. People thought I slaved all day over this sauce. It was very easy. I did not have "italian seasoning" on hand so I used a 1/2 tbs dried basil and 1/2 tbs dried parsely. Also, I used half the meat but kept everything else the same and it was really delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fudge icing

i usually use this on a sheet cake.it really is like having fudge for a topping!

1. combine first 4 ingredients and bring to boil , stirring constantly
2. boil hard 1 minute without stirring
3. remove from heat , add vanilla and beat until spreading consistancy
demonstrations.review: Easy to make. Also it was excellent for cupcakes when you prefer a firm icing. It was delicious but It was a bit too sweet for us. Next time I will reduce the sugar to just under a cup and see how it works out.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai fishcakes with sweet chilli sauce and cucumber relish

posting for chef #29196. 

please see my recipe for recipe #268393.

1. in a food processor , mince fish to a paste
2. add curry paste , fish sauce , cornflour and egg
3. combine well
4. transfer to a bowl and mix in beans and onions
5. wet hands and shape mix into flat round cakes approximately 5cm in diameter and 1cm thick
6. deep-fry in vegetable oil until golden brown , about 5-7 minutes
7. drain on paper towel
8. serve with sweet chili sauce and cucumber relish
demonstrations.review: Very very tasty. Also easy to make.  For me the frying time was too long and I would reduce it next time by several minutes.

target.recipe_text:
zucchini pancakes

this is a great vegetarian pancake, easy to make and is delicious. this recipe was passed to my mother over 100 years ago and has been a favorite of the families.

1. wash and shred zucchini on a fine shredder
2. in a large mixing bowl , beat eggs
3. add shredded zucchini and mix well using a fork
4. add flour , sugar , salt and olive oil and stir well to blend
5. finally , add baking powder and mix using a spoon
6. preheat griddle to 425- 450f
7. if using a heavy duty frying pan , heat to medium-high heat
8. adjust heat if necessary
9. rub grill or frying pan with oil before cooking each batch of pancakes
10. spoon batter onto hot griddle
11. cook until bubbles on the top of the pancake almost stop , about 1 1 / 2 minutes
12. turn pancake over and continue to cook for another 1 to 1 1 / 2 minutes or until pancakes are done
13. when done , rub pancakes with melted butter and place in a preheated 250 f oven to keep warm until the remainder are cooked , or serve immediately
14. serve with your choice of jams or syrups
15. also very good with sour cream or yogurt along with your choice of jams or syrups , or you can eat them just plain
16. these pancakes are delicious for breakfast , brunch or just as a snack anytime
target.review: I made these with yellow squash instead of zucchini. They were terrific! The second time I made them, I used whole wheat flour, but they were much better with white flour. Great way to get veggies into the kids!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
warm eggplant  aubergine  salad

tasty warm eggplant salad, great served with yogurt and my "fennel and sea salt pita bread crisps".

1. preheat oven to 200c
2. peel strips off the eggplant skin with a vegetable peeler , slice eggplant into 1cm thick slices
3. brush both sides with the extra olive oil , then place in a baking dish and sprinkle with sea salt
4. cook for 30 minutes
5. remove from oven , if eggplant is a little dry , sprinkle with water , cool for 5 minutes , then cut into 1 cm cubes and set aside
6. heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat , add tomatoes , garlic , spices , chilli , sugar and salt
7. simmer for 10 minutes , remove from heat and add juice , vinegar and black pepper
8. add to the reserved eggplant , stir through herbs
9. serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: This was delicious. I blackened and peeled (roasted) the peppers. I also scalded and peeled the tomatoes but did not cook them. Threw in a few toasted pine nuts for good measure. It was a hit! Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swiss chard  stir fried  with feta cheese

low cal veggie, high iron. great with the touch of feta & pine nuts. don't overcook. you can include this in a chinese meal as an exta vegetable dish

1. in a wok heat the oil
2. add shallots
3. stir fry 1 minute or until just beginning to brown
4. add swiss chard , toss and cover
5. cook 2 minutes
6. remove cover and cook about another minute
7. if there is any liqiud drain it off
8. stir in the feta cheese , cook 30 seconds or until it starts to melt
9. add pine nuts and season
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review:
This recipe was outstanding! Chard is the "free vegetable of the week" from my vegetable garden. I stumbled across this recipe when I was trying to come up with a new way to cook it.

I used about 1 T of Olive Oil instead of the Peanut Oil and doubled the pine nuts because I love them so much. I also used the stems of the chard.

I will DEFINITELY make this again! Yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
waffle iron french toast

modified version of recipe from williams and sonama january 07 catalog.  this is an awesome breakfast and it was fun and easy to make, plus there wasn't a lot of clean up.

1. preheat waffle maker and spray surface with non-stick cooking spray
2. in large bowl , whisk eggs until frothy , then add remaining ingredients and whisk until well mixed
3. dip 1 slice of bread into mixture and turn to cover both sides
4. place in waffle maker and cook until golden brown
5. top with syrup or powdered sugar
demonstrations.review:
This recipe is delicious and a great way to use up a loaf or wheat bread. I cut the recipe to 4 eggs and 1 1/2 cup milk and it made about 10 slices. 

My kids loved it and the nutmeg and brown sugar really kicked it up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
polenta parmesan

personally i don't care for polenta but this recipe is tolerable. i make it for my friends that like polenta and they seem to love it. (how can one love polenta?) it's better if you serve it with a very spicy tomato salsa.

1. gradually add cornmeal to the salted boiling water , stirring frequently so there are no lumps
2. when it comes to a boil reduce heat to medium , cook stirring frequently for 40 minutes
3. stir in 5 oz of butter , 4oz grated parmesan and nutmeg
4. pour polenta in an oven-proof pan cover with waxed paper and set aside to cool
5. heat oven to 400f
6. dot with remaining butter and parmesan
7. bake for 30 minutes until top is brown and crispy
demonstrations.review:
YUMMY! This was the first time I have ever made polenta and it was divine! It was also quite easy to make. 

I cut the butter to about 2 oz and only used 4 oz of cheese to cut the fat content. It was still delicious. 

I served this with the Swiss Chard, feta and pine nut recipe. My dinner was a huge success! Even my 3-year olds ate it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese pot stickers

these pot stickers are 100% better than any you can buy and well worth the extra effort. i like to make them and then freeze them so all you have to do is the final steps just before you serve them. i make them every christmas to have as a quick appetizer. one review commented that she had trouble with them sticking together when she defrosted them -  i have not had this happen however to be sure it doesn't happen to you defrost them separated.  i have also fried them directly from the freezer. they only take a few seconds more to cook.

1. sprinkle salt over the shredded cabbage and let stand for 5 minutes , then squeeze out liquid
2. squeeze out any liquid from the shrimp
3. mix cabbage , shrimp , pork , soy , wine , onion , oil , ginger and garlic
4. on each wrapper place about 2 tsp of the mix and seal the edges , use a bit of water on the edge , try to press out all the air and ensure they are tightly sealed
5. in 2 large skillets heat 1 tbsp oil , fry 16 dumplings for 1 minute or until golden on one side add 1 / 4 cup of stock into the pan , reduce heat to low , cover and cook , without turning for about 7 minutes or until the dumpling is translucent and most of the liquid has evaporated uncover and on higher heat cook for another 5-7 minutes or until the bottoms are dark brown , drain put on a platter and keep warm
6. repeat for the remaining 32 dumplings
7. mix the dipping sauce and serve with warm or hot dumplings
demonstrations.review: Yummy, yummy, yummy. I didn't have any shrimp so I added more pork instead. I also used "ribbit!'s" recipe for wonton wrappers. A lot of work, but definitely worth it!

target.recipe_text:
guinness beer bread

great-tasting variety on traditional beer bread, this one only lasts a couple of days around my house.

1. preheat oven to 375f degrees
2. sift together flour , baking powder , salt and sugar
3. add guinness and eggs
4. stir just until blended
5. pour into greased 9x5x3 loaf pan
6. bake at 375f for approximately 70 minutes
7. remove from pan and cool on wire rack
target.review:
I had started out wanting to make a cheese beer bread, only to realise when I went home that I forgot to print the recipe.  To make a long story short. I substituted the Guiness Beer for regular beer and added cheese after I added the Beer and eggs and to my amazement the bread came out perfect. I believe this is a perfect recipe for variations of beer bread.  It was excellent!

Thanks Felix

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern pride sweet cornbread

long before boston market cornered the market on cornbread, the women in my family were making up a darn good corn bread themselves. every bbq or potluck this cornbread was in demand. i finally handed one of my aunties a measuring cup (you know they never measure anything) and learned how to make it. it really does resemble the taste of boston market, almost could be a dessert with that sweet taste of honey and some butter on top...

1. grease a 9x13 inch baking pan with shortening
2. preheat oven to 375f
3. mix sugar , butter , eggs , milk , honey and water together in a large bowl
4. mix dry ingredients together in a separate bowl: cornmeal , flour , baking powder , and salt
5. while stirring , add dry ingredients to sugar , egg , and milk mixture and mix thoroughly
6. mixture will be slightly lumpy
7. pour into greased rectangular pan
8. bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown on top
9. serve with butter
demonstrations.review: This cornbread was Excellent! Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
world s best butter cookies

i tested 8 different butter cookie recipes, looking for the "perfect" butter cookie. it had to be buttery, a little crumbly (like shortbread), and not too sweet. this is the winner. i think these are the worlds best butter cookie, courtesy of chef alice medrich.

1. beat the butter , sugar , salt and vanilla together until smooth and creamy
2. mix in the egg yolk until well incorporated , scraping down the sides of the bowl at least once
3. add the flour and mix just until incorporated
4. scrape onto a lightly floured board and knead a few times , just until the dough smooths out
5. turn onto a sheet of plastic wrap and roll into a log , wrap up and refrigerate for several hours or freeze
6. before baking , preheat the oven to 325f
7. line your baking sheets with parchment
8. slice the dough into slices about 1 / 8" thick and place them on the sheets about an inch apart
9. bake until just beginning to turn golden around the edges , about 16-18 minutes
10. you could roll the dough out and cut shapes
11. you could slice them even thinner and sandwich them with chocolate or jam or lemon curd
12. you could make them and then dip them half into chocolate
13. you could just make them and eat them , which is my favorite
14. whatever you do , they will be delicious
demonstrations.review: The ..World's Best description is not a lie.  Very good cookie and now I am sharing this recipe to friends as they loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy garlic penne pasta

this is a delicious, super quick side or main dish. i got it from the back of a pasta box and it is yummy!

1. melt butter and add garlic in a medium sauce pan
2. cook over medium for 1 minute
3. add flour and cook 1 minute , stirring constantly
4. stir in broth and milk and cook , stirring frequently , until sauce boils and thickens
5. add parsley , salt , pepper and cheese
6. stir until cheese is melted
7. toss hot pasta with sauce and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This tasted really good! I did make one substitute, as I had no chicken stock on hand.  I used one chicken cube dissolved in 3/4 cup water.  There was no need to add any salt as the cube already contains salt.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple curry tuna melt

we love tuna melts and this one is very different. love the combination of ingredients.

1. in a mixing bowl , add the first 7 ingredients
2. stir to combine
3. spread 1 / 4 cup of the mixture on each slice of toasted bread
4. sprinkle evenly with walnuts
5. top with a slice of cheese
6. place tuna melts on a baking sheet
7. broil 5 inches away from the heat until the cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: Excellent! This tuna melt has a unique flavour and is very tasty.  I topped it with grated cheddar cheese as opposed to a slice and used regular mustard and it came out perfect!  This truly one of the best tuna melt recipes I now have. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review:
Very Moist and Smooth, the best tasting banana bread I have tried in a while.

Great recipe, It was my pleasure to use my stock of over-riped bananas!

target.recipe_text:
moroccan chickpeas and sweet potatoes

this dish makes a wonderful vegetarian meal. exotically spiced, offset with dried apricots, different and delicious.

1. in a medium saucepan , combine the onion , garlic , ginger , and wine or sherry
2. cover and sweat over low heat for 5 minutes
3. add the cumin , cinnamon , paprika , and red pepper flakes and cook , uncovered , 1 minute longer
4. add the water or chickpea cooking liquid , salt , sweet potatoes , and apricots
5. bring to a boil , cover , and simmer until the sweet potatoes are just tender , about 15 minutes
6. add the chickpeas , raisins , and lemon juice
7. cook , stirring occasionally , for about 5 minutes , until the chickpeas are hot
8. add the sliced almonds
target.review: This was a very tasty recipe!  I substituted 1 tbsp of garam masala for the spices listed, which I realize made it more Indian than Moroccan, but it still worked well and was so good.  My 2 year old even ate it, which speaks volumes for the power of this recipe!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai tofu and squash curry

from canadian living magazine.  recommended for tofu lovers and/or fans of thai-inspired dishes.

1. pat tofu dry with paper towels
2. cut into 3 / 4-inch cubes
3. set aside
4. peel and seed squash
5. cut into 3 / 4-inch cubes to make 3 cups
6. set aside
7. in skillet , heat oil over medium heat
8. cook onion , garlic and curry paste , stirring occasionally , until onion is softened , about 5 minutes
9. add squash , coconut milk , stock , soy sauce , sugar , fish sauce and salt
10. bring to boil
11. reduce heat to low
12. partially cover and simmer until squash is almost tender , about 12 minutes
13. add red pepper
14. simmer for 5 minutes
15. add tofu
16. simmer until heated through , about 2 minutes
17. stir in cilantro and lime juice
18. sprinkle with peanuts
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I added shitake mushrooms and those mini thai pea eggplants and this was a full meal.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin ginger scones with cinnamon chips

this is a delicious flavorful scone that is good at any time of year, not just in the fall and winter. enjoy for breakfast, with tea or coffee or even for dessert. makes a good gift, too.  just made them again for a friends birthday (1/09)  and mmmmm forgot how i love them so much.

1. combine 1 / 2 c sugar , flour , baking powder , cinnamon , baking soda and salt in a large bowl
2. cut 5 tbsp butter into dry ingredients until crumbly
3. in separate bowl combine the egg , pumpkin , sour cream and ginger
4. add wet ingredients to dry ingredients and mix well
5. mix in cinnamon chips
6. turn out on lightly floured surface and knead 10x
7. i add extra flour here as the dough is usually a bit moist
8. divide dough in half and form each half into a 1 / 2 inch thick circle
9. cut each circle into 8 wedges
10. brush wedges with melted butter and sprinkle with sugar
11. bake on ungreased cookie sheet in preheated 425 degree oven for 10 minutes or until lightly golden on edges
demonstrations.review: Excellent.  My scone-hating husband declared he could eat these every week!  I added an extra bit of candied ginger, but otherwise followed recipe exactly.  SSSOOOO good- thanks very much for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zippity dooo daaaa orzo salad

this is a fabulous salad that is sure to please all of your guests.  it is easy to increase or decrease the size of the recipe to suit your needs.
dont use extra virgin olive oil for this salad.  use an olive oil suitable for salads.  i really hope you enjoy my creation!!!

1. first cook your orzo pasta per package directions , cooking until al dente , and drain
2. in a medium sized , nonreactive bowl , gradually beat together the lime zest , lemon juice , salad quality olive oil , basil , garlic , and mustard until an emulsion forms
3. then season the oil mixture with salt and pepper to taste
4. mix your pasta , feta cheese , peppers , tomatoes , capers , kalmata olives , and chopped red onion together in a bowl
5. pour the vinaigrette over the pasta mixture and mix to combine
6. add oregano and green onions , toss , and then add extra salt and pepper to your tastes
7. chill salad for 1-2 hours for best results
8. you can make this in the morning and even serve it in the evening , but dont save it for too long
demonstrations.review: I had just made what I thought was the most amazing orzo salad from one of my Cooking Light cookbooks the week before I tried this orzo salad.  This one topped the other orzo salad, becoming my staple!  I'm making it this weekend for a big BBQ and know it will be a HIT.  It is SO delicious, thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basil lime fruit salad  cooking light

delicious! this can be prepared ahead of time by making the simple syrup and chopping the fruits, just refrigerate seperately and then combine just before serving.

1. make the simple syrup by combining the sugar and water in a saucepan
2. bring to a boil
3. cook for a minute until the sugar is dissolved
4. remove pan from heat , stir in the basil and lime rind
5. cool
6. strain to discard the solids
7. combine the fruits in a large bowl
8. drizzle with the simple syrup
9. toss gently
demonstrations.review: I love Cooking Light so this recipe jumped out at me.  I used fruits I had on-hand (pineapple, apple, grapes, blackberries, orange) and added the simple syrup with shredded basil.  Took it to a potluck and everyone loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
aloo gobi

great aloo gobi recipe from the film bend it like beckham

1. heat vegetable oil in a large saucepan
2. add the chopped onion and one teaspoon of cumin seeds to the oil
3. stir together and cook until onions become creamy , golden , and translucent
4. add chopped coriander stalks , two teaspoons of turmeric , and one teaspoon of salt
5. add chopped chillis stir tomatoes into onion mixture
6. add ginger and garlic
7. mix thoroughly
8. add potatoes and cauliflower to the sauce plus a few tablespoons of water
9. ensure that the potatoes and cauliflower are coated with the curry sauce
10. cover and allow to simmer for twenty minutes
11. add two teaspoons of garam masala and stir
12. sprinkle chopped coriander leaves on top of the curry
13. turn off the heat , cover , and leave for as long as possible before serving
demonstrations.review: I read previous reviews about the bitter taste and was like, "pshaw!  they must have sensitive palates.", but then I made it and it WAS bitter.  Really bitter!  I guess it must be the turmeric?  I don't know what caused the bitterness, but next time I might lessen the dose of turmeric and garam masala.

target.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
target.review: These brownies were delicious.  They were very rich and fudge-like.  I didn't even use any add ins and they were still so yummy.  The recipe does double wonderfully.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese crock pot chicken

this is easy and tasty, the crock pot does the work.  the recipe came from the crock pot cookbook i use pretty often.  it's good enough for company.

1. place your chicken in the crock pot
2. mix together soy sauce , marmalade and ketchup , and pour over the chicken
3. then add garlic and onions , a teeny bit of salt and pepper
4. cover with lid and cook on low setting for about 10-12 hours
5. chicken should be falling off the bone when ready
6. serve with rice
demonstrations.review: This was so easy and delicious.  It will definitely become a "go to" recipe.  My 6 yr old son helped me throw it all together.  He and my 3 yr old nephew especially enjoyed it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
very chocolate cheesecake

don't look at this recipe unless you really love chocolate!!

1. mix crumbs , sugar , and butter
2. press into bottom of 9 inch springform pan
3. melt the chocolate chips , stirring until smooth
4. beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth
5. add flour
6. beat well
7. add eggs
8. beat until just mixed
9. stir in vanilla and melted chocolate
10. pour over crust
11. bake at 350 for 45 minutes or until center is set
12. chill before serving
demonstrations.review: This cheesecake is to die for!  I made it today with my 10 yr old daughter.  We made a crust using some leftover peanut butter cookies instead of the wafer crumbs.  The chocolate and peanut butter blended nicely.  Very simple, very rich and delicious.  We will make this again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crackle top molasses cookies

found this in an old cookie cook book that i bought at a used book sale. they are very delicious and quite easy to make. enjoy!!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a large bowl , combine oil and 1 cup sugar
3. add egg , beating well
4. stir in molasses , 2 cups flour , baking soda , cinnamon and ginger
5. if necessary , add a little more flour to make a firm dough
6. shape dough into 1 1 / 4 inch balls
7. roll in 1 / 3 cup of sugar
8. place 3-inces apart on ungreased baking sheets
9. bake 12 minutes or until golden brown and tops crack
10. cool on racks
demonstrations.review: These cookies turned out perfect!  I used honey in place of the molasses, because that's what I had on hand.  They were perfectly spiced and everyone loved them.  Will definitely make these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat oatmeal pumpkin spice muffins

this is a recipe i adapted from an old favorite, applesauce muffins.   they are high in fibre and low in fat.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. oil or spray muffin tins with cooking spray
3. sift together the dry ingredients
4. add the rest of the ingredients and stir until just moistened
5. divide into 12 muffins and bake for 15-20 minutes until cooked in centre
6. remove from pan after 5-10 minutes and let cool
7. place in a airtight container and try not to eat for 24 hours as they will become more moist
demonstrations.review: These muffins are wonderful.  They looked so beautiful and tasted so yummy.  I used applesauce for the oil, trying to make them as healthy as possible.  Which is good because all four of my children devoured them.  This recipe is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry oatmeal crisp

great topped with whipped cream for dessert or to have with coffee!

1. spread pie filling into a greased 9-inch square baking dish
2. combine the next six ingredients in a bowl
3. cut in butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs
4. sprinkle over filling
5. bake at 375 degrees for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown
6. top with whipped cream and dig in !
demonstrations.review: Everyone loved this.  The topping is crunchy and rich.  It is also so easy to throw together.  Will definitely make again, and will try other fruits as well.

target.recipe_text:
baja black beans  corn and rice

a south of the border blend of textures and flavors. serve hot as a main dish or a side dish with grilled meat or chicken.

1. cook brown rice
2. in a medium bowl , combine black beans , corn , tomatoes , onion , cilantro , jalapeno , lime juice , oil , salt , pepper and hot sauce
3. to serve , place a scoop of hot rice in a bowl or on a plate , top with a generous scoop of the black bean mixture
4. stir together before eating
target.review: Good beans and rice recipe. My husband enjoyed having this for lunch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
edna s apple crumble  aka  apple crisp

a simple and easy to make but oh so yummy recipe. known as apple crumble in the uk and apple crisp in the us

1. put apples in an 8 or 9 inch square baking dish
2. combine the rest of the ingredients in a separate bowl and mix
3. spread crumble mixture over apples and bake for 35 minutes in a 375f degree oven
4. for an added treat top off with a little english custard
demonstrations.review: A very simple and elegant recipe. My family's new favourite apple crisp recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot beer brats

serve these along side of cabbage and noodles for a complete and easy german-style dinner!

1. heat oil and garlic in a large skillet
2. add bratwurst and brown on each side
3. with a fork , poke holes in each bratwurst and cook for 5 more minutes
4. transfer brats to crock pot
5. pour beer to cover
6. cook on low for 6-7 hours
demonstrations.review: Easy and delicious! The family loved the taste, and I loved how easy it was to prepare!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple peach pie

this recipe is from c.a. lynd of lyndsgourmet.com.  every year we anxiously wait for lynd's farm to put out their peaches.  they gave us this recipe with the peaches i just bought and it is simple and wonderful.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. stir together flour , 1 cup sugar , and cinnamon and set aside
3. wash , peel , and slice fresh peaches
4. mix together peaches with the combined dry ingredients
5. turn into pastry-lined pie pan and dot with butter
6. cover with top crust , cut slits in it , seal the edges
7. sprinkle top with 2 tablespoons of sugar
8. cover the edges with foil to prevent over browning
9. remove foil for the last 15 minutes of baking
10. bake 35 to 45 minutes or until crust is brown and juice begins to bubble through the slits in the crust
11. pie may be frozen for future use
demonstrations.review: Wonderful! Simple with a clean peach taste. I had really juicy peaches so I used the entire 1/2 cup of flour and I was surprised that the pie didn't have a floury aftertaste. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chickpeas with spinach  greek

nothing fancy about this dish - just good eating. round off with some feta cheese and crusty bread.

1. in a large saucepan , over medium heat , saute the onions and garlic in the olive oil until the onions are tender
2. add the chickpeas , tomatoes , pepper flakes , and oregano , and paprika
3. cover and simmer for about 18 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. add spinach and cook about 7 minutes longer , or until spinach is cooked
5. add the lemon juice , salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: Good chickpea recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry rhubarb pie

an excellent pie to make when strawberries and rhubarb are at their peak. this delicious fruit-filled pie is a recipe from canadian living magazine, may 1993. you can substitute a plain top crust instead of the lattice top if you like; brush with the egg glaze and cut steam vents. tip: keep a clear plastic quilt ruler with your baking and cooking supplies to measure pastry strips for lattice pies, to measure squares or strips of dough, pastry, or pasta, or as a guide for cutting squares evenly.

1. in a bowl , combine rhubarb , strawberries , sugar , cornstarch , lemon juice and cinnamon
2. on lightly floured surface , roll out half of the pastry and line a nine-inch pie plate
3. spoon in filling
4. roll out pastry for top crust
5. using pastry wheel or knife , cut into 1-inch wide strips
6. brush pastry rim with some of the beaten egg
7. gently weave strips over the pie to form lattice
8. trim and flute the edge
9. brush lattice with beaten egg
10. sprinkle top with sugar if using
11. bake on a baking sheet with sides in a 425 degree fahrenheit oven for 15 minutes
12. reduce heat to 375 degrees fahrenheit and bake for 50 to 60 minutes longer or until rhubarb is tender , filling thickened , and the crust is golden
13. let stand for 15 to 20 minutes before cutting
