demonstrations.review: I must have had really juicy strawberries because the 1/4 cup of cornstarch wasn't enough to prevent it from being soupy. The taste was fantastic, so I will definitely make this again and will add a little more cornstarch.

target.recipe_text:
crispy cheese cauliflower

the original of this tempting recipe came from jean carper's 'eatsmart' column in the 9-11 feb 2007 issue of the usa weekend paper.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees f
2. spray cookie sheet with olive oil
3. in a shallow dish , combine cheese , cumin , cayenne , salt & pepper
4. dredge cauliflower pieces in egg , then in cheese mix
5. put on cookie sheet , & spray with oil
6. bake 15 minutes
7. remove to serving plate , & sprinkle with parsley
8. serve with lemon wedges
target.review:
Excellent recipe.  Hubby & son are usually very anti cauliflower but they loved this.  Had to bake it a fair bit more than 15 minutes, tho.  I'll definitely make this many times in the future, allowing at least 25 minutes for baking.
Thank you SydMike

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moroccan chickpeas and sweet potatoes

this dish makes a wonderful vegetarian meal. exotically spiced, offset with dried apricots, different and delicious.

1. in a medium saucepan , combine the onion , garlic , ginger , and wine or sherry
2. cover and sweat over low heat for 5 minutes
3. add the cumin , cinnamon , paprika , and red pepper flakes and cook , uncovered , 1 minute longer
4. add the water or chickpea cooking liquid , salt , sweet potatoes , and apricots
5. bring to a boil , cover , and simmer until the sweet potatoes are just tender , about 15 minutes
6. add the chickpeas , raisins , and lemon juice
7. cook , stirring occasionally , for about 5 minutes , until the chickpeas are hot
8. add the sliced almonds
demonstrations.review: Excellent!  I served it as an accompaniment to my Chicken B'stilla Roll. I used canned, drained chick peas, chicken stock instead of water & both orange & white sweet potatoes.  Son had some harissa with his.  Definitely a keeper, thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesty low fat chicken breasts

very tasty, you can make it as hot or as mild as you want. quick easy dish - no muss no fuss

1. put the breasts in a 9x13-inch baking dish
2. whisk remaining ingredients together until they are well blended
3. pour over the breasts
4. coat both sides of the breasts with the sauce
5. bake in 400f oven for approx 30 minutes or until the chicken is done
6. remove breasts , keep warm
7. pour the sauce into a sauce pan stir in the cornstarch that has been mixed with a tbsp of water , bring to a boil and allow to thicken whisk constantly
8. pour over the chicken & serve
demonstrations.review: This is a keeper, a BIG hit.  Because my chicken breasts were quite thick, I put some slashes in the meat & marinated them in the sauce for about an hour.  The sauce stayed thick until the final few minutes in the oven, but thickened well with the cornflour slurry.  Thank you for a great, easy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow roast leg of lamb with white wine

this will fall off the bone and makes a lovely rich and intense gravy. you can use oregano instead of the rosemary.

1. preheat the oven to 325f
2. pour the oil into a large , sturdy roasting tin and set it over the stove top
3. slash the lamb with a sharp knife , use one of the sliced garlic cloves , and stick slivers into the meat
4. season the lamb with salt and pepper then roll it in the flour
5. brown the lamb all over in the hot oil for 5-10 minutes
6. add the onions and cook for a further 5-10 minutes , turning the lamb and stirring the onions until both are nicely browned
7. add the garlic , white wine , stock , rosemary and redcurrant jelly , bring to a simmer , transfer to the the oven and cook for 2 hours covered , basting now and again with the juices
8. uncover and cook for another 1 1 / 2-2 hours , basting again at intervals
9. take the lamb out of the tin and place on a large board to rest in a warm place
10. if needed skim off and reduce the pan juices , mash up the onions a bit
11. cut the lamb into thick slices - you'll find the meat falls away from the bone so you may end up with more chunks than slices
demonstrations.review: This is a wonderful dish.  I've made it several times & cook it for longer on a lower temperature.  Sliced & warmed, the leftovers go well with hummos, tabbouleh, baba ghanoush & Leb bread.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork roast with port  star anise  ginger and  tamarind

our favourite pork roast

1. preheat oven to 140 c
2. brown pork all over in oil in casserole dish
3. transfer pork to plate
4. fry onion slowly in same pan
5. pour off excess oil , leaving onion behind
6. return pork to dish
7. add remaining ingredients and season with pepper
8. bring to boil , cover and transfer to oven
9. cook for around 3 hours turning occasionally until meat is very tender , and cooked through
10. set pork aside
11. skim as much fat as you can from juices , strain
12. slice the pork thickly and drizzle with a little of the cooking juices
demonstrations.review:
What an interesting dish!!  Asian flavours with the rosemary & port!! Have to say I was a tad sceptical & didn't know what to serve with it.  Took note of other reviewers & made your smashed taters (a long-time fave now)& that worked.

I cooked about a kilo of stewing pork in my new pressure cooker (any Perthites here, the French lady at Subi has a great sale on now).  Soo tender.  If I'd been organised I was going to use the crock pot, but I think the pressure cooker gave a more tender result.
  
Despite the mainly Asian flavours, the potatoes went well with it.  My husband & son both absolutely RAVED about this dish & want me to make it weekly - and that's high praise indeed.   Thank you, mate:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of applebee s honey grilled salmon by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com  it's all about the sauce with this one. this sweet, tangy and slightly spicy sauce goes perfectly with salmon, but can also be used on chicken or ribs. just be sure to watch the sauce closely as it cooks in case it starts to bubble over. it's gonna get thicker as it cools, so be sure not to overcook it. if it becomes too thick, just add a bit of water to thin it out.

1. make the sauce by combining all ingredients , except salmon , in a medium saucepan over medium / low heat
2. stir occasionally until sauce begins to boil , then simmer uncovered for 15 minutes or until syrupy
3. watch the sauce closely to be sure it doesn't bubble over
4. preheat barbecue grill to medium heat
5. rub each salmon filet with vegetable oil , then add a light sprinkling of salt and pepper
6. grill the salmon for 4 to 7 minutes per side or until done
7. serve salmon with a small cup of the honey pepper sauce on the side
demonstrations.review:
We loved this recipe. Next time I'll omit the vinegar as I think the acidity from the lemon & pineapple juice is enough to balance the sugar & salt from the soy etc. 

Served it with a potato dish with a horseradish sauce - NOT a good accompaniment - & lemon beans, which were good with the salmon.  

Will definitely make this many times again, toying around with a good potato accompaniment.   We eat Asian food several times a week so we want a change from rice.

target.recipe_text:
brownie caramel cheesecake

it is very rich, and worth the time and calories

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease the bottom of a 9 inch springform pan
3. in a small bowl , mix together brownie mix , 1 egg and water
4. spread into the greased pan
5. bake for 25 minutes
6. melt the caramels with the evaporated milk over low heat in a heavy saucepan
7. stir often , and heat until mixture has a smooth consistency
8. reserve 1 / 3 cup of this caramel mixture , and pour the remainder over the warm , baked brownie crust
9. in a large bowl , beat the cream cheese , sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer until smooth
10. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each addition
11. pour cream cheese mixture over caramel mixture
12. bake cheesecake for 40 minutes
13. chill in pan
14. when cake is thoroughly chilled , loosen by running a knife around the edge , and then remove the rim of the pan
15. heat reserved caramel mixture , and spoon over cheesecake
16. drizzle with the chocolate topping
target.review: Very good cheesecake, though almost too rich...I had to make my own brownies because I couldn't find a brownie mix, so I used evelyn/athens' "chocolate fudge brownies" recipe, I mixed the reserved 1/3 cup caramel mixture in with the cream cheese, and because I made this cake for a friend's birthday I spread the fudge topping instead of drizzling it so I could decorate the cake.The flavour was fantastic, but I'd say it serves way more than 12 people (which was good since we were 35 at the party!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple brownies

nan

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. mix butter , sugars , eggs and vanilla
3. mix in flour , baking powder and salt
4. stir in apples and nuts
5. spread into a greased 9x9x2-inch baking pan
6. bake for 35-40 minutes , or until toothpick inserted into center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Excellent brownies! I was afraid they'd be too sweet because the batter was actually overly sweet, but once baked the flavour balanced and it came out wonderful, very moist and tasty. I added a very small amount (1/8 tsp or even less) of pumpkin spice mix. I'll be doing these brownies a lot, thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
duchesse mashed potato mushroom puff

this is a fabulous recipe and one i always seem to fall back on for dinner parties. the potatoes are whipped into a creamy puree with butter, milk and eggs and are sandwiched with a yummy mushroom filling. this all bakes up into a lovely golden puff which magically disappears before all other dishes! this wonderful recipe was given to me years ago by my friend, buzz in toronto.

1. for potatoes: peel potatoes , cut in halves and boil in salted water until soft , but firm
2. drain and dry thoroughly by shaking over heat until moisture disappears
3. mash potatoes using electric mixer
4. add salt , pepper , butter or margarine , eggs , cheese , baking powder and liquid
5. beat until fluffy
6. for mushrooms: saute onion in butter or margarine , until nicely carmelized
7. remove onions from pan
8. saute mushrooms until browned and they have released all of their liquid
9. mix with onions , salt , pepper and chopped parsley
10. soften slightly before filling
11. butter a pie plate or a small pyrex baking dish and line bottom and sides of plate with about 1" mashed potato mixture
12. fill centre with mushroom mixture , cover with remaining potato mixture
13. top with little bits of butter and a sprinkling of paprika
14. bake at 400f for 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown and puffed
15. if my other sides don't have cheese in them , then i'll often add it
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe for a dinner party, all my friends really loved it, though I agree with the other reviewer that a little cheese could take this dish to another level...I'll try again adding a layer of fontina cheese slices between the mushroom filling and the top potato layer. The only thing I changed was mashing the potatoes by hand because in my family mashing potatoes in a processor is a mortal sin...!!!(;P) Thank you for this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
triple threat oatmeal bars

the threat is in that they're so good, you won't be able to eat just one. but it is good to know these bars are packed nutritionally and full of flavour! these are the ones that go to school with my kids more often than not.

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. butter 10 x 14 inch cookie sheet and line with parchment paper
3. cream butter and brown sugar in large bowl until light and fluffy
4. beat in eggs 1 at a time
5. beat in milk and vanilla
6. combine flour , baking powder , cinnamon and salt in a small bowl
7. add to butter mixture and stir until just combined
8. mix in oats , walnuts , raisins and coconut
9. press dough evenly into prepared pan
10. bake until top is golden-brown , about 15 minutes
11. cool in pan on rack 5 minutes
12. turn out and peel off parchment paper
13. cool and cut into bars
demonstrations.review: Apart from the fact that I just made a horrible mess trying to fix these poor little bars (halved the doses of the recipe + had problems (...) in converting inches to centimeters and got a much too small pan -> bars were too thick and weren't cooking through -> tried to cut them and put them on a tray like biscuits -> -> now I have lots of truly delicious tasting crumbs... !(;P)) this is a GOOOOD recipe, and my mum is eating one heap of crumbs (!) after another!!! I only had about half the coconut I needed so I added 3/4 cups chopped dried apricots + 1/2 cup sunflower seeds and a tiny little bit of grated orange peel, great taste, thank you! (hope to do better with the "texture" next time!(:>))

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate in betweens

the in-betweens refer to the filling, but in our house it refers to meals, my dornettes are always nabbing one of these in-between!

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. in a food processor , mix the flour , salt , and butter
3. stop when everything is blended into a fine meal
4. add in the brown sugar
5. add the oatmeal , and pulse it to integrate
6. press about half the mixture into the bottom of a greased 9"x13" to 11"x14" pan
7. reserve the other half
8. in a saucepan , combine the condensed milk and chocolate chips , and heat the mixture , mixing constantly , until the chips are fully melted and integrated
9. pour over the crust in the pan
10. sprinkle the remaining dough over the top , coating it as evenly as possible , and then lightly press it
11. bake until lightly brown , about 25 to 30 minutes
12. variations
13. coffee in-betweens: omit the chocolate chips , and instead use four cups of strong coffee , boiled down to 1 / 2 cup or less of liquid
14. fruit in-betweens: omit the chocolate chips and condensed milk , and instead spread a layer of your favorite flavor of preserves in between the oatmeal cookie layers
demonstrations.review: These bars are quite good, but a little dry, and perhaps the top is a bit too crumbly, maybe a frosting would complement them well. However they're an easy and fast snack, I think the fruit preserve version would suit my taste better, I'll definitely give it another try!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
heavenly chocolate raspberry bundt cake

as if the chocolate bundt cake isn't yummy enough, this has a "tunnel" of cream cheese filling with chocolate chips and fresh raspberries added to make it even more decadent!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. grease a bundt or tube pan
3. make filling by creaming together , cream cheese with sugar and vanilla
4. mix in chocolate chips and set aside
5. for cake , sift together the flour , cocoa , baking powder and salt
6. beat eggs and gradually add the sugar and beat until the mixture is thick and pale yellow
7. beat in melted butter , then milk , water and vanilla
8. gradually add in the flour mixture and mix well
9. spread half the batter into the prepared pan
10. drop spoonfuls of the cream cheese filling evenly over the batter
11. sprinkle raspberries over the top
12. cover with remaining batter
13. bake at 375 degrees for about 1 1 / 4 hours
demonstrations.review: VERY rich, and incredibly addictive! I made it with chopped and slightly sugared strawberries (in Italy in this season raspberries are way too expensive to cook them in a cake...!)and it tasted wonderful, thank you for this great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
my favorite dutch speculaas

really simple, one bowl recipe.

my mum got this recipe from a friend at work as as soon as she made them i fell in love. i don't make them too often because i'll eat wayyyy too many!

1. mix all ingrediants together in large mixing bowl
2. shape into 1" balls and press onto cookie sheet
3. bake at 350 for 10-12 minutes
target.review: Wonderful! This is yummy!! I love the good old-fashioned taste. I followed the directions and ended up with a total of 72 cookies. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hopel popel

this dish could be served as a brunch dish, or for any light meal or snack.  when i came across this recipe tonight in a recipe book - the midweek cookbook: 200 ways with potatoes - i really hadn't looked at since the seventies, the name of this dish intrigued me.  a web search produced nothing  of relevance, just lots of references to dog breeding kennels! so unfortunately i know nothing of the origins of recipe's name.  i'm posting a c21st  adaptation here so that i remember to make it some time!  it's actually rather similar to what i've always referred to as a chip omelette, although i usually make that with diced raw potatoes.

1. saut the bacon , onion , garlic and mushrooms gently in the oil , preferably in a non-stick pan , then add the potatoes and allow them to warm through
2. beat the eggs , add the thyme , season to taste and pour over the potato mixture , sprinkle with grated cheese and cook slowly until the eggs have set
3. brown the top under the grill , cut into wedges and serve
demonstrations.review: Very good! Thank you for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
aromatic sticky rice

i made this in a cooking class at leith's in london. it's a very simple rice that always turns out like the rice served in thai restaurants in london.

1. put all the ingredients into a large saucepan and let stand for five minutes
2. cover the pan and bring to a boil , then reduce the heat and cook over a low heat for 10 minutes until the water is absorbed
3. remove the pan from the heat and allow to stand covered for five further minutes
4. remove the flavourings , if wished , and pile into a serving dish
5. serve immediately , while very hot
demonstrations.review: Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with avocado

from a magazine

1. cook pasta in boiling salted water for 10-15 minutes , drain while pasta is cooking , peel and stone avocados , mash , do not puree
2. mix in lemon juice , season with salt and pepper
3. heat oil in pan , add crushed garlic then avocado mixture , heat without boiling
4. stir in cream
5. pour over hot pasta
6. serve sprinkled with the parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I made this for lunch with a small salad and some Italian bread. This is a simple but tasty pasta dish. I added leftover smoked turkey and extra garlic and cheese. It was very quick and easy to make, and the sauce had a lovely flavour. I will definitely make it again! Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best ever waffles

every sunday morning, my mom and i used to get up early and make these wonderful waffles. this recipe has been in the family for years, and i will definitly be passing it down to my children.

1. in a large mixing bowl , whisk together all dry ingredients
2. separate the eggs , adding the yolks to the dry ingredient mixture , and placing the whites in a small mixing bowl
3. beat whites until moderately stiff
4. set aside
5. add milk and melted butter to dry ingredient mixture and blend
6. fold stiff egg whites into mixture
7. ladle mixture into hot waffle iron and bake
demonstrations.review: I served the waffles with real maple syrup. They were very easy to put together and I'll grant that they were airy and fluffy and tasty, but not the best waffles I've ever had. Though I will probably make them again. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quiche to die for

this is absolutely smashing!

1. trim crusts from bread , and line 9x13 pan
2. layer cheese , ham , broccoli and bread
3. mix eggs , milk and onion and pour over
4. bake 350 for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I added some mushrooms and black pepper. My family really liked the flavor, but the texture of the bread was just okay. This went together very quickly and easily. Thank you for posting!

target.recipe_text:
rice  krispies  date balls  aka angel cookies

another recipe from my aunt's recipe clippings. this one also came from the sept 19, 1969 chicago tribune originally. the clipping is crinkled with old yellow tape holding it together to make sure the recipes stayed intact. :) these are not like the typical angel cookies at all - they are little balls of dates, coconut, and rice krispies rolled in powdered. don't use the prechopped dates as they aren't sticky enough - buy the whole pitted dates and chop them yourself. also be sure to use the canned coconut..the kind that comes in bags is too dry and you will have a hard time getting the cookies to roll up otherwise.

1. in a saucepan , melt butter
2. add dates and granulated sugar and cook slowly , stirring constantly , until blended
3. add cereal and coconut , stirring to combine
4. remove from heat and let cool until you can handle the mixture without burning your fingers
5. form into 1" sized balls with greased hands , then roll each into powdered sugar to coat
target.review: Good, but next time I will make sure the butter and sugar melt together before adding the dates.  And I may use less sugar next time as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kelleigh s peachy special

this adult beverage is based off of dave's special with a peach twist. delicious and refreshing!

1. place ice in tall glass
2. pour peach schnapps , orange juice , grapefruit soda over ice and mix together
3. add cherry juice and cherries
4. for a garnish place pineapple on rim of glass
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Yummo. . .refreshing and the perfect pick me up after a rotten day!  I did add extra soda, but that's just because I was thirsty and wanted it to last a bit longer.  I used diet soda with great results.  THANKS for sharing!  I truly needed it today :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
albanian tomato cucumber salad

this traditional salad is served throughout albania. it is often served as first course.  typically this salad has equal proportions of tomato and cucumber. the rest of the ingredients are stictly added based on personal preference.  i got this recipe from some missionaries that have lived in albania for a long time.  they made a cookbook with other missionaries called "from bugs to beans."  posted for zwt 4.

1. combine tomatoes , cucumber , onion , and peppers in a mixing bowl and toss
2. drizzle the olive oil over the salad and season with salt to taste
3. garnish with olives and cheese
demonstrations.review: A perfect lunch salad.  I kept wanting to add vinegar out of habit and I am SO glad I didn't!  This is a simple and perfect recipe.  Eating it right now with a side of cottage cheese.  Didn't take a photo, as mine wasn't NEAR as pretty as the one currently posted!  Made for ZWT4.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek grilled fish

great for summer grilling and one of our favorite recipes. for variety you may make this using a variety of greek herbs and spices - i do! like adding a grating of black pepper just before it's done.  note ...  i have never used the optional bay leaves -  when using my fresh from the garden thyme or the organic packet of fresh herbs from the market - i let it dry before using and have added - "but dry it first!"to the ingredient list.

1. rinse and pat dry
2. lightly salt both sides , set in a colander over a bowl refrigerate until ready to grill
3. fire up the grill - brush grill with olive oil to prevent sticking
4. if you wish to lay aluminium foil on the grill poke several holes through foil or make the base with the dried thyme , rosemary branches and bay leaves directly on grill , be sure to overlap so they cover a slightly bigger area then the fish
5. in a small bowl combine the lemon juice and olive oil , brush fish with the mixture , sprinkle lightly with the coarse thyme or oregano - baste frequently with the lemon / olive oil mixture
6. cover the fish loosely with aluminium foil to keep moist
7. cook about 20 minutes or until fish flakes readily when prodded with a fork in the thickest part
demonstrations.review: Made for a challenge on ZWT4.  I layed a 1 lb scrod (cod) filet on a bed of fresh thyme, lemon slices and bay leaves.  Grilled at 400 degrees for about 15 minutes and it was perfectly cooked.  Beware that this cooking method REALLY permeates the fish with the herb flavoring so less may be more!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beet salsa

the beet, better known as the beetroot down under, is very popular in australia. this versatile beet salsa turns burgers and fish into something quite special! this recipe is from an australian recipe website. enjoy!

1. wearing rubber gloves to avoid staining your hands , peel the beet
2. coarsely grate the beet into a large glass or ceramic bowl
3. combine the mustard and lemon juice in a small bowl
4. stir the mustard mixture , dill and shallot into the grated beets
5. season with salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: Super easy.  I will be serving it atop some vegan "burgers" tomorrow for lunch.  My shallot was SUPER strong and I only used 1/2 of a bulb (thankfully).  Next time I will add a splash of vinegar and use green onions instead of shallots.  Thanks for posting!  Made for ZWT8 for Team Jammin Jazzberries for AUS/NZ.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer simmered brats

when i saw these on the commercial i had to get the recipe and make them! they are fantastic! serve them at your next cookout with plenty of cold beer to go along! everyone will love them!

1. prepare grill for direct grilling and preheat to medium
2. place beer , seasoning , onion and brats in medium pot and bring to gentle boil over medium heat
3. let brats simmer gently until partially cooked , 6 to 8 minutes
4. do not let brats boil , or they will burst
5. drain brats well
6. after removing brats drain and reserve onions also
7. place brats on grill parallel to grates and grill 5 to 7 minutes per side
8. internal temperature of brats should be about 170 degrees when serving
9. serve on buns with reserved onions and mustard
demonstrations.review: These are quite yummy, even if you don't bother to brown them off after simmering in the beer!

target.recipe_text:
sinfully delicious hot chocolate mix

this is so much better than the store bought dry mix. dont be afraid to be creative with the coffee mate....i have used the french vanilla on more than one occasion.

1. this makes 1 gallon dry mix
2. mix all ingredients together and store sealed
3. when you are ready for this sinful drink just fill a cup half full of mix and top off with boiling water
4. its out of this world
target.review:
I use Dutched Chocolate with mine to make it a bit more chocolatie.  Also, you can try to use a bit of orange liquer or mint with the recipe, but do it in small batches.  The liquer can be dropped into the milk and pulverized with a blender.  Just experiment.  You may try a bit of burnt Almond also.  I would pulverize it in the blender too.

My husband loves this so much, he requested it for his Christmas Present.  My children _Have_ to have it for camping.
Shepardes

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ginger vegetable lo mein

this is a wonderful, light lo mein. if you've never tried fresh gingerroot, try it--it has great flavor combined with the sesame oil. you could also try different combinations of vegetables.

1. place mushrooms in small bowl with boiling water , let stand 20 minutes while proceeding with recipe
2. after 20 minutes , drain mushrooms and reserve 1 / 2 cup liquid
3. chop mushrooms
4. cook noodles according to package directions , toss with 1 tsp sesame oil , return to pan
5. combine egg whites and egg
6. heat 1 tsp cooking oil and 1 tsp sesame oil in large skillet over medium heat
7. add egg mixture
8. cook without stirring until egg is set
9. flip egg and cook until set on other side
10. remove from pan and cut into short strips
11. heat remaining 1 tsp cooking oil and 1 tsp sesame oil in same skillet on medium-heat heat
12. add mushrooms , red bell pepper , garlic , ginger , crushed red pepper , and peas
13. cook and stir for 2-3 minutes
14. add mushroom liquid and teriyaki sauce
15. bring to a low boil , cook for 3-4 minutes
16. toss with noodles and egg strips , sprinkle with salt if desired
17. serve with low-sodium soy sauce
demonstrations.review: We loved the recipe, but added shredded cabbage and half a sweet onion to it.  The Shiitake mushroom gives it a unique flavor and was a hit with my family.  This one's a keeper!!!  Four stars because we added more stuff to it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy honey garlic ribs

you will love these there are better than any restaurant and the recipe may be doubled

1. set oven to 300 to 325 degrees
2. slice ribs into individual pieces
3. in a large bowl , combine honey , soy sauce vinegar , fresh minced garlic and brown sugar
4. stir until honey and brown sugar are completely dissolved
5. stir in the baking soda
6. transfer ribs to the bowl
7. turn to coat
8. cover a cookie sheet with foil , and arrange the ribs meat side up on the sheet
9. pour the excess sauce all over them , and sprinkle with garlic salt
10. bake for 1 hour , turning every 20 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Boy - OH - BOY!!  Are THESE some good eatin' ribs!

I made them at my house [an un-equivicable hit!] and then went to a family dinner over at my daughter's house and made them again!

EVERYONE just LOVED 'em!!

Good going and this recipe has found a home at my house!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s cream of potato soup or broccoli soup

this recipe has a slight smoky flavor due to the deli bacon. broccoli can be substituted for potatoes for cream of broccoli soup.

**this recipe can also be used for clam chowder.  eliminate the broccoli and use chopped clams.

1. empty cans of chicken broth in pot
2. add cubed potatoes and bring to a boil
3. while potatoes are starting to cook pan fry bacon until crisp and add bacon grease to chicken and potato broth
4. crumble bacon and add to broth
5. add diced ham to broth
6. in a sauce pan melt butter and add diced onion , celery and carrots
7. pan fry until soft
8. when potatoes are done add the celery , carrot and onion mixture with butter to broth
9. reduce heat to medium and add about 1 / 4 to 1 / 2 of the quart of heavy cream
10. be careful not to have soup at a heavy boil or cream will curdle
11. add enough cream to make soup look creamy throughout
12. add cheese
13. mix corn starch with very cold water and add to soup
14. continue medium boil until soup thickens
15. if it isn't thick enough repeat corn starch and add slowly
16. remove from heat and enjoy
17. soup will thicken when it gets cold
18. can add milk or water to thin out
demonstrations.review: Wow! We made this soup for Chrismas last year and it was wonderful!  We are planning on making it ahead this year and putting it in our ice cold garage to keep until Christmas [a COLD garage *if you can keep the critters out* is a wonderful place for an extra refridgerator in the winter].  A few exceptions with my notes . . . Use half and half for the cream and go light on the cornstarch, otherwise - OH YEAH!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
patriotic 4th of july cupcakes

patriotic cupcakes that can be used for any occasion.  you can always substitute your own recipe for white cake and white frosting.  in regards to the comment below, i went back to the original recipe to check and it does call for 2 tablespoons of batter per color -- i have never had any problems and i actually get 12 cupcakes out of this recipe.  i use scant tablespoons.  if anyone is worried, try it with teaspoons instead of tablespoons or even 1 tablespoon of the batters per cupcake.

1. prepare cake mix according to package directions
2. in a small bowl , combine 1 1 / 3 cups batter with blue food coloring
3. in another small bowl , combine red food coloring with 1 1 / 3 cups batter
4. leave the remaining batter plain
5. fill paper-lined muffin tins with 2 tablespoons red batter , 2 tablespoons plain batter , and 2 tablespoons blue batter
6. do not swirl batter , leave it layered
7. bake at 350f for 20-24 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in a cupcake comes out clean
8. cool 10 minutes in pan and then remove cupcakes to a wire rack to cool completely
9. frost with vanilla frosting and decorate with sprinkles
demonstrations.review: I loved these cupcakes and they were a huge smash with my grandkids! I would suggest getting a Red Velvet cake mix along with the white, so that one doesn't use too much of the red food coloring to make this. <br/><br/>As for the frosting....get a good cream cheese frosting mix to put on the top. With a very large frosting bag and a very large star tip, paste blue and red colored frosting (or just professional color paste) on the sides of the bag and carefully place the white frosting inside. Squeeze out the frosting for a bit until you get the nice mix of colors. Just to let you know, the colors will fade quickly, so with that in mind, you may wish to only figure on about 6 cupcake per bag of frosting to get the red, white, and blue colors to stand out. <br/><br/>I wish I knew where to find the cute cupcake papers, as those just top the whole presentation off. My grandkids didn't mind the regular blue, pink and yellow ones, but loved the cake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
excellent carrot cake

chock full of flavor, this is the best carrot cake! it tastes even better the next day after the flavors meld. a tad more time consuming than the average carrot cake, but well worth it!

1. combine first 5 ingredients
2. beat well
3. mix flour , soda , salt and cinnamon
4. add to creamed mixture
5. stir well
6. add carrots , walnuts , pineapple and coconut
7. stir well
8. pour batter into greased and floured 13x9 baking pan
9. bake at 350 for 55 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
10. buttermilk glaze: combine first 5 ingredients in large saucepan
11. bring to a boil
12. cook 4 minutes on medium heat
13. remove from heat
14. add vanilla
15. pour buttermilk glaze over warm cake
16. let cake cool
17. cream cheese frosting: mix cream cheese and butter
18. beat until smooth
19. gradually add sugar , beating until light and fluffy
20. stir in vanilla
21. spread cream cheese frosting on top of cooled cake
demonstrations.review:
I looked and looked for a carrot cake recipe that had all of the "goodies" in it and was also moist and tender - after all of my searching I have at LAST found it with this recipe!!
I put golden and regular raisins in the mix along with the nuts and coconut.  On of the reasons that this cake came out so wonderful, was the buttermilk glaze that was put on it while warm.  It's a wonderful cake and my family LOVED IT!  It's a KEEPER!!

target.recipe_text:
nate s italian beef

a friend of mine is a master of delicious meats and this is just one more of his amazing creations. this makes the house smell awesome and is excellent piled high on a roll with melty provolone cheese. oh, and don't forget the bibs...this one is messy!

1. mix all ingredients in a large crockpot
2. place the roast in the crockpot and cook on low 8-10 hours or until fork tender
3. remove the beef and shred with two forks
4. add back to the juices and enjoy
target.review:
Perfect Bar/Gameday food! Took some cold weather & a half day to make, but WELL worth it. EXTREMELY FULL OF FLAVOR! I went to town with the red pepper flake so it added a good kick. Top with spicey mustard, A1, or whatever. Will be making again.

CHART TOPPIN'!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
harvest pumpkin apple bread

all the flavors of autumn combined into one scrumptious bread. this tastes great with coffee or tea! i make this using egg beaters and unsweetened applesauce in place of half the oil to make it healthier. prep time includes cooling time.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease and flour two 9 x 5-inch loaf pans
3. combine flour , cinnamon , baking soda and salt in large bowl
4. combine sugar , pumpkin , eggs , vegetable oil and apple juice in large mixer bowl
5. beat until just blended
6. add pumpkin mixture to flour mixture
7. stir just until moistened
8. fold in apples
9. spoon batter into prepared loaf pans
10. bake for 65 to 70 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
11. cool in pans on wire racks for 10 minutes
12. remove to wire racks to cool completely
13. to make using three 8 x 4-inch loaf pans: prepare as above and bake for 60 to 65 minutes
14. to make using five or six 5 x 3-inch mini-loaf pans: prepare as above and bake for 55 to 60 minutes
demonstrations.review: Oh man was this a good find! I decided to expand my baking skills into holiday baked presents. I gave this to one my friends as a Christmas morning/breakfast gift and it didn't last the night. I also took a loaf to a Christmas Party and once again same result. Gone. Super Moist and Flavorful! The apples were just the right touch throughout to compliment the sweetness. I'm sure you could cut ingredient to save the calories, but why would you want too. This is the stuff holidays are made of!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I have to be honest and give this recipes an average 3 stars. I felt like it is a great starting point, but the end result I felt needed more flavor. Just a jar of salsa wasn't quite enough for my taste. Texas Pete helped out a little, but just didn't give enough flavor bite. I think this could go well on top of Nachos or a something that you can add flavor too. Anyway, probably won't be making again, but it was very easy and cheap to prepare.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stove top  roasted  red potatoes

this is a great and quick way to make red potatoes on the stove top and they still taste like they've been roasted in the oven for a long while. i had see on america's test kitchen how they make roasted potatoes, they microwave the potatoes first before the potatoes go in the oven, but then i thought to try them on the stove top. they turned out to be so good, tasted just like they had been on the oven, and took about half the time. you could also do these with golden or other small roasting potatotes.

1. wash the potatoes well , and slice into good bite-sized pieces
2. put them into a glass microwave safe bowl , and microwave for 8 minutes
3. remove from microwave and allow to cool for a few minutes
4. heat a skillet onto medium heat and add the butter
5. sautee the potatoes and add the seasonings to taste
6. cook for about 6-8 minutes and the potatoes are softened and browned
7. try olive oil
demonstrations.review: So had two lonely red potatoes sitting there with no idea of how to fix them. Jumped on here, and found this recipe and gave it a shot because it sounded too easy. WOW! Talk about hittin' the unexpected jackpot. Never would have thought to make them this way.  Exactly like oven-roasted in half the time. To be honest, I used all the ingredients, but i didn't measure anything. I just spiced it up to my preference. Definitely will make these again! Go to "red potatoes recipes". P'rciate it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red wine crock pot roast

yes, another roast recipe, but so very good!!! try it!

1. place roast in crock pot and season with pepper
2. mix rest of ingredients together and pour over roast
3. cover and cook on low 6-7 hours
4. remove roast to rest on platter
5. turn crock pot to high
6. whisk cornstarch into juices to thicken
7. this makes a wonderfully tasty au jus , or over mashed potatoes
8. enjoy !
9. you can easily make additions to this: garlic , pearl onions , mushrooms etc
demonstrations.review: I read alot of the reviews on this recipes and all the 5 stars convinced me to try it. I was kinda bummed at the result though. I think it was just my personal taste on this one. I added some baby carrots to the wine mixture and alcohol was almost over powering. Maybe I just used crappy wine. Maybe if I try this again I'll cut the wine down and add an onion. Overall this wasn't a a bad meal, just not my taste. The leftovers had a better flavor the next day too, so gives me hope for next time. Oh well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun bourbon chicken bites

this is a copycat recipe for the cajun chicken bites served in the food court in some malls. my family loves it. the prep time does not include the marinade time.

1. mix all the marinade ingredients , except white wine , in a zip lock bag
2. put chicken pieces in the bag
3. refrigerate at least several hours
4. bake chicken at 350 f for one hour in a single layer , basting with marinade every 10 minutes
5. remove chicken
6. scrape pan juices with all the brown bits and pour into a skillet
7. add any remaining marinade and add 2 tbsp white wine to the skillet
8. heat and add chicken
9. boil for one minute and serve over cooked rice , or as an appetizer with individual toothpicks in each piece of chicken
demonstrations.review: Very Nice Bourbon Chicken Dish! I used chicken breasts instead of wings cause that's all i had on hand. Still turned out awesome! I don't care for salty foods and I was worried about his turning out too salty, but it turned out marvelous. I think the 24  hr marinade-a-thon & 2/3 of bourbon (I'm Southern, we like Bourbon) intensified the flavor of this dish ten-fold. I probably used too much chicken cause there really wasn't enough liquid to make a lot of sauce for the end. Definitely will be making again! Chart toppin!

target.recipe_text:
marvelous broccoli salad

you may want to make a double batch of this salad. there won't be any left!!

1. combine all ingredients for salad
2. combine dressing ingredients
3. add to salad just before serving and toss
target.review: Great tasting broccoli salad. My husband who does not like broccoli gave this one the thumbs up. Thanks for posting Christine

demonstrations.recipe_text:
feta cheese foldovers

these are incredible! i always have to make a double batch. they are sure to be a hit and are so easy to make.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f in a small bowl , blend feta cheese , green onions , and egg
2. cut pastry into 12 squares
3. place a mounded tablespoon of feta mixture in the center of each square
4. moisten edges with water , and fold pastry over filling to form a triangle
5. press edges together firmly with a fork to seal
6. lightly brush pastries with the egg yolk mixture
7. bake for 20 minutes in the preheated oven , or until golden brown
8. serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: These foldovers are the best. This is the third time I've made them. The first one my son in law tasted them and took the whole batch. the second time I made them for Thanksgiving. the comment was MMMMMMMMMMMMMM this is good. The third batch is for me.   Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eric mccormack s amazing chocolate almond biscotti

from sandra lee's 'semi-homemade desserts' biscotti from cake mix? sounds too good to be true. one i must try. (eric mccormack is will from will and grace ^---)

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. line 2 heavy large baking sheets with parchment paper
3. combine cake mix , flour , melted butter , eggs , and almond extract in large bowl
4. beat for 2 minutes , or until dough forms
5. knead almonds into dough
6. scrape dough onto 1 prepared baking sheet and form dough into 13-inch log that is 3 inches wide
7. bake for 35 minutes , or until toothpick inserted into center of biscotti comes out clean
8. cool for 35 minutes
9. using serrated knife , cut log crosswise into 1 / 2-inch thick slices
10. carefully transfer half of the biscotti to second prepared baking sheet
11. arrange biscotti cut side down on baking sheets
12. bake for 15 minutes
13. reduce heat to 200f and bake for 40 minutes , or until biscotti are dry
14. cook completely
15. variation: melt dark or white chocolate , then dip bottoms of biscotti in chocolate to coat
16. transfer biscotti to wax paper and set aside until chocolate becomes firm
demonstrations.review:
I forgot to rate this recipe. from my previous review  a real keeper easy and delicious.  
Thanks again for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesecake factory cheesecake

i feel sad for anyone who has never been to a cheesecake factory restaurant. this cheesecake is out of this world! i think you will find the nut crust quite unusual. sometimes i double the crust portion of the recipe just so i can have a thicker crust.

1. crust: mix all nuts and vanilla wafer crumbs with melted butter and press into a 9 inch buttered springform pan , trying to line the sides as much as possible about 1 1 / 2" up the sides of the pan , set aside
2. cheesecake: all above ingredients should be at room temperature before your begin
3. start by beating the cream cheese until light and fluffy
4. keep the mixer on a low setting throughout the beating and mixing process
5. add the sugar a little at a time and continue beating until creamy
6. add one egg at a time and beat after each egg
7. when eggs have been mixed into the cream cheese add flour , vanilla and lemon juice , mix well
8. add the sour cream last and beat well
9. pour cream cheese into the spring pan
10. place on the top rack in the middle of a 325 degrees preheated oven for one hour and 15 minutes
11. when time is up , turn oven off , prop open oven door and leave in oven for one hour
12. after one hour , remove from oven
13. let cool enough before the cheesecake is put into the refrigerator for 24 hours
14. a cheesecake should season
15. the wait is worth it
16. the flavor ripens and becomes enriched
demonstrations.review: I served this wonderful cheesecake for a dinner party of 11, the rave reviews were wonderful to hear. I was told to chuck all my other cheesecake recipes and keep only this one. so this is the one and only from now on.   Thanks again. xannette you made my day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mu shu chicken

this is a very tasty streamlined recipe for chinese mu shu chicken. it makes a lot. avoid overcooking the vegetables.

1. heat the peanut and sesame oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet on medium
2. slice the green onions , using all the whites and enough of the tender green tops to make about 1 cup
3. immediately add the onions , shredded cabbage mix and mushrooms to the skillet
4. raise the heat to high and cook to soften vegetables , stirring from time to time
5. meanwhile , cut the chicken through its width into 1 / 4 inch wide strips , adding strips to the skillet as you slice
6. mix the cornstarch into the sherry and add it to the skillet along with the soy sauce and garlic
7. stir well
8. add the broccoli slaw and carrots and stir
9. continue to stir fry , stirring frequently , about 5 to 7 minutes until the chicken is no longer pink
10. just before serving , put the tortillas on a plate and microwave , uncovered , 1 minute 30 seconds to warm through
11. to serve , spread hoisin sauce to taste on each tortilla and spread 1 / 2 cup filing on each tortilla
12. roll up , burrito style
13. serve at once
demonstrations.review: Wonderful recipe for left over chicken. I added to a few ingredients. i/4 cup sherry and additional garlic. Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bruschetta chicken

i got this recipe from a local cable tv cooking show.

1. place flour and lighlty beaten eggs in separate containers that are large enough to accommodate each chicken breast
2. dip chicken in flour then in egg and place in greased 9x13 pan
3. combine the cheese , breadcrumbs & butter and sprinkle over chicken
4. loosely cover dish with foil & bake at 375 for 20 minutes
5. meanwhile combine remaining ingredients
6. uncover the chicken and bake an additional 5-10 minutes longer until top is browned
7. spoon tomato mixture over chicken , return to oven for 3-5 minutes or until just heated through
8. plate each breast and garnish with 2 or 3 whole basil leaves
demonstrations.review: This chicken recipe is high end resturant quality dinner. It was so good I felt I must give my review. YUMMMMM Thanks for posting Rhonda J

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken tortilla soup   ww

i found this on a weight watchers forum, which says it was from a southern living magazine.  1 point per cup.

1. place all ingredients in a crock pot
2. cook on high 6 hours
3. serve with shredded cheese , sour cream , and tortilla chips if desired
4. i omit the cayenne as we don't like it too spicy
5. also i use leftover chicken , cubed , and homemade broth
6. leftovers of this soup freeze very well
target.review: This soup was phenomenal!!!!  I actually used 2 cans of pre-cooked chicken and you couldn't even tell the difference!!! I put in the whole can of rotel for a little extra kick.  We, too, topped with a touch of shredded cheddar....  the cayenne gives the soup a great bite!!  We will DEFINITELY make it again!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww au gratin potatoes

from the ww website.  3 points per serving.

1. preheat oven to 375f coat a 2-quart covered baking dish with cooking spray
2. melt butter in a large pot over medium heat
3. add onion and cook , stirring occasionally , until onion begins to brown , about 5 minutes
4. stir in flour
5. add milk slowly , stirring
6. add potatoes and stir to mix
7. bring to a boil
8. stir in 3 / 4 cup of cheese , salt and pepper
9. pour mixture into prepared baking dish and level out surface
10. bake for 1 hour , uncovered
11. cover and bake until potatoes are fork-tender , about 20 minutes more
12. change oven temperature to broil
13. sprinkle remaining cheese over potatoes
14. broil 6 inches from the heating element until the cheese is golden brown , about 1 to 2 minutes
15. allow to cool for 5 minutes before slicing into 8 pieces
demonstrations.review: These potatoes are wonderful!!!!  I added just a couple slices of low fat Velveeta for a little more cheesiness (which increased the points a touch), but these potatoes were just as good as the full fat version!!  A little time consuming... but DEFINITELY worth the time... anxious to make again!!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy chocolate chip cookies  ww

these 2 point ww yummies are a family favorite.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. combine first 3 ingredients in a small bowl
3. stir well and set aside
4. beat egg whites using clean , dry beaters at high speed until foamy
5. gradually add granulated sugar , 1 tbls at a time , beating until soft peaks form
6. add corn syrup
7. beat until stiff peaks form
8. set aside
9. combine brown sugar , butter and vanilla extract in a medium bowl
10. beat at medium speed 5 minutes or until well-blended
11. fold brown sugar mixture into egg white mixture
12. gently stir in choclotae chips
13. drop by level tbls 1 inch apart onto baking sheets coated with cooking spray
14. bake at 375 for 10 minutes or until golden
15. remove from oven and let stand 5 minutes
16. remove cookies from pans and let cool on wire racks
17. store loosely covered
demonstrations.review: I liked these cookies!  They are good and definitely chewy!!  I only cooked mine for 8 minutes.  You have to be cautious not to overcook... as the next day, they are rock hard.  But great cookie for only 2 points!!!  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: I have to confess... as I was cooking this recipe, I was quite skeptical about how it would turn out by it's appearance before the cream cheese... but it was FANTASTIC!!!!!  I LOVE the "bite" from the red pepper...   Thank you for the AWESOME recipe... I am already looking forward to making this again!!!!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili s guiltless grill chicken sandwiches by todd wilbur

this recipe came from "top secret recipes, lite!" prep time includes the marinading time.

1. prepare the chicken marinade by combining the ingredients in a medium bowl
2. add the chicken fillets , cover , and refrigerate for several hours
3. overnight is even better
4. when the chicken has marinated , cook the fillets on a preheated barbecue or indoor grill set to a high temperature for 4-7 min per side or until done
5. while the chicken is grilling , make the fat-free dressing by mixing together the ingredients in a small bowl
6. build each sandwich by first stacking 1 / 4 of the lettuce on the bottom hamburger bun
7. stack the tomato slice on the lettuce
8. stack the chicken fillet on the tomato
9. cover each sandwich with the top bun and serve with honey mustard on the side
10. 8 points per serving
demonstrations.review: I actually just used this as a marinade for grilled chicken!!  It was wonderful and flavorful!!  I made a little extra of the honey mustard mix and just used as a dip!!  DELISH!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon better than sex cake   2 ww points

this is a light, lemony cake.  perfect for a summer barbeque or picnic.

1. mix lemon cake mix , egg white and diet soda
2. grease a 9x13 pan with non-stick spray
3. pour cake batter into pan
4. bake at 375 degrees for 35 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean
5. during the last few minutes of baking , put lemon jello and condensed milk in a sauce pan and stir on medium low heat until smooth
6. take cake out of oven and poke holes all over the top
7. pour jello mix over warm cake , filling in the holes
8. cool completely
9. mix 2 tsp lemon extract with cool whip
10. cover cake with cool whip mix
11. place cake in refridgerator until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: To heck with a summer barbeque or picnic.....  it's the middle of the winter and we are LOVING it!!!!!!!  I didn't have lemon extract so just put the fat free cool whip plain on top and it was wonderful!!!!  We are already looking forward to making this again!!!!

target.recipe_text:
chicken garlic bites

simple and fun to make, great to eat! prep time includes marinating the chicken.  use matzo meal instead of the breadcrumbs and this is good for passover as well.

1. place chicken in shallow dish
2. in small bowl , mix olive oil , garlic , and black pepper
3. pour over chicken
4. cover and marinate 30 minutes
5. drain
6. preheat oven to 475f
7. mix bread crumbs and cayenne
8. coat chicken
9. arrange in a single layer on cookie sheet
10. bake 10 minutes or until brown
target.review: OH These little guys rocked!  I love garlic and I love chicken, put them together and you have me sold!  I didn't let them marinate quite as long, my family was getting hungry and I was running late on making dinner.  The next time I make, as there will plenty of next times, I will let them marinate for the full 30 minutes.  The best thing about these bites is that you can kick up the cayenne pepper to make it as spicy as you want!  I served them with some ranch, but they really didn't need it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever shrimp and crab dip

this easy, but awesome, dip will get you rave reviews and requests for more every time you serve it.  it's best if made without substituting ingredients, so please try it first as written (no low fat/no fat ingredients).  any changes will alter the delicious end result.

1. mix softened cream cheese with mayonnaise and miracle whip
2. add salt , pepper , garlic salt / garlic , horseradish and worcestershire to taste
3. add small amount of milk to make creamy smooth
4. add shrimp and crab , stirring in carefully
5. chill for several hours
6. bring to room temperature before serving on assorted crackers
7. a light sprinkling of fresh chopped parsley on top adds to the presentation
8. cooking time is chilling time
demonstrations.review: I wasn't a big fan of this.  It was okay, but I felt like it was lacking something.  Maybe a spice or something.  I didn't use the miracle whip, because I hate the way it tastes.  Maybe I needed the sweetness of that.  Anyway, I took it to a family dinner and everyone else seemed to really enjoy it.  I will make it again, but I will be doing some tweaking!  Thanks for the recipe idea.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate no bake macaroons

great for a chocolate fix!

1. in a medium saucepan , combine sugar , shortening and milk
2. bring to a boil
3. remove from heat
4. add cocoa , salt , vanilla , coconut and oats , mix well together
5. drop by tablespoonful onto wax paper lined cookie sheets
6. chill and enjoy
demonstrations.review: OH MY GOODNESS!  These things were wonderful! My mom and I were looking up some easy to make cookies and did not have peanut butter to make regular no bake cookies.  We found this recipe, just made it, and they ROCK.  We only used a half a teaspoon of vanilla because we found that our vanilla was unusually strong.  (We made a chocolate glaze the night before with our vanilla.)  We also used an extra half cup of coconut in our batch.  Will be making OFTEN. Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken salad and avocado sandwich

i love chicken salad and i love avocado, so i figured i might as well put them together.  oops!  fixed mistake on mayo amount may 2012.

1. chop cooked chicken into 1 / 4-inch cubes and place in medium bowl
2. add pecans , celery , red onion , dijon mustard , lemon juice , jalapeo and salt
3. then add just enough mayonnaise to bind salad together
4. stir to combine and adjust seasoning as desired
5. spread mayonnaise or dijon mustard on the bread , mash half a avocado on each sandwich and top with provolone and romaine
6. on other half of each sandwich add the chicken salad , then put the two halves together and enjoy !
7. to prepare the cooked chicken , try cooking them in pineapple juice
8. it gives them a very nice flavor
demonstrations.review: Well, I got to reading all the reviews and I am guessin the pecans and celery were in the directions part but not the ingredients list.  LOL. whoops.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetable and ground beef soup

wholesome, hearty, and nutritious.

1. saut beef in pot or skillet until browned
2. add the beef , onion , cabbage and water in a large pot and boil until cabbage is tender
3. add the rest of the ingredients
4. add water till you have 2 inches of water above the solid part of soup
5. bring to a boil and then turn heat down and simmer about 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was wonderful. I of course did not go by the books. I dont like cabbage much, so I left it out. I am sure it gives the soup a different feel. This is how I made it. I sauted the onion and added garlic in light extra virgin olive oil and a pat of butter. I then added the meat, and browned it. I added the cans of green beans, corn, and carrots. Then I added a can of stewed tomatoes with basil and garlic and a can of stewed tomatoes with onions, peppers, and celery. I added a can of beef broth and some water. Not too much water. Then seasoned it with oregano, basil, parsly, thyme, salt, and pepper. Then I let it simmer for about thirty minutes. I forgot to buy a potato and the barley. I think next time I make this I am going to use fresh veggies including the potato, fresh herbs, the barley, and stew meat. It was very good, both my daughter and my husband loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steven s world famous to die for sour cream chicken

i've modified my grandmother's recipe for the 21st century. i can't have a dinner party and not asked to make this simple dish. enjoy!

1. clean chicken and pour sour cream over it and let marinate for about an hour in the refrigerator
2. meanwhile , take crackers and crush into medium course crumbs , mix in parmesan cheese and tarragon / marjoram
3. melt half of the butter and pour on the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish
4. dredge chicken in the cracker mixture and set in baking dish
5. repeat until complete
6. melt rest of butter and pour on top of chicken
7. bake@ 350 for 35-45 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: This was really good.  However, I did cut the butter down like everyone suggested.  I also felt like it was lacking a bit of kick.  I used thyme, paprika, garlic, freshly ground black pepper flakes and salt insted of tarragon, because I was out.  I also used bread crumbs, since I didn't have any ritz on hand.  I think next time I will use the ritz cracker.  I bet the buttery taste helps kick it up.  I will also use the tarragon next time I make it.  It turned out pretty good though.

target.recipe_text:
vanilla eggless and dairy free vegan cake

this is a simple yellow cake that is easy to make and very tasty. it can also be cut into slices and served with fruit.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. prepare cake pan: line 8-inch round or square cake pan with parchment paper and grease bottom and sides of the pan
3. then flour the pan
4. whisk together flour , sugar , baking soda , and salt
5. add vegetable oil , soy milk , and vanilla extract
6. whisk until no lumps appear and batter is smooth
7. add vinegar , stir about seven times , and quickly pour into pan
8. bake around 30 minutes , until cake begins to pull away from sides and / or toothpick inserted in the center pulls out clean
9. let sit for ten to fifteen minutes , invert , and cool on rack
target.review: Yummy cake.  Moist and delicious. I used 1 cup white whole wheat with 1/2 cup all-purpose flour and it worked out well. I made a chocolate glaze for the top and it was delicious. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese and garlic drop biscuits

these are very similar to red lobster's cheddar bay biscuits but a lot better than the recipes that start with bisquick, in my opinion. the kids adore them.

1. combine flour , salt , baking powder , cream of tartar , sugar and 1 / 8- 1 / 4 teaspoons garlic powder in a mixing bowl
2. cut in shortening using a pastry blender
3. mix milk and then cheese into mixture with a wooden spoon
4. drop by large spoonfuls onto greased baking sheet
5. bake at 425f for 10-12 minutes
6. mix melted butter and 1 / 8 teaspoons garlic powder together and brush on warm biscuits as soon as you remove them from the oven
demonstrations.review: I tried this using white whole wheat flour and soymilk and it was a bit disappointing.  Not as cheesy and garlicy as I had hoped.  It was hard to make 10 biscuits with this recipe, it made more like 5-6 for us.  Easy recipe though.  I would recommend sticking to the recipe without the above substitutions.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker garlic chicken

it doesn't get any easier than this. intense flavor

1. pour stock and wine into cooker
2. combine salt , pepper and herbes de provence and sprinkle on both sides of chicken
3. put chicken into cooker and add garlic around chicken
4. cover and cook on low for 8 hours
demonstrations.review: This stuff is amazing. I used 1 lb. of boneless skinless breast and used sake in place of the white wine.  Let it cook all day (~9 hours) and it was delicious. I served this over mashed potatoes and carrots with a side of garlic/rosemary green beans. A great dinner. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no fat carrot raisin salad

very light, tasty summer salad. i like to eat it for breakfast.

1. combine yogurt , honey , cinnamon and lemon juice to make dressing
2. add the rest of the ingredients
3. chill at least 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: I thought this recipe was okay.  I've never had carrot raisin salad before, so I can't comment on how this compares to the full fat version.  I doubled this recipe and that might have been my problem, but am finding it has a really strong cinnamon flavor and just find it be a weird mix of sweet flavors between the raisins and pineapple and the nonfat yogurt.  Sorry to say but I won't be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black eyed pea masala

this is a recipe that i adapted from a recipe my mil made while i was in india. it is fabulous, and is even served for breakfast quite often in her house! (i could eat it for every meal lol)  i donut know the actual name of the chilies they use, but at home i generally use either 2 of the small chiles labeled "hot green chiles" from the market, or i use serranos. the ginger i generally just run over my microplane.

1. drain your peas
2. heat oil / ghee in a medium heavy pot over medium heat and fry chiles , garlic , onion , and ginger for approx 6 minutes
3. add your curry powder / garam masala , turmeric and cumin , and then add the tomatoes
4. cook for approximately 3 minutes until it begins to thicken and add your peas and salt to taste , along with 4 cups of water
5. allow water to boil and then reduce your heat , cover and cook for approximately 2 hours until your peas are done and the sauce is nice and thick
6. after the peas are done , fold in your yogurt and cilantro , and serve
7. this goes well with rice or with chappati / roti
8. garnish with minced cilantro
demonstrations.review: This dish is easy and delicious. I used 2 whole, large jalapenos and wished I had only used one. Really spicy, but good.  The yogurt makes it nice and creamy.  I will make this again.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: I was disappointed in how this chicken tasted. The meat was kind of tough and dry and the glaze never really got sticky despite removing the chicken to reduce the glaze.  The flavor on the skin and outer meat was good, but the glaze/sauce did not permeate very deeply.  Glad I tried it, but I probably won't make this again.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s lemon cream cheese pie

a pie so good it is worthy of selling in a bakery!  prep time includes the refrigeration time --- see my recipe#66929

1. in a saucepan , combine sugar , cornstarch and pinch of salt
2. stir in water , lemon juice , lemon rind and yellow food colouring bring to a boil over medium-high heat
3. cook , and stir for 2 minutes , or until smooth and thickened
4. remove from heat
5. stir in butter
6. cool to room temperature for about 1 hour
7. meanwhile , in a mixing bowl , beat the cream cheese and the powdered sugar until smooth
8. fold in the whipped cream and the 1 tbsp lemon juice
9. remove 1 / 2 cup of the whipped cream / lemon mixture for the garnish
10. spread the remaining cream cheese mixture into the baked pastry shell
11. top with the cooled lemon filling
12. chill in the fridge for a minimum of 8 hours or overnight
13. when ready to serve , scoop the reserved 1 / 2 cup cream cheese mixture into a pastry bag with a star
14. pipe stars onto the pie , or garnish with the reserved cream cheese mixture or as desired
15. refrigerate until ready to serve-- delicious !
target.review: When I see Kittencal on this site I assume it is a good recipe. This did not disappoint. It was fairly easy, very lemony, and pretty to behold. This is easier than a lemon meringue, but you get all the tart and creamy goodness. My one slight complaint with my pie was that the lemon layer did not set quite as firm as I had hoped so slicing was a bit messy. The flavor to a true lemon lover made this a non-issue in the long run though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chilean cilantro salsa  pebre

there are many variations of pebres, mildly hot or very hot, according to taste. this one is adapted from "the south american table," by maria baez kijac. you can add one finely chopped tomato to the salsa, if you like. serve in a small bowl with grilled meat, chicken or seafood.

1. mash garlic , salt and pepper into a paste in a medium bowl
2. whisk in oil and vinegar until emulsified
3. place green onions , jalapeno , cilantro and water in a blender
4. pulse until minced , but not pureed , about 10 seconds
5. stir into the oil and vinegar mixture
6. cover
7. let stand 2 hours to develop flavors
demonstrations.review: If you have never tried this--you are missing out on one of life's greatest pleasures. Make sure you get as much stem off the cilantro as possible. It is FABULOUS with crusty bread, tortilla chips or as a nice topping for grilled fish, chicken or pork.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mini chicken cigars with sweet and sour dipping sauce

this savory little morsel was one of the appetizers featured when food network chefs catered a wedding.  (rachael ray's offering).

1. for the chicken cigars: preheat oven to 425f
2. place chicken in a bowl and mix with spices and parsley
3. place a piece of phyllo on a nonstick cookie sheet and brush with some of the melted butter
4. repeat 3 more times , placing each of phyllo over the last buttered sheet to make 4 layers
5. cut layered phyllo into 16 rectangles
6. on one end of each of the rectangles , place a heaping tablespoon of chicken filling
7. roll up tightly to make mini "cigars"
8. cut each of these in half and place on a cookie sheet
9. butter the tops of each
10. bake for 10 to 12 minutes , until golden brown
11. repeat with second half of phyllo sheets and chicken mixture
12. make the sweet and sour dipping sauce by whisking together plum or duck sauce and vinegar in a bowl
13. stream in oil and continue whisking to combine
14. season with salt and pepper
15. fold in mango and sliced scallions
16. serve either hot or at room temperature with dipping sauce
demonstrations.review: Everybody loved these! I am thinking about using them for a catering event so I cooked them a couple hours ahead of time to see if they would stay crispy. They were crisp and delicious after sitting out for 3 hours or so. I did change up the seasoning a bit and added fresh garlic, a splash of my homemade basalmic marinade, paprika and flat leaf parsley. I also did a couple with the filling from recipe #52467 BLT bites and that also held up and was very tasty. I also just brushed 2 sheets rolled the whole thing and cut into 5 pieces. The possibilities are endless. Thanks so much for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curry chicken with coconut and peanuts

when i was in college, i worked in an asian restaurant. my boss made the best curry i have ever tasted, and after much prodding and bothering the poor man, he finally fessed up! i have worked for years to get the recipe right, and i think this is it! i hope you like it as much as i do.

1. cut chicken into cubes , and sprinkle with salt and pepper
2. slice onion in julienne , and mash garlic
3. in a large wok , , heat oil to just below smoking
4. add garlic and stirfry til golden , and quickly add onions , and stir
5. when the onions begin to soften , add chicken , and stir fry until cooked through and browned a bit--liquid from chicken should all be evaporated
6. add wine and reduce a little , then add peanut butter , boullion , ginger , curry and cilantro
7. stir to coat well , and until peanut butter has melted
8. add water , and simmer about 15 minutes , or until flavors have blended well
9. add coconut milk and heat to just below boiling , then add cornstarch slurry to thicken as desired
10. serve over steamed rice , with chopped cilantro and peanuts to garnish
11. i like it a bit spicy , so i also add chopped chilies , or cayenne to the dish
demonstrations.review: This is by far the best curry I have ever eaten. Usually it has a slight bitterness to it and this did not have that at all. I steamed some broccoli separtely and served it over the rice before I spooned the curry over top. It kept it from being over cooked but the broccoli was DELICIOUS with the sauce. Just about any meat or veggie would be good with this! Beyond excellent Canarygirl! Thanks for sharing!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach delight   lana s spinach salad

this is my favorite salad. this is easy to put together and it is always adored by everyone. i could make a meal out of this salad alone. another great recipe from my mother-in-law!

1. mix dressing ingredients together in jar
2. place all salad ingredients in a large salad bowl and toss together
3. toss in salad dressing just before serving
demonstrations.review: I LOVED the idea of the water chestnuts! My hubby hates mushrooms and this sounded like a good alternative. I actually used a slightly different variation of the dressing that was sweetened rice wine vinegar, coarse mustard and hot sauce. Sweet and tangy all the same though. What put it over the top was that I marinated the water chestnuts in the dressing for a couple hours before serving time and they really absorbed the flavor. Everyone commented on how good they were and the crunch can't be beat. My hubby and boss were fighting over the last morsels on the tray. If boys eat veggies I know it is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cake mix carrot pineapple cake

so easy, don't drain the pineapple juice from the crushed pineapple! serving are only estimated depending on the size you cut the pieces. my recipe#90142 works great with this cake ;-)

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. in a large bowl whisk eggs , then add in all remaining ingredients except the cream cheese frosting
4. mix to combine well
5. transfer to prepared baking pan
6. bake for about 30-35 minutes or until cake tests done
7. cool completely then frost with cream cheese frosting
demonstrations.review: This is so much better than nasty carrot cake mix, but is still easy because you still use a good cake mix as the base. I made them as cupcakes for my daughter's preschool class so I could claim at least a little nutritional value. I made a double batch and used a whole 20 ounce can of crushed pineapple (in the double batch). I also threw in about 1/4 cup of ground flax to sneak in a little extra nutrition. I will probably use more carrot and a little more cinnamon & nutmeg next time. I will use this recipe again. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
target.review: This recipe was so good. You can really taste the bananas. It is embarrassing to admit that my husband and I finished the whole bread in less than 2 hours! I cannot wait for the bananas I have now to overripe so I can bake this again! I added about 1 teaspoon of pure vanilla.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean couscous salad

this is a delicious salad containing all four food groups ( if you use the red kidney beans)

1. cook couscous in 1 cup of water
2. cool to room temperature
3. whisk together lemon juice and olive oil
4. pour over other ingredients combining well
5. season with fresh pepper
demonstrations.review: Hum hum hum! This was very good! But I did change a few things: I only used 1 tomato, 3/4 cup of feta, 1 tablespoon of oregano, added the beans and skipped the nuts. It was so good. I will make more for sure! Thank you so much for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
neiman marcus  250 chocolate chip cookies recipe

i received this recipe from a friend

1. measure oatmeal and blend in a blender to a fine powder
2. cream the butter and both sugars
3. add eggs and vanilla
4. mix together with flour , oatmeal , salt , baking powder and soda
5. add chocolate chips , grated hershey bar and nuts
6. roll into 1 inch balls and place 2-inches apart on a cookie sheet
7. bake for 10 minutes at 375 or until golden
demonstrations.review: I have to be honest and say that this recipe is really bad. I threw all the cookies after tasting one. My boyfriend did not like them either and he loves cookies. The taste and texture is not good. To give you an idea of what kind of cookies I enjoy, my favorite store brought cookies are the chewy chips ahoy from Nabisco. If you look at all the reviews I give, I never give under 5 stars. If I did not follow de recipe or dislike it, I dont give any stars, just a review. Because this is not your recipe but from Neiman Marcus, I dont feel bad since I wont hurt your feeling...Sorry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek rice   rice with spinach and feta

this recipe for a delicious and easy rice side dish came from michael at gail’s recipe swap, and i’ve fiddled with it a little.  although i don’t get to eat rice often, this one looks so tasty i have to put it here for safe keeping when i get to splurge!  :)

1. over medium heat in a saucepan , combine the rice , broth , and water , and bring to a boil
2. cover , reduce the heat to medium low , and let simmer for 15 to 18 minutes or until the rice has absorbed the liquid
3. transfer to a serving bowl and keep warm
4. in a skillet over medium heat , melt the olive oil and butter together , then add the onion , mushrooms , and garlic for 5 to 7 minutes , then stir in the lemon juice and oregano
5. add the spinach and pepper , then sprinkle with the sherry and toss until the spinach is slightly wilted
6. remove from heat
7. add the crumbled feta and toss until the cheese begins to melt
8. add to the cooked rice , toss well , and serve immediately
